name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar
detailed_description: The encore to I Expect You To Die is here... Welcome back, Agent! Right now, Zoraxis believes you are dead. To capitalize on this moment, we are sending you deep undercover to explore some diabolical intelligence the Agency has received regarding Zoraxis’ move for world domination. Here’s what we can tell you now...your first mission is to protect the prime minister, who is attending a theater production featuring world-famous actor and celebrity John Juniper. Agent, we need you to: Use your ever-present power of telekinesis to solve puzzles, escape dangerous situations, and manipulate objects. Go undercover using disguises to figure out exactly what Zoraxis is up to. Not die. What to ‘Expect’ in I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar (besides...you know 💀): Embark on six new missions Put your cunning to good use as you solve confounding puzzles and travel across the globe to stop Zoraxis’ plans for world domination. Every mission is a new scene and you are the star! Start your adventure with a brand new 360° intro sequence You are in for an amazing visual and audio experience with the intro credits. Puddles Pity Party belts out the new theme song in his well-honed baritone. Meet John Juniper Rub shoulders with John Juniper, celebrity extraordinaire, voiced by famed actor Wil Wheaton . Play in comfort Explore new locations and environments in this seated experience that can be played with one or two hands. The game was built with accessibility in mind. Experience more of everything In this sequel, you will get more immersive mission spaces, more characters, more music in every level, more food to eat, more disguises, and it goes without saying...more dying! Join our Discord server for the latest intel.

short_description: Become an elite super spy ready for espionage, explosives, and gadgets galore. This popular escape-the-room VR franchise is back with more ingenious puzzles, cunning villains, and dangerous locales.

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You to Die 2 is a prime example of everything a franchise should aim for when making a sequel. if it ain't broke, don't fix it.The narrative is way more thoughtful  and developed than its prequel and it truly makes you believe that you are in fact a secret agent on a mission to save the entire world. While the original took you on many different settings that vastly differed from each other, this one takes you on a more cohesive one that feels more complete.The controls are just as snappy as the original and it really makes you wish that more VR titles would adopt similar controls because they work as intended and they don't hinder the experience in any way.To me, the puzzles felt a bit easier than the prequel but this could be the result of many factors such as me being more familiar with the franchise and the developers having more experience fine tuning their puzzles, which in return, would make them less cryptic than the original. All in all, I'll take easier thoughtful puzzles over harder bur cryptic ones.If you loved the original, than you'll surely have an amazing time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Another incredible VR experience just like the first game, an action-puzzler all from the comfort of your seat. The joy of experimenting with the environment usually squanders moments of frustration that do come with puzzle games, with few exceptions.Though, what I particularly appreciated about this one is the unique blend of comedy and emotional investment that encompasses the style of story telling. It's definitely a mostly fun, uppity and comedic atmosphere. The game is self-aware of how cliche it is, but to also have that perfect sprinkling of seriousness that if anything helped compliment the story, especially at the end, was mind-blowing. Or maybe I just really liked the ending, and the intro, and the dialogue ("ARE YOU WEARING ONE OF MY MASKS?! XD).I nominated this game for the "VR GAME OF THE YEAR" Steam Award!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece. The first one was my absolute favorite VR game that I bought. I had this on my wish list since it popped up and bought it immediately. It's truly amazing the time and thought process these games take to make. Some of the levels are a bit short, but that's my only criticism. 11/10, can't wait for #3!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 1 and 2 are both masterclass games in what can be done with VR.  They're both incredibly well polished games with a puzzle or escape room style gameplay, but there are enough hidden Easter eggs and a built in speedrun mode to keep you engaged on a replay.Absolutely amazing, and I can't wait for the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first one, it was a very refreshing game, beautiful and original. This one has the very same likable aspects, but the puzzles are way easier, and levels are too quick to resolve for being enjoyable. I'm disapointed by the lifetime of I Expect You To Die 2, even knowing that one day some more levels will be published.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first one and this one might be even better. It has a more consistent story line, more interesting environments and puzzles, and more good voice actors. Only complaint I really have is the lack of levels. Now in the first one they added more to fix this problem and while I will love it if they do that with this, it's being sold with the price tag of complete game, not early access.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I can't decide if this game is as good as the original or not. On one hand I prefer the level design and puzzles from the first, although only by a slim margin, but this has a complete and compelling story with an incredible final level. Either way it's an incredibly fun game and once again proves how great VR can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't worry guys, there's even more dying in this one! It's very clear to me that the devs still had tons of ideas they wanted to explore after the first game as every chapter in this sequel is super unique and they all twist in fun directions. The feel of a spy movie is even stronger here and the music is incredible. The mechanical side of how objects look, feel, and are interacted with has thankfully improved dramatically. Other than that what can I say? It's more VR puzzle game goodness.

_childDocuments_.review: From Schell Games presents I Expect You To Die 2, the sequel to I Expect You To Die. Believed to be dead from the last game, go undercover, solve puzzles and missions to foil the villains plan for world domination. Playing on the OG Vive headset, it is a game that is easy to control and play. It is a comfortable game as it is seated, just requires enough space to lean around the position. Though everything you need to interact with in the levels are fine enough to access and interact with. Controls at first may take a bit to getting use to with the telekinesis aspect for interacting with objects and the environment, but do get the hang of it after a bit. Controlling your two hands is very fun, bringing items towards you and away from a distance, throwing and juggling them is also neat.  From food to munch, sets of disguises and the stages and levels themselves, there are a lot to interact with. The puzzles are quite fun to solve as you have to look around the area you are at, from locked drawers, coded passcodes,  pictured instructions etc, you are to find out how to progress. Visually it does look really nice with all the details of the rooms and objects. The sandwich and fruit that are in your own personal mini fridge was quite delicious. Music is also a plus, with the opening credits song being extremely captivating. it is a great sequel to the game, and overall a very nice vr and puzzle game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative "yes" on my recommendation to others. Not because the game is bad, mind you- it just felt drastically shorter than the original I Expect You To Die. I'm hoping that they will add on extra levels, like they did with the first game. If so, that would give this game the shot in the arm it needs.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 2 is a lot like the first game with a little more pizazz. Some of it's missions feel very short, while others had a nice length to them. The puzzles weren't anything difficult, I think there was only one time I spent longer than 7 minutes figuring out. But if you liked the first game, I would Heavily recommend buying this sequel. I'd say its an 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking at this game, you've probably played the first IEYTD game and wondering if the second is better or not. TBH the second is on par or in some peoples opinion even better than the first. If you've played the first get the second whirl of IEYTD The Spy and the Liar and have at it. Me and my sibling are in love with this series and are playing back and forth. Although a 3rd IEYTD might not be possible, I would not be dissapointed if they made a third. Amazing job Schell Games you've done it again!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I HIGHLY suggest you play the original before this one. it's not that expensive and it does help the story a bit.If you played the first game and did not like it. you will probably not like this one eitherNow if you have played the first game and enjoyed it. then this game is for you. This is a completely worthy sequel to IEYTD. All the missions are a little better connected and the story is overall better than the first, the visuals are just as nice if not nicer. There are new gameplay mechanics, especially in the first and the 3rd last mission.This is of course also a cheap vr game, so the length is nothing to brag about. I got through the main story with multiple failures within 3 hours. Bugs there are, few, but there are bugs, though the bugs are somewhat expected of a vr game. just items clipping into eachother and sometimes not interacting with eachother properly.(the game has also been out for just a few hours so I mean it really isn't that bad)I will update this review if I ever 100% IEYTD2.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I loved IEYTD1, but this one has so much more. It's got an actual storyline, each mission is harder than the next and just as hard as the first IEYTD. This game also has the BEST intro trailer than any other VR game out there right now. I think I've watched the intro more than I've played the missions.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first game and this does not disappoint. Almost every new mission trumps what the first one offered. The second mission is possibly one of the best experiences you can have in VR. The music, atmosphere, and puzzle design is phenomenal and every minute was incredibly enjoyable. The fifth mission was a little disappointing, but story wise it was great. Highly recommend and I cannot wait for the potential DLC. Onto finding all the collectibles now!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I never write reviews but the music, puzzles and general storytelling of this game was brilliant, i truly felt like a dumbass agent annoying every being that i came in contact with (Also the games styling is also brilliant c:)12/10 I wish i had no memory of playing this so i could play it again for the first time
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This as well as the prequel is the PERFECT game for anyone who wants an actual puzzle solving experience. The puzzles are incredibly clever and are very fun to solve. The only real complaint I have about the game is that there isn't more post game content or something to make the game more re-playable
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: There's not too much to say for IEYTD 2, if you played the first game and liked it you'll adore this one, and if you didn't like the first game you'll hate it. If you haven't played the first game then go play that first. That said, as more of the first game with a more cohesive storyline you'll adore it.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: My first experience in VR was the original I Expect You To Die which made me a believer and had me hunting for a VR headset everyday after I tried it.I Expect You To Die 2 stays true to it's core and is just as good as the original.  Right off the bat the intro already gives the impression of a high quality VR game and it continues throughout the entire playthrough.  The narrative of the game does a great job of keeping the game immersion while being an entirely seated experience.  It's both comfortable, yet engaging.  The only downside of the game is that I wish it were longer, but mostly because I didn't want it to end.  The replayability is somewhat limited to going back for missed souvenirs. Although I mostly played the original before they added more levels I hope they add additional levels and content to this one as well.  If you are a fan of the original you will enjoy the sequel as it is more of the same.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a VR delight just like the first one. The puzzles and gameplay are a lot of fun. It really nails the 60s-ish spy vibe with visuals and music. I'd say this one is even more thrilling towards the end in terms of story. Overall a fantastic follow up. If you liked the first one, definitely play this. If you haven't played the first one and like puzzle games, go play it then play this. Only thing I think could be improved is I wish more of the achievements showed up on Steam instead of just in game as "souvenirs." I enjoy looking through those on my Steam account from time to time and I like the little Steam popups as I play often saying something funny.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same from the first game. The game is quite short for asking price, so pick it up on a sale.There's some replay value here with per-mission challenges and a speedrun challenge, but that kind of thing is not for me.The puzzles are not that difficult, I'd say they are easier or the same as the first game. There was one step that had me stumped for a while (), but it all can be figured out on your own no problem, just gotta pay attention.The main theme is not as cool as the first game, but it's still good.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing sequel to one of my favourite VR games of all time. I Expect You To Die 2 improves upon the already brilliant formulae of the original with a new polish in the form of better graphics, a full story on release as well as new and exciting puzzles and mechanics for the play to solve.Positives:-Very fun-Mechanics feel smooth -Puzzles are relatively simple but make you feel like a genius when solving them As for negatives the only thing I don't like about it is that there won't be any episodes added to it like the first game, making it longer on release than the original game but less episodes overall. Hopefully IEYTD gets frequent enough releases to keep us all entertained.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: An astounding follow up to the spectacular I Expect You To Die, this puzzling spy thriller takes a more theatrical approach to the gameplay established in the last game. While it did feel pretty short, the set pieces and story this time around blew me away, with the ending of this game leaving me wishing for more as the credits rolled.Rise from the ashes, Pheonix.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: its worth it for the intro alone! if you are a fan  of the first then you will like this one too. its like escape the room but in VR. i was playing the first one, and i think they improved on creating nice and interesting settings.          first one comparatively has more content because they added on lots of free stuff after launch so if you dont have it already get the first one, more bang for your buck. im really happy with these developers, they have such talent and create wonderful virtual spectacles. A unique style thats funny but also classy. the replay-ability is meh but going for the speedruns are very fun and challenges can add to it so you dont blow right through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: How do I even start to explain how great this game is.Just take everything the first game was and expand on that, that is pretty much it.There are more levels, more characters, more amazing voices, interesting twists and so much more.And the intro this time, jeez. It is the best one so far, it is so catchy that I listen to it at least once a week and it gets stuck in my head more often than I will ever admit, it is  amazing.The only thing that I preferred in the first game, is the 'hub', in this case, a tiny van.I loved the office from the first game where you could play around with sticks of dynamite, guns and more in this big space. This time around you're just stuck in a tiny van with barely any place to move. This would be fine if you could like open the doors behind you or maybe just have some special area or something, but no. It makes sense for the story, but personally I still prefer the big office.I cannot recommend this game enough and I am so excited for the third game, I hope they never stop making these! :D
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big IEYTD1 fan. So it's only natural I was going to like #2. The environments are more complicated and missions are much longer with so many more options to learn and master. I have seen people say they completed this in 2 - 3 hours, but my first full playthrough was much longer. It was about 5 - 6 hours. I did struggle on a few of the levels and persisted until eventually found the solutions. I found the game enjoyable and rewarding. I liked how the story linked the missions, which was much better than #1. As with the first game, the replay value is in collecting the achievements and speedrunning. Which is super competitive. So once you have completed the game, there is plenty of reasons to play it again. It's a polished game and definitely worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played the first game yet, go play it. But this game has not only lived up to the expectation it was given but it exceeded it. Even when I beat it the second play through I had chills going down my spine. The only things I don't like about this game is how short it is for the price and that there isn't any finger tracking for the index, but that's really just a quality of life thing. other than that I give this game a 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first game ages ago and it was great. However the sequel improves in all aspects: A finished story from day one, polished level design and a finale that was somehow better than even the finale of the last game. I would have bought this game for twice the price; even though it is fairly short, there is a fair amount of extra content after you finish the main story which I fully intend to take advantage of. I eagerly await the third game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Its ironic that a mediocre actor with delusions on grandeur voice acts a mediocre actor with delusions on grandeur.If you have played the first game in the series, then this game is a continuation of the awesomeness of that title. its easily my favourite VR title and this one offers more of that same game play style that really works so well on the VR headset. If you haven't played the first, while I dont think its necessary to have done so, the game would make a lot more sense if you had. Like the first, the puzzles weren't too hard to figure out, but i still felt a sense of satisfaction in solving them and I am looking forward to replaying them to try and get all of the achievements, including the speed run times. The clues are all there, but sometimes you need to look around a bit to find them. There were a couple of moments where i felt the controls were a little clunky but for the most part it felt well designed.My only real complaint about the game is in the choice of lead voice actor. I find the man unjustifiably smug at the best of times and he is no better in this as he just plays himself and at no point did i really feel like he was this world dominating super villain. which is sad because it could have made the game that oh so much better. That said, his talent is easily forgettable so it really was only a minor detraction from what is otherwise quite the fun puzzle game. TLDR: Game is fun, puzzles are challenging but not insurmountable. I got about 3 hours on first play through. hoping to get another 3 hours getting all the achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this if you like the first game or if you're ok with dying and doing the same thing over and over. It's a stationary escape the room game with 6 missions. It's very polished with good music and voice acting. Some of the controls need work though. It can sometimes be  annoying trying to manipulate small objects. There are multiple souvenirs and hidden objects to find. It took me about 6 hours to finish. My gameplay video is below.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I am using htc vive, and the game "head mounted display is not supported", but the controller is the real problem during the game. The operation of pulling items by the vive joystick is often out of control (not battery problem, no problem when playing other games), which greatly affects the game experience (especially related to speedrun time)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game (minus one giant annoyance which I hope they patch). Same with the first game, it's a chair-only VR, and the comedy is fairly good, and the spy theme is great to play. I hope they continue to make more of these. I know it takes a lot of effort to make a good puzzle game like this, and I'm sure it's annoying when people complain there's only so much content, but I hope the dev can ignore the haters and make more of this series.As for that annoyance, there's one mission where the controller vibrates when you're in an elevator. Literally you spend half the mission with your controller rumble at full power for no reason, draining the battery for nothing (as in I had to plug in my controllers to finish, they were not low battery when I started). At first I thought my controllers were broken because it wouldn't stop... I just disabled the rumble for the game completely at that point. 3 hours to complete, but went back to complete achievements for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A great sequel to a great game. Love the story, the voice acting, the original music and most importantly the game play itself. Only complaint I would have is the same I have for any great puzzle game - I wish it was longer. Don't get me wrong - this isn't one of those VR puzzle games you will solve in 10 mins, I just really enjoy the game, the immersive atmosphere, etc. and want more of it! Highly recommend. Hopefully IEYTD3 isn't too far away :)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Only two hours in and it's clear why this game has such positive reviews. It's incredibly addictive. Good game mechanics allow for a reasonable seated play experience. Good quality graphics and compelling game play, with replay potential as you try to beat the clock. I loved the first game and this second looks to live up to the expectations! The bond-esque intro and credit scene only adds to the anticipation. Well recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Dont get me wrong, i enjoyed this game but compared to the first one it didnt feel like a lot of effort had been put into the scenarios and puzzles. Think about the submarine and the space station in the first game. Nothing like that, just really simple basic puzzles. Add to that the guy speaking in your ear gives you waaay to much help. Too dumbed down imo and the puzzles are so easy that you're doing well to stretch this out to 3 or 4 hours of play. Buy if you're a fan but avoid if you;re expecting something on the same level as the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much easier and shorter than the first game. I felt that the puzzles were much less inventive and intricate. I am disappointed in the game for how much money that I spent on it, especially compared to the first one.It's still a good game, but I would just get it at a heavy discount, as there isn't much in it.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Find my full review at ProsFantastically designed puzzlesSo many little details in the presentationLots of hidden items to findWil Wheaton’s performance as John JuniperConsA few more levels would be niceTrial and Error might be off putting to someFeels more like an expansionI Expect You To Die 2 picks straight up where the original left off, bringing with it fantastically designed puzzles, that take a step up from the first game. Add to these all the nice little details they have put into the overall presentation of the game with the outstanding voice work, and it really does feel like the team have made improvements in every area. However, the game might feel short and more like an expansion to some, so a few more chapters would not have gone a miss. Even taking this into account, if you want an excellent and well polished escape room game in VR, adding I Expect You To Die 2 to your collection is not something you will regret.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Just as good if not better than the first. Much more theatrical than the first and well done. My only complaint is it's relatively short aside from trying to get all the speed run and additional achievements. It'd be nice if there was a hard mode for elevated difficulty. Otherwise the game is fantastic as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun experience, but I see very little replay value. Overall the game shouldn't take more than 2 hours to play though. I did find some of the puzzles rather confusing as far as their solutions go. The plane level being a major thorn in my side. _childDocuments_.review: This game just doesn't compare to the first one. The puzzles are easier, the traps are less deadly, even the deaths feel less realistic (they removed coughing audio when you die to gas). There was way too much exposition in the puzzles, which made speedruns boring. All of this is forgivable, but my main gripe with this game is that I never once felt like an actual spy. I felt like a guy doing vaguely related escape rooms. You can't smoke cigars until the last level, and you don't get a gun ever. Compared to the first game, this is a massive step down. Even based off the first level of both, the first game is still harder and much more interesting. To beat the first level in IEYTD1 you must: find the car key, start the car, dodge the laser, defuse the bomb, roll down the window, grab the screwdriver, roll the window back up so you don't die to poison gas, open the front panel, activate the cannon, load and fire said cannon, then drive the car off the back of a plane. To beat the first level in IEYTD2 you must: , then , then , then grab the , , and then "take care of" 4 people. Only at two points in this process are you in any actual danger, and even then it happens so slowly you have ample time to avoid it. Worst part is you can deal with those 4 guys nonviolently with the exception of one, who you must shoot (with a crossbow, since you don't get a gun). Why was the ability to go fully nonviolent removed from this game? Why was the ability to go fully violent removed as well? Let me do both, devs.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10It's a good game and a worthy addition to the series, but I've got a few petty gripes for its execution.Too many of the combination-lock-style puzzles are easy to brute-force. The locker code in the beginning of the game, the wine cellar towards the middle, The radio during the train section for the last game, the breakers during the plane section of this game. These puzzles all have one thing in common:I solved all of them before I knew where to find the answer.Granted, you can brute-force any puzzle in most games if you're determined enough, but codelocks in base three and binary lighting codes? That's baby's first brute-force.Besides that, this whole game felt pretty anemic compared to the original, and I've got to wonder if it's because after a while you kind of 'get it' when it comes to IEYTD games. And puzzles that fail to innovate or improve upon the established formula are pretty easy to breeze past once all the pieces are in play.I actually found one of the easter egg souveniers in the game because the easter egg was (to my mind) more obvious than the intended path. :/I don't regret my purchase though. Great game all-around.

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 2 is the second game in a VR escape room, puzzle game with an action twist. In the game you play as spy who is on a mission to defeat the evil, Dr. Zor. The game is played seated, and contains 6 levels, a speedrun challenge, and secret achievements for each level.The game has 6 extremely well designed levels, each with their own piece of the story, and different puzzels that can be very difficult to figure out. In each level you need help stop one of Zor's plans, without dying to the many traps. Each of the 6 levels this game offers include a unique setting, unique mechanics, and unique achievements. These achievements always include a speed run, and a bunch of secret ones which range from picking up hidden items, to beating the levels in a completely different way. The speedruns are very cool, as a level that takes 15 minutes the first couple times, could have a speedrun of 2 minutes. This is because some items have multiple uses, and some puzzles have multiple ways to complete them. The games story is pretty good and has a very cool antagonist, John Juniper who is a theatre actor turned evil.The game also includes a very cool and well done opening credits and an original song. It includes a lot of random stuff that you can mess around with during the levels, and sometimes some funny things too. As for the game play hours, it all depends on how good you are at puzzle games, and how much time you're willing to put into achievements. I personally put a good amount of hours into this, but still had to look some up, as I had tried for an hour previously. You might want to wait for a sale, but I think the game is fairly priced as it is the best VR puzzle game on the market in my opinion. I would definitely recommend this game if it sounds appealing to you, I had a lot of fun playing it and can't wait for the next game.Hopefully this helped! :)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty disappointing follow up to the excellent IEYTD1.* There are a lot more "HA, GOTCHA!!" traps than the first game. Sure, infinite retries, but it's really immersion breaking sometimes. For example, somewhere in the game, a glass container rolls out of a chute, breaks on the ground, and shatters causing a fire. Catching it breaks it. You have no way to deal with that trap until later in that stage. It feels like a really cheap way to force a retry.* The danger stakes have raised in some missions, but it's illusionary. Trying hard not to spoil, there's a part where there's "something coming" to blow you up but you have so much time to deal with its countermeasures that it doesn't really feel like a real threat.* In that same stage, there's a kind of cloned version of "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes." That's a fun game, but here the descriptions you get are so incredibly easy, and the actual manipulations you have to do never change. So, really, it turns into whether you can remember or not. It's more fun than trying to find random bits of paper with instructions on them, sure, but the implementation was so lazy on this.* From the description: "Go undercover using disguises to figure out exactly what Zoraxis is up to." No, not really. You still don't really interact directly with people (which is fine), but whether you wear a hat or not doesn't really change up anything, it's really only there for jokes.* Some puzzles have multiple ways to solve them, but it's usually "use this thing" or "use this other thing". Anything with a multi-stage solution is going to be the only way to solve things, period. With the extra experience of the team I was kind of hoping for something a little less spoon-fed.* The voice casting for the villain is probably the worst casting I've ever heard for any kind of game. Such a whiny hipster voice for a character that should have been smooth and sophisticated, considering who he is and what he's up to. It's really out of place for the other voices which are mostly campy with some fake accents and are really fun. Juniper is not fun at all.I really hope Schell Games does better next time.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think the second game would be so much better than the first. The first game was a 9/10, but now that I've played this game, It's changed my whole perspective on VR puzzle games and puzzle games in general. The intro is better, the visuals are better, the story is better, the puzzles are more fun, the environments are more interesting, the puzzles are more consistent, and somehow it takes up even less space than the first game. The first game lacked an actual story for the most part, but this one has multiple named antagonists, and an actual face-to-face encounter with one of them. The only complaint I could possibly have, is that the puzzles were too easy. They didn't have quite the same difficulty or complexity as the first game, so you didn't feel as clever as you did in the first game. Can't wait for the third game!

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first I Expect You to Die, you will also like this one. I bought the bundle. The first time I loaded I Expect You to Die 2 I got a message saying that my headset was not supported. I have an HP G2 Reverb. When Steam wouldn't give me a refund, I tried launching the game from Steam and it worked with no issues.I enjoyed both games, but I felt this one was better thanks to a cohesive story. Each mission plays off the previous mission, with the character Juniper appearing in each. Like the first title, there is no motion. All of your puzzle-solving is done from a sitting position.I wouldn't say that the puzzles are easy, but they're also not so difficult that they are unsolvable. The whole idea behind this series is that each puzzle has about seven to eight steps. You're not going to figure out each step the first time through. Instead, like in the Tom Cruise movie, you learn from your mistakes and get better each time.Since you are in a sitting position, the answer to every puzzle is in your field of vision. I solved every puzzle without resorting to going online, which leads me to another topic – hints. I have to say that I am conflicted on this issue. On the one hand, I think every game should have a progressive hint feature that doesn't give you the answer but leads you in the right direction. One game that has done this very well is the game The Room VR. This game, however, would not be a good candidate for progressive hints. Hints would take away from the satisfaction you get from solving the puzzles.As for graphics and sound, both are well done but a little on the cartoonish side. One thing I noticed with this version was that there seemed to be a lot of red herrings. More than a couple of times I ended up spending too much time on items that didn't help me in solving a puzzle. The one puzzle that took me the longest was the wine cellar puzzle. It took me three tries to get this one. I will say that once I figured it out, I raised my arms in a victory celebration, which probably looked ridiculous.This version seemed to have one or two fewer puzzles to solve than the first one, which is not a bad thing. I know when I solved the last puzzle I was surprised to see the end credits.

_childDocuments_.review: My review for this will be very similar to IEYTD 1, as most of the gameplay elements carry over to this one.As with the first game, this is a very creative way to handle Escape Room type VR games. Rather than just throwing you into a puzzle to solve, you actually become part of the story line and your goal isn't always to escape.The developers keep putting a lot of love into this game and it shows, all the tiny details and carefully thought out interactions with the world and its objects. The music, the voice acting, and the classy intros. They get the settings correct and it keeps things immersive even though it's a sit-down VR game. The first game, after completing it, allowed the player to go through developer commentary for each level. However it appears to be absent in this game, unless I've missed it?Controller sensitivity appears to have been fixed in this game, I no longer had issues releasing objects or pressing the wrong buttons. Other than that it was bug free for my playthrough. Also, Wil Wheaton.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first game, and have been enjoying this game as well now!There is one major issue however, and that controllers with thumbstcks will have major issues with the telekinesis system ingame. I had this issue at one point and so left a negative review, but the devs had responded with the fix, adding the launch option -vrhands oculus, to switch to the oculus hands which the game does have bindings for. This made the game playable.Overall, the game is very fun and a true sequel to the original: keeping the good elements from the original and innovating and expanding on what made the game fun. Level design is very clever, although puzzles can be slightly unclear on occasion. The game now has a proper villain, who is very fun and brings something new to the game. The devs also seem very communicative, so don't hesitate to speak up if you need help!One critisism to make though is that the game is short if you are not going for all achivements and collectables in the game.Overall, the game is definitely one of the best games for vr right now, but slightly pricey for the game legth. If you see this on sale though, definitely pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting a long game out of this or the first game for that matter, you're probably not going to find it. However I Expect You to Die 2 manages to step up its predecessor in a lot of ways including giving you a foil in the form of John Juniper which makes it more entertaining to manage to get a leg up on him and Zoraxis. If you don't mind the price tag, I can definitely recommend this to fans of the first game and fans of escape room games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: ++ Unlike a lot of VR games out there, IEYTD 2 is polished beyond a merely functional experience to the point of artistry. It's not especially complex, but it has a clear and immersive identity that balances aesthetic and function. Schell Games continues to be one of the good ones out there.++ Capital 'Gee' Good voice acting+ It's nice to have a role for Will Wheaton where he doesn't actually have to do any acting and he can just cut loose and be his true self.+ I'd call it family friendly+ Runs well with even lower end VR GPUs (RX480 to RX 6600)+ Works with even the Oculus Rift CV1 no problem.+ A fair enough deal even at full price ($24.99 USD at the moment).+ Has some replay-ability with hidden objects and speed runs+ An experience worth sharing.~/- Not an especially long experience, but that is somewhat reflected in the price point.- I swear they used to have a free demo, but they don't seem to now. I feel having demos should be the industry standard for VR titles whenever possible.= One of the best experiences in VR right now, and the standard a lot of other VR games should aspire to. But it's like a pleasant slice of what I'd imagine a "full length" AAA VR game would look like; if you were polite you'd say you were satisfied, but really a little bit more would be nice. To that end I think the first game offers a better value proposition in some ways at this time, and I might recommend you start there, especially if you can catch a sale. But if you liked the first game, this one is a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterclass on how to put together a great VR title. It's funny, engaging, detailed, immersive, and incredibly intuitive in a way most VR games aren't. It's also an incredible step up from the first, which is very impressive considering the quality and replayability of it. Overall, this game is criminally underrated and a definite must-buy for anyone with a VR headset.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: (Warning VERY minor spoilers for two levels of the game) This is one of my favorite VR games I have played. The game is incredibly witty and charming. I was afraid i wasn't going to like it a much as the first game but It was even better than the first. (And the first one was amazing.) The puzzles were the right amount of challenge. They didn't feel impossible but also didn't feel brain dead easy. the game requires outside of the box thinking mixed with escape room like puzzles. Unfortunately there is not a whole lot of replay value in the game. sure there is achievement but I didn't really care about those all to much. I loved levels like the first one where you got to play a the stage hand for a show. That one was a little less linear and had some replay value to it because you could do many different things in the level. same with the level in the wine cellar. I wish more levels had this replay value. The game could also get annoying when you would get to the end of  the level, then not know what to do, die, and then have to restart, and then do everything you just did all over again. I get is the name of the game but I wish there was an option to start a little before you died so you don't have to replay parts you just did. The levels aren't to long so its not a horrible problem. Those are just a few complaints I have and honestly none of them got in the way of my enjoyment of the game. I love creating my own spy character in my head and I very much enjoyed having the Handler character chiming in. Solid game and I highly recommend especially if you like puzzles or escape rooms. But i think this game can also be appealing even if you don't.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended.This game has a handful of spy missions where you can accomplish everything from your seat. It was clearly designed with the constraints of VR in mind.Most of the gameplay is in a scavenger hunt style, but that didn't hurt the enjoyment.I especially enjoyed the HQ area between missions, where you can touch a lot of things in a small environment around you
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal sequel to a phenomenal puzzle game. If you liked the first you'll love the 2nd. I find the environments very immersive and pretty interactive, and you get to feel like a badass spy the whole time. The puzzles are just as creative and I find the narrative even more creative just around. This and IEYTD1 are must play VR games imo, and if you have any interest at all in puzzle or escape room style games you love it. Only issue with this game is it is a bit on the shorter side. Looking forward to more content though!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Having only played the first game knowing the solutions beforehand (Thanks, YouTube), I was over the moon when they announced a sequel. Let's just say it was worth the wait. Going in blind was a completely different experience, having to figure out the puzzles through trial and error. I will say that this game is much more forgiving than its predecessor, but it was still challenging. The intro music slaps as per usual of Schell, the voices are amazingly done (Especially the antagonist), and the little side missions to get collectables were still fun to figure out. I definitely think this was the better of the two, but you should still play the first to get a handle on the story before moving to this one.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 2 follows pretty well the same formula as the first game, with a few changes or improvements depending on your own preferences.The game's scope is a little grander, with better-looking graphics, and overall better production value. The levels feel less like escape rooms and more like real environments, there's a more cohesive story present, and more voice acting to compliment it. I found the puzzles took a little more brain power to work out, which made my first playthrough last a little longer than in the first game, but with the new larger levels and more complex puzzles took away my drive to go for 100% completion. Overall, the game takes itself about 5% more seriously, with a little lean away from comedy and towards drama, while still keeping the same tongue in cheek attitude towards classic spy tropes.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the first game in a few ways. Same core premise, but new puzzles, more interaction, and just more of the fun.I was able to 100% it (collectibles, easter eggs, and speedruns) in under 6 hours. If you're just looking for story, you should be able to do it in half that.A well polished VR game that is not always easy to find these days.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game.  I would recommend the first one over this sequel to anyone who hasn't played it yet; this is basically another six levels of that same game, and it follows the story set up from the original.  They did nothing to change the formula; which is fine, it still works, and both games are quite short.  If you wanted more of the first game, as I did, this is exactly that.To anyone not familiar with the first one, this is basically a collection of VR escape rooms.  They are well-designed and most problems have several potential solutions, all of which are reasonably intuitive.  You are likely to get stuck a few times but not for more than a few minutes if you're persistent.The game is unlikely to make you motion sick and is appropriate for everyone from hardcore gamers to casual players to children.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Like part one, their unique "telekinesis" game mechanic is superb. I thought other devs would take heed and implement similar ideas into their games but that hasn't happened. Only HL:Alyx's gravity gloves. People in VR don't want to bend over and fiddle with odd drawer physics and awkward item pickups clipping through your actual floor where you can't pick them up. That said the game is a continuation of part one. An utter delight to play and be in this world. Although I haven't completed it yet, I suspect a game that is shorter than expected too as all VR titles are with exceptions. Still love it. These VR devs who have been there since the beginning get it.I hope this is released on PS5VR and makes big bucks, this studio deserves it. Hey folks their other game Until You Fall is great too, check it out.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely delivered. I didn't think that this would be better than the first, but wow I was wrong. No subtitles is a bit disappointing, but it may come in a future update. Every single level was just epic. I especially liked the part in level 2 where you're being guided on what to do to fix the defence systems. The opening song is just perfect. No other way to describe it. Either way, this game is golden.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A fun creative escape room game. Mostly keeping the same formula from the original. Highly recommend for escape room/puzzle game fans and fans of the original. As in the name of the game you will eventually die, causing you to restart that level from the beginning. Which actually isn’t much of a hinderance because it never takes more than a few minutes (if that) to solve the puzzles again to get yourself back in the same situation just before you had died previously.   Once you solve a level the mystery is over so there isn’t much of a reason to replay a level other than for a speed run, but that is the nature of this type of game and not a reason to not grab this game if you are into escape rooms. The only negative I will give to this game is that PC users don’t have any graphical options to increase resolution (I couldn’t find it if there is one). The game does not look bad by any means but I couldn’t help shake the feeling that the graphics are being held back a bit so the game can run on less powerful hardware.  When I finally completed all the levels I was left wanting more levels to play. Definitely looking forward to any dlc and another sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same type of sequel. But it's fine since I Expect You To Die is one of the best VR puzzles/escape rooms.All the strength of the original are here too: good pacing, interesting and varied puzzles with possible alternative solutions, good sense of humor and one of the best opening credits out there. Plus now we have a story and characters to give more context to the puzzles and environments.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Even better than the first. I like that they took the working formula and didn't add anything annoying, just added more awesome unique levels, and a great villain that pulled the plot together that the first game was missing. This and the first one are some of my all time favorite games, and I really hope they make another game or some dlc for this one.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game that IMO is well worth the full price. If you haven't played the first it's an puzzle/escape room type game that's half James Bond, half Austin Powers. I'd suggest playing the first game before this, but it's not strictly necessary.Pros:- I didn't think it's possible, but the intro cutscene for this game is even better than the first- Great level variety- Great voice acting- Great music & graphics- I loved some of the more random things you can do just for fun. Lots of stuff to play with and mischief to get up to.- Plenty of "souvenirs" to find- The speedrun times are challenging without being frustratingCons:Honestly I can't really think of any. I didn't want it to end,  but it did anyway.Verdict: 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Just recently 100% this game and i have to say, it's a must pick up for anyone with a vr headset.The combination of style, charm and amazing level design makes for such an amazing experience.The only gripe I have with this great game is that its only 6/7 hours long, 2 or 3 if you don't grab bits and bobs around the place which in most cases make a game hard to recommend but the masterclass attention to detail this game has from start to finish makes the game worth full price.Highly recommend this lovely game, hoping for another game :)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: this game is incredibly fun and just an amazing experience with some well crafted challenges and masterpiece level design, i would recomend playing i expect you to die (1) before. if you want a view of how good this game truly is just watch the first scene on youtube of the opening creditsi also expect you to play this game
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 2 has an refined story and a stronger cast of characters. Most of the puzzles feel more logical if harder than the first IEYTD. The only criticism I have is that the first game had more variety of exotic locations; but I am more invested in the story now and I am excited to see what I Expect You To Die 3 brings to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Straight to this one as I hadn't played the first but very enjoyable. At first it's frustrating when you're sent back to the start of the level when you die, but you quickly realise it's pretty quick to get back to the same point to try again. Good voice acting, good puzzles and good VR controls. My only complaint is the length of the game which is quite short - this'd be OK if it was a game you'd go back to again and again but this isn't this type of game. Definitely worth it if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun. The puzzles are challenging, but not too far to where they're obtuse. The storyline is interesting, with a fun twist partway through. The replay value is incredible. The base game is pretty short; Just a standard "get through the levels in ~30 minutes each", but the challenges and collectibles provided are enough to keep you going for hours upon hours.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: It's great fun, right from the opening credits and the puzzles are always logical. I did cheat two or three times when I was stuck but the solutions made sense. I don't like resorting to guides but these games are especially annoying when you're stuck as you have to do all the previous steps every time just to die at the same point. It's all over much too quickly, I got about 5 hours out of it.
