I recomend this to all spy fans as a JB fan!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10This game might as well be just an expansion pack of the first game. No new mechanics, no new gimmicks, just you, your skills, and your .If you enjoyed the first game, you will enjoy this game without a doubt.I just wish it were longer, but I am very satisfied.All of the puzzles are solvable, or at least make sense. No hidden tricks required.  Don't spoil yourself, this is a game best explored blind!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: It can be hard to tell whether a VR game is worth it, given that there are many where the main selling point is that the experience is in VR.  I Expect You To Die is not one of those titles.Both the first and second entries are fully fleshed out games that host wonderfully executed puzzle/escape room games.  The puzzles are challenging but not to a point where they are frustrating.  The spy theme works really well in both titles but the story flows more organically in the second entry.The games offers lots of interactive items to play around with immerse you as a super spy, all which make it a robust experience.Both games have a limited amount of levels with 6 in each one.  However, each level is unique and offers lots of Easter Eggs which increase the replay value.If you own a VR set and are looking for a new and fleshed out experience, I recommend getting it, even at full price. I'll be looking forward to what more Schell Games has to offer with I Expect You To Die.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't any other way to describe this game than amazing. The missions and puzzles are varied and satisfying to complete, the soundtrack is spot on, and the story ties it all together, although it is a bit short. The only caveat I have to say is the game's length. I just wish there was more things to do.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin with this masterpiece? IEYTD2 is a true sequel to its original, and much like it, is insanely fun. I only wish there were more levels - much like the predecessor, it leaves you wanting more after.The puzzles are expertly crafted and there is more than one way to do most things. And even after you've beaten the game, I recommend going back and attempting to get every single achievement - beating all speedruns and collecting all trophies. I was only able to put this game down after I was sure I had done everything. Pros:- Literally everythingCons:- Kind of short, despite its replay valueBonus points for including Lisbon! Also - the opening theme is a banger
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It is definitely how a sequel to game should be done. It really improved on it's missions and how to go through them. It feels like there is a good amount of experimentation and will not always lead to instant death. The story, voice acting, and music are also really well done. If you like the first game you will definitely like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A truly great successor to the first game. More of the same fun puzzles and over the top spy missions.The theme song/intro sequence rivals the first, and had me in pure happiness geeking out over it.I hope more people find this game because it's truly a gem, and I can't wait for updates.As someone using a Quest 2, the controls felt a whole lot more accessible for the telekinesis as compared to the first, (and not to mention, the speedrun achievements easier.).
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the first game you'll enjoy this one, but in its current state I feel I should have waited to buy it on sale.PROS:More of the same from the first gamemore of an overarching story Interesting and fun gameplaybigger levelsCONS:more arcade-like (no cigars no guns)a little short for the moneyreplay value is less than the first game (can't really just drop a friend in on a random level)bigger levelsVERY SHORT
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Still a fun game, though it felt like it's a step down from the first one, both in terms of graphics and, more importantly, puzzle complexity and size. Everything felt smaller, more compact, less detailed and overall easier.I can't say I didn't enjoy it though, the overall feel and most of the puzzles are still great fun. If you liked the first game, you shouldn't skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. "I Expect You To Die 2" is another great game in the "I Expect You To Die" franchise. This game is basically like the first one, in both quality and puzzle difficulty. I personally think that the sequel is a more difficult game, but that depends on personal opinion. The "I Expect You To Die" games are the perfect and simple Vr games (simple as in: Not any motion sickness, considering you are sitting the same spot all time), but even though it's simple, it's very high quality.This game definately deserves a perfect score of 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, just like I enjoyed the first, that is overall I enjoyed itLike many Vr games, this suffers from not enough content. Outside of the initial solution where everything is new, and deaths happen frequently, for me at least, the levels start to feel small, which may be purposfull with the speedrun achievements, but it did leave me wanting for content at the end of everything.The scale of the van compared to the office made the game feel a little cheaper, but I liked that all of the items taken from levels were within reach even without the TK. The story was nice, and I liked the more visible villains and enemy's but like the first I really wish that it was longer than it was. So, overall, I liked the game, but I really want whatever the devs work on next to be a larger project with more to chew on after initial completion.Update, I nominated this as best Vr game of 2021
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the story, it took me about 3.4 hours. im going to go back for all achievements later, however i decided that i want to write my review for anyone curious about my experienceI just want to say, the amazing intro alone was one of my favorite parts. It actually had me smiling with excitement. It was a perfect start to the game.The levels arent easy. I found myself dying and replaying the levels over and over to try and figure out how to beat it. I actually got stuck for like 20 mins trying to beat a level only to realize the answer was right under my nose. However the levels arent so hard that you want to give up, eventually you will figure it out.My only negatives about this game so far is the $25 price tag, and how short the story is. I think that a fair price for this game is $15. (yes devs i know you and your team worked really hard for this game and it shows). But i also think that for the length of the story (only 6 levels) the price should be reduced. or just buy the game when its on sale which i was too impatient for. But keep in mind that the story isnt the only way to play it. Like going back and getting all achievements, or trying to get the fastest time on a level.anyways its a good game and i recommend putting it on your wishlist to get notifications for when it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!  Only downside to this is it only took me 2.7 hours to beat.  However, the atmosphere, music, voice acting, and puzzle solving make this definitely worth the purchase!  I can definitely see myself replaying this to get all achievements and feel like a psychic, but I'm also very excited for the next game in the series!  9/10 for short length but extraordinary quality in gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Once again we need to save the worldthis game really delivered a fresh escape room experience Lets start the with the positives.The missions are well designed just like the first game.narrative is excellent as well.The performance is goodCons.sometimes the items would bug out.Just like the first game it provides a fun experience which is rarely the case when sitting down.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The vibe of the game is great, I love the ambiance, the characters, the story and the soundtrack. The artistic design is great, and the puzzles are quite great as well (very different from the classical "find numbers and type them" of other escape-room-like VR games).However, I'm disappointed on a few points:- The game can be completed in 2 to 3 hours. That's shorter than the first game, even if new missions are supposed to come.- The last two missions are VERY SHORT (when you're in the set with JJ, and the grand finale with the elevator). While most of the early missions took me at least 25-30min to figure out, the last two were done in 10min each. It felt kind of rushed to release, and feels like parts were cut because of time constraints on the developer's end (or loss of interest). That's a bummer.- Still no translations, nor at least English subtitles. While I'm very fluent in English, my girlfriend is not, and I've had to do live translations for her, otherwise she wouldn't have been able to play the game at all, as some very important intel is delivered through voice exclusively. Even just English subtitles at the bottom of the view would've made it possible for her to play the game by herself.If you can live with that and assume that 3 hours is worth 20 bucks, then you should definitely buy this game, and I'll recommend it if you're fluent enough in English. If not, maybe wait for a sale, or wait until they actually add more missions and subtitles. I guess so far, it's a hidden "early access" game.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I love this and the original.  Lots of replay value when looking for souvenirs and alternate ways to solve the puzzles.  Love all the objects that can be interacted with. Like Job Simulator, but you have a real job, and it's being a Super Spy!  Love the voice acting, Wil Wheaton is on point, and so is Jared Mason as the Support Agent.  Overall fun without being too frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Another great instalment in the I Expect You to Die series. This games was a bit longer than the first, levels in the same vein as the first and just as enjoyable with a perfect level of difficulty. The story in this game is also much better than the previous and actually has you invested in the events. Can't wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Still great, but not as good as the original. Dont get me wrong, this game still absolutely drips in sauce; but now that the incredible originality of the first game has faded its just not the same. This is like an 8/10 game where the first one was a 10/10. The puzzles dont feel more difficult but they do feel more "fiddly" for some reason. Its easier to accidentally kill yourself a lot of the time in this game when compared to the first, not because you didnt know the threat was there, but because the fiddly nature of VR makes you fail a precise movement and you die. The story of this game is more relevant and just overall better than the first game, and I hear if you're using Oculus this game performs better than the first but on Vive both games perform well. I'd recommend trying the first game before trying this one though, I think overall the first game was better.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The VR market may be a bit slim pickings right now...however...I can assure you this is a solid title for anyone that likes goofy humor and escape room type puzzles. If you've played the first I Expect You To Die, this'll be easy. More of the same with better visuals and more intricate (but not too complex) puzzles. Pros: The visuals are stylized, but not in an overly cartoony way. Not that it's a bad thing. But visually, there's some pretty sweet textures for me to gawk at in VR. More importantly, there's lots of little details from rain on a window to the little bits and nods of humor in the game that you can appreciate if you're exploring your surroundings. The puzzles are fairly simple, but occasionally head scratching. Balanced. As all things should be... Anyhow, there's some moments where you're pretty much just blitzing through the easy parts and the narrator is catching up to you and others you're sitting there trying to piece it all together. This lead to a solid 5 hours of gametime for a single playthrough. There are speedrunning opportunities here and multiple solutions to puzzles, but ultimately, this is roughly where your playtime will sit. Music is pretty swanky though. ConsI think there are a couple of little tidbits that I struggled with for puzzles just because I tried to do things in an unconventional way. So I'd get stuck for awhile and once I found the solution I'd think "huh...why would I think to do that?" I'm sure most people stumble upon this, but there's logical reasons to not do it too. The playtime to cost ratio is maybe a wee bit high, however I felt like it's worth it's price in quality. I've paid $60 for 8 hr games like Uncharted and love them dearly because the experience and quality was worth it. At the end of the day, this game made me laugh and have several "Ah hah!" moments that were fun.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so I came into this with high expectations, Mainly because I played the original on the PSVR. This game is incredible. Sadly its a bit short if you have watched others play it. So quick Warning --- DO NOT WATCH TUTORIALS --- if you do it will harshly decrease your experience.But it was an amazing experience and I felt fully immersed!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: it's a great game. the first game felt more like a casual puzzle compared to this one. they increased the 'stress' factor a bit when trying to solve the puzzles by having more timers. and they also increased the difficulty a tad bit.gotta say the only thing i don't like is the length. 3 hours for $25 seems a bit steep to me. but to be fair, that is just to beat the game. not 100%. (i task i don't think i will be able to do, because the speed timers seem a bit tight to me. but the souvenir hunting will be fun.)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game and its predecessor are two of my absolute favorite VR experiences. Very well done. Feels like a slick AAA production. The only downside to it is that as I progress through the game I see the end in sight, and I don't want it to end!! I really hope there are additional levels in the future, or better yet, "I Expect You To Die 3, 4, 5 ... "
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: seeing this game had a sequel, i was pretty worried that it wouldn't be able to live up to my expectations. thankfully, 'i expect you to die 2' is a fantastic return to form on the original - and executed even better. normally, i'd dock a game for short playtime, but i enjoyed every second of IEYTD2 and found it well worth the price of admission. i'd say this is a must-play for anybody with a VR headset!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: GameplayI Expect You To Die 2 offers some of the best Virtual Reality experiences and game play you can find in 2021 at the moment. From Picking up a clipboard and blocking bolts from a crossbow and turning around and using them, to punching buttons to order food and cutting off the antagonists with a directors clapper board, I Expect You To Die 2 leaves little to be desired. Each mission has its own theme and nothing really feels repetitive or Overused. Within the missions are you challenged in different ways and you are very much rewarded for speed running and trying new things.Lock And Load, AgentComfort And Controls – Schell Games prioritizes comfort over everything else and it really shows. You don’t have to move much at all and all the movement is twisting and turning. This game is great for handicap people who cannot stand or otherwise. There is not much leaning at all and you do not burn a lot of energy vs games like Onward and Legendary Tales. Overall your comfort is their highest priority and saves you a lot of energy.Relax Agent, We Have Everything Under ControlLevel DesignAll 6 levels are easy to play and just as easy to memorize, even for those with terrible memory. Repetition is mastery and you will find yourself learning the levels quickly as you play around with things around the level and discover some very nice hidden scenes and sequences. You will just have to discover some of them for yourself! Final Thoughts I expect you to die 2 is a high quality, well developed game built on the Unity Engine and is very much worth any price you pay from full price to on sale. Even though I have not 100 percent the game by any means, it is well worth the experience for the first play though, and it will leave you wanting more, and I am hoping for some DLC, otherwise we might be waiting another 5 years for a third installment of I expect you to die. This game gets a 10/10 in my books and I highly recommend this to any age group and anyone!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the first game! As a Reverb G2 player, this game has the controls finally mapped to be working correctly, as opposed to the first where you had to "tug" an object towards you. The puzzles were fresh and different than the first, and had their own charm to them. A little more serious tone than the first, but only slightly. My only gripe is how short the game is, so I'd recommend buying when its on sale; but if you're a fan of the first and can't wait, then by all means, pull the trigger.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A solid and fun sequel. More of the same which is a good thing because it's such a good escape room game. Length is the same as the first game according to my playtime for both. The only disappointment is that the game isn't any longer. If you enjoyed the first game, you will enjoy this one. I will say I enjoyed the first one a bit more, but that doesn't mean this game isn't solid. I just felt as if the first one was slightly more creative. Still worth the play easily.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the previous game. Has full oculus controllers support, more intricate and detailed levels and puzzles. I still don't like the idea of replaying levels from the start though. There are a lot of collectibles, some are exclusive depending on the way you dispose of the enemies, but by the time you finish the level - you have tried and died so many times that you kinda don't want to replay the level again. Still, just as with the previous game - the main point is that it is fun, so it gets a pass.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely get it if you played and enjoyed the first one. This time around there's a continuous story as opposed to just being disjointed single levels, which was definitely a big plus. I also really enjoyed each of the levels and their items, mechanics, etc. The new opening sequence was very cool (that was a big highlight of the first one so I'm glad they made another). The game is definitely more of the best parts of the first one. That said, like the first one it's not terribly long. I'm sure I'll come back around to replay it, but as of writing I have 100%ed the game at 7 hours of playtime (and I spent an hour being too stupid to figure one thing out on the second level)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best VR franchises there is. Like the first game it's perfectly executed to be accessible to new VR players, non-gamers, escape-room lovers, etc, but also challenging and enjoyable for even heavy gamers.For £20 though it needs way more content. I would be happy with a 4 hour campaign, plus a bunch of additional escape rooms built by re-using assets, or even just Steam Workshop support so the community can provide this. But £20 for 4 hours of play is not great value.I recommend the game, but unless you're a huge fan of this series or just want to support the creators, I would buy on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what a sequal is suppose to be, an improvment on the first with new fresh ideas but not so much better so it over shadows the first one. The actual gameplay is decent and takes alot of attension to detail to find clues and other tips to help you. You get about 4 hours of gameplay if your an average vr player that doesnt play alot of puzzle games. So in conclusion 1. its a good vr puzzle game 2. it has new fresh levels compared to the first one 3. its well priced at 20 euros
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good.I was slightly let down compared to the first game.  It's better than the first game, but we've had 4 years of VR games and IEYTD was one of the first incredible games I played on the original Vive.  I was hoping this would be MUCH better, but I still enjoyed the game.Opening credits scene still top notch.  You got Wil Wheaton (I guess he sings??).  Puzzles were complex enough, some a little too easy, nothing as hard as the submarine level in the first game.  I found myself breezing through most of each puzzle and getting *stuck* for 30-40 minutes on something.  Whole game took me about 5.5 hours according to steam, but I did replay a few levels to try and get the souvenirs.  The souvenirs also need better hints because I eventually stopped trying..Story is vastly improved from the first game.  WW does a good job the whole way through.I thought the environments/settings could be better.  I LOVED the first zone so the next few were let downs.  It was super interactive and I felt like I was part of the "play".The game is still absolutely worth playing if you like puzzle games.  It's up to you if the short length is worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely enjoying the game so far my only issue with the game is that there is no audio adjustment so i have to go in the volume desktop settings to lower the game audio down sadly but i most appreciate that the 'agent' is pretty much in the sitting position so that you don't feel awkward sitting in vr compared to the first game that you were always standing pretty much so it felt strange  while now it feels strange standing up while in sitting in a vr chair. I also appreciate the levels giving you plenty of time to solve a 'time' sensitive objective as i sometimes misheard a line so i didn't press a button so they repeated themselves.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the first game through to the final free update, I was elated to see this game was coming out, and so soon! I couldn't help but blitz through the story, but I enjoyed every single devilishly dangerous puzzle. It breathes fresh life into an already incredible tale with puzzles and game play just as clean and polished as before, the entire game is a spectacle and a rollercoaster everyone should have the chance to partake in!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I Expect You To Die 2, is a challenging escape room VR experience. You become an elite super-spy who is ready for espionage, explosives, and gadgets galore. I see no faults in this game aside from the occasional hair pulling but hey that's escape games for you. The graphics are fantastic, the challenges are challenging. Would recommend 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: As with the first game, this is a fantastic VR game, though also like it's predecessor it's a little short. Only BARELY this time though!The writing is taken up a notch this time, with fully voiced antagonists in every level and a more coherent story between levels over the first games more general "there is a bad guy" story. There was never a problem with the latter's story, but it's nice to see the narrative get a boost.The telepathic control scheme is back and utilised just as effectively. There's more you can play with in each level too! You're also able to interrupt and skip dialogue cues and events if you either figure it out fast enough or simply know what you're doing and speed through. It can actually get quite funny in certain levels.This fantastic sequel has only just came out and the first got some updates that added to it, so i look forward to seeing what might be in stpore for this espionage escapade in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: You find yourself trapped on a murder-plane 40,000 feet in the air. The service cart delivers you a delicious chocolate cake. Knowing better than to eat the obviously poison dessert you instead grab the silver platter and use it to deflect a laser beam suddenly aimed at your face. With expert precision you maneuver the reflected beam to destroy the other traps in the cabin.You lean back with a satisfied look on your face and click open your lighter to enjoy a celebratory cigar. It explodes. You die. You should have expected that.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you are new to VR, this series is a must have. With intuitive gameplay that's easy to learn and fun to experiment in, this game and it's predecessor are excellent introduction to the medium and will leave you hungry for more.I Expect You To Die 2 absolutely delivers on it's promise of more great, flexible puzzles and improves upon many aspects from the original (My favorite addition? Multiple save files). The hidden collectibles make you feel smart for figuring out a secret interaction, and the speedrun achievements feel difficult but never out of your reach. At the time of writing, I have only played for a short amount of time, and this is my feelings directly after finishing the game. However, I feel these thoughts will not be changing in the near future.The soundtrack this time around is a direct improvement. The dynamic songs that shift in intensity as the level progresses really make you feel like you're in a James Bond movie, especially in the second stage. The opening for this game is a stunning performance by my favorite character in the game's voice actor, wonderfully setting the tone for the rest of the game. The first game's opening was a wonderful experience as a new VR user, and now, even with years using VR actively, this intro surpasses it in every way.The introduction of actual characters in view, depicted as silhouettes with white eyes, adds a lot more tension. The only "on-screen" character in the original was never even given that much, so it gave this game a fresh identity and improved the feeling of being in enemy territory substantially. The writing this time around is very good as well, with some very entertaining characters that are that much more compelling than in the original game. This next section will have spoilers in it, so if the tag fails, this is your warning. The antagonist of this game,  they are much more fleshed out and fun to challenge than Zoraxis plans were in my opinion. Hopefully the next continuation of the story gives some love towards the Fabricator as well. Overall, IETD2 is a sequel that lives up to, and surpasses, the original in every way. Bravo, Schell Games, for outdoing yourselves once again, and I will absolutely be ready for what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first game and thought it was an absolute masterpiece, and when I heard a second one was releasing I bought it as soon as I could. Let me tell you, this game was worth every single penny, and the story was also really cool. The puzzles were challenging and took me a while to get, but they weren't so difficult that I had to look up a walk through. Overall I give this game a 12/10.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: "I epxect you to DIE 2" dosen't really offer something new in terms of VR expirience as it was with first part, but game is astonishing. All levels are great builded, they are interesting and give a challenge, also replaying is much better now. Highly recommend to anyone who loves puzzles.P.S. The Intro is just piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this, if you played the first game, it really is just more of that (which is a good thing). Same kinda early VR wacky humor feeling. Puzzles weren't too hard, they were reasonable. The couple times I felt the need to pull up a guide were usually cause I had missed something (like sending something up on a dumbwaiter and getting sent back a key that I hadn't seen). So the difficulty is reasonable, but you'll have to think outside the box a little bit. If you enjoyed the first game, totally pick this up. You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The price for this game is borderline too much, but the extra secrets per level add replay-ability that it sorely needs. The game is great, the humor on point, the music is catchy, and the villain is great. The levels are not too hard that you need a guide, but hard enough that you will not get it first try. All the levels are unique and fun, making for no "bad" levels.There are 6 levels in total, which is why I think it is somewhat hard to justify the $25 price tag, but the levels are so good that it nudges my review to a positive.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: More of the same and this could basically be an IEYTD1 DLC-pack except for a couple of tweaks to the controls.That isn’t a bad thing though because the first game is still on my top-5 list of favorite VR games!For the price of 20€ it’s a bit thin when it comes to content with me playing through the game in about 3 hours (and NO, I will not call doing a second playthrough to find all hidden items additional “content”) but I will still recommend this title to anyone who enjoys puzzle games…Another great thing about this game is the fact that it’s designed for seated play and that makes it a perfect game to start with if you are new to VR since you are less likely to get motion sickness…I hope they will keep the DLC coming for this title!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The game was much easier than the first one, but that didnt make the game any less fun, honestly its one of the most fascinating puzzle games out there, I got the game also in quest shop so I just bough and finished game from steam to show it on my library, but I would suggest you to buy it if you are interested in puzzling games, I suggest this game!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: A great addition to the "I Expect You To Die" series, and proof positive that Schell Games is still top of the VR Escape Room/Puzzle game.  Wil Wheaton steals the show in this game.I do miss some of the banter dialogue that was in the first game when finding souvenirs, and the game sticking to a single story thread almost seemed limiting at times compared to the more episodic nature of the first game.  However, there's no question that this is a fantastic entry into the series, and should not be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially on the fence due to the price tag but this turned out to be one of the best story-puzzle games I've played since Lone Echo and IEYTD 1. Awe inspiring cinematics and fabulous story. The opening credits alone deserves to give this GOTY. The voice acting makes you feel like you ARE the agent and the music is good enough to listen to on its own. Puzzles are challenging enough that you struggle but doable even by poor puzzle solvers with enough effort. Only 6 missions but they're one hell of a pack of missions, featuring just as much content in 6 jobs as the previous game did in (8? was it?). Similarly to the first game there's plenty of achievements and collectibles to go back for if you're into that. If you're on the questioning whether or not to buy this game, Do it. And, Good Luck Agent.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well made game. The art style is very pleasing and works really well. The puzzles are very fun and feel great to solve. And the story and voice acting is very nice.Some of the puzzles feel a bit short and the whole game can be completed quite quickly. But because its such an enjoyable experience, i really do recommend this game. By far the best VR game of the year!
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Having loved the first game, I couldn't wait for this one. It didn't disappoint. Completed the base game including some of the hidden challenges. Some of the puzzles had me scratching my head for a while, but even when you die, it's fun. Only one puzzle made me think "That wouldn't happen" but the rest made perfect sense. I can still go back and complete the other challenges if I choose, which would give me a few more hours as well. Money well spent.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously brilliant game. If you liked the first one, you'll love this one. If you don't know the first one, get the first one, play it, then get this one.Brilliant humor, brilliant story, brilliant puzzles. Bit longer than the first one I'd say, but it depends on your cleverness.Absolute must-have for every VR gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This is awesome!! I highly recomend you buying it the intro cutscene is awesome it ahs a james bond feel and it may not have many missions but it more than makes up for it because there is so much to do from speedruning to collecting all sovuniors to decorate your van with i am sad you cant burn documents and items to see if they have anything secret but its a step up from the last game this is how you make a great sequel
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just purest deepest love to gaming and VR.If you have a VR-Headset allready, you should have bought both parts yesterday.THIS is how you bring an atmosphere to life.For all those price-for-time-morons: No this game is not long, but that doesnt matter, your experience will balance that easily.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: This is much closer to a negative review than I was expecting. It's still positive on the whole, partially because I don't think my main issue will be a problem for any future levels, but I can't say I wasn't disappointed.So most of the game is great. The first game is one of my favorite VR games, and this is mostly more of that. The levels feel a bit less detailed than the first, but not to a level where it feels cheap. Controls are great, being seated the whole time makes locomotion a non-issue. The puzzles are good, and I only encountered a few bugs.But the main villain is FAR too annoying for a game where you have to replay levels to find secrets. It's fine to have a hateable villain, but have him hateable for the things he does, not his smug slimy voice. The fact that the game seems to act like he's some super likable person makes this even worse. I hoped he would just be in one level but he's there for almost the whole game, and I don't know if I can collect the secrets if I have to listen to him over and over.This sounds like a small thing, and if you can stand him, great, but it made me think about quitting every time he showed up in a scene.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: like the first game, it is somewhat short, but it is pretty fun to go back and get all the achievements, figuring out how to do all the missions in the speedrun time is a difficult puzzle itself. This and the first game are the best puzzle VR games I've played, and this one was even better in a lot of ways, like the story is much better for example. Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Its just like the first game, this is what seated VR games should be like, fun interaction and story, found this game a little easier than the first and I've completed it in a hour and 20 min so I'm a little disappointed its over already, will take me longer to find all  the secrets and do all the speed runs though, look forward to DLC or extra free levels, if not hope they make a number 3 as this kind of VR experience never gets old, only thing I wish to change about the game is more smoke from the cigar, not sure why but I loved puffing on the cigar in the first game, didn't feel like I could get a good drag on it in this one, maybe they where cheep knock off's lol.Played on the Rift S, Ryzen 7 3800X,  (AMD- MSI-TRIO) 6800XT, 32 DG Ram XMP 3200, Windows 10 64, no problems.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly atmospheric and entertaining game. The puzzle are fun but not overtly challenging. We love watching my son play this game while shouting out things he should do to solve the puzzle (to usually disastrous consequences). The intro song for this game is amazing and sets the right mood of tuxes and vodka martinis while secret organizations plot to take over the world with over the top sinister plots.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game fast enough to where I could refund it. I didn't do it on purpose but the story is quite short. But even though it is very short I don't think a game has to be long to be worth it. This game was an awesome experience and I will be keeping it so I can get all the collectibles. I hope they add some extra levels in the future like they did with the first game. I think this game is worth the money just be prepared to beat it fast.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: The first game was one of the best vr games i had ever played and this one was even better! This one had longer levels better puzzles and a plot that blew me out of this world. you can pick this up without playing the first game and there are a lot of references to it so weather you are a new player or old you will love this game
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the first one, you'll like this one too. If you haven't played the first one, I recommend buying it instead.This game adds a lot more story and cohesion between the levels compared to the first one. The story, humor, and puzzles were really fun. Wheaton's performance as Juniper is great, although I don't personally care for the star. The puzzles felt easier than the first one. I'm really bad at puzzle games and often need an external guide, but I only had to look for info once. I had a lot of fun playing IEYTD2, But to be honest, I just liked the levels from the first game more. The game has basic Index support, but it's not great. Sometimes (rarely) things you're grabbing fall, and there's no fingertracking at all (except for the thumb, and only tracks if you touch the joystick, not the other buttons.)
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game and worthy foll-up to IEYTD.  Total playtime to beat for me was about 3 hours but still plenty left to do.  If you enjoyed the original this will not disappoint.  I think the puzzles in this one might be slightly easier or perhaps the first game just trained me to think in a way that I could see the solutions.  This was a day one purchase for me based on the previous game and the fact that Schell Games did not sell out exclusivity to "the Company who must not be named".  Kudos, Schell Games!  I anxiously await the third installment.
_childDocuments_.name: I Expect You To Die 2: The Spy and the Liar

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. It is a great sequel to an already amazing game. If you have played the first one they you should without a doubt get the 2nd game. But I do hope we get more content to this game like we did with the first game as I was able to complete in one day of constant play. name: Teslapunk
detailed_description: 'Teslapunk' is a retro style arcade shoot-em-up. It plays in a Teslapunk (subgenre of Steampunk) universe where all enemies and spaceships run on high-voltage and occasionally explode into lightning. Each of the six levels features a different style, from technical drawings, to pure electricity to organic styles. The final battle features the mars boss himself, as a disco DJ throwing deadly music discs at the player. Teslapunk has bullet hell and puzzle shooter elements. You play through the levels, dodging bullets, and killing enemies with a laser or spread shot. As a special feature you have a 'Voltage Burst', a special laser mode which cancels all bullets and gives you a strong laser for a limited time. Canceling bullets raises the score multiplier and thus the score. The multiplier is also coupled to a rank system and therefore increases the difficulty dynamically. The game play is completely time scripted, developed with a special sequence editor. This results in the game play being perfectly orchestrated with the music giving the player a very enjoyable flow with the game. Boss patterns in sync with the music are another feature of the game. As a bonus game mode there is the survival mode in which you have to fight endless attack waves, collecting coins and power-ups on your way. The coins can be spent in the 'Teslamart' to upgrade the ship and buy extra items. The goal is to survive as long as possible. Furthermore Teslapunk features missions for the arcade mode and unlockable gallery picture. Story wise you play as Nikola Tesla to fight an invasion against an evil emperor from mars. The mars boss has its own TV channel at the side of the screen and comments your fight against the invasion. He will also be the end boss of the last level.

_childDocuments_.review: Doomsday Vault is a puzzle platforming adventure that's super chill, with a really nice soundtrack and lovely art style. The difficulty definitely ramps up over time, which is a nice and welcome challenge. I like that it isn't super hard from the start, so you're able to slowly learn and get used to the mechanics. The customization for the lil space suit is super cute; I have a bunch of fun updating it.I think this game is suitable for gamers of all ages; I can see kids having a good time with this as well, although it might get a bit challenging in the later stages.I highly recommend it! Disclaimer: I received the key for free from the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a criminally unnoticed game.Now, you'll see some complain about the controls. This is because it uses very oldschool isometric controls that not everyone will be able to wrap their heads around. If you aren't familiar with isometric controls, it's best to accept that there will be a barrier to entry. And due to it using isometric controls, it's naturally best played with a controller. If you've played Sabrewulf, Landstalker, Equinox, Head Over Heels, or the like though you'll be right at home. It certainly isn't a hardcore game though, so don't expect that, it's just that the unfamiliar controls provide a barrier to entry.It's a very chill exploration-puzzle game and it reminds me of the kinds of shareware games from ages past that would go criminally unseen. It only has sixteen reviews, so I suspect that this isn't a game that gets a lot of eyes on it. And that's a damn shame. The thing is? There's not a lot being done to really sell the game on its merits, I feel some indie devs are really bad at that.So what are this game's virtues? Well, it has a nifty art style for one but the screenshots don't really do it justice as it feels much better in motion, it's very smooth and fluid. The animations are really neat. It's enjoyable to just pick up and play if you have a short amount of time between other things, the suit customisation is fun, and it has a collectibles aspect (it's enjoyable to find everything).It has a good message about protecting the environment too, but I know that won't matter to most people. More's the pity, but it's important to accept the reality. I think the game is very enjoyable though despite whether you think that's important or not.It's definitely worth a few quid and I think in moments of downtime you'll find this a very cathartic game. It's one of those games that can grant a decent feeling of catharsis over a short period, and it's nice for that. It isn't especially challenging (aside from controls that one might be unfamiliar with), but it is enjoyable. It's difficult to quantify games like this beyond that.TL;DR: If you like cute aesthetics and collecting things? You'll likely dig Doomsday Vault. Just understand that it has isometric controls and it's important to have some familiarity with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Doomsday Vault

_childDocuments_.review: I started out feeling very positive about this game, because it's very cute, the music's alright, and I like the idea of preserving seeds from a doomed world and hopefully make it better. HOWEVER the reason I'm rating this negatively is because of one massive overhanging flaw: the controls. You control with either arrow keys or your mouse, and it's done so clunky that every game session ends with me rage quitting because I keep dying as the game demands precision platforming and maneuvering around lasers, but make it near-on impossible to do so with the controls it hands you. It's a simple and charming enough game, but the controls ensue that I cannot recommend it. At all.(not to mention the price is taking quite a lot of weewee. Get it on 50% or more sale)
_childDocuments_.name: Doomsday Vault

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cute puzzle game with adorable graphics and fun customization. Lots of achievements to fuel the completionists among us. That being said, as the other reviews mention, the controls for mouse and keyboard are....frustrating. If you take your time (along with a few deep breaths), you'll be fine. I would say despite the weird controls, the game is still worth it for a few hours of enjoyment. I would recommend it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Doomsday Vault

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun little game. The aesthetic is cute and calming, I love all the little animations and extras like how the antennas bounce when the robot jumps, and adorable box carrying toddle. It feels nice to see the plants I've saved grow up big and strong... so nice. Plus, the customization unlocks are a fun extra bonus. As a recovering perfectionist, it's fun to indulge in finding all of the hidden things, without really having to, to complete a level. But the chill vibes are a major selling part of this for me. There's no timer, no dangers, I don't have to pause to walk away for a sec, and the puzzles aren't difficult but merely just tricky enough for micro dopamine "ah! I get it," moments. Lovely.There's a few things other might have issues with, but I personally don't. Still, for fairness:- I bought this game on sale and feel like the short-ish playtime is well worth what I paid, but some might feel it's too short at full price.- The puzzles are not hard. Not too easy to not be any fun, but I haven't struggled more than a few moments on any of them yet, halfway through the game. Sometimes I like a break, so I'm good, but The Witness this is not. Good for kids, tho.- The keyboard controls are not great, but using a controller fixed that for me. If you don't have a controller and get easily frustrated (they don't even use WASD???) then maybe save yourself the trouble and pass. All in all, I'm half way through and I'm really happy with this game. I wanted a chill and cute little game about a robot collecting plants, and that's exactly what I got! Delightful.
_childDocuments_.name: Doomsday Vault

_childDocuments_.review: It's a well made fun, cute and easy puzzle game. It's exactly what I expected!Don't expect a hard game. There are puzzles and you do have to think for a short while every now and then, but generally they are very easy. It's a perfect game to relax with on the Steam Deck. As other reviewers has pointed out, it's also perfect for a younger audience. The game will last for about 2-3 hours.The controls are very special. I understand that there's some kind of style here, but I don't recognize it and the game would have been better with a normal movement style. The map is divided into a grid and your character can move forward, backward, right and left in this grid. I takes some getting used to and, in the second half of the game, there'll be puzzles that are built around this mechanic. If you don't play that long, I understand that the movement is a pure negative.

name: Nova Lands
detailed_description: TEST YOURSELF AGAINST CAPITALISM Check out Upcoming Cozy Survival Adventure About the Game If you were to mix Factorio, Forager, and Satisfactory, Nova Lands would be just that. Explore, build, and automate your base in this awesome, open-world 2D game! New planet, new home. Build your new base with all sorts of resources available to you, from basic rocks and wood to rare and unknown materials. Unlock new possibilities with every new building, maximize efficiency, and push deeper to other islands. As you progress through the game, you will be able to automate more and more things, freeing up more time to explore! Your little helper bots will be instrumental in helping you do that. The bots are the tipping point where your ingenuity will begin to shine. These little self-sufficient machines can form entire production chains and sustain your industry all on its own. They’re easy to set up and manage. Just like you’re not the only person to land on this planet, your started island is one of many! Kickstart your industry to get all the tech you need and comfortably explore other islands. You’ll come across various biomes, creatures, landmarks, caves, and some really important people… Of course, there’s a blaster you can fire, and critters large enough to be a real menace! Engage in combat and gather rare materials, or, go the full pacifist route and remain a kind guest to this planet - even when boss creatures are concerned. Be prepared to offer valuables to make peace with them, however.

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the game at this point and obtained every achievement. Took me about 25 hours. Here's the skinny:Game is indeed like a combination of Forager and Factorio but does neither of them better. The beginning is very fun. Probably the first 9-10 hours you'll just be excited to see what's around the corner and what else will unlock. This isn't a bad game. In fact, I enjoyed it a lot. But I feel like I have more criticism than I do positive things to say about it at the moment because the end of the game spoiled the first 3/4 of it.I've put many, many hours into Factorio. The greatest thing about Factorio is the idea that THE FACTORY MUST GROW. You have a practically infinite map with a blueprint system and can make the most massive factory imaginable.This is NOT THE CASE HERE. You have very little space to work with. Towards the end I was cramming all these assemblers on a tiny little island trying to get the last few products (which take a very long time to make by the way) and had no way to speed up production because I was literally out of space to place more production building. This is even with the gem speed-up upgrades.Logistics and collector robots also need a serious upgrade because only being able to have 5 per island is not enough when you start dealing with packaged products. At no point in the game can the logistics robots carry more than 1 individual item at a time, yet packaged products need 100 of an item to make? So you seriously need to make 100 trips per package? Why can't they carry stacks of an item? It feels like the devs themselves only seriously playtested the game's last 25% to make sure it was at least functional before shipping it.And yet I still recommend the game. It's fun. I think it's going to get better. But you'll see what I'm talking about as the game nears the endpoint. We need more space to work with. If it were me, I would make each island about 50% bigger or add 50% more islands. It's silly that there are at least 3 islands we can't actually build on. Also we need about 10 robots per island instead of 5, with stack carrying being an upgrade for logistics bots.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great successor to Forager, with the addition of some logistical challenges to solve as opposed to "eh, just build more furnaces that auto-magically re-stock from your vaults that auto-magically collect their products."  Now you have to consider things like throughput and more intelligently arrange your machines across various islands each with specialized resources.You can play through one save file for dozens of hours to unlock absolutely every single optional, cosmetic item available but you eventually get to a point where expanding production is simply not possible anymore and you've completed every thing else.  So you wait -- and they even included a feature where you can get bonus productivity while you wait.  That bit was silly but hey, if you want to run this game in the background like an idler, that option is available!I'm tapping out at ~20 hours played, which was fun and engaging.  If you liked Forager, I think you'll like this, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong - game is not good, nor bad. It just feels unfinished. (Therefore it's something in the middle)Beginning of the game is fun and catchy, but endgame makes you suffer through wait times, even after efficiently planning productions. Endgame upgrades don't feel rewarding, museum rewards are useless, there are few exploits in the game (which were discovered randomly through play through) and who thought that it would be a great idea to not be able to skip cutscenes?I really hope that Developers won't abandon this game, as it has huge room for growth.I will give this game another visit after some big update (if any planned) and update this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Though I'm recommending the game, please continue reading about its flaws before you buy.The reason I'm recommeding it, is because it's fun to play, it does what it says on the tin, it's simple to control and everything works as it should (at least to my knowledge). However, I felt like the trailer for it is a bit misleading.It feels like it's telling you there's exploration, but there isn't. Everything you see is either part of some minigame, or very integrated into the game. For example, you cannot travel to islands before you unlock them. However, each island is a biome, which provides you with materials you need to unlock the next island or tech. Therefore, it's not that you "happened upon" that part, it's not that you "explored" it either. It's that you had to go there to progress.The skills and bonuses you get are an absolute necessity. I'm currently at end-game, and the grind is real, even with every single bonus in the game. Some rewards are skins for your character, which was also a negative for me. Even completing an area at the museum simply gives you a skin and a boost to max HP. I am only struggling to complete it now because I'm a completionist. There really is 0 reason to complete the museum.The most necessary bonuses (gem tower, house comfort, etc) are gated, and the gate is at a very low limit. For example, you get a bonus where your buildings work faster. If you upgrade that bonus to the final tier (which will take you a while), that bonus is only 50%. Not even 100.Though the game starts in a cool manner, you drop to an alien planet, and have to figure out what to do etc, I almost immediately lost immersion as there are many other people who have already built a settlement next to you lmao. Yeah, they're necessary as you can trade for stuff and buy stuff from them, but again, I was expecting something else.The limit on the bots per island (yeah, there is one) is just 5. Though 5 is initially more than you need (well, u have to upgrade that to get to 5, it starts from 3 I think), in the end-game it's extremely low. This could be solved if logistic bots could be upgraded to pick up many materials at once, there is no such upgrade. In general there is only a few signifcant upgrades, without which the game would grind to a halt. And then there are many completely unnecessary upgrades, like "auto-use medkit" and "auto-use oxygen bottle", which you get towards the end-game and by then you no longer need them.There's also the flying bots. You have to manually tell them what to bring where. Meaning, get this item and deliver it to that specific storage. However, there are item-specific storages, which the logistic bots see. So there could be an auto-button, that simply delivers that item to any specific storage. Or a setting on the storage itself, like, "auto-deliver here". There are no such things. The reason I'm saying this is because at some point in the game you have to deliver up to 4 items to all islands. You have to build 4 storages on each island, then make 4 flying bots (1 for each item), then manually select each route for each island. This is completely silly and needlessly time-consuming.There are no priorities. You cannot set any importance of any item delivery. Not even in world-wide logistics. I don't know how priority is calculated (maybe it's just a loop) but it's really bad that you cannot set at least an "important" button.Anyway, I'll stop here, I'm sure you get the gist. The game is fine, it's cool to play, but for this price (10% discount, 18 euros) it's not worth it imho. I don't want to collect skins, I want my character to be what is advertised (that futuristic girl in the trailer) and then I want actual rewards that matter in the game when I do quests.So yeah, I recommend it, it's fun, but not at this price, and not at 10% discount either. This would be more like a 5-7 eu game. Even 10 would be fine. Anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Your forced into the data mining by default, to opt out you have to click on a link inside the game and login to some website with a notice that if nothing happens when you click the link it a pop up blocker blocking it. To me this just screams, "That way we can tie your steam account and hardware specs we harvested with your agent-user (Data used in browsers to fingerprint you) profile. Why not make it a opt in option instead? Or if you must do so, have a button that sends the request directly to the server to delete any data already collected and stop the game from digging anything else? Why force us to click on a button that supposedly opens a link in a browser where you can login and turn it off? (I assume you have to login because I can't get it to work with 3 different browsers swapping them to default. I suspect it may be a linux thing.) The button does nothing.

_childDocuments_.review: Nova Lands is a great simplified factory builder in a similar vein to Forager.What I really like about it is that the pacing is well done for the majority of the game. You constantly unlock something new that demands your attention, always doing something to improve your factory - setting up new production chains or reorganizing old islands to be more efficient. The game also throws in a little variety to mix things up, there's an occasional simple boss to defeat and an asteroid mining mini game which rewards you with efficiency upgrades for your whole factory. Unfortunately as you're nearing the end game the simplified systems start to show their ugly side. There is no way to set consumption priority for buildings or regulate the flow of resources in any way. This manifests in having no way to control what will starve if you're underproducing some resource because you cannot tell the game to deliver more resources to one place than the other. This is especially annoying in the end game where it's hard to overproduce certain resources so you have to rely on turning facilities on and off or manually moving stuff to compensate. It's not as bad as it sounds, but it sticks out. Also, the last story quest as of writing requires a bunch of end game resources that are easier produced just by leaving the game idle for 4 hours than trying to speed up its production. Despite that I still recommend Nova Lands, It's a fun, rewarding < 20 hour playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Nova Lands is a combination of Forager and Factorio (and a bit tiny tiny of Stardev Valley) but it cannot delivery any nice feature from these games and it feels very frustrating. If you never played Forager or Factorio then you could enjoy it but please first check both games before Nova Lands because you will see how Nova Lands is just a waste of money.Below are some small spoilers to the game (but you will experience them in the first 2 hours of the game).Pros:- Definitely feels like a vibe of Forager- Bots are available almost from the beginning of the game. It can start feeling like a Factorio type of game since the first 20-30 minutes of the gameplay- Fantastic animations, sounds, soundtrack, whole visual effects- You can do a bit more complex "base" compared to Forager (or even Stardev Valley)- Really relaxing and chilling for the first 2 hoursCons:- After the second hour of gameplay, you cannot return the game on Steam and from this point I started feeling like the whole game has been created to deliver fantastic first 2 hours and then it's going down with whole quality.- Costs more than Forager or Factorio and got MUCH MUCH MUCH less content than both games.- Feels more like "copy-paste of Forager" instead of "Forager genre". The way of levelling, the skill tree, etc. Nova Lands is using these systems in a much worse way and the original design from Forager (or Factorio) is much more fun.- Compared to Forager: Skills are boring and you cannot go with all directions in the skill tree. Many skills are not extending the content but changing the numbers ("+15% quicker production").- Compared to Forager: You will have a place to collect items but each collection will give you just a new skin and +20 to health. Disappointing. Each reward is the same and each collection is easy to find in game.  In Forage you could get a star which was used to progress the skill tree or get an additional bonus later but here you have just dissapointing reward.- Compared to Forager: Upgrades to weapons and equipment are just numbers: +25% quicker harvesting, +25% quicker walking, etc. Forager had many weapons, many unique upgrades and tools which upgrade could extend the content. Nova Lands hasn't got any of them. The first weapon is your last weapon.- Compared to Forager: Enemies are extremely boring and easy to beat. Bosses and "puzzles" are even worse and dissapointing. I skipped one boss fight by accident because I resolved really simple puzzle before the fight. I didn't know how I could re-do it and do the proper fight.- Compared to Forager: Except 2 puzzles related to 2 bosses, you will not find any more puzzles in the game. It was a big part of Forager. Both puzzles are very simple and feel like placeholder instead of real proper puzzles.- Compared to Factorio: You can create a more complex "factory" between islands, but what's the point? The "Factory must grow" type of vibe isn't here because the space is limited and the game is not offering tools to do it with the same pleasure as in Factorio (or any other Factorio-ish game).- Compared to Factorio: Bots are very limited. The complexity is minimal. You can try to speed up a bit this and that in your "base" but at the same time game hasn't got mechanisms to do it quickly and without pain. Manual work is always required because Nova Lands is not offering proper blueprints.- Compared to Factorio: Nova Lands is trying to borrow some complexity from Factorio-ish games but at the same time, it's stuck in the middle and cannot deliver the proper "I have automatised my base" feeling without frustration. Many times I felt like "oh man, I could do this so faster in Factorio".- Some mechanisms could be cut out. Example? Oxygen. After the first 20-30 minutes (and unlocking some skills and upgrades) the oxygen wasn't a problem till the end of the game. Why add and continue using this mechanism till the end of the game when it can be fully skipped after the first 30 minutes? It's giving a part of survival like in Forager but Forager was connecting it with stamina and health. Nova Lands simplified it in a bad way.- Some reviews on Steam mentioned missing tooltips and I fully agree with it. I spent a lot of time trying to figure out what is the third item I need for plasteel (it was a scale from one of the animals - the icon was absolutely rubbish and the tooltip was missing, so I spent ages trying to figure out what's that).It's been 1 month since I created this review and since the release of the game and devs didn't update with any future roadmap or future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: 7.2/10 Pros:+ Automation game play+ Nice art style+ Decent casual music+ Worth while 100% achievements Cons:- Very slow late game scaling.- Museum is tedious- Needs minecraft item stack manipulation Conclusion:I enjoyed my time spent playing this. I would usually set stuff up in a way where I could leave and return a couple hours later with everything already made for me to progress forward. Late game even with Diamond dashes (production speed) and Super lubricant (production speed) some items took multiple minutes of waiting. Some achievements did need some help from google to figure out but mostly they unlocked naturally. Automatic farms are alot better than I originally thought. The in-game challenges even more over the top than the steam achievements so i'm defo not doing them. 20$ was a little steep of a price tag in hindsight but would purchase for around 15$. _childDocuments_.review: Hmm, and we have a worthy son of Forager in front of us! A skill tree, an exploration tree, biomes with their own flora and fauna, the ability to improve your equipment to make your routine easier - all of this will be waiting for us. However, I understand that patches or hotfixes will be released for this game. For example, I found several problems:1) Recipes in the ovens have different font sizes for some reason, such as modular bricks. 2) encountered incorrect display of items in warehouses, ie, they just disappeared (but after some time may appear)UPD: I've had items disappear after I put them in a warehouse (modular bricks, iron and copper ingots, charcoal, etc). This happened at completely random moments.3) The thing that annoyed me the most was that backpack items were disappearing, i.e. resources that I was collecting. There was a full inventory, and after restarting the game they were gone...I can say that, the game will still be refined and has a good chance of being a decent indie. Even though my gameplay experience wasn't perfect because of the bugs, I thoroughly enjoyed the gameplay.P.S. I'll be waiting for the hotfixes!UPD: the first hotfix has already been released! Glad the developers responded so quickly to bug reports
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Nova Lands is good. I do have some minor gripes, though.Good:- Solid fundamental gameplay- Solid automation mechanics with some interesting novelty in there, especially moving resources between islands.- Pretty good progression in the late game -- the final tier(s) of buildings require overhauling your factory and really maximizing your space, which I consider a good challenge.Not so good:- Skill tree and research tree are boring.- Replayability is surprisingly *low* for a game like this. Little player choice in gameplay systems (e.g. island unlock order, research order, options for making Kredits, etc.) means everything will tend to feel the same.- Music was really pretty annoying. Obviously, this is personal opinion, but I ended up turning it off completely after a few hours.- The price seems a tad high, compared to other games in the genre, and considering its level of polish. I'd recommend lowering the base price by $5.More thoughts:Many people rightly compare this to Forager. Nova Lands clearly adopts some of the same core setup and gameplay. For my part, I played a lot of Forager, including speed runs, and stopped before the drama with that game started unfolding.In my opinion Nova Lands doesn't do much that's *better* than that "golden era" of Forager. It does do a few things *worse*, though.In particular, Forager's skill tree and experience gain were very impactful to how the game played out. Players had more meaningful choices to make. Nova's skill tree is filled with boring stuff like "15% less oxygen used", and some of the options such as "big rocks start to appear" are (as far as I can tell) literally unnecessary until the late game so they're just a trap for newer players.All that said, the game *is* fundamentally fun, and despite all my criticisms the core is good enough to be a recommend (preferably at a slightly lower price).
