_childDocuments_.review: Nova Lands takes the automation genre and crosses it with Forager and the result is.....mixed.Early game the automation is fun to set up, and the colourful characters and environments are also enjoyable. I spent a good few hours feeling like I was making progress and always had something to do while I was waiting for things to be manufactured.Unfortunately once you hit end game (15-20 hours in depending on your play speed) the game rapidly slows down. One of the final items I had to build took ages, even with almost all of the speed upgrades deployed into my build chains, and producing more items in parallel wasn't really possible due to the size of machinery required to produce said items. I basically left the game on and went and did other things for an hour or two to while the required items were produced. All in all I enjoyed the majority of my time with this game, and despite the last 5 hours feeling like a slog (and the ending being a bit anticlimactic) I do recommend it, but a word to anyone coming in (or reaching that final stretch): Buy the recipe for and make use of the Black Hole Lubricant (oooh matron!)Compared to the regular lube (2x) and the super lube (4x) this is a whopping 16x build speed increase, and actually makes producing additional black holes required for the final solution a hell of a lot faster. I still think some of the late game build times could be reduced (either by the devs tweaking code values or by making other upgrades/systems available to the player, or perhaps at the cost of more complex recipes/material requirements), but as mentioned I did enjoy the rest of the game, and for just under £12 (I grabbed it on sale) I definitely got my moneys worth out of it either way.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, just the endgame feels ... not nearly as fun.There needs to be upgrades to the logistic bots so that they can carry more than a single item, otherwise all the  feel more like an annoying sidegrade than an upgrade and having islands like the rock island be super inefective in both gathering and smelting as you can only have 5 bots and 2+ of those will be collectors.Also the logistic bots could have some setting to shift priorities, not just disable some.Overall the endgame is just a bunch of waiting as there is no real way to speed the whole thing up as you run out of space pretty quick with these assemblers that take literaly a minute+ to create a single item.Why do you get health upgrade from the museum as well when fights are not relevant by the time you complete ~3 out of the 6-ish museum parts (the relic reward is at least nice). Maybe make mounts(or at least the flying one???) able to pass through buildings so that lategame movement is not so annoying? Plenty quality of life things to improve, still gotta recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I have never posted a review of a game before, even for those I loved or hated, but for this game it seemed absolutely necessary. This game is ridiculously fun and I am completely blown away by the wonderful QOL choices the developer has made. I'm a huge fan of resource management and automation type games. I loved Forager and Don't Starve and I get vibes of both in this game. But a lot of games in these genres have mechanics that can feel grindy or cumbersome, and Nova Lands seems to have a remedy for all of them. The pacing is superb and there are very few bottlenecks where it feels like you aren't making progress. The relic progression for making mechanics even more user friendly feels very rewarding. There are many elements of the game that are unlocked gradually and every time it is super exciting to work in the new aspect of gameplay. Also, for an automation sim, they have done a phenomenal job of not making you feel locked in to your original setup, and rebuilding/rearranging your layout to be more efficient always feels very doable. Overall, I cannot recommend this game enough as it is so very fun and satisfying to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Okay this game has me pretty split.Positives:- Great fun when you get started- Nice progression (once you understand some key mechanics)- Factoriolight automation!- Some exploration too (but it's not main gameplay)- Spend some nice 12h that went fast but now I feel there isn't much but grinding left.Negatives:- Sometimes confusing progression (sometimes you get stuck because of some mechanic you didn't realize is vital to the game or a place you wanted to explore later but the game doesn't remind you)- Really, REALLY limited space for building automation- Moving buildings is really annoying. You can "move building" but if you want to move them to another island I don't think it's possible. If you setup iron miner in one island GOOD LUCK moving it to a new one.- Finding and mapping items & machines can be quite confusing. Much easier on factorio- Automation is sometimes too limited (what settings you can choose, what resources you can use)- Sometimes I just don't know how to optimize my automation. I know I have to but I am clueless how. I don't really get this feeling in factorio.- Combat is rarely that difficult, mandatory or fun, especially in the end. Bosses can be hard until you unlock abilities to make bosses piece of cake.TL;DR;Nice factorio light gameplay with severe limitations. If you don't mind spending 20€ on "new" automation/exploration experience give it a shot. Not that lengthy of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I've changed the review to a positive. Came back to give it another shot, and genuinely had a good time. Previous review below, and most of the points made are still accurate:-Still no tutorial-It's still difficult to find items in a sea of items-Still a lack of depth in different branches, and inability to focus on oneBut with that being said: I found myself enjoying this game a lot more than I did previously. Maybe it's just time, maybe I'm in a different head space, maybe there were improvements made. It's not my favorite city-builder, but I can see the good aspects, appreciate the work they've put into it, and enjoyed the game more than the last time around. Also was wrong about the perceived time restraints to at least some degree, and would rescind that point in the updated review.Previous review:This game is unique and interesting, but has some overarching issues that bring the overall game down.First, the pros:*Lovely art style*Extremely smooth gameplay, I never had an issue running the game*Interesting resource-respawn and robot-based system that effectively takes what other games would use as late-game automation and instead makes it the norm from the startBut, the cons are too glaring:1) The game offers progression trees, but the items on each tree are required to upgrade other tree branches. In many ways this discounts the purpose of having trees, since you can't actually pursue one without pursuing all of them since you won't have the items or upgrades needed for the other. So for example if you wanted to just focus on farming and animals and turn the game into a farm sim you couldn't do it without first upgrading the automation, logistics, and potentially combat trees. So perceived choice without actual choice or depth.2) There's a major lack of information in the game of what items are, and instead leaves that part to finding a specific image in a sea of areas. Might be on the upgrade module, might be produced in a building, might be collected from an island you haven't unlocked yet, you just don't know. And when these specific items are needed to upgrade the tree and it's the only thing you need it only makes finding it that much more frustrating, as you're effectively soft-locked in progression until you find a needle in a haystack. At least give it a name, or add a book with items listed so you don't spend 30 minutes trying to figure out what you need to do. 3) No tutorial :( Not necessary if you're familiar with the genre, but could be tough if it's your first entry.4) There's are unnecessary time restraints put into the system that don't add to the game but rather slow it down for no reason. You need a mountain of mushrooms for a specific recipe in order to progress the game, but I was only able to unlock one island that had them, so I wound up spending 2 hours waiting around fully capped in automation because an item just didn't spawn regularly enough to keep things moving.RECAP: It's a beautiful game artistically and in creativity, but falls short on many of the automation basics that are the bread and butter of the genre. Has so much potentially, but just falls short in really critical areas.

_childDocuments_.review: The Forager game is the closest alternative to this game. But multiple Islands economy with strong inter-island transportation issues and lack of space (in the endgame).It's good until around middle game. Then suddenly it become more idler-game with few absolutely necessary complete overhauls of infrastructure over the course, because some of buildings become obsolete/too slow/occupying too much precious space.+ nice game overall;+ easy achievements, few secrets, few bosses, few puzzles;- spacewalk minigame: it's fun first few times, but game require you to grind it many times and it quickly become not fun;- dialogues: skipping 3 of same dialogues every time when you want to buy some seeds? seeing same outdated and obsolete gossip? seeing empty window when everything is bought? just lol- too slow crafting, it's really hours and hours of just blatant waiting for crafts to finish.. I basically quit game at some point, just because I can't let it run in background for so many hours and there is absolutely nothing to do in the meantime;- no option to turn off sounds when alt-tabbing;- some issues with AI and lack of priority for targets, the delivery chain may break completely;- some hidden limits, like robots can't take resources from drone station, if game want to introduce limits they need to be clear (e.g. marking buildings as input-only), giving hints or provide a workaround.. sure, I could just pickup a stack of packed materials and deliver that myself, but why drones can't deliver that too???- lack of direction: I need to google at least twice to figure out what to do next, there is no main quest or anything, there is no help in explaining steps required to finish goal if you stuck, there are some confusion, e.g. at some point game claims you got "new island" (singular), but you get "two islands" and it's hard/impossible to notice it, because map window is not designed to show you new islands;- the game clearly had a long development, because things get changed over time, new content added without respecting initial game mechanics, which may easily confuse, e.g. at start we discover islands by using special device, then we need to deal with "wild" islands, then some islands just pops up from the sea out of nowhere...- some mechanics are dull, e.g. housing, you just need to buy house, upgrade it, unlock furniture (buying it) until last tier, then put some of if in your house and never visit it again... game could as well just ask me for 100.000 Kredits to give me awesome perk to get 1/7 item crafted for free... ><I am really happy I could do 100% of achievements without fully finishing all bloated content, like buying all heads. The number of heads is just stupid. Grinding pearls for unlocking all npc heads is stupid.P.S.: WTF are monuments? I didn't figure out... I wonder who added them to the game and why..

_childDocuments_.review: The Nova Lands is an alright game.  I'm glad the description of the game mentions Factorio, Forager, and Satisfactory, because those are definitely the most apt comparisons, while I haven't played Forager myself, I am a huge Factorio addict, so I decided to take a chance on this game, wondering how it stacks up.I would say that, if you are looking for a more relaxed and casual Factorio experience, this is probably what you're looking for.  While the game does feature combat, it isn't particularly deep and I would not say I was challenged at any point, however for those that DO find the combat challenging, the fact that there are alternative solutions to the few boss enemies in the game that don't involve combat is a neat addition.While you won't get the absolute HIGH of Factorio, you will still get that great experience automation games give you, of having an incomprehensible and complex looking factory, where logistics bots are flying around, collector bots collecting, crafting stations crafting, and items in general just flying around the map to where they need to go, and as such I think it succeeds at being an automation game.I would say the first 3/4ths of the game is very solid, and I have very little criticism I feel I could give.  The last 1/4th however, just after you finish Plasteel research, is where I felt the game was dragging.  process timers in Assemblers and Refineries are pretty excessive, forcing you to build at larger scales, however this comes at the cost of resource generation.  I think ultimately the math works out because I would say there's at least 2 islands that I think you would have no issues if you just filled out the entire space with your actual factory, and the rest you would want to carefully think about how you're laying things out, but once again thinking about the process timers, i feel like there's just something to be said that one of the end game mechanics is just laying in bed to get a productivity bonus, really encourages just speeding up the timer rather than expanding out.The game isn't very long, probably 20-30 hours to 100% it in it's current state, but I think that's absolutely fine for a game at this price.Ultimately, if you're looking for a casual Factorio experience, it's a game I can recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in part for the exploration, combat, and zelda-like presentation, but then I realized it was 90% a factory/automation game. _childDocuments_.review: enjoyed the game, feels like a light resource management type sim, easy to get into, easy to hop on for 30 mins and continue where you left off. hopefully development for the game continues as it does feel a bit unfinished in the late game. art and vibes are on point! complaints: early - mid game is really fun and it feels like you have pretty consistent upgrades and minor logistic challenges to overcome and then you start to hit bottlenecks in the late game. namely production time (even with 1.5x upgrades), island size and bot limitations. things like not being able to set limits for logistics bots so you can control the flow a bit better. eg. only take from an output once there are at least 50 items sitting there. or not being able to set a lower number of max output it's either 1, 50 or 100. the last upgrades for production don't really feel like upgrades and take up a huge amount of space which is already limited.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this might be the first time I have down voted a game. Nova Lands isn't awful or broken, it is just boring. I liked Forager a lot and managed to get pretty into Factorio despite being pretty bad at scaling the factory. In this game, by the 3 hour mark I just had to ask myself "what is the goal of this game?" There is likely an answer but it is not made clear in the gameplay and I didn't find myself motivated to upgrade my gear or keep scaling up the production and going up the research tree. For a game that is $20, I shouldn't be completely bored and over it so soon in. What sucks is that I have been looking forward to this game since it was up for wishlist on Steam. I even really enjoyed the demo that they made. I don't know what happened between here and there, maybe it is me. Who really knows. I think it might be a fun game for some, but in trying to simplify factory games (which I can appreciate as someone who gets overwhelmed by the complexity), I feel that it lost all of the "the Factory must grow" urgency that other games have had that really pushes you to scale up. I'm going to put this game down for awhile and hope that coming back to it later may make it something I can be interested in again but until then I am going to have to say that it wasn't worth the money for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly short game. Definitely very similar to forager. There are definitely many things that could be improved upon, such as the automation system, but the game is short enough that it isn't a huge deal.Note that there isn't much to do once you've completed the game, but there are more things to do than there are achievements.Examples of issues below:As an example, it seems like bots somewhat break if you have too many buildings on an island as some of my bots stopped taking certain actions such as refilling lubricant despite having two of them idle. (This was fixed after a restart).Other issues include that excess stock is not used to fill up the production buildings. I'd expect that it fill the unused slots as priority, but then when the stock of a material hits 100 (cap), that it start using that stock to fill up production building slots. This is mainly an issue for power sources that need to be always running or they break the supply chain and potentially cripple your entire island set.sAdvanced twig farms can only have their first tree turned into a bee hive. Doing this makes the entire tree farm do nothing as the beam is stuck on the first tree and does not automatically harvest the hive.Harvester priority can be somewhat annoying when trying to capture creatures that move a lot as the harvester (on controller) will often prioritize everything but the creature. This can be made worse if you have a fighter bot on the island as you can't temporarily disable them except by removing them from the antenna and in many cases, the bots will often either kill the creature first or it will be very close (bots can kill a creature that is in the capture animation or being mounted).Trying to send bots on more than 7 islands is effectively impossible on m+kb because it will keep trying to return to the top, but there are 8 islands that you'd want to send to. On controller it is just barely possible if you hold down the button.As a note: It is possible to jump into the water instead of onto an island. If you do, you'll just walk on the water for a bit until you jump back onto an island.

_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: It's not really a good game... it's fine. It's basic, but you can tell the devs sort of lost their way as the game went on. I feel like it was heavily inspired by Forager (but Forager is way more fun), and if it wasn't... it's very similar.The "end" is basically a massive grind/wait for some items that take 38 minutes and 24 seconds to craft... and you need 31 of them. I basically just went and played something else and left it running. There's not enough space to scale up massively like other logistics games, so you'll be stuck waiting either way.Also, the game pretends to have a story, but if "land on planet, mine some stuff, send some stuff to earth, earth people try to come to planet so you murder them all" is a story... then... sure...If you're interested wait for a large discount (50%+). There are much better logistics games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: A great little base-builder game! It is similar to Forager in that resources respawn after a time, and new areas must be unlocked by expanding your facilities to manufacture new products. Nova Lands expands on this with amazing pixel-art aesthetics as well as some light automation.My only real complaint is that there isn't more of it, but at the time of this review there is a content patch being developed, so I'll definitely be coming back for another run once that drops.  That said, the game is still worth the pricetag as-is.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off fun with lots to learn and explore, but eventually it turns into an idle game. Meaning you don't really do much anymore when you play except let the game run and farm resources that take a long time. More islands to explore would be nice, or more alternative gameplay like the space walk. I enjoyed that mechanic because it was different from the rest of the game. Factory management / space management / time management / resource management. While the end game is definitely less hands on and enjoyable, don't let that spoil the game that comes early on. It is a lot of fun early on up until you get to titanium. If you can enjoy the game for 20+ hours then its worth the money, even if you run out of things to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game if you're a fan of factory games like factorio. The balance is good, there's not too much grinding involved as you quickly add more types of machine and new mechanics as soon as you're done producing each new thing.Like any good game of its genre, it does a good job of having you go through the process of making the early game resources before essentially saying "now that you know how to do that, let's never do it manually again".Thematically it's a very cute game as well, and some of the character designs are also cute, though they're very much an aside, so they don't really have much personality per se. My favourite moment of the game was the I enjoyed it enough to get all the achievements, and I appreciated that there was some extra content at the end but there weren't any late game achievements which just measure your willingness to waste hours of your time like some similar games tend to have.Only thing I found confusing was that I unlocked the ability to craft sapphire / emerald / diamond efficiency enhancers  before I figured out how to actually get the resources for them, so maybe needs a tweak there (or maybe I did things in an unusual order?)
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Cons:Maybe there's more depth as you progress onward past the first seven islands... but I got completely burned out on the gameplay loop far before then. There's a lot to love here, but I personally had a hard time finding any motivation to keep playing, and got to that point very quickly. Someone looking for a more casual experience might love it, but if you're a die-hard Factorio player like me then I don't think this will have enough depth to keep you hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Very much like Forager, but with a bit more focus on automation and more complex recipes. Expect less exploration. Less tools/weapons. Less fighting. Less puzzles. I'd say I finished the game after some 10 hours and completed all achievements after almost 17 hours. I did some idling in the end to craft some high tech stuff, but no more than 1-2 hours.After it's release into early access the game feels very polished. I've encountered not a single bug.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Slightly different factory type gamePlays really well on the steam deck and thats where I spent probably the first 20 hoursMust say the last 30 hours is basically an optimisation and idle wait game (which the devs clearly know based upon the sleep bonus mechanic)Early game is really fun factory grindMidgame has some fun 'mini' games (spacestation parts)Endgame is basically a mega grind and I only completed it so I knew I did rather than steam achievements as they run out about 20 hours in.All in all, its fun if you like factory automationIt runs well on Steam DeckIts a grind late game that you can leave idle
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Very Forager inspired. And as a Forager fan, as well as a Factorio fan, let me just say that this game ticks all the checkboxes in ways the other games didn't. Forager lacked enough automation while having a bit of it. Factorio lacked enough action while having a bit of it. This game has a proper mix of both.However, the game is very short and it feels like it's easy to clear through everything rather quickly. However, in my opinion, being too short is better than being too long as it's a sign that the devs know how to put heart into the intended fun and make it count. Also, since it is short, it has already allowed me three playthroughs, each getting more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the game. It is fun to play through once.The first ten hours were fun exploring, learning, and understanding the mechanics of the game. The second ten hours were establishing a factorio-esque supply chain to create the required materials to progress. The last ten hours were a slog. The end game knee caps you with materials than take about ten minutes to craft even after efficiency upgrades. The game offers you a house perk that will allow to idle the game and get bonus crafts, but you still need to wait with the game open to craft dozens of end game items (that take ten minutes a piece to craft!). It the majority of the game was fun and I's still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I draw a lot of parallels to forager, good and bad. I love unlocking all the little upgrades, slowly increasing production of everything, finding out there's more and more to the game when I think I've hit the end. But it has the same problem as Forager in that regard. It sticks around too long. I was determined to get the ending and stuck to it, but I felt the last 5-10 hours were filled with me just waiting because there was no way I could speed up production.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: My first thought after seeing a screenshot was 'hmm.. Forager met Factorio'. Read the description, was confirmed and immediately wishlisted for when time would be right. I loved all games this one took inspiration from and was very happy to see old ideas well recreated and new things sprinkled in so it does absolutely not feel like a plain rip off. I quickly lost track of time and just enjoyed the gameplay, which feels natural and relaxing. Mostly. I like games where the devs managed to find the right balance between guiding the player too much or not at all. Nova Lands is like Factorios younger sibling. Ab bit more friendly, not as serious and unforgiving. Basically cuter, more colorful and of course way simpler to deal with in general.Standard early game, collecting stuff, slowly mining by hand and then start delegating most of the repetitive tasks to the bots. Assigning them works mostly fine, only while handling crops they mess up from time to time. I missed some way of setting priorities to prevent the bots from using up complete harvests and not filling up the extractor enough to resow the farm. It felt like this behavior gets worse, when using multiple advanced farms on one island and only one extractor.Except from this I've had a lot of fun exploring the world, the mechanics and the unexpected surprises for the first ten or fifteen hours. After that, when the endgame comes in reach, I should have just quitted, because the next long hours have been nothing but chore. Part of this goes on me, as I tend to overthink the simplest decisions, like what island to use for what production (or only a part of it?), while having a hard time keeping the perfectionist down. But here is my complain: in true style of Factorio the endgame is mostly not exploring or managing new things, but instead repeating everything you've done so far in a bigger scale. You basically have to, or it would take forever to get the massive amounts of everything you need. With completely upgraded everything the construction of the final items take around 15 minutes each. So, of course, you just build a massive machinery that makes multiples of the desired item at the same time, so you don't have to wait for 25 hours for one assembler crafting the 100 hypercomputers. That's what these games are about, right? I'd love to, but in my opinion the map is simply too small to fit as many buildings as you'd need. I planned for at least 25 assemblers for the hypercomputers, to reduce the total waiting time to around an hour. Preferably even more assemblers, but after basically filling most of the map with everything for the final chain, it took four hours of mostly waiting, until the last numbers finally ticked towards 100. I covered 3/4 of Rock Island in furnaces, but even 25 continuously smelting steel were not able to keep up with the demand. I used advanced furnaces, as the game shows the same ratios for furnace 2 and 3. If I had checked the wiki while playing I probably would have realized, that the mega furnace has the same ratio indeed, but is waaaay faster und using it would have probably solved most of my trouble.I'd like to suggest to increase the island sizes in general, for people who prefer to spread out a bit and not like building cramped factories. Also it would be so very handy to have the corresponding times shown together with the recipes.And one more thing: Please change the way the player selects buildings. This 'selection depending on the characters previous walking direction' is just so annoying, especially when navigating between multiple buildings. Please create an option for using the cursors position or at least 'select what the character is facing'. That would be awesome.Even I missed the part with the different durations and scrubbed hard against the rage quit, I enjoyed enough of my time with the game to absolutely recommend it. But maybe not for completionists with a low frustration tolerance.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Mix of Forager and Factorio but doesn't do either of them well unfortunately.  The game is extremely limited in the amount of factory building you can do, it kind of just felt like tedious busywork to me, progression feels bad, especially since there's a 5 bot limit and an annoying amount of inventory management.  Maybe I'll come back to this later if there's a big patch but for now it's an easy skip unless there's a deep sale.  Play the games that inspired this instead.Edit: Got to the endgame by chipping away at the game in short sessions and it's pretty bad.  There's basically no meaningful progression in terms of scaling up your production, and the controls for interacting with your buildings and resource nodes and moving them around are really clunky, especially when you need to start spamming buildings together because of the space constraints.  Bosses have been really simplistic too, not sure if this game even needed player combat.  There's just a lot of bad QoL and a subpar gameplay loop. Sadly this is just one of those games where the idea sounds great but the execution is way off.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Very addicting game. I am always thinking about the most efficient way to do things so this was the perfect game for me. It is very much a thinking game, developing strategies to improve throughput times, and early game is full of exploration. For the end game, it could use some work, it was a lot of waiting for materials to be produced with not many rewards. Nova Lands has very cute graphics and skins; that is what first drew me in :)
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't stop playing, which is a good thing (for the developers, not for my health)! The only other game that has ever done that to me is Factorio, which this game definitely took some inspiration from. Finished the game in 20 hours (over two days...), including all the achievements. Combat is optional, has some fun ideas, but in the end it's just way too easy. The factory part is enjoyable, it requires some revisions of your layout as you unlock more items, but pretty basic compared to the true factory games. It scratched my Factorio itch, so definitely recommend if that's what you like!
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a decent jab at the automation genre, however the items in the final phase take an inordinate amount of time to be build even in the advanced buildings to the point you MUST paralelize production to fill the needs of all industries, but the nature of the game world acts a dectrator because of the fabricator's rather gigantic foot print. this reminds me off the myriad mobile games utilizing that level of restrictions to scratch at your wallet.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Great survivalcraft game for people with day jobs. You know how a lot of open world games are bigger than they need to be and therefore the content is either very sparse or repeated ad nauseum? This game does the opposite. It has no issue with you finishing the game in 10 hours (I took my time with it and expect to get about 15 out of it) and will make sure that 10 hours is a complete experience.EDIT: I was completely wrong. It probably takes about 10 hours to get a third of the way through the game lol. There's a lot more to do once you've reached the last tech tier. Not even close to the end. You should go into this expecting something along the lines of Don't Starve, but with a couple bosses that might remind you of something out of Core Keeper, and a crafting/automation system that's similar to Cryofall but with less micromanagement. One of the game's really big strengths is that it makes sure not to get in your way with anything mildly infuriorating, such as being too picky about how you need to position around a resource node to gather it, or sending you on some unnecessarily long side trip to be able to craft something you just unlocked, It just lets you keep your momentum up and gives you enough to do that you don't ruin your own fun by going too fast. If I had to criticize something it'd be the claw arms- like what purpose do those really serve whatsoever if bots can't grab from them?
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: When I first started playing this game, the only thing that kept me interested was the cute, basic art style of the game. Some people might not like it - but it's a style I love, and one that isn't too hard on most PCs, which is rare these days. Despite there being no tutorial, I managed to figure out the majority of the controls and the shortcuts, which is great. For example, if you hold the ctrl button + and left click on a stack of items it separates one. There's two ways to defeat every boss, and I love that one way is a puzzle - but that you get a sort of achievement for doing both.Initially, although I knew the creators still want to add more content, I was worried that the game would be too short. I ended up playing it for almost 80 hours total to get all of the quests, relics, deliveries, etc., and I really did have fun for the entire 80 hours. I kinda wish I could forget the game and start over. It maybe have just been a great little dopamine boost for someone with ADHD, but yeah - very worth it.

_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely my favorite automation game out there. The eventual issue with Factorio, and Satisfactory, and the like, is honestly building hyper colossal mega factories is a tremendous time sink and isn't really that rewarding. Nova lands changes that. The game is significantly smaller, with progression being a lot faster and more rewarding. The end game isn't some rocket that needs 50 billion items to build, it's a cool ass hat you get to wear while you watch your hypersonic logistic bots break the sound barrier while snagging your twigs from the farm.You very consistently get new content, new machines, new upgrades. There's a whole leveling skill tree. There's combat. There's home building. It does everything in a really enjoyable bite sized snippet that never gets overwhelming or tedious. If you've ever played any of the big factory building games and just eventually got overwhelmed or bored, give Nova lands a try. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. I picked the game up Friday, put 36 hours into it before i went to sleep Sunday. Very simple game with great automation features. Challenging in the sense that if something seems hard, it is because you're simply not doing it right. With limited amount of space to create and automate a large variety and amounts of outputs, Optimization is key! I will definitely return to the game if any updates are created! 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: it's just not very fun. It's a carbon copy of Forager but with less content and not as fun mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game when it was on sale and managed to get 30 hours out of it. You can probably complete it in about 20. I did afk some of it and also tried to go for every achievement. What I did enjoy about this game is that it looks so cute, and I'm a sucker for automation. My game never crashed and I didn't run into any bugs throughout my sessions. I enjoyed it way more when I was talking to someone or watching a show/movie. Would get very sleepy if I was only focusing on the game because it's not extremely stimulating unless you're doing a whole new setup. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, it's just a very laid back game. I do wish the islands were slightly larger since it never felt like I had enough room. You have to kind of cram everything together so it doesn't look very aesthetically pleasing. Also disappointed that the NPCs didn't really bring too much to the atmosphere. The last part also had some odd pacing compared to the rest of the game. I had to afk for about 10-20 minutes here and there. Overall, I recommend it. Enjoyed wasting my time with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Nova Lands

_childDocuments_.review: Factorio, Satisfactory and the likes never really did it for me, because it's just too much like a job.Gotta really think carefully about everything, and a single mistake could potentially ruin a whole production line kinda job.This is simpler, and much more fun for me. There's some complexity approaching the end of the tech tree, a big part of it being simply the incremental upgrading/replacement of a lot of buildings, but it's not TOO MUCH. It feels just right.There's always something new to unlock juuust at your fingertips that feels satisfying.That being said, I know that the complexity is kind of the point of games like Factorio, and that it can give them a huge lifespan; I haven't finished this game yet, but by design, I don't see how I would spend hundreds of hours in it. I figure it's gonna be more like 30-40h to unlock and use everything, and when that's done, the game is basically finished.

_childDocuments_.review: Very "factory" lite.  Good game when you know you want to play Factorio but need to set the mood.Problems...Having a house is somewhat pointless.  It's supposed to be a way to idle while gathering resources.  So you max out your decor and that's supposed to give you a 1 in 7 bonus to everything to make.  Possible a bug but I've been making the green computer, the top one in the game, and if I sit there, I see many being made.  Yet if I sleep in my house, where it shows what "bonuses" I get, I never see the green (the most expensive item in the game) ever incrementing or giving me extra items.Bosses seem kind of pointless.  One of the islands gives you what 2 of the bosses give you  So even if you go back to fight them again, it's kind of pointless.  I mean, if you're fighting them just to fight them, good.  I went in on the first boss probably under-equiped. It was a long, good battle. The others I just smacked to death over and over. In other words, bosses don't scale.  I imagine it's kind of nice to be able to skip them, and would be nice if they were always a challenge if you don't... but they aren't.Bugs.  Mostly bug free. Only issue I encountered was after I filled an entire island with factories.  I would have expected that the automatons would have been intelligent enough to handle all the factories with max out stats.  However it seemed that they gave up on the factories at the edges, only grabbing a single item from some factories and letting others build up output and completely ignoring them.  I'd have expected some kind of queue system, but it seemed like some of the factories got handled, but the rest were skipped.  Fine for a casual player, but someone trying to push the limits might find that the game AI isn't quite equipped for it.Endgame content. I just happened to try to 100% the game.  I will, if I leave it running overnight.  Though no one will know because for some reason the achievements aren't triggering.... IDK some people in the forums said they triggered on restart but i should have 99% of them according to the in game achievements. Yet I have 0. Maybe just a fluke.Is it complete?  I don't know.  There's an off planet section that has like 4/5 parts filled in.  Doesn't look like there's anyway to open up that last part.  I imagine that isn't on purpose.  Maybe they thought they'd leave a part unfilled for DLC or they just ran out of time.I like the game. it's a relaxing factory like game.  Just don't expect much depth.  Mostly bug-free.  The only time it seemed to crash was when I was idling for that last challenge goal.If you just want to chill out a few days, it's a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game at release and replayed it recently to check out the Quantum Gravity update. It's not a bad game, I had a lot of fun, but unfortunately there also were a lot of annoying quirks that I want to highlight. FYI, I will try to keep it spoiler-free, especially for the update.It's impossible to write a comprehensive review without comparing the game to Factorio, so I'll start off with something positive: This game has cute visuals and some light story, whereas Factorio is more serious and does not have a story to speak of. This makes Nova Lands particularly well-suited for a younger audience and people who prefer this art style and aren't looking for over-the-top automatization.Speaking of positives, for the most part I really enjoyed the Quantum Gravity additions, in particular I felt like  extended the previous features in very welcome ways. One thing that immediately struck me as odd, though, was the gameplay pacing. Basically every feature from the update is locked behind the final challenge from the pre-update game, which not only makes it feel very tacked-on but also means there's this point roughly halfway through the game where you're basically just waiting for the last few items to be delivered and feel like you're near the end, only for the game to suddenly open up and throw you into a whole new automation loop. This isn't bad per se, but it certainly seems unintentional.Taking a closer look at the new features, . As such, it is a sensible feature to implement. The problem started when . Again, this "feature" seems unintentional. In general, I had a hard time finding actual uses for , which was not helped by the fact that it takes  ingredients that are not needed for  other building and so I never had on hand.On that note, the skill tree was not changed by the update, which is at least a minor problem because part of it is for removing starter ingredients from recipes. This is necessary due to the very limited inventory space, and because this feature isn't extended for the update, your late-game inventory will most certainly be cluttered.There is one more issue I have with the content from the update. It won't affect your  average playing experience, but I still want to mention it. I'm a completionist and there is a finite amount of things to spend the in-game currency on. So naturally, I want to have it all. There is also a very limited amount of things you can sell, and to have enough money you have to sell . The very last thing you can sell is one package of . One package is 100 items, each of those takes three  which in turn take 10 packages, that is 1,000 items, of . In short, you need 300,000 of those. My late-game setup can handle around 6,000 per minute (using the ). That means that I need to wait 50 minutes while there is nothing else left to do in-game. Why? To be clear, there is literally no reason to sell this last thing other than to be able to afford everything, and there is no way to do it any earlier than at the very end of your playthrough. So why did the devs choose to make it so expensive? Are they taunting me? I feel taunted.Finally, a nitpicky quickfire round of quality-of-life issues that were present in the launch version and weren't addressed in the update:My theory is that the devs don't play this game themselves. It is no secret that Factorio is as polished as it is because its devs engage with the content they're responsible for on a regular basis, for instance by hosting internal LAN parties. And while I know that the team behind Factorio has had a lot more time and resources to get to its current state, I still feel like a lot of bad decisions and unintentional consequences could've been avoided by simply taking the time to test things properly. Have the devs every played the updated game from start to finish? Have they ever tried working with  the way an average player would? I don't know for sure of course, but my hunch is they haven't, and I really wish they had.This game could be great, even amazing, but unfortunately it is being held back by a mountain of quality-of-life problems, some noticable only by completionists, others clear as day from the first level-up. It is incredible that the game is fun despite this, but it could be so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game that makes me wish we had a more nuanced rating system, and regret that the one here actually works well.  The game's firmly B-tier, in my mind.It's not a bad game, per-se.  It's your basic optimization/assembly/automation game with a style that reminds me a lot of Megaman Legends.But there's no tutorial.  No explanation for what the various parts DO.No hinting which things you'll need very little of, nor what you need A LOT of.  (This one starts becoming a serious problem around plastic/plasteel).And a system that takes anywhere from a bit of grinding to hours and hours of it, depending on how quickly you figure out all the weird little gotchas and strategies.On top of that some things feel sloppily tacked on.  You have a combat system that's entirely optional, and completely irrelevant in the lategame.An optimization subsystem that is ABSOLUTELY a grindfest (spacewalks)And a story that, while reasonably dense and interesting initially, becomes basically nonexistent by midgame.Thumbs-up to support all of 2 (two) devs who I feel like are just coming into their own, but with a caveat of "Buy with either a sale or disposable income to spare".(Though if y'all read this, would it kill your plan to let us unlock all 3 storage-zone buildings early on?  Having to pave over my 2x2s late-game for the space feels kinda forced.)

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo for this game, it played incredibly similar to Forager.Not just in the art style, but the gameplay.And after playing the full game, I can say there were a lot more similarities than I would've liked, but maybe that's just the limitation in this style of game. You complete objectives for cosmetic rewards, you slowly automate the collection and manufacturing of resources, you have a 4 direction skill tree prioritizing different aspects of gameplay.A couple things I find strange, or rather am not completely sold behind is not needing resources the more you level up. A grind which plays incredibly similar to forager. I guess except you have to actively play the game to get xp, where as in Forager you could idle for it.If you really wanted to, you could just unlock farming I, and just place a lot of farm plots and plant the water producing plants, and just spam collect them constantly for xp. The game gives you a pretty sh*t amount of xp for just about anything so the only thing worth your salt in xp grind is farming which is incredibly tedious. Maybe you get xp for your drones and bots from completing things like you would otherwise but leaving the game on and coming back yields no results. This is incredibly slow and there isn't much to do during the down time. All you do is wait and spam farm plots for xp. In Forager there were dungeons and puzzles to do in the mean time. This game doesn't really having anything like that. At least from what I can tell.I've only got 6 Islands unlocked, and haven't started plastic production yet. They've got the museum which is a collectathon. Where you need 5 of each item, regardless of how tedious one item may be to get compared to another. I like Forager's abundance based collection system more, where the easier it was to get an item, the more of that item you had to give up. It seems uninspired to make each item needed 5. As well as how many objectives are more rooted in tedium rather than merit. And all the rewards are just a head replacement so you can't even equip more than one at once. It's quantity in something redundant. It's really boring. If this is the full game, and nothing will be added in the future, I wouldn't recommend this. But this review is a thumbs up with the assumption there is more to come because what's here is boring.Edit 1: I've played the game more, and have progressed into the "end game" of manufacturing computer parts. Which if I may add is incredibly boring. The thing that slows me down to a crawl is being unable to fit enough buildings on islands. Resources spawning and consuming real estate, resources spawning randomly rather than specific ones needed.The game is incredibly tedious, at this point. I don't understand why bots have to be told where to deposit items. The yellow bots that transport items see which storages are marked for certain items, yet the gatherers or whatever they're called are too stupid to evenly spread resources. In addition to the fact that the further a construction is from the bot antenna, the more neglected those buildings get, as well as the fact that the yellow bots are too stupid to load packages into large furnaces. There is a clear automatic priority to hike less important resources that don't need to be constantly attended in lieu of more pressing matters. And switching buildings around doesn't fix this issue, because now it's the other way around. I don't want to constantly move buildings around or sort storage depots manually because the yellow bots are too busy. I had a system where the depot marked for delivery for gatherers isn't marked for the yellow guys to store that item there so they hike it out of there. But they're too slow and the system doesn't work the further you get into the game. The bots are incredibly lazy and prioritize what's closest to them. And I don't understand why lubricant makes refineries and assemblers work faster, yet there is nothing of the sort for electric furnaces. I run out storage for sand, I don't cook glass fast enough, I never have enough bottles. It's infuriating to me, even after placing 16 furnaces just to smelt glass, and then 16 more to smelt bottles, that it was faster to have less of both of those because the bots were being stretched thin trying to deliver more sand into the furnaces or glass into the furnaces. Which, let's talk about that, they only deliver resources one at a time, or rather, enough to make one at a time. It's really slow. If you can mark how much of that item you want to make, rather than having it only make it indefinitely when maybe you only need 12 of that item at the moment, or other things where you can tell how much to take, how much to deliver, or having it automatically do so. It's so tedious. It doesn't have to be.And the thing about placing buildings is that you can move through them. Even with the flying mount, you can't fly over the water, you still have to jump, and even then can't jump over buildings. I have created one way gates out of furnaces and transport arms. I literally cannot traverse freely in my island because you can place buildings on top of each other and create hitboxes much larger than they should be.And another grievance I have is how unintuitive the solution for the chameleon tower puzzle is. You'd think there'd be an obvious answer in what the color coded biome hints refer to like things exclusive to those islands, but the fact is there is nothing exclusive to each island, or if there is, there's more than one. I would've thought it had something to do with plants or flowers but no one of them is just a rock. A rock. The solution to the puzzle is a rock. Why? because you find it in abundance? because the crabs on the island eat rocks? Then why was the solution for the mushroom zone a mushroom and not a water orb? There is so much inconsistency with this solution that it's annoying. Why is some of them flower, and other them not flower. They're all resources sure, but based on the multi colored leaves under the chameleon boss, my assumption was that it had something to do with multicolored plants. And like maybe it had something to do with finding an item that matches the color of the biome, but then why is the plains biome a berry? other than the hog and bees eat berries. It doesn't make any sense. The jelly fish don't eat mushrooms. I haven't even seen the sand lizards eat the cactus flowers they ate the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crabs for bones. Long story short, it didn't make ANY sense. And what exactly was the point of the RNG dragonfly fish puzzle in the desert temple. It was just a hang-man like guessing game. I don't think it would be that difficult to create a memory based puzzle or something. Right? Or even just environmental where you place a hidden solution somewhere in the game and you go and find it and solve the puzzle? Or even better yet, the classic make all the icons light up but pressing one activates the ones next to it? Or even like a simon says where you have to repeat the icons of the animals back correctly and having multiple rounds to complete.There was I'd say a lot of better approaches that could've been taken. I also feel like the whole space integration is somewhat of an after though. I don't want to deal with any of it. Realistically because it's genuinely a tedious and painful matter. Everything hinges on steel production, which hinges on iron and copper smelting, which hinges on charcoal manufacturing and mining, which hinges on the gathering of sticks. The face you are forced to still use the basic stone furnaces for ores other than steel is really slow. What's the point of an upgrade if you can't integrate old technology? It's like apple removing the headphone jack.Despite the fact you don't need resources to build buildings, you still need resources to craft items in furnaces despite the face you don't in the workbench. The game seems to be picking and choosing where certain-

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really, really similar to Forager, though I think it's not quite as good as of right now. I enjoyed my time with it, but there is a pretty big issue with the pacing, at least to me. Towards midgame you reach a point where you need a nearly endless amount of steel, and the game grinds to a halt at that point. Up until then, it's right on the money with that feeling of endless growth that is so satisfying with games like this, but you then need to spend a very large amount of time doing nothing except building as many iron, copper and steel smelters as you can. Around this time you also exhaust the player upgrade tree, and you no longer are able to rely on those upgrades to help scale you up- you've just got your tier 2 smelters and you have to fill every single square inch with them. Then you run out of charcoal, obviously, so you need to expand your wood production but again this isn't exactly a fun process, you never really feel like you're actually gaining ground because your drones are already fully upgraded and are barely keeping up. After a couple hours of doing that, I finally broke through to the final stages of research, but I found this somewhat tedious as well for the same reasons as before. I bottlenecked one particular resource that there just wasn't any particularly good way to get a lot more of. I quit playing before doing the very final stage of research, because it was going to probably take several more hours of mostly waiting rather than making any meaningful expansions to my factory. This all said, I enjoyed the time I spent with the game, but I think it falls short of the bar Forager set. It might be worth your time, but it's not a super strong recommendation. I will keep an eye on it, if there are updates down the line I'd be very interested to revisit the game and see if some of the issues I had with it were addressed. As it is, it's close to being very good, the beginning certainly is, but the latter portion is much less enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a GREAT introduction to factory/automation games.- Materials gathering is very easy to automate, you get limited by the organization and size of your factory. - The limited amount of bots and islands (and space) still makes you worry (a bit, it's still very lenient) about your efficiency.- No hassle with pipes and conveyors, throughput  an issue, but easy to resolve (drones really help later on)- The skills are pretty useful with the overall automation and quality of life, for example buildings and items become cheaper, even free for a LOT of buildings, removing the need to keep very basic items on your inventory (no running back to your base because you forgot iron rods for the nuclear reactor)There still are a few weird things:-Bosses are cool, you can "choose" to fight or befriend them,  but they're kind of a one time thing? Their drops become an automated material on end game, but that material isn't that useful before that point.-The space station feels a bit unfinished, like the asteroid game is pretty grindy and the reward isn't that great(1.5x) and it took me a while to understand that the decorations and the house are pretty good (but that could be me being dumb)Overall the game's fun, its not overly complex but not too simple either and you can ride flying bugs

_childDocuments_.review: (Game is a bit pricey for the amount of content it has but other than that it's great)I thought that this game was boring for the first few minutes. Next thing I know, I get sucked in and have fun for the next five hours of the day.There are few better ways to make a game like this.There's no tutorial but that really makes the whole experience better because of the greater feeling of accomplishment it gives you. As you go along, unlocking more things and/or completing goals, you subconsciously keep making more and more goals. This makes the replayability level substantially higher than it seems from the naked eye. While the game gets more and more automated as you go along, it doesn't feel like other games and get more and more dull, one might even argue the opposite happens. It's just so hands on and every step you take makes you feel great accomplishment.The art style of both in and out of the game are amazing. The music fits the theme they're going for perfectly and makes the experience just that much greater. Same goes for the sound design which, even when there's a lot of noise at once, doesn't shove itself in your face and still manages to sound good. Every artistic aspect of this game is simplistic and amazing.On top of everything else, it's very well optimized and takes incredibly low storage space.10/10, Would say more but it's better for you to experience the beauty and fun of this yourself. I'm glad to be here in this game's early days. Can't wait to see what they do with this game.edit: everyone was right about late game problems and if you're considering getting this game I would suggest you wait a while for some more major updates and reworks

_childDocuments_.review: Nova Lands is a very simple and relaxing factory building game, with elements of bullet hell, exploration and resource management thrown in, to name a few. Just as long as you don't mind the relative simplicity of it all, the experience is quite charming and keeps itself fresh by introducing new elements to the gameplay loop.If you've ever found yourself interested in games like  or , but the scope and learning curve seemed intimidating, Nova Lands  could be for you. The overall scope and complexity is toned down, allowing for a more relaxing and easy to approach game. Admittedly, that can be a massive downside to those who are looking for a more robust and technically challenging experience, so be aware of your expectations.As far as everything else goes, there are a bunch of other elements beyond "factory building lite" here, but they too carry a similar level of simplicity. For example; fighting pretty much boils down to holding mouse one to fire your gun, and dodging with i-frames in something that could be seen as -light, but again there is no real meat to it. It all is very surface level to put it harshly. However, what Nova Lands does is give you a bunch of these types of mechanics or mini-games to mess around with, and loads of side goals to achieve alongside what could be seen as the main game-play loop to keep itself fresh. What you do and when is up to you.My gripes with the experience comes to the end of the game. As it is now. You'll end up running into a wall when progression slows down to a crawl and there is nothing more meaningful to achieve beyond an achievement or two. The ending itself is quite underwhelming, being pretty much just a quest to throw end game materials and resources into a black hole, that once finished gives you a text box to click followed by the end credits. My current gaming experience is one where I leave the game running on the background whilst typing this review to collect resources and cash to buy missing items to fill my collection. Basically, the game plays itself and there is nothing to improve or tinker with unlike in other games in the genre.I don't want to make it seem like I haven't had a good time, however. I literally played the game for 10+ hour straight in one sitting on my first day. I found myself  going "just one more thing" whilst tinkering with my machines and traversing the unknown. There is a lot of heart and a lot to love about Nova Lands and I heartily recommend it. You just have to know if it's something you can enjoy and when to be done with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, this game is disappointing for me, especially compared to other games of the genre. The core gameplay aspects a very shallow:•	Survival: You can “eat” to heal and you have a weak gun. That’s all. •	Exploration: There is none. You gather resources to “buy” a new island, to gather new resources. It’s just a click of a button. There is no satisfaction in this. •	Automation: Automation is done by little bots that carry the resources to the stations to fulfil recipes. However, you only get a maximum of 5 bots per island and each can only carry one resource at a time. So it’s very slow to the point where 5 bots can barely handle 10 furnaces at a time. This leads to long idle times for the player, which means boredom. Simply, not a good game design. •	Progress: The tech and skill tree is very small. After 2 hours, I’m halfway through the progression. There are no new tools, just upgrades to the tools you start with. In general, a very unrewarding progression system. Overall, I would say the scale is just too small for this type of game. There is very little to see or discover. Skip this game and buy Necesse instead, which has 10 times the content for less than half the price. For me, I will request a refund and get something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall : 7/10  An enjoyable and casual automation game.  The play area is a nice size.  Not to small, but also not so large that it takes forever getting the resources you need.  There are some upgrades that i feel should be called out for players to get early, like the 400% speed increase on delivery drones and the auto farm.  There are logistics buildings you don't get until the DLC that would definitely benefit the base game.  Amount of content is reasonable.  Some minor combat and boss fights, but you don't get games like this for their combat systems.  Art : 8/10 Clean pixel animations, solid workLogistics : 8/10 Tracking what is going where can make or break one of these games.  There are maps to see what what items are being produced where and what transports are carrying them to other islands.  Nothing groundbreaking but it works well.  Tech Progression : 7/10 Biggest issue is that you still need coal through the game.  Even after getting electric furnaces, the ore smelters still only run on coal.  Lubricant upgrades do well to improve efficiencies on the limited number of machines.  Story : 6/10 Crash land and start from nothing. Do some basic missions.  Not much here.  DLC does add a nice quest chain.  Combat : 4/10 I have pew pew.  Wild animal spit red ball.  Don't tough red ball.  Just send your assault drone after it.

_childDocuments_.review: After 23 hours I got all achievements and I am never touching that game again. It is simply Forager and doesn't improve on it in any significant way. Definitely not for Factorio fans, unless you idea for improving factory efficiency is playing the asteroid mining minigame, not actually improving design. Islands don't share electricity between them and have limit of 5 bots each - it is easy to end up with just a single (and overworked) logistic bot, if there are 3 resources you want to collect, and some hostile mobs.NPC are glorified shops, they don't even comment on you buying out all items. Tech "tree" is narrow, short and interwoven with island unlocking order. Not only it is linear but it is easy to see what you are supposed to use new area for - it feels like player isn't really making that decision.The game works OK when controlled with gamepad, but I wonder if that is just the function of its overall simplicity.A bit surprising but there isn't any targeting in the game (right stick is unused) - resource collection applies to closes resource, then switches to next one. After unlocking livestock that resource might be some nearby animal. With guard bots around that can end up in literal shootout.TLDR: anticipation for Factorio DLC leads some people to poor buying decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: Forager is a good game, yet one that is deeply flawed. In the years since its release there was a few updates that made it better, but it is still a game that exists to be improved upon. Nova Lands is that improvement. In the same way Cassette Beasts and Monster Sanctuary are just straight up better Pokémon games. Nova Lands is the ideal Factorio-lite. All of the QoL things you can think of are already in this game. The flow is great. The automation and unfolding is spot on. I'd still like to see crafting times somewhere in the game so I can really satisfy the urge to know I have the exact best amount of electric furnaces for making glass but otherwise everything else is fantastic.Right now it seems like there is more content to come, which I am excited for. The asteroid mining is a conceptually neat little mini-game to break up the game, though I think it could be made a bit more exciting past the 4th attempt.This is absolutely the kind of game to just install once a year or so and give it a full playthrough again. It's great. It's fun. And it has just enough interactive mechanics to make you feel like you've actually improved at it by figuring it out on your own.If you like any kind of base building/throughput management/skill trees, then you'd probably like this game.I haven't played it on gamepad yet, though I'm sure it's great. I can tell the menus are designed to make gamepad easier. However the ability to just click from your hotbar and drop onto storage without opening the storage window made me for the first time stick to keyboard and mouse.Play this game, don't look anything up yourself, and enjoy discovering it. (Except the 2 puzzles. They're dumb. I would've figured them out eventually but I just looked them up.)[Edit] I play offline mostly right now, I'm at 15 hours not 90 minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: When you start to play a few games, you tend to see what's "new" and what's a "copy".Mind you, there are good copies, and some made their business to build games kakashi-ing their way with them (Ubi much?).This is not exactly the case here.This is a copy of Forager.And I have to reaaalllly emphasize this : this is a copy of Forager.But.But it's not such a good copy. It's not the kind of copy of "yeah we did the same but added a bunch of stuff to make it a bit more that the original", it's the other kind, whatever that is.So let's go quickly over the "issues".- First of this game has less diversity than Forager, it's more centered around crafting/automation, but it does not really deliver that much more than forager. The whole bot thing is interesting, but not pushed to a point where it gives an actual loop around it, just two/three bots, some mechanics and that it's. All in all, it has a lot less content, there were quests/enigmas, bosses, here it's just a few (underwhelming) bosses.- The crafting, that was a bit grindy in Forager is pretty much the same here, and there are QoL stuff really missing. The whole logistics system is subpar and some "advanced" stuff don't really improve on the old stuff (example for the drones, which are just a mess to use). Again the content is quickly done over.- The "big" unlocks are the skins and... well, it's a very blunt pixel art style. The game is okay in terms of graphics, but not so much so that it is a thrill to change the 10 pixels that are composing the head of the character. So ... yeah, not a lot of point to do those. Apart from that... not much.- It's twice the price of Forager and this is a big issue to be honest. It's not "that" expensive, but honestly, again, it pales a lot in comparison to forager. Plus, it's pretty much "over" in 10 hours if you don't count the grindy ending of the game, it's quite short...- Other minor stuff could be mentioned, the "having to jump" between island, the breathing system which is first anoying, then useless, and so on and so forth...

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where you'll spend most of your day micromanaging things. You check the clock and realize that what felt like 1 hour was actually 5. You felt only a very slight feeling of satisfaction, you want to play more, yet again you realize it's not fun at all, yet for some reason you want to keep playing.I guess it's good for someone trying to zone themselves out of their lives, but I hate this feeling of having spent hours inserting materials into factories like they were minutes.Forager in comparison, as I remember it, is a lot more straightforward and gets to the point, the progress is way faster and simpler.Factorio has you spending your time thinking and "engineering", always finding out better structures, redesigning etc., always thinking about new problems, very satisfying.I feel like a lot of love went into this game, but sadly I think it takes the worst out of both its inspirations rather than the best.Maybe through its shallowness and plainness it makes you aware of the wasted time while other games manage to hide it and "trick" you into wasting it anyway. _childDocuments_.review: The game is fun. Fun with a big problem.The moment you tech up to solve a problem, a new, bigger problem is thrown in your face. The last problem you get is that everything needs a huge amount time.In the end, when you unlocked everything except cosmetics, you need to wait 460 second for one quest material, even when you speed up the crafting time to the current limit. Then the next quest is to get 10 of it, what is 1,3 hour! (and there are more quests after that) And this material is also what is used to increase the crafting speed of some of it's components, plus material itself!Yet there are components you can make by the hundreds, even two unlocks before that. _childDocuments_.review: A good introductory factory sim, and I'll recommend it on those grounds, but I don't think there's much replay value for fans of the games named in the store description. The game's fun, but its simplicity really hurts it, especially as you move later into the game.As a veteran Factorio player, the linearity of both the research tree and of actual production make this game essentially an autoscroller. There's very few decisions you need to make at any given point in development, with resource processing being an essentially linear process (wood to iron, unlock copper, iron + copper to steel, unlock plastic, plastic + steel to plasteel, unlock glue and titanium, plasteel + titanium + glue to super metal, unlock behemuttium). A few side chains do exist, but by the end they all converge into computer modules.Space as the primary constraint for factory size makes for some interesting design problems in theory, but the extremely simple logistics means there's not much depth to base-planning, especially once your logistics bots are fully upgraded. The game essentially becomes a single problem of "what production do I do on what islands", which is interesting enough to keep me playing in the later stages, but I don't think I'll revisit it any time soon after finishing it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea that this game exists until seeing it in a recent Riftbreaker (which I already have) bundle. It was on sale, inexpensive, so I rolled the dice. Fun and a little bit more complex (automation) than you would think to look at it. Runs great (even with huge amounts of items on the ground, robots zooming around). I LOVE that you can drag things right from your inventory to production machines - every building game should have this. Make sure you get and use lubricants; speeds things up SO much. The combat is VERY SHALLOW. Nothing special. Getting the last upgrade feels VERY grindy . . . not sure I will finish the game. BUT getting to this point (90%+) has been fun and, for around $15, I recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Nova Lands is a factory automation game that feels like a mix of Factorio and Forager.  There is a lot to like here.  This game has a great visual style, offers plenty of fun and charming characters, has a solid soundtrack, and offers a unique take on the automation genre.  The game starts off very strong and hits it's stride in the first 8-10 hrs.  Unfortunately, you will likely complete 75-85% of the game in the first dozen hrs, and then will probably need to spend another 10-15 hrs to complete the very final content.  The pacing feels a bit off and makes the end game feel very tedious. Consesnsus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  I think Nova Lands offers just enough to please fans of this genre.  To be clear, as long as you manage your expectations, I think most ppl will have a good time.  Exploring a bunch of different islands is fun and adds a nice twist to the automation process.  Being able to have bots work for you at the very start of the game is also a very cool touch.  This game may not be able to compete w/ the juggernauts of the genre, but if you can pick it up on sale, I think it's a solid addition to your library.
