_childDocuments_.review: Well hot diggity dawg...The first Souls-Like to really hit that spot, which only Darksouls was able to scratch!FIRST OFF - The Mixed reviews really does this game an injustice! If you are having technical issues with this game ensure Dlss is on only if your graphics card supports it. Also, use windowed borderless that usually helps. The devs within hours released a patch (for fixes) and guide to help players sort their setting to be able to play the game.       (Stats and numbers at the very bottom)In this review I will compare Lords of the Fallen to Darksouls as a baseline (albeit a very high baseline) and I may also refer to *Lords of the Fallen* as *LOTF*Now onto the review: Lords of the Fallen takes what made Darksouls linear game-play awesome and really expands upon it, especially with the Dual-world mechanic! Expect to find awesome and satisfying loot, which aids you in your quest to beat the overarching story, along with worth-while npc encounters allowing you to 'beckon' them for aid in boss encounters.LOTF has a fun and engaging story, which entices you to play more (for good or bad) and a decent multiplayer system which isn't as punishing as Darksouls, as you do not have to pop an 'ember' / have 'humanity' This leads to easier progression, especially when playing Co-op. This does not lead to the game is easy by any means, while being easier than Darksouls, Lords of the Fallen still has challenging game-play that makes you feel a sense of gratification when pushing through areas and when overcoming tough boss battles.While LOTF may not have as smooth / tried and tested animations as Darksouls, it has satisfying combat which is rewarding when mastered paired with a nice button layout for controller which leads to quick time decisions being easily performed. The community while young, seems just like Darksouls (as many people have most likely came from there) The people I have encountered so far have been very helpful, goofy and tolerant leading to a more positive game experience and finally some faith in humanity ^^I could write more, but this game is definitely worth picking up if you want to play a Souls-like which isn't Darksouls. This game is deserving of peoples time, especially when you compare its state to recent triple A releases!!!                Considering the Darksouls franchise is a 10/10 I can confidently give Lords of the Fallen a overall 9/10Remember this is just an opinion something which everyone is entitled to, along with anyone being able to disagree in a respectful manner. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:- fun level designs with very unique/cool areas- amazing graphics with fantastic atmospheres- best looking armor aesthetic and spells in the souls genre- character attributes/leveling makes using melee & spells easy (rather than investing in a wide range of stats)- found myself wanting to replay the game to complete the different endings and try different builds - combat is just plain enjoyable, it feels satisfying to dodge/parry- the best spell UI in any souls game, flows with combat extremely well & easy to use- very active and passionate devs, listen to the community Cons:- game is far from buttery smooth, almost unplayable at launch but has been much better with constant patches - PvP is almost unplayable until net-code is fixed, host is either extremely laggy or I get disconnected before even invading - enemy variety is a huge knock, each area has the same enemies and many are repeated throughout the game- many bosses are very cool & unique but are far too easy. I beat a large portion of the bosses on my first or second try (they have recently buffed bosses with more health/increased dmg so hope they are tougher on future runs)- enemy AI can definitely be better, many times they just feel a bit off- some weapon animations are "floaty" and combat can be too R1 spammy at times Overall:For anyone looking for a difficult souls-like game with fun combat & unique areas/bosses, this will satisfy your needs. _childDocuments_.review: I took the time to beat the game and get one of the endings, the game still doesn't feel quite what it should be.One of the many issues I had was with too many enemies being on screen at all times, early on with 3 or 4 enemies this might feel somewhat manageable, later on zombie enemies are just everywhere along with regular enemy types. This amount of enemies leads to some real and substantial issues with lock on target being a mess and dodging being less precise and more frantic. This issue of enemy density translates more to the Umbral than anything else in my experience, and while I really liked the look of the Umbral, I rarely took more than a minute or two to look around due to the spawning of so many enemies while I was there. I felt as if I shouldn't spend more time than I have to in the Umbral, just to get in to do the puzzle or the secret and then get out ASAP.On dodging, some enemies have attacks that feel way too tracking intensive leading to proactive dodging being a hindrance in some cases. The most egregious of these was the spike headed enemies and their head slam attack, where they have done full 120 degree angles to hit me while slamming their heads down to the ground.To me, one of these worst aspect of this game is the ranged enemies that just pollute areas in positions that will need to either be sprinted to as fast as possible, line of sighted to deal with whatever melee attackers are with them first or using a ranged weapon/spell. There are few times to really engage these scenarios in any meaningful way, moreover, some of these enemies just can't be engaged with unless you used a ranged weapon or spell to engage.The Character creator leaves a lot to be desired, I feel like there aren't very many options that look like real people and no matter how much time I took to created a character I felt dissatisfied with how my character looked. To be blunt, Most of the NPCs look like time went in to how they look and your character will look like you took 5 minutes with a blindfold.Overall, I know the game is getting better and patches are being put out to fix these issues which is fantastic and is commendable to give it this game the time it needs to get better. _childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, clocking in at about 30h played without active multiplayer. It's not as good as most From Software games but feels different enough to not be "samey". If you like souls games, especially those with interesting worlds, you will like this one too. The game isn't perfect (as you'll see below) but fine nonetheless. Even after multiple patches to improve things, there are still some performance issues. I'm running a 3060Ti+13600k@1440p144hz. If possible, I want to avoid upscaling and stay above 60 fps at all times, even if it means lowering some graphics settings. Unfortunately many graphics settings that do give a nice performance boost have significant visual impact and the graphics settings offer very little middleground. I ended up leaving all settings except foliage at HIGH and turning on DLSS with balanced quality and some sharpening. (a recent trend, looking at other UE5 releases). With these settings the game still runs at 70-90fps in most areas, with rare dips below 60 in intense fights or select areas.Some areas have a lot of stutter for no apparent reason though. One example would be the hub area, which stutters terribly for no apparent reason every time I visit.Combat is much slower (felt more like DS2 than recent souls titles) and long recovery animations make stamina much harder to manage than other recent games. This is a good thing, because it makes roll spamming harder and thus learning each enemy more interesting. I have a few grievances with the action queueing on controller though, because I frequently attacked or casted magic twice despite not pressing anything for well over a second at times (presumably due to pressing "twice" as soon as the animation starts). The worst contender for this is the Graveyard Bog spell.I like that they tried making ranged (either bow or magic) available to every build, but unfortunately that came at a design disadvantage for magic-centered builds, which I primarily used (or tried to, for the inital half of the game).The umbral lamp and the ranged tool (e.g. bow or magic catalyst) share the same button but need to be swapped via D-Pad, which made things a little clunky. What's worse is that your character needs to sheathe and unsheathe their equipment every time you try to cast, adding significant delay for casting after rolls. Against most enemies this made using magic (even specialized close range magic) almost not worth using due to the increased risk of eating the followup attack compared to a simple melee attack.There's also the problem of magic feeling useless early on due to low damage for its risk and big resource constraints. It was only after I got an amulet that allowed me to spam umbral magic at the cost of withered health when I really started using magic offensively, after which the game got significantly easier (thanks to a broken build until then)I liked the parry mechanic but it's only really worth using on a few enemies and bosses, which is unfortunate. Getting the stab after breaking the enemy's posture often felt a little awkward though.The umbral realm mechanic makes exploring more interesting, but also more confusing. Some regions are especially hard to keep track of when in the umbral realm, causing me to actually get lost which rarely happens in these kind of games. Unfortunately when you spend a lot of time in umbral (which you kind of want for loot and currency), much of the area's visual design is sacrificed for the umbral look. This gets a little repetitive over the course of the game and makes areas less memorable.I feel like the vestiges (aka bonfires) are placed too sparingly overall. There's a mechanic to place your own seedling in select locations, which sounds nice on paper but isn't really a good idea for NG+0 due to lack of seeds.I had multiple occasions where I went for long durations with no opportunity to rest or level up without backtracking. Then, in stark contrast, other times where I found multiple shortcuts back to the vestige in less than a minute or two at a time. In late game I was showered with seeds, which was the polar opposite in difficulty.On the positive side: In NG+ some vestiges are purposely removed to make you rely on seedlings (and eventually walk more instead of teleporting I assume). This is where the seedling mechanic shines.This might be due to the timing of my playthrough (apparently there was a network issue which was patched now) but I've had very few invaders. Any invaders I had always came when I was deep in umbral, with no resources and almost out of time before the red reaper showed up. I've also had the "fun" of an invader blocking my progression and just waiting out the umbral timer. I couldn't find him until I got killed by the reaper, which was weird.No thoughts on cooperative play yet since I didn't use it on my first playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game in it's current state is a solid 7/10. I hope the devs are paying attention to reviews and feedback still, because this game can really be something very good. Maybe this content roadmap will help with some of the things I had issue with as well.First off, what the game does well:Level design is honestly top notch, I genuinely enjoyed exploring the world and seeing how interconnected everything is. It's also nice that vestiges are spread fairly far apart, making shortcut discovered actually meaningful for a longer period of time, and the temporary vestige system really helps alleviate the potential issues that so few checkpoints/bonfires/whatever would cause (such as a feeling of being very worn down, or having to retrace a long length of area after dying). There isn't really any solid critique i could give other than some of the umbral flowerbed placements are simply silly. (For example, giving the player a flowerbed after a boss but there is a permanent vestige right ahead with ZERO enemies or danger in between them). If they continue this trend of interconnected levels, then the dlcs will probably also be very good. I personally hope they add more interconnected areas, that bridge into the base game world, making even more ways to go through the game (more instances where you could obtain a key very early and skip half the game lol).Progression and viability is an all time high. I really enjoyed seeing a build come together, and the fact that every weapon type seems viable and fun to use, which with souls games, usually ranged options like bows/crossbows tend to struggle. It was nice to clear entire levels with just the bow, and even bow most bosses to death. The rune system and even some of the umbral eyes are very satisfying to obtain and mess around with. I really hope they expand on the rune system, maybe allowing for armor pieces and ranged weapoins/spell tools to also have them. Also maybe give armor passive effects as well.The Umbral in general is something I enjoyed quite a bit in my playthrough, they way it looks, the added danger, and also the vigor multiplier making it so just going through the level gave more xp than killing the boss, which is very rare in a souls like. I personally like any excuse to not just run past enemies. Lastly, I like getting to change armor color, I like most of the enemy design, and I also like that weapon buffs play very nice with holding 2 weapons. I also like that new game plus varies in someway to base. I enjoyed this aspect of Ds2, and I enjoy it here as well, personally I think you guys should change new game plus even more, make it very different from the normal playthrough, though please dial the health back on some enemies lol. Maybe enhanced versions of items drop in new game plus, similar to the enhanced versions of throwing weapons.Things the game didn't do so well plus whatever feedback i may have on it.As i'm sure most of you are aware, the Bosses in this game are just simply pathetic in terms of difficulty, the amount of times ive stumbled across a boss room while at 0 healing items and just won anyway are truly staggering. Maybe i just have a warped perspective because the normal enemies are actually challenging in a lot of encounters? I saw the devs were planning on changing the bosses to make them harder somehow, I look forward to that.Some enemy design is just downright silly, Why does the only enemy in the game that makes the players attacks bounce off if they don't two hand a weapon have to be a DOG?! Nothing even really tells the player about this either, you just hit and bounce off and have no clue why, at least i felt that way. Personally i feel like making them take way less damage if you hit the armor is enough.. now for the other enemies.. Crimson Rector normal enemies absolutely shouldn't be able to heal multiiple times in a row, there should be some sort of cooldown on it, the boss version having it is fine because the player can stop it, where as that isn't true for the normal enemies. Womb of despair enemies should also have a cooldown on spawning enemies, i've been in a room with 2 at once and my frames tanked because they just did the enemy spawn move like 3 times each in the span of a minute. Shrouded Sparrows DO NOT need infinite poise lol, They have high health, and damage, and ambush tactics. They do not also need to be impossible to interrupt or knockdown. Bringer of stillness and scarlet shadow should make less noise when underground, the noise they make drowns out everything else and is kinda annoying.Ravenous fascinator placement is honestly just odd, the whole point of a mimic is to be random and cause player paranoia, but these just happen so often its comical.Pilgrim enemies also don't need full on hyper armor when doing the shove move, I promise it adds nothing to the game lol.Umbral parasites on regular enemies feel strange, I honeslty wish there was a way to make their placement on regular enemies random, make it more chaotic for the player to see coming unless they are already in umbral. Vigor gain, health, and damage of later game enemies need some sort of adjustment, why does the radiant penitent enemy in pilgrims perch grant the same amount of vigor as the ones in Abbey of the hallowed sisters while having like 10 times the health and three times the damage? Just seems very odd. There really does not need to be an enemy around EVERY corner waiting to ambush you lol. The point of an ambush encounter is for it to surprise the player, but if it happens in every single room, it kinda doesn't surprise the player anymore. Also most ranged enemies do not need to be able to snipe the player from a distance so great that you can't even see them, granted the player can do this to the enemies, so its somewhat balanced lol. Item variety is somewhat lacking, all weapons in a class having the same moveset and duel wielding movesets being locked to whatever is in the main hand no matter what really take away from the weapons in the game. Also half the bows and crossbows being actively bad doesn't really help, same goes for casting tools, most of them simply have no purpose. I'd like to see weapons having more interesting movesets, perhaps make the weaker spell tools hybrid, able to cast different sorcery types? Something to make them viable.The player needs 4 ring slots, that or you need to make a real pass over most of the rings in the game, as +1 to a couple of stats or buffing a single resist absolutely is not cutting it with only 2 slots lol.Allow the player to remove upgrade materials from weapons. You've made it pretty clear you don't want materials to be obtained easily, so let players upgrade stuff in the early game freely, and then be able to extract the materials for when they find the weapon they actually want to use.Please stop auto placing consumables on my hotbar on pickup.For what it's worth, these changes don't seem outlandish or difficult to do, and I enjoyed the game as is. I hope people don't see this stuff as making the game easier or whatever. I just list all the feedback I have because I enjoy the rest of it. You guys have a diamond in the rough here. With polish and dedication, you could really really make something great, this will also hype people up for the dlc too ;)

_childDocuments_.review: In an age where the Elden Ring DLC is getting mixed reviews for performance issues and arbitrary difficulty, Lords of the Fallen brings back the nostalgic Souls-Like journey that fans remember and want (since Sony doesn't want to release Bloodborne on PC).To start, I did buy this game on sale, and it went on sale quite often since it too had a rough launch. I didn't actually play the game until all of its road map patches were finished. Once they were and I made time, I played through the game and thoroughly enjoyed it.Performance is great. I didn't have any issues with crashes, stutters, etc. While I do have a 4080, individuals with a 3000 or even 2000 series should still be able to play the game relatively smoothly with good graphics settings considering DLSS and FSR3 is built-in.If it wasn't obvious from the trailers and the fact it uses Unreal Engine, the visuals here are quite impressive.Unlike Elden Ring, which jumped into the Open World fad, LOTF keeps it traditional by making each area more condensed like traditional souls games. This makes it so that each area has more attention to detail and doesn't feel as bland like in Elden Ring. It's a bit more linear then traditional souls games, so while you can get lost exploring a main area, you won't accidentally make way into another main area, especially one that's way outside your level range (there are a few areas that're exceptions to that, but very few).Just like with other Souls games, there's plenty of NPC's you can find, stories to the NPC's that you can do by completing certain tasks, finding secret items to hand them, etc. There's small sections with unique gear and such that're locked that you can go back to in the future to unlock specific doors and such to grab items. The usual stuff. There's also 3 endings to this game; a good, bad and...chaotic neutral? One where you cleanse all the beacons, one where you don't cleanse any of the beacons, and one where you do special side quests and do special tasks for the secret chaotic neutral ending.I can go on about all the stuff it does similar to traditional Souls games, but that'd be unnecessary. If you've played and liked traditional Souls games, you'll like this one.The Differences. There's a Shadow Realm that can be accessed at any point. This might seem like a gimmick but I thought it was implemented very well. It's not something you can ignore the whole game, or maybe use once every 10 hours. This is utilized frequently and seamlessly throughout the entirety of the game and is pretty cool. It can also be used as a weapon to stun enemies by sucking their soul out and such.Ranged abilities, such bows and magic, use ammo. So, you can equip a bow, throwing axes, throwing daggers, etc. and use your ammo to throw/shoot those projectiles, or you can equip a catalyst to cast spells. Obviously, the more powerful the spell, the more ammo slots it takes up. Yes, you can do a projectile/ammo build in this game and it's quite effective.The game is challenging, but not arbitrarily challenging like the complaints I've seen with the Elden Ring DLC where everything is just a meat shield that 1-shots you regardless of level, making progression nearly pointless since you're equivalent to a lvl 1 scrub anyways. The progression between enemies and areas is pretty balanced. Yes, you'll get into some tough boss fights but you can summon NPC's. As long as you're not in the Shadow Realm from your Lantern, you basically have an extra life. If you die, you res in the Shadow Realm, but when you die in the Shadow Realm, you actually die and restart from checkpoint.Speaking of which, Lords of the Fallen has an interesting Bonfire mechanic. You'll have "main" bonfires called "Vestiges", to which there's only about 1 per main area. This kind of sucks when wanting to go back to certain parts in the game, but because there's shortcuts to everything, it's not as bad. However, there's also "secondary" bonfire locations. Basically, you get a consumable that you can use at certain locations around the area where you can place a portable bonfire. You can only have one portable bonfire up at a time, so when you make a new one, the old one vanishes. There's plenty of locations to place a portable bonfire, and the consumable is buyable from a merchant, and also drops from certain types of enemies (some at certain locations are guaranteed drops and can be farmed).I don't know how much space I have left to type this review but overall, this is arguably the best Souls-Like on the market if you're looking for something that's traditional Souls. There will be complaints about this and that, and obviously no one can say they're wrong because fun is subjective, but while this game did have a rough launch that required patches, it's in a very solid state right now and is well worth a try. Sales are pretty frequent on the game due to its rough launch, so if you find the game on sale, you should absolutely 100% buy the game and give it a try.By the way, did I mentioned there's Seamless Co-op? Yep, Elden Ring requires a mod to do it. Lords of the Fallen has seamless Co-op built in (but is limited to only having 1 extra player with you). This means you can rest at bonfires with your buddy, teleport to different areas and the games version of firelink shrine, the whole deal. No fog gates. No disconnects after defeating a boss. If a player dies, they enter a spectating mode until they're res'd at the location they died at. If both players die, it's considered a death and both players remain connected and both players respawn at the nearest bonfire together. A truly and total seamless co-op experience.Oh yeah, there's no consumables when trying to join or invade players. You just go to a bonfire, select the multiplayer option and pick if you want help, want to join, or want to invade someone and you'll be connected with someone in due time for what you selected. You don't need to wait at the bonfire for this. You don't need to be in a specific area either. Now, this does mean that you can't just help people with one specific circumstance all the time, but that's fine in my book since it lets players help connect and help people out faster and with all types of situations. Whenever you want to disconnect form the session, just go to a bonfire and disconnect from there.Anyways, give it a try :)

_childDocuments_.review: Is this the worst Souls-like ever? No it isn't the worst. But it has many quirks that make it so that it may not be for everyone.Pros: 1. Great graphics and beautiful theme and aesthetics.2. Very cool weapon and armour designs, honestly by far some of the best fashion souls out there.3. Pretty cool lore and world building.4. Cool Umbral mechanic.Cons:1. Combat: So this game does not have the worst Souls-like combat ever, but one of my personal biggest gripe is the side step mechanic. To Elaborate, this game tried combining Darksouls/Elden Ring's doge roll, with Blood Borne's side step. This makes it so that if you want to doge roll, you have to double click the roll button, because if not you will just side step. This has led to many unnecessary deaths, and seriously, why try to fix what isn't broken? (This will be a common trend going forward)2. Unfair Bosses: Some bosses are pretty good, it has a good amount of challenges that feel fair, manageable move sets. But then there are also bosses that feel downright annoying and unfair to deal with. Without trying to spoil too much, there is a boss towards the end of the game who you encounter after killing 2 bosses back to back (so at this point you have attended 2 boss fights back to back), the game throws you this third boss, and his boss arena is literally a 2 by 4 boss arena, and this boss is able to apply damage over time on you, place down explosive mines that can stun lock you, and 90% of the boss fight is getting flashbanged by the explosive mines all while your fighting the camera due to how small the boss arena is.TL;DR: the bosses range from being decent, to downright unfair.3. NG+ (New Game +): So NG+ in souls games is almost a must have. Enemies and bosses get harder and maybe new enemy placement. But this game decided that it wasn't hard enough, so lets basically remove 80% of the Vestiges (Bonfires) by the time the player reaches NG+3. Once again a clear example of "Why fix it when it's not broken?", removing bonfires in NG+ makes the game harder sure, but it makes the game more unfair and players are less likely to explore the maps you have created. Their solution to this issue is to add NG+0, where you basically restart the basic difficulty but with all your stats and gear. This is quite pointless, since by your 3rd NG+0 you will be over leveled for the entire game and all bosses.Summary:Should you buy this game? Unless you have played all other Souls games and played all the significantly better Souls-likes out there (Lies of P, Remnant 1/2, etc.), then no, go play some other souls or souls-like and when your done and you feel like you are willing to spare the money on this game, then sure.

_childDocuments_.review: The shader pre-compilation screen apparently does the bare minimum, because I had shader compilation stutters in the main menu for about 10 minutes. After that, I had two crashes to desktop within the first two hours. After that? 100% smooth sailing. Seriously.The game is f-ing heavy, people. The level of detail in the textures and geometry is absolutely insane. It's one of the most detailed games I've ever seen. But with a Ryzen 5600X, 32GB RAM, and a Radeon 6950 XT (and Unreal Engine hates AMD) I am locked at 60-fps with everything on High except Global Illumination and Reflections (having these on High or Ultra enables ray tracing) at 3440x1440. But if you're running an older rig, a slow SSD, or a budget build, yeah, you're going to have a bad time. Same goes for the Steam Deck; I wouldn't even bother trying (though Proton compatibility is so far good and on a Linux desktop it seems to be just fine).Was able to co-op with my friend, and yes, it's annoying that only the host can pick up items or talk to NPCs; Remnant 2 did this better. The rest of the game is a blast and metal AF. Unlike Lies of P, the parry window is actually reasonable. After six or so hours, I'd best describe it as the unholy lovechild of Blasphemous and Dark Souls III, and I'm here for it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game tries so hard to be hard that it forgets to be enjoyable. The game has some interesting ideas buried underneath a mountain of poor design choices that just make it tedious and frustrating to play. Lies of P is a perfect example of what a modern souls-like should be; LOTF is a perfect example of what a modern souls-like should NOT be.I have so many questions I wish I could ask the developers:Why does this game run so poorly on such a wide variaty of systems?Why would you make the first real area a cliff-side platforming section full of enemies that just try and push you off the thin ledge?Why do all of the player's attacks launch them forward several feet, making combat on the cliff-side platforming section nearly impossible?Why do all enemies have near perfect tracking on their attacks, and why do all their attacks also send them flying forward, making spacing irrelevant?Why is there no "explain" button for stats and numbers in the character menu anywhere? Why are new items not highlighted in your inventory so you don't have to search through all of your items to figure out what you just picked up?Why is the game so overpopulated with enemies?Why are enemies either 2 hit trash mobs or health sponges that can kill you in 2 hits?Why are healing items so limited if the intent is for the player to have to fight through dozens and dozens of endlessly respawning enemies to get to the next checkpoint? All that does is force players to run by and not fight.Why are there Vestige Tree points less than 20 seconds away from regular bonfires?Why in 2023 do developers still think players enjoy bosses with un-interactive mechanics and invulnerable phases?Why does this game still use the archaic coop system from 12 years ago when games like Remnant have proven that there are functioning alternatives?Why was the description for the game's coop mechanics on the store page changed? (Saw images from another review)I wish I could enjoy this game, I want love it so badly, but I just can't. I think the weapon design is great; how you can dual wield different weapons and swap between 1H and 2H attacks MID COMBO is awesome! But that's about where my praise ends. The setting is almost painfully boring and generic, I could probably count the amount if unique or interesting things I've seen on one hand. The idea of the Umbral Lamp being something passed down from bearer to bearer is a really cool idea, and the question of whether your character being un-willingly revived by it is a blessing or a curse is an interesting question. On paper the whole Umbral dual dimensions concept is a fantastic idea, but gameplay wise what does it actually do? All it felt like to me was something forcing me to slow down, and make things more time consuming. If the whole dimension was scrapped, I don't think the game would really suffer, you could still use the lamp to reveal hidden things and passages, but having to go back and forth and back and forth is just tedious. If the story and setting are as generic can be, the combat is floaty and feels unfair, the enemies are nothing new and unfun to fight, the bosses are either "a dude with x weapon" or something so large you cant see what they're actually doing, the coop is outdated and not meant for a full playthrough together, and the only unique mechanic doesn't really add anything fun to the gameplay, then my final question is: what is the point of this game? For me the only reason left to play is that I already spent $60 on it, so I may as well try and get my money's worth out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Seamless co-op" is misleading, it's only "seamless" in the sense that you don't get disconnected after clearing an area or killing a boss, but player world progress is still separate, the guest player (because that's what they are) can't pick up world items, open chests, or make any progress in that regard until they go back to play their own world, leading to the inevitable need to switch who's hosting frequently so you can both make meaningful, fun progression on your characters, which is a really outdated and annoying co-op system that isn't really "seamless" at all.Both of us also didn't realise this was the case until we were a ways into our first session, and past the refund window. We were so sure that this wouldn't be the case because of how stupid it is. Like there's no way this is how it works, right? Wrong.Also, you can't move away from the host without being teleported back to them, and for some god forsaken reason you have to actually walk over "Vigor" (Souls, EXP) to pick them up, it's not automatically deposited to your balance. So even if you could split up, you'd have to go retread your partner's footsteps to go and grab the EXP pickups they left for you when they killed enemies. (Edit: Half true, this is the case, but you can apparently use your lantern to vacuum them up from a distance. Still annoying either way)Co-op was the main draw for me, and as it is currently it's an extremely anti-co-op system. They've even since edited the main description for co-op here on the Steam page, as you can see from this Imjur link: I actually had to go back through my Discord channel to find the "before" screenshot, felt like I was being gaslit when I saw how it was changed. Regardless, it's good that they've updated it so that people know what they're getting before they jump in, because I sure as ♥♥♥♥ didn't, even if I probably should've suspected it, looking back, and having played the games this was inspired by. I guess I just didn't think they'd still use the same terrible co-op system, and advertise the co-op as a selling point. Fromsoft games get away with it because you know it's bad going in, but I thought this might've been more like Remnant 2, or even Nioh 2, which have superb co-op despite their obvious inspiration. (Edit: Also see Elden Ring's seamless co-op mod)At this point, I'm either waiting for them to patch it to have proper co-op or for modders to do it, not sure I'll be interested enough to play it on my own when I mainly bought it to play with my brother.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough using a dual-wielding melee build.Performance was fine. Only problem was at the hub where it dropped to about halve and some rare frame drops when many effects were playing at once.Maps look nice and can have interesting interplay with the umbral world mechanic. Sometimes I did get a bit lost as to where to go next. (Thank you Neo for being so patient with me figuring out your gesture hints.)I greatly dislike their approach to enemies that are not primary bosses. First, there are a lot of enemies. You have to check behind every corner and box in case there is yet another enemy ready to ambush you while you try to defeat several dogs and you also get shot at by some ranged dude up a ledge. I chose more than once to just run past everything. Did not make me fall behind in power as I never felt the urge to farm for vigor (souls) or other resources to make some boss easier.Minor bosses are usually just forced battles against enemies you will fight many more time after that, usually as the main threat of a gank-squad. Not that their mini-boss versions don't make use of gank-squads by throwing in some dogs or something into the arena either.Difficulty through mass, not class.Main bosses are more fun to fight even though they tend to be on the easier side of soulslike bosses. I had an issue when fighting the final two bosses where some attack effects (and some effects of my own) did not display. However, as I had encountered similar style attacks with other bosses, it was fairly simple to figure out what was supposed to show and how to avoid it.All together, I do not recommend it for the full AAA price they are asking. My level of enjoyment did not match the price they ask for the playtime I got out of this. It is clear that this game is made with multiple playthroughs in mind. Different builds, endings, ng+ and such. I just don't feel like going through much of the maps encounter design again anytime soon.TLDR: Performance fine; General encounter design bad; Major bosses good but a bit too easy and predictable; Not worth it at full price

_childDocuments_.review: First, I had no performance issues but that is because I have enough power for that. I also didn't experience any crashes.If you never played a souls game before, just buy Dark Souls 3 with all DLC's or Elden Ring and you will have a lot more fun but if you already played the other souls games and want to really play another one sure, go play this game. It makes a lot of fun but it's not quiet the experience as the fromsoft games but still enjoyable.Looks just like Dark Souls at first sight. I like it.Overall it looks very nice but it's just like everything looks quiet the same. In DS3 every region has it's own unique feeling but here I have the feeling that most of the game takes place in the same setting like if 80% of the game would take place in the first area of Elden Ring.I really like this one. Everything is dark and eyes that stares at you are everywhere. Giant dead entities are everywhere in the horizon. Some boring cliff that would just end in darkness is now filled with hands of demons that want to reatch the top or some other dark stuff. It's very nice how the world does change if you go to Ubral and secret passages or bridges might appear.At first I thought that it might get exhausting to always use the lantern and check for secrets in the umbral realm but its makes fun to explore with the lantern. Also using it to stagger bosses or hard enemies is also very usefull. You can also collect souls from a range with it if some enemie dies outside of your range.For me it just feels like DS3. Played with big weapons and it felt the same. There are also now some throwing weapons that do a good amount of damage that lets you kill ranged mobs or one or two of the harder mobs from a safe distance.Yeah, it's pretty easy if you compare it to DS3. I would say that the hardest boss is somewhere in midgame difficulty of DS3.The game doesn't give you bonfires at every corner and sometimes you realy struggle if you want to keep going and risk to lose your souls. There are also places where you can create your own temporary bonfire but those cost you a seed to place. There are also many shortcuts that you can unlock to a previous visited bonfire or seedbed. Overall the spacing is alright but I felt like in DS3 I had way more pressure to find the next bonfire.Yeah, there are many places that just have many enemies on one spot. Its even more if you die the first time and get send to Umbral where its own enemies will also spawn alongside of the regular ones. It's not that bad, you can pull only a few and kill them and go to the next pack of mobs but after dying on the road and doing the same packs of mobs multiple times is pretty exhausting.I can remember nearly all DS3 bosses with name even after all those years but right now I can't even remember the last 3 bosses I did kill in this game. Overall I can only remember the first and some boss midgame. To make an comparison, its like fighting some dungeon bosses in Elden Ring. They are alright but you forgett them really fast and thats also because they are pretty easy and you will be there for just a few tries till you slay the boss.I think there was a single fight with good background music but overall DS3 has waay better boss musicOverall the game is similar to DS in generell with all mechanics and items but there are a few points that are worse.  (Patched) There is also the weapon rune upgrade system. It works and is alright but it doesn't show you the changes in your character sheet. If you equip an rune that "increases your physical damage" or "increases the strenght scaling of your weapon" it won't show that so you need to go to the nearest enemie and damage test your weapon to see the difference. I also find the teleportation view of all your bonfires messy.  They is also a big amount of rings. Thats alright but you have only two ring slots and the "increase your stamina regeneration" ring is like a must have for nearly all builds so you only got one slot left. For amulets its the opposide. I only did find 6 and 4 of them are for magic or range so I did play the whole game with one that just increases the life stat a little bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so let me start by saying this is a fine game. It has many performance issues, but this is on release and by all means I would hope the studio to rectify these issues sooner rather than later. But here is the thing, one of the huge parts of the marketing for this game was the so called "seamless coop". Anyone that has ever played a souls game has hoped there was a better way to play with friends. So, for a lot of us, hearing that this game was going to have seamless coop when it got announced was incredible news. Now either the game devs do not know what most people would consider seamless coop, or they just straight up lied about it, either way is frustrating anyway.Going down the list for things that I would expect "seamless coop" to introduce: - Being able to pick up items without being the host.- Being able to SEE items without being the host.- Being able to talk to npcs without being the host- Being able to buy/upgrade armor and weapons without being the host- Being able to enter the Umbral without being the host, since you know, that's a huge part of playing the game- Being able to see the Umbral through other people's lanterns (This one is not that necessary, but I am making a point) - Being able to rest at the vestiges- Being able to go into the Umbral when dying instead of needing to be revived, again, big part of the game here- Being able to interact with the world in general, like opening a door, lowering a bridge, summoning a companion, etc.- Being able to These are just the ones I could think of from the top of my head, but I could probably come up with a couple more if I took some time. Of course Lords of the Fallen features none of these at this moment, which makes the game play experience quite horrid.It should be said that not everything is bad. The game still allows you to pick up items dropped by enemies, and not having to be re-summoned 50 times every time the non-host dies is an improvement relative to other games, regardless, in the grand scheme of things, this is just not enough. The point I want to make here is that not being the host in this game right now is just not fun. Without being able to interact with anything you will just find yourself following your friend around mindlessly and without really connecting to what is going on. Also not being able to pick up weapons or armor, or even be able to buy and upgrade them, pretty much gives you two options. Either the host does everything for you, which is a hustle, annoying, and outright inconvenient. Or your character will just not progress or improve at all other than being able to increase their stats. With all this out of the way, I really hope they make some serious changes to how this games multiplayer works. It is still a good game, but sadly it is being completely overshadowed by how bad one of the main mechanics of the game functions, which I will remind you, was one of the main selling points. Hopefully we will see a patch sooner than later that will be able to fix at least half of these.

_childDocuments_.review: This gameplay is NOT challenging as Dark Souls / Elden Ring makes it, it is downright annoying.* In every SINGLE corner, there is a bomb-throwing, or ammunition-spraying, or spell-spamming enemy. Can hit you from miles away with guided missile precision. Unbearably annoying, simply bad design.* Enemies are too packed, especially in Umbral. Even in Axiom, the normal world, some enemies can literally come out of thin air (I've test it myself in various locations), instead of hiding somewhere.* There are lore-related Stigmas (Umbral shades) that you can interact  with only in the Umbral world. However, some Stigmas are placed with densely packed enemies that regenerate nonstop, making it nearly impossible to focus on what the Stigma says and the lore.  * A lot of enemies' charged attack can jump miles away, with minimum jump animation; basically, far-away enemies can all of a sudden move before you and hit you.* An Umbral enemy disguises as an normal glowing item, and when you attempt to pick it up, it eats you into the Umbral, and this happens a lot. This is clearly a bad imitation of Dark Souls mimic. In DS, you can tell the mimic from a normal chest by observation (their chains are different) or simply by attacking the chest. In LotF, there is no way to tell the Umbral enemy from a normal item. * Old Umbral Seed disappears after you grow a new one. Savepoints are too far away from each other, drastically reducing the desire for re-exploration.* There is no savepoint even before boss fight, and if you didn't grow a Umbral Seed because you didn't notice it, and died to the boss, then you'll have go all the way from the last savepoint, which is usually miles away.* Normal roll becomes side jump during battle, with the same input, while rolling in battle takes another input... bad design. Also, side jump dodge window is too tight. * Game world design extremely disorienting. Very easy to get lost even if you've been in an area for a long time.* No inventory sorting by obtain time, making it difficult to find newly-obtained items. * When you pick up an item, the UI does not indicate which inventory it gets in. Sometimes it ends in an unexpected category, sometimes you have to go through the entire inventory just to find it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like people get bogged down in what it means to be a "Souls like", and everybody has their own opinion on what that means. For some people it means that bosses are the absolute most important thing, and they MUST be meticulously designed with engaging movesets while providing a significant challenge. For some people balance is everything, for some people it's about exploration, or customization. Fromsoft's action RPGs are multi-faceted and they aren't all equal, with their newer titles being much more boss focused I feel, and that creates a situation where a lot of people that love the same genre disagree pretty vehemently about what the genre is supposed to be like, or what makes a game in that genre actually good.Ultimately, I recommend this game, but it just depends on what you actually want out of this kind of game. Lords of the Fallen has solid customization, pretty good build variety, fun exploration and very pretty areas. On the flip side its boss and enemy design is somewhat lacking, although not terrible, and NPC storylines are convoluted and difficult to follow even for someone that's used to that kind of thing. Performance isn't great, although not nearly as bad as some people have claimed.I'd say if your favorite Souls game is either Demon's Souls, Dark Souls or Dark Souls 2 I think you'd probably have a good time with this game. If you prefer Bloodborne, Elden Ring or Dark Souls 3 then you might not appreciate it as much. Take that for what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a janky, broken mess. By all rights I should give this a negative review, and yet I won't. Why?For SOME indiscernible reason, this game has me hooked. It naturally reminds me of many other games, like Mortal Shell, Dark Souls 2, and Demon's Souls, and I think that the last is the main reason why I love it so much.I miss Demon's Souls. I miss the days when the areas themselves _were_ the boss, and the bosses at the end were just a means to cap off one section of the game. I love exploring in this game because every area is an ant hill with so many little nooks and crannies that loop around to each other and it's super easy to get lost.I've seen complaints about spammy enemy density, and while that may have been the case pre-patch, I can't really say that's the case now. Also for some reason people are complaining about situations where you have one or two ranged enemies attacking you from a distance and then you get ambushed by melee dudes? As if that's not the case in Lies of P (a game which I also recently completed) or Elden Ring, which is basically ambush simulator.But like I said, the game is far from perfect. Its idea of difficulty is sometimes throwing a bunch of small dudes at you and saying "have fun sucker". Some spells are completely broken. You will get annihilated in PvP by something you've never seen before and just be like "Alright."But the exploration, the variety of character builds, FOUR UNLOCKABLE STARTING CLASSES, the ability to restart NG+0, all of these things made me fall in love with the game and I'll just say it, I like it better than Lies of P, but only slightly.If you're the type of person who doesn't value bosses that take 50 tries to complete and instead prefers slow, methodical exploration, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to give this a glowing review. Having played the first lords of the fallen, this is light years better.  I've played every eldensoulsborne since demon souls. This game is not hard rewarding like those games. Its kind of annoying.Artificial difficulty.  This game is not "hard" like a souls/borne. It starts off alright, but then the annoying starts.  You'll like this if you love gank fights 99% of the time. Mob density is off the chart. It seems like this game cant decide if it wants to be a hack and slash or a souls-like.  Its not uncommon to be fighting 10+ npcs at once, with souls style combat and mechanics.  Fromsoft puts enemies around corners for the surprise attack sometimes. This game takes that and injects it with steroids and cocaine to an obscene amount. Expect to get jumped constantly or pushed off ledges to your death, the enemy will of course be immune to damage, while your taking ranged attacks.  The Immune npc's. Can't damage them until you destroy the little parasite thing with your lamp while getting ganked by 7 more at once and dealing with ranged attacks.  I find myself just running past a lot of fights (which I usually never do in souls games) because I just don't want to deal with the cheese. Several armored dogs that takes heavy or a charged heavy attack to break the armor while dealing with immune enemies and ranged attacks, nah.. I'm good, cheesy.  The parry system. Parrying hurts you. It doesn't take 1 or 2 to break stance, it takes like 6 give or take depending on the enemy. At that point you're once shot. There is a rally system you can get your health back by doing damage which usually doesn't work because of cheese ball stuff.  Some of the shortcuts don't even make sense. I remember saying why the hell is this "shortcut" here its meaningless. A lot of time is spent saying where do I go now? what area is next for progression? and its not a good way that's rewarding when you figure it out.  The bosses so far have been a joke. Trying to figure out where to go next is harder than the boss fight itself.I don't know if I would recommend this. Maybe if this is your first souls-like. It seems confused, it obviously wants to be a souls game but it just doesn't seem to get it.   I'll continue to play since I payed. I'm giving this a thumbs down for now. I'll change it if they fix the crashing issue, and possibly do some balancing work. Aside from the constant crashing and my drivers are up to date, It runs.. I'm getting 49.2 fps with slightly modified Ultra settings, But it does not feel like 49.2fps, it feels alright.6950xt5800xsamsung 970 evo plus32g  gskill trident z neo

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Very positive though. Definitely worth a play if you like Soulslike or old-ish games. To explain what I mean:Made me feel like I was playing Soul Reaver 1/2/Legacy of Kain: Defiance back when I was a middle schooler. Level/map design is similar to first Dark Souls - which's a huge plus, because FromSoft went back from that design a bit in later soulsbornes. Everything in this game interconnects, because developers original idea was that you can only setup bonfires/graces/lanterns (called here vestiges) in certain places (and you can have only one at the time), but there's no normal ones, and thus - no warping/teleporting to other ones. Which means there had to be shortcuts going back EVERYWHERE. Last time I felt a map so interconnected I was playing Dark Souls 1. (Don't worry, this is still a thing but in NG+. First run has all the "base" vestiges. Also, they added ability to "restart" your game, but without adding "+" (so vestiges are still there). People aptly call it NG+0. Wish more soulslike did that. I hate NG+1 and only go there for achievements.)Game is gorgeous, but that is given. Originally I thought it was only eyecandy when I saw trailers and thought nothing of it (because first game sucked VERY hard). When I got information another studio is making it, and that game actually looks Warhammer 40Kish or old Diablo-ish (very dark fantasy, heavy armors, crusaders, everyone in blood, gore, and everything is evil, corrupted and/or sacrosanct), and I felt the need for something like that right at this very moment, I just bought it three days after release. No regrets.Lamp is good. Become a moth. Every mechanic or graphics related to it is amazing. Remember, if you stare into abyss, abyss can usually stare back. Or pull you in.Lore got me into conversations with random people on the internet, so it is good enough, even if extremely dark. Yes, there's no "good" ending. Also, of course, like in any soulslike, lore is very incomprehensive.Coop is more seamless than in souls, but still not as seamless as in Remnant. For me it was good compromise. Examples of this good seamlessness: - you don't need signs to summon people, just pop that you want someone random in, invite friend through Steam, or that you want to join someone (or, you know, invade someone) and it happens- no need for summon items or anything (neither host, nor cooper), so you never run out- cooper isn't kicked after every boss - you get rewards and continue travel- if you rest - cooper rests with you and world resets as it normally would- you can both level on vestiges even when he's in your game- when host wants to travel to another vestige, you both get teleported- host travels to Umbral/Axiom? ("Shadow realm" and the material world) cooper travels with you, host holds the reins on that- cooper dies? No problem, rez him for one estus flask, um, Sanguinarix- if host dies, you both respawn on vestige, again, no kick like in souls- no bounds where you both can go - although cooper can't stay somewhere too far from host, or he'll get teleported back to him- host landed in boss room? Cooper gets teleported in- cooper can use vendors and stuff in hosts world (but doesn't "steal" items from his world, if something has limited amount to sell - he's technically buying it from "his own" npc, and when he goes back to his world he can't buy it again). He can't push his questlines, or host ones, just use vendors, upgrading, socketing runes in weapons etc.Now what is not seamless:- cooper can't pick up loot from chests and other world-related stuff (only what drops from enemies)- coopers progress doesn't go forward when he's in someone's world - so you still need to kill boss twice in both worlds if you want to be in same place, if you're playing with a friendNow because this game is more like old games, it's very imbalanced. It's a good thing, half of fun in Morrowind was making something op. Here you can do that as well. Some builds can floor bosses in 30 seconds. It's a good thing, balance is only fun to certain extent.Now the BAD:- Netcode is ♥♥♥♥. I hope they fix it, but they would need to rework it into some kind of Peer2Peer (currently, host confirms everything, so he can R1 you to death if ping is bad, and you can't even dodge away, because his side has to confirm you dodged in time). In coop it's just problematic if you run near each other, in invasions it means everyone uses cheapest most op tactics available.- yeah, the imbalanced thing I said that was good? It's not that fun in invasions unless you have your own trump card. But then again, if you start using one of these, it actually becomes mindless type of fun, like playing old Quake or something, because everyone can oneshot other ones, so it becomes weird type of mindgames :D so not STRAIGHT bad thingOverall, I had fun. Lots of it. And found it worthy enough to do 100% achievements. If they patch it a bit, it might be so, sooo much more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early in the game, but for what I have seen up to now I would recommend the game.The first thing to consider is that the game makes uses of quite a few features from the Unreal Engine 5 that requires a well maintained PC with quite some decent parts if you want to play with anything higher than low/medium. Even so, there are no guaranties that your PC can run it as well as you might want. The requirement between Low and Epic graphics settings are like night and day so don't be surprised if even your PC cannot run it at max settings.My PC is average, but has parts that are extremely well known/updated and I can run this game at low/medium at a steady 60 FPS.For the gameplay, I would say that it's relatively close to your typical Soul-like game, but with some features that seems similar to other similar game and not just about FromSoftware games.First, the riposte is quite a LOT easier than FromSoftware and most enemies have some relatively well noticeable wing-up momentum before they do their attacks. Still, the riposte is not "perfect" as you will still get a small % of the damage dealt which can be recovered if you hit the enemy afterward. Blocking with a shield also have damage seeping through (obviously more than with riposte) and that damage can also be recovered afterward. Getting hit while you got some chipped health (gray bar) makes you loose said health from being recovered. Hence, it's often a game of tag where you try to avoid getting hit, riposte when you feel confident and hit back if you had to block or riposte to recover any health lost. But you're far from immortal as most enemies have less health then the damage they deal meaning getting hit might requires you to hit 1-3 enemies to death to recover all damage received.The game involves a dual-layered world. You can view and interact a minimum in the Umbral world (2nd world) through a projection created by a magical lamp you can point with or rip open a gate and enter it. While in the normal world, you may die once and instantly revive in the Umbral World. So being in the normal world kinda offers you a 2nd chance. While in the Umbral World, your healing is reduced (some part becomes chipped damage that requires you to hit an enemy to recover) and there are respawning enemies everywhere that becomes more numerous as you remain in that world. (In the Umbral world, there are status-like creature everywhere. The longer you stay in that world, the more status becomes enemies as you comes close to them. Moving between areas respawns those status-like thing even if you are not resting.) Some paths are only available within one of the 2 world and there are some minor/simple puzzle. You can only return from the Umbral World by either using a specific kind of corpse (they break after being used once, but respawn when the world is reset) purposely put around, resting at a crusader corpse which is holding a blue lamp, dying in it and returning to the last rest point.If you're used to the Souls-like genre, you'll feel a familiarity in this game when it comes to combat, but the game does have its own kind of balances so don't get the idea that "everything" you might have learned in other games will work in this one. In fact, I highly recommend that you level up until you barely have any souls left and attempt and practice various enemies to master the controls. As for the multiplayer aspect of the game. You have a few choices:• Being a target for BOTH PvE (anyone) and PvP.• Being a target for PvP and with your Steam Friends for PvE. (No random player can join your for PvE, but anyone can invade you)• Joining another player who is an active target for PvE (or a friend).• Joining another player who is an active target for PvP.As you might has guessed, many players are joining (either for PvE or PvP), but only a few opens up the gate to others due to the risks. Also, you cannot joint another player "further" in the story, hence, early on, it's extremely easy to get invaded for PvP, but extremely hard to find another player for PvE.There's also a revenge system which allows a player to find an enemy (as stronger variant) that killed another player for additional souls and specific currency that can be used at some point.And there's an Umbral possession system which allow a monster to be immortal (with blue HP instead of red) for as long as it's possessed by the Umbral spirit hanging around it. You can only remove that spirit by absorbing it with your lamp deployed. It can requires you to strafe around the enemy while avoiding its attacks until you can see the spirit and can absorb it.The game is far from perfect, but it's a good game when you're used to its kind. I would say that, early on, the game does feels a bit restrictive on the customization as over 90% of the equipment you'll find are drop from enemies you keep killing and, for the most part, those equipment might be worse that any starting equipment with a few exception.

More so than any other souls-like game, this one gives me nostalgia for my first playthrough of the original.Some of the negative reviews here are melodramatic, sensationalist nonsense. I can see some reviews complaining about how every boss fight has two phases and they take too long, other reviews complaining about how every boss fight only has a single phase and are too easy.The game is enjoyable, I don't regret purchasing it in the slightest and I'm looking forward to playing through it at least a few more times once I've finished this current playthrough. I'm not going to pretend there isn't some jank, that's been covered enough across the reviews, but for anyone on the fence about the game, don't pay any attention to the people rating it 2.5/10 or something else ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: Cleared through the first 10 bosses or so.  Performance was never an issue.  I've played damn near every souls/soulslike out there.  I want to be challenged, I want to fail, and I want to master a new game.There is nothing to master here except level layout and enemy placement.  The "difficulty" comes in the form of frustrating encounters, not interesting mechanics.  Everything centered around enemy design is terrible.  Aggro distance, placement, density, infinite Umbral respawns, hidden mobs behind every box/corner, locking on, ranged attacks....it's all designed to frustrate you.  It's not impossible, it's not too hard....it just becomes more trouble than it's worth.  Tedious.  Every souls/soulslike has sections or areas like this, but Lords of the Fallen has this as a core design mechanic throughout the entire game.Bosses are fine, if even a bit too easy.This isn't the type of difficulty souls fans are looking for.  We want our time to be respected.  We want to spend our time improving.  We want consistency.  Sekiro is a perfect example of a game that feels unfair at first, but the more you play it, the more you understand and improve.Lords of the Fallen is more of a "Got you, haha!" type of difficulty.  Over and over and over.  Meh.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a Dark Souls game go somewhere else. Dark Souls is hard, however, it is still possible to play and the game play is still enjoyable during the stress of the difficulty. The creators of this game I am pretty sure was jealous of the creators of Dark Souls cause the creators of Dark souls was able to create an extremely difficult game that was still fun, however, the creators of this game did not understand the concept. In this game there is NO sense of advancement when it comes to character progression or strength. Any soul farm found is patched and made useless (Even if it is a legit farm and not glitched). A normal enemy in this game is just as difficult as the bosses. Most boss fights involve you fighting 5+ normal mobs plus the boss or multiple bosses at once (they attack so quickly all you did is roll, get one shot, or both). The map creation was so poorly made that you not only have to fight the enemies but you also have to fight invisible walls that block 90% of your attacks (they would rather patch and fix farming spots than fix their poorly designed map). Enemies are literally programmed to ambush and push you off a cliff, catwalk, ect. Then you have areas where the hardest enemies in the game you have to just run past because it is not possible to fight them all, but you also have to worry about the sniper, ie, holy beam enemies who one shot you every time, or a crossbow enemy who will two shot you (they never miss. If they do miss you were just lucky). When you roll to dodge the blows, beams, crossbows, ect, they will hit you every time. And if your lucky enough to get past all of that (which most of the time will take you an hour if not more. An enemy player will spawn in and 1 shot you, which will start you back to the point you started. Oh also players who invade you are usually max level players. So there is no point in fighting them. 0% player balancing on invasions). I bought this game cause I thought it would bring nostalgia because I have beat Dark Souls 3 at least 20+ times and Elden ring at least 10+ times. But instead all this game has brought was me re-downloading a game that I thought I wouldn't play again because i have beat it so many times. It is pathetic that I have more fun playing a game I have completely memorized from start to finish than playing this game. If you are a Dark Souls fan don't buy this game. Just re-download Dark Souls and have a good time. This game is dog s*&t in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been so excited for this game for a long time.  I love From Software, I've been playing souls-like games for 20+ years.  Some are better than others, and this one starts off strong but quickly gets frustrating and boring.  I'm sure you've heard other say it but in case you haven't, HEXWORKS idea of 'hard' is throwing tons of enemies at you.  After the first area you mostly see recycled enemies, and its not uncommon to have 2-4 mini bosses and a constant wave of peons in every single room/area you walk into.   Its not fun, its just frustrating.  There's not much a a skill ceiling, its basically just forcing you to play one specific way which gets very repetitive quickly.   The second half of the game is like an afterthought, it gets extremely stale quickly.   If you're okay paying full price for 20% of a good game, go ahead and get your money worth out of it, if you want to pay 60$ for 100% of a good game, skip this. _childDocuments_.review: If you like dark souls you'll like this. They have some unique mechanics, specifically the umbral world and the way ranged/magic works is quite well done.Enemy and world design is pretty great so far, albeit I haven't seen a massive variety in overall enemies the gameplay is fun and enjoyable while still being challenging but not frustratingly so.I haven't had significant performance problems but there is a common UE5 stutter issue that I did experience. Turning on GPU scheduling for your PC is the fix for that. Definitely will be playing more than 1 playthrough personally as multiple builds seem viable and challenging in their own merit.
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Liked the game at first, then started to hate it, and now I love it. Everything I disliked about the game has been patched or I learned how the mechanics in this differ from FromSoft/Elden Ring. Really enjoy the character building, combat, and the visuals are stellar. A lot of the issues I thought were tied to bad game design was just me treating this like Elden Ring. Light and Heavy swings behave and function differently (and effectively). The lamp mechanic is useful in both environment puzzles, and combat (including bosses). If you like souls games, and you pick this up, take time to learn how the mechanics of this game are similar and different from previous souls-likes you've played.
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: With a terrible start and horrible optimization, this game somehow manages to get better and better with each patch. Do not expect Elden Ring 2 from this game, because it is not. However, if you are waiting for Elden Ring DLC and would like to play something solid, that tends to be decent at times, but are not eager to play Lies of P, then this is a great choice for you. It still needs to be polished a bit, so I'd wait to buy it for another month, perhaps. But nontheless, would recommend.Sound - 4/5 Combat - 3/5Story - 4/5Graphics - 3/5Mechanics - 5/5Enjoyment - 4/5Co-op - 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: It's great and very underrated. Nowadays it runs pretty flawlessly, I had no crashes and only minor performance hiccups like a bit of stuttering but I fondly remember last year when it came out I had massive performance issues, crashes and two corrupted saves and I still didn't want to quit this game because it's just a unique and fun game. I'd really recommend buying it especially on a sale and try not to get influenced too much by the mixed reviews because I saw many people giving it "not recommended" because it's not exactly like from software games. Of course it's not it does some things better and some worse and that's alright. No action rpg enjoyer should miss out on this gem.Positives:The Visuals are great. The world, armors, weapons all look great and definitely pass the vibe check. I really like the atmosphere. The world feels desolate and on the brink of collapse just like the story describes. Looking out in the distance makes me want to explore even more of this beautiful world. There are those beams of red light which looks great and guides the player to the next objective and change color depending on decisions made throughout the playthrough. Exploration is very rewarding there are a lots of useful items and shortcuts to find and the feeling I got after I figured out the map and looked at the vistas realizing how interconnected the playable area is, was incredible. The umbral parallel world is great adding a lot of mystery to the world and reminds me of the Soul Reaver games.Build variety is incredible you can dual wield any melee weapon, there are many spells useful for melee and ranged builds and ranged combat is very good. Additionally you can upgrade weapons and enhance them with runes. Also there is the lamp that can be upgraded and you can socket umbral eyes into it for even more build variety.Combat is lots of fun. You are incentivized to use melee and ranged which work very well together. Parrying is very rewarding and when depleting the enemies posture you can perform a finisher that does massive damage depending on your weapon. Of course there is lots of room for improvement in a sequel and some problems but overall it is what it's supposed to be which is fun.Sound design is a plus in my book. Weapons sound impactful and meaty. The ding sound after every kill is very rewarding. Ambient sound is good but I'd have liked some exploration music. Some of the music is incredible. Most tracks are are just there to support the vibe of whats happening but there are some really good and memorable tracks like the main menu music, The hub music, the end credit music and my favorite boss music is from the judge cleric fight.Main boss fights were really enjoyable for me except for The Congregator of Flesh . They are not too easy but also not too hard and the difficulty curve throughout the game does not have extreme rises (like in a certain other souls game) and feels balanced overall. Didn't do much pvp but from what I saw in the playthrough I just finished it's great and attacks connect without any latency. Considering the build variety there is lots of fun to be had for pvp fans.You can play the whole game in cross platform co-opUpdates added a boss rush mode and modifiers for new games which should be standard for every future souls like game after finishing the story once. Mid:Artistically character designs are very good but technically they look pretty outdated. It's especially noticeable in cutscenes like the final cutscene in the Adyr ending.Side bosses are just normal enemies you'll encounter later with more health.Enemy variety is alright but two or three more types in latter third would have made it great.Attacks force you to commit but I'd have preferred a possibility for attack canceling with dodges.Bad:The Congregator of Flesh, Mistress of Hounds and Abiding Defenders boss fights were not fun at all.Projectiles hit me through walls or undestroyable objects sometimes.Too many ambushes and enemies hidden behind walls waiting to suprise you. I'm not saying those are bad but there are too many in this game and it gets old.Some enemies have ranged attacks that can target you through walls or around corners.Dogs, abiding defenders enemy type and those umbral bats were not fun to fight in my opinion. Some enemy attacks have too much tracking the most extreme I saw was a umbral big head enemy almost doing a 180° turn in mid air to hit me.I'm looking forward to a third full playthrough to get the umbral ending and a hopefully great performing and polished sequel so it gets the recognition it deserves if it has the same quality as this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As it stands right now, I can't recommend it.Its terribly optimized and runs really really disappointingly poorly.I was really looking forward to it since the art and the game play look really solid. I just didn't realize how absolutely poorly it was going to run on my less than perfect PC.Maybe it'll get patched to a point where it'll run, but for the full price, I can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Lords of the Fallen and I am glad that I decided to give it a chance. I think it has great sound design, level design, and the Umbral Lamp is a really cool mechanic that adds a lot of gameplay variety.My only complaint would be the final "boss fight" for the Radiance ending. I definitely think they need to rework that boss fight as it was very underwhelming. Other than that though, the game ran just fine on my computer and I found the story pretty interesting. I am definitely going to play through this game again to see the other two endings and fight the other boss fights that I got locked out of.9/10 in my book, definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a better-than-average Dark Souls clone, Lords of the Fallen isn't half bad. Ultimately, it's a pretty underwhelming experience that'll hold your attention enough to enjoy. The Umbral mechanic is interesting at first but after awhile becomes a chore. The combat feels pretty good; it's fast-paced and dynamic. However, the enemy mobs are relentless and you'll find yourself sprinting through large portions of the world to avoid them. The bosses vary in quality and difficulty; I was able to beat the second-to-last boss with a crossbow from a distance. In the last quarter of the game it becomes a slog and you'll be ready for the experience to wrap up. Overall, Lords of the Fallen is a fine way to waste your time while avoiding your existential dread.

_childDocuments_.review: In its current state it really is not worth it. A solid 1/3rd of my playtime has been loading the game back up after a crash, trying to connect when being summoned only for it to fail then stick you in loading screen limbo. Maybe 1 in 15 times being summoned works. Pvp is a joke where invaders have an extreme scaling advantage against you and often times will one shot you. If they don't theres a good chance you'll be rubber banding back towards them no matter how much you roll away. The crashes in the middle of boss fights are infuriating especially when it happens multiple times in a row. A good number of questlines will bug out randomly and make it impossible to complete it on that playthrough. Lots of questionable choices like having a max inventory size but not having a storage of any kind which can also create an unplayable save if you can't pick up a key because of the max size. Some will stay there, others will vanish into the ether.Wait until they've had time to work on the game and get things smoothed out because right now this game is crazy frustrating.
