_childDocuments_.review: So,. here we are now with "Lords of the Fallen" ... I hope i can bring light into the lamp.First of all, i really enjoyed D. Souls a lot as well as many "Soulslike" and I also did enjoy the game in the beginning. It does many things right, e.g. the way ammunition works. General Design of Weapons, Armor and Enemies. And allthough the game has its moments and I spent over 100h in it, I still cant reccomend it by heart.Whys that? The main reasosns for that are the following:- At about half of the game you just chase through the levels. Theres just not enough "new" experience. You heve seen most enemies and they just scale up. At this point i had the feeling i just want to run past them because its not fun or rewarding enough to fight them. Everything just gets tedious.- The Level Design is quite linear. Umbral riddles are more than simple and the constantly spawning trash mobs as well as the horrible sound in the Umbral world are plain and simple annoying.- The quest Design simply pisses you off. I am used to the quests in Souls Like. Its ok for me to just look for a guide online to see where in hell the NPC went now. But this here is a joke! E.G. you get rewards after Bosses in form of remains. With this you can buy their Weapons/Armor. If you have beaten the final Boss in Umbral ending and you click one wrong chat reply the NPC whrere you buy this stuff dies.... please repeat the WHOLE game to get your rewards. Oh, the remains dont transfer to NG by the way.- If you are looking for trophies... prepare for massive NG Grinds. At least 3 playthroughs with backup saves are necessary to get them all and at least 2 of them are not fun, just grind. And i guarantee you, you will need more because of the stupid quest design and you miss something.- Even with the latest patch the Bosses are a Joke! Strategy? Stand infront of them and press whatever button you have assigned to any attack. Its so rediculous that the most annoying thing to me in a bossfight was, when they break your poise and you need more time to finish it off.- After about 20 hours of gameplay I also got tired of constantly pulling out your lamp in order to trigger some stupid bridge in Umbral. Die by falling off the cliffs because your lock on mechanism targets some stupid cocoon miles away. Or you just did not run before you try to jump (laugh now... but it will happen :)- PVP was fun at a very basic level but its quite unbalanced. Maybe this changes in the future.-  Build design? Just watch in Youtube. Every build is valid because it just doesent make a big difference. Its more a hack and slash after 20h.So my conclusion here: If you are not a collector/trophy hunter and you are fine with about 20 to 30h simple, straight forward click and Bash "Soulslike" ... go for it. Some of the graphical design is really nice, if you find satisfaction in that.If you are looking for a long term challenging and motivating game, where NG+ is as fun as the first playthrough. If you want to fiddle arround with interesting builds and tactics to finally beat that next stage. If you are motivatet by complex level design an creative riddles. you might look for something else.I hope this helps some of you fellow gamers in their purchasing decission. As often, if you get your hands on a cheap copy for 10-20 bucks, its ok.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Was buggy/crashy at launch, is really good now and well worth a buy.On release, while the gameplay was good, the game overall was buggy as hell and crashed quite often.Now, over a year later the game runs stable and I have not noticed any bugs.Multiplayer works properly now, including cross platform.I get invaded every now and then, and it feels quite fair.If I need help for a boss I can just beckon a lampbearer and get one in less than a minute.The combat is also quite good, its not Fromsoftware levels of good, but I don't expect that.The absolute highlight is the switching between Axiom(normal world) and Umbral(spooky ghost world).It is seamless and the lantern allows you to peer into Umbral while in Axiom. thus allowing you to f.e. walk over an umbral bridge while in axiom.The game has also gotten constant updates over the year and it doesn't look like they're going to stop that any time soon.

I hate puzzles but they had a good balance of easy and difficult for me.Things that impressed:- DS1 vibes with how interconnected the world is.- Lamp mechanic is nice- Ammo mechanic for throwing / mana is nice- Swapping things in combat is nice- Weapon variety / armor variety is nice- You can add radiance imbue to an already radiant weapon, that's nice. _childDocuments_.review: Good game butWhy in god's name would you make a coop game that the coop partner gets 30% less souls and none of the dedicated loot on the ground, like why at that point put the time in to make coop seemless for the entire game? If you're thinking about it for coop just play ds3 you have to do the same backtrack ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Bruh you also don't get achievements for being the coop partner. just a complete clown showOH but don't worry, I assume they did all that to prevent pvp from being unbalanced, but as a coop partner, you'll get buffs to your healing flash items and boss weapons. Well thought out for sureEditing my review to respond to the developer. Couldn't fit it all in a comment. @Jomochiro If that's the case hopefully you take the mixed reviews, many of which stem off the half baked coop system, and update it accordingly. We want to play with our friends from start to finish, and not have to do each zone, each boss, each niche pickup in a weird location, two different times. Or at least let there be some options for us to select, whether we want true coop where progression is shared or the half version you have in now if we care about progressing on our own. One of the most popular mods for elden ring isn't an overhaul mod like Cinders. It's seamless coop. You must acknowledge this since much of the pre release coverage mentioned your take on a coop experience to allow two players to play through with each other without restriction. I also find it very odd. You DO make progress in coop. I HAVE received health recovery upgrade items while in my friends world. You DO get boss weapon drops while in your friends world. It seems like a technical limitation that you couldn't get chests to both players the items, but then again, buying an item in one player's world will also purchase it in yours, so you do have some things bound to character and not world states if that makes sense. Just a really weird set of choices that betrays the "Seamless" goal. Your game is actually really good. But off coop alone I feel lied to, which is why I left a negative.

_childDocuments_.review: Adding a positive review as I've had no performance issues and the game is easily the best soulslike not made by FromSoft themselves. It's well made, has great visuals, the "gimmick" of two worlds is genuinely interesting in multiple ways, the combat is very fluid and has nice weight to it. The bosses I've faced so far have been well made and never felt unfair. The enemy density is quite a bit higher than typical for these types of game but overall, I've enjoyed my time with it a lot and have had no technical or performance issues.However, I do have a pretty beefy PC and a 4090 with frame generation on, so take that as you will.EDIT: Updating this as I've played more: Still no crashes, great performance still, "two worlds" mechanic is still being used a ton to great effect. Honestly, at this point I think if the game was made by FromSoft instead of Hexworks, everybody would be heaping praise on this. It's pretty much Dark Souls 4. My personal favorite game in this genre is Sekiro, but this is easily my second favorite. Parries that are much more manageable in the midst of combat, even without a shield. Everyone has ranged weapons/spells and these have a rechargeable ammo system instead of ammo being consumables. Lots of upgrades, different weapons etc.Probably the biggest complaint I have at the moment is the enemy variety is a bit on the low side. Guy with two axes, Guy with two axes but fire, hunched mage with raidiance, hunched mage with fire, etc. They also sometimes take "mini bosses" and turn them into regular elites after you've faced one.But I also appreciate that the bosses are just the right bit of challenging (imo). Everyone complains about the first boss but I found her to be very similar to many Sekiro bosses so perhaps that's why I thought she was fun to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this is not a very good Soulslike. It's lacking in several areas and writing a whole list would make the review too long but here are some examples:- The Umbral Lamp, which is a main gameplay mechanic is frustrating and boring to use. It's has long animations and using it in combat is awkward and unfun.- Boring and repetitive enemy design. You'll be fighting the same enemies and swarm of blue zombies all game.- Level design is severely lacking. You'll wander around same looking areas, which are made even worse when you enter the Umbral because of the constant blue filter.- Lame sound design. Bad music, bad sounds effects,  the background noise of babies crying in the Umbral World are not creepy, just annoying. These are just a few examples of what makes this game bad. I can't recommend this game to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the equivalent of copying homework. The results are technically the same, but not knowing the logic behind it comes back to get you later. It's a very amateur take on Dark Souls without understanding Dark Souls, so you get something that is superficially equivalent, but under scrutiny breaks down. And in general, it's a pretty frustrating game to play a lot of the time. Not "hard" or challenging, just annoying. (Most bosses are a cakewalk, standard enemies are usually what'll get you) The graphics are nice but performance at launch was awful (could easily test that by running the game on ultra 1440p ray tracing on vs minimum settings and getting the same 20fps in specific areas/situations on a 4070ti) There's some nice systems in place - like armour tincts and so on. But in general, unless you're absolutely starving for a Souls-clone and you've played Elden Ring 200x and already beaten Lies of P, this one's just not worth it. Co-op does, at least, make it a lot more entertaining and easier to overlook the flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Lords of the Fallen

_childDocuments_.review: Ive played Elden ring, Dark souls 1, 2, and 3, along with bloodborne (no way a person playing a souls like who has played dark souls?!?!?!) but this is a Pretty good souls like, combat is good, exploration is fun/rewarding, it is pretty challenging at some points, and the whole umbral system is done very well. It has a lot to do and will take you a while for the first play through (around 46H for me) It even has quests and endings that you can get locked out from, a classic.Exploration is pretty good, there are some points that are odd, like walking from a stormy mountain to a area that is not wet and has pretty much clear skies all within a 2 minute walk. But there are a lot of interesting areas each with there own little secrets/things to uncover, every area has something in umbral which makes it a fun concept that is actually used throughout the whole game.The combat (in terms of PVE) is very fun and feels a lot like souls/elden ring games, but is still different in its own right. there are a lot of weapons to chose from and the throwable/archery system is very well done, especially with the ammo counter VS just having to find your ammo. I havent used magic much but i know that there are a lot of spells to mess around with.  And of course PVP, nothing wrong with the concept just the fact that people will find broken builds to use and run away and cower behind enemies when they are about to die. Not all encounters are like that but its clear that they didnt really do anything to counter that like in dark souls (aside from disabling multiplayer or using a item to keep invaders away temporarily) The co-op is the best ive ever seen in a souls like, you can rest, travel, level up, ect... all at the same vestage while the other player can be there and level up as well. Its also very easy to summon someone in instead of having to lay down a sign or use a password.My biggest issues are that towards the middle of the game and onwards you'll notice that they use a lot of the same enemies, so some more variety would have been nice. It also feels like some of the areas are too short/could have been longer. And (kinda spoiler?) the last boss is very disappointing if you go for the standard ending at least. But overall its a very good souls like, there is a lot to do and im planning on 100% it, im excited to see if they are going to make big DLC for it and what they will do in the future if they do a sequelTLDR: Good souls like, get now

_childDocuments_.review: I've played LoTF for about 40 hours so far (across 3 characters; I like to test different builds at the same time) and I love it. I've played over 100 hours in Elden Ring, so LoTF really scratches that souls like itch. Between the world, art direction, darker gothic style, builds/classes, and lore, I'm having a great time. I know a lot of people playing on PC are having tons of technical/performance problems, but so far on the PS5 I encountered just a few minor things - the game crashed only once, some texture pops here and there - other than that, the game has run smoothly for me (mind you, I did set the graphic to performance, yet the game still looks great - side note: I don't think graphics make or break a game; art direction and style are much more important in the long haul). It did take me a while to get a hang of the combat and controls - at first I was having a lot of trouble (died ~ 20 times to the first few bosses like Pieta and Hushed Saint), maybe because I was trying to brute-force-Elden Ring it - but once it clicked the combat proved satisfying. The magic system is great as well, being locked to the D-pad rather than a weapon item. Weapons have increased move-sets as you upgrade them, which is pretty cool to see, and there's a lot of different builds to experiment with (probably my favorite part of souls likes). A couple of gripes I do have: the lock-on system is schizo and can mess you up when fighting multiple enemies, there's no move canceling so if you hit a button the move is going to follow through no matter what (a huge reason I kept dying at first), and enemy placement needs to be absolutely overhauled (nobody likes fighting melee enemies alongside ranged ones, that's just **** awful). Hexworks and CI are doing a great job communicating with players and pumping out patches to fix problems and fine tune the game - it'll only get better as time goes on. There's little excuse for the performance issues that people had at launch, but I see they're listening and trying to fix it - plus, is it any different than the buggy games that bigger studios with 10x the budget put out (Diablo 4 for one, plus Cyberpunk came out 3 years ago and that has gotten a full redemption arc). If you don't want to buy right now, I'd understand, but definitely come back and try it out after some time - if you enjoy dark fantasy souls likes, LoTF is a solid entry. Its a shame the performance issues on PC have crashed the user scores.

_childDocuments_.review: Hell, what a journey!Lords of the Fallen creates an impressive dark fantasy setting. In my opinion the darkest setting of all souls-like games. You can explore many different locations (including optional ones). These range from castles to snow-covered landscapes to swamps. As is typical of the genre, there are also many hidden shortcuts and bonfire-like checkpoints to discover to get through the world more quickly.The game faithfully captures the essence of Souls-like gameplay and offers a familiar experience.  The parry system feels easier and more accessible than in other souls-like games, which I really liked. There were excellent boss fights with different mechanics that always gave you a chance to win when you were in the rhythm of the fight. For me, the Judge Cleric fight was breathtaking. It took me many attempts but I got into a flow like I haven't had for a long time. This fight was accompanied by excellent background music. The transition between the umbral and real worlds introduces a refreshing layer of depth, enhancing both exploration and combat. I also found setting checkpoints very refreshing, for example, you could set a checkpoint before boss fights and spawn there again and again and again and again and again. However, the most difficult were some of the enemy combos, which were often harder to defeat than some bosses.As usual in souls-like, the narrative is very cryptic. Players have to dive deep into the game to find and understand the lore. Unfortunately, as is usual in this genre, it feels as if you are detached from the story world, which I think is a pity. Despite occasional technical hiccups, the game generally performs very well. Infrequent crashes (3-4 in my run) and minor frame drops (in some areas) are minor inconveniences compared to the overall immersive experience. Lords of the Fallen delivers a gripping dark fantasy experience, rich in atmosphere and challenging gameplay. With its accessible mechanics and intense boss battles, it captures the essence of the souls-like genre. Despite a cryptic narrative and occasional technical glitches, it offers a journey that will leave players breathless and sweaty.See you soon Lampbearer!

_childDocuments_.review: Very similar to Dark Souls 1 but more refined. The feel and how the story is told so far is in the same way. It is hitting that itch. If you want that scratched, you can stop reading here and get the game, else read on.The combat is fast and punishing, yet way more forgiving than any Dark Souls game. Dodging is great and you can survive without needing to be a tank if you are good at it. Parrying is fun and seemed a bit easier but difficult when engaged with multiple enemies. The enemy count is high and that is a rush. When you die you don't die you go into the Umbral world and get a chance to fight your way out. While the normal world doesn't respawn enemies as far as I can tell, the Umbral does and spawns more the longer you are in there until it gets really wild and frighting. The ammo mechanic took a little bit to grow on me, but now I like it and use my bow a lot. I use the game items a lot in general. What are you going to do? Die with potions in your pocket? No way.It does have a few things that feel unfinished, like no back-stab mechanic. Some of the cut scenes look not great with their fluid animation. Look at how Diablo IV does blood, then look at the cut scene for the boss Pieta and you'll see. I didn't know what the blob was for a little bit at first. Locking on makes dodging slow, which was an issue in Dark Souls 1. The stats aren't explained at all, less than Dark Souls. However, they seem to behave similar to Dark Souls 3. So, just assume based on that and guess. Part of the charm is not knowing and discovering. To get the most out of this game get out of the traditional mindset of waiting for the next better weapon, they are all good. They can all be upgraded to be able to do all that you need.  Other than picking weapons that sync with your stat build, use the one that looks cool and has a move set that works for you to land blows and avoid taking damage. It is more about the move set of the weapon that works with you. Yes, pvp you will might see more builds. My pvp experience has been okay, the winner was who was better as spacial awareness and stamina management.Co-op has been fantastic and better than any Souls Game. Just invite by my friends list and done. No fooling around with figuring out where the summoning sign is. Enemy dropped loot is found. Then has lead to some duplicate special gear. However you cannot pickup found items, you'll have to visit that location in your game. Like Dark Souls. I have heard about performance issues. My FPS does not drop below 80 and I am normally above 100+, can't say I have experienced performance issues using auto set for my setting. I haven't bothered to try and tune anything game settings wise yet. Performance is something that depends on how well the computer is maintained and the hardware. Each configuration is going to perform one way or another. That said, the have been insanely responsive in trying to address these issues. So, fantastic to see they are supporting the game, and patched on a FRIDAY hecc who does that? Real cool. There is a lot of loud negative whining people out there about this game which is why I made a review. I appreciate someone who has thought out arguments about what they don't like and open discourse because that improves the game. Whining I do not care for, going off and making insults, threats, venting and exploding their keyboard is annoying. There have been a lot of those type going around.

_childDocuments_.review: So I remember playing the og Lords of the fallen maybe back in 2016 or 2017, which is also around when I got into the whole soulsborne, and soulslike genre of games. And to be honest, the original was just godawful, like jesus. The only thing the game had going for it, was that it was pretty, and the rest just kinda sucked. But how does the reboot hold up? Well i'm about 5 hours in so far, and it's pretty good. The looks ♥♥♥ fantastic, due to Unreal Engine 5, probably one of the best looking games out there. Combat feels great and level design is awesome, same goes for envoirment. The game does feel a lot like DS3 combined with some mechanics from Sekiro and Bloodborne. Which I don't mind, it adds a lot of extra to the combat, which is already very solid to begin with. And the entire lamp and umbra mechanic is prob one of my fav mechanics in any game, and it really adds a lot of cool gameplay moments. Like for example, I got to this place where it was quite obvious that I was to supposed to be able to get across. As there was a ladder that could take me down, and a bit in the distance, there was a ladder I could use to get up on some different platformes. Only problem, at the bottom of the ladder, there was nothing, until I checked umbra. And it was like a different game/world just popped out. So overall, the game is a ton of fun to play.I know performance has been kind of a mixed bag for a lot of people, but atleast for me I haven't seen af single crash, or extreme framerate drop at any point. And no bugs either. I also saw some people, saying you could not skip cutscenes which I believed until I skipped a cutscene at a boss by accident, I had already seen it multiple times, so luckily it didn't matter XDbut it was a nice suprise, cuz I was kinda getting annoyed at it. And just so you know if you play on keyboard, hold E to skip a cutscene.But overall i'd say this is a brilliant soulslike and most likely one of the best ones out there, a great way to scratch that itch for a soulsborne game until Shadow of the Erdtree releases. And I totally recommend it checking it out. Imma give it a solid 8/10.Now go buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: 1. Devs are constantly updating the game, and are actively listening to community feedback.2. The aesthetic and environment are top tier dark fantasy.3. Graphics are great for the most part4. Art designers deserve a raise5. Co-Op is fun 6. Combat is decent, a little floaty, but satisfying for the most part.7. Very generous I-Frames that promote dodge over parry.8. Story/Lore is fine, nothing great but just fine.9. Lots of weapon variety and charater abilities to experiment with.I'm probably missing a few things, but sadly that is where my positives end for the game, at least for now. I do think this game has the potential to be very good if not great. It could of used another year or so of dev time imo. This is my 3rd souls/soulslike game ever, and I generally dont really care for them. Just not my speed, but I see the appeal for them. I may not be the most qualified to give input on this game, but i do have a lot of hours in it so far, and I feel like i can accurately give an unbiased opinion. That being said lets talk about the negatives (buckle up)1. Performance, Im playing with an RTX 4090, Ryzen 7 7800X3D, 64GB DDR5 6000MHZ Ram. Playing this through an LG C2 4k 120HZ OLED TV. I have V-sync on and cap frame rate via RTSS at 116 fps. Its really a mixed bag depending on the area. There are some huge frame drops in some areas, even towards the beginning of the game. Its starts to stabilize after youve been playing for a little, but the frame time graph is never smooth. This indicates there is a huge issue with frame pacing. 99% im able to hold 116 fps at 80% GPU Utilization, so ample amounts of pre-rendered frames. Yet it still suffers. Unless you have a 4090 or 7900XTX, i would turn Reflections and Global Illumination to low or medium. That being said, it is one of the better performing UE5 games that has come out recently.2. Lock On Camera is so bad in this game, it seems to have a hard time choosing the enemy in front of you as well as just not even engaging a lot of the time, please fix asap3. Mob density is infuriating, says its skill issue but the amount of mobs you have to deal with is what i would consider artifical difficulty, and will only steer away new players and even souls vets. They have updated this recently but its still a problem. Ill revisit this if they change it in the future. 4. Bosses, and theres no concise way to put this, but imho the bosses are probably the most disappointing least inspired aspect of this game. Youre so fast, you swing very fast, I-frame galore. The only ones that present a true challenge are the ones that spawn mobs. Going back that artificial difficulty critique. To make things worse they recycle a lot of these bosses into the game world after youve fought them. 5. Enemy variety is very lackluster, same 5 or 6 enemy types throughout the whole game. 6. Level design is not confusing in the traditional sense, However, it can be very annoying going through endless mobs, through umbral for puzzles that are non optional to progress. You might as well just stay in umbral after a certain point, the umbral entity is a pushover anyways. Lack of vestiges, makes it more tedious if you die, (The projectile throwing enemies can go ♥♥♥♥ themselves). You can only plant one vestige seed at a time as well so use wisely.7. Traveling to vestiges from other vestiges or the HUB spot is slightly confusing. Wish they would make it more clear, the order in which these vestiges are in. So always double check the area you are in if youre going back and forth.8. Multiplayer/Raids are a complete ♥♥♥♥ show. Either lagging players or gear imbalances, that make it seem unfair. I could be wrong on that last part but ive yet to have a good raiding experience.9. CO-OP XP gain, is not a huge deal for me personally, but I wouldnt call this a seamless experience. Only the host will get story progression and full XP, if youre joining a buddy just know that before hand. Overall: This game feels more akin to Outriders/Diablo in a sense that there isnt much of a challenge to it. I cant compare it to other From Soft games, but ive heard people say its like DS2. This isnt a terrible game by any means, but it doesnt really do anything amazing. Im fresh off of Lies Of P which is a better game in almost every objective way. So my expectations were pretty high for LOTF. If you subvert your expectations, then youll probably enjoy this game. CO-OP is an awesome addition, part of the reason why i still play it. Im going to leave a negative review but that can change if they keep updating and improving it like they have been. 5/10 from me right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tried and tried and tried again and again and again. I have given it so many chances. I’ve seen it get updated and then tried again after that. I hate this game vehemently. It’s everything I wanted, dark fantasy, two different worlds you can jump between both dripping with thick atmosphere. Some of the most amazing graphical world designs and armours. The best graphics I have seen in gaming yet. That weird theme that plays when everything is getting more tense in the umbral is genius. All this alone deserves 10/10. I even bothered to hop on a website to give this best graphics in the game awards BUT……the level design is atrocious. More accurately the enemy placement. It is awful. Some of the worst enemy placement I have seen in all my gaming years at least since my 8bit gaming days. This game doesn’t just shoot itself several times in the foot, but it goes one step further and then takes a hacksaw to its knees. This is Kaizo Souls level of design. For instance, in one area you can sneak up on an archer and knock it off the perch. It will fall and survive but you have alerted a second archer who is now whistling arrows past your head. Drop-down attempt to kill the 1st archer but now you are joined by a “surprise” axeman who was further below jumping onto your platform and then a “surprise” 3rd archer from behind. Run forward to get more space (which is near the 2nd archer) and then a “surprise” 2nd Axeman guy joins you. You try to manage these guys and then a “surprise” 4th archer is shooting you from a different perch. So you run off and get “surprised” and either pushed off to your doom or have to run by three magic guys. I haven’t even mentioned that if this was in the umbral dimension you would be joined by constantly respawning enemies whose numbers increase the longer you stay in it.I just cannot believe they let the game out like this and supposedly cut the number of enemies, but it still feels swamped. The game eventually makes you so fed up that you end up screaming expletives and start running through areas to the point that you end up forgetting what game you are playing and wonder where all the springs and loop-de-loops have gone.  I have regretted purchases before but never as much as this because this one hurt. The updates gave me hope that they would work it out and turn it into something amazing but sadly I have begun to realise from the posts that the guys behind it are the macho “git gud” types that spoil Dark Souls boards with their “well I could finish X boss with just my fists as weapons”. I rate the developers to some degree. They have fixed a lot but not enough. My heart breaks for those who made the landscape and world design. It feels utterly wasted in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: **EDITED REVIEW BELOW**I wanted a new souls-like but had just finished Lies of P, which imo is one of the best souls-likes I've ever played. This kind of just ain't it. It's very floaty, but honestly I could see myself enjoying it if there was nothing else going at the time.For now, with how overtuned some of it is (So many other reviews go in to this, so I don't feel the need to repeat it but the bullet points: Enemy amounts are too much at points, making it a slog to walk back to places after you've cleared them a couple times already. Withering on a perfect parry with such a good dodge in the game makes it feel somewhat pointless. I don't mind strong mini-bosses or Elites but this sort of goes back to point one with having too many ranged enemies protecting them, I just want to learn the Elite fight, not scale 6 towers to kill the ranged enemies first each time) I'm putting it away for now. NG+, one of my favorite things about souls games, for some reason gets rid of all Vestiges (Bonfires), which while I appreciate a challenge is so not my jam. You built this beautiful world, don't force me to burn out on it. Even an option for this extra challenge would be better because I could see some of my favorite streamers taking it on.The developers seem to be extremely keen and receptive on feedback so far, so this is subject to change over time but as of right now I can't recommend.EDIT: I'm leaving my previous text in as a good example of how much has changed in such a short time with this game. I feel for the devs if they've been working overtime, which it feels like they have because patches  after patches have been landing fixing up so many complaints people had.I can't lie, enemy density/placement is still an issue for me in the late game, not because it's difficult, just because it's tedium. Spammed elites and trash mobs between your next objective not really placed in any interesting way, just placed so you'll be swarmed and have to get out of it. That is my only issue now, however. The movement and combat is still floaty but you get used to it. All other issues I had have been more than fixed up. Very fun game and well deserving of any praise it gets from here on out imo.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent Souls-like that sadly got negatively review-bombed by whiny trolls from the very first hour after release (and many of those reviews are ridiculously stupid).I recommend to check some videos or streams online to get a first impression yourself.People who played and enjoyed other souls-likes before will feel at home from the very beginning. I'll skip the basics and dive right into some points worth mentioning:- The world looks fantastic and the music is excellent. Every region looks completely different, but all of them are well done. I would summarize the general theme as "holy fire, bloody barbed wire, infernal horrors and you're never safe in the dark".- The Umbra system is the prominent feature in this game and it exceeded my expectations. The whole "regular" world got a second layer: the "Umbra" is a marvellous-macabre realm full of eldritch horros, undead and secrets. You can use your lantern to look into the Umbra at any time (watch out, some enemies can pull you in while being close), you have some limited ways to interact through the worlds or you simply switch into the Umbra at any time (getting out is not as easy as getting in). Many places and treasures can only be reached through the Umbra (for example thanks to bridges that don't exist in the regular world). You'll never be completely safe in Umbra and the longer you stay, the worse it gets. The Vigor-multiplier (xp and currency) also rises over time in Umbra, so it's tempting to stay a while.- most game mechanics are "typical souls-like", but this game got a much bigger focus on ranged combat. You'll meet more ranged enemies than you'll be comfortable with and even full-strength-barbarians will use throwing weapons (axes, hammer, poison grenades...) from time to time. Blocking is also quite different in this game (the general idea is: "shields are more efficient for blocking, but you can use any weapon. You absorb some damage and the rest will be "withered damage" which you can convert back after striking enemies; don't get hit though or all withered damage is gone from your life bar).- expect ambushes behind every corner or obstacle. Some enemies are insane sniper. It gets exponentially worse if Umbra is involved. Expect being ambushed in an ambush.- Nagivation can be tricky at times: I probably opened 150 shortcuts in one playthrough (doors, ladders, bridges...) and it happened quite often that I stood at a crossroad and considered my options to explore the area without skipping important or interesting items (for example: exploring left, exploring right or going back to the previous crossroad since there's a whole unexplored way with Adyr-knows-how-many options will follow on that way). A few things in the previously-explored areas also changed after certain events (like killing later bosses).- You got less "healing potions" than you're used to (the insta-heal stuff that refills while resting), but you can buy or farm consumables to refill ammo or slowly regenerate health or mana (which is nice while exploring the world). Your non-magic ranged options (bows, crossbows, throwables) consume 1-3 ammo per shot. You got an ammo bar that resets after resting or you can use ammo bags (consumables) to restore it instantly. - There are 9 starter classes right at the beginning and you can unlock 4 additional ones ingame (each ending unlocks one class and the Dark Crusader is unlocked in a questline - or you can instantly unlock him with the Deluxe Edition). The same rules apply like in any other souls-like: those are just attributes and equipment to start with; you can develop every single class in any way you want. My first playthrough was with the Condemned (the typical masochist choice in those games) to appreciate the first half of the game even more.- The game is FULL of secrests and I don't expect the playerbase to unravel every single last of them. I like it a lot and it's good for replayability, but those who need spoiler and guides for every little step in the game will hate it since you can't google the obscure stuff like "the stick" without knowing that it exists in the first place.- Fashion Souls: you can easily apply or remove colour patterns to your armor pieces. You unlock those themes ingame by picking them up in the world or through a certain vendor in your main base (those ones are unlocked accountwide afterwards).

_childDocuments_.review: This game consistently falls short of greatness. My main criticisms:Vigor farming and leveling are awful and tedious. Enemies give the same amount throughout. I got tired of farming a single enemy type to level and have all but given up on my intended build.Enemy encounters are bland at best, repetitive and obnoxious at worst. Your typical mob group is 2 (or more) harassing melee units, and one or more snipers that do too much damage, and stagger. Be prepared to get stuck on mobs trying to get the sniper. The combat system and flow meshes poorly with this all too common meme.In addition to this the game makes it difficult to fight on your own terms. Luring enemies out is difficult because they get stuck on terrain, frustrating when a sorceress out of your line of sight can drop bombs on you.Should you decide to get this game, be prepared to be fighting the same enemies, or even reskins of the same archetype all throughout. You'll have zombies in every flavor. Classic zombies, Freeze dried zombies, Hickory Smoked Zombies. Same goes for mages. Fire throwing mage, poison throwing mage, frosty mage. There has yet to be a point in this game where i can call even a boss cool or memorable. Some look neat but mechanically boring.There are plenty of small inconveniences in this game that add up enough that really suck the life out of this game. Just when i feel i could start having fun i'm bogged down by poor enemy encounters, janky terrain collision, and frustratingly circuitous level design.I'd hold off for a heavy sale $15-$20 probably. Theres the potential of a good game here, but even now it isnt there.

Trust me, If I can do this game, anyone can. The game play and combat was amazing, the exploration was super fun and top notch. _childDocuments_.review: Includes some minor gameplay spoilersAs a Souls veteran who has gone through them from Demons Souls all the way to the Elden Ring DLC (even DS 2 lol) I went to Lord of the Fallen with an open mind. I didn't really give the critics and the mixed steam review no mind since most of the time I like to establish my own opinion and I knew I wasn't getting a Dark Souls 4 with this one but something unique with the DS concept in mind. And since I got it as a Birthday present from a few friends who knew I loved Soulslike games, I had to give it a shot. I was honestly surprised how it gives me a similar vibe as the Demons Souls remake gameplay and movement vise. I dont know what the performance issues were in the beginning, but for me, everything felt smooth. Is it a masterpiece? No. Is it an utter failure? Hell no. But did give me a good run, challenge, interesting bosses and lore. Hell Yes.Pros: + Combat and movement feels good and smooth like in the Demons Souls remake. + Variety in weapons and movesets (there are a ton)+ Bosses are intersting and unique. What I like is that they sometimes introduce a new "bigger" enemy type as a miniboss first until they place them in the world as regular enemies. Give you a chance to learn their movesets first. + I personally had no performance issues (heard there were quite the few on launch)+ Umbral lamp world(?) is a cool concept and nicely executed. + Health Potions are balanced and dont feel like you have to chug down 20 of them to get full HP if you got for a higher HP build (just a personal preference)+ Loved the atmosphere of the world+ Inferno build feels nuts!+ Armor and gear looks wicked, fitting to the setting+ Much better than its predecessor Cons:- PvP felt clunky. Hit an enemy, seems like he dodged but loses the HP with a 1,5 second delay- Stamina regens veeeery slowly - Enemy variety is a bit low. In the endgame there is almost nothing new. - Parrying feels useless since rolling and sidestepping feels better when the perfect parry just takes a chunk of the stagger bar on enemies (that or I missed something)- Too much running to Umbral and back to a vestige.- Level Design flow feels off at times- Some mechanics like the lamp upgrade fellow and other lads in the main Hub is just confusing and left unexplained+- Basically character has a "Die once you can keep going til you find a Vestige, Umbral Seedbed or die"Overall: Enjoyed the game. Would recommend to any soulslike enjoyer.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a huge fan of souls-borne games and have played most of the ones available and have enjoyed most for what they were. Most recently I played Lies of P and while I personally didn't care for the more weapon focused play style, I did end up enjoying the game play and learning the mechanics, as I usually do with most souls-borne games. This is not how I feel so far with Lords of the Fallen.For starters Co-op, like most people before me have mentioned, the seamless co-op was a huge marketing point along with crossplay. I understand crossplay not working at launch can be expected, but I was still disappointed to see it not available. I was fortunate enough to have one of my friends share it with me on console to experience co-op with them and oh boy were the reviews on here accurate. There is no cross progression, so if playing with friends get used to doing everything twice. Also your partner cannot do anything to interact with your world whatsoever. Not to mention the severely reduced vigor gains for your partner makes playing together seem like a waste of time. The game was advertised to be 'seamless' co-op yet seems exactly the same as any other souls-like. only differences are you can revive dead summons and killing bosses/dying doesn't send them home. The quality and performance drops severely from solo to co-op play, both on console and pc (I tested by open queue with randoms) Which brings me to my next topicPerformance, it's just awful on console. On pc my pc I haven't experienced the severe performance issues as other people have commented, however I am currently using asus tuf 4070ti with amd ryzen 7 5800x3d so do keep that in mind. So far I have played on ultra settings and aside from occasional fps loss when entering a new load area/going from a cave to more open areas, I haven't had any major fps loss or crashes. Now to move on to my real gripe with this gameThe Combat at the start, like many games of its kind, it seemed well paced albeit a little slow if you're more used to dark souls combat but parry times and attack windows seemed very balanced. Once you get to the first real boss you have a really cool fight, though easy, that really shows how the game's combat isn't inherently crap. The very next area you can encounter, Pilgrim's Perch, is just cancerous. I personally don't like platforming in games where you can't jump w/o sprinting but this game takes it to a whole other level with carefully placed little turds hiding from view to push you off the second you walk by. This isn't a problem in itself as many souls like do this gimmick, however it is vastly overused as you progress seeing about 10-15 enemies through a single path whose sole objective is to knock you off the edge, and trying to fight them is already a hazard itself due to the very small/unforgiving platforms. It persists into further areas as well but worse with, as a previous person mentioned, the Kaminoans long lost Legolas clone army spread out in the perfect vantage points with heavy melee fighters to make taking out these duplicate legendary elven archers a chore to kill.Finally the Enemies, so far aren't difficult their movesets are well telegraphed and mostly easy to dodge or block. The problem becomes, especially in umbral, that you start getting faced with 2-3 big tanky units accompanied by 3-5 little turds who are all supported by a Legolas clone on a rooftop/cliff. So no matter who you try to focus the others punish you severely with stagger, making divide and conquer quite difficult. I like fighting large groups of enemies as much as the next souls player but it seems as you get further into the game there are nothing but these meta gaming dnd parties set up to punish the player, which if you do end up dying and being sent to umbral, only get worse with the escalating threat mechanic. (Also to mention there are occasional enemies that are immune and require the umbral lamp to remove immune node that you can get stun-locked from removing)Overall I don't think this is a terrible game just some design choices that seem like the devs were maybe trying too hard or thinking/testing too little when implementing. The umbral lantern mechanic is intuitive and refreshing but at times feels like a bit too much to manage when being swarmed with enemies and a few are immune to damage/stagger preventing you from even engaging. The co-op was not at all what was promised in terms of 'seamless' (also what happened to 3-player?) and more often than not feels more of a burden than help or even fun. Can't recommend anyone purchase this game until they fix co-op and crossplay at the least. 5/10 for now, maybe I'll play some more and come back to change my review once I see the late game

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't completed a full playthrough yet, but so far, it's mediocre. It's worth checking out if you're into Souls-like games, but not at full price. Wait for a sale.I'm going to explain a couple mechanics here so you can better understand if you're unfamiliar with the game.: Certain actions in the game generate wither buildup on you. Wither is a risk/reward mechanic. If you use a shield to block an attack, you take zero damage. However, some of your health bar is converted to wither. If you attack and don't take damage, you revert the withered health into normal health. If you take ANY damage at all, ALL withered hp is consumed and the health is lost.: There are two versions of the world. There is the "light" dimension and the "dark" dimension. The light dimension is essentially easy difficulty, whereas dark is hard mode. When in the dark dimension, you receive greater xp, have to fight more enemies, and may find hidden paths that you could not see in the light dimension. You can freely switch to the dark realm at any time, but doing this withers half of your HP, AND you cannot return to the light dimension until you find a specific object in the world, or reach a checkpoint.- Graphics are great.- Music is pretty good.- The umbral   is a neat idea. More on this below.- Boss design so far has been pretty neat.- Boss Telegraphs are done well. Elden Ring has this issue where they make things artificially harder by making the telegraphs about psyching you out more than anything. This game does not have this issue (so far). - You can freely switch to Umbral mode, but cannot switch back unless reaching a checkpoint. These are few and far between.- Coop is whatever. I could take it or leave it.- There is a bounty hunt mechanic that lets you track down and find enhanced versions of world enemies. It's optional.- Art style is meh.- Performance issues are a problem, but easily fixed by tweaking some graphics settings. This still needs addressed though. - Put an FOV slider in the game. It's 2023. This should be standard.- Almost every encounter has ranged enemies all over the place. This is unfun.- There should not be a grim reaper that comes to kill me when I stack the difficulty multiplier to 3x. Why am I punished for playing well?- You should not be allowed to be dragged into the umbral because an undead slapped you from beyond the grave. Especially if you aren't going to give us any reliable way to get back to the light dimension.- Remove the unending zombie spawns within the Umbral. It's annoying and does not increase the difficulty in a way that feels good.- The voice acting is bad in my opinion.- The story has failed to grab my attention. I couldn't tell you what the story is even about except that you're a person with a cursed lantern.- Most of the weapons feel the same and have weird forward steps baked into the light attack. It makes fighting near ledges feel very awkward.- After I am introduced to a boss, stop playing the intro scene every time I go back to re-attempt it. I understand the scene can be skipped, but I shouldn't even have to do that. It's just inconvenient.- Checkpoints are too far apart.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting example of a game that has a lot of gameplay and quality issues but is ultimately redeemed by its sincerity and attention to detail.If you play souls-likes as a boss-rush, ignore Lords of the Fallen. Its battle mechanics are clunky, and most bosses are unremarkable compared to industry standards (there are couple of cool bossfights though). But if you seek exploration and always crave revealing the secrets of the world you've been brought into, you may enjoy it as I did.The game features a DS1-like map with many "interconnected" (as they say), lore-rich closed areas, which I heavily missed while spending hundreds of hours in the open world of Elden Ring.I especially liked the "umbral realm", which exists inside the regular world and is revealed by using a special lamp. It basically adds a second area with unique enemies and secrets to every location, which spices up the old souls-like exploration formula. Vestiges ("bonfires") in this game are super rare, but you can buy/farm/find "umbral seeds," which allow you to place temporary checkpoints in specific locations. It sounds interesting, but this mechanic is not quite balanced. It somewhat kills the excitement of finding a shortcut to a vestige, but not using seeds feels like self-torture, because the runbacks from vestiges to bosses are dreadfully long.The characters and their quests are the brightest part of the game. The studio didn't have a lot of money for AAA-level voice acting, but they put heart and soul into the work, and interactions with the characters feel very sincere. Their side quests are also enjoyable, requiring attention to detail and reading item descriptions. I tried them without guides and felt extremely happy after making each step. The more non-trivial the task, the more joy you get from completing it.What I still disagree with is that you have to level up your "good" (radiance) and "bad" (inferno) magic stats to read certain item descriptions. Melee classes should have equal access to the lore!My verdict: a good nostalgic game — not flawless, but with amazing potential. A souls-like which was able to capture the "soul" of the genre — a rare case. Anyway, I'll definitely be waiting for the sequel. With the same level of world design and quest design, but with improved battle mechanics and a few more great boss fights, we could have a banger.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It was okDark souls spinoff with a lot of pretty inspired mechanics but it didn't really have the gameplay to make up for obvious graphical and technical errors. I enjoyed the Umbral gimmick and thought a lot of the puzzles designed around it were very smart. It's a good idea to make your puzzle system hinge on sacrificing security, it freshens up the gameplay a lot. The story was alright and I enjoyed a lot of the aesthetic choices with the Umbral. It just happens that the game is very poorly optimized, lags frequently and has a lot of texturing issues. Collision isn't good and a fair few mechanics just don't work, like locking onto soulflay targets being vastly lower priority than locking onto any other enemy in the game. A few areas in the map have holes in structures, or bad hitboxes, or what have you.Classic Dark Souls-type things with very obscure NPC questlines, alternate endings, and even mainline progression. I had to look up how to progress a fair few times because I sequence broke and the game is very unclear about how to move forward. I skipped  The alternate endings are impossible to get without a guide. A lot of the bosses weren't that interestingly designed, and enemy variety is very low. A lot of areas just have re-skins of earlier enemies, and some are variants with new effects, but only rarely. It actually made me feel much worse about the experience once I realized just how few enemy types there were. Level design on the other hand is very strong. Visual design is extremely compelling even if whatever lighting engine they have in unreal couldn't keep up with it. Aesthetically beautiful, it manages to capture eldritch horror in an extremely cool way. Every level felt very fun to explore, especially when you consider the alternate Umbral environments. It was always cool to pass onto Umbral and see the towering corpses and grasping hands and eyes and things. The areas are very visually distinct and fun to move around in at least, which is something. All in all it manages to be a fairly enjoyable experience but falls flat on basically every single major punch it could try to provide the player. A couple of the bosses were pretty cool, but Not worth the $60 price, but worth playing if you get it on a good sale or get it gifted to you for free. The combat feels very good and I think it is genuinely the first game I've ever seen to make throwables fun to use. Honestly I would recommend it just for the chance you find  on your own. Check it out if you need something to scratch your Dark Souls itch, but don't expect to be blown out of the water. You will find yourself thoroughly impressed by the scenery, and enjoying the various aesthetics and hints of story, and then it will be over.

_childDocuments_.review: "We got Dark Souls 3 at home!"Did you ever have one of those days when you wake up on early weekend morning due to loud construction work noises right across the street, and now your whole day feels ruined? Nothing brings joy, as those fools upset your mood?That seems like the exact case for this game :DI mean, I missed all the launch day problems and yatta yatta, grabbed a copy when some patching was already done and here we are. The game, as I write this, holds a Mixed average rating with 61%  overall being positive reviews. So, yeah, tech side must really got people upset and spoiled the mood for the game in general. What do we have in the end (jk, they still have patches, DLCs and other roadmap stuff to implement) - this is a pretty decent soulslike game which I definitely could recommend to both genre fans and random players looking for some new experience. Why? Let's have a closer look. First of all: it's fun. Yes, I mean it. The world in this game is interesting to explore. There are hidden items, hidden quests, characters, shortcuts, special things. Didn't find any illusory walls yet, though won't be surprised if I'm missing something at this point.  There's a cool new mechanic of traversing into Umbral world (the lamp thing in trailer) and that's basically like travelling to limbo. And I saw some folks complain that "Umbral world is a stupid thing and not a great place to explore". Well, no. I think it's fantastic and adds a great jumpscare element to the game. You see - while you're peeking into Umbra - any Umbra creature lurking there can drag you in with just a touch and trust me, there are times and places where you really don't want to be trapped in there, among the shadow lurkers. Fashion souls - Check!Tons and tons of weapons + boss weapons - Check!Invasions and summons - check! (I'm not a PvP person, got 1 kill, got killed couple of times. No lag or something. Looks good). Literally dozens of rings, amulets and other swag - check!There's also a rune socketing for stuff - not sure if good, but works fine. Customization - nice. Some of the designs are top notch. Couple of cut scenes presenting your fellow boss enemies are pretty solid nightmare fuel. Also there's a plot about some god dudes who want to smack each other and you're involved, and you have a team of some knights in the castle. Yea. Might read about it later. Not my thing.But of course, since the game is "Dark Souls 3 but from a thrift store" - there are definitely some flaws here and there. First of all - enemy level scaling. Some enemies can be met in various locations through the game and what can be killed with a smack of the sword in location A, will demand 5-6 hits in location B. So, no, enemies are not unique. Especially in Umbral world - they are always the same several types. Yet those are plenty and it's still quite fun. Some weapon scaling leaves a lot of questions. So you have this big arse grand sword that demand 25 Str and 20 Agility (yes, yes. AGILITY). Ok. Fine. I'll put 11 points to Agility. Your game, your balance, your rules. Next thing - you find a cooler grand sword with some awesome stats and such. What do you think? 35 Str? 25 Str and 25 Endurance, maybe? How about 30 Inferno? (Magic user's stat. Wisdom, basically). Why? And then you notice that the weapon, no matter how heavy, quick, big or small it is - demands absolutely random stuff. Want this spiked fist - sure, 9 Agi. This one here, that also a fist weapon? Well, how good are you at juggling/cooking/gardening? As if magic weapons were balanced first and all the rest came in as a addon. Sure, as in any DS game you can stick to even a starting weapon and git gut, yet still strange. Bugs, ants and caterpillars. But I mean - bugs, of course. There's still a plenty. Nothing groundbreaking, yet airwalking enemies, stuck stuff and unreachable drops is like - "when is the next QoL patch, again?". Jumping. Iconical DS jumping is here. In terms of - potato sack and unnecessary platforming, because why not. Yet again - nothing critical, yet some rage time guaranteed. Some folks also complain about boss reuses where bosses become enemies later on, but it's a matter of taste. I pretend that those named bosses are basically elite versions of the mobs. Like Captains, ok? And finally performance issues. Yep, My PC is not considered high end, so had to tune down all the effects and glitter, yet at times the PC makes sounds like it's heading for Mars on those coolers. And the game really wants to be installed on SSD, FYI. Didn't complete the game yet. Didn't try co-op. Having lots of fun.The game is fine. Exploring and fighting are two most satisfying aspects for me. It's not a top tier, but sure is a honorable addition to the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a VERY VERY hesitant recommendation, for a few reasons.To start, this game is like, a 7/10 at best. If it retained the quality of certain sections, I think this game would compete with the souls series easily, but unfortunately about 80% of the game is a complete slog.The Good:First off, the combat. On it's own, it's quite good, I liked it a lot! Weapons feel good to use, sound effects are nice, a good bit faster than something like Elden Ring but I didn't mind that too much. The wither mechanic on block/parried moves is fine, though I think parries being punished is stupid, as most of the time they don't even lead to direct reward, making parrying bosses risky and mostly pointless.Also, magic and ranged attacks are handled exceptionally well, in a way that is honestly significantly better than the souls series. I didn't play with it enough, but what I did use was convenient, fun, and useful.Armor, rings, weapons, consumables, etc. are all top quality, easily as good as any other soulslike. Same with leveling up, the classic formula, nothing special about it, honestly, as generic for soulslikes as it gets.Level design, excluding enemy placement, is actually very good, near Dark Souls 1 feeling where everything wraps around and connects to itself in a pretty neat way. Overall they're fine to explore, nothing against them on their own, and the graphics and vistas are stunning, though not Elden Ring levels of art direction.Bosses are a VERY mixed bag. At their worst, imagine a boss that is exclusively summoning enemies, some of which can summon or enemies, or are fast dogs that constantly chase you, and is near impossible to beat alone, followed by waves of insanely annoying projectiles, followed by MORE summoning. At its best, I'd say it's as good as some of the higher quality fromsoft bosses, with a couple really good ones. I'd say about 20% good bosses, 30% gimmicks, and 50% I beat without trying because I got sick of the game and started running an ultra greatsword that chunked bosses too easily for my own good.The Bad:The Umbral is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying. It never was fun, the puzzles were easy as hell, and all of the enemies, and I mean ALL of them, were 2/10 or worse. I get what they were going for, and it's cool like, twice, but after that I just got sick of it. The worst part in my opinion is enemies constantly spawning, which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid, I feel like I never have room to breathe.The worst part of the game is enemy placement. Holy ♥♥♥♥, it's like someone looked at 5 minutes of dark souls 1, saw a guy hiding behind a corner, and a guy protecting a dude with ranged attacks, and was like "yeah, soulslike level design is easy". Every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ encounter is tanky melee enemies, trash mobs, and absurdly high damaging ranged enemies behind them. You die in literal milliseconds. It got to the point that I,  a high level character with more health than any other stat, would genuinely only die from slip ups that resulted in me being blendered to death. I never even had a chance to use my heal. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'd say 50% of corners in this game have some variety of dumbass with a 5 ms reaction time WAITING to jump at you, taking half your health instantly and staggering  you for the conveniently placed ranged enemy to vaporize with some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ barrage of garbage.Basically, I want this game to get noticed, and played, and reviewed, so the studio learns, figures out that maybe they shouldn't give hyper aggressive melee enemies an ability that lays traps on the floor, and another ability it immediately triggers that causes fire buildup and does obscene damage, and will still clip you if you mash roll.I'm gonna go play Lies of P now, I hear that's a much better soulslike this one should learn from.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like how this plays.  There is a risk reward thing going on.  You can go into the umbral realm when you die or at will, but you can't leave it at will.  The longer you are there the more enemy spawnpoints appear, and if you walk near them, there is an increasing chance they will spawn.  In addition, your xp multiplier goes up.  As such, if you find a place where you can go back into the regular world from the Umbral, you are free to run around fighting infinitely spawning enemies which is actually pretty fun and increasingly rewarding.  Once it hits 3x xp it becomes nearly impossible to survive without exploits so its better to just ride that line at 2x whenever you find such an area. I really loved this mechanic as it adds another layer of strategy and also rewards co op play a bit more since your kill rate on infinite spawns goes up.  Outside of that, this game plays like dark souls 2 but significantly easier due to the 2 life thing and no soul memory.  The lamp can also be used offensively to rip out souls so you can wail on the enemy while they are helpless or throw them off cliffs.  This is super helpful vs some of the more annoying enemies.  There are also enemies with these little fortifying creatures protecting them so you have to use the lamp to burn them, but that mixes it up so you can't just go wild with no rhyme or reason to your play.  There are also these blisters in various places where you can use the lamp to drain wither damage from them and then the next enemy you hit, you end up getting massively healed.The world design is also pretty good with various paths that are viable in umbral, regular, or a mix of both worlds.  Some people could find it annoying but I like replaying and exploring areas so learning them in both is pretty nice.After you beat the first boss you also unlock vendors that allow you to buy the lion share of various starting equipment items and spells.  There are some exceptions but nothing that really matters.Overall, I got the game I wanted and I'm very pleased.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly the best Souls-like, if you like the original series.Devs are very responsive and are actively working on fixing the technical issues, but I'm lucky and only had a couple of crash over a dozen hours. Otherwise the game runs smoothly for me. I'd give it maybe a couple of weeks for most, if not all technical issues to be fixed.Combat is a mix of old school Souls, with fast movement, a short distance dodge and a longer dodgeroll, and attacks being a commitment, as your character can't be interrupted once an attack animation as started. It also allows you to dualwield any weapons, and you can parry without a shield, as long as you get the timing right.It also adds a couple of game mechanics that add depth to the combat, and a few innovation such as "munitions" for ranged weapons, which are restored at the game's equivalent of the bonfires.The dual world mechanic is also very good, once you get it, and it helps the game emphasis on exploration a lot.Be warned though: the game is definitely more for the people who like their Souls with a lot of exploration, and you'll have to adapt to the fact that you'll regularly be swarmed by a lot of ennemies, although that is quite manageable, since the game definitely gives you the tools to deal with those, namely the ability to switch stances between single hand (or dual wielding) or two hand fighting, with weapons usually having their single handed or dual wielding stance more useful against crowds, and two hand fighting more appropriate for solo targets.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be flat out honest about this: look at the other reviews. Most, if not all, of the negative reviews will feature 1 of 2 things.1. It is a review from when the game launched (and it was a mess, to be sure, and warranted that bad review at the time, hands down)2. They talk about how they're a From Software/Souls fan and compare it to Dark Souls/Elden Ring.Let me be crystal clear: this is not Dark Souls or Elden Ring.  And frankly, despite what people think, it isn't TRYING to be.  Yes, the influence - especially visually - is right there.  And you got the general flow of combat, levels, "bonfires", etc.  It's definitely a "soulslike."  But if you try to approach it and play it like a From Software made game, you're just going to have a bad time with it.Like another Soulslike I enjoyed - Lies of P - Lords of the Fallen asks you to come to it and play it on its terms.  You'll hear talk of clunky controls because people are spamming R1, totally ignoring the tutorial at the start that talks about stance swapping mid combo (you can go seemlessly from 1h to 2h mode mid combo), weave light and heavy attacks, and even use a "Multi" attack (L1+R2 by default) to start a good multi hit combo.  Almost everyone I've watched play just sort of R1 spams and hopes for the best.  That works in a lot of Soulslikes - it doesn't work here.I also see people tend to lean almost exclusively on trying to parry or dodge - you need to accept that both are needed.  Some attacks - even in heavy armor - are best dodged.  Some are best going for a block or parry.  In fact, blocking is INCREDIBLY strong in this game in a lot of situations: blocked attacks turn into white (withered) HP which can be recovered by damaging enemies (but you lose it all if you get hit).  The game wants you to be more aggressive than the average Souls game, but not quite the ferocity of, say, Bloodborne.I'll also see complaints about there being too many enemies at once.  This is a valid complaint in some areas, but often I'll see this complaint and then see people using their weapon in the wrong stance.  Most weapons have a heavier, narrow moveset and a lighter, wider moveset.  It's also OK to not lock on and go for sweeps.  It feels really smooth and rewarding to be hitting someone with a narrow combo and stance switch mid combo to go wide and catch the new challenger as well.Multiplayer is, frankly, better in LotF than it is in any mainline Souls game, or even Elden Ring.  You can summon a friend and they stay with you until they leave or you kick them.  Kill a boss? Keep going.  Die? Bring 'em back with a charge of your Sanguinex (Estus) or at the nearest Vestige (bonfire). No resummoning needed.  You'll need to occasionally swap host to match a bit of progress (while the summon gets loot drops and boss rewards, they can't loot the actual placed world loot), but it just lets both players get to experience the host mechanic of swapping Umbral states and potentially take a different storyline path (while still playing together).The game is also visually nice - especially since the patches - has good overall voice acting, and some interesting locations and lore as well.  It isn't anything super novel, but it's still solid and works.I encourage you to stick out the growing pains and let yourself take LotF on its own merits, instead of wanting it to be Dark Souls 3.5 or 4.  It's a really solid, fun experience in the genre that dares to do things a little differently and while that may not be for everyone, it definitely is worth your time.You can also do a quest to get a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gilded with gold as a fist weapon to pummel people with.  So, there's that.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I'm revising my review as I've sunk more time into the game.My specs: GTX 3090, i7-12k, 32gb ddr4, samsung 980 nvme m2 ssd, windows 10.Summary: If you're a die hard souls fan, just buy it. We all know how to deal with bugs, bad net code, and other stupid ♥♥♥♥- this game is worth it.Note: for online play, there is currently a bug that can potentially reset your stats when the hosts game crashes or you otherwise end up in a weird state of disconnected- this happens in either co-op or pvp. On PC you can mitigate this some by turning off steam cloud save, so you're only saving locally on your PC, then backup your save(s) in C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\LOTF2\Saved. Then if your stats are reset, you can restore your old save by copy/pasting the one you backed up- obviously you lose progress between those 2 saves but it beats having to re-roll (especially if you can't respec).Now, game breaking bug aside: I think this is a really fun, creative, punishing, and well done souls-like. If any of you played the original Demon's Souls on ps3, you'll feel a lot of its inspiration in LOTF. There's also a good bit of inspiration pulled from Bloodborne, which I appreciate. Difficulty:The game feels difficult without being asinine, which something I think late game elden ring suffered from pre-version 1.05. Boss fights so far have felt good and kill me a few times, but once you figure out their mechanics they just feel good- I can't really describe it any other way. Not so hard that it takes you 30 attempts and 15 summons, but also not so easy that you can go in and one-shot them by yourself (unless you're a gigachad). I also appreciate how the space between bosses is almost harder than some of the bosses, it really makes the journey feel more rewarding. Again this is a hard thing to articulate, but once you experience you'll know and hopefully you appreciate it.Graphics:I think the game looks really good, given its UE5. I'm playing with the graphics auto-set to avoid too many frame drops, but I will say this: Elden Ring is a better looking game. It may not be a 1:1 in terms of graphic fidelity, but the world of Elden Ring just "looks" better- THAT BEING SAID, LOTF looks fantastic too.Gameplay:I appreciate that Hexworks had to make their own game to finally give Faith (Radiance)/Strength builds the justice that FromSoft has been withholding from them for decades. Truly you can finally play the lost cleric/paladin with a series of miracles and str/radiance based weapons that completely slap.Co-op:Co-op over PC seems to work really well, my buddy and I have been grouping via steam (Beckon Friend) and we haven't had any issues. It's made for a fun experience, and it's nice not have to constantly re-summon when one of us dies. PVP:My favorite part- invading. So far it's pretty hit or miss. Invasion connection attempts only succeed maybe 1/3 of the time, the other 2/3 the session won't connect.When sessions do connect, the netcode unfortunately doesn't do us any favors. There's a lot of teleporting as the server (host) tries to make sense of what your client is sending- ultimately this results in a lot of warping around, weird hit timings, missed hits, or being hit by something you definitely dodged. So far, it doesn't sound good...until you factor in ONCE you get a connection AND the host has stable internet AND a good connection to you then the PVP is actually hilariously fun. It has the same fast dodge feel that Bloodborne does and right now the time to kill is pretty quick if you're using some insane miracles or a big 2 hander.

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this at full price, relatively speaking. The Umbral world is fantastic and creative, the lamp feels pretty seamless, and the music is good and on-par with AAAs. That's about it. The animations are super janky (try spamming movement and see how silly you look); the character creator is pretty awful; the NPC AI is pretty bad at responding to player behavior (I've killed all bosses so far by having them accidentally get stuck doing something, or teleporting OOB, and just shooting them to death--and Lord help the NPC summons because they can't even pretend to dodge anything); it's nowhere near a polished product; and the game can't decide whether it wants you to speed through its maps or admire the detail given how many swarms of non-stop, beefy-for-no-reason mobs it throws at you. The combat is too fast and spam-heavy to feel rewarding at all, honestly. Parries are made too easy and, in exchange, too tedious. The game should have been released in UE4, and it should have swallowed its pride. The premise has promise, but this execution is full of both "meh" and "why?"It's a disappointment that I couldn't get refunded because of the issues I was trying to fix while the game was open, so I've kept trying to give it more chances, but ugh, it's more of a chore than fun.

_childDocuments_.review: In the attempt to create yet another derivative of the iconic souls template, this game actually manages to emulate many aspects of these games surprisingly well. For one, unoptimized as it may be, the game is breathtakingly beautiful at times with extensively detailed vistas and impressive play of light and dark. But more importantly, these vistas actually mean something, as the many landmarks presented to you early in the game can be actually reached on foot without any artificial teleporting and loading screens. This way, the world of Mournstead actually reaches a level of cohesion that I haven't seen since Dark Souls 1. On the flip side, after around a third of the game, you quickly notice how the developers lacked the assets and time to actually fill their detailed world with a matching level of gameplay variety. Instead of interesting challenges and monsters, each unique to their own area, you mostly see the same enemy types and mini-bosses repeated ad nauseam (kinda like the second half of Elden Ring). This quantity-over-quality approach to encounter design robs the world of its mythos and chips away at the otherwise impressive world design work. Still, I encourage anyone who is fascinated by From Software's worlds to take a look at this, as in this regard, Souls has rarely been better.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great souls like game, but it is plagued with some pretty significant clipping, hitbox issues, and other bugs. I have fallen through the world twice now.  I'm constantly getting stuck on very small objects that lock my character in place. Sometimes I'm getting stuck on nothing and my character is doing the falling animation until I roll. This has several times gotten me killed. As others have mentioned, the enemy plague density is a bit off. When you go into the umbral world you can quickly have 12+ enemies of ontop of you. Depending on the enemy variation, there's a good chance you will get hit at least once, consuming all of your withered health. Even as a two handed character, this is frustrating... I can imagine this being even more frustrating as a dex build. I've swung straight through enemies dozens of times. I've also had enemies hit me several feet away from where the hitbox felt it was. Most of the time this isn't a huge deal, but when you combine it with the clipping issues, and other various bugs, it does start to feel like your starting to fight with the game itself. All that being said, the art design, general character builds, and overall atmosphere of the game is great. Reusing mini bosses as stronger enemies doesn't personally bother me. The overall level design isn't as great as Lies of P for instance, the maps can be very confusing at times. However, I do love the ability to create your own checkpoints with a consumable item, and then making the general bonfires more sparse. Combining this mechanic with the general umbral lamb mechanic, I thought this was an interesting twist to a souls like. The game needs some work, but I'm definitely enjoying it.
