_childDocuments_.review: This is just a "pre-review" before I get further and finisht the game (if I even do).I am a HUGE Souls fan, you can check my profile for the hours I have in Souls games and Souls-Likes. They are my favorite genre. I would not say I am the best at them or any pro but I am definitely a vet and have beaten all previous Souls games (and many of the Souls-Likes).After coming off of the incredible Lies of P - I was excited for this game.Let me say, it looks awesome. The dual world idea is very cool. The combat is passable, albeit not perfect. But there are some really cool concepts here.This game COULD have been great.However,  lots of very poor design choices break this game and make it a tedious mess, instead of fun.The very main issue with the game is they decided to pull a Dark Souls 2 and just add way too many enemies. There are enemies all over, and all of them are dmg sponges, even if you upgrade and level up they take tons of hits. Throw in a bunch of ranged enemies that you have to deal with at the same time and it's just a nightmarish slog, that is not fun at all. It doesn't help that all of these mobs will hit you for about 50-75% of your HP, without fail. No matter what your level is or armor, etc. Unless you just farm for days and put 100 points in Vitality or something.This is in the normal world, move over to the Umbral zone and it's even worse. I get that the Umbral area is supposed to be dark, scary, nerve racking, but the issues is that the main world is also nerve racking and tedious so that when you do hit the Umbral it just makes it even worse. You never have time to breath or get your bearings.I want to love the game, I still have been playing, 15 hours into it, but the further I get the more of this mindless enemy placement and junk. It's not fun, it's tedious.Update:Couple of updates, in NG+ you do not get Vestiges except the Hub area, and ONE placed seed. So in all of NG+ you can teleport to the HUB or your last placed Seed. Another mind boggling design choice.I also want to respond to the developer, because the copy pasted response acting like the player doesn't know how to play a Souls-like is insulting. This genre is my favorite, and while I may not be the best souls player, I am highly capable and understand about carefully traversing the world, doing things like kiting and pulling. The issue is that this world is not even designed in a way to allow that. You can't pull enemies (well sometimes, but rarely, usually there are multiple mob groups near each other and you will pull multiple mobs or hidden mobs). Even if you carefully succeed at kiting and pulling one group of insanely strong mobs, you will likely be out of healing or whatnot and now you are on to the next large group of insanely placed mobs. Various regular mobs + elite mobs (former boss mobs) and then some ranged mobs, all thrown in a chokehold point where you can't do much.I appreciate them being passionate about their game and defending it, but sorry, the game is just poorly designed all around.It has some GREAT visuals, GREAT ideas, but overall it is just trash.

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna start the review off by saying performance issues are at this point completely gone for me. I am playing on 3060ti and Ryzen 2600x at 3440 x 1440, medium settings. Outside of the hub area I maintain a solid 60 fps. Moving on. This is not a game like Elden Ring or Bloodborne. It is more akin to Dark Souls 1 and Dark Souls 2. I mean in the sense that it requires careful play, patience, and planning. If you effectively use your tools, outside of a couple genuinely terrible encounter, everything is doable and pretty fair. Don't forget about your ranged options and soul flay, they are not really optional, they are baked into the experience. Playing in a tactical way is not only beneficial, but extremely engaging when done right. While encounter design can be hit or miss, level design is generally really solid, umbral is such an inspired idea that is baked into the game quite well. Bosses really remind me of Dark Souls 1 and Dark Souls 2 bosses, however you have a combat system that is much faster, more fluid, and fun. This does make many of the boss fights quite easy, although I still enjoy them. I honestly really do recommend the game, if you come into expecting the correct thing and don't fall into the brain dead hive mind that has seemed to form around the game you will end up having a good time. Below I am just going to give some basic ratings on different aspects of the game, mind you this is my personal opinion, however if you have similar tastes it will likely mean something. Exploration - 7.5/10 (Level beg to be explored and you are rewarded well almost every time)Combat - 7.5/10 (weapon movesets, dashing and rolling, and build variety are all fantastic, this is referring to just how the player controls, not actual encounters)Art Direction - 8.5/10 (There are some truly inspired scenes)Encounter Design - 6.5/10 (While I did say using all your tools helps, there are some egregious spots still)Performance - 7/10 (It was a little rough when I started, however patches have greatly improved that)Bosses - 6/10 (This is likely what I am most disappointing with, really none are challenging, and while a few do have some good movesets, it is overshadowed by bosses that are put in front of you, and immediately used for normal enemies 5 minutes later, that is not an exaggeration. Re use can be okay, however it is not done well here. If you are someone who plays these games solely for the bosses, I honestly cant recommend it. if you're looking for stuff like Elden Ring or Ds3 you wont find it here)World Design - 7/10 (I heard some people hyping this up to be like Dark Souls 1, and while it does have some great moments, it never reaches those heights of world design. It is much more akin to a Ds2 or Bloodborne than Ds1. Many shortcuts are given however just as many are undercut by a checkpoint being right there.Soundtrack - 5/10 (It is serviceable and fine)Story - 6/10 (The world and Npc's seem fairly interesting, however it is brought down by some occasional bad voice acting as well a system that blocks off item descriptions unless you have levels in a certain stat. Personally I would have made all item descriptions available to read, and added extra detail with those stats. This would've been a much better system, being both more inclusive, and more subtle.)

_childDocuments_.review: Lords of the Fallen presents a high dark fantasy setting that is visually striking, with a strong emphasis on stylized, bulky armors adorned with elaborate details. This choice creates a distinct and memorable aesthetic, contrasting sharply with the game's alternate world, Umbral—a decayed version filled with skulls and bones, evoking a sense of dread and decay. This artistic duality not only enhances the game's atmosphere but also impacts navigation and combat in unique ways. Thankfully, the game's cutscenes can be skipped, allowing for a smoother flow for those who prefer to stay in the action.However, navigating the game's world isn't particularly enjoyable. The interconnected world is expansive and filled with winding, overlapping pathways that can feel overly stretched to ensure connectivity between areas. This results in extended bouts of sprinting through corridors, attempting to reach the next objective, which can become tedious. The Umbral world, a key mechanic that triggers when a player dies, adds another layer of complexity. While it offers additional platforms and puzzles—such as finding and removing corpses to open doors—the platforming can feel cumbersome. Jumps require precise timing and placement, but the controls for sprinting and jumping don't feel fluid or responsive, adding frustration rather than challenge.Combat in Lords of the Fallen revolves around managing both life and posture meters. Players can perform light and heavy attacks, where heavy attacks can be charged to deal more damage. When an enemy’s posture meter fills, they can be staggered, allowing for a powerful grievous strike. While this sounds engaging on paper, the execution feels lacking. Regular attacks don't have a significant impact, as enemies—especially the larger ones—barely react unless fully staggered. Moreover, the player character's forward lunge with every attack creates a sensation of skating on ice, making it easy to slip off ledges and fall to your death, especially in tight areas.The combat also feels repetitive due to the abundance of weak mobs scattered between checkpoints, which quickly becomes monotonous as they lack variety and depth. The Umbral world further complicates this, introducing additional enemies that spawn when you’re already dealing with the standard mobs. Picking up a "purple soul" after slaying enemies to collect experience and currency felt like an unnecessary step, adding friction to an already flawed system.Despite these issues, there are some redeeming elements. Kicking enemies off ledges, for example, felt consistently satisfying and was arguably the most enjoyable mechanic. Ranged weapons and spells add some variety, with charged attacks and up to four assignable spells that can either damage enemies or provide buffs. Defensively, blocking works differently from similar games. It mitigates a portion of damage, "withering" the life bar, and if you manage to attack soon after blocking, you can recover some health. Properly timing a block can also result in a parry, adding depth to defensive strategies.Enemy variety, or the lack thereof, is another sticking point. Regular enemies with melee weapons don't pose much of a challenge, even in groups, while those with ranged attacks need to be dealt with quickly due to their constant projectile barrages. Elite enemies provide more challenge but require memorization of their movesets, and while the bosses are a technical highlight of the game, they often feel more like a slog than a rewarding experience.Ultimately, while Lords of the Fallen isn't necessarily a bad game, it struggles to stand out in a genre filled with more polished and engaging titles. The core combat and navigation mechanics didn't resonate with me, and the constant repetition in both world design and enemy encounters detracted from the overall experience. However, for players who enjoy exploring interconnected worlds and don't mind the additional complexity of navigating between different realms, there may be some enjoyment to be found here. For others, there are likely better games to invest time in.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it's unfortunately given me little more than frustration, despite my attempts at reading up on what I could and doing all that I could to improve.  I feel that my time playing it has been mostly wasted, but the worst part of all of it is that I could see the makings of a  better game, only to see it squandered by how the development team looked at the Souls games, tried to copy them, but didn't do quite so good a job at separating the wheat from the chaff. I bring up the chaff, because a lot of what people rightly complain about with the Souls games is  stronger here, whereas the things people admire about them are rather thin and few; but let me get the good things out of the way first: the lamp world is an interesting idea, being able to place down checkpoints is a great idea, the heavier weapons being ever so slightly faster than in Dark Souls and its sequels is also okay, I guess.  Unfortunately, the issues are legion: attacks feel untelegraphed or not telegraphed at all, attacks can damage you at times that feel unfair or just plain silly or will not even seem like attacks to begin with, and the obsession with pushing the UE5 engine to its limits with particle effects makes the visuals of the game headache-inducing half the time; so not only can you not see anything on the basis of its insistence on throwing things in your face at every opportunity, but even when you  see things clearly, it doesn't matter often enough.But some of you might be saying "Well, if you liked the Souls games so much and suffered through them, then why can't you just suffer through this one?" to which I'd like to say that the problem is that the Souls games were difficult as a  of their design, not as a priority.  The design of levels and enemies alike in  game seem designed to frustrate and prove a bother more than to entertain; so that even if you know what to expect, what to do, and have done it a dozen times before, the game will  find ways to defeat you  out of any actual cleverness, but because of what ultimately amounts to cheating.  You can be in the middle of a fight, almost winning, and then the game will pull one of three tricks, usually: either it breaks your lock-on, switches lock-on by its own initiative to throw you off, (usually putting your back to the enemy while it's mid-swing) or decides that it just doesn't count when you hit your enemy this time around; the latter cheat being  the most infuriating way that the game makes itself difficult.  What I thought was going on with this latter point at first was that I wasn't close enough, until I remembered that almost every attack has your character  at the enemy; so I started looking closer during these more difficult fights, started testing things without an interest in actually winning, and yes; there are in fact times when an enemy will be neither dodging nor blocking, but you can't actually damage it because it "won't count" for no perceptible reason - except to make the game harder, I guess.I'd like to explain that I'm not prejudiced against soulslikes, but after playing this game to the point where I could take no more, I think Lords of the Fallen is just a copycat that doesn't care to actually  what it's copying.  Dodging is one example: in the Fromsoft Souls games, you dodge upon  the dodge button, as opposed to when you press it; this means that every dodge has you priming it up and releasing it at the right moment, which in a game like this (especially a game like this) means that you don't fumble as much when trying to get out of harm's way.  A different issue is that every single attack causes the player character to grunt or to yell, which is a  idea; and it's easy to take this for granted, but a Fromsoft Souls game, the player character only makes a noise of any sort as to indicate damage, which in turn means that there's  for when you take damage and  have to look up the upper-left of the screen to see if you took damage at a time when milliseconds count.  Also, the sound design for this game is... really not good; it's all one cacophony of grimdark noises that just melt together into a stressful stew.One final thing: this game has all of the dark and none of the soul of Dark Souls.  It's silly to the point that  has a mixture of metal spikes and what appears to be barbed wire on it; with at least one of the starting weapons having barbed wire .  I will argue and continue to argue that the best part of the Souls games wasn't extreme difficulty, wasn't boss battles and  wasn't having to regain your XP after death; but that it was the experience of being on a harrowing journey and the intrigue that comes with it.  The lore of Lords of the Fallen does not interest me one jot, because I can tell that it was written without an ounce of care for the subject matter and basically all it says is "You like dark? Here's some dark," and then proceeds to tell me that the world is bad and that's why spiky hell-demons are evil.  I even made an effort to try taking in the setting and lore of things, but so vapid is the world and story that can't remember anything aside from the main badguy deity being named "A Deer" and the main goodguy deity being named a faux-Latinate form of Oreo.  Maybe there's something more there, and this game might even potentially (for all I know) have a story of such complexity, scale and nuance as to rival that of War and Peace... but I just can't bring myself to care on account of how soulless it is.So contrary to all that I've said, I  recommend the game to the following audience: to those who like Dark Souls for its difficulty and want a game that drops all pretense of being "hard but fair" in favor of just being hard.  Not only is this a game that you play to  have fun, but it's a game that you play in order to not have a sense of accomplishment; I never once felt that I outwitted my foe or rightly persevered in any encounter, only that I just got lucky and that I was setting myself up for deeper frustration.The short of it is that if you liked Dark Souls but  feeling that sense of accomplishment that comes from playing it, then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Getting where not any souls-like ever got. Yes, they actually did it; HexWorks made a fluid movement and combat comparable to dark souls. From a perspective of the player It is hard to understand why we can not get a proper competition to FromSoftware souls monopoly but finally HexWorks were really close. Unfortunately there are a plethora of gimmicks that are really cool on the paper but are not implemented well, they are janky! Umbral lamp allows you to traverse between the land of living and land of the dead. But it was made as slow as possible. Pulling the lamp will slow you to crawl in the middle of the battle. You are supposed to be mindful when and where to pull the lamp. But the end result is that when you see the place where to use the lamp you just use it and run past the enemies to get the item or pull the gimmick to you using the lamp and then get back to the world of the living. The combat itself is fluid but it is also very very limited. There is only 1 slot for right hand weapon which can not be shield, can not be bow or crossbow, can not be catalist. And there is one slot for a left hand weapon, which can also be a shield or other weapon. But you can not have two weapons without going to dual wield stance. That means you must use both of them no matter what. There is no spear with a dagger build or a greatsword with a sword build, the moment you want to equip something except a shield in your left hand, it forces you to dual wield it. The single slot for both hands also means that if you want to change a weapon you have to go to inventory each single time. This drastically limits the amount of builds you can use in the game.Lastly there is this special slot for long range weapons. This includes all bows, crossbows, catalyst and hand-thrown weapons. This also has its own button on the gamepad as the umbral lamp does. This is an example of a janky gimmick. There is zero reason why not to have more weapon slots for right and left hand that would fit all range weapons and the umbral lamp. They fear of copying good mechanics from dark souls - so they rather tried to reinvent the wheel. Throughout the Mournstad you will fight 5-6 types of enemies and their reskins. Every single location has: Grunts: that are just reskins of the grunts from previous locations, they are used in hordes to just quickly populate the area.Meathead: The big enemy guy that is a health sponge and you can just run past him.Annoying range guy: Of course there will always be someone sniping you from across the map.Regular: And lastly every location has these “dudes”, uninspiring hack and slash mobs with little to no variety.The rest are just variations with one or two new things so they can be classified as a new enemy. I thought the Elden ring had no variety but this takes a crown.All of these enemies will be spammed across the area with little to no thought. And if there is a review pointing out this diablo like hordes of enemies and there is a developer responding to this. They will just totally ignore the whole review and say something along how unfortunately it is that you are unprepared enough for this hardcore genre.  PvP has three possibilities that might happen:You will get disconnected.The host is hosting on Mcdonald's wifi, this leads to a truly unforgettable experience.You will one-shot kill the host or he will one-shot kill you. Spoiler! In PvE, seamless co-op is apparently activated for everyone.So if you want to just help people killing bosses. You are stuck in their world even after killing a boss or dying, so each time you have to leave to the main menu and start the game to do this process again. The world and the lore is very fascinating.The developers are patching something every single day.After each patch a thumbnail on easy anticheat loading screen changes, which is pointless but kinda cute.There are PvP and PvE factions so even though the online is terrible I still want those faction rewards.You can see this remnants of the past thanks to the umbrella lamp. You can listen to what happened before you came to the Mournstad. Unfortunately it is extremely hard to pay attention when there is a horde of enemies attacking you.Graphically it is very pleasing.Tons and tons of fancy armors and weapons to collect.Soundtrack totally rocks, from beginning to end it is banger after banger.

_childDocuments_.review: A true souls-like game with stunning graphics, i have had no issues with performance after i locked my FPS to 60 on Ultra Quality.The atmosphere is there, but a world of its own. I loved Elden Rings open world, but going back into the smaller world is really something, it feels better when your progress and you learn the dungeons better. _childDocuments_.review: LotF fits perfectly within the Souls-Borne family and brings with it a few novel tricks of its own that leaves an impression while allowing it to stand ever so slightly apart from the rest. Fans of the genre will feel right at home and will quickly acclimate to the subtle differences. Skyrest as the central hub reminded me fondly of Yharnam and some of the areas were absolutely breathtaking- the thunderstorm and atmosphere were well designed. In typical Souls-fashion, the NPC quest-lines are often indiscernible and entirely miss-able; while the limited lore leaves one only wanting for more. The glaring complaints would be the limited diversity of the over-world enemies and the disjointed / albeit a tad disappointing third act (after Judge Cleric).  Environments 4/5 Limited platforming and interesting use of Axiom v UmbralAesthetics 4.5/5It is grim and bloody, but sets a consistent tone - some of the named boss designs are just lovelyMechanics 3.5/5Plenty of customization with weapon/shield/lantern sockets but certain weapon styles seem favored over others - neat concept for ammo consumptionLore 2.5/5 Could do with a few more in-game items to tell the tale or decrease the radiant / inferno requirements a tiny bit. Likewise, a handful of cutscenes to further enhance the experience would be a welcomed addition.Enemy Diversity 1.75/5 In every area there is an abundance ranged casters/archers, dogs, and a brute with a large weapon - rinse and repeat as the mob only grows in number- Axiom only. Umbra is fine and scary enough as is~

_childDocuments_.review: Lords of the Fallen is a game you just need to soulflay yourself into. Story (7/10)You play as a Dark Crusader enlisted under the Church of Orian out to shut down the welcome home party of one badass demigod before all hell breaks loose once and for all. The instruction is to go around and flip over the 5 night lights to keep evil at bay. It's upto you to chipmunk the rest of the detail throughout the playthrough whilst watching your six at all times. Gameplay (8/10)There are lots of starting classes, with lots of weapons, with lots of armour with lots of enemies and bosses. You have two stances to adjust weapon strikes and formation plus a range slot where you can cast things or shoot things. Defence is about blocking, parrying or dodging, with your Lamp being a handy tool if you want to suck the life out of your enemy temporarily. If it’s too hard or you’re just a little ***** you’ve got options to call in a fellow comrade (P or E) or if you feel like being the bully you can invade their games and sever their hands off to trade in for merch. Checkpoints exist, and they also exist as seeds so you will become a horticulturist in no time. Some bosses will annihilate you, others will fold like you got a royal flush. The game is hard, easy and in between which you can go again with NG+. You can upgrade stats, weapons, lamps, shields, health but not armor. There’s also a world beyond worlds the lamp allows you to passage to and when you die you go there to get beat by even more enemies, there’s one red one that just uh nevermind. Immersion (8/10)It looks distinctive, runs accordingly and connects together like a do the dot. It’s a big boy’s game as it’s made like a spontaneous road trip where you’re out to put the windows down, find some open country road with no navigation whatsoever just a tank of gas. Overall (8/10)The sheer net enjoyment of dying repeatedly, judging these sinners and double handed grand axe long swording everything within a 2m range has been of utmost satisfaction and has made me forget i run an AMD GPU for now. The devs are blazing through a raft of things, they’ve even added multiple options for the camera. I would hereby give this 8 energy efficiency stars out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly great game, I think the reviews being mixed is kinda crazy with how many updates + the passion you can see the devs have put into the game. I think there's definitely some positives and negatives to this game. Tl;dr I rate it 8.5/10, but if you care read further below. >World/Exploration = 9/10 - Super fun to explore, the way the world blends together pretty seamlessly and you manually explore everything you can see really helps with the immersion. The game is exceedingly pretty, if you have a PC that can run it, and transitioning back and forth between the "real" world and the Umbral Realm is a lot of fun. They absolutely nailed the more "grim-dark" aesthetic they were going for, with each area feeling distinctly ruined. However, I'm knocking off a point due to the specs needed to run this decently. I was lucky enough that I was able to upgrade my PC mid play through, and didn't realize how much I was really missing until then. Otherwise, fantastic exploration/world.>Bosses + Souls = 7.5/10 - The bosses throughout the game feel relatively unique from each other, at least within their "faction". From holy wielding knights to a two-headed psychopath, there's a good amount of variation and mechanics. The best part is that once you have a boss remembrance. you aren't limited to getting a single piece of the bosses armory, like most other souls games. In my first play-through I got the entire first bosses armor + weapon and happily used that for 90% of my play-through. The bosses difficulty I think is a rough sticking point for the game however. Many of the bosses have fun or unique mechanics but are too easy, while many of the more difficult bosses are actually just field bosses with some ads thrown in. I think I beat nearly every boss in my first or 2nd try, though the updates recently may have made the bosses harder. >Combat = 8/10 = Each weapon feels weighty and when the hits connect, you feel it connect. Once you get the combat down it feels pretty intuitive, but it does take some time to get used to. Not as good as Lies of P/Sekiro/Bloodborne, think of the combat more similar to Dark Souls 2 pacing. This does lend itself however in the same direction, in that nearly every weapon type & class is viable. Sword & board, dual-wielding daggers, or even greatswords, basically any build is viable. You could even do an archer based on ammo and sit far away. The parrying and magic are other matters entirely, which...>Magic = 11/10 - Technically this is part of combat, but the way the game allows you to re-attune your spells at whim without having to rest, go to a merchant, etc. makes the magic way more fun. I did three playthroughs, each with magic in them, due to how seamless it feels to switch as needed for enemies. Each spell is distinct in its use, and though some are clearly much better than others, nearly every spell feels like it has a use in this game. Combine that with the fact you can re-attune at any time and it really makes the magic the best it's been in any Souls-like. >Parrying = 5/10 - While the parrying in this game can be helpful... at times, it doesn't feel worth it in any way. Parrying in every other Souls-like feels rewarding/worth it, or is a core mechanic i.e Sekiro/Lies of P/etc., while in Lords of the Fallen, it feels more of an after-thought. Even the indicator for an enemies "poise" is just an additional circle around your targeting reticle. It's unfortunate for this game that it came out around the same time as Lies of P, which really cemented what a parry needs to feel like to feel worth it. Mechanically, you still take wither damage (equivalent of Bloodborne rally mechanic) no matter your parry, which you also do if you just.... guard. The parrying window is much more forgiving with shields, though you can parry while dual wielding or two-handing as well. For every praise I give the Magic, the parrying is just... there.>NPCs & Quests = 7/10 - I really enjoyed the quests in this game, at least those that I could find or didn't accidentally break with no warning. The voice acting was done well, and the quest lines provide a lot of lore for different factions, filling in plot points that you wouldn't have otherwise found out, and really tying the world together. Finding different NPC remembrances can show you their true colors, or reveal a key detail for another. There is however a HUGE "but" accompanying this. This game maybe more than any other is unfortunately extremely vague in how it handles certain flags for NPCs, and what you can/can't do for their quests. Not to mention how unclear and unrelated certain objects might be without just googling it, which I don't do personally in my first play-through of a Souls-like. It was only after I beat the game and started googling did I realize I missed 2-3 entire NPCs because of certain triggers happening for going just a 'tiny' bit too far. Not to mention one of those NPCs had several key items that is fantastic for any build that uses magic (which is amazing why gimp it?), and this NPC can be killed accidentally less than halfway into the game. Horrid design that makes you miss a flavorful addition of the game itself, the devs shot themselves in the foot with this methinks.>Multiplayer/Coop = 9/10 - The multiplayer requires no summoning items, no funny gizmos or gadgets. You go to a checkpoint, you invite a friend through Steam or vice-versa, you join their world. Not only that, but you continue to get drops in their world, can buy items from shops/NPCs, and if they have any NG+ modifiers you can benefit from those as well. A fantastic multiplayer helps the game out tremendously if you have a buddy to play with, though be warned if you're playing online that someone might invade, if people are still doing so. I'm knocking off a point since you don't make any progress in your world if you are in theirs, so doing side-by-side play-throughs would be much more difficult if you do those.>Time Investment = 8/10 - This category is heavily dependent on if you like to invest a lot of time into games, or if you like to beat it quickly and move on to the next. If you're a 100% gamer legend, you might be at this one for a while and I would guess somewhere around 200+ hours of time. If you're wanting to do a single play-through, you can do one in 30-40 hours, which isn't too bad if you only want 1. I did all 3 different endings without 100% anything, and was able to do so just at 149 hours. Well, if you've gotten this far I hope you've gotten a good idea of whether or not you'll like the game. Lords of the Fallen is an excellent game, with a few hindrances that besmirch an otherwise great product, and I would recommend it to play either single player, or with a buddy.

_childDocuments_.review: The first souls-like game I can genuinely say that has left a bad taste in my mouth. I'm refusing to finish this game until maybe years later. This game is NOT Dark Souls 2. Because Dark Souls 2 is actually the best game in the Fromsoft Souls' Series, so just because this game is ♥♥♥♥ doesn't mean it's Dark Souls 2. People with no originality just like to hop on the "dark souls 2 bad" boat and use that for any frame of reference for a souls-like game that's actually bad. lol. Anyways, back on the original focus of what this review is about: This game is tedious, annoying, laggy/buggy (and I am not even a person who cares about its bugs too much, but it just adds to the long list of negatives I have for it), co-op mechanics are annoying (for example: you can't run away from the co-op  host without getting FORCIBLY teleported back to them), the bosses are ass and bugged (I had a whole boss focus on my dead co-op partners' corpse for almost the entire duration of the fight), and the combat doesn't even feels satisfying. I can go on, but I am honestly surprised with myself. I initially wanted to give this game a chance but it just got worse and worse for me. After a while of introspection, I thought there might be something wrong WITH ME, maybe I'm getting older and had enough with many games, or maybe I am just bad at this game or something and I'm just getting frustrated. But, I came to the conclusion that this game just SUCKS.The few GOOD things I can say about this game is that: A. It has "great" "triple AAA" graphicsB. The lore/story seems well thought-out I supposeC. Cinematic cutscenes got me interested in the game in the first place (the story and effects in the cutscenes, so pretty much B)D. Umbral mechanic was fun and interesting for the first 2 hours then it got annoying and played out!Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sad "not recommended" for me, even though I started off having a decent enough time, and may come back to finish the game at some point. There's just too many irritants adding up to making the game just feel more like a partly trivial chore than a rewarding challenge. I've just about reached the second beacon as a pure radiant build with the first major boss's weapon, and am running 40 vitality. I don't have much of a desire to go on despite the fact that this build is crushing pretty much everything, and I'll explain why.There are more nitpicks, but the bottom line is that no matter how much I wanted to have fun, I wasn't. The game is just one dreary environment stuffed full of the same boring enemies after another. I can't even remember the last three or four bosses I fought because I killed them on the first attempt, and after each one you're looking down the barrel of wandering in a straight line through a bunch of extremely annoying but ultimately non-threatening chafflings to get to the next one. Once I started checking the wiki to see how much longer this game was going to go on, I knew the gig was up.

_childDocuments_.review: I can see why this game has such mixed reviews now. Its definitely not a bad game... but its definitely also not particularly good either. I feel like the pacing from the start to the second boss was good, and the game felt like it was building into something much more... but the pacing comes to a halt pretty quickly. It also feels like the combat is just.. meh.. Thats the thing about this game. Its just so... meh. Though the graphics are pretty nice and the Umbral realm is pretty cool.. thats another issue tho. I felt like there was almost no reason to ever be in the normal world...Literally all the hidden paths and stuff are in the umbral world so unless you sit there with the lanturn up ,which is pretty annoying beyond using it for one or two small paths,  the entire time you have to be in it anyways. Its not even much harder until the bar maxes out. Plus you get bonus runes. This is the most 6/10 Ive ever played other than maybe starfield. Theres good ideas here and a good game under the surface, but if theyre planning a sequel they need to listen to criticism with thick skin. They CAN make a good game. Theres so much potential.If you still feel like getting it, get it on sale. I feel like its a solid popcorn game to play a few weekends and its worth forming your own opinion. Im only giving a downvote because theres no neutral/medicore option.

_childDocuments_.review: personal Favourite of the year. whilst I couldn't say it is similarly difficult like to elden ring or such for the experienced souls-like players it certainly is just a nice experience with fun mechanics and smooth combat. rocky launch aside from people screaming about their performance issues without really just lowering the graphics til it is more optimised (which it should have been already at a stable build on release but because I have a theory why it wasn't so, I am more forgiving for now personally, I digress) this game runs really well on my quite outdated machine. this isn't just a massive step up from the previous Fallen title this is a completely different feeling game. personally I am in love with everything in this game. I like the challenge since I often feel that the game gives me enough chances to know when I should "git gud"(practice or take my time to learn for those who don't know the meme) with it's life/death mechanic so most of my deaths I feel are my own making and it helps me improve. I guess the death mechanic in my opinion is the best ever by taking a page from Sekiro with a really reliable second chance but it really idiot proofed some of the annoying ways you can die making it give much more relief if you got cheesed by a glitch or something similar.The combat. oh my.georgetakei it feels so good and fluid. switching stances to combo different attack types as well as get the most out of a weapon is so satisfying to play with. the biggest thing I commend is that they have done duel wielding perfectly (IN MY OPINION) the weapons are all really good to use, look at, take pictures with. now this is a really obscure thing to address but I feel need to say how awesome it is. there is good unarmed combat. that's all I need to say as knowing that makes this game so much more interesting. I will be attempting a full unarmed build.the story. it's good. nothing groundbreaking but it feels like a very large world both in scale and lore. I haven't met a character I haven't enjoyed yet. well except one **** but you'll need to play to know possibly whom I speak however I have attachment to a few characters for various reasons. The lore isn't shoved in your face and the main objective of the game is really specific which I do not mind. go to the mcguffins(bells, lordsouls, the princes of madness' cheese) and do thing person who has lamp to stop thinybober or to rekindle the kitchen oven, etc.overall this game is enjoyable and just feels nice to play. the team are really active with troubleshooting the game and we can see their effort to make the game as enjoyable as it can be. as a personal note and massive community wide critique. do not buy the legendary edition unless you are doing it expressly to support the developers. most of the extra content is amazing such as the artbooks and THE MUSIC.... but you can hold off and upgrade later if you so desire. (which I absolutely will be doing since I want more extra content/another game in this IP) so read and research before you buy as sad as it is to say.  P.S. if you do start playing.... don't... don't trust all the pickups..... they..... they really keep getting me with that.

_childDocuments_.review: I dared to believe and was disappointed. The new Lords of the Fallen makes the 2014 game look good in comparison, which is a shame because Hexwork's game has so much going for it on paper.Lords of the Fallen practices no restraint in the area of enemy placement. Too many gank squads, snipers and spongey enemies were placed in environments to generate artificial difficulty. At least 5-7 enemies populate a typical mid-game zone in Lords of the Fallen in a small, Call of Duty-esque funnel of an area.This does not make the game challenging. It is tedious, repetitive and, quite frankly, quickly becomes dull because of that. If I wanted to play Gauntlet, I would play Gauntlet. The movement feels disgusting, floatey/weightless and as if the character moves at 1.5x speed. The fact that attacking an enemy pulls your character towards the enemy in the wildest ways, often around the enemy or on strange paths through the environment, is just a horrible implementation.Jumping feels unstable and it is never quite clear whether your character will successfully make a jump or not.Talking about the enemies: The enemies often end up exactly next to each other due to their primitive AI and execute the same attack simultaneously, giving them an uncanny air of synchronicity. Not only does this make it harder to break them apart, but it also destroys any immersion you had up to this point.The fact that enemies do not use ladders but perform gigantic leaps instead is concerning. Not only is this somewhat unfair because the player does not have this ability, but it also means that enemies will wait for you to ascend a ladder to perform a surefire hit due to the shoddy design. The controls, in general, are unwieldy. The lock-on rarely produces the desired result, and switching targets does not switch to the next closest target as one would expect. This becomes incredibly frustrating when you are in a situation where you want to interact with something via your lamp or get swarmed by enemies and want to take out a priority target - but you can get no lock. Holding the confirmation button sometimes cancels for seemingly no reason.This game needs another 12 months in development/QA.It either needs to be toned down by carefully reviewing enemy placement once again or, alternatively, the game needs to be made even harder so only the baddest of bad dudes will ever attempt to finish it. This game needs permadeath instead of this baby formula, hand-holding, inclusive nonsense we have right now. Make sure that people who backup/restore their save games get severely punished for their sins. And do not even think about making this an option - make it a hard rule. There is also still so much wasted space in each area that could be filled with even more enemies!

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, what a delightful experience it was, basking in the glory of this game! I was on the cusp of composing a laudatory review, overwhelmed by the sheer joy of this gaming journey. Not a single crash to mar my jubilation, as the game danced flawlessly on my 13900K and 4090 powerhouse.But alas, a chorus of ineptitude emerged from those who appear to have a more tenuous grasp on the art of PC maintenance. The peasants have brought forth a proclamation that has cast a shadow upon the game developers and they were brought to their knees on the altar of INEPTITUDE and deactivated DLSS frame generation. And oh, the travesty! The game now stumbles along, significantly less resplendent in its performance.Rest assured, my review will stand like a sentinel, frozen in time, until this issue is righted. For the game, I must confess, is a true masterpiece. Yet, in the midst of my vexation, I also lament the graying out of VSYNC, rendering the sacred rites of Gsync configuration impotent.---- R E D E M P T I O N ------The issue that once plagued my digital existence has been vanquished, thanks to the wise counsel of a few deft launch options. DLSS frame generation, once dormant, now dances with newfound vigor and enthusiasm.As I bask in the glory of this resolution, it is with great pleasure that I hereby transform my review from a somber lament to a resounding hymn of joy.Slobodan Makinenko

_childDocuments_.review: The game needs some serious optimization. So far I really enjoy what I've been able to play of the game. I'm not sure if the issues i'm experiencing are relegated to just me, or if people are experiencing them on a wider scale. I'm currently playing on low graphics, with a Radeon 5700XT graphics card. I've only had 1 crash so far and it was because the game caused my PC to over heat. Was not running Core Temp, because I haven't needed to in a while, but now while I play this game I keep a close eye on it. I also keep getting scrolling black lines throughout my monitor while in certain areas or possibly certain lighting, I haven't been able to determine what it is, but it goes away as soon as my character starts moving, and starts again as soon as I am idle.The combat is good, the world is immersive and beautiful, the enemies I've fought so far have been really cool, but the optimization makes it a hard sell for me. I have played every Souls game, Elden Ring, Nioh, Nioh 2, Wu Long, Bleak Faith, Lies of P, and Mortal Shell on this PC and have never experienced issues like I'm having with LoTF. I have updated my drivers, and still, the issues persist. If you like combat with cool classes, lots of options and items to overcome challenges and an immersive story and world you will probably love this game. I will probably hold off on playing it more until they release an optimization update.

This really should not be listed as a multiplayer game when that is the case as who would want to be the guy in a multiplayer game that misses out on loot and falls behind in progression. _childDocuments_.review: So, time for some actual thoughts on the game itself. I'll keep the original review of me talking about Performance below, mostly for context sake for all those comments of people who are rather mad when someone points out that the problem might possibly be with them, and not the game itself.Is the game perfectly optimized? No, it's not.Is it well optimized, especially compared to other larger releases? Absolutely.Look, if my four year old crapshoot of a PC can run this game in an playable state, then there needs to be some sort of a problem when your 2000+ buck PC cannot. Whether or not this is an anomaly within your hardware, OS, malware or possibly a weird interaction between the game and your PC is something you'll have to figure out yourself and report it to the dev's support.I have a good story about a friend who bought a 2500€ PC once which refused to properly work a few months later due to him disabling any anti virus & visiting shady sites, so i'll always have my doubt when someone says "It cant possibly be my PC!".Anyways, to my thoughts.>The Good<-The game comes close From's Soulborne games in terms of feel, not as refined but very  close. So far different playstyles seem to be all relatively viable. Fast and light builds work  just as well as wearing heavy armor and timely blocking attacks. The wither system prevents  penalty free blocking, and rewards aggressive play. Weapons feel varied, and i have yet to find a type that is ineffective. Even just using your  bare fists is surprisingly effective at removing the faces of the undesired, and you even get to  dropkick enemies off edges with quite the velocity.-Bossfights are fun, and reasonably difficult. Quite a spectacle, too. The music especially for  the first real boss was amazing.-I quite enjoy the Artstyle as well. Anything from weapons and armor, to the design of  monsters is oozing that grimdark gothic feel. Whether it's the thorn and barb covered armors  of the "good guys", or the horrible deformed creatures from another world entirely to some  more humorous additions, with two broken Buckets being the first fist weapon i found. -Switching between Worlds gives me that good Soul Reaver feel, and i do like the addition of  some puzzles. >The Neutral<-Most enemy encounters have ranged enemies in them, sometimes rather spread out, and  while manageable they have a little bit too long of a range, which seems somewhat fair as  your ranged attacks also go a very long distance.-The switching between your Lantern and Spelltool/Thrown Weapons is a bit clunky, and it is  difficult to tell which one you have currently equipped at a glance.>The Negative<-The Dark Crusader starting class you get with the deluxe edition feels a little bit pay to win,  having a seemingly far superior weapon and starting with a pendant that gives you bonus  stats. While you can unlock this class after an playthrough, i feel like rewarding people  buying an more expensive version with a slightly more easy mode goes against the spirit of a  Soulslike. This is a rather trivial complaint, however.-Many attacks lunge you foward which is fine in open areas and interiors, but becomes a  complete nightmare once you are in an area with ledges that lead to deadly depths. LotF has  no ledge protection, causing you to easily yeet yourself off an ledge with some of the  weapons if you try to attack an enemy near one.-Online play in its entirety. From seamless coop not working as expected, crossplay being  nonfunctional and the netcode being somehow worse than even the Soulsborne games.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------My Brothers in Christ i know times are rough and inflation is booming, but there has to be a time to accept the fact that Windows 7 with your trusty 980 GT is no longer capable of running modern games, or that maybe you really ought to stop visiting those shady sides without an adblocker.I have an 1660S with an I5 9400F, 16 GB of ram and have this installed on an old 120 gb ssd.This piece of crap was outdated 2 or 3 years ago when i bought it for cheap, and it runs this game at medium to high settings at 1080p with steady 60 fps and i don't even have to turn on fsr's vaseline mode for that.For that it's vastly better optimized than most new releases. Hell, look at Forspoken, Jedi Survivor or Darktide if you want to see truly badly optimized games.The biggest technical problem i encountered is a version mismatch between the PS5 and PC version, causing crossplay not to work, and initial stuttering that got fixed by changing it to borderless fullscreen and restarting it once.This review is a place holder to farm points and to assure people that it doesn't run as badly as people claim it does, as i have little to say about the game itself yet.Edit: As an addendum; i have great respect for the developers to manage to keep the game below 80 gigabytes. I know compression is a annoying task and takes forever, but it's good to see some studios still doing it.EDIT 2: Noticed a strange bug that appeared after some amount of gameplay that cleared after changing characters, causing the framerate to drop significantly during the process of regenerating stamina. Check the community thread i created if this has happened to you too, and if you have an idea as to what might cause this bug. Been trying to recreate it. Just search for "Performance drops during stamina regeneration"This bug only occurred twice, and i have yet to figure out how to reliable recreate it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks great, but I won't recommend it based on the fact that this is a game revolved on a developer trying to make a souls game with their own spin on it with horrible effect.  Not to mention the game crashing, consistently.First and foremost this game requires in depth graphics optimization just to make it playable, the in game optimization feature is horrible.  Second is the developers spin on the souls genre.  The game has you use a lamp to change between worlds, peek into one, and fight enemies.  In theory it sounds great,  in practice this makes it difficult to discover areas in the map and eliminates you ability to sneak up on enemies as many have to be debuffed with the lamp in order to damage, alerting them to you.  Third is the overall game play and progression.  From the perspective of a soulsborne enjoyer, it feels wrong.  The controls are not responsive, locking onto a target binds you to them!  For example, when locked onto a target and attempting to dodge back it priorities your movement to dodge in a circular motion around the target meaning it is more difficult to avoid attacks and will hurtle you off ledges in tight spaces or cause the camera to freak out spinning around the target.  Especially when enemy attack are either almost impossible not to dodge or ludicrously ranged, many enemies will wind up then almost slide to your location to attack.   The constant enemy generation in one of the worlds pads out playtime as you are forced to deal with half a dozen or more small enemies before being able to attack the main threat even in small encounters.  This coupled with the relatively slow experience/souls gain makes grinding a necessity just to progress through the game.  Relatively early in the game you are required to buy a key to progress, meaning you have to grind for on overly expensive progression item.  The cost of which you can't use to level up, even though you desperately need to, as when you open the next area with said key ALL enemies are now in packs, buffed, and 3 to 5 times stronger than the previous area.  In conclusion I just don't find this game enjoyable or even challenging, just frustrating!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good Soulslike that gets a recommended from me, but with a few big caveats (check the CONS for this).PROS:- sound design is pretty good- the entire parallel worlds/lamp mechanic is quite cool- gameplay is pretty varied, with lots of weapons, builds, and different ways to approach encounters- overall, the game's art design is very cool- level layout and exploration elements are good- devs care and are working hard to improve optimization problems and fix bugsCONS:- Optimization is godawful. I'm playing on a Ryzen 3700X, 16GB RAM @ 3200MHz, and a GTX 1070, and the game runs really poorly on native 1080p. Changing the graphics settings doesn't do anything (at most it's a 5-6 fps difference). The only real way to get mostly stable 60fps is by cranking down the resolution scaling to 50%. So maybe the game looks good when it runs properly, but on my PC it looks noticeably worse than contemporary games like Lies of P, Mortal Kombat 1, and Armored Core.- Enemy placement/numbers are all over the place. Soulslikes are all about slow, methodical combat and 1on1 encounters. They're essentially about quality over quantity. There's some of that in Lords of the Fallen 2, but there are also numerous fights where you're getting zerged by a ton of enemies. These fights become more and more frequent as you get further into the game. It can get really annoying and boring.- Checkpoint placement and corpse runs later in the game.As you progress past the first beacon, you start getting fewer and fewer checkpoints. This works in Demons Souls and Dark Souls 1 because bosses in those games are piss-easy and there aren't all that many enemies around. In Lords of the Fallen 2, there are like 50 enemies between Crimson Rector Percival and the Ruiner + an infinite amount of trash that spawns in the umbral realm. You have to run past these enemies in very narrow corridors and make a "shortcut" jump that instantly kills you if you fail it. Some of the enemies shoot at you, and can take off as much as 70% of your health in a single shot. Oh, and you also have 5 healing potions for this entire section + the boss at the end of it.What is the purpose of these checkpoint placements and corpse runs? This isn't hard, this is just tedious and frustrating. FROM Software has stopped doing this all the way back in Bloodborne, so why is it in this game? If the devs want to create a truly old school-style experience, how about they begin by creating well thought-out, old school-style encounters, instead of spamming a million enemies in a small area?- Shields have been nerfed into the ground.Shields barely block any physical damage while causing you to lose a ton of stamina when blocking, making them completely worthless. You can literally carry a desk-sized shield and use it to block an attack with a literal stick, and you'll still take damage. Why even have shields in the game, lol? If the devs are afraid shields would make their game too easy, they should design fun mechanics to get around that, or remove shields from the game. Elden Ring and Lies of P are both great examples of how shields can be incorporated in a cool and modern way. This is especially jarring since magic builds are as overpowered as ever, and really trivialize many fights. It really makes me wonder why the devs felt such a huge need to completely invalidate shield gameplay, yet leave spellcasting on easymode.CONCLUSION:Game is good and worth playing, but it has some major problems that can make it annoying and unfun at times. I'd say, you should wait a few months for the devs to iron out the bugs and optimization problems, and then buy the game when it goes on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After some time with this game I absolutely cannot recommend it. The biggest issue with this game by far is performance. If this were fixed I may consider another go, but as it is, you need a very very good (Expensive) PC to get real playable frames out of this game. I have an RTX 3070 and at 1080p medium/low settings I was barely cracking 60fps. But that hardly mattered because the micro stuttering and constant frame drops made it feel like trash. I do not recommend you buy this unless you have at least an rtx 3080, which should not be the case under any circumstances for a modern AAA title. On top of this combat feels both very slow and floaty. My character walks and runs as if they're wearing a ton of armor, even with light rolling. But once combat starts, you and enemies slide and skate through attacks making everything feel very awkward to time. On top of many enemies having poorly telegraphed moves that make it hard to counter or dodge.For a few positives though, this game is absolutely gorgeous! This game takes full advantage of unreal engine 5 and delivers a stunningly beautiful world, for as little as I've explored it. The lamp mechanic of switching between the physical and umbral realm is very interesting and brings with it some neat encounters, albeit with lackluster puzzle solving.All in all I give LOTF (2023) a 4/10. Again if performance is fixed I may have another crack at it, but as is I do not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: At 3.4 hours of gameplay. Recommendation is based on personal gameplay style in previous Dark/Demon Souls titles.It's a souls-type game with neat ideas but implemented in a way that may be kind of divisive. I like the aesthetic but a timer for most of the gameplay where you get swarmed by enemies if you don't progress fast enough made me not look forward to exploring. I enjoy exploring for extra gear but praying for my character to manage to jump a short gap or risk having to face a horde of enemies to reach that point again isn't fun. I'd really like to be able to take my time and explore, but too much time is focused on rushing so the timer doesn't summon a strong teleporting enemy that is accompanied by a swarm of respawning enemies that appear all around you. An alternate world is a neat idea for this type of game but it just feels off-putting for me. Luckily I didn't have any performance issues.I'll keep playing but I feel this gameplay is more suited to a souls-like speed runner that enjoys finding the most efficient route/build or die-hard sadist that enjoys fighting hordes than someone that is looking to take their time exploring the world. Personally, I feel too rushed when in the other world when it's required for progression but I realize that's something that some may prefer.

_childDocuments_.review: [reviewed: 2024/11/08]Lords of the Fallen 2023 is a fairly standard dark fantasy soulslike. The premise: you are using an Umbral Lamp to travel between two worlds, in order to aid the god Orius in preventing the return of the fallen god Adyr. Or don't. on a technical level the game looks decent, visual effects for things like spells are very flashy for better and for worse. In art direction, it's easy to see where they took inspiration from FROM's games, though the most interesting is where they diverge a little. The main strength of the presentation, and the game as a whole, is the soundtrack.  Some tracks are more standard ominous choir, though some like the Adyr-esque tracks are much more unique. It's not got any tracks that'll haunt me forever, but it's overall very good.Sound otherwise ranges from ok to kind of disappointing, particularly for weapons: striking enemies mostly sounds like hitting armour, which makes sense against some but feels odd against unarmoured ones. Not that Dark Souls having gushing SFX made more sense, but it at least made it feel like you were doing more damage. it's mostly your standard soulslike, so I'll mostly cover what's different. First, the lamp can be used as a tool in exploration and combat: holding it up in Axiom shows the world in Umbral but makes you vulnerable to enemies in the latter. You can also use it to "soulflay" an enemy to rip out their soul and whack it for some "wither" damage: they'll recover that health on hit, but withered health is instantly lost on taking damage. In addition,  You can do this either manually with the lamp, or by dying. Umbral progression is usually just platforming with the help of your lamp to move platforms sometimes.  blocking will convert health to withered HP instead of losing it outright, which you can recover via attacking, with block efficiency determining how much health gets withered; and ranged/magic options are tied to a weapon slot that you can swap to with a single button press and quickly throw out some projectiles/spells. Ammo is tied to a bar like mana, replenished with ammo pack consumables. Which is great, and really incentivises utilising these options as a side more. Even just some throwable items can go a long way. Ambushes are constant, to the point of being predictable. The starting area has crates you can roll into with a 50/50 chance there's an enemy behind them, it just gets silly. Bosses are...odd. Their main difficulty often comes from moves that have subtle telegraphs you're likely to miss the first time, and unusual attack speeds (like one colossal boss has one attack that feels borderline hitscan). Once you know that though, it's not too bad. Though by the mid-game you can get so strong it hardly matters. attacks make characters lunge forward, like an early Assassin's Creed game, which doesn't help with readability too well. This is awkward, but  You can be looking right ahead at an Umbral node to target, character and camera pointed there, and instead lock on to an unprovoked enemy 45 degrees to the side. Or have a hound rushing you ~3m away, and instead lock on to an archer ~12m away. It sometimes works, but you will always feel when it doesn't. There are sidequests of the "opening this door too early causes the NPC to die and you fail" variety. This is also the only soulslike where I regularly had to consult the wiki just to find out where I was meant to go next for main progression, though YMMV on that one. There are some with special attacks, but strangely they must be unlocked by sidequests first. Which are aforementioned very unintuitive. However, if you decide to , you have a unique final boss. It's a fairly generic fight, but has a good reveal at the end that recontextualises the game slightly. The issue is it's happening at the . It at least may make me want to play the other endings too, but not enough to consider the story particularly good sadly. when it works it works, however not only is netcode a coin toss, but  PvP can be fun if unbalanced, but it feels horrible to match against someone who's clearly new.Overall, while I had some positives here and there, I can't recommend this game wholeheartedly. It has a Skyrim amount of bugs, combined with some design choices that make the experience so much more awkward to play.There is a sequel coming, which I hope Hexworks leans more into trying their own ideas over following Dark Souls' by letter. Because a game like that with decent performance could be something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: Lords of the Fallen is basically a very painful way to play a far less fun version of Dark Souls. I can't recommend it because It seems to only be for one specific type of player, shield and parry with weapon buffs on the ready.The magic system is incredibly underwhelming, and runs counter to it's "like dark souls but..." hook which is the umbral lamp. The umbral lamp has 2 uses, illuminate spirits, and pull the soul out of a body, but it shares the same slot as the magic, so you have to switch to it during a stressful situation, use the spell or lamp, then switch back, while being pressured by a very poorly designed situation.So then play full melee right? Well that's a good suggestion, but now you are just basically told that if you try any method but the main one, your actively going to have a bad time. That's just bad design.Speaking of bad design, one of the main reasons that DS is still played is because while it's very hard, you also have a design set out to be predictable and speed ran. The Umbral world ruins this idea, so you now have random enemies that spawn in to actively hurt your planned idea's. Good in theory, but you now have to deal with this very unforgiving scenario with limited resources, that increases in difficulty the longer you are stuck there. It did lead to some fun moments, but you are kinda also now SOL if it's one of the poorer designed levels, there is no shortcut and you can lose alot of progress.The boss fights is where I finally just gave up. The first one is a great starter fight, it gives you a chance to learn the system, and overall is what you want the rest of them to be. The second boss was the capra demon's worst parts, small arena, kills you in 2 or so hits unless you spend an hour farming, and is overall just a mess. Then I got to the saint, and it's a hurry up and wait fight that after several dozen failed attempts, I looked up a video and saw even the people that make guides where salty. 2/3 of your starting main bosses being just garbage, tells me everything I need to know about the rest of the game.The worst part of all of this, is that the redeeming qualities, the world they built, is really cool, enough to carry me through a few days of playing. It feels wasted, by the same poor monster placement that Scholar of the first Sin's had. BS placement, with not enough supplies, stress mechanic, and unfun boss fights. While I consider souls like to be more of a puzzle than anything else, and a poor puzzle is one of the least enjoyable experiences that one can imagine.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game for 70 hrs, i'm on NG+, these are my thoughts on the game so far:++ Pros:-Boss variety and enemy variety is pretty good, INSANELY good hitboxes here and there.-SOULS-DRIP like no other, this is basically DS2 levels of armor variety and weapon variety too.-Parry systems is dope, closer to what lies of P/Sekiro offer.-Cool split world mechanic, gives world traversing a whole new experience compared to other souls/souls-likes.-Portable bonfires; you buy them but they can only be placed in specific locations.-POWER-STANCING; you can power stance ANY 2 melee weapons, yes ANY of them, moveset depends on the primary weapon but still hella dope.-Combo-System lets you mix in heavy and light attacks seamlessly, you can use them both in tandem with each other without the delay of the heavy attack so you can benefit from the moveset variety at no extra cost.-SWAMPS AREN'T HELL, LOOKING AT YOU ELDEN RING. ♥♥♥♥ ROT.-- Cons:-Game has a lot of places to explore, you can get lost pretty EASILY. I'd open FextraLife and FightinCowboy for guides.-Some bad hitboxes here and there.-Attacks have so much momentum, you cross so much distance, that goes for enemies too.-If you don't pace yourself properly, game is an ABSOLUTE nightmare, game can feel like a slog fest due enemy placement in some areas being ass and there's almost ALWAYS an enemy around every corner or behind any breakable obstacle.-SOME bosses make a return as reoccurring normal enemies albeit scaled down.-On NG+ runs, you have less vestiges(this game's version of bonfires) to run to in the NG cycle, making each NG cycle even tougher than the last, this is taking into account the MONSTROUS amount of HP bosses can reach and enemies, this does mean you will hit harder as you level up but as soon as you start hitting the caps, it doesn't get any easier.With that all being said, this game has TREMENDOUS potential and the devs seem to be working on it continuously, performance on my 3060 laptop GPU has been fine, i have 50+ FPS on almost all areas with the default medium settings.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as people were displeased from the multiplayer choice, I thoroughly enjoyed the game. The bosses were fun, the theme was dark, Gothic-esque and the lantern usage made the secrets quite enjoyable. You got used to knowing that there was a way forward by using the lantern after a while. Although some of the sword styles were just unfavourable and there was a lack of extension in the Bucket Lord questline, I found that getting aid from him was enough to join the game. Invading enemy players was something that I found quite a hassle, as it took a while to search for someone, even though it does have a large player base. I found the gameplay smooth, and I wished the fire spells were dramatised.The idea of casting spells and getting some retribution from using these invocations is a nice tough (like getting bleeding from using divinity). Although I played mostly as a dual wielding Pieta sword user, with divinity and heavy armour, I felt a big overpowered. I tried to change my style of play, but I genuinely couldn't enjoy any other weapon. Even swords that were massively heavy did less damage than I did with Pieta's swords. I liked the donation system and the secrets involving the NPCs, though I wish they had more of an impact on the story and it wasn't just a massive spin of Souls-like play. Using a style of play with only one or two real changes doesn't make it stand out enough at a full game's price.Again, I found it enjoyable and challenging, but after a while you knew what to expect. You can go for the boss pretty early on, if you're daring, and some areas can be easily skipped. I really enjoyed playing the game, but it still has potential for improvement.I didn't experience any of the poor quality issues some players dealt with, although I received an occasional FPS drop from rolling through puddles. I found some areas frustrating, which is exactly what I wanted, and I found it satisfying when I wiped the floor with new areas first time after learning enemy attacks.I found it thrilling when you would come across the red reaper who would kick you out of the soul world if you stayed for too long, but he was always fun to fight.I'd definitely give this a firm 7 or 8 out of 10 if multiplayer could function in a faster manner and it was polished a little bit more.Additional: you have so many options for throwing weapons and bows and crossbows to boot. It's a nice change. I wish there was some kind of armour upgrade, as I felt a bit disappointed by the lack of individuality armour actually gave, but the stat differences was definitely an interesting idea. It was clear and helped you to understand what armour set would be best against the boss, although I wish there was an option to save sets to quickly change.

_childDocuments_.review: Updating review after NG+ patch. Now recommending game but with some caveats mentioned below.Game is more fun than not fun at this point. When ray tracing is disabled, performance is great. Combat is fun in 1v1, art design and the world building are fantastic. But there are still some issues with the enjoyment of this game (thankfully the developers seems to be committed to fixing some of these issues, for example the NG+ patch).1. Checkpoint system: Vestiges (bonfires) are too few and far between. The fact that you can kill a main boss, not get an actual vestige point (not the temporary seeds) and then immediately have to fight a surprise boss in the very next room is terrible design. (This problem could be mostly solved if we could keep 3 vestiges seeds active at one time).2. Encounter design: with vestige placement this bad, encounter designs need to be less tedious. You could remove a quarter of this games enemies and the game would be much better for it. The developers already are listening to this feedback and I've noticed some areas are easier now post patch (1 less crossbow man and less aggro range) but most encounters in the game are a slog to get through as their are still too many enemies. At least increase the vigor gain from enemies if the mob density stays the same; let me feel rewarded for mowing through 50+ enemies before I reach the next vestige.3. "Gotcha" moments: There are so many tedious, unfair encounters that feel like the developer just decides that you need to your die. I don't want to list out all these in the game, but its safe to say that every other encounter in the game is some type of trap or gotcha moment. Its not fun. When used sparingly these keep you on your toes, but there are far too many. However, if the devs continue patching (good on them) to better the experience, then I think this has the potential to be a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: 90 minutesThat's how long it took me to fall in love with the game. I learned the basic mechanics and the combat flow, then everything fell into place.I don't get why LotF gets so much hate online, because it's genuinely a great game. The game play is more intuitive than other souls games and the combat is visceral -- you can actually feel it. Yes, it can get really punishing, even more than your typical souls game, but every fight is manageable if played smart.Also, I cannot stress this enough -- I really, really like the dual worlds and the mechanics that come with it, from the life recovery to the balance of greed/caution.Last, but definitely not least, my favorite aspect is the exploration. You are actually encouraged to explore both worlds, learn the optimal routes, then wonder around, farm new levels or just admire the decrepit and morbid surroundings. My only criticism of the game is the somewhat poor optimization for certain areas -- you will get lag spikes.But other than that, it's all good and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: LOTF has a myriad of issues which I simply cannot ignore. Game breaking glitches such as the co-op level loss have made people lose hours upon hours of progress. The game itself after a certain point becomes a slog. The short review is; maybe wait on a sale a few months down the line of buy it from a key site, in this instance it is justified! Read on for my longer review!First things first, this was one of my most anticipated games of the year. In the beginning I was thoroughly enjoying it while ignoring some of its missteps; however, as time went on, these missteps became too big to ignore. LOTF is a beautiful looking game, but underneath those UE5 good looks is a game which is frustrating above all. Vestiges are placed haphazardly, along with seed points, it seems there was no logical rhythm in placing the rest points. Enemy mobs are too dense for the sake of it, ranged enemies pepper you from afar while you fight multiple 'mini-boss' regular enemies in a row in the late game. In the beginning my tolerance was high, but this recedes and recedes even more as I play further, each time I pick up the game now, it feels like a slog!  Bosses are actually easier to fight than your actual progress through the levels, it's tedious 30 hours in.LOTF has tried to copy FromSoftware in their craft, but an imitation will always be an imitation. This has made me realise FS are the masters of their craft. Many things have been included in LOTF what seems like 'just for the sake of it' without any true understanding of why FS do it. An example of this is in the story telling and side quests; the NPC side quests in LOTF are strange; some of the requirements are so obtuse you would genuinely need a guide to figure it out. Again obtuse for the sake of being obtuse. Again, level design, enemy placement, and world building is much better in FS games, the only place LOTF beats FS is graphical prowess and the art design that has come with that.My final talking point would be the bugs, I have encountered one annoying bug myself; having to reinstall the game multiple times because the update patches froze on my steam. I have seen many others and my friend just recently experienced the co-op bug. Again just really shoddy practices that PAYING customers have to put up with! One last thing that has got on my nerves is the audacity of the developers to upload an image on the store page with inflated 'user reviews.' Own up to the issues the game has! Rant over. Thank you for taking the time to read my review.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the souls games you'll most likely like this one and I feel it's worth the asking price and wasn't a waste of my money which is always a good thing.+ World exploration is great (full of hidden goodies and optional bosses down just about any and everypath i went down)+ Armor and weapon design is great (some of the best in a souls game to date imo)+ Bosses are challenging enough i didn't really one shot any without being overleveled (did a much later zone about 2 steps too early apparently).+ Graphics and art direction were on point in just about every zone of the game.only a few complaints- Enemy balancing, everything and i mean EVERYTHING hits like a f'in truck.      - Worst offenders are crossbowmen (fire big damage bolts without reloading till after the 2nd shot?) and        the melee attacks from the female archers ( arrow damage is high but they're archers, i lose 70% health        from a melee attack from them though with the heaviest armor in the game and heavily invested in VIT)- Enemy placements get... annoying more than interesting (they really got a hard on for trying to knock you off ledges) -The range on enemy ranged attacks is ridiculous (i've seen them snipe with an arrow or spell from across a zone and through small opening in terrain to the point you don't even see where the shot came from half the time)Long story short as someone who really enjoys this style of game and spent thousands of hours on them it's a really really solid and enjoyable experience and the only complaints i really have are easily tweaked.
