_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I received this game for free in early access.Really fun soulslike with a lot of potential, but definitely still very rough around the edges. Too many sections go too long without a vestige/flowerbed, requiring you to basically sprint past enemies you'd otherwise be interested in fighting. The bosses and minibosses themselves are fun, but once you fight a miniboss it's almost guaranteed you'll see the same miniboss used as a common mob in the next section, usually on repeat. In one area I counted 6 of the same miniboss pretty much back2back, and the minibosses are arguably harder in their mob form than as a miniboss because you're dealing with a load of other enemies onscreen at the same time.There are a lot of little things that I can really appreciate, the aesthetics and voice acting are incredible, the world's lore is pretty interesting, the umbral/axiom mechanics feel a bit "Portal"-esque at times with how you're required to problem solve between switching in and out of umbral, and the general enemy/boss design is pretty dang good. That satisfying feeling of progression as you learn the boss mechanics and get a little farther each attempt is definitely there.The devs do really seem to care, and the game has been receiving daily updates with the devs acknowledging a lot of the feedback from players, but there's still quite a bit of work to do.Overall, if you're itching for a soulslike this is a pretty solid choice, but just keep in mind there are some hiccups that you'll have to inevitably contend with until the game is in a more refined state.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential, but it's currently riddled with too many issues. The repetitive nature of farming items for hours just to upgrade a weapon becomes tedious after a while. I believe people are getting too immersed in this souls-like genre, adhering so strictly to its style that it diminishes the game's uniqueness.Co-op play was a major selling point for me, to play with family/friends. However, experiencing it being broken on launch day was beyond disappointing. I couldn't even return the game because my playtime exceeded two hours, most of which was spent attempting to get the co-op feature to function. Despite these frustrations, I decided to keep trying because I recognized the game's potential.But, the game reaches a level of frustration that's hard to overlook. Encountering new areas only to face beginner-level mobs that can inexplicably one-shot or two-shot you doesn't make sense, especially when I'm at level 170 with around 50 vitality and decent armor. I appreciate a challenge, but this feels senselessly difficult to the point where it discourages engagement with the combat, prompting players to just rush through to the next vestige or seed.What ultimately deterred me from ever revisiting this game was the realization that New Game+ would only exacerbate these issues, rendering the experience thoroughly unenjoyable for me. It's perplexing how modern games, despite extensive beta testing periods, still manage to launch in such a poor state after generating significant hype.I will concede that the developers are making commendable efforts with their updates and patches. Nevertheless, I'd prefer a refund over the prospect of repurchasing this game in its current state. The foundational potential is there, but the execution, as of now, is sorely lacking.

_childDocuments_.review: It's decent, with enough gameplay to warrant the price tag. Another small gripe is the consumable checkpoints being far too common, while the actual bonfire equivalent Vestiges aren't as common as they should be. Some places have the consumable sprout locations so close to each other that it seems like the devs purposefully spread them around to make first playthroughs longer with people spending the seeds needed to make them far more than they should since they don't know there's another spot 20 feet away with only one enemy separating the 2 locations. Those are my main issues, smaller ones are just things like attack recovery times should be shortened to make combat feel more fluid and certain enemies should stagger easier to make them feel more fair due to them attacking fast with little recovery time for them. There's a lot of good things about the game, but it has just a few issues that keep it from being great. Worth buying if you enjoy Dark Souls 1 or 2 specifically with how the combat feels, and %100 worth buying on sale if it is 40 or 50 dollars if you enjoy the genre in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is garbage. I've beat the DS trilogy, Sekiro, and Lies of P. There are so many technical mistakes and poor optimization that make it hard to legitimately play. The experience of playing this is downright disappointing, the game has been in development for 10+ years and the fact that it was published in this state is an insult.Cons:1. Animation stops aren't precise, it's as if the character model doesn't have any friction and is ice skating. You end up moving several inches farther than where you intended. This goes for swinging, dodging, rolling, etc.2. Hitboxes are completely broken, you will still get hit (for a ridiculous amount) even if you successfully dodge an attack. 3. Controls feel extremely clunky, even with the latest patch for my GPU. There are often frame rate losses that eventually stabilize, but they shouldn't be happening at all. It makes playing the game feel choppy and half-baked.Pros:1. Some* of the boss designs are entertaining, if the hitboxes are not completely trash.2. It gives you something to try to play if you have no other Souls-like on your list to beat. That's it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I think it's a good game from a gameplay and art perspective.As a product, it has some rough edges - the most glaring of which is the save issue, which got me twice (luckily the second time, I had backed up my own save).I think the design is solid - the umbral eyes and runes especially offer cool opportunities for varied gameplay and the weapon variety is appreciable.  I think in a world where both Lies of P and Elden Ring exist, it is a little bit of a bummer that the weapons don't have something analogous to fable abilities or ashes of war, respectively, but the combat is still fun in PvE.PvP on the other hand, was rough - I didn't try it until I was relatively high level, over 130, and every person I encountered had an identical configuration - two of Pieta's sword, Orius' Radiance or whatever the thundercloud spell is called, and the Radiance Laser (not the channeled one).  Hopefully there's some improvement there since they've identified that separate balance for PvE and PvP is warranted.The story was solid too, I went for the more involved ending and was glad to have done it - I think it's neat that it appears each path has its own boss, and the concept of unlockable classes in a game like this is definitely cool, as is the ability to just reset your current game level (e.g. NG, NG+1, etc) to get achievements or whathaveyou.  The upcoming fully customizable NG+ sounds great.On the whole, Hexworks did a great job as this game has a lot going for it and feels good in most ways - very much a modern take on the genre.Personally, I do not think it was quite as polished and excellent as Lies of P, but it was still fun, well made, and had beautiful art and sound.  Some of the visual designs were just knockouts.Lastly, the dual-world system is very fun and pretty well done aside from a few places where it's a little too frequently displayed as a way to get around an obvious dead end, instead of letting you explore, but there's a lot of stuff hidden in the umbral realm so it makes up for it.I'd say it's a solid 8.5 out of 10 for me, maybe a 9 if I weren't still a bit bitter about the save corruption issue.

_childDocuments_.review: I have seen strong opinions about this game both one way or the other, so keep in mind that this recommendation is just one person's early-ish opinion.12 hours in, I have yet to beat the game, but it's giving some really strong first-impressions.It's far from perfect, the movement, camera, platforming and combat sometimes feels a bit more clunky than the average Fromsoft RPG, and the strength + amount of enemies can sometimes be very overwhelming, but I think there is a lot to love about the game.The combat system might feel a bit restrictive for some. So far, it feels like it's designed so that most enemies are supposed to be handled in very specific ways. Some attacks you "have" to parry/block as they have ridiculous tracking, some you "have" to dodge and punish as they'll guard break you otherwise, but personally, I love this combination.Both parrying and blocking takes away health temporarily, and it is restored by dodging and punishing, or by breaking the enemy stance and hitting them with a "grievous strike". It heavily incentivizes you both to parry, and to dodge and punish. On top of this, I think every class has one way or another to deal decent ranged damage as a sort of "off-hand" thing.Watching my friend play this game and seeing how it works made me want to buy the game instantly, and I was not disappointed. The bosses feel very memorable and enjoyable as a result.I won't go into too much detail in this recommendation, but exploring Umbral either with the lamp, or by going there yourself is also incredibly interesting to me personally. Seeing the horrors that are always looking at you from beyond, feeling the sense of dread build up as you're on a timer, but also exploring and unlocking hidden paths on top of being rewarded with extra currency for your time spent adds a whole new layer to every single part of the game world.To summarize, this game definitely has flaws, but the inspiration it takes from other similar titles while addings its own ideas feels refreshing. If you can take the good with the bad, imo this game is definitely worth it.EDIT: Finished the game for the first time now. I think the amount of ice and fire damage in the final areas was a bit too high, and some bosses felt underwhelming by showing up as regular enemies later. I started to see the pattern of which bosses were real bosses, and which ones were minibosses. It didn't detract much from the game, but it was noticable. In the end, I still recommend this game. I had a great time with it, and will be checking out NG+ at the very least.

I got a pretty stable 60 fps throughout, playing on high settings in dlss quality. On the content of the game itself, its essentially a dark souls sequel. For me this is a good thing, It is what it is. For me there is not enough dark souls games, I love the formula and am delighted that games like this are being released. Whilst you might hear the community gripes about this and that not being quite as good as X Fromsoft game, but for me the attempts at interlocking level design was a great nod to the original DS, and made the game feel more like a Dark souls game than DS3. It feels a bit like a sequel made by another developer, a bit like New Vegas, or Knights of the old republic 2. The game in its own right is really entertaining. I thoroughly enjoyed it, and was "hooked" . All the areas felt interesting, though none quite matched the complexity of the first. All in all though I thought the game was really good throughout. I would say the last level was a little silly in the extent to which it manned the whole level with previous bosses in a lesser state. I suspect many like me will simply run past them rather then run the gauntlet. Long storey short, This game is good.

My issue with the game has nothing to do with the game itself, but everything to do with how it's programmed regarding file security; I literally feel like the K&P GIF that's profusely sweating whenever I boot the game up.Otherwise, man.... this game is absolutely exceptional. I talked about it here: But, yeah even with all of its issues Lords of the Fallen can stand beside Elden Ring as one of the best Soulslike right now. There's some fine tuning that's needed, but that goes with the territory of building a game as complex as this. _childDocuments_.review: I was wrong about this game. I initially thought it was a souls like that just wasn't going to make the cut, its trope weren't working, its enemy density was too high, and it would feel clunky. But since then I have been proven wrong. With my initial review at about 10 hours, I was frustrated at crashing, poor enemy layout/density, and overall issues with progression through the game. And so I initially reviewed the game as a "do not recommend". Since then the developers have worked hard to improve the gameplay experience, and I can attest to that. The game performs far better than at launch, the enemy AI has been adjusted to ease areas with high enemy density, and progression feels smoother and less annoying. Combat is good, albeit I would like some more variety in weapon moveset among archetypes. Armor is incredible looking, and really keeps the souls fashion true to name. Bosses aren't too difficult, they can prove a challenge at first but quickly become manageable as their moves are telegraph. Sometimes minor enemies may feel like more of a challenge than actual bosses which can be a very big problem. However I do think this game is worth a playthrough, and I would recommend this game to souls enjoyers, or someone who wants to try out souls games. I would hesitate to buy it full price, but if it's ever on sale then it is definitely worth a pickup.

_childDocuments_.review: Look I'm going to be honest as someone who is a massive soulslike fan. This game is just not where it needs to be to be worth your time. My friends and I were all hyped for this game, we were excited to see the LOTF devs finally getting things right (or so we assumed from the trailers and descriptions.) Seemless coop? Interconnected world? Gothic fantasy artstyle and desings? It was all finally shaping up to be what we wanted the original Lords of The fallen to be. The reality? It barely even can spit on the mark. I don't want to make some hyper analytical review because in all honesty I don't think this game deserves one, but here are a few key takeaways that really turn me off and disappoint me. I'm not going to talk about performance (with a few exceptions where it matters), it is bad and it unacceptable imo but others have already spoken at length about it.Before I end though, there are some things I genuinely like about the game.So to recap, I strongly believe your time and money would be far better rewarded elsewhere. Buy this game on a sale if you REALLY want it, but otherwise it's just not worth it. There are far better offerings out there at far better prices right now. The only thing this game has to offer over any other souls-like is the setting/art and the umbral mechanic. If you don't care about skipping those, you're missing out on nothing special. Its such a shame too, because this game was shaping up to be everything we wanted. Maybe in a year it'll be the game it was meant to be, but I'm getting really tired of waiting for games to deliver what they promise.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get right to it:THE GOOD:The graphics and storyline are amazing. The voice acting is perfect. The entirety of the map is fantastic, except, in my opinion, Forsaken Fen. That place was a mess and a labyrinth. Battle mechanics are solid. It is a fast paced game but not difficult to adapt to, especially if you are a souls born veteran. The idea of Umbral was clever. It's a very unique mechanic of the game that I enjoyed. Online gameplay either via co-op or PvP is decent. I think refinement needs to be done but it is not terrible.THE BADEnemy placement is bulls*&%. Infinite enemy spawning in Umbral is ridiculous. I think they should have made umbral enemies a bit tougher rather than making them spawn infinitely. The idea of being able to place your checkpoints with a vestige seed was okay but the way it works in game didn't seem to mix well. Instead they should have made more regular vestige checkpoints. Poise in this game only exists in the form of hyper armor when doing charged attacks, otherwise is non existent. It is frustrating and rage inducing to be staggered with such weak attacks. In PvE, this is manageable. You get used to it but in PvP, it is unbearable. There is no trading damage with an opponent. Whoever lands the first hit gets to win the flurry of hits. Not necessarily the end for you but you you can't trade damage with opponents.THE WORSESome bosses are reused as regular enemies over and over again. Tower of Penance was the worst when it came down to this. You fight a boss at the beginning of the area and then this same boss is used as an enemy more times that I could count. He was in every damn corner of that place. A lot of bosses where gimmick fights. Alternative endings are so convoluted and not clear as to how to achieve them without a proper guide. But in my honest opinion, the worst of the worst for this game was a terrible final boss fight if you are doing the "normal ending". The boss fight was a pathetic, good for nothing gimmick fight that did not felt like you accomplished anything.FINAL THOUGHTSWith all of the above stated, I still recommend this game. If you can play the game for what it is and not compare it to the experience of FromSoftware's souls games, I think you too can enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The netcode for this game is unacceptable. You will be constantly rubberbanding and getting dragged back into attacks that you clearly dodged. Optimization is atrocious. I have a 4090 and the game can't maintain a stable 60 fps with settings on medium. Devs seem more concerned with balancing the terrible PvP than actually fixing the game.If they ever decide to start focusing on things that matter during more than 5% of your playtime then I might be able to give this game a positive review. Having passable netcode during co-op is something that Fromsoft has been doing in this genre for 14 years and it's embarrassing that this game fails so spectacularly.Edit: I was informed today that this game does not have level or weapon upgrade limits on PvP matchmaking. There may be some degree of scaling but it doesn't seem to affect the situation in any meaningful way. This is made far worse by the fact that, practically speaking, this game does not have any level caps. There are damage scaling caps as well as caps on carry weight, stamina and health but defense is uncapped. My highest defense stat is about 600 but tens of millions is achievable through cheats (yet another example of Easy Anticheat being useless). Every invasion is the invader killing you in two shots while your weapon deals about 10-15% of its normal damage and barely scratches them.

_childDocuments_.review: 5.5/10 overall.Essentially just comes to the fact that:- the Boss Design is poor compared to other soulslikes (Incredibly easy, with very little moveset variation). The first real boss is great, but after that it is just kind of rehashes of the same thing to the point where if you took away the "Skins" of bosses, you probably couldn't tell what boss you are fighting because they all end up feeling like "Two hit combo, delayed third hit, big opening for damage, repeat" with *no other attacks*- the loot is quite poor (you have a few weapon categories and every single weapon within a category has the exact same moveset. Boss weapons have nothing interesting about them other than just pure stats)- the enemy placement ends up being a chore more than interesting. You get to a point in the game where you just stop bothering to fight regular enemies because there are just so many (and with no enemy variety, you have pretty much fought every enemy by the time you are 20% through the game) that it just ends up feeling like a waste of your time.- Certain mechanics are poorly done. Parrying, which was meant to be a big important mechanic in this game similar to Lies of P, is literally always worse than dodging. This is because parrying "damages" your HP bar and does *only* posture damage, where as Dodges can do posture damage with certain gear and also allows a follow up hit that does posture damage and real damage. Just a lot of stuff like that in the mechanics.It does some interesting things like the Umbral, but even then they are often double edged swords. The Umbral is cool, but it also means that the entire game looks exactly the same because the Umbral always looks the same and you are almost always in the Umbral realm.Overall, if you are super into Soulslikes, and you have played everything, this game will give you that fix, but there are so so so many games that I'd reccomend before I could do this one, and even then only if you really just need a new soulslike.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - wait till it goes on sale and pick it up it is not worth this price.Pros decent graphics.story seems to be okan ok game but not a good souls gameunique double world idea.atmosphere is pretty good.Cons "souls like" - This feels more like a diablo knockoff rather than a souls knock off ngl. _childDocuments_.review: It's a shame I can't recommend this game because at it's core it's an amazing soul's like that is oozing with potential.Pro'sGraphics are really good (I haven't had any performance issues but many are reporting problems)Sound and Music is pretty goodLevel design is greatAtmosphere is also really good, the dual world idea really works well here.Bosses are pretty good, not the greatest but fun all the same.Con'sMostly everything that makes a soul's game enjoyable.Combat - It's ok, not Fromsoft good or even Lies of P quality, but just ok and feels rather floaty.Locking on - I know there is a bit of a joke about the poor locking ability in Fromsoftware games but honestly, it feels like the dev's took this idea and made it worse intentionally, it's nearly impossible to lock on to something in front of you, multiple times there will be 1 mob in front and the character will 180 to target something 2 miles behind you.Enemy placement - This honestly ruins the entire game, imagine the archers of Anor Londo from DS1, then the gank squads of DS2, put them together and times it by 10 = 99% of encounters in this game. It gets dull REALLY quick and results in the best tactic being > Run past the dudes > Farm some XP if needed > Run past the dudes > Kill boss. I was loving the exploration when I started but it got dull very quickly and it didn't seem to matter how well I cleared up areas, something would just bottle neck you in a tunnel or tight space so often I just gave up exploring and the game then turned into a real chore to continue.My biggest gripe is the enemy placement as I feel they have gotten such a great game here that it didn't have to resort to the cheap "gotcha" deaths 99% of the time. Ye, it's rather funny being pushed off a ledge when your not paying attention, but it's back to back being knocked off something, sniped from miles away, trapped in a tight space or having the dodge roll in the wrong direction, mostly due to autolock but I have been running forward and pressing roll just for the character to roll backwards or sideways multiple times.If this game goes on offer for around £20 and gets some patches, then sure it's a great buy, but this isn't a AAA game and doesn't deserve a AAA price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Some good ideas here killed by lackluster execution and long term tedium.The dual world concept is cool, until you realize that if you feel at all comfortable with these kinds of games you can safely spend virtually all of your time in umbral to ensure you don't miss anything, which really kills a lot of the flavor of having dual worldsBy far the biggest joykiller here is enemy placement, level design, and the completely overindulgent use of "Classic souls gimmicks". Each area seems to pick a gimmick and stick with it. Take for example, an enemy standing around a corner ready to shove you off a ledge to your death. Neat. A cool surprise the first time you see it. Until you realize the entire area is ledges, corners, and dudes waiting in piles of boxes and dark corners ready to shove you.It isn't even a matter of these things being "difficult" or causing a particularly high amount of deaths or anything, it's just tiring to spend each area meticulously checking for overused gimmicks. It wasn't bad at first, but after about fifteen hours, when you can spot the patterns easily, it just becomes boring.Adding to the tedium is the fact that enemy variety quickly fades after the first eight or so hours. The game absolutely will introduce you to an entirely new area with one, maybe two new enemies, and a dozen reskins.The bosses also tend to be far easier than the areas they inhabit, leading to an overall feeling of disappointment and anti-climax after clearing things out.I enjoyed my first ten or so hours with the game, which seems to be a lot more than most people did. The art style is incredibly well done and the visual designs can be on point. But I simply do not want to spend another ten hours clearing the same enemies from these stunning looking areas while checking for which gimmick is in style at the moment.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a "Would you recommend this game to other players? Yes, but..." option. As of right now I would give the game probably a 6.5/10, which is slightly above average. The only thing holding it back from at least an 8/10, for me, are some bugs, level design issues, and slight optimization issues.The story so far, I'm 25+ hours in, has been good. The characters/classes to choose from are decent with the standard play styles available. The enemy types have been well designed, albeit some of them are cheese. The ranged mobs in small areas being the most that come to mind for frustration. The graphics are gorgeous. The boss fights so far have been fair for the most part. The Umbral mechanic has grown on me over time as well. At first I did not like it but it adds a bit of additional adventure/exploration problem solving to find hidden gear or story plot points that I'm liking.To raise my rating from a 6.5/10 the things I believe need to be addressed are:1. The lock-on system needs a revamp. It is unfortunately, atrocious. Trying to get it to lock on to the mob you want or trying to cycle between mobs is like a boss fight in itself. Be prepared for frustrations here.2. Getting stuck in the world, meaning myself, other mobs, and loot drops. On multiple occasions I have had things that move in the game get stuck in the world. I have been knocked down and gotten stuck in some piece of the world. I have had mobs get stuck in walls or other parts of the world. I have had loot drops get stuck in the world after killing a mob where I could not approach them to pick them up. This also leads into issue #3, clipping. Be prepared that sometimes, something is getting stuck and you'll have to just accept it.3. Clipping issues. This is one of my biggest frustrations with the game currently. Often times when trying to move around the world my character will run into something not on the screen. This becomes most frustrating when in a fight and trying to circle or maneuver around a mob to attack, dodge, or block and all of a sudden you can't move in the direction you were going because there is something you can't see blocking your path. I have had it happen on flat ground with nothing in sight and I stop moving and have to move around the invisible thing in the middle of the street. I've also gone into Umbral vision to see if something was there that could be doing it and there was not. There's just random invisible things you will run into. This is most frustrating when there are multiple mobs attacking you and you're all of a sudden stuck and can't move because they have you boxed in to an open area and you're yelling, "Why can't I move!?!" at the screen. 4. The game could use a little better optimization. My rig can run Alan Wake 2 on 1440p ultra settings and keep the fps between 70 and 144 fps with no issues. In this game I am running 1440p backed down to high settings and I get frame drops into the low 40 range at times. It's often enough to notice. Keeping 60 plus fps should not be an issue with this PC at lowered settings but it is. Be aware that you may have to bump your settings down more than expected to keep a smoother experience.Like, I said, I would recommend the game to people because overall I've enjoyed the experience so far, but be aware there will most likely be some frustrations coming from mechanics and design issues that will hopefully be fixed or addressed in later patches. If the lock on system gets some updating that would most likely push my rating to a 7.5 or 8/10 alone.

_childDocuments_.review: The reboot of Lords of the Fallen has the interconnected level design of Dark Souls, the combat of DS2 and the style of DS3/Elden Ring. I would say it is 80% there in terms of general feel but it is certainly closer to DS2 in many ways. The combat is floaty enough with large distances covered by player and enemy alike. Placements and general encounter design can be rather frustrating at times. Feedback can be also improved both in terms of audio and visual cues. Regardless, you can still find enough here to have a good time. For now there are issues that need to be fixed as soon as possible like the lacking performance and various gameplay issues. Unfortunately, co-op barely works, usually having some kind of problem when trying to play with random people. Connecting problems and stability issues are part of the course for now. I even experienced a 'bug' where my character got totally different stats after a rather glitchy co-op session but there might have been an editor hack in play on the other side.Update: the game is being updated regularly but there are still too many annoying things going on - like just recently the fixed drop of Overseer's Halberd vanished after a rest while random loot still persists on earlier maps after many hours. Core things are being changed like boss weapon levels causing players to lose progress in many occasions. There is a gem underneath the problems here but first the ashes must be cleaned up in order for us to be able to appreciate it.Update 2:While the LotF is still far from being perfect it still remains the best non-From Software souls-like to date, only the Surge games coming close to matching its quality. It manages to provide superior gameplay and design compared to the many AA titles in this category expectedly so.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have finally finished this abysmal game and uninstalled it.Still would not recommend it. Nothing but AIDS reused bosses and fire enemies. Buy Lies of P instead.I will finish this game as I'm already too far in to get a refund, but I wish could.Don't bother. It's got a great art style but after not even the second area, every non-cutscene field boss you find will become a recycled common enemy with all the same movesets and HP/phase changes.Every area is overdesigned, overly complex, and everything loops around on itself with tons of nonsensical "shortcuts" and a million one-way doors.The Umbral mechanic is fine and adds a nice flavor to the aesthetic of the game, though some overly beefy enemies become way too common. Also, we get it, the devs really liked the mimic chest idea from Dark Souls, but the way it's implemented here with the fake item pickups is almost indiscernible and just feels like a forced "F you" to get the player into the Umbral, even in places where they otherwise have no reason to be there.Enemy placement is abysmal. You will run into two or even three recycled bosses in the same room in the latter half of the game. In one area, you have a boss fight with the Carrion guy with a spear who covers the arena in poison. After fighting him and proceeding into the tower he was likely guarding, not even 5 minutes later, you're introduced to about 6-8 more of that same exact enemy. It was not at all innovative nor fun. Just annoying. There's no enemy variety.Some enemies clearly were an afterthought in terms of just having too many cheese moves, too much AOE, and too much health. The poise system is pretty terrible; you always have none, every little thing but the weakest of trash mobs interrupts you, no matter how heavy an armor set you're wearing (I'm currently wearing a full set of Soverign Protector armor and the bell head). Meanwhile, many enemies, including the recycled bosses, seem to have random poise status, where heavy strikes that once staggered them out of a move will just not stagger them again out of the same move.The I-frames are... fine, I guess. You CAN side-step a majority of attacks without wasting stamina doing a full roll, and that's often enough for some AOEs. Parry window is extremely tight, but often feels inconsistent.Shields are worthless, don't even bother. Unless there's an item similar to Elden Ring's Greatshield Talisman, you will always take chip damage and tons of stamina damage. You can parry with just about every weapon in the game, so why even bother having a shield?Calrath is just endless AIDS fire projectile spam. Every enemy shoots fire. Even the stupid dogs. Clearly this area was a complete afterthought in enemy placement.This game certainly has some soul, and an acceptable level of Unreal Engine jank, and the artists did a fantastic job. But this isn't worth $60 (I bought it during the Winter Sale). The main bosses (the ones with cutscenes) are pretty enjoyable. They aren't too difficult, telegraph very well, and most can probably be beaten by a new player on their 2nd or 3rd try. Some were pretty fun. Many also have very convenient flowerbeds nearby to drop a quick vestige to shorten the runback.As far as stats, all of them begin softcapping pretty early. I noticed Endurance and Vitality would simply not give me any additional carry weight, stam, or HP every other level around 30, and only a marginal amount of either when it did, making it feel like a slow, grindy, power-creep. After hitting 30 in the major stats, leveling up beyond that just never felt rewarding and more like a waste of vigor I could've spent on Salts or Ammo Pouches, because there was just no noticeable improvement. The biggest influence in your damage output is upgrading weapons. Thankfully, you'll find plenty of upgrade materials before too long so it's not really an issue to upgrade your preferred weapon or a new one you want to try out.Overall, this just isn't very good. I'm tired of constantly fighting the same mini-bosses over and over and picking up the same gear over and over. Nothing is keeping my interest now. But I will finish it.Skip this one, go play Lies of P, an objectively far better souls clone.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: It is clear now that the devs are actually listening to their playerbase and making changes that are requested. Lowering the number of enemies and reducing the annoying parts of the game has been requested a lot and they are addressing the issue. Given how the devs are rapidly patching the game and listening to community feedback, I have decided to change the review to a positive review. That being said I'm going to leave my original review below.--Old--I've never been so frustrated playing a souls-like game. There are so many tedious things working against the player that it makes the game so annoying to play. For every positive thing about this game, it is heavily outweighed by an annoying choice by the developers.-Level Design-The level design for this game is visually impressive and fundamentally annoying. The Umbral transformation has some amazing set pieces, but the game feels like it doesn't want you to take time to enjoy them. Every single area in this game is flooded with enemies. Time to rest and time to just enjoy the scenery just doesn't exist in this game. The real world is already flooded with enemies, but if you need to go into the Umbral for any reason, you easily double the amount of enemies you are going to be facing. New enemies exclusive to the Umbral and also the enemies you were already fighting will show up and fight. Meaning you can easily be chased by 10+ enemies. After a while of being in the same area, fighting seemingly endless (or literally endless if you are in the Umbral), I decided the best course of action was just to run through every area, fighting as little as possible as it just got so annoying and monotonous to deal with all of the enemies. This game just does not want you to take in it's beauty, it wants you through the game and its areas as fast as possible.-Combat-Combat is... fine? I guess? There isn't anything spectacular about it, and there are certainly some questionable parts about it as well. I really don't understand the implementation of the double tap roll. After you roll, you have to wait to do another dodge of any kind. This means that any boss that combos has a 90% chance of hitting you. The normal standing dodge feels infinitely more effective despite it being less committal. Casting a spell means you are fully committed to casting that spell. You can't cancel it, you can't roll out of it, you just have to sit there and be punished for casting something you may have not meant to cast. Blocking in this game feels mandatory, so if you don't like blocking you are just going to be punished as you don't get to interact with the temporary health mechanic (bloodborne) that it has in place. It feels like this game is just shoehorning the player into a certain playstyle. If you don't play the way the game wants you to play, it is going to be harder and more punishing. Spears feel awful because there are so many enemies, meaning any weapon with cleave immediately becomes S+ tier. -Bosses-Oh boy where to start. This game suffers from Dark Souls 2 syndrome. Where some bosses are incredible, and some bosses are so annoying/nonsensical that it is jarring. I recently ran into a "boss" who later became a normal enemy... and by later I mean literally 5 minutes later. On the complete opposite side of that spectrum, some bosses are just sword sponges that will also literally one shot you. The tracking on some bosses is also ludicrous. I've witnessed a boss that is 10x the size of the player do a 360 that makes CoD trick shotters look like a joke. Some bosses are genuinely enjoyable, but not enough of them that I would consider the game to have good bosses. -Cutscenes-LotF has some of the most jarring cutscenes I have ever watched. The first major boss in the game (not the scripted one) has a cutscene that just abruptly ends after you watch some absolutely disgusting 3D liquid simulation. There are so many cutscenes in this game that just make me say "what?" at the end of them. Not to mention you have to skip the boss cutscene EVERY TIME you want to fight a boss. It is SO annoying. They just use this cutscene to teleport the player to the place that they want them to start at. -Coop-I personally haven't played coop, but it sounds like it was falsely marketed. I would look at other reviews that include coop if you want to read more about it.-Performance-I personally haven't had any performance or crashing issues as other users have, but it is certainly something to consider. The game has run at a solid 60+FPS with the autoset graphics the whole time with no frame drops.TL:DRWith all of this being said, I truly can't recommend this game. It so annoying and monotonous to play with mechanics constantly working against the player. If you are hungering for a souls-like, get Lies of P or play another Elden Ring run. This game isn't terrible, but it's not great. Every great thing has an equally awful thing to play with. A solid 5/10 experience so far. Probably wait until this is on sale if you are considering playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game, and what it set out to be. Did it miss the mark at launch? Absolutely. Did it take them awhile to recover? Unfortunately yes. I think the Umbral/Lamp mechanic keeps people away at times. Know that while it's a big part of the game it does become second nature after awhile. That being said I do think the execution leaves something to be desired.Perhaps if instead of so much in.. out.. in.. out.. in... .you get the point. They just had a few places here and there for secrets, and the big portion of umbral was used to traverse things that no longer existed in the same "state" as they do in the real world, a castle that's partially destroyed becomes somewhat whole, this allowing you to explore umbral when it makes sense. That also allows a more fun mechanic with the vestige seeds, as now you use them as checkpoints to push through this large umbral area, until you finally can get out to an ancient one. That is an idea, maybe it's good maybe it's bad but either way, don't let Umbral steer you away from the game, the level design, enemy design (even though limited), and combat system are all top tier. In the end it's a 10/10 idea but an 8/10 execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Imagine being such a degenerate that you browse the reviews for a game you don’t like and spend your steam points just to put a clown reward on each review that liked it. That’s ironic. Thanks for the steam points, though.I’m going to preface by saying that I’ve never been a massive souls-like fan. The brutal difficulty found me frustrated more than ever entertained in the past. At the time of this review, I played the first dark souls, scholar of the first sin, and Elden Ring, with the vast majority of my time in any of them being in Elden Ring. Still, I haven’t played any of them nearly as much as Lords of the Fallen.With that out of the way:Lords of the Fallen is, as many may have guessed, an unforgiving souls-like game where you spend much of your time navigating a large pseudo-open world. Like other souls-likes, the game pits you against everything between pitiful peons and imaginative hellish behemoths. All of which present a challenge to the player.What separates this title from other souls likes is the impressively implemented dual-realm gameplay. You start the game spending most of your time in the real realm where mortals are picking up the pieces of an apocalyptic medieval wasteland. Later, you’ll likely spend much of your time in what is called the “umbral realm,” which is a mirror to the normal realm, albeit with new challenges and navigation mechanics. You can use your lamp, as the lamp-bearer, to travel to the umbral realm at will. But coming back is a necessity and can often be a big challenge, without spoiling it.In my honest opinion, the combat feels very smooth, if slow. It’s more reminiscent of the earlier souls titles than the later ones, which I respect from a design perspective. This slowness means you’re often committing to attacks you may not have time to commit to, depending on your class and weapons. You’ll have to learn each individual enemy as you play. Fortunately, the developers have designed the enemies of lords of the fallen with clear intent on being what I describe as “hard, but fair.” All of them are readable and can be reacted to with the tools they provide you with.Being a pseudo-open world, you’ll find yourself running into bosses, often accidentally. Some of them are designed for players who have progressed much further than you may have up to the point of coming face to face with them. That’s okay. The player can always leave and come back with higher stats and better gear, which will help more than I can describe. Each major boss is unique and has move-sets that can often change during the fight. Learning and defeating them can be a massive challenge even for a leveled player, but it feels quite satisfying once they’ve finally beaten it. I have myself on record saying at one moment “please… please… I’m so close… please…” and in the next moment, “Yeah, that’s right. Eat the dirt, you ain’t sh**” upon emerging victorious. Every boss, with a few exceptions, has felt that way.Finally, I want to talk about the immersion of Lords of the Fallen. I have never felt so vested into a souls-like as I have with this one. The world is DRIPPING with character. You’ll find the world hopeless and bleak as Hell truly creeps upon the landscape. What clearly used to be villages, castles, and various settlements, is now reduced to ruins due to the scourge of the umbral entities and the often referenced ongoing war. All of the enemies feel very thematic and characterize the area you find them in.The negative reviews seem to come from dark souls veterans. I don’t quite see what they are talking about most of the time, as someone who has spent more time in this game than all  of the other souls games combined. It could be based in reality, but in an admitted vacuum, I am having a lot of fun in this title. There are some clear faults, such as the sheer enemy density in some areas often barring you from truly focusing on a fight. The stability of the game is quite shaky at times with new areas loading in with a bit of a stutter as well. But over-all, this game overcomes those challenges with unique concepts and a fluid combat system that gets more addicting as you progress.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: * As of version 1.510 New achievements have been added.These can be easily obtained in a couple of hours though. Simply grab your level 200 character that's still on NG+0 and go to a vestige.. Select Restart NG+0 and enable ALL the new Modifiers. Speedrun the game (recommend the Rhogar ending) and you can get all the new achievements at once.If you have the patience to do 2 runs. I recommend saving the achievements with Vestige Decay since that's the most annoying part.Good luck.--* As of version 1.0Full disclaimer: * I have been ( ) part of Hexworks and on the LOTF development team* I checked the "received for free" box just to be safe, even though i "paid" for the game with 3+ years of my life :)* This is my personal opinion, and nothing else.Now with that out of the way:Getting 100% was... challenging, grindy but addictive and satisfying.approximate amount of time to 100%: 60-120 (latest 100% save file features 113 hours but I did take my time and didn't focus exclusively on achievements)Estimated achievement difficulty: 6/10 [varies wildly based off your experience with this game type]Minimum number of playthroughs needed: 3 Complete (Normal, NG+, NG+2)Multiplayer achievements: YES!. 6 Achievements require multiplayer.Missable achievements: YES!. Certain actions disable quests/achievements for the current playhtrough.Grinding Achievements: YES!. Multiple "collect all" type achievements that must be completed on the SAME CHARACTER. (they do carry over into NG+)DLC-Only achievements: No.Time-gated achievements: No.Speed-run achievements: No.RNG-achievements: Kind'of!. Needed weapons/Armors have a chance to drop from enemies, but no hard RNG, with enough tries they are guaranteed to drop eventually.Does difficulty affect achievements: No difficulty choice.First achievement unlock: In the tutorial section at the beginning of the game.Unobtainable/glitched achievements: /!\ warning /!\. There are users complaining of experiencing progression blockers online. While the team has been (and is) working hard at fixing these issues anything can happen.Notes:- I recommend following guides online to plan your achievement roadmap if you want to optimize your 100% journey... That being said, I do feel it is best to play the game blind the first time to experience it and then start a new character aiming for all achievements while making sure you're not missing any vital collectibles.- By far the most time of this 100% was spent killing enemies repeatedly to acquire their gear. Even with the "item drop chance" items used together (they stack) enemies will still take many runs to drop their respective items. - Community Items (weapons and armors unlocked at the multiplayer shrines) are NOT NEEDED for the weapons/armor achievements!- Due to the fact that most of the permanent vestiges are disable on NG+, I recommend not leaving NG+0 (normal game) until you're sure you have everything you need. I also recommend doing the most complex ending (Umbral) as part of the normal game since that requires a lot of back and forth. - Backing up your save file IS possible if you want to make sure you're not missing anything.Now for my opinion about the game: I think this game is good, great even. It's impossible to not be biased for a product you literally helped into existence but I do honestly feel this way. I had fun moments, I had frustrating moments with it but overall don't regret any part of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much potential that is wasted due to one of the worst map designs I've ever seen in a souls-like. They've tried to connect different regions together and used way too many completely pointless shortcuts that do not help with progressing at all. Navigating the dungeons is a nightmare and every new path leads to the checkpoint from the beginning like you're constantly running in circles.Enemy variety is not nearly enough and they had to make up for it by using mini bosses showing up as mobs after defeating them once. The enemy density too high in most of the areas and they are intentionally positioned in the most inconvenient places. Coupled with the over complicated map design this has resulted in an extremely tiresome and unpleasant experience. which is a shame considering that the setting and the theme of the game look really nice.Auto-locking is terrible and combat system could be better. The game needs a lot of balancing fixes which in fairness it has been getting to some extent but there is still a lot to be done; for example ranged attacks of mobs are too strong and too accurate.Overall the game is overly tedious and annoying without any sense of satisfaction and I think they completely missed the point of what makes a good souls-like. The technical support has been decent so far and I've been receiving patches (sometimes as many as twice a day) but what's holding the game back is some fundamental designing flaws that I don't think can be changed at this point. I finished the game not because I enjoyed it but because I had payed for it and I wanted to see it through and I doubt I will play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: While in the beginning the game was hardly even worth instant gaming prices, now that they spent each day after release working on it(liteally a patch per day) i can say the game is shaping to be really good. Most technical issues have been fixed and the game runs smoothly now. If u are a soulsplayer, the closest game i could compare Lords of the Fallen to would be a mix between DS1 and DS2. Good and bad from both : enemy placement and aggression (which has been already nerfed/reduced), not much variety in terms of movesets, lots of weapons, being a caster in this game is weird since it feels like a tps instead of the usual magic caster we are accustomed to in souls games, a well inter-connected map, graphically okay but it still blends in that ominous feeling that ds1 shares. Lastly, the game is rather easy or i should say: the maps are hard but the bosses (a good part of them) are easy and the player have tons of way of surviving. Overall im enjoying the game and im looking forward for DLCs and if u are deciding which to buy between Lies of Timotee Chalamet and Lords of the fallen, i have this to say: Lies of P offers the closest gameplay similar to Bloodborne and sekiro but it does not do good in any of the game it tried to mimick and it will barely last u 20 to 40 hours(depending on how good u play) and overall i'd say its better than Lords but Lords of the Fallen(at least to me) feels more fun and i can play it a lot more with invasions and coop being a thing. So in a totally non biased way, i'd give Lords of the Fallen a solid 7.8/10 (which with Dlc could go higher). For comparison, Lies of P is an 8/10, dont trust youtubers trash opinions, its good but not that good especially considering it had to copy fundamental mechanics from both Bloodborne and Sekiro, the story is good tho.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried. I really really tried to enjoy this game. Unfortunately, due to persistent and completely un-fixable performance and stability issues, this game is not one that I can recommend.And it is actually unfortunate, because I *would* have recommended this game, had there been some way to stop the game from hitching and crashing. Is the game perfect? No, not hardly. There are dozens of little issues and frustrations I could deep-dive into, but honestly they really don't matter when the game simply does not run correctly.Before you comment to suggest fixes, save your effort. I did LITERALLY EVERYTHING that could possibly be done to stop the game from crashing and to improve hitching and performance issues. It is not a hardware problem, my PC components are relatively new and stable, and fully capable of handling the game (NVMe SSD, RX6600, Ryzen 5600X, 32GB of DDR4 3200). My install of Windows 11 is fresh as of a few months ago and fully updated. My GPU drivers were completely cleaned and freshly reinstalled with the latest stable versions. I disabled GPO via regedit, and also changed windows TDR settings to make driver timeouts wait 60 seconds (per the official UE5 documentation). I made modifications to the Engine.ini, also per UE documentation, to try and fix hitching and timeouts. I even tried stuff I knew wouldn't work, like setting the .exe to run in administrator mode, or in compatibility mode, etc. as some have suggested in various forum threads. Absolutely nothing affected the game crashes, though some of the Engine.ini changes did improve hitching somewhat.Ultimately, the crashes and performance issues are a direct result of the game and the developers. Whether it's due to a lack of familiarity with the Unreal Engine, or a lack of experience/expertise in performance and stability, or some other issue, I can't really say. What I can say is that the game unforgivably crashes consistently, and not just on PC, reportedly it also happens on console.If it weren't for the performance and stability problems, I would be happy to give this game a 7/10 and recommend it for any souls-like fan that's looking for another game to play. As it stands, the game gets a 4/10. Skip it until they confirm all crashing issues have been resolved.EDIT: Addendum-I wanted to add here that most of the game was played through using the seamless co-op, alongside a friend with almost identical hardware specs. His game crashed almost exactly as often as mine did, and the crashes were consistent both online and offline, though the crashes happened more frequently while playing co-op. The issues appear to be localized to specifically AMD graphics cards and *specifically* on the DX12 backend of UE5, and happens in multiple other games that also use the same engine and backend. The problem could probably be fixed by simply enabling one of the other backends in the engine, like DX11 or Vulkan, but the devs have chosen not to do this for some unknown reason.

_childDocuments_.review: These are my first impressions of the game as a Souls Veteran, having played all Fromsoftware Souls catalog and other games in the genre, I can confidently say Lords of the Fallen is a great Soulslike, and an amazing game.In the first set of hours I’ve had with the game, it’s clear every single person involved in this project loves Fromsoft’s games. The structure is quite similar, both in gameplay and menus. If you’re a Souls player already, you’ll fell right at home. In the first hour or so, the game kinda bombards you with lots of tutorial messages to explain its differentiating features, that is if you choose to receive tutorial messages, and you can feel a bit overwhelmed, I thought that while watching a gameplay before buying. However, actually playing for myself it all makes perfect sense and I had zero problems absorbing and using all mechanics, it all feels very natural and intuitive given your toolset.Contrary to some comments, the gameplay doesn’t feel janky or clunky at all, it may not be as smooth as butter, but it’s ALMOST there, combat feels engaging and has weight on the impacts, movements carry momentum, adding to the FEEL of the blows, the sounds and animations are everything you would expect from a top notch souls, oh and running actually feels like running, it’s fast, agile and precise. The default controls are very similar to Elden Ring in that respect. Aside from that, ranged combat takes a completely different approach than in Fromsoft’s titles, and has proven to be a step in the right direction for me, making bows and such actual reliable and useful tools both in combat and exploration.So yeah, the game FEELS really good to play, but it doesn’t just stop there, it is also quite a LOOKER. The art direction in this game is nothing short of amazing, the scenarios and landscapes you’ll come across are stunning, the architecture and placement of objects is very well done as well. Bloodborne and Dark Souls vibes just oozes from every place you encounter yourself in, and it’s not just a mish mash, everything feels right and properly placed within the universe.It's an Unreal Engine 5 game, which makes it very good looking on the graphics department, great lighting effects, dense and “populated” environments. The whole Umbral world, basically the Upside Down from Stranger Things, can be rendered on top of the existing map, which I thought to be a very clever use of the new engine’s tech. It has support for both DLSS and FSR, and that is ALWAYS nice to see. That being said, it’s a HEAVY game to run, my rig is a RTX 4080 + R9 7900X @1440P I can get around 100+ FPS on ULTRA with DLSS on Quality mode, and around 70 – 80 with just DLAA. I haven’t encountered any problems with performance such as stuttering, freezes or crashes, but doing some quick math it’s easy to see why so many people are having issues. I really hope the Devs can optimize the game further and iron out possible problems other players are having with future updates, because at the end of the day, the more people that get to play this game, the better!I didn’t preorder the game because I wanted to wait for day one to actually see if it was what I was looking for and after seeing how quickly the Devs released updates, even after the day one patch, and how they were responding a lot of Steam reviews with detailed steps for troubleshooting, man… I just knew they really want this game to do a lot better than the other game with the same name. I know it’s probably the “bare minimum”, but nobody does the bare minimum today, so I just had to check it out. I will update this review when I’m finished through my first, of 3 planned, playthroughs.Now that I’m done writing this essay, I’ll return to play and have a heck of great time.P.S. Rolling on barrels and wooden structures is 1000x more satisfying than in Elden Ring, both in sound and visual effects.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll leave my original review at the bottom, but I will change to a thumbs up after some much needed attention from the devs. I'm glad they listened and fixed a lot of the things players have complained about. It shows that they do in fact care and want their game to succeed. Showing the ongoing balancing they will be doing, splitting balancing between PVP and PVE, and the extra quests and things they are adding is pretty cool. There have been several poor decisions made, and several decisions that made sense but were poorly handled, but the devs have been listening and doing what they can. Give it a shot, it's a solid Souls-Like and a lot of fun. This game has so much potential. And the world is awesome! But the devs are incredibly out of touch with their player base and the patches they have released are focused on nerfing everything and making things harder to farm, which is ironic given the latest patch ruined boss weapons and their response was "go farm more." Instead of working on the performance of the game, they want to make sure you don't have fun apparently.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely give reviews but I feel like this game should've been better...I was very disappointed at the level of repetition in the game with the enemy placement and types...The level design is abysmal in my opinion, compared to souls games it is very poorly made, sure, the umbral world side of things is cool and all, but it get tiresome after the first 5 times you go into it. As for the level design, it always feels like a maze being in any map, whenever you find a new way to go, the reaction is usually "♥♥♥♥ sakes I'm back here again" rather than "oh this was a shortcut" which is the feeling I get playing souls games...The wither effect and idea is nice I will give that credit, it just feels like with this sort of combat that is relatively clunky, it makes it unfun...The style, weapons, atmosphere and armors are great and all, but it rarely changes to a high degree, so it feels like new areas don't feel as fresh or as memorable as they should be...The bosses are alright at best, no boss made me think to myself "damn I did it" it was always either "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ finally" or "tf was that?"...Overall I just find it hard to respect a so-called 9/10 when it feels like a 5-6/10 at best when playing it, hopefully the devs keep updating like they are already, they seem driven. In all honesty I still respect the attempt, it is a major update from the first game, but still.. it's very very far off of being a memorable souls like or even a game that I might think of replaying after a while like I did with most souls games...

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a good game. Do not buy and save your money. I was excited about this game because of the Lord of the Rings setting and the Soulsborne style gameplay, but it fails on both fronts. My biggest complaint is with enemy animations. The enemies are so floaty! They move around the screen as if they aren't subject to gravity and it makes reacting really difficult. The first boss is almost unbeatable because of this animation lag. Unlike Dark Souls and Elden Ring where a player can identify weaknesses in the opponent's attack patterns and exploit those in the first encounter, in Lords of the Fallen a player will have to die a large number of times before completely understanding the attack patterns. Leveling up is a grind fest. The graphics are a mess with lots of lag and cut-scenes do not play properly. The one thing I do like is the way ammunition/ammo is handled. Overall, the game is not enjoyable and is more frustrating than anything. Save your money and keep playing Elden Ring, Dark Souls, Hollow Knight, or Dead Cells. Those are all way better "souls" games.

_childDocuments_.review: A good soulslike with great map/level design similar to Dark Souls but some questionable design choices. Combat feels good and although most boss fights aren't particularly difficult, they're still fun and well designed. Glad to see they didn't copy paste the spell action system Fromsoft uses and instead went with the more modern version of holding a trigger and having multiple button presses assigned to spells. Unfortunately there are not many ways to regen mana outside of consumables and a few rings/runes. For some reason you cannot view detailed stats? It's an RPG. Let me see stat breakdowns.One of the biggest downsides are the tedious amount of enemies the game throws at you sometimes. I'm talking easily 10+ mobs on your screen at once. At that point you just free aim everything and hope you're using a weapon with a wide swing. Another is the sheer amount of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ranged mobs that snipe you across the map. Honestly, most of my deaths come from getting shot in the back by some random mob 30ft away. By far the biggest negative is the quest system. It's pure Dark Souls to a fault; easy to completely miss and easy to completely break. Some quests also don't make much sense progression wise. For example; one NPC had me collecting items I found along the way and on the final turn in, his next location was an area I had cleared half the game ago. It's still a good game, but much of that owes to the level designers. The whole world is connected and it's great. It's just a shame the performance was terrible for some people at the start and that just negatively(and rightfully) affected their initial impression.

_childDocuments_.review: Not finished so here's some of my thoughts on it:+ The world is very cool and interconnected, it creates a good sense of exploration and when you find several ways to progress some that will lead back to other areas you have been in, good stuff.- The movement is floaty which makes platforming feel as if your going to fall of anything that isn't a full platform and some jumps are surprisingly tight, enemies can also snipe you in the air(this game has a ton of snipers and they do a lot of dmg) which will drop you to your death instead of simply doing damage. In combat your character will launch off from melee attacks or the disjointed roll, enemies will also slide all over the place when attacking, it's comical but feels horrible.- Plenty of small bugs, not being able to confirm with a prompt forcing you to exit and restart dialogue with a character to use any of the options like buy, sell etc. Getting stuck in invisible geometry from jumping where they probably didn't think you would.- I have not finished it but got spoiled and looked up the "final bosses", only one ending has a final boss and it's the hardest one to get.One of my biggest issues in any game like this where you power up your character through the entire game and there's so much combat, to get to the end and not have a final fight is heinous. - New items you pick up get automatically added to item slots.- Hitboxes are all over the place, attacks that do dmg or hit you far off from where the animation or elemental effect is.- Got one npc killed by jumping past it.- Many animations even when finished will make taking out the lantern take about 2seconds, it may be intended but it feels extremely bad when in combat.- It runs horribly.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Weapons, armor and spells are visually cool.- The open world is beautiful.- The Umbral feature is a neat idea and adds depth to the game.- The opening boss and  are proper challenges; the opening boss could be a deal breaker for people not used to the difficulty of Soulslike games (get gud).Cons:- Certain builds are waaaay too overpowered (i.e. a properly built Radiant class, I was able to shred through the game comically easy with some of the spells).- Pretty much every boss is waaaay too easy to defeat; I felt like this game was not a challenge whatsoever with the correct build.- Some side quests are still buggy (i.e. nobody really seems to know how to ensure that you trigger the boss fight with Kukajin to get the None Shall be Spared achievement; this caused me to have to restart a playthrough to trigger her fight and get the achievement which is very frustrating and almost caused me to quit the game due to a bug that shouldn't exist).- The  is way too finicky to achieve; even a small misstep (i.e. ) can throw off your ability to complete this main quest, which could cause you to restart a playthrough to get it.- This game is not very similar to Lies of P, but both are still considered Souslike; personally I think Lies of P is a much better and more refined experience with less bugs and more straightforward gameplay that is much more challenging than Lords of the Fallen.Overall, this is a good effort at a Soulslike game but it is outclassed by another Soulslike game that dropped right before it. I think with some changes this game could be a lot better, but it is still quite frustrating at certain points.6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Starting this off by saying this game is good. I'm not quite sure why this game has gotten so much grief for being too similar to dark souls, It is unique in its own ways and feels rewarding to play. Atmosphere:This games setting and atmosphere is phenomenal, I'm a massive fan of the more twisted art style. They nailed the feeling of unease when in umbral, and not just because of the possible extra enemies that could be lurking there. Not to mention the graphics are very good as well.Combat:The combat feels more comparable to DS2 (my favorite out of the trilogy, seems I'm in minority on that one) with the ability to power stance any two weapons of your choosing. The dodge action is more of a sidestep than the traditional souls role, but while sprinting or not locked on you will do a long range roll with a large amount of I frames (maybe too many, I found it a bit cheesy feeling at times). enemy density feels overall lower than some of the areas in the souls games but the enemies feel more opposing to face. Boss fights felt a bit too easy for me but the devs have already started tuning their difficulty.Loot:The most important category of all... loot. The armor and weapons in this game are truly beautiful. My personal favorite armor so far is the Harrower's armor, paired with the Neophyte hood. My favorite sword design wise is Vanguard Barro's Sword. TLDR: Lords of the Fallen gets my recommendation if you are looking to scratch that souls itch, the setting is great and so are the weapons and armor you can get along the way. The devs have been doing an amazing job listening to community feedback so far and I'm excited to see where they can take this game and series.

_childDocuments_.review: I have completed this game, and I'm still unclear about its intended goals and creative direction. It has left me with numerous unanswered questions, and none of them pertain to the forgettable and misguided story.To provide some context, my initial curiosity and concerns rapidly evolved after reaching the Empyrean section of the game, but I'll come back to this later.Around 90% of this game feels like a grind, artificially inflating difficulty through an over use of enemies rather than offering complex enemy mechanics. This approach is a significant misstep. The extent to which this game commits this "souls-like" sin is frankly unacceptable. It results in frustration, unfairness, and a lack of engagement, leading players to rush through each area, pick up an item, and move on.Additionally, the variety of enemies is quite shallow, and after a couple of hours, you've essentially encountered all the game has to offer. It's not a deal-breaker, but it does become repetitive.The bosses, one of the more interesting aspects of the game, unfortunately lack in difficulty, underscoring the developers' lack of understanding of what makes a Souls-like game special. It fails to appreciate the significance of interesting and learnable enemy mechanics which creating both a challenge and a memorable boss fight. Being able to stroll through most boss battles (excluding gimmick bosses) using dodge and heavy attacks is dull, and I can't recall a single memorable boss encounter.The level design is good but not exceptional. While you'll encounter some interesting locations and opportunities for exploration, the core mechanic of the "umbral world" is hindered by its poor execution. This concept of a world within a world holds promise but is marred by tedious constant switching, slow animations, and jarring transitions, making it more of a chore rather than an intrigue. My most significant complaint is how it worsens the issue of enemy density, adding to the game's frustration.Now, let's get to the point where all the issues and frustrations compound, leaving me genuinely bewildered by an anomalous area.Upon reaching Empyrean, I was greeted with a vast, desolate, and ominous space, free from the cheap ganks and clusters of enemies that had frustrated me earlier. I had discovered an area that felt as if it were designed by an entirely different team. The enemy density was lower but more challenging. These enemies required some strategy and had interesting design mechanics. It was a breath of fresh air, despite being so small. I stumbled upon a unique opponent lurking in the shadows, a generic enemy by the game's standards, but it was anything but ordinary. It fought fiercely with a different move set, using throwables and radiant spells I hadn't seen before. For a brief moment, I thought I had been invaded (which hadn't happened yet). It was honestly the best impromptu fight in the game, surpassing every story character boss fight.How did this happen? Why did the game's tone change so drastically in this one area? Why was this unique enemy type used only once? Why weren't other enemies designed in a similar way?This was the game's finest moment, and it was the shortest part of the entire playthrough.To whomever created the Empyrean area, congratulations on creating the pinnacle of what this game could offer, but at the same time, it highlights just how poorly directed and balanced the rest of the game is.I genuinely want to recommend this game, I really wanted to enjoy myself equal to the time I invested, but based on my experience and the inconsistency in game I find it challenging to recommend. Not to mention the blatant lies and disappointment regarding cross-play Co-op (which is why i bought the game, and never got to experience with my friend).If you must, consider buying the game on sale. At the time of writing this game is not worth your time or money.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a sad feeling to say, but I feel like I enjoy the original Lords of the Fallen game MORE than this remake. I liked how if you used a heavy weapon, it felt like a heavy weapon, but did very great damage; clunky in a fun way. And while the new mechanics to this game is 'neat', it's the annoyance of particular enemies that dulls the experience quite fast, and the constant punishment of, "Hehe, I'm by the corner and you couldn't see me with these tight walls. Goodbye to your HP! :3"..If I wanted to play check the corner simulator, I'd just go to playing any Call of Duty game and be more content getting a kill. And the other thing that I find ridiculous, is the constant hyper-armor. I can understand bigger mobs having better poise, but if I'm mid attack and can't cancel my attack to try and block, I'll immediately lose again, a large chunk of my life. I have to be utterly paranoid poking literally any mob, and backing up or waiting for them to attack so I can either deflect, dodge, or cry in the corner as they pound me to death anyways.I'm hoping that over time, HOPEFULLY, there might be some improvements in some ways to make it not as tedious. I may try back occasionally time and time again to try and give it more tries, but as of right now in this review, I'm going to have to give it a no unfortunately.

name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos
detailed_description: The best-rated paid Oculus Quest App as of January 2021 according to Road to VR! Won the Adventure Category Award for the Famitsu/Dengeki 2020 Game Awards! *Famitsu is the most prestigious video game magazine starting in 1986 in Japan Note: This game contains multiple unlockable paths - don't stop playing at the first credits roll! This isn’t a dream... Dive 300 years into the future of Tokyo. ALTDEUS features 15-20 hours of gameplay with one of the largest branching storylines ever in a VR game. Become Chloe, a mecha pilot who will have her revenge and annihilate the Meteora once and for all. Pilot a giant mecha and make the decisions to determine humanity’s future. Converse with other characters and seek clues in the Adventure Section. The Mecha Battle Section is where things get rough, as you enter the cockpit of Makhia, the towering humanoid anti-Meteora combat weapon. Your choices and actions branch the story leading to multiple-endings. Features: Mecha Battle Section: Your actions in this section lead to different stories. You can enjoy stellar VR concerts. The Libra AI suggests possible choices for you in the Adventure section. Interact with objects in real-time and solve mysteries. This game has high ratings from game media including an 80 Metacritic score. You can experience the anime mecha battles of your childhood dreams and immerse yourself in the deep story of this world. Story: The year 2280. Humanity sought safety and salvation deep underground, establishing Augmented Tokyo. This 2km radius underground city became humanity's last bastion. Chloe, a member of the Anti-Meteora military organization Prometheus, defends the city in her Makhia, a massive battle robot, battles against the Meteoras, alien beings of immense size and strength, with her companions. Everything she does, she does for her fallen friend. Her dearest friend. Coco. Everything Chloe does is to avenge Coco. Crucial choices and decisions are coming to you next by next. Can you pull the trigger? This game is highly recommended for people... looking for a VR game with a lengthy story and replayability who love story-oriented games, anime, or movies who love games but are not good at playing difficult ones looking for a game that doesn’t cause motion sickness wanting to be passionate with their childhood dream experiences wanting to pilot a mecha of their very own
