Become Chloe, a mecha pilot who will have her revenge and annihilate the Meteora once and for all. Pilot a giant mecha and make the decisions to determine humanity’s future. Converse with other characters and seek clues in the Adventure Section. The Mecha Battle Section is where things get rough, as you enter the cockpit of Makhia, the towering humanoid anti-Meteora combat weapon. Your choices and actions branch the story leading to multiple-endings. Features: Mecha Battle Section: Your actions in this section lead to different stories. You can enjoy stellar VR concerts. The Libra AI suggests possible choices for you in the Adventure section. Interact with objects in real-time and solve mysteries. This game has high ratings from game media including an 80 Metacritic score. You can experience the anime mecha battles of your childhood dreams and immerse yourself in the deep story of this world. Story: The year 2280. Humanity sought safety and salvation deep underground, establishing Augmented Tokyo. This 2km radius underground city became humanity's last bastion. Chloe, a member of the Anti-Meteora military organization Prometheus, defends the city in her Makhia, a massive battle robot, battles against the Meteoras, alien beings of immense size and strength, with her companions. Everything she does, she does for her fallen friend. Her dearest friend. Coco. Everything Chloe does is to avenge Coco. Crucial choices and decisions are coming to you next by next. Can you pull the trigger? This game is highly recommended for people... looking for a VR game with a lengthy story and replayability who love story-oriented games, anime, or movies who love games but are not good at playing difficult ones looking for a game that doesn’t cause motion sickness wanting to be passionate with their childhood dream experiences wanting to pilot a mecha of their very own
short_description: A sci-fi adventure full of robot battles, pop music, and emotion. Featuring one of the largest branching storylines ever in a VR game with 15-20 hours of gameplay, Altdeus will place you in the shoes of Chloe, a pilot in humanity's forces fighting massive hostile organisms known as the Meteora.

_childDocuments_.review: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos’ is not so much a game, more a fully interactive graphical novel with some great voice acting and animations. While it does lack interactions most of the time it is surprisingly immersive and I especially like the giant robot fights by pressing all the buttons in time, but I also missed being up close and part of the action at the same time. While it is way too short for its own good there are multiple endings for you to explore and some of them will take you a good while to discover. If you like graphical novels you will love this, but mainstream gamers might find it lacking in excitement. Personally, I loved it even if I wish it was cheaper.
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game I've played so far this year and the #1 VR VN I've played to date by a long shot! The first ending is around 3 hours in but it's more like a prelude. The full game has about 15 hours of content to get all the endings and each branch adds huge swaths of story and character development so you really feel compelled to play through them all. There are also a couple music videos built into the story that you can go back and revisit any time which gives you some reason to boot up the game every now and then even after 100% completing it. Music videos in VR are awesome!This is the single best designed VR VN I've played so far. Everything is voiced, the subtitles work perfectly without being hard to read, there's just a little bit of interaction and freedom to mess around with things to keep things interesting and I like how the scenes are partially animated. One problem Tokyo Chronos had was a LOT of internal monologuing that broke the pace of conversations but there's none of that here. All the conversations flow very naturally which makes it far more immersive.Characters will do short animations to add life to their dialog but then freeze-frame to give the impression of typical VN sprites. It almost always feels like a style choice rather than a cop-out. The exception to this would be a few scenes at the end (that I won't spoil with details) where the camera cuts to black instead of showing something interesting being animated. Those parts are pretty rare, though, and it works great the rest of the time.Another nitpick is some of the English voice actors were *really* flat. Chloe's English VA was a little flat but she's supposed to be emotionally repressed so it wasn't terrible. Coco's English VA, on the other hand, was very flat and really terrible. The rest of the English cast and all of the Japanese cast were pretty great, though.Overall, I highly recommend this to any fan of VNs. If you want to check out some of the gameplay, I have a playthrough up to the first ending available on my channel:

_childDocuments_.review: A warning, this is a Visual Novel, not an Action Game.For players wishing to learn how to find the different branches, there seems to be, in general 4 Heroine Endings, each with Good and Bad, and after each ending, the start screen will display a silhouette of the "heroine"'s ending you unlocked. The first 2 times you play the game, you will unlock "extras" in the next playthrough, so Ending Meteora will be the first, after that, you will be capable of unlocking the second branch for Endings Noa and Anima, and after any of them, you unlock the ability to open the final branch, to the Coco Ending (Final).In Ariadne, a visual representation of the story line and its branches, you can see the ramifications, and can also jump through past events from past branches at any time if you want to complete things. There is also a mini "encyclopedia" of terms in Ar, holding important terms of that event and what they meant at that time, so if you forgot something, check those to remember. However, you can only jump into major events, so sometimes, you may have to backtrack a lot if you want to just check the other option that you just went through because there were no major events in some time.For how to play the game, you will go through 3 types of events:- Novel mode is the most common, as the novel advances through it, and is the easiest to explain: People talk, you read, and so on. On a very strangely adopted method you have choices, which affects hidden parameters, like Obedience, Independence, being Open Minded and so on, but because there are no numeric parameters, my impression is that it changes the options you may face ahead, I would imagine that, if I'm too obedient, I may be unable to go against an order in the future, and if I'm too rebellious, the choices may not allow me to agree with certain characters. This is just a guess, as I have no real idea how it works, but for example, in my second playthrough where I was a little nicer to Noa, I got to see her concert, and I didn't even had such option in the first playthrough, but of course, maybe it's locked the first time, or maybe it was related to the parameters, but this uncertainty is awesome and just makes things more natural, because I don't need to think too much, and just go with what I think will be better, without worrying about missing much either.The main problem is that, unlike other novels, there is no Log button, so careful when skipping text, as you can't read what you skipped, and will have to go back to the title menu and start the current part from the start to see it again.- Search Mode are somewhat rare, but they are basically the moments when you have multiple options to either interact or talk with people. Sometimes it's just to interact with things or talk with the characters, but once interacted, unless they have an extra event, you can't do it anymore, and without Logs, be careful with button pressing again. The worse part of this is that there is no indication on what advances the story or not, so if you went to check on something and you left the place because you thought you would have to do something else to advance the story, well, you will move, and any other interactions will be lost until another play through. You don't lose anything technically, just... That feeling of 100% as soon as possible... Search mode may also be used in small puzzles, although those are linear, basically, find the item you have to interact to advance the story... Well, it's basically the same thing, really.And here is the best part:- Mecha Battles. They are essentially an **overloaded Novel Mode**: It's mostly linear and you don't have much control, but it's more interactive (press buttons), and sometimes you may have choices (attack, don't attack, if allowed, do something else), and is where you will find some branches in the story.But... The experience... It can't be described. Check the official website for the artists doing the sound design to understand what I mean: For the Sound Track, you have someone from MONACA, who is also known for OSTs like the Nier series, although if I were to compare the OST here, they remind me more of Gundam Unicorn, Aldnoah Zero, and Guilty Crown (the three by Hiroyuki Sawano). There is also kz (livetune), very famous for many great Hatsune Miku songs.Please MyDearest, do sell the Soundtrack on Steam!For the sequence of events, all mecha fans are guaranteed to love it: You have a full launch sequence, filled with the boot process, your Operator/AI/Partner Noa giving you her blessings, and mind you, she stays in the cockpit singing the battle theme, with a sound similar to Hiroyuki Sawano's more agitated insert songs.I feel like I'm piloting the Macross, and I'm not talking about the Valkyries, instead, it's heavy and clunky, reminding me more of the the Battle 7, Battle Frontier or Macross Quarter in Battle mode, and everything you do and see is from the cockpit, so for example, up until now, I have not seen my own mecha properly (I could be vaguely or partially seen through monitors, or glasses, or even reflection when I'm inside, but never from a 3rd person view), the movements, although limited in view, feel a bit clunky, but not as in "bad clucky", but as in "I'm piloting a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Macross" type of clunkiness, so you know the weight of the movements, or when you get hit (although, of course, the VR can't make itself heavier).You get all the dialogues and tension that you have to do to defend and attack, like pressing the floating buttons, or holding your hips guns, joining them into some Hyper Gun, and then aim, and as the sequence starts, and you have to press the button the the proper time to shoot, or you miss (The main mecha, the Alto Makhia, is a Cannon type mecha. The Ares Makhia, which uses a sword, is controlled by another character, which is soon to receive a DLC, so I'm expecting somehow being able to battle with the sword).Keep in mind, this is not a fighting game, so if you are expecting Gundam Vs type of action, you may even feel bored by having the whole boot up sequence all over again, but if you understand the appeal of the Mecha genre, it's mechagasm: it's like you are in an anime, in first person, with an excellent OST, feeling the excitement of what is going to happen next, I just had to write this review now without even finishing the game yet! It's just that good of an experience, the feeling of inside the cockpit of your robot seeing the battle only through the visor, having your partner by your side talking to you and acting to help. It's a little sad that they are short, and there aren't thaat many of them compared to the rest of the game, but hell, that's why I'm going full playthrough, just to play all those parts again!The plot... It's quite unique, I found small elements that remind me of Aldnoah Zero (OST), Macross (Divas and the "power of song"), Knights of Sidonia (Tsugumi's case) and Genesis of Aquarion (Much shorter than 12K years, if you catch the reference of what I mean), to name a few, only talking about the good parts, of course.Now, do remember that you may wish to change the voices to Japanese for the anime feeling, I just want to play more and more, too bad I need to sleep, the experience is just that GREAT.In regards to it's relationship with Tokyo Chronos being in the same universe, there are 2 names that come straight from there, and they are not that irrelevant. However if you have not played the previous game, at most you will be missing a reference, you won't lose anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: i'm not good at reviewing games but here goesi understand there's several barriers of entry to this game1. it's virtual reality2. it's a visual novel, not that much of a popular genre over here3. one could click expecting mecha fights, but in fact there's only a few and it's all scripted, because the game is a visual noveldue to that, it's naturally going to be restrictive in what you are allowed to do: you cannot freely move in the environment, there's almost no interaction compared to the usual VR game, etc. after all, you're essentially reading an interactive book here.despite all of that, i can confidently say that ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos is a great game. the story hooked me in way harder than i expected, and the multiple branches as well as  really increase replayability. in fact, i'm confident i've completed all of the game on Quest before, and bought the game here for the minor enhancements the Steam version has.if you don't mind spending 20+ hours reading a great game, do play this.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly immersive visual novel made possible with a VR headset; who woulda thunk? Having hands in-game really enhances the immersion and allows you to act out the dialogue and scenes in game. This combined with the excellent music and action set-pieces, really elevated this visual novel beyond many of its peers. If you're a visual novel aficionado and own a VR headset, I highly recommend giving this game a spin. Definitely a fresh take on a somewhat stale game medium/ genre.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW did MyDearest Inc. team do an amazing job on this sequel to Tokyo Chronos.Almost every con that i had with the first Tokyo Chronos game has been much improved upon with this game and i'm happy to see thatIncase you haven't played Tokyo Chronos, ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos is a very well done standalone experience  with multiple endings just like the first game, and does not require having had played the original game. However there are many subtle hints and references to the original game for extra little enjoyment. Personally i found the characters and story great and fun the whole way through. Overall on average the main story of the game is around 15 hours of an experience, and about 20+ hours if you want to do all the endings. As for the gameplay, while on the surface it is just a visual novel, the VR immersiveness and visuals absolutely create an unique and fun experience to play through the game with. There are many options to choose from during the gameplay that actually affects many outcomes. Although there are couple of fun little action scenes and interactive levels they are pretty basic and simple. The characters are very well voice acted (atleast on japanese VA, i haven't tried english voices) and subtitles never get in the way either which is great. Absolutely a huge recommend for this game!!
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos was truly an amazing experience. I went into Tokyo Chronos about a year ago with no expectations and was really blown away by the charm of the game: the characters, the story and the music. That's the reason I was scared of ALTDEUS. Now I had expectations, and I wasn't sure if this game could impact me as much as the previous one did.But now I feel really bad for waiting this long to finally play it.At the moment I'm writing this I have seen all the endings, I just have to go back and see the other variations of the endings (if you played it you know what I mean).This formula of VR Visual Novel is still really impactful. The voice actors (I played with Japanese audio) were perfectly chosen and could convey their feelings really well. Some of the voices you may even recognize from other anime.The characters were once again really well written with their own backstory and ambitions. Some of them you just like from the start, some grow on you after you learn more about them and some of them you hate even more after learning more about them :DThe music is a big step-up to the previous title. Very good soundtrack and also a lot of beautifully vocalized songs. Some even with their own virtual concert. They always went perfect with the current mood in the game and even out of the game hold strong and are nice to listen to (some of them went straight into my playlist). The different endings are really well executed and make you feel a lot of different emotions. I now once again know how bad it is to cry with your headset on, because it's hard to wipe your tears away :DI thought the choice system was a bit confusing at first, but after playing a while you learn to understand and appreciate it. It really felt like every choice could change the story drastically, which of course isn't always true, because there is only a limited amount of routes, but every choice felt important. Now that I finally have these words off my chest, I will play the other variations of the endings and then the DLC Episode. After that I will eagerly wait for the next entry in the Chronos Series, and this time I won't wait a year to play it.Oh and sorry if some sentences sound weird, but English isn't my first language, so please forgive me :D
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying I have never liked anime. I bought this game because it actually looked interesting to me. After playing about 7 hours, now, I can say that I AM A FAN! I love it! As soon as I started playing, I was immediately enamoured and thoroughly engrossed in the story and characters. After the first playthrough, it took me a bit to figure out how to get the other endings (i'm still working on some of them) and going through the dialogue I've already seen is quite frustrating for me, but I finally figured out how to select which scene I want to jump to, and that helped ease the frustration of repetition. Once I got to the ending with Coco, it was all worth it! Even if you're not an anime fan, if you like stories, this game is absolutely worth getting. I'm glad I did! Very well done.

_childDocuments_.review: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos is another title from MyDearest that does an entirely new take on VN. That is, VN in VR.Do note that the game is a VN and not a game as you may come to believe when you hear Giant mech battles.The game is fully voiced both on english and japanese. The voice acting in the game is excellent and it puts a further layer of depth into this fully immersive experience of a VN in VR. While there isnt much interactions across the game, its story is exceedingly immersive as every choice matters, and it gives different dialogue, and in some cases an entirely different ending. There's been paid a lot of focus on the sound design and they've made 40 soundtracks that are all used well in the game to enforce the storytelling, wheter its to be silly, action-filled or emotional, and it clearly made the experience way better.The dialogue in the game is well written, causing emotions like laughter or tears to appear at times. While the first ending may appear too short and you may think thats all, it isnt. This is where the story truly begins. After first playthrough, the story truly expands in many branches and a lot of choices make big differences in the story, which branches out the story, and increases the replayability time and time again, and if you didnt like your choice, you can go back in time using the "Ariadne" system to try the other choices. If you like a good story in a visual novel, you will love this. If you like action however, it might not be too much into your taste, as the game is very dialogueheavy and doesnt include much exitement in the form of action (altho the mech battles are nice).Personally i loved every moment spent in the game, and i hope they will release the OST soon, as the music is amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I liked this game - much more than Tokyo Chronos. It is bigger, better, and more polished in every way. It offers an experience that only VR can offer, and serves as an even better proof of concept that its predecessor. I feel like ALTDEUS just opened pandora's box, and it might just be the progenitor of a new wave of VR visual novels that will be even bigger and better than it is. Even with all its writing hiccups, I believe it is something special and worth trying if you own a VR headset. It is to VR visual novels what half life alyx is to VR adventure games: a huge breakthrough in the right direction for an entire genre. If you're interested in reading beyond this tldr, then here are my pros and cons:Good:+The visuals are wild. You'll be blown away within the first 30 minutes of playing this game. Sometimes, you'll have to crane your neck all the way up to see what is unfolding. Major events in this game happen on a very large scale. Combine this with the binocular vision of VR, and we have something truly special. This leads me into the next point:+The mech sequences are brilliantly directed and choreographed. As I've hinted at before, VR is an amazing medium for making things look large and epic. I've watched and read a lot of mecha anime and visual novels that put you in the cockpit of a mech, but not a single one of them comes even close the capturing the orgasmic scale of ALTDEUS's mech sequences. There's just something about having your entire binocular field of vision being filled up by the cockpit, watching the action unfold in front of you on a giant scale that completely outclasses anything you may see on a simple computer screen. You just have to try this game to see what I mean.+The music is great. Music plays quite a big role in this game, both plot-wise and atmosphere wise. The mech battles would not be half as awesome if it wasn't for the blaring pop music in the background that makes everything feels orgasmically grand and exciting. Imagine watching the last episode of an anime and the opening starts playing. That's how each mech sequence feels. In addition, even when the exciting stuff isn't happening, the music still manages to be very beautiful and fitting for whatever scene they are in. Overall, stellar in the music and sound department.+Although the game is actually very limited in its graphical capabilities, it hides this fact very well through its clever use of lore and visual tricks to hide the parts of it that don't look good, and put the parts that do front and center. Bad:- There's a dialogue tree system that tells you what stats you will gain or lose if you pick one choice or the other. I.e if you pick this dialogue option, you lose 60% obedience, but gain 50% teamwork. This would be fine and dandy if only these stats ACTUALLY DID ANYTHING. They are completely irrelevant and the game doesn't even keep track of them. They only serve as flair and nothing else, which is extremely misleading as the game makes it sound as if they matter when introducing this dialogue system to you.- The story is overly reliant on flashbacks to make you care for a certain character, which in turn only made me hate her.- The main character sucks; she's moody, grumpy, whiny, always going on about how miserable her life is and how everything sucks. Her arc is also very predictable and cliche. It's the same arc that every edgy, whiny protagonist goes through in every visual novel ever, and more often than not I find myself mashing the A button to get through her incessant monologues in which she constantly wallows in self-pity and regret.- The way to progress in this game is still tedious just as it was in Tokyo Chronos. While the story is slightly tighter than Tokyo Chronos, it is still tedious to have to go through entire portions of the game again and again multiple times to finally get to the true ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Very highly recommend the game, 8.5/10 + Voice acting is superb. Honestly, I was blown away at times, you could really feel the emotions of the characters. + Music. Holy cow, each song is memorable and there are moments where it syncs so perfectly to story beats.+ The storyAlthough it can get a bit confusing, I found myself really caring for the characters especially when Anima is introduced. - *mild spoiler* You will have to revist some scenes and it gets a bit annoying relisting to the same dialogue. _childDocuments_.review: Please don't mind the hours on record; I normally play games only on offline mode, but I had to make an exception because I had to review this. It's beautiful in both graphics and story, and I can't recommend it enough! Please be aware that it is a visual novel, so the focus is on the narrative rather than any sort of action gameplay. If you're not a fan of reading (or listening, with the English voice-acting) then this probably isn't the best. It does however do so much more with VR than MyDearest's previous title, which is another wonderful game.A great story about a tight cast of characters seeking love and running from grief. I loved the question posed about what it means to become human, through the lenses of the "Designed" augmented human Chloe, the artificial intelligence Noa, and the primal Anima. This is the sort of science fiction story that I've always wanted to read.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, that trailer doesn't exactly give you a good impression of what the game actually is. I thought the mecha battles would be more than... press five big static "fire" hexagons, then press the big triangle button, then watch the bad guy die. Okay, so away from disappointing mecha battles,,, Storywise the characters repeat the same lines over and over and over. This is a decent story but poorly written. Basically, the Dragon Ball Z of grieving the loss of a loved one. This is sad because there is a gem here, but man, I am rushing through a lot of this dialogue b/c just like this sentence, the same thing is repeated over and over and over. It is poor narrative to tell the reader something they already know, and it is irritating when the story is progressing only to be interrupted for the hundredth time to hear Chloe talk about missing Coco and her unsure feelings. -----Play-Through #2: Started off really well. In the beginning, the developers dropped some of the excess dialogue. It had excellent pacing before: A) Reusing audio bits that didn't fall in line with my choices/decisions... example: I choose not to kill a monster, and for five minutes my character is on board with my decision and having a conversation with another character. They are both like, "Yeah, let's preserve the monster to study it," then out of left field in the next sentence, "Hey, let's kill the monster for revenge," and the other character responds, "Yeah, that monster killed Coco. Let's kill it." I mean wth??? Similar scenarios have happened two other times in my second playthrough, and I think it was just to reuse a sound clip. B) Chloe has an unsure tone 50% of the time I make a decisive choice which makes it feel like my choices don't matterC) The over-explaining once again rears its head.------No movement at all. No teleportation, no locomotion. Zero, zlich. How this game has soooo may high ratings from various VR sites and magazines is beyond me.------Poor atmosphere graphics for such a non-intensive game.-----Having said all this and given the game a Negative review to catch unaware purchasers' attention, and it is 2021, and ALTDEUS is missing a lot of VR innovation and novelty. Some development choices just appear lazy. The visual novel really shoots itself in the foot a lot. 5/10.::Final Edit:: Yes. The Dragon Ball Z of Grieving. All 200+ episodes of Goku fighting that green lizard dude,  but replaced by two girls. One girl always stuck in flashbacks saying, "You're special, Chloe," and Chloe responding in present day, "I miss you, Coco. Why'd you have to go?" A preview of the internal dialogue that takes up 5 hours of a 15 hour game: "Coco." ::mouse click:: "I miss Coco." ::click::  "Coco." ::click:: "I miss you, Coco." ::click:: "Coco." ::click:: "Coco, you always tried to make me smile." ::click:: "Coco, we miss you," ::click:: "I miss you." ::click::"Coco" ::click:: "Why'd you leave, Coco?" ::click::This story needs to cut dialogue. It feels like a meddling rough draft that has a good story, but it needed a workshop intervention and an editor.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really sure what this strange app is about, but seems it has gotten some great reviews, so I gave it a try. This app certainly is not real VR, it's more a very simple collection of 2D images with dialogue (there're some extremely low-quality 3D scenes, probably made for phone gpus). Even for a Quest game this lack of polys would be totally low-end. Even in the city streets you just get dead non-animated images. The app feels more like some sort of low-animated cartoon, where you really have no choices. The story might make just a minimum of sense if you smoke some illegal substances first, to me the story was inconsistent, extremely fragmented and close to the worst garbage I've seen in a long time.This feels like some strange and very early PhoneVR (GearVR). If I should try to be positive, maybe it's some kind of post-modern feverish Japanese manga/anime-like poem. Sound quality was great though, performance was great using Index res 200% (of course, there're no real polys in this game/app - it's animated 2D surfaces or close with a few ok-ish npcs) and you got finger-tracking for the Index controllers.I'd rate this app 2/10 - it's not VR, it's a 2D presentation (image collection) on a big screen. There's no locomotion - you can't even teleport, you're just stuck in the same position. Even in 2016 there were tons of much more advanced apps. I guess this app makes great sense to die hard fans of whatever this extremely strange app is about. I love real VR like Alyx, Boneworks, Medal of Honor: Above & Beyond, Asgard's Warth and Lone Echo - and compared to such real VR titles, this app isn't VR, it's not even close. This is an instant refund to me, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm... not even sure what to write. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Very emotional and with a storyline that pulled me in and held me until the (very satisfying) final ending. And talking about the ending - do not stop playing after you see the first one, it's more of a prelude and the game then continues.The game is not ideal - some aspects (such as the mecha battles) felt clunky and the sense of scale was a bit off. The concerts were also bit disappointing, though I understand this is not an AAA game and the developer simply didn't have enough resources. That being said, the music in the game is wonderful and really adds to the experience. Though English voice acting (especially Coco's) could have been better.All in all, this is a great game and probably best VR visual novel (of which there are not that many, sadly). Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like stepping into the shoes of a great anime story.  I've played some visual novels and enjoyed them immensely... But this one takes it to a new level of immersion.  Featuring impressive production values: the expert utilization of a memorable OST (41 tracks, but felt like there were even more variations with instruments showing up at the right time); distinctive voice actors that I recognize from anime; pretty designs and a compellingly executed story... But furthermore, the player is in a 3D VR space with everyone.  That adds a level of realism that no non-VR game can achieve.  While there are only occasional points where actual VR actions affect gameplay, already just by being in VR with the characters, it furthers the illusion that you are there, experiencing the story.I give this game high marks.  Room for improvement perhaps; with more interactions, more places to visit; but I really, really liked it.  You are getting your money's worth with this game if you like anime and/or visual novels.On a tangent:Games like this make me excited for the future...  Maybe one day this kind of genre will have a new term, no longer a visual novel, but a VR novel.  Its distinguishing feature being the human as the controller as a necessity for full realization.  Detecting body language, eye target, expression, and of course deliberate actions.  Shielding someone?  Choosing to touch a hand?  Pushing someone away?  Moved to tears?  Refusing to look in the eye?  Smiling?  Laughing out loud?I can see a not-too-distant future where subtle character reactions to the player could further enhance a story as a major feature without distracting from the story.  Do you smile at Noa's concert?  Do you refuse to watch?  Give a character a quick nasty look?  Do you gaze at the stars or lock eyes?  Does Anima mimic your expression?  While decisions should still be deliberately displayed, there could be a lot of natural story branching based on the person acting out the story.I don't know about others, but I found myself standing when Chole was standing, and sitting when she was sitting.  And trying to use hand gestures appropriately during the game to enhance the illusion that I was acting out the character.  The more I put into it, the more I got out of it...

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished the first ending, and I am thoroughly enjoying the experience. Without giving anything away, making a visual novel game in VR format isn't just a cheap gimmick. The game really play around with the fact that you are talking with people and looking at things in the actual environment in a very interesting way. Couple with interesting story and great music, this is how I imagine a VN game in VR format should be made. Just be mindful that, at the end of the day, this is a VN and not an action game. You move and interact with things, but do not expect this to be Armored Core or Persona 5 in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: I've not seen a visual novel so seamlessly integrate the nature and mechanics of its branching paths into its own story before. It really is quite an experience. The story itself is a rollercoaster of emotion - though there are numerous dead-end paths befitting the labyrinth symbolism, knowledge acquired from each one is retained without breaking immersion, and gradually leads to the way out. The story poses difficult questions that linger after finishing it. Unfortunately, any more I want to say ventures into spoiler territory.That said, it would be remiss of me to not also mention a few weak points in the experience. There are few interaction phases where you can actually look around and examine things -- this is not immersion breaking, as the protagonist is someone that wouldn't do so without reason, but having the option to do so could have been nice. The combat mecha is used sparingly, which makes the places where it is used more impactful, however, as with my previous comment, it might have been nice to incorporate an option, or a secondary arcade game mode with it. Yet, even with these two weaker points, it is still a well executed and written visual novel that makes good use of the VR space.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes a bit to get going, but I'm so happy I stuck with it! _childDocuments_.review: This is ABSOLUTELY worth it. They really just knocked this right out of the park in every single respect. The story is very compelling, and once you're hooked (took me 15m), the game doesn't let you go until the very end. You get everything from mecha sections and idol concerts to tense standoffs and heartfelt moments which are all punctuated by absolute bangers! I love the characters and really wish the game was longer, I just wanted more time with everyone.As for the VR interactivity, it's still relatively basic but much more plentiful/varied than in Tokyo Chronos. Most of your interactions will be pointing and clicking to 'scan/select' items, or occasionally being able to 'grab/hold' something. The biggest interactions are in the mech, with gestures and some full arm movements. The idol concerts vibrating the controllers in tune with the music was also a neat touch.Can't wait to see what's next!

_childDocuments_.review: The minute I discovered Mydearest had made a new VR novel I jumped on it and...oh the sweet melancholy they once again managed to deliver..A tree full of beautiful branches that lead to leafs of strife and blossoms of relief; each path you go through with new insight brings you to yet another impasse. All the friends and foes you encounter have such rich hidden reasons for doing what they do, and you often initially mistake their true intention.You WILL be shedding a few hidden tears in your headset.Just remember that everything has a reason, so hang in there and...  .

_childDocuments_.review: Like a good amount of review noted, ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos is an animated visual novel. Don't let the tags and screenshots fool you.I went into this game after reading up on it a bit knowing it's a VN, but the screenshot made me have some hope in it having some giant robot action combat. I won't be surprised if each of the story line there own additional information and background about each of the main characters.Highly recommended if you are looking for a good story with different twists in the story depending on the choices you make.

_childDocuments_.review: So far i rate this as Not bad.I love the styling of the V novel, although it feels like more a interactive story than just a visual novel or game but a good concept for VR, the fight scenes to be honest are just there for the narrative, but besides that the look and feel of this V Novel in vr is good. The story while slow to start does pick up just before the second chevo, when you start to find out more about coco (no spoilers), juliea's creepy look is interesting she a total whack job and someone you would never want to shake hands with.  All in all a good start enough to keep me playing.Pro's The VR look is good easy on the eyes which makes your stay in vr easier for example the colours are mute and not in your face this makes your stay in vr more comfortable.Interactions in VR including controls and operating objects work well, e.g. like activating the mech systems they are nice to look at and smooth in operation. note when you sync the arm controls you get that holo looking shield around your arms, they should have left that visible during the battle sequence just for eye candy... Music is nice.easy to listen toStory  up to now is very interesting. Con's The characters themselves need a little work while they look good they come across as bland to look at mainly the male characters,  just minor issue...Story although good at first did drag on until just before the second chevo, if it keeps up the pace it should be good, but if it drops off again and slows down limping from chevo to chevo it could ruin the story for me.One thing i could not get used to, as a man i find it odd looking down in vr to see a pair of breasts coming out of me..This is my opinion up until now it could change as i play further.....
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: I was honestly surprised how much I enjoyed this game. I played tokyo chronos and while I enjoyed it, I felt like it was missing a couple things to really make it stand out. I found ALTDEUS to have superior writing and characters, and the mech parts while lacking in more interactivity, the music and VO really elevated the scenes. I also really appreciate the fact that there was  English dubbing along with the Japanese. Made going through the story much more enjoyable. Most of the english cast did a good job with only one character really standing out for their sub-par performance, though that could have been a directing issue. My only real gripe is that while the VR space is used well for presentation, it's not really utilized all that well gameplay wise. The mech parts were nice spectacles, but they really just ended up being the same sequence with different plot surrounding them. Still, I think this game was pretty good and I'm looking forward to the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible first impression, wonderful English voice acting and an interesting premise too.While I had issues configuring my VR (my fault) at first after resolving that everything worked perfectly.The mecha sequences I've played are quite linear but it feels really awesome to interact with.If you're a VR user and you enjoy anime/mechs and Visual Novels this one is certainly something to look at.
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos takes on a whole new way to experience a Visual Novel, just like in it's predecessor, bringing the genre to VR. And oh boy did they get it right. Imagine your regular Visual Novel game, but now you are literally inside it, being part of the world and it's narrative. It's that awesome.The developers also increased the immersion of the game when compared to it's predecessor. Now you got hands and you can interact with key objects to the story, which heavily contributes to the VR experience. Unfortunately, we still have the floating torso aspect. Having legs and actually moving in the game would surely be a neat feature, but I understand how limited this kind of animation would be inside a Visual Novel, even if it's a VR one. And after being in the game for a while you totally forget about it.Anyway, let's get to the main points of the review:And that's it. The good certainly outweigh the "meh". If you enjoy Visual Novels, are a VR enthusiast, enjoyed Tokyo Chronos or really just want a good narrative experience where you feel like you are part of the story, this game is for you. You won't regret it.Here expecting more games from the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: I played Tokyo Chronos before this and, though unrelated in story, ALTDEUS is certainly the spiritual successor to the aforementioned game.  Comparing to Tokyo Chronos, MyDearest seems to be more comfortable working in the VR space.  The environments are generally more interactive, proportions are more realistic, and better use is made of the VR medium.That being said, before purchasing this game you should know what you are getting.  This isn't a game in the traditional sense like Beat Saber or Half Life: Alyx.  If you have played any visual novels before then the formula will be familiar.  You are playing from the perspective of a single protagonist.  You can occasionally make choices that impact the course of the game, generally resulting in an early demise, a bad ending, or one of several possible good endings or a "true" ending.  Otherwise, you are mostly a spectator viewing the world from the protagonist's perspective.ALTDEUS has a passable story.  There are plot holes, there are poorly explained revelations wrapped in technobabble, and there are one-dimensional characters making questionable choices.  That being said, if you can suspend disbelief and ignore the flaws then it's easy to get immersed in the story and the better-written characters.In particular, the mech battles feel urgent and give a good sense of scale and danger.  Some of the more pivotal moments are choreographed with the excellent musical score, making such moments more impactful for it.Graphics are passable.  Character models and art is generally quite good and well animated.  Background textures could use an improvement, and in particular some background elements were relatively low-resolution 2D sprites that stood out if you noticed them.The Japanese voice acting (I did not play it in English), sound design, and music were great.  The music especially deserves a nod, because not only is it good in isolation but it is used to great effect throughout the game.I can recommend this game to fans of anime and visual novels.  ALTDEUS will feel quite familiar to such players.  To others, imagine a choose-your-own-adventure style science fiction adventure movie.  If that sounds interesting to you, then give ALTDEUS a try.  If you are expecting a more traditional VR experience like SUPERHOT or GORN then this may not be for you, but you may still be presently surprised if you're open to something different.
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: ALTDEUS:BC is a visual novel adventure game directed by Haruki Kashiwakura, the motion director of .Like "428: Shibuya Scramble", players will experience a multi-ending story. As Chloe, the protagonist.It takes about 10 hours to reach the true ending, even with skipping.The endings, with the exception of the true ending, are also independent stories that delve into the psychology of the characters, which makes for a great reading experience.The characters are designed by LAM, a former ATLUS employee, and the mechanics are designed by I-IV of ALDNOAH ZERO.There are the most advanced Japanimation designs.The adventure part is played with VR motion controllers, but the simple controls do not interfere with the story.Choices specific to visual novels are made through a cool 2D interface.In contrast, the mecha action part is a real-time battle in VR.Your actions will affect all events, including the victory or defeat of battles, the life or death of characters, and scenarios.Your enjoyment of this game will be entirely determined by whether or not you enjoy the combat part.The action part uses interactive music to create a cathartic experience as the story unfolds.This game doesn't have all the bells and whistles of a Western AAA title, but it does have a lot of the sharp appeal of Japanimation.I highly recommend it to anyone who has seen the trailer and felt something for it.
_childDocuments_.name: ALTDEUS: Beyond Chronos

_childDocuments_.review: Inversion is yet another asset flip/construction kit flip from serial shovelware copy+paste "artists", Dnovel/FreeAnimals_Software.  These guys do nothing but rip off asset store assets and game tutorials and templates, and dump them on Steam and into DailyIndieGame bundles as cash grabs. Today's "effort" from these guys is Inversion, and it's a garbage 2D retro platformer where the controls are reversed, slapped together with the godawful Cocos Creator game development engine, presumably a copy+paste from someone else's actual work developing a game.  As a game, it's terrible, of course.   In order to make their terrible game schtick "work", they had to ensure you can't remap controls, or you'd just undo the lame gimmick used in the game template they ripped off.   Outside of that, this is just a lulzy bad asset flip platformer.  For that reason, as a "game", this is below acceptable standards, and can be taken as seriously as the "developers" do, i.e., not at all.Using game construction kits doesn't need any talent or professional game development effort, and results in terrible shovelware like Inversion.  The status of this thing as nothing but an asset flip cash grab is cemented by the "developers" prior history of asset flip/construction kit scams, the sheer number of fake/compromised Steam accounts they used to write fake reviews (all with the same broken English), the inflated $4 USD price tag for this garbage, and they way they dumped it into DailyIndieGame bundles.

_childDocuments_.review: Inversion is a third-person co-op shooter that combines hard-hitting, adrenaline-pumping action with a revolutionary gravity manipulation engine. Featuring the Grappler weapon, players manipulate gravity for their own purposes. The Grappler can be used in countless combat situations by maneuvering massive objects as shields or projectiles, and moving camped enemies out of concealed cover so they can be blasted away. The Grappler is also a key tool for tactical situations and puzzle solving as players can lift, move, or create cover objects at their whim. The awesome power of gravity is right at players’ fingertips. Additionally, Inversion is one of the first games to feature Havok Destruction which bestows Inversion with massively destructible environments including an elaborate cover system. Set in the near future, the tranquil peace enjoyed by mankind shatters with an unforeseen invasion by an unknown enemy called the Lutadore. Armed to the teeth with futuristic gravity-controlling weapons, the Lutadore easily overrun the city’s defenses. Unbeknownst to all, mysterious anomalies have surfaced in conjunction with the invasion. Random regions in the city have entered zero gravity or have suffered vector changes, throwing the world into topsy-turvy chaos. Assuming the role of Davis Russel, a hotheaded 28-year-old cop, or Leo Delgado, Davis’ neighbor, players embark on a journey through the disorienting war-ravaged, gravity twisted streets of their home town and beyond, to find Davis' missing child. [Namco Bandai Games]

_childDocuments_.review: Batora: Lost Haven is a game that could have been really good if it was made by more competent developers. As it is, it's just okay. The story has some great ideas that could have been really powerful and emotional, but the writing is just abysmal. The dialogue feels like it was written by an 8 year old and the characters are inconsistent, obnoxious and just plain stupid.There is a choice-and-consequence mechanic and the story does change based on your actions (apparently there are 4 possible endings, as the game was quick to tell me when I got "Ending C", in a futile attempt to get me to play it again), but... it's hard to really care. All choices feel stupid, all consequences are very predictable and uninteresting, I could not care less about what happens to these characters, and even though the game tries to present things as "morally gray", it's really easy to tell which choices are the "good" choices. The gameplay is pretty good though. Calling this game an "RPG" is pretty generous, I'd say it's more of a hack & slash with the occassional puzzle, but it works.The combat mechanics are fun and even pretty creative, forcing you to switch up between 2 forms ("Physical", in which you only have melee attacks, and "Mental", in which you only have ranged attacks) with each one having it's own seperate set of skills and it's own health bar. I really enjoyed the combat, even though it did start getting repeptitive and some point, as there isn't really any way to customize your gameplay (hence my "not really an RPG" claim), and all enemies are basically the same.The puzzles were decent. Some were more fun than others, but generally I found them enjoyable. They kinda reminded me of the temple puzzles in Breath Of The Wild, and those were great. The main problem I had was that sometimes the isometric view kinda got in the way of seeing exactly what's going on, which made some puzzles a little more frustrating than they needed to be.Genereally, I'd say this game was a decent way to spend the day while being stuck in bed with a virus and a Steam Deck. The story is genuinely terrible, not only because the writing is so bad, but also because it has some really good ideas and interesting worldbuilding, and it just hurts to see those ideas massacred like that by absolutely incompetent storytelling.So just... lower your expectations, enjoy the mechanics, and skip all the dialogue. You'll like it better that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: It kind of feels like a game that was going to be a different game, then changed to this game, then wasn't finished. I actually played the demo and liked it well enough to get this on a bit of a discount around release, but the demo is a bit misleading because you only ever get 3 abilities during the game and you do NOT get them quickly. It makes combat very, very boring - it's like if you took a top-down Zelda game and slapped some Diablo onto it without actually adding any abilities.The story is... not great. The "twist" is broadcast so far in advance and so often that I don't actually think you can call it a twist, but the writing clearly still treats it as if it's supposed to be a surprise. The whole choice system feels pretty meaningless and heavy handed. The dialogue and world building overall feel incredibly confused - almost all the "world" stuff would make way more sense in a more cartoony, light-hearted setting, but instead it's in a grimdark "everything is awful and violent" setting which just makes it feel that much more childish. The heavy setting is not given a serious tone and the nonsense tone isn't given any fun to play with.Visually it's pretty good, there's a lot of details, and weirdly there is a TON more on your minimap than you can get to - not sure if it's to make the map look less plain or if it's an example of plans not being met. However, the tells for enemy attacks are largely terrible and difficult to read outside of boss fights.The rune system feels tacked on because the whole stat system feels tacked on. You can equip different runes to make different trade offs but there aren't enough options to like, change how you play at all. Except for the dash cooldown because spam dashing is the fastest way to get through the empty corridors (I hate when games don't make running the fastest way) so you always want that.The puzzle sections are boring and tedious, dealing with auto-scroll timers combined with janky targeting and hit registration and not being complicated in the slightest, just long. It's not, strictly, a bad game. It just doesn't really DO anything and I have absolutely no idea why I would recommend it over any game that actually does any of the things this game tries to do, better. There are elements of quality here, mostly visual, and there are some clearly unrealized ideas, but it's a fully released game, not something with 2-3 more years of polish coming.

_childDocuments_.review: Batora is a game with no meat on its bones. I would give it a mixed review if I had the chance, it is by no means horrible but at the same time it is such a forgettable experience. The Good :+ Graphics and cutscenes looks nice for an indie game. + Most lines are voice acted, which increases the immersion.+ UI looks clean and modern.The Bad :- Combat. It just doesn't have enough variety. Fight red enemies with your melee and purple with your ranged. Only a few special attacks unlocks by the end.- Choices. Batora gives you the ability to choose your actions on certain missions. While this seems good on paper game just isn't big enough for it to matter. Unless gameplay is phenomenal playing the same locations and fighting the same enemies doesn't sound appealing to me. - Content. Maybe I missed it but there doesn't seem to be any side missions or activities. So the experience gets stale quickly.The Ugly :-- Story. Oh lord what a hot mess. I'm sorry but it just amazes me how people with 0 creativity can become writers in this industry. Dialogue is equally bad if not worse.-- Customization. Upgrade system is extremely basic and not exciting. You feel no joy using a new upgrade for your character. Most stuff are +50 hp - 5% attack stuff. No exciting abilities, no creative changes. This is possibly the worst way to reward a player, it just doesn't feel fun. Tl;dr Batora is your mediocre 6/10 game that you will not remember after a few months. And if this is what you are looking for it is okay to get it on a sale and shut your brain for a few hours. Anyone looking for a fresh experience look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game, but I can't say I would recommend it. I finished it because I'm a completionist, and I hate leaving unfinished games behind.But it was a chore.The main reason is the writing. It's all so rushed, so uncooked. You meet an NPC for the first time "Hi, I'm good!", and then you want to sacrifice everything in order to protect/save that NPC. In the next dialogue another NPC comes and says "Muwahahaha I'm evil!", and then you decide that you need to kill that NPC (that you just met) with all your anger no matter what.In multiple occasions I was like "why am I throwing myself at a war because of an NPC I just met minutes ago?", and trying to find the "I don't give a f..." button, but in vain.As for the combat and skill system, it's "ok". There are good ideas there, but the combat takes a while to become interesting - it only shines when you have enough skills and things to do instead of just use the basic attack. The add-ons and skills are a bit shallow for a game with "RPG" tag - I was expecting to be able to significantly upgrade or modify my skills according to my playstyle and preferences, but that's definitely not the case here.The game is not a complete disaster, there are good moments in it, but the overall experience was poor. It has good ideas, but the execution of those ideas fell short.I got the ending B, and I'll definitely not play it again.On the bright side, the games worked well in 32:9 ultrawide, so that was a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time with Batora: Lost Haven, but if there is a game that is a mixed bad, this is it. It's not a masterpiece, but it's not garbage either. More complex than a casual game, but nowhere near a full RPG. The combat is fairly unique, yet super simple. There are puzzles, but they are extremely simple and forgiving. The story is neither interesting nor unimaginative. There are choices, but each choice is like saving someone you know or saving everyone else. The graphics are somewhat similar to World of Warcraft, easy to look at, but nothing you haven't seen before. Bonus points for the moody ambient soundtrack and minus points for the annoying "cool chick" protagonist. Overall, it's entertaining for about ten hours, but don't expect a life-changing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying myself so far. I was a bit concerned at first b/c of the WASD movement and twin stick-style of combat (since I play with a mouse and keyboard), but I got used to it pretty fast. It helps that I can control my character with either WASD or the RMB, so it's up to me whatever feels more comfortable to use.I'm liking the story so far, it's definitely engaging, with just enough of a hint of mystery to keep me wanting to figure out what happens next. I also really like the environmental puzzles. They are simple enough that you'll be able to figure it out if you stop and think for a bit, while also being complicated enough to not be completely pointless. I'm also a big fan of the graphics and the art style, and if I'm not mistaken, the VA for Avril is the same one who voiced Panam in Cyberpunk 2077.Also, the boss battles are top notch! Having faced two major story bosses so far, I can't praise the boss battle design enough! It's very reminiscent of boss battles in games like Darksiders as opposed to traditional ARPGs where you can usually just outgear / outlevel the content and trivialize the boss. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this one, even at full price. As far as indie ARPGs go, this one is one of the better ones I've played in a long time, and a definite diamond in the rough! Also, I've heard there are multiple endings you can get based on your choices in game, as well as a NG+ mode, so I'll almost certainly be getting my money's worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: There are some good things to say:1. It looks beautiful.2. There are some mechanics to play around, although very straightforward.3. it is very simple, so it's open for kids and very casual players.4. You can make choices. I have no clue what the actual consequences are to whatever you choose but I doubt there's any impact other than a few lines of chatter.But there are also bad ones:1. The first hour felt like a slog. Very boring to make progress in general, I made it to the first miniboss which wasn't anything special.2. The combat system is very bland, it gets repetitive and boring fast. I.e. red enemies = red sword, purple enemies = purple missiles, that's all. It also gets boring fast because the game practically forces you into playing ranged only vs some enemies and melee only vs the others. There's an option to disable this, but what's the point then?3. You get spells over time but it's like a MOBA, except you get them extreeeeemely slowly over time. It just feels like a mobile game in this sense.4. The story is super cringe. Think Forsaken's adolescent dialog while you're supposed to be a super human bound to save the world, but you can't stop making 5-year-old jokes and witty remarks.5. The upgrades system is like 2/10, all you do is get extra points in damage or health, and "low quality" runes sacrifice one to give you the other. Which means you will always want damage.Now the most egregious issue, I don't even know why this game is tagged as RPG/ARPG because there is no role-playing at all. That really makes me mad, why would you market your game as RPG when it's not? All there is here is very low quality elements of statistic management (i.e. health, defense, attack, critical hit chance...) that's not RPG at all.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is decent in many areas. The combat worked alright, the story premise was neat, but the overall game is a big o' pile of meh. The inventory system is complicated for almost no impact on combat, the replayability is made annoying by unskippable cutscenes, and the overall game just seems weaker than others in its category. Decent game to get on sale, but even then, better to spend your time on something else.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: Batora: Lost Haven is a fine adventure with very frustrating combat mechanics. You have the sun, melee and the moon, ranged. Aiming the moon projectile is beyond dumb on a controller so that's where the frustration comes from, with more on top of it later on the game. I'll talk about more later on this review.So, I'd say to get this game on sale if you want a game you can beat in a rainy afternoon and have some fun with it if you can get the hang of the combat, which I'm gonna be honest, I just pressed buttons and somehow it worked. This is definitely no Hades so keep that in mind.The puzzles are super simple and I dig them since they don't hinder the pace of the game... and one thing about the pace, there are some cutscenes you can skip and some you can't, for whatever reason. The same goes for the dialogue which I could simply skip altogether because if there's something I despise in games is slow ass dialogue for a story I didn't really feel interested at all, and trust me-- I tried, even with the choices you have throughout the game, which I saved and tried the different ones for all the achievos but overall I didn't feel affected by them; they're... there, that's it. You get a quick recap at the end but mostly I was like "oh yea that happened". No Mass Effect type of consequences so feel free to choose whatever you think it's best. The characters don't really have a personality sotospeak and you can smell what direction the story is gonna take from a mile away.By the way, the latter half of the game goes by extremely quickly too which I liked it a lot but I didn't like the last few bosses and their multiple health bars; it didn't feel fun to slog through them with the weird ass combat and a very unfortunate runes inventory system that doesn't... change much how you play the game-- it's just numbers for the most part and the enemies still feel bulletspongy. Oh hybrid enemies are very unfun to play against, just not exciting at all. To elaborate more on the combat, the game shows you enemies you can damage using your two stances and, quite honestly, the gimmick gets old pretty quickly since you can also mash buttons and come out on top if necessary. I particularly didn't enjoy it but maybe you won't mind it because the combat is my least favourite thing about this game.Basically, I do recommend it because it's not a bad game, it's just not good either. Batora: Lost Haven reminds me of those simple PS2 games from my childhood and for that, I am glad I bought it and played it to its completion. The game is beautiful and I absolutely adore the atmosphere, however I rushed it, barely took time to explore what the game allows you to (very little) so my playtime is based on going from point A to point B with save scumming for achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Batora: Lost Haven

_childDocuments_.review: I'm always torn whether I should rate a game based on whether I disliked it, or whether I think other genre fans would like it.If you're an ARPG fan and don't mind immature dialogue, you might really enjoy this game.I found it grating and really kind of silly (dialogue). You can't talk about grim subjects with witty quips and slang, and expect players to stay engaged and feel gravitas about the situation.Also, your character levels up but you don't make any choices when that happens. Limited character customisation via runes that just become a math game. Interesting puzzle/shrine mechanic but you can walk off the edges for some reason just adding frustration to navigating an isometric 45 degree view. Uncomfortable.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought as part of a Humble bundle, game looked interesting but doesn't have one redeeming quality, I'm just glad I didn't buy this as a single game.Combat gets boring very quickly, sluggish unresponsive controls don't help.  Suicidal ally NPC's who will stand in enemy AOE's and die forcing you to restart sections.Predictable story with what might be the worst character development and dialogue of any game I've ever played, very much reminiscent of Forspoken. _childDocuments_.review: A dear friend got me this game, so believe me when I say it had to be particularly bad for me to be able to stomach saying so in a review.batora is pretty much bog standard for something released in the later 2010's-- the main character is an insufferable 'chosen one' with little to no redeeming quality, and the game feels almost schizophrenic in design, especially with go-nowhere systems such as the cracked alignment system and the way quests are laid out. I went in expecting an epic ARPG with some gravity and maturity, and instead I got the bastard offspring of League-based ADHD and a Life is Strange fanfic. the story is a total mess, despite this game being sold on being so *story heavy* focused in design.theres like... some ok art direction in things, and the combat isnt supremely terrible, but unless youre getting this on major sale, I'd avoid it. its very much a 'great-value' Forspoken.

_childDocuments_.review: Up front, I want to say that the game isn't *bad*. The core of it is fine; it's not saddled with technical glitches or horribly broken mechanics or anything like that. But a core gameplay loop that's "fine" doesn't carry the other issues.On the plus side, there are some decisions you need to make that have actual moral weight, and which you can't avoid. The story concept isn't bad, and in fact is arguably pretty good. The voice acting isn't too bad either; the biggest issue there is that they didn't seem to have enough different voice actors, or enough different voices (since some actors can do multiple voices), for all the characters who had lines spoken. This is understandable enough for a smaller studio, which I assume Stormind is, but the decision to have so many different characters voice-acted when the voices themselves are often barely differentiated from each other, especially when a lot of those characters are not human and are only set apart by linguistic tics rather than a different sound, is questionable.The problems start, however, with the writing, which fails both the story and the voice actors. The latter is easier to explain—the dialogue is often more literary than true to how people talk. This is OK when you're only reading text, but sounds wrong when spoken verbatim by a voice actor. Put another way, the dialogue would often sound (read) better if you only saw it in text rather than having it spoken by a person.The story is impacted because, while the core concept is perfectly good, the way the writing builds that story creates a lot of situations that don't make sense with how quickly you're intended to move through the game. The main character makes several references to not having time for this or that, and some things happen which I think a lot of us would naturally think should take some time to resolve (early example to minimize spoilers: a broken bridge) but which are dealt with almost immediately. And the speed of finishing the game is obviously intended, because at the end they explicitly suggest playing through again with different choices to find different endings. (You should know this ahead of time; if you enjoy the game, you'll probably be happy to play through it again regardless.)The characters also... how to put this as vaguely as possible... don't always seem to have the same point of view from one situation to the next. I don't mind that their opinions shift in a logical way based on the specifics of a situation, but that I was more than once left saying out loud, "What the f--- are you talking about?"Gameplay is, again, fine, but it's a little tough in some ways. You can attack directionally with your right analog (assuming you're using a controller, which I recommend), and that's cool, but there's a melee mode and a ranged mode, and I found very little use in this when in melee. That's fine; you can also press X to attack (XBox controller), so you're not stuck with a terrible attack scheme. However—and maybe I'm more sensitive to this at the moment because the two most recent action games I've played through are Dreamscaper and Rogue Legacy 2, and roguelites need super-tight combat—the enemies often do not give much, or any, visual clues for their attacks. When you're at range, this is OK, because you have time to adjust, but in melee it's effectively impossible. And the combat system does encourage, or require (depending on the settings you choose), you to be in melee for some enemies. So there are situations, especially later on, where an enemy has a multiple-strike attack, and you don't know it's coming until it's killed you at least once. Then you at least know the enemy has that trick, and you can work around it. But that's a lot different from a game where the enemy has a tell, and they kill you anyway because you don't know what the tell means yet. You see something's coming, but you have to learn what. Here, you don't know anything's coming until it's hit you.Also, occasional enemies are clearly short of striking but do damage anyway. It's not a significant problem, but it's frustrating when it happens. TLDR: Good ideas, fine gameplay loop, but decision-making undercuts most of the positives this game could, and should, have.

_childDocuments_.review: - interesting combat system. Utilizes 2 different "elements". Game difficulty will depend on which you pick. - enemies scale to your level- choices matter leading to different couple endings- has ng+- game is short. 2 playthroughs is enough to reach 100% and in 17hrs.- balancing issue especially in new game+. Regular mob battles can be harder than boss fights. 1st and 2nd boss fights can take longer than the 3rd and 4th boss.- poor NPC AI, you will likely get a game over screen due to NPC just standing idle and getting hit- some puzzle ideas apparently copied from immortal fenyx rising- subtitles persist after cutscene. Spelling mistakes and missing words in dialogue- some of the runes stats will just changed with no prior warning given, including those that you have equipped- majority of the runes bought will not be carried forward to ng+ nor be converted to in-game credits- poor manual save system. The game save technically saves at the latest quest and usually not the current game state you are at. After starting a new main quest, buy a rune, equip it and save the game. Reload the game and you are back at the start of the quest before buying the rune with your in-game credits still intact.6/10And when they name a character "Gao Chao", was it pun intended?If you want to buy this game, wait for at least 75% discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game on a steam deck and although I had fun and recommend it, there are definitely some things that could be better.GameplayThe game feels like a hack'n slash with some light rpg elements with levels, and runes that gives you buffs and new abilities though you don't feel much of a difference with each rune. The mechanics of sun and moon modes are very fun and I wish they explored more of that dymanic. The controls feels a bit slow and some times it is hard do aim at enemies.HistoryI would say that this is one of the weakest points of the game as the main character is not enjoyable and it is not nice to people. That would be okay if the history was not about love and fighting for what you care.There are some parts which would benefit more explanation or more of a character building. _childDocuments_.review: The game has some good points going for it, especially the really nice artwork and environments. It works well on Linux too, even though there is some heavy stuttering during the first 15 minutes of play, after which it smoothens out. Sadly the combat becomes dull and repetitive very quickly, and it doesn't feel particularly satisfying or progressive either. There was nothing in the story or voice acting to keep me engaged. And finally the puzzles are sometimes frustrating because you need to shoot a certain target but the controller simply won't aim, and you have to switch to mouse+kb for specific bits.Tough one, I did want to like it a lot, but can't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game with a refreshing combat system : you get 2 HP bars to manage. And your choices have REAL consequences on the story, it's not only about the chatter but your choice can actually have heavy consequences like a whole city destruction for eg. Your choices also have an impact on how many runes you can equip so it's a part of your build. You'll have to choose carefully which stance you use against different types of enemies, sometimes it can be very tricky. I enjoyed the puzzles too. And I really like Avril, she's a good character with feelings and the voicing is good !* Very good artstyle (kudos to the artists !), various planets, good looking overall* Combat system : tricky, various, nervous, not boring* Puzzles : entertaining, not too easy, not too hard for me* Story choices : really nice, I love RPG with real consequences* Voice acting is good and covers all interactions* Characters feel alive, the whole lore is nice* NG+ !!!* A bit short (~10-12 hours on the first run, I'm not good to estimate it because I tried several saves/routes without knowing about the NG+)* You can't change some controls, I'm not a fan of combos on the right stick* 3D models are a bit old, with this style you could go like Kena* definitely too short, I need more planets :PFull review (in French) on jeuxonline if you're interested ;-)

_childDocuments_.review: I am not quite sure where all the hate in the reviews here comes from. I had fun with this game so far. I got it on sale for five bucks and the game already made up for that with the two hours of fun I had with it. And I expect to have a few more.I would compare the game to Bastion or Children of Morta: A little action adventure some people might consider an ARPG, although that is a bit of a stretch (as it is for Bastion and CoM). The combat is snappy and fun, the character customisation is decent (but nothing to write home about as to be expected for an action adventure), and the story is, well, it exists and is arguably the weakest part of the game. The game really shines at its game mechanic variety for bosses, puzzles, and general combat. But that all is beside the point of this game. Like Bastion or CoM, it is one of these little games which captures you with their serene atmosphere and polished world. There is always something to discover, a new puzzle mechanic, a new boss mechanic, or just some story tidbit (at least so far).When you just want a game to relax with, ideally played on the couch or a handheld device, this will provide a few hours of fun. When you are a hardcore ARPG monkey, who shudders at the thought of less than a quintillion layers of character and combat customisation, this is probably not the game for you. And the story aficionados, well, they better go and read a book and stop pestering us in the comments here ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I feel kinda bad to give this a negative review, since its obvious its from a small studio who put a lot of heart and soul into it, making an interesting world(s), characters, and premise, as well as a twinge of mystery. but at the end its still a video game, and its most important aspect is the gameplay. its just a top down run and gun, with every objective being "go here, talk to them, go there kill the enemies, go back, talk some more, oop, enemies show up, kill them, talk again." thats it. thats this whole game, and thats such a shame. I wish they would have made a film or a series out of this instead, or at least not made it top down?yes there are choices, and yes they change the course of the game...until you get to the next area and you never see any of the established characters again. and yes theres the sun mode and moon mode, which are basically sword mode and gun mode. but theyre only effective against enemies of their own colour. yes there are cool combos to pull off, but theyre more likely to drain your own hp while your character is winding up its punches, than just mashing default attack and dodging. maybe im doing something wrong though, always possible.
