_childDocuments_.review: This review is giving the game a yes, but in all honestly it should be a maybe. I'd say most people who purchase/play this game won't hate it but they definitely won't walk away craving more. It feels unfinished or that they didn't fully commit to the execution of some of their ideas and mechanics.So that said below is a more in depth review of my thoughts after beating the game...Story:A nice premise, they even add in what is essentially a person A/B mechanic (like are you going to make altruistic choices or selfish choices) and that's where the good part of their story stops. The pacing of the story is choppy at best and you have no real time to feel for your character or some of the others you come across which makes certain events in the game seem meaningless. It also felt at times like story or dialogue was missing that would have made me better understand some of the, IMO, wild emotional/tonal swings the character takes at certain points. Then there's the branching choices, you get essentially 2 options at times, to be a defender or a conqueror. I mostly went the route of conqueror and at certain points of the scripted story it seemed like my character was drastically going the other direction from the kinds of choices I was making.Combat:Combat was OK, not as tight as I would have liked for an action RPG. They did have 2 cool mechanics, the first being shifting between 2 fighting styles (one melee, one ranged) which you use to take advantage of doing extra damage to enemies and the second is runes which are used to enhance your character, fighting modes, and skills. Again IMO cool ideas just not great execution. Let's start with the Runes because they effect your fighting in the game a lot. You get 3 types of "skill points" when you level up which they don't do a great job explaining why you get what you get, but you'll need those points to equip runes. You can only equip a rune if you have enough of it's corresponding skill points (i.e. defender runes can only be equipped with defender points). A lot of the runes I came across would have +stat for mode A, -stat for mode B, which I wouldn't have minded if I could really focus in on a single fighting style but they basically force you to have to use both and if you want to make one strong you have to weaken the other. I didn't enjoy that so I mostly used neutral runes.Exploration/World/Collectibles:Overall the worlds you visit are pretty but my gosh are they empty and in many ways seem pointless. It feels like they wanted you to explore and to be able to do other things but ran out of time. For example you can't just talk to people, instead you can move near them and they'll have some dialogue pop-up on screen so if you want to know what they're saying and didn't catch it you have to run by a couple times. Then there's chest, I'm not sure why the game even really needs them. you can't change anything about your character except their runes, so all you get is a rare resource now and again or mostly just currency (which you can get both from enemies you kill anyways). I loathe useless chests. You can also break open crystals which give health or sometimes materials but I couldn't find out what to do with those materials. in the very beginning there's this one smith who makes you a rune and I thought [materials+money=runes or upgrades] but nope, never got any scripted use for why occasionally I was getting materials (maybe someone wiser found out).Puzzles:Puzzles were fun and creative. Not too complex or too easy, just right.Art:GreatCut scenes:GreatProbably won't play it again for the other ending, just doesn't seem like it'll be worth it. If they were to make a DLC or make another game I have confidence that'll only level up as this is a decent outing for what seems like a small studio

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game!Yeah, I'm just in the first few hours of gameplay but the gameplay is hitting really good.The hack n' slash genre is not my particular style, and mainly I bought this game for the graphic style, but overall the base combat mechanics are simple but fun to play and experiment with. A little bit rough since there are no particular impact or effects when hitting a foe ( the don't stagger or else, there is no clear reaction), but is so damn smooth. Even quite enjoyed combo-ing the various skill and going in n' out between the two main damage mode.As for the story even if is a little bit railroaded, I found it engaging ( I appreciated the touch of narrative choices but still have to discover in depth of this mechanic). The game kinda remind me a old style level design where you have a main path to follow and some branches to explore if you want to discover more secrets and collect more materials. Not necessarily bad and it's quite nostalic. One thing that I really love and is its unique art style, the environments and the animations during the cutscene are great.Visually there isn't much to say, it's perfect.In the end, I really recommend this game for those who want to make the first steps in a ARPG game without experiencing a tough approach to the genre. _childDocuments_.review: So, the hack n' slack is "my cup of tea", especially after a day of work and when you add a bit of action rpg is also better and Batora have it. To clarify a bit, the game has an interesting story and it is also easy to follow, so you don't have to wear an elf's hat and a black rune in the nose to understand what is going on (unlike Final Fantasy). The gameplay works very well because it has a lot of positive characteristics of similar games (the way it indicates the street ahead pressing rs is a wonderful feature). The story flows nicely and there isn't any dead points so you won't stay stuck for 20 minutes not knowing what to do.The "fighting" feature is also very fun expecially when after some level the game give you more possibility to personalize it with special move.To conclude I absolutely recommend this game to those who wants to have a lot of fun.

name: The Ramp
detailed_description: CHECK OUT MY LATEST GAME :) About the Game THE RAMP SUPPORTS KEYBOARD INPUT, BUT IS BEST PLAYED WITH A CONTROLLER. You crave for flow? You just want to shred through a halfpipe without all the boring stuff? Say no more, The Ramp is your jam! YES: tons of flow satisfying & unique skateboarding gameplay easy to learn, hard to master BUT: NO unlockable stuff NO score, NO missions NO guns, explosions and helicopters A quick note from the developer: When thinking about buying The Ramp , please keep in mind that it is a very small game. Maybe not even a game, but rather a digital toy. It was created by a single developer (hi that’s me, Paul) to scratch a very specific itch. The Ramp captures the unparalleled feeling of real life vert skateboarding and that’s pretty much it. There is a lot this game doesn’t feature. What it offers you are the 15 minutes of flow that make a boring day great, at the price of a medium sized cinnamon pistachio latte to go. Please don’t hesitate to get in touch if you have feedback, questions or problems with the game. I’ll do my best to get back to you as quickly as possible. Also let me know if you enjoyed The Ramp , because that really makes my day!

_childDocuments_.review: Grinds and ollies and air, oh my! The Ramp is a great little game made as a testament of love. There is so much fun to be had in this little indie game. There isn't much in terms of levels, but what's here is a lot of fun. The developers really did put some care in making it really feel good hitting those ramps, getting air and busting out some awesome tricks.In The Ramp you will play as a generic character, whom you can very slightly customize. It quickly gets you into the action after a very brief tutorial explaining how the game works, and at first, it may feel a bit off because of the camera angle vs your character. After about 5 minutes, I had a pretty good grasp and feel of the controls to get my character to go wherever I wanted, so the learning curve isn't too bad really.After you've mastered your controls you get to hit the ramps and explore the wonderful indie skate game that is The Ramp.Yet another very important gaming element to skate games is physics, and they did it justice. It really does feel like you have to nail those timings on getting your speed to get yourself as high as you can to get the tricks successfully performed. This element really does bring a sense of satisfaction to sticking those super tough tricks. When i landed my first 1080, it felt pretty amazing. Total satisfaction is to be found in The Ramp if you are any sort of skate game enthusiast. Although there is not a ton of content here, which I would personally love to see some DLC maps, there is still a lot of fun to be had. Whether someone would sit down and play this title for hours and hours at a time is debatable, but it works absolute wonders as a filler game for when you don't have tons of time to get involved.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp achieves exactly what it promises: a simple experience that scratches that skateboarding itch. The ease of use and minimal effort required to drop in and execute some tricks is a real testament to excellent game design. If you have a core mechanic which is designed well and works, you don't need the extra fluff. As you’d expect, the minimalist approach to this game also impacts the sound design and music. A simple lo-fi track plays in the background if you want. Or you can listen to the sweet sounds of wheels along the curve of a bowl, interspersed with  the sounds when you make contact with the lip of the ramp.The developer has crafted a simple masterpiece which allows players to turn off their brains and shred. I would highly recommend this!

_childDocuments_.review: The first thought in my head when viewing this title was: ‘Cool, that looks just like Tony Hawk on the Gameboy Advance.’ In a way it is, but much, much simpler (yes, that’s possible) which makes sense considering the price it’s sold for.This isn’t going to be a long review; the gameplay isn’t even long enough to justify that, but I would like to talk about it just a little bit for those who are even slightly interested in buying it. Look, for €4 you can’t go wrong; it has roughly 30 minutes of gameplay with achievements and you can always refund it you really don’t enjoy it (please don’t play it fully and then refund, support the developer if you can).What you will do in those 30 minutes (you can play it for much, much longer, mind you) is select one of 4 isometric levels and just skateboard around, trying to do tricks & stunts or relax and ride around. And that’s all you can and will do. Unlike Tony Hawk there are no objectives to complete or secrets to find. If this does get developed into something bigger later on then I hope the levels will be much bigger and that there will be a points/score system, objectives and/or secrets. So, basically Tony Hawk but without Tony Hawk. Not very original, I agree, but we don’t have anything like that on PC right now, with the exception of OlliOlli (but that game is shown from a 2D perspective).Graphically it aims for a realistic look and succeeds. The sound effects are decent.And the only noteworthy issue I had was that it’s sometimes hard to see depth (i.e. where you will land). This was especially the case in the level with the ‘towering ramp’.

_childDocuments_.review: A game designed for skateboard lovers, the Ramp is a minimal skating game that is said to offer satisfying and unique gaming experience with "no extra complicated mechanics"The Ramp was created by a single developer and is described as more of a "digital toy" rather than a fully-fledged game, and the reason is due to the game lack of content. with only four different ramps to skate on your standard half-pipe, an empty pool, a long ramp and a park circuit. There are no mission, objectives or scoring system.Nevertheless, for its low price, The game does control reasonably well, and even though the range of tricks is quite limited, there's plenty of fun to be had here if you're not bothered about gaming scores and doing missions. The only objective in The Ramp is simply to skate your heart's content. Rating: 10/10 (Thanks Fanatical for the game.)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is a short, simple and relaxing game that is easy to play and does not require any advanced skills. I'm not the biggest fan of skating games, but this one was easy to digest and was overall pretty chill if you aren't achievement hunting. The graphics are alright and the controls are easy to master, with just a few buttons needed to perform tricks and navigate around the environment. It's basically the kind of game that you can pick up and play without much instruction, and you'll be like Tony Hawk in no time. The game's lack of complexity makes it a great choice for anyone looking for a quick and easy way to unwind. However, this game does fall short in terms of content, which is either a blessing or a curse depending on who you ask.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: RAMP sets a good framework for a skateboarding game. The controls are simple, the artstyle is poppy, and the music is super chill. You just skate, there's no pressure or any real objective. This elegance works to its advantage in my opinion. I can see myself playing this game in short bursts just to try a few tricks and just turn my brain off for a few minutes.  I look forward to the possibility of Steam Workshop support; there are currently only 4 levels but I believe user-generated levels could create a lot of replay-ability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: It's exactly what it says on the tin: A digital toy.But it's a damn fun toy. Achievement hunting is all you get if you want to feel like "finishing" this game, otherwise it's just a nice lil sandbox to skate some bowls in. Worth the money, go support a young indie dev.I swear I'll get that Lord of the Board achievement some day
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I love this toy!This game is like no other game if you were the kid that brought a Tech Deck™ to school you'll get so much nostalgia playing "The Ramp". _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and relaxing, works great with both keyboard and controller use, graphics are pleasing, will probably run on a vast array of hardware, cheap, and offers exactly what it advertises to do "to scratch a very specific itch." _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so chill and a lot of fun.  Currently there is not a huge amount of content but there is so much potential here if they open this game up to steam workshop and let players make custom maps.  Also adding more grind options would be great.  Overall though, really chill skating game to kill some time with.  I really hope this continues to get updates.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is about as simple a skateboarding game as one could possibly create, and that's not a bad thing. Everything from the graphics, to the level design, and controls are as simplified as could be, creating a very minimalist experience that is super easy to pick up and start having fun with. The few levels that are available to play on each have their own purposes and invite different types of tricks and flow in your runs. There's enough variety to keep you busy, but the desire for a true skate park level was definitely there. It's extremely easy to put together long combos of tricks and grinds with a little bit of practice. The music is extremely relaxing and helps you get lost in an endless loop of nose grabs and rotations. For $6, there's just enough to do if you're a massive skateboarding fan, but ideally I would wait for a sale or get it in a bundle on Fanatical if you're interested in it. For more reviews, follow my
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is a cozy skateboarding minimalist game where you can skateboard infinitely on four different platforms. I recommend this game since I enjoyed playing it. I also recommend playing it with the controller, since it is easier than the keyboard. The content is quite short though, but enjoyable for the time it lasts. _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Good for Steam Deck when you are on the road.If you read the note from the developer before buying, I think you can not be disappointed.Is it worth the money? _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: It's awesome. I was so hooked on the first map and then tried the others and just wow. Feels like Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 2 and looks like Good Job! amazing combination. Paul, I really like what you made man. I would love to see new ramps and harder achievements. For example Tony Hawk's 900 that he did IRL at the ripe age of 48, deserves homage in a game like this one. On the broader spectrum, ideas like a small skatepark, kickflips, heelflips, grinding and ledge stalling would be seriously impressive. This has a lot of potential, and you are more than capable! It would make such a cool tiny skate game. I would also love to see a scoring system, leaderboards, and multiplayer. All the stuff thps2 had, like game modes and huge maps. _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: But you can also have a lot of fun. The Ramp is a simple game in which you choose one of four available small maps with a ramp, and then you can ride on it and perform various tricks on it, just like on a normal skateboard. The most important thing in this game is to understand how to speed up, and then everything should go smoothly. We can also choose one of four characters, but this does not affect the gameplay. On top of that, we can choose a hardcore mode, and it seems to me that after choosing this mode we have to be generally more careful when steering.The graphics are very simple, and the maps are small but nice, although it's a pity that there are so few of them. What's missing a bit is the addition of new maps by the creator, or what would be better - the possibility to add maps through the workshop. Another thing worth adding would be a multiplayer mode or at least a scoreboard. However, it's worth noting that such updates to the game are unlikely to happen and one should enjoy what is there.There is not much to write about this game. The Ramp is a simple, short and relaxing game that costs little and is a joy to play. It is not a game for long evenings, but rather for an hour because of the small amount of content. The only thing missing is more maps, some multiplayer mode and it would be a really good skateboarding game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what it says on the tin; a solid, simple skateboarding game. _childDocuments_.review: It is a toy like game with 100% flow. Perfect for a little break from work. _childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I don't understand why this has such positive ratings, when you consider the price. You can do everything this game has to offer in 5 minutes. You can 100% the Steam achievements in 20 minutes. My game time is about 40 minutes, only because I started watching videos of Tony Hawk on YouTube (did you know someone has done a 1080 now!?).The gameplay itself is good, but very, very limited. There's a very small number of grabs and grinds. There are 4 maps, and even then they're all basically the same, and extremely simple. There's no real "park" element, where things flow one to another. There's just absolutely no content here, aside from decent flow in the gameplay. This is essentially a tech demo, to show people the basic gameplay idea. If the devs make actual levels (not just a single object to skate), and add a lot more tricks, like different grabs, grinds, manuals, gaps, etc. then I can see this being a great game. I wouldn't be surprised at all if they basically used this game to gain interest and funds, and then in the future came out with an ACTUAL game based on this. If that happens, I'd be interested.I don't understand how this can have a price tag this high (and yes, I know it's a low price tag). Generally I hear people say a dollar an hour is good bang for your buck, so this game should be worth about a quarter. Instead, it's almost 7 dollars, which is grossly not worth it. I got this in a bundle for under 5, and it had a bunch of other games, and I still feel ripped off.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: ❤ Audience ❤☐ Beginner☑ Casual Gamer☐ Normal Gamer☐ Expert☼ Graphics ☼☐ Bad☐ Alright☑ Good☐ Beautiful☐ Fantastic♬ Music ♬☐ Bad☑ Alright☐ Good☐ Beautiful☐ Fantastic☠ Difficulty ☠☐ My child could do it☑ Easy☐ Average☐ Easy to learn / Hard to master☐ Hard☐ Unfair§ Bugs §☐ Bugs destroy the game☐ Lots of bugs☐ Few Bugs☐ You can use them for speedrun☑ Nothing encountered☯ Story ☯☑ There is none☐ Bad☐ Alright☐ Good☐ Fantastic⚔ Gameplay ⚔☐ Frustrating☐ Sleepy☐ Boring☑ Fun☐ Challenging☑ Relaxing✳PC Specs Necessary✳☐NASA's Computer☐High End Computer☐Good Computer☐Low end Computer☑Literal Potato۞ Game time / Length ۞☑ Really short (0 - 3 hours)☑ Short (4 - 8 hours)☐ Few hours (10 - 20 hours) [if you focus on the main story]☐ Long (40-60 hours) [if you complete everything]☐ Very Long (61-100 hours)☐ Extremely Long (101+ hours)$ Price / Quality $☑ Full price☐ Wait for Sale☐ Don't buy☐ Refund it if you canIts cheap either way it doesn't matterThe Ramp is a very relaxing game where you literally just ride your skateboard around 4 different maps with no main objective.This game can be played when you're calm or stressed, but it seems to work well as a relaxing/soothing game which is very satisfying. I have found the game to run out of content rather quick however due to the real lack of content unless you are playing for the sole reason of chilling. I got this game and enjoyed it however i understand that the majority of people will play for around 1-2 hours and possibly refund due to all the enjoyment being used immediately.Now just to go over the checklist above. The game is typically for more relaxed gamers, as its not a sweaty game to tryhard in. New players could probably get the hang of it rather quickly as the controls are very simple however occasionally you need to use your brain slightly. The graphic's are as seen on the steam store for this game. Its very minimalistic and simple with not much happening graphics wise. I cant imagine it would force anything from any PC and is mainly runnable on a potato.The music is really simple however its very repetitive as its the same music over and over again so i turn mine off. I understand that for some people it might add to the experience but i prefer just have something else playing while i hear the skateboard sounds separately. When you turn the music off you can still hear background sound from other skateboards as you cannot turn normal sound offThe difficulty is very low. Whilst you do need to use some brain as you need to time the skateboard, its really easy to master and i do it naturally now. You wouldn't be able to put it in front of your 2 year old nephew however as 17 year old it was very easy.I have experience 0 bugs so far, i cant imagine there ever will be any either. The game is so simple its almost impossible for many bugs to be found. I assume no-one will find any bugs, and if they do it'll be an one off and never see it again. Don't worry about bugs!Literally no story whatsoever. Please do not expect any story (even a training scene). The only training which shows is just telling you the basics of the game. As i said no story at all.The game-play is very relaxing and i see it as a soothing/satisfying game. I could play this game in almost any mood and it'll most likely make me happy or relaxed. Basically its fun lolI don't have the most incredible PC. I would say its average/good to most standards however i really cannot imagine how bad a computer/laptop must be for this to not run well. It is sooooo simple and easy to the point where you could run it on any laptop or PC.The gameplay time is short. I played for some time and whilst i do enjoy it, i can tell it would get tiring or boring fast. However short term the game is amazing. You get to experience the game perfectly until maybe 30 mins or an hour and then its already getting repetitive. 2 hours is a push but its easily done. at that point you probably are either wanting to refund just purely on the fact that you cant imagine you'll play it again. The quality for price is good in my opinion. The fact its literally £4.79 normally and £3.83 really pays off as its minimalistic meaning it should be cheaper and they made it cheaper. This would probably make people want to buy it more. I saw it on my steam page and thought id get it because why not. The price made me want it so i got it. Smart move from them.Overall this is a good game, I recommend buying it heavily. If you like these types of satisfying minimalistic games then its perfect for you. No objective, No aim. Just skating. Please read everything above before buying though just to make sure you understand what you're getting into

_childDocuments_.review: Me: Can we have Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 on Steam ?Mom: We already have it !Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2 on Steam:Memes aside, The Ramp is a small, minimalist skateboarding game. You control a skater and you must chain tricks to collect the most points.Four levels are available.Enough to keep you busy for a quarter of an hour or while another game downloads...The game has been temporarily free to keep on Fanatical over the 2023 Thanksgiving holiday.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A well-made minimalist skateboarding game with eye-catching aesthetics, good physics, and groovy lo-fi soundtracks. I strongly recommend you to watch the trailers, especially the second one  in which the dev gives a comprehensive overview of their game and showcases all the gameplay elements.The control scheme is quite simple: you have one button for pumping, one stick for swerving, one stick for 8 grab tricks, and a shoulder pad for boardslide. The first 15 minutes of gameplay was difficult for me, especially due to the fixed camera angle, but once I got the hang of it, it became a flow. So addictive and satisfying, even for someone who never skateboards in the real life!Be aware, though, this is a very small game (or rather a digital toy, as called by its dev). It has no unlockable stuff or mission, just endless skateboarding in 4 maps (including the simplest one for tutorial) that you can see from the trailers. It takes you around 10 minutes to see everything in the game, and maybe 1 or 2 hours to get all the achievements (mostly about spinning X degrees while airborne or performing an X metres boardslide).For me, this is a little gem that I wish more developers would make: a small game that captures perfectly the flow of an activity. It still has a lot more potential to uncover: more maps, more movements, multiplayer, etc. But I doubt this will ever happen: the dev is now focusing on a “sequel” about snowboarding. How exciting!In conclusion, although the game is short, I highly recommend you to check it out, if you are interested in some casual, relaxing, flowy skateboarding.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I was going to give this game a bad review giving that, although the price is very low, the gameplay is waaaay shorter than I would anticipate. He was honest with it and I respect that so much I kind of want to buy the game a second time just out of admiration.I have no complains about the game itself, and any complain that I could have is just me being demanding about a characteristic that was never supposed to be in the game itself (mods, workshop, leaderboard, etc). So really, the game is a fun, short adventure, and if you have 1 hour to kill in something chill, definitely give this one a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand how this has overwhelmingly positive reviews.Don't get me wrong, it is very up front about what it is and what it offers (and what it doesn't). However, even for what it wants to be I find it underwhelming. The perspective makes it awkward to orientate yourself and leaves the character obscured half the time on landings. The system for gaining momentum is needlessly complicated, requiring you to alternate between holding and release a button at four different intervals in mostly compact spaces. The magnetism keeping the character lined up with the curve of the bowls is extreme and can send you flying across the pool to line up. The only way to check controls is to replay the tutorial.I gave it a second chance taking my time to get used to the controls and the feel, and getting all the achievements. I feel bad giving a negative review based on the personal honesty of the description. It has good chill music, a pleasant minimalist art style. The flow is nice when you get there, and I'm sure those who do take the time to master it will enjoy it more. But I don't feel like 15 minutes of flow is worth the price. It feels like a demo or mobile app game. The features list should also state explicitly that the 4 maps featured in the gallery are the only ones. If it had more, while still being small in scope and minimalist in design, just more variety of levels with degrees of difficulty in their structure and designed to facilitate the flow, then maybe. The lack of substance is the biggest issue, and while I appreciate warning potential customers that this is barely a game and think it's truly commendable, I can't recommend it based on that.

_childDocuments_.review: A good idea, but should have been free or at most $1. $5.99 is way too much for what you get. Also one of the worst tutorials I've ever seen. _childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is a simple but engaging game where you practice sick tricks with your skateboard on a four different maps, each with different attributes that encourage certain mechanics. See my rating at the end, after reading the rest of the review.The mechanics of this game seem incredibly simple, and they are at a surface level to get into, but there are many things that you can do to . These include grinding on rails, spinning in the air, or simply using the carefully curated maps to your advantage. You won't utilize all of these to your fullest at first, but, you'll soon learn how to use everything this game offers in tandem. Once that happens, the game becomes great.This is the main appeal of the game. The controls of your skateboard allow you added flexibility and ease to do tricks. It feels so , and even doing the simplest of motions is satisfying in it of itself. Although, it must be stated, this game should 100%  if a player wants the best experience.As opposed to the rampant development of ultra-realistic graphics found in gaming as of late, The Ramp chooses simple models that get the job done. But, what it does best, is the  of Orange and Blue. The maps were tailored to either have warm or cool colors, and depending on which they have, the background is either a bright Orange or a bright Blue to contrast.Despite the praise I have given about this game, there is one glaring problem.  After getting all the achievements and trying out every map, there's nothing else you can possibly do that you haven't already done before. It's infuriating, as great as this game is, I can't bring myself to play it for over 2 hours simply because there isn't anything new to do. I think that Paul, with newfound experience of his, needs to create updates to this game in order to flesh out this amazing concept more. I believe a map editor and  would be beneficial, as it creates a plethora of potential content without the added commitment of the developer constantly adding things.Additionally, if this were to be a feature, it would be nice to add a  that has an objective of some kind, or  that you must advance to. Unlocking cosmetics, not in the way of micro transaction, would benefit this game greatly. Added skins for your  would give an incentive to doing certain tasks, such the ones that are achievements now, while also rewarding the player for playing.  that can be unlocked would also work to the favor of The Ramp. The contrasting colors of Blue & Orange being substituted for another inverse pair, such as Green & Pink, at the choice of the player, would personalize the game in a way that is not available now.I can't feasibly give this any higher than a 6.5, as much as it hurts me to say. The game just needs more to be whole. Despite this, I would 100% recommend this, although try to get it for a reduced value.

_childDocuments_.review: is a minimalist’s dream come true—a peaceful, endless skateboarding session where you can zone out and live your best skate life. Four maps, a bit of character customization, and the kind of relaxing vibe that makes you feel like you’re doing something productive... even though you’re just rolling down ramps. Oh, and did I mention it’s a steal at this price? You can’t even get a coffee for this cheap. No complicated mechanics, no crazy storylines—just you, your board, and some sweet ramps to ride. If you want another “perfect game” on your list, this one’s got you covered. Only a couple of achievements will take more than five minutes. Easy win! That’s right, this game is a one-person show—and honestly, hats off to them because it’s impressive. It’s like finding treasure in a bargain bin. It’s a fun little experience, and you can’t beat the cost. Highly recommend it if you’re looking for a quick and easy game to unwind with. You’ll be alternating between holding and releasing buttons at four different intervals in a tight space. It’s like learning to drive stick for the first time but on a skateboard.The game is  You can complete it in a couple of hours, which is great for your achievement list but might leave you wanting more.While it’s fun, . After a few hours, you’ll probably find yourself thinking, “Is this it?” If you’re looking for a game with depth, this isn’t it—it’s more of a light snack than a full meal.If you’re not into timing and button coordination, the momentum system might feel like a weird workout for your fingers.The Ramp is a fun, chill little skateboarding game that’s perfect for achievement hunters and anyone who just wants to vibe for a bit. It’s a simple, well-made game with a fantastic price point, but don’t expect to be glued to it for days. It’s more like a casual afternoon pick-me-up that lets you pretend you can actually skate (without the risk of breaking a bone). Definitely worth it for a relaxing ride—just be prepared for some awkward momentum learning curves!

_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The price is fair.  A really neat and engaging take on a skateboarding game.  I'm hooked on the idea.  And I want more.Controls are adequate for the trick-set, but sadly it seems no flip tricks or grind/ slide variations?  Only boardslide and grabs? _childDocuments_.review: This "game" was free on Fanatical and after playing it, I can see why. I only added it to my account because it has achievements and thought it would be a fun little experience, but the horrible and inconsistent controls ruin it for me. If you think this is your sort of game I would recommend waiting for a sale or it to be given away for free again because it's just not worth it for the content there is.You are thrown into the tutorial to start and it gives you a basic run-through of the 4 different controls. The controls are my main issue, the tutorial tells you how to build up speed but I found that repeating the same process as the tutorial would sometimes give me speed and sometimes slow me down, it's inconsistent and not fun. Now it does mention that it recommends a controller so I can't fault that the keyboard controls are bad because I was warned, but trying to juggle 4 different controls is impossible for me. This should have taken me 30 minutes max, but it's 2 hours I will never get back.You are given 3 maps to just play around in, the only real reason to play would be for the achievements, beyond that I don't know why you would. There is a toggle in the settings for a hardcore mode, but it doesn't tell you anywhere what it does and I couldn't notice a difference myself. The one plus I will give this game is that the ragdolls are funny as hell, every time you don't stick a landing or crash into a wall your character will ragdoll and faceplant and I found myself having the most fun when my character would fly into a funny position. The achievements are fairly easy once you get to grips with the controls, if you can play controller, I would recommend it over keyboard because the keyboard controls are not fun. The hardest ones just require following the steam guide and you'll get them eventually, really shouldn't take more than 30 minutes.5 languages supported,  and controller support.Skateboarding simulator with inconsistent controls and a lack of any real content for it's price. If skateboarding is your thing, get it on sale. Funny ragdolls almost save it.

_childDocuments_.review: Took about 20 minutes to get all achievements, and then there's nothing else to do. _childDocuments_.review: I had a pretty nice time with . The control scheme was nice and simple, if a little unintuitive at times, and the audiovisual feedback for executing skateboard tricks was fantastic. The problem I ended up having wasn’t with the quality, but with the quantity. Developer Paul Schnepf acknowledges that the game contains maybe one hour of content by describing it as a “digital toy”, which I think given the context is appropriate. It’s a simple system for controlling a skateboarder, four levels, and nothing else—the amount of enjoyment you get will come from how much satisfaction you get out of learning to master an activity. For me, this was worthwhile. I wanted to execute all the tricks that the Steam achievements guided me to learn, and as a result I have pretty much mastered everything you can do with this game over the course of a couple of hours.Whether or not I recommend  is a very different question to whether I like it. I really like it, even if it’s unintuitive (you gain speed on ascending ramps by standing up from a crouch as you rise), and the way it looks and the general design principle is very appealing to me and no doubt will be for others. The thing is, saying there is very little content means more here than it usually does—there is no progression of any kind, and the game doesn’t even give you a score for chaining or pulling off special tricks. If you play this, you will need to be motivated exclusively by your own desire to get better at it, and personally I think that can be refreshing.I would recommend against this game if you’re looking for a good time-to-dollar ratio, or if you need direction or external incentives to have fun. In general though, I do tentatively recommend the game for what it does provide—it’s just important that you know what to expect going in.

_childDocuments_.review: You ever play a game for eight minutes, get the feeling you've seen all there is to see, and then you read about it and see the developer touting how there's nothing to unlock as a feature?  The store page goes on to tamper expectations, mentioning how it's more of a tiny digital toy, and it's "at the price of a medium sized cinnamon pistachio latte to go."I don't know what that is, but it sure sounds pretentious.  I drink gas station coffee made by an immigrant with a unibrow and four kids, and we're going to laugh at your medium sized cinnamon pistachio latte to go together.The game's six bucks.  I got Yakuza 0 for five.   I wouldn't pay six bux for a medium sized cinnamon pistachio latte to go, nor would I pay that for this game.  Thank goodness this was a freebie, at least.

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is a little bite sized chill game where your main objective is to simply skate. No unlockables, no story, just strap in and play.Gameplay is really fun, it's not hard at all to pick up, it is a little weird compared to other skateboarding games but once you have it down you have it down. The flow is also really great, it's awesome to just pump around a pool to get speed hitting monster spins. I also just like having a game where there is no objective, but also nails the transition aspect.There is nothing to unlock and no story which I don't mind at all, it's fun to just sit around and skate areas, however I do wish there were more maps available or at least some sort of modding integration whether it be Steam Workshop or Modio because once you've played all the maps for a bit, that's just it nothing more. There are some achievements however that might keep you busy, but again once you've unlocked these there isn't much to do and it'll really depend on whether or not like the dev said you want a "digital toy," and can enjoy what's here. I can see people not playing much after exploring what's available and I can see people staying and playing in intervals.Overall I would recommend, but for a lot of people you might have to think of it as "a digital toy" that you play here and there. I also don't know if I would recommend it at full price, that'll depend on you tbh, however getting it on sale isn't going to hurt. Game also works flawlessly under Linux for all mah penguins out there.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A slick but limited experience. Despite the controls feeling a little awkward to get used to, once you learn how to perform stunts it becomes a great distraction for a couple of hours. That's about all I see people playing this game though, a couple of hours.There's a handful of stunts to perform, and 4 maps that do an adequate job to mix up the scenery. The 12 achievements that come with this game are pretty much the only real objectives in this. Otherwise, all you're left with is what the developer described as a 'tiny, self contained toy'.For some that will be a turn off but I'll praise the developer for trying something that is fairly unique and doesn't feel outside the scope of what they are able to create. Whether it's made by a single person or a small team, you often see ambitious projects on Steam which have noticeable shortcomings, optimisation is particularly what comes to mind.So to have a hassle free experience like this, where the developer has organically set limitations makes this game feel like a complete experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A simple indie game with 4 levels, 4 tricks, 2 directions to spin and a whole lotta zen. You play as a skater in an isometric ramp or park and enjoy the physics of skateboarding. You can't push with your leg, only accelerate by crouching on your board at the right times to build momentum into your next jump. You can also do boardslides off of the edges of ramps and do tricks in midair. It's extremely simple and small as a game, but for $1.49 it's a relaxing game rather than something too depthful. There's also a hard mode for the more dedicated skaters who want the challenge. You have to land the board near perfectly or your trucks get caught on the edge of ramps. That's the only extra sort of mode besides these 4 levels that come with the game. I can't recommend this at full $5.99 price with the extreme lack of content outside of 4 levels (1 skatepark with two bowls, a pool,  a halfpipe and a megaramp) such as no challenge or gimmick modes; and no unlockables, but its a must get to all my skating friends at -75% off.Wait for the discount and then grab it!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Simple yet entertaining!Selling itself as a digital toy The Ramp kept me hooked by its state of flow & just one more time gameplay.  While the menu/settings a bit unpolished, the controls without an option to re-bind them in game (as of writing this review) this digital toy has kept my mind focused while chatting with friends and in my down time become an enjoyable way to relax.Rather impressive for a single dev project in my opinion, they found their target audience & also managed to fill that very niche gap they set their goal towards. Keep up the good work Paul, can't wait to see what you make next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Great little timewaster.  You skate around in four, quite small, different sections - two bowls, a halfpipe and a ramp. One button for landing and pushing off, one to grind and the ability to spin pull off a selection (about 5 or so, unless I'm missing something) of tricks in midair (using right thumbstick, not sure about keyboard).There's not much to it but it is pretty addictive and great fun for 15-20mins at a go.  It does come across as almost a demo due to it's minimalism though, which may detract some.There is an incredible amount of potential here and it would be nice to see it open to modding as it would add so much replayability.  Indeed, the biggest flaw I find with the actual gameplay is that I find myself wishing there was more to do.I got this in a bundle and am happy that I did; however given what I've said above, I wouldn't pay the asking price for it.  As fun as it is, it is also very basic - both in gaming terms and options (for example, you can turn music on or off but not sound effects).  If you can get this in a sale or bundle though, then I'd say go for it unless you  hate skateboarding (but in that case why are you even looking at this game, let alone reading reviews for it?)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.The ramp is a minimalist skateboard game where you skate on skate parks that look like small dioramas. The camera is placed far away unlike the only other skate game I played (Tony Hawk) and that makes it easier to see where the characters are going and where they are landing.There is no story mode or tournaments, or any kind of objectives, so it’s more of a sandbox game that you play when you feel like it. There isn’t any system to score and keep track of points either. The game levels are well designed, ranging from the basic half pipe, to the mega ramp, and look good but only 4 levels are available. The characters you can pick are low poly models without the option to be customized. The background music is relaxing and the sound effects are well placed and realistic.The game plays like a sort of rhythm game, where you need to press and release a button at the right time to gain momentum. Once you’re on air you can make rotations using one of most popular tricks like nosegrab, japan air, etc… You also have the option to grind on edges, using a different button. Personally I didn’t like the control scheme on the controller (still easier to get the grinding achievements on it), and ended up completing the rotation achievements on the keyboard.       12 Achievements. Around 2 hours (for me), heavily depending on skill and luck. Easy to play. Medium. I got the 1280 rotation one on the big ramp after a few tries (using a trick helps the character rotate faster) but the 1080 outside the mega ramp requires some tries. There are videos available but the key points are getting enough speed and then doing a semi circle (easier on the second or third levels)  to start rotating to that direction before you’re on air, with a bit of luck you’ll do enough rotations and land correctly.  The ramp is an interesting minimalist sandbox skate game that looks good and plays well, but that offers very little content. Recommended if you can get it at a cheap price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really nice game to start up and play for a few minutes at a time. It's simple, yet you can improve a lot on your flow with pumping the board in the game, finding new lines and perfecting them. The way you can get more spins by how you make a turn before you jump. It's almost perfect for what it is supposed to be.But I do have some criticism and personal things I would've liked in it. There should be an option to lower the volume for the music instead of only having a mute/unmute option. It's too loud at times. I do wish that when you rotate in the air, you can't rotate the opposite way from when you go into the air (maybe make the board itself twist a little further or back if you misjudge the rotation in the jump). Espcially for hardcore mode it'd be a nice touch. I also would've liked more options for grinds by using the arrows, and making two opposite arrows also do a unique grab on the board.I highly recommend this game for anyone looking to kill some time and mess around with the pumping and jump physics.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute treat of a game. A minimal art style combined with a fun music mix makes this a really chill time.  The physics and mechanics are just expansive enough to create a higher skill ceiling for those who want to push the limits of what is possible. There are quite a few moves you can pull off and a handful of parks to test your skills on. There are no leaderboards or point systems, which adds to the chill theme. I've enjoyed playing around with this after long days at work and it's a nice way to unwind. Worth the purchase imo.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: the dev makes very clear what this game is. You get exactly what you are advertised and for what that is I totally recommend this game. Regarding the price the line gets blurry after you get to the 5€ mark. It would be great so see some more ramps added in the future to justify the price tag but imo 5€ for this game is better spent than 5€ for an overpriced drink at a club.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Its a small game with not a lot do to... but for the cost of a beer you get a cool skate game mechanic that really captures the feeling of transistion skating. Would be great if new tricks and levels were added over time (more grinds / lip tricks specifically).. lets hope. If you're a skater you'll enjoy this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: You want a simple skating game without a lot of fluff but some excellent gameplay then this is it. For $5 this game is absolutely worth it. My only hope is that maybe they add a couple more maps or wider halfpipes/ramps. And more moves like kickflips , handplants and some other stuff. But it's really chill fun when you only have a little bit of time to play something.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, stylish, fun. No better way to spend your last few bucks remaining on your Steam account.I bought this game without high expectations. It's not much, but it's perfectly working and feels just as chill and smooth as it should. It is so much more fun than other games that are way less simple and way more expensive. I like sk8.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Gotta hand it to Hyperparadise for not putting a score counter or time attack mode in here. It reminded me that a game could just be for fun. Even similar games like Art of Rally are still competitive. Just sit back, relax and enjoy a moment of distraction for less than a coffee from Starbucks, I think you've earned it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very relaxing, which I feel makes it unique for a skating game. I tend to play it for 10-20 minutes at a time when I'm on break, or when I'm looking for something to pass the time. That being said, I really appreciate the joy it brings me as a former skater. As simple as it is, the game really captures the feeling of carving bowls, doing endless lines, and trying to push your skills. In the future I hope the developer can add a few more levels. It doesn't need to be anything crazy, but here are my suggestions:- small street plaza (two quarter pipes with a funbox)- downhill snake run with bunny hillsIf you used to skate, or if you're looking for a relaxing game this is the one for you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: All of the recent skateboarding games I've played have failed to deliver on one aspect, that being transition. This game delivers nothing but this and it's a welcoming change. My biggest and - realistically only - issue with the game is that the Dev clearly doesn't actually know what a "stale fish" is. It is not an indy nose bone (that being the trick labelled as a Stale fish in this game) and it saddens me greatly. Other than that it took me 5 minuets to get used to the mechanics and I'd strong recommend this game to anyone looking to scratch that ramp itch.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is the chillest skateboarding game in the genre. No challenges to fulfill (aside from a few achievements you'll naturally unlock), no high scores to beat, no time limit... it's just you and your board. It's smooth, satisfying, and perfect as a little pick-up-and-play title for when you just need a 10 minute break.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: As the developers have said this game is not gonna  fill your waking moments , and who'd expect it at that price ! I play in short bursts usually ending in a Jamaican finger slap ( all the louder with physically challenged (all of them ) youths present ) There's not a lot of game here , but what there is has been made with passion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very cool simple game. Some people have complained about the controls, but if you've ever skated a vert ramp it’s basically just like pumping to build speed.If the dev could incorporate different grinds in addition to board slides it’d be perfection! Maybe something like RB: Boardslide, RT: Nose Slide, LB: 50/50, LT: 5-0Regardless… great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game was fantastic, a genuine gem!Easy 10/10!The Ramp is a very small skating sim, you can choose between 4 different locations and just shred how you want.A very relaxing and cool experience, I 100%'d the game in around an hour after messing about. Since then I just come back to the game to wind down after a big day.The game looks great, very minimal and vibrant!Controls are simple, and there's no real objective apart from the chievs you can get so you can do anything at your own pace. The sound design is satisfying, skating around the bowl sounds so good - and the music is groovin'. Even when you bail, the music slows down and it fits perfectly.It is very small, but for the price and the quality it's well worth!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: its fun to learn and easy to pick up. It's simple but very very chill. i'm not the best at skate games, just chilling at my own pace without keeping score was very relaxing. You can do the acheivements. other then that you make your own fun. and the maps do allow for that, to challenge yourself. My fav map was the pool one. looks so good and fun. I do think it would be nice to have costumization or a workshop area to have infinite content content. tho its not a big deal. tho i do like the idea to have other skaters to bomp into or even a 2 player mode. staying simple as is but with more fun and simple things to interct for what it is, its money well spent in a super chill game
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: i think there's a lot of merit in games that look good and feel good, and i knew this game checked both of these boxes in the first five seconds of gameplay. the ramp is the smoothest, sleekest skate game i have ever played, and is a real treat to experience with a gamepad. i say "game," though it really is more of a toy at the moment, with no collectibles or underlying reason for your skating. it's just you and the ramp. would love to see more content for this because, as it stands, this could serve as a very solid base for something really incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, but the only things i would like to see is a real skate park map with railings and all that. and more unlockables like jackets or boards and that stuff. But besides that you should buy it, maybe only on sale because it is not that big of a game so dont go directly buy when you see it. But its a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it, fondly reminded me a lot of the old DS version of Tony Hawks. I thought this was going to be more realistic though tbh, it has crazy videogame physics and no transfers, so you'll turn corners in mid air to follow the ramp shape below. Plaudits to the dev as it looks and feels plenty nice, and the price is agreeable for the content. However I can't see myself coming back to this much, a few runs on each of the 4 screens and I feel like I'm done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: "Look mom, I can skate."This small game is really good and has potential to me more. We are used to play other games where you can get points, but in this game you don't need points or a score. Just chill and do some cool tricks.@Paul when you read this maybe it's possible to add more tricks and some combos? Would be sick.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential. 5 or 6 bucks for some chilling is great. The absence of real goals allows you to set them yourself. The simplicity is the best part of the game. All it needs is more maps (maybe a community mapping tool?) and mayyybe some flip tricks. Once more maps are available, this game would be 10/10 would hit the ladder in the pool again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. There are actually 4 maps, Megaramp being my personal favorite. My only complaint about the game would be that the Lord of the Board achievement is legitimately ♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've done COUNTLESS 1080s on all other maps and it refuses to pop. Really getting on my nerves as it's the only achievement I have left.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the old skateboard toy ramps and boards kids had back in the 90s/00s, fun and very smooth game to play for 20 minutes while you procrastinate your day awayLike others have said, an in-game map builder/workshop support and a few more tricks like lip tricks/inverts would be amazing but for the price of a coffee, its worth every cent
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I hoped it would be when I saw it. It's simple, fun, and addicting! Reminds me of the Tech Decks I had when I was a kid. I think it has a ton of potential to be even better too. I love the soundtrack. As someone who is a huge fan of skateboarding games and has been playing them for a very long time, well done!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful minimalist skating game designed around the concept of flow state that achieves its modest goal perfectly. Though it obviously lacks mechanical depth, it's still engaging through the pumping mechanic which requires good but forgiving timing to build up speed and the different board grabs, spins and grinds the player can perform. A good little experience for fans of skating and those interested in tightly designed, minimalist games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I can't skate for love nor money, but with this game I am flying like the birdman himself. Game desparately needs more levels, but considering the price it doesn't need a gosh-darn thing. If you're an achievement hunter, don't buy it, there are very few. But if you enjoy the visceral, almost meditation like sensation of carving bowls and perfecting your pumping, then get this game. Meanwhile, I'm just over here trying to 540 alley-oop the ladder on the pool level if you need me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I paid: 4€I got: An amazing small skating experience that was fun, relaxing and slightly challenging.The game could add some game modes (such as some kind of "chrono mode" to get as much points as possible in a certain amount of time) or add a few more maps, but as it is today, it is definitely worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: i'm still not sure what hardcore mode does.the maps, while there's only four, are pretty varied and have stuff to do in them that you can't do in the others- like jumping over the ladder in the swimming pool.we (or at least i) really want the soundtrack on spotify or something- all of the songs in this game are great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a breath of fresh air <3I love how simple it is, and how minimalist it is. No BS, no progression, scores, etc. Just vibes. The music is cool and once you get into the flow of things, it's a lot of fun to see how long you can go on a run.Wish list:- ability to upload your own music tracks that could interact with the game (slow down effects when you wipe out)- some different options for boardslide/grinds- kickflips :p- a skate park level - small customization for clothing color, hair, board color- some flat ground skatingreally great for a $5 price point. I hope that there is some future content added, but I'm happy to support the dev and enjoy this. Also! It's rare for me to find fun games that run on my MS Surface Pro, this is great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim when it showed up in my recommended. I sat there and played it for 45 minutes straight with my daughter having a blast with it. It's simple, addicting and just good fun and a great way to kill time. Can't beat the price tag even if wasn't currently on sale. Get it, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Managed to get all the achievements within an hour of playing. For its price, it's a solid digital toy. Been a fan of the Tony Hawk and Skate games for a long time and for me, The Ramp is like the Free Skate equivalent of those two. Content is fair enough. A sequel or new content update could do. (Create-a-park/Build a park, Option to go on foot, BMX mode, +more customization options, etc.) This format has potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: It's a $5 toy that does what it promises  well. This is a small sandbox game which has tight controls and really fun gameplay. Keep in mind that this is a focused experience and not a game as a service. If you like skateboarding this is a must have. Even if you don't like skateboarding games and like to play small indie games, try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: THE RAMP is a very fun game I would 1000% recommend it. It's a small simple time waster/consumer its very fun to play alone and has a good soundtrack, so you never get bored. The achievements are really fun to earn and some even quite challenging. Though quite a small game, you find yourself doing new tricks often. Also congratulations to the creator of this game who single-handedly developed this whole game. Was worth the money i payed and i really enjoyed playing it, will probably come back to it at some point :)for what this game is its a 10/10but in case of all games iv'e ever played 5/10 ( my opinion )
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Very small game but delivers such a big punch in the fun department. The smoothness of skating around and gaining speed is great. This game would be awesome with more maps since I have played everything and 100% completed it in less than 45 minutes. For any skateboarding completionists out there, this is a must buy for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is not a simulator, or a game with A LOT of content. But it wasn't the intention at all, and it's not what I was expecting.Having said that, this game is SICK. The music is ON POINT, the gameplay is pure flow, and the graphics are gorgeous. It is a super relaxing game and I STRONGLY recommend you getting it if you like skating.9/10 for me. Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for people who just want to chill and take a break from everyday life. Can't really play for long though since it gets boring but you can definitely escape life for half an hour or so.Controls are a bit weird but is easy enough to learn and get the hang of and there's kind of a flow to it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cute little arcade-y skateboarding game! It's nice and simple, very smooth once you get the hang of the controls.Definitely  sparse on maps and content (especially for $6) but the core gameplay loop is solid enough, and there's a lot of charm in its simplicity. Would love to see more maps added over time!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Personally I am not a big fan of skateboards, but a game made by a ISLANDERS dev (great game), with one of my favorite art styles, on sale for 4.79, it was an absolute steal. I played it and so far I've played about 45 minutes, and I love it. Only 4 maps, but I hope for more soon as that does not stop the awesome free play this game offers.
