_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a really lovely little skating game.Few skating games get the physics of pushing off feeling as nice as this.Great game to just relax to every now and again, you can "beat the game" in about half an hour or so but its not really about that, this is a game to jump in and chill doing some fun runs to relax to. Love it and can't wait to see more stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill game!Just skate to catchy beats and try out new things! With every time I start the game, I get more confident & try more cool maneuvers.It's not a game you probably play for a long session, but you will keep come back! You get a load of fun for the relatively low price!And props for the honest marketing.. I mean.. Watch the trailers & you know what you're up to!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a minimalist skateboarding game then this is really good. There are three vert maps (a halfpipe, a swimming pool and a bowl) and a mega ramp. Also, I really like the fact that there is a clicking noise to indicate rotation. It's a nice little touch that gives the player a little more control whilst doing spins. I'd love to see a sequel (maybe The Park?).
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: wow. i had £4 to spend in my steam wallet and i kept buying games that ended up being bad and id refund them. 2 weeks of doing this and i found "the ramp" and wow. although there is no score and only 4 levels it is still really fun and the music is super viby. when i go back to school in a couple weeks it will be awesome to come home and play this after a long day. great game! definetly worth the £4.EDIT: I'm not sure about anyone else but for me the game crashes a lot. i have a decent pc and no other game crashes. doesnt change my feelings about the game tho.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what it says it is. It is a simple game. More like a toy, even! Once you build a little muscle memory with the slight learning curve, you will just be cruising around or grinding the mega ramp for 10 or 20 minutes, every time you are bored! In between matches of your favorite multiplayer game, or just as a "fidget" while you watch a movie or your favorite twitch streamer!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this on sale and immediately played for 3 hours straight. I put on some lectures I was catching up on in the background with picture-in-picture and I just played this while listening and sort of watching them. This is the perfect therapeutic toy to play with while you need to pay attention to something else. It's perfect for having fun while not distracting you from the video or lecture you have in the background.10/10 perfect for people who can't just sit and watch something but have to be actively doing something at all times.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Ramp is insanely fun to play, while a small game, its oddly satisfying smashing into the ground at high speeds. I hope to see more of this game in the future, maybe some influencers could boost the game. Either way, there is a lot of potential here and it's so cool to see one person make a game this awesome! Finally I leave you with a pro-tip: Spam shift+space to build up insane amounts of speed while turning, the 2nd and 3rd maps are the best for this trick. Rating - 12/10  (gotta make this a 12/10 because even my friend watching me play, enjoyed the game so much)
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly the best ramp skating out of any game yet, it’s almost a shame there isn’t a full trick list. However it’s is super fun just carving it up and grabbing airs low key, the way it’s meant to be. If you skate or enjoy skating games, for less then the price of a pack of cigarettes or a coffee ( these days ) you should have no complaints.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest I've only played 15 minutes of this, but it's awesome. I'm going to be playing this game via Steam Link because it's exactly the itch I want when I'm looking for a mobile game. The mechanics are wonderful and the maps are all you need in skate zones. I'd love some type of scoring system to keep track of your high scores and try for combos, but for the purpose this developer intended this game delivers 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A small but fun game skateboarding game. It's relatively simple, but a game you can really chill and zone out to. Basically think bite-sized zen mode skateboarding.More maps would certainly be appreciated, but the 4 that are available have nice diversity.The game would really benefit from a few more settings options like video settings or control mapping, but it hasn't stopped me from enjoying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay components are all there to let you chill out, hardcore mode adds more challenge by requiring you to make more precise landings but makes it feel even more rewarding whenever you pull out something good. I would suggest to the dev to add different fixed camera angles to the circular maps like the pool as a sort of little refreshment and variety, and also being able to customize the color of the background behind us; they are small changes in scope but would make for great QoL. The game is  well worth the 5$ and I recommend it fully!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun little game with a LOAD of potential if the dev has the time and/or team to get it going. The only constructive criticism I can give the game is the tutorial is pretty difficult to understand. You are thrown into it without any text to tell you what to do like it does to move your right stick to do tricks. It just keeps flashing HOLD A! RELEASE A! on your screen. When? What? How? Did this for about ten minutes not knowing what I was doing wrong? Does it need to be held or just tapped? Do I release before or after I land? I still don't know when to hit A...Also, there needs to be an option for changing the audio levels. The game is super loud on my PC I need a 0-100 slider to turn it down please.Some things I would love to see in the future:• A music folder where you can add your favourite punk tracks to relive the good old days of Tony Hawk Pro Skater• Character customisation. Skating is 50% skating 50% looking rad. Different options for hairstyle and hair colour (mohawks, buzz cuts, beanies or caps), shirt colour and logo designs like skulls and such, pants style and colour (shorts, skirts, pants), shoes style and colour (classic skate styles like Vans)• An open skate park with rails to grind, gaps to jump, stairs to ride down, and bowls to jump into. Like the Tokyo 2020 Olympic Park skateboarding park. Not JUST halfpipes and bowls.• Game modes like time trial high score or biggest combo or stickers popping up on the map to ride around and collect• Community maps would be killer with assets to plop on a map and share with other players to beat high scores and such
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little skateboarding themed toy, thoroughly enjoyed it.It reminds me of how I remember the vert skating in EA's "Skate or Die" (circa 1988?) but with crossed with the Surfing from California Games (on the Atari Lynx).Control is responsive and intuitive, the control systems have nuance and allow for a pleasing experimentation based progression curve in ability to interact with the various levels to do the harder tricks.The overall play experience is mostly very 'flowy' & natural feeling - and I had a lot of fun getting all the achievements (though a couple require a *lot* of experimentation & practice!)Speaking as a skateboarder with 30+ years experience I'd say that the mapping from input to the various grabs doesn't make an awful lot of sense (& pretty sure what it calls 'stalefish' is a straight leg indie) but that doesn't really detract from the experience.The only 'grind' in the game is in fact a slide, and misnamed at least 50% of the time (what it calls 'boardslide' is usually a lipslide) - however despite my initial disappointment at this I found that it was actually still fun to do that one slide. I would really love to see a few actual grinds added using the trucks, but honestly not sure it _needs_ any more
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying and intuitive to play. I've always been rather rubbish at skateboarding both in real life and in video-games but the general feel and mechanics of this game flowed so easily. To be honest, of my total playtime so far around 90% of it was spent trying to get the final 1080 achievement which was so much harder than i would have assumed initially. I eventually made it after around 150 attempts just before writing this review but it was really rewarding in the sense that i achieved it though pure intuition and experimenting with the games physics engine, rather than going online and finding a tutorial for it (not that there are any at this point anyway). I guess my only issue if you can call it that is that after finally 100 percenting the game im not sure what to do with it anymore, but i cant exactly complain given that I only paid £3 and the game literally only came out yesterday. I feel like maybe more maps or a level editor is the only natural progression from here but with what time i have spent i found the game extremely satisfying to play and well worth its pricetag.Pros:- really nice music - really pleasing aesthetic - fun and intuitive game-play- the tick audio queue is a really helpful system when judging your speed when attempting tricks, not sure if i have seen this in a skateboarding game before but i feel like i would be lost without it. - Price tag Cons:- Tutorial seemed kinda busted for me regarding when i should hold X- "Finishing" the game dint take particularly long and there isn't much replay value. (All really minor issues considering the games pros, the price tag and the fact that the second issue is literally addressed in the games description)????:- Skateboard physics are sometimes extremely wacky. But i used this to my advantage when going for the 1080. Really cool game and does what it says on the box. Will recommend to my friends to see how long everyone takes to land a 1080 outside of the big ramp
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The overall experience is quite well polished and it does provide a relaxing gameplay but unfortunately there's not much to do after a some consecutive runs....Will surely come back to it when it adds more features but for now it's not that interesting for me....That being said it might be fun for someone who is craving for some relaxing time....A few suggestions for the Developer though --More Levels would be amazing to play on.-Community made levels could be a great addition.-Remap the "A" button to any trigger or bumpers which would help in using the Left Thumb stick without lifting the thumb off it for pressing the "A" button.-I know it's supposed to be a chill game but and online/couch co-op would be an amazing addition. It's more fun with a friend as well.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't sure what to expect from this skateboarding game but I am pleasantly surprised. As the description states it's very small but it's actually really fun especially for the price. It only took me about 20 minutes to go through everything it has to offer but I feel like I can and will come back to this often, even just to dabble a bit. I hope we get a few more areas to play in, but if not that's fine too...
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing for about an hour writing this, the game is pretty simple and straight forward, You got ramps, you got a skateboard, and you do tricks. No goal other than having simple fun.Playing with a keyboard was terrible to get used to, so I connected my ps4 controller which was way easier to handle. Would recommend adding key settings.Once you get the mechanics the game is pretty fun, you jump the ramps and do tricks while trying not to fall.When you fall there's no big scene or anything like that and you can just start over with a click of a button - that is highly appreciated by myself.I actually can't believe I spent an hour on this game, it felt like maybe 15 minutes, which is the sign of having fun.For the 5 bucks I would give it 9/10. Just remember this is a small game, and the only goal is to have fun.As the developer wrote - no score, no missions, no unlockables. I usually play mmorpgs so this was a nice refreshing experience.I would hope to see more future content, like more maps and tricks, especially more grind stunts which this game is currently lacking, or I was just unable to get the hang of it yet lol.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole, this game is an enjoyable experience for a short amount of time. It is flow-y and allows for players to develop a sort of rhythm with their moves. The soundtrack (?), while nice at first, does become annoying after the 30 minute mark. The game is "completable" in an hour or less, but nonetheless provides simple yet frustrating challenges. While the developer does offer that the game is very short as a sort of disclaimer, what is more disappointing is the potential that got missed out on. More maps, off-board moves (i.e., kickflips, treflips), an optional score/combo counter, and perhaps even a comedic multiplayer mode might have provided this game far more replayability. In the end, even if I think the game is missing a lot, it serves its purpose.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Even with the limited scope and trick selection, this game is pretty much the best vert skating experience in any game on Steam right now by default, with Session not having implemented transition mechanics yet and Skater XL's being wonky and heavily mod-dependent at the time of writing. Really good fun, while the novelty lasts. Still though, if you have any other skateboarding game on PC, it's unlikely The Ramp will hold your attention for much longer than it takes to naturally complete most or all of the achievements. It really lives and dies by the sword of minimalism; there's an engaging charm to its simplicity, but without a deeper bag of tricks and mechanics to draw from, its novelty doesn't have much staying power.Mechanically, the game is simple, responsive, and fairly intuitive. Not much to complain about. I can't really fathom yet how a non-megaramp 1080 is going to be possible for that particular achievement, but every other achievement was pretty easily attainable, even with Hardcore Mode enabled.Some really basic functionality has annoyingly been omitted from the settings, including but not limited to a volume slider, a rumble on/off setting for controllers, any kind of input remapping, and any explanation of what the "Hardcore Mode" toggle actually does (though it's not hard to figure out from playing). Hopefully some of these will be patched in.Great fun for the money, just don't expect a game that punches too far above its price point in terms of replayability if you've been spoiled by near-endlessly-replayable sub-£5 Steam games like cheap roguelites. This feasibly could change if different grind and stall variations, flip tricks, handplants, etc. are added over time, of course, but the game's already well-worth the low asking price as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Cool toy, and even the dev wants you to know that's all it is.  It's worth the money, tbh.  My one criticism is the tutorial could be more clear:  A text box telling you what you're doing, instead of freezing/warping time when you goof up.  I find that even more confusing, and am not 100% sure I know what I'm doing.  However, after you get past it, and just play a bit you start to get the hang of things.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I've not played the game for very long but it's a super chill skateboarding experience, My biggest problem is there isn't an in game music slider, I had to use volume mixer which isn't really a problem, just means having to tab in and out to change the volume being as the game only has either music on or music off. I've only noticed one bug on the 3rd map where-in if you grind and come to a complete stop above the underpass the character gets sucked into the wall and you have to reset the level to fix it, made the 25m grind achievement a little bit annoying to get.Only one " issue " with the game if you can even call it that. I look forward to future content additions!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game!Love the skate physics. Controls took me a second until I started thinking of the jumping/landing more in terms of momentum/weight, which was fun to grow comfortable with. I love how compact all the levels feel, like every detail down to the pool ladder has been playtested into polish. On the note of the pool ladder, it adds a nice touch of sound design if you wipe out on it. Sometimes I felt like the chill lo-fi music was fading out in sequence with my grinding, which I enjoyed. Overall, the sound design compliments everything quite nicely.I'm still working on the achievement to land a 1080 outside of the final level, but otherwise all the little challenges feel 'just right' for what you'd want to work on throughout a game of this size/scope. I know I'll feel satisfied when I unlock that final 1080. (And if this game sells well enough, which I truly hope it does, an expansion could be a lot of fun one day!)If you're on the fence, pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun! The second trailer (the ramp in 90 seconds) explains the game very well; watch that for a solid explanation.The one think it can't get across is how weighty and technical the game feels. The pump mechanic (press a to crouch and then stand up at specific angles of the bowl/half pipe to gain speed) is fun by itself, but put in combination with spins and grab tricks both are elevated to this tricky little toy that leaves me always wanting to go a little faster, to get a little more air so i can get an extra 180 degrees on my next jump... But if I go too fast or start my turn too early i might run into a ladder or fall off the pipe. Don't get me wrong, it's an extremely chill game. But the mechanics and polish (i can only assume a LOT of time was spent just tweaking how it feels to move) make each jump on the ramp feel like a chip. Crisp, delightful, and ooh maybe I'll go for another one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A great small game that features a good deal of variety in vert environments. The controls are buttery smooth and the sound and graphic design makes landing big spins all the more satisfying. There's no missions or timers or score counters so you can just focus on doing stuff that looks cool. Will definitely be going to this game when I look for something to just relax with for 15-30 minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A very chill game indeed. Not so much in the beginning while you're still figuring out the controls (a gamepad is recommended), but at some point it just clicks - and the whole things just flow beautifully. There's not really a goal or highscore to meet, but a few fun achievements do exist. Perhaps we'll see a few more maps in the future?
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, this game is a very chill game and I like how you can just skate without doing any quests or nothing. I love this game and have done tons of tricks. As the game has been very recently released, I will not push it or anything, but I suggest to the developer of this game that you should add more tricks like kickflips and traditional skateboarding tricks. This game is really fun and I highly recommend that you buy it. They never said you could buy fun but with this game you can! Big fun for little price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: You get what you expect: a really fun digital toy centered on the vert skating experience. Calm, flow-type game with good sound design and simple controls. It's great as-is and well worth the money for a coffee break game to relax your brain.Would love to see small additions like a spine transition or stall moves like the disaster or rock and roll.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: The Flow Is Real! Such a great experience to relax and day dream. It really does capture that feeling of just cruising around, enjoying the freedom and rhythm of skating. This is going to be a great go to on the steam deck as well. Looking forward to seeing some more ramps, maybe a mini ramp?? Love it, thanks for all the hard work Paul!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played this game for long, but I can tell that this is going to be a game I will consistently come back to when I'm bored. It's a great game for zoning out and losing yourself in the flow state. Exactly the kind of game i needed. It has a similar feeling to the pro skater series, with complex combos and lines coming with mastery of the mechanics. Very well done.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful minimalistic and addicting skating gameplay! The game feedback sound and visuals fit brilliantly together creating a really immersive experience.The challange of completing the Steam achivements is very nice, because it doesnt add a strict mission but rather a "hey cool, you made something nice and difficult and I noticed", and gives a lose guidance for exploring the game.Nice game overall, would really recommend it and would love to play an expension of it!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A slick little skateboarding toy/sim. While the gameplay may seem a bit minimal at first glance this feels very much like it rewards repeated play and effort spent on practicing tricks and moves. For the price it's well worth it and I only hope the developer adds more levels later on to extend replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little skateboarding game that is easy to learn and hard to master. Like real skateboarding you want to extend your legs while you're on a changing gradient to build speed. It gives a nice sense of momentum, although the controls can be a little fiddly. It's very easy to launch yourself off the side of the ramp if you're not careful because of the isometric viewpoint. I feel like it might be easier to control if the game was slower overall.Still, it's not like it actually matters if you fail. Plus the ragdoll is pretty funny.There is a limited set of tricks, but it doesn't really matter. The movement is what's really important.A fun toy that I'll probably return to every now and then to play 5 or so minutes at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Ramp

_childDocuments_.review:
You crave for flow? You just want to shred through a halfpipe without all the boring stuff? Say no more, The Ramp is your jam!

The Ramp captures the unparalleled feeling of real life vert skateboarding and that's pretty much it. There is a lot this game doesn't feature. What it offers you are the 15 minutes of flow that make a boring day great, at the price of a medium sized cinnamon pistachio latte to go.

detailed_description: GET THE LATEST VERSION OF EA SPORTS™ FIFA FIFA 22 Ultimate Edition FIFA 22 Ultimate Edition includes: 4600 FIFA Points About the Game Powered by Football™, EA SPORTS™ FIFA 22 brings the game even closer to the real thing with fundamental gameplay advances and a new season of innovation across every mode. What is FIFA? Play The World’s Game with 17,000+ players, over 700 teams in 90+ stadiums and more than 30 leagues from all over the globe. GAME MODES Career Mode – Live out your dreams as both a manager and a player in FIFA 22. Create the newest club in FIFA, design your kits, style your stadium, and choose whether to compete with the elite or rise up from the lower divisions as you manage your club to glory. Or test your skills as a player, with a more immersive Player Career mode that gives you more ways to progress, achieve, and immerse yourself in your Pro’s journey through the game. VOLTA FOOTBALL – Take it back to the streets with VOLTA FOOTBALL. Build a player, pick your gear, and express your style on the streets alone or with your squad in football playgrounds all around the world. Get rewarded for your skill on the ball with restyled gameplay, and play unique events in special locations each season as you unlock new gear through a new seasonal progression system that lets you earn XP towards all of the rewards on offer in VOLTA FOOTBALL, whichever mode you play. FIFA Ultimate Team – Get involved with the most popular mode in FIFA, FIFA Ultimate Team. Build your dream squad from thousands of players from across the world of football, make your club your own on and off the pitch with custom kits, badges, and a whole FUT Stadium to leave your mark on, and take your team into matches against the AI or other players in the FUT Community. Plus, welcome back some of the game’s most memorable players as new FUT Heroes, as some of football’s most memorable players return to the pitch. Unrivaled Authenticity – Play with the world’s biggest players in the world’s biggest competitions, including the iconic UEFA Champions League, UEFA Europa League, brand new UEFA Europa Conference League, CONMEBOL Libertadores, CONMEBOL Sudamericana, Premier League, Bundesliga, LaLiga Santander, and many more! When playing FIFA 22 on Steam, you can use your DUALSHOCK 4 and Xbox controllers to play your way. This game includes optional in-game purchases of virtual currency that can be used to acquire virtual in-game items, including a random selection of virtual in-game items.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had every Fifa since 2002. They have been steadily going downhill since FUT was introduced. The gameplay caters to esports players with no attempt at the realism that career mode enthusiasts such as myself crave. The AI (opponent and AI controlled teammate) logic is laughable. Other than the kits you cannot tell if you are playing against Man City or Norwich - each AI opponent attacks essentially attacks you the same way. I find it exhausting that I need to constantly change players on defense to get them into the correct position (oh CR7 is running thru the center of the park? don't worry about it). My wingers are completely marked by the fullback on the touchline, but perfectly happy to stand there with no attempt to find space. All defenders close down in straight lines, giving the attacker leverage to the inside. I've attempted to fix this by means of the Operation Sports sliders (who have done tremendous work for a decade), but even that cannot fix the gameplay issues. Goalkeepers are letting loose balls lie in the box 6 feet in front of them while players are on the floor, none of the other 10 players in the box can be bothered to collect the ball, so whichever player that fell down gets up first will gain possession. The transfer logic is a joke. Top tier players are changing clubs every other season. Teams are stockpiling 3 world class RBs, but won't address LB. 77 rated English role players are going to Spain. Liverpool is constantly selling Jordan Henderson, Arsenal are featuring Mo Elneny, City aren't starting KDB. They finally brought back create your own club, but I can honestly say I'd rather not have it. The lack of customization is astounding. There are 20+ kit colors that I can pick from, but I am limited to ~10 crest colors, AND they are all predetermined? It's not hard EA, I've seen you allow more customization in the NHL franchise - give me the ability to customize each color in the crest and give me the ability to pick my own colors from the color wheel. I get it, FUT is the EA cash cow, so most of the dev work will go there, fine. Can you spin off a separate gameplay AI for career mode? Or at least give the player the option of which AI gameplay they want (FUT arcade style or realism). You're losing the fanbase (career mode players) that made FIFA the #1 game in the world for a decade. Is it intentional? Make career mode so poor so we all give up and solely play FUT?

_childDocuments_.review: I only play career mode. The last Fifa I bought was 18. Unfortunately it seems that EA continue to neglect this game mode. Just two seasons in and I can already tell that this mode has had zero game testing from the developers. I compliment them on introducing a refined Be A Pro progression system and ditching the accomplishments. That's about it.Too many issues dating back numerous Fifa iterations. Most game breaking at this point. AI that just can't defend. Even on Ultimate difficulty having no issue scoring 2 a game with a 79 rated striker (I'm not particularly good at the game). Managers have names but they never get sacked, never rotate the squad, never change the formation, never pick the best team or pick players in their positions (longer you play the worse this issue becomes.).There's so many ways this mode could be improved but it's pointless wasting your breath as they don't listen/care. As long as you pay for the game and ideally cough up for some UT chits. I regret doing the former. All I can offer now is a warning to any career mode fan wondering if this is the year they properly pay attention to the disillusionment, it isn't.

_childDocuments_.review: The last FIFA I played was FIFA 12 and I had no interest in FUT back then. I picked this FIFA up just to see the FUT experience for the first time. I grinded to Elite division very quickly also got rank 1 in the old FUT Champions system. To be honest my experience started off very good, the game was very fluid. It all started on Black Friday and that time I realised what I got into. EA started bursting out packs non-stop. Until that point I felt like the pack system was okay and fair but after Black Friday I saw what FUT really is about. Nonstop gamble + the pressure of FOMO. Luckily I'm not a huge gambler and I don't believe in spending fortune on an RNG. Paid content like battle passes or quality of life upgrades are fair in games, but paying money for RNG is nothing different than going to a casino and playing slot machines.After the Fire/Freeze promo I also started experiencing the muddy gameplay where your players start feeling like bronze players. This still happens almost %20-30 of the time. Happens a lot on Fridays when Fut champions start, or a new promo gets released. Btw according to EA my connection quality is 99/100 and I have 500/500mbit fibre. There was a huge forum thread about this in the EA forums and they never did anything to fix it. I then found out that this was an ongoing problem that happens in almost every FUT season.One good thing about FUT is that it definitely rewards you if you grind the game. A lot of usable SBC players, couple of squad foundation players, and also a lot of packs are given by the game, if you do the achievements and objectives.Overall though, when you get to a certain point, the only thing that keeps you in the game is that moment when you pack a really really good meta player, which never happens because it's like one in a million chance. I can guarantee that it will not happen to you either unless you are a very very very very lucky person. Gameplay becomes boring when you get into it. Some basic skill moves, ball roll, driven passes, left stick dribble with lean/unique high agility players, green timed shots and that's it, you're in elite division and get to at least rank 3 in the new FUT champs system.EA constantly puts out promos and boost the stats of same players over and over again, If you want to keep up with the game but if you don't want to spend money on promos that will go to waste when Fifa 23 comes out, I suggest you don't buy this game and don't invest your precious time.I have 800 hours, I've done everything that is possible, all the achievements, elite division and rank 1 Fut champs but I can assure you that I don't feel satisfied. All the time I put in this game will disappear when the new one comes out. All the money that people spent is also gonna disappear when the new one comes out. Same players over and over, getting their stats boosted +1 every month, until all the cards hit 99.Stay away and save your time.

_childDocuments_.review: It was supposed to be way better than it is, but compared to other recent FIFAs, this FIFA feels much different, the gameplay is smoother yet broken as there is little to no delay when shooting, which makes the game much less skillful. I had lots of fun yet the AI is annoying as the players love to get offside, and the defense is manual, so if you don't defend your box well yourself, nobody will. Goalkeepers are completely broken, they catch perfectly angled shots yet struggle to catch the simplest ones at times. Efootball sucks, so unless UFL succeeds, EA will have the freedom to keep publishing the "same" game every year. To summarize it: If your last FIFA was FIFA 17 or older, stick with it, if you don't mind the outdated squads and graphics, otherwise, have fun with this one instead, you will get disappointed but unless UFL succeeds, get used to this one being the best football game we've got. If Steam was owned by EA, I would have to pay $5 to post this.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing over 2,000 hours of this game, split between me and my girlfriend this game feels like a big downgrade from all previous FIFA with many problems I can list. The player switching into the wrong player, clearly when I don't want to switch to that player to the passing detection in this game. In previous FIFAs I've never had an issue with the passing, but in this one my players was making much more passing mistakes than normal. The passing detection shows me that I'm passing to the player that I want but suddenly it switches and passes to a completely different player. The game feels too scripty when facing against AI, especially squad battles in FUT. Somehow playing legendary difficulty against bronze team with my full team of special cards and their bronze players can easily keep up with mine. Difficulty shouldn't secretly boost their stats (especially when its on ultimate boosting it to 99), but rather boost the AI intelligence. I've seen some "scripty" moments like when my player is clearly beating the AI when chasing the ball but suddenly my player massively reduce his speed for the AI to get the ball before me. Why does the AI deserve the ball more than me? It should be equally based. The AI can be very sticky with the ball too, like the ball is magnetic to their feet even after clearly tackling them and winning the ball. _childDocuments_.review: With my experience so far of playing FIFA 22, I have found this instalment an upgrade on previous titles in the series (since FIFA 19). I brought the game back in October 2021, after making the permanent switch from console gaming, to PC gaming. I find the game to be a brilliant way for me to chill out with, after doing work for my university modules.By far, the most played game-modes that I play is Career Mode [CM]. I believe that FIFA 22 for PC allows for more variation than console editions, and unlike prior FIFAs, I am able to continually come back and enjoy the game. This has been helped by, the limited, but interesting, modifications that you can apply to the game. I think these modifications provide somewhat more realism, and keep the game somewhat more fresh. I would encourage more mod-creators to work on FIFA 22, as there is a large scope of ideas that can be implemented to give players something new to try for. I personally am looking for a way to extend past the 15 seasons limit.Furthermore, I believe there could be a scope for the possibility of cosmetic changes. An example of this can be seen through modifications which implement the FIFA Club World Cup, and a cosmetic change could be the addition of the badge that teams receive after winning the competition. Although a minor feature, it would add to the realism of the game. Moreover, this would be a great way for EA to expand into more competitions, given their ability to get licensing As mentioned, the 15 season limit is an obvious issue for many players that have complained in the past. While I do believe it is hard to even get to 15 seasons, let alone 10, the ability to have more seasons (up to 30 for example) would allow for more RTG careers, with both clubs or your personal manager. However, I also find it difficult to do CMs which start in League 2, as I like to build a team gradually overtime; I do this usually by assigning myself three primary signings per season. It just adds to a level of realism that doesn't see me just bring in whatever and however many players I want. Personally, I would like to have a player CM that evolves into a managerial career. I know this is possible already, but having the ability to have longer CMs, would allow two senses of progress: one through your player's career, and second, through your now retired player becoming an up and coming manager. Another compliant I may have is the managerial objectives, which can be unrealistic and over the top. For example, I enjoy to make CMs with teams like Wolves and aim for more "realistic" targets such as the UECL or UEL. However, I have had it, where I will finish in a poor position, such as 12th, and the next season, be required to reach UCL places. Now usually, this doesn't effect the job and get me sacked, but it has. I think there should be some sort of option for the player to make more realistic objectives, if they want to. Something similar to what you have with the Create a Club CM.I don't know how many would share my opinion on this next point, but I have a love-hate relationship with player growth. While I enjoy the fact that the potential of a player is dynamic based on their statistics, I believe that player growth can be a bit too quick. I don't have too much of an issue with this, but I think it could be a good idea to have some sort of option where the player is allowed to decide the rate of growth, and whether dynamic potential is enabled. I know this is an irrelevant change and probably wouldn't have anyone that cared enough, I think this would just add to a level of challenge that there is with player growth.When doing an MUFC CM, I find it too easy to grow players such as Rashford and Sancho, especially on growth plans. I believe it is important to focus on specific growth plans for players but, I don't enjoy having Rashford/Sancho rated 92+ by the end of season one. This comes with the added position where it seems that growth plans can be exploited with leaving young players on position modifiers for a season, and only accepting the change at the end of the current season.One of the features that I have liked has to be the Create a Club CM. I think it helps with the personalisation of a player's CM. Obviously the feature is currently limited with the customisation features, but I think it lays the groundwork for future development. I think it would be a good feature if there is a way to add your own personal designs, without a third party. For example, if the player has designed their own club crest, I believe it could be a nice feature if the player is able to load that into the game and use it for their Create a Club's crest. This would be the same with the different kits. In terms of the club crest, I believe that the options are too generic and a feature like this could make the Create a Club CM stand out a bit more. Giving the player more customisation options would be the next way forward for this game-mode.I think the one thing that much of the CM player-base would want is extensions to licensing. Obviously, this is a tedious process, but I remember the hype about the possibility of having the National League in CM. This was only furthered with the licensing of Wrexham FC. I believe having the extra league would one, be an incentive to add longer duration to CMs, but also add a distinct level of extra challenge to an RTG.Adding to this, something I would definitely love to see is an expansion to Women's football. I think with the rise of the Women's game, there is a lot of potential for EA to jump on the possibility for a Women's football CM. However, the obvious problem is that there may be a lack of player-base that would warrant this expansion. I think that the Women's international teams are a start, and the next would be to start adding some leagues from the Women's game. However this is obviously filled with personal idealism.I personally have only more recently got into the FUT scene. With FIFA 20, I enjoyed the back-end of the FUT experience, with the Summer Heat expansion. FIFA 21, I only started playing in the May of 2021. With FIFA 22, I started FUT from the start practically. FUT for me has only grown on me in recent years. I believe this because I never used to enjoy the fitness system that was thankfully removed with FIFA 21. For that reason, I never really had a reason to enjoy the mode. However, nowadays that's a different picture. I should specify, I currently only play Squad Battles [SBs]. I have tried playing Rivals, but there is always too much latency. I am not sure if this is an issue with the EA Servers, which I know from past experience is a heated issue. However, I am especially happy with SBs this year. I think that EA have really turned around a pointless and tedious game-mode, and made it worthwhile. Unless I have just good "pack-luck" I think that the pack odds have been greatly increased. Every week that I contend in the SB, I am always getting fantastic rewards. I remember that my first week of rewards, I received Di Natale, which was 700k coins. That has been the best pack pull I have gotten, but I have also received other good rewards which have helped establish the team that I currently play with.Another feature I have enjoyed more this year are Squad Building Challenges [SBCs]. I feel this year that the SBCs have been more affordable, especially for players like myself that are free-to-play. I think my favourite SBCs are either Player moments, such as the Calvert-Lewin card, and different player picks and party bags. I think EA have made these a bit more affordable and I have enjoyed some great success with them.I think the other game-modes like KO and VOLTA are just a waste. I would personally drop VOLTA has I still feel it is an underwhelming mode.

Powered by Football™, EA SPORTS™ FIFA 22 brings the game even closer to the real thing with fundamental gameplay advances and a new season of innovation across every mode. New gameplay features in FIFA 22 give you more consistency between the posts with a goalkeeper rewrite that brings more composure to the most important position on the pitch, alongside new ball physics, explosive sprint that better matches the acceleration of the game’s quickest players, and new attacking tactics that let you take control of how your team plays. In Career Mode, live out your football dreams as you create and manage the game’s newest club to glory. VOLTA FOOTBALL rewards you for your flair with restyled small-sided gameplay and new ways to play and progress each season. Get the squad together in Pro Clubs with enhanced team customization and updated progression that puts you in control of your Virtual Pro’s development, and welcome back some of football’s most memorable players as new FUT Heroes in FIFA Ultimate Team™ with a redefined competition structure that makes testing your skills against other players more accessible. However you play, enjoy unrivaled authenticity everywhere with over 17,000 players, 700+ teams, and more than 30 leagues including the UEFA Champions League, CONMEBOL Libertadores, and the brand new UEFA Europa Conference League - only available in FIFA 22.
GAMEPLAY
Reimagined gameplay creates fundamental advances that you’ll feel across every mode in FIFA 22. A goalkeeper rewrite brings more composure and consistency to the most important position on the pitch, new ball physics reimagine every pass, shot, and goal, and explosive sprint lets you feel the acceleration of the game’s quickest players.
•	Goalkeeper Rewrite - A brand new goalkeeper system brings a new level of intelligence to the last line of defence, unlocking more reliable shot-stopping and smarter decision-making between the posts. In FIFA 22, goalkeeper positioning personality replicates the different styles of keepers throughout the game - from the lightning-fast reflexes of world-class shot stoppers like Jan Oblak to the aggression of sweeper keepers such as Ederson.
•	True Ball Physics - Real-world data imported into FIFA 22 takes the game’s ball physics to a new level of realism. Tuned parameters including speed, swerve, air drag, air resistance, ground friction, and rolling friction mean every touch, trap, shot, volley, pass, and dribble will look, move, and fly like the real thing.
•	Explosive Sprint - A new gameplay mechanic that changes the dynamic of one-on-one situations, Explosive Sprint gives you more control over acceleration when dribbling or defending. Lure opponents in and choose when to unleash your full speed to get away from the defender as you drive your team forward in attack.

detailed_description: Our Next Game About the Game Far, far away, there is a Forest, filled with dark things, indelibly influenced by the Witch who lives as distantly as she can from its undulating heart. You are a strand of light, coalesced to nurture the dark. Create pathways through the darkness in a top-down open world inspired by dark fairytales. Nurture the creatures of the Forest, repair ancient structures, and ultimately: confront the Witch who broke this place. Witch Strandings dials into the emerging genre of physical transportation. A digital forest that extends beyond the boundaries of your screen, in an all-new Strand-type game. FEATURES Whether swiping your mouse quickly to move through raging rapids, or inching forward to avoid being swallowed by quicksand, a unique cursor control method makes your journey a physical experience. Carry supplies across a twisting Forest to nurture disturbed creatures. Haunting open world with distinct biomes and a day-night cycle. Activate ancient structures to strengthen your link to the land of the living. Create your own pathways through a cursed and ruined Forest. Use haunted mushrooms, mystical artifacts, and more to alter the world. Kill any character at any time—permanently. Confront the Witch, and decide the fate of the Forest. Make the Forest a better place--or strangle it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like I've been scammed into buying this game. The overblown live-action trailer and steam store description gave me the impression that there was something more to this game than meets the eye, but there really isn't.The core gameplay is doing fetch quests over and over for a bunch of cardboard NPCs. Every NPC has a 1-paragraph sob story to make you want to help them, but that's all there is to them. They seem flawed enough to make you think that something about them might change for the better if you help them enough, but they never do. At the start of each new day they're exactly as crippled as they were the previous day, except their quest tally counter will have gone up by one. Once you've done enough fetch quests, the game pats you on the back for being such a nice guy and lets the credits roll.There's also a genocide option that seems like it was tacked on as an afterthought (because there HAS to be an alternative to the nice guy option).
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was gonna be an interesting game to play but as soon as the game started, my curiousness for it was replaced with frustration with its gameplay. It's an interesting concept, you are a small light in a dark forest, in charge of making it better and helping the animals in it. But sadly this just means you are on a long fetch quest to give each animal you discover, the items they need. This could seem like an easy thing to do, except the controls of this game must be some of the most annoying things in a videogame. You are just moving your mouse over and over (and lifting it to reposition it to move it again) to go from point A to B while avoiding the obstacles the map has. A lot of times you are dragging your way to tiles that kill you and because of the sensibility cap you have on the game, you end up dying. Another really big issue it has is with the design of the HUD. When you are moving up, your character goes behind the banner that pops up every time you enter a new zone (which happens a lot) and you cannot see where you are going. The same happens when you are moving down, except it's the health bar the new obstacle you have in the middle, and that one stays there. They have to change the bounds in which the character makes the map move with it.The idea is cute and interesting, but they need to improve the gameplay, because that's what makes this game a chore to experience, more like a fun one and, sadly, that aspect will make a lot of people not experience this game. I wouldn't recommend this game in the state as it is now, maybe when they improve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable but not for everyone. If you want deep gameplay features and hate fetch quests, you should give it a pass. If you want a short narrative experience in a surrealist environment with novelty mouse controls, this is a good one. The moral choices are too shallow though, and disabling two-way fast travel during the end game felt unnecessary.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but i think its worth warning people that this game is actively painful to play and you should absolutely stay away from this game if you have any type of joint pain while playing PC games.The game itself is fine albeit a little underdeveloped. You explore a forest by moving items around to allow you to travel faster/safer so you can make deliveries to forest animals. It has the same hypnotic effect as tidying up or untangling wires. Helping the animals never feels worth it but moving stuff around to help you explore is almost fun enough on its on.The problem is the character you play is basically your mouse cursor and every move you have to make seems almost purposely designed to trigger tendinitis. Almost every action in this game requires huge mouse movements that require you to pick up and move your mouse back to center. Want to explore? Huge painful mouse moves. Want to escape danger? Huge painful mouse move. Did you die? Well you have to do huge painful mouse moves to re-spawn. I played the game less than an hour but still feel it in my wrists hours later and i don't even normally have joint pain while playing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: i wish i could give the game a positive review, because i like the gameplay (although i agree with some other reviews that the trailer oversells the game), but the controls are absolutely abysmal.  even at the highest mouse sensitivity you have to move the mouse a lot and constantly pick it up and reposition it. it's a nightmare. i actually had to stop playing because my wrist was hurting more and more.on top of that the camera only moves when you are almost at the edge of the screen so you can't properly see where you are going. to make this worse the bottom part of the screen is covered by the healthbar and on the top you constantly get a (super annoying) popup telling you that you switched areas further obscuring your view.should they fix the controls i will change my review to positive, since i like the style of the game and enjoy the mechanic of placing specific items to remove obstacles blocking the way. right now however you should stay away from it if you tend to have issues with your wrist.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard "maybe" from me, essentially it's a mouse moving cursor game about carving paths to help various woodland animals. The story is very basic and told entirely through text, and the game is only about 1-2 hours long at most. This is the kind of game I'd expect to be around $5, not $15. It's concept is interesting and unique, there just isn't enough here to justify the price tag.My Curator Link:

_childDocuments_.review: So, somehow you've found your way to this Witch's Forest, and there's a strange claim that this is a "Strand-type" game, but what does that mean here? Unlike Death Stranding, from which this game takes inspiration, there's no asynchronous multiplayer collaboration, but ultimately that was just a side to the point of the game anyway. Death Stranding was about helping people, and forging paths through an unyielding environment, and in that respect, this game absolutely nails being a "Strand-type" game. The whole aim of the game is to restore the Heart of the Forest, which is achieved through helping the folks you find in the Forest while making paths through the various obstacles the Forest presents. Although the game does offer an option to instead kill the inhabitants of the Forest, you can find yourself playing for awhile before ever finding how, and as I didn't pursue that end, I can't say how/if it changes all that much about the Forest. Unfortunately there are some shortcomings to the game, such as the control scheme feeling rather awkward, even at higher sensitivity settings, but this can be remedied by using Steam's controller configuration tools to play the game using a controller, which I would recommend. Besides that, the characters you're helping don't have much of any characterization to them, so there's not much motivation to help any one of them over another, nor to harm them, which simply undermines the help/harm choice presented. They each have a description, and some status text that gives a little more sense of how they are, and that's it as far as I could tell. Despite that, given the game's simplicity it's never too difficult to help folks out, so even lacking much character, it's easy enough to explore and help enough of them out enough times to restore the Forest's Heart and make your way to confront the Witch. If you're the helpful sort, you'll find the game to have a rather sweet ending, but if not...Well, as I already said, I didn't pursue that, so I can't say. Altogether the game does a pretty good job of emulating the "Strand-type" on a simpler level, even if it falls a little short in some respects. So, if you're after a lofi supernatural "Strand-type", well, this is it, and it's an alright little game. I would also note that while the criticisms of this being a simple fetch quest game are generally accurate, it's important to note that that  essentially what Death Stranding was as well if one wants to put it in simplest terms, so I have fewer qualms with that than the lacking characterization. Also as I note, you can breeze through that side of the game simply by helping as exploring, which I found reduced the fetch feel, as I typically was dragging or hauling relevant items about anyway, or they were very nearby.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: Very short, unique experience. Not procedural.My first playthrough, I got the good ending and helped all creatures at least 5 times (for the achievements) in about 90 minutes. It was an enjoyable experience, but felt over too quick. I also ran into an issue where the game wanted me to bring an object to the witch, but turned off the fast travel system. I had no idea where the witch was and suddenly unlocking new areas of the map was 10x as difficult, which was very annoying. Hopefully they'll change that so fast travel is only disabled while carrying the heart.My second playthrough, to get the achievement for killing the witch took about 10 minutes. I had assumed this map would be generated proceduraly, but it is not. Everything is in the same location, making subsequent playthrough negligible in difficulty, because you know where all the hazards, waypoints, and items are found.I still recommend the game as I enjoyed what little time I had with it. But if I'd known what I know now, I probably would have waited for a sale to pick this game up. If the developer adds random maps in the future, it could greatly improve replayability. Right now, the only long-term use of Witch Strandings would be speedrunning the single map.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing and unique experience. Way you explore the forest and slowly put together stories of it's dwellers as you meet them build really disturbing and exciting adventure. Cannot forget about music which beautifully wrap whole ambience of the game together. My life felt full when boffee machine noticed my presence ☕🧈

_childDocuments_.review: For what the game is I did enjoy myself. This pixelated forest oozes character and atmosphere, and the mouse-only gameplay *is* engaging. But I was, apparently, confused by what the general understanding of a strand-type game is. I thought strand games included a sort of indirect cooperation with other players, through things appearing in your world like items or messages or already-built paths. Other people out there indirectly communicating to you with little signs and indications that they were there, and you're not alone. I read an article about what the creators of this game consider a strand-type game, Nurturing, Transportation, and Physicality. Witch Strandings definitely delivers on this front, but it's missing that interaction with a larger world. "A digital forest that extends beyond the boundaries of your screen"? I'm not sure I see it.I know this review sounds negative, but this game *is* very good. I think it's an interesting concept executed very well, and it's very well put together. It'd be worth your time and engagement with the unique systems at play here.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet, simple game.  Haunting. The game play it's self is simple, find lost souls and give them what they need to heal. But it's almost scary in that i find myself worried I'm going to kill myself by accidentally wandering into a death tile. All my deaths were accidents in this game. I think that's interesting. It really pays to take your time, however, take too long and the day may rollover and the soul will move and want something different than what you crossed the map to bring. I got actually scared and and nervous the deeper I went into the forest, hoping I was going the right way. Pros: great game to play while watching a movie or tv show you've seen before or while talking to a friend. You need to pay attention, but the game play is calm enough you can take your eyes away. Rewarding. You spend most of the game only being able to drag an object, once you access the controls to have an inventory, its so freeing. There was this definite power jump that made all the work feel worth it. Cons: It got tiring to play with a trackpad on my laptop. The game is definitely set up for a mouse. I had to crank my sensitivity up to lower the stress on my hand, but I ended up hitting water and shooting directly into a death tile, so there is a balance to be made for trackpad users. I really wish there was a map. I know that the point probably was to be lost and confused just like your character and then you slowly learned where to go and where stuff is, but a map could have helped me a lot. I would absolutely play it again.

It is a really unique and quirky game that makes you really want to care for the creatures and find where the witch is hidden, my boyfriend said he would kill the creatures so looks like I might be single LOL Would really recommend to anyone who has been thinking about playing! Mothmans pad is banging.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughtful game that knows exactly what it wants out of a player. Get lost traversing a scarred forest and build a pathway back to the heart of the woods. Help the lost souls trapped with you in this dark landscape and come to terms with your role as steward. Play as a meditation on connection and community not as a list of goals to be finished.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, interesting gameplay. If you like thinking about games as much if not more, than the play itself then try this. It's look is great, really evokes getting lost in your imagination, like a book rather than an illustration.This game could be good for speedrunning, testing your actual manual dexterity rather than button spam. That said, it is good to think about how you use your mouse when you play this game, some have complained about strain, but the game does not force that as there are no time constraints.Worried that I would find the graphics taking time to get into (ala DorfFort/Roguelikes with very basic tilesets). Instead it is what I hope'd it would be.  Getting the hang of movement made me tear up at the beauty of the game design.  The game is concise, getting it`s point across and then being over. quibbles:
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you play a forest spirit, healing the wilderness that has been cursed by the witch. You create paths, carry supplies to creatures, and rebuild buildings that then function as fast travel points. However, and this has been brought up by a few other reviews, the controls for this game are awful, especially if, like me, you suffer from any kind of joint issues. I have arthritis and half an hour of this game was excruciating. You move around the map by moving your mouse cursor, and the sensitivity is incredibly low. To move at all requires a lot of mouse movement and repositioning, even when you adjust the mouse sensitivity to maximum in the game settings. Additionally, moving objects around requires clicking and holding the mouse button. Sometimes you are carrying items across the map for a good distance, requiring you keep the mouse button pressed while traversing the map for minutes at a time. I like the concepts of the game, and think it could be an enjoyable and chill experience if the mouse sensitivity could be increased further, and if objects could be picked up and dropped with a single click rather than requiring the mouse button to be held down the entire time. Until then I can't play this game, let alone recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept of a strand game, where you build connections that grow in power the more they're traveled.  However, this game is more like a fetch quest where half of the fetching is moving stuff that allows you to move from one spot to another.  The aesthetics are ok, but the payoffs are unsatisfying.  This is an interesting foray into the concept of strand games, but not one that will stand up to scrutiny - or to any player who spends more than an hour with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it. I probably wouldn't pick it up for $15, and just know that it's not an action game. There are some very interesting, moving concepts touched on, but not explored. The premise of the game, centered on rebirth and redemption, is very powerful to me, but may not be for others. Few hours of relaxation and thought-provoking dialogue. Probably not worth $15, but probably is worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially wrote a negative review, but something nagged on me. There was something there. Something interesting, and I knew 20 minutes wasn't enough time. I've finished 1 run, and am eager to do more. The mouse controls are tough to get used to, but they did help a certain area in the ending feel more tense and climactic. The art, sound design, and setting itself is wonderful. If you liked the "help static NPCs by bringing them stuff they need, altering the world so the trips back and forth are more efficient/easier" side of Death Stranding, this might catch your interest.
_childDocuments_.name: Witch Strandings

_childDocuments_.review: too long don't care to read: it's less game and more experience and I recommend it on the basis that you get it on a sale or in a bundle.Witch Stranding is full of atmosphere, from visuals to sound. A lot of the game is conveyed purely from being in the world. There is very little text, but it's well written and mostly between the lines. It adds to the mystique of it all, but doesn't make anything clearer. Most of the game is simply felt.Especially through your movements. You only have your mousecursor, and you will move it around a lot. Quite strenuous on longer play sessions tbh. It is very tactile and a lot of the gameplay, as well as the feeling of your surroundings, is conveyed through your your movements. To me that's the biggest plus of Witch Stranding.Unfortunately the game doesn't really give much feedback on what you're doing. Are you performing well? Are you on the right way? What should you do next? ... I couldn't figure it out.I played the game for 3 hours, unlocked "the heart", couldn't find the witch and stopped playing at some point.I started a new game (which deletes the previous save), played for another hour. I performed better by my own metric (ie less deaths, faster progress towards "the heart", more requests fullfilled), but I do not feel, like I am getting it now. Actually it feels like it makes no difference at all. Helping the animals and reconstructing the structures, clearing hexes and brambles ...I am pretty sure the game doesn't care about anything of it. There is a clock tracking time, and when you die, time is sped up. A new day makes the animals move a few tiles, creates new requests and replenishes some items. But it doesn't seem to make any difference to the gameworld, or the witch ...or me. It's weird. Despite being confused and not able to finish the game I am quite fond of the experience. My only gripe is, that it's way too expensive. The price generates an expectation that Witch Stranding can't fullfill.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is pretty cool. the mechanics felt a bit weird at first given the fact that you don't use WASD to move but rather your mouse. but after around 15-20 minutes i got used to it. aside from that, the game itself plays to your own will because no quests are given and no directions to find certain areas are shown, its purely driven by your own exploration. this means that you have to do a lot of digging around to find pathways and avoid dying to hexes, rushing water, quicksand, or thorns. this game was a short but very enjoyable experience and i do recommend you buy this cause i imagine you'll like it too.

name: Kaiju Wars
detailed_description: Kaiju are approaching the city! Scramble the jets and deploy the tanks in this 2D turn-based strategy game. Command the army We need more time! - Play as the mayor of Floatio city, tasked with holding off the overwhelming strength of a kaiju attack. Park tanks and jets in the monster's path to slow it down (don't worry, we have a good insurance policy). Construct buildings! - Build sacrificial army bases and airfields to distract the kaiju and line the city streets with fodder. Deploy experimental weapons! - Conventional weapons aren't enough; deploy experimental weapons such as freeze rays and transforming mechas to keep the kaiju at bay. Evacuate! - Our chief scientist is working on an anti-monster serum, but it's not ready yet! Be prepared to evacuate the laboratory using transport trucks, boats, or planes when the kaiju get too close. Fight the KAIJU! Five unique kaiju - Each specializing in different types of destruction. They mutate! - Tremble in fear as each kaiju grows stronger and gains devastating abilities through mid-level mutations. Unstoppable! - Kaiju can't be killed, but can only be slowed down and forced to fall back... for now. Pepper them with ammunition, if you can.. Predictable! - They move towards the nearest building, and those scientists have mathed the exact odds as to where they might go next. Use this info wisely! Campaign Mode! Uncover the mystery - Strange things are happening: frequent volcanic eruptions, tsunamis and earthquakes. Find out why over the course of a 15+ hour story-based campaign. Embark on a Campaign - Play missions from all over the world as you progress through the globe-trotting fight against kaiju. Test your wits in tactical puzzles, command dozens of units in large-scale scenarios, and fend off repeated attacks while developing your city economically in city defense missions. Upgrade your ACES - Veteran ACE units accompany you throughout your campaign. Spend medals to upgrade and customize your top fighters. Customize your Project Deck - Unlock powerful Project cards, customize your deck, and bring your best strategy to compete on the online leaderboard! Twitch Integration, Custom Maps, and More! Twitch Integration - Twitch chat are the citizens! Twitch viewers can type commands into chat to have comments appear during certain in-game events Local Versus Mode - Two players duke it out at the same computer (or online via Steam RemotePlay), with one playing as the KAIJU, the other as the HUMANS Create your own battles - Create your own city or scenario - Simple and easy to use, scenarios can be crafted in minutes using the drag and drop map editor Share your creations online - Share your maps online using Steam Workshop integration Weekly Challenges - Try our challenges and play for top spot on the weekly leaderboards You thought being mayor of the world's greatest city was all about zoning bylaws. Then the kaiju came. Good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's got enough cheese in it to make fondue for the entire population of Paris. And yet, underneath all that carefully aged gorgonzola there is a surprisingly intricate game design; full of slowly unfolding elements, pleasant yet firm difficulty curve, enough variety for a quite long campaign, and even some meta progression. And I'm not even a fan of kaiju.That said, something is clearly wrong with the game. Roughly 80% of players start it, while only 20% beat the first act, 9% the second, and finally only 2.7% beat the final mission. As a member of this elusive 2.7%, I'm not sure what the problem is. The difficulty? I found it okay. The long and slow animations? You can make them faster or turn them off. The lack of variety? I don't think so. Let's take a closer look, and maybe we can figure it out together. Worst case, you'll see if this is something you would like to play. Or early 90s? Japanese 80s/90s are most visible (audible?) in the music. It's fantastic, and very thematically fitting. A mixutre of synth, chiptune and epic chorus. Ridiculous? Yes. Glorious? Oh yes. Each kaiju has their own theme song, and it always plays when they're on the battlefield. You'd think that those songs would get old really fast, but somehow, that didn't happen for me.There's more of 80s wackiness than just music. Your Contra protagonist-looking army man is called "Major Danger",  you have a transforming Guncross Robot (piloted by SHINJI IKARI, get in the mecha), there's a Kaputnik rocket, and the cities have ridiculous names such as Bomb Bay City or Uberlin. The fact that the Uberlin's storyline involves a failed opening of an airport is just *chef's kiss*. Not sure if that was intentional, but if it was, wow.Oh yes, there's a plot. It's also very wacky and 80s, but it's also... good? It even manages to be epic sometimes. And it has some interesting twists later on. But enough about that, let's talk about the kaiju, and how to stop them.No, not even with a giant robot. You can slow them down, and make them temporarily retreat, but they will always return. So how do you win? With science, a passive resource generated every turn. The goal of every mission is to gain enough science to pacify the kaiju, which makes them leave you alone for the mission. You also gain some science for "defeating" the kaiju - reducing it's HP to 0, which makes it disappear for 2-3 turns, after which it just emerges from its starting point again.In other words, your job is to protect the science (and money) generating buildings first and foremost. And the higher the kaiju's current HP, the faster it moves - so yes, hitting it hard is important, but actually taking them down requires a lot of coordinated effort. It took me a while to figure out how to play, but once it clicked, it did so for good - I managed to beat most missions on my first try, almost always with the medal for finishing within alloted time, too. I'm a veteran of both Advance Wars games, so perhaps that's why? But generally, it was about knowing when to strike and when to defend, all while maximising science production. That's what wins the game, after all.I mean, fighting the same 4 monsters over and over might seem like Einstein's definition of insanity. Luckily, the kaiju mutate; every incarnation has different skills "equipped" (from their own unique selection), as well as different starting HP. You're used to Ladilan having 18 HP and having a skill that kills one unit not in his way... but suddenly, he has only 12 HP but now fires a GIANT LAZOR that destroys *everything* in a two-tile line? Eurui leaves flames behind her, and is easy to bring down to the ground after a few hits... but suddenly, she has some 25 HP, which gives her a speed of 8? And she turns into an exploding egg instead of dying? And oh god, why Smo-Bong suddenly gains armour in the forest...(genders assumed and names mine - you can name the kaiju)So no, it doesn't get boring. If anything, it gets exciting; when you see a kaiju coming, the first thing you think of is "what sort of skillset does it have THIS time?". Then there are special "core defense" missions, in which the kaiju retreats after a set amount of turns... but then regenerates like crazy, gains a new ability, and sometimes even passes the baton to another monster, which will have the same HP and number of abilities... so you better hurry with that science, as you won't last very long.There's a lot more to the game. There's crisis management, using buildings as bait, project deckbuilding, scientist evacuation, experimental weapons, tactics and technologies, upgrading your hero units... like I said before, this is a huge game; as big as any of the AAA strategy titles of eld. It took me 31 hours to beat it, and I played most missions only once. I did all the optional missions and sometimes replayed older missions for more medals... but I also kept all the kaiju animations on, they're just too cool. That adds up over time.In conclusion - I think the game's good, but I recognise that people might see it as too hard. It requires some shifts in how you think about stuff, and planning well ahead. I also saw a pretty annoying bug when building a project deck, there's a workaround for it in the forums though. I recommend the game if you like tactical games and wacky stuff. Yes, even if you're not a fan of kaiju. Enjoy!
