_childDocuments_.review: Erica presents itself as a thoroughly captivating story and straight up like a linearly told film, but sometimes struggles a bit with itself as a game. You are confronted directly and without detours with the story, which is quite dramatic...... Erica, who is an orphan, one day receives a package whose contents are a bloody severed piece which in turn holds an amulet with a Greek symbol. And it is precisely this symbol that has haunted Erica since childhood in her nightmares in which she sees her dying father, who had this exact symbol carved into his chest. Erica relives this nightmare over and over again and before she can see the murderer's face, she wakes up...She seeks advice and help from the police and, because of the package, also seeks refuge in the Delphi House, a psychiatric hospital that was co-founded by her father and where he met Erica's mother, who unfortunately died very early under unclear circumstances.And this is exactly where Erica goes in search of traces of her past in order to solve the mystery of the mysterious sign and the murders...The “game” mainly consists of cutscenes paired with options/decisions that appear in the ongoing scenes and resolve after a short period of time if you do nothing. However, this often only results in silence and since the scenes continue to run without input, the whole thing seems quite fluid and does not disrupt the immersion.The dialogue doesn't seem to have a long-term effect, but it allows you to play the character Erica the way you want and, depending on your decision, that can be pretty mean. Unfortunately, the replay value suffers somewhat from all the choices and, above all, many of them are without consequence, because there are really only a few nodes in the game where really different paths arise.You play with the mouse or a touchpad, although the latter can be a bit cumbersome for some actions due to its size. A small light effect is navigated like a cursor, which becomes a small bright dot when you hover over it or move over an Interactive Object. This cursor system is very suitable for selecting or examining. But when it comes to turning keys or other things, opening drawers or pulling a sheet out of an envelope, things can get trickier and you occasionally wonder about the reason for your existence, which is not really tragic, but sometimes it is something annoying is repetitive.As a film, Erica actually does quite well. Erica makes you curious about the secrets surrounding the parents and the Delphi House, even if the psychiatric hospital isn't necessarily the most original setting. But this proves to be a successful setting for a psychological thriller. In addition, three other patients with whom Erica can befriend all have their own and exclusive paths, which offers great added value, especially in another playthrough and in contrast to a pure film.The interesting and complex story does not reveal all of its secrets in a single playthrough and in order to find out every detail about the events, you have to play it several times.Basically it's a good idea, but it's also one of its biggest weaknesses.It all feels incomplete, especially because the end comes relatively abruptly and doesn't conclude with either the decisions made or the story arc chosen as a whole. Sometimes it feels like you have a bulletin board in your hand that you haven't worked through to the end. Unfortunately, the game does not offer the option to select chapters you have seen again in order to make a different decision.The game does not offer any saving option or additional save status. Flavorworks justifies this by saying that the decision you make as a player should be lived through to the end. In principle, this is an understandable decision because otherwise the game would have turned into an absolute saving and loading marathon, but on the other hand it has the disadvantage that you have to start from the beginning every time you play through it. Even if the game doesn't last two hours, with (I think there are four) four main endings and easily five to six runs for all achievements, then at some point it's just torture.I think it's a bit of a shame that there's a strange silence and rigidity, especially in the central film scenes, and you might think that all the actors and their performances were recorded individually and somewhere and that the editing didn't manage to create a natural conversation out of these scenes. Added to this is the brevity of the scenes, which do not allow relationships or suspicions to be developed as believably as they could have.Unfortunately, the game also lacks transitions, especially when it comes to changing locations. It is briefly stated why the characters will be in a different location, but sometimes this information is simply lost in whispers and Flavorworks largely avoids panning shots, exterior shots or other cinematic aids to guide the player to the next location.Austin Wintroy's soundtrack, which could mean something to many about Journey, is an extremely coherent one. It's a real shame that this hardly comes into play because it's far too quiet and simply disappears in the background.Erica isn't a bad film or game, but unfortunately it's not quite as good as hoped either. The mood that is created here is rather superficial and emotional connections are not possible because the characters interact with each other too rarely. While it's interesting to see how decisions can influence the course of the plot and it's entertaining to map out the actions, the film and the game are too strictly separated. Which can ultimately make replaying the entire movie/game even tiring.Erica is far from a perfect film-game experience, which becomes most obvious when scenes seem to be cut apart too hard and often emotions and the conversational tone of the following scene do not match the selection made beforehand, which probably has to do with the fact that the Shooting time is given as just 45 days. Hence the many rigid camera perspectives.Despite the criticism, Erica is an exciting game and if you look at it from a film perspective, the picture and sound quality are almost cinematic. The plot is quite captivating and the acting is sometimes even terrifically good. From a game perspective, you get around two hours of horror per round, which can easily be increased to 20 hours.But if you're looking for a classic adventure or even action, you'll be disappointed here because Erica is neither and doesn't want to, can't and doesn't have to be either.✔ good actors✔ good soundtrack✔ exciting story✔ successful atmosphere✔ Additional information by playing through it several times✔ good transition between scenes and selection screens✘ some interactions are repetitive and pointless✘ few really important decisions✘ Single playthrough leaves questions unanswered and seems unfinished✘ short, rigid explanatory scenes instead of conversationsReview Date: December 14, 2023

_childDocuments_.review: - Its price, although its duration is really short: about one hour and forty minutes: like a film.- The actors act really well, and the accompanying music is very good.- The dubbing is 10 out of 10.- It is very replayable, with decisions that mark totally different paths depending on what we choose.- Unlike other games in the genre, we have playable elements where we can interact: open a lighter, light the flame, turn a doorknob... not much, but it is more entertaining than just choosing answers from conversations.- The game has five different endings.- Although it has five different endings, the main plot is essentially left to the player's interpretation.- The story is not surprising, but it is well handled.- Being an interactive movie it is not a game for all audiences.I loved Erica. It's a videogame that some time ago was released exclusively on PStore, and that I always wanted to buy: when I saw it published on Steam I couldn't help but do it. As an interactive adventure the game overflows with quality: resolution and quality of the film, actors' performances, dubbing in different languages, music...- 9/10.Being a fan of the genre it's a must, especially considering its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is an FMV adventure game where the player can influence the story by making dialogue choices and investigating some objects.The story has a good start. When the player character Erica Mason was a child, her dad was murdered and the killer was never caught. Now the police are investigating a similar new murder. As I learned more about events there was an interesting sense of mystery, and I found myself wondering who to trust.My main problem with the game is that its quite short. My 3.4 hours playing time represents two full playthroughs. I think after a certain point the story kind of rushes to the end. Your choices can take you to different locations in the middle of the story, and can lead to multiple endings. Ultimately I got the same ending both times, although my choices did give it a slightly different context.The acting is quite good, I’ve seen better but I’ve also seen worse. I didn’t notice any bugs or crashes.If you value story I think Erica is worth playing, but I would recommend waiting for a sale.

I always find my self enjoying a sequence then all of a sudden camera freezes because it wants me to do something. This not only makes the player feel awkward but also breaks the buildup, it constantly keeps reminding you it's a game, even when it is not needed to. A playthrough on YouTube feels much impactful & intense then actually playing erica. It is a decent thriller underneath everything mentioned. 65/100

_childDocuments_.review: It's amazing to see how far FMV have come since the old days and it's downright appalling to see how bad the controls are in this game. The visuals, the acting and the soundtrack are absolutely great (kudos to the actors and the composer Austin Wintory) but the controls are absolutely terrible and get in the way of the enjoyment of the game. I got stuck right before the end of my run because the game wouldn't let me click and drag to proceed so after trying for a few minutes and reloading the game twice I ended up watching the two last minutes on Youtube (that's as anticlimactic as it gets). Having players click and drag the mouse on the PC doesn't feel responsive at all in this game and it must be downright impossible for players with any sort of disability since at times you need to click and hold and drag the mouse further away in order to move forward with the story (full disclosure I'm not disabled but I've hurt my hand recently and I didn't expect the game to put me through that much dragging the mouse around).I can understand the time limited events being included for immersion but there is absolutely no reason why they couldn't make it easier to play the game. Last but not least, the game comes with audio files in eight different languages which is great (English, Arabic, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish) but chances are you will be playing in only one language so that's 11GB of useless data that you downloaded for nothing (definitely not ecofriendly) that will clutter your drive (the game takes 37 GB) so if you decide to give this game a try I would advise to go to:\Steam\steamapps\common\Erica\data\soundbanksand delete the folders for the languages you won't be using since that will save you about 11GB. I would entreat devs to consider some sort of accessibility options or controller support for the PC, especially considering this is not a genre that should require that much effort or dexterity on the player's part.

_childDocuments_.review: if you've ever wanted to embark on an adventure with a dose of mystery, which without much fanfare and publicity manages to draw you into its world, then... ...then Erica is what you're looking for.Erica is FMV adventure created with a lot of attention and commitment to things that contribute to the atmosphere and the overall experience of maladaptation and going through nightmares. You find yourself floating through life alone in an apartment as the world passes you by.At the beginning the father’s death is that affects you the most, as nightmares bring back visions of his last moments as Erica holds him close with the killer still in the room. You attempt to suppress these memories, until they’re dragged back into the present day when new clues about his murder open the case back up.You control the actions of Erica, played by real-life actor Holly Earl... Holly Earl does a great job of creating a character you quickly feel for as she simply wants to learn the story behind her dad, while remaining timid when needed. Believable and interesting, Erica herself is the star of this game.Holly Earl regularly looks like she's uncomfortable, exactly how you feel as a viewer in most of the situations. In fact, this game does some things not seen in FMV games before. You’ll have to wipe away the condensation on your bathroom mirror, scribble out a signature in order to access flashback scenes. You never know what the game will ask of you next.Perpetual disorientation is the central feeling of Erica, and it's what keeps you searching for the truth no matter how many  obstacles stand in your way. The plot is ever-changing and chaotic; you're attempting to solve a crime by talking to a lot of strange people in an unfamiliar, odd place while having a lot of flashbacks of your messed-up childhood.Erica is an intriguing experience that those looking for something a little outside of the video game norm will surely appreciate. Its cryptic tone is carried through the audio, visuals, and writing... its not allowing you to relax. Using a combination of cinematography and FMV-specific game mechanics, Erica never fails to hook you into its haunting world.

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is a beautifully designed and well performed movie choice style video game. The cast, story, and production was all executed superbly, leaving my only complaint being that I would like to enjoy more of it. This is more of a compliment that a complete game has that reaction, but here we are. The story has a lot of twists and turns, despite being about as long as a motion picture film (approximately 130 minutes). The writing was well done, giving the cast a good structured story to work with. The acting was brilliant, and definitely performed a very believable and enrapturing experience. Upon reaching the conclusion, I am left with many questions. I will not go into spoilers, but I am hoping for more to come, and to include some elaboration on the events that transpired up to this point. I am also going to enjoy taking all of the other options available in follow plays through, and seeing if that clears up any of those questions. I will be taking every single option that I can.The music is beautiful, and fits the mood of the game. I can see this being the kind of soundtrack that you would listen to to relax or have a calming ambiance. The controls and notifications for making choices are subtle and well done. I found myself making some of the choices before the prompts as the game went on, partially because of the suspense, and also because the style became easy to learn and navigate. The first few minutes of choices was much like a tutorial in how to select your paths and interaction, which was nicely done. I also found the interaction to play well into adding suspense and drama, as well as making the choices feel more important. I look forward to trying each and every selection, before I consider myself to have completed the game. In short, Erica is a beautifully made game with a compelling and dramatic story. The acting is superb, with a lovely soundtrack. I recommend this game for those that are looking for a cinematic choose your own adventure with an excellent story and performance. I hope to find more games like these, and will be adding Flavourworks to my list of developers to follow. Thank you for making such a gorgeous movie/game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does everything wrong in an FMV. The plot is a mess, and has plot holes so big I could drive a buick through them. I feel like the devs used the excuse it is a thriller for let's do random stuff and call it horror. Sadly that doesn't work. I grew up on the old 80s/90s adventure games and those made more sense than this did. To top it off, the game also has strange fake interactivity. Listen devs, no one wants to move a mouse to realistically open a door to make it interactive. Take a lesson from the old FMV games of the 90s and make it interactive like say Gabriel Knight 2 instead. Now that would be good interactivity. And whomever decided to give a time limit and also had the choices start to fade...no. Please no. I do not see well out of one eye and can't even turn my head fast enough to read all the choices with that time limit. I hate to think how someone totally blind in one eye would fair, but my guess is they would find this game impossible to play. Please respect our time and give us enough time to read the choices instead of adding fake tension with artificial time limits that in the end make vision impaired people unable to play this game well due to being unable to even read the choices in time.

_childDocuments_.review: 本遊戲由Keylol 鑒賞家提供，可點擊Two things I need to rant before the review.•	There is no native controller support, even it was originally on console.•	The Steam trailer mainly shows how interactive a movie game can be, but tells you basically nothing about the story premise. You will have to look for the PlayStation 4 trailer if you want to know.Erica is a traumatic young woman whose mother passed away and her father was murdered brutally in front of her when she was little, hence her trauma. After that, she was living peacefully until one day she received a broken human hand holding a medallion engraved with a mysterious symbol. By visiting the Delphi House, a mental treatment facility (the story does not specify) established by her father, she learned about what is behind everything that happens to her. That is the story premise you should know, which includes key story elements.As a movie, Erica is a good-quality mystery and thriller for what it is, in the sense that the developer poured some love so it has everything (e.g. good script, actors, editing) it needs to be decent, yet it never goes beyond its plot. It is very shallow, does almost zero characterizing, and reveals no profound meaning whatsoever. Just a typical popcorn movie that delivers what it aims for. If you are looking for more, you are going to be disappointed.As a game, Erica is very simple mechanically, or say games in this genre all are, only consisting of three elements, interacting, making choices, and storytelling. I will more focus on the flaws, as its gameplay is not very polished.Interaction is probably the worst part of all if being nitpicking. It works, it is not insufferable, it is just not good.•	Very frequently, the game stops and asks you to interact with stuff. Open a door, ignite the lighter, pull out a piece of paper, insert a key, etc., all those trivial stuff. I don’t hate interaction, but what is the point of doing all these? Are they important to the story? Will they leave some profound impression? No, they are meaningless and just exist for the sake of being “interactive”. Worse still, the game doesn’t give you a two-minute break before another interaction. All I want is to immerse myself into the story, not constantly getting interrupted by these stupid things.•	The game uses a glowing path to indicate you can interact with objects, however, it tells little about which directions you should move your cursor. Again, it is not insufferable but is a bad design choice that can be mildly infuriating.•	The interactive zone is not very precise, you might experience your clicks being delayed or not registered. It happens to some of the choice-making scenes as well. In the final scene where you decide to keep or throw away the lighter, I clicked keep it, but the game decided for me to throw it away. Yeah, it happened. Making unintended choices is the worst outcome of this problem.Erica has quite abundant different choices. In some scenes, you can pick up to six different choices. This game also have six endings depending on the choices you made, though I only got one as I am satisfied with it and the game is not good enough to motivate me to do a second playthrough (you see everything you need to know in one playthrough). Additionally, the game doesn’t have manual save, you have to sit through the entire game for alternative choices (no skipping), which I don’t want. Therefore, I won’t make a fool of myself trying to analyze meaningful choice variation and stuff. I will focus on the execution side of things.•	Choices in this game are mostly presented as a short sentence or a single word. It is probably for aesthetic to not make the screen too crowded, but I don’t think it does very well when it comes to conciseness, as sometimes the wording is quite confusing, not properly convey what actions the words represent (I understand the words of course), which only happened with choices in a single word. Also, in certain parts of the game, it has a tendency to use some less common words (just my perception, these words look very British), which might create an extra barrier for understanding.•	You only have limited time to make choices. They literally will fade away as time goes by. It is artistic, yet it makes reading harder as the words getting more transparent. In where I was proposed with five or six choices, after I finished reading and thinking (just a few seconds), the choices have already faded away to the point I couldn’t recognize. You can still see them if look harder, however, you have no time.•	Speaking of time, timer for most choices is very tight. Some are clearly on purpose to show Erica is overwhelmed, which is okay, while others, I don’t know, let’s say if I am the developer, I will more value giving adequate time to players making desired choices, than using the timer to show emotion, urgency, or whatever they were intended to do.As I said, Erica is equivalent to a popcorn movie. The story is pretty straightforward. Some metaphors in the story seem to symbolize something, they actually don’t because the limited length never gives it a chance to explore anything deeper. Its storytelling and cinematography are also as conventional as average TV episodes. No special narrative method, camera language, or anything you need to digest. A few scenes might be a little confusing with the flashback, but you don’t need to think too deep as they reveal nothing more than they show you. All in all, it is what it is, a popcorn movie, but it is a quality one. It is believable, entertaining, with good acting and presentation and without plot holes and errors. It did not take itself too seriously trying to be something beyond what it is, and I really appreciate that.I will say though, if it did more characterizing, the story would be more memorable and not that shallow. Also, I felt one stage in the plot development is missing. Erica was just conveniently told the truth and conveniently decided to fight back. I didn’t study enough writing theory to justify it, my feeling tells me it should have an innermost struggle stage before she fights back, so that the plot is more convincing and her character more fleshed out.This game is eye candy. It tends to use wide aperture and shallow depth of field to bokken the background and highlight the close shot, in that way the characters and objects look extra sharp and exquisite, and abundant color palettes give the game a vivid and colorful visual. Most scenes are shot in low-light environment to create a mysterious and suspenseful vibe, but a big part of Delphi House is shot with high brightness. I know it has story purposes, but it looks odd and inconsistent as a whole.As for sound design, people say it is great, I don’t find it particularly impressive nor does anything wrong. I will just skip it.Performance-wise, people mention problems like crashing, freezing etc., I didn’t encounter any, fortunately, although I did notice sudden frame drop every time the game gets into interaction scenes. Furthermore, it is a two-hour game (I finished in 103 minutes), but the file size is 37GB. For whatever reason behind, the developer really should optimize the file size.As a movie, Erica is a 6 in my criteria, a typical rating for movies that are not very impressive but have some aspects I like. In the case of Erica, I find the story kind of blank and forgettable, however, I like what they did with the aesthetic. As a game, Erica has some rough edges. I hope the developer can fix some of these (like adding controller support). Again, you need to keep the positioning of Erica in mind and don’t compare it with some movie masterpieces. It provides enough entertainment value for what it is and for the price (price for a movie ticket).

_childDocuments_.review: In case you are looking for a good FMV game and considering giving Erica a shot, don't. Just don't. Go get Late Shift, you'll have so much more fun. FMV games are usually hit or miss, but sometimes a pleasant scenery and overall tolerable narrative can save an idiotic story, and the other way around: a good, immersive story can carry it all, cancelling out all the technical inconveniences such as uncomfortable interface or weird point-and-click events. In this game, neither happens, because both the story and the gameplay are atrocious. Prepare yourself for the unbearable amount of point-and-click anywhere&everywhere. Ignite a lighter, twist a door handle, open a suitcase (all three of the clasps, one by one), and as soon as you are done, you'll need to pull a paper out of an envelope, cut a cake, pick up a phone, draw a picture... And then some. Don't get me wrong, I don't mind occasional player participation, but when you literally cannot blink without a yet another pointless action, it breaks the immersion severely.By the way, if you happen to decide that you are tired of this and want to exit the game, you'll have to force close it through the task manager, otherwise it'll just freeze on you. Ah, and when you re-launch it, prepare for the ringing phone soundbite from the previous scene to carry over into the next one and ring relentlessly until the scene is over and your brain has deteriorated. Don't even get me started on the plot, where we have a (presumably) mentally healthy main character spend her days among three psycho girls with no supervision whatsoever. Said psycho girls are also allowed to roam around whenever and wherever they desire, visit each other's rooms and pretend to be staff in front of other visitors. I won't get into it too much, since I've only played it through once, but the main storyline also leaves a lot of questions unanswered, and seems far-fetched, if not just plain weird and scarcely believable. Not to mention it was crammed into a time cap of about two hours, which didn't help at all.I won't recommend it, at least not as your first FMV. Actually, I feel sorry for those who'd bought it back when it came out as a PS4 exclusive. I got it on sale and honestly, if it had happened any other way, that would have been the fastest refund I've ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Find the truth, no matter the cost. Story:You play as Erica. She's a young woman that has been plagued with vivid nightmares of her fathers murder she witnessed when she was a child. Years later when she's now a grown woman, she finds a mysterious package which includes a severed hand. After authorities get involved she's sent to Delphi house, a mental institution her father helped create and here she finds that the truth about her fathers murder and the other things that plagued her life.Erica has a very intriguing story, but certain moments of the game feel incredibly lackluster. First of all I have to say that this is a choice driven game, so you can witness different scenes depending on your choices. Some of the writing choices felt really bizarre, especially one of the possible endings which felt incredibly anti-climatic. However there is multiple endings to see, so the different paths could lead to more interesting sequences, but after witnessing my first route I was questioning if I should do a different path.Graphics:FMV is a dying art, but now with the indie market and digital allowing more developers to go this route, it's seeing a resurgence. Visually Erica looks incredibly professional and honestly if the developers wanted to, they could easily take one path of the game and make it into a very competent movie. There's tons of big sets, decent special effects, so they definitely didn't make it as cheesy as some of the other games in the genre. Audio:Erica also has a pretty good audio design. The soundtrack is very good and really makes certain scenes feel more intense or grand. It's not anything overly impressive, but it's genuinely impressive at times. One thing that does stick out at times is  the dialogue audio quality.At times when characters speak the audio feels too quiet and sometimes the audio just doesn't feel natural, like there was some poor mixing done on the ADR, but mostly it's nothing too horrible that it would make the experience poor in any way. The acting itself is pretty decent for the most part, some of the side characters feel a bit over the top, but other than that, it's good.Gameplay: Erica is basically an interactive movie, with very minor gameplay elements involved. You're basically watching a movie unfold in front of you and once in a while you will select a choice which will put you down a different pathway, so something like a telltale game, but in live action.Originally this game was a PS4 exclusive and it used it's trackpad for gameplay sequences where you drag items across the screen, like tearing open a letter. These sequences end up as the only other gameplay you get when playing the game and while something of a cool gimmick on the PS4 is just annoying on the PC version. There's a few cool puzzles, but usually it's just a little pace breaker where you open something up to advance the story, it's very clear the developers just added this as a way to include some gameplay as it wouldn't be just a movie.Verdict:Erica is decent game, but it does have faults from time to time. To see everything the game has to offer would take quite a bit of time so there's quite a lot of bang for your buck. I wasn't entirely fond of the story, but there are some cool set pieces and I'm always a sucker for FMV, so if you're like me definitely consider giving this a shot. Final Rating:7/10Pros:+ Looks incredibly professional + Story has an interesting premise + Tons of play valueCons:- Story slogs at times- Audio mixing is pretty rough at times- Gameplay breaks get annoying after a while If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: Ericaby FlavourworksGenre: FMV-interactive movieRelease: May 25, 2021-----(TL;DR: this is a pretty cool game that has a great story, great cinematic quality, interesting interactions and system of choices that may motivate one to seek a second or third play through, and you should definitely check it out. The following stunned tone is being brought to you by a thoroughly sensory-overloaded autistic person who had a fairly long day out, but who felt he should get his thoughts out about this game as soon as possible. In retrospect, perhaps this review does not have the most fair tone that I normally give my reviews, but my condition today should be taken into account. Just know that I'm not usually this way when I review.)I just got finished watching a pretty suspenseful and entertaining movie. Erica is an interactive movie, but unfortunately there's not much more to say about it. The story is well written, the acting is really good and the visual effects and set design are excellent, and I can say that I was fairly well entertained. However, that is unfortunately all I can say about it. My feeling about the game was that it was actually a movie, with a few mouse movements and button presses. There is the potential for multiple options leading to multiple endings, and I could tell that, but at this time I do not feel the urge to go after them. Perhaps after I have emotionally cooled down and processed what I have seen and experienced.The best thing I can say about this is is most definitely a call back to older games of this type that also used FMV, so I most definitely respect the developer's efforts to keep the dream alive, as I am a huge fan of all things old school. I think a little more interactivity and feedback to the player, as well as a flowchart showing player choice and where the story can potentially go would be beneficial. The flowchart mechanic could be similar to, for example, the visual novel AI: The Somnium Files or even the full-fledged adventure Detroit: Become Human. Stuff like that.I'm not going to talk about the story because I think it is best experienced yourself. And you should experience it, as it is most definitely high quality in the areas I have mentioned above – but only if this is on sale, as it is for the next couple days. For six dollars it is actually the price of purchasing a streaming movie from a service like Prime Video or something like that. And I feel that's what I got out of this, and until I get the motivation to play this again with different choices, that's how I feel I should look at this.And no, I'm not refunding even though I'm under two hours, because I completed the game once, and I feel like it would be morally wrong for me to refund it. Also, the story was entertaining to me, and I feel like I paid the correct price for a movie. If I have the motivation at a future point to watch the movie again, with different choices, that will happen and it will be good and it will be worth more than the six dollars I paid. That is the potential for me there. So, thank you Flavourworks, for about an hour and a half of solid entertainment. At some point in the future, if I play again, I will have had more entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: "Erica" is a very short (ca. 95 minutes per playthrough) thriller with paranormal elements, implemented as an interactive movie. It features an interesting story, good acting, and some choices that do indeed matter, but suffers from a terrible user interface, bugs, and many choices that are just fake.You play a young woman who has lost both her parents. Her father co-founded a mental hospital, and when it turns out that she may be in danger because people start getting killed, the police take her to that hospital since they have a security detail there already. However, you soon find out that the hospital may not only use questionable practices, but might also be involved in mysteries that reach back to the death of your mother, and beyond.I found the story interesting, it definitely piqued my curiosity and I enjoyed its twists and turns. Several characters are not what they seem, and there are a few shocking revelations to uncover. I also appreciated that some of the choices really do make a difference (e.g. leaving a location early will often let you find information at another location that you would have missed otherwise), and I liked unraveling a mystery that required several playthroughs to fully understand and solve.The writing didn't blow my mind, there aren't any clever lines to enjoy or fascinating insights to find. But it succeeded in conveying required information in an immersive and believable way.As usual for interactive movies, gameplay consists of making choices like where to go, which area to investigate, or what to say in a conversation. There aren't any quick-time events, but many choices are unfortunately on a tight timer that cannot be turned off. This definitely made the game less enjoyable for me.The game showers the player with menial activities that have no impact on anything, but you have to do them to advance the scene. I understand that the developers wanted to involve players more in that way, but there's nothing exciting or immersive in constantly having to drag the mouse across the screen in order to open a door, turn a key, pull a piece of paper out of an envelope, etc. - this is just annoying busywork that turns an otherwise enjoyable game into a chore.On top of that, the game's UI is so terrible that it often isn't immediately clear what the game expects from you. Actions are indicated by a faded spot or cone of light, but sometimes those are too subtle to immediately grasp the player's attention, and sometimes reflections on the screen look like they might indicate a hotspot, but there is none. In many cases, the light indicates the exact point where you need to click or drag, but in others, the game actually wants you to click something elsewhere on the screen, without indicating that in any way. For example, you'll have to move or flip photos in several scenes, which is indicated by lights on those photos - but there's also a scene where the lights on the photo are actually meant to tell you that you're supposed to move the paperclip at its side.Moreover, the game is incredibly unresponsive. If the camera moves across a bag with two latches, then you already know that you'll have to click and drag the mouse to open the latches - but if you do that, nothing happens. You first have to wait until the camera finishes its movement, then you have to wait again until the hotspot-indicating lights appear (there's usually a delay there), and only then the game allows you to do the obvious and operate the latches.In interviews, the developers presented this interface as an innovation that they are proud of. I'm sorry, but I have to fundamentally disagree. Any enhanced immersion that these controls may have been supposed to deliver, is lost when players constantly need to repeat their actions trial-and-error style until they find the spot that the game actually wanted them to click, at the right time when the game is finally ready to accept their input. Additionally, the idea of click-and-drag controls that mimic real-world movements is far from new, Frictional did this with Penumbra no less than 15 years ago (and frankly, they implemented those controls in a much clearer and better way).I found the graphical fidelity of the game pretty disappointing. I'm not sure if it's the cinematography or if the videos just have a low resolution, but the image kept looking blurry on my 43" monitor. On top of that, the camera often focuses so closely on faces that e.g. the foliage in the background turns into a mess of green blobs. This is a pity because the game sports a pretty high variety of very different locations, with some interesting details on the sets, so it would have been nice to be able to actually study them in high fidelity.From an artistic perspective, I really liked the scene transitions into memories - you see the scene that triggers the memory, and then click-and-drag the mouse pointer over it, revealing the memorized scene like rubbing the first one away. This is a rare example where the controls, even though inefficient, have artistic value.The sound work is solid, and the music is excellent - it sets the tone without ever pushing into the foreground. The composer, Austin Wintory, delivers high-quality work as usual.The acting is generally decent, though the script and the direction don't give the actors many opportunities to shine. The entire game is held in a subdued, distanced tone, with slow camera movement and long cuts, and even dramatic events don't feel particularly intense. This mode of presentation made me feel like a distant observer rather than someone actually involved in the action.While most actors do a solid job, the female lead carries the exact same confused-and-frightened expression throughout the entire game. This is odd because with big eyes, prominent eyebrows, and full lips, her face certainly looks like it could be very expressive - but she almost never uses it that way. I can't tell if the actress really has such a limited range, I'm inclined to believe that the script simply didn't give her the opportunity to show other emotions.The game lacks almost all settings that players would want or expect, you can't even change the resolution, or adjust the brightness or sound volume. At least there's a subtitle toggle, but no closed captions and no way of adjusting how the subtitles are displayed. The game's audio and text language can be set separately, which is nice for non-native speakers.The game is completely controlled with the mouse, keyboard shortcuts do not exist apart from "Esc" for the pause menu.There is only one save state, and the game keeps overwriting it automatically, you cannot save manually. There is no "chapter select" function either. If you want to find out how a scene might have played out differently, you have to replay the game from the start. However, the game discourages you from doing so by not even including a "skip scene" option - a standard QoL feature that more experienced FMV game designers have learned to include by now.The game also sports several annoying bugs. Sometimes the image freezes while the audio plays on - thankfully, going back to the main menu and then clicking "Continue" usually solves that issue. Selecting something in the main menu sometimes selects the line above or below. Closing the game just freezes it, I have to close the window from the task manager. My achievements from 2 playthroughs never registered after the ending as they are supposed to.Even though the game has lots of flaws, I think the story and the meaningful choices are strong enough to warrant a careful recommendation. I'd get it on a sale, though. Be aware that the game is very short and that you may not want to replay it due to the lack of a "skip scene" function.

_childDocuments_.review: A flawed gem.While I still recommend the game for its good story, more than respectable production values and excellent performances, many things affect the experience in a negative way.In order to make the game feel more personal and first perspective, the player is required to touch a lot of point on the screen when there was really no need for it. It is fake interactivity, just to make the player feel active and not a passive watcher.One alternative, more classic interface, that required pressing keys or selecting numbers would have been effective.The game also suffers from the inability to pause choices. I mean, you can try to pause the screen, but the options disappear. The creators are obviously out of touch with reality about how fun it can be, during stream sessions, to let the audience vote on the next decision to be taken. Also, there is no way to speed up the videos from sessions we already watched, and no way to skip them either. So, if you want to try to watch every possible choice, it is going to take you several dozen hours. Not really worth the effort.The game is good, but it could have been so much better if the developers had avoided some obvious pitfalls.

_childDocuments_.review: I can praise the game film on its filming quality, editing and the actors are decent with what they were given to work with. What I also like personally is seeing my husband's surname in the game (which is uncommon especially in the west). Other than those points, I ran out of compliments and I really hate Erica.Why I hate Erica:1) Story: is okay at best, but dragged out, basic, unexplored and worst of all boring. These factors are more apparent when you have to play a minimum of six playthroughs to see all endings and get all achievements. No matter what choices you make or what ending you get, the story and direction is the same every time with new information sprinkled as a passing thought. I have so many questions about the events of the game but again nothing is properly shown or explained to us.2) Characters: Criminally unexplored and only exist as tools to the story. Nobody is given any traits as characters if they don't contribute to the story. I like Tobi, Hannah and especially Kirstie. Despite what the achievements say I don't anything about these characters outside of their tragedies (their backstory is also quickly explained and forgotten) and I spent one event with them and that's only so they could give me tools for story progression and they're put back in the background. Erica the character is boring. She is no different  from faceless protagonists in anime visual novels, she's emotionless regardless of the situation and is the worst character in the game. There's nothing interesting about her other than she's "the chosen one" and the actor's resemblance to Emilia Clarke.3) Time Limit on Choices: Why did the developers think this is a good?! You only have 10 seconds to make a choice a choice or the game picks randomly. WHAT THE ACTUAL F**K ??!!! That's not even enough time to read everything let on reflect the choices. I can understand this done in dire serious choices for dramatic effect but no it's every single question. The game wouldn't let me have the luxury to think on my choices, feel engaged or even give me any agency as the player.4) You can't Save or Skip: You can't save at any point you want then load or make multiple saves and come back to them later. You can't skip scenes you've already scene or chapter selects. There's only New Story or Resume on the Menu Screen. If you're going to play again you are forced to watch the whole story again. Even if it's 90% of the same story you've already seen, doesn't matter you'll be forced to see it all again unskipped. Again minimum playthroughs for completion is SIX TIMES, 2 HOURS PER PLAYTHROUGH. What happens when you make a wrong choice and you want to fix it? YOU PLAY BACK TO THE BEGINNING !! you either keep playing to the end or start the run all over again. Also achievements will not pop up until the credits.5) Gameplay Mechanics: They're basically opening doors, flipping through pages or clicking on stuff. It's the barest minimum for FMVs and even Point & Clicks. The mechanics don't work well half the time.Erica is such a huge downgrade as an FMV. My time with it is equivalent to watching a badly made moral movie in my classroom and I can't even sleep through it because my teacher keep's pestering me with questions making sure I'm paying attention. There's nothing even fun or interesting in this game. I'd recommend watching a playthrough of the game online (At least you can skip that way).If you're still interested in the game regardless, MY STRONG RECOMMENDATION :1) BUY IT ON SALE 2) PLAY WITH A GUIDE3) SPEEDHACK THE GAME4) HAVE LOTS AND LOTS OF PATIENCE
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty expensive game, production-wise, and some famous actors like Holly Earl who had done a fantastic job with role-playing their own convincing character, and all that is for a decent price (if you're planning on playing Erica more than once).If you've started to get bored of FMV recently, well don't worry, Erica takes this genre to another level with high-quality movie production with the camera work, interesting scenery, and set design which made it seems it could be a TV episode. There is also an add-on of interacting with realistic items, for example, turning the key, opening a chest, or flicking a photo frame which all can be a little jarring at first, but once you get used to it they can make the whole experience more immersive. Thanks to the amount of camera work captured on this title, each scene flows smoothly after another without taking away from the experience, unlike other FMV that cut away scenes to another one after making a choice.  There are also some stylizations like choices slowly fading away or blinking lighting where an item can be interactive with if you're stuck.To not get your hopes up, this is one of those games that encourage you to play more than once to get the full story picture there are certain clues and mysteries hidden within different choices you make, and sadly there's no skip button or a way to fast forward certain scenes. This is a shame because it's one of those games where your choices do matter and the story makes you second guess yourself as it's a little more at face value with figuring out what's happening in the asylum. Also, in case you miss this out, this is a whopping  and that's more so due to the interactive gameplay and the multiple translations, so I don't blame you wanting to skip this one for the moment if you have other things installed on your PC at the moment. Lastly, it may just be me but I'm getting some Pan Labyrinth vibe from the game if anyone hasn't seen that film you should check it out instead if the GB of this game scares you, it will make you cry if you’re an emotional wreck like me.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: It's...ok. It's a neat FMV thriller with higher production quality than some others. It takes about 100 minutes for one playthrough. It's got some interactions other than just making choices (lots of fiddling with things as you would on touchscreen games like The Room) but it has its flaws.As the title character, you're almost *too* central to the story to make much sense of it as it's happening around you; you're not, say, a detective at a slight remove. The temptation is to replay it multiple times to see all the different options and get more context but frustratingly there's no option to skip elements you've seen before, so *each* replay is going to take the full playtime. I'm not patient enough for that, but YMMV.Still, I'm glad I played it through at least the once. I'm glad I didn't get it at full price, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I used to be a huge fan of FMV Adventure games like Phantasmagoria. So after hearing about Erica I didn't think twice before buying this game. After I've played it through, althoughI haven't regretted buying it, I still miss some elements from old FMV games.Pros:Outstanding production qualityVery good actingFair priceCons (if you are expecting a game):Maybe I've had the wrong expectation but Erica is actually an interactive movie rather than an adventure game. Only interaction with the game is quite dumbed down and consist of gestures which belong to a mobile app. So there is no inventory / item interaction and no puzzles.I think they've added gesture interaction to make it more immersive but it didn't work for me it felt somehow too repetitive.I would still reccomend it though. Just expect an interactive movie like Black Mirror: Bandersnatch (which I find even better than Erica they are both worth watching).
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is definitely one of the better interactive movies out there. If you like this kind of genre its an easy recommendation. The story is thrilling and it feels like you reach the credits in no time but of course it has a regular movie length of about two hours. At least after the first playthrough it feels like your choices do matter and has consequences. Acting and voice acting are good and the production value seems high, especially for an interactive movie. Erica is even localized in multiple languages and not only by subtitles but by complete voice acting.Is there anything bad I can say about Erica? Yes, the game crashed on my PC two times (mid game and in the credits). But since the game saves so frequently I was able to continue exactly where I left of. The other criticism is that the game does not seem to support Controllers. When you want to play this in front of your TV you still have to play it with your mouse. But at least for me these two points are minor issues and compared to the thrilling experience you get negligible.

_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: WAUW!Okay, I've played a lot of FMVs and there's a certain quality, charm, and quirk that's consistent among most of them. They're usually a weird story, choice driven, some great acting, some not so much, pretty cheesy, and often a little ridiculous. Erica has a weird choice driven story with great acting and only a slightly ridiculous. But there's a lot of little things this does to really set it apart from every other FMV. Pros: Acting. I've got all the love in the world for FMV. I really do. But a lot of them are really cheesy and sometimes a little bit bad or at least edited poorly. Every cast member in Erica shines and lets you get immersed into the story rather than distract you from some oddly delivered lines. To be honest, in the beginning I wasn't sure about the main character as she seemed super shy and was a bit flat at first, BUT she's super expressive and conveys the emotions well, I think the character herself is designed to not be too dynamic as nothing's worse in an FMV than when you make a choice and your character reacts at an 11 and you need them to tone it down. Having the character be more centered allows the cuts between choices flow MUCH better. Story. The story was straight forward to follow (good for an idiot like myself) and it was compelling! I did finish it rather quickly, but really I think I'd be more annoyed by an FMV that went on for several hours. The story, dialogue, and acting really help the narrative just feel natural and like you're watching a solid tv/movie production. Gameplay. Yeah you heard me. GAMEPLAY in an FMV. Okay really it's a tiny detail, but I absolutely love that you'll interact with items by clicking and dragging them. Opening things and if you're like me, slamming doors repeatedly to make a ruckus. Oh and also...YOU CAN PLAY THE PIANO! Nothing makes me more sad than a game that has a musical instrument that you can't play. 2nd only to not being able to pet the dog. Anyhow, these little elements help a player stay engaged with the game rather than just watching a movie and clicking a choice. I can't imagine it was easy to film those hi res parts and don't think I didn't notice the elements that were masked off and composited back together. There's a lot of extra work for just this extra little detail and I'd be sad if I didn't give them praise for it. Presentation. The cinematography is solid! Lots of the way shots are framed and focus is pulled feels very high quality. I mean look at the screen shots for it. There's some proper shot composition going on there! I will say there are a couple of moments the depth of field gets out of hand, but really it's a super satisfying viewing experience. ConsUhm...alright. Here goes. I'm going to scrap the bottom of the barrel for some cons because no game is perfect. So if you read it and think "That's stupid, who cares?" Yeah you're probably right. This is a solid experience and I'm going to file a small complaint about the music? The music is actually solid. Adds the right tone and atmosphere, but just a couple of scenes here and there it's a little loud. Like I'm having to tilt my head towards the screen (because that totally helps with headphones) to hear people talking over the music. It's not even that bad. It's just a touch too loud. I'm gonna be real here. I had another minor complaint, but I've literally forgotten it...hrm...probably really not that big of a deal then! TLDR; I REALLY like this game. One of the best FMVs I've played (I've played a LOT), great acting, great story, great visual/movie elements, plenty of choices, engaging little parts to keep you interacting with the game and it's just an enjoyable experience. Really. If you like FMV at all. This is easily one of the highest ones on the list.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda impressed. The acting is definitely what made it. I thought everyone did a fantastic job and made the story more immersive. However, be warned, this is more of a movie than an interactive game. Somewhat of a spoiler, none of the choices you make through out the game matters except for the last 3 minutes of the game. There are 6 endings to the game, and I ended up getting the best ending, and I don't think I'll be revisiting the game knowing my actions in the game have no effect up until the ending bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I cant really recommend this title. Im trying out a couple FMV's to play together with my Girlfriend and after the great title Late Shift, we tried Out Erica.The Game Mechanics to use the Mouse on interactive Items is not really executed well and does not add anything to the experience.I even encountered a crash during the Storyline and was glad, that at least the Auto save worked.The Story was pretty flat and not engaging, but at least the actors did a decent Job.I would rather recommend to check Out Late Shift or the Shapeshifting detective.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Visually and sound-wise the game is really well done. The actors deliver their roles well and the motion touch system adds an interesting gameplay element, because you really interact with the movie instead of just selecting text boxes. Overall production value is really high.On top of that, you have loads of choices to choose from during the game. I've only played through the game once and probably many options will have little or no influence on the events, but I like the diversity, even if its f a k e d to some extend.Unfortunately, the mentioned motion touch system starts to get annoying very quickly, because the developers use it on literally every occasion. You are constantly pushing curtains aside, opening containers, twisting door knobs or pulling documents towards you. That's a bit of a shame, because the technology could be used for so much more. Sadly the controls only work semi-well on PC too, since the system is actually designed for touchscreens. (or at least it seems that way)The game is also a bit buggy. I had several random crashes and freezes and when I quit the game it also freezes and you have to kill the process manually via taskamanger. Sometimes subtitles appeared but the voiceover was missing or the subtitles came way too late. Also, sometimes interactions bug out and you need several reloads until it works (eg the tap at the beginning of the game) Fortunately, the game saves every few minutes, so you do not lose much progress. The points I've mentioned so far have all been half as bad imo, but what really bothered me was the story. The plot is just.. well how do i put it.. confusing, weird, far-fetched and hardly believable. Despite the acting being good I couldn't care less about the characters & plot and at a certain point I felt just plain indifferent about it all.Oh, and there is no "skip" function in case you want to do another playthrough with different choices. This is a no-go and should be standard in every FMV.If you're new to the FMV genre better try one of the "D'Avekki Studios" games (I really love them) or classics like "Her Story"Edit: why does Steam censor the word "f a k e d" lol

_childDocuments_.review: Not so much a game as an interactive movie, but it has so many twists and choices that it requires several plays to experience everything. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting and engaging FMV thriller! I've didn't have a chance to play it before even If I knew the game - thanks to Austin Wintory and the fact that he made a music (which is fantastic - as always). But the acting is good, story interesting, level of interactivitiy - well made. Definitely worth playing if you like FMV's
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever watched a  B horror movie and thought ''If I was that character, I wouldn't do what they did!'' Well in this game you're in control of the main character, Erica. You get to choose many of her interactions with other characters and objects in the game with your mouse. No one playthrough is likely to be the same and the acting is so good the ''choose your own adventure'' interactivity drew me in to keep playing and trying to see how many different scenes and endings I could trigger. Holly Earl's  (Erica) acting is especially good...having to act with the concept of the viewer choosing what type of person she is is not easy but she nails it. The emotions she's able to pull out of you will make you want to find out what's going on as much as she does. It's funny, I didn't know this game existed and found out about it a strange way. My sister's name is Erica and we were hanging out a few evenings ago bored and she saw his game with her name on sale and just bought it. We share this steam account together. Glad she did, I recommend it to anyone who likes mystery horror and/or choose your own adventure style of entertainment.

_childDocuments_.review: Played for a short while, will probably finish this game.I am a sucker for FMV games, but there is an overuse of what seems like touch screen controls here. _childDocuments_.review: Wow...I've played nearly all of the Wales Interactive games, but I don't think I've ever been so drawn into a FMV game. Mouse required, and sometimes clicks and drags didn't register.On my first play, I let my mother make the choices, and the game story wrapped up so perfectly that it felt like watching a film. Even some of the dialogue and some choices made in the beginning tied in perfectly with the overall narrative and conclusion. I'm not sure if that was great writing or great luck, but bravo!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun as FMV games go. Acting is good for the most part, very few scenes I didn't quite agree with. If you like FMV games, I think this one is worth playing. _childDocuments_.review: Haven't been able to play, really. I've tried multiple things but at best the performance is bad, at worst the game crashes at launch. I've posted these issues in technical support. There I saw multiple threads of people having similar issues. The developers however haven't responded over a month. Yes, I can see there have been recent patches but I don't see a lot of progress as the game is unplayable for me and many other people.With no controller support even though this was a playstation game... _childDocuments_.review: The price of the product is relatively acceptable, but it is still recommended to buy at a discount.good:The feeling of playing the game for the first time is quite amazing. The operation method and selection of the UI give people a new feeling, which is different from other holographic image story games on the market. The feeling of substitution during the game is also very strong, the excellent production team, and the performance of the actors are also in place. The "horror" element of the game is well controlled.Bad:As a "movie" of nearly two hours, it is indeed not long, but there is no way to save the progress of the game. It makes me very unhappy to have to finish it all at once. The game is not even divided into chapters and fragments to allow players to repeat play conveniently.The point is that there is no way to see all the choices in one game to understand the structure of the whole story, and the game does not even have a "fast forward" button to skip repeated plots. And if you want to see the impact of other choices, you have to play it again from start to finish. There can be no mistakes in the middle. If the game crashes, or the program is closed for other reasons. Then you will only be able to "play it again", even if you have finished an hour, because the game has no real "save"!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on the FMV/interactive-movie formula, with a clever interactive video mechanic. The story was intriguing and the soundtrack very atmospheric and well-fitting. The actors were all true to their character and the dialogs felt natural. Player choices did not feel too impactful at first, but the last chapter throws one bomb after the other, leaving you questioning your choices and regretting them the moment you click.Overall it was a great experience but felt too short and somewhat lacking, although I can't really pinpoint the exact weaknesses of the game, apart from its length. Also, the fact that you can't replay specific parts of the game to see alternate routes/dialogs is a frustrating.I would definitely recommend it, but I can't say I was blown away. One of the weaker FMV titles I have played, but still, an interesting one. I am looking forward to the next games from Flavourworks!Recommended on sale, since it's about 2 hours long. A >=25% sale is very fair.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, I haven't played a whole lot of FMVs. But the commendable acting and script of "Erica' surely made this one of the best ones I've ever had the pleasure of playing. The somewhat cliche theme and predictable plot isn't anything to write home about, but everything else made up for it tenfold.Now, the replayability isn't for everyone because, yes, you do have to replay the game multiple times to see all the endings. Even more if you're an achievement hunter like I am. However, I almost always found ways to make every playthrough feel a little bit fresh and different thanks to the number of responses you're given. The only frustration I experienced was wasting 4 hours trying to get the last 2 achievements, only to find out that an update meant I had to get the first ending again because there was a problem with tailed achievements.I initially hesitated to get the game because the first time I saw it, it had mixed reviews. But I'm glad that the tide for "Erica" shifted and it got more positive reviews in time, motivating me to try it out for myself. _childDocuments_.review: Game's cheap and interesting for a playthrough or two. Getting the achievements is a frustrating endeavor tho so I wouldn't recommend it.Also while you can't save manually to check the alternate paths you can still reload from an autosave if, say, you gotta leave a playthrough halfway through.Gameplay wise, there's nothing. It's basically a choose your own adventure book in movie format with a couple QTEs and some hidden choices. Which isn't much but for its price its enough.The graphics are top notch and a massive amount of care was put into every scene, as a movie this may be one of the best for cinematography and set design. Which is extra impressive due to having to account for how to frame the choices and hidden choices which must've made framing a particular kind of hell.That said, this is where the bad part comes in. Firstly, most choices are meaningless at best, activelly making things more confusing by just causing you to skip scenes at worst. At least most scene skipping is obvious so you usually won't do it by accident anyway. There's a couple large ones but the story is largely the exact same no matter what, with only 1 choice noticeably altering the paths, and even then only for a bit (that is your choice of BFF). Generally speaking, the game will yank you back to the predetermined path no matter what. I for one saw this coming on my first playthrough and decided to actively try to oppose said path no matter what, being openly friendly to the "bad guys" while rejecting the "call to adventure" every chance. Due to scene skipping this hilariously resulted in me getting to the end faster while having accomplished absolutely nothing to alter it until the end choices. Which is just a bad deal really. Don't do that, please. Just let us have player freedom if you're a choice based game, that's kind of the point of the genre yknow.As for getting more info each path, which the game treats as a big selling point... yeah, nah, not really. The predetermined path already spoils most info there is and from what I've seen so far (I do plan to get all the achievements eventually despite recommending against it, I'm a completionist) all extra info is at best some additional bits and at worst just confirmation or in a few particularly irritating cases simply having information earlier than the point at which the predetermined path will shove it right in your face anyway. And hilariously the one bit of information that affects the ending (how epinephrine works) you can just... have irl and use even if the game doesn't tell you. Yeah that happened to me on my first playthrough. I don't even know how to feel about that. On the one hand, kinda feels good to use that knowledge. On the other, kinda feels like the game is avoiding punishing me for not bothering to get that info in that run as I probably should've been. Or maybe it just sees not bothering to get that info as the good ending due to what you do if you skip it.Anyway as for the story itself. Oh god. It's not good. It's really not good. I mean, the first playthrough is really hype, and in my case so was the second as I got more intel by actually going along with the predetermined path while trying some alternatives. Hell even the third playthrough felt good just to get the 3 main choices.  But the more you analyze what's going on the more it sets in that... this just doesn't actually make a lick of sense. Seriously, it just doesn't. There's a lot of elements clearly just added for mystery's sake. The game contradicts itself at times. Particularly when it comes to Greene's "explanations" (which are either full of lies or plotholes, you choose). And Greene also just acts irrationally a lot. And has no firearm safety training apparently. I'm sorry you cannot convince me you wanted to protect the main character when you kept AIMING A LOADED GUN AT HER HEAD AND COCKING IT. THAT'S NOT WHAT PEOPLE WHO DON'T WANT YOU DEAD DO. But the game seems convinced she's telling the truth and had nothing but noble intentions towards THE LITTLE GIRL WHOSE FACE SHE KEPT AIMING A LOADED GUN AT, WHICH SHE ALSO AGAIN, KEEPS COCKING WHILE AIMING IT, AT HER FACE. No I will not get over that I'm sorry that goes well beyond misdirection and into the realm of "the only way this can be explained is if the character is completely insane or irrational".Anyway just. Point is. Yeah story's really bad when you think about it too much so this is the kind of game that gets worse with each playthrough. But it's fun to treat as a movie, and even just watch friends as they play it. So for 10 euros, well, that's less than a cinema ticket's price. So yeah. Thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: It  I don't wanna say the game is bad because there was clearly a lot of effort put into it, but it's just kind of messy. I personally don't like the idea that you have to play multiple times to get the full story as it feels like a cheap tactic at replayability especially since you cannot skip scenes you have already seen so a lot of time you'll be sitting listening to the same dialogue over and over again to find everything. I know some people may think that they'll get the basics of the story after one playthrough, but you really won't. Maybe I'm just stupid, but the story makes no sense. There were a lot of times I was just super confused as to what was happening. Also, the setting and the way people acted made me laugh because it is just so farfetched in some aspects like how the girls have NO supervision like whatsoever. At one point your character supposedly sleep walked OUTSIDE and woke up by the woods and everyone is like "lol" and just moves on. I know there's supposed to be mystery, but it's confusing to the point of frustration.   The acting is......also ok? There are some moments that are kinda silly, but for the most part everyone is fine. I will say the interactive moments feel kind of pointless. There is no time limit to my knowledge and it's most of the time for very arbitrary things like turning a faucet or opening a box. A lot of the choices also feel like they're more there for the achievements rather than the actual story as, from what I have seen, the major choices appear at the end instead of really stacking up, but I could be wrong so take that criticism with a grain of salt.   Finally I will say it is trying a bit too hard, but I suppose I would rather have that than having no effort at all. Overall the game is ok. Maybe wait for a sale though if you're REALLY interested, but like I said the story feels really clunky and I forgot to mention there is a TON of excessive gore.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically, I bought "Erica" just to spend some time in the menu (*) to give it a thumbs up in this review (and to support the developer).I played it right after it launched for PS4 (2019, pre-pandemic, an eternity ago it feels like) and I was very pleasantly surprised.Technically very well done, decent story, great actresses/actors, well filmed and excellent German dubbing.A little slow-paced for my personal taste, but offers a lot more interaction beyond the usual decision making, even if the one-motion-tasks become quite repetitive over time and some tasks can be a bit tricky to perform. That might be even harder to do with a mouse compared to a touch pad, since objects are often moved in real time but the cursor will move pretty slow in the game to support the player, provided it is intentional and not an issue with my PC.There are only a few really important decisions to make (at least that's how I felt) but many of the small ones give the player the opportunity to kinda shape the character of Erica (in the players mind), despite the fact that it doesn't necessarily have a direct impact on the story.However, there are various little details to discover and even the patients of the psychiatric ward have their little mini branches of or alongside the story, which definitely gives a certain replay value.The only downer is that there is no mobile app support (yet). That's a shame, as many players will probably have to play alone, with their mouse wired to the PC. I liked the PS4 version for sitting in front of the TV with several people watching the movie, playing via controller or mobile app. I hope it will be implemented in the future.In my opinion, if you like interactive movies or FMV games, you shouldn't miss out on "Erica", even if you only play it once (should you not be interested in the achievements). And although there are technically well executed features, the developers certainly haven't reinvented the wheel, but this title is clearly one of the better ones in the genre and thus an easy recommendation from me.----------(*) At the time of this review, the menus are a bit messed up due to overlapping hitboxes of menu items and if you click New Story and then Cancel, the game quits instead of taking you back to the main menu or leads to a playing background video with no menu options whatsoever. Here, the developer may like to touch up on it.

_childDocuments_.review: So first off, annoyances.The non-English characters shouldn't even be in the game since this is set in England. Fine the mixed one who is sort of a villain - that's fine. Because God knows we need the "evil white male" propaganda to stop. But for God's sake, give them an American accent or something. I'm sick and tired of them talking like Englishman, when they're not English.GAMEPLAYThat out of the way, I did have fun making the logical in-the-moment choices the first time. (The play time is for two playthroughs; second playthrough was very quick). In the second playthrough, i made some choices that weren't exactly organic (partly because i wanted to see if the fixed points in the story had any variations, and if there was a different ending.Also, the reaction and actions of the actor portraying the cop, are really weird when you make the logical choices i made in the first playthrough. Somehow, the variations of the actions for the cop ended up making more sense the second time through the game. (I am very happy that the fixed points in the story had variations themselves or else it would have felt like you action didn't mean anything.)Also, i can understand people not wanting the action to stop a few times for each scene with the interactions, but the developers wanted the player to FEEL like they are taking part in the story. (If you people complaining didn't want that, then go watch a regular movie!! Simple!! The whole point of you doing the actions of the actions of the main character, is to feel like you ARE HER. That IS the point of immersion with this type of "game". Yes it stop the story momentarily, but nothing is perfect! If we were to not stop the action while making choices, this would have been a holodeck simulation in Star Trek TNG!! But it's not!! So calm the fυcκ down!!THE CAST: They executed their lines and actions very well. Obviously there's variations in what they do because of the B-roll that was recorded to create the interactivity with objects, and in turn create the variations in dialogue. (My second playthrough felt like the non-verbal queues of the character interactions felt more like a movie the second time through; things you'd expect under suspicious circumstances.ENVIRONMENT:Set decorations were well done. Especially for a certain room that you may or may not end up seeing....CAMERA WORK:A lot of fixed views, for obvious reasons. If this were a straight film, then obviously the camera work would be more fluid.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~OTHER PEOPLE'S IDΙΟTIC Negative REVIEWS:- People complaining about too much memory being used up because of the languages supported- Complaints that they couldn't properly use a mouse or find where to click or drag, either because they are cripple, incompetent or lazy, or blind.WHAT IN THE HELL DOES ANY OF THAT HAVE TO DO WITH THE GAME?!?! I MEAN REALLY NOW!!!I had absolutely ZERO problems with the interactions. This is a PC "game", that uses simple mouse interactions. Mouse, and one button to drag and select options. THAT'S IT. If you can't do simple things like that, then stop playing and refund it and go buy a Macintosh that has one giant button.Are these people seriously trying to ruin future games like this because of their own selfishness and shortcomings?!Like one thing that really pissed me off: People complaining about doing many actions like opening doors, or sliding open dresser desks, or opening briefcases with clasps that pop out, or briefcase locks that open with buttons. DO YOU BOOMER MILLENIALS EVEN HEAR YOURSELVES?! I really wonder what would happen to you when the world goes to shιt, and you can't press a simple button or light a fire!!! What... are you going to complain that you can't figure it out, and just sit and die?!?! Or complain that you have to do too many things yourself, and just sit and starve until someone else does it for you?! You people seriously need to be locked up in a Turkish prison and left to your own devices as you eventually have to chew off your own foot because you can't smuggle a piece of metal to unlock your chains.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~BOTTOM LINE:I really enjoyed the story, and I hope they make more.
