_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best FMV game I have ever played but thats really not saying much.Anyway, can't give away much but;Pros.- Good acting.- Likeable characters.- Very cinematic.- Good production value.Cons.- The writing has glaring inconsistencies.- Plot is reliant on the impossible incompetence of at least three characters.- The endings really aren't as clever as they think they are.Heres the thing, this game is very much like a film. Its the most like a film of any FMV game I have ever played but the film its like is a well acted thriller for people who are abit slow on the uptake. If you have any deductive skills or logic in that noggin of yours you are going to strongly suspect whats up about five or ten minutes in. Although frankly those qualities are not a full gone conclusion, I googled the alternative endings after I completed the game and found "the best ending" on youtube. Needless to say what I saw was a video from someone who had completely missed any of the glaringly obvious subtext and evidence that would lead them to conclude it was infact the worst ending and many comments which also did not seem to pick up on clues that are almost thrown in your face. So maybe I'm being overly harsh, maybe this game was precisely as clever as it needed to appeal to the majority of gamers whose most intriguing challenge is usually who to shoot first.That being said, even if you had a PhD you will find this game entertaining. Its not a head scratcher, you won't be trying to figure it out for weeks to come but it will keep you playing.The bar for FMV games was incredibly low and if this were just a film then I would be irritated by the plot holes but this game has succeeded in raising that bar from "bad" to "acceptable".It is for this reason I recommend it, I hope it is the start of a new wave of FMV games that will eventually raise it to Breaking Bad levels.

Accidentally killed Tobi in the 'operating room'. I am not going to replay the game for multiple endings since it will screw with my brain. The acting is the only amazing thing, to be honest. The achievements came right at the end, which was strange to me too. 50% good plot 50% bad plot. Got it on a sale too, so it's not worth refunding.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is a crazy experience in short terms. This game is more like a choose-your-adventure style movie. There's no gameplay or anything, rather, when Erica is placed in a predicament, you as the player get to choose what she does, what she says, or what crimes she commits. And yes, that last line is correct. As this game is purely story based, I will not be saying much more. The acting is good, the story is pretty captivating, albeit a little confusing at times, and the choices put you in a stressful situation to make sure Erica or anyone else doesn't get hurt. If your looking for a choice based game with an awesome story, than this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: This game wont be everyone's cup of tea. I was a fan of choose-your-path story books as a kid, so I enjoyed this interactive film style game. My OCD had me repeating the story several times to complete 100% achievements. I like to complete as much as possible without relying on guides, but this one definitely requires reading some achievement guides to complete. It is frustrating having to run the full length movie again from scratch just to make 1 different decision, and complete the story to earn an achievement. I've seen some feedback complaining about the time limit on decision making. I agree that first-time running through it is hard to read and absorb all the different options before making a decision, but isn't that kind of the point? It makes it a little more "realistic" maybe? IRL Erica would have to think fast and react - so I get why they created it this way. You get used to it and know what the possible options are after multiple re-runs! Perhaps they could have added a configurable setting to either have a time limit or infinite time to decide on all choices?
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admite that  it can be a torture to replay this game without skip/fast forward option,I belive ERICA will be a better game if this problem can be fixed.But It's a good story and the actress‘s perfoemance was so captivating that I find myself drawn into the world of game without even realizing.Also ,it's good to take a lesson that not to easily trust somone
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first play-through and I genuinely enjoyed my experience! It takes common ideas of the genre and shuffles them together in a way that feels thrilling and rewarding to discover and experience! Although, I can't say that it feels original as I was able to guess almost all the components of the story which also got me the ending that I expected! On the other hand, that's also what makes it intriguing as the game has multiple endings and the game was fun enough for me to want to get back into it in order to see how it varied over time! I also think that the ride is more important than the destination and this one was executed competently enough that I don't hold its predictability against it.The game also took me less than 2 hours to finish which is a good thing as it makes it more likely that I'll want to replay it in order to see what could have gone differently! This is also complimented by the stellar acting so, overall, it has a really good production value and it makes me wish that it came with a movie mode!My only negative is related to the controls of when you have to interact with objects. There are a lot of moments where you have to, for example, turn pages by moving your mouse horizontally or open a container in a similar manner but the controls feel like you're playing with Wii joysticks! It's far from precise and feels a little too wavy which can become frustrating on rare occasions. Also, as the whole game is live-action, it takes a while before you start to guess that you need to interact with something! I'm used to playing the Dark Anthology games which look and feel like a video game so having similar movements but in movie format was more distracting than anything else...Overall, I definitely recommend this game and I think that it's worth the asking price! I got it for 50% off and that was a steal... Good job developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: It's really an interesting concept but it is a rather short experience (which can be good if you dont want to get too invested in a game) plus all the endings left me extremly unsatisfied. The timed option selection made it difficult to make the choice you favour the most.Overall I can recommend it if you like choice-based games and snatch it on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of walking simulator and branching games, and I consider Detroit:BH the ultimate incarnation of the genre.So when I heard a RECENT game tried the formula with FMV, I had to give it a shot. Sadly, unlike Detroit where everything matters from the beginning, Erica is essentially a feature film where you make decisions and are given the illusion of choice until the very end, where 5 choice are revealed.This is a PS4 port and everything is FMV outside of vignettes where you control some sort of CGI-enhanced video rewind. To be clear, there is no real time gameplay, or what would be usually defined as QTE - the format makes it impossible, but the illusion is well performed. Evidently being a PS4 title, it will run at 60 fps despite being shot at 24fps without any issue on any hardware. There are NO options to choose from, and the title is 16:9, with no possibility to stretch it to 32:9, again for evident reasons. [The story]The story is very good, and echos movies like Jacob's Ladder, Existenz or The Jacket. It's suprisingly well shot, despite a few stage lights here and there that could have been improved on, and the set design is very solid. The acting really elevates the title, with a protagonist that's likeable. Duncan Casey makes puts forward an almost amusing "midsommer murder", but for me it's Terence Maynard who steals the show, as you're struggling to pinpoint if he's good guy gone mad or straight evil. [Conclusion]The bottom line is this is a movie, not a game, and 5 endings are provided in-extremis in the last 4 minutes. There is one choice that matters (and I messed it up with a misclick) to save the life of a 3rd party character, but this doesn't impact the  story in the least. The ending frame is always a poem which almost begs the viewer "Did you enjoy YOUR version of Erica?" and the game ends.For fans of the genre, considering the price, the production value, the quality at hand and the fact that this game has overwhelmingly good reviews, it's a no brainer - buy it. For those frustrated by QTE games, give this a wide berth, as it suffers from all the tropes the genre obliges.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: This is an FMV which I enjoy playing.The game, acting, image quality, and sound were all very good maybe even excellent. The user inference deserved special mention I thought it was really good in fact I spent the entire game thinking wow this user interface is really good.I've only had one go through but it wasn't enough to understand the plot which I need to treat as a con. I've noticed that the game freezes up on exit not sure what that was about. This a game worth playing. Cheers
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: This FMV is the best one around. Best quality with a whole movie experience, climax and soundtracks. Acting is top notch especially the actor that plays Erica. Could contend with some Hollywood movies. Would love to see a sequel, guys, please make it happen! Enjoyable experience with great repeat playthroughs. Highly recommended if you are into thriller or psychological horror genres.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: The best interactive movie I have ever seen! Actually, I have only seen one, but hey, it's really good. Great thriller mystery story. Not suitable for kids by the way. The interaction is mostly unnecessary but it keeps you feeling like you are taking part, so it's all good. There were times when I wasn't sure what was an option and what was mandatory. They could do with some more words here and there. Also, there were times when the single word descriptions of options were not enough and I really wasn't sure what I was choosing. The story is very good. Not all of the questions are answered by just one play-through so you really need to rinse and repeat several times to get a full idea of what is going on  The general story proceeds in a set path no matter what choices you make except there is differing information, and ultimately different endings. There are a few surprise side branches though that only appear when certain options are taken. I don't know how many endings there are, so far I have only experienced two. It takes about two hours per run. Generally, its all done very well. Acting is competent, with the exception of the lead, which seems odd, but there you go! Some of you may remember her from a Dr Who, Christmas Special. Very light on your PC, I am sure no one will have trouble running it. All in all it's really well done and very well worth the small cost. Go buy it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is a well made "choose your own adventure" type of game, really gets you involved in the story and it has the possibility for multiple playthroughs. However, it can get pretty sequence breaking to do things like open suitcases, turn on knobs, flick lighters and stuff like that unless it really is a moment that decides the course of the adventure. Nevertheless, I think it is well priced for what it is. Definitely recommend it. 80/100
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: ive been meaning to play an fmv game for quite some time and im gald that erica was basically the first fmv game ive ever played. i honestly cant say that the plot is stellar or superb and in fact the whole cult thingy has been used alot in many different movies and games but thankfully for erica they have holly as the main actress and she did a phenomenal job with her acting. in fact her amazing performance was really the only thing that got me through the game, aside from that i thoroughly enjoyed the rest of it as well. i am ashamed that i basically got the worst ending possible on my first playthrough but then again, i have a tendency to f up haha but other than that this game is not bad honestly. again the only negative thing about it is how generic the whole ''cult and groomed for a cult'' backstory has become in todays day and age so the story isnt anything but id still give this game a solid 7/10 just for the experience and holly's brilliant acting alone. seriously just get this game to see holly's acting!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: The acting is really good, better than what I'm expecting to see in a FMV game. Same with video editing and production. It looks and feels exactly like an interactive movie.Production wise, it's undeniably good.The story is a bit confusing. There's a lot of things going on, jumping from one place to another while the narrative drags itself. At some point I had to force myself to keep going to see the ending.This would be a neutral title for me, but I'll give it a plus for the acting and visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game because it gives me a lots of emotions. When you play it you are going through so much emotions during the game and it’s definitely Awesome . It gives you complete interactions and you can choose a lot if that makes sense. Also the game has a multiple endings and I sell mostly every ending. I have enjoyed myself during the game and I hope you would too.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: A good interactive movie with big, huge shortcomings.I still recommend this game because the production quality is amazing, and the plot itself, though rushed, is interesting enough.However, there is no skip option, and that's not good because most of the scenes are the same no matter what you choose. Watching the same stuff over and over again is just not fun. Personally, two playthroughs were enough for me. It's a shame, because the replayability, which is already barely present, is hindered even more.I also don't get why there is not gamepad support, considering that for some time it was a PS4 exclusive
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: One playthrough is 1.5-2hrs, need 5 or 6 times to complete all achievement.After play once, not really feel like repeat it since it don't have skip function and repeated screen is a lot.Pro:- Interesting story- A lot of choicesCons:- No skip function- Stuck one time at the end of selection- Control is not easy and some action is not necessary.- Some story design is not logical.Recommend for FMV fans but not the best one for me. Still prefer late shift.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I did one playthrough, took me 2 hours.You can go to the movies by yourself once for the same price.Or you can get this game, decide where the story goes and replay it several times to do completely different things and get different endings, scenes, dialogue. If you can get it at a discount, it's a must. Bang for your buck right here.The acting is superb, most british TV viewers will instantly recognize most of the cast.Other international viewers will maybe recognize one or two of the cast. They've been in several big productions.So yeah, the acting is pretty damn good.The music and overall sound quality is just great.Gameplay is pretty much "choose your own adventure". If you like that, you'll enjoy this.The production values in this game are great. It's atmospheric, thrilling, relatable.If you like thrillers and mysteries and you want a very decent fix for chilling & playing, get this game.I honestly jumped in my chair a couple times (this is NOT horror, mind you).It crashed on me once, though, but I'm not running anything spectacular. Luckily, the game autosaves and it let me return to the exact moment I had to relaunch. No idea if it's possible to pause.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I actually expected a real game. But then i got surprised thats it not actually a game, more a little movie where you can change the story. But i like this kind of "game". I liked the actors. the storytelling and the places. This "game" can actually be really frightening because you have the choices to "kill" (i know its only a movie) real humans instead of pixels. And Erica does it icecold.Bad things to mention:- Game keeps crashing after 1 hour without any reason at all.- I cant exit the game like any other ones, i need to close it via task manager.- No manual saves possible. If you miss 1 thing you have to redo the entire story.Other than that great work.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game because of a podcast (Level with Emily Reese) interview with one of my favourite videogame composer Austin Wintory. In the interview he mentioned the challenge of composing and directing adaptive music to fit in an interactive movie where the timing, decision, and pace of the player's actions are unpredictable. Wintory also composed for Abzu and Journey, two of my favourite games. I placed the game into my wishlist since I am a big fan of Wintory, but I didn't buy it right away due to the price tag of the game. I finally decided to buy the game when it is on sale, and gave it a try, and it blew my expectation miles away. This is a very beautiful interactive movie, entertaining, engaging. I was at the edge of my seat the whole time, constantly doubting my in-game choices, and even though I did not end up with a feel-good ending , I am so prepared to go back and replay the game to explore other potential endings. The best part of the story, IMO, are story-telling and the element of discovery. You followed along with the protagonist, trying to discover the truth behind mysteries. Of course the music is so amazing that it immerses the player into the story, making you forget that you're playing an interactive "game", but more like watching a movie that you're a part of. Can't wait to see what the studio is going to give us next!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Ad advertised, this is more of an interactive Choose Your Own Adventure movie than it is a true game. Oddly that didn't seem to bother me that much. I have a tough time with replayability with games that have choices because I get bored during replays, but I didn't have that as much with this game (I replayed twice immediately). Definitely worth a snag if it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: The film itself is really good. The actors, the script and the direction are very good. The choices really have an impact on the story. My first part took me 1h30 playing normally. It takes about 6 hours in total to get all the endings and finish the game at 100%.But unfortunately not everything is positive...The controls are really not good. It happens that you click on an action and another one is triggered, it happens that you can't drag certain things and if you have a second screen, the mouse is not fixed so you will often minimize the game without doing so on purpose.Despite this, the game is well worth it and I recommend you buy it (especially at 80% off at the moment).
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: It's like going to thriller movie but instead of screaming for the protagonist not to do stupid S*!T, you can actually control the outcome. So if anything bad happen, IT'S ALL YOUR FAULT. The game length is also like a movie(1 1/2 - 2 hours), which is fair enough as the price is like a movie ticket with unlimited rewatch/replay...
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: it's said that no single path gives all the answers, but in fact the game doesn't give any answers at all. even after you've been through every possible path, you'll be left without any certainty. so, this game will disappoint those people who need clear and unambiguous explanations.on the other hand, if that's the idea of the game – to depict a distorted reality as it's seen by a mentally ill person – then it's almost perfecty executed (something like Nolan's movie Memento).i've played the game around 20 times trying to find new clues (like, who made that photo??) or make the story turn some other way, all unsuccessful. so i'm a bit disappointed with the fact that little can be changed (choices don't matter), but i must note how well the existing paths are worked out, that's a lot of work actually.and of course what made me want to play this game over and over again is that it's made like a real movie. great actors, great camera work, great soundtrack, and a dark and eerie atmosphere into which you immerse completely.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Intriguing and imaginative. Great cast and well crafted interactions. Yet, the story is still too fixed in the sense that little can be done differently or changed every time you play. On the other hand, those things that can be changed and the new details you discover still keep you playing this short but entertaining game.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe my expectations have been set too high by programs such as  Black Mirror: Bandersnatch. I suspect the budget is lower but after completing my first play-through I was utterly disappointed with the story. The occasional interactions with objects such as opening a box or turning a tap are clunky and get in the way. Worst of all are the narrative decisions. Choose your own adventures are often more linear than you'd hope but most choices were so inconsequential and mundane that I was not compelled to choose any of them and they hid the important choices. Even when there were choices like "fight back" the actual response was barely more than a whimper. The production quality is equal to a TV series but unfortunately everything else is lacking.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to players who enjoy story-heavy slow paced games. It doesn't take very long to complete the story once, but it certainly has some replay value. There are several outcomes, and even after that, it can be interesting to see how some dialouge choices have some subtle influence on the world around you.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: The most unique fmv gameplay ive ever played. Most of the fmv, player can only choose an action and nothing else. But this one is different. Player have some action to do, such as dragging a picture towards you, lighting up a lighter, even unlocking a door. The control a little bit buggy but its alright...ERICA also have an outstanding storyline! i ate while playing because im really into the story. Took me around 2 hours to complete a single ending (6 ending available. Maybe took around 12 hour to get all???).Really worth it!! Absolute 10/10! Cant wait for dev upcoming game "HUSH"
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: A full play through takes about 2 hours, if you are taking your time.  I've gone through twice now and completely enjoyed both times.  I don't know how many endings there are but the two I've seen so far were radically different.  Probably not for kids or people struggling with staying in reality.  The filming, acting, and choice selection is all amazingly done.  The only thing I might change is you are required to do a lot of trivial actions that don't seem to require user input.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool game that I enjoyed playing once, even though the ending I got was unsatisfying. The actors' performances are genuinely good, the story has its moments, and the package captivated me enough to go through it in a single sitting. The lack of a way to jump to major decision points from your last playthrough to redo things was disappointing though. This would've made replaying it a lot more enjoyable. As it stands, you have to go through the entire thing, which is not great and even though I liked the game just fine, it's difficult to justify sitting through much of the same content just to change the course of an ending, for example. I wish the game would also chill with the prompts a little and let the scenes play on their own a bit longer. Anyway, it's a fun romp and I'd recommend it if you've got even a passing interest in nonstandard games or FMV games.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Two things I care about with this type of game (or interactive movie, if you will):1. Story needs to be interesting and engaging.2. Choices have to feel impactful to actually make a difference in how the story unfolds.Erica checked both those boxes for me and I can honestly recommend it.The only thing I did not like so much were the 'swipe prompts' to open doors, turn keys, etc. They seemed a bit unnecessary and therefor bothered me a little bit, but they don't appear too often.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up with games like Gabriel Knight : The Beast Within and Phantasmagoria I have a real soft spot for FMV games and there quite a few good ones out there now too .... including this one.  If you are like myself and enjoy the FMV genre then this game offers:Great LocationsGreat ActingGreat Storyline with multiple endingsGreat InteractivityAnd the bad thing? .... no sequal perhaps.10 / 10 Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: A high quality FMV game production. Cinematography is movie level, with very nice bokeh effects, framing, and high quality props. The acting is also great, at no point were there any cringe-worthy scenes which is something that often plagues this genre. There is a decent amount of interactivity, though this is one of those games where only a few choices actually matter when it comes to the outcome of the story. Still, replay-ability is high because taking different paths provides different point of views. What is not so great is that the story is somewhat lackluster. It is a very "artsy" movie, and much of the story is left for the viewer to interpret and much remains unanswered. None of the endings feel like a true end that wraps everything up, but there is a decent amount of variation at least.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is really intensive and mysterious. But such a pity is short. But it seems in case that there so many variants to choose.The quality is cool. And that was entertaining and exciting. I wish there more like these games and serial producing companies should support this way of picturesThe coolest thing of the game that its self-sufficient and where plot asking for a cliffhanger or a second season there possibility to play again another way. That like a parallel seasoning. And I guess this story can continue and have a next multiverseWell done.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: In generalOne of the best interactive experience's that I ever lived through.  In detailsThe wide and powerful cast of actresses that you believe every minute.Strong and smart female characters.Family secrets, true family, and avenge the family themes Bloody but not truly gorish elements and feeling of suspense, that not leaving through all of the story.Tragic, yet beautiful.I could compare this, a bit macabre story, with film - A cure for wellness, and still find it more empathic and engaging.Or with McGee Alice and find it more women-oriented and more psychologically accurate. I could continue worth comparisons, but them would be enough.This experience pays off all of the time and costs you spend on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun. You can control the direction of the plot by yourself. It's very good, but when you play it for the first time, you get a bad ending. It's really bad. I have to say that there are still many mysteries in this game. You really can't understand the plot completely after playing it again, but you have a good time
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. This is the best FMV that I have played. There is a slight chance that some people won't agree to my words. But after all if you take my word for this game I would definitely suggest it. Also it is an under rated game so if u like it give a thumbs up & tell your friends to play it. And if they can't buy it, gift to them so they can at least get the experience & the company can get a reach out.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Very polished FMV and definitely amongst the better games in the genre. If you enjoyed Late Shift you will certainly like this too. Good lead actress and engrossing story which is very well done with multiple endings. Has a very dark, haunting theme and is pretty graphic so nice to see the genre trying new things. FMVs are so often hit and miss, but this is a solid hit for sure. Multiple endings offers great value for money too so grab some popcorn, switch off the lights and play Erica, my new favourite FMV.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: My first try of playing this game I refunded it. Something felt off and it made me uncomfortable. I came across this game again and decided to give it one more shot.And I'm so glad I did. The acting is solid, the music is lovely, you have interesting characters and on your first playthrough you'll be pretty confused. But the replay value is there, the game is just about 1 and a half to 2 hours long. It's one of the better live action games I've seen and I'm keen to see more from Flavourworks.Solid 8.5/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty indifferent on this tbh. Production is higher side of quality as far as these FMVs go, but it is what it is. A choose your own adventure movie with rudimentary choices and occasional interactions (click the thing, drag the thing, swipe the thing, etc.). If you want something more interactive than that, this isn't it. I will say the aforementioned interactions, while very basic are kind of neat in how they matched the "action" with the smoothness of the video. It's like you're really doing the actions as a player without breaking the illusion of it being a movie, if that makes any sense. The parts where it invites you to do something, you doing the thing, and going back into the outcome of it is all pretty seamless which these things rarely pull off. The actors were all pretty great for the most part.The story just really didn't land for me. The one-cent review a meaner side of me considered leaving in lieu of this is "Meh-rica."  It's just a little too goofy at its core and at least in my instance races pretty quickly and clumsily to the end. I think I pulled off what has to be one of the better endings, and I'm just not super motivated to restart. Lots of fun achievements for those of you who are though.  If you're generally into these kind of interactive movies and are on the fence then yes I would recommend you check Erica out. However, If you're rarely wow'd by these kinds of games then you're probably better without unless the price is too good to pass up.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game recently and writing this review. This is one of the best thriller and mind gripping game I played in recent times. Game has excellent graphics and works completely fine even without internet connectivity and even on minimum requirements. It has several languages for dialog and subtitles.You can have multiple ways and options to play and finish this game with every different choice and dialog with multiple endings.The glitch with the achievements has been fixed and you'll be able to see the achievements once you finish the game. To complete the achievements you might need to play the game several times. After ever finish you'll see the achievements that has been unlocked. So this is a awasome mind thriller game you can get for a really cheap price.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Fun short game with great acting. I really liked it. There was one time when my decision was not registered right I think, but that didn't bother me too much. I bought it on sale, which I think the money was totally worth it. The game itself is about 2 hours, but you can replay the game and choose different options to get different endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I have played this game in a few routs now, first one I did by myself, and the second one with a friend. I have to say this game, is amazing, its not game of the year stuff but it is still an amazing game that will keep you on the edge of your seat with its twists and turns. And the acting was great, not amazing but still really good. If you like horror games or FMV type of games, this is one that is really worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game! I don't usually play live-action video games but I was bored and wanted something mystery-based, so I picked up "Erica". I was absolutely glued to my screen while playing this short and creepy game. The choices you make feel important, affect the story, and are sometimes difficult. I was second-guessing my choices until the midpoint of the game, when I realized who the "bad guys" and who the "good guys" were. Is it worth full price? Yes, and no. If you're into thriller-themed games and are looking forward to replaying the game to get a different ending then you should definitely support the developers. Otherwise, if you only play the game once then the content is fairly limited, but still, it was an enjoyable and enthralling experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth playing. Amazing interactive story. From technical point of view I'd say a masterpiece. Great pleasure interacting with the environment. Story wise a bit short, but has a lot of paths. Being short it's hard to develop more connection with the main character, Erica. Not mentioning developing connections as Erica with other characters. The pacing is alright although I still believe there is not much going on. At the end you don't really care about those characters which could have been setup a bit better.So there is room for improvement but this doesn't change that it's a must-watch/play. Acting is great. The visuals are awesome and overall it's designed very well to work interactively. I'm impressed.The replay potential is kinda there but this is not so satisfying. The first play is really important in terms of weather you like the game in the end or not. I played through 3 times and it already felt a bit too much since you can't really skip anything as this is an interactive movie, duh. It's nice design, but I wouldn't force it on player in the next play-throughs.I wouldn't suggest it for people that are here only for the story. It's okay, but go watch some movie instead. If you care about different endings and interactivity then come and play.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I got the best ending on the first gamplay, so im happy with the story! I like the acting, the scenes, its a cool movie to see and with the chance of taking choices.In the game there are 6 endings and many choices along the way.The only thing i never like in this games is the useless actions, like twisting a key... and having to do it like 10 times. Its distracting. After using the lighter once, the rest its one too many.But overall, fun game!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is a Full Motion Video "game" where you take action as the main character Erica and experience her story, make meaningfull decisions throughout the entire time and uncover strange secrets.The start of the story isnt the best, there are lots of moments that replay themselves as flashbacks which can be a bit annoying and the first few minutes are confusing, certain characters act like they will be extremely important to the story but later you find out they are actually not, and while you do have conversations with them even near the end, they are nothing but meaningless. The gameplay is interesting, it reminds me of the Amnesia games, while you mainly pick dialogue options you also interact with stuff. Opening drawers, turning pages, opening doors, using a lighter, all this sounds silly but its kinda cool, and new in these fmvs ( new to me atleast, I never saw anything like this in these kinds of "games" ). Sometimes the interactions are a bit tricky but there are hints that are very well done, they are obvious but not too flashy. They certainly help.Acting, dialogue and camera work are all top notch here, it feels great. The only thing that I could complain about is that the main character mostly whispers when talking unlike other characters that talk at regular volume, could be just me though I dunno.The whole thing took me only 1 hour and 40 minutes and while I did expect it to be longer I still had a lot of fun. I did experience one crash halfway through where the game decided to freeze and close itself off, but zero progress was lost so no big deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a good and recommendable game, fans of the genre can't do anything wrong for the asked price. Sceneries, acting, voice acting and movie quality are all first class. Just the story doesn't make much sense. It's the kind of story that doesn't even care about making any sense and just wants to confuse you with leaving away logical borders, sending you from one emotional direction (Does this person help or harm me?) into the opposite, giving you hints that lead to BOTH directions and make you decide just what feels right at the moment - but always leaving you with some feeling of "What the hell do I know, and how COULD I know - just click something...). The lots of different hints and emotions just don't really fit together. Yes, I'm getting it that it wants to confuse you and it's also about mentally illnesses and that. But I've played enough of those games to slowly get enough of this, always thinking: I would care a LOT more about the characters and the story, if it would be more comprehensible, credible and just way more down to earth. With the quality that the other aspects in this game are providing, a better story could have easily made it an outstanding one of this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: I though they did a creative thing with the interactive cutscenes, which I at first thought they made with a 3dmodelling software , but then I saw they did it with frames of a camera and afterwards edit it in a  image editing software, so kudos for that, also the overal video quality is really good, given it's also a pretty dark enviroment everywhere. Story wise I think it's a interesting story, but a rather short one... I feel they could make it 3 times as long and then the story would have trived more,that said, it's nice to see the FMV genré flying high and the productions are gettingbetter.The casting is also very nice, all the actors are playing great, no FMV clichés so to speak haha.I like that the story is the most important thing, and I don't miss the occasional cheesy joke at all. With production like this the FMV genre and real movies are getting closer to being somewhat the same thing, I think it would be so good if you could shape the story of a full fletched movie.Though I understand it will take tons of time to produce something like that, though if the FMV genré has shorter movies, then Location is something that can add a nice touch and variaty to the production.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: This honestly blew me away. Literally just finished my first playthrough and...wow.The story had my attention the entire way through, and I really didn't know what to believe at the end. Plus the acting was amazing; the actress who played Erica especially nailed the emotions of a scared and confused protagonist.The production value was insane too, I've no idea how you guys pulled this off but I'm floored by the finished product.Also, Austin Wintory, your music was perfect and I felt so many things because of it. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very short, 4 hour long game. Nevertheless, usually movies last much shorter. And in this case, it was a really engaging movie. _childDocuments_.review: First off I just want to say, WOW! This was a truly amazing experience. The music was perfect for the mood setting and environment and the acting was fantastic. This is the first time I have played a game of this style and I will definitely play anything from these guys again! Trust no one, stay true to your first thought instincts. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very interesting and have a sense of mystery, and the idea of the game is really well though, put together, and executed, my only critique to the game is that there are multiple endings to the game, and to see the different endings you have play all the game again, with no way to skip the cinematics, nor a way to jump to a specific point in the game, so it gets kind of tedious having to play the game all over again for like 6 times to see all the different endings and paths.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica may be the new benchmark for interactive entertainment going forward.  Whatever you may think of this psychological thriller's plot, there is no denying the top notch production value that went into this "game".  If you've ever watched a movie and yelled out at the protagonist over a decision they've made, Erica essentially shifts the blame squarely on the shoulders of the viewer.  I can go on and on about how Erica has some of the finest direction, lighting, acting, etc. that I've seen in a movie of this caliber in quite a while, but the main takeaway is that the line is becoming blurred between game and film thanks to this masterpiece.  I want nothing more than to watch friends go through this journey to see an entirely different film with drastically different character relationships.  It's that good.  Please let this set the standard for the artform.  Not just for gamers, but for entertainment buffs all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: So I am a big fan of the resurgence of FMV games. I enjoy the suspense, cinematography, and acting in most of the recently good quality FMV games (The Complex, Night Shift, The Bunker, Five Dates, (New and haven't tried "I Saw Black Clouds")). I also liked this type of game in the Dark Pictures Anthology, Until Dawn and the Quantic Dream series of games all the way back to Fahrenheit in 2005. I purchased this game because I heard so many good things about it from the old PS4 release and wanted to try it. So I'll do a good and bad list here:Good:1) Acting is great, love the people playing the characters. Especially our main protagonist. 2) Story does a great job of keeping me into the game. The last 1/3 is amazing, everything gets better in the last 1/3. Suspense is ramped up and you're on the tip of your toes making decisions.Bad:1) No controller support! Big negative for me. I like throwing these games on my main TV or a 2nd TV via Nvidia Shield for a play through with friends. FMV games I find are great where you and friends play. That's hard to do when I need a mouse and keyboard to play. 2) Cinematography here is a little lacking in my opinion. We can set up these shots a lot better than some of them are in this game.3) Falls into the FMV trap of doesn't matter what you do in the first 1.5 hours, only in the last 20 mins of the game do you decide between the 7 different ending.Conclusion:I'll recommend this because of the $12 CND price. It's worth $12 CND to play through, maybe your own decisions on how the out come occurs. Enjoy the game as you play it. And then just watch the 20 min YouTube video that shows all seven endings occurring in the last 20 mins of the game.Bottom line:Play it once and make your decisions. Enjoy it for a cheap price, Watch the YouTube video for the other endings.PS: Play other FMV games for better experiences!
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: An FMV Choose Your Own Adventure title with some good performances and an interesting story. It can be finished within two hours, but there's enough branching paths that it encourages replays to see every alternate scene and ending. There's some issues with the controls in that they're kinda awkward when interacting with objects since it's hard to tell when the game wants you to drag your mouse, where to drag it or whether it just wants you to click on something, but outside one part near the end it thankfully never happens in a timed section so it's usually not a big deal. What I thought was a bummer is that the endings have the same issue every single game of this type has where it's about the journey and not the destination: there's so many story permutations that almost every ending cinematic is 20 seconds long with a black background afterward with five lines of text saying what happened after. This is one of those things where the interactive aspect of the game works against it. It's also rather glitchy - of the 3 playthroughs I've done so far the game has crashed randomly near the end of each, and it has also crashed when exiting the game after finishing it each time. Collectible achievements that require multiple playthroughs are also straight up broken and won't unlock even if you've gotten everything. Still though, I liked it and wouldn't mind a hypothetical Erica 2: This Time She's Even Sadder.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Erica is a game, no, an EXPERIENCE unlike anything I have ever played. The story writing is stellar, offering so many different paths for players to choose from. The seamless blending between movie cinematics and interactive gameplay keeps players immersed in the world of Erica. The mystery is ever unfolding, leaving players craving more with each corner they turn around. And don't even get me started on how talented the cast and crew were. I give this game a solid 9/10. The touch and drag controls felt clunky at times, and I thought that some of the dialogue options felt vague. Otherwise, this game is an underrated masterpiece, and is CRIMINALLY underpriced for $12. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Erica

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed my first play through. If you can get past the annoying interactions that make you do things the character would do anyway a hundred times, the story becomes VERY interesting and there's lots of replay potential as you are presented with multiple meaningful choices down the line. Surprisingly good acting for an FMV game, which could be a good or a bad thing depending if you enjoy the cheesy acting from 90's FMVs or are thankful for a more polished and professional presentation. Now I want to start again to see what options I missed.

name: The Past Within
detailed_description: Note: The Past Within is a co-op only game. Both players need to own a copy of the game , as well as a way to communicate with each other. Play together with a friend or find a partner on our official ! The past and future cannot be explored alone! Team up with a friend and piece together the mysteries surrounding Albert Vanderboom. Communicate what you see around you to help one another solve various puzzles and explore the worlds from different perspectives! The Past Within is the first co-op only point-and-click adventure set in the mysterious world of Rusty Lake. Features A co-op experience Play together with a friend, one in The Past, the other in The Future. Work together to solve the puzzles and help Rose set her father’s plan in motion! Two worlds - Two perspectives Both players will experience their environments in two different dimensions: 2D as well as in 3D - a first-time experience in the Rusty Lake universe! Cross-platform play As long as you can communicate with each other, you and your partner of choice can each play The Past Within on your preferred platform: PC, Mac, iOS, Android and (very soon) Nintendo Switch! Playtime & Replayability The game contains 2 chapters and has an average play-time of 2 hours . For the full experience, we recommend replaying the game from the other perspective. Plus you can use our replayability feature for a fresh start with new solutions to all puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Great casual co-op puzzle solving experience! We liked that no network connectivity or special invite system was required, the puzzles are cleverly engineered to keep you and your partner in sync over any kind of communication channel (though one or two puzzles might be difficult over text-only). The game played great without any hitch on a modern Linux laptop *without* a dedicated GPU, presumably it should work just as well on a SteamDeck. I really hope the folks at Rusty Lake continuing putting out more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful experience. I got to see the story from both the past and the future and the fact that you have two game modes so the solutions are slightly different is great. The atmosphere is incredible, the music (as always) slaps, the anxiety you feel during timed tasks is so intense and so rewarding, I absolutely adore the parallels between the two timelines and the way they're connected, I don't wanna spoil specific examples but it's amazing. The lore made me go insane. I got too attached to the mouse in the future. 10/10.

Would absolutely recommend, especially at the insanely generous 40% launch discount.

_childDocuments_.review: IMO, it's only really fun the 1st time through. We just finished the bee and the butterfly, changing roles of who was in the past and who was in the future and I really didn't see any difference between the two.  The puzzles and solutions seemed exactly the same. So it was a bit of a let down the 2nd time through as you know what to expect. My last gripe with the game is that the puzzles aren't really puzzles or very challenging when the game is constantly telling you what to do. There were no AHA moments for me...instead of solving a mystery it just feels like you are reading instructions to the other person instead of putting together clues. It is kind of neat how they manage to make a 2 player game without a direct in-game connection, but the novelty did wear out quickly. In a lot of cases, the sequencing between me and my gaming partner was often broken by one person jumping ahead while the other lagged behind. I think something like this would work better with a direct in-game connection so that the sequences are directly in sync.

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a co-op game, but with a slightly different twist than a typical co-op game. In the game, we have to uncover the secrets of Albert Vanderboom, a deceased man, and in order to discover them we have to join forces with another player who is in the future or the past (the choice depends on us and our partner). On the other hand, we don't need to connect with the other player to complete further puzzles, but only need text or voice communication to do so.In general, the game features well-crafted puzzles that require communication with another player to complete. They are often based on the mapping of some patterns. They are not difficult puzzles, but completing each successive one is really satisfying. They are also logical and related to the game's plot. However, over time they can become monotonous.The graphics of the game are very nice. The game has its own extravagant style, and depending on whether you play in the future or the past, you play in either 2D or 3D mode, which is intuitive and I didn't encounter any bugs in either mode.Sound-wise it is also very good, we have dubbing and a pleasant soundtrack, on top of that the ambient sounds are equally good.We can go through the game from two perspectives and, on top of that, by choosing one of the insects, which gives a total of four possible passages of the game, although they are not too different from each other. However, the choice of insects is not very important, it slightly changes some of the puzzles. Therefore, I recommend going through the game twice: in the future and in the past.The Past Within is a really good game. It is not a game that is difficult, the subsequent puzzles were not a difficulty for me and my friend, but we had fun playing it, which is what it is all about. Plus the lack of bugs, a good atmosphere and the evening passed quickly and pleasantly.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

I would wholeheartedly recommend it if you have a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a rank C+ (65-70%)Decent game - a pleasant experience... on sale.See my profile for more details about my reviews.I give The Past Within around 68%, but bear in mind this is because I am a veteran Rusty Lake enthusiast. If not, it would be more within the C- rank (60% and above) because ultimately, the game is OKAY. Its major flaws are:1) you need a friend (though we all do!)2) you need to purchase 2 copies of the game, each played on a separate PC3) you will finish the game in one sitting, potentially twice if you want to see the other side of the game (and your partner wants to see yours) - in other words, it is VERY SHORT4) the game is very easy, no puzzle should pose any problem if you have played just a bit of escape games before - very straightforward, too easy...5) the game is not original at all in its puzzles - nothing innovative6) there could have been MUCH more, but it is quite small in content, depth, reach...Beside that, I mean it is a fine Rusty Lake, typical escape puzzle game. Two new things this time:1) They tried themselves at 3D for the first time, and the major, obvious influence is The Room. Sadly, it does not go as far as a quarter of The Room's puzzles, content, or art. I mean it's okay - just, The Room did 3D escape puzzles better.2) They also tried themselves at real time coop, this time the obvious influence is their fellow compatriot devs from the series We Were Here. Albeit, not real time but a fake one, because there is no connection, you could play by yourself on 2 separate pcs, basically each side of the game gives the solution to the next puzzle and vice versa. So more a gimmick than anything. We Were Here did it better here again.So, yeah, it is worth it despite all that? I mean, it is still the creepy dark character, it is still the experiences of an insane, DavidLynch-esque family, the gore, the bizarre and that damn eerie lake... so sure, it is nice and pleasant, but you should definitely get it on sale. Not bad, but now I expect MORE from Rusty Lake! Their next one, Underground Blossom, is solo and slightly better! and if you did not know Rusty Lake, they did more than 15 game in these past 15 years, so I invite you to do them all, they are totally worth your time. I guess Rusty Lake is great in its entirety more than its games taken one by one - in other words, Rusty Lake is greater than the sum of its parts... no wait, the other way around: the sum of all its parts is greater than a single Rusty Lake game! is  on  on  on

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Not better than the best games in the series, but not worse than the others. It really is a spin-off about Albert and Rose, which adds to the fullness of the universe. As a fan of Albert, his story, and his two women, I enjoyed this game.What I didn't like was a lot of monotonous "look and tell me what you've got" puzzles. There was some variety, like the speed riddle and the old-school "make coffee, make the right piece of meat" type of riddles. I wish there was more variety.The parts of the game where you act as coordinator are the most boring. While your friend walks around the room, you sit and just spin the box. The developers try to innovate the gameplay of each game, and more often than not it has been successful (RL Roots, Paradise, The White Door,) but this time not so much.My friend had a bug on the speed puzzle, and we couldn't finish the game. In the end, I finished it myself. We finished game in another mode.The initial menu is a little annoying instructions that you can not skip and "are you sure your friend joined". It's also a shame that there is no controller support.Overall, I think the game is overpriced. However, it is worth taking into account that this is an independent group of developers.What I liked about the game is the good old Rusty Lake atmosphere, the gorgeous Albert, the story is good. The familiar elements of the game are well done. But I would like more gameplay and more interesting puzzles. Maybe more history of Albert and Rose.In the meantime, I'm looking forward to the next game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't have a single puzzle in it.The gameplay loop consists of:1. Searching around like a madman for inputs/outputs that sync up with your partner's.2. Repeating step-by-step basic instructions to your partner or receiving instructions and doing exactly what your partner/the game tells you to do.3. Repeat for 2 hoursAlso, you might want to consider reducing how much you make the players repeat tasks. There's a reason why, in most games, players are tested on new concepts simultaneously with ramping difficulty or complexity until they master it and can integrate it into other game elements.This game does no such thing. Instead, you're made to repeat chores with your partner over and over again with little variation or challenge. The "challenge" lies in the fact that you cannot see your partner's screen.For example, there's a chore where you read clock hands to your partner and they set a clock accordingly on their end. I know how to set a clock, so it wasn't even fun the first time. Why then, game, do you make us do it like eight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ times? WE ALREADY MASTERED THE ART OF SETTING CLOCKS, GAME.There are many other small tasks that players are made to repeat many times, such as the XYZ puzzles or the dials with symbols on them. This is genuinely upsetting and shows a lack of respect for the player's time. Many tasks are repeated over and over again, and not a single one of them constitutes a puzzle or requires critical thinking.It almost feels like padding to exceed the refund window. And bravo, you got me, game. I am aware it's only $6, but it feels like I am owed money for playing this to the end.Arguably, the most critical thinking you'll use in this game is filtering what information is relevant to your partner. However, this mostly devolves into a brute force approach where we just rattle off everything we see, and it quickly becomes annoying.The initial premise was interesting, and the atmosphere enhanced it, but next to nothing was done with it in this work, leaving a hollow shell of nothing happening. I understand there's a narrative that's expanded upon in your other works that is probably terribly interesting, but if it means playing more games like this, I'll have to pass.That being said, I would be unfair not to say that my partner really enjoyed it and wants to do another playthrough. Maybe it's simply not to my taste, but this is not a game I ever want to play again.Anyway. This was a novelty and the 2-player stuff was innovative, so, thanks for making it. I just wish somebody had warned me.

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a short puzzle game split into two paths. The answers to the puzzles in your pathway can only be found in the other pathway, so you have to play with a partner and maintain good communication throughout.I thought this was a really interesting concept and played it with my partner. We had a decent time - I'd say we enjoyed our time - but I don't think to the point where I'd enthusiastically recommend it to anybody else. There's a spooky underlying plot which definitely holds the user's attention, but the puzzles are just a bit too simple. Essentially, Player 1 finds a lock which needs a number code. Player 2 finds a code somewhere on their screen and reads it out. Player 1 enters the code and you move on to the next part. Ultimately it felt like there were very few actual puzzles in the game - you are basically just reading to each other.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this for the time I had with it. Myself and my partner have two PCs in the same office so we sat down one rainy Saturday and gave it a go. The puzzles aren't particularly hard, it's far more about clearly communicating with each other. If you want something that will last you a good hour and a half on a first play-through and then you will be done with it, this would be a good fit. I personally didn't see the point on a second play-through where the solutions to puzzles were apparently different, it's very much a one and done game. Definitely one I would recommend to get on a sale rather than at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A good game to play with a mate together. Gets you thinking a bit, graphics are cute, and the story is chilling. Very cool that you can play without connecting to each other, just by launching the game with different times and same answers set (there are 2 of them, so you can replay). Killer feature - the game is available on both mobile and PC.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly what you expect from Rusty Lake: a high quality puzzle game with intricate lore and a fascinating aesthetic. This game goes one step further though, having it be multiplayer adds another layer of complexity and suspense that the developers pulled off wonderfully. Of course if you don't have anyone to play with the experience kinda sucks, but besides that this game is great.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game has changed my life. I was once a small wee little lad, who only played fortnite, a TRASH game. Now I have played THE PAST WITHIN and I have realized that I suck. THIS GAME DOES NOT SUCK. it is a 10/10 5 stars. BUY IT. ITS CHEAP. and get a friend to buy it. If you dont have a friend, buy a friend! have fun playing which will you obviously do. thank you game creators for giving purpose to my life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within
