_childDocuments_.review: This is the puzzle-game equivalent of a theme-park ride. Its atmosphere is what you're there for, with its simple puzzles to help pace the story out.  Each puzzle you solve leads you to the next part of the attraction, accompied by some sort of creepy image or audio or change in your environment, and they are all so bizarre that I was never bored.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a short "co-op" puzzle, indie game developed by Rusty Lake. You can play in two different timelines, the past and the future. You and your partner chose one of the two timelines, and now you have to try and figure out how to establish a connection with each other. One player experiences a 3D environment with a cube, and the other player experiences an interactive 2D scene. There are great and unique puzzles in the game where you need the help of your partner to progress through the story. With an eerie atmosphere and a dark story, the game manages to captivate you and keep you in suspense. It is a fairly short game and can be beaten in one sitting, with easy-to-achieve achievements. From my experience, this game is all about communicating and talking to your partner. It was really fun, and I can only suggest this to anybody who likes puzzle or coop games with their friend or lover.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Me and my friends have played through, I BELIEVE all of the rusty lake games. The earlier ones are pretty rough, but we loved the visuals and the puzzle styles (even if sometimes they are a bit frustrating). This installment was a HUGE step up in both quality and overall enjoyment, its a little easy but we never got frustrated or drained. If you played and liked "Tick Tock: A tale for two" you will enjoy this game. And if you enjoyed this game, I suspect you will enjoy Tick Tock. WELL DONE, WOULD HAVE PAID MORE AND WILL CONTINUE TO FOLLOW AND SUPPORT THIS DEV TEAM :)))
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my spouse who really doesn't like to play any kind of video games. He wasn't super excited about playing but gave it a try anyway because I love escape games. It took us about 2.5 hours to complete and even he had a good time. It's pretty easy, even for someone like him who has never played an escape room type game before. We got stumped for about 5 minutes a couple times, but otherwise it's pretty straightforward and made for a fun night in. I'm really glad we played this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice puzzle game! Was a bit confusing at first that we didn't have to connect our games in any way but it was a lovely experience. I played the future and we chose the butterfly. It took us 2 hours. The puzzles were fun and entertaining. Neither too easy, nor too hard.At some point we plan to switch up the roles and play again, maybe this time chosing the bee to get more achievements. Definitely worth the money!Hopefully they will bring out more co-op games like this in the future, we surely would be interested to buy and play them aswell.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: That's nice example of co-op escape room quest. It takes a 90min to pass it with my wife. It have nice visuals and riddles, they are not too complex, all is logical enough. Moreover, games allows you to replay it once again in another role, because riddles will also change using different key. Anyway, the game is good. I can recommend it. Storyline is fine, I like it. In other hand, ending a bit crumpled, but still relevant and logical.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I love the Rusty Lake Series for its complex puzzles and slightly creepy atmosphere but this game really kicked it into high gear with the graphics and the puzzle difficulty. I played this game with a friend who has never played any of Rusty Lake games before and we both had a good time. Kudos to the Rusty Lake team for its first Co-Op game and for creating an experience that anyone who knows and doesn't know the franchise can enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Short and simple but fun co-op puzzle game. It's only around 2 hours of playtime and the puzzles are relatively straightforward. There wasn't really a moment where we felt stumped or needed a hint at all. The atmosphere the game sets is creepy. I get frightened easily so there were a couple moments where I was pretty scared but it's not like terrifying where I'm too scared to progress.The story is decent. There's not much of it since it's a short game but I liked it.I would wait for a sale to buy. Although it's fun, it's short and might not be worth full price for some people.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very fun game to play with your friend. Creativity, communication, and brainstorming on how to solve the puzzle is intense. Currently play as The Past on Chapter 2 and had a few surprising moment but it's fine to keep the game atmosphere. 10/10 would play again and change the role as The Future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun. I was expecting puzzles like an escape room but it's more focused on communicating and co operating with your teammate. The puzzles are very easy to complete if you communicate well. I recommend playing this with a good friend. The story is quite interesting too, and there are a couple of unsettling moments. We did two playthroughs so we could each experience the other side of the puzzle (past or future) and do the other path, although the basic story is the same. I think we will need to do a couple more playthroughs for all the achievements though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Received this game within the GirlStreamers community from Rusty Lake. I'm a big fan of the games and didn't realize at first it was a co-op game. My bestie joined me on this adventure and we thoroughly enjoyed our time! I love puzzle games and Rusty Lake always delivers. One of the things I really like about this game is the replay value of it b/c you have multiple perspectives and outcomes with this depending on how you and your partner work through the puzzles. This is actually a great tool for team building and understanding someone else's perspective. If you like puzzle games with friends this game is perfect for you!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Finally got to play this over the weekend with a good friend. We must be really in-tune with each other because we were never stumped and played through the 🦋 path in the one sitting.Looking forward to trying the 🐝 path next weekend.Very imaginative puzzles with an amount of quirks. I've played a few of the cube escape/rusty lake games and started in the past which was very much in-line with those games with the 2D 'you are inside the cube room' experience.. I almost completely freaked out when my interface changed to other one (which my co-op partner assumed was the norm).Good solid fun.. it really felt like it needed a third act though. Finished too soon, but for the price you can't complain about the experience. Good fun, and very creative use of co-op gameplay that doesn't require any sort of actual direct link between the games.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: So boring it's unimaginable. The other person has to wait while you solve your puzzle. It's not as competitive, clever, or interesting as Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes while simultaneously maintaining the same level of frustration and stress. The story is predictable -- actually there's no story at all. The main story is told within the first 5 minutes of gameplay and the two of you have to sit through completely irrelevant and monotonous 'puzzles' to finish the game. Needless to say, we stopped playing in the middle of chapter 2. We were lucky enough not to have surpassed 2 hour play time so we could request a refund. So I guess that's a win. The overwhelming percentage of positive reviews is absolutely beyond me.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Although this is a 'positive' recommendation because of the binary options Steam gives me, I do have mixed feelings about The Past Within. I knew what I was getting into before buying it and I got exactly that out of the game: a cheap, casual, fun and relaxing but also pretty short co-op game without too much depth. This 'recommended' is for those that are able to enjoy exactly that. And I'm one of them, to be clear. I enjoyed playing through it with a friend, but the game doesn't offer much replay value nor a deep story or complex mechanics - you're essentially taking turns communicating instructions to your partner to progress through the game. Towards an ending that I felt wasn't very satisfactory and that left me feeling like I was missing many pieces of a/the story.Be sure to play with a partner that is open and enthusiastic about trying this game; I think it's a major factor necessary for a positive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool asymetric dynamic between the two parties. The game makes you communicate a lot, but in a very relaxed manner. Partially creepy, but hearing your partner scream about something scary happening on your screen while you don't fully know what's happening to them right now was also quite some fun :DHighly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game. (not for kids xD) + creepy atmosphere+ fun Coop with a friend+ both sides have something to do (not just "onesided" like other games of the genre)+ useful for communication/team building training+ nice visuals/sound/sounddesign - needs a partner (both need to own the game)- 1-3h fun, full price should be 3 bucks- felt a little short, which is sad since the concept is promising + fun.Promising new ground for the series. If it wasn't so bloody/creepy you could use it to train communication skills of kids.But it's way to much horror. Wouldn't recomment: PEGI 16 / USK 16.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The Rusty Lake series is a lesser known gem. The past within is a two player escape room esque game and it was super fun, with just a hint of creepy. The story was fairly easy to put together, especially if you've played other games before. It only currently has a few versions that are unique, but I love to replay them anyways. 10/10 would mutate flesh again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I are huge fans of the Rusty Lake games and we were anticipating this release.This was a different experience for us to try since normally I would play and she would sit next to me and watch/do the puzzles. Wish the game was longer but the sale price was very generous (40% off), definitely felt like I got my money's worth considering I haven't played 'The Past' portion of the game yet.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It is a very fun and enjoyable game, I really like the way the puzzles were created and that our computers weren't connected but was made so no one can progress without the help of the other. Me and my good friend had a great time solving the puzzles, it wasn't too hard but you still had to think and communicate well to help each other! I will def play the BEE the next time! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. The puzzles were tricky but nothing some good teamwork can solve. As its a co-op, the time you play will depend on the skill of both you and your teammate. As of release the discord is super active so there are lots of people looking to play. Very much like "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes" and "We Were Here" but with its only creepy spin. Overall: A solid addition to the Rusty Lake series even if this version doesn't give up as much "story" as previous games. Play it if you love escape rooms, co-op puzzles, and playing with people.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A co-op experiment from Rusty Lake. Always solid art (and 3D for the first time!) and sound effects. However, the puzzles are way simpler than any other titles from Rusty Lake.This title is a spin-off so no need to have previous experience with the Rusty Lake franchise, although it is desirable to play Rusty Lake: Roots first to better grasp the (very light) story.The Past Within is also a co-op only experience. However, you can also open two windows at the same time and play it alone. Two players have asymmetrical roles and views. So after your first playthrough, which will last around 1 or 2 hours, you may want to play a second time in another role.All in all, I recommend this title, even for newcomers to Rusty Lake or fans who only want solo gameplay. I also suggest trying the demo first, which is a short (around 15 minutes) but faithful and independent demonstration of the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I've discovered Rusty lake games when I was younger and became obsessed with the games! I think I completed almost all the free ones available at the time on play store in a span of a week once on summer holidays, afterwar that I kind of forgot about them, olnly occasionally checking if there were any new free games released.   Tpw made me gain my interest back! :] I saw through twitter that a new co-op game was going to get released and immediately texted my friend about it, they weren't as much of a fan as me when we were in school, but tpw got them really exited!  I love how there are 2 paths, each having their own answers to the puzzles, so each of the 2 players could experience both the past and the future! The puzzles weren't nether too hard, nor to easy.   The best thing about playing with my friend was having the same reactions to the same things and getting a little stuck on the same puzzles, which we shared some good laughs about. :> I also had a lot of fun collecting achievements. (We're planning to play tpw again to collect all of them >:] )  This is one of my favourite games atm, it's very fun and overall is a really great game, 10/10, would recommend. (I'm actually planning to gift it to two of my other friends, so that's a fun fact)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game is passable to kill an hour or two with someone you like and want an excuse to interact with. That's about it. The "puzzles" basically amount to extremely simple exchanges of code inputs. It's very similar to Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, except there's no element of garbling the information with tricky ambiguity, so you don't even need to be clever or thoughtful in how you communicate. You and your partner could be extremely drunk and blow through this game. It's intellectually unrewarding. I've followed Rusty Lake games from the beginning and played all of them. This one disappointed me and I didn't feel it was worth the money. The surrealist horror aspect was weak. I don't mind boring puzzle design if the imagery/events are sufficiently bizarre and exciting, but this was underwhelming. The plot was also quite vague and unsatisfying.In my opinion, this game just functions as an easy vehicle for engaging with a friend and providing a sense of intrigue, and the experience can be pretty enjoyable in that regard. But the game itself beyond the co-op aspect isn't challenging or memorable. I hate to give a Rusty Lake game a negative review, but this just felt like a subpar entry in the series.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a cooperative point & click adventure, where the 2 players stuck in two different point of time. The players need to help each other by finding clues, which are the keys for the solution of the other player. Unfortunately these clues are really on the nose without any real encryption, so the puzzles doesn't requere substantial thinking. It is the easiest episode in the series.The atmoshphere much less disturbing then in the previous games and doesn't contains a great deal of lore but still have some Rusty Lake charm.In my opinion it is the weakest Rusty Lake game, but I still enjoyed it. If you like the series and you have friend who does the same it is much fun easy puzzle solving after a long day of work.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly well done! The art styles were so unique and stunning, and the game play was even better! This is the only game I've ever played where a friend and I played together without having the games connected in any way, no shared lobby or anything, which was very impressive! The puzzles were fun and challenging, nothing was too repetitive or too difficult (but it wasn't super easy either!). The whole time playing, we both kept saying how cool and interesting, and quite creepy, yet intriguing it was! We're looking forward to playing through it at least 3 more times since you can choose virtually 4 fully unique perspectives/puzzle combinations! We also weren't expecting to get to play for as long as we did, there was so much content! Would highly recommend to anyone looking for a great puzzle co-op game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: since this one ventured onto 3D for a while i would love to see my character walk around and solving bizarre puzzles while holding a pot of hot soupi have one critique though, regarding the : i would like it if I didn't need to bother my friend every time a new one comes out that requires playing through the game until i reach the necessary input area. i doubt there's something that can be done about it now, since i'm guessing they're all programmed in and the streams scheduled, but well. yea
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: If you love puzzle games and co-op games, this is a good one. You and a friend will each have your own screen and solve the puzzles without looking at each others screen (unless you really need too). It's one of my favorites, my friend and I have replayed this about 5 times already. It's not crazy easy, but also not difficult that you should have to google any walk throughs. Waiting for them to release more games like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME IS SO GOOD OH MY GOD. My friend and I went into this as blind as possible, and we had a great time. I don't want to say much about the actual details, but suffice to say, this was an excellent addition to the Rusty Lake series. Spooky, unsettling, but also really incredibly satisfying with each further step completed. We plan on playing again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: [edit] I regret paying full price for this game after the devs made it harder to open two instances of the game on the same computer. You are known and loved for your single-player puzzle games; why would you make it harder for people to enjoy your product in the way of their choosing? [/edit]Despite the dev team's discouragement, I soloed the game with the help of VirtualBox. The first run took me about 1,5 hours, and the second one was a bit faster.The game's design is refreshing and something I haven't seen before. I really enjoyed hacking away at a little puzzle box that opened up one slot at a time, and also liked the illusion of communication between past and future Rose. Had this game been a solo experience with a button to switch between the characters, it probably would have lost some of its charm.The puzzles are very easy for Rusty Lake veterans, but may appeal to newer players.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like following directions? Do you like using your words to communicate pictures? If so, this is absolutely perfect. However, I hesitate to call this a puzzle game. This game required no critical thinking and... it's not that deep. I was pretty disappointed with the experience. I love the concept of low tech co-op, but not this execution. It took two hours to finish but would have taken forty minutes with no "puzzle" repeats.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a fun experience, so much better than I was expecting for the price (50% off Sale). Puzzles weren't too hard, though a few took us a short while to understand. The way the game and puzzles worked of the other person without actually being in the same game was genus. Definitely worth checking out if want a fun short co-op puzzle game, though one thing I will mention is there's a little bit of creepiness in there
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A little bit too easy. There is not much challenge here as you and the other player are held by hand and even told what to transmit to other person. There is no actual puzzle inside as every 'puzzle' this game offers comes with a solution known by your partner.However the idea is very promising and the game really makes you talk to your partner (but I really wish it would more of a brainstorming rather than passing solutions) and this could serve as an entry point for non-gamers.Overall I had two pleasant evenings with The Past Within so I recommend it but probably buy it on sale :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great way to kill time if you have nothing to do, but I won't  say that it is so interesting that I wanna play it more than once and recommend this to my friends.First, I don't think it's as good as previous games in rusty lake series. The ending is not well told to let me understand the thesis, especially for my friend, a new player for this series, who totally got lost in the sudden ending. You should know although most of us have played this series before, we must call our friend, who probably hasn't played the games before, for this one. At least explain the ending for us.Second, it's true that the communication during the game is fun enough to strengthen the bond of friendship, but I don't think the solving process is funny. I mean, most of them do not meet my expectation. Nothing new. So maybe you need to focus more on the innovation of puzzles, but not the way we play.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Great co-op puzzle game. Heads up - both players need to own the game, but it's fairly cheap so that's a bonus. Well worth the price for the couple hours we put into the game. There was way more to the game than I was expecting, both in terms of the puzzles and the story. It's a puzzle game so if you get stuck remember there are walkthroughs online. Would absolutely recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game play concept! It is the perfect game to play with your partner. Not as difficult as other Rusty Lake games, which may be a pro or con depending on your puzzle game skill level.Critique: This is the third Rusty Lake game I've played and the characters are no longer interesting to me. The concept of the same characters in multiple games might be appealing to some (as it was to me at first), but it now seems a bit tired or even lazy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of all Rusty Lake's games. My daughters love to watch me play and help me solve the puzzles (they're both under 12). When I saw that the Past Within was a co-op I immediately bought a copy for my daughters to play with me (they share a steam account). It took us 2 hrs to get through it. We played at night, in different rooms of the house, and it was a little scary for them; but, just enough that they still enjoyed the whole game and weren't too scared to play. It was perfect for us as a family and not difficult at all for my young kids. We loved discovering clues to help each other. 2 hrs was the perfect amount of time for us.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet experience.Took us a little under 2 hours to beat the game for the first time. There's still the possibility to swap roles for a second playthrough to get more out of it.The story is okay, and in combination with some of the puzzles occationally gave me the creeps. The puzzles are more on the easier side compared to other games of the genre but that resulted in quite a pleasant flow of progressing the game. If you're looking for some really tough brainteasers to solve, look elsewhere though.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I only have praises for every single Rusty Lake game. I always buy them blindly immediately upon release. The Past Within is no exception. If you're familiar with this series, this game introduces 2 basic new features:1) Co-op: yes, co-op, which is pretty amazing. It plays kind of like the We Were Here series or even more like Tick Tock: A Tale for Two, where there is actually no real-time connection between the games. It's not anything new, but it's certainly more thrilling to have that kind of intimate, 2-player experience immersed in the Rusty Lake Universe.2) 3D graphics: the game mixes the past and the future, in 2D and 3D, respectively, and the newly added 3D graphics are just gorgeous.Now, apart from the main story line and its respective achievements, the game also hides some additional Easter-egg kind of thing which have been slowly revealed with clues on their YouTube channel and with the collaboration of a very committed community on their Discord server, where you can also find a partner to play the game with if you don't have one (cos, yes, this game was not designed to be played alone).All in all, great experience, as usual, and well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... Me and my friend just bet this game together and I am stunned. This game is perfect for someone who is looking for a good puzzle game. A few things to note:This game is NOT singleplayer.This game does NOT need internet to play.Communication is needed to complete this game.The past within is such a refreshing game to play with a good friend. Soundtrack is lovely and the graphics are really nice. This game has 2d and 3d levels and multiple endings (depending on what side you choose to play on) I only wish more games could be made at the same quality of this game!P.SShow some love and vote this for best game with friends for 2022 game nominations!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Good and fun puzzle game to play with someone you have good teamwork with, and it has an interesting story and lore behind it.The puzzles aren't extremely hard, although i just wish there were more stories because it was very fun and i'd like to play it more.I got this game from my bf and we had a great time solving the puzzles, i'd definitely recommend this game if you have someone that you can work together with to play with :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Truly incredible concept for a co-op game. I loved how interactive the game was and how much you and the other player really had to work together to solve the puzzles. It was really cool how when you move on to chapter 2, the way you play the game gets kind of switched. It wasn't too difficult and was a really fun experience. Although I plan to play this creators single player games, I really hope they continue to make co-op games in this style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: found this game on tiktok of all places, and what a pleasant surprise it was!! this is a truly unique co-op experience unlike most typical puzzle-type games; while it can be short, there is loads of replayability with this one. my friend and i finished the butterfly route in just under 2 hours, and we plan on checking out the bee and switching perspectives at a later date.well worth the $6! definitely planning on checking out other games from rusty lake after this one
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's such an awesome game to play with your friend/family member/significant other! Its not really about puzzles but more about communication. So if you want a game where you can have every day conversations this is not for you, since all youll be talking about is what the other person has to do. Its a very fun bonding experience! It also has to different modes so both of the people can play the past/future which means both get to experience it from both sides. It also has quite the few horror aspects. Not really jumpscares but if you get the scare quite easily (just like me fella) you will jump a few times which makes it even more interesting since you never know what to expect. Overall its just such an amazing game for escape-game enjoyers and a good bonding opportunity. We really had fun playing this game but its not over yet! I really really recommend this game. Yes, of course, for that price you cant expect THAT long of a game but the average 3h is still a good time. Have fun playing!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great co-op puzzle game! A friend and I played through it in about 2 hours with the possibility to play it again in a new and fresh way if we want. It's was challenging enough without ever being frustrating or confusing. Great art style, a bit spooky and mysterious to keep you moving. Would love more like this!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with my Nephew, It really got our brains working. He is new to Rusty Lake but I have played every Rusty Lake game and must admit, I wishlisted this and bought straight away without realising it was co-op, This game is as good as ever with the added interest of being co-op and it's replayable with different options.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game because I love team games, but this is just extremely slow paced and I'm falling asleep playing this. Half the time I'm sitting here doing nothing waiting for my teammate (I'm playing future). Not sure if there is an imbalance of activities in past vs future, but there needs to be a way to keep the other person occupied if they are waiting on their teammate.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite good for its price, the atmosphere manages to immerse you in the game, while you cooperate with your partner. This got to the point in which my partner prompted me to "look around, see if anything has changed since he touched something"... to which I reminded him that "this game has no actual multiplayer capabilities".Any game that manages to fool its players into thinking that it does something it actually doesn't should be highly regarded in my opinion, and this one does just exactly that.My biggest complains:- Perhaps we need to play additional games, but we were kinda dissatisfied with the ending, since we couldn't really make any sense of the story, feels like the game was lacking a chapter 3 or maybe as if we need to play other games to understand anything, which is a shame since initially the way the story was going piqued our curiosity really fast. - (Kind of as expected, since its a simple coop game) There's really no replayability at all, all of the good points this game manages to convey to its players (all the "magical moments" in which two players cooperate as if there was a real multiplayer connection and the likes) just disappear when you try to replay the game. The game kinda makes you think that you can replay it by playing as either the past or the future, which kinda works but takes a lot of the coop magic away really... and that you can replay it again by choosing among two symbols (bee or butterfly) but we have seen little to no changes from playing butterfly or bee? the solutions to most of the puzzles seemed very similar.All in all, highly recommended in general, just a shame we coouldn't make any sense of the story but the coop puzzles are well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Not really my thing for one specific reason, otherwise it's an OK game.  The co-op puzzles were not extremely easy but really weren't difficult.  About 2hrs of play in total, but I was turned off by the   I only finished this because of a friend who wanted to play - otherwise I would have checked out when they started
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. I've played all the other games and really appreciate the devs' continued experimentation with format, which keeps things fresh and exciting. Their devblogs alluded to the unexpected challenges posed by the two-player format, and it was really interesting seeing how they attempted to overcome these challenges -- like, how do you have a two-player game that doesn't require both players to be playing on the same platform? I hope they keep sharing their process. For anyone new to the Rusty Lake series, I'd recommend something more like Rusty Lake: Paradox to start, followed by Rusty Lake: Roots to get a broader sense of the story, but my bf enjoyed the game without having played any previous game :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game is designed extremely well. Past and Future players sync the game with in-game cues rather than having to connect via the internet, but it's easy to forget that while playing because the experience is so cohesive. My partner and I got stuck once or twice, but our level of communication was more to blame than anything to do with the game. It was spooky and fun, and I very much enjoyed the way the atmosphere created a sense of urgency without actually having many timed puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I guess the game description was mostly accurate. This is a game where you "observe and communicate what you see around you". But that's all you do. There aren't any real "puzzles", as the game claims: no riddles, nothing truly hidden, nothing that will make you think. My friend and I didn't have a bad time, but we had about as much fun as you can have describing a picture to someone else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game was one of the most boring experiences I've ever had. It feels like it was designed for young children. The puzzles were far too easy and often became repetitive. The story felt lazy, with no real depth and senseless. The slight horror/thriller element had potential, but it wasn’t explored enough. It was mildly creepy at the start, which I appreciated, but as the game progressed, it quickly lost its charm and became dull and nonsensical...
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start by saying I love puzzle/horror/mystery games. I played this game with my boyfriend in the same room without peeking at each others screens. (tried really hard not to) The puzzles were fine I guess but there were times where we both looked at each other and thought the other one should do something for us to make progress within the game. The story and the horror parts were not flattering I didn't understand or didn't want to believe that the game has ended because it felt like the story was still not complete. Since it felt like the story was absent I think the horror part was unnecessarily too much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Honeslty this game is a big NO. I don't know how to classify it, I want to recommend it - no. The only things I can say is “if you really want, buy it in discount, please” because otherwhise is not worth it at all.Starting with the price, 6€ for this is just too much, considering that a team requires 2 copies... just no.The gameplay is one hour or a bit more, and techically what in my opinion takes more time is the coop mechanics, since the communication is infinitely long.I personally choose to play it all by myself, yes, alone, (following some steam guide) because for me this type of coop is a big NO.I'm not againist coop, I'm againist at how Devs implement it in this game for three reasons:That's all the game. Player A watch the screen waiting that player B do the cool stuff. That's boring.... (and unfair)Above the coop, the enigms are easy and repetetive, main part of the game is repeat same actions, write tons of codes with letters or colored arrows, and none of them is actual challenging, speaking about challenges like we had in games like Roots (where the last enigm is somehow a mistery to me) or Paradise or The cave, or and specially Paradox. ENGINEAnother thing that makes the Devs proud is the waited change of engine, switching from Flash to Unity, but to be honest the difference to me is minimal. Unity is an engine that can do wonderful things if used correctly, I see games that implemented a real phisic or build and entire planet, here the “great” change is that we have a 3D box and we can use mouse wheel for go back.... Sorry, for me is no difference at all, learn to programm in Unity, please.Also, the Room made a better management using the right mouse for the “go back” movement, that, for me, is better to do. Speaking of the Room, I think it was their inital plan do something like this iconic game, but miserable failed. The Room keep the interest on the box extremely hight for full time. Here the Cubic Device is boring, sorry but true, also 40% of times the “great” 3D box bug and I have troble to move the Device....Letting me trying to resurrect it by clicking everywhere or restarting the game (that this will make you lost the progress if you play in singleplayer)Everything have great potential, but nothing is real developed. The story is new, and as always innovative, the cube inside the cube, memory in the memory blow my mind, I cannot lie, and it's very interesting topic, also Albert is one of my favourite character in-game, so I'm happy I had the opportunity to have some more infos, but even they story can be improved. Of all the gameplay, we not have much info to theorize, that's the best part of the game. Above the gameplay, the enigms, the mechanics, the negine, the coop, what should stay in the mind is this wonderful story, that here is good, is very good, but 70% developed, in my opinion.Little side note, I choose to keep and not refound the game, for the achievements, but to be honest, is not a so good choice, the achivements, that I wanted to proudly showcase on my profile are just black and white undistinguishible scribbles... All other games have the matching achievements in color and frame, here not.... WHY?Also thanks for let me spend €3,59 without giving me a single bagde. WHY?Why everything in this game is just so poorly developed, I dont' understand... 2,5 years for this...I've lost part of my faith in you, Rusty Lake.For end, I'm sorry Rusty Lake, this game is a big flop for me, and if I can use a Golden Cube I would go back in time and don't buy this game again, at this state is not worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I believe I am a true fan of this game. When I saw this new game, I was so excited and couldn't wait for it to come out. Finally the awaited moment! I just finished the game and it was really great. Congratulations to everyone who contributed. I got stuck in some parts ahahah I definitely recommend you to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a creative and fun puzzle game for two. For just a few dollars, this is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice game to play with your spouse or friend but way too short. We had fun at the first run and spent like 2 hours but further playthroughs weren't too enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: its a really fun game to play with a friend! i had been waiting for months to play TPW with my friend and when we finally did, it was superrr engaging and fun! _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately short and a tad bit easier than the Rusty Lake games of the past but I really hope they start doing more of these in co op.  My friend and I have been playing through their games co op for a few years now so it's a nice change of pass to see one that actually supports co op instead of two full grown men yelling at a 1-person puzzle game.The puzzles slightly change each play through (some change on each failure!!) so you can technically replay it on the side you chose or have your partner pick on the other side but we kind of over shared what was going on on our screens just in case we were looking for the next "to do" thing so I won't be replaying the game. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Before reading this, know that I just learned of a new scam. People are playing this game and then pretending to only have the lite/demo version. If that's true, you shouldn't be able to finish the game with them. I finished the game with someone who still made that claim. They then asked for my Steam info so they could download the game and then give control back to me. I wasn't born yesterday, so I said no. But people should know that this game is being used as part of a scam.I love this franchise, so I hate leaving this review. For that reason, I'll start by saying this. If you're just a total Rusty Lake junkie, this game does include one story element that you might really enjoy.By every other metric, however, it's terrible. Since it wants to pretend it's a co-op game, let's start with that.If you play this game as intended, you're in for a rough time. It's great that Rusty Lake has an international fanbase. You know when that's not great, however? When you're relying on someone who speaks limited English to yell symbols at you on a timed puzzle. One of those players only has to relate basic images. The other has to relate abstract symbols. Between two people who speak the same language, that'll still go over without much drama. But if you have to use the Discord to find another player, you're almost guaranteed to be stuck with someone who struggles to describe these symbols. And this happens about 75% of the way through the game, so you might have communicated fine until this. It's only because this one puzzle is randomly timed that it slows your progress to a halt.So why won't communication hurt you outside of this one puzzle? Because putting language barriers on a timer is the only thing that makes it challenging. There's no challenge to any other puzzle in the game. You do some basic point and click until you uncover a code. Then you read that code to your partner. They put in that code and then they're given a code to read back to you. This happens repeatedly. There's very little puzzle differentiation in the game. You'll wind up dealing with the same three puzzles a couple dozen times, while reading back the same couple dozen to your partner. I don't mean there are dozens of puzzles. I mean there are dozens of instances where you read off the same 2 or 3. The game might be less than half as long if not for this repetition.The idea of a co-op Rusty Lake game is nice. But this was not the right execution. It's never difficult and needing help from others never feels like a clever mechanic. It's more of a frustration than anything. The way this plays into the story is kind of neat, but it does so little now that Underground Blossom is behind us that I almost wonder if they shouldn't just kill Rusty Lake and start over with a new story.Oh, and the one thing I left out. My play time would be shorter if not for the glitches. Looking for the bee? Sometimes it just glitches out and doesn't land where you need for the achievement. Playing with a partner? Sometimes their future cube glitches out and the screen won't move forward when they hit enter. Since your games aren't even technically connected, it'll probably take you quite a while to realize their game is glitched. Then you have to wait for them to back out and come back in so they can tell you some things that don't make sense. I waited for my partner to come back so he could tell me that we needed to click a cube at the same time. Spoiler alert, you don't. Click the cube whenever you want. Your progress does not rely on your partner. That entire aspect of the game is a lie. Not sure why no one realizes this. There's even an achievement guide on this site that doesn't realize how little it matters what your partner is doing.I wanted to like this game. It's just not very likable. And sorry for breaking away from the fandom, but it feels necessary. If you really care about these games, then allowing them to release a glitchy mess with broken time constraints is exactly what they deserve. Hold them accountable to make better games. A few good ones doesn't justify this kind of backslide.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so beautiful in a Rusty Lake kind of way. The co-op aspect of it makes it so you HAVE to communicate and work together to proceed to the next task. There are parts that make you somewhat stressed because it makes it seem like you're running out of time. Communication, keeping calm and explaining what you see and what you are currently doing is key to this game all together.The game is so much fun, and if you like Rusty Lake games, and have played the previous ones, you're gonna love this.If you're not familiar with the previous games, and know nothing of the backstory surrounding the characters, timelines, places or nothing, the game is not going to make a lot of sence.The ending makes sence and it makes you feel like you want more. Then again, the feeling of wanting more out of it makes it feel like it's not finished. My first reaction was "is that it?", but it honestly doesn't need any greater ending. You get there, you do the objective of the game, and that's it. The feeling of wanting more just makes it so that the developers can add onto the story line, make up for more unsolved mysteries and more content for us to enjoy!I really do recommend playing through both the past and the future with the same partner.There are objectives to be found both with bee and with butterfly, and if you want to achievement hunt, settle for playing through it at least 4 times in total. 2 times in the past and 2 times in the future. Once as bee and once as butterfly.The objectives will stay the same, but the solutions change from each time. You will not be able to write down the solutions from an older play through, and use it to play alone in the next. Either way, this game is so fun with the communication aspect of it, that you would not want to play it alone.In conclution; it's a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game, does exactly what it says on the tin. Fun to play with partners or friends. I do have to say; the game got scarier than i expected. Fine for me, but maybe for parents with children this is good to know... it's kinda creepy and dark.Feedback for devs:Repetative puzzles with sequences feel a bit cheap. i get that you need a way to verify and sync players. but having me do the same thing over and over was a bit boring (i'm talking about a certain alphabetical and numerical sequence)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I very interesting new concept for the franchise.I have played every Rusty Lake game, and this game fits right in with the others. The atmosphere is just as creepy and bizarre (especially in The Past) and the "plot" now raises more questions as to how the story of the franchise plays out. The only downside is that the puzzles are mostly giving information to the other player, and does not make you think as much as other games. Still, it was fun hearing my friend get scared of the corrupted soul wandering around.I highly recommend playing all their games, they are certainly a ride.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: the puzzles were kinda of easy tbh,  if we toke any time with any of the puzzles was because of miscommunication or that one of us had not find the puzzle slot.brilliant story with a amazing telling but you probably have to play it more than once or see a youtube video explain it.you may see that its just a 2 hour game but there is four ways to play it between choosing the future os the past, and choosing between two modes which are butterfly or the bee mode and you can even replay it just for the story.one of the best co-op games i have ever played 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I didn't like the forced 2-player aspect of the game.  Then I actually tried it.....and it's SO GOOD!!!  You and your teammate have to work together to help Rose with her plan, and it's so awesome to play it with different people each time!  I'm actually trying to help people on the Discord who ask for another player and play it with them....despite that I've played it enough to nearly memorize it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: There's no challenge at all, it's more like a communication game than puzzle.Also the story doesn't make sense if you are expecting something interesting.I would recommend for people who just want to play a game with a friend and don't expect much.If you are like me, you hope to have a unique experience and hoping to have an interesting driven story, I wouldn't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty good! It reminds me of Tick Tock a Tale for Two. It's not too difficult, basically you will each give other instructions on what to do. You just need to communicate clearly. You might find some difficulty in matching what they explain with what you have in front of you. But the game is rather entertaining and mysterious enough to keep things interesting.There is also a mode to make things replayable a second time, from the other perspective, which is a big plus.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Rusty Lake's The Past Within is a unique co-op escape room game that cleverly divides the gameplay between two players. With one in the Past and the other in the Future, communication is key to solving the puzzles and progressing through the story. The game's eerie atmosphere and unsettling motifs add to its charm, though it may be more appreciated by fans familiar with the Rusty Lake series. The asynchronous puzzle system is ingeniously designed, requiring players to relay information and coordinate their actions. While the game occasionally slows down when waiting for the other player, the overall experience is delightful and enjoyable. The Past Within offers a cozy and immersive co-op adventure that will appeal to escape room enthusiasts and Rusty Lake fans alike.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. Go into this game as blindly as possible. It is pretty easy so don't expect to solve sherlock level puzzles. its not too long so you can easily play through one of the two variants of the story in a single evening. I like the artstyle and the game as a whole is designed pretty cleverly.Also for this price, even if it isn't discounted, is just a great deal. Plus you support a self publishing indie company.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: i played the first part till now and i'm not amazed... im a huge fan of Rusty Lake but lately i feel they use more power on 3d and stuff than on the puzzles. i loved everything about their first games, the graphics, puzzles, stories, except the two last ones. im definitely gonna play the second part too, but unfortunately i cant recommend it, it doesn't feel anymore like an actual rusty lake game :(:(
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for cool games to play together with my GF and then i found this little gem of a game and decided to try it, so i played this game with her and we had a lot of fun solving the puzzles and getting scared at times by certain events within the game.I have to say that it was a bit short and replayablity is not that great, because you can see what the other player is doing or at least, understand what he/she is seeing, but for 4eur (the price when i bought it) it was worth the price and fun that we got out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fine Coop communication game, but there are no puzzles here. Nothing ever needs to be "solved", its just a back and forth of one person see the solution and communicates it to the other person.Also, the concept of a coop game with one person in the past and one in the future sounds great, but just like in Timeless Child, that concept is thrown out the window. With two way communication the time difference is just a plot point and have no impact on the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little communication game, kinda like "Keep Talking" but without the stress of a bomb about to blow up. Puzzles aren't really that hard at all, but the challenge lies in recognizing and relaying information that your partner may need to solve any blocks on their side. Solving these together is actually quite satisfying.A single play-through takes about 2-3h, and you can re-do it as each players side has challenges of its own that are unique to their side, so there is some replay value to be had at least for a second play-through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Rusty Lake fan you will enjoy this game. It's a bit short, but it does offer enough replayability for at least 2 playthroughs. So maybe ~3 hours of entertainment.The real genius of this game is that it's a completely offline co-op game. They figured out how to do a multiplayer game with no netcode, and it works great. It's simple, but functional, and makes it very easy to play.We had fun on our first playthrough and plan to do a second.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Rusty Lake games in a while! Coming at this as a series regular, it has a lot of fun tie backs while still being its own thing. The co-op is pretty fun, but the method of it doesn't require an internet connection. Also includes two sets of puzzles so you can play both sides with different answers! ou can also theoretically play on your own to fill out the achievements if you just have a guide for the other side.A couple puzzles are a little unclear, but otherwise really solid.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game since before the demo was released.  I played the demo well over a dozen times and loved it.  The full version didn't disappoint.  Kudos to the Rusty Lake team for another awesome game.  I still have to play the butterfly version, and am looking forward to it.  I definitely recommend this to anyone who likes dark themed puzzle games with an ongoing story line.  I played both parts on my own by also buying the mobile version, so not having a partner, and not being able to get on Discord doesn't mean this game can't be enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Great little two player game. We loved their previous release (Tick Tock a tale for Two) so got this as soon as it came out. Would be really cool if the second person could get this for free rather than having to purchase twice though. A single playthrough took us 3hrs but we're going to replay the opposite selection but after that this has no replay value
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed the game, i was a bit disapointed it only took 2 hours to complete especially since i have been waiting about a year for this game, but $5 on discount is none too bad.It is very inspired by Tick Tock a tale for two. so if you enjoyed that, you will enjoy this.The 3d effects still looked in the rusty lake style which was really good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned that the difficulty of this game comes primarily from the difficulty of communicating.If you're both familiar with puzzle games and good at conveying visual information, you'll probably finish the whole game in about 90 minutes.It's a fun game, I just wish it were longer... which isn't the worst complaint to have, I guess.At a discount, I recommend it. I enjoyed the time I spent on it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible addition to the Rusty Lake series!! The art is absolutely amazing, especially in part 2, and it's eerie and puzzling in the best way. I played it with my best friend - we're both obsessed with the games and usually play them at the same time on Facetime, so I'm SO happy for a co-op we can actually do together!!!! Amazing work as always :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: There's another co-op puzzle series out there called We Were Here that has a pretty similar set up to this.  It feels a lot less polished than this and perhaps even incomplete, but it does understand how to make the idea a bit more challenging.  In The Past Within every puzzle in exactly the same.  One person finds a code, which is always right in front of their face, then relates it to the other person who then inserts it into the only place on their screen the code could possibly go.  then they repeat this 3 to 5 times (I suppose to prove that the person has actually done it and not just guessed?) and then maybe some little things happens like a jump scare or plot development and then the process repeats.The big problem is that you're never asked to figure out a puzzle together.  And, of course that there's only even one code and one entry station at a time so there's never any question about what you should do next.  There are escape room games that do this quite a bit better, and even in We Were Here, which was very similar, at least there was some difficulty in thinking about how to relate what you were looking at to your partner.  Here it's "Z3X1Y2" or "bee, person, house".  The one section where this game starts to come alive at all is in a section toward the end where you relate the codes under the threat of timer, only then do you feel that you and your partner are actually working together on the same thing.The story is a lot more obvious than in the Cube Escape games, and it doesn't appear to me to expand the universe in any way.  I guess if I were you, I'd skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a unique adventure game that combines elements of puzzle-solving and storytelling in a charming, hand-drawn world. It is a co-op only game designed for two players to connect and communicate while exploring, with an emphasis on mutual collaboration and creativity. You take on the roles of two characters separated by time, which adds an intriguing twist to the gameplay.It's weird considering that I seldom play co-op games, yet this one in particular grabbed my attention. I loved how the game encourages teamwork where you share clues and personal insights to solve puzzles together, allowing for engaging conversations with a friend. The narrative can be philosophical, with moments that make us reflect on the choices made.While some puzzles were a bit challenging, they were satisfying to solve. I have few complaints and enjoyed the short experience, though the pacing felt slow at times, testing our patience and problem-solving skills. The game can be replayed once by swapping roles and selecting a different option at the beginning of the game (butterfly or bee). This choice will swap all puzzles for a new playthrough.

Not a lot of achievements.Entertainment value : 2 points : Played the game with a friend and we had a great time. I really enjoyed the different storylines and "perpectives". I might be a bit biaised on that scoring because I love the series.TL.DR : 7.5/10A very short, but very cool moment. Fans of the serie will feel right at home and enjoy seeing familiar faces. For the non fans, you will find a nice little co-op game for a nice little price. And I hope it will make you want to dive into the rusty lake universe.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider a neutral review, leaning positive.I've played many of the Cube Escape/Rusty Lake games, and consider myself a fan of the series. The co-op conceit here is very clever, especially taking into account that there is no connection between the two game clients. However, I think it may have been too limiting on puzzle design, as the puzzles got repetitive by the end. It felt like playing an early Cube Escape or The Room game (depending on the chapter) that gets interrupted by a round of Keep Talking or Nobody Explodes or Spaceteam. For me, the most successful element of the game is how the Rusty Lake style was translated into 3D, even if it's just a taste. I hope they explore that dimension (ha) more in future Rusty Lake games.My playtime as of this review is a full runthrough of the game. I played in The Past. I will probably replay it to check out The Future/play with my partner now that I know The Past isn't too spooky for her. Altogether, it's not a bad way to spend a spooky fall evening with a friend or loved one for a few bucks. I just wouldn't expect anything so mind-blowing as some of the reviews I've seen have said.

_childDocuments_.review: The past and future collide.Story:You play as two characters, one of them being Rose Vanderboom. One of you is in the past and the other in the future and your father Albert has left instructions on how to make a connection between two different years and another sinister instruction and so you set out to make his wish into a reality. The story is very minimal in The Past Within, there's definitely a little bit more added lore to the Rusty Lake series. but this time around it's a lot more gameplay focused. I did like what's here, there's some genuinely good story advancements and I'm really excited to see where the next game in the series will go next.Graphics:Visually The Past Within also tries something new just like The White Door did and this time around Rusty Lake goes 3D. There's still the same 2D segments designed the same way they were in in the other games in the series. And generally the style is just as good as it ever was, however this time around it's a little less surreal.The 3D environments however are amazing. I genuinely loved how great the world of Rusty Lake translated into 3D and seeing some of the visuals that you kept looking at throughout the franchise in fluid 3D was quite the trip and I definitely loved how the unique atmosphere each side gets. Audio:The audio design is generally pretty good and the issues of the franchise like audio crunch has gone away with this entry. There's some decent background music that's not intrusive when trying to communicate with your partner. It's actually very nice and does add to the creepy atmosphere even further.There's some other sound effects, but generally they're either taken from the other games or so minor that they're not really worth talking about. It's made to be as less annoying on the ears as possible to make it easier to communicate which is nice, but when do you hear sound effects they're pretty decent.Gameplay:In the past, the Rusty Lake games were single player experiences where you solved puzzles all by your lonesome, however this time around you're bringing a friend into the nightmarish world of the Lake to help you out with the puzzles. There's still the standard type of puzzles you'll have to solve yourself, but a lot of the game is designed to be tackled with a partner. So let's begin with the puzzles. Rusty Lake games have often been very complex and had their surreal nature bleed into it. The Past Within puzzles are a lot more streamlined and much more simple than anything the franchise ever had. This was probably done to make it much easier to describe to player and honestly while the puzzles were much easier, they were still a great time.The puzzles themselves are probably the biggest negative the game has about it. It's pretty easy overall as you pick up what you need to do almost straight away with only a few puzzles having a stump in difficulty and even then the solution for them is basically a massive hint, you just need to find where to use it.Also it's quite great that this game technically can be played up to 4 times per side as there's two different puzzle settings and then the past and the future which amounts to a decent amount of play value with a single playthrough taking up to 2 hours, so you can really maximize how much you and your friend get out of the title.Also quite a lot of the jank the series used to have is also gone and is a lot more refined. I really hope that the series uses this engine going forward as this generally felt like the most fluid Rusty Lake game to date and I really liked more advanced gameplay. Verdict:The Past Within is a great addition to the Rusty Lake series and a brilliant co-op experience if you and your friend likes puzzle games. While it's a bit too easy than the other games in the series and has some weak design choices, it's yet another worthy trip to the Lake. Final Rating:9/10Pros:+ Visuals are a mix of old and new and mesh very well+ Some really fun puzzles+ Story has some interesting developments to the lore + Audio design is great and doesn't intrude when solving puzzlesCons:- A lot of the puzzles are too easy If you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: The enigmatic allure of this game eludes my understanding, given its seemingly pervasive popularity. Despite its acclaim, the puzzles embedded within the gameplay strike me as decidedly ordinary, lacking the complexity and ingenuity one might expect from a standout gaming experience. Moreover, the narrative arc, ostensibly a crucial aspect of any engaging game, disappoints with its failure to weave a compelling and coherent story. At a certain juncture, the plot takes a jarring turn into the realms of implausibility, detracting from the overall immersive experience that many players seek in such gaming endeavors.However, it is not entirely devoid of redeeming qualities. The collaborative aspect, where two players navigate the game from different temporal perspectives and issue commands to jointly tackle puzzles, introduces a unique and enjoyable dimension. This cooperative gameplay fosters a sense of shared accomplishment and strategic thinking, providing a noteworthy departure from the otherwise lackluster elements of the game. Nevertheless, this positive facet appears to stand in isolation, leaving the overarching gaming experience to be characterized by a notable lack of excitement and engagement. Regrettably, I am unable to endorse the recommendation of this game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A great co-op addition to the series with fascinating story implications. Trying to line up all of the information I had to all of the information my partner had could be frustrating, but extremely satisfying once we got the pieces into place. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The latest entry into the Rusty Lake franchise. The developers have done an amazing job as always and have nailed the co-op experience within their own style. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: My boyfriend's brother gifted this game for both of us and we loved it! Took us three hours to complete the game in both stories. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant game. Really requires communication and cooperation from both parties to work out the puzzles and progress through the game. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great little creepy puzzle game. I recently played this together with my partner and we both thoroughly enjoyed it. It's not a very story driven game, but it provides a creepy ambiance that keeps you feeling a bit uneasy throughout the game. It took us about an hour and a half to complete. The puzzles weren't incredibly difficult to solve, it is mostly about your ability to communicate and describe your surroundings. As I mentioned above, the atmosphere is a bit unsettling but there really aren't any jump scares. I'd definitely recommend this to anyone who enjoys a good creepy puzzle game. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Not much as a challenge compared to other rusty lake games, but still fun and with a unique take on the Puzzle genre, working together with a friend of yours in order to progress was actually fun. _childDocuments_.review: I do not write reviews for video games, but this one is quite special. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Played this with a friend. Very interesting and scary. The puzzles weren't too difficult which is good.The only thing, is that this game has two "modes". Butterfly and Bee. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Before purchasing this game, please note that it requires a partner to play with, and effective communication with them without the ability to see their screen. This review will be short and concise, just like the game is. The better you comunicate with your partner the shorter the game gets.Although the game explores some dark themes and possesses a deeper lore than initially apparent, it is not the primary focus of the game. The central gaming experience is centered on communication between partners and the ability of both players to articulate details about their surroundings, key interactive elements, and the overall situation. Playing this game with my wife, we occasionally found ourselves stuck because one of us overlooked or didn't consider certain information as crucial. These minor details, compounded by communication challenges, led to difficulties in progressing through specific parts—confirming the notion that 'the devil is in the detail.'The game presents players with four potential paths, categorized into time paths and path versions. In both the past and future timelines, there are two variations: version A featuring the bee and version B featuring the butterfly. This allows players to go through the game four times, each experience distinct from the others.It offers a highly enjoyable experience that challenges your ability to express yourself clearly and actively listen to your gaming partner. The game allows the player to explore it four times without repetition of puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I should probably preface this review by saying that I am a massive fan of the other Rusty Lake games. I was super excited for the release of Past Within, and I was not disappointed.Firstly, the multiplayer aspect is great, as is the cross-platform, and it's really nice to finally be able to play these games with other people. I love the combination of the classic art style with the 3D graphics, and the fact that you get to experience both whether you're playing through the Past or the Future is a really good feature, as is the Butterfly and Bee versions having different puzzle solutions. Both players get a full experience, and replaying the game from the other perspective is no less fresh or interesting.In terms of Past and Future, I found playing through the Future slightly easier than the Past, but overall the puzzles are intuitive, without being too easy. One thing that I had found in past games was that some solutions were a little too obscure, but that was not the case here. It was challenging, but I never found myself resorting to checking any walk-throughs for help.As always, the aesthetic, sound design and atmosphere were incredible, and I would 100% recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I have finished the second chapter!My feedback [Playing the past] : I will say that theres an overall creepier feel to playing in the past. For a small game, it keeps a very creepy atmosphere but not overly scary if that makes sense. The idea that you don't know whats going to happen but you can't die just keeps you at the edge of your seat. The puzzles were all very fun however sometimes it took a long time to understand or you may have to search stuff up. The overall story is really good and just made for a great game to play with someone. I wish it was longer but for being so short it has dearly touched my heart. Shoutout to everyone who made the game !!My boyfriends feedback [playing the future] : He says it was good, we'd both play it again, taking the bee side and switching sides! He was incredibly impressed with it for being such a small game. He did say that it wasn't as scary and felt a little bored when i was saying all this creepy stuff was happening. But overall he liked it.Overall: 5/5! Thanks for making a great game

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: As usual, Rusty Lake managed to deliver a game with the feeling of a chilling escape room.Despite the fact I purchased it the moment it came out, I was a little bit skeptical because I love their single player games (which may even count as co-op if you stream them, or play in the same room as friends), and I couldn't think of how a two player co-op could improve that experience.I was dead wrong.I am writing this review after only playing The Future in the Bee mode, and I fully plan on playing the other 3 leftover combinations, and even streaming them. It is beautifully balanced, so that no matter who is streaming/playing what, you both have time to be the one giving AND getting instructions. As a plus, there is no hassle with creating a party, or using Steam Co-op.It is wonderfully morbid, and stayed true to the spooky vibe of its predecessors, especially since this is Albert Vanderboom's story.My partner and I had an amazing time playing this, and we cannot wait to exhaust every single brilliant scenario that the developers never fail to deliver.Edit: Update - the Butterfly and the Bee mode feature identical gameplays, but different puzzle solutions. Still 100% worth it, loved playing all 4 combinations!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: My husband and I were searching for a good co-op (actually co-op - not competing against each other, and not something that was combat-based), and I'm deeply deeply into puzzle games. We found that this one was on the cheaper side and rated very well, so decided to give it a try. We both loved it.The story was outstanding. There were no jump-scares per say, but the atmosphere was definitely creepy and at some points I was a little freaked out, which I loved. The puzzles were absolutely 10/10 amazing for co-op, nothing ever got frustrating, and it just worked really well the way it's all laid out and designed. Absolutely worth the money and we WILL be playing it again with me in the other role/with the other insect, possibly doing it 2x more for all achievements. Absolutely outstanding and we both hope to see more co-op puzzle games like this from this developer.If you want a sort of comparison, it's a TINY bit like a simplified version of Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, but without a time limit/inherent danger. There is one timed puzzle but it's not that difficult and if you fail, you just start over. As far as we could tell, nothing can stop your progression permanently. It was super fun and engaging to communicate and have dual Eureka moments. Can't wait to run through it again!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

He knew nothing about the story but was still super into the puzzles. The visuals and music were 10/10 as always. My only *minor* complaint is the lack of content despite 4 different ways to play. Originally I played as The Past, my husband as The Future, and we chose the Butterfly. We had such a fun time we decided to keep our roles but choose the "Bee" path instead....unfortunately, almost nothing was different except for a few photos on the wall and the codes to input? _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the Rusty Lake games in general, read no further, this is more of the best of the series, grab it as soon as you have someone to play it with. You will need to remember some info from other games to fill out the achievements fully, so if you don't want to need to do an extra runthrough, maybe brush up on your Rusty Lake trivia (or searching skills). If you don't know the Rusty Lake series, check out the free entries in the series, see if it is your cup of tea, then apply that decision to this game. Either way, this is an unshared-screen co-op game where each of you receives different information, but that information needs to be applied in the other person's world. You don't need the games to be linked by data, but you do need the ability to talk (or type, but I recommend voice) to your partner. The replay value is two games (so you see both sides of it), plus maybe another couple of runs to finish out your achievements. Well worth it for six bucks, IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: The past within is a very enjoyable coop puzzle game that requires you to find the solution through communication. While you never have to actually connect to your friend you will be prompted at the beginning of the game to start the game together and choose the same path to sync up the solutions. This style of asymmetrical puzzle experience has been done before but this way of setting up the game is quite smart. The puzzles themselves are rewarding to put together but not never frustrating. I'd imagine this would be a good game to get someone into gaming as it can be played together even if the other person is using their phone. I really enjoyed the look of the game, it gives you a very foreboding feeling. It doesn't look like something you would be able to interact with so its neat when you get to do so. Id love to see more games that use this style in 3D spaces!Its also a fairly simple 100% aside from the "Squeak" achievement that gave me a little trouble. Going for the full completion is a fun way to see both sides of the game. Its well worth doing so even if your not into achievements.  If you need a fun and easy to run coop game pick this up!
