_childDocuments_.review: This is a very well made 2 player coop puzzle game. You don't even need to connect to a network or the internet, you just load the game and communicate to a friend using voice comms like discord. You play your way through a narrative where each player is separated through time and space, one in the future and one in the past. You solve puzzles by relaying information to your partner which helps them progress their game, and they do the same back. It mixes a few different style together extremely well, 2D art drawn with a creepy aesthetic, and 3D scenes that allow you to view objects from different angles, both players switch between them which adds variety to the gameplay.It's short and fairly easy, but it's also cheap, so it fills a niche for this kind of game, If you're a fan of 2 player coop puzzle games then this is a fun little experience. If you want some more substantial with much harder puzzles but the same kind of genre then consider playing the series of games called "We Were Here" the first in the series is free on steam and well worth trying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This type of co-op game was a breath of fresh air. I have never experienced this type of puzzle game before, and I think it was really creative and engaging. I enjoyed the story, and I look forward to playing it through again since I hear depending on your choices when going in, the experience is different. I highly recommend playing this game, but it definitely requires some communication skills with a side of patience.

_childDocuments_.review: Words can not describe how much I enjoyed this game.It might seem a bit short to some "2 chapters" but this is so engaging it is well worth the moneyI played this with my partner for a date night, and it was great to work together on solving puzzles, we werent in the same house so we really had to rely on our communication skillsThe artwork is stunning, the music is hauntingly beautiful.Some of the puzzles are easy but some are challenging, it is made all the more so because you have to work together.I would certainly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game fits the narrative and flow of the Rusty Lake universe, which is what initially pulled me into getting it.  While it did have their charm and art styles, it felt considerably easier than the other games.  As others have said, it is more of a "read this to the other player, wait for them to read next step back" progression.  There were a few times of having to search something out, or find where the missing piece went.  However, it lacked the deeper mental games and puzzles that RL is known for.With that said, it was still a fun game for the $5 price point.  My buddy and I only played the butterfly side, so I have yet to see how the bee is different (beyond what they tell you is different).  I would recommend this game as the puzzles are well constructed and flow nicely, but just don't expect it to have the length or complexity of the previous RL games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Four important things:- At $5.99 and a playtime of about 150 minutes (played through both scenarios), my partner and I both thought this was one of the best ways for us to spend an evening's entertainment money.- It's fun, and a really great communication exercise for a couple - particularly if you don't (or can't) look at each other's screens.- It's a multiplayer experience that doesn't require a network connection, which is really clever and much easier for the company to make and support, which makes it more likely there will be more of them and they'll come faster.- The company had the choice to require multiplayer connections through Steam, and they would have gotten more user data that they could have monetized, and they deliberately passed on that opportunity - that's fantastic for user privacy and it's behavior we should encourage.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: All I want to say is: I NEED MORE of this! I was so sad when I saw the credits roll because I wanted like 5 more chapters. Not saying the game is too short, it's just very fun to solve puzzles co-op style!The game (for us) is about 3 hours long, but fun thing is: Once you're finished you can swap roles  , and game mode which will give different solutions / puzzles, So it'll feel fresh! I hope to do this soon. Both players have a completely different setting / experience, so it'll definitely be fun to see play sides!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This was super cute. It had about a 3 hr runtime when my buddy and I played at a relaxed pace. Second chill runtime was about half that (1.5 hrs ish) since we knew what to expect. (It says I played a lot longer in Steam but that's because my friend and I were catching up on our life stuff while the game just sat open lol. It really was only about 4.5hrs total ish between both playthroughs.)It wasn't terribly difficult, so if you're looking for a really challenging puzzle experience, you may be disappointed with this one. But if you're just looking for a fun moment of connection with someone you like via some teamwork challenges and cute story line, this will do it! Cheaper and more convenient than an escape room experience!Content note (CN) for being a creepy, grotesque (some mild cartoon gore- mostly in the form of body horror) mystery with some jump scare moments. Also for a very brief racist moment with a "voodoo doll" theme.[If there's a particular trigger you want to know about, ask me!]

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game, but the price point makes the game a hard pill to swallow.Don't get me wrong, $6 (or whatever your regional price might be) isn't bad and I've bought worse games for more, but its not REALLY $6, its $12. Sure you can play it with a total stranger but if you plan on playing with a friend you both need to own the game. Theres no real way to play this by yourself. That being said if your buying two copys, one for you and one for a friend, its a must by on sale.Over-all, I'd recommend it. I've played all the rusty lake games so far in one way or another and each one is just as great as the last. Even the shorter ones like this one is fantastic and while its hard to replay it, it still HAS the ability to replay it. _childDocuments_.review: I was bummed when I saw that I had to find another player but Rusty Lake discord channel had a crazy amount of people wanting to play. Played it with a rando and it was an absolutely fun experience!I am still not over the graphics and the animations. I feel like nature of the 2-player collaboration game design forced a simpler flow to discovering the next moves which made the puzzles easier to solve than what Rusty Lake has taught us to expect. But even though, it was fun and some of the clues we as tricky as the older games.The only thing I'd suggest is for players/fans who would play the game in reverse roles is to take at least a week off before playing the reverse role. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the Past Within is an interesting feeling, it has a lot in common with the We Were Here games but it really captures the escape room feeling. The puzzle box one player is operating feels more like "Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes". And in the middle of it all, there is the strange feeling that no part of the game is networked, which somehow makes the game feel like the candlelit version of couch coop. Asking the other player if they are done already could be seen as a normally unnecessary step, but to me made it feel more intimate.Definite recommendation for anyone who likes what I mentioned above, or escape room board games. Admittedly, I don't like Rusty Lake that much, but I felt the intensity of the puzzles here was lower than in those games, and therefore perfect for such a game. The vibe is spooky but never scary. All in all, a unique game in its small genre, and I hope we will see more of this!P.S. Being able to play the 3D part in VR would be incredible!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Super interesting, spooky, and fun experience. Took my partner and I a few hours to play through the first time as we were very thorough. The second time was much faster but still cool - I enjoyed having the chance to see another perspective. Not overly challenging (which kept it engaging on both sides!), but required a good amount of puzzle-solving, communication, and exploration. I much preferred one path over the other. Both had their own quirks and style. Super neat. Good eerie-to-creepy ambience, and a lovely escape-room type game to play with someone over an evening or two.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who knows they are going to enjoy this game. When you play the first time around, only give as much information to the other person as they need to solve their puzzle. Don't describe everything you see, but don't sandbag the mission. You will be given a chance to play it again, with slightly different puzzles, but from the other perspective. So, the less "extra stuff" you know, the more unique the experience will be the second time around. Very few games have accomplished everything The Past Within did, and the Rusty Lake team executed it perfectly.If you want a co-operative experience that isn't crazy challenging, but still fun, with a weird and alluring story, check this out. It's kind of like a less stressful, longer and easier version of Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand the need to play a solo oriented genre (point & click adventure) in multi-player. With that said, there are good and bad ways of doing it. This is the latter case.The main issue is the offline multi-player, which had severely limited the design of the puzzles: they cannot be particularly interactive/cooperative (only information sharing is possible), they cannot be too long or complicated (lest one of the player gets bored while the other is stuck), they cannot even be too diverse (or if they can, they were not here). The most "fun" puzzle was based on time-limited info sharing and that's about it.If we also consider it is fairly short (2 hours if you know/understand the other player), expansive compared to the rest of Rusty Lake (I don't have an issue with supporting them, but then the final product should be at least good) and requires looking for another player (and you might need to buy the game for them too) it does not look so attractive.Don't get me wrong, it is not *bad* bad, it is definitely novel, but that only makes it neutral at best and Steam does not allow for non-binary option...

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a co-op puzzle game based game revolving around a broken family and some (Maybe) unnatural resources to return a family together, Graphics: 2D side scroller as well as a 3D setting based on player scenario, using a rustic/modern graphic styleGameplay: Gameplay is smooth and fluent, interact-able objects operate as intendedAudio: Audio soundtrack is a very nice calming melodyStory: The story is dark, yet heart warming all at onceDifficulty: some puzzles, are harder than others, all n all, causes both parties to think and communicateReplay ability: Since both players can either play as the past, or the future version of themselves, this game would be worth several play throughsPrice: even off sale, this game is easily worth the asking price, you can tell the creators put a lot of love and commitment into this project.

_childDocuments_.review: Made three new friends from it so yeah I recommend, BUT!Okay, lets summarize.YOU SHOULD CO-OP. Otherwise the gameplay would be very boring, half the fun is in describing things to the other person, so taking pictures or screenshots or peeking at the other's screen is not very recommended. Go to whatever community, find someone who is willing to play with you, this game makes making new friends simpler-- just invite a fellow fan to play with you.The plot? A bit underwhelming to be honest. I'm not going to spoil anything but euhhhh there's not much to spoil anyways, we realize what is going to happen one third into the game.Gameplay? the puzzles are a bit repetitive, not very creative. This is both good and bad, good as in it would be difficult not to lose temper if your partner spends a hell of a long time puzzle solving, bad as in UNDERWHELMING AND NOT VERY FUN.There would be hidden achievements and scrolls but mehhh.Honestly? _childDocuments_.review: This game has great atmosphere. The puzzles are objectively very simple (some might argue there are no true puzzles in this game) but the major focus is on effective communication, since you can't see your partner's screen. As my best friend aptly described it, it's basically The Room meets Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. The two times we got really stuck were because one person said something and the other person just didn't hear it, so we waffled around for a couple minutes until we figured out what we were missing. It's straightforward and fun, and the premise is kinda spooky and cool. If you like the aforementioned games or are looking for something short and sweet to play with a friend, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: As this is Rusty Lake's first co-op entry, the puzzles are understandably less complex. Instead, the focus of the game is on communicating the various symbols and codes your partner will need to solve their puzzles and vice versa. Only one sequence in the 1 to 2 hour affair uses a timer to up the stress of trying to translate an input and, while it is fail-able, it is also infinitely repeatable. So don't worry about having to find someone you have a near psychic link with before getting started, fumbling is part of the experience. Despite being a bit shorter than a Rusty Lake title and more on par with one of the studio's earlier Cube Escape games, you'll probably want to play through The Past Within at least twice. Once to see things from the Past's perspective and another from the Future's. Thankfully, there's an alternate puzzle solution mode to avoid memorizing to much too quickly and cheating yourself out of the full deductive process.The same should be said about deciding to play the game alone. Considering its nature, it does seem possible to get through it without a partner(I think there's already a guide to just that effect), but most of the fun and the intended course of the story depend on indulging in the difficult task of trying to reach out to someone similar but still very outside of yourself. Take that away and you're only getting half of what The Past Within has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I've played every game in the Rusty Lake catalog with my friend so we were looking forward to The Past Within.The puzzles in this game were very rudimentary, being solely based on conveying to the other person what you're seeing. There was very little critical thinking involved. There weren't any times where we weren't sure what to do next because the game goes out of it's way to write out literal instructions on what you need to do.I thought the 2D portion of the game looked great, being in the usual style but much higher quality. The 3D section looked great as well, and it was interesting to see the signature Rusty Lake style interpreted for a 3D game. It has the hallmark disgustingness of the Rusty Lake series and includes many of the puzzles you see repeated in previous games. It's definitely a Rusty Lake game.Overall, I wish the game was more puzzle focused. If this weren't a game by Rusty Lake, I wouldn't be interested in playing it and I wouldn't recommend it. I do think it's a nice addition to the series though and I had a good time playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a very interesting Co-Op experience with two players. The two rely on one another to relay hints to solve puzzles. These puzzles uncover the story of Mr. Vanderboom. Still not sure to what the story is but I have only finished Bee. Regardless, took roughly an hour and a half to finish first half of the game. This feels like an alternative take on portal but you two aren't even in the same game.  There's no direct link between sessions which was cool. Completing with a friend in discord is a necessity. In my opinion, absolute steal at current sale price of $4.01. Probably will get about 2.5 hours of fun for only $4. Looking forward to buying more games from these devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well executed co-op game! Although it is quite short, being only 2 hours for a first run through if you have smooth communication, It lends itself very well to the way the co-op was designed, with it being that the two players are choosing a couple of starting things to determine puzzle solutions and whatnot so that they are both synced without the need to connect to a server or anything internet wise. _childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool offline multiplayer puzzle game that requires 2 copies and different devices to run it. The game creatively uses game states to synchronize progress across both players and encourages dialogue between them to solve puzzles. It reminds me a lot of Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes but wirh both players having the opportunity to participate, which is way more fun. The game also has a creepy mystery vibe that makes you want to figure out what is happening here.Overall we loved it, hoping for more in this style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: truly an amazing game, I was a bit concerned when I heard that the game would be co-op but not connected with your partners game directly, as the few games like that that I have played felt "unsmooth" and "jumpy". I am oh so happy to announce that is not the case with The Past Within. the experience was completely smooth with no jarring transitions, everything seemed to happen after your partner told you what you were meant to do, even if you looked around it was hard to notice the moment things changed, and the change in perspective from chapter one to two was beautifully done, with the 3D being beautiful and yet somehow keeping the essence of the very stylized 2D.the paradoxical way that one room is inside the other is strange but delivered very well and the characters are portrayed in a way that feels natural with what we have seen, not introducing much new in the story but still explaining questions that were in my mind for a while and with a couple of puzzles that are still being figured out as of writing is really a show of how committed Rusty Lake is to keeping the point-and-click horror genre alive and innovative

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit I was not thrilled when Rusty Lake announced a co-op only game especially right after the White Door which was not my favorite. Being a long-time follower of the studio and a bit of an antisocial when it comes to video games I cheated and played alone on two different devices (you do have to pay two licenses if you decide to do that). I have to say I did enjoy it, the game is absolutely beautiful, very much in the style of other Rusty Lake games but maybe a little more polished. One of the players is in a classic 2D environment while the other plays in a 3D world reminiscent of the Room franchise (wish I also love). The music and ambiance are great like always. You kind of have to know the universe of the old games to fully enjoy the story of this one (especially Roots) because the Past Within is in my humble opinion almost only about that. The puzzles are not very challenging (probably a little more if you play with someone else and you have to describe everything) especially compared to other games like Paradox. I only played the “bee game”, you get to choose bee or butterfly at the very beginning of the game, and it took me about an hour and a half. All and all I would recommend this game to the fans, spend a little more and you can even play it on your own :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: No actual game invite needed which at first same seemed strange to me but ultimately turned out amazing. Would love to see more games like this in the future...

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, bite-sized puzzle experience for two. It's quick (about an hour and a half for our playthrough), but has some replayability: you can swap roles with your partner and swap to a second set of puzzle solutions. The atmosphere is excellent - I haven't really played other Rusty Lake games, so the unsettling vibe was new and appreciated. If you've played other asymmetrical co-op puzzles, you might find this a touch easy. There's not much room for confusion, and there's never more than one or two steps to figure out on your own before getting to another communication puzzle. I don't think the simplicity detracts, and I'd prefer simple puzzles to those with a lot of ambiguity, but your mileage may vary.All in all, a delightful way to spend an hour or two with someone you like.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately this did not spark joy.At no point I felt like I've solved a riddle - it's rather just executing and working through a narrow list of options.You get a key? There's only one place it can go. Found a code? Only one place where you type it.Good escape rooms have you guessing and puzzled, forcing you to think outside the box or pick between multiple valid solutions.Here all you do is exchange simple codes or actions that immediately lead to the next code/action. Rinse & repeat for 90minutes and you're done.Though it feels polished and well done, it lacks anything interesting that would make this worth recommending.

_childDocuments_.review: No network connection needed!This a very original design and would love to see more in this vein.The puzzles are classic Rusty Lake, but you'll be closely working with a partner, either in the same room or via some other means but you'll have to be able to communicate well outside the game, right from the start.Note: both will be individually solving some puzzles and some will be solved in lockstep.It's possible to get stuck waiting for your partner to deliver info you need to continue, but at that point you can cheat and just have a look, which we had to do only twice.It's also possible to bruteforce some puzzles, resulting in your partner having to bruteforce a corresponding puzzle on their side, so NEVER BRUTEFORCE!

_childDocuments_.review: I love all of the Rusty Lake games so this one is no exception for me. What makes this one even more interersting is that it's a co-op game and the first co-op in the series. I mostly play single player games especially when it comes to point and click puzzle games so it was really fun to play with a friend this time around. The game works really well in co-op and me and my friend both had a great time. What's even better is that there are two modes you can play so even though we finished it once we can play the second mode to get different solutions to the puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: I really like the rusty lake series and I played each game multiple times. I had to say that I am a little disappointed with this one. Pros:1. Sound design is awesome as always. I preferred music from the white door but this one is still great. 2. The environment is doing its job perfectly. I really got spooked a few times. 3. The 3D part is pretty cool and also new experience for old rusty lake players. 4. I had fun with my partner. I like that we need to communicate to solve puzzles.5. My partner has never played rusty lake series and he did enjoyed the game and won't complain about it. Mixed: The multi player part isn't synced or connected which I don't really care. It's not a priority for me at least. It's just a bit confusing when the game tell both of you to do something at exactly the same time. Cons:1. The play time is really short even compared with other rusty lake games. I finished the game with my partner for about one hour (butterfly mode). We bought the game for a 40% discount so 3.5$ each so I won't complain too much. However, if I bought this at full price, I'd feel a bit more disappointed. 2. The play time would be fine with me if there are more puzzles and story elements in the game. On the contrary, the puzzles are quite simple. Most of the story we already know from past games. Maybe I missed some lore but I feel like there isn't much to say about the story. 3. Some of the puzzles are simply redundant. There are multiple puzzles that are just letting you repeat the same instruction times and times again, which isn't really fun. It can be a little frustrating. 4. There's not much point in trying both modes to be honest. Both butterfly and bee has same puzzles only, of course, you get a bee or a butterfly model. The answers may change sequence but it's really the same thing. My partner and I finished both mode in 2 hours. 5. The 3D part is cool but I have to be honest, I'm not that impressed. Different games (the room for example) have done similar things before. It's not bad but it's not impressive enough to let me ignore the previous points. Overall, I don't think I would recommend this game to a new player at this moment. My partner didn't complain about it and think it's okay. But he did say he probably wouldn't buy this if I didn't want to play it (I gifted him one). If you really really do love the rusty lake lore and want to dive deep into the details, sure this game isn't that bad. I just think there are too few features that attract new players or returning players who love puzzles and would like to know how the story develops. I also wouldn't recommend buying this one at full price. Two or three dollars for me is more acceptable than 6 dollars. I have to say I'm a bit disappointed and I did expected more from the rusty lake series.

_childDocuments_.review: Although  didn't end up making my top 10 for 2022, it was definitely a contender. I'm always a sucker for asymmetric co-op, and  shares the cool design of  in that two players can play together without actually being connected online. I played the "Past" side, while my co-op partner played the "Future." I'm unsure what difference it ends up making, but we selected the bee instead of the butterfly at the beginning of the game.I loved the illustrated characters, the items, and the environments in the game, as well as the auditory and visual effects that occur at key shocking moments. The whole thing feels like a creepy voodoo ritual, which does seem to jive with the universe of  from my understanding (I haven't played any other  games). Solving this macabre puzzle box was really unlike anything I've done in a game before, and I had a lovely time doing so.Another thing I came to appreciate more while watching the "Let's Play" is the way that objects and actions in the past correspond to those in the future, as certain streamers were able to bounce between the perspective of the Past and Future player. At one point, the player in the future starts playing some beat-heavy music. In response, the furniture within the room of the player in the past begins inexplicably (from your perspective) bumping and shaking around (which helps unlock a way forward).In general, the puzzles are quite well-designed in the game. They're intuitive without being easy, and I felt a sense of satisfaction at each critical story juncture. The only type of player I wouldn't recommend this game to would be a solo gamer since it's inherently a cooperative experience. However, if you have a bud to take on the ride, you should take it. It's also relatively cheap and short, so it's easy to fit in if you have a lot going on.

_childDocuments_.review: This was an incredibly creative new re-imagining of the Rusty Lake formula for 2 players. It was difficult not to get totally absorbed into this virtual escape room! My wife and I had a blast describing our sides of the screen with enough precision to identify what clues were needed to advance the others'.The puzzles were toned down a bit compared to the usual Rusty Lake, which suited the 2 player gameplay - Imagine it would be boring to wait too long on one teammate getting stuck. Rare are games that inspire such intensive communication between players in a low stress environment. Playing the Past Within felt like playing an enjoyable social board game, but with all the narrative advantages and thrills of a digital medium. Couldn't recommend more for couples or groups of friends playing each side.Absolute 10/10 for a 2 player narrative puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fairly short, but probably worth playing through a second time since the perspective you get of the puzzles is quite different. The atmosphere is just creepy enough without being so unsettling that it would keep anyone from finishing it.As for the puzzles... some are better than others. The linear nature of the game, which allows cooperative play without a networked connection, begins to narrow the puzzling possibilities. At least that's how it felt. I won't spoil the clever ones, but for a stretch the way clues and the interfaces are doled out, makes it fairly obvious what goes where.Grab it for a good price and give it a whirl. I do enjoy cooperative puzzle solving and the barrier for entry here is very low, so it's a great place to start for anyone looking for something on the spooky side.

_childDocuments_.review: It's alright. It's one of those games that doesn't require actual server-client connection between the 2 players, just being able to talk to each other.It's quite short, took us under 2 hours to first playthrough.Of negatives, I must point out lack of chapter select for quick achievement clean up after beating both sides.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This was fun! Me and my friend really enjoyed this game. It takes just enough time to keep you interested and avoid frustration. The story building is well executed even for people not familiar with the Rusty Lake series. We especially liked the option to switch sides and replay the game from the other person's POV if you choose different intro settings. Very well done!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game was probably my favourite out of all of the series! The co - op element was done wonderfully, the graphics were beautiful and the story was intriguing but not too complicated. I love the bee and butterfly element, allowing for the players to both experience the Past and Present but not having to do the same puzzles over again. I definitely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summed up as Rusty Lake meets Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. The problem is it ends up stuck in the middle, being sub-par on both of these ends. The coop tasks almost always consist of simply relaying simple codes to your partner and vice-versa. And the Rusty Lake-y parts (point-and-click escape room) are much easier and simpler than in their other games. While this ease is understandable in a coop game (otherwise one player would be bored to death while waiting for the other to solve a puzzle), it doesn't make for a good game. The story is nice, albeit very simple.I did have fun playing The Past Within, but I was expecting a deeper, more meaningful coop experience. The fact that you need to buy two copies of the game doesn't help either. I'd only recommend this game to hardcore fans of Rusty Lake; otherwise, you're not missing out on much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolute must play for anyone looking for an escape-room style game - but especially for die-hard fans of the Rusty Lake / Cube Escape series. While significantly easier than most of their other games (which I think will help it reach a broader audience), The Past Within expertly builds upon the lore established in many of the other Rusty Lake games (especially Roots, Hotel, etc.). I also LOVED that there is a replay-ability aspect - you can tell that the developers really wanted to make something special for old and new audiences alike. Just overall another awesome release (and I hope it's not the last)!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun twist on escape room style puzzle games. We play a lot of them, and usually you work together in a much more straight forward way, seeing the same room and puzzles. This game you don't, thus it involves a lot of communication.Reading the description, I thought the game would have actual past-present mechanics, but it didn't really have any. Despite that, the game was quite fun and certainly is worth playing. It took me and my wife 105 minutes to beat the game. You can play again with different answers to the puzzles, but I'm assuming that this means that the puzzles are the same just with different solutions so you can't have them memorized. I don't see this as adding any additional value, and consider this a one play through game. Given that, and having to buy two copies, 12 dollars is probably a bit much for less than two hours. On sale though, I'd say it's worth it if you are looking for a fairly easy experience that mostly involves communication.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The game was really short and boring, and the puzzles were too easy. It was basically just a picture-and-tell kind of thing. My speaking skills improved a lot in that 90 mins ：） They didn't really capture the essence of Rust Lake except the art style and characters.As for the background, if you've played Root, you may feel more engaged. But overall, the game is just too short. It only has two chapters, and the story just abruptly ends.All in all, it doesn't compare to the other games out there (considering value for money as well). Thankfully, I played it with a really good friend, so having her around already made me happy enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Very entertaining short simple puzzle game. Depending on you and/or who you choose to play it with, it can either be a very quick playthrough or a lot of sitting around wondering what to do because communication is key and you can very easily do all of the puzzles if you communicate effectively. Regardless I think there is a certain charm in both potential outcomes that makes it worth a play. Overall, 7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's a short puzzle game you can play with a pal (you'll need a pal I should say, but then again, there's a discord server if you need help or someone to play with). It's a little spoopy and had me spooked a few times while my friend couldn't see what was going on as I hyperventilated. Anyway, it's short and sweet and spooky and a puzzle game. If you like all those things and 2d and 3d artwork, this is perfect for you and a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I love this new Rusty Lake game! The puzzles were quite simple in my opinion, but some people might prefer that. I love that the developers used both 2D and 3D styles, which lead to a very immersive experience. I also really appreciate that you can replay this game a lot, since there are both the Bee and the Butterfly versions (different puzzle answers in each), and you can trade past and future roles with the person you play with! This game has been worth the wait and I also look forward to what Rusty Lake comes up with next! :)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Had a blast navigating through this puzzle adventure! The game charms with its striking visual design and cleverly constructed challenges. Although a feast for the eyes and mind, it unfortunately comes to an end a bit too soon, leaving a yearning for more adventures and enigmas to unravel. A short, yet sweet journey that I’d gladly recommend to puzzle enthusiasts.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is here, and it's going to feel different from other entries in the series, mainly for the cooperative mode. If you want to dive in without any further knowledge, well... I'll say that it's a interesting experience and you'll have a great time.If you want to hear more, here are some top of mind pieces of feedback.If you want to see more indie games, many of which I've reviewed, please check out my youtube channel. Link  and after my closing thoughts!It's safe to assume that many wondered if The Past Within would retain that classic, Rusty Lake feeling while at the same time being cooperative in nature. Rest assured, it does. Everything screams Rusty Lake as usual, and the atmosphere is more pronounced here than it was in The White Door, which in and on itself was still a great experience, even if different. Being cooperative isn't necessarily the way to go for this series, but it's been around for so long and with so many titles that this feels like an exciting, fresh experience on top of already successful and interesting games.With that said, cooperation comes at a cost: complexity. While The White Door was certainly different from the more classic feel of The Past Within, I'm afraid the latter did sacrifice much of its complexity in order to mantain the cooperative structure. That's perfectly fine and I can see why they went this route, since your friend/partner/whatever may not be used to play Rusty Lake at all and could have an odd time figuring things out. That has been my personal experience, at least. Being used to the common puzzle structure amongst the series, I've found a gap between me and my partner in how puzzles are approached. With that said, I still think that going the easy route with its estimated 2 hour length may have hurt longevity a little.Given how much it costs, though, there's no reason to be mad about it or anything like that. It's just my personal consideration, and I've enjoyed everything it had to offer and its cooperative structure more than I expected!To my knowledge, this is the first 3D Rusty Lake game. And they absolutely nailed it. Actually, you'll have a mix of 2D and 3D based on which timeline you start with. Eventually, you'll switch from one dimension to the other... but I can't stress enough about how well it mantains that Rusty Lake feeling while being transposed to 3D. From a game design perspective, I can see the challenges that may have been presented during development. Whatever they've done, it paid off. The cube concept is really cool! And it has many things to do in such a condensed space, at least enough to carry half a game. Even though I've talked about how easy puzzles are, I'll say that the concept overcomes this aspect in many way, providing insight to interesting choices design-wise which can and will keep you entertained for its interesting yet brief duration.For my playthrough I've chosen the butterfly and I've started off in the future. Interesting pick, and I'm satisfied with it! When I'll have the chance, I'll replay through the other perspective. Thank you, Victor Butzelaar! Rusty Lake always had amazing, eerie and distinctive piano sections. It's interesting to see that the soundtrack manages to get better at each iteration of this series, and I can't express how well thought it feels and, of course, is. I think I've reviewed every Rusty Lake game, if I'm not wrong. I always wonder what they'll come up with, since this is an evolving story, filled with mystery and eerieness. Story-wise, The Past Within is extremely important and, for me, has set up a whole interesting area which I can't wait to explore. Of course, the game is very peculiar in some ways. It retains some of that "flash game" feeling, something many players wouldn't really like nowadays, but I think this series evolved just right and it now has (since Roots, as far as I'm concerned) a distinctive character surrounding it. Point and click games aren't for everyone, as they could come across as "boring" since there's a lot of stuff to do. But I would invite you to invest some time in the Rusty Lake lore and learn about each piece of media that has been presented until now. I'm sure you'll find it interesting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Really good fun, I LOVE asymmetric coop puzzle/escape games, We Were Here is one of my favourite series of games, so I was very pleased to have a similar style of game in the Rusty Lake universe.A lot of the thematic elements might seem strange to someone not familiar with the Rusty Lake series, but I think mechanically it holds up regardless, but you might want to play the rest of the series first to learn some of the symbolism and recurring characters. This game is the first one that is explicitly coop, but the other games are enjoyable to play with someone too, streaming over discord or hanging out in person.It is somewhat a shame that both players need to own the game instead of having a friend pass system, the price isnt too high so it's not that bad, but it might be difficult to convince a friend to play if they are not already sold on the idea, either gameplay wise or because it's another Rusty Lake game, so I would have the expectation of buying it for your chosen partner instead, which is why a friend pass system would be better but hey. I would say it takes about 1.5-2 hours to beat a first playthrough, but is worth doing a second playthrough from the other person's perspective, taking maybe 0.5-1 hour again, of course will vary for everyone but I think it's a good estimate.So yeah, pretty great, maybe a little expensive for what it is, but I want to show support for this type of game in general, as well as supporting the Rusty Lake series which I have been a fan of for a while now. I would suggest waiting for a sale unless you have the same values I have, ie need to play more games like this and/or anything Rusty Lake asap.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: A great little co-op game that is pretty economically priced to boot. Definitely worth picking up if you have someone to play along with. Do note, co-op is necessary, it is not an option.Pros:1) An interesting, somewhat creepy story. Definitely unique and different.2) Intuitive controls that are fun to explore. The game expects you to poke around and figure things out with the help of your teammate. You will absolutely have to work in tandem and I loved the experience.3) Even though this is co-op, you aren't actually connected to each other, meaning that you can even play with someone across the world without having to bother about latency of the server. All you would need would be some communication channel to talk through.Cons:1) The game is quite short. I finished it in an hour and a half. You could get a second play-through in by swapping around the characters, but that would still be 3 hours at best. Of course, your time to complete may vary. Personally I do not see this as a significant con, especially since the game is so reasonably priced, but it is something to keep in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Normally this is not my type of game to play. But my girlfriend saw this game on TikTok and she really wanted to play. So as I like to think I am a good boyfriend, we both got the game and started to play. We played about 3 hours of this game, playing as both roles. It was pretty fun, there is not too much to do within this game. But it made my girlfriend happy, so that makes me happy.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played the previous titles from this developer but I had heard a lot of good things from my friends about how they do their puzzle games. I think this one knocks those ones out of the park.Having one person work in 3D and the other in 2D is so much fun and makes each players experience extremely unique. I liked also toward the end having that switch so even if you never end up playing the other players experience you still get to see how the 2D version of the game would play out. I got to play the 3D player for most of the game, I ended up playing this with my boyfriend and we did well and also struggled which made for an average puzzle game experience.I would recommend to any puzzle game lovers
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: pretty fun! always been a fan of the Rusty Lake concept and artwork. the puzzles weren't too hard to figure out (same difficulty as other Rusty Lake games). the challenge is in communicating with your partner without looking at each other's screens. played both the Bee and Butterfly modes, which were practically the same. didn't manage to get all the achievements because some of them depend on whether you're in the Past or Future :") overall, was an entertaining way to spend the afternoon
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Actually the worst "game" I played in a very long time - even on sale, this is not worth the money or time spent.- extremely simple puzzles & a lot of repetition of the same basic concepts (which are not even fun the first time) make it feel more like a list of chores - in 95% of the cases, the solution is a verbal copy&paste to your partner and the only difficulty comes from the the actual game mechanics which are incredibly clunky, in some cases it's hard to find objects to interact with or simply clicking on stuff- everything seems spooky and mysterious in the beginning, but in the end, there is no meaningful resolution to the plotline whatsoeverThe sad thing here is that the initial premise holds a lot of potential with the clever method of co-op puzzles without actual connection required, different POV for different players, initially mysterious setting, the OKish but servicable graphics, music and sound effects and so on.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful co-op puzzle game! You go back and forth with puzzles, you give each other solutions and figure out what the hell is even happening in this ominous place! I played with the other person in the room, but it can work just as well over voice chat (or maybe even better cause you won't be tempted to peek at the other screen!)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the rusty lake games ever since I was a wee lad in middle school, and as an avid Easter egg/ cameo hunter, I have always appreciated the little things. this game was an absolute blast to play with my girlfriend, and I think she now has a newfound love for these very Interesting and fun escape room-type games. I can't wait for what comes next!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I knew about the developers of this game from their previous titles (Cube Escape/Rusty Lake Series), if you're into puzzle solving/click adventures with a deep story, be sure to give this game a go with a friend or one of the developers' previous titles. The puzzles are very creative, and they're not too difficult where you'd be stuck for hours on end, it has a very good skill gap for beginners and advanced players who are familiar with puzzle solving. The games have a very cool aesthetic, and The Past Within was just what the series needed, a co-op style game, where you can play with a friend, since all the previous games were singleplayer. Get this game, and get a friend to play it with, and you'll have a fun time. I have next to nothing to critique this game about, but it could just be that I'm a biased person since I loved the other games. tl;dr if you like puzzles and cool stories, play the games you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I have't played any other Rusty Lake game. The Past Within is a rather short puzzle game, me and my friend got through it in about 3 hours playing both the past and the future (so we finished the game twice with reversed roles). I wouldn't say it's a complex game or one that leaves any room for failure. The gameplay consisted of me and my friend just communicating relevant things for each puzzle:- Yo I see this kinda thing- Oh yea I have something that I can interact with that looks exactly like that- Ok so here's what you need to inputThis is basically all of the puzzles in a nutshell. The atmosphere is like no other tho, being lowkey disturbing and with a mysterious story that leaves room for interpretation. For the price, I'd say it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, there should be more games like these. Something like "Keep talking and nobody explodes" kind of vibe going on here. The biggest drawback is basically this can be done in complete singleplayer. The illusion is that you need two people to co-operate and help each other through. From 2D and 3D perspectives and scenarios, this is still a great way to experience it by giving simple trust to your partner and giving hints on what to do next to proceed.Again, seeing how this puzzling franchise have gone so far this is really a great and fresh feel of experiencing something new while also traditionally keeping things simple. It's great to waste few hours if you wanna hang around with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I forgot to review this game when I actually played it a few months back, but I had a really solid time playing through it with a friend! Very well put together. The perfect length. A sinister but fun narrative holding it all together. Not many games handle co-op as well as this one. I definitely recommend this bite sized puzzle adventure!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice new offering from Rusty Lake, with the new element being co-op play. If you've enjoyed Rusty Lake games, you'll like this. As always, great hand-drawn art style and and restrained/muted color palette. Puzzles are interesting and not too difficult. The characters and story have a slightly dark, but mostly a creepy-cool vibe. A must play for fans of Rusty Lake and point & click puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool idea for a multiplayer experience. The gameplay is somewhat similar to the way Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes is, but both of you have to relay information to the other to progress through it. Whats super impressive about The Past Within, is even though you aren't connecting the 2 games together through the internet, it feels like it is. When I first played I was surprised how much the game knew when to do certain actions only based on the information you would get from the other player. Overall a pretty fun time and would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: SO FUN AND A LITTLE CREEPY. Game with communication, similar to Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes gameplay wise, but the story is closer to The Room. The art style is really cool, and the mechanics are smoooooooth. Very impressed, also replay-ability so you can get all the achievements and endings for both sides(:
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this and pressed play so fast I didn't realize it was co-op. Later got it for my friend to play together - such a fun experience!!! The change in visual style was such a cool moment, I was fangirling really hard. Total surprise. The puzzle cube was done so well! I love all the little secrets and achievements to get in-game. I'm still a huge fan of Rusty Lake and probably always will be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointed by how short it was... Glad I got it on launch discount, but really hoped there would be more than 2 chapters if I had to pay for it. Like at least 3. Missed the refund window by 3 minutes so I guess the content was juuust long enough, lol. Would love to see more co-op Rusty Lake experiences like this, but preferably longer if I and my friends gotta pay for it!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's short but good. Me and a friend beat the game twice (so we could take both roles) in about 4 hours.Though some people have tagged this game as Online Co-Op, it does not actually appear to be online at all - I assume so that you can crossplay with a PC player on mobile, etc. Because there's no actual netcode, the game "synchronises" both players by having fixed solutions for the puzzles and hard sync points where players must demonstrate they're sharing information.This sounds like it'd harm replay value, but it doesn't. The game compensates for not being able to randomly generate solutions with two selectable variations so you can at least replay once with different solutions to the puzzles. Which the game does want you to do! There's a bunch of achievements across the chapters and you can't get all of them without playing twice. Loved the art, especially in the 3D sections.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic!!  My daughter and I have been playing Rusty Lake since she was young.  Now she's away at college and this is such a fun way for us to still play together.  Definitely not as complicated as originals, but challenging enough to make it worth our time.  Take all my money, send more games like this!!  I'm in.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Hi, I played this game with my friend. The game was short but good. The story being simple helps the game more. Just don't look at your friends screen for the full experience. I wish that the game has more story but for the price, definitely worth it.On a side note: if you are a scaredy cat, please don't play at 3 am (specially if you're the past since it's eerie as f)
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Completely reliant on teamwork in the most positive way possible. Me and my best friend played the bee and the butterfly mode and switched devices in between modes and loved every minute. Entirely too well made for the cheap pricing. Definitely on it's way to being a popular mainstream game, and I'm here for it. Gonna recommend it to my other friends and anyone else who's interested.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Good game for two. Very atmospheric, like all the other games from Rusty Lake. The puzzles are not very difficult, but interesting enough, so that the game can be easily finished in one breath (by the way, the game takes 1.5-2 hours, which is a disadvantage for me, because it is not cheap for such a short time).
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game, there is one big BUT. It took us 115 min to go through the whole game. I feel disappointed because I waited a very long time for the release :( The co-op mode is perfectly done, unfortunately the storyline is too short. I remember long hours at other Rusty titles. I am waiting for more ... .
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Being a fan since the first games in mobile phones apps and having played every game of the franchise, I can guarantee you that the team behind The Rusty Lake will never disappoint you! Especially after The Past Within, their first try as a co-op game, I can say that in the future we re gonna have many marvelous surprises from this amazing team! It was a unique experience that I've shared my favorite game series with my friend, working together to solve the puzzles. I love the artworks, the style and the story that is so solid and with each game you discover and unravel more secrets about the Rusty Lake. I am looking forward to their future games. <3
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an escape room/puzzle game, you are going to be disappointed. The "puzzles" are very easy to solve. The story and art are great but that's about it. It's about 1 hour to get through the story, then if you missed achievements you might have to go back and play through it a few more times. I find it too expensive for just 1 hour of "fun", I really wish they had not advertised this as a "solve puzzles" kind of game and rather a coop adventure game of sorts. I can see how people that have no experience with puzzle/escape room games, would think this is exciting, but if you have played games like "We were here", "Keep talking and nobody explodes", and expect this to be similar, then you are going to be very disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome visuals and a lot of content, amazing for the price. That said, almost all of the puzzles boil down to "tell the other person what you see" and then its instantly solved, so there isn't a lot of replayability despite being able to play two sets of puzzles as past or future. Most of the difficulty comes from communication and trying to figure out what corresponds to what.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a gift from a dear friend of mine!! I recommend this for friends who lives in distance from each other ^_^ As long as there's comprehensive communication between both parties, puzzles can be solved smoothly! Plus, you can choose either the bee or butterfly mode as well as switch perspectives as The Future or The Past person. Thank you for this game, we really enjoyed it ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. Puzzles are simple and the concept is really fun. Get a buddy or a friend, communicate the puzzles, find the solutions, all good stuff! Well, all with one exception, the spookiness factor. Like, I think it's very obvious right from the get go what the spooky thing is and i'm going to be honest, if the idea was for me to go like "oh no, the spooks", most of the time I was just saying
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: It's the only Rusty Lake game you can play with a friend. It is a co-op game that you can play either in the future or in the past. A network connection is not a must, but you need a means of communication to give each other the hints you find around to proceed the game. The story is about Rose, who will carry on her father's Albert Vanderboom plan. Help her through multiple puzzles with your friend to unravel the mystery. This new experience is exciting, especially with the cooperative puzzles that can be played cross-platforms with your friend. One of the players will play the classic 2d with a creepy atmosphere like how all Rusty lake games plays, and the other will have the 3d mode where he'll have a huge cube with multiple puzzles which can't be solved without a friend's help. There is no in-game chat, you'll have to use either discord or any other communication mean. I always enjoy games' atmospheric soundtracks, and this one was no different. The music fits the creepy atmosphere well. I also liked the concept of this game, which you'll understand by the end. Pros:+Interesting side of Albert Vanderboom and his daughter Rose.+Co-op gameplay (Two players must play the game, and is cross-platform, with no need for an internet connection)+Good soundtracks.+Variety of puzzles.+Eeirie atmosphere.+Steam achievements.Cons:-The story could be confusing; you must play the series' other games to understand it.-No hinting system. Sometimes, you get stuck and don't know what to do next.Although the game is short, the experience was good, and some of the parts were surprising. I highly recommend playing both sides to understand the story more. Each side's gameplay takes about two hours, for a total of four hours to beat the game. Some of the achievements are tricky, though. You might need a guide to get them all.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a bit easier than the other games, but the true challenge is communicating with your partner. If you have someone you're good with one side can be finished in an hour. The gameplay is very similar to Tick Tock: A Tale for Two. In true Rusty Lake fashion it leaves you with more questions than answers about the lore, but that's why we love this series!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly creative, incredibly interesting game. The idea of a coop game with no internet connection is fantastic, displayed very well here. Recommend to anyone who enjoys point and click/puzzle games in any capacity, I see people complain about the easy difficulty of the puzzles but I don't think it takes away from the overall enjoyment and satisfaction of the game at all, just a fun time the whole way. Playing both roles back to back is cool to see both's perspectives and make more sense of the game. Definitely enjoyed my time with this title and very interested to see more from these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: As always from this studio, the game has great quality, contains satisfying puzzles, has original atmosphere and story. A well-implemented co-op mode allows you to play the game again, next time from the point of view of the other person. Great experience, I heartily recommend and congratulations to the creators of such a good game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Past Within

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, really immersive, and great fun with a friend (even though that's the only real way to play it, to be honest).The sound design was great, whether it was mystery man climbing the walls or the subtle piano in the background. Although it doesn't require an internet connection, the game does a fabulous job of making the player think otherwise! Even though occasionally you can tell the game resorts to cheap tricks at the ends of chapters to make it seem simultaneous, the game still impressed me. Graphics are highly impressive for a game studio that only used 2-D spaces before, and the puzzles were challenging but not to the point they made you frustrated, just pleased with the eventual result. Replay-ability was highly important for this game, given that you can play between two different perspectives, so the addition of giving different solutions for a second play-through was a nice touch from the developers. _childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is a unique and fun puzzle game that can be played with a friend over phone, tablet, laptop or PC. One player works in the past, while the other works in the future, and together they must uncover hidden information and solve puzzles to progress in the game. You can play the game anywhere aslong as you have voice communication. The gameplay mechanics are simple but effective. By working together, players can unlock new information that can be used to progress on their side of the storyline. The puzzles themselves were not overly difficult, but fun to solve.  It's a great way to spend an evening, and the combination of puzzle-solving and spooky atmosphere makes for an engaging and entertaining experience.

The game is perfectly prepared to seamlessly include people that are not familiar with any of the previous games (for example, my Player 2 for my first run of The Past Within), because to them the story is engaging and the visuals are interesting, intriguing and just the right ammount of creepy. We had a lot of fun sharing these puzzles, and I will definitely play again in the second mode! Always excited to see what RL comes up with next!

This way both players can experience either perspective once.This is also required to get all the achievements.Intrigueing story, a lot isn't said, but implied. Makes for interesting food for thought, but it's really not that deep at the end of the day.Neat atmosphere. The game has a dark tone to it, sometimes gets a bit "disgusting" if you're not good with looking at blood or dead bodies. It's a rather cartoonish style though, so its palattable.Fun puzzles. The puzzles aren't really very complex, it mostly comes down to communicating a different kind of code to your partner, who inputs the sequence to get to the next puzzle. Puzzles are solved in a pre-designed order, except for the few times you have 2-3 puzzles available at the same time, but often miss some elements you get from other puzzles anyway. Not too challenging, but a fun communication challenge.All in all, it's short, has a dark atmosphere and puzzles mostly focusing on your ability to communicate codes rather than puzzles that are more on the complex side of things.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW!  I've been a big fan of all of Rusty Lake's games for a while now, and it continues to amaze me how they keep making each new game more interesting and more innovative! _childDocuments_.review: I found The Past Within to be a well-executed cooperative puzzle game. Its asymmetric nature allows for swapping roles and doing a second playthrough via the second "seed". Both runs can easily be completed in one sitting or two shorter ones. My one issue was the overuse of flashing lights/screens which, while appropriate for the 19th-century-inspired horror setting, made some of the puzzles uncomfortable to look at. I recommend The Past Within for puzzle game fans looking for a cooperative experience to share over a few hours.The Past Within is a cooperative puzzle game in which two players work together from two different viewpoints. No connection is required between the two devices, instead, players each have half of the information necessary to solve the puzzles. By communicating outside the game (voice, text, etc.), players take turns describing what they see and together make progress to solve their half of the puzzles.One of the most important factors of a cooperative asymmetric puzzle game is how well-suited the puzzles are for the format. To be cooperative, both players need to have something to do at all stages and an equal contribution to the solution. To work asymmetrically, puzzles need to be simple to describe, but not so simple that the solution is obvious to either player. The Past Within delivers on both measures, all while bridging an asymmetric 2D/3D viewing experience for each player.The Past Within features two "seeds", bee and butterfly, which allow the game to be played with different solutions to the puzzles. Both players must select the same seed for their puzzles to match, meaning the puzzle solutions are different on each seed. This allows players to swap roles after beating the game and replay on the other side of the story without knowing the answers. The puzzles themselves still follow the same format, so replaying takes about half the time as the original playthrough. At a time of 2 hours for a first run and 1 hour for a second run, the game can easily be completed in one sitting or broken up over two shorter ones.The graphics of The Past Within are well-suited for the contents of the story. The atmosphere is themed after Frankenstein and the works of Edgar Allen Poe, both with subtle references. The one issue I had with the visuals was the number of sequences with flashing lights or flickering screens. There were a few puzzles where I found myself wanting to hurry up and move on just to save my eyes. While such effects are often thematic and appropriate for this setting, I would've preferred them to be done once for effect and then discontinued so the player can focus on other aspects of the game.

By release date is a good rhythm to follow,  There aren't really challenging "puzzles" to solve but rather the puzzle here is how you and your player 2's communication skills are. Using just your words to guide your player 2 that's the real challenge.Story wise, it does follow the story from the Cube Collection and previous games, so it does connect with the story line although I am unsure if it is canon or not. _childDocuments_.review: All rusty lakes games are great, and this is no exception.The offline synchronous puzzle approach is super unique, and really really awesome and well executed.The vibe is slightly different compared to past games, and it maybe felt a bit shorter than some of the previous cube escape installments, but that's bearing in mind that there's roughly double the content.I also think the reduced run-length is a little bit due to the puzzle loops being a bit tighter by natures of the gameplay loop revolving around communicating information to your partner in order to progress- there was a lot less clicking around & trying to figure out what comes next.By the same token, the puzzles usually felt pretty straightforward - easier than usual, the core gameplay mechanic seemed to revolve less around lateral thinking and more around communication.Overall, it's an awesome and unique addition to the series, and as someone who mainly plays with a friend, it felt perfect.I'm keen to see the format repeated, maybe with a bit more depth of puzzles and a bit more plot.

_childDocuments_.review: The artstyle sets a serious barrier for how you can interpret the story. It's very difficult to find yourself fully immersed when it looks like an old flash-game. Had the past been in better art-style, one might've cared a bit more for the story.The concepts are relatively simple, and are quite out-done by very similar games (Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes) - there's practically nothing that TPW can do that isn't done better in that game, and it brings very little to the table other than a lacklustre story and unfulfilled mystery. This was a great premise, but it lacks execution, and the idea that you don't need to connect the devices ultimately subtracts more than it adds. I'm not refunding the game (even though we beat it in 1hr and 45 minutes, meaning we're eligible) because overall for 6 euros, I wasn't mad. This felt like a game that is worth that much, I just won't recommend it because I believe there's not enough overall creative focus. _childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEThe Past Within is a bizarre/surrealist point & click puzzle game. It's a continuation of the Rusty Lake universe, but this game introduces a new twist - co-op! I was a bit nervous on this front as it seems like some developers really struggle with creating good co-op games, but they did a great job and the end result is very polished. For ~half the game, one person plays similarly to how The Room series works (mostly working around a box that has hints/tricks/secrets within it that need to be communicated to your partner), while the other person plays very similarly to how Rusty Lake titles tend to play.I found this title to be a fair bit easier than most of the other titles in this series, as the game provides instructions for some portions which gets rid of some of the trial and error that I used to have to do. That said, it's still solidly a puzzle game at the end of the day.If you're already a fan of other titles by Rusty Lake, I can't imagine you'd dislike this game. If you haven't tried one yet, I recommend starting with Samsara Room (it's free on Steam and very indicative of the type/style of content in their other games, including this one) and if you enjoy that, then continuing with the rest of the series in order (note that this recommendation does have you playing out of order, as Samsara Room comes towards the end of the published titles to date. I think it's worth it if you're unsure if you'll like it and the game is so bizarre/surrealist anyways, that I don't think it will really spoil anything).The game took about 1.5 hours to complete one run, but it's worth it to play twice to get the full experience (as you can play in The Past as well as in The Future, which are completely different experiences). You'll need to do this anyways to get all achievements. Therefore, it's about three hours to complete both "sides", and then it took another ~hour to do achievement clean-up.All in all, this game is full of good, weird, atmospheric puzzles against a narrative backdrop that is carried across the developer's other titles. The addition of co-op is welcome and incredibly well-implemented. I rated this as "compelling", but it's unmissable if you're into the series.

Here's my contemplative take on this atmospheric adventure:Intriguing Narrative & Atmosphere: 4/5The Past Within weaves a mysterious narrative, enveloping players in an atmospheric embrace. The storytelling, though subtle, captivates with its enigmatic charm. The game's world, filled with cryptic clues and haunting ambiance, invites players to unravel the secrets concealed within its depths. The use of environmental storytelling adds an additional layer to the narrative, making exploration a rewarding endeavor.Puzzles & Cognitive Challenges: 3/5While the puzzles contribute to the game's charm, some may find them a tad predictable. The cognitive challenges, however, strike a balance between engaging and contemplative, offering a thoughtful experience without overwhelming the player. The puzzles, though not groundbreaking, manage to integrate well with the narrative, enhancing the overall sense of immersion.Visual Aesthetics & Sound Design: 4/5The game's visual aesthetics, characterized by a minimalist yet captivating art style, complement the mysterious theme effectively. The subdued color palette enhances the sense of intrigue, creating an atmospheric experience. The sound design, featuring subtle cues and a haunting soundtrack, contributes significantly to the game's immersive qualities.ConclusionThe Past Within is a contemplative journey that beckons players to explore its mysterious tapestry. While the puzzles may not stump the most seasoned adventurers, the atmospheric narrative, unique setting, and attention to visual and auditory details create an experience that lingers in the mind, making it a worthwhile exploration into the unknown.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and Dirty:-Lots of "find the combination" style puzzles-Fairly easy (we completed both the Butterfly and Bee versions while exchanging roles, in about 2.5 hours total)-I would price this at $3.99 considering both parties need to buy a copy.-Great addition if you like the Rusty Lake series-Fun hearing the person on the other end get creeped out by what they're seeingI think this game would be good for those new to these types of games, or wanting a casual experience, and/or are fans of the Rusty Lake series (I personally found some of the previous entries more challenging).I find a lot of escape room puzzle style games get tedious and over-reliant with the "find the key/combination" to proceed. To an extent there's no 'escaping' this, but I do appreciate when games try to deviate from 'clock' puzzles ("The Inheritance of Crimson Manor" is probably one of the worst offenders for how many clock puzzles they have). The Past Within at least mixes it up a tiny bit in this area, but not too much. As such we went through the game twice, though both modes and switching roles, in about an hour+ for each run. While we found it fun, and we both enjoyed the Rusty Lake series, we both were left a bit "hungry" after. I'm not sure if there's even a save and restore feature to return later if someone has to leave (though given how short it is, I suspect this game was only ever intended to be completed in one sitting)Things I would improve on is making the Bee and Butterfly modes different from each other, rather than the same thing but with very minor changes (which seems to mostly just be different code sequences). I'm sure this was to allow for people to change roles and experience the story from the other side, but I had hoped for more than just that. I feel the current 5.99 price is a bit high given the experience, very limited replayability, and that both parties need to buy a copy.

_childDocuments_.review: The Past Within is based on a strong time disparity gimmick which is fun to explore and also does not overstay it’s welcome. A strong contender to enjoy some hours with a buddy, but not an outstanding puzzle game.Having not played the past titles, I was really confused by the presentation of the game. There is lore and a whole world of which you can only catch a glimpse with this game. Most stuff does not make much sense as one can not see the big picture and only gets the fundamental ideas. Because of that I would recommend checking out more Rusty Lake, if you are interested in actually understanding the plot. The imagery is disturbing and works well enough in scaring the player without resorting into cheap jump scares, the game is mostly just calm yet menacing.One can not talk about this game without mentioning the gimmick. Both players start the game (without necessarily connecting to the internet, except for the purpose of talking with each other) and then solve relatively simple puzzles, to then hand their earned information to the other player.These are only difficult, if you are having communication problems or do not know what you can interact with. Most of the time the game is smooth sailing, and it can and should be completed in one sitting. Approximately it takes around two to three hours to finish the game.The gimmick is really the main selling point and otherwise The Past Within is relatively unimpressive for the most part. The puzzles need to stay simple as explaining something without seeing can be too frustrating. Rusty Lake (=the developers) did well in designing like that, but it still lacks puzzles that really ask the player to (excuse the pun) think outside the box. It is not about being insanely smart, more of an:I wanted more unconventional puzzles than following a step to step guide which leads to one player communicating some information to the other player in a specific order. Not really, if I am honest. The visual style is interesting, and the sound design works pretty well for the most part, while it uses certain techniques to flip the script on the player by understanding how to present itself. While it is a masterclass at presentation, it is really difficult to find anything which can be called outstanding (except for the gimmick).No insane positives, but also no insane negatives. You got some hours to burn with a buddy of yours and are interested in time-related games?The Past Within is a great game to enjoy the fun of spending time together while somewhat using your brain cells and inhaling the ambience.
