_childDocuments_.review: Connected with an old friend playing this game and we had a great time going "wait, what's it going to... ohhh" and "ahhh, it's doing something...!"  It's a cool little story with neat puzzles.  The gameplay isn't too demanding and provides a lot of that fuzzy, rewarding feeling you get when a friend helps you figure something out for the first time.It's also a neat trick that you don't even need a functioning internet connection to play with someone!  The game's progression is controlled by the puzzle inputs you get from the other person, so you're effectively just on the phone with them and trading information back and forth to solve the puzzle you each have in front of you.  There's two starting positions and you can switch positions after playing through once in order to see the other perspective, but also with different solutions to the puzzles.  The time I've played (probably closer to 4 hours, since we spent a lot of time talking in between playing) is split between two playthroughs.  We had a lot of fun!EDIT: mentioning time played vs what Steam says is my in-game time

name: Arcadegeddon
detailed_description: Gilly, the owner of a local arcade, is trying to save his business from a faceless mega-corporation, Fun Fun Co. ...and what better way to stick it to the man than with a brand-spanking-new super game. Unfortunately, the corp gets wind of Gilly’s plan and launches a cyberattack, injecting a virus into the game. Now it’s up to you, will you rise up to save both the game and the last remaining local arcade? This ever-evolving co-op multiplayer, roguelite shooter allows you and up to 3 friends to explore multiple biomes, compete in mini games, find hidden chests, and battle a crazy cast of enemies and bosses. Arcadegeddon lets you play at your own pace with its mix of PVE and PVP gameplay. Speed into the action or take it slow, it’s up to you. As you get to know the town, you can dive into additional challenges from the local gangs that hangout in Gilly’s Arcade, earning you much more than just street cred. Though, the view from the top of the leaderboards must be pretty darn good...

_childDocuments_.review: + The music is energetic, bassy and definitely fits the cyberpunk-type vibe. Sound design overall is crisp.+ Game performance is very smooth; I haven't had a single hitch or stutter. The graphics are simple but adequate and look to be accessible to a wide range of system specs.+ Vivid colors and effects keep to the arcadey feel but don't go too far as to clutter the screen.+ Voice acting and production is great; characters have a lot of personality. The writing itself is nothing special, a bit campy at times, but the plot works and the characters are likeable.+ Plenty of unlocks to customize your character in all sorts of ways (powers, outfits, colors, weapon skins, etc.) and all are obtainable in a fair amount of game time. The game was clearly balanced with respect to the players' time.+ Microtransactions are usually a negative for me, but this seems to be one of the fairer microtransaction implemenations. The paid currency is only used to unlock cosmetics, all of which can be unlocked through the in-game earned currency. The in-game currency is earned rather quickly, so there really is little to no pressure on the player to purchase currency. It's a good alternative for those that cannot dedicate the same amount of time to play the game and earn cosmetics normally, but doesn't feel forced.+ Multiple gamemodes which all are great fun. Cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes are also available.- Would like to see some more settings available, like FOV slider and toggle ADS option. Could also do with a text input for the sliders so the player can set them without carefully fiddling with the actual slider.- Gunplay and movement is a tad too floaty for my taste; feels similar to Fortnite.- Game does not take exclusive control of the mouse cursor when playing in windowed mode, thus aiming too far down will reveal the mouse in the task bar.- It's annoying having to double back to collect coins after sliding or dodging into boxes to break them. Would like to see an auto-pickup behavior for coins when boxes are broken in this manner. It's an odd break in the natural movement and pacing of gameplay.Base game completed:  NODLC completed:  N/ARating:  6 / 10 - Above Average

_childDocuments_.review: For the price, I've gotten good value out of this game. The shooting feels really good, the challenge is (mostly) appropriate, and I like the pacing of the stages. However, I think the game is missing a lot of features and some of the gameplay design choices are rather questionable. I'll update the review if the devs fix these things. Let's start with the way loot works. Guns have fixed stats that are only improved by the level of their rarity (or "hacks", which are just perks). Close to the start of stages, you have a shop you can use to upgrade the rarity of one gun. This encourages you to pump resources into leveling that gun to get better damage. The more you use a gun, the higher its level gets, and then you can even start runs with that gun. The rarity of the gun improves with its level. Most guns that drop during stages are of a lower rarity than your starting guns, so most loot is ignored. You cannot salvage these guns for resources, so you end up skipping past 99% of the loot that drops. Ultimately, this ends up discouraging changing your loadout in the game, since your favorite guns are better than anything else you can find. Additionally, having most loot being useless like this makes opening a chest less exciting, as you end up just hoping for hacks. You also can't easily change the slots of the guns that you find. I.e., if a gun is equipped on slot 1, you can't easily move it to slot 2. The hacks that drop are what end up being what changes your damage the most. However, their implementation in co-op is rather bizarre. Loot is either shared or instanced, and you can tell by looking at an icon in the top right of the UI element for that item. But that icon is sometimes missing. This makes it confusing to tell who has what loot during rounds. You also can't drop hacks, so if you are running a sniper build and your friend is running shotguns, you can't drop shotgun hacks you find to share with your friend. Hacks can be upgraded. You sacrifice two other hacks to upgrade an existing hack. However, the rates at which a hack can be improved is not clear. I've tried tons of different combinations and sometimes you can more benefit from leveling a hack, sometimes not. The game doesn't explain this at all.The game does not show you the total hack effects in your inventory either. You have to do some mental math to figure out how effective your hacks are. Assuming you have decent aim, sniper rifles seem disproportionately strong. You can one-shot most enemies you find and you do high damage to bosses. You'll often face enemies that are stationary, sniping you from long distances, so having your own sniper rifle feels mandatory. Most of the bosses are totally fine to face, but the FFC Mech is extremely frustrating to face. That boss has more adds spawn than others, causing you to need to focus the adds before fighting the boss. Once you reach stage two of the boss, it starts moving more quickly and gets a pinpoint laser attack. This laser absolutely annihilates your health and you can't really do anything about it. Typically, I tried to hide behind terrain but the laser went through objects and the boss moves so fast that you can't hide for long. And if you're running, you're not shooting adds, which then makes the battle even more hard to deal with. Enemies can spawn literally anywhere, including directly next to you. You'll find yourself unexpectedly losing health to an enemy that spawned in a place you just cleared. I wouldn't mind this if the enemy footsteps were louder, but as is, it makes the enemies hard to detect.The levels have a lot of vertical elements, which makes them interesting to traverse. However, you cannot grapple onto ledges, meaning that if you slightly miss an edge you will fall. I feel like the FPS genre has moved to a point where grappling ledges is a basic feature, so it's weird that it's missing from this game. Despite all this, I still have fun playing the game, but I cannot recommend it. If these issues are worth looking over, then give the game a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Arcadegeddon is a rogue-like third person shooter, that may remind you of something like Warframe, or a really fast Remnant: From the Ashes. It's not a particularly complex game, but it's a solid title, particularly considering the low price point.The art style is pretty gorgeous. At least for an entry into the rogue-lite shoot genre. Not the highest fidelity thing in the world, but when your competition in the Rogue-Lite shooter genre is stuff like Risk of Rain 2, Gunfire Reborn, Roboquest, ArcRunner, etc. you don't have to look like the prettiest thing in the world to stand out as being visually appealing by comparison. Still, regardless of comparison, I find the art style to be appealing anyway.The gun variety seems pretty good. You've got assault rifles, SMGs, pistols, sniper rifles, shotguns, rocket launchers, grenade launchers, and some "unique" weapons (bat, sword, saw blade gun, minigun, Dig Dug gun, laser cannon, and a few more) . Then there's different "manufacturers" of sorts, for the guns, with themes, such as one focused on corrosive damage, one focused on fire damage (where the weapons have heat rather than magazine capacity), one that has smart weapons, one that focuses on ice, and so on. There's a decent number of different guns of each category, and they're decently unique and interesting.That said, there doesn't seem to be random modifiers on weapons They just appear to get stronger with rarity tier. Why does this matter? Once you find a gun you like, you have 0 reason to drop it for any other gun aside from finding higher tiers, because there's no modifiers to mix things up and make other options more or less appealing. Plus you can upgrade one of your guns at shops for a price, so you don't seem to be likely to be outpaced (maybe this changes on higher difficulties though).Furthermore, the game allows you to unlock most guns to use from the start of your run. You get xp and levels with guns as you use them. Once you clear the first level, the gun becomes unlocked to start runs with, and further levels raise the tier of weapons you start with, so there's  no reason to change guns if you max out your weapons and just pick the ones you like from the start.Basically, you can choose what guns you want and never feel a need to switch, which is pretty strange for a rogue-lite.This is as opposed to something like Gunfire Reborn,  where you may find a gun you like early, but may actually decide to swap it out later, since earlier/lower rarity guns don't have as many modifiers as ones you'll find later in your runs.Similarly, upgrades (called "hacks") dropped from chests aren't a selection (again, unlike Gunfire Reborn). They're just pickups. There's almost no reason to even look at what you're getting, because there's no opportunity cost for picking up any given upgrade (and I haven't seen any with explicit negatives, so far). This really only comes into play in shops, where you can decide to make a hack stronger by salvaging two other ones you don't feel you need.A lot of rogue-lites are about managing RNG in a run by making good selections between a variety of options to try to make the best of your situation. That just doesn't really seem to be the case here. It's more of just a straight-up shooter with procedurally-generated levels and loot drops.An interesting thing about the way this game works is that there doesn't appear to be a set order of biomes or bosses. A biome can show up at any time, and the boss you face at any given time is also random. As you play the game, the difficulty ramps up, making enemies and bosses stronger. This can notably add an extra phase (maybe more?) to bosses, so it's different if you face a certain boss first versus if you face it later in a run. This helps make runs feel different, even if you're dying early, because the first zone isn't always the same biome, like it is in many other rogue-lites.You might think this would mean bad things for enemy variety, since that's often tied to zone in games. It actually seems fine so far. You'll pretty much always start off by facing the same robo-soldiers, but even they're pretty interesting, because they're all equipped with jetpacks, making them pretty mobile. Things like exploders, demonic runners, snipers, riot guards, demonic casters, and even stealth units get thrown into the mix pretty rapidly, and keep the game pace pretty hectic. One thing to note is, similar to Remnant: From the Ashes. All of the bosses rely on spawning a ton of adds. There's pretty much always going to be trash mobs spawning in that you'll need to clean as you take on bosses. That said, they don't feel nearly as oppressive as in Remnant, because it's not hard to keep away from them due to your high mobility in Arcadegeddon, and they're pretty easy to take out with some well placed rockets (at least on lower difficulties), which you don't need to conserve, because regenerating ammo boxes are present in all boss arenas.Anyway, I'm having a good time so far. It's not hard to recommend this game for this price. I'm surprised how far under the radar this game seems to be sailing, though the less-than-eye-catching thumbnail for the game on Steam certainly isn't doing it any favors. I hadn't even heard of this game before seeing it on Steam, and it's been on Epic for a year, evidently.A personal criticism: The music kind of makes my ears bleed, honestly, but it fits the setting and action well enough. I still hate most of it though (there's one or two BGMs I actually kind of like). I turned it down to 0. Don't think the music is doing it any favors, in terms of exposure, either, but that's a personal preference. I'm sure some people like it. I'm definitely not one of those people.And a note: I crashed to desktop the first time I tried to challenge a boss. Hasn't happened since, and the game seems to have saved earnings up to that point, but it did kill my run abruptly.It also looks like there's bug on the downtown horde map in which an enemy can spawn outside of the map, making it impossible to complete.Also, yes, the game is playable offline. I unplugged my ethernet cable to test it out offline the first time I booted it. It allowed me to start offline mode of the game as normal, play the tutorial, play a couple runs. Unlock abilities/cosmetics, do quests, and so on. Seems like the only thing missing from offline mode is Time Attack, achievements, and the strictly multiplayer stuff, like PVP and co-op, but I can't say for certain, since not all modes start as unlocked in the game. At the very least, the adventure mode is available, and it  like boss rush and horde mode are available (I haven't unlocked them yet/haven't used the "unlock everything" function, which is apparently a thing for offline mode). Even the rotating cosmetic shop appears to work offline.

_childDocuments_.review: Do note that at the time of writing this review I've totalled about almost 3 hours into Arcadegeddon, and I'm playing purely Solo as none of my friends love me... + Music is phenomenal, helps pump you up for fights and overall is a great soundtrack that doesn't seem out of place for the setting.+ Sound design is also a plus, weapons sound great when firing and when equipping. Enemy death sounds remind me of Tron (of course, another plus)+ Game has a good amount of stage variety, also reminiscent of other games like DnD/Tron.+ On this note, there's a good amount of weapon variety as well.+ Unlocking new weapons for the start of your run is as easy as levelling up. Unlocking new skills is also done well, progression in general is good.+ Boss fights are unique and different for each one.+ Cosmetics in this game are done right! There are some that can be bought with real money of course, but they're mostly earned through either earning the in-game currency from normal runs, or using weapons a certain amount of times to unlock skins for them.+ Arcadegeddon is extremely stylish, very noticeable in the cosmetics and the game overall. Each NPC's design is unique.+ Game runs exceptionally well, I've only had one stutter but I know it's just an issue with my PC lol- Sometimes the gunplay is unsatisfying, this is due to a number of factors I'll get to in a moment, but a lot of the time I felt like shots didn't have too much impact on the enemies I fought.- Movement greatly impacts your weapon's spread, encouraging you to take breaks between shots or swap weapons to reset it. In my opinion this is a negative as the game seems to encourage you to use your movement options while engaging in a fight (your double jump, dodge roll and slide).- Some guns feel a bit  to use, offering little firepower but a lot of spread instead (like some SMGs) and though I do understand that's the idea of certain weapons, it just makes some of them not fun to use.- Moving away from gunplay, the challenges are a bit confusing when starting out. There are multiple gangs (or NPCs that you talk to) that give you a challenge with some optional ones that you can try to complete in your next run. The content of the challenges aren't the confusing part, but rather the distribution of them.  I'm fine with this, however I wish it was conveyed a lot more clearly.- The enemy AI are sometimes... stupid? I watched one "miniboss" looking enemy just jump off the map the moment I started spraying at it.- Going into a fresh run for the first time after booting up the game, you're met with a  of things. Weapons are one of them as opening chests gives you about 2 or 3 to choose from, with seemingly no grace period between some objectives to test them as enemies constantly spawn and seem to swarm you no matter where you are (save for the  safe areas between some sections of a stage).-   Let's just say it could be better.- Turning in the daily quests is a little bugged, you can turn them in but it'll still show you can turn it in constantly but it wont do anything past the initial turn-in.- It is not explained that weapons that have yellow numbers instead of white for their ammo count, are "special weapons" that do not get ammo back from ammo pickups.- Parts of the environment are bigger than what they appear in terms of their hitbox, so some enemies can seemingly be out in the open and vulnerable, but shots will not land.- Depending on what parts of the environment are in the foreground of your screen (or behind your character), some shots can be blocked by things your character isn't aiming at, as if the shots are coming out of the camera view rather than the character.- Someone else had also mentioned this so I'd like to add it here as I feel the same way, but builds generally don't change much. The upgrades you get throughout the game are more stat boosts and nothing really changes your playstyle other than whatever weapons you find.+ Instead of costing the player to increase difficulty, I think it would be better if they were instead rewarded with more cash for trying to challenge themselves.+ On the topic of movement impacting weapon spread, it would be nice to see a crouch implemented though I don't expect it to be, though it would be nice as it could help the movement feel a bit better when paired with the state of weapon spread as it is right now.+ Maybe a reduced weapon drop rate, at least for solo play.+ I would  climbing or mantling to be added. Please... U_U+ Some more accessibility options, an FOV slider. Overall, Arcadegeddon is a game dripping with style and promise. I'd love to see more updates as time goes on especially since it was just added to the steam store about a few days before I'm writing this review. Personally I'm only somewhat enjoying it, but maybe that's because the game's better with others but I wouldn't know. Coming from just having played a few hours of Roboquest, the gameplay did feel a bit lacking to me, but I feel like it can be chocked down to a "personal feel" sort of thing. To each their own, you know? Don't expect to be eased into what the game has to offer though, right after the lil tutorial bit you're basically thrown into the deep end to fend for yourself, but thankfully the game isn't too difficult to start off with so you should be having an ok time.While I do recommend giving Arcadegeddon a go, I'd say grab it when it goes on sale, I mean there is an introductory offer by the time of writing this so that's neat, and absolutely  use this review to finalise your thoughts on the game. Merely sharing my thoughts and hopefully letting some people know what to expect, whether it be good or bad. Either way if you do grab the game, I hope you enjoy  :)

_childDocuments_.review: This game took me by surprise, in a good way! I really thought i was going to hate this game in the first 30-40 mins of doing the tutorial and fiddling with the menus, but MAN am i glad i stayed cuz this will be a game i come back to, time and time again. Heck I've already bought 5 copies for my friends because i was so impressed with the gameplay. Pros:-The gameplay is nice and smooth. Runs very well on the Steam Deck!-Nice variety of levels and enemies.-No pressure to purchase any battlepass or lootboxes/gacha crap. -Cosmetics are VERY EASY to get. Play 1 or 2 games of Adventure mode and you will be able to deck out your person out with a nice snazzy outfit. (There are a TON of clothes and outfits in the game)-When you level up you get skill points you can use to purchase skills and abilities, that you use for your future runs.-Many choices of abilities and skills allow you to have a wide range of builds you can make.-If you like a weapon, you can unlock it so you get it right away when starting new runs by leveling up and using the wep during runs, and the more xp you gain with the weapon the better it is to start out with.-Killer soundtrack. Dubstep while slaughtering enemies is always soo enjoyable. IMOCons:-Cringe zoomer humor written by a 80 year old.-Forgettable characters that try way to hard to be funny. Almost every character is a wannabe Edgelord.-Nobody hosts or searches for public lobbies, very hard to find a match/takes FOREVER to get a match. You will need friends to play a good run, unless you grind your butt off.-Hardly any bosses, only 4 and they are way too over powered if your by yourself and you pass difficulty 15, when solo. Doable with friends however. Also i will add, this game LOVES the CEO boss.Conclusion: -Solid Roguelike with a very generous reward system, extremely enjoyable with friends. The $10 Deluxe upgrade is Very Nice and gives like 8+ outfits and 2500 premium coins which is ALOT of coins, considering how many cosmetics you can buy.8/10 Could use more bosses and players, but for the cheap price of the game, you will get your moneys worth!Update: As of 7/29/23 the games Cross-Play feature is barely functional. Since you can't add friends to your in-game list if they are on another platform. Instead you have to search for a public lobby at the same time and HOPE you find each other, and even if you do indeed find them, there is still no way of adding them or anything during the match. So if you want to play with anyone not on Steam it is nearly impossible and just not worth it. Great game but they lied about the Cross-Play feature!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: the game is fun, the movement is nice it plays like fortnite which is a good and bad thing for people, personally i enjoy the movement and gun play.The rogue lite aspect is nice, you can equip loadouts with starting weapons abilities and perks. Using a weapon will gain exp for the weapon allowing you to be able to equip it at the start of a new run and further levels on the weapons will increase the rarity of the weapon. Im not sure if it maxes out at legendary or if it will max out at rare or something, (the highest i have gotten is uncommon level 3 on one weapon). there are a bunch of weapons each of them kinda unique but mostly only due to the changes in element. (like you have a ice smg and a fire smg). they split the weapons into a bunch of categories and honestly its quite confusing. as far as i have noticed in a run you cant inspect your weapons equipped, you get a little comparison when looking at a weapon on the floor but that is it. it makes it quite hard to understand what type of weapon it is or how to build around the weapons with the hack items.My biggest gripe with the game are Enemy AOE attacks and enemy spawns.with enemy spawns sometimes enemies will spawn on you or behind you. enemies spawning behind isnt that big of a deal but when taking damage it is hard to discern where the damage is coming from and at higher difficulties with a lot of enemies spawning it makes it hard to avoid attacks and find cover. enemies spawning on you is mostly only a problem when they are exploding type enemies.This leads into my problem with aoe which is that it does way to much damage, the exploding enemies are easy to evade but with the spawn system sometimes they just spawn right next to you and take you down to half health and break your whole shield. this wouldn't be much of a problem but it limits the use of melee builds especially with bosses. every boss i have encountered (and there are a decent amount i have only encountered 5) has an Aoe ability. and every Aoe attack will without question take you down to half (unless you stacked shield and health hacks). combine this with the fact that there is no way to  dodge them and melee damage is actually tragic (and the fact there is only two melee weapons a sword and a bat) makes me question why melee is in the game, melee is fun don't get me wrong and against normal enemies its actually quite good but its not viable especially when the boss fights dont seem very balanced, (especially the shield boss who's only attack is an aoe blast, the arena is too small, multiple normal enemies continuously spawn, the boss can teleport right next to you, he can 2-3 shot you, the aoe blast radius is ridiculous and sometimes he will do two aoe attacks within a second of each other which basically one shots because the first blast should've pushed you away but since the arena is so small it only pushes you into a wall where the second attack will still reach you.).Overall i do recommend the game, its not impossible, yet i have still to beat it with 6 hours as of writing. I like the difficulty setting though am confused on what it actually does apart from giving enemies more health and spawning more. i think the game need more balance or maybe it was balanced for multiplayer more than single player, i have yet to touch the multiplayer side but will try it out. there are a nice set of task/ challenges to do and the player customisation is quite good. Basically if fortnite was a roguelite. ( thinking of it now the zombie enemy type look so similar to the fortnite zombies)

_childDocuments_.review: Game plays amazingly, it reminds me a lot of fortnite. The gunplay and the weapons feel very punchy and there is a lot of instant dopamine colorful explosions and loot. The music is honestly pretty good and fits the theme of the game perfectly! Lotta fun if you have a friend too or a couple but it's entirely optional (except if you really want the unlockable pvp stuff). The game also features the best cosmetics system, you can get anything cosmetic super quick just by playing one or two hours but you also have the option to buy premium currency if you don't like waiting, and the premium currency price is very cheap on top of the rate of in-game credits you get from runs being super high so you get a ton of bang for your buck on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Good soundtrack, but the gameplay is very repetitive and gets highly boring after 20 or so runs. The ammo is a problem at higher difficulties because bosses are bullet sponges. It feels there is little progression so when I fail a run I usually just alt F4 making me feel little to no reason to log back in. There is other games that do this exact game play better. The mechanics are clunky and the inputs are heavily delayed to put the icing on the cake. You cant quick scope with snipers because the delay in the scope out and return. This game is unfortunately just bad in current state.

_childDocuments_.review: Man the Soundtrack is worth the price alone, it really pumps up the aesthetic and they cycle the tracks so they don't get old.Gameplay is a little bit like Risk of Rain with the spawning/item distribution, Roboquest with how the levels are done (Big handcrafted arenas randomly connected together).The style is, man, you are getting Cyberpunk+Tron with a heavy dose of Splatoon and 80/90's Vibe. The sound effects are all great and full of little details like the enemies scream glitching out as they fly apart is straight ear-candy. The art director knows how to build a tone, give this person a raise, it is sick AF! The payout for unlocking stuff is really generous for getting cosmetics and unlocking weapons is simply just using the weapon enought to level it up or leveling up your character to get skills.My only 2 gripes are CEO boss is a slog to fight and he can teleport+OHKO you if you don't have full shield, really sucks to hit him in a solo run.  #2 is minor but the game likes to randomly hop back to Display 1 if you set it to a different one, seems most frequent during cutscenes or if you go change settings.Overall - Fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: So much to criticize about this game. The presentation and dialogue makes me want to seriously hurt myself (and i've played multiple Borderlands games!), the map layouts sometimes get confusing enough to completely sucker-punch the fast paced flow the game is trying to establish, you have to shoot-n-loot a-la Borderlands but it never really works because it's practically impossible to identify if a weapon is a shotgun, pistol or SMG without swapping it into your loadout and the game throws a million 'do X' and 'kill Y' missions at you without any way to track them in a run that i've foundBut with all that being said, it's fifteen buckaronis, and you can easily get that money's worth if the idea of a roguelite Fortnite No Build appeals to you. Which it does to me, so i'll still recommend it. Though with a slight groan and a shrug.

_childDocuments_.review: For a Third Person Shooter Roguelike, it has a lot of positives(Personal Opinion, I don't expect anyone to agree)Pros:Mechanics feel fluent and well fleshed outMusic is a plusGauntlet abilities feel powerful and rewarding when you obtain and use themGun Level tracking through every run, rewarding you for using certain weapons for a period of timeGun Level is tracked by XP instead of kills, so pull off sick combos with it and you could start your next run with a better gunCons:One of the bosses feel a bit overpowered vs the other ones (The Mech with the turret on the slide of it's head and blades for hands, looking like a praying mantis)The music files are not uploaded to the steam store so if you buy them, they don't exist.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah so went into this not expecting much and was THOROUGHLY surprised.Highly recommend this game if you're into roguelites. Movement is great, enemy variety is great, map design, atmosphere, upgrades, all great.One thing that did bother me is that a lot of the fully auto weapons, including shotguns, just have the worst accuracy known to man until you UPGRADE your accuracy. _childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun game! In solo as well as with friends, putting hours in to try to get the best score of the week is really really fun. This game feels like a weird mix of Risk of Rain 2 and borderlands. This game also has guns for everybody. Let it be snipers, heavier guns, assault rifles or a bunch of really creative guns. Price is quite fair for the amount of time that I sinked and am still sinking into this game.There a few things that feel like they could be a little better though:- There are only four bosses and by completing a boss run you are assured to come across them all. It would be fun if there could be more of them to make runs a bit more different each time. This is especially true when you decide to continue a run after beating them all, and just encounter the same bosses over and over.-The FFC mech boss doesn't feel very fair, because his strongest attacks ignore the environment and hit you anyway.- More areas to visit could be a really fun addition.- Being unable to double jump in the arcade feels a bit weird, because after a long run you have adapted to how your character moves, then you get back to the arcade and you forget that you can't double jump and just run into a wall. (happens to me almost every time)- For the love of god... High score meter please!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting third person shooter. It lives up to its name with a very arcade-y feel to it. I bought this game after seeing a couple of people claim that it is like Risk of Rain 2. I don't agree with that other than it being a third person shooter. Risk of Rain has characters with abilities and as you progress through a run, you're adding dozens of different items that alter your offense and defense. In this game You have a "Surge Gauntlet" that you equip with a couple of abilities and some passives, but in game you're mostly trying to obtain better guns. You do get modifications that can alter damage and stuff, but that portion doesn't feel satisfying, certainly nowhere near the fun of what Risk of Rain offers. That said, I am still enjoying the game.

Not only that but the system around "adventure" provides a very fun loop, and you actually feel like you're advancing and making progress.Customization is okay, I like a lot of the costumes and the fact you can get them all simply by playing and buying them makes it for a fun system.Story is just very meh. Voice acting could be better, feels like something from the 2000s, but if that's what the devs intended then they're forgiven.But with all that the game for some reason never really had many players. In my opinion, this game never had any proper advertising and the box art is horrendous. That ♥♥♥♥♥♥ robot logo with the awful ugly text? Looks like shovelware.And it turns out, I actually had this game on playstation via PS Plus, but I never bothered downloading it because it had that ugly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ art! I literally found out about this game via steam's discovery list while on a sale!Don't know how old this game actually is, but I'll simply say that it's very fun and for the price it's actually worth it. Provides as much content as other shooter rogue-lites with a fun art-style. Oh yeah and the music is also just mediocre. Could just be my bad taste for dubstep.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game a lot so far. The third person camera angle and floaty-feeling gunplay gives it a Fortnite type of feel, which for many is an instant turn away, but I can't help but enjoy the fast paced nature of the game. I am worried for the longevity of the game, whereas a roguelike like RoR2 I can always go back and play, having nearly 400 hours in - I'm not sure this game could be the same for me.I love the colors and the soundtrack, which also aren't for everyone. My biggest gripe so far with the game is that weapons don't really give you any sort of insight into what they are until you actually pick it up and shoot it. You can get an idea from the firerate and damage, but if I see a gun that looks like a pistol that shoots every 2 seconds for 300 damage, I'm kinda confused on what its purpose is. I also find it a bit subtle when you take damage. For instance, a boss could be spraying you or one of the explosive enemies could chuck your shield/hp, and you may have no idea unless you look at your health bar. There doesn't feel like much of a visual aid when it comes to taking damage.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: good for the price but don't expect anything super new unless they add stuff later down the line.So far it is a pretty decent game. The two games it reminds me most of are "Roboquest" and "gunfire reborn" in the sense of the way enemies spawn and the different obtainable weapons. They don't add a huge amount to the type of game it is but it is very solid and it has a quest system in order to unlock cosmetics.The one thing I wish for is to be able to purchase stuff with your tickets that are not just cosmetic such as a buff or something that lasts one stage. I feel as if the progression system was not just for cosmetics it would add an extra factor for the game.one big con though, I purchased this game and there are still premium currency. I beleive premium currency should be used for free games like overwatch (crudy game btw) or fortnite. but having to pay for just the game and see that there is premium currency is a little odd. I know its optional but it is still off putting.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom is adding DRM Enigma Protector to its new and even old games on Steam. This DRM decreases game performance by 15 fps, causes frequent stuttering and blocks modding.Most of these games were cracked by pirates a long time ago and while pirates who didn't pay for the game play the games without the new DRM damaging the game's performance, those who paid for the game are suffering from the games' performance being impaired thanks to the new DRM. This encourages piracy.Many Capcom games have problems that have not been officially fixed by the company and there are mods made by the passionate community of fans that fix these problems. Mods greatly improve games, increasing their replayability. Blocking mods is unacceptable.That's why I'm leaving this negative review. If you were planning on buying this game, don't do it. I recommend buying these games on consoles where your performance is not hampered by DRM.If Capcom decides to go back and remove this new DRM, I will go back and remove my negative review as well.

_childDocuments_.review: CAPCOM - How did you get this so wrong?So arcade games are all about the high scores right? Getting a high score, uploading your name and then trying to beat your high score on returning game sessions.So here is how I have found playing a game on CAS.Start playing 1943, get a high score, enter initials. Exit the cabinet but still view it in the arcade. High score is gone.Enter the 1943 cabinet to check - yep, high score is no where to be seen.I would say this is such a major oversight on probably what is a fundamental feature arcade games must have - the ability to save your high score - and yet look at the dramas that seem inherent in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If this was supposed to be competition against emulation and ageing hardware, it's a disaster.The review score summary on the Steam store search list showed 81% positive reviews for Capcom Arcade Stadium, but on the direct store page itself it was actually only 37% positive. Nothing on the page addressed this issue. I'll call the games within it  to avoid confusing any of them for the base game.The product itself wants 4 GB to be a 3D store page that essentially just cycles across some DOS minigames within it that you can buy, but doesn't show their prices, and confusingly the playable one is among them. When it links you to the Steam store page for the minigame you're looking at (making the game itself a bit redundant?) it features a different product, and even if you find the minigame you were looking for (which has its own pricetag on the bundle info page it's listed on) you can't get it unless you by it in an expensive bundle (and there's more than one bundle for some reason).They recreated an arcade but they were so greedy it's like they forced you to put pennies in half of all the machines just to play your favorite. If they cared about these old minigames (which would be about 3 MB in size each, taking about 1 second to download, and we've already paid for them years ago) and genuinely liked the idea of people still playing them, then why did they treat them like they were just opportunities to rake in more money?The free minigame logo wallpapers are not for the individual minigames themselves. The free minigame itself isn't translated into English, the controls are awkwardly all towards the left half of the keyboard, and the arcade screen isn't even vertically centered on the monitor. It doesn't sound like an arcade, as the only ambient audio is an unimpressive music track that loops. Apparently certain buttons change the speed or rewind gameplay, but I can't find the controls page for them.There's an achievement for  Is that a healthy and fun achievement? Or do they just want to pressure customers into spending an unrealistic amount of time on a casual game to artificially raise the profile of it - making people think it must be fun if it's worth playing, when in reality it's a messy cash-grab with a horrendous DLC system.There's pages that come up constantly to explain the most mundane functions of the game, but then when you actually select the free minigame it'll throw you in without even a hint at the controls, and can't be paused, and even flashes  on the screen misleading you into thinking it hasn't started. So you lose the run, and there's no button for , and you find that the game's awarded you an achievement for  because of it.I can't help but feel like the failure was more on the part of the publisher than the customer.

_childDocuments_.review: So far so bad.Who's genius idea was it to map a game speed up button rather than just give you a speed selection in the Start menu?So if you play street fighter. Rather than the 6 action buttons being mapped like normal to a controller, some aren't mapped, in favour of a speed up button. This speeds up the game (not turbo mode - menu's as well). Then you have no way of going back to the normal speed without faffing about.Nothing in menu settings. You have to map a button to the slow down the gameplay. Go back into gameplay, slow it down (you have no idea what the correct speed is), then go back into settings and set your controls again). So unintuitive. This will happen for most people that test the controls, realise they are not mapped and change the controls to proper street fighter controls.Every time you press a button you get a pop up guide telling you most obvious stuff like how to select a game. Buying a game is unintuitive. You click on a game, it takes you to the steam shop. You click on 'buy'. Then you click 'install game' - and nothing happens. No indication if was downloading or anything. I had to quit the game, then check the Steam store which was very difficult to find any DLC content for this. Then click a few buttons with no idea if it downloaded or not. Started the game again and it was there. Not a good system if you are supposed to do this for multiple games.The main camera display is stupid. Made to look like an arcade, complete with screen angled away from you so all the gameplay is in a trapezium shape instead of a rectangle. You can change it but why is this the default?The idea for this is great and I'm sure all the games play well but the front end is a disaster.I played this game for 15 minutes and encountered this many problems already.Install fightcade instead. Made by amateurs that know what they are doing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game collection's got Street Fighter II CE.No.  I'm not talking about Champion Edition.I'm talking about Censored Edition.Who wants that?Can you believe that Capcom censored Street Fighter II in this game collection?I can't!  I never thought I'd see the day.Street Fighter II is one of Capcom's greatest achievements.  It's puzzling to see them ashamed of it instead of proud of it.I want the real thing.  I do not want a watered-down censored, neutered version of a game.Only the original will do.I cannot recommend this game.The user interface is extremely laggy. This means that games made decades ago run poorly, even on the latest hardware.To make matters worse, the games lack online multiplayer. This means that you will not be able to get an online match in Street Fighter if you play this game collection.What's the point in buying it then?Capcom, you really need to provide a lag-free experience in your games.The game needs to play smoothly and the online experience needs to be enjoyable, with no noticeable lag.It's no wonder that the Street Fighter V champ would rather play Guilty Gear these days."Victor “Punk” Woodley qualified to play in his fourth run in the worldwide tournament, but when asked how he plans to prepare for the higher levels in the tournament, the Street Fighter V champ says he’d rather play Guilty Gear – or rather “Imma just play Guilty Gear.”After the confused expressions from the tournament commentators and the flurry of emojis in the livestream’s chat, Punk said “I’m in Capcom Cup. There’s no reason for me to play this game anymore. I don’t like the lag so I’m not going to force myself to play.”

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest I am a bit surprised with the ongoing trend of negative reviews here. Not that Capcom Arcade Stadium is a perfect compilation by any means. Initially I was also very frustrated with Capcom offering only large bundles instead of individual games.But now, since you can order each game individually, I don't see any reason to criticize the monetization. (And this comes from a guy who hates micro-transactions). 2 € for one game - even if it's old - really should not be too much to ask for. And the bundles are still available as an alternative.What you get here is a nice collection of Capcom Arcade classics. Especially if you are a fan of Beat 'em Ups, Shoot 'em Ups or Fighting games like myself, you will find a great library of games here. Of course not all of these games have aged perfectly, of course they are mostly designed with a very harsh or even unfair difficulty due to their Arcade origin. But if you are here, considering to buy this collection, then you probably know that already.I myself am happy to have (re-)discovered 19XX, 1944 and Progear through this collection. And Giga Wing alone was worth getting, simply one of my favourite games of all time.On the plus side, Capcom Arcade Stadium offers Score Attack (or Time Attack) mode with online rankings, choice of english and japanese ROMs for each(?) game, game manuals as well as a few customization options like wallpapers, screen filters and the looks of the Arcade cabinet lineup.Furthermore, if you are not playing Score Attack mode, you can save and load your game (32 save slots available), play at different speeds or even rewind a few seconds. All these options can help a lot whenever you need to practice a particular section of a game.Unfortunately Capcom Arcade Stadium really drowns you in tutorial screens when you first start up the game. This is not only annoying, but also contradicts the "pick-up-and-play" nature of Arcade games. The menues are a bit cumbersome, too. After a bit of time though, you are free to enjoy yourself and chase those high scores. The CASPO and ranking mechanic is nice to have as another exterior motivation. But you can also easily ignore that if you don't like it.Other than that the only real thing bringing this compilation down for me personally is the lack of online multiplayer. And the lack of "The Punisher" (which Capcom probably won't license again), one the most hilariously fun Arcade Beat 'em Ups ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom is adding DRM Enigma Protector to its new and even old games on Steam. This DRM decreases game performance by 15 fps, causes frequent stuttering and blocks modding.Most of these games were cracked by pirates a long time ago and while pirates who didn't pay for the game play the games without the new DRM damaging the game's performance, those who paid for the game are suffering from the games' performance being impaired thanks to the new DRM. This encourages piracy.Many Capcom games have problems that have not been officially fixed by the company and there are mods made by the passionate community of fans that fix these problems. Mods greatly improve games, increasing their replayability. Blocking mods is unacceptable.That's why I'm leaving this negative review. If you were planning on buying this game, don't do it. I recommend buying these games on consoles where your performance is not hampered by DRM.If Capcom decides to go back and remove this new DRM, I will go back and remove my negative review as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome, loving homage to the best of Capcom's 1980s and '90s arcade greats. Each arcade title is available at the DLC, but you can buy a bundle with all of them. Each game is playable with rewind, fast forward, cloud enabled state-saving, and most importantly - infinite coinage.In addition, each game features a loving recreation of instructions for modern players to explain not only what the game is "about", but also how to play. Fighting games include move lists... And both traditional Xbox controllers as well as xinput fighting sticks are supported.IT ALSO SUPPORTS SHARED SCREEN MULTIPLAYER FOR UP TO 4 PLAYERS (for arcade games that supported that)The steam version goes further and supports remote play together and full cloud saves.Truly a gold standard in quality when it comes to bringing vintage video games to modern audiences.

_childDocuments_.review: The games play well compared to the Nintendo Switch version. Lost Worlds' analog controls are simulated seamlessly. Built in autofire and button macros make doing special moves in games like Final Fight easier than ever!  MOST IMPORTANTLY, there's barely any input lag at all, COMBINE THAT with one of the nicest frontends I've seen in a good long while with LOTS of well-researched  throwbacks to Capcom's history, and you SHOULD have a slam dunk..It's not that hard to figure out . Mandating video evidence of someone's skill proves their authenticity AND keeps competition healthy by revealing scoring tricks to anyone looking to push their favorite games even further. THIS URGENTLY NEEDS TO BE FIXED. If there's no way to tell a legit player apart from a fraud, one of the most compelling reasons to continue playing an arcade game is lost !I still highly recommend Arcade Stadium because these are must play games; but it's a very reluctant yes. I know CAPCOM can do better than this. Score verification has been figured out for years !!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has putz'd around with MAME for years, messed with so many front-ends, bezels, marquee art, CRTs, cabinets, and got it all working just to let it sit around unplayed, this simple solution from Capcom could have saved me a lot of time and effort. No technical distractions, just good, fun arcade games that are EASY and inexpensive to buy with scanline shaders and ranked leaderboards. It's so easy to get lost in building a cabinet and fussing with emulators when publishers need to follow Capcom's model on this one (I'm looking at you, Bandai Namco) and focus on making their back catalogs accessible on Steam like this. No, it's not flawless--I don't like they made a second stadium app--but it's easy as hell and gets you playing. On an OLED monitor, the inky blacks and display options work nicely if you're not doing anything too out of the ordinary. I enjoy the controls with a keyboard actually more than with arcade sticks even. If you're not an arcade purist, and if you like this hybrid between PC and arcade gaming (just like with video pinball games), then you'll probably enjoy this. I didn't realize Capcom had so many arcade games, and some are super fun. They deserve to continue to be played, and I'm glad Capcom has made them available like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Capcom Arcade Stadium

_childDocuments_.review: I think Capcom did a good job with this, and making the games as accessible as possible, especially for those of us who just want to take a tour of some games and don't mind having to cheat to do it. We get as many save slots as we want, slow motion, rewinds, and even an invincibility cheat. In that respect it compares favorably to Konami's arcade collection for example. I'll nitpick a couple of things: Why do all games share a pool of save slots, instead of having their own pools? Why do I have to confirm saving in a slot that is empty? That's about it though.

Technically you have the option of buying the games individually to tailor the collection to your liking, but Capcom kind of ruined that as a concept first by making a sequel that doesn't integrate, and then by other collections like the Beat Em Up Bundle and Fighting Collections that overlap with this. I really wish Arcade Stadium 2 had just been additional DLC for this instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - 11/19/2023 - Time for the proper reviewHundo'd both, so time for the proper review...except I keep hitting the character limit here so I'm putting it in the 2nd Stadium which is practically the same as this except different. Short version: the games themselves are good, the bizness decisions and design decisions for the Stadium "Wrapper" are not so good. Lastly, YOU CAN CHANGE THE DISPLAY SETTINGS TO MAKE IT LOOK LIKE A NORMAL GAME SO DON'T THINK YOU'RE STUCK WITH ARCADE CAB SIMULATION AS THE ONLY WAY TO PLAY. That was the biggest complaint most had, so I had to make sure folks knew it wasn't unfixable. See my guide for further instructions.Pre-lim Review starts here:So, normally I would wait until I got the 100% of cheevos in a game before reviewing it and also waiting for the Dust to settle, updates-wise (I never really liked games changing while I'm playing them, unless that's part of the game of course), but there's a cheevo that requires you to play a game 1000 times sooooo....I'mma just post a preliminary review because I see a fair amount of negative reviews that refer to stuff that seems to have been fixed in updates.Date: 6/27/2022Preface: Got the 3 Pack Bundle because I actually knew I wanted to play enough of a percentage of the games in the bundle to warrant not just buying things individually. Might have been a mistake due to some sort of "Time Limited Bonus" you can get after you buy a game for the stadium, but oh well, I hate IRL Time Limited stuff in games anyway. Players should own their games, not the other way around, ya know?Intro: Right away, my first impression was "that's a lot of introduction/tutorial popups for a glorified emulator library program" There's got to be a better way to present this info, ya know? Anyway, the menuing isn't the worst, but to those who are more used to basic no-nonsense stuff for old games, this kind of "Wow, look at all this cool stuff we hired a graphic design to model and everything" menu is probably a turn off. I can understand why. "Why are you wasting my CPU power on this?," they're apt to say. (I say it too, honestly. I would have much prefered a simpler interface without such excess.) But I guess this was to try to hype it up, or something? Anyway, my rig can cope so no big deal for me.Next, I went to get to the game I actually wanted to play first: Bionic Commando. After going through what should have been just a listbox but was instead a bit more, I found the game and started it. Immediately, more Tutorial Pop-Ups. Really, people? There has to be a better way. At least they stop showing up after they're done. Anyway, I get through the mess of pop-ups and find....oh. Oh dear. It's one of  arcade simulators eh? The kind that tries to simulate playing on an actual cab by messing with your view of the game in ways including: wasting CPU/GPU by adding a 3D cabinet as a border for the game screen, distorting your view of the game by making the game screen be viewed from an angle instead of straight on, and having screen distortion at extreme angles instead of actually making the game look good. Now, this gimmick is obviously a nuisance and there are other reviews that call it out as such.  if you go into the display settings, you can change the display to actually look like a game and not a simulation of a game. Change the "Frame" to "2D", change the "Display Size" to "Normal", and change the "Display Filter" to...well, I went with "Type B" but this is the aesthetics setting so it's not like I have a clue what it "should" be. The net result is that this looks like a good emulator instead of a bad simulator. Problem solved. (I will write a guide if there isn't one already.)Next, a different (and old) review mentioned that there was no way to set the game speed before starting. But in the current version, when I select a game and then go to "Game Settings", there is in fact a setting there to set the game speed there. So it looks like the Devs are actually addressing the issues so far.Another old review said that, at least in the case of Street Fighter II, the six action buttons weren't even mapped. In the current version though, that seems to have been addressed. I went into the Controller Settings and found that buttons were set up in what seemed like a pretty reasonable configuration and all the stuff that should be mapped actually was mapped. I also found that you can map buttons as you please, even unmapping some functions (like the speed) entirely if you don't like them (there's literally an Erase function to simply remove the mapped button from a function, which is actually something a lot of games lack entirely). There's even an initially unmapped pair of actions for the Light/Medium/Heavy Punches/Kicks at the same time, though I have no idea where that would go on a controller. I should mention, though, that I was using a normal, non-arcade controller when I did this since I haven't committed to investing in an arcade controller. Yet. So, there's a chance the devs haven't set up the game to work nicely with Arcade Controllers. If/when I get one, I'll update this review with my findings.Buying more games was listed as difficult in a review...and I cannot speak to that because I bought the 3 pack bundle so there's nothing left for me to buy. Honestly, I'd just stick to the steam store for that anyway.Now, I should repeat, this is just my prelim review. I wasn't planning on writing it, but I did anyway because if I had read the currently displayed reviews for this game I'd probably have never given this collection/glorified emulator a chance. Except the problems in those reviews have apparently been addressed. So yeah, it seems like the Devs are actually trying not to be awful here and have been fixing the mess. Good, as the world does not need more "Awful Ports of Old Games as a Cash Grabbing Exercise" rot. This "game" still needs some work though, especially in the "UX" department. But I'd say it's worth the $2.99 per title it offers so far, especially if you already know you like those titles.Edit: Update: 7/25/2022All ya'll saying this game has microtransactions don't know what MTX even is. MTX would be charging you per play, or for play time. Or for wallpapers you don't even want. (BTW, Arcades INVENTED microtransactions, and they still did it better/more fairly than modern games. Getting good meant not paying as much.) But here, for each DLC, you are literally paying for free play of a game forever. An entire game, which was (usually) well liked when it came out, and isn't some trashy mini-game.And the 'nickel'd and dimed to death' gripe some reviews have? I'm sorry, but what about the people who literally just wanted 1 game out of the whole collection? Or the people who only like shmups/fighters/etc? And all the people who can't afford to get all the games at once? Why should they suffer? And if you want all the games, there's literally a button on the store page to buy them all. Not forcing you to buy all the games is actually quite consumer friendly, and a great use of the concept of DLCs. Even the cheevos are set up nicely for that, since they're not tied to any specific game in the collection.BUT! Capcom or whoever decided how to sell it all gets big points off in my book for not using Steam's Bundle feature, instead opting for the Package method. Even though Capcom or whoever doesn't offer any Bundle Discounts for the content, it's still better for consumers if you make sure to not offer any purchasing methods that could result in buyers paying for something they already own and won't get a second copy of. So, Silver (not Gold) medal for buyer friendliness so far. But this is still a prelim review.Edit: 8/2/2022 - Real quick: none of the cab styles I can use so far look like the irl cabs. Kinda defeats the point of the "showing virtual cabs" thing, I think. Not a deal breaker for me though.

_childDocuments_.review: I played many of these games back in the arcades. I actually worked in an arcade (Yes, I'm an ancient teen and no, I never grew up) and I remember all of these games. I still remember changing paper money into tokens in order to play. Ghosts 'n Goblins and Ghouls 'n Ghosts are my all-time favorites as far as arcade games go. The ability to rewind in-game and the invincibility function are what truly made me love this collection. This version (as far as I remember) is the most authentic feel to the original game play of these games back in the day. It is depressing seeing the negative reviews on this collection. It may not be the best presentation as far as the UI goes in selecting games; (very bland) but I still enjoy this collection.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great collection of old Capcom classics. For around $2 per game, you get approximately 30 games from the early days up to the early 2000s, like Progear. What you get are primarily great entries, but there's some unnecessary overlap with the three versions of Street Fighter 2, and the variety of gameplay is reduced to platforming, shmups, fighting, and beat them-ups, with an emphasis on shmups and beat-them-ups. The available game modes are fun and offer an element of score-chasing as if you were really in the arcade. The fact that each game is presented on a cabinet of your choice helps with options to change filters, cabinet type, or the usual on-screen presentation with border images. Some of the older games have poor scaling and don't fill the screen space as much as they should, and you can see that some games have moderate emulation issues. But these are not very annoying things. Still, as a relatively casual gamer, I found most games decent. Overall, it's an excellent collection of games with a few issues, and it is priced reasonably, even before any sales. If you are a retro gamer, this package you will be noticed. Give it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The undying fashion for retro makes dinosaur publishers compile nostalgic collections of their former hits - and they do it with varying success. SEGA had the SEGA Mega Drive Collection, Konami had anniversary reissues of Contra and Castlevania, and Capcom had already turned to the Megaman collections and Walt Disney's cartoon legacy in the Disney Afternoon Collection. Now they have also presented to the public CAPCOM Arcade Stadium – another set of great (and not so great) classics of the era of VHS cassettes.They won't be ruined by the visual presentation either. All games lend themselves to flexible display settings, including an imitation of an arcade machine booth with a tilted screen. And a large set of special filters will easily turn your modern 4K TV into an old father's "Ruby" - and no one will tell you that you can plant a kinescope.Finally, following all modern trends, Capcom tied high score tables, special tests, user-friendly manuals and achievements to the game. From the generosity of the soul, we even brought a choice of ROM – most of the games are available in two versions, English and Japanese, and some are available only in the original.Capcom Arcade Stadium itself is just a platform, only one game is built into it for free – the legendary Ghosts ‘n Goblins. All the others can either be purchased separately or as part of three thematic packages. Gamers in a rage have already condemned the publisher for greed, although let's be honest with ourselves – most of us and our parents did not have (money and opportunities) then in the 90s to buy a licensed cartridge from the NES or SEGA Mega Drive. Now we can honestly pay Capcom for a happy childhood – except that the sale of invulnerability mode and design frames looks very greedy and stupid.As for the games themselves, then, probably, it is not necessary to say once again how outdated almost all of them are now, both morally and even more physically. It is currently not possible to perceive most of the 30+ games without condescension and irony. And even then, perhaps, not all games from the list can be called examples of art.There is no great reason to talk about each game – even a simple enumeration of them with an extremely brief synopsis would take a good couple of pages. Almost all the games from the set can be divided into four categories: fighting games, action platformers, bitemaps and arcade scroll shooters.The former are represented primarily by as many as several versions of Street Fighter II, including Super Street Fighter II Turbo, released on the first PlayStation and Sega Saturn. Another fun addition is the game Cyberbots: Full Metal Madness, which in fact did not leave Japan. There is no practical value in this clone of the "Street Fighter about Mechs", but it is interesting to look at it.There are also quite a few bitemaps in the set – from the legendary Final Fight to the lesser-known Captain Commando and Battle Circuit. Since over the past years the genre has almost died and only recently showed signs of life, even these ancient hits of the past are now being played quite fun and funny.The absolute winner of the collection by the number of representatives of the genre was a variety of scrolling shooters of all varieties and colors. The 194x series was the luckiest of all – it was added here almost in full, from the most ancient parts that came out in the mid-1980s to those that appeared already in the midst of the 1990s. Most of them are arranged according to the same principle, and therefore if you played one of them, you get the feeling that you saw literally everything. Nevertheless, these are still pleasant, and sometimes very exciting arcade games.The smallest and most interesting in the entire collection would like to call platformers, among which two (or rather three) stand out: Strider is a dystopian hack-n-slash that became a kind of progenitor of the God of War and Devil May Cry series and the stylish, dark and incredibly hardcore Ghosts ‘n Goblins with its sequel. These three games are rightfully still considered iconic and there are many reasons for that.Capcom Arcade Stadium is a convenient and comfortable collection of three dozen classic arcade games of a bygone era. Even if not all games have survived to the present, curious and retromans should definitely pay attention to such an offer.Rating 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr review: Don't believe the DRM hating liars, Capcom Arcade Stadium does not have performance issues. The only issues CAS has is the game selection is meh and the whole thing is overpriced. Some are also missing their NA ROMs for ??? reasons. Not bad enough for a thumbs down, but not worth buying unless on sale.----------tl;dr stuff----------Like many people, I didn't buy Capcom Arcade Stadium due to all the negative reviews. I got it as part of a humble bundle and after messing around with CAS 1 and 2 for hours, here's what I've discovered with CAS 1:There tends to be 3 types of negative reviews: 1. Apparently, when it first came out, CAS was in a pathetic state. I didn't own it then, so I don't know how bad. Capcom supposedly ironed out the worst issues since then. Many of these reviews WERE legit, but haven't been updated. 2. There are lots of bad reviews over Capcom adding DRM claiming this makes CAS run poorly. This is 100% BS. CAS runs just fine on my PC. I can only figure CAS runs poorly on a potato PC since it renders a fake arcade using RE Engine. These reviews are from loser communists and pirates who compulsively throw fits over DRM and will do and say anything to make games with DRM not sell. The current top 2 reviews are lazy copy pastes for Christ sake! I wouldn't be surprised if the 'poor performance' is due to getting the free game and hacking/modding CAS to play the rest. These are stupid people who shouldn't even care. Anyone can easily get MAME and play every Capcom arcade game for free.3. Street Fighter 2 censorship. I agree with this one. Capcom, China's militant Communist government hates Japan and capitalism. Why would you censor E. Honda's stage and Hong Kong's flag to appease them? They're just going to steal what you're trying to sell there anyway. This makes you look like a spineless idiot!Overall, this collection is a mixed bag. Numerous classics along with lots of trash that hasn't aged well. Many games included also appeared in the awful Cacpom Arcade Cabinet. I seem to remember those games not being emulated accurately. CAS' emulation is essentially 1:1 arcade perfect outside the idiotic censorship.Nice things about this collection: 1:1 perfect emulation. save states and a rewind feature in real time. The fake arcade provides a nice, yet pointless aesthetic. Bad things: Apparently, if you don't buy all the games, CAS will spam ads at you to buy the ones you don't own. The SF2 censorship is idiotic. No on-line multiplayer. Its missing a few NA ROMs. Where's SF2 RAINBOW EDITION, Capcom? Huh! Where is it?!?that said, here are my thoughts on certain games in this collection:((((( pre-CPS Capcom ))))) Early Capcom era. Capcom knew how to make games, but not how to make them fun. Most games from this era suck. This collection actually has the best ones.Vulgus: Captain Commando himself personally told me this was Capcom's first video game released to arcades in 1984! Thank you, Captain Commando! Game sucks tho.Ghosts and Goblins: Lots of people love this game. I don't like it since its harder than a witch's tit in winter.1942: I'm not sure if this was a hit in NA arcades or not, but I did see it a lot. Its ok. Premise is weird for a Japanese developer tho.Commando: Distinct arcade hit in NA when it came out. I stink at it and find it frustrating. Data East distributed it in NA for some reason.Section Z: Sucks. Showcases Capcom's habit of making frustrating difficult not-fun arcade games and porting a more enjoyable version to the NES.Tatakai no Banka: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, Capcom! You released this in NA as Trojan! You know what? Who cares, this game sucks anyway. NES one was better.Bionic Commando: another example of the arcade version being ass and the NES version being different and better.((((( CPS-1 era Capcom )))))this is where Capcom began to make a name for themselves in arcades with genuinely good, fun games.Forgotten Worlds: Capcom's 1st CPS game! This game needs a spinner for the authentic experience. BTW, if you actually have a Forgotten Worlds spinner, they're rare and quite valuable.Ghouls and Ghosts: One of my favorite arcade games. Timeless classic for me.Strider: Another timeless Capcom classic. Staff behind this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off to make a quasi-sequel for Mitchell Corp called Osman.Final Fight: ANOTHER timeless Capcom classic. Certified hit in NA arcades. This is a game that briefly revitalized arcades in NA, but not as much as Street Fighter 2 did.1941 Counter Attack: Decent. better than 1942Senjo no Okami II: Capcom, buddy... You released this game in NA as Mercs you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot. Where's the NA ROM? This aggravates me since Mercs is another arcade classic for me! Still enjoy it even if its in Japanese. >:(Carrier Air Wing: Slightly obscure quasi-sequel to UN Squadron/Area 88. Its not bad. Almost as good as UN Squadron!Street Fighter 2 + SF2 CE: 1:1 arcade perfect EXCEPT Capcom censored the background in E. Honda's stage for communist China while liars try to convince everyone this was done to please South Korea. If you believe this, there's a forbidden city in China no one wants I can sell you.Street Fighter 2 Turbo: This literally exists because someone from Capcom played Street Fighter 2 Rainbow Edition and was like, "Oh.... everything's faster. And Chun Li has a fireball..." NO, Capcom. Rainbow Edition literally turns everyone into Shang Tsung and you can throw opponents into barely moving fireballs. Get the ♥♥♥♥ outta here!Varth: bit of an obscure shooter, but pretty good.(((( CPS-2 era Capcom ))))This is when Capcom was in its prime and pretty much knew exactly what it was doing.... Sometimes too well!Super Street Fighter 2 + SSF2 Turbo: ♥♥♥♥ this game. Not only does it cheat reading inputs, they changed Guile and the announcer's voice to sound like a gay game show host. Also E. Honda and Hong Kong censorship for China.Powered Gear - Capcom... You released this in NA as Armored Warriors. So why didn't you include the NA ROM? You put the NA version is in your Beat Em Up Bundle, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! This is an awesome game I never saw in NA arcades.Cyberbots - Never saw this in an arcade either. Only as a Jp import on Sega Saturn. A mash up of Street Fighter 2 and giant robots? Its fun! Not sure why it wasn't promoted more in NA.19xx: Pretty good. The 194X games consistently get gooder each seuqel.Battle Circuit: Weird, but fun beat em up. Never released outside of Japan. The character designs give me Gunstar Heroes vibes.Giga Wing: Developed by Takumi, who has a schmup pedigree due to its staff. This is the first game I heard of referred to as a 'bullet hell'. I never saw it in NA arcades (they were mostly dead by this time) so this was a Dreamcast game to most people including myself. It can be frustrating, but its not bad. If you're not a freak who can fly in the tiny spaces between bullets, just clear the screen with a bomb.To finish this up, its hard to pick just 'yes' or 'no'. There's plenty of reasons for both, the censorship and missing NA ROMs being a big case for 'no'. I don't quite get the a la carte model. This collection has some fantastic games along with some real stinkers. I don't know why they didn't just sell this as one whole collection especially since they moved on to CAS 2!Overall, recommend just edges out not-recommend since this collection has some real bangers in it that are still good enough to drown out the mistakes. But again, I only recommend buying the whole thing while its on sale.I'm not sure how well both CAS 1 and 2 sold. They only exist since the Capcom Beat 'Em Up Bundle sold so well. But I'd honestly like to see more Capcom arcade collections with the games they kept making as arcades died in NA that no one got to play. _childDocuments_.review: I rate Capcom Arcade Stadium 4/5. Good overall.I also rate the included game, 1943: The Battle of Midway 3.5/5. Pretty good.Capcom Arcade Stadium is intended to be a collection of various (you guessed it) really old Capcom games which were originally released in arcades, theaters, convenience stores, department store lobbies and other public places. Some of these (such as Final Fight) were also released later as Nintendo games. If you only install Capcom Arcade Stadium you get…1 game for free: 1943: The Battle of Midway and nothing else (other than a bunch of clunky menus)). All the other games have to be bought as DLC, either individually or in packs.Capcom Arcade Stadium has:+ A large number of memorable old arcade style games which can be bought as DLC for relatively low prices (especially during a special sale).+ You can rebind the keys to custom keyboard key configurations for every game. I do not have a controller and so I did not investigate controller compatibility though.+/- Lots and lots menu options (some are useful and others nearly useless). However, the menus themselves are clunky, obtuse and organized in a confusing manner (there are at least 3 layers of them) with obtuse keyboard controls for those menus which (so far as I can tell) cannot be rebound.- Once you navigate away from the main title screen you must figure out how to get back to it (and doing this is not obvious) in order to exit the game.- Running Capcom Arcade Stadium in Windows 10 caused my Windows screensaver to never activate and prevented Windows 10 from displaying the lock screen after the set amount of time had elapsed (The screensaver is not a custom screensaver but the normal photos slideshow screensaver which comes with Windows 10). This could result in a serious physical security issue if Capcom Arcade Stadium is run on a laptop for example. The operating system has to be entirely restarted for the screensaver to function correctly again.The free included game, 1943: The Battle of Midway, is pretty good overall and a definite improvement over its predecessor, 1942. It has better graphics, better sound, better music and includes enemy ocean warships at the end of each level (these warships function as boss fights). 1943 has fewer levels than 1942 but there are still more than enough for a good arcade bullet-hell type game while possessing enough variety to prevent the game from feeling too boring or repetitious. Confusingly, the normal system of extra lives has been replaced with an ever-diminishing energy meter which must be replenished by grabbing floating power ups (I personally prefer the more classic extra life/aircraft galaga-esq. style of gameplay over health or power meters in bullet-hell type games but for me this is 1943’s only major downside besides the fact that it is an old game). It is again interesting how this game attempts to depict a single, actual, historically momentous World War 2 battle (though fairly inaccurately of course) from the perspective of an American fighter plane rather than focusing on a purely sci-fi/fantasy setting as most bullet-hell type games do. This arcade game originally came out in 1987, 44 years after the original battle in which 3057 Japanese and 307 Americans died and yet, perhaps amazingly, was the most popular arcade game in Japan the year it came out. This continues to seem strange to me. If, the same year, an American had made a great arcade game wherein you play a Japanese airplane bombing Pearl Harbor, would it have been so popular here?
