_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a Metroidvania game, that has almost everything in it. Deep lore story, insane fights, banger music, hardcore platforming, just name it. Play as Noctis, the king of Darkness, and claim back your righteous throne! Note that this review is based on the first playthrough on Hard difficulty.Tale as old as time, it’s a clash between Light and Darkness. And Chaos being the God of this world, they curse both Light and Darkness with immortality, fated to dance in eternity with the rights to rules as their prize. Noctis, the king of Darkness, after being ripped out of every power he has, needs to climb back, and face the Queen of Light, just like every repeated cycle before it. Is this cycle gonna be the same just like hundreds before it, or this gonna be the end of it?The way the game told the story is beautiful. Complete with anime-esque cutscene and narrated by soothing voice, read out the tragic and poetic story that happened between the King and the Queen. Not only that, we can learn what happened in the past through NPC and monologue and such. Both the main story and side quest story equally interesting to made me want to keep playing just see what happen next. There’s a lot to unpack here, so I just point out the most notable one. Noctis have a skill tree that you can expand your EXP with to enhance your skills. The good thing is there’s 3 main paths of skills to choose from. The bad thing is you can’t acquire all the skills in the game. It designed that way because the level is capped and all the available skills points in the game is not enough to get all the skills. But the game allows you to reset your acquired skills point and re choose what you want. The content of the game is MASSIVE. Noctis can acquire new weapons, new abilities, new charms, even new music! But it always comes with a catch. With a massive list of things to do, even the main story, the game doesn’t really have a clear navigation to help you to get to your goal. You need to pay attention to the very detail of the dialogue to get the idea where to go next. Speaking of paying attention, you need to remember the details of what you acquired, because you can’t see the details on the Menu loadout, it only shows the legend. A map is a MUST. Because the map doesn’t get revealed after you going through them and it is total darkness. Only by buying a map you can see the map. While it is cheap, it can get annoying if you pass the NPC that sells them and can’t find your way in the new area. Now to the main course, the combat. Noctis is versatile at combat, and so are the enemies. You can build your own playstyle by choosing which charm to use and which skills you level up. Whether you like melee or range, high risk high reward, or play safely. The enemies, both bosses and minions, are exceptionally creative and aggressive. All of them are challenging with their own unique taste and rewarding when you beat them. The platforming, is on point. Not so tight, but not too easy either. My only complaint is there are some places that easy to get in, but very hard to get out, and you end up die in that closed space area and leaving your soul behind. But other than that, you get to experience a crazy kind of platforming challenge. The game even has a special dedicated challenge for platforming with time score globally to compete with other players.The world in Aeterna Noctis has grown on me. I didn’t really like it at first, but after seeing a vast variety of the characters, especially each area with their own unique scenery and enemies, I love it. They have a subtle feeling when you are in it. From a dark grim place, into a colorful sky, even space! But then again, here comes my little complaint. Not only do they put beautiful background, but they also put something on the foreground too, that sometimes blocking the view. It only happened a few times, but still it gets annoying when you fall or get hit by something you can’t see. Not many times have I encountered a Metroidvania game with full dub. Even though they use VA, I don’t know which language they use. It not stopping there, the music especially the boss music, is a total banger. It’s a little bit of enjoyment whenever I need to redo the boss fight, which is nice. The SFX overall is also clean. This is something that sometimes goes under radar until it goes bad, so I appreciate they put thoughts into this too. Final ScoreWhile this game is almost perfect on paper, but I can’t help sometimes I felt the game is too much and end up tired after playing instead of satisfied. Nonetheless Aeterna Noctis is a super solid game in every aspect of it. The dev also announced 2 other new games that share the same Aeterna universe, and I will definitely be checking them out too!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game and at the top of my favorite Metroidvania list together with Hollow Knight. What you need to remember is that is not for everybody, it has a greater focus on platforming challenges so imaging a Hollow Knight-type game with platforming challenges at a level closer to Celeste.I played it fully on the hard mode (Noctis) which was the original vision of the game and I would strongly urge people interested in this game to put the effort in trying it in Noctis mode, only if it really feels like an impossible hurdle then you should switch to the easy mode that was added later.Time to beat was about 50 hours, there's one end-game boss left at this time of review but I beat the final boss and the boss that is considered the hardest boss in the game. It's a really long game and the bosses are very challenging, but the real star is the platforming. The platforming is really fun and while it can be extremely challenge, it always felt fair. There usually are plenty of checkpoints and even the hardest challenge of the game only lasts about 40 seconds. I found it extremely fun to learn these sections as they always felt doable and never unfair to the player. I think the combat with regular enemies is the weakest part and it detracts a bit from the platforming near the end of the game. But the bosses are fun with patterns to learn and execute correctly in order to not get hit and kill them.There are two parts of the platforming that I've seen people not like as much. One is an ability you get near the mid game that re-contextualizes platforming in a way that people found challenging and not fun. I thought so too in the beginning, but you get some some gems (optional limited upgrades) that can make using this ability a lot easier. After getting used to it I really enjoyed this ability actually.The second is one particular section of the game pretty near the end of the game which has confusing movement from what you are used to. Personally I had no problems with this section as in my opinion it was just like a new challenge you had to learn to overcome, it wasn't as hard as I'd imagined it from the complaints and didn't take me especially long to get through.Finally there were some bugs that were pretty annoying, one is the fact that if you press down on the controller then you cannot double jump, this makes some sections harder than they should be. Luckily this was only a real problem in one particular platforming section near the end of the game which has you pushing the stick down a lot. The second is that the leech gem (which lets you automatically recharge a resource for special attacks and healing) doesn't work with a specific upgrade that put you at full health once if you die. While this is annoying there's a "fix" in that it still works if you only spend that skill point on the screen where you want to use the ress. Which means you will have to redo your skill tree for every attempt at a boss where you want to use it, this takes a bit of time because as far as I know you can only fully reset your tree and not some of the nodes. From what I read these bugs will be fixed in the next patch, but that might still be a couple of months away at this time. All in all, even with the negatives I really enjoyed this one, it's a flawed masterpiece in the genre that goes all in on its specific niche, challenging platforming. Looking forward to the patch with new content and the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried to like this game and there's stuff to like about it for sure, like gorgeous visuals and soundtrack for example, but ultimately, it has so, SO many very bad or terrible design decisions that no Aeterna difficulty can fix, cuz they're embedded into the core design of the game so deep, that only complete rework of it can fix, a rework aimed at making a true metroidvania experience which Aeterna Noctis simply is not, not in a million years.Furthermore, it's been a long time since I've seen so many terrible, boring and unimaginative enemy designs, terrible weapons which you almost can't use cuz of stupid blood mechanic (you also use it to restore your health), very, VERY bloated map with endless platforming sections and enormous empty spaces which cannot be explained by logic. It's just mindblowing how much of this game can be cut easily and it would've lost absolutely nothing of value. Aeterna just doesn't respect you or your time and it's terrible game design, even if there's some good parts.I just cannot recommend this game in good conscious to any metroidvania fan, cuz it's not true metroidvania, it's more like extremely long for no good reason, very sadistic and bloated platformer. I got to the Dream Kingdom which is SO freakin' annoying and tedious, that it was more than enough for me to call it quits. I can't imagine Aeterna Lucis will be better and more what I wanted from Noctis - true metroidvania experience without 99% of all the BS Noctis has and again, you can fix all this with Aeterna difficulty.Here are more detailed pros and cons: Visual design, attention to detail and the sense of scale of the backgrounds (there's some bioms in the game that look far better than others, but some of them are so detailed, that you can barely see yourself, not to mention enemies) Soundtrack (one of the best I've heard in the genre) Very-story and character driven, unlike majority of the similar games Somewhat good controls Bloated and unnecessarily huge map (maybe it makes sense for the devs, but most certainly not for me as a player) Very tedious and horrible backtracking, forcing you to get past hard platforming sections back and forth MANY times, not to mention that some areas can't visually tell you that you can't go there yet, so you'll end up wasting your time. Triple jump can make it a bit more tolerable but still, it can't fix the core design of the game. Very long bioms for no good reason other than to prolong the playtime - it's simply not adding much (if any) value to the game and only making it worse. Some I didn't mind cuz there's far better than some of the worst bioms in the game, so there's that. Terrible arrow mechanic which is forcing you to pixel perfect time your teleports - I hate all this with passion, especially cuz you can't skip all this and finish the game Horrible, very basic, unimaginative, very boring and annoying enemies. I mean, honestly, there's not a single enemy in the game (besides like very few) about which I can't say that. Some of them are so basic and so annoying, that it pisses me off to no end cuz... well, read below. Very mediocre, unsatisfying combat. The closest thing I can compare it with is Hollow Knight cuz it feels similar when you hit enemies, weapon bounce off them etc., but that's when all the comparisons end. Default sword is bad, has extremely short range and there's nothing you can do to make it better. Most of what you do in combat is waiting for enemies to attack, then do your thing or sometimes you need to use dash to get out the way. All of this gets old very fast cuz that's pretty much all you'll be doing throughout the whole game cuz: The game lacks interesting weapons, move sets and abilities to use in combat and make it good, not passable or mediocre. There's more than a sword you can use in the game, but the problem is that it is either all tied to the blood mechanic (read below) or simply terrible and unsatisfying to use in combat - the downward spear attack is cool though, but you'll barely use it much. Blood mechanic is one of the worst parts of the game. The fact that you use it to heal yourself and use bad weapons is terrible game design, cuz it adds nothing of value to the game and makes it far worse than it already is, but the fact that there's not even good weapons in the game that use it makes it even more pointless. 90% of the time you use blood to heal yourself, so you can't use weapons during boss fights that use blood cuz healing is much more important. Terrible, just terrible all around. Terrible and extremely big hit boxes. In short - even if enemies or a boss will hit a tiny effin' pixel of your character (dash effect even - not kidding), you'll get damage and there's absolutely zero I-frames in the game no matter what you do, ZE-RO! Have "fun"! And you can't even use dash and attack at the same time with cool moves and such, cuz that'll be too good to have in the game, right? Not to mention that you can't deflect enemy projectiles, use dash to go through them with I-frames, there's no ledge grab attacks and you can't even grab ledges - seriously? For the most part very unsatisfying exploration (backtracking makes it even worse), cuz most of the stuff you'll get for exploring bioms are either boring chests with coins or (10% of the time) the stuff you need to progress through the game, but even less frequently skill points, gems etc. What makes it even worse, is that this 10% is locked behind terrible platforming sections with spikes and arrow mechanics. Now imagine that there's that and on top of it all there's also stuff you can't touch or get through and you need to use the arrow mechanic again and sometimes you need to get all the way back through all this cuz there's no teleports. As if that's not enough, there's only a handful of thrones in the game between which you can fast travel, but at the same time many more checkpoints, so it makes backtracking even more tedious and worse, cuz you're ending up wasting a lot of your time by going through the whole bioms or very long parts of them just to get to where you need to be. The game (and most importantly devs) simply does not respect you or your time.I can go on and on, but I think that's more than enough for anyone to decide whether they want to buy and play the game. Aeterna Noctis has so much potential to be something great and one of the best metroidvanias I've played, but devs made it so that this potential not only is not fully realized, but they also ruined the game by terrible design decisions, made it far longer than it needs to be for the sake of prolonging the playtime and adding "value" which is simply not there. Bigger is not always better and unfortunately, Aeterna Noctis is one of the worst and prime examples of that. But the fact that the game is unnecessarily big is actually far from being its only and biggest problem, cuz Hollow Knight is also big, but at the same time doesn't have the same bad design decisions which ruined the game and player experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I started on Hard and I am going to keep playing on Hard to finish this game eventually, but this bit needs to be said;This game's design is absolute garbage.EDIT: Oh wait, wait! There's more! On top of my rant below I realized after the fact that I had become completely desensitized to how much excess effects and foreground objects are on the screen while you're playing a precision platformer and hack'n'slash game. Especially the Phoenix boss that actually confused me as to how a gigantic flame splash was not an actual attack that could hit me but just fluff, and bullets were obscured by a bunch of particle effects with no meaning to them. Seriously who the hell thinks looking good comes before being playable? Becoming disturbingly used to it makes me want to cry - even Hollow Knight does this, but not to this extent, and that was the worst part of that game to begin with.1. Every single pathway to an item (or a completely useless chest filled with money, which there are plenty of to really piss you off) will ALWAYS force you to just go back the same difficult path back. This is stupid and tedious, especially if whatever was at the end of a jumping gauntlet was worthless. The alternative is using a warp potion, but then you'll end up a long long way back at a save point so that's not really an option if you want to keep progressing, so you simply are required to do every single jumping hell twice, or even more. This is especially aggravating padding since the game already uses teleports to move you back to an exit, but only sometimes, and doesn't even do it consistently enough so that you'd know where to have them.2. There is too much of this game, and that's an amazing achievement; The maps are so massive that you actually get sick of it, this is many times bigger than Hollow Knight, for example, but most of the empty space is just a long tedious corridor that then ends in a "can't go this way" skill block. This even happens at the end of difficult jumping gauntlets so it makes you want to snap your controller in half.3. The game's buggy, absolutely unplayable at parts, especially with the harder 'advanced' version of the bosses. I have had my attack buttons all suddenly stop working and all I could do was die and retry the boss. I've had the slow-motion gem (giving you more time to react when using teleportation arrows) suddenly just keep slowing the game down endlessly in one particular boss attack, consistently, every single time I did it. Seemed that pausing and unpausing the game fixed this but do you really want to start having to pause-buffer during a boss to fix a glitch the devs don't seem intent on fixing?4. I need to point out first that I play Touhou Lunatics for funsies - this game's screen is a lot more cluttered than that and taking damage isn't optional anymore, it will happen because there's so much stuff on the screen, AND the screen consistently shakes non-stop while the screen has several needle-♥♥♥♥ attacks flying around that you're supposed to be aware of. It's torture on the eyes.5. The game wastes your time thinking it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny. One questline has you hear from a terminal you can't use it without admin permission, so you beat an admin boss, go back to the terminal, terminal tells you the card needs charging, so you beat a repeat of another boss, you charge the card, get back to a terminal and update, you go back to a different terminal to open a door, it tells you you need to fight the admin boss' hard version again (during which most of my bugs with the controls happened) and you go back to the door to get a +50% arrow charge speed gem (which you likely don't want because arrows are absolute ass in this game better used for movement than combat except in rare instances).It's tedious and aggravating when the gem could just instead be placed in any single number of challenges or pathways that ARE INSTEAD DEAD ENDS WITH A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ USELESS CHEST.The other negative reviews are absolutely on point: This game suffers from horrendous design, the challenge is the little things, the little annoyances that keep clawing at your ball sack every time they cause you to take damage, not the actual jumping or fighting. The design of the game is making everything much harder than it really is, and that is so far removed from what makes Hollow Knight a challenging game that it's laughable to compare the two at that point. I swear on my life that even something as simple as doing a double jump out of a teleport is a die roll because it doesn't consistently work properly, and I was starting to suspect a broken controller if it wasn't for the fact that every other game works fine with it.How is it possible that someone put this much work and effort into a game but they all agreed that this gameplay design was acceptable and not the antithesis to challenge and fun?I'll give the game this though: Some people have complained that the teleportation arrows and the aiming are a pain, but I thought it was easy enough to align yourself to do just straight shots to always have them work the way you wanted. But that's about it. Their use in the platforming still feels horrendous so I don't blame anyone for hating that part as well.

_childDocuments_.review: What a horrible drag of a game. Its length is way too big for the obnoxious and clunky traversal mechanics, and the insufferable combat (no parrying, no i-frames while dashing, only some trash ability that protects you for 0.1 seconds that you can use once every 5-10 seconds).While it is a classic trope in the metroidvania genre to start with few traversal abilities and acquire more over the progress of the game, here it feels horrendous to do anything while missing these abilities. Adding to this, the overwhelming amount of places where you cannot go because of missing abilities makes this game feel like a Backtracking Simulator - you are going to enter several areas where there are like 6-7 places where you could go, but only 1 of which being available with your current start abilities. To add to this nightmare, a lot of places are blocked by simply some "purple barrier" that you cannot pass until you have the last ability which is unlocked after like 15+ hours in the game, which basically means that you have 2 choices: backtrack to all other locations after getting the second-to-last ability, leaving you with the sour taste of having to BACKTRACK YET AGAIN in the future, or just straight up skip going back - which leads to you missing power-ups of your health, or other useful stuff that you may find.On the topic of "useful stuff that you find", this game feels so unrewarding. 70% of the things you find are chests filled with gold, which you can spend mainly in one location, or at a map vendor which appears in each area of the game. Chests usually contain somewhere between 800 and 3k-4k gold, and if you are a completionist and don't mind backtracking for tens of hours, the map vendor has the generous offer of giving you all places where the collectibles are, at exaggerated prices of 30k gold plus (while you would get from those chests around 10k if you're lucky).One more big complaint that I have is that, after you acquire a traversal ability, the devs think that you become a master at using it immediately, and start sprinkling in horribly annoying platforming sections.What would have made this game bearable (and, why not, a nice try at a hard platforming metroidvania game) was if the size of all areas were halved and they cut down on the useless backtracking stuff, because coherency in this game is like a needle in a haystack.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good (beat the game on noctis) but it has some big flaws, biggest elephant in the room would be visibility on some maps making it hard to spot platforming elements/enemies/projectiles from background. Another one was that controls were a bit rough and i wish character movements were more fluid (for example you can't dash cancel your attacks which also could make you dash in wrong way) but its nothing you can't get used to thankfully.Other than that there was lots of obnoxious stuff existing just for the sake of it like:- having to backtrack from most platforming segments  and do them again in reverse after getting the item - tons of enemies with different trigger on death effects that which mentioned visibility issues would make you lose hp quickly- Game don't explains well what rewards are you getting or what you need to do for a questOther than this i had fun with this game even when some locations made me curse the devs (and i would not be surprised if ppl quit cause of them) but i can only recommend this game for platformer enjoyers, if you are not one of them then its good chance you won't like this game even if you like other metroidvanias.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't even come close to Hollow Knight, so if you're hoping for a similar experience, look elsewhere. It isn't anywhere near as refined, immersive, or fun to play IMO.Firstly, the voice lines aren't in English, although the text is and so is the intro cinematic. It's weird how there isn't one consistent language across the whole game.Most important is probably the skill tree - after playing for 4 hours there are no notable or fun abilities at your disposal - I just acquired an axe but it costs energy to charge and use so it's not very practical. Healing also uses energy but you have to manually pick it up after enemies drop it. Most of the starting skill tree is either increasing sword damage, critical hit damage or critical hit chance - a good 10-15 skill points.I have acquired one "gem" so far which is an equippable item - which increases my critical hit chance.The platforming is needlessly tedious from the get go and the obstacles don't really fit in with the areas at times. When you get an important item, you sometimes have to go back through the annoying obstacles you took to get there instead of having a shortcut that opens up once you get said item.The platforming resets you on a DIFFERENT time marker each time you die - so instead of all the obstacles being in the same place when you restart (so you can quickly speedrun the parts you've already accomplished), you need to wait and figure out exactly how everything was when you started your attempt the first time.The dash mechanic is very annoying - you have to precisely time when to stop a dash by moving in the direction opposite of the dash - and this dash-cancel timing is required often for all the precise platforming you will need to do. The platforms are ALWAYS the smallest size over hazards, often disappearing ones. Some platforms which appear like you can jump through them are actually solid, which usually causes you to die because you're in the middle of a platforming race.Often times it is difficult to tell the background from the foreground and therefore which things will hurt you unless you run into them. Sometimes the foreground will even block enemies from your sight and cause you to take damage.The world is huge, but the map only gives you limited markers and although it marks chests and other items of note for you, you have to zoom in all the way to see them so it's tedious to backtrack and figure out where something you're looking for might be.I don't really feel any magic in exploring the world, and it is confusing enough starting from the second area for me to want to quit the game. There are several different "dungeons" from the main world and so far I have only explored 2 of them. I have 4 or 5 doors that lead to places that I have not discovered yet and it is almost daunting to have to explore the rest. I will need to go back to all of them because there are several items of note that I simply could not reach. I have probably passed 10-20 such items so far but have no way to mark which abilities I need to access each item.The first boss had several different forms and many different types of attacks - far more complicated than I feel a first boss should have. It also took an insane amount of hits to kill (maybe 50?) in my opinion. If this is a hint of what's to come, then I wouldn't look forward to boss fights.So far I've only been able to buy one skill point and one health container piece from the main trader in the game. Everything else is far more expensive than I can afford or has no use I can yet discern.]There is a lack of rest areas, often forcing you to explore for extended periods of time without being able to change your skill tree and try new things out, and fast travel as well.You also can't edit all the controls, so instead of playing on keyboard how I prefer, I was forced to use a controller. However the controller was bugged in one specific area of the game, so I was forced to play with keyboard and remap my key bindings to use the controls I wanted to use partway through the game.I do not think I will finish this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is awesome, dont get me wrong, didnt get to finish it tho because: After more then 50% game completion my map just turned black, so basically i have to explore everything from beginning. No thank you, wouldnt recommend getting the game that has bug that as far as i explored exists for about 2 years now, and its quite game breaking bug.Update:So regardless of a game breaking bug, i continued playing because i actually liked the game. Up until the end game content. I dont like to compare games, but i have to, Hollow Knight was big inspiration for platforming sections definitely, but in its unique way. Its fun until its not. I know its supposed to be hard, but its not hard in a fun way. White Palace in Hollow Knight was fun even tho its pain in the ass (+ its optional stage), but the end game sections here is hard in non fun way, planet gravity physics are cool and all, but inverting your controls in the hardest platforming sections is not fun and game uses a lot of mechanics and abilities and you have to be so precise with everything to succeed, kinda comes close to ''I Wanna Be The Guy'' and ''I Wanna Be The Boshy'', which is trial and error and trial and error and trial and error until you succeed, maybe that was the goal but i dont find it fun to be mega precise on long section while my controls are inverted. Then the bosses, the first few are fine, hard as they should be, but the further you go its less about dodging attacks and more of reaction time, only way to dodge the incoming attack is for you to notice visual or sound warning and react in next 0.1 second or you take a hit.Hurts me to say, but this is gonna be the only metroidvania so far that i dont have the will to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wanted to love this game. It was so close to being a fantastic metroidvania but the problems with it are bad enough to warrant a "do not recommend".In a game where platforming makes up a large portion, to put a delay on jumping AFTER you hit the ground is utterly stupid. To fog the map of areas you have already been, is utterly stupid. Having a huge portion of the game covered in one hit kill walls and floors makes this game artificially difficult. Also enemies have massive hit boxes and if you even remotely come into contact with their space, you get hit AND get pushed back. This game had so much potential but until there have been patches, I'm shelving this and not recommending it to any of my metroidvania-lover friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A good game but not for many players. 5/10Questionable hit boxes plague this title. 0 I-frames on the dash/dodge. Overly busy backgrounds distract from the platforming. Many areas it is hard to tell where it is safe to land. The small pixel and window platforming gets old pretty fast. Celeste has more movement options to work with extreme platforming difficulty. The arrow is a mass of problems as well. Using the same stick to move and aim the arrow is a MAJOR mistake. Too many times you will fall off a platform or lose grip on a wall trying to line up a shot. The aiming line should be free and not cost a gem slot.The mobs in the game are damage sponges with lames patterns. The bosses are a mixed bag. Some are LoZ fights where you dodge and land a set number of hits after a pattern while others are actual fights where you deal enough damage to reduce an invisible health bar. The backgrounds make some boss fight more difficult because the boss and their attacks are the same color as the background.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The GoodMusic and visuals are very good. Platforming and player moveset have good feel. Some sequences like the Tower of Light are unique and interesting. Combat ranges from OK to good. Bosses are pretty good.The BadGameplay - the gameplay is full of bad design decisions. The game is so hostile towards the player in really cheap ways. The player hitbox, especially while dashing, is very punishing. Environmental hazards are very touchy and often it feels like they are bigger than they look. Same with enemy attacks. Enemies will also spawn in from portals and be attacking before you can even see them.Visuals - Objects in the foreground will cover enemies and the player and there are so many environmental objects that do this. Platforms and enemies in the furnace area are hard to distinguish from the background. The enemies are often the same color as the backgrounds, making them really hard to see in general. Sometimes, especially in the ship area, environmental hazards and background noise look almost indistinguishable. For example, there are sparks that damage you, but also random spark animations darting around in the background. And then there are also enemies shooting projectiles at you. And stuff is passing behind foreground objects. The visuals are way too busy and it really detracts from the gameplay.Level Design - Areas where far too large. Even the Tower of Light section, which I loved, dragged on and on. There are lots of big empty rooms. There are too many dead ends or forced re-traversal of tedious and difficult areas. There is one area in particular that has two key items behind a switch gate, so you have to work through the same tedious obstacles twice in each direction. The map fog reveal is not nearly big enough. And god help you if you miss the mapmaker because the map doesn't really reveal itself until you explore it AND buy the map.Controls - About 25% of the way through the game you get an item that forces a lot of difficult button combinations and precise aiming. That mechanic becomes one of the main ways to traverse the levels and it took me a long time to build up the muscle memory to make it work.Despite all these frustrations, I was pushing through. I decided to stop when I entered a new area and a bug revealed the entire unexplored map, totally ruining the exploration.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis had a lot of good ideas but it is mired with so many flaws that it makes it impossible to recommend it earnestly, even if you're a souls-like metroidvania fan. What it has got are an interesting premise that turns out to be just a pretentious and cringey love story, good level design for precision platforming that is ruined by deliberate imprecise controls and really bad respawn mechanics, rooms that just goes on far too long, combat that is unrewarding and not fun, enemies that are deliberately designed to be sponges, extremely slow leveling progression with an uninteresting skill tree as well as an art design that frankly isn't very good. What's unfortunate is that, there is actually a good game here. The platforming is kinda fun if it wasn't so excruciatingly tedious to do. The map could have been more fun to explore if the enemies inhabiting them weren't such a pain to exterminate. So what you get is platforming, combat and exploration that is just not fun. I would only consider this if it was on sale, and even then, there are far, far better souls-like metroidvania that came out this year that has better art, better platforming, better combat and more rewarding exploration. You cannot make a precision platformer with deliberate unprecise controls, and the controls while not exactly bad, it's nowhere good enough for the kind of precise jumps and lands that the game requires you to do. Especially the dash move, which instead of it being a straight drop, has a momentum that will push you forward before you land. The problem is, the platforms are design with straight drop in mind. This wouldn't be so bad but the game punishes you if you mess up by respawning you to the last safe landing instead of letting you continue forward. So you end up having to unnecessarily redo an entire section (sometimes an the entire room) over and over again. It's unnecessarily tedious and unfair. This is really unfortunate because the platforming is actually designed well. And the challenge and the fun was there if it wasn't mired by the controls and the bad respawn mechanic. The art style is just not good. Perhaps this is just a personal preference, but I'm sure the developers could've put in a bit more effort in designing better looking characters. And the story while it had a very interesting premise, devolved into a pretentious love story about King of Darkneess and the Queen of Light. Yes, it went there. 2 main things that are wrong with Aeterna Noctis are the bad combat, and the bad exploration. The combat is just mind-numbing. It lacks any kind of flow or rhythm. You don't even have a parry or dodge skill and your dash doesn't evade enemies of their attack. What you get is an exchange of "I try to hit you, then you try to hit me." It wouldn't be so bad if you could dispense the enemies with 1 or 2 hits, but the enemies are damage sponges. It takes such a long time to kill 1 enemy and some enemies are deliberately placed to block your way. The experience points that you get from defeating them is also not worth the trouble. You gain so little experience points that is becomes grindy. Grinding in a metroidvania game. That is a sin unto itself. The skill tree is also very poor with no meaningful upgrades to your character. Your character will remain underpowered regardless since level progression is extremely slow. The second sin for a metroidvania game is having a map that you don't want to explore. Nothing is worse that this. If a metroidvania has a map that doesn't entice player to explore it then it fails. The world is barren with nothing interesting to look at, the enemies get in your way of exploration and are tedious to defeat and if you get damage, you are not allowed to continue forward but instead you respawn a spot behind because reasons. Some sections of the map just goes on and on and on with nothing in it except more tedious platforming and more spongy enemies. The game goes out of it's way to punish you for exploring it's world, so why would you want to? And if your metroidvania punishes players for trying to explore your world, then it's just a bad metroidvania game. One good thing I can say is that the boss fights are actually designed well and I had fun with the bosses, but reaching the boss stole all of the enthusiasm and good will that I had for the game that there is no more good will to have. It's really unfortunate that the game feels so, anti-gameplay because the platforming and the boss fights can be fun. I did not enjoy my time, and at the current price, the game is just not worth it. Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is being done VERY dirty by a ton of "drive by" reviews with very little time invested. Some complaining  about the difficulty even after the dev implemented easy mode. This game is certainly challenging but the abundance of checkpoints (especially post-patch) means that you'll never be setback very far. Many complain about the controls but what they really mean is the lack of input buffering which is an entirely different issue as the controls are just fine once you get use to that.Aeterna Noctis is hands-down the most expansive metroidvania in the genre surpassing even Hollow Knight in size and content. Each area has its own unique platforming challenges so you never feel like you're treading the same ground. A skill tree and gem system give you lots of build diversity once you start getting better gems. Sidequests and secrets galore that reward you for exploration. Most MVs can be 100% completed in 15-20 hours. I'm only 20 hours in yet I've barely even scratched the surface of this game. If you're averse to challenging platforming, the new Aeterna Mode is there for you to enjoy. However, Noctis Mode (original difficulty) offers a difficult but satisfying experience that is unmatched in the genre. Normally steam reviews are a mostly fair indication of quality, but this is not one of those cases. While not without some issues, this game easily deserves to be in the 90% range if people would just give it a fair shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not a precision platformers vet I can't recommend you to play Aeterna in its original difficulty mode. You'd better familiarize yourself with the genre first by playing something that has smoother difficulty curve, like Super Meatboy or Celeste. This game showers you with pixel-perfect jumps, relentless timings and long stretches of butt-clenching muscle memory endurance tests almost immediately. It doesn't help that teleportation arrow mechanic feels a bit half-baked. You definitely can get used to it and get good, but even after 20-25 hours it still feels like I wrestle with a stick sometimes when aligning the line of sights at an angle. The fact that you have to press yet another button just to stop the character from moving while aiming cements my opinion that there's something slightly wrong with this mechanic's implementation even more.Some minor but annoying glitches are present right now, like sometimes the character model gets sort of stuck in a previous state not allowing you to move sideways until you leave the area, other times your 'bloodstain' is left right on a trap when you die. Nothing gamebreaking though.The map design can get a bit annoying at times, leading you through a series of brutal platforming sections... right into a dead end through which you can't progress at the moment. So if you lack a teleportation stone, you have to get all the way back with no reward traversing these same sections in reverse. Maybe it was the developer's plan all along just to make you suffer a bit more, who knows?Otherwise it's very creative and fun precision platformer mixed with metroid-like akin to Hollow Knight and Ori. While the visual style and many of the gameplay mechanics mimic the above mentioned games a bit too much at times, the gameplay/platforming challenges and situations all feel fresh and original thanks to deviously smart level and traps design. The bosses are a treat - very fair and fun to learn, while also being pretty impressive visually.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The game has two difficulties: very easy and very hard with a switch possible at almost any time. I played and recommend the hard mode.✔ very big metroidvania world with some freedom in the order you visit locations. And even when you are restricted the chances are high that you won't realize it and will be directed by the game in a natural way✔ good boss fights. Maybe with the exception of some last encounters, which I found far too easy for a min-maxed character✔ demanding platforming based on a very wide skill set (triple jump, wall jump, dash and most importantly teleportation arrows)✔ early on it's possible to get those upgrades in different order, but for at least half of the experience you have all✔ you get massively better at using those skills as the game progresses, which feels very good✔ death is not as terribly punishing as it is in most soulslikes✔ customization of your character via meaningful gems with unique effects and a skill tree (with free skill resets!)❔ a mix between a platformer and a soulslike. It leans to the platformer side more heavily❔ had to use a walkthrough a couple of times to get a sense of a general direction of where to go next, since the alternative would be to wander aimlessly❔ platforming can be very frustrating, thankfully checkpoints are mostly generous so you shouldn't get stuck doing the same thing for too long. There were a couple of places however when in between challenges I just went to do the dishes or something to regen life, which I found preferable to starting from previous checkpoint ¯\_(ツ)_/¯✘ arrow aiming using mouse could be much better. Especially when you consider that you can aim for around two seconds at most before it's automatically released and that teleportation arrows are commonly used. Advice: turning off the "Smoothed Controls" option helps to some extent✘ played version 2.x and I still found two very annoying bugs: the character got stuck in place twice ignoring all input (required game restart) and in the Cosmos arena the edges of some walls were springing me in a random direction making a demanding segment ever more frustratingIt's definitely a very good game. So, do I think it's better than Hollow Knight? Despite all the polish Aeterna Noctis has it's not as polished, atmospheric or focused as HK. It is however better as a challenging platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis, wow, I have a lot to say about this one, but suffice to say, it's certainly one of the best metroidvania/platformers out there but with a huge caveat. Read below/conclusion. 👍 +Incredibly difficult+High quality in regards to everything(atmosphere, content, etc.) despite being an indie.+Longest metroidvania on the market. 👎-Frustratingly difficult-Needs some quality of life changes if it wants to capture a higher user base, more details are below.-The endgameYou play as the King of Darkness in a world where you and the Queen of Light are fighting for eternity, each time one or the other winning and becoming the ruler of Aeterna. Obviously, it's a bit more complicated than that but I do want to keep things to a minimum to avoid any spoilers but the gist is, you have a plan to stop this cycle of neverending war that Chaos, which is similar to God in our world, put them through. Naturally, for gameplay's sake, each time a ruler gets defeated he or she loses their power so you'll be starting from almost scratch with none of your king-like abilities. As you progress, you unlock pieces of your past and the story becomes slightly clearer and why you have to do what you set out to do. On the way, you'll meet some unique characters that sorta add to the whole lore of the game. Then as you reach the end, you are treated to a cinematic and then a to be continued. I mentioned the endgame in the negatives and this applies to both gameplay and story. The story in particular because it ends on a cliffhanger and I hate that. For big games, it's not a big issue but for an indie, chances are always extremely minimal, that we will see the continuation of the story. I mean look at Hollow Knight, it's been 6 years and still counting. What's worse the ending cinematic was very, cryptic, you can pretty much interpret it in a lot of ways. I just did not feel satisfied after 55hours in regards to the story. It's not bad, not at all, the cinematics and storytelling are clearly of high quality but it just wasn't enough. Story rating: 7.5/10Oh boy, where to even start...Aeterna Noctis in the entire 55 hours of gameplay, I went through huge amounts of hate but huge amounts of love as well. I'll be blunt, if you have not read any other reviews or if you have, most are correct, even the negative ones. Aeterna Noctis is the hardest game I ever played, or at the very least one of the hardest ones and I have finished Supermeatboy and Celeste and did the true ending for Hollow Knight which included going through the White Palace so trust me on this. It's a metroidvania at heart but it's a platformer on the surface. The game starts as you expect, easy enough but then it ramps up to higher and higher difficulties until it reaches the ceiling and just punches through it and keeps going. Don't let that keep you away from the game, as it does offer an easy mode, though I am not sure in what shape as I have not touched it. If you played Hollow Knight, you'll feel right at home with this and you'll know what to expect. You traverse the environment finding secrets, leveling up your character, backtracking after unlocking movement skills, and just pushing through slowly towards the endgame. It's all pretty basic here, the skills are kinda meh but you can also find gems that alter some of your abilities to help in combat, specifically bosses. You find secrets and collectibles that can also help you on your journey but overall for everything you get, the game will double in its challenge. You will never, ever, feel overpowered which kinda destroys the idea behind "metroidvanias". If you play melee only, well, good luck, you will probably never finish the game. Luckily you can reset your skills at east and just place points in the ranged damage. Now let me talk quickly about the quality of life things and the caveat I mentioned. Some of the collectibles, specifically the soul mirror parts, are just plain dumb as sh#t. These collectibles once touched by your character do not get picked, instead, they float until you reach a "safe" place. Yes, even if you are in a no danger place, the mirror still floats until you reach where the devs decided it was safe, that means, you have to do the insane platforming challenge AGAIN, and if you fail you reset without it, not where you picked it up but where you began. Yes, you read that right. There are also a lot of shortcuts that are not actually shortcuts, you unlock a door and it just closes back and you are forced to redo it all over again if you missed something. Keep in mind this is a 50+ hour game. You'll have to rely on teleporting over and over again or having to do the same annoying platforming sections instead of, you know, giving real shortcuts.There's other stuff but I have limited space, suffice to say, the gameplay is a mix of frustration from bosses having tons of hp for no reason other than annoy you to having to redo platforming sections over and over AND a mix of incredible love with so much stuff to explore and secrets to find, great combat encounters, challenging bosses, fair platforming sections, all quality stuff. Gameplay rating: 7.5/10The audio department has no issues whatsoever, the soundtrack is great, from diverse songs playing throughout each zone to nice boss fight songs. The English narrator voice acting is good and the rest of the weird language spoken is okay, I guess, but nothing distracting. The sound effects are all really good, especially the background stuff being unique for each zone and whatnot. Audio rating: 8/10The amount of work that went into the backgrounds, atmosphere, and most importantly the level design is incredible. Huge props to the people who worked on these things. My biggest issue with indies, especially metroidvania ones, is that they all look boring, but Aeterna Noctis just like Hollow Knight goes above and beyond in these regards. The amount of content and the way the levels are crafted, it's nuts. There are some bugs and the controls in the toughest platforming sections that will fail you, such as double jump triggering for no reason or jump just not working but they are rare cases. The game also has some frame drops when there are a ton of effects but manageable as 99% of the game runs perfectly.Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 9/10I don't think an easy mode that just nerfs stuff was the way to handle the criticism of the difficulty spikes however some changes in how you collect some stuff and maybe adding some actual shortcuts that removes the need to backtrack through annoying platforming challenges, as well as nerfing some of the bosses hp can go a long way. That being said, Aeterna Noctis should be played as it was intended and if you're new to the genre, I would be extremely wary of the difficulty the game offers however if you've played platformers or games like Hollow Knight, I highly recommend the game. As I said, I hated and loved the game at the same time, but Aeterna Noctis is surely one of the best in its genre and if there ever is a sequel I will gladly buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are two main reasons I cannot recommend Aeterna Noctis:Firstly this game should not have been structured like a metroidvania. Even on the easy mode the platforming is crazy punishing (fun), but it's very difficult to design crazy punishing platforming sections that can be traversed both directions, and because this is supposed to be a metroidvania that means backtracking through those platforming sections over and over again (not fun).Secondly, the visuals of this game are all aesthetic no practicality. Many of the glowy attacks have odd hitboxes, often objects in the foreground partially or fully obscure enemies or platforms, attacks and enemies often blend completely into the background (particularly in the fire section), and sometimes the only indication that something is a pickup is that your interaction button will (very briefly if at all) appear over it as you pass it.

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting setting of the world of darkness, where, the protagonist calls himself the "King of Darkness", immortal and rants it to everyone at every step, and he dies from falling into a pit or from a monster strike. But on the other hand.. it leaves a mark and is reborn at a save point where you can continue your journey with full lives.The platformer goes through the metroidvania genre, similar to the Metroid and Castlevania series, where there are closed areas that can be accessed by exploring places and finds of information or the right item.On the one hand, the game entices with Japanese voice acting, qualitatively lies on the ears and the benefit there are subtitles to understand what is happening, but on the other hand, the initial soundtrack is tired of 2 hours of play.I understand that it is pointless to write a review in 2 hours, because you can get false emotions and not fully realize the essence of what is coming from both me and your dear friends, but I wanted to share my first impressions.I was hooked by this genre and I recommend trying it out to fans of platform and adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I've reached a point where I'm ready to say that the game is pretty awesome. I went in skeptical thanks to all the "as good as Hollow Knight" reviews, but after a few hours I started to really appreciate the similarities while also appreciating the differences. Platforming is definitely a much bigger part of this game, the entire game feels like The White Palace from HK with enemies sprinkled throughout. So if you're into that, like I am, definitely dive in.A note on bosses: Similar to HK, expect to die several times per boss as you learn the patterns, platforming is also baked into the bosses which is neat.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it, but only for both metroidvania fans and hard platforming fans.The game is a flawed gem, with a lot of aspects which are great:Platforming, level design (but not world design), respawn places, combat, bosses, lot of content including optional content, difficulty slider which changes the level design (first game that does this maybe?)Some which are ok:Story, artAnd some which are a bit bad for the metroidvania standard:Quests design which are sometimes grindy and obscure. It would have been better to describe things acurately in the journal for starters, or some kind of clue of where to look. The game forces you to double check everything which is tedious in a big, not connected metroidvania as this one. That is another key point, the game is more a hub of worlds than an interconnected metroidvania. It has top notch levels such as Cosmos, the Palace... some not great ones, but they are not connected at all. You will find no shortcuts unblocked by abilities here, only shortcuts in the same "level".At least twice I had to do a difficult platforming challenge only to find out I needed another ability to get the item at the end of the path. So I had to backtrack and come back later, wasting much time.The map does not fill properly, stores are weirdly implemented, some platforming challenges feel more random than challenging, backtracking is tedious specially at end game.I do not want to end in a sour note, this is a hard game. Despite everything I listed it has very memorable bosses and you feel acomplished after beating most of the platforming challenges. Maybe they should have just made an action game with more packed level design, shorter. But there are plenty of reasons why this game is recommended so much by metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Added EAC post-release, which made it so I can't use accessibility programs I was using to play this game. I've already played too much for a refund, which I would certainly get if not for this. Making a game less accessible post-release is unconscionable.

_childDocuments_.review: To quickly put the difficulty into perspective, the platforming is slightly harder than 'The End is Nigh' and the combat is slightly harder than 'Metroid Dread'. If the platforming difficulty is a turnoff for you, the devs are currently working on a gamemode that makes platforming easier.I cannot understand why so many people don't like this game. If you enjoy difficult action-platformers / metroidvanias, you will love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The easiest way I can describe this game is that it is a precision platformer disguising itself as a metroidvania. Unlike The Messenger which is a metroidvania disguising itself as a precision platformer. I say that because at least in The Messenger you know what you're getting into in the first half of the game, so if you enjoy the platforming nature of the game then you'll enjoy it once you get full map exploration. But, in this game if you don't enjoy precision platforming, you don't know that is the core of the game until putting several hours into the game. And then it isn't even a good platformer, the hitboxes are wonky, the controls are floaty and the combat is just meh. The game looks nice and has an interesting story and wonderful soundtrack. But the bait and switch of the type of game it is and not even being an enjoyable platformer makes this a pass for me. I've tried playing it twice and this is going into my uninstall forever list.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game. This is the biggest metroidvania I have ever played at around 80 hours of length and a top 5 metroidvania for sure. Much of that time was spent trying to conquer platforming challenges. I beat it on the original noctis difficulty (which is how this game should be played). I previously though that GRIME was the best effort so far to make the next best metroidvania but it was actually this game. Unfortunately, the game stuck too close to its hollow knight inspirations and copied two things from hollow knight that have absolutely no business being in a precision platformer focused metroidvania. Those two things are the cornifer map mechanic and the corpse run. People have been complaining about the platforming being too hard or the game being too hostile towards players but the truth is they wouldn't be doing so if it weren't for these two things in the game.There are other issues as well unrelated to hollow knight that prevent this from taking the #1 spot:- There is a rare bug that can permanently prevent you from getting 100% completion by failing to register when a quest or part of a quest was completed. For me this occurred when I played the adventurers musical note, permanently blocking me from completing the associated quest.- In dream kingdom, the combination of puzzles, both in navigating the biome and solving its puzzles was simply too much, this is easily one of the worst biomes I have ever played in a metroidvania which is sad because its also one of the most beautiful biomes I've ever seen.- The game has extremely poor breadcrumbing in the cosmos biome. Due to the location of cornifer the player is breadcrumbed into first taking the hardest mini-biome of the 4 mini biomes in the cosmos biome. This has caused the entire to get criticized heavily for its design by other players. However, if you ignore the breadcrumbing and take on the other 3 challenges first, the last one becomes much more manageable and the biome much more enjoyable overall.- Aeterna mode is marked as normal while noctis is marked as hard with a skull next to it. However, this is highly misleading. Noctis is the original game and contains the platforming challenges that make this game so great while aeterna mode replaces most of it with more combat even though the combat isn't very enjoyable to begin with.P.S: ignore any person telling you to avoid the triple jump gem in the game. These people are elitists who are upset that the devs updated the game to be hard but fair instead of being a kaizo mario. They suffered through the game as it was on release and they want you to feel their pain, they do not have your best interests in mind, this is all about protecting their ego. Play the game as it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I've played plenty of metroidvanias, hard games, love the original Castlevanias, and this is just a disappointment from the ground up. My PC is no slouch, and the visuals are just not what is in the trailer. The hard mode would be manageable if the hit boxes weren't incredibly wonky for combat as you can get clipped a dozen pixels out but you have to be almost a dozen pixels in to connect with your weapon. The platforming is a mix of bad hit boxes, egregiously tight sections, and the mechanic of getting sent back to a ledge if you hit anything. The second boss I made it to was tediously designed, mainly using a gigantic hitbox sword attack that you can't punish and if your timing isn't perfect the lack of invincibility frames on the dodge mechanic is going to leave you taking a hit, the only reliable source of damaging it coming from a seemingly rarely used downward thrust attack as the pattern is randomized heavily favoring the slash attack, and occasionally the spike attack doesn't leave room to even dodge damage. More obnoxious than the boss itself is the fact that there's no way to quickly leave and come back to the boss without above poorly designed platforming.The advancement system is extremely bare bones to where it's a wonder it was even added at all.The vendor prices for most of the useful items in game were ridiculous, 5 hours into the game I had barely 1/3 the currency for much of anything. Overall this game needs a lot more polish which considering the developers are off to their next game I don't think this one will get.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok this game IS tough. Actually, I've no doubt it's the hardest game I've ever played. I gotta say, however, that I've been waiting for "that" moment where the game becomes impossible and, so far, it hasn't arrived. _childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not for casuals. If you are into hardcore, platformer metroidvania, then you'll be engaged in this magnificent world. It took me 65 hours to 100% complete this game. This is the first game from Aeternum Game Studios S.L and honestly, they deserve the utmost respect. The art and music are amazing. It is all hand drawn and the music really aligns with each area of Aeterna. The world and levels are so beautifully designed. Combat in general is good and it will shine in boss fights. If you are looking for a journey where you explore, solve puzzles and back tracing for treasures, weapons, upgrades, then you will get what you want. You may get frustrated by some of the hard challenges and platforming, but trust me you will not go unrewarded. Aeterna Noctis deserves to be known in this genre. I really recommend it. My overall review is 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this game a net positive with the exception of one dungeon which is why it gets a negative review.  I had high hopes for this game.  But don't get it unless you like precision platformers and frustrating traversal/combat.This is an action-precision platformer with metroidvania bones.  If you like action-precision platformers then I'd recommend this game for sure.  But if you want a metroid vania experience, there are much better options.First off, game traversal is entirely action platforming.  There's little to no break from the precision aspect of it and even backtracking becomes excruciatingly painstaking.  It's the first time a metroidvania made me not want to explore because of how difficult traversal was.  But it's not really a negative if you like that so it's a neutral point from me.Secondly. unlike Summun Aeterna (a much better game if you ask me) the Dash mechanic has no invulnerability frames.  Again, not really an issue but Not being able to doge out of the way of a projectile or through an enemy gearing up for an attack is frustrating.  Again, not a knock against this game as some games are like that.  I just personally didn't care for how the mechanic was implemented.Thirdly, combat is filled with a lot of "Gotchas" that are frustrating.  Almost all enemies behave in ways you don't think they would unless you fight them multiple times.  Every enemy has multiple ways to attack and it's inconsistent sometimes.All of the above can be solved by me "Getting Gud" and I agree.  So they're not negatives.The Oracle Dungeon is why this game gets a negative review from me.  It's needlessly complicated.  Crystal arrows are needed to show you the "true" path throughout the dungeon and they can'e be placed on traps (which is most surfaces), don't last long enough, and the whole dungeon is a hassle to traverse with doors leading seemingly random places.  There's a pattern sure but figuring it out sucked the fun outta exploring for me.  The game started to feel like work at this point and I was incredibly frustrated.Again, I could just suck at the game but the oracle dungeon imo is just bad game design.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a enjoyable time playing this game. I don't know if I can in good conscience recommend it.Why? Well, it's really hard to determine if you'll like it or not. Do you like MetroidVanias? Do you like hard souls-like enemies and/or difficult combat? Do you like tough-as-nails platforming? Exploring a huge, intimidating world?If you said yes to all those things, it's still no guarantee you'll like this game. I personally enjoyed all that stuff, and I still had issues with the game. The biggest being that it's just TOO big. Seriously. There was no need for some of the quests and/or second boss battles you'd have to do.If you read all that, and the game still sounds good to you, then enjoy! Some say it's the best MV they've ever played. I think its over-ambition hinders it, but you can be the judge.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is more frustrating than enjoyable, even on the easier aeterna difficulty. There's a heavy focus on platforming, which generally feels slippery and is occasionally obscured by foreground and background elements. The platforming is harder on the Noctis difficulty (a good reason to just avoid that mode). I also wasn't a fan of the combat, the bow ended up being my favorite weapon in the game because getting too close to enemies when you have a bad back dodge just wasn't worth it and added to the frustration. Despite my issues with the core gameplay, exploration was fun sometimes, only to then be held back by frustrating bosses. I also couldn't get into the lore and story. There are so many better metroidvanias available on the market today that this is an easy skip.

_childDocuments_.review: **Game reviewed from Noctis difficulty perspective**Probably the most complete platforming Metroidvania that Ive played since Hollow Knight, and in some areas, its better.While brutally difficult at times, the challenge in front of you never seems impossible.  Once you have mastered all of the tricks that you have available, the movement is just buttery. _childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to actually post as there needs to be a 'Mixed' or 'Good with Flaws' sort of review.On the end of it, though, I feel I have more negative than positive but there is a lot to like about this game and I am in a paradoxical place of wanting to say that while this game isn't it for me, I will be playing the other games made by this studio as what I do like they clearly nailed and what I don't like are things that are fixable or hopefully addressed in their next titles.Art is good, music is atmospheric. Controls... 99% of the time are there. As for the bad... Well, Critical Path platforming? Just about right. Fun. Getting all the side collectables and such? It feels actively antagonistic against you to where this frustration from trying and dying over and over (played first on the harder difficulty and swapped to 'normal' around the Infinite Sea zone and while this was easier this was still present.) actively hampered my enjoyment so much as to tilt the scales enough to leave this negative review. Tolerances can become punishingly tight and while the art is fantastic, the somewhat 'lumpy' areas of death zones in some specific areas make otherwise acceptable trajectories and jumps something much harder to judge.  Platforms in the King's Trials, also, feel poorly communicated... Like the edges are too fuzzy and many times it feels I should be landing on the edge only to fall to another failure as the visuals seem to extend a tiny bit further out than the existing collision to cause this. Also the range of the crystal arrow teleport feels... Too short and the size of the projectile has resulted in many times triggering the teleport too early and just instantly failing back to a checkpoint because of it. That is to say, I am unsure if it's the tip or the end of the arrow or somewhere in the middle where it is safe to trigger the teleport on and never managed to figure that out. Also I kinda wish the dash had innate 'dodge' to it rather than being relegated to a limited gem slot but... That's just a personal preference. It's fine.The size of the game itself is fantastic at first but.. After a while, such a scale almost counts against it. Travel stops being fun and more just a slog to get place to place when revisiting areas for secrets. I think there is a happy medium between tight areas and rooms and vast open spaces that trigger my OCD to uncover ever dark corner of the map that exists so I can say there's nothing left to look for even if I know it's empty space.For those wondering, I have completed the game at 93% total completion, killed Garibaldi before the light arrows which I had no idea was even a thing at the time (got a shiny cheevo for it, apparently), and found a lot to enjoy overshadowed by how much frustration and annoyance it took to get to the fun bits. Maybe that's your thing in which case have fun but for most, try something else. That said, I am immediately going to look at the Eden Genesis they just released and give that a play. What was good was *very* good and I hope that they learned a few lessons on the difference between hard and punitive when it comes to platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a very challenging and vast metroidvania full of precision platforming, explosive boss fights and a surprisingly interesting story which kept my attention until the end. The tl;dr is that it's a heavy recommend to anyone who likes metroidvanias and doesn't mind a very substantial but varied challenge.The areas all have really unique feels to them, and I found traversing them and going back for secrets after obtaining new power-ups to be a real highlight of my playthrough. The enemy variety was also very impressive, with the bosses in particular having me excited to learn their patterns and execute a flawless dance by the end. Although, as the game progressed, my motivation and desire to grind the no-hit achievements got lower and lower, partially due to general difficulty but also greatly down due to feeling like a ranged build was highly recommended for late-game fights. I played with perhaps a questionable control scheme using almost entirely keyboard, and after 30 hours didn't really want to swap, but it left me wishing I'd started on controller which I imagined would've made some of the endgame challenges feel much smoother to play.And that's probably my main gripe with the game, or at least my experience with it. My time spent with the projectile mechanics had me swapping from my keyboard to my mouse quickly, and whilst I improved at this over time, it made relying on it as a means of attack feel rather clunky to me. I feel this would've been avoided had I used a controller, so ultimately it just comes down to my personal experience with the controls and struggle to grow comfortable with what I'd started with. It even led me to ignore some of the lategame optional stuff due to melee feeling very subpar by comparison, and not willing to put in the time to grind it out.So really most of my "complaints" are just down to me wishing I'd played on controller, or maybe that some of the endgame fights felt more balanced around melee combat. Overall I found the game to be a great time, and would absolutely look forward to playing a sequel, if the day comes.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a game that is too irritating to really suggest for other people to play.The game itself has a number of bugs and issues that, while not game breaking, are very annoying.  Any time you die, you will see the room you're in reload, then you will see a black screen and respawn.  During some cutscenes, you'll retain control of the character and jump as you move through the dialogue. Sometimes hits wont register, or you'll dodge in a direction you don't want to, and various other minor, but extremely annoying bugs.The game itself, even without bugs, is also far more infuriating than it is fun.  I'm all for difficult games, so long as the difficulty feels good, but this game really pushes it too far.  For reference, I played about half the game on hard mode, then got fed up and moved to normal.  Normal mode makes platforming challenges about right, but it doesn't really help with bosses.  Enemies and bosses generally have about double the health in hard mode, but nothing else about them changes.  This wouldn't be so bad if not for the fact that even in normal mode enemies and bosses have about twice as much health as they aught to.  The difficulty of the game really comes from attacks that often come without warning, or the proper ability to dodge combined with overly long boss fights.This isn't a terrible game, but it is a game that is tuned for people that desire much more challenge than most people will enjoy.  I've completed all the Fromsoft games, along with Lies of P, Ender Lilies, Blasphemous 1 + 2, etc. I've played and enjoyed many games that are considered difficult, this game really goes too far and becomes tedious rather than fun.  After completing pretty much every boss, rather than feeling triumph, I was just bored.
