_childDocuments_.review: To anyone thinking about playing this, you should know that Aeterna Noctis is a long, frustrating, and exhausting platformer. It is a genuinely difficult game that involves sections of extended try-and-die precision, with extra levels of BS in the later regions (If you are interested in reading about this, check negative reviews mentioning "dream", "cosmos", "teleport arrow"). The experience has a chance to be infuriating instead of amazing. Normally, I would say to try it anyways, since it is good to experience negative emotions. However, with a 10 hour commitment needed before you get to the meat and bones, I think its better to err on the safe side. Nevertheless, I found my experience with this game to be one of the best (top 15) I've had with games, personally.Starting out mellow and serviceable (with a good amount of it feeling like a hollow knight clone), Aeterna Noctis hits its stride after the first third of the game. The ambition and passion, along with the abject cruelty of the challenge, kept me enthralled. The game lacks a lot of polish, but I was blown away by the later regions of the game. I don't really want to spoil anything, but these are the most impressive parts of the game.This game definitely leans more into its platforming than anything else. The combat was forgettable, but acceptable. The bosses were difficult, but they can be easily brute forced through damage immunity windows and some of them encourage this. Often, a boss will have very few windows for landing attacks, but will stand immobile and vulnerable during a "bullet hell" phase. I found much more success in walloping the boss and tanking attacks here.In the end, the reason I enjoyed this game so much was that it was daring with its beautiful ideas. But it didn't hurt that when I was subjected anything truly demented, my reaction was to smirk in amusement and relish the mental pain. I would love to see this studio produce a more focused and confident game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: opens with a few animated cutscenes introducing its intricate universe: two factions, one led by the Queen of Light and the other by the King of Darkness, are condemned by the God of Chaos to fight each other for eternity. After every battle, the loser is deprived of all powers and restarts a cycle of life and death in search for revenge.You play as the King of Darkness who, after being defeated and falling into an inferior dimension, must recover his powers and return to fight the Queen of Light who sits on the throne of Aeterna. This is a very light premise; there is a lot more going on and the story will be slowly put together like mosaic pieces thanks to a great number of characters that you will encounter throughout the journey.The gameplay includes classic metroidvania elements and is significantly inspired by . You need to unlock a wide range of abilities and use them to traverse environments filled with enemies and traps that require great precision platforming. You can equip yourself with gem stones to upgrade your stats, use blood energy to heal yourself and recover your spirit by visiting the point where you died or by defeating the enemy who killed you. There is a checkpoint system based on torches and thrones; the first ones are more like points where you respawn after dying while the latter are major hubs where you can upgrade your skills and fast travel. You can also find keys that give you access to trials; by completing them you unlock abilities that are crucial to the gameplay.All these mechanics will sound familiar to those who have had some training from other metroidvania games, but Aeterna Noctis is more a platformer than anything else and it can be very hard even for veterans of the genre. While I love challenges in these games, there were some parts maybe too unbalanced and unfair to the player, requiring perfect timing as well a bit of luck. Maybe this is why the developers recently updated the game with a new mode called “Aeterna”, which seems to be easier, removing multiple traps along the way and lowering enemies’ HP (unfortunately this mode doesn’t unlock achievements at this time). The good news is that now you can change the difficulty mid-game if you feel one area is too frustrating for you; don’t expect it to be a walk in the park, though.The combat system is simple and smooth enough, but it’s not engaging as platforming and becomes repetitive after a while. Most of attacks are melee-based, with the arrow ability used more for moving through environments than for fighting enemies. While there is a decent variety of enemies and attack patterns, the combat feels fun and engaging only during boss fights, which are incredibly challenging.As you progress, you will discover multiple interconnected zones, each with its own distinct biomes, type of enemies and traps. From underground lava caves and goblin mines to beautiful forests and giant towers, there is a great variety of areas, always kept together by dark tones and gorgeous visuals that partially reminded me of . Music and sounds really contribute to the game’s atmosphere, and you know the audio department did a good job when you stop playing the game for a few seconds only to hear the music and sound effects in the background (there is also a piano/organ that can be played).So is it everything perfect? Well, unfortunately no. There are some major and minor annoyances.First off, the game should make clear what abilities you need to move further with the story. I often stumbled on long sections of fights and traps only to realize I couldn’t progress further because I was missing one ability (which nobody warned me about). It forced me to waste massive amounts of time moving back to the closest fast travel point.The other problem is the quest log. Soon after the tutorial, I was overwhelmed by a great number of side quests, many of which I had no idea how to solve. As I was progressing through the story, I accidentally completed some of them without even realizing it. I think that the quest log could really use some improvements, like showing the quest-giver location on the map, and generally mention the area where the player should start looking. Any sort of (minimal) guidance would definitely make quests tracking less confusing and the experience more enjoyable.Even the areas you explore are hidden by a fog of war which can be only removed by purchasing maps from a travelling merchant. And yet, the map doesn’t really do what it states. It doesn’t make the area visible from your menu, it only removes the fog within the area you already explored, which feels quite misleading. There is another map that makes items and secrets visible on the area, but it’s so expensive that it will require lot of grinding, and its price should probably be adjusted to match the amount of money you can get from enemies and simple exploration.It’s worth mentioning that these issues didn’t have a huge impact on my experience and they can probably be fixed with a few more updates.Aeterna Noctis doesn’t reinvent the wheel, but it combines different mechanics to provide a refreshing experience. While the game doesn’t steal the crown to Team Cherry’s masterpiece, it proves to be an awesome game, greatly challenging and polished in every front. It’s a pity that within all these perfectly mixed mechanics there isn’t one that particularly stands out for being original.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly not 100% sure why this game has so many negative reviews.  I've only played a couple hours so far, so maybe something goes catastrophically wrong, but so far the game's been pretty good.  I think the platforming so far has been well done, and the single boss I've fought so far was honestly pretty nice for a first boss.  Both combat and platforming have been challenging, with platforming being harder than the combat so far, but not stupidly difficult.  The controls can feel a bit weird at first, but it kinda just reminds me of Blasphemous where you get used to it and it becomes fine after a while.  I have read there's a glitch with Vsync and fullsreen, so if that affects you then your experience with the controls may differ than mine, but for me they felt rather good.The only real issue I've had with the game is not being able to tell if a object causes damage or not (ie water that you can stand in vs water that damages you and white patches that don't really do a good job of signalling they deal damage).  I can see how this could be frustrating for people, but the respawn points are rather numerous, and once you've gotten hit once you know if it causes damage, so I don't view it as that big of an issue.  Similarly, it can be a bit hard to distinguish background images from climable ledges, but again, you just need one jump to know for sure.  Overall, the game's pretty good so far.  It has some issues, but the overall gameplay loop has been very solid.  Would recommend if you're into challenging metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Best metroidvania since Hollow Knight or Grime. This game starts slow like all metroidvanias, but after a couple hours things begin to click. The entire game is a testament to the dedication of Aeternum Game Studios in pursuing excellence. Difficulty is similar to the end game content of Hollow Knight. It has a modern Castlevania feel like Bloodstained: ROTN. I read the mixed reviews on here and viewed a few in-depth YouTube reviews before purchasing. If you like tough-as-nails difficulty this is your game. Otherwise, you will be beating your head against a wall. Highly recommend this game and it is criminally underrated.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has definitely become one of my favorite metroidvanias. I've noticed a lot of people complaining about the precision needed and big difficulty spikes, but in my opinion its what makes this game so good. Everything is doable its just going to take you time. The combat and platforming both feel incredibly solid, they do require a good bit of time to fully adjust to, but the fulfillment you get after completing a crazy platforming section or a crazy boss is, in my opinion, second to none. I do wish this game got more love as I think its rather expertly crafted. I have some minor qualms about some mechanics,  but the fact that every part of the game felt fresh and challenging throughout made this an amazing experience. To be frank though, if you like metroidvanias, or souls like metroidvanias, but do not like precision platformers, or vise versa, you probably won't like this game. This is a game where you are regaining your godhood and you can feel it in the abilities and progression, but you are also challenging the very nature of the world and its other gods. Which remains a rightfully difficult feat. As for what I believe to be more minor considerations in my enjoyment of the game but still relevant, the music score, art style, and story are all very enjoyable. The world feels very realized, albeit with some pretty large amounts of high fantasy. But most notably for me is that each area felt fresh and new rather than a rif on the last area. The scenery can change greatly and I like that. The score is well done. Although there are times where the tracks begin to grate on you in the more difficult platforming sections, each track suits its area well. As for the story, I personally got pretty invested with the twists and turns this pseudo yin and yang endless cycle story had. I think its well done with its story beats, but my major qualm comes at the end of the game. Spoiler: All in all, if you're like me and you enjoy games that will challenge you regardless of the genre, grab this game. The unique mechanics this game has made the experience enjoyable on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: What is Aetrerna Noctis - it is a 2D platformer with soulslike and metroidvania vibes. It is about eternal fight of good (light) and bad (darkness) forces in some strange world. Some god cursed leaders of darkness and light and condemned them to fight each other for eternity. Every cycle one of them lose their powers and is sent back to the world of living to regain their might anew. This time it was a turn of a king of darkness (who you are going to take control of). The idea is that all of this already happened many times before.This is a good well-written and made game which I would like to enjoy. I like the dark world and some of the NPCs (Although protagonist played on my nerves a bit). So why the negative review? I can definitely recommend this game to hard-core action platformers fans. It will keep you on your toes and won't give you much time to catch breath between all the blades, disappearing platforms and other mumbo jumbo traps and tricky chain jumps. Sometimes you have to perform like a chain of 20 perfectly timed  jumps infused with dashes  (which sometimes have to be stopped in exact moment so you do not overjump the platform). You will fall to your death countless times just to start over. IT IS VERY CHALLENGING (especially the areas with leaderboards). Some of the steam achievements are like near to impossible or they make you to replay the game just for a one-time chance to receive the achievement or not (so if you like to platinium games be ready for near impossible experience for only best of the best). Sweat, blood and tears.I was looking for soulslike/metroidvania game like Salt & Sanctuary with challanging combat and bosses but there is barely any of it in Aeterna Noctis. There is 90% platforming here and 10% souls game (maybe less). All the mobs are just damage sponges that serve as another trap/obstacle put between all the platforming challanges. There are no challanging mobs just for the fighting purpose. They are all very easy and unsatisfactory if faced on normal ground. Bosses also are not like in a souls game - they just require you to jump a lot and dodge projectiles etc. like in any other platformer.That's why with heavy heart I gave up on this one and will not find out how the story is unrevealing and how it ends. I dont mind moderate platforming like in S&S but this I know it will boil my blood down the line so I prefer to save myself stress (and to play something else instead what I am going to enjoy for a change).

_childDocuments_.review: I think I’m finally giving up on this game. I want to like it, as I'm a fan of Metroidvanias in general; unfortunately, I'm just not finding it very fun. It relies heavily on platforming (which I enjoy), but a decent amount of the platforming challenges end up feeling tedious rather than difficult. The further I get into the game, the more often my feeling is “Ugh, more of this” than “Cool, a new area/challenge to get through!” or “A new mechanic to master!” For example, once you get the ability to teleport, the game becomes heavily reliant on this for quite a while, to the point of feeling like it's a gimmick more than a cool ability. Then, a “next step” in this process is to send you to areas where you can’t use it once you get another ability that opens them. In other words, the game gives you an ability, pushes it on you frequently, then challenges you simply by taking it away again. That makes the game feel oddly regressive rather than progressive at times.Similarly, the difficulty is uneven, with some sections being very forgiving only to suddenly become incredibly precise without much lead-in. The save points/respawn locations in these areas also seem haphazard at times, with two or three in close proximity to easy sections and then a long, difficult section having none, forcing you to repeat lengthy stretches to get back to the point where you’re struggling; since most of these rely on instadeath environmental hazards, it slows the practice aspects down to a crawl. It also makes the game’s platforming feel less like a puzzle to solve and more like an exercise in muscle memory, which is why I think it eventually just gets tedious and aggravating rather than continuing to feel like a challenge. It's another example of the game creating difficulty more by taking things away (save points/progress, in this case), and I think that ends up making it feel repetitive and punishing more than rewarding.All in all, it’s like the game doesn’t quite know how to strike a balance between easy and difficult or necessarily and unnecessarily repetitive. That’s a shame, as it does some really good things, avoids some of the overcomplication of other Metroidvanias (like the ones with a hundred different weapons and a dozen different stats), and has a great aesthetic (although enemy mechanics are also a bit repetitive and underwhelming—how many types of exploding blob enemies does one game need?).  My initial impression of it was that it is highly derivative of Hollow Knight; I never found Hollow Knight tedious or boring, however, which is sadly where I am with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Not being a fan of the genre and any hardcore in it, the first thing that caught my eye was a platformer with the ability to control the mouse, and not a piano simulator.The plot tells about the endless confrontation between the forces of light and darkness in the struggle for power. We play for the loser in the next battle of the lord of darkness. There is a restoration of power and the newly lost throne.Gameplay - Metroidvania with all the consequences, large locations with secrets, different biomes and enemies. Everything is as it should be. Of the minuses, I would not fully perfect the mechanics of movement, attacks, animations and taking damage. As an example, it is impossible to avoid damage with a strafe of a visible enemy or a projectile (the question is why strafe then?), Some textures of the platform and GG are broken, in the sense that the hero can get stuck in them or fail when the floor of the body is still on the texture. There are no stanlocks. Enemies with teleportation may appear in your permanent damage dealt before being recognized. What else to say about the gameplay, I do not know, I repeat, I am not an expert in this area.Graphic - At the intro stage, there was an expectation of a murals-style game, but as you can see at the end of the intro, the style is closer to anime. Not mine.Music - Not bad, maintains quality.As a result - a rather mediocre game with a visual effect that is more reminiscent of dark fantasy in the style of anime. Fans of the genre, I think it will be interesting. For beginners, it will do for a couple of evenings if there is nothing else to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this crazy game for 12 hours straight now. It's got Hollow Knight vibes, lots of anime references, crazy-awesome animations, and terrifyingly complex platforming. I'd say it's a good example of metroidvania! And to be honest, it was my very first experience in this genre of games. And it was unforgettable!Here are a couple more points I'd like to highlight:- The plot, you seem to be placed in a cartoon fairy tale, where you pick up the pieces of history of the world exploring it and getting acquainted with the inhabitants along the way helping them.- Since I haven't played Metroidvania before, it's hard for me to say if there are enough enemies, but each location brings new ones to the game and I didn't get bored farming experience. Which is definitely a plus!- A huge number of secret locations, chests, collectibles in different places at any point in the location. And most importantly, you can buy a map that will be displayed all the secrets you have not found.- It was strange for me to control the height of my jump, although I understand that almost all platforming is built on this mechanic combining different abilities, but still as for the first time it was strange.- There are not a lot of abilities, but also no unnecessary, all enough for a comfortable game.- Animation or taking damage. I never understood why, at any collision of a character with an enemy, he loses his balance for a decent "second", perhaps this was done to add a banal skill to recover from damage.- Attacking abilities (types of weapons) are sufficiently elaborated, but to use them all, I did not want to, as well as any special situations for their use.Conclusion. The game is clearly worthy of purchase to add to your collection of this genre of games!Well done dev's! Great job!

_childDocuments_.review: Cannot recommend. Hitboxes are HORRIBLE! You see you weapon go thru the enemy and you still don't hit. You clearly dash OVER the enemy and still get hit... _childDocuments_.review: The most relevant thing about this game is the difficulty: THE GAME IS HARD, like hard hard but its fair (most of the time).There is an easy mode but we arent cowards are we?Both in platforming and in combat the game is unforgiving, millisecond precision is needed in platforming, incredible reaction time and coordination is needed for certain bosses (other that learning the attack pattern of course), all this can make it frustrating but also satisfing to achive.. but there is one problem for the combat: there is a specific build which is basically cheating, you are gonna unlock it late game and if you are not told you probably wont notice but if you use it dying in combat becomes impossible. It turns the late game bosses from borderline unfair to piece of cakes, this ruined the end game for me.-ABOUT THE GAMEPLAY: its a metroidvania on its purest form, Hollow Knight with larger rooms (a bit to large).The combat is perfect: quick, lots of abilities both of movement and of attacks, you can have different styles of combat and the enemies and well designed.The platforming is the most complex I ever saw in a 2D game, you need such cordination between different abilities but its well designed and satisfing.-PROGRESSION: there is a skill tree which also boost your stats and an gem selection menu that works similar to the the one in Hollow Knight. The skill points requires a lot of exp to get and gems are well hidden so the game actualy gives you reasons to explore, there are also hp-extentions to find and collectables which the more you find the more certain NPC will give you in return. The progression is functional and satisfying.-THE WORLDMAP and LEVEL DESIGN: the map its HUGE, full of secrets and collectables, unfortunatly the first 2 areas are a bit boring but it gets better.The world is open and interconnected but you don't always have the choice of approach, like most metroidvanias sometimes you have to follow the path expecialy in the first half.The level design is sometimes very good sometimes a bit plane and boring but most of the times its good.But there is 1 zone which sucks, the heaven zone: the design of that zone is BAD, you get lost in an unnecessary large zone which all look the same, such a loss of time. its one in like 15 zones tho.-MUSIC is good, not Ori or Hollow Knight good but still good. The sound effect even better.-STORY is one of the best of the genre, which is easy cause most metroidvania storylines sucks, but finally an understandable plot with reveals and a worthy finale, a bit intricate about one thing which could have been made more clearn and logical but it works. It actualy hold a big mistery box which get more and more interesting the more you go on.All that said the story still is a small part of the game and you are not gonna give it great importance, there is one cutscene or important dialogue every 5 hours of play or so, its good for giving purpouse to your action in game tho.-THE ART is good for enemies and zones not as great for human characters, they are drawn a bit weird.-IN THE END its a 7.5/10 game which is made for harcore fans of platforming and metroidvanias, very enoyable experience that will take you for many hour (dont watch my hour count, its much more).

_childDocuments_.review: This is indeed my most favorite metroidvania/platforming game.I have never felt so fulfilled and proud after finishing this game with 97.7% in about 50 hours on first try (and yes, ofc I could get 100%).All those *** saying this game is too hard have no metroidvania skills whatsoever.I say it's pretty forgiving since you can die on purpose and then respawn at the closest lantern (if you lost too much health and are not confident enough to advance further).Penalties are not serious trouble since you can just pick up your soul at point of death, no problem. I never lost xp, not once.Yes, bosses are tough and demanding and have unique mechanics but you will git gud eventually :)There are 2 difficulties which can be changed at any point.I kept playing on hard (noctis).BUT I really HATED the cosmos area (second last area), because controls are inverted and this really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ my brain. I didn't enjoy it, but persevered.And I finally know what "platforming" game means. Jumping, dashing, teleporting and wall jumping around like crazy, evading traps, pits and spikes. But in this case on a whole new level.Man, this game is brutal and whoever designed the areas is a maniac and genius.I have never encountered this kind of seriousness and intenseness before.The level design, mechanics and abilites to evolve are without even.Story, art style, soundtrack, exploration, level design, abilities, combat and every detail is off the charts.It's very fulfilling to hit enemies and controls are sugar smooth.Buy this game no matter what, there's love all over the place.I get some nice Hercules vibes back in the day from Playstation 1 :)

_childDocuments_.review: So as you saw i didn't recommand the game, but it's actually not really the case. First of all it's a good game, i personally like platforming in Metroidvania games and this one really gave me a lot of it, BUT BUT BUT, the main issue with that game, and i know it has been pointed out, but it hasn't been adressed by the dev and it's really sad, the game isn't playable after a third of it if you play with a controller.Most player that plays Metroidvania games usually play it with a controller, and there is an ability  that requires to aim, which is nearly impossible with a controller. I usually don't mind and deal with it, but this ability is mandatory, and the worst part is that you sometimes have to use it with extreme precise timing while you are in the air, and you don't have a lot of time to use it (i think that's like 2s whilst time is slowed down) to parkour between platform. That is really sad because it makes the game really harder that it should be (the rest of the parkour is really manageable, and it will seems kinda easy if you played HK). It's sad because the learning curve of the game drastically goes up when you obtain this ability which shouldn't be that case.I'm currently studying game design so i definitely know what i'm talking about, games MUST be tested, and it includes controller expecially with platformer games, and i trully don't think that the devs tested it with a controller because this ability is really not meant to be used with a controller.So TLDR, i wouldn't recommend the game if you intend to finish it 100% whilst playing with a controller, otherwise i would definitely recommend it if you are playing with keyboard/mouse because it really is a good game. The Level Design si really well done besides that ability, if you enjoy parkour, you will be served, the story is really nice, every character has voice acting, the map is huge so it definitely is worth the price for the amount of hours you would put into the game (i have finished like a third when im writing this but i'm a big metroidvania fan so i'm usually faster that most people so i would say it's at least 40h/50h to 100%). Really I enjoy it but this ability really destroy your game experience if you are playing with a controller.I'm linking that reddit post that really sums up pros and cons of the game imho, and I'm asking the dev to adress that issue, otherwise the game is a gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but it's definitely more style than substance. For intending to be a precision platformer, said platforms are slightly off compared to normal dash and jump heights and distances, leading to a lot of unnecessary microadjustment (i.e., more annoying than anything to have to constantly curtail a dash back to its intended platform rather than flowing from leap to leap). Hitboxes are vague (owing to the art style) and the camera is more for someone watching than someone playing, forcing memorization of sections due to not looking ahead far enough or moving with the player quickly enough. Honestly, there are several other titles I'd recommend ahead of this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game loves to punish you, and not just during expected difficult sections. The platforming consistently requires pinpoint precision, and frequently requires you to do it again in order to get out. If you've got bad luck/tilt/etc, it's insanely easy to soft lock yourself by not being able to escape a jump puzzle, since the teleport ability is a consumable. Some of the later maps start introducing purely frustrating mechanics (gravity shift/orbital gravity, constant mob spawning, ~5-10x hp mobs, bullet hell style firing patterns from basic mobs). Even after the main challenge for an area is accomplished, its still a slog to get through. I'm stubborn enough that I'll probably finish it, but at this point I'm shamelessly following walkthroughs whenever I get stuck.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first ever Steam review. I really want to love this game. However, it is way to unforgiving from the get go. Comparable pinpoint precision platforming difficulty to a game like Celeste, and maybe even a bit moreso due to enemies in the midst of it. The souls-like system coupled with the lantern checkpoint system in extremely tough platforming sections riddled with enemies is just not fun. Either the enemies need to be removed in these sections or the devs need to figure out a different method of checkpoints. It just gets to the point where it isn't fun. The controls are not responsive enough in combat but over-responsive where they don't need to be. Playing on a controller I find myself accidentally falling through platforms I don't mean to fall through and then dying, or falling all the way through sections I've already platformed through. And the respawn at your last lantern item is one time use. Just awfully unfun game design. And you can only complete achievements in the Noctis mode which, by the way, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Just make a completely separate achievement for completing the game on Noctis mode for players that decide to do it. Idk - I want to recommend this game but at the difficulty and amount of unfun it is I just can't. Sorry devs - can't wait for Silksong lets go Team Cherry!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished this game on a different platform and i bought it here as well, my save transfered safely and i got all of the achievements i aquired which is nice. This is one the best metroidvanias ever created, its only 2nd to Hollow Knight which might be my favorite game of all time, literally! Aeterna Noctis is hard, oldschool hard, so  hard that it might feel artificial which is true for some areas but that doesn't change the fact that after you're done with this game you will be a better player and not just in AN but a better player overall. The developers listened, not even a month after its release they added an easier mode that focuses more on action and story and less on the brutally challenging platforming so even less experienced players could experience the game's best moments. It took me about 90 hours to completely finish the game, despite it saying i have 10 mins, i have over 1000 deaths... Its so sad that this game will never get the recognition it deserves, its a real shame because it definitely deserves it and its sequel is already in the making from which i am expecting a great deal! I think the only mistake the devs made when they released this game was the lack of an easier mode which they added later, most of the people who complained of its difficulty would have probably finished it if that were the case but oh well - To Aeternum Studios, be sure to include an easier mode in Aeterna Lucis from the start and good luck, don't disappoint us:)!

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a great metroidvania with a few minor, but noticeable flaws. For what appears to be the team's first game together, that is a lot better than I would normally expect - especially self-published and with as large a scale as this game has. I would recommend this game for anyone who is a casual enjoyer of metroidvanias and/or platformers with a little bit of patience, or any hardcore enjoyers of the same genres. Even at full price, the money spent vs time invested alone justifies it, but is further justified but the amount of quality content. At the time of writing this review, it is on sale for $12 USD and that is simply a steal!Firstly, many people comment on the difficulty of the platforming. I do not normally play platforming games, but I personally felt that it was not overwhelmingly difficult. However, there is a specific upgrade that you can choose to use/not use (another jump - up to triple jump max). I also used a controller - I could not imagine the suffering stubborn KB&M users would feel attempting the harder platforming sections. I opted to use that and I did feel that I would have felt much more frustrated in mid-late game without it. There were a handful (maybe 8-12) of challenges that felt exceptionally difficult, but they were all optional if you don't care too much about 100%ing your playthrough. Even then, they are possible. In a game with hundreds of "platforming challenges" though, I feel like the balance was fair as an inexperienced platformer gamer. Rather, what was more frustrating was how it felt tedious at times repeating sections you've already went through. This is partly a problem of the density of fast travel points, though at the same time more fast travel points would have felt unnatural.The early and mid game combat provides a nice level of difficulty, though beyond that almost all encounters, even all the bosses, are a joke, if all you care about is defeating them. Their DPS was far too low to pose a threat as I could out-heal all of it (with two exceptions). Narratively though, that kind of makes sense. At the same time, their movesets felt too fast & complex for me to attempt to dodge reliably. Many bosses are quite tanky as well, so even wailing away non-stop can sometimes take a while. Dodging all the attacks would really draw out each attempt. As a soulslike enthusiast, this was probably the most disappointing part of my play time. The player attack movesets & animations are very well done with satisfying weight & feedback.The character art direction felt weirdly inconsistent, but to a level that feels nitpicky. The art that is presented is nice to look at, but inconsistent. The environmental art is more consistent and certainly above-average.The game's performance was perfect, there were no crashes during my playtime, and I only ran into maybe two or three bugs. The one that stuck out the most was some player physics sometimes not behaving as intended in the one specific area that completely changes how the player physics work (staying vague to avoid spoilers). Props to the programmer(s) for getting it working as well as it did though!The game's music is a mixed bag. There are some certified bangers, many serviceable tracks, and a couple that kind of missed the mark. I can tell a lot passion and skill went into its composition though and I hope they are out there still making more of those certified bangers!Lastly, the game's story is serviceable, but mostly not super memorable. The beginning and middle of the main storyline was not especially gripping, HOWEVER, the world building is some of the best out there, some of the dialogue is excellent, the main character is wonderfully written, and the finale (though felt rushed) was a very impactful surprise at the end there.  I loved it.Thank you for the game Aeternum. I will be keeping an eye on the upcoming sequel and Eden Genesis.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Game seems OK - there's some great pros working in its favour such as visuals and what seems like an expansive way to level, but there are too many diversions from common convention and not in a way that feels natural and good.  Things you might think "you'd get used to that over time" or "aww, it doesn't sound too bad, just give it time", that may be correct, but If it's an annoyance 2 hours in I can only expect it to be a dulling of the irritation than a building enjoyment of the game's systems.I started KBM, and opted to move to controller due to lack of being able to time jumps you'd expect to just pick up and go. for this game there seems to be a disconnect between my brain hitting the button and actually managing  to correctly time the first 2 jumps in the tutorial.  I've put in my fair share of dutiful hours into Metroidvanias and Platformers to know how to manage the first jump of a tutorial (or 2nd / 3rd depending on sleep deprivation), yet this game seems... "Spongy"?  Too many mistakes that feel like they should have succeeded but failed due to possible "spungey" controls.  It 'feels' like jumps should be made. _childDocuments_.review: Colorful platformer in which we will go on a journey into an unusual world created by a certain god named Chaos. We are waiting for the familiar story of the eternal struggle between good and evil and light and darkness, so our protagonist will have to explore the mysterious areas of this world and perform a variety of tasks. All levels are interconnected and present a huge labyrinth, which allows us as a player to explore it in any order. Travel through the game locations we will be by jumping on unusual platforms while avoiding a variety of traps, and in between battles, solve random puzzles. On our way there will be a variety of enemies, with whom you can deal with either melee or with the help of magic. Also, we will come across bosses, the destruction of which requires careful analysis of their movements and finding exposed areas. As the game progresses, we will be developing our main character with the discovery of new skills in combat, magic and survival. Upgrading the abilities of our hero will be useful in order to successfully pass the game levels, the complexity of which is constantly increasing.We must note the high level of design of the game locations and quality control of the game character's movements. _childDocuments_.review: Holy Hell, 85 hours to 100% completion on the games intended difficulty.  About 10-15  of those hours were probably mindless repetitive death. The the rest of them were spent exploring this games incredibly massive maze of a world. From start to finish this game is both very very good, and very very bad haha. The world itself and all its back grounds are gorgeous, if a little system heavy (had to run the game in quality mode  all the way). All of the enemies and characters and bosses look amazing. Some of the places you find yourself by the end of the game are very interesting and unique. However, the game is also undercut by a constant and brutal difficulty that starts at early with "why doesn't my dodge have i-frames" combat, and carries all the way through the game with "I'm going to burst a blood vessel" level platforming. Now I'm no stranger to difficult games. I mean, I beat Sekhiro, and Hollow Knight, and Dead cells is a go to past time. This game might take the cake. Your melee weapon has incredibly short range and most combat up through the mid game is a matter of waiting for an opporunity, dodging in and hoping you don't get smacked as you get a couple hits. then back out, rinse, and repeat. The lack of i frames in your dodge combined with collision damage means no dodging behind enemies as they swing, or getting passed shields. This can really slow the combat down and make it feel tedious and frustrating at points. Late into the game you start getting some abilities to help with this (if you search them out), but even then there is no upgrading your weapon or anything like that to innately give you more damage as you go. Up till you get the skill points and gems to invest heavily into a build your character really feels kind of garbage for being the king of darkness.Bosses are overall good I feel, if a little imbalanced with attacks that seem almost impossible to dodge at times. They are all unique and challenging though, even if the combat sometimes leaves you feeling like a wet noodle while fighting them. Some took multiple hours of attempts to kill and it can be a bit much at times, but they're all dead now sooo... yeah, thats a win.The platforming is something I have a love/hate relationship with. On the one hand, the devs clearly put a massive amount of work into thinking up and enacting many amazingly challenging platforming puzzlees. Much of the time especially in the late game, the movement feels fluid and helps the game with what its doing. Other times the games mechanics and hit boxes seem to be actively working against the player in frustrating and unfun ways. Your character will instantly explode and reset position if even a toe or hair brush a spike. And god but there are a lot of spikes. Thousands and thousands of spikes. Everywhere. On every wall, ceiling , and floor. At times this works, and at times it doesn't. Likewise the teleport arrows you have to use in many puzzles are ridiculously fast and difficult to aim, and you are expected to use them both rapidly and precisely in many situations. Lastly, the way the players jump is tied directly to how long the player held the button is taken to a an unfun extreme here, where your thumb being on the jump button for a 10th of a second can be the difference between being at the right height to hit some spikes or not. I personally had to spend four or five hours on one single puzzle room (Mausoleum 4). While overall good, experiences like mausoleum 4 and the 10th door were very frustrating and didn't leave me feeling accomplished so much as drained.Lastly I would talk about bugs. From start to finish I ran into many issues. Especially in the early game it seemed like my game was bugging out every other screen. Sometimes, my characters walk/run would lock up, and I could only get around by jumping. Jump pads would often fail to interact properly and drop me into a beam of death for no reason. Arrows would fly through switches or enemies without hitting them. And input lag (possibly from using a wireless controller in fairness) would result in missed jumps and dashes regularly. Added to the already brutal difficulty, these things almost made me walk away from the game several times. However from what I've seen, devs are actively responding to and working on many of these in the community, so I don't feel like this is a long term issue. Just know going in that as of this review these are still issues.All in all, despite my many gripes, this review is still a positive. Despite the difficulty it was nice to know I still have what it takes to complete this sort of game (and join the 3% of players with the 100% quests trophy). The game is beautiful and expansive, challenging and entertaining. It is definitely worth picking up and I very much look forward to seeing the next project from this studio. Good hunting friends, and may the dark guide your way.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is one of the best "Metroidvania" like games I have played, and I have completed Hollow Knight. It's world is MASSIVE and the movement is fluid and responsive (played with controller) and the classic experience of getting a new "power or key" to open a previously explored area that is only now accessible is rife in this game. Its music and art style are beautiful and the story is presented at a nice pace that lets you just get on and explore. It is hard and some of the jumping sequences are brutal and unforgiving, but the frequent checkpoint system helps to alleviate that and give you that one more try feeling before you branch out and find a path you could barely see but took a jump in the dark to find. Also I am playing the game on what is effectively "normal", there is also a hard more that adds puzzle elements of some kind... that will be my second play through. Bravo to the dev team, a brilliant gem of a game

_childDocuments_.review: I am no stranger to hard games, but this game's design is just sadistic. Only the most patient and determined can hope to deal with this game's downright evil and frankly demented level and enemy designs.While the game is beautiful looking and has reasonably decent control, a sizeable world to explore and some nice spectacle (I was really impressed by the giant sword boss in the light tower), that's not enough to exceed the level of frustration the gameplay generates by design.Absurd levels of visual obstruction and details ensure that platforming is far more of a chore than it needs to be, enemies and their attacks often obscured by foreground objects all but guaranteeing you'll take damage, and so many enemies damage you AFTER you killed them, have attacks that relentlessly track you, and healing is an exercise in frustration, often completely impossible during boss fights due to how relentlessly the attacks just keep coming. Grinding isn't an answer because it takes forever to level up and gain one tiny incremental level of damage. Nearly level 27 and I still have to hit the game's first enemies several times to kill them.I don't even want to get into the jumping obstacle courses. For comparison, Elden Ring is a game that rewards perseverance. This title seems to want you to be punished for playing it. Life is too short...UPDATE: After the recent update, I felt the need to update my review. While the game is still quite punishing, the devs seem intent upon making the experience as accessible as possible, and I noticed the many subtle but substantial changes to the gameplay. Attacks feel more substantial, buffs are a bit more noticeable. It feels just a bit more forgiving now, just a bit more interested in actually encouraging the player to keep moving forward.I'm going to push on and see this game through, because the only thing I found off about it was the immense difficulty, and that's been smoothed out... a little. Nice to see.

_childDocuments_.review: I would have loved to finish this game, but the platforming was too hard and unforgiving.  The story and art were both really great, and it's what really drew me to this game.  I would have given up on this game much sooner if they weren't so darn good, but I only was able to progress to roughly the halfway mark in the game.  I had to walk away and uninstall after the game introduced the ability to teleport wherever you shoot your arrow.  At this point, all my progress just ground to a halt simply due to the platforming puzzles becoming too dependent on this gimmick.  Each new platform puzzle from this point in the game going forward started to take longer and longer to complete, and started to get less and less fun.  The devs had to add in an easy mode to the game, because the original difficulty was too hard for most players.  They totally missed the mark as what really makes this game difficult is that you get sent back to the beginning of a platform puzzle if you take any damage, with some of the late game puzzles requiring players to make dozens of split-second moves and thread the needle precision aiming. Adding in a difficulty that let me just take the hit and continue on jumping would have been really great for this game, and if one ever does get added in, I may actually come back to try and beat this game.  Until then, this game is a thumbs down for just being too difficulty to be fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game started off with promise, but sadly it grows stale in a hurry. It boasts a HUGE world, but most zones feel like reskinned pallette swapped versions of the same area over an over.  Each area just has the same kind of instant fail spikes, patches of light, lava, etc.. with the same variety of enemies with maybe one or two unique ones per zone.  Even going from point a to b in most zones feels needlessly repetitive.  And the game is challenging sure, but so much of it works against any actual fun factor.  Challenge should have some sort of reward, but nothing feels rewarding.  You always feel weak and underpowered and special abilities are so stacked towards the back end of the game, just getting to them feels like a chore.  I remember going through a difficult area and  I found a key to get another ability and it turned out it was just another charge to the arrow ability which was just underwhelming and deflating.The boss fights in particular are a unique breed of frustrating, not because of the challenge they require, but because they usually just fall in the game design of "throw a bunch of random ♥♥♥♥ at once and hope rng is in your favor" And that's if you can actually see whats causing you damage.  So much of the encounters throw so many things that blend into the art design of the backgrounds.  The pheonix in the forge is  a great example of this, where so many fire effects are going on you have to learn what can actually damage you and whats just a special effect through trial and error, and even then the effects can prevent you from seeing whats going on.  TL;DR: Challenging in all the wrong ways, feels like a chore.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a game I found when trying to scratch the Metroidvania itch I had. In short, it's a fantastic game, combat feels great with a variety of ways to build, and exploration is... well top notch, which includes difficulty. The map of Aeterna Noctis is girthy, with secrets and back-tracking fully utilized. It's not a complaint, but a warning, there are platforming puzzles that are BRUTAL in this game. Like sit there for a few hours as you memorize each section brutal. Patience will win out, but you have to be diligent. And sometimes these puzzles are not well placed.This is mainly a critic for the devs. In Hollow Knight, the hardest jumping puzzles, in the Grey Castle, really just showed cool lore, a trinket for the "true" ending, and weren't holding in game power. Aeterna Noctis has these BRUTAL puzzles which lock actual power behind them and that can really feel frustrating as it feels like you can't progress the game without passing said BRUTAL puzzles. I certainly feel pride in beating those puzzles, but I won't be installing the game... any time soon because I don't want to go through those puzzles again lol.If you're looking for a Metroidvania game with some real GIRTH to it, I cannot recommend Aeterna Noctis enough. But don't go crying to the internet if you can't take more than 5 minutes to solve a puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish listed this game a long time ago. However, I typically don't buy games as soon as they release. Instead, I wait until the final edition comes out….. At 50% off :P. I was looking forward for this game doing really well commercially and a bunch of DLC's coming out in the future. Unfortunately, this game received a bunch of negative reviews complaining about various minor things. It all seemed like people were simply complaining since the game was too difficult. "Damn casuals" I thought to myself. They're complaining about a perfectly awesome game! So I tried doing what little I could to help the developers by buying the game earlier than I normally would and writing a glowing review for it. Now that I've played the game…….I get all the complaints. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, do I get all the complaints.I am no stranger to difficult games. I've finished all the Dark Souls games, Bloodborne, and Sekiro. I've also finished Hollow Knight (White Palace + Pantheon of the Knight), Super Meatboy, Cuphead, Dead Cells (5 boss cells), etc…. Despite all of the difficult games I've played, this is by far the most difficult Metroidvania game by a mile. It's frankly quite astonishing. Within the first 30 minutes of the game, I saw how small the platforms were and how fast the spike traps were and I thought "You've got to be kidding me". Then I faced the 1st boss and I thought "You've got to be KIDDING me". Then I faced the 2nd boss and I thought "YOU'VE GOT TO BE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ KIDDING ME". You get the idea. Whoever designed this game has absolutely no chill. Clearly their idea of a fun evening is to fight a modded Pale Champion in Hollow Knight :P.Despite this, I can't deny that Aeterna Noctis at its core is an amazing game. I mean, this game is basically a combination of Hollow Knight (Combat), Castlevania Symphony of the Night (level up system + general art style), the Ori series (Spectacle + Freedom of Movement), and Celeste (difficult platforming). And it's by no means a cheap knock off of these games. Each aspect of Aeterna Noctis's gameplay can rival the games from which it takes inspiration from. The combat is absolutely great and challenging, with difficult bosses that are rewarding to beat. The game looks absolutely beautiful and the skill tree makes me look forward to levelling up instead of being something passive that I don't care about. The spectacle of some of the bosses is phenomenal (e.g. fighting the giant sword and the phoenix) and the freedom of movement through the teleportation (crystal) arrows make movement an absolutely joy. The platforming is challenging as all hell yet always fair and precise. The music is also pretty damn good.While this game definitely made me rage, there were also plenty of moments where I was having a lot of fun. Sure, there are definitely flaws with this game, but it also has so much to offer. The combat is great. Pretty much every single enemy in this game is well telegraphed and it's very enjoying finding the best way to deal with each enemy. In the beginning, I didn't particularly enjoy fighting enemies because I found them hard and any health I lost would make me upset because that was one less health for me to attempt a difficult platforming section that I knew was coming. Eventually, I got to the point where I looked forward to fighting enemies because I wanted their blood to recover my health >:D. That's a constant story with this game: Not liking something in the beginning but eventually loving it once you master it.I mentioned that this game had spectacle. Part of that is the great art style and how the camera is often zoomed out so that you can really appreciate said art style. Another big part of the spectacle are the bosses. Some of the bosses are similar to the bosses in Ori and the Will of the Wisps in that they're huge and their attacks look absolutely fantastic. It similarly feels really good taking down these bosses, because you're basically David taking down Goliath. While there are a lot of bosses that offer a great spectacle, that's not to say that there aren't some bosses that offer a personal duel style battle similar to Hollow Knight. Aeterna Noctis definitely has those types of bosses too. All in all, it's simply a great variety in the types of bosses you'll be facing and you'll always look forward to beating a boss, because they're always going to be distinct and unique from anything else you've faced.Similar to Hollow Knight, you have a type of mana called "blood" which you can use to heal and use special attacks. What's unique to Aeterna Noctis is that the special attacks don't take an entire mana chamber. They take like 25% of it. What's great about this is that it encourages you to use your sub-weapons throughout the game, not just in boss battles (because otherwise, you'd want to save up your mana to heal). At multiple points in the game I was barely using my sword and using multiple sub-weapons instead, which felt great.The progression system is another highlight, of which this game probably has one of the best in its class. Not only do you have 6 gem slots in which you can equip various gems that provide very strong passive benefits, similar to Hollow Knight, but you also have a skill tree! This skill tree provides very significant passive benefits, and during the later half of the game I was constantly thinking of what the best skills would be in order to beat the bosses I was facing. One complaint from others that I find unfair is the skill tree being too boring, providing lame bonuses like increased damage or critical strike chance. Some people have even compared the skill tree to World of Warcraft! Why don't we compare it to Path of Exile as well? How many Metroidvania's have skill trees? Barely any. They typically have a level up system (i.e. like Castlevania Symphony of the Night) where the stat boosts are automatic. Hell, Hollow Knight doesn't even have a level up system. Compared to those games (i.e. Castlevania and Hollow Knight), the skill tree in Aeterna Noctis is leagues better. I was always excited to level up and work my way towards the more interesting nodes in the skill tree, which I can't say is the case for a typical Metroidvania. You have to compare games within the same genre is all I am saying. There are 2 main problems with Aeterna Noctis. First, this game has 0 pacing. It's balls to the wall precising platforming and combat pretty much as soon as you start the game. For most of my time playing this game, it didn't feel like I was playing a Metroidvania. It felt like I was playing "I Wanna be the Guy". Not that there is anything troll or unfair about Aeterna Noctis. It's just that it's one challenge after another with almost no breathing room in between and it's frankly very exhausting. Second, whoever designed this game was way too in love with Celeste. Pretty much everything is "Blank + Platforming". Combat + Platforming. Spectacle + Platforming. Exploration + Platforming. Puzzle + Platforming. Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I've always believed that difficulty can only add to a game (as long as it's not troll/unfair like "I Wanna be the Guy")….. Aeterna Noctis has shown me that this formula doesn't always work. This game is difficult as hell and there's nothing troll/unfair about it, but I can't say I was having fun for my entire playthrough. However, it can't be denied that Aeterna Noctis is an amazing game with a lot to offer. It's basically Hollow Knight along with a skill tree, more spectacle, and great freedom of movement with the teleportation arrows. It's unfortunate that one aspect of the gameplay, the difficulty, makes it difficult to enjoy all the other aspects. If they can just smooth out the difficulty, which I hope they do with the Aeterna mode, then this will definitely become a game that every Metroidvania fan should experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Metroidvania based around platforming, and it doesn't do that very well.There's a difference between hard and poorly designed. The platforming in this game is poorly designed. The mechanics of the game are clumsier than most modern games. The game drops the player off the edge of platforms sooner and has poorly defined edges. The controls for jumping don't feel tight as well.The game also has a terrible curve on platforming. The tutorial starts off absurdly basic then you're thrown into difficult challenges right away. Small failures are complete failure, forcing you back to the start of a puzzle. These challenges aren't particularly "neat"; the timing often feels haphazard like a Mario Maker level that happens to work. But this doesn't make the game exactly hard, since you can often start very close to where you failed without a large penalty. It just means you'll take a longer amount of time to travel around.The game uses two of the worst features of platforming, "Close Jumps" where you can't quite be sure if you can make it if you can do it, and where making repeated trips is a chore, and "Head Bangers" where your jumping is restrained by hitting the roof.The most egregious examples of not understanding fun platforming are some places where you can't die from platforming but can waste time. These rooms require very specific sets of jumps back and forth to get over a simple wall in the middle. The platforms are just high and far enough apart that you have to jump back and forth left and right to move on with one specific pattern that works. This has no challenge, just a punishment if you are playing a meaningless repeated traversal casually.You can turn off the platforming, but the game has little going without it.  "Exploration" is not a great feature in a Metroidvania and the combat is very thin compared to other games of the type. If the shooting in a Call of Duty game doesn't work well, the developer's solution shouldn't be to turn off shooting. If the game can't get it's primary feature right, it's not fun.*****EDIT: In response to the developer:I played the game entirely after the Jan 10 patch for jumping. The biggest problems with platforming were "hit boxes" for platforms and player which are less than generous, the amount of repetitive jumps that do little to increase challenge but expend time, and the rough nature of many of these jumping puzzles. I didn't even mention how much trial and error was involved in the review.I only played the game for an hour, and that was the specific point I said "I do not want to play this anymore because I am not having fun and the problems are not things that will go away". I'm not being paid to finish this game. I won't give a negative review when I'm just not feeling it for a game but I'm unsure. But when the core design is off I'm not going to play on in expectation that it becomes a very different game.Honestly, the point where I was ready to give up was when I was in a room where all the enemies were dead and there was no challenge. There was exactly one route over a nondescript wall in the middle. I had to make this exact series of back and forth jumps with no alternate option. Failure gave you a short drop to the ground and forced you to jump again. A completely waste of time if you miss. The feeling of free movement is killed every time you come here because you must make the exact set of jumps over again. It's not about the satisfying skill of finally hitting everything right, it's about running the same repetitive steps to get to the challenge. It was a chore.I don't even know how the game would improve with a patch. If the platforms were given reasonable edges and the level layouts were redesigned to be less time consuming it might get somewhere, but this would require belief that there is a philosophical problem with the design.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game looks really nice and has good game feel, it's a slog to play.The main issue is that the game absolutely fails at being a metroidvania. In a metroidvania, you have to explore and backtrack, but here the maps are often needlessly convoluted and filled to the brim with obstacles. The obstacles work in the Hollow Knight way: you get hit, you lose a health point and respawn at the nearest ledge. But in Hollow Knight there were just a few areas that were really focused on platforming between obstacles, while Aeterna Noctis is obsessed with obstacle courses.The Furnace was the point where I realized I was done with the game. A giant, convoluted box with paths that go everywhere and loop back on themselves with no rhyme or reason, where every simple trek from point A to point B was filled with 5 or 6 obstacles, often in a row and with no ledges. Not very hard per se, but very time consuming and definitely not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard.But the sense of accomplishment after overcoming its toughest challenges is incredibly rewarding.Casual players might find it difficult to enjoy, as the map is vast, the difficulty steadily increases, and it takes time to fully complete. However, seasoned fans of Metroidvania and platformer games will likely appreciate its depth and design.Give it a genuine shot. Don't give up just because it's tough—push through, and you'll find the experience truly rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the platforming aspect of Metroidvanias then you might get something out of this game. I look for good combat and level designs in my Metroidvanias. The platforms are irritatingly small and the levels are filled with one-shot-kill spikes to add artificial difficulty. Otherwise there is not much to like. The combat is very shallow and this does little to build on the genre outside frustrating platforming.

_childDocuments_.review: "A precise platformer with imprecise controls." This is perhaps the best summary of my issues with Aeterna Noctis. A game lauded for its unforgiving difficulty, AN is certainly hard, but not for good reasons.In my brief stint with the game (explored ~2.5 sizable areas, beat one boss) most platforming challenges of note felt essentially like slamming my head against a wall in the same place, at the same time, with only slight variations imperceptible to the part of my brain that is deciding where and when to slam my head, until it broke. The analogy is a bit stretched but my point is this: it is usually tedious to perform the same jump dozens or hundreds of times until it is perfectly lined up, and without other considerations to support precision when doing this, it becomes pretty awful.There is a persistent and frustrating issue with backgrounds and foregrounds blending together, and scenery/foliage/etc. can obscure significant parts of the play area. These problems can make it difficult to read what your next move should be, what hazards are present, or even where your character is. Combat felt very passive—wait for the enemy to finish attacking, leaving you with an opening, then get in range and swing at them a couple times. Perhaps this is something that changes further on in the game, but for the first ~6+ hours, you don't have much you can do while enemies are swinging at you. If an enemy starts attacking, you just get to maneuver out of the way, and sit & wait until they are done. Then you attack them a bit, they start attacking again, repeat. Often several times. Most combat encounters ended up feeling like a chore. Enemy corpses exploding after death is also an annoying time wasting mechanic. This is not an interesting challenge, it just forces players to wait around. Character movement is slow.On a separate note, I'm not a fan of the writing nor aesthetics of AN. I think the above mentioned issues are much more relevant in terms of my impression, but it's worth noting that the plot/dialogue has a pretty YA vibe and the artwork is amateur.I've heard people say the game improves as you get further, but I haven't gotten far enough to start enjoying it. Perhaps I will give it a try another day, but for now I'd like to spend my time playing games I think are fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but can't. The game seems to be designed to repeatedly punish the player rather than let them have any fun.  The player progresses through a  repeated pattern of dying where in the fraction of a second they're given to learn patterns before they take a hit and eventually die is tedious and frustrating.The constant use of a one hit kill and reset mechanic also gets very old very quickly. The combat mechanics for some enemies aren't thought out well either. Guys that shoot fire or explosives in a spread pattern straight at you. All I have is linear movement and the enemies track so it's a constant game of avoidance, being on edge and taking hits that feel genuinely unfair. Exploring is sometimes alright but every time I hit a boss fight I just end up getting slaughtered 5 times, get bored then turn it off. It would help IMMENSELY if I could tell what was going on during busy periods. The art style is such that it's often impossible to differentiate what is a platform and what isn't, what can actually damage me and what I don't need to avoid or even where I am on the screen. If this has been done intentionally, I'd ask why?The bosses are an insane step up in difficulty. I can't be bothered to learn bosses by dying repeatedly in cycles to tells that last 0.5 seconds spawning instant attacks and implement unfair and punishing one hit mechanics repeatedly. It's really not fun to die in a matter of seconds to a new boss when you know you're expected to learn patterns but simply aren't given the chance and have 0 ability to rely on skill to get you through.Could this not have been toned down to allow for some actual fun and a learning process that doesn't kill the player repeatedly?I see the devs have previously written in forums things like "keep trying!"  My answer to that after 14 odd hours is no - I won't. I'll very quickly go play something else better designed that doesn't infuriate me with artificial difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Probably the best metroidvania I've ever played at the time of this review. The sheer amount of content you get for the price tag, especially when on sale, is enormous. Not to mention the artwork is beautiful, the visuals and mechanics of the boss designs (for the most part) are some of the best I've ever seen, the skill tree progression is neat to have, the tremendous amount of passive skill customizations through gems is enormous, there are many traversal abilities unlocked during the playthrough that tremendously change gameplay and unlock new areas, the maps are very cleverly designed, and the precision platforming (on Noctis difficulty) is some of the craziest I've ever seen. To top it off, you can switch the difficulty on the fly if at any point you don't feel up for the crazy platform challenges on Noctis difficulty or just want to backtrack quickly. However, I did notice a strange bug in the endgame area (I believe it's called Royal Stairway) though - after dying, the game wouldn't accept any of my movement inputs and I was stuck at the lantern/throne. I haven't had any issues with losing progress on my map or saves as reported in some of the negative reviews.Side note: At the current time of review, I basically shot straight through the story and collected all the shards and ran into a roadblock with the High Aurora boss fight. I will come back and finish the endgame once I generally make more progress and become stronger first.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I have to admit that I vacillated a little bit about whether or not to recommend this game.  I spent quite a bit of the time I played this game really quite frustrated.  I play a lot of games, generally consider myself pretty skillful of them, and yet still had quite a few times that I just thought about putting it down and leaving it alone.Having played through the game and its extended content, however, I clearly enjoyed it enough to keep pushing through, so I will give this a qualified review: get it if you A) want to challenge yourself; B) want a *large* metroidvania - it took me 45ish hours; and C) don't mind beating your head against the wall.

_childDocuments_.review: I dumped 50 hours into this to reach the ending with a 75% completion rating, and there's still a lot on the table.  This is a hard game.  This game has massive amount of content.  This game also has some very questionable design choices that make it very frustrating at times.  This game is basically a precision platforming metroidvania.  It may not seem like it at first as it takes a bit to ramp up, but when it does you will be reeling.  This is an interesting design, but as you get late into the game, some of the level designs are really annoying for the sake of being hard without a sense of good design.  Fast travel locations are not as plentiful as they need to be.  There are plenty of checkpoints, but backtracking through areas to collect stuff is agonizing when the territory is full of hard and outright annoying platforming.  To make matters worse, the locations of some of these points is completely baffling.  By the time I was near the end of the game I couldn't wait for it to be over, as such I have a love / hate feel for this game.The devs are adding an easy mode that nerfs platforming, but what the game truly needs is proper balance to late game areas and bosses.  Bosses seems to have an stupid amount of HP in some cases, combined with over-the-top attack patterns that make them a grind in their own.  This game will probably make you very mad.  It is good, but it is hard, and some of that difficulty does feel artificial later in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hollow Knight without bugs.+Nice visuals.-Bad hitboxes. Touching enemies damages you. The laziest way to increase difficulty.Very short range of melee which, coupled with previous point, makes game much harder than it deserves to be.HORRIBLE aiming which gets even worse because game sometimes demands you to shoot switches with almost pixel-perfect accuracy and as fast as possible because you're on clock.Music is repetative and boring.Two difficulties. Why is it a problem? The "normal" difficulty is actually an "easy" difficulty (with very big quotes, because the game is still unnecesary hard) where you can't get most of achievements, making you think that you're playing a castrated version of game.Annoying platforming. A LOT of jumping demanding you almost pixel-perfect jumps and air dashes. And, of course, the MC can't grab ledges with his hands despite them being free.A lot of "cheap" ways to damage you. Enemies that blow up after death and spawn projectiles (some of them auto-aim at you, others ricochet from walls). Enemies that don't have any attack indicators. The positioning of enemies also works in a way that you will often fight not only with one or several enemies, but also will be trying not to fall or touch some damaging walls.HP points instead of more fair HP pool with different attacks damage you in different amounts. Instead, every attack, every touch of the enemy deals 1 HP point which is a lot.Recurring bug that can erase your map progress. Yes, all your map will become black like you just started the game. I already had this bug twice during my playthrough.Enemies are sometimes very difficult to see because of backgrounds and stuff on foreground.Also game sometimes crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: This one is tough. I enjoyed every fragment of platforming in this game, but the boss fights are just tedious. The platforming is hard but it doesn't get to the level of celeste which is fine. For the boss fights, well they are just not original, difficulty is risen by means of bullet hell and unfair mechanics. You basically need to be on top of your game particularly when reaching the latest bosses.The game is gorgeous, there are some bugs, I'm looking at you "Origin of the machines" not completing, some times jumping, dashing and turning is sloppy. The controls for the arrow are way too sensitive...I'm also missing some QoL mechanics, like being able to kill yourself, reduced loading screens, not doing the boss animation between tries (for the robot it was awful), a mode for practicing bosses, automatic refill of blood before a boss... etcI'm giving it a pass because I enjoyed the game overall, but this is definitely not a for everyone. I did play only Noctis to 100% completion, so I don't know if Aeterna mode could be more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: So, it might look weird that I'm recommending a game that I've refunded, and frankly I'm still not sure if I really recommend because it still left me with a mixed impression, but overall it was more positive than negative (also, I feel like the current reviews makes you think the game is worse than it actually is).The main problem with the game is that the controls are just not as tight as you would expect them to be. This applies to both movement and combat, so if you go into this expecting the smoothnes and precision Hollow Knight offers when fighting, or the tightness of Celeste or Ori while platforming you'll end up being dissapointed. To be clear, I'm not talking about the difficulty, which was fine in my experience, but about how the game feels. It's definitely more challenging in it's early game than HK (you'll keep hearing comparisons to this game but it's hard to not notice the influence), and by no means are these challenges impossible, but the lack of fine tuning makes it feels not as satisfying as fun as it should. The combat is pretty basic so far, but the enemy design it's not as good as a game with this kind of combat needs, often just tanking hits was both easier and faster to do, and the roughness of the controls didn't help here (for example, if you hit something and then want to quickly do a dash backwards sometimes you'll dash forward despite pressing back +  dash, it seems almost random). The sword swings aren't very satisfying either, and the amount of pushback you get after hitting an enemy doesn't feel right. You can also bounce of enemies like in HK, but again this feels way more awkward, and in general hitboxes are kind of wonky, which for a game with rather simple combat it's a big flaw. This doesn't mean it's bad, it's perfectly serviceable and even fun but it's really not as tight as other entries in the genre.The art is similiarly uneven, with a lot of good but also with a lot of less good aspects. The character designs vary a lot, the Guardian and the guy in the Library look good, the Kings are also good looking (though the king of Darkness reminds me a little too much of Alucard, but considering the state of Castlevania that's a plus in my book). The hidden merchant in the starting zone looked off though, and many of the enemies look pretty amateurish. The opening animated cutscene was incredibly rough too. It's not bad looking at all but it sometimes really feels like a really good flash game (though that may have been what they were going for, idk).The level design was actually pretty decent, the challenges were fun and the platforming was satisfying, even if brought down by the controls. The story was intriguing even if typical and suggested a twist. After writing long pharagraphs of my problems with the controls, the combat and the art it might be weird to see this review as a positive, but actually it's not a bad game at all. It's definitely ambitious and is trying to do a lot of things even if it isn't excellent at any of them. The developers definitely put a lot of love and care into the game and it shows. It really feels like a diamond in the rough, and I'm willing to get back into it, but I'll rather give it time to see if the devs can fine tune some of the rougher aspects of the controls. I admit I was dissapointed because it wasn't as tight as I hoped for and it really wasn't the Metroidvania I was looking for right now, but I still think it's worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: War for balance.I was looking for games with controller support and came across Aeterna Noctis. 2D platformers are one of my favorite genres, so I bought the game and have never regretted it.
