_childDocuments_.review: I have played countless of metroidvania and action platformer games in general. By far this is probably the most difficult one to date. The game description is not even kidding when it says 'real challenge'. It's crazy! So before you even consider buying this game, be warned, THIS GAME IS EXTREMELY DIFFICULT.I will make a disclaimer before hand. I haven't finished the game of this writing but I am about to (two levels/areas left). Cleared the cosmos and the optional Abyss area. I play in the "intended" difficulty, Noctis. I have not tried the easier Aeterna difficulty yet.Let us start with the graphics. This game is a 2D game, however despite being a 2D game it is 16gb big. Why? Oh man where do I even start. At your first level/area, you get into Wasteland of the fallen which is a bit of a dark and gloomy place, you might wonder if everything in game is dark and gloomy but don't be fooled. Once you get into the 3rd level/area, it switches to a more vibrant and lighty atmosphere, which deeply contrasts the previous 2 levels/areas, then it dials that up to 11 for the next following areas with visuals that are just amazing.Then you get into the gameplay, I know a bad level design when I see one, but this is not even a bad level design. This is SADISTIC design. I was a bit skeptical when there where alot of instant death spikes on the first 2 levels/areas and I though to myself that perhaps if I get used to this, I will get onto this game quick. BOY I WAS WRONG. After the first 2 levels, the game just keeps introducing gimmicks unique to each level/area. Some reviewer here were complaining about how it was not cool to introduce reversed controls or camera dizziness in the Cosmos, that's cheese compare to Enigma which is the most confusing level/area that I have ever encounter in my life. I am not even kidding. I downloaded this full map (yeah I'm cheating a bit to know what I get to) and even the author of the full map said how pain in the ass the level/area is to navigate even when he labeled each entrance/exit. Very confusing.Then there are the powerups. Boy I though it would be like Megaman X6 where there are some armor like the Gaea or Shadow armor that will make you invulnerable to instant death. Nope. the powerups are design to give good enough options but not overkill that it completely skips the challenge. I though that having the teleport arrows with time being slowed was gonna cheapen the experience until I encounter areas where YOU CANT EVEN USE THE TELEPORT ARROWS AT ALL.The music is also great. Each areas and bosses have their own unique atmosphere. So far my most favorite one was the Second Boss sword. Great music and when I beat that boss, I already felt that I can take whatever challenges this game throws at me.Lastly the lore and area itself is great. There is so much to explore and so many stories you have to uncover on your own. Heck the game even introduces its own language, Aeternian. Which is what all the characters use in the game. All I can say is, this game is a gem. Great gameplay, great visuals, great presentations. Definitely one of my favorite modern games so far and hey it's even self published and is an indie which is a plus.

_childDocuments_.review: Not really for me.  Plays alot like hollow knight, only not extremely polished. Negatives: When you attack an enemy your attacks contact moves you backwards, this frequently results in deaths due to env. Enemies deal damage on contact always.  Your ill equiped to mitigate any damage, your given a doge that doesn't avoid projectiles or attacks.  It sticks on the direction change. IE your running forward attacking, hold backwards and hit dodge quickly and you go forwards rather than the direction you pressed.When you die in one of the platformy puzzle bits, you drop your "souls" or exp or whatever, and you can't die gain any new exp till you go and go back to that spot.  Which is unessicarily punishing, it's not that big of a deal really but it's a bad mechanic,  a few times I wanted to get some more exp and had left my death marker in a hard to get spot that was impossible to backtrack from.  So I had to exit game after getting the death marker back, to get to a previous checkpoint with my stuff.  It just feels bad.That said I think if you like hollow knight this game might be a good game. _childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews but this game is special so i figured i had to.First off, if your looking for a game to fill the whole in your heart, then look no further. _childDocuments_.review: I've been a gamer for years, and I’ve seen my share of both good and bad games, but this one has been particularly disappointing. I went into it with an open mind, but the sheer number of flaws made it impossible to enjoy.First off, the combat feels clunky and unpolished. It’s almost as if the developers didn’t bother testing it thoroughly. The questline is a confusing mess with zero guidance, leaving you to wander aimlessly. As for the dialogue, it’s laughably bad—there’s no immersion, just a series of awkward and poorly written lines.The checkpoints are another major issue. Whoever placed them either didn’t care or didn’t understand basic game design principles. How did that even make it past quality control?Also a frustrating aspects is the lack of an inventory system for quest items. You’re left scrambling, trying to remember what you picked up and where it’s supposed to go. And the boss battles? They don’t even have health bars, making the damage points feel utterly pointless. It’s like they forgot the basics of what makes boss fights exciting.Then there are the platforming sections. The jump patterns are unnecessarily difficult, almost as if the developers got bored and decided to crank up the difficulty just for the sake of it. It’s frustrating rather than challenging, and it feels like a cheap way to add artificial difficulty to an already flawed game.Finally, the story—it’s a mess. It doesn’t flow, it doesn’t engage, and by the end, I was left wondering what the point of it all was.I really wanted to like this game, but it’s clear that it’s riddled with amateur mistakes. If this is the direction they’re heading, it’s no surprise that people are hesitant to buy their new releases.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a solid game, man! It offers an immersive experience with its captivating gameplay. The graphics are on point, creating a visually appealing world. _childDocuments_.review: This is a game that wears its Hollow Knight inspiration on its sleeve and joins the rank of the rare platforming-focused Metroidvanias. I've described it multiple times as "Kaizo Hollow Knight" and I think that's far from a flaw. It is excellent at following up on your mastery of HK mechanics, proposing a massive new world to explore and overall a way more challenging experience both in platforming and boss fights while keeping similar movement (it does also feature an easier difficulty that I've heard is closer to its inspiration).Still Aeterna Noctis manages to be its own thing by switching up the level design frequently, introducing different physics and platforming elements depending on the biome, and introduces an important mechanic at around the midway point that changes how you approach platforming in a way that feels challenging and rewarding.The game also features gorgeous hand draw environments and great use of lighting, although the MC does look a bit janky amongst them (probably for clarity reasons). The soundtrack is decent and while the story isn't anything special I found the dialogue pretty well written and funny at times.Overall I had a fantastic experience with it and will look forward to what Aeternum studios has in store next for us metroidvania fans. Highly recommended for those who want more Hollow Knight and are not scared of challenging experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews that often, but God these negative reviews made me write.So basically, this is a Metroidvania, platformer, "difficult and souls-like" game, literally the exact words are in the tags of this game, and guess what most of the negative reviews are about? "It's too difficult to be fun" "too punishing" "too hard" etc .. like wtf? it's LITERALLY as what the tags/genre said, and since when a game being difficult is a bad thing? Or a bad game design? (Btw they already put an easier game mode) if these genres are not for you or you don't like these kinds of games. DONT buy the game and then gave it a bad review/reputation and backlash against the developers (unfortunately they do respond to these unrelevant critiques).They promised you a game that is "difficult, platformer, Metroidvania" and then they deliver a game that is "difficult, platformer, Metroidvania", don't give them hate for something u don't like to consume but others do, they promised and did what they promised!Imagine you find so much hate towards dark souls or bloodborne or sekiro because of how hard the game is? (btw I don't like these games and I don't like a game that is so difficult like these, but Aeterna Noctis clicked with me and I am playing hard mode).I didn't finish the game yet, but even if I stop playing it because the game gets too difficult to the point that is not appealing to "ME", I will NOT make noises and hate for being what it promised to be and give the developers who clearly put heart and soul in their game a hard times.Pros:-Beautiful art style. They have 2 styles one is for the cuteness which is like church coloured windows, and the other for the gameplay (can't describe it) that is smooth and the lighting/shadows is so beautiful.-Great soundtrack for each region (also you can play the piano, but it's not that important)-Not saying that the story is the best story u can find in these genres, but it's a good and decent story that has some twist and make you wanna continue to see the end.-The atmosphere gives u, old dark medieval and Castlevania vibes.-Love the RPG aspect, they go hard on it. So because you lost all your abilities, weapons and armor, you need to regain them all. 1-You need to find your lost weapons that are scattered around the world and ( also gems to enhance your armor which will give u effects)2- Regain your ability like dash, double jump etc by killing the boss or opening the doors in the library when you find the keys.3- killing mobs give u exp to level up ur skills-tree (passive skills, like increasing crit change or damage etc)Cons:-Levelling up takes too much time.-There are NPCs and characters around the world, but I still didn't find any of them interesting yet (didn't finish the game).-I don't know if I can call them puzzles or obstacles or traps, but most of these things if you make a mistake, u will get back to the beginning. I don't know if this is considered as a con?- I feel like everything takes too long? Sometimes u get bored.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: The first part of the review will be spoilerfree, the second will not.Aeterna Noctis is what would happen if Hollow Knight and Celeste had a son.The game is a metroidvania with heavy focus on platforming and combat, and when I say heavy focus on platforming, I mean HEAVY.In the first couple of hours I was feeling like I was playing a spiritual successor of Hollow Knight, and that's great since is one of my favourite games of all times.But then the games smacks you with the increasing difficult in the platforming.This is a metroidvania, you got your skill tree, you got your regular upgrades from exploring and defeating bosses, and getting a reward after a long exploration or fight feels rewarding.The art style is beautiful, the "3d" backgrounds are stunning.For the OST.. I have mixed feelings, because while there are some great tracks (Forge boss OST is amazing), the normal OST while exploring areas are forgettable to say the least.For the bosses: so far except one they were great, well designed and really fun overall.Now, for the negative part of the game: as I stated, the game takes an HEAVY focus on platforming, so much that going throught areas goes from being challenging to painful, I know the devs are working on making a different game mode to focus more on the action than the platforming, but as the game is now, I need to state it. Since the platforming is so hard, so long and so much, this game isn't for everyone, I'm not that great at platforming (example: I got 100% achievements in Hollow Knight, but never bothered with trying Path of Pain) and this game is like consistently being in Celeste/Path of Pain. I actually felt relieved when I reached the boss, because there I could actually have fun without getting frustrated.This is why, while my review is positive because the game have a lot of great things packed together, I cannot say that everyone should play it, the pricetag is high (but well deserved since the game is massive) and most of the players would drop out sooner than later.Another point I need to tell you is the "arrow" mechanic. This pains me a lot. While it is a cool mechanic on it's own, having basically all platforming tied to it is just crazy, I had to swap from Joypad to mouse and keyboard multiple times to get past some really hard and precise teleport arrows puzzles, and that wasn't fun at all. As another user already said in the reviews: it's okay to create extremely hard platforming for extra stuff that reward exploration, but  doing that over and over and over and over again for progressing the main story is excruciating and will leave you frustrated more than anything else.Another thing is that the thrones are too few and too far away from each other, making the backtracking (a core mechanic in a lot of metroidvania) bothersome, just to redo again all the platforming just to reach some places you couldn't reach before with your new movement abilities. Again, I know the devs already stated that they are implementing more thrones here and there, but this is a review for the state the game is right now.While there were other users that had problems with the imputs, I had none, there are a few bugs here and there that should be adressed, but overall is pretty polished for me. The main thing to resolve imho is that if you are attacking an enemy and try to dash away from him, you will dash in his face, because the game doesn't register the swap in direction fast enough, but I think this should be easy to fix, and you can play around it by hitting the enemy one less time and play safe. There was another bug that happened twice to me, if you hit a "spike" (or whatever that resets your position) while you were getting some momentum from the enviroment (like moving platforms, jumping balls or something like that) the momentum would remain after the respawn, making you lose another life, and once it fixed on it's own after getting hit a second time, the other one (with the jumping balls, I was basically permanently flying upwards) I had to close the game to fix it.Now be careful to keep reading because there will be spoilers ahead:I reached the mothership area, and there I had one of the most frustrating moment in my whole gaming experience so far.You start from the "D-section" and get the key for the "C-section" there, so, once I reached the teleport instead of keep going exploring the D-section I went for the C-section. There I did of course a lot of extremely hard, arrow focused platforming to reach a switch that changed some platforms from horizontal to vertical and vice-versa, than did the platforming back to the teleport once again to go back to the D-section, there I kept going right, doing yet another extremely hard platforming part just to find that there was a "king trials" key locked behind one of those platforms I moved earlier. This was soulshattering, thinking that I needed to go back to the teleport while doing an insane platforming session, to go back to the C-section to do yet again another platforming section to hit the switch, then go back and do that over again to reach the key made me just close the game saying "I'll think about it tomorrow".This was really really way too punishing for no reasons at all, since you had no clue where was the "right way" to progress.To pack it up:Aeterna Noctis is a great looking game with great bossfights and amazing artstyle, but is not for everyone since it is hard, way harder than any metroidvania I've played so far.I think you should wait till the two game modes get implemented in the game, because as it is now, I can reccomend it only if you really liked both Hollow Knight and Celeste (or supermeatboy if you prefer) and want to see them mashed together.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The game clearly takes inspiration from hollow knight, but ain't as polished. The pogo on enemies mechanic to refresh your movement CDs is clearly from HK, the dash is too (even tho I got hurt too many times by trying to dash through damage 'cause of muscle memory, if you played HK you'll know what I mean), and the way you heal is a mixture of HK and dark souls. You have potions, but you can even concentrate blood (soul in HK) to heal.I don't get what people say about the movement's feedback. Your character has inertia, in HK he doesn't, it's just how the game it's programmed. Takes just some time to get used to, but nothing game breaking or worthy of a negative review.I see this game as something to play while waiting for silksong. Game is big, boss fights are well made, it is not as punishing as HK or a proper souls like game, but the idea is here, and the overall gameplay is harder than HK.So far I've LOVED the platforming ♥♥♥♥.The game just came out tho, Devs have time to improve with players feedback, and I don't see a real reason to not recommend the game if you are down for a challenge.So far the only thing I don't like is that you unlock movement skills by opening doors and not by exploration in itself, but I'm nitpicking.The graphics is sometimes average, but there are a couple of breathtaking locations around. As of overall difficulty I'd place it somewhere below blasphemous, a lil bit over HK... Although not as punishing.As hornet would say, git gud 🤣And let's hope team cherry drops the bomb soon...

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best metroidvania game I have played out of about 150 metroidvanias.  It's  good.  When I say this, I mean best  rather than as a textbook example of metroidvania non-linearity and design.  There are better examples of that (Lone Fungus for instance!). 1.  The switch version has performance issues, don't buy it.2.  I recommend playing it on the harder original difficulty, if it gets too much you can toggle that at any time.3.  They poorly implemented a DLC which gives you a triple jump. I'd advise trying to resist using the triple jump gem (Or just avoiding the DLC area entirely) until after beating the game, as it trivialises a lot of the original platforming level design.-----------------------------------Okay, onto the rec/review:Metroidvania + Precision Platformer.  The first precision platformer I've really got into since Super Meat Boy.For both genre's, this game is at the top; everything is top quality.   You probably need to already be okay with precision platformers for me to recommend you Aeterna Noctis.  ..Although conversely maybe this is the game to open you up to precision platforming, as you have the exploration of a metroidvania to compel you to keep driving forward.At the time of this review, this is one of (if not the) largest metroidvania created so far.  The scale of this game is big, and the devs didn't slouch in any department;  It sounds great, looks gorgeous, and feels fluid moving around. The game, whilst difficult, is littered with checkpoints, so that even though you are precision platforming it is very forgiving.  It has an easy mode that I did not try which you can toggle at any time if the standard experience gets too much for you (nerfs the platforming sections considerably).  I've heard that this makes the game feel kind of bland though, so you are possibly better off to resist doing that.This has to be one of the best games I've played in recent years, it felt like a love letter to platforming, as though it was testing me for all those hours playing hundreds of platforming games over the years.This game is far grander in scale and better produced than anything else in the precision platformer or metroidvania genre, and if those genre's interest you then this game is absolutely essential.I wonder how I will go on to my next platformer without that teleport arrow..  It is a daunting tool to have to utilise when you first get it, but by the end of the game you will master it and find yourself using it in combat all the time to defeat enemies.. It's brilliant fun.The game commits a few sins for me, 2 of which are the sort I would normally put a game down for:1.  The puzzle world section is BS!  Every screen teleports you to some other room, and you need to search for invisible things.. It's just flat out bad.  2.  The upside-down areas in outer space.  Suddenly needing to play upside-down for large portions of this area can be infuriating.  It's a good thing though that this area came later in the game.  Once you get past the initial rage, you can't help but be impressed with yourself as you push through this section, and as I did progress, I really started to appreciate this area and it is probably among my favourites in the game.  It helps that this place is quite visually appealing as well.3.  You can't get all of your Steam achievements in one play through without prior knowledge.  You need to beat various bosses without acquiring certain items, or beat them in specific ways.  This is a minor nitpick.4.   There is an npc sidequest late in the game who teleports randomly to one of 10 different area's on the map, and you need to check each of those places to find him.  ..then he teleports away again.  He does this 3 times;  It's just annoying and tedium.5.  Occasional visual bugs, e.g. the killzone that I'm platforming around isn't visible (like light hazard areas), however I was able to at least see these killzones when i opened my map.6.  You eventually get too overpowered for the boss fights.  Some of the later bosses I beat on my very first try (including the final boss).  This is a shame, because most of the early boss fights were a blast and a real challenge, some of which (like the Emperor) took me 4 hours of continually failing before I eventually overcame him.With complaint 1 & 2, they were things I could see myself quitting a game over, However Aeterna is such an amazing game that I was more than willing to push through any frustrations that the game wanted to throw at me.  ===================== =====================  |  Astalon: Tears of the Earth | Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom | Hollow Knight |   Blasphemous 2 | Cathedral |  Afterimage | The Last Faith |  Elderand | Ori and the Will of the Wisps | Doomblade^ |  Ender Lilies: Quietus of the Knights | Depths of Sanity | Environmental Station Alpha |  Blast Brigade | Haak |  Alwa’s Legacy | Steamworld Dig 2 | Islets | Blasphemous | After Death | Pronty^ | Mortal Manor* | Escape From Tethys | Outbuddies DX* | Monster Sanctuary | Elliot Quest | Rebel Transmute |  Haiku, the Robot | The Mobius Machine | Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown | Ultros |  Lone Fungus | Ghost Song | Death’s Gambit: Afterlife | Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night | Kunai | Kingdom Shell | Axiom Verge | Rabi-Ribi | TEVI | Treasure Adventure Game |  Flipwitch | Infernax | Plague of Yamorn* | Column on the Sea | Jrago* | MF-01 Aerostrike^ | Laika: Aged through Blood | Xanthiom Zero | Carrion^ | Chasm | Wuppo | The Mummy Demastered | Momodora 4 | Momodora 5 | Catmaze | Castle In The Clouds | Omega Strike | HunterX | HunterX: code name T | Aggelos | Midnight Castle Succubus | Sheepo |  Ato | EldritchVania | Cookie Cutter | Elephantasy | Rusted Moss^ | Grime | Moonscars | The Messenger | Deedlit in Wonder Labyrinth | Iconoclasts | MindSeize | Ebenezer and the Invisible World | Luna’s Light* |  Castle In The Darkness | Alwa’s Awakening | RIN: The Last Child* | Pharaoh Rebirth | Yoku’s Island Express | Guacamelee! _childDocuments_.review: Do you like half of the enemies in the entire game blowing up in your face after you beat them?  Do you like challenge that screams "I hate everyone, and humanity was a mistake"?  Do you like knowing that the developers realised that their first pass at the game was so incredibly difficult that they made an easy mode for babies that strips what little good there is in this game was a good idea?  How about no i-frames on the dodge, no blocking, no parrying, and no way to avoid taking damage from enemies except to have the ability to see in to the future to try and dodge incredibly fast, bullet hell ludicrous speed attacks?  If all of that sounds good to you, than Aeterna Noctis is your kind of game, and I imagine you're gaming on a seat that is covered in spikes with someone smashing your knee caps and fingers every few minutes because you're a sucker for pain.

_childDocuments_.review: This game immediately gave me Hollow Knight vibes. And it does certainly have a lot of the same characteristics. The combat feels very similar, the way you move and pushback on hit. The art style is similar, with plenty of hand drawn elements, though I will say Hollow Knight's is better. It also has some very challenging platforming areas, and lots of them. The platforming is probably just as integral as combat and bosses, which is unusual for a metroidvania.The game does a really remarkable job at blending the metroidvania and platforming genre. The platforming can at times be quite challenging, but you have plenty of skills to help you clear them. I wish there was a bit more fast travel in some of the more challenging areas, so I didn't have to backtrack and redo more challenging areas when I realized I was missing a skill, or I should have gone a different direction. More fast traveling also would have been nice due to the sheer scale of this game. It's massive.I thought for sure this would be one of those you are done in 10-12 hour type cookie cutter platformers that you see regularly, but was pleasantly surprised at how many areas there were, how big the areas were, how much story there was, how many skills, how many equippables and collectibles. There really is a lot to do!I'm not entirely sure why this game has had mixed reviews in the past and is only about 75% positive. It's a really high quality game that is enormous and challenging, and does a lot of things really well. The visual effects in the game are stellar. The game feels very clean and polished. The music is very high quality and matches the vibe of the game well. It even has a section remiscent of Super Mario Galaxy, which was neat. There were a surprising amount of references to other videogames and anime, which I thought was a nice touch.I do have some gripes and did experience some bugs:1. There are a lot of quests, but it's not exactly clear what you are supposed to do (there are very few markers for anything outside main quests) and the quests are vague at times, but that may be part of the fun for some. Give how huge the game is, for some of the later side quests I had to look up what to do, as I'm not combing the corner of this massive game to find one room to interact with something that was non-interactable before picking up an item, and with no context clues that it would become interacable at some point.2. At times the controllers and some of the movement feels just a little bit off. Like your second jump when using your weapon to bounce off of objects in platforming puzzles. Or jumping after teleport in some of the platforming puzzles. I play enough platformers that I know when and why I die in a jumping puzzle. If the controls could be tightened up just a bit it would be helpful.3. Many of the gems are bugged out. They don't work or work sometimes. For example, The Vampire's Soul needs to periodically be uneqipped to work. When you do, it immediately starts working at an almost instantaneous rate. You have to hit a load screen, come back to a throne, and put it back on for it to behave properly for a short time, but becomes almost immediately bugged out again. And Wild Onslaught definitely does not deal 100% extra damage for Wild Blade. Tested it multiple times and numbers are identical.Other than that, this is a solid game, and one of the better metroidvania's I've played recently. Definitely recommend it. Took me over 60 hours to 100% in game content and 64% achievements. Full price is extremely fair, but if it's on sale, it's a no brainer.I was surprised to see that there weren't tons of developers on the project. It's huge and really well polished for what appears to be a smaller team. I'm looking forward to their other work and the sequel to this game. Keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, up there with Hollow Knight and GRIME in my favourite metroidvanias.I'm surprised I haven't heard about it, it's very fun, plays well, has a beautiful artstyle and a large world with diverse environments.There are various QOL improvements I'd like to see, mostly related to being locked into lengthy animations of elevators, portals, doors, boss intros, etc. as they take up a lot of time when travelling. I switched the difficulty to an easier one a few hours in.The game is very challenging, especially while getting used to the controls, especially the arrows. But the controls do work well, the movement is fast, fluid and enjoyable.Related to that, bosses pretty much require you to use the abilities at your disposal, so they might seem unfair or undodgeable unless you fight smart.Overall I'm enjoying the game very much, and those QoL hitches or rage-inducing platforming don't detract from the experience. Definitely recommended and a solid example of a great metroidvania that will tide you over until Silksong finally releases, any day now...
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

As a result I've had numerous crashes, controller disconnects, and other issues. _childDocuments_.review: How could we miss such a high-quality metroidvania, which has an insanely beautiful and dark style with high-quality effects and a rather intricate plot. Playing as the King of Darkness, we have to restore the balance of power by fighting the forces of light in the world of Eterna. Our path follows through 16 different game worlds, each of which fascinates in its own way, quality of study and abstraction. The combat and the passage as a whole are quite hardcore, because there are not many lives, and the enemies differ in the methods of attacks and defenses. Accompanying our game are 40 magnificent music tracks that will keep our spirits on every move in the level.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A massive and challenging platforming-focused Metroidvania.  Not for novices of the genre, but if you're comfortable with games like Celeste you should be able to handle the challenge.  If not, well, you can still try the easier difficulty, but where's the fun in that?The biggest mechanic that sets this apart from a lot of other platformers and MVs is the Crystal Arrow upgrade.  In short, it's an arrow you shoot and then press another button to teleport to its location.  At first, it seems a bit overwhelming, but stick with it and in no time you'll be jumping off walls, teleporting, dashing, jumping and firing more arrows to get past perilous mazes of spikes and other lethal hazards.  Once you get used to it, you'll find out that most of the challenging mid-air arrow shots can be executed just by firing vertically so the aiming isn't too crazy - plus there is a significant bullet-time effect while aiming to help line up your next shot or even just plan your next move.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

This game shouldn't be hard to run, and seeing this issue in a game that released in 2021 is pretty concerning.Update (10/30/24): A performance update hit today and the performance issues are the exact same, so I'll be shelving this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had a lot of promise, so writing a negative review is definitely not what I wanted.The idea behind it, the music, story and platforming, are all great in essence, but there are just too many glaring bugs to even begin attempting to play.A precision platformer cannot have a bug that randomly spawns you at an older checkpoint than the one you were at when you died, or horribly imprecise hitboxes.There's also a serious problem with synchronized moving platforms, that just de-synch after a couple of attempts.Additionally, there's a bug that prevents the game from closing, which is very frustrating, considering that I am trying to restart the solve AN OTHER BUG.All in all, my partner an I made a huge attempt to like this game, as we've been craving for a good metroidvania as we patiently await the launch of Hollow Knight's sequel, but this game ended up being a disappointment.I believe thorough play testing is needed, as well a serious code check.If you want my help, contact me through steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna is a game that seems catered to people like me. Metroidvanias are games I have come to appreciate due to their challenging nature and exploration elements and Aeterna delivers in every front.Astounding visuals, fluid and responsive controlls and challenging platform sections are the main elements that stand out in Aeterna, elements that come together in one of the most memorable experiences I've had lately. If any of this sounds like something you could be interested, I recommend you give it a shot.I feel very disconnected from current AAA games because they make me see now more than ever that games are business first and have lost the sense of passion that has made me fall in love with this medium.That's why I encourage people to play games like Aeterna Noctis, indie games are the only ones that in my opinion still have that feeling of "magic" when playing them. Yes, it can feel rough around the edges in some regards and the difficulty might not be for everyone, but it sill makes for a very enjoyable and fulfilling experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: People compare this to hollow knight but frankly I don't see it. The story is told via characters dropping large exposition dumps and the main character is basically just a walking cliche.  Contrasting with Hollow knight where most if not all of the story is told via environmental story telling. Story isn't all that important in a metroidvania but world building certainly is. Aeterna's world is flat and boring.  The loading screens break up the world making it feel much less cohesive than your traditional metroidvania.  Obviously, not all metroidvanias need to have seemingly endless level design, but the size of each area makes the likelihood of an interesting hidden area much lower.   Aeterna has decent combat and mechanics but overall it just doesn't scratch the same itch as hollow knight and feels more like an ARPG than a true metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: If this game had just a few more things that could help players out, such unlimited access to a teleport back to the last checkpoint, or an upgrade that allowed I frames during dashes, I could more willingly recommend this game. However, it is simply too brutally punishing for me to recommend it to most people. It is a game that does not feel like it wants the player to enjoy the game, but more a game that wants the player to suffer. I could see it appealing to some, but can't recommend it to most.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Sooooooooo.....this game is NOT easy, but it is an amazing grind. Recommend it to your favorite masochist or that one friend who won't stop talking about Hollow Knight, I can personally guarantee you that both will enjoy it! After 85 hours and 879 deaths, I'm around 97.5% completion overall. It's a bit game with a lot of secrets, memorable boss fights, quirky characters and dialogue, and puzzles and precision platforming unlike any other 2d game I've played. Side note: the developers put a lot of passion and thought into Aeterna Noctis, and it shows in every aspect of its design as well as stopping into live streams and adding minor updates and improvements.

_childDocuments_.review: Very well made game overall with some very few but very questionable platfoming-related design decisions, at least on the original/hardest difficulty.  The combat systems, including the heal methods, enemy types, and control responsiveness, are all on point which make up a huge part of metroidvania games like this one.  If you use a controller, pay attention to the vibration implementation.  It's literally the best in any game of this genre.Back to the platforming issue, I'm very glad to have the option of playing on the Aeturna difficulty, which both lowers combat difficulty (more on that below) and essentially removes some of the killing wispy block things that they put in the way of you trying to platform your way up, down, sideways, etc.  If it wasn't for that option, I'd probably have rage quit long ago due to not being able to move forward.  It's not just that they put those things in place to make optional objectives difficult, they actually put them in the way of moving forward in a couple of places. After 20 minutes or so of trying, I simply gave up and switched to the lower difficulty option, which honestly I NEVER do in games like this and I've played hundreds of them over the years.  All of that said, it's a definite recommend for me given the difficulty options (so far at least, hopefully I don't get blocked again later).  There is, of course, always youtube to get a solution, but if that's necessary to move forward in a game (vs. sidequests, optional items, etc.), then IMHO there is a big problem with the game design. Anyway, overall it's a very fun game.  FYI, I LOVE difficult games and would actually prefer to have three difficulties, 1. the original/highest difficulty 2. one that removes the wispy block things from the platforming but keeps the combat difficulty intact/difficult, and 3. one that both removes the block things and reduces combat difficulty for those that want and easier time with both.  Or, optimally just fix the very few spots that are so difficult that even seasoned gamers like myself can't make it through.  It's not like they're difficult to spot.Cheers,H

_childDocuments_.review: Can I recommend this game? Yes. But only for a very specific crowd of people. It's a game that is very fun, even if its flaws make it fall a little short of a masterpiece of the genre. So the good. If you like precision platforming, intense boss rights and quite satisfying movement mechanics, you'll get a kick out of this game. If you enjoy lots and lots of exploration, collections, backtracking and hunting things down in a metroidvania, you'll be happy with this. The game even lets you pay to see if you've missed anything in a zone, which is a huge boon for some of the more sprawling ones. The art is quite lovely, the sound design is solid and the game mostly runs quite well.The bad though. First of all, there's a lot of screen clutter. The art is nice, but the visual design is often lacking. In many areas you're zoomed out very far, there's a color filter on the screen and all the enemies are very similar colors, which makes everything into visual soup, and it's hard to know where you are at a glance. One magma themed area in particular struggled with this, everything was just a mass of red, even your character. This gets worse in boss fights, when the screen fills with lights and colors and particles, some of which matter and some don't, and it can be intensely troublesome to see what you're doing. There are a few glitches, some of which come up a lot, that lock you out of movement or give you weird animations. None of it gamebreaking, but certainly immersion breaking. None of this ruins the game, but it all adds up to helping it fall a little short of perfect for me. Overall though, if you like your metroidvanias with a very solid dose of precision platforming, go right ahead and indulge in this, and you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I bounced off this months ago but wanted to give it a last go to confirm my feelings which took some time. My feelings are what they are when I bounced off, even having completed a majority of the game and most likely being fairly close to the ending, I don't want to continue completing it, because it's not fun. There is no single thing with Aeterna Noctis that is absolute deal-breaker (but coming back to them the compounded issues really hits you) just constant tiny things and annoyances - controls not working right, inaccessible mechanics, boss (and sometimes platforming) difficulty being at least 50% due to obscuring particle effects (this may have been made better now, I'm not going to play to the next boss), controls not being as tight as they should, I can go on, but you get the point - lots of annoyances that compount.. Even after their so-called accessibility patch, there's still not any decent options for fixing this, which is just bad. Add to that that this is a very long game, but not really having content justifying it and much of what there is goes on for too long. I genuinely this would have been a better game had it been a shorter game - many of the issues would then not be as large due to the shorter time. I really can't recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game for those that appreciate extremely difficult games. If you dislike difficult games, ABSOLUTELY DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME!! But if you appreciate extremely well designed, difficult Metroidvania's, this is a must buy. The developers clearly adored Hollow Knight, which is awesome because so did I. The platforming is insanely difficult and very precise, but never really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ or unfair, aside from maybe one part at the end, depending on how you view it. The combat isn't necessarily complex, but it's more then good enough.  HOWEVER, the boss fights are another matter. They can be extremely frustrating and occasionally unfair, and usually leave me wanting to just skip them and play the rest of the game! But some of them are pretty good, it's just that the bad one's stand out. The game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GIGANTIC. It's bursting to the seams with content. An absolutely massive map chock full of stuff to do. Since this game is a metroidvania, there will places that you see that require an upgrade you don't yet have, so you're incentivized to explore previous places. The level design is great, there are a solid enough cast of enemies, and the direction is simply phenomenal. There was not a single point I didn't know where to go. Which is insanely impressive for these types of games. Even in Hollow Knight, there were a lot of times I was confused where to go. Never here. If you loved Hollow Knight, this game is a must play. It's well worth 30$. I likely would have payed 60 and still be happy with my purchase. The artstyle is gorgeous, which is an absolute Unicorn for Indie Devs. It's not pixelated, it just looks like amazingly drawn artwork at all times. The combat is nothing amazing but mechanically solid and satisfying, and the platforming is insanely difficult but so much fun. If you enjoyed the Path of Pain in Hollow Knight like me, this game is a godsend. I really, really hope that more content is added, because there's no where else that I know of where I can get platforming like this. It's like those extremely well designed mods for games like Dark Souls that are intended for veteran players, and can design with skill in mind, but an entire game.If you enjoy technical, precise, difficult platforming, this is the best game you will ever play. If you enjoy difficult games with an insanely high skill ceiling, buy this game right now. If you really loved Hollow Knight, buy this now. I have to say though, if this sounds enticing to you, and you're unfamiliar with precise 2D platforming, do not play this game as your entry point. Play Hollow Knight. For the love of god, do not play this as your entry point. Unless you are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ironman, you will hit a brick wall that will take a long, long time to scale. Even as a veteran platforming player, an early section (that everyone who has played it knows all too well) took me hours. If you've played Hollow Knight, but it's been a while, and you're rusty, I would advise picking this up. At the end of the day, it's an absolutely massive game that costs 30$. But go in knowing that this will not be easy.Overall, a very specialized game. But if it caters to you, this is a must buy. People who complain about it being "unfair" or "too hard" just simply aren't the target audience. It's not unfair, it presents an extremely difficult challenge and asks you to beat it. it's not 'artificial difficulty". The game throws you one of the best areas in the game, with an extremely hard parkour gauntlet, like 3 hours in. At no point in the gauntlet, is any specific part unfair, or artificially difficult. It asks a whole lot from you, but it makes you better at the same time. You master each individual obstacle until you can put it all together, And keep in mind, there are frequent checkpoints in the game. If you die, you usually lose like 2 minutes. So if, after all this, the game sounds appealing, I would strongly, strongly recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this is a weird one. Because actually, I thought this game was actually really great, in most ways.tl;DR: I will say, despite the rant below, I don't hate this game at all, I hate certain aspects of it that drag it down, and make the rest of the game worse for it. There's some great boss fights (brought down for me by the no-hit achievements for every one of them), great platforming sections (brought down by them being almost pointlessly long, and the game almost always making you manually backtrack the way you came in said overly long platforming sections), some great ideas with moving around and traversing quickly (brought down by terrible, convoluted controls that did not need to be twinstick aiming for 99% of the game). Pretty solid music and art and world building, lovely little cutscenes, and the story was fine. So yeah. It's impossible for me to recommend this game because it's a 20h game turned into a 50h slog because of the design decisions. You might still enjoy it though; I did.... half of the time.RANT FOLLOWS:Rarely have I played a game with so much potential, crippled by terrible design choices by the devs. The controls in this game are absolutely -terrible-. It's baffling how bad they are. You press a face button on your controller to fire arrows, holding it down, and then aim with the left stick. This is terrible. It'd still be terrible if it was right stick, though, you know why? Because there's literally not one shot you have to make with the arrows (to hit switches, and later, to teleport) IN THE ENTIRE GAME that requires twinstick aiming. The only exception is versus two of the bosses of the game, one is a secret optional fight, the other is the final boss. Now you might say, well, just rebind them. Oh, I assure you I did. But, it's worse. There are multiple arrow types, which you have to switch between, and one of those two arrow types itself has another sub-type (dark arrows), which is switched with yet another different button. And the teleport arrows, once you switch to them, require a FOURTH button to then teleport to the arrow while it is in mid-flight. This feels terrible from the moment you gain the ability. Here's an idea: have the teleport arrows simply be an upgrade to your regular arrows, removing the need to switch to them. Then, when you fire the arrow, merely pressing the arrow button again will teleport you. There. I just replaced FOUR separate buttons  with one button, the same button. What about the alternate dark arrows? Who cares. I literally never used them, because they're terrible. And if you really must have multiple arrows, then just have one button to fire, and one to switch arrows. Not four different buttons AND your left stick to mess around with arrows. Just stops the games momentum dead in its tracks, every time you use arrows. And, as for holding down the button to aim, that can go away too, and be replaced with 8-way aiming, like Contra or a million other games that work totally fine without twinstick aiming. I understand these were probably design decisions for variety and yada yada yada I don't care. It sucks. It sucks so bad, it made me just constantly cringe at how it tanked enjoyment of the game for me, and I'm not the only one, looking at other reviews and forum posts.And then there's the achievement design. This is a game with tough boss fights, with screen filling attacks, bullet hell waves of projectiles, super fast counters, etc. That's fine, I like challenge. What I do *not* like is BEATING EVERY BOSS NO HIT. Especially, when the boss design is pretty much designed to beat you absolutely bloody no matter how good you are dodging. I understand they're all possible to be beaten no-hit. I'm not saying it's not possible. But I am saying that YOU, or at least 99.99% of anyone reading this, will not no-hit them all. You'll see why if you play the game. Some of these fights are absurd to no-hit, with so many cheap attacks and multiple forms. Again, I *love* tough boss fights. But if your boss can be memorized to the point that you can no-hit it, that's actually boring and terrible boss design to me. It should be a struggle, it should be barely won. You know, like these fights. Except they still expect you to beat them flawlessly... wtf were they thinking??So, you might be thinking, ok, the bosses are messed up, the controls are messed up, but, isn't this game all about the platforming? Yeah, except, you can't platform nearly as well with an analog stick, and because of their awful, poorly thought out control scheme, you need to use the analog stick to move, since every button on the controller is already used. And besides, you need the left stick for aiming the arrows too. Oh look, another crippling game flaw that would've been neatly sidestepped with better controls, and 8-way aiming, removing the need for the god-awful left-stick aiming. Not only that, the platforming sections, which also should've been tons of fun, are made to be as excruciating as possible in every way.... with every long difficult section that ends in a dead end (with a power-up or switch or whatever) requiring you to then do the section backwards to get out of it. If you hit the spikes, 98% of the time you get respawned at the end of the dead-end, and have to get back out again the hard way. I think this would've been fine for some areas, particularly some optional challenges. But doing it basically every. Single. Time...... it's so obnoxious, it just feels like the devs don't respect the player's time, and just want to jack up the playtime as much as possible. All in the name of it being "ohhhhh so hardcore, we're the most hardcore difficult metroidvania!" I hate to break it to you guys, making obnoxious crap that's just poor design, and to waste people's time, doesn't make your game the most hardcore or difficult. It's neither the hardest bosses nor the hardest platforming I've ever played in a metroidvania, so get over yourselves.

_childDocuments_.review: When I just obtained the second ability (the dark claw) for the character, I’ve already felt too depressed to explore the whole game. I personally prefer employing the hit and run away tactic whenever I play a Metroidvania game but I no longer have fun adopting this in Aeterna Noctis.The main reason triggering me for abandoning this game is the dash mechanic. I can’t recall how many times I issue a hit command with an instant backward dash to make some distance, and it just turned out my character hits an enemy and then dashed into it. There might be occasions like 3 or 4 out of 10 that the character dashes toward the opposite direction while implementing a hit and run, and then ends up losing health points. Even though issuing a dash command won’t immediately cancel the attacking animation, I sometime smash the dash button hoping the character will make a dash move right after the ending of attacking animation. In those cases, the character still dashes into enemies from time to time. I also assumed that the dash command might linger longer than the backward move command do in the buffer, but it still produces the confusing effects, despite the backward move button has been held down the whole time. For clarification, I have tried both Xbox console and keyboard, but to no avail.I also don’t like the design that the character sways back and forth like an idiot whenever I make a minor move on the platform. It annoys more than you think when you’re about to make some platform timings and execution, considerings that the platform elements are hard enough in Noctis mode. Aeterna Noctis has every potential to be an outstanding Metroidvania in scale and people might take their time to practice and sharpen skills to adapt to this game. But as for me, I cannot always achieve the predictable result while playing it, and I was deeply demoralized to spend my time on it.----Edit on April 17th. I have created a post on Steam Discussion to address the dev's reponse.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the conclusion is that I recommend the game, but you really have to know what your stepping into.This is 90% a precision platformer. With one-hit-kill walls, floors, ceiling... or all the above. With pixel-thin margin of error at times. With second-long timing to master.All of these would be kind of ok if at the very least the arrow targeting was smooth and reliable. (Used to teleport later in the game... also everything requires it past a certain point.) It is not.So you'll experience much frustration going through many long passages of paper-thin-margin precision platforming. And not just a "one thin margin to get through and if you die you respawn just after". Noooo. It's often three, four or more of these to go through before you reach a temporary respawn point. (Where you get back as long as you have hit points left.) And if you actually die, you revive much further back.And just to top it all, that's not for optional segments, it's all the way through the main path of the game, starting from the Tower of Light.Now you know.Also, it's annoying to have to struggle through so much precision platforming when the intro scene shows you fighting while flying.Bosses, on the other hand, are tough but fair. You'll die several times learning the patterns before beating the boss.The art is on the average side, but with an interesting style.The mechanics are ok, but the arrow targeting is painful to use. (Would probably be ok if we could see the mouse cursor.)It's also very difficult to use both camera movement and targeting at the same time due to how it's handled by the same mouse movement and you can't move the invisible cursor past the border of the screen...The map system is pretty frustrating as you need to buy a cheap map from a trader in each region just to lift the fog of war. Until you get the map, the places you have been through are blurred and after you buy it, only these are revealed. This goes against most game standards where you can reveal the map yourself or buy a full map (often still lacking details, but more complete than just the places you visited). The frustrating part is that there is no way to know where the trader is until you randomly stumble upon him.The skill tree is a bit lacking. A few key abilities, but nothing feels really game-changing. Gems are what defines your build more decisively, but it takes a long time to collect them. Some are behind even tougher platforming sections than usual.The quest log lacks detail. It would be helpful to add a few lines more, particularly as dialogues are not repeatable.Finally, the game does include two things to help you find secrets: a completion screen with about every collectable listed, and a trader with a map of all secrets. (Expensive, and you need one map per region of the game.)All this rant, and I still recommend the game as it has interesting boss fights and story.There are many flaws in the core design, but I can overlook some of them.And you definitely have to deal with a ton of annoying platforming that doesn't even feel rewarding enough (in my opinion).I'm not sure I'll finish the game in the end. The difficulty of the pixel-thin second-long precision you need to reach just to get through the story quests is starting to get on my nerves at this point. (Got the 4th seal... interestingly enough, not the most difficult to reach.)Note: The devs have announced a more action-oriented mode. Might be worth a look. But right now, it's mostly platforming, with a sprinkle of action.Note2: Scratch the previous note. The "more action-oriented mode" seems to just make the platforming slightly easier with non-vanishing platforms or longer timers.

_childDocuments_.review: STORYRefreshingly, Aeterna eschews the trend of vague Dark Souls inspired lore in favour of a very direct, easily understood story. You play as the recently dethroned King of Darkness, locked in an endlessly repeating cycle of victories and defeats against the Queen of Light. You must now venture out on a quest to reclaim your lost powers and your throne. A simple premise but with enough going on to keep you interested. Written dialogue is decent enough but the characters are only voiced properly in the animated cutscenes. Characters in-game speak an invented gibberish language, similar to Hollow Knight, that somehow sounds like Spanish and Japanese mashed together. The Hollow Knight comparisons don’t end there… VISUALSThis will be a matter of taste but, imo, the visuals in this game are fantastic. The environments are works of highly detailed, hand drawn art with some awesome background work. The downside here is that the foregrounds, while adding depth to scenes, sometimes obscure the action causing frustration during the combat and challenging platforming sections. The animation is also generally very smooth although the main character has an exceptionally odd idle animation that plays whenever you stop moving. I believe he’s supposed to look limber and ready for action but it really looks like he’s doing a little dance; super goofy. Overall, it’s a very clean style that leads to pleasing, if not sometimes overly busy/outright distracting visuals.GAMEPLAY/MECHANICSAeterna is a Metroidvania to the core, though one that focuses heavily on precision platforming above all else. All the ingredients are here; a vast interconnected map full of ability-gated areas, required backtracking, secrets and NPCs to find. There are a few different weapons, several abilities and a ton of collectables including skill upgrades you can equip, very similar to Hollow Knight’s pin system. But how does it play?Well, that depends. When things are working as they should, Aeterna is an immensely enjoyable Metroidvania with the potential to run with the best of them. The general combat is fine, if sometimes a little basic (mostly bait, wait, attack, repeat), but the boss encounters are fantastic and quite challenging. It’s the platforming that makes or breaks this game though and, unfortunately, at the moment it breaks it. Aeterna feature some tough as nails precision platforming comparable to games like Super Meat Boy, The End is Nigh, Hollow Knights White Palace area and the Ori Series (which is far easier than Aeterna). The problem is that the game mechanics currently aren’t responsive enough to support this kind of brutal game design. You will die many times due to your own mistakes but you will die just as often to unresponsive controls (eg. lost jumping/dashing inputs). It’s doable but with a lot of frustration. I read the devs are working on an easier mode; that’s great since many players will not be able to deal with the base game challenge. For those of us who want to play original intended experience the controls are the most important element the devs must address. This game demands tight controls and the current situation is literally killing the games potential. The developers recommended solution to use full-screen and turn off V-Sync to mitigate the issues made no difference for me.A couple of other things to mention. The game uses the, now ubiquitous, mechanic of having you retrieve something upon death however, it seems rather pointless here. It doesn’t affect your money, it only affects your experience and blood orbs which are used to heal in an almost identical way to Hollow Knight’s soul orbs. Even if you die on this corpse run you will not lose anything, you just have to get back to them at some point. In the unlikely event that you can’t, you can pay a guy a large sum to retrieve them. Speaking of money, the economy in Aeterna seems especially stingy, I wondering how I’m ever going to afford all the stuff on sale; maybe there’s a windfall coming later?? The game also has a skill tree where you can upgrade your stats and abilities. Sadly, it’s not particularly exciting.In summary; when everything works as it should Aeterna is a really great and challenging game. "When" being the key word here.AUDIOThe audio is fine, and at least one track has stuck in my mind. I have to say though, this is another area where I felt that Hollow Knight vibe at times.DEMOGRAPHICFine for all except very young children. Nothing too scary or gory. Blasphemous this isn’t.PERFORMANCEI have a fairly decent machine so I expected Aeterna to run well, and it does. The game is very graphically intensive, I could imagine some lower spec machines having trouble but any mid-range PC will be fine.My SpecsRTX 3080i9-11900K64 GB RAMDIFFICULTYOk, so the developers have described the game as being very challenging and indeed it is. Platforming and bosses that starts tough and only escalates as you progress. I can see even seasoned Metroidvania fans giving up at early skill-checks (looking at you Tower of Light). It really depends on what you're looking for in the genre, if you want easier combat and exploration you might want to try something else or wait for the new easier mode the devs have planned. I personally love the base game difficulty, but only when it’s not screwing me over with the aforementioned control issues.BUGS & ISSUES- Unresponsive jump; this one is very repeatable and easy to demonstrate. Pressing jump and nothing happens, often leading to frustrating death. (v-sync/fullscreen makes no difference)- Unresponsive dash; I'm not talking about cool-down here but more about the direction of the dash. When attacking an enemy and trying to quickly dodge away, the directional input is completely lost, causing you to dash right into the enemy, either dying or losing health. Also easily repeatable.-  Not sure about this but enemy health is weird in this game. I enhanced my base attack an extra 30%, yet the enemies from the start of the game still took the same number of hits to kill, making the upgrades feel worthless. It was only after a 50% upgrade over base damage that I noticed a real difference. Is there some crappy scaling going on here? Also the same early enemies have clearly buffed health the further you progress in the game but without any reason or indication, no different colours or attacks, they just have more health because...???. There are clear enemy variants that do have different colours but I’m not referring to these.- Foreground obscuring the action. Not sure how to solve this but it’s a clear issue in a game that demands such precision.GRINDNo required grind but skill points start to come at a snail’s pace as you progress. If you want to earn certain skills before you take on a particular boss, you might need to do a bit of exp grinding.DURATIONHUGE game, at least 25-30 hours.PRICEThis game offers a LOT of content for the money.OVERALLThere’s been some awesome Metroidvanias this year; Astalon, F.I.S.T, Ender Lillies, Metroid Dread to name a few of the best. Right now, Aeterna sits below all of them, imo, simply because its controls don’t support the demands on the player, leading to much frustration. If they fix the issues? It could be the best Metroidvania this year. I originally gave this game a thumbs down but I can’t in good conscience keep it that way since I’ve been playing and enjoying the game and will continue to play it.EDIT: The devs have done an awesome job in the last months fixing nearly all of the key criticisms of the game, including control responsiveness and a new game mode for those who don't want the intense difficulty of the original. Top tier metroidvania.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I normally love Metroidvanias, but I just couldn't get into this one. Nothing about it was , but it overall felt very dull and janky, and I felt no motivation to explore the world. The starting environments are so dark and muddy I could barely see anything; I'm told later environments are more colorful, but that doesn't do anything to help first impressions. The writing is also very clunky and amateurish, with several typos, punctuation errors, and awkward lines. I would have preferred a silent protagonist over the King's need to whine about everything constantly. (It's also very awkward when the protagonist is an old hand but the player, obviously, doesn't know anything. Every tutorial is constantly getting interrupted by the King insisting he totally knows how to do this and how dare the tutorial NPC teach me how to play the game, which just makes the tutorials hard to follow and highlights how nonsensical they are diegetically.)Additionally, I'm not a fan of how platforming-heavy the gameplay is, even on the platforming-lite difficulty mode. This is exacerbated by the jump feeling extremely heavy -- you need to hold down the jump button for the maximum time to get any appreciable height, which kept tripping me up because that's different from most platformers' physics. I found it very difficult to accurately gauge my jump distance and whether I could reach a given platform.Lastly, this is minor, but something about the art style just feels off to me. I think it's that there's almost no shading on character sprites. It makes everyone look weirdly flat, especially when the environments are so shadowed, in contrast. I also  dislike the distortion effect around the player character in the black-and-white trial rooms, as it makes it even harder to accurately judge distances.

_childDocuments_.review: Editing review to negative.The movement/platforming mechanics in this game are absolute trash.I ran into what it looks to be one of those Ori and the Blind Forest style endless climbing levels and I died so many times because of abysmal controls; game not registering my inputs; game registering my inputs incorrectly; horrible level design that if you do not do the action perfectly, you will die; the level just going on endlessly with no progress in plot or anything interesting. First 2 hours impressions (+ 4 hour negative remarks using EDIT):- Harder than Hollow Knight, but not as hard as Blasphemous. EDIT: Harder than anything I played because how bad the controls are.- Definitely a metroidvania.- Some movement/platforming mechanics can get annoying (ledges generally push you off instead of allowing to make a jump). EDIT: Jumping wall to wall feels "slippery" and easy to mess it up. Dashing also feels "slippery". All the movement abilities I acquired are poorly implemented.- Platforming challenges are designed to be unforgiving. You character is tall and there is little room to maneuver. EDIT: Combined with horrible controls, these can create showstopper results even in some main quest areas.- Can pogo on enemies. Cannot pogo on spikes.- Confusing story and easy to miss out on key messages. Quest log exists, but not very useful.- Secret challenge areas that feel challenging (platforming challenges, combat challenges etc.)- Great soundtrack, amazing background design/art. EDIT: Foreground art is annoying, it gets in the way too often and there is no transparency effect to be able to see yourself, checkpoints, loot or enemies behind the art.- Massive world, I got lost a few times already. -  I do not recommend this game anymore. Once you play it 3-4  hours, it gets dull and poor movement controls will make your life living hell.I won't refund the game though. There is an easier game mode that reduces platforming difficulty or something coming, so will wait for that and check the game out later.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite difficult (started on the difficulty of Noctis), from the very beginning the player is introduced to the basic mechanics, after which the complexity begins to increase quite noticeably. The visual style is very nice, everything looks really nice, chic musical accompaniment. I also liked the presentation of the game mechanics through the story and the interaction of secondary characters with the player, and not just tooltips. Platforming is moderately difficult, boss fights require certain approaches. All in all a great platformer that can challenge you on the Noctis difficulty level (there is also an easier difficulty level). Definitely recommend to buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, this is a great game. Have you ever played classic Metroid games, Castlevania, Super Meat Boy?? They are all difficult in their own way. This is a blend of it all. Sure some people say the controls are tricky..... but let's be real, not everyone is always gonna be in tune with the controls of a game when they start (professionals don't complain). Everyone wants a game to be straight forward right off the bat with no mystery or wonder. Give it a chance and keep trying. I've failed miserably on so many portions of this game but I NEVER gave up. I Still haven't gotten used to it but I'm getting better.I didn't want to play another Metroidvania game that was straight forward and the platforming gave you room for error. IN FACT...... this game, more often than not, gives you little to no room for error and that's what makes games like these fun. Blasphemous was super challenging in terms of the platforming and combat but I can't say the same for Death's Gambit. Hollow Knight's end game platforming was challenging but I can't say it was in the first half and the combat was always fun, amazing game to say the least. As an added note, and I think an IMPORTANT NOTE at that, I noticed that sometimes the game is actually forcing you to sacrifice HP to achieve an objective. I've had a couple run ins with this and this meant I needed to be good enough to get to the point where I had enough HP to proceed with the sacrifice portion (I very well could be wrong about this and might be missing something, maybe an upgrade that would have made it easier but I still managed). As for the rest of the game:1) Challenging bosses2) Beautiful art3) Lovely music4) Story is great 5) Occasional arrow markers you'll find telling you where to go (I did get lost early game but I like exploring every nook and cranny to see what is in my reach before moving on).6) Map is very well thought out7) GIT GUD and enjoy the challenge.1,000% would recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily the most beautiful metroidvania I've ever played. I am really enjoying the challenge and the varied environments. I wish the controllers were a little tighter since the platforming is so precise but once you get used to it it's not too bad. Also a few grammatical errors but those can easily be fixed later.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion, one of the best platform games with a story. Excellent translation with minimal bugs, and the controller support is nice as well.At first glance, the battles seem simple, but it all pays off with a huge selection of weapons. At the same time, the hero has many abilities and skills that are easy enough to unlock. Some abilities are hidden in tombs that you have to look for the keys to.The boss battles are interesting, but in the second half of the game they are getting stronger, and this makes you think twice.I also want to praise the graphics, yes it is simple, but how pleasant it is to look at the picture during the game. Unobtrusive music helps to immerse yourself in the game, but only poorly remembered.The game is definitely worth its money, so fans of the genre will be delighted. If the developers had had a sufficient budget, the game could have garnered one of the nominations, but alas. I hope this project will continue to be supported and developed by the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: As stated in several reviews, the game might be fine if you're willing to put up with unresponsive controls and lost inputs and the insane tedium that the platforming is. Half of the enemies run at you to explode, explode when hit or explode AND scatter projectiles when hit, the other half zone you and you're standing there waiting until their animation is over until you get a hit in. Hitting enemies is pushing YOU away for whatever reason, which is a mental design choice in a game that revolves around getting on a platform.Several zones so far are absolute cancer, with as someone said Super Meat Boy segments all over that have nothing to offer once you clear them, mixed with before mentioned suicide bomb enemies and enemies gating platforms, not to mention pitfalls, spikes and whatever floor/wall hazards there are. To make it worse the game "allows" you to go to areas you can explore more than half of, only to realize you don't have the ability to finish them.The first "real" boss is literally a full blown SMB climbing segment, stretched out to oblivion. The visual clutter on the screen does not help at all and navigating though a diarrhea of particles and foreground obstacles can get insane.All in all the game is draining and the demo does not represent what the game revolves around and might be misleading in a way, giving off the impression that this could be a solid Castlevania homage. Give it a go if you feel like it, however I believe there are better ways to waste your time.

When you play more than half of the game you may think I will finish it but don’t exactly believe that cause you will face a new challenging mechanic and something like up side down and gravity pattern that may end up your journey because you cannot pass through.But trust me this game is come from the real gamer cause the patforming and game play is beatifully crafted and doable you just need to keep dying again and again until you passHope you guy support this game this is a real challenging metroidvania

_childDocuments_.review: Update. December 2023This game has had enough updates to make it playable in my opinion. I understand a difficult game I have completed numerous games up to and including 100%ing them. Games such as hollow knight, cup head, Celeste, numerous castlevania games, etc. This is my genre, this is my bread and butter. Honestly the game is probably a solid 6/10 it is clear a lot of thought and care has gone into this game. Now that I've put some time in to it my biggest complaint outside of controls is this game is a mess. It's like they had a great core idea but just kept tacking things on to it. I'd be okay if this game was renamed feature creep. The controls and movement for this game leave a lot to be desired... I've played on pc and on steam deck. The game still suffers from the same fatal flaw. The movement just feels stiff and off. Nowhere near as bad as it was previously. But still far from great. The game in and of itself is good albeit flawed in a fundamental way.This is a 2d action platformer. But it is failing in one of those words.The platforming aspect of this game is it's biggest draw back, the movement is clunky and unreliable at the best of times. I actually appreciate the aspect of having to time how long you hold the dash.Jumping: the height of the jump and the rate at which you rise both just aren't right. This is the main part of platforming and it's just wrong.  I've died countless times due to the movement just not behaving as you would expect it to.If this got adjusted to be a bit more intuitive this game would be amazing. I really love 2d action platforming games, they are primarily what I play, and I really would like to love this game.The combat so far has been decent if somewhat uninspired, but that's okay this is a 2d game there is literally only so much you can do with combat in 2d.

_childDocuments_.review: For those concerned whether $30 price tag is merited, it is. I was skeptical at first due to games in the metroidvania genre typically being cheaper, but the vast amount of content and uniquely challenging gameplay exceeded my expectations. Character ability customization is relatively in-depth with impactful character progression. You can expect to put in well over 40 hours in Noctis mode (base difficulty) if you backtrack and are somewhat a completionist. The sheer number of collectibles cannot be overstated. The combat (excluding bosses) gets easier as the game progresses with the introduction of more customizables and better healing whereas the platforming gets significantly more difficult. Most platforming is manageable at mid to late game, but some are genuinely difficult. This is especially true for various collectibles gated by platforming. The vast majority of negative reviews are related to difficulty, specifically platforming and controls. The developers chose to introduce Aeterna mode (easy difficulty) to accommodate. Overall, the game is excellent and highly recommended.
