_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I didn't realize how good it was until I played a few more metroidvanias and realized that I was missing the movement abilities and platforming challenges from Aeterna Noctis.There were many points at which I got to a platforming section, took one look, and said "this is literally impossible." And then half an hour later (not including a few rage quits) I managed to do it and felt like a god. A lot of platforming sections remind me of things I'm used to seeing in fan-made mods, like "Hollow Knight but the whole world is Path of Pain", or Kaizo levels in Mario.Part of the genius is the teleport arrows that you acquire about.... halfway through the game, I think? After this point, all the platforming involves perfectly timing your teleport arrows, wall jumps, double jumps, and air dodges. And I loved it.Will you love it? Depends. I'd compare the difficulty to Hollow Knight's Path of Pain, or Celeste. If you've played these games and loved them, I think you'll have a good time. If you haven't, I'd recommend starting with either of them.On the subject of originality: I've seen some people say it's a ripoff of Hollow Knight or other games. And certainly, there are elements that are *very* reminiscent of other games; I remember entering the cave levels fro the first time and having a moment of Deja Vu, because they looked so similar to Crystal Peak from Hollow Knight.But I can forgive it, because the execution is so good, and there's enough originality in other regards. Specifically, there are two things that surprised me. I'll spoiler them. First, when exploring the underground area, you stumble across an , and then go to the bottom of the ocean and fight through the . Gameplay-wise, that plot twist doesn't have much of an impact, but it's still a fun departure from the typical fantasy story these kinds of games tend to have.But something even more surprising and impressive, that did have an impact on the gameplay and opened up whole-new frontiers in platforming, was when you go to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  and the game turns into 2D . Is this game perfect? No, there's a few rough edges here and there, and the translation to English isn't stellar. Nevertheless, it's a fantastic game that does enough original things to be worth playing. Indeed, it does enough things well that I hope other developers take inspiration from it.

_childDocuments_.review: Will review again after completing but wanted to give my positive review since I can't understand why people give the game a bad review for having EAC. I don't mind them having it because I came to play a game not to cheat on it wtf it totally beats the point of playing the game if I'm gonna be using cheats to complete it lol. The game is really good, the platforming is difficult but rewarding and the combat has been fun and engaging for the time being. The map is gigantic but you have multiple methods for traversal and the platforming sections is where the game shines the most in my point of view. I'm playing in the Noctis difficulty (though you can change at any time in the pause menu) and it feels much more fun since it takes the best of me to succeed in some of the parkour challenges. If you enjoy platforming, big maps, lots of upgrades and an interesting story with good characters this game might be the next Metroidvania you should be playing n.n

_childDocuments_.review: My quest for the great metroidvania experience hit yet another bump with Aeterna Noctis. It seems that no matter how many things devs do right, they inevitably sc** a few things up beyond belief.Aeterna Noctis has a great story, a great atmosphere and surprisingly good platforming mechanics, and even the checkpointing system is reasonable. The great atmosphere turns unbearably depressing after 15-20 minutes - switching off the music helps. The same great atmosphere is supported by great visuals, which are rather poorly implemented technically - the amount of loading the game does between the usually small scenes is shocking, and whenever there are serious particle effects on the screen there are huge drops in the framerate. At the same time, the awesomely multilayered goblin caverns run without a hiccup...The map shenanigans are hardly even worth mentioning - the game has a very capable automapping feature, and true to the genre, it drops many come-back-later locations. It even provides mapping pins to mark these - but you have to buy these gradually, and any given moment I'd need around 3x as much as available. Why????What really did me in in this game were the bosses. Not the difficulty, although the sword boss fight felt interminable - it was the audiovisuals, which is something new. There's the graveyard boss, that goes bwoaaaaaa like every 3 seconds - after 3-4 minutes it was incredibly painful. And then the phoenix boss, which looks absolutely amazing, but is so heavy on the bright colours that I had to quit after 15 mins of trying, and I couldn't see properly for some further 10-15 mins afterwards. I wonder how this stuff got through testing... (sigh)Update: I found a way to get through the phoenix without getting my eyes burned out. For a while, the game was excellent, then starting with the Dream Kingdom, it went downhill again. Some of the locations are beautiful, but they are oh-so-empty, and some quests seem to be deliberately aimed at wasting the players' time. Prime example is the Celestial Dragon, but there are also others. There's a lot of fun to be had with the game, and there's a lot of frustration, not due to difficulty. Still no thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Caught up in an ever re-birthing fight across the ages, you take control of the king of darkness in his adventure to overcome the light, which the game allows us to very rapidly get into without much hesitation. As you hit boots to ground you are quickly surrounded by a world that looks to be in shambles, but a world that is beautifully designed and hand drawn/animated. The visuals in Aeterna Noctis are a real treat to experience. From the special effects, to the smooth animations, there is so much here to appreciate. This world, although grim, is very beautiful. Artists who designed this world also used some very crafty imagery to create a real sense of 3d space despite this game being 2d. To accompany the visuals, the sound effects and music really do go nicely with the world as well. From character voice acting to the sound of cracking lightening, this world really feels alive.Aeterna Noctis is a game styled heavily after the metroidvania genre with a great dose of difficulty to supplement the flow of battle and a nice set of RPG elements as well. You will gain experience, levels and skill points as you kill enemies. Your gained points allow you to invest in a few branching trees that have things such as weapon damage increases, critical chance increases, critical damage increases and dash refresh rate increases making the enemies even more exciting to slay for that next level.The leveling system is not all Aeterna Noctis has to offer in terms of appeal for evolving combat as the game progresses, however. Engagement is kept refreshing as you move forward by the slow trickle of combat modifying elements that you encounter be it enemy tactics, new skills or ever changing world elements from the level design that create new challenges to overcome.Metroidvania style games typically are heavily focused on combat, and Aeterna Noctis follows suit here, but with something done a little different. This title also brings dangerous platforming to the table, which is dashed nicely throughout breaking up the reliance of combat. At times, you will find that your largest enemy is your ability to puzzle solve a tricky platforming section, which really does force you to think due to the crafty use of hazards and platforms. As one would expect, you will also encounter bosses, which I do say was a very refreshing experience in Aeterna Noctis. Unlike many games I played in recent times, there is some real challenge here that went beyond discovering a simple gimmick that crippled the foe, but instead relied heavily on my ability to judge when to attack and how to maneuver myself around the battlefield to victory. I feel that this game is a fantastic addition to anyone’s library, who really appreciates this kind of game. The player will be able to really feel the love that went into this title and enjoy every aspect of the adventure. This title is one I am glad I got to experience and has definite put this developer on my radar to keep my eye on.

_childDocuments_.review: $30 graphics with $5 controls.I really, really wanted to like this game, but the more I play it, the more I realize that the ONLY challenge you face in the game is the fight against the controls. The level designs don't even look particularly challenging, you know, typical drop, dash, drop, dash, slide, dash, jump, dash, etc. If Celeste was a playable character, I imagine I would have been disappointed in the lack of challenge, quite frankly. _childDocuments_.review: Because of some design decisions I cannot really recommend this game. Often it feels not like I'm fighting the enemies or evironments in the game, but more the game and controls themselves. QoL and movement features on highly restricted slots is a terrible decision. You decide if you want your movement to feel fun or if you want to be effective in combat. (no changing except on actual save points)The interact button on the same button as an attack. I cannot count the number of times I have accidentally read a terminal or activated doors or whatever mid fight because the enemy moved near the interactable. The aiming stick being the same as the movement stick. So many accidental moves or misaims.Also, you move while aiming. So if you want to aim right you move right, too. You can stop that by pressing yet another button, the interact and attack button, even more accidental misspresses.Not recommending this game was hard for me. I really liked the aesthetics, the general feel and the metroidvania aspects. But too often was I frustrated by the controls and other design decisions that it felt more frustrating than enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: You might be like me, you played Donkey Kong as a kid, you played Metroid, you played every Mario and every Megaman game. You've smashed Hollow Knight and Ori. You're a 2D platformer master with fast reactions and decades of experience.This game is absolutely kicking my ass.It's nearly made me want to give up quite a few times, and just when you mastered one challenge, the next one is even more difficult. The developer is borderline sadistic, they know exactly what they're asking of you, and they ease you into each challenge then bend you over and mess you up proper.This is a hardcore game. The single hardest 2D platformer I have ever played.It's also quite beautiful and well polished. It's not perfect by any means, sometimes the artstyle is a little TOO much form over function for my taste (hard to see platforms, enemies, projectiles, etc at times) - but I've also just chalked that up to the difficulty.You will die A LOT. But in it's current state, warp points and checkpoints are both plentiful, and there's no "game over" that sends you back more than a minute's worth of gameplay. You just have to take a deep breath, think about what the game is asking of you, then execute it. Or die trying.NEVER BEFORE HAVE I HAD TO PRESS ALL 4 FACE BUTTONS AND ALL 4 SHOULDER BUTTONS IN DIFFERENT ORDERS WITH FRAME PERFECT ACCURACY and I love it.There are a lot of nods to both Hollow Knight and Ori in this game, even Megaman X/Zero vibes at times.Not for everyone, probably not for most. I live and breath 2D platformers and I'm getting absolutely destroyed.Here's to hoping I can make it to the end. Stuck on a boss fight as we speak that feels insurmountable!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Your enjoyment with Aeterna Noctis will be determined whether you like or dislike platforming sequences. Because they are omnipresent, and they are hard, which combined with floaty controls and not the best hitboxes, can cause frustration. If you get used to the controls and you don't mind challenging platforming, then you're gonna have a blast. The metroidvania aspects of this game are done really well, with each of the abilities (at least those that I found 10 hours into the game so far) don't serve only as opportunistic gimmick to let you progress, but also have their purpose in the normal gameplay. The platforming is very well designed and creative for the most parts, unfortunately, almost every enemy type just feels intrusive and tedious to fight with, the combat with basic mobs isn't handled very well. What is handled well on the other hand, are the bossfights, which are like the platforming, well designed and creative and also pose some degree of challenge, although they are arguably easier than some of the platforming. Oh, and give the game a chance past the first area, that one does a really bad first impression. All in all a definite recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The TLDR here is Aeterna Noctis is a very VERY good game.If you are a fan of Hollow Knight then you'll love AN. Art style, music score, sound effects and even a few in-game mechanics are straight out of HK so you'll feel at home here.Where these 2 games differ significantly is where HK is a brutally difficult game which punishes you for failure, AN is just as difficult but death doesn't send you miles away as there is a well needed checkpoint system. AN does have a souls-like death mechanic but its easily negated with a simple one slot charm.Its a huge game with a massive map. I'm 40hrs in and around 75% complete so still got a little way to go.I do have a few gripes as follows but its great to see the devs reading the reviews and remedying some of the early teething issues.1. The map feels a little disjointed. At will likely be around 50+ hours, its huge but unlike games like HK or Ori, it lacks the interconnection with little more than a single entry point and single exit point for each area, sometimes even the same point out as in.2. Metroidvania gating could do with some work. Again, at 50+ hours of game time, it doesn't need to be 'padded out' but the vast majority of areas allow for 95% completion only to be thwarted in the last room where you find out you a are missing a key skill or ability. Personally, I would have preferred to have been stopped in my tracks a little sooner on my travels rather than have to back track though an entire area to resume my search.3. The arrow / celestial shot abilities are frustratingly difficult to master. If you've played either of the Ori games, think of Bash but here the left stick feels overly sensitive. You will eventually master it but you'll find aiming a constant challenge.4. When you eventually make it to a late game area called 'Cosmos' you'll have you're head in your hands with frustration. While its probably one of the most uniquely designed platformer levels I've ever see, when up is down, down is up, left is right and right is left you'll be screaming! Oh and then it will want you to complete a tricky platforming challenge as well.In summary, this is an incredible game and one of the best precision platformers out there. If you struggled with the Path of Pain in HK then give AN a bash. Its just as difficult (if not more so) BUT the check point system and lack of any punishment on death allows you to die > try > die > try > die > try x 100 and you'll eventually get it.Great work to the Devs - Will keeping an eye out for more from you guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Updated 08JAN2022Now we're talking!  Aeterna mode is made for the 99% of us.  This is a platforming Metroidvania we can all enjoy and my review is now updated to recommended.  I really do appreciate the devs updating this game to make it more accessible to the average player.  I was able to easily backtrack and continue the game.  While there are still challenges and work to do, it's very much less maddening and frustrating.In response to the dev comment that my review didn't make sense, i think you more have a marketing issue vs my and many others interpretation of your game.  Yes you describe it as a platformer and you use the word difficult.   But that really doesn't convey the sense of how extremely challenging this game will be to the average player if you play on Noctis mode. You made a game that could only appeal to the very top players.  There's nothing wrong with that but you certainly didn't work to advertise it that way.   This can be shown the easiest by playing the demo. (Was on the Epic store last i checked and i did play before purchasing.)  Your demo goes over the starting area and demos an average platformer that the average player has come to know and enjoy over the years.  If your demo has been a little more realistic of gameplay and shown how every step of the way was going to be one extremely challenging jump/arrow sequence after the other, perhaps the shock would have been less for us and the reviews would have been better for you.(1st update below)(Update 22DEC2021) Almost 40 hours in now and i must say, i'm done with this game and i CANNOT recommend that you buy it.   I'm was at a point that i was just playing to see it to the end, but i long stopped having any kind of fun.  The death by 1000 spikes is now complicated by one shot barriers that require you to shoot an arrow, teleport, shoot an arrow, teleport, jump, switch arrow types, shoot a target, switch arrow types, shoot an arrow, teleport and pray that you hit the platform.    If you do happen to make it, you're rewarded with the chance to do it all over again on the next puzzle.     I'm now at a point where i'm so deep in a dungeon that i can't make it past the incredibly hard to hit boss, and the thought of backtracking makes me want to cry.Don't buy this game.(Original review begins)I'm 22 hours in at this point, let's' give my thoughts so far.  Have you played Hollow Knight?  (If not, drop what you're doing, buy Hollow Knight, thank me later.)If you have played it, remember the White Palace?  (Google if you have not seen)  Imagine an ENTIRE GAME of the White Palace.   Complex mutli jump patterns over moving items that one shot you.   That can be fun at times but not every other room in the whole game!  (What we're you guys thinking with that light tower sword thing. holy crap!)   To be fair to the devs, sounds like they have heard this and are making a mode to tone that down some.  I may change my review later own depending on if that works out.The foreground is also very annoying.   It's fun to get the feeling that you're actually running through a room based on items moving in front of your character.  VERY BAD when it's moving through your vision as you're trying to jump the 1000 spikes or fighting mobs and bosses.  They always seem to be onscreen at the worst possible times.During the first level, there's some scenes and a level that look terrible. (light boxes that look very out of place.)   It's like the dev's got lazy, or maybe they were just trying to relay an atmosphere that i just don't see.  Thankfully that's the only place so far and the other levels to date look great.Sometimes there's not enough distinction between background and mobs.  Trying to fight the Goblin King's mobs is tough as a lot of the projectiles and mobs blend in to the crowd.One good thing i like though is the ability to reset the skill tree whenever you're resting.  It's nice to be able to swap from gold farming, to ranged, to melee increases depending on what you're doing at the moment.Overall this game has potential but as it is right now, be prepared to be frustrated and annoyed a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is very subject to change, as I am only 13 hours in, but 13 hours is long enough to beat a lot of the metroidvanias out there, so my first criticism/warning is that this game is too long. A lot of that time could be chalked up to dying - I've already died 1000 times since I started. Most of those deaths are cheesy environmental deaths, with the rest being boss deaths. In short, the game is probably over-tuned. I've played a lot of MVs. It's one of my favorite genres. I never thought any other MV was too hard - Hollow Night, Metroid Dread, Vigil, you name it I've probably put hands on it. This one is frustratingly hard, and the progress does not feel good as it does with something like Elden Ring or Dark Souls. There is triumph in surpassing challenge in some games, but I'm not feeling it with this one. That said, there is something pulling me along. The difficulty is an obstacle to what is otherwise an enjoyable game. It feels good, hearkens back to Symphony of the Night in very obvious ways, and is very pretty. I like the environments, I'm even a little drawn in by the story, despite its mess of bad grammar and dialogue. If the game were easier, and I don't mean easy, but easier, I would be very much recommending it already. As it stands, I'm doubting I have the sheer mental grit to keep bashing my head against a game that seems specifically designed to make me angry. I wish they wouldn't have tried to force so much challenge in here because I think they could have had something really special.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: It's not without issues and I wanted to wait until I was finished instead of only about 60% done but there aren't too many reviews and I wanted to quickly say and support the game; It's honestly probably the best looking Metroidvania I've seen and it's one of the longer ones too. Challenging and frustrating but those are what these games seem to kind of like :P Progress is rewarded with increasingly cooler areas (for the most part), there's plenty of ways to go, lots of secrets (though not really of the false wall or breakable section types) the abilities you get throughout are interesting and cool, plus you'll have to adjust use as you get further.All in all it's wonderful and very hard to put down, I'm so looking forward to Aeterna Lucis (Which I don't think is too far away now ^_^)  Great work on this game Devs, it's beautiful and runs great even on my bad computer; plus there's a lot of game for your money which I find hard to say about most games that I play. Very sad it isn't more popular.Wanted to add since I'm ~80% complete now; It's very much more of a puzzle/platform type Metroidvania. I've played on Noctis Difficulty the whole time, never changing and have to say some of the more end game platform stuff just gets annoying instead of feeling tough. It's also not a game where you earn equipment and for the most part most abilities aren't fought for really or platformed for; typically you'll suffer most for not much more than a skill point. To me it makes more sense for the super tough sections to have something like a nice weapon, though this is more like Soul Reaver than Castlevania, in ways.

_childDocuments_.review: The elevator pitch is "Celeste the metroidvania". A very pretty metroidvania with a heavy emphasis on precision platforming (on Noctis difficulty) and awesome boss fights. It is also very long for a MV, with an extremely large map, taking me 43 hours to 100%, and could easily take longer depending on your platforming skill. If that sounds like your cup of tea, then you will probably love this game (and if it doesn't, Aeterna mode heavily tones down the platforming, although the platforming is one really makes it incredible for me). One of my all-time favourite metroidvania games, and I eagerly look forward to the sequel next year.

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is an excellent Metroidvania that offers a huge world to explore featuring demanding precision platforming and brutally difficult bosses.I want to emphasize again that this game is difficult. There are several aerial-based mechanics that you must master in order to simply traverse compromising terrain. Double jumps, air dashes, teleportation arrows, environment-altering switches, and down-attacks must be used very precisely (often combinations of several of these) as being off by a fraction of a second can lead to hitting a spike and having to start the sequences again. There are areas in this game that would make Celeste blush.The areas are also HUGE. You'll enter an area thinking you're exploring a building but it ends up that's just a hub area that branches out into several large sub-areas with their own goals and challenges. They are fun to explore, though, with a good amount of secrets to discover. There are tons of collectables for completionists, including treasure chests, skill points (used to boost attack power, health regeneration or arrow power), gems (that grant buffs or abilities), dark material (used to "unlock" purple gems), musical scores (to be played on the church piano), keys that unlock a series of platforming challenges, Lion crests that unlock another series of platforming challenges, and mirror shards (which give you rewards for collecting specific amounts). There's a bestiary to complete and loads of side-missions to work on as you progress. It took me 60 hours for one playthrough (in Noctis mode, the equivalent of "hard", because most of the achievements require playing in that difficulty), and I completely abandoned the "breaches in the matrix" series of yet more platforming challenges. There's a lot of content here, basically.And while the controls are tight and responsive, they're also often extremely demanding and things like aiming your arrow seem excessively finicky. There are MANY points in the game where you have to slide down a wall, then air-dash underneath that wall to progress, but you're given a very narrow space to fit in, under which are spikes. My anxiety goes up every time I see one of these areas. You'll notice early on that even most of the small fry enemies can't be approached haphazardly and need at least a little strategy. Many are an outright pain. As previously mentioned, the bosses are also very demanding, and you generally can't just brute-force your way through them. You have to make quick and regular use of your teleport-arrows to dodge damaging attacks and it took me a while to train my brain into being able to do so intuitively.Which brings me to something I really enjoyed: The gem system. As you progress you build a library of blue, purple and red gems, and you slowly unlock slots you can use them in. While I originally didn't give this much thought and spent large stretches of the game using the same loadout, my frustration with some of the bosses had me experimenting with different loadouts until I discovered one that worked well against that boss. For instance, one particularly obnoxious boss with difficult-to-avoid attacks had me depend on a gem that severely limits the duration of my shield in exchange for a much shorter cooldown and another gem that makes me invincible during a dash. This allowed me to establish a rhythm that kept me centered and required a lot less teleporting all over the place. I won't spoil what loadout I used for the final boss, but I followed a hunch and ended up beating her on my first try.I should also note that some of the missions are not at all clear about how to resolve them (I wasted a lot of time trying to hunt down a Celestial Dragon until I learned from a friend . There's another puzzle in a room with four bells where . Oh, and that temple with the bell room? I HATED that level, as it is entirely based around invisible environmental elements, visible elements that aren't actually there, and room exits that warp you to unintuitive other rooms. There's a point in that level where you need to . I can understand why one might want to figure all that out on their own (which is why I put it in spoilers), but the game doesn't give you any hints so don't be surprised if you waste a lot of time. I sure did.While I did mention several things that annoyed me about Aeterna Noctis (and there were points I was VERY annoyed), it's still a joy to play. The world is very well-designed and often visually stunning. I haven't even mentioned the music, which is spectacular (especially near the end). While it's very difficult, it's also very satisfying in the way only difficult games can be. Despite some opaque tasks, there are some quality-of-life additions (like being able to buy expensive maps that will point out items you haven't collected yet) that I appreciated. I wasn't a big fan of the story (which I found too ambitious and difficult to follow), but the game won me over mechanically if not narratively. Highly recommended if you like difficult Metroidvanias (like Hollow Knight).

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis could be a really good game if it didn't annoy the player so much all the time. The fact that the game is a rather strong Hollow Knight clone can be easily overlooked. It's better to steal well than to invent badly, and some regions are quite strongly inspired. Some special HK mechanics were also copied 1:1. But if the game were really well thought out, it would actually be a perfect mix. At the beginning, Aeterna is also a lot of fun. But with increasing playing time, the areas and challenges only become annoying. The level of difficulty is so absurd in many places that the player is only annoyed. In Souls-like, there is often this feeling of having accomplished something and being proud of oneself. In AE, you struggle through a section, rarely get a reward for it and usually end up in the next annoying section. The longer the game goes on, the more intense this spiral of annoyance becomes, and with the teleport arrow at the latest, the game tips over massively because the function was poorly implemented. Aeterna is not a bad game, but rather one you would rate around 60%. Nice try, but there are so many better games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it was more frustrating than fun. Basically, it is trying to be a harder version of Hollow Knight by taking away some of the typical mechanics or locking them behind ability points. One mechanic that almost every game gives you is the ability to dodge through your enemies without taking damage, yet Aeterna takes every opportunity it can in order to remove health from your character, including no real invincibility after being hit. And that's on "Normal" mode. I put it in quotes because the difficulty seems to be a little askew from the typical normal difficulty in these type of games. The "puzzles" are more of putting the item in the back of the area with so few platforms and tons of death walls. And, even if you manage to get said item, some of the items like the Mirror pieces aren't truly collected until you've passed through the "puzzle" to get back out. I guess that's what makes it "fun" for some, but it kinda destroys the gameplay for me.

_childDocuments_.review: + No cap on max FPS, and the game doesn't freak out if you run it at really high FPS numbers+ Voice acting is good, though they speak "Aeternian", so you won't understand anything. According to a post by the devs, "phonetically it is a mixture of Japanese, Italian and Basque.". Cool stuff!+ You can switch difficulty at any time, without missing out on anything. Some achievements are disabled when playing on "Easy" mode, but that only applies to major things like boss fights+ Music and sound effects are well-made and on point+ The game map is gigantic, and exploration is actually fun. You can explore in a non-linear fashion+ Secondary weapons are actually pretty cool (and some are a bit edgy too)+ The game is full of references to other video games, songs, anime, books, movies and stories+ Interesting story that is more than just "light vs dark". Noctis is not evil for the sake of it, and takes morally good decisions depending on context. Worldbuilding is also neat+ All abilities you get are useful and relevant at all times+ All animations and cutscenes are high-quality. It's easy to tell that they're hand-drawn with genuine love and effort+/- A lot of collectibles. You can even play the piano in this game, and get to collect note pages to do so! +/- Art style is phenomenal! However, foreground objects can sometimes obscure things in some places. Really frustrating when that happens, and you get hit unfairly because you got distracted by the gigantic whatever that clouded your vision+/- Dodging has no iframes whatsoever, and there is no way to add any+/- Controls are serviceable, but may feel a bit finicky, especially during precise platforming. Sometimes you dash the wrong way or the game outright eats your input, but it wasn't common enough for me to write it off as a negative. Made me furious when it did happen, though+/- Combat is alright overall, but enemy variety (in terms of their abilities) is a little lacking +/- Combat feels passive, since the best strategy is to wait for the enemies to attack or move and exploit the openings+/- Questionable health system. It depends on the number of hits you can take instead of a numerical bar. The only relevant damage numbers are your own, and nothing has a visible HP bar, including bosses. You can tell how close to death an enemy is by checking the color of your damage numbers, but that sucks because it's impossible to tell how "dead" an enemy is before it's actually dead. Did it have to be this vague?+/- Death prevents EXP gain until you grab your "souls" or buy them back at a specific NPC. You can't permanently lose anything through dying, and death becomes irrelevant after you hit max level+/- There are tough achievements related to not getting hit during boss fights or doing some stuff in a speedruning manner (like finishing the game under 5 hours). You'll either have a field day with those achievements or have an absolute meltdown if you're a completionist+/- You can slot in a grand total of 6 crystals into your armor for interesting bonuses and mechanic changes. They add some variety+/- A healing resource is shared with some of your weapon abilities, and the other healing method is made of consumables that may drop randomly or bought at a vendor- You can't warp to your previous checkpoint without changing the difficulty or reloading your save. Come on...- Your level is capped at 20, and you have to find all skill points to get the most out of the skill tree. Even then, you can't max it out completely for some reason, as far as I'm aware- Character movement is really slow, especially when you're travelling across large and flat areas. I wish we could hold dash key to just sprint after around a second of holding. Spamming dash gets tiring really quickly, especially on a controller- Some accessibility options like fixed camera and reduced flashing lights are nonexistent. No colorblind filters available either- The wobbling animation that plays after you stop moving is pointless and usually lasts for far too long for its own good. I think I saw it last up to 5 entire seconds a few times, despite not pressing anything during the animation- Enemy contact damage. Makes sense, but only for some enemies. Cheap way to damage the player and make the game more "difficult"- Uneven difficulty (mainly in platforming). Coupled with questionable checkpoint frequency, it can get really infuriating- Pretty often, you're (practically) required to backtrack through an entire gauntlet you just went through to get back or go somewhere else- The "transition" spots between two map segments are NOT visually connected when you go through. While this can be useful to discern the borders of map segments, it looks outright ugly and partial- You can't use the DPAD to move, or even select things in most menus. LS is just not precise enough for some things, to add (like aiming arrows)- Some encounters might be hard for colorblind folks. I couldn't tell the falling feathers apart from the background in the Phoenix fight until I paid really close attention to what I was getting hit by- You move while aiming, since LS is also how you aim arrows. This can really mess you up during precise platforming and combat- No ledge grabs or any noticeable "ledge tolerance", so plunging into a spiky death because you missed a platform by a millimeter is a common occurrence- Doesn't seem like you can skip boss intros or other cutscenes. I spammed everything in a cutscene once to try it out and nothing worked. Not a personal problem, but a negative point nonetheless- There is no way to quickly restart a boss fight with full HP and full blood orbs. Changing difficulty or reloading won't restore anything, so you basically have to die every time you get hit if you're trying to do no-hit runs, and potentially AFK for a few minutes to fill your blood orbs (if you have the crystal for it equipped)- Bosses are vastly more frustrating and tedious than being challenging and fun, for the most part- Do we really need more than half a dozen different enemies, which some of them are the same archetype, to explode on death and spawn projectiles or a noxious cloud? How much area denial is too much?ENDER LILIES: Quietus of the KnightsSundered: Eldritch EditionOri and the Blind ForestOri and the Will of the WispsDust: An Elysian TailGRIME-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The world feels desolate, not only because there aren't many NPCs to interact with, but also because Noctis (somehow) has no followers or a cult dedicated to him. I mean, creating some robed figures that worship/support him, so the world doesn't feel absolutely empty would've been nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is from the perspective of playing on Noctis difficulty (I guess it was the intended difficulty level. The easy mode (Aeterna) was added later)I'm really on the fence about recommending a game like this. It really overstays its welcome. Platforming is about 75% of the focus and difficulty of the game, the other 25% is boss fights and mob enemies. The platforming was very hit or miss with satisfaction. To clarify: I love a challenge, the kind of challenge that comes with a sigh of relief and joy after completing a difficult task after failing repeatedly. This game has a mixed bag of that satisfaction. I found myself just saying "finally" and rolling my eyes after some of the bosses and platforming sections.In a way, it's definitely worth the price with how much of a game is in here (look at the playtime) but at the same time, it is just fatiguing. However, If you are a "hardcore" metroidvania enthusiast, this a MUST try if you enjoy threading a needle levels of precision combat and platforming. If you are on the fence, look up tower of light map (if you can find a picture of the ENTIRE tower), I think that's the first point in the game that a good portion of people will decide the game is for them or not. Another make or break it point is when the game introduces a teleporting arrow mechanic. It's very satisfying at times, but the learning curve is a little steep and it is required for the rest of the game. That's just the tip of the iceberg with this behemoth of a game. If you look into the Tower of Light and that looks appealing to you, you are in for a platforming treat and nightmare.I don't know where else to put this, but some boss fights area foregrounds get in the way of your view. Other times some attacks for a couple bosses moves would blend in with the colors of the back/foreground. Also, there is a free DLC gem that was added not far into the base game that adds a triple jump. If you don't want to spoil the game for yourself, NEVER use it. I am under the impression the original game was designed around only having a double jump, so it's like using a cheat code.Overall I'm kind of bummed I had to throw in the towel because of the time I sunk into the game and self imposed restrictions (no triple jump or Aeterna mode). I can't bring myself to lower the difficulty to easy mode (Aeterna) just to get through it. I only stopped because I got stuck on a boss so far into the game and got too fatigued after 60 hours of C&B torture. I came to this realization as I was looking at a video guide for this one item to make one specific part of the boss fight I was stuck on slightly easier. Knowing I had to backtrack to the one of the the most frustrating parts of the game just to get it is where I closed out of the youtube video and called it good.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best and most infuriating metroidvanias I've ever played.Pros :- excellent (I mean excellent, on par with Ori and HK) platforming.- tight and precise controls- movement may feel hard at first, I strongly encourage you to get the double jump and dash asap.- HUGE world map and tons of content- frequent checkpoints, including before bosses- you can tackle the map pretty much from where you want, meaning you may miss sometimes important upgrades.Cons :- some head scratching design choices that feel tacked upon without much prior thought because they worked in other MVs :- corpse runs for... no reason other than having a corpse run- cluttered screen and enemy animations making some bosses unfairly hard (some bullet hell stages, urgh)- no smart implementation of collectibles : ie, when you go to collect, say, an important gem or skill, you have to do ALL the way back 99% of the times, even if you spent 50 tries on it. Portal backs are few and far between. It's my major gripe with the game, because really anything can kill you and it feels a bit like being stuck against the f**** undead archers in the swamp in the old Dark Souls.- on that note, being able to roam freely the map, you can start a level, go half up there and realize you dont have the right upgrade to keep through. _childDocuments_.review: Ok, so Steam has stolen about 12 hours of total gameplay from my stats: I'm at 30% and this is my GOTY. I can see from videos that some elements have changed with each version release, but this is an outstanding game. Gorgeous. Music is thrilling (especially the forge and the Phoenix theme). I love everything about it--I grew up on Strider, Bionic Commando, the original Castlevania, Castlevania II, Zelda II: A Link to the Past and Metroid. I fell in love with RPGS as a young woman, but now in my 40s I have explored this amalgam genre of Metroidvania and this game. THIS GAME. Yes I get frustrated, yes I get delirious with joy when I beat a hard boss or a tricky setting. I got nothing to prove, boys, and achievements are secondary to the sheer pleasure of timing, fighting, and exploring. You can't make a jump? Die 1000 times. Equip the gem that ends the corpse runs. Turn down the difficulty. I can't wait to see where the story goes. So what they stole from Hollow Knight? Theft is flattery. I will play everything this studio makes, because this is a 5 gig ONLY labor of true love. Respect.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Do you think Hollow Knight was too easy? Did you quickly get bored of "impossible" Mario Maker levels? Do you want the most absurd platforming puzzles in a Metroidvania game this decade? Then try Aeterna Noctis! Make sure to play on the hard difficulty, the way it was intended. And when you get stuck, just keep trying! You'll get it after an hour or eight!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Runs perfectly on the Steam Deck. The art style made the game feel very empty to me. The boss fights are brutally punishing. It’s really a platforming game more than anything. If you don’t like precision platformers or floaty combat you won’t enjoy this. I tried over and over to get into it but the floaty combat never grooved with me.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful visuals, excellent movement/traversal (with some very difficult but enjoyable platforming), alright combat. There's actually a halfway decent and explicitly told story as well which isn't always the case with Metroidvanias.My main issue with it is that it can get a bit confusing as to where to go or what to do - I had to consult a walkthrough on a bunch of occasions. I also sometimes found myself wishing it had less combat and more platforming, but the game switches between the two often enough.The demo should be a good indicator for if you'll enjoy the game or not. Beware though that you'll need to copy save files from the demo folder to the main folder if you want to keep your progress.Also note that the "Noctis" difficulty is the way the game is "meant to be played" (as it is the original difficulty before they added the easier mode) - I'm surprised this isn't made explicit. You can swap at any time though, which I've done a few times when I got bored of dying to some bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I'm assuming you're probably a fan of metroidvanias if you're considering this game, so I'd describe this game as an interesting blend of Ori platforming combined with Hollow Knight bosses.First things first - I played on Noctis (hard) difficult, and this game is very hard. As someone who's played through and beaten Hollow Knight, Celeste, Blaspehmous 1 and 2, Cuphead and many more, this probably stands out as the hardest I have played. New areas will really force you to learn how to maximise platforming abilities, learn enemy attack patterns and triggers, and navigate the map well. With that out the way here's some pros and cons:Pros:- Amazing boss fights - they will destroy you over and over until you learn their attack patterns, but never in a way that makes you feel like you're forced into taking the fight excessively slowly as you might find in soulslike games.- Genuine open ended exploration - I have no idea what the standard way to explore the world is, but I know for a fact that my route of exploration was only one of many. If you like non-linear metroidvanias this is perfect for you.- Quest log - unlike some metroidvanias, this game logs quests and quest progress in a quest log which means you won't lose track of all the tasks you can complete, and gives you helpful direction while navigating the open world.- Responsive controls - when I first see metroidvanias I'm considering getting, my first thought is to how the controls feels. Aeterna Noctis feels great to play, and I have almost never felt like the controls were floaty or hard to control (some free aiming is required on controller which isn't always perfect but I can only think of one instance where this felt annoying to use).- Great soundtrack - I don't care for reviews that overstate soundtracks, but this game had a good soundtrack that brought out the right feelings at the right times.- Lots of unique feelings areas - each area you enter feels like it poses new levels of difficulty and challenge with different motifs. The variation in setting makes for an amazing game that stays fresh.Cons:Frustrating inventory system - unfortunately, you cannot view your inventory in a logical way in this game. If you pick up a key to a door, you cannot see what keys you have to direct your search for the lock. Sometimes you pick up a collectible and you're not told what it is. This isn't usually a big issue, but it can be really hard to tell what you have collected without a system that lets you actually search what you have collected.- Map is unclear and a pain to navigate at times - While exploring, your map is painted in with places you have been. However, for some reason the amount of map that is painted in does not align with what you can see on your screen. As a result, I've backtracked to rooms, assuming there may be an unexplored area of the map, only to find that it was the corner of a room I've stood in with nothing in it at all. In some cases, in order to properly record a full room on your map, you're forced to jump into every corner of said room such that the minimap properly shows what you've explored.- Quite a lot of open space in the map - This is mostly an issue when first exploring an area, but I found that some areas had a lot of rooms that did nothing for the game besides add volume. They didn't lead anywhere, they contained a single optional reward such as a chest containing gold etc. You can argue this is good if you like exploring for the sake of exploring, but at times it felt like I was running between huge cavernous rooms only to find nothing worthy of note.- Some optional challenges are underwhelming - I've tried to challenge myself to complete all the optional parts of this game, and unfortunately some of the rewards for this feel a bit weak - i.e. a chest containing currency and nothing else. Considering some of these are behind very difficult platforming challenges, this can feel a bit underwhelming.Overall a really good game to play, despite its drawbacks. It took a while to click but once it did it became an instant classic in my mind. I'd give it a solid 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Greatly deserved positive review, especially because you could summarize like 90% of the negative reviews in a simple but evergreen "skill issue".Yeah, the game is challenging, especially compared to others metroidvania, but that's what makes me enjoy it so much: like every challenging game you're put up to a test of your skill every time you wanna progress and it feels satisfying every time.Gameplay is solid, character is pretty responsive, the game itself is massive and every area feels a one of a kind for visuals, enemies and some stands out even more for their particular mechanics.This game is an absolute gem, bought on release hoping for a good game and it absolutely skyrocketed into my top 2 of the genre, can't wait for the release of the sequel.instead of spending time criticising this wonderful game, maybe you all should follow an old and sacred advice passed down through countless centuries: "GIT GUD"
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best Metroidvanias I ever played, very closely after Hollow Knight (which it's kinda inspired by).The challenge is great - and never unfair since many checkpoints are scattered throughout the map. Some mechanics are pretty innovative and enrichen the game with even harder and sometimes more unforgiving platforming passages. The amount of exploration is insane and soundtrack is beautiful (Vinyl, when?). There were some occasional hickups with my two Xbox based-controllers, but I guess it's taken care of by the Devs. My only gripe is the little bit weird/unusual weapon mechanics - I wish I could rather equip than tackling with multiple buttons for different weapons - this sometimes interferes and overlaps with platforming button settings...and at times remapping is necessary. I feel original (Noctis) difficulty is perfectly paced - and it's not too hard - just not a walk in the park which should be expected with a true Metroidvania. A game which fully respects the player and doesn't sacrifice difficulty for the mainstream. Eagerly awaiting the successor in 2025. The amount of love and work put into this massive game by such a small dev team is still beyond me. Kudos!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses are alright, having not played the DLC the latter half largely seemed to be more focused on using a healing build, but solid combat outside of that. But that's not what i was playing for. I wanted platforming. Good, difficult, creative platforming. And that was exactly what i got. Stellar. Couldn't recommend more.(minus the mario galaxy section, that was a bit finicky. But still fun)also, side note, never seen a game where difficulty level affected platforming. I didn't use it much, but cool that it was an option.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Hollow Knight level perfect.  Haven't played a game like this since then.  The world map, story, ability unlocks, secrets, music.  Everything is just so perfect.  Highly recommend this if you love Metroidvanias.  It even has a touch of dark souls.  The bosses are freaking amazing. I will try this on hard mode but expect to die often, and I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Sunk almost 60 hours in to fully complete and enjoyed every minute. Absolutely solid Metroidvania. Has just enough new and interesting mechanical tweaks to make it feel unique, whilst also having a familiar mechanical feel to games like Hollow Knight. Great art style, great soundtrack and great game play.It's definitely more challenging than some of the other Metroidvanias out there. The platforming needs pixel-perfect timing at points and mastering the crystal arrows takes practice, but damn you feel good perfecting the mechanics. Boss fights range in difficulty from medium to brutal, but a lot of the end-game boss fights can be brute-forced with an increased health pool and the right gem set-ups.My only minor criticisms would be some of the localisation grammatical errors/oversights, which can take you out of the game a little. Not having an "item menu" to see quest items you've picked up also makes keeping track of progress a little difficult sometimes. Did notice some FPS drops in locations too, but usually only brief and could be ignored.Would 100% recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis has a huge map like Afterimage but doesn't feel as long, and has challenging platforming and bosses, but feels more fair than Hollow Knight. The area of No Man's Land (End of the World / Edge of Reality) and the adjacent areas have become some of my most sentimental memories in gaming. The music, the atmosphere, the mechanics wowed me. Looking forward to the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Metroidvanias, mechanically, of all time. The story and lore are good enough to give the player purpose, the art is beautiful at times and frustrating at others, enemy AI is clunky and predictable, the world is a bit too complex, but the platforming and movement is in a tier that few games reside in; and that's what Metroidvanias are all about, is it not?You'll find areas throughout in the game that continue to offer fresh takes on platforming and precision movement. The formula doesn't get stale, and each challenge feels rewarding to complete. There is little reprieve, so the game does feel exhausting at times, so don't walk in expecting bursts of tough interlaced with periods of power; your skills are constantly being tested with little reprieve. Two major complaints: -The art style is not my favorite, but that is purely preference. The issue with the art itself is that the environment is often too busy and cluttered, hiding information from the player. Not ideal for a metroidvania.-It took me a couple tries to get into the game due to lack of direction and immediate complexity. It's easy to get lost when you first start, and many of the game's systems are thrown at you at the onset. It's certainly overwhelming.One major point of praise:-The uniqueness and design of the platforming challenges are equal to, if not better than, Celeste and Hollow Knight. If you play Metroidvanias for the precision movement and difficult platforming, I'd say Aeterna Noctis is the category of "must play".
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 8.5/10, definitely underrated and I don't really understand why, but I would imagine it has to do with the difficulty of the platforming in certain sections of the game.It takes a lot of the best elements that are common from the metroidvania genre, but it is unique enough to set it aside from the rest. For example, there are certain traversal skills that can be acquired in any particular order if you are good enough at platforming, and even unique achievements for doing this.If you enjoyed Hollow Knight you will definitely see some similarities in terms of movement/combat/graphics, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing. Hollow Knight was just the trend setter. One thing that has to be said about this one is that it is tough as nails. Both the combat and platforming can be incredibly unforgiving at times. About 1/2 of the way through the game you get a traversal skill in the form of an arrow that you aim which you can then teleport to (think of the skill in symphony of the night, but requiring more expertise), and the game will FORCE you to perfect this skill. At times I had to put the game down because I got so frustrated at how reliant the game was on making you utilize this skill for movement, especially near the endgame, and particularly if you want to find everything on the map. I just kept hoping for something that would make it easier to use or replace it, but that never happens. Overall, I highly recommend this one, but only if you enjoy a good challenge. I played on hard mode (noctis) which is the 'intended' way to play, but I'm sure it's still good on the easier difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I'm still in early game I think(5 hours), BUT DAMN!! I'm so impressed by the graphics, music, story,  and atmosphere. And the platforming is really good, it really feels like a very good Hollow Knight successor so far.Maybe i haven't reached the point yet or missed something but this game feels extremely underrated! I'm just so happy i found this as a hardcore metroidvania junkie, It's up there with the best so far. ¨'Edit Nr:2 I'm now 20h in, and I'm still in love with this game. It's really up there as one of the best if you ask me. Edit Nr:3 I've now completed It and to sum It up, It's Hollow Knight without the perfect combat and more heavy on the platforming and with It's own unique and beautiful story, for me It was a fantastic experience and I have no idea why I haven't found this game for so many years, especially when i go into steams metroidvania list and buys everything that seems like a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is, without a doubt, one of the finest indie games I've ever played.  It's a must-play for fans of Metroidvanias and people who want to experience the genre, and exemplifies the formula with an original and compelling world.  Bursting with satisfying challenges of skill, reflex, and observation, at no point did I feel mastery was out of reach with enough practice.  I loved the visuals, the music, the build variety, and just about everything.What can I say about it negatively?  The game has a handful of bugs that may impede play.  The script isn't perfect English and occasionally lacks punctuation.  Filling out your map is sometimes a chore because in certain areas, you need to be physically present in every corner of the room.  I can see how the endgame zones can be confusing to navigate.  Other critiques have been made, many smacking of blatant skill issue and severe cases of butthurt and hyperbole, but the developers have continued to listen and support their game.  Ya gotta give it up.This game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rules.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: If you plan play this game with controller I can't recommend this game.No aim assist with controller on high precision platforming game.No dead zone settings. My controller are slightly drift up and I always do upward attack when I stand still.When respawn for a brief moment you CAN move but CAN'T jump.Teleport are inconsistency sometimes you can move or dash after teleported sometimes not.Bow freeze movement end when slow time end. Game should freeze movement as long as I hold down bow freeze button
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: It seems like they made this game difficult just for the sake of being difficult.  I can appreciate a good challenge, but most of the time this game felt very largely unrewarding and a waste of time.  One of my first impressions was that it felt like they were trying to incorporate a lot of aspects of Hollow Knight, without really understanding what made Hollow Knight fun.  The controls, hit boxes, etc. are too inconsistent to feel good as a precision platformer.  Despite all of that, I probably could have kept powering through to the end if it weren't for the horrible level design.  Between the excessively long, repetitive platforming sections, the backtracking, and the general poor direction from the game narrative, it became quite the slog.  Eventually, I just decided it wasn't worth it.It's a little sad.  I don't think there was really much with art or music direction that I had issue with.  It seems like it actually could have been a pretty good game if it weren't for some unfortunate design choices and maybe lack of game testing (or willingness to put out a game with flawed mechanics).
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game and an excellent challenge! I have fallen in love with metroidvania games and this one did not disappoint. It features some of the best and most challenging platforming and bosses. It is quite possibly the hardest metroidvania that I've ever completed. I had so much fun playing this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I was torn on whether to recommend this or not. There were moments of rage that weren't the "I need to git gud" kind, but the game design kind, which is extra frustrating because it feels like the devs personally spiting me and not a skill thing. However, it's been a long time since I beat a game, let alone 100% it (on the easier of the two modes), so I figured that counted for something.I went and bought the soundtrack after beating it because I think it was really well done. I found the art to be very nice, especially backgrounds and bg lighting effects, though up close character art could be a little rough around the edges at times. Overall the game was pleasing to the senses.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Noctis Mode (no Vertigo gem): 109%, all simulations goldTo get to the point, challenging precision platforming is the singular aspect of the game that I believe to be noteworthy. From the beginning of the game, before you unlock any additional abilities and are limited to a dash and grounded jump, it’s clear that the game will be demanding more from you than your typical metroidvania. Levels are designed such that there’s relatively little lenience when it comes to even the most basic of platforming. Basic traversal does get more forgiving when you unlock more abilities, but the difficulty is shifted to dedicated platforming sections, especially the optional challenges. There’s a nice difficulty curve, but by about halfway through the game, you’ll already be doing Path of Pain-tier platforming more often than not. This obviously isn’t for everyone, but if it sounds appealing to you, Aeterna Noctis really does deliver on that front.Unfortunately, this is where my praise ends.My main gripe is with Aeterna Noctis is its visuals. Visual clarity is often poor and occasionally downright unacceptable, and that’s hard to overlook considering its direct effect on gameplay. Not only are platforming elements often hard to distinguish from the background, but the visual clutter from all the bloom and particle effects only exacerbates the problem. In this regard, the game is one of the worst I’ve seen in a platformer. On top of that, stiff animations and minimal visual feedback for certain mechanics are issues as well.Furthermore, the game’s art direction is non-existent. The artstyle is inconsistent, with individual models, backgrounds, effects, portraits, and cutscenes all having different styles. There’s a constant visual clash. I also think some elements are outright embarrassingly amateurish and ugly (to the point where I cannot believe they’re in the game), but I admit that’s more a matter of taste, and I’d be willing to forgive it if it were part of a cohesive vision and not an unholy amalgamation of styles that evokes Walmart Hollow Knight at best and Deviant Art at worst. Aeterna Noctis looks like a Flash game in 4K in the worst possible way.Moreover, the is not a particularly “good” metroidvania. By that I mean its critical progression felt relatively linear. It’s open in that you can tackle individual areas in different orders, especially in the front half of the game, and achievements outright acknowledge these sequence breaks (though I use this term lightly). For example, there are achievements for defeating certain bosses before getting the light arrows, teleport arrows, and double jump respectively. I got two of these three, but I never felt like I did any special platforming to bypass soft gates and do content in an interesting order. I just completed whichever self-contained area I came across.And that’s just how most of the game felt, especially in the back half. You enter a big, vaguely squared-shaped area for the first time, and complete it without having to leave. Sure, you might have the option to return later for quests and optional power-ups, but this is the most shallow form of non-linear progression. I’d much rather have the critical path bounce me back and forth between areas, with optional stuff being made available to be gradually and organically. Aeterna Noctis doesn't do this at all.Here's a lightning round of other criticisms I have of the game: unbalanced combat and wildly inconsistent boss quality with very low lows, generally tedious area design with some areas being exceptionally bloated, poorly designed quests, shockingly unclear UI (most offensive being how little of the map you can see at once), and just a little bit of glitchiness as a cherry on top.I’m really torn on this game, but it's probably worth your time if you're into precision platforming and somehow aren't turned off by the visuals. I feel like I got my money's worth, but I have a hard time praising this game as the masterpiece that it could've been with a little more time in the oven.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I originally bought Aeterna Noctis because it was on sale and I heard it was a pretty extensive game.  The reviews were fairly mixed, where many people enjoyed it while the detractors generally said it was unfair, unbalanced, etc.  I am so glad I gave this game the time it deserves because it's turning out to be one of my favorite games of the genre.  It's an absolute triumph in just about every regard.  The level of detail in the worlds is gorgeous and the gameplay is very fair, even with a high degree of toughness.  When I look for a game, I want something that will continually introduce new gameplay mechanics and use those mechanics to intelligently to force me to hone my skills, while preventing frustration.  I was reminded of the classic, Super Meat Boy as I played Aeterna Noctis due to the instant restarts after death and the constant feeling of thinking "just one more try."  It's also rare in a game that I feel so motivated to hunt down every collectible and item.  Usually, games present a multitude of options but no necessity to use them since the enemy and level/puzzle designs  don't require much thought.  Aeterna Noctis constantly forced me to use all my tools and made searching for every item extremely fun since this process usually requires backtracking to extremely tricky regions of previous areas.  For me, this game shines and absolutely deserves to be placed with Hollow Knight as one of the best Metroidvanias available.  This game just gets better and better as unique challenges are revealed and always made my jaw drop.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of the reviews compare it to hollow knight which is just not the case. Hollow Knight was a work of art and this just hasn't really even been a positive experience so far. I am also experiencing some screen view bugs where I move to an area and the camera isn't following. Not really complaining since I only paid 1.50 USD for the game but I haven't gotten attached to any of the characters and the game is pretty easy so far. After 2 hours of playtime, I am having a hard time picking it back up.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Beat 105% of game. This game is about as good as it gets for Metroidvania.  The developers put in the time to actually make a decently hard game, similar but much harder than many of its predecessors. Its pretty hard, but it has an easy mode.. not sure how it is, but super fun to play on hard.  Dont miss this game
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is *very* difficult. If you finished the path of pain in hollow knight and thought to yourself "huh, was that all?", this game is for you. I don't think it's for me, but that isn't for a lack of quality. This game is a huge, beautiful, well crafted adventure. I am very happy that this game exists even if it is a bit too extreme for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: What a massive and awesome Metroidvania!53 hours (in-game time; difficulty: noctis) for 97.5% of the game and only 33% of steam achievements. This is a lot of bang for the buck.Caution: This game is hard. If you like it hard and sometime frustrating, buy this game. There are a lot of check points so you can try a lot of passages over and over again (and often you have to). And (!) there is a lot of platforming. I myself wouldn't consider myself a friend of excessive platforming in Metroidvania, however in this game I fell in love with.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing video games since Gorf on a Commodore Vic 20 and this game is easily in my top 5.  Really challenging battles and platforming, but not frustratingly so - smooth controls - beautiful graphics - great story and humorous at the right times - varied areas - incredible level design - and such an amazing attention to detail.  The game is so much bigger and better than I was expecting.  Cannot wait for Aeterna Lucis.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I felt compelled to write a few words about it myself. Aeterna Noctis was an incredible metroidvania experience that kept me busy for 50 hours or so. The game felt like a mix of Hollow Knight and the Ori series, although leaning more towards platforming than combat. The world to explore is huge, gameplay smooth and the story interesting enough to keep the player invested in it all the way through. It is clear that a lot of love and effort were put to this title by the developers.I played the game on its intended difficulty (Noctis) and I personally felt that the game was really challenging yet fair, giving true feelings of accomplishment as I overcame yet another difficult platforming section or a gruesome boss fight. There were only few occasions where the difficulty felt insurmountable at first, but even these sections were doable in the end. And thankfully an easier difficulty is also available, altering the platforming sections so that not every jump or dash needs to be pixel perfect.The biggest and most serious issue that I read about the game where some of the progression was left unsaved when loading a save file were not present in the PC version of the game (hopefully that has been fixed in console versions as well). The game seemed overall stable, as I didn't encounter any other game breaking bugs, and only a handful of small ones like missing animations.All in all, Aeterna Noctis earned a place from my heart as a truly wonderful experience right next to Hollow Knight, and I could easily recommend this title to any who enjoy metroidvania games. There has been a lot of criticism towards this game, but along with the easier difficulty setting and fixing of the bugs I'd say that the developers have rectified these issues found since the game's launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10Platforming and exploring deserve solid 10/10. Even though some mechanics feel quite hard in the beginning, after you learn how to use them it feels really rewarding to survive. Definitely challenging, but for people like me who have spent their whole life playing 2D platformers like this is really fresh, really enjoyable. A lot of areas to explore and things to collect too, truly living up to its metroidvania genre.Outside the platforming and exploration parts, I unfortunately didn't enjoy the game that much. Boss battles are seriously tedious (some bosses take like 15 minutes to beat since their damage windows are so small!) and the world building lacks personality and interesting characters. But even with its problems, this game is definitely a top tier metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Not a perfect game, I have a couple issues with it. But overall, a very, very good experience! Not 100% yet, definitely is getting hard. But the music is great, some areas are quite beautiful, bosses are hard but engaging, and definitely rewarding in terms of you exploring for secrets.100% a hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favourite new age metroidvania. The movement and combat abilities give you more than enough freedom to never feel stuck or like there's only one path forward. You are faced time and time again with challenges that at first seem humanly impossible, but can be overcome with either a well planned strategy or a miracle. Luckily, this game is designed in such a way that miracles seem to happen often, and I have surprised myself many times with sequences that I pulled off.The music, art, world and story are all great too. I would consider the characters to be the only weak point, but I really like the king of darkness - the player character who talked the most.Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. It is hard, but the way they set up "check points" makes it really fun and not frustrating. If you like games like Hollow Knight or Sundered, this game is worth it.  The music is very atmospheric and really adds to its charm. I purchased this when it was on sale, but I'd pay full price knowing it was this fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aterna NoctisA mechanically sound metroidvania with satisfying platforming, combat, and exploration. What I found shaky was the world design, and the quest system. The game did a poor job of encouraging me to care about its characters/world/and quests. Toward the end of the game, the platforming sections get pretty trollish and reminded me of the precision platformers like The End Is Night or late game Super Meat Boy. That said, I do think this team has the chops to improve and produce a better title with a tighter world design that succeeds in making me want to 100% it. As it stands, this is a damn fine metroidvania, but one that did outstay its welcome, but excites me for what comes next from this game dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis surprises you with its high difficulty and enchants you with its addictive gameplay. While the game is a solid production, some design decisions prevented it from reaching its full potential. Some platforms are too difficult, but passable, and some bosses are simply absurd. It's good that in the game you can make an immortal build and pass all the main story bosses quite easily. But it won't work on some endgame bosses :)
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Too demanding to the point that it isn't fun. It's a chore. Aeterna mode isn't even worth trying because the devs clearly don't believe that it is, or else they wouldn't have locked it out of most of the achievements. The game is clearly meant to be played in its original state, i.e. Noctis or hard mode. You may enjoy this game if you have excellent reflexes, excellent spatial awareness, and don't mind banging your head against the same platforming sections over and over again. Then you usually have to do it again to get out. Otherwise skip it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played such games, I decided to try something in this genre, I accidentally saw this game in the recommendations. After watching the trailers, I was charged with a huge desire to play this game, against all expectations. Initially, to the extent of my stupidity, I did not understand anything😊. But after sitting and a little understanding began to reach what and how to do. The gameplay of the game seems to be very similar to all other metroidvanias, there are also some secrets, abilities, skills, character leveling and the like. _childDocuments_.review: If you like Metroidvanias, you will definitely be absorbed by this game. It excels in (almost) every aspect. With an occasional grind, the better part of the game is a Hollow Knight - type beauty. Easy to get confused now and then in which direction to explore next (it's vast!). The map teleport system works from the very beginning as you explore. Yes, you do get a double jump at some point. When I've reached about 30 h of gameplay, my brain froze when I saw I was <50% into the story line. That was the moment I understood the complexity of the game, with it's HUUUUGE map full of well-inspired scenery and calming piano-organ soundtrack specific to each biome. From some point forward, the platforming gets FU***NG HARD. I don't remember the last time I've played a Metroidvania that requires so much concentration. It has the mechanics that make Dead Cells great, like the gap-step jump and action override but...the double jump that I was mentioning earlier?..even if you would have 10 jumps (and you don't), the game WILL punish you for being either prudent or fearful. Even the game tells you that if things get overwhelming, you should reduce the difficultly.... Just buckle up for the ride, it will be a long and rewarding one, well worth 20$ !

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Metroidvania games I have played. Finished the game on Noctis mode with the (current?) max of 109% completion.The controls are smooth and responsive. I never had any problems controlling the King of Darkness. The weapons/skills are all fun to use and felt useful.I really loved the soundtrack.The game features two difficulty modes: Aeterna and Noctis. I haven't played on the easier Aeterna Mode but you should probably play on that mode if the platforming is too much. The platforming on Noctis mode does get quite hard once you get one particular upgrade in the game but it was never frustrating to me.The boss fights are very challenging but you have the ability to change your build by resetting the skill tree for no cost so if you are struggling just try a different build.The game is also huge. At about 75% it started to drag a little bit mainly due to two rather difficult to traverse areas but I appreciated those afterwards because the platforming challenge was fun.I had a blast with this game and fully recommend it! Looking forward to Aeterna Lucis!
