_childDocuments_.review: I have a love/hate relationship with this game. I get sucked into it and then I have to walk away from it.It's certainly most inspired by Hollow Knight as many in this genre, and it does it really well, though it is much more than that. The devs took a lot of chances and made a huge, slick and often maddening game from it. It's a brilliant precision platformer that will have you swearing, and one of the most difficult games that I have played. There are two difficulties, and I've only seen video of the hard mode, which significantly changes to landscape to ultra hard precision platformer. To those who have completed this game on that mode, hats off to you. To those who did 100% on that mode, I question your sanity. All of that said, I'm not a hardcore gamer. Easy mode is tough and frustrating, but also a blast. I'm taking more breaks to play something casual as I near the endgame, but I keep trying. Of note, the game uses lanterns as a spawning point, and there are many, so when you fail a platforming section 100 times, you usually respawn just before it.Some quests are a bit too obtuse, and I feel that I would have not figured them out without online help. It's definitely a well-made game, and even when I almost made the decision to bail on it a few times, I was glad that I had played so much of it to experience what I had.

_childDocuments_.review: Curb your expectations. I've read reviews saying that this is like someone took the hollow knight path of pain, and made a full game out of it. That's true'ish, but there are a couple of things that need to be mentioned here. 1. The controls are clunky. I can't really think of a better way to describe them. When I play hollow knight and die, I know that *I* was the one who died. In Aeterna Noctis, when I die there's a pretty good chance that lack of responsiveness will be a factor. It's not BAD, so much as rough. Hollow knight felt fluid, and smooth, and this feels almost abrasive in its control.2. The foreground objects are completely out of control in some places. I'm currently playing yet another part with enemies that spawn in waves. While that's unoriginal and boring, it's not exactly terrible. The issue is that there are areas in the corners and edges of the arena where the foreground details used to create atmosphere actually obscure the view of the character and sprites. In a game that's trying to focus on fine-tuned and frame-specific controls, I don't really love that.3. The game opens up FAST. You go through the tutorial bit, and within an hour or 2  you'll have branching options to explore the world. This can be great, but it has to be scaled well by region. Some areas I've explored are... unforgiving relative to my progress, with no clue as to where I should be looking. Normally I love this, but coupled with the janky controls and annoying foreground obstruction, it makes for an unpleasant experience.Overall it's a decent game if you're itching for a metroidvania, and it's not a bad game, so much as a decent game that's thoroughly overreaching to be a great game, without doing its homework first.When the controls are responsive and smooth, it feels pretty satisfying to play. But coming from games that prioritize smooth controls and game play, this feels like a near-miss. I'm hoping updates make this a more enjoyable experience. There's a lot of promise here.

Also the story is absolutely wretched beyond comprehension, there should not have even been a story in this game if it was going to be this bad.  Combat needed refinement, there's no reason whatsoever for so many enemies to have on death attacks and there are way too many teleporting enemies and enemies that constantly try to stay out of your melee range.  I give this game one Hollow Knight out of 10.  Avoid.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great example of punishingly precise platforming that requires learning from your mistakes to do better the next time. Some of the later platforming challenges feel downright impossible until you do them just right, and then just when you think you've made it through the worst part, it throws another section that's equally or even more difficult at you. Enemy density can get a little too heavy in some areas that require platforming, and unless you're running a ranged build it can be hard to juggle killing enemies and not falling to your death or being pierced by spikes. The one major complaint I have is how scarce the currency (dogmas) can feel, especially in the post-game when all quests are completed and you're having to buy Knowledge Atlases for every area just to pin down the last few collectibles. _childDocuments_.review: Ooookay... so, here's the deal. The game is really good at what it is. And what it is, primarily, is a hardcore precision platforming game, like Celeste and similar games. It is super hard and could do with a couple more checkpoints. If this is your jam, go for it, it's definitely worth it, even for full price.You get a choice whether to play in this intended "hard" difficulty, or play a significantly more relaxed "easy" mode where muncher tunnels have been replaced by regular floor and a handful of enemies. If you play in this easier difficulty, I imagine you may be a bit disappointed in the game, as what remains is an ok metroidvania with a handful of semi skillful platforming segments. If this is more what you want, I recommend waiting for a sale.Also important to know: the enemy AI as well as boss difficulty is entirely unaffected by the difficulty setting. The difficulty setting ONLY affects the platforming.Outside of this very important differentiation above, what you get is a metroidvania game with a gigantic map to explore. The similarities to Hollow Knight are very obvious as well, for example, you need to find a dude who sells you the maps to locations before a "fog of war" is removed from your map screen. The "secrets maps" that reveal all item locations in an area, by the way, do not contain the base map, so you have to buy both versions in order to actually reveal the explored parts of the map and its items.The game at its current patch also still has a few bugs in it. They are not too bad to work around or avoid, though.1. Once you get the teleport arrows, you may accidentally (or on purpose) teleport into light areas (which kill you instantly). Upon respawning, you may be softlocked as you are unable to move, attack or jump. The workaround for this is quitting to title through the menu (which still works) and reloading.2. Late in the game, you may invest skill points towards a trait called "Guardian Angel" that automatically revives you once. Currently, there is a bug with that skill: If you have the skill equipped and transition between maps (or die and respawn, thus reloading the current map), the game freaks out and "forgets" to apply most of your traits and effects from gems correctly. The workaround for this is: first reset your skill tree at a throne, then quit to title and reload, subsequently re-equipping the traits from the skill tree as you wish. If you wish to use the Guardian Angel skill against bosses, save 1 Skill Point in order to apply the trait inside the boss room. This gives you one shot of having all of your traits working correctly for the boss, although sadly, in order to get everything working properly again, you have to find a throne again to reset your traits.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard for me to describe how incredibly happy I am having found this title, it's the reason why I play indie games such that I occasionally stumble upon something like Aeterna Noctis. I know that a great majority of people, regardless of whether they're fairly experienced in metroidvanias, will either not give the title a chance or consider it too hard in the first place. While yes, the intended difficulty is relentless, the developers seem to have added an easier mode which essentially cuts the difficulty by a factor of maybe 3 or 4, but for me the regular one was precisely the right amount of challenge to keep me thriving. After around ~30 metroidvanias I've played in my life I didn't feel the same playful yet tormenting degree of platforming until this game, it's so satisfying and precise that you know exactly what you did wrong if you moved an inch too far to the side. Whilst this difficulty is exactly what I was searching for, I do believe that Aeterna Noctis made me better at metroidvanias, it's not about having mastered the specific movement set but instead actually realising that you're progressing in terms of timing, precision and haste, which is a feeling I rarely ever get from any game. Yes of course there were a few bugs and one item caused my basic attacks to become useless, but that can't outweigh my appreciation for the creators of this game. I'm aware these words will be read, thereby, thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been spending a lot of time trying to fill the void left in my heart after full clearing Hollow Knight. Eventually I stumbled across Aeterna Noctis and decided to give it a shot. I played on the noctis difficulty, which is the enhanced difficulty. I've gotta say, this game is incredibly challenging, but also incredibly rewarding when you push through areas. While there is enough similarity to Hollow Knight to scratch the itch, the game leans MUCH heavier on platforming than Hollow Knight does. If you've done the White Palace in Hollow Knight, that's like level 1 baby level in this game. What kind of challenges you end up doing by the end of this game is super difficult and wild to get just right. However, I got really good at joystick control and precision after this game!The other really positive about this game is the size of the world. The map is freaking HUGE. I thought I had explored everything, then realized I hadn't even explored 50% of the map. A lot of great content, interesting puzzles and mechanics in various areas.This game I would say is not for the faint of heart, though I've heard the lesser difficulty is not quite as painful (less spikes and traps), so maybe that is an option for those who aren't masochists. The story was fine, art is charming, music is nice. Nothing about it to write home about imo, but it's not bad. Would highly recommend this game to the gamer that loves platformers or metroidvanias and a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game / At least for me a Top 10 ever metroidvaniaPros:good story , badass MC , superb levels of art ,Huge map ( maybe larger than symphony of the night both castles),DEV is a really nice guy , music Neutral : Too much work for collectables  , most of them are really not worthy  ,Some rage quit inducing platforms but on the plus size if you fail ,the game is very fair and dont punish you a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I love these games, I really like this genre. This game has a nice soundtrack, interesting gameplay and excellent game design, a complex platformer that challenges us. The mechanics of souls are taken from dark souls, which made me very happy and liked it. I highly recommend it to anyone who loves this genre of games!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A game in the genre of Metroidvania with good gameplay will occupy all your free time, and interesting locations will not let you get bored. in the game there are 16 different worlds that give you a sense of the beauty of the gameHaving only begun to play it immediately I liked it, because worked out games in general a little bit, but it is included in this number)
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent 2D action adventure in the style of metroidvania, in some places it is quite difficult, but this only increases the desire to play, the levels are quite interestingly designed, where sometimes you have to think how and where to go.Quite a good soundtrack with no less interesting and complex bosses, for fans of "hollow knight", this project deserves attention!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game, because I like it when my ass is on fire from when these damn creeps kill you.  Now I will write the pros and cons that I found for myself in this game: Pros: an epic story with its own intrigues;  many large, diverse locations;  exciting classic gameplay;  the game is amazingly drawn;  with music, too, everything is fine and on topic; Cons: The complexity of platforming in places may seem inadequate;  management is not the most responsive;
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended but not for everyone.You should be warned that this game is HARD even on Aeterna (= Easy) mode and INSANELY HARD on Noctis (= Normal) mode.Only play it if you are able to bear the frustration of having to try many parts dozens of times or if you don't mind cheating.Besides the difficulty and a few minor flaws, this is an excellent game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game just wasn't for me. There are some things to like about this game but ultimately I got to a point where it just wasn't fun anymore and I wasn't even at the halfway point. I've played plenty of souls-like games and metroidvanias but these are some of the toughest bosses in a game that I've come across.In my opinion, this game crosses the line of punishingly hard difficulty and just stops being fun. I enjoyed the first 15 hours of this game but the areas are REALLY long and part of what stopped making it fun for me was the fact that as you are travelling it's difficult to know where to go. This is normally fine, but because the areas are so huge, you can waste a lot of time traversing and executing the extremely difficult platforming only to find an hour into an area you don't have the correct skill to progress further and need to backtrack.Another part that just stopped making it fun for me is after the 4th or 5th large area you acquire a skill that can help you reach treasure and items that weren't accessible in all the past areas. This means to get these items you have to basically go through all the past areas again, which wouldn't be a big deal except the areas are so large  you have to spend hours just backtracking.If you are really into extremely precise platforming and bosses that will make you want to break the closest thing around you then you will enjoy this game. Kudos to everyone who beat this game. This might be one of if not the most difficult game I have played.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:• Quality hand-drawn animation, a rare thing to see these days• Environments are beautiful• Huge world to explore, lots of content• Solid combat and RPG mechanics• Great-feeling traversal and movement mechanics • Plenty of (gameplay-useful) collectibles to find Mixed:• Game has a large focus on platforming content. If you prefer more combat-heavy games, this may be an issue.• Something like 70% of the enemies in the game explode after death. This isn't necessarily a huge problem on its own, but takes getting used to and is kind of a weird choice by the devsCons:• Most of the boss fights aren't great. • The puzzle-focused area kind of sucks. Overall though, it's a great metroidvania and a solid game altogether. If you enjoyed Hollow Knight, you'll probably enjoy this, as the games feel quite similar at times. I'd recommend giving it a shot if you're a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a great metroidvania, and from Hollow Knight there's an awesome living world in which you immerse yourself, and you can just listen to the sounder for hours and the combat system is magnificent, and the plot is a mixture of dark souls and DotA, where they took all the best and increased it hundreds of times. It's just a bomb. The best metroidvania I've ever played. Lvls, bosses, enemies, everything in this game is top notch. Especially deliver references to pop culture in the plot)P.S.I'm very upset that Steam doesn't allow such a great game to release cards, although we get cards all the time like second-rate manure like a mosaic with hentai...They have such backgrounds in the game, such a cool profile could be made, but alas ... Steam GIVE CARDS TO THE GAME !!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent metroidvania with an emphasis on platforming.The hero has various abilities, skills, he can be pumped (and this is done quite easily, you can farm mobs as much as you like), some abilities are scattered in ten tombs, to which you need to find keys during the exploration of the world.Overall, I am very happy with the game. It has a huge potential, and I wish the developers a huge creative and commercial success, as well as to bring their creation to the ideal.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Map transitions look like places you failed to discover. Combat movement is wacky and isn't comfy. (Many enemies explode, throwing projectiles. It's like every kill makes you wait.) Platforming is quite weird, definitely isn't comfy compared to games like Celeste. (Quite a few games exists which I DISLIKE dashing. Really thin platforms block your chonky bodies movement) Bad PC port, as in menu navigations are unintuitive and weird, and some keys are not customizable.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely demanding metroidvania focused on precise and tight platforming.Full of creative ideas regarding level design, art style and power-ups. The technical execution is lacking at certain points: a clear sign that this is the first professional experience of the developing team. Still, in the end the memorable moments, the satisfaction after clearing tough stages and the baroque music score triumph over the occasional bugs and the lack of polish.Is this the next Hollow Knight? No. But it is a genuine effort to produce a challenging and original experience, well worth your time if you can indulge some mistakes.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves a lot more praise.Easily in the top 3 best metroidvanias of all time and I'm not really sure where in that top 3.For reference the others are Hollow Knight and Blasphemous. Maybe even Grime (fantastic relatively less known game).I 100% the game (Noctis difficulty / the hardest) in a bit more than 65 hours.+ The plateforming is on point. Challenging and rewarding. Very well designed. Even if I compare Aeterna to pure plateformers, the only game that beats it is Dustforce.+ Boss designs vary in quality. Some are very good, others less so (advanced robot....). They are challenging but you can facetank a lot of them with a proper build which is a bit silly. You can't do that with the emperor though, a very nice end game optionnal boss.+ The build system with a skill tree and gems like Hollow knight is very fun. It's a bit silly towards the end like I mentionned with the bosses though.+ The world is very large with a lot a variety and in the latter game its very colorful and pleasant. Most games starts with the colorful and finish with dark and barren environments. Aeterna does the opposite. The starting area is the worst.+ Even though you have the traditional metroivania progression, you have quite a lot of say in the order you'll explore the map.+ The art direction is good and it gets better as you progress and the soundtrack is surprisingly good for an indie.A few negatives:- The knowledge atlas (you can buy one per region) reveals the secrets in each region, which is a good thing to wrap up the game in the end without making it horribly tedious but they are way way too expensive and you will only be able to acquire like 2/3 of them without grinding like a mad man.- The Garibaldi (he is a boss/npc) story line is being teased but it's a dead end.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Huh? Why are people not playing this game?!This is an absolute masterpiece.Aeterna Noctis obviously copies most of what made Hollow Knight fantastic and does it well. A truly huge Metroidvania, with lots of enemy types, areas, secrets, abilities, satisfying boss fights, and very difficult platforming.It's very unfortunate that it gets very hard later in the game and I am not sure if I will put in the time to perfect dodging a specific boss' insane attack. (literally need to hang to a specific point on the wall, jump, dash, jump again, use ability-maybe twice, and don't fall down) and all that on like a two second warning... three times in a row).That said, even if I stop now I feel like I've gotten a great deal on this game. It's tons of fun, it looks great, the music is excellent, combat is fun (though grindy), the areas are very creative, and generally the game does respect your time with lots of checkpoints.Absolutely give this a shot, it is a worthy successor of Hollow Knight.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: AeternaNoctis is a complex (complexity increases with each level) two-dimensional Metroidvania with intense battles and platform sections, where you will have to show all your skills. Taking on the role of the King of Darkness, you must help him restore his power in 16 different and related areas in the original epic story.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Where to start. This game is dope. It's hard but not that hard. The level design is great. If you like tricky platforming then this is the game for you. The bosses are really hard. I'm stuck on one right now and that's frustrating but it's my fault I can't beat it. If you like Hollow Knight you're going to love this. It at times challenges that game for the best metroidvania of all time. It's not just kind of great, it's one of the best games I've ever played. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: After spending 18 hours playing this game, I'm honestly not sure if I like it or not.  The fact that it's a platformer with levels/skills/RPG elements is really cool, but a lot of it is *really* unpolished.  The game is very difficult, and can even be quite punishing at times.  I kept at it because I liked the general premise of the game (Both mechanically and narratively), but I eventually gave up when they started having a lot of required twitchy traversal puzzles after getting the . With a polish pass and reduced difficulty though, this game could have been extremely enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good game. I was pleasantly surprised by it. It looks great, has an interesting story, diverse areas, cool concepts, and great music. They could have used a bit more offensive capabilities though. It does have a bit more platforming than I expected and some are pretty crazy ones at that, but nothing I couldn't handle. The whole 4 bells thing is ridiculous though so if you're the type who wants to complete everything 100% that will drive you insane so good luck with that. Some of the bosses feel a bit cheesy since it can be hard to dodge them and your healing is quite limited. In all as of this review I have just beat the game and completed most of everything save for that 4 bell crap and beating the optional boss in the . I recommend this if you like metroidvania type games and don't mind a heavy dose of platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that clearly wears many influences on its sleeves, it does not learn much from them. You'll fight the same enemy types over and over, just in different skins; the world feels aimless in general as you have little sense of a critical path, then constantly hit dead ends until you unlock new abilities, which leads to a lot of irritating backtracking.Combat is incredibly bland to the point of skipping around enemies feels like the better and more efficient strategy, and the movement/jumping is just loose enough to be frustrating in a game that relies on high platforming skills. The graphics and music are probably the best part of this game, however the amount of foreground graphics that block your vision is maddening; I shouldn't have trouble seeing my character so often in a game.The concept on paper checked so many boxes for me, but unfortunately it did not deliver on any of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: My initial "review" was a recommend based on my first impressions, but having played the game more, I find it hard to recommend, even to those who enjoy really challenging games. I enjoy precision platformers like Super Meat Boy and Celeste quite a lot. Pixel perfect dodging and platforming with precise timing and high speed reflexes is my forte. This game has that and I do enjoy that part of it. What I don't enjoy is the atrocious backtracking. I recognize backtracking is always going to be a factor in Metroidvanias, but typically the best games remedy this tedium through shortcuts, movement abilities, and fast travel. AN has these things, but fast travel points/shortcuts are few and far between. You will fight tooth and nail to get one of a f*** ton of some collectible (and there are a LOT of collectibles) only to have to backtrack all the way out of that area likely with all enemies respawned. This is not fun or challenging. This is just tedious for no good reason. On top of that, this game has the worst visual clutter I've ever seen in my life. For a game that blends precision platforming with bullet hell boss fights, why in God's name would you make enemies and their projectiles the same color palette as the background with excessive bloom and obnoxious s*** in the foreground obscuring your vision? This is horrible in certain areas like the Forge and the awful Phoenix boss fight. It's a beautiful game, but this isn't a painting. Artistic expression should not come at the expense of visual clarity. The soulslike death mechanic adds nothing, but more tedium to the game. You know how when you die in Souls, that spot is where all your souls are until you get it back or die and have a new spot with all the souls you gathered along the way? Well this game got the first part of that. Basically, if you died in some extremely hard to reach area and you just can't get back there, so you just wanna move on, you can't. Your bloodstain will sit there forever until you go retrieve it or pay a large fee to get it back. It doesn't matter if you die again. That bloodstain will remain there and you need it, especially to get rid of that annoying visual effect that's excessively taking up screen space. Combat feels weightless and your sword has all the range of a paper towel. You can't just quickly cut down enemies and move on since at least 50% of them have some sort of on-death effect that can do damage to you. Aiming arrows (which you WILL be doing a lot) just feels awkward playing with a controller. You move in slow motion while aiming, but there's no way to just lock him in place while aiming to prevent running off of the incredibly small platforms you stand on. The camera has to be manually adjusted constantly to see if there's any platforms to jump up/fall down to to avoid taking a needless leap of faith. The lack of input buffering makes movement not feel as tight as it could be. Everything in shops is absurdly expensive to the point where you will need to grind for gold. You'll collect over a dozen gems and still only have 1 to 2 gem slots available. Even the UI is visually cluttered and trying to navigate the game's MASSIVE map is a nightmare. It's stupid that you can fully explore an entire area, but still have the map be darkened because you didn't buy the map from the archaeologist in the area. Areas are just absurdly massive and take so long to explore that I lost any interest in going back to previously explored areas to get items that I couldn't get before because of an ability I lacked. This completely kills a big part of the appeal of metroidvanias.The story describes our character as a prince of darkness who is absolutely not a "good guy" and is not afraid to just kill someone for disrespecting him, yet he still agrees to do fetch quests for NPC's who talk down to him like the Goblin King. Even after he sets you up to be killed in his arena instead of rewarding you, you still don't get the option to kill him. This is some ludonarrative dissonance.Aeterna Noctis is a game that starts very strong, but becomes more and more tedious as it progresses. If the narrative was tighter and more focused, levels more condensed, visual clutter reduced, soulslike bloodstain removed, controls much smoother, and difficulty curve more even, this game would be an easy recommend as it looks and sounds great, and is packed with content. As it stands, it suffers from some massive design flaws that just made the game less fun and more frustrating. I'm not asking for an easier game. I'm asking for a less tedious game. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent addition to the Metroidvania collection, one of my favourites. This game was made for the sort of player who has played a lot of Metroidvanias and is looking for a game to step up the challenge. If you're a glutton for punishment, you'll enjoy Noctis mode. It's not impossible, but some of the platforming sections require persistence and sometimes you just have to get lucky. The artwork deserves commendation as well. Overall, Aeterna Noctis really exceeded my expectations and was more than worth the purchase price.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game?Beautiful graphics, good effects, gameplay with a lot of different abilities that will open up as you go through the game. Also pleased that the game supports a large number of languages. The only thing I didn't like about the game was the music. Other than that, it's good. To buy advise)
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.  Finished on Noctis mode.  It is mostly a platforming/puzzle game.  I have two gripes with the game.  First is the weird soulslike aspects of the game.  If you die from a platforming challenge, not only you lose your soul but you also lose the ability to gain extra experience/souls so you are basically forced to go through the platforming section which you died and then complete it backwards if you simply just want to collect your soul.  Alternative is just to pay a hefty price in town to get the souls back.  Its very counterintuitive.  Sometimes you don't want your unspent souls but you are basically forced to go and get it back otherwise you simply won't gain experience/souls again.  My second gripe is that the usual mobs are not interesting enough to fight and don't offer a challenge even on hardest difficulty.  Even the bossfights are more of a puzzle/platforming challenge with the exception one or two which are dps checks.  I would give it a 7.5/10.  Very good if you are looking for a platforming focused metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis combines Hollow Knight and Castlevania SOTN in a very good and fun way. I thank the developers from the bottom of my heart for adding the "Aeterna Mode" (easy mode/ true metroidvania mode), because the difficulty level in the standard mode sometimes requires inhuman reflexes. Aeterna mode is still challenging but very doable. At no point does it reach the level of Elden Ring/Dark Souls. Noctis mode on the other hand..yaaaa...The platforming is brutal.The atmosphere of the game world is melancholic and mystical. The map is very large and full of secrets and hidden paths. Exploring and fighting all the enemies doesn't get boring because you'll constantly find new ways and abilities, which provides variety. The motivation curve is very well done and this game is  definitely one of the larger metroidvanias out there. There is a lot of content and unlockables. The background music is also very well done. It sets the tone very well and fits the melancholic and somber mood of the game.I had to get used to the hero first. His character sometimes varies between really cool and kinda cringy. But the power fantasy that comes with him is not bad. Not bad at all! Anti-heroes are better than regular heroes anyway. And after a time he kinda grew on me.In conclusion, I love Metroidvanias. And this game does a lot right. It stands shoulder to shoulder with modern gems like Bloodstained, the aforementioned Hollow Knight, or Blasphemous. It's a shame this game is more of a hidden gem. It deserves a lot more praise and attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real complicated metroidvania. When I say challenging, I mean VERY challenging. It tests your platforming, combat, and navigation skills. But when you achieve your goal, all your efforts pay off. The game knows exactly what it is and what the player wants to get out of it. I definitely recommend it if you are tired of casual games.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game not 100% sure if I would love it or not. I definitely enjoyed it more then I thought and it did a decent job of merging platforming, Rouge Like, and metroidvania elements.Pros:- Great art style- Many secrets to discover without feeling overly tedious- Cool power ups and ways to level up each run throughCons:- Lack of blocking- Some of the back tracking is a bit annoying.- The base plot isn't revolutionaryThere isn't a lot to hate about this game and it runs well. I can see where it got it's accolades but for me personally I don't know if I would buy it full price. I give it 7/10 cycles.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A good and moderate metroidvania revolution. Excellent graphics, gameplay with a bunch of different abilities that open up as you progress, cool, given boss fights, and of course it's great that there is a translation into Russian. The plot here is of course not the most important thing, so the game is for those who want a challenge and lovers of interest in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game perfectly honoring the metroidvania genre. Amazing boss fights and neat platforming (the second changes with difficulty) making the game extremely fun. While some side quests and secrets are not intuitive, they're mostly not required to complete the game any%, leaving the pleasure of discovery to the completionists who want 100%. I would not suggest this title to newcomers in platformers/metroidvanias, but if you already played a couple titles and you feel confident in your gaming skills, start a run in Noctis mode and face this game at its hardest difficulty (which i feel is its finest). I bought it on a discount, but in hindsight it's for sure worth its pricetag and despite being an indie game, its gameplay quality is on par if not exceeding triple As of this period.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, but definitely not for those that are expecting an easy time.  I've played 25 hrs and have only reached 65% of the game while going through the entire map looking for all the hidden items.  Many of the boss fights are very challenging, some are near impossible if you haven't progressed far enough to gain the proper damage and heart fragments.  If you were able to beat Metroid Dread or Ender Lilies, definitely give this a try.  This game is way better than Hollow Knight, in almost every way.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Art is great- Jumping puzzles and mechanics are tightThe bad:- The environments are huge and empty- Enemies are repetitive- Leveling up (skills system) is paced way off. It takes forever to get skill points, as enemies give very little experience and they are spread extremely thin over the maps- Language is extremely annoying, and what's worse is that one second a NPC is speaking perfect English, and 2sec later the same NPC is speaking the gibberish language- Boss fights are boring and repetitive. Lacking creativity, simply repeating attacks randomly from a pool of 3-4 different attacks.It tries way too hard to be just like another game. But ultimately, teleports spread way too thin over a huge map sparsely populated with danger and a story you end up skipping because of the unbearable gibberish makes this one a pass. If you have exhausted all metroidvania games, sure, otherwise your money is better spent elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A massive metroidvania with good music, graphics, and atmosphere. The platforming sections are very satisfying to play through as well, and thankfully the map is built in a way where (for the most part) you don't have to do anything too absurd to get around after clearing certain sectors of the map. As you acquire more abilities you start feeling really BA. There isn't a button excluded when it comes down to the tough fights. There's a shield, multiple weapons, ranged options (and options for those options). The amount of huge brain plays you can come up with whether it be in combat or platforming is very satisfying once the King is kitted out with all his abilities. After playing for hours and seeing stuff I thought I could never pull off feel like a simple flick of a few buttons is a really awesome feeling, there's a lot of gratification when playing this one and improving compared to most other platformers due to their more tame nature. This game isn't afraid to whoop you and turn up the notch just when you thought the notch couldn't be dialed up further.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Fair bit of butthurt in some of the other reviews because of the game's difficulty.  It is indeed difficult, but it is very polished, has a great soundtrack, a very large map with awesome original levels.  I suspect that unless you've completed Ori (both), Hollow Knight, and Ender Lilies, you may this game more challenging than fun at first, but it does give you plenty of opportunities to practice the skills you need, and dying/ressing is not that big of a deal (compared to Salt and Sanctuary, where it was really just very annoying).  Some bosses are a bit ridiculous.  Looking forward to playing the sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the negative reviews, this game is awesome! Amazing music, incredible visual direction, an interesting story, and a huge beautiful world to explore. Is it hard? Yes, it is. The platforming in particular is extremely challenging in places when playing in Noctis mode. Does that make it a bad game? Certainly not! I for one appreciate the challenge and always felt elated when I finally got good enough to over come them. Bosses are also challenging but not quite on the same level as Hollow Knight.The only real complaints I have are lack of D-Pad movement and some minor issues related to the teleport arrow that probably apply only to me.All in all I would *highly* recommend this game, it's easily one of the best metroidvanias ever made.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original (hard) mode and 100% the game.This is an amazing metroidvania that left me positively speechless and in awe in various occasions.The amount of content for the price is insane, the music is top-notch, many bossfights are memorable, some levels come as a big surprise and there are novel challenges here that I have not found before in other metroidvanias.The game starts hard and the difficulty curve increases at a steady pace but you will be surprised to find your skills improving as steadily.Looking forward to future titles by these devs.Rough edges like others mentioned are the brutal plaltforming (I personally loved it and there is a normal mode that modifies the level layouts) and the fact that in certain areas background and foreground art make it hard to understand what is going on (nothing gamebreaking anyway).Some reviews criticized the responsiveness of the controls but I did not have any issues with them. Others claim this game does not respect your time and I would say that is a lie, there are plenty of checkpoints in basically every other room.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like a good challenge? Are you okay with running your face against a wall multiple times until you happen to notice the door handle just within reach? Then this is the game for you!The game features some pretty fun and very precise platforming, as well as some very clever teleporting puzzles with various abilities. The creativity is present in a lot of this game's mechanics and I had a lot of fun beating and playing the game to 100%.That said, there are some negatives about the game you should be ready for. It will feel like the dash doesn't obey your control stick if you're expecting it to be like hollow knight, celeste, or sympony of the night. It takes time for the King of Darkness to turn, which is why some teleport-above-a-floor-of-spikes-after-dropping-off-of-a-perch-near-the-wall areas can be a bit painful to get through. Luckily the game has a lot of checkpoints which makes this not too terrible.Most of the bosses are really enjoyable to fight and I enjoyed getting achievements for defeating them without having certain abilities yet because I happened to explore down to them before going over to obvious story areas first. There are some nasty bosses though who have way too much RNG (looking at you robot round 2) that make for some pretty frustrating bosses. But, that said, the game lets you reset your skill point tree at any throne and you can try out different builds. Some bosses are extremely tricky with just a sword, while they're piss easy with the three-arrow + homing gem. I beat the final boss of the game on my first try because of that arrow build and I laughed my way home down the credits.The ending of the game leaves things open for a sequel, and hopefully we get one soon because there's not many games that offer the kind of lore, world, and challenge that this game brings to the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I just beat the game today on normal difficulty (took about 4 hours) and I think it's awesome !Personally, I love the art style, the locations, the animations (which can be make or break for me in games likes these) and the general chara design. Music is up there too.I started playing on hard difficulty and I thought the game was hard as hell. So I lowered to normal and still thought the game was pretty brutal. That was until I realized I was earning gems that could let me make upgrades (as well as unlocking checkpoints) and then everything clicked and started getting easier.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: A very tentative positive review. The art and music are fantastic. All dialogue is voiced, and although I don't know Spanish it sounds nice to the ear anyway, with every character sounding appropriate for their style. Exploration and careful review of the map for secrets is typically well-rewarded. Character building in the skill tree and gem loadout feels very versatile and can be respecced for free at any fast travel throne.But... slime enemies are always miserable to fight, there's no real challenge to them but they waste your time with their lingering post-death effects that you just have to run away from and wait out. So many enemies have janky hitboxes, where their collision hitbox is apparently much larger than their attackable hitbox, especially dragons. Some enemies, especially those dragons, have way too much health and take way too long to fight when they appear a dozen per area and can barely be avoided. There's a level cap for some reason, which was incredibly obnoxious to find out when I realized I'd be two skill points short of the build I was going for. The oracle area of fake walls and floors is miserable to navigate if you don't track down a third-party map that labels the room exits.I'd usually be enjoying myself in this game, especially when the story could come to the forefront, but it can be so frustrating to play at times. Exemplified with the the Abyss, which is the best and worst of the game at the same time. Wonderful art, tons of story reveals, a new power that opens up a new movement process through the second half of the area, and yet every single enemy is a slog to fight.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Update: The game ended up as a 10/10 for me and the only part you really have to know is that it's hard but very well made and if you like challenges you will prob love the game. The issue in update 6 is the only issue I had with the game but overall is insignificant.Update 6: Ok so there is one jumping puzzle (door IX) that is indeed badly designed as you don't know where to go at some point and the moving parts make figuring out the way annoying and not fun because it's not hard but just not CLEAR. Then there is a later area that let's you fall down on platforms below requiring significant backtracking to get back to the area you droped from. This made the game a 9.5 for me. I will update the review when I am finished playing.Update 5: Adressing other reviews: All those people complaining about hitboxes are just bad players. The hitboxes are perfect and the precision platforming is god tier. I really like the one guy that called the jumps "weighty" because you have to hold down the button to jump higher... Oh really? How the F are you supposed to make a precision platformer without that mechanic??? One of the core skills is to learn how high to jump and it's a BASIC feature. He also goes on saying other games he played don't feature that mechanic, and guess what: They prob are not precision platformers! Ofc. you don't need it in simple jump and runs or roguelikes or anything else that doesn't need precision. But even then there are plenty of those games that STILL use that mechanic to give the player more CONTROL. Like I get the people who say I am not good enough to beat the game, but I really hate those whiny people that blame the game instead of themselves. You are the reason we can't have hard games because unless someone tells you it's cool you can't think for yourselves. All this souls games are hard ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ has people believing they are actually good at games without trying. Trash games like Jump King are being held to such high regards because people expect to fail a lot, then people bash a geniusly designed game (esp. by comparison with that turd jump king) for its difficulty. Like sometimes I just wish you could auto flag bad players for reviews so you can ignore those...Update 4: Not done yet but as it stands now this game will end up one of the best games I have ever played and the best metroidvania I have played. It's an absolute masterpiece of gamedesign and artdesign (man the music and art on this one is spot on). There are areas that feel more epic than I can describe. I am feeling like a kid again discovering new worlds and challenges. So far only Miyazaki's games could give me that feeling (although souls games are easy compared to this, the game is genuinely hard later on, but in a good way). And I am not a kid anymore after over 30 years of gaming I am thankful whenever I can have this sensation again, thank you devs!Update 3: Once you get used to the difficulty level so far it's been very fair and you really get much better at the games movement with time feeling a real sense of improvement few games can give you when you traverse the map again to get stuff you couldn't get/missed. Also the amazing thing is most puzzles are reverse designed so you get 2 puzzles from one challenge design which I really like since you are never limited to movement in one direction or spamed with tps to skip backwards (and no this is not lazy as you actually need to design it that way it isn't reused level design like in other games that aren't platformers)!Update 2: Ok so the game get's crazy after a certain point when you get a new ability and becomes one of the hardest games ever created. BUT it is masterfully crafted and NOT TOO HARD as it has super fair checkpoints! But in all seriousness the bosses and the platforming are insanely fun if you like a real challenge (not like soulsborne games which are rather easy by comparison). def a 10/10 for me so far!Update 1: The game has some really epic fights and is very well made so far. Very unique and epic use of background layers in fights and jumping passages!So far the game is really good (playing on hard mode) and not too difficult (I am a precision platformer and metroidvania/soulslike games veteran so take that with a grain of salt) but maybe later it will get crazy IDK but since it has two modes which are designed for different players I suspect most players can enjoy the game!Most negative reviews are just people who are bad at platformers and don't want to get good at them, and that is fine because if you are that type of person the game will prob not be the best pick. But grow some balls and admit that YOU are the problem, not the game :)The art is really nice the world looks epic and the movement feels good. Actually I was really surprised how much better the game looked in motion than on the screenshots!

_childDocuments_.review: Smooth and fluid combat, compact skill tree, somewhat challenging in parts dependent on the mode (You can switch between "normal" and "hard" at will at any point with no repercussion - hard has a lot more challenges, spikes, traps, etc - a fantastic challenge well worthy of taking on), nice story, beautiful art - very reminiscent of Hollow Knight again, and HUGE (I mean breathtakingly huge) map, which unlocks more as you gain more skills from challenges.  I rarely write reviews, I rarely play through games fully, owning thousands makes it very hard to grab one and stick with it but this has held my attention for 36 hours at the time of this review and it will hold it until I grind through all of the challenges and all of the bosses on Noctis mode. _childDocuments_.review: Dare I say this is better, for me at least (put down the pitchforks) than Hollow Knight? Sure, I only have 4 hours on record, and I chose to play on the Aeterna difficulty, but in terms of presentation alone--the colorful environments, the character with a voice, the smooth and fluid controls, an actual skill tree to add a sense of character progression, etc. I've found myself enjoying this more than Hollow Knight. The game looks beautiful, it's colorful, it's inviting, at the outset you already have a brief, but good understanding of the character your playing and why he's doing what he's doing. The platforming, even on Aeterna difficulty, can be somewhat enraging, especially when you get to the end of a particularly challenging corridor only to land on a spike or other hazard and have to start the corridor all over again, but at least check points are plenty so it alleviates some of the frustration.A lot of people who've been looking at this game probably got the gist that this game is hard, so far in the first few hours of me playing it has been challenging, and I can only surmise that it's going to get harder, but don't let that throw you off--It's a good game that should be tried out by even the passing metroidvania fans, like myself.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I am reviewing Noctis mode, the mode the game was designed around.The game starts out strong, but after the half way point the game gets difficult due to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Bosses have too many particle effects to see what can actually hurt you and the game turns into a bullet hell without the required clarity, The platforming challenges become about doing way-too-long strings of blind jumps under time pressure, with input delay and imprecise hurtboxes on spikes. The game demands precision from you, but doesn't give precision in return. Some concrete examples of issues with platforming precision:1. Wall jumping regularly fails. You touch the wall but do not grab on, resulting in falling.2. Grabbing a wall instantly starts a slide. There should be a moment you grab the wall where you stop moving completely, before starting to slide.3. Firing an arrow off the wall shouldn't require holding B to not move. You should stay stuck to the wall by default.4. Dashing while on a wall, holding towards the wall, dashes away from the wall instead of in place.5. Teleport arrows do not teleport you instantly, which can result in you dying mid teleport animation from touching spikes.6. Jumping has a delay, and is sometimes arbitrarily locked out. There was one section in the underground fortress that requires you to attack a switch midair, and then double jump on top of a platform that appears. Your jump is locked out for a few frames after hitting the switch, so you have to do the double jump first. The order here should not matter.7. Aiming arrows without the gem upgrade that gives a line, on controller, is actually impossible, this should just be on by default and should not take up a gem slot.8. Following up from 7, trying to aim an arrow with a controller is extremely frustrating and just feels bugged. I think the direction is still being changed for a few frames after you fire it. Something doesn't feel right.Removing all the platforming with an easy mode isn't the correct fix. Just fix the damn platforming. In the 4th door of the Emperor challenges, I shouldn't have to do 10 maneuvers, most of them blind under time pressure, without a checkpoint. Even if I only fail each maneuver half of the time, I still have to do 2^10 attempts to clear the challenge. That is over 1000 attempts before I can reach a checkpoint. Again, assuming. That is way beyond proving mastery, and is just a test of player masochism. Putting a checkpoint half way through is 2^5+2^5 = 64 attempts, which seems more appropriate for a platforming challenge.Finally, some of the late game bosses are designed in a such a way that it feels like it requires luck in order to progress. Bosses have different attacks, and some of them have windows where you can do damage, and others have no windows where you basically run for your life until they are over. The issue is that the moves are random, and they can even use moves twice in a row. So one run you get a bunch of easy moves that let you do damage, and another run you get a string of 3 or 4 moves in a row, some of them immediately duplicated, where you do nothing but run for your life. Considering some of these moves have essentially unavoidable attacks, you will eventually get attrited out. A concrete example of what I am talking about is advanced cradle of light. The boss has an attack that randomly fires lasers across the screen, but there are also the following obstacles to avoid: electric saws that circle the stage, a very tiny bouncing particle, randomly respawning landmines that can explode the instant they respawn, and a tracking aoe missile launcher if you fail to kill it in the charge attack. Due to all of these hazards, you are continually put in situation where you have no choice but to take damage. I feel like a hitless run of this boss is 100% luck based.I so desperately want to recommend this game, but the design just falls apart. It is clear there was a lot of love and care put into this, but it was not play tested enough. The game is hard in a way that doesn't feel fair.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to love this game and I do conceptually, but in spots the game is just to hard. I'm not a fantastic player, but I've beaten many of the tough metroidvania games, including Hollow Knight. That being said, some of the boss battles, especially once you start getting about half way through the game are just too frustrating and unforgiving. There are two seperate bosses that I had still not beaten after about 50 tries each and that's very frustrating. I don't know if it's the play mechanics, like dashing not being a way to avoid taking hits, or the limited number of health boosters that can be carried, or something else. You've got to pretty much be flawless to beat some of the bosses and that's a tall order when the battles sometimes go on for 5-10 minutes each. An enhancement that would really help a lot, and would probably be fairly simple to implement, is if the health vials would restore more than one spot on the health meter. I've sunk a lot of time in thus far (about 80 hours) and don't really want to give up, but I'm just about at that point. I know it's lame to say the game is just too hard, but that's really the long and the short of it for me. I don't want to give the game a thumbs down, but it's really hard to recommend to anyone that's just a novice gamer like myself.

_childDocuments_.review: I posted a really lengthy review but Steam lost it... so, thanks Steam. Unfortunately, I'll keep it short this time around.Look... the devs care a *lot* about this game, and you can see it in literally everything -- the visuals, the music, the story, the voice-acting... even the responses to negative feedback. They're invested in this passion project, and it shows.This game isn't necessarily for everyone, but it was made with particular types of players in mind. If you 'expect' to win, then 'noctis' mode isn't for you. It requires a lot of finger dexterity and creativity, but the adrenaline-rush is amazing and it's supremely satisfying to succeed. There are 3 key elements that I think trip up some players, and so I'll try to outline them so you can set expectations and make an informed decision:1. It's hard... the platforming challenges in 'noctis' mode are ridiculous (and ridiculously fun, provided you have the right attitude). Fortunately, you can play in 'aeterna' mode, which is more 'Symphony of the Night'esque, and better still, use 'aeterna' mode at any time if you begin to suffer from 'noctis' regret.2. It's huge... I felt like I was plopped into this amazing, gigantic world with little direction, and I loved it. I don't want this type of game to be overly structured or linear -- it rewards curiosity and doesn't care if you access an area earlier or later (with the exception of some places locked behind abilities). If you played Noita, it's nowhere near as directionless but that should have prepared you aplenty. I'm just fascinated everywhere I go, and part of the thrust is exploring. 3. It's hypnotic... the visuals are some of the best I've seen in a side-scrolling action platformer in a long time. They use both foreground and background elements to add a lot of depth. In some cases, those foreground elements can be distracting, especially if you let your guard down or are in a tight situation. You have to look at this as not so much an oversight but design intention. To put it simply, sometimes the obstruction is meant to be another layer of challenge. Use the force, lol. It's worked out for me so far. The beginning of the game was a little slow, IMO, but as soon as you defeat the first boss, the entire world opens up and you'll find yourself deeply invested. I haven't loved/hated a game this much since pre-2.0 Dead Cells, and I'm thoroughly addicted. I was thoroughly enraptured by The Tower of Light, and in fact, coincidentally, the last time I felt a simultaneous sense of awe and adrenaline since ascending the Ice Caverns in Dead Cells. Everything from the music to the craziness to the layout... *chef's kiss* perfection!Seriously, originally needs to be rewarded, and it's tragic that this isn't better known yet. I've been telling everyone I know who might be interested about it. You're not paying for a game to auto-win; you're paying for an experience and these devs deliver. I'd love to see this take off so that they can continue to pour their hearts into it (and they're generously response to feedback). I'm certainly not ready to be done exploring this beautiful, deadly place. Thanks devs! This is exactly my speed of game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have enough space to fit all my thoughts cohesively, so, lists:Presentation:* The visuals are beautiful* The music is beautiful* For the most part, not too graphically busy - only exception is The Undersea Kingdom, which is an absolutely nightmare, and some effects during boss fights - in particular the light bullet in the Cradle of Light AI fight is nearly impossible to track with how much is going on in that fight, and there are occasional issues that crop up* No indication or guide for what moves you have acquired & how to use them. I'm still not sure what an "Instant Recovery" is and there's probably other moves I just forgot.Level Design:* I appreciate that every area feels unique, albeit in some cases it can be detrimental - the light tower's giant laser kinda breaks its flow, the back-and-forthness of the undersea kingdom is frustrating, and trying to fight in End of the World or The Royal Staircase feels like a fools' errand with how sporadic platform placement is.* However, the Cosmos is just. No. Sorry, that's not how this works. Rotating the player's entire perspective, including aiming arrows... it's frustrating and not fun. And pressing left and moving right also feels bad. Tack on a few overly demanding platforming sections with the reversed/rotated controls and it's just a mess.* Overall, the game is less of a metroidvania and more of a platformer with occasional path branching, but areas are not very interconnected and exploration is generally restricted to going in a straight line; I personally don't have an issue with this but be aware of what you're getting into, is all I'm saying.Platforming:* The teleport arrow should not be 360 degree free movement. It feels awful. The teleport arrow generally feels awful. If the tip of it touches spikes at all, that's it, it's gone. Timing teleports can thus be a pain. Aiming anywhere other than straight forward feels bad. Precise angles are always a hassle. 360 control is fine for the combat arrow but the teleport arrow is just a completely botched mechanic that feels bad every time you're forced to use it.* I've noticed that the wallhang hitbox is slightly shorter than your active/dashing hitbox, meaning you can fall off a wall, dash, hit a corner, and then just die. * In general, hitboxes feel too big. The King has a heckin' fat hitbox, spike/instakill hitboxes always are point-by-point for the sprite and you can sometimes walk off a platform and insta-die to spikes (but not always!) I point to Celeste which secretly has super tiny hitboxes that makes its needle platforming permissable - here things tend to feel a bit too tight* Speaking of Celeste, no platforming lookahead for the really long platforming segments is kind of inexcusable in this day and age. Dying over and over because you can't predict what's coming feels bad* Falling into a dash always feels awful because of how fast you gain downward velocity - the cap is way, way too high for some of the platforming asked of you* In general I do like a lot of the rest of the platforming, though - jumping puzzles, sword bounces, dash timing, obstacle dodging, take away all the teleport arrow nonsense and I don't think I'd notice the issues as often or as glaringly. It's not the tightest or most creative platforming ever (there's a notable lack of level-based platforming gimmicks and the platforming can get a bit stale after a while as a result, but it mostly stays fun* Subsequently every area ends up feeling slightly too long/big, and this applies to the game as a whole - there's probably a much tighter but still sprawling RPG in here but it's hard not to get a bit sick of every area by the time you're done with them and the game is, like, HUGE...Combat:* Many enemies that are reasonable to deal with in isolation are a pain to deal with in groups, or on unstable platforming ground. Some enemies control way too much screen real-estate (the light circle enemies in the last area being the biggest offender* Move pool is very large but very few things feel stronger than basic attacks, especially when you get endgame gear. I used the scythe pretty heavily during the midgame (since it doesn't consume blood) but basically stopped using it outright by endgame, and while the spear saw a few uses, the katana, axe, and shuriken basically never saw the light of day after I first got them* Boss RNG is really egregious. Attacks don't tend to be balanced, some are easy to dodge but give you little to no opening, some take skill to dodge and give you and opening, some are easy to dodge and let you wail on bosses, some are hard to dodge with little to outright no chance to attack back, sometimes the RNG within attacks can be way worse than other times. Bosses are allowed to reuse a move after only one other move in between so any boss with 2 bad moves can basically lock you out of attacking for a good chunk of time* Also, the Undersea Kingdom AI boss. Just. Sometimes it goes into Death mode after only one cycle and if the boss enters Death mode there's literally no reason to not just reset and try again, it takes like a minute, you get no chance to attack and the boss can even heal. Worse single attack in the game, literally not worth dealing with. You have to fight this thing twice to 100%, too* There are bosses I do like, most of them -feel- good to learn and get better at, but the inherent unfairness of some of them kind of ruins them for me. They're a good challenge though* By endgame sword builds become unviable against bosses, where arrow builds not only out-DPS sword but don't require you to get close to bosses who are often cluttering the screen with tons of nonsense; compounded with the RNG issues above. For the Emperor I'm fine with it but for the last two story bosses I felt a little bad arrow-cheesing them to oblivion... but it worked, so.General* Difficulty curve mostly feels good for the first half, slowly ramping up to match the player's expected skill level; once you reach End of the World I feel like the difficulty hits its upper cap and never really ascends past that, just finds different ways to be mildly annoying* Generally any platforming with moving saws/objects feels bad as they move too fast and have huge hitboxes; not super common but enough that it's noticeable and annoying* Until recently, there was a huge performance issue in the Infinite Sea that made me stop playing the game for over four months until it was patched; this made the aforementioned lack of a skills/controls list even worse* The story is a bit basic, technically ends on a cliffhanger, and even what did happen I'm not sure quite how to parse... the attempts at lore are alright but the game never really feels like a "world" so much as a sequence of platforming levels, every area "feels" different but I wouldn't say they have much "atmosphere"?* Some really long animations for a few things like save point warping, elevators, the train, oh god the train, boss start-up cutscenes... cutscenes pre-boss are skipped on refight, thankfully, but the animations are not and it can get gruelingConclusion:The scope of the game is really impressive and there's a lot of good to be found in both the platforming and bosses, but it's also... unpolished, in a few key areas, and over such a long game, that lack of polish can really wear you down. I can't say I fully loved my time with this game, but I enjoyed a lot of it, and I was motivated to keep pushing through to 100% completion more out of stubbornness than anything. If you want a huge, challenging action platformer (only kind of a metroidvania) then you'll get it, but this absolutely will not be for most people and it's far from the best version of itself regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a precision platformer Metroidvania with a high level of challenge. If that sounds appealing to you then you'll probably like this game despite its issues - most of the negative reviews are from the launch window when the game had some major problems that were patched in the first month (e.g. unintuitive jumping controls and too few fast travel points). The devs also added an easier difficulty mode that heavily simplifies the platforming, and you can change the difficulty at any time if there's a single part that is really frustrating you.The game is very challenging but it is also extremely generous with checkpoints, and you respawn pretty much instantly after hitting a spike or dying. It starts out pretty simple by precision platformer standards but it gradually ramps up over the course of the game as you learn new abilities, ending up extremely difficult by the last few areas. The game does a good job of keeping the challenge level high without resorting to Kaizo BS or requiring pixel-perfect precision. It does copy the annoying collect-your-soul-after-you-die mechanic from Hollow Knight but it ends up not really being a big deal due to the numerous checkpoints. The game looks great visually, aside from the player character's idle animation which looks ridiculous. What is he even supposed to be doing in that animation? The graphics are hand-drawn and look much better than the graphics in many other indie games. The main negative with the graphics is that one or two areas can be very graphically noisy which can make it hard to tell what is part of the foreground and what is part of the background.Combat isn't really the focus outside of boss fights but it gets the job done, although enemy variety is a bit lacking. The boss fights are very good; they're difficult but as long as you take advantage of your entire moveset they don't feel unfair. Some bosses are much easier or harder depending on your skill point allocation but thankfully the game lets you respec your build at any fast travel point so there's no risk of permanently screwing yourself over. If anything you're encouraged to frequently change up your build as needed to deal with the challenges that you're facing.I do think the game is a little too long. Each area has distinct level design and challenges which is great, but many areas feel like they're a little too dragged out. I think the game would have been better overall if it kept all the same areas but compressed them to be like 30% smaller. I just reached the final area at 27 hours in-game time with 79% completion and that's apparently a moderately fast pace, with many people taking 40-50 hours just to finish the game and 65+ hours for 100%. (edit: Finished the game in just under 30 hours with 84%, took a bit over 36 hours to get up to 100%. Fair to say that your playtime will vary a lot depending on how much you struggle with the platforming.)The game could also use a few additional quality of life features, a big one being some way to view the details of the items you've collected. There's a progression screen that shows what you've found but you can't view the details of what anything does, and there's no way to view what key/quest items you've collected (although there is a quest log that serves sort of the same purpose).Lastly, this is pretty minor, but the game could use a new English translation. The existing translation is serviceable but there are tons of lines that sound very unnatural to a native English speaker, like it was translated fairly literally from its original language (which I'm assuming is Spanish based on the developers being Spanish).Overall this is definitely not a game for everyone, even with the easier difficulty mode, but if you're part of the intended audience of people who like both precision platformers and Metroidvanias then I definitely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Having an absolute blast so far! The closest comparison I can make to other titles is that Aeterna has the atmosphere and combat of Hollow Knight and the platforming of Celeste :) this game has two difficulty settings: Aeterna mode, which is light on platforming, and Noctis mode which is an intense platforming experience. Luckily for me, a platforming-heavy metroidvania is exactly what I've been looking for, so I've been playing on Noctis mode!!It must be pointed out that this game is gorgeous! The visuals are stunning and the soundtrack is fantastic. Combat is somewhat simplistic so far, but feels responsive and appears to have a good progression lined up. Enemies are designed and placed with intent, and the two bosses I've fought were excellent. The bosses each had a limited set of moves which were highly telegraphed, yet kept the fight fast-paced and required some platforming maneuvers in the heat of the action. As of this writing, I just beat my second boss (in the tower) and my god, the entire sequence leading up to the fight and the fight itself were so well done! The platforming requires patience and good timing but has yet to become frustrating. There have certainly been some difficult moments, but these challenges always had a warm up before to ease you in. Furthermore, the checkpoints are very forgiving, which means that failures have never resulted in an unfair setback. The metroidvania aspect seems pretty solid so far, with a collection of routes to choose from at any time and clear ability-gated exploration.Can't wait to see what else this game has in store, it's shaping up to be absolutely massive.Edit 1: having now put in 6x the time since my initial review, I just wanted to update this to state that this game is an absolute masterpiece and exemplifies everything I love about metroidvanias and platformers. It's a real treat. Will plan to update this review after getting 100%.Edit 2: having now achieved 100% completion, I stand by what I said. This game is a masterpiece. Rarely have I been so enthralled by a game and emotionally invested in its success. There's so much I could go on about, but here are the main takeaways. (1) The world of Aeterna is incredible. It's huge, with extremely diverse areas that really make you feel like you're on an epic adventure as a larger-than-life being. Each area has a meticulously-crafted atmosphere, from detailed assets to beautiful soundtracks. The soundtrack might be my favourite of all time, and I listen to it regularly outside of the game. (2) The level design and movement abilities are a platforming fan's dream (Noctis mode). I was constantly amazed at how fun the puzzles were to figure out and execute on. The  is absolutely genius, including the way that boss fights were designed around it. The  is also one of the most unique areas I've ever come across in a game (took some getting used to, but once I got used to it it was so damn cool). (3) Like I just said, the bosses were built around the game's mechanics so cleverly. You will not find boss fights like this in any other game that I know of. The boss quality is just off the charts, and although many were quite difficult, they rarely felt unfair and they all seem possible to master. As soon as I achieved full completion today, I immediately started another playthrough and started working on hitless achievements. I don't know how far I'll go with trying those, but they definitely seem possible and I'm looking forward to re-battling some of my favourite bosses again!Hats off to you, Aeternum Game Studios :) Looking forward to DLC and Summum Aeterna!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I love all difficult games, especially those of the platforming and metroidvania variety. This game includes numerous abilities which I adore that boost navigation around the map, such as magic arrows, dash, double jump and wall jump, as well as many weapons to improve combat such as a scythe, katana and sword. The abilities included within the skill tree do an excellent job of making the player feel powerful over time by adding a new twist on attacks, as well as the three trinkets the player can carry to provide bonus stats which compliment these abilities. The combat of this game feels fluid and satisfying, despite being slow at the start. I enjoy the blood mechanic of this game, as it prevents the player from spamming powerful attacks and is quite balanced. The player must regain their blood supply in order to perform specific attacks or to heal themselves. The player is also given a rechargable shield that provides them with brief invincibility frames. This game has an experience mechanic, where the player is capable of losing their soul in the last place they died (like dark souls.) They are also capable of resting at thrones to regain health, equip new items and to also level up. It does not take an extremely long time to level up according to the game's length (approx 50 hours for full completion). The player is capable of reaching the level cap before defeating the final boss and even then, they are in for a difficult time. The world variety in this game is astonishing, as each world is different from the last. My favourite worlds in this game were the cosmos, mother ship and goblin mines, as I had favoured the dialogue, aesthetic and enemy variety of these places. From robots, to goblins, to dark matter worms or space guardians.  I also happen to adore the main character's personality and sense of humour when he does talk, which is quite often. If I had to describe this game by comparing it to other games, I would say that this is a perfect mix between Super meat boy and Hollow Knight in the best way possible. The only negative criticism I can think of is the use of the teleporting arrow in the cosmos. The gimmick of this world is that the player can run and jump around from planet to planet, teleporting over to each as they stand upside down. My main issue is that aiming controls reverse according to the players angle and do not respond to user input in the ways that I wish reliably. I do think something such as player tips on the loading screen could help the player base tremendously in regards to this issue. Despite this, I happen to like the fact that this game doesn't hold your hand and teach you everything. This game was a solid experience to be had, and I have not even completed it yet. As a final note, I enjoy the colour palette and music of this game quite a lot. I have found that most bosses in this game are challenging, distinct and enjoyable in their own ways. Final rating for me is 9.2/10
