_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write up reviews for the games I play, but this game now holds a special place in my heart. after 30 hours or so I started playing hollow knight (now 7 hours in) just to compare both games, and I have to say that Aeterna Noctis is better in my view. The only thing that keeps it from greatness, is the main character's design, the main menu interface, which can sometimes appear not so instinctive, and some other minor design choices, but other than that, the game is a masterpiece. I'm so sad it's not getting the recognition it deserves. I understand that most likely the developers didn't go for a more charming main character, while running the risk of the game looking too much like hollow knight. But this risk would've been worth it in my opinion. I will list a number of things this game does better than hollow knight: 1. Bosses- these bosses are a treat and a delight. The way each stage prepares you for the final confrontation with a boss just feels so good. It's as if each staged worked as a narrative leading you to the final act and well prepared. 2. Variety of scenarios. The variety of levels makes things feel fresh and not so dull like in hollow knight. 3. Enemies are intriguing and their difficulty doesn't seem mindless but makes sense when you realize that they prepare you for the final boss on each stage. 4. Platforming is amazing! and doesn't feel to me, that it affects exploration. I believe the platforming in AE adds to the exploration. 5. Difficulty is sweet and rewarding. I haven't played a game where I devoted 40 hours in a long time. Only Mass Effect, Tekken 7, and Resident Evil 2 have had me submerged. When I started Hollow knight the first time I quit 5 hours into the game. This game has made me want to play hollow knight. 6. Mystique. This game has a mystique I can't explain, it is beautiful in a way that makes you sad that the main character is not more charismatic. If the game had a charismatic character like Ori, Shovel Knight, Alucard or Hollow knight, the game would stand as the gratest. Hopefully developers could improve on the character and the silly swaying when standing still. Or at least the avatar durinng dialogues. All in all, it's a masterpiece. I only wish they sell many games so they can capitalize on the mistakes made and create something even better. If they do, they will have created the best metroidvania ever. Congrats!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a hidden gem. I had never heard of it before and was looking for some nice metroidvania game after I finished Batbarian (I really recommend that one by the way). So I stumbled upon this one, reading few reviews that praise the game, some with more than 50 hours in the game. That's a lot for a metroidvania.So I bought it, and you know what? It's awesome.  At first I thought the game was pretty easy actually, but at around 24-25 hour mark the difficulty ramps up, and now after playing for five days I need to take a break.  However I grew up in NES/SNES era and I like to complete games as they are intended, no matter how hard they might be. So how hard does it get? Well take Batbarian optional areas, mash them with Guacamelee! hardest parts and up the difficulty about 20-25%. It's actually quite amazing how they managed to get to that point that getting from checkpoint to another makes you feel like a superhuman. It's also nerve wrecking and if you are like me and like to spend your days off from work just playing something for six to eight hours, it's taxing as hell. Now don't let what I've said this far scare you off, as this might be the best metroidvania ever made. The music is awesome, story is interesting, the world is literally  and it's most likely the largest metroidvania ever made. The art is truly beautiful and even though the world is so big, I don't think anything is copy/pasted. It even has RPG system, quests and you can reset your skill tree if you want and try different builds.It truly is a love letter to metroidvanias. It's like the developers took all the good parts from other games and thought "Yeah, we can improve that a little". Overall I really recommend the game, it's well worth the 30€ price. Oh and by the way, I have not finished the game yet, I think it takes over 60 hours to finish this beast.

_childDocuments_.review: I was sitting around bored, an thought "yea, I didn't like it before (Jan. 2021), but maybe I should give Aeterna Noctis another chance". And I'm glad I did.WHILE I STILL HATE AND THINK THE BOSSES THAT YOU'RE REQUIRED TO PLATFORM UP TO IN A TIGHT TIME FRAME TO EVEN HIT (MAKING FOR FRUSTRATING AND NEAR INACCESSIBILITY IF YOU HAVE A DEXTERITY PROBLEM, WHETHER FROM AGE OR DISABILITY) ARE DUMB......... behind that I saw a really fun Soulsvania game.Do not get me wrong: some of the platforming, even on Aeterna mode, will make you curse up a storm, but it fills you with the type of rage that turns to elation as soon as you conquer it.The combat, only the bosses really presented a challenge. I did play on Noctis mode, sure, but I can't imagine normal enemies would be that much worse for a Souls veteran.The good:GORGEOUS visualsRapid fire gameplayI LOVE that there are two modes (I've seen normal and hard affect enemies, but I don't think I've ever seen a game make platforming have an easy and hard mode)Personal: an early double jump gem (after the sword boss. Go find it and make the platforming 100% easier)Personal: I appreciate how close together checkpoints are (don't know if that is only Aeterna mode or not)The badPersonal: I wish the map didn't break up like it does between roomsI owe these devs an apology for anyone influenced by my previous negative review.This is a frustratingly fun Soulsvania.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a few hours in and loving it. The movement is crisp, which is probably the main thing I look for in a Metroidvania. The combat flows smoothly. The art style (especially the level design) is very nice and gives Hollow Knight vibes. There seem to be tons of collectibles and a huge map.The main complaints I hear about the game are:1 - unresponsive inputs: this is simply not true to me. The controls are very tight. I think what people are really complaining about is the lack of a buffer mechanic, which is a fair but different point.2 - difficulty. The game is definitely harder than your average Metroidvania. However, I'm greatly enjoying the challenge and none of it has felt unfair up to now. Luckily the devs put plenty of checkpoints in, which means that, even if you fail a jump, you will be able to retry the challenge with minimal backtracking (if any).3 - visual clutter. I have to say that this is sometimes a valid point. In some cases I have had troubles recognizing hazards and distinguishing platforms from the background. The main difficulty for now has been telling apart "solid" platforms from platforms you can drop through. However, for me the good outweighs the bad.In summary, I would recomment Aeterna Noctis if you are looking for a Metroidvania with a distinctive art style, challenging platforming and smooth combat.

_childDocuments_.review: My original review at about 20-30 hours in is below.  I put another 50-60 hours in afterwards and 100%'d the game, because it's that good.  I almost never bother to 100% a game.  It's that good.  The devs listen and have made some great changes since then.  Boss rush mode/pantheon type thing is hopefully coming soon.  I can't recommend this game enough.  Yes, half of the game is path of pain on steroids.  Yes, you'll suffer.  Yes, you'll die 1000 times.  Yes, it's worth it.  Original early review: I'm about half way through and so far it's a great metroidvania, very similar to Hollow Knight, but with a major focus on difficult platforming. Tower of Light was a very steep difficulty jump which I feel could have been better placed later in the game, but aside from that everything has been pretty good.  Combat is tight and feels good, but relatively shallow. Some of the weapons (axe) are kind of useless compared to the scythe, since the axe costs blood and the scythe gives you blood, but the axe doesn't do that much more damage.  Spear is okay, situational at best.  Haven't gotten everything else yet though.Everything feels mostly fair so far, but there are some bugs here and there that are frustrating, like double jump not working off of a wall sometimes, maybe 1 in 5 or 6 times?  It kept happening over and over again trying to do a specific sequence so I know it's not just me, I even recorded my inputs to see if I was jumping twice by mistake and I  wasn't.  Aiming the arrow can be.. annoying, and in my opinion the gem for the aiming line should just be there by default, or enabled in the menu.  It really turns aiming into an annoying timesink tbh. Speaking of timesinks, more teleport locations are desperately needed.  The ability you get that allows you to teleport back has to be bought (although once in awhile it will refill on it's own, but this has only happened twice in like 20+ hours), which means you can teleport back once or twice before it's spent, so backtracking requires covering a lot of ground you otherwise wouldn't really want to cover.  It gets better with more movement abilities, but early game it can be especially frustrating feeling stuck and lost in a specific location, with no real way to port back out.  Overall it's probably the best MV this year, but the platforming is very extreme, so if that isn't your thing (I personally like the challenge), then this is probably not the game for you.  It isn't overly difficult in my opinion, but does require practice and can feel tedious if you make mistakes.  That said, there are enough checkpoints to allow you to reset close to the start of a platforming sequence, so it's not all bad, but again as I said before, I can see players who aren't great feeling very stuck in situations like these, especially since they will probably not have the ability to port out of the area they're stuck in.  If you liked Hollow Knight, definitely pick this up.edit: 100 hours later, easily in my top 3 MVs of all time. Absolutely incredible game.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal. I had already played and enjoyed the demo previously, so when it released I've been playing it pretty much nonstop despite the buttkicking I received. The early gameplay feels a tad basic but once you get more weapons and abilities(particularly the teleport arrow) it really starts to shine. The game picked up for me once I got the Light Tower, where the regular enemies started feeling like more of a threat and the platforming started to get harder.The platforming is probably what caused me the most deaths, and I imagine I did most of the difficult platforming sections in the game since I finished all ten stages in the Temple of the Kings. Some of the bosses felt pretty difficult, but you can get so powerful at certain points in the game that the upgrades felt a bit broken. In a few cases when I had plenty of health I could just button mash the basic attack, and the extended invulnerability kept me safe to let me out-DPS the boss.I thought the areas were the best looking parts of the game, probably better than a lot of the actual character and enemy designs. The soundtrack was nice at some parts but not super amazing. The VA didn't bother me but it seems to be a low point for a lot of people. I HIGHLY recommend this game if you love: Difficult platforming, exploration in Metroidvanias, and pretty challenging bosses. The devs are adding a new mode with less platforming, so if you're interested but unsure of purchasing maybe just wishlist it and wait to see how that is.Edit: If you're on the fence due to the difficulty the easier mode is out now!
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone that finds the controls weird or unresponsive should give the game a bit more time to get used to. The biggest complaints I've read are the jump feels weighty and you cant jump right as you hit the ground, but after playing a few hours these issues went away and now platforming and movement feel great.The game definitely plays like a difficult fan-game with tough platforming that requires pinpoint accuracy and a lot of trial and error. Whether or not that sounds amazing or irritating completely depends on your taste- but even if you're not into that a game-mode that makes platforming easier should be coming out soon.Enemies actually feel like a threat especially later on because they really try to kill you or have challenging attacks, unlike Ender Lillies for example where many enemies just stand in place or have attacks you could dodge blindfolded. I've never been frustrated with the difficulty of the game because checkpoints are placed at basically every new platforming section or boss, so it's never a slog to get back to where you were.The hand-drawn visuals are very pretty and the soundtrack fits well with areas. One thing that pleasantly surprised me is boss fights so far have all been pretty creative and often require you to use power-ups you've acquired leading up to them. Exploration is definitely rewarded and there are a lot of secrets, and so far I've found at least one throne (fast travel) per area so it doesn't take long to backtrack.Only downsides I can think of so far are the level design early on is somewhat linear, but after the first few areas it opens up a lot, and the skill tree is nothing special. I also wish the dash cooldown was shown on screen but once you upgrade it a few times it basically has full uptime.Overall the game is a really well put-together and challenging metroidvania, probably the best that's come out this year. From what I've heard the game is actually pretty long so I'm excited to see what else it has to offer :)
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve been playing few hours and I have to say that those 2D designs, apparently done by hand, are really beautiful and gives the game a very attractive environment. For those who like to play Classic games with a Souls like touch this would be perfect for you. You might die few times trying to go trough certain areas so is not the typical easy game but neither too difficult as the more you keep trying the more it hooks you up as you are getting more powers along the way and grow stronger. It’s relatively easy to move between maps and you can always go back to discover new secrets. The story is quite interesting and the narratives in Japanese are actually very cool as the typical Japanese anime. I hope to see more games from these developers in the future, I believe they can do great things and even triple A games if they have the budget to do so. Companies like this should get more support from the Gamer community.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: The best metroidvania I've ever played, but it's also the most difficult. The controls are tight and they need to be for the precision that will be required of you. The map is beyond large, and the environments are beautiful. The music is great and fits the theme of the zones/bosses. A couple of the late game bosses are quite difficult to beat as melee. Overall though, this is an amazing game with a ton of love put into it. If you can handle the spirit crushing difficulty, you will find a real gem here.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about 25% completed (on my game save) after 13hrs and am absolutely loving this game. As far as Metroidvanias go, this checks all/most of the boxes. The grand scale of the game is amazing, if not a little daunting! The amount of sidetracking / branching opportunities while exploring will keep you busy for hours and is definitely not a linear experience. If you are not a fan of Super Meat Boy or Celeste type platforming, or if you find that type of difficult platforming too frustrating to play, then this game may not be for you. However, there are many, many checkpoints scattered throughout this game where it isn't very punishing for failing. Also, things like death spikes respawn you at the nearest platform you were on while only taking away one orb of health, so there are some trade-offs to the difficulty. I would highly recommend this title if you are currently on the fence for difficulty reasons.Edit: Typos.
_childDocuments_.name: Aeterna Noctis

_childDocuments_.review: Aeterna Noctis is a challenging 2D Metroidvania drawn by hand, with intense combats and skill-based platform sections. Taking the role of the 'King of Darkness' you must help him regain his power across 16 different and connected areas in an epic journey with environmental storytelling.

name: Welcome to ParadiZe
detailed_description: SUPPORTER EDITION About the Game Do you want your very own zombie companion? A faithful friend that protects you from its peers and accompanies you on all your adventures? At ParadiZe, we make it happen! Here, the zombies do all the dirty work. In the beautiful country of ParadiZe, ingenious survivors are testing a technology that can be used to control the zombies that have overrun the world. Once hacked, they become invaluable allies, even though they are not that smart and sometimes rather unstable. It's not all rosy in ParadiZe, but if you're reasonably clever and handy, maybe you'll manage to survive… Explore ParadiZe and meet a colourful cast of extraordinary characters. The unusual flora and fauna will surprise you at every turn. Set out on adventure, in the snow or desert, alone or with your Zombot companions, and feel free to get rid of any pests that try to disturb your stay with us. Fancy an expedition into the wilderness or would you prefer to laze about at your camp? It's your choice, so tailor your stay as you see fit! However, we recommend not getting too close to the locals: they can be somewhat… aggressive. Shortly after arriving, you must build your camp, a cosy little nest that you can gradually upgrade. Comfort is important, but don't forget to set up defences! Add multiple traps and fortifications to repel zombies, which have the bad habit of never leaving you alone. It takes effort to maintain a camp, but if you don't like such menial tasks, don't worry: as we already told you, zombies do all the dirty work here. You can be a loner during your stay or more sociable. Invite up to three of your friends so they can enjoy this unforgettable experience with you. ParadiZe welcomes everyone with open arms!

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be so fantastic, but unfortunately it's monotonous and boring and WAY too expensive for what it offers.(In my opinion it's worth a maximum of €20)Everything said in the trailer is just extremely exaggeratedYou CAN have multiple Zombots... 2 of them (after you progress in the main quest), that's all you get!!!!!With specific upgrades in the skill tree, your Zombots CAN have up to 2 Zombots each (so 6 total), BUT they're just dumb Zombots with no armor or weapons (these do almost no damage), so they're just useless and just meat shields.They are also very stupid and usually don't do what you want them to do. Pathfinding can be annoying in some places.There are buildings to build that in normal survival games are just chests and workbenches.They do work for you? You set up a beacon that requires energy to operate you have to produce first. So you can only build a very limited number of them since there are only three “fuel” points on the map, these are just wooden sticks that you burn for energy. Set how many Zombots have to work there, and then you never have to go back there again.The enemies are fun and some can be tough, but overall the game is so easy that there is no challenge at all, which makes it very boring very quickly. I play with the bow and can kill groups of 20 zombies without even getting hit and with no zombies protecting me, with ease.The fast travel spots are placed in strange places and result in a lot more "walking simulator" (or let's call it what it is) "content stretching" than necessary (which also makes it more boring quicker).Weapon progression is not good at all. I still shoot almost every zombie with the bow.Some have to be killed in melee so I use a spear to fight them, but there aren't many that require you to fight in melee, all can be killed in ranged combat, some only have armor so you do less damage , so you COULD even play the whole game with just ranged combat.The auto aim is the worst of all, it makes the game so easy even my dog could play it.Not everything is bad, you will have at least a few hours of fun playing this game.The biggest problem I have is that it's a finished product (so not early access), so I'm afraid there will only be small hotfixes and no major changes. I hope I'm wrong about that.Because in its current state I can't recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta say I was pretty intrigued with the hack and slash style of gameplay for the first 30 minutes. Getting a zombie minon to help mow down hordes was pretty fun too, especially with my coop partner. The game then introduced camp building and pylons which was the peak of excitement for me. Unfortunately it all went downhill after that. I think the game has a really neat idea, and tries to bring a lot of cool mechanics to the table. However most of those mechanics are short sighted, and lacking the depth needed to make them fully enjoyable. Ill start with what the game does well.Hack and slash combat. This game does the mindless combat where you can do silly combinations of things with your minions and partner really well. This doubles down when done as coop. Though I think any more than 2 and the game would become too trivial. Unless the game spawns in zombies per player then that could get bonkers at points. Combat was a 5/5 for meRPG elements. The skill trees offered are simple, but neat. I opted for full zombot control while my partner dabbled across all three skill trees. It really didnt feel like our playstyles were directed much by the leveling paths we took up until I had 6 zombie minions to her 2. I would say the RPG elements are a 3/5Tactical/strategy elements. For this I basically just mean the zombot control with a tiny lean into base mechanics. The zombot's were an exciting thing to me. I was in LOVE with Pikmin, and Overlord, and the idea of controlling zombies to do my bidding and keep me safe in the apocalypse was mouth watering. When it got down to it though, I was pretty bummed. Being limited to 1 zombot for about 50% of the game limited my options of tactics, meaning I just had to smack and shoot as much as my partner despite having all my points into my zombies. The zombots have neat automation triggers for in or out of combat, but fine control of them is nonexistant. Once I got to my second zombot, and they controlled two of their own zombots each it started to get quite funny. I didnt have to hack and slash much any more, but that is more because we had 4 zombots with flamethrowers and had very little to do with my extra zombies. A negative side note to the base part of this is the game takes the time to teach you how to capture your zombie, then as soon as you build a camp the pylons can just spawn in up to 9 infinitely. I would have much rather had to go collect each zombie I wanted to control and then leave them at the base. Tactics/Strategy elements were a 1/5 for me in this gameSurvival elements. I have very little to say here. Crafting outside of bandages and ammo is basically nonexistant. You can make weapons, but the combat is so spammy and simple that the differences came down to if it was aoe or not and if the damage was high enough to one shot. I just crafted the ranged weapon with the biggest numbers and found a spear and never looked back. Survival elements are a 2/5.Base building. Awful and pointless. Unclear and wonky hitboxes mean base spacing is inconsistent. There really seems like there is no point with only 1 trap and wall type up to the halfway point of the game. There is really no need to have a camp, not even for your crafting needs because you rarely need to craft, and it could have just been a shop or npc you did it at instead. The prebuilt camps you can fight are built in a way more effective and compact way, making your base feel even worse. It fully feels like it was added just for the purpose of saying it is there and that is it. Having said all that, I am entering the part of the game where you are required to defend your base from zombies, (chapter 4) so maybe the next hour or two will change my mind. As of now Base building is 0/5Overall the game is not worth what I paid for it ($25). I could see it being a great get at $15 maybe even $20 if you can couch coop or remote play it with a friend. Solo, or if you each have to buy a copy I wouldnt spend more than $10 on it. Especially since they have over 5 cosmetic microtransactions already. This game is a fun little lighthearted couch game to play, I could see kids especially enjoying it with how simple it is.

_childDocuments_.review: I just don't agree with the negative reviews being posted at all. I'm loving every moment of the game so far, and can't wait to play it co-op with people. The humor is on point, the base building isn't extensive, but it serves the purpose it is there for very well. I'm loving the "light" survival crafting feel of it.No stupid fiddly little meters to keep happy, no boring weapon durability, just you, your zombie bros, and a stick vs the world. I don't regret the money spent at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Keep in mind, this is for a single player, I have not played Co-op so I can't comment on that. I very much enjoyed my time in How to survive 1, I finished that game at least twice, but not so much on How to survive 2, but it was OKish... now Welcome to ParadiZe... I was waiting for this as I liked how it looked, it is very much my type of game, so I pre-ordered. Day of release, I had my beer ready, after work, time to relax! I open the game and at first launch the game felt very nice, looked great, played great, fought zombies, started the story and I was feeling good about this game! fast forward 12 hours in game later and well the truth is that the game is just very boring, the only gimmick is that you can kinda control zombies, but trust me, that wears off very quick! the game is full of these tiny things that irritate you in the worst kinda way, you can sometimes clip over some walls by rolling, but you can't get out unless you destroy the wall, the animations of the cut scenes are just horrible, I don't care much about that in particular, but I do hate that I cannot fast forward the dialog, either you watch the whole cut scene or skip it completely, if you choose to watch the cut scene, then sometimes the characters stop talking for a few seconds... then they continue, but you don't fully know if the dialog is over so you end up skipping half of the dialog scenes, not that it matters, the story is just plain simple, there is no meat and no real interest to find out about it other than to continue with the same missions as the missions all seem to be the exact same with minor variations, the enemy variation is meh at best, I have fought only 2 bosses, and they were as easy as they come they were more of a nuance than a real fight. The game feels easy and there is no way to change difficulty, most of the times I've died is because of stupid mistakes by me. The UI looks nice, but its very cumbersome to use. Building is VERY limited, it seems they want this to be part of the endgame, I guess for some reason they think people will keep playing the horde mini game after they complete the game? There is absolutely no survival elements present, the food and water just give you some healing and some of them status effects, but they are absolutely not necessary.  I am not sure if I have it in me to finish this game, but if I do and something changes my mind I will edit this comment. Maybe they should have not wasted so much time trying to create day 1 cosmetic DLC  and focused on QOL improvements

_childDocuments_.review: i'm always kinda baffeld nowadays by the expectations people got; there's no other explanation for some of the reviews on steam atleast. it's a very fun, cute, little top down arpg. it's not a survival, Ark or whatnot zombie game, no Project Z, etc. . you control your mc from a fixed top down perspective, do action combat (quite good actualy), with a wide variety of melee and ranged weapons, you find and craft new gear (armor, weapons) and build (very basic) a little base and ressource extractors to partake (later on) in some basic base def. the main focus of the game is the exploration, combat and power progression. and it clicks after a while. it's fun to explore rare corners of the map to find some unique (looking aswell) armor piece, or some lore (tongue and cheek). it's quite fun to mow down hordes of zombies and collect the drops afterwards (crafting mats mostly). this cycle worked in many other games aswell..nothing new on this front, but what is here is very competent. the "twist" or what makes it kinda special are your zombots. think A.I. controlled drones, just...well zombies. you can capture one early on and use him as your companion. in a basic menu you can equip him/her to serve specific funtions and you get a wide variety of on/off A.I. commands, like to collect in and/or out of combat or to heal you or to taunt, etc. then you discover the "expert"-mode and realise that you can do even more to adjust your zombie drone. you will get more, i think it's 2 later on. thanks to the ingame skill tree these zombie drones can also "hack" (control) their very own zombie drones. which is just fun. it's a fantastic little feature. beeing it the wobbly zombie animations or em running around to collect some leaves for you...it's endearing. similiarly you can build seperate pylons which can control up to 3 zombots for you. these can serve as a base-patrol-defense, they can work as ressource extractors (to collect wood for your generator for example).there are some minor pathing issues but apart from that i have had a lot of fun with this system and i still think it's a great addition.it's pretty telling that the skill-tree is mostly power-ups (and modified new funtions) for your zombots and not your mc. your own toon gets stronger via gear. which can also be upcrafted. like finding a basic pumpgun to get it to a very rare or legendary status later on, which means more damage basicaly. or by equiping new armor to get higher def. technicaly the game isn't Starfield or Cyberpunk but it's nice to look at and ran pretty well on my rig (RTX 3070, i913, 32GB, HDD). about the only technical issue i got is when starting or closing the game, perhaps it's because i got it sitting on an HDD, but there's always a very long black screen (long enough that i think the game crashed everytime). but ingame there's basicaly no loading. it's weird to be sure. my HDD is pretty fast, playing something like Rogue Trader and the loading times are seconds, here it can take a min? but that's the only technical issue i found.no one cares about the story in these games. but it's kinda here. again very tongue and cheek. some memorable characters, like the nurse (probably in name only) Mary, some not quite hitting jokes about popular figures in real life. the dialogue and great, it ain't terrible either. npc models are a bit sketchy. but again: who plays these games for the plot.the major isssue i got is the balancing. there's some work to be done here. escort mission are a mess, the npcs you escort pretty much die instantly, which leads to a restart of said mission. you can kinda work around this by clearing the path beforehand...but that's just not great design.and the base defense missions later on are just plain terrible. doesn't matter much how strong you build your base or the defenses: it's to many enemies and to strong ones. there's whole guides already on how to cheese these missions, cause doing em normaly is beyond frustrating. bottom line: balance needs patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the other zombie top down games these guys made, pretty interesting but nothing earth shattering. For some reason I guess adding an empty world with the same 4 things to do is worth making another game. $30 is way too much, maybe if it was early access but as it stands its a pass. _childDocuments_.review: Everything is OK'ish. It is at least worth it on sale.Story: It is a little shaky. Seems not so polished, because they continue to animate and have you waiting after the dialog is done. Nothing worthy to remember.Co-op: Never played. Easy enough as it is.Combat: MINDLESSLY slaughtering with button mashing melee or ranged. There are mods to zom-bots which are really the only thing keeping it interesting. Watch your HP drain if you try to melee a zom-bot with spike armor. You can also tweak some settings: when or what your zom-bot strapped with explosives suicides (Tip: they can blow up those metal walls you will run into... or actually them). Also, let your ranged weapon zone-in for that head shot.Base building: Kind of frustrating. You can't remove terrain. If they decided some low bushes are a no-pathing zone then you just need to deal with that. You can't remove trees and nor can your structures. It is ok, but games older have done better. Seems limited to just the forest. Just find a nice wide open area with little entrances to you. You don't need your base near water or wood, because the pylons (zom-bot spawners) can be anywhere on the map (in the forest).It is ok enough to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but it's not great. I was amused for a while, the humour was a nice touch and it's a fresh take on zombie survival. I laughed out loud when I hopped on the back of a zombie and rode him. Aesthetically, it's a good looking game and runs well but that's about all the positives I can think of.I haven't finished it but if there's something in my suggestions that's already in the game feel free to point it out and I'll change my review.The combat needs some more variety. Zombies should hit harder and getting swarmed should be dangerous but instead I'll voluntarily roll into a group and start swinging my bat knocking all the Zs around. Ranged combat felt nice at first. High velocity shots hitting with power that knock enemies around or make them fly if they die but once you realize that ranged weapons can take out groups in no time at all it just becomes a monotonous game of auto aim and fire while walking around. I'd like some skills to add to the weapons, maybe add modifiers to the ammos and weapons to do different things or add an extra skill or two to melee weapons. Blades (or sharpened blades for already bladed weapons) for some bleed chance or insta-decap chance, weights to knock Zs around, fire to set ablaze groups, shocking to electrocute and briefly stun, etc. A sprinting attack and two handed weapons with some ground attacks would be a welcome addition too think. I do love slamming around zombies with a sledgehammer or big axe. Speaking of axes, in the wood farming areas (stick spawners) there's an axe right there that you can't take. I was super disappointed. Then I was even more disappointed when I started building my base and the only tree in the middle of it is permanent and has a huge area around it where I can't build anything. Base building feels so restrictive when it comes to building around existing pieces of the world. I understand not being able to cut down trees on the borders of the paths but let us cut down the solo trees for some extra wood, sticks and leaves. Setting up material farms is pretty lackluster too. They take up power from your generator, you choose how many Zs to spawn, you give them a couple commands and never come back. Let us have to to give the Zombots axes to smack around trees instead of having them eternally pick up sticks, or have us have to set up defenses or walls for them to help them defend against small hordes or something.Zombots are a unique mechanic but not very deep. I have no attachment to my zombie companion. Why bother with wasting a skill on being able to revive them when I have 50 more helmets in my inventory. What else am I going to do with that 2000 scrap and 150 broken helmets? They should be given a random name (so we can bond with these lovely beings) and they should level up separately from me, though have them level faster and have a low max level so you don't feel gated into having to keep them. Maybe two types of helmets that pick between our current limited Z or a levelable companion, the latter being a lot more resource intensive to make. Just something to make us choose between wanting to have an actual companion or a disposable self-destructing meat sack that will run into hordes with spiky armour. Maybe give them a small set of skill points and move my skills that boost their skills into their own skill tree. So I can hack a zombie, give him a gun or machete and as he levels I can put points into levelling up his damage, attack speed, health/regen, or even give us the ability to make them a pack mule and add points to help them carry my junk. I'm also a bit disappointed that you don't really equip them with items from your inventory and if they die, the next zombie you hack immediately has the item and armour of the last one. Final complaint is more around the NPCs dialogue flow. Their animations are randomly looped and constantly played and make them feel like puppets instead of humans. Bob swinging around his arms opening and closing his laptop 20 times during our conversation was super weird and felt like a lazy design. NPCs need to be less animated during dialog and when they do animate it should be for emphasis or at least related to the context of the conversation.Overall, like I said it's not bad and definitely has great potential.I think was hoping for a bit more of a survival element than an this arcadey auto aim filled left click walking simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: You know what?  The game description didn't lie.  You do capture a zombie and have a companion (Eventually two.  Also they each get sub-zombies (and the sub-zombies don't equip anything), so ).  You do build a base and defend it (it's terrible!).  You do explore the wilderness (a lot!).Talk about a rather boring and linear game.Capture one zombie to fight alongside you.  Collect a lot of garbage (wish this were faster/easier to do.  Mashing a button repeatedly for every item is very 2010), trash the garbage to get scrap, use scrap to build your base...!  Woah a base?  Yeah it's like five buildings.  Seriously.  This is the weakest base building in a zombie game, ever, it really shouldn't even be in the game.  Feels tacked on and not very well thought out.Anyway, run around the map, killing zombies non-stop because zombies, and ... that's the game.  Do fetch quests!  Do more fetch quests!  And of course, fetch quests!  Wowee!Welcome to Paradize is very repetitive and the gameplay loop is not even that fun.  It could use a lot of work improving itself to be a very good something, not a bunch of little things.  Want to be a base builder?  Improve this, a lot.  Want to be a squad leader?  Improve this, a lot.  Want to be a loot crazy action RPG?  Improve this, a lot.  It does none of these things well and makes the game a yawnfest.Welcome to Paradize is very braindead, literally.

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a review for Welcome to ParadiZe after playing it for 15 hours in one day. I had a bad experience playing it with bugs and just general repetitiveness and it's monotonous boring mechanics and features.Here I am, almost a year later to edit/change my review based upon the current version of the game - E.G many patch's later. Has my opinion improved? Would I recommend the game now? Well, below I will give a pros and cons with my opinion but first a small disclaimer!  ⚫So my first MAJOR issue with the game is how falsely advertised the trailers are. At the start of the game you could only have 2 zombots. MAIN ones and those 2 could have 2 minions with no weapons or armour, which each equals 6. That is not having "MULTIPLE zombots". You only have 2 that you can actually customise and are viable in combat.: The developer has made it now so you have 3 Zombots and each can have 2 equalling 9. Still not good enough.⚫The "half-buried trunks" are so tedious to remember if you have already dug them up and looted them as the icon on the map does not change when you have dug them up.⚫Another note about the point above, the same is said about locations. You can "RE-LOOT" chests and destroy camps you have already looted/destroyed meaning you wont know what part of armour you need for a set e.t.c.⚫I had a game breaking bug where my FOG-OF-WAR on my map would return over and over again forcing me to RE-EXPLORE all locations on my map.⚫Another note on the point above, when my map reset the FOG-OF-WAR it also reset all of my unlocked teleport locations and removed all of my found locations.⚫The "ZOMBOT" AI is atrocious. They get stuck on everything which shows TERRIBLE pathfinding. They refuse to fight at times and they refuse to listen to commands given at times also.⚫The building system could use a revamp. Sometimes it is VERY tedious to place items how you want to place them. Why not give us a grid view of the floor? Not only that most buildings are just plain and have a singular WORKBENCH to use.⚫Another note about building - you can place multiple objects, walls, traps e.t.c. If you have placed several defensive walls you cannot pick them up at the same time or destroy them at the same time. You need to manually go around them one by one to move or destroy them BUT when you need to repair everything you can REPAIR ALL at your main area (the tower)⚫There are only three areas for fuel in the game which is just zombots collecting STICKS for you. Why only three? Could you not have a COAL mine near the mine for zombies to harvest BETTER fuel?⚫The enemies in the game are WAY to east to kill which makes the game very boring, very quickly as it offers no challenge whatsoever to the player. You can sit back with a gun or bow and kill groups of 20+ without needing to panic.:  The developer has added in a new difficulty mode which is a bit harder but it still lacks a challenge.⚫Fast travel locations are placed in stupid areas to "STRETCH" the content of the game out. Let's be honest, that is exactly what the developer is doing here.⚫The weapon progression system is terrible. You will practically never use anything else but ranged weapons. Zombies do have defences such as sandbags on them - meaning you can only shoot them to kill (or spend a century melee'n them to death) or head armour which means you can only really damage with a melee weapon BUT you can still kill everything with only ranged weapons and the skills of increased ranged damage and stealth damage.: The new difficulty seems to make it a tad harder to kill everything with just ranged weapons which is a welcome addition.⚫Another note based on weapon progression - you get the next tier of weapon almost immediately into a NEW zone which makes upgrading EARLY pointless. The moment you can kill a zombie or 2 in a new zone, go, kill, collect, craft new weapon, repeat till game is complete.⚫The auto aim suffers so much in this game. You have to aim at a target manually with your mouse and if the target goes LOWER (like down a hill) your reticule target will cross out and you will miss, not only that if there are multiple targets running at you it will swap targets constantly. This got frustrating to much. The developer has still not fixed this.⚫It is classed as a "FINISHED PRODUCT" so if the developer want's to abandon the game, then they can without any hesitation.⚫The game is HEAVILY over-priced. Buy at a HEAVY discount. £10 or £6 I'd say. ⚫The ZOMBOTS can work for you making tedious tasks as - collecting water or burning sticks to produce power.⚫The combat was fun for the first half of the game. Learning the weapons was enjoyable!⚫The map is pretty large all accompanied with difficulty zones meaning you cannot just go anywhere you want to begin with.⚫: They have fixed the majority of crashing bugs and freezing issues. Since I came back to the game I did not freeze, crash, stutter e.t.c once. Before, I had a constant stutter and it occasionally crashed but now the game runs smoothly. So, I thinks it's safe to say that it's much more optimised now.⚫: The good ending of the game gives me hope for DLC or a possible sequel that has more variety in terms of content, better optimisation on launch, a better progression system e.t.c. Think what I am trying to say is this - the ending was satisfying enough for me to somewhat, want some sort of DLC or more content to drill into. All in all, I've waited almost a year for improvements. Optimisation. Content. Changes. Have we seen any of this? Yeah, some. The developers have listened a little but not about the right stuff. All they have done is added in "HARD" mode, some turrets and a 3rd ZOMBOT which we should have had at launch.I cannot recommend a game that is classed as "COMPLETE" when it is missing/lacking so much optimisation and content to justify it's price. If it was half of it's own price then yeah, maybe it would be a more positive review but for how slow and boring the game can become... just go buy How to Survive 2 instead. Trust me. In it's current state - It's a decent game but it has no soul of it's own. It's a tedious, monotonous, boring How 2 Survive (2) that is sadly behind on the times. It feels as if the game was slightly falsely advertised/over-exaggerated via the trailer and after playing it to 100% completion... I just cannot bring myself to recommend it over How to Survive 2.

_childDocuments_.review: You can have your own zombies and run rampart against other... things and zombies, yay!Lots of weapons, some with boom, some with wooosh and some with brrrrrrrt.The so called expert mode offers you the illusion of some smarter zombots, i mean, let's be honest, they're still braindead, right?Graphicwise it's not exactly oscar-worthy, but it gets the job done.The quests, well, let's just say it's the usual go there, kill them, find x.It can get a bit grindy here and there, but it's mostly fine, aside from getting armor sets, which can and will get grindy and frustrating.Bugs, well, they are there, although i haven't come across game-stoppers or other unbearable bugs, stuff tends to glitch through other objects, most of the time it's no biggie, sometimes though it can be more crucial stuff as quest items. I've fallen through the map, get stuck in objects and so on, i'm sure you know what i mean.The difficulty, something that makes a lot of players mad. Personally i've enjoyed the learning curve, but others not so much. Maybe the option to set up the difficulty for your liking would be an idea, although i think it would get too easy which in return would make the game just boring, but that's of course just me. YMMV. The game tends to get repetitive after the initial part. The bosses are too easy. (the waves leading up to them are another story)The building menu. Well, i dunno how to put it politely. It sucks. Whenever you try to build something you get no real indicator where you can build something, it's pure trial and error. Seeing as the base building is somewhat of a core element of the game this is a dealbreaker for a lot of people. The inventory (management) could use a general overhaul. You can't sort the base inventory, deleting stacks of items from your inventory is tedious at best. Speaking of inventory, items often (?) simply disappear/vanish, which isof course bad, even worse when it's something that you crafted with one of the harder to find ingredients.Crashes. A lot of people seems to encounter random crashes, some aren't even able to get into the game.Should you buy it? Well, it depends on what you're expecting from it. For around 20 bucks it's not exactly "cheap" per se, although still far away from a full price product. If you can deal with its quirks and if you're lucky and don't get any bugs, then it can be fun lil timewaster. Maybe give it a chance and see for yourself, there's still the option to get a refund if it's not your cup 'o tea.

Dying isn't punitive - you lose some XP, but can get it all back if you kill the zombie version of yourself where you died. I liked the story - it wasn't deep, but it was the right amount of campy for a zombie base building, tower defending, quest giving RPG.I had fun getting all the achievements and truly hope there is more DLC to come. _childDocuments_.review: It's my first time purchasing a game in Early Access and my first time writing a review in English, but I'll do my best to provide reasons to either buy or avoid this new zombies game, Welcome to ParadiZe.I've had a good time playing both the demo and the full game itself, so I believe I have a solid understanding of what players will encounter in the early stages of the game.Main gameplay mode it's like a campaign mode. So if you're solely interested in playing a survival mode akin to the zombies mode in the Call of Duty Series with friends, that option isn't available at first glance. I hope that the game evolves and then bring us more modes and more challenges. - Easy to play (either keyboard/mouse or joystick).- Unique and innovative approach.- Good translation - Many constructions and items.- RUN USING (O)/(B) IN JOYSTICK IT'S A PRETTY BAD CHOICE. I think that's the only complain about the controls itself. - Too easy in some moments. Except for a few instances, most of the time, the game feels a bit 'too easy.' It lacks the sense of 'desperation' and 'challenge' that other similar games, such as Project Zomboid and even 7 Days to Die, provide. I'll elaborate more on this in the 'Is it worth buying this game?' section.- Bad optimization. It's a joke that a game like this requires 12 GB of RAM and sporadically gives errors warning that 'The game will crash,' which are caused precisely by the lack of available RAM on the PC. This is clearly a serious mistake that needs to be fixed if the game wants to reach a large audience. Definitely, a game like this should not require 12 GB of RAM.So,I paid approximately 18 dollars and I genuinely believe that the game has a lot of potential. Considering its already robust structure and well-established physics and gameplay, that can worth the money if Nacon doesn't abandon this game and creates new modes, maps, etc. (please create a Survival Mode for Multiplayer) This game has the potential to be one of the best ever made in the zombie genre.But, if they don't improve with more zombots to get and stronger zombies I really think that this game will be a big waste of potential. I believe in Nacon. Ps: I really thinks that they need to balance the early game. That needs to be harder. Just nerf the damage, put the max health character in 50 and it's done. And then enable more zombots

_childDocuments_.review: This a *soft* recommend... for now.Welcome to Paradize is the kind of game I see myself coming to when I don't feel like playing anything else. Mindless button mashing and killing zombies, that's about it. That's a lot less than I was hoping for out of this game when I first came across it.- The map is very expansive, but feels sort of lifeless beyond moving from objective to objective and the occasional enemy base.- The UI could be a little better. Some of the gun icons in the inventory look too similar, I find myself hovering over ever gun to determine whether is a pistol, rifle, etc. I'm sure with another 5+ hours they'd start to look a little different, but when I want to change weapons on the fly, it can be difficult, it cant take a second or two.               - Moving items from your personal inventory to your camp inventory could also be a lot better if I could just Shift + Click on the items I want to move.- Weapon upgrades. To me, it seems pretty silly to me that you have the ability to upgrade weapons that require XX level to use, when your character is currently below that level. It took me a solid minute, minute and half to figure out why it wouldn't let me equip my upgraded air rifle. Turns out, I was Level 14, and I couldn't equip that upgraded rifle until Level 15. Seems it would just make sense to lock those upgrades until the appropriate level is achieved.- Melee combat could be a bit better. With how the AI zombies move from time to time, your swings can be wildly mistimed and misplaced. I wish I had the ability to pivot my character mid-swing to adjust for that.Besides the few downsides, this is a fun game to just hop on and mash away at zombies. But as of right now, that's all I really see this game as: a time killer.Looking forward to seeing what QoL improvements come over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to own a pet zombie? How about multiple Zombies, how about a complete slave labor force of zombies to fight for you and do menial task? Well, stop because that's weird. This game isn't for you. You personally, the guy or girl or alien whose eyes are reading this comment right now. This game is not for you. It is a game for anyone but you. You the individual reading this comment from your phone, or carved in an apple, or sitting at your computer or standing on your desk in the middle of mars. Stop doing that, why are you even there. Jupiter is the planet that all the cool people visit. Mars is a big red dead desert. Jupiter has a big ass eternal hurricane, and its made up of different stages of hydrogen. its a big red hydrogen rusty looking planet full of cookies and kool-aid. Well, anyways it seems to be trying the go for a Borderlands-esque style humor, while also being a survival game. and for 25 or 33 dollars (at the time. dont blame me for inflation, or sales ending or starting resulting in this price being higher or lower than it was when I posted this comment.) You get a pretty decent experience.  Its like pokemon or Palworld, but not as detailed, meets diablo. It has that top down dungeony crawly look....but, you mostly dungeon crawl through Nature's Dungeon, The Forest. But, not the Forest from the game the Forest, or the Forest 2. Hold your horses. if you have some. if not, ill wait for you to go down to the local wally world and buy a horse. hurry though, we are all waiting. basically you can capture and collect Zombies, you can give them bling. It has some base building, i guess.. you can't build things brick by boring brick like in Minecraft, if you progress through the game, and get the resources you get a choice of pre-fabricated buildings that you can construct. The best experience is gaining back lost experience. Which, you probably will die. Probably because you do something stupid, or smart but the game slaps you around anyways.. This isn't dark souls though. or Elden Ring.  So, its not gonna slap you hard. just a light slapping. Youll be fine. so tl;dr - You make zombies your servants, and you survive. thats the gist here. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying the game is ok. I can't recommend it for more than $10 though. It was definitely released incomplete. They fell under the map, but they didn't die as under the map was still a walkable area? Since they didn't die falling through the map, like I had a few times, I ended up needing to release/capture zombies in order to not just leave them trapped/taking up a precious zombie slot. You will need to find a secure area for your base, and you'll be fine for the boss fights/zombie hordes. This isn't due to the fact that you're using an area that is better defended. It is due to the fact that the zombies will get stuck on the map, and sit there waiting for you to come kill them since a small piece of corner sticking out broke their brain. I also wish that I didn't have to be sprinting to step over a small walls/logs. It took me way too long to figure out how to get into buildings, because I forgot that you need to be sprinting to step over small obstacles.

_childDocuments_.review: The game makes sense for it's $30 price point. It's bigger than I thought it would be, and there are a lot of options for your zombies that you don't see right off, as the game opens up and you get more equipment for them that causes them to behave differently.You open up enough new stuff and areas to keep things interesting as you go, so it ended up being one of the few games that I actually finished.While the zombie skill line is definitely the most interesting, it feels a bit weak compared to what you can learn in the other lines.There is a skill respec, but I've seen a bug report claiming that using the skill respec makes you lose the extra skill points you picked up in side quests. I haven't verified that the bug exists, and if it does, I assume it will be fixed very soon, but for right now, you may want to watch to see the news around that little hiccup before using respec (I assume this part of the review will be outdated very soon, but it still felt like it should be mentioned).The base building really isn't very expansive, but you do eventually get more things to put in it. The better defenses don't come until you're extremely deep into the game, though. It's really more about what you can set and program your zombies to do, rather than the base and tower defense parts.The DLC is a bit overpriced, it should have just came with the game. If you're doing single player, you probably won't care to get it. If you really want to set yourself apart for co-op, then maybe it will be worth it to you.It doesn't really go super deep, and yet it's still a fun and compelling experience. I base game reviews on the value for their price, and it wouldn't feel like it was right if it was a full priced game, but at half the usual cost, it is well worth the experience for its price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't read the forums before I got it on a 3rd party key selling site and didn't realize that despite getting the supporter edition, I wouldn't be able to get the 48 hour early access and I'm sure plenty of others had similar issues if they also got a key from a 3rd party site. I still got all the cosmetics that came with it, so I don't really mind. I would've only had a couple hours to check it out before working all night until the game launched anyway. Granted, I've also only played a few hours so far and am only on the 2nd chapter of at least 5. From what I've seen so far, I like the focus being more on exploring and combat because as far as I know, that's the best way to keep leveling up and getting more skill points. It's not that the base building isn't appealing so much as I don't have much unlocked to build yet and am being encouraged thru quests to keep exploring and looting and fighting.The skill points are used to do things like increase your health or your zombots' health, damage, heal and replace them when fast traveling, give them different abilities, and other stuff. I'm trying to work towards making my zombot recruit another zombot to also fight for me and then you can level that ability up to make those zombots recruit yet another zombot each to roll with a whole crew. With how many different tools and weapons and combinations you can make with them, plus the different settings you can use to control how your zombots act in and out of combat-I don't know if you're being encouraged to change up your zombot's setup on the fly or if I just enjoy doing so.Anything you can equip on your zombot can be found on other zombots in the wild and is obtained by collecting a certain amount of it, then you just have it unlocked to swap onto your zombot(s) whenever you want. Things like spikes to damage enemies (or you if the enemies have it) when someone gets too close-or heavy armor to make them resistent to melee attacks, or a target to draw the enemy's fire leaving you free to make a more stealth based build if you wanted. As far as weapons, they can wield anything you can and extras of those items can be easily disassembled in your inventory for the parts used to make them. Once you make a weapon workshop at your base, you probably won't need the random weapons you find enemy zombots wielding anymore as you'll be able to relatively easily make and upgrade both a melee and ranged weapon.Speaking of weapons, you can equip any 2 at once, but your zombot can only have one weapon and one tool at a time. I have only been using melee with my zombot so I don't know if they need ammo for their ranged weapons like I do, but ammo is also easy/cheap to craft even if they end up needing that. If you don't need them heavily focused on combat, I recommend equipping the saddle to at least one of your zombots so you can ride it to get around the map faster and without using your stamina. If you do want them heavily focused on combat, you should keep in mind (at least for me for now) your zombots can only have up to 4 different commands toggled at once. I currently have mine set to collect resources outside combat, heal me both in and out of combat, plus use it's equipped item/weapon in combat, but I could set it to taunt enemies in and out of combat and not heal me at all but try to draw enemies away from me (combined with the target tool they can have, it's probably decently effective).As far as biomes/regions/the size of the map of the game world, I've only made it to the forest right outside the entrance you start at and the desert just north of it, but I haven't fully explored either biome/region fully. It looks like there's islands to the east of the main land mass I'm on and the map seems to be a pretty good size for a $30 indie game with some extra cosmetic dlc if you wanna fance up your zombots for some reason. There are also fast travel spots you can use to get around the map (and if you have that skill unlocked to heal/replace any hurt/killed zombots you had, they'll be spawned next to you when you fast travel) but in order to do that, you have to actually go to one in the game world and interact with it. You can't just pull up the map and fast travel-instead you'll just place a marker on the map you have to remove.As far as the base building goes, I don't have much experience yet with it in the game because I've only placed my shelter, the weapon workshop, a wood generator, another item needed to complete chapter 1, and a pylon to get free zombots to gather wood for me and also keep the generator stocked. I thought about putting up a wall segment or 2, but given the other stuff from the trailer I know I'll be able to craft later, I wanna wait in case I place it in a bad spot and block future buildable spots.I heard/read the level cap is 50 and with only a few hours under my belt and only being level 12, I'm excited to see more of this game but I wanted to make a review before too much time had passed cause I hope it doesn't just fly under people's radar with all the games that have come out recently or are coming out within the next month or so. Even if you don't plan on getting it now and waiting for another different sale, I recommend keeping an eye on it at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended with caveats. Good:(1) The humor/parody is great(2) Unique characters, Biomes, Weaponry, Tools, and Biome Gear. (3) Killing Zombies is fun. Bad: (1) Base Building is janky. It would be fine if you also didn't have to defend it. It become a nightmare late game to balance the weird power scaling and placement to defend against hundreds of zombies. (2) The pacing seems weird, and you'll notice this when you walk away from a new zone with 2/6 gear, missing other upgrade blue prints, and already moving to the next zone. To get the rest of the gear from a zone it is pure RNG. Good luck. All the gear and blueprints are RNG. You can get the same forever and never get what you need or want. In example, you want a Mythical X blue print, you have to farm a boss until it drops. That boss can drop the same one 10 times in a row before you manage to get the one you want. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a solid foundation that is unfortunately hindered by many bad and annoying gameplay decisions. I really enjoyed the start of the game and am also still enjoying doing side quests and continuing the main plot but for the love of god why am I forced to fortify my base against random zombie attacks that happen every 15 minutes? I think the base building might be a good addition for some but I myself only did what was needed as I am simply not interested in it. But now the game is  forcing me to "waste" my time on a game mechanic that is not fun to me.That not being the only issue. There are also many small things that simply make the experience more annoying instead of harder or immersive. For example the random storm that can happen in the desert, it makes you move slow and just annoys the player because you are simply slower. It adds no immersion or difficulty in any way. Like I said before, while the core gameplay is nothing special, it is a solid foundation and plainly shooting zombies, upgrading your skills and getting new stuff is fun and enjoyable. The skills aren't anything special but they do the job. If only the game wasn't plagued with bad and simply unenjoyable mechanics...Graphically the game looks decent and also runs well for me. My only gripe is the forced TAA that introduces extreme ghosting and just smears everything over the screen.My review might change as I continue playing the game but for now I have to consider to even continue playing it because games should be fun and not full of annoyances you only bear with to get to the fun at some point.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Paradize instantly charmed me with its irresistible blend of retro aesthetics, synth-laden soundtrack, and a surprisingly engaging mystery simmering beneath its sunny surface. Developed by solo indie dev, Soleb, this title exudes personality and a distinct passion for the era it lovingly recreates.Step into Welcome to Paradize, and you're instantly transported back to the glorious 90s. The low-poly visuals, vibrant neon color palettes, and chunky CRT monitor effects create a nostalgic playground that perfectly captures the visual spirit of the time. Every environment, from the sandy beaches to the dimly lit arcade, oozes authentic retro charm.The synthwave soundtrack is a standout element, infusing every moment with an infectious energy that propels you forward. Each track expertly balances catchy melodies with a sense of underlying intrigue that hints at something lurking beneath the carefree facade.Initially, Welcome to Paradize presents itself as a relaxing and aimless exploration experience. You're free to roam the island, interact with quirky characters, play arcade mini-games, and bask in the nostalgic ambiance. But as you dig a little deeper, the narrative starts to unfold, revealing a central mystery and a surprising level of depth.Without delving into spoilers, this mystery element kept me thoroughly engaged. Discovering hidden messages, piecing together clues, and encountering increasingly bizarre situations became the driving force behind my playthrough. The narrative strikes a satisfying balance between humor, strangeness, and a touch of the existential that makes it feel entirely unique.While the visuals and music might be the initial draw, the gameplay in Welcome to Paradize kept me hooked. The island is surprisingly packed with activities.  You can perfect your skills at arcade classics, try your hand at fishing, test your luck with hidden slot machines, or even partake in some impromptu car races.I was impressed by the amount of hidden content and unlockables scattered throughout the island. Exploration is consistently rewarded, fueling a satisfying sense of discovery and a desire to see everything the game has to offer.Welcome to Paradize took me by surprise. It’s more than just a nostalgic visual treat. This is a surprisingly polished and content-rich experience that weaves a compelling mystery alongside its laid-back, summery vibes. If you have a fondness for retro aesthetics, synthwave music, and enjoy a little strangeness mixed into your games, Welcome to Paradize is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is one of those that needs a neutral button. It was fun at the start but it grew more and more frustrating the more/further you played in the game. I got to the warehouse district and I rage quitted now and uninstalled the game. Reason is, the game is just too janky. Collision with your own zombies was a dumb idea so I had to respec away from zombots getting zombots because they just kept blocking me. _childDocuments_.review: Overall ThoughtI am a little put off by some of the bias in the quest writing, but overall it's a spectacular game. Sure there are a few things that I would tweak here and there in it, but then again I can get somewhat picky. PriceThinking on the price I would've paid 15 bucks for the base game, but the supporter edition seems more than fair.  Is it fun? Sure is fun. Do yourself a favor, and run through the quest line one time. Then, just skip future cut-scene sessions. The writing of the desert quests is very bias against "slow folk". To me, that really strikes a nerve. Not all people that take a little time to think are lesser people. Anyway, it is as advertised, but not as comedic with that kind of writing is all I am saying. Some features this game offers that I like:-You get a purge tactic. (Kind of like in Conan Exiles. You get to choose major encounter, although, your base can still get attacked from time to time.)-You get a necromancer hoard vibe. (Like in Diablo, instead of skeletons it is zombies.)-Base building. (A forgiving base building dynamic. -Challenging exploration. You get to adventure. Some people tend to forget this, but when you are done exploring you are done exploring. There is no more adventure. There is basking in the art of it. Kind of like when the gold-rush was over back in the old western days. Build your darn fort, and do what you came here for!-OMG, the music! The music on combat is so great. I get annoyed at a lot of games when going into battle with all that bongo style bs. This though, it changes in zone, and the music at home base is so chill. I don't say this much about some game, but the music is good.Things I wish were fixed:-Camera Unlocking (Would love to be able to rotate the camera. This game as a top down thing going on like in the game Dismantle. It's kind of a deal breaker for me, but I am sticking around in case it changes.)Anyway, get the game, it's worth it. We are who we are, and don't let a little bad this or that keep you from enjoying some of the great art this is. It is stable straight out of the box. Much more than I can say for some of the games out there that you gotta damn near have a college degree to start up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you find yourself captivated by titles such as Dead Nation or How to Survive 2, then it is highly likely that you will derive considerable enjoyment from Welcome to ParadiZe. This game seamlessly weaves together elements of cooperative gameplay and strategic survival, mirroring the thrilling dynamics and engaging mechanics that characterize those earlier experiences.Much like Dead Nation, which immerses players in a post-apocalyptic landscape teeming with relentless adversaries, Welcome to ParadiZe presents a richly detailed environment that challenges your tactical acumen and resource management skills. Similarly, the survival elements found in How to Survive 2, which demand a careful balancing of exploration and combat, resonate strongly within this new title, inviting players to navigate treacherous landscapes while crafting vital tools and defenses.Ultimately, if you appreciate the blend of cooperative action and survival strategy found in these esteemed predecessors, Welcome to ParadiZe promises to engage your intellect and provide a rewarding experience that resonates with your gaming preferences. The intricate design and compelling gameplay mechanics are sure to captivate your attention and immerse you in a world where every decision counts.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating 8/10 ( Go For IT ) Full Gameplay Walkthrough - Welcome to ParadiZe is a game that feels way more enjoyable than you might expect it to. It’s technically weak and occasionally ugly to look at, but it has a great sense of humour and satisfying combat and crafting systems that elevate it above the surface jank. It’s a game for putting your feet up and having fun with, untroubled by complex systems or massive levels of challenge. And sometimes, that’s all a game needs to be.In Welcome to ParadiZe the world is already buggered. Zombies have wrecked everything and the rich have pissed off to live in a new habitat on the moon. For those few survivors left on Earth, there is only ParadiZe, a walled-off Utopia where technology has allowed us to make servants of the undead hordes. As the game begins, your chosen survivor has made their way to PAradiZe to find it not exactly like the brochures.Zombies still run amok, given that the brain control tech is not quite there, and most of the human survivors who live here are, well, a few chickens short of a henhouse. If you’re to survive in this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ world, you’ll need to construct weapons and armour, build a settlement that acts as a homebase, and learn to control and utilise your own “Zombots”, mind-controlled zombies who’ll fight for you, pick flowers for you, blow themselves up for you, or even give you piggy-back rides everywhere.It’s hard to quantify Welcome to ParadiZe for several reasons. Firstly, it’s incredibly, almost unashamedly janky. It crashes quite often, for one thing. My character once fell through the floor in a never-ending death-dive until I alt-tabbed out and quit, for another. There’s nothing I can do to get rid of the screentear or stop-start framerate. It’s a technical shambles to rival the decaying fiends at the centre of its story – and yet it’s also really bloody playable.Like How to Survive before it, ParadiZe refuses to take itself seriously. This is no meditation on the futility of survival, no musing on the supposed tragedy that humans are the real monsters in a zombie apocalypse, no characters to get attached to and no hard moral choices to make. This is a game where you can ride one zombie into a pack of other zombies and scatter them like bowling pins. It’s a game where you can attach massive spikes to your Zombot’s clothing and watch other zombies wander into him and get instantly diced. It’s a game where fresh zombies are spat out of giant pneumatic tubes until you shut them down to prevent the spawning. It’s weird and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ silly – and I’m absolutely here for it.There’s an overarching plot about reaching the moon that may or may not be poppycock, and to accomplish your goal you’ll need to navigate this strange world where roaring hot desert sits literally across the road from dense forest, and human survivors exist in their own little pockets of civilisation, served by brainwashed zombies, and like nothing better than to give you fetch quests.As an isometric action game Welcome to ParadiZe offers an enjoyable addictive gameplay loop that sees you hoovering up endless resources, crafting weapons, first aid items, ammo, and armour, all to get strong enough to keep doing it. Combat is surprisingly meaty, with satisfying feedback on both melee weapons like machetes and baseball bats, but also on air-powered shotguns, crossbows, longbows, and, eventually, actual guns.Zombies fly apart with relative ease, and if you knock them down you can either finish them off messily or force a mind-control harness onto their heads and “recruit” them. Killing hostile zombies will drop their equipment, and picking it up fills a progress bar that eventually allows you to craft the item and equip it on your Zombot. It’s a fun mechanic that means you’re always progressing.While you’re shooting, swinging, and dodge-rolling around the place, you’ll earn XP to unlock skills in three different skill trees. These focus on hacking Zombots, combat, and survival, and while there’s not a great scope for full-on build-crafting, there are enough skills and abilities to shape your survivor in a certain way.It can be a tough game, though, which kind of necessitates playing with a friend. You can absolutely tackle the whole game solo, but be prepared to get overwhelmed a lot. Death simply respawns you with zero cost, though, so don’t worry too much. While it’s built around creating a working base with other players, it feels like a game you should play at your own pace, exploring, crafting, and progressing through the straightforward but bonkers campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly enjoying this game. It's more fun than I anticipated. Base building is enjoyable, though it can be challenging at times. The ability to control zombots is fantastic. The variety of weapons and armor adds depth to the experience. The engaging story keeps you wanting more. While acquiring top-tier weapons takes time, even the starting gear suffices until you find or upgrade better ones. I appreciate the diverse biomes, each with unique challenges like temperature management. Finding armor tailored to specific conditions is a nice touch. Crafting various items, from bandages to ammo, is a fun aspect of the game.However, the game isn't flawless. Here are some issues I hope Eko Software addresses:1. Inability to rotate the Shelter in the base limits base-building creativity.2. Lack of control to turn on/off buildings or traps can be frustrating when managing power levels.3. The necessity for walls to consume power seems unnecessary since they primarily provide protection.4. A centralized area in the base to oversee all operations would streamline management.5.Limited camera movement can lead to visibility issues in certain situations.6. The ability to equip leveled-up weapons to Zombots and the Zombots that they hack allowing them to acquire gear from hacked units would enhance gameplay.7. The limitation of only being able to craft basic armor, relying solely on the game to provide better gear, restricts player customization and progression compared to the satisfaction of crafting one's own armor.Despite these issues, I've found the game enjoyable and would recommend it to anyone interested in a base-building zombie experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game totally caught me by surprise, it is such a blast. The unique hook of being able to "recruit" zombie (Zombot) followers is great. I love finding new pieces of gear to give to my Zombots - pieces of gear that range from a simple gun to a trumpet that attracts zombies and even a saddle that lets you ride them, because why not?The game itself plays great, I've only ran into a handful of bugs - none of them serious enough to hinder my playthrough so far. It's also great as a coop game and, again, runs really smooth. I was expecting a more survival-focussed game like 7 Days to Die or Project Zomboid but the survival elements are fairly light. No worrying about food or thirst meters and the building is simplified. Definitely a recommender so far if you're into survival and/or coop games.
