_childDocuments_.review: Very good survival/hack and slash game. Unlike most survival games you don't have to worry about annoying food and water meters. The fact that while at your base it takes right out of the storage to craft is a plus. You also don't have to grind to keep your generators running as your zombies will do that for you once set up. Lots of quests to do so you can upgrade and learn new buildings and weapons keeps you busy. The combinations of things you can have your zombie companions do for you is also a huge plus. _childDocuments_.review: I love Zombie games and story driven games where you have a clear objective of where to go and what to do. So far, I am really enjoying this game. It's funny, it's satisfying to just demolish a mob of zombies with your weapons.This is partly base-building, but it isn't super in depth - you're not chopping down trees or mining rocks. Instead you collect the stuff on the ground around you and place buildings. You do not have to have your pylons near your base, so you can set up collection pylons near gathering spots and build your base somewhere in the open.There are some really challenging enemy bases, and the "broken" zombots are honestly the real challenge. The rest of the zombies are just fun whack and smash mobs. The Zombots you control are pretty neat and customizable. You get more of them as you go about the story and you can create pylons to spawn in worker zombots for you and those are also completely customizable. As a casual gamer who enjoys games that are challenging but not outright HARD to beat, this game scratches all my itches. I tried out a local co-op game and my friend wasn't really having fun since it was basically just him following me around so I just play it by myself. I would say this game is like a mash up of Boarderlands and Diablo but with Zombies.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to Paradize is a welcome update to the Zombie Survival sim genre that adds just a little more to what we know and love:Pros:Unique Gameplay Mechanic: The core concept of controlling zombies to do your bidding in terms of combat and base management​​.Humor and Setting: A fun humorous take on the zombocalypse that brings a balance of zanny without trying too hard.Crafting and Combat System: The crafting and combat level up system is relatively smooth and easy to understand.Cons:AI Issues: The zombies AI feels a little rough, even accounting for them being zombos. In combat it feels like it takes way too long for them to react.Base-Building issues: When building you are limited in how to build and place your buildings. In addition being in a forest a single tree can force you to have to place things awkwardly instead of making a base that feels correct.Gameplay issues: Some things regarding movement and combat feel a little off. It's not bad I just feel like it's something they can enhance to feel a bit smoother and effective.In conclusion, "Welcome to ParadiZe" is a game with a great sense of humor and an innovative take on the zombie survival genre that can provide a fun experience. I can't wait to play with friends because it seems like it has the potential for hours of fun together. I give it 4/5 Zombots.

_childDocuments_.review: This game's got some seriously cool stuff going for it. Imagine the perfect blend of cut-scenes and humor, like a lovechild of the Borderlands franchise – it's that good!Now, when it comes to wrangling zombies, let's just say it's a bit of an exaggerated adventure. You'll corral these undead dudes into doing your bidding, but they're not exactly your pets – except for that one special zombie you get to call your own. And oh boy, the helmet-swapping shenanigans are a hoot!As for the world and base building, well, it's got that mobile game vibe, for better or for worse. Think prefab buildings plopped down wherever you fancy – easy peasy, but lacking that personal touch.Now, multiplayer? That's where the real magic happens! Team up with your buddies, and you'll be rolling on the floor with laughter. But if you're flying solo, things might start feeling a tad repetitive after a while – like hitting the snooze button on your gaming experience.Overall, not too shabby, especially if you've got your squad by your side. But if you're planning a lone wolf adventure, well, let's just say it's not exactly a solo masterpiece. Stick to the buddy system, and you'll be in for a wild ride!

_childDocuments_.review: If you have played their first zombie titles: How to Survive 1 & 2 you'll find similarities with Welcome to ParadiZe. Improved features and gameplay - promoted main feature being that you can control zombies to fight for you.  The only downside is it feels like the same janky combat just slightly better and questionable flaws such as the quests, fast travel placements and the resource + base building aspects. The loot system could use an overhaul or better fun weapons cause it does get repetitive, just main the one weapon that does the most damage otherwise the others would just feel weak and useless (even when fully upgraded). If you can look pass those flaws you might get 5-10 good hours before the repetition and questionable mechanics kicks in. The price tag is fair, not cheap and not expensive, if it was a $60 game I would say no.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the same dev of How to Survive 2, if you play that game before then you know how good this series is. Pros:1. Fun & humorous2. Easy to learn, hard to master3. No cowdung, straightforward zombies killing 4. you can build a cozy homebase with traps to protect yourself5. a variety of weapons to choose from (guns, shotguns, bow, grenades, melee weapon etc.)6. satisfying combat!7. you can have up to six zombies to aid you in battle if you choose to be a zombies master in the skill tree! (they are cute and helpful, you can assign them to do various tasks for you)8. you can level up your character and choose which skills you wanna specialize in. e.g. become a Kung Fu master or shoot 2 arrows at once!9. you can craft armor for your toon to boost his/ her defense rate (whatever you wear will portray on your in game toon so not just stats change)10. the combat though not top-notch kind of fluid, but 8/10 fluid combat is already very good for this type of top-down ARPG. I have played too many top down ARPG  that have disastrous clunky aiming and controls. If Diablo 4 is 10/10 fluid combat, then this game is 8/10 in terms of flow of combat to give you a better picture.Cons:1. The graphic somehow is blurry around the edge of character especially when you are moving (so you must turn off FSR) but even turning that off, you can still see some blurriness here and there. Hopefully the dev can address this problem soon.2. Camp storage management can be improved. e.g. pressing space bar should be able to store items directly instead of clicking it one by one. 3. I hope we can have more in depth building system, e.g. decorate our house, paint the wall, put on lamp post, flower pots etc. to make it more lively.4. my toon should have an obvious feedback when getting hit, now often no response when my toon get hit so I have to pay close attention to my life bar. When hit should get the hurting sound at least for a sound cue that your toon is under attack.Overall, a must buy if you like to kill zombies!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.It's basically a narrative led, open-world, 4 player co-op, hack-and-slash/twin-stick shooter. You fight lots of zombies and can 'hack' them in order to program them to do tasks for you. The skill trees are fairly simple, but do help the fun factor. There's light base building in the game that allows you craft and upgrade weapons, and have your zombies collect resources. I initially thought the programming aspect of the 'zombots' would be annoying, but it's actually very easy to understand. Combat is basic, but satisfying. The world has secrets to find, enemy camps to dismantle, and bosses to fight. Different regions have temperature ratings that you have to keep track of, but it isn't super intrusive to the gameplay, which I appreciate. Haven't tried the co-op yet, hopefully it's stable. I believe you can use your characters in singleplayer or multiplayer interchangeably, but it does appear that singleplayer and multiplayer worlds are separate. So if you plan on playing with others, make sure you make a multiplayer world. The npc interactions and cutscenes are all very well done, with full voice acting and camera perspectives.Overall, I'd say it's been fun so far, and pretty darn good. As far as zombie games go, this one has some ideas that freshen up the often overdone genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a travesty. There are many things I can write about and complain about but.. I'll just stick to what really bothers me the most out of this entire game... the dumb animations. There have been several times where my wide receiver's get open or run a timing route perfectly and then the defender makes a play on the ball, have it be intercepted or swatted down because the game makes it that the defender can magically catch up to your offensive player. You can have a player run a streak and beat his man by at least 5 yards and for some ungodly reason he'll slow down and try and make a over the shoulder catch or stop dead in his track to make a possession catch. why?? because the game is animation based. You'll have a guy opened in the flats and you throw it to him and dude will make a possession catch and fall down... about 2 inches away from the first down.. it's a hit or miss too, so you can never know if the player will allow you to go for the first down or just fall.. You have a player running a crosser across the middle of the field wide open and you throw it to him and the defender who was behind him by 3 yards can somehow teleport next to him to swat it down. Several times I have been cheated out of first down passes and touchdowns by the animations. It's ridiculous... You'll have TJ Watt covering one of your best players in pass coverage and dude will somehow keep speed and pace with your best players and make a play on the ball.. now I know T.J Watt is a good player, but no way he can keep up with one of my skill position players. I had to replay a game several times because of how unrealistic the game got and how the AI and animations just kept screwing me over and over. One more thing too, my skill position players will make a catches in traffic and just drop the pass, after securing it and tucking it in.. dudes will just drop it. Throw a slant? Drop, throw a hitch? Drop. Throw an in, drop. Only thing that seems to work are screen passes or if you run a slant and just let Y run until he gets open on the outside and throw to him.. I started a franchise thinking that I would be able to open up the play book and throw different routes and run plays but I quickly realized that slant routes, run plays and screen passes are the only way to move downfield at a consistent rate.. This along with the AI and Animation based gameplay.. forces you to spam cheesy plays which makes the game not fun.. and this is based on my experience in offline franchise.. I can't imagine how it feels to play online and knowing you're calling the right plays and making the right reads only to have the AI and animations screw you over. I grabbed this game on sale but even then.. this game doesn't feel like it was worth the amount they were asking for.I'd say, if you can.. grab a PS2 and get an older Madden games on there or NCAA 06. You'd have a better time.. trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale for around $20, mainly wanted to get it to honor John Madden (R.I.P.). The last Madden game I played was Madden '17 and I was hoping this years game would give me a reason to get back into Madden games. What it gave me was only a few game modes, controls that made me feel like I wasn't even the one playing, and unsatisfying overalls.Seriously, who puts TJ Watt at a 96 overall after leading every defensive line stat except for forced fumbles (and at the time of typing this, he just won DPOTY for this recent season as well as tying the sack record. A weekly update of overalls for players who set records would be nice as well (if they don't already have it, but I would be surprised if they do). Rookie Najee Harris comes to mind because even though he had the most touches in the NFL, he had no fumbles. Imagine my surprise when I jump into a game of Madden and he fumbles right out the gate.I will now list more overalls I was shocked to see: LB Myles Garrett 99 OVR (what is Madden thinking?), QB Aaron Rodgers 97 OVR (likely to have back to back MVP seasons), MLB Robert Spillane 70 OVR (stopped Derrick Henry on the 1 yard line), C Creed Humphrey 82 OVR , QB Russell Wilson 89 OVR, RB Austin Ekeler 86 OVR, QB Josh Allen 86 OVR, QB Justin Herbert 84 OVR, ROLB Robert Quinn 84 OVR, TE Dawson Knox 82 OVR, QB Matthew Stafford 82 OVR, QB Kirk Cousins 81 OVR, ROLB Jason Pierre-Paul 80 OVR, WR Juju Smith-Schuster 80 OVR, CB Joe Haden 79 OVR, MLB Leighton Vander Esch 79 OVR, TE Pat Friermuth 77 OVR, I am sure that there are more cases of players playing WAY better than their Madden rating, but I guess most of the people who judge these star athletes know what they are talking about. Except for TJ Watt. They are smoking something funky there.Other than the basic function of the game, I have figured out that Madden has a big problem running on my computer. When I tab out of this game, it crashes 20% of the time. The reason I am actually writing this review is because Madden won't even launch, and I can't tell if its the worst launcher ever to be made in Origin, or Steam not being very compatible with the game.To conclude, it really doesn't seem like EA doesn't care about what they put out or if their audience enjoys it because one of the very first things that comes up when you open the game is microtransactions. You think that Madden would have already got their enjoyment for scamming you out of $60 (which is double a reasonable price for this game. I love football and I just want to see a halfway decent football game come out. I would rate this game a 2/10.Also, I enjoyed Axis football much more than this game.  (28 hours)Update: I have played this game more probably about 50 hours worth and it continues to prove how my first part of the review is correct. It is really sad that Madden has what is essentially a monopoly on the football video game market, otherwise I would be playing any other game. The only game mode of interest is Madden Ultimate team, but even that is broken. You can have a 99 overall defensive lineman get locked down by a 90 overall guard with no double team. You can also have your 97 overall safety along with a 97 overall cornerback and another 98 overall safety get mossed my a non x-factor 86 overall wide receiver. In conclusion, whether you win a game is essentially up to either abusing glitches or a coin flip, whichever you believe the case is.ALSO, I figured out that Madden updates ratings. TJ Watt won defensive player of the year and still has only a 96 overall with 88 block shedding after tying the record for sacks on a shortened year due to injury, which is almost the biggest mistake this game could ever make if it wasn't for rating the 2 year in a row MVP Aaron Rodgers at a f*kcing 95 overall. Seriously, what is this game smoking. This review isn't worth any more of my time. The only reason I wrote this much and spent this long reviewing this game is because I love football so much and I care about how it is viewed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review primarily for those interested in Franchise Mode, as that's all I play (I have dabbled in Ultimate but its not for me), and without prejudice for or against EA (which seems to be rare with EA game reviews!).THE BAD -THE FULL PRICE. The full price is clearly crazy and insulting in the PC market considering this is an annual ported release with PC compatibility issues and some missing console features. It's enough to put off proper NFL fans like me. That said, it's recently been discounted on Steam to £20 and £15 ... which is what I paid and a reasonable price point I think and likely reflects at least some acknowledgement from EA that it isn't quite the game it could have been. £20 or less is what I'd recommend you pay. £30 at the next release would be a good starting point EA!THE FREEZE-CRASHING. This is the big one. By this I mean the video just stops, some sound continues, and the game has to be Force-Ended from Task Manager. This happens to me approximately once per session (usually early on and usually during games, but it can happen on the menus as well just the same).  I know I'm not alone on this by any means (it seems that you can basically expect this unless you're lucky), and I don't have a weird config. Its definitely unique to this game and seems to be a "feature" bug, they haven't coded out.Although definitely annoying, there are two factors that prevent this from being game-breaking (with Franchise Mode at least, and with my rate of crashing - I appreciate some people may have more crashes). The first is that the game auto-saves seamlessly ALL THE TIME (maybe BECAUSE they know its not stable?). This means every time it crashes, when I get back into it, I can carry on exactly where I left off. I can honestly say that despite the number of crashes I've had, I've not yet lost a single play or roster change from it, which is surprising, but is essential to stopping me giving up on it.THE OBVIOUS - YOU NEED A CONSOLE CONTROLLER. Ok, you don't, but you kinda do. I have played Madden in the past with keyboard, longer than I should have. I now own a wireless XBOX controller JUST for this game, and it's worth it.IT'S BASICALLY THE SAME GAME AS THE LAST ONE. I never actually played Madden 21, but it's similar enough to Madden 20 that I can extrapolate, and really by now nobody should be hugely surprised. The rosters are updated, the players are updated, contracts are still way over-simplified, just don't expect much else changed in game play, but I'll come to some subtle Franchise tweaks below (at least since Madden 20) which are more important than they first appear.THE GOOD -THE GAME-PLAY. So whilst people moan that it's no better than it was in 2001 etc etc, well ... it just is. Iteratively so, yes, but it's still a really good and fun game, with lots of polish around the commentary and background sounds so it FEELS like the NFL. The updated rosters and named commentary ARE cool, even if it's easy for them to do. Yeah there's glitches and blah blah, but you can tune things for better simulation with sliders for (which I can confirm DO work (at least they do now), and aren't placebos. Simply, there is no game like this to compete with it in the NFL genre, not even close imo, and its FUN.STAT IMPROVEMENT. As noted, I'm comparing with earlier versions here so bear this mind if you own Madden 21. One of the best and most important 'new' tweaks is the evolution of players improvement. In past editions, a bad player, (especially the OL and QB with an interception-sack-machine QB controlled by a human) would decrease stats to the point of self-destruction, meaning only trades for experienced players would be viable on higher skill levels. Now, stat decreases are temporary and handled by Morale, and they can pull out of those slumps. It's a small change, but really critical to the Franchise mode that in-game player's mistakes are learned from, not reinforced. The Normal/Star/SuperStar/X-Factor progression seems to work really well now too, with players more realistically changing up or down a level following personal success or failure.DRAFT. Another improved area (though a LONG way from great still) is the Draft. If you're anything like me, in previous years I've just given up on trying to find anyone good in the Draft, and trade all my picks for known players instead (which the other teams are far too willing to give up). Now its still a bit of a lottery, but you have a chance. The scouting system is better (though still weird) and you can get an inkling with revealed stats and the Mock Drafts what kind of player you might be getting. You may still be better off just trading all your picks for the players you ACTUALLY want, but you can find a few gems in the Draft now if you go that way. I debated whether I could count the Draft improvements as GOOD, if the Draft is still BAD, but it is what it is, and the difficulty of it is now part of the game lore it seems, so in terms of being better than the past implementations, it is. :)ITS ON STEAM. So yeah, Madden is on Steam. For quite a few recent years it wasn't on PC at all, nevermind Steam, and I wasn't going to buy a console just to play one game. It seems to me - for all its flaws - still by far the best NFL game overall, so personally I'm happy I at least have the option to play it, and I hope EA don't just give up again in years to come just because of negative feedback or sales (or lack of effort on their part). I think some people think we're just entitled to Madden on Steam and EA have to provide it to us - we aren't, they don't, and whatever you think of EA and the slow development of Madden, it being here is imo a definite good thing, that should be appreciated. THE FRANCHISE MODE VERDICT - So is it worth buying, for Franchise Mode alone? For under £20, and if the last version you played was Madden 20 or earlier, then yeah, for me it was. I've already had my money's worth and I'll be playing a fair bit more. Unfortunately I can't easily compare with Madden 21, but hopefully some of my thoughts above will give you some guidance if you are just considering a 1 year upgrade. As with Football Manager, my general advice is to buy every other year and limit any disappointment. :) EA could do more yes, and they only have themselves to blame for poor sales on PC - but at the same time, hey, its Madden, its fun, and until someone makes a game on PC that can come close to competing with it, I'll take what they have. Just be nice if they patched the freezing ...

I play my favorite team and I really like how the roster is constantly being updated to match teams current rosters. This Madden is my favorite of all time so far, and I started playing Madden with the '08 release. Get on board and enjoy the abilities of your players on display. They can be upgraded, and practiced to elite status., being able to make fantastic catches in traffic; run the ball with jukes , spin moves, and hurdling. WR can run like gazelles and make cuts in routes that are amazing. Play your favorite team, take them to the Super Bowl, and enjoy the end game celebration. The AI of Madden 22 will gear itself to your gaming style, and give you enjoyment for hours, game after game, and play after play. I highly recommend this Madden and can't wait to stop this dissertation of the game and get back to playing. Oh, yeah. I almost forgot this part...GO BOYZ!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Listen this is right on the line for of thumbs up and thumbs down........frankly the game is what we all knew it would be. I will leave out the fact that it is basically a 60 dollar roster update, lets not kid ourselves, anyone who is a real madden player knew what we were getting when we bought the game. The real issue is absolutely no next gen changes, the major selling point of this game are included on PC. I mean we have PC because they are better machines then PS5 and Xbox yet we cant play the actual game. I played over 2,000 hours of Madden 21, I will without question get my money out of this game, always do with madden, but if that isn't you, this game is not worth buying on PC. I also have no expectation of EA releasing the next gen game on PC at all, always better to have zero expectations with EA then any given the state of madden that last few years. If you plan on and can actually get your hands on a PS5 I would hold off buying this game until then. Generally, I would wait until at least 100 or 200 hours into a game to review it but I feel completely comfortable saying this is literally the same Madden game as last year. In all honesty if you were to put 2 screens next to one another having Madden 21 and 22 up you would not be able to tell which one is which. That being said we will all continue to buy them, continue to play it for thousand of hours. I will however say the fact that they basically lied to our faces promoting the next gen updates and not having a great reason or any reason at all for it to not be the full game.Next issue is with steam, had I not looked at the reviews and actively searched out if next gen upgrades would be included I would never have known until after I bought the game.........Bad on steam, it should be in big bold letters at the top of the store page that this is not the full game they are promoting. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, completed my first Franchise Mode season as an owner during this free weekend. I rebuilt the lowest rated team and one of them happened to be the Texans. So I rebuilt parts of their team and earned them a spot in the playoffs with a first round bye. However, I lost in AFC championship against the Chiefs. Including that lost, I lost 3 times. Once to the Rams and once to the 49ers. Had some close games, but I managed to get a good part of my team into the Pro Bowl.That being said, this wasn't without some issues of course. The game liked to crash and freeze at random times. Sometimes I'd be setting up the gameday goals or adjusting the X-Factor skills and I wouldn't be able to control anything despite the game still going on the background. Other times, the game would freeze and crash as it loads into a game. This is a reoccurring issue that I don't think will ever be fixed as it's common in Madden 19, 20, and 21.But I do like that you can choose and set your X-Factor skills as an owner. I hated not being able to do that in previous games and leaving it up to RNG in hopes that your players get the abilities you want them to get.Now onto the gameplay. It's typical Madden gameplay. Nothing has changed really except that banana peels that are now left on the field every time my running back handles the ball. I don't know what it was, but there would the perfect hole for my running back to cut through and after cutting through, they would trip on an invisible banana and tumble forward. Ruining what would've been a touchdown. This occurred frequently until I started using Balance Beam on my running back and they practically disappeared, but I didn't want to have Balance Beam as his ability. I had to stick with it though because of the constant slips on the invisible bananas on the field. This wasn't an issue for the previous games and I've put over 100+ hours on Madden 19, 20, and 21's Franchise Modes. I've never seen my players slip on invisible banana peels.Defensive Ai still love to teleport. They teleport through players to cause either an interception or an incomplete pass. Then they like to teleport onto the ballcarrier and tackle them. It's just annoying when this happens several times a game through a long ass season. This has always been a thing and it's one of the things I hate the most.As for the Franchise Mode Ui, it's uh... pretty much a hit or miss. At times, it's very unresponsive. Other times, it works fine. However, I really don't like that the tweets like past games. They seem to only care about possible trade rumors that never happens. That's what happens the entire season. They'll mention a game or two being, but other times they're like, "Yo, Kareem Hunt is thinking of the Rams, Buccs, Chiefs etc etc." It's just very robotic and not like previous years.I do like the weekly gameplan feature as I hated needing to do minigames to improve them in previous games. Being able to sim them and still get the bonuses for the training help a lot. Along with being able to choose if they go full-pads, half-pads, or whether you want starters to go full practice, just back-ups, or have it split. The chance that people could get injured is a bit iffy, but I found a way to have a player's 4 week injury be brought down to 1 week because of the practice feature in the game. Saved my running back a whole 4 extra weeks of his 7 week injury because of a high ankle sprain that took 1 week to heal. Forget his fractured foot. That doesn't exist now that he has a high ankle sprain!Otherwise, I would much prefer to play 21. I'll deal with Enforcer there since Enforcer still kinda does the same in 22. Ah, I can't wait for Enforcer to never be changed for future games and for invisible banana peels to be all over the field.

_childDocuments_.review: There are plenty of things to do in this game between starting a franchise, playing the story campaign, online matches, building an ultimate team or playing in "the yard" which is a small team backyard pickup game style of play. But although there are plenty of different things to do, the game itself is full of problems. Starting with the ultimate team, within an hour of starting to build a team, you're able to start putting players on your team that are "legends" that have been retired for years. I expected that the ultimate team would make you have to keep playing to slowly progress your team to become better and better. I also expected you to have to play with backup players while going through this building process. Unfortunately this instead focuses on starting you with legends and then if you want to make those legends better with upgrading it, they just want you to buy it. Ultimate team = money grab.The online games don't really need to be talked about, the gameplay feels worse in the modern Madden games than it did 10 years ago. Although I will give them credit, as bad as if feels to play, it looks way more natural than the old wonky animations. There is also crazy delay spikes when trying to play against other players. I tried to play a online match against my roommate and although we never have internet issues, we were constantly getting delays where the game would freeze for only one of us, players on one of our screens were not there on the others.... it was just unplayable.The Yard was actually really fun to play when I opened that up. We played with a couple people and we were having a bunch of fun, but the bugs just ruined the experience since very quickly, 1 by 1, we weren't even able to open up "the yard" or join each other. Another one of the constant bugs we saw was that your challenges wouldn't show and you couldn't even earn those when they weren't showing. All that being said they constantly push the marketplace and all the things you should buy to put on your character, where a single outfit is priced somewhere around $20 to $40. Again this game mode is just another money grab.The last, and by far the worst, the campaign. Anything outside of the football field gameplay is just complete garbage. Whatever the story was supposed to be was ruined by the weird delays in between conversations (some times there are over 30 second pauses of silence when two characters are talking to each other), the loading times (a 10 second cinematic scene with no audio, and no facial movements could take 30 seconds to a minute to load). I thought there was no way they would release a game like this and it had to be a problem with my install, but it seems that everyone else I knew was seeing the same problems. TLDR: Everything about this game is designed awful and I couldn't believe that a tripple A game company would release something like this. Complete money grab and you shouldn't buy it, especially if you already have a different version of Madden already.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm  a major football fan, and a serious gamer at the same time. In all honesty... this game sucks. Let's start with the this game in it's optimal form (on console). Just creating a playable team requires an excess of one of two variables: time or money. While this is true on basic level for a lot of games, EA takes it to an extreme on Madden. One has to spend in the hundreds of dollars monthly, or put in roughly fifteen hours a week to create previously mentioned playable team. That's insane. Now, if that was the only issue, it could be overlooked. Fine, I won't have an optimal team, you might say. Unfortunately, this game has utterly failed to recreate NFL football in any way shape or form. On defense, there is one of three plays that will allow you to cover receivers, or get any pressure whatsoever on the QB. Most games I play online devolve into my opponent running the exact same play repeatedly. And since their no learning from my defense, they'll continue to pass for thirty or forty yards on attempt without repercussion. This is frustrating at best, and controller breaking at worst. (Not saying I've done that before, but... it happens to the best of us, ok?)And yet, this isn't the worst part of this game. Despite paying full price for an official Madden title, EA has made it abundantly clear that they have no real intention of supporting PC Madden play. There are glitches in the game currently that have been there since day 1. And yet, not a finger has been lifted to fix them. I'm talking basic issues, such as randomly blotted out score boards, or game crashes for no apparent reason. Not only does EA not want to help with these issue, we aren't even allowed to play the full game. The "Next-Gen" edition has been locked behind the purchase of a new console, meaning that even a top tier PC is unable to access it. This edition of Madden is essentially everything new about this years Madden, including a constantly moving Momentum bar, and more realistic player movement. Essentially, Madden 22 is giving you practically nothing that prior Maddens did not, yet still for the same 60 dollar price tag.All in all, I'm disappointed. This franchise is one of the most profitable of all time, and has a sturdy player base to boot. These issues that I've mentioned are easy to fix, yet boil down to simple laziness on the developers part. Anyways, I hope you've gotten something of value out of this review, and can now make an informed decision regarding the purchase of this comment. (I mention this as most reviews tend to sound like an eleven year old raging at a game, and fail to accurately summarize the problems this game has in a clear fashion.)

_childDocuments_.review: Last Madden I played was 20, and somehow this was worse.  Like most people I played this from the Free Trial period.  Face of the Franchise has got to be hands-down the worst version of it yet.  The voice acting was horrible, the cinematic moments were poorly scripted, the scenes themselves were buggy and just an overall mess. My player would straight up glitch through his clothes.  Interactions with J or Zo would have mixed dialogue compared to what was written in the subtitles.  Trying to skip these scenes would just replay the same voice line again (or twice even).  Your player will cap out at level 6 or 7, but not by design.  The game is bugged and refuses to hand out XP per game.  There are some "fixes" provided by other players, but this rarely works.  I found there was even a patch to correct this which I can confirm did not happen. The AI is pretty garbage as well regardless of the difficulty. Things were either disgustingly easy or impossibly difficult with a hard time finding any middle-ground.  The Yard, which on paper sounds cool, is just boring.  With all the paint and flash advertised with it, it's just nothing special.MUT is micro-transaction garbage and has been for as long as it's been out.  Not worth time or further mention.Everything else is pretty much the same minus some new coats of paint.  My game bugged out in a number of ways that were just ridiculous.  Was it playable? Sure, I played a season on Face of the Franchise and other modes.  I can't believe that anyone would legitimately pay the full price tag for this game.  It's definitely a $10 classic in the discount bin at max.

Other cases include the controversial execution of John the baker, who refused to sell his wife and 14 year old daughter to an Arabian merchant and was thus charged with attempting to incite ethnic conflict. As such, the baker was set to be executed in the morning, swiftly and with undue empathy to provide at least some consolation to the executees immediate family and friends. After several agonising hours the footballer was released from the medical abode, or more appropriately was thrown out the backdoor into a muddy ditch. Despite grievous wounds he was spurred on by vengeance and crawled back to his wooden abode. There he carved two slits for his eyes into a potato sack and placed it over his face, hiding his disfigured face for all eternity, acquired his beloved shiny broadsword and then returned to the city with eyes engorged with blood and flame. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond the franchise, Madden 22 returns with the same eclectic set of modes as last year's game, usually with some notable differences such as more cosmetic rewards in The Yard, a new half-decent story in Face of the Franchise with a new linebacker option, and the ubiquitous growth slightly better visuals, commentary and presentation than the year before. In any event, all changes appear marginal to the targeted franchise fixes.Pros.+ The atmosphere on the pitch improved significantly.Cons.- The new endurance system needs improvements.Madden NFL 22 is the first iteration in years that has gone all-in in the most popular community mode. While we may scrutinize the unusual sentence another day, the truth remains that fans of the franchise finally have something to get excited about this season. Coaching skill trees, metric based demonstration, and improved training give players a deeper sense of ownership. While the other modes have a few new layers to get excited about, and the story engine and endurance system will need tweaks, basic improvements to what has always been the die-hard mode's preferred mode should be seen as commendable, albeit delayed, fan service.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it during the free weekend, have not purchased. Madden is what it is at this point. The lack of competition over the past 15 years had led to the series resting on its laurels. It's more of the same, I still find as a Franchise player that the PS2 era of Madden games are miles ahead of anything released in the past 10 years, including Madden 22. There are some improvements to Franchise mode this year which is more than usual, but it's still hugely bare bones compared to 15 year old Madden games and modern basketball and baseball games like NBA 2K and The Show. Face of the Franchise is also absolutely terrible this year and bug ridden, I don't know why they keep making this mode every year, it sucks. Longshot in Madden 18/19 was average but that's the best it has ever been.If you play for ultimate team or online you know what you're getting into. The game is still heavily buggy during gameplay due to the fact its based on the broken Madden 2006 360 code base, and the AI leaves a lot to be desired (especially AI running the ball, will just completely miss huge holes on all pro difficulty). You can have fun with it, but the game is so lacking compared to pretty much any other modern sports game. NFL fans get totally shafted in this aspect and will continue to get shafted until EA lose their exclusivity and competition forces them to stop being so lazy with the entire game, excluding Ultimate Team which gets all the attention and focus because it prints a ridiculous amount of money each year. The PC version of Madden 22 is based on the XB1/PS4 version, not the XBS/PS5 version, no idea why PC hasn't been upgraded yet but it's definitely a perplexing decision. For all that, I can't recommend it despite the fact you can have fun with it, the issue is that it could be a whole lot more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a comment on the game itself, but rather a warning to anyone who may be wanting to buy this game for an older PC. This game will NOT run on older hardware (specifically any Intel processor that won't support the AVX instruction set - google "intel avx madden 22" to learn more).  Even if every previous Madden game worked on your PC, this one won't.  In a practical sense, that means that older Xeon processors (like mine) won't work.  EA has known about this issue for quite some time and has chosen (unsurprisingly) to do nothing about it.  I received a full refund from Steam with no problems, but I figured I would let others know about this uncommon hardware incompatibility so they wouldn't waste their time trying to buy a game that won't run.  I hope this helps somebody.  Thanks!

I'm using too the Xbox controller from Microsoft, wireless version for PC.  I contacted EA and asked about some concerns and though EA responded to me by saying welcome and sorry I had problems with Madden 22, they had nothing to say other than a link to the required PC specs which I already took into consideration. It loaded up fine and I was able to install the EA "Origin" software and check the box to where it will not open and run upon my PC's starting up.   The game installed and loaded up and worked fine. With cool eye candy and realistic AI movement unlike any of my earlier life Madden experiences.   I think it would still run on Steam, not to sure why I was having problems at first. Maybe I was missing something with the Origin software. "?"   But now it is running very well as I just downloaded it straight from EA.  Some people have said it runs a bit slow. The players have been digitally scanned and their sweat, actual face, skin pigmentation spots are all upgraded to the next level, even their hair is so much more realistic and it moves. I'ts on my radar and a real plus for serious Maddeneers.  I think later too I would like to invest in a PS5 or most likely the Xbox series X.   I also enjoy Steam here as it plays very well. I am very pleased with the new digital scanning of the players and the new AI overall within the game makes a better feel and realistic flowing action unlike any Madden version I have experienced.   the play books are better these days as I am having fun in the practice mode getting familiar with controls and play selection. _childDocuments_.review: I've waited until I had put a good amount of time into this game and this is my honest review.Positives:Outstanding GraphicsBetter Tackle AnimationsSmooth TransitionsFace Of The Franchise Continues In The NFLGreat UIMUT Is Playable Without Spending MoneyDraft And Rookie Changes Promised SoonHaven't Experienced Any Crashes YetNegatives:PriceFranchise Has Minimal ChangesFace Of The Franchise Story Isnt BelievableStill Pushing MUT Over All Other Game ModesPoorly Optimised For PCSome MUT Challenges Are Basically Impossible Small, Annoying Bugs (Clothes Not Fitting Properly, Camera Glitches)Bigger Bugs (Fumbles Flying Across The Field, Players Not Picking Up Lose Balls, Slight Hits Making You Spill The Ball)Reviews On The Game Modes:Exhibition- Self Explanatory, Quick Matches against people online or the AI. Training drills now give you MUT 75+ overall players when completed for the first time. Franchise- Unfortunately, not many changes to franchise yet again this year. However, EA has announced an update on drafting and rookies in the next month, so it's something to look out for. Franchise is still fun to play with mates.Face Of The Franchise- FOTF has recieved a great change, as the story now extends to the NFL and you can now play as a MLB, which i've found entertaining. _childDocuments_.review: I'm an older player who enjoyed Tecmo SuperBowl as a teen.  In my opinion, there has never been a decent football game since then.  I tried to play Madden on Sega Gensis, Super Nintendo, etc and they never really captured the multiplayer season long games that Tecmo had.  I basically gave up on finding a multiplayer NFL game until my daughter came over with her X-Box which had this (Madden 22) installed.  On that platform it wasn't bad.  The online head-to-head was quite challenging knowing I was playing with someone online which is the only thing I want to do with NFL games.  She left and steam had the PC version on sale for 10 bucks.  I instantly bought and started the download.  In the meantime I started online searches about the PC version and found: crashes, unable to kick, etc.  For 10 dollars I'm willing to try it out.  I would say my machine is Mid-tier gaming.  I was thinking many of the complaints could be due to server connection, low end hardware, etc.  My first two games were flawless except for many strange bad kicks which later can be helped by waiting a few seconds before you snap the ball.  I have had more than a few crashes where I never join a game and I get stuck in a loading screen, could be due to my opponent leaving game during loading, don't know.  The controls to me seem clunky possibly due to server connection.  I try hard to defend this game as its the only game like this I have even attempted to play on PC, again I have NOTHING to compare this to.  My first attempt at whatever "Franchise" mode is was a disaster.  Not only was the menu difficult to navigate, the game does a poor job with any tutorial they attempt to provide.  For 10 dollars I would say its 50/50 on being good or bad.  Full price of what? 49.99?  No!  No way I would recommend this at full price.  Even at 10 dollars I kinda regret filling up my machine with 56gb of data for a game I only play at most 4 games per week and those don't last long due to whoever fumbles or gets an interception first quits for the day.  A good full NFL game this is not manly due to clunky controls and bad kicking controls.  Cheapest multiplayer NFL game with online support currently though.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I haven't played a Madden game since 08 and have been itching to get back to it. So this year I have the ability to afford the game, and start researching it. To my dismay, there is much negativity surrounding the madden franchise. The games have become progressively worse and have lost many features, or so youtubers claimed. Ok, I won't buy the game I thought. But then it came on sale and well... I had to see if it was as bad as people were claiming. After playing 85 hours, this is what I thought about this game:1. The quality of big budget gaming has gotten progressively worse over the last 10 to 20 years. This Madden game is a really great example of that. To have played a ps2 Madden and had the ability create a team, customize uniforms, relocate in franchise mode, create a player and follow them through their career (for any position); these features have all been removed or replaced by strictly worse features. The Madden franchise will continue to get worse until they either stop making these games yearly or lose the exclusive license to make nfl games.2. This game is much more engaging for casual players. If you wanna flip on some vs and watch silly time unfold then this game is cash money. If you want to get down to the wire and go hardcore with another person then prepare for rage. If you play this game on higher difficulties, the ai doesn't get better, but rather gets cheaper, making the ai players have super human reactions in order to screw the players with cheap outcomes that wouldn't really happen in football.3. I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone because there are much better football games in this series and others which you could mod with a roster update to make into a better current game. 4.  If you want a casual experience with friends I'd recommend something else, as this game can leave you feeling cheated. If you want a hardcore football experience, I'm sorrry, but we'll have to wait to see what the future has in store.

_childDocuments_.review: All I want is a game that does a reasonable job simulating an NFL strategy & play performance with evenly scaled challenge on both sides of the ball. 14 years after I ragequit this half-assed joke of a franchise I bought last year's iteration on sale and, to the surprise of no one who's played this game in the intervening years, I'm still looking for one.No matter how I adjust the difficulty level and gameplay sliders, no matter how I build my team, no matter my weekly strategy, no matter how conservatively I attempt to play - the second my quarterback has a positive TD:INT ratio I turn into an interception machine. I've tried every kind of different game mode, I've watched passing tutorials, I've called audibles, I've cheesed QB special abilities...nothing. When I lower the difficulty to Pro I am so good at defense that I regularly score three touchdowns via turnover in consecutive playoff games. Even then, career 22:5 TD:INT passer Russel Wilson finished the season with 44 TDs and 22 INTs.For the "git gud" folks - I don't care about winning every game, I want to feel like it's fair when I win or lose. I also want to feel like when I buy a new game it's somehow different than the previous version, but other than the rosters I can't really tell how this is any different from the Madden 2004 that used to make me throw my PS2 controller at the wall. I guess I'll pick up Madden 2042 when I get the football itch again, but hopefully in the meantime either congress has broken EA's monopolistic hold on NFL licensing or the planet has died a horrible climate change-related death and put me out of my misery.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Just don't buy it. It's nowhere near worth it. The improvements they made to franchise are nominal and its even buggier than the last Madden I got, Madden 20. Where do I even begin with this game? I'll start with the very few positives there are in this game. The overhaul of the scouting game is decent, and better than before. There are still some issues with it, and it is not as deep as I would like though. The additions of OCs, DCs, and Personal staff are also welcome readditions, but again, they are not deep enough to be great. The retirement ages seem much better as well. Though there are still some bugs (Like Mitchell Schwartz playing 25 seasons and still getting resigned at 42 overall), it is much better than before. That's where the praise ends though. Game play is still marginal at best with clearly broken plays and playbooks. Downfield blocking logic is very broken with players standing around or aimlessly walking around instead of blocking. Zone coverage is still very exploitable, as is coverage when a play breaks down. The CPU trade logic is still Bill O'Brien level. Graphical glitches are very frequent. They're actually somehow worse than Madden 20, which is impressive for all the wrongs reasons. The servers are still just as bad as before. Essentially, all the old major issues are still in the game. I've also noticed that there has been a power creep among player in the game. Its very easy to get above an 80 overall team with just one free agency period and draft in the game. So long as things are balanced, this wouldn't be a problem, but the game is not. Once you know the tricks to rebuilding, one year is all you need to rebuild without fail. I get one year rebuilds are possible, but consistently being able to do it is boring and points to a problem with game difficulty, not player skill. In game events are also completely broken. I consistently get the tandem breakout event throughout all seasons, so I end the season with two 95+ OVR X-Factor WRs at all times and throughout the entire players careers, meaning I can arbitrarily hold their overalls high. This is beyond busted. I have a feeling the logic to fire the event is just broken. This is not the only event like this I have found. These are only the issues I've found with franchise mode. I will update this review if I play any other modes, but outside of Face of the Franchise, I doubt that will happen. Even at sale price, the game does not feel worth it.

You will dedicate all your resources (assigning scouts, choosing focus players, hosting private workouts, etc) to only 3 players and the game will tell you that you have 95% of the scouting reportfor those guys. Then you will immediately notice that only about 75% of the skill grades are shown and you are still missing the most important grades for the given position (WR will show a A+ Impact Block rating but will have a ? for their Deep Route Running or Catch in Traffic). _childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely one of the worst ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ games ever made. I mean wow, this game could be used as a torture device on prisoners of war. Playing this game will lower your dopamine levels to the point where you will no longer want to carry on leading your life, regardless of the success that you enjoy outside of EA Sports Presents Madden NFL 22. I could win the lottery and get every single woman I have ever wanted and I would still lead an unhappy life because I have experienced the displeasure of playing this game. Never once while playing EA Sports presents Madden NFL 22 have I ever felt even a speck of joy in any way, shape or form. Genuinely, I would not wish my worst enemy to have to play even one down of this horrific game.Let's start with the physics and animations. Every single part of this game is based on a predetermined animation so that around about your second game, you know the exact outcome of any given interaction because you have already seen the stupid ass animation that always triggers the exact same scenario. Nothing is realistic in any manner, sometimes the ball will just bounce around on the helmets of players until it in inevitably picked off, because of course the defense is 500 times more likely to catch any of your passes than the people you're actually throwing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ball to. I can not explain the amount of pain that this stupid game has caused me.Next, I would love to touch on the horror that is the announcers of this monstrosity. They have used the exact same voice lines since well before I was born, to the point where I know what an announcer is going to say next because all the voice lines are repeated so often and are so incredibly generic and boring. It will genuinely drive you insane hearing the same lines over and over and over and over again without any emotion behind them or any even remotely dynamic feeling to any part of this horrible, terrible game. Let's talk franchise. Franchise is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dumb and stupid, it feels like it was developed by a small indie studio of roughly two to three people, and you almost begin to forgive some of the mistakes when you begin thinking this way. Nothing ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ works even remotely. One of the biggest problems with this game right off the bat is that you are throwing to AI all the time, and they make the dumbest decisions possible every single time, to the point where I am able to accurately predict the dumb ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid ass thing that my receiver is going to do next in order to ♥♥♥♥ me over in a fun new way every single time. Sometimes, a man will be wide open in the middle of the field, so I will decide to throw it to him. Unfortunately, the second I throw it, he makes the decision to move directly behind one of the defenders, so that's where my quarterback is going to throw the ball. When the AI is running a slant route, they will often stop directly behind the defender instead of continuing the route out to the sideline, where they would be open. Receivers are not the only problem with the broken ass AI in this game however, as blockers are arguably worse. Every single offensive lineman I have ever had has ♥♥♥♥ up their own ass the entire time, allowing my quarterback roughly 1.3 seconds on average to get the ball out before being sacked by every single player on the opposing team. On a designed HB screen, the o-line will not block the d-line and will instead shift out with the HB to block for them. That's cool and all, except they will often not block for ♥♥♥♥, so then either the QB is sacked because there are no blockers, or you do get the ball out to the HB and the HB is tackled for a 10 yard loss because the o-line that shifted out specifically for the purpose of blocking that one player did not do their job for ♥♥♥♥ and let the defense directly through. Trades are broken, the draft is broken, rankings are broken, nothing works for ♥♥♥♥.I cannot play this game for one more minute or I will genuinely go insane, if I haven't already. The 141 hours I have spent on this game have been markedly the worst of my life, and any positive aspects of my life outside of EA Sports Presents Madden NFL 22 are completely offset by the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that occurs when I am playing the game, causing me to fall into a state of irreversible depression.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this - then there is hope for you. It means you might actually not purchase the game, which in my opinion would be wise.Me, I've long lost faith in EA and Madden, yet still buy it every other year as it's the thing on the market that comes closest to scratching my franchise/career football itch.Game Play:+- The parts you like, are still probably there, while the parts you don't are there as well too.Franchise Mode:+ More coaches - in an OC and DC to level up+ Momentum is a thing that can be activated through meeting game play objectives, which gives a game buff to the team.- Menu / UI is horrible, worse than what I recall from Madden 20- Colin Kaepernick is a FA QB who is rated higher than more than half of the Starting QB's in the league. I can appreciate what the guy has done, his kneeling doesn't bother me, yet this - this bothers me. They may as well have added Mickey Mouse for all of the sense it makes.- Game crashes for me when a game is finished and I try to exit back to the Franchise view, about 1 in 4 games played.Face of the Franchise- 'Story' cutscenes that lag so bad you end up quickly not giving a damn about what they're saying.- Subtitles that don't match actual dialog (typos), or that flow quicker than the actual discussion is going.- Numerous typos on Story type training buffs, where it says one thing, then when activated, the actual result is different (1000 xp for the team - ends up being 500xp, or a buff that says it's for your OL generates a cut scene with your DL).- A veteran on your team is apparently a rookie, as I was 'mentored' by a Veteran in an event, that turned out to be a fellow rookie. And one that was a back-up at that.- A long time veteran on another team is also apparently a rookie, as the Patriots Mac Jones had this event interaction where he was talking about how his career was wrapping up, and I had the chance to be the new face of the NFL.- Made the playoffs with the Jaguars - only to then have the podcast/radio show bit afterwards talk about how disappointing it was that the Jaguars were once again eliminated from playoff contention...- Your Face of the Franchise player is tied to your Madden Avatar, and improving him involves improving your overall Avatar ranking, as it's tied into your position improvements. Would make great sense if for some reason you wanted to play through the mode multiple times, as it'd be akin to a new game+ as the second time you play with the same position, would still be leveled up - but who wants that kind of torture?MUT+- It's still MUT. You either enjoy it, or you don't.- Menu text overlaps.- Mandatory tutorial missions that you have to play before you unlock MUT proper had a bug that kept disconnecting you from the EA servers, so you had to log back in. Might be fixed by now, but I can't say as I'm past that point.I'll still play it. Still grumble. Still wish it was better. Still skip the next Madden version, and probably return for what'd be Madden 24 I guess, as the itch would become too great to resist.

detailed_description: SCHiM is a game about jumping from shadow to shadow, while interacting with a relaxing and lively environment. What is a schim? A schim is the soul and spirit of an object, thing, or living being. Everything in the world has one. A schim should never be separated from their thing! This does happen to your schim, this schim who is attached to a human being is separated from them early on in the game. Can you get back to them before it's too late? Features Unique 3D platforming through shadows. Animated shadow platforms and environments. Each level has its own scenery with small stories. A story of a person losing their shadow. A beautiful abstract world.

_childDocuments_.review: SCHiM is a cute little 3D platformer about a shadow blob frog thingy that can traverse the world by hopping from shadow puddle to shadow puddle. Alas, that's about as deep as things get. After a sweet if slightly boring opening montage in which your host human goes from regular kid to heartbroken teen, to clumsy adult, your klutzy adult host manages to somehow trip so hard that you come unglued, separating from him entirely. Which is extra bad, seeing how the devs have described schims as souls, and everything—right down to the delivery truck—is supposed to have one.  The rest of SCHiM involves you hopping your way back to your host, but boy is he hard to pin down, never staying in one place for very long. And so you’ll hop. You'll hop through the city. You’ll hop through the park. You’ll hop through the day. You’ll hop through the dark. But no matter how far you hop, you’ll always stay one step behind your host until he beats you back to his apartment and you’re for some reason forced to wait outside with all the other little schims until sunrise. Oh, and I guess schims value their beauty sleep, because by the time you creak open your little shadow frog eyes the next morning, your host is already a mile up the road doing whatever it is he does all day. So hop to it! If you already haven’t gathered by my tone, I was fairly disappointed by SCHiM’s plot. It sports an interesting premise but fails to do anything narratively compelling with it (the guy lost his dang soul and went right back to moving furniture for goodness’ sake), and I found myself growing tired of the “chase after your host” repetition within the game’s first hour... and the game goes on for several hours after that.   But maybe that’s my fault? After all, SCHiM was marketed as a relaxing experience, one in which you take your time hopping your way through the cute scenery... but the problem with that is that I never really felt relaxed playing this game. You see, ol’ schimmy here gets a charged jump whereby holding down the jump button longer results in a farther jump, and then he gets a little follow-up hop that only covers a few feet, so you’re always very manually invested in the game’s moment-to-moment. While these jump mechanics feel pretty tight and landing a tricky series of leaps is satisfying, if you fail to reach a new shadow in your two jumps, you’ll warp back to your last one.... unless the game arbitrarily decides to send you back a dozen shadows or more, which happened to me many times because each level’s checkpoints are invisible, meaning you’ll always be at least slightly on edge not know if you’re safe to experiment with a risky jump or are going to get bumped back and have to repeat a lot of hopping—not a very relaxing reality. Additionally, SCHiM doesn’t let you zoom out much, nor does it feature any real UI, meaning the only way to know where to go is to hold down a button that will  pan the screen to the level’s end or next checkpoint. I would’ve preferred an unobtrusive indicator arrow you could immediately turn on or off, because as is SCHiM forces you to constantly pause your progress to pan across the screen to make sure you’re still going the right way (and it will often lead you in the wrong direction). The last mechanic of note in this simple game involves environmental manipulation. Certain objects like umbrellas and signs will allow you to preload a big jump over an otherwise shadowless area. You can also click buttons to open doors, raise the arms of gates that cast new shadows, or even pilot a drone. Even better, a flash of lightning will streak new shadows across the land and open up some fast-twitch shadow hoppin’ opportunities. I would've loved to see more levels like this that center around a shadow gimmick of sorts, because as is in SCHiM’s 50+ levels, these moments of ingenuity are pretty few and far between, and I wouldn’t say I ended up impressed overall by SCHiM’s gameplay or content.  Which leaves us with style. After making a strong immediate impression on me, SCHiM’s minimalistic visuals never evolved beyond portraying simple albeit charming slices of life. They’re cute but samey. The same could be said for the game’s calming, chill lo-fi soundtrack and gentle sound design—nothing here grabbed my attention, in part by design. This is  to be a soothing game, after all, so I can’t really fault those stylistic decisions.  What I can fault SCHiM for is skimming the surface of its fun premise. By keeping everything so surface level, SCHiM begins growing repetitive the second you start playing it and is therefore pretty hard to recommend, especially when there are so many other games out there that do so much more for $25. In the end, I’m giving SCHiM an aggregate MEGA score of 2.63/5 and am happy to answer any questions you have about the game or my review. Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy playing SCHiM, but there were some things I loved as well as did not like about the game. I loved the story and following the main character from childhood into adulthood, and the ending was sweet. I also like the art style of SCHiM and the use of minimalism and color. Furthermore, the puzzle element of jumping between shadows is unique, and I liked figuring out how to get from the beginning of the level to the end. That said, the reset points were inconsistent in the levels. During some levels, if you made a wrong jump, you would reset at the jump before whereas with other levels, you would be halfway through the level when you make a wrong jump and it takes you to the start of the level. This was especially frustrating and added unnecessary stress to the game. Another issue I had was that it was not always clear how to complete a level and the goal button did not help, so I became stuck during several levels. That said, SCHiM is an interesting and unique game, and there is replayability with finding all the collectibles and completing the Steam achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: It is cute but incrementally gets more annoying and infuriating to play. Its game design is charming, but at times the world feels a bit too blank. The plot is alright, and honestly I had no idea that it would jump straight to the adult life crisis segment, not to mention, the entire cat and mouse routine with the owner of our shadow, and the shadow itself, got annoying after the first 30 minutes of the chase. Not to mention, all the times when the shadow was right about to reach the owner (especially that supermarket segment) all felt annoying and infuriating, when I were being forced to watch a cutscene when the guy is literally ONE JUMP AWAY. A much more enjoyable plot, imo, would have been if the owner were the one who were rejecting their shadow. Something a bit more along the lines of a "lost pet finding its owner" type of a plot, followed after the breakup, would have fit this game much better as the current plot is just annoying.Additionally, the game would have been much more enjoyable if it weren't senselessly trying to be difficult. It has a lot of unforgiving timing, as well as janky shadows all throughout its map. Another criticism that I have is with how the F key does not guide us to anything specific on the map.At a lot of points all throughout playing this game, I would reach a "technical checkpoint" only for it to move forward to the next without letting the player know. This game really needs indicators of when the player has reached a significant point, after which they should double check the F key.For example, at some points the game may be leading you towards the bridge, which has no significant indicators to allow the player to understand that they have reached the area to which the F key was leading them to. But at other checkpoints, there are specific buildings that act as that indicator (IE the ice cream parlor, the hotel etc.) This game needs more ways to make the players feel satisfied that they have reached a certain checkpoint, instead of endlessly feeling like they are playing through an auto-generated world where they only see the final goal once they are almost near it. This ends up making the gameplay be nowhere close to being as relaxing as they wanted it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I say anything else about this game I want to acknowledge what I’m sure must have been a painstakingly difficult process the developers of this game went through in order to get this game out the door with the level of quality shown throughout. It is genuinely impressive to me how much they crammed into this while maintaining not only the vibes but also the art and music never getting old. There are some games that you play cover to cover and really have to wonder how there was such a consistently high level of artistic flair, games like Gris, games like Ape Out, and now, SCHiM.It is wildly impressive to me how cohesive the art is throughout the game. This is not a game that looks great in the trailers and then kinda bad in the actual game. This is (assuming you don’t rush) at least a 3 hour game with like 60 different levels and new color schemes to each level. They go so far as to retread old levels in the same town but with new twists to how you get around. I kept going “oh thats really clever” every couple of minutes because in general the game design on show here is just downright impressive. There was two or three spots that I got stuck because I didn’t make a weird logic leap (and for the record I had like 30 people watching that also didn’t get it, god bless those ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that post full walkthroughs with no commentary or I wouldn’t have known my game bugged once and couldn’t progress). I will say, having a “hey I’m super stuck what do I do next” button would be a great idea beyond the current button that just kinda shows you your goal. The fact that the amount of times I got stuck in a game as long as this, which I 100% did not expect to go for as long as it did (in a good way) is a testament to how strong the game design really is. The few instances of me being stuck I think are probably going to be spots where other people get stuck too because they were just really odd leaps of logic (using the shadow of a toaster to launch yourself, driving in the shadow of a toy car, both things you haven’t had to do at all really) so unless people go around spamming the interact button on everything they leap to odds are there’ll be a couple spots like that. Beyond those errors though… I mean ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shadow frogger is such a clever game. The jumping between shadows was something I was a bit worried would feel bad to do, like some of the shadows are really, really thin and it looked like a pain but the game cheats a bit in your favor to help you land those jumps and kinda splashes you into the shadow if you get close, not so much that it feels like you didn’t do the jump but enough that you don’t have to worry too much about whiffing all the time. The moving elements in each level kept things mostly fresh, and the only thing I was tired of by the end of the game was that damn Zoo level that bugged out on me. Some NPCs that were supposed to move between areas werent doing it and so I quite literally could not beat the level and beat my head against it for far too long looking to game the system because I thought I was just missing the real solution. Thats it, though. Every new level had an “ooh, shiny” moment where I was impressed by the way they had you solve something or the way they incorporated shadows into the game. And it helps that the music is so f*cking good. When I say this reminds me of the Wii soundtrack I mean it in the best way because its banger after banger and none of it is frustrating to hear even if you sit in a level for quite awhile. All of the little sound effects, the plops when your shadow frog lands in a puddle, the sound design compliments this gorgeous game very well. I’m writing this out as I ended stream after beating the game (a few days before release, thanks @ devs I appreciate ya’ll) and I’m really hoping that I don’t see a specific kind of review. When there are short, art driven games a lot of the time you see “this is too short for the price” and I think frankly anything 25$ and under is fair for this, but this game isn’t short, really. They put a hell of a lot of game into this game beyond the art, its not just pretty to look at, and I’m desperately hoping that no dipsh*ts leave the dreaded other side of the coin review of “this is too long”. SCHiM is fantastic, its one of the more gorgeous games I’ve played in recent memory and I will absolutely be downloading the OST to use in youtube videos when its out. This is a really relaxed game with a story that I wont spoil for you, but one that I thoroughly enjoyed. I wasnt expecting the “pretty shadow jumping game” to have great music, gameplay and a heartfelt story, but here we are. I highly recommend SCHiM and will keep an eye out for what these devs have in store for future games down the road. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: There’s a lot of value in great visual design. Schim has a style that’s hard to compare to others and brings to life a relatively grounded world for you to traverse in the most whimsical way possible. However, for all of the design accomplishments, the handful of hours it takes to complete the game are still more than is necessary to become bored with most of the mechanics it contains.Abbreviated Review: In a quiet monochromatic Dutch town, the shadows are inhabited by weird little dark frog things. You take on the role of one of these creatures attached by an elastic band to a child running around doing typical child things. Schim’s intro has you getting acquainted with the idea of leaping from shadow to shadow as you follow along with this kid’s adventures outdoors. You’ll stick by his side through school and into graduation as he gets a job and is subsequently fired on his first day. And as his life spirals, he trips launching your froggy form into the street disconnected from his body.This is the foundation of Schim’s premise. You trying to get this little frog creature reunited with the distraught human that lost it. This seems like it would be straightforward, but this dude always seems to be one step ahead of your effort to make it to where you last saw him in this game of  “the floor is lava.” There are some additional story elements as you go forward from the prologue/tutorial introduction that are told through short cutscenes with characters miming action under the soft soundtrack, but primarily the next four hours or so is you leaping into and out of the shadows.The shadow creature you control in this puzzle platforming adventure can’t survive outside of its murky environment for long. With the default settings, you can land in the light and take one small extra hop before being instantly teleported back to your last shadowy checkpoint. The checkpoints are fairly numerous, but they are specific shadows that you can potentially miss. However, even with that, you probably won’t find retreading a few extra seconds of jumps to be challenging.Schim is a puzzle platformer, but only in the softest version of that definition. Your goal is to navigate across levels through whatever shadows allow you to get to your destination. Most of the time, the path is linear, and the process takes mostly well-timed and aimed jumps. Leaping from light posts and guard rails to the shadows of moving cars and bicycles to ride them to street signs, trees, garbage cans, or any other vertical objects that cast a shadow on the ground.These objects are where the most interesting parts of the game are contained. Almost all of them perform some kind of action when you hit the ‘interaction’ button. Most of the time, it’s just moving a bit, clanking, or spitting out a piece of garbage. However, there are moments where you can raise a forklift, lower a traffic cross guard, or switch on and off a light which all have effects on the shadows created within the world. This is the foundation of the small number of puzzle moments where you’ll be manipulating the environment to make it toward your goal and on to the next level.Most of Schim’s levels only use one pastel color and define all of the detail with comic-styled black lines and heavy use of shading. This makes for a very distinct style that is visually interesting on each level, but also very clean and easy to discern what you can do with your shadow jumping power. However, as pleasant and detailed as this world can be, it lacks the variety that you’d expect from a game of this nature. You’re far too often shuffled back into the same sort of streets, parks, and stores that you’ve seen previously. The occasional shifts to factory, beach, and zoo environments were welcome but fleeting.This repetition carries over to the interactive objects in the environment – which also are reused quite often. Even in circumstances where multiple objects allow you to fling your frog across the map, they still manage to be reused in all but a few of the 65 levels. It is possible to spice things up a bit by disabling your extra jump or removing checkpoints in the options, but only the former felt like it allowed the game to still be fun. There’s also an optional ‘hard mode’ that unlocks after you complete the game which gives you a limited number of lives to complete the run – but this seemed to take away more fun than it added considering how easy it is to accidentally end up outside of the safety of a shadow. Even with these issues, I think the game would probably be worth recommending… if not for the price. I know every game gets cheaper over time, but a four-hour game with minimal replayability and a mildly repetitive experience doesn’t feel to me like it justifies $25. Perhaps in the future, if you find Schim at half price or less, it might better justify the short romp through the shadows of The Netherlands, but at full price, it just doesn’t seem like it’s worth it. Not while there are so many excellent indie games available, and often for much less.

_childDocuments_.review: Far too expensive for what it is. The idea and artwork are whimsical, but the gameplay is repetitive and not particularly fun. Hop around trying to figure out where the game wants you to go. I got it at half off and that might be a little expensive at that.
