_childDocuments_.review: This game is great for me, though I do recommend buying only if you love being patient for games.  I keep coming back to do another NG+ run, just like Darkest Dungeon, because:the art is fantastic,the music is chill,the character design is 100 out of 10,the strategy to choice to chance ratio is part of the progressive resource system! (Dying = souls, which you need to upgrade.  No big deal to have a total wipe, or the other option is to retire a character from combat to get the souls while retaining the ability to reproduce, which brings me to the next point),Traits and stats are randomized enough that the optimal party isn't going to cause a rage-quit if they die.  You can use Warrens to pass on high stat rolls and traits, which gives you a second pool of goblins for combat (the babies hang out in the warrens and don't take your barracks slots until you move them to the barracks),The cutscenes are both engaging and have a skip hotkey.Not so great:several memory leak / lag bugsat this time, there are ability bugs and combat bugs that take me out of the tactics and into needing a break.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a smorgishborg of game genres like a Fallout Shelter / breeding / deck building but the devs made a bunch of asinine design choices in the game that just made it feel eh. The art is interesting and the animations aren't bad but you're only allowed to choose one path and at the end of every match it shows what you missed on the other path like 4/6 fights, 3/3 treasures, and 3/4 resources. WHY? Why are you showing me what I missed like I had the option to complete it? You can't go back and forth only forward even if you clear anything. Why? There are merchants and upgrade smiths on the paths you can take but it takes gold to upgrade items and you can't bring gold with you on a run. So depending on your RNG for gold if you don't have any (like me my first time going to the blacksmith) you can't even use the blacksmith to upgrade anything. Next is the merchant same thing, sure you can sell any junk you have on you to buy something like an upgrade orb for your weapon but you don't know how to equip them and if you don't use it that run its just gone. So the item I bought for over 100 gold I didn't even get to use. Then you get pieces of meat which (Meat = health potions), but you have to use them during that run and aren't told this. Lastly your loot doesn't auto stack to maximum in your lair for . . . some reason? It stacks to 20 of any particular resource but when you get them sometimes you'll just have three stacks of 12 or 8 and 7 or whatever IDK why. That was a little nitpicky but you get the jist. I think this game is interesting and has the potential to be pretty great but it is really held back weird choices by the devs in my opinion.  I wouldn't recommend it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Darkest Dungeon 2 I was hoping to get. The game is adorable and the fighting mechanics is pretty nice. I still can't fully understand goblin breeding, but it's kind of in that zone where you're eager to figure it out step by step. The only real annoying issue I have with the game is the UI. It feels like the developers have spent a huge portion of their art budget on fancy animated UI, but at the end of the day this only leads to frustration. It's cute to see for the first ~5 times, but after that it's just a waste of time. You might ask why is it such a big deal, and the reason is that there are no useful summaries or lists of anything you need - you gotta click on every building and then the upgrade button to figure out if you have resources to upgrade it. You will constantly be denied certain actions because you hit a limit of weapons, space in the storage, goblins in the barracks, etc. And none of this info is visible anywhere but in the view of the corresponding building. So, most of your base building gameplay is just this endless clicking and watching the UI animations. I hope the developers realize that no matter how much they are proud of it and no matter how pretty it is, they should work on improving the UX of the base building.

_childDocuments_.review: 3/23/34 REVIEW UPDATE: I'm over 40 hours into the game and its started opening up quite a bit. The early game felt very slow, and honestly the mid game feels very slow as well. There are plenty of reviews about game bugs and yes there are quite a few, as well as mechanics that simply don't work yet, but they are releasing updates constantly. I personally don't like the gatekeeping that they devs have built into the game that slows your progression. I Agree with a lot of the other reviews that the base building system missed the mark on what could be. I was really excited for a polished base building component that took inspiration from games like fallout shelter, but it's just not there. The lack of content in the base building components makes the mechanic overall feel like another form of gatekeeping. Gold has little to no value in the game, you quickly rack up tens of thousands of gold with nothing to spend it on.The souls system doesn't seem to provide anything of value for you losing goblins, the progression just feels cheap. I hope as I get into the end game that more mechanics will be revealed but currently its underwhelming.All in all this feels like a game with a lot of really solid mechanical ideas, but very few of those ideas are fleshed out.. they all feel like they fell short of what they could have been. This game needs work.With that said its still a solid game and i will be finishing it, which is rare for me. i rarely dump this much time into a single player game.  I am lowering my score to a 7/10 as its got all the basic foundations for a phenomenal game, but simply needs another 6 months of polish and content updates to feel like the game should have felt upon release. Still recommended if you're looking for more content similar to Darkest Dungeon.Darkest Dungeon but instead of fear and terror its hope and joy. Interesting take on an established genre! The early game can feel a little lackluster but the mid game opens up to some pretty interesting complexity. I am definitely going to be thoroughly exploring this game and will update my Review as I play. I've noticed a few UI bugs during the tutorial and early game, but all in all no crashes, so no complaints! Pay little to no attention to the petty reviews of people crying about a rough launch. This is a single player game, aside from a few non game breaking bugs it's pretty solid.  8/10 on early game review. I'll update in time.

I haven't really had a need to do any breeding as I get good enough new goblins from rescues and squatters. Some of the resources feel alot more scarce than others but not enough scarcity that I ever felt the need for grinding. One thing about this game that I love is that you do not need to stress much about your goblins dying in combat. the first fatal strike brings them to 1 health and they get a permanent debuff reducing their max life by half and if they do die, your remaining goblins get a massive buff and you still get the souls of the dead to help build up the base. _childDocuments_.review: I do not usually write reviews but I feel like I need to because it is criminal that this game is getting mixed reviews so I need to add to the positive ones.The general gameplay system of Goblin Stone is similar to Darkest Dungeon but without a lot of the things that make that game incredibly frustrating and grindy to play.  Not to say that Darkest Dungeon is bad, it is made that way by design, but if you liked Darkest Dungeon but never ended up finishing it because you just didn't want to grind as much as the game requires you to, this game will scratch that itch.  This game is much more forgiving (Not easy necessarily) healing is plentiful enough that while damage doesn't feel great, it doesn't feel like you're going to get absolutely destroyed because of one mistake.  While goblin death is permanent, I'll get into why that isn't a big deal later in the review.The art-style is cute and charming, the combat system is simple to understand but has a deep underlying complexity to it, it has enough rogue-like elements to make every run feel just different enough even with the exact same team to keep things fresh, and the meta-progression is unique compared to other games like this.There are fun synergies between all of the classes, so far at the point that I am at, I have 5 classes, and all of them have felt great to use and useful in conjunction with each other.  Some goblins get powerful abilities if the enemy is under some sort of crowd control effect, and some goblins are good at applying said crowd control effect, so there's a real strategy in putting goblins in your team in a particular turn order.  Goblins cannot level up, so the only way to get more powerful goblins is through the breeding system.  It's actually pretty simple though, so don't be intimidated.  There's only 3 stats to worry about and while the trait system is important, the base stats are much more important.  Some classes want a lot of one stat, and the other doesn't matter, some just want their main combat stat and some health.  You will get some goblins with incredibly skewed stats and all that should tell you is that they will be good to breed into a particular class. The game wants you to cycle through many goblins to continue progressing, as need a currency you can only get by permanently retiring goblins to the old peoples home to continue upgrading your base and unlocking new abilities for goblins.  So just go crazy, make some goblins kids every day, and see what you get.The loop to this game is: make some new goblin children every day and see what class would be the best for them, take them out on adventure, acquire loot for your base upgrades, see what you can upgrade at the base, make more children, go on another adventure, retire some of the goblins from your previous team to get souls for base upgrades or ability upgrades, make more children, add the new blood to your old team, rinse and repeat.  If a goblin dies, while it is sad (Especially if it was a good one),  you still get the soul you would have gotten for retiring them, so their life wasn't wasted. Ultimately even though you lost a good goblin, you can just make more, and the new kids might even be better than the one that just died in combat.There ARE some bugs, but this game is finished and only needs a small patch or two to iron out the kinks.  Do not let the bugs scare you away from a great experience, this is a fresh take on the genre and if you enjoyed Darkest Dungeon, you WILL enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this the game sits on mixed reviews, 51% positive, 318 reviews total. Even right now a lot of negative reviews praise the game but cant rate it positively because of bugs, so I am expecting the overall score to rise soon (and you can check if I was right, teehee)The game is fun and I havent had any of the big bad bugs the reviews mention, some hotfixes already went out. There is some work to do regarding quality of life, for example if you wanna scroll in the merchants inventory by clicking and dragging, you have to click inbetween items instead of on them, which initially made me believe you couldnt scroll by click and drag at all on that screen. Scrolling in the base screen doesnt work with awsd but only with click and drag or by edgescrolling. Some important tooltips dont show up on mouse over while the character portraits still come to a standstill from scrolling further down, so you have to wait for them to be perfectly still again before you can see the stats of the goblin you wanted to look at, and everytime you open an item cache in a mission you get a narrator voiceline, which would be fine, but you also cant press space bar again to collect all loot immediately, but instead have to first wait 1.2 seconds for the narrators voiceline to be finished, the first button press just skips out of the lil oneliner, small unnecessary stuff like that. None of this is a big deal and should hopefully be fixed soon.Underneath all of this small stuff, however, the game is genuinely good. Varied enemies and bosses, strategic breeding of desired traits, a fun core combat loop, I also really like how they worked permadeath into their player progression, if you dont lose any goblins you  will end up retiring them instead because that yields souls that you need to upgrade your townhall - and goblins dont level up anyway, the only stat that increases through play is how many souls you get on retirement, so you have incentive to use the newer, stronger generations. A lot of love in this one, deserves a way higher rating than it currently has and it hurts me to see when I get a new, rather basic achievement (for example breed goblins 30 times) and then I see that im only one of 1.5% of players who got this achievement. I suggest getting this game and seeing for yourself, they just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ their launch by having a few major bugs initially. Overall it's already way better and will be very good once they sort out the smaller quality of life stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Wake up babe. New Darkest Dungeon-like just dropped.If you can avoid the allure of the trailer, I suggest go in completely blind, the narrative is a joy to unfold.The hand-drawn backgrounds, storybook aesthetic, and lighthearted tone belie the unforgiving combat. You are frequently on the backfoot facing opponents far tougher than you. You will send your companions to die, and die again. You monster. They do not sell their lives in vain. Their soul energy unlocks new combat abilities, and grows your X-Com style home base. Your lost friends will continue the fight on with you in spirit.As Darkest Dungeon veterans will know, strategic use of deceptively weaker combat abilities that inflict status effects like stun and bleed is key. Each balanced character class has their roles to perform, and excel when you play to their strengths. Use your tanks to absorb hits intended for squishy glass-cannons. Combo your class abilities to pierce armored opponents, or inflict critical damage, and win the day.One of my favourite wrinkles is if one of your allies are killed, their grieving friends will rally. Enraged, they gain a brief strength boost that may turn the tide against a difficult boss.All in all, a soft calming fantasy game to unwind and vibe to after a long day.

_childDocuments_.review: -Overview-Looking past the bugs, I think the core mechanics and game play loop are really fun. ( 7.5/10 )For me the game really picked up after chapter 3, which was about 8 hours in. I would say if you're not enjoying the game in the first hour or so then you probably won't enjoy the rest. So far I have enjoyed it a lot, even if the bugs make it hard to do so.-My Opinion-First of all it is frustrating to be soft locked once every 40 mins or so by mating goblins and them doing nothing, which forces you close the game and restart. Expect to have some patience if you're going to play the game as it is.I don't mind the UI, although I agree with others that it could be optimised, especially in the base building part.During dungeons I don't see the value of finding temporary weapons from chests that you can't take home, I'd rather they didn't exist or offered something actually valuable. Also there are encounters in the dungeons that often are the first thing you run into and require gold to participate in. You don't take any gold with you so they are pretty pointless and leave you feeling like you missed an interesting opportunity. These are some minor points that don't stop me from enjoying the game, but I hope they can be improved.The most important thing for me, which I feel has been missed somewhat, is that the goblins aren't that gobliny. Also a lot of the potential for the RP in the RPG part of the game is lacking. Other than class, weapon and appearance there's not much else you can customise or control about the goblins. They don't talk or have much personality beyond what you interpret in their expressions. Add the fact that they are supposed to die or be retired means you can't really get attached to them. I would like for them to add someway of customising the goblins further, or immortalising you favourite ones with a statue or shrine in game. I also think the world building in general could be improved. The overall lore/story is quite minimal/slow and I think would benefit from being sped up or introduced in other ways for example item/place descriptions that can be explored in the players own time. The narrator is an interesting way to introduce the narrative, however, for me it kind of breaks my immersion (similar to Biomutant). I found myself thinking "is this voice a part of the games world in any way? or just someone reading me a book?" I'd rather it be a character in game, or even an old goblin (like in overlord) that narrates.Take everything I've said with a pinch of salt and if you're unsure, I recommend you play the game yourself, potentially after some updates :)

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Wishlist this game and check back in down the line. If they can fix the problems, it has sky high potentialMan, this is a hard one to write because I love a lot of parts of this game as a long time turn based/base builder/roguelite fan. I have almost 20 hours played and will probably grind it out to completion and have an overall good time, but the experience is significantly hampered by a terrible UI (ranging from everything to tool tips to menus, from moving buildings in your base to trying to figure out which Goblin has the most power when changing up your party) and a plethora of bugs. While only one of the bugs I've experienced has been "game breaking," the issue (my screen was stuck on a previous image even though that event was over) was thankfully fixed with a reload, although I had to redo the previous fight. Speaking of which, for a game that says it saves constantly and there's no going back, I've had to redo things every time I had to quit mid run.Of course, that's not touching on the plethora of frustrating bugs that weren't completely game breaking. I've run into significant issues with Hunter traps activating but doing nothing, the Guard's intercept/guard abilities not triggering as other goblins get attacked, and a couple other abilities either not working as intended or  not working as intended and I have no idea what the intended interaction is. Sometimes it does exactly what I think it will, sometimes it doesn't. Which really sums up the crux of my negative review: either these core mechanical interactions are fundamentally bugged, or there's something mechanically going on that is not explained anywhere in the game. For this latter, it is a common frustration. This game's UI almost never gives you the information you want or need to make informed decisions, and when it does, it's usually displayed in a way that is hard to find, too vague to be useful at a glance, or simply just a pain the butt to navigate to because you have to go to a different menu screen (in another room) to find out stuff you want for the screen you are currently on. This can be even more annoying with the clunky and slow-responding UI. And don't even get me started with how you view your goblins themselves/how terrible the sorting options are. For a game that focuses so much on the breeding of Goblins and the importance of items, they make it incredibly hard and frustrating to navigate those aspects. I dread growing my base and having to try to keep track of even more goblins even though that would normally be a management genre inclusion that I'd love.And these are just the most glaring issues, I could write another 10 paragraphs on the UI design problems of this game. To say it's not a polished product is an understatement. All of that being said, from what I can tell it’s the first game from this studio and I imagine they are still learning the ropes. I sincerely hope they learn from the criticism and keep working on this game, because if they can address the wide of variety of problems, they have the potential for a top tier indie game.To start, the style, narration, and overall humor has been very enjoyable. The combat system is super interesting too. It took a while to grow on me, but I wound up loving the turn-based system where “time” is your combat resource and turn order affects party positioning. It can be a little difficult to follow or predict, especially when various slows and hastes get introduced into the equation and the turn order display doesn’t seem to take that into account. Which again goes back to the game simply never giving you enough information for your choices, but the base of a cool system is there. Same can be said with the breeding system. It’s a great idea that fits in super well with the intended disposable nature of the goblins. Normally I would love spending time on a breeding system like this as sort of management style optimization, but it’s so clunkily done that I dread it as much as enjoy it. The more I play, the more of a time-sink my base becomes, and not in a productive way. It’s just so hard to navigate effectively that I waste time completing basic game play loop tasks. I can also start to feel the grindiness creeping in, although this doesn’t bother me as much as it does some other reviewers because I enjoy the adventure loop overall and its combination of roguelite elements in temporary buffs/weapons and enhancements and permanent buffs/recruiting new goblins to replace your deaths and increase your gene pool.While I obviously could go on about the bad and the good, the bottom line is that this game is early access quality, and for that reason I can’t recommend it. I would highly, highly, highly, suggest that anyone interested in this title wishlist it and check back in down the line, though, because if the devs are able to fix even the most glaring bugs and UI/QoL problems, this review would turn into an easily recommend. If you are like me and a big hobbyist gamer who really likes the ideas of this game, it might be worth picking up now, but that's up to you

_childDocuments_.review: I want to enjoy this game, as it has a charming visual style and im a sucker for the games where you play from the perspective of the "monsters" in fantasy.But its severely lacking overtly clunky....The pros:For the most part, relatively balanced combat where you frequently just barely scrape byInteresting class mechanic and dynamics between themDetailed info blurbs on mechanicsCharming art styleThe cons:The UI is extremely sluggish and tends to eat inputs.Mouse over tooltips exist for everything but they tend to refuse to show upSome of the non-damaging abilities are flatout useless vs just doing basic attacksEffects and buffs dont last that long, making it feel like you have 2 groups of 3 goblins instead of a group of 6.Armor is kinda pointless since things hit so dang hard the 2-5 damage less per attack doesnt mean anything in the end.Difficulty spike is real...Despite not having access to all 6 classes right away you still find gear for those classes for some reason, bloating your limited inventoryBase building is a massive grind. I am selling off bushels of leather or bone because i also need wood or stone to use them and i have basically none of the latter. Confirmation bias perhaps, but the % for bonus effects and resistances is a lie. For only resisting Slow 20% of the time it seems to be resisted more than 2/3 of the attempts....and i dont think i ever had my raiders' slash 20% bleed go off. Ever.The game has promise, but right now its more aggravating than enjoyable. Also the difficulty spike is ridiculous...you go from an "end of area boss" fight having 1 ~50hp tough target and 2-3 other mediums of about ~15-25hp to suddenly "Here face 5 halflings that have 2 armor, 50hp, fast as hell, and intentionally single out your goblins to kill them faster" I wiped on that fight 3 times before beating it, and i beat it with 2 goblins at a thread of life left. Prior to this, i think had 3 goblins die due to bad timing rather than oppressive difficulty.Things i'd like to see improved:Fix the UI so it stops eating button inputs, also the scrolling in the base building section needs help. I keep finding myself hitting a key or clicking with the mouse 2-3 times to initiate something like selecting the desired point on the world map.Make effects like "Intercept" last longer. Things like Haste is fine, but most others are pointless.Bleed needs a huge buff. Its initially better since it does 130% damage and ignore armor, but very quickly i can kill the enemy faster by just attacking through the 3-4 armor anyway especially when i have a high crit chance (of which bleed has no benefit from). Know how fast i stopped using bleed? 4th area. Perhaps improve it to 150% and drop the duration to over 4 turns instead of 5, since the main issue is speed of the kill.Make armor actually worth it. I notice that the better attack for your Raiders is a multi-attack that gets somewhat neutered by high armor but NONE of the enemies seem to do multi-attacks, only debilitating or heavy hitting ones. You know armor is bad when my guardians' are just shieldbashing trying to get the stun and doing 4-5 damage to PREVENT an attack rather than soak it for another goblin.Beef up the Mechant so he actually has things to purchase. Since you dont lose weapons when goblins die (or even if you party wipe) you dont need to buy many weapons and he seems to only have weapons 90% of the time. When he does have crafting supplies its like 1-3 leather or bone and thats it. I have thousands of gold i cannot use because i dont have any materials i need to build with. Except leather, man do i have a lot of leather for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: I like to give games as much of a chance as I can, so unfortunately with my time played I don't think I can get a refund. That being said, there is a good game here but its buried under bugs and poor optimization.The concept of Goblin Stone is great. Its essentially a Darkest Dungeon kind of game with 2 major aspects. The first is base building. The base building takes more from Xcom than it does Darkest dungeon and involves building rooms underground that's viewed as a 2d slice. The second major part of the game is the missions which are very reminiscent of Darkest Dungeons missions and combat. Stack on top of these two major elements the theme of goblins being the good guys or underdogs, and it's already a good recipe. But... the game released with two huge issues. One, the bugs. Crashes, things going missing, effects not applying, etc. I encountered a run ending bug where I was unable to build the guild halls for any new classes going forward from the Acolyte. I was stuck with 4 classes because I couldn't get access to these rooms. Some games I can endure the initial launch bugs. But if there are bugs that essentially destroy my run on a campaign based game I can't reload from? Its death to that game. Two, poor optimization. I don't always have access to the best hardware. Over the years I have jumped up and down and played my games from everything from a laptop to a desktop. One of the best things about being a strategy game lover is that most strategy games run really well even on low specs. They tend to also be very optimized. Unfortunately Goblin Stone feels very un-optimized. There are constant stutters in everything you do. From closing menu's to moving in missions. Exiting in and out of various screens can be very slow. In strategy games this can be a killer for me. Because of how frequent you tend to pop in and out of various UI elements in a strategy game it needs to be pretty smooth and quick. I wanted.... to really love this game. The art, the concept, the combat. So many things are fun and a good idea. It's just not where it should be for a 1.0 release. Kind of really sad about this one. Was looking forward to a good xcom/darkest-dungeon campaign strategy game. Hopefully the developers can turn it around and fix the issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Goblin Stone

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game but currently it feels like Early access...I really like the concept and art is amazing but:- flooded with bugs of various severity- game is laggy- UI is clunky, slow and sometimes unresponsive (doesn't reflect changes on screen)- poor QOL (terrible base navigation, junk selling, missing tooltips)And then there are some questionable design decisions/flaws:- temporary items, buffs and upgrades which makes game unrewarding- base building is very railroaded- no difficulty settings, ascension settings unlocked after run are not really answer when run takes tens of hours- so far enemies feels same (doesn't really require specific tactic)I will continue playing and happily switch review over if issues are addressed and fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR in case you don't want to watch the video:1. Art, story, and voice acting is stellar - this is a story that is funny, heartwarming, and totally unexpected! This isn’t the traditional RPG where you get attached to a few characters and level them up with experience - but instead you make their offspring stronger by breeding those with desirable attributes. Don’t get too hung up on them dying - goblin souls are what’s needed to upgrade your base!2. Combat is tight and fun in many ways, but it gets repetitive at times battling the same packs over and over on some maps. 3. That said, the occasional unique enemy and boss fights are where its at - intense, tough, and requires a lot of thinking and prep to get through.4. I wish there was more enemy and map variety - aside from the themed biomes, most maps are basically picking the right choices between resources, items and rescuing more goblins from captivity - this really is the main drawback of the game!5. Some buggy gameplay and UI issues at the time of launch - but I’m confident they can patch these out with time!6. The base building is pretty basic to say the least - but the ‘breeding’ of goblins and using of souls to make better variations is pretty interesting.I’m hoping the devs patch out the bugs and add more gameplay variety - both in maps and enemies, as this is a very charming and lovable game!
_childDocuments_.name: Goblin Stone

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bit of Darkest Dungeon, light card-based combat, with rougelike style branching missions, and XCOM style base building. Plus of a few fresh ideas like combat (being a balance of time and position), breeding, and character loss being integrated into the gameplay loop. Plus it looks great.Overall quite fun but a couple gripes would be that the menu systems could be streamlined. When you're managing your goblins, you end up having to bounce around multiple buildings/menus a lot. It is also a bit on the grindy side if you want to get materials to upgrade your base. Not too terrible, but a bit slow in that regard. Seems a lot of negative reviews have to do with bugs, but personally I haven't experienced any. They have also had a patch since launch so they are working on those problems as well.

_childDocuments_.review: First off the art style is great, the goblins are cute and the narration is absolutely fantastic, the game is a mishmash of several other games like Darkest Dungeon/Fallout Shelter and Monster Crown. The first zone is fairly simple difficulty wise but as you progress the difficulty slowly climbs and eventually becomes rather intense, now it's not near the intensity of say a Darkest Dungeon but in all honesty that's fine. The game isn't overly punishing but you will lose a few of those gobbos on your journey and each one will bring a small green tear to your eye.So now we get to the Bugs, there is a few right now which will hopefully get sorted quickly, the devs on the discord channel have been responding to each report and have said pretty much of all these will be addressed in the next major hotfix.That being said i do recommend this title, but if you are worried about the current state of the game regarding bugs, wait a week then pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: It is with a heavy heart I write this, but sadly I would not recommend Goblin Stone to other people in its current state. The game is a bug filled grind, with limited content. Which is a shame for such a visually beautiful game.Resources are far to scarce, and concentrated only on specific types (mainly wood and even more so on fiber)Progression is non existent. Combined with the fact that combat is painfully easy, means that the main mechanical theme (breeding goblins that are better) falls by the wayside, as there is no need or urgency for it.The breeding mechanic itself is very lackluster in and of itself. The barracks is to small to really delve into any sort of customization of goblins and the traits are hard locks between story progression points.I had initially thought you'd gain new traits or be  able to breed higher stat goblins by, you know, mixing and matching types and breeding them. Nope, grind until you reach a story beat and bam! You just find better goblins. So whats the point in breeding them?I could go on. But there isn't a need. This game has a lot of potential to be the Darkest Dungeon successor it wants to be, but it still needs a ton of work, but that's just my opinion. I really hope the Devs continue to fix and update this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Definetly doesn't deserve a 50% review score. It's a lot more fun than many modern gamesGreat game for the price, it's a turn base RPG game with base management and gathering resources.Later you can buy better items for your goblins based on their class and breen goblins with specific traits so they become stronger. You also gather resources in missions and have alternate pathways.Sounds familiar? yes, it's influence a lot by Darkest Dungeon Pros: looks great, charming, hand drawn is timeless, combat is interesting since you can't brute force your way, gathering resources feels rewarding, base management is overwhelming but becomes fun, a lot of variety in gameplay because of the turn order mechanic, decent storyCons: combat takes a while if you do it right, confusing and conflicting mechanics when it comes to abilities since you have a lot less control over your party rotation, might be too linear, takes a few hours to get started.But, overall, definetly one of the best indie games ever made

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine game and only a soft recommend. I will admit that it mostly gets by on its charm. I love myself an underdog storyline, cute visuals, and monstrous humanoids. The gameplay is ... good enough, which is why I would suggest buying it on sale. If the game was not pandering to me specifically, I would have probably quit it by now. Also still needs a lot of ironing out.It's not particularly challenging nor particularly innovative. It's like DD but not as good in terms of gameplay loop, variety and basebuilding. The breeding and "deckbuilding" mechanics are really underbaked, but at least each of the classes are balanced. They all have well-defined roles and each of them justifies themselves in gameplay. However, both in terms of abilities and genes, there really isn't much variety because there are always options that are very clearly the best. It's always just "max out the attribute scores and take genes that accentuate the class' purpose and further drive up its main attribute".The game struggles with variety in general. Variety in enemies is the biggest culprit to me. For the first 20 or so hours of gameplay you just find different power levels of the same handful of enemies. Only in the third map do you encounter new enemies AND get variety in scenery, too.Truly, the single saving grace, and it's a BIG saving grace, is that it's so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cute. The goblins are adorable. The orcs are adorable. The gnolls are adorable. The kobolds are adorable. Somehow, the trolls are adorable.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this one is ready quite yet. There are some bugs still but I'd imagine those will get fixed soon and they aren't that frequent. The game loop is pretty simple and a little grindy, (36 hours with one restart and I just got into act 2) but I find it kind of fun. There's not a lot of meat. Pretty much what you see is what you get.  I don't really think that's a bad thing.The story is fun and I want to see where it goes. I particularly love the narrator.My biggest problem comes from what you do when your at the goblin base. It's very much a chore navigating through everything. Navigating your base consists of a lot of zooming in and backing out. It's super jarring.One of the big draws to this game is breeding the gobos. The big problem is you have no real way of organizing them. What you get is a single file list that takes up 10% of your screen with 1 single filter. Which means when you breed your goblins (something you are given incentive  to do after every mission) You are stuck shifting through a lot of goblins 1 by 1 . It's just painful...I'll probably come back and check this out later and see if navigating the base has gotten better. Until then I"m going to put this one down. _childDocuments_.review: The good, the drab and the downright bad.Oh yay I have created a Retirement Village for 122 ill used and mistreated goblins only for it to get instantly deleted upon completion.After 100 hours to complete, this game then asks players if they would like to go again on a slightly harder difficultly, to then unlock the next slightly harder difficulty.The simple answer is NO! All the fun stuff in Goblin Stone is undone by the undercooked economy and bloated number of quests required to progress through the chapters. The ponderous and repetitive nature of the late game gameplay gives players a lot of time to consider what works great and where the Devs went wrong.Good = breeding, guilds and visual designDrab = combat AI, base building and weapons & weapon upgradesOutright Bad = bugs, crashes, economy, length of each chapter, resources for upgrades and combat difficulty being way to low.Please play 300 hours to unlock a mode that may be challenging = BS

_childDocuments_.review: It's not terrible, but I can't recommend it. The UI is sluggish (which impacts the controls) and it could be making better use of screen space to present more info. I think its biggest problems come from the presentation not matching with the actual game mechanics.1) It has little side-scrolling areas that you traverse without having gameplay elements that depend on traversal. The branch navigation could have been done on a map, like Slay the Spire. It's doubly unfortunate that the controls feel bad and there IS a branching map you can consult. It seems like we are only moving goblins across the screen because they're showing off the art style.2) It's borrowing the theme of "cards" without needing to. This is an area where the game feels like it's trying to lean into the inspiration from Slay the Spire. The abilities are presented as cards you can play on enemies, rather than a simple menu-driven selection of options. There is no deck, no draw pile, no discard pile. You're just asked to choose from a random selection of 3 out of a character's 4 abilities. 3) The art style is cell-shaded 3D that is trying to appear as hand-drawn 2D. The environments look great, and most characters look good (although some are really rough). However, the game is played in barely interactive 2D side-scrolling areas and the 3D doesn't add to the game's mechanics.Most of what you get is bloated 'polish'. The area movement and the card dragging UI could have simply been menu selections. Given how bad the UI feels, they really should just be menu selections. Some of the atmosphere is good, but the controls prevent you from enjoying the art assets to their fullest. Also, a narrator isn't the best idea for a game where you immediately have to replay areas to grind for materials. You'll start hearing repeated dialogue clips pretty quickly. Bottom line: If this had been a cozy menu-driven game for $5, I'd probably recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to say pretty much the same things other reviews already say, and I know I only have 3 hours right now, but the game has some weird issues.Here is what I can say for now :- All goblins feel samey. The breeding aspect of the game pretends you can create goblins with specific stats and traits, but the stats seem limited by invisible hard caps, resulting in all goblins having pretty similar stats.- The grind is real. I've done 3 missions in search of wood so I can build the last of the 3 first guilds (guilds are rooms that allow you to change the class of a peon goblin) and I got 2 woods. From a merchant. It's absolutely insane because I need 15 to build the room, and 20 per upgrade. You have to get extremely lucky to find harvest spot, or for the mission to reward said material at the end.- The interfaces are absolutely awful. Some things straight up don't work, like scrolling, and some things work half the time, like clicking "outside" of the interface to go back. But that's not my main issue, the interfaces are slow and HUGE, but lack important informations like stats. You have to go one interface deeper to get the information you want about a goblin, and then go back and do it again for another goblin. it's especially annoying when breeding goblins.- Some effects seem really weak. Like bleed. For example, you can apply & stack bleed that will deal 15 damage over 10 unit worth of time, or just deal 10 damage 2-3 times in that time. It's the same for healing, which is very weak (while enemies hit quite hard).- Lots of bugs, mostly minor ones, like the narrator spamming "the inventory is full" when I pick up stuff that is stacked in my inventory.- Some things are really convoluted and confusing. I have slots for goblins in my barracks, and slots for retired goblins, but also slots for the goblins in my team ? Meaning if I remove a goblin from my team but don't have space in my barracks, I can't do that. Why ?- A LOT of "temporary stuff", like temporary weapons you keep for 1 run, temporary buffs, temporary ability upgrades, temporary weapon upgrades. It's not that much of an issue but it's really annoying to taste the power of a new weapon and it vanishes at the end of the run.- You can find food to heal your goblins but once the mission ends it is instantly sold (I think) and you can't start a run with food in your inventory. Which is quite annoying considering how bad healing is and how hard enemies hit.It's really a shame because the game looks really interesting, you can see combinations of abilities and perk that would make for a great team, and I really enjoy how the turn system works.But oh my god the grind for materials.(By the way, despite what the game's store page says, it cannot be shared with steam's family sharing)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I have been following and supporting for just over three years now, I fell in love with it very fast and signed up for every open and closed Beta that I could find.Seeing the game released I was admittedly initially concerned with the amount of bugs minor and major I encountered despite the game having been in development for so long, I wonder if they simply did not have the time to do the proper bug-testing despite fans (me included) asking if they were going to do more public Betas.Regardless the game early on was far from unplayable, the gameplay was better than it had been throughout the various open Betas and things I had noticed like buttons in the Village simulation section not properly registering input were all but gone. The game is definitely worth you picking it up at full price, The Developer Discord are fast to respond to feedback and critique with the game having received constant updates and bug fixes since launch in response to reviews and feedback.It is a game with a ton of love put into it from both developer and players with a fun, unique take on the standard rogue-lite RPG system. It is far from a perfect game balance-wise, I found it was quite easy to breed my race of UberGoblins early on with just a little good RNG but I will still lose Goblins (as is intended) to Boss Battles or even merely strings of bad luck. People saying it is easy are lying to you. Give the game a shot. It has given my 78 hours of enjoyment as of writing this at full price and has been worth every penny,

_childDocuments_.review: You can watch my short 5 minute review on the game here:Goblin Stone is a story driven turn based roguelite which sees us manage a goblin settlement by farming resources on expeditions through beautifully stylized levels, where we face off against a handful of copy pasted enemies by following the amazingly narrated story of likeable orcs and clumbsy goblins, while a few major issues plague the whole gaming experience. We follow the journey of a few goblins who got driven out of their home by a third of the lord of the rings cast. Shelter- and homeless they find refuge in a settlement which we extend with additional rooms to stack the gathered loot, train new goblins into different archetypes, trade with a friendly orc merchant and give them a private room to breed new generations of goblins. With new genetically evolved allies we start our expeditions in the war room picking a mission to gather resources or a story relevant episode on the beautiful table. Once we pick a destination we see our goblins tread on a path with a few twists and turns replacing the simple roguelike themed maps of other games and giving us a sense of exploration not to mention the breathtakingly stylized enviroments. Amidst the pretty scenery we encounter first and foremost enemies which we face in the neat combat system.These battles see our leather skinned group take turns with our enemies. Each character has an aray of actions to choose from with different cooldown times. Using a powerful attack sees our goblin move back on the time bar with the next one stepping into the front line. Since most enemies attack the goblin closest to them the combat system gets far more strategic since we not only have to take into account when our goblin will react next but who he will receive the next attack from. This simple yet clever change to the typical turn based combat system gets further effected by the few unique effects our skills can have, by slowing down the enemies, speeding up our own allies, or entirely stopping them in their tracks and on the time bar. The variety of abilities increases further with the different classes our goblins can become, with the guard shielding himself and others or the acolyte healing his allies or the hunter setting up a poop trap which blasts our enemies... thats some explosive diarrhea...Apart from the combat encounters we can also find merchants, new equipment for our goblins, caged companions we set free, camps to regain our health or shrines and trainers to upgrade our stats and abilities for the ongoing expedition, to name a few examples. Furthermore we encounter well written events which challenge our team to amass a certain stat to successfully finish this encounter. These stat points furthermore dictate the classes our goblins can become and are heavily influenced by the traits each goblin has from birth, but more on that in a minute. These classes can be assigned to our companions through the integral rooms in our settlement. If we want to have an acolyte in our team we require the room. This however opens up the first issue the game shows since not only do we need to encounter these classes to unlock their room, but also are the building costs of these rooms quite expensive. The rarity of the classes amounts to me having only five of the seven classes available after over 8 hours of gametime, while the building cost requires us to venture out 2-3 times before we have enough resources to build a single room.This grind is one of the more annoying hurdles of the game, since it blocks our path to creatively setting up a varied group composition and are forced to fill the team with the same class multiple times during the first couple of hours. Apart from issue number one we get back to the variety of our companions and their love to each other, since breeding is a fundamental part of our settlements progress. Every goblin has three stat points and possible traits effecting their combat power, health, armor or crit chance. These traits can be adjusted when sending two goblins with the wanted traits into the love making room which results in two new goblins with a mixture of their parents traits, while the OG goblins die during the mating act (death by snu snu)Even though death is constantly around the corner for the green skinned folk their deaths are actually an integral part of the game, since goblin progress is being built on their ancestors backs, meaning every killed or retired goblin rewards us with souls which we can use to upgrade the settlement as a whole and gather more companions with more traits.As mentioned the traits heavily impact the stat points which are essential to the class system since a brute with a high body stat cannot become a shaman, while a goblin who has the religious trait cannot become a fighting class, which makes sense since religious people are never violent... okay bad example.Entangled in the class system are also weapons each goblin can carry which often come with unique traits of their own but feel like a missed opportunity since we cannot upgrade them in the long term but either temporarily for an ongoing mission with the gem stones or the blacksmith, yeah drop your head its a shame I know.The enjoyable combat, mixed with the great artstyle and nifty settlement system, sadly cannot outway the current issues with the grind, the weak customization system and the fact that many players even encountered gamebreaking bugs. Therefore Goblin Stone currently cannot be recommended but once they fix the main issues, it can become a great game for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really enjoy the game and it's a great idea, however there are some problems. There are a lot of small glitches that can be really annoying/frustrating. Traps for the hunter not working, enemies stacked on top of each other because of the turn meter, etc. However they are small things that I hope get better over time and they don't happen all the time, just often enough to be a problem. Nest, there needs to be more buildings and more resources given per play. Not types of resources, just more of what we already have and an easier time getting souls. their is one change to the current buildings that I think should be changed as well. The barracks max level only has 24 slots. If you don't wanna give us another barracks due to the buffs it gives, that's fine there's another solution. Just have the guilds house that type of goblin instead of the barracks. This will allow us to hold a lot more and also makes logical sense. Finally, we should have a couple more game modes, aside from just story mode. (I think it would work great if we have new buildings that unlock game modes when you buy them) Some sort of pvp with other players would be cool, as well as a trading function where we can exchange goblins/resources. Only idea that I have at the moment, but there should definitely be more game modes. (and buildings)Overall though, it's a great game that I thoroughly enjoy.  Hopefully they update with more content and bug fixes in the future. You got something good here though, so keep working on it and don't give up!Currently I have a quitch where almost all of my characters take damage after dealing damage or healing. _childDocuments_.review: Goblin Stone is a turn-based adventure game with roguelike-esk runs, base building, a compelling story, great sense of humour and fantastic narration. The game is like a cuter Darkest Dungeon without the extreme devastation of party wipes. You may still get party wipes but the goblins are kinda designed to be killed and easy to replace (sorry my Goblin friends, but it’s true). In fact the game requires Goblin souls as a resource to expand and upgrade the base! I think my biggest gripes with the game was the grind and the repetitive nature of the runs. Neither of these were deal breakers for me but both have been addressed in the 1.2 update, which is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for a few hours, I am forced to question whether or not the developers have actually played their own game.The main issues are:1. This game is completely unforgiving. Each and every single move you make is properly logged, right down to each move you make in the fights, so If you make a mistake, the game will force you to regret it. This is exacerbated by the fact that you can't get your hands on resources without completing missions, missions that will force you to take casualties if you are not careful. Also, there is no way to effectively replenish losses in the early game. So if you make a single mistake (I.e. forget to equip one of the goblins with a weapon.) You can very easily be forced to start a completely new game.2. The grind is real. There is a clear and defining change in difficulty with each mission you unlock/play. However, you can't upgrade/improve your goblins with the same relative ease. The only items you can equip on your goblin are weapons, and those are very difficult to improve/find in the game. There is a way of improving the general quality of your goblins through breeding lines. However, you are forced to play a mission after each attempt to breed, so you will have to play several missions before you are capable of raising a whole new squad of useful goblins. 3. RNGesus plays a big part. There are only a few moves that each particular class of goblin can make so teamwork and the synergy of each party is important. However, the problem is exacerbated by how the combat mechanics work. During battle, goblins are only given a choice between a few randomly selected abilities of the entirety of the abilities that the goblin actually possesses. I.e. There is no guarantee that you can actually use the combination that you want to use.4. The turn based setup. While there is a merit to their way of playing a turn based game by making a character wait a certain amount of turns before they can move again. However, the game makes this happen by forcing both teams to face each other standing in a line, with the order being determined by how many turns it takes before they are allowed to make a move again. But the problem with that is that the vast majority of moves involve attacking the person who is standing at the front of the enemy team. So you constantly have to be on the lookout for how many turns it takes for your goblins to start moving again and you have to balance out the cost of the moves you make in order to actively prevent your own goblins from being stacked out.All in all. This game gives you very little diversity and very little opportunity to make stronger teams of goblins, essentially making the game very grind heavy and tedious. The game has to be much more forgiving and the player has to be given more means of modifying and increasing the capability of the goblins before it actually becomes playable.

_childDocuments_.review: There's quite a bit to like about this game, but also room for improvement. I wish there had been an early access mode so that the developers could get more feedback and implement it into the game for a polished release. Pros: -Unique sense of design, both for the characters and the environments. They're beautifully rendered by the artists, and that's by far the biggest 'draw' here. (Get it?)-Interesting story also gives us a novel take on the classic RPG format, having us play as the fodder mob that we're so used to farming xp with. -Emphasis on the synergy of your team, rather than the individual strength of a singular unit-Several classes to play around with to accommodate for your play-style. -Branched pathways/procedurally generated levels like Slay the Spire.-Goated narrator-Runs smoothly, small download size. I'm playing on PC and have noticed zero bugs since launch day. It seems to be a different experience for other people though. Cons:-My only real con, like many others have mentioned is how big a grind it is to get the proper resources to develop your base and to upgrade your team. Think 'Hades', but instead of new dialogue options, you run into the monotony of revisiting the same areas. (I think this could be alleviated by increasing the resource output per mission that you do, to decrease grindy feel). Additionally, the currency that you do receive in bulk (GOLD) quickly becomes useless, and you accumulate so much of it, without a significant way for it to transfer over to the resources that you actually need.Comments:-I've seen a lot of people commenting on how you don't feel a personal connection to the goblins, and I honestly don't see that as a con. Unlike games like Darkest Dungeon where you intentionally are meant to use the same mercenaries, goblins are the quintessential fodder mob. They reproduce like rabbits and are weak as hell. Those are essentially their two core traits. They overwhelm you with numbers. Some of these reviews make it seem like the players were expecting to get to know every single goblin as though they were going to watch them as they raised their families and coddle their grandkids...I just don't think that's a priority for me in this kind of rogue-like, and you get really good at min-maxing the breeding to generate your lil elite goblin lineages. Bottom line, I'd still recommend this game to other players, but do make sure you understand what you're getting into. It's a slow-progressing roguelike where you're oftentimes grinding to ensure that your goblin team can keep up with the increasing difficulty of enemies. If you can make it past that, you're rewarded with some truly beautiful, hand-drawn art and a fun story to work your way through. At the time of this review, I can't attest to the replayability, but right now, due to the progression-locking of the game, it seems like the game follows a linear story.

_childDocuments_.review: For those of you experiencing the soft lock bug w/the weapons and the chest at the end of the tutorial, here is a possible work around. When you reach the campfire, choose to restore health instead of talk strategy. _childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review. In this episode im checking out a recommendation by some of my viewers with Goblin Stone, which was developed and published by small indie developer Orc Chop Games. Goblin Stone is a Turn Based Strategy/RPG Game that takes a unique approach to classic Fantasy Game Tropes by having the player in control of one of the traditionally evil races, the Goblins. In the fantasy world of Goblin Stone, the heroic factions have successfully driven the monstrous races like wolves,   Orcs and Goblins to the brink of excinction. The survivors are forced to eke out a miserable existence underground. However the situation changes, when a band of desperate goblins find a powerful magical artifact, beginning a quest to restore the goblin race. Along the way you will need to contend with deadly predators, greedy adventures and Band Of Heroes who might not be as heroic as they seem.The game takes heavy inspiration from the excellent turn based strategy series Darkest Dungeon, adding an additional layer of difficulty by placing you in control of one of the weakest races. Your foes are bigger, stronger and more numerous than your little goblins, so you will need to use cunning and stealth to survive, as well as taking advantage of breeding your goblins to create a powerful race that can survive a hostile world. Goblin Stone released to mixed reviews on steam, with major issues with save files being deleted. I also experienced this problem. However the developer has reported this issue to be fixed and i have confirmed that this issue is no longer occuring on my saved games. Therefore i am happy to recommend the game.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. Game was provided by the developer for review purposes================================================Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Bitchute: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Twitch: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Odysee: Skill Incarnates Gaming Channel on Rumble: Twitter: Facebook: Email Enquiries: Goblin Stone on Steam: Goblin Stone - First Impressions: ================================================

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little turn-based strategy game that borrows lots of its combat mechanics from Darkest Dungeon, and its base-building from XCOM. The game has a charming hand-drawn storybook aesthetic that fits the game well. Also the role reversal between the fantasy good guys and bad guys is heavily reminiscent of the Overlord game series from a decade ago.The game suffered from some bugs at release - or so I'm told - but the game seems stable nowadays. It doesn't seem very likely, however, that this game will get any further updates, so the current state is the best we are likely going to get.Even as is, though, this is a lovable game about brave little gobbos. Not the best game ever - the mechanics are a bit shallow and the missions a bit repetitive - but certainly worthwhile for anyone with a soft spot in their heart for the little green gremlins.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, The theme and mechanics are great. The artwork, sound design, and narration are all top tier. On top of that the game is not balanced very well. It requires certain materials to upgrade your lair to progress in the game, but you'll quickly be overloaded with gold you can't spend, and you'll never find enough wood or fiber to upgrade important components quickly. This results in tons of unrewarding grinding to gain little progress. Moreover the game starts to become very monotonous and way too easy, especially when they ask you to repeat areas and bosses over and over to continue further. These issues could've been easily spotted and solved if the game was properly play tested, but clearly it wasn't.All those problems aside, it seems the development team doesn't work very hard to fix these bugs and takes 3 day weekends every week when they have a nearly unplayable game.I want this game to be good so badly (hence my 45 hours of gameplay). Unfortunately it just isn't, and they don't seem to care enough to fix it in a timely manner. Maybe give it another 3 years and it'll be better, but until then save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this release for a long time, but I have to say I'm disappointed with what I've experienced so far. The roguelite elements don't go past anything but random map generation, only being able to retain collected resources through the incredibly short runs leaves you frustrated at having to essentially restart over and over with your blank slate of a goblin squad. What's the point of finding a cool weapon or upgrade for your goblin if it's going to be gone in ten minutes, having to start the increasingly difficult missions with inferior weapons and cards EVERY single time? If nothing you do matters, you have to ask yourself, why even play the game? And for a roguelite there doesn't seem to be any randomness in the core way you can "create" new characters-- breeding. The stats of each parent are pretty much just rounded up to be the same or worse, you can't get ANY new traits through it, those are locked behind the odd goblin you may find, though I've never seen any traits other than the base three in the supposedly "large" pool of them. There's just no uniqueness in the goblins as individuals, even though they're supposed to be THE main characters! Just like the enemies, there are no variations in them. Heck, even the physical traits all look the same other than skin tone, a flabby goblin looks the same as a thin goblin, the curved ears have no visible difference to the straight ears, etc. It's just not the experience it was advertised to be, and while I understand it's made by an indie team, that doesn't feel like a valid excuse for the state the game is in. I just don't feel any love or care put into it, as I would expect from indie developers and their passion projects. I sincerely hope it improves because make no mistake, I WANT to love this game! I just can't at this moment in time.

_childDocuments_.review: The first playthrough was pretty fun. Nothing super challenging (way too easy imo), but noticed in the achievements that the game is intended to have multiple playthroughs, each with different functions to make them harder. "Cool", I say to myself, "glad that it does get more challenging".  I started the Story+ a week ago now and can't even get past the first group. You get 3 goblins around 25 health that do 3-6 damage (pretty much have to land a crit to get past enemy's armor. so even then, you're only doing 1 damage....and that's if you're lucky). Let's do the math: 3 goblins doing 1 damage each per round (at best) against 4-5 enemies with 60 health plus armor each. How many rounds do you need to progress to the next battle? Oh nevermind.... you just got mortally wounded on the first attack!  I've restarted the Story+ mode probably a few dozen times now, just hoping that I'll get a good random draw on the starting goblins or starting me against easier mobs ...i dunno..... something that would at least get me through a mission or two. Because right now, I need goblins. To get goblins, I need resources. To get resources, I need to make it through a mission. To get through a mission, I need goblins. To get goblins....... do you see where this is going? You don't need to be a rocket surgeon to see just how flawed it is. I love a challenge, but after the first playthrough, the game is nothing more than a Kubayrashi Maru, except no lesson to be learned other than the devs gave up on balancing their own game and sold you a game with ZERO replayablity.The game is definitely not worth the price tag. 5 bucks, at best. Even if it was free on Steam, I would probably  NOT recommend it to anyone I know. The lack of common sense on the developer's end is just....wow..... just wow.  This'll eat up about a week or two to get past the first playthrough and you may even have a little bit of fun, but after that, it's just another bad game that'll sit uninstalled in your Steam library that you will never touch again. Save your money for developers that use common sense when making a game.Cons: Everything above plus very very VERY annoying gameplay mechanics. Pros: Everything is autosaved and the game never logs itself out. Perfect if you're someone who tabs out and gets caught up in RL.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Do not buy. Besides the bugs everybody else is mentioning, the overall gameplay loop is simply too based on random numbers to feel productive, and too slow and cumbersome to work as a roguelike.This is my first ever review and I'm heartbroken because this game has so much potential but it simply isn't there with execution I have tried and tried to find the fun and it simply does not deliver.Gameplay itself is relatively slow, with goblins barely able to fight at best. All upgrades available during missions are temporary and are taken at the exclusion of permanent resources and money, but even those are randomized to the point that it's difficult to predict ahead of time whether the expedition will be worthwhile. These missions take about half an hour to complete and eventually feel samey because each individual goblin has so few abilities... and those are randomized, making it difficult to plan ahead even in battle.There are theoretically permanent upgrades available via goblin breeding and improvements of the headquarters, but breeding is also completely randomized and can only happen once per day (so one time between 30 minute missions.) Base upgrades require resources which, because of random chance within missions, are impossible to plan ahead for and extremely slow to collect.There is an extremely steep difficulty curve outside of the starting area, leading to all-but complete permadeath party wipes. Theoretically we could upgrade via breeding and resources... but in practice, that feels impossibly distant. I've played for 23 hours because that's simply the sort of time investment this frustration requires.I wish I hadn't purchased this game. Please, save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought it would be so much fun killing hobbitses, wizzies and men-folkses hunting XP.With names like Slaghacker and Windranker, this game can leave you gobsmacked. Especially if you're English!EDIT:Now that I have completed the game:This game is Ironman mode only, great for XCOM players who enjoy this mode.Upon completion, there are escalation settings for a replay that will make the game more challenging - I have not tried this yet.The story and narration was good, I like to read books and the story plays out like one.The RPG mechanics are quite simple and there are Crowd Control skills that can be utilised - I haven't seen streamers use them effectively yet but I found that they certainly reduce the amount of hits you will receive and made the tactics fun deciding which skill to use.Deaths of your goblins are not that painful and are actually rewarding as you need to farm their souls anyway to upgrade your base and unlock skills.The breeding of your goblins is intuitive, it just takes many attempts to get what you desire.(HINT: build more than one breeding room and upgrade them)Goblins do not level up, upgrading your guilds will upgrade their power, so new replacement goblins will be similar to the one that died. No more rage quitting a campaign like I used to do when losing captains on XCOM ironman mode!My PC: 1080ti graphics, SSD drive, 7 years old. The game ran smoothly.There are bugs and each time the game locked it required closing and reloading the game which did not take long. Fortunately I did not experience my game save ever being corrupted. It did lock during battles but upon reloading I was able to continue the battle with no problem.It is understandable that anyone with a HDD drive will be frustrated because of load times; with SSD's its quick as the game is not huge.Overall for the £18 I spent, this game is fun, well worth it and I believe they will fix the bugs over time. For me none of the bugs were game breaking and this game has me hooked! Now for my 2nd playthrough...

_childDocuments_.review: The closest game I can see to this would be Darkest Dungeon (the original)  Just with a lighter and friendlier theme.  It can get a little grindy at times as the random levels make it difficult to guarantee you get what you need.  I was amazed it had voice acting, not much but good quality.  The whole package comes together much better than I was expecting, especially at this price.The biggest issue is the early game grind.  You will get tutorial style quests to build certain rooms that are critical to improvement.  However getting the materials for these rooms will likely take a long time unless you get lucky.  Rewards are better to look for rather than resource nodes becasue of how random finding nodes are and then needing to get lucky you get the right one.   Once you  get your initial class guilds and start upgrading rooms the game opens up a bit.  I have a feeling this will get even better as we move along to new areas.  If you don't like grindy sessions that at times don't seem to give you anything you may want to pass on this.  Otherwise it has a bit more depth than it seems at first and the main loop is interesting, if a bit time intensive.  Even  when you don't get much that you can use every run gives you something.  Losing or crippling your goblis can be disheartening but you should quickly find the rooms and mechanics that actually make these seemingly crushing events helpful in the long game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: 3/27/24 They recently had a big update that fixed a number of bugs and fixed many broken saves. It seems the team is going to do maintenance on it and look to fix problems. I've personally ran into a couple bugs that have required restarts still, but its better than it was.While I still wouldn't recommend it to my friends at this moment, the fact they are working on it and seem to have plans to continue to do so changes my opinion to give it a thumbs up. I would suggest waiting until May unless your someone who easily deals with bugs. Hopefully by then they will also make the pacing better. Beyond that, I did notice a new animation for the goblins in the base, so it looks like they may try to add more life to the base which is wonderful. Or perhaps noticed one I just missed it before.-----------Old review.The game is super charming, and I really enjoyed it until I got save data corruption at 36 hours. I can't decide if I was lucky or unlucky for it to take this long to hit me.Man, you can't have this much save corruption on a game that only has one save file that auto saves. Saving has to be 99.999% stable to do that. Something really got messed up on QA. Not sure if they didn't have any, QA was ignored, QA did a bad job, or someone through in some code before the game came out that QA didn't get to test, but you can't launch like this. Its honestly so hard to get a game that stable I don't recommend doing that kind of save system, I say this as someone who used to love doing such a mode in other games and now does it with normal saves but a rule that I can't save scum. Loading on bugs only.I really like how they helped counter the deaths on a mission run by giving you the chance to pick up more goblins to replace them, an innovative way to deal with death spiral that happens in a lot of squad based games where your expected to have people die. Enjoyable story, lighthearted with a heart string pull here and there. Music is relaxing, atmosphere is very pleasant. Love the art style in general and especially on the gnolls.Beyond the save issues, it does have some balance issues with resource income at this time, and the fact that I hit late game with still the basic squad of goblins and was wrecking everything. I was using the breeding mechanic, but man it doesn't feel like the first 3 classes alone should be this good this late. It also has a number of decisions that make it far too much of a time sink. Animations that are cute the first time but annoying the 100th, some animations that take longer than others or could be sped up by a 1/2 second. Needs 2x and 3x speed options for combat. The constant load screen between sections of the map is very annoying, would be easy enough to ignore if it wasn't for all the other time sinks.The merchant sucks, and the resources trade is laughable. You get so few from him even as your overflowing with gold. He either needs more, or they need to add in a 2 to 1 conversation rate for resources. That would help deal with the imbalanced resource income as well.The base needs little goblins running around doing stuff in places except the retirement home, barracks, camp, and war room. Most of it is an empty ghost town that feels so much like their should be goblins that I swear its another bug in a long list.I honestly think the "scouting" missions and the "story" missions should be condensed into the same mission. Sp remove scouting missions all together and just have the story missions do the scouting as well. This is a large time sink that doesn't bring anything interesting to the table. I'd also change the bounties you need to do in some areas from "5 of any" to "kill each of the three once time". I've accidentally avoided potentially interesting bosses because its just "kill 5 bosses", and needing to kill more than each boss once seems like a time wasting grind. The only visual issue i can think of is its really weird how straight faced the allied races are. Its kind of uncanny running through an allies camp and having them all stare at you with one or two completely still faces. It doesn't help by how dynamic and good the art is in the cut-scenes is either, the contrast makes it worse. The goblins can get away with it because of their many different looks, and you honestly stop looking at them after a while. This game has such charm in so many places, but just too many save breaking bugs and it doesn't feel like it respects my time. I say this as someone who has put 1000s of hours into the Xcom series, many 100s into other games similar to this, and enjoyed many hours into city builders, factory games, and 4x. I specifically like playing time sink games. I think part of the problem is some of the ways this game sinks time makes it feel like a grind, not like your progressing. How to fix that? Not sure. But it needs help.I hope the devs are able to patch this boat up, bail out the water, get their reputation back and get lots of sales.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully thematic piece where art and style carry the simple but likewise thematic gameplay.Many reviews have a fair point, but also one that likely misses the point of a goblin-based game: Longetivity of characters.In Goblin Stone, the theme isn't an individual hero or long-living ones even.  It's the idea of the tribe- the idea that an individual goblin can almost never be truly 'special' or 'legendary', but that as a whole the little greenskins pull together to succeed in feats that others would never expect them capable of- even with lots of death and doom along the way.I enjoy that level of theme, but it does take the attention off of the little guys we do spend a lot of the game staring at.  So I can understand why some people have a harder time engaging when other games like XCOM fulfill the RNG/Hero fantasy urges of us people way better.That being said, if you are a fan of goblins and want to play a good, medium-low difficulty roguelite about a tribe of goblins trying to make it in a wonderfully created world?  I really recommend this.Overall: 7/10For enjoyers of Goblins and the idea of flipping the traditional script on fantasy adventures: 8/10Solid game, loving my purchase.  Keep up the good work, Devs!
