_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE:  As the save issue was fixed, I put quite a few more hours into the game.  While the previously mentioned QoL issues are still present, It is nice to see that they are being taken under consideration.  I want to mention a few additional findings while playing through the game.1) There is an infinite item glitch that I stumbled upon and was able to replicate about 50% of the time.  This can lead to infinite gold & or resources. Without explaining it fully here, it involves the larder & how overflow items that are recovered after a quest are handled.2) Some gems seem to be worth more when broken down into smaller gems. If you start with a large green gem for example, you can break it down into its smallest unit and come out +50% in value when you go to resell. If it were consistent across all gems, it would seem intentional. The fact that is is not makes me think otherwise.3) The game does not know how to auto complete stacked items.  For example: If you have a stack of 17 stone and stack of 5 stone, and you drag and drop the stack of 5 stone onto the 17 stone, the game will tell  you that stone only stacks to 20.  In most modern games the stack would peel off 3 stone from the 5 stone stack, maximize the first stack, and leave you with a stack of 20 stone and 2 stone.  This gets tedious when having to manually spit several stacks of resources into specific piles in order to save room in the larder. This is especially frustrating when you have a full inventory and want to combined items to free up room on a quest.4) Wood seems like a vastly overused material.  The amount of wood that is required compared to the other 5 resources seems disproportional versus the amount of any of the other 5 resources you need relative to the rest.  At this point the game is definitely in a much more playable state. I am going to switch my review to a 'would recommend' but honestly I wish there was a middle option.  I feel that if you enjoy similar games like Darkest Dungeon, you may want to pick this up as it scratches an itch.  But on the other hand, if you enjoy similar games like Darkest Dungeon, you may not enjoy this game as it is lacking some more polish.If the previous QoL issues and the ones mentioned above are eventually resolved, this could shape up to be a really solid title.----------TLDR:  Another Bug.  10 hour save reverted to a save state just after tutorial. - progress wiped.Thankfully I have not had to deal with the bugged tutorial section that many have encountered. However upon loading back into the game today after 10 or so hours of play time, my entire campaign/save file was reverted back to a previous state, about 20 min past the tutorial stage.  This is a deal breaker for me as I can not reasonably push forward without the concern this may happen again.Other things I noticed that while not game breaking, are real QoL issues / minor frustrations.* You can not remap keys* Fullscreen-Windowed forces the game to minimize upon clicking any other window in a multi-monitor setup.* Fullscreen does not keep your cursor contained within the bounds of the fullscreen.* The game seemingly does not support ultrawide monitors.* The game seemingly does not support 4k resolutionI can't recommend this game until the bugs are fixed.  How can anyone play this when your save files aren't guaranteed to work correctly?

_childDocuments_.review: Currently slightly buggy and very grindy, but has a lot of potential.You can do many missions for fairly little gain, mainly construction materials to upgrade your base. If you get fancy weapons or upgrades during an adventure, those are all temporary. Progression happens through breeding/finding better goblins, unlocking more classes and more abilities for those classes.The only way your individual units "level up" is through increasing the amount of "souls" you get when they die or retire. A goblin who has been only on one mission will give 1, which is the same amount you get if you disband them (which is different from retiring because it doesn't take up space in your lair), but bringing them to many missions will get them to 3-4 souls (probably more, 4 is the best I've gotten so far) for when they either get killed or injured enough that you don't bring them anymore. You choose when they retire. I haven't been forced to do so yet, at least.I like the retiring system, and I'm glad that more games like this make sure that losing your troops isn't the end of the run and is actually preferable. For another game that does the same in a different way, check out Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters.Visually, it seems like all the retired goblins end up looking roughly the same as they walk around in their quarters, which is a shame because this mechanic has a ton of potential.Maybe check in on it in a few months? I'm still loving my time with it, but I could see the game being a lot better.

detailed_description: REMEDIUM - OUT NOW IN EARLY ACCESS REMEDIUM: SENTINELS - OUT NOW! SCHOLAR OF THE ARCANE ARTS - OUT NOW IN EARLY ACCESS Join chat in Discord! About the Game Demon Skin - is a brutal hack’n’slash set in a rough dark fantasy world, which combines unique combat mechanics, RPG and fighting game elements, and even some platformer features. With the flexible combat system each player can come up with their own unique tactic by skillfully combining stances with various types of weapons to achieve the ultimate efficiency in battle. The darkness has got into the far off corners of the universe and threatens the world. Only the mighty Order of Wanderers whose members possess superhuman divine powers can resist that threat. One of the Wanderers witnesses a sinister ritual of restoring a powerful ancient artifact. In an attempt to break off the ceremony he gets into a flow of energy released by the artifact and instantly turns into a demon! Wanderer is now eager to regain his former appearance but to do so he needs the artifact which was stolen afterwards. The hero sets on a path to find it, fighting the hordes of demons along the way. Improve your skills by mastering various stances for lightning-fast parrying and inflicting maximum damage with spectacular finishing moves! Keep an eye on the level of stamina and other indicators of the character’s physical condition - all these features directly affect the outcome of the battle. Collect shards of Crystal and become even stronger, build up your bone armor and turn into a fearsome demon. There are more than 30 types of edged and blunt weapons at your disposal and each type is only effective against a certain type of enemies. You can destroy enemies even with your bare hands - it’s not as effective but still a lot of fun! An extensive skill tree. Gain experience to learn new combos and enhance health, stamina, and attack power! Dozens of enemy types. From skeletons, zombies, and spiders to werewolves, lizards, and golems - fighting each of them requires a different approach! Secrets and artifacts. Some rare and ancient artifact weapons are hidden in the secret places of the game world. Find it to unlock the impressive super skills after achieving a certain level! Gloomy landscapes in the spirit of dark fantasy: from the icy wastelands and deep dungeons to the twilight forests and abodes of the undead. This cruel world lives a life of its own, but terrifying creatures that inhabit it are not always hostile. On your way, you will not only meet enemies but also powerful allies!

_childDocuments_.review: One simple concept in a game... if you use checkpoints and you have some sort of boss fight, even a small one, put a checkpoint just before. Not miles away that oblige to re jump a series of platform, to "rediscover" a secret, to re manage your inventory to re throw some swords against ice blocks to re break them, to finally re recover the weapon you re dropped from your inventory to re break that ice and to reapply points in your skill tree for the level you just re earned...This kind of UX does only help to answer the question: Who does that???Consider what follow that question to rarely be a compliment...That deserve a thumb down and make think to a potential refund.That is sad considering the game is coming with nice visuals, a lot of weapons and combos for each including special strikes, plethora of nicely designed monsters, for some staged, bloody finishes, cool secrets...Playability with a controller is also tiedous. Having to block using the right stick while the same fingers are used to strike... That makes the combination of blocks/strikes barely possible for non professional pianists...The block hud spoil the visuals. Try bigger next time to cover more of the screen...Some clippings and other small bugs are present.Music is ok. Sounds also.I am not sure I am going to continue to play it for long since I am not masochist. I may ask for a refund as well.So, I am not going to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Demon Skin~~~~~~~~~~Demon Skin is a fantastic new Hack&Slash game that implements a challenging yet interesting combat system. Demon Skin seems to be trying to combine its unique new combat system, lore, and the overall character-arch to put together a fascinating mixture of dark aged souls-like experience. Although the game is very early on in its age, and certainly not without its flaws, from where I stand it seems to be in capable hands, constantly trying to polish off the rough edges, which is very comforting to see. I will discuss more of the game’s current issues later on in the review but for now, Demon Skin seems like a mature enough platform that can be shaped into something much greater than it currently is. Plot: The world slowly falls into the darkness. Dark demons and entities start to cover the world and beyond. The dark powers start to perform a dark and sinister ritual to restore a powerful ancient artifact. Witnessing this unholy sight is the mighty Order of Wanderers, whose members possess superhuman divine powers. Only the Wanderers can resist these unholy powers and rituals. Seeing an unholy ritual, a brave-hearted Wanderer jumps in; in an attempt to break off the ceremony he gets into a flow of energy released by the artifact and instantly turns into a demon!Eager to restore his former glory, the demonized Wanderer sets off to find the artifact that will restore him as well as removing all the unholy power from the face of the earth.  Gameplay: The game starts off with a short yet brilliant intro that pretty much sums up the game's plot nicely, but with terrible voice-over and sound effects. You wake up as a degraded demon with a broken soul but with enough rage, anger and will to keep on fighting until you regain your former glory. As you go through each demon and unholy creature, you start to regain some form of sanity, structure, and strength to keep on fighting and face off stronger foes.  Regaining some strength and structure in your body by killing demons, you also get melee weapons. There are few types of weapons available but in multiple variations and in varying stages of upgrade.Each different type of weapon, with the variety of upgrades, was supposed to be effective against different types of enemies, but that didn’t really seem to be the case. A weapon with high enough DPS was enough to get through most. Also, there is a skill upgrade system available that helps boost the player’s state in exchange for points obtained throughout combat. This system helps with player stamina, attack rate, etc. Combat system: Now let’s get into the cream of the crop, Demon Skin’s unique take on hack&slash combat system. Demon Skin’s combat system is simple yet unique with its three combat stances, combined with movement, unlockable combos, artifacts, unique items and skills. As you face an enemy, you have the option of attacking using heavy or melee blade weapons in three different areas - Head, Mid-section and Legs - while at the same time blocking incoming attacks by simply pointing the mouse crosshair at the level of the incoming attack (which will be indicated). Although this blocking system works, it’s neither efficient nor convenient. I would’ve preferred a key or a right-mouse-click blocking system instead, and this system's animation seemed to be poorly done as well. The Combos work just fine and are very powerful if performed in a timely manner. While playing with keyboard and mouse the combos are performed with mouse left-click attack and attack level adjustment, which is rather annoying to use. But on the other hand, it’s pretty enjoyable and easy with a controller. I would recommend sticking to a controller for Demon Skin. Demons and Bosses: A variety of well-designed demons and bosses with a decent amount of combat capabilities and a fair amount of challenge for the player.  The only downside here is the animations, that are pretty rough and could be improved upon. Music and sound effects: Let’s just say, it’s not quite there yet, and needs a lot of work. And the same goes for the few voice-over bits available in this game. Positives: + Decent plot+ Unique, enjoyable hack&slash + Well-designed demons and bosses+ Skill system plays an important role+ The fights are challenging but not too much+ Decent progression system + Controllers work just fine+ Atmospheric Negative: - Voiceovers need to be redone - The blocking system could be improved- The attack animations could be improved - Sound effects could be improved - Unpolished in quite a few areas In a world ravaged by darkness and unholy powers, a brave-heart wanderer must step in to face the Demons of darkness. 7/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to recommend this game with the caveat that you do not expect it to be a simple hack and slash side scroller.  There is an element of puzzle combat, matching the stances of your enemies to block.  The system is a bit clunky at first till you begin to understand the intended game play.  I was a bit confused, I thought I had to use R stick to switch stances, but just hitting the corresponding attack button (Y for upper, X for middle, and A for lower) it automatically switches the stance for you.  It's a slow steady paced game that draws you in with consistent progress and learning.  You will die a lot finding the right jumps but it is never so punishing or difficult that you don't learn from your mistakes or get stuck and can't move forward. It keeps track of every death even if you go back to a previous load just to experiment with a section...so keep that in mind...I racked up an extra 15 deaths thinking there might be a way to kill the werewolf you run into at the end of the level after racing an avalanche behind you....It might be possible if you put all of your level points into attack before you get there.... Just a heads up.  I did not do that. Full price, I would say it's a bit of a niche recommendation, but on sale, I would recommend anyone try it out for a change of pace from the usual hack and slash fare.**EDIT: After coming back to the game again, I remember why I put it down and I wonder who I was when I wrote my previous review.  The game is terrible.  Absolutely terrible.  Completely unresponsive controls.  Unexplained attributes of weapons.  Just terrible.  And totally abandoned by the devs.  If you like games that cannot figure out what they want to be or how to be fun, and if maybe its on sale for 90% off, maybe flip a coin on it before you buy.

name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed
detailed_description: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed brings the magic of Disney to life in a vibrant 3D platformer. This beautiful remake sends Mickey Mouse on an epic journey through Wasteland, a realm of forgotten Disney characters. As Mickey, you will dive into a fantastical world and, armed with paint and thinner, shape your adventure and the fate of this alternate world. Every stroke of your magic brush matters! Use paint to restore beauty and harmony or thinner to alter your environment and uncover hidden secrets. Your choices influence Mickey's destiny and change the outcome of this artistic odyssey. Will you become the epic hero Wasteland needs? Encounter various iconic characters like Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, Walt Disney’s first creation, as you travel between lands in Wasteland. Collect virtual Disney pins, tackle creative challenges, and uncover secrets, all while exploring classic platforming levels inspired by animated films and shorts. Originally envisioned by Warren Spector, reimagined by Purple Lamp, Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed employs state-of-the-art visuals and improved controls to breathe new life into a beloved classic. Experience new movement skills for Mickey, such as dash, ground pound and sprinting. The game’s compelling story makes it an unforgettable adventure for long-time fans and newcomers alike. Join Mickey Mouse and unravel the mysteries of Wasteland in this homage to Disney's legacy. Explore a reimagined Wasteland, full of Disney's timeless characters and stories. Wield the magic brush: Paint to create, thinner to alter. Every choice shapes your story. Meet Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, Disney's original star, in a rich, narrative-driven world. Enjoy advanced gameplay with new abilities and enhanced visuals in a classic setting. Mickey has new moves such as dash, ground pound and sprinting. High replayability with multiple endings based on your unique playstyle and decisions.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, THQN is being THQN here, charging $60 for the game despite its release being very close to several flagship games, including some lower-priced titles like Frostpunk 2 or Lollipop Chainsaw (priced at $40). They do this with their collector’s editions as well, and most end up as dead stock despite being marketed as limited in quantity. And yet, they will keep doing this. I have no clue why but it's their characteristic. While I cannot justify the price tag, long story short, Epic Mickey is a very good game. A bit annoying at times, but still a journey that is somewhat fulfilling and worth exploring. You can expect about 15 hours of playtime if you want to complete almost everything. It’s one of the best remasters I’ve played—competent and seemingly very true to the core.Epic Mickey: Rebrushed comes from , the artisans behind  and  The original Epic Mickey was crafted by the now-defunct  to be a classic flagship game for Wii. I will always respect —not just for his work in creating one of my favorite genres, immersive sims, but also for his involvement in one of the all-time greats: Deus Ex. Of course, at the time, many were surprised to see Warren getting involved with Epic Mickey until he would eventually reveal that it was a dream of his. Who can judge him, everyone loves cartoons, right? Warren's vision is definitely present in this game. You mess around, and you find out—almost like an ImSim. I love it, I really do. Of course, I wasn't expecting it to reach the complexity of Warren's previous works, but I was pleasantly surprised by the level manipulation mechanics. You have a brush that can thin the world’s layers or repaint what is alreay thinned. Doing this changes the environment and adds complexity to the levels, allowing you to discover collectibles and new ways to traverse. However, while there are multiple options—thus fulfilling part of Warren's vision—the levels never quite evolve in complexity. By complexity, I mean utilizing your abilities to skip portions of a level (similar to how Prey’s goo gun lets you do) or creating unique vantage points. While Epic Mickey offers some choices, they aren’t as expansive. You can select between a certain array of options, sure. There are ‘Thin’ and ‘Paint’ paths (a sort of quasi-morality system), which you unlock by completing quests in various ways (though you can also fail them if you don't finish before progressing to the next area). Painting (befriending) or thinning (defeating) enemies has a slight effect, but the truth is, combat isn’t challenging. You can spam paint all over the place and befriend almost everyone, except for the Beetleworx types of enemies, which can’t be befriended. Thinning them out of existence is an easy task so not being able to befriend them is not quite a feat. The lack of meaningful impact from your approach to combat is ultimately disappointing. And while you can manipulate certain parts of the levels, the limitation that only specific areas can be thinned or painted makes things painfully obvious. If I had played this as a kid, I might have gotten lost a few times. It's not overly cryptic, but there are moments when backtracking or finding ‘objects’ to complete quests is required. Now, though, it’s just a matter of running into them as I spread paint everywhere like a mad man. A prominent con is that the levels reset to their initial state after you exit them (the objectives you have completed of course do stay but the paint will be gone) and it's kept like that in this remaster too. Speaking of quests, it’s great that this game includes plenty of side quests, though most are ‘fetch me this, fetch me that’ tasks. Even the main quests often involve some form of hidden object hunting. This gives the game a bit of an early 2000s sandbox collectathon feel. I don’t have a serious problem with this, as some of my favorite platformers (A Hat in Time, Spyro, Banjo-Kazooie) do it as well. However, the collectibles don’t feel as rewarding, nor are they crucial to collect. There's barely any fear of missing out. You'd be opening up bunch of chests and buying some 'unlockables' from the shop but they don't even count towards any achievement. Though the extra stuff does include some cool artworks etc. Some side quests reward you with health or paint upgrades, or they provide a ‘spark’ needed to repair projectors and progress to the next level. So, I rarely felt like I was wasting my time by completing side quests.The 2D levels ooze charisma. You need to traverse through these in order to progress to the next 3D level. While it's a creative idea, these levels are very short and lack challenge. There are far too many of them, and you may have to revisit some locations multiple times. E-Tickets (the in-game currency) always respawn in these levels, allowing you to grind hence making the best out of your time, but playing them back to back only highlights how limited their scope is, which further trivializes their importance, even though they differ thematically. . The 3D levels are often open areas (though not particularly large), with questlines usually chaining 3 to 4 similarly themed levels. Most having quests exclusive to each level (either acquired through the main hub or through in-level). Personally, I would have preferred larger areas for each theme and fewer (but longer) 2D levels, possibly featuring boss fights at the end. But that’s just me. The bosses are fun, but they lack meaningful gameplay elements—you can thin or paint them, but this doesn’t really create any emergent gameplay during the fight. The game also includes multiple hub areas, with one arguably serving as the main one.The camera, from what I’ve read, was a major issue in the original game. It seems completely fixed now, and the game runs smoothly on Unreal Engine. I encountered one animation bug where I got stuck, but I was able to break free.The soundtrack is good and dynamic, shifting from light to dark as you progress through the levels. It's very artsy and colorful game, contributing to the magical world of Disney. The cutscenes are well-done and look astonishing in particular. And now you can photo mode all of these. The story is serviceable for what Epic Mickey sets out to be, surprisingly an emotional one though the lack of voice acting is a bit disappointing, as it could have added a lot to the game’s overall charm and the tone.All in all, Epic Mickey Rebrushed deserves a chance. Not an all-time great platformer (inevitably looking at Sunshine) by any means but it's a fun, memorable and intelligent one. Trivia: I believe Warren labels this as a sim-lite. Of course being the one who coined the term and also being the director of the game it's hard to argue against such claim. While there is not really a consensus on the term of ImSim, it could have been relatively harder to market this game as one but Warren is most definitely set this game out to combine the said genre with a platform in a mainstream IP and some of these are rooted in his words back in time. I personally feel a sandbox collectathon is also a great term to use colloquially because there are lots of shared aspects and the lovers of that genre will know what to expect. ★★★½☆☆

Other than that this game is magnificent and I highly recommend you play it, THQ and Purple Lamps team did fantastic and I trust that the Epic Mickey franchise will rise from its slumber with a Epic Mickey 2 Rebrushed and Possibly Epic Mickey 3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for Disney lovers. Not just people who like Disney - people who LOVE Disney, Disney history, Disney parks, Disney characters. This game is for us. You'll be able to thoroughly enjoy it even if you aren't a Disney lover - but the details will really stand out to the hardcore fans. If you're like me, this game might be why you become a hardcore fan. The original did that for me.This is a remake of one of my favorite games ever made, and in my opinion it withstands the test of time. 3D platforming, simple yet effective combat, your-choice-matters, puzzles, hidden secrets to find and hunt down ... it's got a ton of amazing gameplay mechanics. The characters are lovable, the plot is fun and easy to follow (but not too simplistic), there is plenty to do and see, and many beautiful worlds to explore. Each world is a twisted reimagining of beloved Disney parks destinations. Be warned that this is the sort of game that will hold you hand a little - mostly by giving you some wide view shots of each level when you enter it, which gives you a chance to see where "hidden" items are or may be. I've heard some people found this annoying, but I didn't mind it at all. I just love this game. It changed my life when I was 12, and now at 27, I am getting the thrill of enjoying it all over again - elevated. It's been a joy. Epic Mickey: Rebrushed is not a game that has to take you a long time to beat, so I really recommend you try it out and see for yourself why I love it so much!

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Epic Mickey as a 12yo who had been obsessively following the development of the game since I was ten. This remaster is everything I wanted and more - the art direction is gorgeous, the controls are fluid even though I'm playing keyboard + mouse, and the quality of life features added keep the game moving. At parts where I'm expecting a loading screen for a few seconds out of instinct, it instead loads in a second or less. Gus no longer asks if you want to enter into doors meaning getting in and out of subareas like shops and houses is much faster. The sparkling around the borders of thinned items makes aiming easier. I got a huge wave of nostalgia seeing they kept the old jade elephant in the ice cream parlor even though the one in Disneyland has been removed for a while.I may come back and add more, but suffice to say I played this game many times as a child and I'm definitely going to be playing it many more times as an adult.UPDATE (SPOILERS): I've finished my first playthrough. H-h-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Really good game. Excellent remake. Best remake ever. The inside of the Blot? Just as ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up as ever. The additional details of pieces of Wasteland inside of him and the blot-toons being recognizable as who they once were (Noticed when I caught eye of Petetronic's silhouette)... chilling. Very much a '♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ he's eating people' moment. I do like how they made it so you can still jump on top of the bloticles to avoid the enemies because being cornered by blot minions is pretty deadly in there. Only two things I'm disappointed with: One, the golden e-tickets no longer have Oswald on them, they're all Mickey. Like c'mon man, getting the golden tickets doesn't hit as hard without Oswald's silhouette. Two, in the very ending area, Oswald is now animated and looking around - you can't talk to him. He should've had dialogue if he was conscious. In the Wii version he was basically frozen and like yeah sure if he's frozen he can't talk - but he's conscious in this version and I Wanted To Talk To Him So Badly. I guess to broaden that, I was really hoping for new content to help flesh out Wasteland, and while you'll NEVER catch me complaining about how this is a good remake I was hoping they'd dig a little deeper. So I guess this is a sign for the developers PLEASE make a DLC. PLEASE make a DLC that digs EVEN DEEPER into Wasteland's lore and digs even deeper into this dark side of cartoons. I'd start giving ideas, but I know if I say anything and the devs read it they can't use it, just PLEASE don't destroy the original mood and vibe of Wasteland. Wasteland is a grumpy, dejected place, even after it was restored by the destruction of the Blot - and that's why I like it so much! It's why I fell in love with the game as a kid! It was a 'finally, a piece of media that isn't forcing me to be happy!' moment which, ironically, is what made me happy!  Anyways, off to 100%ing this game. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: **If you're thinking about getting the game as someone who's played it on the Wii version, then here is a lil review to look over:I thought about it long and hard, and have concluded that if you want to get the game for the experience... then I think it is worth it. Whether you think the 60 is pushing it is up to you, but having the game at all times and anywhere, with THIS game specifically was okay for me.But looking past that price tag, the experience part is something that I didn't expect. Put it this way, the experience is completely enhanced and better, but because of the faults of the original Wii version.Realistically, you LOVE this game for the world and characters. BUT, the game-play itself made it hard to just enjoy it solely for that. Oh you remember the camera... it was awful!Sometimes the game fought you and that is why you never really 100% the game, you only pushed through that to get to the story because of how much you enjoyed it.Of course there were other things like how sometimes aiming with the controller was wonky or would aim a completely different way, or maybe the "morality" system didn't have as much of an influence and could have enhanced the story further.**Point being:  The Wii had plenty of issues, and only really stuck with the people who loved this iteration of Mickey, and this cartoon world in ruin.** I am one of them.On to the part where the experience took me by surprise, it controls REALLY well.Now hold on, I mean Mickey himself is very nice to move with, and the move from Wii to the cross-hairs really worked out!     (I'll explain the little hiccup the game has later on)That alone has made this playthrough so different, it was really just the controls.Going from a broken adjusting camera, to a standard control has done wonders and DOES have an effect on how I enjoyed this game series. I LOVED playing this time, I was in control and wasn't being held back anymore, I could just go and play. No dread!I felt like I was finally PLAYING the game for what it was and taking in everything, of course with the help of the new look.Playing the game, without that constant camera feedback has made it much easier to soak in, and is why I do think playing it this way does enhance how you perceived it on the Wii version. Check it out!Moving on,I want to expand on the game play real quick.I don't need to go further into the issues with the Wii, but let me just say that if you are hoping that it has some cool gimmicks like what the Wii tried offering, then tough luck because it really is just some standard game play outside of what the GAME has to offer with paint and thinner.The entire point of the Wii was to be an independent console with its own features, that was the selling point, so going in with an expectation of carrying over those features (assuming you ignored the trailers) is kind of pointless, so be open to this new layout.And if you think that the game needs something unique to make it more interesting (game-play wise), I kind of agree!!It's an "Epic" game so you'd want to maximize what the game could offer, and I completely get that and somewhat wish it had that now that I have experienced it playing and running the way it did.However, the game itself offering the paint and thinner, and a couple new move sets, is probably all they could do to keep the game the way it was without having to make major changes, defeating the purpose of keeping it true to the book.On top of that, if you just wanted that CHANGE for the sake of making the game-play have more to offer, then I'm afraid that this just isn't the game for that.THIS version of Epic Mickey was created for that story and is going to continue to be that way, which stinks for me too because I now want MORE.If we were to get that, it would have to be an entirely new Epic Mickey game that was made to function with more/better game-play and still have a very good narrative and story to follow.This one keeps things simple, and if you want more, the game will need more. Simple as that.Oh, and a quick thought on the new visuals being more polished and *BRIGHT*, it does grow a bit. Going back to the Wii, it was just rustic and darker, and I think it added more to the atmospheric feel of it being devastating which I still love to this day. However, despite the new colorful look putting a sense of worry into how the game would feel, it actually works fairly well. In fact, the color tones contrasting the way they do add to how diminished some things in the game are. I will say it is still preference, but it doesn't lose that essence.You get used to it fairly quick, and feels a little more fleshed out.***Now for the NEW GAME ISSUES***Of course, the remake is still young so there are bound to be issues. Some I expected and a few I didn't.Remember earlier when I said the controls feel good, they really do.That hiccup I was going to mention was actual the world you move in. By no means is it funky or anything, however, I have had several occasion where I was almost soft-locked, and was actually locked once. THAT is an issue.You'll notice if you play that you like to move more now that the controls are better, that means your jumping everywhere... a lot.And several times, I was stuck in a falling animation because I either failed a jump or slid back down between two things and couldn't move for a little bit, and on one occasion I was turning a gargoyle to aim a beam and tried to jump around it, but in the process I got caught on the wall and was soft-locked.BUT REALLY QUICK, getting locked isn't all that bad because of how damn often the game saves. I collected a pin before jumping and got locked, so I just reloaded and I didn't lose any progress, so the game was lucky with that one...Either way, it does make it so that as I play I am more conscience of where I *try* to explore in the hopes my character doesn't get stuck for a little bit.It's weird, it should be a big issue but given how the save works, it isn't the end of the world, still a problem.Other weird moments are from hanging. When you try to hop on a platform but catch the edge, you simply lift yourself. Easy... Buuuuut there are some moments where you hang and suddenly can't unhang? I haven't gotten locked that way, nor will I because it's not like I'm wedged, but getting stuck hanging for a decent amount of time does make my tiny brain start thinking I am. This isn't common but can happen once in a while.^These are some issues I believe they can iron out easily so I am not too worried^These being the only major issues so far is kind of a good thing, if they continue updating.**Okay now these issues... are just silly hahaI do enjoy going though the collectibles, but sometimes I see a typing error which can take me by surprise. I don't know how long it takes for them to notice stuff like this, but the "Just Friends" pin says "firends" in the description which is pretty funny.OH, but I will say that there is a slight problem with the extra content, whenever you get to an animated cut scene, there is a movie section that lets you re-watch them when you unlock them.But sometimes they just don't unlock.For example, the goofy animation of him being repaired I have, but the previous one where you just talk to him is locked. Weird. Not really an issue but if you wanted to watch a particular one and its still locked, I guess there is a problem.The final thing would be performance, it's smooth for most of the game, but there can be some frame drops at bigger fights. Kind of expected tho lol Man I said a lot, but that is just because I grew up with the series and love to see it get some new life.  I'd say it is worth the purchase to replay the game in the new look and controls, it keeps the charm... hell I think at moments it adds to the charm. Still love Epic Mickey!

_childDocuments_.review: THQ Nordic continue their streak of amazing remasters and sequels - after the Spongebob Games, Outcast, Jagged Alliance, or Destroy all Humans they deliver yet another banger with Epic Mickey Rebrushed.A remeaster that is faithful to the charm and joy early Disney games and cartoons evoked, switching from 3D and 2D platforming action in a colourful and sweet environment. The game is never too difficult (it doesn't intend to be) but always just enough to not be trivial. The levels allow for exploration and the discovery of secrets, the controls are crisp and sharp on an Xbox Elite Controller and the game is just an utter delight to play.You can tell how much love and work Purple Lamp has put into this game and how important it was for them to be faithful to the original from 2010. I found myself playing way past my usual bedtime without realizing how much time had passed and am looking forward to continuing when I come home from work today.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally finishing the game after 2 days here are my reviewsPros: This game is super nostalgic for people who played on the Wii, im super happy I got to finish the game 13 years later before my wii broke on me. There graphics are a lot better, and helpful when it comes to sometimes seeing using your thinner. Cons: It is a little bit easier to play on controller, so I would recommend that.  When finding the animatronic parts it is a little bit harder as they are not in the chests like last game. The game is easily finishable so its not worth to some the $60 for a 12 hour straight gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Finally after 14 years, we get to experience the Wii cult classic Disney Epic Mickey on modern systems!This game is a pure passion project filled with content and love. The story, the world, the characters, the choices and the music are simply divine! (And the best side-scrolling levels ever)It's something you have to experience yourself!I really hope that many people will enjoy this game as I did. The sheer amount of good memories I have with this game cannot be described by words alone!

_childDocuments_.review: I am completely and utterly biased: I had the original as a kid and practically grew up on it, I played it so many times. Seeing it completely redone graphics and gameplay-wise has made me extremely happy. It's such an incredible upgrade from what the game started out as. I was tearing up during the end credits just looking at all the concept art and the people who came together to make this game better than it was when it first came out.The graphics and set design are absolutely spectacular. There are some levels that get a big redesign and it adds so much personality to the game. I also love the change in lighting. The parts that are Paint are very bright and it contrasts so well compared to the parts that are "thinned." It really conveys the feeling of you exploring a half-demolished theme park that is past its prime.I didn't come across too many bugs, but there were some that are notable enough to mention here:- Tiki Sam has a quest where you have to find his Tiki masks. I found his masks. I returned them to him. He proceeded to ask me again to get his masks and then gave me the silent treatment until I went to Skull Island and came back. Guess he didn't like being told that I can't get him more Tiki masks?- The debris from things you break can actually block your Paint or Thinner stream. This is such a minor nitpick but as someone who loves to dash around, break things, and then immediately paint or thin things, I often got caught on these debris.- In the final castle area of the game, a part didn't load, leaving only a window far off in the distance with no floor or anything else. I understand the Blot wants to demolish me but cmon bro you didn't need to disappear the whole castle- (thankfully the fix for this was easy, just had to backtrack a bit and get the shy part of the castle to load in)Other than that, I've had an absolutely fantastic time playing this game, getting nostalgic for the past, and enjoying all of the things that the present version has to offer. I am absolutely going to be dumping too much time into this game to collect everything and get all the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: This is peak fr fr. I went in expecting a nostalgic experience and mediocre story, but I was pleasantly surprised to see that this game hold up surprisingly well. While the gameplay can be a tad tedious at times, there werent many moments that I wasnt having a good time. This game shines mostly through the design and story, using some of the most unique approaches to gaming I've seen in a long time. The two ending system and granting you a choice is probably the best plot device I have seen naturally used in a game. Nothing feels shoehorned in and every aspect has lots of charm and care.

That, the missing Bog Easy music and a couple other audio nitpicks, this game surpasses all my expectations! I can’t get enough of this masterpiece though! Astonishing work from everyone and thank you for recreating my childhood!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me just preface this by saying that yes, I am biased, as the original was one of the first games I ever played as a child, and it holds a special place in my heart.With that being said, I still recommend this game. Is it perfect? No. Is it worth checking out? Heck yes. I'm not even much of a platformer person, but it's still worth it, if only for the visuals and atmosphere. And the soundtrack, man I love it.Now, for those of us who have played the OG, there are some various differences, like all mention of anything related to the Wii being sort of obviously cut out, some music tracks not matching the correct timings, (e.g. Bog Easy just plays the generic Lonesome Manor music rather than it's special track, Oswald's room in Mickeyjunk Mountain plays the generic ambience rather than his theme, the music timing for raising Smee's boat and the cutscene to the Jolly Roger is off, etc.) and some very minor touches, (pickup noises or paint/thinner being highlighted when trying to pick up another one when full) but overall it's very well done.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is downright amazing. I have wanted a remake of this game for so long ever since Junction Point closed. Purple Lamp did such an outstanding job with the visuals. Everything from the original is back and reworked to make it better and I think it's done really well. I love Mickey's new abilities and the option to skip some of the 2D projector sections. 10/10 in my opinion. I hope they also make a remake of the second game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Epic Mickey Rebrushed means alot to me. The original 2010 game being my first that I have ever finished in my life. So when the I heard of the game being remastered I was pumped with joy. The game came out in 24'th of September and I finished it in 3 days (which I am suprised myself).The game overall has a great soundtrack, really good 3D platforming feats compared to other titles in the genre, improved graphics and enviroments compared to the original 2010 version and just a fun game to play. They somehow kept the original feel and likenes from the 2010 version which I applause for them.This game was my childhood and I am beyond happy that I finished it 14 years later.PS: I am gonna play the game a second time to get all of the collectibles.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5 Get it right now what are you doingI literally can't put the game down. I said I would get off to eat like 45 mins ago and I still want to play more. Very faithful remake of the wii game Epic Mickey, so fluid and fun to play and the story is pulling.  Fantastic, love the elements of Disney History and the portrayal of the characters. Perfect, and has remapping. Admittedly moves like the dash and ground pound are kinda useless when we now have a run, but still fun to mess with and dash everywhere. Menus look fantastic and are not confusing. GORGEOUS. Run down Disney Land and it looks so cool and colourful, I want to explore everything. Jim Dooley is a fantastic composer, they used the same music as the original, but it sounds so good you wouldn't notice its from the Wii era. Main menu music is a bit repetitive tho :( Really simple achievements, you don't have to go out of your way. So unbelievable fun and addictive. My only issue is I miss the hearts being little mickeys. Also there seems to be a couple audio issues, theyve fixed a lot of them though.Overall, fantastic game and remake of EM1. Go play it if you've never played an epic mickey game, but like platformers and story based games. Definitely go play it if you played EM1 on the Wii as a kid and feel super nostalgic for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Epic Mickey is a game I hold dear to my heart. I remember the day I got surprised with this game after getting home from school and seeing previews of it online. Now looking back to the reveal of the remake I was shocked this game would ever get a re-release let alone a full on remake after so many years. This remake is what every Epic Mickey fan could ever want. It improves the games controls, improves a lot of the originals visuals while staying faithful to the original games art direction, and irons out a lot of the flaws the original had. If you had a bad time with the original with the clunky camera, pointer controls, and slow platforming this will fix ALL of those problems. The only problem I have with this remake isn't even a flaw with the game, but a flaw with the pricing. I was happy to pay 60 dollars for this game as it's something I've waited well over a decade for, but for people wanting to get into the franchise the 60 dollar price tag is pretty steep. Especially when the original game was only 40. On the bright side THQ games are pretty quick to go on sale and even for the price I think 60 dollars is pretty fair for how much you get out of Epic Mickey. I've only done 1 run of the game and got a good chunk of time and still need to do the thinner route.

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid this game was my absolutely my favourite game, I kep replaying it over and over never tiring of it, I was following this games process when there was talks about a remake and as soon I saw you could pre-purchase it, I bought it without a second thought. And me being such a fan, when I saw the first trailer of this game I cried, happiness of this game finally seeing the light. The small change I noticed with a surprise is the added feature of the paint drying, when you paint something you get the effect of it being wet and after a few seconds it dries up! the devs also added an extra effect around paint-able surfaces with "glitter" around the edges making it more obvious where you can paint or not. As a kid I always feared the end part of the game as it was being too hard - still think it is - but purple lamp changed that around and made it so much easier and actually fun. The graphics are gorgeous and very deserving of such a nostalgic and amazing game, and the added "aim" help when fighting bosses was a small change but with a big impact. I completely love the art the purple lamp devs have put in and the QoL changes with dash and stomp it adds something extra to the platforming and also making the combat much easier.I was fearing this game would be released and having many game-breaking bugs like crashes or missing elements or such but to my surprise this game is very polished! with a few graphical errors here and there but that´s something I can overlook. I´ve been longing for this day for a very long time, and the result is breathtaking!  I urge anyone who like this kind of genre to get this game, being a new player or a OG player. Now as someone else mentioned on here I do hope purple lamp - together with Warren Spector - remake epic mickey 2, that game also needs love, being the fact it was rushed and not properly done, but for now I hope purple lamp can get proper rest for amazing work done. I give this game a solid 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who wants to play Epic Mickey: Rebrushed on the Steam Deck, you need to force Steam to launch it in Proton 8.05 as well as putting "-d3d11" in the launch options. If you do not do this then you will get black screen crashes whenever you try to enter a projector or the Cinema.For my actual review, I say that if I were to choose a good example of a faithful remake, I would pick Epic Mickey: Rebrushed. This remake keeps to the original game's core mechanics of painting and thinning objects and enemies in the Wasteland. They kept the decaying vibe of the forgotten world and the colorful cartoony visage nearly the same as the original art direction, though I wish that they dialed down the saturation a bit. They added quality of life changes such as adding fixed camera angles for boss fights and platforming. The best QoL change by far is the Cinema which now lets you replay projector levels that you may have missed as well as any collectibles in there. Speaking of collectibles, they went all-out on making some of the most beautiful concept art and backdrops I have seen from Epic Mickey. As much as I praised Epic Mickey: Rebrushed, I have quite a few complaints about the game starting with the Collectibles. They stepped in the right direction when they made the Cinema have replayable projector levels because you can easily mess up on collectibles in the original. So what I don't understand is how they added Collectibles that are even more missable. Rant: A few minor nitpicks include the reuse of the animated cutscenes, especially the tutorial ones. Remember how the original Epic Mickey was made for the Nintendo Wii and how the tutorial cutscenes showed which Wii buttons to use as well as the motions for it? Well, the developers decided to edit those out so it is either Mickey just swinging an invisible rod or a blank chalkboard. Another minor nitpick is the skins, you are just giving us two hats for the default Mickey to wear. Just the hats.Overall, I would recommend it especially if you have played the original Epic Mickey. I feel like this game is a solid remake but if you're playing it on Steam Deck then you'd need to do what I said in the beginning or else you'll be stuck.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think anything I say could do this game justice, so buckle up for this yap fest. Epic Mickey: Rebrushed outdoes the original in many aspects. It is an absolute masterpiece, true to the original for the most part, with a few changes that were necessary to make it even more enjoyable. If you're a fan of Epic Mickey you will (most likely) not be disappointed by this remake, and if you’re new to the series you will absolutely enjoy it.From a purely gameplay perspective, it is so much smoother to play. The camera is a million steps up from the original game, which is wonderful considering that was the major issue most people had with it.  The new movement mechanics are really useful in many situations, especially sprinting. Ground pound felt a little unnecessary from the beginning but I eventually learned its uses later on and grew to love it. The new ability to jump higher using the spin attack proved very useful in many areas of the game, however it seemed that a lot of the jumps required the player to master this change most people wouldn’t even know existed. Some jumps require pixel-perfect accuracy in order to make. This makes it difficult to get all the collectibles in some of the side-scrolling levels especially. Other than this, the rest of the game felt significantly easier than the original, and the challenging aspect isn’t really there,  however, this change is good in certain situations because the original did have some frustratingly difficult time based challenges.Looking at just the visuals and audio, it is absolutely stunning. Gorgeous graphics. It seems that they took a less scary, more child-friendly approach on the designs of some of the enemies, but they still look really good so no complaints from me. The OST is the same as the original game, which I love (thank you Jim Dooley). Sometimes the transition between neutral and dark/light/combat themes is a bit jarring and could be a bit smoother but it’s not a big issue. From the perspective of a hardcore fan of the franchise, overall it is wonderful and I am satisfied with how the game turned out to be. However, while the game is super true to the original, there have been some changes that can be seen as either good or not so good depending on the player’s preference.Here’s a list of some changes that I felt were absolutely necessary:The third-person perspective.Toon objects that you’ve painted/thinned in areas of wasteland stay painted/thinned after leaving and returning to that same area. Gus doesn’t stop you mid-gameplay to tell you something you already knew, his hints are optional to read.Higher jump is possible by using the spin attack after the double jump.Sprinting and dashing were absolutely needed considering how slow Mickey runs.The option to skip projector screens you’ve already run through.No forced camera during the tutorial segment.The extra tombstones outside Lonesome Manor are hilarious.Oswald inside the blot actually moves and isn’t a stationary object fused with the wall.You can temporarily knock down the lost souls in the blot by spin attacking them. Thank you, those things are the stuff of nightmares.Now, here’s a list of some of the changes that I felt were unnecessary:WHY IS THE STORM BLOT SO DAMN FINE YOU DID NOT NEED TO MAKE HIM BUILT LIKE THAT ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 🥵Many of the original puzzles are significantly easier or nonexistent.Guardian guidance doesn’t consume a guardian anymore.Guardians are much easier to attract.Using the opposite material (paint/thinner) changes all 3 guardians forms at once instead of them disappearing one by one and reappearing as the opposite type. (Does that make sense? Sorry, I don’t know how to word it.)The way befriended enemies work is a bit odd? I guess it makes more sense than the original for painted enemies to paint other enemies, but still removes the challenge from blotling fights.Enemies not being able to thin out befriended enemies is also an odd change.You can kill the bunny children now. Why?The slobbers continue sucking til the end of time and don’t do much else anymore.And here is a list of things that I feel should have been changed but were not:Having to fail some quests in order to complete others. Should just remove the other one from your booklet instead.Prescott needs more attitude.The chest animation does not need to happen every single time you open a chest please.Guardian guidance should be entirely removed because it doesn’t really serve a real purpose. The game tells you what to do anyway.Finally, here’s a list of some bugs and little annoyances that I discovered:Requires quite a powerful PC if playing the steam version, otherwise will crash most times you go through projector screens.100%ing certain things in the game is impossible due to the way New Game+ works.The Great Big Tomorrow slobber took 1 shot to defeat, I don’t think that’s supposed to happen??????????????????Ventureland projector keeps bluescreening my PC, so that’s fun.Achievement for defeating all bloticles happens before defeating all bloticles.Lost souls attack the bloticles for some reason.Sweepers inside the blot will paint each other without you even doing anything. I was doing a thinner run, I did not paint any of them.And that is about all I can think of. Overall, super fun, I will be playing every day for the rest of my life. Thank you Purple Lamp and THQnordic for this work of art that Epic Mickey fans have been praying for for what feels like an eternity. I hope Epic Mickey 2: Rebrushed is a possibility not too far out of reach!

_childDocuments_.review: Epic Mickey: Rebrushed is near one-to-one Remake of an Astounding 3D Platformer that had some unfortunate problems back in it's initial 2010 release. Epic Mickey: Rebrushed is absolutely a game that you need to play, or at the VERY LEAST pick up when on-sale. I look forward to seeing how Purple Lamp Studios and THQ Nordic continue to develop this amazing series.

_childDocuments_.review: It passed 13 years since that our famous cartoon character used to paint his environment across whimsical yet haunting world. Being only available on the Wii console at the time of its original release, a lot of people, including myself, probably missed out on this enchanting painterly adventure crafted by Warren Spector. However, with this remake edition, the long-forgotten world off Disney characters has been given a new life making it more accessible to a new generation of players as well as may to bring back fond memories for long-time fans.The whole brush mechanic is essentially quite fascinating in a platformer game. Using either blue or green liquids to spray around the environment, it allows for a unique level of interaction that gives you a freedom to shape new ways forward. E.g.  removing walls you may discovered hidden collectibles or repairing parts of machinery can help you through level segments. The influence of Super Mario Sunshine not to mention old school 2D Mario and other games such as Banjo & Kazooie, is quite evident.The game is segmented into multiple new areas connected by one hub-world, but none of them are big. No matter if it’s 3D world or 2D segment that serves as in between connection, everything feels relatively small where each of which gives its own charm. If you’re type of player who wants to discover every corner, it’s very good way of design as you never get lost and overwhelmed by what to do.When it comes to quest’s, the game is fairly linear and progression comes down to the fact that each time you have to flirt with a character to get info where to go and what to do, while also figuring out how best to accomplish the mission. Spending a good 8 to 10 hours, makes it seem like variety of each level are nice and wonderful, but the more you spend the eventually you ask yourself: The quests quickly lose their sense of adventure and become repetitive fetch tasks, draining the excitement from the game. Many quests feel like part of a larger puzzle, where finishing one is just a small step toward solving a much bigger problem, which kills the pace. Adding to the frustration, I encountered multiple bugs but this one particularly in one of the side worlds, Ventureland, where it didn’t register as completed upon collecting all items - not game-breaking, but frustrating if you’re aiming for 100% completion. On top of that, talking with other characters who gave you mission can sometimes be that they don’t register next time through conversation on first try, but to babble about other things. At least from positive side, even during side quests the game rewards you with collectible pins or concept arts, giving you something worthwhile to collect despite the monotony.Using your brush can also be useful in enemy combat, and it boils down to either defeating or convert them to fight alongside you. This dual approach gives a bit of flexibility in how you handle each encounter, adding a strategic element to combat. While enemies themselves are quite easy and fairly straightforward, the real variety comes from the boss fights. Though there aren't many of them in game, each one has a unique style of defeat, often requiring creative use of combat and paint/thinner mechanic. For example, fighting the boss offers two ways to win - either by using paint to fix the situation peacefully or by relying on thinner for a more destructive resolution.The remake improves the overall experience, especially when it comes to the camera, which was a major issue in the original Wii version for tracking enemies and traveling through tight corners of the levels. It also adds new moves, such as the dash, ground pound, and sprinting, making Mickey more agile when he’s making parkours. Additionally, the Guardian Meter has been updated, which allows to use either paint-based or thinner-based "guardians" to assist during combat.The visual presentation of the game is nothing short of stunning, perfectly capturing the dark, gloomy recreation of classic Disneyworld. It masterfully blends its eerie atmosphere with the charm of Disney’s old-school animation, making it feel as though you’ve stepped into a cartoon book. The attention to detail is impressive, with countless references to other iconic Mickey Mouse media. One of the standout features is the 2D projector screen segments, mostly presented in black-and-white, mimicking the style of old Disney short films. The animated cutscenes take a different approach, using a vibrant storyboard-like art style that feels reminiscent of classic Disney sketches, adding to the game’s unique artistic flair.While the world and concept are dark and gloomy, the story itself is fairly simple and too predictable, giving you the feeling that saving the world with the help of Oswald and defeating enemies could be better told. The adventure lacks any deep moral dilemmas or significant choices like it tries to present it.Although there are consequences to Mickey’s actions, like characters either refusing to help or criticizing you based on your choices, these outcomes don’t really affect overall. The world might react to your decisions, but the content remains the same, and nothing new is unlocked or changed based on how you play. As a result, the replayability feels limited where there’s little incentive to go back and make different choices since the outcome is mostly the same.Epic Mickey Rebrushed succeeds in delivering that distinct Disney magic, with its beautifully crafted world, nostalgic nods to forgotten characters, and vibrant animation. The brush mechanics are a highlight, offering a creative and interactive way to explore and reshape the environment. While the Unreal Engine provides some visual polish, it also causes occasional stuttering during certain effects, disrupting somewhat flow of gameplay.Next to that, the repetitive and often dull quests quickly become tiresome, and with general enemies you encounter that offer little challenge, there’s not enough content to justify the game’s price. While the story feels like the weakest aspect, lacking any real depth, longtime Mickey fans will appreciate the references to the old comics and characters, despite not fulfilling its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Several bugs here and there but nothing entirely game breaking. Mickey gets stuck on some geometry and foliage once in a while, the subtitles skip at times, after the first few cutscenes the rest of the animated ones are really low res and blurry, somehow some stuff in the prerendered 2d cutscenes just doesnt load sometimes??? like every time gus explains sketches there's nothing on screen for cycling between them. The framerate dips often, there's tons of stuttering at certain points, some of the enemy AI is bugged, and it feels like they made the game a good bit easier than I remember it.Even with all this, however, this game is still phenomenal. Purple lamp did an incredible job taking the game I played as a wee baby boy and made it absolutely gorgeous, going above and beyond the aesthetics of the original and further than I'd ever pictured it. Yes, it loses some of the mood of the original in brightening the environments, but it helps exponentially in clarifying the world around you. The new moves in Mickey's kit are fantastic additions to the game and I am in love with the pause menu redesign. This game isn't just how you remember it, it's better than that tenfold. At last I understand how fans of the Spongebob game felt when Purple Lamp took on that project. Much like with the spongebob game, however. I worry there's not much here to grab newcomers. If you didn't grow up with Epic Mickey, Rebrushed is going to offer little more than a short but pretty kid's game you missed the boat on the first time, as Gus overexplains every minute detail of the game from basic controls inherent to the genre to the exact steps needed for some missions and even the consequences of your actions before you can find out for yourself.At $60 this children's game from the Wii era you either bought for $40 back then or can buy used for the console for $5 now, it's almost unjustifiable. Had I no history with the game I'd be offended they'd charge this much for the game. At the very least I would have liked to see them do the sequel as well, and bundle them together like the Crash N. Sane Trilogy some years ago. If it ever goes on sale for around half off, that's when it'll be worth it, but if you're really looking for a way to reexperience a childhood classic, this is a stellar way to do it.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let me say that I've had a weird obsession with this game since I was 8 years old (I'm 17 now so that's half my damn life) and have probably replayed it on the Wii at least once a year since then. I was pretty worried they'd butcher the ♥♥♥♥ out of it like some of the "remakes" that have came out lately.Clearly, I had nothing to worry about. They managed to stay faithful to the original game AND improve upon it at the same time, something that I thought was impossible for a game studio to do until now- Graphics are far, far superior to the original- Camera no longer makes you want to send an IED to Junction Point Studios headquarters- The cinema is a really nice touch as you can now go back and get film reels you missed- Quite a few game behavior changes that just make the game a lot less tedious to play. Skipping side-scrollers for projectors you've already used is huge. Quests feel much less clunky and most no longer require talking to the NPC fifteen times to get them to say what you want. They got rid of the god-awful timed steam pipe patch in the castle near the end.Overall highly recommend, whether you're a fan of the original or new to the game

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed is a love letter to classic Disney. The gothic atmosphere gives the game its own unique identity, setting it apart from other 3D platformers. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really good, and I'd recommend playing without a doubt, but the 100% maybe a bit time consuming considering the 2 playthroughs.: Everything that has to do with the actual game mechanics is wonderful, from Dashing, to Bouncing, to the improved controls, everything feels wonderful to play. I have my gripes with dash being on B and Bounce on Y, so I switched them around to make my moves feel more natural, though keep in mind if you do this you'll dash & talk to NPC's simultaneously and maybe get some unforeseen consequences like leaving a building but still having the 2.5D angle outside if you dashed out the door when you meant to talk to someone.And every benefit from the Japanese port (minus the Thinner flood to Thinner toxic gas cutscene which I feel the imagery of the Castle rotting would've set up the ending better when it comes back to life) is here, like skipping Projectors (Talk to Gus at a Projector that leads from Mean St. to Ostown, Bog Easy, or Ventureland and vice versa) though it does cost 10 E-Tickets, it's really useful if you're going for 100% due to the quests. 10/10: The Visuals I do have some gripes with, the Cutscenes are beautiful, from 2D to 3D, they look wonderful, but the in-game visual style is significantly different, everything feels brighter and lighter, some darker tones have left. Mean Street for example, instead of a foggy day with the castle ominously sitting far away in the background, it's now constantly a starry night which clashes with the castle, what it represents, etc. The game overall is a lot less darker, and specifically removes the yellows, from the brighter days of Ostown to the Pollution of Mickeyjunk, Yellow has been oddly removed in a lot of ways, which I think is a byproduct of the teams style being more emphasized on the Ink motif, and less on the paper used for ink to be placed on top of, you can see it from every menu, UI element, and the title screen. Whilst I like the inky style I think it fits a lot more in a game like EM2, instead of EM1.The paintable areas in particular though, I do not find look good. the way the paint was sort of embedded into objects felt better than when the paint seems to splat and droop off of buildings and floor and everything feels a lot less sharper, not in graphics, but the ways that rocks, patterns, and certain background elements feel softer, which in a world in absolute distraught doesn't match completely.The game looks graphically pretty good though, it's just the style from the original that seemed to fade and was replaced by something slightly more generic. 7/10: 100% is very odd, as I'd advise going for the Thinner route first, then via NG+ go through the Paint path, as there are certain areas and pins you cannot access like Oswald's Diorama on Mickeyjunk (anymore, kind of wish that Gilda let you keep the axe like in the original, even if it was a glitch) without a couple broken hearts, which even the game itself via Achievements wants you to go for. But after going through the Thinner areas, most things are locked behind good decisions on playthrough, all Projector levels being unlocked after you go through a chapter is much appreciated though, so you can play some you skipped because you took a different route and still get all film reels on a playthrough w/o NG+ (wish you could teleport too like in EM2, but EM1 likes to close you off from certain areas most of the time).Unfortunately you can't buy pins or find them in areas you'd been in like EM2, like the opposite path pin for boss fights, or buying them from a pin collector for events you missed, but could still get 100%. Keep in mind that in NG+ all pins, concept art, films (not cutscenes), E-Tickets, and Film Reels are kept (you will have to talk to the Usher 15 times to regain everything he gave like upgrades, as those are not kept), but this means all the money you gained from doing the wrong thing will now be more helpful in this playthrough (though even then money wasn't an issue even on the good path).To reiterate:8/10

_childDocuments_.review: even though i havent completed Epic Mickey: Rebrushed, I can confidently say it’s a stunning evolution of the original game, turning it into an unforgettable experience that brilliantly marries nostalgia with innovation. From the moment I stepped into the vibrant world of Wasteland, I was mesmerized by the artistic redesign and meticulous attention to detail. The fixed camera angles provide a unique perspective that enhances exploration, allowing me to appreciate the lush environments without the distractions of awkward controls. Every scene is a beautifully crafted painting, showcasing breathtaking lighting and rich textures that elevate the gameplay to a new level. The shadows dance across the landscapes, creating a dynamic atmosphere that draws you deeper into the experience. One of the standout features is the clever use of the painting and erasing mechanics. Each brushstroke I made felt impactful, whether I was creating new paths or solving puzzles. This creative element not only challenged my problem-solving skills but also encouraged a sense of ownership in shaping the world around me. The gameplay feels seamless, with intuitive controls that made me feel like a true artist in a living canvas.The soundtrack deserves a mention, too—each note perfectly complements the whimsical tone of the game, enhancing every moment from epic boss battles to quieter exploration. It’s a nostalgic nod to Disney’s legacy that resonates throughout the experience.What really impressed me was the depth of the story. As I guided Mickey through this enchanting world filled with familiar faces and hidden gems, I felt a genuine connection to the characters. The narrative beautifully intertwines themes of creativity, friendship, and redemption, making it resonate on multiple levels.Epic Mickey: Rebrushed isn’t just a game; it’s a love letter to Disney’s rich history and a testament to the power of imagination. It’s a journey that invites players to explore, create, and embrace the magic that comes from art. I wholeheartedly recommend this game to anyone looking for a unique and enchanting experience—it's a masterpiece that deserves a place in every gamer’s collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Habits play a significant role in the lives of people on Earth. These habits are a reliable foundation and comfort individuals because they are familiar and predictable. In contrast, life changes commonly usher discomfort because they deliver challenges yet to be faced. These dilemmas test a person’s ability to adapt and cope with a changing environment. The short film Mr. Hublot by Alexandre Espigares and Laurent Witz explores this aspect of living. Individuals tend to be creatures of habit unless love offers a reason for them to change. Compulsion does not necessarily define who somebody is. Mr. Hublot, the main character of this story, lived a very by-the-books life before he adopted his robot dog. He seemed to prefer doing everything the same way every day and seemed distant from other people. He also appeared to be a perfectionist, taking the time to clean and organize his house as much as possible. Despite this, he proved he was more than a person forever locked into an unaltering plan. A different side of Mr. Hublot revealed itself over time when he spotted a robot dog being abandoned by its owner. Looking and focusing on the pet slowly began to interrupt the rigid routine he had set up for himself. This indicated his strict schedule was not the only thing Mr. Hublot cared about; he was now concerned about the safety of this homeless dog.Everyday habits are ingrained over time and can be challenging to break. Mr. Hublot originally appeared to have poor coping skills. He became out-of-sorts when his daily routine was disrupted. One day, this was highlighted when he believed the robot dog was moments away from being turned to scrap by a passing garbage truck. He ran and unlocked his massive front door, only to be torn between rescuing the canine and flickering the lights of his house since that was what he always did. He darted between the outdoors and the light switch until finally shifting his priorities to the real emergency. This was the first time (as far as the audience knows) Mr. Hublot had disobeyed his habit for the sake of something else. Traditional matters of course need to have exceptions or else they will guarantee disastrous consequences. The same solution to an old problem will not work on some things. Some degree of change will always be necessary when aiming for success. Love is powerful and can be an unsettling surprise. Upon finding the robot dog, Mr. Hublot attempted to give it the home it deserved. This began his most critical trial. As it grew, the dog’s roughhousing caused problems. It knocked over his living room table, so Mr. Hublot gave a scolding which seemed to get the message across. However, the dog ended up growing much larger than Mr. Hublot himself and became unable to dodge furniture or compromise in their current living situation. At the end of the episode, Mr. Hublot was able to find a solution to the problem. He disassembled the dog for transportation and sold his house. Love guided him to alternate solutions and different living arrangements. His care for the dog allowed room for flexibility.   Change remains a constant and well-known truism. Although he appeared content on a surface level, Mr. Hublot was robbing himself of opportunities by limiting everything he did to yesterday’s agenda. It was only when the main character heard someone’s cry for help, that he jumped outside his comfort zone and did something unorthodox. This decision forever transformed his situation for the better. Mr. Hublot’s life transcended into a more enriched and meaningful state after bringing his new dog home. He now owned something he did not simply appreciate, but loved unconditionally.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say that I enjoy the game, I really do.I loved the game in the past and played it to death, but this sorely lacks the details that make it a 60$ remake as opposed to just playing the 20$ on Wii.Reused Cinematic Cutscenes - the EXACT same cinematics used for the Wii. They just edited out the Wii Remote and Nunchuk. And not in the fancy different style, no. They just blacked out the controls for it. Exact same animated cutscenes, nothing new at all. It would’ve been an amazing detail to add new animations or in-game cutscenes. But they simply recycled in the laziest way.No improvements or alteration to the story - Some might say that's a good thing, but to me that just means that didn't bother improving or touching up the game. Its the same game from 14 years ago with a shiny new appearance, but literally the same thing but with a bigger price sticker on it.I guess it was my own interpretation of what they meant by “rebrushed”.I was hoping for a remaster, but alas, its just texture changes.3D Cutscenes - Now the original had a certain limitations, but it was also impressive animation style, however for the remake, it felt as though they ripped it from the original, slapped a new texture on it and called it a day. The cinematic cutscenes like the intro  are its selling points, but the other cutscenes don’t sit right.Movement - No auto sprint and the sprint button is ctrl key, so that a new unneeded feature. Sprint control. Why?Purple lamp defiantly got the world and feel right for the game, but they really should’ve gone with a $30 deal instead of $60.(Backtracking aspect would've been a nice touch too.)It’s not a remake, it’s a retexture port with slower pace, dated story, and unneeded movement “enhancements”. If you want to replay a childhood game, go for it, but it’s the same gimmick with a fresh coat of paint.
