_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous, ground-up remake of a flawed Wii exclusive gem.Upon its original 2010 release, the game was unfairly criticized for being too traditional as far as platformers go -- while there is some truth to it (its collect-a-thon nature, for instance, and the level design does not go anywhere near its contemporaries such as Super Mario Galaxy 2), the game's tight controls, lite immersive sim elements, and of course the level-altering paint and thinner mechanics make it more than the sum of its parts.Purple Lamp uses the bones of the Wii original to build a complete remake of the game which completely overhauls the main criticism of the original: The controls and the camera system. Rebrushed's controls are tight and Mickey himself feels fantastic to manoeuvre, while the camera has thankfully been reworked to disregard its Wii origins in favour of a more traditional system.The game's price is high, but it's not a knock against its quality, which is impeccable.Epic Mickey represents the best of what Disney used to be: Heartfelt and earnest -- if the name "Disney" has ever meant anything to you growing up, Epic Mickey's conclusion (depending on the choices you make) is bound to elicit some strong emotions.Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s VERY good. It often introduces obstacles and collectibles in ways that players can get in multiple ways that don’t feel arbitrary. Movement is satisfying, combat is more fun than most platformers, and the paint/thinner system has a really cool dynamic in the world. Despite being a linear game, its areas feel very open and fun to explore. However, and this is a problem with the original as well, it has a lot of areas in the game that can only be accessed once. The idea is to include replayability and challenge to the game, and some of it pays off for the better, but a large majority of it is arbitrary. This is rewarding for first-time casual play through, but if you like to 100% games (which is something that appeals to 3D Platformer Fans), then it can be frustrating and you may wish to use a guide.It’s not very deep, presenting “be evil” or “be good” options, but I honestly don’t think that’s bad. It’s fun to be a mischievous monster, and it’s fun to be a hero. However, where the depth in the options lie is mostly in shortcuts. The malicious path tends to be quicker, where you aren’t encouraged to 100% and are encouraged to take shortcuts. I think if you look at it, not as “good vs. bad”, but as “a slow opportunity to 100% it vs. an opportunity to speed run and melt everything”, the moral options will seem more interesting.It is also very good! Many (or quite possibly all) of the graphics were recreated and it’s a very drastic difference! The liquid physics of the brush also look very good. It doesn’t look as graphically amazing as most of its peers and it’s obvious it doesn’t use most modern graphical conventions, but the art style is incredible. The new control options don’t add a ton, but they are appreciated. The dash goes the furthest, being viable for both combat and quick ground movement, but the sprint might as well be a permanent speed improvement since there’s no reason  to sprint, and the ground pound has so far only helped in platforming segments rather than combat and is incredibly minimal. The camera was never a major issue for me on the Wii, but playing Rebrushed makes me realize how necessary a good camera was. Partly to take in the beauty of the world, but mostly because the game has so many nooks and crannies and one-time collectibles that being able to take a moment to scan the horizons is critical. The only drawback is the cursor will never be as fast as it was originally, solely due to the change in hardware. If you’re using a controller that can support it,  It makes an immense difference and is incredibly fun.The new menus are nice as well, and I enjoyed using and unlocking the new costumes, even if they don’t fit the themes of the world very well.The only thing I dislike, and this is a major nitpick, is that the assets in the side-scrolling projector segments don’t look as much like cardboard cutouts as they used to. I really enjoyed how artificial the moving parts looked on the original Wii release. It’s absolutely incredible. If you’ve been to Disneyland, you’ll recognize the landmarks. If you watched the classic cartoons, you’ll recognize the platforming segments. If you’ve vaguely seen merchandise, it’s here as set dressing. There’s some obscure Disneyland trivia that’s integrated as part of the environments, which shows how much care and attention it had.Its biggest problem is clearly the price tag. Despite clearly being a passion project with a lot of love and care, there are other remakes for the same cost or cheaper that have done far more. There are also several quality-of-life improvements the sequel made that would’ve been nice to see here, such as full voice acting, less arbitrary one-time opportunities, and faster travel systems. A piece of me wonders if a back-ported co-op would be possible after first meeting Oswald, but that’s very unrealistic. Bundling the two games together a-la Spyro or Crash remakes would’ve made it absolutely incredible.That said, if you’re a Disney fan or a fan of the original. It’s worth it. If you’re a 3D Platformer fan, you won’t get anything like this, but there are other very good platformers that are less expensive out there. But if this remake is a commercial success then we might get more Epic Mickey so please buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Epic Mickey: Rebrushed is a masterfully crafted remake that excels both graphically and in gameplay. The improved visuals breathe new life into the dark, yet charming Wasteland, making it feel more immersive and stylistically coherent with its unique blend of vintage Disney aesthetics and steampunk influences. The gameplay is solid and easy to pick up, providing an intuitive experience that is accessible for players of all ages.The story remains faithful to the original, offering a well-constructed, though somewhat light, plot. While it doesn't dive too deep into complex narrative elements, it manages to maintain a sense of purpose and progression that keeps players engaged. The presence of numerous familiar faces from the Disney universe, including Oswald the Lucky Rabbit and various iconic characters, adds a sense of nostalgia and charm to the adventure.Gameplay-wise, Epic Mickey: Rebrushed offers a variety of collectible items scattered across its world, giving completionists plenty to explore. Additionally, tasks and challenges can be completed in multiple ways, allowing for some flexibility and player choice, which enhances replayability. However, while the boss fights are creative and visually appealing, they tend to be on the easier side. Like many of the game's quests, bosses can also be defeated in different ways, emphasizing the freedom of choice in the game's design.Overall, Epic Mickey: Rebrushed delivers a well-rounded experience with its engaging world, solid mechanics, and the perfect mix of nostalgia and innovation. While it may not push the boundaries of difficulty, it offers a polished and enjoyable journey through a world filled with Disney magic.

_childDocuments_.review: I still can't believe that i'm getting this game remaked after so, so many years. This game was my childhood and it is incredible how beautiful Purple Lamp remaked it. The graphics look fantastic, the gameplay is so wonderfully modernized (no ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cam anymore), and they even remade some of the cutscenes and put so many new things in addition. Thank you Purple Lamp, for letting me relieve my childhood again <3
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! I played it on the WII when it first came out. It brought back so many good childhood memories, and did fantastic at making it even better than before. The animations and graphics were sharp, the art was beautiful, and there were so many side quests and collectibles to keep me busy! Took me 16.5 hours to run through. I HIGHLY recommend this game to everyone and hope to see epic mickey 2 rebrushed as well in the near future!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when I beat the original Epic Mickey, I had a really hard time with the platforming, some of the collectibles, and several of the bosses. At the time I assumed it was my own fault, but now having played this version with the improved camera, extra movement, brighter lighting, and more clear direction- I can't imagine going back to the old version!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the original wii entry, I do really love the game as it's a faithful remaster with greatly enhanced visuals finally accessible on all platforms, but this review does come with a couple warnings:It is quite buggy and at its worst hard-locked me out of progress mid-playthrough while trying to do the thinner route because characters would not talk to me anymore, despite efforts to fix it.The music is quite messed up, with many tracks completely missing and/or playing at the wrong times; which is a shame given the care the original games dynamic music system had.I'm hoping this will be rectified in future patches because otherwise this would be unquestionably the definitive experience.Overall still probably a solid 8 out of 10, with potential up to 9 if fixed up.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth $60? Oh my god, absolutely not. Like seriously it is not worth the money at all, however I would buy this game again because I personally loved it so much. This game has just as much charm as the original only this time they've fixed some of the glaring faults of the old game. The graphics have been improved, camera has been fixed, and they've even made it less annoying when you're traveling from place to place. Overall I don't think anyone should buy this game for the price it is now unless you were just seriously into the original game, but if you're not I highly recommend getting it when it's on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I've never actually written a review on here before, but after just finishing my favorite childhood game again, I decided to post one. This remake is amazingly well-done. I didn't think anything could improve the original, but I was definitely wrong! Purple Lamp made multiple improvements over the original. The original was very dark in terms of lighting, making it rather hard to see (in my opinion). The lighting in the remake makes everything so colorful! I would have been happy with just this to be honest, but they also added in some much needed mechanics, such as giving Mickey a dash and the ability to run. This came in very helpful, particularly when it came to boss fights, and saved me a lot of deaths/restarting boss fights.My only major complaint, which was also an issue in the original, is the autosave system. For people who didn't play the original, the choices/actions you make effects the areas, story, quests, and collectibles you unlock throughout the game. However, the game autosaves very frequently. So, there were a few times I did something in the game, didn't like the immediate result, and couldn't do anything but restart the game or just keep going (I may or may not have restarted a couple of times). It is frustrating if you, like me when I played the game when I was younger, get really far into the game and realize you messed up a bunch of quests and can't even reload to retry them.Despite that, I was so happy to be able to play this game again! It has really good replayability (it probably took me about 12 hours to finish when not counting restarts) and has a fascinating (and surprisingly creepy) story and setting for a game about Mickey Mouse. Purple Lamp gave Epic Mickey the remake it deserves, and it felt like they really cared about it, so I highly recommend picking it up and giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly charming update to a game that always had the right ideas but was bogged down by the genuinely terrible camera and truly insane amount of backtracking. This update does many things, some of which are:- Adds movement to speed up the pace of the game by a considerable amount- Has a much better camera and especially in boss fights is very forgiving- Livened the graphics and color palette leading to a more engaging view of the world- Adds systems such as the Cinema that allows the individual 2D sections to be played along with a fast travel system with a negligible fare that you will always be able to pay (begs the question of why there is a fee to begin with but I digress)Now, is this game perfect? No, more modern platformers such as A Hat in Time infuse more innovative ideas and concepts into the experience. However, for a game that is technically meant for kids? It's relatively sophisticated and will require some precise movements and a keen eye from the completionists out there. Also the notion of a player potentially controlling an "Evil Mickey" that literally erases the history of a prolific organization is a creative risk not many developers would be allowed to toy around with today.For $60 it is a steep asking point, but if you were a fan of the original, love Disney/early animation, or are fascinated by a "corrupted" version of Disney's past, I'd say give it a shot! If you've never played the game, wait for it to drop down on sale, as a regular play-through of the game will take 12 or so hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: The studios who worked on this project delivered every promise they made. It retained all of the charm of the Wii game while implementing modern game design and graphics. What did not change: story, established lore, most side quests, soundtracks, audio effects, and the cartoon-style cinematics. The game may not be worth the price tag to those who are not nostalgic for the game, but it will be worth it during a future sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: this game is great im a very hard person to like a game im not great with all the buttons etc and fighting but this game is great for a person thats not that experienced with gamin anf coll enough for someone that is also i normally would never pay this much for a game but am not regretting the price
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Overall Disney Epic Mickey Rebrushed improves on what the original game couldn’t do at the time, however that doesn’t mean the game is perfect. There’s still are a lot of performance issues, but if you overlook the performance issues which is a mixed bag, some people have them some people don’t it’s still a great game honestly, I’ve had some performance issues with FPS dropping as low as 4 here on PC however I’ve also had some crashes recently during a speedrun at around an hour in right as I was going into the projector of ventureland, so there is still some kinks to work out but game development hard and also making the game from scratch pretty much again can you blame them for a few performance bugs especially in the current day. I still give this a good 9 out of 10 yes some of that is from nostalgia. If you get rid of nostalgia factor gets a 7 out of 10 once a performance issues or fixed it will be an 8 to 9 out of 10 even without nostalgia. It’s still a great game and I highly recommend playing it once a new patch comes out. You can try it see if it works but if it doesn’t, stay tuned for a patch bc knowing how they will work they will probably release a patch.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever considered playing the original but hesitated because you've heard bad things about it, GET THIS GAME, it's literally everything that made the original game good but with so many of its issue fixed. The addition of a sprint, dash, and ground pound feel natural in the original controls but just add so much more speed and depth to the movement of the original game. Fast travel makes side-quests so much less tedious and there's way more secrets and collectables than the original, just to make it feel like you're finding new stuff constantly. The only thing wrong with this remake is that they're charging 50 quid for it, it's not worth 50 quid, but if you find it on sale and its the kind of game you're interested in, its an easy reccomend.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game i can not recommend highly enough. I played the original release back on the Nintendo Wii and it quickly became one of my personal favorite games. Fast forward 14 years later and the game is completely repainted and re-released. The game play improvements made the platforming so much better and the camera angles were perfect (the Wii camera angles were hot garbage on this game). I'll be honest and admit a lot of my love for this game comes from the nostalgia bomb that i got the moment the main menu music started playing. Let me at least lay out the most unbiased pros and cons i can.Pros:-Platforming and combat revamps make the gameplay fluid and fun-Graphics are beautifully remastered-Soundtrack is mesmerising-Heavy replayability with multiple endings and added New Game + mode-Perfect for gamers who like hunting for hidden secretsCons:-Platforming is simple and pretty obviously designed 14 years ago-I beat the game in a little under 16 hours. granted I beat it many times on the Wii and knew what to do, but the price feels a bit too high for a 14 year old game with a 20ish hour story, especially if you don't plan on doing a NG+ run-a few Wii based animations were removed and not replaced so some tutorial cutscenes have awkward empty green spaces where drawings of Wii remote used to be-The Wii version of the game had really cool Credits animations that were removedI'm sure I'll think of other smaller things later on but I was beyond happy with the game and highly recommend everyone give this game a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: While in my eyes, they've clearly tried to make this a little less scary for younger players this time around (which is kind of a loss in my eyes as the game loses a bit of what made it unique), it is the original game but better in a lot of ways. I am very impressed with what Purple Lamp has done here. As someone who beat the original more times than i can count, every single year up until 2020, this is a remake well worthy of praise.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Rebrushed is an imaginative and revamped take on the original classic that rekindles nostalgia while bringing fresh energy to the gameplay. In this reimagined version, the game retains its core premise: players control Mickey Mouse as he explores the twisted world of Wasteland, a place filled with forgotten Disney characters and neglected theme park attractions. However, the “Rebrushed” edition introduces several improvements and new elements that make it a must-play for both new and returning players.One of the most notable changes in this version is the enhanced graphics. The visual updates bring Wasteland to life, making it feel both more enchanting and foreboding. Character models, environments, and animations have been refined, giving the game a more modern look while staying true to its dark yet whimsical art style.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: A remake made with as much love and care as it could have, with every single asset having been remade and new movement options that actually enhance the gameplay. Prettier, more fun, and more replayable than the original. Aside from some bugs (game hasn't even gotten the first patch), it's as perfect as it could've been.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best games I've played in a while! This game on it's own was a real masterpiece when it first came out and I am really happy to see that the good people at Purple Lamp and THQ Nordic did such a good job with this remastered version!If this is a sign that Epic Mickey 2 Rebrushed could be made and eventually an Epic Mickey 3 too, I'm all for it!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I preface this review by saying that before this remake came out i had this fear that i was gonna play this game and find out it wasn't all that good and i was just being nostalgia blind when i said that this game was fantastic since i hadn't played it in a good few years.But now that i've played and fully completed it i can confidently say that my fears were not validated and that this is now in my list for my top 5 games of all time.the remake basically fixed all the problems i had with the game like the camera, while giving it a fresh coat of paint with beautiful graphics that really did justice to all the games great concept art.For the game itself, It is superb and still holds up all these years later.I've always loved the morality system for this game because it usually gave you an easier outcome for any situation presented, that was morally wrong, while also giving a bit of a harder objective to do the right thing and in the end if you did help out by taking a harder route or doing an additional side quest the game would reward you with a pin while scolding you if you took the easier and worse outcomethe brush mechanic is also really great and makes the game very unique, it's always so satisfying painting in a part of a wall or solving a puzzle by thinning something out revealing a secret passageThe world building is easily the best i've ever seen in a videogame, i love wasteland and all of the cool and ruined locations it includes and just seeing how mickey's ♥♥♥♥ up at the start of the game impacted this once peaceful world really makes you sympathetic with all the inhabitants of wasteland and Oswald himself (Which is my favourite character btw)The music is also a very strong point with every track dripping with atmpsfere and melancholyOverall i fully reccomend this remake and think it's a must play and seeing that final scene where Mickey and Oswald put their hands together on the mirror always makes me misty-eyedTLDR; Great Ass Game
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I waited more than 10 years for any kind of new game of the Epic Mickey series, and I had tears in my eyes when I got the news one of my all-time favourite games will get a re-work. It is beautifully remastered by Purple Lamp Studios, keeps the magic of the old, and makes it so much better at the same time, for a new generation of graphics and devices. With all my heart, thank you Warren Spector and Junction Point Studios employees that helped Purple Lamp create this masterpiece, creating lovely memories to my childhood, and making me feel heartwarming nostalgia today.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty faithful remake of the original game, Epic Mickey: Rebrushed tells a great story about what happened to the forgotten toons of Wasteland. The graphics are a noticeable step above that of the original on the Wii, as well as pretty to look at. The controls feel tight, which is good for the platforming challenges the game may provide. The only complaint that I would make is that sometimes certain objectives are not explained to the player. A solid 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Currently been playing for about 5 hours and it's been a delightful experience. From big details and design touch ups to the small things, like big scene backdrops and added details, to Mickey's he tip-toe animation having sound queues; this remaster has been lovingly faithful, and thusly expanded upon the original game in a fun way with the new mechanics. Added photo mode is a lot of fun as the world is absolutely gorgeous. . I've very much enjoyed my time, and pleasantly ran into minimal issues, with the occasional frame dip here and there when loading a new area.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing remake!! makes me feel like a kid again! however, it's not built perfect...The Good:The graphics: THEY ARE SO GOOOOOD I LOVE THEMThe achievements: they fit really well! only complaint is that fragile should have kept it's old name: "Rage Room"The new moves: while I was skeptical at first, the dash and sprint really help the flow of the game! however I feel like the ground pound was under-utilized for puzzle purposes.Projectors: THEY'RE SKIPPABLE!!! THAT MAKES VENTURELAND ACTUALLY ENJOYABLE!! (it's my favorite area)The cinema: I really like how you can do all projectors in 1 run instead of doing multiple.Blotling Improvements: They attack with pain now! it was so annoying in the og when you were fighting a large crowd and they kept thinning each-other.The Clock tower: The entrance to this boss really makes up for it not being there in the og.Petetronic: looks AI generated. I just thought that was funny. (PLEASE TELL ME IT'S NOT ACTUALLY AI GENERATED)Captain Hook: much easier to thin him now! makes the boss much easier!Inside of the blot: I LOVE the addition of the hubs! really makes the blot feel more dangerous. kinda just wish ostown had a cameo there...Inside of the blot 2: also real quick, the blot spirits sticking out of the wall is horrifying. I love it.The Underwhelming:The cutscenes: The changes to get rid of the wii remote weren't really done fluently, especially in the sketch cutscenes where you can hear the sounds, but it just shows a blank chalkboards. (however mickey waving his hands wildly during the guardian tutorial is extremely funny_)New Game +: Great! only problem: WHY DON'T CUTSCENES TRANSFER OVER IT DID THAT IN THE ORIGINAL! (although keeping e-tickets through playthroughs is a blessing)Costumes: at first I thought: "woah cool! 3 from the 2nd game are getting added as DLC! I need to pre-order this!" then I found out that the rest are ALSO from EM2 and are unlocked from the cinema. makes the DLC feel a lot less special... (nice to have some EM2 rep. though.)The Bad:The Glitches: the glitches are extremely game-ruining. from the hub projector glitch, where whenever you go into a projector on Mean Street (on Steam Deck) the game most likely just crashes. (however there is a way to fix it), and I don't really know of any other glitches.The stutters: right after going into a loading zone or after a cutscene, you can see just for a single second mickey standing in the position he was before the thing happened. kinda just effects the immersive-ness for me.So, to shorten this, it feels a little unpolished, but still amazing and PLEASE BUY IT PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE THEY DID SUCH AN AMAZING JOB PLEEEEEAAAAAASSSEE!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on this game so it's very nostalgic for me and holds a lot of sentimental value. I was super hyped to see this be remastered and released on steam. They did a really nice job of polishing up this game, there used to be a few portions of the game that were a bit confusing to get through on the Wii but I feel like they did a good job reworking it and it felt way smoother of an experience. That, or I just got older and understood it better lol. The visuals were well done and I liked the few items they tweaked in the game. Hope the game does well and they remaster Epic Mickey 2 as well and make it co-op, would love to see that on here as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: So just gonna say, I am very happy to once again experience this game. Its nice remembering how dark this game can be lol. The game is really beautiful too, definitely a great recreation. Now that doesn't mean it has no faults, there's quite a lot of them. Well, atleast for this version of the game. I hope they get addressed and fixed, I want this game to succeed.Pros:-Jumping has been improved-Speed Dash addition-Running addition-Ground Pounding addition-Movie Theater allowing you to go to past projectors for missed collectiblesCons:-Bugs, quite a lot.-Audio bugs/cut outs.-Bog Easy's main hub music doesn't play at all, instead its the Lonesome Manor's music for some reason.-Enemy AI kinda janky.-Certain dialogue is bugged.-No indicator of new side quests, there was one in the original.-Certain cutscenes don't unlock in extras.-The certain main hub event doesn't thin out all the buildings in other hubs like it should, only for Ostown-Thinned Toons don't stay thinned! Oswald needs his timeouts! >:TThat last con was moreso just a silly one.Anyway, would I recommend this game despite the flaws? Yes, yes I would! Enjoy restoring the world with paint! Or be a monster and thin it to oblivion! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a nod to the original, and so faithful to it as well. The little combat and movement upgrades you have add so much to the game play and movement and make it feel so much less at a snail's pace compared to the original. and the graphics have stepped up phenomenally. Yes, i do miss the more eerie, darker, look or the original but the graphic step up was needed i could actually see where i was going. Do i wish there was some more darker themes conceptualized originally in this remaster, yes. Are some of the cut scenes a little choppy and just copy pasted from the original game minus the Wii remote, yeah. Does the Hidden Achievement SUCK.......yes. Do i love it regardless, yes. Even if you haven't played the original on the Wii, this is a great way to play it as well, maybe betterand you actually get control of the camera 100% of the time immediate 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: To put in simplest terms: they got it right. I was nine years old when the original was released and it was one of my favorite Wii games. When I heard it was getting a remake, I was so excited--and somewhat skeptical. This remake, however, blew my expectations away. Purple Lamp did an absolute amazing job at keeping the same, great feel the original had, while also giving it a breath of fresh air. You could even make the argument that Rebrushed is better than the original; lots of enhancements (not just graphical) and more depth. Anyways, I am having a blast and I highly recommend. (I even think It's worth it at the current release price point of $59.99)
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: The amount of detail is insane. If you haven't played the WII version or already played the WII version it feels like playing it for the first time. The experience is PEAK. The story is PEAK, the environments is BEAUTIFUL and BREATHTAKING, the NPCs have so much character. The $60 was so worth it so much replayability its not even funny. Give it a try you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible remake of a beloved game from my childhood. They've ironed out most of the issues the original had while improving the game feel and adding a couple new features. The atmosphere and music of this game are truly something special. It's a unique experience that I'd always recommend, especially if you're a fan of the collect-athon platformer type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: The original was already sweet, but the remake blows everything away. Great upgrades and graphics. The camera, which was annoying in the original, is much better here! Skipping projectors is also helpful if you want to get to a location quickly. You can really say that the remake is epic! Let's hope that THQ Nordic and Purple Lamp are also working on the second game, or a new Epic Mickey.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. The controls including camera are smooth. It is just that the map hub should be made clear, along with objectives which are on different maps. They should have gone step further here.The graphics while cartoon-y compared to realistic in the previous game are still great. The 3D is appropriate, but the 2D level art is next level.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I never in a million years would've expected a remake of this game but here we are.The biggest improvement is the fact that the game actually remembers stuff that's been painted and thinned, so it doesn't reset between loading screens anymore.The biggest disappointment is the fact that despite being a psuedo collectathon, the game still allows 90% of the collectibles to be missable. Would it have killed the devs to just, not make the projectors one-way like they were in the original? The saving grace is there aren't any achievements for grabbing everything, but it's still annoying.The decision to rip the cutscenes and music directly from the original was a smart one as they were both important, stylistic components of the original game.Buy it please, so they can do more projects like this.A few bugs I've noted so far, before entering Lonesome Manor:- Obligatory spots you can get stuck and softlocked in any 3D platformer- Minor mesh clipping issues, namely with the bunny children- A lot of sound effects seem to be missing or not playing correctly- The ambiance in OsTown is extremely loud for some reason- Hopefully just a bug, but Oswald's theme wasn't playing in his throne room :(- Tiki Sam gave me the mask quest a second time before I had turned the stuff in to Smee, so now I just have it sitting there incompletable- Captain Hook's dialogue for climbing the masts triggered after the fight was already over. There have been a few other incorrect event flags like this but I can't name them off the top of my head right now- A number of destructible objects are indestructible, it's becoming more common the farther I go- In one of the Tortooga projectors with the log slides, something happened where Mickey's friction didn't revert (I assume) and I started sliding around the rest of the level at mach 10- Goofy's leg extended a hundred feet into the nearest wall when he started vacuuming and I don't know how to feel about that
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing remake through and through. From the camera and new controls being way more responsive than the original, Mickey feeling much better as hes much more floaty with a lot more aerial control than before, the art style popping out like never before, even going as far as to make certain elements look more like the concept arts and betas. This is a remake that is absolutely sure to please the adults with a hankering for some childhood nostalgia, or the younger people who have no easy way to play the original. This is gonna be a 9/10 for me folks.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite games of all time remade to near-perfection. A true triumph limited only by minor bugs and a few nitpicks.For newcomers, this is easily a 15+ hour adventure in some of the best environments I've seen. It's vibrant and perfectly dark. Compared to the Nintendo Wii version, the colours pop more and everything has more significance.For returning players, I highly recommend this remake. It's a remake, alright. Everything has been changed, except the music. The worlds are more vibrant, more lived in. More secrets to find. The layouts are different too, every 2D Stage has been remade differently, the action stages are much wider, and have different layouts whilst retaining some of the original layouts of the Wii version.But most importantly, the camera is fixed.The only complaints I have are:- Costumes kinda suck. Couldve added a bit more- There are a few minor bugs, most notably audio (e.g Bog Easy plays the Lonesome Manor theme, the dynamic music is a bit wonky, Oswald's theme doesn't play once you reach his lair) and NPC issues (Some NPCs reuse dialogues in non good scenarios, the goat NPCs are replaced by Cow NPCs, they didn't add Gremlin Barry and in the ending the gremlins still have Gus' mustache)But these are just nitpicks. The meat and quality of life that this game adds makes this, to me, my perfect remake. I cannot recommend it enough
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played this game originally on the Wii, this is a very faithful remaster while bringing the mechanics and graphics to a 2024 standard.The amount of content in this game is sizable and even after 20 hours in, there is still plenty to do as I work towards 100%.I would definitely recommend picking this game up! Especially for those nostalgic for the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Epic Mickey: Rebrushed the best remake of a game I have ever played!Epic Mickey is my all-time favorite game, and having this remake is amazing. The levels, the projectors, enemies, effects, lighting, quality, and bosses have all been polished over.The props in the levels are different, and it looks like the lighting has been completely redone. It is beautiful.The projector levels are longer(?) and some have multiple film reels, rather than just one at times. The projector levels have also been touched up. There's a lot more effects, details, and overall polish.Many of the enemies behave "smarter", from what I can tell. When the enemies get stuck, they will teleport to a better location. The enemies also have a tweaked appearance to look much better.The bosses are also better. They look much nicer and more detailed, but they also have a couple changes to make them more challenging. For example, the first boss in the game has a new attack and different attack patterns.It has felt like such a long wait from the announcement to the release of the game, but the wait was entirely worth it. Epic Mickey: Rebrushed has taken the original game and made it so much more. The potential of Epic Mickey has been fully realized in this 2024 remake. Huge thanks to THQ, Purple Lamp, Warren Spector, Jim Dooley, and Junction Point for making this childhood game come back again better than it has ever been.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remake of the original, with so much new content it might as well be a brand new experience. Fluid and tight controls, amazing graphics, steller soundtrack and more will pull you right back into this timeless masterpiece. Hoping for an epic mickey 2 remake, and then hopefully, maybe eventually, an epic mickey 3
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the original when I was younger was and is one of my favourite memories. And Rebrushed has reawoken the wonders of Wasteland in my inner child and brought the most amazing experience I have had with a platformer in a long time. The camera works beautifully, the visuals are simply stunning, and the overall experience is just pure brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Since it firstly came out in 2010 i have loved and followed this saga as if I were the actual game prducer, and now that the rebrushed has taken place I feel such nostalgic as well as amazed by the work and effort that has turned this game into one of my favorites.In the case you are new to these saga I honestly feel these games are worth playing. Thank you Disney.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2010 when the original came out, I was 7 years old. My family got me this gift for Christmas. I loved the absolute crap outta this game, so much that I would replay it over and over again. But when Junction Point closed down after Epic Mickey 2, I thought the game series was a thing in the past. Fast forward to 2024 where I am now 21 years old, I am at work and on my break I find out that Epic Mickey was getting a remake. My inner child was ecstatic for this. After playing the demo, I thought I was ready for this game. But now that the game is fully out now, I am proud to say that THQNordic & Purple Lamp knocked it out of the park! They stayed true to the original game and I was satisfied when I completed this game on the good ending. I extremely recommend this game to the die hard Epic Mickey fans, or even new Epic Mickey fans who never played the original. Thank you THQNordic & Purple Lamp for making me and my inner child very happy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game! A bit of stuttering when levels first load, and I've very occasionally gotten stuck on terrain, but nothing has been too big a hassle. It's great to see this off the stupid Wii finally, and the crisp clear graphics are a treat! Even the art pieces you collect in game have been cleaned up so the art is crisp. _childDocuments_.review: It's the original with a fresh coat of paint (Get it). I love the visual update and updated controls. _childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the original game on the Wii like I did, then you already know its a masterpiece. However, Purple Lamp has gone above and beyond with this remake, and I can certainly say its better than the original. Music has been left untouched. Graphics are far better. Areas have been modified from the original and expanded. The NPCs are more expressive and interesting. The new moves are all useful. Small quality of life changes have been made to make the game's pacing faster. Even a few of the animated cutscenes are tonally different, like the thinner disaster cutscene. Bugs and glitches are far and few between. All around it is everything I have ever wanted from a remake and more. If you have played the original, and are still thinking about whether or not to spend $60 on this, let me just say: You can finally enter the theater. Need I say more? Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up with the original game on the Wii. I only just recently finished at 24 Hours in.This is an absolutely amazing and deeply faithful remake, made by people who understood and loved what made the original game so special. It's brilliant for those looking to go on a nostalgia trip or for people who were interested in the original but could never get to play it. A very fun experience regardless of who you are.There are some issues with the audio (Certain tracks playing at the wrong time and one being missing entirely) and while there aren't a lot of bugs, the few that do exist are very debilitating unless you put in "-dx11" in the launch options. I also would have liked to see some more changes with the actual gameplay, particularly the stale combat, as it's more or less the exact same with a couple of new cool but ineffective additions.Overall, this is a very solid 9.5/10, brilliantly done by Purple Lamp.I hope we get to see more of Epic Mickey in future.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: Going off of my memory of the game I play on the Wii and playing this years later. I'm glad to see this get a remake. Gameplay- AA pretty basic platformer, but with a little bit of caution when using either paint or thinner to fight or make a choice which might affect you either in good way or a bad wayStory- A+I found the story to be really good. As someone who grew up with these cartoons as a kid. I felt as if I was watching those old cartoons for the first time. I also learn that they was someone else before Mickey Mouse became known among the masses. Plus the choices you make in the game affect the story as well.Look and Feel- A-While a lot of the game does look the same as it did on the Wii. I am giving an extra point for a few small details that made this a much better version than the Wii versionFinal Grade- AI really did love playing this game from start to finish and even finding concept art that shows what could have been and what was cut out and put in instead. Overall if you a fan of Mickey Mouse or just a fan in general for this type of game. Then I would recommend you try this game for yourself and see what you think of it. For me I think this a faithful remake of an old classic that got the remake treatment and it payed off big time.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far one of the most necessary game remakes yet. It was a game trapped on a dead console reaching its 14th birthday with no sign of return. Yet, here we are. This game has already proven to me it's not only a major improvement given the beautiful graphics, costume pack, and photo mode among other things, but it's also proof that these developers are listening to our non-stop encore after all these years of the Epic Mickey series being ironically 'forgotten.' All Purple Lamp and THQ Nordic need to do now is remake the 2nd, and have there be some possibility of a 3rd in production.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed

_childDocuments_.review: This is the start of a brand new era for Epic Mickey, I feel. I think something really special is happening here. Warren Specter's dedication to making a story about a forgotten cartoon rabbit led astray by his own hatred, and a cartoon mouse just trying to get home THIS GENUINELY INTERESTING, will never cease to amaze me. I've been a fan of Epic Mickey for as long as I can literally remember, since I got into it when I was only 5 years old at the time. This remake is pretty much everything I could have EVER wanted in Epic Mickey. The visuals are a spectacle, the QOL improvements literally left me in tears, and of course... keeping the charming aspects of the original such as the music & 2D cutscenes. It's so clear that this is a labor of love and I am ALL for it.I do recommend getting this game once some hotfixes have been made if you have a lower-end PC, as there are some bugs and the loading can make a copy of Sonic 06 blush. Sometimes it'll also crash out of nowhere according to others, which hasn't happened to me but it is something to keep in mind.Overall... 10/10 in terms of my very biased "I LOVE EPIC MICKEY!!!" side, and a 8.5/10 in terms of genuine honesty.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. Recreated everything that made the original had perfected, and touched up on some of it's flaws. The new models and animations are gorgeous. _childDocuments_.review:
Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed brings the magic of Disney to life in a vibrant 3D platformer. This beautiful remake sends Mickey Mouse on an epic journey through Wasteland, a realm of forgotten Disney characters. As Mickey, you will dive into a fantastical world and, armed with paint and thinner, shape your adventure and the fate of this alternate world.

Originally envisioned by Warren Spector, reimagined by Purple Lamp, Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed employs state-of-the-art visuals and improved controls to breathe new life into a beloved classic. Experience new movement skills for Mickey, such as dash, ground pound and sprinting. The game's compelling story makes it an unforgettable adventure for long-time fans and newcomers alike. 

Join Mickey Mouse and unravel the mysteries of Wasteland in this homage to Disney's legacy.

name: Orcs Must Die! 3
detailed_description: Orcs Must Die! 3 ushers orc-slaying mayhem to a previously unimaginable scale. Solo, or 2 player co-op, arm yourself with a massive arsenal of traps and weapons. Slice, burn, toss and zap hordes of repugnant orcs in this long-awaited successor to the award-winning series. New to the series, War Scenarios pit players against the largest orc armies ever assembled. Mountable War Machines give players the essential firepower to heave, stab, carbonize, and disarticulate the abominable intruders. More of Everything - Orcs Must Die! 3 is everything fans loved about the first two games and more. More orcs, more traps, more weapons, more upgrades and even better looking. It’s cranked up to at least eleven. New Story - Play through a brand new story set more than 20 years after Orcs Must Die! 2, where the War Mage and Sorceress have rebuilt the order and trained new young apprentices. War Scenarios - All new War Scenarios deliver on the promise of massive scale first set out in Orcs Must Die! Confront overwhelming armies of orcs outside on the battlefields surrounding the castles. Thin out waves of orcs hundreds strong before they breach the walls and crash your rift. War Machines - You’re going to need new weapons of death and destruction to handle these hordes. War Machines are traps on an oversized scale. Lay down your mega flip trap and launch dozens of ragdolling orcs. Mount your mega boom barrel launcher and unleash pyrotechnic glory. It Never Stops - The legions of orcs keep coming long after the story is completed. Etch your name into the orc-slaying hall of fame through Weekly Challenges or see how long you can survive in Endless Mode. Take Drastic Steps - Orcs Must Die! 3 comes with the Drastic Steps campaign and content for free, including terrifying flying enemies, heroic war guardians and of course more tools for orc destruction! Scramble to Survive - The new Scramble Mode pits you against vile orcs who evolve with increasingly difficult and sinister tricks up their chunky sleeves. But each level you survive, you collect your own modifiers to fight back with!

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die 3 has a great progression system that allows for personalised defences and weapon preferences throughout the experience.The difficulty gradually increases and as you progress each scenario & map will make you think about your decisions, especially during the mid to later sections of the campaign.The soundtrack & sound design are incredible with every queue of audio fitting the theme of the game's universe.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an evolutional improvement over OMD2!. There are some questionable decisions here and there, but overall it's fine.Instead of porting maps from the previous games to this, they developed a new game mode called Scramble. It's completely random and simply annoying. But complete all 5 maps in a row without encountering game-breaking bugs and you'll be rewarded with grand 10 sculls! What a joke.Game-breaking bugs? Yes, the game is FLOODED with bugs. And considering it was out for over a year, it's simply unacceptable. Orcs walking inside the walls. Enemies appearing in the passages blocked by barricades without any apparent reason. Orcs not leaving the spawn. Scramble buffs and debuffs are not working correctly. I just lost my three stages of Scramble with the insanely fun seed because the game decided to hang in the menu.I am a huge fan of the OMD2; hence the issues are tolerable for me. But for others, I'll suggest waiting a year for more content and bug fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: The game design is very loosey-goosey. I really, really enjoyed OMD1 back in the day but this does not feel like a culmination or development.For one, there's a lot of options but most of them are clearly sub-optimal. Even in the weirdest stages, the way to get the best score is to build the same exact killbox and route everything through it. There was exactly one mission where I couldn't get all entrances routed to a killbox with walls/ceiling, so I had to use only floor traps. Besides that none of the obvious bait laid by level designers (lava pits for pushing in, and such) were as efficient as the standard killbox. Decisions don't mean anything if one option is clearly superior. (There's something to be said for player expression as well, but it doesn't apply here unless you're self-imposing a challenge because you're bored of dunking on monsters the same way over and over.)Another example of loose design: in the final mission, enemies can spawn from anywhere at any time. This might appear to violate the idea the game has built the entire time, that you get advance warning of where the enemies will come from and get to plan out your emplacements in advance (i.e. basically the whole point of the game). But don't worry, you can kill them all with your standard weapon. Ahh, okay, so you need to watch the map and go attend to emergencies, okay, I'll give it a pass. Until you play for 30 minutes and suddenly toward the end of the entire stage, no, you CAN'T kill them all with just your weapon, you NEED traps for them because suddenly it spawns a crazy number. OK so this completely violates the basic design language and invalidates the entire design. And what's worse, when you say "got it, I will move the killbox ultra-close to the end zone so it can catch everything" and restart the level, the "anywhere at anytime" spawns turn out to be HARD-CODED. Meaning there is even less reason to hide that information from the player. It's just a big middle finger to the player's first attempt at the level, and the entire reason why, in the FIRST GAME, they realized they needed to show where enemies would come from before the level starts. And at the end of it all once you know it's going to pull that BS, it's not even different, just the same killbox as always.These are a few particularly bad examples but the whole game feels like this. They didn't know where to go but they had a profitable franchise and so they churned out another one, with no clear idea of how to go bigger and better. (The "big big battlefield with big big traps" thing is bogus, because it's usually better not to waste money on the battlefield and just let them into the end area with... you guessed it, same killbox as always.)The art is quite polished, but the pathfinding and player controls are very buggy. Sometimes enemies will walk through a barricade, or you won't be able to fire your weapon until you stop moving because it thinks you're still sprinting when you're not, or any number of other annoyances.I played it to the end (kind of a short campaign, disappointing) and it killed some hours decently enough, but overall I'm just... disappointed in the execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great piece from the dev studio. Really like the visual upgrade and all of the modes and traps. Even though I like the game there are some minor/major things that drags the game down a little bit.First of all the difficulty bar is set kinda low. As long as we have weapons and all of the alternative uses that stun/freeze enemies there won't be any challenge. Besides that levels doesn't seem to be difficult at all (in terms of design). Bringing back multiple portals to defend per level could tweak it a little bit however I don't feel like it would matter that much.There are some weird design choices that are pretty annoying:- Levels that are "overcreated". There is plenty of space to do stuff but its usually designed so we have one tactic better than anything else and we don't even have to think about it. With all the budget that we have we feel kinda forced to use the only choke point to set everything up. Its not like we can experiment that much.- There are bunch of different enemy types but in the end we kinda separate them into can destroy barricade/cannot destroy barricade. Would love to see more types that would be more vulnerable or more insensitive towards different kind of traps. Like fire/ice ogres from OMD1/2.- There could be more upgrades / special usages on traps. The worst thing that I've seen from the devs was a creation of that orange box and making it strictly trinket-related. Either remove it from other traps or make it work for everything. The biggest dissapointment so far (when I realised that there are no hidden requirements for that - you guys just forgot to remove it)- No possibility to change your equipment during the game. We need to check map and come up with the tactic and then leave back to the menu and actually change the trap/items setup- Levels that force us to use different type of traps (like refuse to allow us to use ceiling traps only because ceiling is kinda.. rounded?- Potential for the war-scenarios was used moderately (technically we can feel the bigger scale but its not as fun as it could be)- While ingame we cannot sort traps by the upgrade levels (and its barely visible in terms of visual representation). We have to mouse-over it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is alright, I guess. There's a lot less freedom compared to the other games, though. Traps are very expensive, don't deal enough damage, and the level layouts only allow for certain setups to work. It's not as fun to experiment in this game as the previous games since it's clear that you're supposed to use specific strategies in order to do well. As a result, you're incentivized to just use the same loadouts all the time. To add insult to injury, tons of the traps have fire-based upgrades that synergize with other traps, then halfway through the campaign they introduce armies of fire-immune enemies that make all those upgrades worthless. No other synergies come close, so it feels like you're being punished for no reason.I had fun with SOME of the game, and it was kind of nostalgic to use a lot of the old traps and equipment, so I can't say that this game isn't worth playing. It's just frustrating if you've played the first two. The new playable characters are fine and I don't really have much to say about them. The story, as always, doesn't really matter, but it gets the job done I suppose.I wish I could leave a mixed review, but I'll give it a thumbs up simply because there are enough moments of satisfaction to just barely edge out the frustration and monotony, so pick it up and sale if you're looking for an o.k. way to pass the time on a weekend or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Orcs Must Die! 3

_childDocuments_.review: Well.. they said they set out to make Orcs Must Die 3 the best in the series. I don't see that happening with out a major overhaul of core game mechanics and a complete rebalancing. First off the weapons feel great to use and are in handling a good update. But do also a LOT of damage wich is detremental to the tower defense nature of Orcs Must Die. you can defeat the first wave EZ without the Orcs reaching any traps. That is till the first Ogre shows up and lets the entire wave just breeze though your kill box.The traps are way less effective than in the other iterations and cost way too much. You hardly get any money from kills so forget about making baricade paths ways and actualy playing Orcs Must Die.The endless mode is a joke. If the general balance issues are not enough there is now an artificial HP multiplyer per wave that makes low tier Orcs tank as much damage as Ogers in the first waves compared to the other games where an algorythm just scales the TYPE of enemies spawning to rediculas levels. Wich felt WAY better. But don't worry. To top it all off, for all your effords you don't get any skulls to unlock new stuff, wich was the main reason to play endless. Even the new and interesting War Scenarios can not camouflage the piss taste in this soup.Sadly Orcs Must Die Unchained was the best in the series (that's why I bought Orcs 3 blindly without any information), but due to it's free to play nature the "service" siezed years ago. It also should have been the benchmark of how to introduce and design interesting new characters, where Orcs 3 falls flat on it's face by just ticking some inclusivity checkboxes and demanding your acceptance.oh.. the music is garbage too.Overall I find myself playing Orcs Must Die 2. I have it with all expansions and it is the far superior game. It's finished, the balance is great and it has a metric ton of content. The graphical fidelity makes me sad... could have been great, if the real talents continued producing it and not the new kids.

If you're a sadist who love getting losing because the devs didn't even try to balance their game, then maybe you could enjoy this piece of ♥♥♥♥ for a few hours. _childDocuments_.review: Just like its predecessor, Orc Must Die 3 is just a fun game. No false pretense, no huge overarching story, no complicated gameplay, no RTX.You're a dude or dudette, and you gotta kill Orcs by placing traps.Contrary to what some might say, there's actually a good variety in traps, and most are useful (yes, some are garbage). I actually had to use different strats on some maps, something I never really had to do in the previous games because well, tar + darts was just too strong.I feel like Orc Must Die 3 invites a lot more to experimentation than the previous titles did.I also feel like weapons are a lot more situationnal. Contrary to what I've read, melee weapons arent trash. Well, most are, but the regular melee weapon that gives you lifesteal is great.The crossbow isnt so great compared to the domination staff, however it's especially good vs fire elementals and lord with the explosion bonus.The stone staff is amazing against flyers.Monsters have strengths and weaknesses, which makes levels more varied depending on which type of enemy you're going to face.Overall, OMD3 is what I expected. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Changed from recommended to not recommended after the release of the 2nd DLC. I only recommended the game because I was hopeful that future updates and expansions would make the game what I want it to be, but at this point I am now more than ever just wishing for an update for OMD2 to fix the performance issues. The developers have no clue of what they are doing with the game.As a long time fan of the series, I am glad to get some more content from this franchise. But while I am having fun with the game, the actual length of the campaign, the number of available maps for endless mode and the low amount of traps, make Orcs Must Die! 3 seem like an OMD 2 DLC turned into a standalone game.Playing this game made want to revisit OMD 1 and 2, which unfortunately made me realise that OMD 2 had way more performance issues than I recall and if it weren't for that reason, I would probably have recommended that you get OMD 2 instead of this. But because of these issues that I have only partly been able to fix, I would still say that this third (fourth) game in the series is probably the best Orcs Must Die experience that you can have in 2021. I must say that after one whole year on Stadia before coming to Steam, I was expecting way more content. Especially because the Steam release includes a DLC that was released in Stadias time, but the DLC itself is so lackluster that it feels like it should have been part of the base game. Articles online do confirm more DLC in the future, so I remain hopeful that the game will get the content it needs to feel like a full game. I'll still be playing for a while to try to scratch that OMD itch, but it's probably gonna need some chunky updates to do the job.

_childDocuments_.review: The best FPS Tower Defense out there. _childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die 3 is a fun game, although it can get quite repetitive. It is a fairly difficult game, even with friends, but it rewards clever thinking over everything, which I love. Some levels will seem impossible, until you really think outside the box. There is a large variety of traps however the game is stupidly unbalanced, meaning you will no doubt find the powerful traps and avoid the majority of poor ones. The weapon variety is a lot more limited, and most of the weapons are pretty trash, however the strong ones are not difficult to obtain. It goes without saying that this game obviously does not aim to provide an amazing story, however I doubt anybody would play this game with the intention of looking for one. The war scenarios are really fun and where the game shines the most, however the boss fights that accompany them are extremely underwhelming. With the very anti-climatic ending to the relatively short main campaign, I assumed that the Drastic Steps campaign would provide some much needed length to the game, however it was miles shorter than the main campaign. This game is fun, but even with friends it can start to feel a bit repetitive. I would only recommend this game if you have a friend to play with. Despite everything that has been said, it is still a quite fun and enjoyable experience, just don't expect anything crazy.

_childDocuments_.review: I dreamed that  featured Maximillian’s vacation home as a level—a lavish cabin tucked away in some snowy valley in the middle of an intense blizzard. Shadows of horrific creatures danced across the walls as Max napped in front of a comically-huge fireplace. Not so much as grunt or a groan came from him as I painted his walls with bile and gore.I awoke with a feeling of disappointment when I realized such a level would never exist. Will I hold that against OMD3? Let’s find out.::::If you expect OMD3 to be just like another one of the titles in series, it’s not. It’s more of a mix. Gone are the effect status combinations you have to memorize so you can maximize your killbox’s efficiency. Gone is the large cast of interesting characters from Unchained, but a few of their traps and weapons remain and a new version of a game mode from that title. The characters don’t have their own traps or weapons, but have a single, unique ability that affects movement.A lot of people complain about the level design and feel that there are too many paths or that they are too spread out to efficiently complete a level in solo. While the layouts made some levels a lot more challenging, it didn’t ruin the experience for me, but you may want a co-op partner if you don’t want to deal with too much multitasking and rushing back and forth.

_childDocuments_.review: A continuation of the Orcs Must Die! series, making it a trilogy. Unfortunately, however, this installment is a disappointment compared to the other two games in the series. Let's start with the positives. They added war scenarios, with almost cinematic hordes of orcs and other beasts going for your rift, with access to a unique category of traps to match. It's a great addition, but has no endless mode for it, which is severely disappointing actually and left a bad taste in my mouth, as I enjoy playing endless. New traps and weapons are added and while some feel particularly useless, it still adds more variety and flavour to the game. Briar patches (A DLC ITEM.) are a pretty unique take on floor traps, for instance. The improved graphics are a welcome part of this installment. The rainy levels are brilliantly atmospheric, in my opinion. Level details are also pretty good, and layouts unique. Unfortunately, all of that is completely overshadowed (in my opinion) by the horrendous tragedy that they dare to dub a story alone. They give us a pair of braindead protagonists (And while I acknowledge that Maximillian himself is as dumb as a bag of hammers, it was well executed throughout the first and second game.) who provide little value to anything and are really, *really* forgettable. The story is a cliche "well, here's this guy that was actually erased from history but he's evil now and he wants revenge" and executed in probably the poorest manner I have seen. And I'm not even going to talk about the Drastic Steps campaign. It just doesn't need to exist and was added to inflate playtime at best. Unfortunately, this game commits the cardinal sin of DLC for the sake of DLC. Not as bad as HOI4, of course, but not long after the game got released, they stopped adding content to base game and SOLELY added content in the form of DLCs. An absolute money-grabbing thing to do. Not to mention that the DLCs themselves also lack content, and usually just add a new class of enemy, a few maps and mediocre weapons (What the heck is this gatling gun? It's crap and has no use other than holding it down in the general direction of the enemy.) Now a flaw I saw through the whole (♥♥♥♥♥♥) campaign and endless mode that ticked me off quite a bit. The main way of ramping up difficulty? Spam heavy units! Ogres and trolls, groups of 4. "Just spam them." They must've said. Instead of adding a new threat to adapt to, just send the same threat, but more. And after a certain point, just armoured ogres. Adding onto the above point, in endless mode, the only indicator of increasing difficulty is more heavy units and GIVING THEM MORE HEALTH. Seriously. It gets to the point where Kobold runners don't die in one shot. It's a cheap way of ramping up difficulty, especially when compared to OMD!2, where light orcs became medium, then heavy, then got shields. Absolutely rubbish system for OMD!3, unfortunately. They also DECREASED enemy variety in a way. This might be a personal preference, really, but I'm unhappy to see fire and ice ogres go. They are a nice enemy I miss sorely from OMD!2. Also noteworthy is the lack of the Swamp troll. Why even cut them from the game save for laziness? As a final point, this is one of those games where you can't 100% the achievements without buying the DLC, which is - in and of itself - a poor practice. Overall, sorely disappointed by this game and left a poor taste in my mouth after OMD! (250h~), OMD!2 (300h~) and OMD!U (50h~). I grew up with the games and was left hanging by this one. Play Orcs Must Die! 2 instead. The only loss is graphics.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, as much as I enjoy the OMD series, and as much as this game scratches the itch for more, I have several gripes of varying sizes.1. The two protagonists of this game are a lukewarm replacement for the previous protagonists, and only really resonate with me because I understand their dispositions personally, especially Egan's. Otherwise, if the Warmage and Sorceress were like mixing sodium and water, these two are like mixing baking soda and vinegar for how little chemistry they actually have.2. The UI for this game took a couple steps forward, and several too many backward.-You can now refund skulls on individual items. Yay!-But now you can't refund item purchases, only their upgrades, and skulls haven't been made more readily available to compensate. Boo.-You can now switch characters at-will, with their unique weapons and activated abilities being available to you from the get-go. Yay!-But now you only have one save, and you can't readily erase your data without messing with the steam cloud. You also are stuck using the character's primary weapon during the story mode for no discernible reason, since you can swap it out anywhere else. Boo.-Traps look good, and orc pathing isn't as glitchy, so more consistent results are possible. Yay!-Sound effects are less crunchy, and the overall feel is kinda flat.3. War scenarios are cool as hell, but the war traps themselves just kinda feel like bigger versions of the same traps we've been using all game. Would have preferred the traps to feel more wide sweeping. The mounted machines are certainly a good idea. Just wish I could justify using them over just... participating in the fight myself.Overall, it's okay, wish they'd put some old features back in. Multiple saves would be nice, full skull resets, even if they were on a cooldown, would be a godsend, and updated sound would be pretty cool too.

_childDocuments_.review: As of right now I only have a few hours in this game. I played OMD 1 and 2, and by played I mean played the absolute s**t out of them. I love, love, love Orcs Must Die - the gameplay, the art style, the fun figuring out cool trap combos, and the humor and physics.  So far OMD 3 feels like an organic extension of OMD 1 and 2, and there are some noticeable improvements as well as disappointing changes (although some of those changes may be in the game and I just have not unlocked the expected features yet.) I have been waiting for this game to move over onto PC, and I am stoked that I am able to play it on the platform now.So, if you are contemplating getting this game, here is my two cents:1. You can enjoy this game even if you have never played an OMD game before - there are hints and tutorial-like levels to get you started. The game's strategy style will take some time to learn, but learning is part of the fun. If you find yourself too confused or frustrated on how to beat levels, you could benefit from looking up a few videos on YouTube, even of OMD 2 gameplay strategies as pretty much the same approach to beating levels and getting high scores is the same in this game.2. The new war mode is great so far - really adds an epic large-scale battle feel to the game. So far it seems way easier on co-op than single-player, but as with all OMD games, the more you level up and unlock more powerful traps, weapons, and trinkets, the more fun and easy the levels get.3. So far I have not been able to find any games hosting on Steam, but the game just dropped and I have only tried a couple of times. Hopefully the word will get around how good this game is and more people will be hosting games.4. This game really feels like it could have easily been a $60 game - but it is HALF that price. Sure, it is an older title that we had to wait to port to PC, but I have dropped $60 for games with far less content and were nowhere near as fun.5. This game feels more grindy already than 1 and 2, but not much. I am already finding myself having to go back and replay levels I already beat to get enough skulls (what you use to unlock/upgrade) to get the necessary power needed to beat newer levels. But going back and beating these levels with newer gear means they feel different and are still fun.6. If you play this game or any OMD game - do not be afraid to experiment and restart levels - this will teach you what works and what does not. This is one of those games where you might get close to rage quitting only to find yourself really wanting to try something new to see if it works better.Lastly, if you are reading this and want someone to play it with, by all means add me on Steam and message me. I love meeting new players, have a discord with other OMD fans, and the game is always more fun co-op.Now, hurry up and buy this game already, and start killing some orcs!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all of the OMD series, 1,2,Unchained and now 3.. I was a little annoyed when Robot originally announced that they were going to do OMD 3 and it was a 'Stadia' exclusive because that felt like a kick in the teeth to those of us who had supported them through the years, I mean some of us brought things for a now FAILED product (unchained).. So it was great to actually see OMD 3 come out of exclusivity and to the 'masses'. If you've played OMD 1 & 2 then you know what your getting into, traps, traps, witty banter, 2 'new' characters to start to move the cycle on from Max and Gabs (But don't worry Max and Gabs aren't gone) for those whom only played UNCHAINED there gonna be in a for a little bit of a shock, this isn't unchained.. It doesn't have the PVP eliments it removes a lot of the game play unchained 'played with' and returns back to OMD's roots.. and I know some people will find that a reason to say this game 'sucks' that's their choice, unchained failed though because in the end Robot didn't know what they were making, a MOBA, a tower defence game.. both.. etc.OMD 3 however is a Tower Defence game just like OMD 1 and 2. And I love it for that, I love that I can sit and play Co-op with my wife and kill the green things like we spent hours and hours doing on the previous games, I love the return to form that has come with OMD3, it's not perfect but it's still a return of Orcs, Must, Die.So the Good• Well thought out Maps• Return of all the old fav traps• Orcs Dieing• Gab & Max and the Tongue in Cheek humor that they bring... • Willing to make fun of itself.• 4 'new' characters*• 2 'campaigns' * * these also have some bad points... The Bad• Rather small campaigns compared to the older games.• New characters feel more like reskins and less like 'new' characters.. I get that they were trained by Max and Gabes but really it's more like 'Female Max, Male Gabe' then 'new' characters.• No Fliers at all in the 'main' campaign, even though the 'second' campaign (if you can call 5 missions a campaign)  has them.• Some pathing/routing issues on the maps that were pointed out back in DEC by stadia users which STILL haven't been addressed (Last mission of the main campaign for example).• Removal of Gnolls dropping things when they die giving you a reason to actually kill them rather then just.. running them to the rift.• Removal of some of the items that did make unchained an improvement on OMD 1 & 2.Over all though If you want a good OMD game, buy.. _childDocuments_.review: Welcome to my totally original and hilarious review of "Orcs Must Die! 3," where orcs aren't just a problem, they're an infestation - and it's up to you to exterminate them with style!Imagine this: You're one of the last battle mages, standing between a horde of dim-witted but deadly orcs and the peaceful townsfolk who are blissfully unaware of the rusty axe-end they could meet. Your tools? An arsenal of traps that would make MacGyver jealous, and a trusty crossbow that turns orcish heads into pincushions.But wait, there's more! The game throws a curveball with ogres and kobolds that laugh in the face of your simple spike traps. You’ve got to strategize and choose your tools wisely because, let's face it, not all traps are created equal. And when your carefully laid plans crumble? It's time to don your battle mage pants and jump into the fray, swinging swords and slinging spells like a medieval superhero.Let’s talk upgrades: You're showered with funds to pimp out your character and traps. It's like a home renovation show but with more orcs and less shiplap. Choose wisely, though, because you can only upgrade from one skill set per stage. It’s like picking your favorite child, but every stage you get to pick again.Now, the pièce de résistance: War Scenarios. Picture this - giant maps, hordes of orcs, and traps so big they make your head spin. These levels are a spectacle, but they scream "Bring a friend!" because tackling them solo is like trying to juggle flaming swords... blindfolded.Graphically, the game is like a Saturday morning cartoon, if that cartoon featured orc dismemberment. The ragdoll physics? Chef's kiss. Orcs tumble and slide across the floor like they're in a slapstick comedy. And at the end of each level, there's a dance loop that's... well, it's something.But what's the catch? The game, while a blast in co-op, feels a tad short and is a bit light on post-campaign content, unless high scores are your jam. It doesn’t reinvent the wheel; instead, it takes the old wheel and adds some shiny orc-slaying spikes.In summary, "Orcs Must Die! 3" is a joyous romp through orc-slaying mayhem, especially with a friend. It's like hosting a party where the guests are orcs, and the party favors are traps and arrows. So gather your traps, call your friends, and let the orc-slaying party begin!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly? Been lovin' it.
