_childDocuments_.review: Just as fun as the previous games, these orcs really need to die and you have to help them out using traps, giant meat grinders, blunderbusses and other kinds of ridiculous contraptions.What's new this time? Well, you can upgrade your gear and there are several different tiers. First are your basic more damage/faster reload type, the next is a choice between different types of damage (arcane/lightning etc.) and then the ultimate upgrade, which I have yet to see. Unfortunately there's not much to choose from, but your arsenal is quite extensive, so that's probably why that is. Haven't seen any new monsters yet, but I'm still pretty much at the beginning of the campaign, which is rather long. 18 levels is reasonable number. Just like OMD2 you can play in coop if you so desire. Haven't tried it myself, so I have no idea how balanced the coop is.Unfortunately you don't play as the War Mage or Maximilian right at the start, instead you have to choose between two stock characters- either black guy or a girl, I didn't bother to remember their names. And they don't have a lot of chemistry together, at least from what I've seen so far. But the War Mage we all know and love is in there somewhere, so that's something to look forward to.Just something I need to mention, selecting different language is busted. When I first loaded the game, it was in my native language despite the fact, that in the options menu was english. Quick search on the forum brought me fix for this- just choose random language, that's neither english or your native language and quit the game. Then change the game to your prefered language and quit again and you're set.This is not an in depth review, just a first impression. So far I like the gameplay and really dislike the new characters, at least we got fully animated opening sequence, which was nice. Anyway, this game is really fun. If you wanted to kill more orcs, this game has you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels to me as if they took a "tower defense game" and added far too many OMD regressions so-as to make the game more "accessible" and less "niche". That's all. My frustrations come from the perspective of a Tower Defense fanatic. I love them and I've played most of them. Because of this, the following points are quite biased. Take that into consideration.Pros:+ Core gameplay, animations, character design, etc...: It's great and very much just as good as OMD2. Not better IMO. Fancier maybe. But still a parallel to me.Cons: (spoiler: literally everything about OMD3 feels like a regression to me from OMD2)- interface still sucks. All the unimportant stuff is obtrusive and all the important to the gameplay stuff is like an afterthought. Consider the level selection screen. Almost three quarters of my whole display is "cinematic orc models swaying in the wind". While the actual level selection is hugging the left side and I have to LITERALLY SCROLL PAGES AT THE BOTTOM TO SEE THE LEVEL MAP. Like jeez. Who designed this? The sales team?- Why are traps _still_ missing an upgrade level icon in the loadout selection? There's a ton of traps and I'm drunk, how am I supposed to remember the ones that I upgraded with the TINY amount of skulls I have available after near 20 hours of gameplay and after REFUNDING ALL UPGRADES for the upteenth time?- War games traps should be in their own sections, war games are still cool, but they feel too disjointed from the main game. Trap exclusivity, especially when upgraded from the same pool of *ridiculously sparse* skulls, is LAME.- Stop making me refund my skulls every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ level!!!!! Just give us enough to actually tinker with builds OR, hey, here's a novel idea: LET US REFUND THE SKULLS FOR A SINGLE TARGET TRAP. PLEASE.- Traps still suck. Traps can _not_ hold back enemies on Wave 1. Maybe if you're late in the game going back to apprentice with a bunch of fully fleshed out traps, but with the hours I've put in with active play as an OMD veteran, I can take ONE or TWO fully upgraded traps, or otherwise do "just a couple" upgrades into 4-5 traps. I've yet to find a combination of which can successfully hold back Wave 1 by themselves in anything past the first couple levels.- Considering the last point: ORCS MUST DIE 3 MOVES AWAY FROM TOWER DEFENSE IN FAVOR OF FRENETIC, CONSTANT RUNNING BETWEEN ENTRANCES AND SPAMMING YOUR WEAPONS/TRINKETS. I can understand... hell, I can even appreciate the time spent finding that balance between trap damage and weapon damage to effectively complete a wave. You really did a good job there. Truly. But why do we need that severe level of balance? Why can't I play the game like I could play 1 and 2 if I want??? Why does everything these have to be so pErFectlY bAlancEd? Where's the "passion" and the "fun"? Feels like I'm playing homework from one of those "cool teachers" that add memes to my results. It's still homework. I want to FEEL the change in my power after I've found a good trap combo. It's clear that Orcs Must Die as a franchise is moving in... a direction. It's also clear that it's not the direction for me. I've loved this franchise for a lot of years because it was a fun, challenging, and engaging Tower Defense. It's not that any longer.See you for OMD4 and hope it's a better successor to OMD2 than this game has been. I appreciate the work and I haven't lost faith. I'm just one random gamer that finds this game soulless. I really, genuinely do hope for another installment that feels better. Or a new OMD2 DLC would be sweet.TL;DR: I love this game, but I've already played it back in 2012. Except the last time... it was way better. OMD2 > OMD1 > OMD3 (IMO) Three doesn't bring a lot new to the table outside of OMD2-DLC-worthy trap additions and doubled-down forced gameplay constraints.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it overall, for the same reason I liked the previous two games, so if you like this series then you should probably get it. However, I think it does have some design problems. If you haven't played the previous two games, I recommend playing them first to decide if you want to buy OMD3.Pros:  * The war maps are a neat addition that breaks up the monotony and has a different pacing and feel from the usual levels.  * The structure to upgrades and skulls allows you to do much more experimentation with trap and weapon combos compared to OMD2.  * The levels are pretty and have a good deal of variety. You spend a lot of time looking at them, so good environment art goes a long way.  * The upgrades have more variety. Double-width barricades are very cool!  * You get a pretty broad choice of characters compred to the previous games, each with their own unique mechanic.Cons:UPDATE: They released a balance patch and now I think the issues with trap nerfing are mostly gone! The game feels a lot more fun now.  * The environments feel less interactive. In OMD2 there were a bunch of minecarts that could ram enemies, and sometimes you had control over what path the minecarts took. These hazards reduce the pressure on you to be everywhere at once.  * This may sound dumb if you haven't played the series, but the dance animations are super disappointing compared to previous games. I always liked the little touches of atmosphere this game had.In OMD2, you really had a lot of control over whether to focus on weapons/trinkets or focus on traps. There were traps that existed specifically to help you fight better, like a wall-mounted mana pool. That variety feels like it's missing from this game. Other reviewers have complained about the small size of the paid expansion, but I can't comment on that as I haven't bought it.I suspect the game plays better in co-op, though I haven't tried it yet. Co-op was super fun in OMD2 as well, so if you buy this game, convince a friend to buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get this out of the way: the game is buggy. So why am I still recommending it?It's FUN.  It's a really enjoyable game with a great sense of humor, and I want it to succeed well enough for them to be able to beat the bugs out of it. _childDocuments_.review: The game feels just the same as OMD2... which is a good thing. It (also) requires you more than simply spamming left clicks... which is a good thing. There's variety on traps, upgrades, possible combinations on both traps/weapons ... which is also good. It requires you to actually LEARN the game or else you will get steamrolled over and over.Story is rather cheesy... quite vague, honestly. It can be resumed into simply "Your master used to fight side by side with some cool guy. And this cool guy is now back for some reason and is now a monster because of whatever." Not really a fan... but I can live with that.Voice actors don't feel natural, but are okay'ish.Gameplay is very action-oriented -- you can't be a "trap specialist" as the trailer advertises. It's more hero-oriented while the traps just tickles things up a bit so you can finish em up.There's a little "optional" competition you can do with other players... point-wise.Soundtrack is fine -- no complaints there.Main characters personality are fine. One is a sassy girl (aka Zoey 2.0 if you ever played OMDU) and the other one is...forced. Let's leave it at that, I guess.Enemy variety could be better imo -- troll and mountain troll (aka samey troll but with more hp and a different skin)? That felt lazy'ish.Tactics can be quite simplistic -- you can solve most problems by simply rushing to a "risky" monster icon on the minimap, kill it, and then go back to your killbox.Difficulty can be a nuisance for someone who never played an OMD game before. I've played em all, so that wasn't really a problem. Other than forcing me to play Apprentice because I lacked traps and upgrades. (If you managed to play the game on War Mage difficulty with almost no traps and upgrades and reached the end...? Then I salute you -- you are a much better player than I am.)Would I call this a true OMD3 game...? It's OMD2, but with new toys and maps... so yes, I suppose.I'd give it a 7/10 -- in a nutshell, its a fine "Action-packed hero which can modify enemies behavior with traps while defending a blue light of life" game. Definitely a must-have if you are into "pushing buttons to see what happens" kinda guy like I am.Oh, and I forgot to mention that I played it on GeforceNOW, with my pi 4, 2 GB. Performance-wise it was flawless. Think I've found only one bug (Orcs kept attacking my large barricades, no matter if it was blocking their way or not.) and thats about it.Played it solo... but I'm pretty sure it'll be much better with someone else.Alright, its my 3rd('ish) day playing this game... and just want to add that the grind is a breeze (Took me around 3 hours to get enough skulls to unlock all the traps) and that the highest difficulties are 100% bs at the first wave (Sorry, giving me a wooden stick to poke a armored orc to death is not a challenge in my book.). Its possible to get past such bs... it just feels a lazy attempt that makes the game cheap rather than interesting.Oh, and spoilers:OMD3 starts when the game ends. :^)...and I just beat the game (Base plus dlc, on the war mage difficulty). Technically, it took me 19 hours since 3 of em were spent grinding skulls to unlock all traps (Yeah, I let my inner collectionist flow a bit. It was fun, so no complaints there.)... and the last two levels "felt" OMD3 as much as the whole game itself, as weird as it sounds. And Max voice acting kind of "saved" the game imo and gaved me some "...this is OMD3" feel to what I should have felt right at the very first seconds playing the game.Now I'm at the "fun" part of the game -- where I have my "just right" setup of traps and with the appropriate killbox setup in mind. Will I start religiously play and try to achieve best scores than the players who are at the top (Yep, that's the endgame.)...? Not -THAT- much. More like, every now and then and see if I at least stay in the top 10. Will I be able to do it? Not really. Will I try it? Yes, definitely.But I've got to admit that the "Max and Gabby are now old and now theres some unfitting-looking kids dressed as heroes for no apparent reason" kind of messed up with the game. Max and Gabby are both orc-killing machines -- not babysitters. It feels like a forced attempt to appeal to a certain demographic "for the hell of it".But I still recommend it. It could be better, it had potential for it -- but this is what we got.

_childDocuments_.review: Just as a heads up: I played the game a lot with Steam in offline mode, so my playtime is more around 100-200 hours.Saying that, it's a good game for a low price.It has some issues, not that much content, but a lot of replay value in form of unlock able upgrades and testing strategies.Some of the mayor issues the game has are that the game eats up to many resources (on whatever setting you play the game), traps and projectiles sometimes don't work properly (on whatever setting you play the game) and the map difficulty is all over the place with a few maps (giving you not that much options on how to play these maps).If you can handle these mayor issues you might have a lot of fun with the game and if not... well, I'm not sure if the devs are able to fix these issues, since they seem to don't know what's causing it.Oh and the story is as stupid as it always was, so don't expect to much from it.Besides that the chaos mode where you have to play 5 maps in a row and choose positive and negative effects after each map is pretty nice, the endless mode could be better and more rewarding but it's nice to have, the "weekly challenges" are pretty nice (and don't be fooled by the name... you can do them whenever you like and only the ranking is weekly for one of these missions, but who cares about the leader board anyways), the dlc is kind of nice but way too short with only 5 maps and these maps are the only ones where you have flying enemies... and yeah that's about it for game modes.Weapon/Trap/Accessory variety is pretty nice but the character variety on the other side is lacking because there is not much of a difference which character i play besides one ability with most of them being kind of underwhelming.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing this third game in the series, I've come to enjoy this installment the best out of the entire batch. I don't know why the reviews are mostly positive. Orcs Must Die! 3 is a fantastic sequel to the series and it got a much needed makeover.  The game changed art styles, engines and for once, this is not a bug infested crash inducing mess like the last two games are still. One of the things I like about this game is a more refined customization tab for all your traps, weapons, and skins. I really like the simple change that allows us to change characters that was missing in the second game. I for one actually like the new characters and don't mind their existence. The story is good too and not that complex. The one thing that annoys me is that the game still has broken stat system which won't record your stats prompting some achievements to never unlock. Hopefully the devs can re-implement this system. I like the DLC content albeit it is a little short. I wish the game includes previous campaign stories from previous games. Other than that, there is really not much to complain about. Heck, there is even any monetization for this game. Shocking. This is a really good co-op game and I am so happy I manged to finished it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a completely new player to this franchise, I wish I had read more of the negative reviews. I thought I was buying a tower defense game with some third person action elements, but instead it's a shallow third person action game with towers that do things sometimes. Overall they feel weak and ineffectual. Watching a mob walk through your setup of 10+ traps completely unhurt because the traps are all on vacation is painfully unfun.The high cooldown trap balance just makes them all feel terrible, and the points economy feels incredibly stingy. At no point throughout the campaign did I ever feel like I got my ideal tower setup, instead it felt like "I guess this'll do for now". I never got to look on in awe of my untouchable setup, instead I was always having to deal with mobs that made it through no matter what I did. On top of that, the game seems to punish you for wanting to shape enemy paths, destroying barricades or making them consume so many of your points. I couldn't even bring all the traps I wanted to because so much of my bar was consumed by weapons and active abilities for my hero.Maybe I was missing some knowledge about the combo system, or deeper synergies to get me more points or to avoid ineffective trap setups, but the game teaches you nothing about any of this. On top of that, levelling traps with Skulls meant you were married to traps and had to invest a lot to even seem them at their proper performance. Don't like them still? Too bad. Oh you could also respec your entire character, but doing that more than once is cancer.If you're looking for a tower defense game, this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Although recent changes have fixed many of my issues with this game, I still can't recommend it. I appreciate that traps actually do damage now and that weapons than your primary are viable. However, I still can't recommend this game. It doesn't match the quality of content as OMD 1, and doesn't have the quantity of content as OMD2 or Unchained.Original Review:This game feels unfinished and rushed.It has less content than "Orcs Must Die! 2" and fails to match the quality present in the first game titled "Orcs Must Die!".This installment has a much stronger emphasis on combat, as, traps aren't very effective. This makes the game play like a stale third person shooter with one weapon. The only decent weapon is the primary you choose, everything else is ineffective, as, even the series iconic blade-staff hits like a wet towel that's not even wet.I am displeased with the level design, as, the solution to every map appears to be to choke at or slightly before the rift.Physics kills aren't really a thing. When I finished my first playthrough, it felt like I played half a game. By far the worst game in the franchise.Tbh, unchained, despite its flaws, was better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: A good return to form compared to OMD: Unchained. More accessible than OMD2 in terms of beating the highest difficulty, but in return has less total hours of play. I have around 80 hours in OMD2 and 40 in OMD3 and have a similar game state in both (maxed out set up with 200+ extra skulls to toss around). BUT I did not completionist OMD2, and I did in OMD3. Bottom line is, if you are a fan of the OMD series, it is worth playing this game. If you haven't played the other games, I'd recommend OMD2 for it's broader scope of content and difficulty. For both games, bringing a friend improves the experience, except perhaps making OMD3 rather easy.Update: After writing original review, the devs released an update that fixed a long list of things that were wrong in game, including bugs and some healthy balance changes. I find myself playing the game just to try out traps I haven't, so very happy with game's state now. Nice job devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Got it when it came out. Was great. Checked back later and realized there was new achievements after they added new DLC, which removed my 100% achievement status from the game. That made me feel really disappointed, since it felt like my progress was removed. But I guess that's also a method of pushing people to buy DLC, I guess..? I hate how marketing of games have changed over the years. This is a great example of a great group of devs moving in the wrong direction.I don't remember if the first and second games had issues like that, but I loved those two. I felt like the Moba game was a bit intriguing, but lacking. now with this minor misshap, I feel kind of cheated by them. The game itself was great fun though. I still love the concept.[edit] if you get "Cold As Eyes", it will add a mob which "makes it harder". also known as "limit your options by force". for me, this expansion was a fun challenge, until I realized those mobs are now on the other maps as well in different gamemodes... that decision from the devs really kill my fun, especially since there's no option to turn off the expansion as far as I know. now I no longer have the option of placing sporadic traps in tactical locations for amusement and mess around casually, but I have to create more dedicated killboxes with specific traps to make sure totems die by AOE explosions (or me) in 99% of the times. otherwise those mobs will turn off every trap on the map. skipping that expansion definitely improve the gameplay since the game in general is addicting and fun. however this expansion made me tempted to flip it to no longer recommend the game.[/edit]Overall, I love this franchise... excluding the moba variant, which kind of fell flat for me. the art is goofy yet clean. the music is nice and the action is addictive. it feel very rewarding to figure out which traps and combos work well together to work around different enemies and maps. however it can sometimes make you tunnel on specific strategies you notice work well. it also have less of a novelty feel since it feel very similar to the previous games. but overall, I've had lots of fun in this game and find it a both relaxing yet engaging way to spend some time. personally I'd say this is one of the few types of games I can enjoy solo as well as coop, without getting bored super fast. in the beginning it was a bit lacking once you had beaten all the maps and difficulties though. not sure how the DLC change things.. not a fan of the DLC concept overall, so I'm a bit biased.if it's on sale, it may be a great grab.[edit]if you avoid Cold As Eyes.[/edit]especially if you and your friend enjoy this type of games. it's fun both solo and coop, but personally I tend to think gaming is overall better with someone to enjoy it with~

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off by saying I very much enjoyed playing through the campaign of Orcs Must Die! 3.  The trap system is easily superior to alternate versions like Dungeon Defenders 2, primarily because in OMD!3 the traps and character do not upgrade during play.  This forces you to strategize on how to beat the obstacle, rather than just constantly bumping up numbers. I also appreciated the various enemies in the game, the voice acting for the orcs was always fun to hear.  The bosses were mostly great, except maybe the lich one that revives its allies.  That one was one of the last bosses so by then I knew to go straight for it.  Its health was not so great so it died right away and couldn’t revive anyone.  It probably should have been boss 1 or 2 instead so people would be less prepared.  I almost feel like the campaign should have gone on longer, ice enemies would probably have been a *cool* addition after facing the fire enemies.  Mainly I think this because I used freeze traps a lot which made the fire enemies seem not so effective, ice enemies would make it tougher and could force more interesting trap combinations.My main complaints would have to come from 2 things.  1. So many traps felt pointless to use, the most important thing for a trap to do is stun lock opponents.  Traps that do not do this end out not being used.  Don’t even get me started on the snow cannon, a trap that pushes enemies out of groups and sends them sliding past traps.  2.  Collision.  I love and hate this mechanic.  Ogre starts running, throws everyone everywhere.  They usually do this when the player shoots them, so mostly this is a fun addition that provides extra challenge and unpredictability based on where orcs land.  However, 5 skull runs can easily be lost because some ogre on the other side of the map gets annoyed and starts throwing people over barricades.  Even hearing the announcement that the enemy is at the rift gate does not cause the appropriate amount of alarm, because more than half the time it’s wrong.  Also endless mode is boring.Overall: the game is pretty great, it sucks the stadia fell through but I am very glad this got ported to steam.I make videos on youtube, blah blah, check me out,Dead3y3

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Tower Defence games, I have been disappointed by the Orcs Must Die series. Tower Defence games that are part Third Person Shooter (or vice versa) always fail to excel at either genre. In the case of Orcs Must Die the problem is just struggling to work out where to place the traps and determine the range of the weapons. The 3D environment leaves too much to guess work. The game forces you to juggle a stingy number of traps that never seem to be enough to spread around such large maps. It always feels like a compromise and you never feel confident that you are placing them in the most effective places. More than anything, it is just too stressful when the orcs get past your defences and you have to resort to standing in front of the portal and shooting them in the face at point blank range. In a traditional tower defence game it's a more distant spectacle and so not quite as frustrating.I'm not saying that the game is not fun or well produced, but as a strategy game it just isn't very satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was off to a pretty rocky start, launching with some of the traps way overpowered and then later nerfing everything that was good into the ground. The last update found a decent middle ground in regards to trap balance, and I think I can finally recommend it assuming they leave it at this.As for the game itself. It's more Orcs Must Die, any veterans to the series should know exactly what to expect from it. Brief summary: you play as the Warmage to defend against waves of enemies that try to reach the goal portal. You fight off enemies in 3rd person combat and place traps in strategic locations to thin out the hordes. The game can be played in single-player or in 2-player co-op.Stuff I like:-It's more Orcs Must Die, what more could I want?-New enemy types keep veteran players on their toes.-Good number of stages and game modes. The new scramble mode is pretty fun.-Endless mode feels much better balanced, and more engaging than it was in OMD2.Stuff I don't like:-A few of the maps feel a bit too tight in difficulty when playing in single-player.-Probably could have done with a few more new traps. The selection overall is pretty good, but I still would have liked to see more new stuff.-The 2 new protagonists (luckily, Max and Gabriella can be recruited after finishing the campaign, but would have liked to see some of the Unchained characters return rather than the ESG trash they came up with for this game.)-The large siege maps are a nice idea on paper but in reality they just kind of drag on and generally aren't that fun. It's a good thing there aren't too many of them.Game's a good value package for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs must Die. - A series that has had some hurdles indeed! -I've had a long history with the series, and followed Robot since the first game release way back when I was a kid. Honestly, the game has been replicated a number of times since but nothing quite matches the original! Orcs provide a returning pleasure of setting up effective kill-boxes, providing constant entertainment alongside casually unlocking skulls to further improve traps to try out new combos...Orcs must die 2 improved on everything, Character variation, victory dance variations, subtle animations, new traps, clever use of character design and sound. Having studied game design myself, the talent was clearly there and I honestly loved to support it by buying up the game multiple times for friends to enjoy in hearty co-op.I feel Robot themselves had some freedoms taken when trying to jump into the MOBA craze, and converting their property to a different type of game was incredibly jarring, resulting in a poor reception that strayed a little too far from its roots... but the fact that towards the end they took critical feedback and made massive changes to completely convert into a more old school experience. Changing a games genre that late on by completely refurbishing everything is a massive time soak, where as other companies would of simply dropped it.MASSIVE respect for the hard working employees.IF this was any other company, you know they would of pulled the entire team and left the IP to decay, but they tried so hard to make it something we could all enjoy and if given more funding and advertisement, I believe they could of pulled it back to some degree.Moving on finally to Orcs 3... and wow, they have returned to form with gameplay but not without difficulty. Some scars of the bad call launching on Stadia killed a decent launch chance, and some obvious cuts to staff and project scale have forced a few extra features to be downsized or simply removed. The trimming isn't all bad though, they have taken the best items and further balanced and improved them. I find myself using trinkets more often now and the variation of traps aren't lacking either... though I thirst for more! They have properly taken to the elemental damage system which can carry them with more trap variants in the future for sure, and despite these pains I can see them clawing back to the top in time.As I write this they already are patching in and listening to feedback... Though I don't know them personally, the attention they put in the games is enough to give me more faith than most triple A companies these days. I'm happy to keep buying this game to support them, and expand the roster of friends I play co-op with.I'm going to mash more orcs for sure, and ROBOT, I do hope you read this as you are appreciated for the work, and I'm honestly looking forward to whatever you add in next. (P.S the bounty hunter enemies that came after you during waves in unchained remind me of the bosses in war scenarios, they even have some similar abilities, would love to know if any of the old models and even ones unreleased could even be spruced up and implemented to make life easier for yourselves in future expansions!.. same as those unique guardians you could set up, like that fat pirate orc.. what a unit!)

_childDocuments_.review: So hear me out. There are orcs, and they must die. It's a 3rd person tower defense with heroes. Negligible story, fantastic art style and gameplay. Scramble mode (TD with roguelike runs) is frickin fun. Hells to the yeah play this if it's your genre. It's worth the full price of admission.If you have no idea what Orcs Must Die is, try out the first and/or second game first, the idea is the same but there's so much refinement from the first and second iterations. This iteration has a tighter design where traps often time only soften up or reduce the number of orcs leaving the player to pew pew them down only to have a second door busted down and frantic building of traps to whittle those down. It's very hectic and the difficulty of the levels ramp up quick. Bosses can absolutely be the cause of failure the first time but learning the levels is a part of the game. And by the time scramble mode unlocks, all that knowledge gained by replaying the levels come back into use and then some. And scramble mode is fantastic because the player starts a run with a choice of two levels with debuffs attached to each. Upon clearing a level, the player picks one from three buffs. These buffs and debuffs carry on through the run. The levels are also more difficult with less pauses in between each wave leading to some interesting panic tactics that wouldn't otherwise be used normally. It's just a heck of a lot of fun.Then there's the weekly challenge and endless mode, The former with restrictions to a level forcing the player to do weird things and the latter leading to using larger portions of maps that wouldn't normally be used in the other modes. It's a lot of variety all efficiently reused in a smart way that the levels feel familiar yet fresh.There's also coop that I've not touched at the time of this writing but hopefully *nudge* *wink* *stab* some so-called friends will want to try it one day. OMD2 was really fun with friends.In short, if you've played OMD1 or 2, this is more of the same with really good refinements. It's a return to form after Unchained (I still liked that one but it was a detour from the series) so people who hated Unchained but liked the original OMD style, this is that. For those who have not played OMD, go play the first two, they're still pretty great and decide whether or not this is one's cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've just wrapped up Orcs Must Die! 3, and let me tell ya, it's like they finally got their act together after the first two games turned into bug-riddled disasters. Seriously, were those games or crash test dummies? But this one, it's like they gave it a facelift, a makeover, and suddenly it's not a digital dumpster fire.They've pimped out the customization options – traps, weapons, skins – it's like virtual fashion week in there. And finally, we can swap characters without feeling guilty, like cheating on a game. The new characters? Yeah, they're alright, no biggie.The story's not some labyrinthine mind-bender – it's good old-fashioned fun. But seriously, devs, sort out that wonky stat system. It's like trying to keep track of a drunken snail.DLC's a bit on the short side, but hey, it's there. And can we talk about the absence of money-grabbing schemes? I'm genuinely surprised. Overall, Orcs Must Die! 3, you did good – a proper co-op gem. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game and I loved the last 3 orcs must die games, so it pains me to put a negative review.  Theres just so much content missing to the point where its frustrating.  Especially after paying over $38 i feel like ive been bamboozled... If we look at past games you can see theres too much stuff taken out... and lets not forget ORCS MUST DIE UNCHAINED..what a beauty.. hundreds of hours on the xbox... awesome maps and so much content that it was worthy, even better than the last 2 games.  Did i mention how awesome and well constructed the maps were? and when you compare them to this OMD game, youll ask yourself WTF happened...  the gameplay in OMD3 is still amazing dont get me wrong, I really love it.   For some stupid reason, only half the campaign maps are available in endless.. very few of the good ones either and NOT A SINGLE War Scenario level is in the endless mode... over 11 traps just for war scenario now useless...    I feel like I bought an alpha that runs and works damn good, with amazing and addicting gameplay, but most features and content coming soon sort of deal... for $38 WTF...I guess I gotta wait till they release the rest of the game to get my moneys worth. The first 2 war scenarios were awesome but they got worse and worse in the sense that most war scenario traps were useless as youd be fighting in doors 90% of the time and they cant be placed in door(some can with perks).  The best traps were ones you needed to activate by being close, but since theres alot of directions that they come from, you cant exactly activate the traps..so why place them?  The hordes tho are awesome..FINALLY hundreds of enemies at once...but only for a few waves.  Endless is the only replayability here so its stupid not to include war scenarios in endless.  I guess theres scramble mode and replaying campaign but after awhile you'll be disappointed by not being able to see how long you can go with the cool setup you made.. and the best maps aren't available in endless.... The first DLC that was free for steam users is pretty short.. 5 levels and only one is in endless...ONE...ONE... smh... The paid DLC is pretty short too. Bottom line, this game has solid, addicting gameplay but lacks ENOUGH content... I hope I can change my review to positive but at this point I cant recommend this game at FULL price..WAIT FOR A SALE.2 YEARS later and they havnt even bothered to add the rest of the maps as endless.. Buy on sale otherwise youll feel ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this review with this: I don't think this is a bad game. No, far from it actually. I'm just disappointed with too many things to give the game a recommendation.I absolutely adored OMD:U, spent hundreds of hours in it. In that game, you felt as useful as the traps did. You were useful for picking off certain powerful enemies that would be able to reach the end of your killbox. There was a balance to the playstyle. In this game however, you have to do all the work to kill off anything because traps are way too weak and money is way too tight. Even in Endless mode, you still can't even build a full killbox that can handle even basic enemies before the difficulty ramp up lets them push through all your traps. I don't see the point in war scenario traps being restricted only to those specific maps. Perhaps just let players use a limited number of them in normal maps so people have more of a reason to upgrade them. There aren't any endless war scenario maps so outside of the campaign, war scenario traps are useless.Perhaps things will get better in the future, but considering how little has changed since this game came out originally on Stadia .  Overall, I cannot in good faith recommend this game for $30. $15 or so, sure, but not full price.tl;dr:Game is indeed fun, but is ruined by poor game design decisions that were not in previous entries in the series.Purchase at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die! 3 Review: An All-Out Orc Annihilation by DeathbringerOrcs Must Die! 3 is the ultimate battleground, where warriors live and die in a storm of steel, fury, and fire. Forget everything you know about defending a rift—this time, you're wielding the power of a metal warlord, facing down orcs in numbers so insane it’s like charging headfirst into Ragnarok itself. And you’ve got the heavy artillery to match! Catapults, grinders, walls of spikes—each trap is crafted to leave a brutal, blood-soaked path of ruin in your wake.This isn’t a battle; it’s a crusade of chaos. Every wave of orcs thunders forward like an unholy army, and it’s your calling to bring them down with the wrath of a true metal warrior. Enormous battles unfold with an intensity that’ll shake you to the core, and every kill feels like a rite of honor as you crush, smash, and obliterate anything that stands in your path.As Warmage, you’re not just a fighter; you’re the harbinger of doom, the axe-wielding reaper these orcs feared in their darkest nightmares. Orcs Must Die! 3 dares you to conquer on a scale never seen before. The battlefield is yours to paint red, and the enemies? Nothing but fuel for your warpath. This isn’t a game, it’s a testament of strength—metal mayhem, glory, and the roar of victory await!Do you have the metal for what it take to win!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time OMD fan, I can confidently say that this is by far an inferior game to what Unchained was before it shut down. I miss the large variety of characters and varying play styles that each of them had. The maps in Unchained were a lot more enjoyable than this game. As well as the traps and how they functioned being much better in Unchained. While the War maps are really, really cool and probably the single best feature of the game, going back to the bare-bones root gameplay of the OMD series compared to what Unchained had to offer after it stepped away from the primary PvP elements it was originally developed for, just feels too basic now.The characters in OMD3 exist essentially as skins and offer nothing to the table. Where as in Unchained, each character had their own unique kit which made playing missions different depending on what character you brought.Overall, it's a good game for anyone who enjoys a well made tower defense. Pick it up if you want some quick satisfaction, but I wouldn't bet on any longevity or unique replayablity. Hopefully things get added down the line to create some variety, but as it is right now, there isn't a whole lot offered.

_childDocuments_.review: Main points:- lower money in rounds, leading to less traps.- traps are (mostly) significantly weaker than previous titles, with a large focus on active player combat which is unfortunately bland- the games been balanced with a co-op partners active damage and presence in mind, esp on Rift Lord. - story? don't expect one.If you haven't got a coop partner, enjoy getting overwhelmed in Rift Lord repeatedly unless you want to be forced into very specific cheese/stall tactics.Unchained's PvE mode was better than what we've got here - given a handful of the maps from it have been reused, its disappointing how little you can cover any of the maps in comparison.Siege mode - inspired by Unchained, you get a giant map and hundreds of enemies but.......you can't cover in many traps or do much repathing due to lack of currency.Hero options - they exist, but have minimal gameplay differences once you've unlocked them by completing the campaign and weapons to swap out.TL:DR - if you want a 3rd person tower defence, go with OMD1 and OMD2. They probably would have been better off repurposing Unchained to offline given the 3 person co-op, numerous varied heroes and tonnes of maps.

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die! 3 sticks true to the winning formula of its predecessors, delivering yet another round of delightful orc-slaying chaos. For fans of the series, this installment is a no-brainer – it's everything you loved about the earlier games, but with a fresh coat of polish and some exciting new twists.The core gameplay remains as satisfying as ever, blending tower defense mechanics with action-packed combat in a way that feels both familiar and invigorated. The addition of new traps, weapons, and enemies keeps the strategy and excitement fresh, ensuring that each wave of orcs brings its own unique challenge.What really shines in Orcs Must Die! 3 is the sheer scale of the battles. _childDocuments_.review: A great return to form. It's pretty much OMD2 again, but I mean that in a good way. The game is more balanced to be played (and full completed) solo, for one thing. That should always be the core experience design, with co-op (which I'm also a huge fan of) being an additive experience.The level design is, as a result, much improved, and less in the vein of difficulty-through-annoyance design. They removed fliers from the main campaign, which is an improvement, and the aforementioned annoyance-design enemies from the OMD2 DLC are missing, thankfully. Instead they added outdoors "War Scenarios" which are silly, because the player's best course of action is always to ignore them and build their defenses indoors anyway. This results in just a drag on playtime, and is otherwise not a significant negative. Much of the old glitches are still around, but the game is noticeably more polished than its prequels ever were. I do wish there were more new interesting enemies added, but some of the new traps made up for that, although the selection was still noticeably small. I felt like most of the improvement effort went into making a more solidly designed core experience, with higher quality level design and level balancing. Despite the appearance of OMD3 as bare-bones, I think this grounded focus is why I enjoyed this game more than OMD2, which got lost in balancing issues that led to more stressful than satisfying victories. OMD3 was immensely satisfying to full complete, and took what I would call the ideal amount of time and challenge to do so. I would easily buy an OMD4 in this vein day 1, with more confidence than I had this time, following Unchained. I'm aware that there are probably many Unchained fans a who feel abandoned by OMD3, but so were OMD1+2 fans abandoned by Unchained, which (I haven't looked into it, but I understand) didn't financially perform in turn. Hopefully, incoming DLC can add in some of that further complexity for this game, and the next game can be the next step up in overall design. I would love to see Robot create a polished and strong core OMD experience for each new game, which then has additional modes that branch out into the experimental gameplay their team is clearly fond of innovating. The added Scramble mode was an inch of this, and I would enjoy seeing attempts at PvP modes be made, preferably at smaller scales which grow with the interest in them.So if you liked OMD1 or OMD2, this is definitely the superior version of those games. (And if you're a fan of tower defense, you probably don't mind similarity in your sequels, let's be honest.) Considering that the scope of this game was intended to be a return to form, it definitely delivers, and it was probably the wiser choice to only take a few steps up, rather than attempt a whole staircase at the same time.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fun, but isn't quite as deep as I'd like. I feel like I've got a criticism for almost every area in the game, but I did have a great time while playing. For me, it was addicting for as long as the campaign lasted. So on sale, this game hits good for me. I mention criticisms in the hope that they'd make for an amazing OMD4. My biggest request is for split screen co-op. I love when I can play tower defense with a friend. Especially for a game like this which is fairly easy to pick up.The sandbox of traps is pretty wide, but doesn't feel too rewarding to experiment with. I pretty much kept using barriers, butterfly boxes, ceiling lazers, saws and grinders. I swapped standard spikes for fire tiles and didn't notice much better performance for the cost. Beyond orcs burning lol. Instead of increased damage taken, I think exploding orcs with fire traps, if the orcs are poisoned, would be cool. But I'm glad there's weekly challenges that force trap combinations for you to use. It adds a lot of variety to the experience. Otherwise, there's a bunch of traps I don't feel inclined to buy and use.I like the variety of map sizes and layouts, but feel like there's a path I'm forced to take to beat them sometimes. For a crude example, on a map with three paths to the tower, I'll just slap a barricade on two of the paths to force all enemies down one; a path I've set up as my kill zone. I felt doing this became pretty common place. Because it works so well. The only occasional obstacle to combat with this is to defeat enemies designed to break barriers. I think I would've preferred increasing the money earned for traps so that I could try different traps on each lane, or be forced to try something different because, say, one path doesn't have walls or something. I do like the map variety all in all. The war scenarios are my favorite. It feels exciting to have hordes of orcs approach the tower, with maybe one path breaking through a barrier, so I've gotta rush to defend.The combat feels satisfying with long range weapons. It feels great to land headshots or freeze enemies. I do wish DPS upgrades were as viable as stun/freeze upgrades for weapons. It's way more viable to freeze enemies so they'll stay in trapped areas. I didn't like the close combat weapons because of the ogres, who stun you when they get close. And I do wish on Endless Mode, the weapons didn't become useless beyond their stunning abilities after a certain point.On that note, I'd love if Endless had an option to tick off for double or triple the funds so that I could try crazy trap layouts. I'll get really far in Endless and feel limited solely by the number of traps I'm able to purchase.The orcs are a delight to fight against. Their silly one liners are my favorite part, or their little grunts when they die. It feels epic to see them dismembered on traps as well lol. I would've like to see more of a use of enemies that disable traps around them, but keep a steady pace towards the goal. Or protect their nearby orcs fron trap damage until killed. And I'm not as much of a fan of the fire-resistant enemies, as they're fairly similar to the orcs, but just have a resistance to the fire. The crossbow orcs and the explodey runners, I'm a fan of. They have me rethink my gameplay in combat.I don't regret my purchase here. It was nice to get back into Orcs Must Die 3. There's just some elements that stop it from being amazing for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, This is a tough review to write. I want to like this game. It runs great on Steam Deck, FYI. But, man is it difficult. I'm not sure why. I think it's the game's main Schtick - The combination of a 3D Shooter type game with a tower defense. It's a cool "what if," like "What if, in our tower defense game, we made it so you ran around on the map actually placing traps instead of acting like a god that places traps." It's an interesting idea that ultimately makes it feel like you are playing Fortnight or Minecraft. Because you can run around in the world on the map, the maps are huge, the enemies are hard to contain (funnel through usual tower defenses), and you cannot play the game without shooting things. In fact, most of the actual time while the level is running, you MUST shoot constantly, because nothing you can build for defenses can stand up to the horde. They force you to fight. I mean, it's the game's main Schtick. Let's be clear: This is NOT a tower defense game. It's a First Person Shooter that can use traps for some reason, despite the traps being useless. And the first War map stopped me in my tracks. Stopped all progression. It's impossible to solo, even on easy mode. Apparently, it requires friends to do 2 person things? I think, IDK. I mean, the traps trigger and have cooldowns, so they don't even hit a quarter of the mobs that strep on them. Basically, the traps are boring and mostly useless.TL;DR It doesn't cure the itch I have for a good tower defense game because you can't tell you are playing one.

_childDocuments_.review: OMD! 3 puts a heavy burden on the system. Even though the official system requirements are indeed lower, it only runs on my PC with the occasional hiccups and quite often lags, and it also tends to get my machine to heat up. That's one of the main downsides of the game. Apart from that, it is indeed a fun game: Lots of new enemies, some of them immune to certain traps, while the upgrades to your traps don't add elemental effects but replace the original damage type, which makes choosing the right gear to equip more of a challenge. Also, the game seems more action orientated compared to the second installment, in-game money is harder to get at (unless you get very good combos), and more often than not you can't just rely on your trap build, however strong you try to make it, which is bound to give you quite an adrenaline rush as you try to catch up with those enemies that are getting past the kill-zone. Some maps are more fun than others, some are less forgiving and force you to build a certain way, allowing less creativity (unless you are way better at gaming than me, at least...). Usually it takes up to the last wave to really get a good trap-combo build going. I wish there were just one more wave to each map to reward me with at least one chance to get to see the traps do the work (almost) on their own. All of that made the game quite a challenge for me, but I made it a point to get through all of it (at least in apprentice mode) on my own before giving my first co-op run a go.I foun doable, with a decent amount of failing, reevaluating and training, to five-star all maps at normal difficulty. For some of the Rift Lord difficulty maps I needed co-op support though, at least to five-star them. So, if you feel OMD! 2 gets too easy after repeated runs, OMD! 3 might be just the thing for you, unless you mind having a bit more action inside your tower defense. It could be argued that this is partly a tactical fighting game now, but with VERY important strategic elements (tower defense) still at the core of it. There is one exception to the game-play points I mentioned above, though: Sprinkled throughout the game, there are so-called War Scenarios. And they are HUGE - bigger maps with tons of enemies coming at you! These War Scenarios can look pretty scary when you are just starting out, but once you survive the first wave (or two) and have found your bearings on how you can use the map (setup) to your advantage, money will flow in like crazy, which means these war maps will reward you for all the struggles in the "normal" levels that came before any particular war map. Usually, these maps have some sort of castle or stronghold plus a larger environment surrounding that building. So it is up to you whether you want to defend outside or inside its gates. Most of the time, both ways will work (or a mix of both, inside and outside defences), so you can really experiment there and have the game "your own way" - beating it in various ways that are still fun and not too much of a challenge either. So, basically, War Scenarios mean having a good clean MASSACRE TIME! One downside of the game, however, apart from its high system requirements, is that while in co-op mode you cannot pause the game, neither is there an ingame chat function, and you also have no way of seeing your partner's equipment choices - which makes planning extremely difficult. You can basically only sketch out a plan ahead of starting a map using external communication. Or you will have to rely on your partner's intuition and adaptability to whatever you are doing, and both of your improvisational skills in adapting to another person's playing style. This makes co-op needlessly inconvenient and also more of a challenge compared to OMD! 2. Co-op using an additional communication program might still make the overall experience of playing easier than going solo, because two players can control more than one heavily trapped zone at once. Going solo, this becomes a burden, due to loss of time running around trying to micromanage the trap setup while the orcs advance. Furthermore, co-op in OMD! 3 has one advantage over co-op in OMD! 2, and that is that each player will keep the same number of item slots as they would have when playing solo - so more combos are possible with two players than with just one. And higher combos will earn you more in-game cash. A great addition of OMD! 3 is the new Scramble mode, which means a campaign extended over five random maps - but with a new randomized disadvantage (and also some boosts from the second map on) added before each map that you play - and these disadvantages stack onto each other. So each of these five maps will get harder to beat! It is also a win-all-or-lose-all campaign when it comes to being rewarded any skulls for a Scramble run. This mode is especially fun in co-op. At least if the system requirements of OMD! 3 leave you and your partner enough room for an additional intercom program to discuss which perks to keep and which to exchange for a random other one. Will this make it easier or harder? If you like fast-paced, action-orientated Tower Defense games with a special focus on Action/Shooter elements, this might be just the game for you. If, however, what you MOST enjoyed of previous Orcs Must Die! games by Robot Entertainment was their "Sand-Box" factor of not only killing orcs, but doing that all over again (each time trying to outdo yourself by coming up with even more creatively outrageous, next to absurd and FAR OUT ways) - maybe think again before opting for this one. To be honest, I am a bit disappointed in "OMD! 3" in general.I get that many players appreciate the new type of challenges posed by escalating the difficulty (of any but the war maps) - especially when played in Rift Lord mode. But I guess this heightened challenge could also have been brought about in quite another (better) way; say by adding yet another difficulty level beyond Rift Lord (including altered pathings! - and/or addional gates with even more enemy types) - while at the same time PRESERVING most of the sandbox feel that prior games offered to CASUAL players.Visually, "OMD!3" is indeed quite stunning - but this does come at a hefty price:Once you have finished your first runs through the different game modes, the shine quickly wears off - something that was not typical for the previous games - including the much maligned but (after many workovers) ultimately more than passable "OMD!: U" (a game that, to be fair, already offered excellent graphics years prior to OMD! 3 in its map designs - and even more variation of themes!).Honestly, this might sound worse than it is - other players might indeed prefer OMD! 3 for the sheer vastness many of its maps have in store; it all works on a bigger scale, rivalling and sometimes even outshining OMD!: U. Granted: I had lots of fun with "Orcs Must Die! 3" initially; I still do enjoy the occasional co-op run; and I will continue my attempts at the second DLC offerings (which are harder again than the 1st DLC already included in the main game's PC version); but LONGTERM the whole gaming experience - especially if compared to OMD! 2 - feels a bit MEH...

_childDocuments_.review: Alright so idk whats going on with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is the Review section, but this game is very fun. I played the first one during Xbox 360 days and this is the recent one that i've played since then.Youve got two characters at the start but more are unlocked at some point when you progress in the game, one with the bow thats accurate used for headshots while being able to powerslam the orcs, and one with a shotgun that can levitate. (these both use some mana) Both of these items can be upgraded using SKULLS, the item you get after completing a level, the higher the difficulty the extra you get. The regular upgrade is something like faster fire rate for the bow, or faster reload for the 4-shot shotgun, THEN youve got the milestones. Getting a certain amount of headshots for the bow unlocks unique upgrades for the bow and using the shotgun's alt fire to kill a certain amount of orcs (like a grenade launcher) unlocks the unique upgrades for the gun. (You can also use both weapons on one character if you prefer a certain ability that they have, it just uses a trap slot if you do choose to do this.)Now onto some traps, using these SKULLS you unlock, you can upgrade the traps to do certain things, for example tar can slow orcs even slower, etc. In addition to these regular upgrades traps also have milestones to unlock unique perks like the weapons. Also which I just found out from playing, you can use the SKULLS you get from levels to purchase new traps, (or even a cosmetic if you want it - for the character youre playing). So you can purchase a new trap (or gadget) and instantly level it up if you want. I bought the wind belt that lets you push orcs and just power leveled that with my SKULLS just cause I remember using it in the first game and I enjoyed it.Now if for some reason you purchase an upgrade for something and it turns out you DONT actually like it, you can REFUND item upgrades completely. I do recommend this. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, very fun. There are a few frustrations however, the satisfaction you get from a tower defense game is in creating nearly impossible to pass bottle-necks. This game tries its hardest to prevent you from being able to do this for some reason (multiple spawn points that don't intersect). I don't get it, it's as if they are saying "oh haha, players like to play this game to set up defensible bottlenecks, so let's stop them from doing that!". A much better solution would have been to simply ramp up the number of enemies they were sending your way. And that leads me to a second point, the endless mode, are you kidding me? The game will automatically start deleting your barricades (I checked this, barricades that were completely out of line of sight were disappearing) after you have passed wave 20 or so. Why?? Again, just increase the number of mobs your sending. They also scale down money as waves increase which is another frustrating mechanic, and finally, they increase enemy health. Endless mode should be thought of as "about 20 to 25 waves at maximum....mode". Overall, good for a solid 10 hours or so of fun, so I would recommend to buy this on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die! 3 successfully builds upon the beloved formula of its predecessors, delivering a satisfying blend of tower defense strategy and third-person action. The game's core loop of setting traps, unleashing mayhem, and mowing down hordes of orcs remains as addictive as ever, with the addition of new features that expand the scale and variety of gameplay.One of the most notable additions is the War Scenarios, which introduce massive battles with significantly larger maps and orc armies. These epic encounters push players to think on a grander scale, utilizing new traps and weapons designed for crowd control. The sheer chaos and destruction in these scenarios are a joy to behold and add a fresh dimension to the series.The game's humor and charming art style continue to be strong points, with witty dialogue and exaggerated character designs that perfectly complement the over-the-top action. The variety of traps and weapons allows for creative problem-solving, encouraging players to experiment with different combinations to find the most efficient (and often hilarious) ways to dispatch the orc hordes.However, Orcs Must Die! 3 is not without its issues. The difficulty curve can be inconsistent, with some levels feeling frustratingly challenging while others are a breeze. This imbalance can lead to moments of both boredom and excessive frustration, potentially turning off less patient players.The game's progression system, while functional, feels somewhat lackluster. The unlock rate for new traps and upgrades can be slow, and some of the later unlocks don't feel impactful enough to justify the grind. This can lead to a sense of stagnation in the mid-to-late game.Multiplayer, while a welcome addition, suffers from occasional connectivity issues and a lack of cross-platform play, limiting the player pool and potentially impacting long-term engagement.The story, though not the primary focus, is rather thin and does little to contextualize the action or develop the characters beyond one-dimensional archetypes. A more fleshed-out narrative could have added depth to the experience and given players more reason to push through the campaign.Performance-wise, the game generally runs well, but there are occasional frame rate drops during particularly hectic moments, especially in War Scenarios. These technical hiccups, while not game-breaking, can disrupt the flow of gameplay at crucial moments.Despite these issues, Orcs Must Die! 3 remains a highly enjoyable experience that successfully evolves the series formula. The core gameplay loop is as satisfying as ever, and the new additions bring welcome variety to the table. With some balancing tweaks, performance optimizations, and perhaps a more robust progression system, the game could truly excel.In conclusion, Orcs Must Die! 3 is a worthy addition to the series that fans will undoubtedly enjoy. While it has room for improvement in several areas, the foundation is solid, and the game provides hours of trap-laying, orc-slaying fun. It's a recommended pick for both series veterans and newcomers looking for a unique blend of strategy and action.

The particle effects from the various weapons and traps are stunning, specifically the Blunderbuss' secondary bomb attack. The dozens of blue effects that come from the attack look amazing as they all scatter off in different directions. It looks great. _childDocuments_.review: I own OMD 1 & 2...loved them both. I tried Unchained, pure garbage. It was sad when they went the microtransaction scam route. When I heard Unchained was scrapped and OMD3 was going to be "normal" I was excited...until now. They've had a year with the game on Stadia which means it should be well optimized for Linux/Wine/Proton...yet it stutters like a dude who got drunk to talk to his crush...and now he can't talk. Right out of the gate you have to edit INI files to stop the game from turning your machine into a fit pit with race conditions. Never mind the fact you can't do something as basic as edit your keys...oh there is a options panel for it...where they let you map your JUMP, and next wave keys...oh GEEZ...basic functionality games have had from the late 1980's this game lacks!Worst for me is I bought two copies of this because my roommate was super excited for it...She woke up to me having to tell her not to launch the game lest it set her machine on fire and that she'd have to play backwards (she's left handed) because you can't map your keys...you know because that matters when your CPU and GPU hit 100Cel for a game that needs 30FPS max and you have to power off to let your machine cool half way through a round...I mean it's not an eSport game and even if we had 244Hz screens the game is just uncapped so it maxes everything out no matter what...244hz screens YOU NEED TO HIT 900FPS!...until you thermal throttle, or the caps on your GPU pop...Honestly ROBOT...what the hell!? I'm a dev...I know launches can be jarring or down right nightmares but what the hell did you expect? You've set this up for pure failure. I mean did you hire gerbils for QC and beta testing? Are you hiring your dev's from PreSchool? My lord there are so many rookie mistakes and no no's in the game it's unfathomable.Now I know there are a lot of trolls on here. I'm sure there are more than a few people that think I'm one because I tell the truth...but this is a dumpster fire. From the potential to literally nuke your HDR enabled monitor, pop the caps on your GPU or VRM on your motherboard this is needlessly sloppy. The forums are littered with "works for me" idiots trying to flood and take away from people with legitimate problems, some of which could cost you a few $1000 if it kills your machine...(Think Amazon Games New World - Proven to nuke GPU's with a similar issue.) As a developer one of the #1 things you should know is RACE CONDITIONS == BAD...uncapped frame rate == RACE CONDITION! Do not confuse this with high FPS and trying to max out things in a beneficial way. The game makes API calls like a run away for loop. We're in the menu...toss in a needless while/until loop shooting non-sense to /dev/null to ensure the GPU stays at peak wattage! There is a fast car and then there is a fast car brake torquing for no reason because the driver is too stupid to realize the eBrake is on...this game is both the throttle wide open and the eBrake...and the devs foot on the brake...and the other dev is pouring gas on your car...the the CEO of ROBOT is shooting roman candles at the dev with the gas can...If you're brave...check back in a year...maybe two (no I'm not exaggerating). Look at CyberPunk 2077. No matter what the reason for why it launched as it did the bottom line was that was the result of 12 years of work. So if you think ROBOT can clean this up in a year, you're optimistic or a fool...or an optimistic fool.First I'd be happy to eat my words about the time it will take Robot to fix this (if they do). However while they are releasing hotfixes I can't help but go back to the fact this isn't an EA release. The game has been out for a year. Sure on Stadia there is "one machine" they had to support but there is so much of the game that is flat out NOT FINISHED this isn't even an issue of technical issues. To in game chat...no keybind support...backtracking on features...barely anything new. It's like they got a half baked prototype port of OMD2 ported to the Unreal Engine and took a big long break...then forgot it wasn't finished.**I've rebought this game for my roommate (though now we loose the preorder skins, whatever they were) since Robot actually made good on adding input mapping...Still not word on if they are dealing with stuttering and the zillions of other issues being reported. I won't rebuy until I see a patch for the stuttering. While I'm glad to see Robot dealing with things their communication about it all has been horrid and the fact the game has been out for a year on another platform and they never addressed any of this is a massive WTF!?***I set up in home sharing so I could occasionally test to see if the stuttering was fixed. I fired up the game to test and just uncover more bugs, unfinished bits of game and stupid design choices that make OMD3 unplayable trash...I had so looked forward to this but looks like I just need to give up on Robot...stuff that was a "given" or obvious needed game design for OMD has been omitted from OMD3...like being able to SEE if you're up against something. FOV/Aim was already a weak point for OMD2. Odd aspect Ratio's could make playing impossible but in OMD3 you can't see period if you back up against something. Camera just zooms into the back of your characters head. Good to see Robot didn't think anything through or test jack before launch.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fantastic time playing Orcs Must Die 3 with my friend, especially since we both love to strategize and achieve the maximum 5 skulls on every level.Overall, Orcs Must Die 3 is a great game! However, I believe it could benefit from some improvements. Personally, I find the presence of boomers and the ability to destroy blockades a bit frustrating. In my opinion, tower defense games should focus on optimizing tower placement rather than allowing them to be destroyed, except when they are poorly positioned and blocking enemy paths. Additionally, it would be incredible if the game could support 3 players, possibly by scaling the difficulty according to the number of players. This could be achieved by empowering player weapons and implementing a shared gold account for a more cooperative and balanced experience.One tip for new players: You can enable the timer in the settings to keep track of your progress towards earning 5 skulls. In my opinion, this feature should be a default setting, as it enhances the gameplay experience and encourages players to strive for better performance.In conclusion, Orcs Must Die 3 is a highly enjoyable game with its strategic elements and cooperative gameplay, but addressing the concerns mentioned above could make it even more satisfying for tower defense enthusiasts like me and my friends.

There is far too much active hampering in the game levels that ensures that traps far too rarely shine. Using enviromental dangers? Nah. it fits very badly together. Kill corridors? Nah, make your own with barricades. Actually made your own? Nah, constant sappers. The huge "army" trap levels are the WORST. Like, one of the new traps is this huge structure that's literally covered in places to put traps, but NAH, every damn level in the game is so damn short that even the maps that explicitly market themselves on epic size never see any sort of trap saturation. Endless mode? Gimme a break. The mode is "endless" but pressure is so insane that even an "impressive result" still nets you a short and frantic fight with a pitifully small amount of traps.I played 1 and 2 and loved them both, but it seems 3 learned something new in that live service game they made. They learned to suck ass.For good measure, endless mode is my favourite, the most fun I had in this series is running around a staircase for 3 hours dumping trolls off ledges or slamming earth elementals down 6 flights of stairs. It's too bad about campaign maps but if they made improvements to endless mode it'd at least cater to what this old fan wanted.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun 3D tower defense game. It's very addictive and the flow of the campaigns are nice. The Good: 1) increase in difficulty from wave to wave has a nice flow. Not too much too fast, in most cases, which is nice especially for new players. 2) Endless mode3) Unlock new traps and weapons, but the main weapon is locked in the campaign until you complete it. 4) New heroes unlock5) Upgrade traps to make them more efficient or to change the primary damage type in case you're facing a foe with resistance. 6) War scenarios give a change of pace and a break away from the main character/hero gameplay.7) Small learning curve especially for those who enjoy strategy games or tower defense. The Bad: What I hope for improvement on is the ability to see more details from to wave such as the following: 1) How much health do the monsters have?2) How much increase is applied to speed/health/etc from wave to wave? 3) How much damage does each trap apply? Crowd Control- What percentage to decrease speed and how does that change from wave to wave? 4) More information on the trap selection screen at the start of each game. 5) Better information around the impact of the trap upgrades. How much increase in base damage will apply on a damage upgrade? Speed on speed upgrades? etc. 6) Forced to only receive 3-10 seconds between waves in endless after a few waves.7) Inviting other players and joining from an invite can't be 100% done in game. If the person being invited is already in game, they have to leave the game to click on a link to join the game they've been invited to. This would be so much better if all of the invite and joining could take place in the game. The Ugly: Endless is very fun, but the title of the mode doesn't quite fit. At a certain point the monsters ignore traps, attacks, players and run straight to the rift. Why? It is so much better to have the monsters continue to be aggro'd by damage from players and traps. Even the crowd control traps are ignored at some point. The wave for which this occurs depends on the map, but I hate it. I love the endless mode up until this point. If I can survive for 8 hours with the normal mechanics applied (though it should become harder with more focus on health and attack from the foes rather than speed and ignoring everything), why not allow me to play for 8 hours. Isn't that why it's called endless? Apparently not. As you progress through Endless mode you'll a point where you won't receive more than 3-10 seconds between waves. I should be able to make adjustments as long as it takes (especially solo or with a friend I know) between rounds in endless mode. Or how about a setting that allows the players to toggle this ability before the game? Final Result/OpinionNeither of the above cons are deal breakers. The game is still very fun and addictive. I recommend it for anyone looking for a great experience in a strategy game or a tower defense connoisseur!

_childDocuments_.review: Very solid 20 hours of initial gameplay (at the time of this review), with an unknown and possibly absurd amount of end game replayability.if you've ever played dungeon defenders, this is basically that in terms of gameplay loop, but it fixes 3 fundamental problems in DD, those being: 1: There's no gear, thus the towers and weapons you can use are actually balanced to the content you're doing, meaning that you don't become so geared that you place one tower and it has infinite range and one shots everything 30 times per second, but you also are never undergeared in the same way.2: You can influence enemy pathing with barricades, meaning you can funnel them into one or two choke points on most maps for actual strategy instead of having to defend all 8 entry points to your rift (core).3: There's only one objective to defend. personally, i appreciate the focus.(another thing that i like, but is more of a preference thing than a mechanic improvement is that there's no real "classes" in the game, so every character can do everything, the only fundamental difference being the initial default weapon (but they all get unlocked later for everyone) which may be a draw, may be something you didn't want because class fantasy is important to you, but i thought it ought to be mentioned.)another thing that I thought was perhaps the best feature of this game that is not present in DD, is the War maps. basically a 4-8 times bigger map, 10 times the enemy spawns, special war units and traps to mow down the hordes, arrows literally raining from the sky... it's just a good time... perhaps my only gripe with it is that it doesn't have an endless wave mode yet like most of the non-war maps.
