_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die! 3 is an action-tower defence video game and the fourth installment in the Orcs Must Die! series. The series focuses around the defence of magic rifts with the use of a variety of weapons, traps and trinkets. The first and second Orcs Must Die! installments focused strongly on a solo or co-op experience across a campaign and endless modes, whereas the third installment known as "Orcs Must Die! Unchained" aimed to bring back the classic survival mode with introduction of new features and gamemodes but however failed, and has since been shut down.Orcs Must Die! 3 is the direct sequel to the successful second installment and incorporates many similar features to the second installment in comparison to "Orcs Must Die! Unchained". Orcs Must Die! 3 currently contains two campaigns. The first campaign spans across 18 levels, and the second campaign across 5 levels. Orcs Must Die! 3 also includes the classic endless mode in which players must survive on a level with never ending waves of enemies to see how many waves they can survive. Introduction of two new modes, Scramble and Weekly Challenges add new playability to the game and extends its life significantly.The game can be played completely solo or with a co-op partner, whichever method is chosen both can experience the story and levels together from start to finish.RATINGSGameplay× Unplayable× Terrible× Satisfactory✓ Upstanding× Endless FunGraphics× Unacceptable× Poor× Satisfactory✓ Beautiful× Realistic Game Duration× 0 - 1 Hour× 1 - 5 Hours✓ 5 - 10 Hours× 10 - 50 Hours× 50 - 100 HoursGamemodes Included✓ Campaign✓ Endless✓ Scramble✓ Weekly ChallengesPlayer Limit✓ Solo✓ Two Player Co-Op× Three +So... is the game any good?Orcs Must Die! 3 is an absolutely amazing and enjoyable game for any person who loves the style of tower defence games. The game offers a variety of weapons, trinkets and traps that can be combined to create fun circumstances for you and another friend. Gameplay is smooth and will provide both players with hours of fun on first play.The downfall of the game however is its lack of levels and in general equipment to purchase. Previous games provided players with a large inventory of equipment to use, this game NEEDS more equipment. Compared to previous entries the upgrades on equipment are lackluster and rarely provide the player with much to grind for. The developers will need to continuously add more content over time to make this game really shine, but it isn't known whether they'll drop the game just like the previous entry. Speaking of levels, the campaign is far too short and endless provides the player base with little option of maps to play on. For the price, the content in the game is far too low. I recommend purchasing the game on a sale as I personally feel its amazing gameplay and potential is ruined by a lack of content. Changes can always be made and I strongly believe the developers will not abandon this project.Overall, Orcs Must Die! 3 is a definite grab if you love tower defence, planning traps and destroying large amounts of enemies. If you're willing to pay the price go ahead, I promise you will not regret it, especially if you're a returning player from "Orcs Must Die!" and "Orcs Must Die! 2". OVERALL RATING8.5/10

It is no longer available for acquisition.Highscore list is also not Steam compatible, you don't see your friends' highscores.As a game it is "Ok" but it is vastly inferior to its predecessor, OMDU (Orcs Must Die: Unchained) which was free to play version of OMD3, but was cancelled after not providing enough financial compensation and had a heavily mismanaged marketing.As a game OMDU was near perfect, it even had PvP maps at one point, the only problem it suffered from was severe unbalance between new and old players.OMD3 is missing a majority of enemy subtypes, not a single themed map and most traps are missing entirely and their customization is extremely weak compared to what OMDU provided. _childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die 3 is a rather delightful game. I've found myself enjoying every hour I've played in this game. My personal favorite part of this game is just how stupid orcs are. This may be a turn off for more competitive players wanting a challenge, but it is so funny to see an orc walk up an entire flight of stairs, be right next to the rift, but still turn around just because there's a barricade blocking the path. They then go down the entire flight of stairs then go up the OTHER flight of stairs. It's absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hilarious and makes it easy to funnel everything into your death rooms. Just be careful to not barricade everything completely off or they will actually break down your barricades (and quickly, I might add)I enjoy the amount of customization you can achieve with every trap weapon and trinket. You can add elemental effects to traps or have it stun, and weapons might get other unique effects. Trinkets in particular are a passive with a strong active attached to them. Take for example the crown. It gives you passive health regeneration but when activated heals both you and your teammate. There is a lot to this game and you can absolutely mix and match to your liking. This game also has a focus on score, which gives the game a bit of replayability if you enjoy beating your friends. I personally really enjoyed how different the game becomes when your goals change. If you want 5 stars in a level, you just try to absolutely obliterate everything in your path as quickly and efficiently as possible. But, if you want a high score, you want them to suffer agonizing entire hallways and finish them off to rack up score. (since you get more points for each trap that hits them) It can become genuinely exciting trying to figure out what kind of traps you want for which purpose and abusing their strengths for maximum effectiveness. This game also is very good about upgrades. If you end up throwing your skulls into traps you discover you don't like (or just don't want on you anymore) you can refund either EVERYTHING or just an individual trap at a 100% return rate. This makes life soooo much easier especially if you're not that far into the game and want to experiment or need to repetitively optimize your layouts. I also like that the game isn't lazy about difficulty levels. Instead of just giving enemies more health, they instead give shields for them to block attacks so you approach your kill boxes a bit differently. I really love that.No game is without its flaws, though, I, for one, HATE that they only have one other type of ground unit that is completely immune to fire. Normally that's fine, but they have no other units that are immune to anything else. (except flying units, but nobody cares about them since they will die to pretty much anything anyway) I know the purpose was to make it so you don't just spam an effective element, but why did they only apply it to fire when they could have done it for every other element? There also is a surprising lack of elements anyway, since despite there being quite a few traps to choose from, your options get very limited because if you want a specific element you really only get to pick between 2 or 3 traps. I'd personally want more elements in the game or at the very least more traps. Endless mode also gets pretty annoying, because this game has multiple bosses in the game but only choose to ever throw the same one at you every single wave. As the waves go on, their health also starts to add up rather then them mixing it up with interesting enemies that might just disable traps around them or something. high hp bars just feels lazy and doesn't really feel rewarding when you make a good trap setup. (however I do know that the endless mode has to be losable somehow) Conclusively, this is a pretty good game if you're looking for a fun little strategy game. It may not have incredible amounts of replayability, but you will still get some good bang for your buck. There's 23 levels for you to play on and then weekly challenges on top of an endless mode. If you really enjoy getting high scores then this can be a good game to play since you can get some pretty satisfying combos going on. This game also has online multiplayer, but unfortunately only supports 2 players at once.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of the Orcs Must Die! series for quite some time, and I've particularly enjoyed diving into the endless mode. However, it's disappointing to say that the current state of the game has introduced some significant problems that are seriously affecting my experience.One of the most glaring issues revolves around the Unreal Engine 4 (UE4) that the game utilizes. While playing the endless mode, I've encountered repeated fatal errors stemming from the UE4. To my dismay, this issue has cropped up three times out of my seven total runs on endless. It's disheartening to witness top scores on leaderboards being achieved through exploiting these glitches, which casts a shadow over the game's competitive integrity.The problematic state of the game, coupled with its persisting bugs and glitches, compels me to share my negative feedback. Despite the passage of time and the lessons learned from the shortcomings of Orcs Must Die! Unchained, it's disheartening that an unfinished and buggy game has been released.Unfortunately, even two months after my initial encounter with the fatal crashes, no fixes have been implemented, and technical support remains unresponsive. This lack of attention from the development team paints a concerning picture.Fast forward to three months later, and the situation remains unchanged. The developers continue to overlook these issues, leaving players frustrated and unable to fully enjoy the game. The game feels as if it's stuck in a pre-alpha stage, with the prospect of more resets looming.Bugs have undoubtedly marred what could have been an enjoyable experience. It's disappointing to observe the developers' apparent lack of concern for these issues. This sentiment is further compounded by the release of new DLC that introduces even more bugs while failing to address the existing crashes.A year has passed since my initial encounters with these problems, and it's disheartening to note that not a single response has been received from the development team. Technical support seems nonexistent for the game, leaving players like me to deal with a multitude of bugs, crashes, and cheaters. Even the scoring system is riddled with inconsistencies.As we approach the two-year mark, a new patch has been introduced. However, it's disheartening to see that the major issues that have plagued the game remain unaddressed. The Orcs' AI still leaves much to be desired, and barricades continue to break unexpectedly. Archers, cannons, and ballistas still exhibit subpar AI, rendering them ineffective against hordes of enemies. Crashes persist, the lack of in-game communication is glaring, and even the basic game resolution settings are broken.Additionally, Robot Entertainment has reset the leaderboards due to trap balance adjustments. Consequently, players are now unable to register new scores, as they must achieve new high scores on all maps in order to record their latest achievements.It's baffling that ROBOT Entertainment seems incapable of rectifying the technical issues that plague the game, preventing players from enjoying it to the fullest. The journey with Orcs Must Die! 3 has been marred by the frustrating persistence of these problems, and it's a shame that the potential for a great experience remains largely untapped due to the lack of adequate fixes.

_childDocuments_.review: Certain players will enjoy Orcs Must Die 3: (1) those who are good at twitchy shooting and crowd control involving rehearsals and keeping track of enemy numbers/spawns; (2) those who like skin-of-your-teeth 5-skull victories wrenched painfully from stingy budgets and hostile map design; and (3) maybe the odd survivor of Orcs Must Die Unleashed. Anyone expecting a sane return to the charm and fun of the first two games in the franchise should watch some gameplay videos before pulling the trigger.On the plus side, most of the bestiary and quite a few of the traps/weapons/trinkets of previous games return for this third outing. Additionally, the developers include a decent amount of endgame content in the form of Rift Lord difficulty, endless and scramble maps, and challenge scenarios. The heroes have interesting unique abilities, and most of the enemies retain their well-crafted threat designs. Some of the new traps are downright clever, an example being the Window of Butterflies, which if placed strategically can distract tanky threats like armored ogres. Some players may be cheered to know that death no longer subtracts from rift points, and 5-skull endless victories can be achieved at the end of the 25th wave even if all but one enemy makes it into the rift.Appealing as all this sounds, one can't shake the feeling that Robot Entertainment is intent on driving away the audience that supported the first two titles. Like so many other developers, they appear to be caught up in the cult of difficulty that equates success with impeding and antagonizing the player. Getting 5-skull victories in War Mage difficulty is not especially challenging in and of itself, but the high cost of traps and the absurdly low coin budget require the player who was expecting a casual tower defense game to spend the first two thirds of every level playing a third-person shooter. The Rift Lord maps are difficult not because of the ramped up enemy rosters, but because there simply isn't enough money to get past the first two waves without relying excessively on weapons and trinkets.The budget issue might be tolerable if -- just occasionally -- maps didn't have multiple orc spawn points and few if any defendible choke points beyond the rift area itself. The map designs, admittedly, are very impressive, but combined with an unreasonably low budget, they require more time and trouble than the real target audience for this game wants to put in.This audience celebrated a game franchise that absorbed much of their time with ingenious ways to overcome silly fantasy enemies. Orcs Must Die 3 substitutes hostility and deprivation for ingenuity. Some parts of it have a spark of that old charm, but the player will take a beating finding those parts. Consider buying at half-price or below, but not at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a positive..ish review. I'm going to assume you have either played OMD1 or 2, or unchained.In short it's a 3d tower defence game with amusing orcs and comedy traps. It's lost a lot of the "juice" that made OMD2 such good fun. It's just the feeling I get that it's gone from a hard fought war of attrition(in OMD2)  to the player in OMD3 needing to tailor their EXACT build to clear a level and without the EXACT build there's always one wave that completely screws you. The result is, the levels can now be intensely frustrating rather than a puzzle to overcome through repeatedly trying things out. The level of frustration has been amped up by the player needing to replay or grind through on a lower difficulty to get skulls to upgrade the traps needed to complete a level. Beating something like Armoured Ogres becomes a massive annoyance as they are vulnerable to only a select few traps and you can't get those traps or upgrade them enough without going back through older levels. Forcing grind on a player is always going to make lots of people frown.I have a nasty feeling some of this is as a result of the Stadia launch. There feels less gibs and body parts flying around and there are only 18 levels - something that means to increase the longevity of the game they had to give it quite a steep difficulty curve. The levels very quickly ramp up from "ok this is quite fun" to "How the AF am I supposed to stop that lot!", with a dawning realisation that you need to grind more skulls to boost your traps - making you go back and redo levels quite a lot. Again.There is the possibility to reclaim any points spent upgrading traps whenever you like and this sounds like a really good idea to avoid the grind, but this just means you have to actually tailor your EXACT build to this EXACT level, and I find myself spending too much time in the trap screen deciding exactly what to upgrade rather than actually playing the levels. It soon become clear that even with a refund of upgrades I haven't got enough skulls I need to boost enough traps of the right type. Back to grinding levels on apprentice for Skulls I go...There's some new features that are pretty cool, like the War scenarios that have massive fortresses to defend against a monumental amount of orcs, and some of the new traps are quite good fun. The new characters a likeable and although I've only really tried the souped-up bazooka the weapons seem quite well balanced.Don't get me wrong, it's still quite good - but any game that makes you grind your teeth and shout swear words a lot should only be played in short bursts. This is one such game, so it's not a bad buy if you fancy playing it for a little while, getting through it on apprentice or war mage and never going back to it. Don't expect to be playing it over and over again like OMD2 or Unchained, as OMD3 played for any length of time will give you blood pressure problems.

Kill orcs. Win. And yeah, it's fun. I'm still going to pour time into it, and get my orcs murdering on, I'm just underwhelmed with a game that took nearly a decade to come out with. I would have expected more, or something more different.If you're here because you enjoyed flinging orcs off ledges, or mowing them down, or because trap defense games are your thing, then this is going to be a fine game. Perhaps the previous model did so well they didn't want to make large changes to ensure the success of OMD3. Whatever the case, it's still a game worth getting, but I'd point people towards OMD2 for price and entertainment value at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by saying that while I do recommend this game, it's because it uses it's previous title as a crutch.Been playing this game for the better part of today and haven't ran into a single problem, no bugs, no dropped frames, no crashing, even running all settings on Ultra the game has been buttery smooth.As far as the gameplay itself goes, it's more of the same but with improved graphics, a dozen or so new traps, and of course new levels. Basically it feels more like a fresh new expansion to OMD2 than it does a whole new game. I guess OMD:U's total earthshattering failure left them shaking in their boots so much the very thought of innovation triggers their PTSD.OMD3 is a good game, but only because OMD2 was a great game. If you loved the gameplay of OMD2 and want more, then this game is great and resuscitates a dead classic... if you're new to the series, OMD2 is probably the better purchase because it has more maps, has about the same gameplay for around the same price, and it's characters and dialog is overall better.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with OMD1&2 and picked this up on the recent sale.This is a return to form of the franchise after the disaster that was OMD Unchained. It feels a lot like OMD2 with new maps and and a few new traps and enemy types. The war scenarios are fun large scale maps with far larger numbers of orcs and bosses with special traps to compensate.Unfortunately the game balance has been changed to nerf traps and increase the importance of personally fighting orcs. Traps are weaker and more expensive than previous titles. This is moderately annoying on most maps since you won't have enough money to build a decent trap defense (especially the first couple of waves) and are required to do most of the work yourself with the traps just funneling orcs to a killzone and slowing/thinning things out. On later game (and especially DLC) maps with multiple independent routes this can be incredibly annoying to infuriating depending on the map since you'll be frantically running back and forth all the time, and makes some of the maps nearly impossible to complete solo.I really miss the balance in OMD1 where you could go all-in on traps or personal abilities depending on how you wanted to play, and since it didn't have co-op the maps were much better designed for solo play unlike many of the maps in OMD2&3.The big saving grace of this game is mod support. They'll disable leaderboards (fine with me, I don't care) but allow for fixes to the not great game balance so it can be played much more trap heavy as a tower defense should be.Either way it's still plenty of fun with a great art style and comedy and I can easily recommend the franchise. I'm still baffled at the extremely poor design of many of these fortresses though with multiple routes for orcs to come through, if these were built with the intent of being a gateway fortress then they should have been built very differently.

_childDocuments_.review: Truth be told unchained was a better game in pretty much every way but it’s gone now and this is still fun and if you’re just looking for a relaxing single player experience with a meh story then it delivers. The gameplay is of cource excellent as in all Orcs must die games but it’s more a rework of game 2 than a new game and to not confuse players that never played OMD before unchained is basically the real OMD3 and this is OMD4 and a lot of the features of the real OMD3 disappeared in this one. The game has issues but most of these things can be fixed and improved through updates and I really hope they consider the feedback they’re getting. The multiplayer is by far the worst out of all the games (with the exception for 1 where there was none). No chat, no voice chat and voice commands with no indicators like in unchained so impossible to actually know what people want.The level designs seems to just have been thrown together without thinking about giving the player the freedom of controlling the flow of the battlefield, reducing the strategic element in the game. Barricades are also very strong even without upgrades so once placed you rarely have to protect them against zappers. Also the doubletile upgrade gives a very poor discount so you’re better off not using it.This is what I hope that they’ll change in future updates;-	Give us a proper chat and give voice commands indicators like in unchained so they’re actually useful.-	Fix the multiplayer lobby and make it one single list for all available game modes.-	Let us play chaos trials (or survival mode as it’s called in OMD3) with strangers online.-	Make money gradually decrease slower in endless and instead gradually increase the difficulty by spawning more and stronger enemies. As soon as we can’t build anymore it’s just not much fun especially since the characters in OMD3 are kind of weak and boring compared to unchained.-	Add new traps that gives us more strategic freedom. For example since the level design is already in there give us bridges so we can create our own routes for enemies. Maybe zappers will still attack them like barricades just to make it a little more difficult? And give us coin generators where we can sacrifice trap space and early income for stronger late game economy (also in unchained).-	Give us more customizable traps, bring back the part slots like in unchained where we sacrifice one stat to improve another. For example increased damage but decreases speed or increases speed but also increases cost etc. We also need to be able to see the stats of the traps so we can actually make an educated decision on what to bring and why. In unchained there was also a preview on how to use the different traps for beginners.-	We should be able to place Guardians on other maps than warzones. It’s just a distraction piece not an invincible wall of death and it should stay that way. It had strategic value now it’s just an overpriced floor trap.-	Add warzone maps to endless and survival mode, like it’s the only new cool feature in the game yet it’s not in “survival mode” or “endless”. That’s so dumb!Despite all these issues It’s still a good game and worth picking up and supporting! Hope to see lots of updates and dlc’s in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: War scenarios don't quite add enough to make this game feel disparate enough from its predecessors for me to consider it truly special. The game hasn't evolved much since the first iteration.That being said, who cares? Orcs Must Die! is such a singular gameplay experience that it kinda doesn't matter that it hasn't evolved much. I'm not sure, if I gave it thought, that there are many areas for improvement or evolution. Sure, there's quality of life stuff that can be fixed. More keybinding options, for example. There are issues with map structure where enemies will destroy your barricades if you have them set a bit weird. I guess what I'm saying is that this might just be it for OMD. I can't imagine this series accomplishing much with additional iterations.It's still so damned fun, and it seemed to hit Steam at just the right time.If I had suggestions for the sequel, it would be to limit the players more. Get more creative with the characters and restrict trap selection enough, so that you have to get creative with each character's loadout. It sounds like a step backward, but I feel like this could open the door for individual skill trees for each of the characters, where you find new traps/weapons/etc that are restricted to those characters. Ultimately, you would be forced to take advantage of each of their strengths and compensate for their weaknesses. Just a suggestion. At the moment, all the characters feel the same for the most part, and I feel like that the characters should be the focus. The gameplay forces restrictions on the maps, with everything being 4x4 squares and orc behavior being relatively simple. I don't know.What I do know is that I'm happy we have more OMD, but this should probably be the last hurrah for this rigid gameplay structure. It's time for a change. Definitely recommended, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for this game, but despite the high level of polish the core mechanics of OMD3 are a letdown. There might be dozens of traps to choose from, but none of them have the impact to create an exciting and dynamic experience going from level to level. Individual traps don't do enough damage to be of much notice, but are too expensive to create elaborate gauntlets to grind through the waves of enemies. If traps were more potent then the game could be a placement puzzle, creating chokepoints and killrooms that rely on synergy to maximize their potential. If traps were more plentiful, then it could be a game about creativity and experimentation, letting you place dozens of traps all across the level. In the end, OMD3 inhabits the awkward middle-ground, where you have a few patches of traps which wittle away at the horde, leaving you to spend most of the mission grinding through the majority of enemies yourself.If you plan to get this with a friend, the co-op might be enough to save it for you, otherwise look for a mod that lets you place twice as many traps as the developers are willing to give you.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid tower defense game, easily the best entry in the franchise. Robot Entertainment just flatly knows how to make one of these games fun, well-balanced, and just difficult enough for the "just one more map..." mentality that makes this genre so satisfyingly addictive.The art direction is fantastic (war mage animations being a little too "bouncy" is my only complaint). The DLC was also short for what they were given at full-price, albeit the art and full redesigns of enemies and added animations definitely do earn the sticker price, I don't think most gamers will see how few maps were offered as a fair trade. I personally disagree with this, but I also got the entirety of OMD! 3 on sale, so if you're one of those people who disregard all the hard work that goes into the full experience and only care about more content for the sake of content, then I would also wait for a sale. $4 for the two DLC's was a dang steal.All of the mobs have wonderful personalities and reactions to traps. I found myself spamming haymakers just because I loved how the orcs would say 'wheee!' or throw in random dialogue. Charm of the series is on full display, basically, and if you've never played an OMD! game, then this is a great one to pick up for co-op or solo play. If you're a weaker player (e.g. not as skilled or have trouble with shooters for whatever reason) than some parts of solo play might be frustrating - there are some genuine skill requirements to some of the maps if you want a good score.I just really like it. Tower defense perfected.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure, I spent 2 years working on Orcs Must Die Unchained at Robot Entertainment as a Quality Assurance Lead. I played that game A LOT in that 2 years, and while I think that by the end of the projects existence it was a solidly fun game, I also KNOW that it failed to meet the expectations of players (myself included) when compared to OMD 1&2.With that said, and with me no longer working at the company, I ABSOLUTELY LOVE EVERYTHING THEY'VE DONE WITH OMD3!Kudos to all the devs that worked their asses off to make this game and really hone in on what made OMD 1&2 so successful. They took the lessons learned from OMDU and refused to repeat the same mistakes here and have delivered a thrilling, challenging, and supremely silly dungeon building experience. They didn't even play it safe either! They took great technological leaps to create the immense War Scenario missions with literal HUNDREDS of Orcs and other Rift creatures on the map at one time.TL;DR:- OMDU under-delivered on player expectations- OMD3 succeeds where OMDU failed- It's everything you loved about OMD 1&2 but SUPERSIZED!- Buy the game, support the devs, this was a labor of love for them <3

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to not recommend this game, despite enjoying having played it. So why wouldn't I recommend it? Because you should buy and play 'Orcs Must Die! 2' instead.As a semi-veteran player, Orcs Must Die! 3 just presents countless missed opportunities and disappointments in terms of what a worthy successor *could* have been. At best, the new additions are forgetful, at worst they're annoying.As a new player you won't mind any of these disappointments, but you might as well buy the older game at half the price yielding pretty much the same experience, with a slightly more dated look.Looking at the history of 'Robot Entertainment' their previous game 'Orcs Must Die! Unchained' represents a pretty serious bomb in the series and thus they must have needed a sure 'hit'. Unfortunately, the result is a game that feels nearly like a carbon copy of Orcs Must Die! 2, in a newer engine where every slight innovation is entirely forgettable.And I almost forgot - the game sports so many odd Ui choices, and usability issues that on their own are tolerable, but together drag the experience down a bit. Not the end of the world, just unfortunate.Thus, as much as it pains me, I would simply not recommend buying this game. Buy Orcs Must Die! 2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a gift, so my review really doesn't matter to Steam. But I have to get this out there. I love OMD3, but its anti-piracy measures are awful for the future of the game. While you can technically play the game offline, you're gonna have a bad time. While playing offline, you don't get your money back for selling traps, and you can't unlock the unique upgrades for your traps. I like to play OMD on my Steam Deck, but I'm often at a place with no WiFi connection. I have to turn on the hotspot on my phone with its limited data and pray that my connection stays stable. If the connection has a single hiccup, then I won't find out until halfway through the run when I sell a trap that the entire run was a waste and I have to restart the game. And what about in the future when their servers are inevitably going to be taken offline? There's already very few people playing this game, so it's only a matter of time. This game has been out for 3 years, and they're making a new game in the series - the DRM has to be disabled.I'm not going to say you should pirate this game. I would never say that. But I will say that if you're only interested in playing this game singleplayer, people figured out how to take out the DRM a long time ago. Please, Robot Entertainment, take it out for the people who have honestly paid for and supported this game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you asked me if I recommended this game 2 weeks ago, I would have said yes. But at the moment, no. They just released an update that nerfed one of the best traps in the game in a way that makes it useless. I get reducing the effectiveness of a trap, but reducing the damage AND enemy detection to even do damage? The hell is that. Half the time enemies run right past it now without taking a single hit of damage because it doesn't hit them. Beyond that so many traps should have been buffed but weren't. Endless mode should have been changed to give more cash, but it wasn't.The last patch also quite literally broke the game. There are elite enemies in this game, similar to the previous titles, these are large enemies such as Ogres and Trolls, their variants, etc. The last patch broke their pathing so that even with an open path to your Rift (defense objective) they will stop, destroy your barricade and then walk straight into the rift. The game is built around good use of barricades, as the previous two titles have been. The recent nerfs to the Ceiling Laser traps (first paragraph) has also made 5-skulling several maps essentially impossible, even with a second player. Why? Flyers now run rampant and you have to dedicate your time to them 100% of the time, but can't because the cost of traps means you can't setup an effective killbox like you could in previous Orcs Must Die games. The cost of traps at this point need to be cut in half since most of them are complete ♥♥♥♥ and the ones that aren't are nerfed without buffing traps to shore up the weakness that was just opened.TLDR: Don't buy this until Robot Entertainment fixes the game breaking pathing bug with elites, and balances traps in a positive manner.

The battle is massively large with hundreds of orcs and monsters. So cool!- The graphics are impressive. I really love the spell effect, especially the fire (cause it burnssss a lots of orcs). - The soundtracks are still epic.- Lots of fun and upgrades.- Smooth gameplay.Things I don't love:- Co-op in the main campaign is kinda easier than the 2nd version. _childDocuments_.review: I know what you are thinking, the game has been out 8 hours and this guy has 8 hours played, but hear me out.Do you like tower defence? Do you like a fun sense of humour? Do you like solo / coop games? Then this game ticks all of those boxes! If you are looking for a AAA PVP or more than 2 player coop then unfortunately this game does have what your looking for.I have played this on both Stadia and Steam (It was out on Stadia first) and the performance on steam is a substantial improvement. Personally have had no issues in game play and have finished my first run of campaign. The game has tonnes of replay-ability and so many different ways to play, i love playing with different friends because you can see how different people tackle different situations.---If you have played Orcs Must Die 1 or 2 ---The Game is what you would expect, its just the same (more or less) as orcs 2 but with more traps, as well as a really awesome new type of map which you fight substantially more orcs but have access to siege equipment and larger traps, very very fun and a nice natural evolution of the franchise rather than a complete overhaul like unchained was. If you enjoyed 1 or 2 your sure to enjoy this!---If you have not played the orcs must die franchise before---Orcs must die is where you have 1 or 2(in coop) players that have to defend your rift from waves of orcs trying to assault you, there are 3 difficulty modes, easy is very easy, Warmage (medium) feels quite naturally the difficulty its meant to be and rift lord (hard) is where you would go to use what you have learned after a while of playing.You can play as a one man (or woman) wrecking machine and have numerous weapons and trinkets and go around killing the orcs solo, you can set up intricate mazes of traps or you can mix and match and find how you prefer playing somewhere in the middle. The franchise has a great sense of humour, if your on the fence about getting this, my recommendations would be to buy 1 or 2, they are very very cheap and this game is basically a natural evolution of them so if you enjoy them you'll enjoy this. The game has some day 1 bugs but already the devs are throwing out hot fixes so please don't negative for no reason, the devs care about the game and the community and will get it all nice and polished just give them a minute.

_childDocuments_.review: OMD has been around since the Xbox "Summer of Arcade" days, i remember as a kid getting hyped for games like Battlefield 1943, Toy Soldiers, and OMD. Didn't play OMD 2 and haven't played OMD 1 since i was like 12, but OMD 3 proves that such a simple idea and have fantastic results even 10 years later. The core gameplay loop is a simple tower defense with the added 3rd person shooter, allowing you to stand next to your traps and fight along side them. This isn't like Bloons where one tower reigns supreme and you spam that everywhere, you need to be creative with route blocking barricades, wall ceiling and floor traps, and what traps you upgrade. Synergy is key, place a flipper trap near a pit for instant kills, or a slowing trap near a spike wall to maximize its damage. It all works and experimenting with different traps and routes is alot of fun.My only complaints are minor, like seeing overall damage/kills on placed traps to see how they are doing. Couple of annoying bugs have made me rethink strategies, like enemies walking through a barricade or sawblades flying through walls. These issues only happened a few times in my playthrough in the main campaign, it sucks but its not game breaking. OMD 3 is great if you like the TD genre, its an OG thats still kicking with the best and 100% a buy at $30 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr varsion:Compared to OMD!2, this game is as twice as expensive (I've pre-ordered both OMD!2 and OMD!3), has less content and is full of bugs. I'm not familiar with Stadia version, maybe all issues are inherited from it, maybe it's unpolished Steam port, can't tell. Surely the budget was very limited, there's quite a bit of rounding the corners and most likely beta test were cut short.Now, time to elaborate a bit :).Gameplay is pretty much like in previous games. There are changes, like now every enemy costs 1 rift point (no more armoured ogres costing 10), there's no penalty for death (though it feels like it's easier to die, probably because of these pesky ranged mobs) and (the controversial one) almost all ranged weapons can register headshots (including blunderbuss). It makes game easier compared to previous two (it seems like trend since OMD!2 was easier than OMD!). Not really a deal breaker, there's still Nightmare mode around. I've noticed that enemies no longer speed up when close to the rift after patches, it seems like someone thought it wasn't good change (or it was just a bug). There are some strange changes in equipement. For example, Lightning Ring (which is now trinket, not a weapon) abilites are now split into two items - ring is used to summon thunderstorm while chain lightning is Chain Lightning Staff's ability. Some traps are altered - for example Grinder no longer recharges while idle but not completely drained - which sometimes makes these less useful. Some items, like Coinforge :(, Vampiric Gauntlets or Polymorph Ring (whyyyy...), are gone. Unfortunately few useless ones still are here (Ceiling Pounder). Interface is much "lighter" than in previous games, which is good, but at the same time it doesn't provide "health bars" for almost all traps (except Grinder and Barricade) that indicate recharge time or charges left in case of traps. Furthermore, it doesn't accentuate differences between player characters by different mana/health bars' lengths (which have different mana and health pools, from tanky Vorwick to squishy Cygnus). Just like items, some enemies gone gone too. There are no more Fire/Frost Ogres, Swamp Trolls, fliers are all shifted to DLC campaign levels. There's whole "orc-reskin" class of enemies which are all immune to fire - this outhright makes all fire related upgrades, traps and weapons obsolete because these new enemies come in hordes, just like orcs.New "big thing", War Scenarios, are, um... Aside from bosess (which are pain in the rear in some cases, not all though, for example the one in Dragon Boneyard can be left to be mowed down by killbox which player has set up by the final wave which is boss wave), there's not much. These maps are larger, there's lots of enemies but that's all. Beacuse of huge amount of starting cash and huge number of enemies, it's easy to set up efficient killbox using regular traps and ignore expensive war scenario traps completely. The fact it's easy to set up kill box early means that getting par time on these levels is extremely easy, unlike regular scenarios, where par time is quite strict. It's noticeable on levels like Sludge Shelves or The Basement, on these maps being in right spot in the right time is essential. It's not often though, most maps allow funneling enemies into single area (having single rift on every map helps a lot too, this is shame actually because previous game had lots of maps with multiple rifts) where it's easy to build efficient "death zone" for orcs and their allies.Visually the game is ok, I guess. The OMD!/OMD!2 style is preserved while all bells and whistles are (more or less) upgraded to nowadays standards. Sometimes these get in the way - having lots of lasers, traps spilling ice, acid and whatnot, player tossing frost bolts - it all obstructs the view to the point where sometimes it's actually hard to see enemies. The cinematics are no longer hand drawn stills, these are kind of fmvs now. It's ok, though video after last level is... underwhelming - not entertaining and quite basic. The Drastic Steps videos seem to be much better, at least these bring that not too serious approach from previous games. Which is not present in main campaign, unfortunately. The story is pompous, lacks that lighthearted approach. It starts with "the earthquake" (which is fine), rolls out some retrospection levels and then it loses all tempo and becomes dull. All the hilarious bickering between characters from previous games are gone, instead there are two uninteresting wiseass teenagers and one "mother figure". Drastic Steps fixes this by bringing back that chemistry between Gabs and Max, but that's just short 5-level campaign. There are too few nonsense oneliners thrown around by player's character, even in case of Max. Personallly, I don't enjoy ost as much as in previous games. It's a bit in the background now, less noticeable (lacks that "something" which made me to listen to ost outside of the game in case of OMD!2)."Unfortunately", I've left the worse for the end. There are some weird design choices. For example option to reset scramble mode is placed not on the scramble mode screen but in the game options. Speaking of scramble mode, buffs and debuffs are grossly unbalanced - there are crippling ones (boss spawning at each wave, doubled cost of all floor, wall or ceiling traps), almost meaningless ones (barricade cost incerased by 50%) and overpowered ones (item dropped after every kill by headshot). The ESC key doesn't work in some areas in menus. The spellbook looks plain and unfinished - at least upgrade "cards" could use some artworks. Texts in these rectangles often align weirdly or stick out of text area, not too mention font scaling which sometimes makes upgrade descriptions barely readable. The ragdoll is grotesque - severed limbs fly like helium filled balloons. Some enemies are still "colour-coded" while others blur into shapeless blob (which makes threat assessing a bit difficult). And the worse - the bugs. These range from nuisances - like occasionally wrong images on loading screen or low res images in spellbook (or broken translation, broken score display in particular non-English versions) through hilarious ones (like ceiling/floor trap which can be placed partially inside the wall or enemies just standing and doing nothing unless player gets close to trigger their aggro) to game breaking ones. These are really painful. Sometimes enemies clip through barricades or smash these for no reason (it's easily replicable on Colosseum where Gnoll Hunters, which should ignore barricades, aggresively attack these if these are placed in particulas spots). Sometimes (it seems to affect enemies which have been frozen multiple times) player's weapons stop dealing damage - I've even encounererd few orcs that were literally invulnerable - nothing could harm them. Quite often game stops to respond to keyboard commands for few seconds. On some maps crowd control items that affect enemy pathfinding don't work at all - on these levels charmed enemies still walk (end enter) towards rifts and run through Jar of Ghosts active effect. I haven't play multiplayer yet - people say it's broken in many ways, which (if it's true) is step backwards when compared to OMD!2.To sum it up, OMD!3, even after 4 major patches, is still far away from pretty much bugless OmD!2 (at the release day), it's downgrade in terms of contents and biggest novelty is just a knick-knack. Scramble mode is much better at bringing fresh air into franchise, but, as I mentioned before, it needs some serious tweaking. If you really want to experience OMD! style gameplay and you've never played any game from the series, go grab OMD!2 (and maybe OMD!, at least to unlock Classic levels in OMD!2), it's much cheaper (even full package), bugless and has much more contents. If you're fan of the series, I recommend waiting until RE fixes at least the worst bugs. Or maybe just wait for OMD!4.

_childDocuments_.review: Is OMD3 a bad Game?No, I can't go that far. but it is the 3rth or rather 4rth installment to ROBOT's most popular franchise. And at that point getting an incredibly mixed bag as a whole package feels very unprofessional. This game could- and should-have been so much more!Mechanics:Despite some minor glitches in co-op OMD3 feels very stable and play's very clean compared to OMD2 which alway's felt a bit wonkey on some area's. maybe its even on par with OMD1 in terms of polish. aside from a minimalistic and uninspired visuals for your lifebar and magic meter playing the characters feels solid and satisfying. visual effects, sounds and weapon impact feel great overal. I do find the swords a bit on the light side in terms of impact but 9/10 times you'll be using a ranged weapon anyway as they are safer to use.Trap Library:The trap library has some things to be desired though. As they failed to include the price of each trap in the library  and you can't change a traps secondary ability when you are already in a level before the waves start. this is incredibly annoying cause if for example you have creature with fire immunity and you wish the change a traps elemental ability to avoid that you have to exit the level and restart, which is just dumb.Also i'm missing SO MANY traps compared to OMD2 and none from Unchained where included either.Acid Spray, Boulder Chute, Coin Forge, Dwarf Guardian, Healing Well, Ice Vent, Void Wall, Floor Portal, Web Spinner, Steam Trap, Spore Mushrooms, Arcane Phaser, Cursed Ground, Fire Cracker, Ice Shard, Icicle Impaler, Overload Trap, Spitfire Wall etc. What also seems to be a returning issue is overbalancing, especially in a singleplayer game I find it incredibly dumb to nerf traps. just make the enemy's harder instead! Swinging Mace is a pale imitation of the slaughtering beast it used to be.And guardian archers have such a slow startup fire-rate in this game they are completely unusable. especially since this game has been out for nearly 2 years as a stadia exclusive these balancing issues shouldhave been worked out long ago. there is no excuse for it!Characters:OMD1, OMD2 and Unchained had great characters which we loved because of their over the top snarky cartoonish personality's and flaws. Maximillian, Gabriella and Signus have been around since the first game and are the heart of OMD. they are the star attractions we come for. we Love Max because he's the idiot that gets the job done. we Love Gabs because she's a snobby diva orc slaughtering sadist. mixed with the reluctant Signus who has to deal with their shenanigans it's a great cake of comedy. and Unchained added a great cast of additional characters which enriched the OMD world.In contrast the new Main Characters just feel like forced tokens in every regard. they are both inspirationless Mary Sue's which where clearly pushed onto the project for whatever diversity agenda Stadia thought was more important then writing actual characters. it doesn't hurt the games experience they are harmless additions but they don't add anything either. When this could have been such a great possibility to re-introduce some chars from Unchained as that game is now lost forever. and you can especially feel this with the other two additional characters of OMD3. Young Signus and Vorwick. which do have that classic OMD charm.What I do appreciate is that every character can now handle every weapon unlike OMD2 where your main weapons was classbound. now only your jump ability differs and this is enough to create of unique play style in my opinion.The Stages:The storymode has good leveldesign in overal. I have nothing to complain about and enjoyed all but 2 or 3 levels in total.stages are usually open and diverse enough to create a setup to your personal liking.Scramble mode has to be one of the best additions to OMD period. it adds a great variety to the multiplayer and replayability factor of the game.Endless has been greatly reworked to be more challenging and less monotonous and is a great step-up from OMD2 instead of stagnating at a capped difficulty which you could endlessly milk. OMD3 makes enemy's tougher and faster in small increments which means you will fail in a more realistic fashion.Still no Level creator. THIS HAS THE BE THE BIGGEST CRIME ROBOT HAS EVER COMMITTED.This game is DRIVEN by it's need for diverse levels and ever since OMD1 came out people have been asking for a level creator . which would breathe ENDLESS life into this game. it is truly boggling. I would pay full price of this feature if they had it. JUST DO IT ALREADY!Strategy Meta:A game like this SHOULD NOT EVER have a meta. yet there are still levels which are clearly designed to only work with a single strategy in mind. and this is a combined fault of Traps, Coin and level layout. The barricade trap is practically mandatory in nearly every stage. as OMD3 is very stingy with gaining cash through kill combo's. this leads to every map being steered into funneling orcs through a single small passage with all traps in one big killbox and all other roads locked off. and ofcourse we have many traps that are balanced very strangely causing many of the trap library to be completely unusable.Fire damage? never wanna use it cause half of the levels have fire immune enemy's.which means you'll never use Brimstone with Fire, Fire arrow walls or Floor Scorchers.Decoy? un-usuable! never regenerates after it gets destroyed unlike it's OMD2 counterpart. complete waste of cash.Swinging Mace? nope. doesn't do nearly enough damages for its price and 3x1 space.Elven Archers? incredibly slow startup time they nerfed them so much you'll never use them.DLC'sThe DLC's for OMD3 feel incredibly small and lackluster. I wish they'd sit down and make a proper expantion pack a full story with I dunno 10 new stages, 8 new traps 5 new weapons. and not these lackluster mini-DLC's.Drastic Steps as a prequel is what I would consider the bare minimum to a DLC and I wont complain about it much since they did add it for free on the steam version. but it's not impressive on its own.I was stoked for Cold as Eyes and now I realized everything I saw in the trailer was all there was. for 6,- yes it's not a big deal. but it isn't worth much more then that either.And one final gripe is that the partime for the stages is EXTREMELY tight and allows very little room for creativity. also Frostbitten it the WORST map ever designed for any OMD game. come on ROBOT, I love OMD, but get your ♥♥♥♥ together!Edit:Ever since the Last Balance Patch the game has been significantly improved. while many of my overall critique points still stand. The games gameplay is much better for it. and has earned the game an upvote from this point.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this is definitely a recommend BUT.....If you love the other OMD games you should like this as well.  However there's some technical issues that take away from the game  play in my opinion.There are huge issues with accuracy aiming that I never experienced with OMD1 and OMD2.  You can have the crosshairs dead on an enemy, and miss, even or especially at point blank range.  This is so frustrating and the number of rounds I've lost because of 3-4 enemies getting through that 'should not' have gotten through is frustrating.  Even more frustrating is using the alternate attack on your weapon and missing, this really hurts as you often only have 3-4 shots with the alternate even from a full charge.Another frustrating thing is the traps actually deflect your shots with your weapons and block you sometimes.  There are a lot of trips that pop out of the ceiling and walls and these will actually block enemies behind them.  This is a 'feature' I don't recall having an issue with in OMD1 or 2.  Seriously guys if we wanted realistic physics would we be playing OMD?Finally not really an issue, just a comment.  It's faster.  Much faster.  The kobolds are much faster than previous games, the flames that spawn when you kill a fire elemental, forget trying to kill them if you destroy the elemental remotely close to your rift it won't happen.  These mini flames are now as fast if not faster than the kobolds.So in short I would say it's more dificult and more challenging than OMD1 and 2 which is what you'd expect.  I found it harder to earn skulls to get all the weapons and upgrades.  There's more masters, some new traps to try out.  One final criticism would be that it seems to have lost the humour of the original 2 games, the dialogue just isn't really as good in my opinion.So the good?  Great levels, some interesting new modes to play, scramble, graphics are a step up but keep the feel of OMD so there is a lot to like.  The biggest issue for me and the reason I stop playing from time to time is the accuracy where you have the aiming cursor directly on an enemy and miss.  You feel like you lose not because you're not good enough but because the game is broken in this area..Solid 7/10 those that like the franchise will look past the technical issues and love it anyway.  Those that don't wont.

_childDocuments_.review: (OMD3) is a third-person shooter / tower-defense hybrid with a fantasy setting. After the events of OMD2, the now-retired guardians Max and Gabriella gave their position to two young apprentices, that will have to do their best in repelling a new Orcish offensive led by a legendary figure of the Order, now corrupted by dark powers.Instead of making massive innovations, OMD3 chooses to deliver more (and better), of what was already seen in its previous chapters - which is exactly what most fans of the franchise wanted. "Don't fix what isn't broken", they say. The orc-killing mayhem has never been greater in variety, enemy numbers and scope - now with even better fine-tuning and more than a few new additions.Along with the well-known series classics, new traps and weapons have been added, while some have been reworked significantly. It's very compelling to progressively unlock, upgrade and test many new traps and trinkets, to elaborate a play-style that suits each player best. There are countless loadout possibilities and combinations to be tried on the field as levels progress."Rift Lord" (Hard) difficulty, unlocked after a certain point in the "War Mage" (Normal) campaign, is no joke. With only a few seconds pause between waves, huge quantities of high-tier enemies and more dangerous foes, this is the ultimate challenge for any Rift Guardian. Achieving 5 Skulls, the highest rating, in each map on this difficulty, will really test any player's strategy.The beloved Endless mode is yet again present in OMD3, along with the new Scramble mode, a set of five maps with progressive random buffs and debuffs, along with Weekly Challenges with dedicated leaderboards. Even after finishing the two main campaigns, these modes offer more enjoyable content.To get 5 Skulls (the highest rating) in each level, stages must be completed within a given time. Despite succeeding myself at doing so, I still think this is a bad concept, as it goes fundamentally against what Tower Defense games are about: strategy. Forcing players to rush and use sub-optimal strategies for the sake of time limits, is not something that goes well with this genre's concept. Furthermore, there isn't early wave calling in any shape or form, when there should be.At the end of the day about half of all traps, weapons and trinkets are gimmicky, useless or have better alternatives found in others of the same kind. After extensive testing of pretty much everything, I sadly realized 50% of them is just not worth using, especially on Rift Lord difficulty, where such flaws or balance issues are emphasized.War Scenarios will each feature a unique boss with special powers, such as disabling traps or changing its resistances, to name some. Not that it matters much, as these bosses don't prove challenging or really threatening at all, not even on the highest difficulty. They will usually get caught up in the trap arrays and die like normal mobs, plus they can be stunned, frozen and debilitated by most statuses, which makes killing them quite simple.Happens at the start of each map, where players have unlimited time to analyze the level layout, choose traps and trinkets (ten maximum) from their grimoires, and place as many as possible with the money at hand. Holographic projections show the path enemies will take, and are updated in real-time if players choose to block one with barricades. On War Mage difficulty, such "unlimited" break happens every few waves, while on Rift Lord only a few seconds to sell traps are allowed between every horde (which is quite annoying). Traps can be sold for their full cost in-between waves, but built at any time. In "War Scenario" maps, basically normal stages on steroids, unique traps not normally usable also become available, but for a very high cost, in line with their tremendous power.Starts during each Orc wave, with characters playing a role as important as traps, in contributing to the overall defense effort. Especially on the highest difficulty, only a synergy between player actions and well-placed traps will result in a 5 Skull victory (or victory at all). Death has no penalty except losing some time and respawning back at the Rift. Some defenses like Archers and other living ones can also "die", and need to be sold / replaced. All weapons and trinkets have a secondary firing mode which costs Mana, and often result in powerful effects that can decimate enemies. Accuracy is rewarded, with headshots dealing devastating damage to most foes, also using the elemental effects smartly is recommended (for instance,petrifying a flying enemy will result in an instant kill). Most traps have cooldown times between activations: not all the work can be done solely by traps.Is performed between levels, at the main menu. Skulls earned from victories can be spent to upgrade, unlock and enhance traps or weapons, each of them having two unique modifiers that can only be unlocked by beating a specific challenge with that piece of equipment. Each trap and weapon can be refunded at any time to invest in other traps that may be better for the next level at hand, this allows great flexibility in strategic options. Is a special mode that pits players against five randomly selected levels, each carrying a buff and debuff that progressively stack together, like increased enemy health or more strong enemies, but also reduce traps cost, give more mana for players and so on. There is a good variety of effects, and it is definitely fun to try and beat all five stages of Scramble with these unique modifiers coming into play.Is a classic of the OMD series, that allows playing any map (except War Scenarios, sadly) against infinite enemy hordes that progressively get more powerful, while at the same time monetary gains become lower and lower. There's always a breaking point, all that is left is finding it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a game built around well placed traps and clever tricks to lead AI's to their doom, this is a 3rd person shooter where you place traps to funnel enemies into your crosshair as you spam M1.  Maybe I just don't know how to do it right, but when the spike trap does 30 damage (3/5 of the health of the weakest orc in the entire game) every 15 seconds, and your starter blunderbuss dishes out almost 100 dps and has an underbarrel grenade launcher that can fire 7 times in a row with no cooldown, you quickly realize that your better off just upgrading your gun and making a wall of barricades with only one way through and then filling that space with tar traps to slow them down and keep them in the murder tube and turning on an autoclicker.  Even on the "war scenario" I found that the only way to survive was to build a giant back and forth queue out of barricades and then spam the middle with the giant catapult.This game can definitely be fun, but if you came here looking for the same things I did, your better off elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried Orcs Must Die! 2 a fairly long time ago, and it didn't resonate much with me. When a friend offered me the third installment, I have to admit I was a bit skeptical.The concept of these games is fairly trivial. You deploy various contraptions to damage or stall waves of enemies who are trying to reach a magical rift. There's a counter that ticks down for each enemy entering the rift. The more efficient you are at killing the enemies, the better your score and amount of unlock points is. There's a campaign mode with two levels of difficulty, an endless mode and a "scramble" mode where various buffs and de-buffs are dealt over 5 stages. You can play alone, or with one other player. Oh yeah, there are also these weekly challenges which are normal stages but with predetermined characters and load-outs.There's plenty of stuff to unlock. Contraptions and weapons seem to overall be better designed than in the previous game, but familiar enough. Campaign mode has been beefed up a bit with the occasional large scale siege stages with some special contraptions in addition to the normal ones. There are also more characters to play, and these sieges forces you to try them out. There's plenty of achievements to get too.I found myself enjoying this much more than I expected. All in all, it's a decent experience, and I think it's much better than the previous game. There are a few annoyances, but all in all, I approve.

_childDocuments_.review: Truth be told this will be my first ever added comment to a game on Steam or ever. I am a huge fan of Tower Defense type games. I got addicted to it when I started playing TD in Warcraft 3 where I used to create some myself.Encouraged by a friend of mine, we recently started our adventure with Orc Must Die 3. I'm incredibly positively surprised at how addictive this game is. A large variety of turrets and boards awaits us, which are incredibly interestingly prepared. In addition, you can buy weapons, which can be upgraded and each of them has its original power. Turrets can be upgraded too.The game doesn't have any bugs (I didn't come across any) which is a huge plus, because nowadays the finished product isn't finished, only the developers wait for bugs to be reported.The campaign is interesting, fun, yet simple and short, even on the hardest level. I'm the kind of person who always looks for the hardest level in games. The harder the better. After finishing the campaign, there are several modes waiting for us, of which Endless is the most interesting for me. Why? Because it's the longest and the enemies are getting stronger with each level.In other modes, such as scramble, where we choose buffs for the enemy and debuffs for ourselves, it would be nice to see the possibility of choosing the level of difficulty.  For example, level easy means 5 waves, level medium 10, etc.Mod Challenge has amazing potential, but I think it's just a quick points game. I personally haven't reached the level to be able to challenge people at the very top, because I don't really know how to skillfully collect points in this game either, but definitely mod Challenge has a lot of potential. We have imposed on what kind of turrets we can build, and if it was combined with Endless mode it would be something great. Alternatively instead of combined with Endless mode it could be for example like before difficulty levels. Easy 5 waves, medium 10 waves, etc.In the end it would be a big plus to expand the stats in terms of damage to a specific turret. Unfortunately at the moment we can only see how much damage our character did, and how much damage all turrets did.The game has definitely been a lot of fun and I will continue to try my best turret setup. I'm really hoping that with time new things will come, new ideas will come and the game won't stop with just what it has released.Endless mode for the win. (ADD WAR SCENARIO ENDLESS)

_childDocuments_.review: OMD3 is not a bad game, but it does not compare to OCD2 and that is a shame.First off depending on your GPU ( running a RTX3080 ) there's a good chance it will max it out despite just running in 60fps despite the primitive cartoony graphics ( your electrical company will love you ) - so I hope you like to listen to your fans run at max for hours..Second and more importantly the maps are not trap-based - you constantly have mutlple enemy spawn locations close to your rift with very few options to make the killboxes that the first 2 games were all about - WHY?Thirdly you don't get enough money to build up your trapzones - when playing endless don't even expect more than 3seconds between waves so good luck selling and building before under attack again - and when enemy arches keep blowing up your blocks that is where your money will go in an endless cicle of frustration..No workshop support either btw :(So I'm finding myself stuck using archers in drowes because you simply do not have resources enough to make good trap-setups and all the time playing ( the campiagn is short and endless is limited ) I wish I was playing OMD2..Honestly just play OMD2 it's a better game in all ways!

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth it, If a trap based defense game is what you are looking for then go get the Second one. The base game is split into two campaignsThe first campaign has 18 levelsThe second campaign has 5.......The DLC adds 3 more...I really wanted to like this game but it just doesn't feel good, at really any point.The Characters are bland with little development other than the smart girl and the magic guy who doesn't know how magic works. For the first 18 levels you are forced to use the characters respective weapons, the guy gets the bow and girl gets a shotgun. Which seems foolish considering there are other weapons to pick but to use them you have to use an additional slot. Not that it really matters since most of the traps aren't worth it, most do little except kill the smallest orcs. The kobolds run past nearly every trap, and all the big enemies don't take any damage. That turns into the biggest issue I had with the game, it was almost nothing but big guys. The ogres, trolls, elementals all present a good threat and require your attention when they show up but thats just it, they are constant. The game starts each wave with a good number of smaller guys that set off the traps and then just throw dozens of big guys who require multiple headshots to kill, dozens if its the mountain troll or the Armored Ogre. So I just ended up bringing three traps and using several trinkets since it seems to be more of a FPS now. Which is really annoying since the headshots don't feel as good as the first two games, they feel finicky I would get them on one enemy then another would walk up and nothing. I am willing to accept I am not the best shot but it really felt like more of a hit box issue. Not to mention times when I was playing with a friend and he was hosting there were enemies the game would not let me hit. My attacks went right through. Whats annoying is that the best weapons (In my opinion) are locked until you beat the main campaign. The crossbow and Dom rod. They are great, and feel good to use, probably because they aren't nearly as slow as the bow and shotgun. Yet once you get them you have 5 levels to enjoy them, I mean sure you could play endless mode but I at this point the other problems were just so glaring. The plot is bog standard for fantasy, dude from the past turns evil and is  here to reenact his revenge, except hes looking for a guy who has been dead for decades. So many quips that seemed like they were teasing at foreshadowing, How does the new guy use magic so easily? Never answered. What will the big bad guy do once he learns the man he is after has been dead for years? Never comes up. What happened to Max? Literally doesn't matter. Constantly there were places the story could have been better, maybe a twist ending boss, where he closes the gates because the reason for opening them was gone. Maybe have the new guy be able to effect rift magic like the main bad guy does. ANYTHING. and I know the plot is not the most important part of these games but they certainly didn't focus on the gameplay. All in all the game doesn't feel good, not like the past ones. It lacks any new charm while dulling all the charm it had from the past games. Pass it up unless it really cheap, and even then don't expect what the last games had.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite game series for co-op gaming! My husband and I originally played  together and loved the humour and the combination of tower-defense strategy and action.We were excited when  came out, and we had just as much (if not more) fun playing it than OMD2. The war scenario maps were a great addition, and you have enough variety of traps, weapons, and trinkets to to let you vary your play experience quite a bit. The humour and the cartoony art style keep it light-hearted and fun, but the game can be challenging if you don't plan carefully. You can adjust the difficulty if needed, which can be helpful early on when learning the game play. If you've ever played a tower-defense game before, the mechanics will be familiar. It's very satisfying to come up with effective trap (the "towers" of OMD) placement and just watch your traps do their work. However, for those that like a more active role, you can also use trinkets and weapons to deal with the enemies directly as well. We recently completed our second play-through, which is something we rarely do with games. But being able to play the entire main campaign this time with Gabriella and Max (who were the main characters from OMD2) was an added incentive. The variety of traps, weapons, and trinkets available with all the DLC allowed us each to play it differently the second time. If you're looking for a fun two-player co-op game where you can use both strategy and action, this is a great choice. I can't recommend it highly enough. I really hope the developers keep making co-op games that are so entertaining and engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: The Story mode is REALLY good and Fun. The Maps are great and I like the War mode. But sadly the second Campaign dlc und the other ones are just eh... Bad. Didn't play the Desert like dlc, but the Second campaign is REALLY Bad Map design, doing this alone is just to extrem. I never struggled with any map befor, but those are just too hard for me. Defending 3-5 separated lanes all on your own without any way to funnel them together is just insane! And then also keeping track of the 5 different Flying enemy types that have the potential to stun lock you and having so many Enemy types that are completely immune to 1 damage type doesn't really help.For example why would I give the Archers the flame upgrade when I know I can't rely on them because they will focus on 1 enemy that can't deal damage too. Same goes for other traps too. Just give enemies a resistance not a full Immunity. Same when i want to use the Wand, i always need to take another weapon with me, just so that i can kill the elementals and so, because they are immune to Arcane damage.Don't get me wrong, I can see why the mechanic is in there, I just think it's too much to have them completely immune to it. I never saw a Tower Defense game do this before and maybe with a good reason.So still I recommend the game, but I can say it doesn't have so much content in it. You can stretch it if you like the game's mechanics and try different difficulty modes or approaches to maps. Doubling the time i played from 8h to 16h i would think.So Get the game and have fun with it. Completely ignore the Frozen DLC, desert one i can't speak. _childDocuments_.review: Monotonous grind upgrading traps which you sometimes need to back out of a map to the main menu to respec since some enemies are immune to damage types granted by a few upgrades. Enemies seem needlessly spongy compared to earlier Orcs Must Die, taking way too long to kill unless you upgrade a trap to their weakness.The new player characters are also a stiff as cardboard.Update:Questionable design choices aside, the game is riddled with bugs. There is equipment that won't level up properly and when maps get too busy with lots of traps and orcs the AI gets wonky. _childDocuments_.review: So, this review isn't a hard "no" on the game so much as it feels like it desperately needs more time in the oven.  If nothing else was wrong with it, the balancing is a train wreck.  I don't have much to say that other negative reviews haven't already, except one lasting impression:  Nothing FEELS good in this game.  This sentiment repeated itself throughout my entire experience, and I committed to the grind anyway to confirm it.  Sure, it LOOKS a lot better than previous titles.  But everything else is a downgrade, from costs, to weapons, to story, to maps, to pathing, to grinding, to bugs, god*ammit nothing FEELS right when you play it.  I spent almost 40 hours going through every trap and weapon with most of the upgrades, I've tried endless combinations, and absolutely nothing feels like those "Aha!" moments you used to get when playing OMD2.  Not once did I feel like I had "beaten" a map, not even when I got up around Wave 50 (achievements only go to 25).  There's no sense of reward here, only this vibe that the developers resent you somehow.Enemies are spongy, weapons and traps are weak and expensive, maps are myopically designed with a narrow solution range, characters have boring abilities, favorite weapons or traps from OMD2 were nerfed to sh*t, the list goes on.  And all of that's assuming nothing breaks or bugs out.  Hell, for awhile you couldn't even look through your spellbook while your friend picked a level without hard-crashing.  And when all was said and done, a SMALL DLC almost half the cost of the game?  Look, if you're reading this, you're already a fan of the franchise and will probably eventually buy it no matter what anyone says.  But get it on a steep discount.  And the DLC on an even steeper discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Orcs Must Die! 3

_childDocuments_.review: Orcs Must Die 3 is a tower defense, 3rd Person Shooter. You place barricades and traps to thin and control the orc waves, and help mow them down with a variety of weapons. Overall this game is a step back from Orcs Must Die 2 and I therefor I only recommend it if you are truly done with 2 but still thirsty for some more. There is good enemy, weapon, trap and upgrade variety, to keep things fresh but there is not much new from 2. The variety is good because they didn't change it. That said though there are fewer maps. You have endless mode and weekly challenges to keep you busy, but I never much cared for those, in large part because you don't unlock anything for beating them.Also, and I am unsure if everyone will have this experience, the combat does not feel as good as it once did. The physics are less cartoonish, weapons have less heft to them. Something just felt worse in the moment to moment gameplay. Not bad per se, just worse...And it must be said that the writing and humor kind of sucks. Max, the main protagonist from the previous games, is a dumb but likeable action hero, and the short, stupid quips they write work best for him. But that same style of writing just does not work for the new cast of characters who have different personalities. I mean, to be perfectly honest, the writing didn't work well before either but it just sucks more now.So with almost everything being worse now, why am I still recommending this game at all? Its because of the "War Scenarios". Some maps have really scaled up orc invasions and give you massive amounts of money and access to more powerful traps. While there is only a few of these War Scenarios around, I really enjoyed playing them because of the absolutely massive orc hordes you murderize, and the new traps make it feel different. Its a shame they are so few.Orcs Must Die 1, 2 and 3 are all basically the same game. 2 was a huge upgrade from 1, so really feels worth it, but this entry is more of a lateral move. I spent 44 hours in Orcs Must Die 2, running through the game twice, and still occasionally going back to it, but that won't happen with this one. At 12 hours of gameplay I feel like I got my money's worth but only because I got it on sale.And that is the bottomline. Go buy Orcs Must Die 2.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like it is a massive step backwards from Orcs Must Die! 2. After beating the main campaign I had only used maybe 1/3 of the available traps and had enough upgrade points for about four of them. If I wanted to experiment with traps I needed to undo all upgrades, reapply the points I wanted, load the game, see what the upgrades did, realize it was a bad investment, rinse and repeat. I don't understand how a game like this decides to punish experimentation.Also the boss levels, called War Scenarios, are incredibly boring. Someone at Robot Entertainment thought that fighting 10 times the regular amount of orcs would be fun but they didn't give you the tools to deal with them efficiently so it just becomes a slog.
