_childDocuments_.review: A mediocre third person shooter at best that is sometimes played as a Tower Defence. Head shot your enemies, avoid getting hit by the projectiles, and if the map layout allows you to build a decent kill box - go for it, you'll finish one when the map is about 80% completed and you can have your bit of fun. You can't rely on your traps for the majority of playtime, you always need to babysit them over and over, making sure nothing passes through and oh boy almost everything is gonna get through, which leaves you really with piss-poor "shooting", and that is arguably the weakest part of the game. Aside from great visuals I really have nothing to complement this game for. Melee combat is redundant, it's inefficient, too high risk with no reward at all, lots of weapons are poorly balanced, hero skills are garbage, fake death, float in the air..very slowly etc. And although I haven't played previous titles of this franchise, from what I've heard, I can see how they just slapped a new engine, put a "3" on it and called it a day.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little tower defense game/shooter hybrid where you set up various traps and try to stop the hordes of monsters. The hero you choose will be there during the waves of enemies and you can (and should) use him/her to fight off the monsters and keep them away from the "rift" (their goal). Every rift has rift points which are lost once an enemy reaches it. If your rift points get to 0, you lose. There are several game modes, but the main one is campaign mode, where you'll play various interesting and increasingly difficult maps and advance a game story. Threr's also an endless mode where you play ona chosen map and endless and every time more difficult waves attack. Once you complete a map, (or get a better score if you replay it) you'll get awarded skulls which can then be used as currency for buying or upgrading weapons and traps. The game is fun but can get frustrating at times. It has a good replay value, since you can replay every map and try different strategies, heroes, weapons and traps. I fully recommend it if you're into tower defense games.

_childDocuments_.review: OMD3 just feels inferior to 2 in most ways, but most of all it just feels frustrating and unsatisfying to play. The first campaign is a slog - no matter how cleverly you arrange your traps, there will be too many quick enemies and meat shields that trigger your traps without dying to be able to handle the horde, so 90% of the kills you get feel like they come from you directly shooting the enemies. Barricades are so expensive and necessary to every single level that your economy is always in shambles, with no way to boost it. Even a fully invested, upgraded barricade costs 800 gold and dies in 1-2 bomber hits despite the "increased health", causing you to spend even more of your gold rebuilding barricades if you let even a couple enemies slip through during a wave. Games like this should feel fun and satisfying, watching enemies funnel into your well designed minefield of traps and deadly tricks, but the more I play, the more annoyed I am by the games design, the enemy design, and it seems the optimal "strategy" in OMD3 is to spam as many cheap traps as possible and use your weapon to shoot enemies.It's a shame, because visually the game looks great, the new characters are fun and have vibrant personalities, but the balance and flow of the game just feel off.

_childDocuments_.review: OMD2 was a fun game back when it released in 2012, but it became an all-time favorite of mine when I showed this game to my sister back in 2016, who instantly fell in love with it. We proceeded to not only 5-skull the normal co-op campaign, but also 5-skull the hard mode versions too.Then Unchained comes out...and it was a dud for us. We weren't interested in the pvp-side of things, but we were hopeful for something good out of the co-op experience. Nope: felt undercooked in a lot of aspects and we would just go back to OMD2 (for a little bit anyways before putting the series aside).Now, a couple years or so after playing OMD2, we finally get a real sequel in the form of OMD3...and it's largely the same as OMD2, for better or worse.Which, IMO, is not necessarily a bad thing. Hell, this isn't one of those franchises that gets milked every damn year. Besides, very few things in life beat the satisfaction of holding off tough early orc waves long enough so that you can get your trap hallways up and running to do most of the work for the rest of the level.In addition to the big sieges (the first one was hilarious for watching tons of red dots fly off the minimap), there is one extremely positive change that I cannot express enough gratitude for:Hard mode unlocks early.This is such a big change, especially since me and my sister tend to do well enough that we steamroll through normal mode maps. It's nice that we can be challenged early on with what little upgraded traps/weapons we have and see what we can make work for each stage. It's also nice to be given that little choice in how we experience the campaign - sometimes, we can figure out how to handle the hard mode map and 5 skull it early on, other times we had to progress a little bit on normal for some much needed traps or upgrades, then go back and finish them on hard.But again, for better or worse, it's more of OMD2 with some big sieges thrown into the mix. Not sure how solo feels, but as a 2 player co-op game, few games rival the thrills of working with your partner to fend off the endless orc horde.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most sophisticated Tower Defense game I've ever played. Probably most graphically rich tool. In general runs very smooth though on Endless at high wave counts 50+ It can get choppy or chaotic in a crowd and I've had the issue where the game just crashes (just once in 80 hrs) as a result. For bugs I've had a few. The above crash I mentioned. In the same game of said crash I was playing Endless and for some reason it just stopped counting enemies into my rift. Another is a pair of blades never counting any damage by them so I could not unlock its upgrades. Overall I thought it was a pretty good purchase even at full price. The campaign if you do a single play through is short at less than 15 hrs on normal. Though there are some other game modes like the Weekly challenges where certain restrictions help you learn what the value of different traps, trinkets, & weapons are. The mode I prefer most is Endless. With the campaign and challenges it never seems like you quite get to building your masterpiece with the points allocated within that sequence. Endless really lets you get creative and be an architect of the Orcs destruction. Though I do have a couple significant issues with Endless. Increasing slightly with each wave but becoming very noticeable by wave 50 enemies become damage sponges, damage over time effects like fire seem to vanish almost instantly, and the enemies start moving at a nearly running speed. Its so ridiculous that they move faster than the traps can even trigger. A single enemy can run over a dozen flip traps with them flipping well after they've passed. Essentially it makes it feel like the game is rigged. Flip traps sorely need fixed at least in respect to large enemies. Physics go bonkers at points when using them. Large enemies end up half submerged underground. Or they end up floating 3 feet above ground. Even with flip traps on a clean edge pointed towards that edge enemies seem to float above the pit and it can take minutes of trigger dozens of traps and bouncing around on invisible objects before they finally plummet from a trap if at all. Sometimes even instantly zooming or teleporting 30 feet to the inside of a pit. FIX the TRAPS for large enemies. You can counter it but it comes off as a very cheap mechanic. Though really by wave 50 the game can start feeling very grindy. Another issue with Endless is you can't save and come back to it later. And if you quit the leaderboard won't save your progress,  you have to loose for it to update. I quit endless at Normal with over 51 Million placing me at #10 globally and it didn't save it and I sure wasn't going to do that ♥♥♥♥ again. As for getting Skulls to upgrade your equipment don't grind a single level over and over for them. Its not worth it and not necessary. Play the weeklies and if you like Endless you can get quite a lot from some of them. You don't need to have everything upgraded, just refund points and move them around as needed. As a suggestion to the developer I'd like to see a Architect mode where you have an unlimited amount of points to begin with and can craft your level immediately and then set the mob aggression so you can test it right away. I shouldn't have to spend 6 hrs just earning enough points and dealing with weaker waves to begin to get to that point. 1440p monitor Intel 10850k 64 GB RamNVME storage1080 ti

_childDocuments_.review: It frustrates me to have to write a negative review about a game in a franchise I like so much. But I do it to vent out some of my annoyance with the changes they've done to the game compared to Orcs Must Die! 1 and 2.This is the reason this game feels so unfulfilling. It seems like the game was tailor made to be less rewarding and less pleasant than it was before.A lot of traps are unbalanced and many are so weak/expensive that they just don't cut it for Rift Lord, the highest difficulty (just to name a few: Decoy, Swinging Mace, Acid Geyser, Floor Scorcher). Nerfs when they happen usually make traps near useless while buffs are so meager they barely help change anything at all.Weapons suffer from lack of balance too. Only a handful are worth using in higher difficulties and some are so weak they're not even worth considering (Elven Shortswords, Alchemist Satchel). Even weapon Mana Regen is completely absent.The game does its darnest to counter the use of certain traps (Arcane Dragon and Saw Blade Launcher) for no reason other than the "balance". Such thing did happen before, but not the extent of OMD!3.Characters have just marginal differences between Health and Mana, but no special trait beyond a small mobility skill triggered by double jumping, so all of them feels "samey" to play and nothing helps you try out new playstyles outside your own self-interest. Again, the reasoning behind this was, most likely, "balance". OMD!1 had Weavers and 2 had characters with a big enough difference in Mana and Health (and exclusive traps) to force you to adapt and learn or test new builds, but there is no such thing here.In the end it seems Robot Ent. was too worried about balance, so much it ended up making for some very obnoxious level design and questionable enemy and gameplay choices. Whenever a company worries too much about game balance it inevitably ends up killing a lot of the fun in the game.The War Scenarios in particular could've been done better. They drag on for too long and overstay their welcome. The War Machines can be only used in these maps. However, in most cases, you're better off arming places with regular traps instead of placing War Machines which is a pity. Later maps are designed in such a way that War Machines can feel downright detrimental and being a waste of money. Another thing is that you cannot place them inside buildings. This kills many would-be nice strategies and is just another factor in what makes War Machines so underwhelming for veteran players.Even bosses add very little to the mix due to how easy they are to deal with. Scramble Mode shows they could've been into the regular game just fine (albeit not on EVERY wave), but they are present mostly in War Scenarios.Having two currencies and enemies that should be specifically targeted by War Machines would do wonders to avoid the problem of War Machines being outdone by regular traps. Downsizing them or their effect a bit so they'd fit into buildings would also be a good option to place them in tandem with the regular traps.Sadly, comparing this game to the previous ones only serves to highlight the flaws of this game.The game lacks pre-battle music except for War Scenarios.Graphically, the HUD design was changed from colorful to a bland, minimalist, dull style:Characters (and Orcs) have nowhere as many lines and start repeating the same phrases and one-liners very often which is particularly noticeable in longer games, like War Scenarios or Endless, and they don't even have wave start/end lines. And ALL of them share the same animations, including victory dance ones. Everything just feels lazy. Quality over quantity should be the lesson here.The gameplay was simplified and some status effects and damage types were removed. Chill, an alternative to slow, is absent. Damage types; impact, cutting, piercing and explosive were reworked into a single type (Physical).This simplification becomes a problem because Physical damage type is resisted by the vast majority of enemies in the game. And by vast majority I mean that it's easier to pick enemies that AREN'T resistant to it than the other way around. This renders Physical traps and weapons, one of the most common damage types, very ineffective.On enemies, we have Fire Fiends. Fire Fiends are enemies that are as numerous as Orcs and are completely immune to fire element. Why? What made the developers assume bringing an entire enemy faction immune to an element was a good design decision? In previous games Fire and Frost Ogres (which are unexplainably absent here) were enough of a threat to force you to mix different elements, an entire faction of enemies feels just ridiculous.Enemy design also became blander. Regular Orcs are all copy-pastes of each other instead of having a few distinct features (different skin colors or different armoring, like OMD!2 Orcs had) which could help players visually gauge how dangerous an Orc mob could be. Elementals also suffered from design change becoming boring, generic, looking enemies that could be seen in any fantasy game. Armored Ogres instead of wearing armor now seems like they just have bits of scraps all over them.Many weapons are absent here too: Vampiric Gauntlets, Dwarven Missile Launcher, Polymorph Ring, Bone Amulet. As for traps that are missing: Boulder Chute, Healing Well, Acid Sprayer, Ice Vent, Dwarves, Mana Well, Coinforge, Void Wall, Spore Mushroom, Web Spinner.Strategy-wise, the game became too focused on using a single core strategy: using Barricades to funnel enemies into a narrow space instead of being able to create big, open, killzones, which the game makes sure to discourage as much as possible with the small map design and weak/expensive crowd control and larger area hitting traps. Whereas Barricade killzones was a polite suggestion in previous games, in OMD!3 this strategy is so blatantly superior that not using it makes most of the maps more difficult.Par times are needlessly demanding which punishes many, less aggressive, strategies as well. Previous games had maps with tough Par times, but OMD!3, again, exaggerates doing this in almost EVERY map.The decision to cramp three storylines (the new Apprentices, the two ancient War Mages, and finding Max) with such limited time and levels to tell it was also a bad idea, as bad as leaving the face of the game, Maximilian, out of the 99% of the story. Again, everything feels rushed and ham-fisted at best and at worst half-heartedly which, for me, feels worse than not doing it in first place.Kelsey and Egan, the newcomers, lack any of Max and Gabriella's charm with their lines being most about uninspired and soulless banter or clunky exposition.Multiplayer also has a lot of missing features compared to the previous game: no in-game text chat, no pause, no in-game Voip, the inability to see your partner's loadout and not being able to see where they'll place a trap are the key ones. The host can also move to the next screen without your input before you upgrade which can be annoying.Lastly, there are several bugs and glitches that were reported by players a year ago and most of them are still in the game. Like pre-order skins having no voice since *day 1*, no "Final Wave" warning in Rift Lord, clunky physics especially with Sappers and several Scramble Mode glitches in the wild.If you're coming from 1, 2 or Unchained you will notice the flaws right away, so this is a big cautious recommendation.EDIT:As of v1.2 some of the weak trap problems were addressed buffing some traps and reducing the price of others. It doesn't solve all problems, but it certainly made the game more enjoyable and the learning curve less steep.

_childDocuments_.review: So, this game is pretty fun, and currently on sale for a huge discount. I haven't tried playing with a friend, but solo at least, it's enjoyable, but really annoying at times. The thing to know about Orcs Must Die 3 is that it's basically Orcs Must Die 2. That is to say, it feels like it's 10 years old. (No idea when the last game came out but it's not that important.)So, to the point. In the time since OMD2 came out, we've seen a lot of progress in the field of game design. We've come to expect certain design decisions that make games more intuitive, accessible, fun, whatever. OMD3 did not notice this.Featured in Orcs Must Die 3:- A linear campaign with zero branches or shortcuts- Headshot system with atrocious hit detection but huge damage multipliers- Your character calls you a moron when you misclick placing a building- Refund all your upgrades for free!**only item upgrades, not new unlocks for some reason (makes you not want to buy new stuff cause it's the only permanent choice you can make)- Your character does the fortnite default dance at the end of the mission and you can't pick up any items that droppedAnd the greatest sin of all:- Next to no warning that enemies are going to attack from a new locationSeriously, it's absurd. The thing that you have to pay attention to is a tiny icon on the minimap changing colors. That and the ghosts of a bunch of orcs coming from the new location. Which sounds like it would be easy to notice, but it's just not. You just tune them out unless you're building barricades. This is so dumb, and so annoying, that I just don't understand how it's in the game. There is literally a voice line to warn you about this, AFTER you've already placed all your defenses. Why? I have to sprint off and try to stop an entire army of orcs with nothing but a blunderbuss and my leftover 17 cents, just because the game didn't tell me they'd be coming this way.And after you get used to that, the game will simply give up on telling you anyway. The logical thing to do is to mark out where the enemies will be coming, then let the player build defenses, then spawn the enemies. But for some godforsaken reason, consecutive waves can have a time limit on the build phase in between them, AND spawn enemies from new locations. AND you have to somehow notice that the orcs are coming from this new location by looking up at the minimap for the tiny icon. And did I mention that the time limit isTen. Seconds.I hate it. But it feels like one of those things that you just put up with in an older game like "yeah, they didn't know any better at the time." Like quicktime events, or extra lives, or something. It's just annoying crap that feels dated.But, I mean, underneath it all, it's fun. Half the fun is crafting new defenses, trying to work within your budget, theorizing how best to deal with what the game's throwing at you (once you actually figure out what it is). And the other half is executing on that once it goes live.Overall, a tentative recommendation. It just feels like the game forgot that it needs to be played by its players, instead of the devs who already know everything and have everything unlocked.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I loved the previous games; this just isn't making it for me.I'm sure some people like it - perhaps even more than they would the first two games - but the change of genre is clearly not for me.So what do I mean with a change of genre?The previous two games felt like Tower defense games with a healthy deal of Shooter thrown into the mix.This game, however, feel much more like a Shooter with some very limited Tower defense mechanics thrown in there to waste your time on.Sure enough, a few of the maps actually do live up to a similar standard of the previous installments, but overall theme has definitely changed towards running and shooting at everything in sight, rather than trying to come up with thoughful combinations of traps and good timing.Most of the traps are simply completely useless. Some of them could work in combination with others, but only a few of the maps (the ones I like the most) allows for any such combinations to be used.And all of this could not be easily fixed with a couple of changes to balance. It's not JUST the price of traps, nor their poor damage output, or even the fact you can't find good places to build them on the maps - it's all of those things combined.I'm not entirely sure how I'd like to fix it myself, but I'd probably try doubling both the money and number of enemies on each map, before making a serious effort to make the traps actually do some damage. With money to spend on building actual kill zones, and too many enemies for your weapons to handle alone, it would start to look a lot more like the previous 2 games.

_childDocuments_.review: The replayability of this game lies mostly in the endless mode so the issues I'll have with the game are mostly there. Robot listen well. 1. Pathing issues are a real problem, getting your barricades destroyed for no reason is frustrating enough to make you want to leave the game right then and there. 2. The cash diminution in endless is too severe. It's not even that it is too steep, just it goes too low. It's nearly impossible to make money on maps where you cannot have huge kill streaks to make money. Have enemies return a minimum of 5% of their original worth, rounded up, would be my first suggestion to try.2.1. Enemies scaling in endless. Again I have an issue with this... I understand the player eventually needs to lose, but I feel like certain things should probably stop scaling or have a kind of diminishing returns to how fast they scale. I do not know for example how mountain trolls regen works, but if it scales off of their max hp it's a problem, they take way too long to kill too early. How fast enemies get is also not very fun, they become too fast for your traps to hit them. I do not know the perfect solutions for all those scaling issues but there certainly should be a discussion about this.3. Items balance in general. This also pertains to replayability. Trying new combinations makes it fun. But the problem is so severe you have best in slots (as in best ceiling trap(s), best wall trap(s), best floor trap(s) and also best weapons. Trinkets also have issues for me they are only a shadow of what they were in orcs must die 2. There is a lot, and I mean a lot to say on issue number 3 and I might keep posting in steam discussions to go into details and to give suggestions.3.1. Fire element. It is garbage. Few enemies are weak to it, a lot are IMMUNE, immunities aren't quite fun to begin with, and the "on fire" affliction is a real joke. The slow and damage over time are ridiculously bad. If not reworked entirely both the damage and the slow should be drastically buffed.3.2 You do not seem to understand how to make similar traps all viable. Some uniques need to be looked at. Trinkets need to have better passive effects before any purchase are made. Again I can't go into details here, too long4. This is just as important as the rest if not more. The map themselves. They do not make use of possible trap combinations or specific trap themselves that need a particular configuration or type of monsters to shine. The most cruel thing of all, the war scenarios are most of the time easier with normal traps, making the use of the special traps very scarce. Why is there no game mode where you can bring war scenario traps to regular maps for fun? Most of the traps should be placeable indoor, not be a unique upgrade. Terrible decisions you have made there. The choice of maps for endless is also horrible, there would be a lot of better choices for endless maps but you picked things like the basement or switchback,where there is almost no spots to place traps before orcs reach the rift and you have to barricade to path the enemies all around the rift, and that's it, that's the whole and only strategy. Overall I am not happy with the maps and what you do with them. I wish I could be more specific and I hope others voice their complaint about the maps. I am sure they require great efforts to make, which is why you should think a lot more of their configuration and their specifics. Hopefully you do before releasing new ones.I'm sure I have a lot more to complain about, but unless the game is improved, you will lose your Orcs must die 3 playerbase way quicker than Orcs must die 2 ever did, despite its flaws orcs must die 2 felt more of a solid game with decent replayability, and I think it is because it has more levels, a nice difficulty curve, better balance for items. In game chat wouldn't hurt. Keep making this game better and I might change my review. I do not hate your game, I love it, indifference is the opposite of love. Keep up the good work team Robot.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall it is fairly decent, not as strong as 2, and the characters feel very "prepy" and cringe. Those who are familiar with the OMD will quickly find familiarity, and the game itself is easy enough to pick up on. There are way more traps and weapons this time around (fewer trinkets), however, these vary wildly in usefulness and seem to be too far below the power curve to use when you unlock them.Unlocking things is also the same grind it was before, with upgrading and unlocking there is a lot to do and the ability to refund skulls (upgrade points) is a very much welcome feature.Enemies have a lot of variances in resistances and weaknesses which has advantages and disadvantages in that you need to diversify your kit to be able to challenge the harder content effectively, however, that means more unlocking and upgrading to be able to compete, and testing out these can take a lot of time. Also they have their own voice lines which usually just tends to be a lot of whining and cringe. It gets old pretty quick. Maps are definitely worse this time around in my opinion. Less ways to push orcs off edges, nothing really fun like the minecarts, and some levels are literally just 3 straight paths that don't use 90% of the level. A lot of levels are very open and lack good kill zone areas. Some maps on the other hand will literally spawn in enemies in places that you aren't expecting, haven't set up for, and have no hope of holding out. It's a decent edition with a new of mechanics and features, lack unfortunately lacks the charm of OMD2. Still worth it for the price.Note: Haven't been able to test the Co-Op or online components as of this review.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great discount game that lands somewhere between an indie and AAA title. It's a third person shooter/tower defense hybrid. Hordes of extremely stupid, lemming-like orcs will march their way straight into your base unless you stop them with a combination of deadly traps and your own weapon-wielding character. It can be played alone or with a friend as well. My own experience and review of the game is based entirely on my own preference for solo play, but you might enjoy it even more in co-op mode.If you had fun with either of the first two games, you will like this installment as well, although you won't notice much has changed. The gameplay formula is pretty solid though, and when you've landed on a winner, it's usually better to air on the side of "if it ain't broke, don't fix it." As a result, if you've played any of the other OMD games, this will seem very familiar. As much as I liked them, I never spent as much time with the other OMD games as I have with this one. While there are more levels than previous installments, it isn't enough to make it significantly longer in length. Rather, the longevity lies in my drive to gain perfect ratings on levels I'd previously only been able to squeak by on, and unlock/upgrade all my favorite weapons and traps. Despite the familiarity, I haven't found the core gameplay lacking or outdated in any way, and the fresh coat of paint and new features have been more than enough to keep me interested. That said, your mileage may very depending on how you felt about the previous games, and how much time you spent with them.Graphically the improvements aren't super noticeable at first. The older games featured a very cartoonish art-style, very heavily inspired by the likes of Warcraft II and III, and this one is no different. The technology was there ten years ago to do this look justice, and it looks as good as ever but with subtly better lighting, textures, and shadows. The interface also feels more streamlined and professional, less like a small indie game, and closer to something you might see in a AAA title. Some of the levels are also very aesthetically beautiful, as the developers have expanded out from the usual dark, enclosed, interior levels to many that take place in outdoor environments with open skies and foliage. In addition to a wealth of new tools at your orc-killing disposal, most of the traps and weapons from previous games make a return also, with the main exception I noticed being the seldom-built, single-use traps from OMD2, such as the ceiling boulders. Several levels still have these built into them from the start though, so using the environment to your advantage is still very much a thing. Everything from traps, to weapons, to trinkets is now upgradable in multiple ways, including everything making a return from previous games. For instance, the brimstone square can be upgraded to either deal arcane damage (instead of fire), or refresh more often depending on your choice. Other new additions include new enemies (of course), but more notably war scenarios which are levels designed to grant a better sense of large-scale battles. These maps are usually much larger than average, and allow you to use specific, powerful traps that aren't normally available to you. War scenario traps are much more expensive, and are usually designed to take out more enemies across larger areas. They tend to have longer cooldowns or require some baby-sitting, however. Such as the Indiana Jones-like ball launcher which requires you to manually activate it after it resets, or the auto-ballista which functions more like a turret you have to sit in + manually aim/fire. These war scenario traps can be a lot of fun to use, but still require a lot of consideration for placement, use, and cost. All of the war scenario levels can still be beaten by sticking to your usual arsenal of traps as well, but this usually requires its own placement considerations to bottleneck the horde into more of a killbox area. It's an impressive testament to careful balancing and level design that so many options and strategies remain viable while still keeping the game challenging.The other new additions include additional characters and campaigns. Each character has his or her own special ability, but otherwise all play exactly the same, so it's mostly an aesthetic choice unless your strategy specifically compliments a given character's abilities. I've seen some argue that some special abilities are much better than others, but I don't think they make a major difference. Campaigns are also a nice addition, as it means more content can/will be added to the game over time rather than the older games' release-and-done model. These keep the game relevant and fresh, adding more traps, maps, and enemies. The first one comes free with the Steam version of the game, but the most recently released "Cold as Eyes" DLC has a small cost. Still, there are no other microtransaction options or obligations in the game, so paying for new, optional, content like this feels perfectly respectable.If you liked either of the first two games, or are just someone who likes tower defense games in general, this game is a must-have. Not only for just a playthrough or two, but for new content that may be coming down the pipeline later. You'd be supporting a polished and finished game which doesn't include microtransactions or price gouging, has a ton of replay-value, and is just a ton of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally!!!! After years and years, plus a failed attempt at 'Dying Orcs as a Service', Orcs Must Die 3 returns to it's roots as a Steam local co-op game. 1. Classic style gameplay that made the series great2. New fun and creative traps3. New fun and challenging levels4. The new war mode is SO MUCH FUN5. THE MUSIC. OMG.... Such a fantastic soundtrack! I can't get enough of the victory song!6. The improved graphics engine is gorgeous (but it has some negatives I'll explain below)7. One of the BEST co-op experiences for PC! Thank you Robot!!!8. Not a "as a service" game9. Lower buy-in price makes me more accepting of future add-ons when they are also reasonable10. You can play as Max and Gabriella after you beat the campaign (This saves the game long-term)1. The new young characters are kind of annoying2. The dialog is awkward (in a bad way) with the guy always sounding like a total moron by asking dumb questions, and the girl answering to correct him constantly because reasons.()3. I miss the more diverse outfit choices from OMD2, especially for Gabriella4. Points 1, 2, & 3 have me wondering if they're trying to be more politically correct or woke. I certainly hope not. If they go full woke I'll be forced to disown the franchise and Robot. Just make great OMD games!!4. While the sound effects are phenomenal, I miss the old swinging mace sound and the skull pickup sound because sometimes it difficult to tell if you picked up a skull if you have to dive in the middle of horde5. The launch was a little rough on Steam. The team had to force FPS limits of 60 and disable HDR due to problems, and there was a weird mouse clicking glitch where the game would only register 1 of 3 clicks.I can only imagine how hard it must have been to adapt the game from the Stadia environment to the local PC environment, but they had a long time to work on it during exclusivity.1. Stadia exclusivity. I've followed OMD since the original. I'm aware Robot mentioned OMD 3 would not have happened without the Stadia partnership because Robot was broke after OMD Unchained, BUT if they hadn't wasted so much money, time, and energy on the HORRIBLE "game as a service" FAILURE, they wouldn't have been in the position to need the Stadia exclusivity to begin with. I hope they learned. Don't abandon the winning formula!Having said all that I am SO HAPPY that OMD is back where it belongs on Steam and NOT "as a service". It's a shame that Robot had to learn the hard way that very few PC gamers voluntarily choose to support the "as a service" model. I certainly avoided OMD Unchained like it was the plague, and think, we could have been on OMD4 after the success of OMD3 by now!Overall, this is a fantastic addition to the OMD franchise, and I greatly look forward to future additions of DLC to it, and eventually, the next OMD. If Robot sticks to classic model of local games with co-op, I will continue to buy every title and all DLC for them!

name: Stargate: Timekeepers
detailed_description: Stargate: Timekeepers is a tactical game in which you lead a team of specialists through a story-driven campaign featuring an original narrative set in the Stargate SG-1 universe. Sneak a newly formed team behind enemy lines, use your characters’ unique skills, craft the perfect plan and defeat the Goa’uld threat. DIVE INTO THE STARGATE SG-1 UNIVERSE Stargate: Timekeepers departs from the end of season 7 of the Stargate SG-1 main plot to create an original story, unfolding over 14 narrative-rich missions . Your adventure starts during the Battle of Antarctica, where Commander Eva McCain and her team are supporting the SG-1 against Anubis’s fleet. Sometime later, Eva and her team of specialists are tasked with a new mission in the Stargate universe: help the Jaffa Resistance, prevent brutal rituals, strike against Moloc’s army, and seek an alliance with the Unas. LEAD A TEAM OF SPECIALISTS Lead a team of specialists operating behind enemy lines. Use your characters’ unique skills to come up with perfectly synchronized plans to overcome Kull Warriors, Jaffa Generals, Moloc’s Officers and many new and original enemies. Natural leader and long-time soldier, Eva McCain is a master of automatic rifles and experienced at spotting weak points. Extremely agile and an expert sniper, Max Bolton can hide in a ghillie suit to find the perfect spot to take down enemies from long distances. Sam Watson , trained spy and technical officer, is an expert on alien gadgetry. Derreck Harper’s drones carry out some of the most difficult tasks, including healing allies and deactivating hostile electronic devices. The core team from Tau’ri makes friends along the way: A’ta , Jaffa rebel and sneaky thief who carries a Ma’tok staff for short-range combat; and Xugga , a powerful yet good-natured Unas veteran who joins your team along with a little friend. Each individual has a set of unique abilities: play smart and combine them to silently eliminate your enemies in quick succession. Tactical Mode allows you to synchronize your characters’ actions perfectly.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I would like to point out that I was one of the developers (and creative director) of the fan game called ‘Stargate Network’ that received a cease and desist order from MGM right after the Timekeepers announcement in May/June 2021.Although I am truly saddened that we have been forced to shut down Stargate Network after 14 years to clearly avoid any possible competition with this official game, rest assured that this is not the reason why I am giving a bad review.I also specify that I participated in the beta test phase of Timekeepers, and I'm not allowed to talk about it (NDA).This is not a criticism of the developers' hard work (I have great respect for video game developers because I know how this business works), but rather of poor decisions, directives, mismanagement, maybe a too low budget, and not enough interest or respect for the IP in my opinion.I will try to be as detailed and objective as possible while being factual. (Lot of spoilers)Personally, I don't care if it's a RTT, not a FPS, not a X-COM thing...I love and play all kinds of games, it's stupid to give a bad review just because the game is not in the genre you would like it to be.Timekeepers could have been a very good RTT. But it suffers from what appears to be a lack of polish, budget and time.As a Stargate fan, I wanted Timekeepers to be a success, I would have really liked to be able to support this game, say that it is good and that it gives a positive image of the franchise.But I'm not having lot of fun with this game, unfortunately.The only things I find nice are : levels environments, loading screen drawings and few other things.In my opinion this game should have been labeled "Early Access" on Steam.Charging full price for half of a game is not normal, especially considering that it suffers from a significant lack of polish.It is not normal, especially for those who pre-ordered the game, that on the Steam page, 1 month after the initial release date (December 12), it is added in the description that the game will ultimately be in two parts.With the second part initially announced for April 2024, and now changed again to "later in 2024." Summer? Winter maybe?I'm glad people no longer have to dig the internet to know that and I really hope that people who purchased the game will have the chance to get this second part. You have to trust Slitherine, I guess. Fortunately there is no extra to pay.Do not expect to see or play the Unas character visible on the game cover. Likely in mission 8-14.This is the things that gives me the impression that this game was rushed to meet a certain deadline.The cinematics are not too bad for the first 3 missions; there are some nice animations and cool shots, even though it remains quite basic and classic for a RTT. Don't expect stunning graphics with complex visual effects.However, from the 4th mission onwards, it feels like everything was rushed.The majority of the cinematics revert to the traditional flying camera above the map with spawn and despawn of characters and pnj clearly visible lot of times. (Lack of polishing again)(The only few ‘cool shots’ are in the launch trailer, nothing more, nothing less)What happened to the very cool 2D cinematics presented two years ago?? Nothing like that in the game anymore.It would have been very qualitative and at least nicer than the very basic 3D cinematics that we have in the game now instead.The dialogue lines follow one another without real coherence sometimes.You feel like a story was intended to be told, but everything seems to have been cut and recut.It feels like there are missing scenes / connections between things or removed parts that they didn't have time to make.I will explain more on this point in number: 6) Storyline and lore.- End of missions + some objectives can easily been rushed at some point by running in the middle of Jaffa shooting at you.(in Normal mode) Is this intended or is this poor level/game design?- Enemies can often see you or shoot at you through environmental elements.The same environmental elements that block you from shooting as a player.- The enemy AI lacks complexity or ‘life’; they can be easily bypassed, predictable, or just plain stupid.- When you knock out an enemy, he wakes up and go back to his routine as if nothing had happened…- 2 Jaffa speak to each other, you kill one, the other continues to speak alone.- Enemy detection is sometimes strange, sometimes they detect you doing something or killing someone when they are not looking towards you and are not supposed to hear you…- Sometimes it's the opposite, they are totally blind when their friend is killed in front of them.- Characters can speak aloud in the middle of enemies without any issue...You can watch my test and review during my Twitch streams re-uploaded on Youtube here:Part 1: Part 2: Part 3 + full debrief at the end:

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so, this would be a 'Maybe' review if steam let you.I want to like this. Infact i mostly *do* like it.However. _childDocuments_.review: As a long time Stargate and strategy game fan, I really wanted to like this game. Unfortunately, I didn't.The game feels rushed in many respects. Up to a point that the basic game mechanics do not work well, yet. I say yet, because I feel that the game could actually be pretty good if the developers would rework the underlying mechanics a little. It plays like a proof of concept or early test, as many of the flaws can be traced back to a lack of feedback from actual players.Stargate Timekeepers is a stealth strategy game. However, the game runs in real time whereas the controls do not facilitate this in the slightest. Doing anything required a lot of focus and giving commands is very slow, especially when commanding more than a single character at a time. It truly feels like the controls were made for a turn based game.The graphics are a positive note. The levels look very good and feel Stargate-y. Just look at the images on the store page and you can see what it looks like.As for story... oh boy. Characters are flat, some are never even introduced and are just disembodied voices, and some lines feel disconnected to what was said right before. The game does not even try to connect the missions together.The worst part is that the game is not loyal to the source material. For example, the first mission is about stopping Anubis' forces in Antarctica from shooting a big block of ice (?) behind which SG1 supposedly is in the Ancient outpost. This makes no sense for several reasons:First, there are ring transports that allow Anubis to teleport his soldiers to the outpost. He does this in the series. He does not need to dig into the ice.Second, the outpost is miles below the surface and the mission is above ground (the warriors also make no progress at all).Third, Anubis' army is using hand weaponry to blast the ice while they litterally have a big cannon at their disposal. This cannon is the focus of the mission and the player uses it to (you'll never guess this) DESTROY A HUGE BLOCK OF ICE.Fourth, the bulk of the army is just standing around, waiting for the handful of warriors to blast away the ice in a very time sensitive scenario.Okay, to fix all of these problems at once, they could have simply had the army construct some sort of super drill and have the player stop them. That would have made some sense and be believable. What we got, for anyone who has seen the series, just doesn't.One last thing I want to mention is the AI. You probably read it in other reviews, but I had to include it myself. The enemies are really simple. They ignore having been knocked out after waking up. They will ignore missing friends. They will even walk into bushes one at a time after seeing three of their friends dissappear in that same bush. Once, I tied up all enemies except the last, who I knocked out before running on. I was on the other side of the map when I realised I could no longer save the game. Apparently, the enemy had woken up and was alarmed to find all his friends tied up, and was looking around for me. I was long gone, and had to go back the entire way to take care of an enemy that was no longer relevant just so I could save the game again. I still wonder why he didn't just untie his friends... maybe they slept with his Jaffa girlfriend...I really wanted this game to be half decent and give me an excuse to throw some money to the franchise I love. But I cannot rationalise spending 29 euros on this game. I refunded it. Maybe, after the devs fix the most glaring gameplay issues, I'll buy it again. But I doubt we'll see such major improvements to core game mechanics. Very disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.And despite the game being pretty awful in the beginning I still tried to give it a fair shot. I took a break. Took a deep breath....and then came back to it with a clear head.But I don't like this game.It's a STEALTH GAME.Don't come into this expecting it to be a tactical game or a strategy game like you'd expect. (Yes it does have some inkling of strategy and tactics) But the whole point of this game is stealth. You are severely punished for trying to fight your way through as you are always at a massive disadvantage and are punished for even attempting to actually fight.There's no unit upgrades, no base upgrades. No customization. There's no choices or decisions of any kind. There's no role-play here at all.There's no gear. There's no iconic characters or worlds.There's not even any stargates in this stargate game.It was a waste of an IP. Imagine if they had made this game like X-Com or Aliens: Dark Descent. Now THAT would have been fricken epic.Even if it had just been controlling a squad of 4 or 5 units and fighting around each map would have been better then this. I mean there's not even a cover mechanic. The game has good graphics and great sound but that's pretty much it. Oh and the game isnt' finished yet. I know it doesn't say early access but only part 1 of season 1 is available right now. Wanna play the full game? Then wait till later on this year when part 2 is released.This game isn't worth 30 dollars. And despite being a big stargate fan I would still pass and encourage other people to pass as well. IMO it's just not worth our money or time.If you'd like a more in-depth look with gameplay please check out the video on my YouTube channel (link below).Otherwise thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a stealth game with the dumbest stealth mechanics I have ever seen. During the tutorial, you have to sneak over to a gun for one of your soldiers. So you stealth over, get past a guard, and then see two Jaffa discussing it. They are just chilling talking about guns vs staves, and one of them is saying that even our "simple" weapons can be effective. Side note, I love this bit of world building. The Jaffa are having interesting conversations in the background! That's pretty awesome!But back to my point. We have to grab the weapon, so we have to knock them out (we are unarmed at that point). We go over, we knock them both out, and we retrieve the gun. Enemies don't stay out for long, just a few seconds really, so I am curious what will happen when they get up. I wait, and they both get back up. They don't even look around, they just pop back into their original positions, with no further dialogue or noticing the gun is gone. I also couldn't take their staff weapons?! What's the point of knocking out the guards if they have no ability to discern they were unconscious, they don't react to it, the other AI don't react to it, they are only out cold for a few seconds, and you can't disarm them?Immediately killed the mood. This is a stealth puzzle game. You just have to know in which order to go where, and occasionally press a button that knocks the opponent out. This is going to be a tough sell for most people, so I can't recommend it. If you really, really want more stargate media, then go for it. If you want a Commando clone, go for it. But this game isn't for me, and I am guessing that it isn't for most other people.

_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews have said that this should not have been a tactical stealth game because that doesn't fit the Stargate setting, and I for one completely agree! How dare they do this?Didn't they watch the finale of season one, "Within the Serpents Grasp" in which SG-1 stops Apophis by boarding his flagship and clearing every single room with fire from their belt fed M60's, leading to a standoff between O'Neill and Apophis, which the colonel wins by making a "Duke Nukem" reference and blowing him away with a rocker launcher? Oh, wait. I got that wrong. SG-1 sneaks around the ship, laying ambushes since they are completely outnumbered.Okay, what about the first episodes of Stargate: Atlantis? You know, the one where Col. Sheppard rescues everyone on the wraith ship by kicking in the front door and killing all the wraith in single combat with a claymore. Oh! No, I got it wrong again. Sheppard and the gang rescue everyone by sneaking around the ship. I guess Timekeepers actually does a pretty good job as capturing the feel of the Stargate shows, and I am left wondering if many of the people leaving reviews that are critical of this have actually watched any of the Stargate series.My snark aside, if you like Commandos, or the newer Mimimi games, like Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3 then this a good choice for you. If you like those kinds of games *and* Stargate then this is made for you. If you hate that kind of game then skip this one. I understand that it sucks that so few Stargate games make it to release, and that you wanted a fps, an MMO, or something like x-com, but that didn't happen. I don't feel like dog piling on the one game that did make it just because it's not tailored to your individual taste in video games is constructive. I hope all the angry people down here in the reviews get their dream Stargate game one day because I would love to play that too, In the meantime Timekeepers is fun to play, runs well, is $30 at release and is clearly make by people who love the franchise. That's a recommend for me, especially as someone who loves stealth games.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the franchise, but this isn't it.The game is simple, repetitive and could be improved a lot. I finished it in 9 hours, there are seven missions, including the tutorial mission, however, they were still introducing new mechanics through about six of them. So it always felt like you were in a tutorial.The game has potential, but is not a real time tactics game at all, it's more a puzzle game. They have set a map with challenges and you need to figure out how to overcome those challenges with artificial limits on your resources. The story is ok up until this point. But incomplete, however, how they present the story is horribly flawed. You will see events happen in the lead up to each mission that didn't happen in the previous mission, you will get told of things that dictate why you are doing these things in this mission, and those things didn't actually happen.It's like they had seven different people design seven different story fragments and then tried to cut them together with ham fisted exposition. There is no replay value that I can see, and the puzzles and challenges you have aren't actually that challenging. Is it bad, no, is it worth the bucks, probably not.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - If you want a difficult stealth game, this is a good buy. If you want a Stargate game, don't bother.---This is a stealth game with very,  little room for error. Enemy visual cones fill up quickly when they spot you and take a while to empty if you can get out of sight in time. They are also very quick to call for backup the moment they register you as a target.There is also no autosave, which makes sense because you need to save almost every couple of minutes, and after you pass every tiny section of a level. Requiring to save that often makes an autosave obsolete. If you haven't saved in 3 minutes, you need to save. Anymore time than that is being cocky.I found some of the animations to be stiff, wooden and the character models have limited movement cycles. It's not so much of a problem in the game as you have visual distance from the models, but it definitely shows in the cutscenes. The environments are beautiful, though. A lot of effort clearly went into the visual element of each level and I do appreciate that.The voice actors sound pretty good and I wouldn't be surprised if any of them were professional, but I found some of the tone of voice and phrasing to be off. I'm putting that down more to the script and directing that the VAs themselves.None of this bad, so to speak. Brilliant games can have iffy graphics or subpar voice acting, and there's nothing wrong with difficult games.However...I can confidently say that I would not have looked at this game twice if it hadn't used the Stargate IP.The lore and terminology are on point, and I credit the developers for doing their research. But sadly, that research doesn't hold up in the mechanics.I understand that limited ammunition is a staple in stealth games, but certain weapons (like the Ma'tok staff weapon and the Zat'nik'tel) don't have that limitation. Forcing the Zat to have 10 charges and making the staff completely melee, it just isn't what those weapons are. And they are staples of the franchise, so having them on only one character each is also immersion-breaking.Another issue is that this game is entirely linear. Yes, you get to choose which fork in the road to take, but both will lead you to the same end. There is no exploration. There is no character interaction beyond cutscenes and scripted banter at certain parts of the level. And, as other reviews have pointed out: You. Do. Not. Get. To. Use. The. Stargate. You are on a planet, you go from point A to point B, to point C and finish at point D. You start at a random site, you end at a random site.Simply put, this does not feel like Stargate. None of it feels like Stargate.I have been a part of this fandom since the movie first came out in 1994. I grew up with SG1, along with the Atlantis spin-off. As such, it is very near and dear to my heart. I wanted Timekeepers to be a success, and hoped it would capture at least some of the magic that made the movie and television series so fantastic.I am disappointed that it hasn't, both for myself and for the game.This could have been any other IP or an entirely new IP and the game would not have suffered. If anything, it suffers by trying to be a part of Stargate. If this had been a WW2 era game, and you had played as Allied Forces going behind enemy lines, I imagine this would have received glowing reviews.Timekeepers is a decent stealth game with a higher than average difficulty, but it is an absolutely abysmal Stargate game. And for that, I'm afraid I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge Stargate fan and was incredibly excited for this game.  I really really really wanted to like it, but unfortunately I really can't recommend it.It is a stealth game that is begging to be turn based so badly, but isn't.  It is not a strategy game, there is no base, no upgrades, no customization and no role playing.  You are punished for playing the game any way other than in a stealth mode and are forced to sneak up behind the majority of enemies to knock them out and tie them up.  You spend most of the game checking the line of sight of the Jaffa and quickly bouncing back and forth between the characters dealing with the clunky controls.  It might be worth suffering through all that if you got to play as your favorite iconic characters like O'niel, Carter, Jackson or Tealc, but instead you get to play as some no name red shirts.This game is begging for some sort of turn based play similar to XCOM, Baulder's Gate 3 or Divinity 2 which probably could have saved this and made it a really compelling game.  It also might have been more compelling if you just had 1 character to control, trying to control 2 characters concurrently in real time is clunky and frustrating.If you are looking for a strategy game, high action combat, customization or to play as your favorite characters this game is probably not for you.  If you are into real time stealth games this might be right up your alley and maybe it just wasn't my cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you played , , or ? If so, and if you liked those games, then you'll like Stargate: Timekeepers. A lot of the negative reviews on here are because people were expecting a Starcraft version of Stargate. This isn't that game. It plays exactly like Desperados 3. It's a  game where you control a small party of soldiers and eliminate enemies along the way. The exact same mechanics exist in Desperados 3. For starters, there's a tactical pause. In Desperados 3 this was called . Here, it's simply called . The cool part is you can synchronize commands. When you pause, you can issue commands to your party and then choose to either execute those commands immediately, or have your party members synchronize their attacks so they land at the same time. It's a feature I loved in Desperados 3 and it works precisely the same way here. And just like Desperados 3, the game revolves around trial & error. A timer will appear at the top of the screen to let you know how long it's been since your last quicksave. The idea here is that every time you successfully dispatch some enemies, and you find yourself in a safe location, save. If your next attack goes back, simply reload the latest quicksave. All of your companions have unique abilities that allow them to distract enemies, and they all have unique attacks. But keep in mind this isn't a roleplaying game. You're not going to be earning XP with these characters and increasing their from mission to mission. The game could probably benefit from that sort of design. Also, the one feature that's missing here - a feature I absolutely loved in Desperados 3 - is the end mission time-lapse replay. Desperados 3 has this really cool feature where it will show a time-lapse replay from overhead of all the moves you made and all the enemies you dispatched. It's a really awesome way to see how you got through the scenario. I love it, and I hope Slitherine considers adding it to this game. Outside of that, not much else to say. These sorts of stealth/tactics games aren't deep. They're just fun and, at times, tactically challenging. It's a puzzle sometimes to figure out the most efficient way to dispatch a group of enemies given their locations, patrol routes, and vision cones.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really hoping this was going to be another Commandos game but this game is far from being polished and optimised. The AI in this game is a joke; i can literally knock out an enemy right next to another enemy and no one notices. When the enemy is alerted, they seem to meander around aimlessly, with no logic to their pattern. And when they do see you, they seem to be able to shoot through solid objects when you cannot.  I can also run passed an enemy and they don't notice you either. The developers should really take note how they did all this in commandos, this game was awesome. I'm going to quote a review from IBREC, and all this is spot on:- Enemies can often see you or shoot at you through environmental elements.      The same environmental elements that block you from shooting as a player.- The enemy AI lacks complexity or ‘life’; they can be easily bypassed, predictable, or just plain stupid.- When you knock out an enemy, he wakes up and go back to his routine as if nothing had happened…- 2 Jaffa speak to each other, you kill one, the other continues to speak alone.- Enemy detection is sometimes strange, sometimes they detect you doing something or killing someone when they are not        looking towards you and are not supposed to hear you…- Sometimes it's the opposite, they are totally blind when their friend is killed in front of them.- Characters can speak aloud in the middle of enemies without any issue...I also would have thought my Geforce RTX 3080 would handle this game on high settings but I experience stuttering and map generation slowness when i move across the map. I was really looking forward to this game as a replacement to Commandos, but it is severely under-cooked. Looking at early previews of this game, why on earth did they remove the HUD they had?? It was much better to what they eventuality went with!!

_childDocuments_.review: Really don't get why people are giving this a bad score. Actually, I do get it, they expected an action game, while it is a Commandos-style stealth game. Honestly, with Mimimi studios closing down, this game is a godsend, especially because it is about one of my favorite franchises ever (see profile picture).Really, what's there not to love about it?Well, you see... I can think of a few points, and leave it here as feedback for the devs.- One of the first things I noticed: the voice acting, while good, is a little... I don't know, forced, cheesy. Don't know how to describe it. But one of the main characters keeps talking as if he was the hot star of a 60's era action movie. Maybe it was intentional? It just feels weird.- Few stealth kill options. Although I get that in modern-era warfare (especially futuristic warfare) guns are the standard, I think it is strange to go into an area spraying a SMG when there are many enemies gathered together (also see my next point). I would also have really liked a knife skill for all characters. Just stunning and tying the enemies up is a little bothersome.- The ability to control more characters during missions. This would allow for more diverse strategies for taking out a large number of enemies. Maybe it would make the game too easy, but again, spraying enemies with a SMG is not how I prefer to play stealth games.I haven't played through all of it yet, so those are the points I didn't really like about the game. But they're FAR from a deal breaker. Just minor details.Anyway, if you area fan of Commandos/Mimimi studios types of game, this is a must buy! If you love Stargate, it is a very interesting addition. If you love both, don't even think about it, just get it!But if you expect an action shooter, or Metal Gear like game, this is not it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very suprised and happy when this game was announced two or three years ago! At the beginning I was a bit disappointed it wasn't going to be an FPS, which would have been very cool.Than I read and heard something about strategy game -> so I thought, oh cool, it's going to be one of those games where you build a base with various buildings and create armies and so on...Well the first showcase (a year ago) made me realize it's a so called "stealth game" - basically you sneak around. I was kind of like "well ... I don't know if this is going to be really fun but let's see!". Than I got lucky and invited to the beta and I was actually a bit disappointed -> I didn't even finish the first level, because the game simply didn't click with me. (Compared to now it was far less polished!)Since I'm a big fan of the show it was clear I would buy the game either way, liking it or not. So the game got a released a few days back and I downloaded and played it. Please keep in mind, I'm not a "gamer" - I don't care about ultra up to date graphics. Sometimes, depending on the game, I prefer "simple" looking 3d assets. Also I'm on Hak'tyl right now - so I'm currently playing the second mission:+ I like the graphics and it's design+ I do feel that the developers are passionate about Stargate themselfes, even though some complained it was not the case. I think you can see that they put a lot of effort into making it+ so far (I'm at mission 2) the story seems interesting, I'm looking forward to the rest!+/- I like the dialogue - but wish they would add more of it, for example make the Jaffa say something when you click them... +/- I have never played a stealth game before - so I don't have anything to compare it to. So far it's fun, but I do wonder if it's going to get boring later on. Seeing the environment/maps -> it would have been cool to add some type of "first person view" in order to be able to immerse yourself even more - sure the sky and everything above is missing, but maybe they could have come up with something.A little hint for others who haven't played yet a stealth game: I didn't realize in the beginning - it is not necessary to kill every enemy - it's okay to just sneak passed them using non-damaging actions. In the beginning (beta) I got hung up trying to kill them all instead of using tactics to pass them by. - I haven't played all missions yet but checked the maps online - I really hope that they are going to add more maps later, like the SGC, Tok'ra base, Tel'Tak, Hatak, Abydos, Asgard ship.... Maybe sometype of exploration mode - I don't know. - Also you should be able to go through the gate itself, even if it's just starting at the SGC and going through to the planet where the mission is going to take place.You know a scenario could be: You are looking for a vaccine - go talk to Dr. Fraiser in the infirmary, bring the results to Carter -> Carter remembers (Jolinar) the Tok'ra could give some insight -> mission briefing -> dial tok'ra world -> pass through the gate - next mission starts -> find entrance to the tok'ra tunnel system -> tok'ra get suprisingly attacked - sneak out of the base.What I'm trying to say is - don't make it all about sneaking around, let players just walk/run around and complete objectives without having enemies around 100% of the time. I think the game has great potential, if they add more functions.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, play the demo first. The game is decent, but it's mainly stealth/real-time tactics, so maybe not for everyone, but i think it deserves a chance! While not perfect, technically the best stargate game in a long time, or ever? Well, the SNES Stargate was okay, yes I remember that, but it was hard as well. So, I was never a big big fan of stealth/infiltration games, and yet back in the day i was fascinated with the game Commandos. A friend had it, he let me try it, and I was terrible at it, but i thought that game was incredible.Fast forward to now, what is this, a Stargate SG-1 themed Commandos? Well I had to try it. I am not super patient, but my life changed when i noticed that you can actually quick save and quick load? Life changer truly. After that, the game slowly grew on me, because the save system will save your life. And the game is actually very helpful (too helpful?) and gives you info and tips constantly (but i also play on Easy hah). There are a couple of characters in this, with each their own specific skills. It's kinda fun sneaking around and picking these jaffas one by one.This isn't XCOM style, or real time strategy, or full action. I'ts real time tactics, and this game is in fact truly reminiscent of old "Commandos Behind Enemy Lines" games, or at least, how i remember them. And by the way, i heard that Commandos 4 is planned for 2024? Coincidence? Well, probably.I know that the game is currently facing a lot of, possibly undeserved, criticism for not being what some were hoping for. Tough crowd. But the game runs well, it's not terrible, the gameplay is a little bit niche for sure but this is a fair attempt at making a stargate game connected to the SG-1 lore, set between seasons 7 and 8. And if you have had any interest in Commandos style games, at any point, or stealth games with some leeway for action, then give it a chance maybe, even if you don't know stargate!A fair warning though : the game currently only offers 7 levels out of the promised 14. That's fine, the remaining 7 levels will arrive in a free update later. I don't usually like this kind of thing because the game is basically half incomplete at this time and it's not early access, but i wanted to support the game so i bought it right away.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a stealth game. A lot of people seem to have a problem with this, claiming that  stealth doesn't fit Stargate and its frankly pretty baffling. If you've actually watched SG-1, you'd know they do a lot of sneaking around (its a team of four after all). So it makes sense for the setting and the stealth here is well executed. Is this the best stealth game ever? No, and it doesn't match Mimimi's stealth strategy titles but this is a solid entry in the genre. If you are a Stargate fan that enjoys stealth then this game is great. The main negatives are 1. the story here is super lackluster and 2. the game is 100% on the easy side if your experienced with this genre. That said I've still had a great time with the game and I'm looking forward to future missions. Its a shame to see such idiotic reviews (being mad its a stealth game) tanking this game to mixed as that will likely hurt sales and reduce the chance of us getting another Stargate game, good job guys.Edit: Part 2 was just as enjoyable as part 1. The new character is a lot of fun to mess around with and the mission objectives in the second half are quite varied. Fair warning there are two timed segments but they are very easy and short, nothing to worry about. After experiencing the full story, I like what they were going for but I don't think they stuck the landing. As a huge Stargate fan, I enjoyed it for what it was but it wasn't standout. The lack of compelling characters really holds it back. Everything I said about the gameplay remains true in part 2, although there are some sections where they ramp the difficulty more, which was nice (I played on hard).

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: With what I've played so far it's a fun game and story in the Stargate universe, despite it being a tactical stealth game which I usually don't enjoy. Give the game a shot and have fun. Limited playtime review so far.Not my usual type of game play style but between the Stargate theme and the company that made it I was willing to give this a shot. It's a fun stealth puzzle game where you need to sneak around instead of going guns blazing. Even this season in the series we're totally out numbered and gunned so the stealth approach isn't that crazy. Would a X-Com style Stargate be great? Sure. Would a Stargate base management Exogate Initiative like game be great? Sure. Can we have a Stargate tactical stealth game like commandos? Sure, this is it and it's been fun so far. This is not your Escape From Tarkov, Red Dead 2 level of graphics but does it need to be? It makes no difference to me, and this game does look quite good. If you're a fan of the publisher and their games you understand the usual graphical level of their games and you know you don't need all the super shiny graphics to have a fun, deep game.  Is it silly that bad guys don't hear their comrades getting taken out 2 feet away? Calling off a search 2 min after a comrade was killed? Is it silly that after an arbitrary distance they can't partially or fully see you? Of course it is, but this is a game. If it was made to total realist levels it would be almost impossible and would exclude many players from playing. If you're a Stargate fan this is a fun adventure, so far, in the universe and I'm excited to see what comes next. Know what you're getting into and give the game a chance, especially if you want more content for the game, and maybe even more games in the franchise. Oh, and yes the game is split in 2, 7 mission segments, the second coming later in the year, but it's included free with the current 7 you get. You can check the game details and confirm for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, Stargate fans have a complete game in the franchise! Called “Season 1,” Stargate: Timekeepers may be a spark for reviving this beloved universe, hopefully paving the way for more games or even a new series.First off, I don’t usually enjoy tactical games; they tend to feel slow and repetitive to me. That said, I decided to play on “Story” mode, the easiest difficulty, hoping it would make the game more enjoyable. Unfortunately, it still felt a bit tedious, largely because of the game style and an assortment of bugs that kept popping up.One of the more annoying bugs came early in the game: tied-up enemies somehow escaped, forcing me to restart the level. After that, I chose to either hide or “zat-zat-zat” every enemy I encountered, which got monotonous quickly. Smaller bugs also affected character responsiveness—issuing commands too quickly caused characters to freeze until a quick reload.The first few levels, released almost a year before the rest of the game, felt disconnected from the Stargate world, aside from the characters. The environments seemed generic, which made it feel less like a Stargate experience. If I hadn’t been a big fan of the franchise, I might have quit after waiting nearly a year for more levels.Thankfully, things improved! The story involves a time-based adventure, though it was sometimes hard to follow due to fragmented scenes and timeline jumps between levels. By level 7, the game started to feel more like the Stargate I know, with familiar plot twists, intense moments, and an atmosphere that echoed classic Stargate elements. The levels were filled with Jaffa warriors whose predictable behavior evoked memories of SG-1’s victories over them.The level design involves some basic puzzles that are straightforward to solve. The AI often ignores any environmental changes, allowing you to sneak around and eliminate enemies one by one without them noticing a thing. While this makes the gameplay easier, it also reduces the challenge.For Stargate fans, Stargate: Timekeepers offers a nostalgic journey with familiar objects, decorations, and locations from the series. The environment evolves from generic to iconic, rewarding fans who stick it out to the end.For other players, if you can look past the glitches and rely on quick saves, there’s still quite a bit of Stargate charm to enjoy. It’s a small but memorable piece of the franchise, showing promise for what future Stargate games could achieve.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE after completing part 1 of season 1 (= the first 7 episodes, 7 more are supposed to be released later this year).I had lots of fun during the playthrough. If you like realtime tactics/stealth, this is a competent game. The levels offer a huge variety and often you can take slightly or noticably different paths. The characters all have different skills. I think hide and whistle (to lure enemies) by Max is most powerful. I hardly ever used my weapons. Looking at some videos, I think people can have very different playstyles and thus experiences. It is more intended to be played more or less stealthy, at least on normal and hard difficulty, because you don't have infinite ammo.People who say there is NO stargate, are wrong ;-)I really like the TV like recap and outlook at the beginning of every episode. Sometimes there are additional ingame cutscenes, too, and your characters talk on the radio. You unlock new objectives during an episode.Because it is a classic realtim tactics/stealth game, it includes (at least for me) lots of quicksave/quickload and the areas are pretty much like puzzles. If you are not familiar with the genre, both might be offputting. Try out the demo and see if you like the genre. If you don't like the genre, the game, in my opinion, won't be that much fun for you, even if you love Stargate. If you like the genre though, you are likely to have a good time :)---------------------------------------This is a temporary review after having finished 3 out of the currently 7 episodes (7 more will be delivered later this year). I have never really watched Stargate because at the time it was popular I hardly watched TV (time, voice dubbing). This means I can't say if something possibly is against the lore. I am here for the tactical gameplay, but the game actually makes me want to give the series a proper shot.Stargate: Timekeepers is a realtime tactics game with a big stealth element, meaning the enemies have vision cones. They can't really hear though, which can create slightly odd moments. The game is the same genre as Commandos, Desperados or Shadow Tactics. To be honest, it is beyond my understanding why ppl downvote Stargate simply because they don't like the genre.The game gives you some TV show vibes, in particular with the recaps at the beginning of episodes. There are also fully voice acted cutscenes and ingame cutscenes, also during the episodes. Graphics look pretty nice and you can and actually sometimes have to seemlessly rotate the screen. You can also zoom in and out. UI is clear und understandable. The map, also the minimap, has a lot of information (enemies, bodies, etc).Every mission you are put into a very different environment. And then you basically have to puzzle your way through to the objectives. Your characters have a ton of unique abilities and often you have to have them work together in order to progress. The different skillsets also mean you can take a unique approach for every situation/puzzle. In some episodes you can even go down totally different paths which adds to replayability. Also, there are special achievements for e.g. not triggering an alarm at all. I had one bug so far where the screen turned black but quitting the game and loading a savegame (you also have 3 rotating quicksave slots that you really should use) solved it.In my opinion (so far, after 3 episodes) Stargate: Timekeepers is a very competetent representative of the genre and I am having a lot of fun thus far, even with out a "Stargate bonus".I think the video-review by Bandanner is done quite well and does the game justice:
