_childDocuments_.review: This game has actively resisted every effort I've made to enjoy it. My main issues:I really wanted to play a beastmaster group with a lot of animals. Turns out that most animals are not worth their food cost. Most eat about 1.5 to 2 times as much as a human unit, and even though this is offset somewhat by them not needing wages, you will be eating town markets bare and chasing merchant caravans trying to buy/steal enough food if you want to have several animal squad members because apparently ponies can't graze and wolves and bears can't hunt or even say, get extra food from corpses (unless you invest in fairly high level perks that I haven't gotten to, suspect wouldn't be good enough, and would have to be taken in place of a combat-oriented perk for the animal). In combat, animals die more easily than human units because all except the pony can't wear armor, have similar or less health than most human units AND don't even go into a 'dying' state for one last chance to save them on hitting 0 health, they skip that and die outright. Even bears get wrecked by poison, fire, and bleed damage because those deal % of max health damage over time. So the one tanky animal can't tank in a lot of situations and eats as much as FOUR human units. I guess animals might work as expendable shock trooper type units but that isn't how I wanted to use them. You also can't capture ghost units (outside of one quest), which feels like a missed opportunity. Even outside of combat, animals don't seem to have any interactions with quests, they can't be entered in the arena, they don't have professions (professions give bonus attributes, so this further weakens animals in combat compared to human units), and with the exception of the pony they don't have any camp equipment. Their skills also can't be upgraded with the training books you can use on human units, and there don't seem to be animal skill books/trainers. Without saddle bags, only the pony has carry capacity (and saddle bags don't even add that much capacity). Apparently some of these things were different prior to a patch back in 2022. Animals didn't eat as much, could carry things, and could use skill books. If those changes were rolled back I guarantee I would like this game 5 times more.The difficulty scaling is way too aggressive if you set it to scale with your group. Like I was having Elder Scrolls Oblivion flashbacks aggressive. Every fight will wreck your armor and probably leave you with at least a couple of injuries as the fights get bigger, and even if you invest in knowledge and camp equipment to make repairing and healing more efficient you will need more and more resources to repair and heal after each battle as you go along. However, contract payouts don't seem to get much bigger so you end up with the same reverse difficulty curve Oblivion had where it's better to stay weak. Unfortunately unlike Oblivion there's no way to avoid leveling entirely and you need to recruit about ten or so human units to cover all the professions you need to get through quests, tombs, etc. so you can't stay as a tiny squad either. I HIGHLY recommend setting the scaling to 'region locked' so at least some areas stay manageable and you have places to go grind money and resources.Finally, and this is by far the worst issue, the fights all start to DRAG as you get further along, because there are too many units. You will probably have at least ten units or so because you have to cover most of the professions to be able to do quests/make items and you can pretty easily get to 20 units or more. Assuming the fight is about as difficult as the game thinks is should be (meaning you've set it to scale or are in a region that's about even with your group) the enemy will almost always slightly outnumber your group. Before you know it one round of a fight is taking 5 to 10 minutes and each fight is going several rounds. It started to feel less like a game and more like work tbh. This is somewhat alleviated by choosing 'region locked' scaling because at least the early areas will have small enemy squads and you can probably get strong enough that even some 'medium' regions' enemy squads go down pretty fast, but this obviously won't save the hard regions. I briefly wandered around a swamp region, and I have no idea if it's the hardest region or not but there were small armies around every corner on region locked. It was still better than EVERY region turning into that by level 6 though.EDIT: I played a bit more after the initial review with region locked scaling and a squad of five human units. I found out this was possible because you can actually change the profession of your units (I thought it was a permanent selection). However, the devs clearly didn't intend for you to change professions often because when you do you lose all progress towards the next level of the profession you switched out of. For example, if you want your Experienced Cook with 99 out of 100 exp to Journeyman Cook to switch to Angler, you can, but they will be back to 0 out of 100 exp to Journeyman Cook when they switch back to Cook (They will at least retain their Experienced rank instead of reverting to Novice, though). So if you want to manage all the professions with a smaller squad, you have to try to do activities in chunks - go around picking all the locks, mining all ore veins, etc. until you hit the next level of the profession, and then switching to something else to minimize exp loss. This gets old really fast. So the devs seem to really want to force you to get a bigger squad where each unit has one profession, regardless of how YOU want to play the game. Prefer having a smaller, higher-level squad you can invest in, customize, and maybe actually care about? Who can go fishing for an afternoon without forgetting everything they've recently learned about cooking? Too bad, the devs want you to have at least a dozen units and are willing to resort to artificial bs force the issue. It's a shame because the smaller battles were a lot more fun to play, at least for me, and they were still challenging because the number of enemies compared to my group was roughly the same, it just didn't take ten minutes to get through one round.Unfortunately I kept running into things like this. For some reason the devs really want you to play a very specific way, down to the size and composition of your squad, so this isn't really a sandbox at all. So many quests only have one way to finish them, or maybe two if you're lucky, even if there are alternatives that would make sense there're simply no options. Mechanics that might allow other playstyles are unfinished, broken, or got patched out/nerfed. The nail in the coffin for me was when a main quest in the Vertruse scenario outright broke, though. You are supposed to capture (kidnap, you don't get to choose your group's morality either) a specific unit. Well, I have chains in my inventory, the unit I'm supposed to capture has less than half health but more than zero and is engaged in combat with one of my units. When I move another unit into melee range no option to capture appears. This persisted through one save/reload and two battle restarts. So I guess the whole region scenario is now broken for me (or else the devs have failed to explain what I'm supposed to do). This is NOT a 1.0 release, no matter what the devs say. Almost half of the path perks are still blank and say 'coming soon' for crying out loud. Unless this game gets serious mod support to fix/finish it, I think I'm done.

_childDocuments_.review: This Isometric turn based action game takes place in an open world where you can decide to be good or evil if you wish. Crafting is a thing; You can do black smithing, thievery, fishing, and several other trades. You can build up a large group of companions who go with you everywhere, but you do need to pay people who you hire though, so you have to be careful about managing this properly. Additionally you can knock out the final enemy in a battle to take them as a prisoner. When you turn them in at the jail they reduce your suspicion meter. When you steal something your suspicion meter goes up and if it hits 100 you can get in trouble for having it maxed out. Even as bandits you need to choose carefully what you actually want to steal because the suspicion meter goes down at a fairly slow rate. Turning in prisoners is a great way to mitigate this. Rating: 10/10 I am not usually much a fan of isometric games but this one is pretty great. It has a cool original style and most importantly it's fun. I've been playing it in co-op with a friend and we have been enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but unfortunately it is a prime example of "A mile wide and an inch deep."I gave it some leeway in the beginning, thinking "Surely they will fix buggy or incomplete mechanics, surely they will flesh out the world and story more, surely....."If you look at this developers other games and the release schedule for DLC's on this game, its pretty clear what Shiro's intentions are with WarTales - create a base game just good enough to hook a cult following (done), then spam DLCs that should have been part of the base game at low enough prices people don't really consider whether or not its worth it (in progress). Look at Northgard having more than half of its content locked behind DLC, with a new DLC released every few months.Shiro games could be an absolutely phenomenal developer if they were only willing to take a little more financial risk for the benefit of their products. For example, when the first DLC got released for this game and I saw features that should have been part of the base game, and were clearly planned from the start of development, I put the game down and bought NOTHING ELSE for it. If, instead, the developer had completed the base game and fleshed out the world and story and not tried to sell me pre planned dlc, I would likely be hundreds and hundreds of hours in and buying any DLC they put out for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to stop playing this game around 10 hours ago, as I had reached the Early Access lvl-cap and thought to myself I should wait until the full game came out... Now, 10 hours later, I am still playing it because it's just so darn good! Damn you game!! :pReally deep combat with loads of different abilities. Turn-order and positioning is SO important, and you will often be forced to think wether you want be aggressive and go for a kill, or be defensive and use one of your characters action to nullify an opponent with a spearwall to stop them from moving or a shot from your archer to slow them down and stop them from being able to reach your warriors on their action.The story is pretty good too. Much better than what a game like this needs actually! It's fairly simple, but it takes some chances including a refugee-crisis as one of the main plot points, which I think is brave considering the current state of the world, instead of just going for traditional "good vs evil" stuff.Managing your troop of fighters work pretty well too, with food and wages being the main concern. There is also a morale system, but from what I've seen so far it needs a little more work as I was pretty much able to ignore it in my 32 hours of play.Crafting is solid. Nothing new, but it works.All your warriors are able to take secondary proffesions too. Everything from cook to smith to thief to alchemist to fisher and other stuff. Some of them are used for crafting, some are used for other stuff, but they all give a cool little extra dimension to each character, along with some minor buffs to different stats.TL:DR If you liked Battlebrothers, you will love this game! If you like tactical turn-based games with some management, you will probably also like it :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rather decent strategy RPG that I actually find very few gripes with. The graphics look very good, the music is nice and doesn't get on one's nerves when repeating, the combat system is challenging, makes one think about the gravity of every move made, and to me is very D&D-like (minus the dice rolling). Lastly, the open world aspect where you can go anywhere and do anything in any order as you progress is refreshing in a gaming epoch otherwise full of linearity.The only gripe in my 3 hours of play so far (as of Nov 7th, 2023) is that there really isn't a sufficient tutorial to get you started. 3 hours in and I'm still finding myself saying, "gee, THAT's how that feature works? Wish I'd known sooner." It's not too terrible of a setback but for people less acclimated to strategy games, it may be more annoying for them than it is for me lol.If I had a star-5 scale to rate it on, I'd give it a solid 4 out of 5 at this point, possibly higher if not for the annoyance of having to compensate for lack of feature tutorials. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best tactical RPG I've played I've played since DOS2. It takes the battle brothers formula, improves the combat, adds a story, and removes all the obnoxious RNG. There are no hit chances in this game, theres way less RNG when it comes to character development and recruitment while still retaining depth, and you aren't going to run into some magical witch who prevents you from... doing anything at all for 90% of the battle. The zone stories are all interesting enough to actually bother reading and thinking about, which is pretty much the highest praise you can give a game like this in terms of writing. Although I would like to see a sort of late game where you can revisit these zones to see the results of whatever choice you made. The only real downside now is a lack of content compared to other similar titles. It's still a solid game for EA, but with only three zones the game feels very small. If you're looking for a deep dive, this isn't quite there yet. It really just needs more regions, which are apparently coming soon.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot of potential in this title, but being able to become something great hinges heavily on the direction the developers take it, and there's no indication yet that it will go in a good direction purely based on how the combat encounters are currently designed. I've been burned by more than a few Early Access titles that failed to realize their hypothetical potential, and I can't recommend this game at face value.The combat difficulty is largely artificial at the time of this review. Basically every fight forces you to split up your team to be intermingled in nonsensical ways with the enemy forces and you are almost always outnumbered. Even if you successfully ambush an enemy, you start almost every fight with your team fractured and typically surrounded. Not to mention the weird arbitrary traps and such in every fight which barely accomplish more than being an incredibly minor boon at best, and a negligible annoyance at worst.Of course, the arbitrary and artificial combat setups seem like a shoddy attempt to make the combat actually challenging, as the AI is currently incredibly basic and predictable.Generally speaking fights come down to a grind of numbers, meaning you typically only lose fights because the enemy simply overwhelms you with sheer numbers and/or having vastly superior gear/levels, which is generally only an issue if you're trying to tackle the higher difficulty contracts too soon.I'd hope that this approach to setting up fights is discarded (maybe with the exception of cases where your group actually gets ambushed) after more work is done on the AI, but it remains to be seen how much the developer insists on arbitrarily forcing you into disadvantageous arrangements for your troops.The current economy of the game is also a bit... Questionable. The power level of the enemies you face in higher contracts jumps up dramatically if you try to take on a Hard contract, but the reward for the contract doesn't seem to match the increased danger involved. You can just take on Easy contracts and still get paid about 1/2 what a Hard contract pays for dramatically less effort, and in general a lot of the payment for contracts feels arbitrary and not particularly tied to the difficulty of the task.It also tends to be the case that you earn as much or even more money just from random looted trinkets and money from defeated enemies than whatever contract you're on pays, though that's unreliable income based on RNG. It seems a bit odd that random loot would factor in as such a big portion of your income compared to your payment for taking on dangerous work, but spoils of war as a supplement to direct coin payment isn't exactly unheard of, so it's hard to say this is really an issue.The Trade skill and Knowledge systems seem very promising, at least. They only need to expand them with more content, but even in their current state they are great secondary systems for expanding the abilities of your troop, upgrading gear, provisioning, even making extra money if you acquire excess resources.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that this game is just fantastic. Wartales is a mercenary, strategic, survival, rpg game with a turn-based combat. So it really doesn't have a pure linear story that you could expect from a rpg game. It has a regional stories when you advance through provinces, but the main experience is focused on your company.That makes it great and kinda make this game exceptional in my opinion. For me, this is pure tabletop/dnd experience that I always wanted from a video game.That being said, please remember that you are not buying AAA game. This is an indie title, so there are shortcuts or some minor problems(that will probably be fixed in following patches). Yet this game has something, the idea and execution of it is top notch in my opinion. Game worth it's price.Would recommend to every fan of turn-based strategies and crpg fans.

_childDocuments_.review: In the couple of hours I've played this, I am absolutely hooked.Customize your party and off you go. Combat is turn-based (Like Divinity or XCOM).Your party can learn specializations based on their class and additionally crafting professions. There are all kinds of wild random encounters to come across. Fought a pack of wolves, weakened one down, and captured it. _childDocuments_.review: A few years ago I played the demo for this game and it had potential to be a fun but it was very raw, janky and needed a lot of work but the diamond in that rough was a fun open world game about exploring and tactical combat. With the game being released I have to say that I am pleasantly surprised with how the game turned out.Wartales is a game with a lot of similarities to Expeditions: Conquistador and even a little of the Banner Saga.At the start of the game you decide what type of initial squad and backstory you want to go with like being a bunch of wanderlust farmers wanting to seek their fortunes to former soldiers running from the war to bandits who have escaped prison. The decisions at the start helps to ground you to the world and inspire you to role play as the type of squad you chose. You get to fully customise four characters like choosing the sex, appearance and character traits, one for free but if you want two positive traits you must pick a negative trait to counter balance it. For example with my squad I made a big viking dude with a shield and club who was strong of arm and very stout but his negative was that he ate more food than the others because he was so big and strong.The comparisons to Expeditions: Conquistador begin when you start moving around the map to explore and find new locations that have different quests and events tied to them as well as fight tactical battles battles on a square based grid (Expedition: Conquistador used a hex grid though) and begin to level up your companions and have some minor role play events with them as time goes on. Each area of the game has its own story/quest line and there are different endings for them. The first area of the game is a hot bed of refugees running from away from a war in another kingdom.The comparison to Banner Saga is that initial battles are very much you take a turn then the enemy takes a turn but unlike Banner Saga you are not punished for killing enemies and as such you get more turns to use. The battle system also allows you to chose which character to use on your turn so for example you wanted to start combat with your big shield dude you could run them in first turn or you could use your archer and shoot at the back line on the first turn. This is different from most tactical games because in those games you have to take turns in a certain order but in this game you can chose the character you really want to move instead of having to wait till the end of the turn to use that really slow character.The game is very fun to play and enthralling; it is the little moments that help make this game like when my archer Erin kept accidentally shooting the de-facto captain of my bandit group in the back and while camping he tried to have her kicked out but the other bandits said it was a mistake obviously and to forgive her just for her to shoot him in the back again in the very next encounter and for the de-factor captain to get a paranoid trait after it happened.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Tactical RPG's like Final Fantasy Tactics as the gold standard.. This game is quite good!Frustratingly difficult at times. Normal mode seems pretty tough to start, 30hrs in and I'm considering I should have started a game on easy to get the hang of things. I can't tell if the enemies match your level.. I've been blown out of the water a number of times from hard enemies, or large squads, even as I level up. But then I did find a few low level enemies too. I would lean on yes 'the game matches your level, enemies get harder as you level up', but can't confirm 100%. It's driven by a fairly tight attrition mechanic, where your squad have wages and food requirements. This drives you to do tasks/missions to stay on top of the upkeep required to maintain the squad. No real main story line, but there are 'factions' that it looks like you can go further down their paths (make friendly with one will put you against another). I think there is some imbalance in the classes, but there's a good support mechanism that makes every move count and even weak units contribute. And sometimes you need to level up a new recruit. There's no wiki for the game yet, so it's like the early 2000's when you pick up a game and have to discover it yourself with help from your brother / friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: It is a nice game, but I can't really recommend it. It has too many small problems that sum up and cloud your game experience. I like parts of it, but as a whole after 13 hours I have no drive to explore the game further.It has a nice idea and many small cogs you can tune. I like the crafting part and the overall posilbiity to customize your group. I like the graphics. The first combats are interesting. The mini games are short and simple enough to not be a pain a few hours in and are a good alternative gameplay. There are many small stories keeping the word alive.My major points are the the controls, the lack of depth in gameplay and its generic world. There are multiple weapon types, multiple skills and many levels. I played the first region and a part of the second and I mostly encountered humans. The combat is mostly the same without interesting twists. You move, you hit, you do damage, you repair, you repeat. Some parts of ranged, most of it is melee and not really feeling impact full. I was bored playing the next one because there was no tension. I could loose someone, but most of the time my group never received any damage.The controls are a big problem. The pathfinding in the overworld is bad, I got stuck on a mountain cliff multiple times. The camera is not really helpful. In the overworld is tends to always be in the wrong place. In combat it tries to switch to another person automatically, but doesn't cancel when you want to move in the process. You want to move a unit, but don't know if its in range? Rightclick on the ability to see the range. Why is this not the default? Sometimes I moved without getting in range because it was not clear. Some enemies are auto counter. I can only find this out when I inspect the enemey OR after I started a multi attack... At the start of the combat your group is randomly distributed and I need a minute or two to sort my group before the battle. Played with 10 members, can't imagine the chaos with more.My last problem was the very generic medieval world. There are some "misterios" elements like tombs to explore or rat plagues, but the first biggger encounter is a generic and confusing refugee crisis? Most of the game are human problems, but nothing exceptional or a deep story. Many small stories, self contained. But no real identity with a NPC or a goal to achieve. I wasn't interesting in exloring the world because it looked generic. The three towns were looking the same.All in All: Game with potential, but it is missing a unique character. It presents the standard stuff, but with very little own.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully unique game that has come so far since early access. Very fun and engaging mechanics, from combat tactical choices that make or break a fight to balancing your load, loot, professions and the quests. The leveling system is very engaging, I love leveling my unit as well as my characters. Definitely going to be ending up with a couple hundred hours on this!

_childDocuments_.review: The game delivers exactly what it promises (rare thing these days). A nice experience, simple, but complex, adjustable difficulty at any time (note that if you find it too difficult on "easy" or "experienced" mode, it is not the game's fault, just grow your skills and reasoning). Also, no woke nonsense, just pure, relaxing, high quality escapism. I've seen comments that the game does not provide enough help, tool-tips, and no tutorial per-se.  In my view, this is not true. All the clarification you need are to be found in the game. Just have patience and explore (UI and/or the in-game World). Also, the fact that you are not suffocated by hand-holding is extremely refreshing. You've been given a nice World,and you are free to engage it and experience it exactly as you wish!

_childDocuments_.review: A challenging, open-world, turn-based RPG that lets you explore at your own pace. And the map ISN'T randomly generated, thank goodness. I'm having a lot of fun exploring and leveling up my party. I can easily see putting dozens, or even hundreds, of hours into this.Some issues I've had:- Sometimes when you reload, your save gets disconnected from the current game, so you need to make a new one. Not a huge issue, but weird.- Being able to randomly shoot your allies by accident isn't very fun. Every time this happens, I just restart the battle.- Pathfinding on the map isn't great. And I really wish there was an option to click places on worldmap and head in that direction.

A few pathways up mountains are also a bit difficult to navigate in places. I am sure I probably have missed a few because I gave up trying.

_childDocuments_.review: When you start a game you have a choiceregion locked meaning enemies lvls and party sizes are fixedorenemies lvles and party sizes are always scaling to your lvl and party sizeI have chosen region locked first and I started building my party, recruiting new ppl and catching animals, quickly I outnumbered any enemies by 3 to 1, which was very boring.So I restarted a game and chosen scaling and did the same, recruiting and catching animals, enemy party sizes were scaled to my party size, so each fight was 30min long 10 vs 12. This is where I had the most fun, it was challenging and satisfying to win a fight. One mistake and your mercenary was outnumbered 3 to 1.Unfortunately there are too many fights in a game so this becomes a slog quick, this took too much time.I wondered would it be as fun if I restarted a game and chosen scaling again, but limited myself to small party of 5 mercenaries? The answer is no, the game is too easy again + you have to do weird things like have prisoners to fill professions(why can't you recruit civilians? :( ).scaling mode with big party has the most potential, but fighting 15 boars get boring quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lacks any tutorial. If you are a fresh player to this genre or at least not well versed into this kind of strategy genre...you gonna have a bad time.Wartales is a bit of mix of real time strategy with turn based cobmbat. In fact it play a lot of like old Fallout games. Problem is, while old Fallout games lack official tutorial also the UI was so intuitive that you had no problem figuring everything on the fly. Wartales...its not like that. The UI is very, very confusing. Which is kind of weird actually, because the look of UI is actually very non intrusive. There is no plethera of icons, there is no constant pop up infos, in fact it is build on the way that the only way you would know how to use it is...if you build it yourself. The Guild 3 suffers from same damn problem.And this coming from a man who figured out old Fallout inteface on first go despite the game being same age as me. Kenshi too lacks official tutorial but, that it still have few lines that pop up in beggining to inform you of the basic concept. Wartale, has NONE and i man 0 as 0. The game makes it clear enough that you can figure out the crew build/class archetypes but anything more than that apperently was a NO NO for devs who did not gave a single F about explaining anything to you.If you want tutorial go and watch lets play series. It will take you 2 hours to start figuring out anything of any base value.Iam just lucky that i did not went over 2 hours window with it. So yeah, i refunded it. Which in a way pains me because the rest of art style is soooo good. The world, the characters, the overall color pallete. Everything is so down my alley that this was by far the most heavy hearthed refund i ever requested.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a fun game. I haven't played a lot of turn based games lately, but the combat is OK. The quests are doable most of the time. I'm currently on the second area.Some nitpicks:Micromanagement is getting to be an issue. Keeping up with everyone's potential equipment upgrades is annoying. You have to unequip the item from the merc then have your smith see what can be upgraded. The more mercs you have, especially when you get above 10, the longer this process takes. Personally, I liked how mount and blade let you equip a few companions and then the other soldiers could be upgraded as a class without individual equipment decisions. Maybe if you had an armorer to "recommend" upgrades and you could click yes or no. Similar with cooking. why do I have to make all the decisions. Autocook for 12 sounds like a good addition. Similar to inviting people to your house, having 4 people in your party is fun. Having 14 is a major commitment. Especially, if it's just you doing all the work. Overall, worth the money if the game is on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game. Took a little bit of figuring out and am still learning stuff as I go along. Equipment tiers seem to power spike units, if some units are below the level thresh-hold to use certain stuff they feel kinda under-powered. Combat is fun and world feels alive with complex decisions allowing you to direct your mercenary group into whatever alignment you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but its nothing alike to Bannerlord or Battle Brothers to those who are comparing it.Its more like a puzzle game where you have limited resources and time to complete set objectives in a almost entirely static world. The game uses self contained scenarios to tell a story, in which you usually get a A or B choice (for example the first scenario makes you choose 5 times whether to side with bandits or refugees for the main story). After that you're done and get the next scenario to do. There are some random elements, like RNG patrols or bandits, but 90% of the world is static. So dont expect infinite replayability like you might expect from BB or Bannerlord. Unlike those this game has a set start and finish which IMO is a major benefit as it gives a solid world to explore and experience multiple times.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying it so far. The basic mechanic of locking melee combatants into fighting eachother was a genius idea in my opinion. A lot of reviews spoke about the Tavern DLC. Maybe that is even more fun than what I am doing now, but I've been having a lot of fun so far. The story seems to be little small stories for each area, which you decide the outcome of. I like it, I don't need a big giant story to keep me interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: Really good sandbox CRPG that you may grow bored of as time goes on. The major gripe I  have is that battles can become incredibly long and boring, especially when it's something like 20 vs. 20.I liked the game overall though, and the dark, gritty tone. Yes, unlike many mainstream RPGs, you can be make your band of mercenaries into really bad guys if you want, ambushing merchant wagons and keeping prisoners. Or you can be noble, chivalrous mercenaries. It's up to you.The game is separated by regions, each with a mini-campaign and sidequests. The story is nothing to write home about, but exists. I 100%'d the campaigns and the majority of sidequests in 140 hours. I did not play the DLCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm, this is a weird one.In the beginning you are starved of gold, food, repair materials and medicine. Usually you would overcome these issues as time progressed, but they persist here.You can get to a point where you have a decent amount of gold, but as soon as you want to stock up on the above necessities and unit / gear upgrades you're back to being broke.Almost every battle is the same and there is a lack of enemy diversity. What makes this worse is that battles take ages and that gets worse the more mercenaries you recruit, as the enemy numbers just scale. The perma-death mechanic is really out of place here, it needs to be saved for hard core mode or it needs to be an option.Near the end of a 40 min battle, if one of your units randomly dies due to random AI, you will be forced to start the battle again. If you choose to take the loss, you can spend hundreds of gold recruiting a new merc who is half the level of the rest of your party and completely useless for tens of hours until they catch up. Wait, what? You managed to avoid any one dying on your third attempt at the 40 min battle - well now all your units are wounded and have no armour, making the battle a net loss anyway. Back to town again I guess.I really want to like this game, but I kind of feel like I've wasted both my time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: Just over 20 hours in, and it has been a fun ride so far. Could do with more of a tutorial or more tooltips, so if you are just starting I would watch a couple videos on the basic systems and what resources do as you will have to make some choices when you start that will affect the early game at least.Overall, this a good base that has a lot of potential. I am excited to see where it goes between the devs and what the modding community can do to expand on it. Most of my complaints are minor things, like the camera being a bit wonky, not being able to see anything when walking through the woods, and not having a dedicated quest log. The pros far outweigh these. The combat is fun and requires some thought and planning. A lot of freedom to play the way you want as far as what you focus on. The crafting is pretty good, the mini games seem a bit finnicky at times but having a chance to get extra resources or better equipment is cool. 7/10 as it stands, I could see it becoming a 9 or 10 down the road.
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great game. This is EXACTLY what I was looking for. I wanted something similar to Divinity: Original Sin 2 and Baldur's Gate 3, but less "focus" required, if you know what I mean. I work a lot and I do not have dozens of hours to invest into those games regularly (only when I'm off) so I was really looking for a game that I could lose myself in for a few hours, that isn't incredibly deep, and/or easy to follow and this is DEFINITELY it. I'm over 20 hours in and I feel like there is still so much to learn/do, but I don't feel as overwhelmed as I do in those grander RPGs and I can pick this game up and put it down whenever I'd like with no consequence.Cannot speak highly enough about this game.. it's like they could see inside my head when they made it. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is smooth fluid and i enjoy the 3D dioramas they do for inside of buildings the relationships and permanent character traits you unlock for your permanently dying characters Allows for a deep investment into their wellbeing and all of the systems they have are well fleshed out and its fights are balanced. I'm persaona;lly working to 100% this game because it has been well worth both my time and money

_childDocuments_.review: This may sound strange and I'm definitely sure that the HC fans of DnD (paper and pen) will not agree on this one with me, but for this ca. 35 hours of playing Wartales, this is a 1-on-1 DnD on screen can be played by myself. You have a sandbox in front of you, free to roam wherever you want in a (relatively) big open world, with no clear main quest at the start, slowly finding the gameplay roadmaps... perfect. Planning to buy and manage a tavern, want to go sailing and fight pirates... I think I just scratched the surface of this great game. I'm not too fond of the time that will lost on this one :(

_childDocuments_.review: I have recommended this game as I'm sure it has potential to be a good, if not great, game with plenty of depth and longevity. However it still needs work. The graphics are reminiscent of RPG games of the late 90's. To be frank they just don't cut it in today's gaming world. While the cut scenes are ok the basic game interface and overall look is best described as 'muddy'. I play on a highish spec laptop and the graphics just aren't clear. The whole thing looks as if it is covered in a layer of fog.As for the text, even on the largest text settings it is mostly unreadable. The mini games, of which i have discovered fishing and lock picking. Fishing is ok the first few times but i suspect will be extremely boring after a while. Lock picking is virtually impossible, given how often the picks break and with no real indication as to where the sweet point is. Then on top of that the  rewards are not worth the effort.Where is the fast travel to already discovered points. I don't want to spend 10 minutes clicking along a road to get back to a point i discovered hours before!!!I will give it another 10 hours or so, I suspect, but unless something revelatory appears i doubt if i will see the end graphics (if there are any)
_childDocuments_.name: Wartales

_childDocuments_.review: In short: Pro: Immersive, well designed, stableCon: repetitiveIn not so short: I like the game. Don't get me wrong. Wartales is pretty much what I expected. And if I am focussing on the not so great part of it, it is for potential buyers to make an informed decision.You are a band of mercenaries looking for a fortune. That's the story. The smaller stories, the scenarios in each of the games provinces are independent and you can choose if you want to play them in any order (it's a setting in the options). That gives the game a bit more of a replay value than it would have otherwise. Because to be honest: It gets a bit stale after 50 hours or so but you can always take a break from playing it for a week or so or start a new group that focusses on a different aspect of the game. My guess is that this game will entertain me for at least 100 hours before I stop playing it at all.I basically hoped for a bit more depth and character development but all in all I would recommend the game. Strongly so if it happens to be on sale.

Trade is a little too lucrative later on, the traits might be better reduced to 5% reduction in cost and increase in value but that's just me. I do have a few gripes about it though... these are not game breaking annoyances though so I very heartily still recommend it.1) I find it very weird that the towns and most businesses are run by women and mercenaries can randomly have camp events that tread on their 'preferences' in the bedroom. Not a fan because it doesn't fit the time period/ genre very well. They've interjected these agenda's into a lot of games lately and I'm tired of it. Obviously the developers are either fearful of the whole ESG system and are bending over the sink and taking it up up the... well, you know what I mean. Or they are a very 'diverse' office that feel they must interject everything with the 'MESSAGE' and you become an -ist or a -phobe to say anything against it.2) Just not a fan of the ancient ruins puzzles and runes minigame. Just a personal gripe.3) there is a very clear lack of combat map variety. you end up seeing the same ones over and over and over again. also, the random bear traps make very little sense, as do the spears. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. However, there are a few small things I'd like to point out that if changed could make the game so much better.1. ScalingI know a lot of the negative feedback from other users has been the scaling. I never knew how overwhelmingly negative people feel about scaling in games. I'm personally a fan. I love a game that continues to give me a challenge no matter how strong I get. There are in my opinion, three ways you could deal with this. a. Have scaling be a togglable option in the main menu options or when selecting any new game.b. Tie scaling to areas. As in, the area you start in is scaled to an easy level, and every area you unlock after scales up in difficulty the farther into the game you get.c. Tie scaling to your progress in each areas storyline. As in every time you complete a quest that advances your area progress (purple bar) the world around you gets stronger. Honestly, I think option a. should probably be done no matter how they handle this issue as it is never a bad thing for a game to have more ways to customize or tailor it to your liking. But I look forward to seeing how the developers end up handling this. 2. Targeting abilities. I have a love/hate relationship with the enemies whose only ability is a targeting ability that only executes on their next action. This can 100% always be avoided by anyone who has any sense what-so-ever. It is just too easy to avoid which means I can ignore those units almost completely until the end of the fight. Now, that is nice at times when you find yourself in a tough battle and can ignore a unit or two instead of being overwhelmed and killed. Still, I feel like this should be changed so that if you do not move before the end of the round, they get to use their attack if you try and move out of range on the next round. That way you have to be careful to not allow them to target a unit who has already used their turn on the current round if you don't want them to get hit next round. But even if you do, you could still use other units to try and kill the enemy before he gets the attack off. 3. Archers firing flaming arrows onto of themselves after they are engaged. This just feels weird to me, no other units get to use abilities while engaged and it just seems strange that they suicide themselves. SPOILER ALERT4. The quest where you are commissioned to capture slaves in trade for wood. I'll avoid names and locations in to create fewer actual spoilers.Please adjust the time allowed for this or turn off the need to turn in a slave every day after your first. It is fine to require you capture someone in 1 day as an initial requirement, but afterwards it's pretty lame to have to turn in another slave every day after. I mean, you could get completely overrun with wood this way. I mean, you could always sell the extra but it's just weird to me that you basically have to kill your associates if you ever want to end the endless cycle of attacking refugees and turning them into slaves. If you want to make this a challenge and give a negative to choosing this option, perhaps require 3-6 slaves turned in before you are allowed to ignore it for a time. If you want the quest to have an end, maybe include an option for them to come attack you if you don't turn in a slave for a week on the grounds that they want to get rid of loose ends. To me, it just felt really odd and immersion breaking to turn in a slave, head off to the other side of the map to complete other quests and get chased down and attacked the day after by an enemy claiming I never turned in a slave as agreed. I did, just not a second one the next day. 5. RecruitsI think there should be a way to recruit one of the starting choices, take them away from town, and let them die or kill them yourself and get back your money. This could come with some suspicion increase if you want. it would just be nice to have a way to get recruits you don't want in your troop to leave so you can have better options to recruit.6. HappinessI think there has to be a way to include happiness and not have it feel so weird. If you are paying your wages, feeding your troops meat every day, and not losing battles, I don't think you should have units abandon you just because the troop size is too large. I'm totally behind happiness dropping if you lose fights, aren't paying them, or aren't feeding them anything but bread for days on end. By all means, make a requirement to diversify their diet or even let them sleep in an inn every so often. Even possibly visit a town, give them leave, or have some "companionship" in a tavern. You know, let them spend that money you keep paying them for their work. I'm still exploring the world but felt it was about time I wrote down some feedback on the game. I've been waiting for it's release every since the demo dropped and have been very happy with it despite these small issues. I look forward to the dev team making this game even better than it currently is and can't wait for future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a brutal, never ending war of attrition. X-com style turn based combat, combined with a Mount and Blade style management sim, this manages to combine the 2 in a way that enhances both. You will spend hours completing garbage missions for tiny amounts of gold, killing pigs and selling what you don't eat just to get ahead. You'll finally crack a huge bounty and break even, only to lose half your squad to  the monsters in the dark.This game has a shocking amount of content, with a surprising amount of variety. 10 second mini games are used in conjunction with a job system to keep things fresh - I had a lot of fun with fishing and blacksmithing in particular. The tomb raiding was also freaking incredible. The game stayed fun for much longer than it should have, if I'm honest. The combat has enough evolving depth to keep you interested, but you'd better really like the combat because that's most of what you'll be doing to fill your time.On that note... The combat scaling in this game is a touch unfortunate. I don't actually enjoy the combat enough to justify having a fight every 15 minutes against 20 pigs for no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reason. After the first 5 they end exactly the same way - an autoresolve feature would be greatly appreciated. Knock 150 armour off my troop and let me get on with my adventure please, I've killed Babe about 900 times. PETA has been sending me warning letters and they're starting to get... aggressive.At the moment, this game has about 2 music tracks. They're inoffensive, mostly, although the battle music does occasionally annoy the ♥♥♥♥ out of me. Near as I can tell it's on a loop, but restarts if you get to a specific stage in the battle (essentially when the enemy is nearly routed). Occasionally, I have made an attack thinking I was in this stage, only to realise the music baited me into killing myself. So. Learn from my dumbassery. There's also no voices, although occasionally you will hear 1 or 2 random women doing battle cry's in combat. which is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ weird. It seems to be exclusively 2 women, and I don't think I've heard a guy yet, so that's... a thing.The storytelling in this game is OK. It's not stellar - I'm not super invested in the lore. I wish I had more choice, honestly. Sometimes it feels like the game is letting me do whatever the hell I want and still get paid, other times I feel a bit railroaded. Still, the actual story that matters to ME is the tale of my troop, a living example of the Ship of Theseus. Sure, everyone who set out with me died horrifically along the way, but the troops still going! We've lost men to the plague, wolves, whatever the ♥♥♥♥ is in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ temple and, on one occasion after I got desperate and stole enough food for the group to eat, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ guard. You can save and restart frequently in this game. The menu has 3 different options for resetting (load, load from beginning of the battle, and load from town). I think that, if you do that, you're robbing yourself of the chance to experience the story of your troop. Death and failure are a part of this game. They're what makes it worth experiencing. Don't rob yourself of the joy of the adventure by constantly resetting.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect example of a game you can play while watching Twitch, Youtube, or Movies on Plex while you play. Or what I call: "ADD Games". Sometimes I just want to watch a movie or TV show and play a game that won't matter if I stop when a good scene comes on.I do not know what has happened to me in this game. I first booted it up, got absolutely slaughtered got mad, and quit. Then I came back, and followed what someone on the Community Hub told me to do. Now I am clearing my 3rd area, trying to do everything possible and beating those dirty Champions. I thought "Okay, this is it I guess..." and then .....I got into the Skills/Trades. Realised the reason I was losing is because I was playing and equipping my units all wrong. Each has a specific role it fills, which is obvious, but when you are peasants. Heres a tip if you are a dumbdumb like me and don't read: "You always have your Polearm users are range for double damage".  My strategy for most fights is to engage all range and "Experienced" fighters. After that, you can have fun with your Rangers, Archers and Sword-masters. Each "Shield" variant can also use a 2-hander. I prefer shields and having one sword-master with a 2-hander. It's fun! You engage, and then backstab them (Works on any class).The Tradeskills are amazing. So much depth, and their mini-games are considerably easy but also add a "fun factor" to  doing it. I don't know if its desirable, but I have one of every tradeskill and any new Companions I want will "learn" from them and boost their Tradeskill Level gains. If you like the Tradeskills, a majority of your time on the "Map" will be running off the apth to get them. You WILL need Wood, and you WILL need Iron in the beginning. Make sure you have a Tinker to dissemble all found weapons for components to make your own.Each area has a "Story" and its not entirely in-depth, and you may find yourself skipping the talking just to get back to the action, and thats okay. The stories are not hard to comprehend, and if you don't want to search for them, you can pay Influence in the Taverns to get "leads" on them and have them show up for you on the map. For every "task" there is a way to spend influence to either speed it up, bribe, or get information so you don't have to explore.There is so MUCH here that I could keep writing. I am absolutely blown away by how much content, how much fun I am having, and how hard it can be. I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys TBS and RPG's.Oh, did I forget the Tavern DLC? Pirates? War Pits? Oh gosh my friend, there is just too much to speak on.Tavern DLC will make the immediate game easier because if you run out of money, you can take funds from the Tavern to pay your Mercs. But the Tavern has its own little stories and it is fun to know that things you do in the Main Campaign, will change up the tavern and offer more and more choices. I am on Tavern #3 and they just get bigger, allowing for more people, allowing for more money, and having chances of finding recipes you wouldn't find otherwise.I have no ventured into the Pirates DLC but my friends tell me It is awesome. The reviews are "Mixed" on the DLC's but its simply because it makes the main game easier, but is that so bad? The game can be very challenging and having some lee-way is nice.War Pits is not out, but is coming soon.Thjis game will suck you in, and not let you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Wartales is a solid 7.5/10 game. It's got ideas in it that I absolutely adore, that I would love to take and put into another game.I've played 70 hours, and not completed the game, haven't even really done both DLC's because the ship one is for level 10 and I'm only level 8 and levels make a big deal here (there is another way to adjust levels, but this is the one I went with as I like having a feeling of progression). The reason I'm only level 8 is because I avoid combat as much as possible because it is unfortunately a chore to me now. Each combat plays out mostly the same, there are 10+ enemies, alongside my 20+ squad. The rounds therefore take forever because the AI's decision making takes longer than I do and barely do anything. Some of my characters are overpowered, so why not turn up the difficulty? Because other characters are weak simply because they are a level below. Maybe this game is meant to be more Battle Brothers with more unforgiving combat but I like keeping people alive. It's what I do.So why do I give this a positive after that long rant? Because for the first 50 hours I had a blast. I loved the tavern DLC, I wish it was more drawn out in fact. Sadly didn't get to experience the ship stuff. But I love a lot of the parts of this game. It made me feel like a group of people building a mercenary squad.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game, build with many additional mechanics which keep things fresh - almost, but not quite enough for 120 hours I had to spend to complete most quests in 5 regions.Now I understand why this game took so long to develope, to the point where I thought it to be vaporware at some point: they put every additional mechanic they could think of in. Resource gathering mini-games, crafting mini-game, fishing mini-game, cooking, puzzles of several kinds, treasure hunts, relationships, trading, arene combats and even rugby. That's not couting DLCs, which add even more. This approach kind of remind me of a JRPG, or a mobile game, where new activities are introduced over the course of the game to keep it from getting boring. And it succeeds - for the most part. WarTales would be a genius 80-hours game, but at 120 houts it took me to complete most of it (without DLCs) it's still a bit too much: by the 4th region I was not looking forward to combat any more, and character development slowed too much. Still, for the most part it was very enjoyable, and I recomend it to all lovers of tactical games.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a band of mercenaries making their way across a beautiful isometric overworld; moving from town to town, taking on quests, camping etc while managing resources for fighting and travelling. The battle system is decent turn based combat on a flexible grid system. Each class of mercenary has a skill tree, levels, attributes, traits & professions (which allow them to do things like tinker or cook, and give them combat bonuses). Line of sight also actually matters; I shot my own rogue in the back with my archer by mistake. And you can rename characters, which is always fun.- In combat, instead of it going Ally 1, Ally 2, Enemy 1, Ally 3, it goes "any of your units", "Enemy 1", "any of your units", "Enemy 2" etc, so you get lots of control over things like focus fire or making the most of where an enemy is at that moment, rather than in some games where you can only delay your character's turn.- You can customise your units' appearance and name them- The engagement mechanic is really nice. If you attack a unit, you become engaged with it. This enables backstabbing, and opportunity attacks if one of you leaves. It also ties into other combat abilities.- Units take more damage if they're surrounded- Everyone can be inspected- Sometimes you get finisher "cutscenes" where you see your character end an enemy- Status effects like mud, poison, slow, burning- Environmental effects: lightning, rock falls- Everything is voice acted- Your characters unlock more traits over time based on what happens in combat- Each character can have one of 8 professions for crafting and gathering- Occasionally when resting, small events happen with your companions, like getting sick or someone thinking a new companion doesn't fit in, then you have 3 choices of how to react, with different outcomes, sometimes needing items for special outcomes- There's a system whereby every new thing you do earns you knowledge (like discovering places, or creating an item for the first time). Knowledge can be spent on perks or crafting recipesIn addition to knowledge, there are also 4 main paths. Each path has a set of challenges. Completing challenges fills the path progress bar, which unlocks new kinds of perks- There are old ruins to explore. Fights in these ruins are pitch black, and it matters if your characters are holding torches. Fire also lights up the area and reveals nearby units- After 10 hours in the first zone and doing some reading, it looks like the game doesn't change - new regions are just more of the same. Given that's the case, it's kind of entertaining, but way too long and repetitive- Don't get me to make permanent game-changing decisions before telling me how the mechanics work. How am I supposed to know if -1 carrying capacity is a lot, or if -1 happiness when resting matters?- Lacking in tutorials. Valour points unexplained. No idea when units get healed- Lag between when you use abilities and when they happen. For example, using Encouragement - my warrior shouts, then 3 seconds later my allies gain the effect- After a fight, you're given the option to repair one person's armour in exchange for one Raw Material. - Materials cost money, and it repairs 10 armour points. Id' like to maximise how much repair value I get, but the game doesn't show you how much armour you're missing on that screen, so it will eat up your materials- People with first aid can't heal themselves- If you accidentally sell something, you have to buy it back at full price- You can give ranks to members of your party, like assigning a captain. That's great, but the game doesn't tell you what that does. I had to google the fact that it gives them a new ability to use.- You can sort the inventory, but you can't filter it - which makes it difficult to see how much food you're carrying- All the wikis are out of date. None of them mention the Pugilist class- Although the game appears to be about adding more companions and growing your party... there's literally no upside to doing so. Having more people means more gold expenditure and more food consumption. Battles add more enemies if your party gets larger, and fewer if you don't, which means there's absolutely no point in it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adventure game. You control your group of adventurers on quests of various kinds. Or you can simply be a trader and walk goods back and forth between cities. It is a manager game and a questing game. You can even knockout the bad guys and take them to prison for good rewards (and you should, it helps pay your groups wages). You can capture wolves or even boars to fight on your team. The side gathering skills like fishing are not complicated, they just add a bit of that you need to catch it to eat it thing.  Stuck on a mountain path and want a short cut to the road? They even put pitons into the game that remain in place for you to use later. Be warned though, this is not an action packed thriller, it is a management game about questing. Pay your group, feed your group, earn funds, capture bad guys, deliver goods between towns, and hey, even maybe even help to overthrow a mayor. It is a relaxed atmosphere with enough challenge to keep you up late at night to keep you grinding. Just one more quest, then off to bed. Not.

_childDocuments_.review: You have an employer perspective. Your business is managing mercenaries, paying them wages, managing resources and logistics. Tavern DLC allow to also manage your own tavern while camping. All good until the game begin to force private relationships on your business. And there is no option to turn it off or skip. You're forced to solve both hetero, ♥♥♥♥ and zoophile relationships. You have a horse by default and eventually someone announce their love to it... Where is zoophile tag, if this is intentional? :)Also, the game favour female gender everywhere. All village leaders are female. All mercenary quest handlers are female. The majority of quest NPCs are female. And often 3/3 recruits sitting in taverns are female. Its faster to delete 50h save file than to recruit a new team with features you prefer or would like to try. Recruits change only once in 2-3 ingame days. Maybe you also need to travel between districts to trigger it. There is no customisation past the first 4 character creation screen, and those 4 characters are not fully customisable despite that you can replace everyone past the creation screen. Why not allot player to fully customise at least the first 4 characters? You can pick colours for clothes, but clothes you smith later do not maintain the colours you picked... Why allow to customise colours in the beginning? There are many weird design choices that can create false impression that the game offer more features than it has.Devs are pushing DLCs instead of polishing the base game, so I do not expect anything to change. If you have other RPGs to play, I advise to hold back from this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick verdict:Initially thought this game was super easy and repetitive and was giving it a thumbs down, until someone on the forum suggested I check the option to where the regions are pre generated with enemy levels and they do not scale with your war band.  Once I started a game with this on hard/hard it became really fun and a real nail biter.  It is extremely difficult, especially early on with these settings so those players that like a challenge and enjoy running from fights you know you cannot win will want this on for sure.Having lots of fun playing the game, even in early access which I tend to avoid like the plague.Pros:Lots of classesTons of skills and abilities you can learn to personalize your companyGood crafting options it seems likeGood graphics/immersionGood selection of jobs/quests to choose from but again doesn't compare well to the challenge of battle brothers which is obviously very much in this space tooCons:Combat could use some improvement as terrain has minimal impact and the load out of your guys is not very customizable. Doesn't seem to be very much you can buy weapon wise from the stores so crafting a must which may be a pro depending on how you like to playNot a huge fan of the pre generated world as everything seems kind of genericCombat system needs to glean from agmes like battle brothers or xcom but the potential is thereAll the shops and what not seem a bit repetitive because of the auto generated world formula but not a huge deal since combat is at the heart of a game like thisConclusion:If you like your games easy you might enjoy the combat but even then it seems super repetitive.  Hopefully the dev makes some easy changes to the combat system to improve it because the potential is there for everything else.  I definitely plan to re-evaluate this game after it is finished and released.

_childDocuments_.review: Update:  With the release of v1.0, this game is even more impressive - this is tireless and outstanding work on the part of the devs, and it shows.  While many of us have played games of this nature before, this one has taken the time to really nail down the details - the things that I've so often complained about in other such offerings.  One of my crew dies in battle... but I get to retrieve their gear to use for other companions, yes, THANK you.  A full 360 degree view both on the travel map and in battle, intricate and beautiful turn based battles, a sandbox layout where you can get your ass handed to you if you so desire, and a wide variety of ways to accomplish your goals.While I'd love more character customization, and perhaps some refined dialogue from the NPC's, there are so many gleeful little details to discover and go, "Yeah, that's the way it should have always been..." that I just can't summon up any real desire to rail on this game.  It's a solid piece of work that keeps getting better, and has enormous room for expansion.  Each time I sit down to play, I find something new and cool, and that's usually my highest praise for a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now around 22h In. I can happily say that this game is amasing. It ticks off allot of the boxes I want from a game and brings out a very pleasant experience that just keeps suprising and giving me more and more. The moment i feel i figured things out. They introduce a new mechanic or a new approach to things. An item that seemed useless just suddenly gets a great value based on it's utility/crafting or simply by it's flavour/lore description giving you small hints what it can be used for. The game as depth and Thats something i Like allot.All this ontop of a very very solid grid based turn based combat game that encourages experimentation and allows you to figure things out yourself. It doesn't hold your hand but it doesnt lie or hide information from you. It just allows you to pay attention. When you wish to do so. The world is bigger then i expected. And even if most quests bares down to 2 choices. I still feel i'm happily amused by the decisions and that they moved away from Black and white. And everything just sort of greyzone. Where your own morale views is key to deciding what is the lesser evil for you. Now they dont re-invent the wheel. And you still notice the Indie-level of quality in terms of voice acting. Facial animations and story telling. But it get's the job done. On top of this it's also an amasing 4 player coop experience that doesn't force 1 player to be the main character. That allows the entire party to feel like a part of this world with there own responsibillity to the camp and it's fellow soldiers. And that doesnt take you out of the experience or punish you for playing with friends. The experience stays true and faithfull so far. I will finish the game before i decide more about it.

_childDocuments_.review: ***NOTE: Updated at 1.0 Launch on 4/12/2023***Pros:++ It's a "party" survival game where you control the little figures and send them scrambling everywhere. Oddly entertaining.++ Battles are a lot of fun. You have to consider troop placement, abilities and gear for not just your own troops but also for the enemy.++ The music is beautiful and fits really well with the atmosphere of the game.++ Different seasons, weather, etc. You really feel like you're part of the world as you play.++ This game does not hold your hand & can seem very punishing. But this works out well with the survival aspect.++ Combat is challenging which I consider a plus. Again, they don't hold your hand and enemies scale with you, so you will always be challenged.++ Dynamic Happiness Gauge. Your troops still need to be fed and paid or they will leave (which I think is a great idea because they are mercenaries after all). That said, they won't just up and disappear on you in battle or something like that. They've done a great job on this since initial release for early access.++ Customize your party. This includes adjusting their gender, physical appearance, names, and skills. You can design your party to be the way you want.Negatives: -- The only thing I can think of is the near non-existent story line. But the game is so much fun that you practically stop caring within minutes of starting a new game.This game is absolutely incredible. It is challenging but still fun, immersive, and has great music. Battles are fun. I was eager see the finished product and any improvements to the game; I am not disappointed. Since the first time that I tried this game, I felt that it deserved a thumbs up. I am glad that Wartales 1.0 release has not let me down!

_childDocuments_.review: It combines all the worst features of a mobile MMO into a singleplayer grindfest. Incuding the design for addictivenessThe mobile/mmo progression got me hooked enough to waste 100 hours on it, but I regret investing so much time on ... nothing. The game you play after 100 hours is the same you played after 5 hours. Just with bigger numbers. No variation at all.At first the no-fantasy medieval setting is nice and novel. No Orcs and Elves and Demons. At some point you realize that also means no variation. You keep murdering the same humans and animals over and over. At some point they break the mold just a bit with some ghost animals and obligatory zombie-likes but never more than scratching the surface. Totally missing in this game: Any kind of agenda. You don't want to see a story unfold, you don't want to achieve anything (aside from literally checking off Steam Achievements). You don't want to discover anything since there is nothing to find. Like any sandbox game, you play until you lose interest and leave with a sour/salty taste in your mouth.Instead you get time wasters everywhere. There are crafting/farming minigames. There are hunt-the-pixel hidden-object scenes. Your army toddles through the world at just above snails pace. After the umpteenth 15 vs 15 battle against forgettable enemies you start to realize why other games limit the squad sizes: bigger numbers doesn't add anything.Everything just takes so much longer than it needs to for less reward than you expect. Just like your average free-to-play daily grind mobile game

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't had a game in over a decade grab me like this one has. You have a ton of customisation and the game does not hold your hand throughout any of it. I jumped in blind and played adaptive mode, and 150+hrs flew by. Huge props to the dev team for creating such a brilliant game. Thank you for reigniting my passion for PC gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: The following summarizes my 113 hours of gameplay on the hardest difficuilty available. I have completed most of the quests, tried most if not all the available weapon and armor types as well as skills / professions. My rig is as follows: I5-12400F with 32 gb ddr4 ram. Gtx 1080 Ti, the game is installed on an SSD and the drivers are up to date. Pros:- An old style RPG with very nice graphics.- The beautiful art style reminds me the Baldur's Gate series.- There is a good amount of freedom for the party the player is responsible for.- Good weapon and equipment variation.- The worldmap is huge.- Camping system is the best i have seen so far in similar games. Cooking is a serious profession in this game. You can capture low hp enemies and put them to work during a camp break. Well thought.- The skill system is not complicated, easy to learn and satisfactory.- Turn based tactical combat part is well implemented. - There is a nice exploration system with puzzle solving mechanics. - Crafting system is good. I enjoyed the mini-game for forging superior equipment.- Losing a character is not the end of the world.- Higher difficuilties are recommended for a better experience.Cons:- There is some sort of stuttering. I was unable to find the reason causing it.- AI does not recognize the hazards, such as buring oil or mud, and does not try circling it. Bad pathfinding during the combat phase.- Regrettably the player has to endure the same voiceline again and again especially from the traders.- More enemy types would be a good improvement.- The world feels empty.- There is no 'Grand Story' to stick to. Zones are disconnected from each other. - Existing storylines are regrettably boring.- The game becomes stale after 40-50 hours.Conclusion: Even after the cons i have mentioned above, I recommend a purchase as it will provide good content for at least 40 hours. Playing multiplayer is also fun.

_childDocuments_.review: You know what? This was initially a positive review. But the final couple of regions just broke me. The snowball of poor game design, atrocious balancing, bad UI and horrendous, Heavy Rain tier writing crushed my motivation and broke any ounce of hope for this game to stay good until the end.So, initially, this game feels like it's great. Like your choices matter a lot, and the world is your oyster. Well, it's not. Let's do this "Gaming sins" style, by categories.1. . Writers tried to be cheeky and fiddle with grey morals, but ultimately you have only side A or side B to pick. No in-betweens and no alternatives. Oh, you hate both lords fighting over the throne? Well, too bad, you have to pick one of them.2.  after any of your choices. Heck, nothing changes even when you complete the region's storyline. Nobody acknowledges anything and keeps repeating the last dialogue option spoken. You've had to kill a wife's plague-ridden husband? Well, you'd better never come to her house again. But not because she's mad, oh no — she'll just keep crying until the end of eternity.3. . Nothing makes sense, and because the devs chose to have self-contained region storylines, they feel meaningless and laughable. But the worst offender is the Fate of Grinmeer quest, in the capital city. Without spoilers, this murder "mystery" has the stupidest option for a culprit, and they have the worst motivation possible.4. Sorta tying into the previous point — . You won't receive a single legendary item from the main quests (there is only one exception, somewhat. One of the ruins is locked behind the regional storyline) — you won't even get worthy rare items from these. Hell, you won't even recoup your gold losses from fighting, eating and paying your mercenaries. So, ultimately, you don't even have any motivation for doing the "main" """storylines"""1. . Many other players mentioned here, that the problem ultimately lies in the difficulty settings. But that's only half of the story. If you play with region levels locked, you'll have "just right" beginnings, an insanely easy middle point, and a ball-busting end. If you pick adaptive levels, however — you'll never feel like your party is growing stronger.2. . You can get some of those through gear, but not even close to all of them. Instead, you're treated with the most situational perks in your skill tree imaginable, with the archer being the most daunting choice here.3. Since the devs couldn't program a somewhat smart AI, they instead use insane . Enjoy such hits as "-30% damage taken", "+30% crit chance" and. my personal favorite, "+40% (yes, ) damage for  buff on the target".4.  And you usually solve those in the deployment phase, without even engaging with the boss. Oh, and almost all bosses are just bigger versions of generic units! They couldn't even bother with a unique model. The one cool, gigantic boss you will stumble across, isn't even a boss — it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decoration which spams mass AoE "Fear".5.  Unless you're feeding a maximum amount of mercs — you'll just start piling up food just for its buffs, around the mid-point of the game. There is 0 management involved.6.  Once you get a perk allowing you to "negotiate" the prices and take more of those in one go, you'll be swimming in gold. And a batch won't take you even half your endurance bar to complete, given the right food (which is easy). You'll be swimming in gold. And since 90% of these are randomly generated, offering nothing but gold, you'll get tired of them, real fast.7.  For some bizarre reason, if a unit didn't hit\kill anyone he'll get less XP. And you get the training dummy rather late to remedy this even with its help. The damn ponies you desperately need to level up to get more carry capacity and gear slots will be out-levelled by your troops by 2 or 3 levels. Even if they've travelled with you the entire game.8.  And the last tier requires an outrageous amount of resources to craft. And the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ smithing mini-game — my bro almost lost his marbles, trying to forge the final tier. So, get this, it's a rhythm, mini-game where you have to hit the hot metal parts just as they "shine". However, you do this with your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mouse, and both the order and the time window are random — on top of the time window being already very tight. It's just rage-inducing and the most horrendous mini-game we've ever experienced. All for what? An armor piece with 0 useful stats?1. The game will randomly decide that you're not reloading together with the host and will leave you in a previous session2. Atrocious navigation, worthy of a bad 2D precision-platformer — but here's the kicker, you click with your mouse and play a strategy game. You will get stuck. You will struggle to reach and activate a climbing hook. You will stumble onto unreachable resources and fishing spots.3. Sometimes player controls during your turn just bug out and you can't do anything, but restart the encounter or reload a save.4. The game sometimes just outright refuses to connect and properly load. This is a known issue, persisting for quite some time. Nothing was done to remedy this or at least explain how to avoid it. It's just there.All-in-all, I'm insanely disappointed by Wartales. And finding this out in the endgame just feels like a betrayal. Honestly, I'd probably be better off finding out the game was bad from the start. Wartales took a lot of stuff from BB anyway.
