_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me and have been on a weird itch to play a game like the original Digimon World from 1999, then you might find something here. It still plays like the original, but with a lot more improvements in conveying information to you and making Digivolution less of a mystery. In my time playing, I don't think I ever had a digimon pass away before hitting ultimate. However, unlike the original game, I don't think it presents its world and setting as well as the 1999 Digimon World.This game is a monster raising game where you have to take care of and raise the stats of a virtual pet. Unlike a certain other franchise, your monster does not have just one strict path of evolution, but multiple paths which depends on how you raise and train your Digimon. Furthermore, on the day to day you also need to tend to your Digimon's hunger and bathroom needs as well.You will also travel various areas in the game world, along with finding numerous NPC Digimon to recruit to bring back to the city of Floatia where they will take on jobs and services that can help you through the course of the game.I must stress above all else here, however, I do think you really have to love the idea of playing a game where the core loop is mainly about raising monsters, evolving them, and making them stronger. Because if you're looking for a deep and engaging story, you may want to look elsewhere.I have to stress this a lot because what story there is is extremely short, and acts as an awkward roadblock recruitment more than anything. So you really have to be sold on the monster raising experience as something to sink hours of gameplay into.The main loops of the game will find you in the day to day feeding your digimon, taking it to the bathroom, and training your digimon to fight other stronger digimon.In battles, you do not directly control the Digimon. Your digimon fight of their own accord, however you are able to issue orders which your Digimon can enact. Pressing the L1 or R1 button on your controller will bring up a radial menu for either of your digimon, which in turn gives you commands that can be activated with Order Points. From this menu, you can either directly tell your digimon to use one of its attacks now, or if you have enough Order Points accumulated you can use their special ability.A caveat I will give is that while there is a gym you can take your Digimon to train at, this really isn't the most optimal way to train. Your best means of training your partners stats actually comes from battles (especially when they are still Rookies), and because a battle doesn't progress time at all, it is extremely optimal to find a spot, do battle, leave the screen, and come back again until your gains depreciate. There are a number of guides online about where you should go and what to fight, and at what stat ranges, and I stress this knowledge greatly.I do wish in that way that way this game struck a far better balance in how to train, because it does feel like they were aware of combat EXP being as effective as it was and chose to purposely limit it.The story of this game is extremely disappointing. You should not be coming into this game expecting an especially good story, and honestly you should feel insulted for the weak fanservice they attempt to do with the story.It's a real shame, because they are clearly trying to pull on something with some things they pull from the 1999 game, but they really do amount to "blink and you miss it" cameos (especially in one instance at the end of the game).It is disheartening to listen to a review shrug and say "It's bad, but you weren't really here for the plot, were you?", because I think it misses something.Touching on the original game, a lot of the backstory could actually be missed even by the time you beat the games final boss. The game let you recruit all sorts of Digimon at your own pace, and none of the content was gated off by plot, just by recruitment alone. I think that worked a lot better, especially for the kind of person who is just here for progression and monster raising.There's also a loss of atmosphere between these two games. Words I'd use to describe the original would be things like "Lonely", "Dingy", "Rebellious", "Grimy", "Mysterious", and more. The original game certainly had an atmosphere that has greatly struck a chord with me for over twenty years now, along with the feeling of exploring a large and mysterious world.In a way then, I lament the loss of a feeling of "Exploration" the previous game did well that this game just does not do whatsoever.I wouldn't mind them acting like this game never happened and just focusing on making another game that attempts to capture Digimon World 1 and improving upon it.Alot of the original tracks aren't all too memorable or just feel really out of place. The song that plays in the first area you can explore, "Blue Sky Big Step", sounds like something from some sort of Sonic game for example. It's not bad, but it does feel out of place. It's not tonally dissonant with what's on screen, but I think that just brings to mind a critique of aesthetics.There are also a number of tracks are re-arranged versions of songs and tracks from the 1999 game, and I'm not sure how to feel about them. For the most part, something about them just doesn't land too well to my ears, like some tracks have lost a bit of their soul being re-arranged the way they have. They're passable tracks, but I don't really appreciate the File City Day and Night re-arrangements among others. I do appreciate the Entertainment District remix though, somthing about that clickedThere's another neat tidbit with this game where it also uses a lot of sound effects from the 1999 game as well. Things like menu sounds and even the calls and cries of some monsters. Something tickles me about that, and they've been mixed in a way to not feel too out of place in this game. That's one bit of pandering I'll give a thumbs up on, especially with execution.I really wish I could be more positive about this game, but unfortunately I feel like that bit with the writing is just inexcusable. I don't deny the fact a lot of hard work went into this game, and it's clear to me people who were big fans of the franchise were also working on this game. It's in those little failings that all this hurts a lot more. I think they got much of the core gameplay right, but I'm also not the kind of person who plays games like these for hours on end trying to get all the Digimon, collect all the things and stuff like that. I'm not a huge achievement hunter, collector in these kinds of games, and so forth. I do like addicting systems though, and I do wish there was something that really clicked that gave me more of an excuse to just go through the cycles of the game, raising digimon, and wanting to keep on going back at it.In the original game, that was the desire to explore the world. In this, what world is there to explore?I give the game a thumbs up simply because the gameplay loop fundamentally did scratch an itch for me. Were I able to, I'd gave this a sort of "Eh" hand gesture.

_childDocuments_.review: With a passable story (please for the love of the gods don't subject yourself to the English dub, I promise it's just better in Japanese this time), throwbacks to the original title, a meaty main storyline, and having an actual sense of direction thanks to baseline quality of life digs like a , this spiritual successor scratches that Tamagotchi itch that the other World games after '99 just couldn't get.Now, I wouldn't say get this at full price (as it has some.. drawbacks), and even if you really liked the original World despite its tedium, progression obfuscation, and major flaws, I want to tack some a giant, bold caveats to those interested in New Order.Overall it's a very worthwhile venture if you're either someone who liked being a masochist with Digimon World 1999 (and would rather come back with some basic direction and less frustration), or if you're interested in an RPG battler with Tamagotchi elements. Again, I wouldn't suggest getting it at full price, because a $75 Dollarydoo pricetag for a semi-polished port is laughable.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the digimon world series since the 1st playstation game I was really excited to see some of the old gameplay features would come back. The game isn't like your traditional turn based rpg, like the recently released cyber sleuth. It feels more like a pet sim like the original playstation game. Unlike the original you are in charge of two digimon this time around. Each digimon has a personality and likes and dislikes, there are in game days and you have to figure out how you spend them. Training your digimon doesn't consist of grinding battles, but taking them into the gym and choosing a stat to raise. The magic of the game is digivolving your digimons, there are multiple digivolution for each digimon to achieve. The challenge is that the required stats for digivolution are hidden. In order to unlock them you have to interact with your digimon when prompted to by the game like after battles or training. This is a the best and worst part of the game, the fact that the stats revealed from the digivolution chart after these interaction are random makes it super tedious on top of the interactions themselves occurring at random intervals after battles and training. It can take a few in game days for the full requirement of a digivolution. This is also another thing that can make the game frustrating seeing as each digimon has a life expectancy of a few days that only increases when you digivolve it. I highly recommend you play the game on easy as it would not change the battle difficulty but the digivolution requirements. Over all the game is great if you're a fan of the series specially an old fan but be warned it can be very frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game if you are already a fan of the Digimon World franchise. If you haven't played a Digimon World game then this wil be a very unique experience for you as it doesn't really have a direct comparison point. Digimon World is basically Animal Crossing with the way you need to gather new entities to join your village, Pokemon in the way that you exclusively use the games mons in order to fight, and then Tomagotchi because you need to take care of your mons and they wil eventually pass away and get reborn. Expanding the village is a really nice way to make you as a player feel that your actions have immediate affects, convince a Digimon to join the village and now your training centre is beter, or you have access to a item shop (just some early game examples). And due to your Digimons having lifespans this sortoff functions like  a roguelite game where your mons can die-die, but at least you will have all the city upgrades making it a lot easier and faster to get back to where you were last time. Exploring the world in order to find new Digimons to try and recruit for the village is a really nice motivator to explore every area possible. The games battling is also very different from any monster-taming game. The battles take place in a 3D environment that's sortoff cut off from the world around you, within this area the Digimons will move around by themselves and attack as they see fit. The only way you can directly impact the battle is through telling the Digimons who to target, when to defend, and to order them to use set moves (note you need to have available OP points to tell a Digimon to use a move). You can build up OP points by cheering after your Digimons hit attacks or defends againsts a attack properly. My suggestion is to unlock the ability to block through your Tamer skills as soon as possible as it's basically a requirement to beat the first boss in the game. Oh and don't bother using OP points on normal attacks, rather build up to 150 and use your Digimons ultimate attack (if both Digimons have 150 OP points then you can trigger to have them both do their Ultimate together, which does a bit more damage than doing it seperately). And lastly the Tomagotchi element. So your Digimons need to be fed when their hungry, need to rest when their tires, poop when they have the need to do so, and sleep when they are sleepy. If you don't fulfil these requirements then your Digimons lifespan will be shortened, and you could end up with one of the worst Digivolutions in the game (the Digimons themed around filth/poop). Combat is very focussed on stats, as it should be, so be sure to always have your Digimons in fighting condition (enough HP, MP, Strength, and Stamina, to mention the main combat ones), but your stats also directly impact what your Digimon will digivolve into. Each Digimon (up till the last stage) will have branching evolutions, every 2nd In Training Digimon has a handful of Digimons it can turn into, and the evolutions following those also have their own handful of Digimons they can in turn turn into. So stat management is very important if you're aiming for a useful or cool Digimon. TIP: Rather fight Digimons to gain stats than training in the gym, training takes a hour of ingame time while fighting pauses time, meaning you can early the stats you got from training a hour of life away in like 2 minutes if you rather did battles. Your Digimon eventually passes away, due to old age, or dying in combat (if you revive while in combat it will always be fine, but looks like there's a percentage chance that the older a mon is that the death will be permanent if they are dead at the end of comat). Once your Digimon partner/s pass away they will be reborn as one of the available digi-eggs (you choose what egg you want them to be reborn as). You can increase your Digimons lifespan by always making sure their needs are immediately met, by getting them to the max evolution stage (each stage will add a few days of life), and by feeding them restuarant food that increases their life span. There's a lot more to learn about the mechanics about the game, but this breakdown has already gotten a bit to long haha. So if you enjoyed Digimon World 1 then this is a very nice return to formula and deserves your attention, if you are a monster-taming fan then you should also definitely give this game a go. As a monster taming fan I give Digimon World: Next Order 4/5, it's a really fun game that I would definitely recommend if this is your type of game. _childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order is a sequel to the original Digimon World. The Digimon World games are not your typical jrpg. They are virtual pet jrpg hybrids. This is important to understand because if you buy this game assuming it's going to be just like your typical jrpg your going to be seriously confused.Digimon World games are all about taking care of your Digimon. And how easily you progress through the game is dependent on how well you manage your Digimon's care. If you neglect your Digimon and raise it poorly it will grow up to be completely useless. On the other hand if you take good care of your Digimon manage its needs and give it the proper care and training it needs. It will grow up to be a badass and tear through anything in its way. That's the core appeal of this game watching your Digimon grow up to be strong and capable from your training and care.If you like virtual pets but want something deep and satisfying, with some jrpg adventure element mixed in then this is the perfect game. You will have endless hours of fun learning the precise stat builds that will get you the Digimon evolution you want while exploring the wide and fascinating world.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever wanted a game that perfectly captures the experience of parenthood, but with more pixels, digital monsters and impending Doom? Digimon World: Next Order is here to fulfill that oddly specific dream that all of us old school fans  of the series have dreamt of since Digimon World 1. This isn't just a game.it's a glorified Dad Simulator. Picture this: You’re managing not one digimon now but TWO Digimon partners, each with their own needs, quirks, and vendetta against your sanity. One moment, you’re fighting for survival, unleashing devastating ultimate attacks; the next, you’re desperately sprinting across an ever so populated sand region to find the nearest outhouse because again, not one but TWO of your Digimon is doing the Bathroom tango of terror. This game has it all. Strategy? Check. Virtual pet mechanics? Yep. The occasional existential crisis because your favorite Digimon just got reincarnated into a literal poop emoji? Yeah, that's in here too. What other game has it where you treat your children to a 5 star meal in a restaurant just to have them yell at you for not giving them a snack and then digivolving into a booger? If this isn't epic fantasy, i don't know what is. So, if you’re ready to embrace the chaos, raise some digimon, and debate for about an hour on google on what digivolutions you want. Congratulations: Digimon World: Next Order might be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order captures the tamagotchi niche very well, although it will be more enjoyable for everyone than the average tamagotchi, it doesn't change that this is a niche game.Depending on what you want in your monster taming games, this can be more or less enjoyable than Digimon Story games, while also being more or less enjoyable than Digimon Survive depending on your appreciation for that game's niche.- This is basically a straight improvement from Digimon World 1.- Digimon World 2 to 4 have mixed to poor reception, which means DW:NO should stack up quite well by default.The flow of the game is really nice, building city and slowly methodologically training Digimon means that you get into this Stardew/Animal crossing type of daily rhythm which makes it comfortable, relaxed and easy to get in a flow while the game provides significant battle challenges when you are ready. It takes a while to get used to the balance of the game, but once you are ready this is very enjoyable and definitely worth a shot.One of the most enjoyable aspects of explroring in the game is how enemy AI functions and how the world flows into different areas to form one big landscape.You will grind several things here, materials to upgrade the city, stats for your Digimon, tamer rank by walking/collecting/fighting, food ingredients and money. The main obstacles will be stats and materials to upgrade the city. The visuals are fine, but outdone in every aspect by Cybersleuth, and the pixel sprites of older Story games are clearly timeless and hold up better than these 3D graphics. Then there is Survive with amazing HD skill effects and beautiful drawn art for digimon. The OST is okay, it functions as it should and does not annoy, but it is nothing special. I prefer the OST of the old NDS games. Of course Survive has significantly superior soundtrack too. I'd rank this bad boy as a solid 7,7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: to me this is the type of gameplay Bandai should be focusing on with digimon.there are multiple franchises that use the tactics turnbase battles but nothing plays quite like these digimon tamagotchi RPGs.The goal here isn't to hoard mons, instead you're focusing all your attention on one (2 in this game, actually) to raise your mon propper. you know, like the v-pet devices.and in true V-pet fashion you not only need to oversee and decide the training regimen for your digidude for stat alocation, you will need to feed it, run him  to the potty and praise or scold him according tohis behaviour, since weight, care mystakes and even happyness will affect which form your mon will grow into.Being the third iteration of this v-pet meets rpg formula (the first two were world 1 for the PSX and world re:digitize for PSP) the franchise has been establishing what I consider the begginings of a new subgenre.Thesegames center around making friends with diferent mons around the digiworld, either by helping them out or beating them into submission (just like in the real world). Ok, maybe I lied a bit, you really are hoarding mons but not to add to your roster of fighting dudes, the goal here is to consolidate the efforts of these diferent guys towards a common goal which is to build up your digivillage into a digicity as to get you the resources to fight the looming threat and save the digital world. In these games you are not a typical digidestined like in the anime, where the mons there digivolve when it's time to fight and revert back to their rookie or in-training forms when done. Here, however, you have to earn your form and keep training to achieve the next one, you won't revert to prior forms unless your dudes revert all the way back to eggs.And to Eggs they shall revert to, embracing the mon life-cycle is part of the fun to me, when your digimon gets old enough to have a heart attack (age is based on in-game time, you can sort of make it go faster through training  at the gym along with other methods), it will, and you get to raise it all over again into potentially diferent forms, which is something impressive about next order is the variety of forms available so you can, even with 2 partners, send a long time uncovering that digivolve chart.Not for everyone, quite a niche style of gameplay but I fit the niche so yeah, nothing else quite like it, worth the buy on a sale, even if just for the novelty.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: You want a game like Digimon World 1 and you enjoy Min-Maxing and raising Digimon? Then this game is for you. Just buy it. If you are NOT enjoying raising Digimons and Min-Maxing then this game is not for you. It has a decent long story where the main difficulty comes from properly raising your Digimon.  I´m 20 Hours in but just managed to finish act 1 of 3 recently and I still have a lot of mechanics to unlock and missions to do. There is a lot of min-maxing stats and grinding involved in this game but so was the first one. You will have to research a lot on your own and think about how to approach fights. The fighting system is surprisingly deep and once you get further into the game you are going to pay attention on who your Digimon attacks, at what time and how to chain those attacks into a bonus. Since you have 2 Digimons they are able to combine their attacks. The fighting later involves a lot of hand holding. You are not just watching them fight but also tell them to block at the right moment and use their ultimate attacks etc.Warning: This game is clunky, this game doesn´t explain a lot well but that's the typical charm of old Japanese games but it also has the upsides of a Japanese game. If you dive into it and learn how to use the mechanics it will reward you and develop a sense of satisfaction that comes with finishing something challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: Training, battling, caring for your digimon, and trying to get all of the town digimon to your cityBasically Digimon World 1 with new story, whole new digimons, and dual partnerGo get it, TamersEdit :After playing additional hours, still feel the game is big enough but also a bit repetitive. Well, at the end of the day, it is still a good game but maybe I am the one who is not able to play that much anymore. recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, if you played Digimon World 1, you will love this game.Now allow me to save you some time and give you the trick to high stats. Training will be important at the start, but your real goal will be to fight using Rookie and Champion stages. You get bonus stats based on what I believe are the enemies stats, affected by their evolution stage. Simply put, go fight champions with rookies and you will get big bonuses, best used near area entrances so you can respawn them. Your best friends for this are the defense command, upgraded to block full damage, and items. The money and items you make from fights should make you rich as well.Otherwise just take the game at the pace you like, explore it, learn it, but when you eventually hit that wall that feels impossible to surpass, just keep the above in mind, fighting is key.

_childDocuments_.review: My big question when I was deciding to buy this game was: how much is this game like the original Digimon World? Turns out, quite a bit! Obviously, you get to raise two at a time, but the main gameplay system of raising your monsters is fairly similar. You train, you fight, you evolve, you explore the world and fight bosses and get Digimon to join your town, thus unlocking more options for training, fighting, and so on. The number of Digimon you can obtain is huge, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that you can even raise old school jobber Digimon like Tsukaimon (black Patamon), Aruramon (blue flower Palmon), and Psychemon (Magenta Gabumon), which is weirdly neat. Basically: if you see a Digimon somewhere in the game, you can raise it yourself!My only complaint is that, compared to the immense charm of the original, there seems to be something lacking in this one. Some areas seem strangely empty, many Digimon are tedious to befriend, while others are so simple you only have to go up and say hello to get them to join the city. Don't get me wrong, it MOSTLY feels right, but sometimes it's just a bit bland or anticlimactic. The main storyline is a decent length (probably 30 or 40 hours if you don't screw up too terribly), and it's pretty decent- the characters are a hell of a lot more likeable than those found in Cyber Sleuth! The endgame, so far, feels a bit dull and grindy; there's just a bunch of new boss monsters you can fight, who will absolutely kick your ass if you don't have min/maxed mons. With that in mind, I don't know how much I desire to finish the game, as I'm not much of a completionist. But the rest was great, and I don't mind too much for having paid full price to play the next-best thing to the original Digimon World!
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Bandai for making such an amazing game reminded me of digimon world 1. Loved visiting  other arenas in the  game and facing cool digimon in battle , as first time going trough game I had a ton of fun raising different partners.Still not done with game and I keep having fun and recruiting many digimon to the city of Floatia.

_childDocuments_.review: The game does pretty good justice to the original Digimon World game, but now with a lot less sukamon. It's got rough edges, and could have been designed a lot better in a lot of ways but it maintains a lot of the core of the original game that the sequels moved away from: Raising your mon through training and rebuilding a home base to facilitate that.It doesn't have a lot of depth outside of evolution requirements. Combat is basically hitting recharge button on a timer, and triggering specials when possible. It's all... serviceable. It could be worse from an auto-battler standpoint. There's a lot of tedium you can tell was left over from console and poor design, a lot of small extra seconds here or there such as material gathering that add up pretty quick. Thankfully, since you're on PC you have access to a handful of quality of life mods, that remove many of the long drawn out moments between animations and some actions.To be fair though, this game should be priced about as much as an old PSVita game tho as that's the era the developers who designed it are probably from. A lot of bad habits here when it's using a modern engine that should make much of these pain points more manageable by modern game design standards. Nah, these were choices.Combat left me wanting a lot more from this. Raising specific mons is really the only drive that kept me going as the plot is about as shallow as any pokemon game gating a linear story peppered with steep changes in enemy difficulty. If you pick this up, realize that level means very little and that digimon stage means a lot more. Look at the colored lines on their nameplate to judge challenge, blue is easy, white is an average, red is hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order feels like a dream, more specifically, the dream of the creators of the original Digimon World and those that enjoyed it. Digimon is already arguably a mess of a series, mashing a whole bunch of ideas together, and Next Order tries to contain all of them that it can. Raising Digimon, making new Digifriends, battling Digirivals, exploring the Digital World and trying to save it, and bringing Digimon together to a village where they can make use of their unique talents.That said, I don't actually recommend Next Order for most people - though I could be wrong. Perhaps new souls could start their journey here. It may be a bit of a strange one, Next Order and the original Digimon World follow their own rhythm of gameplay and don't properly explain a lot of it. Next Order is a lot easier in that regard. More things explained, more supplies available. Not suddenly having a Greymon camping outside your front door.A lot of time is spent looking after your Digimon companions like tamagotchi. Feeding them, training them, taking them to the bathroom. This gets easier over time, and you get a better grasp of how far and where you can explore with your Digifrens before age gets them and you start raising them again from egg form. There are a bunch of Digimon cameos from the various series and games, some just want to fight strong opponents, some are there to make friends.I don't even know if Digimon World and Next Order are particularly good games or what optimal Digimon games would look like. A bunch of inconvenient menus making you trade for certain items one at a time, training and losing your friends can be a strange and tiresome loop. It can be difficult to get Digimon you might want, and then you might not get them for long. Face-checking Digimon strength to find out you couldn't possibly fight that right now. I do however know that it feels like a proper Digimon Adventure.While the other Digimon World games likely have their own merits, when I had the opportunity to eventually try one years later I was immediately put off by how dissimilar it was to the original - this is the sequel I was looking for. Years late, later still to PC, with many flaws, charging far more than it should relative to the rest of the game market, and looking like it was developed for the PS2; but a very specific beauty to some.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the original PS1 Digimon World you'll probably enjoy this one, it's basically the same core ideas with a lot more stuff added to it, plus tons of QoL elements to make the gameplay way less obtuse / grindy. It's basically a virtual pet (tamagotchi) with TONS of things to do and a semi-passive combat system.Still there's a lot of experimentation and hidden stuff in this game, just because they've made it easier to understand doesn't mean that they took out one of the best aspects of the OG: the element of surprise. Anyways just like the OG this is a very avant garde kind of game, I just can't ignore the charm of experimental stuff done right, Digimon World: Next Order is a very unique title and definitely a fun time if you're looking to play something off the rails.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: PC port of the 2016 sequel/remake(ish) of the 1999 Playstation 1 "Digimon World" game. The port seems okay, so far. I've been saving frantically every 5 minutes, but the game has yet to crash on me. I will keep on saving a lot, though, especially before tough fights.You have two partners, so gaining all the digivolution codex entries is faster. Better graphics, UI & QoL - which are all still trash in comparison to other titles released in 2016, but they have their charm and, c'mon, you can explore the digital world!IN CONTRAST TO THE PS4 VERSION, YOU CAN SPRINT!Prepare for all the grind and then some more. This is a slow game. On Steam, I just finished chapter 1 after 20 hours and I've played this game on the PS4 before. If you're just starting out and don't know what you're doing, you're going to take a LONG while to get anywhere. Don't be afraid to read some guides.If you have played this game before/know what you're doing, you're gonna take slightly less time.All in all, this game is amazing for shutting your brain off, enjoying the nice BGM and that sweet, sweet feeling of min-maxing your digimon to eternity and beyond.And most importantly above all: Angewomon is still 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World Next Order continues to be a fun pet game only now it's on PC and no, you DO NOT need a controller. Devs really MUST edit and patch the tutorial part at the very beginning of the game as it's showing the player how to play with a controller but upon pressing some buttons on your keyboard, you'll easily figure out the keyboard's controls to play and get past it. After the tutorial, you just go to settings and key bindings to see everything you need to know for controls. It's really not that hard. :)As for the game itself; I do feel that it's about time we got a true Digimon game about caring, bonding and battling and this was always the perfect game based on the original 90's Digimon tamagotchi. The acting is a little cheesy but the story itself is fun. The perfect nostalgia of Digimon World from the PS1. I do genuinely hope we get more Digimon games like this one. The only thing I don't really understand is why the developers put an even easier mode when "normal" mode is already incredibly easy compared to the original PS1 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order is the next installment and the true sequel to the original Digimon World on the PS1, with this in mind, this game does everything that the original does but better and adds a whole wide more features that the player will enjoy. First, the evolutions are much easier to get by, and as you progress into the game the game will become more accessible and opens up the more digimon you have in your city. That includes the likes of seeing what requirements you need for certain evolutions and even locking out evolutions you do not wish to take by blocking them out completely.The game runs beautifully on PC with a smooth frame rate and i dont have the greatest GPU out there, Game looks decent for what it is and does, graphically. The player will have a great experience with this game when it comes to performance. Overall, Digimon World Next Order takes the PS1 classic and turns up the volume to 11 with many features, many areas to explore, new and more digimon to recruit and obtain for yourself. This IS THE digimon game to play, especially if you're a big fan of the Vpet-esk type gameplay it offers, and it does it very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: I completed this game on the PS4 several years ago.This game is a big grind and has a huge time investment while you are training your digimon to get past the next 'wall'.It's a pretty fun game outside of that and is a great creature caring/battle simulator. The PC port runs smoothly, however the game does not display ANY mouse and keyboard controls ANYWHERE. This includes during the tutorial and on screen prompts, it's all controller icons. The buttons work and it is possible to play with Keyboard and Mouse, but unless you are used to playing games on an emulator chances are you will have no muscle memory for them and will find the game very tough without a controller.I will end up completing the game on PC, but I cannot recommend this to anyone looking to play with Mouse and Keyboard.

_childDocuments_.review: I added this game to my wishlist after finding out it's play style is similar to Digimon World 1, (which is one of my all time favourite games) and bought it after it went on sale. And honestly, Next Order really does itch the scratch of wanting another game like the first! Having two partners is also really enjoyable, I love the interactions they have with one another! Definitely recommend if you're a fan of the OG Digimon World :) Haven't finished the story yet, but loving it!

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it. Just finished all achievements, should explain itself lol. Now onto the review:If you're a Digimon fan it's a must buy and play. But even if you've never played any Digimon game it's still good and probably the most comfortable "Digimon World" Game to start with because of all the QoL stuff compared to other World Games so you can get easier into it. Unlike the first World Game back then on the PSX, things get explained and shown here. You don't need any guide. No tedious very low % encounter recruits. It's not "too hard", but on your first playthrough you still might get into scary situations because some Digimons are VERY strong if you come (blind)unprepared. Not going to tell more because it'll spoil the game more. It's great.. And even has replayability since you can start over again just raising different Digis throughout the main story for a somewhat different experience with different Techs (yes, techs really do matter). You can also make yourself challenges by playing the hard mode thats unlocked after beating the main story. Or come up with something for yourself like simply dont use items in battle etc.. really gives a different experience and surprisingly, it really was fun again, because then you'll rely more deeply on mechanics like the Defense Order, Item management, how you're approaching Digimons/bosses..Get it and play
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: As good of a sequel to DW1 on PS1 as we can get. It follows the same formula of throwing you into this world without many explanations (although still much more than the original DW1) and just learning by doing. For complete newcomers to the series this might be incredibly overwhelming and even frustrating just like it was to us 90s kids when we played DW1 for the first time. Even with knowledge from back then this game can still kick your butt in the beginning. But at least you probably won't get nothing but Numemon from your first few digivolutions :DThis game gets exponentially easier the more you play. You unlock more and more Tamer skills from just about anything you do in the game and those will make your Digimon stronger with each new reincarnation and give you lots of other perks. So don't stress progression too much in the beginning when you hit a wall and can't defeat story bosses immediately. It is possible to hit Mega digivolution from the first generation but you'll most likely only unlock them later and that's fine. But if you really want to get as powerful as possible quickly then look up training spots for battling. Because compared to DW1 or Re: Digitize, stat gains from battling are actually very viable and I'd say better than gym training if you know the right spots and it doesn't take any ingame time. You'll hit digivolution requirements (of which a number of battles is often a part of) much more easily and this'll allow your Digimon to live longer. Overall I'm very happy with this game and as a sidenote a quick thank you to the dedicated modding community of this game that make this game even better than it was on PS4. For example I understand why the camera was so glued to the player on the original small Vita screen but dear god it is so much better when you can zoom out a lot more with a mod and actually see your giant Mega Digimon fully when following you around.I hope we'll eventually get a new installment in the Digimon World series. But I'd already be happy if we'd just finally get any updates on the new Digimon Story game that's been in development for years already.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game overall, a must play for Digimon fans, yet it is inferior compared to Digimon World 1.[Pros]:• Plenty of Digimon you can raise.• A lot to explore (yet DMW1 did it better).• Expanding your hometown is really fun.• There are upgrades for the facilities in town which is very useful.• Skill tree for the main character.• There is chance when your Digimon die to turn into a new stronger Digimon. It is really exciting every time happens![Cons]:• Too much grinding is required for almost everything in this game (tamer, partners and facilities).• Too many re-colours Digimon that you can raise.• Unbalanced. Overall most battles, even regular enemies are tough, sometimes too easy.• Art direction, areas felt empty compared to DMW1 (I like the realistic art direction in DMW1, felt like a real world with strange things).• Camera issues, I prefer zooming out so I can see more. Every time I zoom out and enter new area, it reset to zoom in.• Kept some Japanese terms and names such as Omegamon. Omnimon would be better for the English release. There are other translations were translated based on Japanese like one line for example where the villain says could make a stronger Form than Ultimate (Mega), actually Ultimate in Japanese means Mega in English.

_childDocuments_.review: This game brings up my sweetest memories from the time I played Digimonworld on psx. I love how the game works without being buggy and the fact that time pauses when you need to use items during battle or escape from it. Battle mechanics are a bit tough to understand at first but you eventually get used to them. After progressing in the game and getting some levels up, you can make Digimon lives longer which is great, especially when having an Ultimate Digimon. The only thing that I don't like, is that when at a certain part of the game (Early in the game), you unlock quick travelling with Birdramon, he sends you at the entrance of each place and not further in. (There is no option to go further in a place you want, even after exploring it.) Overall, it's an amazing game and I would strongly recommend it, especially to players who have tried Digimonworld on psx, because, although the story is different, these two games are very much alike.
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: As an old time fan of the original Digimon World, I must admit that this one is an improvement over the previous one. It is without a doubt extremely fun, specially once you finally understand the mechanics. Nevertheless, it is still a monster raising game where you Digimon die after a set amount of time and where, depending on the difficulty, you will have to do either "a bit" to "too much" grinding.The Pros:- Engaging battle system that is easy to learn, but hard to master. Getting the timings down can be difficult, specially for Boss fights- Great number of skills and Digimon. Every single pair can give you new ways of facing the enemies- Once you get the mechanics down, it can easily become a power fantasyThe Cons:- The grind in higher difficulties- Rather old graphics, specially considering this is originally a Vita game from 2016- Once you get the mechanics down, it can easily become a power fantasyThe Differences to the original:- Digivolution is WAY EASIER than the original one. Now, you can actually see what is needed to digivolve and plan accordingly. You can easily get Mega Digimon (even if rather weak) in your first generation if needed.- Battle training is actually worth it compared to the original one, as in the original they were worthless.- Gym training is worthless now. It reigned supreme in the originalEDIT: after finishing the game, I can confidently state that if you are a Digimon fan, you will enjoy it. However, in my opinion I believe the original Digimon World is more fun. If you had to pick between either of them, go for the original one. The way the world is conceived, the music, and the areas were far more enjoyable and charming in the original game
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be honest I really liked this game to begin with as I found it to be a drastic improvement over the original PS1 version but the fact remains the lifespan mechanic is still here and admittedly having to raise your Digimon from scratch again over and over becomes a Chore. Their stats do improve each time however upon rebirth and you can increase their life via Tamer Skills but still this is something I will never really like. The toilet and feeding mechanic grates after a while too especially when I'm trying to train them and they never stop making this irritating noise to get your attention. The game also suffers from artificial difficulty spikes too which requires you to spend quite a bit of time grinding to overcome these barriers and tbh the older I get my patience for this type of gameplay starts to wear really thin. As a person who grew up with the first 2 Seasons of Digimon I'm willing to overlook all of these gripes and appreciate the game for what it is and what it has to offer but if you're the type of person who doesn't like time management games and isn't into Digimon then this might not be for you. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the naysayers that thought this game would re-release with the price of an ongoing Playstation Store sale.This is a great Digimon game that will last you on average 60 hours and around 100 if you are a completionist.It also includes all the extra content and DLC that released over the years for the original version.A direct sequel to the original Digimon World, but with the tamagotchi-like features streamlined and made simple so that they are enjoyable and easy to handle and master even for a complete novice to pet-keeping games.The grind has also been much lessened, and even more so if you equip yourself with this guide, that will tell you which enemy mons give the best stats/experience and propel you to your desired megas as early as Generation 2:This game is the ultimate experience for any fan of the original Digimon World games, and it is finally available for PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 9/10. Starts off really basic and tells you practically nothing, but the further you go along, the more you start to understand. The other characters are interesting, but some of the better parts are the references to the first Digimon World game for PS1. My biggest complaint is that your partners never get to say much during the story, forcing another character to take their place in blindly loving the player character. (Look, I get it. There's too many digimon your partners could be at those points in the story for them to use voices, but you could at least have them play an animation or something) There seems to be a significant post-game, as well. Gameplay: 7.8/10. Kinda grindy at times. Getting the digimon you want early on is a nightmare, but later you unlock the ability to block off evolution paths you don't want, and it gets better. The thing that drags it down the most for me, though, is the amount of guide dang its the game has. The game will generally point you in a direction and give you a digimail to remind you of what you're supposed to do, but sometimes, it won't. (The Meat Troops vs Veggie Troops subplot is especially guilty.) And don't get me started on the block mechanic. You have to spend tamer points to unlock it and its upgrade and yet they're MANDATORY. The game does not tell you this. (Thank goodness we live in the age of the internet, where guides are easy to find.)Digimon: The digimon gameplay is more akin to the vpet devices, which is what got me into the series. Feed, take them to the bathroom, train them, fight them. Etc. They have lifespans, and when those are up, they get reborn so you can make them go another route. The game keeps track of which digimon you've had, giving you a possible motivation to Raise Them All.

It's not quite as hard as World 1, but you still have to get those stats right if you want to get your favorite 'mon. I just, unfortunately, do not like the main character! The female especially. _childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, do I don't often review games but here goes:this is clearly a substandard port from the PS Vita, the controls are not at all built around keyboard and mouse, the resolution caps out at 1920 x 1080, the graphics are... not great.that being said, your here most likely because you like digimon or similar games. and honnestly even if you weren't a fan here's what I have to sayGet it, because despite the lack-luster graphics, the annoying controls, the low resolution and the sometimes annoying repetitive back and fourth quests, this game is fun, its different, you don't "keep" your digimon, you train them, evolve them and fight with them for around 20 in game days, then they die of old age, revert to eggs and to do it all over again, with a portion of the stats you trained up carried over, meaning successive generations are that little bit more powerful than those that came before, what this does is give you possibilities, unlike other monster battling games you don't end up "stuck" with the same old team because you are often to worried about levelling new ones up, or because you have grown attached to that little creature you keep in a ball on your belt, you can try new and differing combinations and see what you like. (and good news for those of us who get particularly attached to one form of our digital pets, you can at later times in the game buy (for a minor in game fee) "Digicores" that allow you to evolve your familiar into the form you want, some cores are harder to get yes, but a large enough amount are purchasablethe story isn't terrible either for what its worth, its certainly no AAA plot full of intrigue, mystery and backstabbing, but that's not what this genre of game is about.so yes, despite its short comings, you should absolutely buy this game and try it
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: Too much of the game time is spent walking the same paths (the game's pretty linear) and fighting the same enemies repeatedly to grind stat points with a battle system that just isn't satisfying. The formula worked in the original Digimon World on PS1 because your digimon aged and died quick enough that the gameplay was constantly changing and because there were enough branching paths that you could try something else if you're running up against a wall, but this time you'll be stuck with the same guy retreading the same ground for hours. Bumping up to two Digimon instead of just one is a great idea, but if you get their power levels desynchronized, you fall into a weird spot where you either instantly win every combat or get walled. Combat is also a bit of a mess because it's not really balanced around the game design. There's not really a clear curve of which enemies you should be fighting when, so you'll often end up either one/two-hit KOing enemies or way over your head spamming the defend command (blocks most to all incoming damage based on your upgrades, and is pretty much a mandatory skill to buy to progress) until you build up your super meter while hoping your guys don't get stuck doing other skill animations when the enemy starts up an attack. Player Digimon all have a high-damage super move that you have to charge a meter for that deals significantly more damage than every other skill, which will be your ticket out of most combats. The super meter charges slower if you're defending, so the strategy is to charge it just after your defend animation ends and then immediately go back into defending. You spend more time negotiating the animations than actually thinking about what skills you should be using. Maybe I'm playing the game wrong, but this is the gameplay that presented itself to me as the most effective in my 17 hours of playtime.This is a watered down sequel to a classic that misses its mark. If the combat was more engaging/less tedious or the progression was faster, I'd be more forgiving, but instead I ended up really bored. (Please god Bamco, don't let the World series die ;_;)Furthermore, being originally a Vita game, ported to PS4 and now Switch and PC, the game lacks some serious polish and did not introduce QoL features like a greater render distance; which causes items and enemy Digimon to pop-in directly in your face.Despite all this I still enjoy the game greatly after 40 hours of gametime and personally place it just after DW1, but far ahead of Re:Digitize (= DW1 > Next Order > gap > Re:Digitize).If you really liked DW1 and could stomach Re:Digitize you can buy this at full price and get a solid and fun experience out of it.If you unsure you are better off waiting for a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The "Recommended" comes with a huge caveat. Maybe so huge I'm doing you a disservice by adding to the game's positive review score. Still, I had such a fun time with it (when accounting for my caveat) that I think you should play it if you like Digimon, Digimon World, or other monster raising games like Monster Rancher.That caveat is to use mods. To say this game is grindy would be an understatement. Not even a coffee grinder that grinds coffee beans 12 hours a day at a Starbucks is this grindy, and mods help reduce almost all of that. There are mods that even skip the bending over animation your character does when picking up items, which is a seemingly minor change, but over a 35+ hour playthrough amounts to a huge amount of time saved. It almost seems like these small delays, from having to hit material gathering points multiple times to a small delay to wave at your digimon before opening the care menu (e.g. to feed them) were meticulously engineered in order to pad play time, but be unobtrusive enough to be only slightly grating."Slightly grating" they would be if not for the fact that some aspects, like gathering materials to upgrade certain buildings in the city, is utterly dull and lengthy even with the mod to allow you to combine all attempts at gathering into one. Speaking of lengthy, training digimon is also quite a chore. Optimally training your digimon can take quite a long time as you grind out meaningless battle after battle increasing your stats since that is more efficient for your digimon's life span than training at the gym. All of this is even worse if you select "Normal" difficulty which should just be renamed "Tedious" as it doesn't seem to make the fights harder, instead making everything cost more money. All of this is to say that you will start to have an existential crisis as you grind the 100th training session or battle, wondering if this enormous time sink to watch numbers go up like a monster taming Cookie Clicker is an intelligent use of your time. It isn't.If you use mods though, all of that disappears, as much as you want it to disappear. You can grind out stats in a few battles, add to your material count at will, and skip that annoying bend over to pick up items. You can get to the fun part faster, which is battling NEW digimon and talking to them in new places across the world which is genuinely fun to run around in and explore. If they make a new Digimon World game in the style of raising, I hope these things change.

_childDocuments_.review: In someways worse than the previous game, Re:Digitize Decode, and in someways better.RE had more nicer looking locations and especially the main city, but It also had lot of back and forth running between the various services in the city that were spread minutes apart in the opposite ends of streets.Next Order has everything you need close together, but the city is just one screen with fixed camera and it looks really bland and booring in comparison. I have gathered that the city is supposed to change drastically as the story progresses (it is only a one hut and shack next to outhouse at the start of the game), but it doesn't seems to be that impressive in the screen shots that I have seen from the late game either.Having two digimon partners at once is arguably a great improvement. It speeds combat up where as before there was a lot of running around in circles waiting for the both your and enemy's AIs to sort themselves out. That still happens from time to time but generally one of your digimon is pressing for the attack while the other retreats.It also helps greatly that if you fail one digimon's training and get what you didn't wan't there is still chance with your other guy.That said I'm mildly overwhelmed by now having to manage two monsters at once when before even just one was at times too much to handle.The current system for hinting you what evolutions you can get and what stats they recguire is in my opinion the best one in the series. The game gradually reveals first the digimon evolutions names then key stats and then the excat values those stats need to be.I don't think Digimon World 1 had this info avaible in game at all and Re:Digitize had a hint text that told what you need to level, but not the actual numbers or the name of the evolution that reguired them.My only complaint for the matter is that the said evolution info was a bit hidden in the pause menu. In Re:Digitize the hints were in the digimon database that is also a menu option in Next Order, but the evolution info is not displayed there.Instead you have to open your partner's stat screen and then flick left or right several times and I really really didn't figure this out until about three hours in.Seems to have no animated cutscenes that Re:Digitize Decode had which is a shame, but the evolution and attack animations are way better than previously.Plot has always been "just there" in these games so I don't mind it for either way.Video options are very bare bones. No vsync, you have to force it on from the video card control panel. Also you have to turn the depth of field off because it fogs up the entire screen from time to time and won't go a way.That's about it for early review. Too expensive for a identical port of the Playstation 4 port of the Playstation Portable port. They should have at LEAST modded in some of the newer digimons to excuse the price as the identical years old PSN version is cheaper and still available.Buy if you can't help yourself and if Digimon Survive wasn't your thing.

_childDocuments_.review: My opinion on Digimon World: Next Order.For me, this game is excellent. It combines the gameplay of the original Digimon World PSX with a more vast gameplay loop, more taming possibilities, more RPG elements, improved mechanics and clarity in terms of taming and better structure of game areas. All this combined with a more action and fast-paced combat system makes this the modern day Digimon World that is rife to be expanded upon.Only a few cons come to mind, this includes the resolution limit to 1920x1200, if that would be fixed, this game would be almost a 10/10. But this is my rating for its current state:Graphics: Graphic Design is good, pretty much PS3+ quality but held down by the resolution limitation as mentioned above. 8/10Gameplay: Addicting collection, good combat dynamics with a more in-depth mechanic regarding in-combat digivolutions. Also the training system has been overhauled and is actually fun now. 9/10Sound: Great sound design, heavily influenced but improved from Digimon World. 9/10As a Whole: 9/10, Excellent Game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is effectively a sequel of Digimon World 1. Many of the same mechanics are used and improved upon. It's much easier to obtain ultimate (and now mega) digimon and the economy is much more fleshed out (autopilots and portapotties are easier to get).As a PC port, it's fine but not great. The camera doesn't zoom out much at all so 60% of your screen is usually obstructed. You can use B to run, but the game doesn't tell you that. You can change the camera zoom slightly, but the game doesn't tell you that.There's 232 digimon you can have as your partner so it's a massive game. The city is also a lot bigger than the original too with a lot more to do.The price is steep but I'm getting a lot of enjoyment from this so its worth it. Overall it's a good purchase if you're a fan of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, despite its efforts, this game doesn't score. Poorly developed, poorly designed, poorly translated, the quite interesting main story gets drowned in a sea of "whats" and "whys," all while feeling like an unfinished beta for an MMO. Offline.+ The story and characters are kinda cool, with a couple of well-delivered plot twists, and the narration is not too bad.- Immediately ruined by early 2000 Google Translate translations. I understand Japanese is hard, and at least it's not localized by multicolored mentally ill lolcowlizers, but at least the basics—holy fu.- The fights are shallow and boring. It's just a spam of skills and items, quite abysmal compared to the old one where you could actually give orders to your Digimon, things like Calm Down, More Aggressive, which are arguably more important with 2 partners.- The list would be extremely long, but to provide some context to the "poorly developed and designed": The transition from one phase of the day to another is a sharp, blinding, unpolished cut that makes you feel like playing a match of CS:GO where the whole team has thrown flashbangs at you.- Navigating the city menu is frustrating. You have to scroll down an enourmous list cluttered with useless choises like the Meatery Entrance which is a step away from the actual Meatery.A map would've been better- If you train at night and your Digimons get tired, they'll ask first for a nap and only then to actually sleep, making you waste 1 in-game hour- Minigames are boring. Fishing is just a bland and RNG infested quick-time-event. Digimon World 1 had an actual fishing minigame and after 20 years, I would've expected the same. Graveyard Keeper has a better one, ffs- The input lag on several menus is atrocious. 1-2 seconds to register Buy/Sell, like, cmon people.(-) Still no Commandramon. This is a joke, but I was lured into buying the game after seeing him in the promotional material. Unfair

_childDocuments_.review: Game's ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass, and let me tell you exactly why. It's an action oriented game where you have basically no control over what your digimon do beyond a couple of commands. _childDocuments_.review: This is a long one, Critiques and Jokes are near the top, while the Scorecard and Conclusion are near the bottom below the big line.For many who have played the Original Digimon World game, Next Order it may feel like a bait and switch.This may seem at first glance like an opinion to be expected from someone who played the original of a game as a kid and you would be at least a third right, however there is more to this.A part of me cannot help but feel as though they worked hard to remove all traces of made the original a unique and fun experience.A second part is feeling rubbed the wrong way from the poor choices in game design.A third part is hoping that they do better in the future.While a fourth part is questioning how Bandai can believe that the price tag is anywhere near justified. I don’t think that anyone in their marketing team have ever played their own games.All critiques below are in consideration of the fact that this game was made and marketed in an attempt to match the same original style and popularity as Digimon World 1 as its true sequel and not, DW2, DW3, DW4 or any other Digimon games that came afterwards, which anyone playing this game or planning to play it should be in the know of.---The Design and Feel:On my first impression, they seemed to have tried to use references to the original Digimon world game in the starting location, which was a start that briefly had my hopes up, however they were in small, cheaply made ways and the village needed to be at least twice the size on the first zone with multiple terraces and creative flooring themes ready for when it fills up. A huge part of the original game was guessing what the town would look like by the end of the game without many hints and if you show plots ahead of time it removes the pleasant surprises.They could have even built on the original concept and allowed players to move buildings after they are made and allowed you to decorate with the random junk and computer parts that come into existence throughout their world, but they didn’t and instead of making it fun they chose to create a grinding excuse by having you collect materials with set plots. In the original you only had to recruit their builders and wait, Jijimon would have the others do the rest like any real mayor would. File City is not what is used to be.They had a good idea to give Wild Digimon warning tags if they are too strong, which may have been a good idea if the areas had a mixture of difficulties as to what appears in them and could have had scaling blue, green, yellow, orange and red tags to represent difficulties faced by stats and Digi-volution stages, but instead they spoiled it by giving them strictly set levels per zone which broke any sense of adventure that remained left over by the empty bowls made from crunched up tinfoil they chose to call maps.Lead Level Designer: *unrolls a piece of tinfoil onto the table after finishing his lunch and pounding it with their fist a few times* “Raise the edges and throw in some used batteries, this will be our map!”Co-Worker: “Do you want us to remove the crinkles?”Lead Level Designer: “No.”Overall bad maps with little to no design work. If they had a quality department they most likely were in a coma ward the entire time.As briefly mentioned, there is no sense of adventure or mystery in this game and even the soundtrack was designed to remove any sense of adventure by blaring in your ears the entire time leaving no room for contrast in the battle music, let alone the laid-back and often mysterious tracks that instilled feelings investment throughout the original so well received and still loved.---The Gameplay:The combat is somewhat similar to the old game, although the control are different because you control 2 Digimon with either side of your controller, unless of course you’re using a keyboard, which is less relaxing because you have to micromanage both, although it was an overall good idea.The combat is still suggestion based similar to the original which plays into a unique experience that has you anticipating the success of your team and throwing in support somewhat similar to an RTS instead of using mind-controlled meat-puppets like other monster raising games, however the tinfoil terrain has a lot of wrinkles that cause the hit box to often go above or below wild Digimon even though the attack pass right through their bodies, needs terrain polishing and modern hit boxes.The Wild Digimon see you a mile away and often can’t be avoided unless you make large circles around them due to running twice as fast as you do, in the original game you could dodge them because they were sometimes equal speed or faster but could not turn as well as you could adding to the game play when entering smaller areas, because it was fun to play dodge-ball with them, instead of having them run you down like Ghengis-khan on the high plains. More grind than a 17th Century Windmill.---The Graphics:Changes in the art style were something to be 100% expected, however it seemed like they used an engine meant for PS2 games and somehow ended up having graphics are worse than the PS1 game, where as the PS1 game had a unique art style in using pixel art that gave it a certain charm, for this game they never polished any of the landscape, assets or character models.The areas have repeatedly copy/pasted assets that could each be remade in Blender within less than 20 minutes each, these assets do not match the art style of the environmental patching, let alone the character models or color schemes.Between the map, characters and features that were haphazardly thrown onto the map, they all look like they are from three different games with each made decades apart.Overall it felt like something someone new to the franchise would make as a half-hearted project while half-way through school watching 2/5 star anime shows on a second monitor and using a bootleg engine from a PS2 game._______________________________________________________Conclusion:This game used the “Digimon World” name to make sales as a sequel, while re-branding it away from the laid-back monster raising game it was and into the generic JRPG it was never meant to be.As it stands, this is just another grindy JRPG with no heart or sense of adventure.Score Card:Design: 1/5Gameplay: 2/5Graphics: 1/5Story: 1/5Nostalgia Effort: 3/5Company Effort: 1/5---To BANDAII, you used to make good games, you still can if you actually try.Maybe make something original that gives a sense of mystery, adventure and randomness like the Original of this game instead of having the “Big levels = Big Strong” mindset, texture maps that feel like empty cereal bowls and all of the cheap, passionless dialogue boxes.There is a massive market for laid-back monster raising games that no one is tapping into without devolving into 3rd rate JRPGS and the only conclusion I can come up with is that many of the older game companies no longer know how to make games, let alone how to make money.Next time that you reboot a franchise, don’t just put someone from your previous games in charge, find someone who legitimately loves the franchise, have them fill out an essay on what they loved about the original and make sure they understand how to represent its atmosphere.Your other Digimon World games were fine to be different because they were not sequels, you tried new things back then and your fans liked you for it, however sequels are a different ballgame.Stick to the old and work with the strengths of your franchises OR do something entirely new, if you try to do both or water things down you be continuing on this same path, you won’t get new fans or maintain the old ones.Many of your customers are nostalgic and easy to please if you hire the right people for the job, you just have to try.Make a little effort next time and you'll remind us all how to "Momentai."

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly this is just not a good game.I usually don't mind occasional repetitive mechanics in games but this one could be called "Digimon World: Soul Grinder" and it would be the most fitting title for it. Even the menu system is grindy! Like, if you want to exchange materials for example, you need to click through the menu literally every single time, no bulk exchange. It doesn't even show you your stock so you need to interrupt the spam clicking several times to check your stock at another NPC. What this game really excels at is giving you insane amounts of unneccessary clicking tasks and not showing you data where you need to know it. The further you progress the game, the more of your Digimons lifetimes you need to waste grinding them back up to the stats you need just to continue where you left off in your questing. Those things live for like 20 days if you evolve them to mega and dont feed them life increasing food and with a maxed out training hall it takes you 15 days to get their stats to around 5-6k each which is what you need in chapter 4 and 5 and that takes around 2-3h of your real time. Story is the typical "save the world from whatever" and interrupted by mandatory side quest requirements, but entertaining enough (when you grinded back up to continue with it).Battles are mainly you watching them fight and occasionally activating a signature attack, so its neither tactical, nor is there any real action for you to control. Said signature attacks even bug out occasionally, freezing the fight for a while or sometimes even not activating at all. Graphics are... well, this game was originally released in 2016 for a handheld console and they never bothered improving anything for the ports to other devices. It really looks the part. The zones feel rather bare too.Movement feels very slow, you can't skip attack cutscenes, evolution cutscenes, anything really, and your mons do their one sound every time you do something with them until you finally deactivate sfx sounds to not go insane.Even the main selling point here, having a variety of more or less popular Digimon to team up with, was done kinda lazy. Some Digimon have several color or element variants while other, rather important ones even, are missing entirely and many digivolution lines are very awkward. Like, there is Beelzemon but no Impmon and it can only evolve from Garudamon or BlackWarGrowlmon even though at least Myotismon exists?? There is Rosemon but no Lila- or Sunflowmon, Meicoomon doesnt have its usual Mega Raguelmon and so on. Many very weird decisions have been made here and you really need to love the Digimon franchise a lot and also have a very grind resistant soul to really enjoy this game.Edit: There are Mods for this desaster and I highly recommend getting them. I immediately got 18 of which most just make this bearable to play and let me finish it with my sanity intact. Its nice to play now. Still, a game shouldnt have to rely on Mods to be playable so my review remains unchanged.

_childDocuments_.review: When comparing Digimon to Pokemon you‘ll end up comparing a light comedic novel with works from Orwell. All they have in common is that they were printed on paper. That is what makes the Digimon franchise so much better than anything that came before or after in terms of monster taming stories. I have more mental traumas from Digimon than I have from so called ‘canonical masterpieces of literature’. Given, that was due to the fact that I was a kid when Adventures 1 and 2 came out. I will stick to this statement still, however, because those foggers at Bandai did the same to me when I was an adult, watching Tri and last evolution Kizuna. Fogging broke me… And that's why I love this franchise, it’s brilliant at what it does. Now to the matter at hand, the games. There are, in my opinion, exactly two games that are not only good but amazing, this is one of them. It just so happens to be the successor to the other good game. Digimon world offers the next best thing to the experience of the series you can get. I can not state enough how much potential this franchise really has and how little they do implementing it into games. But hey, who am I to judge, there is a reason some execs at Bandai are settled for life and I am not.Pros:-	It’s beautiful, as simple as it is complex -	Same battle mechanic as the first game-	Same raising mechanics, basically a tamagotchi simulator, who knew-	The moment you get the hang of it it’s ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing to figure out your strats, digivolutions etc.-	Mega levels, Omega levels, ♥♥♥♥ ton of evolution tracks-	Meicoomon and the entire evolution track for Diaboromon is in this, including Armageddemon. As a guy who loved tri and the first movie this is nothing short of a gift from Homeostasis.-	ExE evolution gives the edge here. You will have the feeling from the anime that a spontaneous digivolution will save the day. Hell, they even did an emergency version of it in this. You lost a battle, you are ready alt F4 here unly to just see, for some rng reason, your Digimon Exe into omega form and rekt the enemy within 2 turns. It’s fogging amazingCons:-	Being the product of its time one has to remember this is a ps Vita port of a game from 2017ish. Don’t expect the best graphics or even engine performance.-	I can imagine it can be very complex and therefore overwhelming for some people who didn’t play the first game. -	It is an amazing Digimon game, however, it is not an amazing game in general. There are oh so many things fan boys will ignore but the average gamer may not. Not being able to stack-buy at some points, the fact that there might be and overreaching map for larger parts of the map but for the life of me I couldn’t figure out how to access it or the facts that entire mechanics appear to be pointless when playing a certain way.If you love the series (Adventures 1 and 2) for one reason or another this is a perfect enough game for you. I would love to see an mmo or multiplayer based game with these mechanics to exist but as I said, Bamco is great in writing stories for their series and especially movies but absolutely terrible in tapping into the full potential of the franchise. I never had hopes for this one to exist and got surprised so Imma try to keep an open mind and see what the future brings
