_childDocuments_.review: From someone who wanted a game like the original Digimon World for the PS1 I'd say I'm satisfied with what I've seen so far in my short time playing. However I can both recommend and not recommend this game.This game is definitely for fans of the very first Digimon World game back in the day. There are returning characters and even remixed music reminding you of the first game but there are still new tracks so the entire soundtrack isn't just a copy of the original.To raise your digimon, you once again have to feed them, train specific stats at the gym, and making sure they get to the bathroom on time. There is also the factor of weight, happiness, and discipline along with reaching certain stat numbers to reach different forms which while unknown at first, seem to randomly be revealed by just doing things. This saves the need to look up a guide which was at times required for progression in the older game with how specific some ultimate requirements were. It makes aiming for needed forms way more convenient and you can always ignore looking at the digivolution tree if you want a surprise that is hopefully not just numemon.This was the main gameplay loop I loved and wanted in a digimon game and it is simply recreated here. You mainly raise digimon to a decently strong form before venturing out into the world to find NPC digimon to unlock upgrades in the city though this time there is the addition that you are raising two digimon at once for the possible fusions in battle.Battles are again mainly automated making the outcome determined by how you raised their stats, (or possibly spamming recovery items) but there are still commands allowing you to activate attacks whenever you think is a good moment. This requires more of an active role compared to the previous game as your digimon will fire close ranged attacks from any distance and miss instead of running up to the enemy and attacking. You can also just watch them fight and they will run around and do their own thing like the previous game, though having two digimon this time around makes commanding combo attacks pretty satisfying.If you are a fan of the original Digimon World game back in the PS1 days then this is the game for you. It has almost everything from the first game which makes it a fun single player experience and I will continue to play it.But if you have yet to get this game on the PC?So this game has two major flaws that ultimately makes it kinda terrible on PC.The first is a personal reason which is the lack of multiplayer battles. It is a major disappointment that this was not a feature retained from the original PS1 game. Back in that game, you can save your digimon's data to a memory card and you friend can do the same, then you can watch your digimon battle through the in-game mechanics to see who has the strongest. The possibility of having my digimon fight a friends digimon was my main decision to getting this game on PC over consoles as we all have a PC for multiplayer, but this is just a single player game in the end.There's techincaly an online battle feature here but it is in no way multiplayer. It is a very dumbed down 3v3 battle where you watch your digimon fight as the original tamagatchi-like device and not in 3-D as you do in-game. You can only do it 3 times a day and you can't even choose to fight your friends for what little that would of been worth.The 2nd reason is for PC players as this game dosen't really have PC controls in mind. I heard this game was originally made for the PS vita, and the controls reflect that with the entire game having a twin stick setup. The left stick is associated with one digimon and the right stick with the other. It is actually a really good setup if you have a controller but there was little effort put into making it without one.Some games get away with this problem simply linking one stick to the mouse movement but the mouse movement dosent seem to work for things such as the battle radial menu. You can change key bindings in the games options with default bindings having wasd keys for the left stick and tfgh keys for the right, but I did not find any options for the mouse movement. One can say this makes the game playable but it feels ultra clunky and not good to play with a mouse and keyboard at all. You can easily plug in a PC compatible controller to fix this issue but it will feel horrible to play without one as a PC player.There's also the argument of this being a port with a new release 60$ price tag. I'm usually one to ignore the price if it gives the convenience of being ported to a playable device but this isn't really convenience. Unless a patch makes more PC friendly controls, just get it on a console instead if your a fan of the original PS1 Digimon World game.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought the game in discounted price at September 23rd. Finished 100% achievement at October 8th. Steam duration 146h. In-game duration 139h. Previously have played Digimon World (a big fan). I played the game in Easy Mode with available guides as I wanted to 100% the game since the beginning.Plus:- The graphic is really beautiful.- The music (including the remixes from OG DMW) is really good.- Banger OST.- Wide variation of Digimon.- Improved quality-of-life (QoL) features. My favorite is the Dojo.Minus:- The battle system is broken (will rant about it below).- Ugly human character design.- Strange prosperity per Digimon system.- Recruitment seems less impactful than in OG (maybe because there are so many and the Digimons are not even unique i.e. findable as normal enemy).- The 200 Digimon achievement makes the game. This kind of achievement is really painful for this kind of monster-raising game where you cannot raise another before the current one's lifespan ends. - The story is meh, especially that it is not explained why the MC has two Digimons, despite actually being "seen as strange" multiple times during the story.Verdict: I only recommend this game to someone who enjoys the OG Digimon World - but only during a discount, or if they have many dispensable funds. The battle is a hard turn-off because it is game-breaking.REGARDING THE BATTLEThere are major changes to the battle system:a) We will be transported to a point in the map and battle within a circle. In the OG we just battle as is, which enables Hand-to-Hand Digimons to gain advantage on certain maps.b) It uses a Command Point system to order our Digimon to use certain attacks, guard, special attack, or jogress. You can literally ignore the system (except for the special attack a.k.a "finisher").c) The battle seems asynchronous. In the OG if a Digimon is attacked during finisher or attack charging, the attack will be canceled. But not in this version (or sometimes). It's just a mess.d) No friendly fire.e) The finisher is not charged. As long as we have 150 CP we can do it. It will cut into a short animation. It kinda function as a dodge as well, somehow. And we can do the finisher with both of our Digimons at the same time.f) You have two Digimons. And will face more than one Digimon most of the time. It's just a pure chaos. Now we get into the main problems.- Irritable slow-motionThe game will enter a slow-motion whenever we use a finisher, until the animation is played. It seems so random, especially during DigiFuse. I often use boosting moves before launching a DigiFuse, only for the boost to be running out during the slow-mo.- Frozen DigimonSometimes Digimon freeze during a battle for no reason. It won't read any orders. It won't animate. Just there. I thought this was due to it being somehow "knocked out of the red line" because it was when it happened to me once. But other two times, the Digimon is perfectly within the red circle.- Soft-lockThis mainly happened when I DigiFused (finisher with both Digimon). One Digimon refuse to "unleash the yellow aura" thus making the game stuck, as no input will be accepted before the DigiFuse is executed. This happened three times:1. Armageddemon fight in DT. My MetalEtemon (or Titamon, cannot really remember) refused to unleash the aura. Gladly as it was in DT, there was a timer so I could exit the battle.2. Darkdramon fight in MOD Cape. Probably because the map is the narrow bridges. My Ophanimon just froze. I tried to do a DigiFuse, but it still froze, resulting in an un-exitable game state. I had to reset.3. Something in Faulty Ex Machina. I cannot remember well but I think I used a finisher with my Digimon but it froze. Gladly somehow the other Digimon still "attacked on its own" and finished the battle.This seems strange to say, but I far prefer the original Digimon World battle system.

_childDocuments_.review: The long awaited sequel to the PS1 game Digimon World that has some of the same mechanics as the first game where like the long forgotten tamagotchi toys of the 90s where you have to train them, take them to the bathroom, and feed your companion. But with a slight new twist compared to the first version in which there's 2 companions to take care of. Story: You are a teenager dragged into the Digimon world under mysterious circumstance to save the Digi-World. Where you'll meet other people who were also dragged into here and many digimon, some willing to come help you and others fight against you. It's very bog standard story that's pretty vapid. You got all the generic tropes where all the protagonists and antagonist knew each other in the real world. Friendship and all that stuff. It's connected to the first Digimon World game but overall if you are looking for a deep engaging plot, this isn't it. Gameplay: There has been improvements in the battle system compared to the PS1 version but also some significant downsides. The two companions seems like a great idea with newer digimon games adding dna evolution and having them work together to chain combos but with the limited camera distance when your companions hit champion the screen is mostly blocked by your companions backsides standing side by side to you. Also because they evolve and die at different times your companions work on different timers which just gets very annoying. I feel like the game would of been better if it focused on 1 companion.Art/Graphics: Simply put, this game is ugly, the world map is devoid of detail and many areas are just flat textures, with severe lack of any forethought in areas. Character Design is very uninteresting with the male PC having the widest hips i'v seen. It baffles me how ugly some of the designs and areas are. I wouldn't be surprised if the digimon themselves are just 3d models reused from other games like Cyber Sleuth. Overall this game is plagued by bad decision after bad decision. It's a shame that this game is so bad because the roots of it is something that could really be something fun and unique in creature collector but this is probably the worse DIgimon World game i'v ever played. TL:DR Version: A experience not the worth the asking price, Avoid this and check out something else.

_childDocuments_.review: Tbh, after almost 20h with Digimon World Next Order, I still have no idea of what I'm doing.They've made an overly complex system of how to level up & evolve your Digimon, and they never last more than 14 in game days (which is about 90 minutes).They constantly have to eat & ♥♥♥♥ when you train them, it's like playing Tamagotchi on crack, and when they die you have to restart the process from baby Digimon all the way up to Ultimate & Mega (which I haven't successfully been able to make yet, even though I had the right stats for it).And it's useless to go out in the field before they're at least Champion or higher, since most wild Digimon that you have to battle are also Champion or higher. In short, you have to progress through several cycles of training before you can even progress with the story or else you'll be too weak to continue, but if you do too many cycles your Digimon will die of old age (14 days), meaning you'll have to restart from Baby again.And sometimes you get stranded with an evil Digimon that refuses to evolve, because it needs negative stats to evolve (i.e. unhappiness & disobedience) which are stats that you want to avoid since they kill your Digimon faster.However when you actually get to battle & progress the story, it's a fun game, it's just all these in between things that drag out the game. I think the excessive amount of grinding is what's holding back an otherwise good game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun until it wasn't. The major issues here can be unpacked by explaining the game loop. 1. Train your digimon. This is entirely menu based, and is the primary way through the first half of the game to raise your party stats. You will spend, no joke, at least half of your game time in the gym screen. 2. Explore the areas outside of town, collect items, do quests, battle enemy digimon. You must collect items to level up your town. Area exploration is... fine. It is nothing special. 3. Battle. Your digimon attack on their own, and you can occasionally press A to increase a command gauge. Manual commands take command points. The crux of combat revolves around using the "Full Defend" Tamer skill (learn it early, or you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥) to defend against telegraphed attacks. The camera is awful, animations are the same for every digimon, and they skate around the battle zone like an ice rink. 4. Death. Your digimon will die, and when reborn, they are only a fraction of their previous strength. You have to grind money to level your gym to gain enough stats to ensure that they are strong enough to level into stronger digimon to ensure that they live longer so that you can venture further and complete the game's quests -- *gasp* and they don't just die overnight, they can die at any time. Like when you're walking towards a boss encounter.Apparently, stat growth is heavily diminished on higher difficulties. I chose "Normal", and now it's uninstalled.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I'd recommend this game for $60. I got it on sale for $30 and I feel that's a fair price. I'll come back to why. This game does an amazing job at satisfying Digimon nostalgia. If you liked Digimon World on PS1, you'll like Digimon Next Order. You play a tamer that has 2 digimon training them and digivolving them to be as strong as possible. When the digimon get old enough, they revert to an egg and start the cycle over. You have tamer skills that will effect this and other aspects of the game. So you get rpg-lite and roguelike elements if you're a fan of those. You're also getting other digimon to come live in the city to expand lots of different things you can do there. The story is also pretty good and is entertaining and enjoyable. The characters are perfect for the Digimon world as well.My criticisms are are that the UI is basic, the controls aren't great, and there isn't a great way to track things within the game. There's only a few menu's and they aren't the most intuitive. It feels like the game was designed for a controller, I haven't tried using a keyboard so I can't say how that is. But the controller works well otherwise. There isn't much of a tutorial for keys; so look at the key bindings, because key's you'd expect to open a menu or perform an action don't. Quest tracking is pretty terrible and it's unclear what is active or completed. Sometimes I just wander around because that works better, I'd recommend taking notes.42 hours in and still having fun. Definitely recommend and a lot of fun, but don't expect a high end super polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, are you wanting to get into Digimon, but you know nothing about it, and just want to get the "definitive" experience?Well, look no further, friend!So, for those new to this franchise (and probably visiting from the Pokemon series): Digimon debuted around the same time as Pokemon, conceived by the makers of Tamagotchi as a sort of "Tamagotchi for guys". It started as toy-like devices where one would raise monsters, who eventually would evolve into stronger forms.In 1999, this same concept was made into a Playstation 1 game called Digimon World, where they added a story adventure to it (which was just before the various anime REALLY took the idea and ran with it).This series comes in all kinds of tones and genres. Lately, it's done turn-based RPG (Cyber Sleuth) and visual novel (Survive). Some with a story that's light-hearted, and some that's  surprisingly dark.But this game... is basically Digimon re-visiting its roots. And paying homage to where it came from. And it is wonderful, sort of coming home.------Q: "Lore-wise, how are Digimon different from Pokemon?"A: Digimon are fully sentient, with almost all of them able to speak. They generally have the same level of intelligence as humans, as well.They benefit from tamers, by naturally receiving energy from them, which can unlock greater strength and allow them to evolve quicker than in the wild. So humans are basically Chaos Emeralds to partner Digimon.Gameplay-wise, Digimon also have branched evolutions (unlike the more linear ones in Pokemon). And many evolutions even re-converge.To put it in Pokemon terms: imagine a Pichu choosing to evolve into an Abra, then evolves into Charmeleon, and then finally evolves back into a Raichu. Complete with a flow chart in-game that even shows what else it could have become. Returning to the game: Your character raises now two digimon at the same time. Due to a strange event, your character gets digitized and pulled into the Digital World, the mysterious homeworld of Digimon, where you are met by your two partners.In this strange world, you operate out of a dilapidated hub city that you must help rebuild, serving as your HQ. You'll help to uncover the strange events going on that are messing with the Digital World.You continue to train and feed your partners (plus maintain their health, and make sure they have needed bathroom breaks) as the three of you explore. It's not easy at first, but as you recruit certain NPC digimon, they'll unlock features that make things easier, like a farm to grow food, an item shop, a hospital, etc.At one point you even have a gym that helps to stat train.Your digimon will over time grow up, and evolve into stronger forms.But beware - they also have limited lifespans, and will eventually grow old and die.Thankfully, digimon never truly die, and your partners will reincarnate as hatching eggs, ready to resume their training.As a tamer, you too earn EXP, and can acquire skills that assist you in raising your digimon (such as one that allows your partners to keep 10% of their stats when they reincarnate, allowing them to be even stronger their next life)As for exploring and story, your progress is only really limited by how strong your digimon are. They stronger they are, the farther you can safely travel. The graphics are very nice, the camera is excellent.(Especially for those coming from Cyber Sleuth, this camera is a full 360 degrees. And the world is lovely terrains (grasslands, deserts, volcanoes, etc))And the menus are very nice, especially compared to the original Digimon World.In general, it's a lovely new(ish) game based on the style of the old games.If you're a fan of Digimon: you should get this game.If Cyber Sleuth's story and missions (and limited setting, and fixed camera) weren't your taste: then you might well love this game. If you're new to Digimon, and want to try a "definitive Digimon experience": then this is probably what you're after, a series returning to its roots.And yes, I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: One of the worse Digimon Games to release, on par with Digimon World 2.The PC Port is riddled with problems like screen tearing, unoptimised Mouse and Keyboard controls, and crashes. The Options Menu is Sparse due to it being a Port from the Vita -> PS4 -> PC. It's a 7 year old game... improve it or put some effort into making the PC experience better, not worse.The Translation is basically machine translated since the sentence structure is often wrong or simplified to the point where it conveys no information.The budget and philosophy behind the game reeks of an unexperienced and uncaring director. Every system and mechanic is designed to be a time sink. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------It takes the breeding experience from previous games such as World and Digimon Adventure and plays around with the idea. It is completely simplified in the worse way. The time limit is still there but now there are only 6 stats, HP, MP, ATK, DEF, CRIT, and SPD. Spells and Physical Attacks all scale off the same stat and eventually you're going to max everything anyways. Since all Digimon share the same skills, there's no real reason to pick one over another. It's just RNG combat at that point. There is ONE big improvement and that is after a battle, you can unlock the ability to see what stats will allow you to digimon to digivolve. That's about it for improvements. Everything else is worse than before.Something that could've and should've been improved on are the moves. You learn moves through select enemies and it's completely based on RNG. If the Digimon doesn't use the move, you can't learn it. If they do use the move, there's a small chance for you to learn it and it's all up to the RNG gods. You can spend hours farming 1 move and never get it. It's made worse in the worse way. There is no variety to any of the attacks. There are 9 elements with 7 moves in each but they all behave the same. There are single target attacks, multi target attacks, and buffs and some will have status effects tied to them. However, single target attacks are all fireballs, multi target attacks are all light fields, and buffs have almost no effects. Fights are very lacklustre and you just end up spamming your ultimate.The worse possible change is the hidden stat gate. Rookies, even if they have superior stats to Champions, will never be able to beat Champions.The overworld... is your typical bland, empty, vast, and linear world. There's not much to do but there's so much to travel through. Every map is a small hallway to travel through. There are times where you will need to pick up materials but you're not incentivized to do so since there are 3 cutscenes each and every time you need to pick stuff up. This applies to the town as well since Cutscenes are everywhere.Overworld skills... are a deal breaker. When you start the game, you have a skill menu full of nonsensical and bland skills. Most of them have to do with expanding your inventory or increasing the amount of items you gain when you pick stuff up. It's an obvious time sink. None of the skills are actually interesting. None of the skills actually change the game up or make you feel powerful. They just give you more of what you should already have. This leads to the costs in the game to scale at an exponential rate rather than incremental. Everything is just straight up expensive and bad enough that I'd recommend playing with a mod just to speed things along.The quests are largely uninspired. It's mostly go from point A to point B or fetch. Lots and lots of fetching. 90% of the game require you to just grab a ton of items you cannot farm for.Commands are removed. Instead you have this strange pseudo system where you ask them to use specific attacks. You can no longer tell your digimon to fight at a specific range or mainly use specific skills. You basically just tell them when to escape.The most major bug is the fact that pathing is broken. All digimon has trouble managing corners. The larger the digimon, the worse it is. The arena you fight in is pretty small and when your digimon tries to navigate the outside ring, they will clip, stutter, and be straight up unresponsive. You can apply this to the overworld as well. If a digimon chases you, you can run into terrain and they'll have trouble following you.The music... it's one of the only games where it's offensive enough that I turn off entirely. The loops are broken and there are even times when the sounds either don't line up or don't play at all during important cutscenes. You might as well fire whoever ordered the composer to come up with this garbage.The game doesn't respect your time and designed to be grindy. Everything scales exponentially meaning that you need to invest an absurd amount of time just to reach any goal. This is especially true if your digimon decides to off itself right before you fight a boss. Of the 20 hours I've played so far, I can say that only 5 of those hours were spent actually playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on good reviews, I was hopeful to get a modernized and improved experience of the beloved Digimon World PS1 game, but once the nostalgia starts to wear off it's clear that the game is unpolished and has major issues in the world design and visual aspects.TLDR; If you loved the original Digimon World game and don't care about visual design, level design, pacing or balancing, then you might enjoy this game. Not worth the full price, get it on sale or from other marketplace. PC port is bad, maximum resolution is 1920x1200.The game is essentially Digimon World 1 with expanded game mechanics. You have two digimon partners instead of one and there are a lot more digimon to raise. Now you're also able to gradually discover digivolution info, which is the most welcome addition and it was implemented really well. The game is also more transparent when it comes to raising your digimon, it's much easier to avoid care mistakes because everything is explained and all digimon conditions are shown with indicators.Combat is better for the most part. You have more control over you digimon's actions and the mechanics are expanded, you're able to do combo attacks and use DNA digivolution during fights if conditions are met. They have made rearrangements of the original songs and the nostalgia train hits hard with these ones, the music transports you right back to the childhood days of the original game. Also many of the sound effects like digimon noises have been done faithful to the original, which was a nice touch.Despite almost nailing all the digimon raising related stuff and basic gameplay mechanics, everything else in this game feels rushed and unpolished, like the developers didn't just care. Worst issue for me was the total lack of any kind of visual or artistic direction. The game is just absolutely horrible to look at. Compared to the original Digimon World, this game has no charm or style with the world. The environments are bland and boring to a degree which is honestly just baffling. It also makes no sense that the most unpolished areas are the starting areas, which you will spend the most time on while leveling up a new generation of digimon. You would think that most work was put on the areas where the player spends most of their time, but clearly no thought was put on this. Making things worse for the starting areas is the music, which sounds like it belongs in the main menu where you only have to listen to it for one second max. It doesn't fit the atmosphere at all and becomes jarring really quickly.Adding to the horrible level design, it doesn't help that all the recruitable digimon are just scattered all over the place with no pacing or rhythm. You just see them standing there, in the bland environment, with nothing interesting happening and the way to recruit anyone is to either fight them or do a fetch quest. Compare this to the original game, where you actually had to explore to find the recruitables and often times do some detective work based on hints the game gives you, which was much more interesting. In Next Order everything is handed to you on a platter and you just mindlessly wander around the god awful environments.While I felt the combat was an improvement from the original game, it's also dragged down by the non-existing balancing of the game. Think you can beat that rookie digimon with your two ultimates? Think again. For the most part the difficulty is tied to the area you're in and how far it's from the starting city, but there's still massive variance. In one area it was easier to fight my way to the "boss" than beat a single generic champion digimon in the same area. The enemy digimons have their levels shown when you approach them but in multiple cases the levels didn't mean that much. Also when it comes to training your digimon, it quickly became clear that WIS and SPD stats are nearly useless, the power of your digimon is mostly based on all the other stats.I was also disappointed to see that the fishing minigame was butchered too. In the original game fishing was at least somewhat interesting, in this game it's the worst excuse for a fishing game I've ever seen.Trying to summarize, the game feels like the devs were given a task to implement all the basic stuff from the original game with some exciting additions, but when it was time to design everything outside the city, the deadline was only few days away. I had fun training and raising the digimon but soon enough just the thought of having to travel to the outside world became so uninspiring that I had to drop the game. Also the PC port is pretty bad, you can't have a resolution higher than 1920x1200 for some reason.

_childDocuments_.review: I was coping hard about this game being fun but its really not. Everything is a pain in the ass to grind, you need to spend more time balancing the needs of your digimon to ♥♥♥♥ and getting items is painfully slow and sometimes you just might run out of critical items which are locked behind quests you can't do, if you're even aware how to do them. This game is impossible to play without a guide and even with a guide, all you learn is how much of a pain in the ass it is to do.Let me give you an example: there are constant random encounters that wipe the floor with you if you don't excessively train. In fact, you're supposed to spend like 2 in-game days as part of the tutorial doing nothing but grinding your partners up into rookie level - this is gonna be a repeated pattern because the world outside is that dangerous. Even rookie levels can kick your champions ass - not right away, but there is so many encounters and you simply don't have the funds to get enough healing items to last more than a few battles. Unless ofc you grind for it, notice a pattern? When your digimon reach the end of their lifespan, which is like 20 in-game days, they die and lose ~90% of their stats. _childDocuments_.review: Besides the key chain games, I am not very aware of the digimon games as a whole. I know that some of the PS1 era games hold a special place in some folk's hearts.I do like monster rearing simulations, this is what attracted me to the game. I'm not sure how I feel about this game yet, but there is a serious lack of polish on it. There's very few animations in the game, when your character collects resources, it's just text boxes. Same with stuff like training your digimon. I would have really enjoyed little cut scenes, like they did in Monster Rancher when it came to training.The combat is "meh", for me. It's alright, but I feel like it also divides your focus because you got two digimon in your party, you need to worry about them both. I've also already encountered a problem where some digimon simply don't have any sort of standard attack. I really would have preferred a more standard JRPG style combat system. The game maps aren't great at conveying what's going on, things like map entrances and exits aren't shown so it feels like you are wandering around looking for the digital gate to move between maps. The game also has this weird thing where it dumps a ton of text on you and then kind of just shoos you out the door. There isn't a ton of direction in the game and it's pretty likely you're going to end up wandering in to an area you aren't supposed to and it's going to be full of monsters of a way higher level than you. I wish there had been better character customization. You really just choose between two main characters. I don't regret buying this game, but I regret paying full price for it. This really feels like a $30.00 game at best. I was really hoping for more simulation and less Pokemon, but this is what it feels like. It feels like an unpolished, watered down version of Pokemon. Some of the screenshots gave the game a bit of a Persona vibe, but I don't believe that now.

_childDocuments_.review: After all these years, this is the Digimon World remake/remaster we ended up with: A revamped Unity engine from another digimon JRPG.If all you care about are graphics and having a bigger rooster of Digimon to look at, then go ahead, you gonna have a good time. You get to raise 2 Digimon at once this time around.For Digimon World fans, this game does not have any of the essence or charm from the original.Combat tries to trick you into thinking its similar to the original but digimons just gravitate towards and away from one another randomly while appearing to be floating, the camera keeps zooming in and out and switching angles in an attempt to disguise how terrible everything looks. The interface is designed to look deep and interesting but its just unnecessarily confusing. Attacks dont cause interruptions, digimons just joust through each other so there is no strategy, just like in any JRPG, whoever has the bigger numbers win. You dont get to learn attacks from defeating digimon, there is no list of the attacks you can unlock in the game, but then again, its not like it matters anyway.As far as raising digimon goes, somehow they managed to make the already limited options you had on the original even more limited. You are not allowed to praise or scold whenever you feel like, you cant take your frustrations off on your digimon and you cant just sit and have a good time petting it for a while completely disregarding how spoiled you are making it, you dont get to enjoy the cute grunting sounds they make now and then, instead, most digimon will constantly make loud annoying screeching sounds while text says exactly what they are trying to say, which is often just "yeaaahhh!!!". You dont get to see the giant poop they make, you dont get to see their fart in the toilet either. To put it simple, the people who made this game never owned a tamagotchi.There is no room for imagination and there is no room for discovery. This game has a enforced tutorial for everything and 2 tutorials for combat.Finally, the only real reason this gets a negative review is because of how much they are charging for whats essentially a mod of another game.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was brainwashed by Bandai at an early age to associate Digimon with happiness, I am fairly confident when I say this game is not good from any perspective, despite all it has going for it, and if you expected a holy grail of Digimon games that excels beyond its predecessors, this isn't it. That's the tl;dr of this review and you can stop now if that's all you needed. If you're interested in my reasoning, you can keep reading.This is a port of a PS4 game, which is a port of a PS Vita game, which is a sequel to the original Digimon World game (that is quite a mess I will get into later). The original is a pretty unique game even in its own franchise. Other games in the series typically aped other genres and didn't really set itself apart well, but the first Digimon World was a unique experience I've never seen replicated by any other franchise to date. It's a formula I felt was charming and had a lot of potential. Next Order sought to take that formula and enhance it for a modern audience. The problem with this game is that it retains far too many of the original game's flaws, what is changed isn't well thought out and doesn't go far enough, and what is entirely new isn't all that great. It's technically better, but given the time that has passed, these improvements are pretty basic and insubstantial. This gets more obvious as the game goes on and you begin to realize that what you experience in about the first few hours of the game is basically all there is to it, and you won't be seeing any of its mechanics mature or transform over time as the game gets harder. The result is that the game becomes less, not more, engaging the longer you play as it quickly turns into a set of repetitious tasks you've been doing from the very beginning, and will be doing until you conclude the story. You may come to this bitter realization quicker or slower than the person next to you, but most people who are not die-hard Digimon fans will figure this out well before the end of the game.This is also, compared to the PS4 release, a barely enhanced port. An easier mode, a run button, very few graphical options and the ability to play on your PC for $60. That's a hard sell. I also guarantee you the positive reviews you see are from die-hard Digimon fans unconcerned with boring gameplay. If you're expecting this to be a solid game on its own, you will be disappointed, fan or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World Next Order is really just a mediocre game that is fun to play. If it wasn’t for a certain place in town and a certain Digimon to buy stuff from, I wouldn’t have beaten the game. I liked the game, though.The GoodIt’s sort of nostalgic because of all the old Digimon that you get to see in the game.It kind of feels like you are adventuring through the digital world.If you do the coliseum and then buy a certain cheap item using the coliseum money, you will never need any other items. Though, the other items that you can buy do help a lot.The graphics are nice. It looks old and outdated but new. The game is voice acted for most of the game.You can save whenever you want.Nice skill trees but I feel like certain skill tree paths should have just been giving to the player. Like, how am I supposed to know that if my Digimon lives longer, they digivolve into a new Digimon? In the show it just happens during moments of weakness.You can upgrade stuff in town. Like make trips to areas cheaper. Why make the cost to fly to an area expensive to begin with? Just make it one cost! The BadThe difficulty spikes are all over the place. If you aren’t prepared or didn’t save before talking to a random digimon, you will be sorry. I don’t think the game was balanced.Boss fights for some digimons, and boss fights at the end of the game were straight up cheap. They would do so much damage to your Digimon that you’d have to revive them cause if your Digimon survived, the next hit will kill them.Another thing I hated was that your digimon die. When I was going through the very end of the game, one of my digimon died. I just used crystals to digivolve it to a champion form and I was training and waiting for it to be an ultimate so that I could digivolve it into a mega. I used so many chips on it and since it died, it was wasted. Like, once your Digimon dies, you have to start all over. And when you speed up their digivolve with the crystals and make them a mega, they are still super weak. The whole process of leveling with your Digimon depends on them experiencing fights for a very long time. I spent in game days training that one Digimon that died, after I made him a mega. He was still so weak that he just wasn’t good enough for the end game but I wanted to finish the game. My one digimon who survived had to carry the other.That one Digimon that died near the end of my game, I think was bugged. I tried to heal him at the hospital and the angelmon did, but he still kept coughing. I tried to use a medicine, but that didn’t work either. I’m sure it was bugged. It sucked.The story is crap. It’s just not good enough.I think the game is too expensive. This felt like a $20-$30 dollar game. Buy on a deep sale.Music was okay. It was calm. One track I liked.Multiplayer portion of the game is stupid. You get matched with peoples Digimon who are at megas, even though you are weaker. And they make you have to sit through and watch each battle one by one. They should have just had all three of them fight at the same time instead of wasting peoples time. Also, you don’t get any money for losing so it’s again, just wasted time. The only good thing about doing multiplayer, is that if you do win and get multiplayer money, you can use 4000 to buy a chip. It’s hard to win and honestly, it’s not worth your time doing.Again I must say, the stats of your Digimon don’t carry on. Not even a little. So these expensive 1 time use chips gets wasted, and the game doesn’t tell you that, when your Digimon dies, the stats that you boosted for them goes away too.The map is so confusing. I memorized a lot of the areas but some places I didn’t remember how to get to. If it wasn’t for the bird in town, it would have made getting the places a slog to get to.Whenever you try to go against the narrative when they give you  option to do so, they force you to go with their plan. I guess it’s nice but why give the player an option to begin with?I don’t understand how Digimon look human. I never really liked that. And for a certain thing regarding the story, I didn’t like that as well.Because this game is like a pet simulator, the Digimon make so much noise all the time. When they are hungry, when they need to poo, when they are tired, when they are out of mana. Literally everything. It’s so annoying that I turned off the sound effects to stop hearing it sometimes. And then sometimes when they’d not want to wake up or something they give you an option to say something to them. I said that it’s good that they want to sleep in and not wake up. But the game doesn’t like that so it decreases your digimons mood and stuff. It’s stupid. If you want to force the player to do an option every time, then why bother?The player is a silent protagonist.It’s a very grindy game.Digimon randomly digivolve into something else every time. If you think agumon will turn into greymon, don’t.Luche’s voice actor sounds annoying. Like she’s doing a fake girly girl voice. I don’t know. It sounds so fake. I didn’t like it. That one blonde bad guy sounded bad too. His voice trying to sound evil and maniacal was so bad. I didn’t even know he existed for most of the plot.The game ran bad when I was recording the game. When I wasn't it ran good.The Digimon that follow you, take up so much of the screen.In-game settings and options leave much to be desired.Lore dump at the very end of the game sucks!ConclusionWord count is getting too big so I must stop. I liked the game but I really think that if you are interested in getting this game, and are trying to get some nostalgic feelings towards digimon, then wait for a deep sale. Trust me.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE Digimon. I absolutely L O V E it. There is not enough QUALITY Digimon games, etc...Just lots of expensive, sub-par merchandise and mediocre video games, unfortunately.Personally, my favorite game iteration is Dawn/Dusk. I know people don't necessarily want their Digimon games to be "pokemonified", and I understand that, but that game made the most sense to me in many ways, especially being a childhood Pokemon player.This game, on the other hand, is apparently a port of a PS4 game that I had no knowledge of because I don't play PS. The game itself is built off of DW1 on PS1, another game I did not play much of, but enough to assure you that they didn't improve upon the concept at all.With all of that out of the way, I DO NOT enjoy this game. I've tried and tried but I just don't understand it. I understand the CONCEPT (Tamagotchi City Game) and wish it was better... But it's not. It is what it is and I have to judge it based on that.This is just tedious nonsense. There isn't much of a game here... It's just like run around, pick up sh*t and watch your Digimon fight terribly by themselves and die. That's it. That's the whole game. The narrative is trash, the characters are trash, the graphics are trash, there IS no combat, there is no control of digievolution until a certain point in the "story" (I use that term lightly) which I never made it to because I'm so bored and confused that I have no drive to get there. I could go on and on and on. This is a massive waste of time. I would rather play Dawn/Dusk for like the 10th time than continue trying to play this. There isn't much "progress" you are actually in control of, and the issue with this is when you look up help from people who HAVE played this game and DO enjoy it, it seems like a lot of "lol git gud" or that you just don't get it. And maybe they're right... I don't get it... Because it's not fun or logical.Before I finish, I want to mention that the people who love this game and will hate this review aren't looking for another Digimon JRPG, but I WAS, so you can hold your complaints.I understand your perspective and my opinion on that is: You deserved better. This sh*t is terrible and the only reason you like it is because there is no other alternative.I am PAINFULLY aware that there is no other game this like.Great concept, horrible execution... I have NO idea why this is even a port. It was clearly dated ON release and put literally NO effort into making it a proper PC port. This seems like a port for those who have played it before, not for those looking for more Digimon games like myself. With that said: I WOULD LOVE TO SEE THIS CONCEPT AGAIN BUT NOT HORRIBLY EXECUTED IN A ZERO BUDGET GAME. I will not refund it and will simply encourage Bandai Namco to continue to make Digimon games, although it feels like my confidence is misplaced as they clearly do not care about making quality Digimon games. I mean, this ORIGINALLY came out in 2016 and yet it feels like a mid PS1 game. Wtf happened? This is legitimately embarrassing for PS4 game, and I should not have to explain why.You may have a different experience from me, but as a Digimon vet who LOVES the Vital Bracelet, etc, and has an extensive experience and knowledge of the franchise and the concepts this game tries to play on, this port and game doesn't need to exist at all.I would love to see a new version of this game with a budget higher than a single Snickers on the CEO's desk split amongst the team.DO NOT BUY FOR $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order from the offset seems to present improvements in design upon the classic Digimon World 1 formula. Yet manages only to complicate an already inaccessible system in a way that makes the rough original look like a masterpiece of game design.The game is incredibly imbalanced where the game seems designed to make grinding the only option, and is so poorly communicated that it’s own methods to present more information to the player like levels for enemy monsters only serve to mislead player to the difficulty of the content.I loved Digimon World from back on the PS1 so I thought I’d finally give Next Order a try. I played on Normal Mode up to the start of Chapter 2. What awaited me was a series of increasingly ridiculous difficulty spikes and utter hard stops on any town building progress behind singular battles. Situations where your Rookie can wreck level 1 enemies and get destroyed by level 2 enemies in the same area. Unsatisfying progression where Champions will smashed by random rookie enemies in early areas. Ultimates can get smashed by random level 3 Red Veggiemon. Talking to the wrong "friendly" NPC can start a battle with a “level 20” Black Agumon and Black Gabumon that plot-wise are pirate apprentices who'll hand your Ultimates their asses with ease, each stronger than the Mega end-boss of Chapter 1. While level 30 something Psychemon in the desert go down with ease, and a lone level 30 Seadramon is reasonably challenging, this confusing mess is all stuff that happened during the opening section of the game. Digimon Next Order tries a more story-driven approach that is actually completely at odds with the design. In Digimon World 1 you only need to recruit Digimon to the city, to gain access to 90% of the world you only need to meet Coelamon, defeat Drimogemon, obtain a champion to move a boulder, and fight Meramon (and not need to win) something you can accomplish with your starting digimon, opens up the world. An advantage of World 1's freeform nature is if you have any difficulty w/ one encounter you can go do something else. Where you’ll only really ever need to grind in order to face a handful of Ultimate Digimon battles and the final dungeon, which allows you to obtain all city/training upgrades in advance.Digimon Next Order has other ideas, feeling that you need to grind just to face up against anything but the lowest level rookies on literally the first screen. Digimon World Next Order takes a very bizarre approach where areas a locked off by progress, early game areas are filled with enemies you can beat alongside immensely powerful foes that aren’t accurately portrayed by their evolution stage or even the level displayed. Many Digimon that can be recruited can't be until certain main plot events. This creates a problem where it's very easy to exhaust all recruitable digimon and get brick-walled by a plot encounter.The mandatory bosses go Meramon (Champion) --> Birdramon (Champion) --> Kyubimon (Champion) --> Machinedramon (Mega) Skipping any kind of gradual difficulty curve in favour of an exponential jump the games only desire is to brick wall you into grinding! Make sure to unlock the guard command with tamer points because the game is practically impossible without this entirely optional skill as enemies tear humongous chunks out of your Digimon's HP pools if not one-shot them if they aren't guarding. Progress isn’t rewarded in Next Order, you’d think the evolution to a new stage would result in you being able to test out their new abilities to see how strong your mon has become. But it really isn’t. This is a game where evolution stage is irrelevant and only achieving a certain level of stats matter. This results in a game where evolutions don’t feel special or a step up  and are instead only valuable in that they extend your mons lifespans to do more grinding!  Your rookies get torn apart by other rookies, your champions may get beaten by rookies, your ultimates will struggle two on one against a Champion and so on...Considering this is a port of a 2016 game I cannot believe they didn't go back and smooth out these issues, I refuse to believe in the last 8 years its only now these issues have been pointed out. I can only recommend this if you're willing to play a game that bewilders you with confusing information and expects you to master it right out of the gate or be locked out of progression.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited way too long for the proper sequel of OG Digimon World from PS1. I've waited some Digimon World game that is *designed for PC release*. Yet this is it! THE sequel! THE proper one!So you know Tamagochi? That virtual pet-care franchise give inspiration to the original Digimon virtual pet; the concept was Tamagochi but for boys, where the creatures do battle and (in later versions) jogress (JOin proGRESS - basically a fusion) instead of marriage when two device connected. You must train and care your Digimon prior to those all, and the way you care will determine on how the Digimon will evolve and perform later. After the target market for the game think "I trained my vpets and continously winning, then what next?", the dev then developed the original Digimon World PS1.This game is exactly that, but now in full 3D environment AND with a VERY long story!You basically warped to Digital World and must fight against Machinedramon terror. While doing that, you will slowly restore the city of Floatia and uncover the mystery behind the terror!Pro:- The STORY! A surprisingly well-paced story for its niche and genre, even after you get your Digimon into Mega (the highest possible level of a Digimon)- The GAMEPLAY! Compared to the prior Digimon Worlds, it as very wide roster for Digimon partner choice! The battle is straightforward; it evaluates your care for your Digimon instead of making you whining about enemy difficulty. It also has settable difficulty choices to ease/harden things up. The game also has justification why several underleveled Digimon in the anime series can have insane battle performance. And yes, they have minigames - the true quality-time mode to make memory with your companions when they are approaching their end of lifespan.- The SOUND! The BGM especially is AAA grade so you don't have to worry having your adventure very bland.Con:- The STORY! It features key people from the other games: Re: Digitize and Cyber Sleuth, so new player will be confused.- The GAMEPLAY! Economy is hard in this game! In the late game, you will be forced to farm something to fund your Digimon training program. By the meaning of "farming", no, it is not your regular RPG farming ritual; it is very grindy and in the long run, you'll 100% wonder whether you have bullied or scammed those digital lifeforms. About the monster-collecting aspect, I'm not sure you will be able to collect all the Digimon here on time, because unlike other monster collecting games, it really takes time to collect them all (unless you want to speedrun for it after you unlock certain game feature).- The SOUND! The dev really reset the sound during building change in the same district, which ruin the really chill atmosphere if you try to roam around in that district.Conclusion:My playtime spent speak itself: a very good game for the rare and niche monster-caring genre. It feels more adventurous than the VN-style Monster Rancher and less clunky than the original Digimon World. A good game if you need to take a breath from your daily activities and decide to chill literally in Digital World.

In this game when I raise my digimons to Mega, they can become powerful which could be a rewarding experience.Only get this game if:- On heavy discount- You are a diehard digimon fan- You want to turn off your brain to grind- You don't mind your digimons got an expiry date (They die around age 15-20, there is a way to keep them alive forever but that's end game)

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing sequel to Digimon World 1. It has a TON of content, and really can be as hard or easy as you want it to be. Compared to Digimon World 1: Well this game has way more Digimon and features, doesn't run at 10 fps, the battle system is more engaging, and it has MEGAS. I like how you can easily get stats and life in the end game. Unfortunately it gatekeeps a ton of Digimon behind story and town progression. I also don't like how tedious grinding materials is, materials take forever to grind, they could lowered to 1/3 of what they currently are, you will have MAX stats Digimon before barely upgrading anything with the builder.However to this day Digimon World 1 still has this game beat in a few ways: Open world, far more choices in what Digimon you want to recruit and when you do it, better animations and sound effects for eating, pooping, happy/angry, faster paced. THE MOST IMPORTANT: Digimon World 1 had the best arena to this day, every day you would go to Greymon and it had RNG decide a random tourney to participate in, in this game and Redigitize they ruined the arena with premade challenges that you beat one time and forget about it. _childDocuments_.review: I'm exploring beyond my level, when a stronger digimon challenges my partners. They get defeated, and the screen goes black, I expect to go back to Jijimon's house. Instead the main theme starts playing, and my partners begin to do the fusion digivolution, and go into their ultimate attack. They defeat the digimon, and unfuse, and I feel like I just lived something out of Digimon Adventure or Digimon Tamers.Digimon World: Next Order understood the assignment of making a game that appeals not only to Digimon nostalgia, but that also is a worthy successor to Digimon World. Quality of Life improvements like showing the required parameters to digivolve to certain digimon, giving you information about digimon questlines, a moveable camera, notifications when items are around, a toilet in the gym, and fast travel in the city!Downsides are, well, two digimon means twice the food and recovery items, new items to collect for city development, it's easy to get lost when the camera repositions after battle, and sometimes you're struggling to get the right digivolution because your digimon's stats are just too good. There are probably other problems that my nostalgia riddled brain cannot see.This is a great game to experience the first Digimon World for the first time, it's a great game to relive your nostalgia, and given Digimon World's complexity it's also a great game if you're looking for a more advanced creature battling game than Pokemon.

_childDocuments_.review: No Gammamon = Thumbs down.However, your two rookie-level digimon can randomly jump out of excitement while making cute noises, and that’s enough for a thumbs up from me.They also get pouty when you don’t give in to their silly demands, but they immediately forget about it when you offer them sweets or a good greasy steak.And if you have the heart to scold one of them for being a little brat, the other one helps with the telling-off. Absolute sibling behavior.So... yeah, cuteness overload here.I had so much fun with those little interactions that I even forgot that the actual embodiment of cuteness wasn’t one of the available digimon. Sometimes.... Nah, who am I trying to lie to?Unfortunately, there is no option for petting or head-patting, so that's a big negative.Now into the actual game... well, in summary, it’s.. not a bad game.Graphics feel kind of old, and the music is... forgettable for the most part.There is also a story. With words and a plot, i guess. But... erm... sorry to say it didn't caught my attention. At all.Gameplay is like one of those Tamagotchi games, where you take care of the basic needs of your creature-thing, but with battles, experience, levels, and evolutions. And... there are two of them, so you have double the fun, double the advantages, double the issues, and of course, double the poo.Like... they make a lot of poo. Like... a lot. Like... they release a turd the size of their body every three hours.And they don’t even eat that much. They must suffer from diarrhea or something...Maybe that’s why they live so little...Also, the game is hard. _childDocuments_.review: It is a fun game for people who like Digimon. There are a lot of Digimon to get in this game, and their Digivolutions are not as wildly disconnected as the ones from the original Digimon World. I have never been unsatisfied from the results of one of my partner's Digivolutions. The game's story is really basic, and after having played it once before, I am just skipping all the cutscenes and dialogue as quick as possible. The best thing the game has done is capture the spirit of the original Digimon cartoons, in its battles' secret mechanics. I do not want to spoil this mechanic, because finding out about it from experience is one of the most memorable experiences I have had playing video games. Yet, even after figuring out how it works, I still get goosebumps when it happens because it is designed extraordinarily well. All the elements come together to make for iconic moment, so I still get goosebumps. This is really the reason I recommend the game, because it has managed to capture lightning in a bottle. The game must have been designed around this mechanic, and it is such a great design choice that I am convinced other developers should aim to recapture similar moments and experiences in their games.Next Order is also a really difficult game that does not provide a lot of guidance as to how you should progress. It is extraordinarily absurd at times, as otherwise "weak" Rookie Digimon can absolutely and unexpectedly destroy you and your Ultimate Digimon, if you are unprepared. Some general tips are to dedicate yourself to training in the game's gym for a week, before leaving the village, and then training by defeating enemies. Stat increases from training in the gym take an hour of in-game time, and your first Digimon will die after 16 days. On the other hand, you can battle other Digimon 30 times in two hours, so you can get 15x stat gains from battles, as well as money and trainer experience, in the same amount of time as a single training session. Essentially, this mechanic is the same as the one from the original Digimon World, because when your Digimon die, they will resurrect as babies, but their stats will be higher than they were in their previous life. For this reason, I suggest playing the game in easy mode, the game's difficulty simply changes the amount of stats Digimon gain from battles and training. In other words, the difficulty setting simply changes the amount of grinding you must engage in. The battle system is simple, and gets more engaging once you figure out how to time blocks and Order Points. Simply block before an attack hits, and time your orders immediately after Digimon strike an enemy, or defend from their attacks. You can also stun enemies by using your special attacks, as this will sometimes launch them into the air. Because you have two partners, you can time their special attacks to keep enemies perpetually in the air. Overall, this is a fun game. If you like Digimon, you should definitely get this game. Postscript: The Digimon I fight to grind stats are: Goblimon/Psychemon (Lvl. 5, 8) in the first area, Black Garuru/Gururumon (Lvl. 8), Piddomon in the Logic Volcano (appears in the afternoon only), Psychemon at Server Desert (Lvl. 23), Black Gururumon (Lvl. 24) at Server Desert, Seadramon in Mod Cape, the lone WarGrowlmon in Faulty Ex Machina (Lvl. 34), WereGarurumon in the Bone Cemetery and Platinum Numemon in the last area of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- It is a Digimon game.- Both in terms of aesthetics and building, the new City is vastly better compared to Re:Digitize Decode.- The Tamer Skill system adds a welcome spin to the DW1 formula.- The Interface is cleaner than Re:Digitize Decode.- The story isn't getting in the way of the gameplay. I thought the game would be more story-heavy like Cyber Sleuth, but I'm glad that wasn't the case.- I like the design of the places in this game more than I thought I would.- The new Gym is less visually stimulating than DW1, but it is nice they made it less of a chore.- The bonus system in the Gym is better than DW1 too.Cons:- I get their goal with giving us two partners, but it isn't worth it. One partner would be better.- Why always prompt a window when I'm near a pickable item? I don't need that hint to appear every time.- I'm not a fan of the threat level system. The digimon levels (Rookie, Champion, Perfect) should've been sufficient.- The digivolution requirements are often more complex than DW1.- Sometimes the lighting on the Digimon models can be off-putting.Overall, this game is fun. It is on the same level as Survive but way better than Cyber Sleuth.As a successor to Digimon World 1, it marginally succeeded on giving me the same vibes.It is not a better game than DW1, but that would be a tall order.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely similar to Digimon World: Re:Digitize and the original Digimon World, but with the added twist of raising two Digimon simultaneously. I'd recommend playing one of the others first, or at least being familiar with the Digimon franchise. Cyber Sleuth & Re:Digitize are much better starting points for first time Digimon gamers. You'll focus on monster raising/training for the most part with traditional RPG elements like visual novel talking with NPCs, small quests, exploration, item gathering, and upgrading your home base. Progression is slow and tedious. There's a lot of repetition as well. Honestly, the difficulty level is a bit high and there's a huge amount of traveling/back-tracking. Being patient with upgrading the tamer level/skills and the home base/village facilities is needed. Also, taking advantage of daily handouts at the village is necessary.The graphics are serviceable, but could be better. Just like how Re:Digitize was originally a PSP game, this one was originally a PSVita game. So I can be a little forgiving. The aesthetic of the digital world is a little basic. I think they tried a little too hard to make some areas large/open, which resulted in emptiness? I vibed with it better in the original Digimon World and Re:Digitize, but I haven't finished the game yet.The controls can get a lil bit of getting used to. Especially getting used to the different menu navigation or each individual Digimon. (I've been playing mouse & keyboard). Be aware of the mouse location when navigating menus. I wish there was slightly better camera control. I didn't find out about the zoom in/out at first (Q, E on keyboard). The game world is made up of small interconnected areas/rooms just like the other World monster raising games. The map could be more serviceable. You can zoom out all the way, but it's just boxes, although accurately placed. Getting area completion to 100% is tedious because of the discovery radius and big pixels. Not even sure what function it has either other than having a map with clean edges. Sprinting (Holding down right mouse click) is extremely necessary. The fast travel is extremely handy for navigating the village as it grows. The transportation system is very inaccessible due to cost early on in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly entertaining. There's no time restriction and you can play the game at your own pace. It is as grindy as you want it to be, but if you're not interested in sinking as much time in, switch to easy difficulty. The difficulty levels don't determine how strong the enemies are, just your own digimon's growth.Absolutely recommend.

Yes, there's some grinding to be done, but at least everything in the game is freely accessible, along with DLC content such as eggs and extra missions.Pros:+ Huge selection of different digimon to get; it's nice to be able to play as the variants of the original digimon e.g. Psychemon (who's one of my favourites).+ Good replay value.+ Very good storyline, if a little predictable.+ Great graphics; at least great enough for me.+ English VA (including Richard Epcar voicing MetalEtemon again!)+ Good homage to Digimon World 1 such as having Mameo featured, his references to his adventure years ago and the continuity which connects them both.Negatives:- Almost all of the music from Digimon World 1 isn't featured. (I would buy it as DLC quite happily).- No curling.- Fishing isn't particularly exciting, though neither was it in DW1.- Missing some iconic digimon such as Digitamamon, Frigimon, Ninjamon, Shellmon, Drimogemon et al.I haven't played any Digimon game before this since Digimon World 1, so I am probably bereft of the cynicism and disappointment of the other games and therefore I can rate this game very favourably.It is worth it; especially if you enjoyed Digimon World 1 back in the day: it's the closest we've/we'll got/get to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very similar to Digimon World on the ps1, maybe a little easier to mechanically understand. Of all the games to come out since then as far as I know this is one of the only translated ones that scratches that same itch. Just front loading with a little bit of good to know information:- I would first play either digimon cybersleuth (a very good, collect em all type rpg game with a bonkers story) or the physical digimon toys (which if you haven't, are slightly more involved tamagotchi, almost literally. One of the digimon is literally a tamagotchi) before going into this game. The information you can glean from understanding those games is transferrable to this, as stat gates and requirements work similarly. This is much more complicated than either, and you can probably orient yourself with the in game tutorials but having a background helps tremendously, and both of those options are regularly cheaper than this, and cybersleuth on steam is basically two games.- Play on easy mode if you like. You can change this later, but it basically only affects digimon growth and doesn't affect combat difficulty. It is the original mode the game was balanced for. Normal and hard are good for quickly cycling digimon when you better understand the mechanics. - Dispel the idea that your digimon will permanently be strong. The mechanics incentivize your digimon dying and being reborn, to be built up to be stronger, to die and be reborn again. Don't go into this expecting to collect all of the digimon and put them into your bank, instead, work towards getting an exciting new rabbit-named-like-a-dog-with-blue-jeans-and-a-minigun as nature intended.------------------------------------------------------------For the review itself:This game is very charming and cute. The plot plays out like you're a digidestined, the dub has a very charming kinda stuffy quality similar to the original dub of the show. It feels very intentional and I enjoy it. It's not as "mature" as cybersleuth in the sense that it's not basically just smt but replace demons with digimon, but it does feel a little less childish in tone for the most part, at least to the point that it doesn't feel aimed at literal babies.The graphics are spartan, this is a second time port of a ps vita unity game. They've definitely made it look much nicer, and I think it being on Unity means it's a better port than most bandai namco ventures by default, but most of the visual upgrades are in texture fidelity and toggleable affects like focal blur. That said, the models are pleasant representations of the characters, and I think the visuals are charming. They even have both your digimon follow you around in the overworld basically everywhere, which is something people complain about not happening in pokemon games. The gameplay is... bizarre. It's kind of an autobattler you're intended to interrupt to either charge up meter for a special, or give tactical commands, but the digimon move and space themselves (I believe) according to stats and attacks with little involvement from you. Depending on which digimon you change to, your default attacks can be virtually useless, but after you learn some attacks you're able to give them to other digimon. You can also throw items to digimon and if they have a good bond you can have them combine attacks or do a cross transformation, but in practice this is basically just a really flashy special attack. The meat of the game is actually managing the digimon outside of battle. What you feed, who they fight, what they train, whether you train them, whether they use the bathroom, whether you make mistakes all contribute to how your digimon will grow into its next evolution. Seeing what they become, good or bad, is what's interesting about the game. The digimon will die. This will stop forward momentum in the story, so you spend another 5 in game days growing them from scratch (much faster this time thanks to all that killer progress you made the last cycle) and get even stronger, only to have it happen again. How fast this happens or how fast you gain stats  is what changes between difficulties, so really it just comes down to how long of a grace period you want between cycles, which for 100 percenting, normal is probably a good thing to toggle to.I haven't finished the game, because I'm always compelled to screw around in games like this. I may never finish the game. But I'm fine with that, I'll just keep making broken digis. That's what I like, and it does that incredibly well. There are a few downsides, for one I wish there was some other level of interaction with your digimon. I think having a bond between trainer and digimon grow via discussion or cutscene would have been interesting, especially since you effectively have the same two digimon mentally throughout the entire game. I think they should make them romanceable, like that insane digimon director wanted in that other game. I'd pay to romance gargomon.The other thing I don't like is the price. I had this game on ps4, and on there it was cheaper on release, possibly around 30 dollars? so the intro price on this is shocking for how little they added (you can hold b to move faster) I think for anything under 30 it's a great buy if you even vaguely want a game that fills the digimon world void. I feel bad for complaining about the price considering that, but it's just not a good pricing structure for how little they did on what is a twice-ported ps vita game that was probably shockingly easy to port given the engine.

_childDocuments_.review: Got the Steam version (because I love this game that much) so here are my thoughts.Stuff I like:- It's Digimon! A Digimon World game, even! They're so cute!;- Many of my favorites (Piedmon, GranKuwagamon, Cherubimon Virtue, Vikemon, Machinedraymon etc) are in the game;- Battle system where you can influence your partners' actions and make them stronger;- The postgame stuff is fun such as how cute they made Diaboromon and Machinedraymon in their respective portions, and how entertaining the Lucemon fight can be even with max stats;- The Realm of Outdoor Poop and Malevolent Fist quests are really entertaining, I especially like Kaoriel's name and the crown's supposed prophecy;- The leadup boss battles were quite challenging and fun, although VoltoBautamon was surprisingly easy (at least at first);- The sound effects and music make me feel old (in a good way);- Rina is in this game.Stuff I dislike:- A lot of digimon are just recolors or several variations of Royal Knights, and many of my favorites didn't make it (Andiramon Virus, Koemon/Cannondraymon, SaberLeomon, Babamon etc);- Your partners can get a major injury just from losing about 1/2 of their health by the end of battle especially if nearing the end of their lifespan, and this can happen very early on when you have no resources whatsoever;- A couple of game-breaking bugs like your digimon freezing mid-battle or the menus getting stuck, requiring a hard reset;- I already save scum by default, just how I play games, but it's still annoying that I have to do this sometimes due to the above issues;- Your digimon no longer eat their toilets like in the original;- Rina is in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I wish I could put a neutral on. I'm putting a yes to help the publisher see that there is interest in digimon world 1 style gameplay.As fun as it could be and the fact there is a good game here is the fact that it's under a major problem. The game is unpolished. There is many problems that aren't major but they add up more and more. The dev team either did not have enough resources, was given to the wrong team, or worse.. they didn't care about the ip and what it's based on.Functionally it's what I look for in a digimon game. Raising digimon, fighting others, recruiting into a town to build and grow. It's great it's not them trying to copy other generic rpgs for once and going back to what digimon was supposed to be.Don't get this game at full price. Wait for a sale, this is not a $60 game.
