_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but there are glaring issues that just ruin the experience for me.- The game environment is huge, ugly, and dead. There are no beautiful environments to look at and are all uninspired. The game just feels like it was developed half assed and lazy. The environments are so unnecessarily huge that it takes FOREVER to traverse. There is one area where it literally takes half a day to get to the other end of it and there is only ONE Digimon along the way. It feels amateur. It reminds me of those amateur Unreal Engine projects where the developer has no sense of scale.- Digimon are not encountered in unique ways like in Digimon World 1. The recruitable Digimon are just standing on the path on every area with no rhyme or reason. It feels like they are just randomly placed. They don't move either. There is no life to them. Not a single talk-able Digimon moves in this game. They all just stand 100% still at all times. The recruitable Digimon either just join the city, battle you, or send you on a boring fetch quest. That's it.- No spoilers but the main story is awful. Sometimes I have no idea why I'm doing the thing I'm doing. The writing is miserable and sometimes hard to make out what exactly is going on. This game is a fetch quest simulator. I knew I was in for a bad experience when the first 10 events were fetch quests. There is a side quest that sends you to Leomon, Leomon sends you to a castle, then you go back to Leomon, Leomon tells you to go back to the castle, then you go back to Leomon, then Leomon tells you to go back to the castle... You do this about 6 times. For no reason... They are far apart from one another too, At one point the castle is going to fire a laser and destroy the entire map and you are only a few steps from the boss but since this game needs to waste as much of your time as possible the quest makes you go back to Leomon to get his advice on what to do about the laser and boss... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WHAT?! When you go all the way back to Leomon he's like do what you can to stop the laser. NO ♥♥♥♥! Then and only then can you go all the way back to destroy the laser. Bony Resort does this go back and forth ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ also and it takes... FOREVER.- Many of the items are just color pallet swaps. There is nothing unique about them. The digivolution items are awful to look at and they are named with a random name generator. You'd have to be an autistic savant to remember names like Miserusimamane and Lureskerditinane and associate it with the proper Digimon. All the Digivolution items are named that way so have fun. I've acquired about 100 of them and can't recall a single named Digivolution item. Color pallet swapping is the theme of this game. Most of the Digimon are color pallet swapped as well.- In Digimon World 1 you can generally tell who you can beat in battle. This isn't the case here. Think you can beat that single rookie level Digimon with two Megas? Think again. I've had 1 rookie Digimon wipe my two Megas in less than 20 seconds. Then there are cases where I think a Mega will destroy me and it goes down in 5 seconds. The balancing is abysmal. This game uses levels to determine the difficulty of an enemy Digimon. But it makes zero sense. I can fight one lvl 40 Ultimate Digimon and beat it in a couple seconds and then I'll fight a different lvl 40 Ultimate Digimon and it will beat me in about 5 seconds.- There is only one stat that matters in this game: Stamina. You can pretty much ignore the rest. The game tells you to train one Digimon with STR and the other with STA. DON'T DO THIS. STA is the most important stat for both Digimon. Without a ridiculously high STA stat your Digimon will die instantly to Rookie Digimon. I have two Mega Digimon with 4000 Stamina each and they get 2 shot by the last boss. I don't know what I'm supposed to do. Training grinds to a halt at that point and enemy Digimon no longer provide stats after battle unless they are lvl 40 Ultimates in the last area of the game but they are almost impossible to beat. Also they are a long hike away so... It would take me roughly 4-5 hours to grind the stats needed to even attempt the last boss again. That's insane...- There seems to be a bug in the game where all praise and scold events stop permanently and this is what made me quit. I've played the last 9-10 hours with hundreds of battles and hundreds of training events with zero praise scold events. This means I can't get digivolution hints or other benefits like Digifriend from praising or scolding. After 3 generations of no praise scold events I just couldn't take it anymore. - Also some of the perks just seem to not work... I took the perk for raising the benefits when I was getting praise and scold events and nothing changed whatsoever. Same stat increases. Even if the perk did work correctly it is still useless because those events don't trigger anymore. The perks to boost happiness, bond, and Digifriend also do not work. The perks that do work just suck and are beginners traps. The boost to happiness when feeding and pooping give you an extra 1% which is completely worthless. The perks for rebirth that increase stats are so minimal it's almost worthless. The perk for extra stats after battles gives you a measly +2 bonus. It's one of the most expensive perks too. What a damn shame.- Training at the gym is awful and a waste of time. Even the maxed bonuses you can possibly get you will only increase your targeted stat by maybe 40 at a time. When your stats go to 9999 that's mind blowing.- The grind was bearable at first. Then I started the grind for Red Digizoits. I played for 60 hours and only received five when I need around fifty. So I looked it up and yeah... They spawn in only two locations and they are ultra rare. I even maxed the perks for mining and I played for 4 hour grind session and received JUST ONE... Great! It'll be a lot of fun playing another 60 hours to get those materials. It wouldn't be such a big deal if it wasn't required for upgrading the damn Training Hall.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order is a PC re-release of an older PS4 game with the same name. The main difference you'll find here is, the addition of beginner mode and boosted move speed by holding down the O/B button, otherwise it's the same game. Starting out, players should be aware that the game offers 4 difficulties, you would think "Normal" is the game as it's intended but really "Easy" is that option. The only thing it changes is how fast you can get stats, enemies do not get weaker and you do not get any handicaps, it strictly cuts out grind time which this game already has plenty of on "Easy".Old fans of Digimon World 1 and Digimon World Re:Digitize will immediately be at home as they get through the opening sequences and are brought to File City. Like the aforementioned games, you'll be recruiting Digimon to the City to improve your facilities and progress the story line. Unlike the old games, you will have 2 partner Digimon to help you do this, both of which you will have to raise and take care of. The addition of the 2nd partner Digimon opens up many possibilities from ExE attacks (a sort of DNA digivolution that temporarily merges your partners into 1 stronger Digimon like Wargraymon + Metalgarurumon = Omnimon) to intentionally (or accidentally if your not careful) letting your partner Digimon's lifespans go out of sync in order to have a stronger partner around to help power level the freshly reborn Digimon. I think the 2nd partner Digimon really opens things up and brings what the series needed in order to stay fresh and give more advanced players like myself to play with.There isn't really any difficulty curve to this game, you either immediately figure out that battling and moving on to the next area is the best way to make progress with your partner Digimon's stats or you waste a few lifespans trying to train at the gym. Personally I had 0 issues getting Megas on both partners on their first life-cycle, but I can see how a new player might get tripped up by this if they're not willing to experiment and explore right away. The good news here is that you can lose battles in this game and you aren't limited to 3 lives before expiration like the old games, your partners will just be a bit upset.The game has a good way of making you use your resources if you want to be truly efficient enough to raise the kind of Digimon that can take you through the whole game. By forcing the play to explore to find new Digimon to bring back to the city, you are constantly making use of items and city facilities like the restaurant, courier, and stock market to squeeze the most out of every in game hour and not wasting your partner's precious lifespans.There's honestly a lot still left to be desired here, like the lack of day/night cycle specific events from old games for instance. The game is made in Unity and you can tell, it's a bit buggy sometimes (thankfully never game breaking) and there's nothing impressive graphics or animation wise here. The story is subpar, something we've seen a million times in the series, someone/thing trying to destroy the digital world, save it. Despite all of this, I think it's a great game that old time fans will love and new fans could easily learn to love. I hope one day we'll see a high budget Digimon World!

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe I'm just bad at this style of Digimon game, but it was hard as nails. At a certain point towards the end of chapter one I was just lost and wanted to give up because the game was really hard and my partners were getting beat to a pulp. It took a lot out of me to push myself to get passed that initial hurdle, but once I started to understand that pushing your digimon to new heights is key on each generation I started to enjoy the game more and more. After my partners died about 14 times, grinding money and food and resources, I beat the game and was so proud of myself. It was a weirdly exhilarating feeling. _childDocuments_.review: First and foremost let me say this, I love Digimon. I absolutely adore it, would I suggest this game to people who enjoy raising creatures and seeing them change form and get stronger? Of course that's the nature of these types of games. I personally think a remaster of an old Digimon game will bring you more enjoyment than a current Pokemon game by a mile.I will however stress this immediately if you're a completionist and looking for an easy completion I would look elsewhere. A couple of achievements in this game that make the game time shoot up a staggering amount just for the sheer RNG Elements in it. If you've played Cyber Sleuth you might be familiar with the Medal achievement it's also in this game but with 564 or so cards you need to find it via harvesting materials.That aside! _childDocuments_.review: I loved Digimon World 1 on the PS1 as a kid, and I love this one even more.Initially wasn't a fan of having 2 Digimon partners, but I quickly changed my mind after having played for a bit (ExE and DNA Evolution are awesome!) Although, keeping both Digimons' lifespans in sync was a bit tricky at first, but I found it easily manageable after upgrading the city enough to unlock certain features.The battle command system has also been improved, and the Digimail system makes it easier to keep track of quests/where to go next. The bonding system adds a new depth to the game and has made it even more enjoyable (my favorite experience so far was thinking that I've lost, but then suddenly triggering a miracle since I was at max bond. It truly felt like an anime moment!)I haven't finished the story yet, but it's been interesting so far. It really is a direct sequel to the events of Digimon World 1. Overall, it feels like a modern and improved version of the OG, while still staying faithful to the genre. So if you enjoyed the first game, I'd definitely recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: Really brings back the nostalgia from the original Digimon World 1 game.  Story is decent, pacing is okay, but most importantly, it's a Digimon World game, so you decide your pace.  It could take you multiple generations to complete the story, or you could do it in two or three generations.  That's up to you.  Handling two partners seems intimidating compared to the original, but there are many more mechanics and guides to help you manage them both.  The only thing I can highly recommend is taking a visit over to the NexusMods and grabbing a few mods to increase the quality of life of some of the mechanics in the game.  For example, having to click multiple times on a resource gathering spot and watching a dinky little animation everytime gets old extremely fast, especially considering how much gathering you'll need to do later in the game.  There's a mod that deletes the animation and gives you all the resources at once.  Amazing QoL adjustment there.All in all, definitely worth a shot if you're looking for the DMW1 nostalgia.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, I like the story. It's a ported game and so the controls are keyboard-based. I don't have a controller and it worked out fine just playing with my keyboard. The game is a bit grindy at times. In this game, you gain stats mainly from battling, not by leveling up. I would recommend people to do a few extra battles as soon as they're able, just to get the stats of your starters up right away.Now for the big question: Was the digimon death and rebirth mechanic an issue?My short answer is No, it's not an issue. Digimon die after about 18 ingame days (without talents or buffs).I understand why they went with it. It was probably introduced to keep people from sticking to the same 2 digimons throughout the entire game. You start by picking 2 digi-eggs from like 12 different eggs. These routes will, for the most part intertwine with one another and all options are viable. It's also possible to start with one digimon and then swap to another using digi-evolution stones which starts to become available pretty early game.80 hours in, my digimon have died a total of 5 times, but that is mostly because I let them. I enjoy trying out new combo's. I'm currently somewhere in the mid-game and I already have plenty of ways of keeping my digimon alive for much longer. I wouldn't be surprised to find that you can keep your digimon alive indefinately later in the game.I hope this helps!
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation comes ignoring any issues with the port and it's price tag and I would encourage anyone interested in buying this to wait for a sizable discount.That said this game and it's fore-bearers, Digimon World, Digimon World: ReDigitize, and Digimon World: ReDigitize DeCode, are all in my opinion quintessential examples of the "Pet Raising" genre of video games while still containing violence. It's not about collecting an army you mostly just end up shoving into a box, it's not about assembling a team with carefully managed attributes and skills. These games give you "partners" you have to care for, protect, and lovingly raise to bring out their full potential. They're not perfect and they're not for everyone but I think everyone should at least give them a try.

_childDocuments_.review: The nostalgia in this game goes straight to my feels. It's like they remade the very first Digimon World for the original Playstation. I was a lonely kid. When I was 7 or so, I used to like to imagine I had digimon and pokemon friends. Therefor I played the first game to exhaustion - one of those games that you'd have thousands of hours logged on Steam. There's this way this game tears at my emotional seams when my partners get hit in combat, train hard, lose a battle, and eventually die. There are so many emotional cues not only in the story but in just normal gameplay. On top of that, a special friend I met while playing another childhood game remake introduced me to this one. We've spent hours talking about digimon since. It's like the lonely kid in me finally made a real friend!This remake struck a chord with me. Not only is the old play style the same, it introduces new and improved mechanics that felt like the old game just got a modern content update. I have very few complaints - all of which can be fixed with a mod on Nexus. Thanks for stealing my adulthood to relive my new and improved childhood!
_childDocuments_.name: Digimon World: Next Order

_childDocuments_.review: So I never write reviews on games. However i have played this on PSVita and PS4 for about 1,000 hours on both. and have beaten the game many times with First generation life of all Digimon Types.For New players into the Digimon Series of Games there is many different styles and each style is vastly unique and quirky in its own right. Just note knowing that they are all different depending on Series and Genra of the digimon line you like to play.This Style of Digimon game uses a lot of the Core Mechanics from the Original Digimon World on Playstation 1 and are very Loyal to the Key aspects of that game with a lot of improvements on how you go through the pathing of the game.The Key Mechanics being1. You Use a Raising System instead of a Leveling system. The Key aspect here is since we Raise our Digimon. What this means is that Your Digimon has a Life cycle before dying and you restart on new Digimon! (Extremely Important! IF YOUR DIGIMON DIES IT COMES BACK SLIGHTLY STRONGER THAN BEFORE PRESUMING YOU RAISED ITS STATS). If you raise it correctly to reach Champion/Ultimate/Mega you will also increase the life cycle of your Partner digimon. Later in the game you can give 6 hours of Life between them and is useful if you want to Offset or Onset there life cycles so they remain together or apart. There is also a few Items and Food that can Extend or Lower Life span!. The other part of Raising System is that they have a Bond Level/Dicipline Level and Happiness Level. What these 3 do is really a Key aspect of the game for all Combat aspects. The Higher there bond is with you Influences there Combat Power in the game to use abilities without wasting MP. The Higher the bond is with 'Each other' Influence when they help each other out in combat. For example as Combo attacks to Raise damage by 1.4x or if one is about to take a big amount of damage the other will teleport beside them and Guard with them to reduce damage. Dicipline influences both Combat and other interactions with your Digimon. so if you want to feed it specific food to boost stats it can refuse that. or when you are Mid combat wanting a specific ability out it can also refuse to listen to your Battle Orders mid fights. Happiness influences generally all of the above plus a lot more However if they are happier it is a Higher chance for Bond increasing to happen and make the game a little easier. One thing I didnt mention above with the Bond system and its a Key aspect of the game. Which is if you Have 100 Bond between yourself and both digimon together. you can EXE at Will once a day for free as long as the Digimon are Either Compatible with each other or if you have any single Mega. and create a much stronger digimon.2. My favourite part of Digimon world 1 was Recruiting digimon to your town to help you progress and make progression much easier if your digimon ever die. Each Chapter in the entire game requires a Prosperity to reach further into the game or you can not proceed any further. Chapter 1 requires 25. Chapter 2 is 50. and so on. (only 100 out of 200 is required to beat the game) However all the digimon you recruit offer you Various benefits either from Shopping items to heal your digimon or to fly around the map without wasting game time in exchange for Bit. there is also an Upgrade system to each aspect after you recruit Veemon to the city and have finished Chapter 1. For all New Players to Next Order I do highly advise you upgrade the Dojo once you get Grap Leomon in the city. The reason for this is you can have him Lock Specific digivolging lines so as you dont accidently digivolve into something you dont want. (you have a very slim chance to Digivolve into any Digimon even if you dont have all the requirements for said digimon but if they dont do the digivolve they will die)3. I was going to only do 2 things here. However for the sake of anything that doesnt want to grind forever lose digimon and repeat the cycle. There is 2 Ways to train your Digimon the Gym and Combat. I will split this very important detail here because it fully changes how a lot of people play the game. The Gym Only use this if u are in training 1 and In Training 2 digimon. Reason being In Training digimon get a Huge boost especially later when u have the gym upgraded. If you use the Gym it passes a few hours of the day and lowers the Natural Life Span of your Digimon significently faster than doing Combat. Combat No time passes at all during Combat. so if u find an area u can get some stats on 200 HP & MP and 20 on any stat you want to raise. Abuse fighting those digimon without training to Maximimze how long your digimon are alive. Most of all just to take full advantage of the Stats get some Tamer EXP for more Useful Skills! (Guard is the most Broken when you obtain High Guard as all damage is 1! also if u Go into the Guard Animation u can redo the ability to cancel it and redo it instantly! ABUSE IT!) Also without spoiling anything major on what the Stats do or the Abilities. just know that High Attack Power doesnt always mean 'Stronger Ability' even basic level 1 abilities are really strong if used correctly ^_^I do hope this was useful to some new or old players to the Digimon Series and Enjoy the game. Key Note Digimon World 1 on PS1 was only 25% Complete and half the items did nothing because it wasnt finished. This Updated variant on the Raising System Everything works with a few game breaking things in between. it is a Really relaxing and fun game when you get the hang of the basics and just want to go through a general story or achievement farming. I have always loved and will always enjoy this as a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Blow me for not having played it for long and already reviewing it, but this here is a No-Brainer to me.It is the original Digimon World for the PS1 i loved so much but cranked up to 11.So many new additions while mostly sticking to what made the first one so great for me. Yeah having two partners at once is something i didn't like too much at first, but it already feels like i will enjoy it soon. I didn't like the majority of the newer Digimon World titles lately, because it felt like your Digimon partners were just throwaway pets like Pokemon. And i hated it.The new Digimon World makes it finally like your partner(s) and especially your decisions matter. Don't let it fool you that your Digimon doesn't stick long on it's higher Levels for long and you have to retrain them overand over again. This was common in the old Digimon World. It encouraged you to learn from mistakes and train harder to get the Digimon you wanted. I can understand if it is frustrating for others, but for me it was what made it so great. You can always look up a statsheet and see which stats to train the most if you wanted a specific one and you can still do it in this new one. But even better so becaues the game itself does give you the information the longer you train your Digimon and over time you know what to go for. Then there are more than welcome additions to the gameplay. Skills by itself. Your trainer finally isn't just some.. kid that runs around and yells it your Partner anymore. You actually can get your Digimon to live far longer now and get the stats you desire faster once you trained yourself enough.Obviously though there are downsides too, but honestly? They aren't that severe as some make them to be.Yes the graphics could be better, but the first thing i did was get myself a upscaled pack to get the graphics to an actual really good looking standard. The resolution is one thing that bothers me really myself, but it's okay. My 4k screen just helps make it look the best it can be even there.Aside from that the only thing i really hate is that it is again a plain console port. Bias against consoles aside, it just makes every game worse if graphics and other things are kneecapped just because consoles never gonna be up there with the graphical fidelity a PC can bring to the table.But that is how it is.. It's awful but that is what the industry became. 90% of all AAA games are by now just console ports. So holding it especially just against this game would be wrong.Price already got slashed. And i got it on a sale for even less, so for 30 bucks i won't complain about a game i will be able to play for weeks again. No. If you are a Digimon fan and especially if you enjoyed the first Digimon World.. this is a must buy. Don't let some bad reviews here fool you.Update:As i expected this game completely consumed me again. Just like the first Digimon World, i have a game again i absolutely love to play day in and day out. Even just messing around and trying to get that one Digimon you love so much is a lot of fun.Of course i do have seen some more negative aspects in the game, but compared to the upsides and how miniscule they are, it is just ridiculous reading these as major flaws from other reviews.The more you play, the easier it gets to get that one Digimon you aimed for. And once you have the upgraded Digivolution Dojo you can even directly block Digivolutions you don't want.The random aspect you think is "random" is what Digimon always was and it works just like the first real Digimon games had it in mind. Your stats decide which Digivolution shows up. The rules you think are "how it is supposed to be" is something the Anime made up. The "randomness" everyone is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about is the true nature and intended way how it should work.The only thing i can still say is negative like it was annoying in the old Digimon World is of course the lifespan. Even fully upgraded it feels short, but it is of course meant for you to have a chance to not just upgrade your Stats from the get go, but also right wrongs you made on your first try or even try a new Digivolution line. Hell i at first intended to have a Gatomon and a Guilmon. I restarted, because i realized how hard it is at first to even get there. Then i ended up with first two Renamons which i wanted to be Gatomon and Biyomon. Later i had a normal Kiyubimon and a Silver one which then ended up with Taomon and Silver Taomon. Which did kinda gave an RP feel to it of two Fox gods watching over you, which really kicked ass hard. I am not gonna say the game is perfect. Obviously you can see that it is an "older" game by now, since the graphics really are lackluster. All i can say is to mod it a bit. Helps a lot to make it look serviceable. (4k Texture mod with Reshade and Special K for the resolution itself, also adding V-Sync)The game isn't released long yet for PC and i really hope the modding scene is picking up. Trust me. If enough players really get passionated about it, the modding community is going to make this the best Digimon Game we will have in a long time.Cybersleuth was boring to me. Your partners in there feel like throwaway one time use Digimon often, since you get them so fast to what you want and then never change them, making it boring fast. Having this system of your partner changing his form all the time makes it so much more fun to explore new ways to play the game. Sadly we won't see much more official content updates for this game now, since it is obviously just a old port from the PS Vita from 2016. But that is why the modding community behind it would become so important. I doubt we gonna get a similar Digimon game again anytime soon. Most likely it is just back to the old 08/15 boring ass JRPG formula. (Don't get it how this Genre is still so popular after over 40 years, it has been done to death)No. If you just play it for an hour, you barely get a chance to really see what the game has to offer. This is sadly the reason so many people dislike it, since they just think the Anime Formula is the actual real way to get your Digimon, which it isn't. Many things the first Digimon World has done horribly wrong are gone in this new Digimon World. Best example are the stats getting revealed you need to aim for, if you want a specific Digimon. And it really isn't as hard as it seems to get them. Later on it not just gets extremely easy to get those stats, but you also get literal blocks to ONLY get the Digimon you want. Lifespan can be extended with items and even through just talking to NPC's. In other words you can keep your Digimon forever if you know what to do. (Chain Melon extends Lifetime by 24 hours, same as talking to two Digimon do later on.)Give the game a fair chance. Past older looking graphics, it really is mostly your time you need to be ready to invest. The time you can play this game not just is pretty much limitless, but even if you just want to get through the story you have TONS of playtime ahead.There is no "blazing" through the game unless you cheat.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a unique blend of virtual pet simulation and RPG-style exploration and battles, and it's an absolute must-play for fans of the franchise.Let's start with the gameplay. As a tamer, your job is to take care of your Digimon companions by feeding them, training them, and helping them evolve. This adds a whole new layer of depth to the game that sets it apart from other RPGs. The mechanics are easy to understand, and the controls are responsive and intuitive. But what really sets this game apart is the bond you'll form with your Digimon partners. They're not just characters in a game; they're your companions on your journey, and you'll get attached to them just like you would a real pet.Moving on to the story and characters, I have to say I was hooked from the very beginning. The narrative is engaging, and the characters are all unique and well-developed. The game strikes a perfect balance between your responsibilities as a tamer and the need to explore the world and uncover its secrets. Every character you meet has their own personality and backstory, making it easy to become invested in them.Let's not forget about the graphics and sound. The visuals are stunning, and the sound design is top-notch. The music is catchy and fits the game's vibe perfectly, adding to the immersive experience of being in the world of Digimon.But what about performance? Well, I'm happy to say that Digimon World: Next Order runs flawlessly. The frame rate is smooth, the loading times are lightning-fast, and I didn't encounter any game-breaking bugs or glitches.This is an excellent game that truly delivers on all fronts. Whether you're a fan of RPGs, virtual pet games, or the Digimon franchise itself, this game is a must-play. The mechanics are easy to pick up, but offer enough challenge to keep both new and seasoned players engaged. So give it a try, and get ready to be hooked!

_childDocuments_.review: A virtual pet RPG where look after and train your Digimon to go out on an adventure in an open world. Originally a PS Vita game, but has a unique style of gameplay no other series tries to replicate. As you raise your Digimon like a vpet, they eventually die and pass on a fraction of their stats to the next generation. The way the gameplay loop works, you're always gaining power, you'll never start with less stats than you had the previous generation, even if it isn't immediately apparently, progress is always being made.The game has some problems, the gym becomes very pointless after your second or third generation, where battles become more effective, instead of being able to train your Digimon up in an irl hour, it takes multiple, which can feel like a grind. Also, as you raise two Digimon, eventually their lifespans desync, which makes training them together much harder and requires micromanaging to fix.This game is Digimon in it's own element, doing what it does best instead of trying to replicate other series. It won't be for everyone, but there's a reason it has a dedicated fan base and I highly recommend trying it out.

_childDocuments_.review: Digimon World: Next Order was originally released on the Vita and PS4 as the second act in Bandai Namco's attempt at revitalizing the formula of the original Digimon World, an ambitious semi-non-linear animal raising sim that were released way back on the PS1 back before the anime even existed. As a result, Next Order is something entire different in comparison to the Cyber Sleuth duology that originated alongside it on the Vita. With that in mind, is this unique title the kind of game for you?The basic concept is the same as the original Digimon World: your main goal is to raise your pet monsters so you can traverse the Digital World in a semi-non-linear fashion in search of more monsters that can aid in improving your town so you can raise the next generation more efficiently once your current companions inevitably reach the end of their lifespan. Unfortunately, Next Order also inherits some of the original Digimon World's problems, especially on Normal mode (which significantly lowers training benefits and your companions' lifespan in comparison to the Vita version) and above, namely that you basically start off with virtually nothing to your name, making progression quite difficult as you've got little leeway and don't get much direction on which skills benefit your survival the most in the long run. That being said, Next Order, much like its PS1 predecessor, is also a game about momentum. Stick with the game when the going gets rough, and you'll soon start building up your resources and get the hang of what you need to focus on to make efficient progress. Still, the early game on normal mode and beyond is going to be a slow burn, and even when you get a reliable set of partners, they'll usually pass away soon after, making it feel as if you're right back at square one yet again, even with the slight stat boosts that the next generation receives. Nonetheless, the feeling you get when you finally get to the point where you pass the threshold to where everything clicks and moves along smoothly is extremely cathartic and rewarding. That said, the game does have an issue with relying guidance. Many players will usually get to the point where they can finally evolve their crew to Mega level and then hit a wall that they can't pass through since they can't get much stronger. Players who stick with it will eventually realize that ExE Evolution isn't just a neat comeback mechanic that can give you a little push towards victory, but is actually going to become the cornerstone of your gameplan once you meet the requirements to manually trigger it on command. While the game does teach you about the ins and outs of the mechanic early on, this explanation is tucked away in a densely packed dialogue tree that does a poor job of emphasizing its long-term importance, especially since you won't be able to make proper use of the mechanic until much later on (in my case, I eventually decided to attempt to utilize it for lack of a better option back on the PS4, since I had already tried everything else that the game recommended). The information is there, but it's far too understated and easy to forget about for such an integral mechanic, which can make the game seem far harder than it really is until the player decides to experiment with their approach.In short, Digimon World: Next Order is, much like its inspiration, an exceedingly unique animal-raising sim/pseudo-open world hybrid that's all about perseverance. You start off with little more than your wits and guile, and there's little guiding you on what you need to focus on to proceed. Nonetheless, players who stick with it will eventually realize that this is also a game about momentum that gets easier the farther you get and the more you experiment with your approach. If you're the kind of person who can enjoy the process of sticking with games through adversity in order to feel the satisfaction that comes with figuring things out and reaping the rewards that comes with it, this might be the game for you. If nothing else, there's still nothing out there that's quite like the original Digimon World, Re:Digitize and Next Order, so you might as well give it a try and see if this is something that you'd enjoy, though, waiting for a price-drop might be prudent if you're unsure.

_childDocuments_.review: These are my problems with the game:1. Post-battle Stat Gains is not Communicated InstinctivelyThe game should communicate the stats gained through battle better. For example, at the end of each battle when you get stats, highlights the stats number blue or red like in Etemon stock market so that players instinctively know when they get good stats or bad. The truth is, most players ignore the numbers and just generally don't read when they don't think it's important.2. Effectiveness of Gym Training Fell Off in the Late and Post GameGyms are only useful to get your digimon to rookie/child and passing in-game time, otherwise battling is the best way to gain stats. Here's a suggestion to fix this: raise the level of training gear provided by Kabuterimon from 3 to 5, and the building upgrade as well. This way you can still provide a challenge for the early game while having better stat gains in the late and post game. Having better training gear to improve stat gains in the late game will help a lot.3. Bad Interface for Certain Specific Menus.I’m tired of spamming X in front of Antylamon to unlock the digivolution info. Same goes for crafting with Guardromon and exchanging materials with Tyrannomon and Gotsumon. Let the player craft multiple items at once, or submit multiple evolution stones at once, or exchange multiple materials at one. This is a major quality of life oversight in my opinion.4. Lack of Control of Camera Angle During BattleThis is a simple fix that was not implemented only because the game was originally designed for PSVita: the ability to control the camera position during battle. L2 and R2 to zoom in and out, R stick to move. Especially since R2 and L2 has no binding in the game. 5. Certain Caviat When Sleeping in the TentWhen you sleep in your tent, you'll wake up outside and have to use it again if you want to cook breakfast for your Digimons. So being able to wake up in the tent and cook all in one is a really neat quality of life improvement. Deduct 2 usage from the tent if the problem is balancing issue, the point is: just provide the convenience of finishing what you have to do in one swoop.6. New Game PlusWhy not exist?

name: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle
detailed_description: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is a third-person story-driven survival horror game Prequel to the critically acclaimedDaymare: 1998 . Step into the shoes of special agent Dalila Reyes , a former government spy now in the service of a unit called H.A.D.E.S. (Hexacore Advanced Division for Extraction and Search), and get ready to enter the most advanced experimental research center in the United States of America. Be careful, though, because in the darkness of the desolate, labyrinthine depths of the military research center there is something creepy and lethal awaiting you! Grab one of the most innovative and technologically advanced weapons of all time and prepare to face never-before-seen creatures while you make your way through a series of frightfully evocative settings all ready to be discovered. A perfect mix of fierce and deadly enemies, hardcore action game mechanics, environmental puzzles, a chilling soundtrack, plenty of exploration and massive doses of concentrated horror wait for you in Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle. No place is safe, especially when you’re being hunted by your nightmares. New characters and big comebacks – take part in the top secret 'Sandcastle' mission as the game's main protagonist, Special Agent H.A.D.E.S. Dalila Reyes, and reconstruct the past of some of Daymare: 1998's most beloved characters. Lethal and terrifying enemies – fight, kill and dismember the new enemies that stand between you and the resolution of your mission, so frighteningly intelligent, aggressive and realistic in every detail. Revamped interface – the D.I.D. is back, though in a completely redesigned way. Manage your inventory, ammo and health items directly from the new game interface, which has never been so simple and intuitive. Eye to the Scanner – thanks to the innovative device installed on Reyes’s arm, you can analyze portions of the environment and reveal new puzzles to solve, pick up secret documents and detect hidden items! Environmental puzzles – the solution is often right in front of your eyes! Search for all the clues and overcome the environmental obstacles to obtain resources and collectibles. Are you sure it’s dead? – in Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle, prepare to confront the toughest and most aggressive enemies you have ever seen. Moreover, even if you’re sure you’ve killed one, you’ll find out it can come back in a completely new form and even deadlier than before! Breathtaking and immersive graphics, sound effects and soundtrack – thanks to the power of Unreal Engine 4, you will live the most terrifying of experiences! Back to the 90s… again! – if you loved the nostalgia of Daymare: 1998, in Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle will feel like you’re living and playing a typical action horror/film of the 90s. Expect to be transported back in time to many familiar references and a frightfully authentic atmosphere with a retro flavor. Freeze! – there will certainly be no shortage of guns, but prepare to equip one of the most innovative and powerful weapons ever created: the Frost Grip! WARNING: it may contain liquid nitrogen. Veteran or rookie – choose the most appropriate game difficulty based on your ability in combat and your experience with survival horror. Either way, it will be a serious challenge for the faint-hearted!

_childDocuments_.review: This prequel to Daymare 1998 puts you in the shoes of special agent Dalila Reyes, a HADES military combat engineer sent to the iconic Area 51 in order to secure vital intelligence, after an unexplained loss of communication with the facility. Of course, some secret experiment violating most ethics and treaties went terribly wrong, so the President called the cream of the crop to clean up that mess, and cover it up in the process. The story is narrated well-enough despite its unoriginality, with decent VA and cutscenes; however, the character animations are definitely stiff in many cases.It’s a clichè, overused premise, that doesn’t introduce anything new in its sci-fi horror plot; it inspires mainly to the Philadelphia Experiment and the innumerable Area 51 tales to build up its lore - if you’re a sci-fi enthusiast, it will certainly feel already-seen. Nevertheless, the atmosphere and visuals are top-notch, much better than you’d expect from a small Italian Indie studio - combined with the exceptional sound design, they can really deliver an atmosphere I’d put on-par with AAA titles, without doubt.Each level takes place in a different section of the gigantic Groom Lake facility, and plays out in a linear fashion, meaning that there will be one-way points you won’t be able to backtrack from once crossed. The notable absence of a map, usually customary in the genre, isn’t a big problem given the modest scope and size of each stage; you’ll unlikely lose your bearings, as there aren’t many side-areas to get lost into, enemies don’t respawn, and the way ahead is rather clear most of the time.Exploring every nook and cranny won’t be as satisfactory as in other titles of this type, as the interactivity with the environment is down to a minimum: there won’t be opening closets, chests or rummaging through debris to scavenge ammo or consumables: everything will be conveniently-placed on shelves, crates or inside bodies, and highlighted with a marker when close enough. Still, it’s definitely worth it to spend extra time scavenging, as you’ll need all the ammo you can get, especially on higher difficulties. That being said, there won’t be “secret” areas or entirely optional chunks of levels, or any meaningful backtracking; at best, you’ll have a few side-rooms with an extra minigame to get some extra resources, or an upgrade if you’re lucky, and that will be it.Your foes will be lethal, and fast even more so. DSC detaches completely from the relatively slow-paced enemies found in most survival horrors, instead opting for blazing-fast, teleporting, grab-heavy foes that will hit like trucks, and may still be dangerous even after death thanks to the corpse-reanimating mechanic that migrates one enemy’s “soul” to another to either create a new foe or upgrade an existing one to a fearsome Red variant. Luckily, the Frost Glove, acquired early–on, is there to help you in slowing and freezing these monsters - the only way to kill their red “upgraded” variants, and generally a good way to deal with the rest. Combat is based upon managing the limited gas reserves for the glove, usable to fuel various active skills, and of course being accurate with your shots, while kiting enemies around to not get grabbed or hit by ranged attacks. Ultimately, it’s a challenging combat system, that however feels more like an action third-person shooter than a survival horror at any point; it doesn’t have the methodicalness, deliberateness and pacing expected from the genre – a pacing instead found in the first Daymare. The constant QTEs to get free of grabs and the teleporting instant-kill enemies are unnecessary, frustrating additions that make many encounters more annoying than they need to be. In case of death you’ll be respawned at the nearest checkpoint or save-station, whatever is closest.There’s only one real boss fight, and it’s not even a “true” one at that. The final boss is a complete disappointment, an escape section with infinitely-respawning enemies and an immortal boss you need to slow and avoid until you reach a certain location. It seems like the developers wanted to make this a “real” fight, given the massive amounts of ammo and resources given before it, but then ran out of time / willpower, instead making it into an anticlimactic “freeze the boss and keep running” meme that feels like a boring chore. You won’t even need ammo for it, trust me.The limited weapon and tool selection, having only a shotgun, a SMG and the glove as implements, doesn’t really evolve at any point. Despite the presence of various upgrades to all of the above-mentioned tools, they never really feel any different in functioning, despite improved capacity, rates of fire, efficiency and so forth. Sure, they’re fine and do the job, but they don’t feel like improving at any point. This lack of variety, united with the lackluster enemy roster, makes combat encounters repetitive not after long. Upgrades can be useful and by all means, you should seek them by opening all side-rooms and solving all puzzles, but don’t expect the gameplay to be more deep or revolutionized by them at any point.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to mark this as "not recommended", but honestly I can't see any other way.  This prequel to Daymare 1998 is losely tied to the main game, and when I say loosely it has almost nothing to do with said game besides a throwaway line in the after credits scene.So was gameplay improved?  It's more a one step forward, two steps back.  You're more well armed this time, however the enemies are so frustrating to fight it borderlines insanity.  One of your main mechanics is a frost weapon to slow and freeze enemies.  You're going to need this because they're fast.  They're so fast it's insane.  If any enemies are close to you, get ready to be chain grabbed continuously while you mash A to escape. There's new enemies that can teleport behind you and instant kill you, which in my mind is absolute bullcrap when any game does it.  Every time this game catches you trying to have fun it just repeatedly beats your ass with frustration until you hate it.  This game LOVES hiding enemies behind corners that sprint full speed at you and grab you just to get a cheap hit in.  They did this in the first game but it's turned up to 11 in this one.  The sad part is I want to like this game, I really do.  The first game wasn't perfect, but the interesting reload mechanic plus the cool puzzles were a good throwback to old resident evil games.  The reload mechanic is gone in this one (To be honest it's gone because with it and how fast enemies are the game would basically be impossible to beat).  Puzzles are severely dumbed down in this one.  None of them feel cool or rewarding to complete.  Without the things that set the first game apart, this one really doesn't feel unique at all.  As far as the enemies and mechanics go, I can't imagine the dev didn't look at how frustrating the encounters were, ignore player feedback and decide to implement them anyway.  Play at your own risk, but I legitimately don't know how much fun you're going to have.[Edit 12-19-23]  After taking the time to replay this game, the aspects of the gaming making it very frustrating to play have been tweaked and it is much more enjoyable of an experience now.  Devs did a great job at listening to player feedback.  Will change to a "recommend" now.
_childDocuments_.name: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle

_childDocuments_.review: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is a good example of an iterative sequel (or a prequel in this case) that takes one step forward and two steps back while delivering a mediocre experience that in some ways improves on its predecessor but also introduces a host of new problems.I finished the game in roughly 7 to 7.5 hours on hardcore difficulty while getting all of the collectibles and had a fairly decent time with it but there is no denying that it was an experience with hefty amount of jank, incredibly dull and repetitive combat and there were more than a few moments where it just sort of dragged on.This time around combat is a much bigger focus, so much so that I would call this an action horror title rather than a survival horror one - however combat also proves to be its biggest weakness due to a myriad issues such as:- Combat does not feel very satisfying as it lacks impact, has rather poor hit reactions and in overall it simply lacks polish.- Encounter design is very formulaic and if you'd take a shot every time there is a single enemy hiding at a dead angle in a corridor you would probably die from alcohol poisoning over the course of your playthrough.- Poor weapon variety (only two weapons in addition to the freeze abilities)- Incredibly poor enemy varietyThat being said it wasn't all bad as the game did manage to nail some aspects such as sound design, visual design of environments and even the overall story was surprisingly entertaining, although I won't lie that one of the things I was sort of looking forward to was seeing if we'd reach the same level of hamfisted cheese or the hilariously bad voice lines like "he's going there... and then he'll be there" from the first game - didn't quite reach that tier but there were certainly a lot of moments that made me laugh for all the wrong reasons.If steam reviews could have a neutral rating this would be a perfect game for it as it can be recommended to genre enthusiasts who will likely find their fun with it perhaps for the wrong reasons similar to myself while those new to the genre will likely find the game to be a frustrating or lackluster experience and there certainly are much better titles to consider for those new to action or survival horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of players will probably compare this game to RE2 and RE3 Remakes. And it's kinda right. From the moment when you start the game you can see how heavily it was inspired by those. However to compare these games won't be fair, because Daymare 1994 isn't an AAA game. Hell, it's not even AA game! This is literally an indie title! And honestly it's pretty darn good for the price devs' are asking.Personally, I'd give it a solid 7/10. Some things the game does better than Daymare 1998 and some things actually worse...Alright, let's start with some positives:1) Gameplay and combat feels much better. It is sighnificantly less "clunky" compared to Daymare 1994.2) The story is also more simple and easier to understand (as long as you read the files and watch cutscenes). D1994 is a prequel and there are numerous throwbacks to D1998 along with some characters from the first game. Overall the "Daymare" universe has been expanded, which is great!3) Many cool pop culture references as in the previous game;4) The price is more than adequate even without a discount.5) Finally some bonus content similar to RE games (weapon skins, unlockable artworks, infinite ammo, "extreme" difficulty mode);6) The game has way more manual save points compared to previous game and it doesn't require "ink ribbon" or anything else, save as many times as you want. Very convinient!7) Easier and totally not clunky inventory system and good controls in general.8) Another story point. I'd say that the lore is where this game beats RE games. It is definitely written in a much more believable way compared to RE2 and RE3 remakes. Especially RE3R with all of the BS feats that the "Cringe Jill" has performed there.9) New cool ice weapon mechanics that makes the game different from D1998 and RE games.10) You can get all of the game's achievements in one go. Though I need to WARN you! There's one particular achievement where you have to finish the game without dying. Sounds easy, BUT there's one particular enemy with a frustrating one-hit-kill attack (can be a problem if the area is infested with other enemies as well) and if you die it's not enough to just go the menu and and hit "continue". If you do that your death will be added to the count! The game corrupts your last save file. So you should use 2 save slots instead. Meaning if you die and your latest save file becomes corrupted you can still use the first one.Neutral points:1) Reworked hacking mechanic. Not gonna elaborate, but it's probably gonna frustrate some players A LOT. Others however may even enjoy it. Personally I think it's cool.2) VERY fast paced combat. Prepare yourselves, because enemies are very fast! Don't even bother trying to outrun them. There's no stealth in the game. If the combat has started you gotta fight your enemies, there's no way to somehow speedrun past them.3) The puzzles were simplified and their number has been decreased.4) Playing the original Daymare 1998 is very recommended for the better understanding of the story.5) Unique reload mechanic from the first game is gone. Which actually might be a good thing, considering how fast paced the combat is.6) The game is set in 1994, and well, I don't think that the game has captured atmosphere of that time really well. I mean, it kind of feels like 90s, there are some very cool references. Maybe it's just the fact that the game's taking place in the Area 51 I dunno. Well, I think there should've been more references then. I mean, it's all advanced military laboratories stuff and such, sometimes it's hard to say that it's 90s... You're probably thinking that I am making a huge deal out of it, lol. But I am big 90s sucka. 90s were THE BEST! But hey, the references which they made are really cool! Devs also tried really hard to make tech stuff look apropriate for that era. At least I didn't see any inconsistencies (like CD-RW disk in Robocop: Rogue city, which was not possible at that time).Negatives:1) No mini map! I kinda get it that the game is somewhat linear and there's not a lot of backtracking. But honestly the game is so dark and the flashlight works like an ass that a couple of times I even got lost, lmao. 2) I think the bonus content for the game could've been better, honestly. I mean if the main character received at least 2 bonus costumes that would increase the replayability of the game. The reward for shooting all of the alien figures is underwhelming to say the least.3) Only 2 weapons, though it's good that now they at least have a couple of upgrades.3) The weapons don't feel impactful when hitting the enemies.4) Very few types of enemies. There's one particular artwork in the game of a certain enemy that was scrapped which is a total bummer because of how cool it looked!5) Somehow the world feels less alive compared to previous game. There's less interaction with it along with many areas full of nothing. Not many locations where you want to stop and look around (Though some are very beautiful and breathtaking).6) Cheap enemy encounters strike again! Remember how in the first game during the exploration sequences there were single enemies hiding behind the corner of some corridors? Yup, they are back in this game as well. Good grief. I hope those aren't gonna become one of the "main features" of the Daymare games. 7) I wish there was a way to read all of the collected files in the game menu.Conclusion:For what it's worth I really enjoyed Daymare 1994. Gonna replay the game on the new diffuculty that was added after the release and get the last 2 achievements. Considering the size of the team and budget the developers did put much more effort into the game than Capcom did with the Resident Evil 3 "Demake". Not to mention that I find lore of the Daymare games to be superior to Resident Evil franchise. It honestly is ming boggling when some people say that the story in Daymare is bad. You know, I also happen to be a dedicated Resident Evil series fan. And let me tell this when it comes to "realism" and immersion RE has nothing on Daymare. If you wanna I can give a 36+ hours long lecture on what's wrong with every RE game. While Daymare isn't perfect either, it features a very realistic story with ZERO BS, Mary Sues, or total nonsence. I am gonna die on the hill that Daymare series has better lore and characters compared to Resident Evil. Even though the game was greatly inspired by Resident Evil, Daymare 1994 has its' own atmosphere, even different compared to D1998. I would say that the game feels more like "Call of Cthulhu" type of game atmosphere wise rather than Resident Evil. But I do understand that not everyone will be touched by the story. To me though it felt very personal, like a letter from the beyond the grave. Like a main character I also happen to have a very complicated relationship with one of my relatives who has "jumped into the abyss". Yeah... The story has resonated with me very much and moved my heart in ways unimaginable... Anyway, as I said, I recommend to buy it even without a discount, it is really worth it, when you put all of the things into consideration.

_childDocuments_.review: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle was very disappointing, specially compared to the first game. (SPOILERS AHEAD)I won't talk about the plot which is, to say the least, really dumb and riddled with clichés, you can read the Daymare wiki if you want to learn more about the story, here's the problems I have with this game from a gameplay perspective:WEAPONS: In Daymare 1994 you get only 2 guns for a 6 hour long campaign (at least it took me 6 hours on hardcore on my first run, and I walked through almost all of it), you get a sub machine gun and an automatic shotgun, RIGHT FROM THE START, the former has a high rate of fire and initially low recoil but the more you hold down the shoot button the more recoil you get, to the point where the screen shakes uncontrollably, and the latter shoots really slow and has massive recoil per shot, they both can be upgraded with parts you find to shoot more accurately (smg only), hold more rounds (shotgun & smg) and to up the rate of fire (shotgun only).You also get the Frost Grip, which is a device mounted on your wrist that sprays liquid nitrogen which you can use to freeze enemies in place and then punch them to death or shoot them to kill them immediately with only a few shots of your smg or a single shotgun blast, it can be upgraded all throughout the game using these sparsely scattered upgrade stations and right at the end you get THE single upgrade to it that turns the "spray" attack into a laser that both freezes enemies and kills them with sustained fire.The problem with these guns, isn't the fact that they're really basic and feel bad to shoot, it's the fact that you don't really get any other weapons besides these two and the frost grip, basically making the gameplay loop very repetitive and shallow with heavy reliance on the frost grip and with no depth whatsoever. Since the frost grip recharges overtime, there's entire sections you can beat only using that and maybe your smg once or twice, none of these weapons take up inventory slots either, so the layer of inventory management difficulty they could have added to the game with these doesn't exist. ENEMIES:  They are janky, like SUPER, you essentially have 3 types of enemies, you have the Decoys which are your average zombie type enemy, they sprint towards you and once they reach you they grapple you and you have to mash the crap out of your spacebar to break free, the problem with these is that their running speed is much faster than yours so they will catch up to you fairly quick and keep trying to grab you, you will struggle to turn around and shoot at them due to how much slower you run in comparison to them, so you'll be forced to keep your camera focused on them while backpedalling through (mostly) dimly lit environments, this can be difficult to do but it's mostly annoying and not fun, since you only get 2 weapon types and the frost grip, every encounter with these guys ends up playing the exact same way, the devs also put a lot of these enemies to the right or the left of doorways, to "surprise" you, but they overuse this so much that it just seems like a cheap way to take health away from the player, it gets old fairly quick.Then there's the Mutated Decoys which are normal decoys that can teleport and attack from afar shooting rays of electricity at you after a short animation which can shock you and keep you in place to leave you defenseless against other enemies, they're alright.And finally the Sparkers which are gigantic bug-like beasts that float around and teleport, chase you down and insta-kill you if you get too close, I won't even try and explain why insta-kills are dumb and obtuse specially with a pool of enemies like the ones I've described before and with no mechanic to escape from them, like you could escape the Ivys in REmake 2 with grenades or knives (you know, the game OR games that they are trying so desperately hard to copy), there's one instance in the game where you get to a nest of these (which is laggy as ♥♥♥♥) and there's a special one that takes more bullets to kill than normal despite it looking exactly the same as all the other ones you encounter up to that point.The end boss is basically a sparker that instead of grappling you and insta-killing you, teleports you back to the beginning of the map making you have to run and fight through decoys until you finally get to the end trigger, lol.In conclusion, the tools you are given aren't fun nor all that useful or satisfying to use, the gameplay is reduced to "running backwards focusing the camera on your enemies while trying to not get hit by ranged attacks or get insta killed, wait for the decoys to all play the grappling animation at the same time, aim and freeze them in place, kill them, and then dispatch the other enemies" you can't even run away from them and outsmart them that way because they follow you around indefinitely or the "arena" gets conveniently closed off by fleshy barriers so you are forced into fights EVERY single time.Another aspect of them that I did not like, but is more of a personal thing, is their design and the logic behind them, "fast zombies that can teleport and get revived by spooky electricity from a rare metal" doesn't seem all that interesting or scary like the concept of a normal zombie is.Misc gameplay aspects I find annoying and nitpicky bullsh1t: - Reyes takes a long time to go up and down ladders, you can't control her while she does this, you don't even get control over the camera.- Items like medkits and recharge capsules for the frost grip don't stack, the only instance in which inventory management is a problem, despite the game being survival horror, no item boxes to save your items in.- The scanner is an useless mechanic that serves no purpose.- Shoddy animations and uncanny facial expressions.- Saving stations are placed in weird, non-intuitive places, no save rooms.- Forgettable soundtrack.- Subpar voice acting.- Some environments are way too big for no reason, making exploration take more time than it should due to Reyes jogging slowly, a crazy amount of HALLWAYS, blocked off paths.- Invader borrowing heavily from Resident Evil, there's a few props in the game that literally look identical to those in the recent remakes (for example the platform that takes you to the OGRE, the lab locations looking like NEST), not only props or maps but things like for example the results screen (identical to REmake 4's), this isn't annoying per say but I just wish they would do their own thing instead of trying to emulate the remakes, if I wanted to play resident evil, I would just go and play resident evil, I want to like these games because of their own merits.- Commander Foster LITERALLY being in the family guy death pose upon finding his body.- Easter eggs not being subtle like the REDRUM door in the hotel with the hatchet stuck in it, the hotel that's also called "Neville Residential Arts" but only the letters that spell out EVIL RESIDENT are lit up.- Little to no bonus or unlockable content, I shot all 20 aliens in the main campaign only to get a concept art piece, which don't get me wrong, I love and think is great, I just don't think the reward for shooting all bobbleheads should be something so trivial and unfulfilling like that, no bonus or unlockable outfits for any character.- Almost no replayability.- Ending is left on a cliffhanger, AGAIN, mega unrewarding.- Misc performance issues.Final thoughts:I really want to love this game, these series, I really do, I think people at Invader Studios have the means and the talent to make a great survival horror happen, however, if the next one in the trilogy is gonna get even more streamlined than this one and keeps borrowing from other survival horrors then It'll sadly not to be a very good game, I genuinely hope that they are able to adress some of these things for a future release.GET ONLY IF ON SALE, thank you Neko for the game <3.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of mixed rating than a negative.To Invader Studios: I respect your ambition to go above and beyond Daymare 1998 but this ain't it. visually the game is several steps above the previous game but at the cost of almost everything else. You need to go back to the drawing board, do not aim for visual fidelity, but for game design, because Daymare 1994 is essentially a corridor with frustrating combat. The story is there but the presentation is lacking, I'm not talking about facial animations, but the line delivery (and the writing feels unnatural). VA sound competent but lacks direction, they switch from mellow to intense too often (and the sound mixing is a bit off, some lines start when the previous isn't done yet). I'd like to see you work on a smaller project, lower your visuals to the level of other indie survival horrors and prioritize what made classic survival games work: puzzles, backtracking, combat loop, resource management, replayability. I hope you can break even with this project and learn valuable lessons. I'm going to sound harsh in the actual review, Please don't take it as mean spirited.to the players:pros:-improves a lot visually from Daymare 1998-good ambient soundscape-a main character that isn't a wet noodle-many logs to find, giving insight to what is going on behind the scenes-surprisingly large variety of environments-the character controls smoothly (I advise to sprint on push and not toggle though), aiming is snappy and responsive.-The weapons feel good to shoot, the smg is a bit weak but will do adequate damage when aimed at weak spots, the shotgun just blast enemies away.-good checkpoints, whenever I died I didn't feel like I lost significant progress.-this is highly subjective but the arrival at the base sequence is very Dino Crisis.cons:-puzzles are very simplistic-combat loop doesn't work, the enemies are too fast and surround you, there's a delay between pushing the button and actually spraying nitrogen, and they take a couple seconds to freeze over. Like in Daymare 1998, they rush to grab you, no real attack to speak of. There are ranged enemies that will almost never kill you, but rather annoy you and prevent you from dealing with the basic rushers. There's also an insta kill grab enemy.-enemies teleport in. While it makes complete sense within the story, it's really cheap-when they are actually placed in the environment, it's always behind a corner, and they also rush at you. If you have the shotgun equipped, you might stop them before they grab you.-Damage doesn't matter however, because the game showers you with medkits, to the point that half my inventory was medkits (and frost grip cartridges, which refill your frost gauge which recharges over time slowly)-no inventory management, no storing items, no combining. At most you'll inspect an object to make it usable.-Only two weapons, a shotgun and an smg. Yes, the frost grip has several attacks that you unlock as you progress (spray, mines, bomb, bullet), but they don't damage the enemy. Only the frost finisher does that and it's not a guarantee that the enemy will not release an energy sphere to reanimate another body.-The writing isn't good, it feels unnatural and falsely deep (the music will even swell to tell you the feelings you should be having in that moment).-to add to that, there's a million easter eggs to pop culture, which break the immersion. One character death is portrayed as tragic but when you find the body it's layed out like the Family Guy Death Pose. Really?-Almost completely linear design, everywhere you'll see easy to pass obstructions that block off sections. No real backtracking: whenever you come across a locked door, the key/passcode is either in the same room or the level will loop back around. It's convenient, but not interesting.-forced walking sections-Supposedly the enemies can drop ammunition if you're low, but if you're like me, you play just well enough that you'll never see one.-a final boss that will troll you into quitting the game. Seriously, it's not difficult, it's just designed to be tedious. You won't die, you will beat it first try, but you will hate it.-Practically no relation to Daymare 1998, aside from the DiD, the D-Toxin references and the most stitched together contrived plot devices.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game as I enjoyed the first one a fair bit despite its shortcomings, but for every shortcoming this game "fixes", it adds new ones in their place. most of all, the combat is just frustrating more than it is challenging. the base enemy being one that both sprints at you and teleports seems a bit much for a survival horror game, and thats definitely amplified when you have to fight off 2 or 3 plus other enemy types. the freeze mechanic is just so slow in these situations, even tapping LB to shoot a freeze "projectile" which should be the quicker option, I do that to freeze one enemy and before the animation is even finished, another guy has sprinted up behind me to instantly throw me into the QTE attack animation. not only do I feel it's too slow, but the camera pulls in too close to the player, leaving virtually no room to see oncoming enemies coming at you from the sides - which again is not a good combo with sprinting + teleporting enemies. it also feels like there's very little i-frame cooldown after you've been grabbed, as sometimes as soon as I've broken free from one enemies grab, another one grabs me almost immediately after, leading to situations where I get stunlocked quite easily.it might have just been me, but i found placement of some items - mostly aid kits, to be a bit unbalanced. they were showering me with an unnecessary amount in the early portions of the game when I didn't really need them, but i wanna say around the part where you reach the outside area with the gas station, from then on i feel i've barely been able to find any. Another issue is readability of the environment. as others have said, the flashlight in this game is pathetic. there was a decent 2-3 minute stretch there where this is with the flashlight ON, by the way.combine this with the game having no map, and i've more than a couple times found myself not exactly sure about where I'm going. the above link was after turning on all the fans to get rid of the gas and had to return to the doctor, and backtracking through a now pitch black hallway instilled very little confidence that i was actually going the right way. i don't feel this game is any more linear than Daymare 1998 was, so i'm not sure why that game had a map and this one does not.also, personally i just don't find never-ending facilities and labs very captivating as environments, with a lot of areas kind of just blending together imo. '98's city environments may not have been all that unique but there were distinct locales that stood out from each other (lab - city - backwoods - hospital, etc), whereas this game is more like (facility - other facility - another facility, and so on). though again, this would have been less bothersome if there was an in-game map.last couple things are purely nitpicks. there is a rather annoying amount of forced walking sections in-game where your character is talking to someone over the radio, or even just talking to herself. i'm not sure why she needs to slow down to do that. and lastly, is just those facial animations. i can tell they're using that Epic store facial animation software whatever it is. I've seen other games like Stray Souls use it and i just think it does not look very good.overall though, this is still an otherwise pretty competently put together and decent looking survival horror game that should appeal to you if you like Resident Evil or Dead Space and REALLY want something else to scratch that itch.but the above issues bothered me to a point where i wound up dropping the difficulty, something i don't think i've done with any other survival horror games since i was a kid. and even then, i had enough after a while and gave up playing it, and i'm not sure i'll be coming back to finish it which is a shame. most reviews are still positive so you might still enjoy it anyways if you're a big survival horror head. the €27~ price is also pretty reasonable i suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: Every single thing that the first game did well was fundamentally altered or completely removed in this one. As a fan of both classic AND modern survival horror, I find this game tedious, frustrating, and overall excruciating. Sandcastle suffers from what I call Callisto Syndrome, where every major issue is to due to fundamental design choices and not just bugs or technical issues. The first game was slower and more methodical in its overall pacing and gameplay loop, but it still had a sprint button. This game has more artificially frenetic combat, larger more sprawling level design, and painfully pointless exploration and backtracking yet there is no sprint button and the base run speed is agonizingly slow. This game has just as much if not more open ended level design with fast paced combat that can very easily turn you around, say nothing of the ridiculous amount of times you will get stunlocked by command grabs and lose control of your camera and very easily become disoriented, yet there is no map. Exacerbating this further is the lighting. Quite possibly the worst lighting I've seen in a 3rd person horror game in general. At every possible setting even on subsequent playthroughs I was having an awful time trying to see where I was going at times and if you turn the brightness up too high, the lighting elements on the Frost Grip corsage makes it even more difficult to see what's going on around the character. There is also a poor sense of power progression. The only useful tool provided by the Frost Grip would be the mines, and even they become cumbersome to use during the points of the game where your actual recharge is cut in half arbitrarily. Imagine rolling up to Radagon and then From Soft is like, "oh yeah, by the way, we're turning the dodge roll off for this one. Have fun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" There are only two weapons and you start with them both, so there is no real sense of power progression. There are attachments for each of the guns, but there is no meaningful difference made in either case. My first playthrough of 1998 was on Classic Mode + Daymare and I had no issues whatsoever outside of the chase near the end, if you know, you know. But for Sandcastle I opted for Normal since I was told by the game itself that enemies did not drop resources on Hardcore. I wanted to have the intended first experience and even on Standard I found this game to be excruciating. Also, only 3 times total did I see enemies drop any items so it's not an RE4 situation, it clearly only seems to happen if you're low on, or completely out of ammo. The game is technically higher fidelity than 1998, but due to the lighting issues alone, I prefer the look of the first game. The cutscenes are obviously more impressive this time around and there are way more of them, but I can't appreciate them as much as I would like to because they obviously came at the expense of gameplay. Style will ALWAYS trump graphical fidelity. Signalis and My Friendly Neighborhood both released in the last year and proved that. Even the original song in the credits was less enjoyable for me. This one is more subjective of course, but overall I found "In My Name" a more intriguing composition with a more interesting and emotional vocal performance. Although I do love Lacuna Coil and Cristina Scabbia, it is clear she was singing someone else's lyrics on this one. It just sounded like artist-for-hire and lacked the emotional impact of the original song from the first game, however, overall the OST was stronger in Sandcastle. Alessandro Galdieri is a phenomenal composer. I want Invader Studios to be successful. We need more developers like them. Even though I consider this game to be a failure in a lot of ways, I would still take something like this over another remake of a game from 20 years ago. These developers clearly have a vision, but why they abandoned everything from the first game genuinely baffles me. However, I do believe that there is a genuinely great game somewhere between the two.
