_childDocuments_.review: I love this genre. I’ve played my first run in Hardcore, so my opinion will be based on such difficulty settings.The tutorial is smooth, divided into short prompts of low cadence that allow you to be absorbed in the game’s introduction sequence without breaking immersion. You can also re-read the completed tutorials in the pause menu.Simple and minimalistic, the UI works well and doesn’t distract the player from in-game events. Similarly to the first game, the pause menu and inventory are strongly based on Resident Evil 7 and its sequels.The control scheme is your typical WASD with some additions for the frost-grip that feel great and are easy to learn. You can equip and unequip items with the same number (1-4) or d-pad arrow, which means you may accidentally unequip.Graphics are gorgeous; the play with light and shadow is superb, but I got some artifacts every now and then, just enough to notice, caused by Delilah’s hair on my 1070 on ultra.Animations overall are decent, but [n]the bad ones, are CRUCIAL[/n] and in your face.Delilah runs like she has spring-charged boots.When characters use a keyboard, their hands literally go through the device in random, incoherent moves.One specific death animation is straight up stolen from Dead Space (you’ll notice, don't worry).The eyes and eyebrows are dead. They take away all attention during cutscenes. Such dead eyes in a heated exchange between characters completely break the scene's dynamic. It seems to be the work of an amateur animator; such a shame this is the final result.Death animations are violent but not unnecessarily gorey.The music's good, a serious improvement from the last game. The game is mainly silent, making the player listen to the environment for hints of danger, but when the music kicks in, it is gorgeous.Voice acting needs some work. I blame the sound director or whomever was supervising the dialogue. Some characters are flawlessly voiced, while others seem to be on a budget. The lines go from irate to worried to soft-spoken in a single output from the same character. Having good and bad performances together only accentuates the contrast even further.Excellent sound design. Keeps you on high alert and doesn’t let you disconnect from the potential danger you may find behind the corner. Feels like they truly tried to polish and work hard on environmental sound design.The level design is dense, and no room feels empty or maze-like. It is easy to locate yourself and find your way around the place without a map, which is important. This is important because you explore many locations more than once, in different conditions. Finding your way in a place that is no longer lit is easier when it is well designed and coherent. Generally speaking, they are well written and have an elaborate backstory. The interactions between characters need a bit of work; they are mainly comprehensible and get the job done conveying their ideas and feelings, but certain key moments seem to lose coherence and get confusing. I believe this may be caused by the voice acting being badly paired with the situation.For example: During Chapter 1, many interactions occur between Delilah and Ivan. The relationship between them seems quite inconsistent. Are they friends? Just comrades? Ex lovers? Professional beekeper federation associates?They are best friends at times, then they hate each other's guts in the first chapter, or was it badly performed sarcasm?The game’s exposure comes in the form of text walls, recordings, and cutscenes, which are typical for this type of game. Sadly, there is no environmental story telling at all.The story structure itself is decent but a bit cliché by now. You go on a mission, things get messed up, and now you fight for your life, with a bit of a plot twist at the end. The fact that the game uses a tested formula and simply shapes it in a certain direction makes it harder for the studio to mess it up. This results in a simple story that is well executed and adds value to the previous installment. I strongly suggest playing this game after Daymare 1998, since it puts things in a different perspective and greatly shifts how you perceive the characters and story.Either if you are a survival horror veteran or a newcomer, you’ll enjoy the game if you like a challenge, a bit of thinking, and adrenaline. The game rides on the back of giants, taking what worked for most and mixing it all together with its own twist and unique mechanics without resulting in an alienating experience for non-fans of the genre.The game is full, and I mean FULL, of references, tributes, and easter eggs to the Resident Evil saga and other big genre titles, not only games but movies and books too. I ended up hunting for Easter eggs; I've taken about 30 screenshots so far.Other than being a solid action-horror experience with a unique twist, there is not much else to say. The game knows what it is and does it right.Manage your resources and inventory. Solve puzzles and open doors. Fight dangerous creatures.Explore unknown locations (without a map). There is very limited backtracking (no useless gameplay padding here). The game isn’t short of savepoints and has 30 save slots, so it’s easy on mistakes.  The frost-grip (nitro-gun) is what differentiates this game. It is a tool you will have to learn to use for fights, puzzles, and environment unlocks. You can upgrade it and unlock new functions as you go, and the finisher move is quite satisfying and makes the game feel more dynamic.Tragically limited choice in weapons. Machinge gun, Shotgun and Frost-grip. That's it.Weak point of the game.Only 4 enemy types are in the game, but 2 of them have 3 forms that make them change and gradually become stronger.I’d say 8-9 hours if you’re thoroughly observant. It took me 12h in hardcore mode and I searched every nook and cranny. Sadly low replayability: There is a serious jump in difficulty and changes between normal and hardcore, but no extra difficulty is added after completing hardcore. No extra outfits or weapons are unlocked upon completing the game, and no incentive to further runs except for the "challenges" and the missed collectibles. You can unlock concept art and some other tiny extras, but it’s not something that pushes you towards another run, imo. Hardcore difficulty can be absolute 𝐛𝐮𝐥𝐥𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐭 in 2 specific bossfights. "Faster reaction time" for the enemies means that if you mess up (during the boss), you are as good as dead. And if you don’t pick the right upgrades for the nitro-gun, you may soft-lock yourself into an impossible bossfight because of this.Only 2 weapons + Frost-grip are available to the player. No knife either.Low replayability incentive.Bad animations and half-baked voice acting.Somewhat confusing dialogues at times.100% recommended. Decent price and worth the experience. I would suggest first playing in normal mode, then in hardcore, unlike what I did. Nice game for achievement hunters and a solid action-horror experience. The studio is improving and learning, and it shows. They got rid of the realistic reloading mechanic of the previous game, which was a big loss, but it would’ve been hard to pair with the new included frost mechanics. Good tutorial, nice UI, fluid and comfy controls, some nice graphics, and level design with a good story. Character interactions need some work, and animations and voice direction need a ton of work.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of  and greatly anticipated the release of this title. It embraced incredibly cheesy dialog and janky mechanics, but was true to form, very entertaining, immersive, and atmospheric. Which is what we are here for right? You really weren't expecting a AAA title experience  improves immensely compared to the quality of the first game. The story is well-written with relatively impressive scientific explanations for what's unfolding. The characters are largely well developed with decent facial animations and the voice acting vastly improves from the first game. The combat underwent a massive overhaul, with a lovely mix of action and resource management. It is difficult, the enemies are extremely fast and demand quick reflexes and spacial awareness. It's disappointing you only have two guns at your disposal, but this is made up for with the awesome Frost Grip mechanic which I find to be fun and original in this context. The sound designer knocked the ball out of the park and the musical score is absolutely phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is not what I expected for the follow up game of Daymare: 1998. I absolutely loved 1998, it was a true old style RE1-3 clone and it really showed. However, 1994 is a little different. I think it's probably easier to jump into the pros and cons list before I get into too much detail. So let's get to it! Pros:* As I stated it's very similar to the first 3 Resident Evils and their counterpart remakes, if you like those games you'll like Daymare.* Controls are better and improved from Daymare 1998, for instance reloading isn't a pain like it was in 1998.* The in game graphics aren't too shabby at all, the environments are creepy and scary. Very low light which will require the use of your flashlight most of the time.* Music and the SFX department did well again, lots of creepy sounds and the music is worth a good listen. * There are jump scares again, but mostly from non enemy surprises, the dark and damp atmosphere drives it to the next level* I'm not finished with the game at the time of this review but there are some puzzles, not nearly what I remember from the Daymare 1998 though* There are collectibles to find, which unlocks infinite ammo on certain weaponsCons* My biggest issue with Daymare 1994 is that it's f**king . I'm sorry but that doesn't interest me at all, especially when your game is basically capitalizing on the RE franchise.* Daymare 1994 also really lost some of my interest when enemies teleport (ALL ENEMIES)... yep they teleport around the map, that's their gimmick and I despise it. * Combat is so-so, I noticed quite a few times specifically with the shotgun where enemies will be too close, lunge and mysteriously you'll completely miss. BUT they'll successfully grapple you. It's frustrating, because it can get you killed!* This is a game made in 2023, there's no F**KING MAP! You don't back track a whole lot, but still WHY NO MAP!?!* Daymare: 1994 added a scanner for you to scan items, well sorta, you can only scan 1 or 2 items per map and they are all story based things to scan. Very under utilized mechanic, it's too bad because a lot more could have done with it. * There are lockers that you'll come across in the game that you'll have to "hack" to unlock. Things like attachments to weapons are in those lockers, BUT each locker after the first one you come across can only be attempted a handful of times. If you fail, it locks you out forever. That would be okay, except eventually the lockers become ridiculous. They have a timer that requires you to hack it within a certain amount of time and they'll throw other mechanics at you as you progress.   They become so stupidly difficult, that I had to quit and start writing this review. It pissed me off and I needed a break. * AGAIN it's bad voice acting with poor dialogue, these voice actors have zero passion. At times, it's just sad how terrible it is. They are suppose to be saying something that is dire and deserves emphasis, but instead is delivered as if they are relaxing on a beach. * Very little in the environment to interact with, this is the exact same situation as 1998. Visually things look great, but very little to explore with dead ends everywhere.* Cutscenes are awful looking, character models are almost laughable for a 2023 release and they look almost the same as they did from years prior with Daymare 1998. I can't believe they didn't improve on this! * Not particularly likable characters, the main protagonist is boring and other npcs are forgettable My overall opinion for Daymare 1994 is that it's not better than 1998, yes they did improve on some things but at the same time there's a lot of changes I didn't like. The enemies being the biggest let down for me. I'm not even for sure if the games are tied in together because they are so radically different story wise. I think I'm more disappointed than anything. I enjoyed 1998 and this was a let down for me. I recommend buying on discount if you do decide to get Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle, otherwise avoid it.

_childDocuments_.review: Daymare: a drawn-out pain.To be honest, I was sure that the team would work out their mistakes made in the first part, and that the second part would turn out to be a full-fledged B-grade game (the first part was like the heat of enthusiasm of a fan of a well-known series of games). However, I was disappointed, but I was disappointed for free - the game was given to me by a friend. This somewhat smoothes out my generally not the most pleasant feelings from the game.Almost everything in the game is weak - the plot, narrative, representation of characters, level design (it is especially bad). More or less bearable is only the gameplay, which has been tightened up since the first part. The funny thing is that in the first part there were quite a lot of problems with it, but with the rest everything else was relatively good. In this part the situation is mirrored. Everything except the gameplay is either terrible or tolerable at best (I would hardly call that a successful rating scale for a product that is actually supposed to keep you entertained). If you're very interested after going through the first part, then don't rush in - the full price game isn't worth it. It's better to wait for a good discount and then already suffer your six to eight hours. Though even then I can't recommend this mixture of toothache and hot delirium.

_childDocuments_.review: After 6 hours I think my conclusion is that it may be ok on sale for 10€ or so, as long as you don't expect triple-A quality. Or if you're starved of survival horror games because you played them all and still need your fix... I would like to compare it to the first one, which I actually liked quite a bit. But it has very little in common with that.Lets start with something minor - the running animation, which is weird. The character has this weird way of jumping while running, which is a bit distracting. But so be it.The puzzles are incredibly easy, while the hacking sucks. You will fail the harder hacks and you have only 3 attempts before you can reload your save, otherwise you can't open the door. I don't know why they designed it this way, no one is gonna think "Oh well, I missed one of the few upgrade machines, let's just move on". Saves WILL be reloaded due to failed hacks. Mind you, I played on the hardest difficulty available before the first playthrough and I don't know if this affects hacking. But the choice to have this hacking system at such a difficulty is odd.The enemies suck. They aren't creepy, they just spawn (= teleport) in and rush you, triggering a button mashing prompt to shake them off. Or they spawn in and shoot at you. Many of them need to be frozen before you can kill them, which means fiddling with your frost gimmick while there's still other enemies around. One enemy type is an instakill if he gets close. So far I have encountered 3 enemy types in 6 hours. Now the first game also didn't have much variety in this regard, but since ALL the enemies teleport in and work the same way, it gets old quite fast.The weapons were a puzzling choice - you have your 2 starting weapons and that's it. You don't find any other weapons (or rather: You can't pick any up). You don't have any sort of ammo or magazine management like in the first game, no different ammo types. It's really just a machine pistol and a shotgun. And your ice gimmick thing. Which isn't a terrible thing - freezing enemies, putting out flames, having a puzzle or two... All neat. The amount of enemies requiring its use is a bit meh though.The characters are.... Well, there really is just a handful of them and they're pretty much all just soldiers. No variety at all and nothing one could actually call much of a character. Again unlike the first game, where you even played different characters each with their own story.The environment so far is "military base". So don't expect too much variety here either.I suppose the game was meant to be way more action oriented than the first one (as was the case with many sequels in the survival horror genre), but I don't think this was the right choice here, nor do I find it to be executed very well. Basically the game is worse than the first one in pretty much every regard (in my opinion, although some disliked the tedious ammo management of the first game) by dropping a lot of the survival horror elements (such as item management, ammo conservation etc., see above).Now don't get me wrong, it's not "bad". It has its creepy moments, atmosphere and environments. It has some sort of a basic story. I just don't think it holds up well to the competition out there, nor to its own predecessor. Add the price tag and recommending this starts becoming really hard. Thus, my conclusion: If you played it all and need more, maybe check it out during a sale. If it drops to something like 10€, sure - take a look at it. At its regular price I can't really give a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought their prior title, and while it was incredibly rough, I gave them the benefit of the doubt. Because it was their first run. I expected a much better experience, competent writing, and dialogue that doesnt sound stilted and recorded from the VAs personal computer. Unfortunately that didn't happen. The animations for the game are very poor, especially the running animation, its absolutely jank. The writing and dialogue was clearly done by a non english speaker with someone who is not a native english speaker translating it to English, or perhaps AI translation, and the VAs are very amateur, I can hear the chair the female VA was sitting on in real life while she is speaking in game, as well as echoing and general poor artifacting in the voice lines from the recording device. Like they recorded on a walmart headset. The combat is not fluid, and the general gameplay of the combat encounters is very clunky. Overall, an amateur effort from a studio who apparently did not learn their lessons on their first go around and just said "good enough". I will be refunding the game, which is a shame. I wanted to like it, I think the general premise is very interesting. But work just isnt there. It feels like an early access game. I got this on sale and its not worth the $24 dollars I spent on it. _childDocuments_.review: To start the video reviewMy stream , subscribe to my channel ^^ I played beta last year , this project was very hooked , and then she waited for this moment , bought it yesterday and played until the very morning , liked it so much that I am very happy with the gameThe survival horror genre has certainly gotten its renaissance recently with titles such as Resident Evil 4 Remake, Dead Space Remake, and Signalis; hopping on the trend would be Invader Studios’ Daymare : 1994 Sandcastle.Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is the prequel of its previous title – Daymare: 1998, but now with a different UI and varying gameplay mechanics in it.StoryThe story follows Dalila Reyes, former government spy now a member of a specialist squad of H.A.D.E.S., now tasked to uncovering the mystery of an underground research facility. The overall pacing for the story decently paced, however there were some sections where it felts a bit sluggish but it can be overlooked.One minor gripe with the story is that some instances of the plot doesn’t fit quite well, where they build up the suspense of certain story beats. only to be forgotten about later. That being said, Daymare 1994 does an excellent job in terms of building up the story and I was constantly interested in it.PresentationIn terms of graphical presentation, it’s relatively decent. Admittedly, I only play the game on Medium graphic settings, so I won’t really go into the quality of it. The flies in the jail area are just PNGs moving around and the animation of the character during cutscenes look a little awkward. However, the environment design team does a great job in terms of creating the atmosphere, In the earlier level with the overrun lab, it looks technologically advanced yet creepy at the same time because of the black goo that spreads around just about everywhere. Later on in the residential area, the setting and the vibe does make it feel like an abandoned underground city that is overrun by monsters, which makes the game a lot more immersive.Speaking of monsters, the visual designs are fine, and it doesn’t quite look scary or creepy to me. One thing that’s an improvement over Daymare: 1998 is that you can easily tell if they’re really dead. When alive, the monsters would glow blue or red, and killing them despite them still standing, their eyes and body won’t glow anymore, which is nice for ammo conservation. In the last game, it’s hard to tell if the enemy’s dead and you’ll end up putting more bullets in them than you should.In terms of audio, there’s minimal BGM when exploring and trying to get to the next stage. To me, this is perfect, because instead of blasting eerie and creepy music, the only thing you hear is the sound of your footstep, with that echoing in an open space just amplifies the overall creepiness. When it comes to the voice acting, the delivery sounds a bit out of place. The tone of some of the lines that were delivered doesn’t quite match what they said in that situation.ExplorationThe exploration of the game is pretty much just like any other game where you run around finding clues for the puzzles, collecting resources like ammo and first aid, then continue progressing in the story. In Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle, there’s very little backtracking that you need to do. In the rare occasion that you do need to backtrack, you don’t have to do back far, and you can unlock a shortcut when doing so.There were two instances where I went through different routes only to go back to the same place that I needed to go to, which is neat and makes the game feel fresh even though you’re going back to the same place. That being said, the exploration for the game is quite linear where there aren’t branching paths, just a single line ahead with the occasional backtracking. Daymare 1994 has you solve puzzles along the way, and there will be things that can be scanned using the new mechanic the H.A.D.E.S. Scanner. If something nearby can be scanned, there will be a visual and audio notification where you can equip your scanner and try to find out where it is. The close your pointer is to the scannable object, the smaller the circle is, and then you can proceed from there.It’s a pretty useful tool that lets you know more about the world and setting of the game. Aside from the scanner, you’d also occasionally find documents laying around, which will also fill you in with some lore, and even give you hints on how to find the passcode required in a certain area or puzzle.Combat and Encounter DesignSuffice to say, Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is more geared towards action game fans. Gone are the realistic reloading system from the previous title that would be detrimental to you, in with the common reloading system that most games adapts, which makes combat much more enjoyable and responsive.Frost GripThe Frost Grip is Daymare 1994’s unique mechanic which is a glove that is connected to a tank of liquid nitrogen which is carried on your back, and you use it to solve puzzles and kill enemies. It’s a well designed mechanic that isn’t just for a one time use gimmick. In fact, the more you progress through the game, the more you have to rely on it.Ammo is scarce in this game, and if you’re not careful at managing your recourse, more often than not you’d find yourself running out of ammo and being overwhelmed by hordes of enemies. While bullets are still the best way to handle a horde, the Frost Grip can be a saving grace in terms of ammo conservation since you can perform a finisher on a frozen enemy. Daymare 1994 Sandcastle ReviewYou can also upgrade the glove if you find a terminal. Early on in the game, you can only do small upgrades like increasing its capacity or increasing its freezing speed, but you can unlock new functions like frost mines or bombs later on. Speaking of, I found myself abusing the frost mines pretty frequently considering it’s such a useful tool that prevents enemies from ambushing you by using the corpse you walked past a minute ago. While the bomb is useful in combat with multiple enemies, the wind up animation takes a bit longer. Daymare 1994 Sandcastle ReviewOn the topic of encounters, while I think the mechanic of the enemies are fun and requires for you to think before you go guns blazing, some of the encounters are pretty annoying where they throw in way too many enemies at you, and you don’t have the time to stop and do anything.D.I.D SystemThe D.I.D system is a main theme of the Daymare series, which is the inventory system and the UI for you to solve some puzzles. D.I.D in the game is a portable computer that is equipped onto the character’s hand, much like a Pip-Boy in the fallout series.Daymare 1994 Sandcastle ReviewThe UI for Daymare 1994’s D.I.D system has improved leaps and bounds as compared to its 1998 counterpart. It looks much cleaner and it’s a lot easier to use, which has honestly been a big blessing considering how annoying it was to navigate in the previous game.VerdictDaymare: 1994 Sandcastle is a solid game with tons of well designed stuff that complement each other and fits into place. The Frost Grip is a really fun and unique mechanic that definitely comes in handy when dealing with enemies.Daymare 1994 Sandcastle ReviewThe exploration part of the game is pretty enjoyable too with the environmental design that gives off the vibe of a creepy underground lab mixed in with an abandoned city. Paired with the minimal backtracking that you need to do, I enjoyed the overall level design of the game.I do have some minor gripes with the game though, like the weapon handling, especially when it comes to the shotgun which I feel like can be improved. All in all, I would still recommend Daymare : 1994 Sandcastle if you’re looking for an enjoyable survival horror game.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: When the first demo was released, I wrote a feedback to the developer regarding the combat, that the hyper aggressive enemy does not fit the ultra slow control. At that time there were also many posts in the community having the same concern, however, little has improved in the final product and combat is the weakest aspect of the game.The game has a sluggish control to imitate the tank control from classic Resident Evil for more tension, but was done in a horrendous way – slow to aim, slow to swap guns, slow to reload, slow to shoot out freezing gas, painfully slow to move while aiming (almost not moving). In addition, shooting feels bad and plastic, with continuous shooting causing obnoxious camera shake. Tank control in Resident Evil works because enemies are slow, but in Daymare 1994 Sandcastle they are fast, aggressive, and come in horde, with many can teleport mid-combat. What’s worse, combat is further complicated by enemy mechanics:I don’t think these intricate mechanics are bad design on their own, but paired with the slow control and the very short amount of time to react on, combat just feels cumbersome, hectic and frustrating.It is hectic but manageable when enemies all spawn at the front, but in some levels, enemies spawn from multiple directions, that is when combat becomes extremely annoying and frustrating of you being grabbed repeatedly because you either can’t see enemies from the sides or back while dealing with those in the front, or you notice but are too slow to do anything because of the control.In particular, I really hate the imprecise hitbox, where you can be grabbed despite seemingly being out of range. This is extremely infuriating in the gimmicky final boss fight where the grab can send you back to the beginning of the fight (the fight requires avoiding being grabbed and aiming at teleport destination in advance by observing the flash produced by teleportation). The developer also have a bad habit of putting enemies at entrance corners as cheap jump scares, leaving you spilt second to react on. In short, the irritating and poorly balanced combat is worse than the combat of the first game (Daymare 1998).The game also suffers from a general lack of content: It is quite a shame and wasted potential that the game is not quite fleshed out, because the environment design is amazing and the ominous atmosphere is enjoyable.In timeline, Daymare 1994 is the prequel of the first game, but the story is basically unrelated as Daymare 1994 is an Area 51 horror with no focus on the zombie outbreak in Daymare 1998. This time the story is decent and storytelling has improved a lot to be more cohesive compared to the fragmented narrative of the first game. While character eyes occasionally seem out of focus in cutscenes and fighting scenes remain stiff, cutscenes are done much better than Daymare 1998, especially in terms of character models.As a Resident Evil style survival horror, Daymare 1994 Sandcastle surpasses many counterparts on Steam in quality, but the combat is just so poorly executed and infuriating that it significantly degrades the overall experience. I literally smashed my keyboard many times because of the combat. It is a hard pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like it, but it fails at almost everything.Pros:- Cool gimmick with the frost grip, you can freeze enemies and have some abilities.- Sound design is above average.- Music although few, are nice. _childDocuments_.review: The instagrab feature of the enemies ruined the gameplay and in turn the fun of this game entirely. The game itself, setting, story, graphics whatever is interesting and I want to play it, as I really liked the previous Daymare. But this feature of the enemies giga-sprinting toward you and instagrabbing you, forcing a button mash that always results in loss of HP just completely ruins the gameplay. I get that they want you to use the frost stuff to slow and freeze the enemies but that's neither fun nor a reliable way to stop many enemies at once. The use of that mechanic really, really should have been a tool in your arsenal and not a requirement.The gameplay loop becomes such a slodge because of this, all you can do when enemies spawn is run away, freeze a few enemies, shoot, repeat until there are too many enemies to freeze or you run out of freeze juice, or one gets too close and then you just get grabbed the millisecond they come into range and you have to buttonmash to get away and still lose HP. This just feels like a poor design choice and is a downgrade from the first game. This could have been so easily avoided if the enemies didn't sprint like Usain Bolt for the instagrab but rather had some variable movement speed and attack patterns that you could evade using traditional movement or a dodge ability. And if your weapons actually had any meaningful impact stagger. Or if they would simply perform an attack that you could dodge or you know... get hit by when they get close, but not get locked into a buttonmash.

_childDocuments_.review: I really freaking loved Daymare: 1998 so there was no way I would not play the studio's next project: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle.A quote from a fellow player that seriously sums up the genre:People complain so so much about this game, expecting some sort of AAA production and quality, nitpicking flaws and reasons why this is not good enough.But they forget that this is a project made by such a small handful of people with a heavy focus on 90s horror gaming style of creativity. The people of invader Studios share such a strong love for the RE series that they even collaborated with people who actually worked on the RE games, and they even have a cameo of the guy who portrayed Chris Redfield in the 1996 Resident Evil cinematics!Here is the short version of my take:Everything, and I mean EVERYTHING is an upgrade from the previous game. Combat, animation, graphics, physics, direction, photography, animation, character design, voice acting.You can see that there has been so much care and love and attention put into this game. And this is the kind of things you don't easily find in the AAA industry.The elephant in the room ever since the reveal trailer has been, and I get it, that the lore is going to a different direction than the traditional zombie survival that we all love and wanted.Quite honestly I was also very sceptical. I would so love to see a return back to a RE1, 2 and 3 level of zombie survival horror, starting with weak weapons and limited resources and try to make my way through killing creepy undead, and not starting with a SMG and a shotgun killing electromagnetic anomaly infused monsters.But the whole experience doesn't want to be that. In fact the game doesn't try to push and give us direct lore connections to Daymare 1998.For me this could easily be the equivalent between 2 games that exist in the same world design. And maybe some time in the future we might get a title that connects them. And maybe not and that's just fine for me.I loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get the quite medicore review score and the people saying that this game is not an improvement over Daymare 1998. In my opinion this is almost in every way better than the first game. I'd say for an indie survival horror game it's actually pretty good.The good-it's looks all right (except character models but even those are much imroved)-good atmosphere even though it's not that big on horror-performance is almost always pretty good-story is actually kinda interesting, cutscenes, voice acting and writing is all right-decent length for the price (first playthrough took me about 8h to 100% on medium getting all collectibles)-mostly fun combat-thankfully this game got rid of the annoying reloading mechanic of the first game-surprisingly polishedThe not so good-there are only 2 guns in the game (mp and shotgun), and you start the game with both, which is kinda weird. Even though it still works I would have wished to get more weapons during the game. At least find a revolver or something.-And while the shotgun is pretty good, the mp is kinda underpowered.-then you get the frost grip, which basically freezes enemies, which is fine, but it can also kill them. And especially once you get this upgraded a bit, a single enemy poses no threat and will also cost you no ammo as the frost grip recharges over time. Which means the "optimal way" to play this game is kill a single enemy with the frost grip, then wait quite a long time, till it gets fully recharged, then go on. Not only the waiting is obviously annoying but this is also op, as won't lose any ressources this way. The game kinda recognizes this issue and throws pretty much always multiple enemies at you at once.And even then you can often kill all enemies during a fight with the frost grip but you will probably have to use an item to recharge it instantly during the fight. So basically the frost grip is your third weapon and I feel like the later in the game I was the more I used it. To the point I don't think I ever fired a gun in the last 1-2 hours, having tons of ammo in the inventory with no way to use.-there is one enemy which can teleport himself, insta kills you on a melee attack, has tons of health and summons other zombies. This package is just dumb.-the final boss (which is also the only boss in the game) pretty much sucks.

_childDocuments_.review: , it was janky, goofy but had a ton of effort & passion behind it. & the demo of Daymare 1994 felt really impressive for the most part, so I was excited for this.1994 has some really cool improvements over 1998, but there are a few iffy bits to 1994, which again warrant some caveats.BUT, I still want to recommend this (try the demo!), it's just a bit of a side-grade to 1998, play it on Story difficulty at least before a patch that handles the slightly conflicting enemies, mechanics & ammo drop system, so that combat remains minimally annoying, but even on Story it kind of becomes frustrating in all the forced arena fights because you don't feel like you have similar tools & moves someone like Isaac Clarke or Leon Kennedy has in DS or RE4 at their disposal for proper crowd control.Frost Grip is cool, but it's slow, you don't instantly slow enemies with the spray, & missing frost bullets is a huge cost when enemies have fast dodges & literal teleport moves, it becomes tedious & frustrating more than balanced & challenging. Reyes has no dedicated melee move or dodge move. Shotgun isn't crowd control, it's your semi accurate short range magnum that just as easily misses when enemies get close fast, SMG has no stagger/flinch/stun/slow capabilities & is only worth using for frozen enemies to kill, but good luck managing freezing enemies when you are being rushed by 3-4 runners with 1-2 spitters stunning you at a distance & oh now a runner grabbed you & you have to button mash to free yourself & the one you killed spawned an orb that now quickly floated to resurrect a corpse in an instant while you were grabbed & then necromancers show up who infinitely spawn orbs, & if you get too close (or they teleport too close to you) then it's an insta kill move. There are forced combat arenas. Ammo only drops if you have none even on Story difficulty.It's not all bad. For one the shotgun, SMG & Frostgrip feel really good, their audio, visuals & overall handling (barring enemy hit reactions) are really juicy & solid, & though the arsenal feels more limited than 1998 still the shotty, SMG & frostgrip all have upgrades that are well thought out and provide a good sense of progression.Enemy designs are for the most part pretty fun! & they do have roles in combat that makes sense, it's just that they don't cooperate in unison with all other mechanics properly.Your main character handles pretty nicely, movement, aiming, all feel like an improvement over 1998, & 1998 was already pretty solid on the third person character controller handling for the most part. It's just a shame Reyes doesn't have like a melee like Isaac or some other options in combat arenas like Leon jumping over fences or kicking, & the game could have really used some environmental hazards to exploit against the enemies, picture the stasis canisters Isaac could shoot/launch at enemies in DS2, now picture explosive nitrogen tanks littered around combat arenas here, would only make sense & fit the combat loop perfectly.The environmental artists, level designers & audio designer did a killer job, I loved navigating & looking around the albeit linear levels, 1994 ditches the restraints of sticking to only zombies,, which means many of the locations, the stuff it plays around with, the visuals of some of the aftermaths and secret laboratories and such have a lot more variety & freedom to create more cool looking weird extravagant facilities. Picture Black Mesa underground facilities with the scale of some places like in Control.It's hard to pick any favourite, but I want to pick one kind of mundane location just to make a point.There's a section where you go back outside, need to get to a helicopter, there's a massive sandstorm in the nighttime, & the look of it all, the oppressive darkness, sand blowing & cables banging around, volumetric lights shining at spots, the howling & creaking sounds everywhere, it felt like Hadley's Hope from Aliens, these devs would probably make a killer Aliens game (as long as they'd get the balancing/gameplay right). All the sound design, OST & locations, come together REALLY well, probably some of the best UE4 devs out there to make this engine not look as ugly as it can often, I saw none of the usual issues I tend to notice in UE4, ambient/indirect light tastefully used and worked around, SSR not overdone, ambient occlusion limited & decent, just none of the usual pitfalls anywhere, & so many cool dynamic lights/shadows in smokey foggy dusty areas with striking colors. Rivals the REmakes in many ways visually (& like I said I was having happy Black Mesa & Control sensations admiring all the impressive architecture), some lower detail textures weirdly in faces almost exclusively? Maybe DLSS was degrading the quality, not sure. (& lip syncing too isn't perfect, but mocap is much improved over 1998.)Story is pulpy & cheesy, I do think the writers know & intended it, this is still inspired by the old school 90's survival horror titles & old cheesy scifi horror movies, there's a lot of effort in background logs, environmental details & the setting, & honestly I was so relieved when in the end they Final "boss fight" is a bit frustrating, but nowhere near the frustration of 1998 boss encounter, this at least felt sort of doable, just wish there was a bit more delay between the warning you get & the teleport Performance was 60fps 97% of the time, had a dip into the 40s in a cutscene where Reyes wakes up & looks at what is maybe a planar reflection that they used in that cutscene, & towards the end there were a handful of rooms that fluctuated a bit, but not massively.Played with all maxed/Ultra/"3" settings with some  Had DLSS at Quality, resolution 1366x768, looked really nice, one of the better looking UE4 games that like I said didn't suffer from some usual issues.(laptop, win11, 16GBRAM, i5-11400H, 3050RTX 4GBVRAM)Despite some frustrations with game balance, that will most likely see some patching, the hacking, & the fact that you don't have a huge arsenal like in DS or RE or even 1998, enemies are a bit limited & frustrating in the mechanics, & levels are DS2 levels of linear & not as open as 1998-- Still, the overall feel of each weapon & their upgrades, enemies, the wonderful locations visually, atmospherically, Reyes our character, the pulpy story & the direction it took towards the end, the goofy cutscenes-- I still enjoyed this a lot, I'd recommend this, on Story difficulty if you aren't typically S ranking RE games on hardest difficulty-- Which could change with a patch.I hope Reyes returns in a future installment, & we get to see more of this utterly crazy world Invader Studios are making.Try the demo!
_childDocuments_.name: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle

_childDocuments_.review: - Its setting is a mixture of the Resident Evil and Dead Space sagas.- Combat is a lot of fun, especially when we get our hands on the Frost Grip: you'll love it!- The sound is outstanding, both its soundtrack and its sound effects: totally advisable to play with headphones.- It has a multitude of very funny easter eggs.- We can't pet the dog at the beginning.- The variety of enemies is very scarce. - Some enemies can kill us when they trap us, something very frustrating: it would have been great to have an escape mechanic like in Resident Evil.- We only have three weapons available: the submachine gun, the shotgun and the Frost Grip. Although in reality with the Frost Grip we will have enough: freezing enemies is the best. Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is a remarkable title that improves on the first part in many ways, while in others it is a step backwards, for example with the enemies. As I said before, there is less variety of enemies, although in its favor we must say that they have gained in agility compared to the first part, so the game forces us to think well how we face the different situations.7.5/10. Have I mentioned that playing with the Frost Grip is very fun? Thanks to its use, the game becomes less repetitive and gains in fun, and that its duration ranges between 7 and 10 hours, depending on whether we want to get all the collectibles or not.If you read all its reviews, you will see that there is no unanimity: either you love the game, or you hate it. For my part, as a great lover of survival horror, I have to say that I liked it a lot and I had a lot of fun. Being objective, I think that if you like the genre you should get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In this episode I return to one of my favourite Zombie Survival Series Daymare, as I cover Daymare 1994 Sandcastle. This game is the prequel to Daymare 1998 and was developed by Leonardo Interactive, who also worked on the Visual Novel Shattered Heaven ive also reviewed. The game has moved from Destructive Creations to a new publisher 4Divinity.Daymare Sandcastle takes place four years before the events of Daymare 1998 and follows Dalila Reyes, a skilled engineer and operator for the shadowy HADES Organisation. Dalila is deployed as part of Operation Sandcastle, a journey into a secrety underground facility located in Area 51, where an experiment into an advanced new metallic compound has gone terribly wrong. The player will venture into the depths of the facility, mastering experimental new weapons and tools, solving puzzles and battling a terrifying new type of predator. Along the way you will learn more about the Hades Organisation and the Iconic Characters from the Original Daymare.This game is a departure from the more slow paced, horror approach of the original Daymare, favouring more fast paced gunplay, which some players didnt favour. However the introduction of some inventive new weapons and tools, some clever new puzzles, as well as far more savage and deadly new enemies ensure that the the tense atmosphere from the series remains intact. Players can also tailor their gameplay experience with a plethora of new difficulty options. This game is an must play for fans of Daymare: 1998 as it fills in many of the unanswered questions, providing more details on the iconic characters and the origins of the HADES organisation.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. _childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game in order to satiate my never.ending hunger for survival horror, however, It's scary and tense the first hour you play it, but once you get accustomed to how the enemies act, it becomes a repetitive and tedious slog. Dont worry though, you get not one but TWO choices regarding guns to you can use, a shotgun with so much screen shake, you feel like youre having a seizure, or an mp5 that has the same exact issue if you shoot more then 15 rounds at one time. The freeze mechanic is a nice twist wich i did thoroughly enjoy to a point. But it just becomes to tedious to be forced to use it on most enemies in order to progress. Between the terrible flashlight and GIANT blue beacon from the frost grip on your back, its going to be almost impossible to see anything in dark rooms for a large portion of the game. All in all, go buy Daymare 1998, FAR superior game by the same studio.

_childDocuments_.review: The developer prides itself on recreating the atmosphere of action-horror films from the ‘90s, but outside of an admittedly strong opening track in the style of John Carpenter’s best tunes, there is not a single reference that sounds or feels fun, genuine, or worthwhile. Simply quoting X-Files and other sci-fi horror titles from that time is not a wink, but rather a reminder of how the player’s time could be better spent watching these films and shows. Even the voice acting, which could embrace a campy tone, is a total flatline, with the quality of the performances lessened by the lifeless facial expressions of the character models.While it is an overall improvement over Daymare: 1998, Sandcastle is still not a game worth playing. At around eight hours in length, it is a slog to get through, with a serviceable opening hour with good use of Unreal Engine 4, yet nothing of interest from there on. Invader Studios should try less to recreate the success of bigger titles, instead refocusing their energies on something smaller and more original, because they have the potential for something more than a modern Resident Evil clone without the nailbiting combat or the challenging puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: I recently had the pleasure of discovering Daymare 1994 and I have to say, it's certainly one of the best horror games I've ever played. The game immerses you with visuals that are reminiscent of classic films like Alien and Resident Evil, while the sound design and atmosphere remain unique and engaging. The gameplay is challenging but rewarding, featuring an array of weapons, puzzles, and enemies to keep you on your toes. No matter how well the player performs, there's always something to be gained—which makes the experience all the more satisfying.In comparison to many AAA horror games, Daymare 1994 far surpasses them in quality. The visuals, sound design, gameplay, and level design all receive high marks, while so many games in the genre tend to fall short. Furthermore, the game follows a horror narrative without relying on cheap jump-scares or recycled clichés. In the end, what I found really impressive is that Daymare 1994 managed to remain engaging throughout its runtime, while a lot of other horror games just tend to drag. If you're a horror fan and are looking for something fresh and engaging, I highly recommend Daymare 1994.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from someone that had played the first game, I am thoroughly disappointed.My issues with the game are: bad facial animations, bad lip syncing, bad story, absolutely awful characters (everyone sucks), attack delay, and inconsistent rewards.First I want to address the lip syncing and the facial animations. Considering I have written a few english dubs for french cgi projects, I was baffled the entire game. I just kept trying to understand how the dubbing was handled. Considering the faces had no emotion and their lips didn't sync up with a single thing said. Normally we'd just capture facial animations with mocap.Next the story. So, the overall concept is not a bad idea. The execution is the problem. I hated absolutely every character in the game. They are all just awful, hateful, arrogant ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Not to mention just bad people in general too. Plus, they expect me to care about some of these people. Without any kind of buildup or anything. This is a problem I come across whenever I have rough draft for scripts. Usually needing to fix the narrative to help it make sense. Making character profiles, trying to create some background to help link everything together. Here, it is just a mess.And last, the gameplay itself. My biggest issue has to be without a doubt the lag in attack response time. Having died many many times when I really shouldn't have. Plus running is slow and janky looking. Although, I will not forgive the bonus / reward system in the game. Finding every secret item in the game will only reward you with concept art....even though it is an absolute pain to find every dang bobblehead, you only get concept art in the end.However, all of this is not what prompted me to write a bad review. Oh no, I was just going to choose neutral, but then I encountered the final boss.I don't know what it is with these Daymare games, they just cannot plan a good final boss fight. This was my biggest gripe with the first game. Now it's even worse.Where the boss will grab you, bringing you back to the very start of the area over and over and over and over and over and over again!!!I had rage quit it soooo many times over such a stupid and pointless mechanic that achieves absolutely nothing!!!I bought the game to help support this developer since I had a good experience with the first one, but this second game is just awful!
_childDocuments_.name: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the first Daymare in both setting and gameplay. I was really hoping this one would improve upon it.I will get straight to the point. In this new installment, all fights are irritating. Every fight is in tight arenas and hallways, and the enemies sprint at twice your speed with insta-grapples and teleport with insta-kills. While you do have the ice gauntlet with CC capabilities, it is very slow to inflict CC (even with upgrades) and the enemies tend to come in packs and resurrect quickly if you are not constantly paying attention. On top of their fast speed they will input read and teleport out of the way of your shots which feels very punishing when ammo is already so limited. Overall, there was no encounter where I had fun as the enemies always felt cheap. Also, why so many hidden enemies around corners? Just felt like an unnecessary health tax.The story and setting is similar to the first. You are alone running around a military complex where all the walls got a fresh coat of red paint, trying to figure out why everyone is taking a forever nap. It is your typical B grade story line and setting.Graphically it is good. Everything looks nice and sets the mood. Although I wish the enemies were more interesting than electric zombies.The sound is also something they nailed. Nothing to complain about there.It is unfortunate that this one just felt so bad to play, since I really like the world they are trying to build here.I really do look forward to their next installment and hope to see them improve on the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: I would only recommend this game when it goes on a bigger sale. One of the most atrocious flashlights in any game I have ever played. You will spend most of the game squinting your eyes trying to find your way around dark corridors and tight passages while trying not to get lost because the flashlight barely illuminates anything at all and it also has such a tight radius.Combat is simply enough but the enemy's way of dealing damage is simply horrendous and down right annoying. The common enemy's only attack is a lunge that forces you to do a QTE by smashing the space bar as fast as you can because it deals damage to you the whole time the QTE is active. Don't even get me started on the Sparker's ability to insta-kill you when they manage to get close enough to you.The addition of freezing powers is a fresh idea in the beginning but ends up being an annoying alternative to not wasting ammo when dealing with enemies. It does not help that enemies are really fast and if you try to shoot them with a freeze bullet and miss, you end up with very little time to evade their grabs. Without upgrades, the freeze power ends up being a tool that you will have to recharge while running in circles inside a room full of enemies waiting for it to fill up in order to have another chance at freezing them. Voice acting is just bad, honestly. It barely kept me invested in the story but it did manage to make me laugh every now and then when the characters sounds like they were just reading from script as they are being attacked by enemies.Honestly, go play the first game instead. At least that game was in the category of "so bad it is funny" and it is what made me excited for Sandcastle because of its cheesiness  and campy feeling. Sandcastle tries to take itself too seriously and failes at the execution, ending up just being a bad game without the charm that made the first one special.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ... something. First of all, a few words of praise. Aside from the absolute terrible facial animations of the characters, the visual presentation is stunning. The problem with the presentation is that this game tries really, really hard to be the Resident Evil 2 remake. You can tell where the designers got their inspiration, e.g., with the frost grip device that is essentially there to mimic Isaac's suit from Dead Space. The inventory and the entire menu were ripped straight from the recent Resident Evil games, leaving Daymare 1994 with very little identitiy of its own, which is a shame because the setpieces and level design (visually, not conceptionally) are amazing. If you're asking yourself how hard this game wants to be Resident Evil 2, there is a building in which you need keys designed after the four colors in a deck of cards.The voice actors did an ok job, nothing to complain about.The controls are what you would expect from the genre (as I said, it tries to be RE2R really hard), but they can be clunky, especially when Dalila gets stuck on microscopic pieces of level geometry.The puzzles are kinda charming, really good, honestly! The one exception to this are the little hacking puzzles, which get way too hard as soon as the red dead zones are introduced. These could be cool, but the time limit is just too pressing. I feel like I missed out on a lot of resources that I would have needed for combat, but I just ignored these puzzles in later stages because I couldn't bring myself to save, practice the puzzles and come back after loading.The plot is neither here nor there. During your playthrough you will have a lot of downtime and typically the game will fill this downtime by giving you numerous folders and files to read. Those try to emulate the charm of "itchy tasty" diaries from the early Resident Evil games, but there is just too many of them and while some of them contain some useful information on upcoming puzzles, most of them are nonsensical flavour and designed to steal your time. I'll try to avoid spoilers, but the "Helen" plot the players will face in the late game is bad writing and this is a hill I am willing to die on.The flashlight is pathetic and the game is, overall, very dark. That works in some areas, but doesn't work in most.This game must have some of the worst encounter designs in the entirety of the survival horror genre. While the combat gameplay with the two different weapons and the "frost grip" (essentially a spray pistol full of liquid nitrogren) offers enough tactical value, the combat is not designed to make any use of the tools you are given. More often than not, the game will throw endless amounts of enemies at. Currently, I have encountered three different types and to be honest, they all suck. The regular zombie type will grab you and drain your health. The bloated type will stun you from afar using bursts of energy that can be dodged (unless you're being grappled by a zombie) and the third type is essentially a bullet sponge that will kill you instantly when its close range to you. The problem is that you have no downtime between attacks. You might just have successfully gotten rid of a zombie grapple, just to be instantly grappled by a bloater who just teleported right into. Enemies will also not really stay dead because as long as there are dead bodies nearby, their "spark" can jump over and resurrect another body. All this makes sure that there is a steady supply of new enemies to attack you as soon as you're free from a grapple or stun. The only way to deal with these fights consistently is to play them over and over, letting yourself be killed as soon as ending the fight would cost too many resources and just try again. All fights seem to have one perfect solution, but in order to execute it on your first playthrough, you just have to grind the fight and memorize all enemy spawns beforehand. The frustration is really high with this one because the individual enemy types are kinda cool and the mechanics could be awesome, but there are just too many enemies in any given encounter. A special moment of idiocy occurs whenver the player is near large amounts of electric sludge because it impairs your frost grip device in that it will take away half of your tank. This could be cool for a one off encounter, but it happens at least twice. During those fights, you would really need your tank. In the fights were you get to keep your entire capacity, you don't need it at all, leaving the sections in which the device is not working properly exceptionally awkward. Oh, by the way, hold on to whatever shotgun ammo you find because its the only useful weapon in the game. You have an smg and you find plenty of ammo for it, but it absolutely sucks. Your shotgun can help you get rid of enemies that are about to attack you, but the bullets from your smg have no stopping power and six hours into the game I have not encountered a single situation in which the smg was in any way, shape or form the superior gun. I mean, technically it has more range than the shotgun, so its great to know that I can use it to do little to no damage over great distances ... I guess.The final boss fight was a frustrating mess. The developers seemed to really love the idea of one hit reset enemies who teleport into your back. Probably the least fun section of the game.In sum, Daymare 1994 looks great, but it doesn't play great and missing out on this story you will miss out on absolutely nothing. Maybe check it out once the price drops!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great indie action-adventure survival horror game. It features a mixed vibe from the Resident Evil and Dead Space series. The excellent music and sound department matches a visually well-crafted creepy atmosphere. In terms of gameplay, you will encounter puzzles, zombie aliens, and bosses to defeat. The game offers players three weapons to alternate, including the Frost Grip bracelet, which can freeze monsters and wipe "energy" entities. Players must scavenge for essential items and collectibles while managing limited healing resources and ammunition. The plot is engaging, thrilling, and intriguing, with a few unexpected twists. The game's performance is smooth without any major stuttering issues, though there are minor hiccups after loading new sections and occasional framerate drops during cutscenes. So, despite the project's budget constraints, Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle is a commendable and enjoyable story-driven, third-person survival horror action game.
_childDocuments_.name: Daymare: 1994 Sandcastle

_childDocuments_.review: Operation Sandcastle is a pretty solid action-horror experience, definitely a lot of improvement over the previous "Daymare" title which I enjoyed, but still plenty of room for refinement. The story/narrative is much stronger and more a focal point this time around, with some surprisingly lengthy cutscenes and solid voice work. The lighting and sound both do wonders for building a decently spooky atmosphere. There is more good than bad for sure. Two of my biggest gripes are the lack of enemy + weapon variety, cmon only two guns? And the nerfed puzzles, the first game has some pretty nuts puzzles kinda was missing those here although the pipe/water valve one is good. The Frost arm is a great addition without that I feel the gameplay would be pretty meh, kinda like Dead Space's "Stasis" type of weapon to slow/cc enemies, it's pretty cool. The final boss is also underwhelming, they tease a huge fight that never comes instead you get this gimmick fight that's more annoying than fun. The simplicity of the gameplay loop does often work to it's benefit though not every game needs to have a novel worth of tutorials to be fun. It's much less survival horror than the previous game it's mostly straight action-horror which is both bad and good depends what you're after. I do really like the main character her story is interesting and she is well voice acted but her animations are a little wonky at times. The collectable alien coins all depict classic recognizable otherworldly beings like Predator/The Thing/Yoda/Mars Attacks ect which I thought was a nice touch. The performance is mostly great except some minor dips in the last segment, and I didn't notice any bugs or crashes ect, nicely done. Overall it's a fun game with some flaws but especially on sale well worth while to action-horror RE/DS type enjoyers. 7.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Daymare 2. Gotta say this one for some reason got me excited, maybe because I am a fan of small Development teams at the moment and some of the absolute belters for games they put out and Daymare 1 was a good homage of that. Daymare 2 however whilst it is a prequel plays absolutely no part in Daymare 1 in the slightest until the final moments leading up to the results screen, Daymare 2 is entirely it's own thing. Now I don't mind prequels in the slightest but when you go back in time and end up with better equipment than you did in the first place it kinda doesn't make any sense to me but we'll go along with it.Story - The story is well told in it's own light, once you make sense of all the things being said at the end of the game everything seems like it is starting to make sense with some confusion left over, possibly for further titles or just bits that have been skipped over by mistake (Nobody is perfect)However upon playing Daymare 2 the story is frantic in it's way of telling a story and setting up character relations (Mostly through notes and Cut-scenes).It isn't the worst but it's not my favourite.Game play - It feels dead responsive and very modern compared to 1998 which is good, sounds, lighting, gore, real time bullets projecting from the guns when they're fired. Frost Grip adds new elements to the way the game is played giving 3 new features, spray, projectile and a melee finisher when enemies are 100% frozen, Further upgrades include Ice Mines, A Shield (Which I got 0 use out of it just did nothing all game) and Cluster shots which were the most effective at freezing enemies until I got the Ice Beam in the very last area (Save the best til last, eh?). Disappointingly the Ice Beam is short lived and therefor not very useful in my opinion which is a shame because this could have been an unlockable or something to go into NG+ with (Had it existed)Enemies - There is not alot of variety going on at all...Basic blue zombie/Red ones which are immune to damage until frozen, Blue and Red Decoys (One's that shoot projectiles) and finally Sparkers which are the most original in design and what they can do but other than that enemies are few and far between when it comes to variety... I don't even think i've faced a boss of any sort quite lack lustre given Daymare 1998 had quite a lot going for it in terms of enemies, The Final boss is still better than Liev, that was just a dumb joke. Still kinda feels like the Devs put more effort into modernising the game than making the actual game.At the end the game sets up this huge boss that could have been a fight only to be killed by Cut scenes...And the Final Final Boss after all that isn't even a boss at all so yeah bit disappointed in that regard.Arsenal - Besides the Frost pack and it's upgrades the only 2 weapons so far the shotgun and SMG (Upgraded HADES edition) with I think I found 3 upgrades in all for faster reload and faster fire rates for the Shotgun and mag cap for the SMG...that was it really missed a trick with this one especially after having the like of RE4 and RE2Remakes showing you what small amount of upgrades they had yet how effective they were within the game.Hacking system is good to a degree but to have a Very Hard achievement tied to it is a big pig headed, these things aren't for everyone. Having opened all if not most of the Hacking systems the rewards aren't worth a dime, you get skins for weapons or upgrades but if you fail you miss out...pretty dumb when most of the Hacking games are all Very Hard or hard.The maps/level Design - The areas within the game feel fresh, new and to be fair quite enjoyable to be within, some are like mazes where you are to remember where you saw that door that needed a key you've found in latter areas others are just A-B there that stage is finished onto the next area with no warning that going beyond this point will make all collectables miss-able and you will need to replay, which is annoying and as I think I have stated before but i'll say it again there is no Map, everything looks the same in a lot of areas so going around and around not knowing where you're going or where you have been can be pretty annoying but if I had a map like the in 1998 i'd be able to find my way around easier so thanks for that Devs ¬_¬Music - has it's moments to add to the drama but there are times where it just doesn't seem to fit the mood are is even able to be heard in most cases.Graphically - Not the most blown away graphics, they're good but not the best yet they're making my GPU wanna kill itself at maximum setting so not 100% sure what the issues are there. We seem to be missing a map, although the areas are fairly linear so far.Having finished the game the lighting in the game has really fallen short, I've had to turn my brightness to 10/10 and I still can't see a damn thing and the weasel flashlight you've been given barely light a room without aiming a gun to focus the light, alongside the lighting failure there seems to be a lot of lighting particles on walls and textures making graphics appear grainy and unpolished.Something I have noticed regarding the scanner that finds hidden files...since you first arrive you find a magic door that appears using the scanner and since then i'm at the end of the game and I haven't come across this feature since, finding hidden doors within this underground military base would have been a good idea for finding new weapons,skins and upgrades but ah well.	Good 1990's asthetic along with the game, there's cassettes old time desktops and even the tech feels like it's from the 90's, it's really good.Feels like a lot of menus, extra screens and even collectibles are reminiscent of RE2RE, which is good it feels modern and upto date unlike Daymare 1 that needed a loading screen to open up a menu...Weapon swap feel so and realistic as they should be, not snappy. Perfect for causing panic when in Combat.Overall I have enjoyed my time with Daymare 1994 - It is a vast improvement over 1998 with some short falls. A Sequel I feel should come with what the predecessor sets up that is successful and adds new features to that build but Invader haven't done that with 1994, the game feels like Daymare and plays like Daymare but alot of the charm from the 1998 along with a lot of feature have seemingly not made the cut, no new weapons, no real upgrades along the way besides the cryo pack, enemy variety is stripped down to 3-5 enemies tops. There's just not a lot going on...yet it's a survival horror...advertised to be this huge scary overwhelming new threat and all this ♥♥♥♥ yet here I am at the end of the game still waiting for something to happen that enticed me during the likes of the demos and the trailers. I think the game is fair to be £25 as there are things to do beyond the story with achievements and getting S ranks and so on but I really think Invader have dropped the ball on this one. If the game is to receive any DLC or any updates I can only hope the majority of what I have mentioned either gets taken into consideration in future titles or DLC because it's a bit of a scam from the studio if you ask me. It kinda feels like RE3Remake, all the mistakes included, the maps are linear but the game feels great, exploration is to a minimum but you don't realise until you pass a point of no return with no warning. It's a shame really.7/10 hopefully future titles will improve on this formula.Nice little twist there at the end, all game waiting for some reference to 1998 and there it is, that was worth the wait so well done for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved 1998. This is complete trash. 3 enemy types - blue,  red and a floating thing.  Two guns and endless linear paths. Minimal exploration required. _childDocuments_.review: Solid action oriented survival horror so far, sound design is on point and probably one of the games strongest elements. My only real gripes are quite a few of the subtitles don't match up to what is being said by the characters and the controls/movement feels a little off, especially when I seem to randomly quick turn sometimes. Maybe a patch/QoL changes would help there.All in all really pleased with it so far, definitely an improvement on the first (which I still quite enjoyed tbh). Looking forward to playing more and maybe seeing what this studio puts out in the future too.Went back to this 6 months after release as the combat got very annoying with insta kill enemies and monsters spawning behind you with no indication and I'm glad the team balanced the game as I really enjoyed my playthrough for the most part!7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I understand that some people may feel that the controls are clunky and not very user-friendly, but when I look at the game as a whole, I think this was done on purpose. Perhaps have the character wear a suit that limits movement and makes the character slower. But the suit is necessary for the environment investigated. I like the story. It's not without some flaws but it is easy to follow and make sense. I have not played Daymare 1998 yet, but I will after this.  It definitely had Resident influences but it manage to be its own thing. I am looking forward for a third game of this series. Thank you developers for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I  think people are being a bit unfair to this game. I'm a Daymare fan and the only thing that was a major letdown for me in Sandcastle was the poor weapon variety (I get it that we were supposed to love the Frost Grip and I did, but seriously couldn't have devs thrown us a Magnum as well??) This is why people are finding the combat repetitive, I believe. Also barely any bosses. D98 had some fun creative boss fights, why weren't any of it here? ( I'm that minority who enjoyed the sparker arena, I thought it was very creative. Final boss was boring though). Also I hate the dumbed down healing system (why only one type of medipacks?) and inventory looks like a lazy RE2 copy (why not at least make it green like the DID screen?) Also the puzzle design is sadly a disappointment. I was expecting more environmental puzzles like it was originally shown in 2022 demo, like putting down the fire to find hidden items, but they weren't present nearly as much as I hoped. There are maybe 3 clever puzzles in such a long game (loved the water puzzle and hacking) but most are just point-and-click minigames, too easy and unmemorable. Also the freeze beam (which is FUN) is not  an unlockable option, and it's such a waste when it's easily the best weapon in the game. BUT despite my 5 paragraph rant here, I am far from being disappointed because everything else was a major improvement, especially the technical side of things, it's definitely a better optimized and polished experience than the first game. I found the controls and AI a lot more responsive and the combat is fun and has more to offers when you figure out how to utilize the Frost Grip (wish we had more guns though...) The art direction is stunning (I especially enjoyed scenes with Blue/Red lighting contrast, simply gorgeous). Dark hallways and corridors also fit the theme of the game - loneliness (the protagonist clearly has depression, so maybe this is why this game made such an impression on me). The writing is definitely a step-up in quality and the dialogues sound more natural. I was hoping for more lore-related material like the foundation of HADES, but still: if you didn't think Liev was the best character, you will feel for him now. AnywayI hope  will reunite... I don't care how, just do it🥺

_childDocuments_.review: Is it a good game? No. Is it a bad game? I don't think so either. I think the current "Mixed" rating status fits here. As many others have pointed out the battle system is completely off kilter. All the baddies do is run at you and grab you, one is an instant kill.  You really have no defense with how fast they run at you, you can freeze them but it is a gradual process, which results in a somewhat frozen baddie grabbing you. This game desperately needed a melee counter or a dodge mechanic. As it stands, you really have no defense against them. I got so frustrated with it that I just changed the difficulty to "Story", which I hardly ever do. Not including the final boss there are only three enemy types in the entire game and it is clear there were more planned at some point. So you are left with the story which sadly, is as by the numbers as they get, all building to one of them non-endings. I'd only recommend this to peeps who really like games of these types. Otherwise i'd pass. I give it a thumbs up due to the fact that there was clearly some passion here, despite the many problems. It's not a good game, but it can be entertaining at "times".

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm giving a positive review, biggest disappointment of the year.While the rest of the world was on full on hype over Baldurs Gate 3, Armored Core VI and Starfield, I paused all of those and got this on day one, because this was the game I was expecting.  I was playing the demo over 1 year ago, trying to give constructive feedback. I was hoping for a survival horror game, I was hoping for improving upon the previous game. Well, can't say it doesn't improve on the technical side. And it's the biggest reason I'm giving a positive review, even if I absolutely hated the game.Graphics are great, sound design is awesome, level design is absolutely incredible. It's just boring to play for me. Combat feels terrible, 2 weapons for the whole game. A powerless feeling SMG and a shotgun where if you miss the first shot, you won't have time for a second. The ice gimmick is boring and this combination makes every single fight follow the exact same formula.Game has like... 3 enemy types? I just finished and can only remember 3.I really understand why the devs made a more action game, I've read a ton of user reviews for the first game and I'm sure this will have a more palatable approach for "mass audiences".Just as the first game, the demo shows a very clear picture of what the full game is. If you like the demo, you'll like the full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Just got all of the achievements with just over 20 hours time played and I have to say this is a significant improvement over 1998.I actually enjoyed it, the gunplay was good, I liked the Frost abilities, added a different dimension to the combat. I thought Dalilia and Radek were good characters although some of the dialogue was a bit corny (not an issue).Only things that bugged me were the running animation during gameplay and facial animations/lip syncing in cutscenes (minor nit picks). Enemy variety however was lacking, this is something I feel alot of horror games like this don't get right very often, it got a bit boring fighting the same 3 enemy types the entire game with the only change being when they turn red and invincible to gunfire. Also, fighting in small areas was not all that fun with how easy it is for the Decoys to grab you (especially on hardcore). I'm not sure if it was just me experiencing this but on my first playthough the only deaths I had were from Sparkers with the instant death, especially with how far they were when grabbing me, it felt a bit cheap, it was easy to avoid this on my second and third playthroughs knowing to stay well clear but I do think their grab needs to be altered or atleast an ability with your frost grip to counter if you have enough energy left (we have this ability for when Decoys grab you so why not for Sparkers as well).Overall Good, solid game, would definitely recommend playing!
