Built 25, turned on auto, was expecting 25 planets to be colonized. Nope. all 25 went to exactly the same planet. Build 5 more while it was on auto. Exact same thing, all went to the same planet. When clicking colonize in the colonization screen, you can't send another ship out until the first one is colonized. Another stupid idea.Same for combat like pirates. You can only target 1 at a time (regardless number of ships). Playing with max pirates? It's literally take days in RL to wipe them all out. Since it takes about an hour per.Tech: Looks like a lot, but more like an idler game. Research one (like crew quarters), then next one is just 1 more crew. And it's like that for almost every friggen tech. Revised update  5-3-24:It has the exact same problems as DU1. Too many whys? It's infuriating and frustrating.:Why won't my colony ship load colonist, but instead just move or refuel? There's plenty of people there.Why won't my colony ship colonize a planet that's within range.Why won't my ship retrofit, even though I know it's not the lastest version.Why won't my constructor build a mining base here? I know it's in range.Why won't my explorer move anywhere?Why won't my fleet take my orders?Why won't my ship refuel when I tell it to?Why is there no option to repair my ship?Why won't my automated planet AI build any facilities?Why do I have to do all the planet facilities myself?Why isn't my AI doing any colonizing?Why does my automated AI just colonize 1 planet with all my colony ships?Why is my AI using my colony ship for exploration? Gee, how many times has this happened. Left without colonists to explore. What a dumb mechanic. Don't you know how long it take to build a colony ship in the first place and then to just send it off.Why does it take over an hour to attack a target I designated? I have more then enough for everything.Why are not my fully automated colony ships not loading colonists automatically? Instead they just sit there and do nothing.Why do I have to load them manually?Why do I have to manually colonize every planet? This is just what I could remember.Why can't I order a constructor to repair a damaged ship that can't move? That's just stupid. So I just leave it there forever.Why, why, why? Why are there so many why's?A lot of things only the AI can do and you can't. Welcome to the age of the cheating AI because we're not able to actually make a good AI.Adjust your UI scaling, expect problems.You can't turn pirates or monsters completely off. When you start you immediately encounter pirates that want you play a protecting fee that you really have no choice in not paying since you don't have ships to defend yourself with.When you sort info in the tabs, sometimes all the sort options aren't there. I had to click different tabs then come back to see if my preferred sort option was there.Also often times the combat is behind a planet where you can't see unless you're zoomed in all the way, then the planet disappears and you can see behind it. You can't zoom out, because if you do, you'll end up just looking at the planet. That's a lot of zoomed in scrolling around. What idiot thought this would be a good idea in a strategy game?Then there the heroes That I never figured out how to use so I left them on auto. After 15 hours some were still sitting in my pool waiting. Waiting for what I don't know.Never did figure out diplomacy. I tried multiple times to make a deal but never found a button to proceed. Think it's the case that it was at the bottom off screen. If you can't see it, you can't click it.Also lagging your game are private ships that are built in your construction yards. You have no control over them, you cannot queue them, they just do their own thing. Only thing I really like is that it tells you what resources you have and are short on. What I think was near mid game I almost had the whole tech tree done at the slowest speed.All they really did with this is add some shinies. Same issues as the first one and some new ones. It's littered with fanboys that will imply that you're an idiot because you don't understand the game immediately. And whatever you do, don't post a problem that you ran into. _childDocuments_.review: Took until the 1.0.5.3 Beta but I'd say it's perfectly playable now IF you've already experienced the rough-edged original. This is a 4X War-focused game. It's no going to indulge anyone's Federation dreams. There is a STEEP learning curve. Many players will bounce off it, just like I bounced off the original. Understanding how the automation works will transform the game from an irritating, often baffling, grind to a well-oiled machine. Thinking that the game "plays itself" is akin to finding a mouldy old MG Spitfire in a neighbours garage and assuming you can drive it home. You have to perfect your settings for the automation to work for you before you can confidently let fleets automatically guard your borders and harass your enemies, while you work on that masterplan that will break the spine of the enemy using your manually controlled fleets. Dastactic on Twitch and Scott on YT have streams and videos that will give you an education. Das is very methodical explaining what he's doing during his streams, and as he is playing with the latest Betas, whereas some of Scott's videos are months old, so I'd recommend that.

_childDocuments_.review: There is lots of good in this game, but also many fundamental problems.Let's compare it to Master of Orion 2 released in 1996 - as in "you probably weren't born yet".Ship design: Both games let you design your own ships.Space combat: In MoO2 the player has fewer ships but you control them directly. While in DW2 ship combat is fully automatic and most of the time you have no idea if your latest big guns actually contributed anything or not.Diplomacy: Pretty similar.Races: The races in DW2 are very similar with just small % changes here or there. MoO2 had races with fundamentally different mechanics.Planet management: Managing planets towards the end game in MoO2 is quite tedious as you have to build the same number of buildings over and over again. DW2 solves this by having almost no buildings.Pop management: Managing pops in MoO2 was fun, always trying to balance food, production and research. In DW2 pos are just a number on a spreadsheet.Automation: While there is of course none in MoO2, DW2 prizes itself with this feature. I ultimately find it annoying, because either the game plays itself, or the "ask me first" feature keeps pinging me with things I don't want like an influencer on social media.Overall after trying to play DW2 for a couple of hours I got bored and started Stellaris again (which has its own problems, but at least it is better at make believe).

detailed_description: You feel like every time you blink it moves a little bit closer. Several days have passed already. Just keep your eyes on the red fridge and everything will be ok. Right? SIX TALES FROM THE RED FRIDGE This is an anthology of six different first-person horror stories. Each one of the episodes explores a specific theme and gameplay idea. Staring contest with the fridge monster. Infinite maze of the hospital hallways and archive backrooms. Haunted road trip through the snowy highway… Experience many more liminal spaces, surreal encounters, and uncanny strangers in the full game. Could all that be connected somehow? Will you reveal the biggest secret the Red Fridge is keeping? ANALOGUE HORROR Spiral down the dreadful trip inspired by PSX-era retro horrors. Turn on the analogue post-process and FPS lock for a truly immersive experience. Do you have a memory card for the save slots?

_childDocuments_.review: This gamer/reviewer will attempt to explain what about The Fridge Is Red seems so compelling to many, and why TFIR is worth the time of many gamers (and that is no simple task considering the degree to which so many players have spoken out.) Perhaps the answer can be summarized simply: the horror in TFIR resonates so strongly (perhaps too strongly for many players) because the horror of TFIR is not the comfortable and escapable horror of zombies or attacking space aliens, but instead it’s the reality that people experience every day of their lives, which then becomes expressed in the most cyclical and inescapable nightmare scenarios our minds can concoct. Where does game-context IRL end and the nightmares begin (if nightmares are truly even what the game so vividly expresses)? That mostly indefinable, significantly nebulous point separating reality and nightmares seems perhaps best identified as… The Fridge Is Red.We all, including TFIR developers, know why nightmares are so terrifying. Whatever logic we possibly encounter there is contrived and specific, and we are trapped there with our only resources being any possibilities for escape that may lie within ourselves, and perhaps then only after we realize where reality ends and the nightmare begins. But does that point of separation actually even exist? TFIR seems to say that it may not, and to say so with frequent, potentially karmic, brutality. So, when the actions of living become horror in themselves due to their cyclical and inescapable natures (and they then translate into our worst fears, expressed as nightmares or similar) we have few tools to protect or extract ourselves. This all too frequently results in endless circles of wasted effort, confusion and frustration with the contrived “rules” encountered within our dreams. That is perhaps the best way to summarize TFIR: endless inescapable circles/cycles based on the very actions begun in our waking lives but magnified geometrically once nightmares are given free reign with the most hellish personal aspects of our lives. You live a private life of guilt, fear and loss? The Fridge Is Red says that the hell you live will only be magnified by how you process that pain and fear internally.As TFIR developer, cosmonaut wrote, “….we often have to deal with a soulless system in our lives, especially where we need ordinary human empathy the most. We tried to show that in our game.” And in at least one player’s opinion, SWORD Team succeeded unconditionally.The Fridge Is Red is made of six individual stories that seemingly originate in the waking world, and without connection with each other. It doesn’t take long for connections between the various scenarios to be apparent, as each one quickly migrates to a hellish state with little means of exercising control, understanding or solution. While all six scenarios are shown in time to be connected (if only seemingly peripherally), when the game is completed, the story told is a truly horrible one from the character’s IRL, as heartbreakingly permanent as any story imagining could create. The point of TFIR seemingly being, “nothing in your nightmares will ever begin to prepare you for the horror within the waking life you live.”Admittedly, The Fridge Is Red is not a horror game for everyone, even if it’s questionably either a “game” or “horror” (although it is most assuredly horrible.) Sometimes games feel too real to enjoy entirely as a game, and perhaps should be experienced more as a life lesson. TFIR seems to belong on that list. Perhaps the negative reviews say more about those choosing to play TFIR than the game itself, and it is unfortunate that a large number of players have failed to notice what may be (as developers have implied) the true point of TFIR. Yes, TFIG is painful and confusing to a maddening degree, but that’s because it’s meant to reflect the life we each live, and The Fridge Is Red succeeds both admirably and uncomfortably.While I’ve seen TFIR referred to as a “walking simulator”, I’m not sure that observation actually hits the mark. It’s a game involving substantial searching, puzzle solving, and with much trial and error as numerous out-of-the-box solutions toward escape are attempted, with failure resulting in restarting the episode or returning to an earlier point. I’m admittedly a purposefully slow gamer, and with almost 13 hours of “loving almost every minute” gaming in TFIR, I’ve managed to solve all but one episode, and have seen how all (completed thus far) episodes come together at the end for a final bout with brutal reality. I can imagine that many gamers want games they can exit and walk away from, and The Fridge Is Red is as much (with apologies to Lizzo) “not that game” as any game I can recall playing in my almost 40 years of PC gaming.As far as a well-developed game, The Fridge Is Red succeeds (to me) on all levels. The artwork of TFIR is exceptionally effective, and to be commended for walking a fine line with a task that is more demanding than in a more traditional horror game. The sound design is also very effective and using AI voices creates a state of encountering even less humanity when we often need it most (in the thoughtful words of TFIR developer, cosmonaut.) Attentive developers seem committed to their project, and equally committed to making it as good as possible technically, as small issues are steadily and quickly resolved.On a personal note, I’d like to thank the developers for including material that has a very personal impact on my life. (I would not be surprised if most TFIR players were able to make a similar observation, though perhaps not specifically this.) Not only in Seaside, as I noted in a discussion topic, but the connection of that episode with the last one, Chili Handled, reached out to me individually. Just as these issues are connected in TFIR, they are similarly connected in my life, and I was shown myself in a manner that I very much needed to see. Thank you one and all at SWORD Team for helping me survive life at least a bit more effectively.Thank you all for reading.(4K)EDIT: 10/113  It turns out SWORD Team has another game! I'll try to let readers of this review know what I think of it in the near future. (DLing as we "speak".)

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of horror, and The Fridge is Red barely counts as horror. Its scares are few and far between. It seems as if the dev was given a larger TinyBuild-sized budget and didn't possess the confidence to expand upon their idea in a meaningful way. The atmosphere and general ambiance are top tier, but are dragged down by the meandering gameplay. It's disappointing because there are so many good ideas in The Fridge is Red executed in the most pointless, limp way. It tells a bog-standard story with bog-standard gameplay. The first section is actually amazing and features an elevator ride through hell. After that, the game becomes a self-indulgent mess of "tortured father" tropes. I wanted to like it. I wanted to suggest it. I can't in good conscience do either. I hope the developer can take this experience and move on to a project with more oversight, because they've obviously got some bad habits that need to be reigned in.

_childDocuments_.review: don't take the negative reviews for this game too seriously if you're someone who enjoys indie walking sim horror with a strong emphasis on fever-dream passages and chilling lo-fi atmosphere. i encountered a very minimal amount of bugs, i believe they were all on one level and were easy to get past.what you're getting with this game is pretty similar to a dread x collection game, or something like the door in the basement, or puppet combo games. except all of the vignettes have an abstract, overarching narrative. a little bit of indie jank here and there helps solidify the creepy factor rather than working against it, i had some genuine moments of cold chills up my spine while exploring the environments and recalled a lot of bad dreams i've had in my life while playing. a simple, moody, feverish, surreal and haunting set of short stories, definitely worth a playthrough.recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Before I got around to playing the rest of the levels in the game a friend streamed it and stuck around for level 5 and beyond where I got and... it's more going in circles. Real buzzkill because some of the horror elements in this are super strong, the references are on point and I want it to be good, but running in circles is annoying not scary and any atmosphere they build gets spoiled by completely lackluster progress gates in each level. Really great concept, some great ideas, very poor execution. Really hoping they clean things up by the time they release their next game, its obvious these guys are talented.While I understand that reviewing things before finishing them completely is frowned upon I have to do it sometimes because I don’t want to force myself through any more of a game, this one is on that list. The best way to describe this game is tedious.Currently, I am a part of the 1.5% of players that have beaten the second level. Yup. The first level takes about 4 minutes. That means that the overwhelming majority of people that have picked this game up have not gotten past something that you start 4 minutes into the game, that explains a lot on its own, but I'll tell you why.Sometimes when it comes to horror games there is a puzzling element to how you are supposed to progress, in this game they said f*ck it and just have you walk in circles forever and ever. I wish I was kidding. I got all the way into the 4th mission until I lost my patience with it, but on the third mission there is a section that I legitimately spent 10 minutes in an archive section of a hospital walking around because there was no discernible hint to the "puzzle". I know I'm not crazy too because I had 20 or so people watching my stream who also were confused as to what I was supposed to do. When I "solved" the puzzle, I had no idea how I did it, and I still cannot figure out how even after watching the VOD or watching my friends play the same level blind. Its ridiculous.The biggest shame of this game is that the style and some of the actual horror elements are really strong. There is some genuinely strong world design and while the spooks arent going to have you jump up a wall, its entertaining which is nice, but I think that this is essentially a 4ish hour game that the developers sadly padded out with tons and tons of confusing progress gates. I don’t know if they just wanted it to get past the 2 hour mark so you can’t refund it or what but either way it results in a waste of time and it kills any atmosphere or spooks they had set up.I wish I was kidding but every single level I played had you walking in circles. The hospital level is literally about walking in circles and good lord do they stick to the theme there. I was so ready to love this, and while I have not finished the entire game yet, when 4 of 7 levels are the exact same, super lame gimmick? I have little hope for the rest. If/when I do eventually play the other levels I'll update this review, but barring a major update from the devs I would be very surprised if this one ever turns around. Damn shame, has a lot of potential.Thanks for reading, I review a lot of games indie and not, if you're curious my curator page is linked on my profile feel free to join and I left comments open if anyone has questions about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really cannot in good faith recommend this.The idea? It's great. A collection of short stories that together are sort of telling us a tale. The individual levels are each probably between 15 minutes and an hour, depending on how long they take you. But I never finished it.This filter. My god, this filter. You may as well play the game with a blindfold on and cover your screen in Vaseline for how easy it is to see anything. I cannot for the life of me understand, why does anyone think this is a good idea?There's a story around...4 chapters in. Where you have to go to a church, and do some stuff. Creepy atmosphere, a neat little encounter, if a bit silly. Then you go into the catacombs and can't see a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing. You're chased by a madman who kills you as soon as he finds you, with limited stamina and the vision of an 80 year old legally blind person with astigmatism.Then the next chapter. You're driving around and looking for parts to help fix your car. So you get to a barn, go inside, and suddenly are hunted. Except the barn is actually pitch black, and as best I can tell, there is no brightness setting at all, or any way to adjust it. You have no light, no way to improve gamma, and your screen is broken up into this horrific blocky nightmare. You'll see people in the reviews reference "the car section" a lot, and it was the point where I was just disgusted and didn't bother.I don't get what happened to this game. The initial idea about the Red Fridge was neat! It was creepy, it was scary, it was nerve wracking. Then the next level or two were...okay. A bit silly, a bit too artsy for my taste, but at least I finished them. But then it was all downhill. I regret purchasing this game. I regret whatever trend is making developers think "filters where you cant see ♥♥♥♥ are the next best thing". I regret the fact that so many people bought this and played *just* far enough to cross the refund threshold and then were too disgusted to bother anymore.Developers, for the love of god, let us boost brightness, and remove this horrific filter in your games. Otherwise, they're just not going to be played; this was one of the worst experiences I've had in a long time with a game, entirely due to the visual design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: The Fridge is Red is an average game. Sometimes fun and interesting and sometimes confusing and tedious.Video Review:Written Review:It’s nice that the game's chapters have different environments, objectives and stories, but many of them share the same kind of slow boring gameplay - getting lost in maze-like areas trying to find a way out. It wouldn’t be too bad if there were things happening which would keep you entertained, but unfortunately most of the time you will be running around in circles without experiencing anything interesting or exciting. All the other gameplay elements were enjoyable.The game isn’t very scary which is not necessarily a bad thing. I don’t really like to play horror games that much because I get too stressed by good jump scares. I scream and swear which is entertaining for my viewers but I don’t get any satisfaction from that kind of shock. So for me personally the fact that The Fridge is Red doesn’t have any good jump scares is a positive thing. All I wanted was a creepy walking simulator with solving puzzles and that’s what the game delivered.I didn’t mind the retro look of the game, but what I really didn’t like was the colors and their intensity in some of the chapters. I don’t have a problem with playing in very simplistic environments, but I still want to see the path I am walking on and the items I need to interact with in order to progress in the game. The Fridge is Red definitely influenced me emotionally in the end when I connected all the pieces of the 6 chapters and realized what a tragic story it was. The things happening to you and around you can be quite confusing, but it’s because we can perceive things differently when we are not alright mentally. Just remember how it was with Senua in Hellblade: Senua’s Sacrifice. Very different games but I would say that they have something in common.I ran into a game breaking bug in one of the chapters where I drove a car. I kept replaying one of the parts and dying over and over again. I even looked it up and did exactly what other players did and it worked for them. It didn’t change a thing. I still got killed. I loaded the game from the last checkpoint and then it got super confusing. The objectives would send me somewhere but it was already finished and I was struggling to find out where I was in the story. Luckily it all worked out then and I survived, but it made me dislike the driving which I originally enjoyed and appreciated before the problems started.Would I recommend the game? Once the game breaking bug is fixed and perhaps some attention is given to fixing the color explosions in some of the levels so players can actually see all paths, I am sure The Fridge is Red will be worth playing for some gamers who enjoy indie walking simulators with puzzles and almost no hand holding. I am definitely interested in more games from this developer in the future. They seem to have great ideas but hopefully they will learn to carry them out in a better way next time.

_childDocuments_.review: The first two stories are good, especially "For Daddy to Work". After that the game goes downhill. Unless I missed something on the store page stating otherwise, the maps sometimes seem to be randomly generated leading to infinite loops. The third story had me restart three times and push four hours trying to find ICU Ward 7, and the fifth story had me leave the cafe to drive into an invisible wall to get stuck, then restart the checkpoint and drive a good five minutes away from the cafe (no turns in the road, just a straight path laid out in front of me) only to come BACK to the cafe.And oh the many times I was glitched into immobility and had to start from scratch because loading from the last checkpoint breaks the game (as specified above). It also doesn't help you don't get a flashlight unless you find one in the map, and given the options lack an ability to increase or reduce brightness I wound up lost in some darker stories (like the fourth in the catacombs) as my Nitro 5 laptop at max brightness still has a heavy saturation on darker colors.I CANNOT recomend this game at $15 US. I got it on sale for $10 and wish I heeded my bad game spidey sense and refunded it. This has potential in the analog horror gaming sphere, but the glitches, bad controls, constantly getting physically stuck and restarting a story from scratch, and all the frustration that comes with all its faults make this one of the most infuriating (albeit still playable) first person horror games I've experienced on this platform.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential, but it is incredibly buggy.  One storyline did not spawn a flashlight (required, as the game is incredibly dark in places).  Another time I respawned from a checkpoint and it seemingly changed the map--there was a pipe in my way and I could not progress forward.  Another time I was attacked and it 'locked up'--I could look around but not move or click on anything, and i could not get to the menu as usual with ESC.  I had to ALT-F4 and lost progress, with no desire to restart that storyline.These and other bugs make the game unenjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a work of art, it tells the story of a family dad in a very depressive but also soothing way. There are many small details hidden throughout the chapters that give you more insight in what actually happened in his life. The gameplay consists out of a walking simulator and solving some simple riddles. There is little to no handholding and you need to explore and think for yourself, but stuff isnt hard to solve in the end. There are also a few bugs but most of them werent gamebreaking and done with rather fast.The Fridge is Red is probably one of the most immersive games out of my past few months and the story really hooked me and delivered emotions in a believable way. That feeling lasted even after closing the game when i finished it.The artstyle and sounds are very unique and create a thick atmosphere. It was totally worth my money. Really looking forward to your next project Cosmonaut!

_childDocuments_.review: So to start off I can recommend this on sale or if you love psychological horror games. _childDocuments_.review: Some years ago, from nowhere, a new kind of virus started spreading in the indie game-developing community, called low-resolution horror, or more simply, PSX-style horror. These aren’t games made in the PlayStation 1 era - while the actual origin of this genre is unknown, I think it all started around 2013 when a developer named Puppet Combo released “Babysitter Bloodbath”. The genre’s popularity has been growing steadily since then – but what is the specific reason for this? To tell you the truth, I don't know the answer to that myself – but for some inexplicable reason, these games have a particular atmosphere that is unique to them. The cohesion between graphics and gameplay is unparalleled, the sounds are entirely reminiscent of that time.“The Fridge Is Red” is a PSX-styled horror game, which tries to mimic what worked for other bigger titles, but sadly fails in the execution.The game (or anthology, whichever you like more) is constructed from six different tales, which seemingly are only connected because of their weird storyline – the locations range between a hungry red fridge, an infinite hospital, a haunted forest, and other sweet things. They are all essentially just walking simulators with occasional interactions here and there – but this is not meant in a pejorative sense since the stories are all enjoyable – but not the games themselves. Apart from walking, you will occasionally experience some chase scenes which are intense (even for an experienced horror player), but most of the time you will only follow the basic “go to point A to get item B to deliver to point C” scheme, even if you don’t recognize it at first glance. For the actual story, I don’t want to get into details since understanding it is part of the game; therefore, I don’t want to take away from you the enjoyment when everything finally clicks - but I can assure you, it is like an acid trip told almost entirely without words. If I had to choose a favorite, I would say it was the second episode, The Office, mainly because it was the longest and scariest for me. My first and biggest problem was the saving issue. The game automatically saves at numerous points during each chapter but this number is too low in my opinion for a game, where you can die and potentially lose progress. In the 5th chapter, there is one scene where you are required to get an item and escape from a certain place - of course, this is not an easy task and you can easily get spotted - if this happens then you are sent ~10 minutes back in that chapter, and you need to do everything again. There are also various texture, hitbox, and model issues, which were addressed in quite a few updates but not all of them got patched.  As I mentioned in my introduction if there is something that is flawless in this game, then it’s the graphics and the sounds. As this is a niché genre I hope people understand that the graphics are intentionally looking like this, and the main purpose of the visuals is to add another layer to the ambiance. Apart from the textures and 3D models, the animations are also wellmade - all of them combined totally give me the PSX vibe! The sound design is another key point here - the sound effects and the music altogether share the same characteristics - the small number of jumpscares here are all screamers.The Fridge Is Red could be a great example taught in design schools for horror developers, but the fact that it is unpolished takes away from the overall enjoyment. It is exciting, good-looking, and frequently scary but because of the little details it fails to deliver a pleasant experience

_childDocuments_.review: Six scenes combine to form a single narrative, all of which center on everyday, stressful events. However, our minds frequently deceive us and distort the truth to make things seem worse than they truly are.Stories are displayed as foods that are kept in a large red refrigerator. Most must be unlocked by gathering the proper item within the previous stage because only two stories are available at the start. These are located within the first few rooms, saving you the trouble of searching for them or replaying the entire stage if you miss them.The gameplay involves running around, gathering items and using them where they belong, and experiencing strange events. Death is a possibility but it won't be frustrating because you can instantly revive nearby. This typically happens in the thankfully rare chase scenes, like the one in the sewers, which sounds and actually is incredibly generic.While items have a white outline one you point at them, you still need to carefully search the surroundings because they could be everywhere. You don't have to worry about inventory, which is nice. The game will use an item for you if you have it and click on the appropriate spot. The boring part is that you’re mostly looking for keys to open a door forward. Puzzles are not worth mentioning; there are only a couple of places where you need to search for the right number. The graphics and audio are from the 1990s, a decade characterized by software rendering and blocky graphics. It's nothing new because modern horror games frequently use this. Despite the lack of details and occasionally difficult-to-distinguish items, this style can evoke a spooky mood. Voice is fine, but I don’t like the choice. Now, everyone uses a voice that sounds like it was made using a generator with the robot setting activated. By default, subtitles are on because it would be difficult to understand anything without them.Overall, the game is a forgettable thriller with almost no jump scares or overly disturbing images. The game’s not that long, either. If you want to see everything, you can explore the stage for a hidden fridge with a TV inside that shows you some backstory.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Horror Games? Then this isn't for you, as someone who is weak to horror and gets scared quite easy, this games only really gave two to three moments where I actually jumped but nothing more than that. The overall story of this game isn't bad but the gameplay is, which is just as important to a game like this.Notes: This review is for 1.1.4First is that the game needs a way of deleting saved data, I would of liked to have been able to unlock all the levels once again and start a new. Second is that when I start a level again and click 'New Game' if I am to click on 'Load Save' it will send me further into the level, usually towards the end (may be a bug).The Levels:Fidgeted Sherri: Honestly a fun and interesting level, it's a shame it's the shortest one the game has to offer though. Nice mechanics to it as well as RNG spawn locations for the letters which was nice.For Daddy to work: A fun and well build level, it keeps the atmosphere creepy all the way through the level, probably the best one in the game. The only downside to this level is that you can get soft locked. I originally got stuck at one point (due to not understanding what to do so that's on me), I clicked 'Load Save' and it sent me back to the elevator, however the room you exit to is different in design than the one you enter when playing normally (I can only assume that this was a scrapped room design that was still left in the game). Because of this there is an object that blocks you from continuing the level.Seaside: It's a pretty boring level where you just roam around a hospital, I failed to understand this level on my first play through, not understanding where to find the child. The phrase "Somewhere in the hospital" wasn't very helpful.. You're suppose to follow the signs to the 'Maternity Ward' which is fine, but I would of preferred if the character we spoke to say "In the Maternity Ward" instead of "Somewhere" as it implies a better understanding to the player of where to look. Keep in mind the 'Maternity Ward' doesn't appear on the signs until you speak with him so you wouldn't know it existed until now.Charleen Mufi: It's not actually that bad, a bit short but I had fun playing this level; it's just that the second half didn't feel as fun or creepy to me. I do appreciate that you keep the keys you collect after death though, it was nice to see that I didn't need to redo my progress. However I should say that it might be better for you to spawn the chaser at a random position in the level as to having to wait for them to get aggressive again as it gives quite a bit of time to explore safely.Goldi Vern: The most boring level by far where you don't even see the Threat until the end, where it only appears for about one minute which is disappointing since I had to spend around twenty to twenty five minutes driving back and forth, back and forth, back and forth from that Gas Station. This one really needs to be done differently, maybe have the Threat appear more often, or change up the level a bit.Chili Handled: I liked this one quite a bit however the twist was too easy to see coming, it's also not very fun having to make my way back to the chair to play Hide and Seek again and again, this is just something that should automatically happen after talking to your daughter, where it would then teleport you back to the chair when faded to black. I do like the added RNG locations for the daughter to hide though, as well as them being well placed. I do think this level could of added a bit more physiological horror to it though, I feel as if that could of been a nice bonus to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, check it, I'm staring at this red fridge, feeling kinda lost,In a world full of chaos, trying to count the cost,Got dreams to chase, but here I am, wasting time,Sitting at the computer, where every second's a dime.The fridge hums a rhythm, like a beat in my head,But instead of chasing goals, I'm lounging here instead.Got deadlines looming, but I'm stuck in this trance,Feeling like time's slipping, lost in this dance.Red fridge, ticking clock, wasting moments away,Got plans to conquer, but I'm stuck in today.Gotta break free from this cycle, find my prime,No more wasting time with this red fridge of mine.In the glow of its light, I reminisce and I ponder,On the paths I've yet to tread, the dreams I let wander.But excuses pile high like leftovers in a bin,As I drown in procrastination, letting chances thin.Should be writing verses, making moves in the game,But I'm stuck in this rut, feeling oh so lame.Red fridge, you're a symbol of my distraction,But it's time to break free, no more dissatisfaction.Red fridge, ticking clock, wasting moments away,Got plans to conquer, but I'm stuck in bad gameplay.Gotta break free from this cycle, find my prime,No more wasting time with this red fridge of mine.No more excuses, no more delay,Gotta seize the day, in every single way.The red fridge may call, but I won't heed its plea,Time to hustle hard, and watch some Tv. So here's to the future, to dreams yet untold,To breaking free from a bad games weird hold.No more wasting moments, no more being blind,we will conquer the world, leaving that red fridge behind.2/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is awful, not a Dread X rival like I hoped it would be.I liked the looks, it plays well, and has atmosphere going for it. Theres a bunch of times where items have no gravity and can be pushed around. Physics are funny. But the map designs suck.Over half of the episodes have you run around in huge labyrinth like places, looking for something specific, and you find items with no hint on what do to. You have objectives in the upper left corner, and sometimes they just disappear.In the elevator level theres a point where you get a crowbar and have to smash vending machines, but it never mentioned anything about that, it only showed that you can interact with the buttons of said machines. The next episode starts up interesting but then devolves into you searching a child in a huge ass hospital, with chasers that dont even chase or attack you? Next episode starts out very cool, with a casket trying to smash you, which can be blocked with holy chalk, very creative, and after that its key hunting in a catacomb system.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where I wish there was a sideways thumb option for reviews. I genuinely loved and hated different aspects of this game. _childDocuments_.review: It's just not good. It feels very poorly crafted. The scariest thing about this game is the fact that they're charging 15 bucks for it and feel proud of that pricing. The facts are: Only 62% of the people beat the first level. 61% beat the second. And then you get to the 3rd level where only 35% of people actually stuck around to finish it. The first two levels are fairly straight forward if a little buggy. The third level is a nightmare consisting of hallways that are constantly changing where you have to go from floor to floor seeking a specific room (but sometimes within the space of one room, you'll end up back where you started).I stopped playing after 30 minutes of running around because it's just not worth the headache that it will inevitably cause, because it feels as if the room I was already in that I'm supposed to go back to just doesn't exist.Important tools also have a bad habit of suddenly disappearing/not working.  Levels also don't load in properly forcing you to restart from a checkpoint (which is a plus, because if there were no checkpoints, I feel like more people just *wouldn't* have beat this game), which will also strip you of your equipment. Guess what? Both of these issues appear from the first level. I picked up a flashlight, which I couldn't use, then I opened the elevator doors to just an empty space. If I stepped into it, I fell into the void and got reset to inside the elevator, but when I reset the game, the area loaded in properly, but without the flashlight, which I couldn't use anyway. I don't understand how devs can feel good about just leaving their game in such a state where the most basic components don't even work. You'll have a better time watching someone play it on Youtube who can try to make light of how horrible of an experience this is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is at least for me, an incredibly original concept. It's very dedicated to its themes which I can respect. It takes the spin of "its better then you remember". However this game requires some polish saying the least. I encountered various bugs from graphical glitches to softlocks and even a couple hardlocks. Each level I had to restart at least twice. Additionally the objectives are rather vague which sounds fun right? Well... theres 'vague' and then theres 'vAgUe'. I'm sure the bugs are something that will sort themselves out in time but if you are an avid fan of analog horror.... and fridges then go for it lads and laddettes.

_childDocuments_.review: Wishing there was a neutral option for games like this.The narrative is good, the aesthetic and visuals are outstanding, it's genuinely scary, and some of the segments are very touching.However certain levels are a major slog to play. For example in one level you're carrying something and have to get through what's essentially a maze to pick it up. On your way back you see a shadow figure, which have never once in the game hurt you before, and if it gets even remotely close to you it takes the item and you have to completely backtrack all over again. This is never explained and there is no warning. The backtracking is what makes it a slog.Additionally, some of the game feels like padding just to make the game longer. I also ran into a few bugs that made me have to repeat segments which was frustrating.Despite the negatives though it really is an interesting and gripping experience... If you have the patience for it.I made a video that talks about the narrative themes toward the end of this game (toward the end of the video). It does include spoilers about the game so be wary!

_childDocuments_.review: Analog horror, check. Liminal spaces, check. PSX aesthetic, check. These are three elements of horror that are pretty popular now when it comes to indie horror games, and this game succeeds at all three. I've only completed about at hour of the game, but so far I'm really liking what I see.My Playthrough:

_childDocuments_.review: Another great concept just becomes a tedious boring, explore and stumble upon things game.I will break down the chapters  I played 1 by 1 below:CHAPTER 1The first act, with the fridge slowly coming towards you I could not complete.I found the first 5 magnets, however no matter how many times I tried I could not find the last.So I died over and over. The creepy concept soon loses its scare and appeal when it just becomes spooky sounds and the same creepy generic horror sounds, You are in a fixed position and can't move for some reason.I think a better idea would be the Fridge slowly follows you and gets quicker as you try and find the magnets, at least that is what I think you are supposed to do. I got bored and gave up after the 10 death.Also I must point out that the death scream of the player is laughably bad and it sounds like he is having fun time not death time. Please re-record the death scream it is laughable.CHAPTER 2For starters the text to speech really does nothing for the spooky atmosphere, I will happily do the voice acting for the male characters for free and I am sure there are female upcoming voice actors that would do the female lines for free too.It would add so much more to the world than just listening to terrible voice to speech words.Now you start off in a room, and lights turn off. You walk for ages to a elevator. A pretty cool event happens, then after that you are stuck in the lift. Now I could not figure out what I was supposed to do after the eyeballs starting showing up. After I put all the buttons back into the elevator. Nothing happened. I spent 15 mins just clicking everywhere. I am not sure what was supposed to happen but this was one of the most boring chapters. Needs more scares, more things to happen on the way to the elevator. The spooky ring like lady is cool but she needs to be around from the start.Example when you turn the light back on, you should force the player to turn around to see the lady standing behind the desk, or outside the window. Also force the player out of the room and slam the door, making the player feel like he needs to run to the elevator instead of just going home.CHAPTER 3The spooky hospital with gravity issues. Cool idea. Boring as hell. I wondered around for ages, finding pools of blood.  To find 1/4 journals that I could not find or see no matter what I did. I am not sure what spooky stuff was supposed to happen but all i did was walking into floating things for 15 mins and got bored. There needs to be some sort of guide or hint system to help players find things. I am never a fan of look for ages and happen to stumble across something. Click-ables are not obvious and I found this map to be the most frustraiting and not scary at all. Very disapointing.CHAPTER 4This is the last chapter I played. Er? walk up to a chruch, dude with red eyes talks to you. (again voice acting with a voicemod would be 100% better here) I did it with my voice mod. Sets the tone better than text to speech stuff.You go into the church. Your apparent wife is dead in the casket. The casket glows red and starts to attack you (laughably so) you run to the booth only for the casket to constantly attack you while you talk to the npc and find chalk. Once you have that you can defend yourself. I just found this hilariously bad. It was not scary at all the glowing floating casket was just dumb. It got stuck and bounced into everything. There was no tension here no scares. I am not sure what this game is trying to do or what even the story is. 6 Separate stories are good if they have a start, a middle and a end.These stories make no sense. They have poorly scripted horror events that are predictable and just plain stupid.I found this game to be very generic in its horror approach and I honestly thought this was going to be so much more enjoyable. I have great respect for the dev team and Tiny build and anyone else that has worked on this project.However please add voice acting to the speaking elements to the game. Add unique and different horror sounds and events that can catch the player off guard. There is huge potential here for some scares and creepy game play. However it needs time to breathe in the scenes and tension and build up must come before any of the events happen. Horror is not just about spooky stuff and jump scares. There needs to be elements to let the scene settle, let unsavoury and unsettling things happen to generate the fear in the player.This just throws stuff at you and hopes to get a re-action.I hope this feedback proves valuable.I am willing to voice act for free in this game to replace the text to speech stuff too.I will keep an eye on development of this game and will play this again in the future.However right now I would suggest you wait for the finished game before purchase.Thanks again for the key.Much Respect.

_childDocuments_.review: The Fridge Is Red is a survival horror adventure broken up into 6 different episodes. You play as Frank a repair man who fixes household appliances. You will guide Frank through 6 different spooky situations including liminal space hospitals and archive rooms, corrupted churches and cemeteries, evil elevators, snow-falling remote highways, and more.Can you escape the evil fridge?Full Review - The Fridge Is Red offers a unique take on survival horror games. With different episodes to work through, there are plenty of puzzles that will confuse and frustrate you, scary and gross visuals, and a soundtrack that will creep you right out.Some may be frustrated by the retro graphic feel, but it definitely makes you feel like you are playing an old-school Playstation horror game.The Fridge Is Red is a surreal trip into madness and nightmares that you will enjoy exploring.

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed this game this other day after getting it as a gift and man...I think the #1 thing I can say about it is...disappointing.The first two games of this were interesting and creepy, and lived up to the horror vibes the game gave off in all the marketing and trailers. However, they were the only well-done sections of the game (and even then, not by much).The rest of the games are vague, don't give much direction, and even when they do, you're still left trying to figure out where to go or what to do.Even in the second game, it doesn't give your a flashlight until about halfway through, and it is DARK. I only found it by mistake, because I didn't even head to the room I was supposed to go towards because I got a key item (apparently there's more than one) far earlier than that sequence. So I never went to the locker room. And even then? YOU HAVE TO FIND IT IN A LOCKER.The third game was a maze that literally had the path on the wall, but I didn't realize that until a LONG time after I had started, and even then, only by watching a previous playthrough on YouTube. It was still a slog to run through the halls, though.And the fourth game? More darkness, only this time no flashlight. Just reddish and blueish walls once you get to the maze section. I literally had to watch a video to figure out the path, as I ran around for 30 minutes getting fed up.Finally, the 5th game (the 6th is short and straightforward, except for the TV watching and drinking bit. Took me a bit to figure out that I had to turn on the TV in order to get drunk) is what killed any love I may have had for this game. Terrible driving mechanics, and then a section that I got stuck in because I thought it was a bug! IT WASN'T. More than one review here has said it was put in to make this game last longer than 2 hours and I'm inclined to agree. It was terrible.All in all? This game was something I was expecting more from. It was less horror and more a depressing introspective on grief and loss...which is fine, if done correctly. I feel this game did NOT do it correctly. Plus, after each game you got a cutscene of 'what really happened' to maybe explain the previous surrealism? I dunno. I felt it was less interpretive at that point and more just being slapped across the face with the story.Unless it's on sale, I'd pass. Otherwise, go in knowing it's not a great game, and certainly could have been done better.

_childDocuments_.review: PLEASE NOTE, even though I have left comments on, I am not interested in you telling me that I should put 4000 hours into a game I don't enjoy so I can "git gud", and then I would like it. That is a stupid argument. Don't be stupid. Skill is not indicative of enjoyment, and I have better things to do than bash my head on what I personally feel are bad / mediocre games on the off chance I could maybe like them one day. I have a life and don't play games in order to develop Stockholm syndrome.I played in 4k on a 4080 & Intel 13700KF processor with all current drivers and patches manually installed on Windows 11 x64. All options were set to their highest level.I played with an XBox One X controller and a keyboard and mouse. The keyboard and mouse was preferred because there is no way to run with or remap the buttons for the controller.I will update this review if I continue to play and have more to add and will leave comments on.PROS:- Achievements.- Out of 1.5 hours, about .25 were some decent entertainment that I found enjoyable enough to keep going in hopes it came together.- Music and audio design is solid throughout with the exception of...CONS:- When the audio would stick and just keep looping over and over forcing you to quit the game to stop the noise. This happened multiple times.- The aesthetic is just horrendously ugly. I recognise that it's a stylistic choice, but it's actively worse than all but the ugliest of PS1 games. Even the menus are hard to read for no real reason.- It's been over a year since they said they'd add the option to invert the Y axis and the option still isn't in the game.- If you are using a controller, you can not run.- The levels would randomly generate in such a way that you could be stuck for no reason trying to figure out what to do. For example, on multiple occasions the level generated a pipe on the critical game path and I could not move forward without reloading from checkpoint. It's such a short game and they couldn't even be arsed to just manually build some boring hallways instead of generating them. It's inexcusably lazy.- Simply pausing the game breaks audio, kills subtitles (which makes things VERY hard since the voices are indecipherable and do not say what the subtitles do), and sometimes doesn't unpause correctly.- Events did not trigger until I restarted from checkpoint and I didn't know that they didn't until I started the game up a second day. The game is actively broken.- Nothing was even mildly frightening or even unsettling during my time with it. The game seems to operate on the idea that something being odd is unnerving.DID YOU FINISH THE GAME?:No. I was never sure if I wasn't making any progress due to the game being astoundingly obtuse or because it had randomly generated something I could not complete. It became frustrating and I quit.CONCLUSION:This is a horrible "so bad it should be free and even then I'd argue not to waste your time" excuse for a game. If you must know about it, I beg you to watch a YouTube video runthrough instead. This was awful.

_childDocuments_.review: I streamed this through for my audience and I wanted to play it because I like weird, esoteric horror experiences and though this had mixed reviews, I find small indie projects like this are often most interesting when they aren't universally loved or hated. Unfortunately, I am firmly in the camp that this game is a slog that is not worth your money.This is a series of horror vignettes that take place in different settings with different mechanics, but all end up tying into a singular narrative that's comes together as you go through it. I won't spoil anything, but it's obvious not that far in where things are going and it's a narrative that is dark and disturbing, but not really original. It's cool that each of the episodes play different, but the problem is, none of them play . The longer episodes are full of boring mazes with weak stealth mechanics that will just end up frustrating you and the second last episode is a driving sequence that's so long, so boring and so full of backtracking, I agree with another reviewer who said that it was likely designed that way to pad out the length past the refund window. All of the dialogue is read through a text-to-speech voice that often doesn't match with the subtitles. It kind of works with the creepy aesthetic, but is also somewhat low effort.Oh yeah, there's also the bugs. After release, they added checkpoints because many of the levels have failure states and people didn't like starting over all the time. Except, even after multiple patches, the levels still have many bugs in them that can soft lock progression and these are written into the saves so you'll end up stuck, reload from a checkpoint and still end up stuck, so you have to restart anyway. Multiple times, I spent tens of minutes trying to solve what I thought was an obtuse puzzle, only to find out I had it right all along, the game scripting just broke, so I couldn't move on.Even with all these headaches, it only took me 3 and a half hours to finish the whole thing, which has no replay value, no secrets (aside from one achievement that is a grind) and no alternate endings. The price is a lot to ask for all that.I don't like crapping on games as a rule, but this one left my audience and I frustrated and while I think there is a good base of ideas here, the execution just doesn't hold up. There are many better (and often) cheaper short horror experiences like this on Steam and I think those are much more worth your time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: The Fridge is Red left me thoroughly unimpressed and, frankly, annoyed. While the game bills itself as a horror experience, I found it to be more of an exercise in frustration than anything else.First and foremost, let's address the supposed horror element. Despite the game's attempts to create a tense and unsettling atmosphere, I failed to find anything remotely scary about it. The jumpscares felt forced and predictable, and the overall tone came across as more laughable than frightening. If you're expecting genuine chills and thrills, you'll be sorely disappointed.Beyond its lackluster attempts at horror, The Fridge is Red is plagued by a myriad of annoyances that only serve to detract from the experience. From clunky controls to nonsensical puzzles, every aspect of the gameplay felt like a chore. Rather than immersing me in its world, the game's mechanics only served to pull me out of the experience time and time again.Furthermore, The Fridge is Red suffers from a severe lack of originality. The premise feels stale and derivative, borrowing heavily from clichés and tropes that have been done to death in the horror genre. There's nothing here that sets it apart from the countless other horror games vying for your attention on Steam.In conclusion, The Fridge is Red is a forgettable and ultimately frustrating experience that fails to deliver on its promises. If you're looking for a genuinely scary horror game, look elsewhere. This game is more likely to leave you rolling your eyes than jumping out of your seat. Save your money and invest it in a title that actually knows how to deliver a spine-tingling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This type of game usually isn't my cup of tea, but since I got it in a Fanatical special, I decided to check it out.-Moderate Spoilers Ahead-Initial impressions were confused, since I had a preconceived notion that this game was about a red fridge. I wasn't exactly wrong, but finding out it was an anthology rather than a single game was unexpected.Level 1/6 is the poster-child for the game, the titular red fridge. Survive the red fridge while solving a puzzle. Quick, simple, punchy and tense, leaves a strong first impression. 9/10Level 2/6 is where those notions I mentioned fall apart. Its a 20-ish minute linear experience with jumpscares and a sprinkle of plot. It's also where the pixel filter causes some problems, particularly in dark areas where you have to find small objects that aren't marked or highlighted. Regardless, the visuals were impressive, the puzzles were... fine and the story finally began. Solid, but flawed. 7/10Level 3/6 is where the magic finally left. Taking place in an infinite hospital, you're given esoteric instructions and directions to arrive at your various destinations. This level presents the games biggest issue, lack of clear instructions. As a spoiler-free example, you're asked to find someone inside the hospital. "Hardly an issue" I thought, before spending the next half-hour looping through the same corridors until I realized the solution. Just in case anyone needs it like I do, the directions on the wall of each room are renamed depending on the objective. Anyway, an interesting concept ruined by monotony. 6/10Level 4/6 takes place in a snowy church, and finally proved to me that this game needed more time. Despite a fairly strong opening, upon entering the next area, it devolves into your bog-standard pursuer encounter, avoiding danger while searching for a key. A key I needed a guide to find since these cramped corridors have shoddy hit-detection and the narrow field of view made me nauseous. Regardless, it ended soon after and I was glad it did. 5/10Level 5/6 is one of the worst experiences I've ever had in a horror game. you may have heard of this one if you've read other reviews, "the car level." Easily the most potential out of any of the levels aside from the first, but was ruined by bugs, long sections of driving in the dark and poorly placed checkpoints. Nothing about it was scary. 2/10And finally, 6/6. The penultimate level, the final story revelation, the last piece of the puzzle, THE ENDING! Unfortunately, it doesn't live up to the first level's qaulity. While it never falls to the pits of level 5, it never soars above 'okay'. The ending was fine, the gameplay was boring (though thankfully short), and the story was fairly good. 7/10My thoughts wavered from level to level, starting at "this could rival DreadX" and ending with "please stop". I can't in good conscience recommend this game, though I wish that wasn't the case. It's full of interesting ideas and creative visuals, but the gameplay is consistently stale and monotonous after the first level. Spend your money elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my 30 hours in Blacktail with one glaring exception, which is what prompted me to write this.Overall, this was a wonderfully surreal narrative adventure. It conjured up fond memories of my youth, playing games like Kings Quest IV, seeing new spins and clever twists on classic fairy tales. Story is first and foremost. For a non-triple A title, this game was mechanically brilliant, with writing and most of the voice acting (about 95%) absolutely fantastic.  A few examples of what this game did well include:- A codex whose quests re-write or add to themselves the more you progress- Character entries get added to and further explained the further you get- You unlock skills using collected materials, but most skills aren't described or able to be unlocked until you first find a corresponding scroll in the game world (ensuring you don't grind to max level in the first few hours, and always have something new to see)- Side quests are based on exploring, and you need not worry about accidentally stumbling upon an area too soon, breaking a quest (things work as intended)- The challenge is well balanced even after you've acquired most abilities- You can backtrack to earlier map areas when you want to complete side quests, find items you missed, etc- Music and most of the voice acting was great, particularly Jack and Borvy, the Voice (same person that did Megaera in Hades), and YagaThis is a narrative action/adventure game, with story and exploration at the forefront. What is there is enough, and the side quests are sometimes even more interesting than the main quest.I could explain the game, but so much of my enjoyment came from going in and making sense of the mechanics, the world, and the characters all on my own that I do not wish to ruin that for others. All Steam Achievements can be completed on a single save profile. However, it can take you hours upon hours before you unlock a single one.  I thoroughly enjoyed everything I did in Blacktail. I loved it. I was so excited to see how it ended and declare this one of the only "perfect" games I've ever played (and I've played 950+ commercially sold PC games from start to finish... I keep track). But the ending... was terrible. I'm not going to spoil it, but suffice it to say, it went against the format of every other quest you did. After all game events, the codex updates, giving a recap, detail, clarity, on events, people, and backgrounds for everything that transpired. Often, the game does a unique spin on a classic fairy tale, and you can read about that too (particularly side stories from world collectibles). The game's ending though brushes aside key plot points, driving motivations behind why you just sunk 30 hours into this charming, colourful, and memorable world. Considering that everything else was fully envisioned and ultimately explained, that the ending cinematic is left vague and confusing, not to mention brushing aside, like I said, a key plot point prior to the final battle, left me massively saddened and upset. There is so much good. So many things done brilliantly. Alas, I felt they worked more to justify not having more than one ending (which they didn't need anyway, one good ending would have sufficed), than giving me what I was seeking all the way along. That being, their vision, their unique take on the Baba Yaga lore, their unique take on the characters and the world that they presented, just as they gave for everything else. I don't think "artistic intent" can be used as an excuse, when nothing else in the world was left vague or lacking.Long story short, Blacktail was a whisker away from being perfect. I'm very saddened that all those pleasant hours are now tainted, much like the roots, by my last memory of the game, that being bewilderment and disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a phenomenal and unique experience, like nothing I'd never played before. It's a great game... with a few glaring flaws that are impossible to ignore. Foremost among them: it has a complete clash of tones that can easily break immersion. The Steam page paints it as a dark survival/suspense game where we have to hunt down the spirits of our past, paired with the fantastical origin story of the Slavic folktale. Yaga is a young girl exiled from her village, who wears a mask because people believe the evil Baba can see through her birthmark, and was even almost burned to death by the villagers. It's intense, gruesome and realistic stuff about superstition and paranoia... And yet the actual world we get to explore is a cutesy children's fairytale world divided into seasons, populated by Alice in Wonderland-type characters like talking mushrooms, gnolls and imps, and the skybox has clouds, stars and a sun drawn like a child's drawing you put on the fridge. Despite this already weird mix of tones, the characters are swearing and using modern slang--the Voice is cussing like an angtsy teenager, the mushroom kid unironically called himself a 'douchebag' and the fish actually used 'hella' in a sentence. It's like taking puzzle pieces out of multiple different boxes and trying to fit them together. They  try to explain why it feels like two different world towards the end [mild spoiler?] with the quote about the Roots changing everything "like it's from an entirely different story". It didn't really make much sense, and considering the modern lingo on top of everything, I feel it would've been better to either stick to one world or merge two together in a more seamless way. It was alienating at first, and judging from the reviews, I wasn't the only one who thought so.Then there's the voice acting. While Yaga had a sweet voice that was fitting to her character, and her performance was good, her accent was constantly slipping. Most accents did not fit--the kids (of a medieval Slavic village, let's remember that) had variations of British accents and Volko inexplicably had an Irish one. The Voice was American, which clashes with the big reveal at the end of who she was the whole time. The Black Cat is one of the few characters whose accent actually fits the setting, and as a result his narrations were tonally perfect, even if his performance could've been better (his voice was oddly soothing though lol, I adored it). They had a few other characters like Mr. Larva and the Ant Queen who also fit well. They should have cast other Polish/Slavic-background VAs like them.Otherwise, the game was top tier quality, far exceeding what you'd expect of indie devs. The combination of magic/archery combat was great, the skill tree and how to unlock it was inventive and unique, the side quests had charming stories, the world they built was relatively coherent (in everything but tone), good collectibles and very creative ways of getting them. The soundtrack was PHENOMENAL. The environments are all well-made and beautiful with nice little platforming puzzles. Graphics and rendering were excellent. Honestly it was just really nice to look at, so much so that I spent most of the game wandered around exploring instead of doing the actual quests. I loved the missions where you had to rearrange time and space to piece the memory of what happened to the kids back together, although I wish they did like the store page implies and made the spirits creepier and more vengeful instead of just following them and fighting a tree. I liked being able to choose whether you're good or evil and having that affect the world (and the title where you find out what you thought was good was actually evil). I really loved the cute pinecone shellocks and hearing them whisper about what you've been doing.It's an absolutely terrific game, if you're able to look past the feeling of it being three different games sewn together... and an ending that made absolutely no sense. TL;DR: Great game, fun gameplay and nice environments, but weird clash of tones that ruin immersion, unfitting/weak accents for the setting, and a bad/confusing ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a partial review after 10 hours in the game and I've yet to finish it. It is an ongoing adventure and a very heartfelt, intriguing and beautifully illustrated one. Props to THE PARASIGHT devs and their labour of love. The graphics, the voice overs () and beautiful music come together to make this game an amazing experience so far.I am not going to get into what the story is about beyond how the devs described it for one main reason,  you should experience this game for yourself. The world and narrative is supernatural and mysterious and I went into it day one with only the game page to guide me. I fully believe if your into games with a magical setting, combat (yes you do have combat in this game and you will die, it is not always easy and the bosses can be a challenge) and a narrative with dark undertones then this is for you.  And the game IS dark, not some feel good fantasy. There is some enlightened moments but the world itself is creepy, twisted, and uneasy.  However you can decide if you will follow the path of light or dark ultimately and the choices are not clear cut. I had no crashes, the main game-play supports ultra wide screens and you can rebind your keyboard and mouse. I recommend a programmable mouse if you have one. For the price I recommend it. I am not sure the full amount of hours in total but so far with 10 hours in I've gotten my money's worth both in playtime & entertainment value.  If you decide to play this game for yourself I wish you a great experience. 🖤

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: A really good hidden gem. It's definitely worth recommending.Longer version: It's a first-person shooter (bow with special abilities/arrows), open world (with areas opening after each one is completed), with a little bit of Metroidvania (you get abilities with which you can backtrack to previous areas to do additional stuff/missions/locations).The theme is Slavic folktale/mythology which is really unique in nowadays gamescape.I found the combat interesting all the way to the end of the game. As you progress through the game the player unlocks new abilities and modifications of already existing ones, which makes the combant fresh and interesting all the way to the end of the game.There are also some interesting collectibles that have some story tied to them so it's not only collecting useless items/timer-fillers like in some other games.The VO is good and the story is also very interesting (will not write anymore to avoid spoilers).One of the unique aspects of the game is the morality system in which some actions are considered bad and some are considered good and which one you take does affect the narrative. This also gives the game some replayability, but the game also gives you chances to switch the morality and with it, you can get all the achievements during one playthrough without the worry of needing to go through the game a second time which was a pleasant surprise, tbh. Focusing only on the main story would take around 7-10 hours, but as this is an open-world game, exploring this intriguing and interesting world is definitely a must, and, personally, it took me 24 hours to get all achievements and pretty much complete the game 100%.The price is also adequate to the nowadays market.The only issue I encountered was with the upscaling graphics option. I have an AMD graphics card and with upscaling FSR 2 turned on, the game looked a little bit blurry and after turning it off the game experience was definitely better.That's all from me folks, have a nice day!
