_childDocuments_.review: I had essentially zero expectations going into BLACKTAIL. A newly formed developer, creating a game based on folklore I am not particularly familiar with, to release at the tail-end of a year with very little in the way of marketing behind it. Thankfully, this game ended up surprising me in almost every facet, and while not all of its ideas work together perfectly, it is nevertheless one of the most unique games I’ve ever had the pleasure of experiencing.Playing as a young and naïve version of the Baba Yaga character, you’re thrusted into a mysterious fairy-tale-inspired land to uncover lost and repressed memories of your friends and family, and decide how you wish to leave your mark on this unusual world. While I think the narrative is too puzzling for its own good at times, the voice acting is hit-or-miss, and the ending did not feel wholly satisfactory, it was nevertheless a well-told story. It is primarily moved along by the compelling dynamic between Yaga and a disembodied voice, whose intentions for the girl initially seem wicked, but become more complex as the narrative progresses. The standout moments come in the form of beautifully hand-drawn cutscenes that recite Yaga’s memories and segway into short 2D-platforming segments to explore an aspect of her psyche reacting to the memory. They were simple to play, yet phenomenal to observe as you move through them, offering multi-planed environments with an incredible amount of detail which is unlikely to be fully captured on your first experience. The game’s beauty continues when moving into its open world. BLACKTAIL’s art direction is absolutely gorgeous, with numerous examples of pretty yet unsettling areas spread across the map, supported by an equally eerie original soundtrack. A couple of segments even had my jaw on the floor in awe of what the artists produced for this title. The world is also surprisingly large; each of its four zones introduces you to the area with incredible landscape shots which make you wonder how big its world truly is. And it’s not just for show either; large open spaces containing various threats are interspersed along the main and side quest pathways, and require you to manoeuvre through them with great care to avoid a swift death. Furthermore, substantial sections of the map are solely utilized for specific side quests, each of which stands out in terms of completion requirements. One asks you to recover some lost mushrooms from a previously unexplored area of the map, there are various unmarked tasks which you’ll find by interacting with the world’s voiced animal inhabitants, and there’s even a tower-defence-style mission which works surprisingly well for this game’s combat system; all of the side content is killer, and worth putting the story on hold for. Speaking of the combat, its bow-centric nature had more variety than I was anticipating. You’ll start with a standard bow and arrow set, and eventually come across the more powerful honey and crystal arrows which offer an area of effect burst and higher-damaging shots respectively. Encounters are most easily won by using all three, especially when dealing with the later enemy variants which are most effectively dispatched with a particular arrow. You also have access to ‘Hocus’ abilities, which can be fired without holstering your bow, and can offer knockback, an area-of-effect attack, or a slow-down or leech effect depending on your position in the game’s morality system. Indeed, various small and quest-centric actions in the world contribute towards this, and while their impact on the narrative was not evident with a single playthrough, their gameplay effects were noticeable, and really makes you consider your choices carefully if you want to attain your ideal setup. You can also dash to avoid attacks, place down a broom to lure enemies away, and drink a potion to temporarily increase your speed and make stealth an easier feat to achieve. While combat has a bit of a learning curve to it due to how greatly it deviates from other archery-focused titles, it is very satisfying to engage with once you figure out how it flows.All of your items in combat are fuelled by resources which can be scavenged across the open world. The design of this aspect is most akin to Horizon Zero Dawn’s approach, in that they can be scavenged in abundance and do not require much searching to enter an encounter fully prepared. These resources also fuel the game’s skill system, which is unfortunately structured weirdly in the sense that the majority of the skills are locked unless you find a specific skill page via either a quest or exploration, meaning that progression occurs incredibly slowly. I never felt that seeking these out was required though since there is little consequence to death. Checkpoints primarily occur by interacting with souls-like shrines, but nothing is lost upon death aside from your location, ultimately making repeated runs back to an area you died within a rather frustrating and seemingly pointless endeavour. This is emphasized by the fact that most bosses have their own checkpoints disconnected from any shrines, so I think the flow of the game would be improved if the entire experience adopted this system. Finally, the bosses themselves are too simple, as most simply require numerous shots to highlighted purple spots to dispatch, thus posing less danger than simply traversing the open landscape. Unless you search every nook and cranny in your initial playthrough, the ending of BLACKTAIL really acts as the beginning of an even more exciting journey to discover what the rest of the world has in store. From hidden boss fights with skill page chests to uniquely designed side areas, I felt that I only began to scratch the surface of what this world offers after I finished the 12-hour-long campaign. Its content-rich nature is further evident with the game’s excellently designed achievements; only one can be obtained simply by completing the story, with the remainder offering various tasks you’ll be able to achieve by exploring the landscape, and using your gear to experiment with its inhabitants. Completionists, or really anyone who loves exploring a good open world, will feel well accommodated for here.In terms of Steam Deck performance, the game offers a specific Steam Deck graphics configuration which locks it to 30fps. However, this felt too choppy for me, so I switched everything to low and obtained a framerate which varied between 35-60fps depending on the area. Nonetheless, it was smooth to play in most places, and it’s truly a testament to this game’s beauty that it still looked incredible with this configuration. Finally, BLACKTAIL is very polished, though there are two bugs worth noting: there were various pathing issues with the creatures in the open world, and more seriously, I experienced a main quest progression blocker in the second zone. The developers are aware of the issue, so hopefully this will have been fixed by the time you experience it.BLACKTAIL is an incredibly impressive effort, especially given this is the first release by this developer. Its narrative and design aspects combine well to create a unique and satisfying experience that cannot easily be compared to another title. Once I got past the initial learning curve of this weird and wonderful world, it hooked me for most of its runtime, and I’m looking forward to returning and discovering its numerous remaining secrets. I cannot wait to see what this developer comes up with next. Click  to see what my review scores mean!

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like Alice in wonderland on shrooms!My wife’s German boyfriend describes it like Fable and breath of the wild had a baby.I've got recent Polish ancestry that I'm relatively disconnected from because America but this game's folklore and art direction resonated with me in ways I didn't expect. It gave me Alice in Wonderland, Pan’s labyrinth and David bowies labyrinth vibes. I think that Slavic mythology is so underrated. One of my biggest gaming wishes is to see Kratos fight Chernobog in some future GOW. As a slav it’s so nice to see Slavic myths and legends represented in games. We need more video games set on folktales, fables, and slavic mythology.Blacktail was one of the biggest surprises for me! I hadn't even heard of the game until right before release and I'm so glad I took a chance on it. It’s such a unique and quirky little game. It does the core things really well and doesn't over reach. The world’s small but packed, unlike say Forspoken which is huge but barren.It’s a first-person open world fantasy/magical game. The world is very beautiful. It feels like you’re are in a Pixar movie. It has trolls, fairies etc. It’s a really must-have for anyone wanting to dive in a beautiful fantasy/magical world with a nice story and charismatic characters.You play as Yaga, a teenage girl who's been driven from her home by villagers who believe she's been corrupted by the witch Baba. In addition, all of Yaga's friends have vanished, and she's now wandering a large fantasy land in search of her lost sister. And accompanying her is a mysterious Voice, both mocking her and acting as guide as she stumbles through the landscape looking for answers. I won't say anything else about the story, since aside from Yaga's destiny being very obvious, exploring the hows and whys of her situation are the main narrative. It does help that the actors for Yaga and the Voice are both excellent, even if the quality of the other actors goes up and down a bit. They're never terrible, but some clearly aren't pros. At least the dialogue is usually witty and well written, far more interesting than in Forspoken for sure.The map is the true star of this show though. It's broken up into four chunks, with Baba's hut serving as the hub (and upgrade center) in the middle. The regions are broken up by cardinal directions, but also according to season, giving each a distinct look. It also reinforces one of the game's central themes of natural cycles, death and rejuvination, as your adventure begins in spring meadows and ends in a bleak winter wasteland, before bringing about the next cycle.Every inch of the map feels lovingly handcrafted, and it's a joy to uncover with a wide range of terrain and climate types. The layout is excellent, constantly giving you glimpses of odd landmarks and interesting features that beg to be explored. It's one of those games where I continuously found myself going "Ooooh, wazzat?" and wandering off the plot path to see what's was beyond the next hill, and that's a vibe that's so hard for many modern open world games to capture. I don't think I've enjoyed simply “exploring” in an open game this much since Skyrim.The handcrafted nature of the map also gives it a quaint artificiality that I found quite charming. It reminded me at times of 1980’s fantasy movies, like Krull or Neverending Story, where the swamps and forests were all constructed on soundstages with an eye towards aesthetics rather than realism. And it's a good thing the map is so compelling because, honestly, the main plot doesn't make very good use of it. You could easily speedrun the plotline in under ten hours, but you would only see around a quarter of the map. Which is a shame, because so much of the sheer joy comes from abandoning the plot line. The map is full of weird residents of the forest, especially a group of talking mushrooms who are all absolutely nutters. This gives the game a bit of an Alice in Wonderland vibe, as you constantly have to play along with the weirdo’s you meet.This led, for example, to one of the funniest side quests I've done in a while. You're told that there's a massive battle occurring between two factions of rock people. When you arrive at the battlefield, there's nothing happening... until you look closer and realize that there are boulders scattered around, with faces painted on and vaguely sword-like rocks stacked beside them. Is it a real battle, or just someone's crazy staging? That the Voice seems fully invested, shouting to be heard over the din of a melee you can't hear, just makes it more surreal. Further complicating things, kind of, is the game's morality system which feels like it's taken straight from a 2000s Bioware game. Which is to say, you're either Good or Evil, and you're expected to pick an alignment and stick with it for the best rewards. You decide which morality you want to lean towards, by doing things such as offering honey to bees or killing / saving birds. On one hand, this gives the game real replayability, as you will receive different quests from different quest-givers, depending on your alignment. Also, as the opposing faction is hostile, this means you'll have some optional bosses to fight if you feel like it. In fact, there are a bunch of optional bosses scattered around, if you want extra challenge.On the other hand, there is only one ending so arguably your choices "don't matter", but that kind of plays into the games' themes. It’s a great good game design! Play how you want, see the results, but the grand narrative has its own thing to tell you! This is very much a case where it's about the journey, not the destination. So enjoy the journey and don't rush things.The biggest issue with the game is probably its combat, which is... adequate, but that's it. You're an archer, and your bow is your only weapon. You eventually unlock three different types of arrows, and you get a magic staff which can be used to distract/lure baddies, but that's it. It's pretty basic. Then again, most combat can be avoided. There's no XP, and few enemies drop truly valuable materials, so you can usually just run straight past encounters you don't want to deal with. You can also unlock a potion that improves your stealth, specifically for this.Meanwhile, boss battles reminded me of the Metroid Prime games. They're more about positioning and anticipating the enemy's attacks, while making use of the environment and figuring out which points need to be shot. You won't ever be standing in one place rapid-firing, Legolas-style. It loves throwing a lot at you to keep you moving, and the first few boss battles can be pretty tricky until you figure out how the game expects you to play.Everything in this game was pure joy. I thought it hit an excellent balance of being a fairly dark game overall, but remembering to include elements of humor and beauty to prevent the atmosphere from being oppressive. In fact, the only reason I wouldn't say to play the game right now is that it could be one of the most perfect October games ever made. It FEELS like Halloween. The autumn section, in particular, is like it's straight out of a made-for-TV holiday special. Not to mention the whole thing where you're playing as a budding witch.In short, if you enjoy first-person adventures, Blacktail absolutely needs to be on your radar. It's not a bad value even at full price, and is definitely worth it on sale. For 30 bucks it's a well worth experience, especially compared to 70 bucks for "AAA" games like Forspoken.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR-Awesome fun start of an action adventure with a good hook for a story; that dwindles and becomes a nebulous and cryptic walking simulator. Combat was iffy, not great and not bad; overall clunky in many areas. The end game story was incredibly disappointing and left me with more questions than answers. I will admit the story relatively doesn't hold your hand and perhaps that's why I do not understand. Unfortunately, this only gave me a bitter taste at the end.To start I would give this probably a 5/10 overall and would not recommend it. The use of the Bow, assorted arrows, magic, and accessories were fun to use and get used to. I'll admit I did not get good with the mechanics, and the constant kiting of enemies and often times not knowing where they came from as they can randomly flank you/are hard to see; was not my cup of tea. Some of the quest's were fun and engaging with nuanced components not employed in other games that I am aware of. Such as the Rock War quest, this was probably my favorite one; and literally had me laughing aloud. The Spider Quest on the other hand, was too nebulous and did not make much sense to actually complete (Having ?'s on all the spider's locations vs an area without them - therefore not having a chance to progress the quest -  would have helped more). I literally checked the entire circle area for 20 mins until I randomly check a Spider. A lot of the quest's and dialog were also overtly theatrical and excessive, almost like a glorified sock puppet as essentially all the NPC's were just a talking head. It was fun at the start, and it turned into a chore to get through the dialog and it's unneeded fluff. The world was beautiful, the items and art, music and sound effects were very spot on for my taste. That overall feel was great, and I was happy to experience that overall.I also did not know about going back to the previous area's, and looking for secondary quest's/item until I made it to Autumn. As such, had I not gone back I would have been gloriously unprepared for the final component of the game, which you could (Sans one item) bull rush towards. Thus also "locking yourself out" of ever going back, and would probably not be able to complete the game and have to start over again. This is because you would not have access to 75% of the items and upgrades you would need. Which, is a choice; and has been implemented in other game's and to be fair it did have a "warning" at this area. I would just suggest better direction's for the player such that they don't get/feel trapped by the design. Perhaps I missed something along those lines and it is my fault, regardless it was my experience.Lastly, towards the later portion of the game there seemed to be puzzles/repeating designs that didn't really add anything to the game other than just stacking time, tension, and esoteric dialog before the end which only hindered it's performance and the overall end was lackluster. Again, maybe I am wrong; maybe it was there, as my experience did not find it this only lends credence to my displeasure at the end. Which other's' certainly can also perceive.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never make reviews. especially on release of games. But this time ill make an exception. Im pleasantly surprised. Its hard to describe. Its like a mix of conkers bad furday character design, brutal legends map design all the while its Slavic folklore equivalent of Alice in wonder land. But Alice got treated like a witch. The plot is actually good? the voice acting is good? im not use to indie games being good on release I have incredibly low expectations. The collectibles tell you about Slavic folk lore. its pretty nice.I accidentally beat the game at 19 hours as good. I unlocked a +play through and actually I feal like beating it again.very rarely do I 100% a game im very flaky as a gamer. But this game I might put more effort into. I guess I missed content because I wasnt even full build when I won. So easily im guessing i missed 30% of stuff? I only had 2/3 of talent tree unlocked and about 70% of collectables. Your first playthrough can easily be 20-30 hours depending on how bad you rush it. The mechanics of the game give it replayability. Theres good/bad alignment, good/bad alignment quest givers and apperently a campaign+ so Ill see how that goes. hardly any annoying bugs. So far I have had an audio glitch at the END of the game and two chests not being opened at the first fight due to enemies stuck in ground.I just kept try until they spawned out of the ground or I was able to AOE them through the floor. I have to say VERY UNUSUAL! most indie games are beyond buggy but this was clearly polished before release.My critiques of the game? It is WAY too easy to poison yourself and its WAY too easy to get fall damage. Some of the environment you slide off hills. Jump is too low. But these are minor gripes. The game is good and IMO its worth the current price. some things seem hard to unlock? the "specialist" alignment I didnt even touch until the end of the game which to me is too late. I didnt even get it upgraded. having certain changes to the environment due to your alignment with for example larva/ants would have been nice.I wont spoil too much. I guess ill post a thread in discussions if anyone has questions.

_childDocuments_.review: Starts off interesting enough, but quickly turns into a slog. I feel like I spend most of my time collecting sticks and feathers. Boundaries aren't always clear either and there have been a handful of times I died trying to drop down on a ledge only a couple feet below. Very frustrating when you realize that you respawn at the last waypoint you put your flower in, which could be god knows how far back. Treasures aren't exciting to get either because it always the same item.The world is very vibrant and characters are interesting, that's probably the best part of the game really.I can really only recommend the game if on sale, not at $30.

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me a lot of American McGee's Alice.Pros:Interesting story and visuals. The game world is well put together.Simple upgrade path (basically collect components and upgrade everything... though you need to find specific upgrades in random locations to progress some of the others)Main character voice acting is great.There's really no penalty or frustration with dying. Travel is fast.Cons:Minigames are jarringly out of place (cook meat, mouse maze). The most annoying though is the flashback "match the memory".Combat seems a bit more difficult than it should be for the casual nature of the game, but they have another play mode for that I guess. You can win most fight pretty easily, but some areas don't have much for healing, so you'll limp around for quite a while with low health.If you go exploring you'll have a bad time. Even though it's a semi-open world, stick to the story path or you'll wind up in areas that require items from later in the story plot, or enemies well beyond your abilities. The only this you gain from exploring is chests, but the story will eventually take you to that area anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing story, even if I dont understand half of it, is pretty wild. Gamplay is a bit like a survival game where you collect resources to craft arrows, potions and a broom to help you out in battle. It gets pretty intense in some situation, when you have more than 3 enemies attacking you and you have to think quickly how to kill your enemies quickly or get swarm. This is probably what I like most of the game, it requires your full attention, and being careful while exploring because you dont know when enemies will attack. The morality system is also well implemented and has weight. It gives you bonuses and titles that give extra perks according to your choices and actions in the game. Also, sidequest resolution will have impact on the choices you make, and will change how characters response to you in the game.One of the shortcomings i see with the game, is that pretty much the bow and arrow the only thing you will get to attack your enemies and nothing else, you get some power attacks, dodging skill and pushback, but that is it. The difficulty is above average in my experience, Difficulty is a mixed bag here, some parts are easy, but it has some difficulty spikes since you can get easily swarm if you stumble into the wrong areas. I would say is Above average, since the game really requires you to think quickly before getting killed, but what makes the game difficult and a bit annoying is my next point.Be prepare to SAVE often, the game does not tell you exactly, but to save the game you have to put flowers in the pillars, so far is the only way i found to save the game or going back tot he hut. I cannot stress enough how important this is, because from my almost 8 hours playing I am pretty much spent 2 hours wasted by dying and not saving. There is no reason why not to put an auto save system in the game but I guess it was developers choice.Overall the experience is enjoyable, I will play the game to the end to see how it all ends since I am actually enjoying it even with the shortcomings I mention.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game so far on PC and Steamdeck. _childDocuments_.review: I am amazed at what a small team of Polish (<3) developers achieved. It even has New Game +!The story is a little confusing at times, but most if not all of the things get explained in the end. The game, although janky here and there (slav jank) is actually way more playable than most AAA games I recently experienced. On top of that, the entire world, the artstyle-- it feels like I'm in a fairytale (because I was) and I love that I don't have to spend hours to grind resources to get meaningless abilities or craft stupid stuff. It actually goes pretty fast and I never had too little resources to do what I wanted. It sometimes felt annoying to constantly craft arrows on the go, but it added intense moments in combat.The combat is something similar to Doom Eternal, where you have to dodge enemy attacks with dashing and shoot the enemy. There are arrows and skills to help you damage enemies and survive. The broom becomes a valuable tool as it can heal you if you are good, or help damage enemies if you are evil.Yes, there is morality system, which seems to actually have some impact on what happens to your character and other characters in the story. You can of course always do an evil thing now, then good thing later, but it seems the game is encouraging you to either commit to evil or good side, as there are special rewards if you commit to either path.On top of all that, we have this amazing music. It adds sooo much to this game, I loved almost every song in the soundtrack, except the very last boss fight and the very last level where you fight the boss. We could have used more higher tempo songs for the last boss instead we got this... weird... slow..  piece. I don't know , it just felt off you know.Bugs? I actually don't think I noticed any.Graphics? Gorgeous. And from what I could see, optimised.Story? It's not something super epic but it got me hooked and I wanted to see it through. It's like I said a bit tough at times, there is a lot of this ...angsty teenager like -- angst-- in a lot of parts, so it feels a little sluggish at those moments but other than that I actually had an enjoyable experience.Overall, I love this game.For an indie studio, and the price and how big the world is, the side quests and things you can do, I think it's worth it. 11 hours in and I still havent explored more than 50% of the map and none of it is empty, there's always stuff to loot, creatures to fight or help.I really recommend it.I hope to see more adventures of Yaga or more adventures in this world.

_childDocuments_.review: You know a game is great when the first time you stream it to your friends their only response is “what the ♥♥♥♥ are you playing?”I adore this game to pieces and I can’t believe this is the second time I’ve purchased an outstanding exploration game only to wait and play it a year later  Outer Wilds .  If I had a nickel…  Anyway, I was going to split this review between good and bad, but there’s so little I dislike or had problems with so this is going to be a very lopsided review.  If any of the positives tickle your fancy then I would recommend scooping this game up.: Extremely vibrant and colorful world where you’d be hard pressed to find any muddy colors without a purpose.  It’s full of uniquely designed characters and creatures.  The skybox being crafted of symbols rather than a realistic sun, moon, and stars is probably one of my favorite bits to sell the fairy tale themes.: All connected and all great.  Probably some of my favorite performances from the last year and considering half of the cast is voiced by one guy (bless you Beau Marie), well that’s quite the feat.  Spy is the best character overall.: Not just filler!  Each one feels lovingly crafted and they aren’t just “collect x to give to y.”: I enjoy walking around the bright forest and the unique modes of transport you unlock as you progress are mostly useful in their own rights.  Nothing too exciting though and you are quite limited in your own abilities to get around the map without totems.: Enjoyable, but a little limiting (you can jump and dodge separately, but you can’t jump then dodge mid-air for example).  Depending on the encounter, you burn through arrows really quickly. You’re likely going to have to pull up the crafting menu at least once every other fight.: I really like that it's not all black and white mortality.  Sure some of it is, but there’s other instances where, for example, letting someone die is the “moral” choice.  Different upgrades are tied to different moral compasses and you interact with two different mushrooms depending on if you’re good or evil so a second playthrough is slightly varied.  : There are a couple of sections in the game where platforming becomes necessary for some exploration.  Some of them can be done with just normal jumps, but some problems arrive when the gap is just a little too big.  You don't have much, if any, aerial control of your character, so once you hit jump, your trajectory is locked in.  Better hope you didn’t screw up, otherwise it’s back to whatever save point you hit last. There are a couple of scenes where you see the main antagonist attack various spirits.  You do a puzzle before the scene plays out and as soon as you finish the puzzle you are bombarded with tons of images of the short scene before it plays in full.  It can be interpreted as Time and Space syncing up, but it still feels unnecessary and prevents me from recommending the game to my epileptic friend. - Great for story, not so much in the gameplay department.  They aren’t all that interesting the first time around and I was downright dreading them for a second playthrough because they take so long to get through.  At least I had a friend to keep me company.There are other things I didn’t get to touch on, like the fact this game has one of my favorite side quests ever and the use of “quantum mechanics” to add to the fairy tale feel, but I think it’s best for you to discover these things.  I really hope you give this game a chance!Oh... and uh...Stepping Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: Hark, good sir or madam, and lend me thine ears, for I have a tale to tell of a game called Blacktail. 'Tis a game of curious nature, with an art style so bewitching that it doth draw the eye and capture the heart. But alas, 'tis not without its flaws, flaws that doth mar the experience and leave one feeling less than satisfied.The story of Blacktail is one of depth, the characters, too, are a colorful bunch, each with their own quirks and personalities that doth add to the charm of the game.But alas, the combat, a crucial component of any game, doth leave something to be desired. 'Tis tedious and lacking in excitement, with enemies that doth respawn without end. And worse still, there be glitches and technical issues that plague the game, with enemies getting stuck in walls and other such mishaps.In short, Blacktail is a game of two halves, with much to commend it and much to criticize. The art style and story doth make it a game worth playing, but the combat and technical issues doth make it hard to recommend. So if thou art a lover of art and story, then Blacktail may be for thee, but if thou art seeking excitement and thrills, then perhaps look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: BLACKTAIL is kind of a conceptual game where the story of this game is presented as a fairy tale. What I like the most about this game is its combat system which is simple but fun.Nonetheless, bad things still exist. The narrative of this game is "verbose"; instead of telling the story straightforwardly, the developers chose to be long-winded, turning a simple sentence into 5-6 sentences. Plus, there are moments when the character tries to say something out of nowhere to make it sound like a poem with hidden meaning. Sadly, instead of being cool, such a dialogue gives players the "WTF" feeling all the time. Therefore, if you plan to read the dialogue in order to immerse its story, it might be a bit boring for you. Well, if you are a skip-it-all type of player, then it's fine.Luckily, I got this game from Humble Bundle, so it is a short and fun game for me (good enough to give a positive review). It is enjoyable and suitable for killing time. However, if I specifically bought it (without getting from the bundle) whether with discounts or not, I would have some expectations and my review would surely be negative.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game is AMAZING! It's very atmospheric and reminiscent of Alice: Madness Returns and Hellblade: Senua's Sacrifice. Add in a bit of Valheim-esque monsters and combat that reminds me of my times as an archer in Skyrim, and you have this game! (So far. I'm not finished yet). I'm really pleased with this game so far. It's enthralled me and felt so magical since the beginning. The story can be predictable at times (through main plot of the story) but that doesn't take away from the magic of it. I feel like I'm so close to the end of the main story but I also feel like there's so much more to do. The world is open and you're not super limited on where you can go no matter where you are in the story. I like the mixture between classic fairytale twists and the world's own mythology. It's very unique and I have high hopes for the rest of the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game. I picked it up and spent all my free time on it until I just ran out of content. My computer couldn't run this very well and I played nearly 60 hours at 20 fps so that should tell you how much I liked this game. The story was really engaging and I liked the characters a lot, the combat was really fun, it was overall just a great time.There were only a few things I wasn't crazy about that I'll say for anyone interested in the game. I spent a lot of time doing trial and error to figure out what I was supposed to be doing, which is agonizing in a game with save stations. Sometimes you just aren't very well told how to deal with something or what to do in situations, or what directions you're given are very vague. It can be frustrating, mostly because the game is new and finding help was difficult. Second, no idea why but cut-scenes ran really badly. It was really disappointing to get more story and it's buffering, this could have been my computer. If you do get the game for your own sake disable steam overlay while playing, I absolutely died because it would pop up because I tried to make arrows while running.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game, so things are fresh.Mandatory good stuff:1. Easy to manage resources. You will find them in piles. Mostly you will find more than you will ever need.2. Some attempt at a morality system, which affects your item(s?), 1 ability, and 1 passive trait. It is also supposed to affect your resources but I have noticed no issues while playing as evil either.3. Some of the voice acting was superb. Some.4. Some of the scenery and statues were worth staying around and marvel in them.Bad stuff:1. Story explains absolutely nothing. It leaves you with more questions than answers. It assumes you got whatever it was trying to tell you and moves on. Maybe this game needs studying some old slavic legend before playing? But isn't it supposed to tell it to us?2. Ending did not explain anything either. It was underwhelming, confusing.3. Sure, there are good and bad choices and there is morality but aside of them affecting your abilities and some of your items... the story will literally have the same ending and the same gameplay. No difference. Not enough to warrant the morality system the way they did.4. Stuff I shot down kept dropping below the map, staying on high ledges, or dropping into water and gorges.5. Enemies seem to have a magnet that tracks your movements, even if you dash out of their way and hit you even then. There is some fancy extremely specific timing involved that just makes things way too annoying. You better use the 'Broom' to lure enemies to attack it so you can pick them off.6. Personally, I had issues finding NPCs. There are some signs pointing you the right way but then it stops. I kept missing their location and finished the game with just a single side-quest done. Their location needs to be more distinguishable in the terrain or have some of the main quests depend on side-quests in that area, like the first one.It is extremely easy to miss half of the gameplay.Thumbsdown because it failed at storytelling and the morality system.Its literal selling points...

_childDocuments_.review: Imma keep it quick. Is this game somewhat clunky on certain aspects, yeah, it doesn't have the best combat, you'll get stuck on terrain etc. Do I think any of that matters for this game, no.What this game does incredibly well is the unique execution in both narrative and art direction of its concept of being a story based on central/center-east european folklore and fairy tales.The landscapes are often stunning, the attention to detail is always there and the side content is expansive and as well executed as the rest of the game.If you want a story driven game with Vermintide 2 level combat you won't find it here but you will find a beautiful, unique narrative and world made by clearly passionate artists.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want something unique - play this.Gameplay loop is ok - nothing super fancy, but solid - movement is just the right type of smooth, bow and magic give you just enough ways to approach enemies, and resource management is... actually pretty easy, don't expect something like The Forest. That being said, while the gameplay is fine, it’s far from being the real star of Blacktail.The setting and story is where this game really shines. I can honestly say I've never experienced this type of world in any game I've played. My expectations were basically Alice: Madness Returns but Slavic (which is an automatic thumbs up from me) but describing Blacktail like that would actually be unfair to both titles. The inspirations are obvious, but both the source material and the flavor of the dark twist put on said source material are completely different. It’s like saying that hamburgers and hotdogs are the same, because they’re both a piece of meat in a bun. Technically correct, kinda misses the point.What doesn’t miss the point is the dark fairy tales on display. Without going into spoilers, Blacktail takes a lot from old Slavic traditions and fairy tales, especially the Grimm Brothers, and melds them all into a cohesive world that serves as a backdrop for a story about finding oneself. A story supported by some top notch voice acting, my I add.All in all it’s a 100% recommend for anyone who wants something weird. And a 150% recommend if you’re interested in Slavic folklore on top of that.You can’t pet the hedgehogs, but you can help them get the apples.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game would have been a great adventure or a walking sim, but they decided to add "gameplay", and it's really mediocre even for an AA game. I wish Steam had a mixed opinion as an option. Blacktail is not bad, but I cannot recommend it for its game mechanics.The visuals are great, the story is ok, but the gameplay is just meh. Half walking sim, half really bad shooter, this game fails to deliver any memorable moments, and essentialy just repeats the same combat encounters recipe over and over again. Besides, difficulty curve is all messed up: it's ridiculously easy at the beginning, but some fights later on are pretty frustrating, mainly because there are some enemies that teleport to you and attack immediately, and you can't do anything.Also, there are some 2D platforming sequences in the game, and they are extremely bad. Not hard, just bad and boring, and the controls are horrible.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally, I enjoyed the game. The story was intriguing, and I was invested in the adventure. However, as I progressed, the game started to feel like a tedious slog. The excitement faded, and it began to lose its charm, becoming increasingly boring.More frustratingly, the controls started malfunctioning. During combat, they felt sluggish and unresponsive, a stark contrast to normal navigation. Running became impossible, and you had to rely on dashes, which often stopped abruptly. This made no sense because you could only walk around slowly, leaving you open to attacks all the time. The sluggish controls turned what should have been dynamic combat into a frustrating experience.Boss battles, which should have been thrilling, turned into a nightmare of frustration. The enjoyment was drained, and the game felt like more of a hassle than a fun experience. The breaking point for me was the Dragon scene. Dying three times due to control issues—where suddenly I couldn't dash—and constantly running out of arrows was infuriating. The sense of adventure was overshadowed by these persistent problems, and I couldn't be bothered to continue.Others might find it appealing, but for me, the game became frustratingly boring and a slog to play. It's a shame because the story had so much potential, but the gameplay issues ruined it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just gonna be super honest and directly address a few other comments:1. Killing birds is bad, killing dear is okay. THE REASONING: birds drop their feathers all over the place, so killing them for more feathers is greedy and unnecessary. Deer do not just drop their meat, you need to eat it to survive.2. There's a hyperfixation on young girls. A HYPERFIXATION???? No. The characters are all kids, yeah, but thats a part of the myth? The crux of the connections is based on interpersonal relations between the kids of the village, and one of the main ones, S.... (I am not great with slavic names admittedly) is categorically the "bully." There's no creepiness or weirdness, touch grass, they're just kids.3. The game is woke for having a female main character.What? A guy literally gave this game a 35/100 in due part to the main character being female, and because there's a platforming section that is made "artificially difficult." Seriously? 1. Women exist, again, touch grass. 2. The platforming segments are not difficult.Now, my actual review.The games aesthetic is a major point of it, the style and the story telling do a wonderful job of imparting the mystical folklore of a traditional myth that is quite fascinating, while incorporating a lot of interesting gameplay elements into the concept of being Baba Yaga (Such as using the cauldron to upgrade skills, ya know, witch craft) And the progression of the skill tree incentivizes exploration and the side quests, but it is entirely possible to make it through, relatively easily, without achieving every upgrade.Some of the story telling is a bit hand fisted with narrator and a couple of the side characters (mushrooms in the introduction notably) but it doesn't take away from the game in any way, considering you have the option to skip those segments of the dialogue if you already have the understanding from what they say.So honestly, if you enjoy folklore as I do, and well made gameplay that has a few... quirks (Don't touch water, there's an explanation for why if you do), its an amazing game to get on discount, but also worth it for the full price as well (But who can say no to a 67% percent discount?)

_childDocuments_.review: I am not really sure what this game is trying to be. It seems like it wants to be an open world  fps story driven survival game yet none of the mechanics have been fleshed out enough to make the game a good example of any of those genres. It is closer to a walking simulator with a few other mechanics from other genres tacked on, tacked on being the operative term. The open world is unnecessary, the combat is atrocious, quests are very limited in number and the story is neither here nor there. Let me expand a little:Open World - I am not sure why the open world is there, there is next to nothing to do in it, most of the world is there as a time waster while you travel to the quest objective. Don't get me wrong it is very beautiful, there is just very little for you to do. It is like a painting, you can only look at it for so long before it gets boring, once that initial novelty wears off you are left with nothing else, that is Blacktail. A very pretty open world but also mostly just there to be looked at and not interacted with. Combat - I am not going to complain about there only being one weapon as that was clearly advertised. However if you are going to only have 1 weapon in the game, make it interesting. You are supposed to be a witch, witches have awesome powers. Why is the bow so boring and muggle like to use? You have 3 types of arrow, normal, honey (for some reason) and crystal and that is it. Why can't I infuse my powers into the arrows? Or use my abilities to fire multiple arrows, explosive arrows, fire arrows, blood arrows etc? Nothing has any weight at all, it feels like I am firing a kids bow at foam targets.Quests - Where are they? If you spend the time building an open world, give me a reason to explore it thoroughly. There seems to be only a few quests per area, I spent hours just wandering around hoping to find side quests. Nope, the 3 I got almost immediately are all there is for the first zone. This comes back to my previous point about the lack of things to do in the world. There are very few quests and very little else to interact with. Why have an open world at all? The quests that are in there are fine but again, same with the bow. If you are only going to have a few quests in the game, at least make them memorable.Story - I do not know much about Baba Yaga and the stories surrounding her, this game does not make me want to know more either. I always thought that Baba Yaga was a very dark character, this game makes every thing cartoony and kid friendly. The few characters I met were all non-human who I could not care less about, the story seems to be a very generic "find your sister" type thing. All in all, this is not making me want to read further into Baba Yaga. There is a morality system but I am not really sure why, the impacts of the choices you make are so light it would have been better using the development time fleshing out some of the other mechanics. I think this is one of the main problems, the devs could not decide what mechanics to keep and which to scrap so they kept them all and as a result did not have the resources to make anything other than lots of barebones sytems. I see others complaining about the crafting, inventory etc. I did not see that as an issue personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Linux: perfect under standard Proton [5800X3D/5700XT]Ultrawide: Full and glorious 21:9 [starting menu is 16:9, in game is fine]DualSense: Options for Adaptive Triggers and Sony buttonsFirst impressions: an eerily beautiful game of a classic tale, with [sometimes] clear morality choices that directly affect everything elseSkill 'Lost Pages' are hidden in chest throughout the map, and there is no in-game indication as to where they even might be. You have to actively go hunting for them, meaning you can complete the game without finding most of the advanced skills. This makes the endgame  harder than it needs to be, even on Story mode. So... search everywhere. All the time.Difficulty can be adjusted via in game pause menu, with Story mode still being deadly. It does get noticeably easier as you unlock skills, but can still be very challengingThere are 'platform' interludes where you control animals and collect acorns. They do not feel great, but if you manage them well enough you can put the acorns towards your chosen Morality path [which helps to unlock advanced skill effects]The world is beautiful, but the developers have decided to lump all visual effects into one non-descriptive slider, meaning you  turn crap like Chrom Ab and Lens Flare off independently. This is a massive oversight, but can be corrected with an Engine.ini file [see Discussions]. Either way the art direction is very 'fantasy' and works perfectly. You can and likely will get happily lost in the world they've createdThis game is amazing. It's also very obviously intended to be played through multiple times, since Morality explicitly dictates which actions you can take and how certain abilities work, and you're unlikely to unlock/find everything during your first run without a walkthrough. You can complete most of the central story in 7-10 hours having explored very little of the map, but you'd be robbing yourself of a fantastic experienceBuy

_childDocuments_.review: So far, it's... okay, I'd say 7/10. Get it if you like bullet hell games or heavily action-packed, fast-paced games. Pass it up if you're a cozy/casual gamer. Consider it if you are a fellow collector of witch games, but be prepared for a challenge if it's not your usual cup of brew.My qualms are these, and this is surely a cozy gamer ranting off:The pinecone things are too often impossible to collect as they fall into unreachable places, but the fact they're so plentiful makes it passable, just makes me waste a lot of resources, and as such, waste time when I can't collect more than half of them I knock down.I don't much care for the short distance that arrows have, AND I wasted a bundle before figuring out there is no gravity effecting the arrows (you know, like Skyrim) so they land *exactly* where your reticle points, which is cool and all, but unexpected, considering rpg games with archery (not even as the primary/only weapon) that I've played prior.Small "loot" chests seem to respawn, and quickly at that, making it hard to tell if I got the teeth already and I'm just wasting my time and energy taking out the constantly-respawning enemies next to this chest that may not contain teeth, but just some other over-abundant resource. I could also be confused in the mayhem, and ALL these little chests could be outright useless and it's just the BIG ones with teeth. Suddenly I'm forgetting.I'm in STORY mode, not Adventure... so I'm assuming I'm supposed to be given more story and exploring and less/easier combat. Three situations have entirely felt like I was tossed into hard mode - frost gnoll, and two measly sad little bat-infested caves with basic-ass treasure of what's most likely a fancy box of f*****g sticks. I've reached an area, guided literally by the storyline by the way so I can't possibly be in the wrong area, with a frost troll that I can barely damage and has a few lackeys that all summon lesser creatures that just surround me. I'm assuming I can't face them yet, so I'm running around this zone screaming my lungs out trying to avoid the troll (well gnoll I guess). If I were streaming, it would have been HILARIOUS CONTENT at least. It's really chaotic for a more casual chill exploring gamer, having to stress and worry about making 1 broom at a time, putting 1 broom down, make another, oh shoot I already shot off my whole 9 arrows and only 3 hit because I'm massively panicking as my health just goes down and down and I can't keep enough arrows in stock thanks to the panic and swarm, better make more arrows! Ah crap 2 seconds later I'm trying to make more arrows and put another broom down and struggling to hit enemies outright swarming me, and wow won't ya look at that, the broom also makes me press the dang button 2-3 times before ACTUALLY putting any brooms down, that one took me a few fails to figure out was happening - the broom icon will just FLASH at me or otherwise appear, and do nothing until I keep spamming the button. I've GOT the broom made, PUT IT DOWN, ya witch!Utter f*****g chaos.Also, don't get me started on the bats. The game tells me to use my Hocus on them, and both good and evil Hocus had absolutely NOOOOOOOOO effect on the bats every time I attempt them, making any caves impossible, plus they continue to swarm you even when you run into the sunlight. What a glorious death. Not.I'm trying to "git gud," and it's overall fun, though not my usual style of game. I guess I'm on the fence to keep playing as it surely gets harder for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gamer like me, but I can tell others will love this game and would likely rate it much higher. I'm a HUGE fan of witchy titles, so that drew me in. I love historical witchcraft and this is exactly that, with a touch of humor slapped in - but lots of action. I'm not at ALL an action/fast paced/bullet hell gamer, I'm ONLY here for the Baba Yaga story which is highly enjoyable so far. Maybe close to 7 hours into the game isn't far enough to take on some little oddly CUTE bats, or swarms of little lackeys, or frost gnolls... maybe 7 hours in, you're meant to still be a whelp who can barely fend for her witchy self.That means it's a long game, right? With a second replayability, because you can either be totally good or totally bad. At least the chaos and stress is worth the money for the hours of game you get. Plus, there's a side-scroll goat game that surprised me while getting Drag's memory unlocked. PLUS PLUS the music while matching up the witch memory was "FIRE" as the kids say, too.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this on my wishlist for a while. Several years actually. I only recently got it from a friend. Do i wish i got it sooner? Oddly, no. This is a game to play in between other games. Where you want a story but desire to not rush it. I truly did enjoy this game and will keep it downloaded to keep playing it since I have yet to see all the corners. There is as much or as little hand holding as you want. Simply turn off hints if you dont want them. The bad, well not really a whole lot of bad. The only bad I really have to state is that the terrain you can get stuck on easily or bump yourself off and fall. This is an older game so hard saves (placing flowers at shrines) is very necessary. As far as bad goes, that is my only gripe and can simply be maneuvered around with patience and watching for your surroundings.This is not Aloy, this isn't just focused around bow combat, this is a story game. But that does not mean its not fun. Its quite a lot of fun. Your skill with a bow does do good but you don't need any kind of twitch skills. This story revolves around Yaga and discovering herself. _childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with this game in the first 15 minutes when I, stupidly, tried to fire my bow without an arrow only to have the main character playfully strum a tune using the bowstring as an instrument. There a TON of these little details embedded in the game. As a kid, I loved 'Labyrinth' with David Bowie. I can't help but get all kinds of similar feels here. Talking mushrooms, speedy gremlins, angry blobs, toad princes, and a weird cat that you can't shake is more than he puts on. All of this in a stunning, beautifully conceived world that is equal parts childhood fairy tale as it is dark fantasy. As if that wasn't enough, the soundtrack and audio as a whole is incredible. Guttural throat singing, some pagan chants, and an eerie undertow accentuate every step the character takes. Easily one of if not the best indie title I've played in years. Bravo, Parasight. Bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: Initially I just grabbed this, because I saw archery and an atmosphere that looked interesting. It turned out to be a lot more.Blacktail's atmosphere that gripped me turns out to be both a vibrant and gloomy fairy tale land. Your character Yaga, is a girl that appears rather conflicted, scared and looking for answers. For you however, in the start all that seems extremely confusing as you've been put right into it. A lot you meet on your journey is based on various child fairy tales and you meet rather odd characters like talking dead fish, mushrooms who are shadowy or knightly in "origin" and really creepy rocks.The story is great as how it's told and shown. Yaga's journey to "find herself" and her answers to her past are both the main quest through normal gameplay and various little odd minigames on how you patch together the answers.The game doesn't throw a lot of side quests at you. Instead there are only a few to each "season", but they are fairly memorable this way. One quest sends you into a quarry to defend it in a tower defence style, where you have to shoot anything that moves with your bow. Another quest sends you across a battlefield where stones are fighting each other, except stones show no movement when looked upon, so the entire battlefield fighting only happens behind you as you look away.Yaga sports only a small arsenal being her bow, a bit of magic and a few utility items. You have 3 different arrows, but overall encounters and enemies require you to switch between these and it feels neither too annoying nor too simple. The boss battles can feel a bit easy, but as some require awareness of the field, then it could prove to be a challenge.A really great take on the old fairy tales :)

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a game made with both love and humour. It very quickly became one of my favourite games of all time. _childDocuments_.review: Right, so... I've just spent a couple of hours of my life - time I'll never get back, by the way - playing this game, and I have to tell you... it's absolutely mental.Whoever did the casting must've been having a laugh. You've got this bizarre mix of accents that makes less sense than David Brent trying to give a TED talk on quantum physics. You've got these mushrooms - MUSHROOMS of all things! - and some voice in your head chatting away like they're from Camden Town. But here's the best bit... they've got this cat that sounds like it's doing a bad impression of both a Russian Bond villain AND a Japanese anime character AT THE SAME TIME!But wait til you hear about the morality system. Most of it's your basic "pet the puppy or drop-kick it into next Tuesday" type choices, but then... then they hit you with this absolute goldmine. You've got to choose between letting some lying monster get literally torn to shreds by his angry mob of followers or... help him keep lying! And guess which one's the "good" choice? The bloody murder! Because apparently fibbing is worse than watching someone get turned into confetti! What sort of backwards morality is that?!Oh, and another thing about this game - it's like going on a date, right? Starts off all promising and lovely, got you all excited... then two hours in you realize you're just collecting twigs like some demented squirrel with OCD. Brilliant.The combat... oh, the combat. They're calling it "intense archery combat" - about as intense as watching paint dry in slow motion. You just sort of... prance around like a dad at a wedding disco, firing what feels like rubber bands at monsters. I fought this boss, right? Just stood there like a lamp post, shooting arrows at him for what felt like three ice ages. It's like the world's most boring game of darts, except the dartboard's trying to kill you and you're armed with toothpicks.If you want a laugh, sure, give it a go. There's some properly ridiculous stuff in there, like when you run out of arrows and start playing your bow like you're at Glastonbury. But then it gets all serious on you, like when your mate Dave switches from talking about football to explaining the meaning of life after his eighth pint.At least I got it on sale. Though there's no compensation about how much time I wasted playing it, I'll tell you that.

_childDocuments_.review: A great example of taking existing tales and making them your own, with a generous helping of weirdness.  Baba Yaga, the Three Little Pigs, and more.Pros:* Excellent storytelling (great example of a )* Good voice acting, though the British (?) accent on the main character is a bit odd for a Slavic-themed story base.* Great world-building, huge world, including mini-dungeons.* Combat is a blast, once you have most of the upgrades unlocked.* Morality-based bonuses that provide unique challenges either way you play.Cons:* Character moves a bit sluggishly, even if you put the bow away.* Game doesn't explain most mechanics very well - expect experimentation.Meh:* Morality is consistently applied, but compared to traditional systems is a bit all-over-the-place.  Don't expect to know what's 'good' or 'bad' for at least a cpl hrs.* Combat can be a bit punishing at times - but my reflexes suck, so take that with a grain of salt.* Expect to get lost on finding main quest objectives - follow the trail of crumbs, when you do.TL;DR: It's a great exploration/bow-shooter with some replayability - 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've been calling this game American McGee's Metroid Prime when referring to it around my friends specifically in an effort to get them interested in it.It's brilliant. Excellent blending of mechanics and narrative themes that gets the player confronting the same questions that the protagonist is, assuming said player is not losing their mind stressing out over which choices are tied to which morality out of habit. (Advice: Don't! You're missing the point!) The cast is charming, and the blend of exploration and simple FPS combat give those of us who've never heard the Call of Duty ample room to find our footing and enjoy ourselves at our own pace.As drawbacks go, there's some jank here and the odd bug there, and the combat itself is probably a bit factional and shallow to engage someone who's looking for the next great bastion of encounter design. Basically any problem can be solved by plopping down your broom, which is sort of a shame, as there are mechanics for more high-level play like employing different arrow types wisely, timed evasion and your trusty upgradeable Hocus, which can just eat through certain foes and save you the resources needed to craft up more ammo. It's no game-breaker here, but a wrinkle in the form of an enemy or two that just ignore the broom, or more mixing and matching of enemy types, could've gone a long way here.All in all, though, I loved it. I cannot recommend this one enough. I cannot believe I'd never heard of it before Humble dropped it on my doorstep like a gift from a cat. A talking cat. Meow!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly captivating, imaginative and fun to play. It is a real shame it is not getting more coverage. It truly has the feeling of playing though a fairy-tale of old. Even though the tale of BabaYaga is an actual ancient fairy-tale, few games can capture what that actually FEELS like. I think the reason its not getting as much notice is the flat visual style, which is my one complaint. It seems conflicted between "stylized" and "traditional PBR" visuals. The result is a somewhat bland looking Unreal game that doesn't stand out and doesn't know what it wants to look like.  I assume it is a budget issue, but still it does hold the game back a bit. I personally wish they went all the way with the stylized visual style. Still, I would highly recommend it none the less. :)

Graphics are good, the world looks incredible.The game runs smoothly and is optimized very well, I haven't encountered a single bug/stutter in my playthrough. The gameplay itself is fun but the game feels a bit easy, I would suggest sticking with adventure difficulty instead of story.Since you have the option of choosing between good and evil, a New Game + is a good feature to experience the game from a different perspective and have a slightly higher level of difficulty. _childDocuments_.review: In the first few hours of Blacktail, I found myself struggling to stay interested. The gameplay quickly became repetitive, and I only kept going because I felt like I had to, not because I was enjoying it. It honestly tested my patience, and I just wanted to get it over with. The environments are visually appealing, with vibrant details that create a nice atmosphere. The artistic direction shines through in character and world designs. The story draws from Slavic folklore, which adds an interesting cultural touch. The conversations feel shallow, lacking the depth needed to make characters memorable. There’s nothing here that makes you care about or remember the characters you meet. The morality system feels superficial, and your choices lack meaningful impact on the game. The narrative is hard to follow, and it lacks the cohesion to keep you fully invested. The core gameplay revolves around shooting your bow, but it soon gets tedious as you’re constantly running around collecting feathers and sticks. It feels stiff, with janky hitboxes and awkward attack animations that make it hard to enjoy.Blacktail offers a visually pleasant world and an interesting inspiration from Slavic folklore, but the lack of engaging gameplay, forgettable characters, and an underwhelming story made it a chore to play through. It’s a game that shows promise but lacks the substance to make it truly enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Good:Bad:Blacktail is a good action-adventure game that immerses you effortlessly in its story and world. It offers a dark fantasy story with surprisingly some more grounded perspectives about how people react to the “other” and how they deal with something which they do not fully understand. Sadly, it’s held back by a combat system which could’ve used some improvement. It’s functional and it does the job but it never seizes to feel janky and unresponsive when you have your bow out. Yet for most of the game the combat system does the job all the way until the last 10%. After that point combat is all you’re going to get, and the devs even put you in a few combat arenas as if your playing Doom Eternall. Black tail’s combat system can’t make this a very enjoyable experience and thus this last 10% did sour my experience with the game a bit. Due to the combat I wouldn’t recommend it at its current full price, but if you can find it for a 30-50% discount (or the current humble choice) then there’s a lot of fun to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: So I only have ~45 minutes into the game, but want to post a positive review as it starts out rough but it's already growing on me.Starting with the negatives - Path finding/objectives - Not quite intuitive, it takes a bit of stumbling, fumbling, mumbling to get the feel of what's going on.Combat/Tutorial - The tutorial is good in some areas, sparse in others.  This leaves some jank in areas such as combat.  Like I dunno if there's just a straight melee skill at the start of the game, even just a basic knockback skill.  There's a "dash" that only seems to activate in certain fights...?  But being left with just a bow in smaller arenas isn't a fun combat system.The positives - The world - Graphics aren't AAA quality, but I didn't expect them to be.  But just the world has a somewhat cartoony yet gritty fantasy feel.  The best way to describe it is experiencing American McGee's Alice during a positive drug trip as opposed to a bad one.The characters - So far, all unique.  I interact with NPCs and feel that there's a story behind them.  Voice acting is up there with the RPG heavy hitters.  All the lines are unique, and two characters going back and forth sounds like actual dialogue as opposed to two voice actors recording lines at different times.Morality system - I'll admit I'm still getting the hang of it, but so far it seems like it's actually based in gameplay, not just the occasional choice.  What resources you collect impact it as well.I'll likely update this review later, but I got the game on sale and feel it's a solid purchase.  Takes a little getting used to, but it's unique and I can tell it's a labor of love.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the world, lore, story, and art style of this game. The gameplay was fine at first but by the time I got to the last act I grew increasingly frustrated and bored with how repetitive everything had gotten. The combat felt clunky at times and the maximum range of the bow is just not enough. It felt like I spent more time lost and picking up items than actually doing anything of value.

_childDocuments_.review: Dive into slavic mythology as the girl Yaga who wakes up only to discover that she can’t really remember much. Like who are you, where are you and why? What about your sister Zora? On your quest to find your lost sister and memory, you will have a lot of decisions to make, for instance which path are you going to take? Will you do good or will you do bad? Also, who is that voice speaking to you?I had tons of fun playing this game, the universe and the story in which it takes place was super interesting, with lots of tales that you will probably recognise. The voice acting is amazing and made me laugh out loud several times. You start out with pretty basic skills that you can evolve by questing and exploring the different seasonal maps. The game definitely has potential for a second playthrough if not more. There was one part of a secret that I just couldn’t figure out how to get to, well, that is going to bug me for sure xDI was however a little confused by the ending of the game, and there were a couple of times where I thought my game might have bugged a little. After doing some research I can see many people were left a bit bewildered by the ending, but there are some REALLY good theories out there, which I really enjoyed reading. I don’t mind having to think and theorize a bit myself. I really enjoyed the ride and hunting down the achievements, there aren’t complete guides in English on how to do everything, but it was still very fun and very doable. This will probably be on my top games played for the year - can definitely recommend!This games also have a cat! In deep voice: Meeeow!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it completely.I must give this hidden gem a thumbs up.Very well written story with a spice of uncertainty to let us think on overall picture.The gameplay is well polished though some mechanics are underwhelming and are there without a point (like meat roasting).Bow-mastery and potions are also add incentive to the gameplay and actually I enjoyed them.Morality mechanics are quite fun to play in both ways.Overall:Pros: - Story - Voice acting and narration - Exploration - Music - Quality Slavic mythology settingCons: - Some features are cosmetics and don't add much to a gameplay or a story - Could use a bit more balance tweakingWill observe what other games this studio will come up with.From that game I can tell that their strong aspects are scenarios and visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game as a gift. Nonetheless, with a clear conscience, I cannot recommend this game. Killing enemies offers no progression. And yet, areas you've cleared keep spawining them just to waste your time. You get no experience by staying and killing them. Some mechanics seem stupid enough, like having to keep crafting arrows mid fight or being stuck when you dash.I don't know, I expected something more. It has the foundation but fails at the output.

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a game with a rather interesting story and a wonderful world. For me, its strongest point were the gorgeous visuals, the immersive nature and the varied environments. It really was pleasing to explore this world, with all of its vibrant colors, hidden trinkets and cryptic characters. The artstyle felt contradictory at times, featuring realistic yet fabled nature alongside childish stars and hearts. I wonder if it's a hint to the character's maturity state?The story had a promising plot, however it could have been revealed a little better. Instead of unloading onto us all that transpired in the past after each chapter, I think it would be better if we discovered fragments of the story as we went and if there was more foreshadowing. I really liked the voice acting of the protagonist but not much that of the woman and I disliked the cat, character and voice. Also, I understand that for plot reasons some important questions can't be answered early, but I felt that the dialogue obscuring these during the game was weak and irritating at times, making the woman appear overly snob and sadistic. And, some main questions for me remain unanswered.The combat was nice, a little repetitive, circulating around the broom. I would have enjoyed a few more tricks up Baba's sleeve.Lastly, I think the weakest point was definitely the morality system, as many people have already commented. Many choices felt goodwilling to me but were treated as mean by the game, not to mention . But I guess that was the point of the story, that good or evil doesn't really exist? I think it could have been communicated better though.All in all, I really enjoyed playing this game and losing myself in its world, for which reason I can't wait to see more from its creators.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. I am a huge fan of story driven gaming, and this was a breathe of fresh air in a world where story gaming is few and far between. Combat requires skill and decent thinking, yet still not too hard when you get the hang of it. Puzzles were fun and finding all the little secrets were too. I honestly hope this studio expands on this project because this is Top Tier for me

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for August 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before September 3rd, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A tale of Baba Yaga, maybe.I’m taking a few guesses on this game, but with the story about a witch named Baba, and a character named Yaga, I feel like this is a safe bet.   This game reminded me a lot of Hellblade Senua’s Sacrifice, maybe a B-tier version of it, but there’s an interesting world and characters, with more of a focus on exploration than heavy combat so far.  There’s a lot more to do in the world with collectibles and upgrades and a bit more survival or crafting ideas though nothing too bad so far.   There’s also a morality system that feels more about the grayness of both sides than just pushing people to the side of the light.There’s a weird design choice where if you continue the game, you don’t recover your life, so you can get stuck in a harder fight with only one hit point left.  That’s a bad situation.  The gameplay feels like you can be vastly overpowered so far, and for some reason, the first boss only had a quarter of his life bar filled.   However, there is a bigger problem.  When I beat the first boss, I was on the evil path and the chest didn’t unlock.  I even quit back to the main menu, then beat him a second time and the chest remained closed.  That sucked a bit of the excitement out of the game.   Hopefully, it’s a one-time bug, but it’s not something I’m glad about. Pick this up if you like interesting stories or wonderful worlds.  I enjoyed exploring this game, and I kind of want to see where the story is going to go.  I want to find out if I’m right about Baba Yaga, and I have some guesses about other things as well.  I’m mostly upset about the glitch because up to that point, I was having a lovely time.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: This game attempts a bit of everything but only scratches the surface. Besides, the combat is basic, the story lacks depth, and the voice acting is completely amateur. Visually the game is standard, even running on the highest settings.I can't recommend this game, even at a discounted price.

_childDocuments_.review: There are small things about this game that make me grumpy. They are petty things, you can argue.  I'm going to lay them out here so you can argue if you want to.But I don't mind the game, and it may not be a long game, or even that hard of a game, but it's a fine enough game.The theme is all Slavic mythology, and a lot of is very bright and cheerful and highly saturated, almost cartoonish.  It's almost childish.  Fairy tales also have a very bright and cheerful tone to them.But then there's some burned-out areas, some angst, and things are dark and murky.  You don't need blood spatter and body parts strewn around to make things feel moody and dangerous.  Just atmosphere.  And this nails it.Combat is fine, mostly you shoot things with your li'l bow and arrow, occasionally using a spell or something to deal with trickier/tougher/faster/many enemies. Boss fights may require the occasional scoot-dodge at the right moment.I described it to my wife as, "American McGee's Baba Yaga.  Except with American McGee dialled down to about 0.2"  What was with that guy, anyway?  Why was he a big deal in the first place?Anyway, sorry, tangent.  Let me tell you what bugs me about the game:  It's the Inner Voice.The Inner Voice is anachronistic, and uses modern turns of phrase with a bit of cussin'. I'm not bothered by the cussin', I'm a foul-mouthed guy sometimes.  But absolutely everything else's speech patterns are cleaner, a trifle more formal, and fitting the game world better.  So Inner Voice is kind of jarring.  And maybe the snide, sarcastically aloof thing annoys me, because that stopped being cool when I stopped being 15.There's secrets to the game, the protagonist is repressing memories or whatever.  The Inner Voice Knows.  And just won't share anything yet, even though it would have been appropriate a few times, because I get the vibe that there needs to be more time spent before we get to the Big Reveal.The change in character in parts of the game, from the bright and cheerful flowery fields to "The Scapegoat Level" for lack of a better term, that was startling, and that's got some merit to it.So I'll play it, of course.  My wife caught me playing a bit and will probably have me start over, streaming as I go.  I've got a couple weeks off so I might just do that.It's a fine game so far. Though it won't be to everyone's taste, but I kind of go for the weird and ambitious sort of thing anyway.
