_childDocuments_.review: I want to state this first - BLACKTAIL looks great in the trailers and looks really fun with the gameplay that is shown in the trailers also, It genuinely does. I thought I'd have fun playing it because I like the story of Baba Yaga. I also waited almost 2 years to finally play it, I'm more than positive I got it apart of my Humble Bundle anyway.The question now you may be asking is this - "did you enjoy it?" or "is it worth it?". Well, honestly... no. It felt like I was on some sort of drugs when I began the game. Below I will explain my opinion and let you know why I think it's not worth it so let's get to it but first a small disclaimer!  ⚫So my main issue so far is this - in 3.5 hours of playing, I have felt confused, lost even. One minute I am in a "dream" the next minute talking to giant talking mushrooms and the next I am talking to a "voice" in my head that sounds WAY better than anything else in the game.⚫The "2D" goat puzzle segments are just... not needed. These felt like "padding" to add more time onto the game. Who want's to play as a goat when the game is being advertised as "one-of-a-kind blend of intense archery combat"... will my goat be able to hold a bow and show us this "one-of-a-kind intense archery combat" later on?⚫While playing and you listen to the dialogue you will notice that words are mis-pronounced at times. I can understand "accents" but come on... she speaks CLEAR English and this feels like a butchering of OUR language. If "us" "english" speakers done that to ANY other language (with an accent) we would get crucified.⚫The enemies seem to be "copy and pasted" everywhere as they seem to respawn the moment you turn your back or walk a tiny bit away. ⚫The Voice Acting is not the best. The cat sounds like a Japanese stereotypical "deep voiced" english crossover. Your character "YAGA" seems to struggle with English words at times. The "mushrooms" sound like pre-pubescent teenagers... the only good VA in the game was the womans voice in your head... why does she sound so CLEAN, so CRISP... so... angelic in your ears?!?!⚫The so called "one-of-a-kind blend of intense archery combat" is a CLEAR lie. I can name a few other games that have "ARCHERY" combat that feels better and MORE intense than this. Far Cry Primal for instance. Horizon Zero Dawn (and Forbidden West), Crysis 3... The Legend of Zelda: BOTW (and TOTK). This is HEAVILY falsely advertised to me. Nothing is "one-of-a-klnd" with BLACKTAIL, if anything the combat is DULL, boring, repetitive, sluggish - EASY. ⚫The open world is very poorly designed. It was "linear" with very little in terms of exploration. To call it "open-world" is a bit much. Areas are tight, nothing really hidden hidden. ⚫The story is NOT interesting at all. It's the same thing over and over again. The same rock that needs to be moved. The same mushrooms that need to be talked to. The same "voice in your head" telling you what to do. A story is supposed to keep you wanting more, keep you at the edge of your seat.⚫The game does not feel rewarding at all when you complete quests. You get rewarded... wood... to... craft... arrows... thanks I guess. Not only that, any material you collect is used to upgrade "PERKS" but first you need to find "magic pages" to unlock these perks. So the game locks "perks" behind "collectables" behind "side quests" behind "exploration"... wow.⚫The price. For a "INDIE" game, they are asking for £25 for it and, IMO, in no WAY, shape or form is BLACKTAIL worth £25. It should have been £15 (or £20) for what it offers. ⚫I liked the woman talking to me in my head. Her VA is very well done compared to a lot of other VA's in the game.⚫The game looks very nice. Vibrant even. Each area I visited looked right out of a fairytale.⚫I didn't experience any bugs, crashing, FPS drops, stutter e.t.c. So what I am saying is - it seems to be very well optimised. Before I get crucified - I know it is a "INDIE" game. I know they need to start somewhere but you have to be honest here, making a game that confuses the player, has lack of "explanation" of mechanics at the start of the game and calling it a "one-of-a-kind blend of intense archery combat" seems VERY falsely advertised to me as I can name games that have BETTER archery combat that is TRULY intense combat.So, after all that is said - would I recommend BLACKTAIL? No. For £25 I could name COUNTLESS other games that are superior to it in almost every way that is either cheaper or the exact same price.After boring me senseless for 3.5 hours, I am no longer going to play BLACKTAIL as it just is not fun. Not good. Not... enjoyable for me anyway. Everyone has their likes and dislikes and I think Blacktail I just don't like. PERIOD.

_childDocuments_.review: BLACKTAIL is a wonderful indie addition to FPS/RPG hybrid scene. Somewhat less intricate than ruling titans of the genre, but in a good kind of way. Its smooth, artistic, and ingenious FPS experience with impactful RPG-lite elements doesn't compromise on anything, and stays true to its heart, the looks, the technicalities of gameplay, and the remarkable takes and twists on Slavic myths and legends.I love the graphical whimsicality being a bit more restrained, as compared to other pieces in a similar family of visual styles, e.g. Tim Burton's, or American McGee's, that kind of thing. While I absolutely adore the latter as arguably a pinnacle of heartfelt creativity, I believe they may come as somewhat off-putting for audiences that don't quite understand them. BLACKTAIL, on the other hand, is developed in a 'toned down one step' kind of way. I find that shrewd because this way it can also attract audiences that want more streamlined products, and still be deemed as poetical and artistic.It plays a lot lot like other, classical FPS/RPG hybrids in terms of 'explore, shoot, cover, dodge, use skills, explore, loot items, talk to the denizens, craft your potions and ammunition, etc.' In general—combat and quests alike—the game revolves around moral choices. For example, you must mind not hitting innocent animals occasionally appearing during combat with baddies; decide what to do with trapped birds; shoot bee-hives to acquire more honey (crafting ingredients) or appease the bees to gain moral points but get only a little of honey in process; decide which warring factions of termits and bugs you help, etc. The overarching message is 'you reap what you sow', and you will feel and hear the outcome from your environment and your inner-voice quite a lot. Literally. There is an inner-voice narrating some parts of your journey, but I won't go too far as explaining this, so as not to spoil anything. It's part of the game's charm and a result of your actions and exploration. Play the game and you'll see what I mean.That leads me to the last but not the least thing I must write here: the voice-overs are an absolute treat!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this, but I was unable to get into it.I absolutely hated the way the story was told.The main character speaks like you already know what's going on, and there's so much gibberish language, characters, and motivations thrown at you that don't make sense in a very short time. It felt like the first quarter of the game was just gone and you were dropped in the middle of things, and like it was translated from another language to English and something massive was lost along the way.Being in a fairy-tale style does not mean that you can just say something happens even though it makes zero sense in context - you still need a narrative through-line where things happen because of other events, not just one thing after another for no reason. Narratively, that means that nothing is of any consequence since things can just be whatever the writer wants whenever they feel like it; it's poor storytelling. This is especially a shame since the things I read outside the game sounded like a great setup.It also commits one of the largest sins in game writing: nonsensical naming. You know those games that name their "Magic" something like "Syndrochronic Destabilisation"? That. They do that with everything and it becomes a mess to keep track of. There's no reason for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, where to begin? If you buy this game hoping you will get to be an evil witch with cool powers and make people suffer and laugh while learning about Baba Yaga and maybe doing a second run through while trying to save her soul... Well, let me tell you how wrong you are.The story revolves around Yaga and her sister Zara, Yaga is an outcast and she's bullied by her friends, protected by her sister who is just much better than her.There is a witch named Baba and she seems to be the reason why everything goes so badly around there. Gosh, I really have a hard time not spoiling the story because it was terribly disappointing.You will spend your time running after your lost "friends" to learn about your past while seeing a story develop through the tales of a black cat with a weird accent.The morality system is not that important in the end (except for a few things maybe? Not even sure the morality change cinematics because it's all pretty neutral in the end, what the morality will change is the npc shrooms you will befriend at the very begining)But the good thing is, along the way, you will meet a few mushrooms which talks are rather fun and they make the story pretty nice and will bring you into a weird tale about honey. (forget about the cat and all that)Now, the game is divided in 5-ish regions (Well, 4 since the first one is pretty small and is the tutorial region), you will progress through the story as in a metroidvania, not an open world.1 main quest and 3 secondary quest in the 3 main regions, the last region beeing the "grand final" in which you can't do much. The hut of baba yaga is the central hub where you will upgrade your powers.Now, the gameplay is pretty disappointing, you have a bow and that's it ! It's the only weapon you will have through the entire game with 3 different arrows, a normal one, an honey one which slows and damage over time and a crystal arrow which applies crystals on the enemy, firing a crystal arrow on him after that makes him explode, the more crystals on him the bigger the damage... Then you have a broom which attracts the attention of enemies.You have a power to use three different ways, a single press on F and you will send some kind of shockwave in front of you, a long press and you'll use a power associated to your morality, and using that power while charging shot can release one of the three power you decide to chose in your skill tree (you can change anytime you go back to the hub)You also have two potions, one to cure poison and another one to run faster (basically)Basically, you will create all those items by "crafting" them on the fly, press "TAB" and a wheel shows, if you have enough items (wood, feathers, crystal, ...) you will craft them instantly with a single click.This system wouldn't be such a problem if the game wasn't sending enemies in your face as if you were playing doom !It was pretty refreshing to have a break from monsters. You can also meet a devil giving you temporary boost powers with some side effect, cost nothing, influence nothing in your morality path. This morality will give you a few passive abilities like getting health orbs and whatnot. When you reach max morality by doing good or bad stuff, you will have a task to accomplish asking you to do 3 things (kill a bird, a hedgehod and a fox) before being fully dedicated to path (good or evil) and you will get a final bonus which will be removed if you destroy the wrong the thing by accident making this system horribly frustrating.The skill tree isn't anything exceptional, carry more stuff, potions now also heal, more damage, faster arrow charging, more mana, ... You will be able to chose a special power and what they call a hex which can "specialise" you in one kind of arrow (either jack of all trade, honey, wood or crystal)So you will move forward, gathing ingredients for your items, gathering teeth and hearts to unlock stuff in your skill tree and most important of all, gathering lost page which basically allows you to move further in the skill tree (without those, you can't improve). The world is pretty okay-ish to bland to explore, a few cool things to find, some npc with some fun quest and winks to various things like lord of the rings or Goldielocks and other stuff.Now blacktail isn't a bad game but it's tiring and boring in the long run, the gameplay never renew itself with incredible new items as in a metroidvania, you never feel you're really getting stronger. The things you will unlock are traversal powers (to move a bit faster through the world) but nothing that will blow your mind, just another fast travel idea.There are interesting things but I feel like the devs lacked of time to develop the game more (more items, more powers, ... more fun stuff, making good and evil more impactful), instead you're left with a character who can never decide if she's evil or not even when you spend your time killing stuff to be evil. A character who's on the verge of crying when you should be an evil sorceress wreaking havoc.Recommending this game is really hard for me because I kinda liked it but got frustrated by little things which could have been improved with time. The game can feel a bit janky but I think it's mostly because the bow is the only weapon you'll ever have and the dash is limited. Otherwise, it plays well, voice acting is fantastic, music is pretty well made (nothing unforgettable but it goes along with the story). There are some really cool moments while exploring and while doing side quests but the main quest is not really what one can expect while playing a game about baba yaga.As it stands, price is okay with what you're offered, limited replayability, new game plus is included so it's a thing for people interested.In the end, I was glad to play that game but I'm happy I finished, I will class it in the "finished" title and will probably never touch it ever again and it's a good thing from my point of view.

_childDocuments_.review: For Parasight's first time game, Blacktail is AMAZING! The story is intriguing. You get thrown into this bizarre fairy tale. A mix between cute and grotesque, funny and brutal. You are Yaga, trying to find out what happened to your friends, trying to find your sister, Zora, while juggling the problem with the Roots, trying to figure out what Baba wants from you and dealing with your own personality (so to speak - without giving spoilers) It's much more in depth than that and really is best experienced by just diving in. The ending had me a little emotional for sure. It was beautifully done, albeit somewhat vague. It's nice to have room for your own interpretations BUT it also wouldn't have hurt to have a bit more explained, too. It has a nice amount of side-quests all of which I found unique and entertaining. As well as the various characters you meet on your journey. Yaga herself is lovable and timid. While The Voice is the stark opposite. I thought that was really well done and the voice acting, especially of those two, was absolutely outstanding. And the black cat - meow! The 'world' you're in is diverse and beautiful. You'll get to see four different seasons all of which are beautiful in their own rights just like the real ones. There's plenty to explore. And once I figured out how to work the teleport pillars - which I realized was their own creative way to implement a sort of Fast Travel - I was zipping around quite quickly and conveniently without losing out on the exploration part.I love all the different fairy tale tid-bits they threw in. I am amazed they could combine so many in one game. Made me smile whenever I recognized one. Lots of classics in there with little twists. The morality system is quite interesting. I tried to be Pure Good in my play through and succeeded. I had to grin each time some of the meaner mushrooms told me what a living saint I am, to watch my step and flat out told me to get out, lawful clown that I am. The only thing that irked me was the fact that for one bad deed, you really have to make up for it with three good ones. The dang birds would sometimes fly right by during a fight, and bam! Back down to Noble.. back to hunting for Anthills and what-not to make up for it. That got a bit annoying, especially towards the end as some did not seem to respawn? Anyhow, I managed. What I didn't manage was the Specialist title. I looked it up but come one.. I am not gonna kill the dang birds on PURPOSE! Can you imagine how much Good I would have to do THEN to make up for it *sigh*So, that was a bit tedious, I suppose. Although also a refreshing little side-thing. The enemies were, just like the world, a mixture of creepy and semi-cute. A few reminded me of a Tim Burton version of The Muppets. And as someone who was viciously afraid of dolls of any kind as a child, this was a trip, alright.. There's a nice variety of enemies. Nothing TOO broad or huge but plenty for the size of the game. The combat itself was probably my biggest 'complaint' - and not really even that. I just found it a little tedious, as I tend to play more aggressively with melee weapons. You do have a bow and can find some different arrows. Plus you can cast some magic. The broom was my biggest friend. But still, I did feel a little klutzy the whole time. But I am saying *I* felt klutzy. There's nothing really 'wrong' with the combat system. I also encountered no bugs/glitches and that's impressive indeed! So, all in all, I would give Blacktail a solid 8/10 Well worth getting. And I am personally hoping for a Sequel!

_childDocuments_.review: Personally this is a mixed bag of a game for me, but i do see and understand how a lot of people enjoy it. I do have to give high praise with how smart the dev team is with their spacing of the gameplay variety. The archery gameplay is pretty basic, but with custscenes, puzzles and transitioning to a 2d side scroller at times, and a boss fight what felt like every hour or so, it does a good job at not making one aspect of gameplay too repetitive. Its writing is by far the weakest part, Things in the story change so quickly to the point I dont know whats going on, it felt like they had an idea but it was in development hell in the writing department and it transformed into a incoherent mess and the cinematics are supposed to make me feel something but after a while i skipped over knowing i wont get whatever message they were trying to make. the core combat is pretty decent, upgrade tree is expansive, the game is absolutely beautiful. Sadly after the 8th hour you have seen everything the game has to offer as its just 2 hours of repetitive grind to reach the end. For a Indie studio's first game this is amazing, despite its flaws its very different game than the usual ones out there, it's worth a purchase on sale and I hope the devs take the skill from what they made here and make something even better in the future

Unfortunate.

_childDocuments_.review: budget price but AA quality!+ Beautiful "semi-open" world with interesting and colorful artstyle (sometimes similar to Alice Madness Return) + Interesting exploration with quite lot of stuffs to discover and unlock.+ Gameplay is alright but combat might be a bit tricky sometimes because of a too short FOV.+ Story is ok. + The devs did a great job at diversifying the gameplay: hunting, crafting, a moral system, even a couple of 2D platform parts. + The openworld part reminds me a little bit of Far Cry Primal (one of the most interesting and original Far Cry game!) while the story telling is something similar to Hellblade Senua's Sacrifice, but better!+ the voice acting for the main protagonists is solid. However the rest of the cast is here to remind us that this is after all a budget game. Some characters (like the goblings or bugs) seem to have been voiced by the devs themselves... Not the game of the year, but an adventure defiintely worth trying, especially for the decent price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: The story is very fun, one of my favorites.The combat is less fun. I feel like I never do enough damage, can't run from things due to traps and degens, and during combat I often get stuck on things or slide off the map. I would still recommend it, perhaps play on the story mode that it allows you to select.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game.  The world looks beautiful and the story interesting.  But I just find myself dying over and over due to a combination of not being able to pick out enemies or traps through the foliage, not being able to do enough damage when i do and getting stuc on invisible walls when retreating.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game overall and highly highly recommend checking it out! I loved the lore with the Baba Yaga folk story. The gameplay felt smooth between your spell abilities, the different arrows you could use with your bow, the cooking mini game, the story telling between season of the game. _childDocuments_.review: The Good: I was very positively surprised by this game, since I never expect much from indie games.Story was interesting, voice acting was really good. It was fun to see some slavic myth mythology for once, the direction for the game felt very creative, big dark fairytale vibes.Combat in the game is decent, it could be challenging sometimes.The Bad: The main negative points for me was there is a low enemy variety and the side content gets pretty repetitive, and I just stopped doing side content half way into the game so it didn't kill the phasing of the main story, which is usually a problem for many open world games in general.Over all I really liked the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. It's pretty, but it's clumsy and it doesn't know what kind of game it wants to be. It's a bad shooter (but you can't avoid combat), a fair explorer game, and probably okay as a visual novel but I got sufficiently frustrated trying to play it that I gave up in disgust. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is an action adventure game where you play as Yaga, a girl who has been banished from her settlement for practicing witchcraft. Your story begins trying to find your sister and your missing “friends” who are no where to be found.The world of Blacktail is very beautiful and filled with animals and enemies throughout the world. There’s lots to explore and hidden areas that will unlock lore, collectibles, bosses, side quests, and scrolls to unlock abilities. Exploring in this game is encouraged as there’s a ton of content that is not part of the main games story. The combat consists mainly with your bow. You will have different types of arrows that can inflict freeze, slow, poison, damage over time, and your basic power shot. You also have hand magic that can deal damage and break enemies shield barriers. It’s also fun to squash hedgehogs with your magic :PYou also have dodging abilities where you can dash and avoid enemy attacks. It’s very fast and useful. You can use it while running to move extremely fast across the map.The voice acting is pretty much a 10/10. It’s so well done for all the characters in the game.The graphics are bright and pretty, the atmosphere of all the seasonal areas are well done with lots of details.I had a lot of fun exploring and playing this game on steam deck and didn’t run into any issues. A solid game to play if you like adventure games.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I'd say it's a good game, but not great. Some bugs, annoyances and sometimes lengthiness can tarnish the pot just enough to sour the meal, but I don't think you'll leave famished. It's a fairly dark fairy tale, without much explanation to anything, but to discover the world and its inhabitants is one of the main goals, so I don't want to spoil too much. The best way to know if you'll like it is to play the intro yourself, and decide if you want to continue or not.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Visually amazing. Top notch voice acting. Handles well. But oh my god the story is so dreadfully boring, Not slow burn, boring. I'm about half way done with it, but there is just nothing keeping me engaged. I feel like someone's little girl came up with a fantasy story, and the proud parent ran with it, fleshed it out and made it into a game. I WANT to love this game, but i just can't. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst i love most of this game,  some things in the game are beyond frustrating and really shouldn't have been implemented. most noticeably the 2D platforming sequences after cutscenes.it adds nothing to the narrative, the controls are clunky, and nothing gets really explained about what you are doing and what things do in the level. you just have to figure it out. its annoying because there is also an added collection system, where you lose one every time you take damage, and you don't know what will or won't as it doesnt get explained at all.all the while having to hear the main character whine and have some deep monologue.there is a moment where the game explicitly tell you to crouch to be quiet and avoid an enemy's gaze, but then fails to give you any objects to block said gaze, and running around touching their asscheeks doesn't even matter.why was i told to crouch then?this is within 10hrs of the game, and whilst i love the environment and the other storytelling elements, it seems to suffer from a lack of quality glue to put all the pieces together seamlessly.tldr; whilst the game has good ideas,some of them are badly executed. id suggest getting this discounted or via humble bundle
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with a fanciful world to discover. Mythology, witchcraft and legend all blend together to form an intriguing story. By the end of my play through, I still had not found many of the secrets, missions or places to explore. On the surface the game seams pretty basic and straight forward but there is a lot more under the hood. I really admire the dreamy landscapes and graphics. The art style and music are very cool too.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Solid indie FPS adventure/platformer/puzzler sprinkled with role playing elements like abilities/weapons upgrades and a morality system. The story borrows and reinterprets slavic folklore and while interesting, it has a tendency to border pompousness toward the end, tendency that isn't helped at all by some game mechanics being improperly explained or some choices/limitations being left unjustified. All in all, a very good game clocking at about 20h (double it if you add another run with the opposite moral choice) with a very nice atmosphere and graphics that i bet would look/feel awesome in VR. (Yes, the voice acting can be a bit cringey at times but i found it to be part of the charm)
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Minor things/misses that I didn't really mind but they complicated things nonetheless:- Combat pacing. I can see how ppl may experience problems with it, may seem clunky. But possible to manage + you get buffs later;- Res management. Holy cow, do I REALLY need to re-craft these 6 arrows every time? Can I have an option for auto-crafting those? It's already a mess with all that resource gathering. I'm that guy that clears Skyrim dungeons for junk, but even I was baffled at the system here. No crafting = no arrows = failed combat. Either increase arrow/res capacity or re-work the system, please.- Yaga being the same even while having "Rotten" persona. I don't care much, but would be good to see some reflection of this fact from the voice actor? Every Grand mushroom screams of me being filth incarnate but when Yaga opens her mouth - it's the same innocence talking. - Add Phase ability or something similar. I can easily dash myself backwards into the corner and it's pretty much death after that. I think overall combat disengagement is kind of lacking esp. on earlier levels. - Pointers to skill scrolls - please? Why this review is negative:THE PLOT - IT JUST DOESN'T CONNECT. That was the biggest challenge for me when side quests made much more sense than MC's words/actions. Mini-games were a torture for me, because of constantly trying to listen to Yaga's mumbling. Maybe it's just me, but by the end of the game I was pretty much Gameplay aspects need polishing and this game will be solid 4/5 (given that someone loves the plot as it is)
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I want to write a review for this because I think it deserves more and reviews help push the game in the aglorhythm. If you just want the tl;dr - it's a diamond in the (sometimes very) rough, but a diamond nonetheless. Get it at a discount.For everything this game does well, it also does something meh. Or sometimes even bad. First off, Blacktail delivers a world unlike any other I have ever seen. It's creative, it's colorful, it looks pretty amazing for the most part and has quite a few creatures unique in design. The hand drawn cutscenes are also beautiful to look at. All the voice actors are well cast and the soundtrack, especially the songs with female choir like vocals, are amazing and almost of Wticher 3 quality. For having only a bow as a weapon the combat feels good, the bow is intuitive to use and the game gives you a clear indicator when you will hit something/something is even hittable in the first place or not. And while it has a quite simple, binary morality system, it is very interesting to see how it was implemented. Even getting just basic resources can mean an evil or good action. Do you shoot a beehive down for some honey? Do you free a captured bird or shoot it because it's an easy target and you need the feathers? It takes into account far more than just some dialogue options which is really neat and I would like more games to do.But then come the rough edges and I think most of them stem simply from this being the first game by this studio. The open world feels almost implemented just for having an open world, because exploring it often times yields nothing but basic materials. I'll also be quite honest... I did not care for the sidequests. I did some in spring, but after that I just ignored them completely. Many mechanics are also not or improperly explained. The game told me that I can plug enemy spawners with honey arrows... in the very last part of the game, beyond the point of no return. That knowledge would have been QUITE useful beforehand. Yaga would slower suddenly sometimes in combat. I don't know why, it wasn't like with the snail enemies that slow you down and you get an indicator for that status effect, it was almost like an invisible stamine bar that sometimes ran out. Danger indicators are basically non existent and I had quite a few deaths where I simply did not know what kileld me. I just dropped dead. Some types of enemies can be very tough to spot, depending on the terrain. The voice actos are good, but then use modern terminology sometimes that feels completely out of place. The skill tree was also infuriating, because for most skills you need a specific book page to unlock it. Where those book pages are - your guess. It makes specifically going for certain skills impossible. And while the bow is fun to use, having only three kinds of ammo (one of which basically just being a "slow down" arrow) makes it quite repetitive. I could feed fish to that thing near the hut, but I never really understood what it was even for. And whiel the morality system is neat and all, you'd have to be some kind of maniac to make certain evil decisions. It would feel not only out of place to side with evil in many cases, but just plain dumb.  For every piece of light there is some shadow. I think it's still worth playing because I don't think there is anything else quite like it. And if you go for unlocking all skills or doing mor sidequests you can easily get more playtime out of it than I did. But buy it a discount. 30 bucks is quite steep considering all the flaws here. But I sure hope those guys keep at it, get more experience, and deliver more rounded experiences in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: - The game is visually appealing and the story seems to be promising. - I can also appreciate the skill-tree, which fits the game quite well - it offers enough variety but isn't too overwhelming.- However, the gameplay is a letdown because combat and character movement feel awkward, slow/laggy, and not well-optimized- There are also some other annoying aspects, such as lighting issues (with random spots being too dark/light) or an appalling cursor hitbox that only works if you aim slightly above or below the target item in any menu (which turns any menu interaction into a little nightmare).The technical issues made the game unenjoyable enough for me to ask for a refund. If those issues were resolved, I could see it being a solid 6-7/10 experience.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: BLACKTAIL is a great idea for a game that could have been better realized. I really  the world and atmosphere of the game. You have witches hut as a main hub and 4 different regions, each of different season from spring all the way to the winter. Each of them gives its own unique vibe. Pair it with the beautiful and even at times breathtaking graphics, and you can really immerse yourself in this world. The game also has quite good cast of characters, mainly talking mushrooms. They are all fun, a bit one dimensional, but it fits the atmosphere of the game pretty well.  Voice acting for the main cast is also solid.Now, we are getting into "" category and the main thing I would consider meh is a story, which for the story-driven game is weird I know :) I won't go into the details here, but I liked the protagonist, but that's about it. Plot is boring, things we do for the main story repetitive, but that's has to do with the overall idea behind the plot (we are searching for the children and each sequence of finding them is similar). Ending was ok though.Another meh is a morality. I really love it when the games let you choose whether you want to be a hero or a villain. But here, outside of mechanics (different magic and perks, different side bosses) it doesn't matter much story wise. This has its own justification in the story, I guess, but I don't like it.Now, the . And for me, it's a gameplay and mechanics. While shooting with the arrows is realized ok, the combat and mechanics could have been better in my opinion. Fighting becomes tedious at some point, you don't feel the power behind any shot arrow, it all feels artificial, but that's just the feeling I got after I played for enough time.  For the weapons, we have the bow and the magic, two kinds depending on morality of player, I played as evil Yaga and got vampire beam, quite nice ability and fun to use. We have 3 types of arrows, wooden (normal), honey arrows (slow and dot) and crystal arrows (used to break crystal shells and stack mana stacks on target which we can trigger for the explosion). I mainly used wooden arrows, there is no need for anything else to be honest unless mechanics of the enemies require it. Crafting is very simple, and I feel like it if devs were to cut it out from the game, we wouldn't feel it. And for the supper I left the  mechanics. I really hated the 2d parts, sometimes within the story play sequence of 2d platformer(?) that usually signify Yaga exploring her own psyche. This is stupid in my opinion, and it could have been cut from the game. Another annoying thing is metrics used for game completion. The game won't tell you how many times you have to do something to unlock it. Just that you have to do it "a few times". It's always like this within this game and a few times could be 10 or 100 :) It makes planning things for the completion unnecessarily problematic.To summarize this, I have mixed feelings and would give it that verdict if I could, but I can't, obviously. Instead, I am going to give it a hard recommend. It's a good game overall, just poorly realized in many areas. But the world and graphics are top-notch, and it's worth checking out just for that.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Regretfully i have to mark this not recommended currently, there are some very jarring things that ruin an overall great game.  I'll list them in no particular order. Voice Acting - Jesus Christ the voice acting was GOOD i mean it was really good (not for this type of game), but imagine picking the most jarring annoying american accent for a game based in Eastern Europe with American slang, it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful take the dialogue for GTA 5 and slap it on Elder Scrolls and that's the equivalent here.  It's not a technical issue by any means  (and i'll get to that).  It's taken this beautifully crafted world, which is immersive from the start and just ripped you out of it almost straight away.  Technical issues - these are just the technical issues I've experienced so far experience may vary.  Game looks great combat feels pretty good, but i'm getting consistent frame rate drops just running from point to point.  This was getting so bad i was unable to track enemies.   There was very little wrong with this game but it was enough to make me want to wait until it's either been fixed (the VA won't be but i can move past this eventually)  I would either wait until the performance issues are resolved or go in with some expectation it runs a bit ♥♥♥♥. But i want to stress if they fix the performance issues i truly believe it will be an awesome game overall.

The result is far from perfect, but, boy, it has soul. The Parasight did a great job in turning stories of an old witch in the woods into something very bizarre. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is uniquely beautiful in a twisted sort of way, with a well written, emotional core narrative.The combat is fun, though the somewhat hidden stamina system takes a bit of getting used to.The side quests are very much worth doing, each offering memorable experiences in unique locations. I also personally enjoyed the morality system, and I felt terrible whenever I accidentally did something cruel or good intentions in a side quest backfired.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game in every way, and I got exactly what I wanted/expected from the description/trailer. I love European folklore, and I've always wished there was a Baba Yaga game like this, and now there is! The only warning I can think of to give about this game is the following: This game's story is one of mystery, confusion, and discovering how complex/challenging things like destiny and good vs evil can be. The story is obtuse on purpose and the story bookends are open to interpretation on purpose. Don't go into this expecting a standard "good guy vs bad guy with easily explained motives/plot" that most games have, just go into it to enjoy the emotional fairy tale ride paired with the excellent art, game play, and writing. I love this game, it's of the most enjoyable I've played in the last few years. I give this an 8 out of 10, and hope to see more from these devs, they did a great job with Blacktail and I expect even better from them going forward!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: My first impressions of the game are good, the world is beautiful and magical, you will soon learn that not everything is as it seems, the story is developing slowly but there is plenty to to learn that makes the pacing well done, the game also communicates well when you are not yet ready to take something on. The gameplay has been feeling solid, the movement feels natural and flows well and generally when you die it is your fault, the only thing I did notice was that after dashing or attacking if you want to use magic it does not always register the button press or chooses to ignore it because you are not done yet with the previous animation, it would be great if it would still do the skill after the animation is done if you hold the button instead of having to re-press it.I will update this review as I get further in to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst I've not finished the game, this is the most aggressively average game I've played in such a long time. The environments are stunning, but the audio is pretentious. The exploration is great, but the combat is bland. The variety is impressive, but the bosses are repetitive. There's nothing wrong with this game, but it bothers me as I feel there's something more here, it's just not fully realised, and that is why I don't recommend playing this game.[EDIT] I've now finished the game, my initial impressions stand. Also, with the morality system, sometimes the decisions make no sense. Sending people to the underworld is apparently a good thing sometimes? I just don't get it.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I enjoyed the game directly interacting with stuff without knowing what they are or how they are affecting the morality is not a good thing. I don't wanna pray to the underworld lord or take the life of a funny bug. At least some name description for intractable things would be nice. Since there is also no save/load option you cant even try what that stuff coast/do but blindly do those things and live with the consequences. As a player who wants to dedicate to the good this is really annoying and buzz killer.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: A great game!Original mechanics and abilities, that change based on the affinity of our character. There is a variety of enemies, not too many, but each type needs to be approached differently. Here and there you'll find bosses and challenges, which are fun and yield good rewards.The world design is truly amazing, every season sets its own mood. Every time I reached a new area I was super excited to see what it had up its sleeve for me. The music is pleasant with a hint of sadness.Just the right amount of collectables and a big plus - the game will give you the means to track them, so no pointless running around. Besides, there are 3 types of fast travel!The story is based on Slavic folklore, but the backbone is timeless, and very much relatable. Childhood traumas, hardship, loosing loved ones, trust issues, coping, growth, etc.The ending is a bit vague, some may feel disappointed, but it gives way to discussions and opinions (which I think is even better, than a clear and cut ending).P.S. I love how the stars and the moon are a little bit cartoonish and stand out from the rest, they look similar to decorations one might find in a kid's bedroom - I may be digging too deep, but I think it was done on purpose to underline that we're in a fairy-tale of sorts.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: This turned into a gem of a game for me.  Has about everything I'm looking for in a little action-adventure.Collectibles, character upgrades, decent combat (actually really liked the magic-archer combo, even if it could of delved more into the magic aspect), Slavic folklore inspired story, interesting art design and world.  Not to mention the great music (ended up buying the soundtrack). It really did feel like a fairytale.  Definitely interested to see what this studio can do next.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: A truly lovely game full of adventure and curiosity in an enchanted forest. I bought this game on a whim and am so glad I did. The story is great, the characters are memorable, the voice acting top notch, and the world is intriguing and very enjoyable to explore. If you enjoy old world folklore and supernatural stories with heart you’ll love this game. The only complaints I have are that the combat feels pretty floaty until you start picking up more traits and the ‘story’ difficulty I played on is way too hard for what I consider ‘story’ difficulty. Bottom line this is a game that’s worth your time!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Semi-open world with some survival-like elements, like hunting a deer for meat, cooking and then eating it to recover HP. There's combat but it stinks, in my opinion. The difficulty is not my cup of tea. Visually, it's nice. Pretty sure your bow's appearance changes as you level it up (skills and all that jazz). Big, talking mushrooms. Check! Doesn't hold your hand I guess...I could be wrong. My brain is like mushy peas. Some light crafting like gather some wood and feathers to make arrows. Not a bad walking simulator if you turn on God mode I guess (the game is not very forgiving). Only cost me a grand total of £0.79 so not many regrets but it has ultimately failed to hold my interest at this time. I'll save it for a rainy day.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a breath of fresh air.Very interesting take on the Baba Yaga folklor story and very interesting and creative world they built.A lot of things to do and discomverSure it has it's flaws. Like movement is sometimes janky and you should avoid exploration till you unlock all 3 arrow types. But after that, the game opens up and gets very exciting.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is an interesting game. It's quite easy to get into, there aren't many systems and things to learn. You just go on an adventure based on the Slavic Baba Yaga tale. You collect several different ingredients for crafting a few potions and arrows for you bow and explore a really beautiful world divided into 4 different time zones.Enemy variety is fairly minimal. You hunt bad mushrooms, exploding bees, goblins, slimes and golems. There are several boss battles, but nothing too fancy.Most of the combat you use your bow and with 3 different arrow types. You can dodge, but it's not a very reliable option most of the time. Combat can be a bit janky, especially when fighting multiple enemies. But as a game it's not hard. I didn't like that basically everything respawns in this game very quikcly. Enemies, various flowers, items and stuff. You go a few screen away and they are already there to be your pain in the a$$ once again. Exploration is quite fun actually, but at the same time you don't discover many things to be excited about. There is a morality system, but it has no meaningful influence, except for some achievements and stuff.Some story sequences are exceptionally well done. Especially the ones where you control animals during 2D platformer scenes. I really liked voice acting, both Yaga (main character) and "Voice" were great. "Voice" character is voiced by the same voice actress as Megaera from Hades.The biggest downside is that this game can get repetitive quite quikly. Limited guidance on what to do sometimes is also tiresome. Field of View even on max is a bit too narrow and claustrophobic. In other words, it's a playable game that has no real hook.It's not a groundbreaking game by any means, but it has charm and it's good enough to waste 10-20h of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Well good! Here you certainly can.F*** that fox, f*** that hedgehog, and most importantly - f*** that stick-bug!They shall know who rules this forest.The game looks childish at first, sure, but it is made with love and care, and the story is certainly not suitable for children at all - it IS dark, and I loved it. Fear, suffering, desperation, inner struggle, even a healthy dash of humor - it is all there, right below beautiful landscapes that are ready to tear you to shreds if you're not ready to fight back.Solid 5/5 even for the full price.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't even the kind of game I usually enjoy and play, but something about it intrigued me when I saw it on sale a couple weeks ago. I finally started it today and I AM HOOKED. Such an immersive environment, with a story that doesn't feel boring or slow. It pulls you in immediately and doesn't let go. Not terribly difficult, but not terribly easy either. Kind of a lot of dialogue, but easy to zip through. They have this one dialed in! This is the kind of game you sit down with and suddenly it's hours later.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: This games has so much potential! But overall I would not recommend it.What is good?- The story is intriguing and is what lead me to finish the game. It's cryptic and the ending leaves a lot of room for interpretation. It does not explain much.- Overall the exploration is fun ...What is bad?- ... but not very rewarding. You mostly just receive ressources.- The progression system is weird. There is a talent tree, but to unlock the talents you have to find a certain item through exploration or story progression. Then you have to travel back to the main hub, unlock the ability, but this does not mean that you get its benefits. Because after unlocking it, you have to invest ressources to obtain it. And you do not know beforehand if you have the ressources for that. - Crafting (Ammunition and certain items) feels unnecessary. At some point later in the game you are bascially flooded with ressources. This makes the double-unlock progession system even more strange.- The game gives you little feedback if you can carry anymore of a certain ressource. After picking things up, you get either a pop-up or you dont. Not getting it, means you can't carry any more of that item, but you still run to collect it. Feels kind of wasted time.- Controls are a bit overloaded (played with mouse+keyboard)- General explanation of mechanics. The first hours I felt like I had no idea of what I was doing nor understanding the consequences of my actions. There are pop-ups explaining basic mechanics, but they are very lackluster.In the end I only finished for the story and endured the fruststrating mechanics. After chapter 2 of 4 I basically only followed the main quest and skipped almost all exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: A different experience of sorts..... i quite enjoyed the journeyThe storytelling, the music, the focus on duality and the creepy elements to it.... give it quite a unique feel and are executed just right.What I felt a bit lacking was the ending, after such a powerful and convoluted story, too much is left to interpretation and to pick up the pieces by yourself to build your own conclusion. That's not inherently bad, but i expected better and a more concise clarity.I also wished, given the focus and importance of the duality aspect in morality, that there would be a significant impact given the choices made..... but maybe the fact that it doesn't speaks as part of that same message.The gameplay itself its pretty solid, it's not hardcore but it is satisfying and poses enough challenge to make it interesting (again, not hardcore or anything like it)Great game and feels pretty different experience than most
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough and reminiscing on the story and gameplay while a smile is still imprinted on my face.If you like the idea of a twisted fairy tale as a game, you will enjoy Blacktail hopefully as much as i did and probably will some more, because there is also a new game plus mode. I suspect you can replay this game at least 3 times.I want more games from Parasight.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up. Its simple and cute. The game uses the same models often. The voice acting is nice. The game has a simplistic fantasy style. If your looking for a game that is not overwhelming but still has enough to go around and collect things then this is a good choice. The story is okay. The game is not very long and so i would recommend it on sale. There is a morality system(it does not effect the ending).
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay open world game with a rich dark fantasy world and plot featuring superbly voice-acted characters. The combat is strictly around direct combat with a bow with a few spells along with it, no stealth despite what it might lead to believe. Repetitive, but the story and lore are what get you through it.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a real gem from a small studio. I love the interpretation, art style, soundtrack and story of young Baba Yaga. Story and gameplay are interesting and engaging, sometimes - even challenging. There are several bugs I encountered (I had to replay one mushroom fight probably like 4-5 times as the boss was resetting several times), but nothing game breaking. If you enjoy mystical games, with amazing art-style and soundtrack, or games like American McGee's Alice, you will like this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail feels like a game that was made with genuine love and care. It combines aspects from Slavic, Celtic and Germanic folklore into a beautiful world that is both delightfully whimsical yet quite scary and disturbing in a very tangible way. The atmosphere subtly slips from one to the other, and even the lighthearted characters can be quite disturbing, or at the very least unnerving. The story and game play is simple with you going to different Seasons, sort of like regions, where there are clusters of quests to do and reoccurring characters, and you gain new abilities, namely arrow types, in said regions. The morality system is easy to follow and adhere to a chosen side, though it doesn't really effect the ending in a meaningful way, more just flavours your story, and being good or bad suits the story. Combat starts relatively easy until you get arrogant, then realise you actually have to demonstrate some form of skill to be able to deal with higher level situations, and regaining health isn't quick, situations often not having enough resources to get your health back up to max, adding to the challenge. I wouldn't say its a 'girls game', of course anyone could enjoy it, but the 12 yr old girl in me who loved all things dark and fantasy would have adored this game as it scratches that itch for a perfect blend of fantasy and dark. Its not the longest game, I completed it with all the side quests completed, though not 100%, in under 20hrs, but it felt like longer. Definitely would recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as a gift and I've loved every bit of it. Blacktail has an incredible atmosphere and a wonderful story that keeps you engaged at all times. The combat is smooth and pretty easy to get into, the enemies can be figured out how to deal with after a fight or 2. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: What a phenomental game this is, engaging combat, interesting story and vibrant world to explore. It's a story about Baba Yaga but told through a journey that reminds me of Alice in Wonderland quite a bit. Combat and exploration are its main features and they deliver, at first you will most likely be underpowered but will soon get required upgrades to even the odds.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is a little hard to write about and my review comes in two flavors: story and play. My best piece of advice is to come for the story and try to ignore as much of the mechanics and game play as you can.I'll try to keep this spoiler free.The story doesn't have a ton of surprises in it. By the time you're an hour or two in you probably have a pretty clear idea of what's going on even if it's not one hundred percent correct. That said, the story is well written and the dialog is very good. You get invested in the characters and you want to find out what happened to them. The story is heavily based in slavic mythology and it does represent it very well. The world is large and engaging with satisfyingly unconventional visuals. Most of the world is flat out beautiful. Some of the characters are a little too cartoony to take seriously but those are all very minor characters. The moral system is actually fairly interesting and you're given incentives to become pure good or pure evil. My only gripes with the system is that it's hard to tell exactly what to do. You'll be able to access special options based on goodness and what specific actions you've undertaken but the hints about how to reach these titles is pretty vague. Also, in certain cases it can be hard to tell what the 'good' option really is and the game autosaves as soon as the points are awarded so if you made the wrong choice, too bad. I had one issue where I defeated a boss and he asked me to lie to his people for him. He promises that if I persuaded the people to keep following him, he'd keep them from attacking anyone. Otherwise, they would kill him and kill anyone who came close. I mulled it over and decided the later was probably the 'good' option since it reduced violence in the area. Nope. I had just supported a dictator, lost my 'pure good' status and all its buffs and got to listen to a variety of NPCs scold me for being so stupid. Most of the choices are pretty clear and the writing is engaging, it's just in a few cases where you're really not sure what to do and the ambiguity can be confusing.My only complaint in regards to the story is that it doesn't always establish itself very well. It assumes you know something of slavic mythology. You encounter a Hut that stands on chicken legs, which anyone familiar with the mythos would know is the legendary lair of the witch Baba Yaga but to anyone unfamiliar with the mythos, the Hut looks weird but it doesn't have the same gravitas. And what the Hut is, is never really explained. You're attempting to gain power over the Hut but the reason you're doing this is never really explained either, I took it as a given that I was doing it because it would someone help me find my missing sister and just rolled with it.The combat in the game just sucks, imho. I'm sure that if you understand the mechanics it sucks less but on my first play through, I just didn't know what to do. The game does not do a good job of teaching mechanics. It explains most of them ONCE and then you're on you're own. There is a difference between explaining a mechanic and teaching that mechanic so that the player understands how to apply it. This distinction is where the game really stumbles. A good maxim for great games is 'easy to learn, hard to master.' I can teach you chess inside of an hour but you could spend decades studying it before achieving mastery. Blacktail's combat system and mechanics are very poorly demonstrated and when I picked up the game there weren't any available walkthrough or guides online so I basically had to wing it. When I first started playing, I had no idea how to restore my health. That's a pretty fundamental thing for a typical player to be confused about. I didn't purchase new skills until I was 3/4 through the game because I had completely forgotten that there was a skill tree with items for me to unlock and the game never reminded me.  One of the best examples of the bad teaching methods involves the broom. You get the broom early in the game and you'll probably think it will be very useful. However, I went through more than half the game unable to use it. Every time I tried, it wouldn't activate. Why? Two reasons: One, even though I now HAD the broom, that just meant that the skill necessary to use it was unlocked. I couldn't use the broom (even though I had already used it in combat) until I went back to base and purchased the skill. Secondly, you need to build every broom you use (single use items). If you don't have a broom on you, the technique doesn't work. Which is fine but again, it would have been nice if this had been explained. I never understood the magic system and I'm still not sure if the 'force push' thing I'm using is the magic I should be using. I haven't found anyway to change it so it's what I've got.You're welcome to dismiss these complaints as just me being stupid but I think that a game's mechanics being opaque and hard to understand is a serious strike against it.The fights tend to be pretty hard. Yaga is an archer and just about all of your foes will charge into melee range to attack you. Yaga doesn't have a melee attack as far as I know so once the mobs reach melee range you're in trouble. All of the fights were pretty annoying. I ended up dialing down the difficulty out of sheer frustration and I was still getting my butt kicked on a regular basis. Again, I'm sure there is a better way to handle these situations but I never figure it out.My final thoughts is that the game really is engaging and is absolutely worth a try, especially if you're into myths and folktales. The mechanics and the combat are aggravating but on the lower difficulty setting, I managed to power my way through most of the game without really knowing what I'm doing. I assume that within a few months, third party walkthroughs will explain the proper way to manage all these mechanics so the game will become much more accessible.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Good game.The main story is rather short, but there're a lot of side quests and collectibles (which aren't tedious) to get. It isn't really an open world game, more like a FPS metroidvania, which is cool. Took me around 19 hours to 100% it (and you can get everything in 1 playthrough). Voice acting, scenery, combat, lore is all great.My only complaint is the bosses are way too easy, the regular mobs are much more difficult.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: A really fantastic spin on first person open world RPGs. The writing and voice acting are great, and the different stories based on european folklore are really fun to play through. It really feels like your running around exploring a fairytale wonderland. The main story really pulls you in and ends just perfectly.Your main weapon is a bow and couple spells, and you have a ton of movement options available that makes you really feel like a pro when it all finally clicks. The enemy design and encounters are all really well thought out and designed. Everything in this game shines. Absolutely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding! Very stylish and full of character both visually and narratively. The voice acting is also impressive, enjoyed it a lot!It can be said that sometimes I was getting the "Alice in Wonderland" kind of vibe, which is more of an association rather than a strict description of Blacktail. The game certainly has it's own unique, quite palpable atmosphere and a nice world to explore, which doesn't outstay it's welcome, making it even better!The story is quite nice as well and, while the ending can be a bit perplexing at first and may have multiple interpretations to boot, it's more of a master stroke to me. Provided the player was attentive to what Blacktail's characters have to say, one can definitely arrive to a conclusion, which reveals quite a depth of the story in general and the protagonist's development in particular. In this regard it reminds me of "Bioshock Infinite" - not in scale, but in spirit.Looking forward to the future of The Parasight, the game's developer. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard of this game & put it on my wishlist, I figured we would see a dark & grim world. I was surprised to land in a fairytale full of colours. This said tho, BLACKTAIL is a beautiful and well crafted game. The atmosphere, the voice acting, the story progression - everything in this game is really well done. The only criticism I have to put out there is the incosistency concerning hints & lead the game offers you. I like the overall approach of giving the player freedom to find out themselves on a lot of occasions, the game struggles tho with finding a middle ground since at points all you need to do is follow the games' instrutions and at other points you see yourself lost on what to do.Overall I can only recommend this game to everyone, scoring an 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know I needed this game but here I am, 11 hours later after a first playthrough and just... I love it. It's whimsical, yet compelling. Very fairy tale, but also very personal. I like the characters and the story, and the voice was entertaining! The game is great, too. The bow is fun to use, hocuses are awesome, the different arrow types and their uses are cool. If you like zelda bosses, this game is for you! If you like drawing a bow, firing it, dodging attacks, and feeling like a real WITCH (or kindred from league of legends), this game is for you! It's charming, looks gorgeous, plays fluidly (I didn't encounter a single bug aside from... well, the in-game bugs), and it's cool. Play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on maturity and grief, viewed through the lens of an FPS metroidvania adventure. The story's roots might seem alien and strange to American audiences, leaving the ending as much of a Slavic Wonderland mind-screw as the setting, but that's a cultural gap rather than a writing shortfall. Similarly, the character growth and the morality system are far more horizontal than vertical, which is a bit of a shock to the system. A surprise to be sure, but a welcome one.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: - The game looks pretty good.- OST is pretty good as well. The issue with it being mostly that there doesn't always seems to be an active OST.- Story is interesting. - Gameplay is fun. Fast-paced and rather unforgiving, but even as a rather mediocre FPS player rarely (if ever) really challenging.- The exploration can feel quite sluggish at moments. The lack of a fast-travel system lets you experience more of the world, true, but having to walk to the same remote location several times even with all abilities unlocked hits the pacing of the game rather hard. small spoiler:  The lack of such a system in a limited open world setting like this also creates the issue of sometimes being able to get on a rock/bush, only to get stuck 'behind' an invisible wall at other parts of the rock/bush formation with no means of getting out.- While the gameplay is fun, it can become quite repetitive. A lack of enemy variety () doesn't help this matter. Most of the main story bosses were rather similar as well, but the side bosses had a little more variety.The game is fun and can keep you interested, but the repetitive gameplay along with the sluggish exploration has to be something you can overlook if you really want to enjoy it. Despite being repetitive, the combat can feel rewarding when you get better at it and the pacing is fun. The story pushes the game solidly into the recommended spot though (at least for me it does), even if it's not that groundbreaking and somewhat predictable.A cat said that a stone said to me I should give Blacktail a solid 7.5/10. There is enough in it to be enjoyable, but there's plenty of room for improvement. I'm looking forward to seeing what the developer has in store for us next!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Had my eye on BlackTail for along time due to the Baba Yaga theme it had.I was not disappointed. Graphics were beautiful & the story was great.There are multiple side quests and a Morality system that will allow you to interact differently with NPC characters. I went ahead and completed this 100% as it was refreshing to see a Morality swap item that can also be reverted so i didn't have to grind the morality to the opposite side if I wanted to experience the other side.Morality plays a big part as it will also effect your skills and combat powers which i thought was really interesting. You can unlock all of the skills and items but they will be weaker or stronger depending on if you're "Good" or "Bad"Great game and at 60% off on sale it was a steal.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful little game that takes you on quite a journey in a beautiful world. The main story takes some very interesting turns; the storytelling is plain exciting, the music is amazing, the visuals are a joy to behold - unlike anything I've seen before, and the voice acting is stellar .Unfortunately my vehement praise for the game stops at the boundaries of the main story: the side content is merely okay. It's fun and exciting at first, however you quickly realise that there's a very narrow selection of enemies the game will throw at you in the side areas, that those enemies are very one-note in how they behave, and that their design is fairly plain, especially when they're surrounded by the breath-taking vistas the game has to offer. Even the fights that seemed like they might be unique are mostly the same as all the other "unique" fights. In addition, while some of the side quests are interesting, a lot of the gameplay involved feels very samey. In short, the side content feels repetitive, though not unbearably so.A bigger pain point for me was what I alluded to earlier: while most of the voice acting is amazing, there is one voice actor (who's fairly prevalent in the game) whose work just didn't do it for me. His lines feel like they should have weight to them, but they fall flat: where sounds should be hard they're soft, and parts of a sentence that should have emphasis are glided over.Overall I still recommend Blacktail. I think it's a genuinely unique experience that's executed reasonably well, and the main story is a joy to go through. You just need to go into it knowing that it's not flawless.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Really great storytelling and voice acting. Game play can feel a bit linear but good high paced, spacial awareness in terms of combat. The game is inherently dark and you need to embrace that to enjoy the story.Beautiful artwork walks the line of fairy tale and cautionary dark folk tale. Definitely recommend for a good story-based game.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: At first it looked somewhat generic, mostly artstyle wise, but that changed relatively fast and since then the game has been consistently surprising me in regular intervals. There are some seriously beautiful environments.Sure, some elements feel out of place, like some sequences felt very unnecessary. Some elements are too clear cut, too video game-y perhaps. Good and Evil choices, resource collecting, the map is too dense with these, they are at every corner.The story doesn't start too hot for me but gets quite interesting down the road. The way it incorporates slavic folklore is great, both in gameplay and story. The story was however somewhat confusing, I am not sure I understood all of it and I'll have to look up the rest, nevertheless I like it. This might be on me, I wasn't paying close attention throughout its entirety.Music was awesome, I am talking about the folk type during cinematics, really awesome. Should be used more.As for gameplay, it's solid but not exactly fun after a while. It has legs, it could be really fun under the propper circumstances but this isn't that type of game. Crafting and replenishing resources should be streamlined, especially with how abundant resources are.The skill tree was interesting but maybe over half of the abilities require that you find some specific item for that ability which effectively locks you out of half of it, me at least, but I am a player who generally explores a lot and even I didn't find half. It' a shame because there were many gameplay altering ones there, I wanted to see more.All in all, if the game leaned more on the story it would be incredible, because as is I think it spreads itself thin. The map and regions are really big and you spend perhaps too much time in it. I decided to focus on story only after some point.The only real complaint that's worth mentioning is that there is something off with lighting. Some areas were super dark, others the light would create a weird image at distance. The gamma settings only partly helped, at some point I cranked it up near max values.But it's unique, stylish, has an interesting story, fairytales, slavic folklore, a servicable gameplay loop. So all the flaws and unneeded stuff didn't really matter, I enjoyed it and what it offered.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Dayum dude, I didn't expect such a solid game for this price, it nails a lot and honestly I think the positives outweigh the negatives heavily.They took a lot of inspiration from Kena Bride of Spirits, at least that's what it felt like to me, a mix of Enderal, Kena and a hint of Fable which is a good thing.Positives:+ It is just dropdead gorgeous, seriously a stunning looking game.+ Amazing voice acting for the most part, especially Yaga.+ Large amount of variety given the (semi) open-world design+ Technical performance was solid, everything you could ask for though could've been more optimised.+ Movement and combat is a lot of fun!+ Good length, it doesn't overstay its welcome and leaves room for the player to hunt for achievements which I did.+ It's not too hard or too easy, the difficulty seems well tuned for the most part, the upgrades can make it very trivial though.Mixed:~ The voice acting is really good don't get me wrong, there is a good portion of dialogue where you have trouble understanding what they mean, maybe poor translation or just weirdly cryptic? Yaga and The Voice were easy to follow and understand. Some parts of the voice acting also had me just not care, either taking too long or just being filler like the ants and whatnot you find and give items to.~ The story is good and I see what they were going for, but because of the weird delivery of dialogue it made it hard to keep track of at times.~ 2 side quests you unlock early on were locked because you lacked and item you get later on, you can only really find this out by attempting the quest and figuring out you're wasting your time trying to progress.Negatives:- The environments suffer from its visuals, the grass being too tall so it's hard to see what's on the floor (enemies, loot and other bits) for example, things can be a bit difficult to see at times.- The collision on objects is annoying, getting stuck on things and dying because of that is not great design, not everything needs collision.That's all I can think of, the Mixed and Negative points I brought up didn't ruin the game at all, some frustrating bits that could've used some more polishing/playtesting.I think it's like 10 bucks on-sale and for that price it's an absolute go and get it game.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Finished my first playthrough. It's a good game.Firstly, BLACKTAIL's tone. It's a silly game. It has wacky/funny characters and nonsencical (stone-cold) logic. Honestly, at times, it feels like it was designed for kids... but swearing and adult themes like death and depression make it an teenager-adultish game. I do think that the tone is kinda all over the place, but it didn't bother me that much.The game's setting is  interesting. You can find many different influences, like medieval europe and nordic themes. It keeps the game varied and it all blends quite well.The story starts with this young masked girl, Yaga, who has left her village to find her missing sister. All she has is a bow, a gauntlet and her mask... and a mean voice on her ears. The premise is simple and, to be honestly, quite predictable at times. It's themes have been explored before, but it might still make it relatable if you deal with loneliness/finding out about yourself.  Anyhow, the story does it's job and kept me interested, but it didn't blow my mind. The game has some interesting symbolism and good storytelling sections, though, at times making you feel like you are reading a well written book. Made me feel goosebumps sometimes.The gameplay is dynamic/mobile, but slightly janky at times. You have this cool spell that reflects/pushes away enemies, but it's kinda hard to tell how far it reaches. After playing for 18 hours, i still can't use it precisely, and i use it all the time. The game feels too easy at times, but it has some weird difficulty spikes (screw you, DRATHEFFKHA). Besides that, the gathering mechanic (you know, gathering matherials and stuff) is satisfying, the menus are easy/intuitive to use. The game encourages exploration to find new skills and interesting/wacky/silly sidequests, you can take your time to do them all.Oh, the sidequests. They are well done. You can find this larva guy. He's like "excuse me ma'am, i need to decompose bodies... help". Really cool guy.Later on, you find this little hut. You try to open the door and... nah. you can't. You actually need a licence to open it. So you go find these huge, bureaucratic spiders, to find a licence. To open a door. To a stupid little hut. Yeah.The morality system is ok. Done before, choices "matter", in the sense that you get powers/changes of dialogue depending on what you do, but nothing too substantial. The choices are fun, though.The voice-acting is great at times, cringy at others... overall good, though. Some pretty funny lines. Made me laugh out loud at times. The world design is superb. Each corner of the map represents a different season, so you have variety and some uniqueness to each section. Personally, i was in awe of some of the structures/landscapes in this game. The game's world is it's strongest characteristic.The graphics are pretty well done. BLACKTAIL has this fantasy design that fits the wackiness quite well. Not like, triple A graphics, but pretty good.The songs are cool. Some are quite good, most are just serviceable. The audio design is fine. Nothing too special, but it fits the game. No complaints.TLDR: So, is the game worth it? If you like amazing world design, sections of good storytelling,  wacky characters/situations and dynamic gameplay, sure. The story is 50/50. You might like it a lot if you find it relatable, but it's themes have been explored before, so you could find it predictable. Choices don't matter that much, but they are fun. Some good songs, good audio. Voice-acting good-amazing most of the time, kinda cringe sometimes.Personally, i think it's worth the price.
