_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are great, story is interesting, but has gamebreaking bugs that were reported as far back as April that are still unresolved, so I was forced to get the game refunded.As some people don't seem to understand what GAMEBREAKING BUGS means, gamebreaking bugs are those where you get to a situation where the bugs halt your gameplay and or ability to progress the game.You don't "laugh them off" and go on and "don't refund for that", this is exactly why you should get a refund, you received a broken product.This game has audio bugs that with certain chipsets and CPUs will cause the entire game to lag severely (single digit framerates aka unplayable), where normally high framerate would be normal, then start fragmenting and doubling up all the audio for the rest of the game. This happens almost instantly around water areas (which are numerous in this game).This bug was reported as early or even before April 2022 and was left unresolved even though several people supplied videos showing what happens, together with their hardware specs.

_childDocuments_.review: Thought this game was silly to begin with, just a kinda goofy open world game, but the more I played I developed a few gripes.- Though it's not clear where this game is set, the cast is a weird melting pot of accents and dialects that kinda clash against each other. The mushrooms and the voice in your head sound like Americans / Brits. The cat, which is really jarring, sounds like a stereotypical Russian / deep Japanese accent, and for some reason seems to have worse mic quality than everyone else? Pair that with some of the characters struggling with pronunciation which is just odd in any setting, and the voice acting alone took me out of the story.- There is a morality system inbuilt in the game, which are USUALLY bad in most games I've seen. Basic stuff like "Help X instead of Y" or "Kill the bird in the vines, or spare it" are what you can expect for most of your choices. But then there are some instances where I questioned which answer to a prompt would side with my alignment. There's a quest in the game where you are given the option to handle a monster that is lying to others for power and influence. (Should preface this by saying; this character, and his followers, are enemies) You can either; Snitch on him to his followers, leading to them LITERALLY TEARING HIM APART, or, you can further his charade of lying to ACTUAL monsters, which will stop them from attacking you ever again. Which option do you suppose the "good" choice would be? The "good" answer is to let his followers ACTUALLY MURDER HIM while you listen. The takeaway is that lying justifies murder :D. Also the morality system is VERY fragile. You of course have tiers to your evil degeneracy or your pious goodness, the maximum of either require tasks to be completed upon having enough "good or bad juice" in your system. Now, you'd assume that after you've dedicated yourself to one side of the coin, and doing the prerequisites for reaching the highest tier, you'd be locked into that angle, right? Nah. Your max tier morality can be broken and sent back a tier by making the wrong choice in dialogue...- The combat is marketed as a "one-of-a-kind blend of intense archery combat", the store page says so in the second sentence of the description. While yes, the combat is "one-of-a-kind" (to my knowledge :p) with it's blend of bow stuff and quick magic moves, it is FAR from intense. Every enemy encounter just involves you kiting enemies around while you pepper them with low to medium damage toothpicks at an arms length, or doing measly tick damage with one of your spells. Bosses are pretty much immobile, except for the copy paste mushroom fights. When I fought the boss mentioned in the last point (the fella who got ripped apart), I genuinely stood still and just volleyed arrows at him until he stopped moving, which I might add, took a few minutes.Realistically, you'll want to go into BLACKTAIL expecting a goofy game, cause it is! Mashing m1 with no arrows left so you pluck at your bowstring like a guitar is silly. Holding down your spell button and whipping your hand around a flock of birds and watching them just plop out of the sky is funny for a while too. But as you progress, the game starts to take itself too seriously.And that's where I began to lose interest.Got it in a humblebundle so hey thats neat!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to leave a review even though I haven't fully beaten the game if the map is any indicator of progress, this is going to be an action packed game. But I wanted to leave a review for the nomination trophy badge because I nominated this game in several categories but it really deserves best game or story rich!I unfortunately would probably be done with the game by now, but a windows update had halted my progress. I wish I tried upgrading my system to Windows 11 or doing something different that could have helped. But I had given up trying because I had gotten into  Disney dreamlight. Bleh. After being so bored with the Disney game that I decided to see if this game would work again, it did! So for anyone having issues, just keep trying, and go to the discord with any issues. Look it up in the community section or they have a website as well with a link to their discord. They offered to help me and everything but luckily it fixed itself! On to the game... It's AMAZING. I don't have a system that can handle the graphics on high, I have to play on low, but even on low it looks great, and I can see from screenshots how great it can look on something besides a laptop, which is what I'm using afterall. Can't wait to get a desktop.The voice acting and the story are both fantastic. Really drew me in and even though the story can be a bit hard to follow at times, re-watching the clips on YouTube all together helped me understand the story a bit better. The gameplay is fun, exciting, and immersive. There's so many different options and upgrades, spells and attacks, ammo type variety, enemies and bonus' are all to the brim in this game. When I took a break and came back, it took me quite a while to get back into the swing of things because there's SO many commands and options. But the game explained it all so well as I went along, I hadn't realized how complex of a controller mapping I had learned for this game. Impressive! The characters are all so cute  quirky and interesting! I love seeing who I'll be talking to next and what smartass things they have to say to me. XD The mushrooms are the best. _childDocuments_.review: I never do reviews of games, but this game seems to be a sleeper hit and it's truly an amazing game. There are so many hidden secrets you'll only ever find by actually exploring the open world. The main quest is actually very confusing at first. But that fits because even the PC, Yaga, is confused about what is happening. The main quest very quickly gets deep and strangely uplifting while still managing to be dark.  The side quests range from being quite silly in an amusing way, to being down right intense.The morality system rewards you for really sticking with your chosen path. It's not terribly open and is kinda black and white, but mechanically, it definitely has an impact on your playstyle.The combat is rather enjoyable with a variety of enemies being thrown at you that, once you start getting higher numbers of being thrown at you, makes you start having to think rapidly and use every tool the game gives you to keep yourself alive. At later levels you'll get tools to deal with some enemies you couldn't touch too early in the game and it encourages you to go back and explore past areas some more for the hidden gems or skill pages/ hearts. Don't sleep on your magic either. It seems weak at the beginning, but it becomes a fantastic tool if you learn to use it correctly. Personally I'm just sad there's not much I haven't done yet left as I wish I could keep experiencing new things in this setting for a long time to come. The ost is also a joy to listen to and truly sets you in the correct mood for the setting. I really encourage you to get the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I tend to enjoy open-world action RPGs. And although I can't say I've historically been very interested in folklore, I do have an abiding love of the Russian realist authors (Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, etc.), so I thought perhaps something in  would appeal to me.I tried repeatedly to get into it, accumulating almost four hours of playtime (according to , the full game can be completed in eight hours), but unfortunately the game just never grabbed me. I found some aspects of the gameplay to be intriguing, like teleporting with the shimmering blue flags and fast traveling using the black cat, and I loved the visual design of the Hut and some of the enemy models. I also had fun with the "Peewee" boss fight.But much of the time I was just aimlessly wandering around, picking up sticks and feathers and shooting bobok shells off of tree limbs. I got lost near a field of poison mushrooms around the point in the story where players meet the character "Boruta," and this is where I finally put the game down for good.Perhaps if the combat had felt a little smoother or if I had been invested in the story and curious about what would happen, I would've persisted. As it stands, however, I might recommend players to try a Bethesda-published  game () or  if they're looking for an FPS/ARPG with satisfying story and combat.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely phenomenal. The game supposedly should take around 15 hours from start to finish but for me personally I anticipate spending closer to 25-30+ hours with it just because I prioritize exploration and taking things slow rather than moving right through the story. It keeps intrigue up by introducing new terrain or enemy types right when I start to think 'huh I wonder if there will be any other enemies', and there are such a variety off abilities and mechanics within the game that leave me wondering what else will come next in a good way. The open world puzzles are fun and not so linear that you can't go back later on down the line and explore again with new knowledge and tools.The boss fights are fun and very much puzzle focused in that there is a certain kind of gimmick to each one that you either need to figure out or manipulate to win, but you can also brute force your way through it if you have enough upgrades and materials to keep crafting up. Both dodging and sprinting come in very handy, and I personally changed some button mapping on the keyboard to organize it better for myself so it is flexible in that regard as well.The pinecones, or Boboks as they're called in game, are really not all too difficult to find. As long as you are looking around your surroundings while going through the world, you are going to find lots of them, and you ought to be looking around just on account of how beautiful the game is in terms of graphics. If you explore, you will find an abundance of materials needed to both craft and upgrade, and the game is very forgiving when you run out of materials too, even on the 'harder' difficulty which I have been playing at. The game runs smoothly and I've not encountered any bugs or glitches.The visuals in the game are intriguing as well as beautiful to look at with a very pretty drawing style that I think sets it apart as a unique game, as well as a interesting take on something many might have heard of at some point in their lives. And while others may call the story predictable, I personally was left asking myself how things would go from point A to point B given what you learn early on in the game.My favorite aspect of the game overall is by far the morality system. A lot of games have implemented this sort of feature and it's easy to overdo a morality system, but the game isn't so cut and dry in what is morally good versus bad. There were multiple times where when faced with an issue, I did something thinking it would help just to find out that there was another option that would have been far more helpful. Another huge bonus to the morality system in Blacktail is the fact that your abilities change and alter according to your morality, allowing for replayability but also a chance for you as the player to cater your abilities to how you want to play the game. The dialogue between characters as you make decisions is so so juicy too regardless of what sort of choice you make because it serves to either make you feel bad about your decision or entice you into making a bad decision next time for the excitement of it all, which I think is a fantastic way to interact with the player's choices.The upgrade trees are extensive but clear, the character design is fun and phenomenal, the voice acting is wonderful and each one carries a lot of weight in what they're saying in that you can tell people who truly love this game worked on it and with it, which I think is another bonus as well. I was personally shocked when I learned this game is indie and came from an indie developer because it's on par with many AAA games nowadays, and looks just as good if not better than some of those games as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I fell in love with Yagas voice and her character and the dynamic between her and The Voice is fun to listen to and you can really tell how Yaga is developing throughout the game. All the other characters have distinct and interesting personalities as well. The art style looks wonderful and I especially like the atmosphere of the different seasonal areas and how the mood changes from area to area. The design of the collectible toads in particular are really creative and they give some useful buffs and gameplay features. For example one of the toads gives you a location of a treasure each time you activate it when you return to the hut. The story telling sequences in the form of picture book scenes are very fitting to the fairy tale setting and the general style of the game. At the beginning of the game I thought the game would develop mainly into a walking simulator because the distances you have to traverse were pretty long and you could only walk/run there but with more progress you unlock different ways to get around much faster such as the cat to return to the centrally located hut, the blink arrow which can teleport you to statues that are targetable and teleport stones which link two set location with one another.During the game I found that the respawn time for some of the enemy camps are sometimes very fast and sometimes very slow. I couldn't figure out what triggers the respawn of the enemies because they were all over the place. It certainly was very annoying when they respawned too fast. Some of the enemies felt very repetitive and annoying namely the Will-o'-Wisps but luckily they can be pacified by earning one of the three titles.The ending is a bit confusing and leaves many questions open to interpretation. It also seems like the decisions for your morality don't really impact the ending from what I can tell and from what I've read from others because I completed the game with good morality and people who completed it with evil morality had the same ending as me. I don't particularly mind that good and evil morality get the same ending I just wish the game would've explained some things a bit more in the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made with the purest intentions. And, as they say, the road to Hell is paved with them. So you have an indie game that is full first person, single player and narrative driven game. No microtransactions, no shady mechanics, no nothing. Just a pure game that the devs and the artists put the heart in it. And it shows how much love went into that game and for me that's enough reason to recommend it.But of course there are a ton of shortcomings. An open world and exploration that doesn't work and in the end you will treat it as a story-driven game. A morality system that has consequence except where it matters in the story. Side-quest that are optional but I didn't even bother because of the bad open world. A combat system that has interesting ideas, but terrible execution. A leveling and survival system that kinda work but also feel optional so you might just ignore it. A story that is interesting but its pacing is weird. I could complain for hours, but I'll be honest. I would rather complain about an honest game with pure intentions, than have a game that is trying to rob me of my time and my money, even if it has all the merits in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played one hour so far, so obiously you should take the review with a grain of salt. One common problem i have the older and thus more games i play, is that the worlds ingame often dont fascinate me anymore. Often when i play a new Open World RPG i often come to the point of "Yeah i have seen this world in this game only that it was implemented better."  What sours my experience is that while new games might have engaging gameplay and an memorable and interesting story, but the world itself doesnt really fascinates me. Its more of a sandbox where hopefully interesting stuff happens, rather then an object of awe and fascination itself! The World of Blacktail is different. In all of my 20 years of gaming did i ever experience a world that feels so similar yet so different. Like a beautiful fairytale..that is also very dark at the same time. I would recommend you to take a look on the many trailers of the game that you can see here on steam and ask yourself, if the atmosphere that the trailers practicly bleed is one that intrigues you or not. If yes then i can only recommend you to at least give the game a try. Because at least i love it! I cant remember a game since Pathologic 2 where the world itself fascinated me so much, that i had shivers running down my spine! The amazing music, mysterious story and quite nice graphics make the feeling of wandering through the world perfect! That is why, even though i havent played the game so much, i can already full heartly recommend you to try out the game yourself!

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to like this. I'm from central Europe, so Slavic myths are something I love to see represented. But this... You choose in the beginning if you wanna be good or evil. Then you can change that by helping/harming NPCs etc. Some skills are depending on your  morality (and I have no idea what happens to them if your morality changes). And some actions are blocked - you can pick up (and kill) a stick insect, if you're evil. If you're good, Yaga will just say "I'm not gonna kill it". But killing a deer for meat is perfectly OK...What pushed me out is combat. You have a bow and some magic skills. Holding your bow slows down movement. Drawing a string takes three to five business days even for a "quick" shot. Charging a shot needs to be planned weeks in advance. Your magic skills also take forever, as does turning around. With a boss that burrows underground and emerges elsewhere, it just sucks. I fought soul-like bosses that were more difficult, but not in this idiotic way.Thanks, but no, thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I am Baba Yaga. I love all animals and wildlife. When I kill birdy I become evil. When I help hedgehog take apple I am good. But hang on a second. There is this majestic Deer. Hmmm. I will kill him because I am hungry and that's fine because I am hungry. I hate plant based food anyway. Who eats green stuff or veggies? It's for peasants. And when I kill this huge beautiful deer I will only take a tiny slice of meat out of it for dinner and let the rest go to waste. Because I love you deer -we are the one and I love all animalsOnly I see it as ridiculous? I wanted to kill a bird instead so she could eat it and leave the deer be. And that was considered evil. Plus bird's body just disappeared after hitting the ground. Tormenting the deer with 7 arrows, chasing after it through the forest and ultimately taking only a tiny tiny bit of meat out of its dead body was considered completely fine.EDIT: I gave it another go to see if maybe I will like it down the line. And the answer is no. I do not. This game is pretty and graphics are beautiful. Voice acting is done right. But everything is so exaggerated. Enemies are silly monsters which appear and vanish into thin air. NPCs are overly literate they just talk so much and also many of them just vanish after they say their long piece. _childDocuments_.review: What can I say - I enjoyed BLACKTAIL a lot! Its visual is amazing, quests are simple and fun, quite a big map with minor activities to complete. Crafting is kept to minimum and combat relies on bow and arrows. Meet Mushrooms - main NPCs. They talk a lot, swear and even flirt, can drop buffs, and will be your first enemies. Initial missions investigate honey situation, where fairy creatures show they bipolarity, rough identities and force you to make decisions, which will shape your path.There are few more interesting objectives to achieve (tower defence from peculiar depiction of Snow Whites), awesome references to discover (dropping a head into a well in the dungeon, huh?!), and even hidden mini-games to win. So, please, do explore a bit.Choices affect the game. Balance is fragile af. One wrong dialogue and your careful "imma be a goood guy" operation goes to drain. Killed a stick bug in a mindless button smash? Oopsie. Fed a hedgehog? Pat-pat. Is that what you wanted? Carry on and see how the Forest responds to your presence now. Complex and dragging system, honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: A tough review to write, I really wanted to like this game. Theme and potential for story are all there, and it's such a cool world idea to explore.Story: the writing is atrocious. Feels like teenager fanfiction in the way the dialogue is paced, the overreactions, the hilariously unrealistic turns of phrase. Every cut scene takes me out of the world, it's one of those games that you say to yourself "I'm in this for the beats, just ignore the characters and their comments. Summarize them in your head or you won't make it through." The voice acting is quite decent, actually. So it's not delivery. Sound/Music: It's fine. Forgettable. I haven't played in a few days and don't remember anything about it.Gameplay: It's just not tight. Arrow shots feel weak, the majority of game is running in circles trying to collect the same two basic materials to spam arrow creation, and at least in the first hour and a half, very little interesting combat opportunities. level design is extremely limited, the maps are extremely constrained. Jump mechanics are not clean, and it's possible to get stuck in places as you attempt to explore, which are encouraged by the hidden chests scattered about. Theme: The only redeeming quality, as the concept is interesting but just can't support a bad game on its own.I bought the game for $10, unfortunately it just wasn't polished enough to warrant that price.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a love-hate relationship with this game, because on one hand it offers a quite nice fantasy world that is different from the usual orc/elf/dwarf stuff, but on the other hand this game keeps annoying me more and more with doubtful game design decisions the longer I play it...Let's start with the fairly mediocre gameplay: Your only weapon is a bow with three types of arrows, of which only 2 are actually useful against most enemies. You also really suck at being a proper witch, because you only have two spells, one of which is a pretty useless "push" spell similar to the "fus" in Skyrim, which allows you to push some small enemies away from you. The other spell is a "drain-health" spell that allows you to heal yourself by sucking an enemy's blood, but it is pretty useless in a boss fight and against most tougher enemies. The only other option to heal youself is to collect some berries from a bush (if there is one around) or to collect some healing orbs from fallen enemies, the latter of which is only available after you have unlocked it during gameplay -- there are no other healing spells or potions, so in consequence you will be wandering around the map looking for berry bushes quite often. So if you hope to become a powerful witch worthy of the name Baba Yaga, which can turn the world inside out with powerful spells and wicked potions, then you're in for a major disappointment.Then there's the enemies, each one of which falls into one of the three following categories: boring, annoying or frustrating. Some enemies can only be hurt by that drain-health spell, which makes them a real pain in the *** -- once I have been fighting some bat swarms in a cave for almost 10 minutes. The only good news is that Yaga is a fairly fast runner and running doesn't use up any sort of stamina, so I have turned to simply running past most enemy encounters instead of actually fighting.Next is the savegame situation: The game does save automatically sometimes, though irregularily and unpredictably. You have to use some "save shrines" which are scattered across the map to manually save the game. These save shrines are scattered over the map and sometimes you find two shrines within three minutes, but sometimes you might wander around an uncharted part of the map for half an hour without coming across another save shrine, which can be really unnerving when you accidentally fall off a cliff or into the water.Then there's the skill system: Yaga can learn new skills, but most of them require you to find a "lost page" (aside with some crafting resources) in the game world before you can unlock them -- so if you happen to be unlucky enough to run past one of those lost pages, you won't be getting that skill upgrade no matter how long you keep playing. To make things even worse, some skills do not only require a lost page, but also require that a skill of a lower level has been unlocked previously -- possibly also with a lost page. In other words: if you miss a first-tier lost page skill, then you will not be able to unlock a follow-up second-tier skill even if you find its lost page. This happened to me on two occasions and I had to tend to a walktrough guide to find the missing lost pages...The game does not employ a "proper" fast travel mechanism, but it only allows to teleport to the hut (which is your "homebase") by "using" a black cat and back. Moreover, there are a few teleport-stone-pair scattered around the map, which allow you to teleport from one stone of the pair to the other one. Even with these stones, you still have to do a TON of backtracking and running around forth and back through already visited areas if you want to finish all side quests, which is really tedious.Next are the dialogues with the NPCs, which are extremely tedious and full of "eeermmss" and "ooohss" and "wells" and stuttering and mumbling -- I have started skipping pretty much all dialogues after the two few dozen times, because not a single NPC can get to the point without painfully stretching the dialogue. Thankfully, there aren't that many dialogues in the game.Finally, there's the good/evil morality system, which allows you to solve different issues in a good or evil manner (somewhat similar to the Paragon/Renegade system in Mass Effect) and if you dedicate yourself more and more to become fully good or fully evil Yaga will be rewarded with certain useful perks. I really like this morality system and I have decided to become a fully evil Yaga, but there is a problem here: In several of the main quests you have to make a good-or-evil decision to finish the quest, however, the game does not tell you which of the two choices will be considered good and evil, respectively, and in about 30% of all cases the game's view of which choice was good/evil did NOT match up with my personal view (You might think that  is always evil, but the game disagrees . The frustrating part is that the game also saves automatically right after you have made your choice, so even ALT+F4 rage-quitting the game cannot make that choice undone. If you intend to play this game and you care about becoming either fully good or evil, definitely have a spoiler-free walkthrough at hand to figure out which of the choices and actions are considiered good or evil.Now after all that complaining, you might wonder why I gave this game a thumbs-up, and the answer is simply that even with all these annoyances and flaws, the game still kept me motivated enough to finish the game along with all the (rather boring) side-quests, so giving it a thumbs-down would simply be unfair. In total, it is not a terrible game, but it does not deserve more than a 7 out of 10 in my opinion.If you intend to play this game, definitely watch/read a "Things I wish I had known before playing Blacktail" video/guide, because it might spare you a lot of unnecessary frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: People are complicated.There, you don't need to play the game anymore.But, you should?In a game that plays as a parody to the moral binary let's rejoice in the fact that it has a lot of good and a lot of bad. How ironic.Or, maybe it is neither and it is just "a game".Ha.Do you believe in good and bad? Right and wrong? The game wants to know. In swoops the grey clouds to say that we get to decide. Just don't say meh about something someone put so much work into, amirite?Blacktail is a dazzling display of ideas. Some of them work, like the homage and humor. The delightful side quests. The brilliant voice acting.Others don't. Like the storyline about relativistic morality. In other words, the main quest means well but misses the point. To summarize before I devolve into angst about people who fear to judge and be judged: The side quests rock. The combat is repetitive, but serviceable. The game is short and respects your time. It has loads of fun ideas and likes to play dark twists on fairy tale classics.The mushrooms are lovely. Talk to the mushrooms.There are secrets worth seeing. They will bring a smile to your lips.How can we judge others? The game, like so many tales of mud, says that we can't. Nice blanket statement, yo.But, you must. You must if you believe in life and fire and light. You must if you believe in choice. In health. In growth. Perspective and context.Objects don't need our validation. We make them more than that. This game does so marvelously.So, despite itself, I say this game is good. Not Meh. Not grey. Not just a game. A good game. By and by.Have fun, think about things. Ignore the ambiguous cat, no matter how sultry his accented voice lines. Remember that you get to decide many things, and sometimes you will be right, and sometimes you will be wrong. But you will always be you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot going for it. It does tend to buck the trend for games of it's style. It's a first person rpg, but not like Skyrim. It's more like an RPG was built on top of a dedicated first person shooter game. The result feels unique, but familiar. There's a lot to do on behalf of the denizens of the forest, and you do get a choice in where your moral compass points, and your moral alignment will have an affect on you both mechanically and narratively. The premise of the game is great. I love the idea of playing out the origin story of a forest hag. Yaga is an interesting character. Her story is compelling and witnessing her growth is fun and cathartic.I do have two minor gripes with the game design.1: It's not always clear how a decision will affect your morality gauge. Things that seem beneficial will net you negative morality. In some cases, I still don't understand why after having finished the game.2:The skill tree requires you to unlock nodes by finding hidden pages. Pages unlock particular abilities, and there's no mechanism in the game to point you toward things you want, or clue you in to how much you want them, because you can't see what they do until you have collected them. Often times these skills are prerequisites for other skills, creating choke points on the skill tree without any idea how to unlock them. Once a skill is unlocked, you still have to purchase the skill using another currency. This seems unnecessarily complicated. I think one or the other would have sufficed. To do both is a little contrived.My gripes aside, I loved the game front to back. I considered playing it through a second time immediately, and that was before I knew that the game had a new game+ option.I highly recommend this game to fans of FPS, rpgs, fun stories, and an artistic style which I'm gonna call 'dark whimsical.'

_childDocuments_.review: A 3D Metroidvania with every classic flaw of the genre, plus annoyances from other genres as well:- No free saving.Which kills exploration by design, and would defeat the purpose of being open world, if it were open world as advertised.With 50% of the rating removed straight out of the gate, the rest will have to be flawless just to make an ok game, then bring some really good stuff to deserve a good review. Spoiler: it won't be the case.- Respawns.Cheap, lazy content; artificial lengthening; repetition simulator; Ubisoft-approved. In one word: crap.Good game design is simple: The player clears an area, saves & quits, comes back 2 weeks later, and continues right from there.In Blacktail, like in its countless incompetent models, when you press Continue, you appear somewhere you don't recognise, open the map, try to remember where you were at yestermonth, run a few kilometres back there, redoing all the chores and kills along the way, clean the area again, and if you don't die to restart the entire process, and if a game-wrecking bug doesn't make you quit and restart the entire process (4 times in my experience,) then you'll finally be able to start playing.The combination of checkpoints and infinite respawns is an old bane of gaming that tradition will never justify.And here, things respawn almost immediately.- Rotten visibility. This encompasses several aspects.There are the many areas so dark that you can't see anything, and your witch can't even cast some light or craft a torch.There are the innumerable invisible things (and respawns) constantly gnawing at your feet or poisoning you. It's a 1st person view, you can't see your toes without looking down, and if you do look down, then you can't see the other enemies and hazards.There are all the little creatures (mini-quest givers) that you can hear nearby but need to locate by physical triangulation or near-pixel-hunt.There is the illegible, useless compass; you must open the map any time you want to know what you are facing.There are the tiny, unseen creatures you keep killing as collateral damage, things you'd never want to kill, screwing your morality, proving that your choices don't matter.- Constant garbage collecting and crafting.The chore of choice of the survival genre, here on steroids.With petty capacity limits, so that you can never be prepared, must craft all the time, for anything, including in the middle of combat.Your skill progression doesn't deal in skills much; mostly in reducing said limitations. An alleviation of punishment is not exactly what I'd call a reward.Anyway, you spend as much time reading GUI numbers as looking at the world.- Timed choices.That's right, the stupid that erases your options while you are reading them and decides for you; the most asinine design bug of all times; the anatomical proof that a brain can be made of gray anti-matter, the seat of anti-intelligence.No reloads allowed, as you remember.Minus 100% to my game rating.And of course, like every game that defecates on player agency, they sell it with the laughable "choices matter" keyword.You can't teach stupid, but you can blacklist stupid.- Interminable loading times.That's not related to a genre, that's just poor coding. Acceptable at the launch of a session, not when all you need is to respawn where you just died.Combined with the flaws above, there are many places where you'll spend 10 times longer looking at a loading screen than actually playing.- Weak combat.Aiming is awful and slow; mobs are either too small to be seen, or speedy bullet-sponges; ammo is limited, as mentioned earlier; lures as well; ammo types are few and funless; moving backwards is ill-advised, what with all the poisonous hazards crammed all over. (Ever heard the saying that, in Australia, everything tries to kill you ? Let me tell you, Australia is a haven compared to the Russian countryside.)The early boss fights are better than average, then they shift to the cliche multi-stages grindy garbage, often in cramped spaces, feet stuck in the terrain while you try to dodge waves of spawns and falling trees.Not a fan of grind, I switched to story mode. It's not a true story mode. You still have to kill things every 3 steps forward. The bullet-sponges are slightly less spongy. The game is still a grindy borefest, best suited for a 1995 console, but without the cheat codes.Any positives, any redeeming qualities ? Not many; not enough, by far.It's pretty enough, but the storytelling is a bit of a mess; it's confusing, and delivering the exposition during the action, like during the 2D side-scroller, was a terrible idea.(Did I mention that there is an entire sequence of 2D platforming, complete with mini-bosses ? Now I did. Too long to be called a mini-game. Completely out of place.)Also, verbal indications for quests are often unclear; sometimes outright misleading.One feature I do like: idols you shoot at to get teleported near them. Neat for traversal, I instantly thought. Then my first shot landed me on a mushroom for instant poisoning. Sigh. Anyway, it's still good most of the time.One feature I love is the ability to place your own markers on the map. That's an old idea, yet very few games implement it, and this one does. If only the rest was on par...Not much else, I'm afraid. Nothing that remotely repairs the daft damages of miserable mechanics.My award for biggest disappointment of 2022.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could have been great however... it has a lot of problems. First off no game should have a fight in which a NPC yells "kill yourself" for no reason. Second this feels well made enough that you shouldn't get stuck on a random piece of wood on the ground which makes you die in a fight however I've found it happens a lot, maybe I'm a scrub but somehow I don't think that's the case. Third the gathering system is very similar to horizon zero dawn but fails to include the quality of life aspects that make the one in horizon a part of the game you can engage with if you enjoy it and for the most part ignore if you don't need all the goodies. I don't want to have to exit a dungeon, at the boss fight, to gather sticks to be able to have enough arrows (the only way to attack) and then redo the dungeon to be able to retry a boss fight that could have been done first try if I had enough basic attacks. I'm saying that as there is no other options. Crafting systems can be great but this one could have been done well but in it's current form feels like a fantasy game is making the user have a worse experience for the sake of realism. Yes I'm saying that a fantasy game made it's self worse to make itself feel more realistic, how the game designers didn't see this as a flaw I don't know. Honestly there are more problems but if you try the game you will find them for yourself and I would recommend trying a different game, there's a good chance it'll be a better time. This feels like a game that could have been a 10/10 but the creators forgot that it's supposed to be fun and instead made it tedious and frustrating. I'm probably going to play through the rest of the game at this point but know that it's going to be a grind that will make me swear way more than is reasonable because I want to find the great game behind the bad game design.

_childDocuments_.review: So like, the gameplay is a blast for me, a lot of exploring and slow, almost plodding, but very fun, combat. The problem, which I don't see being talked about, is that they're using symbols and characters from old Germanic folklore without understanding their origins.This is steam, so I expect a backlash of 'funny' clicks to increase my engagement metric when I post this, but I gotta tell you something that's not a big secret: There was a LOT of antisemitism in the time and place that these fables are taken from. And I mean a LOT.I was starting to feel sketchy about it before I reached the first major boss, and I was talking about that to my audience, and then the very next character we see is a short, pudgy fellow with a massive hooked nose, whose main personality trait is that he is a greedy little person. Also he's literally the devil. Like I said, antisemitism. If you know, you know.There's two schools of thought here: The first is that the devs used imagery from this place and time without having any idea what they represented, which is irresponsible, but unfortunately, common. The other being that the devs are antisemitic, which is terrible, but unfortunately, common.So no, I can't recommend it. That desperate stank colors everything else in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly good game. Interesting for about two-thirds of it's runtime, while being really not that interesting in the last third of the game. If it is something that I really need to address, it is the pacing of the game. To put it in perspective, in the first third of the game, you are learning mechanics, enemy attacks, hazards and how the game's morality system works. Great start, interesting characters, and decent story development. In the second third, you get new abilities, more ways to traverse terrain, a lot more combat options and overall keeps the game alive. However, after you beat the boss of the 2nd area, you gain the "last important upgrade" the game needs you to have in order to finish it and...it kinda falls flat after that. Yes, new areas and puzzles are now available in the first two areas. and that is about it. One new type of enemy is added and....now you have to explore the largest area of the available ones, whilst not really feeling that good exploring the same area. This, third area, feels too big and bloated for its own good. I noticed that I spent more time here just traversing it rather than enjoying the surroundings and trying to find secrets, like I did in the first two areas. Because of it, I started to get bored, fighting the same enemies, doing the same types of puzzles, and doing the same linear exploration. Another topic I want to address are the characters. Outside of the main character and the Voice that follows you throughout the game, not a single other character was interesting. Most of the other characters, especially the "evil-moral" ones, were really dull and not interesting to listen to after like 10min of their talking. Almost everything else is pretty good. Areas are interesting and different, combat is fun for the most of it, and overall game felt good. A warm recommendation for any indie lovers. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good one for sure.  It nails the faerie tale vibe better than really, anything I can think of.  Mind you, I mean Grimm, not Disney.  It evokes the spirit of the fae very well throughout. There's a certain whimsy behind the characters and setting but both are also intertwined with an undeniable undercurrent of darkness.  That dichotomy is an inextricable part of nature itself, and obviously where the fae and thus faerie tales get it from.  These things aren't good or bad, just or cruel, they simply are and the game leans into that theme quite heavily. A tad heavy-handedly at times at that. The game does have a morality system but it's far less bothersome than other games that implement them.  It's easily manipulated and doesn't boil down to "evil people take things but good people don't and help others instead" like so many do.  Plucking the eyes from flowers is a good deed but giving medicine to the ant queen is evil, for example.  Indeed, certain actions even invert their moral value, depending on your choices and suffice it to say, the "good" characters frequently don't live up to the descriptor, and vice-versa.  Did I mention there are reusable shrines that grant you the benefit of both moralities at once?  You do you, this isn't Star Wars and its tired, rigid and exaggerated notions of morality.The combat is fun, though as a fan of archery in general, I'm absolutely biased there.  There is no melee option or guard, just your bow (with a few different arrow types), an evasive dash and some short-ranged magic, plus a plantable broom that can draw ire for you.  You don't have to worry about headshots or aiming for weak points, save for enormous bosses, so instead combat is about positioning, timing and situational awareness. Your ammo is quite limited but your material reserves are more generous and there's nothing stopping you from crafting from the quick pie menu mid combat so realistically, resources aren't a problem unless you're really squandering them while simultaneously not snagging things along the way.  There's no XP so many fights are strictly optional.The map is divided into a few major regions, each representing a different season.  These regions fit their season's themes and aesthetic and as a general comment, are quite scenic and spacious.  The world feels good to traverse and explore, and there are a few fast-travel options you'll unlock as you go along to help as well.  It's populated by a variety of animals, insects, talking mushrooms, sentient stones, spirits, a demon or two and of course gnolls.  Sadly, not the hyenafolk you might think of but lumbering, stony, ogre-esk creatures, some of which wear red caps to impersonate gnomes.All in all, the game's well worth a go if you're looking for something different.  A setting that hits familiar notes but draws from mythology less commonly seen in media these days, beautifully realized graphically and accompanied by well-done voice work throughout and solid combat and action to differentiate if from the walking simulators.  It does what it sets out to do well, ties its components together nicely, doesn't overstay its welcome and is priced fairly.

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a first-person action-adventure game developed by the Polish studio The Parasight and published by Focus Entertainment. Released in December 2022, the game follows Yaga, a young girl exiled from her village on accusations of witchcraft.She must navigate a dark fairy tale forest, hunting down memories of her past that have come to life as spirits while searching for her missing sister: Blacktail draws heavily from Slavic mythology and folklore, particularly the legend of Baba Yaga.This has introduced many players to aspects of Slavic culture and mythology they might not have been familiar with.: The game features a morality system that affects gameplay and interactions, encouraging players to consider the consequences of their actions.: The game's unique art style and atmospheric world have been praised for their beauty and immersion, contributing to its positive reception.Blacktail has been well-received for its storytelling, art, and innovative gameplay mechanics. It's a beautiful indie gem that has made a mark in the gaming community.Taking the light path in Blacktail can be pretty rewarding. It’s interesting how the game intertwines morality with gameplay, making every decision impactful. The way it plays on the themes of innocence and corruption, set against the backdrop of Slavic folklore, is really something special.Totally, the voice following Yaga in Blacktail adds a layer of psychological tension. That voice keeps you on edge, reflecting Yaga’s internal struggle and the darker themes of the game. It’s an intriguing way to convey narrative through audio design, making you feel the weight of Yaga’s journey. It’s details like these that really make the game stand out.It's fascinating how a voice in a game can play such a pivotal role. It's like the developers wanted to keep you constantly questioning your actions, adding to the psychological depth of the game. That passive-aggressive tone really creates a sense of unease. Even though it didn't sway your choices, it probably made the experience more intense. It's those layers of subtle storytelling that make games like Blacktail so compelling.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is somewhat of a gem, that you first have to uncover, before it reveals itself to you. While the gameplay never goes deep and some would describe the morality system as shallow, it does know what it is doing. The gameplay is deep enough to keep you engaged, but the story and characters are the true draw. And even the morality system, which is somewhat part of the story itself, and also not (no spoilers), only feels outdated, because it is supposed to be this way.In the end, you get a fun game, that varies between thought provoking plotlines, over questions of morality, down to straight up humor and grotesque dialogue. The only downside I could find is, that a lot of the best content is in the side quests, that many will miss, because you need to explore without much guidance, and when you play all side content and explore everything, the game gets too long for its own good, but those are more nit picks than actual issues with the game.I can highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is... Different, to say the least. It honestly reminds me of a bit of a Walking Sim with (generous) crafting elements to it, and centered around a morality system. You do more than just "Hold W" or "Solve Puzzles" of course, it's closer to a first person shooter that is heavily story based. And overall, it does work out pretty well. But I do have some gripes with it:The biggest one is First Person + Platforming. Unless you have snap ledges (Dying Light series) or a climbing system closer to Breath Of The Wild, try to limit the amount of platforming you have in your games. Especially over instant-death pits when you have 0 control over yourself when you hit the jump button. Mix that with two speeds: 'slight bunny hop' and 'leaping across brooks' it can be hard to tell which one to use at a glance and your progress depends on it. There's not a Lot of this, but when it appeared I just instantly groaned and questioned if putting myself through this was even worth it.Morality. Normally, I don't really care too much about this being added into games, and adding some bonuses to each side does change things around a little. However, what's infuriating is that final one on each side: "An extra life/Second Chance after dying." Sounds fine on paper, good even. Considering some of these jerkwads tend to spawn under the map/in objects. The issue lies in "If you gain anything in the opposite morality, you Instantly Lose It." Several times I earned that bloody thing only for a freaking bird to run into my AoE/Crosshair in the middle of a fight. Shattering what felt like 10+ minutes of work because you need to 'Re-earn your Blessed Gift, even if the wildlife is suicidal'. Be it birds, bees, foxes, Stick-bugs were the freaking worst. Just sitting on the walls where (venomous) spiders were hanging out, only to be caught in my Hocus and get cleared out along with the eight legged freaks. With so little saves inbetween, this was beyond frustrating....And Do Not Get Me Started On "The Specialist" Title. If you know, you Fishing KNOW....Two last things: Special Arrow Powers: (Spreadshot being your first one). They're good, but you can only select one at your home base.  We can carry multiple kinds of arrows and such, why are we limited to one of these abilities? The stances or whatever, sure. I get that. But there were several times where I thought "Oh, I could really used This ability here instead of the one I currently have" or "What I currently have is just useless on this enemy, I wish I had That other ability to deal with it." Even if you had to change it through a pause menu or something, whatever. It's so strange.And the last one: "Walking while in combat."  Just make us auto-run. What good does walking in combat do? Holding down the run button all the time. Just... Why?Okay. Done with complaints. I really needed to get that out.What Blacktail REALLY does well is honestly the story and setting. I liked it a lot. At first glance it almost comes off as a Survival game: managing hunger, hunting around and such, but it quickly ditches that. The ideas they have are relatively good, the voice acting is okay. I honestly liked a lot of voices (some were more annoying, but I think purposely so). Skipable cutscenes/dialogue, plentiful resources so you don't always feel like you need to gather stuff all the time. There's a lot of little things that the game does well and I'd say makes it worth it. If the trailers look fun to you, and it's at a good price, it's a great game to try when you're inbetween/waiting on other games.

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail presents a captivating story, keeping you guessing till the very end. The narrative is carefully crafted, leaving room for interpretation and offering rich lore through the Grimior book, which serves as an in-game codex. If you take the time to explore this lore, many plot points become clearer, adding depth to the experience.The gameplay in Blacktail is straightforward yet engaging. You wield a bow, enhanced with magical techniques called "hocus," allowing for unique combinations such as poison or stunning effects. The moral alignment system adds an intriguing layer to the game, where your choices push you toward good or evil, unlocking special bonuses based on your path.The world design is compact and thoughtfully constructed, allowing for quick traversal without feeling overwhelming. The map system is user-friendly, with options to add pins for revisiting areas. Quick travel options become available as you progress, and certain areas can be accessed by shooting arrows at totem poles for instant transportation.Skills are easy to understand and are earned by finding parchments through exploration or side quests, with "teeth" serving as the currency for upgrades (along with a small amount of resources as well). Although grinding is an option, it's not necessary, as bosses and chests respawn, offering additional resources if needed.In summary, Blacktail offers a well-balanced experience with a strong narrative, enjoyable gameplay, and a world filled with secrets to discover. The developers' attention to detail is evident, making this game a must-play for those who enjoy a mix of exploration, lore, and moral decision-making. While there is some repetition in enemies and optional grinding, the overall experience is highly rewarding. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite a fun but messy game.The world design is fantastic. It's a rather big but still limited map (in size) but so dense and filled to the brim with interesting stuff that it feels bigger than it is. Exploration is really fun and interesting. The game looks great too, with nice art style and graphics.But...I played this game from start to finish, and still don't know what the story is. I didn't even understand the conclusion at the end. Maybe I didn't pay enough attention.CHARACTERS TALK TOO MUCHIt's common in indie games. All that babbling makes my ADHD brain lose track of what's being said, and I honestly have no idea what the story is about. This is the first thing I find messy.Due to the above, I also don't understand some of the game mechanics. First, there are dolls to collect. I have no idea what they are about. Are they part of the main quest? Collectibles only? Why are quests categorized in the four seasons (winter, spring, summer and autumn)? Beats me.COMBAT IS BADLike others have said before me.It's not possible to heal during combat unless you find some blueberries, and those become extremely rare in some areas, just like the resources for making arrows. Frustrating. There's also some fantastic mechanic (sarcasm) that makes you move in extreme slow motion, making you an easy target for all the hoards of enemies that already outnumber you, that are also able to melee you (an ability you lack). Did I say frustrating?BUGGY AUTO SAVEThe auto save is inconsistent to say the least. But it's also buggy. While playing the game and making progress, the game claims that you can save said progress at shrines. But after following a long path, defeating a boss, walking even longer, defeating difficult foes, and finally activating one of said shrines 30 minutes later... That's when you think you are safe. But no. One path I followed ended at a pretty steep cliff, with the protagonist commenting on what was below. So it was clearly an important location. It looked as if it was possible to jump down to a ledge further down. But the hit boxes thought otherwise and I fell to my death. The game ignored my last attempt of saving and restarted the game at the point 30 minutes before that.MORE BUGSSometimes, after killing all enemies in an area, I still get shot by arrows coming from nowhere. The only solution is to run and leave the area. Boss fights can "end" before the boss is dead. The boss simply vanishes and doesn't come back. But the treasure chest (the reward) can't be opened, since the boss isn't dead yet.Some quest markers seem broken. After going to the location on the map there's nothing there to be found. It's just an empty area.In the side quest "Until it sleeps" you are supposed to find some keys. But the keys cannot be picked up. The interact icon is just a cross when it should be a hand.The cross hair disappears randomly.CONCLUSIONBlacktail has a fantastic map/level design and a nice art style. But the problems are too many. Not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the visuals, the environment, the music, and combat was satisfying and fast-paced. I'd play it again just for that. The characters are whimsical, and the voice actors were phenomenal. I cannot stress enough how visually stunning this game is, and how satisfying it is to play.However, and I hate to say this- the story falls a bit flat.Whenever there's a monologue, it feels almost like a word salad. They're using phrases that sound cool, but mean nothing ("The ways we walk are lit by glimmers of our dreams. There are no heroes, no villains, just us"). I can see how this could be a result of translation issue- this is a Polish developer, after all, and there might be some turns of phrase I just don't get as a native English speaker. Unfortunately, the result is a fever dream of a game that checks every box aesthetically but leaves players baffled and unsatisfied at the end. But I'm going to start a new game+ anyway. The aesthetics and feel of the game alone make me want to just live in this mythical world- and maybe a replay will help me understand what on earth is going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a bit of a rough gem that earns a shaky thumbs up from me.It’s quite impressive work from a small studio. Rambling across genres, the meat of the game is exploration with Skyrim-style archery combat. The visuals are gorgeous, the narrative evocative, and the Slavic origins of the worldbuilding make it all feel fresh and different to my Australian cultural sensibilities. Even the music was of a high quality.As an environment to explore and as a story, Blacktail excels. It’s a charming and immersive reflection on grief, trauma, and family. The woodcut art, impeccable voice acting, and striking directorial choices combine to produce something very unique and compelling.Where gameplay is concerned, though, things aren’t as rosy. Earlier I said the combat was ‘Skyrim-style’, and that should give you an idea of the problem. The mechanics are just a little bit dated, combat just a little too ponderous and repetitive. You’ll often be forced to bring up a crafting menu in the middle of battle, too - hardly streamlined design.The other black mark is the length. I didn’t feel like I played through particularly quickly, and yet I was done with the main story in a single evening. Sidequests and extra playthroughs may extend that somewhat, but many other reviews cap out at about twelve hours played. That’s not a lot of bang for your buck.Still, there’s a lot to like here. If you’re in the mood for an evening or two of exploring a highly sculpted environment, or if you have an interest in the ‘fairytale gone bad’ genre, you’ll have an excellent time here - but do your best to get it on sale. The chances of buyer’s remorse are strong with this one.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its various flaws, I strongly recommend  for fans of open world exploration/collectathons with minimal hand-holding.In structure its world reminds me of that of : see something interesting, try to find a way to get there, and when you do you discover a surprise, a reward, a side-quest, or ... a strong argument to leave and come back later. The world is gorgeous, combat is fun and challenging, and progress is slow but steady. The gameplay loop does get repetitive around the mid-game, but there are enough things to do and find to keep your game sessions exciting.As for the flaws, well, it might be because the game tries to do so much that inevitably some of it would be mediocre.In particular, the story is very meh. Without spoilers—you should be able to figure things out very early in the game—I'll just say that the potential of the premise is wasted. There's an attempt at some depth, but it falls flat. Something about society and psychology and ... it doesn't stick the landing. The side quests are just bizarre, with wacky characters that are supposed to be charming (I think) but are mostly annoying. The dialog is long-winded and awkward, and it doesn't help that the voice acting (in English) is bad. I like stories, but in this game I found myself skipping through these boring yarns to get to the adventure.The game systems also get caught in their own shoelaces. There's a "morality" mechanic that feels very opaque, arbitrary, and unnecessary. It barely affects the story (and does not alter the ending), just another RPG thing to do to gain abilities. There is not enough enemy variety to make the big game world feel diverse, and since enemies regenerate over time encountering them can become grating by the time you get to the late game. And the resource economy is, well, let's just say that everything is available everywhere and you should rarely lack what you need.My biggest personal complaint, though, is about affordances. The game is spectacularly bad at teaching you how to interact with it. There are countless examples: It took me a long time to discover the controller button that reveals quest markers, or where to find the list of the collectibles I had gathered so far (it's not in the inventory, nor the journal, but ... in the almanac!). In one boss fight I was told to do something, but not how to do it. It took me 10 deaths and painful reloads before realizing that I just needed to press a controller button. The description alluded to something quite different (a common issue). Also, why does the "deflect" magic open magical things? How was I supposed to know that it would do that? Etc., etc., etc. Even the online guides tend to assume that you know how to do all the things.But enough of my gripes. The game does a lot right. It's a fun, not-too-serious romp through a cartoonish version of Slavic folklore. Quite big, quite juicy, and quite satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: "Blacktail" is an exceptional game that immerses the player in the fascinating world of Slavic mythology. Playing as Yaga, gamers have the opportunity to explore the mysterious corners of this fantastical realm, intertwined with mystical stories and legends.One of the most captivating aspects of the game is its engaging storyline. Players take on the role of Yaga, allowing for a deeper experience and connection with the protagonist. The stories from Slavic mythology are a unique element that gives the game its distinct character.Playing "Blacktail," we not only enjoy a fantastic storyline but also savor the beautiful graphics. The game's creators took great care to craft a visually stunning world, paying attention to detail and atmosphere. Every corner of the "Blacktail" world is meticulously designed, enhancing the immersion in the game.The sound design also deserves recognition. The soundtrack blends seamlessly with the game's atmosphere, emphasizing emotions and key moments. The ambient sounds and dialogues are carefully chosen, adding depth to the overall experience.The gameplay in "Blacktail" is highly enjoyable and satisfying. An intuitive interface and smooth mechanics allow players to focus on exploring the world and deriving joy from the gameplay. Also it's worth to mention, that there is a great amount of humour (dialogs with stones :D, cat and The Voice ;)).In summary, "Blacktail" is an incredibly successful game that skillfully combines elements of Slavic mythology, beautiful graphics, a captivating storyline, and excellent sound design. For enthusiasts of adventure games with elements of Slavic culture, this production is a true gem that is sure to be well-received.

_childDocuments_.review: What a feeling, it's been a long time since my last review!For those that only wants to read a brief review and a score:  this is a good game and I want to do a long review, I'm sorry!I've read other reviews and it was fun to see someone say that this game is like an FPS, but with a bow. lolI don't think that this game is an FPS, but to be honest I also think that Blacktail doesn't fit in any category.I will start my review telling that I fell in love with the lore and the dark fantasy setting. At first I had the impression that the exploration was limited since the game is divided in seasons and you need to end the main quest to access a new area and a new "chapter", but I realized only now that I'm at the middle of the game that is better to do a full exploration of the map once you are fully equipped ( in the game, these areas/quests are marked with a skull sign). I didn't do that and I tried to complete many crazy areas full of enemies and without any defence so my experience with the difficulty is not the best, but after doing that every bossfight seems easy! The combat involve a lot of dashing and dodging and not always the best thing to do is to maintain a long distance from enemies because you can be easily poisoned by a spider/a plant: is easy to be overwhelmed without even be aware of your surronding. A wrong dash can be lethal.In this game you have a morality system that will change also your beneficts and how some skills/items works ( a system very similar to the morality in Fable ). As per usual the dark path is better than the light ones, so if you are like me and want to be good prepare yourself to  be always in search of ways of healing.What I'm hating about Blacktail is that you need to farm some collectibles called "lost pages" because you need them to unlock the skills+you need to farm the mats that are used in the crafting/levelling+ you need to farm the potions that adds a new heart to your char.Yes, that's a lot of farming, but the mats are not a problem, they can be easily obtainable with a brief exploration.Luckily I've seen that there is also a story mode, but I don't know how much it change.If you're still not convinced to buy this game, I'll tell you also that one of the main voices is portrayed by the same actress who provides the voice of Megaera in Hades. Imagine constantly hearing her voice whispering in your ears...9+/10

_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend it. It's grindy (in that you have to replenish your arrows after every fight), annoying the "Good" path is massively harder in the early game to the point where you kinda just feel like you have to be evil, the combat is sluggish and you just get poisoned, crushed or killed even when to your view you had avoided whatever attack. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun. Not for everyone. If your interested in a bit of a delve into Slavic lore and a different approach to combat instead of melee all the time it'll peak your interest. Bosses were satisfying though the regular enemies can get repetitive after a while. Nice art style with mythical creatures that give you something different instead of ork or elf clones all the time. With most side quests and exploration for abilities.Main critique is the morality system is more little bonuses you want and what secondary spell you want. _childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRI think that the first 6-8 hours are great and worth buying on sale for less than half price, but for the rest I wouldn't recommend. I give a thumbs up for that and to support an indy game. I think a part of not liking BlackTail is me: I have open-world-itis. I thought it would be more linear that it is. I love the characters, the ascetic, the voice acting. I really got hooked on the story as it slowly unwinds. But - while there are stones that you can shoot at to teleport to, and others that you give a hug to be transported to like coloured stone, there is no quick travel as such, and the world being more open than not means you will be running around alot - sigh. Combine this with enemies that respawn when you leave an area, so if you run out of arrows and need to forage, there they will be AGAIN. Add to this no on-screen compass, which means you can run around in circles, heading back the way you came because of way the landscape pushes you, it's really not for me. I think a lot of people will really like the above, but I'm into games that entertain and don't stay around too long. Once I got to returning back again an again to the same spots over and over that was it for me.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: What is there to tell about the black tale of Blacktail... Well, first of all, it got me hooked, With a bit of background knowledge on slavic and central european mythology and old folk tales, I'll had a ton of fun exploring the world little (or not so little) Yaga calls her twisted home. The journey involves normalizing the weird, accepting the struggle within, overcoming it and finally... the choices. You get to make a decent amount of choices throughout the game and although most of them are pretty obviously pushing you in a certain direction, some will make you wonder, what the "right" decision will be. And by right, it's not only the choice you'll personally make, but also the choice that would lead to the morality you want to follow. The morality system isn't too overly complicated. It's also not too grey-toned, mostly you'll have the classic good vs. bad. BUT: I was surprised to see a few more "grey toned" questions, decisions and quests, which rather focused on chaos vs. order, individuality vs. society, the own vs. the greater good. The gameplay isn't too complicated, I played with a controller since that feels more intuitive to me, and I didn't have more of a trouble than to be expected from playing a first person shooter with a controller ;D It's also pretty repetative, that I can agree with other review. Some bossfights feel a bit too easy once you get some perks ready and are far enough on your path of morality. But I don't want to be too harsh on the gameplay - I'm by no means a pro gamer and I like my games casual. If you're looking for a soulslike difficulty, look elsewhereI've seen some reviews that mentioned the ending. They were a reason why I was reluctant to buy the game and took my sweet time. But don't let them fool you. While the ending is kind of foreshadowed here and there and, as I mentioned before, with a bit of background knowledge in the mythology surrounding the Baba Yaga, it may not come to a surprise for some. Still, I liked how it played out in the end. Some confusion sure occured, but with a bit of thinking afterwards, it's solvable. The team sure did a good job on the details and on how they used tales and stories I grew up with, twisted them and made me look for it. No game is perfect and so is Blacktail - but you will be well entertained. Don't take it too serious and just have some fun :)
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure what the detractors thought they were getting when picking up this gem? It's a very well put together amalgamation of different folklore, put into one story rich game! Graphics are amazing, and it has a very whimsical/fantastical feel. Voice acting is also great. I'm sure I can think of a couple cons to down for this, but they'd in no way detract from the overall greatness of this title. Put down the haters, and pick up this awesome experience!!!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: So.. Blacktail overall is a decent game. It's beautiful, has fluid combat, shares an interesting storyline, contains a good amount of exploration, and has fun boss fights! Obviously with every thing there are pro's and con's. A major issue I had with this game was healing, either I was not able to completely figure it out, or healing in this game is strictly based on finding specific flowers that heal you, and checkpoints, which all heal you very slightly, making it very annoying to heal back to 100% HP.. They also use a good/evil choices system in the play-through which I assume really only matters if you are going for 100% completion, considering I played the entire campaign and never really saw a consequence/reward for doing good/evil.. idk, maybe I didn't dive as far into that system as other players.I'm a little conflicted honestly.. this game is not bad, but it's not great either. If you have a few dollars to spare and this game is on sale, I'd recommend trying it for yourself because in the end I did have some fun, especially if you are into dark-fantasy theme'd games!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, its more of a meh game than a bad game. Some of the gameplay is good. but most of the time, it feels kinda clunky. _childDocuments_.review: Review update. Wish I could give a "meh" instead of a thumbs down.Initially the game is fantastical and creepy, both great ideas to begin with, it's not exactly what I was hoping for when I started.The game presents as a crafting-type thing, but at worst, you're looking for sticks and feathers for more arrows.The areas of platforming are awful, and I could have easily gone without them.The progression of good vs. evil is just too quick, too on the nose for me. I get that so much of the game is meant to be who actually is "good" or "evil", and you're meant to be guessing, but going down the middle isn't an option, because you get no gameplay benefits from making your own assumptions.I'm a huge fan of using a bow and arrow in video games, so at least it felt kind of satisfying there?I can't recommend this one.The game gets too repetitive too quickly, and I wish you had a larger arsenal of tools or magic.
