_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is a game that is really inconsistent in many ways, and in general feels like a partial experience. The morality system is not terribly nuanced or interesting, with most choices boiling down to murdering or not murdering a thing (and murder is sometimes the good choice). The morality system had me really keeping an eye on when it might pop up and paying attention to details so I could make informed decisions but anytime I found myself in a situation where I wanted to make a choice, and it felt like the game was leaning me towards making one, I found no choice to be made. The strongest example of this is a tragic character that turns into a boss fight. Its made very clear what the issue is, whats making it worse, why the creature is attacking you, and the boss has repeating dialogue that its hard not to read as instructions given the repetition. I wanted to help the poor thing, but instead I was forced to ignore what it was telling me and actively make the issue worse. That right there is where my interest took a nose dive because everything about the lead-up to, and the fight itself, really strongly indicated some kind of moral choice was to be made. And there wasn't. And that's a lot of the game. The morality system is also tied to the abilities of the character, something I have seen before and it never works, and it doesn't work here. Being evil boosts some things and gives access to different abilities, being good does the same. So if your play style doesn't match up to how you want to role-play the character it can get pretty annoying to constantly be at odds with what you want to do and what the game lets you do. As other's have mentioned, the combat is repetitive and sluggish. Frankly it feels tacked on, like the devs made a walking sim and realised at the last minute they needed some action. There isn't enough variety to keep it enjoyable for long, and there are far, far, far too many enemies in the game. At some point I just started running past them all and only cleared them if I knew I needed to be in the area for a bit. Its not fun, and the moment you start doing it you start questioning why you're trying to get better gear and powers when you're just running away so you stop searching for items to buff yourself and at that point 2/3rds of the game is gone. Also the game lets you look at future powers you could get, and nothing I saw made me think it would make combats much easier, or very different, which further pushed the feeling that upgrading my combat abilities was a waste. The story is...odd. Which in itself isn't a bad thing, however I was constantly feeling literary whiplash from the things the game would do. It is like there are elements from 3 different stories all competing for attention. A serious story about a young ostracised girl looking for her sister, a dark fantasy story about the strange creatures in the woods, and American McGee's Alice as written by someone trying really hard to be American McGee. You'll have a dramatic tale followed up by talking mushrooms who use anachronisms and swear. I have read other comments that claim the ending makes some of it make sense, but the elements fit so poorly together I can't help but feel any explanation is just an excuse for poor writing. Beyond that the story wasn't terribly compelling, and consists almost exclusively of chasing after your sister the whole time and doing side missions with woodland creatures that not so subtly "hint" there is more going on than you think but even the characters willing and able to be open about it are annoyingly unclear. When I first saw trailers for this game I thought it was like a wilderness survival game centred around a witch. And really that's what I wanted. I wanted to hunt in the woods, and master spells, and navigate the challenges of superstitious villagers. Kinda like a Slavic witch themed Valeheim. Its obviously not wrong they didn't do that (though I maintain their first trailer did not accurately describe the game) but what we did get is not a good experience, and feels like a too many cooks in the kitchen situation. Where everyone wanted to do a bunch of different things and it all got put in with none of it being properly balanced with the other elements, or any of the elements being fleshed out and made into their own experiences. That game looks and sounds pretty, but not in anyway I would consider unique enough to warrant buying the game just for it. And if you're here for representation of Slavic myth I can say that for the first few hours it barely shows its face at all. I'd say its the equivalent of "inspired by true events" where the word inspired is doing heavy lifting. Would not recommend at any price.

_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Would i recommend this game? If you are interested in slavic folk lore and interesting style of RPG, then yes.But after completing the game, i feel unsatisfied with what it presented.Scenery, and the sillyness of this game is sometimes beautiful, different styles and curious design sometimes that made me wonder if there is more than meets the eye.The story and the adventure becomes more and more entertaining and engaging the longer you play the game, but the combat system is very unforgiving, if you do not go for side quests, treasure hunting and maximizing your abilities, you will struggle and suffer, this world is not a friendly one, even more at the begining.With how the game function i am annoyed until the very end on how the dash mechanic has some sort of cooldown, and very often gets in the way of other interactions/mechanics if timed right. Additional lack of option to upgrade movement speed in this wild combat world where enemies sometimes glitch out and teleport into your face instead of actually jumping doesn't help.The other thing that bothered me is that this game is made by Polish Studio, yet there is no Polish Audio. The only Audio that is always in Polish is the buboks whispering in Polish, no matter what language you select, i find it bizzare. The story itself is quiet easy to speculate as you go, and i also encountered few places that are in the game just for the sake of being, and not utilized for main story at all, which is a shame. Ending has a very powerful scene and an interesting message, but the story feels incomplete.Hopefully there will be a DLC to fully expand on this experience, or else in my heart, this game will be forever unfinished.6/10 overall raiting.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice game. Beautiful story and aesthetics, captivating characters, world building to die for, and generally very well designed. The sidequests were also very fun,  written in a way that lets you explore the world. Same goes for side characters, many of whom were very unique and engaging.My only problem with it would be the actual gameplay. Fighting system was just tiresome at some point, and I didnt really feel rewarded by getting new skills or collectibles. Turned it to story mode for that reason. What mechanic was nice was morality, though also feel like it could have a bit more of impact on the actual story.To be fair, im  a little angry with myself I didnt do more sidequests as they were very good and interesting. But gameplay, mainly fighting system, tired me so much that at some point I just decided to finish it. I guess my advice to the devs would be: less enemies, but make them fighting them more engagingn and the rewards larger. Personally would have been happier with fighting some folk type monsters every hour and then to get a cool skill, than having to deal with swarms of crappy and annoying enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Slavic Lore, for those interested in that, its a buy for certain imhoNot finished yet and I won't spoil anything.I was surprised by the more lean back take it easy feeling this game gives.In other games I always feel rushed to "need to complete main story" but this one makes me slow down and look around.I like the writing and storytelling but I can also see it will not be to everyone's taste.I'd say give it a go if you are interested in some Slavic Culture and like the bow gameplay.Very reasonable prized, no reason NOT to buy it when on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a totally underrated gem. Great story telling and absolutely fun game play. I went into this game with no expectations and absolutely obliterated any chance I had of a sleep schedule even after my first play-through. I have spent over a day of my existence on this game and it was worth every second. I will probably even do a third run with the good morality just to feel what its like to be a square.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: It's been quite some time since I have played an FPS, but Blacktail's premise of Baba Yaga and bow-only combat intrigued me enough to give it a chance. And I am glad I did, because this turned out to be an excellent AA-game with polished gameplay and fundamentals, a dark and mysterious story and atmosphere and a bit of role-playing mechanics and side questing sprinkled in as well. The characters in this game were brilliantly written and voiced, which made hunting for and completing side quests that much more entertaining.As for the negatives, I guess that the gameplay loop has its limitations in terms of entertainment. You are fighting pretty much the same enemies all game and some of the upgrades can feel superficial in terms of impact on the gameplay. The morality system, despite its interesting premise and entertaining commentary, has no bearing on the ending, which may turn off some players. I was fine with it -- as I play a goody two-shoes in most of my games, it really would not have impact my decisions whether there was a morality system or not.Regarding difficulty, I started with Adventure mode, but changed to Story about half-way through, as the enemies were too spongy and samy for my liking and I rather wanted to see more of the world and the story than the fights. In fact I ran and blinked past enemies towards the end, as there was nothing new or interesting for me anymore in the combat.The boss fights were rather fun, though, and I did enjoy the three minigames after the season changes -- although I think that some people might be turned off by those, as they were totally linear and unnecessarily long at times. That being said, the music and voice acting (as for pretty much most of the game) carried me through those sequences and I ultimately had a fun time.Overall this was a very pleasant surprise and I would give this game a good 8 out of 10. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just finished the game and loved every bit of it. The choices you make are relevant to the game and gameplay in general but not in the grand scheme of things, not for the ending (and it makes sense to me personally). The story and world building are awesome. Slavic myths and legends are represented in a story-like fashion and mixed in you will also find easter eggs from westerns stories (I found a Lord of the Rings reference as well a Matrix reference). It was a blast exploring and interacting with everything the world had to offer. When it comes to gameplay, the game is fun, responsive and very enjoyable (after getting used to Yaga's different skill/arrows).
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Gud game, go play.Pro's:- Stunning, and I mean stunning visuals- Smooth and fun gameplay- Story is interesting- Enemy design is quite well and diverseCon's:- The open-world doesn't have that much to offer besides one or two (literally, didn't find many) sidequest and a few errant runs for you to do- There are one or two times where the dialog felt out of place with frases like "When ♥♥♥♥ hits the fan"- The ending is somewhat cryptic (won't say more to avoid spoilers)Tech:First startup was very buggy for me, since the game didn't seem to capture my mouse correctly and even crashing my whole system after a while. But after this the game ran beatifully, sure had a crash or two in my playthrough but nothing major. It's also quite well optimised I would say, ran on an RTX 3080 at 4K with an average of about 100 FPS.Bug's:Didn't encounter any, I only managed to get myself somewhat stuck on some geometry, but was able to get out through wiggling myselft out of there.So again the game is good, play it!
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail honestly isn't a bad game, but it does have some issues. First of all, he game looks and sounds great. I loved the music and the visuals are so fairytale-like and vibrant. I really liked exploring the world, although it got rather repetitive after a while. Characters are charming, but conversations can go on for way too long without really saying much at times. The story is also a mixed bag. Some things are cool, but it all feels a bit dragged out by the end. I liked the gameplay with the bow though, but certain 2D platforming sections weren't very fun, and they had some heavy chromatic aberration, which wasn't exactly pleasing to look at. All in all, I could definitely recommend this game during a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Ran into audio issues (lagging and crackling) after 30-60 minutes of having the game open, restarting the game fixed it. Felt it wasn't enough to not recommend the game as it may be a thing with my PC, but it was there so I'll mention in case someone else has them.Gameplay is okay-ish, not amazing but not bad either. Story is really interesting and immersive. I'd say it's worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Blacktail is rough around many edges, but it's valued at the correct cost. It's not super long, which I'm happy for these days. It looks incredible. The sound is good, but could have been balanced better. The voices get drowned out by all kinds of things pretty often. Everything else is pretty B grade, maybe teetering on A grade: story, voice acting, pacing, and the rest. There's lots to do if you care to scour the world, but traveling around can get pretty tedious since there's no easy way to quick travel around the map (there are ways to speed it up by a lot of course but it's not like Skyrim or Fallout's quick travel).If you want a fun little game that doesn't cost a whole lot, try this. Or Hi-Fi Rush.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: If you're into Slavic mythology, this game is great. It tells a nice story, though not in the best way possible. The visuals are cool, and the music is great.Where my superlatives come to an end, though, is the combat mechanics. There's just not enough there to keep me playing. It's the same type of collectibles, the same way of fighting, with the same enemies over and over again. I hate when companies hire people with British accents to play Slavic characters with names like Slavitza...It's just odd and doesn't work for me.I'm not compelled to finish the story at all, it just gets stale after a bit, but if you're into that type of game then you'll like it.
_childDocuments_.name: BLACKTAIL

_childDocuments_.review: Now THAT...Was a good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.Sure the combat may be clunky and the dialogue is lost in translation sometimes, but the voice acting, plot, interesting mechanics and amazing environmental design more than make up for it. Plus it runs very smoothly and has a good sense of humour.The philosophical tone of the game may not be for everyone, but just set your expectations right. By which I mean - the game is linear. The "choice" you make is a well-crafted plot point, for each player to interpret as they see fit. Goes to show just how powerful games can be at storytelling, when the interactivity it offers is used correctly.Set your expectations as I've said, and give it a try. You will not be disappointed. _childDocuments_.review: With a creative combat system, lovely mix of artstyles, and relatable yet completely fantastic story, this game is a very easy recommend for me. The visual design is excellent and there was clearly a lot of thought put into it. The art of the main game is hard to really describe, but the best I can get is "similar to Don't Starve, but in 3D". There are also several 2d-animated sections which are done in an astounding, storybook-esque style. The only REAL complaint I have is that the combat is rather easy. There's a bit of a steep learning curve in the beginning, but once you learn how to properly use the given tools, everything falls into place. Even playing blind, on the hardest difficulty, I found most of the combat encounters to be rather trivial. Including the boss battles. The core of the issue is that the enemy movement and attack patterns have an unfortunate combination of 'easy to predict' and 'easy to avoid' that made even the toughest battles a total breeze. Still, the combat system IS fun, although it takes a bit of getting used to. If you play on controller, I recommend that you turn the joystick sensitivity up as fast, snappy aiming really helps with the pacing.

_childDocuments_.review: What a remarkable game!I gave a shot to this game way outside my comfort zone, because I wanted to try something else and thought I would like the atmosphere, the story and the art, but I didn't expect to get hooked so much from start to finish.I enjoyed trying to make sense of this big world -- at the same time as our playable character, a young girl named Yaga -- by exploring it thoroughly and getting rewarded for the curiosity, solving riddles, progressing fluidly, that is with the right amount of difficulty to make it interesting and not discouraging, in the gorgeous scenery and its huge fantastic structures (the... special... bridge was breathtaking!), punishing hostile creatures with arrows and black magic!  What makes BLACKTAIL stand out so much would be the emotional roller-coaster, its high intensity at times matching Yaga's stress, anguish, mood swings, trauma, painful repressed memories, through rampages fueled by rejection, treason, and cruelty,  through epic battles against (her?) gigantic demons in sinister and overwhelming environments and locations, also mediated by the well-thought use of music (and its choice and composition), sounds, visual effects, the fairy tale graphics, the dialogue with that older bossy -- at times abusing -- voice following Yaga who wouldn't say its name... until the right moment to do so.I liked the ending too, it felt like ending a really good book or movie. We got to share the confusing aspects of the story with the young Yaga, and I liked there are still a couple of unresolved questions left, also consequently to how close we were to her experience I suppose, which was a great choice of point of view. It seemed to me BLACKTAIL's story is another interpretation -- as in "divergence" --  of (the little I know of) the original (if that makes sense) fairy tale, and some ambiguity is played with to disorient us... Oooor I might be totally wrong on this one and perhaps the confusion is all mine.BLACKTAIL does a superb job at positioning the specificity of gaming in story telling with respect to movies, literature and art, and might just incite casual players like me to play more and discover more outstanding games.I also hear BLACKTAIL is brand new and is a first for the developing studio, so here's to another encounter with the cat!

I loved playing this game and would highly recommend to try it if you're looking for a world to get lost in for a good amount of hours.  The game is also beautiful visually as well.  Game developers, you did an amazing job!  POSSIBLE SPOILERS: There's a huge mushroom in the fall that is a guardian of some sort, and I am not sure if/how I can continue to uncover it's secrets yet after defeating him.  Likewise, I don't think I traveled all the caves, the big skeleton and the worms intrigue me.  I did find something with an onion, and I am not sure if it's just an easter egg, or something I have yet to do. _childDocuments_.review: A great adventure in a wonderfully conceived setting!   Thoroughly enjoyed playing Blacktail and found myself getting a pleasant deja vu feeling from a time long ago when I was playing American McGee's Alice - maybe 20 years ago or so.  Both games share some common roots insofar as bringing to life an amazing world that is populated with interesting and dynamic characters that help to provide needed background about the world and story and who breathe character and life into the game.    Yaga's story is an interesting one that continues to allow the player to peel back layer after layer of her story to reveal some deeper truths as the game progresses.   The world itself is beautiful and well rendered (playing on a GTX3080) with only very minor visual issues found in the game (very occasional stuttering and clipping).  You'll explore areas that are lush with life and vegetation with vibrant and lively colors as well as other areas that are more barren or ice encrusted.   Combat requires skill and some precision but isnt overall challenging for this middle aged gamer :)   There are a limited number of creatures you will encounter and some mechanics (such as those with ice encrusted creatures) takes a little getting used to but becomes easy once you've figured things out.  There are opportunities for improvement in the game imho.  Getting around in the game can take a bit of time - the use of the hut as a hub makes alot of sense but it would have been nice to teleport from the hut to any of the black cat locations.  The game breaks the map into different areas only accessible from the hut (and gates your access as the story progresses).  Each area also has colored teleporters you can unlock that facilities travel within that area.  Still - I spent a decent amount of time moving from point A to B that while visually interesting could get frustrating after a while.   The other suggestion is to differently treat falls to your death - there are areas, though limited, where platforming is necessary and a single fall sends you back to your last save.  Other situations, like falling into water or falling within the set event area for the bastion cause you to lose all but 1 health.   Honestly these are generally minor inconveniences once you know to save first but would be nice quality of life changes.Overall if you're a fan of ARPGs, fantasy settings and a novel story you'll be pleased with Blacktail.  I'm excited to see what this new developer (The Parasight) will continue to work on in the future

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful tale of an outcast child and a mystical forest she's forced to live in. First-person action adventure with a vibe not dissimilar to the likes of The Lost in Random or the Ori series; also contains a glance or two of the masterpieces like Senua. Beautiful and thought-provoking although troubled in its very core by the affinity to the nonsensical binarism of morality and a clumsy flow during story quests.(++) The plot story is very interesting rendition of central European folklore (that is, a mixture of Slavic and Germanic). Not completely however, as there's an undeniable Victorian influence (namely Alice's Adventures), so expect a bit of generic elements that don't fit in well.(++) Beautifully-crafted 2D map that depicts the world exactly how the locations felt like when walked through. Helps immensely with recalling the correct associations with the places and thus easy navigation.(+) Very nice environment oozing with atmosphere. Although very often hard to read as it is too busy, cluttered (due to the choice of materials, asset size, light effects, etc.).(+) Great general vibe that shifts as the story moves on.(++) Very good art direction with clear understanding what benefits the product the most, that is well-aimed towards things that matter for this type game like the character's hands and their animation, points of interest to help navigating the map and so on.(+) Exploring the environment feels adventurous. I enjoyed the implementation of the whole color palette differentiating the certain parts of the map. (Although later parts of the map feel very sloppy, generic and empty.)(+) A couple of nice touches to help you feel more like a part of the world, example being an option to hide a bow so that you can act civil and embrace friendly parts of the map or enjoy higher running speed when not interested in a fight.(+) The core movement and combat is on-par with today's standard.(+) The size of the open world is not overwhelming.(--) Problematic principal design elements. The character development revolves around the questions of morality -  a concept challenging the binary outlook on us as a society. The equivocality is inevitably embedded in the story, and completely refuted in the RPG system where all of your acts are graded on a binary scale good/evil. It is very nonsensical especially as the system is based on actions that highlight this dissonance - is releasing a bird from a carnivorous plant a morally just decision? The game says so but one could argue that interfering with nature's way is definitely not the 'right' decision. The design defectively sticks to the black and white spectrum of outcomes of morality, denying the very concept of it. The moral of the story is, don't make a game about morality if you don't want to deal with what morality brings to the table.(--) The dialogues and the cutscenes (although visually very enticing) are very lengthy, overstay their welcome and undermine the flow of the game. The information keeps repeating itself constantly, there's a lot of unnecessary bloat, and empty clichés burying otherwise interesting plot. The dialogues are not written well.(--) The voice actresses did amazing overall, that is, including the main character. I really enjoyed their performances. Unfortunately the male actors are not up to par and the narrator, to be brutally honest, is abysmal. The voice actor's overdramatic tone is very awkward and his accent so strong he's very difficult to understand as his pronunciation is far too off. His toolbelt for proper delivery (in English) is very limited, it's just too small of a foundation to build upon any decent performance.(-) Optimization (didn't dig into this but it seems like the usual suspects: mismanaged asset LODs and placement count, unnecessarily complicated shader logic, lighting leaks and world partition rules).(-) Invisible collision walls have no space in a hand-crafted world.(-) Some effects and visuals can be annoying (rain effect on the screen, many materials are set up weirdly: are too flat, unpleasant specular/roughness values, some icons are too low-res not fitting the general art direction).(-) The open world would benefit from less enemies and more exploration/adventurous/story points-of-interest.(--) The marketing (esp. the trailers) shoots the title in its own leg as it is extremely generic, and is not making the title a justice. It completely misses the target audience. I skipped on buying the game twice when seeing the trailers until one time I said to myself 'What the hell, let's give this a try.' I'm happy I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my god.I don't consider myself a completionist by any means. I usually won't go out of my way to 100% a game unless I really just love playing it. _childDocuments_.review: Blacktail managed to hold my attention throughout with an interesting story, premise, and a vibrant world to explore. I found most side quests interesting and not too tedious to complete. One side quest in particular had my laughing out loud at it's dry, goofy humor. The different characters I met along the way were each unique, interesting, and well voiced. The collectibles were fun to find and didn't feel like a chore as through pure exploration I managed to find most of them without too much difficulty.With only being armed with a bow and a little dark magic, the combat did soon feel repetitive. The bosses weren't too difficult but a couple were a pain to fight. The skill tree helped unlock more abilities, like arrow types, some more powers and potions, and an increase on basic stats like health and magic, but nothing in terms of diverse gameplay which I found a little disappointing. Traversing the map can become tedious, thankfully it's not a huge map, with portal like fast travel points unlocked later in the story. Also, checkpoints are scattered about which are utilized as save as well as respawn points. The players good or evil moral stance grants bonuses depending upon witch path they choose. This can add some diversity to gameplay, however it was difficult to see what kind of impact these choices had without choosing the opposing moral choices through a second playthrough. I'm not quite sure how morality effects the ending either but through searching online forums it seems the ending you get is the same for everyone regardless of player choice (think Mass Effect 3). In my experience I found the ending to be somewhat predictable, being familiar with the Slavic tale of Baba Yaga, but also a little lack luster which unfortunately subtracted from my ending experience.Overall, I found Blacktail to be a decent game with simple mechanics and engaging story for the majority of the game. I think it's worth buying considering price. 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review I have logged 31 hours in this wonderful delight of a game.I cannot express enough how engaging this game is, it rewards you only when and if you deserve it. If you die? It was probably your fault or lack of reasonable preparation. Resource management is ESSENTIAL, and logically makes total sense and doesn't feel terribly grindy as you must constantly craft and brew different recipes. I love love love the different game style mechanics you can choose from by switching out different effects on your bow, on to how you move in game, and what boons you may have. Morality also impacts much of your game play and character, I plan to go back again once I finish a good run through and try being morally evil because I know how different the game will feel that way. I actually can't stop playing this game and enjoying this full package of beautiful visuals, wonderfully woeful story, and game physics that make me cry tears of joy. I am invested in every character, story beat and playful reference this game has to offer, what a rare treat and wonder of a game!!Honestly, it's close to a perfect 10 by this gals standards! I can't wait to continue Blacktail and all the new twists and turns it takes.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: Encountered game breaking bug towards end of the game and unable to progress and complete the game. Buyer beware.What is it?Slavic/Eastern European folklore action RPG. Novel when it comes to storytelling, full voice acting but gameplay is basic. Would give it a strong 7/10, but my current score is 5.5/10 due to game breaking bug with no remedy. An earlier save cannot be loaded due to the nature of the save system.- Bought after seeing splattercat's video on it.THE GOOD:A. Environments, world building and exploration. - Eastern/Slavic folklore is not regularly touched on in action RPGs, think Witcher light with similar influences from black book (card game). The devs have wonderfully implemented interesting maps and environments which make you go -> "Hey I want to go there". Ironically, the lack of any point of interest markers like in Assassin creed encourages players to simply walk around and explore the map (which is hand drawn and very nice).B. Voice acted interesting characters. - Surprisingly, the voice acting in this game ranges from medium to great. Some characters are played extremely well and come off as high quality/memorable such as the lead (Yaga)/ mushrooms (BB and SJ). However, the casting of some of the cast feels a bit off due to the heavy accent (narrator/cat). C. Novel story.- I haven't played a game with a story like this, almost reminding me of an Alice in Wonderland book but Slavic. I would like to see the story expanded in a sequel, like a modern (cyberpunk fantasy?) rendition with Yaga in full Adidas tracksuit.THE MIDDLE:A. Mobility. - Surprisingly, this game has quite a few varied ways of moving around, from dash/sprint/teleportation/warp and builds the environment where the player has freedom to use any/all options available. The inclusion of late game areas with "destructible" environments should be expanded on in the sequel to encourage revisiting early areas and puzzle solving.NEEDS IMPROVEMENT:A. Combat. - Ranged is the only viable option in this game and while serviceable, needs to be strengthened. Pacing of enemies and difficulty curve when you do not have access to specific upgrades make combat extremely janky and frustrating. IE: Encounters involving unseen enemies (rushman) can easily swarm players because the hit registration is hella jank and the delay + difficulty to register a pushback using F makes for a dead player very quickly. - The method of save point utilization to prevent save scumming makes the walk back to the encounter a slog depending on how far you are from the spawn point, which can be quite far away. Save point allocation around the map is either too sparse or too many for some reason. No idea why.B. Platforming.- I have not experienced such janky 2d platforming on mouse and keyboard, but maybe this was not the intended mode of play. However, it is extremely difficult to listen to the story and dialogue when you are time pressured to platform while doing so.- See recommendations.C. Inventory and crafting.- Ironically, you have an inventory screen, but don't have any notable items/weapons to use that aren't pre-assigned a hotkey to use. All materials for crafting are fairly generous, but there is actually no "loot" in this game. Not sure what the intent of the crafting/inventory system was by the devs.RECOMMENDATIONS:A. Expand ranged combat with more branches/skills/arrows. IE: Expanded skill trees to fire faster / stronger / AOE arrows and you could include even more arrows -> Teleport/portal, healing, protection, summoning arrows and a user customizable "magazine" with combo effects would amplify the gameplay significantly. You could also implement a completely real archery system with all the explanations so players can learn how archery works -> Think workbench with modifications/upgrades to the bow itself.  Currently there are only 3 arrows with a special skill F to last you 20 hours. If your only option is to use ranged combat, it should be satisfying rather than frustrating.B. Remove stealth completely or allow for encounters to be skipped. There is no point in stealth because all chests are locked behind pre-requisite clearing an area. This can be changed to support some encounters to focus on stealth and reward the player for avoiding enemies. Alternatively, some area designs can factor in unkillable enemies/turrets that forces players to stealth.C. Allow for melee combat or expanded magic abilities. The lack of other viable options to complete encounters other than spamming arrows limits the player to a single playstyle. This is fundamentally not a bad decision but the ranged combat must be extremely satisfactory to succeed.D. Separate story experience from platforming. While 2D platforming sessions were limited to a few sessions during a full game, there was a design choice to enforce a "time pressure" on the player. While this is not a bad thing, it is very difficult to focus on the good dialogue/story when you are trying to time jumps with the janky platforming system. - A way to work it in is to have "pause" sessions in between the time pressure, like a time slowdown or mini flash back to let the player experience the story and keep the platforming time pressure segments separate.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Breaking this into 3 different parts:Gameplay: Fine. Some things don't feel right - platforming, movement, how arrows fly all feel just a little wrong. There's enough variety in enemies in combat that the combat isn't necessarily boring at any point, but there's a layer of polish in it that's painfully missing. Exploration is well rewarded, usually with gameplay enhancements and sometimes a story augmentation. World: The art is great, the atmosphere is definitely "dreamy" and feels very foreign. Some parts aren't well demonstrated - the hut feels like an incomplete asset, and some animations don't necessarily communicate what they should and many are very stiff. With advancements in animation and modelling tech, there's not necessarily a reason to have such pitfalls in this department. Writing: Not great. The story just isn't very compelling after Spring, and generally the game had me frequently saying, "Stop talking." Many of the lines that are supposed to be clever simply aren't and feel forced. The story itself isn't hard to follow, but the sequencing, set up, and payoff are all contrived. Actual clever ideas are usually deflated with some quip or an uncompelling narrator. Just a note, if the narrator isn't interested... well, usually the listener isn't interested.Overall, if you're looking for scratch to your open-world (ish) scratch, this can help with that. Don't expect perfection, and maybe turn the voice volume off outside of cutscenes. Maybe leave it on during.

_childDocuments_.review: - The game plays well and the game is so far enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review:
Create the myth of Baba Yaga by living out the origins of this classic Slavic folk story in BLACKTAIL, the first-person action-adventure from THE PARASIGHT. Experience a one-of-a-kind blend of intense archery combat and dark storytelling set in a vibrant fairy tale world. Choose your path to become either the guardian of the woods or the terror nightmares are made of.

You play as Yaga, a 16-year-old girl accused of witchcraft and expelled from an early medieval Slavic settlement. When living memories of her past return as foul, walking spirits, Yaga is faced with no other option than to hunt them down in hopes of unravelling her own mystery.

name: Neon White
detailed_description: Neon White is a lightning fast first-person action game about exterminating demons in Heaven. You are White, an assassin handpicked from Hell to compete with other demon slayers for a chance to live permanently in Heaven. The other assassins seem familiar, though… Features: • You play as Neon White, an assassin plucked from Hell to compete with other demon slayers for a shot at redemption. • Collect “Soul Cards” to attack your foes or discard them to use unique movement abilities. • Compete for the best times by cleverly combining cards to discover massive shortcuts. • Uncover Heaven’s mysteries by getting to know the other assassins… did you know them in a past life?

_childDocuments_.review: Very good at doing one thing, and there is a lot of it. The actual mechanics are neat and getting from point A to B fast is really fun, at first. I think the game honestly runs out of ideas pretty fast and never surprises you or takes it's core game play beyond what you see in the first level. Sure there are a small number of weapons slowly doled out to you and enemies but how you approach each level remains the same throughout. Add this to awful dialog which is intentional I know but it still sucks and I hated every character and could not care for the story. The combination of these things made my enthusiasm for the game erode faster than expected. I still recommend it in the end cause the core idea is good fun and I put a lot of time in it, and keep coming back to it, but I don't love it and think if could of be so much more.Sound track is GOATed though.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve already played Neon White, liked it, and have a literal minute of spare time to play something similar you can try my own game: Jungle Fever . I’ve made it in 2020 and it is similar to NW in idea, I guess. Now to the review: Neon White is amazing! GOTY’23 contender for me already. It is an interesting and unique mix of 3D platformer, puzzle and shooter with an emphasis on speedrunning and sequence breaking. You run around, shoot stuff and use your gun cards as movement techniques and it is so fun because level design is top-notch. You’re almost never lost even though you go through levels with lightning speeds. The trail you’re going through is designed to be fun and challenging but open just enough so you can skip certain sections and get the sweet ace medal. And that’s not all! You can also spend some time looking for the prizes hidden in almost every level. Every one of them needs you to use all of the instruments you have and some ingenuity to get to them.  The only gripe I have with the game is its story. It has an interesting premise and world, some good character moments, an ok plot, cool setting, cute jokes (sometimes) and lots and lots of anime bull$hit. The most egregious examples are the main character, White and his friend, Violet. White is a chosen one with amnesia that is confident around everyone except women. And violet is an edgy horny brat that runs around blowing stuff up and dreaming about brutally murdering everyone. I couldn’t stand them in the first half of the game. The villain was annoying too. Later, when the tragic backstories are revealed and they all calm down a bit it’s not that bad. But jeez it was hard the first few hours. _childDocuments_.review: Just one month after its release,  got a huge spike in popularity, which caught my interest. I wanted to see what this game had in store and why it got such a huge following, so I played it. I can definitely see why this game has so many good reviews, it’s the gameplay which in itself is what mostly kept me hooked throughout the whole thing. On top of that,  voices the main character so some bonus points are added.The story starts with an assassin named , who has died in a previous life and was hand-picked from  to exterminate demons in . If  wins, he has a chance to live there for one year with a . Currently, the person who holds it is  and he has been the number one  for a few years. However, he will be going up against other assassins, some of which seem familiar to him.  is run by these people who are called , who explain they are taking part in . All of the  are sinners who did crimes in their previous lives. They all wear these masks and if they take them off, they will explode, killing them.The story for  is rather interesting in its own right and I did enjoy it. The characters all have their charm and interesting personalities that I liked. However, I need to say this:  is voiced by ,  gives off massive  vibes - What I am saying is that  is a massive  reference and I love it.Although,  does have an issue that while I myself did not really mind others may find annoying. This has to do with some of the dialogue in the game being a bit cringy. I myself am someone who can deal with some of this stuff, but others may not. I have also heard some issues with how the story presents itself, mainly with it being a VN. I personally think a game should not be judged on how it presents its cutscenes but rather on its story but that’s just me. will have you go through levels with these card-based abilities. They have a certain weapon for you to use to take out enemies. Certain cards will only grant certain abilities, so for example, the yellow card will give you an extra jump, the green one will give you a stomp-based ability, and the purple one will give you a bomb. My favorite ability card to use has to be , it was a rocket launcher where you can rocket jump and if you discarded it, it would be a grappling hook. Perfect for someone like me who has practiced their Team Fortress 2 rocket jumping.The gameplay is really fun and is honestly the best part of the game. I just want to play more of it, and this is one of those few games where you don’t want it to end. To progress through the game, you will need to acquire a certain . To get a higher , you will need to achieve gold medals. To get them, you need to beat levels in a certain amount of time. Sometimes you will get the gold rank in one try, at other times you may need to replay the levels - however, they are short so you won’t have to worry about that taking too long. You can also view the leaderboards of your friends and other people when you get certain ranks on levels as well. At the end of it all, when you beat a level you will hear a voice saying that you could do it faster.The level design is really good, it’s creative in what you have to do in the levels. You must kill all the enemies to beat the level, or the goal won’t open up. If you happen to die, you will have to redo the level from the start. As mentioned before, they are short, so you won’t feel pressured. You can reset the levels if you so choose if you want to get a time bonus or whatnot or if you mess up and get screwed over from a certain jump.You can also give certain people gifts that you can find in the levels, this will give you access to a certain cutscene and character development to them. To find gifts, you will need to find them in the levels that you play in the game. Certain characters do like certain gifts, and this will open up side quests for you to do for them and you can also unlock memories. These memories are required in order to unlock certain endings of the game.I really like the soundtrack that  has, it’s done in such a manner that I found no song bad. This is something that is rather hard to do for a game like this, only a few games seemed to even do such a thing like that. The entire soundtrack was done by  who by the time of writing this review actually has a merch store. You can buy the soundtrack for 11.99 CDN if you wish.The game has a nice, interesting art style that is very unique. The backgrounds feel empty and lifeless, but I think that’s what the developers wanted. They made Heaven feel empty and the only thing around are demons in the outskirts. I tested the game on an NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 3GB, AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor 3.50, and 16 GB of RAM. I ran into no issues while I was playing, and the game ran at a nice steady 60 FPS is a fantastic game with some really fun gameplay. I enjoyed it from start to finish and I just want more. The story, while it may have some cringe dialogue to some people, is good enough to be a story. You don’t need to be a speedrunner to enjoy this game and will have a lot of fun playing it. I can recommend picking up this title even at full price as the value is worth the price.If you want to see some gameplay for this game, then check out my video

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White manages to make fast-paced speedrun gameplay addictive rather than monotonous. Levels are fast and can always be faster, and the satisfaction of shaving a few seconds off your best time never fades. I especially like how Neon White at times becomes a puzzle game. Seeing a collectible in the far off distance and thinking "how the *hell* am I going to get there???" only to figure it out with clever & precise gameplay makes you feel like an unstoppable genius. The story, for all its cheesy anime-esque dialogue/writing is surprisingly touching with convincing displays of the vagaries of emotional connection. At the end I was fully invested in the characters and their arcs - a rare feat in a game such as this.And, of course, as everyone and their cat has mentioned, the soundtrack is *incredible*. For a game like this, where you are often constantly starting and restarting levels, you'll be hearing the same tunes over and over again. Machine Girl managed to craft a soundtrack that is both pulsatingly addictive while not being overly distracting or grating. (I highly recommend checking out the rest of their discography if you haven't already.)Overall, I can highly recommend Neon White for those interested in going fast and jamming out.

_childDocuments_.review: WE'VE GOT A SHIMMERING GEM!Neon White, a ... Heavenly Delight ... and devilishly goodNW is a fast but fair parcours-shooter with unique and highly enjoyable mechanics. While traversing a level you can pickup weapon cards that have secondary parcours abilities when you discard them (e.g. pistols give a double-jump, assault rifles give you timed bombs that can kill groups of enemies and give you a rebound boost from the blast, rifles let you dash far forward etc.)While trying to master a level as fast as possible (several tiers with different rewards), you also have to kill all enemies before you can exit. Every level takes a combination of wit & skill to ace. Collecting a level's hidden bonus gift on top is usually a parcours riddle on its own.The learning curve is as fair as the levels and not as brutal as in Ghost Runner, e.g. The complexity increases with each level and you learn to combine the different cards to constantly improve your movement. The graphics are more on the functional side: no high end structures and textures but fast and still pleasing to the eye with a coherent style. The excellent electronic soundtrack fits the game's speed and is usually more pushing than annoying.Controls with mouse & keyboard are perfect and highly responsive (you can control your jumps midair too). The anime style and story might not be everyone's cup of tea (I'm enjoying it), but even if you ignore it, you still have an excellent action game with good replayability: after the first chapter you can revisit any level and try to beat your own time or those of the global leader board (if you ignore the obvious cheaters in the top spots).Gotta love those Annapurna Interactive games. The publisher has a good eye for unique and fresh games, ranging from Indie to AA titles. I think I've got half their portfolio by now, Angel Matrix' Neon White is a welcome fast-paced addition. Looking forward to Stray next week!Comparable titles:Ghost Runner (harder and maybe more frustrating), Mirror's Edge (more bling, less ideas), The World Ends With You (similar atmosphere/setting), CloudbuiltMy system:i7 8700k, 32 GB, RTX 3080ti, Soundblaster Z, Samsung 870 EVO SSD.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is an fps-platformer with puzzle elements.You go through various obstacle courses as fast as you can while killing every enemy. You find different weapons to kill those enemies, but you can also discard them to use alternative moves. Each gun has a unique move like double jump or dash. Diabolically simple concept, but it works perfectly. If you've ever played games like Celeste or Doom Eternal - you know what the game flow is: you run, you shoot, you jump, you dash, juggle your weapons, do many other things but most importantly do them really really fast without stopping. This game is all about that and believe me it IS really really fast.After you've finished the level you will get the score. There are 4 medals: bronze, silver, golden and Ace which is the highest one. Since the level is so short (they usually take less than a minute), since you most likely didn't get the Ace medal on your first try and since you almost certainly have noticed a way to do beat the level faster, why not try again? And that's where the game truly starts to shine.You start experimenting to get the better time. And the game is absolutely ready for you to do it, since it was purposefully designed with that in mind. Level design in this game is phenomenal. Each level is a complex structure where developers have left many different skips for players to find. Some major ones, some smaller ones, some weren't even intended by the developers but still work. Exploring the level and figuring out how you can use your limited resources to improve the time may feel like an actual puzzle sometimes. There is no better reward in this game than getting a new record after finding another trick to optimize your route. But if that's not enough you can compare your time with your friends or other players around the world - the game has a leaderboard. Levels are very short and you move very fast, you truly in a state of flow when you play this game and finding different ways to break a sequence, skip some part of a level, do something out of order, cut some corners and so on is so easy and so satisfying - replaying levels and getting better time each time in this game is simply addicting.If anything this game is a speedrunner simulator. You don't have to be good to move fast in this game, you move fast whether you like it or not. You don't need to compete with other runners to feel fulfilled, just getting a better time feel good on its own. And you don't have to meticulously explore every pixel of the game to find a few obscure skips, since developers manually put them in here for you to find. This game makes you feel like an actual speedrunner without all time-consuming training and other not so romantized parts of a speedrunner routine.The gameplay is fantastic and somewhat unique, the visuals are stylish, the music is a banger and the story is a complete garbage and waste of time. This is my game of the year so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I consider myself a casual gamer. My two most-played Steam games are Stardew Valley and Binding of Isaac, with hundreds of hours each, yet my farm is still a disaster and I haven't gotten further than It Lives. Timed gameplay gives me anxiety. I hate platformers. I can't aim. But, after finishing the story mode and getting all the gifts, I can say Neon White is one of my favorite games.The way progression goes,  You start being able to run and jump. That's it. You don't even have a sprint button. With movement options that have limited, but very straightforward uses, each level is first an adventure, then a puzzle, and finally, a time challenge--but only if you want it to be! You can have a  just finishing the main game and skipping the collectibles. Some progress is gated behind achieving fast times on the levels, but, listen. I never finished Little Big Planet 2 because the platforming was too hard, and I *STILL* got Gold or higher on most of the levels while collectible hunting. It's doable.. Each level is less than a minute long, and all the consumables you need to complete the level are located in the level itself. With each death or reset, you only lose seconds. It's way easier on you, the player, than a roguelike or a precision platformer.The writing is . The humor is silly, with references that actually caught me off-guard. The game knows when to take it down a notch, though, and let it breathe during moments of intensity. ! Steve Blum (Neon White, Spike Spiegel, Orochimaru) and SungWon Cho (Mikey the Angel, ProZD voice) are recognizable stand-outs, but everybody is great, with stand-out performances from Ian Jones Quarterly (Neon Yellow, Radicles from OK KO) and Alicyn Packard (Neon Red, Jibanyan from Yo-Kai Watch).( Neon White has jamming tracks that you won't get tired of, no matter how many times you reset a level.)The story will hit some recognizable tropes for any JRPG fan. That doesn't make it bad. In fact, with the game's setting and focus on death as a learning tool, . Story-wise, it's not a What Remains of Edith Finch, but Neon White doesn't  to be.Neon White is not meant to be dissected for revolutionary movement options or insane game play innovations. It's meant to be a fun experience. You should buy Neon White, because it will give you that fun experience--even if you're bad at video games like me.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a vibe.Lemme start off by saying that I absolutely love this game and can easily recommend this to anyone who loves fast-paced FPS or speedrunning games in general. This game has so many good things going for it and is, so far, one of my top 10 games of 2022. There are some shortcomings but they're mainly just me wanting more.For this review I played through the entire main story once with 100% completion and have not done any of the post-game unlocked content. I completed every level with at least an ace rank (I did not beat any dev times) and have done all sidequests with max insight with every character.Here's an introduction to the gameThe Premise:You play as White, a dead man and a sinner with amnesia sent to heaven and forced to fight off demons in order to stay in heaven. You and your fellow sinners, or Neons, need compete and kill as many demons as you can in 10 days to see who gets to stay in heaven and who goes back to hell, but only one can stay. There are also some old comrades of yours here, but whether or not they're allies anymore is up for you to find out.The Game:Neon White is a speedrunning FPS where you need to complete short levels as fast as you can. Times per level depend on how fast your brain is. You need to kill every demon in the level before you can open the goal. Your weapons are cards that serve 2 purposes, to shoot and to discard. Shooting guns uses ammo, using all of the ammo will delete your card, you can get more ammo by picking up ammo cards or copies of the same card. Discarding cards lets you use their abilities like extra jumps, dashing, sticky bombs, etc. Use cards to kill and traverse your way through levels as fast as possible.Now here's where my review startsRuns: Unbelievably SmoothThis game runs immaculately, there were no bugs or crashes when I played. It's not like it's that intense to handle in the first place though.Graphics: It gets the job done (Has a good style though)This game runs at 60fps on the switch and you've seen screenshots, this game has a good art style despite it's simplicity. It's also easy to see enemies, cards, and obstacles because of it. It still has a surprisingly diverse set of level types. Also I like the color contrast it's going for. Gameplay: "Flow"Flow is a good way to describe this game, playing through levels at a lightning fast speed while popping off card abilities and shooting multiple enemies in rapid succession. This game has such good pacing in it's gameplay that you enter a state of constant flow in which your mind unlocks, you begin to see the level structure and it feels like a roller coaster that you control. Story and Characters: Good (But I want more)During the story you meet a good cast of characters that have distinct personalities, problems, and backstories (some aren't fully explained). Here are some of them.-Yellow: A freerunner and, as he describes, best bud. He's your muscle bro. (not literally but you get what I mean) sadly you don't get very much in terms of story from him.-Violet: A crazy girl that likes "cute things" (like bunnies, gore, and bombs), she's quirky but she does have more going on with her than "I'm the quirky girl".-Red: A sniper that you have a "history" with (She also likes to gaslight White). She gets the most screen time and has the most story.-The characters have a good amount of personality and motivations but their pasts are not very well defined, you're never going to get a "what was their childhood like? what's their origin story?". It's one of the only parts of the story that I wish was there. -Also there's not really an epilogue like a "where are they now?". But you do get a glimpse of what happens in a final screenshot before the credits and a final flashback VN depicting something referenced in a photo earlier in the game. -And finally the villain's motivations and an undefined character involving the villain that isn't fleshed out.These are just story pet-peeves that I have, I don't think the overall story is bad, it's cool but I wanted more and I didn't get more that's it.Also, Devs, if you're reading this I would pay out the ass for a DLC involving more story and levels.Just saying.Please.Pretty Please.:"-(But other than those things I can easily recommend this game to people.And to Freaks.Especially Freaks.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cool as hell (no pun intended), the vibes, the aesthetic, the gameplay, it all flows very well. It's 1/4 visual novel with very interesting characters, a mysterious plot, and some great moments. And 3/4 a puzzle-ish flow-ish shooter-ish parkour-ish game. It has aim assist by default, but I don't know how useful it is, because I turned it off before I played the game, and honestly you probably don't need it on.I like the character depth, even when you feel like you get the whole story, you just have more questions. The characters feel compelling, the levels feel VERY well thought out. They reward you constantly for a knowledge of your cards, enemies, and abilities. Some levels feel great, then feel even better when you learn/figure out the Ace route. Then feel EVEN BETTER when that ace route you manage to do the first time, because it looked like a faster and more fun route. I didn't expect to like the gameplay as much as I did, but in some of the later missions, I have said, out loud "Oh ♥♥♥♥, that was cool as hell" because the levels are so considered and well designed that I can't help but be impressed. Not only do the normal routes seem well designed, but they are weaved with faster paths that make you feel like a genius for spotting them without the guide. Other times, the guide is amazing, and is a wonderful addition for people who care to Ace everything. None of this is to even speak about the execution, which, I don't know if I've seen done better in a first person setting. This game absolutely drips from head-to-toe with style, and combat and movement is no exception. Rarely does the game put you in the same headspace as your character, but you really do feel like you're channeling Neon White when you blaze your way through a level. Especially while the incredible OST blares in the background.If you played and liked "The World Ends With You" you'll feel right at home with this game. Unique setting, off-kilter game-runners, plenty of secrets, interesting characters. It's all here, and it was more than what I was hoping for.Edit: After getting the "Secret Ace" time on every stage in the game, I have a newer and fuller appreciation for the truly staggering amount of effort that went into designing each level. Some of them are so cleverly designed that it's truly stunning how smoothly the stage plays for silver to gold, gold to ace, and ace to secret ace. Each one feels right at home, some stages are just about pure speed and skill, some require lots of lateral thinking to knock out every demon, and/or find paths that feel amazingly clever. Also, go watch some world record times on youtube, they are SO cool to watch. The difficulty also scales beautifully, bronze to silver maybe a 10% increase in difficulty. Silver to Gold, 30%, Gold to Ace, 70%, Ace to Secret Ace: 250%, Secret Ace to near WR: 400%, but damn is it fun to try. Anyway, I didn't think I'd get 30 more hours out of this game since my initial review, but after beating White's Hell Rush and putting in my first few attempts at Mikey's, as frustrating as it was at times, this game has yet to stop impressing me.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is exactly the type of game that makes people scoff at games. A first person shooter with cards, speedrunning, and a set of anime-inspired killers in its mix should be a mess, but developer Angel Matrix weaves a tale of forgiveness into a frenetic and satisfying shooter that carves its own identity.Neon White is really NOT a shooter, it's more of a first person platformer where you must clear demons out of the level to complete it. On your path, you'll pick up Soul Cards, which function as a specific type of weapon (from rocket launchers to pistols), but can also be discarded for a movement ability, like a double jump, or a forward dash. The game quickly ends up becoming a set of momentum based puzzles of figuring out the fastest way to kill the enemies and launch yourself to the finish. It's an engaging loop that never wares out across the hundred or so levels throughout the campaign. Doing better on each stage grants new bonuses; from hints on the optimal path to the "Ace" ranking, to a collectible gift found in every level. These gifts change the objective from speed to puzzle, as you need to figure out the correct path to reaching the usually distant presents. The process is a welcome transformation to every level, and ends up becoming Neon White's strongest element of its level design.After completing a run of levels, you return to Central Heaven to receive your next mission and talk to the other Neons. By picking up the aforementioned gifts, you can develop your relationships with each character further. The gifts are all the same object, which is a disappointment. I wish unique items could be picked up that said more about these people's lives before death. That lack of character depth extends to the dialogue scenes, which are funny and well-written, but lack any sort of narrative function and serve as cute banter to pit White against one of his comrades. You can also unlock sidequests with gifts, which are challenge levels to test a certain restriction. For example, Neon Yellow's don't allow you to discard abilities, and Red's require using only one variety of Soul Card at a time. The upending of the main game's formula make these levels a welcome addition, and include some of Neon White's best moments.Neon White is a game made to be replayed. On top of the gifts and four levels of times to beat per stage, in the post-game you unlock Rush modes. This has you going through a gauntlet of every type of stage in a row. It's a challenging reframing, forcing you to act on instinct and a hint of memory. This will be a game you'll spend a lot of time perfecting if you want to hit that 100%.Overall, Neon White is a fantastic package. Its fast combat never feels incomprehensible, and with almost instantaneous respawns and airtight controls, at its surface level Neon White is one of the best games this year. Add in an entertaining cast and story, as well as hours more gameplay to completion, and Neon White is an easy recommendation, freak or not.

_childDocuments_.review: AMAZING GAMEThe good: The entire concept of the game is very unique. The idea of picking up cards that you can both shoot and discard to trigger a special ability gives you a lot of room to experiment with the path you traverse through a stage. The level designs are conducive to this experimentation and keep the game fresh throughout its fairly lengthy run time. The feeling of accomplishment after shaving that last half a second off your run for that ace medal is unrivaled. Even though I find collectibles generally kind of tedious in most games, in Neon White it was more like a puzzle to solve from the order of what cards to use to shortcuts to secret areas. It gave a very different feel of gameplay from the typical speed running and that made it a nice break at times. Plus, you get to use the collectibles to unlock new conversations with the characters around the map (ps Red best girl no competition) and see flashbacks to when the MC was still alive on Earth. Also, the OST by Machine Girl is f*cking amazing, go check out the soundtrack and his other music even if you don't play this game.The bad: I liked the characters, but there is a little bit of "every female character drools over the protagonist" that was a bit too much in my opinion. I also wasn't the greatest fan of the boss stages, they were too long in my opinion, especially some of the later ones, although it was a cool idea to try and keep the speedrun mechanic going even in the more "combat-focused" boss battles. And not really a true negative, but those hell rush achievements kept me away from my 100%, curse you devs lol.If not for Elden Ring last year, this game would have totally been my GOTY, so that shows you how good this game really is. All my complaints are very minimal problems, and such I strongly recommend this game to anyone even remotely interested in it.

The card sacrifice system is genius design that both restricts and allows for creative use of the powers to cut time on the professionally designed stages. Great soundtrack that reminds me of some of the best 90's video game electronic music. Not a fan of the dating aspects of the game. The dialogue is, uh, an acquired taste. If you really like meta anime humor, then maybe you wont be rolling your eyes to the back of your head like I was. If its too much then there is a skip button which, in any dialogue heavy game I appreciate. Beyond that one of the coolest games I've played in a long time and I see myself coming back to this game over and over just to shave that little bit of time I know I can.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a first-person platformer-shooter that is purpose-built for speedrunning. It has a plot and a primitive relationship system but it is designed to be played, and played quickly. The gameplay is undoubtedly its strength, with the rest serving as a palate cleanser more than anything. I recommend it to anyone looking for gameplay that rewards precision and persistence (wrapped in great art direction and soundtrack), but would not recommend it for anyone looking for plot. Oh, you'll also hear references to "simps" and other internetisms, so if the thought of that makes you cringe unbearably consider yourself warned. However, if you can grit your teeth through those brief moments you'll find a fast-paced game that has the bedtime-ruining "just one more" power of any game out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative recommendation. Gameplay feels nice, I really enjoy the feeling of going super fast! That's enjoyable.But there's a handful of things that make it difficult to fully recommend, most of it has to do with writing.Have you ever watched a television show that desperately tried to keep up with modern-day memes at the time of its production, but by the time it's been released, those jokes are burnt and old? Yeah. Sadly, that's the writing for . I'm usually not such a stickler for humor, but the constant lame lingo being thrown around isn't charming, just kind of annoying. I end up skipping a lot of the spoken dialogue and just reading, but I do like a couple of the voice actors (Steve Blum and SungWon Cho) so I generally like their dialogue better.Some of the weapons don't really feel like they have much weight to them in their primary shoot attack. It takes a lot to nail that balance and I don't think  achieves that, but if you don't care about something like that, i.e. you didn't spend hundreds of hours playing shooter games, you probably won't care.And finally--just because gameplay is fast doesn't mean the story has to move so fast, too! But that could just be the consequence of only spending ~10 minutes to complete a slew of levels (about 10 levels per in-game day). Characters are showing up just to die. Prior relationships are being called to question without any buildup. It feels a little sloppy. If the game wanted to just be a super-swift shooter and swiper, I'd be fine with that. By all means, there are plenty of games that forego a deep or meaningful story to just have fun gameplay! But I think  tries too hard to get people invested in these characters, when there isn't really much to feel invested in. Our main character is a total amnesiac, and not in a "let's discover this world together" way, more of a "wow, everyone has some kind of relationship to me and they refuse to delve any deeper about it" way.So... Yeah. If you feel fine with skipping out on "story" just for the fun gameplay, do it. There's a nice dopamine hit you get from being faster than your friends (and don't bother with global leaderboards--botted games lead to people who finish a level in an impossible amount of time). I recommend the game for that. If you thought there'd be some interesting story here, there really isn't. A lot of "Heaven is corrupt, isn't that WHACKY?" schtick. If I was interested in a somewhat compelling story with angels and demons, I'd go watch .
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 Fairly solid platformer. Game contains ample number of movement options that vary in availability per mission.Levels are initially slow but quickly become fairly satisfying once more and more movement options are introduced and you begin blazing through missions, discovering shortcuts and such. In terms of getting the medals on every mission, the game is geared more towards knowledge than execution- if you know the path and understand your movement options it is very easy mechanically to obtain the ace medals. That being said I imagine that if you're speed running there is a quite a bit of depth in the execution of your movement though personally it was enough for me to get the ace medals. The only thing I personally dislike is the floaty jump but I'm not knocking off any points for it. I do however dislike obtaining the secret items that are present in each level. At first they are fairly simply to obtain but as levels get more and more complex I found myself aimlessly wandering through levels just to find them. For me they slow down the gameplay/progression quite a bit and dull the highs I get after I ace a level. The story is appreciated and at times interesting, though the moment to moment writing is fairly bad. Voice acting is carried by Steve Blum while everyone else is mostly fine. In between missions you can use gifts obtained in each level to interact with your fellow neons and heaven denizens. Like the story, the fact the social links exist is appreciated but the writing brings down the overall experience.I enjoyed the game's aesthetic even if the environments and enemies are somewhat basic.I didn't 100% but the achivements don't seem particularly hard - just requiring ample levels of patience. The (likely) hardest achivement requires completing every mission in the game in one go without dying. There is NOT a timer on this achievement so you can take the simplest and easiest routes on missions but forgetting a solution to a level or making a simple mistake can cost you an entire run. Since the completion of levels is more knowledge based rather than skill based it can be done over time but I just don't have the patience for it. Honestly something as simple as having somebody else's run on another screen as you go through levels one by one would probably get it done.

_childDocuments_.review: I've done plenty of speedruns and time attack-focused games before, but no other game has motivated me this much to think hard and get creative about shaving fractions of a second off my time. The satisfaction of putting together a route, improving it bit by bit, seeing yourself move up the leaderboard, and finally pulling off the perfect run is fantastic- and then you think of something else you could do that might be even faster.The game is super snappy and responsive, there's no delay between restarts, and the barrier to improvement is often your strategy rather than pure execution. That said, the gunplay and movement are great, with the weapons' unique but limited abilities letting you dash through levels like a ninja while making you use your resources wisely. The game's not hard and can be enjoyed by anyone, but it really shines when you're pushing for fast times, so keep that in mind if you're expecting a standard fps- this game is NOT that. Also, the soundtrack is bangin. Wish they'd bring back the demo, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Annapurna Interactive partners with Angel Matrix, and Machine Girl. It's by far one of the most unique trios to have come together to make a game that appeals to people who like anime, people who like FPS action games, and combines it all into one to make a story that many could argue to be critically acclaimed.As a player, the replayability is what makes this game worth it's price. It's straightfoward and clear, reach your destination. Eliminate demons. Neon White's originality, and especially fast-paced gameplay is what makes this speedrunner-esque single-player game both rewarding and refreshing. Not to mention that since each gun has a different ability, and since the UI is designed with simplicity; it's as if the game wants you to act efficiently. What's the fastest way up there? What can I do to show flair, show style? These questions are answered solely by the player, and greatly so, since it's all about the way you play your cards.Oh, and did I mention this game is perfect for breakcore and drum 'n' bass lovers? Yeah. The visuals are stunning. It's sharp, clean, and somewhat smooth. The songs are erratic, and have a celestial feel to it; never sacrificing its genre, and instead appealing to its fans. Heaven is ironically wicked, and if you want to feel like a freak, well, the world in Neon White is good enough to make you have a general idea that you are.So... Should you get the game? Absolutely. But only if you want a new experience, or if you like an action game that is almost literally a puzzle game mixed in with a first person shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly interesting Puzzle game/First Person Platformer. More than anything else, this game really needs to be put up as a great example of steady/incremental difficulty and balancing. Every set of levels introduces something new and does a wonderful job of playing with those ideas and iterating in a local way. There were levels that I platinumed on a first try, purely because of how hard I was vibing with the level designs (seriously though, not a flex about first time platinums, I'm bad at video games). The weapon variety is a little thin, but the secondary abilities they all get definitely helps, especially the last 2 which I won't spoil because they're really fun!My one serious criticism is the dialog is bad. So bad that after sitting through the first full cutscene in game (not the intro), I noped out of the rest of the game's story purely because I didn't want to hear any of these characters ever speak again (which sucks, I like Steve Blum). The game itself gave me a final playtime of 6 hours and 30 minutes, so my time on Steam additionally reflects skipping through cutscenes and restarting levels (and maybe 15 minutes when I first started the game and was fiddling with the settings). HLTB seems to be averaging people at 10.5 hours (accounting for cutscenes I guess).Overall, I really do recommend this game. Very interesting mechanics and great art design for fast paced FPS action/platforming. I just wish the script was better or you could turn off cutscenes entirely in the options menu. 4/5, grab it if it looks even a little interesting to you!
