_childDocuments_.review: Tl;Dr: Gameplay is worse than Cyber Hook, story is worse than cyanide.The game is good. Uh... mostly. The game can be split into two distinct sections, FPS & visual novel. The FPS segments (aka most of the game) are fantastic. They're a little cramped until you unlock Dominion about halfway through playing, but after that I wouldn't call a single level bad. I don't really have a lot to say about the levels that isn't obvious by looking at someone playing them, but they're hella fun.And then there's the visual novel. Jesus christ. Hire a writer. Like, any writer. You have ProZD money, you certainly have the money for a writer. Dialogue is stilted, voice acting is sub-par (except for Mikey all my homies love Mikey), and the characters are two-dimensional at best. You know your story has bad writing when the most complicated characters in it are the himbo and the yandere. This game's story just feels like something 9th grade me would've come up with in a daydream. "It's like, bad guys, but they're in heaven, and they have GUNS, but uh oh they're sad! and catholics are EVIL." I do agree with the general moral of forgiveness, but I feel like the characters could've used a lot more time in the oven. Except Mikey, all my homies love Mikey.And in case you're one of the psychopaths who cares about any of the Neons, well don't you worry, cuz the ending of the game will make you want to punch a developer. Yeah, so to get the "good ending" you have to play the dating sim. Like, to completion. Don't worry, that just means you have to get a collectible AND an ace metal in EVERY. SINGLE. LEVEL. THERE ARE 120 LEVELS. I'm playing a movement shooter, not ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Deltarune. And if you don't complete the dating sim, GOD HIMSELF calls you a bad person. Oh, and by the way, in case you were wondering if Green would learn his lesson if you get the good ending (the ending where you forgive him), HE DOESN'T. Alpharad's GOTY, ladies & gentlemen.But, of course, only a madman would spend that much time grinding just for a PNG of God to give them the thumbs-up. _childDocuments_.review: I literally do not know how to review this. I feel very indifferent, and the game is very mixed.This game has one of the most generic anime character tropes and terrible writing. The plot itself is intriguing, and the first plot twist is interesting, but the writing just makes it seem like it was written by a person who desperately needs to touch grass. White witnesses how, for example, the villain kills someone, and then the next day, when he publicly says he wants to talk to White, White blushes and acts like "oh no, that is so embarrassing". Furthermore, the plot convenience is next level. Somehow, everyone unanimously agrees to not tell White about his past. However, they still talk about the good moments they had. Like, you don't tell me about my past, but you share memories you had with me, even though I have no context whatsoever. That is just so odd and convenient writing to make the obvious twist stand more out.The characters are mostly one dimensional. We have the typical introvert who is really OP, the comic relief, a girl that belongs to TikTok, and the "ara ara" mommy character. That is unfortunate due to the simple fact that 50% of this game is a visual novel. It does give you the ability to skip all the text. On the other hand, I really like to actually know what my mission is. What I do not like is how at the end they just tried to cram in as many twists and turns as possible.The gameplay itself is alright. I like the idea of using the cards and each card has a discard function, adding a temporary move to your move set (like stomping, dashing etc.). However, there is only so much you can do with that. The basic movement is very limiting and feels very slow. You are rarely able to truly break a level, but are more likely to perfect your movement to its fullest.Enemies here are more of a requirement to get to the goal, but the foes themselves are fairly basic, they don't do a lot, except the coolly designed head that shoots instant-kill lasers.While I think the gameplay is alright, it somehow feels like there is much more you can do with it, and if you're not a hardcore speedrunner, I would recommend Ghostrunner instead, cause there is more of a game experience to it.Just like the ending of the game, I do not know how to feel about it. I 100%ed it, however, I wasn't glad to have a chore off of me. I wasn't sad that the game ended, I just kinda moved on, feeling very indifferent.6/10, a very mixed game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a fast paced, adrenaline fueled romp through the different layers of heaven on a quest to be redeemed for your mortal sins by slaying demons at incredibly high speed.I make no overstatement when I say this game has some of the best feeling game play I've ever, well played.Everything feels crisp and precise, yet its also forgiving and smooth enough that it doesn't require thousands of hours to "git gud."Its one of those things that just has to be played to be felt, I could fill this review with paragraph upon paragraph describing each level and each new movement option you unlock a long the way. But whats the use when they all feel fantastic?Neon White's levels are so fast paced that you could play a decent number of them well before refund time is up and easily decide if you want to keep the game. Sadly it lacks a free demo which is a huge draw back honestly. The music is another great part, I bought the OST almost immediately after I got the game and while it may not be to everyone's taste its exactly the kind of loud abrasive sounding techno I enjoy and it goes very well with the overall tone and style of the game.Last positive, graphics are good.Sure they're not revolutionary, but damn if they don't look distinctive. Maybe that's more of an art direction thing?I just hope the real heaven looks kinda like this.The only negative is the writing, the story itself is functional if predictable. A basic tale of friendship and redemption. While the cast of characters are very colourful (pun intended) they all stand out and have their own quirks and problems that I at once found understandable and compelling.But the dialogue writing is atrocious. Some scenes are quite fun in a campy way. While other "jokes" are just memetic phrases copy and pasted from yesterdays Know Your Meme pages. Many emotional scenes in the story are unfortunately cut down by Marvel Cinamatic Universe style "SO THAT JUST HAPPENED" humor that just brings down the whole pace and makes me want to hand feed White or whoever an entire floor. It hurts the games pace and does not provide comic relief, its just annoying. If you must have those kind of jokes, save them for the side conversations and keep them well outside of the main plot.(The technical term is "logos" because such reactions of disbelief are "logical" but it is also the antithesis of "pathos" which means the emotional context of a story)Put simply, if the characters are cracking jokes about a scene, which should I take it seriously?If the characters take it seriously. So will the audience. This carefree attitude to story telling, the idea of all fiction as some kind of big meta textual joke has been a long running problem across pretty much every medium and its sad to see an otherwise flawless game face plant so hard on what could have been a perfect landing.I bring all this up because, while I can explain exactly why a story doesn't work tonally. Good game play can't be explained through the context of words. And I strongly encourage you to give Neon White's sublime game play, at least a try. If you don't like it Steam is generous with refunds.Seriously though, give us a demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game, really similar to Lovely Planet, another great FPS "puzzle" game, but with more mechanics and polished level-design. If you enjoyed fast-paced movement and/or speedrunning, this game should be for you.The price for me completely reflects the amount of content in the game if you're into trying to get all medals for each level, which was a blast for me. Mastering a level to get the dev-time can give such a rewarding feeling! But just finishing the main-story can give you around ~12h of gameplay, and it might be enough for most people.I have over 50 hours and I didn't even finish the final two extra courses, although I do think the game ran out of steam for me around the ~40h mark and now I'm only trying to be a Completionist with these final challenges.The only thing that I disliked was the narrative. I found the plotline pretty weak and the characters not as amusing as the game tried to make them be. Maybe if you're a teen you'll get a kick out of the sexual innuendos and generic anime villain plot. But all that didn't stop me at all from enjoying the gameplay, the soundtrack and aesthetics. _childDocuments_.review: Recent years have been very lacking in traditional FPS content (AAA). Doom Eternal wasn't the game Doom fans were hoping for. Halo Infinite's multiplayer was too slow and was lacking meaningful content. And... that's about it. Meanwhile these are tons of small indie studios making traditional FPS games. Most of these games take Doom's and Quake's recipe and bake their own versions. This game doesn't do that and that's what makes this game the best FPS game I have played.The map designs are excellent and the movement feels good. The mechanics aren't evolving into overwhelming mess I feel like Doom Eternal was. The game uses the same philosophy as BotW had - few tools, many combinations. You can save tens of seconds when you find out you can combine x and y cards. The maps and the cards play in such harmony that you can just play the same level over and over. The music is excellent. The DnB/Breakcore songs give the game its quirky feeling. +1 new fan to Machine Girl.The story and characters are okay. Dialogue style clearly borrows eastern games/novels and the characters follow Enneagram of Personality (very eastern style). The story was fitting for the game. The pacing was good but the turning points were predictable. I highly recommend getting Ace in every level because that's when the game shines. The game is all about figuring out different ways to complete the level. The game was just pure joy to play from start to finish and that is a sign of a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White has slowly found its way into being a mainstay game for me that I am always able to come back to whenever I feel like just zoning out.  The gameplay loop is very satisfying where you are constantly playing the same levels over and over again trying to set a time that's just even a little better than the time you just set.  However, even though the levels are the same it's finding those small details that even let you shave off a fraction of a second that makes every run feel different.  The music is consistently fantastic as well and fits the rapid pace that the gameplay has perfectly.  The characters you interact with are interesting changes of pace that give the game a real sense of character while progressing through the main story that may feel a little choppy at times.  Overall, I recommend this game as both from a value standpoint and an enjoyment standpoint this rated very highly for me

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying the game so far. The gun play, while far from the main focus of the game, feels pretty good despite how quickly you're moving around. It's really satisfying to slowly shave the seconds off of runs, or even somehow manage to clock in several seconds below the diamond time on your first try. The aerial movement is pretty floaty, but I think it works with the pace the game expects. As many have mentioned, though, the dialogue is a little dodgy. _childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most brilliant level design I've had the privilege of experiencing. I like using combination analogy when assessing a game's worth, and Neon White is a marriage of the best versions of Mirror's Edge and Portal, with a bit of Sonic's thrilling rush-through-the-levels style of play. Intense, difficult, but nevertheless achievable and hugely rewarding to reach the finish line. Being given the chance to explore the levels more thoroughly to find the gifts adds even more to the fun, as I find it very satisfying to walk around such a smoothly designed clean space and architecture.Many people rightly point out the cringeworthy dialogue during the early parts of the game and the Free TIme phases. I'll admit it makes doing the sidequests and finding gifts less exciting when thinking of the reward being yet another meaningless, unrevealing dialogue. The game would be so much improved if each Free Time dialogue have a bit more substance, which the Memory sections only slightly make up for.That said, giving attention to the main storyline is  a total waste of time. I quite enjoy it, myself. It's pretty clear that so much of the game's elements are a homage to Quentin Tarantino. The colors as names, the brutal, but stylish depictions of blood and death, and of course, revenge as the characters' ultimate motivation. As the plot unfolds, everybody does become more mature, and seeing the main plot's progression while revealing more of the Memories offer some intriguing nuance for each character's development. By the end of the game, I find I was able to forgive the cringeworthiness of the early game dialogues.If you find the super fun gameplay existing alongside the awkward writing at the start to be so incompatible you can't get through the rest of the game, I think you would be missing out on one of the best indie games of this early decade. All of this, and I haven't even mentioned the high tempo soundtrack by Breakcore producer MachineGirl, which does wonders to crank up the energy of each level. Add to all that the slick art style, and Neon White is worth enduring.

_childDocuments_.review: It's wild to me that this game only has 10,000 reviews and a ~3,000 concurrent player peak. This is by far and away one of the most fun games I have played in my entire life, and I have played a lot of games that I love dearly.In Neon White, you are a dead criminal who went to heaven, but you only get to stay if you kill more demons than everyone else that was also brought up with you. Only one of you get to stay. This is the initial premise, and it only gets more absurd/fun as it goes.This is a "speedrunning" game where you will play levels with the goal of reaching the end, but the exit only unlocks after you kill all of the enemies present.Pushing for fast times in the very creative and well designed levels, full of shortcuts and optimizations, is an extremely satisfying experience. On top of that, the movement feels so, so smooth. Combine that with the abilities stored in cards you find in each stage, you can find a bunch of different ways to complete most of them. It just feels so good to play.On top of how good the movement feels, it is also very precise, making for gameplay that you can always improve upon. How fast you complete the levels is all about how you can land that one difficult jump, meet that time window to make it to the shortcut, saving your cards until the perfect moment to create your own shortcut, etc.The dialog is kinda bad/cringe throughout most of the game, but to be honest that didn't detract from my experience much at all. The premise of the story is already absurd and unbelievable, so I personally didn't need realistic conversations to be invested in the experience the developers made. It can get so bad sometimes that it circles around to being hilarious and sort of engaging. I can definitely see how this would be a downside to some, but it wasn't for me.What the devs spent a lot of time on is the core gameplay, which in my opinion is as perfect as it gets for a small studio making a game like this. It's obvious that they put so much care into how the game feels, and all of that work shines through in nearly every possible moment.If there are any downsides in the level design, it would be in the final stretch of the game, where you gain a very powerful ability that simplifies the last few levels quite a bit. Even then, those levels were still a lot of fun and full of spectacle, so I can't say it is an actual downside, but rather an explosive and fast paced finale.They included hints in the game similar to a ghost in a mario kart time trial. These show you how you can achieve the good medals without too much thought. The best part about these is that they make sure that anyone can figure out how to get decent times to proceed the story, but they are usually not the actual fastest way to beat the level. You've gotta make a plan while exploring and execute good movement to really push better times.Also, I won't talk about it much, but the soundtrack is CRAZY good. It matches the energy, theme, and tempo of the levels very well.With hidden collectibles to find in most levels (these affect the ending of the game, while providing you a meaningful reason to stop and actually learn the level you are playing), time thresholds to get better medals (which affect your progress), extra challenges and time attacks, you really get your money's worth here.If you have 25 bucks, buy it and try it out, you will find out if it is for you or not within an hour, it starts out quickly showing you what to expect.This game is clearly a passion project made by talented developers, and they knocked it out of the park and all the way to Heaven. The vision they had I feel is pretty obvious, make a fun and stylish speedrunning game that rewards creativity and paying close attention to the details and clues they provide. They took that and ran away with it, making a very unique and wonderful experience that will stick around in your brain for quite some time.tldr:I can't recommend Neon White enough, just give it a shot and find out for yourself, trust me. The biggest downside is that no more content has come out since release, that's genuinely the only real negative for me. I played the game close to its launch and my opinion hasn't gone down one bit, I only appreciate it more.I was only going to write a quick review just to give this game another recommended score, but once I started talking about it I got carried away and wrote this essay. It's that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a first person platformer/speedrunning/FPS game. You play as the epooymous Neon White, a sinner who has been brought to Heaven along with a bunch of other sinners to kill demons for ten days. Whichever of these sinners – called Neons – gets the highest rank at the end of the ten days gets to stay in Heaven, while the rest are cast back out once more.Neon White has lost his memories, but other sinners who knew him in life – Yellow, Red, and Violet – are all also competing to stay in Heaven as well, and may be taking advantage of his lack of memories for their own ends.Over the course of the game, you uncover what is really going on, your relationship to the other neons, befriend some angels, and gather gifts during levels to give to people back in the home base to level up your friendship levels, unlocking conversations, additional secret levels, collectibles for your room, and eventually memories of your interactions with them in life.Overall, the plot aspect of the game is not particularly good – it is very anime (despite not being made in Japan) and the characters are fairly simple and archetypal, and don’t really feel much like they were assassins in live (with the exception of Violet) as they ostensibly were. My favorite character was Mikey, an angel who looks like a cat with a cigar and a hard-bitten voice.But that’s not really what you’re here for. The plot is mostly just an excuse for the action, and the core gameplay of this game is quite good.The game’s central premise is that you need to beat the levels as fast as possible for medals. Traversing these levels, you have the standard running and jumping, but you also get guns – these can be shot to kill demons or interact with some environmental objects, or can be discarded to give you a traversal power, like jumping, air-dashing, a mid-air rocket, a grappling hook, or a ground slam. Each weapon corresponds to a different secondary power, and there are six weapons in all in the game. Most of these weapons can’t break barricades with their normal shots, so you usually have to use the damaging traversal powers to break them down or bypass them.You have to kill every demon in most of the levels, so when you are trying to find a more efficient route, you need to be able to kill all the enemies even if you are cutting off big chunks of the levels in terms of traversal.This leads to an interesting core gameplay loop of going into a level, learning its layout, then mastering it, figuring out what routes you can take to save time and how to kill demons that are “off route” without going near them. It works really well, and the game has a fast pace and solid level variety, finding a good number of ways to show off the game’s mechanics and create interesting platforming experiences.The game gives out four ranks of medal at the end of each level – bronze, silver, gold, and ace – and there’s a fifth, hidden red rank that is not needed for 100%ing the game. Acing the levels takes some doing, but isn’t prohibitively difficult; getting those red medals, however, is a very difficult challenge indeed.The game also has built-in level rush modes which you unlock when you beat all the levels in the game, with internal leaderboards that both show how well your friends did on them, as well as how well you rank globally.The game also has a hidden gift in almost every level, which you can collect to give to characters; some of these require you to notice them in unusual places, while many are difficult to reach and require you to use your resources cleverly and efficiently to get to them.All of this combines to create a quite solid gameplay experience. If you like the idea of speedrunning, this game has fun with the idea, and the movement of the character through the levels is a lot of fun.All in all, I’d recommend this game to more mechanics-focused players who enjoy speedrunning/beat the clock, but people who are more story/narrative focused are likely to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, first off, Gameplay.A very simple (at face value) game. Get from point A to point B while killing everything in your way. Simple right?Well, yes, it is. In fact, this game is cleverly made in a way that you will rarely fail to do so without a passing grade. But where's the fun in that?You want that shiny blue Ace. You want to go and get every ace in the game. You want to find those tricky shortcuts that make you feel oh so very smart. You want to feel like you REALLY beat the game.And it will feel oh so good......Until you grind a level a bit TOO much... and IT appears. The Red medal. The Dev Times.God help you if you want to get those. They. Are. HARD.As for the story?Pretty good. Nothing to write home about, but it's enjoyable enough, and it serves as a good vessel for the gameplay. It does sometimes lean REALLY hard into anime tropes, but it never feels like it's trying to be taken seriously at those moments. There's a very definite sense of self-awareness in a lot of the game's more "memable" scenes, and this is further reinforced by the fact that when the story wants to take a more serious tone, it does so rather well.Overall, I give Neon White an 8/10. A very solid game with a fairly basic, but entertaining story, with a delightful cast of charming characters.Yes, I will be buying DLC if Angel Matrix makes it. This game is too good to not aggressively hunt any more Aces I can possibly get.

_childDocuments_.review: The most of the time, I don't care for speed-running games because they are typically no different from one another. The competitive nature of the situation makes you want to achieve the top rank or at least beat your friends, but in order to do so, you need the appropriate linear approach to accomplish this goal in a timely and efficient manner. The fact that I felt this desire to do so was more or less in good sport, rather than frustration. I was learning the many different ways to complete a stage in a quick and effective manner, and the better you did, the more unlocks you would get to nudge you in the right direction. After that, you could come back to the stage and just tear up your previous high scores as you progressed through the game. Gameplay that is both rewarding and forgiving, with a terrific story, great characters, and music that is crazy great. There is no doubt that you will discover something in this place that will keep you fascinated, regardless of what you may choose to believe or enjoy.

Ignore the guns, it's not an FPS, it's a First Person Puzzle Platforming Speedrunning game. And the soundtrack adds so much to the game. It's hard not to get pumped up every time you start up a level.

_childDocuments_.review: I would HIGHLY recommend this game even to casual players that aren't into speedrunning. Great music.Bought this game 3 days ago during a sale and ran through it. _childDocuments_.review: This is a weird one for me. The gameplay is so spectacular, but the angsty trope-filled battle royale visual novel that consistently interrupts the flow of levels is a blemish on an otherwise brilliantly designed speedrunner simulator. On the 'emo scale' of emotional intelligence, Neon White's predictable story lands itself somewhere around pre-adolescent poetry and attempted self-harm with a plastic spoon.Skip every cutscene and you've got yourself a clever shooter that's addictive to improve at. Color-coordinated enemies and minimalist visuals make obstacle recognition and split second reactions more intuitive. Shortcut hints and hidden items encourage you to replay and experiment with every level. Each chapter introduces new concepts that add to an amazing pool of well-integrated movement mechanics. Juggling every weapon/ability makes you feel like some sort of WASD wizard. Despite the general intensity of gameplay, getting the highest rank on a level isn’t particularly unreasonable as long as you’ve puzzled out the best route and practiced a fair bit. Ignoring its embarrassing narrative, Neon White is made to be ingeniously engaging and any fan of movement shooters should experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play shooters. I'm not a speedrunner. I don't play competitive ranked games (except hitman maybe). I don't even like games I have to play with a mouse and keyboard.But neon white has made me dust off the old mouse and spend hours replaying the same levels over and over again just to shave off a tenth of a second from my time. And there's something about this game that *made* me want to do it, and still have fun every time. Watching the videos/trailers doesn't do it justice, don't even bother with the demo--just buy the game and take off a few weeks from work--you'll need it :)
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: When the Neon White came out and I saw it, my first thought was that it is some kind of fast paced, procedurally generated rhytm game, which I am not a big fan of, so I skipped it. Now I've found out that it is an absolutely beatiful 3D action platformer, I immediately loved it.Story is beatiful as well, presented in the visual novel form, main dialogues are dubbed by professional voice actors, all characters feel alive, having their unique tempers. This is a rare case for such a game to have an interesting narrative.As I mentioned, this is a fast paced action platformer. There are 12 chapters in the game, each having 10 levels with some exceptions, giving in total 97 levels + 24 side leves, which you can unlock by collecting gifts on the levels, and giving them to other characters. In each level, again with some exceptions, you need to defeat all demons, using weapons, which are represented by cards. You can discard any card to get some mobility boost, like dash etc. Gifts also unlock additional dialogues and memories of the past, almost all of them expand lore greatly, telling more about main character and side characters, so I highly recommend beating the game 100% to watch all of them.Game is not hard, but long if you complete it 100%, took me 30 hours, to get every achievement. After beating the game, there unlocks 5 races, 3 of them are races through side levels, and two of them are races through all levels in the game, and for two achievements you need to beat all those without dying. Took me about an hour run to beat 96 levels without dying. So in theory it can take you about 2-3 hours to finish the game without any additional gameplay, if you complete all levels first try flawlessly, which is highly doubtful. Anyway, it means that you can rush through the game very quickly, therefore I again recommend to take your time and enjoy the game to its full potential.All locations in the game are also made beatifully, having pretty simple art style though. There are a lot of different demon types, each having their unique attack patterns, and the game combines all different abilities very good, giving an amazing platforming experience. Game design in general is also very good, I've never had a case where I did't understand where to go, or whom to kill, everything is clear, without making it completely easy to complete, but making it funnier to complete.This is the best 3D platformer that I've ever played, astonishing game, that gave me a lot of emotions. If you are into platformers, than this is a must have choice.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good speedrunning platformer. I consider myself an avid fan of games like this and there is a lot of good here but also some bad. The story is pretty awful, and the way the characters interact is pretty cringe. I think the character design overall is okay, but the game plays as a speedrunning game with a visual novel shoved in as an afterthought. The physics of the game are somewhat strange as well. Your character is very floaty, which can make some levels feel slow. Once you get further into the game you unlock a power-up that lets you drop quickly, and I wonder if they thought giving the character some weight would make that power-up feel less powerful. The floatyness is really off-putting but it is something I am trying to get past. Your character also walks fairly slow unless you are using abilities or running on waterways. This can make some levels feel slow in the early stages of the game.Despite these negatives, this game is actually pretty fun. There is resource management with your power-ups, and some levels do feel pretty fast paced. The game plays pretty well on controller if you are willing to change the default control scheme, though keyboard+mouse will always be superior in games like this. I think the graphics are nice and simple, not overdone, but not boring either. There are plenty of levels and the game seems like it is probably worth the money, even though I haven't finished it yet.Overall, for $25 which is what I paid for this game, I am on the fence about recommending it. It is a fun game and if you enjoy this type of game you should get it. I do think it is fun, and when this game goes on sale it would absolutely be worth the money. This is a pretty niche game genre and if you like games like cloudbuilt, or other 3d speedrunning platformers, you should pick this up, even if it does feel a little 'slow' in comparison.

_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a speedrunning FPS, puzzle-platforming game where the player has one simple objective in almost every level; kill every demon and finish the level fast. Originally conceived as a "card-based arena shooter" by lead designer Ben Esposito, Neon White has players control the titular Neon White using soul cards which not only acts as weapons to use, but also as parkour moves to navigate through the levels. By default, you have a Katana that can be used at melee range and reflect enemy projectiles, but it doesn't have a parkour move to it so you will want to keep an eye out for soul cards placed in the levels. You'll have soul cards making up weapons like a pistol and shotgun for example, but if you sacrifice a soul card, you'll discard the weapon for a single use of a parkour move.You can carry two different soul cards at once and can stack three of each soul card, allowing you to make use of multiple parkour moves in quick succession. Most levels are short and linear enough to make it clear on what to do with the cards at hand, but experienced players can think of clever use of the soul cards to perform shortcuts outside the main level path. This freedom for the player to make their own shortcuts is all intended design and there is little randomness to the game, so you are in control of improving your times as you replay levels. All this is what makes Neon White addicting to play, creating that dopamine to make one more attempt to beat your own best time (or your friend's best time).For additional replay value, the game has a feature called "Insight" which is designed to incentivize replaying a level for a better time. After completing a level, you are awarded a medal which ranks your performance. The four medals are Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Ace. The medals are what grants the player Insight after level completion, with each medal giving the player further aid in their replays of a level.The first time a player enters a level, they are given no visual aid on how they can go fast in a level, so it can be normal for your first run of a level to be a bit sluggish. Completing a level will reward the player a Bronze medal, however it also allows players to see their time in a level in all future replays. Going faster in a level can reward the player a Silver medal, which levels up your Insight to include a ghost reenacting your inputs from your current best run. By mastering the main level's path, you will be rewarded a Gold medal, with your Insight now leveled up to show a hint to the shortcut required to get the Ace medal.Neon White gradually builds up the incentive to replay a level multiple times over, the Insight system helps give players a hand on seeing where they can do better in replays. Insight gives players the confidence that they can achieve those once seemingly hard to get Ace medals, you'll feel like you are becoming a skilled speedrunner in just mere minutes. If you really want to push yourself, you can go for the hidden Red Ace medals (developer best times), which will require you to be at your best and figure out shortcuts not hinted to the player. I have obtained all the Red Ace medals and it's a challenge for sure, but the feeling that you can do better even by just a couple milliseconds does do a lot to someone like me!Also found in the levels after completing them once are gifts that you can find. These gifts are often placed far out the main level path and will require the player to think carefully on what parkour moves to make and what soul cards to keep in order to reach those gifts. Some gifts can be difficult to get, even the ones in plain sight can be hard to reach. You can give the gifts you collected to other characters in the hub to get rewarded new dialogue, side quests in the form of additional levels, and lore to the game's story.After you beat the game and go towards 100%, you can unlock Heaven Rushes and Hell Rushes. There are both Rushes for the main game's levels and the separate side quests of the different characters. A Heaven Rush is just going through the levels like normal, just in a singular run. You can restart as many times as you need to, you just need to complete all the levels in said singular run.The more interesting Rush is the Hell Rush, which is also a singular run of the levels but with the twist of having to complete every level in one life. Your health is also shared between levels, meaning you need to play with extra care. Failing the level by death or missing an enemy you cannot backtrack to will force you to restart the whole Hell Rush. To help you out, your default Katana can be discarded to refill your health and grant a soul card of your choosing in case you need to save yourself and avoid a restart. You can only discard the Katana once per level and you can only do this up to three times in a Hell Rush. The main game's Hell Rush will test your skills, be fast but don't die.I haven't brought up the story but to summarize, it's cheesy 90s/2000s anime you would discover on TV by some chance. You got corny lines, Steve Blum voicing the main protagonist himself, a love interest with some angst towards said protagonist, and the main characters are deceased assassins. The story is for a niche audience and the bad writing is very much intentional, though admittedly the game's story does pick up to be interesting later on. Still, you do have the option to skip the dialogue if you're not interested in the story nor want to hear the dialogue.Oh yeah, the soundtrack is composed by Machine Girl. I don't really listen to them personally but the soundtrack of this game is pretty good. If you love their music, I feel you will love the music of this game too.Overall, Neon White is a fun, addicting speedrunning game that hooks players into becoming speedrunners themselves. I played quite a lot of this game and even through a lot of fails in many runs, I had a blast playing this. It's my favorite game from 2022 and I highly recommend this game to anyone who wants a fast game that will make them want to go even faster. This is a game For Freaks, By Freaks!

_childDocuments_.review: So, let’s get the game’s biggest flaw out of the way first. The story is *bad*. Its like it was written by a fourteen year old boy from the suburbs who has never actually just ‘talked’ to a girl in his life and thinks reading non-canonical gospels is the height of rebellion. It’s so full of edge™ and quirk™, that if it wasn’t so heartfelt in its writing it would have seemed like parody. But forget about the storyline, because the gameplay is AMAZING!Playing this game is how I imagine driving a luxury car on an open road would feel. The speed, the way the character drifts through the air, the spacing of enemies and powerups is just so perfectly crafted. It communicates perfectly what the player is supposed to do and when so that the player has just enough time for their fingers to react. It kept me in a constant state of high-rush engagement, never feeling quite like I’d lost control but always like I was on the edge of tumbling into disaster. What’s more I felt like the developers really respected me as a player. Levels are short enough that I could get two or three runs in waiting for dinner to cook, but diverse and challenging enough that I could burn an hour or so striving for that gold rank. It caters to both skill and cleverness in equal parts, allowing players to progress either by mastering the standard pathway or finding shortcuts in the run, but to achieve the highest rank the player must both find the shortcuts and also master them. And to top it off the level design is a treat. An elegant, thematic world that is distinct in each section but with a thread of stylistic continuity in it that ties everything together.*Chef’s Kiss*In fact, the gameplay is so good, it actually made me like the story. Don’t get me wrong, it’s objectively terrible writing, but because I liked the gameplay so much the story went from simply bad to *endearingly* bad. It was no longer just a horrifically edgy narrative told by someone with only a passing familiarity with how the world and relationships work, it was a horrifically edgy narrative told by someone I wanted to succeed, and gosh darn it, at least they’re trying.

Everything down to the UI is perfectly crafted.This is well worth the money. The fact that it is less than half the price of a full priced game is insane considering the quality and quantity of content in this game. If you like first person platformers at all, buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: about an hour and a half into the game and I love it. The soundtrack, style, and voice acting are all enough to carry the game on it's own, but the gameplay is the most satisfying and fluid feeling thing I've felt in a game period. The Gameplay: It plays exactly how you would want it to. Each level is essentially a puzzle trying to figure out the exact way to finish it as fast as possible. If the Gun card mechanic worries you, don't let it. It was a little bit worrying initially but it didn't take any time for it to feel natural. If you enjoy the fast pace style action of Ultrakill, this is exactly what you're looking for.The Voice Acting: The voice acting is very good for the most part. Some, specifically the main character played by Steve Blum of cowboy bebop fame, put in much better performances than others, but no-one feels downright bad. The visual novel aspects taken from Persona are very natural, and if they don't interest you it doesn't seem to have any real effect on the game (only an hour and a half in tho)The soundtrack is godlike, literally the reason I bought the game. Machinegirl is a great duo and their contribution to the game really takes this experience from great to amazing.My only complaint, and this is very much personal preference, is that I don't really like Vaporwave aesthetics. The level design certainly does have this artstyle, and by no means is it a turnoff for me nor do I think it's a fault of the game. It's also worth noting that it's very tame with the aesthetics, it's not overbearing whatsoever. Overall, I'm loving this experience and I wholeheartedly recommend this for anyone a fan of Persona, Ultrakill, Machingirl, or good games in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought it, played it for 6 hours straight and felt absolutely zero fatigue from it, went to sleep at 4am, woke up, played for 5 hours straight the very next day, ate dinner, then when I was done I finished the game and got 100% completion, ONE DAY AFTER PURCHASING. _childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun and addicting game with amazing playability. The game is highly replayable, incentivizing you to improve your records, earn medals, and surpass other players. The dialogue is extremely cringe-inducing, and while I think it was made with that in mind as a parody, I understand why some people may be turned off by it. Personally, I find it entertaining with how over-the-top it is. The levels are really short, with some exceptions, and the point is to play them over and over until you think, "I did good enough". With that in mind, if you're the type of person who plays once or twice and moves on to the next level, you may find the game to be relatively short. I have 79 hours in the game, and while I spent some time messing around, that's the time it took me to 100% the game while setting some relatively high goals for myself in the rankings.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the only game that has ever gotten me to really try to perfect going fast. _childDocuments_.review: This game blew my expectations out of the water, and sent it straight into orbit. This game is a masterpiece.Gameplay is absorbing, creative, challenging, multifacited, and smooth as butter. The difficulty setting is really awesome in that they don't ask too much from the player to continue throughout the game but invite a substantial challenge if that's what the player is after. The level design invites problem solving and creative thinking while making each moment to moment interaction really engaging and fun.The story is interesting, not too overdone, and it has some really great moments. I like that it breaks up the gameplay and keeps you from burning out from playing the levels. It also makes your efforts feel like they're worthwhile when you get different interactions with the characters. The music is beautiful and fits so well in every different area of the game. It definitely makes me a fan of Machine Girl and want to check out more of their music.The graphics and UI are really stylish and unique. I love how clear everything looks. It makes it easier to know what's going on when you're flying through the levels. Not only that but the UI has everything right in an industry where practically every other game developer is doing it wrong. Neon White makes everything simple and informative. It looks fantastic and I think more games should strive to have a clean and thoughtful UI like this one.Every element of game design has been customized to fit together perfectly in Neon White. The gameplay is the core framework with enough horsepower to keep you going through the levels; the story enriches and gives background to the gameplay and the environment (so that everything you're doing doesn't feel completely meaningless); the music enriches the experience tenfold;  and the graphics are the artistic touch that completes the whole package.If you're a fan of fps, action games, puzzle games, or vibing to badass music, then I recommend Neon White. If you like all of these things, then I recommend you put it at the top of your list of games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect combination of FPS and puzzle-platformer where everything is fast and stylish. It's very addicting to replay levels again and again to get faster times. Every level has something unique to solve and every card is fun in its own way.On the technical side of things, the performance was totally smooth the entire way for me, and I didn't encounter any bugs during my playthrough. My game time was about 20 hours when I completed the game 100% with both endings. But, there is still lots of stuff to do, like level rushes and hidden red medals for each level.The soundtrack is really very good, compliments each mission and the game's style perfectly. I found myself listening to some tracks outside of the game-- it stands on its own really well. Same for the art, it fits the tone of the game perfectly and is very well done.The characters' personalities and plot was not bad and I found myself liking the cast and setting of Neon White's Heaven overall. The voice acting maybe not so much though, and didn't quite hit the "so bad it's good" mark for me. But, the good thing here is that voices can easily be muted in the options. Writing overall I didn't love but there are some funny jokes in there. I will say think it works better just as text.Core of the game though, and most of the game time, is running through missions and levels which again are just so enjoyable. It's not all that often that such a unique and creative project feels as complete as Neon White. I really recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, has an old school score based feel to it, you end up wanting to replay levels over and over in an attempt to go faster each time.Gameplay is sort of a FPS, puzzle platforming, speedrunner; each level features a series of obstacles and your goal is simply to figure out how to get to the end as fast as possible, often while making sure every enemy in the level is dead. The most unique feature is the weapons that function like standard FPS guns (pistol, shotgun, rocket launcher, etc) but with the added mechanic of being able to discard them to use a special ability; pistols launch you vertically, SMG's fire out a sticky grenade, and so on. This is what adds the puzzle element to the game as you try to figure out where best to use the limited number of weapon abilities you have.The presentation is excellent, at first glance it might seem very simplistic with plain looking levels, basic enemies, and no gun models. But once you play the game it's clear this is by design, you need to see as much as possible so weapon models would just be in the way, and enemies/items need to stand out clearly against the plain backgrounds or the game would be borderline unplayable.The one thing I didn't like is the story and characters which initially put me off purchasing the game when I first saw it. Luckily you don't need to pay any attention to the story to enjoy the game and can fast forward through all dialogue and most cutscenes, so it's not too intrusive.

_childDocuments_.review: Mastering a game well enough to speedrun it takes hundreds of hours. Neon White makes you feel like a speedrunner within the first few minutes of play.Neon White is a first person platformer, with soul cards that act both as guns and offensive movement abilities. For example, the “Godspeed” card is both a sniper rifle and a dash that kills enemies. Every card opens up the game further, and gives you choices on how to best navigate your way through the levels.The level design is on point, and is what makes the game. You are eased into new mechanics as you go. Part of the speedrunning theme is finding optimizations and skips within the levels. To that end, the game provides you with a hint each level, as well as a gift hidden in the level to encourage you to take a step back and explore the level. The environment in the levels is stunning, but also readable.If I had to give some nitpicks, I think the rocket launcher (Dominion card) was introduced a bit late. I am sure there’s plenty of people who put the game down before reaching levels with the Dominion card, which is a shame, because it has the most fun mobility out of all the soul cards. I also found the side dialogue (which is part of your reward for finding gifts) a bit cringe at times, and sometimes off-base with the main story.Neon White has been receiving its praise for a reason. It is super satisfying to go fast and find clever skips and execute on them. Neon White is absolutely great at what it does - play it and become the speedrunner you were always meant to be.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game that is a bit complicated to describe to someone else if you're taking all of its parts into account. It's a first person shooter, yes, but it's also a high-speed, high-precision platformer with deck-building elements, and a story presented in the style of a cheesy visual novel. Any one of those elements might sound like a turn-off, but all of these disparate sounding elements feel totally in sync when you're actually playing it.Its bite sized levels are beautifully designed, providing high amounts of visual spectacle while still being clean and readable as a player. The art direction reminded me greatly of Mirror's Edge, where the levels are mostly comprised of white and grey colors while enemies and important level design elements are bright primary and secondary colors that stand out against the stage layouts. They are perfect for speedrun optimizations, with entire sections able to be skipped with creative applications of the card system. While some levels can be quite difficult and allow for very little error, your own character movement within those levels is never the obstacle. Movement as the titular Neon White is super smooth and responsive. There's a perfect level of floatiness to the jumps that, combined with extremely high levels or air control, can allow you save yourself if you do make a mistake. In the case that you do mess up completely though, restarting is a breeze. Just one button press and you're back at the beginning of the level ready to go again. The speed, game feel, and the ease of restarting can easily make you go into a "just one more level" flowstate that only ends when you reach the end of each chapter. The music is a major part of why this happens as well. Machine Girl's original soundtrack feels uniquely tailored to fit this game's surreal world. It's a dreamy and otherworldly electronic score that is punctuated with vocal samples that somehow never get distracting even in the midst of a difficult level.You'll also be motivated to explore each level further to find the collectible items hidden in each. That's because the collectible items help advance your relationships with other characters in the visual novel parts of the game in a system very similar to the Social Link system from the Persona series. You get not only extra dialogue which lets you learn more about each of the characters and their history with the protagonist, but also entire new levels with unique gimmicks that are challenging in their own right. This gives an extra dimension to the collectibles that make them feel less like a checklist item and give them extra meaning if you enjoy the characters.Speaking of the characters, they can be  cringey at times. I would understand why some people might be turned off by the story because of how the characters are written. The game's art has a strong anime inspired look, but it is written less like an actual anime and more like an anime fanfiction written by internet dwelling, trope-loving westerners. Maybe it's just because I read a lot of anime discourse on the western internet and have watched some abridged series, but I found this style charming despite how over the top it was. The good news is that it doesn't ever detract from the gameplay.I implore you to check this game out if any of this sounds interesting to you. As odd as all of the elements sound, it all clicks into a game that is pure fun for the entire runtime.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny all the complaints about Neon White are related to the cringey writing when the actual game part of this video game is the real issue. First few areas are a blast and got me super hooked right out the gate to the point where I was aiming for all the dev times on every level. Problem is that thrill doesn't last, and it's all because of the level design. I don't think the devs had enough faith in their own gameplay because they start to follow the sort of default video game blueprint of adding boss fights, making levels longer, and uping the difficulty. These things aren't in inherently bad but the combo of all of them on top of many levels being pretty bad at telegraphing what to do/where to go makes the later half of the game not fun in the slightest.Gone was my immediate want to replay a level to grind down my time instead replaced by a relief that I would never have to play that level again. Boss fights just don't work with the speedrunning feel of the game, having to wait for a boss to move through phases and shooting him while he's standing completely still does not translate to fast paced or fun game design. I think if the game just focused on ramping up the difficulty and introducing new mechanics into the shorter paced level design of the first few areas it would have been a great way to progress the gameplay while still keeping that great speedrunning feel. Sadly the devs did not have enough confidence in their own gameplay formula and relied on industry norms to progress the game, which leaves the later half of the game an unfun slog. I don't think I'm the only one who feels this way either as at the start my friends list had way more people on the times and as the game went on more and more people stopped playing. Oh and yeah the writing is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful too. I had to actively look over my shoulder out of embarrassment every time violet was on screen hoping no one would hear any of her dialogue. It's funny because I think the main issue with the writing is similar to the gameplay, the devs not having enough confidence in their own writing and instead relying on painfully unfunny internet humour. I know people say "it's supposed to be cringe" but just because you made your writing suck on purpose doesn't make it suck any less.

_childDocuments_.review: Speedrunning is cool, but I've never seen myself realistically getting into it. Its just such a time commitment while there are so many games to play. Neon White gives you the experience of speedrunning and its fantastic. Levels have an 'intended path' but as you repeat them you find ways to break them and skip huge portions to save time, or little optimizations to shave off just a half second more. However, because each level is so small restarting is effortless. Failing right at the end isn't so frustrating when you were just 20 seconds away from the start. The game is very smartly designed to accomplish its speedrunning experience. Only giving the player ranks and leaderboards after they have shown to understand the level keeps you from being overwhelmed.This game is fantastic, and good luck finding a game like it.

_childDocuments_.review: Best of Ghostrunner, Mirrors edge, and seasonal shounen anime. Has everything you would want in a video game. Only real issues is things outside the game play but those are skippable if you can't handle anime-isms.While Neon White says its an Action-Fast pace-Freerunning-Yuighoi-First Person game, its feels more Puzzle-Fast-ish Pace-Freerunning-Yuighoi- First Person game.---- . Filled with fun, replayability, and mechanics that you won't be bored with. Like I mentioned before, NW is a puzzle and action but I feel it uses action as the mean to accomplish the puzzle. You will be using your critical thinking skills and puzzle solving more than you reflexes and FPS tech skills.- . NW has a ♥♥♥♥ tons of stages but I never felt it was bloated. From starting to end, each Chapter introduces new cards, enemies, and mechanics that builds on top of the crazy foundation NW laid out for itself. Scoreboards, metals, and bragging rights will keep you playing the same stage for 50+ times to get that red metal.- . TBH, blue metals are pretty easy to get when you learn the built-in short cut and have pretty decent movement FPS skills. NW is pretty clear in its difficulty. There is the straightforward path and then the shortcut. However, there is another layer where the actual freaks come out. In order to get red metals, you have to either do the shortcut path perfectly or find a new pathing to shave off milliseconds. NW is pretty easy to get into, pretty easy to do well, very hard to be amazing- Machine Girl brought in the heat. Take the music of Ultrakill, then instead of dark, hellish, ugly edgy its more of an otherworldly, artsy, modern edgy. The sound does its job pretty well. Nothing out of place and provides good feedback to the player.- . Take Mirrors Edge, Western take of anime style, and celestial elements and mix it into a modern abstract design direction. Very bold and confident. Very readable and little clutter. UI, menus, etc all work well. While i can easily nitpick specific things, these things don't effect gameplay and the core aesthetics elevates everything else.- . A lot of the core themes and concepts are actually not that bad. Themes such as redemption, religion/religious organizations , and loyalty are used and sometimes work. Only a few characters are like-able. However NW is a very gameplay first, second, third type game. Still story is workable for what they are trying to do Some aspects of the story works well such as Red and the angels. Hell the believers aren't that bad from a story perspective. I actually liked Red's redemption story, Mikey's loyality to god, and Rez's sympathy for the sinful. The believers is a pretty on the nose with the religious organization theme. These parts work pretty well.However characters such as Violet, Green, and Yellow needs some work. Violet's struggle is feeling not good enough in the crew and always comparing herself to White. I feel NW leans way to much on the psycho-yandere too much which doesn't build her into a sympathetic character. She is desperate for Green's validation however I don't remember any part of the story where the player would see a reason for said validation. I don't remember any point where Green actually complements or acknowledges violet. This relationship needs to be fleshed out more in order for us to even care about Violet's struggles and actions.Yellow dies early and is just a "bro". IMO dies way to early for any interesting real development.Green is "too evil". In a game where redemption and forgiveness is a theme, hell one of the endings is forgiveness, Green is barely forgivable. Green hates blue so much that it costs everyone's life but why does Green hate Blue?  He goes mad filled with revenge and hatred but we need a reason to even consider forgiveness. If blue was a character we meet in-game, it could have provided a good avenue to flesh out Green-  While the aesthetics are on point, it usually masks the actual graphics. If you look closely you will see the graphics are actually very average. Some 3d models, shading, etc are kind awkward. The maps are very bare. BUT you don't play NW for graphics and what they have optimized, still looks good, and is good enough for the game platforms NW is on.  - Not much tbh- . _childDocuments_.review: Alright, I have 100%'d this game so I feel I can make a review now.I'm gonna start with the story, as its by far the most contentious part of the game. Personally? I don't hate it. I found myself caring about the characters more than I thought I would. The writing is self aware but it's not rubbing your face in it. Though, maybe I'm a bit of a sucker for sappy stories like this. But, no-one is coming to this game for the story (I hope, anyway).The gameplay is... superb. Whenever I played this game I was constantly reminded of TrackMania, where you're competing against yourself and medal times. Shaving off those hundredths of a second feels so good, and when you discover a skip by yourself, it's a fantastic feeling. Everything in this game feels polished to an absurd degree, and I love it. Small details like adding a small plank leading off a platform so you can hold forward through the whole thing really adds up, and this game is full of things like that. Stuff that is easy to overlook, but with how insanely good the devs are at this game (I have 2 author medals, with a handful of top 100 times for reference), you can tell that the levels have been refined over dozens if not hundreds of hours per level.The movement is top-notch, and extremely fluid. This game is a pleasure to play, as it's very easy to get into the rhythm of the level and blast through it, making you feel like a gamer god.Comparing it to another very similar game Warstride Challenges, I prefer the movement in this way more. You don't have to constantly bhop, or anything like that to gain speed. It's nice, and lets you focus on your actual movement instead of making sure you hit the same buttons on a 10 frame window. The gun-card mechanic feels great, and you rarely feel like you don't know where to go next due to the great level design. I could go on for ages about this game and all the stuff it does right, but it's hard enough focusing my thoughts on the game enough to get this review to this point. It does so many things right, it's hard to list them all.10/10.

The anime tropes are a pretty common complaint I hear about the game, but frankly none of it got too overwhelming for me. I really did enjoy the story and I like most of the characters, maybe one or two get a little grating. Regardless, this is genuinely one of my top games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: So, for most of the game, the gameplay here ranges from pretty good to really, really good. I like doing speedrunning routing-type things, but I kind of hate the fiddly parts, and the way neon white streamlines out the obnoxious parts while still leaving room for a ton of small tricks and ideas is very well done, and both normal movement and the card discard movements feel great. If you'd asked me how I felt a little before halfway through, I would have said it's a great game tied to an absolutely terrible story, but would have given it a recommend for people who really like this type of game (this is reflected in my hours, since I spent a lot of time optimizing the early chapters before moving on to later ones)However, there's two reasons that, now that I've beaten it, I wouldn't recommend it.The minor reason is that the gameplay gradually gets worse, until by the last few chapters, I wasn't really enjoying it very much. It tries to make each chapter more complex than the last, but by doing so, they mostly make them more linear and force you onto their chosen path through the level more and more, until by the end there's rarely a meaningful discovery the player can make to save time beyond just doing minor adjustments to the developer-intended line. The final chapter in particular gives you an ability that is supposed to be extremely fun but instead fully puts you on rails.The bigger problem, though, is the story. It starts out pretty cringy, full of obnoxious anime things that they're knowingly doing intentionally out of a misguided attempt to feel like shlocky 90s anime. It just keeps getting worse, though, and the game keeps forcing you to engage with it by kicking you out to the hub, and not even allowing you to skip the story, instead only reluctantly letting you "fast forward" though them. The story is still THERE, however, and I suspect most people will end up seeing it anyway simply because it's a full half of the game. The story gradually shifts from annoying, to unpleasantly horny, to outright reprehensible. By the end, the game has:Given you an absolutely terrible panty shot from the woman who looks, acts, and is treated like an underage girl.Made the main character have a weird, predatory gay abusive relationship with the main villain (who is the only gay character in the game, and is absolutely depicted like the stereotypical gay panic villain from something that, well, would have been released in the 90s, so I guess the game successfully did a throwback in this case)Made the moral of the story "you should forgive your abusers".Even if the story wasn't "problematic", it's just awful, unpleasant writing that is failing even at being knowingly bad. It makes you sit through several character arcs, all of which are doing the exact same thing over and over while trying and failing to be campy. All of these arcs end by dramatically revealing something that was already discussed several times previously, confusingly acting like we don't already know? I was one of the co-captains of the anime club in high school, for god's sake, I SHOULD be the target audience here, and I only stomached it because I was streaming it to my friends and we all had to know how much worse this got. The story gets in the way of the gameplay where it can, too, and vice versa. Narratively, you're supposed to be in constant danger from demons, but since this is a speedrunning game, the enemies are basically just still targets. By the end, it didn't really matter to me if I was enjoying the gameplay or not, the whole package of the game made me wish I'd never enjoyed it in the first place, because that just made me think about it more.The music is really good, though. If you want to play this game, I'd recommend getting a machine girl album instead, and then playing that while you do a surf map. It might not have as much variety as this game, but at least you won't be giving money to people who are somehow still 90s anime perverts.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon white didn't quite stick the landing for me, but I'd recommend it to people who like time trial platforming. While I enjoyed my initial few hours playing through these fast paced and tightly controlled time trial FPS/platforming missions, they started to feel repetitive, though the levels themselves were different. Part of that is that while the environments changed, there were no environment specific mechanics, which mean the levels all felt like they blended in. Another reason for this is that the levels feel very scripted the movements and weapons you get clearly point you toward how you are "supposed" to complete the level for time, and leave little justification to explore how to get better times. Despite these downsides, the controls are great, and the feeling in an individual level is fun, it just wore out after a while. Beyond that there's nothing much to write about. The flat, cliche characters and uninspired writing cannot be saved by the literally legendary voice talent (Steve Blum, SungWon Cho, among others) or, frankly, the interesting premise. If you are the type of person who enjoys tight control time trial platforming, and would be interested in best breaking a game to get the fastest speed, you will thoroughly enjoy this, but if you are looking for a deeper experience with stronger game and character development, this isn't for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is an extremely fun speedrunning FPS game where you use cards to traverse through well-designed levels as quick as you can. There is some neat dialogue that can be pretty cringe-y at times, but it's the goofy cringe you'd see in most modern anime, so it's not a big deal. The only downside I can point out is that the difficulty seems to be a pretty stale line, but considering I have only played till the 4th Mission, this could change.Oh, and the soundtrack is pretty dope.I would definitely recommend this to any fan of movement shooters, it is a very unique, non-linear experience!

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome, White Neon, to a land that is not yours. Your mission is to kill these demons with the killers around you to have the chance to live here. And the way to kill them is either by using the weapons in the world or to sacrifice these weapons in order to use their abilities. It's a very unique and beautiful game system, I enjoyed it from start to finish and when you finish each stage, other things will open for you, such as collecting a gift in the world to gift it to one of the characters or trying to finish the stage as fast as possible. As for the gifts, you give to the characters, they either open up a new discussion for you to know the characters story, or they open up new challenges for you to play.Each game has its own drawbacks. In this game...the story here is the big disadvantage. the story has no meaning at all. And thanks to the developers that they put the skip button because the story never got me hooked. Because in the beginning and at the end, you came to play the challenges and not to listen to the story.The game uses cartoon graphics to express itself and also uses 2D graphics when talking, which is acceptable and somewhat beautiful. As for the music, it is very beautiful and makes you immerse yourself in playing.There are few jumping games that deserve praise and this one is one of them but unfortunately.. its story is below average. If you are looking for fun and jumping games, then this game is for you without a doubt.aaaaaaaaaand that it <3

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really really good. I don't even know what genre to put it in. I guess it's technically a movement shooter/parkour game, but what it really feels like is a puzzle game with the pace of a million miles a minute. It's incredibly fun, not only to just play through, but also to replay levels for high scores. I normally don't do that - I almost NEVER have motivation to do extra stuff like that in a game, but I do for this game!  I also really enjoy how, in most speedrunning games, going fast is contigent on good fine motor skills, reaction time, and reflex, of which I have none. Here, it's based on quick thinking, good planning, and recognizing landmarks. If I had one gripe, it's that it's a bit too easy to get those high scores, and you get no in game rewards for doing so. Getting 'gold' means perfecting the signposted route, getting silver is doing the signposted route meh, getting bronze is "wow, you managed to beat the level at some point." Ace is the most fun one by far, and its goal is to find an alternate route in the level that's way faster. Finding these routes on your first pass requires some fun lateral thinking at very high speeds, and it requires you to not just blindly go forwards. Sadly, there are hint markers that unlock once you get Gold (which I usually get on my first pass through the level) that kind of spoil the fun. There's also gifts, which are either very well hidden or very difficult to get to, or both. You need to take your time, conserve cards, and take time to look at the scenery to find these, and these are more of a slow-paced puzzle in comparison to the main "hyperspeed" pace of the rest of the level. The art style is really great, I love its portrayal of heaven as a super-sanitary, kind of unpleasant tourist-trap tier vacatino town, a la disneyworld and the surrounding area. The aesthetics in general are top notch with use of color and detail and just everything.The music is really great. I'm not a massive breakcore fan, but this soundtrack does it just subtly enough to be incredible and genuinely fun and disarming, matching the pace of the gameplay. It is so good it has me looking up other songs by this artist. I highly reccomend the soundtrack. The writing is the one weak part. It ranges from "so-bad-it's-good cheesy anime" to "kill me now". I genuinely felt embarassed listening to the writing and voice acting - I looked behind my shoulder any time the dreadful e-girl character came on just because it was so cringy. It gave me actual shudders. I despised EVERY. SINGLE. CHARACTER. with the slight exception of the main character, who is the most sane and talks in a non-annoying voice making sarcastic quips.  Every other one has awful writing and awful voice acting. This normally wouldn't be a problem, but the gift mechanic is borrowed from Hades, and you can give gifts to characters to build relationship status. The issue - giving gifts MAKES THEM SAY MORE DIALOGUE! I was actively discouraged from finding the gifts in levels, even though that's very fun content, because I dreaded having to hear more dialogue from these characters. It especially sucks since they have super fun, challenging sidequests that are gated behind this awful dialogue! I reccomend using the F key to fast forward through all dialogue, otherwise I'd go insane. Unfortunately, this left gaps in context as to why I was here and such, however, I didn't skip the important cutscenes and got the general gist. If anything, it makes a fun game of how much of the story you can piece together from just the snippets of cutscenes you get alone. But god that voice acting... and writing.... I want to drown myself.Overall - the gameplay is top tier. GET IT NOW for that alone. Never touch the story with a ten foot pole unless you are a weeb who's mind has already been rotted from the inside out. It's not "so bad it's good", it's "so bad it's painful" in the way a bad comedy movie is.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a game I can only kinda recommend. It does some things very well, and others.. not so much to the point where it's a huge drag on an otherwise good platformer.At its core, Neon White is a game made for going fast and speedrunning. Levels are graded only on how fast it took you to finish them, but the developers did a surprisingly good job making it not suck in that you only need a time that's usually pretty easy to achieve to "clear" the level, and can then beat a harder time to unlock speedrun leaderboards. When it's fun, it's really fun. There are a lot of levels you can clear without ever stopping and in some cases without ever touching the ground because you're constantly explosion-jumping like a deranged human kangaroo with dynamite for feet, and these levels feel amazing. There's good signposting, it's not hard to figure out what it is you're supposed to do, and a lot of the technique to getting a good time is figuring out how to cut corners or what the "secret" of the level is rather than optimizing button presses.Then there's the not so great. A couple of the powerups kinda suck, namely the "Godspeed" one, which causes you to airdash in a straight line without gaining or losing altitude. Godspeed consistently feels either too long or too short for whatever you need it for - I can't even count the number of times it kills an enemy but then stops short of destroying the explosive barrels two inches behind the enemy that I needed to be able to jump over an obstacle. What's odd about this is that you eventually get a powerup called "Fireball" that does everything Godspeed does except you can gain altitude off it, and it feels fine in most cases once you get the hang of maximizing height gain with it.The problem is that for every good level, there are several that made me question if they were designed by an entirely different team. One in particular, about halfway through the game, effectively requires you to precisely snipe with a grenade in order to kill a set of enemies halfway across the stage - it's a crapshoot at best to the point where even speedrunners can't seem to get it down consistently. It's an oddity in a game where precision aiming usually isn't required.Then there are the stages where the developers go "Screw it, let's turn this into Super Meat Boy" where every surface is lined with death spikes that have a hitbox about twice as large as they need to have. The problem is that the underlying mechanics really don't support this, and a lot of levels feel like they need frame-perfect or near-frame-perfect input to complete. A few of these I looked at and said "I have no idea how I would do this if I was using a controller" because there's simply no way to turn fast enough.The game is good when it's good, but then becomes godawful at certain points. I would not recommend trying to 100% it, and it might be worth waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game with a unique action + reflex + puzzle mix with well designed levels.Very fun to replay the levels and figure out how to beat them faster to get the high score, or to beat your friends times.Story is ok, with a surprisingly good voice cast + voiced lines.Easily skipped by any that want to just play the levels.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White does an amazing job making you feel like a speedrunning pro. It starts off almost every chapter introducing a new mechanic, whether that be a new enemy type or a new weapon (which also doubles as a movement ability). You get a few levels to learn about its quirks and play around with it, then it starts ramping up the difficulty by weaving in mechanics you've seen and mastered from previous chapters. You don't really think about this while playing. It feels very natural and intuitive, and you never end up confused as to how something works.Even if your reaction times aren't super fast, Neon White is fairly generous about its time requirements to clear each level. You can finish the game by only going for Gold medals, earned by clearing par times that allow for a couple mistakes. More seasoned players will probably want to go for the Ace medal (or even the Red/Developer medal), which are largely for bragging rights. It's all the more reason to replay levels again, and again, and again.Your mileage may vary on the writing and voice acting. It leans into some anime tropes to the point of being cringey at times, and the developers were no doubt aware of this. I enjoyed reveling in the stupidity of it, but it's certainly not for everyone. Thankfully, you can just skip all of the dialogue.Topping it all off is the excellent soundtrack by Machine Girl. It's not quite as crazy as some of their other material, but it fits the gameplay perfectly. Seriously, whoever got them for the OST is a genius.If you love speedrunning, you will love this game. If you don't like speedrunning, you will love it after playing this game.
