_childDocuments_.review: I feel like a lot of games like this one have a tendency to lean really heavily on being extremely difficult to execute-having deep but sometimes impenetrable control schemes and mechanics. Neon White is not that game. Neon White wants you to go fast. It captures the FEEL of getting really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good at one of those games, while still feeling very doable and accessible. There's not really any other game I can think of that so effectively sucked me in, made me NEED to keep trying every level until I got that medal, no matter how unimportant it was in the end.I'm also quite a fan of the story, although I fully understand why it's kind of divisive. It starts off with some VERY aggressively tropey anime nonsense, which I'm fine enough with to get past and into the rest of the story, which I think has some very genuinely interesting things to say with its depiction of Heaven and angels. I wouldn't blame anyone for being turned off by the initial impression, but it's a lot better than it might seem.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a game that right from the start you'll be putting yourself into a flow state finishing the levels. The movement and abilities you use all feel natural and satisfying, the enemies are weak but they still have a presence in the level due to you having to use them and the items they drop to progress, and the levels are extremely short, taking only around 30 seconds to complete on average, and a minute when they start to get longer. Because of this the game isn't very long and it's quite easy, to beat the game, but the game rewards you and encourages you to go beyond and put in the extra effort to get better times on the levels and not just complete a level, but master it. The level designs provoke imaginative shortcuts and small optimisations that go a long way when every second saved begins to count.The art style is unique and appealing while not distracting you too much from the gameplay, the music is made by Machine Girl so you know it's gonna be fire, the only downside is the story and dialogue, but even that I came to appreciate as the game went on. Early game it felt like the writers lacked confidence in their writing, and tried to make the game a self aware parody of itself while also trying to progress the story, and it ended up only coming off as cringey, however it seems like as the game went on the writers gained more confidence in the story they wanted to tell and the writing, while nothing phenomenal, was interesting and appealing enough that I was still entertained.Neon White goes hard.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is a testament to its inspirations, a lovely ride to hop on for, and more than well worth the money. being a fast-paced card game FPS with speed-running elements may initially be a bit of a mouthful - after all, how can you even incorporate a card game into something that runs so fast as to describe itself as speed-running? but this game weaves all of its separate elements together in an endlessly replayable package for whoever wants to pick it up and learn. all of the mechanics are incorporated in a way that is easy to understand and use, yet hard to master (which i think is what keeps me coming back.) let's start with the lore. you take on the guise of Neon White, a sinner who was pulled out of the Ocean of Heaven and scouted as an assassin to deal with Heaven's rampaging demon problem. he becomes part of a competition against people he... knew? it's all a bit fuzzy, as our protagonist faces amnesia for himself and his life before heaven. seems straightforward enough, until you slowly yet surely realise that what you are facing has more covetous corners than you could have foreseen. learning that no one is to be trusted and that things aren't quite what they seem is a slow yet inevitable realisation that comes with its fair share of questioning as you blast through level after level. the card game mechanics of this game are unique and refreshing, offering up individualised ways of completing each level. if one person can do so the intended way, another can totally break the level open like a fresh jar of heavenly cornichons. the varied paths through each level are not only present but encouraged, as you compare your time against every player who opts to have their time shared on the leaderboard. one thing that brings this feature down is the presence of hackers, however the devs seem proficient in removing them from the rotation. competing against yourself and others to get the fastest time on each level is a delight, and while monotonous at times, you tend to forget all about the repetition in favour of just improving upon yourself. the medal system is an excellent incentive, and each rank unlocks something new for the level. not only is there combat and high-score based gameplay, but there is also more visual novel-esque gameplay features. you scout around levels finding gifts for your buddies and baddies alike, all to uncover more and more about the past you're not yet privy to. the characters are slightly one-note, but do bear pretty complex and intriguing stories once you take the time to get to know them. in terms of its lore, while very streamlined, it offers up a lot of room for interpretation. with rich lore stemming from the depictions of the Hebrew Bible, it is most certainly is not an experience to be missed. slowly piecing together what happened in order to bring our protagonist, deuterotagonists, and even our antagonists to heaven is awesome, and brings with it plenty of unexpected twists and turns. it's best to go in blind, so i won't spoil much - but you're 100% going to want to get all the endings. in terms of how the characters interact with each other, well... for some, it can be a bit off putting. it fits the theming of the experience well, being modern, quick, and snappy. however, it is very much so on the cuff of current culture, so we can't fully tell how well the dialogue and interactions will age... but for the time being, it's satisfactory, if a little cringey at times. but that's exactly how i, personally, love my games to be. overall, Neon White is a fantastic experience with excellent gameplay, awesome music, and compelling characters that sucks you in with a rich world and many features to keep you coming back for more. i would most certainly recommend it to anyone and everyone. addendum : my first review for this game proclaimed my love for the level Canals, and i can still say i absolutely adore it. while i'm no longer in my previously achieved top 400 spot, i still think it's the most fun level and i look forward to returning to the grind to get back into the leaderboard! boy do i ever love Canals.

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the only game ever where I'm seriously considering getting 100% completionAmazing game. Very easy to learn, but getting good times is where it gets hard. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is stunning and addictive in the best way, making you want to try again and again to shave just that extra millisecond off your run. _childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: Ok finally finished Neon White and boy is it a great game. Break neck action, style and character in this shooter parkour hybrid. Your goal is essentially to clear the stage by defeating every enemy and reach the stage clear platform. To do this we are given cards which are both a weapon and a movement gimmick. Every single card has a firing mode and a movement gimmick attacked to it where the firing works like any other weapon in any game and has a limited number of ammunition but the movement gimmick discards the card entirely. This creates situations where you need to decide if you want to use the card's movement to clear obstacles or if you want to use the card to kill demons. You can have two weapons at the same time and you can stack cards 3 times meaning you'll be able to use the movement ability 3 times in a row. Cards are all color coded so the player can identify them from afar. Every shotgun card will be red and work as a shotgun or as a close range omnidirectional charge, every pistol will be yellow, work as a pistol, and provide a double jump etc...It's one of those games that make you want to get better, you know you won't ace the stage right away (well sometimes you do but that's another story) which makes you want to get back in there and shave those seconds off.The pros:- Fast paced action.- There's a real flow to the game, you start getting into a trance like state where the stages are like dances and you're weaving pinpoint accurate shots in between dashes and platform jumping.- I felt like I've become actually better at playing fast paced shooters after clearing every stage on Ace and some on the red trophy.- Finding some of the shortcuts was super fun, you can just follow the path, you can use the shortcut the devs intended or, in later stages, you can just rocket jump up a skyscraper and then drop on the finish line for some sweet 8 second clears.- Machine Girl made a great soundtrack.- Art's great, characters are interesting and the feel of the game is....- The characters are fun, there's some good humor.Cons:- I feel like there weren't enough times where you had to juggle the weapons around, most of the time whenever you are given a weapon you are meant to use it to kill or to clear obstacles. I only ever did this when I was skipping stuff and that was mostly because the section I'd skip to would demand a different movement skill.Personal Cons:- The story. It's not bad, it's a story and it's perfectly functional. Story spoilers start now. Tl;dr if you wanna get better at twitch shooters while you're having fun, forget those trainer games, get this in stead it's incredibly fun.A more than solid 9/10. Don't forget: you can't ask a girl if she's had incontinence.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a deft blend of genres, half of which are misnomers. Neon White has been regarded as a “speedrunning” game and a “card-based” game, but how much does that actually say about the experience of playing the game itself?Personally, I’d wager Neon White is more similar to games like Trackmania and Super Monkey Ball than it is to a speedrun of any game. Sure, you go fast in Neon White, but speedrunning encapsulates much more than just that. Speedruns are engineered to carefully pick apart an intended gameplay experience, to forcefully bend a game to the needs of the speedrun. There’s a sense that you’re breaking something in a speedrun; Neon White provides that feeling, but gives it structure.Moment to moment, in the heat of its levels, Neon White pulls you into a flow state of mastery. Once the funky Machine Girl soundtrack kicks in, it’s go time. The goal is simple: kill all enemies and get to the end as fast as you can. The movement is tight, air control is perfect, and the levels are designed to keep you moving forward. Cards are used as weapons like pistols, or they can be discarded for some sort of movement verb like slamming down or gaining an extra jump. Chasing new records is half the appeal of Neon White, and the levels are designed to accommodate that.Neon White trains you to aggressively look for faults in its levels. If there’s a long parkour section, there is usually a way to bypass it entirely using some cheeky movement tech. Collectible gifts are also present on most levels, shifting the gameplay from a speedy time trial to something of a movement puzzle. Learning to save cards for just the right time to nab an impossibly out of reach present is satisfying every time.The enemies that litter Neon White’s levels usually aren’t dangerous. They serve as guideposts on where to go in some of the larger levels, and they provide more cards when killed. Mimics are particularly evil.In accordance with videogame law, Neon White has a story. Whether or not you’ll like the story depends on your tolerance level of the Devil’s Paintings. Neon White is aggressively anime; the game’s art style is a dead giveaway, voice acting wonder Steve Blum voices the protagonist, and there’s lots of opportunities for men who stack no paper to pop their eyes out ogling at cartoon women. The writing is definitely made up of words and sentences!In all seriousness, I enjoy Neon White’s story, but it often feels very rigid. Going from main story content to side story content in its intended cadence feels inherently disjointed. Characters that were at each other’s throats in the main story will be having a peaceful cook-off in a side story. It’s goofy, melodramatic stuff, but the game usually maintains a good balance, and when it hits a stride the story glows. The overarching story of a group of killers summoned to the afterlife to do heaven’s dirty work is interesting all the way to the end.The labels we use to describe games like Neon White are in flux. What was once a time trial game is now a speedrunning game. I don’t think this shift is bad or even meaningful in the grand scheme of things, but it’s worth noting that I almost skipped this game because I didn’t think it’d be for me. I would have missed what might be my personal GOTY. Especially if the labels are off-putting, give the game a go; running through paradise might be just what you need.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: Before you ask, No! the statement above is not a joke. Neon White is probably the best title to introduce you into speedrunning genre. The core gameplay is superbly fast, flexible and precise (except the jump can be a bit floaty than neccessary) that you are always in control.Each level is well designed with various vibe so that you can get familiar with new variant of soul card or the combinations of them, and being short as to instantly restart whenever you feel like something is not right, that you can readjust/optimize your actions in the next attempt.And to help you further understand "the view of a speedrunner", devs are not hesitated to show hints on how to acquire the Ace medal in the level. With this, you will instinctively start to see unusual paths and want to experiment them out.As a result, the experience goes from you just following the casual paths chillingly, to taking devs' guided paths, then to you bruteforce your own ways out, that you keep getting more aggressive, more daring in your playstyle and pacing, to the point of entering Hyper mind focus state like an ascended person, pulling off insane shots and impressive maneuvers that you couldn't even believe yourself, and by the time you earn that one Red medal thing and see your score among the leaderboard, YOU NUT! And that is the only thing you should come looking for from Neon White, also the thing that carries the review score to 9 from me. The only downside is that there is no levels editor and workshop. Hopefully there will be updates on this. Just quick notes on others: - The story and visual novel stuffs are only serviceable for the gameplay, not too impressive nor being disasterly bad. - Because the voices are great yet the dialogs can be cringey most of the time, oh well at least in a good fun way. - The visuals are intended to be clean, colorful Mirror's Edge like, that your eyes can focus well on enemies, soul cards and path navigation.- People gets hyped up because Machine Girl is behind the game's OSTs, although I'm unfamiliar with the group I believe that should proves no problems, as the main menu track is vibing as f*ck.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game built on an absolutely terrific movement system that is a joy to play with and and massively satisfying to master; beating the dev times is just pure bliss. One of my favourite games of this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is simply fun to play. The levels flow well. They didn't add unnecessary complexity to running a level. One simple detail that I really appreciate is that the cards are picked up in the order that makes sense for running the level. They could have made it a mess to figure out which cards to use in which order and made you weapon swap a bunch, but they didn't. Generally, if you can get through the "intended" obvious path without wasting any time that will get you a gold rating. To get the Ace rating you usually need to go "off route" once or twice, or possibly do a weapon swap. My standard procedure for working through a level is first figure out how the path works and just complete it. Then look for the gift and figure out how to get to it. Then work on getting the ace for the level. I generally find the ace route, by thinking about what parts of the level feel slow or like I don't kill anything for a while. I figure out how to cut those parts out, and get the ace. A lot of times this will involve some sort of trick shot while moving that feels really good to finally pull off just right. Then I move on to the next level. I enjoy the whole process. I am generally a more slow and deliberate sort of player and I have trouble hording ammo and power-ups and never using them in most other games. I want to be better at free flowing and using what I have more freely. I feel like this game is helping me unlock that sort of game-play style for me. It encourages and rewards fast paced action, and makes me feel like I am good at the game.The story isn't very good. If you want a story, read a book.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok Neon White... Not bad for a dead guy huh. It ain't a FPS per se, it is more a set of stages where you race to do Time trials, good for speedrunning. The mechanics are fun, you have to proceed each stage with a "weapon" card which can shoot or do the weapon skill (stomp, dash, grapple, air jump, etc) and you have to use these cards in a certain order, like a puzzle in order to finish each level fast and good. There are a TON of them, almost 140+ stages. The game provides you a lot of variety so it does not feel repetetive, sometimes a little bit annoying with certain stages but nothing you'd be mad about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Speedrun focused first person action platformer where, apart from jumping, your abilities are decided by two currently held cards. Cards are either found or taken from certain types of enemies and give you a primary ammo based weapon attack, some that cause explosions that can be used to launch you, as well as a special more movement focused move that causes the card to be discarded. A pistol can give you a double jump, a rifle allows you to dash forward and through some obstacles, an SMG sends you slamming down on the ground while breaking obstacles, a rocket launcher acts as a grappling hood, etc. Levels may also include traps, obstacles, terrain that increases your speed, different types of explosives to propel you forward or upwards, and often a variety of enemies that need to all be killed to activate the level's exit.Controls are very responsive, the abilities are fun to use and can be combined or used in inventive ways to cut down on your time, levels are well designed and new mechanics, abilities, and level design focuses are introduced constantly, even sidequest levels you unlock from the rest of the game's cast put an interesting spin on how the game typically plays. Stages can be instantly reset at the press of a button, and it never really makes the mistake of a lot of games like this often do where the need to make things more difficult or complex as it goes on leads to just having long and confusing messes of stages near the end game, Neon White just continues to change things up so it's always interesting.Each stages allows you to finish within five frames that give you a different type of medal, unlocking a ghost of yourself to see your fasted run and path, a gift in the level that can be found and given to other characters to unlock side missions and story details, in level hints showing some of the potential shortcuts, the global leader-board once you hit platinum status, and the final rank unlocks nothing but is also completely hidden and will only be given to times far faster than what is expected out of most players. After you finish the game you unlock a mode that times you in playing through every stage in the game with the option to randomly shuffle the level order.The writing is generally at least entertaining but the slow start of the story seems at odds with the fast paced and rapidly replayable gameplay before it starts to pick up more in the latter half.Neon White is an extremely well made game that is fun enough to play through even for people that aren't good at or aren't particularly interested in speedrunning to compete with friends or other players.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is the second best game I have played this year behind only Elden Ring. The only things that could improve this game are fully voice acted dialogue and fully animated cutscenes, but as this is an indie game, I understand that is unreasonable. I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I'll start this review with the phrase "I am really impressed!"The game rocks, there are so much things about this game that are good so I'll make a list:+ Wonderful visual style, aesthetics and art design, the game looks wonderful even on not particularly high-end PCs;+ Solid plot and excellent narrative with cool characters throughout the whole game;+ Optimized & polished;+ Great and various music that goes with the main pro of the game which is the following one:+ THE GAMEPLAY. _childDocuments_.review: Neon White: A Mind-Blowing Ride Through Heaven and HellRating: ★★★★★ (5/5)Neon White is a game that doesn't just push the boundaries of what we expect from indie titles; it obliterates them entirely. This brilliant creation from developer Angel Matrix and Annapurna Interactive delivers an unforgettable gaming experience that takes you on a roller coaster ride through the afterlife, mixing elements of first-person shooters, platformers, and a surreal narrative that will leave you stunned.From the moment you dive into the world of Neon White, you're immediately struck by the game's stunning visual aesthetics. The neon-drenched, angelic and demonic realms provide a dazzling contrast of colors and atmospheres that never cease to captivate. The visual design is simply mesmerizing, and the unique art style helps create an immersive, dreamlike world that stands out in the gaming industry.The game-play mechanics in Neon White are equally remarkable. As an assassin in Heaven tasked with eliminating demonic threats, you'll find yourself sprinting through beautifully designed levels and dispatching foes in exhilarating fashion. The game encourages players to embrace both speed and precision, and the feeling of soaring through the levels is truly electrifying. The unique card-based combat system adds depth and strategy, giving you the ability to customize your character's abilities to your liking.But what sets Neon White apart is its engrossing narrative. The game explores complex themes of redemption, morality, and the afterlife, all wrapped up in a captivating story that keeps you on the edge of your seat. The characters are intriguing and well-developed, with voice acting that adds an extra layer of depth to their personalities.The game's replay-ability is enhanced by its collectibles, hidden secrets, and multiple endings, encouraging players to explore every nook and cranny of this twisted version of the afterlife.Neon White is not just a game. it is a AMAZING experience. It's a game that pushes the boundaries of storytelling and game-play while delivering a visually stunning and thought-provoking journey through Heaven and Hell. If you're looking for an indie game that breaks the mold and leaves a lasting impression, Neon White is a must-play. It's an absolute masterpiece that will have you pondering its philosophical themes long after you've beaten it and found all the secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is such a fantastic game with an addicting gameplay loop, godlike art style, and headbanging music by Machine Girl. I am not particularly good at first person shooters however the downtime of the player restarting the level and the visual clarity of the enemies helped me with being able to enjoy the shooting aspect of the game without bogging down my experience with the game. In order to progress through each level, you need to defeat every enemy using the limited gun cards along the path before making it to the end of the level. The gun cards provide an interesting and unique gameplay mechanic of using limited cards that mimics guns with the primary fire but discarding the card with the secondary fire button allows you to do a movement option which allows a bit of strategy and planning when attempting a run. The level design shines through as every level is fine-tuned to accommodate for this mechanic.The speedrunning side of the game is well done as the game is tailored to each type of gamer that either wants to beat the levels once and move on or for people chasing that high of achieving a faster time. At the end of each level, the game shows your time and the time required for each medal. By getting faster times, the game rewards you with enough clues to guide you to shortcuts in the level and getting the highest medal allows the leaderboard function to open up for the level. From there you can compare records between everyone who played the level or friends which can motivate you to replay and get a faster record. It's such a great way of easing players into the genre of speedrunning by providing a helpful clues for a beginner and a great reward for the overachievers. It makes me wish that they add a level creator so that the community can provide infinite levels for people itching to play even more Neon White.Now, the point of contention for Neon White is the story of the game where many feel like the writing and dialogue lacked the same polish as everything else. Some criticisms I hear were that the lines were cringey and the plot feels convoluted which takes them away from the gameplay whenever there was story involved on screen. Personally, I disagree with how much the story gets flak for but I can understand some reservations people have. For a game that makes you play as a dead assassin that is put into a death game to hunt demons for angels for the chance to live again, I am glad that the story isn't trying to be full on edgy but rather they tried to go towards the comedic melancholy routewith characters spouting witty lines and interact with each other in a goofy way.I say "try" as there was some jokes that made me roll my eyes but I can't help but be charmed by these idiots. The voice actors definitely felt like they were having a fun time recording which made their performance more endearing to me rather than them doing it just for a gig. If only the story in the beginning didn't rely too heavily in being comedic that when it eventually picks up near halfway, I think it provides an engaging story about redemption where the later jokes were more tasteful. I appreciate the game taking a chance to be cheesy to help me care about these demon hunters in a fun way rather than if they were hard boiled characters in game about angels and demons.Overall, this is one of best games to come out in 2022 and I recommend this for someone just looking to play something so freakishly unique with it's gameplay, art style, and music.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White got filtered out of my Steam recommendations from hitting 3 of my instant no criteria: First Person Shooter, Dating Sim, and Anime. Incredibly satisfying to fly around and shoot things at hyperspeed for good times and then puzzling out the bonus stuff.Too bad so much of the time is bogged down by anime with the quality of a high school creative writing class, but it was very polite of the devs to put in a fast forward button. Nothing is lost skipping the dialogue and getting back to the good stuff. In the RPG of life, the devs put all their points into game design and music composition. If they left the anime out entirely Neon White would be a 10, but the anime keeps interrupting the fun so minus points.Still worth. Gonna be real sad when I run out of levels.---Adding to my review after almost 100%ing (there's 2 achievements that I'll probably never be good enough at video games to get), can confirm I'm sad that I'm out of levels. It can't be emphasized enough how good it feels to be flying through these levels at a good clip, then going through and unraveling the puzzle for the fastest time. And it pisses me off so much that there's so much garbage story bogging down the game! Halyway through I started mashing the fastfoward button as soon as one of the animes starting yapping the most nothing sentences you've ever heard in your life, yet the damage is done. You'll be in a flow state, zippin and rocket launchin and having a good time, then the anime sneaks out of no where and kills the vibe. 10/10 (with anime removed) will instabuy dlc with more levels pls

_childDocuments_.review: This game is probably one of my favorite parkour games I have ever played. Gameplay-wise, it's very fast paced, and ramps up even more so as you progress. The powers that you unlock keeps the game feeling very fresh with the variety of movement options. Although it's FPS by definition, the shooting in the game only serves to essentially "unlock the door" at the end, giving it a more precision-based puzzle aspect. On the parkour side of things, the movement is very satisfying (although it does feel a little floaty at first). The routes you can take early on are pretty much dead set, and serves as a way to get the player used to the controls. However, as more movement options are introduced, you'll notice the freedom of movement-- you'll eventually be straying from the path, seeking ways to improve your time. The lack of rigidity really enhances the "parkour" experience.Artistically, the game is very aesthetically pleasing. It has this modernized feel of an anime from the 90's. The voice acting adds on to this, albeit a little cheesy. The music on the other hand is amazing. The drum n' bass/it's subgenres really add to the fast pacing of the game. The sound itself is almost reminiscent of the Bomberman Hero soundtrack. Story obviously isn't the point of the game, and although it's not amazing, it's not necessarily bad either. The characters are enjoyable, and the setting really sells the edgy antihero aesthetic. Despite this cheesy/edgy motif, I still found myself invested into it, especially the characters. However, if it's not your cup of tea you can fast forward through all of the dialogue.Of course, there are some minor/nitpicky things that bother me, such as ESC being the only key that can skip the intro, or how dash cards are misleading (Specifically that it's stated you're invincible mid-dash, but still die to 1-shot attacks), or just weird geometry collisions. There are definitely some other things that I didn't take note of, but not enough to warrant huge problems.Overall, amazing game and anyone that loves fast paced games should give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the first to say it, but oh dear god the writing is TERRIBLE. I sat through it because I'm stubborn. it was not worth it. Any "plot twist" can be seen from a mile away, the characters are all groanworthy (violet is the worst character I've seen in ages) and the plot macguffins... the purpose of them never really gets properly explained even if you follow the story closely, so, whatever man.Game looks beautiful, OST is a mixed bag - a few okay tracks, a lot of Epic Gamer Music For Gamers (this kinda game works best with calmer music to contrast the high-speed action - dustforce, celeste, even lovely planet to an extent get this right).And the gameplay itself is good, too - maybe trends a bit -too- easy for the ace medals and the level design starts falling apart a little around mission 9 (and there are way too many marathon levels in the last quarter of the game, christ guys) but for the most part I enjoyed the hell out of it. Lots of variety in the guns and abilities you use (though the katana itself is so rarely used there's almost no point to it) and some of the combos they make you do to stay in the air for dozens of seconds at a time are exhilarating. There's a light puzzle aspect to it that all the best platformers in this vein have and rarely any absurd requirements for, like, shot accuracy either. The difficulty curve is pretty smooth too and the game is constantly introducing new mechanics so it never gets stale. I dunno, it all just feels good and Works™ and even with the painful dialogue you're still gonna be spending at least, like, 75% of the game just playing the shooty jumpy bits, so. Yeah, if you can suffer through/skip the cutscenes then you're golden.

_childDocuments_.review: After an addition 8 hours of playtime, I feel the need to change my review to give a bit more thought as to why I like this game so much. Neon White feels like the gateway drug into speedrunning as a whole. It is very difficult to describe in words the feeling of beating a level only to see that you've shaved 8 or 9 or, hell, 30 seconds off of your previous best. The dopamine of seeing the red ace medal pop up after completion of something you put half an hour into is incredible, and is what has kept me hooked throughout my time playing Neon White. That feeling of improvement and the joy of blasting through something faster than you ever expected is so addicting. Tiny optimizations in movement and ability usage (or crosshair placement in the second to last chapter that can allow you to skip through the level 40 seconds faster than you'd expect) make or break runs through levels, and it's so satisfying to have it all come together in the end; not unlike how I assume full speedruns feel.Neon White is incredible. Its style and characters are not for everybody, but to quote a great image of our time: "Do not kill the part of you that is cringe. Kill the part of you that cringes."

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, now that I’ve beaten the game, finished every level with an ace medal, some of them even with a red one, and collected all gifts, I’m going to review it now.Neon White is all about time and precision movement and shooting enemies with your card deck. You’re a neon, a sinner sent by the God to clean up demons in Heaven in a style like a competition where are other neons. The goal is very simple, every level has some group of enemies and you need to clear them all to finish the level. BUT, that is not all. See, you could just spend 5 minutes per level, however, as you progress your rank on the leaderboard lowers, and with that, it’s opening your options to progress through more missions. So, to lower your rank you need to set better and better times. Every level has 4 medals (bronze, silver, gold, and ace) which you can get. With a gold medal your rank is lowered. PSSS, there is also a fifth one (red medal), which you can get if you beat developers' times set for that particular level. Really good from them, except I didn’t even realize it till I accidentally came across a youtube video that showed just that. There should be some kind of visual representation when you finish the ace medal, that you can get a red medal. Anyway ..., this game really kept insisting me to continue, to push myself to set better times. There were a few times when I should have gone to bed a long time ago, I even told myself "just one more level and it's over" which I finally did like at 2 AM. It was a kind of addiction but in a good way.OK, so you have medals and to collect these medals you need better times (ohhh, btw. kind of neat features, as you get medals for level, you also get a ghost from your best time set on that level, option to collect gifts which are scattered all over the levels and hint for a better route in order to get better time aka. cheat) and the best part is killing the enemies. How you may ask? Well, weapons obviously, but not just normal weapons, there are like card deck which is a really good choice while also keeping your screen clearer because there's no weapon covering the bottom right quadrant of the screen. This type of visuals when it was for the first time worldwide revealed, immediately hooked me up. There are a few categories of weapons aside from katana and fists which are by default all the time even if you run out of the others (some levels give you an vending machine option where you can get one more card if you're stuck). All of it is very fun to use, and each one of them is fairly easy to master, you get them when you kill enemies which are all color-coded like the card deck. Aside from shooting, you can discard them which has also an important function which can destroy obstacles and enemies or launch you in a certain direction. Basically, first-person platform style game, easy to learn, slightly harder to perfectly master for some people. Each level is well designed in a way that it gives you options on how you as a player want to make a route to the finish. Enemies are more or less stationary so it’s not that kind of hard to kill them. The mechanics are incredibly tight and responsive. Side missions were more or less ok, some of them were a challenge for example: more turrets, not using right click, or just jumping without falling down (actually it wasn’t so easy when you hear like this). Even though I’m not heavily speedrunner fan,  overall I liked it. Decent sense of progression and reward.Oh boiiiii. I will just say that it is a kind of surreal yet compelling story about the main character and a  group of his colleagues he encounters on the way. Some parts of the story were really touching and charming, some of them were quirky and some of them even horny, like a teenager phase horny (look boobs). As the game is progressing story becomes more serious than it was at the beginning. The story is made in a visual novel style which fits really well (voiced 90% of the time). Voice acting is godlike, perfecto magnifico. Music is also incredible from Machine Girl, not much can I say.UI is minimalistic:Graphics aren’t a technical marvel, typical 3D, although the visual style is kind of the strength of this game because of that visual novel. I liked the character art. Everything fits together aesthetically and cohesively. Considering that this game was very well optimized on Switch which runs 60fps both in dock and handheld mode (according to their playtest), it’s not at all that hardware intensive even for PCs that are 5 or more years old.For 22€, overall this game really justifies its price despite the gameplay loops. It’s so addictive, especially if you invest your time to compete with the rest of the online players or friends which you can see after you finish each level. Definitely deserved to be on the list as one of the best indie games of 2022. I’m really kind of hoping for DLC in the future.Rating: 9 / 10Recommendation: YESRecommend pretty much to anyone, unless you think it’s more first-person shooter, which is not, and you had a different expectations. On the other hand, you might probably enjoy it even if it's not exactly what you imagined.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is one of the most satisfying games I've played in a while. The goal is to navigate through short levels as quickly as possible using guns and limited movement abilities. Replaying levels to improve your times is not only fun, but it's also what the game expects from you. The great level design and smooth movement system make it feel like you're a pro speedrunner, even if you're not that good at it.Unfortunately, the story of Neon White is a letdown. While the premise of being a demon-slaying assassin in heaven sounds exciting, the execution and characters can be described as "cringe-worthy." However, the story can mostly be ignored.Overall, the story should not be a reason to avoid Neon White. It's such a fun game that more people should try out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, if you like shooters and 3D platformers, that is. It has some very good level and character designs, good voice acting (Spike from Cowboy Bebop), a bopping soundtrack (made by Machine Girl) and some great feeling movement. You get graded on each level and unlock more things the better you do, like presents for the NPCs and hints on where to go to beat the stages faster.The end game challenges might be a bit much for some (I'm looking at you, White Hell Rush), but you'll inevitably get better at it the more you play it, so it's a fun thing to strive towards. Some of the shorter ones were very doable and a nice little challenge.I'm a fan of speedrunning content, and this is 100% made with that in mind. The snappy level restart, in-game timer, and global leaderboards will attest to that. The levels are so much fun to explore and find alternate routes in and try to get better and better times.Story was interesting as well. It was more than what I was expecting, given the type of game it is. Some funny dialogue too, it had me bursting out laughing. Definitely a modern game, that's for sure.Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this game and will inevitably come back to it from time to time for another fun romp, or to improve my skills at it. Give it a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: very fun game - accessible but deep, with great presentation all around (albeit the occasional weak dialogue), good level design, satisfying and fluid gameplay, and a LOT of (optional!) challenge as you try to be speed.Neon White is an incredible game. I'd describe less as an FPS and more as a game that alternates between puzzle game and platformer with shooting elements (oh and a dash of dating sim) and it is phenomenal.When you start one of the many excellently-designed levels, you're in puzzle mode. How exactly do you use the weapons/movement abilities (which are pretty fun) to reach the finish line? The levels themselves are not necessarily that difficult - you don't have to have great aim or twitch reflexes. As part of the great level and art design, things are very readable so after you play a bit you often can pick up on the 'naive' route on your first try. Maybe you get a gold medal, that's pretty good!For those of you that just want to play the levels and see the story, you can just do that. Not everyone needs to be a god gamer and you can beat the game with gold times. The levels are fun and you feel pretty cool making these last second dashes and jumps on the fly. For those of you who see the ace medal time and say "oh I missed it by 3 seconds - well that one section was slow, maybe I can shave some time if I.." - oh boy you're in for a treat. Between short levels and instant restarts, retrying a level is really simple and enables you to chase those high scores. It's honestly kind of addicting. By default, you'll see your own ghost as you race yourself to get better and better (it's always just out of reach and it's taunting you). Now it's a puzzle as you try to figure out the best route but also a high intensity, high skill racing game as you try to execute that route. There are even secret developer times that are often insanely hard to get (i.e. some are faster than the top 5k players which I consider pretty fast). There are shortcut hints you unlock, some of which will blow your mind and give you some more techniques for later levels. There's only one shortcut hint per stage though, and there'll be quite a few stages where you find your own shortcut which is also satisfying.To give yourself a break between breakneck runs where you need to nail a really tight sequence of actions, almost every level also has a 'gift' hidden around. Most are somewhat obvious/visible from *some* part of the main path, but often times it's not obvious how to reach it. Now we're back in puzzle mode - how can reach something all the way up there, out of the way of the main path?? They're usually not too hard, but some were pretty tricky and it's great for pacing.Speaking of good for pacing, the gifts you find in levels can be given to characters to level up a relationship meter - this gives you some down time between levels to get some character backstory, funny conversations, etc. To be honest, didn't love all the dialogue but some of it is pretty funny and I actually liked the overarching story - even if its presentation is a bit simple. The voice acting is pretty solid and definitely helps in that regard. The music is also good and fits the game/aesthetic. Side note: this game is surprisingly long - I thought it'd be like 10 hours of a few cute levels and then it'd be over but there were a lot more levels than I expected. Admittedly my play time might be a bit on the higher end because I really wanted to beat my friends' times, then crack top 10 or 5k for each level so some levels I ended up grinding for a while. Even though I'm not a big fan of the "hours played/$" metric, neon white is actually pretty good there!

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a first person platformer with some first person shooting where you're racing through stages as fast as possible while some total anime nonsense plot kicks around where a handful of 90% too horny assassins named after colors are brought to heaven to kill some demons in a yearly competition for a spot in heaven. When racing through stages, you'll get awarded medals based on your time. Gold medals or better are required to lower your neon rank which gates off new missions. This makes it so you don't have to get great times on every stage to beat the game but you're going to need gold on about half of them to see credits.I can see this game being really difficult for people that are not great at platformers but as someone who has been playing platformers for their entire life, the game was engaging but not really tricky until the last few chapters once they start working in less straight forward paths and making it so the card you just picked up isn't always the card you should be playing next. Depending on your platforming skills and whether or not you're skipping story moments, your playthrough time is going to vary wildly. For me going through all mainline story moments and getting all gold or better medals on all stages, it took me about 6.5 hours to finish but HowLongToBeat has this clocked in at an average of 11.5 hours for the main story.I would recommend Neon White to anyone with any interest in platforming with a bonus recommendation to anybody into chasing leaderboards or into anime about sexually frustrated assassins, cat angels, John Cena, and big sweaty boobs.

_childDocuments_.review: It is rare to play a game so mechanically punchy, satisfying, and hyperactive as . Each level is an acrobatic rush through minimalistic, yet otherworldly, scenery and obstacles. The variety of "Soul Cards" available keeps gameplay fresh without becoming overwhelming or confusing. Quality of life features such as the quick restart button and transparency of collectibles, ensures you can stay focused on the best part of the game. After you've gotten the medal/ranking you're looking for (which is reasonably achievable), you can leisurely replay the level to search for the clearly marked collectible, which can later unlock more bombastic stages!The adrenaline-pumping music extenuates each second of the uniquely addictive platforming, while never overloading your senses, allowing the player to reach a perfect feeling of zen. The action is balanced by lighthearted visual novel dialogue, which is both endearing and doesn't overstay its welcome. Definitely recommend this one, especially if you enjoy other hyper-stylized speed demons such as , , and .

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on ~4 hours and 100% up to mission 2 (~20 levels + a few side quests/levels)tl;drIt's a FPS speedrunning game (and very controller friendly if Kb+m isn't your jam) with a very 90's-00's saturday night anime vibe. Voice cast and voice direction is on point! Gameplay is simple yet addicting. You pick up cards that have a primary gun function with limited ammo and a discard function that throws the entire card away in order to do something (dash forward, extra jump, etc.). So far, the levels are "same-y" in the sense that structures/models are reused but every level so far feels unique in how each level plays out. Each level serves two functions: 1) get the fastest time possible and 2) find the hidden gift. Gifts are used to increase your relationship status with other characters, unlocking dialogue/skits and more challenging side levels with some quirks such as card mastery, instant death, or no discard function.Music is subjective but I personally find the music choice to be great for its genre. The graphics options are lacking but the game runs super well (144 fps on my 2070 super and apparently 60 fps on the switch so use that as your benchmark).Up to mission 2 doesn't give me much insight on the story but I wouldn't go in expecting it to blow your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is an absolute blast! The mix of speedrunning, puzzles, and FPS elements is super refreshing. The story is gripping, and the characters are really well done. It's addictive and rewarding.If you're into fast-paced, innovative games, you need to play Neon White. It's one of the best gaming experiences I've had in a long time. Don't miss out!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun...... but definitely for a niche type of player.You can pretty much finish the first 2 episodes within an hour to give you a taste of what the game is like. You're going to eventually have to Gold (or better) as many sections as possible to advance. Now, there are people that like this kind of challenge. _childDocuments_.review: You want an awesome 3D platformer? You want an aim trainer? You want a speedrun game? You want to have fun? You want comedically cringy anime dialogue? Look no further! The last cards you unlock are absolutely fun to play with, and if you need an action packed platformer, play this. _childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is an innovative 3D platformer at heart, utilizing a combination of weapons and abilities to quickly traverse a level to defeat enemies. The main goal is to do this as fast as possible, with a secondary goal being to find a collectible in each level that allows you to unlock more backstory and dialogue between your main character, White, and a variety of side characters.Speaking of characters, the story itself is nothing to write home about (though there are a few interesting twists), but the voice acting is great and the dialogue is fun, so even though there wasn't a lot of depth to the story, I found myself enjoying the interactions with each character and the story itself was enough to bring me to to the end of the game with all platinum medals and all collectibles. This took me about 17-18 hours. You also unlock a level rush for each character's sidequests in which you complete them all in order. I am guessing that completing all of them unlocks another level rush you can do based on how the screen is laid out. I haven't done this yet, and probably won't, but even so I'd say I got my money's worth out of this game having gotten it on sale.If you're less dedicated than I am, you can probably beat the game in 10 hours or so if you don't bother trying to get platinum medals (only gold is strictly necessary, and you don't have to get it in every level if you don't want to) or collectibles. Arguably worth it at full price, but definitely worth it on sale. You don't see a lot of this kind of game (especially in a way that is fairly easily accessible) and the good voice acting and fun dialogue keep you invested in the characters, even if the overall story isn't superb.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best speedrun type game. It's fast, it's creative, it's fun. I didn't care too much for the religious themes and the story taking place in Heaven and the really just kept laying on this and it really made me un-interested in the whole setting. The first emotional moment in the game resonated with me enough but by the 3rd one, I really didn't care much for it anyway, they felt a little same-y. Getting gifts and ace medals also is a great challenge that I'll slowly keep working on in the future. 9/10, I love fireballs.

_childDocuments_.review: Razor sharp first-person platforming, marinated in devilish TF2 jump maps, drenched in hip anime from the 2000s, and seasoned lightly with the PAR-obsessed design of Lovely Planet. The game's vibe is on the same level as Nomura-style gaudy necklaces and belt buckles, in the sense that it's hard not to look away if you're completely alienated from what it's going for, but makes you feel right at home if you spent time growing up with its inspirations.There's some admittedly embarrassing writing in this game occasionally thrown around by its cast, but it is done in a self-aware fashion, and is sparse within the whole of the script. Overall, the dialogue is not only authentic to its peers, but honestly manages to do some clever things with its setting, and builds up typical character cliches in its own unique, loveable way. There's a heart of gold underneath it all that makes it come together nicely.Those familiar with this style of gameplay will find its mechanics fitting them like a glove. However, there are plenty of twists and turns within this game's arsenal and maps, enough to keep one on their toes until the very end. Reaching the credits is manageable, though going for side-content will put your reaction time and spacial awareness to the test. Tough as nails, but satisfying to master, Neon White is a fantastic addition to the genre, and it excites me for what's to come.

_childDocuments_.review: was recommended this by a friend and was hesitant at first, but this turned out to be one of the most plain fun games i've ever played, and very unique in terms of mechanics. some of the dialogue is very cheesy and will have you genuinely cringe, but i was still a pretty big fan of the story despite some of the criticisms of it i've seen. the real meat however lies in the gameplay, and it's one of the most addicting i've had the pleasure of experiencing in modern indie gaming. this game is best defined as a pure dopamine rush, whether or not you're aiming for the fastest times. genuinely required playing for any conscious being, i rlly need to replay it someday. if you're reading through reviews, this game is probably up your alley,, just get it you will not regret it i promise.

_childDocuments_.review: The best game I've played all year.Neon White is certain to become a classic. Its unique, nuanced gameplay blends multiple genres (FPS, platforming, puzzle) so well that you can't help but think, "How have we not seen a game like this before?". But truly, the developers struck something new and exciting here, which has become a bit of a rarity these days. The best part of the game is its accessibility. Anyone can play it and find themselves trying to outdo their previous attempts on certain levels. While the levels themselves are not too difficult, each of them encourages experimentation and creativity for you to beat it as fast as possible - and that's where the true challenge of this game lies. Some of these levels can be solved incredibly fast by circumventing the intended routes, but doing so will require a lot of trial and error. And if your wild curiosity is successful, you're rewarded with a top time and a blissful feeling of "that actually worked!". It does feel great to either outsmart the developers or at least match their clever insanity. But even if that's not your cup of tea, you can easily play through the levels at your own pace. I spent around 50 hours beating the main game since I wanted to top my times on each level before moving on. I'm sure, however, other players can beat it in 20 hours or less with little issue if their preferences differ. The developers found a strong balance of difficulty in their game design, allowing everyone to find their own joy in it.I highly recommend this game, not only for its brilliance in gameplay and level design, but also as such a new and unique experience that warrants your attention. Godspeed.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite genres and this game is a masterpiece of the speedrun genre. Amazing soundtrack by Machine Girl. Character designs are awesome, voice acting was awesome. Gameplay loop is addicting and fun (gotta get them Ace metals baby)! Whole game just feels top notch quality to me. _childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: You ever wanted to try speedrunning, but don't have the patience to sit for hours to shave seconds off your time? Neon White gives you the joy of Speedrunning in shorter bursts, and it's extraordinarily fun. A lot of people seem to not be a fan of the story, and that's fair. I personally enjoyed it, but that's because I genuinely enjoy a lot of the anime tropes the game plays into. Either way, the gameplay more than makes up for the story's faults, and if you really can't stand it, there's a fast forward button.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of 2022 so far. I can find so many things to praise about it.Overall, great game design. Just to name a few things - the levels are quick and easily digestible, while still having depth in the form of collectibles and shortcuts to bring down your run times. This is what makes the speedrunning aspect of the game addicting even for those who normally don't have any interest in that. The movement abilities are presented in an intuitive way so it doesn't take the momentum away from an otherwise fast-paced game. I also think it was a smart move to push the player to reach a certain time in the level, but not require perfect execution to progress.The soundtrack by Machine Girl is 10/10; it's full of catchy songs that'll be stuck in your head for a while after playing.The story is presented in a sort of visual novel format, and some people might find it ridiculous and over the top, but I just thought it was whatever. This might be the one thing about the game that isn't excellent like the rest of it. At the very least, I do think the voice acting was well done. Neon White is one of the few games I've actually taken the time to review and I'm probably gonna be shilling it to all of my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely going to be my videogame of 2022 (gameplay-wise). The card mechanic is one of the most ingenious ideas I've ever seen in a videogame. The soundtrack being by Machine Girl has me playing for HOURS just to jam out. If you're on the fence I recommend pulling the trigger (that's a gun joke.)9.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I recommend this game, but there's a bit more to it than "I just don't like it." On the contrary, I really did want to like this game, and the gameplay way actually pretty fun. I liked the fast paced style of the game, but the way that you're supposed to beat the levels in a certain way in order to get a good time gets pretty annoying after a while. And if you don't care about a good time score, you still need to get a good time, otherwise you can't progress. Seriously, the game locks the next missions if you aren't a certain rank or higher, and rank is improved by getting gold medals or ace medals, which is completely dependent on your time. You'll probably find yourself grinding for it for a bit, even if you don't care about it.The way I see it, the story kinda feels like an afterthought. Random snippets of story and dialogue are thrown in in the middle of different missions and you're left like "Oh yeah. This again." It kinda interrupts the whole flow of the level.The story is probably the worst part of the game, which sucks if you're a big lore person like me. There's so much potential for the story and lore, but I feel like the way it's written is so random. Almost like the writers didn't know how to write certain parts, and were just like "yeah this'll probably work." The story felt very scattered and random without any actual flow to it.The dialogue is pretty unnatural. And like the story, it feels like it was sprinkled in after the gameplay was already done. Like I said before, it interrupts the flow of the level sometimes, by being thrown in right after a level, in the middle of a mission. I don't like the voice acting. It feels like it fits, but it doesn't at the same time, and I don't know how that works. The voices work for the characters themselves, but the things the characters say don't really match up with the voices, or their looks. Yeah, that sounds right. The jokes are sprinkled in at probably the worst times possible, and it really messes with me.The graphics are actually alright. And considering the fact that this game can run on a pretty weak computer, that's pretty good. The only thing I don't like are the 3d animated sequences after you beat a mission. The dark lighting makes it just look kinda bad, but that's my only gripe about it.I think overall, I wouldn't recommend this game to people like me, who are big on story, and like voice acting. But the gameplay is pretty good and fun. I think the price tag is a bit much for a game like this, so if you really wanna give it a try, I suggest you get it on sale. On a scale of 1-10, i'd probably give it a 5 or 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Neon White

_childDocuments_.review: I asked one of my friends recently, "Would you consider someone your favorite artist, even if you don't like over half of their songs?" His response was "Weezer fans will say yes".  I consider myself a bit out of touch when listening to most of Machine Girl's tracks. I'd just say the majority of it isn't for me. However, one of my favorite albums of theirs, "Reporpoised Phantasies", really helped to re-contextualize their sound for me. Every song has this dreamy quality to it, like your exploring this other world in your headphones. It has this confident tone with some sick drum breaks, but doesn't go all in your face like other MG songs have.  I feel this way about a few other songs off of the album "The Ugly Art", but that's about it for my history with this band.And then this got released. Holy.I had no warning before another 2 and a half hours of Machine Girl was brought to me on a silver platter. It capitalized on exactly what I love about their sound. Part 1 is where all the meat and bones are, but the inclusion of a large number of shorter tracks in Part 2 really demonstrates their flexibility across a wide range of themes. The hard parts still go very hard though, and despite the shift in focus away from the thrashers of MG's discography, a few hidden bangers are still waiting to go all out on your eardrums and it is magnificent. Oh yeah, the album comes with a game too. It looks neat, I'll probably play it one day idk

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a true FPS game. Yes, it's first person and you shoot things, but the "enemies" are more like target dummies. Which is fine, because this kind of game doesn't need deep combat or complex AI.If anything, it's more like a puzzle game. You can "discard" your weapons to get strategic movement boosts or perform a special attack. Figuring out where to do these (and in what order) is very much a puzzle. The game is very short. If you generally play a game only once, you might only spend 5-6 hours with it, even less if you skip all the dialogue. Part of the charm is to replay levels for better ratings, which are solely based on your time to completion. The difficulty fits a nice medium. If you get a gold (the second best rank), replaying the level will show you a hint animation at a specific shortcut. In general, if you reached gold without the shortcut, then the shortcut will save you enough time to guarantee the diamond/ace on a subsequent run. However, there are still more shortcuts to find, and in many cases you can still get the highest rating without using the hinted shortcut. If you are looking for something extremely challenging, this isn't it, unless you are very much into the speedrun scene. I'm not particularly amazing at these games, but most levels took me 2-5 tries for the best rating. However, the game DOES feature level rush modes, both with and without limited lives, if you are interested.I've heard people complain about the story, but it isn't that bad. The amount of dialogue is nothing compared to games like Danganronpa or Steins' Gate, it just seems long because the levels are so short. It's your standard anime story affair. Don't take it too seriously, and you can enjoy the ride. My only complaint about the game is the lack of extras. 100%ing the game doesn't give you much. But I enjoyed my time with it, so that's a minor complaint at worst.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute banger. An FPS platformer with a unique ability system. The abilities sound more complicated than they play and I thought I wouldn't like it before playing, but it's done in a fantastic way.The cards you pick up are used in two different ways. One is shoot (with m1), there are multiple card colors, and each one has a unique style of shooting as well as damage profiles, yellow shoots a pistol, blue a semiauto rifle, purple an automatic rifle, and so on. Each weapon also has a secondary ability (with m2). The secondary abilities range from a simple double jump to a fiery omni-directional dash. Every secondary ability has the capability to kill enemies and instantly break red barriers, except the pistol's double jump. Using this burns the all the ammo left on that card, you can shoot the ammo until you have one shot left and still use the secondary ability. A Godspeed with 1 shot will dash the same distance and speed as a freshly obtained Godspeed with 4. You can pick up multiple of the same card, and it gives you an additional use of the of the secondary ability or more ammo, with a maximum of 3 like cards. You can also only have two different cards, and picking up a third will replace the one you dont have equipped no matter how much ammo or stacks of that card you have. This is the concept that I was iffy with before launch. I loved the speed aspect of it and the fact that it was an fps platformer, but managing these abilities felt like it might be a no go. Fortunately, it's implemented beautifully. There's never a moment where I feel like I needed to hoard cards and only shoot enemies.The level design is mostly built in a point A to point B style and every small section is kinda of like it's own little puzzle. The designers wanted the areas to flow with what the player would want to do. See a bunch of enemies in a line and you were just given Godspeed? Dash through all of them without worrying about the consequences of losing all your ammo cause it's what they wanted you to do. Though, there are moments where you can get stuck and have to restart because you don't have access to any cards, it's usually due to player mistake, and it's obvious that you overly used them, or flat out used them wrong. I also often found myself making it to the goal without any cards left, every card has a purpose and it's almost immediately apparent what it's purpose is.Progression is tied to medals, every level has 4 medals (bronze, silver, gold, diamond) each earned based on speed. Each medal you unlock will add a tiny bit to the level, such as presents you need for lore and bonus levels, and a waypoint that shows you a shortcut. Each of these are received at the same tier with gold being the one to go for to unlock the waypoint. About halfway through the game and I haven't encountered any level that I haven't been able to get gold on, and the waypoint usually aids me in getting the diamond. I think the difficulty is fine, although I do think it's a bit weird for there to be a guide a shortcut only after you've almost got all the medals, leaving the people who are struggling without any guidance until they get faster. I don't think it's all that hard, but I can see some players, especially controller players struggling to get a decent time on some levels. This game's difficulty seems lower than other similar games, like Super Meat Boy, or Wavedash both games I never progressed much in because of being a completionist and wanting highest rank on every level. The difficulty of Neon White comes from actually speedrunning, which "unintended" routes can you take, and which cards can you pass to still make it to the goal after killing all the enemies, and being able to do it fast. I frequently find myself wanting to rerun stages even after getting diamond and the present just to better my time. I also can't recall any moment where I actually disliked a stage, sure I like some more than others but haven't came across anything that I explicitly hate.Speedrunning this game seems like an absolute blast. The only issue I had with controls was how floaty it is, I've been getting used to it, but it was bit of a shock at first to see myself slowly gliding down after jumping, there's also a couple of times I will jump near an edge, and instead of getting my jump I end up falling. I think that it has decent repercussions of mistiming a jump, as it's gonna a full second for you to land. Restarting is quick and easy, just the press of a button and you're back at the start screen. The only complaint is that there isn't true multikey binding, I wanted two keys to switch cards but after playing for a while, there really isn't a need for it, and there isn't a plethora of bindings anyways. There was something that I was saving for this section but I've forgotten it for now.There's a couple of QoL changes I can see coming in later patches. One is a complete skip button rather than the fast forward, would make future re-runs/full game speedruns better. Another, is changing the "Next Level" location after collecting a present. After almost 10 hrs I've just realized it's at the top of the screen when all the options have been at the bottom left. I think either adding it to the bottom left like everything else, or to the bottom right to symbolize progression or moving on to the next one. The last is save files. I'd just like to have a completed save, and be able to start a new one where I do tests and speedruns. It's a personal thing, but I don't see how the addition of it could be a negative thing.Fantastic game and highly recommend to people who like fps games, and platformers, cause this is both in 1. It's got great mechanics, and level design that even if you aren't a speedrunner you can still feel like one when you get that diamond, or shave off a second or two on your time for your own Personal Best. Also, if you like anime/VNs the story is pretty good, and I usually dislike story in mechanically focused games. The story isn't woven into the gameplay, but for the style of game that'd be kinda hard to do, and the majority of it can be skipped by not giving presents, to anyone and mashing through dialogue.EDIT: Red Medals are for passing Dev Times, like TimeTrial Ghosts in Mario Kart. Getting them is not necessary for 100% but def fun challenge. Getting Gold in a stage is not necessary for the shortcut hint, as you complete a stage, you get "Insight" which sorta levels up the stage, you just get insights boosts for getting higher ranked medals, so you don't have to rerun a stage you've already got a good time on. I can tell I'm going to have an insane amount of hours on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is an exhilarating first-person platformer that combines shooting and speedrunning mechanics perfectly. The game's protagonist, Neon White, is a sinner who has been plucked from hell to participate in a demon-killing competition. The winner of the competition will earn forgiveness from God himself and a place in heaven.As you progress through the game, you'll encounter characters from your past life and uncover the secrets behind their masks.The core gameplay loop of Neon White revolves around eliminating demons and reaching the finish line as quickly as possible. This is achieved through the use of cards, which function similarly to guns without obstructing your vision. When wielding a card in Neon White, you can fire bullets, and when you discard it, the card's unique secondary ability is activated. The pistol provides a double jump, the LMG fires a sticky bomb, the SMG enables a ground stomp, the rifle allows for a forward dash, the shotgun offers an better version of the rifle's move, and the rocket launcher provides a grappling hook. These abilities are common movement mechanics found in many other games, making Neon White's gameplay easy to grasp.The enemies in Neon White are relatively weak, allowing you to dispatch them quickly with most weapons. Since it's a speedrunning game, your time shouldn't be wasted on dealing with bullet sponges. This design choice proves to be beneficial when you need to defeat multiple enemies in rapid succession, providing a much smoother and more enjoyable gameplay.Once you complete a level in Neon White, you will earn a medal based on your time. The game offers five different medals, including two consolation prizes that you may obtain after your first completion, two medals that require you to optimize your routes, and one final medal that I will discuss later in this review. I found this medal system to be highly enjoyable as it provides a sense of progression and motivates players to strive for better medals. Additionally, the game offers hints on how to optimize levels, making it feel more achievable to obtain the precious ace medal. If you're feeling particularly adventurous, you can even explore alternative routes and save even more time.I was genuinely impressed by how easy it was to pick up and play Neon White. Typically, speedrunning involves investing hundreds of hours to learn and optimize the game as much as possible. Neon White takes a different approach by dividing the entire game into numerous levels, with each level typically lasting under 15 seconds. Rather than investing an excessive amount of time to reach a specific part of game to practice, you can simply replay a single level to your heart's content.Another feature of the game is a global leaderboard that allows players to compete with others worldwide, as well as a separate leaderboard for competing with friends. However, it's important to be aware that the global leaderboard may attract cheaters, as is unfortunately often the case with any games that have leaderboards.I was able to easily achieve ace medals on all levels, and while the game is enjoyable, I found that it became stale the more I played it. I couldn't quite put my finger on why that was the case.Maybe it’s the difficulty? I found the game to be less challenging than I expected, so I decided to take on White’s hell rush - a speedrun of all levels with only one life. I went back to redo all the levels to get a better understanding of them and to find faster shortcuts. While watching world record runs on YouTube to learn from top players, I was amazed by how quickly they could move and their need to shoot every enemy projectile. After researching the speedrunning techniques used in Neon White, I discovered that shooting and parrying projectiles actually gives you a speed boost. This discovery made me realize that the root of all my problems with this game was that I wasn’t pushing myself to go fast in a speedrunning game.Not only did I pick up speedrunning techniques by watching other players' runs, but I also stumbled upon a hidden medal in the game. To obtain this medal, players must surpass the time record set by the developers for each level. The requirements for achieving this medal are notably more demanding than those for obtaining an ace medal. I found this to be a fascinating challenge, and after earning one of these valuable red medals, earning an ace medal now feels like a mere consolation prize.It's a game that improves as you invest more effort into it, to the point where it becomes addictive, and you find yourself spending half an hour just to improve your time by a few milliseconds.While Neon White is an excellent game, I do have a few gripes with it.Each of the colored Neons has their own mini levels to play, except for White and Green. It's understandable for White, as usually, to play those levels, you have to gift them, and you can't really gift yourself, can you? Now, you can gift Green in a way and unlock more memories of the past. It's pretty disappointing to see that the antagonist of this game doesn't have unique little levels that fit his theme.The gifting animation is also unreasonably lengthy, especially considering the game's focus on efficiency. It's puzzling why there's no option to skip it, considering that you can skip dialogues in this game if you wish.Also, there are invisible walls in this game. They can be pretty annoying, but fortunately, there aren't many of them. Off the top of my mind, I can only think of Glassport, Forgotten City, and Streak as areas where they are notable.Neon White is an outstanding game that you shouldn't miss if you're a fan of first-person platformers or speedrunning games. With its emphasis on fast-paced, fluid movement mechanics, it delivers a thrilling experience that is hard to match.While the game offers action-packed gameplay and challenging level design, some players may not find the story appealing. However, the captivating gameplay alone will keep you engaged for hours. Neon White also offers significant replayability, allowing you to continuously challenge yourself to beat your records and compete with others on the online leaderboards. This addictive nature of the game ensures you'll keep coming back for more.In conclusion, I would rate Neon White as 9.5 out of 10. If you're seeking a challenging and addictive game that will put your skills and reflexes to the test, Neon White is an excellent choice. Its thrilling gameplay, high replayability, and accessibility make it an absolute must-play.
