_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a truly phenomenal experience and a superbly designed game. It combines speedrunning, cards and guns for a highly original and enjoyable concept that is executed incredibly well. Despite having a rather mediocre anime narrative tacked on, it doesn't detract away from the pulsating action on offer. There are stacks of levels and these can last from as little as ten seconds, up to and even beyond a minute sometimes. The game ultimately works by collecting and utilising cards on the go. Each one acts as a primary weapon but the real power is the discard ability - when you right click to discard your currently held card, you receive a power such as a boost jump, explosive bomb, boost jump, dash etc... If you time these right, you can chain together some incredible moves. Levels are easy to learn and the gameplay flows remarkably well. You will be able to master the card types and discard ability/timings very quickly and this makes for a very easy to pick up title. Soon you'll be chipping away to beat your best times and look for shortcuts and other ways to complete a level efficiently and earn a higher medal and rank. All enemies must be killed to finish each one and then you are graded between bronze, silver, gold and even an ace medal. The overriding story was not to my taste and quite uninspired but thankfully you can skip dialogue and overlook all narrative aspects without the action being affected. The core game is simply outstanding with excellent, easy to pick up mechanics and gameplay that is addictive and a joy to master.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exceptional. From a purely gameplay perspective it allows the player to achieve mastery on each level. Short levels mean repeating a level isn't tedious, then eventually finding the optimal path is so satisfying. Levels feel bitsized and have you thinking in creative ways. After a session I feel like I have been in a flow state that not many games ever achieve. The dopamine hit from nailing a run perfectly is sublime. Its both a twitch reflex game and puzzler wrapped into one. You need to figure out how you are going to complete the level and then its about your execution. On top of this you have gifts to find which are complete puzzles in themselves incentivising you to think out of the box or use your powers creatively. Completing all of this makes the game feel really substantial. The game does a great job of building on previous knowledge and layering complexity onto this. I tried showing a few of the later levels to my friends to show them how great it is but they seemed pretty overwhelmed, a testament to have the game slowly ramps up alongside your skillset. The story is camp but somewhat charming. Its truly shocking how this didn't beat out Stray at the game awards the year it was released. This is honed to a fine point and in terms of gameplay  joins the pantheon of the greats.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not 100% done with this game but I have definitely played enough to recommend it. This game is worth your money and time. The pitch for the game is that it's a full 3d platformer where the goal of the level is to complete it as quickly as possible. Solving the puzzle of how to complete the level just a second or half a second faster is the joy of the game. If you have steam friends who play it you can also compete for the fastest times.For this game to work, the platforming needs to feel good and there needs to be a large diversity of levels and traversal options to make sure things don't get stale. This game fulfills it completely. It will consistently add either new powerups or interactable enemies/items in order to give you time to master that element of play. Then after you've gotten used to it, it adds another aspect until by the end you're juggling all these factors like a pro. Buy this game.There is such a thing called rush mode for different characters or hell rush mode, and I haven't played that yet so I can't speak on it. Where I see this game getting a lot of criticism though is in the story and the dialogue. I don't fully agree but I can admit that the narrative isn't nearly as good as the gameplay. This game is story light and while it has some cringe moments, it also has some surprising and moving moments I think.Ultimately I believe this game is a masterpiece with and indie price tag. This game is what I will now hold all other 3d platformers to as the gold standard.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, unique, clean and stylish art style and soundtrack. Mechanics are simple and introduced at a reasonable pace, ensuring you have a good mastery of each individual one before being given a new one. On most every level you can find multiple ways of reaching your goal and quickly develop an intuition on how each power/weapon can be used to shave off a few ms that will make you feel like a pro.The game doesn't enforce any particular times for completion (outside of achievements) and coupled with the hints and the generous time thresholds most people should be able to get at least gold medals in every level without much effort.The story exists, I don't personally think it's great or bad, it's mostly unobtrusive and together with some quips and references makes it at least reasonably engaging, though you can skip if you are only interested in the gameplay.Other than that, the game is incredibly well polished, with tight controls, fluid movement (and an absolute steal even at full price) and I found no bugs or problems at any point during playtime, not being required to play multiple playthroughs* to unlock all achievements is also fantastic.TL;DR Absolutely recommended, but only for people who enjoy fast paced platforming intermixed with some puzzle-solving and FPS.*Technically some of the Rushes are full playthroughs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem.I absolutely love how this game encourages you to speedrun. It's like the game is asking you, 'If you're not playing for the best time, are you even playing at all?' I remember reading something from the devs about how they intended this. The ingenious 'insight' system really pushes you to replay levels to at least grab the gold medal, but let's be honest, we're all chasing that ace medal.The game's design, with its super short levels, is brilliant. Failing a 20-second level feels way less frustrating than having to restart a full-length level. it also you allows to become a “mini speedrunner”. You can focus on perfecting 2-3 levels or just your favorite one, without having to master the whole game like in regular speedrunning.The levels might look simple and straightforward at first glance, but there's so much room for creativity. You have the hints that help you save some extra time, then you explore the level and possibly save more time, but afterwards you go on youtube and OMG you realize you can cut down your time even more, I love it.This game is the definition of “easy to learn, hard to master”. he gameplay is smooth, and the 'low gravity’ jump is really forgiving. For the tryharders, there are hidden techniques to discover that can speed up your play (like getting a boost from parrying a bullet, or jumping even after starting to fall off a ledge).The shooting is a bit weird but consistent, so you can learn the patterns but it doesnt really matter because if you play casually its fine and you mostly discard anyway. I also love how they introduce one new thing each chapter (card or enemy).The content is just insane. Trying to beat the developer's time for the red medal is a real challenge (damn, he is good) And FINALLY, a game where collectibles aren't just filler. Hunting for gifts is fun and adds a ton of content and completely changes the way to approach the game.If I had to point out a flaw, it would be the slightly cringey dialogues. But hey, you can fast-forward through them, so who cares.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is goofy, dead serious, quick, and intense. It's mechanically tight enough for high-octane speedrunning while still being forgiving enough for those just looking to experience the story without giving themselves RSI. While the plot isn't be for everyone, it has a charm that is appealing enough even if you aren't in the target demographic (2000's anime fans, probably). Progression is broken into a series of maps or chapters. Each map/chapter requires completion of all the levels it contains. Each level involves zipping around Heaven, completing objectives (usually killing demons) and getting out. The quicker you do that, the better the medal you'll be awarded at the finish. Moving to the next map requires all levels in the set be completed as well as a certain number gold (or better) medals. Every level is, at its most basic, a puzzle. Early on, the solutions are quite simple, and will typically just involve using abilities as they're given to you with wide margins for error. As the game progresses, the window for making mistakes closes somewhat, but never becomes tight enough to become unbearable. It's fine to walk around, admire the scenery, and casually shoot some demons, but I'd argue the real fun of Neon White comes from chasing the fastest possible times. The real puzzle is looking at every level as a miniature speedrun, and it completely changes the feel and pace of the game. Most of your decisions will come down to pathing through a level and card usage. When you pick up a card, you can either fire it (like a weapon) or discard it to gain some ability. These discard abilities offer an additional way to move around the level. Be it an extra jump or a midair dash, using your discards at the right time is critical to breaking out of the "normal" routes. While the game is nominally a first person shooter, at its best a "well executed" run will look almost like a platformer - you'll be barely looking at enemies before pulling the trigger and flying off to the next spot; ignoring the "intended" route to shave fractions of a second off every movement. Every time you enter a new level, you'll be looking for corners to cut and areas to skip in the pursuit of the quickest time. Enemy locations are static, so your final run through a level will likely be a highly choreographed and practiced dance around the stage. This is where the game shines, and in this regard the game is practically flawless.Where it may fall a bit short is the aforementioned plot and some of the dialog (both text and voice-acted). The voice acting itself is good for what it is. The lines match each character's archetype, and the voice actors do a good job given the over-the-top personalities they're meant to portray. However, in the sections in between chapters, there is a distinct lack of voice acting and character lines are repeated each time you speak to them in a given chapter. It doesn't matter too much, but when you give 3 or 4 gifts (a collectible you can usually find pretty easily in levels that are used to advance some subplots) in a single chapter, you'll see the same text each time. Usually it won't be voice acted, and if it is it'll be the typical reused anime gasp or grunt. It's a minor nit, but it's noticeable. The asymmetry of subplot progression with main story also can lead to some minor dissonance in character interactions, but it's not a major issue. For what it's worth, all cutscenes are skippable and it's well worth a playthrough even if you skipped all the plot. To round things out, Neon White's got a great soundtrack courtesy of Machine Girl, and a solid art style both in-game and in the visual novel sections. The game also has a leaderboard for global and friend times to add some competition if chasing medals doesn't quite do it for you.It's not for everyone, but it perfectly fills its niche. If the concept appeals to you, it's definitely worth a shot. It was one of the best gaming experiences I had all year, and I'm sure I'll be back someday to chip away a few tenths off some of my records.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a good game. A very good game that has some faults but honestly I could overlook themThe core structure of the gameplay is that you run around in each level slaying demons with cards (basically weapons) and use said cards to do some honestly fun platforming. After which you can then return to the hub to chat with characters and get dialogue if you have any gifts for them.At first I thought that the gameplay was shallow bouncing between the sections. But as the game gave me more tools and expected me to fully use them the run and gun gameplay started to become fantastic. Bouncing around in some levels where you barely touch the ground is honestly really fun.Now the biggest gripe that I see commonly with the game is that it's story sucks and honestly I can't see why. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent. Saw a friend playing and decided to pick it up. Worth every penny. Movement is fluid and polished to perfection. The cards are an original gimmick that have not gotten old yet. After a while, discarding becomes very natural, and it's surprising how quick you make decisions to keep or discard a card just to save off fractions of seconds. The quest to be on the bleeding edge of speed is intoxicating. Completing White's hell run was one of the hardest things I've done in a game, and out of the maybe 60-70 attempts, I was only frustrated on about 2 of them. Because the movement is so fun I never felt bored, just encouraged to play the first couple levels faster to get back to where I died.The only complaints I have are nitpicks. Everyone you see complains about the voice acting, and while I totally understand where they're coming from, it didn't bother me. I would say there should be a way to rewatch the heavenly delights, as on my playthrough I missed an icecream scene and cool swimsuit scene and didn't really feel like deleting my save to watch them. However image searching "neon white swimsuit" just yielded swimsuit model pictures. My final gripe would be that the gift giving animations were very drawn out. I tend to hoarde things in games until the last minute and giving all the gifts at the end was a chore. The animations take like 15 seconds which doesnt seem like much but after the 90th gift it adds up. All of those gripes are an indistinguishable blemish on a mona lisa of movement gameplay. Soundtrack bangs, tooCalling it early, my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I am so happy I played this game.  I was worried that the speed element of the game would cause too much frustration for me .  The devs make the power curve perfectly and you get used to the mechanics and physics.  By the end of my first night playing the game I felt FAST.  By the end of day two I was hunting ace medals and gifts, overall having a BLAST with this game.  The characters are fun, story is focused and full of intrigue. _childDocuments_.review: The gameplay premise is pretty simple - you are put into a level and need to kill all the demons on the level, and then you need to get to the end of the level, as fast as possible. Throughout the level you will find soul cards, these cards are actually weapons like pistols and machine guns. Specific enemies also drop specific soul cards. You will lose them if you run out of ammo, but you can also discard them - each soul card has a special ability, for example, a pistol gives you a sort of a double jump effect and the machine gun gives you a sticky bomb you can use to kill multiple enemies at once, and you can bounce off the explosion. It's all very fluid and it feels very nice to go through the well designed levels, especially while going through shortcuts. So yeah, gameplay wise, the game is fantastic.The story is decent, BUT the dialogue!? I've played games for 20 years but this is the first game to actually make me physically cringe from embarrassment.Anyways, it took me 29 hours to complete the whole story, get all the hidden gifts on all the level, go through all of white's memories and all the level rushes for all the characters in the game. But you also unlock a level rush for the main game, which has a heaven and hell mode. In heaven mode it's just, complete all the levels as fast as possible. But hell mode, which took me the last 7 hours, is complete all the levels in the game without dying, or being put into a situation where you mess up your soul card usage and now you can't finish the level. You can use an ability 3 times in a run where you heal and you get any soul card you want, once per level.Even if you're not into speedrunny games such as this one, I'd say give it a go, it's a pretty unique take on the genre and unless you like to take anything and everything you do very slow, I'm sure you'll have some fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neon White is a masterpiece. Most players would probably just buy this game beat it one time and call it good but once you understand the game's premise you are eventually hooked in the gameplay loop. Once you beat a level you unlock "insight" for the level (max 4) yielding the player 4 benefits for each level. One of which is 1 developer shortcut. The genius about this is the game is extremely flexible meaning there may be more shortcuts if the player sees something the devs didn't almost reminiscent of sequence breaking. The soundtrack is pretty on par with the smooth gameplay. The graphics are simple which isn't a bad thing especially for dated pc's. Some of the character archetypes are as stale as Evangeline however the characters do have levels that accurately coincide with their bland archetypes which is at the very least consistent and offers a bit of appreciation to the devs for being creative with it. Neon White isn't just a game for speedrunners. It's a game for all and I'd say Neon White was just ahead of it's time along with similar titles like SEUM: Speedrunners from Hell. It's a shame it was overshadowed by big release titles such as Elden Ring. I hope the devs have the passion to continue to make games or concepts similar to this because I will be watching.

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game. It's beautifully fast-paced, the controls are tight and responsive, and things are kept simple and elegant.The graphics and looks:It's got a unique look, and the 2D art is fantastic. The character design is remarkable and memorable. Some levels look really cool as well. It's got a nice art style that makes it stand out. The graphics themselves aren't something to write home about. You're not gonna gaze in awe at a beautiful light engine and highly detailed levels.Overall, it's 1/1.5.The story and dialogue:This is really the weakest part of the game. The dialogue is so incredibly awkward and genuinely hard to read. It's just... cringe. I just skipped it all in my first playthrough, but if you force yourself to read it, there's a surprisingly solid plot under all that garbage dialogue. There's actual character development and something more than just obstacles to the goal apparent from the start.Because of that, it's 0.5/1.The gameplay:This is really where the game shines. Everything it does, it does well, and it doesn't have anything that's simply bad. The gunplay is good. It's fast, you don't need to switch between 10 weapons, and the vast majority of the time, the game will put the right weapon in your hands whenever you need to use it. It's simple, it's reliable, and there's no silly gimmicks. Everything is built on movement, including the weapons. Each weapon can be discarded, which will activate some sort of movement and damage ability. They're intuitive, simple and easy to understand, but that doesn't mean they can't be used in creative ways. The game does an amazing job at giving you the right tool at the right time, allowing you to chain these fantastic sequences of moves and abilities that you want to perfect to finish the level as fast as possible. In addition to that, the levels are short, with no random stuff, to make you want to speedrun them even more. In every level, you can find shortcuts, skips big and small, that reward you for thinking and looking around the levels. Things only get better and better as you get more tools towards the end. Watch someone beat a level called Marathon to really see what I'm talking about.There's also some side content, which is pretty fun. There's getting collectibles, with the challenge of getting some being in how you even reach them, and there's the less fun challenge of just finding some. The additional levels are pretty inconsistent in terms of what to expect. Some are fast and require a bit more precise timing than standard levels, which I loved, but some play more like puzzles, which are slow and I'm not a big fan of them.There are a few instances where the level just doesn't feel overly well-made. Where your momentum is just kinda killed and you're forced to spend a lot of time walking/falling. Minefield would be an example of that. But things like that are rare.Overall, the gameplay is 7/7.5. It's more than good enough to carry the game all by itself. The total score is 8.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: So, Soul Nomad is probably one of my favorite Nippon Ichi games of all time, and I still have my PS2 copy to this day, so I was incredibly hyped when I heard this was getting a steam port.With that out of the way however, the game is ultimately, a straight port of the PS2 version, so that may dampen it for some people. That said, this is the first time ever that the game has ever gotten a re-release and tracking down a physical copy is quite the endeavor, speaking from personal experience I had to scour every gamestop and used game store around me for 3 months before I found a copy, and this was more than 10 years ago now, so it's probably harder now than it was back then. So this makes the steam/switch port the easiest way to get the game.Now lets discuss the gameplay: so the core of the battle system is that you control squads of units in battle, the sizes ranging from 1 unit to 9, and in many ways it reminds me of an old game called Ogre Battle for the SNES/PSX where the premise was the same mixed with the turn order system of Final Fantasy X. You will always have the Main Character's squad deployed at the start of every battle, and at the start of the game, it will be the only squad you have access to. Once you advance along in the story however, you open up more squads, and equally important, more squad room types.Squad rooms function as the core bonus of the squad they're in, the starting room you have access at the start has no bonus, but as you unlock more rooms you get bonuses like damage increased by tiles moved, to bonuses like stats increased by percentage of stamina missing. Stamina also plays an important role in combat, every action taken be it, moving, attacking, defending or using squad skills uses stamina and if a squads stamina hits 0 that squad dies, you also incur a stat malus for having your stamina below 50% and finally, special attack skills can only be used at 80% or below making it something of a balancing act. There is however ways to recover stamina, if no action is taken at all in a squads turn they recover a portion of their stamina and items also recover stamina.Squads are staffed with units obtained via the story, or much like Disgaea created by you. Each unit has an ability or attack used in a specific row of a squads formation, healers for example heal everyone in the squad when placed in the rear, other classes may hit a row or column of the enemy squad depending on row placement.Squads can also be equipped with items, with the caveat that they are used up after the battles completion, with one exception. These items increase stats like attack, magic, critical chance, and movement, making them useful for getting though encounters without needing to grind much.It would not be a Nippon Ichi Software game if there wasn't an infinite dungeon to grind in, in this game it's called inspection. Inspection is the way you upgrade your squad rooms in Soul Nomad, as well as level grind. As you increase your rooms strength the bonus it gets from equipped items increases as well as the room bonus, it is also how you increase squad capacity taking it from the base value to 9, not all that necessary early on, but becomes very useful as you progress. Inspection is also that aforementioned exception to squad equip items being used up after a battle's end, during inspection every item equipped is carried over into the next battle and remains after you finish, only being used once you go into a normal battle.As for the story, it's a bit more heavy than say, a Disgaea story, though not without humor, mostly in the form of Gig's commentary on the on goings around him. The second story path unlocked after you start a New game Plus is... probably the darkest thing NIS has ever done and probably will ever do.Speaking of Gig, the dub voice is amazing and Yuri Lowenthal absolutely owns the role as Gig. The dub overall is one i would consider NIS' best dubbings barring how annoying Danette can get.All in all the game might not be what some people wanted, but for 20 bucks, it's still a solid port and still cheaper than trying to track down a disc copy of the game for PS2. I personally recommend getting it if you are a fan of the more non-traditional NIS games and/or want to hear more Gig if you're a fan of him in Disgaea 4 and 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Nomad & The World Eaters is an experiment with a questionable outcome. During the PS2 era, when NIS would make a game, it would always end up as a Disgaea clone. Both, being kinda-the-same in both gameplay and the story. A tactical RPG with a light-hearted story and a ton of replay worth. Soul Nomad, however, turned out completely different. Soul Nomad is more or less an old-school Japanese strategy game with some RPG elements. It has a ton of endings and quite a few of easter eggs, but honestly though? - it's only worth finishing two times. Once a normal campaign, once a second campaign. Your first playtrough will be quite enjoyable and will hold some challenge. Once you finish the game, it restarts and you will be given an ability to do the second campaign off the bat.. but the difficulty will be broken. Without abusing the leveling strats it is literally impossible to finish... luckily it takes about 10-15 minutes of farming to powerlevel all your way trough as long as you have the items to do so. Unless you're willing to manually increase your level before each mission, you'll likely end up having a completely busted character. That is a trap, however. The "best" ending cannot be achieved if your character cannot die. The story in this game starts as your average Disgaea title but slowly goes a completely different route, becoming serious, depressing and emotionally taxing. The author combines both campaigns not in a way of them being connected somehow, but in a way that the second campaign will become desirable. "You didn't like what you saw during your first playtrough? - just destroy it then". It's a very unique type of storytelling and, so far, I haven't seen any other game utilizing it.However, it works only as long as you're using English version. The Japanese original... well... It would be a praise to call it "bad". No matter if you understand Japanese or not, just don't use neither the VO or text. Forget that they exist. The translation here isn't a "translation". It actually changes the text in quite a few places to improve the overall story & characters. And about the Ja VO - it's just bad (quality included). If I'd make a guess why it wasn't a big success - it's this, the original Japanese version. The port itself is quite K but far from being perfect. The sprites are just stretched (even the fonts) and honestly, you can get a better result running the game on a specific software with the DX11 support.The mouse controls are good, but the game suffers from native PS2 UI so it plays kinda the same on the controller too.  Basically, it's literally a PS2 port and that's about it. It just works and doesn't suffer from any bugs or optimization issues. The price is a bit too much for a PS2 era game and what is even more strange - it rarely has discounts more than 20%. Don't get me wrong, it is a good game but it certainly isn't worth the full price. Grab it on 20%+ discount.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original game so I cannot give you a proper review just yet but I CAN give you a quick technical breakdown of the port:- A few UI elements are brand new. If you tried to increase texture resolution on an emulator, you would get tiny gaps between some of the textures. The port displays everything correctly.- Sprites are unchanged. There is an option to make them look softer but, as with other NIS PC ports, it looks pretty bad.- 3D elements have not been upgraded either but they look much better than on a PS2 by virtue of screen resolution being higher.- By default, the game plays on a 4:3 aspect ratio with black bars on the sides of the screen. You CAN choose to stretch the picture to fit the whole screen, but it looks squished.- You can use windowed mode, fullscreen or windowed fullscreen. There are several resolution options as well as the option to change keybinds.In short, the game does look better than what you'd get on a native PS2 or even an emulator but it's not necessarily a huge step up  for the higher resolution font. I think it's a serviceable port but would agree that fifteen dollars might have been a more suitable price. Whether or not you pay the original price depends more on how much you want to play this classic as well as see more classic ports on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games from my youth, and honestly holds up to this day. I don't think I can really name another game that is quite like Soul Nomad/Soul Cradle other than maybe X-Com with a ton of mods installed, or maybe X-Com blended with Fire Emblem/Advance Wars.The basic concept of the gameplay is as you progress through the story, you unlock units you can put into individual squads (or Rooms, as the game calls it), with each squad led by one unit who will be able to provide different bonuses or abilities. You can make any unit a squad leader, and this will allow them to do different things in the map during a battle. Think of it like Fire Emblem, except instead of just one guy against one guy, it's entire squads duking it out. And outside of individual fights, you can use different abilities to provide buffs or debuffs, AOEs, instant-damage attacks, all sorts of things. You can do a lot with this, and it only gets deeper from there. Each room you have can be equipped with "decor" items that give bonuses or unique effects to their squads, and you can run through RNG dungeons from the squad organization menu to give individual rooms points that can then be used to modify stats of individual units in a room. On top of this, you have multiple other systems in the background, some working off RNG, some not, along with two merchants you buy from at all times. The merchants in question don't upgrade their shop inventories on their own, so you have to fight the merchants, kill them, and then they get replaced immediately with better guys. Rinse and repeat. In towns and cities, you can interact with various townsfolk through the use of "Gig Edicts" (basically this game's equivalent to items). There's a lot of stuff you can do in this game, and in NG+ and onward there's several different bits of content you can experience. The base normal route story is roughly 30+ hours, though your first run could last a while as you organize your squads and run through side content. There's a lot of things to experience in this game, and I highly recommend anyone at least try it. This game deserves a resurgence, and I'm glad it finally has a proper PC release to encourage that.Also: if you have any gameplay/mechanics questions, feel free to comment or message me and I'll help you out. I had to learn about a lot of this game's mechanics the hard way as a kid, and still remember a lot (along with learning some new things on my current replay).Also on topic of the PC port itself: it's pretty much a 1 for 1 port of the PS2 version with some basic options for video settings. Honestly, you don't need much else besides that. It runs very well, looks gorgeous, and has some great spritework and music. Everything looks, feels, and sounds great. This port could've gone so very badly, but I'm glad it works so well.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn on Soul Nomad because at its base there's a lot of what I love from other NIS titles I've played. In essence the mechanics relating to playing the game just aren't good and it suffers for it.My main issues stem from the mechanics of the game itself. Combat is played out in a single round of attacks between attacker and defender through squads placed in 3x3 grids. Units perform different attacks and abilities based on which row they're placed in. You can choose different leaders for a squad (barring the one with the hero) and they each have different abilities they can use in and out of combat.It's a good system that works well, but there's a problem: Rooms.Rather how many you have, when you get access to more and determining how many slots in which spots exist.Maybe I missed it but I've not seen anything to indicate how many rooms you can have at max. You can utilize a "change" command which will randomize the maximum number of rooms you have available (save for those that are locked which you cannot lock all of them) and this affects the type of room (which passive effect it has) and the slots. Which means you wind up gambling for a good setup more often than not. Rooms can be "inspected" (similar to the Item World from Disgaea) for room points and at certain 'depths' will unlock more space in the room for units. Before performing an inspection you're given an estimate of what level enemies you'll face (along the lines of level 5+) yet the problem is that these estimates can be wildly inaccurate. Yes, level 30 IS covered by saying "5+" but it's a significant gap in strength particularly early in the game. More than once I've gotten a game over from an inspection simply because of this. It's frustrating because if I save inbetween every inspection just in case it gets tedious but every time I don't there's an enemy significantly higher than the base level estimate and I suffer for it.You CAN play the game with just one squad but that feels more than a little disappointing given the variety of classes and room effects.Solid ideas but just awful execution.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Nomad & the World Eaters is a game made during Nippon Ichi's peak. This is the first time this game has been ported off of the PS2, and as such it isn't as pristine as some of the other ported games in the series. Most other games ported thus far were on the PSP, a handheld device released during the end of the PS2 era which had a 16:9 aspect ratio unlike the PS2. While games such as Makai Kingdom, Disgaea 1 and 2 and such were able to make it, Soul Nomad was not, and for good reason. As such this port lacks the same level of care built into the others. Not from a lack of trying, but because the PSP is significantly closer to the PC than a PS2 is, and because the other ports are straight rips from the PSP versions, with a thing or two added on.The game is pretty edgy, and as such, probably had a harder time garnering a more wide spread audience. The game is not bad by any account though. Don't go into it expecting Disgaea, and you may just find your next favorite NIS title. It's a good strategy game and has many unique mechanics that can not be found in any other NIS title. Some innovations that would later be ported to later titles started with this one, such as cross skills, which is something you'll notice right off the bat, with even generics having their own combinations for devastating attacks.I've heard this game get compared to Tactics Ogre in terms of it's squad mechanics, but I've never played that so I wouldn't be able to tell you. The squads in this game are not to be confused with Disgaea 5's though, as it's more of a squad of allies to make up a "Unit" with a leader who commands them. Should the leader fall in battle, the entire squad will pass away after they finish their attacks. I'm already enjoying the combos you can set up with the customization options, but I'm only 3 hours in at the time of review. It's likely to get even better.Honestly I haven't played enough of the game to thoroughly review the gameplay, and as such I will return to this at a later date and update my review. Right now positive reviews are imperative for this game's success, and I happen to have enjoyed the game in the past and presently as I replay through it, so I will go ahead and tell you about the real game seller.This game has an evil route you can unlock after clearing the game. Ever wondered what it would be like if the game let you be an absolute scumbag? Crack open the evil route and completely screw over the world. With Gig at the helm the game goes complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and things that you typically wouldn't see in, say, Disgaea, will start happening. For once, you are the bad guy, and in an already dying world where survival was never a guarantee, I'll leave it up to your imagination what you can manage to do to a world that is already screwed. Let's just say that if you like edgy content you won't be disapointed.This game doesn't have much of an end game, as it's very straight forward. It has five seperate endings, not counting the romance options or anything like this. Yes, if you're a woman you can romance the evil guy locked in the sword, Gig. With the two seperate routes, I think that you'll be pleasantly surprised with the base gameplay. Just don't expect Disgaea, and you'll be good. The writing and characters are a lot better in this than in later Disgaea games, so if you enjoyed the early PS2 games on steam you'll probably like the writing here. Gig is the best character, and this is his game. Check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: is a strategy RPG and a port of the PS2 game from 2007. It has some unique features even in today's booming gaming scene that make it fun to play.The game sets in a small village after a long war. You and your friend Danette get the assignment to protect your own village by Layna who protected the world many years ago. You are given a sword for this purpose, but it has a sealed soul within, Gig. The World Eaters that once threatened the world now reawaken and it's up to you to save the world from the World Eaters. And of course as expected, the story will gradually unfold as you play on. There is a decent amount of storytelling in this game.This game has some unique strategy elements in that you are not commanding individual units but groups of units in squads. The different individual units can be placed in the front, middle, or rear of a squad, and they will take on different roles with different attacks/skills. You will find new units while playing the game, or you can buy them. The different types of units can help strengthen the entire squad as well. You will be able to create multiple squads to take into battle. The squads will attack and will be countered. Likewise, when you get attacked, your squad will automatically counter attack against the aggressor.This is an older game, and so the graphics are a bit dated. But everything felt right in place and they did not bother me in any way.There is voice over for most of the text, and this was really well done. The music also sounds fine.The game can be played with a controller or a mouse and keyboard. It is a console port, so it probably feels most natural with a controller.I think the price of €19.99 is really fair. There is a lot of good gameplay.This game is very good and the unique battles will take some time to get used to. The idea of commanding squads instead of individual units gives a fresh look at this style of tactical strategy game. Once you get the hang of how things work, the mechanics will seem to work really well.For this game, I enjoy the battle system the most, while the story is just okay. The voice over for most of the text is a nice touch.Overall a good title: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Entirely unaltered from the PS2 version, except you can now play it on PC.Good stuff, although I do wish there was a proper widescreen patch and better sprites. The game itself is a fun quirky mix of a Disgaea game and Conception style squad management, with interesting room and item mechanics, and fun characters. Just, don't play the demon route unless you genuinely want to feel disgusted for what you do to all of the characters.Given the insane prices the PS2 version sometimes sells for, this is a reasonable deal compared to tracking one down, and now you don't need to worry about having a working PS2 or making PCSX2 work, should you have chosen the less legitimate route.
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Nomad & the World Eaters

_childDocuments_.review: When you consider this came from the same company in the same console generation where they made Makai Kingdom and Disgaea, the mechanics of this game are extremely simple. Abilities aren't well explained, tons of mechanics aren't explained and so you just see options in menus and have to figure out for yourself what they do. Trial and error is fun for some of the stuff like realizing I can use items while shopping and then attempting to steal an item from the shopkeep, or fighting then kidnapping someone in town, but plenty of other things REALLY should have been better explained or at least had an entry in the help menu(most things don't). The story isn't engaging, dialogue isn't bad but isn't all that great either, and the gameplay is just so simple. Not simple in a way that's still fun, simple in that if you're looking for a SRPG you'll be bored to tears. Also some really annoying and tedious mechanics.Example, the more people you have in a squad the better. How do you get more people in a squad? Roll. You roll a random number of squad members in a random configuration on a random room(different rooms give different effects). Early on 4 members is the norm, and maybe 1 in 50 rolls gives 5 or 6 members, so you're just stuck hitting the button over and over and over hoping to get a larger number of squad members in that room and that it's a room you want.NIS was very experimental in that era and I wouldn't consider this one of their successes. Play a different NIS game. Any Disgaea, Makai Kingdom(though it isn't without its flaws), I've heard good things about Phantom whatever. Just don't play this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Straight port from an oft overlooked NIS game that came out at the end of the PS2 lifecycle. This game makes me feel old because I realized that I am playing on a 32 inch 4k screen from 4 feet afar at best and I am noticing how thing used to really look and how much being far from  a CRT  made this game better looking in my mind.That aside it's a great NIS SRPG and has one of Yuri Lowenthal's best performances.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul Eater and the World Nomad is a game where an ashy twink tries and repeatedly fails to dominate you, despite literally being inside of you.In World Eater and the Soul Eater, you play as Insert Name Here, a protagonist stand in who can only communicate in one-option dialogue trees. After suffering the least impactful mentor betrayal in the history of anime games, your body becomes host to Gig, a man who allegedly orchestrated a global genocide but who spends most of his runtime being the kind of misanthrope that mid-2000s teenagers would find "edgy" and "cool." Together with several other personality possessing characters, you embark on an epic journey to have pointless, completely avoidable fights, and then maybe eventually do something about the doomsday devices parked all around your world.NIS titles are known for their unique, almost experimental takes on strategy RPG combat. Fittingly, Soul World and the Nomad Eaters gives an engaging and lightweight twist on squad-based combat. This is something of a departure for NIS, whose games largely focus on individual units. Because of this, World of Nomads is foreign territory for NIS veterans and newcomers alike. The mechanics of Rooms (the game's method of forming squads) are obtuse and quite poorly explained. In addition, a feature that is notably missing from this title is the ability to replay previous maps. This is bad because it hinders the player's ability to experiment, to try and drill down which units stand where and how to make the best use of the game's randomized squad formations. It also makes onboarding new units incredibly frustrating. While the game features the classic random dungeon mechanic (in the form of Room Inspections), these have all the problems inherent to random dungeons from other NIS titles. Nothing is more annoying than watching six squads of Pyremages gang up on your new unit with their instant kill "Terror Blaze" tactic, or to see half-dead enemy units dutifully commit suicide by running past the guys I'm training to go throw themselves at my veteran squads.That having been said, the game is not nearly as reliant on level grinding as many other NIS titles. The ability exists to buy new characters at higher levels, which makes onboarding a lot smoother. As a general rule, the pace of the game is a lot faster than in other NIS games. Boot it up, and in one session you're already squaring off against the Giant Death Mecha or whatever.The presentation of the game is... anemic. Gig is easily my least favorite protagonist in all of NIS, and that's down mainly to what his role in the party eventually becomes. The man openly states that he's responsible for the apocalypse that happened a century ago, and he goes out of his way to tell Insert Name Here that he will possess his/her body at the first opportunity. Gig also is just a massive prick. He's verbally abusive to the people around him and responsible for a million and one misunderstandings that, ultimately, lead to violence. Despite this, Gig is treated like the leader of the crew. Everyone takes his abuse on the chin, acting like he's nothing more than a wacky foul-mouthed comedy ghost, and not a clear existential threat who's trying to possess one of their friends. The main character, themselves, seems to be more concerned about whether Gig can see them pooping than what the violent, genocidal maniac would do with their body, if given the chance. The description I got of this game was that it was more "adult." But, let's not kid ourselves. It's "adult" in the sense that people say swear words more often. In every other respect, this is teenage nonsense straight out of a mid-tier mid-2000s shonen.In summary, Soul Soul and the Soul Souls is a game that does interesting things in the genre of SRPGs. Once you get past the initial learning curve, it's genuinely fun to play. However, like a lot of NIS titles, it throws you into the deep end with very little assistance. Veterans of this developer will no doubt enjoy the game, regardless, and my issues with the overall presentation do not detract from the game enough to change my recommendation. I give this game a "ha ha funny genocide man said the R-slur" out of 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Outdated and frankly unfun in modern age of gaming. Only approach equipped with Overflowing Nostalgia decor.Main cast is well written and interesting, but side characters are criminally underdeveloped. Excuse being that they "are not there" due to Domination system.Plotline has some interesting moments but is way to contrived and jumps between finger pointing city erasing gods and mundane way too much, after sopem point you just cannot treat the story seriously as the characters who live in it are not making any sense. Bosses are barely introduced and have zero personality or development beside the Wizzard and his Warrior pal. The world itself has *some* depth with teh way NPCs move from town to town and change their dialogues but the world itself and its history makes zero sense.The amount of missions that are designed to make you lose in order to progress is criminal (although power leveling in this game can be done pretty efficiently).The battle system was pretty fun but is is completely ruined by absolutely awful one-time-use decor system and Casino Room system that is literally designed to waste your time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a port. It runs. I finished the game without experiencing a single bug or issue that interfered with my playing experience.It's a squad tactical RPG game. You get heroes, you recruit generic dudes of various classes, and you build squads using "rooms" that you unlock over the course of the game that start with only a few members but will grow as large as 9.  Each unit will attack differently based on what row they are positioned in the formation, whether it's front, middle, or rear.  It's probably where Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga got all their ideas from, as both systems are indeed a bit similar, although the only resource for recruiting units is GP in Soul Nomad.The game was absolutely fantastic.  There was excessive use of the ableist term  but wholly from a singular toxic demon character, so if the term really bothers you I wouldn't recommend this title.  Despite how terrible a demon imprisoned in my soul was at conversation, the game still yielded a fantastic and alluring story that kept me playing until the end, only to learn you can take things in a drastically different pathway in repeated cycles (new game+), giving way towards replayability as you seek this games' secrets. I don't want to spoil anything, it was just a really awesome and more atypical type of story and setting compared to most RPG games.The music was phenomenal. The english voice acting was terrific and well done from all performers.  Some of the combats can feel like slogs but it is a tactics RPG at its heart so can't really complain there.  Plenty of story to even give visual novel enthusiast types a story worth playing.Also if you have difficulty with difficulty in game, there are items that you can purchase from a store to either strengthen or weaken the world level of your opponents, so you can make the game as hard as or easy as you desire.  also it really helps when you need to boost levels as you level up, as max level is somewhere in the four digits I think.I'm very happy to play this game through to completion and after giving myself a break I'll definitely be going through the NG+ mode for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Soul nomad is a difficult game with a lot of mechanics, based off of random RNG. Like most NIS games is about power leveling but the options that they hand to you are very harsh on beginners for this style of game. I have played three hours and spent most of that time in game over screens. Story is quite interesting and the character models are gorgeous. I cannot equip individual characters but rather the room with disposable items.
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Nomad & the World Eaters

_childDocuments_.review: 3D models and music are ok, but the rest of the game didn't age very well. The story isn't captivating, pretty much every character is uninteresting and most cutscenes just feel like there isn't much effort in them. The combat system often targets random enemies, which leads to unnecessary waiting until you hit the right one. And if you decide to do some grinding, any challenge from the campaign will just disappear. Overall it's a no from me.100% boils down to grinding random room stages, and going through the game a few times to find some secrets.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I really wanted to like, but I just don't think I can recommend. This game tries to do a lot of cool stuff, but only a few parts of it really end up working. The story starts out strong, but meanders through the second half. There are a lot of cool mechanics in the game, but you really only need to care about a few of them. The writing is really well done but is also full of early 2000s humor that has aged like milk. The most consistently positive thing about the game for me is the art style. I really like seeing NIS try an art style that is different from their normal Disgaea style (not that that's a bad art style).I wish this game had been popular enough for a sequel so that there was another chance to iron out the problems with this game. But there are plenty of other strategy rpgs out there that do what this game does, but better.

_childDocuments_.review: Go play disgaea instead, this game has too many issues many of which being balance issues. This game is a total RNG fest when it comes to leveling. The story is actually interesting in a way but you're really not making any meaningful decisions at all 99% of the time. I believe the only time it matters is when you see the skull which is a bad ending btw aka, a game over but you can do it anyway if you want to. The combat is okay but as I stated, an RNG fest so sometimes you can get lucky most of the time you probably won't. Also the stats don't even matter half the time, you can literally use items to more than double your stats, be twice the level of an enemy with doubled stats, and they can still hit you and debuff you because reasons. . . Doesn't sound like a big deal, until you realize that these debuffs LAST FOR THE REST OF THE ENCOUNTER AND YOU CANNOT REMOVE THEM!!!!! So when you see those blasted witches that lower your defense murder and pillage them with no remorse because they can, and will spam that skill until you get one shotted because balance! Seriously though, go play the disgaea series instead. This game isn't absolutely unplayable, if disgaea didn't exist, MAYBE I can give this a mixed/positive review, but it does exist, so why would you even buy this? You shouldn't. This line is old and used up but I played this so you didn't have to, seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm here because of my love to this game and because it holds a special spot in my heart.I don't think I can recommend this to new player especially those who've experienced crazy graphics and gameplays out there.However, I am still a fan of Nippon Ichi's turn-based tactics game with unique comedy and art styles, that's why I have faith Soul Nomad.It's different from Nippon's previous game like the Disgaea series; I find the battle system unique during its era since it's not your typical TBT. Instead you play by "Room" and each Room have 3 slots; Front, Rear, Back. Your characters' skills are set depending on where they're positioned at, so all you need to grind is pure status (HP, ATK, DEF etc) by levelling up. No equipment, no skill adjustment.Grinding has always been fun and I still aim to be at level 9999.In my PS2 era, I spent 100+ hours just to grind.The plot is there and Gig is amazing! Ain't we all just love Gig like how he loves his Hotpod, heh.1000000000% best soulmate.Silent protagonist is one of its weak point I guess, altho it doesn't make the game less interesting.It's also unfortunate that the dev doesn't make a single effort to revamp or polish the game (like they did Disgaea), not even to adjust it to wide screen (even WORSE, it's a STRETCHED 3:4). Having an alternative to have black border and keep it 3:4 would be much better.P.S.: Another thing to be fond of is the fact that Nippon Ichi's games always have crossover meta boss/character, aaaaand... a DEMON ROUTE! Because being a hero is boring, yeah?
_childDocuments_.name: Soul Nomad & the World Eaters

_childDocuments_.review: The PS2 era NIS games are always a treat to play and its no different with Soul Nomad. Chocked full of unique and experimental mechanics, the puzzle of mastering this game was a real treat.I need to make a complaint first. NIS literally put out this port and clearly didn't playtest some aspects of it.The Switch port which I also own, crashes during certain story cutscenes, forcing you to skip them altogether. This port however, I didn't have any crashes... on my first playthrough.Upon revisiting the game to try and get the Demon ending, it kept crashing on the first map and I was forced to give up, which isn't a great feeling and I really hope NIS take more care of their future ports as game preservation is an important thing that should never be half assed.Do I recommend this port? Yes, the main story is still really good, it had a lot of twists and turns that I was not expecting and Gig is a really fun and likable character.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended just for the story alone. Very immersive, the characters are very memorable and feel very alive, and paced just right with just enough twists and turns to keep your attention.  Gameplay on the other hand will either be somewhat challenging and engaging for first timers, or too easy once you know about power leveling. If it is you're first time ever playing, i would recommend just following the story and only doing inspections (random dungeons) when you absolutely need either to be a higher level or more resources (GP, Decor, Edicts). After both stories (there is one where you are now the bad guy), then I would suggest raising your levels to astronomical numbers, and finding all the secrets. Because the only real challenge left after both campaigns is inspection grinding.But anywho, everything else (music, art style, sfx, etc) is very nice. Game is easily 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was playing Disgaea 3 since I was in high school I was introduced to this game.  I have been a really big fan of this game and I wanted NIS to have a sequel game, I wanted to see so much of their beloved one off games to have sequels. Phantom Brave and Makai Kingdom received some love on their end. Soul Nomad in my opinion deserves a sequel, and possibly have the Disgaea Treatment where it can have it's own story separate from the first and still introduce newer concepts of the races we have presented with different units that can really mingle with the game play.Honestly I am very happy that I have the game that I love back in my life and now working on new cycles/achievement hunting . I highly suggest this game to those who have a similar taste in squad building, strategy, and enjoying a simple story that will satisfy you.

_childDocuments_.review: As a non-nostaliga player this game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast. After reading several reviews I took a chance on this game and I am so glad I did. I didn't play this when I was younger, but have really been enjoying my time with this one. Pros:Can go full screen- despite some reviewers stating you couldn't change the black box around the screen, I have found this to be incorrect. You can make the game go full screen without issues and it looks great.Updated graphics- again, despite some reviews saying otherwise, you can tell that there has been some clean up and sharpening of the character and map sprites. I even went back to images of the original game to make sure. It isn't a full remaster, but it doesn't claim to be so I'm okay with that. The art is charming and the images are clear both on my monitor and on a TV. The characters- I love Gig with all my heart, and I am so glad that there hasn't been any censoring of his lines or personality. The other characters are enjoyable most of the time as well, and although I am never really in a rush to find out what happens next, I am enjoying cut scenes, and battles with the cast of characters. The voice acting is also on point for the most part.Squads- such a fun battle mechanic. I really enjoy finding the classes that work together, the rooms that suit them best, and the placement that helps me win battles without casualties. Battles- they are fun. Simple as that. You can turn off the system voice- thank ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ godCons:Not everything is explained- be prepared to do some googling to find out the best way to level grind, how room decor really works, and other questions like that. There isn't any hand holding, and the game as a whole is better for it, but I'm also glad we have the interwebs and a wide collection of how to guides.Challenging until- this game can feel brutal until you figure out a few things and put in some level grinding. It is possible per multiple players to never feel grind buuuuut I feel that the game is way to hard for ME to do that. I love grinding so this isn't really a con for me, but it might be for you. Overall- so worth both the time and the money. I am enjoying every battle and every cut scene. Gig is the best, and the game has a level of humor that wouldn't be allowed today that I find refreshing and hilarious.

name: Imp of the Sun
detailed_description: More From Fireshine! About the Game Imp of the Sun is a non-linear 2D Action-platformer that combines fast-paced combat and exploration set across a stunning Peruvian-inspired world, from the bright peaks of the Andean mountains to the dense Amazonian jungles and much more. You play as Nin, an Imp created from the final spark of the Sun, who is sent on an adventure to defeat the Four Keepers and restore the Sun’s power, ending the Eternal Eclipse before the world is plunged into darkness. End the Eternal Eclipse Stolen by the Four Keepers centuries ago and hidden in the distant corners of the Empire, life cannot go on without the Sun’s power. With its dying spark the Sun creates Nin, sending him on an adventure to bring back the light and restore balance to the Empire. Use your Inner Fire As a creature of the Sun, you have the power of its flame at your fingertips. Refine your skills in streamlined gameplay built for fluid movement and combo-based combat and discover new abilities to become more powerful as you venture across the Sun’s Empire to defeat the Four Keepers. Explore, Collect and Learn Our ancestors recorded their history through artefacts known as ‘Quipus’. Collect Quipus to unveil the story behind the Eternal Eclipse, and find unique hidden items based on real relics from the Andean cultures. Explore the Sun’s Empire and defeat unique, punishing bosses in any order you choose; each with their own complex mechanics and backstory. A Stunning Peruvian-Inspired World Discover the four corners of the Empire, from the bright peaks of the Andean mountains and dense Amazonian jungles, to dry, blistering deserts and the dark depths of the underworld. Every land and creature are lovingly hand-drawn and crafted with detail, celebrating the civilizations that once roamed and ruled Peru. Features Streamlined gameplay built for fluid movement and combo-based combat. Unique Peruvian-influenced art style and soundtrack, inspired by real-world relics of the Andean culture. Experience five unique and punishing bosses in any order you choose each with their own complex mechanics and backstory. Keep powering up as players learn how to better control the Imp and its power and navigate the environments. Imp of the Sun is built to be played and then re-played, players may even find short cuts along the journey. Play Eclipse Mode for the authentic experience in a darkened kingdom, with all areas shrouded in total darkness until explored by the Imp. Join our Discord:

_childDocuments_.review: The influence of this game seems to be very clear: Ori and Blind Forest/Will of the Wisps. It has the Metroidvania-aspects where you get new powers like dashes and slides to get to areas unreachable before, although all in all the game seems to be much smaller and more linear. You even have a very similar animation and sound effect for the air dash, for example. Exploration besides the path seems to be only rewarded with bonus items which give you orbs which you can use to level up hp/mana/attack power.The artstyle is quite unique and I like the hand-drawn style very much. However, there are literally no graphic options and the game seems to be locked at 60 fps, which seem to be solid 59-60 on my display - however I get some little stutter effects which seems odd, I don't notice any drop in frame rates (except loading screens). You should at least be able to configure resolution, vsync and such, even though this is "only" a 2D platformer.Now truth be told, the platforming isn't as crisp as Ori. It works fine though, most of the time, but I wish it would feel more fluid, I loved dashing and jumping around in Ori - it's not the same here (not yet, at least), where I could get stuck at a slightly overhanging edge.The combat is another thing - I don't think it's well thought through, to be honest. First of all, you have no dodge or anything which can make you invincible at least for a short amount of time. Which would be fine, but with most, even the basic enemies, the attack frame is way too short and you are not able to get out of the way. You can overhelm most of the enemies by stunlocking them on the ground or with air combos, however, this is not working when the games throws like 8 enemies at you at the same time, where you need to employ a hit and run (and heal) tactic because you can't get to them all the time.The game needs to communicate hitboxes and attacks better. This got to a point where it was really frustrating - the first boss (Desert Temple for me, although you can go anywhere you want at first it seems). I got knocked over by handle of his weapon on the backswing, I couldn't get away from him because he pushed me to the edge of the platform, I died like 10 times wishing I had a dodge move to get away from his attacks instead of just staying at least 2 meters away each time he swings his weapon like he has Corona. Good combat shouldn't include staying out of the way when the enemy attacks, good combat should be engaging the enemy and dodging, blocking or parrying his attacks. In the end, it brute forced my way through this boss, hammering him with air attacks, ignoring his attacks until I needed to heal. This didn't feel good but it was the only way it worked for me.Summary:

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is a good looking little platformer nevertheless. And it is the first game I ever played inspired by Peruvian culture and tales. You play a little imp made of fire, sent by the (dying) Sun (Imp of the Sun, now I get it) and tasked with defeating four Keepers that brought an eternal eclipse to the country. You do so by platforming and fighting enemies. Find keys, collect lost maps and pieces of forgotten lore, get sun (coins) to upgrade your health, strength and inner fire. Double jump, throw your sunspear, slide and attack foes in close combat. Your imp can heal itself with his inner fire, which can be recharged at bright spots (close to a lit torch). Fluid movement and combo-based combat are at the center of gameplay, the whole game mechanics are Metroidvania inspired. Learn new abilities to be able to reach formerly unaccessible parts of the four worlds, find hidden stuff to learn about the background lore, find shortcuts, and most of all master difficult jumping sections under time pressure and defeat the bosses to advance. Gamepad support is good, the completely missing support for different screen resolutions is not. The game is saved at an old (actually, deceased) explorer, who also has some hints for you and helps you to level up.Short (four worlds) Metroidvania-inspired platformer, quite challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost stopped playing the game due to its subpar game design, but I did finish it and it was even somewhat enjoyable. In the next paragraphs I'll explain why I do not recommend this game. It's actually not that bad, but I don't think it's worth its money.First of all, the art is gorgeous and one of the reasons the game caught my eye in the first place. The animation on the other hand could take some improvement though. The animated sprites look like they have very little frames and the cutscenes are mostly static artworks with some animated zoom and distortion. This animation style is certainly not my favorite, but also not a reason to dislike the game.The movement feels mostly good, except for the jump. Pushing the jump button will always make you jump the same height, no matter how long you press it; this doesn't give a great amount of control. This is most annoying when doing consecutive wall jumps while trying to dodge spikes on the wall. The mid air dash feels also pretty bad, especially when you want to dash on a diagonal; You have to be very accurate with the analog stick, otherwise I'll either go straight up or to the side. It was a much better experience on the D-Pad, because it's much easier if it's only 8-directional, but who wants to play with a D-Pad?The level design isn't really impressive, but it's ok, except for the few instances where it's god awful. At some point in the beginning it was showing me something to collect when jumping down a ledge; I wasn't able to look down, but the fact that I was able to collect something suggested that I can jump down. I just ended up standing on another ledge in front of a closed door. There was no way out except jumping into the abyss. The game wanted me to approach that door from the other side, but I couldn't really tell without jumping down. Misleading things like this occurred a few times in the game; not very often, but they're there.The enemy types lack creativity and the AI is pretty terrible. Nearly every enemy works the same way: Walk towards player -> attack when close enough. This basic logic was only operating on the x-axis though; when enemies are on the platform above you, they'll just try to stand just on top of you. When there is a ledge, they'll walk down that ledge, even if they jump to their death. It's the most simple behavior you could give an enemy, and it applies to most enemy types (not to bosses, of course).The game tells you that enemies get harder the more you progress and with that it basically means that it gives them more HP; it's the most lazy difficulty scaling possible.The game will always spawn the enemies in the same position, and it doesn't care if you are standing in that position; it'll spawn the enemy on top of you and you'll receive damage immediately. Enemies will also spawn outside of your vision while locked up in an area; at one point I was wondering why the room was not opening, until I realized another enemy spawns off screen once I've beaten all the others.The bosses are imo also not a great experience. I don't want to spoil any mechanics, but the bosses range from "easy, but high HP, and infinite heals for the player" over "annoying but two good combos will kill it rather quickly" to "undodgeable attacks without any chance of healing". Last but not least, there is this annoying little girl that is talking to you all the time. She is basically a backseat gamer who tells some obvious things. When you stand in front of a closed door, she tells you that "there must be a leaver somewhere around"; the first time this might be helpful but once I know that leavers are used to open doors, she really doesn't have to tell me for every single door that I need to pull a leaver. In some cases she just says "Woah" when I kill a bunch of trash mobs. In the few cases where she provided valuable information, I was probably not even reading the text because I was just annoyed by her talking all the time. There was a lot I had to criticize, but the game can still be enjoyed. It just felt to me like it wanted to be another "Ori", so it set very high expectations that it wasn't able to meet. Furthermore it's beaten in about five hours, which is rather short, even for a title that costs just 20 Euros. I am not saying that this is a bad game; I am just saying that there are better titles in the same price range.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great looking and sounding gameand that's about all i can say about it because it just doesn't ''feel'' rightI was using a controller to play and it still ended up feeling stiff and clunky in little waysThings like the double jump not quite feeling as high as it should or your melee attack not quite having the reach you need,The wall jump feeling off since you need to push into the wall but if you jump while holding the direction into the wallit won't launch off the wall so you have to press into the wall, let go of the movement button, jump before you press the directional key to press yourself into the other wall and continue up that way until you reach the top, awkward huh?some other stuff i found to be somewhat bothersome is that your character moves just a bit ''too'' fast You can't really make use of that speed due to the level design so it's an odd choice to have in the first placeAside from that the character dialogue can't be skipped as far as i can tell and that's not a problem until you need to chat with the character that's both the level up and warp mechanic, i'm no stranger to ''Bearer seek seek lest'' but that got old really fast, maybe there was a skip button? but it wasn't the usual suspects so... no idea?also the achievements don't seem to work as of writing this review, i found this out after a frustrating boss fight that used a lot of the mechanics i described above, not a big deal if i were having oodles of fun but i just wasn'tAll in all i'm sure some people will have fun with this and maybe the visuals will be enough to carry dedicated people through but it just didn't do it for me, with a bit of spit shine on the gameplay i think whatever the dev team decides to make next could be a homerun though!

_childDocuments_.review: Glad to see Chimchar finally gets his own game, I wanted him to be in smash but this is even better!My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like a Dollar Store Ori.Wow! It is Ori like! And this does not mean that it does not have value, literally the opposite. It’s so much like a brighter version of Ori.First off, I wanna say the game is so cute, I really liked the NPC designs, and the main character design is ADORABLE, I love little fire monke Nin. The backgrounds are really pretty, the areas are really beautiful, and I mostly really like it, although it's really really easy to feel very lost and confused at the beginning. The environment designs and the vibrant colors were just gorgeous. There were things at first I wasn’t sure about, but having finished the game I can say it’s definitely a fun and worthwhile little game! Takes a lot of influence from Ori, but until you find the movement upgrades the game feels a little sluggish, although you should find them fairly quickly. Once I found that it became a great ol' time running around destroying enemies, though the loss of resources when you die can be a little aggressive when you are trying to get the bigger upgrades. I feel like the combat throughout most of the game is fairly easy but each boss presents a significant difficulty spike and this can definitely be frustrating. Exploration is pretty fun, the four areas are small enough that the lack of a map isn't too much of a problem (although a more detailed map of each area would have been appreciated) and big enough to have a bunch of fun collectibles hidden around them. It's a lovely little game. Inca mythos is so under rated, so I was very glad to see a game about that actually being well made. It was great.  Little on the shorter side at around 10 hours.  But was a blast all the way through. If you enjoyed Ori and Metroidvanias in general you'll like this.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Short but sweet little metroidvania, after the tutorial segment the entire game map immediately opens up and lets you go off in one of four directions, the controls are fast and fairly solid (the dash mechanic doesn't like going diagonal but that was the biggest issue I had) and the platforming and combat, while never super deep, are pretty fun. It also looks gorgeous and there's a fairly diverse array of environments. Bosses are a mixed bag, the darkness one in particular is... not good, and boss fights either tend to feel like "bosses go down immediately or they take forever and then you end up losing" which... ehh, it's not super polished and, like, I 100%ed the game in just over 4 hours (though my IGT is a lot higher for some reason) so it's not super long, but I did enjoy what it had to offer. Not essential, but if you need a quick fix it'll satisfy you.Of note: Achievement integration is completely broken, I used SAM to toggle the achievements I had actually earned in-game but there's no way to unlock them naturally.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated for Steam award thingy. Recommendation comes with a big fat *, but I'll get to that later.So obviously the visual and audio design is among the best of any media in the century, like this game is a playable illustration book with a symphony weaved into it's pages.The story is fairly light, not delving too deep into any specific area, especially so if you ignore optional collectibles, but despite that I felt engaged, wanting to learn more. The story's length also benefits the game's pacing, keeping things from staying still too long, because you'll probably get around 4 hours on your first play through.Controls are a dream, constantly darting around and juggling enemies like an acrobat hyped up on caffiene is fun to master and beat the game in quicker times.Because you got a choice between any of the four areas, you can get abilities in any order, said abilities letting you potentially skip parts of other areas.So if one area is giving you trouble, you can try other areas, gain powers there, and then return.Now for that big fat * I hinted at earlier.While the game itself is a great time, the technical issues I had, weren't.The more obvious problem is steam achievements are broken for most players. Personally, that's not a problem for me, however this issue is: Music doesn't work often.I don't know why or what can cause this, but for my playthroughs, The majority of the music would not play.Only tracks that played consistently were Overture, Hubworld and any tracks part of one of the game's cutscenes.Despite those technical issues, I still recommend the game! It's really fun and has a lot of effort put into it. But you might want to look into other versions and see if they don't have the music issue I described.Thank you for your attention!
