_childDocuments_.review: Great visual style akin to Ori but unfortunately the execution couldn't be more botched. Theres so many problems with the game it would take less time to list the things right with it. Platforming is some of the most slippery and floaty I've seen in a long time, and for many parts requiring precision it is baffling. The hitboxes are also some of the worst I've ever seen in a game as they are super inconsistent, and I even got hurt by attack animations that were already completed. One boss you have to hit his head and 2/3 of the time I would swipe at his head it would count it as shoulder. There also is no video options, but there are constant frame drops and stuttering built into the game, which is wild for a low graphic 2d platformer. The story is pretty uneventful, you need to kill some guardians to get back the sun. The upgrades are boring, as its just more health, attack damage, and mana. You unlock 2-3 hit combos in air and ground which is just attack spam. Then theres the other issues. The dash doesn't have i-frames for some inexcusable reason. Also your i-frame after being hit lasts around .5 seconds meaning you can easily be hit again right away, strike 2. The wall jumping is super buggy and inconsistent. I encountered multiple bugs in my playthrough with new screens not transitioning, as well as others like getting stuck in damaging pit and it not allowing me to dash up. One of the bosses is super poorly designed based on all the basic issues with the game making it a chore and you never feel like your death was earned. The map is also useless, and if a platformer semi-metroidvania can't be bothered to put in a working map showing you where you are and the layout, that says it all. So many of the simplest things required for this type of game were put in a flawed state it's sort of mind-boggling. The devs also abandoned the game right after release and never even released ANY FOLLOW UP PATCHES. No wonder there's still so many issues, was clearly just dumped and forgotten. And if they can't be bothered to fix any of it or put it any effort, I can't be bothered to enjoy it. 5.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, coming back to this game after nearly 50 HOURS in this game, and I would have to say that it has strengths and weaknesses.Firstly, love the setting. I haven't really seen that many games set in Peruvian mythology or whatever, but this game pulls it off pretty well in my opinion. The art is great for the most part (some background elements are at a lower resolution which becomes pretty noticeable at 1080p), along with good animations. I love the movement in the game for the most part, as both the intentional and unintentional movement feels real nice.However, I do have some gripes with this game. Firstly, no remapping of controls whatsoever which is incredibly annoying. Secondly, this game has some jank. When grinding for the "No leveling" achievement, I started to notice some annoying bits of oversight. Tui's attacks have poorly programmed hitboxes and just linger, enticing you to actually try approaching. This is the only main annoying bug in this game, the rest are mostly just good speedrun tech. But the attack hitboxes along with plenty of questionable game design tidbits are only really annoying when going for the achievement runs.Overall, I'd say the game is pretty good. Although I would personally aim to buy the game on sale if possible.Oh, also, Steam achievements aren't synced. Which completely sucks because I put myself through the pain of getting them all.

_childDocuments_.review: Imp of the sun is one of those games that despite some flaws still has that oh-so-wonderful indie charm to it. The game is bursting with it! From the colourful characters, to the beautiful backgrounds, and from the whimsical music to the heartfelt story. Each and every aspect of the game is a true joy to experience except for two things, one mayor and one minor. These being the floaty controls and achievements not working. The latter is not that big of a deal although it's a bit of bummer, however the former is kind of a shame.The game, while playing very smoothly, is a bit too fast paced. You run and jump around at double the speeds of other sidescrollers, it even makes ori seem slow in comparison. Falling is also super fast so if you miss a jump you can fall down quite far, 'getting over it'-style. These controls would hamper my enjoyment but the rest of it is just so good that i can't help but love the game. It's pretty short but suprisingly fun and a definite recomendation to any platformer/metroidvania fan. It's also quite accesible in terms of combat, with easy but fun bossfights and fast paced combat. The platforming is quite tough at times but only for short bursts. All in all a fun and charming game that any fan of the genre should play. 8/10On a last note I'd like to give a shoutout to setting, that being either inca/aztec/mayan or something else (i'm not sure). Can game developers please start making more games with said setting? I swear every game is either a greek, norse, roman or medieval setting and it's getting a bit stale. We need more southern american settings! Also more ancient egyptian games would be appreciated. Thank you for coming to my ted talk. Bye!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a sweet metroidvania, but more of a starter type as it is very short and the combat is more of a hack and slash than anything more difficult like Hollow Knight, or Nine Sols. I had a fun time playing it, but some of the game mechanics annoyed me at first, especially how there is a ramp up to your movement speed, which can make precise jumping a pain. There was also a bit of a lag between button inputs and actions happening sometimes, especially when climbing areas. Overall I'd give this a 6/10. A fun simple game that will allow you to while away a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game if on the shorter side. Story (or rather the way it's told) very inspired by Ori. Some decent puzzles and platforming. Combat is nothing special, but doesn't get in the way of the fun either. You can do each of the 4 areas in either order, which gets some openness, but on the other hand each area needed to be designed to only need the ability unlocked in said area (though having others helps) which limits the level design. This is true for the bosses, though hilariously, if you unlock the smokeform & dash abilities before heading to the wall jump area you can absolutely triavialize the boss in said area, because you don't actually need to wait for the boss to make itself accessible to attack. This is not a criticism, but a complement - this is good stuff. it's a good game if you take it for what it is. As for the comments I see about this game having bad controls, I can't say I noticed any of that.
_childDocuments_.name: Imp of the Sun

_childDocuments_.review: It starts off rough, but turns into a fun metroidvania.Like any metroidvania you have to unlock movement and combat options as you progress, but with this one it felt like the character was too underpowered to survive any combat and the movement felt awkward(i.e. the jump is useless but the double jump is strong and the game doesn't tell you you have it from the start). By learning timing for platforming and grinding for stats in combat the movement and combat becomes more fluid and fun. Aside from the gameplay the story is a neat one. The setting and influences aren't too common in a lot of games I've seen, which is great. The story it self is fine, it's simple and works.The Art and sounds are gorgeous. The hand painted look for everything from the characters to the background is stunning and the sounds and tracks perfectly fit the areas, bosses and provide a but of personality to the enemies.It may have a slow start, but once it gets going this is a great game for a great price.
_childDocuments_.name: Imp of the Sun

That said, it's not perfect, there are bugs, some aspects of the game play are annoying, most of the gripes you hear in the negative reviews are accurate. Regardless, I enjoyed the game more than enough to give it a thumbs-up and a hope to see more like this soon!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a metroidvania, similar to Ori but significantly worse.Controls are unresponsive in an annoying way for something that rely on platforming.The biggest reason i do not like this game however is the NPC's, the speaking is horrible, the text is slow and pauses half way through for no other reason than forcing you to listen to their nonsensical rambling. You cannot lower or turn down the sound of it either since the only options you have in the game at all is SFX, Music and Master volume. You are forced to pick up the radio from a girl that clearly is attempted to make "cute" but to me was just obnoxious, to make it even worse she keeps backseating while you are playing. Anything from popping in to say "how are we going to solve this puzzle?" to "awesome you killed an enemy" (that has been killed multiple times already....) when she eventually started SPOILING things i had enough. "we are getting close to the desert", "try attacking under its shield", before i can even get a chance to try it myself.Game is not just badly polished, they assume you are a complete moron who cant figure things out yourself, and therefor give you the solution before the fight/explore/puzzle.Sure, this might just be because its early game, but this is enough for me to ask for a refund, and i LOVE metroidvanias, even the bad ones... but this is too much spoiling my fun. I recommend looking at the egoraptor video "Sequelitis - Mega Man Classic vs. Mega Man X" This game does everything that video touches on wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: *STEAM ACHIEVEMENTS DO NOT WORK FOR THIS GAME*An accessible Action Platformer with "Metroidvania Lite" elements.Probably the biggest thing I want to talk about in this review is the difficulty of the game, a topic on which I have many thoughts (which I hope are useful to you, the potential buyer of this game):-Difficulty (normal game) is below-average unless you self-impose it by avoiding leveling and not taking every healing opportunity (pretty much every combat area has a torch, which provides unlimited healing and special ability "fuel" if you choose to utilize your fuel).-There is a skill tree for normal attacks, a leveling system, unlockable special abilities, and unlockable "ultimate moves."==The skill tree didn't seem to make that big of a difference because it just seemed to change your style of normal attacks (not sure how much damage varied between regular normal attacks and these unlocked normal attacks).==The leveling system made the biggest change in character strength and durability. You can level up health, energy capacity, and attack power. I focused on attack power first, health second, and energy capacity third, and it seemed like an effective strategy because I breezed through the game (though it seems like many breeze through this game, so perhaps the order doesn't matter). Overall, I think that if you are playing the normal game and want a challenge, you should probably limit yourself on leveling or abstain from it entirely, because you very quickly become OP. The upgrade prices are remarkably cheap, which means you're typically going to be overleveled for every boss you face.==Unlockable special abilities were primarily useful for exploration but also have utility in combat as well.=="Ultimate moves" (I forget their official name) are charged up by quick, repeated succession of normal attacks on enemies and then can be used for a limited time once fully charged. They are basically one-hit-KO moves (except for the healing one) and I rarely felt any need to use them.-I steamrolled every boss except the final boss because for some reason the devs decided to put torches in the boss arenas. I don't know why you would give a player unlimited healing and special ability fuel in a boss arena, but they did (except for the final boss). Bosses often were easier than some of the "enemy horde waves" rooms that you get locked into at certain points in the game, which doesn't make sense to me from a design/balancing perspective. Enemies in the horde wave rooms, despite individually being weaker than the bosses by a wide margin, at least had the advantage of "strength in numbers." You could end up backed into a corner with a mob in your face and you rarely would have time to heal (despite having unlimited fuel from a torch) because even if one or two enemies weren't actively attacking you, another one or two were. Bosses, meanwhile, were 1v1 affairs and they had plenty of periods of inactivity where you could heal pretty much at will.-Overall, boss fights were one of the biggest disappointments of this game because even though the game was overall on the easy side, the bosses were just total pushovers. One boss in particular was actually embarrassingly pathetic; I literally just jumped at his head, held the "down" button, and mashed attack until he was dead. It took probably 10-15 seconds and he had no chance. "Attack bouncing" overall is pretty OP in this game, but this was the most glaring example. Very few enemy attacks provide knockback, so you can just tank the hits without being displaced from the weak spot you're attacking. It then just becomes a race to 0 health, and your character typically wins (unless you're intentionally underleveled).-After completing the main story of the normal game, you unlock Eclipse Mode +, which from what I read is a New Game + version in which the energy recharge benefit associated with "sunny" areas is removed. In the normal game, if you are in a "sunny" area (indicated by an icon next to your energy bar), your energy bar slowly recharges on its own. This auto-recharge makes healing and using special powers much easier because all you have to do is wait if you are low or empty. Nothing I've read indicates that any other aspect of energy recharging is different (defeating enemies still regenerates various levels of energy and torches still top up your energy). Overall, I really like when games are accessible to a variety of player skill levels, but while this game kind of does that, it is unfortunate that it imposes mandatory "easy mode" upon players for their entire first playthrough and only gives a chance for a better challenge to players that have already seen everything the game has to offer. I, for one, rarely replay games, even the ones in my personal "hall of fame," so the expectation that I will be willing to play through the game twice in order to get my preferred difficulty experience from start-to-finish is a bit presumptuous.-As you can see in the last screenshot featured on the store page here, there are times where dialogue from your character's friend will pop up on the screen. This dialogue is recurrent throughout the entire game and functions as a hint system. I checked the settings and did not see any way to turn these hints off. I would have preferred to have these disabled if given the option because they will pretty much explicitly tell you what you need to do any time you reach any section with any sort of puzzle aspect to it (and these are not exactly brain-breaking puzzles, mind you). IIRC the audio of these dialogues are not in English, so I guess you could potentially try to ignore reading the text, but I reflexively just read them when they popped up.Now, onto other aspects of the game:-Runtime is on the short end (I did not 100% but did complete the main story of the normal game and it took me 5.3 hours per Steam).-There is opportunity for backtracking if you want to 100% the game, but if you just want to beat the main story you don't really have any reason to revisit any areas you've been before. The four domains connected to the hub area can be completed in any order, but there are some collectibles blocked off in those areas that require a powerup from another area in order to be accessed.-Controls were tight and responsive. My only gripe with the controls is that, When you hold left or right to move, you'll start moving at one speed but then will start moving at a faster speed for as long as you continue holding the button down. The transition between those two speeds just felt... off, and some jumps with short runways felt very unnatural as a result. Not intuitive like Mario games are.-I think the visuals are an obvious draw (HEH, GET IT?) here. The game really looks great. I didn't notice any sort of performance issues, and the load times were reasonable (probably 5-7 seconds to move between domains or teleport). Very great work in these areas by the devs.-In terms of music, it all was very "fine," but also very forgettable and unremarkable. I guess I can say that it at least matched the ambiance of the environments, wasn't distracting, and wasn't annoying or repulsive in any way. Perhaps people with different musical tastes than I have will enjoy it more, but I at least don't think anyone will walk away from the game saying "man, I HATED the music in that game."-Price. I got this game for $7.49 and I would buy it again for that price. $19.99 seems a bit steep but $10 or less is probably a good price point given how short the game is.Overall, I enjoyed the game but wasn't blown away. A PERFECT game for a younger audience, lower-skilled players, or higher-skilled players willing to self-impose restrictions upon themselves in order to achieve a desired level of difficulty.

name: Disney Speedstorm
detailed_description: JOIN OUR DISCORD COMMUNITY [/url] About the Game Drift into the ultimate hero-based combat racing game, set on high-speed circuits inspired by Disney and Pixar worlds. Master each character’s unique skills on the racetrack and claim victory in this thrilling arcade racing experience from the creators of the Asphalt series! DISNEY & PIXAR GO FULL BATTLE RACING An incredible cast of characters including Mulan, Mickey Mouse, Sulley, Baloo, Captain Jack Sparrow, the Beast and more are suited and revving up for racing combat. Upgrade each racer’s stats and make the most of their unique skills that can impact the outcome of a single race and dramatically change the way you play the game! ARCADE RACING REDEFINED Anyone can pick up and play Disney Speedstorm, but mastering skills and techniques like timing your nitro boosts, precisely drifting around corners, and adapting to dynamic track environments are crucial to dominating each race. RACING TOGETHER HAS NEVER BEEN EASIER Pick your Racer and speed through action-packed tracks solo, or challenge friends in local and online multiplayer modes. You can even face off with players from around the globe to become an online legend. DISNEY & PIXAR INSPIRED RACETRACKS Start your engine in environments inspired by some of your favorite Disney and Pixar films. From the docks of Pirates of the Caribbean’s Kraken Port to the wilds of The Jungle Book’s Jungle Ruins or the Scare Floor from Monsters, Inc., you can experience these worlds from a fresh, exciting perspective geared specifically for racing! CUSTOMIZE TO YOUR OWN STYLE Choose your favorite racer’s suit, a flashy kart livery, and show off stylish wheels and wings -- all of this and more is possible with the extensive customization features in the game! NEW CONTENT RACING YOUR WAY The action never slows down thanks to fresh seasonal content always around the corner. New Disney and Pixar Racers will be added regularly, bringing special skills for you to master (or overcome), and unique tracks will be created often, to pump fresh strategy into the mix. Support Crew characters, environments, customization options, and collectibles will also drop in regularly, so there’s always more to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember getting into the playtest and then noping out I think before my first race. I admit now that I struggle to recall why I did. It might have been the interface.However, I was listening to the MTTG podcast for the first time in 7 years and heard one of the guys raving about this game and thought "Huh? What did I miss?" and that was enough for me to go back and give it a fair shot. That and hearing that this season (season 9, concluding yesterday or today I think, whoa... the playtest couldn't have been that long ago... could it?) was Pirates of the Caribbean theme which is my favorite Disney series.It's a live-service game, nothing changes that, but at its core, it is a really good racing game. BUT it is still a live-service game.In 20 hours of gametime I have managed to unlock 12 of the 69 current racers and unlock 12 of the 24 achievements. I have only spent $10 on the game for the golden pass? (season pass? I can't keep track of the names. The pass for the Pirates of the Caribbean season) because I had already unlocked all 50 tiers so it gave me all of the locked rewards in one fell swoop. That allowed me to unlock 3 of my 12 characters right after.The single-player racing is fun, the multiplayer racing is fun with low queue times (yay cross-platform! Even Mobile getting in there!). As I saw in another review, Disgust and Anger need voice actors. I would love to use them but they feel lifeless rn so I am not pursuing unlocking them. Barbossa's special could use a nerf although at higher MR many more racers are skillful at dodging it.One thing I REALLY appreciate in particular, it might just be a me thing, is the uniformity in racing suits and karts between all characters. Growing up playing primarily sports games I would get slightly irritated that anytime custom teams/characters come into play, people wanted to go with something that would take away the continuity of the league/teams/participants. Yeah they are free to do so, I learned to get over it, but with that being said, the fact that all racing suits and karts look like they have a set standard they all have to follow, I enjoy that :)OH, also, the music for many tracks are remixed versions of recognizable songs from Disney movies and I LOVE THEM!This game makes me feel like a competent racer in that I reasonably have a shot to finish inside the top 3 of every race but am not guaranteed it. A little too often someone runs away with 1st place by >10 seconds.After playing a bit you unlock local split-screen races to which my kids love racing against each other and bots. That is part of my fuel to keep unlocking whatever characters I can.I'm thinking I'll go for all the achievements since it's not that far away, I'll enjoy whatever season passes that come out as I am a Disney fan. If some of my friends pick it up I could see myself playing more.Remember, it IS a live-service game. But the racing is great and if you love Disney, you'll enjoy the diversity of characters they've added. Not sure if I'll spend any more on any season passes, I don't regret the money I put into it.If you enjoy racing/kart games or Disney, I suggest you check it out. It's free, and I think there is enough free content there to enjoy for a bit. When it comes to unlocking characters, you need 10 shards to unlock one and some events allow you to get all/close to unlocking them so it can get annoying but you just need to concentrate your efforts. Again, it is a LIVE-SERVICE GAME, BUT...There is a lot of fun to be had...Enjoy...Or don't... it's free! :)

_childDocuments_.review: A Kart Racer feels like one of the easiest games to monetize via cosmetics alone. There could have been stickers, kart bodies, trails, boost effects and character skins. Instead they decided to muddy it up with a super convoluted character progression system where you need 20 toilet seats, 5 screws and 10 12-sided die to upgrade Goofy's top speed by 15 points. Unfortunate because the actual core game is incredibly fun. The driving feels great, I love the addition of a really big jump to traverse the tracks, and giving every character a unique kit + character specific specials makes races feel chaotic in all the right ways. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT: GameLoft's gonna GameLoft. This was already a negative review, but this game makes me whish I could give it more than one thumbs down.I didn't think the monetization could be much more greedy and devious when I wrote the original review, but ,wow, I really, really underestimated GameLoft in that regard.It is hard to explain just how incredibly vile this game has turned out to be:STAY FAR, FAR AWAY! And don't let your kids play this, it's disguting.Original Review:"Oh, cute, a Disney Kart Racer, my kids will love this". That's what the thought process was, when I picked up the cheapest Founder's Pack on the Xbox. I didn't fully realize, how much of an 18+ title this was - I wouldn't let my kids near this, it's far too predatory.Luckily, purchases and progression are cross-platform, so I could resume playing it on my Steam Deck - where the game works and plays absolutely flawlessly.There isn't much to say that hasn't already been written: At its core it's a wonderful kart racer with a great variety of tracks, racers, power ups and a shockingly good sense of speed and control. It also looks good and runs well, easily exceeding 140fps even on mid-range hardware. At a different place in time, this would have been an instant classic like Mario Kart. Alas, we don't live in that time anymore:It's covered in the most ridiculous, over-the-top, monetization that I have ever seen outside mobile gaming. The variety of in-game currencies and various gambling loot crates is so mind-boggling, it borders on self-parody. And, nope, the monetization mostly isn't about just cosmetics - in fact, what little cosmetic customization there is, feels like more of an afterthought with little variety - this is a full-blown pay-to-win, pay-to-progress title. And prices are absurdly ridiculous. And every week, the devs find new ways to make progression even worse, nerfing the few remaining ways to earn free currency and items along the way.I honestly have no idea how this is even playable without paying for it: even with the founder's pack that gave me a couple of Gold Passes, racers, premium currencies and a huge head start, progression is glacial and walls are hit constantly.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be keeping my old review up for transparency reasons, feel free to give that a read if you want some of the good things about this game, but I'll be outlining the problems in the newly revealed 7th season, that being the Wreck it Ralph season.If you want to give the changes a read, the link is here, but for those that don't ill give a quick rundown.As of the start of Season 7, the season pass will be split into two halves, both having 50 levels during a singular month, and those levels will have their xp requirements halved. Essentially meaning the new seasons will have 100 tiers of rewards if you take part in both.The issue arises though that each half of the season will be priced at $9.99 or equivalent. Meaning the pass will now be twice the cost. On top of this, the option to purchase the pass with premium currency, either bought or earned, has been removed. You now must pay the $19.98 to get both halves of the pass. Once the first half of the pass has expired, you can no longer get the seasonal character within that half of the season unless you pay outright for them in the shop. You can also no longer go back to the first half of the seasonal circuit to complete those races for rewards.This change is, honestly, baffling to me. According to the communication this was done so that players could easily hit level 50 during seasons as a good majority of players wouldn't. However, the way they have done this, they've made the same amount of work for players, but have now added a month-long timegate for each half of the season, while also increasing the cost and preventing players from spending earned currency on passes.During the span of Season 6 I continued to give the game the benefit of the doubt and thought that maybe the changes being made in terms of the MTX would end up getting us more content for the game itself. This has not happened, we're getting the same content for twice the price, with added timegates and a requirement to pay in cash.I cannot recommend the game in its current state, and as much as I love the gameplay and theme, the micro-transactions are slowly strangling the game of any joy I've had for it. If you have a lot of funds to spend, you might still enjoy the game for what it is, but for those that have tight wallets or are just conscious about how you spend your money, you're going to have a pretty poor experience, at least right out the gate.I'll still play it on occasion, but this game is no longer going to be pulling from my wallet.Alright, I'm gonna get one thing straight before I start reviewing this game. It's dev/publisher is Gameloft, a company known for MTX, so going into this I knew what I was getting into, and I told myself I'd not fall for any of the bull that they'd throw at me. My current total playtime in terms of actually racing is at around 30 hours, 600 total wins, with 17 racers owned. (As of December 22nd, this has gone up to 46 total hours racing, 1117 wins, and 25 racers owned. As I state later, the events in this game are a great way to get characters, and this should show it.) I've not put a single cent into the game, and with the rewards that the game has been giving me for both events and ranked, I've been able to unlock some good racers, and even been able to get the season pass just from in-game rewards which helped me get even further in terms of leveling characters. 9 out of my 17 racers are above level 20, and 2 of them have been 3-star'd. That's the limiting factor in this game, getting character shards outside of events/seasonal track/seasonal circuits is like pulling teeth, but there's something even harder to get around. The base upgrading materials in this game are very, very limited. Maybe this is just because I went around trying to level every character I had right off the bat, but getting a racer to level 15 is a struggle for me because I continuously run out of the base leveling component. You can earn these daily, from a daily event, but you only get enough to level around once per day if your character is at levels 7-15. Now, how do these things affect ranked? Well, you cannot lose ranked points until you get to Emerald league, which is a good ways in, and by the time you get there you should have a character at least at level 25. Anything above emerald I cant comment on so if it ends up being a P2W grindfest then sure, that's an issue, but before you get there you won't really run into people that are just straight up paying real cash to get to first faster. (This is also being addressed in the November 2nd patch, where you will be matched with people of your level and not someone like 20 levels higher, yet to see if this actually fixes this problem so we'll see.) Outside of ranked, you have Regulated, which sets everyone's characters to level 30. You've also got a rotation of free racers so if there's someone you want to try, there you go. Private Races unlock all racers, and you can race at level 15, 30, 45, and 50? (I think, I've only ever raced with friends at 30s) so playing this game with friends is great, really accessible and Im glad they didn't paywall racers here. There's also local 1-4 player races as well, same as Private races, everything is unlocked. Ranked early on now feels a lot more coherent. You'll be paired up with people of your level 90% of the time, there are still sadly some fringe cases where you wont, but skill level seems to be a factor here too. Genuinely an improvement. The Seasonal content in this game is nuts, genuinely. Normally I hate games that do content like this, but what speedstorm does is something I enjoy a ton. There's seasonal racing circuits that give you rewards, and give you seasonal track progress based on objectives. They open up in wings every week, which gives me some downtime which is nice, I can knock out the races in a day then spend the rest of my week doing other things, its not a "you need to play this every single day" game unless you really want it to be. You also don't need the season pass to do the seasonal circuit races. The issue I  have with these races is that sometimes they require certain racers from a series or a type, and you will run into optional races that you will need a character you dont have yet, these paths are optional however, and aren't needed to get to the next racing circuit, you're just gonna miss some rewards until you get those racers and go back to do them.(Chapter 5 of the Aladdin season was terrible with this, where all the optional paths required racers from The Jungle Book, Beauty and the Beast, Mulon, and Hercules. I only was able to get the first two done because I got lucky with the daily boxes and the Gaston event. The other two you end up getting pretty early so they were fine.)The music, tracks, gameplay, all of that is great. It's Disney after all, music seems to be one of their main strengths, I've yet to hear a track's ost that I've disliked. The MTX is pretty predatory, and the discounts listed in the shop are all fake, games need to stop doing this, just ignore the shop and get your free stuff, don't give in.The game is fun, the shop is bad, ranked is meh, but regulated is great, solo content is great too and the events are pretty generous if you're a good racer. It's free, try it out, get to collection level 3 (when the tutorial is done/you've got the basics down), if it isn't your cup of tea, then the only thing it's cost you is your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the concept of the game, but my positive review ends there. If you enjoy racing/kart games and Disney, you'll likely enjoy playing it... at least initially. However, a major and glaring issue arises when your progression comes to a halt due to everything being locked behind a paywall. It feels like a cash grab. While the game had good potential, I don't foresee Gameloft addressing this problem anytime soon, given their notorious reputation for structuring games in this manner.You'll find yourself unable to fully participate in events, as some races require racers you either don't possess or aren't at a high enough level to use. Acquiring the necessary racer shards and/or tokens typically entails purchasing them. Ranked play is entirely pay-to-win (P2W), with unbalanced matchmaking resulting in lower-level racers being pitted against much higher-level opponents. Expect to lose unless you've invested money to boost your racer's level.The game lacks any means of grinding to earn currency, and it's evident that this is an intentional design choice, as the free options for earning currency are extremely limited. If you can't afford to invest in the game, you'll find yourself at a severe disadvantage, unable to fully participate. Consequently, I cannot in good conscience recommend this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: A free-to-play kart racer with tight controls, a solid soundtrack, and a nice variety of racers and tracks. Playing through the seasonal content is fun, and daily and weekly events keep you more than busy. There could be more features for the online aspect, and the ranked mode becomes extremely grindy. Speaking as a game's founder, I have had no trouble unlocking every racer; however, new players will need to wait for specific character events to come around or spend money (which I don't suggest, unless you really want a specific racer). There is a fair amount of FOMO of keeping up with all of the the events and ranked mode leaderboard; however, that can all be completely ignored by playing the Private Track and Local Freeplay modes. This is something that is often ignored in user reviews, but if all you're interested in is having fun racing with your friends, you can do so while having access to every racer. There is plenty to enjoy here without spending a dime.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an racing game similar to Sonic & SEGA All-Stars Racing and F1 Race Stars(RIP), etc.Pros:-Fast matchmaking. You will be seeing people from other platforms like consoles and mobile devices, sometimes I get connection warning but I did not notice the lag. I got disconnected during a race 1-2 times but that's pretty rare.-Fast loading times.-Nice tracks and shortcuts and techniques to discover.-Various frame rate options.-You can change steering sensitivity.-Supports private games.-Supports local splitscreen gameplay.-You can earn premium currencies in various ways by playing the game.Neutral-As a free player, getting enough resources to level up a character can be frustrating. For the first 10-15 hours you can probably have fun playing it casually, but after you hit the limit it's pretty demotivating to continue to play.Cons:-You cannot customize your key bindings or controller.-Daily box has a countdown timer of 24 hours after claiming instead of using server time to reset.-Ranked multiplayer has some serious issues with the balance which always puts you in a game with several people who have much higher level than you, making it impossible to win and even finishing in top 3 can be quite difficult in this case, I also feel that some characters have overpowered abilities and some feel absolutely useless.-There is another multiplayer mode called 'Regulated Multiplayer' which forces everyone to play with the same level and you also get to try some new characters that you haven't unlocked yet. However, you don't get much reward in this mode, you can fill up the meter pretty quick and afterwards you won't be getting anything new until the server reset which would take several days.

_childDocuments_.review: To start, the music is on point! Amazing remixes on fun classics!If you are wanting a racer game that's a neat blend between Mario Kart and Crash Team Racing, this is a great game to pick up. The core game play is solid and has a lot of potential and has had me pretty addicted. The biggest drawback has been the amounts of currency and micro transactions but optional. However, they have tried to mitigate the difficulty of getting new characters by giving "character shards" (10 required to unlock character) away through the Starter Circuit, current Season, Battle Pass, Daily Loot Box roll, and having Limited events (i.e. Figment event). One neat feature is local play (couch play) has all the racers unlocked regardless if you have them unlocked on your account. Ranked and Regulated multiplayer can also be enjoyed with a party of 3 that you can queue into races together--this is a big plus for me as I want to be able to play with friends and family that own the game.I look forward to seeing how the game will evolve and future seasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is fine but lots of loot boxes, and unlocking racers keep a lot of content out of reach.  if you play local you do get some "guest racers" to try out, but this game is definitely a lottery on what you unlock. _childDocuments_.review: Game requires a lot of singleplayer grinding, and the singleplayer sucks.  The ai is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, they will stay with you no matter what the level no matter what you skill until the end of the last lap and just let you win.  Heavy manipulation of every race to make it 'seem' like you barely won.  tryharding and putting along within the lines will get the same result.  Very unsatisfying. If it changes, I'll change my review.update: as long as you avoid any single player levels that you aren't at or above the manipulation isn't too frustrating, it just makes the race way too easy as the ai will just forget how to drive in the last 30% of the race.  Kinda boring but, you can get through your single player missions pretty quick.Multiplayer is a hot mess as your racer's level will make a large amount of difference on the race track.  Regulated multiplayer is pretty fun, but you will unlock all the rewards for the week in about 30-45 minutes.  There are 'time trials' where you are trying to beat other players times... they aren't regulated and they take place with random item drops and ai players.  Way too much rng for a 'time trial'. You can get a universal box and a free daily box every day with very little grinding, but most of what you will get is 'crew shards' for racers you don't even own, so that feels mildly frustrating at that stage.  The pay 2 win in this game would honestly make battlefront 2 devs blush.  It is very aggressive.  You could spend quite a bit in this game and feel like you didn't get very much, and if you're f2p don't expect to grind things out, after a couple hours of playing expect to have to wait a week for more events to unlock before you can continue the grind.I'm slowly warming up to this game, but it still has too many problems for me to be able to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun, it's free to play, good mechanics, good music to go in the tracks that were also decent and have several variants of a course to change things up a some each race.Everything was going good and was fun..... until the Pay To Win wall hit:"Increase Character Star Level To Level Character Further".This game features a Gacha mechanic, which is done in a bit of a scummy way mind you. Instead of straight up getting characters, you get character shards. It takes a different amount of shards based on if you have the character, and if you do it's increased based on their current star level to increase them to the next star level. Yes characters rotate in and out of the shop, but you only have so much to spend at a time. In order to actually progress your characters you need them to have star levels so you can level them higher (max level for a 1 star character is 15 btw).This straight up gates you out of ranked because a character's level also influences that character's racing stats. It's night and day between a level 15 and a level 30+ character. The level 15 you can finish a map in around 1:15-ish depending on skill level. But a level 30+ can finish that same race while racing the same way in under 1 minute.Do I like the game? Yes. But I cannot recommend it to anyone. I refuse to spend money on this game just for ranked, I'd rather spend it on a pizza because pizza is good. It's one thing if you got characters without the shard system, but because of the shard system it takes way to long to get extra copies of characters to increase your star levels to anything meaningful just for ranked play.If you play this game, play it for the single player or the casual races where all of the characters are forced to be level 30 at 2 star, it's the better PvP experience. But do not spend money for the pay to win mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate myself for enjoying this game.The game play itself is very fun. Karts handle great, most powers are fun. The grind is a fun one, as I'm someone who enjoys games you have to grind.Where this game goes off course is the pricing of things, way overpriced on everything. (yes I get we can't spend real money yet, but judging by Dreamlight's pricing and the pricing of items in the shop with Premium currency, it's going to be awful)It's a shame, Gameloft makes really fun games, and I don't know if it's their greed or Disney's greed, but just the overall greed from their games brings them down. Also, the ranked multiplayer could be a lot of fun if A) it had players and B) it was fair. Being a level 15 and racing against level 33s and 34s is not fun, fair, or even remotely balanced. Been like this since Day 1.Overall, I do enjoy the game and will probably continue to play when better games aren't out. But between broken multiplayer, a near dead player base, and a developer that treats it's few players like wallets full of cash, I cannot give this game a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had fun with the gameplay. It's pretty decent. Track designs are generally pretty cool. I like the concept of roles for the characters providing different playstyles. I don't recommend it on the basis that the progression system is extremely slow and grindy, unless you spend a hefty amount of money, which is absolutely not worth it. Upgrade coins, which are earned to level up characters, are particularly way too hard to come by, IMO. The battlepass career mode also likes to require characters and levels for certain optional events that you do not get through the pass directly, and are very unlikely to meet such requirements if you're newer to the game, unless again, you spend a hefty amount of money, which is a major bummer.Overall, a potentially good kart racing game that is greatly ruined by grindy progression systems and greedy business practices.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the game for a good 30+ hours on the Steam Deck and PS5. Whilst I enjoyed it at first, it is starting to feel more and more like a purchased free to play game.My issues with the game:1. Monsters Inc season pass - currently up to the 2nd last chapter and races can be close or you can lose when 10+ levels above the recommended level.2. Racing can feel like 50cc or 100cc Mario Kart in terms of the speed.3. There are times where it feels like the game lets you win races (earlier chapters in the season pass).4. You have the ‘Universal Box’ which is basically a loot box for getting character and crew shards (pieces to unlock them/upgrade their levels). You can open 20 boxes in a row and barely get any character shards, especially for the characters you need.5. The game requires you to grind in order to earn materials to upgrade character levels, then once you reach certain levels (15, 30 etc) you need shards to upgrade the characters star level in order to continue levelling up (there are 5 star levels).6. There are only a limited number of tracks at the moment (they do have different variations of each track), this isn’t ideal with the amount of grinding required.7. Being unable to do races in the season pass because you don’t have a character from a certain franchise or of a high enough level is the worst. The developers want you to have FOMO so you go nuts with the universal boxes or spend premium currency on offers such as upgrading a characters star level.

_childDocuments_.review: If developers are reading the comments and ensuring the community then these are my thoughts on the game: While fast paced action is always good, the rubber band AI is too tight for comfort. The moment you have an instant lead and/or maybe some extra time ahead of you, the AI somehow snaps a little TOO quickly. Thus creating this sense of "no hiccups" or it'll cost you. Character models are decent for now, but do need a polish over time. For Steam Users, a windowed mode should be added as having the game on a single monitor is a burden for some players/streamers of the game. A few in game bugs are also noted, such as a limited event where a AI racer somehow marked at 0:00:00 during one game and I thought otherwise in negativity. Overall though, music is AMAZING! Tracks are fun and somewhat diverse but many aspects of the track remain, creating a sense of "I've been here before" so it doesnt feel TOO new. 8/10 for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Speedstorm

_childDocuments_.review: Despite all the cryout about microtransactions and whatnot, if you want a fun, casual kart racing experience with the nowadays trending "collector" twist, give this game a try. It's free after all! Also it runs pretty well on average PCs, the graphics are nice, the music is blood pumping (as you would expect from a racing game), the gameplay is solid and I haven't encountered bugs either so far.EDIT: So after a playing for some time, I just realized that the game is still fun as long as you avoid multiplayer. It's full of cheaters... There's always one guy who somehow magically blows up the entire lineup 1 seconds after the match starts, than there are the people who somehow appear to be immune to all skills (yep, without the green shield!), there's the Micky mouse who constantly has his special ability up during the whole match... and the list goes on and on. Oh, and don't forget the times when you reach the finish line with 3 people right behind you and somehow you still end up as 8th.

If you aren't a fan of Disney that could be a negative, but the game would still be awesome regardless.I highly recommend Speedstorm if you like kart racers, and if you don't this one could change your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not just a game. It's a marathon....Unless you give in to microtransactions, at which point it's actually the developers that won the game against you.If you plan to stay F2P, you should know that progress will be very slow. There is no way to continuously grind to unlock and level up any racer in this game without hitting a progression wall. At some point maybe ~20 hours in, further progression involves waiting for a new season chapters and daily/weekly events.This appears to be intentional, as the developers want you to spend money to progress at seemingly every step of your journey.If you can afford it, you might get a lot more value by buying season passes. _childDocuments_.review: This racer is greedy and awful. The worst aspect of this game is that you will sometimes race nothing but bots (even while in a party) which will result in NONE of you getting any reward points. Speaking of bots, multiplayer will rarely add them, so you're often facing off against 3 or 4 other people instead of 7. This game is pay to win like many other freemium games. It forces you to play as characters you have no interest in, wasting valuable resources and time in the process. The first unlocked mode is multiplayer ranked which is filled with whales that have crew members and boosted stats, so count on losing 99% of the time to people who play this game a LOT more than you do. Regulated multiplayer is ok, but the rewards aren't plentiful, they are limited to certain characters items per week, and reaching a decent collection level basically requires that you give them money.Edit: The power-ups are EXTREMELY unbalanced and are distributed very poorly. Certain characters have MUCH better powers than others (nerf Stitch). You'll be in last place CONSTANTLY getting stupid items you don't need like the reverse arrow and flame when you should get the "teleport forward in the race" clock item which rarely shows up. If someone is in first and pulls slightly ahead, they are gone for the rest of the race. The end. No blue-shell, no stars or lightning bolts for players in last. No red shell. If you fall behind you have to hope the game gives you the clock item or you're stuck behind forever. There is no fairness. Only whales and bad development choices.I don't know why people can't simply release finished games. Even when this game finally becomes free, it's going to be dead. _childDocuments_.review: *Updated review*While I do like the game, I fully understand people's issues with it. The game has good mechanics and is very responsive, it's fun to play. All of the characters have a special ability unique to them and the 4 different classes means there are multiple ways to play depending on what you prefer.Now that I'm 85 hours into the game as opposed to around 20 when I originally wrote my review, my views have changed slightly.Season resets are worse than I anticipated. When you play ranked online races, you receive rewards for the particular character you're playing as when you level up. When the season resets, your level goes down, but your rewards do not reset, meaning you have to play a bunch of races for no reward just to get back to where you were so you can continue to receive much needed rewards. Huge time waster.I've also hit a bit of a brick wall, because I have a handful of characters up to level 35, but can't upgrade them any further because the items needed to level up are non-existent. I believe you can get a few of them if you get really high in the online ranks, but getting that far is extremely difficult. I also can't do a bunch of races in the Chapters section without grinding 8 hours a day because there are a lot of characters that I have but aren't high enough level, or I just haven't unlocked. The pay to win style is much stronger at this point.I don't know how much I'll play in the future, this might be the end. Whether you have money to spend or not, this game is fun for a limited time. If you're aware that you will eventually plateau without grinding or paying and just want to play a fun game for a while, then go for it, but if you're looking for a long-time staple, this ain't it.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, here we go. This game is such a fun game! Yes, it has bugs, glitches, and the way to level up makes it seem like a mobile game instead of an actual PC/console game. I've been playing this game and streaming it for a while now, and quite frankly, I am loving it! I am currently Plat with Mike, since he is a broken character, and I am trying to hit higher levels with all the other racers, so to me that gives me a reason to keep playing this game. Overall the mechanics are very easy to learn, and easy to master so there isn't a huge learning curve.Now, the mobile part of this game. I absolutely despise it! I get what they are trying to do, but come ON! Only getting 1 shard per universal box that you open and making it cost 10k SEASON TOKENS?!?!? Like that right there is a bunch of nonsense! For you to unlock racers, or crew members you need their shards. You can get shards by either, Playing the events, playing the story, or of course by spending your tokens in the shop! It kind of makes the game feel like it is "Pay 2 win," and quite frankly that is NOT okay.If they want us to grind out the game that way we can collect the shards, they should at least add shards to the "Golden Pass" and make everything cosmetic as well! It is dumb that to level up characters you need to collect racing flags, you need to collect trinkets just to level them up! What if we just ditch that, and the characters level up with EXP instead of trinkets? That would make the game better and more enjoyable for others as well. There is so much more to say about this game, but honestly I want everyone to play this game and judge it for yourself. I've been enjoying this game, even though I do rage at this game due to the glitches/bugs, but people are giving it a 5 out of 10 just because they suck at the game, and because they aren't getting paid the right amount of money to review the game? This game honestly deserves at LEAST in its current state a 7 out of 10 at the moment, once they start adding more racers, which I am hoping for a Tron collection, or possibly a Nightmare Before Christmas collection for a Halloween event which would be awesome, this game can and will flourish as long as the devs ACTUALLY pay attention to the CONSUMER and NOT the INVESTORS! We get it, they want to make their money back and MORE, BUT PLEASE LISTEN TO US! WE ARE THE GAMERS AND WE ARE THE ONES THAT ARE GOING TO SPEND MONEY ON THIS GAME! I promise you, that if you take out the trinkets to level up, and just replace it with EXP by doing the limited events, the "story," and ranked races, and possibly give double EXP to golden pass owners, and making amazing cosmetic items, the game will be a HUGE HIT!

_childDocuments_.review: + Ultrawide Support                                                                                                                                                    + Steamdeck Support                                                                                                                                             + Multiple options in the graphics settings                                                                                                              I'm a big fan of kart/arcade racers so Speedstorm instantly got my attention. I also love Gameloft's other racing series. "Asphalt", and have been playing Asphalt 9 consistently since it's release (on Switch, Xbox, and Steam), so that was another plus.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              *   Anyone familiar with Asphalt 9 will recognize the Speedstorm's menu and game mode setup. There is a tutorial mode that has a few cups (each cup has several races) that introduce players to different racers/racer classes(you can't select the racer during this mode) and the game's mechanics. Then there is a robust single player campaign in which you are free to select any of the racers you own. There are daily and weekly events where you can earn extra prizes. There is also multiplayer of course, both local and online. I have not played much of the multiplayer races so I can't really give input on it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         *  Each racer can be leveled up(causing stat increases) using upgrade parts won or purchased by in-game currency or real money.  There are also unlockable crew members (similar to the Nickelodeon kart games) that add different bonuses. Also, each racer has a special skill unique to them (obtained from item boxes on the tracks), and then there are a few different items acquired during races that are the same for all (such as a shield, a boomerang, etc).  These can either be activated immediately, or the player can hold the button down for a couple of seconds to get a charged version.                                                                                          *  I think the graphics and art design are excellent (whether it's on my rtx 3080/4K screen, my rtx 3070ti/1440p laptop, or my steam deck) and the frame rate is smooth and stable. The music is good, but not my favorite among kart racers (Modnation Racers wears that crown for me).  The controls for racing, jumping, and drifting are very tight.                                                                                                                              -- The only major complaint I have is that the driving speed feels to slow for me.  Compared to all of the other kart games I play (Crash Team Racing, the Sonic-Allstars series, Modnation Racers, the Nickelodean Kart series, Mario Kart, and Chocobo Racing), the sense of speed is the slowest. And then, compared to Gameloft's ultra-fast Asphalt 9 (I know it's not a kart game),  it's like comparing a snail to a cheetah. Even boosting barely increases speed. On local play, you can adjust the speed from three choices, and only the highest speed option feels somewhat fast. On all of the other modes, I have not seen a way to increase velocity.  I suppose choosing a higher difficulty slightly increases speed, but if so, it is not very noticeable to me.  I'm hoping that Gameloft will bump up the speed a little by the time early access is over.                                                                                                                                                                                                             * Aside from the speed being slower than I prefer, I do not regret spending money to be able to play Disney Speedstorm early.  I still am having a lot of fun playling it and I sincerely hope that the game is successuful and supported for a long time...and PLEASE increase the speed Gameloft! Lol

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great Kart racer. If you like Kart games, check it out. If you don't want to pay for anything though just wait till the end of the year/Q1 of 2024 when I believe it's scheduled to release as F2P. Now let me address some MTX issues:1) You cannot refund the gameYou're paying for cosmetics and to be able to play it early. As the game will launch free2play you're not exactly buying a copy of the game but just cosmetics and the EA. And per guidelines there are no refunds for DLC content. 2) In-game currenciesYou cannot purchase currencies in game, at least currently. I can't speak for when the game launches but at the moment you have to earn the currency by playing. _childDocuments_.review: UPDATE #2:Total Garbage Fire Of A GameTerrible management, backwards Discord moderation, delayed updates, poor communication, catering to whales only, abusive mechanics.Run far away, for your own good.You've been warned. Take care.----------------------------------UPDATE: Recent changes made me recommend against picking this game up as a new player, just coming into the game now.The catch up mechanics are close to non-existent at this point. The ability to play anybody in local freeplay was also removed; this is a huge hit to being able to avoid the grind.Review edited to fit the changes. It's sad but c'est la vie.----------------------------------*snip*You can play with friends for fun – no progression gained here though. Plus, you can only play as some racers. The rest need to be unlocked through a hefty grind.That's disappointing. You can play customs with less of a grind, and you can play regulated MP online without much of a grind as well. You'll still need to unlock racer for these modes, just not upgrade them. It's still a hefty grind for legacy (non-recent) racers because you can only unlock those through lootboxes and events if the game is kind enough to provide them.Other than that, the bigger, main grind is for the standard ranked mode where you earn better rewards than in regulated, or the singleplayer/weekly/daily events. And I guess for any skins you'd want but those are recolors so largely ignorable in my case.Other than that, they lend you 4 guest racers that rotate weekly, along with tiny rewards in regulated MP (not ranked). It takes about 1-3 hours a week to max out these regulated MP rewards. Playing friendlies in custom lobbies is still completely free, but several racers need to be unlocked.Tl;dr:"Bottom line, I'm pleasantly surpised and now I don't think the game deserves all the bashing it's been getting. I stand corrected for now. I misjudged Speedstorm."^^^ That's what I said before but now I would recommend against anybody picking this up as a new player, right now. Maybe that changes with updates. If so, I'll update this review.They're still making improvements for seasoned players but the new player experience has been nerfed with the changes to local freeplay.It's a shame because there's a really fun racer here. It is just buried under a thick and shady monetization and meta progression system. If you're willing to deal with that, you'll be able to have fun but it's completely understandable if you aren't.A big personal gripe of mine with the game is how little player agency and actual skill matters. If you've the recommended racers at the recommended level, PvE events are mostly trivial to beat. Even leaderboards events are pretty easy. But if you don't have the stats – which are just a matter of trivial grind to get – tasks are going to be really tough to impossible to complete, even with really good racing and skills. Very rarely will it be your skill that makes the difference. When that happens the game truly shines, but it's marred by the times when that doesn't happen.

_childDocuments_.review: First, let's talk about the positives.Gameplay is great. Short learning curve for basic mechanics (driving, items, etc.), and races are very exciting. I'm having fun in every single one. I've been playing single-player for my first couple of hours, but the bots are competitive, so you won't be disappointed if you want higher difficulty. There's plenty of modes, whether you want to play single-player or online. You start with a "starter circuit" that you need to progress on in order to unlock the other modes. If you want to race as Mickey, Donald or Goofy, you're in luck because you unlock those characters within the first hour or so.Graphics and the overall look/feel of the game is good. Soundtrack lowkey slaps (remixes of classic Disney songs in electronic/club style) However the cars look extremely generic. Would have loved it if each of the characters drove in their own themed cars like Mario Kart but the liveries for the cars fit the characters well. Another thing I want to say is how blown away I was when they announced Figment as a character. As a fan of the Disney Parks and the lore/history surrounding the character, I can appreciate him coming into the limelight more. And if Figment was the first Parks related character that the devs announced (he IS in the Walt Disney World collection), I can bet that they're going to add more as the seasons come and go. (Hell, we even got our first Dreamfinder reference in YEARS, even if he's only a crew member. And I can appreciate seeing Orange Bird and Sonny Eclipse as well. Huge surprises.) The Figment announcement is what compelled me to buy the game in the first place.Which brings me to the negatives; of which there are a few:The amount of grinding one will have to do in order to obtain the characters/cosmetics/upgrades and whatnot will be long as hell. This is because this game is designed like a typical mobile/gatcha game. The amount of microtransactions here are overwhelming. No game should have FOUR in-game currencies. It will take me a LONG time to unlock Figment because he is the rarest character in the game, and the whole character shards thing being pegged to the rarity level makes it even worse. You also can't unlock the loot box that these shards are in unless you have 10,000 "season coins" that can mostly only be unlocked if you have the season/battle pass. (I will say that the standard founders pack gives you two credits towards your first two passes, but after that, it's money out of your pocket.) There's also no excuse for early access and the standard founders pack to be worth $30. Most people can wait until the game goes free-to-play later this year. It just isn't worth it for most people just to be able to unlock special skins and be a couple steps ahead of everyone else. I have heard that people aren't receiving refunds on their editions since it is technically DLC and cannot be returned. Really scummy thing to do. I also think the whole upgrading/crew experience is more complicated than it needs to be. I think many people will find it overwhelming. This also kinda plays into the microtransactions; if you want your car to go faster, drift better, etc. then you either grind for a long time or pay your way up.Overall, for the average person, I would definitely wait until this goes free-to-play if you want to check this out. Early access isn't worth it, at least for me. But everyone is different. If you really like Disney characters and love kart racing, and simply can't wait a few months, then go ahead and get it. It really is a fun kart racer, but the obvious cash-grab elements and convoluted progression system stick out like a sore thumb. I hope Gamestop and Disney can get their act together on these fronts.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game destroyed by macrotransactions, shifty marketing practices and stingy rewards, that focus on pay to win to get those whales on board.The good: The racing is fun, using unique and normal abilities to spice up the mariokart-esc gameplay as well as introducing different racer types that specialise in 4 different sets of abilities.The bad: The "micro" transactions are abysmal, oh you need to spend about £10 to unlock the special battlepass, well the battle pass doesn't give you any coins in return so suck it up and pay £10 next time as well. The "micro" transactions are also mired in some scummy marketing practices as nearly everything has a high percentage off them. The full value to just unlock a character at level 1 star (out of 5) is around 6000 points or £44.99 of which is for 10 character tokens to unlock them, but they then go oh wait it was 50-85% off, aren't we so generous. They then step it up as the cost to level up a character to 2 star is 8000 points (not including fake %off) of which would cost £56.24 of which is increased to 20 character tokens, that is the price they have put on their characters.More nonsense is there is another level up system under the star system of which is driver level of which requires special resources to upgrade, at first it is plentiful unlocking stuff from the battlepass and seasonal story, but afterwards it dries up making leveling up characters a chore, oh but they have bundles in the store for that... for 350 tokens you can get one driver level up. Keep in mind that the maximum driver levels at a 5 star character is 50 and it has increasing costs.The driver level increases stats for the driver, so acceleration, handling, attack power, top speed. so getting them high is worth it to win multiplayer races that get you paltry rewards for the current character. Now this already bad but you have to do this with every character, so about 37 characters with more on the way. The term pay to win is strong as those who can and want to splash the cash can get their characters so much more powerful than everyone else that they are almost guaranteed to win most races.The single player season races are just as bad, forcing you to use the seasons characters of which they give you, ok cool, but later down the line they show sudden curve balls and tell you, you cannot progress without a certain racer at a certain driver level, so a newbie wouldn't have anyone from that category, so you need to pay for them to even get the reward that might include a character token.Sorry for the rant, i loved the racing mechanics but when everything started going pay or can't play it became unbearable.

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, I think this game has some of the best gameplay of any racing game I've played, including the Mario Kart series. On the other, this game is plagued by the predatory monetization techniques introduced in mobile gaming. Want to race as Mike Wazowski right out the gate? I hope you have $50. But you won't be able to use his special skills. Or level him up. And if you do have the materials to level him up, you're capped at level 15 until you earn 15 more character shards.While you can completely avoid paying any money by sticking to 'local play' (solo or local multiplayer) or 'private track' (online multiplayer) to race as any character on any track, a game like this cannot survive if it doesn't make money. Unfortunately, the only other way to support the game besides buying characters and upgrade materials is to buy racing suits, victory animations, or kart liveries. All of which are mid. Want Mickey to wear his original outfit? No can do. Want a kart that actually has personality? No can do.It's a real shame this game is built upon pay-to-win foundations, because, again, the gameplay is really good. Sure, some characters are more balanced than others, but when everyone is on equal footing, skill takes precedence and any character can win or lose.Another problem? Because of this game's focus on players' wallets, we're getting eight new characters this season, but only a single track to race on. Yes, for every season of six+ characters, we're only getting a single new track. And also yes, there are variations of each track, but once you've gone through a single week of 'Season Tour,' you'll be ready for the next season's track.Finally, this  a mobile game. Literally. While Gameloft claimed they were pivoting to PC/console, and even closed one of their studios for that reason, there is currently a mobile version of this game in Early Access in certain regions, with a full release coming later this year or early 2024. So if you're wondering why so much of this game resembles a mobile game, that's because this was always meant to be one.I really want to believe this game will be around and thriving in a year, and maybe it will be, but in the past week, the active player count has fallen abut 25%, and today was a  in the United States. And that's only on this platform. That said, the current player count beats Early Access, which by the end of Season 3, felt like a ghost town. Next season, not only is Gameloft locking two racers behind their Premium Golden Pass, but Tokens can no longer be used to purchase a Premium Golden Pass. Run as far away from this game as you can.
_childDocuments_.name: Disney Speedstorm

_childDocuments_.review: Having read the reviews, I would just like to set one thing straight: this is NOT P2W.The main content the Season Tour, which is completely Solo content. The Season Tour is completely free and provides the player with many valuable resources for obtaining and improving new characters (universal resources earned can also be used on owned characters).Limited Events are simple challenges providing additional resources.In Ranked Multiplayer you race your best owned character or just any owned character of your choosing. Character Level is NOT matched meaning level 5 characters can go up against level 50 characters. Winning is inconsequential! You get XP toward your character's multiplayer track whether you win or not.Regulated Multiplayer as the name suggests matches character levels and stats for the most skill-based content in the game.As a matter of fact, the ONLY content worth paying for is the Golden Pass. Even then, that's only useful for obtaining additional resources that you can acquire by any other means, and fast-tracking newly released characters.So yeah, all I have to say is that these P2W-whiners clearly haven't been playing the game right. Disclaimer: The only money I have put into this game was for the base Early Access pack which gave me the first Golden Pass.Do I recommend this game?Absolutely, 1000000%, yes. It's a blast and Stitch was the main selling point for me.
