_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good but it's honestly embarrassing to recommend.Pros:* You can play with friends as long as everyone completes the starter circuit.* This entails you have access to all characters at a regulated level and private play which is full fair play.* Soundtrack is amazing. Best i've ever heard for a game besides rocket league*Models need a little work cuz mickey's ears for example are shaped like octogons instead of circles but the * car models are really nice looking.Full Cross-Platform compatibility (even with mobile) which all games like these thrive onCons:* Literally everything else about the game:* Ranked Multiplayer gacha'd to death even after they made an attempt to balance the leveling matchmaking over MPR(Multiplayer Rank) patch. Depending on how high you go you can still encounter maxed out racers regardless of level* The store is overpriced garbage however you look at it. some bundles are worth over $100 when you ignore the "marketed sale" they provide which is just a scummy scheme to make it seem like you're saving prices.* This game is obviously catered to mobile consumers with the way how outrageous the prices are and the problem is that children is what this game's business model will attract and could lead to a lot of mindless spending on the useless pay-to-win gacha system they implemented.* The only little compensation this gacha racer has made was the ranked rewards system which is FINITE. This system is a feature in ranked where every character you race with receives small rewards of in game currency, personal character shards and multiplayer coins (Cosmetic currency) (costs real money) to be rewarded in increments. The problem is the rewards never reset per season and they made SUCH A SELFISH DECISION as to increasing the rewards this patch because they are aware the rewards were literally crumbs of what is required to upgrade a character in an article it stated, "veteran players will not be able to benefit from the aforementioned increase in rewards" meaning if you maxed out your mpr before the ranked system feels like pay to win, you just simply miss out of the extra rewards you desperately need and you get no benefit from the patch. They're insulting their diehard players and basically telling them well. just spend money like everybody else then. A game that treats their most dedicated players badly is not a game. It's just a scummy business model.* The game has a terrible upgrade system which is again is like mobile game. Sad part is the game plays as good as Sonic Team Racing or Mario Kart 8 it's just wasted potential. Upgrades for a character can only be received daily at complete random by limited timed events or weekly but the limited timed events that have been provided for you. You would never catch up to a pay to win player.* Lootboxes to upgrade. How is this not illegal? I thought lootboxes were banned in most countries.* Don't even get me started on the character shard system. The shard system works in a way where you have 3 variants of character: Blue(common) Purple(Epic) and gold(Legendary) Purple and Gold basically are the rarest shards that would have under 1% guarantee in the lootboxes they have for free users to access daily. The issue is that characters all require the same amount of shards to upgrade meaning you can kiss ever maxing a legendary character in your lifetime goodbye without spending money into the game. The daily shop charges shards that they are aware of that one of your characters is close to upgrading with the real money currency almost teasing you in a sense for $10+. There are some characters that have "sales" to getting shards (not the full 10 shards required to unlock the character) for over $10.. and the most i've seen for a character was $30 for 5 legendary shards. WHY. THE. ****. WOULD ANYBODY SPEND THAT MUCH MONEY ON A CHARACTER THEY DON'T EVEN OBTAIN AFTER THE TRANSACTION. WHO THE HELL IS COMING UP WITH THESE IDEAS? I just wanna talk..* Even buying the battlepass is no guarantee to own a 5 star character because the battlepass only provides what looks like an adequate edge above a free to play player but no guarantee of maxing a player even after completing the battlepasses. The pros are: - you can pretty much have a greater chance for owning all the characters for that battlepass which is fair, -however it seems kinda odd that you can't max a character after spending money in the game. - To me, i think it's better than nothing but everyone is not equally fortunate so I find it kinda unfair if you wanted to use those characters you practically paid for in ranked. - You can still play with them but you definitely can't peak in the ranked rewards.* The rewards in this game literally just feel like a reimbursement after investing in the gameBecause game really is lacking a respectable and reasonable upgrade system.* Upgrading characters is complete gacha and you have to get lucky to get a just a shard of a character's upgrade from lootboxes or pay through the teeth for everything you want.* At this point this game might has well should've just been a buy to play and take this entire star, shard upgrade garbage out of the game because I hate seeing games like this and overwatch being killed not for the gameplay being bad but how stupid the micro-transactional management and how unreliable the patches can be. TL:DRIf you wanna play this game casually or like cart racers, it is mechanically good, one of the greatest cart racers you can get for free to date in my opinion.Just don't invest in this money grabbing, Overwatch-like managed for cart racers, game.I'm surprised it's not negatively reviewed because of it at this point.W GameL Management.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I got this game out of curiosity. I've been an avid fan of Disney and kart racers like Mario Kart and the Sonic Racing trilogy, so it immediately peaked my interest. Oh boy, when I started my first race I immediately fell in love. I'm not saying this as a fanboy, but as a gamer in general. The graphics are pretty, the gameplay is fast and heart-pumping, the characters are expressive, the tracks are fun, and the soundtrack slaps so hard that I listen to it when I'm doing other things like driving or drawing. I do have some gripes with the game, though. This game contains loot boxes. I know it will be a free to play game later down the road, but I don't like relying on luck to unlock certain characters, kart parts, or crew members since I payed for the whole game. Thank god you don't have to pay actual money for them. They do, however, offer alternative ways to get certain items through the shop, limited events, the golden pass (Basically this game's version of battle passes), and by completing races in the season tour and starter circuits. But it may take a while depending on what item's you're looking for. Another gripe I have is how some races in season tours require specific characters and levels to even be able to keep up with the computer races. Of course it's supposed to get harder as you progress but again, it may take a long time to even bring your characters up to that level. So you either have to rely on luck with the loot boxes and the shop or spend a while grinding for upgrade parts to level up your characters. All in all, even with the problems I have, it's a lot of fun and gets me pumped every time a race starts. I'm excited to see what the future of the game has in store. (Please add characters from Cars and Wreck it Ralph lol)

There's no way to play this game competitively without handing Disney literally hundreds of dollars, and that's not an exaggeration.  It's pay-to-win in the purest and most evil form.It's so over the top it literally feels like a parody game making fun of modern-day monetization in freemium games.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game-play, Good graphics, Fun racing with friends and random players BUT...Matchmaking can be abused, It's a bit complicated and you should look into it if you want to know more.Time to talk about the money. You can spend a ridiculous amount of money to progress faster by buying character shards to progress star levels, this will increase duration of abilities or size of instants like bombs however it will only make the characters signature ability and a class specific ability get better so your opponents aren't going to have a million powered up items. you can also buy level up items as each character needs XP bottles, a class specific item and an item for that characters collection (e.g; a character from monsters inc will need a scream canister). you can also buy shards for 'crew' perks characters from the collection that didn't make it in as racers, these will give stat increases and you can have up to four on your character (increasing with star level)As for the free to play experience, It's not as bad as people are saying however your progression could be slowed if you don't progress a character available in the free side of the gold pass (battle pass). you should be playing the game for fun anyways but if you want to rank up, I'd suggest playing one character from each class and from separate collections, as I mentioned you'll need class and collection specific items to level up your racers. doing this won't hurt you as much as only playing Mickey mouse racers. a game with slow progression will always feel.. well, slow but like an MMO you won't be maxing out in twenty minutes anyways. If you're looking to get into this game even for a bit, I'd recommend playing a defender, they have invincibility items and two very strong ones can be picked up early on for free. Overall I'd give this game a solid 7/10 with its only downsides truly being the pay to progress faster and matchmaking abuse. I'll recommend this to you if you like Disney characters, Arcade style racing games or just want a bit of fun with some friends

_childDocuments_.review: "Disney Speedstorm" brings the magic of beloved Disney characters to the world of racing games, offering a colorful and entertaining experience for players of all ages. However, while the game captures the essence of Disney's charm, its monetization model may leave some players feeling frustrated and limited in their progression.From the moment you boot up "Disney Speedstorm," you're greeted with vibrant visuals and familiar faces from Disney and Pixar franchises. The racing tracks are beautifully designed, featuring iconic locations from movies such as "Toy Story," "Frozen," and "Cars." Each character comes with their own unique abilities and special moves, adding a layer of strategy to the races as you compete for the top spot.The gameplay itself is simple yet addictive, with responsive controls and a variety of power-ups and obstacles to keep things exciting. Whether you're drifting around corners, dodging obstacles, or unleashing your character's special ability, there's never a dull moment on the track.However, the shine of "Disney Speedstorm" begins to dull when you realize the extent of its monetization tactics. While the game is free to play, it heavily encourages players to spend real money on in-game currency and loot boxes to unlock new characters, upgrade existing ones, and progress through the game faster. This creates a frustrating barrier for players who are unwilling or unable to spend money, as progression becomes slow and grinding becomes a necessity to unlock new content.Furthermore, the game's gacha-style loot box system can feel predatory, as players are never guaranteed to receive the characters or items they want, even after spending real money. This can lead to a sense of disappointment and dissatisfaction, especially for younger players who may not fully understand the concept of microtransactions.In conclusion, while "Disney Speedstorm" offers a fun and engaging racing experience with charming Disney characters, its heavy reliance on microtransactions and loot boxes may deter some players from fully enjoying the game. If you're willing to overlook its monetization model and are simply looking for a casual racing game to enjoy in short bursts, "Disney Speedstorm" may still provide some entertainment. However, if you're expecting a fair and balanced progression system without the need for constant spending, you may want to look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: : Somehow the developers have managed to create the most mechanically polished and fully-featured kart racing game since Mario Kart, easily trading blows with the legendary franchise, if not blowing it out of the water completely. Polished racing feel, a vicious sense of speed, a badass cinematic camera that ebbs and flows with your kart's acrobatics, tons of new mechanics (Burnout-style slams and takedowns replete with slow-mo camera, a boost meter that recharges on drifts/drafting/takedowns, Hero abilities)… mechanically, it is a pitch-perfect game and by far the most innovative and meaningful contribution to the kart-racing genre in nearly a decade. There's still some polish to be done in the balancing department, but this will no doubt be worked out in due time.And that's not all they nailed. The artistic  is . Tons of characters from across the entire Disney pantheon—from beloved favorites like Mulan and Mike Wazowski; to live action heroes like Jack Sparrow and Elizabeth Swann; to animated classics like Belle, Beast, Hercules, Megara, Mowgli and Baloo; to surprising deep-cuts like Figment of DisneyWorld fame. You even get tons of side characters from every franchise, like Celia Mae and Randall. Every character is lovingly animated and voice-acted (by what sounds like the original actors, if not extremely talented soundalikes) and overflowing with personality. And the SOUNDTRACK ABSOLUTELY SLAPS. It's brimming with fantastically mixed and designed traphouse / electroswing remixes of all your favorite Disney classic music, plus plenty you've probably never heard.All of this is tied together by a slick and flashy UI that's beautifully rendered/animated and carries a strong sense of attitude and style.: They took all of this graphical and gameplay  and buried it under a mountain of live-service BS. Racers AND their performance upgrades are locked behind pay-to-skip grinds. There's a confusing smorgasboard of currencies and crafting materials. There's a battle-pass and dozens of time-limited events. It is a GaaS nightmare.:  All characters are fully unlocked and leveled right from the get-go if you play it offline. So the split-screen experience is basically perfect. Get it for that alone. The same can almost be said of the "Regulated Multiplayer" playlist. All characters are fully leveled with all performance upgrades unlocked. The only thing not unlocked is the characters themselves, but it does give you a rolling set of guest characters that you can play.: Visually, the boost meter is visually way too small on the screen, so it's hard to keep track of your boost status without taking your eyes off the action. You can't revisit any tutorials. There's no in-game encyclopedia for things like character classes.

_childDocuments_.review: After the game went f2p, I decided to give it a try.It's a f2p game, so of course there's an ingame store. there are many currencies that each can buy different things. They are separated from where the characters come from, not the currencies used, except for certain activities which have been given their own tab. Which makes the store is very difficult to navigate, especially if you are looking for something specific. It is a premium currency that you get a bit of during some activities, but the prices in the shop are astronomical. some costumes cost as much as a small game, even with 90% off.On some activities, unfortunately, the game is very pay to win. Activities that give rewards above leaderboards, you almost have to have max level to get something out of them. And even if they try to balance the multiplayer part, it is almost always those with the highest level who win. That's just the way it is.The collecting part of the game is very bad. you unlock the players very slowly and after they are unlocked you also have to level them up for them to become usable.You increase their max level by staring them up, which requires character parts, and you level them with equipment, something everyone uses and something unique to the class and world they come from. This takes a very long time to collect. it seems manageable at first, but after several characters are unlocked it becomes difficult to keep up.Now that all the negatives are out of the way... The actual racing part is real fun. The driving feels pretty good, but needs some skill to do well. There is almost an abundance of skills on the track which makes it quite brutal to drive in groups, and with natural jumping and side dashing, gives a little extra to the gameplay. There aren't that many courses, but each course has several sections, alternative routes and can be driven both forwards and backwards, so there is rarely pure repetition of the courses. The music in the game is mostly remixes of the old Disney classics. They are very well made and I think they fit quite well.The gameplay itself is, in my opinion, quite good. You need to like racing games, and if you want to really get into the collection, there are many hours of grinding to do. This is mainly a multiplayer game. There are a number of single player activities, but what is available per day varies greatly. so if you don't like multiplayer, you may not have much to do. Since it's f2p I'd recommend trying it. You might only get a few hours of enjoyment out of it, but it won't cost you anything to try.Finally, I just want to mention that there are still a few bugs, very rarely something that breaks the game, but my game crashes sometimes between 1 and 2 hours. Without fail. I have only manually exited the game 5 times. I think around an hour and a half is a decent day's session anyway, so it doesn't particularly bother me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game had so much going for it. The racing mechanics are actually very fun, the Disney IP is a great idea for a racing game, and the idea of being able to progress your racers is a neat one.However, the game is FAR too focused on gating its players' progression through insanely overpriced microtransactions. I began playing with the launch of F2P at the start of season 4, and I played a total of 261 hours through the first week of season 6. My interest had been steadily declining throughout season 5 as I was continually gated off from progressing despite playing daily and consistently getting in the top tier of rewards for timed events. To add insult to injury, they kept changing the ways you could procure upgrade materials, marketing the changes as benefits for players but in practice betraying those who had spent time in ranked mode and not actually providing a consistent or meaningful method of character progression.When they introduced the Racer Boost daily/weekly event, everyone thought it was going to be this great new way of choosing which characters you can upgrade. You DO get some choice, but at most, you can earn two shards with a specific character a week. At the time, it cost 35 shards to upgrade any character from 2 stars to 3 stars, and 50 shards to upgrade them from 3 to 4 stars. You can do the math on how many months it would take to improve a character from 2 to 4 stars using this method, especially if you don't have another method of procuring shards for that character (like previous seasons' golden pass epic characters) outside of spending money on them. And you can only get those shards for them in the Racer Boost event if you've unlocked the character at all. That's only one example of the massive gates to progress they implemented.As time goes on, Gameloft has shown that they don't actually care about implementing features that are good for players; they care most about features that will cause players to spend more money. I'm writing this at the start of season 7 (I have had the game uninstalled for an entire season at this point but stay informed via the subreddit), and I can't help but figure that their most recent monetization changes are designed specifically to get as much money out of people in the final stages of their support for this game before ditching it altogether. Don't download this game, don't play it, and if you do that, DON'T spend money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: first of all the game is nice, but the reason i'm giving negative review for this:-Fake Discounts, pay to win and unblocking blocked playersProducts advertised as 'on offer' for longer than they were sold at their full price, or increasing in price when they’re on multi-buy offer.Bait and switch: Promoting one product with the intention of selling you something else.Limited offers: Falsely stating that a product will only be available for a very limited time, or that it will only be available on particular terms for a very limited time, in order to elicit an immediate decision and deprive consumers of sufficient opportunity or time to make an informed choice.False free offers: Describing a product as free or without charge if the consumer has to pay anything other than the unavoidable cost of responding to the offer and collecting or paying for delivery of the item.Similar case with Fallout 76 (which resulted in removed of the fake discount):the fake discounts is illegal here in my country, at least going by article in our constitution about consumer rights.

_childDocuments_.review: Of course it's a pay 2 win game with lots of micro transactions but underneath all of that it's a Mario Kart type of game which you will have some fun even if your not in the top 3 in every race. For a free to play game it's a good game. It's not just a Mario Kart clone. It does more than that. It lets you get takedowns like Asphalt 9/Burnout with a dedicated takedown button to hit your opponent. It's not instant takedown if the character is durable like big characters like Beast. There are 2 Specials for each characters which is unique to there own and doesn't feel like just a copypaste of other characters. There are character type also. It's like a hero racer. There are brawlers like Donald duck which has offensive specials. There are just characters that uses speed specials like Mickey Mouse. There is also Aladdin Genie which has unique special like gives 3 consecutive pickups and another special that either gives him speed invulnerability, guided projectile depending on how many is in front of him. Genie is great if you want to strategies and played best in the middle placements during the race to maximize his specials. There are also variations for each item pickups. There are different ways to unleash them. There is a defensive way and an offensive way. You can also unleash it behind your character. You level up you character in this game which will give you access to more powerful specials and more powerful item pickups. There are also some grinding involved with the vehicles. Some you need to jump to reach them. There is also jump to reach consecutive speed  boost in the air. Those are fun. It's like playing a platformer for a bit. The other positive thing is that there is no limit for racing in this game like Asphalt which you wait for fuel to recharge. Also this has local split-screen multiplayer for 2 players. Some special events are timed though. My only gripe about the micro transaction for this game is that the current battlepass doesn't let you purchase the next battle pass for free. You need to buy the battle pass every season.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for a long time and it doesn't disappoint. There are some cons for sure, but at its core, this game is very fun.The maps are absolutely the highlight of this game. They are gorgeous with thematic gameplay elements added in and the classic disney songs remixed really get you in the mood. Every collection has its own map with several variations (with Hercules having the most). I know this is just a racing game, but the worldbuilding is excellent and each map really fits the movie really well. I'm super excited how you guys bring more Disney titles to life - hopefully Sleeping Beauty will be coming in the near future with Aurora and Phillip as racers. :)The racers themselves are also pretty well done. There are four different racer classes that provide a different playstyle (my favorite so far is Speedster) and each racer has a unique ability and so far they all fit the characters so well. There is also quite a bit of visual customization for the racer themselves and their cart. The crew system is a little boring, but it is nice to have other characters make their way into the game in their own way.Events and circuits. When you press Play, you have a ton of different modes to choose from - 2 multiplayer modes, custom lobbies, solo play, the Starter Circuit (recommended to get your base characters to 2 stars!!), the Season Circuit (a really solid way to get Season Pass XP on top of daily/weekly missions), and rotating events. I really like the rotating events because they're quick races that have you complete certain tasks to get a variety of rewards. Now for my cons. As others have said, this game is insanely grindy. So far my favorite racer is Belle, but I'm kind of at a standstill with her because I still don't have her at 2 stars yet so when I play her in Ranked Multiplayer, I don't even have her ability. Every base racer will be 2 stars once you complete the Starter Circuit and even the Monsters Inc. racers can be bumped up to 2 stars instantly by paying (mobile game lol), but the side characters you can also unlock with a Founder's Pack (Belle for me) have to be grinded out. I don't really know if there's even a better option for progression than the parts system you guys are using, but it is kinda boring and annoying.Also, in Ranked Multiplayer, I've definitely noticed console players skipping around. Not sure if it's because they're on Wi-Fi, but having someone disappear then reappear right on top of you, sending you flying into the guardrail, really sucks.I'm also really concerned with such a consistent method for getting the parts needed to upgrade AND shards AND really good cosmetics (in some cases, the best) being tied behind ranking up. Unless getting to the highest tier is more about time put in than skill, it would really suck to miss out on good rewards because we're not "the very best," ESPECIALLY because each racer has its own rank.

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Speedstorm at its core is a fast paced, action packed racer with very catchy music and visually nice boards, beyond that there are some good points and bad points.The bad points are there are too many currencies. Currently there are blue tokens from various sources, yellow tokens from the battle pass, and light purple tokens from multiplayer, plus other one off tokens for free boxes. If they want to avoid problems going forward they need to combine systems for ease of accessAs mentioned this game as loot boxes, of a sort. Some boxes offer purely cosmetic items for your character or car, the main box though which you buy with battle pass currency gives you a chance at getting crew for your car (which increases your racing stats in the wake of not being able to change kart)  or racer tokens which is how your character levels up, but it not their racing level, more on that in a secondCharacter leveling and racing levels is where I think this game is going to make or break itself. Your character has a star rating, better star rating better stats and abilities. They also have a racing level which dictates what level difficulty you are capable of doing, but sadly it also affects stats, meaning that if you are a level 5 racer and queue for ranked, you may very well race off against people who are level 10 and able to go MUCH faster than you. Some may view the system as an incentive to keep playing to get more items and subsequently and get better, others may not.The good points are the game actually feels very good to drive, it’s got very tight steering, nice manual boosting and character specific battle items that make the game fit to your style of racing, personally I prefer ramming people off the board so I play Donald 😊. Compared to Nickelodeons kart racers, this feels much better and in some ways feels better than Mario KartThe tracks, while few in number for early access, in my opinion do feel varied based on the fact there are 4 different version of each track to where each race you’ll have a moment of “which version is this?” And I personally enjoy that.The music which is a mix of new songs and remixes from their corresponding franchises (Mulan features a remix of Ill make a man out of you for example) fits well. Personally I think the music is great and really pumps you up for a good time..Realistically, if you look at the game as a whole with all its pluses and minuses and have the sense it is early access, I think it ranks more of a 7, 7.5/10If you are looking for a Mario kart clone, go play Mario kart. This game isn’t trying to be Mario kart, it’s trying to be its own racing game and calling every racing game that comes out a Mario kart clone seems unfair biasBut that’s me.

_childDocuments_.review: Very polished kart racing game that features hero abilities and passives, as well as gacha-style progression in the single-player mode. So it's similar to the latest NFS and Forza games in terms of progression. You can also quickly get into games without being bogged down by windows, reward screens, or loading screens. Multiplayer is normalized and in ranked stats don't matter. Unlike Mario Kart, there are no obvious "time to ♥♥♥♥ over the pole position" items, and every item that can be used forward has to be aimed. This means that going fast from the start doesn't mean you have to endure and onslaught of certain items constantly being chained into you.While there's nothing really that aggravates me about the game, the AI can be quite brutal. It constantly bullies you by crashing into you and hunting you down like you're a criminal on an American highway. This becomes especially apparent at higher difficulties, when the game introduces map events and modifiers that change up the gameplay. Some people might appreciate the challenge, because you can even lose the initial games, but it's really annoying for me.However, playing in multiplayer is much smoother and more enjoyable, as real people tend to play passively, so you can go super fast in them. Also despite some criticisms, the game isn't full of MTX. All the micro currencies can only be earned through gameplay. The game also has exceptional performance and a super responsive and clean UX.

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Speedstorm and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe are both popular racing games that have captured the hearts of gamers around the world. While both games share similar elements of fun, fast-paced racing and colorful graphics, they have some distinct differences that set them apart.One of the most significant differences between the two games is their character selection. In Disney Speedstorm, players can choose from a variety of Disney characters, each with their unique abilities. In contrast, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe features a range of characters from the Mario franchise, each with different stats and abilities. This difference makes Disney Speedstorm more appealing to Disney fans and children, while Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is more geared towards gamers who grew up playing the classic Mario games.Another notable difference is the track design. Disney Speedstorm's tracks are inspired by Disney's theme parks, such as Space Mountain and Pirates of the Caribbean, while Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's tracks are inspired by the Mario universe, featuring familiar locations like Bowser's Castle and Rainbow Road. Disney Speedstorm's tracks are more visually appealing, with more detail and a more significant emphasis on theme park theming, while Mario Kart 8 Deluxe's tracks are more focused on gameplay mechanics, with elements like jumps, boosts, and obstacles.In conclusion, both Disney Speedstorm and Mario Kart 8 Deluxe are excellent racing games that offer hours of fun and excitement. Disney Speedstorm is more appealing to Disney fans and children, with its unique character selection and visually stunning track designs. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe, on the other hand, is more geared towards gamers who grew up with the classic Mario games, with its familiar characters and traditional power-ups. Ultimately, the choice between the two games depends on personal preference and the audience's age range.

_childDocuments_.review: As of season 3 I no longer recommend this game not even when it goes F2P in September.They have nerfed rewards from certain modes to push players towards buying tokens to buying more coins but this makes character shards very expensive when converted, you are looking around £20 just to unlock a character if you missed them never the less to actually level them to 2 stars for their much needed skill.RMP rewards went from 20 shards to 3 shards of a character with still  needing the same 5000 points to get everything, RMP no longer counts for MP missions pushing players into MP which is still broken 2 seasons in. Players still lag everywhere to where your hits do nothing to them yet they can destroy you, desync the map so they are in one spot on yours but still placing items right along side you and popping back on your screen just before the finish line funny enough. This is also not counting the players who sit on lap 1 only to move when 1st place is near finish line, stealing 2-3rd off those who worked hard for it.This game HAD promise but no more, Greedloft has struck as expected and they will never listen. I want the game to work but with how greedy they are and main appeal being a broken MP it will not last long even for whales.They not added anything for those who don't want to grind MP, no world cup or anything, the LE and seasonal chapters are nice but waiting every week for new ones which you are done with in 5-15minutes is not content to keep the game going.-----------------------------------------(Pre-season 3)So far I only been racing bots (though they do give a challenge) and I am loving it!Controls are fine, it is easy to do starting boosts and drifting feels great.Plenty to do for those who don't want to race with actual players such as unlocking parts to upgrade your favourite racers and mini missions to keep you going.So for those worried it is P2W, so far I not really had issue leveling up any character and shop stuff is just minor colours or starter packs if you wanna give the character a jump-start in level or two but not needed at all to race and enjoy.As for the tracks, I love them, some have added stuff to keep them fresh and their backward versions are enjoyable too, it took me a while to realise I was racing on some tracks backwards.Lastly, the soundtrack is awesome, I can tell which franchise it is from and still love how they have remixed/made it more jumpy for the racing genre so look forward to getting the soundtrack when possible~If you love racers I say give this one a shot even if just the standard version, otherwise you will have a fun game to look forward to when it comes F2P (said to be next year but who knows)Edit: I will say however I do agree it is scummy to add the packs to even play the game at the moment as DLC so you cannot get a refund if you don't like it or it does not agree with your PC.SEASON PASS - The xp is NOT slow,  go to the Seasonal Tour, the race missions give 400xp each (3 per race race) so easy 1200xp to level up the pass.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a qualified "yes" - the game itself is great. Very mechanically sound, the sense of speed is top-notch, the characters are fun and it has a banger of a soundtrack. But the monetization is abhorrent and actively makes the game worse. You want to race in this race? Too bad, if you don't have a level 40 Goofy you aren't doing anything. You want a level 40 Goofy? Feel free to drop $30 in the store and you might get enough shards to level him up if the RNG wills it. There's an excellent kart racer in here with some ideas that even Mario Kart could learn from but I can really only recommend it to people with a ton of patience and impulse control. Look, game development isn't cheap but there are better ways to handle it than this.

_childDocuments_.review: Just for some context, I am a very big racing game fan. This includes casual racers like Mario Kart and Burnout to full-blown racing sims like modded Assetto Corsa.Disney Speedstorm feels really fast, with a considerable amount of depth in the gameplay. In addition to the normal drifting and item usage, their slipstream mechanic is done in a way where boosting is encouraged very frequently. This means that, instead of being taken out of a first place lead due to a Mario Kart-style blue shell, your opponents will be consistently competing with you at the front. The races are finished quickly, lasting only 2-3 laps, making the them feel less grueling than an unlucky Mario Kart race where you keep falling off the stage and getting pelted by items. The stages look absolutely great! They capture that Disney aesthetic with cool remixes of popular songs. They have branching routes with creative transitions like jump pads, wall driving, and rail grinding, without there being "secret" fast routes. One unique combat mechanic baked into every character is the ability to hit other drivers to the side of you, gaining you some temporary buffs in addition to stunning the target. I love the gameplay as it is great for quick stints. Playing locally allows you to customize race length as well if you prefer something longer. Speedstorm also supports cross-play and cross-progression!Unfortunately for us, this game falls into the live service trap of milking its players of real world money for in-game rewards. Not only does this game charge for a battle pass, but this game is 10000000% pay-to-win. Characters must be leveled up individually in order to increase their base stats. This requires in-game currency in addition to the characters' shards which can be purchased with your hard-earned money. Earning shards and the in-game currency will require too much grinding; therefore, ruining a decent gaming experience.Instead of giving us a free-to-play game with predatory microtransactions, why not charge us $40 for this game and include all characters, stages, and a complete offline experience?Will check back in a year to see if this game is even alive.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not care if the gameplay is great. This needs to be said, and developers need to pay attention to this.Disney Speedstorm is a F2P kart racer that was in Early Access for a while, and just came out of said access lately. It features popular Disney characters, hence the title, and you just race your way to victory in order to get stuff that you want! The game is chock-full of monetization just like every other free-2-play mobile game where microtransactions are the dominant form of progression and the amount of intelligence needed to play the game is, in all honesty, almost nonexistent.This game requires so little thought into playing and I really don't think it would've been acceptable to release as a free-2-play game in the first place, but alas, that decision somehow came to fruition!I 100% do not trust mobile-type games, and even pure mobile games to be totally honest. While some people may argue that they do have a place in the market, they are the real reason many egregious business practices/models exist that have even leaked their way into console gaming due to them. I'm not a fan of mobile gaming, more power to others who are I suppose, but I just cannot put up with... whatever the hell this game's monetization is!I made it 12 minutes into the game before I noticed the "NEW DEALS" in the Shop menu, and the moment I saw what was in it, I turned the game off immediately! That was it! That was more than enough for me to stop playing the game and uninstall it for good! I'm not giving in to that kind of deal, and the developers should be ashamed of themselves for putting that kind of stuff into a game that had high potential!Just to add insult to injury to this ♥♥♥♥ sundae, the first Hot Wheels Unleashed game did this much better by having absolutely NO microtransactions at all!Pay-2-Win types of games aren't even games at that point because there's absolutely no sense of achievement in them! You either grind for hundreds of hours of your life to make so little progress that it's not even worth it in the end, or pay up hundreds and thousands of bucks to get what you want and have an easier time! What's the point!? I fail to see the good in either option!Apologies for the sour reaction for a game like this that likely has its fans, but I'm not one of them, will never be one of them, nor will I give this game a single compliment aside from the gameplay! It's just as horrible as all other monetization heavy mobile games out there! It's PREDATORY. The character roster has items that are locked off and require in-game currency to purchase, and the freedom in this game is much more strict than even that Mickey N64 racing game!A game from the Nintendo 64 era had more freedom than this! This strikes me as nothing more than just a quick cash grab that preys on young kids who try to get their hands on their parent's wallets, credit cards, what have you just so that they can dump tons of money for content that is not even physical!I know I'm preaching to the choir here, but time and time again, the industry constantly gets away with this even over a decade and a half later and we shouldn't rest until something is done about it, that is IF something will be done about it in the first place!Lego 2K Drive can also rot in hell for this kind of business practice, since both games are very similar! Disney Speedstorm is going into what I call, the "Arcade Racing Game Bargain Bin"! Do not get this game, seriously. Your wallet will cry so much with this one, and you'll be sacrificing your dinners for it.These reviews for both games are identical because they're pretty similar despite the fact that one's an arcade racer, and the other a kart racer. They may not be exactly the same, but they're very similar regardless of the differences.LEGO 2K Drive Review:

_childDocuments_.review: Leaving a positive review because I don’t want this game to die and the bad reviews certainly aren’t helping.Sure, it needs some work, that’s why it’s in early access. It’s definitely in a category of games titled “Hard to Master”.But seriously it has so much potential. If you love Disney and Kart racing games, what are you waiting for? Characters are astounding and look good, maps look fantastic, music is incredible, powerups are very original. Also very important, not used to this by Gameloft, but the developers actually seem rather active, giving a lot of updates and listening to the community.The AI in this game definitely needs some tweaking because the rubberbanding just isn’t fun. The several different tokens and coins makes this game more difficult than it needs to be. Lastly, FOMO is big with this game, you shouldn’t have to log in everyday to complete some challenges just because otherwise you won’t level up enough and therefore can’t keep up with players in Ranked Multiplayer. This isn’t a mobile game, Gameloft. Regulated Multiplayer on the other hand is fantastic, glad they have that.TL;DR: Leaving a good review as I still have some really high hopes for this game. Tremendous amount of potential and I don’t want a bad review percentage withholding other gamers to buy or try out this masterpiece in the making.

_childDocuments_.review: GOOD:One year ago this game went free-to-play ... and since that day I'm playing it almost every day, for over 358 hours (135 hours on PS5, over 60 hours on Switch and lately, almost exclusively 163 hours on SteamDeck). Crazy, because I've never been the guy for long time multiplayer or free-to-play stuff. But the gameplay and driving in SPEEDSTORM is so addicting and in my opinion way more satisfying then in Mario Kart or Sonic All-Stars, plus the Seasons give you so much single player stuff to do each week, so you're not only focused on doing multiplayer all the time ... I love it. The tracks are all beautifully crafted and always a joy to discover when they are adding a new one. The performance on SteamDeck is great and the game looks better as on every other platform I played it on. MONEY:About the in-game economy, if you are a person that get's FOMO easily ... maybe avoid this one, because it's stupidly expensive (and sometimes even downright impossible) to get every new racer day one.But sooner or later you will get chances to add them to your collection after a few months have passed. In this last twelve months I spend round about 25-30€ on stuff/characters I really, really wanted in that moment ... that's a more than fair deal for over 358 hours played I guess ;-) BAD:Besides that my only major criticism of this game is currently, that there are always some new characters that won't get voice lines. The joy and magic of all these Disney characters is based around them constantly talking during races and commenting in their unique ways on what's happening on the tracks. Their are 6 characters out of all 69 characters currently (8%) that are completely voiceless. Too bad that especially very expressive characters like for example "King Candy" (Wreck it Ralph) or "Anger" and "Disgust" (Inside Out) still don't have voices to this day. That's my main reason why I rarely use these characters...

_childDocuments_.review: Got the Founder's pack when the game launched and was overwhelmed with the stuff you could do but since the beginning, you couldnt progress the "Story Mode" if you didn't have certain characters like Hercules, Sparrow and Belle (not sure about the last one). After coming back to the game on S3, you couldn't progress the season tour if you didn't have characters that were available before during LTE (limited time events). If you got them, cool, if not, you will be missing out on certain rewards and content. This also affects new players as most of the game will be locked away behind content they cant get or money.They recently changed how the LTE work. Previously you had to place on a leaderboard. If you made it to the top 25%, you were able to get ALL the rewards. Now they have made it even harder by raising the difficulty and now making the highest rewards be behind top 5%.LOOTBOXES: this game contains lootboxes. In order to unlock a character you need "shards". How do you get shards? by buying the season pass, playing the season tour, multiplayer, opening lootboxes, daily rewards or LTE. The problem wit this is that you need 10 shards to unlock each one of them. And their level is capped by how many stars you have have on the characters (afetr unlocking a racer, shards are used to "star up" the character) So this means that you have to grind or get lucky to get a character and level them up to level 25 in order to be "safe" and be able to get almost all the content".TLDR: This game is fun if you only play locally with friends or really dont care about spending money and progressing that much. other than that, i would stay away from this game until they change how the game is played

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mostly fun but also frustrating arcade racing multiplayer frenzy. The single player modes are good for obtaining free items to add to and boost your racers. If you stick to the single player modes you'll win lots and have fun. The main game mode is Multiplayer Rank however which starts off easy enough per unlocked character with all the other online racers more or less newbies. However, as you climb the MP ranks it soon punishes you with ever increasing negative points should you finish in the bottom 50% of each race after MP rank level 16. This makes you need to grind or pay to level up your chosen racers as high as possible to remain competitive. However the truth is when you think you've "made it" by levelling up your racer to say level 25 all you've done is now place yourself in races with mostly level 35+ players and losing much of the time as a result. And when you've eventually levelled up to 35, you're now regularly facing level 45+ racers at least half of the time and therefore losing often once again. So while the goal is to level up your racer, as soon as you do you'll very quickly hit a ceiling putting you near the bottom again. The game has too many lottery & gambling elements that can drain you of your money if you're not careful. Just know that you cannot constantly "win" and while levelling up your character is momentarily satisfying you will quickly realise doing so was actually futile as you still can't consistently "win" - you're actually mostly just making up the numbers as the "also rans" for the pros to beat. Then there's the random game crashes. But overall the game is very well made and fun to play, as long as you don't take the need to consistently win in MP Rank mode too seriously. Level up your characters as much as you'd like, and then quit the online mode for that particular character once you start to lose too often and move onto a new character to play. _childDocuments_.review: Disney Speedstorm is an extremely well made kart racer... The issue is Gamneloft's predatory practices. _childDocuments_.review: Was fun while it lasted. You could play it as a solid F2P, the cross-compatibility between Steam and the Switch was a very nice touch too. But Gameloft has to do what Gameloft does, meaning that they went the greediest way possible. It started slowly, with unobtainable objectives for free players (even by playing this game every damn day), they added cheating AI in their missions (If you are under the required level, you will see one to three racers being pulled with strings, like 700mph fast, until they have something like half a circuit between you and them, and then they will adopt a "normal" max speed until the end of the mission). It was dumb, and it was ugly, but hey, I still played since the game had its times when it was still fun (to collect, upgrade, play online, etc.).But now, several characters are behind pure paywalls, the kind of paywalls that state its name, not like before where they were pushing the greed, no, complete assumed greed. You start the new season with "Battlepass now only accepts real money!"; so you had a way as a free player to gain the same tokens that people paid for, of course you would never have anything close to enough to be able to max out more than 3 or 4 racers, but now, you will simply not be able to have several racers, and this, each season. What's the point anymore?It makes me think of what Blizzard did years ago with Hearthstone, one day they said "Fu*k free players, we are going to make some OP cards that you can only get with real money" (I'm looking at you Reno), and they paid for that dumb decision. Like this game will pay, BUT, Speedstorm is no Hearthstone, this game will certainly die before the end of the year. I'm sorry for anyone who ever gave any kind of money to this thing.

_childDocuments_.review: GENERAL CONCLUSIONIf you're a fan of kart based games then it's worth a try for the gameplay variety, fun maps, and really beautiful visuals. I've had fun and I'm going to keep playing. Consider the price tag it's great.HOW IT FEELS TO PLAYIn some ways this is taking me back to 2003's Disney Extreme Skate Adventure which also did a perfect job converting disney themed settings into skate parks, but in this case with Speedstorm it's raceways. I've found it well paced and matches have felt fair. New characters have new skills to try out as you progress and there's a very "Easy to learn, difficult to master" feel to the driving. Some reviewers mention the shortness of the matches but I like it. You get your 2 laps to try your best, and then that's it. It keeps me engaged whereas longer matches where I'm losing all the time would make me close the game i think.MONETIZATION ISSUESI've never been a "collect them all" type player so the gacha stuff doesn't bother me, it's pretty clear there is a grind though. I htink you can pay money to get characters if you really want to, but so far with 3 hours in I've gotten mickey by default, and Donald Duck by doing single player missions. The coins/shards/stars thing is honestly so confusing I ignore it. I click the upgrade button if it's glowing, otherwise, enjoy the Kart Racer game you got for free.

_childDocuments_.review: LE: as of the last few chapters in the season (Frozen, season 5) I can't really say that the game is F2P anymore; to be able to finish or, in some cases, to even compete in a few racers you need to have specific racers which you can only get by paying real money. Besides this, the biggest rewards you could get after completing some races are for the races where you must use a character you can only get after paying and also that's where the rewards to unlock a character that you don't have and need in further races are..Not to mention the fact that simply buying a racer would be enough, since in the last 2 chapters the requirements for those hard-to-come-by racers were for them to be at level 25-30, which would imply more money spending to get the needed upgrade parts.So...I don't see where the "free to play" is, since it's only free to download, but not to fully play.I SOMEWHAT recommend the game, around 60 to 40%.It's and fun to play, it can get addictive and it's also a nice way to pass the free time; the characters are cute, the races are fun and the challenges can just be challengingly fun.BUT-if you are up to date with the progress, there's not much left to do in the game besides the multiplayer section (will write about it soon after), because the daily challenges aren't many at all and with too little reward; also, the weekly challenges should come in a greater number in my opinion...for them to last at least or even more than a week for you to complete, maybe. And I got to this point without even playing too many hours at a time or even daily.-you will be 'greeted' quite a few times with pop-ups about new things added, mainly things that you need to pay for in order to get. Oh and yes, regarding this...there are quite a few challenges that you WILL NOT be able to fulfill because you don't have the needed racers aaand in case you were wondering, yes, in order to get to have them, you'd need to pay real money for them -> if you don't, you won't have any way to complete certain achievements, challenges or objectives.-the multiplayer section sometimes works just fine and what I mean by this is that you get matched with other players very similar to your level, but, the thing is that a lot of times you don't - especially in the higher ranks and when you're about to reach a new level...and as a bonus, if you don't get to a high enough place when your rank is 16+, you'll start to lose points and maybe even get deranked.YAY, such joy. 8-|I also believe that the multiplayer rewards should be a lot greater, considering how tedious it can actually get.-the game also used to have an issue with shutting itself off at random times for no reason and hence I haven't encountered the issue anymore, maybe because I haven't really played more than an hour at a time since the new season released, I don't know if it's still there or not (they haven't addressed it as a solved issue, so idk)In my opinion, playing a game should be downright fun and make you enjoy the time spent as a wholesome experience, not make you angry, frustrated and/or upset - and Disney Speedstorm managed to make me feel like this a couple of times.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a mixed button - There are items that make me love the game, but others that unfortunately make me annoyed with the gameI'm currently jumping into season 10, so I'm not too sure how the previous seasons performed.Let's get into it - the Pros of Disney Speed stormThe music/soundtrack to a movie/game can make or break it - I LOVE the remixes that they've done for the game and wish it was some form of download to listen to, on the go or to have at my wedding reception.The NBC models have a lower frame rate to the characters to add the sense of time to them. I think this was a nice touch, but I think they could've used the same frame rate and fluidity as the other models and animations.Cross-platform!! I haven't tested this out fully yet, but I'm happy to find a game that could actually be something to play on a Friday night with my international friendsAnd now for the Con's;The Halloween town requirements  - I'm not too sure how the previous seasons worked but I DO NOT like the way the game is forcing me to play certain characters from the franchise. Let me pick! Maybe I don't want to play as Sally....You can't play the mini-races on the world map unless you have a character from that franchise. On the world map you have something for Mickey and Friends, The Little Mermaid and a few more. However, at this current time, I cannot play anything in "The Little Mermaid" map as I don't have any of the characters unless I want to wait for a long time...or if I want to pay for Loot boxes to unlock the characters.Now...The Servers! I heard that there is a discord server that I could join, but so far I have been told to avoid it due to some of the Gamers/mods being unfair and harsh.As for the games servers, I have been dropped and disconnected on MULTIPLE occasions and being so close to the finish line!!! I've noticed it spikes more towards 7PM-11PM PDT. You can tell if it's going to be a weird race when it takes a moment for the other players to join the race. I've had bad lag before the Wii version of MK, but they had all of that down. I think there's just a little room for improvement in this area the most - At least have server options, NA, EU etc.MY OVERALL THOUGHTS:In short, I love that this is a free-to-play alternative to Mario Kart, but I'm annoyed about the way that you get minimum shards that unlock the characters you want to play and how some of them are behind paywalls and passes. I'm still going to keep playing it as "I have nothing to play"Thank you for taking the time to read my current thoughts!

But even if they didn't do that, I would still hate the way they have things setup, because I find it impossible to find what I'm looking for.But other than that, I recommend this game for anyone who loves arcade racing games. _childDocuments_.review: Do you really like combat racers like Mario Kart? Are you really, really good at them? Then this is a hard "Maybe".The gameplay is absolutely solid. Driving feels mechanically responsive and the controls are good. The music features several catching remixes of the Disney library. The graphics are crisp and clean. The game is clearly paving the way to be a traditional Gameloft coin-operated game experience. Multiple currencies, a needless upgrade system with it's own currency system that ensures any progression you may is diluted across all the possible racer combinations that you might not even have yet. is an excellent experience. All players are on the same footing. It's a real show of what the game could be. It rewards only cosmetics. contains the main progression methods outside of Single-Player content. It is a show of what the game WILL be. Item power efficacy, and even just accessibility to items powers to begin with are governed by an inane Racer Level system that can only be raised by casino rolls. A level 1 racer doesn't have their full kit. A level 5 racer has abilities that last longer, hit harder or faster, and are simply more effective. This could be accepted as a modern progression system if the progression was equally accessible, however the ranking system to date confuses the community and is largely unapproachable; not even having a basic MMR setup. As a result, for most players, the only way to realistically progress your imaginary stats and unlocks is through... isn't even good or bad. It's just straight deceptive. Each single player race has a "Recommended Level". When you begin a single-player race, the game assigns a finishing pole position to the player and bots. The bots will do whatever is necessary to maintain that position. This means if you do not meet the Recommended level, you will be assigned a position under first place. The bot(s) assigned to 'beat' you will simply increase their base speed infinitely until they are ahead of you, and often even become invulnerable to items.The inverse is true. If you are at the Recommended level, the bots will intentionally sabotage themselves if they are going to win. You will witness wonderful comedy in the last 20 seconds of every race as the formerly flawless 1st place bot irrecoverably slams his face into a wall and stays there until you pass him. Or as every other racer on the map sudden has their top speed cut in half on the last lap. This would just add up to being a comical checkbox exercise except that you constantly hit walls in progression where if you can't hit the magic number required to play; there is no actual way to win the race to unlock the next steps because the bots can and actually will just teleport in front of you if they have to to ensure your unworthy upgrade number is punished.: Gameloft updated the single player mechanics some. The game no longer manipulates speed behind the scenes, and your kart speed is now shown in game. Instead, if you are under leveled for the content you are attempting to clear, but are outskilling the CPU, it will begin using 'clock' items to warp ahead repeatedly until you are in the 'correct' position.---------Ultimately, the base game is solid and could become something legitimately fun; however it's clear by some very core design choices that that is likely not the direction that this is going.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game the first week of season 7, the little mermaid season. At the start I enjoyed it, unlock a character here and upgrade there. Now it seems just like a mundane task.Here I am with 300+ hours and actively playing daily, however I cannot recommend the game to new players. It is a great controlling game, driving feels good and so does the drifting. Where it falls short is sense of progression, it is a game you grind to progress. It's not a pick up and play kind of game, your either in it for the long term or give up early on. I hit a wall in season 7 where I could do nothing to progress unless I spent money. That's not how a game should work. Why can I not recommend it?This is a fun game to play but only if you have been playing for a long time. New players will have little to no chance in participating in a majority of what speedstorm offers. Sure you get some hand outs in the beginning but once your out of upgrade coins, that it. You buy them to keep playing or grind to get enough to upgrade what you need to. Once they changed from upgrade parts to coins, I hoarded them until I had 300,000 before I started to upgrade a lot of my characters. That's $300 worth of resources I grinded for months, no money spent. Just my time.Online ranked is unfortunate for new players.Say you just started playing and want to level a character up, you play online to get shards. Your maybe level 10, well here comes a guy with a level 46 character who they have never used online to get the shards they need to level up or maybe complete a challenge. You have no chance of doing anything but being lapped multiple times and just taking the loss. I've been that level 46 guy, there seems to not be a bracket for a level gap. Making the task just a chore for myself and not fun for you. Unless you do regulated multiplayer, but then you don't get shards for who you want to level up, just who ever is the reward that week.Season pass and tourIt's fun but again only fun if you have the characters, as a free player you can participate so long as you have upgrade coins. You used to need high level hard to get characters to progress but those high level characters now have their own chapter as a Hard mode chapter as a challenge with special rewards for doing so. If you got money to throw at it by all means but its not new player friendly.You will learn to hate mid season racers.I started playing In March and its November as of this review, It took me nine months to unlock Minnie mouse. That's just 10 shards to unlock her.  I got really lucky with most other racers but she was the last one up until the inside out season. For most mid season racers you need at least 3 or so characters at a maximum of 40 or higher lowest being 25 as of lately. If you just started, unless you put money into it or the time to grind to max online rank with 3 characters its not happening. Sometimes those characters are difficult to unlock just by themselves. Example: It took almost 60,000 upgrade coins to upgrade the characters I needed to unlock rapunzel the newest mid season racer. It was essentially $50 worth of upgrade coins to unlock one character.If you start playing save all your resources and have a very high patience level. Maybe by February you will have enough saved up to enjoy playing as your favorite Disney character. Best of luck to you.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is very fun for what it has to offer. Soundtrack is great, race tracks feel unique, graphics are good, and the game play is very fun. All in all I recommend this game for those who just want to relax, play with friends, or jam out to the music while racing. However, be warned about the heavy micro transactions that come with this game in terms of getting shards/resources for racers. It is worth noting that you can make a lot of progress naturally in this game without spending at all as long as you're consistently playing it and taking advantage of all the free opportunities to gain more shards/resources for your racer(s)Ranked is the only P2W heavy aspect of the game but only at the very top of the leader boards while the other modes can be done with 0 dollars put into the game. I am a prime example of that since I've haven't spent money since it went F2P back in September and have a lot of racers at a high level. So if you are considering playing this game then no the micro transactions are completely optional and you can enjoy this game without spending any money. It will take longer to make progress compared to paying, of course, but this games DOES reward you over time and that's a fact. Thank you for reading this review and have a great day!

_childDocuments_.review: This should not be considered a racing game. It has casino mechanics as its core over racing mechanics.This game reduces your racer's stats while going in first place to allow the players behind you to compete, but this race mechanic only applies if the algorithm decides that you're not allowed to win. The determinating factors are your racer level (artificial level based on how much time and money you've spent in the game), the number of tries and other stuff paremeters behind the scene.This also seems to determine whether players get a teleport item that moves you an unknown number of positions above, allowing you to automatically go from 8th place to 3rd place, destroying any effort made by the players to defend their positions. Sense of Speed feels fine but inconsistent and does not match real speed. Addictive. Slipstream is noticeable. Arcade, Responsive, every character feels different. Arcade. Challenging. Main aspect  of the driving mechanics. Needed to charge the nitro bar. There's a bug (or a feature) where the car drifts based on the nose tip last position instead of your inputs. The drift button is a dedicated one which has nothing to do with the brake, this locks the car position based on its Y-axis rotation. This is a failure point in hardcore time-trials. Taking shorcuts it's important and it's challenging, which goes along with the different character sensations. The huge problem comes with the disability of controlling your car stats which are variable. Every lap you car feels different because of 'the balance' of the game. Extremely inconsistent. The only engaging experience is a fair fight with you opponents; a thing that does not happen very often. You're usually over/under level. Characters are very unbalanced, which becomes more evident with the leveling system.The free stuff that must be earned follows the pattern of giving you 34 out of 35 pieces of any stuff in game, forcing you to pay for the extra piece that is sold in packs from from 5 dollars up to 60 dollars each, or play a a raking PvP that follows the pattern explained before and penalizes you for losing or for disconecting. This also applies for the random disconnection that usually occurs (3 to 5 times a session).Lag is also a problem, but this can vary depending on your region. It is also not important in this bad structure design.There is no skill level match-making nor even racer level match-making which makes you play with your lvl 15 character against a lvl 40 character only having the luck of the algorithm to play with. (Levels are locked behind the upgrade system)Being very skilled only allows you to reach 2 stars racers (lvl 25) and a few 3 stars (lvl 35) without paying. Leaving you without any possibility to compete in top tier ranking PvP. It's not optional since you must reach those ranks to upgrade your characters, but you can't reach those without upgrading them in the first place. It's a false reward design.Extremely overpriced. Over 10.000 dollars would be needed to unlock the full experience (price at november 2023) if you don't expect to suffer. Just as a reminder, the price of 5 upgrade 'shards' is 8.5 dollars at a 50% discount. You need 170 shards to BE ABLE to upgrade (this doesn't count the upgrade items nor the extra 10 shards to unlock the character). This is 289 dollars per character at discount or 578 dollars full price. This stupid progression system also makes buyers feel dumb, since you can earn the same shards with 30k-80k in game coins, which you can obtain in less than an hour playing events or in 5 days playing regular stuff. The huge problem is that those items spam randomly at the store, forcing people to check the store every 8 hours for months.Neither the people who play freely nor the people who pay for this can feel it worth earning or owning anything, just the accomplishment of calming their anxiety created by this gambling FOMO system. ( 3 / 10 )One of the worst PvP I've ever played. And an extremely obvious casino core implementation. Its design destroys any vestige of a good racing game.I can only recommend this game if you plan to play locally without any intention of progression.ALSO IT'S A BUGGED MESS. YOU GET PENALIZED FOR GAME CRASHES THAT OCCURS BECAUSE BAD PROGRAMMED PATCHES.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is a bit lengthy, but basically this is the most mismanaged live service game I've ever played. If you decide to play the game do not spend money.The game is fun. I've had plenty of fun with it. I started playing the game once it became free to play and what I thought would be something I just try for a couple of hours became something I was playing daily. A solid kart racing game with constant updates and daily challenges just really clicked with me.So why do I not recommend the game? Mostly because Gameloft has no clue what they are doing with the game. There have been so many changes since I started playing the game. Some are good, but the bad ones are really bad. For example, they decided to increase amount of rewards you get when playing Ranked Multiplayer by a lot. Sounds good right? Except if you already ranked up your characters you don't get the rewards as they are only redeemable the one time. Basically players were punished for playing the game. It didn't help that when players expressed concern about the change, a Gameloft Community Manager on Discord stated that the change would be minor and there was nothing to worry about. Whether that manager was lying or misinformed doesn't really matter as either way it made future info that much more unreliable. When people complained the community manager then claimed it would be impossible to give players the new amounts (again another lie). After even more complaining and it was clear that this affected a large portion of the player base, they caved and said players would be given the difference. After over a month, they have yet to give that difference or even an update on when players might receive it, Other problems are Ranked Multiplayer becoming pay to win garbage after a certain rank, single player content continuing to become more and more restrictive to the point it's ridiculous, and shop prices being all over the place and constantly changing and never being reasonable.I really wanted this game to be successful, but Gameloft continues to make bad decision after bad decision. Feel free to try the game, there is some fun to be had (though maybe not for much longer if Gameloft continues to change things), but do not give Gameloft any money. They don't respect the players and they do not deserve your patronage.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate this game because it's so fun. Let me explain. If this game had been a $60 or even $70 release with planned DLC for racer packs and stuff, I'd have given it a thumbs up. The racing is tight, the progression of the characters is interesting, the skills and unique abilities are legitimately enjoyable. However, if you couldn't tell by my thumbs down or by the fact that it's a "free" game (emphasis on the air quotes), it's not a $60 or $70 release with planned DLC. This is a gacha game pretending to be a great cart racer. Not only that, but it's a very predatory gacha game, complete with:Loot BoxesConfusing currenciesInconvenient currency exchange (explained below)Fear of missing out tactics with time based events limiting when you can get charactersShard system to star up your characters in order to unlock more abilitiesOnline competitive scene favoring the whales who spend to max star their racersDemo races with paid characters to show how good they are, which seem to be suspiciously easy...?The loot boxes are 500 currency each. They give between 2-8 shards. A character requires 10 shards to own. So, one Loot Box can't even get you a character. 500 currency is equivalent to just under $5. Why under? Because, $5 gets you 530 currency. Now, does this make the currency exchange nicer giving more than 500 for $5? No, it leaves you with extra. This is a very common tactic to trick your brain into buying more currency. It's used in pretty much every game with microtransactions. Let's say you get 530, then you spend 500, now you have 30. Well, now the next pull is only 470 so you could spend $4 for two packs of 200, but then you're still short, so you might as well spend the $5 again. Now you'll end up with 60 left over. It continues on and on. Nothing in the cash shop will ever equal exactly some amount of currency you can get because they always want you to have leftover currency. It's scummy and should be illegal.You only start with one and you unlock a handful of other racers for free through the single player mode. I have cleared the Mickey and Donald Cups and just begun the Goofy cup. All three of them are fun to play, but this game boasts a huge roster of racers. How do you get most of them? Money! I saw a bundle egregiously listed as 75% off (which makes no sense because you can't buy these characters individually) which gives 10 shards for six different characters, unlocking them at 1*, not even enough to use their unique skills. This bundle costs 6,990 currency. If this is 75% off, then these six characters should cost 27,960 currency. If we are to believe the percentage, that breaks down to 10 shards for a character costing 4,660 currency. If you buy that at the lowest package, that breaks down to $46.60 a character. This is another tactic to get people to buy more bundles. There is no actual cost per character so 75% off refers to nothing other than a number they can put up there to make it look like a great buy. I mean, who doesn't want $280 worth of stuff for $70?! Don't fall for it people...I have seen a lot of scummy gacha games in the past and I don't hate them. I dislike them and warn people to avoid them, sure, but hate? No. This game, I hate. I hate it because it's Disney. I hate it because it's aimed towards children. I hate it because it's pretty. But mostly, I hate it because it's good. It's a game that could have been successful as a full release without a scummy cash shop and gacha mechanics. It's a game that would have had an audience with such a successful set movie properties fueling it. It could have gone the Fortnight route, been free with a cosmetic shop, but instead, they decided to make one of the worst cash shops I have seen to date, one of the best cart racers I have seen to date, and create something so evil, I cannot simply dislike it, I must hate it. Damn you Disney.
