_childDocuments_.review: After playing for quite a while, as someone who appreciates different racing games, I can finally say that I recommend the game, BUT, with some warnings included. As always, I will be listing pros and cons, as well add some ideas to balance things out.I recommend the game for the experience itself, but if you're not willing to spend a lot of time playing and grinding for characters/upgrades, this game is not for you.Pros: • The gameplay is actually fun and unique on it's own way, and adding the special ability gimmick makes it an interesting game.• Visually, the game looks astonishing, the tracks are actually well made. But not only that, tracks have randomized variations, unlocking different paths and making races less repetitive.• The voice acting is not bad, and the characters are lovely, it's everything you'd expect from a Disney game.• Seasonal events are easy to catch up as they give you the right amount of things you need, until things slow down a bit. And weekly events are doable, especially if it's a level locked one.• You can get the "Battle pass" for free every season, by simply reaching rank 16 with all of your current characters. Anything past that is a bonus if achieved. You can actually unlock things for free, regardless of how much time it takes.• The pay to win aspect is not that bad compared to what I've seen. There are variables with characters, levels and upgrades. It's completely possible to win if you have a small level difference, and if you're better at the game. (Ranked only, other modes are balanced automatically)• The game has dailies which is a good way to keep things fresh on a daily basis.Cons:• Bad business practices, technically predatory. Characters are overpriced with an applied, old trick, of a fake discount. The store is scripted, luring you to spend money. They follow the "free mobile game" aspects.• Characters are hard to obtain, it takes a long time to get a character you want, without spending money.• Unfortunately pay to win on Ranked mode, small level differences are bearable, but once there's a bigger gap, higher level equals better placements, making it impossible to rank up at higher ranks, with low level characters. Ranked mode needs to be reworked ASAP• I haven't confirmed this, but the game seems to run on a global server which favors low latency. You will often experience lag, which makes the game unfair, especially when you're using abilities that relies on low latency. • The game doesn't introduce you to the ability of bumping into others, which is something quite important and helpful during races.• The one catch up mechanic (Time travelling clock) heavily punishes 2nd,3rd and 4th place. If the front runner is too far ahead, those behind will have to deal with players using the clock item, thus, losing their placements in an instant. It should be balanced.• There's no mechanic to stop front runners, the closest we have is Jumba's ability which is similar to a Blue Shell in Mario kart 8. I personally think an item should be added to at least punish front runners, otherwise it becomes an eternal battle for 2nd place.It's a fun game but with bad business practices, if you have enough free time and you don't mind the grind, it's a pretty solid game. But if you're expecting to unlock characters quickly and play competitively on ranked, I don't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm taking advantage of the game crashing for the 11th time after finishing a race to write this review. At first I was having quite fun while playing tutorials and vs IA mode, guessing where did the bad reviews came from.The thing is that this is a phone game with very good graphics and gameplay, but the pay to win and slowed down progression is there. The game is built to make you feel like this: vs IA races (oh, this game is so fun) -> you finish all the IA races available (now you have to play events or multiplayer) -> multiplayer has a balanced short mode -> you finish it and start ranked multiplayer or events -> you realize there's always one person that doubles everyone else in levels and it's first no matter what. Also that events are based on lvl and equipment. Still, that's not the worse for me. What is throwing me of is that there is too many skills that stun and it's too easy to get 5 stuns in a row. Staying with the main group is like playing russian roulette and only first and last positions can play properly.Ranked progression is just based on games played which sucks, but with this game system I'd still prefer having access to the rewards than being locked for a month at a division because of my items lvl and not my skill.To conclude: Play this while is fun for you and don't spend any money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is yet another game where a neutral opinion on recommendation needs to be a rating option for Steam.Disney Speedstorm on paper, and in some areas of execution, is a fantastic addition to the always prevalent mascot racing genre of games. The representation of iconic characters like Mickey Mouse, Captain Jack Sparrow, Woody, and Aladdin are done well, as are the scenery of the race tracks. And most notably, this game does make a decent effort to try its own ideas for power-ups, rather than mainly cloning all of Mario Kart's like the Nickelodeon Kart Racer games.However, the free-to-play model for this game has some major downsides compared to Gameloft's fellow Disney collab, Dreamlight Valley. Prices for adding new racers to your collection are a bit costly, though credit is due for having options to directly buy them instead of ONLY relying on random drop lootboxes like some games. In terms of cost, the best method for unlocking characters is to participate in the battle passes, Thankfully, there is usually one character you can unlock in the free tier. As of this review, it is Jasmine, due to the season being themed to Aladdin.There is definitely a great game hiding in here, as long as you're willing to be patient on aspects like the daily rewards towards unlocking new racers or upgrading your current ones. So while I can't say it's a complete loss of potential, I can definitely say that this probably should have been a game with a regular price tag updated with new content over time. That being said, the F2P aspect does allow friends to join you fairly easily, but they might be bummed out that some of their favorite characters (in my case, Woody, Buzz, and Baloo) are just out of reach.

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Gameloft likes to copy/paste every game in existence to port on the android store, Speedstorm takes notes from several decades of racing games, wether it be Mario Kart, NFS, or even new-3D Sonic games and F-Zero. Having Disney characters is supposed to be an added bonus, but honestly this game would not have seen the light of day past early access without them.However, the business model doesn't make me very optimistic about it's future as a game. P2W is extremely abundant and abusive and we all know where it's going to be headed in a few months.The best thing about this game is honestly the OST, I love how they took parts of legendary movie soundtracks and turned them into bangers. I am not happy that the streamer mode removes them completely though.EDIT: After several dozen hours, If there is one feeling I have is that this game has been hastily & lazily put together : There is not much to do besides racing, no battle mode, no racing minigames, no cups or tournaments, basically barren content besides boring solo (and they did not keep the previous campaigns ???), netcode is dogwater 90% of the time meaning the interactions with other players often leave to interpretation if they were glitched to begin with since they obviously didn't test the maps (I have found several mesh clips in ranked) Ranked is a stormfest of unbalanced P2W showcase where you cannot even think for one second that you can rank diamond+ without money unless you're both smart and skilled. Lastly, making the battle pass progress only by missions is a chore that should be removed. If all of those problems were fixed, they would pave the way for Speedstorm to be a great F2P game like Fortnite, but as of right now, I don't see this game survive past 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Speedstorm is one of the newer kart racers out there, and to understand it you really have to get three things.1. The serious alternatives are either console exclusive, i.e. Mario Kart or old, i.e. Sonic Racing Transformed; 2. Considering the Free-to-Play Pay-to-Win process that many online and mobile games use, whereby money isn't merely spent on cosmetics, but actually upgrading your racer's performance, you will be heavily incentivized to pay. 3. Gameloft has put a lot of work into making the game extremely endearing and fun, legitimately so, in spite of it.It's within these parameters that Disney Speedstorm exists. So what's good about it? Simply put, you get to race as your favourite characters. Not only that, but they have the legitimate voice actors for almost every single character released thus far. You want to hear the original voice actor for Ariel? She's in it. You want to hear the original voice actor for Buzz Lightyear? Yeah, Tim Allen does the voice in this.Gameloft, likely thanks to Disney, was able to secure a lot of the Disney Animation's A-List actors and voice over folk to make this a very engaging experience because you get to play, as say Aladdin, saying his iconic lines but transformed for the racing arena, whilst exploring immensely beautiful tracks. And I mean it, the tracks are something else.Similarly, the music, because it's licensed Disney content, are extremely well-done remixes, and adaptations of beloved classics. Zero to Hero from Hercules, I'll make a man out of you, from Mulan, Let it go from Frozen, and the list goes on. All of them very engaging, and they're extremely iconic. The alternative games, with a few exceptions from Mario Kart, are pretty forgettable, and Gameloft once more, put effort into their music.So if the game is so nice, and the content so engaging, what's the problem? Again, the simple answer is that everything is locked behind neverending bits and bobs, called Shards, in order to pretty much do anything.Want to play as Beast? Sorry, you can't until you unlock him. Can you buy him outright? No, you can buy the loot boxes, for a *chance* to get shards for him. Once you get 10 of those shards, then you can play him. But is that? Nope. Now you have to level him up with points, and these you get from racing, or you can purchase some. If you don't level up your racer, you'll be underpowered for when you do either single-player challenge races, or multiplayer ranked races.Leveling up in Disney Speedstorm has a tangible effect on your racer. They actually get faster, stronger, handle better, etc., so every level counts. Similarly, when you gain enough shards, you "star up"; this is a secondary level-up process that increases the effectiveness of your racer by buffing their pick-up items on the race track, and grants them access to unique abilities.Now, to be clear, you can access all of this - getting shards, getting loot boxes, and getting upgrade coins for free, but it's going to be a serious grind. If you're a casual player, or a non-competitive player, or even a competitive player who's used to leveraging their skill in racing games, you'll be seriously stymied and locked out of any number of activities, races, and challenges, until you level up your character(s). Inevitably expect to at least fork over $7.99 for access to the seasonal bonus items you get as you participate.What does this all translate to? A subscription, without a subscription, essentially. And money adds up; buying your favourite character's shards when they come on sale in the market, shelling out $5 here, and $5, eventually leads you to realize that you're effectively gambling. You purchase a loot box for roughly $2.50, for a 5% chance that you'll get shards for Lefou, Gaston's epic crew (because yes, each racer gets their own crew, that also grant additional bonuses, and even a starting item when the race begins).The issue here too is that because the game is Disney, it's marketted to children, and I only assume that parents are either shelling out money so that their children can play their favourite characters, or they themselves, like me, are fans of certain characters or Disney franchizes, and with disposable income of your own, reluctantly but voluntarily shell out money to all these nikel-and-dime monetizations.So, the most important question. Will you have fun, with your friends, if you play this game? I'll say *maybe*. If you only have 2 friends, you'll be fine, since multiplayer, at least in ranked or regulated (the two current modes of multiplayer play), allow you to only form parties of 3. Otherwise, you can host your own private races, but only if, you guessed it, everyone involved unlocks Tier 3 collections, which you can do either purchasing cosmetics, or doing enough solo content that you naturally unlock cosmetics and characters through rewards.Repeat: You cannot simply install the game, and play multiplayer with your friends. You must all commit to a certain degree of either spending, or playing, beforehand.So my final verdict is, as of right now, until multiplayer is made more accessible, at least, I can't in good conscience recommend the game. Play only if you have money, are willing to fork over more than you would playing any MMORPG subscription a month, and if you're utterly in love with Disney.Anyone else, move on for the time being. I'll be happy to update my review should things change.

_childDocuments_.review: 30-06-2023 EDIT:We're a few months into this games life and it has improved MASSIVELY! The rubberbanding AI has been adjusted, making the daily grind a lot less tedious. There Regulated Multiplayer now gives out shards for new racers every week. If you do well in these races, you can unlock a new racer in abour an hour. Even if you already have the featured racer, it's still worthwhile to do get these shards to Star Up that racer. Most racers don't become great until they have three stars, so there's good incentive to do them.This game still isn't perfect. For example, Ranked Multiplayer is broken and very unfun to play at times. They group you with players in the same Rank, but don't take Racer Level into account. So when trying to play Ranked with a character with only 1 or 2 stars (so level 15 or 25), so can still be grouped with racers that are level 30+. It's very hard to win those races and gets even worse when you get to Platinum Rank and actually start losing your rank if you lose (or even if you're in the top 3 sometimes??? Another very annoying thing about this game).I am changing my review to recommend this game now. The devs are actively listening and patching up the game and it becomes a better experience (almost) everytime. The fact that I've been playing this game literally everyday since launch says a lot. It's very addictive and feels amazing to play at higher levels. Definitely give it a go if you like combat racers!__________________________________My old, negative review:Under all the p2w trash is a fun game at times. This game WILL be ruined by monetization, because you actually get a gameplay benefit from dropping cash on upgrade items and shards. Another annoying thing is you can't even finish the Starter Course if you don't buy the more expensive Founder's Pack, because you need the characters that come with those to play those. You can also get shards for some of these characters in Limited Events, but they don't give out many and for some of these missions you need high level characters from specific collections. Right now there's a Mulan event, but as of now there's no way of getting Hercules unless you buy the more expensive Founder's Pack.The absolute worst thing that's close to ruining the experience for me is the insanely aggressive rubberbanding. It doesn't matter how high your level is, how perfect you race, the AI will catch up until the last few meters of the lap. I've also encountered AI opponents teleporting right next to you before crossing the finish line. I'm not sure if it's relevant, but that only happens to me when I play a race with a racer that has a lower level than the recommended level for that race. It's unfair and needs fixing.The good: The soundtrack is great, the graphics look quite pleasing, runs fantastic on Deck and, despite the monetization and rubberbanding, it can be fun to play. I'll definitely put some more hours into this, but I sincerely hope they tweak the monetization and rubberbanding before official release. For now, I don't think I can recommend paying for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I regrettably have to update what was formerly a positive review of this game nearly 9 months later to reflect my current feelings about where the game is and what has happened. When Speedstorm launched the game was in a fantastic state, yes there were bugs but the online experience was well balanced and rewarded effort and grinding, and most importantly for me the steam deck experience was phenomenal. So let’s flash forward to December 2023. What’s changed? Well to start the games previous rewarding online experience and far more rewarding experience for being a passionate or dedicated player have been thrown out of the window. Remember this game was made my Gameloft? Yeah. Micro transactions are thrown in your face constantly, and the online experience is pitifully unbalanced due to people being able to outright buy and max out characters with money. The skill ceiling has collapsed measuredly and the new experience for the average free to play player is honestly pretty miserable. All of that is to say on top of the fact that what was formerly a great gameplay experience, has become borderline unplayable on steam deck. No care for scalability to visuals or alternative ways to play the game have been considered whatsoever. When a game looks better with updates great, but when it affects a whole player base experiencing your title in a way that makes them genuinely want to quit it’s not okay.All this is to say that I genuinely loved Speedstorm for so long, and I firmly believe it’s not too late for these issues to be rectified. However right now? Don’t bother touching this game.

_childDocuments_.review: All the resources are there for this to be an awesome game but it absolutely isn't. Gameplay is OK but leaves a lot to be desired and the Pay to Win and poor industry practices over shadowed my experience.- no sense of speed- boost plays a large roll but there is no passive fill so although most of the time will be spent boosting when it's gone the action really slows down- Rubber Banding is atrocious. Battling it out with the AI the race is just a crowd of racers and your position depends on the leveling of your car in comparison but this only matters when you're a lower level (being higher in level won't help the player)- Lack of Rubber Banding in Multiplayer. There is either little or none so if you're behind then that's probably where you're staying. - Lack of skills. Some of the skills are pretty cool but for the most part they're lackluster or just outright annoying.- Mike Wazowski. This really could change to any new character through balancing tweaks but with the lack of multiplayer rubber banding characters really show their trait differences and because of this certain characters will usually be seen taking the race by storm.So there are more pieces that are frustrating or mildly annoying but most of the stuff so far will probably get tweaked and fixed over time.So the real problem here is that this game is absolutely, 100% TRUE Pay to win (And this includes while in Early Access)Character skills are based on their level and just like the majority of mobile games you can play to get those levels but that grinding will take a long time and while people that grind away are constantly losing in multiplayer the other players who poured more money into the game will be winning. This is not just simply loot boxes or cosmetics. By paying additional money for the "DLC" players can get Additional credits and coins (true to a mobile game there are a TON of different currencies.)With those additional credits players can then purchase loot boxes, seasonal tickets, and various other currency based item. These items are then used to level up cars. This is the definition of Pay to Win (just like the Asphalt series)The final nail in the coffin on this one for me was the way this was sold. I (and many other players out there) could have probably done a little better of a job researching but what can I say, I was excited for a flashy Disney kart racer. It may be the consumers job to research what they're purchasing but that doesn't change the fact that this is an awful business practice. Unfortunately 5 minutes into the game I realized what type of game this was when I was limited to only TWO Racers. and at that point I couldn't refund it because the actual game is considered Free even though it's not listed on the store and by buying the bundle you are only paying for the DLC. of course you can't return the whole bundle. This alone earns this the Negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: I am putting this up at the top as this is a legitimate question I want to know."My biggest concern is when they release the "Cars" series. Will the Cars themselves be the go karts, or will the Car Racers be driving the Karts!!!" I grew up in a video store in the 80's that left me with a deep connection with all the Disney and Pixar characters and their stories. This game brings it all to life for me and gives me the ambition to keep grinding to unlock more and more characters that brought me such great memories growing up as a kid, and even still as an adult.Overall I love the campaign mode and progression, but after a while the tracks really start to get repetitive as the grind seems never ending. Everything artistically has been done quite well, and I like most the voice actors except Genie (No one can replace Robin Williams). The game play is fun and interactive to force you to use your skills and drifting appropriately if you want to be a competitive player. They are continuing to update the game and are accepting comments and concerns for patches and updates fairly frequently. However, one thing they will not budge on is the overly complicated "Unlocking System" and "Upgrading System" for Characters and Crew members. There are so many items you need for each specific character/crew member and group series. If you are not careful, you might make a mistake like I did recently and use up all the bread upgrades between two characters of the same series (i.e. Aladdin). Now I have Jasmine and Genie hard stuck at lower 20's, forcing me to grind every way possible for bread.The worst part is I have almost 50 hours into this game, and I am doing everything in my power to unlock the Beauty and Beast series characters. The Beast is the closest and the only way to unlock brand new Racers is Daily and Universal boxes for the specific racer shards. You will spend a ton of time grinding for coins just to gain progress on your battle pass (if you have it) and then countless time unlocking stuff in the store. I would almost say 50% racing, 50% opening items in the store praying you get the Racer, Upgrade component, or Crew member you need to progress through the season.You will be fighting through Limited races which are quite helpful, and pushing through the seasonal racing. Once you have that all complete for the day, you will be forced to go online for either regulated or Competitive racing. The regulated racing changes weekly on what awards you get, but the competitive gives you awards that will benefit your character specifically such as shards to upgrade your Racer, and upgrade items that allow you to upgrade, but know that shards will play a major role. They have a 5 star system and you start with one if you are lucky enough to unlock the Racer. One Star racers go to level 15, then you need a certain amount of shards to unlock two star and so on. The grind is real here.As time goes on and they keep tweaking the game, lets all hope they add more base skills to make the game interesting, and to remove the bump stun. It is absolutely ridiculous while playing online with others. If you are lucky to be in the front and miles away, you live a great life, but if you are in the pack, prepare for H3LL to break loose.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself has very good gameplay and mechanics, it´s definitely one of the best kart racers on the market. It looks gorgeous, the handling just feels good, the art style, music, etc is awesome if you like Disney/Pixar.BUTthe ranked multiplayer is one of the worst i´ve experienced in f2p games so far. It´s not the fact that this race is pay2win/pay2progress, since i´m a founder with over 500h playtime i absolutely can compete. It´s the fact that there is NO matchmaking whatsoever that completley destroys the fun in ranked MP, at rank Diamond and above you get placed in 1:1 matches that you just can´t win. 2 minutes later you get a full lobby of low level players which you dominate. Since you only do 2 rounds (which is 2-3 minutes for a whole match!) you´re also doomed to loose points if you get stunned at the very start of the match (which unavoidable happens every other time).This is also nothing new, for 10 month´s now the only thing you can do in ranked MP are free4all races with 2 (on very short tracks 3) rounds with way to many rng elements like starting skills, special abilites etc. (most of the time it´s not skill or even money/p2w that get´s you the points in ranked, it´s plain luck if you get a good start and don´t get stunned in the first ~10 seconds) which brings me to the conclusion that Gameloft has no intend in changing this. Beside ranked, there´s a balanced MP mode which can be super fun and is way more skill based but it has so little rewards that they are done in 30-45min (once a week!).Also, don´t get fooled and think that you´ll ignore the p2w ranked mode and just play private lobbies or balanced mp casually with your friends (it´s f2p after all), you HAVE to play singleplayer for 1-2h TO UNLOCK multiplayer so you have convince all your friends to spend an evening playing alone so they can play a f2p online multiplayer game (!) with you.Disney Speedstorm may be (technically) one of the best kart racers available on PC, but with the current state of multiplayer (which should be the core of a f2p kart racer) i can´t recommend it to anyone even if you´re willing to spend a few hundred dollars on racers and loot boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering there are almost no popular big karting series on Steam (like Mario Kart or Crash Team Racing), a game like this one is probably one of your few remaining options. However, as you might have noticed from the game score, there’s a catch: it’s pay-to-win. But more on that later.First, the good parts. And it’s a real shame because almost everything else other then monetization is great. The audio and visuals are superb. The characters are really well made and animated. The gameplay takes elements from the abovementioned games and mixes them in a really nice and fun way. I’d say some of the game elements are even better than its competitors.But all of this is tainted by egregious monetization. I personally don’t mind battle passes or loot boxes with cosmetics in a free-to-play game. But not when it’s p2w, especially with ranked multiplayer. Let me give you an example. Some racers have the ability to start the game with items, including an AOE skill that can eliminate four racers right at the beginning. After getting hit by this bs a few matches in a row, your desire to play the game drops to zero.Additionally, almost all other mobile games try to ease you in by offering numerous rewards and quick progression at the start. This one doesn't even do that - I was locked out of all progression by the third day of playing. If it's this hard to progress from the start, I can't even imagine what the higher levels must be like. You’ll be unable to continue playing normally until you spend some cash. And even if you decide to spend some money, you’ll be required to spend even more constantly later. I’ve played too many similar mobile games to know how this works, especially given the track record of the developer behind this game. So, I really can’t recommend it if you decide to play it seriously and sink your time into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Although I have played over 100 hours of Disney Speedstorm, I find myself hesitant to wholeheartedly recommend it to new players. The core gameplay offers an exhilarating experience, with fast-paced races through tracks inspired by beloved Disney properties like Aladdin, Frozen, and Lilo & Stitch. However, the game's reliance on a live service model significantly detracts from its potential greatness. The presence of mundane loot boxes and everything having timers to induce FOMO diminishes the excitement of progression. Certain characters or levels are inaccessible without resorting to spending, which disrupts the fairness of competition and player progression. You are able to spend real money on skins for your characters, however they are just alternate colors of the same racing suite the character wears as their default costume.Furthermore, the seasonal changes implemented by the developers often have a negative impact on the overall gameplay experience. While streamlining certain processes, like the upgrade currency, is appreciated, alterations such as the shift towards the characters' speed stats being the only stat that matters disrupts the balance and enjoyment of races. Additionally, the decision to remove the ability to purchase season passes with in-game currency feels restrictive and counterintuitive. In its current state, despite its enjoyable core gameplay, I cannot recommend Disney Speedstorm.

Was really hoping they wouldn't keep the progression this bad, but the "single player" content is fun, and leveling up stuff can feel somewhat okay but it keeps coming back to the monetization.I advise extreme caution in buying.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameloft's best attempt to go full Activision-Blizzard by embracing the digital STD that is microtransactions. Not just any REGULAR microtransactions though, these are the best kind; pay to win. At the absolute best this game is a fine kart racer. Not bad but certainly not good either. Drifting doesn't feel impactful, traction feels very light, steering feels a bit too loose and bumping into another driver is a 50/50 between nothing happening or being thrown in the opposite direction. Then there's the stats, for some reason someone legitimately thought adding stats for racers in a game with ranked multiplayer was a good idea. Gameloft has it's own half hearted feel in their attempt because of their experience in mobile games. A platform that seemingly operates on the wavelength of "why try to improve when we can just charge you money." This would be a fine enough, ableit underwhelming, game if it just weren't for the egregious and predatory mtx model. Let's break it down here. 37 total characters, 34 of which are ultimately locked behind a paywall as the game does give you access to Mickey, Donald and Goofy for free. The game operates on earning a set amount of "shards" (resource number one) to unlock each character. More shards gained for that character will allow them to "star up" (rank up) to increase their stats. Don't worry that's not the only way they make characters unfair in multiplayer because they can also be individually leveled up as well. All this is bad enough but don't worry, it gets worse. Shards are mainly earned by either buying an "unlock pack" or by spending money on loot boxes because of course this game as loot boxes. In the loot boxes there's a set one for the "season" with X amount of days to get it and you have percent chance breakdowns on each item. There is no guarantee aside from an unlock pack for shards. There is a free daily box but the chances on it are notably worse than the premium box you can buy. So on to how much you are expected to spend on characters. The issue is that it depends on which character it is, I assume it's based on overall popularity of the character. Currently there are six packs that can unlock characters and seemingly rotate after X amount of days. Each of these is suspiciously tagged with "XX% OFF" which is not a good sign. the bundles for Herc, Meg and a pack that has both of them are 2000, 1500 and 3000 in order respectively. The pricing for tokens are as follows; 200 for $1.99, 530 for $4.99, 1150 for $9.99, 2400 for $19.99, 6400 for $49.99 and 13500 for $99.99. This means you need to spend $19.99, $19.99 and $39.98 for the Hercules character packs each...discounted for 50%, 55% and 60% off.The next four they have are Jack Sparrow at 690, Belle starter pack at 1490, Unlock Pack for 4990 and Mega Unlock Pack for 6990...at 92%, 90%, 70% and 75% off in that order. I'll spare the math en masse this time because I think the picture is clear but I want to break down the Mega Unlock Pack. 6990 tokens requires you to spend at least $59.98 at 75% off. So normally it would cost 27960 tokens totaling over $209.97 at full price. $209.97 (plus tax mind you) for 6 characters. That means each character in that pack costs $34.99 (or $9.99, what a deal). Characters that have defined stats that require recurring payments to upgrade that directly give you an advantage against other players online.How have we allowed these things to get THIS bad in games. EA is salivating at the idea they can bring loot boxes back and ActiBlizz is getting ideas on how much more they can charge people as we speak because of this. Not even to mention the Aladdin box doesn't even feature him as a possible racer to earn right now but proudly features him on the image. Hooray for false advertisement! Gameloft should not be taken seriously as a developer at this point, they could've turned the contract down but actively chose to subject not only their playerbase but the Disney fanbase to extremely predatory mtx based gameplay and pricing. I really hope this game gets shut down because no game is better than one that tries its best to force you to spend as much money as possible for minimal and middling gameplay at best.

_childDocuments_.review: I have 200+ hours of this game across all platforms (mainly PS5 and Steam Deck) and am usually in the top 10% of every event. I am a Founder so have played since launch date. This game is fun. I’ll start by saying that. As a racing game, I deeply enjoy it. But it is one of the biggest disappointments for me as someone who LOVES Disney and loves Kart Racers. DISNEY SPEEDSTORM is a greedy Mobile Game disguised as a Console-Quality racing game. I was very disappointed to learn that, when I was given a “Free Racer Unlock”, it actually meant I was in fact only given enough shards to unlock a 1 Star Racer. Every racer can be leveled up to 5 Stars by, you guessed it, grinding and opening Loot Boxes. You can also spend about $100 to unlock a SINGLE 5 Star Racer to save time. There is a HEAVY INFLUENCE on visiting the in-game Shop where you are greeted with 3-5 pages of items to spend real money on and spammed with deals that are ALL a rip-off. Karts, Kart Pieces, Victory Poses, Character Shards and Crew Packs (gear to give your Kart better stats). On top of this there is also a Battle Pass system. The current system has you purchasing 2 Battle Passes per-Season to access them at $10 each (A Season Pass and a Mid-Season Pass) and you don’t even unlock a 5 Star Racer through them. It usually contains shards for one popular Racer and one meh Racer from the respective IP. A new currency was just implemented as well that is now required on top of the Racer Shards to level up a Racer and you are not given NEARLY enough.All of this greed is unfortunate because it does in fact ruin the game experience. But if you can get past the 2 Battle Pass per-Season payments, Loot Boxes containing scraps, Racer Shard/Level-Up Coin collecting, beneath all of the corporate greed is a really fun racing game with amazing graphics and great music. I can’t help but wish they had just made a $60 Mario Kart-style Kart Racer and had Season Passes instead of this Free-to-Play, ever-changing for the worst, money guzzling machine that targets children and Disney “super-fan’s” wallets. On a side note, they recently can't even be bothered to give voices to most of the new Racers, but are still charging full price on them. If I were you, IF you spend money in this game (I’m talking to YOU, Disney Adult), I would NOT SPEND A CENT on a character who was given half the effort and that they couldn’t even be bothered to voice. After all, the other half of a Disney ANIMATED Character IS their VOICE. But you do you.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:    Beautiful Graphics: The visuals in Disney Speedstorm are stunning. The vibrant colors and detailed environments truly bring the Disney universe to life in a way that is both charming and visually engaging.    Diverse Roster of Drivers: The game offers a fantastic variety of characters to choose from. Each driver, hailing from various Disney franchises, adds a unique flair to the racing experience.    Gorgeous Maps: The tracks in Disney Speedstorm are not only beautifully crafted but are also full of thematic elements from the Disney universe, making each race a delightful journey.    Great Music: The soundtrack perfectly complements the game's atmosphere. It's a fantastic mix of energetic and thematic tunes that enhance the overall racing experience.Cons:    Frustrating Gacha System: The lack of a pity system in the gacha mechanic can be very disappointing. It often feels like a gamble, with little guarantee of obtaining the desired items.    Pay-to-Win Aspects in Ranked: The game leans heavily towards pay-to-win in ranked matches. This can be off-putting for players who prefer skill-based competition.    Extremely Expensive: The overall cost of the game, especially when considering in-game purchases, is excessively high. This might deter players who are looking for a more budget-friendly gaming experience.Conclusion:Disney Speedstorm, at its core, is a visually stunning and entertaining racing game that can provide hours of fun. The diverse selection of drivers and beautifully designed maps are its strongest points. However, its competitive aspect is marred by a pay-to-win structure and a gacha system that lacks player-friendly mechanics. This makes the game less appealing for those seeking a fair and balanced competitive environment. It's a great game for casual play, but for competitive racing, it might not be the dream experience one would hope for from a Disney-themed racer.

_childDocuments_.review: Argh i don't know how to review this fairly. One one hand i want this developer to be wiped off the store for it's predadory and abusive sales model. On the other hand, i have to admit that the game itself is extremely good and i want the playerbase to grow...Since this is initially a game review, i'll keep it gameplay related.I'm a fan of arcade racers and played a bunch of them, including Team Sonic Racing which was fun, but lacked content and a healthy playerbase. Speedstorm is extremely well polished, feels great to play and i do like to unlock things as it keeps me playing and getting rewarded for it. The issue here, and i call it a bit of a red flag, is that everything looks like a mobile game. Shards here, currencies there..On the first look i get why ppl want to steer clear of it and expect a p2w system. I expected it as well. But so far, it's not. Everything can be earned in-game without paying. And i like the fsct that they have a currency only for multiplayer games(which unlocks cosmetics only). This motivates me to hop into multiplayer every now and then. Aside from MP there's a lot of content, daily/weekly events, a more classic mode where you can unlock the base characters through chapters.And then there's the "battlepass" with its own event filled to the brim with race events. There's no boredom as there's always something to do. Is it grindy? Kinda, but due to the fact that the gameplay is tons of fun, it automatically makes grinding endurable.The developers however aren't very community friendly. For a start, they deliberately chose to sell the game as one of three DLCs, which doesn't let the player request for a refund. This should be illegal.Another red flag is the use of the "early access" tag. This game is NOT an early access title! Do not be fooled. It's polished, it's filled with content, barely any bugs or performance issues and no roadmap. It's a straight up lie!I do believe that all these things keep potential customers away, and it contributes to a dying, rather than growing playerbase. I can't understand the decisions their marketing department took, as they are counter productive. The game itself is great! I do recommend it. But i also do not want this game to die after 2 months like every other failed service game so here's my request: REMOVE the early access tag. Sell the game for 30$, NOT the dlcs. Add a supporter pack as dlc if you want, i don't mind. But ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on your community is not acceptable!As i said, it's a game review, and i personally recommend the game. But if it wants to survive, many things need to be removed, such as the real-money in-game shop, and a refund should be granted at all times, in compliance with Steam's policies. The way this game is sold and marketed is unacceptable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is purely for Disney and Gameloft to make money. I have stopped playing as of Season 9 because of the changes they have made.First and foremost: this game is very Pay-to-Win. F2P players (such as myself) will struggle with making real progress in nearly all aspects. Each character has their own Unique Skill, and a lot of the Epic Rank characters (the highest rank) are basically locked behind a paywall. You need to collect character shards of a specific character to unlock them, then even more to Star-Up them. Those you need to pay for with the premium currency. Then you also need to use more resources to level them up, which can be tedious to get for free, or you have to pay for the needed resources.As far as gameplay goes, it's fantastic. As a long-time Mariokart player, I was able to quickly adapt to the game's controls (using an Xbox Controller). It can get very fast-paced, and the track designs are excellent. The environments are very pleasing to look at, though I'm not the biggest fan of the artstyle of the character models. (Be warned: if you try to stream this game to a Discord vc, I've suffered the game randomly freezing. This occurs even on low graphics, and I have a pretty good pc. Typically hitting the Windows button on your keyboard to pull up the taskbar fixes it. Streaming to Twitch has only made me experience lag spikes, not full on freezing.) The music is easily my favorite part of the game, but I just enjoy EDM music in general. (Racers now need to be level 30 to be used in Regulated, which is another block F2P players will struggle to overcome. This basically renders the game largely unplayable for F2P), but in Ranked it becomes difficult for F2P players since the matchmaking seems to be whoever happens to queue up at the same time as you, regardless of how upgraded their racer is. You can wind up with someone MPR 1 and someone MPR rank 30+ in the same race. This can especially be a problem since one main way to get character shards is increasing your MPR. If the character you're playing as hasn't hit 2 Stars yet, you don't have access to it's Unique Skill, which is a major handicap and makes the races near unfair at times.The singleplayer is very lacking. There's no Time Trials mode, . There's a Starter Course, a Season Course, and Limited Time Events in Singleplayer. Players just starting out will eventually hit a wall later on in the Season Course since they can't upgrade their racers enough to keep up with the difficulty curve, and oftentimes don't have the required racer(s) for some of the races. Some Limited Time Events are impossible to do for new players for similar reasons: not having a required character or their racers not being high enough level. This can prevent them from getting a character only available through said Event without paying money for it.Overall, the Pay-to-Win aspect of the game is a real dampener on what would otherwise be an unparalleled kart-racer, arguably better than Mariokart if it weren't for this. Along with the lack of a real Singleplayer mode, it's hard for me to really stand by a completely positive review. I definitely recommend giving the game a shot, but be aware that it's not F2P friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game as it's somewhere between Mario Kart and Modnation Racers in terms of game play, which is pretty good.It's pretty much a Disney themed kart racer complete with items for each character for combat. Characters can be upgraded so their items and skills become stronger as well as their uniforms and karts customized.Gameplay is pretty good overall as it's not too difficult to steer. Drifting works fine as well. Modnation Racer fans will also be pleased to know Side Swiping is in the game. I do wish they'd move towards a 3 to 5 lap race system over the standard 2 lap races for most tracks. Races seem a little too short in my opinion.So what's the issue? The current monitization system. I kind of feel like it would be better if it worked like Brawlhalla instead of paying to unlock racers through randomized games of luck, limited time purchasing opportunities, paying to upgrade racers and competing to earn certain characters such as Oswald. I kind of wish you could earn coins that you can use to buy any racer, upgrade parts, and crew members you want at any time based on your racing style and performance so paying doesn't give you a competitive edge.I get that this means they'd have to make money some how, which is why I think alternate outfits such as traditional outfits for characters such as movie Jasmine and Talespin Baloo should be considered for monitization along side the season pass if they don't want to charge for the full game. I'm not a fan of the racing uniforms. I would suggest charging a small fee for the base game, but I'm not sure how it be receive on mobile devices.In terms of future content, I wouldn't mind seeing Zootopia, Talespin, Robin Hood (animated movie), Tron, The Little Mermaid (animated version), Chip and Dale Rescue Rangers (animated cartoon series), and the Animated Aladdin Tv series spin off to expand the cast as I wouldn't mind seeing Nick, Judy, Mirage, Robin Hood, Maid Marian, Ariel, Ursala, Gadget Hawkwrench, Don Karnage, and Rebecca Cunningham as racers. I also wouldn't mind seeing Tron tracks and vehicle designs such as the light cycles.In terms of other things I'd suggest adding is the ability to do limited time events and season tours with online friends.Here's hoping that Gameloft and Disney work on polishing this game up so I can change my recommendation status for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: No game's perfect. This one's no exception, because it does a few parts right, but gets everything wrong at the same time.tl:dr: racing good, but has a problem, monetization is as predatory as a lion, and no, the Lion King isn't in this game, the game's tracks aren't interesting since they're doing an 'all-in-one' sort of track layouts, along with a few others.The racing part is very nice, every racer has their own way of racing. Those like Stitch could easily zip past their opponents with ease while those like Donald Duck could keep the first place with mean attacks. It reminds me of Crash Nitro Kart with the way you need to 'chain' drift boosts.The problem with the races however is the lack of disruption for First Place, or a fair comeback mechanic.If you're somehow lucky enough to break free from 2nd place, and get a sizable distance away while you're in first, there's nearly nothing the opposition can do to stop you without Jumba, since every item in the game has a Range limit that can be upgraded with Crew Members, and nearly all Combat skills are focused on Close Quarters Combat.The monetization of this game is also a problem.Excluding Events, the way to unlock characters is probably the most predatory thing I've seen. You wondered why Loot Boxes have faded throughout the 2020 years, and this is the prime example why. Gambling for Advantage. Doesn't seem like a fair way to enjoy the whole game when you can't unlock things in the more traditional senses. And these chances of earning even a sliver of a Character Shard are criminal: You're better off opening a Counter Strike case and making a profit than actually try to earn Character Shards (Stitch's shards are about 0.27%, dumped under the enormous slog of Crew Member shards).I also have a problem with the game's Tracks.They tried doing a 'one-size-fits-all' thing, which immediately doesn't work when you step back and look at the track as a whole.Andy's Room is a prime example of how it *doesn't* work, and it has several bugs with lobbed items while you're upside down.The Little Mermaid stage's short track is a 3-Lap race, but no other stage with 'short tracks' are 3-Laps, and is incredibly infuriating to play as a part of the stage pushes you off, making heavy characters unviable. Various parts of that stage are completely ridiculous, failing jumps that you should be able to make with any character at any speed.Pirates of the Caribbean stages generally feel the same, only with a split removed in a few instances. Also, you can fail a jump due to poor collision, also has no short tracks.The same issues from the Pirates of the Caribbean stages also apply to the Monsters Inc. Stages, minus the jump failures.The same *same* issues also apply to the Aladin stages, with the short track only being 2 laps long when it should really be 3.Toon Town's stage is a great starting stage, but a section has way too many splits.Hercules' stage is just kinda there.Arbee's stages seem to be the only stages where their track laps make sense, but two are literally just Nascar circles.The only stages I think are personally well done are the Oldschool Theatre stages, and Ku'aii, but even those have problems.They're still missing stages for Wall-E, but I'd rather have 2 one-off stages set on the desolated earth and the Axium, because an 'all-in-one' simply won't cut it.Anyways, a lighting round, because this has gone on long enough.Costume Designs are somewhat plain, and 'premium' cosmetics are just palette swaps. (Would it have killed you to add hula Stitch?)Most base kart designs are shared in their respective collections, which makes them feel less unique, and their paintjobs less important feeling.Gold Crew Members are borderline unfair (any racer who has one gets an item at the start of the race).Ranked makes no sense (shouldn't *that* be Regulated?)Seasonal Tours limit your use of characters to that season's characters unless otherwise.'Elimination', 'Floating Objects', 'Single Skill' Races aren't used in Multiplayer, and cannot be set in Local/Private Play, reducing options for Offline Play.No sort of 'Battle Mode' that would benefit these racers and tracks much more.Despite being able to pair up with a buddy or two, the game does NOT incentivise team play, even if some skills help those around you.Characters can just chug down nearly 35 cans of Energy Drink, and are casually fine. Not a problem, but it's sad that it's gonna be gone soon.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good kart racer. Like, REALLY good. CTR Nitro-Fueled/Mario Kart 8 good.So, what I like:- Currently the in-game shop uses currency that is only obtained in-game, so no "true" microtransactions (yet).- Good cast of starting characters, and the developers promise more will be added over time. They all also play differently! Offensive based characters have more weapon-like item powerups and pickups while more defensive/speed based characters will pick up more powerups related to shields and turbo boosts. Making everyone have slightly different options sounded like a con at first, but I actually really like it since it allows everyone to feel more unique from one another besides just having their own special powerups.- LOTS of activities, game modes, etc. to play.- Multiplayer has crossplay functionality across all platforms. Finding a full grid of people to race against takes me, on average, 10-20 seconds.- Music, sound effects, and voices are really, really nice.- Regulated multiplayer is super fun and the best way to play this game if you're not gunning for constant rewards/unlocks.- The core gameplay is very fast, frantic, and fun. Learning how to maintain your drifts and boosts are essential.- Track design isn't the best we've seen in a kart racer, but it ranges from average to pretty good.- Performance is really good! I have everything maxed out on my aging 5-6 year old computer, and the game runs silky smooth. No hiccups at all.- Powerups aren't super varied, but enough to keep them interesting.What I DON'T like so far:- AI, and race results, in event races feels artificial. It's clear that the game forces the AI to stay EXTREMELY close to you, and they back off tremendously from you in the last 10 seconds of every race if you're already in the lead. It sucks a bit, but the multiplayer is great and makes up for this.- Battle pass feels like it's going to be pretty slow to progress through.- Character graphics are a step down from everything else in the game. Mickey's ears aren't even fully rounded. I mean, the models ARE decent enough, but they could have been better.- Gacha/loot box mechanics when opening boxes from the store make it harder to unlock specific characters, crew members, etc.- It's advertised as free to play, but this is not the case (at least on Steam). You need to purchase a bundle that includes a founder pack, the cheapest is $30. Still relatively cheap if you go for that bundle, but advertising it as free to play feels very misleading.- Shop is set-up in a way that definitely alludes to spending real money eventually when (not if) they add this to the game.- The game is very grindy. Unlocking new characters and such will take a good amount of time. Casual players will probably never have the full roster unlocked, especially when we inevitably get additional characters added over time.Overall, the core gameplay is what definitely keeps this as a thumbs up in my review. The cons aren't deal breakers at all, and it's encouraging that (at this time) there's no way to spend real money in the in-game shop. As long as you're not too bothered by the grind, there's a lot to do in this game so far and I'm sure it'll probably be a blast to play with your fellow kart racer loving friends. As a whole, considering this is listed as early access, the game's currently looking and playing very good!----------------------------------------------EDIT AFTER 70+ MORE HOURS:----------------------------------------------This is still a really good game, but there's a glaring issue with its monetization. Unfortunately, it HAS become extremely grindy since becoming F2P because, being a F2P game, they want to slow down progression so that you open your wallet to speed things up. Same deal as most games out there nowadays, but it's discouraging to see it in a kart racer.Ranked multiplayer EVENTUALLY becomes pay to win at the higher ranks because whales to throw lots of money at their favourite racers will dominate. If you don't care much about ranked, it won't be much of an issue. Regulated multiplayer is still fair game and is a level playing field. Private online games also have all characters unlocked (outside of the most recent season's batch) and is, again, an even playing field.If you only care about ranked play and don't intend on opening your wallet? The game is playable, albeit grindy. Expect a lot of frustrating results in later ranks.If you just want to play casually, or with friends, this game is very fun. When the playing field is even in regulated/private online races, or in early ranked, the gameplay is A LOT of fun! There's still a decent amount to do in the game outside of ranked, but it IS at the heart of the game's progression systems and is closely tied to racer levels which, again, whales can freely increase if they so choose to do so while a F2P player will take weeks to achieve the same results. How much ranked matters, and how much you're willing to open your wallet, will probably determine your overall mileage with this game for better or for worse.----------------------------------------------EDIT 100+ HOURS:----------------------------------------------Okay, I've uninstalled. The core gameplay itself is AMAZING. The OST, graphics, and track design are also really, really good. Outside of those things, everything else about the game is TERRIBLE now and the game is designed solely to try and get you to spend more money with every passing season. The monetization in this game is, simply put, disgusting. I cannot recommend this game to anyone who has never played it, because you'll have fun for a few weeks before you start to grow frustrated at how the game is managed.Screw Disney Speedstorm and screw Gameloft for making me invest over 100 hours into this game. By this point, it just feels like a messy divorce for me and I hate it.

_childDocuments_.review: I clearly enjoy the core gameplay, which is evident from the significant hours I've invested into it. However, my frustrations with the game's monetization strategies and ongoing issues are very apparent.Here's what I think of the game:- Fun Racing Game: Enjoyable with great handling and mechanics- Competitive Edge: Challenging and rewarding for those willing to put in the time and effort- Nostalgic Connection: I have a love for racing games, starting as a child with Mario Kart, which this comes very close- Pay-to-Win Mechanics: Essential features and competitive edge require significant financial investment- Poor Matchmaking: Unbalanced pairing in ranked multiplayer, making it unfair for new or lower-level players- Expensive Season Passes: Story content split into two paid passes with unchanged, high racer requirements- Limited Time Events: Inaccessible without spending money, favoring those who pay over core gamers- Character Acquisition: Prohibitively expensive for new players to obtain characters, adding to the financial burden.While the game itself is enjoyable and has potential, the aggressive monetization tactics and lack of effective fixes for existing problems make it hard to recommend. The game's current state forces even dedicated players to reconsider their involvement due to the financial demands and unfair gameplay dynamics.I hope I somehow made my passion for the game and disappointment with its direction clear. This review should serve as a cautionary tale for potential new players and a heartfelt message to those who, like me, love racing games but are wary of pay-to-win models.Game on <3

_childDocuments_.review: Disney Speedstorm is a great kart racer trapped behind every mobile game trope. Needing character shards to get/rank up characters, needing extraneous upgrade materials to level characters up (increases stats), loot boxes, THREE different kinds of currency, crew members akin to Smash Bro Spirits; its all there.Gonna say this first and foremost, this game is goated enough that you can play this game locally with NO mobile ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. You get access to all characters and they are all level 15. So if you wanna have some normal cart racer fun, you actually still can surprisingly. Im not sure if you can set up a friend lobby online with those rules.Let's get to the actual game stuff first. There are 4 classes of racers: speedster, brawler, defender, and trickster. The differences I can tell are probably their statlines, and how they attain boost meter. Speedsters get boost by hitting boost pads (boost pads speed anyone up, but speedsters get some meter too), brawlers by attacking opponents either with items or side bashing into them, defenders by staying in opponent's drafts (behind them), and trickters i think by using items(??) idk really i couldnt find the info in game.Every series in the game has a track, and all tracks have multiple configurations. They are all fun and they all look good. Each configuration has its own music track, and the music in this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rules. They are usually remixes of songs from whatever series the track is. The Toon Village has a remix of the Mickey Mouse Club from ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 1960, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chant is so good. Or this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Bear Necessities, god the chorus is implemented so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ WELL. There is usually at least 2 remixes of a song, like they use Gaston at least twice in the Beauty and the Beast castle. Yeah im just gonna post some more highlights now. Monsters Inc. theme, Hercules, even the main menu.Also its got some character picks I ♥♥♥♥ with. Celia Mae from Monster's Inc, Gantu and Angel (pink Stitch) from Lilo and Stitch (I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wish Pleakley was playable), Meg from Hercules.You have to collect 10 character shards (mainly through loot boxes) to unlock a character, then the amount needed increases ever time you want to increase their rank. Every character has a unique item box power, but you can't get them until you get rank 2; further ranks upgrade how strong your item box powers are and allow for more crew members. Leveling up your characters is pretty easy at first, but as their get higher, you need rarer materials and every character (maybe its every series) also has unique epic materials so good luck getting that. Also you are level gated by character ranks, i.e. a rank 1 character cant go past level 15, rank 2 25. Every season you get a free character from whatever series they add to the game; the season I started was Alladdin so you get Jasmine for free. They give you enough materials and shards to get her to rank 2, and to level her up to the required levels to play the single player stuff. They don't really provide you with stuff to get her past rank 2.The season passes are cool cause you get a long single player campaign over 3 months i think? There are multiple chapters (they unlock weekly) and within each chapter is a little path that leads to races and loot chests. Each race has 3 objectives to do for medals, medals can block paths and also get you battle pass points. Like I said last paragraph, you get a free character from the season and are provided with enough materials to finish the main path of the season. Eventually, however, you will not be able to do side paths if you don't have other characters leveled. There are some races that require you to have characters from a series you may not have, OR those characters may not meat the required level and you will not be able to out skill the npc's, they are just faster. You can't do those races, you miss out on medals and rewards, and then slowly more and more paths are locked from lack of medals. The AI naturally just gets tougher, as they also start getting their unique abilities from boxes and it kind of becomes and annoying item cluster♥♥♥♥ sometimes. Some characters just have really annoying abilities, like Gantu just sends a spaceship forward that drops goo on the ground that makes you hard spin out.One of the currencies is season specific, and you get it from the battle pass or from loot boxes in the single player. You can buy some daily stuff from the store (usually inconsequential) or some lootboxes. There are lootboxes for every series, but those cost real money currency.I played some online ranked to get a fuller understanding. Each character has a different rank, and their own battle pass progression through the ranks. Usually resulting in loot that is for that character (shards, upgrade materials, cosmetics), but there are also multiplayer points, the third currency. There wasn't a whole lot I could see to buy with them. So yeah, ranked is a progression bar and not really like a rank you can loose. The higher places in races, the more points to fill out the bar. Side bashing opponents always gives you a shield to protect from dangers in this mode for some reason so its always good to do that.So yeah, I think this is a fun kart racer, and it is only hindered by stupid mobile ♥♥♥♥. Its fun to play, it looks good, its got some great character picks, and the music is so so good.

_childDocuments_.review:
Drift into the ultimate hero-based combat racing game, set on high-speed circuits inspired by Disney and Pixar worlds. Master each character's unique skills on the racetrack and claim victory in this thrilling arcade racing experience from the creators of the Asphalt series!

DISNEY & PIXAR GO FULL BATTLE RACING
An incredible cast of characters including Captain Jack Sparrow, Mulan, Mickey Mouse, Sulley, the Beast and more are suited and revving up for racing combat. Upgrade each racer's stats and make the most of their unique skills that can impact the outcome of a single race and dramatically change the way you play the game!

ARCADE RACING REDEFINED
Anyone can pick up and play Disney Speedstorm but mastering skills and techniques like timing your nitro boosts, precisely drifting around corners, and adapting to dynamic track environments are crucial to dominating each race.

RACING TOGETHER HAS NEVER BEEN EASIER
Pick your racer and speed through action-packed tracks solo, or challenge friends in local and remote multiplayer modes. You can even face off with players from around the globe to become an online legend.

DISNEY & PIXAR INSPIRED RACETRACKS
Start your engine in environments inspired by some of your favorite Disney and Pixar films. From the docks of Pirates of the Caribbean's Pirates Island track to the wilds of The Jungle Book's Jungle Ruins map, and even racing on the Great Wall of China itself from Mulan or the Scare Floor from Monsters, Inc., you can experience these worlds from a fresh, exciting perspective geared specifically for racing!

CUSTOMIZE TO YOUR OWN STYLE
Choose your favorite racer's suit, a flashy kart livery, and show off stylish wheels and wings -- all of this and more is possible with the extensive customization features in the game!

NEW CONTENT RACING YOUR WAY
The action never slows down thanks to fresh seasonal content always around the corner. New Disney and Pixar racers will be added regularly, bringing special skills for you to master (or overcome), and unique tracks will be created often, to pump fresh strategy into the mix. Support characters, environments, customization options, and collectables will also drop in regularly, so there's always more to experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much wasted potential it made me write my first steam review in almost 20 years.The pixel art is great, it's basically bug free on launch, the music is decent and the controls feel tight enough. Combat is fun.But the second combat ends, it takes about 15 seconds for me to go "this is so annoying".The problems of Hammerwatch 2 are design flaws, which are all unneccessary. All of these problems were figured out and avoided by game devs so long ago, gamers forgot they existed.It's really weird to see them come back so confidently, as if Crackshell never actually played the game or completely ignored its beta testers.The loot economy is completely broken. Gear drops very rarely and basically never impacts your character.Usually there's some kind of reward at least at the end of a dungeon, here there's just punishment.When I enter a dungeon in Hammerwatch 2, I always think "I'm gonna get nothing for this, I'll just have to backtrack in the end because there's no fast travel".I stopped checking my inventory completely because even when you do get something, you'll just be disappointed.Gear just ends up on the tiny pile of other useless stuff.Discovering another cave is just a chore at some point. You just hope it won't be multiple levels so you have to backtrack less.Crafting material however drops endlessly, which I've never used because:1. It's never directly explained what you might need it for2. There's tons of different traders scattered over the map that offer you to craft a specific type of item. You'll have to click through the all the vendors/recipes to see what item needs which material, PLUS GOLD.3. If you actually craft something, you'll get an item that is just as useless as the drops you don't care to even look at, and now have lost some gold.Which brings us to the worst part of the economy: Everything costs a lot of gold.Travelling to specific quests, dying, unlocking travelling options, unlocking skill tiers, even just passing time.It's the one resource everything is locked behind, even just getting to a quest location to maybe make enough gold to break even.Every time the game asks you for more gold, It's going to be painful to spend, because it's also tied to your skill tree.It's so annoying that if they removed that resource completely, it would probably make the game flow a lot better. It's just sad.The quests also seem pointless to take on after a while, because a lot of them just fail after a while without notifying you.This is not a bug, just also bad design. Some quests have hidden time limits.They'll stay in your quest log after failing as if nothing happened though, just the quest giver stops being one, and you won't know who it was because he loses his marker.So not only is finding a dungeon not rewarding, even starting a quest will at some point turn into "This will just fail at some point and I'll have to click on random NPCs just to get this out of my quest list."Even for the quests you didn't fail, half the time you won't be able to turn them in by the time you walked back to the quest giver, because he won't be there.The game has a day and night cycle, which effectively just means NPCs disappear for a while and you have to spend gold to pass time to make them reappear.What's bothering me is that it took more work for the devs to screw this up than to just get it right.They added mod support, which could easily fix all these issues.But the game is campaign based, and you'll have to mod it before your playthrough.By the time you notice what you'd want to fix, you probably won't want to throw away your save and start a new campaign.I can't recommend this game right now. Most of these issues could be fixed in a month, but they seem like deliberate decisions, so I doubt they'll be adressed as quickly as a bug.----------------------------Edit:Interesting range of viewpoints here, I didn't expect this (or any) response. Even the steam level seems to matter to the people reviewing reviews.I'll try to adress some responses, matching the tone.Yes, my steam level is 0. I don't know how or why to level up a shopping site, and I don't want to find out.The points I made in the review are the reasons I stopped playing after 7 hours.That's a large amount of free time devoted to one thing (3 full movies worth), enough to form an opinion.It's 7 because I really wanted to like this game, but couldn't. It would be 1 if I was the wrong audience, or 20+ if I loved it.I don't understand how only high hour reviews should be valid. Devs should make the first 2 hours count, and probably aim for less.If you post a 50+ hour negative review, that's a lot of wasted time, and that's on the player, not the game.On the "gold drops are fine/awful/git gud"-debate:What bothered me most about how gold is handled here is that it's a resource I need for upgrading my skills, which is constantly drained by just moving around without even buying anything.I've never run out of it and rarely died, but asking me to spend it inevitably makes me look at what I'm getting for it compared to what I actually want to spend it on.In Hammerwatch 2, I feel like I'm constantly being mugged. Every interaction costs something, even interactions that don't need to exist at all. It stings me, other players don't care since you don't run out.Yet they still argue that it's not badly designed.Most of the positive reviews seem to come from people playing it in multiplayer. Of course backtracking/downtimes aren't as annoying when you're talking with your mates while nothing is happening gamewise.You probably should try the game and ignore the reviews if you've got a group that's interested, it would have been a different experience for me as well.I love the crafting comments.Yes, other games implement crafting badly too. This is the review for Hammerwatch 2.And no, I'm not going on the devs discord to get me interested in using core game mechanics.I've just paid 20€ for the software that was supposed to do that, and it didn't work.To the publisher that responded "loot drops are fixed": a bug that I didn't mention or encounter was fixed, but thanks for actually tracking this.If you like this game, good for you. I envy you guys, since there's very few games that fill this niche.I might check back on this one when there's mods for everything and I stopped caring about the char that I have to delete to use them.
