_childDocuments_.review: It's not a roguelite like Heroes of Hammerwatch but it proves that it doesn't need to be pretty early on. Graphics and sound wise the game is just a strict upgrade from its predecessors. It's not so much of a change that it is jarring but is a noticeably nicer version of the same style.First thing you'll notice is that there are only 5 classes available at the start: Paladin, Rogue, Ranger, Wizard, and Warlock. This seems like build diversity would go down but what you haven't seen yet is that the skill trees are have been massively upgraded. For example, in Heroes of Hammerwatch the Wizard skill tree was 4 active abilities and 3 passives. In Hammerwatch 2 the Wizard has 16 different actives/passives to build from all of which have multiple additional passive sub-perks to upgrade as you see fit for a truly custom experience. The wizard alone has ice, fire, and lightning damage at their disposal and can get other elements through their gear as well rather than every different element requiring an entirely new class to support. There might be half of the classes as Heroes had at the end of its life but each single class is more complex than 2-3 of the old classes combined.The quests are pretty much just as you'd imagine. Go here kill these things or grab this item and bring it back to me. They aren't anything to write home over but they move the game along and get you exploring all the different areas the game has. The game is pretty massive as well and much like a classic Zelda game (think Link to the Past) you'll have massive series of interconnected caves and dungeons with multiple overworld entrances to explore and much more complex puzzles than the previous games had to offer thanks to the nature of the static world rather than a randomly generated one.This game has improved on pretty much every system from the previous games while changing genres from a Roguelite with rpg aspects to a full blown open world rpg and preserving the core feel of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cleaned the game in two sittings, hats off to the developers, they made a terrific game. If you enjoy late 90s PC rpgs, such as Wizardry, or Might and Magic, you're going to have a terrific time with this gem. The world's chalk full of secrets, you find yourself having to read quest text, you gotta remember when things are, where to go. Not every secret you find rewards you with that dopamine hit you might be craving, but hey that's a nice change of pace in my book. The reward is in figuring out the secrets themselves. Combats fun, character progressions great, gear system is neat. It's a passionate love letter to open world PC RPGs of old, wrapped up in modern ARPG combat. There's a lack of "quality of life" features, but honestly, I don't want the same life in every game. Here's a game trying to be different, and I appreciate it. Dying sucked, losing gold was tough, back tracking was time consuming.But it made me play differently, chase different stats, go for the speed buffs. Cool stuff! Looking forward to more campaigns and mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: They've finally added the co-op persistence feature that players have been eagerly anticipating.Imagine the enchanting world of Zelda colliding with the visceral thrill of Diablo in an action RPG that stands out as a masterful fusion of nostalgia and innovation. It's a title that easily earns a remarkable 9 out of 10. The pixel art is a work of pure brilliance, the music strikes the right notes, and the gameplay seamlessly blends elements of looting, crafting, questing, and the grand endeavor of saving kingdoms.While some have voiced minor grievances, the game's strengths overwhelmingly overshadow any purported weaknesses. Speaking as a seasoned gamer with roots tracing back to the 80s, I can attest that certain "issues" raised by critics are, in fact, attributes celebrated in other Steam games but somehow perceived as problematic here. This title thrives on nostalgia but transcends being merely a pixelated Diablo clone. Though it shares some loot mechanics, it primarily delivers an engaging single-player campaign with optional co-op gameplay. The developers are even diligently working on enabling players to seamlessly integrate their characters into others' games, a feature that, while currently unavailable, holds immense promise.Combat is robust, and the debate surrounding the absence of instant dungeon exit teleportation is overblown; exiting dungeons takes a mere 10-20 seconds at most. Personally, I've encountered no bugs, both in the demo and the full version. It exudes the essence of a Zelda adventure with the added depth of Diablo-style leveling and stat management, beckoning players with a wealth of secrets and rewarding exploration. In my estimation, it outshines even Diablo 4 and does so at a significantly more budget-friendly price point. Furthermore, the developers remain actively engaged and responsive to player feedback. I must confess that the negative reviews leave me perplexed. As someone with exacting RPG standards, I find this game truly exceptional. My advice is to disregard the naysayers, give it a try, and if it doesn't align with your tastes, you can always return it. It's as straightforward as that.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: Unleash Hilarious Mayhem in Hammerwatch 2: The Poopocalypse Chronicles!Dear Fellow Gamers,Are you ready for an uproarious adventure that combines strategic combat, quirky humor, and an utterly unique premise? Look no further than "Hammerwatch 2: The Poopocalypse Chronicles." Yes, you read that right – you'll be flinging, splattering, and strategically deploying your, well, unique abilities to overcome challenges and uncover the mystery behind the poopy catastrophe that befell the grand dragon castle.Gameplay That's Both Hilarious and Engaging:Hammerwatch 2 takes the classic hack-and-slash formula and turns it on its head by introducing a range of classes with unconventional, yet side-splittingly funny, combat abilities. _childDocuments_.review: I loved Hammerwatch 1 and Heroes of Hammerwatch but the latest version just isn't as good as the previous titles. $22+ is also pretty steep for what's on offer. NPC schedules don't make the world feel more alive, they just lead to waiting around for shops to open. Similarly, time sensitive quests just lead to frustration. _childDocuments_.review: DEVELOPERS PLEASE READ: Despite this being a thumbs up it's a matter of long term experience that I recommend this game to people. But it still needs work.1. Aesthetically this game achieves a mark much higher than most indie titles, if I were to explain the feeling this game evokes it would be 'Link to the Past' but with crafts and classes. This is a gross oversimplification of what the game is but that is for more casual readers who don't know more specific gaming terms. The controls feel tight, combat is tight, fights can be punishing and the game doesn't roll over unless you build meta. The best way to play is to go in blind with some caveats. Character builds and co-op feel really good when they're running smoothly. If the previous Hammerwatch have proven anything it's that their developers care about making a good product. PLUS- the developer are looking into fixing the co-op issues including how characters migrate to other lobbies.2. This game lacks 'hand holding' to a degree that it can be detrimental. The crafting menus are not intuitive and left me trying to insert key ingredients into the craft UI but in reality I was dropping my inventory on the floor. It's not made clear immediately that potions are permanent and refillable so the variety can be mistaken for being limited consumables that delivers choice paralysis to newer players. Having to assign buttons for things like using your shovel is plain silly and should have a dedicated button somewhere.IN THE GAME'S DEFENSE- this game does have extensive explanations in it's journal. But we shouldn't have to thumb through poorly labeled journal pages for a simple answer of some kind. Please give tools like the Shovel a prompt of it's own as Fishing does.3. Class building is rich and diverse. You can build as mixed or straightforward as you see fit. Admittedly I don't think respec should be attached to an NPC. You should just let players pay the fee anywhere they want and respec on the spot if you so choose. I understand the developer's need to foster more NPC interactions, but as it stands most NPCs are text dispensers with submenus with no real thematic or emotional weight- so the insistence on this is unnecessary.4. Despite Hammerwatch's roots there is no reason to every go backwards in terms of character migration. Co-op should always be first and foremost a fun and responsive experience. The biggest drawback of games like Baldur's Gate 3 and Divinity OS2 is that nobody wants to sit there and slog through an entire campaign while also having to wait on those players to continue. It's archaic, unreasonable and frankly reveals the developer's desires to not allow players to invite high level friends to stomp out the game.It shouldn't be the dev's decision to decide how players tackle that experience- not because their opinion isn't valid but because it denies convenience to players that would otherwise not abuse it. As an artist and writer myself I know what it's like to watch braindead idiots ignore the meat and substance of your work- but if you design around denying those types they'll just cheat or quit the game while we're left to deal with the weights you placed to address them.5. The music can be alarmingly repetitive to the point I need to turn it off only 4 hours in- but what IS there is good if it weren't for the frequency of those loops.6. Enemies get too tanky too quick by the time you leave the first island while also being able to dish out massive damage. I understand the idea behind this but a lot of these enemies are in directed zones for quests available to me. This makes me think the defense and HP values expect multiplayer but don't dynamically scale per-player. Please address the power scaling and design philosophy to remove the tedium of wittling down enemies.7. Summoned companions should just automatically return to you after a set cooldown time and shouldn't occupy a skill prompt. If I chose to get a summon spell that clearly means I want that companion up at all times, so the UI bloat from it isn't needed. Just make companions a passive that upgrades that remains present with a on-death cooldown timer.8. I agree with most reviews that describe an abundance of dead ends and long winding caves/dungeons with nothing much in them minus combat encounters. There's some really good loot in between like Skill/Attribute increases but there could be more gear drops or more world skill nodes for crafting. You could also generate chests that might come back sometimes.9. Increase player movement speed outside of combat encounters. When a player engages an enemy or vice versa, revert them to the stats they have proper. Unless you fill the overlands with more rich content other than site-seeing there's no reason to maintain the pace that it does.All in all I think everyone should buy the game and look at the previous titles- they will listen to feed back and work on this. I can't say this very often about devs, but the track record is strong here.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game. It's got so much going for it that I love. Overall, it feels like a modernization of some of the very first MMOs I played as a kid, and that's a wonderful feeling, and I really looked forward to playing it on the Steam Deck. Where I unfortunately run into problems is saving. The game has autosave, but every time it autosaves, the game freezes. Sometimes it's only a second or two, sometimes up to 5 or 10 seconds. And it autosaves *frequently*. It's completely immersion-breaking, and also makes it tough to maintain the concentration necessary to play any ranged classes, as these require a good bit of kiting to avoid enemy attacks. This wouldn't be a problem if autosave could be turned off in Settings, but there is no option to do so.If either the autosave freezing was resolved, or the Settings menu gets an option to disable autosave, I would wholeheartedly recommend this game. Unfortunately, this single issue renders the game practically unplayable at present.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give a negative review to this game but i have to be honest.I have 300+ hours in heroes of hammerwatch and i always supported the devs, suggesting their games to my friends. You can buy new gear (but most of the times vendors have useless items, if you are lucky you find one good item in all their stash) and potions, but except from that there's not really much to do.- Crafting is useless: not much to say, crafting is mostly a waste of time or a way to complete some specific quest.- Enchanting is useless: you can only enchant item up to the rare/blue level. It's kinda stupid that in late game i find caves with just beetles in it where i find no gold, no items, no secrets. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: Not gonna lie, what is below this edit was technically true, but after what I've experienced on the last patch, you probably should stick with the original or Heroes of Hammerwatch. If I need to use '_cheats\' to properly finish the game, then it is NOT a proper developed game...Not saying it was great before, but it was fun and functional for most of it, again what is below this was true, everything, but you probably should give this one a wide berth for a while until the developers fix its problems...Original: Well, gonna be honest: The game is not bad, it gives exactly what says on the tin, HammerWatch open world, just that (‘-‘). Not saying the game is in neutral because people expected more, which is kind of true, but it has its issues, like an useless crafting system that’s only good to for emergency money and some side quests; some balance kinks for the melee classes with makes the early game much more harder than the ranged counterparts, some technical issues on the multiplayer side (but this ones are being fixed and with the addition of the Persistent Characters, it’s not that much of a problem anymore) and a few bugs here and there, but literally EVERY OPEN WORLD GAME EVER have these, so yeah. Now, should you buy this game? Well if you like HammerWatch and RPG’s in general, probably (‘˽‘) , it’s more of the same and you can have fun with it, the history is not bad and have some humor, you can build any class in several ways and its very fun seeing it become helluva broken, and there is a mod/workshop scene with several adjustments for your taste; but if you just like fantasy games, retro games or open world sandbox games you probably will be disappointed, again it’s not a bad game and the devs are fixing it, but the fact it got the need to be fixed should say that you probably should wait on it for a while, at least until the first DLC for the obligatory desert campaign like the other games (XD) or for any major patch.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Hammerwatch and enjoyed Heroes of Hammerwatch a lot, but this is currently a complete misstep.Going for an open world RPG is fine, in fact it makes sense compared to the other games in the series, but it's done so badly. You die way too easily, and you're punished by paying quite a bit of money to revive and then you have to walk across a massive area to get back to where you died (if you can remember where that was). It's just a way to make the game more grindy as you "freely" lose money and have to travel large distances without any real clear idea of where you've been or caves you've cleared.The level design is generally pretty poor. The first island is basically cut in half and if you're in the south you have to walk almost all the way around west then north to get to the east side. You'll also get caught on all the terrain too easily.I don't really feel any true progression. Yea, you level up, you throw some points in, and yes, you do more damage, but something's just missing from. It just doesn't feel rewarding.Oh, and the "voice acting" is painful. Turn that slider to 0.Maybe some patches (or some good mods) will fix the current glaring issues... we'll just have to wait and see...

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: 8/10I've played the game through once as single player Wizard on normal difficulty using mouse+keyboard, so this review is coming from that perspective.Pros:+Good, smooth, combat system+Graphics are pixelated, but not harsh to look at. Gives a nice retro look+Runs well on Linux+Lots of character customization options in how how to develop your character, all of which are resetable if you don't like the way you built them+Lots of side quests and optional bosses+Plenty of rewards for just going exploring, typically in the form of XP or stat boosts.Cons:-In an extended session, saving takes longer and longer. Should be a fixable bug. Annoying when fighting near a loading zone as it triggers an auto save each time you get close.-Day/Night cycle. The day/night cycle is frustrating when many important NPCs are simply not there or not talkable to during the night. Having to wait until 5am when it is 10pm just to turn in a quest or buy some rope from a shop is annoying.-Timed events. Some story quests, when you turn them in, require you to wait "1 hour" or "a day" to keep progressing the story. Waiting for this is also annoying, especially the short 1 hour ones. Do you wait the 5 minutes at the quest giver? Or do you go off and just barely get to the start of another quest when the next one is ready to start? I normally used these to take a break and go to the bathroom or whatever, but still, not a fun experience.-Stats on items need better explanations. There was so many icons, and they all do different things. What do they do? Well, if you don't know, you have to go to the stats screen and try to find that icon to see what it means. Would be nice to have a better way of showing stats on items that was more immediately clear.Neutral:~Seen lots of complaints about the hidden timers of quests. Don't really think this is an issue, since if you actually read the quest text, I found it obvious which ones were time limited. It would be nice if there was a message for quest failed however.~Multiplayer drop in/out support. Personally, I don't think this game would work very well with that kind of mechanic, due to the nature of being an RPG. What fun is it to have your level 50 friend power through the game for you? I don't see this lack of a feature as a negative, but others do.~I found the difficulty to be fine. I died around 10 times on my playthrough, and that was coming into every fight without knowing any of the enemy mechanics. Death penalty wasn't too severe as gold was fairly plentiful.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game. It's an ARPG, and people in the reviews are claiming it's not because it's not Diablo obviously don't know what an Action RPG is. It feels like Dark Souls and Dragon Quest had a 16 bit baby. It's a significant step up from the original Hammerwatch, and it's clear a significant amount of care and love has gone into this game.As a traditional ARPG, you level up through combat and questing. There are lots of quests, and they are varied enough that I've not felt like I'm doing anything to often. From digging up a lost toy, to wiping out a pirate cove, to painting signs in a cave while trying to find a lost child, there is lots going on and I've found it all to be fun. There are also repeatable quests that are there for some easy money or XP that cover typical fetch/kill quests and so far I've found them useful and not tedious.Levelling up grants you stat and skill points. There are only 3 stats, that primarily govern your HP, Mana, and Stamina so it's not bogged down in this respect. As well as levelling up, classes have 4 tiers that are locked behind both a level cap and purchasing the tier unlock from the relevant NPC. Class skills are separated into 4 tiers of 4 skills based on this. You can invest skill points into skills available based on your class tier, and each skill also has a couple of modifiers that you can invest points into improve the skill in fun/interesting ways. Equipment will have both a stat requirement and a tier requirement.Combat is fun and brutal; if you aren't careful things get out of hand quickly and you will die. Enemies have sufficient logic to feel different from each other, and there are sometimes set pieces (like canons) that the enemies will interact with in combat. There's also lots of traps in dungeons. The death penalty is a percentage of your gold, and although you always have the nearest town as an option, you will get other options like the entrance to a dungeon if you're in one, which is really nice. I don't feel like death is punished harshly, and the penalties of time and money are enough to motivate me without hurting the fun.The graphics are gorgeous, crisp, and beautifully animated. The sound is also fantastic. Exploration is fun and satisfying, with lots of secrets.And all this is in the first scenario. This is a game engine, with a scenario included. There is so much potential for the community to use this engine to create some amazing stuff, and to me that's all just a bonus on top of an already satisfying game.9/10 - Arbitrary score. It's a beautiful, fun, and exciting ARPG. It's not perfect, but it's really good and I'm loving it. The included scenario is a traditional ARPG with a finite story/content. It's also potentially a base for a lot of free content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple and nice, not overly polished game- would probably be even better in multiplayer. Here fast travel mod helps with faster exploration -so you won't get too bored running around. b) Failed one quest due to timer but that increases replay value and immersion also. There are many ways to get that gold. Admittedly fast travel mod helps with it- since you can plan your spending easier and revisit places easy. _childDocuments_.review: I finished game after 25 hours(did only paladin run on normal and got all achievement not including beating the game as “” and other difficulties) and have a lot to say. Overall experience of playing was good, but let’s discuss for a bit.And I want to start with good sides.- The game shows you almost immediately that there is no big ass marker showing where to go like in other games. It pushes you into exploring and thinking which I truly love. Same with quests and some of encounters(but it’s a 50/50 I will return to later)- Progression of your character feels really good, you can see your character becoming stronger.- Game has a lot of things to explore in first couple of hours(6-10)- Equipment feels good to find/collect/improve. When I saw opportunity to craft Dragon Scale Armor it became a goal, a first priority no matter what.- I played as Paladin and it was cool to have combinations of your passive skills, enchantments on weapons and armor, I can’t speak about other classes cuz I just didn’t play them.- I like an idea of shops located in different places(for example you can craft keltonite armor only in Sild and shiny beetle armor in Scalem)- Graphics and animations. They look really good except loading screens(wtf)Let’s discuss bad sides- 50/50, time limited quests in this game have no markings or any other signs of it being time limited. I love exploring but game just don’t care sometimes. When I see another “Mystery cave” I am like “okay, I will get nothing 99%”- Enchantment system is complicated and there is some obvious enchantments like poison, cuz they require wasp stingers, but how the hell am I supposed to know what troll skin or wolf liver or archon essence will do. Yeah there is official wiki rn, but in first day it wasn’t there. It would be okay if I could easily enchant another less valuable item and see what enchantment each material gives. Every time when I was loading a location and saw loading stop on first move I was like “not ♥♥♥♥ again, like, bruh, it’s 10th time it’s happening cmon”That’s it. I can’t recommend somebody pay 20$ for this, the game don’t worth that much.-------------Upd: thanks for reading all this stuff :)I am well aware of fast travel via boat or carriage. But a lot of backtracking locations are pretty far from any city you can travel to. I am not against walking but after hours and hours it can get not that interesting.Looking forward for future updates so I will complete the game playing other classes.

_childDocuments_.review: Hammerwatch 2 IS a great game, it's an addictive action RPG ( loot, skills, progression, ect. ) with some open world exploration, all set in a ridiculously cozy and stunning pixel art world. The music is absolutely amazing, and I appreciate them continuing that tradition from the prior game. I loved the first game, so this is a no-brainer for me, and you better believe I'll be checking out that Anniversary Edition. The primary issues involve the game not allowing you to transfer your singleplayer character over to multiplayer, having to stand there and wait AWHILE for time to pass to even talk to some NPCs because of the obnoxious day/night cycle, the difficulty seeming to be way too difficult for solo play ( remember to block, Paladins ), and you can't progress as smoothly since there is more an emphasis on exploration so you'll end up finding caves or dungeons that don't progress the game or only progress side quests. I mean, I seem to die a lot with my Paladin, making me wonder if I did something wrong with my build. However, I'm still having a wonderful time if I keep on my toes, and it's a great alternative to other action RPGs out there. But please, this is one of those instances where you need to read the Steam reviews rather than look at the "All Reviews" rating and percentage. I wish there was more than just thumbs up or thumbs down, like "informational" or "consider before you buy". I like solo play, so the issues people are having don't quite resonate with me as much. This is why you need to read reviews first before making a judgement about how good or bad a game is. Heck, there's even the ability to have custom campaigns, which is awesome unto itself. With that in mind, Hammerwatch 2 is a great game and a good platform for other campaigns to be built upon. But please, if you want to play multiplayer or you loved playing the original with friends, consider the issues people are having first with the multiplayer and day/night cycle. Updates will very likely improve this game over time. _childDocuments_.review: Disappointed and I'm going to go ahead and ask for a refund sadly.I can live with some of the features choices, this is not *Heroes* of Hammerwatch II and I get that. I was actually really prepared for a somewhat more linear adventure to experience with my friends (altho I do want HoH II one day).However, sadly I found the game too buggy to play. Lots of freezes and a few crashes later and I've lost hope. My computer is well above the recommended specs and I've tried every setting can. It's outrageous and I'm not exaggerating when I say it's unplayable for me. I'm glad that not everyone has had this experience but I can see from other reviews I'm not alone.Outside of that here's my thoughts from having played for basically 1 hour:Class Design is pretty good (but for all their talk of flexibility they could have easily gone much further and I'm a little surprised by some of the limitations)Dungeon design is pretty goodThe new loot system seems fun (tho I saw very little of it)Some of the crafting elements seem pretty cool (but I saw very little)On the other hand:The UI is very bad, very hard to readDifficulty curve is out of control, even on easy with people who have played the other games we were like "woah this feels kinda hard" for the short time we could keep it workingIn general for a game that was "designed for co-op" it feels like it would play better singleplayer, which is not what I wanted or signed up forEDIT: One more thought, if you're going to leave a positive review please don't discount how many of us are experiencing game-breaking bugs. I'm tired of seeing positive reviews that act like the only things to quibble about are design choices. They released a game with serious QOL issues that aren't affecting everyone but are real and again, were completely game-breaking for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Heroes of Hammerwatch (more than 300 hours on this game gem).Hammerwatch 2 is not a Rogue-lite but an open world RPG ? Why not I was waiting for it !I played solo with Thief until the final boss.Good points :- pixel art graphism are amazing, there is a lots of animated environment, lights effects are great.- fight mecanics are as good as older Hammerwatch games, I love this kind of nervous shoot/dodge fights with pretty simple controls,- skills tree with enough promises so I wanted to explore them all.Bad points : - inventory is complex for bad reasons, we loot so much things we don't even know what to do with. _childDocuments_.review: My previous review talked about crashing on death reloads, but I figured out that the game sometimes just takes a REALLY LONG TIME to load for some reason. Like at least a minute. I haven't experienced such long load times in a while, and it's crazy that it's from a 2D pixel game. This game needs to be optimized ASAP.That aside, I finished the game on default difficulty as a wizard.I did have a lot of fun, but some aspects of the game were frustrating. For one, like another review mentioned, some quests are time-gated. For no real reason, really. This didn't add anything to the game. And the game does not inform you that you failed the quest until after you meet the NPC again. Why?There's no "true" map to open to actually see where you are and what path you should take. A lot of traveling is learning locations, which some might like, but I found it annoying more often than not. Fast traveling is limited to towns, and the time you REALLY need it (like leaving a dungeon), it is just not there. Backtracking is very annoying, and learning the maze-like layouts of each dungeon can be stressful.The day-night cycle is beautiful, but putting NPCs on schedules was unnecessary. This also didn't feel like it added anything. It doesn't fit the context of the game. Like Skyrim this works because it makes sense in the context of the game, but here it just doesn't. The game isn't that complex or immersive to warrant a system like this, it just seems like an arbitrary obstacle because it "sounded cool".Combat was excellent, but the hotbar is so invisible in combat. You can't sneak a peek at your cooldowns because that split second may mean being hit by an attack and dying. Having the option to see cooldowns next to your character during combat would really help.Crafting may as well not have even existed. There never was a point where crafting anything would've helped progress the game. You can only upgrade armor and weapons to blue tier (there's white, green, blue, purple, and orange), so why bother? The only thing I crafted were a few potions, which can be refilled for free, which is GOOD don't get me wrong, but it also meant I just have a few thousand flowers that I have nothing to do with. And if there was anything hidden to craft that was like a legendary weapon or something, there wasn't anything in place to hint at it. No NPCs saying, "Hey, that material looks mighty unique, maybe X can make something out of it!"You also pay a percentage of your gold to resurrect when you die. I think it's roughly 20% of your entire gold balance. This meant that selling things was POINTLESS unless I had literally no money. I should be EXCITED to sell the cool golden goblet I just picked up, but instead I begrudgingly hoarded it because I might lose all the profit I made from it on my next death. It would've been cool to sell everything and be super rich, but the game punishes you for it if you die. Not that death shouldn't ever be punishing, but to this extent that it makes gathering gold feel pointless? It should be a flat value based off of your level or something, and then just cost nothing if you have 0 gold left.So why am I recommending the game despite all of these grievances? Mainly because there's no middle option. But besides that, I recommend it because despite everything, I did have fun beating the game and completing most of the content. The combat was satisfying, the story was basic but tongue-in-cheek, the graphics were absolutely stunning, and finding out secrets was fun.All that's missing is a wiki to detail all of the quests I was unable to finish due to ignorance, because that's going to annoy me forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Finished main campaign in ~27h playing as a ranger. It is the best Hammerwatch game to date, the world, exploration, combat, character development, everything is improved compared to previous games. I can easily recommend it and I hope that we will see a lot of new content being added in the future. If you buy it and enjoy it, I recommend leaving a positive review. It's a shame that a game this good has received such a negative response. Ofc It is not a perfect game and below I tried to summarize my experience more in depth. Few key topics that are being discussed in other reviews:1. Bugs - I didn't encounter any, maybe I was lucky, maybe they fixed most of them2. Day/night cycle - IMO It adds flavor to the game and makes it more interesting. First, you can plan your day ahead and go explore somewhere during the night just to come back to open shops in the morning. In the case of death (which causes time skip) you can go to the tavern and sleep so I really don't get all the hate that this system is receiving. Even if you need to wait just an hour you can go to the church and pay for sleep per hour. Some people also argue that sleeping is too expensive which I also disagree with, because if you pay attention during exploration you can get more than enough gold for daily expenses (sleep, food). The only gripe that I have is that there should be some NPCs that come out only during the night, so it would be more interesting to explore towns in different time3. Multiplayer - didn't play, don't know4. Not clear quest description - It encourages exploring and the world is small enough that finding the thing needed is usually quite simple/fast. Additionally, (usually) you can go do other things if you get stuck and return later. There are a few timed quests but they are definitely not hard to complete. I never found myself being stuck/wanting to look on the wiki.Now few things that I found annoying/unfinished:1. Inventory management could be improved by a lot. For example: simple filters to switch between EQ types (accessories, weapons, armor); button to sort items by the rarity;consumables divided by ones that you can actually eat and mats only; place to store items for other characters/builds would also be nice. Mainly QoL stuff. 2. Something to spend the money on in the late game. If you know the game making a lot of money is easy enough and it would be nice to have something to spend it on for example: item gambling. 3. Main quest: 3. Location of the Master tier trainer. I didn't have to respec many times, but I can imagine it getting annoying after a while. Imo the NPC should travel to one of the cities after being discovered. 4. MINOR: Description of spells, effects etc could be placed in a better spot. You can find them in the Combat Mechanics menu but it would be easier to just hover over said effect and read the description. Some items also were confusing for me, for example: %dmg/%crit modifier on a weapon only affect said weapon slot (main/offhand) but on accessory it affects all slots (I played ranger with only offhand so main hand weapon was for stats only).5. I'm not a big fan of the music, it often felt uninspiring and not appropriate for the moment. Combat sounds were also lacking, especially when it comes to hitting/slaying enemies. It would be great if the combat sounded more like an rpg than hack'n'slash.Now the things that I liked:1. Class progression is great. Like I said I finished the game with ranger, but I'm already doing my second run with paladin. I really like the unique weapons each class have and the fact that you can optimize your build for each of them. For example ranger can be build as a Dexterity based, single target, ranged, heavy-hitter but also can be made into a Strength based melee brawler running with the wolf(s) companion(s). Each build feels complete and can be also mixed together depending on what is needed. 2. Items. Finding epics with just the right stats for your build, or dropping something that inspires you to change your talents feels great and I found it many times during my play through. 3. Crafting is also good, you can make simple upgrades for an early game boost or you can go wild with the enchanting, which was one of my main gold sinks during late game. I really liked trying to optimize crafted accessories for desired build. One thing I would like to see is the ability to craft some unique, higher quality items, which would require some hard to gather materials (maybe from mini-bosses?). Crafting food is also okay for a regen/stat/dmg buff, but I found myself wanting more variety (maybe specific regen buffs, resistance for specific dmg type, crit modifiers, mana increase?)4. Exploration. When playing for the fist time everything felt fresh and I was eager to explore every cave and talk with every NPC. I imagine that the novelty will run out with future runs, but the world is still gorgeous to look at. Some locations (especially regarding side-quests) are random generated and their entrance might be in a different place, but it still doesn't change that much. I personally don't mind that, but I would like to see more of the hand-crafted world. I hoped that the frozen and desert zones would be exploitable in such depth as the main island, but that turned out to be a disappointment.5. Combat (non-bosses). I personally like the change from "endless" waves of enemies to less but tougher ones. It makes combat slower and more thoughtful, which suits me well. I understand that people that expected HW1/HoH type of combat might be disappointed but IMO it is a change in the right direction because (with the other systems in mind) it allows for a better flush out combat system. it also allows for enemies to have more dangerous abilities, because it is easier to track the specific animations/clues. Great change for me, would love to see more variety though.6. Combat  (bosses). I enjoyed every boss fight that i went through. Some of them more challenging than others but I really liked that none of them seemed the same. Each boss have their own unique mechanics which are thematically appropriate for that kind of mob, which is great if you are preparing for the first time for said fight. 7. Quests. I really liked the quest system, both with its ambiguity and progression. There are also few quests that are totally optional and require player to follow through/investigate on their own, which was great. The story is not something that you will be thinking about for the coming weeks but it gets the job done and also is interesting enough that you want to keep going. I only wish there were more side-quests related to other than main factions. So in summary I really liked the game and will probably replay it at least a few times to enjoy each class (which I am already doing). I really hope that this kind of format will be developed further and that we will see additional content being published in the coming months (years?)

_childDocuments_.review: Was recommended this game by a friend and was perplexed by the mixed reviews. Turns out, it's a very smooth, action-packed game. The graphics and music are a delight, especially if you've grown up on SNES games. Fights are intense (more like Path of Exile than, say, Secret of Mana) and challenging, but not too hard. Money is pretty plentiful, I can't really relate to those who says everything is expensive. Leveling and character building is fun and rewarding, even with fairly limited skill options (reasonably limited if you're not expecting anything like PoE). The crafting system gives you options to get really good stuff if you take a minute to familiarize yourself with it. For example, one merchant in a small village specializes in crafting armor made out of various scales. I had cleared the sewers when I found him, so I had enough monstrous bug scales for a full set, which was a huge improvement that I easily could have missed. Boss fights are carefully crafted, mechanically rich, and much more interesting than in for example Diablo 3 (haven't tried D4 yet). They also always give you a unique item, often with a new skill attached. Six such charms (think D2) can be equipped at any time, which is a brilliant enrichment of the build variety.  Running from point A to B can be a bit tedious sometimes, though it's really not a huge map. You never need more than a minute, and I don't even bother with the fast travel coach service. Running to the exit of a cleared dungeon seems to be a pet peeve for many, and it's a fair criticism. The devs are looking into it, though.All in all, a charming indie title. Looking forward to trying multiplayer, should be a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a fun, interesting, and unique game.  While I understand the complaints of: No fast travelNPCs sleepingHard to make gold when you are still learning the gameNot every cave is its own mini-dungeon with a mini-boss and lootquests aren't always complete-able I don’t believe these are well thought-out complaints. I haven’t played any of the previous games, So I didn’t come into this game with any preconceived ideas about what the game-play should be like. In-fact the negative reviews that pointed out these points actually helped convince me to purchase it.   I think most of the bad reviews are from a product to audience mismatch rather than bad game-design. The game is an interesting blend between rouge-like, rpg, and arpg. It sits right in the middle between a hardcore game with survival mechanics and a casual game with any distraction removed.The lack of fast travel is meant to make each skirmish feel like more a true journey. Yes you will spend time back tracking, however you may see something you didn’t see the first pass through, a secret area or an alternate route. You might discover a cave entrance while taking a short-cut back to town. These design decision make the game world feel bigger, more real and more lived in. A more casual game would create a portal where the end of quest boss dies to teleport you directly back to the quest giver. A more hardcore game would require you to prepare for the journey as well. Buy food, make sure you are rested, stocked up on healing supplies and spell ingredients. Hammerwatch 2 tries to find a balance. It’s not hardcore, but it’s not completely casual either.  If it leaned more heavily into the hardcore survival aspects, people wouldn’t be complaining about NPCs sleeping and having to walk more. However the casual gamer would be even more frustrated by the tedium of having to eat and sleep etc. If the game leaned more into the casual aspects with no day/night cycle and town portals and giving the player more gold than they need. Then the game would feel more dull and uninspired. Games need to make certain things tedious so when you do get a pay out it feels earned.  The developers will have to be very careful in how much they listen to these reviews and what they change based on this feedback. If they follow the suggestions exactly they risk diminishing what makes the game special and unique. While the complaints may have a sliver of truth in them. They are not criticisms from sophisticated game designers so what they are attributing as causing them frustration, is timed quests. However the real issue is the game making it appear like the timed quest was even important to begin with, and not-completing it is a bad thing. Time is limited and you have to make a choice with how you spend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thoroughly enjoying this game. I understand its a significant deviation from the last release, but I enjoy the direction taken.I think there are a few things that can be done to improve the game. For one, there isn't a quick-leave dungeon. Your account also seems to be locked to save which I was disappointed to see. So much time is invested into one character, its unfortunate that its scenario locked.Those complaining about a lack of gold haven't progressed past the beginner island, I usually don't know what to do with my money I have so much.The loot table may need some adjustment, but generally high tier loot is attached to certain bosses and quests.I recommend exclusively following quest linesTL;DR Fun game. Change in direction is fun and adds more variety. Plenty of QoL updates missing, and maybe rethink item drops.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugs and mechanics making the game needlessly tedious are killing the experience.The worst:Game soemtimes crashes when changing locations. Not a huge problem unless you forgot to save. Need an autosave feature with multiple save slots. I do not care about multiplayer so will not refer to that.Weird mechanics and lack of well established ones in the genre:- unable to move around the minimap to check what has not been explored yet, It only moves with the character.- global map does not show what got explored already,- quests do not show who gave the quest and where on the map,- crafting is confusing,- day/night cycle and npcs going to sleep, no wait option other than sleeping in the tavern for money (useless money sink),- violet areas that make the explored area on the local map reset, just stupid, like someone has had an oh ho  have a cool idea and lets make it without thinking about the golden rule being if it will make the game more fun. It does not,- grapling hook appears to late in the game, so you will need to revisit all the places you have been to once you get it. Boooring.- no waypoint teleport system to travel around explored areas,- no return to town spell,- weird menu where you mneed to toggle between tabs rather than assigning specific key to then (like i for inventory),- no putting notes on the map,- universal keys that you have to buy in a number. Better make more hidden switches and specific keys only,Finally - no necromancer with skeletons that do not dissapear after a few seconds... A big one. This game is perfect for a necro with minions like in diablo 2.The good:Without the issues above the game would me much more fun than diablo series really. I had a lot of fun but just got burned out.The game is a blast just not polished fully. It really requires some dialogue with the players before it is playable and enjoyable.I also love the fact that the game requires you do fogure out things on your own rather than just putting a marker to the goal. That is very retroish and cool.Will wait for news from the devs and once stuff gets fixed will gladly flip to 'recommended'.

Loot drops arbitrarily, crafting is poorly explained (seriously, why can I spend all my crafting materials at a guy and only get one kind of armor my character doesn't have stat proficiencies to equip?)All around disappointing, especially given the history of the franchise and the beautiful palette. I'd love to play this game, once it's fixed. I might even be willing to recommend it to my friends someday - a party of four in HoH was a blast, and I imagine this game could, someday, be just as fun. Once it's retuned.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this game Plenty of chances to meet my expectations. In my first save, after I defeated the thief boss, I was unable to leave the room after he died. He was supposed to drop a specific key that was needed to exit the area. No key, no exit.After deleting the save, I created another character. This time, I created a persistent character to make sure my progress wouldn't be for nothing. While exploring the Spider Cave, I ran into yet another impassable bug: there was no Spider Boss room.In both of these instances, I found out that many other players were experiencing the same game-breaking issues. _childDocuments_.review: I love the game but I've become fairly bored and frustrated, and it didn't take long.I was so happy the game was out and I was happy playing it until it's flaws became far too apparent. The main flaw of this game is that it's maps are terrible: They are mostly the same 3 enemies over and over with no distinctive features aside from the occasional brittle wall hiding loot that might be exciting and might not. They are rife with dead-ends and often unrewarding. You would think I'm only talking about the randomly generated maps, but the designed maps that are the same on every play through have the same flaws somehow. Character progression is really fun, the combat is fun too when I haven't been fighting the same 3 trolls in an endless crawl through some pointless caves that are full of dead-ends and missed opportunities. I think some clever modders will find some ways to spice up the maps. But I don't think the game should be using mods as a crutch. There's no town portal, so when you hit another dead end on another pointless cave map you just have to walk back the way you came.

_childDocuments_.review: Review bombing is a seriously bad habit the Steam community has gotten into.Upon launch, the game lacked a persistent save, which the developers implemented IMMEDIATELY. The game is more story-based but you can ignore most dialogue if you just want to dungeon delve. Complaints of having to walk out of dungeons seem to be nit-picky because dungeons will always connect with other dungeons, or take two minutes to walk out of to collect missed loot or kill respawned enemies for extra exp.Give the game a try. It's gorgeous and fun and it's a shame it will always have its scar of bad reviews because of an oversight on launch.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. I'm playing on the hardest difficulty, and although I am save scumming because it is unforgiving, I'm having a blast. I love how every level up feels important, every piece of gear you get can be game changing, the spells feel satisfying to use, and it's worthwhile to use everything you have at your disposal. Most games of this kind, I find a few skills I think are pretty good, and end up pumping all my points into them, and using only said skills, but this game is incredibly well thought out, forcing me to decide if I want more survivability, more straight damage, or to start leveling up a new skill that adds something completely new at my disposal. It's a rare sight, and feels very tight and well polished.The story is interesting enough to keep me going, but all it really is, is fuel for the fire. That fire being my need to go slay massive hordes of enemies. And the hordes are great, not just cannon fodder. I'm always making sure my position is advantageous so I don't get swarmed, double checking that I have potions or buffs so I don't run out of stamina or mana while stuck in a corner. And then bossfights require a different approach, since bosses hit hard and move fast, it's not just about positioning, but timing my dodges perfectly, while avoiding at times a bullet hell, or a large attack. It feels very rewarding getting through a boss fight, or a portion of the game where the enemies are thicker than Kim K's artificial ass. While I understand the issues people have with the game, and bugs are unfortunate, the game itself is just incredibly fun (and I've played the previous Hammerwatch games, Chronicon, Grim Dawn, and dozens of other top down RPG's and shooters and roguelikes, so I feel like my opinion is somewhat valid, yet this game had me counting down the days till release, instead of playing any of those). Now about the issues people seem to be having-The way I play multiplayer games with friends, the fact that I have a character tied to playing with my friends directly isn't really an issue, since I have a character dedicated to playing with a certain friend or friend group, and I do most of my progress solo since my friends aren't always online. It would be nice to have a borderlands drop in drop out type system, but I guess it wasn't in the devs vision to balance around people at different levels in different parts of the game trying to play together. Hopefully the devs find a way to work this out, or mods fix it. I'm thoroughly enjoying this game solo, and that alone is honestly worth your time.And regarding the time mechanic, there's a fast travel mod that moves time ahead by 8 hours, which basically lets you sleep for free. Lots of "amazing" games are nothing without their mods, and honestly this game has way less issues than most, with the time mechanic, and losing money on death, being some of the few mechanics I don't like, but those are the only 2 glaring issues I see. And there's nothing wrong with using mods to fix something you don't like in a game, to make it more your style, especially with how phenomenal the mod support for this game is, it's more than worth the buy just to see what talented modders will come up with for this game.Also, these devs have plenty of time to fix and balance the things people don't like, it's not like this is abandonware, the devs just released it and I'm sure all the kinks will be ironed, or modded out. I'm so sad to see such an amazing game being ♥♥♥♥ on for just a couple of issues that aren't even related to the core game being amazing. So many triple A titles come out barely playable, meanwhile an indie team drops this ABSOLUTE GEM of a game, and people latch on SO hard to the negatives, while the game itself is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome! Like, from the negative reviews I've seen, I don't see any complaints about the game itself? And yet it's sitting at mixed? That's beyond unfair, in my opinion. Anyways, that's the end of my essay, long story short, BUY THIS GAME, if you like RPGS, if you like top down games, or if you like killing hordes of enemies and challenging boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Diablo 4.5! Sadly, loud comparison also comes with a lot of bugs and weird decisions. I am refunding this game, for quite a few reasons:1. As stated in various reviews already, multiplayer is a problem. You have to create a new character every time you join a different stranger. This totally kills all the fun. 2. Items disappear when droped on the ground. I mean, if you drop an item from your inventory, you don't see it on the ground, but other players do see it. This is extremely weird, because it does not apply to gold drops. Which leads to the next point.3. You can drop any amount of gold, but the gold will be dropped right under your feet. If you move, you will instantly pick it back up.4. Items randomly disappear for no reason. I bought a blue bow for my ranger. Wanted to try enchanting, but once I put the bow into the enchantment box, the bow was gone. Not in my inventory, not dropped, just gone.5. Generally weird UI. Quest overlay is totally missing. Tedious to track what you need to do. Map overlay is awful - too bright. 6. Overheats the video card of my potato laptop for some unknown reason. To be fair, Baldur's gate 3 on Ultra settings does not do that.  If you are looking for a good co-op ARPG, than it is not your game. As for the single-player experience, I wouldn't still recommend it for the current price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great retro-feeling RPG. A lot of these negative reviews are really weird and baseless and totally disregard the design choices of this entry - like a lot of these are positives for me. No waypoint on the map, you have to use geographic/geologic landmarks. No quest marker, you actually have to read the quests to determine where to go, and no fast-travel makes you explore the world. These are immersive design choices, not a malicious exploit to pump up game time metrics, frustrate you, or as a personal slight... The terminally-online cynicism has prevented legions of people from just enjoying things. Music is fun, classes are classic, gameplay is simple and straight forward but skills allow some really interesting and fun game play. The itemization is deep enough to be interesting, but not so deep where you are spending a long time reviewing items. Plenty of side quests, things to craft, potions to make, and systems to break for god-mode.Hard is HARD, I would recommend starting on normal until you understand some mechanics.Multiplayer saves are MULTIPLAYER SAVES, which is EXACTLY how these types of multiplayer games HAVE ALWAYS WORKED. People thumbing the game down for NOT UNDERSTANDING SAVE-GAME MECHANICS THAT HAVE EXISTED FOR LITERALLY 25 YEARS are the reason online-reviews should have a writing and reading comprehension exam before posting. Host machine retains the save file. How is this so difficult to understand?

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adored the original. This, however, hasn't been implemented very well. There is no overlay tab or the option for one for quests. Meaning, in order to check quest progress, you must go into inventory, then to the quests tab, then to the specific quest to see the details. Seeing as though you get 5 quests offloaded onto your character right from the beginning, this would get annoying fast. There is also no way to change the positioning of the health/mana/exp bars. The massive walls of dialogue, without voice-acting, is off-putting. The story isn't captivating enough thus far to engross me in pop-up text blocks.  I've just finished playing Grim Dawn for like £10, so maybe I'm subconsciously comparing. With this in mind, it feels that the entertainment (bar combat) to be derived from this game is based on playing multiplayer (which, judging from other reviews, has its own unique issues). The soundtrack and graphics are what I expected; I adore the pixel art-style and the music appeased my nostalgia. Combat is fantastic, albeit pretty much unchanged from the original. I see great potential, however first thoughts of the beginning village (and one of the NPCs violently shaking as another NPC runs past them) leads me to believe that this has been released without proof-checking. Other reviews seem to remark similar about glitches previously reported not being addressed. With this in mind, I've had to refund the game. I will be overjoyed to witness an update that addresses some of these issues, but for now; not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good, and there's fun to be had with a group of friends. Unfortunately exactly that is the case, since it's quite impractical to play this game with a pug of random people like it was in the other two games. They opted for a more long term open world approach instead of a match based one, and the gameplay and combat reflect that slower pacing significantly. An unfortunate example of this would be the lack of the combo mechanic; it was cool, I miss it.Obviously like any recent release of any computer game nowadays, unfortunately, there are bugs; and if you want to avoid those then wait a year before playing, like you should with any computer game, and which is what I typically do. I knew I would enjoy the game enough regardless of the new-game issues to disregard that typical practice in this case, and it hasn't disappointed, mostly... of my complaints with the game stem from the actual class design compared to what they were in the other two games. In particular, my favorite three classes: the priest, sorcerer, and wizard.Both the priest and sorcerer are entirely missing in this game, so there's not much else to say about those two... and the wizard feels like a hodge podge of ideas cobbled together, and has significantly lost its identity. The wizards basic abilities have been redesigned into "arcane" skills that can have their element determined by what weapons you're equipped with, including what your primary spell actually is. Gone is the big radius explodey fireball, and in its place is a pseudo explodey ball that can be either fire, ice, or lightning element; Fire breath is completely gone for unknown reasons; Blast wave is now an optional spell choice determined by your offhand weapon; And meteor is the same I guess? Then for their passive effects: flame shield has been redesigned into a preemptive spell instead of a passive reactive effect, and the free blast wave is gone, and the burning ground effect has been turned into a boring firewall spell, which has a needlessly long cooldown and is the only actual fire spell they get other than meteor, meaning they don't have a low cooldown fire spell at all if we don't count the grimoire spells.Aside from those bastardizations of the iconic wizard things, since they now also have ice and lightning features included into them, those features were essentially gutted from the other two classes that had them: warlock doesn't have lightning stuff anymore and feels a little worse for it I think, and as mentioned sorcerer doesn't exist. Instead, wizard now has an arc lightning in place of the warlock's ball lightning, and frost nova; both of which are low cooldown, which further makes me ponder why firewall has such a long cooldown.  Meteor has a modifier for it called Comet that makes it do ice damage, so that's totally still in the game... totally no differences there...Paladin is mostly the same except with some cool fire stuff added. The notable complaints there are that the shield block is an activated effect instead of passive, and lay on hands has another needlessly long cooldown.Ranger has the option of a melee build now, but in my experience it's extremely weak currently so you shouldn't bother. Just spec bow basic attack and delete the screen.Warlock is practically a new class, so you'll either like that new class or you won't.Rogue is essentially the same, except with the same kind of issues that every class is plagued with.A good thing shared by all the classes, except wizard, would be the addition of the Str/Int/Dex stat system that allows you to actually feel like you can spec your character and have one character be different from another of the same class. Unfortunately it's a little limited and needs to be fleshed out more in my opinion. Wizard can only practically spec Int of course... The bad shared by all the classes would be the janky feel of trying to do anything other than a basic attack build, because so many of the abilities have needlessly long cooldowns, or bad feeling activations like channel times. TLDR: It's good, but not the same gameplay as the other two, so don't expect it to be, especially from wizard.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I do want to say the pixel art is gorgeous, the music is amazing, combat is fun, I'm only being hard on this game because Heroes of Hammerwatch (I know this isn't a roguelike but  the inventory systems, maps, and lots of other details can be and should be compared, saying "well this is how it was 10 years ago, doesn't cut it, things should be better this time around, not less features) was one of my all time fav games and I played it constantly with friends and had a blast.  I really just want this game to be the best it can be.  If I didn't care I just  would not post or even review the game.  A lot of  this stuff might seem like nitpicking but it's a microcosm of the whole game, there's just a lot of work that needs to be done on some of these systems to make this a smooth experience for new users and old alike. Again, I love the game style and direction, the art and music, the combat, I just want it to be as good as it can be.Why do my potions lose all charges when I drag them off my inventory bar. I have my 3 potions with 3 charges, but as soon as I move one into my inventory, boom the charges vanish, if I move all 3 of them off guess what? No more potion charges? why? Is this a bug?  My friend says he can see my potion has 3 charges but mine show 0 and I can't use them.The keys don't bind right, it always adds a n extra keybind that I have to remove manually and it takes like 2-3 times. Don't even get me started on binding food to your hotkeys, it's clunky and badPlease let us change where our health bars, etc; are on the screen, having them on the left and right is just bad, especially on bigger monitors, but even as a dev rule. You never put important info on the far left and right sides of screens, especially when you need to read them all the way vertically, people with big monitors have trouble seeing them and it's just bad.  There are small health bars on the character themselves (they don't show you numbers or %'s so it's difficult to actually see what they are at, but at least let us change where these big ones go/are.  There is an option to display details on your cursor but it looks ugly and I don't need more clutter on my cursor. Let us change out cursor size, color, and type.  Would make it easier in combat for aiming and QoL and so users don't have to use 3rd party mouse apps.Why do the vendors sell 4, 5, or 6 of the same item?  Just have 1 stack, this is bad UI design. And I can't sell my gear to any vendor, it has to be a specific weird vendor that's spread out all over the map with no icons so you have no clue what each vendor even sells or is, make me be able to just sell everything to one vendor, make it easy on the player not harder.  It's anti-fun, again, ask yourself, is this fun for the player? If the answer is no, then why include it in the game at all.  Esp with so many item menus and useless items in the game.The inventory system needs an overhaul, have jsut 1 inventory where we can filter / sort, or a materials bag in our main inventory.  The inventory system needs another pass for sure.Why can I have 6 cloaks on? Why not just have a cloak slot.  What even are the 6 weird slots for, what can even go in there? 6 rings? 6 cloaks? like why, just have a ring slot and cloak slot, what's the point of this? And why do I have to put each stack of 3 potions in a new inventory slot?  Inventory system is ham fisted, clunky and not that well thought out. I can bind a carrot to my inventory but can't see it in the top left - i have 2 slots, just for potions? 3 stacks of 3 potions? why? Just give us 1 potion we can upgrade, why give us the ability to craft multiple 3 stacks or potions at all if you want to balance the game around 1 stack of potions, just give us 1 stack.Why can't I see what I bind? Carrots, etc; anything, potions, it's a mystery. If you I can buy 3 potions and all use them, let them stack, or only let us buy 1 stack of 3 potions or whatever, why can I buy 10 stacks of potions if I can't even stack them. A ping systems would be nice, it's not Elden Ring, you're not going for a minimal UI here, give us some options to communicate. It's simple but an effective way for us to communicate in battle and in maps. The game has trouble with progression. it's all over the place, so many vendors all spread out, you don't know who does what, who sells what, some don't buy your stuff,. I've got so many quests, no clue where the hell all of them all, the maps are not detailed, there's no quest markers, not that we NEED quest markers but there's just so much text happening and the lack of mini map and the ability to zoom out with nothing detailed like what each locations are called makes quest hunting and resolution difficult and cumbersome. What does training adept again even do? Lack of tooltips again.  It just   said train adept, great, then retrain adept, what does it even do?, Adept did not give me access to any skill points or anything so what does it change if I retrain? Lack of tooltips, again.  We also need tool-tips to explain what everything does and all modifiers do. It's a straight up mystery you make the players work for to figure out what all the modifiers do by their tiny little icon. Un-fun at it's peak.  Let us hit a button to display a cursor and mouse over the icons with a nice tooltip telling us what it does and affects.  HUGE QoL improvement to new players and old alike, this is an EASY win. Can't use my pre-existing character in a new game? I think this is getting fixed, thankfully.Lack of fast travel is really struggling.  So many useless dungeons with nothing at the end of them, and I just have to walk all the way back at the end with no fast travel or town portals. Waiting for 45 minutes just to use the damn fast travel boat, day/night cycle is stupid. Add a town portal for damns sake, make our lives easier not harder. I know you can sleep at the inn but it costs money, if you have no money, you can't sell to a vendor because it's night time, it's jsut BAD. Also it's a a game FULL of magic, give us a town portal please.  A lot of the early cave dungeons are just empty and badly designed, give us something, throw us a bone, make them interesting.  Hopefully this gets better as I play it more but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ the early caves are jsut boring. Let us zoom out the map overlay, let us have a minimap, let us see where we are on the big minimap, the large game map is pretty much useless, I guess you might need a sextant for that, than maybe explain that to us? Or just include it from the start?  There's no quest tracker on screen that we can toggle either, than make the interface somewhat manageable so it's easier for the player.  Edit* I found the sextant after 6 hours*Day/Night cycle is really dumb, can't sail to the previous town ever because it's never "the right time" just let us sail... I waited 50 minutes in game time last night just to use the vendor to said to the next town, I guess there's an INN but it costs gold and as I explained, this is tedious. The towns are disorganized and clunky.  There's vendors all over the place, you can't even see what crafting materials you need, there's no vendor icons,  you have to click on each vendor and remember exactly what vendors need what, and even if you do craft, the items are useless. The game needs 6 months in the oven more at the very minimum. It's just so unorganized, the direction is lacking, the systems are clunky, it's just not fun right now, my friend and I played for 6 hours and we were confused the entire time about what the hell was going on what progression was needed, what island we had to go with.  Did we finish the last island or not, dozens of weird little caves right zero rewards and just the same caves each time that we have to back track all the way out of wasting our time.Will revisit this review as they hopefully fix things in the game but right now it's tentatively a not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't write reviews, and certainly not serious ones, but I felt the desire to go over this after finishing my first playthrough. Unfortunately because of this it won't be on par with actual reviews by other folks, but eh, I don't care. As of writing this I have only beat the game as a solo Wizard on the Normal difficulty. I have yet to start a second playthrough. I have also not played the original Hammerwatch (or remastered), only Heroes of Hammerwatch.Setting: It's about what I was expecting, I have no major issues with it. My gripe with it is how focused on the player character being the hero and all results in it feeling weak in places because it tries to justify why we can do the things we're meant to do. This is only a couple of 'em:----The game very much isn't meant to be serious, I accepted that very early on, but some of this stuff is just beyond silly.Difficulty: As I mentioned, I played solo as a Wizard. Accordingly, I never really found any one place particularly hard and seldom died. I don't mind this, but I do wish the game had a more clear indicator of how "difficult" an area is meant to be exactly, beyond the area icons for Apprentice/Adept/Expert/Master. That's.. really vague, I found the best way to realise I was perhaps underlevelled for an area was the much faster XP Gain I was experiencing from killing the enemies there.Equipment: So bloody much of the time I just had the same equipment, going so far as to still be running an Adept Wand even after I'd hit Master. The simple reason was because shockingly enough, random drops were still not besting the damage output of said wand. Now expand that for most of my equipment. Again, I played on Normal, but I had little issue running equipment that was perhaps "underlevelled" at the point I was still using it because the random drops were just not actually improving my loadout at all.Crafting/Enchanting: Can I just ask, what's the point of crafting ultimately? Besides being used namely for potion/mana upgrades (which I do like), it just felt.. empty. It feels like it could've been so much more useful for actually upgrading gear (per the above), which leads me to..Enchanting feels even worse for me. I only seemed to find the one fella in Aventurine who could only enchant Common/Uncommon gear, so the late-game gear couldn't be touched. Now add the randomness of enchanting (and how I'm still not sure why I couldn't use most of the stuff I had) and I'm left feeling like, what's the point of this. I would be so willing to pay more money and lose some runes/mats as well to be able to disenchant gear and re-enchant it for a better roll.Minimap/Map: This one is a no-brainer but can I please just have something like Heroes of Hammerwatch where I can view the local map and actually pan the camera around. Thanks.Also, why bother with the map menu when you only get maps for like 3 Actual locations; Hammerfall, Fallowfields and Blackbarrow. i feel like this menu could be so much better used to display maps of previously explored locations, especially to better keep track of where I've been.Locations: I said we'd get back to it so here we are. Other than for future expansion (which, I am hopeful for), what's the point of multiple locations. Why even have Lockdey, Brisk Observatory, the desert or the Summer Keys. Maybe I made the mistake of doing Obsidian Tower before going to any of these, but it felt so excessively silly that I go to a location, talk to an NPC And then leave it and never come back. And then you have places like the Wishless Resting Place that are expansive, and yet I don't understand what I even got out of it long-term other than XP.Merchants/Keys: Hot take, but why do I get so much gold relevant to how little the merchants actually have. I found myself with so many valuable items late-game that are worth large amounts of gold and yet I could seldom sell the damn things because merchants barely have any cash to spare, often requiring me to buy multiple items of theirs just to do such, which..Just to be able to sell the constant equipment items I'd get, I'd end up buying SO MANY KEYS, and yet key-doors seemed extremely rare. I wouldn't mind random chests requiring bronze/silver/gold keys to open because it would atleast make buying the damn things worthwhile.This ultimately sounds like a lot of ranting and yeah, it is. In the end though, I enjoyed the game, I definitely think it's worth picking up and placing atleast once even with the rather limited content right now. I do worry that other class playthroughs will suffer as a result of the game being.. well, rather linear, but I'll definitely give them a go. I do hope future updates/expansions increase the available content and certainly hope some mods fix some of the gripes I have.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of HoH and HW1, I expected this game to be a lot more than it is. Unfortunately, it's lacking basic quality of life features that have been present in the genre for a long time, such as the ability to skip in-game time or teleport to waypoints. I might have been able to look past these issues if not for how multiplayer is handled, which is the main reason I am requesting a refund.I discovered, much to my chagrin, that I would not be able to play with my friends using my already created character and that character data is tied to campaign save files. In other words, unless all involved friends happen to be online at the same time and can commit to playing a specific file, no one can play. This is a massive departure from how things worked in the previous title by this developer, and honestly blindsided me.Hopefully the dev sees the trend happening here - just look at the other reviews! - and does something about the atrocious state of the multiplayer and QoL. Or just decides to make HoH2 using this new engine, and stops wasting time on whatever this is. Either way, I'll be keeping an eye on it to update my review.
