_childDocuments_.review: Hammerwatch and Heroes of Hammerwatch are two of my favorite games of all time, and I am also having an overall great time with this game in both singleplayer and multiplayer. If you enjoy the previous titles or open world ARPGs then it is probably at least worth a try, but there are a few things that really stand out as issues to me that keep me from fully recommending this.First and foremost is performance. Specifically, I think there is a nasty memory leak related to auto saves and loading zones. I just built a new PC. At full price, the parts would have cost around $4k and even with a rig like that I can usually only play the game for 30-90 minute sittings before the game starts freezing for 10+ seconds at a time (my longest session I ever did before needing to restart was 2 hours). When the game recovers from a freeze, it will sometimes make my keyboard stop responding and have my character start walking in random directions, requiring me to plug in a controller to open a menu so I can save before restarting the game.Second problem I have is the fact that a lot of the optional content doesn't do a great job (in my opinion) of letting you know it is optional (an admittedly common hazard in open world games). When coupled with the fact that a lot of the optional content is extremely cryptic or otherwise impossible to do at the stage of the game that you first come across them, it makes for a sometimes frustrating and unrewarding experience full of backtracking for already outdated loot.My third problem is some of the art. Overall, the art is really quite nice... as images... I have found that the art is much less nice for gameplay. I have died quite a few times to not even seeing the attack because the art is just so busy. There have also been quite a few times where I completely relied on the map to navigate an area because I couldn't see anything at all because there were trees and rocks and weird perspectives of slopes and such being in the way of seeing where I am going (I understand that sometimes this is to obscure a secret area, and sometimes this is a fault of the semi-random generation, and some of this is normal jank of a 2D game trying to show slope of hills and mountains, but I'm still going to mention it). There are also a few animations that look flawed. For example, the red flowers you can see in the grass some places (not the harvestable ones) have some random yellow pixels that flash for just a frame or two in their animation, and the white flowers have some red pixels that flash in their animation. It looks almost like the artist straight up forgot what color of flower they were animating for exactly one pixelMy fourth problem is the merchants. They are annoying. Really annoying. They each have their own schedules within the day/night cycle, which is cool at first, but gets old fairly quickly (particularly if you don't have the money needed to rest to quickly pass the time so you can hurry up and sell stuff). Also, merchants have specific lists of things they buy and sell, which is also cool at first, but some don't always even buy the thing they say they buy (a great example of this, I found a fish merchant that doesn't buy marlin... is marlin not a fish? It's a fish in real life... and you get it in game by fishing... so why exactly can I not sell it to the fish merchant?)There are a few other things I noticed (mostly other QOL gripes), but I noticed that others have already covered those points thoroughly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the original Hammerwatch that improves on its predecessor in a variety of ways. The most obvious improvement is the graphics. The game features beautiful pixel-graphics with much more clearly readable sprites than either Hammerwatch or even Heros of Hammerwatch. The controls have also been vastly improved compared to the first game.Gameplaywise, HM II features a lot more RPG elements than HM like quests, buildcrafting and random item pick ups. Combined with five different playable classes and four difficulty levels this gives the game a lot more replay-value and that's not to speak of day 1 mod-support.Regarding the most common criticism, the save system, I don't know what people have expected. Having your character of a multiplayer session only saved on the host-side is common practice for online co-op RPGs, Baldur's Gate 3 uses the same system and it just released to critical acclaim. This is an RPG where you play the story with friends and then are done with the run, not an MMO where you spend hundreds of hours grinding your character.Also people seem to be disappointed that the game is so different to Heroes of Hammerwatch when it isn't even the successor to that game.That said, exploring can sometimes feel a little underwhelming with dead-ends leading to nothing but common item pickups but this is far from a dealbreaker to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this game if you're expecting roguelite like Heroes of Hammerwatch or Hack&slash ARPG like Diablo, Sacred, and Hero siege.You don't start by creating a player character, instead you choose a campaign to play, and a character you created belongs to the said campaign save file, you progress in the character stays with that campaign. This also applies to MP. You join another person's campaign, and you're not going to play 'your own' character, instead you're going to create a character that belong to the host's campaign. If he decide to stop playing, your character goes with the host and will be never seen again. This is kind of weird design choice if you expects usual ARPG multiplayer approach, which you can drop in and drop out anytime you want with your own character.Of course being able to drop into other people's campaign with your full kitted character is invitation to balance issue, but who cares when it's 4 people coop that you play for fun. I hope the devs rethinks this design choice and make your progress with character stays with you, instead of campaign or host. Until then, I will stick to single player only because 'Playing and itemizing individually until your friends logs in' is just not possible in current design.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to preface this review with a few statements I am sure that many of you reading reviews would agree with:Hammerwatch was (and still is, to be fair.) a staple RPG dungeon crawler that brought old school gauntlet gameplay to the modern, online co-op ecosystem.Heroes of Hammerwatch expanded this design and refined the way that characters played, added much needed customization and implemented Roguelike systems into what was already a good foundation.Now, I understand this game isn't Heroes of Hammerwatch, however, all of the systems that game had are present in this game minus the Roguelike progression features.This is where the review will take a turn. If you are having fun with this game and were able to make it through the first ten minutes, that's good for you, I certainly do understand why. However, before even loading into the game I noticed things that felt incredibly off. Horizontal UI design at the main menu? Controller and Mouse inputs that conflict with each other and make menu navigation and absolute nightmare on gamepad? The main campaign loading off what is essentially a mod list? Longer than average load times between screens with what looks like a brand new developers loading screen they put in their prototypes? Oh man, I haven't even gotten into the game yet and this is the level of quality that a first release of an early access game of a competent studio would have ironed out before even releasing the game, let alone asking for over average price for whats supposed to be the full release of an indie game.Being this disappointed in just how a game feels and runs before you even get to the gameplay is certainly not what I expected from this dev team. Every single one of their releases before this game have had minor flaws and issues that hardly changed my perception of the game and the development team's integrity but this has changed after giving what I experienced some thought.This all came to a head when the game starts. I'm given a character and press up. The character walks backwards. I look in the menu to turn off the strafe lock as it is not a feature I want to be on at all times and every other game I've played that has a strafe lock mechanic has it toggleable or binded to a button. Nope, it's just how the game is. Unless I'm missing an option to swap how strafing works, I'm forced to relearn how to play the game. While this seems like a nitpick in the grand scheme of things, it is yet another sign that the developers rushed something and or are incompetent when it comes down to the fundamentals of how to design around player expectation when it comes to input.Alright... so I move on and am immediately stuck. I figured out that the planks in the starting area are destructible but then what? I'm in a room with nothing in it, nowhere to go and nothing to interact with. I am genuinely confused until I watch a YouTube video and see that I had missed a corner pop up of a quest that said something about a breakable wall. Alright, so I look around for a breakable wall and would you look at that, I didn't find one and resorted to attacking every single wall until I found it. Now, I may be naive or blind but if you are going to tutorialize what seems to be an important mechanic, having signposting for that mechanic is necessary. I don't want to go through an entire game where breakable walls are either indistinguishable or nearly impossible to see and lose out because I didn't decide to hit every single wall tile in the game. Heroes did it great, the hidden rooms had subtle yet hard to miss hints to the perceptive. This game either has no hints or the devs genuinely expect the player to notice how a line on a wall is slightly shifted.I almost quit right there but decided to walk outside. There's a reason that art design in nearly every game is designed with dynamic and static objects being ever so slightly differentiated so that a player knows they can do something with something. It turns out in what was essentially visual noise of mixed perspective, poorly discernable tiles that the pile of planks that would have been a random blockade for the player in any other experience was the way forward.Yep, I didn't want to deal with this for an entire 30 hour RPG. I refunded the game right then and there.Again, being a fan of both previous hammerwatch games and Serious Sam (but actually hammerwatch) this game is clearly made by a different dev team piggybacking off of the success of the old Crackshell. I realized it was published by Modus and looked at their back history. They pick up indie games and rush them out before they are ready, charge premium indie prices for them and then drop the developers who dont get a positive reception.I realized that it was Modus who forced them to release a broken switch port that had everything in 3pt font* and had to talk directly to the dev team myself to get a zoom feature implemented.I'll get this game in the future if it gets fixed, however, looking at the track record of Modus' previous titles it looks like updates won't be funded and Crackshell will either have to go back to self publishing or shut down because of this mess.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to say it, but at this point I cannot recommend this game. There is a lot right with it. I love the detailed world map, which really feels alive and full of stuff to do. The graphics are superb, an easy 9/10, with the only faults being some visibility issues at the beginning. The music is great as well. However, the game is just not very fun to play. Most classes / builds will rely on just holding left mouse button pressed, with passives or temporary cooldowns for enhances autohit damage. Pretty boring. The dodging gets tedious really fast, there's just a million effects to doge, so you'll likely end up being as tanky as possible, even with ranged classes. The day/night cycle is just tedious. There's one event that only happens at night, which encourages you to revisit an old cottage at night, but mostly it's just boring and a chore. Want to take a ferry to another continent? Too bad, rest at an inn for a couple of hours first. Want to buy something from a vendor? Nope, he'll be here tomorrow. I was slightly worried about the classes being not very fun for me ever since they released the Gladiator in Heroes of Hammerwatch and, sadly, I was right. TL/DR: Great world and presentation, very unfun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant about buying this game due to the sheer volume of negative reviews that bombarded this game when it launched.  Currently, a week after launch, it's still "mixed" and at 64% positive reviews after being down to around 56% right after launch.  All I have to say as a huge fan of "Heroes of Hammerwatch (2018)" is that every negative review is lame as hell and I'm super happy that I made the plunge on this game.  I expected to play this game for an hour or so tonight and was addicted for 4 hours and only stopped playing because I have to go to work.  It's incredibly fun!The controls are responsive, fluid and the enemies are pretty smart at times keeping the game challenging and rewarding.  The world is fun to explore and there's tons of secret tunnels and caves to find and traverse.  The game offers a massive amount of depth with skill and attribute upgrades, tons of loot, item crafting, enchanting, and so much more!  There's several classes each with their own unique skills and abilities, there's four difficulty levels to choose from, and you can always change things up by playing online with friends too!An absolutely INCREDIBLE VALUE... and Hammerwatch II here is easily one of my best and favorite indie games of 2023 so far.  ..I look at the negative reviews and scratch my head wondering what the hell is wrong with people.  Maybe people can't handle a game that offers challenge, a consequence for dying, and want a casual game that holds their hand the entire way through and they can never lose.  I really don't know.  To all the haters of this game, maybe go play "Palia".  You can never ever die in that game and it holds your hand every step of the way!    I want to play more, but if I had to give this game a first impressions score right now, it would be an easy 9.5 out of 10.HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.  ..Unless you are a crybaby who wants your hand held every step of an RPG game and you never want to die or have to figure out to actually "get good" and beat a challenging boss or tough mob.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Decent game.  Is very unforgiving, but the game play is pretty good.  In its current state I can only recommend you buy if it's discounted as there are a few features I think are lacking to make this a whole game. I've really enjoyed the Hammerwatch franchise up until now and I hope these problems are fixed.The game play is pretty good.  I've played a few different characters with friends and found the combat to be pretty good overall. Resource management is a thing when calculating how to approach fights and it's rare to be able to just charge in to fights without a plan.I understand that this game is supposed to harken back to the days where games didn't hold your hand to show you exactly where you needed to go for everything, but there's a few things missing for basic QOL.A more detailed explanation of my complaints with this game:Opening the menu and reading the quest text doesn't always give you a good idea of where you're supposed to go, who you're supposed to hand the quest into and where that person is location, and in the event that you've got a timed quest how much time you've got to complete the quest. One quest in particular, when I was unable to remember where I got the quest from, I turned to google for help.  The help I was given: "The cave spawns randomly behind a tree in fallowfield".  Fallowfield is a massive area with hundreds of trees, and the cave is not marked on your map so there's a high chance you can just walk past the entrance if you're not meticulous in checking EVERY SINGLE TREE. Words cannot express how frustrated I am with this quest as I still have not found where to hand this quest in at.If you've failed a timed quest sometimes you won't know because, even though you might have completed the task, too much time has passed and the quest giver is no longer highlighted.  This means you may talk to the NPC at a later time only to be notified that you failed the quest.  This could be fixed by allowing the map to highlight the quest giver, but have the NPC ultimately tell you that the quest timer ran out. This happened to me on more than one occasion and it's very frustrating and once made me just quit the game.Perhaps I missed something in the introduction to this game, but it took me longer than I'd like to admit for me to figure out the number next to the stat on the upper portion of an item was not how much str/int/dex it gave, but rather how much it required to equip. There are so many symbols for all the different stats, and there's no easy way to view what they are; you have to switch from the inventory screen to the stats page, then find out where that symbol is on the page to see what it correlates to and there are many symbols which look very similar, so if you've got to go back and make sure you've got the right symbol you're switching back and forth multiple times.Since there is no hotbar(I'm not sure why this was decided against) the devs thought it useful to allow you to quick bind a skill/item to a button on the fly.  While this is very convenient, it does not care if you bind something to a key which bound to another item/skill.  This seems like a very big oversight as you can easily find yourself becoming frustrated when you realize that certain keys are also bound to other skills by default.

_childDocuments_.review: At start you are welcome with Excellent opening music. Once you choose type of game (Single/Multi) and Campaign + difficulty, you can pick your Class: Paladin and Rogue as Melee; Ranger, Wizard and Warlock as a ranged (I have seen in file Priest and Druid, but I am not sure what they are doing there). Speaking of Files, Game include modding tools.Once you pick Class you start you main story, but you won't be limited, as there is many other thinks to do including daily quests - which can be helpful due loss of gold if you get killed, but you can "git gud" to minimalize its occurrence. Game have Crafting system and Enchantment that due its simplicity is easy to use, and resources are usually gathered as you go doing other things, but these can be focused while waiting for NPC to wake up and you have no gold to sleep in INN. Ah yes, sleeping NPC, Hammerwatch have day/night cycle: Most of them are accessible only while its day, and at night they go sleep, while Undea... other creatures wake up from their slumber.Map conveniently is relatively small, but its good - doesn't feel like things go into each other, and each region have its own theme with different OST - these are also great.Character progression is also great, allowing each class for different build and play style, not limiting to go with eg warlock intellect only casting from afar - if you want go str, and be summoning tank - sure!Although map is rather small, be not deceived - there is plenty to explore and discover.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing and experiencing the game and hearing the credits theme, I really can't say that it is a bad game! Just like with HoH I played this one with a set group of 3 and we really had a great time playing "Rolands Revenge", with a Wizard, Paladin, Rogue combination. Throughout this journey we came to notice that every class had its benefits and strengths, and when combining them correctly, all weaknesses can be outmanuevered. The class kits are interesting, quite elaborate and satisfying to use. Maybe a lot of buttons, but we managed with some training (and extra mouse buttons). Fighting through the game, having each others backs and working out the patterns of the bosses together was lots of fun and felt fulfilling. The graphics are of great quality and the soundtrack is epic and melodious. Quite some people disliked the fact that the game takes some reading to understand, however at this point I'd like to appreciate the way those texts and answers were formulated; clever and witty.Overall, those 20 hours or so were a great adventure, filled with fun, challenge and appreciation.However, some things revealed themselves as somewhat annoying. Firstly, Mysterious Caves. The small portion that actually has some use is engaging and all, but the overwhelming amount of time-waste-caves kinda disappoints.Secondly, at some point, your role in the story feels like a messenger or carrier, not a hero. Lots of running around, checking things, giving report, checking things again and so on. Adding to this, I didn't see the point of the "Return in some hours again" sequences. This didn't add anything to the game-experience, no challenge, no *value*, no nothing. It only wasted time. The last major issue that comes to mind, are the items. Overall, those are fine and often feel impactful and effective. However my problem is that the levels of the items didn't really fit at times. A weapon of the Master rank should always be stronger than an expert ranked weapon/armor. However all too often I found myself with strong expert equipment, and no Master-loot in the late game overpowered those, hence my loadout didn't change much in the last third of the game, which is sad since at this point you ought to get the most powerful items, after all you achieved the highest rank and feel the strongest.All in all though, the positives weigh heavier than the negatives for me. The game runs solidly, the multiplayer perfomance was satisfying, apart from some minor bugs, and the loading times were never long.The game has great potential. The first story was already very enjoyable, if expandable here and there (like the desert part for example), but overall a good first experience. With a great foundation that this game created, many interesting stories might find their way to us, and with some luck some more classes as well (As this would add a lot of value for re-runs and multiplayer. More classes are the best way for new content aside from new stories, much like in HoH. Though I can see that the kit-development of these classes takes some more work than in HoH as they are more complex and thought-out)So yeah, all I can say is; Good Job, everyone who worked on this game, I appreciate your efforts, and recommend it wholeheartedly to whoever wonders about playing it as well!

_childDocuments_.review: this game is NOT NEARLY as boring as the negative reviews would have you believe. 16 hours in and i've enjoyed every minute!gameplay is what we all loved from the previous entries, the music is memorable, character building is super enjoyable and makes a significant gameplay difference, new elements such as crafting and enchanting are straightfoward and useful, the legendary pixel art mixed with complex particles and effects is a fantastic combo... i do not see what people are complaining about in regards to quality. though, granted, i haven't tried multiplayer as of writing.even what's most talked about, the pacing: the objectives are clear, reasonably distanced and, although this game loves its big walls of text, you can skip through all of them and just read the text excerpt at the top of your quests, for enough information on where to go and what to do.the only problems i've had so far are minor annoyances, such as the game not making it clear what areas you're supposed to explore at what points of gameplay, but that can be figured out by just going to them and seeing whether the enemies kick your ass too hard or not.overall, i say this totally lived up to the hype. can't comment on replay value because i haven't done a second playthrough yet, but my first experience is going great and i'm genuinely engaged in the story and everything about this game.ONE WARNING: know that you're buying a game that requires patience! it's not as slow as others say, but it is still a rather slow, chill game when outside of combat. i'm all for a slower pace though, so i'm lovin' it.

_childDocuments_.review: Made this after 100% achievements earned. (also Heroes of Hammerwatch 100%)     I'd say the whole journey feels like Terraria, where bosses mark different stages of the game. I appreciate the vast map, and the complicity of the dungeons (especially later ones), they basically remind us to slow down, solve the puzzle and discover a loot chest or new short cut. It is a hack-n-slash game if you choose normal or easy difficulties. But in serious difficulty it almost feels soul-like. The game sure tests our patience and memory. Many other newcomers might not like the fact about its fast combat-yet slow exploration style, but I am sure there are plenty like me, enjoy seeing all the dots (Hammerwatch I, and Heroes of Hammerwatch story lines) connect within this game. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty different from previous games in the series. Where the first two games are action roguelikes, HWII is a love letter to Zelda: Link to the Past, Divinity, Nox, and other now-ancient arpgs. I grew up playing those, so yes the nostalgia feeds me, but I really enjoyed this experience. That said, running from point A to B can take a long time, caves are too sparse, and I managed to beat the game without ever figuring out how to activate the elven waypoints for more fast travel options. I hope the devs improve some of this in the future, but two weeks after release there are already mods addressing these things.I've played the hell out of Heroes of Hammerwatch, and based on the ongoing support and quality dlcs that game received, I'm excited for HWII's future.

_childDocuments_.review: Hammerwatch 2 is, despite what some people have been saying, a very good game. I've finished the campaign on single-player mode, and thoroughly enjoyed it. It's *not* Heroes of Hammerwatch 2 as it's not a roguelite, rather a story-based RPG. The story is a little convoluted at times with walls of text being used to progress things, and reading them can be a bit tiring, which is a complaint. Gameplay itself is great - combat feels satisfying, and (as paladin) levelling up provides with a range of skills which allow you to shape your character pretty well. That said, it is a very difficult game, even on normal mode - so be prepared to die a fair bit. The pixel art graphics are really nice, and the music is great as well.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played all of the Hammerwatch titles, and I was genuinely surprised to find a normal story rpg instead of a roguelike/lite game like the previous 2 titles. However I really did enjoy the game in its entirety,but that doesn't stop the issue's I did notice. Some content felt a tad rushed, Kinda wish there was more progression and like kind of larger side quest lines like the cult in the graveyard keep. As for gear progression, I kind of found some areas very sparse in terms of enemy level and the associated gear they dropped. Master level gear felt like it came a little late and I was already struggling to find pieces to replace, and crafting didn't seem horribly successful in providing the stat's I went for on rogue. Gaining gold was actually very easy, and I'm not exactly sure why so many people have this as a sore spot. It's a arpg, grind some and make gold using the various methods provided. I farmed literally. At first I thought I was fulfilling my rogue fantasy and stealing crops, but in reality you sell them to the right shop keepers and make a nice chunk of gold. Farming mobs in an area I just cleared proved fruitful, especially past blackbarrow. Utilizing the coach to the retreat and other "far off" style retreats were always cool and had some sort of fun mechanic associated with them to earn LOTS of gold.Getting a hold of good gear wasn't the worst thing if you built your class decently. I took advantage of the maze and farmed the boss for extra levels before progressing in the story to prevent myself from dying by getting new gear in a new zone area, but the issue I ran into was all the gear that was "better" but it's stats were naturally still worse than my lower tier gear that had a very good roll on them for a lot of stamina. This can be a good or a bad thing, but I didn't mind as my build came together the more I played, and I felt plenty powerful and balanced in fights. The story, the gameplay, and the big bad spider in the cave. I found the story decent, entertaining in a comical sense, it doesn't take itself to seriously, and it also doesn't become a massive gag show. I love that it continued off of the first original Hammerwatch. Made my character immediately feel more valuable to me as I immediately chose a rogue as per my first game of Hammerwatch. I feel like the content is pretty consistent, but some places felt more empty later on and I was yearning for more higher level enemies to fight, or new side quests to explore. Lastly end of the game almost felt like it should of had some post game content to do on at least Hammerwatch island to maybe make it your own "base" per the significance of the Island to the name of the first game and the franchise as a whole, but you can sort of get a house there from a quest? So it's not all bad apples. Honestly it's fun, I feel like there is some bulking to the games content as a whole as I noticed in the trailer that they had Hammerwatch, and Heroes of Hammerwatch running in some base form in this version of their franchise, and I am craving for it and hopefully modding people who make awesome stories too. I look forward to what Crackshell can do and I hope they take the feedback in stride.

_childDocuments_.review: So far I like this game a lot, but I understand why other people are not thrilled by it.It's a very different experience from the the other Hammerwatch games and has some funny design choices that may or may not bother you much. If you like older open-world RPGs like Morrowind and you want to see what that experience is like when merged with something like Gauntlet, you may be the target audience for this. It's a bit brutal and directionless at times, but if you read your quest tab or spend some time walking around with your minimap you usually can figure out where to go next. I love the combat and the world is gorgeous. Have not paid attention to the story although there are some genuinely funny dialogues and item descriptions. I've really enjoyed the two boss fights I've done, especially the second one. The open world is hit and miss, but it really depends on your preferences.I wouldn't recommend playing the campaign with a group larger than two as the design of the game doesn't handle groups splitting up very well. If you play with other people, play with people who want to play at your pace.TLDR; It's not for everyone. Liking Hammerwatch 1 or Heroes of Hammerwatch may not be an indicator you'll like this game. I like classic rpgs that force me to plan and think, and I find this simplified version of that design very entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little confused about this one but let's keep it short.Gameplay was great, the usual Hammerwatch goodness. I had fun but there were definitely some weird design choices that didn't make sense coming from a veteran developer. It wasn't anything game breaking though. I played solo only.But I finished the game kinda... disappointed. Not because it was bad but because it was so short. If I didn't spend hours lost on one of the quests (because I'm blind lol), I would have like 16h? Maybe you could go up to 25 if you wanted every secret.At some point I started having more fun with the combat, I found nice items and.. the game ended. Just like that, poof. I know not every game needs to be 100h long but this one just didn't have time to expand. Devs definitely could spend less time on useless small subsystems (like cooking, fishing, crafting) and add some more dungeons/loot. I barely used those subsystems because they are just too simple and impractical.I was hoping for at least an NG+ option or something.Anyway, it is a really cheap game so if you are fine with it being on the shorter side, definitely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: After 40 hours of gameplay, I'd give this game about a B-. This is not the roguelite we remember from Heroes of Hammerwatch. It's a Diablo-style crawler RPG. I am a sucker for the graphic style and I enjoyed HoH a lot, but at its core this game doesn't offer a lot that's particularly new or interesting. Some of the areas felt way too large, adding space for the sake of making you walk more. The day/night system is very frustrating to deal with, as there's no real interesting mechanics there aside from 'vendors and quest-givers aren't there where you need them'. Combine that with a respawn mechanic in a lot of dungeons (and no Town Portal tool), it means that an emergency trip out to resupply could result in effectively losing a *lot* of progress through a tough area. Still, it was fun more than boring. I played through the primary campaign after all, though if I'm being honest it was more as a palate cleanser from some other games than because I felt it was particularly compelling. Overall a decent game, especially on Switch, but nothing I think you should rush out and get outside of a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: EXCELLENT GAME! I am so happy that I had an impulse purchase with this game. It is wonderful! I can't stop playing. The developers did such an amazing job when putting this together. I tried hosting a game just to see what would happen and it really allows gamers from all over connect and become friends as they work together. I highly recommend this to anyone!I see a lot of negative reviews, however, it is a little strange as to why people wouldn't like the added challenge to the game. I felt that the mechanic of having to gain and manage gold safely added an extra challenge, rather than just getting endless amounts of gold and being extremely easy to just purchase everything. A lot of games I used to love have become extremely "baby mode" easy. I love that this game challenges players. Speaking of, the boss fights are tough and so are the dungeons. Way better than other dungeon crawlers where if you die you just shrug and say "Oh, well...I'll just respawn and the monster will have saved damage on it." You have to actually try to get through the level and boss fight and there are actual consequences for dying. This is the type of difficulty and challenge that brings back great memories of good gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm salty about the negative reviews because I think this game is actually incredibly good so I'm leaving a review to help out. Its a complete upgrade from the first Hammerwatch in so many ways however it does have bizarre shortcomings. Pros:The game looks and feels satisfying to play. The skill tree is good.The itemization is good.The combat is rewarding.The game has the ability to be challenging.It has a oldschool no hand holding vibes which modern gaming needs.Zones and bosses provide difficult and unique puzzles/challenges/design elements.Cons:It has some of the worst UI in gaming history, its only achievement is that it technically works.Crafting is good bad. Seems half baked. Food and items. You have a 50/50 shot it will explain or reveal anything you care about. (God forbid you have to think)No form of teleport home is an odd choice but manageable. (Git mobility git gud)Its got a couple random bugs but its actually just the UI.There's probably more but I don't really care, ultimately the game is good. Most who are complaining are either A: thinking this was Heroes of Hammerwatch 2, B: legitimately bad gamers who like hand holding or C: people who are incapable of looking past the UI and enjoying the game. This is definitively a good game. Should they have done an early access or a longer deep beta test? Probably. Should you buy this game? Yes. If you liked Hammerwatch and like a game that doesn't give you a map marker, map, compass, gps, assistant, radio, teleporter, car, airplane, autoplayer, bots, and/or install pre-won for you like most modern games then buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty fun hack/slash RPG game. The pixel art and retro style is beautiful and brings the game beautiful scenery. The combat is fluid yet fast paced so you do need some fast reaction time, which can make combat difficult. The amount of grinding so far is not that bad and the game is reasonably balanced (Unless you play the hardest difficulty, that mode go hard). There is a lot of exploration within this game so get ready to do some walking. The game is a bit strange to understand and get used to at the beginning, but if you keep pushing progress, it becomes really fun to see your character grow strong... and still die (skill issue). So far game is an 8/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Hammerwatch 2 II. Takes the "twin-stick" gameplay of Heroes of Hammerwatch and the crafted campaign of Hammerwatch to the next chapter. There are less classes than in HoH, but each of the classes now can have their abilities modified as you level up and find loot. The day/night system is nice, but kind of a pain as NPCs go to bed and the game makes you spend gold to pass time, and there are some 'Timed' quests that I'm not really a fan of. The graphics are still pixel, but there are some really nice effects going on, like fog and lighting. Overall, I'm enjoying it so far. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I have tons of fun with this game. PROS:- Really beautiful pixel art and filled with decorations- Fighting is a lot of fun.   - Some enemy abilities are hard to dodge and need to be anticipated, others are clear and telegraphed   - Every little mob has multiple unique abilities and behaves differently. - Classes are easy to use but can be very versatile  - They start with simple abilities   - One can change their mechanics with skill points, which leads to really interesting combinations and scalings.  - A lot of potential for unique builds (e.g. dodging mage tank) - Stats system is classic but extensive enough for gear optimizations and crafting- NO FARMING / GRINDING (but you can, if you want)- Nice soundtrack- Better with friendsCONS:- Sometimes items and paths unclear visually because of the lush artworks- Playing in Multiplayer is kinda weird. Characters are bound to save files. Once joined changing the class not possible...- Difficulty levels are too easy. I play on max difficulty since the beginning and it is challenging, but i would like to increase the   difficulty with more mastery of the game.- Story is mediocre and NPC dialogue not very interestingIf you like adventuring through a world, while getting stronger, testing out skills, playing with loot and stats and mastering 2d fights, this game is definetly for you! P.S.: This game starts at the end of Hammerwatch 1, which is also a fantastic little game. It is worthwhile to start with Hammerwatch 1.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not quite done yet with the main campaign but I can tell that I'll be spending many more hours in this (especially when the community comes up with great mods!). My only fear is that many people seem to dislike it a lot, reducing its chance to build a growing community.I do understand certain criticisms (and many of em have been fixed like loot and saves). I played with a friend but I assume Singleplayer means you are good to go from the start without issues. Tho, one thing stuck with me because it became more apparent the futher I delved into to Hammerwatch II. There is some emptiness every now and then. The devs cannot obviously bombared the Player with millions of high tier items, but why bother at all then? Holes in the ground, secret doors. or just mines. Some of em' are just empty. Filled with a handful of enemies and that's it. Feels like a cheap way to fill an open world.But still, these are issues that can be worked on by the community. We can create stories, maps, and quests that are enjoyable and full of things to do (and loot!). And I might even be wrong agreeing with these critics. Maybe there is something in there that I cannot reach/see yet. That's the thing, Hammerwatch plays like a metroidvania kinda. You unlock skills and tools to reach new places in places where you'd been already. Maybe I'm just too impatient for a new tool.But man is this fun! The gameplay is just pure fun. Working on your equipment is great. The strongest of enemies become so easy to fight its hilarious and only takes about a few hours to reach that point. The boss fights are cool! Teaming up with friends makes all of that even better especially knowing that you can build a set of skills together, plan out fights, and exchange gear.There is even so much lore in this, world buidling, and funny moments, which I really did not expect.But I also ran into bugs every now and then. 2 crashes and my buddy (who was hosting) lost connection to his server? What does that even mean? How can you lose connection to something that  It's probably more lore to be discovered with deep meaning, idk.Traveling also gets to me at times. Music and art style are cool, but going back and forth again and again and again is booooooriing. I WANT A HORSE! I saw the racing mod! Give me a car or a horse! (maybe there is somehting like this down the road, I reaaaaally really hope!)The music is also cool, Sounds in general are awesome. Its not too buggy and runs pretty well on old hardware (my laptop is definitely happy).Love it! Keep it up!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been having a lot of fun with the game so far. The combat is very Hammerwatch, but in a more open constructed world with quests and a bit more player agency. _childDocuments_.review: Hammerwatch 2 is a really good sequel to Hammerwatch and I can not wait what modding will bring to the game.So far I explored the island and set foot on the mainland, which raised the bar in terms of harder enemies or maybe I just went in the wrong direction. Hopefully there is no planky catch this time ... ^^Art style is very good, music supports the atmosphere excellent. I am really thankful there is good customisation for mouse/keyboard and controller bindings as left handed people this is always important. (Only one small thing is that when using a controller, items in player menu should be selected even when switching sub-tabs, somehow it always opens split stack popup or some other popup so i cant see which item is now selected, also opening the popup/context menu should have a focus and selected first line so you can continue to select and execute an entry with the controller.)Many people here are criticising day/night cycle, but seem not have visited e. g. a graveyard at night.Also cooking and crafting stations function as easy as clicking recipe, select something from the list and then see what ingredients are needed.Gold is there in abundance, just sell mushroom, thistles and all the stuff that you randomly pickup.The only thing that could be better, if there was kind of a town portal to get out of a dungeon fast, i don't mind backtracking it just gets a bit tedious having played for a while. On the positive side, the cities and villages are not too far apart on the mainland, so no vast empty space and there is almost anytime some monster or quest on the way.That quests get obsolete is hinted at, quests text often state, "do x, maybe y will solve problem themselves". I like that, reminds me of the first Elder Scrolls games.What I would like better is if everyone in party would keep their progress means being able to bring their char to the table even if there would be an imbalance, at least as an option. Host saved progress is in many online co-op games these days, and I have yet to see where this should be fun and or useful, e.g. a friend of mine quit his Conan Exiles Server and was not able to pull the save so > 100 hours progress lost, and it completely killed my motivation to start again. So maybe if clients could request a copy over the in-game interface or something like that, so that you can continue with your party char even when you are not playing as party anymore.Overall I recommend Hammerwatch II, now back to squashing some bugs! =)

_childDocuments_.review: for an open world game the worst thing you an do is go out and explore said open world, there is no fast travel back to a village even if there was a 1 time use item it would be better than having to walk all the way back every time, half the time dungeons just lead to a dead end with no loot no nothing and you find your self questioning what was even the point of going down into this cave and again no fast travel so now you have to walk all the way back to the exit...also something that bugged me since i started playing is there are these grapple hook shortcuts you can use except at no point is it explained how you get said grapple hook, is it a guest i missed, is it class based, do i buy it somewhere who knows. on the other hand i've had a pickaxe since the start of the game and i'm yet to find a use for it...also if you want quest to have a time factor to then go for it but make it more clear when you accept them that its time limited along with a timer in the quest screen, rather than just failing them after a while. its infuriating to do some stupid fetch quest just to have the npc belittle you for wasting their time, double so if you failed because you had to sleep for it to turn day because there's a day night cycle and the quest automatically failed in the morningis the game fun? yeah its alright, but save yourself some time and just go after the main quests since exploring or doing side quests in this open world game is just pain.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, it's still Hammerwatch. The main gameplay/combat is still the good old Hammerwatch style, dungeon crawler hack n slash, feels good, character/level progression is nice as well, feels like you're in control with stats and abilites like heroes of hammerwatch. Now, the character saves. I can see how having personal character profiles can have its merits, and I guess in today atmosphere it would be better for user experience, since it seems like a lot of people want to be able to play with randoms, and the issue of gathering the squad all at the same time is a big one always. With all that said, I don't think the character saves is the worst part, since its a design choice that works in many games where the characters are locked to specific worlds, such as minecraft or hammerwatch. I still feel like having them personal would better the user experience though, makes it easier to play with friends i guess.mechanics I thought detracted from the game the most were- to me still minor, but inconvenience nonetheless- the time system and the open world aspect surprisingly enough. The time system is just there, it's just something you have to work around maybe I haven't gotten far enough to see its merits, but right now it's just forced wait time/money spend to be able to interact with certain NPCs. The open world aspect is not the worst, but I think the pacing/flow of the game can become too slow when you're exploring along the way to the next area and there's some garbage mysterious caves along the way that just waste time, but you have to know what is inside, or you just get lost/sidetracked doing something else.I don't like the quests very much. Atleast the early game quests so far were pretty lame. Go fetch a stone, go get my book. there some that were alright like go save the captain from the pirates makes you feel like you're doing something meaningful, but they feel quite lacking so far, I'm hopefully not too far into the game, and this will change. I hope. And bosses. I love a good boss. and I hope to see some impactful bosses like zeus in god of war, the deer in elden ring, or the maggot queen from the first game, they leave an impression of a good boss fight. So far in probably 4 hours of gameplay-for me- there was just that pirate boss from the beginning. There's something about having a big boss health bar on screen that sets a mood, and I think a little circle in the corner of the screen with the bosses avatar wasn't having the same effect for me.The crafting feature seems like it could become annoying, but seeing as how so far it's not an integral part of the game and you can obtain everything from crafting by purchasing as well, it's just an additional feature that people can use if they want.Overall, as a simple co-op hack n slash I enjoy it enough to give it a positive review, it would be nice if my friends weren't always ragging on the game and everyone wasn't comparing it to heroes of hammerwatch, since it most definitely is not a roguelike/HOHw2. my opinion may change as I fight more bosses and get further into the game. I also heard they are already planning to change the character saves to be saved locally, so maybe my friends will play with me again.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent visuals and satisfying combat. If you're looking for an open world ARPG, this is one of the best ones out there. However, compared to Sacred and other ARPGs like Diablo, the combat in this game is more arcadey and less about numbers. Character builds are still important, but a greater emphasis is placed on agile movement and avoiding getting hit than tanking damage and out-DPSing enemies. There are some gameplay design decisions that are contentious, such as NPC schedules (most NPCs sleep at night, so traders and quest givers may not always be available), quest time limits, the lack of fast travel, and the lack of quest compass markers but I think these are all good designs that borrow from a better era of videogames. Though I do think that resting at inns to pass the time should be a lot cheaper.The open world map design is quite nice, with beautiful outdoor environments and bustling towns. As far as I can tell, there is no level scaling system in place, so wandering off the beaten path will lead you to dangerous enemies that will make short work of low level characters - another great gameplay design choice that I approve of.However, the class variety is only passable in my view, they feel a bit too similar. Every single class gets a similar skill tree: Tier 1: 1 dodge skill, 1 main hand skill, 1 off hand skill, 1 spell Tier 2-4: 2 spells, 2 passivesGiving even the Wizard class a stamina-based dodge skill just feels uninspired.The biggest flaw in the game are the caves that you can find throughout the open world. Their placement on the world is fixed, their layouts are semi-random, but nearly all of them feel like a waste of time. I think I found a secret treasure containing disappointing loot once, but that's it. It's such a missed opportunity not to have unique enemy encounters or traps and other hazards and rewarding loot in these mini-dungeons.

Though, if i had to critique something, it'd be the HUD. Those huge bars on the left and right of the screen are obnoxious, and there really isn't ANY reason for them to be so damn big.

_childDocuments_.review: Special note: Mods DO NOT WORK if installed mid-game. Be aware of this.I hated this game when I first got it, but I've really turned around on my opinion. It has its flaws but many of the issues I found were due to misplaced expectations. Specifically that I was under the impression that this was HOH2 NOT H2. I've revised my list belowGood- Combat is fun and interactive for all the classes (with the possible exception of the warlock but I may just suck).- The skill system is a big improvement over HOH. I really enjoy the sub-traits of each ability. This only gets better as the game goes on.- The free form map is great fun, after some initial teething problems.- The fast travel is a bit clunky but very immersive. Note that I installed a mod to get out of dungeons (town portal).- The dialog for the characters can be really funny if you read it. Some of the quests are great for this, particularly the necro quest ("I'll be taking that!").- The controls actually work great, they just take getting used to.- Fantastic art, really charming style. Generally pretty good soundtrack, adventurines theme is a bit too earwormy for me. - Feels like it's more of a "platform" or "engine" than a game experience. The main story gave the impression of being a demo of what the engine can do, more than about itself. This got moved from bad to good, as I want more of this game now.- Quests having real timelines means you need to get stuff done and not take every quest and forget about them.The less good:- The game could still take it easy with the loredump at the start. I know its important but it also is excessive with its words. - Trudging out of dungeons isn't fun, mods fix this but an inbuilt solution would be good.- The time of day mechanic can get in the way some times. Espec when you're in a town with no inn.- While the controls are good, not being able to bind scroll is a bit annoying. The "cs_enabled 0" thing still sucks though.- (from my previous complaints) Nearly everything costs gold. Want a snack? Gold. Want to fish? Gold. Want to pass time in the game? Believe it or not, gold. This gets better later, but not having a good way to store gold does make it hard (mining shares only go so far)- The crafting system could use some more UI prompts to show whats needed during the first few crafts of each type.- Quests having real timelines needs to be more obviously advertised in the quest log.- The character menu could use a rearrangement. Move the Attributes and Spells together, make the quest log more obvious. Make the TAB map scroll-able. Generally though, these are nitpicks. The game is very fun and I'm finding more and more things I like. Makes me feel bad for being so mad before.=== Original review below ===Good- Combat is fun and interactive, if you play paladin. It's block mechanic makes combat feel alive and fun.- The skill system is a big improvement over HOH1. I really enjoy the subtraits of each ability.- The freeform map is cool*The less good:Other than these two points, this feels like such a miserable game. Everything but combat is a chore.- WAY too much talking, NPCs talk your ear off about nothing, unprovoked. Get dunked head first in the lore from the very start.- No fast travel, its a nice enviroment the first time but after trudging back and forth for the 30th time, it gets old. *this really kills the freeform map idea. I end up killing myself to get back to the starting town. The ghetto hearth is real.- Not really like HOH1 at all, its a persistant RPG, NOT a roguelite (which, admittedly, is not in its genres list on steam). They share an art style, but that's all.- Gimpy controls. Has some action wheel thing that gets in the way. Opening the console when trying to drink a pot is par for the course. For other players: add "cs_enabled 0" to HW2.exe.cfg to disable this. This should have been in the game from the start btw, not in this comment. Are most players really going to need to be opening the console from minute 1 of the game? - Nearly everything costs gold. Want a snack? Gold. Want to fish? Gold. Want to pass time in the game? Believe it or not, gold.- Crafting is jank. Trying to use items from your own inventory doesn't work (can it work? couldn't find info on it).- Feels like it's more of a "platform" or "engine" than a game experience. The main story gave the impression of being a demo of what the engine can do, more than about itself. There seems to be a big push in the construction of the game to make it not about one single thing, but that the workshop is what its all about: map making, mod making, etc. This makes it feel like what you get out of the box will be compensated for later, but I just want to play a game folks.- The mod install thing.Generally a pretty unpolished experince. The graphics are nice and it looks like a lot of time went into them, but it's all for naught when the frustrations pile up like this.
