_childDocuments_.review: New player? Read this!** This is a COOP game, not an A-RPG like Diablo, enemies do not scale, boss give guaranteed loot etc **Many bad reviews about lack of gold etc, yet only 2% have reached the " adept " training which only cost 1500 gold and is reached within 1 hour of gameplay, which is right after the Pirate hideout.This is a campaign game, not a Diablo style game where you farm enemies and bosses.This game doesn't hold your hand, you may find yourself getting 2 shot and what not. That's because you are at the wrong place at the wrong time. Imagine Zelda, where map is limited and you must adventure and solve your adventure.Classes like Paladin are very strong, but you must invest in HP, armor, heal etc.Their class fantasy is strong.TIP: Explore the spawn, you will find 2000g worth of red dragon scale from Hammerwatch 1. At the start, talk to the potion maker, clear the Inn basement and you will receive a potion.Get these red flowers and buy a small empty bottle to craft a second potion.Potions are equipment, once equipped and filled they will have 3 charges or more.Find red flowers, buy a small empty or large bottle, get another potion.Complete the pirate hideout, you will get a notice to travel to the second island where you will get your adept training for 1.5k. By then you have over 5k gold.It cost around the same for reseting your skills, 10 000g for your attribute at a potion shop.Fighting: You must be careful, you must kite them and use corner, use doors etc. Don't rush in, you will die ( unless you are paladin ). The combat if unforgiving, but you will be able to take hit with the proper gear and stats allocations.Gold: Artifacts can be found and they will sell for a lots of gold, rare gears also.  DO NOT SELL ITEMS UNLESS YOU NEED GOLD as dying will take away 20% of your gold!You will not starve for gold.This game is an amazing sequel to Hammerwatch 1 and builds on the class fantasy of Heroes.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game! It's sad to see the 'mixed reviews' tag because (as others have already said) it feels like it stems mostly from people who went into the game with different expectations.The game has surprised me on so many fronts with little features (I do enjoy the day/night cycle, the fact you have an actual date aids in the feeling of time progressing). The story is your classical fantasy story line, but it is presented in such a quirky/funny way that I don't care at all. Plus the detailed explanations of quest givers are a lot of fun to read through!Combat feels fluid, the skills you can learn feel impactful and level progression doesn't feel tedious. The rewards you gain (gold and items) feel balanced and you get them regulary enough without it happening so often that it clogs up your inventory space. Exploring caves or dungeons as a completionist feels actually challenging because of the maze like design some of them possess and it always leads to an 'aha' moment once you emerge from them through a different entrance/exit onto the main world map. And the enemy types don't feel repetetive (yet, I have not finished the game).Lastly the game looks absolutely beautiful and the music is fantastic once more. I really enjoy playing the game and if you're looking for a dungeon crawler like rpg with an open world and multiplayer option, I recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, looks great, plays great, and the levels are deep and contain lots little secrets.It doesn't hold your hand though, so you need to like that kind of thing.That said, doesn't take long to learn the different things (love the mini card game) and not being given a quest GPS is a bonus for me (its about exploration).
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Familiar but not similar to Heroes of Hammerwatch, another game by the devs. I actually like that its not a roguelike! Building a character is fun, finding new gear or crafting it was interesting. I enjoyed exploring all of the locations and I'm not even done yet! I definitely recommend this if you like a more open world experience rpg diablo-like. It's not a perfect game though, I ran into a decent amount of crashing, mainly on loading screens, but the autosave was never far away luckily. More of an annoyance than actual lost progress. I lost like, a full dungeon floor ONCE, so it doesn't matter that often but still annoying. NPC schedules are also a minor gripe. I'd like to be able to return to town and sell or upgrade my gear! Nighttime feels more like just skeleton time more than anything cuz nothing else really changes at night. Oh and near the end of the game I had a hell of a time selling valuables, as vendors only buy specific things THEY'RE interested in. I would have liked more vendors to take my useless stuff off my hands, but again, minor gripe. Myeah anyways great game! My complaints are stuff that can be patched out, I'll be running through the game with all the classes eventually, was absolutely worth the wait for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Game is sprawling with secrets, cool boss fights, lots of RPG elements and the pixel art is really nice. Had a fun time on my 1st playthrough, albeit some things in the game are borderline cryptic to figure out - most can be done if you bother reading while on your journey! Highly recommend for the single player experience and also for multiplayer - assuming you understand how the peer to peer host thing works.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game so far. I've been playing Hammerwatch 1 and Heroes of Hammerwatch for years now, this game is quite a bit different from the other two. The others were about clearing out levels to go higher into the castle. This one is about doing quests, take on a quest to rescue a girl, or kill a pirate, etc. The quests will get you to explore most of the caves and dungeons in the world. Some can get a bit tedious, especially if it's a fetch quest, or a quest to clear out a cave you just went to, forcing you to go back through and clear it again. However most dungeons aren't all that large (at least the ones I've gotten to), so it doesn't take long to clear them out. I've seen others complaining about having to backtrack to get out of caves after clearing them, and there's a teleport mod that solves this, but it would have been nice to have some kind of mechanic to get out of a cleared cave quickly with a magic item, granted there are caves in the game that have exits at the end, or that have secret connections back to the beginning.Playing as a wizard there are so many attributes and modifiers that will make this a really fun game to try and minmax my character. With stats for resistance penetration, spell crit chance, 6 different types of damage, cast speed, etc. It's going to be a blast to experiment and try new builds I might not have tried in the previous games.Multiplayer has been a bit of a mixed bag so far, but the devs have been on top of listening to feedback and making changes. They added options for loot sharing in the last patch, and that was my biggest complaint so far. Playing with friends is really fun, however I found that we were going really fast, trying to match the pace from the first two games, and generally skipping dialogue and rushing through town to get to the next area. playing solo I was able to slow down a lot, read all the text and get a much better understanding of the lore and world. It's definitely a different beast than the other games, for better or for worse. The world is beautiful and vast, I've had a lot of fun exploring and getting into trouble taking on areas that are way harder than my level is capable of. It's definitely a game where you have to double back and re-explore previous areas once you acquire the right gear to do so, namely the hookshot. I'm excited to see what else it has to offer, and how many hours it'll get out of me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: This has been amazing and I haven't been able to put it down. I love the talent trees, combat and the pace of leveling! The weather, the water, the air going through the trees, the not having my hand held and having to actually read and try different things in my adventures... Awesome. I keep looking for the loot crates for cash, some kind of low quality forced gambling for gear, a different colored hat you can buy for your toon for $35... I'm looking at you Blizzard. I don't really understand the negative reviews, I hope they don't change a thing and ignore all of you.Looks like a lot of posts whining about "QoL", the people that refuse to read quests and want arrows directing them to piles of loot and instant teleport to anywhere they want to be. "This dungeon didn't have epics for me waste of time" kind of players. Please find another game you can google your way through and leave this one alone. graphics 10/10story (so far) 9/10combat/movement 10/10music 9/10puzzles and hidden treasures to find 9/10optional content 8/10 some quests are just walking to and from Someone already stole my immediate thought but i'll double down... This is way better than D4.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Game has been tons of fun, and is exactly what I expected after playing the Demo. This is NOT Heroes of Hammerwatch 2, and that's fine. This is a much more open world version of the original Hammerwatch, with some considerably improved combat (rest in piece Spam Ranger). My biggest complaints are the loading screens with how frequent and how boring they look (when I first saw them in the demo, I figured it was just a placeholder screen), as well as the time system being terrible when all NPC's are bound to it.Overall, game has been a blast, and the devs have spoken about their efforts to fix a lot of the issues people are having, and I overall trust the devs can fix these issues.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game does have a lot of really obtuse game-design and QOL issues that you can read all about in the abundance of negative reviews this game has. However, despite these issues, I am having so much fun with this game. If this were a $60 AAA game I could understand why these issues, which are mostly minor annoyances would be a big deal, but a $25 indie game? I think its easy to overlook it, especially with how much fun im having. Plus, the game is pretty as hell!
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give this game a neutral rating, I would, because the game is simply average. There are numerous strange and disjointed solutions that I'm not sure whether they are mistakes or intentional choices. For instance, the pause upon opening the inventory... what sense does it make to fight bosses, learn their mechanics, upgrade potions, when you can just fill your backpack with baked apples and heal after every boss attack. It's a complete mess, but it leaves a significant sense of disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Due to a huge amount of people that complained to the Devs about the Character you make being tied TO the world you play in (This isn't BG3 and yet they compared the games?) ... they caved and now the main gripe I had with the game is gone... Co-op to your heart's content...Also can re-roll your world and start-over whenever you want but bring your leveled character with you ... Enjoy doing that on games I beat all the way through.However the game should've launched like this ... the Dev's did basically tell us (I'm paraphrasing here) "We made it this way, we aren't going to add the ability to use your save elsewhere, it's impossible because we tried and the game isn't coded to do that" ... so if you like the 'look' of THIS game? Go look at Heroes of Hammerwatch ... it's much better... If you like that game (but are more fond of the first game?)... try this one out ... it's a solid 7/10 for me. (Would've been 9/10 but the Dev's had to be difficult for months on end about fixing the save system)CLOWNS!!! I guess you feel the need to be included so ... hurrah to all 3 of you I suppose?
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Here are my thoughts having played the demo and now a couple hours with my online group.This game is FUN!  The combat is engaging and challenging without being impossible.The writing is clever and amusing!  The result of rescuing little red riding hood is a hoot.There seems to be enough flexibility to adjust characters to multiple playstyles.And of course the graphics are a pixellated delight.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: my only two gripes atm are1st the character voices i personally don't like them and there is no voice for silent or like i dunno a bit crushed pixel voice in other rpgs.2nd the hookshot is incredibly un-intuitive to find seriously, the big reason is on the tutorial island you a presented numerous spots to use the hookshot but you won't find it for possibly many hours, why? because the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing isn't even on the tutorial island it's in the second zone in a place called thief's tower and i have no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clue how to get in besides vague directions from one steam discussion saying you need to talk to a dude near a river and do his thing and then find a chick south of the capital who will only talk to you after you help the first guy WHO I STILL CAN'T FIND 6 HOURS later. but seriously it's really kind of stupid from a game designer perspective to put on tutorial island hookshot pillars every where in the first dungeon as it can unintentionally bait players into wasting time looking for something that isn't there
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Please let Co-op have separate loot. It sucks to go Into a hidden room then get loot but you or your friend doesn't. That 1 attribute I got from a flask? Yeah that can easily make a difference. And IF their the same Item, just make It available for everyone to grab. I believe Heroes of Hammerwatch did that so why can't this one? Bc It's not strictly a Dungeon Delver Rouge Like? It's just ass. Most RPGs will have Items drop for each player.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: There's the potential for a great game here, there's just too many problems holding it back.One of them is the needless backtracking, a simple fix for this would be a portal back to the last visited town or dungeon entrance function (could be an item like the shovel or hook) along with some kind of sprint or mount system to take the pain out of backtracking in the world map zones.I get the occasional game crash when loading maps but with how many map transitions there are to move around it does get annoying. Another issue is the resource management of skills that use a % of max stamina or mana, especially with stamina and mana regen scaling along side max. I'd much rather these skills be a set cost to not punish specking into mana or stamina.Skill disabling enemies are an extreme pain for the melee classes and a complete non issue for ranged.I think gear could use more of a mix up. Class weapons are very much set drops with only a few mixups with the type of armor (strength, intelligence, or dexterity armors). An example paladins only get a mace and shield. A mix up could be flails (wider swings, ignore shields, armor break), warhammers (smaller aoe, overhand smashing), and maces for the paladin's main hand that have different base attacks and round (weaker blocking, parry window), kite, and tower shields (always imoble, more damage absorption) for the offhand with different blocking stats so its not just endless maces and shields.I also feel that there's a lot of potential for new classes to fill more fantasies. I'd love to see a class use polearms, swords, axes, etc.Character customization could also use some work, all the portrait options need better looking sprite work, and I'd love some small outfit tweaks in addition to the color changes, and possible a way to set the over all scale of your character to be larger or smaller.I feel like there's a missed opportunity to show some different sprite work on each character for apprentice, adept, expert, and master tier head and chest pieces.And the card game is a complete mess, every time I've played it its an exercise in frustration as I get to sit back and get shot by the ai because no shooting cards are drawn, with one being drawn every 8th turn with the ai seemingly being able to shoot every other round.I think the card game should either be real time, or have a deck building aspect to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I have enjoyed Hammerwatch games from the start.So far I have only played around 2 hours of Hammerwatch II and I have to stop playing!I wish I didn't have to stop, as I am enjoying playing this game a lot!I am happy with everything I have seen in this game so far, and have no complaints.The game feels solid and is a full step up from the prequel game.I only wish I had more free time to enjoy this game. I will have to wait a few months, then I can just crush a few hundred hours. I will update the review once I have played more as well.Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I'll play this game through, because I already bought it and am this far in. But they went backwards in quality with games, not forward. They changed how characters are saved during multiplayer matches and it completely ruins the multiplayer experience. I would avoid this if you are a fan of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm at 11 hours ingame in single player and i can't stop getting pleased by this "Boomer's like RPG Wet Dream".I only play multiplayer games usually, but this, this is keeping me entertained because it's all in realtime, no turnbased, but it is actually very well cured in depth. It has the leveling of character and skills, the unlock of new skills, the equipment, the crafting of equipment and armors and much more obviously, as it is meant to be in any good RPG.The commands with the Joypad that is quite well implemented are doable and the game flows very well thanks to it, as i prefer Joypad for this sort of games compare to Mouse + Keyboard.The openworld seems very wide, i visited 3 main islands by now with it's villages and dungeons, but seems i'm still at the beginning. Can't wait to explore more.in single player as an RPG is very well done, playing this pleasantly.The multiplayer is what seems tricky to many people, but is just a wise choice because i guess they want to avoid allowing overpowered players during the course of an adventure, so the teammates joining a host will stay on a similar level of cash and xp to the host.Ignore all this stupid kids lamenting of the design of this product because it is really well done.RECCOMENDED.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: 20 hours in and I've beaten the game, done most of the dungeons, found most of the secrets, did maybe 60-70% of side quests.Does it feel like a Hammerwatch game? No not really, it should have been a new title and then I don't think it would have gotten such negative reviews. Pros:- Art style is nice.- Bunch of quests and side quests.- Areas to explore.- Enemy variety.- Bosses are unique and fun to fight.Cons: - Time gated quests and other time gated stuff.  Locking traveling, quest progression and story progression behind time is kind of a cheap way to prolong the game. If I hand in a quest item, I shouldn't have to travel to an Inn to sleep to pass time until the quest giver is ready for the next part of it.  -Dungeons are frustratingly long and most of the time, not worth it.  If you're slightly under leveled for a dungeon, it'll take forever to clear, just to find out that there's no secret rooms, no crystals or any alternative exits.  - Quest updates need work. If I turn in a main story quest, let the player know where to go next, don't just delete the quest out of the quest log and just expect the player to know where to go next to find the next step.  - Not really a con, but there are areas on the main land that are restricted (I'm not sure if these are placeholders for DLCs or something I've missed in the main game).- Game needs more mini bosses for dungeons and other areas. Maybe something like a world boss that spawns at certain times in caves/open world. Also, it seems the bosses in the game only drop one specific piece of equipment, there should be a loot pool of purple/orange items depending on the difficulty of the boss.- I've never been a fan of NPCs having a certain amount of money to buy loot from the player, and I'm not a fan of it here. After 20 hours and beating the game, my inventory was absolutely littered with items that I would have to spend an hour traveling between towns to find NPCs that have enough gold to buy the equipment. And that's another thing, certain NPCs buy certain type of items/gear is not needed. Let me sell anything I want to any NPC, it doesn't change the game at all.I did enjoy the game overall, but there are a lot of glaring issues that is holding me back from doing another playthrough on a new character, or continuing on with my Mage. I don't think I can recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are much better than the other game, and it's the first time, for a 2D game with an upper view, that I can say; Wow, this is beautiful. The attacks are super smooth, and the gameplay just feels really good. As for now, I am in love with the game, and as someone that tryharded the older games, I will surely continue to play a lot to this one. It is really fun with friends, as everyone feels unique with their classes, as they all are drastically different.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the game and find some things worth mentioning, both good and bad. The good: Graphics are nice, music is nice, game-play is solid and fun.The bad: Performance would just kinda crap out intermittently (esp. after a solid 2 hour play session). I have a 3080, installed on SSD, but sometimes the first cue would be the audio would just start repeating (like a cd skipping) and then the actual screen would freeze up for several seconds or stutter for a bit). This only happened once before the 2 hr mark, then happened quite a bit (esp. in the town you come to after leaving the first island). The cost associated with dying is annoying, I wish I could turn it off. Skills lack explanations regarding the details of their mechanics. I'm a paladin, a starting skill of mine seems to drain souls or something, but it doesn't explain what effect that has. And whatever it does, it's not obvious from playing. So basically for me, some performance issues, dying penalty in both gold and time seems high, and mechanics aren't clearly explained / symbols aren't defined as to what they mean. Still, a fun game and I've been enjoying it. I don't generally play things in multiplayer, so that hasn't been an issue for me, but if the character save is tied to the leader's world save, that would be frustrating for sure. Oh yeah, price was a bit steep ($32.50 in Canada) but the price on Fanatical was great ($21 and change CAD). This is my take: for the right price, I'll look forward to a game, eagerly buy it, and be positive even if I encounter some issues, but when I feel the price is too high, I might refrain from buying or if I do buy, I'll probably be more critical about issues I encounter. With this game, I wasn't gonna buy at first even though I enjoyed the demo. Price was too steep. But for $22? This game is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: What do all of these icons mean? Why do I have 15 different quests after 30 minutes of playing? Why is there an stamina and mana bars and why are they vertically on the side of the screen? Why doesnt the game tell me which items in the world are interactible and which are not unless im standing right next to them? Why teleport ability "doesnt  teleport" between two ledges? Why is there no dedicated button for each menu screen and I have to always press C and then cicle through the tabs? There is so many of these things and all that together completely kills any sense of enjoyment I might have had. The pixel art is amazing and it is satisfying to look at your character running through the fields, but that about it. Also the UI as a whole is just a bit of a cluster ♥♥♥♥.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: A game that is supposed to be a quest based, non randomized open world has next to 0 character customization.Regardless of the gear you have your character look will stay the same the whole time.The only thing you can select is your colors at character creation.Absolutely unacceptable, even for a low budget pixel art game.Oh and the editor is unintuitive and confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I dont really have a problem with the save system, and it does seem the developers are addressing it. It seems like a solid game to time, but I do like playing with friends specifically, not randoms.I think my  main concern is the performance of the game on cross region. It feels like there is quite a lot of rubberbanding and  latency when I play with my friends over in the US from EU even if all of our connections are  in good shape and even with a ping of just shy of 150 ms. Perhaps the game needs a bit more time in the oven and have that addressed before I can give this a good recommendation
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: People are expecting Heroes of Hammerwatch 2, but this is Hammerwatch 2. Its more RPG than any of the prequels. I for one have longed for this and while there are rough edeges (help page is a bit thin, stats not explained, a few bugs, exploring _can_ be a bit tedious due to dead ends, etc.) the overall game is great and very promising. I have faith in the devs to address these issues and i am enjoying the game regardless!If you loved HW1 and want something more RPG-ish, buy. I tell my friends that HW2 is like a more dedicated/hardcore thing that you have to play with your group at scheduled hours to progress together, whereas HW1 is more casual and drop in/drop out friendly.Edit: Unfortunately there are still severe issues with multiplayer and it has not been addressed by the development team. As the game is being marketed right now (multiplayer game) i cannot recommend it. As a single player experiences there are still some bugs but not game breaking (that i've personally encountered) but multiplayer is literally unplayable. You will get disconnected every 15-20 minutes and some spells (e.g. summons) outright don't work. I don't believe this game has had its multiplayer beta tested. Or if they did, they did not address the multiple and immediately obvious issues.Hate to say it, but i can't recommend this game for anyone that wants to play multiplayer right now.TL;DRSingleplayer: Yes! Win! Buy!Mutliplayer: I'd wait to see if they will actually fix the issues or if will be abandoned.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Solo is fun. Multiplayer requires the user to have reliable friends who will stick it thru to the end as you cannot continue if someone decides not to play anymore, nor can you substitute people in or out. So buyer beware if they are only looking at multiplayer. Other than that, worth 25 bucks imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful step up from all previous games. So far it shows true polish, creativity, and scope.Multiplayer was the focus of Heroes of Hammerwatch as an ARPG roguelike, this however is not that, perhaps falsely advertised to some that were expecting something different, multiplayer in this game functions more as a DND party, where all players are needed at all times of play. My honest recommendation is to play Hammerwatch first, see if you like the formula and gameplay. If so, this game is a must.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game so far! It is different from the original game, but I believe it is in a good way. There were a lot of difficulties with the original game that this one fixed. The revival process is better, and the graphics are amazing. I could list all of the good things, but I don't have the time. Highly recommend the game if you enjoyed either Hammerwatch or Heros of Hammerwatch.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: I really quite like it.The character controls and movement are a very comfortable improvement over the previous 2 games (though the stiff controls in the first game added to the "Gauntlet" feel). The new inventory and equipment management add depth not present before as well. Art design and music are, once again, fantastic.Multiplayer requires people joining to create a new character that's then tied to the host's save. Doesn't bother me. It's not an endless meta-progression/level grind like Heroes of Hammerwatch, or endless loot farming like diablo. Puts a damper on co-op progression if you aren't able to organize a game night with at least the hosting party.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review: Very good simple pixel ARPG. Satisfying mechanics, great pixel art. Doesn't take itself too seriously, and its pretty well polished.Caution: Set a framerate cap in game, if you leave it uncapped you will have runaway CPU/GPU temps and your game/PC will crash.Edit: This game is abandonware, don't waste your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

_childDocuments_.review:
Blight the Horrible and his dragon army have succeeded in the sinister plot to overthrow King Roland and bring destruction across the Kingdom of Herian.

Not all is lost as hope hides deep within the sewer system, where the King's resistance movement holds strong. On the King's order, a select few of mighty and skilled heroes have been entrusted with defeating Blight's dragons and restoring the Kingdom.

Adventure alone or gather your party to aid King Roland's resistance, all while helping villagers along the way. Battle beasts, finish off hordes of the undead, and face the forces of evil in this epic ode to classic ARPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Hammerwatch II

name: MONARK
detailed_description: Get special soundtrack with purchase of Deluxe or Ultimate Edition! About the Game Descent into Madness: Jump between exploring the Mist of the real world and fighting within the enigmatic Otherworld. Call upon allies, fight enemies, and unravel the mysteries surrounding your academy. Will you save the world or go mad and destroy yourself? Into The Mist and Beyond : Dive into a dark realm where reality and the self collide. The mysterious worlds you’ll explore are brought to life in a surreal, dark neo-fantasy style, with intricate character designs and evocative settings. Power of the Ego: Strengthen your Ego and customize the appearance and abilities of your Fiends. Unlock different Fiends to command in battle, and use the freeform tactical system to position your units and unleash destruction upon your enemies. Story How far will you go to save the ones you love? Could you face the threats that surround you? Could you face yourself? Your world is plunged into madness when the mysterious and deadly Mist surrounds Shin Mikado Academy. In order to save your friends, you enter the Otherworld, a Daemon-filled dimension beyond the real world. Within this enigmatic realm, you must learn to harness your Authority of Vanity and conjure a battalion of Fiends, whose power comes from the Ego of their master. Develop your Ego through various psychological tests to enhance the power of your Fiends, and lead your forces into battle to fight with and against the seven “Pactbearers” that are corrupting the academy. Embrace the power of your madness to gain strength, but take care not to delve too far, lest you risk losing yourself. Fellow students and instructors will lend you their aid in your quest to resolve the anomalies throughout the campus.

short_description: Could you face yourself and the threats around you to save the ones you love? Shin Mikado Academy is engulfed in a madness-inducing Mist, and only you can save everyone inside. Develop your Ego to break the pacts set by the Pactbearers and remove the corrupting Mist.

_childDocuments_.review: Obtained all Achievements in just under 80 hours. The game itself is fine; probably a solid 6.5-7/10. If you've played other FuRyu games, it is quite similar and has aspects from previous games. There is a rather empty overworld with a lack of meaningful exploration. Lots of empty classrooms and such. You'll be wandering different buildings for pieces of lore and some other benefits like permanent Stat boosts in the shape of Alter Egos.The combat gameplay is similar to Lost Dimension; turn-based tactics with back attacks, Assists, and the ability to Defer units, which will use up a unit's turn to give it to another at the cost of increasing the Madness gauge (similar to Sanity in Lost Dimension). You have regular attacks / Arts that cost HP, and Authorities which are similar to Magic / Skills. The MC has a unique ability called Resonance which lets you link up with unit(s), sharing buffs, debuffs, Statuses, etc. It's important to take advantage of it. Overall, the combat is good but you are very limited by the MOV stat, which determines how far you can move. Expect to grind a fair amount as well.Story is interesting enough, and the store page does a reasonable description of it. It's divided into Acts, and like some other FuRyu games, you'll have to go back to a "reset point" to go through different scenarios (in recent mind, Crystar had something like this) to then reach the True Ending.Graphics are pretty mediocre, but not the worst. It's serviceable. The art and character designs are nice, though.The music is mostly good. There are insert songs for the boss fights which are great; the normal battle themes, which differ in the areas you are in, are also pretty good. Overworld and cutscene music are overall fine. While traversing Mist areas, there's no music to keep you in suspense while exploring the unknown, which is a neat touch.Overall, I recommend getting this game at a discount if you can. I mostly got it because I wanted a new JRPG on PC to play after awhile, and I did end up enjoying my time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of anime games, so I’ve had my fair share of edgy plots and settings . This one though? It might actually take the cake.So the entire thing plays as a very structured turn-based JRPG. You’re thrown into this mysterious school setting with a main character that has amnesia and a “mist” that causes other students to go insane. The general game loop is extremely linear and follows the same pattern all the way through. You get some story dialogue, search a floor of some building within the school for a phone call, answer that phone call to engage in a battle in another realm, another story dialogue to close out that section, and then repeat this process over and over.That’s the entirety of Monark and honestly, it’s a bit too structured for my tastes. I don’t have anything against linear games, but I also like JRPGs that don’t just recycle the same pattern to completion. In Monark, the most exploration you get is maybe entering a classroom and picking up a healing item before moving to your actual objective. That’s it. Otherwise, you simply need to solve a small puzzle to find the source of the mist for that given floor.And I say puzzle, but that’s pushing it a bit given that most of the time you just need to memorize a small number or word sequence and enter it elsewhere - like the combination for a safe that you find on a sticky note in another room. The vast majority of the “puzzles” feel more like obstacles than something I enjoy doing.None of the combat actually takes place in the school setting, instead being set entirely in this “other realm” that you have to dial into. Upon doing so, you select which units to deploy, where to deploy them, and then go at it in a neat mashup of different combat systems. It’s turn-based, but you have freedom of movement and can shuffle around your units as you please. Positioning is key as there are things like back attacks and assisting other units based on their proximity to a given enemy.I liked the overall approach here. It’s not as strict as your regular turn-based JRPG, but still stays true to that experience without going full action-based. And there’s a good bit of depth too. You get entire skill trees per unit, the ability to outright defer your turn to any other unit, a full slate of status effects, buffs, and debuffs, and this cool madness and ascension system on top of it. These mechanics build on each other in cool ways, allowing you to set up combos with a bunch of assists flying everywhere or even situations where it becomes beneficial to let a unit go mad.Ultimately though, this all comes with one major flaw: you hardly ever need or get to use these mechanics. About 90% of fights you can finish simply by using basic attacks and a lot of the time, you have to go out of your way to actually use the more complex mechanics. Boss fights are really the only time I ever got to see units go mad, use ascension, or ever felt the need to inflict status effects and debuffs.There are two difficulties: normal and casual, with the latter simply reducing damage taken by 30% in exchange for a decreased item drop rate. Both difficulties, however, are subject to the game’s absolutely insane difficulty spikes. I thought I was doing completely fine up until the second boss, which one-shot me numerous times until I dropped the difficulty to casual, which simply made it a two-shot instead.Monark is a game that purposely keeps you underleveled and I found myself repeatedly grinding the optional fights over and over just to stay up to par with the bosses - there are no "normal" encounters. In most JRPGs, you can get by by simply fighting all encounters you run into or even dropping the difficulty if you want to play more leisurely, but Monark throws out both of those options. What you are left with is an incredibly grindy, repetitive, and unfulfilling game loop. And the fact that skeletons are the only enemies you fight does not help either.I feel it’s important to note that the dialogue and cutscenes take up probably about 50% of the game’s playtime, so it’s pretty beefy in that regard. That unfortunately doesn’t make it good though, and that’s ultimately the impression I got here. Mainly, I couldn’t shake this feeling that the story was trying to be too much and lacked focus.I understand what is going on, but not what the writers are trying to convey with the story. It’s like a mess of ideas all cobbled together that sounds cool on paper, but lack the depth and direction to really work. The entire first act, for example, works like a series of short stories about individual student’s psychological problems and a slight dive into each of their backgrounds. Each gets expanded on later, but I should note that the first act alone is like 15 hours of gameplay so you will be waiting a while for the story to really kick into gear.And it’s incredibly tropey too - to the point where it was hard to tell if I was playing a parody, but no, the game is actually taking itself seriously. This is the kind of anime story I would expect to appeal to 13 or 14 year olds, with so much edge I am surprised my controller didn’t cut me.Monark looks about what I would expect from an early PS4 or late PS3 JRPG. It’s not outright terrible, but not good either - just bland. The music though might be my second favorite thing under the combat. The vocal tracks that play during boss fights absolutely slap and the regular background music isn’t that bad either.You get a small set of graphical options to change and the game ran flawlessly at 1440p, 60 fps on my 1070 Ti so I guess I can’t complain. I had no issues with the controls on controller and the default keyboard and mouse layout isn’t that bad either. You do not get a cursor on screen though, so the mouse is just used for its buttons.Monark is a bit of a mess of ideas - some good, some bad, but most leaning a bit towards the latter. You get some nice combat, but coupled with some very grindy progression and lackluster gameplay outside of that combat. You get a story with some nice themes, but little coherence between all of these themes and filled with so many anime tropes that it’s hard to take seriously. A disappointment overall as a big JRPG fan.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr not a game worth the full price tag. If you decide to get it still, wait for a sale.I am honestly not sure how to feel about this game. If there was a mixed options I'd go for that but since there's only yes or no on steam, I think ultimately I have to go with no. I gotta preface that I am probably not the target audience. Apparently the game was made by former SMT Devs and the difficulty shows imo. Not even is the combat sometimes unfair even the puzzles can be hard to solve. The only reason I even got notice of this game was through the Boss themes. All of the boss themes are sung by the girls from Kamitsubaki Studio. When I was getting into them, I found the album and got interested in trying the game. The soundtracks are really nice but sadly the ingame versions aren't the full songs but like cut and looped.The story isn't to outstanding. You wake up in your school that is put under a barrier cause some mist is spreading that causes people to go mad. The rest basically follows you trying to get rid of the barrier and free everyone. The game has chapters but it isn't linear. Once you are done with the first boss you are free to start any of the other bosses in any order you want. The story itself is split into two parts. The second half focuses more on each individual party member and was better than the beginning but still its a rather mid story. Though it is somewhat darker/edgier in its tone. Personally I wasn't to fond of any of the main characters either. What I did like though was the small banter they had. Once they joined your party they would be in the clubroom. If you stood by idle they would start bantering with each other or goof around. The story is fully voiced both in eng and jp.The whole game takes only place in the school outside the fights. Each building you enter consist of basically 3 floors before you fight the boss. Each time you get to a new floor you are faced with a small puzzle section before you can do a fight to proceed. As mentioned earlier some of these puzzles are quite awful. Maybe its a skill issue but man I'd still be stuck on some if I hadn't looked them up. There are some that are really straightforward to solve, some require you to read carefully through the scattered notes you collect and some were so hidden or obscure I'd wonder how you'd find the solution. Fast travel is done from the map in the phone menu. You only get to the entrance of a building though so if you wanna backtrack somewhere you gotta walk up to the other floors. But then again the maps aren't big that it would make it a nuisance. They do tend to feel somewhat empty at times though. One of the bigger issues I had are the models though. Especially the teachers look horrifyingly bad, they are butt ugly. The students are basically a copy paste of each other but differ in size and pose. Like it feels like they just moved the height slider in a character creation mode and called it a day. Only the major characters have unique appearances and look more polished but it still not something I would have thought of a game that's priced at 60 eur.Finally the gameplay. Idk if there's an actual term for it but its basically a tactics game. You have a map where you move your characters around into position to do you various actions. After you are done its the enemies turn to move and do their thing. Next to the mc you will have four other main character that join your party. The rest of the party member consist of so called Vessels. These are the same characters as the enemy NPCs. They even share the same skillsets. The game has backstabs and counters. If you use a physical attacks from the front or the side the enemies will hit you back. If you attack from the back you do more dmg and no counter occurs. Also if your allies are in range, they will do an assist attack on the same target. This goes both for when you attack or when you are getting hit. There are two types of attacks. Arts and Authority. Arts are basically all the physical moves (+ some support and debuff skills on some units). Outside the basic attack and the resolve skill they all cost HP to use. Authority are instead your magic skills. All of which costs madness to cast. This is where the difficulty comes in. All human members can use the resolve skill to increase their awakening gauge (getting hit also increases it). Reaching 100% causes an awakening state that raises stats and sets madness to null. This is one way to clear and reset the madness gauge. While awaken you can also cast spells for free since you don't gain any madness. Reaching 100% Madness on the other hand will cause you to go berserk for 3 turns after which you self-destruct. Now the crucial part is the MC who can resonate with others to share buffs and debuffs. Since the Awakening is a buff if you resonate, you can share it with your party and clear madness that way. If you do resonate with someone with 100% Madness while being awakened (or someone else that is) you enter into Enlightenment instead. While enlighten you gain even more stats and the madness gauge stays at 100% instead. Early to mid it can be hard to plan around this though but once the buff goes it also resets your madness. Now what the game does not explain well is that the both buff state stay only for 3 actions (goes for all buffs tbf). So if you resonate with say 3 other members and they each take one action, after the third move the buffs ends. There is a skill you can learn that resets all the buff duration when you use your resonate skill again. Being mindful of the actions you have before the buff expires and resonating again to prolong them is key for the fights as not only does it buff your stats it also makes you tankier. Another benefit of resonance is that you will also share all your skills with each other. Two of the main characters for example don't have access to any authority skills themselves even though one of them has a very high psy stat (basically the atk stat for the spells). So the full potential only gets unlocked through the resonance with the right units. Now while the combat has its depth and nuances another issue is the heavy grind needed in this game. One thing this game does is that it has no random encounters. All fights you have to initiate yourself from your phone by calling a number. Throughout the game you will find various numbers to call that will lead to fights with certain drop. The Fertile Ground ones are the numbers you wanna call to farm spirit points for leveling. Something the game again does not tell you. Story related fights have jumps in their levels so you are expected to grind inbetween them to progress. There is no traditional level system. You have a skill tree where you spent spirit points to unlock new skill or raise a skills level. For each skill raised or unlocked you gain a level and your stats increases. Now the unfun part is spirit points are shared. There are 7 Vessels that will join you and with the 4 other members that join you you have a total of 12 chars to raise. That basically means 12 times the grind. And mind you the fight aren't done in under a minute meaning alot of time is just spent on grinding fights. So while the combat is imo very unique it becomes rather tedious than enjoyable. I personally sped up the process through some dishonest methods cause otherwise I probably would have not finished the game.In conclusion I feel like this is a flawed game. I can see a vision but the execution wasn't done well. It certainly has unique things to offer but the overall package leaves to be desired. While I did finish the game and even did all achievement I would find it hard to recommend trying this game unless it was on sale. Alot of playtime will just be fluffed out by grinding for levels. The actual story outside of that would probably just amount to 20hrs if I'm being honest.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game even though nearly every influencer/reviewer stated that it is mediocre at best.I cannot agree with the mixed to negative reviews I read for IMHO we got a niche but awesome experience at our hands.It gives of Persona/SMT-like vibes with the focus on the story and characters, everything and everyone has some kind of distopian vibe to it and it works pretty fine for me, the chapter as really enjoyable and the plot (as for as I have played) was interesting enough to keep me going.Only downfall is the battle system which is basic at best, it seems a bit like they wanted to dive really deep in a strategic direction but did not quite get to where they wanted to be. There are 2-3 differtent layers of buffs and debuffs (with an 100% super mode for your chars and a 100% madness/lost controll mode) but in the end you can (after some grind at the start of each level) play every fight with almost the same strategy. It really depends on the player how much you wanna dive into the systems.All in all I would strongly recommend the game for everyone that a.) likes challenging turn based tactics and won't mind a bit of grindb.) seeks something Persona-esque c.) likes games that are based around darker themes like the seven deadly sinsd.) people that like to make personality tests in their free time.

_childDocuments_.review: The first section of the game is fun but part way through the second section and closer to the final part the games problems really start to show. The sound track in the game is an absolute banger especially the boss themes each theme is unique and fits well with whats currently happening with in the story. The gameplay is your typical turn based strategy game so theres not really anything all that new here you summon your fiend partners all based of the 7 deadly sins and that leads in the games other problem. Variety. Everything in the game is a different variant of a skeleton and after awhile it's hard to tell if any of them are different aside from what abilities each one can use. It's especially a problem on the enemy side it's just bland and repetitive. The game does has a pretty unique art style to it i will give it that it was certainly interesting to look at. Back to the forced level grinding if you don't know of certain phone numbers which i highly recommenced looking up you are going to be grinding out a lot. Once you know the perfect method to levelling even then it's an off shoot because the skills you'd use also attacks you directly and that has a pretty frequent chance of critical hitting your main character killing you instantly no matter what level you are on. Theres not much more i can say sadly i really wanted to like this but i just couldn't even bring my self to finish it. Just the final section of act 2 really drags the game down. Repeating the same dungeons over and over again is not a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Judging by the first impressions, it is what it seems: an edgy low-budget jRPG with some neat ideas and uneven execution. Locations are empty and not detailed, characters look like crude dolls, even stylish filters can't entirely hide this. _childDocuments_.review: is a story-driven JRPG with a decent amount of grinding that's a fairly recent release from NIS America, Inc. Aside from the expected anime-style 3D artwork, the game is accompanied by fantastic music and all spoken dialogue. For the price, you can probably expect a bit more than the game has to offer, though it is still an enjoyable game overall. If you don't like to read story dialogue or if you don't like to do any kind of grinding, this game is probably not for you. Otherwise, it's reasonable to give it a shot if you think it's the right price.In  you conveniently take on the role of a student with amnesia with the goal to safe the world. A strange mist appears in the halls at Shin Mikado Academy, driving people into madness if they stay in the mist for too long.Inside the mist is another reality, the Otherworld, where the Daemons and the Monarks reside. There are 7 Monarks and they are based on the 7 deadly sins (pride, gluttony, etc.). Some humans can have contact with this Otherworld, these are the Pactbearers. You are one such individual, and you will need to face the growing darkness in order to save those you care about.The story is rather interesting and at times eerie. This sets the tone for the game.Each time you step into the mist, you need to find a Pactbearer. Along the way, you will need to solve various puzzles. To gather clues, the other students in the mist will lead you in the right direction. You also cannot stay too long in the mist, since it will also drive you increasingly crazy. The infirmary is where you go to heal up.The actual battles in the game are turn-based. Each member of your team can walk a few steps and then use an action. If the enemies are too far away, you may need to wait a turn. Waiting heals for a percentage of your health as well. At the price of increasing madness, you can use one teammate to give another an extra turn.The attacks and usable skills will cost certain percentage of madness or your overall health. You will need to keep a close eye on both in order to succeed.After winning each battle, you will get some items and some spirit points, these are needed to level up. In leveling up, you will will choose to upgrade a skill and your experience level will also increase.Each member of your team need to be leveled up individually, and new members start at level 1. So you will need to do a decent amount of grinding in order to gather enough spirit points. for the level-ups.The graphics are in the usual 3D anime style and they are okay. For a €59,99 game, I guess I expected a bit more from the artwork and graphical details.The music is really fantastic, especially during the boss fights. All of the dialogue is spoken, with choice of Japanese and English, so that is very nicely done.The game can be played entirely with a controller.I think €59.99 is a bit steep for this game. It does offer a lot of gameplay, but considering everything together as a whole, I would wait for a sale. has its ups and downs, specifically it's enjoyable if you get into the story and are okay with grinding a lot. So there are limitations on who might like this game.Personally I don't mind grinding, and I have really enjoyed the game until now. I have not yet finished the game. I can recommend the game based on my own experience.Verdict: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to recommend and I'd much rather give it a mixed review if I could.Thematically this game is a banger, I love the art style a lot and the boss OSTs are phenomenal, worth listening to by themselves honestlyCombat is pretty fun, tactics-esqueCharacters are cool each with their own personality and well written backstoriesThe story itself is pretty good and is done in a non-linear fashion, after the first building you're given options to go wherever you want. The second half of the game is a similar thing although it's kind of a time-loop so it can end up feeling really same-y and I was definitely over it by the time it came to an endThere's also fun personality tests/quizzes from both NPCs in the buildings and from one of the characters, was a nice additionOverall, the combat, the characters, the art, the music is great!But the game has a lot of negatives for me personallyFirstly, I had crazy stuttering issues throughout, doing a workaround posted in the discussions helped but didn't fix it completely which obviously detracts from the experienceThe puzzles are kinda wack, some are okay but some are straight up evil with how you're expected to figure them out (luckily google exists)Enemy variety is really badThe overworld is bland and all of the NPCs are pretty much copies of each otherThe actual gameplay loop is pretty repetitive/stale - Go to building, clear 3 floors (Each floor is basically puzzle->fight), fight boss on third floor, repeat until end of game, of course most games' loops are pretty meh when broken down like this so maybe it was exacerbated by the boring worldAlso this game is grindy - there's an easier difficulty but this does nothing to lessen the grind, it doesn't give you more exp or anything like that, My advice would be to either use a cheesy build to farm exp or just straight up cheat, pick your poisonOverall it's mediocre but it's highs outweighed the lows for me, it definitely has it's fair share of problems but I think if any of the game seems to call to you grab it on sale, it's a niche title but it's not horrid

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not TOO far in this game, but I have, mixed feelings about this game so far. Combat is interesting, plot and aesthetic are interesting, but the thing that turns me off of this game, is the pace, it is quite slow, I don't really have a problem with slow RPGs, but this game is, well, designed to be an interconnected almost open world JRPG, which is fine. I don't mind very open ended RPGs, but this game ends up being almost a tad directionless in places. It feels, not undercooked, but overcooked, it's very experimental but they went all in on the experimental part, and just didn't really bother making the game anything OTHER than this weird experimental open world RPG. It's VERY unique, but you either like the absolutely unique nature of this game, or you don't.I LOVE the idea of having your level DIRECTLY result from currency use and your XP also being used as money, I love the idea of having several minions who's ranking and power directly result from the parts you build them with, and your stats. I don't mind the trademark FURYU combat jank. What I do mind, is the first area being a railroad and then suddenly transitioning into a directionless next step. I didn't really feel like there was a point to anything other than "objective", and then suddenly I felt like I was just wandering around triggering story events for the sake of finding things to do.This game is unique in whatever it's doing. That much is for sure. But is it anything other than a fun curiosity? Not really. I almost wanna say "less is more" when it comes to this game's ridiculous open nature. Like, gimme sidequests that make me want to go to SPECIFIC areas, and put events there to get me interested in that area's events. Put sidequests everywhere so I GO everywhere.The reason VASTLY open worlds work in most games is because it makes you FEEL like there's something to do around every corner. This game doesn't feel like that, it's just, see scene, get story chunk, see next scene, except localized to one of many chunks you can bounce between.I WANT to like this game more, the aesthetic and story are interesting, but I feel like I'm playing a Visual Novel with light gameplay elements. That wasn't really what I was expecting, and I'm probably going to come back to it later. There's nothing WRONG with this game, and it's a GOOD game, it's just lacking in key areas, and the rest of the game is so well thought out, I just have to assume the devs didn't WANT to make this game more traditional.Also, more minor complaint, literally every single basic enemy in this game is a Skeleton with different swappable body parts, there is no enemy variety, but my lizard brain kept saying "WELCOME TO THE BONE ZONE" internally every time I entered a new Skeleton filled Otherworld area.7/10, grab this on sale, and if you specifically want this experimental style of game. It's more good than bad, despite all I've said, but it's a very much "this could've been cooler, but it wasn't from a lack of time and effort, the direction was just unclear" situation, kinda like how I feel about Monster Hunter Stories, or even Caligula Effect, or like, Zwei The Arges Adventure, or even Ni No Kuni - Shikkoku No Madoushi and all of those games got improved sequels/remakes (in the case of the last one, the remake, Ni No Kuni - Wrath of the White Witch, is literally one of the few 10/10 games in my book), so here's hoping MONARK 2 fixes on these flaws.As a side note, what in the everloving ♥♥♥♥ did Lancarse do in this game's development cycle? I don't really see their usual marks anywhere on this game, this feels entirely like a FURYU project and it's strange. Lancarse previously made several games that have hit VERY high on my ranking scale for one reason or another, such as Etrian Odyssey 1 and 2 (Not the Untold remakes, although those are VERY similar to the originals), 7th Dragon (DS Original, fan translated to English), Shin Megami Tensei - Strange Journey (and Redux too), and Persona Q2 (Not Q1), also Lost Dimension and Zanki Zero and some other games that have been on my list of games to play.This game is so unlike the rest of their catalog I have to wonder what they actually did to get a credit on this game. If you haven't yet, do yourself a favor and play Etrian Odyssey Untold 1 and 2, and Shin Megami Tensei Strange Journey Redux, they actually emulate QUITE nicely in Citra, and are LEGENDARY games in my opinion, and they are apart of what sparked my love for DRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: I won’t spoil any of the game’s plot in this review. I will only provide a brief synopsis of the first hour of the game’s story and characters. Any screenshots shown herein will be non-spoiler in nature and will be from the first few hours of gameplay. I’ll explain game elements present later in the game, but I won’t spoil its associated narrative.You play as a protagonist you name, who is a student in a Japanese private school named Shin Mikado Academy. There’s a strange mist surrounding the school that is also seeping into the school’s buildings, such as its library, the first and second-year buildings, and the school club building used for gym activities. You team up with other students and the faculty to remove the mist and to eventually escape the school. The premise I provided is very simple, but there are a lot of interesting plot twists and the plot is heavily character-focused.The cutscenes are done in a visual-novel style, with beautifully illustrated character portraits on-screen as they voice their lines. The 3D character models in the background, however, aren’t too detailed. You can choose to play the game with either English or Japanese voice acting. I played through the game with the English voice acting and all of the voiced dialogue was very professionally done.Monark is an extremely plot-heavy game. Most of the cutscenes in this game are actually very long, and my controller would turn itself off regularly because it would think I’m not using it (not pressing a button for over half an hour). The plot is very character-focused and there are many scenes where the characters overcome their inner conflict. In later parts of the story, characters will explain their backstory in significant detail and reveal their insecurities, and then as the plot progresses even further they will work on improving themselves. These kinds of internal struggles vary vastly between the different party members you recruit, such as a child prodigy who has difficulty connecting personally with her family and peers, to a man who is seeing his family business struggle with corruption and incompetency.Tadashi Satomi, the writer of the first two Persona games, is a writer for Monark, as well as the The Caligula Effect series. He did a great job as the writer of this game because there is a significant amount of attention to detail with the main characters. If you played The Caligula Effect and enjoyed the character development in those games, you can expect to see more of it in Monark.My big criticism of the game is that the beginning is extremely slow, and I can see it putting off a lot of newcomers of JRPGs. Too much jargon is unfortunately a big problem in Monark, and although it doesn’t start off too bad it starts to compound further and further, like how in school if you don’t understand one concept early on you start to get lost very quickly when new concepts begin to build on the earlier concept.It’s really meant for fun, and your ego stats aren’t the same as your combat stats so answering the questions and also reading the answers was very interesting and didn’t add stress to the game. There are also plenty of opportunities to max these ego stats out and they never get reduced.But at the same time, it’s all reading-based and not a voiced cutscene, so I can see it putting people off too. Vanitas even gives the protagonist several “Choose Your Own Adventure” kinds of personality test, one of which has your protagonist saves a princess in an over 30 page text adventure minigame. It has really good writing and is chock-full of illustrations, and when you complete them for the first time you can look at all of the answers and the mentality behind them in the lore menus.The plot is very slow in the beginning and the plotline between Nozomi and Kurama is boring compared to the plotlines seen later in the game because it involves politics in the student council. You actually don’t have experience to level up in this game, you level up naturally by buying the skills in a skill tree with points, which is also a nice idea I don’t see often in other games.The game is pretty hard early on because you need to get used to its mechanics. Each strategy RPG has its own quirks: Fire Emblem, Final Fantasy: Tactics, and Disgaea for example all have their own mechanics, and Monark is no exception. Enemies will counter attack unless you strike them from behind, so if you’re normally striking enemies you can get defeated early on from their counterattacks.The game adds a lot of different gameplay twists the more you play and it does get complex, but the gameplay really grows on you as you unlock more options to break the game. You have moves that consume a percentage of the character’s HP, but it’s often worth it because these moves may deal a lot of damage.Your characters have a “madness” and an “awakening” bar. Using certain Authority skills causes madness to go up, which you don’t want because when they go mad they will indiscriminately attack both enemies and allies.Another criticism I have is that for most of the game, you can only use the protagonist and one human character as your only human characters, even though you recruit several other human characters. As well, when you recruit a human character as part of the game’s narrative, you are separated from the rest of the cast during that plot line with the exception of getting two extra cutscenes for returning to the student club room and going to the infirmary. There’s not an easy way around this though because the game lets you choose which order to recruit the human characters in. The game scales enemies stats up as you progress through the game, meaning it doesn’t matter which order you choose to go through the game in.The plot really gets going though when you recruit all the characters, then they all interact which each other normally in the story, but when you’re recruiting human characters it definitely feels discrete and formulaic for a while. To get to the actual ending, you need to complete all four character routes in the second half which involves going through all of their backstories, and some of them are really good. The intermission between the two halves of the game is full of plot twists that shocked me and even made me feel emotional. It’s just that it takes a while for the plot to get good.Although I really enjoyed learning about the characters in detail in their routes, the game does recycle a lot of content in its second half, so you’ll have explored each area twice.After completing all the character routes in Monark you’ll get to the ending of the game, which has enemies and bosses in the level 70’s. After that, there’s a postgame where you can get more endings as well, but the postgame is challenging and involves you facing level 99 enemies, it’s very difficult.In total, I spent 60 hours getting to one of the post-game endings. The time you spend on the game will vary significantly depending on if you stop to gather collectible items and lore, and if you talk to the generic NPCs. I played through the Persona 1 and the Persona 2 duology when I was younger, and it had similar faults to Monark: repetitive gameplay, but there was a phenomenal narrative and characters tucked away if you were looking for it. If you’re willing to go through it and are patient, give this game a shot because the plot really does get good and I was amazed with all of the foreshadowing there was in the beginning. If you don’t care about graphics too much and can enjoy a game for its narrative, give Monark a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually love this game. The battle system is a breath of fresh air for a JRPG fan, and I want more monark if not just for that. People complain that this game is too grindy, but i honestly cant complain because the amount of levels available, the fun battles and the ability to do said grinding whenever you want at your own pace. The story is also very good, while the location and some plot points may seem familiar the story itself is unique and has some genuinely surprising moments. This game comes from Devs that have previously worked on SMT titles, and thats what made this a day one purchase for me, but this game stands on its own, feeling 'inspired' by SMT without being a low budget carbon copy of it. Speaking of low budget, I agree with everyone complaining about the graphics. I have a $4000 pc, and i like my resolutions and frame rates high, but this game does look like a switch game. The designs and art direction are top tier, dont get me wrong, but internally the game is 1080p no mater what and locked at 60fps and the models lack most facial animations. that aside everything else about this game is amazing, including the soundtrack. i havent heard a soundtrack this good in a video game in a very long time. persona can eat its heart out, this game dosent have a single dud track. its all straight bangers, and i reccomend the soundtrack dlc. TLDR, its sad this game released a couple days before elden ring, as 90% of my friends list on pc and consoles playing that right now. this game is gunna get slept on for awhile, But I swear that if you are a fan of JRPGS this is not one to miss, there is so much to love about monark, and after 90 hours and 100% achievements im praying for a sequel and the game hasnt been out for a whole month. Thanks Lancarse, Monark is a breath of fresh air, and you released a game that gave an atlus shill a chill.

_childDocuments_.review: [This review contains minor game mechanics spoilers but NO STORY SPOILERS.]I was very hyped about Monark back in June 2021 when I heard some people that worked on Shin Megami Tensei worked on the project. You can definitely feel the SMT influence in Monark's atmosphere, and as a Megaten fan, the game didn't need more to grab my attention.After getting the 100%, I decided to write a review, because Monark deserves some more love. There will be a little list of pros and cons, followed by some others stuff I thought needed to be mentionned, and my overall thoughts about the game.Pros:- Stunning artworks and artistic direction as a whole is very effective- The atmosphere in the Mist is very creepy and oppressing, and I'm all for it- Resonance, Awakening, Madness and Enlightenment are very interesting and fun mechanics to play around, especially when you know what you're doing- The phone numbers mechanic is so cool and fun to use- Characters aren't as bad as people make them seem, I personally enjoyed most of them- Story isn't stellar but is definitely good and deserves your attention- Gameplay is great and fun, but...Cons:- Gameplay loop gets very repetitive, especially towards the end- Graphics are VERY underwhelming for a 2022 game, and the characters personalities suffer a lot from lack of good animations and facial expressions - Getting a "game over" either by dying in battle or getting your MAD to 100% in a dungeon doesn't have any impact whatsoever and isn't punishing in the slightest. You'll just respawn at the infirmary like nothing happened, without losing anything. - Using Ailments and Stat Debuffs is pretty much useless. Why would you try to charm an enemy with 30% chance to do so, when you can just one shot them? Makes almost half of the spells available useless.- Protagonist is very uncharismatic outside of battle.The game as a smooth learning curve, and you'll feel pretty powerful once you know how to play around your Fiends, Enlightenment and Resonance, even when being underleveled. People saying you can "auto attack your way through the game" either don't know what they are talking about, or they played in Casual mode (which I don't recommend). And if some of you reading this need a bit of advice to master the art of Enlightenment, my discord is in my profile... Some "guides" online are physically painful to read.There are some puzzles that you'll need to solve to progress, they aren't extremely difficult, but some will require you to think a little still. I thought it was a cool addition, personally. There is a bunch of collectibles that gives you a lot of lore or student's background stories, and I had a good time reading them all, helps with the world building.Monark could've been an even better game: you can see the developpers couldn't go as far as they wanted with some of the aspects of the game, especially technically, which is really a bummer. But overall Monark was a great experience, and I really recommend all JRPG fans out there to try out the game. You will have a good time for sure! (And I'll be happy to discuss the game more in depths on discord if some of you are interested!)
