_childDocuments_.review: This game does a good job introducing more mechanics as you play through the campaigns. They stories are pretty awesome they totally have that Tales from the crypt feel. My only minor gripe is that i feel a lot of the difficulty is just not knowing what's going to happen. Usually takes me one or two tries for every map but once I know whats coming it becomes incredibly easy to win. I still had fun though. I wish there was more voice acting cause the voice actor for the puppet is really good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This is a worker placement game with the fantastic aesthetic of the old EC comics. I enjoyed my trip through the game and felt it had a good value at the asking price.The ending is suitably over the top and very much in the spirit of the old Tales from the Crypt.My only complaint is that I cannot believe there isn't a "auto-pause game when Agent activity completes" setting.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic strategy game! The mechanics are easy to understand and use in the game. They never get stale because they keep intoducing new twists on them in every campaign.The pulp art style is amazing and the stories are bloody and really fun to follow along.The only complaint: I WANT MORE!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a huge recommendation from me. The art alone, which reminds me of old-timey/pulp comics, was enough to get me interested but there's a great game behind the art. Trying to figure out how to best expend your influence and how to best assign your agents seems easy at first glance but there's a lot of room for optimization - something the game lets you change mid-run so you don't have to be afraid of messing up. I was also genuinely intrigued to learn more of the story behind each character, including my agents, and it quickly became apparent that there's more going on here than the game first lets on. As a fan of board games, Fear Machine also does a great job of capturing the feeling of playing a board game. Overal, can't recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a blast with this. Love the optics, the subtle Cultist Simulator vibe, the sound. It is a strategy game but it also has semblances of a puzzler to some extent. On the normal difficulty it is also quite manageable if you think about most of your moves, I only had to redo like two missions overall.I'd gladly have a DLC, it is over a bit quick.One more thing, tho, although the game is obviously satirical and comedic, it also has very serious undertones which sometimes took me by surprise. Just a heads up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: More like a conditional recommend but that's what you get when Steam has a binary rating system!!! It's a neat kind pulp horror Monkey's Paw story which is largely about how Corporations and various Right Wing movements create and exploit fear in order to advance their agendas. That, like, theme works well, and the game never lets the leaders off those movements off the hook with its supernatural conceit. Also, the stories are fun and the art is cute. On that level the game is a success. It makes reference to various urban legends, including some particularly homophobic and antisemitic ones, and while it doesn't explicitly deal with that homophobic or antisemitism, it does always operate on the level of "these myths are false and are working against your interests," even within the logic of the gameworld. The less successful bit is, like, the gameplay. It basically plays like a very simple strategy game, and the strategy matches the theme well, but it's all a bit too... Simple. Like, it's not far above the level of the kind of phone game where you just click on the right things at the right times. There's no challenge, difficult decisions or deep thought required. To the creators' credit, they obviously know that, and so the game doesn't outstay its welcome or try to provide a pointless Endless mode. But I do wish there was a bit more I could sink my teeth into on that level.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The art style and theme is so fun that it makes up for what is kind of a shallow gameplay experience. It's the kind of game you hope gets a bigger sequel where they can take the good things with their art direction and marry it with more complex mechanics. The game is really pretty simple, but I'm definitely pleased with the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me of the intrigue & mystery I felt when first playing Cultist Simulator. The world-building and the art both make long strides in helping to keep the gameplay loop fun. The cards you play each help to weave the story you're telling, which is often quite brutal. In my last run, I helped to gaslight all of Europe into banning all useful pharmaceuticals in lieu of my own flawed products, and that's some of the more lighthearted content. Overall, if you appreciate card games, strategy, and horror then this game is a pretty good call.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: It is a short game. I finished it effortlessly in about 10 hours.The presentation is top notch, it really nails the aesthetic and it's the game's big selling point for me.The sound design is maybe sometimes a bit obnoxious or confusing. But nothing too distracting.The mechanics... you get it dumped on you at first and it may a bit too much at once, but once you've sorted them out they flow properly without an hitch, and you get a few new twists as chapters progress to keep you entertainemend.The story is dark. Conspiracy theories, betrayals, and all the worst crimes all around. A bit predictable once you get the gist of what it will be like, but enjoyable.Overall, enjoyable but not a real challenge, and a bit short, though the game's format really lend itself to additional chapters so I won't be surprised if DLCs pop up later
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The Fabulous Fear Machine is, oddly enough, a strategy simulation game based on pulp horror comic books of yesteryear. There's a few gruesome situations depicted alongside old myths like sewer gators and alien invasions, but most of the time you're going to be staring at maps and timers ticking down as your agents finish their tasks. Across three campaigns, each of which stars someone who puts their own desires over the well-being of others and gets hit with karmic repercussions in the end, you'll be establishing bases, gathering resources, and using them to spread fearful propaganda until the whole country has been influenced into believing you're the only one that can save them from the imminent peril you convinced them exists. I'd make a politics joke, but one of the campaigns actually is all about helping a guy using racism to get elected president of the USA...I beat this game's three campaigns in a little over ten hours, intentionally delaying on occasion to fully rank up Fears and fill up the compendium. Everything after that has been attempted cleanup, with the most infuriating being an achievement for taking out the final rival in the final mission of the game, after weakening them in earlier missions of the campaign. This is because, when they show up, they don't do anything, probably because I've already basically conquered the map to keep my resources from going negative. Do I need to self-destruct my own headquarters and start building back up from scratch for the enemy to decide they can interfere? Did I accidentally mess up and need to restart the entire campaign for the opportunity to arise? Spending roughly an hour to even reach the end of the final mission and then be just flat-out denied the event needed to take them out has made me rather grumpy! (UPDATE: I did in fact have to restart and purposely not fully investigate the zeppelin before the final mission so they wouldn't be stuck in an endless Thinking loop on my next attempt.)Aside from that, however, I suppose I don't have major complaints. The art and aesthetic are fantastic, and something I rarely see in the media I consume. Difficulty feels fair, having beat every campaign on Normal on my first try since that and Easy are your only options when you start, and are in fact the only difficulties even after winning the game. I can see some people calling the mechanics far too tedious and repetitive for how much time you have to sink into playing it, but I felt like there was still enough to keep me interested, at least my first time through.In conclusion, I'm not sure this Fear Machine has really earned being called Fabulous, but I'm willing to promote an Adequate Fear Machine to strategy-minded people interested in a good creepshow.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sorry, but this game feels less like "Tales from the Crypt" and more "INFOWARS".A lot of it seems to be about how the "big pharama" manipulates your fears. This borders on covid denialism. Maybe things change after the first scenario, but I found the story to be less paranormal and purely conspiratorial. The first "legend" the game has you fabricate is climate change. Getting people to wear masks generates more control over them. Most of the "legends" I employed weren't folk legends or paranormal events, but actual political issues. Maybe I was unlucky, but it didn't sit right with me.Gameplay wise, it feels like someone took 'Plague Inc.' slowed it down and made it far too complicated.The only pro was the comic book style visuals, which are very nice. I will be trying to refund this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The game is heavily inspired by 50s-style comic books, especially those like EC Comics' Tales from the Crypt and similar horror comics. As such, the stories tend towards unsympathetic protagonists getting what they have coming to them through ironic punishments, and the art style takes its cue from those comics as well.The gameplay is fairly simple - dispatch your minions to gather resources from the cities you've influenced with the seed of fear planted at the start of the mission, and use those resources to explore further, expand your influence and spread the message of the Fear Machine in the form of urban legends and conspiracy theories, while also countering your rivals' attempts to do the same.What brings some challenge to the game is the limited number of minions you have - never more than two, and you always seem to have three or four things you want them to do, so you are always having to prioritize your tasks to get the most bang for your minion's buck.While the game as a whole is fun and engaging, I wish that the campaigns were longer - there are only three campaigns, and none longer than four missions. The second campaign is especially short. This means that while it might be worth going through each campaign more than once to hunt for achievements or better your results, there's still a fairly short limit on the playtime of the game. I hope the developers get the opportunity to put together some more campaigns for us, as I'd love to revisit Kirlian's machine in the future if they do.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely masterfully crafted game. The gameplay, art style, and music and tie together beautifully. Each new mechanic meshes with the others and builds upon the others, and each is explained in an easy-to-understand way. The writing in this game is a major highlight, with grimly amusing card descriptions, great character interactions, and genuinely unnerving Agent narration. An amazing experience that kept me hooked the entire time.I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys strategy games, pulp/horror writing, or the art style. If you enjoyed Cultist Simulator, you'll love this game.I have two small complaints. The first is a minor UI issue: please change the Exit Game button to say something other than "Abandon Mission." It made it seem like a Give Up button. The second is that some of the words you choose when upgrading cards should definitely fit, but don't. One of the words in the Mystery Meat card is Skull, which I thought fit perfectly given that one of the clues mentioned finding rat bones in food.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: for those this game resonates with it is one of the most refreshing game experiences in a long time I loved every minute and it left me wanting moreits not huge but is a ride well worth the entry feeif you enjoyed tales of the crypt keeper and creepshow you will feel right at homeif you like satire on the way those in power manipulate through fear then indulge your evil sideif you like conspiracy theories then maybe you too can be one of the lizard peoplewile this game isn't for everyone for those who dig its vibe it stands out as something special
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: An unusual strategy game with some interesting themes and a distinctive style. Spoiler warning: Yes, we are definitely the baddies. Some of the rivals are, too. Others, not even remotely.The writing is intriguing and illuminates a number of concerning trends in our society, in between the large collection of spooky urban and rural legends, myths and campfire tales the actual gameplay revolves around. It's sort of an odd mix of distressing and refreshing, like watching Jon Stewart or Last Week Tonight. The irony may be lost on some, but there's definitely more than just some random atrocity fanfiction on display here.All of that said, there are some rather dark themes being explored here and sensitive players may wish to steer clear. It is by no means going to be a  journey through the darkness of the fear machine and the hearts of men and women... but it might invite some thoughts that a lot of people need to have more of, in which case I must recommend it as a spooky and potentially eye-opening experience.If you're already well-supplied with the spirit of caring about your fellow human beings and being reasonably wary of demagogues and divisive rhetoric, you'll likely be fine without it... but it's still a kooky, morbid, weird time of a game, if that's your cup of tea.Somewhat recommended for fans of creepy fiction, modern delusion and blobs of fear spreading across maps.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This an unfortunate game for me.If you get intrigued enough by the style and light jokes after 2 hours, it may work for you. It excels on presentation and art style, in a nostalgic way to some.If it is not enough to get you hooked than... it's not for you.I painstakingly played tutorial + 1 full stage and got bored of how the entire game was monotonous and repetitive. Most of the time, it was just a waiting simulator.Even liking a lot of slow pace simulators (Potion Craft, Sim City, dotAge, Kingdom New Lands...), it managed to be too simple and slow without giving me any curiosity, challenge or novelty. Truly sad considereing how unique it looked.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The fabulous fear machine is an amazing game hosting such incredible characters as-Unethical eye-ence-The nice one-Misfortune teller-Satantos-and more! The game follows you attempting to control and spread your political agenda by spreading rumors to create fear in adults and children alike in order to prey on their insecurities and (in)secure their votes for whatever you're doing while also managing your rivals, who are probably morally better than you in most cases. You get to spread noble causes like animal testing, christianity, man made viruses, and even homophobia! The game features an incredible artstyle, fun gameplay, and some weird death plants. 10/10 i like Jimmy. Really hoping for a dlc or prequel or something.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I have noticed absolutely 0 Gameplay-Progress this far. The only thing that gets unlocked is new levels for your Agents, which results in a Statbuff - underwhleming to say the least. The 2nd Campaign plays the same as the first one, and i lost interest. The game looks amazing, i love the artstyle and Narration. I love the premise aswell, controlling the masses through fear e.t.c... its just the gameplay which bores me. Its repetetive and i most often dont do anything other than press the "Fast Forward" button. Strategy seems to be irrelevant, or barely influental as so far i have not had to think about mmy actions. This game was destined for better
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The theme and premise of the game are executed extremely well. It would be incredibly easy to teeter into different political leanings, but the writers here managed to acknowledge widespread paranoia + propaganda without taking a for/against side, which is admirable. The writers here do, naturally, argue against corruption and valuing profits over human life, but do so without being pedantic or patronising. 90% of games that attempt something similar lack the history and the application of potential solutions to complement the writing of the game, not because people are stupid, but because to accomplish what has been done here is extremely challenging, despite the developer's making it look like a simple novella in game format. Kudos to the devs and writers. 5/5 Story/Atmosphere. 3/5 Gameplay. Well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy staring at a map and cackling maniacally? If so, this might be the game for you! As far as map-staring simulators go, the Fabulous Fear Machine isn't the deepest or longest. You can finish the entire campaign over a weekend if you know what you're doing, and it wasn't quite engrossing enough for me to redo campaigns just to unlock all the lore and such.Still. It was worth it. If you aren't put off by the game's nihilistic cynicism and the utter bastardy of its protagonists (even if they do get their comeuppance at the end) , you'll find a lovely, darkly entertaining, and absolutely fiendish game. If I hear they're putting out DLC, I'll be right on board for that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Map Game Weirdo or even a Misinfo Weirdo, this game is very engrossing. The mission-focused gameplay makes things very digestible, as opposed to EUIV or CK3, which can take hours, days or more. The story, graphics and sound are all entertaining but don't go too deep. If you're into this sort of thing, if you love diving down rabbit holes, spreading your influence and aren't afraid of... THE FEAR, then give this game a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Comic book art and story telling are great. Game play is interesting and could be expanded upon with updates. Needs a game plus as the campaign felt a little constrained. Not too crazy about the woke political overtones. A lot of gamers might be disheartened if the developer make so much familiarity political characters a little too familiar to real life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: While I only played the tutorial, everything I saw in it felt way too reactionary for the game to have anything meaningful, or even simply true, to say about media's constant fear narratives. The game basically opens with climate change denial.But hey, if you're a weird and fashy Alex Jones enjoyer, you might like it. At least the art was nice.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: VERY VERY fun game. Beautiful artwork and nice atmosphere. It gets pretty easy once you get the hang of it.There is three campaigns. The first and last one are great, lovely protagonists, good and interesting stories, fun concepts. The second campaign is very short and the protagonist isn't interesting at all. The ending of that campaign is bad. All in all It feels shoehorned in.I would LOVE a DLC for this. I enjoyed my playthrough a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I just love this game. It's not incredibly difficult and the game doesn't take that long to complete ; perhaps one of my gripes is that this addictive ghost train is over quite quickly. However there's a bit of replay value as you can't unlock all the games fears on the first play through. However what I would have liked to have seen is perks / rewards / fears at the end of each scenario which you could unlock depending on how well you did. At the end of each scenario you're currently graded on how well you handled it's challenges however these "scores" dont seem to do anything except I suppose give the perfectionist in me a little pat on the head.The game really is quite fun watching the world fall under the shadow of fear as you progress and the stories are quite entertaining and dark. You start off small with a bunch of regional objectives which are fulfilled with the spread of chaos and fear using your limited agents. As each scenario progresses and you ramp up your dreaded campaign there's various elements thrown in for you to deal with but with limited agents it ends up being a game of priorities and juggling to ensure you balance out the spread of fear with combating those who want to stop you. A great little gem and I can already see the DLC potential!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Really neat game, I found the concept to be quite original, and the mechanics may seem a little confusing at first, but you get the hang of it in no time. There's a nice tutorial in the beginning, too.It gives me a strategy board-game feeling, with a very cool art style and storytelling, definitely worth the play for anyone interested in indie games. So far the game felt moderately challenging and very fun and engaging to play. I do wish they added some more variety to it, but I'm definitely enjoying it very much.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: So, I would recommend this game, but with a few caveats.First off, the game is short. I've played for less than 9 hours and got through all 3 campaigns.You might get more playtime out of it if you like reading descriptions, but probably not *that* much.Second off, the game doesn't shy away from grim subject matter and can get quite graphic.Third off, this game is very political. Not a bad thing, but something to keep in mind. It's less of a "you're the leader of a bunch of pulpy monsters" and more "the greedy and hateful manipulate the masses".Fourth off, while the overall message is pretty clear and I'd say decent, there's some weirdness that can raise eyebrows, as some negative reviews point out.The gameplay is decent, but the story is, ya know, less than pleasant. But if you're in for that, go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the negative comments I see think this game is trying to trick you into believing conspiracy theories or something. It is really just a game. It is not trying to trick you into believing or doing anything.It is, however, a very good game that I highly recommend to anyone who likes strategy or card games. You play as someone who is willing to do whatever it takes to gain power, money, or fame. You will often be racing against the clock with people trying to accomplish the same thing.It also has stories that aren't necessary to the gameplay, so it's not a big deal if you don't want to do much reading.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A hidden gem of smart storytelling: immersive, replayable, and pleasingly pulpy.First of all, some reviewers completely missed the point of the game. It’s about how fears control society by dividing people, creating and spreading rumors, superstitions, and stereotypes. The game does not endorse the messages or behaviors of its characters, which becomes very clear as their stories unfold and through Krilian’s interactions with them. In the end, you can't control fear, and at some point, you just become another cog in a world-destroying machine. It’s a shocking but ironically real concept (in the realm of metaphor... I hope!), and despite the colorful art style and fantastic nods to Tales from the Crypt, this is a pretty scary and bleak piece of media that mirrors some real-life events, people, movements, and social anxieties.The game is tricky at the start, but once you get the hang of it, it’s surprisingly addictive. I haven’t had this much fun with a strategy game in ages, and discovering each piece of lore was the sweet icing on the cake.The stories are interesting, and the only thing I would ask for now is... MORE! Please give us more stories (on Halloween, maybe? :>), because the whole concept is so original, exciting, and leaves room for more narratives, mechanics, and social issues to explore. Maybe stories from the past? The point of view of the Our Country party president (from the second and third campaigns)? The possibilities are endless. I just hope the game gains the audience it deserves.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely amazing game, only wish there was a free play mode and saying you want more of a game isn't exactly a criticism. If you're a fan of strategy games or games where your protagonist is (at best) morally gray then I highly recommend this game. If this game gets a sequel I am buying it day one, mark my words.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: It is a short game: a bit weird, fun, with a nice graphic identity.But what I really loved is the narrative, not the stories themselves, which are fine but short, but how it keeps you and red herrings you and surprises you even when you know you understand where the story is going. The stories and the overarching story stick with you. It was worth my time.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game with great vibes and mechanics that aren't overly complex.It takes a few runs to get the hang of things, the tutorial is pretty good at teaching you the basics of how to play, but it doesn't really teach you what to avoid doing. My first two runs I put myself in impossible to win situations because I didn't fully understand the mechanics yet. Luckily the levels aren't that long so it's not a big deal to just restart them with what you learned.Overall I feel like it's a fun game, with a bit of a learning curve.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome! it is a good strategy game filled with storytelling, it is challeging enough and the details of what youre doing is the true spice of it, pay attention and ready everything that appears in front of you for this game, otherwise you will miss out on its experience! they could've made narration and voicelines for your enemies conversations , it would've been cool, a couple more background music variations and shifts depending on which chapter you are would've been a nice detail as well, you know just more stuff to immerse yourself more.all in all 9/10 game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant gameplay and storytelling, from the moment i first launched the game i could not stop playing, after an uninterrupted 9 hours i managed to finally finish it and all I can say is I want more, the game has such a satisfying finish to each story and the overarching plot that takes place is so good. When I saw it was from the creators of Do Not Feed The Monkeys i knew it was going to be good but I did not expect it to be THIS good.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I was optimistic about this game and it surpassed my expectations. It's unique and a lot of fun. It's like a series of Twilight Zone, presented as a graphic novel, in the form of agent-based political strategy game. It took me about 30 hours to complete and all I can say is I want more! Great, dark writing backed up by strong, although limited, voice-acting. Gameplay is easy to get to grips with and made for a relaxing and interesting playthrough. Just a well put together game with great style.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend this game, Its giving Tales from the crypt and other old school comics. the only thing I would of like is VA the whole time not just for some parts and a skip button for the opening. I also hope they add more stories maybe a DLC like " Tales from the past"  where we see past user or "Even more Tales" stories of circus,school ghost stories ect I feel it so good you want more and MORE. all in all I give it 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The Fabulous Fear Machine is a boardgame-like strategy game about strategic resource management. It has a pulp art style and an interesting take on the villain protagonist narrative instrument. The player finds himself guiding the fates of one of three unfortunate souls who have taken a dark bargain to gain power to change the world, undermining and defeating those who oppose them to make a single wish come true.The voiceover and the music are fitting and interesting as well.What I especially liked were the many pop culture references that can be found at every turn.If one likes strategy games with a dark narration without that much difficulty, I absolutely recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Narrative and story driven.  For those of you who are old enough to remember Tales from the Crypt and the Twilight Zone then this will tickle those old bones once again.  The game is overall an easy game to play once you learn the mechanics.  I will say that this game is perhaps not for those who aren't the best with background and knowledge of American folklore and inferences.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game has a very strong sense of style and a very interesting story that just pulls you in. My only gripe? It's too short!!! I hope they add more scenarios or maybe even introduce the tools for players to create their own. For how cheap I managed to snag this game (while it was on sale) I would even be willing to pay for a DLC if the creators decided to do more with this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A delightfully dark and compelling homage to EC Comics. The gameplay is solid and entertaining - never too difficult, rarely too easy - and the graphics are MAGNIFICENT.If there's anything that disappointed me, it's that the game is on the short side, but it's still a blast while it lasts. Here's hoping Fictiorama puts out some more campaigns as DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know, maybe I am at fault, but after finishing the game, I really don't understand the point of it.It was a bit of a worker placement game, but it didn't felt strategic at all.The stories were interesting and the graphic was nice, I think I kinda agree with most other reviews, but personally I feel a bit like I have wasted these 10 hours of my life.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game, didn't think I would like it, but gave it a try. The mechanics of evolving legend cards and stopping the rivals are nice touch, some things with fear expansion could be presented more clearly, but overall it is a good game.My only problem with it is that it still tends to free / crash (3 times in 4h of play - finished 5 maps and trice almost finished C2M2) and HOW HARD IT IS TO DO A WORKING AUTOSAVE FEATURE!?!?!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Fear mongering the game. Urban myths and legends are the tools that nurture fear in regions across the globe. The superstitious tales are pre-chosen cards based on the specific region of the world. They are placed in cities to expand fear from the origin point which the player can place down on certain areas of the map. Fear itself (described as Oleum) is a quantitative resource that allows the player to move their agents to explore new cities to corrupt later on, perform deals with shady characters, and possibly change the course of random events as they occur. Player-controlled agents need to extract specific resources (which there are eight in total) to upgrade the ferocity of the superstitions or resolve events should one of the eight resources be needed rather than Oleum. They are the most important when fighting against the good factions that try to reverse the fear mongering.  The gameplay is methodical; the player needs to carefully plan out multiple actions ahead for the best chance of success given that basically the game is a resource management of the different types of human paranoia. Three main campaigns with their own overarching stories through four to five missions plus the tutorial. Story development, in pulp comic format, is the reward. As more of a map is consumed by fear, a comic page is revealed in multiple sections for a mission. Embrace the visual art and read the great flavor text with patience because those two aspects of the game are its strengths.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: What a Journey!Every second of it was so much enjoyable.Every in game mechanic was very well thought-out: easy to control and in harmony with the themes at hand.Characters were all interesting, captivating with their own dreams and human flaws.Every little detail of the stories were written so well and supported with such beautiful art direction, it flowed like a movie, made me hold my breath till the last second. 10 Although selfish still well intended dreams, out of 10 crushing disappointments by horrifying old reality of our universe since time immemorial.With my single coin, my wish from the fabulous fear machine is: for the machine to free itself from all of its knowledge of life and death, and come join us one day, in our wonderful and tragic lives. I believe Kirlian would make a good friend, and maybe one day in the future, we could save all the agents too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad little game.  Later levels get quite complicated in how you manage the various, almost overabundance of resources available to you.  The core gameplay is pretty fun and addictive.  The stories are intriguing, and feed into the political intrigue and deception plot nicely.  The second campaign is a bit weak though, should have been more fleshed out I feel, could have done with another level at least.  The big drawcard is definitely the art style and aesthetic.  Fantastic job capturing that pulp style hysteria feel.Biggest letdowns for me though were the second campaign length, and the fact that there's no "new game plus".  Once you finish the game, the only thing really to do is replay the same levels again, perhaps on harder difficulties.  It would have been nice to change things up on a repeat playthrough, with your unlocked agents etc.  Was disappointed this wasn't the case.  The tutorial only barely gives you enough information to proceed, and the first level or two is a bit overwhelming in the amount of information you get from the UI.Definitely worth a first playthrough though if it interests you.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very resource management oriented. The story and graphics are great and the narrative currently is making me wonder when the other show is going to drop but overall I found the game rather boring. the interesting aspects of the game quickly lose their flavor as the monotony takes hold over the games mechanics. I'm currently unsure if the games mechanics open up in some way but essentially it's a game about waiting for timers to ding so you can do stuff. less about overcoming obstacles or getting attached to some characters or narrative. Long story short, the game's reliance on time activated mechanics shields it from the terrible mini-game-centric designs of games much older than an entire generation of people but comes at the cost of... well; your time. it's not engaging you in any way other than asking you to wait and see what happens next.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game. You're constantly given choices and have to make tradeoffs in what you decide to do with your agents and furthering your goals. Rival mechanic is well thought-out and gives an additional layer of strategy.Atmosphere and aesthetic is what really makes this game special, though. Love the comic book art style and the stories are actually really good and told in clever ways. Game difficulty seems tuned such that if you understand the mechanics and the general strategy then you shouldn't be able to beat each mission comfortably. I thought the difficulty was perfect but don't go in expecting anything hardcore.Also, ignore my playtime, kept the game running all night a few times. Game can be beat in about 8-10hrs, less if you don't fail any missions.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: In The Fabulous Fear Machine you are in control of a machine that produces myths to instill fear in people and make them do whatever you (or is it the machine?) wants. You get the help of agents that perform tasks for you.This game is a cross between a board game and a comic book. I know that may sound weird, but it really works. The main rules of the game are pretty easy, you get tasks that you can complete by having your agents do things, but these agents have limited time and so your choice in where you place them will be important.While it certainly isn't the deepest strategy game, its comic book style presentation totally makes up for it.I loved the mix of these two things.I am not sure how well the game is doing, but I would hope Fictiorama comes out with some DLC. It is the perfect game for it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simulation game that you try to spread the seeds of fear to the cities in order to confuse the citizens and dictate your authority on them. Its gameplay mostly consist of on puzzle and character management. Each fear you put into a city will have their own type of fear. Furthermore, each fear card has 3 phases find the word related to the card mini game. Finding correct words gives you bonus resources upon upgrading the fear. The game has too many layers to play. But none of them has a complexity, or debt in a way. Most of the mechanics are covered in the tutorial, which was a bit slow and boring.The Fabulous Fear Machine presents a linear, level-based approach to its story. There are three characters to follow stories of. Each of them has their own difficulty, comic book that reveals their personality and cruelty page by page. For the time I'm playing the game I can easily say it's not a hard game. I didn't encounter a challenging moment, which might cause some players to get bored, and drop the game (if they didn't during the tutorial.). For me it wasn't the case because the concept and the art style are astonishing. Besides these, revealing story points for each character and learning more about the fear cards were intriguing and this never dropped my attention for a moment.Overall, I believe the game has strong points for its art and it owns some interesting gameplay ideas. The stories make you guiltily happy about letting the characters rule over the world cruelly. Then reaching their doom and facing the result of their acts. It was a satisfying journey from beginning to end. I would really recommend it to conspiracy, comic book lovers, that can play puzzle and character management games.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun. Relatively short (only 3 campaigns, each campaign has 2-3 levels) and sweet, not super hard but still engaging. The aesthetic is awesome, love the campy pulp horror aesthetic and the stories. If you like Plague Inc you'll enjoy this. Even if you don't like Plague Inc give it a shot, the art and narrative is really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty good lil horror game where you help manipulate the masses through fear to get your truest disirePros:- A great strat game that starts basic and grows in complexity- Art direction is lovely- A choose your own adventure element that adds a fun narrativeCons:- Would be nice to have your choices feel more impactful- Would be nice if it was voiced- The tutorial isn't 100% clear on some mechanicsIt's a lovely game and def worth playing if you like strat games or want to play a reverse pandemic. I give it 2/3 wishes fulfilled.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Cool puzzle game with overwhelmingly cool style and stories that have really dark themes. I like the fact that you're not playing as the clear good guys in the campaign. There also a special kind of joy in trying to see the full picture of an upgraded card. My nitpick is just that sometimes the card and the stories doesn't connect well. I don't know why a rumour about man eating predators makes people want to buy more vaccines. Sometimes it's a bulleyes to the middle hit, sometimes it's a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Nice art style, well done but limited voice acting. It took be about an hour to beat each mission, with each story having between two and four missions. I think an hour is way too long, especially since you're mostly just waiting for resources to come in or events to happen. I would say double all resource gains or halve timers. That would be a much more streamlined experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun mix of macabre, misinformation and map spreading. This game tickles so many parts of my brain, there's all this gradual unlocking of rumours and plot. As story and incidental story as well as a virtual panini album of all the game items you unlock as you progress.Then there's the dark tales that each of the 3 campaigns hang on.Then there's the comic aesthetic.Then there's the fact the Machine itself is definitely modelled after the one Tom Hanks uses in BigThen there's the delicious spread of influence across regions of the map. So slow and deliberate and hampered and satisfying. While you balance the means methods and countermoves with you're finite resources. This is something really fun, unique and special. My only criticism is that I want more. 3 and a tutorial are fun and juuuust enough. But also not nearly enough. Who's next? What do they want, what are they willing to do to get it. What will they compromise, what will it cost. Why is there no rumour card for Birds not being real?I really hope there's DLC to come. What if there was a Game of Thrones Expansion? Can you imagine?
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It has story campaigns reminiscent of episodes of Tales From the Crypt, with gameplay that reminds me of a combination of Plague, Inc and Cultist Simulator. If you like those things posed as a strategy game, I recommend picking it up. I will say that the game is a little short, but that's the only real negative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I only finished the tutorials for now. I have to say, this is the most gorgeous I played.I planned to refund this game and left a no-recommend comment, but I think the artiest in the team deserve my thumb up.The game mode design is not interesting. Introducing to many weird new concepts make it worse, for example the fuel, mining. It would be better to use some noun that related with horror itself.I could understand that, it's based on the "horror machine".But I bought this game because I want to play a narrative-driven strategy game with horror element, instead of a game about horror machine.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: reader beware, you're in for a scare(perfectly nasty in the tradition of TALES FROM THE CRYPT and other pulp horror comics; fun gameplay loop; even more fun references to urban legends and spooky stories of yore. I only wish it was longer, but I have the feeling that there will always be more souls willing to throw themselves into the gears of the Machine...)
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable, especially for the asking price! It actually reminds me more of an old board game called Illuminati: The Game of Conspiracy than it does old school horror comics, but that's not a criticism at all. In terms of game play it feels very board-gamey too, but I personally enjoyed that aspect. Though I think it might be just a little too complex to be an actual board game, but still feels very close to that experience. It is definitely on the easier side too, as I was able to pass probably 90% of the missions on the first attempt, but it does a good job of continually adding features to keeps things fresh. Overall, I look forward to the inevitable DLC campaigns!
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, this strategy game is a twist on plague inc with a HEAVY horror comics theme and it does that perfectly. I'm not actually a "tales from the crypt" guy, but even I could enjoy the humor and art.This is an absolute gem. I'm not going to spend a lot of time praising it, if you're reading random reviews you're about to buy anyways.There are exactly 2 complaints I have and I'll list them both here.1 -- This is a turn based game with a gimmick real time mode. You right click to pause / un-pause and hold right click to fast forward. Realistically you never want the game un-paused; you're either fast forwarding or inputting orders. Un-pause being on the same button means you accidentally un-pause and lose turns. This is a (small) problem.2 -- The game is SHORT, like REALLY SHORT. Of the 3 campaigns, the second one has only 2 stages. We need more stages / some kind of procedural mode / something. Maybe make it an expansion and charge for it, whatever it takes... but this is a SMALL game. Buyers know that going in.Anyways, still, massive thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Borderline recommendation.The game is very, very short.  I finished it all in under 8 hours.  It's also insanely easy.  I found myself frequently having to wait until the enemy caught up, so I didn't miss the narrative.That said, it's atmospheric and creepy.  The story sucks you in.  The gameplay is merely a way to have the story and pulp art be displayed.  Some of the art is properly disturbing, not graphic, just in what it conjures up in your head about myths and legends of fear.It's a game that will stick in your head, just not a game that will be played for long.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This was an impulse purchase that ended up being a lot of fun, hope they make a sequel or some new campaigns as DLC. The game-play is simple but there's a often a light puzzle to solve and it's satisfying to upgrade your cards & see the fear spread across the map. Some quibbles/suggestions for the future:- Game did feel quite short for the price, one more campaign, maybe in a different time period would have been fun.- Linked to the above it wasn't until late in the campaign when all tools at our disposal were given to us (or at least explained). - The card play could be more complex, would love the possibility of cards combining if located in the same town/region, even if this was locked to specific combinations. - The local legends mechanic was great - wanted to see it used more often. Would have been interesting if, on returning to a map your previous actions could trigger a local legend occurring. - A challenge where you had to take over a much larger area, with all the cards you'd collected up that point, would have been great. - *Potential spoiler* - "Returning agents" - would have been nice to see them level up or have cards attached based on their stories.Overall the game was a lot more fun than I expected and excited to see where they go with for the next system.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Once you dive into it its hard to put down, I've literally only been playing for the last few days since I got it. The management aspect is really well done and even though I sometimes wish you could cancel agents task mid-assignment, the lack of cancelling makes me think a lot more about anticipating rival movements and such which I appreciate. Regardless if you like resource management games with a bit of thinking this game hits that nail on the head.I don't know where you report for bug fixes so i'm just posting it here; on Campaign 2, mission 2 the game basically said I needed to explore "the Athena Magazine office" but, when I go to look for it on the map it isn't there. I have played out the game long enough for all my legends to be maxed and for the flame to exceed my oleum production so I don't think its due to a lack of waiting but just a bug, hope this helps.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: 5/5. Consistent use of effectively presented "Pulp Comic" styleCompelling game play loop that rewards strategic thinking and punishes carelessnessCarefully balanced scenarios that match up with the thematic style of the gameContains a narrative that pushes players to consider the philosophical implications of the game's contentsCompletely captures the attention with high stakes, time sensitive opportunities to progress through each campaignIt is not possible to offer feedback for improvement without asking for just MORE of what is already here. One considers the idea of making a multiplayer version, but that would arguably be an entirely different title.A functional piece of art whose sum exceeds the combination of its separate components.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. The comic book style works well with the overall theme of the game, and it's overall a lot of fun to play. My only complaint is that it's a bit short, unless you go completionist. I'm really hoping to see more stories come out soon, hopefully at some point one truly grandiose and global.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I love a game I can finish under 10 hours this game has very much left me wanting more. With 3 stories and each having but a few chapters I don't feel there was enough game. Which isn't the worst problem for a game to have. The game loop is fun and each story adds new challenges that vary it just enough to keep it interesting. I the pulp fiction vibe works really well for the game. I'd just love to see more. More stories, more challenges. maybe even some different modes. Like a time challenge or a world fear mode. Just something to come back for once you finish the story lines.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A throwback to great horror series such as Tales from the Crypt, Creepshow, The Twilight Zone, and so many others.  The Fabulous Fear Machine is a fascinating game as you take three protagonists down the predetermined path set for them by the haunted Fortune Telling machine.It is a little short. Only 3 campaigns, though there is replayability for those completionists who want to get all of the classic Horror Comic Cards.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played an "outbreak" game since flash game days.  But the demo interested me; with the Creepshow-esque comic art, the story, and ability to use things like spooky legends to stoke fear turned out to be really fun to me.   Not normally interested in being "evil" per say.  But this game is unique enough to keep me coming back.  Would definitely be interested in more potential stories to this game in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game really is a fun combination of:-painting the map your color like a 4x game-a decent resource management system-conspiracies both as gameplay and as in-game tools/items-a delightful artistic direction referencing pulp horrorSatisfies for about 2 to 3 solid gameplay sessions.Difficulty keeps your brain at a low simmer which allows you to appreciate the art and narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short but enjoyable and unique indie strategy title with a narrative and aesthetic inspired by pulp horror comics; if that vibe appeals to you at all the art and storylines are very well done and worth experiencing.The gameplay loop is somewhat similar to outbreak sims like Plague Inc, where you play as several tragically flawed and/or demented masterminds who use the Fear Machine to manipulate the local populace by spreading various conspiracy theories and urban legends. The gameplay itself is not that deep but does keep things fresh by introducing new mechanics in new scenarios; overall it's enjoyable to experience the unique pulp art and storylets. There are currently 3 campaigns with about 10-15 hours gameplay; I hope the devs will add more scenarios or random maps in future and look forward to see how this develops.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely oozes style. The game's store page description of "narrative-driven strategy game with a pulp horror style" is spot-on. The cautionary tales you play through as the ill-fated Masters of the Machine and the art style make me feel like I'm playing vignettes that shouldn't have been cut from Heavy Metal. Everything in the game feels like a coherent piece of a cohesive whole.The gameplay itself is a little manager. It's more active and strategic than other games in its "Outbreak Sim" genre - which tend toward things you wind up and watch them go - and as you advance more complications are added that keep you on your toes. I thought it was a little easy at first but by the end of the first Master's story, the game was keeping me on the top of my game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very good at what it does.At the surface, it's a sort of Plague Inc. clone with more refined features about taking over regions with fear. Where it breaks the mold is its presentation and its hand-crafted scenarios. You are guiding characters through their villain origin stories, where they get a chance to achieve their secret wishes after a sort of 'deal with the devil' event.As cartoony and over the top the atmosphere is, some of the stories and tactics emerging are gut-wrenchingly real. This is a story where you really are the bad guy, not your standard goofy villain protagonist story where you are fighting against some greater evil and have some spooky skeletons in your army.The game made me feel genuinely uneasy a few times but in a good way. It's not a political game per se, but it shows you all the disgusting, manipulative and plain nasty tactics that are so prevalent in politics and the media. Even more impressively, it does this without being preachy or forcing some message.The game mechanics are simple but effective, they fit its theme and presentation perfectly. The artstyle is a huge plus, just make sure you are ready for some gore, because the game doesn't pull any punches.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun strategy game, with new mechanics added each chapter to spice up the gameplay. The stories in each chapter are interesting and it is thrilling to see how they resolve despite being very obvious with what fate will befall each character. The game is on the shorter side as of right now, but new content may be added in the future. Overall a fun game about spreading fear through rumours and urban legends.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

_childDocuments_.review: The Fabulous Fear Machine is a narrative-driven strategy game with a pulp horror style. As the Machine's new Master, you must sow fear and expand your influence by creating Legends, harvesting resources, manipulating events, and spying on your enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: The Fabulous Fear Machine

name: Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow
detailed_description: The story of an elderly bedridden man who is approaching the end of his life and is burdened with life's hardships and disappointments. In his altered and fading memories, he imagines himself as a little boy named Griffin who finds solace in the company of a teddy bear that embodies the spirit of his deceased son. Trying to evade the ever-present grasp of Death itself, you will meet the most important characters of Griffin’s life in this mysterious world: a cruel and harsh father who turned into a giant knight, and a fragile but protective mother embodied in the form of a flower fountain. Travel through a mysterious world of craggy caves and floating castles, fairytale forests and rolling plains. Prepare to be enthralled by the captivating world of Daydream, discover the transformative power of resilience, and accept the bittersweet beauty of letting go. Key features — Dive deep into a sprawling story, revealing secrets and unravelling the mysteries of an enchanting narrative; — Step into an unforgettable world accompanied by dreamy melodies and mesmerizing music; — Encounter memorable characters, such as the endearing young Griffin and his steadfast teddy bear companion Birly; — Command an adorable teddy bear friend who assists you along the journey; — Collect all memory moths to help Griffin find peace.

short_description: Experience the altered memories of a dying man, reliving his entire life as a little boy while lying on his deathbed. Explore the profound depths of his subconscious as you assist Griffin to shed the remains of his miserable life before his impending demise.

_childDocuments_.review: is a puzzle platformer that likely attracts players due to its great presentation. As someone who loves atmospheric platformers, I was also drawn to it not only because of the beautiful visuals but also because of the theme that made me think it would be a very enjoyable and casual experience. What can even go wrong when you have a mix of colorful environments, the journey of a boy and his teddy bear and a seemingly wholesome storyline? Well… much more than I expected. I tried really hard to like the game, but the number of issues this game has strongly impacted my immersion in a deeply negative way, to the point where I ended up feeling as much hate towards it as my initial excitement was.Let’s start with the positives: visuals and ambiance. The whole game world defies physics and reality, essentially looking like a figment of young Griffin’s imagination. Since  is played from the perspective of a child (Griffin), everything looks bigger and scarier. There are friendly toys, green fields, floating castles and colorful trains, but also eerie elements like shadows on the walls, evil spiders, dark goo and a creepy hand that tries to grab him sometimes. The game does a really good job of depicting the wonderful creativity of a young and innocent mind, and the mix of emotions that he experiences.  gives a strong  vibe, although less creepy and disturbing. It is dark to some extent, but being rather mild on the horror scale (close to no horror at all), it can also be played by those that dislike scary games.Now, onto the negatives:A lot of reviews mention that this is an easy game. Personally, I found it quite difficult, partly because of the extra repeats needed to overcome the bugs, but also because of the level design. There are several timed sequences (when some entity chases Griffin), and others with tight jumps and precision movement. Learning them is done through trial and error because the game doesn’t tell you in advance what to expect. Luckily you encounter  checkpoints quite often, and lengthier sequences contain at least two or three checkpoints. Therefore, while the gameplay is above casual difficulty, the game is overall quite forgiving, allowing the player to repeat only a short sequence to get back to the point they were before they died. On the other hand, if some puzzle is contained in this short sequence, the whole puzzle has to be solved again, which uselessly wastes time.The puzzles are largely ok, neither too easy nor too difficult, none of them being out of the ordinary. There are two puzzles in which you have to find the correct order of activating levers / the right combination, yet no indication is given to the player about how to solve it.The game also features 14 achievements, thankfully none requiring speedruns, zero-death runs, or solving puzzles from the first try. They are all awarded for finding 14 collectibles that aren't missable in the sense that you can always revisit a previously completed chapter from the chapter selection menu. is a short game that can be completed in two to three hours, or around five hours if you’re a slowpoke like me. The rest of the time I spent in the game (almost four hours, which is half my playtime) was wasted on redoing platforming sequences over and over again, due to the various issues listed above. The game has a lot of potential, but unfortunately in its current state, it was a disappointing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game tries to imitate another one like Little Nightmares (beautiful game), especially in the early scenes, but it does so with worse graphics, art style and gameplay quality, and without succeeding in creating a particular atmosphere. On the other hand, the game is quite substantial, with many puzzles and action scenes, sometimes not exactly easy to deal with. It is a longer and overall more difficult game than the first Little Nightmares, to understand. A casual gamer or one not used to this kind of game might find it difficult.Those who complain about the gameplay of this game in most cases do precisely because it is not as easy as it looks, not so much because of bugs or flaws. It is true that the game is a bit "rough" in some aspects, but not so much that it impairs playability.In short, if you are looking for another Little Nightmares, you will be disappointed, however, if you like these kinds of games, it is worth a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Teddy NOT approved game!  wouldn't approve it too... because the main character looks like Til mit der Brill' and Gin doesn't like penguins. Down with the penguins! :)Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow is that kind of game you really want to like. I mean it has a teddy bear and looks like a puzzle platformer in the fashion of Little Nightmares. It even has new game mechanics compared to Little Nightmares like giving orders to your teddy bear. So what can go wrong? Almost everything!The controls and movement: are just sluggish, slow and everything else than accurate. To do precise jumps is more or less luck. The graphics: are most of the time ugly and grainy. Also very bright at standard brightness settings. Game still has many bugs, crashes a lot. Sometimes it's funny. When you fall down through a level on a certain point and save half of the time this way because the next save point activates while falling to your death. The level design: is pure simple. You can't get lost in any way. Even the hose levels of Jedi Fallen Order look like a labyrinth compared to that. There are basically 3 kinds of puzzles... 1 - none at all, means you run just through. Examining all the things on your way is also not necessary at all. 2 - very easy puzzles you can solve without using your brain and 3 - so weird, illogical and most of all unintuitive puzzles you will need quite some time to recognize what to do or even where. The story: is never motivating or even really explains what is happening. And the end of the game... I don't want to know how many bottles of vodka have been emptied before writing down this kind of story. I mean the story of Little Nightmares is also weird... but in a good, interesting way. This story here is just... weird and amateurish. It also lacks to give you motivation to play the game from the first minute onwards. The music: is okay at the main menu and more or less non existent within the game. I wonder to what music all the other "absolutely awesome" reviewers have listened...?!?So... what are the good sides of this game? It has a teddy bear and it's easy 100% achievements. That's also why I've tortured myself through the game.So summed up: the game is so bad. Sometimes you really would wish to have a gun to shoot your way through. Oh... while you're already here and we talk about having good fun... with a gun! :) Please take a wishlisting-and-following-look at the upcoming good game from a nice friend of mine: But anyway! What more to say... rather than: DON'T buy, buy, buy for full price! (© and ® and ™ by )★☆☆☆☆1/5

_childDocuments_.review: "Recreate the feelings and emotions we had as children" - well, you certainly succeeded with this in my case.Playing this game gives me the same feeling of dread, not knowing what to do, feeling railed into actions but not given clear goals and - being punished all over again. Not really something I want to revisit in my Me-time...So, after playing twice for some hours I couldn't be more frustrated and enraged with this game. As beautiful as it is, I hate this game. I'm still in the second chapter and I've given up.First, I play the PC version. It is playable, but it took AGES for me to understand I can use the mouse to change between the command circles of Birly. Until then I was totally clueless what exactly it was that made pressing the right mouse button into a command for Birly.The control is sloppy at best. Throwing Birly isn't consistent. Most of the time he falls down after a very short length - just until he doesn't. This IS connected to the puzzle in the scene, but after two or three short throws in the wrong direction, you start to rule out the right one, because surely that's too far away?!This is 2D-perspective, kinda, and it is hard to gauge if you've got the right angle for anything. It is also forced perspective. This means there can be objects obscuring my chars (which is especially nice when you have to blindly jump off something), or make them tiny compared to the scene.Sometimes you miss exits because the lighting makes them hard to see - but okay, most of the time the scenes are as simple as enter left- exit right.And that's exactly what you do most of the time - enter left, run to the right. Sometimes two or three scenes long, where there's nothing happening - if you don't count looking at the very nice graphics, but I could do that on artstation, too.At the start, you get vague hints in form of red flags/handkerchiefs/fabric waving at a POI. But not always, certainly not if you are stuck. There also aren't additional hints if you are stuck - throwing a bottle around on a ledge between two doors doesn't tell me I'm supposed to throw it at that picture of a lighthouse, and oooh, it is not a PICTURE, it is supposed to be a glass window! How about just giving hints like "Maybe throw that elsewhere"? So I'm at least certain I'm supposed to throw that thing instead of, say, hit Birly over the head with it???And why is Birly totally capable to climb about broken stairs two times, but the third time I have to throw him over? Consistent behaviour, anyone?And let's not talk about the bugs. Or, let's do it. Grabbing the locking mech in the window floor room somehow made Birly and me swing on it 270° to the left. We hovered over the stairs, but letting go made us fall down.Or the one time where I climbed onto a cage lieing on its side, and climbing down I somehow fell to my death?Or when Birly got stuck on high places and didn't come back down?It's a visually pleasing game, but it is just too frustrating for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A man lies dying in his bed. Whilst waiting for his time to pass he dreams about his life through the eyes of a boy called Griffin and his teddy bear. Trying to evade the ever-nearing grasp of death, we go on an adventure which has symbolic meaning for the old man.Daydream Forgotten Sorrow is a puzzle adventure with light horror elements. Game play revolves around your typical puzzle adventure with switches and levers, pushing and pulling objects, jumping on platforms and swinging on ropes. Throughout most of the journey you are joined by your trustworthy companion in teddy bear form. Together you can work together to solve puzzles. Griffin can command the teddy bear to pull switches or levers, or untie rope ladders for him to climb, and being smaller he can also get through gaps that Griffin cannot access. If a gap is too large for the bear to cross, or a ledge is too high, Griffin can pick up the bear and throw him to safety.Later in the journey Griffin is joined by an archer who can shoot at targets or other objects to manipulate items. Griffin is also able to command and work together with this character too. There are swimming segments, quick time events, chase sequences, and even a few boss fights, but these tend to be quite easy. I was quite impressed with the puzzles. They were often imaginative and quite difficult in places, resulting in the need to seek guidance on a couple of occasions. The mechanics can make puzzles a lot more difficult than they should be however, and this can cause a lot of frustration and anger. For example, there is a segment where you have to usher a spider along a maze so he sets off a trap. Whatever I did he would not go the way I wanted him to go. Eventually, he did cooperate but I was left drained from the whole puzzle because I knew what was needed but it just wouldn’t comply. I fell off ledges, bridges, logs, you name it and I fell off it. The controls are uber sensitive. Sometimes when you die, and he re-spawns, he immediately starts walking in one direction and I had to jump or press the opposite direction to correct his walk of death. There is one segment with very narrow ledges and I swear I have never felt so annoyed in a game before. Continual deaths for no reason had me ready to quit the game.My controller doesn’t behave in any other game like this. I must stress that it will try your patience and unless you have the resolve of Gandhi it will irritate you. It’s whether you can keep trying and muddle through or not.The game takes around seven to ten hours to complete.The game is very beautiful with some original environments which are often dark and claustrophobic. There are lots of opportunities to take screenshots. I missed a few of the cut scenes because it kept asking for me to hold A on the controller, rather than hold A to skip, and I only realized what was happening later. Please amend this. A lovely soundtrack and special effect noises.

_childDocuments_.review: Daydream is very, very heavily inspired by Little Nightmares...  which is a good thing, since LN is great.  And, overall, the game is pretty good.  Quality visuals and creative puzzles in a curious world.  However, it's rough around the edges with how you have to micromanage the bear (which can result in getting softlocked), how you die to every fall/jump, and other small frustrations and inconsistencies with platforming, movement, and interacting with objects.  I also found the soundtrack to be fairly basic, with loops that are too short/repetitive.  And for the love of god, turn down/off the controller vibration... it is a privilege not a right!Worth getting, but maybe wait for a patch or two to address the bugs and polish the gameplay a bit more.

_childDocuments_.review: I posted a negative review as I feel this game needs a round of polish. A good Quality of Life update is desperately needed. The platform jumping is just off in places. The mechanic to point the NPC needs to be better. The flying and running scenes are incredibly frustrating. The controls for the sprinting and interacting should be swapped. Sprint should be assigned to your right trigger and interact should be the "X" button (at least on the XBOX controller). It would make for better sprint jumps which are required in a number of areas. To thumb flop between the face buttons to perform this action makes it much harder to pull off.A few more rounds of play testing and then an QOL update would really improve this game tremendously. It is a good game. It is a fun game. It has good graphics and music. It just needs some tightening up in the control department. It does have that Little NIghtmares and Limbo feel but just not at the quality level of those games which is too bad. I do hope the developer rolls out a solid quality update. If they do, then I would recommend the game but in the current state I can't.

_childDocuments_.review: Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow is a Little Nightmares a-like with beautiful environments a decent story and tricky puzzles.The basic gameplay of this title is what has become the fairly standard puzzle platformer fair , chase sequences, complex puzzles, sudden deaths. In the game you play Griffin our main hero and his bear Birly who you can order around to solve puzzles. Later in the story other characters join the team but you will predominantly play as these two. While puzzles start simple such as having Birly push things for you to climb or throwing him onto ledges things do get very  complex by the end of the game and at times things will really leave you scratching your head and perhaps getting frustrated.The games flaws are more apparent when your doing more complex puzzles with characters not always responding to your instructions, sometimes glitching out and vanishing requiring a puzzle restart. The platforming controls also do feel a little off and floaty at times leading to some frustrating deaths. That said the general quality of most of the puzzles and the fact these issues only occur occasionally means these things can be overlooked especially for fans of the genre. There is a story here that will gradually reveal itself towards a fairly shocking conclusion but I won't spoil, it does however tell a great story combined with whimsical visuals and music that blend the world together very well. Daydream Forgotten Sorrow is not the best puzzle platformer out there however it stands over most of the competition and is well worth a play for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow:~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ There is one guarantee in life, and that is that we will all need to confront death. From events foreseen and unforeseen, everyone has their own story, creating memories along the way. It is super important to make the best of the lease on life that you have been given. In Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow, you’ll be playing Griffin as a youngster who is accompanied by Birly, his teddy bear, reliving his memories as he faces his inevitable death.    Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow is a puzzle platformer developed by Frozen Line and published by Ravenage Games on the 15th of June, 2023, on the Steam platform. The game will also be available on PS4/PS5, Nintendo Switch and Xbox One Series X|S later on.In this game you will be immersed in beautiful visuals without narrative. The atmospheric story took me around seven hours from start to finish. The game starts with Griffin sitting on a black-and-white tiled floor that looks suspiciously like a hospital room. From the left extremity of the screen, one of the Grim Reaper’s hands starts closing in on Griffin. Thankfully, on the other side, Birly opens the large door and makes signs to follow him, and Griffin’s last journey begins.This is mostly a puzzle platformer game, but the developers have included some stealth, combat and racing elements, too.  And the game needed it to elevate it further. As I was playing, I felt that the pace was a bit slow, specifically the character’s movements. So, having a few fast-paced pursuits felt good.  I enjoyed the level where Griffin and Birly were flying on a bike through valleys and caves with obstacles. The puzzles are good and make sense without being too difficult to complete. Most of the puzzles involve giving commands to Birly and also to the female character Griffin will meet later in the game. With Birly, the commands will mostly be to activate something. Griffin can also throw Birly across platforms and vents, and command him to go through cracks in walls to get from one area to another. The other character has a bow and arrows. You need to command her to shoot at targets and activate an action. The level in the cloud was probably the best of all for me. I like the fact that you felt more depth, as the level had a bit of a switch between closer and more distant platforms. I like that! Within each level, there are one or two dragonflies to find. They may be located in secret rooms and will be revealed as you place, throw or open an object. I found most of them, but because I missed a few, I don’t know if they unlock anything extra. Keep your eyes open for anything out of place in each level.  Regarding the controls, I found them adequate for most of the game, but I did have a few issues aligning objects to reach another area.  Apart from that, it was smooth sailing. Be prepared to feel all of Griffin’s emotions along his special journey, perfectly evoked through stunning visuals and the accompanying soundtrack.You can play this game with your keyboard, but I strongly recommend using a gamepad. The game has been translated into 19 different languages, including English, German, French, Dutch, Spanish, Italian, Chinese and others. Positives:~~~~~~~ +	Beautiful graphics and soundtrack+	10 well-structured levels full of fun, interesting puzzles+	Well-constructed visual story with plenty of emotional moments+	Translated into 19 different languages+	Has achievementsNegatives:~~~~~~~~ -	I had a few issues aligning objects to reach some areas-	No trading cards as yetDaydream: Forgotten Sorrow follows the emotional and beautifully illustrated final journey of Griffin, with well-structured levels with plenty of good puzzles.7/10  Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!
