_childDocuments_.review: As an indie game reviewer, I'm delighted that I was able to receive this game to review - no strings attached! All opinions are my own. If you'd like to listen to the review in video format, check out my video! Now we move onto the game itself.. with the tutorial! Let's keep this section brief because, surprisingly, the tutorial section itself goes by quickly! From the moment you start the game, it eases you into the controls slowly but surely. From moving your character, grabbing items, and even manipulating Birly - your adorable bear companion - the game instructs you seamlessly while still moving you through the story itself.Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow is a game very much reminiscent of Little Nightmares and Gris; it certainly shows in the gameplay! You control a young child named Griffin as he explores an ever-changing landscape full of mystery, mysticism, and memories. Much of the game is solving puzzles using only your wit, your own hands, and Birly. The little bear himself is a wonderful addition to the game, as you can control Birly to help you with puzzles, making the solutions very interesting! Given the type of game it is, there are some high tension sequences that incorporate both puzzles and chase mechanics. While it is not a horror game, it does get the heart pumping!Since the game is a very story-driven game and the characters are a huge part of it, we will keep this section short and talk about just the very basics! As you've seen before, the main two characters in this story are Griffin, the young main character, and his bear, Birly. Though Birly is a large part of the story, it mainly revolves around Griffin himself. We follow him on his journey through the various scenes: a child's bedroom, a windmill, beautiful forests and plains. Every single piece of this journey builds to an absolute crescendo by the end of the game. All in all, the story itself is one of the best parts of the game and should be experienced for yourself!Second only to the story, the stylistic graphics of this game really shine bright! The character models look appropriately young for someone who pictures themselves and those around them as children, while the landscapes that you travel through are absolutely mystical in nature and beautiful. The game itself feels like the most surreal of dreamscapes in the most beautiful of ways and the stylized images truly capture that. While most of it is beautiful, even the terrifying moments are handled with such distinctive flair so as to not take away from the majesty of what you've seen up until that point. It is a delicate balancing act that I feel Frozen Line, the developers, really did well.And now it's the time where we move onto the pros and cons! Every video has to have one, right? All in all, there aren't a lot of negative points in this game and more pros than there are cons. Let's go over it.	• Tutorial is enjoyable, the gameplay loop satisfying	• Puzzles can be surprisingly complicated	• Inventive "boss" battles	• Atmospheric tension is delightful and horrifying	• Sound design and music are top notch	• Ragdoll physics are hilarious	• Birly gets distraught when you die	• Perfect for lovers of Little Nightmares	• Controls can be finicky, flight especially	• Minor texture glitches in areas	• Has issues alt-tabbing if using a controller	• Likely needs a bigger Arachnophobia warningAnd that's it, sweet blooms! Overall, I really think that this game is an indie gem waiting to happen. As someone who played  the whole way through and is working on some of the smaller secrets, I fell in love with the game. As much as the puzzles could be difficult, the absolute joy from completing them was what got me through even when I felt stumped. On top of that, I found myself spending hours upon hours in the game - a sure sign that you've enjoyed something! If you happen to love puzzles, atmospheric storytelling, and some small spooks, then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but at the state it's currently in, I can't recommend it. It definitely is not terrible. It is a beautiful-looking game with a nice story and cool puzzles, but everything else seems to be rushed and unfinished. Animations are clunky and lifeless, AI needs some work, sound design doesn't sound natural, and the story just doesn't feel smooth. I hope that a good update fixes a lot of these things, because other than the visuals, all components of the game seem to be more in their draft phases than in their finished phases. There is so much potential for it to be an awesome emotional experience, but, in my opinion, it needs a lot of work.

_childDocuments_.review: At first I thought it was cute. It's a bit like Little Nightmares, although the mood is completely different. Unfortunately, I got disinterested in it quickly, but I played through it because I don't like to give up on games.It was frustrating a lot of the time, there were parts that I tried to replay too many times... Maybe it was the frustration of not making it, I don't know. I didn't really like the movement and handling, the view was often wrong, I fell down a lot because I couldn't see where I was jumping properly.In the end I really didn't like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Daydream: Forgotten Sorrow

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo a few months ago and loved it. Couldn't wait for the game to drop. It has a Little Nightmares vibe without being poop your pants scary. It came out and I finally bought it on sale and can say it was the biggest let down. I wanted SO BADLY to love it. From the start it is pretty easy. Puzzles were pretty easy to figure out, if not it was at least obvious that there were hints in a previous area to help solve it. Great. As it progresses the puzzles are in my opinion, next to impossible to figure out without wanting to rip your hair out, not to mention that the controls are downright janky. Ex. puzzle involving grabbing a lever to move things constantly glitched and I would move the lever twice only to have to move it back to the position I actually needed it in, meaning I actually had to move the lever 3 damn times for one movement. Don't even get me started on the companions. First I hated the bear, then I hated the girl. Then I got to experience hate for both of them at the same time. Half the time they don't respond to your commands, the other times they just sit there frozen staring off into the abyss. Bear would go flying at one point when throwing, but in another area he literally couldn't be bothered to get thrown 2 feet in front of my. Super inconsistent.The story in my opinion was impossible to figure out. I thought I had a clue, but by the end I actually ended up having absolutely no clue what the hell was going on. This game LOOKS great, the art is amazing. The atmosphere is spooky when it needs to be and quaint all of the other times, but that alone can't make me give this a thumbs up. Fix the janky controls and make the story easier to understand. Streamed this with intentions on making a video, but there is absolutely no way to present it without an insane amount of cursing and repeatedly saying "I am going to lose my mind." I'm shocked this has so many good reviews to be honest.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game and development team! I won a free key by participating in a best screenshot of the demo contest and have been following development and testing for the past year or so, and I am so excited that this game is finally released for everyone to play.  I have tested on the SteamDeck and it works great!

_childDocuments_.review:
Daydream - puzzle-platformer adventure game. Go through the trials in the fantasy world, controlling the hero and his teddy bear.

The mechanics of the game is simple - the player is playing for the hero in three-dimensional plane. Character control is tactile. The set of actions that he is able to perform is small: climb, jump, grab and use objects, as well as interact with secondary, but no less important characters.

Also the player can give instructions to his partners - wherefore the gameplay becomes even more pleasant, because it is always more fun to spend time with a friend.

name: Beyond Galaxyland
detailed_description: Inspired by classic sci-fi movies, Beyond Galaxyland is an intergalactic, 2.5D adventure-RPG set among the stars. Step into the sneakers of high-schooler Doug, as he’s whisked away to ‘Galaxyland’ - a zoo-like solar system of planets - on an epic quest to save Earth itself. An all-new take on the beloved RPG adventures of old, prepare for a journey like no other, skyrocketing through teeming jungles, neon-lit cities, and cybernetic casinos, with each new planet brimming with intriguing characters, fiendish adversaries, and many other surprises. Accompanied by Doug’s pet guinea pig - the pistol-wielding Boom Boom - and a sentient robot called MartyBot, together you must defend the world against an all-powerful entity known only as ‘The End’, before it conquers the Universe itself… No pressure. A Bold New Take on the Classic Sci-Fi Caper! Experience firsthand all the thrills and spills of a retro sci-fi adventure, in an all-new take on the fish-out-of-water tale that sticks you right in the centre of the action! Laughter, loss, peril and friendship, Beyond Galaxyland has it all and then some, dipped in a dazzling layer of neon-tastic pixels. Explore a Solar System of Extraordinary Worlds From the blizzard-swept planes of Arcos to the tropical jungle ravines of Erros, the neon-buzzing cities of Neo to the arid sand dunes of Xalm, explore a cosmic cluster of unique worlds, each with its own quests, environmental puzzles, and out-of-this-world characters. Overcome Cosmic Foes in Tactical Turn-Based Combat Engage in strategic turn-based battles against a vast range of galactic nemeses, with time-responsive defensive gameplay to minimise damage. Each party member has a range of unique abilities at their disposal, but for an additional tactical advantage, sneakily scan your enemy pre-battle to discover their strengths and weaknesses. Experience Epic Boss Battles Each planet boasts its own distinct perils, but none more so than the epic bosses you’ll encounter throughout your extraterrestrial travels, including colossal space dragons, flesh eating flowers, and the all-knowing bionic behemoth that is Nexus Mind. Capture Enemies to Use in Battle Successfully capture the many weird and wonderful creatures you encounter, to later unleash them in battle, with each possessing a number of exclusive abilities. Will you acquire every last one? Features: Explore the many extraordinary worlds of Galaxyland in an adventure to save the Earth Experience a thrilling story that pays homage to your favourite retro sci-fi movies Form a party of diverse companions to overcome foes in tactical turn-based combat Capture enemies in combat to later unleash as allies or buffs during future battles Craft new armours and consumables to aid Doug and his pals on their journey Engage in over 25 epic boss battles with the Universe's most-feared adversaries A truly unique soundtrack unlike anything you've heard (at least on this planet) with over 50 diverse tracks spanning a myriad of genres from electronic to hip-hop to piano-heavy blues.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Galaxyland is an absolute treat of a game. The music, the art, and the gameplay all mesh well together to create a memorable experience as you traverse the galaxy.Much of your time will be spent playing turn based battles with a handful of different characters that can be swapped freely. In these battles you are also rewarded for learning enemy attack patterns and blocking at the right time which makes the whole battle experience more engaging.The storyline and quests are unique and varied which avoids the repetitive slop that I find so often in modern games. Puzzles and quests are straightforward enough that you can discover their solutions without outside help or frustration. You can really tell that this game is a labour of love and passion. And it thrives because of that.Hope everyone else enjoys the game as much as I have c:

The 2.5D concept was pretty cool, the soundtrack was fantastic (mostly trap, but tasteful and catchy), combat was OK and on par with pretty much any turn based RPG I've played (the ability points were a decent change up). _childDocuments_.review: Fantastic 3D pixel / voxel art, great music, and a decently strong story make for a great sci-fi JRPG.  It's a well made game all around and I was hooked the whole way through.The only real complaint I have is that there is a sidequest which results in an optional party member.  The party member is not scaled to your level and starts at level 1, and the earliest you can get him, you'll be at least 10 levels ahead of him, so if you decide to use him, you need to spend some extra time grinding levels with him.  He also has no abilities or weapons, aside from a few bonus attacks per turn and some decent stat growth.  He gets a couple lines at the end of the story, but has no story significance otherwise.  He basically feels like a complete afterthought to the game and doesn't really add anything.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing 2D sci-fi epic with memorable, well-developed characters, great dialogue, good variety of locales, and a punchy soundtrack. Decent monster variety with useful skills that can be captured via RNG pokemon mechanics.Game play is mostly 2D exploration with lite platforming. Also has some side quests with optional challenging bosses, racing mini games, and brief top down stealth areas. Notable influences include Star Wars, Aliens, Final Fantasy, and Out of this World.Would like to see the capture mechanic revised to be based on enemy health instead of pure RNG.Highly recommended for all sci-fi, turn-based battle, and creature collecting fans.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice game. I'm not super far into it but I like what I see. I have few issues with it but otherwise this is a fun time and I look forward to putting more time into it. Pros:+The art style. I actually dig the pixel sidescroller 2.5 HD ish look.+The fact it's a sidescroller turn based RPG. Not many games look like this that aren't hack and slash. +Customization. You have several "relic" slots that are basically accessory slots. There's various types of equipment and you can build how you see fit. You also can equip multiple "summons" aka monsters you catch like pokemon that act as magic essentially. -The characters so far are...  Ok Martybot is really fun. The protagonist Doug doesn't seem to have a personality unfortunately. Haven't met many other important characters yet. Cons:-Summons, aka Magic seems really pointless. You have like 12 max MP and a single cast of a summon (depending on what it is) is like 6 MP. So you can use 2 spells before you're out lol what in the hell type of design choice was this? I don't understand. You gain MP when you level but it's 1 point every 2-3 levels. Maybe it opens up later I'm not sure. Besides the magic system the game is definitely good enough to recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Galaxyland is, theoretically, a great game.  Its got good music, good art design, solid writing, and interesting gameplay.  I cannot recommend it, because it is only about 2/3rds of a game.  It is a three act story that abruptly stops at the end of act two.  It does not even deserve to be described as a cliffhanger; cliffhangers have dramatic setup and an explicit "to be continued", while this game does not.  It just ends.  Roll credits.

_childDocuments_.review: why haven't you bought this game yet?-active-time-battle-combat done right-which goes hand in hand with excellent character-systemsyou get stats over stats, like you'd expect in a much bigger budget titelstr (for raw damage), accuracity (important cause of other mechanics aswell), crit, counter, armor, etc. it is all here;but then it goes to REAL rpg levels with an extensive amount of gear choices.while the weapon (type) is fixed per character the other slots are all open for "artifacts" (all gear basicaly)and these artifacts are incredible well done:on hit procs like blind or slow; armor or pure damage up/side grades, active turn buffs, increases to your stats, resists and whatnot: the list is on a level publishers/developers like Square can only dream of.but it don't here: combat ain't just attacking, ability use and/or casting spells (summons), there is an ability point system aswell.basicaly each attack you hit, each attack you deflect (active parry, but with an easy timeframe and good windup) nets you ability points for this bar, as does a kill or skipping a turn for the selected character (up to 3 points); this bar starts out at 10 and you can find upgrades (power cells) throughout the game to increase it's max. each character has their very own unique abilities which use this bar as a ressource.then there is the summon/capture system. basicaly nigh every standart or boss enemy can be captured (think SMT). bring down their health bar and use the capture-ability; these summons are not quite like spells in other games like reviews claimed. they are more akin to summon. your cast pool is quite low and at best you will be able to use summons 2 or 3 times per battle for much of the game (without popping consumables). but their "spells" become ever more helpfull: standart damage spells (with an elemental affinity system), party wide buffs (protect, haste, etc.); for some of the optional stuff/bosses they are down right critical.then there is the photo- or scan feature: two characters in your party can scan enemies or other people, critters, etc. out of combat; which nets you a neat photo (with a small descibtion in a photo-menu), but lets you see enemy health bars or serves as a collectathon for side-quests.then there is a crafting system which lets you craft consumables and artifacts (gear). materials are dropped by enemies or bought in stores.each dungeon is tight and doesn't overstay it's welcome. each area and dungeon feeling unqiue, not just cause of audio-visual design (excellent), but because each has their own little puzzle, riddle or gimmick.there is minigames and while i usualy hate those in (j)rpgs i 100% each one i encounterd here cause they were actualy fun.like the hover bike racing: think a very basic Wipeout 1 meets  SNES. you get your own spaceship, where your crew hangs out (for conversation) and you can travel between different planets, heck even warp to over systems all on a very neat looking "overworld" map.and there is so much more.all this looking stunning. beeing eldricht-alien-like factories, mechanical contraptions walking across endless fields of snow or lush and vibrant jungle planets, with a more deserty area beeing one of my favorites (the backround detail is out of this world): this is one of the best looking games i got in my collection. the colors pop, the anmations are lovebale, each scene has clearly been designed with care, love and integrety. somone realy wanted this game to look good. and to top it all off: the OST is brilliant. the quality and mixing make even something like Persona 3 Reload look old. electro bangers, deep base, mixed with more instrumental inspired compositions...this is an OST you can listen to while driving.the plot also touches on some more intersting concepts and actualy managed to surprise me here and there; but despite what your first impressions might be: there is quite some murder, horror and thriller elements here.the game starts out feeling more like your run of the mill artsy 2D/3D mini rpgbut it quickly turns into a real meaty game, developed with so much care and skill that it makes some of the "bigger" releases the last couple of years look realy bad.it is downright ciminal how little attention this masterpiece has gotten. one of my all time favorites and well earned.

The graphics are charming, the story, as far as I got, was somewhat interesting... but stop trying to put aspects of platforming into non-platforming games. There's no damn reason for it and the clunky as hell jumping in this game turned me off. I wanted an RPG with neat mechanics, but there are tons of other ones that don't have clunky jumping.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Galaxyland is a delightful blend of classic RPG elements with a rich story and a charming cast of characters. The pixel graphics and immersive worlds are filled with engaging quests and exciting turn-based combat. Boom Boom, the super-intelligent guinea pig, steals the show with his humor and heart. Exploring diverse planets and battling unique creatures will keep you hooked. If you're a fan of games like Final Fantasy and enjoy a well-crafted narrative, this game is a must-play!

_childDocuments_.review: No untagged spoilers. Tl;dr cautious recommend for puzzle platformer RPG fans. Pass for everyone else. Initial warning, there's no Steam cloud save and the save data is stored in the Windows registry. Good luck playing across multiple devices easily.+ High quality, polished, beautiful environments and lighting. Really stunning stuff for a pixelart game. I actually think it's just as good if not better than the "HD-2D" style from Octopath Traveler and similar games since.+ Good quality of life overall. Something I wasn't expecting was being able to skip most puzzles entirely. Great addition for people who either don't want to do them or can't.+ You can tell a lot of passion and creativity went into this which really helps the player experience- Outside of a couple boss battles, combat is mash the A button as quickly as possible and simply restore your HP at every save point. Every character is also essentially identical outside of 1-2 unique skills, one of which was often only used in specific boss scenarios (e.g. to Negate a boss shield). It got to a point where combat was a chore and made me not want to play instead of being one of the driving factors to play.- None of the puzzle platforming elements build on each other. Each "dungeon" that involves platforming uses unique puzzles and never builds on past knowledge.- Sluggish world animations. Best example is taking an elevator. It's about 30 seconds from when you first access some elevators to when you're allowed to move again. Why?- Writing quality varies heavily between characters and story beats. MartyBot is quite funny for who (what) he is. Some static location characters are pretty neat and have that "... whoa" factor. Most of the main characters speak quite strangely... at times somewhat human and at others like the script didn't get out of the outline/bullet point stage.- Mini games... added, then underutilized. You get to ride a hoverbike on a race track... once, assuming you win your first time, then there's no reason to do it again.- Limited save points in 2024 is weird, even if they are frequently placed. It's not 1994 anymore, especially since this isn't an "old school style/difficulty" game. I get using save points to prevent cheesing things in games, but there's nothing to cheese here. Could easily just have everyone recover fully after every fight which allows much more free use of abilities and skills (and aggressive encounters).- Story pacing and content. The first third is extremely slow burn, except for when it throws a bunch of exposition at you and says "now care!" The middle third is solid once things get rolling, characters are established, and the world gets fleshed out. The final third and ending  Not the biggest fan when all was said and done.- No Steam cloud save. I saw the dev discuss this in another review where it would be difficult to implement at this stage... but that's really something that should be planned for from the beginning. Edit: I've found out the save data is stored in the . This alone deserves a negative review, even if we exclude everything else.+/- The OST is well made and often fits the environments... but it's just so sluggish most of the time. Add that to combat's slow pace and I'd get tired from being somewhat bored after less than an hour of playtime. +/- The UI is... fine? Clean and clear, gets the job done. Scrolling long lists becomes a chore without the usual feature of hitting left/right to scroll entire pages or some equivalent.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: Only 3.5 hours in but everything I have seen so far is very promising. Well-written dialogue, good but not great combat (yet), great music and art style.Edit: After finishing I can definitively say this is a great game, well worth your time and money. The combat started really easy, but in the second act it started to increase to a satisfying level of difficulty. The visuals remained great throughout, the cinematography is really fun and adds a lot to the experience. I think the strongest factor in Beyond Galaxyland is in its pacing. Chrono Trigger, a classic JRPG, is a good analogue to BGL. It's quick and snappy, and you find yourself in a new location every hour or so. The story got more and more interesting as the game went on and I liked the ending.As far as negatives go, there isn't much to complain about, but I'd say the character arcs themselves needed a bit more fleshing out. The character of Pablo mystified me from start to finish. The music, while fantastic in its own right, feels a bit samey the longer you play, with heavy emphasis on trap beats. Overall my take is Beyond Galaxyland, while flying under the radar for most currently, will be regarded as a cult classic in the years to come. Especially at this price point, if you are interested in narrative-driven turn based RPGs, this is a must-buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Galaxyland is literally the game I would make if I had the time, money, and gumption. I make no hesitation to say that. A beautiful blend of some of the best game mechanics over Final Fantasy, Bioshock, and Pokémon, as well as sci fi story beats ranging from classical authors like Douglas Adams to Larry Niven. The story is of teenage Doug being whisked away by DreamCore to their corporate intergalactic nature preserve Galaxyland after an apocalyptic entity known as "The End" destroys Earth, and makes Doug a prime endangered species for preservation. Throughout the game, you befriend robots and aliens and some of the other preserved humans as you traipse around Galaxyland, discovering the true nature of DreamCore, "The End," and the mysterious terrorist known as Malefactor. The game has extremely varied gameplay with diverse minigames galore so you'll never get bored. While art direction is a bit weak on the human pixel art, hand-drawn portraits and everything else in the pixel art is amazing quality, and major kudos to its cinematography and use of dutch angles. The soundtrack is so good I bought it off sale at full price. Game is a perfect 14ish hours with decent challenge and progression throughout the whole game. It easily earns a 10/10 for me, and will be a studio I'll be eyeing for future games. P.S. -- controller extremely recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing irritates me more than when a game I've been thoroughly enjoying begins to pick up in terms of character development, story, and world building, just to abruptly cease for no apparent reason. Beyond Galaxy Land is one of those rare JRPG experiences that is exceptionally well-designed. It has a lot of character and aims to tell a story about humanity and all culture throughout space time facing an extermination event like no other. A combination of turn-based response time combat, exploration, and the freedom to play each character however you choose, rather than being confined, there is a lot of freedom here, as well as loads of enjoyable mini-games. My biggest gripe, unfortunately is the fact that while I really do like this game. The ending is what kills it for me. I can't think of any other games that left me with such a bitter taste in my mouth, but imagine playing your favorite game with the ending removed and replaced with a "make up your own story" ending. That's how the game ends, after all of the struggles, all of the build up and the sudden emotional twist in the story bringing you closer and closer to each character, it's over.Don't get me wrong, the game itself, the build-up before the climax, is fantastic; you can capture bosses, use their powers, and do a lot with the 15 hours of content this game provides to you as a gamer; however, if you're looking for a very powerful story and a new game plus, both of those features are severely lacking. It's as if they lost interest in the last stretch and put it off to save time. The story was also rather predictable.

_childDocuments_.review: its not bad, exactly.  that said, i'm struggling to get into it a bit, like after 5 hours the game feels like a bit of a chore. For some folks, you might like it more.  I suppose i'll try to explain.The good:- the environments are well polished.  honestly they feel well done.  this is probably what made me want to buy the game.- the writing is funny at times.  - the game definitely has its charm.- there's some light platforming that's alright enoughThe bad:- the combat is kind of, idk something.  its a mario rpg style battle system (timed presses of the a button, well sometimes).  its got some glaring problems though.  there's a whole like capture enemies to give your heroes powers mechanic.  this is usually good, but you have enough sp (mp) to use literally one attack, and then you've got to use an item to recover to do another one.  Its not hard to get items to refill the sp, but it really slows down combat.  And, given the penalty for using these abilities, most of the time they don't really do enough for you to make it work it.  Its also got an AP, ability point system, where you get ability points as you fight. This is also normally a fine mechanic, however the way its implemented in this game just ends up making the combat feel slowwww  The party shares ap, and if you fail to get a timed button press right, you lose AP.  The max cap on the AP is super low.  And, I think this is the kicker, there will be things you pretty much have to do in combat that require ap.  you'll kinda spent two turns grinding enough AP to remove an enemies sheild, only to have to do it again for the next two enemies -so its just, slow grind through the battle.  basically, the AP and the SP are kinda pointless and you end up just mashing the basic attack almost exclusively.  no real strategy needed - depending on how much you like combat in your jrpgs, this might be a good thing for you - for me though, i'm kinda bored.- you get a level up, every two levels you get like 1 SP.  I mean, its just a slow game.  And its clearly designed around this because the best course of action is basically not to do anything interesting or have to think about what you're doing- everything so far feels kinda linear, not a lot to explore, but not as exciting as a FF game when its on the rails- heroes are white, supporting characters are disabled poc.  idk, how about a white person with a disability and a black person as the hero?The, other?- the music is both good and not my favorite.  Like the game is sorta this mandatory whismical all the time, and the music really drive that home.  It just gets, idk, kinda old, feeling like you're constantly playing in a clown car?  Its not bad music, i just wish it wasn't constantly reminding me that 'this game is supposed to be funny'.idk, i'm not sure if i'm gonna make it through this game or not.  I got it on sale for 10 bucks - i don't feel ripped off.  The environments are good and the story is interesting, but the combat is kinda annoying me right now.  its just, so, ugh, slow.  maybe i'll take a break and give it another shot in a couple weeks.  Depending on how much you like 'funny', easy combat, simple puzzles, you might be into it - but  yea, there's a pretty particular audience for this one.  ymmv.

_childDocuments_.review: 10 hours in and I'm absolutely loving this game - there's something about this that has me absolutely hooked.  The environments are stunning, the characters amusing, and the story intriguing enough to make me come back for more and more and not want to stop. I used to say I wasn't a fan of pixel adventure games with simplistic combat - but after playing this and Eastward I don't think that's the case any longer. Maybe it's because I'm older (early 40s) and don't need the rush of hard or complex combat to enjoy a game.....I don't know, I'm not really sure - all I know is that I now understand why people play games just to watch a story unfold. Maybe it's because it's my first turn-based RPG but I can't fault the combat for what it is - simple to understand with enough complexity to not make it feel mindless.I was going to wait until I was done with the game to post a review, but I just wanted to thank the developer and encourage him (or her) to continue to produce games because they definitely have talent.I'll update my review once I've completed it but this is one of my favorite games I've played this year - and I've played a decent amount.Edit:Just beat the game. I really, really enjoyed the experience. I saw one reviewer complaining about the ending but I thought it was more than good enough. I really hope this game gets more attention as I think it's one of my favorite indie games I've played and I think a lot of people are missing out. I hope to see this universe expanded on.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun rpg. When i saw it pop up on the green man gaming discord i immediately bought it. I am a sucker for smaller team jrpgs and will always support them when i can. i wasn't wrong about this one either First of all the sound track is pretty unique a mix of dubstep and a bit of pop flare i could be wrong there im not musically inclined but either was it was a great listen through out the game. especially the final battle. Good stuff. Now on to the game it self honestly the story was ok you play as doug who was forcefully pulled from his homeland and sent to galaxyland where he is safe from " the end "  which destroys anything in it's path. galaxy land isn't immune from the end so he tries to find a way back home. in the mean time you run into all sorts of jrpg shinanigins such as enemies on the field turning in to turn based battles captureing monsters leveling up plot twists and a baddie at the end of it all. The captureing machanic isn't really all that unique as you just weaking the monster a bit to capture it then you equip it as a summon then it levels up to unlock abilities. You can probebly ignore this but i wouldn't as the abilities monsters have are usefull.   This game is good old turn based fun accept with a small twist which i liked. Each character has a set amount of turn points these are the amount of times you can attack per round you can increase these with accessories and make your hardest hitter a tank. Each character shares an ability point pool which decreases every time you are hit and every time you hit the enemy you can also end your turn to add to your ability point pool which i liked. If you are looking for a good time to kill before the next big release this game you can't say no to.

_childDocuments_.review: - Soundtrack: 8/10 (Self-made, evolving music, sometimes a bit too aggressively electronic for my taste, but overall very catchy, not annoying and memorable, if I were more into this type of music, it would probably be an easy 10/10)- Graphics: 9.9/10 (Best Pixelart I have seen in ages, would be 11/10 if the character portraits were more in style with the universe. Honestly they almost broke the initial purchase for me. They look completely out of style with the rest of the game and way too young.)- Story: 8/10 (Highly engaging, asking existential questions fitting our current state of the world, I would love to deep talk with the devs, they seem like true world and self-explorers! Also, so far no annoyingly stupid character desicions/stupidity. The first half was overall more engaging.)- Gameplay: 10/10 (The fun doesn't stop, moving around, exploring, flying your ship, combat, jump and run passages, puzzles, stealth like Metal Gear type passages, different types of Racing games, it has A LOT to offer... AND it lets you skip any racing or puzzle passages, so you can actually adjust the broadness of gameplay experiences to your liking.)EDIT: Update after beating it for the first time, my save file sais I only took short of 18 hours and I have to admit it feels way too short. There seem to be a lot of systems that are underused and the game was also way too easy overall and I am not even an RPG veteran.That is all the critique I have, tho. Ending was bittersweet, don't know how to do it better, but it felt like something was missing. Gameplay experience in the time I played was consistently top tier! More sidequests and more utilisation of existing areas and/or mechanics and shops (catching/releasing/crafting/puzzles) it seems to be a perfect base to expand upon. Here is to hoping for DLC! Because the game is well priced at 15€ imo!EDIT: First update, because WOW! The game just keeps on giving, opening up, going deeper. My only fear is that it will end too soon. I also thought that it was way too easy for any seasoned RPG player, and that might still be true, but a) it so far has not detracted from my enjoyment and b) it got WAY harder after it really opens up and most importantly c) it is perfectly challenging without expecting you to try hard and master for example a race just to get all the rewards. I feel it maybe rewards the player 15-20% too easily, but it is nicely designed in a way that let's everyone get this feeling of accomplishment of going the extra mile to nail every passage of the game. It also bolsters my intent of replaying it in the future and re-enjoying unlocking everything. It's just a fun world to be in, with - for me - the exactly right balance of engagement vs. enjoyment and relaxing chill gameplay of just being there. The combat is also evolving into more and more fun with each progression and deepening of the system. Oh and let me just give you a hint in case you are reading this and start to play: GET THE SPARE PARTS ASAP! You are not gonna regret it ;)---Original Review after ~7h:So far, I have loved every inch and every second of this game! It feels to me like it has set alight a new love for what good games contain and should play/feel like. I'm beyond amazed by the awesome tutorial and the option to "just get the basics" and so far, every hour or so the game opens up even more when I don't even expect it anymore. I feel there are great ideas around every corner. Will update after I finish this gem and I am gonna take my sweet time.

_childDocuments_.review: Beyond Galaxy Land is an excellent RPG. Indie devs definitely have all the free reigns on how they envisioned this game. Very unique look and could highly appeal to people who enjoy old school RPG's.But I have 2 complaints. 1 small complaint and 1 big complaint. The 1st minor issue is not being able to swap characters when you're on your ship. It doesn't matter if you're exploring the Galaxy or inside your ship hanging out with the other characters you simply can't swap characters regardless. Now you can swap characters when you land your ship on a planet or if you're in combat. Weird design choice and I'm not sure whether the devs overlooked this or if it's intentional.The 2nd complaint of mine and it's a big one is that there's no support for steam cloud. Why? Why am I not allowed to play this game on the go with my Steam Deck and swap back and forth with my PC? I get it that they are indie dev and they have limited resources. However there's a bunch of Indie RPG's that came out last year and I'll name a few like Chained Echoes and Sea of the Stars which both support steam cloud saves. I have both in my library and played them on both my PC and Steam Deck when I'm on the go and I know for a fact that those 2 games have steam cloud support. It does hamper the experience quite a bit considering that this game is also on Steam platform but doesn't take advantage of a good optional feature.All in all this is a great game however if having zero steam cloud support bother you then I suggest you wait until they add that feature... That is if the devs of this game wanted to do so. Had I done my research properly may be I would've avoided this game but at the same this is really a good game. You decide what you want.

You can also capture enemies to use as summons, which act like moves / buffs / debuffs, so it scratches that Pokemon itch too, which I feel like is undersold for a reason: because this game is not a 'creature collector' at the core.Enjoying the story so far, and off the top of my head it isn't one I've seen before. Light early game spoilers but basically an alien race creates portals to get a bunch of intelligent species from various worlds through, but there is a question of whether you're actually be helped or something more nefarious is going on. The world building is really nice, aliens and robots all think humans are hilarious for lots of reasons which is kind of cute. This is one of those games where you can tell the developer really, really cared because of all the minor details and polish. Sadly a rarity these days. The only thing it is missing is Steam Cloud Save support, but I'd imagine that is coming as I'm sure the dev has seen the feedback.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art and an interesting story are what drew me in. The game also has a pretty solid turn-based combat system with some real-time elements, monster capturing mechanic and the ability to take photos of enemies and creatures you encounter in your travels. It has a good number of sidequests and a racing minigame too. For me the only downside is that the game is fairly short (it took me 27 hours to 100%) and has little to no replay value. There's a new game + mode, but no reason to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like jrpg sidecroller.I like the atmo, the story so far (3h in) is more catching than other big productions. Battle System is round based fun. Nothing special but it works and keeps it interesting.Regarding the prize and if you like jrpg's and scifi setting, there is not much to regret for only a couple of euros.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Beyond Galaxyland. The art style drew me in and the music, characters and the worlds to explore kept me interested. The 2D gameplay works well in the simplistic approach the game takes to the RPG genre and although sometimes it feels like the game tries a bunch of ideas to see what lands, I think it executes most of it pretty well.I have mixed feelings on the story. Its very simple as I said, most of the side quests are pretty straightforward with the exception of some more obscure things like finding hidden objects or creatures on the screen. But I don't think the approach of simplicity necessarily hurts the game. I didn't love the ending, though. It leaves things pretty open, almost like there could be more in the future, but at the same time it 'wraps up' in a way I could see it being left alone like this. I dunno. I wanted to see more and the game cut me off.Overall though, it was good. I'd put it at about the same score as 'Sea of Stars' - probably a 7-8/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: What nice and atmosphering RPG. Well written Texts and cool Character's. After some minutes you are into the Adventure Story. The jumping it's sometimes a little bit tricky but this at moment the only negative point. I am really impressed about a one person game development. the most AAAA Company's cannot make a good game like Beyond Galaxyland 😁.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: I am adding my review because there are not many, while the game deserves some attention - even though I am early in the game, I feel that it might be a gem!The settings is wonderful and the jokes land perfectly. The way jRPG fights, platforming and puzzles intertwine is surprisingly cool. The characters are already taking shape - I am starting to like them. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review: Popped out of nowhere for me. Never seen a preview or anything. Watched the trailer here on Steam, loved what I saw and purchased it. Really funny so far. I'm usually turned off by games that aren't fully voiced but the dialogues are fun to read so far. Visually it's going into that Anno Mutationem/Star Ocean Second Story R direction. It's not as crisp as those two games but it's still full of details and pulls me into its setting.The story is also not really telling you much about what you're going to experience. I like that a lot of weird stuff happens and that I get to be a passenger, just like Doug who has no idea what's going on. It(so far) did a good job of pulling me in and wanting me to hop onto this ride.Combat is turn-based and has a light creature collecting feature. (Creatures you capture don't fight for you but you're able to use their unique abilities in combat)It's very simplistic so i'm not sure if it gets boring later on or if encounters gradually become more challenging and new mechanics will come into play but I'm eager to see what the game has to offer.Platforming feels floaty and the platforming animations are a bit stiff. If you're coming from a Metroidvania, you may get disappointed by what the platforming in BG is offering. I'm here for the setting and story for the most part so I may be able to ignore those downsides.For the price it costs, I can  highly recommend giving it a try. It's fun to read, look at and mostly fun to play as well. If this is rly made by 1 developer, I have to say that he did a fantastic job!
_childDocuments_.name: Beyond Galaxyland

_childDocuments_.review:
Inspired by classic sci-fi movies, Beyond Galaxyland is an intergalactic, 2.5D adventure-RPG set among the stars. Step into the sneakers of high-schooler Doug, as he’s whisked away to ‘Galaxyland’ - a zoo-like solar system of planets - on an epic quest to save Earth itself.

An all-new take on the beloved RPG adventures of old, prepare for a journey like no other, skyrocketing through teeming jungles, neon-lit cities, and cybernetic casinos, with each new planet brimming with intriguing characters, fiendish adversaries, and many other surprises.

Accompanied by Doug’s pet guinea pig - the pistol-wielding Boom Boom - and a sentient robot called MartyBot, together you must defend the world against an all-powerful entity known only as ‘The End’, before it conquers the Universe itself...

name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew
detailed_description: Ahoy, cursed pirate! This is Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew , an all-new stealth strategy game set during an alternate history of the Golden Age of Piracy. The Curse of Lost Souls haunts the mysterious island chain known as the Lost Caribbean, which is under the control of the terrible forces of the Inquisition. They despise all that is supernatural and use soul devouring fire to hunt cursed pirates like you! Pull-off an epic heist and salvage a mysterious treasure of otherworldly power to defy the army of the Inquisition. Infiltrate their fortresses. Sneak behind enemy lines. Cleverly combine the magical skills of your crew to take out a variety of enemies with carefully considered tactics. Feel like a brilliant mastermind when your plan clicks perfectly into place! Embark on a journey with cursed pirate Afia and seek the legendary Black Pearls to revive a cursed crew of your own. Each of your eight shipmates is a playable character with an individual personality and armed with unique supernatural powers. Launch friend or foe with Gaëlle's magical cannon, use Mr. Mercury's soul anchor to open a magic portal or dash across spacetime for split second stealth attacks with Afia's mythical sword. Join The Red Marley, a ghost ship with a living soul. On deck, plan your next adventure or just hang out with your crew mates while they enjoy their un-life. Get to know these legendary cursed pirates of the Lost Caribbean. With individual character missions find out about their backstories, learn who they are and what led them on their cursed journeys. Freely select your crew members before embarking on each mission. Utilize their unique abilities to find new strategies against the forces of the Inquisition. Plot your own path to enter and exit each island, be stealthy or more head-on in your play style and use the environment to your advantage. It's your playground to experiment in! Go ashore a variety of exotic islands in the Lost Caribbean. From locales oozing with cursed soul magic to tropical beaches and lively pirate shanty towns: Every island is a unique hand-crafted sandbox where adventures await. The powerful time-manipulating magic of your ghost ship is yours to wield. Pause time to consider your strategic choices or queue up multiple character actions. Capture a memory of every passing moment, to instantly return to if things go south. Change your approach and tactics to discover own unique solutions to each moment in the game – in your own time!

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. It's the usual Mimimi quality and unique game play that they do so well in. A ton of content and variation to one's play style, as well as being able to tailor the difficulty to whatever you like. I personally like playing these games at the max difficulty right away, and I can defiantly say that it gets pretty damn hard halfway through to the end. I was a little worried at first because this game unlike the other two games, Shadow Tactics and Desperados III, the game felt fairly easy in the beginning. Although as soon as the first "boss" type stage happened, it finally felt like one of the hardest challenges in this series of Mimimi games. And unlike the other two games, this one actually includes the fact that you save and reload extremely often, into the lore similarly to Undertale. Again, as per usual the story and music is amazing as well, and it certainly has a lot of visually artistic flare to the maps and characters. One more comment, I don't know how but every one of these games has incredibly good voice acting for every single character. The same generic enemy you see in droves in every mission, had like 20 voice actors listed in the credits. It just shows the artistic quality to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if you played any of the prior entires, or just like stealth games in general, this is basically a top tier distillation.Finished the game, and now currently playing for badges. This game unlike the prior entries has far more replay value if you're going to be hunting for 100%. Generally speaking, you have more of everything the prior entries tried to do, better abilities, more abilities, more characters, more inventive levels, longer story and personalities. Just more of everything. This is the developer's last game and they've done it justice. A final DLC with two more characters was added which is just wonderful, and level editor modding tools added as a parting gift for a proper send off.Basically a 10/10 game in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit is Mimimi's crowning achievement. Made in the rather niche genre of stealth strategy this game has you take a crew of pirates across several isles and spy on and assassinate the inquisition. Each character has two abilities which can be highly different from the others; for example Suleidy can spawn a bush to give you cover to hide in almost anywhere. This allows you to find different angles of attack and take care of bodies easily. Meanwhile Toya can place a beacon in a small radius around him, and then teleport back to it from anywhere. Really useful when trying to infiltrate a centralized position as you can place the beacon in a bush, sneak in, shank a guy, then teleport to the exact opposite side of said compound while the inquisition fruitlessly searches for you. A big risk this game takes is with its openness. After the first three missions to get your sea legs under you, you have a choice of which of the several islands to go to next. Additionally, if that wasn't enough, after you get the first character, Afia Manticato, you have a choice of two, and then after that, all the rest. Desperadoes 3 and Shadow Tactics, Mimimi's previous games in this genre, had each character limited to certain missions and the missions were in a set order. While I have heard complaints that this causes each mission to be unable to be made with exact characters in mind, I think there is much to be gained from the many choices available. I wouldn't want it to be done with every game in this genre, but I applaud Mimimi for taking this risk. The characters have interesting personalities, and varying backstories. From Gaelle who accidentally shot out her stomach with a cannon ball, to Toya's belief that cooking is a war he doesn't intend to lose, each of them are larger than life. There are also two dlcs, one of which reintroduces Yuki from Shadow Tactics, and the other Zagan, who has some interesting abilities. He can render enemies catatonic from range, but it costs him a hit point. No matter, his base melee attack restores a hit point. Very interesting use of health as a resource, in a game where you don't have much of it.

The game is good, but a bit hard to compare to shadow tactics or desperados 3 due to semi-open gameplay it offers, especialy that it's been some time since i played them.Overall the game is good and even if mentioned games were i think better at some aspects this one is still worth a recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 are both games that easily go in my top 5 all time best games ever. I was so excited to play Shadow Gambit and so sad to hear that its Mimimi’s last game. When I first started playing The Cursed Crew, however, I didn’t like it as much as its predecessors. Maybe I’m an old curmudgeon yelling that things were better in my day but I just didn’t vibe with the UI at first. And I don’t really enjoy the undead pirate theme, as popular as it is.The more I played, however, the more I grew to love this game. It has a lot that is different from the previous games. You select characters rather than having specific ones chosen for you. The undead thing allows for magic which added a lot more variety to the powers the characters can use. No longer are you limited to throwing shuriken or knives or setting traps and dressing in disguise. Now you can teleport, possess your enemies, disappear into an alternate dimension until its time to reappear, or make bushes to hide in grow anywhere you want. I still don’t care much for undead pirates but I enjoyed the way it opened up gameplay.It does result in some imbalance. Some characters, like Gaelle and Zagan, were helpful but almost always just along for the ride. Others, like Afia, John and most of all Suleidy could almost take out an entire island by themselves. Suleidy routinely accounted for 60-80% of kills and a plurality of play time in a mission.The final mission in this game isn’t as difficult as Desperados though it’s unique within the game in the same way. The difficulty I experienced in it was mostly just in understanding what I needed to do to overcome the main boss. Once I knew that, it was over pretty quickly.Overall, a 5 star game and a definite recommend. Due to the theme, I probably wouldn’t put it on the medal stand with ST and D3 but it’s a very good game and a great swan song from favorite developer.

_childDocuments_.review: - Probably the best stealth tactics game out there, overtaking Desperados 3. Very good gameplay overall, felt like the next logical step for the genre.- The characters felt equally overpowered in a good way, all of them had their upsides and it was hard to have a bad team setup- Mission length and difficulty was toned down compared to other games in the genre, which is only a good thing since these games tend to be very hard and have very long missions- Because characters could be unlocked in any order and islands were reused for several missions and could be done in any order, there were very few good, memorable setpiece missions that stood out from the rest. In contrast, I still remember a lot of Desperados 3 missions because the environments and team compositions were specifically designed for their respective missions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant creation from the too-short-lived Mimimi studio. It takes the original stealth strategy genre from the original Commandos series to new heights. I really can't say enough good things about this game, from the script to the voice acting to the game mechanics it really is amazing. It's not a AAA title, and it's not full of action and explosions, but it's a 100% solid game that will keep you thinking and entertained all the way through. I just completed the main story at 75 hours in, and will come back in a few months to revisit the extra missions that remain.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is likely my indie game of the year. The developers have truly outdone themselves with this title. The game offers exceptional tactical gameplay, with action queuing mechanics for each crew member and intricate timing to take out guards one at a time. Each unlocked character is unique and entertaining, offering a variety of abilities and gameplay possibilities. The setting of cursed pirates and supernatural abilities revitalizes the basic strategy gameplay. Players have much more freedom in mission selection and building their cursed crew. The game's music is excellent and fits perfectly within the game's context. Although some levels can become repetitive, especially when replaying to complete special character missions, the game overall is an exceptional stealth experience and a must-play for fans of previous Mimimi games. I highly recommend this game to everyone, whether you have played games in the genre before or are new to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Game is not worth a full price but I would recommend buying it if you can get it on sale - especially if you liked other games of this studio.Both fans of stealth tactics games and people unfamiliar with the genre can enjoy Shadow Gambit, as it offers more diverse gameplay mechanics than other Mimimi productions, but it is also more accessible to new players. However, don't be surprised if you get bored with the uninteresting story and abandon the game halfway through.Full review:The first thing to discuss is the world setting. The theme of magical pirates did not seem very interesting to me initially (and I think it may be the case for many other people). Fortunately, it is not that bad once you start playing. However, the game visibly struggles with creating a believable vision of this weird world. It did not put me off completely but at the same time the game was never able to make me feel immersed.In terms of mechanics Shadow Gambit is definitely a step up from previous Mimimi games. Characters now have access to the powerful magical abilities. You can also choose any combination of crew members for most missions. This makes the gameplay more diverse - there are a lot of possible approaches for solving every level. It also adds to replayability (but only a little bit as game gets boring quite quickly due to other reasons). The downside is that the puzzles had to be designed so that they can be solved with any trio of characters, making the missions much easier than in previous Mimimi games. Nonetheless, gameplay is very polished and definitely enjoyable.The major weakpoint of Shadow Gambit is story. Main plot is just boring and the way whole story is structured makes things even worse. On the top-level the story is a bunch of small missions which in other games would be considered as optional.For example, at some point in order to proceed with the main quest you have to resurrect your crew. Gathering a party is a quite common motive in many games. But the way it is implemented here is just bad. Game just shows you something like "Resurrect crew members (0/N done)". Then, to resurrect each of them you have to collect two items. These items are exactly the same for every member and they are obtained as rewards for completing missions. Then, shortly after gathering the crew you will see another quest with a counter - "Complete N missions of X type to proceed further".Such design is extremely predictable and generic. Although the missions themselves are decently implemented, they contribute little to the main story, making the whole experience bland. Due to the lack of clear storytelling, I spent most of my time feeling like I was playing level 1, level 2, ... of some a puzzle game.The same goes for the crew members, which were one of the main selling points of the game. They have different skills and each one has their own little story, but due to the generic way they are unlocked and how their subplots play out, they quickly became for me "member 3 with skill X", "member 4 with skill Y", etc.However, despite the shortcomings listed above, my experience with the game was still positive. Shadow Gambit is as polished as all games from this studio. Clearing levels is generally enjoyable thanks to the well-designed game mechanics and the variety of tactics that can be used to solve puzzles. Unfortunately, these low- to mid-level elements are poorly combined at the top level of the main story, resulting in a repetitive and generic experience.Overall rating: 8 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: While the game systems are more crisp and there is more variety the game-play and story was much less interesting than Shogun where each level was custom made to work well with the characters you play as. Also the missions were much less inspired, in shogun you were poisoning tea and overheating bathwater, in Shadow Gambit you are just travelling from island to island to collect black pearls etc. Having magical abilities was interesting but really takes away from the charm that Shogun had.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Easily Mimimi's best game yet. The amount of freedom Shadow Gambit gives players to approach each mission is really something to behold. I'm only about 10 hours into my time with the game, but I'm constantly finding clever new interactions between all of the crew I've unlocked. I also love how much personality each of them has. Plus, I love how clever Shadow Gambit makes you feel when you pull off a deadly double or triple assassination.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of games like Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, so I was anticipating something along those lines. Nevertheless, this game managed to truly captivate me. With its fresh abilities, new character classes, and entertaining storyline, it pleasantly surprised me. Despite a few remaining bugs, they didn't hinder my enjoyment. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a big fan of Mimimi’s two previous stealth strategy games. However while playing Desperados 3, there’s always a nagging feeling that I’m basically playing a western reskin of Shadow Tactics. This is absolutely not the case for Shadow Gambit. The core of the game have been expanded to allow for a player progression system, many more new and diverse skills to distinguish characters’ toolsets from the other games, and the writing/setting now feels grander with more focus on fleshing out each crew member’s personalities. Enemy variety has been improved and there's now a sense of freedom on how you choose to tackle each map. All of the QOL features introduced in D3 are present here as well. It all comes together to be one of the most fulfilling gaming experiences coming out this year despite the tough competition.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Being a massive fan of Mimimi's previous games, I was really looking forward to this one.When I first started playing, I wasn't sure if I was going to like it. Some things are the same as before but some things are new. The first few levels seemed to be too easy but it really clicked after Act I had finished. The characters are a delight to play, some of the new skills are very clever. The difficulty went up a notch but never frustratingly so.EDIT: Now I've finished the game, I can honestly say this is a fantastic way for Mimimi to end their development. The ending actually brought tears to my eyes as it felt like I had become part of the crew of the Red Marley myself! What a way to go out, Mimimi.EDIT2: I also want to add that this game provides extreme value for money. There is a ton of stuff to do after the main quests are done. I'm only at 50% completion after 40-odd hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I kept an eye on this game through development and it looked promising. Now, after playing it my expectations have been exceeded. I am completely impressed with the gameplay, the depth put into each character, and how each character's unique abilities can be used is so many unexpected ways. There's a lot of creativity in the design which, in turn, gives the player a plethora of options to be creative,The built-in F5 replay/retry is really great. Pulling off successful moves and being able to try the scenario again right away if you want to. Or, of course, if you fail you can press F8 and BAM if you saved you are right back where you were before you messed up. lolKudos to the team at Mimimi Games on this gem!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: The developers have tried to make this not just a Desperados clone, but to make it unique in its own way, sadly they made one wrong decision, which basically destroyed the whole game: the ability to choose your crew. It may look like an interesting, but rather unimportant feature, but it is way more important than you think it is.Lets start with the recruiting of the crew. Instead of giving each member their own unique entrance, you will get all of their corpses, without any background story. There is no attachment created, or feeling involved, you can select who you want to revive just based on facts, or their looks. This destroys the whole feeling of having a team. They try to repair this by giving each character's own quest, but the quests are boring and basically consist of some sentences spread across 1- to 3 missions, on maps you have visited 3-4 times.And then you get the map itself though, I will ignore the idiot who thought it would be a great idea to force player to play the same map 5 times!!! I just want to talk about the mechanics. Your crew is not balanced, there are strong alrounders and there are useless characters, who are only useful in certain conditions. So the developer had to make the map finishable with any crew constelation, by macking the maps very easy. There are surely some tricky part (mostly because you don't have the right members with you), but for the most part the maps are just a joke.   And last but not least the story: sadly this is the worst part in the whole game. Shadow Tactics had a great and engaging story, Desperados 3 was not as good, but still pretty solid, while this is just awful. _childDocuments_.review: I'll keep this short because I want to get back to buckling all the swashes. This is the best entry in the series. Replayability is massive. Great character roster with interesting skills - and solid voice acting from the cast. Catchy (yet entirely unobtrusive) music, which is a nice touch in a game where the missions can sometimes go long. Really sharp and vibrant visuals. And the whole thing is nicely tied together with a great little undead pirate story that concludes with an absolute gem of a final mission.Finally, on a note of personal preference, I loved how the quicksave/load mechanic of this series was incorporated so well into the story. _childDocuments_.review: As of this moment, the reception for the game is Overwhelmingly Positive -- it's not enough; this game should be the standard by which a new, higher, review classification is created.This is the best fantasy stealth tactics game available in recent memory. Gameplay, dialogue, art, music -- all top-notch. Controls are smooth, responsive, and intuitive. The game runs very stable and seems to scale well with available hardware resources.If you're a stealth perfectionist, this game will frustrate you in a good way; the game's design actively encourages iteration and revision to form an ideal plan of attack, without making it feel like a slog. _childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed CrewScore w/o Context: 90% of my butt hanging out of a bush ruining my carefully laid plansThe Context:I don't do well on boats. Seasickness washes over me like a fetid tide whenever the ship crests a wave, and eventually i devolve into a drooling, hyper-focused on the horizon, puddle of a person. Now insert stealth games for boats, and.....well you wont get a coherent sentence but the point is that stealth games and I don't mix well. That changed when Shadow Tactics was released a few years ago, and I had my eyes opened to games that had rebuffed me before. This genre is, to me, perfected in Shadow Gambit, and I'll dearly miss the devs behind it.Shadow Gambit does follow a lot of the conventions previously established in Mimimi's previous titles: top-down, real-time with pauses, unique small team-based stealth. Each scenario presented gives you a small sandbox to play in, objectives to complete, and multiple pathways to reach them. This works just as well as in previous games, with your characters avoiding view-cones, hiding in shrubbery, and meticulously picking off enemies when possible until the entire map is a graveyard (or one big naptime, if you're going non-lethal). Light sources, distractions, and traversal all play a big role as well. What sets this entry apart for me, is the characters., and strangely enough, the repetition.The cast is much larger and diverse than in previous games, each oozing with flavor and skill expression. While my favorites were the blind sniper and the bulky cannoneer, there's something for everyone here. While this may seem overwhelming as you collect more and more team members for a game that allows only 3 per mission, it actively encourages you to try each with the multiple revisits to a map. The sandboxes are large enough to encourage this pursuit, and allow for experimentation that previous games did not. While some get stale eventually, I never thought any overstayed their welcome too long.

_childDocuments_.review: One word: Demo!So few devs do demos ... or, they take down the demo the moment the game is released. Will it run on my PC? How does it perform? Will I like it? I'm restarting from the beginning because it's that fun.Love the art, music, tone, humor, and ... well ... everything. Not a huge fan of the key bindings but easily remedied. And honestly that's the  thing I could complain about in this game. Try the demo now!

If you really want to go the extra mile in supporting the people who made this game, you can go to their website  and buy the game directly from there at the same price it is listed on Steam, which takes 30% of profit from any given sale. _childDocuments_.review: I have been anticipating this game since it was first announced. It's exactly as I would have expected. No, BETTER.It's so satisfying to pause, set up multiple commands and then execute them all at once. Sneaking around view cones, and stuffing bodies in bushes or chucking them off cliffs so no one sees them. I like to be very sneaky and quite. No alarms ever, and I try not to use any noisy guns. I don't let my team get damaged at all. If there is an environmental kill I will do whatever I can to use that. I like that I can save a lot, pause a lot and load as much as I like. I don't feel rushed and I can really plan an attack. If I can take down many at once, I will. I turned the difficulty up because I played Desperados 3 a couple times. I still like to run away from moving view cones so I left that setting the same. But I keep my guys at low health and low ammo. And I maximize the enemies. I take a very long time to look at a situation before I move in. Lots of planning and quick loads! I'll use bushes, elevated terrain and buildings as much as I can. I use all the hot keys, so it feels like I'm typing commands. Satisfying!The pirates theme is awesome! Amazing story and dialog! Every line is perfectly written and the characters are well spoken. What is said when given orders is often funny or motivating for the player. Afia is a great character. She's bold and fearless yet kind to her crew. The enemy force is unique! It works very well. The ship is fun and I look forward to more of the story around that. I'm actually paying attention to the story, so that's a good sign!The elevated terrain and the island environment is so beautiful. Day time watch out for leaving foot steps. Night time, put out lanterns so they can't see you. They can hear you in the water so be quite! The uniqueness of each characters abilities I've never seen before! I haven't tested them all out yet but having them work with each other is a fun part of the puzzle.This game is made for me! I wouldn't change anything I don't think. Except, I think the hot key reminders of the quick save and quick load at the bottom right of the screen doesn't need to be there taking up space. I recommend this game fifty times if I could!!! five stars, two skeletal thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game.  Like Larian, Mimimi has honed their craft and created a place in gaming where they are king.Shadow Gambit builds on the previous (great) games of Desperados III and Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, each an amazing game in their own right.  So far, I am thinking Shadow Gambit is the best of them all.  Sadly, the game developer is closing its doors after releasing this wonderful opus.  If you like isometric (or top down) stealth and tactics games like Commandos, Partisans 1941, or Heat Signature, you'll enjoy this game.  If you've played Mimimi's previous games of Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun or Desperados III, you'll  know exactly what you're in for.Shadow Gambit, like others in this genre, has you controlling one or more characters to predominantly sneak through a map to multiple goals given a different sets of abilities depending on your characters at play.  You have the ability to pause the game and plan your next move.  Also incorporated in the game is the encouragement to save and reload- frequently.What makes this game interesting is the large variety of paths and methods to accomplish your goal, mostly how to get past or subdue guards who are in the way of your objective.  Shadow Gambit weaves its game play into a pirate story line and is interesting enough to entertain and provide plausible in-universe explanation and narrative.Shadow Gambit also lets you build your pirate crew, choosing which shipmates (each with different abilities) to join you as progress.  Because you can potentially have any one of the crew on a mission at any given time, each map must give multiple ways of accomplishing the goals; this is good and bad.  In one way, it gives you many options, and you're not stuck with having to have certain character(s) a particular mission.  On the other hand, sometimes maps feel watered-down in that an obvious but less creative method can simple be used to progress.  In many cases, you can just hide in a bush and stab a guard at the appropriate time.I haven't gotten far eough to see if there're replay incentives- there seems to be achievements which may require the player to return to maps with only specific characters as a challenge.  Currently, I've had to replay a map because I missed an objective, so I'm trying to accomplish it with only one character.  This may be difficult since some enemies require cooperation between characters to subdue.Shadow Gambit is a lovely game of strategy and planning, with dash of pirate humour.  I recommend you pick it and experience this genre at its zenith.

I do hope they come up with some more missions and islands to keep it alive (or rather undead) for a little longer since I would love to see more of the world they are building here. Or maybe they'll put all their effort into a second installment, where we get more locations, new abilities, new characters and more of Shadows Gambit: The Cursed Crew.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest I find it really hard to recommend this game... I still do, but not really because of the game itself.The genre is sadly far underrated and one which I favor the most. Mimimi games has my full support and created various great titles... especially shadow tactics was a great hit for me!This game ... is kinda mediocre, sadly. If you like the genre it's still worth the buy as you wont find to many other examples.Let's be objective - what is my critic? Sadly this game wants to much and forgets the core.- You can hire various crewmembers, but you need some grind to get them and it feels like the game has to pay orginality in maps and story to allow this. I would prefer maps which are designed for certain characters and therefore feel more fluent instead of this...- I like some characters, so far I even like most characters. Still their little stories feel more like additional work and I would prefer to learn more about them in the main plot instead of having seperated stuff that feels kinda blut, despite it being original and funny from time to time. Still it feels forced and also needs grind as I can't follow the stories, but need to do them bit by bit between missions...- Talking about the between missions.... not a fan of the ship in general. Just feels like a time waste to me, it's basically like the run from that guy to that guy and deliver a message quest you have in mmorpgs. Nobody needs that! Just start the missions from the menue and spare the ressources for tha main game. Same for the seperated character tutorials and all such stuff...- The mechanics in this one feel less well balanced, some characters seem quite strong, but they need to be! Because the timing has to be on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ point! To be hones I play on legend and that might be the reason - but do I need to lower the difficulty to have fun? It's more about unforgiving and poorly designed mechanics. Distractions for example give you EXACTLY the time to do a kill or whatever, if u waste a freaking second you will be detected. Thats not good design or difficult, but simply annoying and makes me basically pause the game at every action and use the tactiv mode on close to every action just to hit the right timing! Thats simply doesn't give the game a fluent feel, but feels like work and grind <.<'Give the spy a constant distraction! Why nerf such? Give the distractions a little more time to use them.
