_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Stealth RTS game we have so far. If you like Commandos as well previous Mimimi titles, you'll love this._____________________________________ is Mimimi Games latest (and last) title, and their very first self-published game, which gave them tons of artistic freedom into crafting the ultimate Stealth RTS and take the genre to a new level.I've been a huge fan of their games since  and they never fail to deliver;  is no exception.It's clear as day the passion the dev team has for the Stealth RTS genre, and it shows in every single aspect. They're is always trying to find ways to expand and reinvent the genre with new mechanics and abilities.Much like other Stealth RTS, the game encourages players to reload their quick saves and try again. What I like about this game is how they made the save system as part of the game's narrative, which is brilliant and exceptionally well executed.✅ The game is actually surprisingly long. I'm a veteran on Mimimi games and finished most missions without many issues, but still took me around 40 hours.✅ The story is simple yet well written, with some exploration on themes such as dealing with grief and the corruption of power. Characters ooze personality with the amazing voice acting.✅ Art direction, soundtrack and voice acting is absolutely top-notch. Completely nailed the atmosphere.✅ UI is tidy and clean while still being gloomy to fit the whole "cursed pirate" motif.✅ Gameplay is more streamlined, which will make the title more accessible to players who are new to the Stealth RTS genre. However, characters have supernatural abilities which greatly spices up the genre.✅ The skill effects are flashy and super satisfying to watch.✅ The quality-of-life changes compared to  are truly a welcome addition. The top view when zooming the furthest out is very handy as it shows the map and all enemies that are still alive.✅ The hub area in the form of the Red Marley (the ship) adds so much to the narrative and atmosphere of the game. In addition, players can use their abilities on the skeleton crew, which serves as a good playground to test character synergy and combos.✅ The training ground to learn the mechanics of new crewmates was a brilliant addition.✅ Each character have exclusive and optional quests, called Crew Tales, which help flesh their personalities and backstories better. There are also story-related missions to further explore their backgrounds.✅ The whole system to unlock new crewmates feels rewarding and adds strategical planning. You can see their whole skillset before reviving them.✅ Players can change the shortcuts for select crewmembers at any time.✅ The Landing Spots for missions, the different crew member combinations, and the whopping 606 badges to unlock (in-game challenges) add tons of replay value.✅ Meticulously crafted stages with a lot more vertical space than previous games.✅ The accumulated Vigor system (used to upgrade abilities) encourages players to use different characters in missions.✅ Toya has the coolest crouch / stand-up animation ever.❌❌ Performance-wise, the game tanked a bit. I have a relatively decent PC (Ryzen 5700G, 32GB RAM, RTX 2060) and installed the game on a SSD, but I was getting some minor stutters and FPS drops (especially when using abilities), and sometimes my GPU temp would get as high as 80C; I've noticed that specific portions of the map trigger that issue. I even lowered graphics quality to the minimum in-game, as well capping FPS and forcing V-Sync on the NVIDIA Control Panel (on top of having V-Sync on in-game too), but still didn't fix the overheating. This was a problem back in the demo that persisted in the final release. Now that the team has disbanded I highly doubt it'll ever be fixed.❌ Less stages compared to previous games, which makes the game lack a bit of variety in scenery. Despite stages being massive and having multiple missions tied to them, said missions are short and focused on specific parts on the map. On top of that, every mission in the same map uses the exact same enemy placement, which can make playing the same map to complete different missions feel stale quickly.❌ Lack of enemy variety. You still have the trinity of Guard (Acolyte), Sentinel (Commissarius / Iudex) and Enforcer (Prognosticar) with some twists, but I was truly expecting more inventive enemy types. The Kindred were a nice, interesting addition, though.💡 The game is actually a bit easy if you're a veteran of the genre. The supernatural skills make a lot of obstacles and traversal faster, as well tackling on opponents easier. Enemy AI and placement is not very punishing either; and if you ring the alarm, the enemy patrols will return back to their base after the alert timer is over, as opposed to previous games where they'd become permanent patrolling enemies. I wish there was an option to increase enemy density and make ringing the alarm more punishing.💡 Given that the you have freedom to choose your party, most missions are designed in ways that they can be cleared with any team combination, which kinda holds back the developers to craft more intricate levels and enemy placement that are tied to specific characters; this is explored in the final level of the game, though.💡 Would be nice to have more keybind options for "inactive skills", like there is for non-lethal takedown. An example of that is how Afia has a non-lethal version of her Blink, but there are no keybinds for it. Could even be something like holding the keybind for a second to swap between lethal and non-lethal.💡 Given that players can choose their own teams when tackling missions, character interactions are more limited and stakes feel less personal. Also, in the Red Marley, only Afia can talk and banter with other characters. This makes character development feels a bit underwhelming; you can't for instance, talk to Gaëlle using Toya. Characters do have specific banters and comments depending on who is brought to the mission.💡 One thing I missed in this game is actual treasure hunting, with maps and everything. There was a very specific mission that had that, and wish this was more expanded on. Edit: they did add side missions where you can actually do that, in the latest patch._____________________________________Overall, I absolutely loved the game, even with my nitpicks and criticism; I'm really not trying to be harsh on the game, and I hope that if any of the devs see this message, don't take it personally, because they really are among of my favorite game dev teams ever.A lot of of my criticism regards fundamental design choices that I feel could've been better implemented, but they don't hinder the experience. I know it's a small indie team and they still delivered a fantastic game.It's great to see Mimimi continuing to give us amazing titles and further experiment with the Stealth RTS genre. I really hope this game sells well and get more content, much like  had Aiko's Choice and  had the Baron Missions.Edit: with Mimimi closing its doors after this game I find unlikely we'll ever get a DLC, though they did promise a huge content patch in the future, so fingers crossed.Edit 2: well, we did get DLC after all! Two, in fact. Nice to see we got it before they closed the doors.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit is a nostalgic return to the golden era of stealth strategy games like Desperados and Commandos. It captures the essence of those classics while adding its own magical twist.From the moment you embark on your pirate ship, you’re immersed in a world of magic and meticulous planning. The beautifully crafted environments and cleverly designed challenges demand strategic prowess. Each character, with unique abilities, adds depth to your tactics, making teamwork essential and immensely satisfying.The gameplay blends planning and execution seamlessly. You’ll find yourself pausing to plot the perfect sequence, then holding your breath as you watch it unfold flawlessly. The addition of supernatural elements keeps the game fresh and exciting, offering creative problem-solving opportunities.The narrative, rich with rebellion and redemption, is brought to life by excellent voice acting and captivating plot twists. Shadow Gambit’s story hooks you from start to finish.In summary, Shadow Gambit is a triumphant return to the stealth strategy genre. It’s perfect for fans of Desperados and Commandos, offering a well-crafted, modern adventure. Gather your crew, hoist the sails, and embark on this challenging and fun journey.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Shadow Tactics enjoyed it very much, then I played Desperado III, which I too enjoyed very much, and now I have played the last and final game the Shadow Gambit, which I also enjoyed very much. Quite sad that this is the last and final game, as I like how they make stealth games. It's quite unique and there aren't many games like it on the market, so very sad to lose such a huge developer for this genre. The overall story and little character stories, as well as the captain quests, were charming. Nothing really mind breaking, but it was definitely enjoyable. This is also the best game for completionist, as you have the most freedom and quite a lot of badges to collect if you want to.If I had to rank all games it would be Desperado III in last, because I found the characters and story to be the most lackluster, apart from the voodoo woman which I absolutely loved. _childDocuments_.review: ufff, where to start with this review...first off, this genre of games really isn't for everyone, and it isnt in fact for me. only 65% of players have finished act 1, 39% act 2 and 23% final act, according to steam achievements, that's really low and dropping massive amount of players between each act. this is due to the reason that once you've played a few hours, you've seen everything the game has to offer and its just a matter of you liking the gameplay enough to play 15/20 more hours of it, or not. i dont think the game is faulty of this, it's just the genre itself that is like this, so beware. also if you've played one of these games before, you've played them all basically.overall the gameplay despite genre limitations was quite nice, with characters having distinct and varied skillsets, and map usually allowing different options to complete objectives. however, enemy variety isnt great. also, the overall UI and keybindings is poor. many times I goofed around my actions because of wrong key inputs. this never happens to me in any other game.the graphics are 10 years old, the presentation is lackluster. at least the OST and the voice acting are serviceable. the story is terrible, unengaging, and doesnt help to push the player forward when the gameplay is already being repetitive. some characters are likable, other fall into the modern trope of unlikable selfish high-horse characters which we see everywhere now. not necessarily woke or anything, just people you wouldnt want as friends. the lore is utterly lacking and the world is poorly introduced. the bad guys just seem like they're actually trying to do good which is purging cursed and undead people, who wouldnt want that? on top of this with the studio closing and devs likely not gonna benefit from sales anymore, I cannot in good faith recommend this game knowing that only a tiny portion of players, even among those reading the reviews for this title, will enjoy it. the genre is THAT specific and niche and this will rebuke the mast majority of people.

_childDocuments_.review: I *want* to like this game, but damn the controls are fickle.  At least 3/4 of my rewinds are due to control issues.  Sometimes, I can press one of the attack keys and target an enemy and it works just fine - dead enemy.  Other times, my pirate runs dumb, fat, and happy right into their detection range and I have to rewind yet again.  And then, if you press pause to assign orders, you have to press <enter> or click the "Execute" button as quick as you can.  Not good if you hit the pause button to mitigate detection or attacking enemies.  And then, there are times when I give orders in the pause screen and cancel it, but I try to give them orders un-paused and it still tries to execute the paused action (usually running).  Pretty much all of this results in detection, usually resulting in rewinding.While I cannot recommend or reject this game (Steam requires a recommendation thumbs up or down; therefore, I have to rate it down because it's not the easiest "yes" I'd give to a game), the best suggestion I can give is to play the demo as far as you can.  If you like it, retry the main game here and skip as fast as you can to try to get beyond the demo and play as much as you can within the 2 hour limit Steam allows for returns.  If you're not outright loving it by then, refund.

Characters with different skills, that are not reskin of Desperado or Shadow tactics. There are more different enemies, some of them are "linked" together and will die only simultaneously for example.Art is something very subjective, so I'll leave it in the middle. And the ship is also just gimmicking, there is really nothing to do there.In terms of story and characters, it compares to Shadow Tactics and Desperados like Star Wars Resistance to Clone Wars or Andor.It doesn’t matter that the game is childish, you can wright engaging pirate stories without violence, take Piratica from Tanith Lee for example. In Shadow Gambit the world building is simply nonexistent, and all the characters lack any depth whatsoever. There is Inquisition and they are stupid and bad, there are cursed pirates, and they are fun and good. Why are they cursed? Who cares, they are good guys! And there is tressure just to move characters forward. "Riddle" in plot is just some lightly stylized gibberish.Characters most of the time tell you how cool and exceptional they are, with some names from the world that have no meaning. For example, some of your crew stole something from MAGICAL ACADEMY. That's all we know. We won't see this ACADEMY in the game, we won’t know anything significant about it, no one else will ever mention it. It is so generic, that If you throw away all "Arrrgh", skulls and other pirate stylization game could be about mediaeval mages, or space rebels.

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I'm surprised at what high praise this game is receiving when it's such a noticeable step down in quality from Mimimi's previous games. The devs kept the core gameplay mostly the same, and it remains fun despite a few criticisms I'll get into later. I'll even say I actually appreciate the direction of making things more gamified with progression systems and adding variety through starting locations and team loadout. However, the game fails *outstandingly* in every single other way. It completely lacks the charm the previous games held, it's riddled with bad decisions and tedious content, and I'm sincerely disappointed. The biggest issue I have is with the painfully dull story and characters. The characters in Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 had depth and dimension to them. They had conflicts, aspirations, emotion, histories, humor, and engaging diverse perspectives. The stories involved revenge, betrayal, redemption, and intrigue. The writing and characters were solid. The characters in Shadow Gambit, on the other hand, are all formulaic, gimmicky, and shallow. They can all be summed up by "ethnicity/accent + 1 trait". This character is a Japanese chef--prepare for dialogue after dialogue, line after line, of him only talking about food, and how "cooking is a battlefield" and yada yada. This one's the Scottish shipwright, have fun with 5 levels of "side quests" involving making soap to clean the ship, what a thrill. Even the "main" character Afia doesn't have anything going for her beyond "I'm a pirate, and I'm here for treasure", which unfortunately reflects the painfully shallow depth the overall story has. You're pirates--get the treasure. Yarr. The "side-content" between missions, if it can even be called that, is a joke. Run to this area and sit through weightless filler dialogue related to your character's one identifying trait. Now run to this person and engage in "banter" that fails to be more amusing than mildly silly and quirky. Repeat ad nauseum. On gameplay, the levels maintain variety through differing starting locations and objectives, but that barely makes up for the samey feeling when they all have the same tropical island aesthetic. Characters are massively unbalanced, which undoes the intent of adding variety as you'll want to bring the OP characters on every mission and ignore the useless ones. And overall, despite playing on the second hardest difficulty, the game just feels... easier. I'm rarely caught in a tricky knot of guards to untie, and the lack of challenge makes it feel less engaging compared to the previous games.TL;DR: The core gameplay is fine, but Shadow Gambit completely fails to capture the charm and draw of the previous games. It feels watered down for children in its writing, gameplay, and style, and fitting to the theme, the game is disappointingly shallow and soulless. If I could rate neutral I would--get it on a 50% off sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played and enjoyed Mimimi games previous installments such as Desperadoes 3 or Shadow Tactics, expect more of the same. The variety of character personalities and their unique playstyles made this one of my favorite tactics games from 2023.  The two character expansions only add to the enjoyment.  And it is a fine send off as Mimimi Games final release.

If you can chose any character for a mission, does not that necessarily mean any character can solve any problem? n short - they feel a bit OP at times.Alarms do not spawn guards. And you are mostly stuck to 3 characters a mission. I would have liked a bit more variety with this.Nonetheless - it is a great game - the most fun I´ve had with any game this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, really good game. But not as good as its predecessors.Desperados in an all-time top3 game for me. D3 was a worthy and equally great sequel. I love Shadow Tactics too.Thankfully Shadow Gambit kept the same solid core gameplay, so all good there.But...I found the difficulty level way off. It's too easy even on the harder levels. Sometimes half of a map or even the whole mission can be finished by using a single character and leaving the rest of the crew behind and catching up with them every now and then.I didn't like the storytelling at all. The setting is fun. But the story is driven forward by some hazy soul magic mumbo jumbo that makes it uninteresting. Nothing against fantasy, but this didn't even try be cohesive within its own world.Playing on the same islands over and over again became quite boring after a while. When you've already solved the _exact same_ situation a few times, and you have to deal with the same situation again, it's just not exciting.Running around on the ship between missions felt like work. Especially the crew tales. These are not funny (they try to be), not entertaining and don't add anything to the game. Please please please less - or better: none - of this in future games.Oh, the open world-yness. And by this I mainly mean the illusion of choice between missions and the 'resource management'. Former is completely meaningless. And latter could have been handled much better IMO. See below.I personally much prefer the more story driven mission design of the previous games.What I liked the most: the captain's challenge missions. These short background stories that all characters got were the most fun in the game. Why not connect the character and ability unlocks to these? It would have been way more rewarding and thematic instead of the boring and unnecessary resource collections stuff.What I still missed from these: seeing how the individual characters become a crew. The previous games were quite good at this, the team members had meaningful discussions and their experience helped them to become a team. Almost none of that is present here.OK, those were a lot of things I didn't like and I have to admit I'm very critical because I like these games a lot and the bar is high. Despite all the above the game is still a lot of fun and highly recommended. I just hope the next games won't have the similar nonsense around the otherwise great gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit is easily one of the best games I played this year.Shadow Gambit is a pirate adventure about a cursed crew looking for the treasure of Captain Mordechai, who, unlike the rest of the main cast of characters, is dead-dead.You play as a woman named Afia, newly cursed with a sword in her chest as big as her heart. You find the Red Marley and revive her crew using black pearls and soul energy you find on your adventures… wait, no, that’s not a good opening. Hold on, let me try that again…Core to the experience of Shadow Gambit is The Red Marley - Captain Mordechai’s ghost ship that serves both as co-protagonist and supernatural battery that powers both the game’s central time travel mechanic and its cast of characters.Shadow Gamit is the rare game that tries a lot of unique things and pulls it all off flawlessly. The way that it perfectly combines gameplay and story is commendable. The world is engrossing, the characters are charming and lovable, the stealth gameplay is enough to make an Alaskan musher proud, and there are so many fun and unique ideas here that I wish I could turn the clock back in real life just so I can experience them for the first time again.It’s a tragedy that Mimimi is closing down, but on the bright side, at least they’re going out on such a high. In a year that has brought a lot of great and big-name video games, I can easily say that Shadow Gambit is (so far, anyway) the best game I’ve played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi does it again!They truly understand what makes this genre so much fun and they deliver another quality entry.If you aren't familiar with them, they made Shadow tactics, a true love letter to the genre. They demonstrated their complete understanding so well that they got their hands on the Desperados IP, a classic, well loved, series for the genre, and knocked it out the park yet again.True, some of the missions are quite a bit easier than previous or other games in the genre. But when you factor in that they're designed to be approached by almost any team from almost any angle, the brilliance really starts to show. Loved every minute and hope there's more to come. Please support these guys, they've truly earned it.If you're on the fence, the demo is quite sizable and should give you more than enough information on if you like this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Bit conflicted about this one.On the one hand, it is still mimimi game, it's decent, quite good. You definitely won't regret playing this game (at least I did not).But, the quality drop - in comparison to their other titles - is significant. In this game, developers seemed to release title with lower PGI rate. Their dark-ish, serious mood from the previous game is non-existent in this one. Feels like they made a game for a much younger audience, with goofy-ish characters, and close to zero character development (found only one companion that actually 'been through' something serious and grew up from her experiences, changing her viewpoint and growing up), the suspension from the previous game is nowhere to be found.Additionally, I remember the previous game as being an actual challenge. Here? half of the characters have built-in body hiding mechanics or stealth. using the environment for success was bastardized - why bother? if you have a character that can quickly kill someone, hide body and himself at the same time, which action also gives him access to 'jump' in a high radius allowing him to emerge in safety far away. In fact, there were maps and missions, which I finished while only using 2 characters, one for distraction other for killing, and again, not as a challenge for myself, but rather simply because other characters were not needed. Summarizing:candy graphics (bad)Silly characters and lore (bad)Great story concept which wasnt used to its fullest (going for child-like narration really) significant step down from game difficulty, undermining what the studio was built onnice "time waster", a good game, but not worth remembering or re-playing.I advise you to get this game on a discounti would give this game 6 or 7 in scale to 10. Bit sad to see devs going this path, but not enough to give the game a bad rating. After this game, I am in mood for some Shadow Tactic.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the mechanically best entry into the series, I do not think there is another game in this genre that is more fun to play. If you're into real time stealth strategy it's very much worth a look. The story doesn't hold up nearly so well, but let's be honest, we don't play these games for the story (Though Shadow Tactics remains a stand out success on this level).The ability to select a landing and departure point to choose your own way through the level is not as freeing as you might hope. A lot of the time this is technically a choice, but it's fairly obvious that a particular start point (or at best one of two) gives you the easiest route to the objective. The exit point tends towards "Whichever exit point I've left the fewest live enemies near to."However the ability to select a crew is incredibly freeing. The crew all have meaningful abilities that make them play very differently to other members. The ghost pirate premise has given the designers a magical excuse to include basically any ability that they think is cool and they've taken advantage of it to offer a wide variety of tricks. There are also some neat synergies, things like your canoness firing your treasure hunter on top of a tower and him then using his fishing rod to pull her and the rest of the crew up to skip an area. It feels great to try all of the different combinations of crew.The upgrade system is pretty bare bones. Each member of the crew has exactly one upgrade, you'll unlock them all in time. It'd have been nice to see it more fleshed out. Particularly as getting upgrades means using characters who you didn't bring on previous misisons, so it could've done a good job of motivating you to use the characters you are less familiar with (or to be honest who are less good, the variety in abilities does mean that some characters do simply feel better to use). On the other hand, maybe "It's more interesting to mix up the crew" is motivation enough.Some reviews have complained about the small number of levels and reuse of islands but I did not really experience the game this way. The islands are vast. You can play a satisfying level and then the replay at the end will show you only visited 1/3 of the map. Most times I revisited an island it was to do a mission on some other part of the same map, so while I was technically on the same island I didn't feel like I was repeating content.Value for money seems to have improved, it took me 33 hours to finish every mission (Maybe 27ish before the credits rolled, you will have some left to do once the main plot is over) which compared to the last title meant I paid less to get more content. I'm on the fence about post-game content, it's largely replaying levels in different ways, but some of the achievements look like they might breathe new life into the levels. I never found "Do it fast" or "Make no mistakes" that interesting, but things like "Do it with one crew member" or "Do it without climbing any ladders" means finding new approaches or new routes to achieve the objectives and sound like they'll be more fun.Long story short: If this is a genre that you enjoy, then this game is a really exciting example.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit might just be the best game Mimimi has made. It takes what works in both Shadow Tactics and Desperados III and evolved it further.- Choosing crew members for your mission helps tailor the game to your playstyle- Choosing landing spots can make a mission even on replay feel at least somewhat different- Upgrading abilities unlocks even more possibilities- Visually even more stunning than their other gamesEasy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike Desperados 3 (D3), which had more linear, sculpted, levels, Shadow Gambit Cursed Crew (SG) goes for more open ended, larger, levels. Also unlike D3, the story of SG is much less serious. D3 was a tale of revenge and a team of thieves and criminals who slowly became friends. SG is a supernatural tale about a ragtag group of pirates who try to take down an inquisition in the caribbean. It a (much less serious) story of a group of rebels. I do prefer D3, in both levels and story (and most characters), but I personally prefer the gameplay in SG.This is because SG lets you *choose* your teams. The key gameplay element is mixing up your team and figuring out what does and does not work. In D3 sometimes you'd get to control all of the characters and utilise their abilities together, but sometimes you'd be pigeonholed into only controlling 2-3 characters per level. I want to stress, it was *different* not worse. The levels would be tailored for each team you'd control and MiMiMi really knocked it out of the park with the level design and story. But in SG, picking and choosing your team is just so much damn fun. Pairing a ninja with a dude who can throw his golden skull, a Scottish pirate with an anchor strapped to his back with a woman who carries a giant canon, a crotchety old sniper with a plant lady, etc, etc. The levels are open ended but they have tons of replayability.  it took me almost 50 hours before I felt any kind of boredom.My verdict: 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was impressed by the demo that it was an instant buy for me. I liked the writing, the characters, the visuals, the voiced dialogues, and the QoL updates to the top-down stealth genre. However, I think the devs were trying too hard when it comes to increasing the game's mass appeal to the detriment of the game's difficulty. Sure, you have lots of characters to choose from but you'll eventually gravitate to a few that the others feel like.. bloat to the roster. Lots of islands to visit, but the same enemies. I did so many go to X and do Y and go back to Z kind of missions that it's all a blur to me.What I'm trying to say is that the game feels padded and is lacking in meaningful content. By the time I got access to the sniper and spy plus their upgraded abilities, let's say I've seen everything underneath this game's skirt so it no longer garnered my respect and I just went Sniper Elite.I just finished Act 3 and saw the credits roll so I think I'm done. Will not play again.TLDR: Very good production, bloated game.

It was a blast.The characters are amaizing, the way you can tackle each and every level is so much fun and variety!I am so sad the game is over and Team Mimimi (the Devs) is no more.Its the biggest "YES BUY AND PLAY IT" u will ever hear from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: After loving Mimimi's previous games Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, Im sorry to say that Shadow Gambit is a disappointment. Maps are beautiful to look at, but their new open layout harms level design and simplifies the puzzle of enemy encounters, many of which I could simply charge straight in and melee everyone(yes on hard difficulty). That would very rarely work in previous games. I enjoyed some new gameplay features like Pinkus possession, Gaëlle's and Quentin's transport abilities. Though for example having 3 characters with samey teleport-attacks feels uninspired. I believe the new characters' lack of specialization compared to previous games adds to the simplified nature of the new level design. Since Im now mostly free to pick any characters for a mission, the mission cant be designed in any way that requires specialized skills to be used in any areas. Ive seen people write that this game is big, but I disagree. Main missions using each map 3-4 times isnt big, its tedious. Clearing an area I just cleared, to do yet another fetch quest does not make me feel in awe of a sprawling game world. I still played them all, hoping story and dialogue would make up for it... I'd say most of the characters' entire stories and character growths are so miniscule they can be summed up in 1 or 2 sentences per character. If you, like me, loved the more emotional moments of for example Mugen's "fate" and how characters used to slowly grow from distant strangers into close friends, you will have little to none of that here. Most of the dialogue is bland jokes and memery. Suleidy and Gaëlle show some potential of character depth, but its largely left untapped. I'd say Shadow Gambit has gone for quantity over quality in every way possible. And I for one dislike this development, even though I seem to be in a tiny minority. Often if I dont like a game, I dont get upset, I simply think that game wasnt for me. But this is a Mimimi game. And Shadow Tactics is one of my favorite games ever, so I feel like that doesnt apply in this case. This is my first review ever. Thats how disappointed I am. I hope Mimimi and players resonate with anything Ive written here, and with the very few other critical reviews Ive seen, and that Mimimi's next title will be better. Or maybe I should just go back to Shadow Tactics and give it the praise I should've given it long ago.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Even with the repetition, Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a great stealth experience and a must play for fans of previous games from Mimimi. With a tonal shift to pirates and cool supernatural abilities, the basic strategy gameplay from their previous titles is revitalized. Sneaking through patrols and pulling off flawless plans is addicting. The sentient ship, with its ability to store memories, becomes a central part of the narrative in a smart way. Crew tales and special character missions expose quirky personalities, even if some tasks are not engaging. If Mimimi find a way to lessen the tedium of revisiting levels, then the framework of The Cursed Crew should be used in future endeavors, wherever the currents take them next.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi Games' swan song and probably greatest game of it's genre.Shadow Gambit perfected the formula Commandos started more than two decades ago, and deserves all the accolades it got. It is the best starting point for the genre, and while it is slightly easy for veterans the openess of the scenarios and new abilities of the npc's more that make for it. Huge recommendation for anyone interested in the genre, it will be a long time before it is surpassed.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I don't tend to pay full price for games, but I made the exception here. I have enjoyed Mimimi games since Shadow Tactics and their recent closure has been deeply saddening. _childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow gambit is truly something unique. It´s sad to see the developer stopped making games after this one , but they went out with a banger of a game. It feels more than just a puzzle game and a strategy game combined. _childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: An expertly-designed stealth-tactics game. The gameplay is thoughtful and creative, the cast of playable characters have really fun powers and likeable/memorable personalities, and the story has its fair share of surprising twists. All of this is wrapped up in highly polished presentation with lots of little neat details and extra touches that certainly didn't have to be there, but are, and the game punches well above its weight for it. Between Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, Desperados III, and now Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew, Mimimi Games have cemented themselves firmly as the masters of the genre, delivering undoubtedly the three finest 'Commandos-like' real-time stealth tactics games ever made. This is sadly their swan song, but what a hell of a way to go out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Another great talented studio is killed by the apathy of the masses. So many releases right now are souls clones or at least they use the same color palette & press "E" to pet or press "E" to drink. The Stealth RTS genre is a gem for the mind, it's like having to figure out a moving puzzle, this is the apex of all MIMIMI GAMES + although i prefer the setting of shadow tactics - shogun ancient japan, Shadow Gambit takes inspiration from Sinbad & the legend of seven seas + Treasure Planet --> but trust me the story is much more mature, but hey like the great art of animation between 1995-2005 (Atlantis, Titan A.E., etc.), an era that was ignored until PIXAR came along and ruined everything, the same will happen with Shadow Gambit &  all games that don't have DLC & hyperactive gameplay. I recommend this game from the bottom of my heart, you will feel challenged & enjoy a great story & great stealth gameplay.

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Well put together, engaging, and fun--though not without it's drawbacks. The gameplay, mechanics, voice acting, level of challenge, and art direction are excellent. Discover fun synergies between characters, your favorite groups, and gives you an incentive to change things up to get bonuses. It is however lacking in its engaging and diversity in storytelling. Every narrative progression consists of "go to this place on this small ship, talk to this person or interact with this thing. Got very bored of the crew stories. _childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to see the current state of "Mixed" reviews for this game. If you've played Shadow Tactics Blade of the Shogun or Desparados III you definitely know what you're getting into. If you haven't played those games and you're reading this, you've found a great place to be introduced to this style of game. This Cursed Crew is far more inviting to you and will be easier to get into the game. You'll understand how these games are played and develop good quick saving habits. For you more experienced players don't fret, you'll find more of what you love except...The powers are far more creative and fun to use than this games predecessors. Not only that but the game is designed in such a way that it encourages variance in your crew composition. Instead of bringing the same set of characters or having the game decide what characters you use. Not only that, but you will for the most part decide what order you get your crew becomes available. If you want lore and fluff, the game will allow you to interact with it, but for the most part you can stick to the core gameplay and not interact with it much at all. Without going on too long. If stealth tactics are what you're looking for, give this game a go. It's a great example of the genre and, to me at least, a very fun one too.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game because it told me it was similar to the Divinity series. The only thing similar to Divinity is the fact that it's a top down game and you click to move.I would say it's more similar to a Hitman style game. _childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit proves to be yet another great tactical stealth game made by Mimimi, who are one of the best stealth game devs in the business. It also proves, unfortunately, to be an excellent swan song for Mimimi as they announced that they would be closing after support ends for the game in the coming months. (Just the day after I beat the game early this week too) It truly is a shame because as I said they’re among the best in the business of the genre and really are like the only ones that do the isometric style stealth tactics ala Commandos. The silver lining least is that this was on their own terms and hopefully they can move on to achieve better work/life balance.Anyway I do think that among their games, which also include Shadow Tactics and Desperadoes 3, Shadow Gambit is the best one. It definitely feels like an even more polished refinement like Desperadoes 3 was to Shadow Tactics. There are some differences, one of the major ones being is that the game is more freeform. Shadow Tactics and Desperadoes were more like puzzles to solve, observing enemy visions cones, and figuring out openings to take them out with your character skills. Usually in those games there was more a rigid order you had to approach them in, especially because the game picked the characters for a level for you. Shadow Gambit eventually chooses to let you choose any crew member you want on missions and they have all wildly different powers. Shadow Tactics and Desperadoes were mostly grounded aside from Isabelle’s voodoo ability to kill two enemies at once. In contrast, as the title implies, the crew in Shadow Gambit are all undead pirates and they all have more fantastical abilities. Because the cast have more wacky powers and the game lets you choose your crew roster, the game is easier in a sense, but it does give you more freedom to play how you want. You can also choose which missions you want to complete first, unlike the previous two games which were completely linear. In Shadow Gambit you revisit each island to complete different missions, but they have it where a mission will just take you to certain area of the island, while another takes you to a different part so it keeps it fresh enough. I think the tradeoff of the gameplay is ultimately worth it because the supernatural powers are fun and they really take the abilities from previous games into fun directions.The writing is actually rather good too, like the characters initially seem rather one note but the last half of the game is essentially doing each character’s personal sidequests and they all do mostly a nice job fleshing them out. The setting is a neat one; funny enough it’s actually a bit annoying to me because the game legit has good lore tidbits that are teased at and drip-fed at you throughout the game but they never delve into them too much. I’d actually would have liked more exploration of them, but that’s less of a con and more that they did a good enough job where I was interested to want to see more. Teresa’s sidequest especially has some real neat lore and character stuff with ramifications that explain the entire villain faction of the game that’s just kind of mentioned in passing.Overall Shadow Gambit is a fantastic game and of my favorites of the year. I wish Mimimi was able to keep improving on their formula, but they should be proud they went out on such a high note.

_childDocuments_.review: I've finally beaten the 100% out of this game, but my general opinion about Shadow Gambit formed way long before that. To me personally this was the least enjoyable experience of all Mimimi games. While trying some pinpoint tweaks to the Commandos formula in Desperados III, here, in Shadow Gambit, they practically went to a full-scale bonanza. Here are few examples:- Instead of a linear engaging story, we have fragments consisting of main and secondary missions that can be played in mixed order based on the player's choice.- There is a set of 10 maps (8 main ones, 1 starting one and 1 endgame one with the final mission only) that are played repeatedly under different circumstances like day / night, enemy setup, etc. But the map layout always stays the same at each location. Some maps can have up to 5 different missions.- Instead of 5 distinctive appealing characters we have 8 (+1 secret) crewmembers with sometimes similar abilities. And those abilities that are unique, are often insanely overpowered and include but are not limited to full-scale teleportation, hiding bodies in plain sight or even hiding crewmembers (!) in plain sight at any given location.- There is no classic save system, therefore you can't load a save from the already completed mission, ever. In combination with unpolished badges mechanics this makes earning those a real pain sometimes.I couldn't stop thinking that the developers drew some inspiration from Partisans 1941 game, which I reviewed as a potentially subpar experience to Mimimi games in the first place… TL;DR. This is still quite a solid game, especially true if you haven't played Shadow Tactics or Desperados III before. So definitely a recommend here, but a hesitant one. I personally didn't enjoy the twisting of the classic formula THAT much. As if quality needed to be turned into quantity and the target audience needed to be switched to more casual oriented players. Also, the voiceover immersion is completely destroyed with almost every single (!) crewmember and other main characters voice actors doing the lines for various enemy units. As for the details, first and foremost I'd like mention that I sort of picked this game as a gift from my other, well knowing that the game has been released only recently. Making a pre-order or buying a game right after it becomes available is something I never do, because for quite some time now the developers are often “veeeryy sooory” for what they release instead of a game. On the other hand, something like once in 6-8 months I still tend to try a fresh release, mostly to see whether my approach is still valid. And unfortunately, the more time passes by, the more solid my point of view becomes - if one would like the developers' attitude to change, one should stop pre-ordering things and only buy games a year or even more after the initial release. Until that people making important decisions will have no motivation to stop feeding one with raw and unfinished ♥♥♥♥ secured in a shiny marketing cover. Shadow Gambit is clearly not such case, but it has certain issues which may or may not be addressed later, so, perhaps if I’d pick up this game in 2024 or even 2025, my review would have more positive things to say.As I’ve briefly mentioned, I was unpleasantly surprised by how many similarities I noticed with concepts introduced in Partisans 1941 (P1941 for short). Just as in P1941, the number of playable characters has been significantly increased, and just as in P1941, the quality of these characters was somewhat sacrificed in the process. Frankly, I wasn’t able to see a reason for having so many characters or any advantage in their numbers other than artificially boosting the game length. Just as in P1941 some of the characters have very similar working skills between each other and just as in P1941 you can’t take more than 3 crewmembers on a single mission at once (with an exception of several plot missions). On a side note, I found Pinkus to be such an extremely annoying and dislikable character that I even skipped his mirror missions while going for 100% achievements.Just as in P1941, there is no linear and engaging story, because just as in P1941 there is now a central hub (bonfire camp in P1941, ship in Shadow Gambit), where you can do some talking in-between opening a map and choosing a region as well as main or secondary mission to play. The skill tree concept from P1941 also seemed to have a certain influence, but thankfully a very brief one – each crewmember’s unique ability can now be upgraded once, and the upgraded ability in most cases is added as a new one (it can be used separately from the basic version). Well, at least they didn’t introduce a P1941 looter shooter system in Shadow Gambit, phew. And that should conclude the comparison thoughts.The whole game save system has now been tightly incorporated into the game lore, and in fact, I found this overall ship memories (save files) thingie quite interesting. How about a game force-loading your save because the plot dictates so? Sounds actually cool. But from a practical point of view, this system is far from being perfect. For instance, saves work only for a current mission, so after you’ve completed or abandoned it, everything is completely gone, poof. You can’t make a load to check why on the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Earth you haven’t been awarded the “kill everyone” badge after spending 2 hours on it; the badge simply didn’t appear in the results screen, and nothing you can do about it. Also, you can’t control which saves to overwrite, nor can you name or differentiate those. They simply stack one after another and at a certain moment new ones begin automatically erasing the most old ones. This can be a pain in especially big and / or difficult missions. And finally, the saving and loading process itself is taking a good couple of seconds; in such games where this procedure can happen more than 100 times per mission, it means that you can spend as much as 3-5 full minutes in total saving and loading only. A couple of random matters that got caught in my memory.In-game character art is either lazy or… I don’t know. It looks like the art team was working separately from the 3D team, because they clearly mix-up crewmembers' looks. Try looking for differences in a 3D model and art for yourself: which  is in skeletal form and which is normal or which  is a hook and which is normal.Controls are very clunky when a crewmember is carrying a body – it’s difficult to move around, because the cursor is automatically proposing the body drop locations instead of just letting me move and changing the cursor only when I’m holding CTRL.The voiceover… my God… Don’t get me wrong, OMUK studio team did an outstanding job in all four Mimimi Games, the roles and the voices were a 101% match for the characters every single time, and the actors did an awesome job as well. But accepting Mark’s offer (I personally heard this offer at least once) to use the same voice actors for miscellaneous character lines in order to make the voiceover a bit cheaper is, in my personal opinion, a complete disaster. This already showed in Desperados III, but it had fewer main characters and their voices weren’t THAT much unusual, so hearing them from random citizens wasn’t that often. But in Shadow Gambit, where we have Afia with a very strong African accent or John with a very strong Scottish accent, I don’t understand how you could ask these voice actors to provide a voiceover for a Kindred or a Prognosticar and expect not to hear that it’s the same person!! Again, the voice actors match their respective main characters perfectly, the way they speak and their tone is top notch. But hearing the very same voices from a random enemy destroys any attempts of immersion.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. If you liked Shadow Tactics or Desperados III, you'll also like this. Oh, and from a privacy perspective: the game lets you disable tracking right from the start (Looking at you, other games where disabling tracking also quits the game!). So, I'd give this game , and say it's worth the full asking price, if you like the genre. If you're curious about this kind of games, you can choose to lower the difficulty a lot. The game is very friendly about saving and loading.The mechanics are just as fun as in Desperados III, and perhaps even more fun. Since they're doing a magical setting, this affords Mimimi more latitude with abilities. Instead of throwing a ninja star, or a knife, why not teleport yourself forward and plunge your cutlass in the enemy's chest? I liked Isabelle Moreau's (the voodoo lady) abilities best in Desperados III, and I feel Shadow Gambit takes those further. You also have more characters, and you can choose in which order you unlock them, and when to upgrade their abilities. In general, we get massively expanded gameplay which works well with the setting, and it's fundamentally... fun.The difficulty system is more customisable, including choosing easier or harder enemy placements. At max difficulty, I feel it's roughly as difficult as Desperados III on max.Undead voodoo pirates (and there's a ninja, too). Way wackier than Mimimi's previous games - which, aside for a few jokes here and there, were downright somber - but it works for me.  I am having fun, both from the gameplay part of things, and from the story. You have a skeletal monkey you feed bananas and pet, what more would you like - a three-headed skeletal monkey?Quicksaving now has a full-screen effects that kinda interrupts my gameflow for half a second. And I feel it takes longer than it took in Desperados III. Nothing major.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you, Mimimi Games, for revitalizing the Commandos-like genre! Your three solid games have provided us with countless hours of joy. I look forward to any future endeavors from your studio, though I acknowledge that my review might be slightly biased, given that it comes shortly after your studio's termination announcement.This game is the epitome of a mixed experience. While some aspects left me disappointed, it also managed to keep me entertained for a substantial amount of time.In contrast to their previous two games, the developers opted for a high degree of freedom in this one. However, I believe this freedom was taken to an extreme. While the idea of choosing entry and exit points, as well as characters for each mission, sounds promising, it results in much easier levels compared to the previous two games, regardless of the chosen difficulty. I appreciate the studio's intention to provide players with a sense of freedom, but I believe that making just rare, well-considered decision-making moments would be enough to enhance the overall experience while preserving the original feel of the game. Although it's enjoyable to select which character to revive first, the freedom to continually choose reviving characters can negatively impact mission design. Moreover, there is little incentive to choose different characters, aside from the rest bonus, as the enemies in each map remain the same. Consequently, we often end up selecting their preferred characters without considering the mission's requirements.The addition of mission stories was also disappointing. While the studio aimed to enhance the storytelling aspect, these segments lack any gameplay involvement and feature overly simplistic, didactic stories that do not engage the player. Allowing players to make choices within the stories could have made them more entertaining. Reading cliché stories presented as visual novels with shallow characters and dull narratives is not enjoyable. While I personally did not love the stories in Shadow Tactics and Desperados III, I found them more engaging than those in this game.Another disappointment was the uniformity of the mission design. Nearly all the levels are strikingly similar, with only minor adjustments and texture variations. While the pirate theme is understandable, it does not necessitate that all maps must resemble the same island. The missions could have taken place in diverse environments, such as a large ship or other exciting settings, as seen in Desperados III. Despite its cowboy theme, that game managed to create levels with distinct feels.I did not anticipate sharing so many negative points in this review. To end on a positive note, one of my biggest complaints about Shadow Tactics and Desperados III was the similarity in characters' skills with minor variations. In this game, they introduced a variety of unique abilities, approximately 20 in total, that can be combined with each other. Although some abilities may be overpowered, I find this diversity of skills to be a shining aspect of the game, and it compensates for my reservations about other aspects.This has turned out to be my longest review ever, but as they say, the more you love something, the more critical you can be. In any case, thank you once again, Mimimi Games. You will not be forgotten! Shiver me timbers!

_childDocuments_.review: Has the strong tactical gameplay and varied characters similar to Mimimi's previous games, with a new bafflingly terrible mission structure that starts to make the game a chore to complete.Shadow Gambit takes the gameplay of Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 to a new setting, this one focused on undead/cursed pirates fighting against a tyrannical order that is trying to destroy them and control the citizens of various islands. As a pirate looking to make a name for herself you free a captured sentient ship from the inquisition with the hope of finding the former Captain's hidden treasure. To do that you have to join forces with the ship, who has the ability to record events and move time back to those former spots, and revive her former crew in order to follow the clues left by the Captain.In the base game there is a total of eight playable characters with an extra unlockable one if you reach 80% completion by doing different stage and character challenges. Each character has a slow or fast kill/knockout attack with their weapon of choice, a pistol that has one shot per map unless you find ammo, and usually two other abilities with often one of them changing to something else under certain conditions or when something else is in use. One of the more unique characters has the ability to possess other enemies and can then move them within a certain range of where he took over their bodies and he might gain some of their abilities, one character can grow a bush almost anywhere on the map to hide characters or enemy bodies, one has a cannon she can use to launch allies to distant places or that can be used to attack enemies, many characters have a item or animal partner that allows them to distract or lure enemies to a location. The crews various skills can pair together in useful ways and can allow you to handle locations in different ways. The characters are also likable and have their personalities brought out by their banter during gameplay, having some unique dialogue based on who is chosen to go on certain missions, story elements on your ship in between missions, and in the later game a mission or series of missions that focuses on some part of a character's backstory.You play against the usual types of enemies the the genre has become known for having. You have the generic grunts that are easy to fool with distractions and traps, sentries that won't move or be distracted long from their set locations and line of sight, one that activates an alarm to summon reinforcements, a sniper with a longer and more quick to activate line of sight, a stronger types that requires multiple characters to take down, and in a new more setting unique enemy a pair of two enemies that need to be killed quickly before one revives the other. You have the helpful time stopping planning button found in their previous games that allows you to chain multiple actions together and the always nice to have fast forward button that Desperados 3 had so you aren't needlessly waiting around for enemies to get into certain positions or for alarms and alerts to end.In this genre Shadow Gambit would be of the same excellent quality of the developers previous games, if not for suffering from one area that those previous games didn't struggle with.The game unfortunately becomes something of a chore to finish, even more so with the DLC, due to the constant need to replay the same locations with little changes 3-5+ times. Even with the ability to bring a different set of crew members and to start and finish in different locations the repeated visits to the same maps is easily the worst part of this game. It's so bad you might get into a situation where you have to go to the same map 3+ times in a row. In Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 a map was designed for the mission and characters it was made for (Desperados 3 eventually giving modes where you could try different characters), the maps here are made to play for multiple missions where almost nothing changes except for the minor mission objective targets or the time of day (a much bigger change than just about anything the objectives will do). Many of the missions will focus on you really only needing to complete your objectives around a portion of the total location with you being able to pick from a few starting locations and exit locations once your tasks are complete. The problem with the approach is that it leads to some very short uninteresting missions in the worst times, but there is also the problem that they didn't necessarily spread out how those missions tend to limit themselves. You might play a mission that focus on a third of the map, only to find your next mission focuses on pretty much the same area of the map, then to find you have another mission on the island that now deals with 2/3s or the entire map that again will have you dealing with that same 1/3 all with the same enemy groupings and locations. There being a lot more playable characters and being able to take the 1-3 you want to each time does help to alleviate some of this problem, but it still ends up getting dull as you end up playing a lot more total missions than in Minimi's previous games, less interesting missions, much less challenging missions, and the types of enemies you are facing doesn't really expand as the game goes on.The challenge badges for each map and crew member are a lazily handled mess where it is needlessly difficult to check your progress or what you have done on the revealed badges, the logbook is a mess that you can't even access for some reason while on the mission planning screen, some badges just don't seem to want to unlock when you complete them, and the challenges aren't all revealed until you complete the game. Because you really want to go back to that one map you just played six times, however many more times to try to hit a ridiculously high 80% badge completion rate to unlock a hidden character so you can play the same maps some more times with them.Both sets of DLC adds a new character, giving you total of 11 playable characters with the additional unlockable one, one new location that will have three missions on it and three new missions on the older locations. The characters are both fun to use but the new islands tend to only have one mission on them that is actually interesting and the other three missions mean you will be going back to areas you've already played even more than you have to in the base game. If you are really playing the game a lot and see yourself frequently replaying missions or just really like having the varied characters then they are going to be worth getting just for that.Screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: This is not only Mimimi Games' crown jewel, it is a genre-defining title -- the amount of polish and robust mechanics in Shadow Gambit raise the bar to unrealistic levels for the real-time stealth tactics genre. While some of the voice acting isn't the best, the characters are enjoyable and the story is interesting. Having said this, literally everything else is second to none. The only game that comes close in the same genre would be Desperados 3 (less polish feeling than Shadow Gambit, but the characters, voice acting, and story in Desperados 3 makes me want to replay it over and over again).If you are even slightly interested in the real-time stealth tactics genre, you cannot go wrong with anything from Mimimi Games. The worst thing about Shadow Gambit is the fact it's Mimimi Games' final title -- they began as a kickstarter with Shadow Tactics and ended by leaving fans with the best games the genre has seen. They will be missed, but not forgotten.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Mimimi's previous stealth action/real-time strategy games (Shadow Tactics and Desperados III), then you are going to love the latest game coming from the masters of this genre. While I initially wasn't too sure about the supernatural pirates setting this game takes place in, after only a few hours of playing, I was definitely hooked. The game's missions play out across numerous islands/locations and have been beautifully created, The story is quite funny with a sense of humor that driving the plot forward. Each character's backstory and the voice acting associated with each, is superbly done. And of course, the brutal difficulty and the insane amount of quick saving that Mimimi and this genre is known for, is most definitely in abundance with this game. Believe me, even the most well thought-out plan will go belly-up on numerous occasions and you will be glad that you spent those extra few seconds saving you game. If you enjoyed Mimimi's previous stealth-action games and want something with an amazing story with unforgettable characters, to go along with the difficult challenges you will encounter, then do yourself a favor and purchase this game!UPDATE: After playing this game a few more hours, my review still stands that this is an unbelievably fun game. On December 6, 2023, Mimimi will be releasing DLC for the game, which is exciting but also sad since this is the very last content, outside of patches, to be released from the developer before they close shop. Godspeed Mimimi! You made unbelievable fun games and you will be sorely missed!

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: this game is absolutely fantastic. the story is intriguing from start to end, every character is memorable and lovable (with stellar voice acting performances from everyone), the art direction and designs of both the environments and the characters (enemies included) are outstanding. the combat is tight, each mechanic feels purposeful and integral to enjoying it to its fullest. the "memory" mechanic tied to quick save was a delight, in particular. and i'm always a sucker for combat puzzles; love picking at a problem until it all falls into place. it's rare, i find, to play a game with an array of characters where each of them feels like they NEED to be there, but i regularly started missions and thought 'dang, wish i had x with me' and it didn't really matter which characters i took, someone else would always have a skill that would've made some sort of encounter easier. (yes, i unlocked virgilio, the guy who can be any character, which is a cool gimmick, and i enjoy having him for the treasure hunts and badge cleanup, but prior to that.) there is a pretty robust post-game too, and even though it's mostly just replaying previous missions, there's something so lovely about seeing how much better i've gotten at using each crewmate or taking a different combination to try out some fun shenanigans. i was initially on the fence about the dlc, also, but truly those two characters are outstanding and well worth it.i bumped into a few bugs and crashes while i was playing, but they were mostly things where the game very clearly did not expect me to try something and it freaked out about it. like trying to possess someone as they entered a door, or manipulating the alarm system to snipe half a map's worth of enemies using a panicked pinkus to scramble around picking up the bolt. (he was way more useful than some reviews had led me to believe, definitely a favourite for me). some of the badges (the game's system for tracking progress) also wig out on occasion: i got a couple even though i had not done the things the badge required, or i didn't get ones when i did do the thing (the badge for landing at clam beach on calamity reef, for instance, REFUSES to pop for me). other than that, the game ran flawlessly.it's truly a shame the studio shut down because this game is a masterpiece, my pocket pick for 2023 game of the year. i wish the absolute best for all the devs in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: The good: the graphics are pretty, almost all the mechanics are new (compared to Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics) and there are some UI improvements.  The character accents are fun, if a bit random.  I'm not sure why a Japanese pirate is in the Caribbean or why the German has a posh English accent.  I'm guessing Sweet Baby Inc had a hand in that, and the 50/50 pirate gender split...The bad: the characters are overpowered (working together is rarely required) and the punishment for setting off alarms (more guards) is gone - its too easy.  The music is far too repetitive and a step down from previous games.  All the side quests / dialogue make you redo maps, without forcing significant changes to the tactics used (unlike the achievements in previous games).  Multiple landing places don't seem to have a purpose and killing the custodes seems to have no real purpose.  The upgrade system is unclear and makes characters even more OP - seems like a copycat feature from another game genre.This seems like a "my first commando" game.  It makes it onto the "recommended" list and it tried hard, but the previous games were significantly better balanced, had much better story-telling, general execution and re-playability.

_childDocuments_.review: The abilities of each character offer a great deal of diversity to how you approach a mission. Do you want to go lethal? Sneaky? What about setting traps? Luring enemies to you? Sending them away from you? You can do any of those, and you can mix it up in each mission. For example:You can use Afia to time stop an enemy for 5.5 seconds, then lunge to another enemy and take them out. While Pinkus runs up to the time stopped enemy to possess them. Simultaneously you can have John dive underground, throwing Sir Reginald at another enemy to turn them away so they don't see what you're doing and appear under another enemy to instantly take them out and hide their body.This might sound like a lot, but luckily you can pause the game and give each character a single command, then execute the commands at the push of a button. What if you want a more direct approach?Use Toya to drop a paper doll trap at a location, then play his flute to draw enemies to the location that you are planning to ambush. Lets say 3 enemies come, and all you have in the area is Toya and Afia - Perhaps John is feeding Sir Reginald, who knows - They walk toward the sound, you time stop one enemy with Afia, teleport to the third and take him out, then use Toya to recall to his Paper Doll, taking out enemies standing in the inner ring, and then use either of them to finish off the time stopped enemy.The point is, each character has 2-3 skills that you can use and because of how they're designed can be used in many different ways. The characters are odd, but not annoyingly so, and their personal tales are entertaining.Edit: Now after doubling my time played when my initial review posted, I'm going to add that all of the characters bring something unique. I have seen some reviews saying that since some characters have similar abilities (John can distract, Gaelle can distract, Pinky can distract) that they feel uninspired. But I would argue it opens the door to additional playstyles. In my last mission I used all three of the above and the thing you have to keep in mind is that the distractions only last a few seconds, so while you can have a guard turn around for a few seconds, that isn't some grand amount of time - But having two characters that can cover one performing a stealthy assassination is.In one situation I was essentially in a box, with a strong enemy patrolling, I wanted to clear the room of the smaller guys first, but each of the 4 corners of this square room had a guard and they were staring at one another, while the big guard patrolled to each corner. So, I had John go underground, preparing to stealth kill through a wall, using Gaelle to launch Pinky onto a wall, she threw her firecracker over the wall to distract a guard away, John teleported to the intended target and while the animation was finishing the distraction began wearing off - Enter Pinky's distraction to keep the 2nd guard turned for a longer span of time, allowing John's assassination animation to end and hide himself underground without triggering an alarm.Is all of this necessary? No. I could very well have shot the other guard, but that would have resulted in an alarm triggering, and time spent hiding. So my method, while involving more planning, saved a 30 second alarm timer and allowed me to play stealthy - As I wanted.Alternatively, I could have had Pinky assassinate the second guard, while Gaelle distracted a third from another corner as it would have seen the assassination attempt. Then I could have used John's upgrade to pull Pinky and himself underground to hide, though Pinky likely would have taken a hit in this example, unless I threw Pinky's distract at the third guard (assuming it would have been in range) then assassinate, and Gaelle distract the third while the two assassins hid the bodies.Of course, had I brought Suleidy I could have tossed a bush between John and the second guard, preventing the need for distractions in the first place, which only works if you're trying to distract from a single direction - Not usually the case.My point is, all of the skills can be used to play the game so many different ways. I haven't played Mimimi's previous titles, though I believe I own Shadow Tactics through Epic's free giveaways, so I may have to try it out sometime after this one. The game is a lot of fun, and due to all of the different strategies you can employ for each situation it can be a great deal of fun. Even some characters that I didn't expect to be strong are outstanding with the right plan.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: There's nothing quite as satisfying as picking off a weak link or two in the enemy's defenses and watching the rest fall like a row of dominoes. Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a hugely satisfying game with beautiful level design, puzzles around every corner, and a ton of creative character abilities to play with. My one complaint is that the character stories in between each mission are just point-and-click affairs with no real depth, but they're optional anyway. If you're a stealth-based tactics fan or you think you could be, this game is well worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game. I love Desperados III and thought that it was the pinnacle of the genre, but this really set a new bar.More playable characters, upgrades to unlock, the ability to choose the party load outs for (almost) every mission, great maps, crazy fun powers, and side adventures with fantastic characters that have fantastic voice actors. Not to mention a great narrative tying it all together that is well paced, well written, and even surprisingly moving at times (the way that they integrated save scumming into the story was brilliant as well). All of this packed into game that stays true to what made their previous titles so fun and rewarding to play through.I'm looking forward to taking on any DLC that may be in the works along with all of the challenges as I work my way up to unlocking the final playable character (who looks like a ton of fun). It makes me really sad that Mimimi Games is shutting down despite developing 3 of the best real time strategy stealth titles of all time. Truly an incredibly talented and passionate group of people that I hope go off to do more amazing things in the industry.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi's grand finale is a triumphant romp through the genre they single-handedly revived (RTS Stealth) with Shadow Tactics in 2016. The eponymous crew is a wacky and dramatic bunch, each painstakingly balanced to thwart tricky stealth challenges.Up front, Gambit suffers a few flaws compared to Shadow Tactics or Mimimi's other game, Desperados III:- Because you get to choose crews to take on missions, there are no puzzles crafted specifically for particular characters' abilities.- Because you need to be able to win with any combination of characters, difficulty has been toned down.- Because the cast is so big and each member is basically optional, none of them (save protagonist Afia) feel particularly integral to the story.That said, Mimimi's level design is as sharp as ever, controls are tight and fluid, and characters' abilities are all fun and flavorful. Mimimi's "instant reload" mechanic is, delightfully, integrated into the plot as an in-universe power. Instant classic that I plan to come back to many times over the years.As a side note, getting to see Yuki again in the DLC was a real treat! I heard her voice actress speak and got chills flashing back to Shadow Tactics! Thanks, Devs!
