_childDocuments_.review: When Mimimi announced their next title to take place in a “pirate fantasy setting”, I admittedly wasn´t too pleased at first. For me, “Desperados 3” was my personal GOTY 2020, I just couldn´t believe that a small German studio was able to deliver such high quality standards (perfect gameplay, no bugs, very good performance, good story -> perfect game) in a time when the AAA industry just seems to release failure after failure. Same goes for “Shadow Tactics”, I really adore this game since it helped to revive the genre. Having now played through all the main missions (defeated the final boss), I can say that “Shadow Gambit” couldn´t meet my expectations. It´s not even close to Desperados III or Shadow Tactics. There are so many things that I didn´t like about it: Let´s start with the repeating scenarios. Remember such iconic places like the train bridge (Eagle Falls) or Mississippi River in Desperados III? Well, you won´t find something like that in Shadow Gambit. Although the islands are designed in a “visual appealing way”, these scenarios get old really fast because you have to do so many missions on them (some of them have to be revisited five times throughout the game). That also means that you have to work yourself through the same enemy patterns over and over again (feels like open world stuff), especially in the later missions which send you to different locations on the islands. It got very, very boring to me. Really, if I had the choice, I would always prefer LESS CONTENT and instead have MORE QUALITY (like they did in “Desperados 3” and “Shadow Tactics”). And what about this nonsense hub world between the missions (the ghost ship)? In my view it doesn´t contribute to the overall experience at all. Why do I need to play training missions? Just let me experiment with new characters directly within the missions. Why should I do these boring side quests on the ship? I want to have fun playing a RTS game, not a bad RPG. Talking about the story, well, I think there isn´t really an exciting story here, it´s all just about getting your team members and chasing after a treasure. Wow, that´s about it. Very disappointing and boring, especially, if you compare it to “Shadow Tactics” or the “Aiko´s Choice” DLC. Moreover, there is far too much bland / empty talking in this game, the writing is really, really bad. The endgame seemed to take forever, it really felt like a slog to get through. However, the core gameplay in Shadow Gambit is still good, but having played through all their former titles (with all DLCs) and the other classics (D1, Commandos, Robin Hood etc.) it mostly feels a lot easier (I´m playing on the second highest difficulty level). I think that comes from the fact that these scenarios aren´t designed for a specific squad anymore but in a way that you can complete them with any squad. That leads to the fact that the “puzzle factor” is almost non-existent anymore (except in the boss stages, these tend to be very hard). I often was just blazing through the standard missions, mostly completing them in about 20-30 minutes without raising the alarm even once. And I mostly was playing with the same team, because, as the game doesn´t require you to play with a specific team, there´s always a tendency to choose the “stronger team members.” (The balancing is not great so there definitely are stronger and weaker team members, you´ll soon find out). Therefore, let´s be honest: “Shadow Gambit” is a casualized version of Desperados 3 / Shadow Tactics. Much more content, but much less quality. It´s not really a bad game, but it obviously was made to reach a broader audience (especially younger gamers) and therefore didn´t challenge me enough as a big fan of their previous titles and classic games in this genre. As this game has received so many very good reviews, I decided to give it a negative rating (overall rating likely won´t change anyway) because I just expect more from Mimimi. All things considered, I would give it a 7 / 10. If the success of “Shadow Gambit” helps the studio to create more high-quality games like “Desperados 3” or “Shadow Tactics”, well then, fair enough. However, I´m afraid they´re heading in the wrong direction from now on. Remark: I´ve read that Mimimi is about to close down. Even if I was somehow disappointed with "Shadow Gambit", that´s very sad. "Desperados 3" and "Shadow Tactics" will remain one of the greatest games in this genre forever. I was really hoping for another Mimimi game in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi´s last hurra it´s a pure gem. With Shadow Tactics they brought the genre of Stealth Strategy from death, with Desperados 3 they refine it, and finally with Shadow Gambit they revolitonize it. This game takes the genre and spins it around, taking away what were though to be pillars of the genre. A static quest by quest structure, quest design around the specific character you are forced upon in each map, or a focus on realism and historical periods that were all until this point pretty much standards of every single game in this small nitche genre.You will take control of Afia Manicato, a cursed pirate, pirates whom have ended up with a magical black pearl in their chests, turning them into undead magical inmortal creatures. Above all she wants to join the Red Marley, a sentiant voodoo ship that recently lost it´s captain. From here the game opens up to a non linear (for the msot part) structure hwere you will play in between main quests missions, collecting black pearls and energy to revive more crew mates, and playing small quests on the ship itself, which serves as a hub area. Beyond the story the gameplay is as tight as previous Mimimi games, probably even more, since the game allows you to choose in most missions which crew mates to take there, the game it´s more open, providing tons of options. Maps are also far bigger, but you won´t need to traverse them entirely, in fact the open nature of the game means you will visit the same island several times so they are clearly design to be divided into parts. But the big focus it´s the characters, all with tons of powers that you would have never imagine in this genre, they are all extremelly usefull, fun and they are all releated to the type of creature each undead crewmate has turn, which generally it´s releated to their previous life, plus they all have side quests of all shorts that give them lots of personality. The whole package needles to say it´s very unique. There isn´t much else to say, if you have played previous Mimimi games this is the perfect parting gift for their amazing trayectory, if you have not then you are missing out, even if you never dwell into the genre, you can´t go wrong with this unique and amazing pure joy gem. I mean, it´s voodoo undead pirates with supernatural powers, just the theme alone and the devs great track record is worth the entry ticket. Although I advice the game has a rather catchy shanty that has not left my head for over two weeks... AND THAT´S WHAAAT WEEE DOOOOO
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi are the GOATs of this genre and this game mostly lives up to their lofty standards, the overall story and most (but not all) characters are great in this one.Where the game kinda missed for me though was in the map design, they're constantly recycled, over and over again, and some of them I really disliked, the church ones are particularly bad, so much that I found myself doing everything I could to postpone playing them.SCORE: 9/10. It's still an amazing game, I personally rank it 3rd in Mimimi's catalogue, Desperados 3 is still their magnum opus.PS RIP Mimimi Games, I'm glad I got to play your amazing games, I just wish you would've stuck to making games for gamers instead of blackrock, maybe then you'd still be around.

_childDocuments_.review: Another excellent commando-like game form Mimimi. Shadow Gambit has the same level of polish as their previous games, but this time mimimi decided to finally inovate on the abilities of their characters, and its a blast. While some abilities like the genre staple "whistle" remain unchanged, a lot abilities have a interestign twist on them. For example afiast blink seems somewhat similar to coopers knife, but the twist is that Afia teleport with the "knife". This means no more double kills, but also allows for repositioning, which I think results in more fun gameplay. And than there are completely unique abilites, like wanderdust, that makes (lurable) enemy walk direction opposite of the character for some time.Unfortunately there are also some Op abilities, like th eability to summon bush anywhere. But given the ability to freely pick characters to take on a mission, its possible to avoid the OP characters or at least vary the charcaters so that challenge is not completely gone. In general im not a fan of player having to balance the game by limiting themselves, and I would much prefer if all charcaters were balanced, but this isnt big enough issue for me not to recommend the game.

Not to mention being able to choose which 3 characters to use on a mission, instead of previous games where this was chosen for you, is awesome. _childDocuments_.review: After resurrecting the genra of "commando-like", Mimimi Games now blesses us every 2 years of so with another stealth-strategy-puzzle game. They are all good, they are all unique in their setup,  and they keep bringing as much joy everytime.This time, the setup is fantasy pirates, with its own peculiar universe. This is of course an excuse to shower us with brand new characters with supernatural abilities. I wasn't much appealed by the "neon pirate" style of the trailer, but the colorful characters seduced me quite rapidly while playing them. They clearly understood how to improve each typical character: the spy doesn't need to fine a disguise but has limited movement and range, the sharpshooter has unlimited shot, but needs to retrieve it, some other offer unique movements to pass guards easily, ...Compared to the equally excellent previous games, I'd sayPros:- new fun characters with original game-changing capacities- choose your crew and missions, feels less linear- new types of enemies for interesting challengesCons:- no-kill runs are more useless than ever, still regretting the insane no-kill medals of "blade of the shogun"- night-time missions feel really easy compared to day-time missions- footprint mechanism is under exploited

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games.Some gameplay spoilers ahead. Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is Real Time Tactics game, from the same developers of Desperados 3 and Aiko’s choice, where you control a group of Undead/Ghost pirates in a world with several different islands, ranging from the usual tropical island to a prison, or a sanctuary and many others. As your adversary you have religious fanatics, loosely inspired in the roman catholic church, easily noticed by the latin names, some of the clothing and the deity called the Maiden (a mix between jesus christ and the virgin mary) and its iconography.The story takes place in the fantasy world and is divided into three acts. Besides the missions where you face your enemy, there are others designed around your crewmates and their backstories. They all have different skills, personalities and motivations and their stories are interesting and captivating. There’s also the crew tales, a sort of short tasks you can complete in between missions.   The graphics are what the developer has already done in previous games. The islands are well designed, with some interesting details, but it’s on the character design that the game stands out, each character is unique and their look is very well connected to the skills and abilities they can use. The abilities and visual effects are also very well done and really capture the supernatural element of the character’s abilities.   The game’s music fits the “pirate” theme very well and the voice acting is also excellent: you can guess the country of origin of each pirate just by the accent that is used, ranging from the standard caribbean accent to a scottish one.The gameplay is the same as previous games, but given the supernatural nature of the characters they also have a few different abilities that allow different approaches to each engagement and offer more tactical options. The game also incorporated the save often advice into the game story and gameplay itself which was very clever.I played all the missions in Legend difficulty and it still felt easy at times, but in some parts I also had to reload a lot, but overall, if you’re familiar with the previous games, this is the right difficulty to play the game. To get the badges (in-game achievements) I lowered the difficulty just to save time and get as many badges as possible in each single run.  26 Achievements. Around 45 hours, without help. Medium, depending on the difficulty you pick. Medium. Most achievements are easy, only the completion and secret one will take more time to get. Getting 85% completion might seem hard to accomplish but after you finish the main story, the game will help you by displaying a warning if you fail any possible achievement so that you can reload the game. The badge requirements can also be checked online, and thus you can get some on your first time playing each mission. In my run, I replayed some missions twice, trying to get as many achievemetns as possible but focusing on the character badges helped me reach almost 90% faster, and I haven’t even finished all the easier island and mission badges. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: A bright, undead pirate adventure with plenty of humor, strategy, unique character powers, and a fun crew to sail the seas. Another solid tactical-strategy entry from Mimimi Games, and highly recommended for fans of the genre!Shadow Gambit’s undead theme is bright, with a peppy setting and cheeky feel. The graphics fit the vibe down to the font. While Mimimi's other titles have sharper graphics, the portraits and icons have a subtle movement that makes them livelier. The game adds a whimsical spice to pirate tropes with many irregular twists.Where Shadow Tactics and Desperados felt more serious, Shadows Gambit has levity throughout. The voice acting has a Caribbean tinge, the banter is full of quips and puns, and the sound effects are great. I would have liked more punch from the music as it lacks a standout rhythm and portrait variations for the cast.The narrative is fun and fits the adventurous and light-hearted tone, although less memorable than previous titles with the trade-off of an open exploration narrative instead of a driven story. The game is too glee when I prefer more grit still, I applaud the unique feel the game brings. The ship as a base also introduced more side characters who add to the narrative and a living world. The core gameplay is here--stealth, vision markers, enemy field of sight, environmental kills, timed party skill execution--and each crew member is viable. The supernatural spin allows for various powers, enemies, and environmental mechanics unfamiliar to the genre. I enjoy the introduction of CDR instead of set uses, and skills can be ungraded. The new RPG mechanics for the ship and crew relationships is a nice touch. With the ability to customize the difficulty, everything works exceptionally well.Missions are selected from the world map and carried out by a party of three from a crew of eight. Each island and character have badges [challenges] to chase down. Complete a mission for upgrades and return to maps to earn more badges. This keeps a constant progression—the introduction of side-quest rounds out the story and cast.While I enjoy Mimimi's other titles slightly more, Shadows Gambit does a lot to push the genre forward, and the subtle art touches are necessary. I highly look forward to the next title with implementations learned from Gambit.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never tried stealth tactics games or enjoyed one, this is the bridge that will change it."Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew" belongs to a niche genre of real-time stealth tactics. In the past, the developer has iterated on it with "Shadow Tactics" and "Desperados III", which brings us to this game.Story-wise, we navigate a roster of undead pirates with a sentient ship that search for the treasure hidden by the former ship captain. Unfortunately, there's more going on due to the actions of the fanatical inquisitors. The lore is intertwined with game mechanics in many ways, which I'm not going to spoil to you.The idea of gameplay is still "enter, infiltrate by any means, perform the objective, extract", but, because of the setting, the player has more freedom in every step of the plan. The main difference is an ability to select the mission members (up to three for most missions). You can also choose the entry and exit points on your own. Since your characters are undead, you can revive fallen crewmates — death doesn't mean "instant failure". Certain abilities can be upgraded, the currency is routinely acquired by completing missions.Regarding "select your team": there are definitely both pros and cons to it. Side quests expand on characters' background; level design is more inventive to allow unlikely teams and motivate multiple mission replays. On the other hand, some abilities have strong resemblance; while there is an incentive to cycle your picks, characters are widely different in terms of their viability; even the story can be considered somewhat weaker because of the absence of a preset narrative.However, after all points listed, I think the implemented amount of flexibility is good. I have my preferences in terms of how I approach missions, I've found what I consider "the A-team", but other players might have different tastes — and that's great.I'm incredibly sad that the studio that brought the genre back to life is closing down. I'm grateful for their work. With "Shadow Gambit", I knew what I was getting and I had fun every single moment (32.5 hours for the main story on the hardest difficulty) with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi Games have done it again. After the fantastic Shadow Tactics, Desperados III and Aiko's Choice it should be clear the developers are masters of this genre and Shadow Gambit is no exception. I should point out I never buy games at full price. I have games on my Wishlist that have sat there for over 2 years waiting for the right sale price. I bought Shadow Gambit, at full price, the moment I saw it purely because I trust the developers to deliver excellent games and I am not disappointed. The story is interesting. I personally find the characters a little over-done and not as relatable as those is say Shadow Tactics, but the core gameplay has been massively improved over what was already a brilliant formula. The new skills allow for completely new approaches and tactics which really bump the gameplay and replayability up another notch. The improved UI provides excellent natural feeling shortcuts to the common actions. I've only completed 4 missions so far and am already at 17 hours played in just 3 days. I can't say I'm really a fan of the new hub. I see no reason for it and honestly it just gets in the way of the game. So far at least I haven't found the game as challenging as Shadow Tactics was. This might be due to the new approach of being able to choose which characters you take with you and maybe the difficulty has been eased a little to allow for the different skillsets. I'd much rather have set characters and a harder challenge, but I am not going to criticise the devs for trying something new as the game is still wonderful.While the couple of negatives I've mentioned are not really an issue, more personal taste, I do have one more serious criticism. As I alluded to earlier, you can now choose which characters to take with you but before you can do that you must choose which to revive. To help decide, you can bring up information about each character. The problem is this information is, in my opinion, not very clear as to what the new skills are or how they work. Mr Mercury, for example, has a fantastic ability to sink into the ground and re-appear elsewhere, attacking enemies from below, bypassing walls and avoiding sand footprints. Great stuff. What wasn't made clear in the profile information was that this ability can only be used to sink and reappear on land that is at the same height. That's pretty important! The same character also has a fish that you can use to distract guards. Sounds just like characters from Shadow Tactics and you'd expect it to work the same way, but no. The fish will only distract acolytes. Commisarius' won't even turn to look, it has no effect on them whatsoever. Another piece of information missing from the profile. This is an area that I hope the devs really improve as it is critical to decision making. Despite the small issues and that one criticism all in all I'd still give the game 9/10 and highly recommend it, even at full price. Well done Mimimi once again.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic stealth RTS and one of Mimimi Games's best works. The game gives you a ton of freedom in how you can tackle challenges, from the characters at your disposal to the routes you can take towards objectives. For instance, if you've played any of their previous games, you've likely encountered an enemy that can generally only be killed by certain characters (the Samurai/Long Coats), but in this game those enemies work a little differently. Here, they can be killed by any character, as long as they have the help of one other character. This means that no matter the enemy layout, you can always find some solution that works for your setup, which I think is neat.The story isn't anything to write home about, partially due to the above mentioned freedom. Because you can freely choose your teammates for any mission, outside of special missions, the main story treats your party members as though they don't exist for the majority of the time. Since you can pick any combination of characters to bring along, this just the sacrifice the studio probably made to allow for more flexibility during gameplay.All in all, if you're looking for stealth pirates, you'll find it here in spades. I'd give it a personal 9/10 for my enjoyment of the game. Give it a go if it's on sale!

There are definitely characters that are way better and more useful than others, but the variety in skills keeps you from getting complacent. There is also a game mechanic that encourages you to try a different crew each mission.The downside of the freedom is that the game feels way easier than the last 2. I played on the second hardest difficulty and it still felt easier than Desperados 3 on the same difficulty. There is a "Long coat" type enemy in this game as well, but they are always more annoying than threatening. The overall variety in enemy types could have been larger, as it's mostly the same old stuff we have seen before.The story is fun and I really enjoyed the weird and goofy magic elements in the world. There is a lot of banter between crew members and you really get to know them all by the end of the game.I am sad this will be Mimimi's last game , since they were basically keeping the stealth action genre alive. _childDocuments_.review: An wonderful refinement of the genre; the culmination of an excellent studio's excellent track record.Instead of a linear path of puzzles, Shadow Gambit is something like a stealth playground. The player chooses where they want to land on the mission area, and may approach their objective as they see fit using the crew's large variety of tools. With every member I unlock, I think "this one is OP, I'll never have to use someone else" and then find some new synergy for old members that makes me feel like a genius.This game is really, really good at making you feel clever, with a mode that allows you to pause time so that you may issue simultaneous commands to your crew, allowing for big brain multikills of groups. I find myself laughing when a crazy plan actually works, and not too frustrated when it doesn't, thanks to the quickload feature available at the press of a button.And the UI; my God. Subtle cues during exploration, soulful visual menu design, and smooth controls for gamepad combine to make a complicated game with dozens of simultaneous moving parts easy to understand and play.This game is worth full price for any fan of stealth games. With adjustable difficulties, optional challenges, and more hidden jokes than you can fit in a pirate's buried chest, Shadow Gambit's clever levels and flavorful crew will keep you playing for hours on end.

_childDocuments_.review: I have not gotten to Shadow Gambit yet, I have still been finishing up Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 on PS4 (long story), I assure that not only will I be playing this game, I will complete it entirely. A terribly sad day for gaming, when I found out that Mimimi is closing their doors. They very quickly became one of my very favorite developers, because not only am I a huge fan of RTS/RTT style games, but with every one of their releases they continually set the bar higher and higher. As a result those of us began to get more and more excited with the announcement that another game was being developed. They did not release very many games, but every single one of those that they did release were always of the highest quality, in every measurable metric possible. The graphics, the writing (every game has been a roller coaster ride of tense drama and intrigue, to laugh out loud humor) the gameplay and controls are always spot on, and if there were any bugs you knew you could count on Mimimi to resolve those issues very quickly. The quality of each release made us even more comfortable in spending our money to preorder the next game, something I simply have not done in years, because so few studios actually meet these same standards anymore, these days. Mimimi was a welcome return to the games of old, back to when you knew you could count on high level releases, back to when the thought that a game might release in an unfinished state, or overflowing with game breaking bugs was not even a possibility.Well, I wish for everyone at Mimimi to know that so many of us appreciate all that you did. I would like to say a personal thank you, to each of you, and to give you my assurances, that should you ever return to making such wonderful games again. I will be one of the first people in line to purchase anything, and everything, you do. I wish you all, and all of your families, nothing but the very best, now and in the future, may you find all the happiness that you are searching for!

_childDocuments_.review: After the Shogun theme with Shadow Tactics and Western theme with Desperados 3, they now tackle the Pirate Fantasy theme with Shadow Gambit. Like the other games you are sneaking around in a top down view, with a varied cast of characters that all have different abilities. You pick your crew, sneak around the level while assassinating enemies in various ways, and complete the objective. Some enemies have powers of their own to counter yours, and each location is a puzzle for you to solve because your cover, the amount of enemies and their positions and powers, and it being night or day will make a difference in how to approach a situation every time.It's a great entry in this genre, especially if you enjoy this theme.

_childDocuments_.review: Short version:Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a grand old time of combining the unique abilities of a few characters to take down guards and complete objectives unseen, with fun pirate flavor thrown in and supported by a great cast of characters.Long version:For context, I've played some stealth action games, many turn-based tactics RPGs, and a fair few real time with pausing RPGs. Shadow Gambit was my first experience with stealth tactics, and I've greatly enjoyed it.The basics of the game - sightlines, visibility, attacking, and character abilities - are easy enough to grasp. The main loop of the game usually involves systematically taking down guards at opportune moments using the crewmembers' various unique abilities, hiding their bodies, and moving towards an objective. Alternatively, you can try completely avoiding guards, though eventually this becomes impractical. You can even go almost completely nonlethal for the entire game, which I always appreciate (though it does make things a bit harder, and sometimes you can softlock yourself accidentally by hiding the unconscious body of someone you need to kill). Overall, the loop feels quite good. The game has a pause ("Shadow Tactics") mode that allows you to execute a command to multiple crewmembers instantaneously or whenever you next press the "Execute" button. This was extremely helpful for taking down multiple guards at a time and managing emergencies, though I had a couple minor gripes with this feature that I'll mention later. One of the most important features is quicksaving, which by default can be done at any time. This is a common feature in games, but it's particularly important for this game (there's even a nice in-game explanation for why you're able to do it, which is neat).Mechanically, the crewmembers feel like they each fill a distinct role, which is made reasonably clear before you recruit them. Each crewmember has several abilities, some of which can be used in several different ways, and every crewmember can receive a permanent upgrade that opens up new tactics for them. Figuring out different applications and combinations of abilities was great fun, and the game encourages it by rewarding you for choosing different crewmembers for each mission (specifically, choosing a crewmate you didn't use during the last mission will accelerate how fast you get new upgrade tokens for your crew, though you can absolutely just stick with your favorite crewmembers). No complaints here.The controls were a bit unintuitive since I'm used to WASD camera control, but by the end of the game the controls were comfortable enough that I could direct my characters using hotkeys, which saves a lot of clicking around. However, I did have some difficulty with issuing commands in pause mode: First, it seems that you can't group select multiple crewmates by clicking and dragging in pause mode, which made coordination a bit more cumbersome. Second, by default, a character given a move command will walk upright (un-crouched) to their destination, which makes them more easily spotted. Furthermore, characters would sometimes stand upright after completing some actions. It's easy not to notice this, and it can be frustrating when a character gets spotted as a result. I eventually worked out how to largely avoid this, but it could be made easier. Thankfully, the game slows down time while a character is being spotted, which helps prevent mishaps somewhat.As for the levels, I enjoyed the vast majority of them. There are about a dozen maps in total, and though most are reused for multiple missions, they are large enough that you often won't need to go anywhere near where you were for a previous mission. One map represents a significant difficulty spike in the game, which I found to be a bit overwhelming at first, but not terrible. The maps feel like they were made with care, as guards will largely cover each other with sightlines, but there are still plenty of vulnerabilities for the player to discover and exploit. Each mission/map also has several special challenges, which lend to replayability once the game lets you go back and play previous missions.Graphically, these maps and the rest of the game look quite nice. Getting close up to the 3D models reveals them to be a bit low-fidelity, but 99% of the time in this game is spent from a bird's eye view anyways, and from there the game looks great. The 2D character art that shows up in dialogue and in portrait frames is stylish, and it compensates for their somewhat low-fi character models. As for the narrative and acting, I enjoyed the main plot and the characters. The writing and voiceover for the characters was very good, with some standout performances here and there. Some of my favorite moments were on the personal missions for the crewmembers (Mass Effect 2, anyone?), and I'm glad that the game gives you the opportunity to dive into each character's story. The main plot felt good, though I'm not great at judging the quality of stories IMO.Lastly, the soundtrack is great, I've been listening to it on repeat while I work. Very fitting and very groovy.Overall, Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a fun time, based on a solid core gameplay loop that encourages experimentation and supported by a strong cast of characters. This was a great introduction into the stealth tactics genre, and I'm very sad to hear that the developers will be shutting down for the foreseeable future.

_childDocuments_.review: Damned to be compared to ST/D3, Shadow Gambit feels like a great step forward and great step backward at the same time. Let's skip positives, as they are already reviewed - the game looks gorgeous, plays smoothly and is overwhelmingly polished, thumbs up. What went wrong?- Difficulty scale doesn't respect skilled players. Lack of puzzle-like enemy setups on hardest difficulties. You can just cut the entire map using a mostly single character, which nullify the grand new feature of this game - cool team/skill compositions.- There is random dice button when selecting a crew for a mission, which is a kind of fun. The downside is the maps designed for this button working as expected regardless of difficulty scale - so you should be able to complete any mission with any composition. Skilled players already concerned about this during announce days, but it's not have been addressed.- Quantity over quality for badges. And what make this even more worse, you have no access to badges until the main campaign finished. If you are a challenge seeker for the first walkthrough, you should use a Google. And you have to, since it's the only way to slightly compensate the lack of difficulty if you are a skilled player.- Intermissions gameplay on ship might be meaningful story-wise for some ppl, but it's meaningless gameplay-wise. And it's time-consuming regardless of your meanings preference.Nonetheless, I'm enjoying how the game plays and feels - Mimimi put all their love into making this. But if you are a skilled player, don't expect to find a big challenge here. I've found it relaxing, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit builds on what made Mimimi's previous titles great, and polishes the experience to near perfection. In terms of execution, this is their most refined (and very sadly last) title.A significant shift in design is the scope of the game: the maps are bigger, there are more characters (which you unlock in an order of your choosing), and a larger number of missions. This means there are more combinations of special powers of each crew member that you can play around, and in a considerable amount of scenarios. This is a lot of fun - it keeps the game fresh while giving you the freedom to experiment.The optional Crew Tales have you go through 5-part crew member centered comic relief between missions, in the form of dialogue and brief, simple ship-related tasks. These were often surprising and amusing to follow.Unfortunately, the decision to expand on everything comes with a price: repeat visits to islands may start to wear you out, some crew members are significantly better than others, and perhaps most disappointing of all - level design has to account for different combinations and thus provides inherently easier gameplay experience.Despite this, the game is still a great experience, and certainly sets a standard for what games in the genre should hope to achieve. If you liked previous Mimimi titles, or if you are even somewhat into real time stealth tactics (or stealth strategy as they would have us call it) - you will almost certainly have a good time.Thank you Mimimi, and goodbye <3

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit is a good stealth tactics games by one of the masters of the genre, Mimimi. The game resembles Spellbound's Robin Hood in that you have a base for in between the missions and you can pick which 3 characters you want to take on each mission. There are 8 vanilla characters plus 2 from the DLC's. They have the usual Commandos / Desperados skills like the lure, the sniper, etc. With some surprises. There are about a dozen maps that you visit repeatedly during different times of day and for different missions in different zones. The pacing is slightly off and the game starts to drag toward the middle. The setting is magical undead pirates. Normal pirates or just magical living pirates would have sufficed.Overall, Shadow Gambit is a solid and polished stealth tactics game. But I think that both Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 were better. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit is an absolutely amazing and fun game in the same genre as Shadow Tactics, Desperados and Commandos. Honestly it's hard to compare it to Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3, as all three games are very similar and most players who like the genre will eventually get all three anyway.Shadow Gambit is extremely interesting in that the missions are not linear. You have a team of eight characters (though not all of them are available from the start). For most missions you can actually choose which characters will go on the mission. The crewmates are very different from each other and some have quite interesting abilities.In this regard Shadow Tactics and Desperados were very similar and only differed in the setting - Cooper and Hayato were almost equal, Kate and Aiko were quite the same, Hector was a combination of Yuki and Mugen etc. The only unique character was Isabele with her voodoo. In Shadow Gambit everyone is very different.Your first character already has quite interesting skills - Blink for short range teleportation (can be combined with a takedown) and Time Stop - freezes a guard for a short while. The other seven you'll unlock will be even more fun. There are of course obligatory team members: spy and sniper, though both are quite unique, too. Your sniper only has one shot, but she can pick it up again and shoot again. Your spy doesn't have to find disguise first, but instead possesses enemy soldiers. However, he only has a limited range on how far he can get in the possessed body. Extremely innovative and quite fun.However, Pinkus (the spy) feels weaker than Kate and infinitely weaker than Aiko. This is a prime example of how the crewmates in Shadow Gambit are relatively well balanced. There are no obvious outliers, i.e. nobody clearly stands out as absolutely overpowered or totally underpowered (others might disagree, though). The screens at the end of each mission usually confirm this - I've even spent about the same time with each crewmate.Long story short: the game still plays the same, but feels very different from its siblings - both due to the setting and its mechanics. If you like the genre, definitely give it a go!

_childDocuments_.review: Guys, I finally nailed it! 2 months, 300 hours, and I’ve conquered this game. If you’re into strategy games, this is a must-have.🕹️ Controls: The strategy’s intense – like playing a game of international chess. Planning 2, 3 steps ahead, sometimes even more. The climax? Coordinating 8 characters to simultaneously take down 5 bosses. Took me a grueling 2 hours, but the feeling of accomplishment? Priceless.🎨 Graphics: The maps: Each one is a classic. The final map? I’d call it the ultimate challenge. Every new map is like a stunning piece of art, super exciting.👥 Multiplayer: Characters : there are 8, each with unique abilities. The combo of Teresa, Suleidy, and Afia? Unbeatable. :碰:📖 Storyline: Plot’s kinda weak though. To be honest, it doesn’t match up to ‘DAVE THE DIVER’ which I played earlier. But for a strategy game, it holds up pretty well.👎 Cons: Game mechanics can get a bit redundant. Unlocking new characters means revisiting old maps. I get the devs’ point – different experiences with each character, but it can get boring, especially since I clear all enemies on every new map.But overall, it’s been an unforgettable and exhilarating experience. Loved every minute of it.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel mixed about this game.On one hand, I really enjoyed the discovery, the new powers / combos available and the shadow mode is clearly a plus for execution. The music is lovely, and the graphics / atmosphere is well done. The first 20h flied by like a good dream.On the other hand, characters are clearly not balanced between them, and overpowered compared to the enemies. The story is akward and mostly boring. The end game seems pointless and a lot of the content feels here just as a filler. I recommend Shadow Gambit if you're a fan of tactical stealth game, but I feel a real downgrade compared to their other games (Desperados III and Shadow Tactics).For the price, I would advice to play their other games before, or even the Commandos series, they're much more well written, immersive and fun than this one.But if you've already played those and are looking for refreshment/change, Shadow Gambit does the work ok. ___6/10___More details down below :PROS : - mechanics and levels design are well rounded. The devs know what they're doing. It's very enjoyable to read a map and understand the components and dynamics of it. Great satisfaction to press enter and see your plan executed at perfection.- graphics and music give a beautiful atmosphere.- characters have quite fun abilities, some synergies and combos are just insane to experiment. Nice touch and the discovery is entertaining.- some scenes / puzzles where quite challenging and well staged, but there are too few of them.- some characters gimmicks are fun, but it gets old rather quickly.CONS :- the story is by far the worst aspect of the game. Compared to other games of the genre, this one is a joke. Characters are one dimensional caricatures. Crew tales a tedious and boring, I stopped engaging in them and spammed the "skip" button like i never did in any other games before.- It seems they put a lot of efforts in the voice acting and writting, but nothing is really said, it's just filler conversations and bad jokes, no one evolves during the story (except some light realizations)- there are very few moments where you feel in difficulty. I played in Legend difficulty and didn't feel the challenge most of the time. - characters are not balanced, some are just overpowered and it feels you're never in danger to fail. I took my time and finish the story in 40h+, but mostly because I wanted to execute twisted plans and synchronize actions with my crew. When I was bored of the story, I could rush the level easily. Yes the characters powers are original and fun sometimes, but this is too much if the enemies are just meat bags wandering about waiting to be taken down.- the "end game" is just repeating what you already finished, playing some maps more than 6 times. I didn't get the last "hidden" charcater because I would have to play again and again the same maps to finally unlock another overpowered character, to do again the same missions ? I don't get it.Overall, Shadow Gambit is a nice steath tactical game, but is far below other masterpieces of the genre. I'm disappointed for the price, it's worth if you get it under 20€ (max).I would have prefered a cheaper, shorter game, with less acting and content, but more intentional in the design and character building.Anyway, thank you Mimimi for the beautiful work over those years and for allowing us to play quality stealth games.

_childDocuments_.review: For the most part Shadow Gambit: Cursed Crew is the culmination of all of Mimimi Games' Learning since doing Shadow Run tactics and it shows. This is a no brainer if you enjoyed either one of their previous titles. In my entire play though I only had 1 bug. That's not the say the game doesn't have a few flaws that can feel apparent after 30+ hours of gameplay and yet if this strategy game resonance with you, you can expect to double that amount of time. I think a big criticism is the revisiting of island while you can tell each has been crafted to be the staging ground for multiply missions. The same enemy placement can often feel like a repetitive slog completing the same puzzle.The lack of enemy Variety also becomes a pain after multiply missions. Despite these shortcomings, the music and environment is wonderful with each island having its own certain mistique. Being able to bring in different combinations of crew members helps keep the puzzle going but does limit some of the mission designs. Even the story which sometimes feels a bit predictable can feel charming if you let. It's just a really good game and the publish deserves all the awards and success for creating it.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew has 95% and it absolutely deserves that. However, there are a few negative reviews out there and I want to tackle the common complaints you can find in them:1. Negative reviews:1.1 "This game is a downgrade from Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, story- and gameplaywise"Absolutely not, especially not storywise and I honestly don't understand where this comes from. For example, different from its predecessors, the game finds a way to explain the Quicksave-feature as part of the story. The characters are all unique and bring with them their own story as part of the main quest.Sure, some of them have comparable abilities, but that isn't something new to this genre. It is, in fact, not so easy to find a big variety of different abilities that all would still be fitting for such a game. And Shadow Gambit simply has more characters then Shadow Tactics and Desperados. So of course it might seem as if the characters are more similar to each other. 1.2 "The game is too easy/The game is easier then ST and D3/The freedom of character choice ruins the game"Highly subjective, as all of this is, sure, but finishing a mission has never been too difficult in any of these games, atleast not for me, even on the highest difficulty. So the real challenge in Shadow Gambit is, as in the other games, doing the badges. And they still exist, so I don't see any problem here. If you truly think the game is too easy, challenge yourself and choose those characters you never chose before and start at the most difficult Landing Spot and do it on highest difficulty while also doing the Island badges like not touching any hiding spots and so on. The game definitely gives you the options to make it difficult, so this isn't really a valid complaint. If you don't like freedom, don't use it. 1.3 "The characters are dull/one-dimensional/can be described in one sentence/weak in comparison to the characters from ST and D3"Once again, I don't see where this comes from. A game like this doesn't offer too much opportunities to create real character development, and just as in their other games, Mimimi does that as well as possible. Each character has their personal missions in which they can show what type of people they are. And even if it would be true that the characters aren't deep or anything, I still don't see what the problem with that would be. If you need tales about the rise and fall of heroes, read a book. And for those who claim the predecessor games were better considering the characters: Here is the Story of Desperados 3 in a nutshell for you: "My Name is John Cooper. You killed my father! Prepare to die!"Wow, I can describe something in just one line, crazy. Must mean the story is bad, right?Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a very good game and a worthy successor of Mimimi previous games. This comes from a true fan of the genre who is playing this since the days of Desperados 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, Shadow Gambit Cursed Crew has a wide Range of Pros and a single huge Con, so lets start with The Pros:- Many abilities which give each character a unique playstyle- Progression systems- Likable characters which seem flat at first but you get to know better over the course of the game- Long campaign with an interesting storyline- Islands are so big that every island has between 2 to 4 unique locations- Very solid OST- No bugs, glitches or performance issuesNow the Con:There really is only 1 real problem I have with the game - The campaign is way longer than either shadow tactics or Desperados, so how excactly did they manage that with roughly... 9 islands?Well the fix is easy, have players play the same island maybe 6 times to complete the campaign. There can be several interesting locations on an island you dont get to visit all in a single mission, there are several landing points to choose from and maybe your crew loadout is different and there might be difference if it is night or day - but ultimately it is still the same map. With, for the very most part, the same enemies at the same places doing the same thing. Luckily I am no completionist, because all of those half a dozen missions on a single island count as unique mission, meaning each of them have their own set of achievements - which would mean I would have to play the same island at 'least' 6 more times again to get all of them. Overall the very good writing kept me afloat when i realized that all those islands I already finished 2 to 3 missions on I have to visit 3 to 4 more times really peeved me. Otherwise I have to admit I wouldve quit right then and there - And I wouldnt blame anybody who did.

_childDocuments_.review: This is like previous Mimimi titles - Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 - and similar to Commandos, a real-time tactics with stealth elements, utilizing character's toolkit to solve "puzzles" designed across specific levels/missions. However there's some nuances that make it different from its predecessors: in previous titles we had a limited number of characters (4-5) each with specific skills, and to solve puzzles/levels we had to utilize specific tools to succeed, and the number of solutions to the puzzle was limited. Here, in Shadow Gambit, the game was designed with flexibility in mind: we have 8 characters to choose from so our toolkit for a mission can be varied, therefore each mission and each section of the mission had to be designed in a way that it could be solved and approached in different ways regardless what characters we've selected for that mission - therefore the puzzle of enemy encounters is simplified to fit any combination of our selected team's toolkit. In some places there are great puzzles to solve. I did enjoy it and I'm glad the studio tried a different design approach intended for more open varied toolkit which has it's positives and drawbacks.

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal real-time tactics game, Shadow Gambit puts you in control of a colorful crew of undead pirates as you hunt for the treasure hidden by their very dead captain. It takes some small inspiration from Star Trek Away Team, as most missions let you put together your own three man team out of the crew members you have available at the time. While each crew member will fit into certain archetypes (e.g. infiltrator), no two crew members are the same and any team composition is viable.Speaking of crew members - you unlock (revive) the roster at a steady pace as you complete missions and you do it in a non-linear fashion, meaning you choose which crew member you want to revive at any given opportunity out of the entire roster of eight (you will get them all by the end).The mission/story flow is also less linear than a usual RTT game, as you will have several missions available at most times and you can complete them in any order you want (you still need to complete them all though). There's some optional content as well that you can progress through in-between missions, while you are on your ship. The story will take somewhere between 30 and 40 hours to complete with at least 10 hours more for any leftover optional narrative content. The game is highly replayable, so you may even want to complete in-game badges (challenges) after all the story stuff is done and get that last unlockable secret.Technically, the game is well polished and runs smooth as butter - no stability or performance issues of any kind. There's no online-only requirements, no live-service bs or anything like that, just a nice, polished single player game. Money well spent for any real-time tactics game fan. I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Really sad to see Mimimi (the devs) disband.  The game is as good as anything Mimimi previously did, but their timing was terrible; it was released between Baldur's Gate 3 and Starfield! Although I loved their previous games and admired them for reviving the tactical stealth genre and improving it, when I saw the first trailers of this game I was turned off because of the art style and the undead pirate setting. Moreover, the new skills looked overpowered. Yet, trusting Mimimi, I got the game as soon as I could, and played until 100% completion. I ended up enjoying the game quite a lot and was pleasantly surprised with their world-building. The guard routes & types are pretty well-balanced with the skills despite my earlier doubt. The missions are also well-designed, the characters are well-sketched, had good voice-acting and are fun to have as crew. The completely optional crew tales also come to be something to look for between the missions. I enjoyed the soundtrack as well and was joyed to notice a subtle tribute to "The Curse of Monkey Island". (I think there were Monkey Island influences in some of the visuals and artwork. e.g. Dread Vine Cove in the game.) I also admired the way the quicksave/load feature is integrated into the story line so as not to break immersion. playing several missions on the same map, having control over crew composition before a mission and semi-free level progression (there are a few missions that you have to play next, but you can play the others in any order). Lastly, you do not get to see the badges until you finish the whole story. (In Shadow Tactics, you get to see them after the first completion of a mission.) Some of these choices were risky, especially playing several missions on the same map. However, your targets are on different sections of these very large maps and you do no need to kill everybody (except for achievements).  would be the grind that some of the badges required. I always admired Mimimi for inventing clever and fun challenges, but some of the badges in Shadow Gambit were not challenging or fun, but simply required grinding. (Like doing something uninteresting 20 times over or the most notorious badge of them all; "right under her nose" which is ill-designed as it confuses the player by taking into consideration the water animation over water sound effects.) If you are not interested in 100% challenge completion, this criticism shouldn't bother you at all. But note that the majority of badges/challenges are still in the classic Mimimi style, which take you out of your comfort zone and you end up enjoying it more.Since the devs passed the test of world-building by making a stealth-tactics game in a magical fantasy setting, I hope that they will get back together one day and make new stealth-tactics games in different settings & genres, such as sci-fi, steampunk, cyberpunk, vampire, werewolf etc. Goodbye Mimimi, will miss you a lot. Hope to see you again.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a Real Time Tactics game in a fantasy pirate setting with a heave emphasis on stealth. It is the third Real Time Tactics game the studio has released, the others being Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun and Desperados III. Shadow Gambit is definitely the longest out of all of their previous titles with a lot more freedom of choice than we've seen previously.The gameplay loop is simple, you have a mission to do on an Island and you pick which crew are available to you and bring them on the mission. You can take three crewmates per mission and experience the same map in different ways due to having up to ten (If you include the DLC) to pick from.Each mission requires stealth to get any true success, moving from bush to bush and utilising your crewmates abilities in order to succeed. There will be many times you'll be thinking that your mission is impossible and then you make a tiny bit of progress, just taking down one guard at the perfect time and next thing you know, the whole scene opens up and the dominoes fall. The game is a lot more light-hearted than previous titles, Shadow Tactics and Desperados III had their funny little moments but overall the tone was a lot more serious. Shadow Gambit has its serious moments but you can tell that the overall tone of the game and story is less tragic and gritty.The characters and crew are definitely what makes this game special. In my opinion these are the best characters Mimimi have made, Afia Manicato (Main character) sticks out as a much stronger protagonist than any of the other titles and the others in the crew also have their noteworthy moments. It seems a great emphasis has been put on making each character feel unique during the development cycle and I believe they've achieved this to a great extent. I'd also like to add that playing this game with both Yuki's Wish and Zagan's Ritual DLC, for me, feels like a must as it slots into the story very well during the mid-game and both characters feel at home with the rest of the crew.There are a few little issues that are worth noting especially in comparison to some of the previous titles.The majority of the game you are confined to only three characters per mission, now this is consistent all the way through for the most part (there are exceptions for more and fewer than three) and I understand how hard it would have been to balance for more than three with the way the Islands are set up, but I do miss the missions where you'd have five party members and having to manage everyone to success.The Islands as well, there's only a handful of levels, maybe like ten or so and the guard positions are the same in more or less every mission. Now they are somewhat different, challenge wise, if you take a different comp every time (which you should do) but in some Islands it seemed a bit easy, when I know how to tackle a guard set up I've done once before.Other than that, Shadow Gambit is absolutely solid.You'll 100% get your money's worth out of this game, I clocked 64 hours in one playthrough just doing the story and the DLC's, this isn't grinding for badges or 100%, I imagine that'll take much much longer.It's sad that Mimimi closed down because on a personal level, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun was one of the first games that left such a strong impression on me that I started to leave reviews on Steam, so it has affected me that we won't get anymore of these games from them.Overall Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew is a great Real Time Tactics game from a great development team and you can feel the love and passion put into this game from start to finish. 8/10, I wish the developers all the best.

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi Games has been making the same game over and over since 2016, and goodness gracious if they aren't masters of the form by now.Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun updated the 90's Command and Conquer-style stealth-based RTS to the modern era, with compelling characters, fun abilities, and a strong thematic vision.  Desperados III built on this, polishing the style with UI improvements, the ability to pause the flow of time to plan out multi-character ambushes, and an emphasis on replayability.With Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew, they've polished their previous works to a mirror sheen.  The QoL improvements to UI continue, with streamlining of common actions like lifting/dropping bodies, activating objectives, or interacting with environmental objects.  The core stealth-based RTS gameplay is still in full display, but the improvement this time around is a central hub and RPG-elements, allowing you to  upgrade the primary skill of each crewmate by accomplishing certain meta-objectives.  Side missions also lead to greater characterization, and instead of a set sequence of levels, players are granted a level of agency when the game opens up and they are allowed to begin choosing upon which island they want to perform their piratical capers.Theme has ever been a strong point for Mimimi's games, with Shadow Tactics in the turbulent Sengoku Era, and Desperados in the slightyly-less-turbulent-but-we-like-cowboys Wild West Era.  Shadow Gambit (SG:TCC) deviates from previous games, based in historically-inspired settings, and creates its own universe, with the much-maligned Cursed waging a shadow war against the oppressive, totalitarian Inquisition.  You get glimpses into the universe through the side missions and conversations with your crewmembers, and the addition of fantasy to the mix allows for increased complexity and creativity with character design.In that vein, the cast of characters has increased from the 5-person casts of Shadow Tactics and Desperados to a pirate crew of 8, each with dialogue and side missions that can be accessed in the between-missions hub that is your ghost pirate ship.  As mentioned previously, the game has a clear framework for replayability, incentivising (and somewhat, requiring) players return to some of the 10 islands to complete different quests.  Replaying levels is made interesting by different starting locations, guard deployment/patrols, and different mission objectives.All-in-all a great improvement on previous games, which I liked already.  It's fun, the writing is entertaining, the characters are charming, the gameplay is satisfying and rewards creativity, what's not to like?

If you enjoy stealth games or even puzzles (in a more abstract sense) then do yourself a favor and buy this game.  10/10  Mimimi, you will be dearly missed.
