_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game has the perfect pace of exploration, unlocking, and a really fun, gripping story. Each character felt unique and it was a blast trying to pair them up to maximize their strengths.I will cut to the chase. I have had a very hard time finishing games for the last few years which I feel like is in line with the general populace now days and I finished this. This game just does it right. It opens up new characters at the perfect pace and right before that could feel stale the plot evolves at an amazing pace which brings a new approach to the characters again.If you like games where you have to be sneaky but is also low key enough to let you try your own thing then this is a good one. This also plays amazing on the steam deck. Even if you don't do on steam deck, a controller felt a lot more organic for gameplay. Finally, you can play a lot of characters and what I LOVE is that it gives you plenty of reason to play as everyone but also there is no one (or two) who stand above the rest. The personalities were wonderful and there is even things to do after you beat the game that still sound like a ton of fun.I don't do this game justice but it is worth full price as I was never bored and there seems to be a lot of love spent making it.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: tldr; if you're a fan of Mimimi Games, buy it.From west world, Japan and now world of magic and curses of the sea and pirates!- It's easier to control, pick up corpse and drop it. - dialog between characters feels like anime style, good one.- speedup with X key is good for impatient!- map key / map view feel a bit strange plus I didn't see red dots of enemy on map- F5 save animation is a bit sluggish, not thing importantJust land the first island so far! Feeling a bit easier than Shadow Warrior and Desperados III but we have to see further.Will come back and review from time to time!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it. Does nearly everything right for a stealth tactical game. Characters are all unique in personality and play style, tons to do, challenges are fun (and they didn't have the hard AF speedrun challenges like their other games), story was solid but nothing special. They did something really cool with the quick save mechanic I don't think I've ever seen anyone else do before. Love the amount of choice you are given for unlock order and missions.My only real complaint was I wish there had been more variety in maps other than islands and some more missions designed around using more than 3 characters at a time.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: This game is HUGE. 25 hours only for main story, but after final will open real treasure - badges. Badges for island. Badges for missions. Badges for characters. Global badges. Real riddeles. Real challenges.Oh. Game was big, but with badges - its become huge. Hundred hours, no less. Thanks you, Mimimi. Your swan song is awesome!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Great game as expected. A lot has changed compared to ST or Desperados but the core of the game is still the same stealth strategy engine. This time comes with more choices in teammates and approach as well as more story driven campaign. Unfortunatly at least at this time the game also has some flows:  Some teammates seem overpowered while other have a lot less usefull abilities. The difficulty suffered and the game seems easier than predecessors.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: everything in this game you call improve the movement of the  character intrection is much smoother also all the character feel powerfull not like the other titles, has a intresting  story and op powers so what is there not to like and alarm when you get spotted is not that punishing as the previous titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Having fully completed the game in ~40 hours, it's an impressive achievement and a fitting finale for the developer Mimimi. Highly recommend. This game is for anyone who liked the old Commandos or Desperados franchises, for anyone who liked Mimimi's two prior games, or anyone who enjoys deep stealth games. The studio refined many elements from their prior games, allowing more of a sandbox approach to levels via the ability to select which 3 of the 8 characters you want to take onto that specific mission (with incentives to rotating your cast). The game also fully embraces the quick save/quick load mentality for these games in a unique way with clever story implications. You are able to setup the dominoes to eliminate complex guard patrol pattern, then quickly tweak when things go awry.Overall, a solid 9/10 and a reminder that not all great games and studios make it if we don't support them.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. It has Pirates, Magic and Stealth. The Pirate theme is perfect and it´s beautifully crafted. The stealth/strategy gameplay is very engaging and has improved since the previous titles (Shadow Tactics & Desperados 3, which are still great games so check them out!!). The characters are so interesting and fun, along with a compelling and very fitting story. Even the captivating music and ambience are solid. I wish they never stop making this stealth-strategy kind of games. So if you like pirates, infiltration, cursed magic, have fun or wanna have a good time solving these challenges don't think twice!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more open-ended and less puzzle-like than Mimimi's other games. Instead of missions with maps, you have maps with missions. You choose 3 out of 8 crew members, your entry point, and your exit point for each mission. After each mission, you'll advance the main story, chat with crew member(s), and progress one crew member's individual story. The writing is entertaining but nothing groundbreaking.Each character is very unique and can fill at least two roles (distracting, hiding bodies, killing, etc.). You can upgrade each character once, and you're encouraged to try them all since benched characters give you more progress towards upgrades. Even if you've played Mimimi's previous games, you'll find that every character brings at least one interesting and fresh mechanic.The open-ended nature of the game means less in-mission banter and character-specific solutions, but there are more ways to "make your own fun" since swapping your team and changing your entry/exit points makes for very different runs. Granted, this is somewhat dependent on enjoying the kill-body-hide-body gameplay loop. If you enjoy cleaning up maps in creative ways then you'll love this game. I also highly recommend randomizing your team if you want to keep yourself on your toes!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent a bit of time in the game now, so I've begun to notice lots of little details in the lost Caribbean which demonstrate the passion of the team behind it.In many ways, Shadow Gambit is MiMiMi's best game. The quality of life improvements make playing a smoother and more enjoyable experience. Embracing the supernatural has allowed the game to break away from the status quo laid down by Commandos. Having the Red Marley as a hub makes the game feel more congruent.The difficulty has been toned down significantly from the previous games, even on the hardest mode. This is one of many things that was done to make the game more broadly appealing, but I would be lying if I said I didn't miss the enemy setups that you used to have to watch and ponder over to develop a plan.The studio has announced that this will be its last game; bad news for gamer's and the game industry as a whole. Although, maybe I'll actually be able to get some work done now.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Mimimi's weakest entry.Feels like the game was either extremely rushed, or had like a third of the budget of Desperados.The tone is much lighter and cringier than the previous entries, which at least tried to tell an engaging story. Here it's every pirate cliche in existence (curse, treasure, zombie monkey, etc). And everyone's just so... carefree, like there's nothing at stake.Instead of carefully constructed backstories for each character, shown during actual gameplay, we have some banter between the characters and "Crew tales" which are 2-minute micro-quests for each character where they don't interact with the party at all, just with the ship.Since the missions were designed to be completed with any combination of characters, none of them feel important. None feel unique. Most have an enemy reposition mechanic, a jump over things mechanic, a long range attack, etc. All very repetitive. Different flavors of the same thing. And speaking of repetitive, OH BOY! No longer are maps done when you finish the mission, you must revisit previously completed maps MULTIPLE TIMES. This is legit my biggest problem. It's so boring. It makes no sense in-game why I fully depopulate an island, and the next time i get there, it's fully populated again, with all the guards in the SAME place as last time. Did they not find the cadavers? I quit the game half-way through the 3'rd ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ time on the same map. Same enemies, same patrol routes, same placement, same bushes, only difference is sometimes it's night. The lack of care and polish is fully on display. All the encounters feel extremely similar, even on different maps.I love these RTT games, and the hand-crafted levels and encounter design they had to offer in previous titles, I'm sad no one else is making Commandos-like games. Here, Mimimi goes out with a whimper rather than a bang. RIP
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the DEMO and I was hooked. I bought the full game and I am loving it.The only main off bit is sometimes the selection of items in the world, but nothing I cannot pass over.Overall this is a very good game, I highly recommend. The game play is solid and the sound design and voice overs are very cool.Hats off for the team!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the Commandos series always but only in theory because the setting wasn't really mine. Now with undead pirates and some magic skills shenanigans I am really digging this kind of game. The banter of the characters is nice, the story is fun to follow, the music is very shanty-esk all the time, whats not to like. And the save system can make the game very forgiving if you are into that. But it can be a challenge, too, if you want it to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished the vanilla story questline. Overall, this is the most complex game from Mimimi Studios compared to Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics.The new mechanics make it quite easy to clear out a stage by selecting a crew whose skills complement each other perfectly (sometimes a little too well). My MVPs are Suledy (the ship's doctor) and Theresa (the sniper). With these two and another random crew member, I could easily clear out the main objective without any difficulty, even without upgrading their powers. Suledy's bush ability is just too convenient, allowing her to hide herself and any enemy she takes down. Theresa's most useful skill is shooting dust to reduce enemy sight from a super long range. Combining these two skills makes the game feel like "Easy Mode."In my experience, selecting random crews makes the game more challenging.I definitely  will buy the two DLCs when it is on sale later.Since Mimimi Studios has closed, I hope the talented individuals behind this game can continue to deliver more titles in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Mimimi's Stealth Strategy Game,I love it so much, the operation system is getting smoother and more user-friendly comparing to Desperados III & Shadow Tactics.Also I like how they added new elements to the game to make it more playable (E.g. Flexible team choice, character stories)The only thing I don't like is the art.Game design is good but it'd be great if there's good looking characters...Goodbye Mimimi, hope we'll meet again in the future :'(
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but it feels too much like the developer's last two games, Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3. It's almost like playing the same game again. The enemies are nearly the same, and it still relies on the quick save-load feature a lot. The gameplay and character abilities are nearly identical as well. The only big difference is you can choose which missions to do first and which characters to bring. If you're looking for something new in this genre, you'll be disappointed. I'd only recommend this game for people who haven't played the earlier games from this developer, or for those who don't mind more of the same thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. So well designed. With each combination of characters you find new ways of how to approach the missions. Good music, good graphics and pirates!! Arrrr.... I can play it for hours. Just bought both add-ons for some extra fun and to reward the sun-setting developer team for their great work. Farewell and thank you Mimimi. I wish you all the best on you future endeavors.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to the stealth RPG genre but now I'm hooked. Every single level has it's unique challenge and since you can choose which characters to play, there's an infinite possibility of strategies to solve the puzzles. Gameplay is smooth and the story keeps you interested. Definitely recommend if you're looking for a strategy game!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Undead pirates ? Hmm... 8 characters? I don`t know... It is Mimimi! So, yes!!And I was not disappointed, another masterpiece in my opinion.You start with the character, who turns out to keep it all together and have to earn to  "revive" the rest of your crew by solving missions, exploring more and more islands.This is build up very wise, it is up to you, whom you wish to add to your crew next, you get all information about this character beforehand and even have a training deck, where you can practice the special abilities.And what fun abilities!! John for example: not to be spotted, he can use his anker and disappears into the deep and then can pop up on an enemy`s position to drag him down or distract him with his fish companion Reginald.I was worried first to be overwhelmed by having 8 characters, but besides of the finale and one other mission I recall, you always take only 3 characters with you, but having 8 characters to choose from is fantastic to built up great synergies.The whole story is so well put together - during the main story you have special missions for each character, very fitting and often touching.I very much enjoyed the crew tales too, where you have the option to choose one character for a special story on board.Very well written, funny and touching again and perfect to relax between the challenging missions.I usually don`t play stealth games, but Mimimi games are always special, for everybody who loves strategy, loveable characters, good and funny writing. Not to forget the fantastic (english) voice actors (all very good and fitting, but especially Sakana and Gertrude to me) - a combination I rarely found elsewhere.Thank you Mimimi , Iam looking forward to the DLC`s and still hope to see more some day in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of this type of strategy game, this is a must have. It's fun and engaging and the story is well done. I've enjoyed every minute of it.edit: I'm not usually much of a competitionist, but after beating the main game I've found myself still having a blast going back and finishing the badges. Usually I find doing that to be a slog, and some of them were, but overall, earning Vergilio and trying to 100% every one and everything is still enjoyable. Nearly 200 hours at this point with DLC, and I'm still having fun puzzling things out.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible. I'm a big fan of the Mimimi stealth games and was excited for this even when I thought it would be a magic piratey rehash of the previous games. I did NOT expect as huge of a formula change-up as they did here. This is Shadow Tactics on crack and then some. It's straight dopamine shot through my withered brain.If Desperadoes 3 disappointed you because most of the characters are just ability shuffles of Shadow Tactics characters (personally still loved that one), this is for you. Interesting characters with sick new abilities, fun personalities, and cool ass designs. The abilities from Desperados 3 are mostly still here, but feel like bread and butter next to some of the meaty new stuff.Also, the Japanese skeleton cook says "Hesitation is defeat." 12/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm new to the stealth tactics genre entirely, but this game is really fun. It's a bummer that the developers closed up shop shortly after releasing such a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is still pretty darn cool and creative, as expected of a Mimimi game. The characters' personalities and stories are a big step back however, Desperados and Shadow Tactics runs circles around it in those departments. Which is kind of a shame, because who doesn't love a ghost pirate story? Anyway, I still recommend this, but I don't think I'll be replaying this one - I'd rather play Shadow Tactics again.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: This is another and very unfortunately the last great game from Mimimi Games. And while I mostly enjoyed the game I can not recommend it, when comparing to Shadow Tactics or Desperados. In several parts of the game it feels way to repetitive and just like grind. All crew members are aquired in the exact same way: travel to the same island twice and collect a pearl and energy - that's it. They reveal some of their background story in the captains tasks, but that could have been so much better and way more interessting.The second point that I disliked is the map design. If you get to an island for different missions they are like at least 90% the same and while most maps are quite large, you only need to access a small portion. Also the freedom of selecting characters and then only three of them for each mission  made the maps to easy, because it's required to work in many ways. That in the end leads to playing the same tactic again and again and not really using all characters. Of cause you can try different things and play around, but you want to get things done (especially on highest difficutly) then you'll have some favourite characters and you'll stick to them.Which leads to the last point: some characters are just sooo much more powerful than others. Especially teleporting, instant hiding of bodies or creating cover anywhere are just to op. That create bush thing should at least be restricted to soil ground or something, but you spawn a bush on a wall or inside of a building and guards don't even care. In my opinion less is sometimes more, I would have prefered the game with a straight story, where levels are finished one after another and I would not even mind playing a level twice when the setup would have been different, like one level invading the Inquisitions Citadel and the next being trapped in the end while enemies are in high alert, insteat of slaughtering everyone, just to return a second later and everything there is just as the first time.All in all I want to thank Mimimi for their great games, each of them is very unique and technically in an extremely good state, I hope another company will emerge to continue their legacy and keep the RTT genre alive.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolutely awesome game by Mimimi. It`s great to see how the devs matured from Shadow Tactics, going through Desperados III, Aiko`s choice to this one. If you`ve played any of those, like the setting and enjoyed the mechanics, absolutely get this one. If you haven`t played any of them but think it`s your kind of game, start by this masterpiece, I envy you.Once again, great work devs, proud to support such a great team!Cheers!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: First off, if I had known Sweet Baby Inc. was involved with this game I'd have never bought it. However since I did and now I'm  past the time limit to return, I'll probably put in a few more hours. So far though it's very underwhelming. Loved D3 and ST but this is just a step down in almost every way. Story is boring me to death so far. Artwork is not nearly as good previous titles and the voice acting sounds ridiculous. I've been skipping the dialog because it is just cringe. You could tell after 20 minutes SBI was involved and that probably ruined the game as much as anything. The game is just silly and a big let down. If this is the direction Mimimi was going then I say good riddance.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has played Mimimi's other stealth tactical strategy games (Desperados III and Shadow Tactics) will absolutely love this game.  Anyone who hasn't played those games, will still love Shadow Gambit.  Extremely high production values, funny dialogue, great characters, and challenging puzzles await as you solve the pirate mystery.Fully 10/10 recommendation on this one, and that's a rare recommendation these days when even the best AAA games leave you wanting.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with a few flaws. Firstly I would buy first Shadow Tactics or Desperados III first. Their story and game play differ from this a lot and a way better story.Negatives- I personally don't like the 3 person team mechanic.- Story is kind of meh.- Multiple characters but they basically got same talents.Good- Talents are interesting and fun- A good number of missions- "Big Guys" are easier to takedown. I like this change
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: A great successor to their previous stealth tactical game. Here are a few things that I disliked:- Following the stupid trend of giving the user many options and making the progress too dynamic-- Ability to select entrance to the map-- Ability to select exit of the map-- Ability to select hero to play the map-- Ability to unlock characters in almost any order-- Ability to see backstory of characters in any order-- Ability to choose mission and side missionNot a fan of the above. IMO splitting the game flow in all these aspects takes away part of the story's charm. The story is forced to be splitable and the dialogues are forced to be generic, so that nothing "out of context" is said as the story pieces come together. Nevertheless, the game has a great story, my point is that its flow would be better if user's interference was taken out. The majority of games where the user decides how the story progresses suffer from small talk when the dialogues cover the dynamic parts, making it poor.Another thing I disliked are the "crew tales", as most of them are silly filler "missions". Still, I must admit I was touched by Gaelle's poetry on the crew tale, even more than on her mirror missions.Generally though, the mirror missions were a meaningful backstory addition for the crew members, I liked those.Many badges to do a full completion of the game, I love and hate this at the same time, most probably will hate it by the time I'm finished hehe, maybe it can be more enjoyable if I take a break before going for completion.Now, on the bright side, the game is full of interesting characters, both allies and enemies have rich character development. It has beautiful scenery, smart and wonderful character skills/abilities. It gave me exactly what I expected from gameplay's perspective. I'd never expect to have 8 characters and none being too boring to play. The music is great, though I didn't like the lyrics on that pirate song, I found the rhymes a bit weak and weirdly positioned.Definitely suggested and definitely going for completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a step backwards from Desperados 3.The level design in Desperados was tight; the situations you had to solve had you scratching your head; the level designer knew exactly what characters and abilities you had and you had to come up with something tricky with these.In Shadow Gambit however you can be at any point with any combination of characters and abilities and everything feels pointless; there are so many ways to resolve every situation; it totally lost me. It's overall just more of the same; the same game for the third time is one too many.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: What a beauty of Stealth Tactics game. I knew we could leave this genre to Mimimi but I didn't expect it to be this good. Everything is just great. The subject with pirates, the dialogues, the voice acting& characters. But mostly the newest styles of killing enemies. VERY well done!Played the demo, now 3 hours into the next levels. It's already a classic.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent work by Mimimi Games. I absolutely loved playing this game after grinding Shadow Tactics + DLC and Desperados III for countless hours. Although I was sceptical with the pirate scenario in the first place and had to get used to the game during the demo I am amazed by the end product. The skill tree, the side missions and character development + the amount of jokes during the conversations...and of course the huge number of different possibilities due to char variety/skill variety - super good!I can wholeheartedly recommend this piece of beauty, it's worth every penny! Sad to hear that this is the last game from Mimimi. <3I rate this game with 95 points out of 100. My only two points of criticism: 1. The final mission wasn't my kind of thing and I couldn't motivate for days/weeks to end the game. 2. I would have loved to see more maps rather than repeating some of them 3-4 times for progress.Advice: I would call myself veteran by now in those games. So, if you are experienced as well start the game on the highest difficulty. I did so and some maps/situations were still easy to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: A unique game. It is a casual game that you place your pirate in bushes, setup ambushes, and hide bodies (if you want). Each one of the crew has abilities and different ways to use them. Some of them swim and climb but other, not so much. It is fun if you want the prefect run because of the quick save.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: This ... was (and still is as I still have a lot more to complete) ... an absolutely wonderful game. As per my other reviews of Shadow Tactics and Desperados III, Shadow Gambit just keeps on building on the already beautiful engine and made even more great with random stuff like Crew Tales and the story is amazing. This is an absolute must have game. Can't wait for the next game from Mimimi as they are absolutely owning this Commandos genre. Been a massive Commandos fan since it came out and replayed and finished that multiple times as a classic ... but Shadow Tactics has been out for 7 years already ... so I'm starting to think that also falls into the classic category now being such a great start to this engine for Mimimi and definitely deserving a replay ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Characters 10/10: Some of the characters followed tropes, but ultimately they all felt rounded and entertaining. I found myself deeply caring about some of them and every conversation lent to a few laughs. The script was spot on when it came to character.Story 5/10: This is the area that will feel the most lacking. On the one hand, the story was pretty average. I found it interesting and well written, but it didn't keep me up at night. Missions also took long enough that I didn't always notice right away when story beats referenced something said or done before because it had been a while since the reference point happened.Combat 9/10: The gameplay is centered around stealth take downs rather than combat. Unlike most stealth strategy games, you can take your time and one small mistake doesn't ruin your entire stealth. I thoroughly enjoyed all the options for analysis that made me feel incredibly smart when I pulled off something difficult. The reason this rating is 9 instead of 10 is because there were times when missions brought you back to the same location to do something different, and while the purpose of that was to give you a chance to experiment with a different team, it would've flowed better if we had the option of performing both tasks during the same mission.World 7/10: Much of the world layout is standard, but each of the islands you visit has some lore and background attached to it that I found greatly interesting.I enjoyed every minute I played this game. I think it's great if you like stealth strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic tactical stealth game. It's amazing how they allow for so many solutions to tackle the same problem. My way of completing a level will be different than the next player, or even another playthrough, and that makes this game so incredible.Outside of the gameplay, the characters were enjoyable, the story was straight forward, and audio of abilities were solid. I am not usually a fan of stealth games, but enjoy tactical games. I think if you enjoy either stealth or tactical games (doesn't need to be both), then this game is an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Desperados 3 and/or Shadow Tactics, you will like this one. I think the other two are better, but this is still great. The reason why I think the other two are better is mainly because this game is too easy. Some characters are way over powered and you can select them with every mission. There is not a designated character for a specific mission. Even when playing a pirate specific tale, you can bring along two more over powered characters. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This is for those save scumming pirates who's in for some hilarious fantastical pirates in real time stealth tactics game.I have so far bought every Mimimi games and played over 100 hours each of the game to get 100% on all of their games except this one so far (88% by the time of this writing) and I think this is the best game they have so far by building upon its predecessors. The previous two iteration of stealth tactics game, Shadow Tactics and Desperado III had save features but this is the game where they actually considered why this is part of the game from the narrative and I love how they used it to the central part of the story. if you are looking to get all the badges in this game, get ready to smash that F5 and F8 quite a bit.The previous games had 5 characters and shared very similar features, the quick one, elusive, sniper, infiltrator and the strong one. This time there are 8 characters to select your load out for most of the scenarios and their duo or trio combination are quite unique. For instance, Quentin and Gaelle has pretty neat trick of getting places without climbing ivies or ladders. Terresa and Pinkus has interesting snipe and hide bodies combination. The developers at Mimimi games have done fantastic job at creating compelling characters and in this game they have a stellar job of bringing their characters to un-life with their backgrounds, side stories and character development that ties to the main story. I really enjoyed how the characters evolve over time. nor, niscule sgivingsSo far I praised the game and there are some features I would like it to have it improved, There are certain times the camera zoom in and out was bit too extreme and tossed me off to the different part of the map or bugs where camera position was or never ending alert because a guard was stuck in a door and cannot be killed or leave because he was sure the door was a accursed. these are minor things in I've encountered in my near 40 hour play so far and nothing really break the game for me. Thank you Mimimi games for this delightful game!

_childDocuments_.review: More of the great formula of Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, now in a pirate setting. _childDocuments_.review: I LOVED Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, and was hoping this one would live up to those standards. Unfortunately, this game really let me down. The characters just feel like generic pirates set in a generic pirate world on a quest to do generic (fantasy) pirate things. The art and character designs are great, but they're just boring on the whole.Gameplay wise, at least from what I played, it feels too easy. The characters you get at the start have really powerful skills that make it easy to get past any obstacle with relatively little planning. The quick save reminders might also contribute to making the game feel easier than it is. There are some good level designs, but it feels like a downgrade from the constant tension you'd feel when playing the other games from this dev... or maybe it felt like that to me because I didn't care about what happened to the story or characters.The pirate ship/hub world feels like a waste of time. It's basically a chore you have to do to start the next mission, whereas Desperados for example had a simple menu where you could just use your mouse. I get why they'd feel the need to add a pirate ship to a pirate game, but a hub world offers nothing to this type of game. Shadow Gambit isn't awful, but it's hard to recommend when Shadow Tactics and/or Desperados 3 would be much better ways to spend your time. If you already played those and REALLY want some more, maybe you'll enjoy this better than I did. Otherwise, play the other games. Those are fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: While a worthy successor to D3 and Blades of the Shogun, Shadow Gambit lacks some of the charm and concentrated pacing that made it's predecessors iconic. What it does right: character variety, attention to narrative, and progression. Shadow Gambit ups the playable character count (in main game) to 8 and they each have a somewhat fleshed out story to tell. This allows the player to explore multiple backgrounds instead of focusing on just one main character's arc. Furthermore, the gameplay is solid - as always from Mimimi - with varied abilities and head-scratching encounters. New to the series is a very shallow but welcome progression system in the form of ability upgrades which helped to spice things up when it started to get stale.What it did wrong: "open" maps, lack of enemy variety, and lack of challenge. All of these factors ultimately made for a nearly 35hr main story which ended up overstaying it's welcome. While the core gameplay loop is extremely addictive and polished, the game's re-use of open maps paired with only 7-8 types of enemies got repetitive after 20-ish hours. In addition to that, the mission party size is maxed at 3 for basically the entire game which really limits the complexity of most encounters. Previous games let you take control of 4+ characters per mission which allowed for much more creativity to tackle various challenges.Look, there's no denying Shadow Gambit is an extremely optimized and satisfying game to play. The setting and vibrant colors are a huge upgrade from past titles. The story is not earth-shattering but there is plenty of narrative content to keep the player busy. Personally, I would've been satisfied if this game was roughly half its current length but most folks prefer more content rather than less and I respect that. The main problem suffered by this title is it's lack of linearity and therefore, challenge. It's still a fantastic title deserving of its $40 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: Ninjas, cowboys and now pirates! Mimimi Games never fails to disappoint, and they have successfully carved their niche with their line of top-tier stealth strategy games over the years.Shadow Gambit is no different from its predecessors, and in fact improves upon the tried-and-tested formula, introducing non-linearity to several aspects of the game, such as mission progression, character selection, and level entry/exit. This creates a sandbox that allows players to truly play their own way, and Shadow Gambit only benefits from this expansion of freedom.On top of that, Shadow Gambit introduces character upgrades, the first in a Mimimi stealth-strategy game. Each character in Shadow Gambit can be upgraded once, unlocking some kind of new ability, which players can even disable, and renable, if they so choose.Shadow Gambit was the next step in the right direction for Mimimi Games, and it is such a pity that it will be their last game. Thank you Mimimi!

_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: At this time I cannot fully endorse the way Mimimi is heading. Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew plays easier than previous Mimimi tactical stealth games. The lore is a bit burdensome and long while still being skippable. Previous games had a story that was much more acceptable so to say that it doesn't impact playing the game in a negative way. It feels like skipping makes you miss the lore/story but following it completely and watching/listening to everything will (at my current expectation) result in a story line completion time of 1:2 with 1 part watching lore. The RPG part (boat/hub with side stories) feels somewhat unnecessary but perhaps I'm just not into that as much as others would be. Some characters are way too overpowered, I've completed several missions with like 85% use of only one character while also finishing the mission in just over 15 minutes on my first play through. As an experienced Mimimi games player and a tactical stealth game fan this game is a disappointment while not being bad at all. That being said I'm now a little over 6 hours in. And have opened up 11(!) tickets for in-game issues/problems that could've been squashed completely by simply play testing it. I do not remember other Mimimi games being this rough around the edges on release. I do not experience any game breaking bugs but I would personally recommend to hold off for now and perhaps play this game in a month or two when they hopefully fixed some annoying bugs. In the end it somewhat feels rushed (compared to the previous games) but has that nice feeling to it. If you liked previous Mimimi games this will suit you just fine, the price is fair (so far) but I have doubts about the way Mimimi is heading with this. I will update this review when I finish the story line and when I 100% complete the game.**UPDATE** at 10 hours:It feels to me that Mimimi tried to knead (or push) the game towards a stealth tactic game with RPG elements. Such as: the choice which members you revive first and which you bring to a mission. But apart from the choice of revival order of your crew members there isn't much actual choices to be made. Let me explain. To revive you need an item and 'energy' and to get that you need to complete specific missions. But in act 1 and early act 2 you don't really get a choice which missions you want to complete. You unlock like five islands but it's all locked by a specific mission order. So you get a feeling of making your own path but it's actually predetermined by Mimimi which is completely fine since the previous games did that just great but you get to see the carrot of choice while actually having a choice. You can also do some side lore semi-missions to get some background on your crew members, but you can only do one mini-mission on the ship/hub in between two missions so it's paced for you. Furthermore the item and the 'energy' required to revive characters is also paced for you in the same matter. Specific missions give this and you can't really deviate from the mapped out path. Last but not least for now is that you can (must) complete multiple missions on the same island in sequence. But the lore part on the ship doesn't feel to add much for me to remove yourself (from the pirate perspective ..) from the island to return in the night to find the item on the same island you just cleared moments ago. Just stay on the island and pickup the item as well. It somewhat feels like a cheap way to reuse the islands to reduce development time while creating a bigger game. I think this wouldn't be as bad if the return to the same island wasn't the next mission afterwards (it happened multiple times now) but after like 4 or 5 missions. It also is noticeable that 90% of the enemies are exactly the same and have exactly the same pathing and positioning for a 'new' mission on the same island. At this time I'm changing my view on the game, I would recommend against buying it, my views on this might change again in the future if I finish more or complete the game, it doesn't feel that good for the 40€ (-10% opening discount) I paid.**UPDATE** at 30 hours:So 20 hours later I've finished all missions, the story but there still is some lore left due to the fact that you cannot complete the ship intermission lore (mini-quests) one after an other but need to switch it up with a normal mission. Following the in-game global statistics I've played a little over 20 hrs. The other 10 hrs is cut scenes, lore and I guess the ship intermission lore mini-quests (bear in mind 30 hrs of actual play and not idling menu's and taking breaks). If you don't really dig those parts they are completely skippable (space for a full skip or enter for a text line skip). The same points still count: it's somewhat lacking, it could be more. The multiple missions on the same island do not feel repetitive on the bigger islands. But this is purely because the missions only use a part of the islands and thus are not really repeating the same parts of the islands again. Only the most advanced missions of the mirror-missions and let's say the last 2 story-line missions are actually big and in depth. Most missions of the game can be completed with one character with a help of a second for some specific cases. Especially the more overpowered characters are a somewhat sore sight and give the game a more entry-level feeling on normal difficulty. Increasing the difficulty doesn't increase the depth of the game but merely makes it more troublesome but still somewhat shallow.I enjoyed playing this game after all, while I'm still of the opinion that it is a step down from the previous Mimimi games! Nevertheless if you enjoyed those I would recommend playing this game as well. Mimimi recently posted a news update that they will close their studios. Due to that and considering the fact that a reader of this review probably has resisted the urge to buy this game so far. I would suggest to wait for a nice Steam sale. The only ones that will actually benefit from more (and higher) revenue are the owners of Mimimi and Steam. While they both can make a nice buck in my opinion we players of games have little use direct or indirect of that. Would I recommend this game to people that have played previous Mimimi games? Yes. Would I recommend this game to people that based on trailers/gameplay and reviews are interested in this game? Yes. But in both cases if you can resists the FOMO I would strongly recommend to put it on your wishlist and buy this game in a future sale. **UPDATE** at 35 hours:Got all achievements and finished all lore, doesn't really add much to be honest, and I'm somewhat disappointed that more badge completion isn't required for 100% achievements like previous Mimimi games were.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike previous Mimimi games Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics, in which their characters have exactly the same abilities and are just re-skins of each other, one in Japan and another in Wild-West, Shadow Gambit brings new abilities that we didn't use in previous ones. Also, the fact that the game lets you pick which character to use is another positive thing in this one compared to previous Mimimi games. Along with that, the game has more entertaining stealth situations.But the only thing I don't like about this game is that it's far easier compared to Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics. Even at the highest level of difficulty, I need way more challenge. The reason that the game is easier is because character abilities are OP and also because enemy soldiers stand up on the map with high distances together, so it's easy to kill them without noticing others. It's the only negative point about Shadow Gambit, but it's very enjoyable for fans of the RTT genre. I hope Mimimi Developers can revive their studio and publish more games.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Mimimi game. seemingly the game core was born from the question, "how can we make really unique abilities while still feeling like a great real time strategy game". There answer, Magic Pirates.  This sold me on the game as i have always been a sucker for magic and they deliver. Keeping the general feel of their stealth RTS games with familiar mechanics and skills with new inventive powers that offer new paths to how you complete your objectives.With a great soundtrack as found in all of their games you get a songs that fit in both old world pirate swashbuckling feel and the spiritual of their new world. New to the games is  hub area were one can interact with your fellow crew members getting to know them and if you are so inclined do there wonderfully written side story's.  With the great styled art of their mystical Caribbean setting and their foundation on great game play systems with fun new twists  it its a recipe for a great game. I would highly recommend to those new to the genre and those familiar for the interesting takes on abilities that can be found from the colourful crew found aboard the Red  Marley.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfectly distilled stealth game that thrives on creativity, ingenuity, and planning from the player to succeed. All wrapped up in a surprisingly compelling story with an excellent cast of characters. Seriously, if you've ever found yourself enjoying games like Hitman or Splinter Cell, this game scratches nearly all of the same itches despite its different perspective. Often times, it does it even better than those games ever could. I'm sad we will never see another true follow-up from Mimimi games, but what a hell of a game to go out on.I should also point out the sheer value here. The game is a budget title already, regularly on sale for 20/25 dollars, but a single playthrough will easily run you 30 hours. This is all killer and no filler content as well, even though not every mission is technically a "new" location, you're often exploring small parts of larger maps so each mission feels brand new. Then, once it is all done, there is an extensive end-game of challenges and treasure hunts, with a tantalizing reward which I won't spoil. I, personally, was happy to leave the game where its story ended, but if you're looking for a game you can play for hundreds of hours, Shadow Gambit has both the content and mechanical complexity to make that possible.Oh, and it works great on Steam Deck. What's not to love?
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I held off on writing this review because I knew this would be the last game published by Mimimi and I wanted to play all the available content (main game, DLCs, treasure hunts) before reviewing it.Having played every stealth strategy game of Mimimi and being a fan of the genre for many years now, I can say that Shadow Gambit blew me away with how it managed to evolve the genre.Let's start from the beginning though.THE BEST-In Shadow Gambit, you take control of a cursed pirate crew venturing in many missions in classic stealth style. This is something that has been seen before in the past.The new thing here is the presence of a HUB of sorts (your pirate ship aka Red Marley) where you can see your crew hanging out after each mission and interact with them. This not only acts as a nice break from the tense game missions, but it also gives you an understanding of the personality of each crew member.-Each crew member has a personal quest, which is irrelevant to the main story and is there for ♥♥♥♥♥ and giggles. Most of the time it's quite non-sensical, but it manages to get you hooked nonetheless. I personally enjoyed watching the tale of a mere fish trying to become a ninja assassin, while mentoring it with Toya, the ship's cook.-As I mentioned before, Shadow Gambit evolved the game formula in many ways. Where in the previous games if you wanted to attack someone, tie the body, pick it up and hide it in a bush you needed to press 3 buttons, now you can do so just by holding the left click. This saves time in a game where time is crucial and even half a second can be the difference between a perfectly executed combo or a total fiesta.-Each crew has a distinct skillset and identity. That's not to say that every member of the crew is equally powerful or useful, but that there is a huge pool of characters and skills that fits every playstyle. Furthermore, since your crew starts dead and you have to ressurect them one by one, you can try ressurecting them in a different order in a new game save for an entirely different experience.-Each character has a skill that can be upgraded if the necessary conditions are met. There is an energy bar which gets filled slowly after each successful mission. This gives you the option to select which crew members you want to upgrade first and some of the upgrades are very essential for the characters (and borderline OP in some cases, I'm looking at you Pinkus and Gaelle...). You need 25 energy for each upgrade and by default you get +1 energy when completing a mission and +1 for each crew member in your team. Or more if they have been sitting for a while in the Marley. Which brings us to...-You can select the characters you want to have in your team in the beginning of each mission. With the exception of a few missions where one character is by default included in the team, for the rest of the missions you can customize your whole team. This compliments playstyle diversity and the experience between two people playing the same mission can be entirely different as a result. In my opinion, this is one of the most important features of the game and I cannot praise it enough. Of course you can just spam the same (most powerful) crew members in each mission, but as mentioned in the above point you will get less energy and thus delay the upgrades of your crew. -MOD and scenario editor to create our own exciting missions as a parting gift from Mimimi. THE GOOD-The environments are interesting and unique and every island you visit feels different. Furthermore, there is a variety of enemies (6 in total) with each one requiring a different approach to beat them.-The voice acting is very good and immersive, and the banter of two NPC crew members while on the Marley can be entertaining to watch.-Even though the graphics are not top priority in this kind of games, here they are more than satisfactory, with the cartoon-ey vibe fitting perfectly with the whole undead pirate theme.-Save scumming is not just something that you can spam until you execute a perfect combo, but it's implemented in the game in a seamless way and even in the story, making it more than just a feature of the genre.-Yuki and Kuma from Shadow Tactics are back! And Dragon's Dream island looks so beautiful. -Treasure hunts are a nice free addition to  the game, which serve as small challenges that can be completed in a short time. THE NOT SO GOOD(Of course the game is not without its flaws, but do not let this distract you. Even with these flaws, it's an amazing game.)-The dialogues. Compared to the previous games (Shadow Tactics and Desperados III) where in dialogues you had the character models interacting with each other, here Mimimi opted for static images of the characters with boxed speech (more like a comic book). This is a step down compared to the previous games.-The game's difficulty tends to be more on the easier side. One of the things I personally enjoy about stealth strategy games is how difficult they can be and how it forces you to find the perfect plan and the perfect timing to execute it. While the difficulty of the planning part is somewhat lowered by default, since you can choose your team and not have the game forcing you to play in a certain way with certain fixed characters. But for the timing part, I believe they could get away with being more strict since you can already save some time with the simplification of controls as I said above. One thing that should not be present is the pausing of the game when in Shadow Mode. In Desperados, when playing in the highest difficulty, the game was not paused when you were using Shadow Mode and this should have been the case here as well.-Some crew members are (inevitably) more powerful than others. Of course, in the previous games there was a character that was overpowered compared to the rest (i.e. Isabelle in Desperados III), but they tried to have the rest of the characters balanced out by giving them different features. For example, Kate in Desperados was one of the more useful characters since she could infiltrate anywhere when she had her disguise and she could reduce the viewcone of every guard. But to compensate she had only non-lethal melee attack and she could not tie someone after she had knocked them out. Furthermore, she had different speed on her attack skill and movement and her pistol had a significantly shorter range. Here, all the characters have the same movement and attack speed (with the exception of Suleidy and Toya), this makes the characters that have a strong feature standing out even more. Of course, once you unlock the last (hidden) crew member the game becomes a walk in the park, but thankfully to do so you need 85% game completion so it's almost at the endgame.-The story was... well, it just was there I guess. I have played this game for 95 hours and I'm still not sure I have entirely understood its story. The main villain is a whiny b**** most of the time and the non-sensical time bending mumbo jumbo does not help in making this any easier. Of course, story is not the main reason for playing these games, but it's nice when you have a solid story (Desperados III) or a really great one (Shadow Tactics).-The missions are island based. This means that you may have to go back to a specific island you have already visited to play a mission with a different objective, but on the same map and with same enemy placement as before. This can make the game a bit repetitive, but thankfully this does not happen more than 3 times per island.VERDICT: 8.5/10All in all, despite the above flaws, the game is a masterpiece and definitely an addition to any stealth strategy fan's collection.You can see the love the developers had for the genre when making this game and it's honestly a shame that we won't ever see another game from them.Thank you Mimimi for such an amazing game and for all the amazing games you have offered us in the past!

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Tactics is one of my favorite games of all time. When Desperados III came out, I already felt there was kind of a downgrade in the difficulty. Honestly, with Shadow Gambit even more. That doesn't mean I don't like it, I think this game is litteraly the culmination of all the crafts the studio acquired making the two previous games : you can really feel they mastered the arts of creating compelling and enjoyable characters to play, great wordbuilding and solid story. The multiple islands across the map are unique and more detailed than ever.Now the "openworldness" of this game makes the strategy feel less hard to put in place. In some moments there was a lack of ennemies, this is even more present when you have to go through almost empty areas to go to your objectives. Bigger doesn't mean better, especially in stealth games. Give me more little maps but packed with guards that are really thoughtfully placed, make me believe I could never figure it out ( maybe I'm exaggerating a little but you see the point ) Shadow Tactics alsmost felt like a puzzle, each pieces unlocking another as you put in the right strategies in place, and that's what I felt missed in Gambit in some parts.The problem could also come from too much characters with so many powers, so too many strategies to think when creating the levels, resulting in feeling a lack in difficulty / ennemies. A thing I didn't liked is the Marley save reminder, good thing we can turn it off in the settings because I hate being "taken by the hand" in games. Failing and missing to save is part of it, so let people fail and learn, don't remind them every five minutes they need to save.Still very great, this opus confirms Mimimi as one of the new leading indie studios in my opinion, and I'm sure they are going to experiment different things for each new game, my only wish is they would focus a little more on really thinking about the strategy and add more difficulty for future games.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 80 hours I reached 101% completion on Cursed (still some badges to go though).All in all it is a great game that extends Mimimi's portfolio by their next iteration on this genre. It keeps what is good and adds some new features.The best aspect is the diversity of abilities in the characters. I love how versatile Gaelle's Kanol on its own is or how much you can do with Quentin's fishing rod. That (in most cases) you can only take up to three characters on a mission is a perfect limitation to incentivise experimentation and strategy.However, there are a few albeit severe negative points, which I would have liked to see solved after the third iteration:-  Noises are too inconsistent. They work too much FOR the player, not enough against them. Most prominently, you can RUN past an enemy over a wooden surface and they do not notice. Please let running make noise (like when carrying a body). Making it dependent on the surface gives level designers more degrees of freedom for creating challenges. And WHY does Gaelles Kanol NOT make a huge noise when firing?...Please...That borders onto stupid...-  Bushes were one of the big additions to Mimimi's games and they are great. However, I have the feeling, that there were too many of them scattered around considering how powerful they are (Hiding inside, cover behind them, hiding infinite bodies), with no real downside to them. I would suggest two/three features: 1) Bind the cover density to the difficulty level. With less cover, the player has to plan ahead and adapt to enemy movement more. 2) Make it that characters moving into, out of or inside a bush notifies guards watching it at that moment. I got this idea by seeing how papers fly around when I jumped someone into a pile of papers. It would take away some of flawlessness of covers. 3) Maybe make it, that guards can burn down bushes when they see someone walking in. I sometimes heard them comment "We should have burned these weeds" and thought "Yes, why not?". There can still be covers that cannot be removed, but "One-Time-Use" covers seem to be a worthwile thought.-  Actually my biggest point - While there are new types with the Kindred and Iudex (Prognosticar being the Samurai/Longcoat as the "You need two"-type), I feel like Mimimi has to be more bold when innovating on enemies. A fictional setting like this is perfect for introducing all kinds of enemies with weird or fantastical abilities that pose awesome challenges onto the players. Some examples I thought of are: 1) Inspired by the custodes and the dogs from D3, a guard that is "blind", thus immune to visual distraction, but recognizes characters in a 360 circle around it even in cover and behind walls or above/below it, walking towards them if possible and alarming when very close. 2) An "Anti-Custodes" that triggers a delayed spell upon takedown, temporarily knocking out all player characters around it, so that it has to be taken out from range or the player cannot stay around until the spell has popped. 3) A "hitman" that spawns every once in a while and permanently tracks down the nearest character to kill them. Moves slowly but can climb and swim, so that the situation becomes more dynamic. 4) A guard that projects a shield either to specific enemies or to all enemies in a radius, so they become immune to attacks until the shield guard is taken out.I enjoyed this game so much that I hope that Mimimi's next installment will be even more bold, more innovative and more challenging by providing more tools to the enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: Have to say I'm disappointed,  I was pleasantly surprised when randomly saw this game close to release (I haven't been following much gaming news lately) but was put off a bit by the art style. Now, after playing for several hours, I can look past that, however, level design is really really shallow compared to their previous games that I really loved - Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3. It's fine or probably even necessary to innovate, however for this particular genre I think sacrificing level design is not the right way, the levels I've played so far have been significantly shorter and easier than previous games, while the "open world" side of things doesn't really add to the experience, and felt almost tedious. I was considerably less engaged with both the story and the characters at this point compared to their previous games. I may come back to finish the game at some point, but sadly it's just not that exciting to me.You may enjoy or even prefer this one but if you want a "true" stealth tactics game, I'd really recommend their previous games.

_childDocuments_.review: Fans of the old fashioned real time strategy in the style of Desperado and Commandos will be well served with this colourful, pirate themed entry. For those new to this sort of thing, they will find a fun game that presents combat in the form of a series of puzzles to solve, forcing you to use your magical powered, undead pirates to isolate, outsmart and kill masses of enemies.The game is somewhat easier and more accessible than older titles in a similar mould, even with the difficulty turned up to max. This is not a negative however, as the sometimes torturous difficulty of those older games I mentioned are a real turn off. Overall, its a better balanced and less tedious experience as a result. If you want my advice for the game, you'll get a more enjoyable experience if you avoid unlocking the most powerful pirates early on: Toya and Pinkus are notoriously OP, their powers allowing them to solo most of the map. Rather than let yourself depend on them every time. Give yourself the challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed the time that I've spent with this game, and its DLC. I enjoyed the storyline and how they've woven in the "save scum" mechanic as a central story point. The characters are also varied, and have their own personalities. I'm currently 90 hours into playing and  finding good synergies between characters.If I had to choose a "con", it would be that some of the badges require more precise timing than what I'm able to pull off. It's nothing that prevented me from completing the story, and most of the badges, though.I would like to have seen another game that takes place in this universe. Hopefully the rights will get picked up by another company, or continued by the former Mimimi devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: What am amazing game.Everything in it is just godlike: Gameplay, story, characters, music, artstyle.It's truly a work of art. I was really appreciative of them for bringing back one of my childhood games, Desperados, but I played this first just because I loved the pirate aesthetic. Hopefully the other games aren't far behind in terms of mechanics, because this has everything you could possibly want.If you've played the other 2 games, this is a nobrainer...just buy this ASAP.If not, the short version is: This is a Real Time Tactics (mostly stealth) game, meaning you play in real time, but you have a pause system where you can plan actions,and you can quick save at any time. So, depending on the difficulty you select, this game becomes kinda like a puzzle, where you have to take out enemies, mostly quietly so that you don't attract more guards, until you complete your objective and then extract. You have 7 characters that all have really cool abilities and you can sync them using the pause system. Like I said, because you can quick save the game is just pure fun, but you can also challenge yourself by limiting pretty much everything or just giving the enemies better reactions or greater numbers, your choice.The game might not be long, but it is highly replayable.Just a masterpiece overall, buy it now!
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi Games should be an example other devs everywhere learn from, it's sad that Shadow Gambit is their last game,But I can confidently say they said goodbye on a perfect note. This is their best game by a good margin.The campaign and crew stories are long enough on their own, but level challenges add infinitely more fun angles to the game, leaving you with over 100+ hours of fun.Thank you Mimimi, and goodbye, moah xoxo
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game, fun mechanics, interesting world building. The real-time stealth tactics works really well, and the characters synergies are really fun.2 recommendations: First, use the random button a few times once you unlock everyone and are comfortable with all the characters. You would be surprised at how well some of the characters work together, and it forces you to not lean on the same 1 or 2 characters. The game does have an incentive system in place for that, though.Second, wait to buy the DLC characters until after you complete the story. The DLC characters are VERY powerful. They mesh well into the game/crew, but Yuki is in a league of her own, in my opinion. All in all, a solid experience, that I am still thoroughly enjoying.
_childDocuments_.name: Shadow Gambit: The Cursed Crew

Graphically, it's a much inferior indie game compared to Desperados. I requested a refund; the first impression was horrible, and it was even worse to be stuck in the initial tutorial for 40 minutes looking for a passage.
