_childDocuments_.review: Probably not my game according to all other reviews and I wish I could recommend it but I can't. By the time I had reached halfway mark I felt like the game had overstayed its welcome. I had fun in the beginning then I got more and more bored and only powered through because I wanted to see the story unfold as the voice acting is amazing and the presentation is fantastic. But the level design and game play is just so incredibly repetitive. And unfortunately in the end I found even the story incredibly lackluster.Why bullet time is even a thing in this game I don't understand. Most enemies you are fighting are melee ones, no real gunfire you need to bullet dodge.And achievements are broken as well. So if you care about 100% the games you buy I would hold off. Actually I would hold off regardless, would not buy this at full price again.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: "El Paso, Elsewhere" stands out as a remarkable hidden gem of indie gaming experience, boasting stunning visuals, a fascinating narrative, all complemented by an incredible soundtrack. These elements truly shine and make it a game worth exploring firsthand. While other aspects of the game may be passable, it's these standout features that will capture your attention and hold it throughout your journey. Without delving too deep to avoid spoilers, it's safe to say that these are the game's strongest assets.In terms of gameplay, "El Paso, Elsewhere" channels the spirit of classics like Max Payne, but with a supernatural twist featuring mummies, werewolves, and ghouls. The storytelling is poetic, offering a unique and immersive narrative experience. The music adds to the atmosphere, providing a badass backdrop to the action. Surprisingly lengthy with 50 levels, both the gameplay and story captivate from start to finish.One of the game's most commendable aspects is its portrayal of female-on-male abuse, a topic rarely explored in media. The narrative delivers a moving and thought-provoking depiction of this issue, adding depth and emotional resonance to the overall experience. The soundtrack is so exceptional that it warrants standalone listening, and the environments are breathtakingly atmospheric, immersing players in a world that is as beautiful as it is haunting.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really admire what the game is going for, and it gets there in terms of narrative and atmosphere and stuff. But the gameplay, good grief, it is a game about bullet time which almost completely misses the point of bullet time (BULLETS, anyone?) that is also so insanely repetitive and tormented by bland and uninspired looking levels and a monotone enemy gallery it becomes a chore to play through in sessions longer than 30 minutes. The gameplay even's not bad, pointless bullet time aside (you know, the core mechanic), it's just terribly paced. Being set entirely in one of those "whoa dreamy crazy space stuff's floating and random and ♥♥♥♥" locations games love to abuse certainly doesn't help. I'll try to update the review when I finish it as the story and vibe are really great, and I dig that they're trying to do with Max Payne and From Dusk Till Dawn references, I am intrigued where will it all lead, but this has to be the most painfully dull game to play I've seen this year.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Indie Max Payne is an accurate description of this game, but it doesn't do it justice. The core is definitely inspired by the bullet time shootouts, but every aspect brings in something more that's unique to this game. The combat isn't just about going from one corridor to another as you constantly hide behind cover. Instead, there are several enemy types which require using different weapons and tactics.The story may be told through familiar, gritty cutscenes where a man talks about his tragic woes, but the directing itself is on another level compared to Max Payne. Despite the low-budget production, you always are aware of what the protagonist is going through, even though the low-poly models can't really show expressions, and every shot is interesting.There's even a rap album, probably made by the dev, that plays over the gameplay in crucial moments and fits well. The game shows heaps of effort and care that were put into it at every turn.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome- a paranormal Max Payne with werewolves, mummies and vampires. It's also weird as hell, has fantastic sound design and really takes you on a journey across 50 different levels that take 8-20 hours to complete depending on what difficulty you play.The only major issues with the game have to do with repetitive chunks of game play and some nonsensical level design. The whole idea is that the protagonist is going into "the void", a nondescript mess of various map assets like slaughterhouses and hotel rooms with no ceiling, to rescue his lover. The story is convoluted and has many cringeworthy moments, and the cutscenes are just long bouts of exposition. Max Payne told a much better story with just a few comic panels between each level, but this game seems to want to get the player lost in thought the way its protagonist seems to be.The combat is great, as you have ragdoll physics and each weapon serves a specific function. The rifle can knock out long range enemies with ease and the molotovs can set up a barrier to block off a hallway from incoming enemies. There are some weird suit of armor enemies that are best dispatched with the shotgun. The game also gives you "stakes" which are melee weapons that deal devastating damage up close. These are great because if you run out of ammo you might be able to stake enemies coming at you as a last resort.Generally speaking, the enemies in this game are great, as each one has its own specific movement and attack programming. This is one way I like this game better than Max Payne since you occasionally need to use specific maneuvering to take out enemies in a certain order to survive. The werewolves jump across the screen to attack the player but they have little health. Unfortunately, the game uses certain enemies way too often. There is a female creature that is always above the player and launches an instakill projectile. It would be okay if you confronted her once in a while, but the game likes to throw her in every other room in the second half of the game.You can slow down time and do slow mo jump like in Max Payne, but the jump is pretty useless since it drains the bar way too fast. Rolling makes you invincible so if you play on hard you want to roll everywhere to avoid dying. You can really play this game anyway you want since the game lets you activate cheats like infinite ammo and increase enemy health at the start of each game. Still, I got really frustrated playing this game. The last 1/3 of the game is really annoying because no new game play mechanics or enemies are introduced. It's just a long slog through a bunch of areas you've already seen rearranged to keep whatever semblance of a "story" there is going.I actually kind of loved playing through this despite its flaws. There are two difficult boss fights that are very well-designed. I think if the level design was a little bit more careful and deliberate this would actually be a better game than Max Payne 2 and 3, though it doesn't come close to the original Max Payne. And while I compare it to Max Payne a lot this game is very much its own thing, not quite being film noire but existing in kind of a dreadful washed out pulp comic without much of a story to tell but a large amount of vibe to express.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Gift this game to a friend who said, "I can fix him/her," to prepare them for the endgame.Just finished it:If you like Max Payne or atmospheric games/shooters, you will enjoy this one. Personally, this game resonated with me because I’ve been in three (jokes on me) really painful codependent relationships before I worked on myself and turned them into life lessons. The feelings of hopelessness, hurt, and anger, but also growth and the willingness to escape the hell you’re living in that this game captures with its dialogues, music, jokes, and even Easter eggs, are nothing short of outstanding. Mix in some truths and knowledge behind the dialogue, and you see that this really must be a passion project and a work of art from the developer for people who can relate.And a solid Max Payne clone for everyone else.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: just saw credits, what an incredible achievement.the combat and the encounter design are good. almost every mechanic in the game exists from the jump and over the course of the game you get into the corners of all of them. the difficulty is mostly a slow ramp with a few big spikes for encounters.the music is WILD. i'm struggling to remember a time i've seen better needle drops in a game. the experience of playing a game where the protagonist is also doing vocals on music tracks is overwhelming. it's like getting a mixtape from somebody and realizing that they wrote and recorded every song on it.the environment design is, and i mean this as high praise, budget remedy. like how do you take some of the mindbending geometry from a game like Control and achieve it with a small team? that seems really hard to do and the team executes it wonderfully! and the level design? i think one of the biggest challenges of making environments that are geometrically impossible is that it should make levels harder to navigate. my sense of direction is hot garbage and i can count the number of times i got lost on one hand.the narrative got me. the difficult and isolated moments hit. the tender conversations hit. the jokes land. the game grabs me by my own self-destructive tendencies and twists just a little bit. "dying good is easy, it's harder to live good" hits me right in the gut.i have exactly one problem: i had a couple of brutal performance issues with per-object motion blur enabled, big drops in FPS. i disabled it and had no other issues.congrats to the team
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely rocks. Certainly more than the sum of its parts. A beautifully directed and well-told story with gameplay I never got tired of before credits. Some minor gripes with hitboxes and technical performance did nothing to damper how fantastic I felt finishing the game. It's hard to describe beyond just "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick".
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:Repetitive gameplay that plays worse than either max payne 1 and 2 due to enemy designInsane asset recycling that makes for unmemorable and almost randomly generated feeling levelsFun but very hit and miss soundtrack.Absolutely miserable performanceYou take max payne 1 or 2, and downgrade them in every way(beside movement which is better than 1 but worse than 2), then somehow stretch that to 8 entire hours. I kept waiting for it to add enemies that were a challenge or even fun to fight, but it kept wasting more of my time with repetitive levels. I love supporting indies, and this game is downright intimate, but demonstrates a lack of understanding of what made max payne good to play in the choices made, and a lack of competency in implementing the things they didn't change. I am holding in a cheapshot regarding the lead dev complaining about gamers potentially having higher expectations for RPG's after Baldur's Gate 3 and failing to live up to or surpass in any meaningful way something made in 2001.Verdict: Buy Max Payne 1 or 2, if you've played them? play mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Man's out here fightin' demons. Metaphorically and literally.Addiction: Painkiller abuse. Sobriety tossed away for the sake of your trip to Hell.Mortality: Death will come. You can't change that. Though some make the decision for it to arrive faster.Morality: Dying a good person is easy. Living as one is agony.Abuse: You don't have to lift a finger to leave a mark.Vampires and Werewolves: Turns out you don't need those fancy silver bullets.This game strikes so many chords from fighting your feelings to f**king up folklore monsters.Not to mention the absolute BANGER of a custom soundtrack that blends so well with the gameplay.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Where'd this game come from?A lot of love was put into this Max Payne-em-up.  It's literally Max Payne, but you're fighting vampires and werewolves.  Still poppin' pills, though!  So many pills!!!Most of the music is great, but some of it was downright obnoxious!  Also, I feel like the protagonist speaks WAY too fast during his dialogues.  Slow down, Buddy.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I like A LOT about El Paso, Elsewhere. The style, the storytelling, the music (includes an entire rap album of really cool songs), the top notch voice acting.But I can't recommend this game to anyone in good faith because of the level design. 50 levels with a constant structure and very rare changes to them make a 9-hour game feel like a 20-hour game. And as the initial wow-effect wears off, playing through to the end of it is a slog, and nothing that's actually good about the game can fix that.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: A strangely captivating fusion of influences, reminiscent of Max Payne and From Dusk Till Dawn, with a drop of Total Overdose, concocts an intriguing blend that might give one pause before diving in. Set against an engaging and peculiar backdrop, the narrative spins a compelling yarn of the supernatural, adding an extra layer of intrigue. Complemented by a stellar soundtrack that sets the tone, the voice cast delivers performances striking just the right balance of edginess. It's the kind of game you don't realize you've missed in your life until you've played it.Here's to more stories like this from El Paso!4,5 puppets out of 5 - Chad Shakesprear

_childDocuments_.review: I very much enjoyed my time with this game. The gameplay is just solid and well done, but the VIBE of this game is SO good. The writing, the cutscenes, the music all help the game punch WAY above its weight. Maybe not for everybody, but it absolutely worked for me.Will be keeping an eye on Strange Scaffold going forward. You guys did great.Game TW:
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: While a little rough in some levels, and running smooth as butter in others, those can be chalked up to my personal computer limitations. Overall this game is an experience, each needle drop was a moment to be celebrated as you gun through the supernatural and horrific. Each little bit of humor a reprieve from the dramatic story of a man working through his trauma while also saving the world while high as hell in hell itself.Some of the strongest vibes known to man, a fun gameplay loop, music I will listen to in my off time, and overall a very complete package that delivers just the right amount of itself. But I definitely would not mind more, if there are plans in the future to expand on this game in whatever shape or form.Extremely great, play it if you like action shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: What a love letter to Max Payne. The vibes are immaculate outside of a couple moments where I felt the OST didn't match what was going on. Gameplay is satisfying, but nothing you haven't seen before. The voice acting is excellent, brooding internal monologue and all, and the tidbits of lore you get in the levels is great. Exceeded my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's even better then initially expected. If you ever thought that the mind game sections ontop of the regular gameplay in Max Payne were cool then you'll love this.The otherwordly feeling you get is really unique and kept me playing between levels as they go by really quickly. And I was not expecting the rap but when it happened I could not stop smiling as it fits so weirdly well and contrasts the somber whispering of the main character during gameplay and cutscenes.I really don't know how to describe this other then a more trippy version of Max Payne but you usually get a feeling for a game after about an hour of nonstop gameplay, and after not even that long I just want to play more of El Paso, Elsewhere.This was a great suprise, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the story more than I should've, and it's definitely due to presintation, this game is so low poly and yet framing of cutscenes is more cinematic then last three movies I've seen. Gameplay-wise unfortunatly not everything is as flawless as I would want in terms of movement. It's a bit rough around the edges to the point where Max Payne 1 feels more polished then this, but it doesn't mean I didn't enjoy ragdolling werewolf into the abyss with a shotgun. I liked the replayability sliders, will probably beat this game again but on increased speed. Didn't like the amount of levels at graveyard, and some of them showed up kinda randomly when you though you finally moved on from it. Music is amazing though (but maybe will take a minute to get used to)
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I can see a lot of work went into the story and visuals in this game, but not that much thought went into the actual gameplay.The game itself is quite boring. Slow movement, repetitive and boring enemies, silly "hostages" to rescue. Tedious monologues between each level that try to be "deep and moody", and each level is quite short. Just not much in the game.The slow motion/dive mechanic looks pretty but doesn't add much to the game. I can see the visual inspiration from Control (which I absolutely love), but as a game this doesn't even come close.Unfortunately I'm past the refund period. I might play it through just to see where the story is going, but it's just not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Did not like this. Didn't hate it... but didn't like it.The gunplay is bad and awkward, the Max Payne comparisons superficial, the noir affect all surface-level, and the levels repetitive. I was able to beat the whole thing without using slo-mo or diving and without running out of resources. _childDocuments_.review: Currently leaving a negative review to ensure the attention of the developers that a bug has made the main character invisible during cutscenes if he is wearing his jacket. _childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game is GREAT! It has a story. It has a character backstory. The game mechanics are on point. You can shoot things. You can burn things. You can slow down time and shoot or burn things, or you can dive through the air while shooting things. The healing mechanism is simple, the play is simple, but you still feel deadly when you clear a tough spot.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid overall. The core loop to this game is similar to Max Payne: diving around a level in slow motion shooting enemies, with a semi-similar style of storytelling - Noir with a gravelly voice narrating everything. The first half of the game is quite slow with respect to the narrative and the encounters, but the second half really sticks the landing. It takes a while to add variety to the combat encounters but it mostly gets there by the end. The storytelling is very direct but still interesting to see play out.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Random number review: 8.5 out of 10Solid gameplay. Surprisingly longer than I expected, but short enough to not overstay its welcome if you don't care about 100%. Can probably play and finish in 6 hours if you move fast.If you enjoyed the gameplay of the first two Max Payne games, you'll enjoy this one. If you're a Remedy fan in general, you'll enjoy it even more. I felt elements from Max Payne, Alan Wake, and Control all mixed into this game, and it ends up being a nice ride. Took about 11 hours to 100%. I feel like maybe the endings are not quite what they could have been, but I'm still okay with it  for the most part. A moody main character goes through the melodramatic neo-noir pathway while recounting what got him up to that point. Sound familiar? Hope so.Difficulty: I played on Intended the entire time, and it's a bit up and down. I found enemy damage to be a bit confusing on occasion, but since you do have bullet time, it's kinda on you if you get hit. Never, ever, ever try to reload in bullet time, or that bullet time is straight wasted. I found the big boss fight in the middle of the game actually a bit more difficult than the final boss. I feel like his movement needs to be slowed down just slightly. Otherwise, it's not really difficult.Some cheese: in the late game, find objects to stand on in one room, and you can potentially snipe enemies in other rooms. Particularly useful when you find the rifle for the first time. The game's rules are solid enough that you can't abuse this all the time, but it can save your life if you're hurting for pills.Achievement issues: I played through the game normally and I know I visited most of the projectors, but for whatever reason I did not get credit for any of them until I finished the game and replayed the missions that had them. Not sure if that was a bug or what.One of the later chapter titles literally just said "Chapter Title" in game, but if you look at the chapter's title in the main menu, it's properly listed. Not sure what the deal is there.I got a good kick out of the humor in the game. The comedic relief helped break the tension in the dark corridors in certain levels. Speaking of dark corridors, I do kind of wish they had a manually operated flashlight. Only a couple of levels actually give you a flashlight.Is it perfect? No, but it does make very few mistakes. This is a much appreciated love letter to an underappreciated genre and game series. The story's spin is unique, though I wish the ending was better.Things I did not mess with: alternate modes outside of campaign(? I don't remember seeing anything else, I just wanted to play the main game lol); I did not mess with difficulty, either.Original impression: I have only played 49 minutes and just started Chapter 8, and I am beyond stoked for this game. So far, it's checking all the boxes.

The camera angles, the subtitle placement, stuff like that.  Gameplay is serviceable. I love 3rd person shooters in general so... But the way it drip feeds you story between every other (5min) level is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: A classic throwback to Max Payne, a Max Payne em up if you will.  The story, voice acting, art direction, and soundtrack all excel at what they're aiming for, but for me personally, the levels and gameplay get too repetitive too fast for my liking and with 50 some levels and getting burned out 20 or so in, I can't heartily recommend it. I feel if the game was shorter it would be to its benefit. But that said, I'll be looking forward to what this team makes in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game is longer than it needed to be and "bullet time" is more of a gimmick than a viable game mechanic.But the levels themselves are short, it's just there's 50 of them. And no game ever got worse because of the slo-mo, even if it feels unnecessary.The main attraction for me was the story and characters. _childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere is an incredibly compelling game, thanks to the excellent writing and tight combat design. Despite being a clear send-up to the Max Payne series, playing El Paso doesn't feel like playing any other game out there. This title packs an emotional punch that will catch you unawares with its sincerity. Despite strong themes of abuse, lovesickness, and self-destruction, El Paso has plenty of comedic moments that land excellently - and you somehow never get tonal whiplash.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: A true spiritual successor to the first two Max Payne games.It's earnest and sincere, surreal and haunting.When it's serious and personal you feel the stakes, when it's goofy camp you laugh.Presentation is mature and impactful, making ample use of lighting, framing and color.The voice performances and writing deliver a lot with very little, both succinct and purposeful.The hip-hop pounding guitar blaring soundtrack  through a 6 hours-ish 50 chapter campaign that . You can modify the amount of damage you take and how much painkillers heal or turn on infinite ammo and painkillers for maximum fun or challenge, depending on what you want.It's an easy recommend not only for any fan of Max Payne but any fan of over the top action.(Even if you have a slow/old computer I'd encourage you to try it, my CPU/GPU are well below the minimum specs but I've played through the game twice now with mostly 60fps)
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: The writing, audio design, and cutscenes in this game are masterful in ways most games can only ever dream of. This is like dogme 95 for videogames. It challenged me to rethink the lines between gameplay and writing, and how one can resonate with the other; it explores mature themes usually far beyond the scope of videogames, and it does so deftly and sensitively; and it does it all with a self-assured swagger and sense of fun that is so damn endearing.A magnificent game in a year jam packed with magnificent games - and well worth its place at #2 on my goty list for 23.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: IMO if you think you will enjoy this game based on your history with Max Payne or pure vibes (because this game has a sick vibe), you are probably correct. Fans of Remedy games might also find something to appreciate here if they're willing to accept a lower production value.One major criticism is that the bosses (of which there are blessedly few) are animated pretty poorly making their actions sometimes unclear - at the very least, the major bosses in the campaign left me feeling pretty underwhelmed compared to some of the more hectic shootouts with adds. I felt that the game took perhaps too long ramping up the difficulty via additional enemy types. It takes far too long for the game to apply enough pressure that i was forced to use any weapon other than your starting pistols. Additional enemy density or variety earlier in the story would help the combat feel a little more engaging earlier, as later levels can definitely get you thinking on your feet. While the voice acting is overall high quality, the lead VA can be a little indistinct during the game's more somber moments. Some of the dialogue and some of the lyrics definitely feel a little tongue-in-cheek, so if you're expecting the experience to be self-serious some of the humor will potentially bounce right off you.If you are on the fence, you could wait for the game to go as low as $15, but I already felt like I got a great story and a mostly-fantastic campaign for the full cost despite the complaints above.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's just really good tbh. If you find it getting tedious then you can do what I did and bump up enemy damage and painkiller healing to 1,5 instead of the baseline. This made encounters overall more tense and interesting to me.Other than that, yeah, it's like Max Payne inside a more classic 90s FPS like Quake or Unreal. The OST has some absolute bangers and the story gets surprisingly heavy by the end of it. Content/spoiler warning for some potentially upsetting material surrounding emotional abuse in relationships.I thoroughly enjoyed this and can easily recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso Elsewhere is more than just a love letter to the original Max Payne games, it manages to carve out its own diverse lore, that feels wholly unique. The writing is incredible, from the opening cutscene, right until the emotional crescendo at the final moments. The gameplay itself is a little flawed, and there are some levels here that do feel a like a little filler, but the story alone was more than enough to carry me through those parts that were lacking. If you like noir adventures, and want to explore the dynamics of a mentally abusive breakup, this is definitely worth checking out ASAP.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Every moment of this game drips atmosphere, and the shooting and slomo is satisfyingly solid. It overstays its welcome a touch - it gets a touch repetitive in the long term, but the levels are reasonably sized and come up with new stuff often enough that it's only a minor issue.  The story is a well done examination of the ways we remember bad relationships and try and find the good bits and ignore the damage done. The voice acting is camp yet effective, carrying a lot of emotion through some overwrought dialogue.The soundtrack is great - a mix of intrumentals and vocal tracks, with raps actually in character for the main character.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty much all the stuff an improvement in every way on EL PASO, NIGHTMARE. Digging it so far for sure. _childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible journey this game is. Your Ex is the Lord of the Vampires, and she is about to destroy the world. You go on a pill infused journey to stop her.The storytelling and soundtrack especially are world class. There were so many times I couldn't put the game down, as I felt a strong need to see what happened next. You learn about how you were with Draculae, how you'd speak to each other, past dramas, your inner struggles as you are faced with a decaying body, and wanting to go back to a simpler time, while still feeling the need to keep going to stop the world from ending. It's enthralling. The cutscenes are shot perfectly, the voice acting feels very real, and the soundtrack lifts the entire experience to the next lvl. Despite the game's indie budget, it feels incredibly AAA (in a good way) in these departments.The gameplay itself has you running around, shooting monsters. You have a full arsenal of guns, a dodge-roll, and a slow motion mechanic (that I forgot to use throughout the entire game, oops). You can also dive, which I also forgot to use. Oops.Despite the simple premise, the game is quite satisfying to play. The enemies are placed in ways that make you really have to think about who you want to prioritize. Shooting werewolves in front isn't going to be of much use when you re being sniped by energy-balls from the back.That said, what is holding this game back from being a full 5/5 stars, is its pacing in the gameplay lvls. While the story pacing is great, you can often feel like the game drags on. The game spends a very long time between introducing new enemies, so you are stuck fighting just a basic enemy that runs towards you for a good hour or so. Then they'll introduce one more enemy, and it once again takes forever before you see anything new. After everything has been introduced, the same issue persists, it takes too long before something special happens. That's not to say the gameplay isn't fun, I think more the issue is that the devs did not have enough resources to make everything they wanted to.A side-complaint I also wanted to mention is that for most of the game it is simply too easy. Out of all the levels, I think I only died on 3 of them, one of which being the first boss, and one of my deaths was because I got stuck in the geometry and was unable to move. While not a huge issue, I would have loved to see a difficulty mode where they don't necessarily boost any numbers, but make resources and ammo a bit more scarce, forcing you to use your whole arsenal while not having instant access to healing, and without the slow-motion bar. While I played the entire game without using the slow-motion, if I were to use it it would completely invalidate any challenge in this game if I were to use it.Usually when a game offers a slow-motion mechanic, the enemies and world design is balanced around it. For example, the enemies that charge energy-balls are very easy to locate and take out, even with full-speed gameplay, before they ever get to shoot. They could have made it a lot more interesting if the player was forced to use the slow-motion to deal with situations like these.It feels like there should have been more enemy typed, it feels like there should have been at least one more environment to explore, and it feels like there should have been more secrets. Because of what I can only assume is budget constraints, they had to do the best with what they had. They wanted the story to have this length, and they wanted you to have this amount of time between the hard hitting story beats, so instead of making something new, they remixed what they had. While not a big issue, it can sometimes feel like the game drags on a little too long before new things are introduced.Personally, with this many levels in the game, there should have been more enemy variety. Once you overcome the challenge of one enemy, and how they are combined with other enemies, throwing more of the same at the player is ultimately pointless. They should either have added more variety, or cut down on the repetitiveness.That said, the game is full of awesome moments, unique setpieces during the lvls, and the main character's monologues never get old. In the end, "I wanted more game" is probably not the worst critique a dev can get.I really hope this game does well so they can make a sequel. I need to know what happens next.

_childDocuments_.review: God, this game made me feel things.I've loved all of strange scaffold's games, but this is the first one that is going on my list of favorite games.The writing is some of the best in games, that was going to be a given.This man made me feel things about dog .jpg's.But this is gorgeous, the music slaps, and is insanely fun to play.Ran into a few bugs, some things broke.But oh my god was this game an experience.Xalavier has the keys to my tear ducts and my feelings, and he has zero issues abusing that access.It's good.Play it.

_childDocuments_.review: The word to describe El Paso, Elsewhere is the vibe. It's the immaculate vibe you're paying for when you buy this game. It's a raw, unique blend of numerous inspirations from cinema, video games, literature and music that never really feels derivative of something, despite how proudly it displays its influences. It's like From Dusk til Dawn, Max Payne and Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind had the messiest, most emotionally damaging break-up of all time. And you're watching it unfold in glorious slow motion.El Paso, Elsewhere might look like an elaborate ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ (let's be honest, most of Strange Scaffold' games do) or some sort of darkly comedic parody, but it's not. Underneath vampires, werewolves and slow-mo shootouts hides a shockingly depressing, relatable story of moving on from abuse, addiction and coming to terms with your past. And yes, that's in a game where female Dracula tries to end the world by conducting a ritual in the dirtiest texan motel. El Paso, Elsewhere feels like the only game since Hotline Miami that accurately portrays descent into madness -- or at least what it would feel like to watch the reality fall apart around you. Infinite corridors of the motel bend into each other, collapse, expand endlessly. The further you go, the more absurd and unreal it all feels. Infinite void intertwines the memories of the protagonist and his vampire ex, recreates monsters, places and moments from the past. It looks morbidly beautiful and uncomfortable. El Paso, Elsewhere might have a deliberately lo-fi visual style, but the game never feels cheap or lazy. Everything, from the artstyle to lighting effects and art design, works perfectly in sync. Also, the cutscenes that often play between levels have a surprising level of direction behind them. It looks cinematic as hell, and shows that the devs have a perfect understanding of what exactly makes the whole aesthetic so memorable.And the music... Oh, the music. El Paso, Elsewhere plays fast and loose with its own soundtrack, in a similar manner to level-design: it never stays exactly the same, but still clicks into all the right places. There's some heavy electronic tracks, witch house, ambient, droning noises and low, hypnotic base. rj lake, who's credited as the composer, did a fantastic job. One moment you might be blasting werewolves to some rock, while on the next level you traverse an infinite labyrinth to hip-hop -- both classic and experimental. In fact, there's a whole mixtape stuffed inside El Paso, Elsewhere. Can't say anything about the quality since i'm no expert on the genre, but it's worth mentioning that most hip-hop tracks are performed by Mr. Strange Scaffold himself, who also voices the protagonist. So, mowing down monsters while your hero spits bars feels very cheesy and strangely empowering at the same time. It doesn't happen too often, but each occasion feels earned.While the story itself might sound silly, the way it is written and presented is anything but. As previously mentioned, the game has a definite cinematic flair to it, and the narrative reflects that. It feels like a movie script in the best way possible, right down to stage directions, cuts, plot reveals and the pacing. Strange Scaffold games have a unique sense of humor, but El Paso, Elsewhere has a battered, bleeding heart. The doomed romance between paranormal investigator James Savage and Draculae, the ancient lord of the vampires, sometimes feels too real. And yes, again, it might sound silly -- but you often can't help but feel for the characters, both of them. The cliche monologues of James often sound very similar to Max Payne's philosophical ramblings, and yet... It's like there's more life to them. Stellar voice performance only elevates that effect further. Xalavier Nelson Jr, the man behind the whole project, is by no means a professional actor, but he still does a surprisingly great job. And the actress who played Draculae also sounds perfect for the role.There's only one thing where El Paso, Elsewhere falters, and that is the gameplay. Many journalists and Steam users are praising it as a true spiritual successor to Max Payne, but that couldn't be further from the truth. Strange Scaffold is an experienced developer, but it is their first time creating a third person shooter with (presumably) tight budget -- and it shows. Gameplay often feels sluggish and sort of outstays it's own welcome, despite the fact that the game is fairly short. Poor enemy variety, repetitive combat scenarios, the weapon feedback feels hit and miss: the shotgun is great, while the high-cailber marksman rifle sounds like a peashooter.Don't get me wrong, when the shooting feels good, it feels almost orgasmic. Blasting fiends away with shotgun point-blank, watching their bodies spaz out and fly straight into shadow realm never gets old. Just like catching werewolves mid-jump with a well timed shot, or putting mummies down with your stake inbetween reloads. El Paso, Elsewhere has a surprisingly good hit marking, both visual and audial, so headshots always feel juicy.But the main problem, imo, is the structure of the game. El Paso, Elsewhere consists of 50 unique levels, but more often than not they play out in the exact same way. You arrive at the next floor, find and rescue trapped civilians -- and then run back to the start. There are monster ambushes and some light key-hunting, but the only thing that changes are the decorations. Unfortunately, decrepit motel, medieval castle, run-down graveyard and an ancient egyptian tomb are populated by the same enemies that never deviate from their behavior.  After playing for an hour you clear the levels practically on auto-pilot, since great setpieces (and there are some) are few and far between. I'll be honest, the only thing that made me finish the game was the story, and that is probably not a good sign.It's also worth mentioning that the legendary slow-mo feels rather pointless, because El Paso, Elsewhere plays more like Painkiller then Max Payne. Vast majority of monsters attack you in melee, so swan dives lose their appeal as a repositioning tool. It does look stylish, but never feels mandatory to survival -- or playing the game in general. In fact, just slowing down time, without any jumps, is far more useful in most situations. Besides, there's often not enough space to really show off your acrobatic prowess, since most of the game is spent in tight corridors with little room to maneuver.In other words, the gameplay of El Paso, Elsewhere is rough, and not just around the edges. Like a promising prototype that could use some (a fair bit of) refinement. It's competent enough to bear the weight of the story, perfect aesthetics and music, but you should really temper your expectations. However, that is by no means a demerit: El Paso, Elsewhere is so much more than a simple Max Payne clone. It's a bad one-way trip in the best sense of the word. It feels genuine, like all independent games should. Strange Scaffold added another bright, unique game to their portfolio, and i'll be eagerly waiting for their next endeavor.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is escalating narratively unlike any shooter I've played this year.The guns are inherently satisfying. The level design is consistently insanely creative. The needle drops are transcendent. And the acting rules.This game punches way above its $19.99 pricetag ($17.99 if you buy now), which you NEED TO DOIt's incredibly fun. Then you feel the tone start to shift. But then it's fun! And then someone says a line phrased *just so*, and it hits you like a truck. A really precise truck.I think the concerns of El Paso becoming monotonous over time are likely overextending their play sessions wanting to see more of the story. If you played tetris for 3 hours straight you'd get bored too, but tetris doesn't have an insanely good narrative pushing you past Being Done Playing For Now.I'm not gonna binge this one. The story resonates with me on a personal level and makes me wanna lay in bed like the depressed Squidward meme, but it also has gameplay that tickles my fox brain and makes me joyous as well as a lowpoly surreal horror aesthetic that tantalizes my 'tism. All these things mixed with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ banger OST makes this game a rollercoaster for me, the story has stuck with me ever since I finished it, and I still listen to this OST everyday while doing everything. _childDocuments_.review: It's a banger. The gameplay, soundtrack, writing, voice acting, movement, easter eggs, replayability, all of that stuff: tight as hell.  If you're here because someone said "hey what if Max Payne saw a werewolf in a bathroom and dropped the album of the year" and that sounded interesting, you're gonna love this. If you got here otherwise, the game is like that, and it rips, so buy it and play it.Anyway yeah I beat it twice, 10/10, will wind up going back to finish Pill Cop.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that wears its heart on its sleeve. It is, in many ways, self indulgent-- and it knows this. It takes itself seriously while delivering the goofiest lines you've ever heard but the genuine way it does so just makes you think it's rad as hell anyway.And then? Once it's buttered you up? It punches you in the gut with some seriously raw, emotional writing. As someone who's been a multiple abuse victim, it hits extraordinarily close to home, and I feel for both James and for the game's writer-- who has mentioned before that there's a lot of himself in this one.Then the game itself is quite fun, simple and effective shooting-- it's hard not to enjoy slo-mo werewolf fights, ok? It also makes incredible use of its limited maps and assets to create surrealist levels that continually wow you as you delve deeper and deeper into the game's campaign.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: In a seedy motel down in El Paso the lord of all vampires, Draculae, has opened a rift to Hell and is ushering in a ritual to end the world. A drug-addicted monster hunter, James Savage, ventures into the bowels of the motel to stop it, knowing that this adventure may be his last; but hey, he can’t let his ex-girlfriend destroy the world after all.El Paso Elsewhere wears its influence from Remedy’s oeuvre on its sleeve. The opiate popping hardboiled detective soliloquizing in between shooting down enemies in John Woo slo-mo clearly hearkens to Max Payne and the motel’s hellish depths of dimensional shifting corridors filled with supernatural aberrations are akin to a fusion of Max Payne 1’s nightmare sequences and Control’s eldritch halls of The Oldest House. El Paso uses these elements as a springboard to make its own identity though.Mechanically the game is similar to Max Payne though its focus on tighter corridors and mix of melee and ranged enemies does bring its own sense of hecticness that sets it apart from Max.  You have a full arsenal of weapons here ranging from stakes, which you can only hold a limited amount and guarantee an instant melee kill on any basic enemy, shotguns, molotovs, and rifles. I was constantly switching between weapons throughout the whole game as they all have their uses; even the basic dual pistols stay viable throughout as they are fairly long-range, accurate, and good for getting critical hits off of headshots.Narratively the game does an actually real good job being a supernatural neo-noir. Max Payne 1 and 2 were mainly just noir pastiche, purposely goofy in a way that didn’t give its cast much depth beyond archetypes. El Paso actually manages to be a quality character study of abusive relationships and addiction through a noir genre lens. James yearns for the past, that one perfect day of his relationship as he puts it; even though he knows nothing but pain and self-destruction awaits him down that road. Affection and care had devolved into abusive control and thinly-veiled threats of violence as true characters were revealed. But like the drug addict he is James still can’t stop trying to regain that impossible high. All of this is well portrayed through the quality voice-acting in between levels as James is transported to each floor through the dimensional elevator. The game also has some levity with its Remedy-esque easter eggs like the continuing adventures of Pill Cop that you find throughout the levels. It does have its share of flaws and jank though. One thing is it takes some time for the game to actually start taking off, the game has fifty levels, and for around the first fifteen or so you’re basically just fighting basic vampires and werewolves where you not going to really have to bother using slo-mo that much. The first boss is also a bit of spike and I think they probably could give you a bit more ammo for the strongest weapons for him. I still managed but just be sure to rebind the roll onto something where you can hit it faster and easier for that fight.Despite any missteps El Paso Elsewhere is still a genuinely great game and I actually like it over most of Remedy’s games aside from Control. Definitely worth checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's been quite a while since I've felt a game click like this, an extremely fun and satisfying shooter that wears it's max payne 1 inspirations on its sleeves and knows exactly what it is, voice acting for the protagonist and antagonist blew me away and each level felt fun with some extremely cool visuals too, an excellent addition to any library.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Look, if you are familiar with the old Max Payne and want a new experience like this, El Paso Elsewhere is probably the best game for you. If you are not familiar with this old game, that's perfectly fine cause this game is so much more than just a Max Payne tribute. El Paso Elsewhere is a true piece of art with his dark distorded atmosphere, greatly paced gameplay (so far, I haven't finished it yet), amazing storytelling with one of the best performance I have ever seen in a game. And don't let me starting about the music and sound design. It's a masterpiece. Do yourself a favor, play this game, it's one of the best unique experience of the past ten years.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game - it's repetitive, but the narrative & voice acting were SO good, I had to see how it ends.The already mentioned 1st big boss fight (Djedefre) was really rough and frustrating - I must admit I managed to finish it because on the 15th try, the boss was buggy in the 2nd phase and just walked in a circle towards me, letting me strafe around him, making it way easier.The other boss fights were no way as tough - still a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere is a beautiful and tragic jaunt through a myriad of locations, more often than not mixed together into a horrifying amalgamation of memories, both bad and good. You play as James Savage, a man tortured by his past of drug addiction, abuse, and bad decisions. You'll experience his memories through projectors and cutscenes, slowly beginning to understand his relationship with Draculae, his ex. The gameplay is great, a mix of Max Payne and DOOM in all the best ways. It's satisfying and fun. The voice acting work and cinematography is also top notch, some of the best I've seen in terms of storytelling in quite a while. This is an absolute must play, and the story will give you a good 8 hours of gameplay. I'd say it might be the most profound and interesting indie title I've played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: If the story doesn't interest you, it'll be a repetitive chore of a game.Fun Supernatural Indie Max Payne game. The gameplay loop of shooting, dodging, diving with on demand bullet time is well executed and feels great. Great voice acting. Story kept me engaged. Music was a blast. Gameplay can be thoroughly customised to give desired experience.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's a monster slaying third person shooter about a man trying to stop his ex from ending the world that is brought to life by amazing voice acting. It even manages to work in an OST performed by the lead voice actor and studio lead of Strange Scaffold. There isn't much depth to the combat but running around in slow motion and shooting anything that moves is still a lot of fun. Definitely check this out!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: For a straight-up supernatural Max Payne clone, this game is shockingly well put together and engaging in story and gameplay. The voice acting is pitch-perfect for the paranormal noir vibe they're going for, and the levels are intriguing crawls of combat challenge that put your slow mo and dodging skills to the test (although you'll also test your character's liver with the number of painkillers you're chugging). It's maybe a little one-note for a modern video game, but what it does it does well, and there's nothing wrong with exploiting your core competency. Anyone who wants to replay Max Payne should give this a go first.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a Max Payne inspired throwback and while that is the obvious inspiration, the game evolves into much more than that.Gameplay wise, I think it isn't until 1/3 of the way through that this thing starts to cook.  The overall feel is much closer to Hotline Miami at that point and it's worth pushing through those early, somewhat boring sections to get there.  That's when you the banger soundtrack kicks in.  Let me tell you, having your guns pop in time with the beat as you react to a monster unexpectedly jumping you from a hidden corner  is an effing high.  This was the game at it's best.Story wise, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ there's an actual story here?!  And it's good?Yeah, it reads like a book you'd pick up off the rack at the airport - you used to date rule-63 Dracula, now you have to kill her before she destroys the world - but it explores toxic relationships in a way I've never seen another game do.  You used to love her.  Maybe you kind of still love her?  But also she makes you hate yourself, at least when she's not in her love-bombing moods.  The whole thing feels like it comes from somewhere genuine.  Like some version of this happened to the writer and this is their way of working through it, even if all the emotions have been dialed up to South Park levels of symbolism.I would recommend a play through.  By no means does this replace Max Payne.  The game goes in very different directions and it's worth trying out for the story alone.

_childDocuments_.review: My serotonin receptors run on a vibes based economy, and this game has vibes in spades. James' VA knocks it out of the park, the art style is simple but has it's moments of glory (when it hits, you'll know), and the music always fits the mood (spooky built atop equal parts depression and anger). The gameplay loop didn't start hitting for me until the second enemy type was introduced, but I was never bored before that due to the previously mentioned factors. That said, once I had to deal with more than one enemy type, I started to become hyper aware of the spaces I was in. Wide open spaces and tight corridors are both threatening, but require their own modes of awareness. Figuring out how to handle each just heightens the vibe already laid down by everything else.Finally, the one liners. They are good. That is all.(Edit) Post-Completion Thoughts:First off, the narrative of this game hits. I don't know a whole lot about one of the big themes it touches on, so I'll leave that to others to dissect, but the exploration of addiction hit home. I won't say it's all that deep, if you've gone through/are in recovery you've probably heard/experienced much of what it has to say, but sometimes it just hits to see your struggles presented in a heartfelt, raw as ♥♥♥♥ way in media. This game did that, and made me ball my eyes out multiple times because of it. It's all backed up by excellent VA performances, an art style that they make full use of, and incredible direction in the cutscenes, 10/10 narrative banger.The gameplay was a bit more mixed for me. To be clear, when it hits, it HITS. However, there was kind of an ebb and flow between levels (until around chapter 31). For 3-4 levels, I would be 'in-the-zone' and super engaged in the gameplay, and then the next 3-4 I'd feel like I was just going through the motions. That said, post chapter 31, it started to hit a lot more consistently, seemingly because all the tools were in the toolbox and they could start to mess with them in ways that felt novel on each level.Baseline: if you want a solid third person Max Payne inspired game and an incredibly well presented narrative touching on addiction, definitely check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice little game, but not a safe recommendation for everyone, I'd say. If you're immensely thirsty for some kind of retro Max Payne-experience and just want to shoot at stuff in slow-mo, you might like it. Cool style, story, and soundtrack - but not drawing the full potential of any of those things.- Level-design is highly repetitive with little to no variety. From 50 levels in total, there are like 2 or 3 where you're giving a flashlight to find your way in the dark and make for a stand-out level, every other is interchangeable and the settings (motel, graveyard, pyramid) are not enough to create memorable environments as you re-visit them again and again. Which wouldn't be as boring as it is, if you would not have to find your way to corridor mazes to press "E" on soulless hostages in almost every one of them, find the exit, repeat. Overall, even though levels are short and entertaining enough, the game feels a bit too long due to the repetitiveness - even though it's just 6-8 hours of a playthrough on standard difficulty.- Neo-Noir story, characters and dialogue are probably the best thing. It's basically a borderline-romance underneath a demonic plot to save the world from a crazy ex. Relatable. Voice actors are doing a great job, but Draculae in particular, the way she talks and expresses herself, has to be seen as a metaphoric energy vampire, not a century-old actual vampire. While the protagonist does express himself quite well and you get to know him through monologues and snarky comments, all other characters fall flat.- Gunplay is fun, weapon variety is there, and they feel heavy enough. But, bullet time only really becomes a requirement to use on higher difficulty, except for some rare situations. Balancing and enemy placement is sometimes a bit tricky, especially if checkpoints trigger at a bad moment, but fine overall and it doesn't happen all that much, to be honest. - Soundtrack is very cool - but again, falling short, as the memorable segments where it really drives the action, are used too sparsely in between the amount of repetitive levels. Sure, it's a small game, recourses are limited and a multiple hour long original soundtrack hard to accomplish. It might already help to use the available songs more often. The repetitiveness is already there due to the level design - the music to appear more often would probably help if placed carefully and not too excessive. It's overall a good game, not an overwhelming one in my opinion, but there's enough stuff to like if you can overlook some stuff. For whatever the developers do next, I hope, they refine the quality of level design and make it more interesting to get closer to the depth in gameplay and presentation they're aiming for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game massively overstays it's welcome. It is *so* repetitive. I am 20 levels in and I have *just* reach the third level theme... And that's just a visual theme, the actual content of the levels has barely changed. I am not exaggerating when I say in 20 levels played there has been genuinely only 3 or 4 levels that have stood out in any way at all and that's being generous. Otherwise every single level has just be walking through extremely boring mazey corridors using extremely boring guns against extremely boring enemies.What makes this so sad to not recommend is that the *core* of what here is pretty good. The voice acting is amazing, the atmosphere is amazing, and the story is amazing... but the gameplay is so unbelievably repetitive I cannot bear to put another minute of my time into this game just to find out where it goes and I'm just gonna look up the summary after writing this and be sated. This game would get infinitely better if they actually cut out huge amounts of content. At 20 levels in I think if I had played only 5 of them and go to the same point in the story I'd be enjoying myself a lot more and be super ready to carry on to the end. Sure the game might be only 25% as long then, but it'd be nearly 100% awesome and engaging as opposed to 25% awesome and engaging with 75% bloated tedium.I cannot understand the overwhelmingly positive reviews and was unfortunately fooled into persevering with this for much longer than I otherwise would have in the hope that it somehow "picked up"... Nope, it just goes on and on and on with the same basic boring pseudo maze of copy paste corridors and rooms and the same 3 - 5 enemy types which all die in 2 bullets or 1 melee anyway.Huge respect to the devs for the atmosphere, writing, music and everything else. But man it just needed A LOT more variety or A LOT less content.

_childDocuments_.review: This doesn't need to be long. Shooting feels good but not tight and pointed and sometimes you'll be jumping into walls so much you'll realize it's better to just find focus and slow things down without every diving. Seems like that misses a point but the point ends up being more in the words and what's being said to you and how that feels alongside the pulsing music. It's synesthesia. It's a man trapped and suffocating and with a broken person that can't seem to be better than they are. It's a man stuck in cycles and the endless, almost repeating corridors at least fit the vibe, if not someone's capacity for repetition. If you've found yourself unable to find a worthwhile good wholesome piece of you again, out of abuse or alcohol or any other ailments, it's worth the ride and rhythm and all the loud shooting. James Savage has a story worth hearing.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! 9.5/10 Really solid game - if I'm super picky there's def some polish notes here or there, but I had a blast. Played on intended difficulty and felt it was a pretty good level of challenge mixed with flow. Tutorial was perfect. Levels have nice lengths and designed quite well to hide the linearity. The action is solid and the game's atmosphere is harmonious with the narrative. Just enough sprinkled in comedic elements to not take away from the vibe.Occasionally the difficulty spikes, sometimes a tad too much, particularly with boss fights, but was fine. You learn the patterns of each enemy type and get into a flow of how to take care of them effectively. In a couple spots, wished there were some more checkpoints. Bullet time was great, but never figured out how to effectively use the dives. Rolled into the endless abyss and got stuck a few times and I enjoyed the ending. I did feel the build up to the ending could have been 2-4 chapters shorter actually, or could have used a new enemy type to keep things interesting.Would highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, but it did leave me with some mixed feelings. You definitely have to be into the narrative, otherwise the whopping 50 chapters will seem like a huge slog. I did almost give up on it once or twice, but there's a few reasons for that as I see it.Firstly, the gameplay is great, but the level design gets very repetitive. Some levels are really short, some are really long, but all of them are the same thing. Rescue hostages, shoot things, get to the elevator, chapter over. It's between the chapters where you get cutscenes adding more narrative context that really kept me going. The Max Payne inspiration is such a central part of the game, but I don't feel like it's done very well. James is *extremely* moody, bordering on sounding bored. I just don't think he has the noire voice in him.The game suffers also from a lack of any form of progression or levelling up system. There's no inventory upgrades or health upgrades or weapon mods or upgrades. Just run and gun, and while it does feel vaguely like an arena shooter, I feel it stretches itself in too many directions and doesn't excel at any of them.Having said that, where it really shines is it's style, narrative and world building. James is a burnout alcoholic who has been in an abusive relationship with a reincarnation of Dracula for who-knows-how-long. Not only that, their twist on the Vampire formula is very unique. The cinematography and style is absolutely stellar, too.Fully recommend this to anyone who likes a shooter or likes Lovecraftian voids that are filled with ancient Egyptian Pharaoh/Vampire hybrids, formless all-powerful entities, werewolves and creepy puppet masters.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I thought this would be good as i've tried their other games demo, but its so very boring. Walk the same corridors, shoot brainless zombies and dogs. Insert some pretentious monologue between each level. Get a new gun every 5 levels. Thats the game. And its got 50 levels bro, why... You cant make a cool narrative work with zero interesting mechanics besides slomo. Add something more (weapon upgrades, new moves) or introduce things quicker or cut the game down. As much as I would have liked to get to know the story, I cant make myself launch this game again. Dont buy unless you can do the same thing for 7-10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game based on vibes and was very quickly disappointed. Clunky controls paired with simplistic and incredibly repetitive gameplay. Some of the positive reviews say it wears thin by the end, but for me it wore thin in the first 30 minutes.The dive mechanics, featured heavily in the trailers, is a microcosm of this game's flaws: as far as I can tell, there's no reason to ever dive, especially since a dive leaves you stationary and vulnerable at its end. You can dive through windows to get a little distance from enemies, but the level layouts are so lazy and, again, you're left stationary at the end of the dive, that it doesn't seem worth the trouble since the enemies you're diving away from are still likely just around a corner and will catch up to you while you stand. With less recovery time or more interesting level layouts, or maybe different enemy types, maybe this mechanic would be worth using, but as it is, you're basically better off just kiting enemies around patiently taking taking your shots, which, while it works, is pretty boring.I'll add that I never played Max Payne, which the positive reviews mention frequently, so perhaps if you're a fan of that series, this game would feel better. If you're like me, though, don't expect much.

_childDocuments_.review: I have very mixed feelings on this game. It does everything phenomenally...except the actual gameplay. The story is a fantastic and genuinely moving depiction of female on male abuse that we really never see in media. The soundtrack is so good I'd honestly recommend listening to it on it's own, and the environments are intensely atmospheric and absolutely stunning at times. Honestly though I'd recommend watching a playthrough of the game or just the cutscenes as a movie, because to be blunt the gameplay is a slog, with only the first and last few levels truly being enjoyable. This is due to three major factors. First it's shockingly difficult. This unfortunately is for frustrating reasons like poor enemy dispersal, insane spawn clusters, almost all enemies gank rush you, and dodging projectiles is a crapshoot. Dying in this game feels random as opposed to a challenge to be met. I ended up having to drastically reduce the difficulty to even play which I'm not used to with other shooters. Second this game is quite repetitive, with almost every level having the exact same formula for mapping, enemies, and hostage rescue with new challenges or components rarely if ever being introduced. Third, the game is very, VERY long, far longer than is justifiable for a tps in general but especially with its gameplay issues. With 48 levels ranging from 10 to 30 minutes long the vast majority of this game feels like filler. If this game was 12 levels gameplay issues would feel minor compared to the compelling story. If the gameplay flaws were fixed I could even see 24 levels working. But even if this game were perfect 48 levels with a minimum 10 minute length would still feel like a chore, let alone with such glaring flaws.So ultimately I'd recommend you WATCH this game in a playthrough or cutscene comp and listen to it's soundtrack on spotify, because the story and music are both something special. But because of that I wouldn't taint those things for yourself by grinding though 48 versions of the same level.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely worth a play-through.Do buy it!The rest of this review will be nitpicks.This baby has FIFTY levels somehow, but not all of them are bangers. Some are mash. Most are fun.There are a lot of levels that feel similar, because they follow a similar pattern (explore, save the innocents, return to the elevator. Rinse and repeat.)Not all of the armory is particularly useful IMO, I mainly used two of the guns and switched it up only a couple of times when I ran low on ammo. YMMV.I also didn't do *that* many slow-mo dives, because it's actually kind of hard to aim when you're doing it.Binding slowmo to a thumb button on my mouse and maining the Strikebreaker (Thompson) made combat so trivial that I had to just stop doing that.Not all of the bestiary is that compelling to fight, and it takes until late game to see more interesting combinations of enemies in "combat puzzles". Some of these combinations are bafflingly frustrating, but most are fine.For some reason, melee enemies have no windup or telegraphing for their attacks, they just come out instantly and do a ton of damage (on intended difficulty, at least). This explains some of the complaints I saw about boss fights in this game, of which there are three, because they all kinda have this problem.Last, the story is a bit of an overwrought homage to Another Thing. I can tell they had a very fun time making it, I just got a little impatient with the super serious, flowery monologue that runs through the entire game.The levity you get from the musical levels doesn't fully offset it to me, either.Some of these freestyles are a level of corny I did not think was possible.Break ♥♥♥♥, Kill People is an all-timer, though.Anyway that's it.Sorry for the ♥♥♥♥ sandwich, it really is a good game and you should play it :))))))))

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Get this game even if you're not into the gameplay. Get it for the amazing story.When I heard about this game, I wasn't someone who was familiar with the Max Payne franchise, still not. What got me interested was the action horror & the melancholic but sentimental as ♥♥♥♥ story, the tone of which was what grabbed me especially. From the demo & Nightmare, its spin off, it looked like this game was gonna be amazing. And I was right!The controls feel nice & responsive, with the gunplay feeling amazing, making for satisfying gameplay. I can't stress how amazing unloading a whole shell into a knight feels... That and having modifiers at the START is also an amazing choice. The lore reason of the void pulling from memories to make the levels and doing the twists it does with them made levels very memorable, not once feeling like a location is overstaying its welcome. The music is also another stellar aspect, not too distracting but also energetic enough to keep things fun, the rapping included. And of course, the story is the game's biggest highlight. Right off the bat (heheh), James is already an interesting & likeable character, and seeing him develop felt so good! Overall, all the named characters are interesting, understanding and then some!In terms of bad things, the game *is* a bit glitchy. Sometimes you get stuck in things, sometimes when you die, you instantly respawn with invincibility and no guns and the amount of enemies the game spawns can make it start to slow down & stutter, visuals & audio included.With that being said though? I honestly think this might be my GOTY. It's a thrilling & hard hitting experience that made knowingly getting the game BEFORE the price correction more than worth it.I'm going to be thinking about James Savage for a good bit now. I hope living gets to feel good for him again, even if he falls down the well for the last time.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the gameplay is bad and this is because the Max Payne, bullet time style doesn't mesh well with melee focused bad guys. You don't really need to use the dive and it's often a bad idea to because it leaves you vulnerable on the split second stand up. On top of this there is very poor enemy variety, you'll spend the first hour shooting the same guys and you'll get the shotgun at the 40 minute mark. The writing and voice acting are good but as a gameplay purist the minimum is the game being at least as good or better than Doom.

_childDocuments_.review: Passion project with a lot of love put into it. Sadly did not equate to me loving it. I beat 15 out of the 50 or so chapters, so obviously, I didn't get the full experience. That being said, it only takes a couple of chapters in a novel to realize whether or not the prose is to your likingEvery single line of written dialogue was just awful to me. Shockingly bad writing. Made even worse by the performance. All lines are spoken in whispers, in what I could call a very misguided delivery. Didn't care for the soundtrack either.The game heavily, HEAVILY pulls from Max Payne. The painkillers and slo-mo dive are the most obvious comparisons. The thing is, that dive worked very well with the type of gameplay Max Payne was going for. Diving from cover to cover, with bullets zipping by, is what made that mechanic work. When you are being pursued by zombie-like enemies, the absolute worst thing you can do is plant yourself on the ground prone. You aren't diving through doors breaching rooms either, instead majority of time enemies are busting into the room you are in.Judging by public opinion, there is a high chance you'll like this game, it just grated me in the wrong way.

_childDocuments_.review: This game wanted to be like max payne, but diving just locks you into an animation where you'll likely just get mobbed on because you belly flop. So you actually end up just doing dark souls rolls instead to dodge everything rather than the slow mo dive shoot. Slow mo gives you a damage buff, and you can turn it on without diving so I found myself just turning it on for a single frame before landing a headshot, then turning it off again. This left me in a state of infinite damage buff which I don't think was the intended way to play, but I still had a good time playing this game, and despite this it still had its challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: To me this was a bit of an unpolished slog. I thought the game feel was slightly worse than the 20 year old game it was emulating. It's stylish as hell visually and musically but it just didn't feel very good. Animations always felt like they were interfering with each other. Enemies are brain dead and are really only a threat when set up as traps or spawned on top of you. Slow mo was most useful standing straight up and just taking the time to aim. Really not much incentive to do cool dives and rolls. You can't really shoot through those animations anyway! There were some solid moments of fun though. It wasn't all bad. Sound FX were on point! Good shotgun!As for story. It took me about 9 hours to beat which wound up being a little too long to spend with characters that ultimately felt like irredeemable plain old bad people. I did like the writing and voice acting but our hero and villain are maximum toxic. Maybe 15 or so fewer levels might have been best for this game. Mild thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere wears its inspiration clearly on its sleeve, and that is of Remedy's Max Payne series. The gunplay is very reminiscent of those games, as is the "bullet time" or slow-mo mechanics. The gunplay is very tight, and the guns are satisfying to use.The game starts off interestingly enough, with great ambiance and intrigue. However, after 6 hours in (and defeating the first major boss), I was feeling the tedium of the gameplay loop, enemies and environments start to set in. So, I decided to check on how much game was remaining, and I was shocked to learn that I likely have several more hours left!While I don't feel there's anything fundamentally wrong with the game (it gets a lot right), it very much gives me the feeling of "are we there yet"? I want for it to be over so I can learn about the conclusion to the story, but I don't want to slog through more of the same levels and combat scenarios.
