_childDocuments_.review: I quite enjoyed the vibes, music, and general structure of the levels! This is the 1st game of its kind for me, so I had some learning to do. In that regard, I find El Paso Elsewhere one of the most approachable action games I have played. You can adjust the gameplay options for an extra challenge (or extra help) if you want it. I look forward to diving into this world again and continuing James Savage's journey.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is it clear how much the creator improved from the last El Paso, this is an amazing game on it's own. A bit corny at times, but it's so heartfelt and endearing in it's story, it felt very personal. I loved the exploration of the main character.And the gameplay is very good. It's Max Payne yes, but the level and enemy design really elevate it. Encountered a bug or two, and started having some pretty bad performance issues at times on the second half of the game that actually messed me up on some encounters. But they didn't take away from the overall experience. I absolutely recommend this, and hope this developer and his team the best
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Hey do you like guns? Slow-mo? Guns in a slow-mo dive? While things explode around you?Well okay you don't always get that last bit but you DO get everything else as you take this wild and absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ depressing and sobering trip into Hell while watching our main man come to terms with the trauma and abuse he's received via his ex girlfriend who is a vampire, and how this prior relationship absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ him up forever. You might cry! Or at least have a long hard think.In all seriousness, the writing and acting and soundtrack are outstanding. The presentation does have chances to be a smartass, which is nice, so it's not entirely doom and gloom. Between that and the super-focused gameplay of gunning down monsters Max Payne slow-mo style, it is one helluva crazy experience. I was enthralled with every second of it and I am very glad that I live in a world where this game exists.Game of the Year material, hands down.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that completely nails and understands the run and gun feeling of Max Payne 1 and 2, the problem is that most of the levels get too repetitive with the main mechanic being go in > rescue hostages > leave, but that can be somewhat fixed by playing in bursts, play a couple of levels then continue later. Story is good, dialogue and voice acting also carries a lot of this game, go in blind as much as you can, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso Elsewhere takes elements usually found in walking simulators, and mixes them into a short but satisfying Max Payne-esque third person shooter. It's one of those kinds of games that if you vibe with every part of it, it'll feel like one of the best games ever- but if you're not keen on any singular part it won't feel as good. The shooting mechanics are solid, but don't push any boundaries. The slow-mo, dodge roll, and dives are fun to play with, but ultimately it was easier for me to blast them away with the shotgun up close, hose them with the repeater, or snipe them from afar with the rifle rather than engaging in combat acrobatics.The level design is equally serviceable, feeling more like a chaotic funhouse maze than an explorable environment. There are a couple of large setpieces that help break up the monotony from time to time, but they were few and far between. It fit the story quite well, as you’re trapped in a twisted liminal space conjured from the antagonist’s tormented past, and the repetition was an intentional game design choice to highlight James’s struggle against the void. Making the level design more ‘fun’ would have created a disconnect between what the player is feeling and what James was. El Paso, Elsewhere is meant to be a struggle, and while that limits its replayability and fun factor for people who don’t vibe with the plot, it made everything feel far more interesting for me. It’s also fairly short, so the drudgery never became a true negative.The collectables were a neat highlight, but few and far between. The projectors were a neat window into James & Janet’s deteriorating relationship, but the radios and their hilarious non sequitur pill cop episodes or one-off jokes provided small bouts of levity that inspired me to actively seek out on every level. Unfortunately, some are pretty hard to find, so I didn’t get them all. Visually, El Paso, Elsewhere belongs roughly 18 years in the past, with low-poly models, visibly pixelated textures, and modernized lighting that creates a very brooding, liminal aesthetic that feels both unique and nostalgic. There’s a very distinct visual style and intentionality to how El Paso, Elsewhere looks that I think helps set it apart dramatically in a market that went past oversaturation years ago. Some people might dismiss it for looking archaic, but I personally love how it looks. The OST is in two parts- the background music which is solid score with a surprisingly number of tracks. I’m not kidding, there are more songs than levels to the game- and while a lot are pretty short, the sheer variety present really helps break up the intentional monotony of the core gameplay loop without undercutting the immersion.The second part are 11 tracks of experimental rap songs that kick in during pivotal moments of the game. As someone who rarely listens to rap/hip hop, I found myself rather drawn to each song as they played, as they’re quite catchy and due to their tailor-made nature fit the gameplay of each moment perfectly. The story is where El Paso, Elsewhere really shines through however, told through a series of skits and monologues during gameplay and between levels, where James reflects on his life while traveling through the void on an old hotel elevator. They’re very raw, emotionally, and I could not help but be sucked into James’s mixture of self-depricating humor, genuine regret at a life lived poorly, his enduring love for Janet, his rising resentment towards the void and its denizens, and his compelling acceptance in the face of his looming death.I didn’t expect to empathize with James as much as I did, and now that I’m finished I feel an odd sense of relief and loss. On reflection, I think it’s because most protagonists tend to be blank slates and everyman type characters, so having a game where you play as a distinct and distinctly broken person felt like an incredible breath of fresh air for me. Ultimately, the El Paso, Elsewhere wasn’t particularly deep, nor did it go particularly far, and it didn’t need to. Instead, it delivers one of the most emotionally immersive experiences I’ve ever seen in a game. On a pure gameplay level, it loses its novelty after the first hour or so and drags on for another six, but every other core element of the game carries it hard for the rest of the duration. It’s an art house film in gaming form, with all the benefits and handicaps that brings, and even though I only finished it a few hours ago I’m already craving more- both of games of a similar caliber, but also from Strange Scaffold as well.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable homage to Max Payne in a supernatural setting. The gameplay is well crafted even if it is a bit easy, I had to raise the damage taken in the modifiers menu as I was almost constantly filled with maximum ammo and painkillers. The story did not quite work for me, but it was engaging enough to make me keep playing. The game feels a bit longer than it needs to be, due to a lot of reuse of level environments. As for the soundtrack, I am not a hip-hop fan, but it wasn't as off-putting as I expected it to be.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix fun Max Payne gameplay, vampires, great voice acting, a tight narrative, and PlayStation 2 graphics but with 2023 camera, lighting, and shader capabilities? You get the phenomenally made El Paso, Elsewhere. I wasn't even 10 minutes in and I was already sold on the experience I was about to have. One hour later and I can safely say that this is one of my favorite games of the year and I'm thoroughly looking forward to seeing what the upcoming hours have in store for me as it's only going to get crazier I feel.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: What a truly great game. You can see the developers passion in every ounce of this game, it absolutely oozes style and is all the better for it. The voice acting is great; I would say to the same level of AAA studios. The soundtrack absolutely slaps and every track I could see myself listening to out of game. The gameplay is... well basically max payne so you know; fantastic. All of that said the only issues I had were that it ran a little long and can become slightly tedious/boring due to the gameplay never really diverting from move and shoot; with very little interaction with the levels themselves besides breaking objects for resources. Boss fights were generally quite easy as well and lacked evolving mechanics.Otherwise; this game is fantastic, especially for it's price point, and the entire development team should be proud of what they've accomplished.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I'm mixed on this game (and I'm not finished with it yet, probably). BLUF; Maybe get it on sale if it piques your interest. - I enjoy the narrative style, and the story being told. The narrative style is easily the best part of this game. - Though the music is not to everyone's tastes, I enjoy it for the most part. Blood Pressure sounds corny on the surface, but if you listen to it without any of the in-game sound effects covering stuff up you get a disturbing tale of a mass shooter that has no right being as catchy as it is. - The gameplay is...very basic feeling. It's not bad, but it's not great. The diving slow-mo was/is virtually unneeded except in very niche situations up until the first real Boss fight of the game - and I can't tell if I'm just bad at that fight or what but I've found it very tedious in an unfun way, so much so that I put the game down halfway through that fight and haven't fired it back up yet. I'm not certain how much I'm looking forward to the final third of this game as a result. - Complaints about the game feeling padded are warranted, imo. The first 30 chapters went by fairly quickly (4 hours minus cutscene run times, I guess), but a fair number of levels felt unnecessary and didn't have story-critical scenes or beats tied to them to really justify going through a rapidly repetitive number of set pieces and the same 4-5 enemy types. It hasn't ruined the game for me, but I can definitely sense a hesitancy in myself to go back to doing the same rote combat for another hour just to see the next plot beat.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's very clearly inspired by Remedy's Max Payne, from the slow mo shooting, to the audio drama's playing on the radio. The game is also dialogue heavy like max payne. The game plays smoothly except for a glitch where your screen can become black a simple restart will fix the issue. The story in this game is pretty good and will keep you playing to find out what happens in the end. However this game suffers from being too long. This wouldn't be an issue however the variety in locations and enemies are not much and therefore you keeping revisiting the same areas changed a little and fighting the same enemies. However I definitely recommend picking up this game when it goes on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Huge fan of noir, urban fantasy and Max Payne, and still wasn't fully sold watching the trailers. Picked it up though and man does it deliver. The cutscenes and music are the highlights for me, it's movie level voice acting and direction. The gameplay is great as well, when you have a small dev team like this likely did, everything works together in concert so well, really sells everything. Brimming with passion.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Max Payne meets From Dusk Til Dawn.  Did you love Max Payne 1?  Gunplay: 10/10Shocking good VO work, I was invested in both gameplay and story. And the music?  Holy hell the music.  The main character even starts riffing to the songs mid battle, it works oddly well.Played it for two days straight, finished it in about 9 hours.  Highly recommend if you're in the mood for a twitchy action shooter on a trippy level
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Much like the hero in the game's story, I felt myself being pulled deeper the further I went in El Paso, Elsewhere. It's Max Payne turned a few degrees. You kill a lot of vampires, werewolves, even a strange puppeteer or five. The controls are tight enough to help you do it in style, especially in that Payne-like slow mo. You'll stay for the story though. That's what puts its hooks in you and pulls you deeper. Get those headshots, find that next elevator, get that next hit to the heart. Or to the ears, from the soundtrack.I think I'll remember this game for a good long while. Like I do a couple others: CrossCode, for one; Haven, for another. If you're looking for another good time. Anyway, I think you should give this one a go.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere is one of the best video games I’ve ever played. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The writing, the narrative, the voice acting, the soundtrack, the level design, the gun feel, the difficulty, the secrets. Chef's kiss. Best video game soundtrack ever, easily. It starts a little samey but give it a couple hours and you'll be in love.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't finished it yet, but I wanted to thank the devs for making the exact sort of action horror game I love. Distinct and interesting enemies, surreal environments that you are rewarded for exploring, and the only jumpscares are ones that show up organically during gameplay. You guys are scratching an itch I haven't had scratched in a long while
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: If you love the original Max Payne games, this will be up your alley. Pros:- Fun gameplay- good weapon feel- unique music- good writing- great voice acting.Cons:- Sometimes the camera movement does act weird now and then but never during combat.- Felt the game did run a bit too long and levels started to get a bit boring - I wish there were more variety of enemiesOverall i say get the game if you're into Max Payne mixed in with cosmic horror.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if all the fantastical metaphors in the first Max Payne weren't actually metaphors, but were very real in the world and you played as Constantine from Swamp Thing. A really refreshing and surprising indie release paying its tributes to the likes of Max Payne, with certain influences from Control in terms of presentation and the surreal vibe it has going for it. The slow-mo combat is really satisfying, the presentation is really stylish and competent and I love it. The OST is also great and adds a lot to the game, is always used to heighten the adrenaline and I have to commend the effort by Strange Scaffold. The flaws it has is the lack of enemy variety and that it's a bit too long for what the experience asks for. Though the level progression and the mixups of familiar environments helps make the already seen locations stay fresh, with the present arsenal of weapons and amount of enemies, it simply doesn't warrant the game being 40 chapters long. Since it took so much from Max Payne 1, it also should have studied its careful and air-tight pacing a bit more. Otherwise, a worthy effort and a good game overall, I enjoyed my experience with it quite a lot and the core gameplay loop is really fun and engaging, which it has to be since that's mainly what you're going to be doing for the 99% of your game time. This is easily one of my favorite releases from 2023!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: A real boon to anybody looking to play an action game channeling the boundless energy of early 2000s bullet-time shooters. Great selection of weapons, the mechanics around melee and staking are excellent, and the movement options between diving and wall-kicks are fantastic.The soundtrack is incredibly deep across FIFTY levels and will continue to surprise and delight with a huge range. It's a perfect complement to the narrative which is full of poignant moments and deep cuts. Excellent game!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem from Strange Scaffold. I have been following the game's production and director himself for a while, and have been so excited to see this game's eventual release, and it plays SO damn well and smooth, and the art direction and cinematic shots are beautiful. However my favourite part of this game (as a sound designer) is the music, audio and sound design. Everything about the audio is so tasteful and perfect and I have great respect for RJ Lake. I already have the vinyl for SWOTS and definitely would love to have a physical edition copy of the EPE hip hop album.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Strange Scaffold games have always had a pathos underlying the absurdity with most of their games. Be it a walking sim with PNGs of dogs where you explore the touching relationship of the last two people on earth, to a thrilling mystery about found family and tragedy playing poker with a bunch of ska loving animals, but this has to be the rawest, hardest they've ever hit me directly in the soul. While it is as every bit a loving, tongue-in-cheek homage to Max Payne style shooters, it also has some utterly crushing moments, propped up by some exceptional voice acting. It took me about 8 hours to beat this game, but I promise you I'll be thinking about it for weeks.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game during a year of amazing games. It starts off as Max Payne at its craziest and escalates from there. One part love letter to old shooters, one part comedy horror love story and mix-tape, one part processing the trauma of abuse and the cycle of addiction, non-stop fun from beginning to end. Impeccably written and voice acted, it's a guns blasting, bass thumping, wild ride taking James Savage down to the bottom of the world, full of oddities and surprises.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: this game is amazing from top to bottom, it's fun and funny and honestly super cool, I love it! the story and voice acting is incredible too. It's hard to put down after a level because that narrative and those cutscenes keep drawing me back in.... the soundtrack blows me away on top of all that, just really excellent game, would recommend hands down
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game that pays homage Max Payne, which I'm a big fan of.  But, it's also a good example of a game that both starts and ends strong, with the middle being weak.  It took me 7 hours to roll credits, and it feels like it should've been trimmed down to about 4 hours long.  After a while the fatigue sets in as you fight the same enemies in the same level design over and over again.  The story is interesting but it's drawn out and also needed tightened up.Overall, it's worth playing, but I would wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: its good.It took me time to get into writing and vo but once i did i really started to appreciate it, there's a lot more going on than i thought from just being an outside observer, and even after that i grew to really appreciate how the story and writing is handled.The game is maybe a bit to easy outside of one bad boss fight, and is also maybe a bit to long, even for as short as it is, I had a very good time, much better than i thought i would. and i understand that the music is going to be hit and miss, but when the music does hit, it goes really hard.I do recommend El Paso, Elsewhere, even for the hesitant, Its worth taking a chance on.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I came for the Max Payne feel of the gameplay, I stayed for the story. Was a lot more meaningful and close to home than I would have anticipated. Only major complaints I have is there could have been more variety in the boss fights (or more in general for that matter), and that using the grenade launcher on a large group of enemies is playing Russian Roulette on whether the game will turn into a stuttering mess afterward. Could be my PC, could be me streaming it, could be the game, not sure really.Gameplay absolutely FEELS like Max Payne. It's slick, smooth, and stylish, and your best bet in a combat arena is to keep moving at all times. Graphically it may not seem to impress for those wanting more than PS1 style characters, but the atmosphere will make up for it in level design. Music had a good variety that kept me bobbing my head to the beat wanting to avoid death just so I don't interrupt it. No major game breaking bugs aside from the grenade launcher possibly tanking performance on use, though I did encounter some smaller ones like infinitely reloading the shotgun (fixed by swapping through all my weapons), or somehow having TWO rounds loaded into the launcher (even firing both off lol).Overall if you like Max Payne or Remedy shooters, this is a love letter to them with it's own uniqueness. Buying this was no mis-stake.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: While I struggled so much with the Egyptian king boss that I had to set the damage modifier to zero and turn on infinite ammo, the rest of this game is excellent. I just wish the mid way boss wasn't so impossibly difficult. I don't know if I'm not dodging correctly, or doing something else wrong, but this is a great game!It's funny, I hardly died throughout the 50 levels, and the final boss is very easy compared to the level 30 boss. This is a fun game, the amount of enemies you effortlessly massacre through is crazy, the slow mo is awesome, and the soundtrack is unique and BANGING. I got this for full price I think, $20ish, so just get this game. It's not much even at full price and it's a damn fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's absolutely nuts how good this game is. In a world full of bloated, lifeless AAA open world games with absolutely zero passion or substance to be found in them, El Paso, Elsewhere is a wonderful reminder that video games can be stylish, fun to play, and above all, incredibly emotional works of art that actually have something to say. This game has INCREDIBLE voice work, an INCREDIBLE soundtrack, and FANTASTIC writing, all bound together by gameplay mechanics that know that they don't need to be complex in order to be fun and, most importantly, very very cool. The soundtrack alone makes this game worth it, but everything else on top makes this game an INCREDIBLY easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: The combat in this game is really fun and the music is great, but for me the real standout qualities are the story and the graphics. Without getting too much into spoilers, the story takes a surprisingly deep look at a bad relationship (with some very funny bits thrown in). I didn't think I would like the simple graphics at first, but they are used to great effect. The environments are inventive and will re-use elements you've seen a hundred times in interesting ways. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Story and voice acting are definetely my favorite part about this game, the cutscenes are simple but well made and there's  alot of them, really good stuff. The gameplay is fine i guess? gunplay and movement feels good but there's not enough enemy variety to force you to use all of your fancy max payne like dodges and bullet time.Overall i enjoyed my time with it even if it felt like it could've been 2hrs shorter.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Max Payne-style shooter that plays better than most modern shooters but *looks* like a PS1 game. And I do mean that in a good way. It is DRIPPING with style from the way James Savage slow-motion dives through windows to the music that accompanies him as he rescues innocent people from the ritual sacrifice his vampire ex girlfriend has planned for them.I'm so glad I checked this game out, even though it didn't look like it would be for me.- Matt
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is assembled perfectly- the story, the voice acting, the gameplay loop, the level readability. The game is extremely addicting.At first, I was bothered by the fact that the MC shoots both pistols at once instead of one at a time- then I realized how overpowered the headshots are in these game. It takes after Max Payne 3 in that regard.The Level Gimmicks are well spaced. Some things you'll have to dive through, sometimes you need a key for a door. At first, the nosferatu looking "feeders" will be all you face- but then they add new ones at the perfect time.And another thing- the cinematics, writing, and performance is incredible. They all hit extremely hard, like this was the passion project you had after college and yeah it took a long time to make but it was absolutely worth it. The gaming market is better with this game in it.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the price of admission this is a game with good game play and  a mood which carries you through the game. Heads up for discussion of  abusive relationships and addiction.The one thing you should be aware going in is that the game has some of that indie jank to it. all of the bugs I ran into were fixed by restarted the level but I'd be lying If I said that they didn't kick me out of it and make me put down the game for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development eagerly, fully sold on the premise of a heavily Max Payne inspired game by Strange Scaffold. I'm not disappointed!I'm only a couple of hours in but I'm thoroughly enjoying the experience, both the bullet time shooter action and most importantly the amazing story line, cutscenes and soundtrack. The vibe is just what I was looking for, an indie gem that doesn't hide its inspirations but sublimates them into a unique and artful experience.Oh and that sexy voice acting...!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere is a deft, hefty game that sucks you in and doesn't let go until the end. Best played in chunks, the game has a total of 50 small levels that each contribute to the narrative while providing dense, packed microcosms of gameplay. Despite some bugs and running just a touch too long, this game is going to keep you on your toes and stick with you until well after the credits roll. Highly recommend. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I had initially tried this out via... naughty means, however almost the moment I started playing, when I first came to the radio playing "Pill Cop", I realised this is more than just "inspired" by Max Payne; its a full on love letter to Remedy and Sam Leak's whole body of work. You've got everything here, Payne, Wake and Control too. When I realised just how much of a work of passion this is I had to go actually buy it IMMEDIATELY.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface this by taking this review with a grain of salt, as someone who's not played and/or seen much of Max Payne itself, something this game takes a lot of inspiration from (and appears to excel in narratively.)- An overall absolutely incredible journey, from beginning to end, and would easily be my pick for one of the best stories of 2023. There's a great balance of comedy vs tragedy to keep the metaphorical roller coaster structurally sound in the light of a lot of recent games that steer too hard in either direction. - The soundtrack is absolutely phenomenal (Blood Pressure is my honest favorite of the rap tracks) and I like the mix of genres it's got going to really work in tangent with the craziness of the void. While there's a lot of instrumental tracks I personally wasn't really attached to there's absolutely none I could say are necessarily "bad" or "garbage." - The gameplay loop itself does get a little bit boring towards the end, even with all the cool gadgets and enemy varieties they hand you, to the point that I found myself really just trying to run for my life instead of dispatching everything (and getting killed a handful of times because of it to be fair.) - I found myself pretty much only using slow-mo and dive movements if I was in a REALLY bad spot, despite both being seemingly core to the game, rather than rationing the slow-mo as the game progressed since it almost felt a little too easy with it, though I'd also argue that's not a bad thing either as having the overall difficulty be tailored so that really ANYONE could pick up and play is great for accessibility. TL;DR an amazing game that I highly suggest getting.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso Elsewhere's strong style and even stronger, very humanizing writing continue the trend set by Strange Scaffold's previous games, this time in a more ambitious title and genre. While the combat encounters can get a little repetitive towards the back half of the game, the short mission structure make this an easy game to play in small chunks and ensure the VERY well directed cutscenes are paced out well.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. Like REALLY REALLY good. I love every little part of it (well, as much of it as I played anyway). I am just really really bad when it comes to games and their prices. Even at $19, and that's with tax, I still just don't really feel justified in the purchase. I still really recommend this game though, it's excellent. I love the voice acting and cutscenes, I love the weapons, I love the combat. The enemies are quite fun, and the reactions the main character has to each one is enjoyable. It's an excellent 10/10 game, I am just incredibly frugal and cheap. If it ever goes on sale for like $15, then I will absolutely rebuy it. Or if they add like mod support or something idk.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much more than I expected. A masterclass in how to use an indie budget to make something that punches way above its weight class. The writing is crisp and funny. The music is innovative and unforgettable. It's a love letter to Remedy Games that also manages to be everything Max Payne or Control are, and in some ways even a little more. Protect Xalavier Nelson at all costs, he is an industry treasure.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Max Payne? Do you like the noir genre? Do you like action games? Do you like bullet time? If you do, you'll love El Paso, Elsewhere.You play as a drug addict James on a motel elevator going down "hell" to stop your ex-girlfriend, who happens to be the lord of vampires, from completing a ritual that would cause the end of the world. The elevator takes you to various pocket dimensions called The Void and it is in these pocket dimensions you fight the enemies. There are fifty levels in the game and I kept playing because I wanted to know how the story turns out. My first run completion took 8 hours. To be frank I didnt use that much bullet time feature, everything in the game can be killed without bullet time. I probably used bullet time less than 10 times. The rap soundtrack in this game is amazing, I am glad I bought the soundtrack lol. Overall, I really enjoyed the narrative and action gameplay. I recommend it to people who want a fun action game with noir style story telling. Like I said, if you loved Max Payne 1 and 2, I think you'll love this.I give this a 8.0/10!
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: It feels a bit rude to say "wow this is such a remedy game" since it's going above and beyond, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if it isn't hitting just constantly hitting every single high note that max payne and control made me feel. It's rhythmic, it's goofy, it's impossibly heartfelt and earnest. It truly is something special and I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an interesting concept.The story, though told in short snippets is plenty good.Where it truly shines is the gameplay.Max Payne inspired and polished to an incredibly formula.Also, the dialogue is as wonderfully Payne in delivery. Even the protagonists name fits. "James Savage"It's Texas. Of course they'll have guns.Each is unique enough to stand out. And always useful in it's own way.Never did I feel like any were pointless.Also, you get to insult an indestructible being into turning off god mode so it can have a fight that matters."Because of all the mysteries of Egypt, you were the one, that no one cared to solve."P.S. Just don't forget to hit roll while diving. And try diving while jumping near a wall.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: A game dripping with chilling supernatural action that only Strange Scaffold can deliver. It's a beautiful game with amazing set piece action that will make you feel like a badass, a great supernatural noir action story, and a soundtrack that has the perfect needle drop making you feel like an action star every time it plays. Get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Really strong third person shooter. Feels tight and well constructed, the story goes interesting places and the enemies are mostly fun to fight. The Max Payne elements don't seem to 100% fit to me, feeling a little more like a reference than a considered part of the design, but IMO it doesn't really detract from how strong the game is generally, just maybe a little too much Max Payne gravy on top without having the enemy types to require it for a good 15-20 levels.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Max Payne if Sam Lake from Remedy was less into Chandler and Twin Peaks and more into deadly goth e-girls and experimental hip hop.edit: way more varied that it initially leads on. Some of the set pieces really have modern Remedy level of creativity in them.  Wish shootdodges acted more like in MP games where they take a very little amount of Bullet Time resource. A little movement tech tip for you: The game does not tell you this but you can cancel out of a prone position when shootdodging. You have to time your roll when you are about to land. So you get a shootdodge that changes into a roll (it has I-frames like in From Soft games!) to a standing position really fast and the animation looks cool when you do it. Very fluid.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this one...Gameplay-wise the developers took the best of Max Payne and put a horror spin to it.The shooting is fun, the weapons feel good, especially when you dive headfirst into vampires like an idiot (i love it)What i did not expect to be this good was the writing, the cinematic take on cutscenes, very well done and fits the tone perfectly.A true gem if you ask me.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this generally aren't what I go to for fun. El Paso, Elsewhere is my exception. The punishment system isn't needlessly harsh for dying, increasing the enjoyment for someone of my skill level. The Multiplier sliders for things like Gun Damage and Health really help to take the edge off, too (Or pile the pain on!)Such a big game with So Many levels, each one backed by an amazing soundtrack. I love this game, and will continue to keep my eye on this studio.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: So, it´s basically "Max Payne fighting vampires and Old Testament angels, like the bizarre burning wheels and many eyes ones" set in a motel in El Paso which is also a gateway to hell. And Max Payne´s ex is the vampire trying to end the world.The action is tight, the writing and direction are spotless, the hard boiled noir-ish monologue is amazing. This is a game that knows what it is, and it is heckin awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased El Paso, Elsewhere thinking it was going to be a simple schmup with a simple plot made by people I like.  A day later and I've had the crap beaten out of me by a brutal story about addiction and abuse and what love really is.  I don't know what mental depths the writers drew from but for a game with such simple pixels and polygons, I felt every drop of James' pain and despair.  This is my favorite game that's come out this year.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Explosive and stylish, with a narrative that is instantly engaging and many steps above what games normally strive for. This game threads the needle to deliver a powerful mix of gameplay, aesthetic and audiovisual entertainment. It is not always in a smaller team's scope to develop a product capable of punching above its weight, but clear direction and bold, unapologetic style choices hit this narrow mark.While paying homage to action classics and committing to a lightweight, retro visual style, the Strange Scaffold team has also made the game a UX treat. The game looks old but plays new - and personally I was having too much fun to ever question its looks. The developers know what was important to making the game clear and enjoyable, and were not distracted by anything else.An inspiration for the indie games scene! If there was an endless/procedural mode I would play it for the rest of my days.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I've always been terrible at shooters but even more so in my 40s and it's the same case here with this game, which you'd think would be frustrating. But the story, gameplay, and music are all so compelling, I'm pretty sure I just fell in love with shooters again. Excited to push my way through the rest of this fantastic game.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic video game.  The game mechanic borrows from Max Payne, but the setting characters story are all it's own thing entirely that sucks you in quickly.  I was already hook line and sinker into the game, but when the hip hop kicks in, whoa baby.  Playing on my living room TV via Steamdeck, just a great, very polished experience all around,
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I dived, shot, and staked my way through El Paso in one long adrenaline-fuelled, heart-pounding sitting. And I absolutely loved it.It's a sincere homage to its influences, but totally confident in itself. Beautiful writing, fantastic voice work, striking art direction, and one incredible soundtrack!Superb.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: I think the most succinct review I could give was to say it's a modern take on old games and old mechanics. This is most obvious in the graphics, but also when you have to manually reload instead of just clicking the fire button over and over to auto reload. You have a health bar. Max Payne is obviously a major influence but there are mechanics that remind me of Doom. Just how well the soundtrack matches the gameplay reminds me of Hotline Miami, as does the sometimes frantic nature of the combat. The somewhat surrealistic and changing environment reminds me of Alan Wake.In short, the most succinct review I could give was it's a modern old game. The long form is to say it's like playing games I first played 15+ years ago for the very first time all over again, with the same excitement I had 15+ years ago. It's a really cool game.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is Max Payne-esque goodness. It is very enjoyable. But the story... The story is something else. I am blown away at the quality of the cinematics, the voice acting, and how into everything I get in our interstitial bits of story. It is well worth it. Please buy it. If for nothing else than another game to fight biblical angels in.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Slow Mo Rag-dolls flying around & f++k a werewolf in a bathroom... wish the game had vibration support when firing a weapon as it feels a bit hollow without it, also enemy's don't seems to collide with the player when they are close range and in you're face so thus stabbing is a bit on wonky side its more a swirling battle before you diepretty solid GameCubey ps1ish Psychonautsy max Payne chair breaking simulator with some janky slo mo its very nice needs some polish and more QA as i have fallen threw the map a couple of times and had issues getting stuck on lights and solid structures 'doors' but i  think that's just more me pushing the games physics... i think.... hopefully i can update this after some patches :) solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: im super hyped 3 hrs in, played the demo before release as well, my love for the game might be biased but here it goes:walking a hallway and suddenly slow mo kicks in -a bunch of monsters bash the doors on the sideways - a super hyped track kicks in as you jump forward and blast the heads with your dual 1911 and the protagonist wraps up everything with a perfect non cringy deep analogy about what just happened. its awesome
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: a great Max Payne-like; it's wild that this is the closest thing we've come to the greatness that is Max Payne 2.+ story and voice performances are fantastic+ guns, slow-mo, movement all feel really quick and smooth+ level design is super playful, just like Max Payne 2- the game is a bit too long- the first 1/3 has great setup and the final 1/3 really gets going, but the middle 1/3 drag a bitOverall worth it if you love Max Payne 1/2 (like me)

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible from beginning to end, imagine twin peaks meets max Payne meets mythological creatures like vampires and werewolves for enemies.Real avant-garde ♥♥♥♥, love the art, love the presentation. _childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: El Paso, Elsewhere so far is a beautifully crafted, immaculately presented and wildly fun homage to some of the classics of the 2000s shooter genre, a truly incredible experience from the jump. Also it has some of the best audio design and original music in a game ive heard in quite awhile, an easy recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Innovation is in the eye of the beholder. 'El Paso, Elsewhere' takes us on a journey that combines voice acting reminiscent of the Max Payne era with graphics that transport us to a new tale while retaining a classic flavor. This game offers a thrilling shooter experience, stunning aesthetics, and the unmistakable mark of Strange Scaffold throughout its world. Don't let it pass you by.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review: Bought at the launch day anti-discount because of Dog Airport Game.  On the surface it's a Max Payne love letter with its inspiration on its sleeve, but very quickly works to set itself apart through its story and hard commitment to psychadelic limbo spaces.  Storytelling and gameplay goes hand in hand and it had me hooked; on top of that, the player input feels perfect.  I had one big performance problem on one stage, found out I was playing that stage incorrectly, and aside from *very small* issues it's been all smooth sailing.The story starts out fun and stupid, but it's done with heart and care and before long you're fully invested in the journey.  The cinematography, voice acting, everything is top notch quality.  The soundtrack is the last thing I expected for this game but man, these tracks are great.  I normally object to lyrics in games as an unnecessary distraction, but here they fit as some hardcore needledrops that amp the pace up, and are spread out across a number of more atmospheric or instrumental tracks so you really feel the weight of those tougher levels.If you're coming from Max Payne the player controls will feel all the same to you, but you'll quickly find yourself dealing with mostly melee-range enemies that swarm you effectively.  It becomes more a game of avoiding danger than dodging it, and I find myself in real-time as often as slo-mo in many situations.I think ammo balance in the early stages can use work and a few other early stages are on the easy side, but as it goes on the game really hits its stride.  It keeps going and I just keep getting pulled deeper in.  I think if you were to wait a bit for a patch, some of the issues like occasional rough checkpoints would probably get a little fine tuned.  But I must stress that the game launched in a great state, and it's worth picking up... right about now.I think it's worth your time and your money, and then some.  No idea how this ties into the Dog Airport Game lore but I've had a great time tearing through this one.  It took me a while to reach the ending and while I do feel that the rescue mechanic is a little surface-level and on the easy side, the story and scene variety had me not only carrying through to the end but dying to see what the next floor would bring.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

_childDocuments_.review:
Somewhere in El Paso, Texas, a three-story motel gained another 46 stories... all below ground.

So, yeah. This is going to get loud.

El Paso, Elsewhere is a supernatural neo-noir third-person shooter. Hunt werewolves, fallen angels, and other damned creatures in a vivid slow motion love letter to action classics. Fight your way through a reality-shifting motel, floor by bloody floor. Save the victims of Draculae, lord of the vampires. Destroy the villain you loved--even if it means dying yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: El Paso, Elsewhere

name: GigaBash
detailed_description: HERE COMES THE ULTIMATE TOKUSATSU SHOWDOWN! Play as a rampaging Titan and send skyscrapers flying with a single punch; or pilot a Titan-hunting Mech and strike your foes with lightning from the heavens. Wreak havoc or chain thrilling combos to gain Giga Energy to transform into your final form, the terrifyingly titanic S-Class . More crossover characters from legendary IPs available as DLCs. Go solo or co-op with a friend to challenge against endless waves of enemies and collect perks to help your journey. Some enemies have mutations too, and even Godzilla characters will invade your playthrough. The further you go, the more epic character skins you’ll unlock. Face off alone against a lineup of 8 random opponents and one Final Boss to get a higher score. Do you dare to crank up the difficulty for a merciless yet satisfying challenge? Uncover the origins (and misadventures) of the Titans in 4 unique single-player storylines . It’s simple, 1-4 players battle each other in a variety of fully-destructible maps to be the last Titan standing. Did you suffer an early defeat? Exact revenge on your foes by firing Orbital Lasers or dropping meteors from the convenience of your grave. Available as Local Play or Online Mode where you can cross-play with friends from all platforms (Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, XBox, Epic Games). A casual party game mode filled with wacky minigames for new and veteran players to enjoy together.

_childDocuments_.review: While I do gave the game credit for providing a fun monster combat game with each of the kaijus actually feeling pretty unique, I still do find it a bit disappointing that I can never see any of the DLC characters I've bought as random opponents in single player.  Take the Civilization series as a weird example.  if I buy a DLC of new civs, then lo and behold, not only can I play as these new civs, the AI has a chance to use these new civs against me when randomly selecting civs.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great homage to games like War of the Monsters and Godzilla Destroy All Monsters Melee!Lots of potential with a fun story mode, couch co-op and online play. I bought it for single player and couch co-op so it works for me.Not a lot of online players at the moment but I'll edit this when/if that changes! The $35 price tag might be a bit daunting to most and may be a stopping block in getting the online portion of the game players. Some free-to-play weekends might help, but I think a $20 price tag would have worked wonders.I look forward to spending more time with this!! Hope to see more Titans/arenas added as time goes on.EDIT: They've added Godzilla and Ultraman. I swear to god if they add mechs from Sentai I'll cry tears of joy.

_childDocuments_.review: I got to play this game and meet the developers at PAX East 2023.  I was instantly hooked after I tried it out. _childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly torn on this.I love the concept and it's a good throw back to some older kaiju fighting games like King of the Monsters, plus they have DLC available for both Godzilla and Ultraman, who wouldn't like that in a game like this? -Unfortunately, the gameplay is limited and the AI can be very cheap (such as clearly aiming only for the player when it's supposed to be a 4 monster free for all).-Actual gameplay, is in fact similar in style to Super Smash Brothers along with some mini game party modes similar to Super Mario Party. Not a bad idea, except...-...There is no option for adjusting the knock back physics. This isn't Smash Brothers or Brawlhalla, these are supposed to be giant monsters in a city. Seeing them being knocked around like a ping pong ball takes away some of the fun of using giant monsters. Giving them some actual weight would better have the experience.-While the maps are mostly pretty nice and look to be a good size, you're restricted to a just a very small piece of them during a fight.-The non-DLC characters provided in the vanilla game, while a nice variety, are also limited in number, if you discount the skin color options, making you almost needing to get the DLC just to flesh out the numbers.-To add to that, the DLC aren't available to the CPU for any random encounters in the single player modes, like the arcade and endless, they're only just for the player to select from.-There is clearly effort put in to flesh out the background on the vanilla monsters which is always good, even a story mode for them, but it's a bit shallow.-The game has online play, but as something of a niche game, unless you already have someone to play with, you likely won't be seeing many online matches.-Range attacks often ignore cover, even for small tanks. The giant buildings on the maps that require actual effort to destroy are just there to annoy you by blocking your movement only, not attacks.In ending, if you like giant monster fights, this is definitely a fun game to play for short periods, but content is limited for it's full price, especially when most everyone is only going to want it to play with the provided DLC monsters. So for the sake of hoping they'll continue to add more to it, I give it a recommended, but only buy it on sale or at least be sure to try the available demo first.
_childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: Like many other reviewers, I have fond memories of games like War of the Monsters and Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters.  This will scratch a similar each thematically.  There are moments that will feel a lot like War of the Monsters, in particular, because of the interactivity with the levels, but I actually think it's a bit more like Power Stone in that it's an arena brawler.  Now that I've laid a comparative baseline, let me just say that I think this game is great, independent of its game influences and give a few reasons why.  Presently, the online matchmaking is very quiet.  I wouldn't bet on finding games at the time of this review.  However, if you've got some buds to play with online or in-person and you like the theme, I don't think you'd be disappointed.  It's worth it, even just for 1v1 IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: This brings back my childhood, reminds me a lot of Ultraman, Godzilla and other monster games from the PS2 era, hoping for more characters in the future. I'd also like to support the developers giving interesting ideas and so on, this game has great potential for bringing back the lost genre that I loved so much!
_childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love it, big fan of the monster design and fighting dynamics, must admit I've been looking forward to this game for quite a while now and I am not disappointed.Honestly if you were looking for a worthy successor to the kaiju battle genre (and I was, I used to love King of the Monsters back then) well you clearly have it. So yeah, great game, good learning curve, unique characters, must admit I like the story mode so far as well, and I'm looking forward to fighting people online and try my skill.So do not hesitate: Destroy Cities, Fight Kaijus, Have Fun, Play GigaBash
_childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brawler, a fighting game for a group, from 1-4 players.The menu gives this away the aim of it being a game aimed at groups though, with Couch play being the first option, then online, then story.There's an Arcade mode, where you have three lives to battle each of the other main characters one after another, like the towers in Mortal Kombat and similar games.An onslaught mode where you can play as an individual or team against growing strength of CPU players.Then there are a fair few mayhem modes to play around with, where you can only hurt other monsters with trees or burgers, or the floor is lava (Literally)The 4 single player campaigns are short, probably around 20 rounds in total, and it's all story-board.Each campaign is 5 maps long, and as you go through the campaign, they get a little longer on each map.Still, an hour or two max.I liked the first 3 campaigns, but then it took a nose dive in the last one, rolling out all the tired old manga tropes and just giving up, losing all the fun that it had flowing.All in all it's a fun game, and you can extend that by ranking up your monsters.Each monster rank only gives news skins, artwork and Background music, there are no actual gameplay improvements from it, so it doesn't become unfair like that.For what it is, it's good, fun and the game AI is quite good.Each monsters plays a little differently but they are all decent enough, no outright stinkers that I could see after unlocking them all.If you intend to play this in a group, then go for it, it's worthwhile and fun to play.But for single player, it is going to be limited, so I'd suggest to wait for a sale, if that is how you intend to play it.I've been playing it with my young nephew and he's really having a lot of fun learning the monsters and playing around with them, as am I.
_childDocuments_.name: GigaBash

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary of all the stuff below: Gigabash is an amazing tribute to giant monster media and a great party fighter to boot. It’s got a really charming personality, the combat delivers pure chaotic fun, and you can easily tell this game was made with a lot of love and care behind it. That all being said, the price tag and a lack of crossplay and releases on other platforms severely damaged the online playerbase since day 1. If you’re a fan of kaiju stuff, I recommend it with some friends on remote play. If you’re here looking for a new party game to play, wait for it to be half off during a sale. I’m sure the devs are already hard at work on adding content and more online support, but as of now there just isn’t enough replayability or players to make the full-priced purchase worth it.The very first video game I ever played was Godzilla: Save the Earth on the PS2 back in 2005. Ever since then, giant monsters and gaming stuck by me. And also ever since, the two rarely mixed. The last decent kaiju games I’ve played (haven’t gotten around to Dawn of the Monsters yet) was Godzilla Unleashed on PS2 in 2007 and a download-only PS3 title in 2012 called ‘Eat Them!’. Pretty long wait. So now, ten years later, comes Gigabash. Was it worth the wait? After 45 hours and nearly 100%ing the game, I can answer that with “Kinda”.Getting the technical stuff out of the way first, controller support works great without issue. I’ve seen a handful of bugs but nothing game-breaking and remote play works surprisingly well, though I’ve heard others having problems there. The online lobbies are peer-to-peer so that means occasional lag. I’ll get more into the online stuff later on.The controls are incredibly simple. It’s similar to Smash Bros. in how moving, blocking, grabbing, or dodging paired with a button performs a different attack. Because of how easy it is to pick up and play, you can have friends who’ve never touched fighting games catch on in a couple matches, which is fantastic for remote play. Chances are you’re here because you’re a fan of the kaiju genre and the old PS2 games like me, and you want to know about the monsters. I’m happy to say the devs did a wonderful job. There’s ten of them currently, all with great animations and designs giving nice twists on their inspirations to help them stand out. I’m really glad the devs went with a campy light-hearted tone for the monsters and their world, it’s a great complement to the party game aspect.Each character has their own strengths and weaknesses in their playstyles. Some focus on speed and projectiles, others are slow but tanky, there’s even a good variety in mobility for each one too. The combat’s depth is in juggling your opponents around in the air with combos, but blocking and countering at the right times to prevent switching places with them.Then there’s the stages; my favorite part of the game. Everything can be thrown, toppled, or torn to pieces. By the end of every match, the whole area is levelled to debris. The fun comes in how each stage has their own creative playground of items and hazards. There’s a Hawaiian city that’s gradually flooded with lava, an Air Force base with all sorts of tanks to pick up and use as weapons, an oil refinery with a missile you can ride on, and over a dozen other maps. I really enjoy how almost everything can be picked up regardless of size. It gets the message across right away that you can experiment a lot with the environments. When it comes to the music, all of the tracks are surprisingly catchy and stick in your head after playing. They sound like music you’d hear in classic kaiju films but modernized and more playful. My favorite gamemode is Mayhem Mode, a series of minigames showcasing all those different items and hazards. These include fighting on thin ice that breaks, sudden death using trees as clubs, and a game of hot potato with a giant sea mine. It’s a shame that it’s exclusive to local/remote play, but I’m sure it’ll be added to online soon.One neat twist to the gameplay is the S-Class mechanic. Destroying the stage and attacking other monsters fills up a meter. Once it’s full, your monster triples in size, giving them a kind of boss fight form. Not only does this encourage players to stay in the fight, but when an S-class monster reverts, energy orbs fly out to make more monsters turn S-Class. It’s a really nice alternative to a timer or sudden death mode while also keeping up the chaotic nature of the combat. There’s also an ultimate ability orb that shows up about two minutes in, allowing for the tables to turn with flashy powers. I kinda wish it took more damage to open since some characters can break it way faster than others.For the single-player experience, there’s four campaigns. Each one’s about half an hour long with five stages each. They have nice artwork during the cutscenes and do a good job teaching you how to play the first four monsters, but that’s about it. It’s serviceable, but nothing special. Think of the story mode as a decent extended tutorial with a little bit of neat lore thrown in to keep you interested.There’s a nice practice range mode and stage for trying out combos. I’m a casual player, so I didn’t use this much, but I can see competitive players getting a kick out of it. Speaking of which, competitive play doesn’t seem to be implemented yet. There’s a grayed out ranked option in the online menu so 1v1s and brawler modes are your only choices. The monsters are balanced fairly well but not to the point of making deep strategies. There’s also no lock-on mechanic so you’ll be missing about a third of your shots. I know I’ve made comparisons to Smash, but if you’re hoping for competitive play, this game’s just not really designed for it. I’m personally ok with this, it is a party game after all, but I just wanted to point that out in case.The few big gripes I have with this game is the online support and the price tag. According to SteamDB, Gigabash’s highest number of players at a time was a little over 200. On average, it ranges from 10-40 players a day, and this just under a month after release. Some people think this is due to a lack of marketing or the kaiju genre being too niche but I believe the major cause is the price tag. $35 is just too much for too little content. You can see all the game has to offer in about 5 hours, and when several other party games are releasing for $15-$20, I really don’t see the price staying the same for long. Don’t get me wrong, I’m all for continuing support for Gigabash through buying future content or merch, but I’d prefer a cheaper game with paid DLC. I hope the game comes to subscriptions services like Xbox Game Pass and PlayStation Plus, feels like a perfect fit for something like this.Gigabash is the giant monster party game I’ve been dreaming of playing for a decade now. The combat is delightfully chaotic and over the top, the characters and stages capture the fun and spirit of kaiju perfectly, and a lot of talent and passion from the devs can be felt when playing. However, in its current state, Gigabash can practically only be played locally, which I really hope is temporary. If you’re just looking for a neat party game to play with friends, wait until a sale or content updates. But if the wait for a good kaiju game’s been long enough for you too, try it out and spread the word if you enjoy it.

The difficulty in each story ramps up slowly, providing a good constant increase in challenge as you go... then you hit the final boss and the difficulty spikes to near impossible levels, becoming a horrible and frustrating experience. _childDocuments_.review: GigaBash feels like a game from another time and I'm here for it. I kicked off a recent games night with this and nothing else got a look in. We all had a blast. A GigaBlast.GigaBash is like Power Stone but with supersized supercharged beasties and other fighters, ranging from a snail that can launch its shell like a mortar to an abominable snow-Kirby that sucks opponents in. It's big and silly and just a ton of fun with friends. There's a solo campaign which I've not touched yet but multiplayer can be enjoyed online or locally, and there's even the option to play in teams, which sounds great.Despite being such an immediate game, it's a lot deeper than it looks. It can seem shallow and chaotic initially but as you get familiar with each character's abilities and movesets, you start poking and retreating, timing certain attacks, blocking, grabbing, throwing things (like buildings. You can throw buildings at each other) and trying to seek out any possible advantage you can get. There's plenty of room here for crafty and skillful play.The arenas are varied and often feature their own quirks like an erupting volcano whose lava slowly covers the map, to some kind of desert test site that houses a big robot you all have to fight/avoid amid the occasional sandstorm. It's also worth mentioning that this is a really polished, well presented game that's got a cool soundtrack too.I can't speak for solo play (with the campaign or online) but if you've got some friends who love a good scrap, then GigaBash comes highly recommended. We don't often get multiplayer games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is as close as you can get to the pipeworks trilogy of godziller fighting games in this day and age besides just emulating those (or playing them on OG hardware). It's a fun monster slapfest with destructible/throwable environments and somewhat super smash bros-like combat where strong attacks frequently send enemies sailing up/backwards. I got the game on sale so the godzilla and ultraman DLCs were definitely worth it for more characters, especially cause I'm a huge Godzilla fan and the dlc packs included most of my favorite Toho kaiju. I'm really thrilled to be playing as Heisei Godzilla, Destoroyah, Kiryu (Mechagodzilla 3), Gigan, and King Ghidorah again! and they all play really well with pretty movie-accurate and seemingly well balanced abilities. This game is much-simplified compared to the pipeworks games in that it uses fewer buttons and has way fewer attacks but the attacks it does have are all much more impactful than the lighter attacks in those 3 classic Pipeworks games (Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee, G: Save the Earth, G: Unleashed if you dont know) but that's not necessarily a bad thing, because like i said each attack is more meaningful to make up for there being less of them so choosing the right attacks, timing them correctly, and comboing them together is even more important than it was in the pipeworks trilogy. there's no ring-out kills like there are in super smash or some other fighting games, but launching an enemy far enough to hit the energy barrier that encapsulates the combat arena does damage, so knocking/throwing enemies over the edge is still powerful. especially since bouncing them off the wall can set them up for another fat smack. I already talked about the inclusion of the monsters from the Godzilla universe but the original Kaiju included in the base game are also really cool and play great actually. I thought they looked a bit too goofy for my taste at first but I warmed up to them pretty quickly. Woolley is still a little too silly only be cause his art style appears to clash with the rest of the game, but Pipijuras, Thundatross, Skorak and Rawa are really awesome imo. I dont hate woolley cause he's kinda cute and funny he just looks a lil too lovable and dumb for my liking. I think they could have made him look a bit more bestial and powerful while still having him look cute and fluffy. But that's okay. I think the rest of the OC characters I havent mentioned are okay-to-good. I havent played the ultraman characters yet but i just bought that DLC because the game is good and i wanted more characters.I have been craving playing as giant monsters and destroying cities while chucking buildings, shooting beams, swinging tails and claws, and jump-kicking at other giant monsters. Get this game and it's DLCs if you like Kaiju action, especially if you enjoy both the pipeworks trilogy and the super smash bros games. It's a lot like a fusion of those 2. I would still kill for a new pipeworks-style Godzilla 3d fighting game with both monsterverse and Toho kaiju but this is the closest i'm gonna get for now and I'm happy it exists. I haven't been this excited about a game in awhile. once you get accustomed to the feel of its combat and the moveset of the monster you're playing, this game feels very smooth and fun and exciting to play. this combat is high impact, high stakes, fun, simple, and easy to pick up but there's definitely enough skill to it that you could spend some time mastering it. TLDR: Highly recommend, you can be Godzilla and 3 more iconic Toho characters if you pay $10 more but the base game is cheap af and the DLC is reasonably priced for the amount of content it offers. Each new character in a game like this offers hours of content if you're gonna actually learn play as/against them. roughly $2.50 per new character is not a bad price at all especially when those characters include Godzilla, Destoroyah, and Kinky Dora. and Gigan. I still recommend this game if you just like the idea of giant monsters fighting but if you like that stuff yet arent a godzilla or ultraman fan, that's strange. Also I just wanna be clear that not only  can you be godzilla, king G, Dest, Hedorah, and mechagodzilla but these characters play ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastically. despite having smaller movesets they have pretty much exactly what moves you'd want them to have and they feel good to use. I thought mechagodzilla kinda sucked until i played him for a few 4-player free-for-all fights, then a couple one-on-ones vs CPU godzilla, then absolutely dominated arcade mode with him. he's just got a little bit more of a learning curve and slightly more drawbacks to consider which can be avoided/delayed by playing better (running out of missiles, guns overheating) This game isn't exactly what I specifically wanted but it's pretty close and also a cool thing in its own right. I do enjoy the smash-ification of the kaiju fighter and the very goofy, slapstick nature of this game. I haven't been this excited about a game in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Gigabash, the kaiju game you need. You can see the love put to this game everywhere: Both their kaijus and the locations of the game have got big texts of lore, not only related to these titans, but also to political and economical situation of the place.About the fights:-It is balanced, and each kaiju has got a very original play style, so you surely find one that fits you the best.-You really have the feeling of actually fighting as a gigantic beast. You have a lot of attacks that hit hard your opponents and destroy the enviorement at the same time.-You can interact with the enviorement in lots of ways: Using it as coverage, picking up buildings to use them as projectiles or even as a melee weapon, use it to lengthen your combos... Now, some "problems", or, more likely, things I don´t like, are:-There are only 4 kaijus with a story mode, it would be real nice to have story mode for each of the original kaijus, cause they´re all so cool, and with a bit of extra lore added with the story mode, it would make it perfect for them.-Online is dead, but it´s not fault of the game. Sadly, not much people know about it, hope it starts becoming more popular and more people can enjoy it.-Lots of DLC characters are being added, that are pretty well known, but it would be nice that some new original kaijus were added to the game. Passion Republic Games sure shows love to each kaiju they made, and would like to see more of these, asides the already well known kaijus from both Godzilla and Ultraman sagas.So, conclussion, if you love kaijus, buy this game, completely worth it, you´ll have a real good time with it, and if you´re feeling lazy to fight, you´ve got a big chunk of lore to read for a while, and also a real good soundtrack to hear, or even watch the art of the game, which is obtained easily by just playing.Basically, the perfect kaiju game.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely addicting, & super fun combat!Love the default monster titans, & heroes like Gigaman, plus the boy with his giant "Gundam or Megazord like" mech! They are very original designs, & I really like all of them. I own the DLC for Ultraman, & Godzilla packs! So awesome being able to play as those in a decent American game for once done right. The combat in the game is so cool, & easy to learn the controls for basic attacks, all the way up to chained combos! I also really enjoy the effects for finisher power moves, & Ultimate attacks you can get to use when you break the energy ball during a fight. You gather Giga energy during each battle that fills the purple bar under your red life meter bar, & when full you can grow even taller with extra abilities, plus enhanced current attacks! I've not played the online battle mode yet vs other players, but to be honest the game itself has a classic retro feel to it like older console games of long ago, and back then there wasn't really online modes for multiplayer. If you didn't have friend with you to use a 2nd controller it was solo mode all the way vs the game itself playing your foes. I feel that this game is perfect as is for that, very fun overall even without online battles. So if you are like me, and just want to enjoy a fun Tokusastu / Kaiju battle 1 vs the game itself as enemy then this is a perfect game for you! If you simply must have online multiplayer battles, it has that too, but I am sure being this isn't as well known a game, the player count for online battles may be slim to poor at best most times. Highly recommended to Japanese Anime, Kaiju, and Toku fans the world over! I will be playing this for a long time to come for just how fun it is! Thanks for reading my review! ^_^ <3

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:It is 12/6/2022, the day of the Godzilla DLC arriving.They have added CROSSPLAY, arcade mode, and Onslaught Mode - a gamemode where you fight off waves of enemies until you fall. My thoughts remain relatively the same, and I am very grateful for the new modes that we received!Crossplay should help shoulder the lack of people playing online. You can also do all the wacky mayhem gamemodes online in private matches, too! More skins, an emote wheel to boot during the character-selection process online...Gigabash has reached a new peak, and I encourage everyone to still try it out.-----Gigabash is a quirky little arena brawler reminiscent of games like Godzilla's Pipework Studios Games (DAMM, Save The Earth, Unleashed). It is a funny little game and I love it.The Kaijus really fill all spectrums; you got your funny little guys, your cool ones, freaky ones, and LOTS of references. I'd say each Kaiju in the game has something similar to another already existing Kaiju out there. This is NOT a bad thing, as it's more of something in passing, like "oh, this guy has a move similar to ___!!!" and not blatantly another character.Story? Good. Stages? Good. Nothing stood out to me, but I can tell you, they're both bops. This isn't my mind just filling in like "oh yeah they exist" but straight up, they're good. When I first booted up the game, I kinda sat there in the main menu cause the music sounded so nostalgic despite me not ever hearing anything like it. Gameplay is cool too, there's little intricacies where if this game had a bigger community there could probably be a meta-game! That doesn't exist right now cause of the limited people (also I haven't joined the discord lol), and even then, that should CERTAINLY not stop you from mashing buttons, cause mashing buttons in this game is fun.One random thing to note is the Story Mode: it is REALLY good for some reason, like, I initially got this game cause I heard Godzilla was coming to it. I felt no incentive to play or learn any other character besides Rawa, because he's basically Godzilla before Godzilla. But after learning the cool backstories, seeing the awesome cutscenes and art, you can TELL the developers not only put their love and soul into this game but burned it into each character's story.Seriously, I side main Woolley now. I might pick up Gorogong again just cause of his story.I mean, I didn't WANT TO come out of this game thinking little annoying timmy in his giant mecha (which he probably has because he's probably privileged) was actually a cool character... but, Gigabash Story Mode. And it was AWESOME LIKE HOLY HELL. If anything, it's criminal theres not MORE of it, I would love a Gigaman and Rawa story. I hope with Godzilla's arrival, some sort of hole through space time brings him here and literally everyone ends up fighting him. I would LOVE more story oh my GOD.Overall, final thoughts. This game is the most solid 9/10 I've ever seen. The only thing holding this game back is it's lack of community preventing online (this can probably be fixed by crossplay between all platforms) and it's steep price. I guarantee you, this game ever drops to $20 or below? Instant buy, it's such a great party game, really good and really fun to sit down and play. Grab some friends (if you have those none of my friends like giant monsters or giant robots :<) and go gigabash some giga monsters. I don't normally like playing against CPU's except when I have some sort of incentive or I play with friends, but I sat there and played 30 minutes straight of free-play CPU battles. This game is monstrously fun.
