_childDocuments_.review: I have been craving a spiritual successor to War of The Monsters for a long long time and I feel like this is closest to that. Fans of that game know that it was stylized as a more '60s monster movie/kaiju type of game and this game isn't exactly the same vibe, but is very similar with a much brighter and more vibrant art style. The combos feel good to pull off and each of the characters is different and varied enough that they're all fun to play as and there's some truly neat and silly designs. The only community is just finding it's footing since the game JUST came out only a few days about, but I was able to jump into some matches. The online feels solid and responsive. Friendly fire is on by default (at least in quick play) which I love and is a good addition to this type of game. I've only played through the first monster campaign, but I'm enjoying it so far and definitely am looking forward to seeing what else the game has in store. I'd definitely recommend picking this up. At only a few hours of play the game feels cohesive and polished enough that I'm not upset at the price tag. Also, this looks like this developer's first game, so I totally don't have a problem with paying an un-discounted price to make sure these folks work is well valued and respected.

_childDocuments_.review: While early into the game, it's a lot of fun with great art style and visual effects. Everything about this feels very classic. I really like how the game looks visually, getting it just right between detail and artistic. The battle maps are a lot of fun and contain various mechanics that damage your fighters. This is a step up from what I'm used to from Godzilla's fighting game line and a welcome addition.The combat style is easy to pick up, but there are micro mechanics that you can learn and master to put together combos and outplay your opponent. As for content, there's a decent amount of stuff to do, with multiple modes and a short campaign, and you unlock new chromas by leveling kaiju  for some. The character roaster is a bit small at the moment but what characters are in the game feel very unique in how they fight.If you want some retro style monster bashing, this is a fun game to get, and I hope to see more content come for it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into it I will say here: If all you want is to support a potentially great future game, or to play through a flawed but occasionally 'functional' game reminiscent of older kaiju games, then go ahead and pick this up. But if you are wanting a solid, completely functioning experience, you might want to wait. I've long waited for the return of games like this but this game is just not worth the full price (or even 25% discount) and it certainly hasn't filled that craving at the state it is in now.I want to try and keep this review shorter than a giant wall of text, but for a bit of background the first video game I ever played was Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee. Not only did that start my love of that franchise, it got me into video games as a whole. I have a lot of respect and admiration for what the team making this project is trying to do and what has already been accomplished, and one day I think it might be an amazing game, but it has an enormous slew of issues that marr it.To go over the positives, the game has a unique and eye catching art style and is chock full of personality. So many of the monsters here are incredibly inspired and great ideas. A giant building that wants revenge on kaiju, a snail that uses it's shell as a living weapon that doubles as another kaiju's skull, these are fascinating ideas that never would have occured to me but once you see them in action you fall in love. On the pure aesthetic check, this game nails it. All the details in animations, taunts, and lore snippets are great.Unfortunately, every other part of the game just doesn't work. The Online is by far the worst offender. I have over 100 games on steam and across multiple platforms have easily played at least 200 titles, and this game has the worst multiplayer connections of non 'early access' project I have ever seen. You are given options to attempt to fix this with ping limiters and disabling crossplay, but both are literally non-functional. I disabled crossplay and still matched with play station users, and put in a ping threshold of 100 and was getting matched with players 200+. If you host a lobby, you might wait for 10 minutes and not get any other player joining you. Even if you can join a match and get past constant rubber banding and long lag spikes, if any player disconnects the match will end, even if it is not the hosting player. Worse still, in rounds with good connection once a player starts losing they will quit the game to force the match to end. With all these problems, I would say that unless you are doing private matches with a friend, this game should be treated as purely single player until these issues are resolved.The single player is definitely better, but still flawed. The story mode only has campaigns for a few of the characters, and is extremely buggy. I think I have encountered every possible bug; enemies stuck looping animations, enemies getting stuck at a certain health threshold and not being able to be killed, enemies being unable to deal damage to the player, falling through the world, getting knocked out of level bounds, and multiple straight up crashes, being unable to complete sub-missions, etc. I am not exaggerating when I say that there was not a single story mission where I did not experience at least one of these bugs. On one mission, two allied monsters are supposed to attack you in a story mission, but in my case they spent their time trying to attack each other, but were unable to actually damage each other. DLC monsters do not seem to appear in any of the single player modes unless you play as them, which means given the relatively limited roster size it gets stale pretty fast. Outside of the actual game 'problems', being terrible online capacity and myriads of bugs, I also find that they game's camera is very frustrating. Outside of bugs where the camera 'disconnects' and zooms to an out of bounds corner of the map, it doesn't actually focus on you , but rather on a sort of 'middle' point between you and your foes. This can make it very confusing and hard to 'find yourself' if you get launched, and from a purely aesthetic choice it makes you feel very small instead of a giant monster because the camera is zoomed so incredibly far away. An option to make the camera focused on the player's monster and more zoomed in would be greatly appreciated.I don't want to be too negative because at the end of the day I want this game to succeed and I think if the glaring 'functional issues' were resolved it would flip over to being positive. Just the ability to play a match online would be great. But as it stands now, it is literally unplayable online and the constant bugs offline make it incredibly frustrating to play in that way as well. I've still had enjoyment reminiscing on nostalgia and there are definitely good things here, but overall this needs a lot more TLC and I desperately hope it gets it.

_childDocuments_.review: When was the last time I tried my hand at playing a Kaiju game? I can't even remember. It has been a while, but this game has the ability to bring back that feeling of exhilarating and wholesome joy you had when you were just sitting about on a couch with your friends and cousins, or even your brothers or grandparents, and kicking each others butts!I don't particularly like playing fighting games, but my heart was won over by each and every one of the characters. To be more specific, Wooley, that lovable Yeti, simply desired to make friends and return home, and the manner in which they did so in spite of his story and the events that transpired was absolutely outstanding. Rather from being stingy, the game pulls out all the stops to give a highly graphic, immersive, and engaging experience that will not disappoint you. Rather than simply dissolving into a plume of smoke and dust like most games do, the world around you crumbles and shatters into pieces. This is a game that will not let you down.If you are not very interested in fighting games in general, then that is completely understandable; though, I would not consider this to be a typical, run-of-the-mill fighting game that you are accustomed to seeing. It is something that you can sit down and have fun with no matter what type of gamer you are, especially when you are with your friends, because it is genuinely trying to be fun and entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Kaiju game I've played since Rampage.  Imagine a cross between that and Freedom Force with a bit more fluent combat akin to 3D Smash Brothers or TMNT Shredder's revenge.  Very bouncy, beautiful graphics that feel akin to a Nintendo game with some indie polish.  The original Titans are adorable and a lot of fun and quirky spins on the tropes make them pay sweet homage to Toho and Ultraman.  You have a slumbering rock monster, an alien squid man, a floral goddess, an out of shape Ultramyoungan type, a  Gundam Mech fighter, and of course my favorite, Whooley the big domb loveable yeti that eats projectiles and people like kirby.  Added to the DLC are Godzilla, Mechagodzilla, Gigan and Destroyah.It's been a while since I bought a new game on Steam and sat down to play it for hours straight.  There are 4 storied campaigns for the rock man, squid alien, yeti and the gundam mech.  3/4 the way through so far and they are pretty nicely written for this type of game.  Not too much, just niuce taunts and text and storypanel scenes.  It's perfect for this type of game.  You can destroy environments, throw tanks, topple cities, etc.  Throw buildings too, but my aim is rarely good enough for that.  Sadly, you cannot squish people or eat them, but hey, this game is very fluffy and PG, so I'm fine with that.  You can feel safe with little kids as young as 6 playing this one.  It's so freaking adorable!  A great game to play with your kids, very silly and cartoonish.  And lots of play options too, online, solo, tagteam, vs.  So you can help them out instead of just beating them and making them cry every time.REALLY amazed by this game.  My only complaints so far are that flying monsters feel like they should have a bit more charge for their flight meters, and that Destroyah in particular having wings, should at least get a few extra double jumps like Kirby.  He is rather ponderous, and the extra wing jumps would be a nice effect.  I am hoping there are sequels and more DLC for it, imagine that, yes I want more DLC. Please add more unique character packs and little storied scenarios for them.  Those quests and characters you made are interesting as hell and I want to learn more about them.  Not sure what kind of deal you have with Toho, but if you can add more from their franchise as well, please do! After adding say, 2 more 4-packs of those monsters, a Godzilla-specific campaign with the classic movie soundtracks and scripted lore would be most excellent.  Some of them might need some gameplay tweaking of course,  It would be so worth it though.  Top monsters I'd like to see addedMothra: FLyer with lots of regenerations and defensice aura, hypno pollen stunsMothra Caterpillar form: Like the snail but more webbing, tail attacks, regenerations, make it a regenerating one to offset his poisonHedorah: Toxic sludge monster? yes please.  Play with his alternate forms perhaps, and let him switch styles like Fang from SFRodan: Flyer with dash and fire attacks.  Probably the fastest character, so make him have a glass jaw and weak when groundedVaran: lots of grapple attacks and spine launchersAnguirius: a quadraped would be interesting.  Instead of grabs perhaps a trample? Definiely a lot of rolling attacksKING KONG? Goes without saying.  Though Rock guy has the influencesBiolante: big bio plant monster, I would emphasize slow speed with lots of encumbering moves and long distance grabsSPACE Godzilla: why? because he exists and it's cheap easy reskinned DLC, lolMinizilla: Make all of his moves based off the power of cute as he flops and follies across the battlefield. Like the Wii Fitness trainer WTF moveset of the game.  Go crazy with itJet Jaguar: although we pretty much already have him, maybe a ken to his ryu?Kumonga: Ok if you can somehow tweak the engine to include a giant spider, color me ultra impressed.King Ghidorah?  I don't know.  Obviously we want to include him, but he's three times the size of everybody else and could probably kill them all at once.  I would love to see him, but it would take some fancy nerfing like Destroyah.  Maybe include him as the boss battle, definitely.  You cannot not include him if you do Godzilla campaign.Other than that, larger environment and play areas.  Might be something for a sequel to think about, making this open box.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest, I went in wanting to love this game, but came out hating nearly every aspect of it.First, this is not a fighting game so much as a brawler. Slap those buttons, baby. Which buttons? Doesn't matter! Slap 'em! I mean it, win or lose, my strategy never mattered so why try? I'm sure one of the half-dozen people who get sweaty over this has an itemized list of why I'm incorrect at the ready, but I don't care. We should be past this button mashing thing...Two critical components make the combat unforgivable to me, though. The "smash orb" concept desperately should've died with Smash Bros. Brawl. It did not. Break a ball, gain an anti-everything super move. Thanks game. Screw skill! I also love how I can just wallop that thing in Giga Mode and it won't break only to immediately sidle up to an opponent who'll wink at it and promptly break open. Thanks, game! Skill is overrated...That leaves Giga Mode itself. Hit stuff? Fill a meter. Get hit? Fill a meter. Gather some...glowing orb things...Fill a meter. Once full, hit two buttons and become more gianter!!1! Psh, crash. Wragh, boom! Except, this is a fighting game, right? Whose brilliant idea was it to institute this? My reward for kicking butt should be victory, not a glorified god mode that can be countered by other god modes, rendering it into just another layer to manage over the existing game. Why would you do this, unless for the visuals alone?People, of course, love to reference Godzilla games when talking about this. Unlike in the Godzilla fighting games people keep, mistakenly, referencing, there is no sense of weight or scale, here. The monsters seem big until they are dwarfed by the nearest building, while even the smallest tank is bigger than your feet. Likewise for the objects. Multistory skyscrapers get picked up and thrown about like it's the old pigskin, so even the environment doesn't have weight.These "giant monsters" also zip and zoom around the map willy nilly, ruining the notion that these are massive creatures. They may as well be hyperactive children hopped up on MTN Dew wrestling in their dinosaur PJs. It spoils my immersion is all I'm saying, but if I don't have that giant monster feel, why bother playing this?The story mode  I mean, it's just an excuse to have a collection of fights so it does it's job. However...if all you want is the catharsis of being a giant monster wrecking things, why not just leave it there and have the players be giant monsters wrecking things? Get your Giant Robot anime out of here, and that story being in the same one as the Yeti's silly one just doesn't sit right with me, tonally.If it sounds like I hate this, please don't read this like I'm angry. I'm not. I did however want a satisfying monster game and I don't feel like I got that. I wanted a fighting game and don't really feel like I got that, either. What I did get isn't a satisfying experience for me and I genuinely don't think I'll ever play it again.Didn't like the story, didn't like the fights, didn't like the maps. I'm even ambivalent about the monsters. The best are DLC crossovers, anyway, so get that outta here. There is nothing that I actually like about this game, so of course I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game except for one thing. I use an xbox style controller because it fits better in my hand. The game works with it except for one seemingly small but very annoying to me issue. The game will only use the bumper buttons and not the triggers. It would not bother me so much, but  one of the things assigned to it is the dash button which I use almost constantly. I have nerve damage in my hands and while I can use the bumper buttons, I can not use them constantly without a great deal of discomfort. In the few minutes I played the game my hands were already starting to ache. If I could switch these buttons to the triggers instead I would be fine and they fit my hand very naturally. Hence why I use this controller.  Unfortunately, this game does not recognize the triggers so I can not switch to them.  Make no mistake, I WANT to play this game. The brief period I was able to play it I was having a blast, but if the tutorial and a single mission is enough to make my hands hurt to the point where I have to stop playing, there is no point in me having it. If this ONE issue is fixed I will play the hell out of this game, but until then I requested a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun - If you've ever wanted to be a giant monster and fight other giant monsters, this is the best choice to do it since Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters. Combat is simple enough that casual fighting game fans can enjoy it, but there's enough move variety that it doesn't get stale - Very much like Super Smash Bros., not so much in how the game controls, but moreso how easy it is to pick up and play. Street Fighter this is not.The biggest surprise for me was the variety of game modes:- A simple story mode that helps a great deal with getting you to appreciate the game's 10 base characters- Free battle mode for 1-4 players- Arcade mode where you go up against progressively harder foes- Onslaught mode where you'll fight 30 waves of enemies back to back, and- Mini-game mode, where you'll compete in a number of combat-based challengesHonestly, there's a lot here on its own, and the DLC adds a lot in the way of 6 Godzilla characters, 4 Ultraman characters, and 2 original characters, one of which borrows heavily from series like Power Rangers and Voltron.There's plenty of minor things to unlock as well, from alternate colors for most of the fighters, to lore, to character art and music, if that's your thing. And of course, there's Online play.All in all, GigaBash offers the kind of single player experience you saw a lot in the N64/Gamecube days - There's plenty of modes and unlockables to keep you invested, as long as you enjoy the base game enough to stick with it. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, this game is hella fun.Gigabash is an arena fighting game where you play as different giant monsters based off classic kaiju media fighting in fully destructible environments like cities, military camps, research facilities, etc.One of the best things about this game to me is how simple the controls are yet you can still pull off impressive moves or combos with them. It’s very much an easy to play, hard to master type game which is a genre of games I love because of how many hours you can sink into them. This also makes the game ideal for multiplayer as it makes explaining the controls to others a non-issue. The different characters you can select from are all fun to play as and do a really good job at being a homage to what they’re based on (my current main in the game is Kongkrete). My only main issue with this game is the lack of substantial content. There is a story mode which follows 4 of the characters in the roster but they’re extremely bare bones and are just a series of minigames or fights. Other than that there’s an arcade mode, an endless waves mode and a minigame mode but all of them kind of run their course after a couple of plays. The gameplay more than makes up for this lack of content but I would be lying if I said I wasn’t a bit disappointed by it. Overall, it’s an extremely fun fighting game that you can have a ton of fun with.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little 3D party fighter made by people who wear their love of Tokusatsu media on their sleeves. I'm not sure how the devs got the OK from both Toho Studios and Tsuburiya Productions, but I'm glad they did. Now all we need is one "giant flying turtle" and the trifecta can be compete.

_childDocuments_.review: A wildly good game with plenty of nuance in its mechanics. In my opinion, the most fun giant monster game I've played in a local multiplayer setting.The greatest times I've experienced with this game are in chaotic scenarios with 4-players on-screen; it has been an amazing time. I practiced playing without S-Class and Ultimates for a while in 1v1s, though after my experimentation with playing in that context, I'd not recommend it. Playing without S-Class and Ultimates can often reward players who play passively, which can make for tedious matches. In addition to this, there's a wide gap between character tiers (at least in that ruleset); meaning fighting a Gigaman player as Skorak is a very difficult matchup. Mixing in more chaos (Ultimates), and/or incentive to not play passively (S-Class), really helps make the game shine. I've yet to experiment much with 2v2 matches, but there seems to be lots of potential there as well!Overall this is a very fun game I had anticipated in the years leading to its release, and I continue to have a great time with it. The visuals are stunning, I greatly enjoy the music and sound design, and the gameplay is immediately fun while having enough nuance to reward players who spend more time with it (universal tip: you can jump cancel dashes, but you can also block for a split second after a grounded dash to cancel the cooldown).Best of wishes.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️GigaBash is an absolute gem in the world of party brawlers, delivering a KAIJU-SIZED punch of a good time! This game was created by kaiju fans, FOR kaiju fans! GigaBash masterfully combines the chaotic charm of classic monster movies with crazy and silly multiplayer action, resulting in an experience that’s as awesome as it is fun.From the moment you stomp your way into the battle arenas, you’ll be introduced to a collection of creative original kaiju. Each monster is uniquely designed with a blend of creativity and nostalgia, they fit in this world perfectly. It's impressive how the developers figured out a way for the monsters to jump around and do combos, yet still feel like they have height, weight, and power. Whether you're unleashing devastating attacks or using the environment to your advantage, the gameplay is consistently fun, engaging, and most importantly, destructive.One of GigaBash's greatest strengths is its accessibility. The controls are intuitive enough for newcomers to pick up and play, yet there’s enough depth to keep seasoned players engaged, always trying to find new tech to use in the next fight. The variety of modes, from chaotic free-for-alls to the story mode, ensures that there’s something for everyone. Plus, the local and online multiplayer options make it easy to jump into a match with friends anytime.What truly sets GigaBash apart, though, is its sense of humor and charm. The whimsical animations, quirky character designs, and lighthearted tone make it a joy to play. It’s clear that the developers poured a lot of love and passion into this game, still making content for the game TO THIS DAY!If you're looking for a game that offers endless fun, competitive excitement, and a trip down memory lane with giant monsters, GigaBash is the perfect choice. Grab some friends, pick your favorite monster, and let out your inner kaiju!Highly recommended!

I am disappointed that they didn't add any new singleplayer options with the recent patch, however.  The core game is very fun, but it is still in dire need of more things to do outside of online matchmaking (which isn't always reliable).  Once that aspect of the game is dropped in 10-15 years when it's no longer financially viable to keep servers up, there needs to be more than what we have for local play.The story mode, while charmingly presented and a great primer for getting used to the game, has seemingly been abandoned and it seems like the rest of the base cast won't be getting their campaigns.  I hope more development time is spent on that.  Additionally, another more ambitious singleplayer mode feels needed too, something modeled after Godzilla Save the Earth's Adventure mode and Ultraman Fighting Evolution 3's Invasion & Dada modes come to mind.  I would personally sacrifice the time and resources needed for a hypothetical Gamera DLC in favor of ensuring this game has longevity with modes.The bottom line is that there needs to be more to do for singleplayer.  I love the core of this game and the DLC adds even more characters to play with, but this is a game I can only casually whip out for friends, and not all of my friends own it.  I hope Passion Republic gets more funding and manpower to make it more feature-rich, because this game is really special and deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun multiplayer Kaiju brawler with enjoyable mechanics and features with solid gameplay, which is (mostly) fun. There are also monsters original to the game, as well as a Godzilla DLC pack that adds the all-time great Kaiju himself, along with some of his more noteworthy enemies, such as Mechagodzilla and Destoroyah, giving the roster a unique flavor of building smashing and brawling. Although the game is a solid title, it needs more cross-platform party support and more content to experience. As a result, it will likely struggle with longevity, given the game's already tiny player base.This is sad to admit, considering this is a fun title with a respectable level of heart and care put into the experience, with unique animations, movement, and special attacks that reflect these characters' larger-than-life personalities. Along with a dwindling player base, the game lacks content with a single-player mode that, while fun to play, is so short and only features a few of the Kaiju as the focal point of the different story missions that make up the single-player. Once you finish the few story-based missions on offer, that's it for the single-player side of the experience. Despite some impressive set-piece moments, the game continued beyond knocking out enemies and bosses or smashing specific objectives.On the multiplayer side, we have a free-for-all with up to four players, 2v2, and duel mode, which is just 1v1. Additionally, some party mini-games are available, but the biggest issue is that you can't play them with your console friends through the public lobbies but instead must be in the same private party. The other modes can be played online with cross-platform public lobbies, with the caveat being you won't be able to party up with your friends on consoles due to the lack of cross-platform party support, which is unfortunate and odd considering cross-platform play is already in the game. It's currently my biggest gripe with the game since someone I play with regularly only has access to the PS5 version, and we have to luck up and hope nobody else is playing public games for us to be able to join up and play together. Then we're stuck playing the same two game types repeatedly, unable to play the party mini-games at least. It's unfortunate not to be able to party up with friends on other platforms with this kind of game, and actively hoping no one else is playing when we play so that we can get (hopefully) matched up. It's a lot of fun, but these issues hold it back from being far better and more engaging to play in the long run.The downside, though, to this type of experience is that with a more exciting story mode or more multiplayer game types, the game quickly becomes stale after a short while, unfortunately. While the Kaiju combat is impressive with destructible environments and unique levels to fight in, it does suffer from being noticeably repetitive after some time, and that isn't necessarily the game's fault, as it's just the design and nature of this type of game. Others may have a different opinion on that, as is the heart of most multiplayer-only focused games. Your mileage will vary. However, this game is quite fun if you're a fan of giant monsters or fun brawler-type games that let you bash your friends with fun and exciting characters. I wish there were more on offer, as what's here currently isn't enough to recommend it at the total price.Recommended, but only if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Monster Melee Mayhem for the Ages!🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 Five GigaStars! Best Monster Bash on the Planet!Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, kaiju fans of all ages! Gather 'round, for I have had the unparalleled pleasure of sinking my claws into "GigaBash", a game so monstrously fun that it can only be described as the Godzilla of party brawlers! And speaking of Godzilla, the Big G himself has stomped his way into this game as DLC! It's a veritable King of the Monsters convention in here, and you're all invited!First, let's talk about the characters: the original lineup is already a titanic roster of fierce and fabulous beasties. From skyscraper-filled cities to tropical islands, each battlefield is more destructible than a gingerbread house in the hands of the Hulk. No game has ever made me feel more like a 300-foot-tall, radioactive super-lizard on a rampage. (And trust me, I've tried.)The controls? Every punch, stomp, and tail whip feels so natural and responsive, you'd swear you were born to wreak havoc on these poor, pixelated metropolises.But let's not forget the humor! "GigaBash" never takes itself too seriously, injecting a healthy dose of comic relief that will have you chuckling in between all the kaiju chaos. The clever little Easter eggs and silly visual gags scattered throughout the game are like the cherry on top of this deliciously chaotic sundae.So, my fellow monster mashers, don your rubber suits and practice your best roars, because "GigaBash" has it all! If there's a perfect recipe for a monster melee game, this one has all the ingredients, masterfully mixed and baked to perfection. It's no wonder it deserves a whopping five GigaStars! _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It's a total homage to the Godzilla games of the 00's, but even better. It's faster, and more fluid. The 00's game walked stiffly so this game could run fluidly. I already like how this game had its references to Kaiju lore, as well as a Notzilla, Notkong, and Notultraman. That's always fun, but the fact they got a few of the actual Godzilla cast in it is great. They're very fun to play as and on point as far as character and balance goes. But, like most things, this game has it's cons, tho. Two of it's biggest cons are it's A.I. and glitches. It's A.I. is Ultra Instinct level of input reading. It's doing things no average human can do. Insta-blocking or insta-dodging. That's nothing new for fighting game A.I. tho. But what really sucks are the glitches. At this point, I only recently picked up the game and am learning about it. Just minutes ago, I did a arcade run with Godzilla and was smoking it. I get to the final 9th round, against a Kongcrete and something happened to where it was sent upward, and that was it for my run. I tried several minuets to hurt it or end the match in some way, but I could only attack it as an S-Class jumping, but that only knocked it around. I wasn't actually hurting it. With no other option available (no reset or time over), I had to end the run to move on (with no end result whatsoever). So all my effort spent on running a new arcade record was wasted. Devs, please address this. Anyway, fun, fluid Kaiju game. If you're a fan of Kaijus, give this one a go. My biggest hope is that with further content, devs will add levels to DLC characters too. It'll give more incentive to play them.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend GigaBash. The game is a colourful arena brawler where up to four players each control a Kaiju, or titan, and then duke it out with each other. There's a wide variety of monsters, some inspired from movies and tv shows. Rock monster, plant, snail, giant human, a building sized mech, favourites are sure to be had here! The game features several modes to play, including a recently added arcade mode where you fight a set number of random titans before the last big fight against a titan in permanent S-Titan mode.Oh, the gameplay! Every titan has it's own Normal attacks and Special attack, hold respective button to charge the attack and/or add utility to the move. You can dash around the field and you can block attacks, but not too much or your foe will break your guard. Block and Attack or Special Attack to utilise your titan specific block related moves: Gorogong can either bash around with his arms fending off nearby enemies and destroying projectiles, or make an uppercut, good against jumping enemies or higher positioned ones.You can grab an enemy(counters it's block too) and punch it up, throw it away or use titan specific grab moves: Pipijuras for instance can place a timed mine on the opponent. General brawling and building destruction rewards you with Giga energy, reap enough of that and enter S-class titan mode: Titan becomes even bigger, and does more damage and is invulnerable to all attacks save from other S-class titans. Attacking S-class titans as a regular titan increases your Giga energy income.Each map features loads of destruction and become more desolated and the skirmish continiues. Vehicles, terrain pieces can be grabbed and thrown, or sometimes used as clubs to batter your enemies. Even entire buildings can be picked up and thrown! Each map also has a unique feature to mess things up. A tornado might appear, or an avalanche will storm a city. In the map Area 51 you have a sand storm and Mechajuras to content with! After a set amount of time an orb will appear on map, crack it and unleash an Ultimate attack for great justice!Other modes of play includes free for all and two vs two, both with or without bots. There's a survival mode where you try to defeat as many titans as possible. Mayhem mode, now available in single play, tasks all players with wacky conditions that leads to victory, instead of beatings, such as playing "hot potato" with a giant bomb or throwing UFOs at each other.GigaBash features four short but sweet campaigns and wonderful music! The tunes are often splendidly spirited, and really fit the Kaiju vs Kaiju action. There's also training modes, unlockable skins, artwork, a juke box to play the music out of battle. Optionally you can enable visual filters on the game giving it the atmosphere of classic Gojira/Godzilla movies.Speaking of Godzilla, Passion Republic Games have teamed up with Toho Co., Ltd., resulting in DLC that adds four classic Kaiju, including Godzilla.GigaBash is fun, has heart and is a joy to play, and I recommend GigaBash!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, I think of those old king of monster arcade games where you are a monster and beat each other and your surroundings up, it's also got a bit of power stone in it. The combat is simple which is great, I think you can find a decent amount of depth in the match ups, the footsies, the combos but ultimately I would deem this game to be at it's funnest with 4 players, either FFA or 2v2, and that's just chaos. All the monsters are fun to use, I personally really enjoy Gigaman and every character feels viable and useful, there's depth to really master how a character works but also simple enough that you can play random and have fun. If there is a character who is really top tier and ruins the game, I'm not sure but Gigaman (and whoolie the yeti) potentially feel like that dude. There are a couple of characters you have to unlock through story but it's not very hard, so the accessibility to try everyone is fast enough (there's also a playable building, no seriously "it's" super cool). My competitive theory to playing this game does seem to boggle down to how well you play early, this game has a come back mechanic (by destroying the "smash ball" which can unlock your super attack) but very much favors whoever can get S class first and use footsies and combos to make it very challenging to allow your opponent to get S class themselves.The stages are cool, some are fair with no hazards and others seem rather unfair and are littered with them, but that's ok it's supposed to be like that. You can unlock stages simply by playing all of the ones available to you, on a base level all stages are "enjoyable" but some people might want to avoid ones with lava or the avalanche which will just melt your health.The training mode (gym) is surprisingly good, I didn't think it would have the options it does, but it's satisfactory to help you elevate your game.The musical score is incredible, plenty of references to the Showa Godzilla era but is also really funky too.There are some cons, we need the ability to team up with a friend and play online in 2v2s, that doesn't seem to be an option. You also can't veto a stage, everyone playing picks their stage and the game will rotate between which players stage is picked, but being able to veto a stage and hit random would be best for those who don't want to deal with hazards. The net code seems ok but I've only been playing a friend in the same state and no issues, however the other day for some reason we just kept lagging and had a desync, unsure why. I wouldn't call the net code a con if you play to play couch co-op, because that seems to be the focus which is cool, not a lot of games allow that (which means you can also purchase one copy of the game and play online with parsec). The game also needs more rule sets, such as more stocks per match, the ability to turn off the "smash ball" (which enables supers) and possibly to disable item pick ups (like trees, buildings as well as the S class orbs). And finally, a fast rematch option would be welcomed, because the only game type is a 2 stock match, they can go pretty fast and it always returns to character select, I enjoy fast paced matches but rematch would be nice.I'd give it a solid 8/10, a real fun game.Edit: I've tested this with the steam deck and it seems to run just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 - Makes you feel like a bad-ass monster.Longer Review:Game play: Even though the premise of this game is simple (you're a monster and you beat things up), the mechanics are surprisingly deep. There's a plethora of options while fighting (grab -> block -> attack -> dash), and much of the combat is about timing, spacing and utilizing each option effectively. There's also a nice balance between easy to learn but hard to master, that makes combat extremely satisfying. The emphasis on different options make this game shine in PVP. It's obvious that every monster had different ideas of how they should play, instead of all being clones of each other, giving more variety. I do wish there were more monsters, but having a few distinct monsters (in game play and visuals) is much better than a large variety of monsters that mostly play the same. So I think the devs made a great choice here.Visuals: Very well done. The design of the monsters are all very distinct, and each looks great IMO. The game executes it's art style very well, without being visually noisy.Story: Not too long, but pretty fun. It gets into the monster bashing pretty quickly (which I like). It's great how it introduces you to the rest of the mechanics. IDK I don't really play games for story I just like to beat things up. Conclusion: Get it if you like fighting games, monster bashing games or any kind of hack n slash and beat em ups. Definitely has some fresh ideas in the genre and is well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast if you enjoy party-style fighting games. Seemingly inspired by War of the Monsters (2003), but just better than even my rose-tinted glasses would have me remember that game. The easy-to-execute special moves and simple mechanics make this game accessible to newcomers, but the depth of character interactions will delight players like myself looking for a nuanced metagame.The action is explosive throughout a match because every monsters has 2 ultimates.  One comes from a Smash Ball-style power-up that enters the arena as a pinata; the other comes from eventually dealing and taking enough damage.  The Smash Ball version is very similar to a Final Smash, with it usually dealing high damage and having some flashy effects.  The second version defines this game.  Going "Giga" makes your monster 4x the size, gives you a visual upgrade, and powers up all of your moves.  Dealing damage to Giga monsters also gives you lots of Giga energy, so before you know it a chaotic brawl becomes an apocalyptic clash between gods that annihilate the city around them.Incredible character animations make these mechanics sing in a fiery chorus and steal the show from the other aspects of its production. When this game's overweight version of Ultraman pirouettes between buildings to do a magnificent flying spinning split-kick that sends the Godzilla knock-off exploding through a skyscraper, it's really hard not to smile if you appreciate anything about Kaiju at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Gigabash is just a whole bunch of silly fun; I'm sure there will be those out there trying to be all serious with it but at least for me this is a game to just sit back and laugh at the madness of it all. It does a lot of things well, the core combat is easy to pickup and satisfying to play, the roster all looks great and has some nice variety, and the stages....honestly they steal the show: Every stage has its own gimmicks and events and potential items to use, they even have their own different effect you can do to people if you're ever knocked out of a match before the round has ended, it's honestly fantastic and just adds so much to what would've already been a fun brawler; the love and passion put into the game is impossible to not notice, it's wonderful.I've only played the 1st of 4 story mode episodes and it was fun; not super long but I did enjoy it and a scenario involving cultists just constantly abandoning their Gods had me laughing my way through it. Online is fun if a bit basic, no real communication features or anything like that, it is Peer2Peer and as with anything new with a potentially low population count your experience may vary but what I will say is that the matches I've had have been really fun and nothing too laggy just yet; that said a single disconnect can boot the lobby so unfortunately if you get caught up with someone being way too serious and rage-quitting I'm afraid they are potentially taking the lobby with them; that said this is one of those games that will shine a local multiplayer setting as just a fun crazy thing to play so if you're in a position where you're able to do that then this game will definitely be a winner there :)That and you can play as a giant sentient building that can pick up and throw other buildings....I probably should've started with that tbh :)

After centuries spent slumbering in the bowels of the earth, the primordial beasts known as Titans have awoken. Now they must battle humanity - and one another - for total world dominance.

GigaBash combines the chaos and creativity of titles like Power Stone, Super Smash Bros Ultimate and War of Monsters with the jaw-dropping scale of the classic kaiju movies. name: Overboard!
detailed_description: JULY, 1935. A MURDER HAS BEEN COMMITTED aboard the SS Hook, eight hours out from New York. Only one problem: you did it. Can you get away with murder? GAMEPLAY Overboard! is a tense, highly replayable detective game from the creators of 80 Days and Heaven's Vault . Blackmail a spy. Fall in love. Murder a rival. Cheat at cards. Drug a witness. Lie, befriend, betray, console, sneak, seduce, steal, borrow, pray, eavesdrop, kill... There are clues, evidence, suspects, accusations, secrets and lies. You’ll need all your cunning, coercion and charisma to ensure that someone else takes the fall. DYNAMIC NARRATIVE CLOCKWORK * Next-gen visual novel : go where you want, when you want, and say what you want * Simulated story-world : other characters move and act independently, remember everything they see and hear, and everything you do * Every minute counts : you have eight hours to escape justice. Time is always ticking * Who can you trust? Some characters are friendly, and some are out to get you. Who will you befriend? And who will you betray? Built using the award-winning ink narrative engine, Overboard! 's narrative twists itself around every choice you make. Play once for a thrill, or multiple times to uncover all the secrets and achieve an ideal ending. One play-through lasts about 30 - 45 minutes, but achieving the perfect crime run will take a lot longer. Can you get away with murder?

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is that you're a passenger on a ship, waking up on the morning after you've murdered your well-to-do husband. From that point, you're free to go anywhere on board to do whatever you can to avoid justice within the time limit. You could just try to play dumb and cover up enough evidence to put your guilt into doubt. If you're more devious you could try to frame one of your fellow passengers. You could even go the And Then There Were None route and murder everyone else on board just to be thorough, if you can pull it off.Overboard! was clearly designed for replayability. The ship is full of evidence and red herrings to tamper with, desperate schemes to attempt, and secrets to learn. The first playthrough reveals only a small slice of all this, leaving a collection of unsolved mysteries and unfollowed leads to pursue on the second. The second playthrough prepares you for the third, and so on, until finally you beat the game... but there's much more to it than that. Vague, but I don't want to spoil anything.This game was released today without any kind of announcement beforehand from inkle. As usual, their writing and design are superb. If you're captivated by the premise, even by a little, you won't regret the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I want to love it, I really do. But it's falls more into repetitive hard work rather than intelligent deduction.Argh it pains me to thumbs down. I normally guilt myself into thumbs up for games like this as I like the style, or the attempt, or the idea. I am an avid fan of story-based games/walking simulators so am very forgiving.It’s hard to compare it to anything, but I guess it has similarities to Return of the Obra Dinn and Detroit. In a sense that you’re trying to work out sequences of events and you will repeat and dig through facts to try and work things out. What makes Overboard! more difficult to like is that you have to repeat the whole day choosing options to unravel the ‘solution’. Common logic says you change one thing and see the result. But the trouble is if you are only making a minor shift, it’s a LOT of clicking to go through the day to see the result. So do you change more things? But then you get to the end and it’s often not possible to know what lever you pulled that changed something.For a player point of view, the results often feel random. I know they are not random, quite the opposite… but without being able to lock down the logic it *feels* random. What’s also frustrating is I’m sure something has changed in the outcome yet I felt I did nothing to do that. Why for example doing an action results in an outcome at the end one turn, then you do that thing again and it doesn’t... you think what did I do?You also have to put up with what feel like logic jumps for the characters. With very flimsy evidence, they will make very grand accusations. In fact sometimes they accuse based upon absence of evidence. There is a certain joy when you unlock an area, or make a deduction, but the joy is shortlived when it’s again like a feeling you’ve pulled one lever successfully but you have to still pull another ten – in the dark.I feel it’s missing a feature. It needs some sort of decision map like Detroit, so you can have some understanding of your impact.Theme wise, as someone who loves the vibe of this era, I was a bit underwhelmed. The images are very much focused on faces so you get little sense of the rooms the characters are in. The music could have been a love letter to that era, jazzy and decadent… but it's largely forgettable.It pains me to give it a thumbs down, as I like their idea here. But I have to honestly say “Would I recommend it to a friend?” I’d say no. I’d say get Return of the Obra Dinn or The Invisible Hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played it for too long, but after 6 playthroughs, I want to say this game is pretty interesting. Inkle has been experimenting a lot with the loop format. In 80 Days the game encouraged you to play multiple times through a long-ish narrative that honestly, made more sense to me as a "single-journey" type of experience. Heaven's Vault's lore made it pretty interesting to replay the game, but being too long, didn't really made me want to play it again immediately. Last year's Pendragon was a pretty interesting approach to a shorter format where every playthrough you learn more about the world and you get to mix and match the variables, but I thought it still was somehow lacking.Maybe this opening paragraph sounds a little too harsh, but I genuinely enjoy Inkle's games and I'm always interested in what they do because I love experiements in narrative design and interactive storytelling, so when I saw "Overboard!" releasing out of nowhere I immediately bought it to give it a go and I must say it might be of the most interesting games they've released, and I think it might be due to them further developing the concepts they've been toying around with in all of their past games.I love the presentation of the game. The 1920's aesthetic brings a dynamic and sometimes satirical approach to a synopsis that's already pretty great. It's a whodunnit where YOU'RE the criminal. Then in a series of playthroughs you get to see the multiple outcomes that may arise from toying around with the variables. Try to kill everyone, try to get x and y in your side. Try to commit suicide, why not. Try and blame someone else. See what happens when you confess, et cetera.While Pendragon was a game I thought was pretty interesting, it never really hooked me beyond 4 or 5 playthroughs. Maybe because I thought the game was somehow limiting and limited by its approach, yet, Overboard! just pulls me back and back after each playthrough in a speedrun-ish kind of approach where you want to toy around with the outcomes. It also comes down to the story and set-up in the end. The fact YOU'RE the one who was to hide all evidence makes it attractive to find new and better ways to wrap up everything in the end. I think the lenght of the playthrough really helps, because it can take from 15 minutes to 30 minutes to get to the end, and each time you get more and more familiar with the characters, opportunities and mysteries the game has. It really serves this game well it doesn't have that many characters, so from the get-go you really have a pretty good idea of the scope of the narrative, which has made me even more invested since I know I can maybe get to figure out everything in a relative short period of time, which may be "bad" for people looking for long games, but if you're into experimental games with a shorter duration, this will be the perfect game for you.I'm still eager to keep playing and see what else the story is hiding. I still haven't figured out many character's "secrets" and I'm still in doubt about what happens when you try to do certain thing at a certain hour after doing 'x' or 'y'. Maybe this game has much more to offer than what I think! But it's been great even after only 6 playthroughs and will be coming back for more.The fact I'm reviewing this game right now is due to it being pretty exciting for me to play, and just because I want to support the studio, which might be one of the most interesting indie devs out there. So go! Buy it! Play it! It might the most approachable game they've done yet and one of the best (in my honest opinion).TL;DR: This game is pretty interesting. The story setup is really compelling and makes you want to keep playing to toy around with the multiple variables and outcomes the game has to offer. It's really fun in a mischievous kind of way and the narrative structure is really interesting (even more seeing it as the progression of Inkle's past endeavors).

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a quick, bite-sized game that you can tear through in less than an hour with the help of a guide,  has you covered. If you want a rich story full of layered characters that you can spend ten hours on or more - without a guide - it's got you covered there, too.But here's where I must caution you - if you want a complexly-branching narrative with several different endings, hyper-specific context-sensitive dialogue, and a game that will constantly surprise you with how the developers anticipated every outcome... You need to dial back your expectations. is a small-scale indie title that is $15 at . It has not been polished to a mirror shine, and it has a relatively limited scope. What's there is very good - the characters are charming and memorable, and the story is well-told. Although the game usually railroads you into only a few types of major ending states, they are generally very effective and the small flourishes are endearing. In the end, I suppose saying "it left me wanting more than it had" is a compliment, of sorts.That said - I still recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun game, re-playable over and over again!Within moments you kill your husband, try to frame someone else for it, plant evidence elsewhere, there are many paths to choose and I'm trying them all!The voice-overs are all top-notch, great writing, pretty to look at as well.There is no manual save; there does not need to be because you can follow paths that don't take a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Attempting to get away with homicide in the presence of a detective is pure folly, but that’s never stopped Agatha Christie’s villains, has it? Still, they all stumble in the end – Poirot and his fellow sleuths are just  good, ain’t they? has no such detective figure (well, not quite), so the plan to push my broke, fascist-sympathising husband into the ocean and claim his life insurance ought to be a doddle. But it turns out – can you believe it? – murder just isn’t that simple.inkle’s (, ) latest is a visual novel whodunnit placing you in the role of one Veronica Villensey, the aforementioned murderer. Travelling from miserable England in the mid-1930’s aboard the SS Hook to America, you’re not far from port when Veronica decides to push her husband Malcolm overboard.But there’s no careful, intricate plan to follow in the hours succeeding the murder, no setup in which suspicion is immediately allayed. No, Veronica Villensey had simply had enough of sordid little Malcolm, took the opportunity to rid herself of him, and proceeded to make it up as the day unfolded.Or rather have you do it for her.In  you have several key goals, chiefly pertaining to either pinning the murder on someone else or framing it as an accident. Sadly for Veronica, suicide will not lead to the handsome life insurance policy she covets (and why shouldn’t she have it?, I kept thinking to myself). But each step forwards fulfilling those goals presents new complications; if, say, a passenger saw you commit the deed and yet declined to dob you in, what exactly do they ?Because everyone wants  – it’s just a matter of whether or not it’s to your advantage.And the SS Hook is full of desiring souls. Well-written, funny, and cheeky personalities, you’ll find getting to know them – and their secrets – is as rewarding as it is amusing. Which is good, because you’re going to be meeting them again and again until you properly nail down your strategy for success.The potential for tedious repetition is largely minimised by the ability to fast forward through scenes, and previous choices are indicated in green. You can also restart any scene you’re playing should you wish to take a different tact.But even with these mechanics in play, the surprise consequences laced into every choice make the repeated journeys worthwhile. Just when I thought I had it down – secure in the knowledge that Malcolm was gone, his money mine, and his eccentric mistress framed for the deed –  threw another curveball, that bugger.And so back to the beginning I went, frowning in consternation but eager to commit that perfect crime. I’m determined to succeed, having grown to rather like Veronica, in spite of the sly, flirtatious sociopath that she is. It reminded me of the 1994 film , where I found myself rooting for Linda Fiorentino’s sadistic killer, who was likewise saddled with a repellent husband. It’s the men, see, they’re just rubbish...Pretty, funny, with sharp writing and plenty of surprises,  is a delight. Even when you finding yourself nodding away at homicide, which I feel obligated to remind you is Bad.Unless you're Team Veronica, of course.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I liked this one more than I do because the concept is great and so is the presentation along with a really interestingly reactive narrative but it's more a game of repetitive trial and error more than any sort of induction and past the first couple of hours I started to find it frustrating due to what I think are sort of idiotic relationships between actions and results.I kind of gave up on it when I achieved a double murder and attempted to pin on it someone else with no logical flaws in the arrangment, only for a character to verbatim say "No, that would be too perfect, therefore it had to have been you." which is absolutely dumb as hell, but it sticks because game says so. _childDocuments_.review: Overboard! is a reverse whodunnit choice-driven game and it is incredibly fun to play. After killing your good-for-nothing husband in the middle of the night you must now avoid getting caught by any means necessary, regardless of who you have to frame or kill to get what you want. Despite being the murderer of this case, the game sets up an excellent mystery and each success you earn reveals yet another layer to unravel, drawing you deeper and deeper into the depths of its story. Everyone has a secret and Veronica is strangely self aware of her many second chances, allowing the player to easily go back and make new choices. It's a very stylish looking game. It looks fantastic and sounds just as good, truly immersing you in the time period that this game is set in. If any of this appeals to you, I full-heartedly recommended it. I’d love to see more games like this, as it’s just the type of game I want to get lost in for hours on end.10/10 Would kill my husband again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute idea, and I wanted to like it.Disappointingly, the gameplay does not involve logic or planning, instead relying on the repetition of "Groundhog Day"-style trial and error.Far from allowing you to plan a murder and attempt to get away with it,  puts you in the shoes of a charming protagonist who has impulsively committed a crime in full view of several witnesses, left clues scattered around the ship, and so forth, putting you at the bottom of a proverbial barrel you must struggle and scrape to climb out of.  Worse, you don't and can't even know what you did wrong without blundering through the CYOA-style story several times, being captured over and over.The game touts itself as "highly replayable", but it does not strike me that way.  Having to fail over and over in order to unravel a single puzzle does not make a game "replayable"; it just means you have to start over a lot.  There may be different secrets to uncover on different CYOA paths, but the necessity of finding the optimal path to survival sucks the joy out of exploration, as every wrong guess (and that's all you are doing - guessing) seems to bring down the Game Over screen.It's a shame; the art looks good, there's a nice atmosphere, the characters are well-written and likeable.  I wished I felt a sense of freedom to explore, to plan, to plot a path to victory.  Instead, every retry added a new necessary task to my time-limited "to do" list: misdirect this inquiry, blackmail that witness, cover up those clues; racing around like a homicidal Bill Murray, spinning an ever-increasing number of plates in an effort to iterate on failure until it finally becomes success.Above all, the illusion of free will is progressively destroyed, as option after option leads to death and the list of  options gets shorter and shorter.Reluctantly refunded.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Steam user who is wondering if this visual novel is worth their time. I'm going to tell you right now that the short answer is an absolutely if you love interactive mystery.Actually this game isn't a visual novel (at least not in the traditional sense) but you are giving dialogue choices and decisions that change the outcome of the story. Anyway now on to the pros and cons list.Pros– the story. I really like the story of this game I could easily as a novel or a movie. The basic premise is Veronica Villensey, a London aristocrat murders her awful husband in cold blood by pushing him overboard on a trip to New York. Now she wakes up the next morning and realized that she had eight hours to not get caught. Basically the premise is a reverse of whodunit because in this case you want to get away with it. Of course there's more to it than just an unhappy wife killing her miserable husband but more would spoil and this really is a game where you want to walk in fresh.– Veronica Villensey and the other characters on the SS Hook. Each of them have their own story and are more than they appear to be. Honestly some of them are so terrible they actually make Veronica look saintly but interesting in their own way.– The art. Perfectly styled and really fit with the atmosphere of the 1930s. It really gives the game its own unique identity. I played visual novels with great art but with the professional glam and the style they all feel the same instead of being its own unique identity.– The mechanics. The very good about letting you know if you're screwing up or not I there are bubbles at the top with red text that tells you what people know, what people think and what you just did to help you keep straight your story.Cons– time management. Oh boy if you are not very good with time management then you are going to utterly hate this game. The timing of things is incredibly crucial and if even just a few minutes late you could completely destroy one of your runs especially when you're working on the speedruns or trying to get the true ending. Characters constantly move on the ship so whoever you want to talk to may not be in the same place they were ten minutes earlier and if you're trying to break into real that can be very bad because you may not have enough time to actually accomplish that.– Going to need a guide. Now I recommend for after you've played a few times but there are something that just aren't super intuitive so you'll probably need to find a guide so you can get all the ending achievements especially during the speedruns.No neutral this timeI honestly would like to say more about how great this game is but I really think that with no knowledge at all is the best way to play considering the mystery aspect. It's also pretty reasonable price and even though the game seems short you'll have to play it multiple times to see every bit of the story so I think it's well worth the almost 15 dollars you pay for it.So have fun and get away with murder~

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little graphic novel-type game and a fun twist on the detective games I usually play since you're trying to get away with a crime instead of solve one. There are many different achievements you can unlock which are fun and don't necessarily even mean going trough the entire game again - once you get that achievement you can reset to the start of the day (and you can also get multiple achievements in one run). I recommend trying to get away with the murder once, then after that, look up what the achievements are and try to get them.Only downside is the game can get tedious when you're constantly repeating conversations and restarting over and over again. (You can reset to the start of a scene once each scene though if you don't like the choices you made, which helps). I've got the game for free because I've helped to test it... but be sure I'm buying Overboard! on other platforms.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had a 'meh' button rather than thumbs up/down, I'd take it. I kinda like the idea of the game, but I got bored with it very quickly. It only took me an hour and a half or so to check off most of the endings. The rest of the time I've spent playing has mostly been achievement-hunting, but even that got boring. _childDocuments_.review: This is a sideways recommendation, not negative nor positive. It's a great game that's bogged down by forcing you to repeat the same things over and over again. The auto pick button is a crutch to the design because A) it's still too slow B) you have to be constantly paying attention not to overshoot or you'll have to restart the game all over again. I wish there was a way to just restart the run from a specific point / location instead of forcing the player to start from scratch and spend tens of minutes getting to the same point. And if it makes the game too trivial then at least make it an unlockable option after beating the game once.The developers clearly thought about this and gave us an undo button that is a half-fix, since it only rewinds the area you're in and only works once per run which is still way too punishing.It's like they want to punish the player for experimenting all the different paths in their story-branching game, which makes no sense.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine for what it is, but after a handful of runs it completely runs out of steam.My big issue is that I can't see a clear correlation between my actions and the results in game. In my first run I was able to successfully meet two of the three victory conditions through random bumbling. In subsequent attempts I had far worse results, despite taking more decisive actions. This had me feeling as though I was trying to suss out the path to a particular ending, similar to branching narratives in visual novels, instead of making meaningful decisions about how to get away with murder. And, frankly, I don't have the patience to try everything until I figure out what combination will trip the complete victory.Overboard! is fine for a few runs, but the longer you play it the more likely you are to see behind the curtain. Once that happens the fun of the game dissipates and you're left with an extremely repetitive game that doesn't have a strong mechanical hook to keep players invested.

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolute banger from Inkle. If you've enjoyed Inkle's previous games, this is a must-buy. Overboard! is a detective puzzler where every action increased the clock, and you have to solve the murder to escape.... except the game opens with you doing the murder. oops. So the game becomes a sort of turn-based race against the clock to somehow create an alibi, find an alternate suspect, learn what each character knows and use it to your advantage. You will go to prison, multiple times. You may even die. But in the end, you'll get away with murder in the most satisfying convoluted solution ever. Also the game opens with you murdering an arsehole husband, what's not to love?

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept of this game.It's a simple yet cool graphic novel game where you play as the killer and you have to make sure you get off the boat without being arrested.The game itself is quite short (~20min per run), but it is designed to be replayed and discover new ways to get away with murder.Sometimes you think you've got it all figured out and covered, but in the end you realise you've missed something and get framed. You have to plan your timing and actions to get the perfect murder. This game offers a multitude of endings and clever, well thought out and funny moments/dialogues.The only downside is that replaying the same dialogues can be tiring, although there is an option to replay your previous choice.I recommend this game if you are looking for something original, short and exciting

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally positive on Overboard! There's a lot to like about it. It's got that signature Inkle flair that jazzes up its simple visual novel interface with colorful art, period-appropriate big band swing soundtrack, and snappy writing. While there isn't a lot of depth to the narrative in its pulpy detective story and two-dimensional characters, it's got enough intrigue and charm to pull you into discovering its secrets, puzzling out the steps to cover up your not-so-perfect crime, or just making fun choices to roleplay your femme fatale fantasies. Also, it touches on the politics of the time with a deft hand, reflecting the regressive ideas of the 1930s while approaching it with modern sensibilities without being ham-fistedly finger-waggy.It's important to note that your choices are limited to the character you are playing as. Veronica Villensey is her own woman; she's a film starlet, conventionally beautiful and confident, and she can wield those assets as gracefully or as bluntly as you desire. But you're no agent 47, so you can't just go around killing people then easily hide their bodies if things go to ♥♥♥♥. At least, not without a lot of effort or facing immediate consequences. I 100% appreciate the limitations and the conveniences of these mechanics. Veronica's character is well-realized in whichever dialogue option you choose, revealing different sides to her that coalesce into a believable sexy thriller protagonist you can sympathize with and root for. The rewind feature gives you some leeway for mistakes without completely robbing decision-making of any weight. However, I can't deny that the shiny veneer of the aesthetics and writing wore thin at times, as I bumped up against the walls of what you can do and discover on my way to the ending that gets you credits. Even with the breezy runtime and ways to speed up sequences, I found myself getting impatient while stumbling through the "right" way to beat the game. Comparing it to other time-loop games like Outer Wilds or Deathloop, I find that even when I'm repeating actions in those games, the more direct control you have makes the moment-to-moment gameplay more engaging than skipping through the same lines of text. Comparing it to other detective visual novel stories like the Ace Attorney series, the more intricate logic puzzles and wilder plot twists in those games make for more satisfying rewards than the straightforward obstacles that give way to soap opera reveals in Overboard!Maybe it's unfair to compare this small indie game to more ambitious titles with bigger productions, especially after finding out that Overboard was made during this pandemic in only 3 months! But yeah, there were moments when I was working towards the "true" ending where I felt like I just wanted it to be over.Funny thing is that after the credits rolled, I saw in the achievements that there's actually a way to kill all 7 cast members, which I hadn't even really thought was possible. Turns out I had as just a devilishly good time solving that murder puzzle as I did for the first quarter of the game, as the possibility space in this tiny ocean liner was bigger than I initially thought. Of course, I am such a typical gamer that doing six more murders was the thing that left me on a high note in a game with the setup of just getting away with one. It does help that the ending for getting a septuple homicide left me hootin' n' hollerin' in absolute bewilderment!Overboard! is not a bad way to spend a couple of hours doing light reverse crime investigation. The premise is novel, which in itself is something I find praiseworthy in this medium, and the pizzazz carries the proceedings for a handful of playthroughs. Just lower your expectations for what's possible with its structure and short development, and you'll have a good time... or be a real sicko like me and try to murder everyone for a totally unexpected ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like to get all the achievements in games (minor spoilers ahead).Overboard! is an indie visual novel detective game where you play as the killer and not the detective. Your goal is to avoid being arrested: you’ll have to talk to possible witnesses, hide or plant evidence and coarse or seduce other passengers to take your side. The dialogues are well written and all the characters have their own personality and motivations, and a specific way to manipulate.The graphics are cartoonish and have an original style that I haven’t seen anywhere else. The illustrations are vivid and colorful and overall are great to look at despite their simplicity. The sound effects help create a realistic ambience and the feeling that you’re on the ship, but unfortunately there isn't voice acting so you’ll have to read everything, but the game has mostly short sentences to choose from.The gameplay doesn’t anything new to the genre, but the time plays an important role as some events and conversion are only available in some places at a specific time, and this is why you’ll have a lot to uncover despite the fact that each game playthrough can be completed in 5 minutes and a lot of runs will be needed for you to uncover all the secrets and get all the achievements.  26 Achievements. Around 4 hours, with the help of a guide for the harder achievements. Will take a lot less if you follow a guide more often. Easy. Easy, with a guide. Getting the harder achievements requires a lot of trial and error until you find the right sequence of actions or conversations, but fortunately there is a guide that has the right sequences you need to follow and the timeframe. Overboard! is an interesting visual novel with colorful cartoonish graphics and a very interesting story and characters. Despite being short, you’ll have to replay it a lot of times to uncover every secret and get the best ending for your character.

_childDocuments_.review: A short story that you have 8 hours to escape from murders.To open all branch and ending, need to keep repeat the game and 1 play-through can be short.I am puzzle and detective lover but not really like to repeat the story over and over again to discover more.1 hours is my play time to repeat at least 5 times above until first time escape from murder accuse.If you looking for a short puzzle game and interested to repeat the story and discover more, then this is your game.
