_childDocuments_.review: Extremely clever little game with a lot of charm. Absolutely recommend for any fans of detective fiction, especially since this puts you on the reverse end of the script. Even once you've figured out how to shift the blame from yourself, you'll still have a lot of potential things you can do in subsequent runs, so there's a lot of replay value here.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Great interactive crime-detective game. Refreshing short length of each playthrough (like 15-30min) and good replay mechanics combined with that. Consider it a puzzle game aswell, you're supposed to go back in time repeatedly to discover all the stories and events that are going on in the short time frame the story occurs in. If one only enjoy to rely on intelligent deduction to solve the case like you do in most murder mystery games, this might not be for you Enjoyed a bunch of of playthrough getting various good & bad endings. After that I equally as much enjoyed reading up on walkthrough guides that lay down the game's content flat, to see what I "missed". So much interesting things in there, don't stop playing just yet! Kudos to story writersHad some doubts first reading some of the negative reviews of it being uninteresting, to narrow, few key decisions matter, etc. But for the price tag of 15$ and goin in with reasonable expectations, it's worth it
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, little whodunnit set aboard a cruise ship. The twist? Youdunnit!The story takes place the morning after you’ve murdered your hubbie. The reason isn’t important. What is important, is that you need to spend the few hours you have left before docking, trying to get out of the predicament. Dodge people, shift blame, play ignorant, murder -- it doesn’t matter. You just need to avoid suspicion.The great thing about Overboard! is that it works on the clock. Not in real-time. But every choice you make will cost you minutes or hours. And usually, those are minutes or hours you could have spent elsewhere. It ends up being one of those games where your choices might feel limited and few, but where the consequences for each one of them is huge. They’re all a commitment. Especially since everyone else on board has their own schedule and agenda; moving about, talking -- pointing fingers. .Recommended if you wish The Occupation took place on the Oriental Express. At sea.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an immensely fun and clever game with loads of options and challenges, a fun cast of characters, excellent writing and a great sense of humour. If you have any love for Inkle's previous title 80 Days or if you like Agatha Christie-like detective stories you'll love Overboard! It may not be as expansive as 80 Days but it's very fun and it's easy to just give it another go if you've ended up in jail once again.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: (+) Great story. Fun, not too serious get-away-with-murder plot. Charming main character.(+) Interesting setting of an upscale ocean-liner, period and genre respecting varied ensemble of characters.(+) Fresh take on a loop mechanic - scheming and social-engineering people around you.(+) Nice art direction including whodunnit-stylized audio (mix could use more care)(+) Multiple endings, multiple solutions.(+) Although a loop mechanic is generally tricky, the core design of this title is fun. The loop mechanic is not too overused, nor exploited. Also the game keeps track of what you learned in previous walkthroughs and guides you away from frustration as it sets your new (optional) goals accordingly.(+) Solely story-based gameplay, no unsolicited mini-games. This design coincidentally allows you to play with irl partner(s)-in-crime in couch co-op as - regardless of who has the controller - everyone stays invested and can steer the character's schemes.(+) Single day/loop doesn't take very long. Generally a great length for a nice afternoon - not too long, doesn't overstay its welcome.(-) Some shortcuts were taken in dialogue logic and continuity(-) More viable solutions and ways to reach your goals would be great(-) All of the weight is based on what you say (correctly navigating the dialogue options), how you act is irrelevant (in other words: how well you lie). That is very unfortunate since the main character is an actress and the topic itself is specifically broached by another character in the game.(-) You cannot use many objects and those you can are only designed with single purpose in mind. On top of that certain actions are unintuitively hidden behind other, seemingly unrelated actions.(-) No anchor points in your walkthrough - inconvenient repetition of the same dialogues is required in certain cases
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little puzzle game that has a lot of replay even after you "beat" it. It's charming as heck, well-written, and funny. I also think it's extremely generous with its mechanics and UI. You can fast-forward parts of the time loop you want to do the same way, you get one re-do per scene to help in case you screw up... this game really respects your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: You can see the DNA of Inkle's previous, excellent game "80 Days", but the interactions in Overboard! are much faster-paced, racing through a tense 8 hours in-game vs the other's leisurely 80-day journey.The narrative unspools delightfully, giving reason to repeat even after you've gotten away with murder - each playthrough gives you more understanding of what tools you have at your disposal to "manage" the various passengers and crew, challenging you to find the right order to execute your scheme before time runs out.There are at least three "victory" options, and each has a host of subplots to tie up along the way. Groundhog Day meets How To Get Away With Murder, wrapped in a charming period bow.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A short enjoyable reverse murder mystery adventure that reminds me a lot of 80 Days. In the middle of the night you push your husband over the railings of a a ship that is on its way to America in the 1930s. What might have driven you to kill him, can you get away with it, and what secrets are the other passengers hiding? You are given a few hours (likely closer to minutes in real time) the next day to answer those questions.I definitely liked the main character and was happy to help her get away with murder, lucking into the best ending on my first playthrough.Screenshots:
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super well done version of a simple twist on a played concept.  Many games tell the story of the detective who finds the clues to a murder, but here is the murderer needing to hide their tracks from the ship.  Just describing it as a game where you cover up murdering your husband had my friends chomping at the bit to try the game out.  I would recommend this to detective players that need a twist to spice up their adventure games.  As this is a smaller game with less reviews, I would like to be a bit more precise in a critical breakdown of the gameplay.  Having the timer at the top lets the player slowly figure out optimal times for strategising their killer routes.  It is well done and should be kept in any iterations of this game.  The main character is purposely dislikable and it makes fail states less dooming.  The other characters' reactions to my dialogue choices were not always what I expected, but any important conversation was well enough written and hinted that dialogue choices arent a shot in the dark.  The game lost its intrigue for me when I started getting bored with only playing to find out more about the few characters that had secrets or independent goals.  The game is not very replayable after exploring to contentment, I wouldnt really watch someone else play it, but I would recommend it on sale to a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is entertaining and delightful! It feels like a more updated version of The Deed, another game in which you must murder someone and lay the blame elsewhere. Overboard! begins with a brief scene of your character throwing her husband off the deck of a ship, then awaking the next morning to have to deal with the aftermath. Do you lie about the last time you saw Malcom alive? Do you say he's missing, or do you tell everyone he's in your cabin? Do you go to breakfast, or do you snoop? Do you ring the bell to notify everyone he's gone overboard, and try to deceive everyone early, or do you wait out the day until someone discovers Malcolm is missing?Each time you play, you can try a slightly different route in hopes of the best outcome, and the game does a fanatastic job of trying to build you up to your ideal escape. First, you may fail. Maybe a few times. Next, you might succeed, but not be eligible for receiving insurance money. Next, you might need to address some loose ends. Can you keep people's mouths shut? Can you get them out of the picture? Can you escape faster?The game also gives you a running task list of different things to try (can you earn a certain amount of money on ship, or find out a secret about a guest or crew member?) that might help you discover new ways to win the game. So although you could play and "beat" this game in 5 minutes if you're lucky and crafty, the numerous pathways will keep you murdering your husband over and over again, ever in search of the perfect crime. I would say the only minor critique I have is that occasionally, certain dialogues in the "trial" scene seem a little unfair. Occasionally, I will choose NOT to lie about something, and a character will still claim that I lied, and then I have to come up with an excuse about why I lied. That can be a little frustrating as I'm crafting my narrative, because some choices of dialogue don't feel like they matter quite as much as I need them to. But I'm still figuring out the ideal way to get away with murder, so hey, I'm no expert!The rest of the gameplay is easy and fun: clicking through dialogue and navigating to rooms, with the very clever option of having a speed-replay with all your previous choices from a scene so that it doesn't get tedious. (This is something Twelve Minutes desperately needed.)This is definitely a game I'm going to keep popping into from time to time!
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is surprisingly addictive. Once you think you know what's going on with the characters, a new twist comes in the form of visiting a room at a different time, or choosing a slightly different dialogue path. 30 runs in, I still don't think I've discovered everything in this game. Really impressed and love everything about this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: With its deceptively simple mechanics, Overboard! gives you so much to experience, brilliantly combining the need to strategise with the tempting potential to unleash absolute mayhem. It’s brimming with well-realised characters to fall in love with or kill (or both!), and it’s all packaged in a beautiful '30s art style. It's smooth sailing all the way in this entertaining inverse-Cluedo-style story, so don't miss the boat on inkle’s latest glorious narrative adventure. Good:    Multiple dialogue and action choices give you many, many ways to cause carnage    Attractive Art Deco-like graphics    Excellent sound effects and jazzy score fit well with the time period    Bonus mini-objectives make the game highly replayableBad:    I only wish it were longer
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting visual novel-esque game where you try to escape blame for the murder you definitely committed. I was absolutely enthralled at the beginning, as there were so many options and it felt like so many things to do. I finally 100%ed the game after around 8 hours and 43 attempts, and i think i was a little disappointed that the game didn't have as many options as I initially thought. It's easier to learn all of the secrets than i thought - I would explore different options, and they would lead me back to the same information I had learned a different way. This is great game design, I just kind of expected there to be more things to discover.  I still highly enjoyed my time playing this game and it's multiple endings, but maybe wait for a sale if you're as frugal as me, since there is less than 10 hours of gameplay. Will probably continue to play with other people (Want to see if my mother would like it!) and if that is the case, I'll edit my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A game from the creators of 80 Days. It's more of a puzzle game than narrative/adventure game, where you have to figure out how to get away from murder by replaying the day over and over again and use what knowledge of everyone's schedule and circumstances to manipulate the events. Each playthrough is short, but you're meant to replay it over and over again to figure out how to manipulate everyone to the perfect ending. It's quite interesting, but don't expect something too similar with 80 day. If something like that sounds interesting and you want to try something similar, you can try a much cheaper but also much less production-valued game titled "The Deed" and its sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so I was very unimpressed with this the first and second time I played through. But, on my third playthrough, I saw the magic. It's a complicated game and every little moves matter (partly because a playthrough is about 30 mins). This is a game to revisit over and over, to try and get a good (or perfect) ending. I have yet to get away with my husband's murder, but I shall...I SHALL.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! I love the concept and the art style especially. Playing the killer instead of the detective is not something I've come across often and was a really fun. For having such a small group of characters and each play through being fairly short there is a good amount of depth.I am glad I bought it on sale though. I "won", meaning I got away with the murder, in just under an hour on my third run. I will still play some more to get achievements and try to discover new things but if I had paid the full $15 I would been a little annoyed I finished that quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: [May contain spoiler]While I do like the game and the strategy I need to use to get the "best" ending. I did coming in after seeing the trailer thinking that I can pick and choose who I want to pin as a murderer. But apparently it's more complicated than that.There are pre-written character relationships that exists that affects the story. The fact that  I like the replay-ability of the game. And that there's a lot of branching storyline with untapped potentials. I haven't explored all, but I'm not sure if I'm interested enough in the characters to want to find out. Once I knew how to get the "best" ending, finding more details about the others are kinda ...useless? Because in the end, As a player, I play as the wife, that's surrounded by these characters. She knew their names, but didn't tell me, the player, who / what they are in her life. I had to find out her secrets by playing the game, choosing certain dialogs. Maybe it's just me, but I would love to know those info beforehand, particularly  But I do see the fun in revealing the mystery of who's who, like reading a book and find out you're the real murderer--oh wait, they spoil that part already. So, why hide the others?I do like the checkmarks that kinda hint you on what you're supposed to do. I like how time flies just by talking nonsense. I like how you just do things because the option is there and then still don't understand what it's for, lol. It's a fun, different, game. I've never played anything like this before!! But...I wish I can like it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit worried about this game because inkle's previous game was a bit of a flop by their standards. But where 80 Days and Heaven's Vault felt like there was an overwhelming amount of content, Overboard! feels really tight, easily explorable, and lots of fun.It's a reverse murder mystery: You start the game committing a murder, and the rest of the game is replaying the following day Groundhog-Day style, trying to get away with it.As with all inkle games, the real depth is in the writing and the branching narrative. There's a bunch of reading - the whole game is driven through text, with visual annotations - but the story is funny despite its darkness.A single playthrough is a lot shorter than the studio's other flagship games, you'll get through a loop in around half an hour, and this gives it much more of a casual feel than something like Heaven's Vault, which was more of an epic.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable little game, I enjoyed all of the dialogue, and the the tone felt perfect for what the game was going for. It was incredibly satisfying getting all the endings, especially the 'true' ending, which made me feel far smarter than I actually am when I managed to get it! The sheer amount of solutions to every single problem you encounter was impressive, it adds a lot to the replayability of the game, which is definitely a big draw.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I've often considered how to get away with the perfect murder, and this was my chance to live the dream without going back to prison.  Our heroine, though not possessing any redeeming quality beyond fashion sense, is very likeable.  Every character has their dark secrets, and there are multiple successful and unsuccessful endings to encourage replayability.  The developer was brilliant to allow you to quickly re-trace your path to save time.  The art is colourful and charming, with music and sound effects that truly make you feel just like a homicidal passenger on a luxury liner in the 1930s.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually one for visual novel type games. (This might not fit squarely in that genre, but close enough.) However, the styling and the unique premise got my curiosity and I'm glad of it. The art, the music, the characters, and the clever ways to trigger certain events were all a joy. The game is quite short if you're really working at it, but I think of things in terms of movie tickets. I'm willing to drop more than $10 for two hours of entertainment in a theater, so a fifteen dollar game that entertains me for five times as long is a good value.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up after listening to the Besties podcast recommended it and I was not disappointed! If you're a fan of the Hitman series but always wondered "Huh. I wonder what it would be like to play this game but from the other side of the kill." and you're a fan of branching path, visual novel type games - this is the game for you! The art is beautiful, the persistent tips are really helpful as you will have to do many different playthroughs but with each playthrough you get to learn other passengers schedules, item locations, until you really get in the flow. 10/10, the best indie game I've played in a long time!
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think you'll be surprised that an Inkle game has wonderful writing, but it needs to be said again. Overboard! has absolutely top-shelf writing. The characters are all amazing, especially Veronica herself. Also, the ship is a wonderful toybox and it's a pleasure to figure out how everything works.I do wish though that the Subedar-major was a little more astute though. Sometimes he let things pass that I would have liked to be caught on. There was a an ending where I thought he accepted a very dubious motive. Hercule Poirot would have definitely caught me on that one.Nevertheless, I thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. On top of everything else, it features some truly terrible poetry that cannot be missed.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little reversed murder mystery with strong Agatha Christie vibes. With a very fast loop and many, many paths to explore the game is made for dozens of replays and good at it, as with almost every loop another level of the mystery comes to life. It's fun, unapologetic and I surprisingly challenging at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet but very memorable. The art style is quite striking and the interactions are fun. The game is short, even with the multiple replays it won't take too long to figure out most of it, but it is very fun nonetheless and the writing of the interactions is gripping. Veronica is also a very entertaining protagonist!
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I had never heard of this game till I received it as a gift.  I started it up, just to see if I'd like it and I was instantly hooked.  I just finished my second play through and I am loving this game.  It's short but you will play over and over with different choices and scenes.  I highly recommend this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I said, I'll play a little bit, just to try it. Famous last words. This game made me LATE! I could not stop playing. I am a big fan of every single Inkle game, they honestly never MISS. And this one is a relatively short game, with a lot of fun choices, and a real sense of amazing storytelling. You feel the need to rush, you feel the danger, and you even feel the satisfaction of a well done murder! It also had a hint of creepyness (how else to describe it? That dream like unsettling feeling that you get from an unexpected turn in narrative) that is always amazingly done in all Inkle games.I know I played just a bit, but I can't wait to go back and explore all the options!
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, entertaining game with high replayability. Though there is something to be said about the price point, its something I'm personally willing to pay for an experience like this. That being said there are comparable free games or cheaper games that are mobile games. Though I think think has a certain charm and polish to it. I'd say if you like interactive CYOA games you may be interested in this, give it a try, otherwise you may not enjoy the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a handful of games that have marketed themselves as being "Like Groundhog Day," and to my delight, Overboard!, despite not marketing itself as such, does a better job than all the others. As much as I loved "The Sexy Brutale," this is a lot similar to what I expected going into it.The scope of options at your fingertips aboard the boat are robust to an unbelievable degree; despite having what appears to be very linear choices, Overboard! is built upon beefy systems of If Then statements that continued to surprise me at how well it remembered my personal choices several hours and plays of the game. As of typing this, I've played it 81 times, and only just now feel as though I've seen everything there is to see (and I may even be wrong with that).Of course, being able to play a game 81 Times in ~8 hours feels a little silly, but that is the point: players are expected to use knowledge they learn about their options aboard the boat and explore what happens if they try X with Y at Z O'Clock. Plus, it also doesn't do that-one-thing that these types of games does, where replays of it quickly grate on your patience. A single play can take as quick as 2-10 minutes, so you won't be spending too much of your time mashing through dialogue options to get to the next thing.This is assisted by just how much breadth there is. For example, it's astounding how often doing the same things just 10-20 in-game minutes apart will yield different results, but it's not so so deep that you lose track of why or how it works. You'll quickly pick up on the patterns and feel like a master of the boat, expertly maneuvering each character and learning the dark secrets everyone has. Between this and Obra Dinn, "Murder Mystery on a Boat with a Twist" has quickly become one of my favorite genres. I firmly and strongly recommend this game to anyone, no matter their experience or opinion of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite short compared to Heaven's Vault and 80 Days but the price is reasonable and fun to work out how to get the best endings (or the worst.) It would be nice if the game had some more helpful features such as a timeline and a log so you can see what you've done in the past and what the characters will do so you can plan ahead. The game can also be a bit linear with certain endings only having one path or one important action but as you learn the full picture, you understand that you really shouldn't have many options.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Overboard! is not very long but has tonnes of replay value. Set in the 1930s on a Trans-Atlantic voyage from London to New York, Overboard! starts with the villain-protagonist Mrs. Villensey murdering her husband at night. The game starts at 8 AM the following morning and you must cover up your tracks and manipulate evidence before people notice your missing husband. There are multiple ways to tackle this and multiple people you can frame. You can find out the dark secrets of fellow passengers to blackmail and manipulate them. Remember to keep your story straight right from the beginning. In the end your goal is go free and receive the insurance payout which will be lost if Mr. Villensey's death is ruled a suicide. Artwork is great, I love how the characters keep a track of your statements. There are many ways to get your objective so there is a lot of replay value. It's kind of like low tech Hitman or if Hitman was an interactive text game.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Charming, sharply written, dense little puzzle box that's very easy to get into and full of intrigue without being too overwhelming. I picked this up to play with a friend over stream and it worked out very well to have someone to bounce ideas off of, and also be able to have two people each egging each other on to do very bad things.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I. LOVE. THIS. GAME! I've literally been playing for 4 hours straight today while I avoid my responsibilities and it's so fun. It's hilarious, campy and involves murder, which is great. You play as a woman who has murdered your husband the night before the game starts and throughout the game you must either silence witnesses by blackmail or murder, convince the group of your innocence, romance them or be arrested. Your previous runs highlight new parts of the story and give you new goals to complete, so even once you've restarted 15 times like I have, you probably haven't finished all the goals. In fact, I still have 14 achievements to go! The one minor downside I see is the card game. I HATE IT. It's painfully confusing for me, who has never played a card game in my life. I've been playing with my partner and he's managed to win the 1000 once, but we've never cleared him out for the achievement and he's dreading it. I wish it had a skip/autoplay feature that maybe gave you RNG on how much you win through the cardgame.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Each run is short enough to let you play in bite-sized chunks but there's enough depth as you gain knowledge between attempts to keep you coming back to uncover the game's secrets.  I've managed to get away with the murder, but achievements and lingering plot threads are enough to make me want to dive in and try to find a better route.  Really unique little game.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: a wonderful gem of a detective story! You have murdered your husband on the high seas and, regrettably, there was at least one witness. How can you spend eight hours to frame one of the other people on the ship? The first game of reverse Cluedo ever created, this will keep your little grey cells going all the way through to the denouement....
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Overboard! is a great "getting away with murder" game taking place on a cruise ship. Each run (around 20-30 minutes) starts with you getting up in the morning after killing your husband the night before. The objective is to avoid being accused of murder, or even better, to put the blame on someone else. With each run you get to know the other characters better, learn about their schedules and secrets, and understand how you can manipulate or frame them. I didn't enjoy Heaven's Vault mainly due to the boring exploration and trying to do too much. Overboard! is a smaller game stripped down to the core elements Inkle does best: a text adventure build around deep and dynamic dialog trees. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Very well written. Your choices in this game really do matter, and there are a number of different ways that things can play out. It's important to keep in mind who knows what, and you can influence this throughout any given playthrough.It's a clockwork game, which is why you'll definitely want to play the game many times over to try out different approaches.You will eventually reach a point where you've seen everything there is to see so it is not infinitely replayable, but that's not necessarily a bad thing. There's more than enough to justify the asking price and if you like story driven and/or detective games then this one is definitely for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: A frequently hilarious graphic adventure where you've murdered your husband and try desperately to cover your tracks over the course of the next day. As the other characters remember the things you've said to them and done around them, keeping your story straight is essential. This is harder than it initially appears, and it may take a few runs (that each usually take 20 mins or so) before you don't see the inside of a jail cell. Even then, there is a difference between getting away with it, and getting away with it .Eventually I got to the point where I saw pretty much all there is to see (I think), but I'd more than had my money's worth by then. Anyone who likes their graphic adventures or visual novels should give this a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely not-so-little game: you're a 1930s femme fatale on a ship bound for America, and you have just murdered your husband (as one does). What follows is a race against the clock to cover your tracks, get rid of incriminating evidence (and witnesses) and gain accomplices for your cause before you reach New York and are sent to jail. A single playthrough is short (maybe 10-15 minutes), but the game cleverly pushes you to replay, try different things and push for better results (first you're only aiming to get away with murder by making it look like a suicide, but later you have to try to pin the murder on someone else so you can cash the life insurance check). A delight for anyone who likes narrative games and whodonnits, beautifully illustrated and very cleverly designed.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short and sweet narrative game. Each session takes around 30 minutes, and you could clear everything in a few hours (depending on how long it takes for you to solve the several mysteries/puzzles).The graphics and sounds are very good, the humour is on point, and the small changes in each play through makes it fun to chase for the different endings and variations.In short, a classic Inkle game :-)
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely enthralling. The premise is delightful -- a classic murder-mystery scenario, except *you're* the murderer, and you have to get away with it (complete with outsmarting the ship's very own amateur Poirot, who has foiled me many times). Like Inkle's other games, the narrative feels infinite; I've done 13 runs at this point, and I feel like I've only scratched the surface of the possible interactions and routes through the day.In short:  meets  meets .BEST:- Loop length: About 30 minutes if you're going through each scene carefully; much shorter if you're doing reruns and speeding through interactions you've seen before- You can restart to the beginning of the day at any time without losing anything!- The UX design is great -- the running checklist of suggestions gives you nudges toward possible new routes to explore, without feeling like a quest journal you're obligated to complete. The visual design of the inventory, characters moving around the ship, and the conversation flow is super slick as well.- Failing this game is hilarious. Spoiler for one way to lose:
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful little game playing well into inkle's storied traditions!This game plays right into the 80 days aesthetic in UI, narrative flexibility (obvious for an inkle game), and art design - BUT everything has been stylizing a bit more. Overall this leads to a great feeling game in a small little package that you can play again and again.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I was going to play a visual novel. I was wrong. Overboard! feels less like an interactive novel but more like a streamlined version of Hitman. You slowly uncover the characters, their motivations, their behaviours, then plot your moves. Cleverly designed, wonderfully acted, with visual and audio to match.
_childDocuments_.name: Overboard!

_childDocuments_.review: [DIsclaimer: Helped with the testing of the game]One ship. One murder.Get away with it or behind bars. Or use plenty of opportunities to create more chaos, frolick away, find a new love or have a nice chat with God (or something). Peel away layer after layer and discover more of the complex mechanics hiding behind the minimalist design, discovering even more interactions.Just stay away from the dolphins. Very sharp teeth, y'know.

_childDocuments_.review: There isn't much to say about this game, but off the bat I will say that this feels unfinished.  Anywho, on to the positives first. The artstyle is very VERY nice and stylish. It was a treat looking at all of the levels from start to finish and I only rarely lost sight of enemies because of it, which is kind of astounding given that there is no color. The music is also really nice throughout, didn't think synth would work with this kind of game, but hey, it worked really well. Now for the downsides. Oh lord where to start. Biggest point  has to be that all of the bosses are braindead easy, even on the hardest difficulty. All they do is run at you or near you and you never need to change your tactics once to beat them. That itself is a damn shame because all of their designs are excellent, but they are weighed down by their fights.  Number two for me is the animations. They're just unfinished, I don't want to be mean but the character animations are really stiff and weird, the enemies sometimes look like they are clay figures melting in the sun anytime they stop to aim at you. You could make the argument that this is a retro inspired game, but I don't think that gives it a pass.  Last thing I'll touch on is the requirements for the hardest difficulty. I am going to spoil what happens in the first level, so if you still want to play the game even after everything I said please stop here. Okay cool, right so for the first mission on the hardest difficulty you need to get the deed from the mansion, if you don't you fail the whole mission. What makes this dumb is that THE WHOLE MANSION BURNS DOWN AT THE END! It is like this for E V E R Y mission! You free civilians and kill the big even, but by god you forget to get the milk... MISSION FAILED! It drags the game down for me a smidge, I know it sounds petty and is probably a me thing, but it bears mention.  All in all it's a okay game, but 15$ seems steep for a 1 playthrough game that's pretty jank.

_childDocuments_.review: I was nervous about buying this one. Many complaints on the Steam forums suggested serious problems with sound design, physics, level design, etc. Also, the people behind the game disappointingly were briefly trying to solicit positive reviews in an unethical way, but it seems they realized their mistake (or had it indicated to them) fast and took that down. Despite all of this, I went ahead and bought it, and, so far, I'm happy with the game. With shooters like this I know quickly whether they'll be good from their basic feel. Simple run-and-gun games that have the right feel from the start almost always end up being good on the whole. So even though I've only played the first level at this point, I'm already inclined to give my opinion. The bottom line is that it does feel great to play. The weapon sounds aren't especially powerful, but they are pretty solid--earlier on, based on old gameplay footage, it seems the shotgun and rifle might have used the same sound effects, which would've been bad (and lazy), but this is no longer the case. Considering the four guns I've gotten to use, revolver, shotgun, rifle, and gatling gun, each has its own sound effects. The sense of impact the guns have on enemies seems to be a particular strong point of the game (except with the bosses I fought in the first level), which I think is partly due to targeted dismemberment (you can blow the arms, legs, and head off of certain enemies). Someone complained about the game seeming too slow, which is not the impression I got. Ordinary movement speed is slow, but there seems to be no limit on sprinting, which allows you to move at a quick pace. The only problem here is that as far as I can tell you have to keep L-shift (or whatever button you have sprint bound to) held down. There should be an autorun button, so that you can be permanently set to move at maximum speed, as the original Doom games have, for example.Where the game shines is in its large-scale fights and visual presentation. In just the first level, on the second-highest difficulty, I faced a lot of enemies at once multiple times. There was very little dead air in the first level. Enemy variety was impressive for a first level. Some are melee only, some have guns, some shoot typical straight-line projectiles, some shoot homing projectiles, some attack from the air. A nice touch is that you can shoot the projectiles and destroy them in midair before they hit you. The first level was reasonably challenging at the difficulty I played on (I died a couple times), but the two boss fights were a bit disappointing--it was too easy to take down the bosses. I saw a complaint about the AI. I haven't seen anything unusual about the AI for a swarm shooter game such as this one. The enemies in these games don't tend to be smart, but instead pose a challenge because so many are thrown at you at once and because of the varying behaviors they exhibit requiring a bit of strategy and triaging in taking them out (in this game for instance, there are bird enemies that divebomb you while you're trying to deal with melee enemies and projectiles at eye level). On the visuals, I don't have much to say other than that I like the black-and-white artstyle. A handful of effects stood out, such as the feathers of those bird enemies I just mentioned flying around and then drifting to the ground after they're shot/killed.There also seems to be a satisfactory amount of content for the price. Looking at reviews of the game (not on Steam but on game review sites), it apparently takes about 5-7 hours to finish the game (one guy mentioned that it took him about 7 hours on "normal" difficulty specifically). Since there are 8 levels and it took me a little under an hour to beat the first one, and also I don't tend to play games very fast, that seems about right.Now for the problems: The physics can feel a little off at times. I haven't gotten stuck in level geometry yet but it might happen later as it seemed I sort of hitched on some things here and there. When taking running jumps off inclines the movement can feel a bit too floaty, almost like you're being flung in an unnatural way. Certain sounds seem to have a crackle in them, especially some enemy noises--not sure if there was a problem with the sound mixing or what. Moreover, enemy noises in general seem screwy, almost cartoonish at times. The music might not have started when it was supposed to for a stretch. Also, I noticed the occasional enemy clip through the ground after getting killed, or have its lower body sink into a surface while it was still alive and moving around. It seems strange to me that you can't use your sword to destroy padlocks but can only shoot them off. Finally, the crosshair turns red when it's over enemies that are already dead, when it should stay white. Hopefully the dev can fix these things.Overall Kingdom of the Dead (so far) is fun--nothing mindblowing but fun. If my opinion changes from now until I beat it, I'll update this. But I think that most people who like 90s-type PC shooters will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: How hard must it be to make your first-person shooter stand out in 2022? Sometimes it seems like every concept under the sun has been covered, with every possible aesthetic and system thoroughly explored. Yet, somehow we still get games like Kingdom of the Dead, that manage to carve out a unique look and feel from the vast fields of shooters. Dark, pulpy, funny, and grim, it strikes a singular balance that you really won’t find anywhere else. I certainly can’t say this one breaks new ground in terms of gameplay, but there’s plenty of spooky action and neat twists in the missions you’ll undertake to rid the world of the walking dead.The dead are restless, and have designs on the late 19th century United States. A professor-turned-general named Chamberlain is tasked with stopping them, being a member of a clandestine paranormal enforcement agency and also the possessor of a demonic sword. Man, sword, and horse have a big job ahead of them, closing gateways to the great beyond that have sprung open all over the eastern seaboard. This grim adventure will take you to crypts and skyscrapers, ships and trains, wilderness and battlefields, all populated by the walking dead and their monstrous retinue. An assortment of time-period-appropriate firearms will let you cut a swath through the shambling hordes, eventually earning you a confrontation with the force behind this onslaught of death.Easily the most striking thing about Kingdom of the Dead is its appearance, and it’s an important factor in enjoying this game. Unlike the vast majority of 3D shooters, this one is almost entirely monochromatic, with figures textured in the bold lines and cross-hatching of classic pulp comics. Item pickups come in colors, to helpfully highlight them against the dark environs, but the rest of the game is stark whites and blacks, and can admittedly be hard on the eyes, despite the impressive aesthetic. Fortunately, there’s an entire menu of palettes you can swap to at any time to give the game a more palatable appearance for you. I certainly experimented with the many colors and tones, but eventually settled on a more gentle rendition of the original black and white.However you choose to perceive it, this is a first-person shooter from a more reserved school of thought. Your boy Chamberlain moves at a decent clip, but combat is paced to be very deliberate here, with a single headshot doing the work of a dozen bodyshots and larger creatures falling most reliably to concentrated fire. Nothing in your arsenal fires particularly quickly, not even the Gatling gun, nor do enemies swarm you with any great haste. However, losing track of foes to flank or snipe you is a leading cause of death in the war against Death, so carefully winnowing enemy ranks is the way to go. There aren’t too many enemy types in the game, but the individual levels do a decent job of varying the challenge by offering your weapon pickups in different orders and presenting wildly different environments in which to wield them.That was a distinct highlight for me, the variety found in the levels. Each of the nine missions in the game are set in unique locales, from manors to ocean liners to battlefields. Some of my favorites included the train, which speeds along the countryside and offers a number of interesting encounters despite the linear layout, and the skyscraper, which involved some rather Thief-esque scampering across rooftops. A few of the setpieces are truly remarkable, including one on the ship that I won’t spoil. Each level has a boss with its own unique look and mechanics, though none of them presented too much of a challenge. On higher difficulties, you’ll also need to complete secondary objectives (always finding some extra item) or rescue trapped humans. It’s not a very challenging game on any level, and part of that is owed to the simple combat and enemy behaviors. Don’t expect any wild shootouts or ridiculous gibs, because this one is a very straight-forward trek.The star attraction here is certainly the tone and atmosphere, encapsulated by the wry dialogues you get with your sword and the demonic commanders you have to dispatch. Kingdom of the Dead is firmly rooted in pulp horror, complete with insane synth soundtrack and dark twist waiting for you at the end. The aesthetic and unique levels do so much to keep you coming back, wondering what else might be lurking in the shadows or where this whole grim journey will be leading. It won’t take you much more than three hours to find out, since the combat won’t be holding you back in any part. But again, even now you don’t really get many first-person shooters like this, and it’s a worthy experience to see what can be done with such a singular look and feel.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: KINGDOM of the DEAD is one of those games that made me want to play it by the sheer greatness of its style. The trailer looked and also sounded amazing and I could already see myself running and gunning through masses of undead hordes whilst banging to the great synthwave soundtrack. Now, when I first started the game, I couldn't help but feel slightly underwhelmed, even cheated on a bit. The artstyle looks superb and there are even options for a vast array of different color settings if you're not into the black and white original. The gameplay itself however feels slow, or at least much slower than I had anticipated. The music does have more of an atmospheric, eerie vibe with occasional synth woops, which surely fit the overall tone - but were not what I wanted after watching the amazing trailer. There is a wide array of missions to choose from, each with three difficulty settings. There surely is replayabilty but personally, I did not feel the urge to replay one level. It just wasn't as much fun as expected. Monsters and bosses were not badly designed but especially the melee versions lacked some sort of challenge and variety, except when they attacked in big numbers.This is by no means a bad game, hence the recommendation. I like that your sword is some sort of sidekick, sporting some special ability as well if you fill up his charge meter. Overall, it is a slow mix of doom, nightmare creatures and the color palette of paper sorcerer. If that is what you are looking for, you'll surely not be disappointed. Just don't look at the trailer and expect the same head nodding, blood pumping atmosphere as I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I was kinda underwhelmed by the game. The visual style is nice. _childDocuments_.review: Kingdom of the Dead is a unique and stylized shooter with some interesting ideas, that ultimately suffers from a lack of polish and excessive jank.Pros:- Really nice visual presentation with a distinct b&w artstyle.- Solid gunplay and decent enemy variety.- An interesting Lovecraft inspired world.- Varied levels with decent level design.- Cool soundtrack.Cons:- Terrible audio mixing. Inconsistent volume levels on ambient sounds, and some sounds like the distant monster growls are repeated too often. The river in the fourth level is especially loud.- Poor weapon sounds. Nearly every weapon in your arsenal sound more like toys than real gun, and that can make combat feel unsatisfying.- Extreme jank at times. Movement can feel awkward and you can get stuck on geometry, enemies get stuck in walls, escaped prisoners will run through objects like they don't exist.- No FoV options, and lacks custom keybinding of individual weapons.- Lack of gamma options or a flashlight. Some rooms in the game are pitch black, which can make navigation a pain. The flying harpy enemy can easily blend into the dark sky, making them nearly impossible to see. The game also suffers from lighting bugs, as a room was suddenly lit properly after reloading a checkpoint.- Boss fights are repeated and extremely easy. The strategy to win every fight is to strafe and hold down the fire button. Some bosses have the added "challenge" of endlessly spawning adds into the arena, which accomplishes little besides being an annoyance and tanking the framerate in a game already suffering from performance issues.- Checkpoints seem weirdly implemented. Respawning will take away most of your ammo and reset things like already picked up weapons and prisoners already freed.- Dull and unsatisfying melee combat. Your sword has oddly short reach and doesn't feel useful when guns get the job done better. It's only really used for a gimmick boss.Overall, a classic example of good idea but poor execution. There's a foundation for a solid game in here, and had it gotten an extra year or two of development time and polish, I believe it would've had the potential to be quite good.

_childDocuments_.review: • : Kingdom of the Dead successfully creates a dark and atmospheric world that draws players into its eerie and captivating narrative.• : The game features a compelling storyline with twists and turns that keep players engaged and eager to uncover the mysteries within.• : The variety and creativity in enemy designs contribute to challenging and visually interesting encounters throughout the game.• : Exploring the game world is rewarded with hidden secrets, lore, and valuable items, encouraging players to venture off the beaten path.• : A well-crafted soundtrack and ambient sounds enhance the overall gaming experience, adding to the tension and immersion.• : Kingdom of the Dead offers a range of unique weapons and abilities that provide diverse strategies for tackling enemies.• : Some players may encounter glitches, such as invincible birds or impassable stairs, which can disrupt the flow of the game and break immersion.• : The decision to reset ammo to the minimum upon respawn rather than retaining the player's previous ammo count at the checkpoint can lead to frustrating and challenging situations.• : While some aspects of the game shine, there are instances of inconsistent quality, with certain areas or features feeling less polished or thought out.• : Some players with ultrawide, or larger monitors may encounter issues where going up in resolution causes the game to be cropped and zoomed. The only remedy is to play at a much smaller resolution.• : The absence of clear communication from the developers regarding bug fixes, updates, or community feedback may leave players feeling unsupported and frustrated.• : Once the main storyline is completed, the lack of meaningful side quests or alternative paths diminishes the game's replayability, potentially reducing its long-term appeal.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good FPS with unique graphic style that I loved. I liked that there were many art styles to choose from so anyone can pick their favorite. This game also has good feeling guns that all pack a punch and are pleasure to use. I liked also how the levels are build as they are logical in their layout so you don’t need any map and I like that there is a secondary objective to do and civilians to be rescued. The banter between you and your living sword at the start of each mission is also a nice touch.The synthwave music in this game is great and it fits to the world presented and gives you an eerie feeling that there is danger around every corner. And while music makes you want to run and gun you really need to move cautiously and slowly to be sure to pick your fights and fight enemies in advantageous positions to not get surrounded. I liked that the difficulty levels don’t give monsters more HP but instead they make monsters deal more damage and also higher difficulty forces you to complete the secondary objective and to never let a civilian die or you will fail the level. It makes the game harder but still fair and your guns still feel like real guns not some peashooters. I hate it when games thinks that harder level just means inflating monsters HP as that is just lazy design.The enemies that attack in melee have big problems with pathfinding if you are somewhere higher than the same ground level they spawned on. Also the collision system is not great as sometimes you can basically stand on a table and shoot the enemies while they don’t know how to get to you so they are just standing there looking at you while at other times they have no problems getting to you and climb on the table or anything. Also melee enemies sometimes clip thru the terrain when they run at you and I had also some range enemies stuck in the wall and shoot at me while I was not able to shoot back as my bullets were hitting the wall. Sometimes I even saw melee enemies running past me while they head and eyes were fixated on me and it was funny to see their head move around to see me all the time while their body was running away to a location where I was before.If you die you continue from a save point and while you keep all the hearths you did find and the rescued civilians and picked up weapons you lose almost all the ammo you picked up and if you try to backtrack from a checkpoint you will find the ammo in the same places like you did before but also all enemies respawns so checkpoints are not really helpful and they seem to work more like just spawning the player into a new level filled with enemies and items but with some basic amount of ammo and in the checkpoint place instead of the start of the level.This is a good FPS with many flaws that keep it away from being great. A little more work and this game would be great.Rating: 5.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting art stlye and setup, but generic shooter gameplay with little to offer. Another game with focus on visuals above gameplay. + The art style is indeed interesting. Not just the black-and-white, comic-aesthetic but also design of the enemies and even levels. + Intriguing setup. + The cacademon-equivalent's orbs being shotable was a good design choice.- Lackluster weapon design. Especially the sword. You would think that a demonic sword would be powerful, but you need to hit the head or you'll just be chopping off limbs, and even then you need luck. The rest of the weapons are not interesting: shotgun, rifle, hand-cranked gatling gun, dynamite and canon. There are alt-fire, but only the shotgun's is useful (okay, the rifle's and handgun's is sort-of cool too but not very much). - Bosses are especially lackluster. They mostly just hover around, are easily defeated even on highest difficulty. It's not just that they have low life bars, it's that they don't do much which is a pity because they are imaginative in design. There is a bat boss that doesn't fly. - The enemies also have limited intelligence and the creativity kind of ran out at the higher level monsters that are drawn from Doom (classic). We have a cacademon-equivalent and even a mancubus, complete with canons for arms. - You have to practically hold down the left shift for the entire time for the game to effectively move and dodge. An "always run" option would have been nice. - The setup of the story is intriguing but doesn't deliver very much. More banter between the sword and the main character would have been great. Hell, a somewhat deeper exploration of the setting and bosses would have been more interesting than end-of-level bullet fodder. - Once you feel out the gameplay of the game, how movement and gunfighting works, most of the difficulty is gone and feels like a chore rather than a challenge. Even on highest difficulty.- Janky. No ultrawide support, enemies clip into the walls on occassion, hit detection can be weird, you need to enter the options menu every time to apply any keybind changes, controller support is awful and those are just the bugs I noticed and remember. There are missing keybinds and other options. Steamdeck compatibility: the game technically runs without obvious visual glitches, however the very first level has performance issues (the second didn't, didn't test it on all the levels) and the game controller support is incredibly awful, I had all sorts of weird issues and the UI requires a mouse. The game needs optmization, bugfixes and proper controller support for it to be actually enjoyable on a steamdeck. I feel a retro-fps is the wrong gamestlye here. The artstlye and setup would have been better served with a more horror-centric survival-horror gameplay with more focus on exploring the scenic areas, delving deeper into this macabre, black-and-white inspired, gothic(?) world with a more mortal character. Overall, I regret buying the game. It fell short on the promise I saw on alphabetagamer's video. If you want to see the interesting art stlye, it might be worth a look but otherwise there are better retro-FPS games out there. This is another example of focus on visuals over the gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has... something going for it. It has weapon alt fires. That's about the only positive. The sound design is all over the place, with really only 2 enemies able to be distinguished from a sound cue alone that they just spawned into the room with you.  The guns are mostly okay, though the melee hit detection is pretty janky which makes it annoying to use, which sucks cause it's alt fire is pretty useful. Pistol is the bread and butter but it's alt fire is garbage. 1 Shot to the head kills most humanoids. Shotgun is pretty weak, the spread is huge and even adsing doesnt help nor does shooting 1 barrel at a time. Either the shotgun kills 8 dogs or none. The rifle is pretty useless, doing about a little bit more damage than a shotgun blast? Unsure, as it has no scope but increased zoom but doesn't really matter since the pistol is a sniper anyway. Chaingun is just the chaingun, does the most damage and the game gives you ammo like candy since it's usually the last gun you get for the map. Visuals wise its... okay? The art style is fine by itself but when you pair it with the lighting and the level design it just doesn't work. The lighting is pretty simple too, if its pitch black you're probably not supposed to go that way. Or maybe there's a hidden heart. If it's lit up, you're going the right way. All enemies have lights on them to help you see them against the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ void that is a majority of the game levels.Level design? Needs a couple pass overs. Way to many holes in the geometry that makes you think you can go forward for a secret, knowing its pitch black, yet still hoping maybe they didn't just leave all these 2 foot square boxes behind doors. But they did. Or narrow corridors. Try to do any ledge surfing and you're gonna get gibbed as an anti stuck feature. Cause its easy to get stuck on stuff.Also the animations and enemy designs are really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bland/bad. The regular enemies with swords or guns just contort like the exorcist to point at you. Or they stop moving altogether. Or they spawn in the wall with just their gun sticking out and shooting you. Shoot every enemy in the head/eye/weakspot and you win. Pistol only would be extremely easy, and this is on the hardest difficulty. Which, by the way, does not increase enemy health or damage, just the amounts of enemies and spawning later enemies earlier. Badly designed game all around. The trailers gave me a boomer shooter vibe like Blood but its really not and it almost punishes you for trying to play it like that. You can kind of bhop around most of the melee enemies and zoom through too since as i said enemy damage doesnt seem to scale.Overall game needs a lot more polish/ maybe better trailers to show the game is perhaps meant to be played slower/more methodically considering the speed at which you shoot your guns and swap through the small amount of weapons is very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slow.

_childDocuments_.review: I know it seems unfair to write a review with such a short time in game, but this just disappointed me.First off, the obvious. The game is gorgeous. Like, it's just beautiful. It looks as good in motion as it looks in the screenshots. That's where the positives end though.The devs expected the graphics to carry this game hard, and it just doesn't. I expected a competent modern-old-school FPS a la Dusk or Amid Evil but apparently that bar is way too high.The level design is nowhere as good. There is a lazy marker telling you where to go. Music really don't match the graphic's vibe. The AI is just pathetic.The game is super easy. Most enemies deal 1/4 heart dmg and I had like 8 hearts at the end of the first level. However, the final boss of the first level one shots you. Okay, second try, beat him in less than a minute. It just isn't fun.I really wanted to like this game. I love new old-school type shooters and I love hyper stylized games like this one. It's such a shame that the devs just said "Man, this looks great, why bother making it actually fun."I won't refund though.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: Visual artstyle is interesting, but you are getting used to it after 30 minutes of playing, and then the game starts getting repetitive, boring and clunky.Enemies are running into you like headless dummies, eagles can't be seen in the skies, and bosses are just bullet-sponges for your shotgun. When you are getting the minigun, you just don't need it in the late part of the mission. Interaction with the explosives is clunky, you can't be sure that it will detonate on an impact (instead of unfortunate bouncing). Locations are okay, music is average, system of saving on checkpoints is strange - if you decide to go back, all enemies will be spawned again (though you killed them during your previous life), but the weapon drops are already obtained, so you can't simply go back without loosing all ammo. And you have to release all the hostages one more time (who said it's a good idea?)Poor optimisation on some locations, though I have fine specs. Animations for enemies are done poorly. The same goes about sound - some enemies will be louder than the explosion in front of you, though they are miles away.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so close to being really good, however there are too many glitches that cause you to clip out of the map and then have to wander around until you find a spot where the game recognizes you're out of bounds and kills you.  If you can't do that, you have no choice but to restart the whole level since there's checkpoint loading unless you die and the game only autosaves in between missions.  There are also terrible and constant glitches with enemies being stuck in walls and being able to shoot you but you not being able to shoot them, which is especially obnoxious in the hard difficulty.  It's a shame, because I like the time period, I like the art (mostly, I think shades of black and white instead of strictly black and white and red would make the maps a little more user-friendly), and I like the concept.  I just wish the dev would fix those glitches.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through 5 levels so far, what I assume to be roughly half the game, and I think I've played enough that my opinion will not likely change upon finishing the game.This is just good.  Not amazing/great, but good.  The FPS gunplay is competent.  All the humanoid enemies feel good to kill, the non-humanoids don't feel as good, but they are the minority by far.  Very much reminds me of Painkiller but more stylized and a bit better combat.The art, style, music and resulting atmosphere make the game.  If it wasn't for this, the game would be mediocre at best, and let's be honest, I wouldn't have bought it in the first place and you probably wouldn't be reading reviews for it.  You get what's advertised.To go into more specifics on why the combat isn't great, this game thrives when you're popping headshots with the revolver or rifle.  None of the other weapons feel great.  The shotgun's reload animation makes it feel like you should be able to shoot again before you can, and the chaingun (gatling gun?) is underwhelming.  Therefore when you are facing non-humanoid enemies that you can't headshot as is most easy with the pistol and rifle, combat becomes tedious.  Bosses are visually nice but are a joke in difficulty, in fact the difficulty of the game as a whole is quite low, even on the highest difficulty setting.There are also a few signs that the game is unfinished.  Enemies regularly get stuck in the walls (3 times in the 5 levels I played).  No matter which level I'm on it always shows the secondary objective from The Mansion in the pause screen.  If you change one of the controls and then reload the game (I changed secondary fire because I use a mouse without a middle mouse button), the custom controls won't be in effect until you open the Options menu again (your custom controls show up as you set them, but they won't be in effect until you open this menu again to check).Ultimately I believe the game is worth the price and clearly LOTS of effort was put into it's development.  I get the feeling the developers had a vision, and executed it to the best of their ability.  If they put as much work into the gameplay as they do into the art direction, their next game could be a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: KINGDOM of the DEAD is a pretty average shooter with an excellent atmosphere. The gunplay and level design are pretty average. The game is really straight forward and can be completed it a few sittings (I managed to 100% it in about 5 hours). The music is zany and the color really complements the theme. I recommend it, even if you only play it a few times to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: A game with great style (which is inconsistent in its goals), acceptable substance, but unacceptably buggy gameplay, which is why I refunded it (because numerous times PER LEVEL on the first level, I was getting stuck in level geometry and either having to hope an enemy knocked me back out of it, or restart the level...because no "return to checkpoint" button exists). That's the TL;DR for why this is a game that should be considered in early access, but isn't. Read below for more.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The art style is phenomenal and probably the greatest draw to the game. Enemies, weapons, and environments commit wholesale to this ink-drawn noir style and the only splashes of colour add some much needed visual variety to ensure the style doesn't get stale. Style alone is pretty much why I originally bought this. But in-game, the quality of this style is inconsistent. It's all good, in a vacuum, but smashed together, it doesn't work. The music is great and very stand-out, but it doesn't really fit this kind of game or action at all (veering into synthwave at times which is an odd pick for a gothic noir horror game); the animations are stiff and lacking many keyframes for detail, which would be fine in a lower-poly kind of retro shooter but this one isn't quite low poly enough to make it work; and the aforementioned visual style, whilst great, doesn't match the rest of the package. It's all a bit disjointed.The actual substance - what's on offer, unlocks, progression, so on - is pretty fine. Gunplay is acceptable, though weapon sound effects could be better, and the animation stuff as mentioned previously hampers the "cool factor" of a lot of them. I guess the elephant in the room I should mention is just because this game has a grim style and albeit occasionally freaky encounters with enemies, that doesn't make it a survival horror, and you shouldn't go into this expecting that. It's a boomer shooter with horror elements. I guess if you played on the hardest difficulty (I played on the second hardest) and had awful aim (since most basic enemies die in one headshot) then you'd be strapped for resources, but whilst tense tonally, it's not a survival horror. The only egregious example of a gun I didn't like is the minigun, and not because the manual cycling of it made it fire pretty slowly (which I actually think was really cool), but because the muzzle flash is obnoxiously bright and flashy in an otherwise dark and understated game.Now, the reason I refunded the game - because even with all of the above, this game was still pretty fun - is the bugs. From enemies hitting me through solid objects, enemies walking THROUGH walls, headshots not registering properly, to being hit by an enemy and it pushing me INTO level geometry, making me stuck and hoping he would hit me back out of it again. This last circumstance was not rare - it happened to me three times over the course of my play session, and all three times I eventually just had to restart the level (because there is no "restart from last checkpoint" button despite checkpoints being in every level). I played the same level three times before I gave up because I just kept getting stuck in something new, further along the level each time, and having to replay the same introduction to the game over and over. I could have played and enjoyed the rest of the game just fine if I wasn't constantly being forced to stop playing the game, and with a "restart from checkpoint" button, I probably wouldn't have refunded it either. Overall, the game is fun, but buggy to an unacceptable degree that prevents me being able to recommend it. I can't talk about the depth of the story, or how the gameplay evolves for the better, or anything more detailed than above - because I literally could not progress without having to restart the level over and over because a new corner of geometry decided to ruin my play session. Wait for bug fixing updates that put a special emphasis on not getting you stuck in level geometry every ten minutes.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: I was a big fan of the developer's previous game, Depths of Fear: Knossos, so I was excited to jump into their latest work here. So far, it hasn't disappointed. The art direction is an obvious standout here, and they've managed to create a really compelling atmosphere to play in. It makes for a very cohesive and stylish package, especially alongside the incredible synth-wave soundtrack. The game itself is fairly straightforward shooter fare, but it's executed well. The enemies dismember in satisfying ways, and the levels themselves are expansive and well-realized. I've only played through the first area but it's an astonishingly well put together spooky mansion and courtyard that I enjoyed exploring every corner of.Looking forward to playing through the rest of this, and highly recommend it based on my experience thus far. My only real complaint is the lack of Controller Support because I'm a stickler for playing games on the couch, but it hasn't been too tricky to bind functionality with Steam Input. Just expect the game to show controller players little mercy since it seemingly wasn't designed with that in mind.
