_childDocuments_.review: while visually great and having a fun premise, I just... couldn't get into this kind of game. the AI are just rush-down or ranged enemies. if they are rush-down, they obviously run right at you. however, they have no unique mechanics to them besides how they come at you (minus the Harpies, who just... fly with strafing runs). the ranged enemies are all the same though, where they walk up to their minimum range requirement (they only move closer if their AI says "you're out of range"), stand still, then take potshots at you. each of these groups are only distinguished by their health pool and their slight visual differences.the maps look good though, but can be a bit iffy with the weapon placements. and said weapons are... sorta underwhelming. the pistol is what you will mainly rely on, cause it's the starting weapon + the unlimited uses sword. the shotgun is what you will then rely on to kill bosses, as it *can* shred if every pellet lands. the rifle is... just a longer pistol. the minigun is a minigun, and it comes in a bit late from what I can tell for most missions. then you have the TNT. it's your grenade.overall, I wouldn't say it's a bad game, however... I personally don't care for it. it's a speedrunner's wet dream, and I much prefer to take my time blasting the little blighters as they come. which is... near impossible in the higher difficulties unless you're fine with dying a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a good FPS with unique graphic style that I loved. I liked that there were many art styles to choose from so anyone can pick their favorite. This game also has good feeling guns that all pack a punch and are pleasure to use. I liked also how the levels are build as they are logical in their layout so you don’t need any map and I like that there is a secondary objective to do and civilians to be rescued. The banter between you and your living sword at the start of each mission is also a nice touch.The synthwave music in this game is great and it fits to the world presented and gives you an eerie feeling that there is danger around every corner. And while music makes you want to run and gun you really need to move cautiously and slowly to be sure to pick your fights and fight enemies in advantageous positions to not get surrounded. I liked that the difficulty levels don’t give monsters more HP but instead they make monsters deal more damage and also higher difficulty forces you to complete the secondary objective and to never let a civilian die or you will fail the level. It makes the game harder but still fair and your guns still feel like real guns not some peashooters. I hate it when games thinks that harder level just means inflating monsters HP as that is just lazy design. The enemies that attack in melee have big problems with pathfinding if you are somewhere higher than the same ground level they spawned on. Also the collision system is not great as sometimes you can basically stand on a table and shoot the enemies while they don’t know how to get to you so they are just standing there looking at you while at other times they have no problems getting to you and climb on the table or anything. Also melee enemies sometimes clip thru the terrain when they run at you and I had also some range enemies stuck in the wall and shoot at me while I was not able to shoot back as my bullets were hitting the wall. Sometimes I even saw melee enemies running past me while they head and eyes were fixated on me and it was funny to see their head move around to see me all the time while their body was running away to a location where I was before.If you die you continue from a save point and while you keep all the hearths you did find and the rescued civilians and picked up weapons you lose almost all the ammo you picked up and if you try to backtrack from a checkpoint you will find the ammo in the same places like you did before but also all enemies respawns so checkpoints are not really helpful and they seem to work more like just spawning the player into a new level filled with enemies and items but with some basic amount of ammo and in the checkpoint place instead of the start of the level. This is a good FPS with many flaws that keep it away from being great. A little more work and this game would be great.Overall score 5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: What I'm about to say may be controversial, but perhaps you should view this game as a kind of speedrunning training...?Don't get me wrong: it's a fine descendant of Quake with a monochrome style (which actually hurts it in some regards, even though the aesthetic is cool), and you're supposed to be doing headshots for ammo conservation and swapping weapons according to the type of enemies in front of you, BUT, besides of the interesting setpieces on each level, the most effective strategy is either to fall back on every encounter for maximum safety and cover opportunities without getting mobbed or to instead dash like a maniac and take very precise specific shots here and there to clear the way as fast as possible until you reach the next checkpoint (where you will respawn with minimal ammo but avoid a bunch of encounters this way).The music is decent, the achievements are kinda buggy, and I swear over my own life that the only pumpkin available to smash for the achievement is a single prop (quite visible) at the beginning of the Tower mission; everything that's not a headshot is mildly effective at best and the balance seems to be most leaning towards learning each encounter rather than being adaptable on the hardest difficulty.Speaking of, the last level is quite a spike in difficulty due to ammo scarcity and tougher enemy concentration on terrain where you can fall to your death. The final final boss you have infinite ammo but you're not supposed to be taking hits or you'll miss the Sunrise achievement, and I would be pissed if I had to go through that level again just for 100% completion to be honest.But, if you want, you can just do the side / meaningless arena mode. You basically get a single life and a castle terrain to fight in, where enemies start spawning at increased rates and harder kinds the more you kill them. That definitely has some replay value if you're the kind of score-hunter with proficiency in older arena shooters, even if (to my knowledge) there's no unlockables for any placement (and thank you for not putting a leaderboard, I'd have hated that myself).I do recommend Kingdom of the Dead. It's an interesting time. Tells a small story in several setpieces and has the right vibe for what it was trying to accomplish. Makes you wish more things could be simpler like this game.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most fun FPS I have played in some time. It is heavily Golden Eye inspired with age/secret agent/00 agent difficulties and the level is a grid of files that all have a theme. The levels are all totally unique from one another fun (train, farm, frontline, mansion, etc. etc), they for the most part have unique bosses and mechanics. The shooting is simple, but in a way that just works. You point at the head, you get a head shot, satisfying plunk. Many of the enemies move slow, so the challenge is doing it in quick succession which is just utterly satisfying. All of the weapons are great except the sword, which basically fulfills the function of a slap and is not meant to be super powerful like melee weapons in Hexen. The biggest draw of the game is art style and music, but honestly these speak for themselves-- the quality seen in the screenshots is maintained throughout, and feels like a style rather than a gimmick. The red blood splashes against the black and white is just excellent. The soundtrack is extensive and so so good, perfectly fits the vibe.The most unexpectedly cool part is the writing. Though the dialogue and story at limited, they are really well done and set up a really compelling Vampire Hunter D style relationship between hunter and weapon. The people who wrote "high on life" could learn a lot about brevity and wit from this indie title. Overall I can't recommend this game enough, definitely makes my 2022 top 5. I am jaded and play a lot of indie FPS games, but this one keeps bringing me back in a way few have in recent memory. I think I even prefer this game to Cultic, although it is more slow paced and stilted.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool! So far I've beaten one of the areas, and the art is one of a kind, and doesn't hinder the blood or anything like that. Very satisfying to kill the demons. Gun play is great. Feels smooth to move around. Has some difficulty with the bosses, but beatable after some attempts lol. I recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: So, my playtime represents a full playthrough of the game.And that's because the presentation of Kingdom Of The Dead is wildly different from the mechanics of Kingdom Of The Dead.It looks like an atmospheric Betrayer-style fps where the pacing is slow and deliberate and you're meant to drink in the vibes. The art assets, music, and individual enemy encounters are all built around this sort of approach, and if you play this way you will have a really bad time.The correct way to play Kingdom is to skip all fights, speedrun, only shoot when you have to, and fly through the levels at maximum speed. The actual mechanics of the game are built around you doing this. Kingdom is a survival sprinter, and it fails at telling you this.To be fair, even when you're playing correctly, there's a *lot* of jank. You get stuck on enemies and the environment really easily. There's a persistent bug that can happen in any cutscene where you start autofiring all of your weapons and can never stop. Bosses nearly all have instakills, and these come out fast and have hitboxes the size of the moon. Also the last two boss fights are some of the most unengaging non-encounters I've seen in an fps.However, Kingdom gets pretty close to a good game at points, and I hope we'll get more from the developer.The art and overall style of Kingdom are excellent, and it just needs to make up its mind a little more clearly about how you're incentivized to play to be a genuinely good, easy to recommend experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks great, but that's it.  It runs like diarrhea; dropping frames like a greased up photographer.  The enemies don't really telegraph when they're being hit or showing up.  The sounds only sometimes work.  It's laggy as all hell.  Somebody gave up on this game long before finishing it.  That person was also me, but mostly it was those that made the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was definitely a fun experience and I'd recommend it. Core game play is a soft-narrative FPS, where you play as an agent whose trying to stop a war with the undead. You chose your path from an office hub, where you can practice combat or select the story missions from dossiers Ala Goldeneye. Great art style, cool level design and themes. Story isn't anything deep but is as entertaining as it needs to be. Soundtrack is pretty decent too  - although one or two songs don't quite fit what I'd consider to be the vibe. Guns all handle well and feel solid. Bosses are awesome to behold, and at times the art style really shines. I have an enormous amount of respect for a team that makes something this stylistic and sticks to it, and I'd like to see some more content for this if I'm being honest.Game is not without its flaws, however. Some levels have dead zones where I had to restart. I had serious difficulty remapping keys and had to play with the default binds. Sometimes the stat tracking at the end of levels was off, saying I'd died when I hadn't - or in one instance an objective failed even though I completed it.  While the game offers several difficulty levels, I was able to complete them on the hardest without much of a challenge, and I feel that the difficulty system in general could use a revision - for example turn off hostage icons at harder difficulties. This feels like a polished late stage project, but with a little bit of refinement and I daresay another ~5 levels from a DLC / patch it would absolutely be worth the asking price point. My suggestion is get it on sale. 5$ is a steal - but don't hesitate to support the devs here as they clearly care about it.Ii your interested on the visuals alone it's worth the play. I 100%'d this without any guide in about 10 hours time.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so absolutely broken, unfinished and artistically bankrupt I fail to find any points of praise, even looking at the other reviews they seem like a stretch. This game is worth like, 3 bucks at best, honestly. Maybe. If you're feeling generous.The weapon switching is completely broken. I've reached the end of a level only to find out because I was quick swapping the game somehow deleted my melee weapon from my inventory. So I couldn't end the level. And I couldn't kill myself because I didn't have enough self damage. And there's no retry from a checkpoint button. So I was just softlocked, either restart the entire level or quit outright.The bosses are recycled over and over are die pathetically easily, even on the harder difficulties. Not that you'd want to fight them for very long since their movesets are not very interesting in the first place.The style makes the game kind of hard to look at and it's definitely a style over substance kind of deal. The enemies are all fairly uninspired in look and move in a super janky way. Also, the AI in general is not the smartest.The music... . God, I hope it's from some stock library for free, because the music is honestly actively terrible.So no, I can't recommend this game. Especially with this price tag and in this current state. But even if the devs actually care about this and fix the bugs, the game has a lot of inherent problems that just make it an uninteresting slog.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, get it on sale.  It isn't bad, just mediocre. I would say a 6.5 out of ten. Here are my thoughts:The game's ok. It has an excellent art style. Honestly pretty fun gameplay although the AI isn't much to boast about. Good response mechanics. Weapons feel very powerful.However, the game has multiple issues:- gets repetitive fast. Really fast. Maybe I just don't like boomer shooters enough or something because I only played for half an hour. This is likely the most subjective of my critiques.- music sucks. The music absolutely ruins the experience, honestly. It's really grating on the ears, and it repeats endlessly. It doesn't even fit the vibe of the game AT ALL. Turn off the music if you want to enjoy the game.- BS enemies. Eagles come out of nowhere and you can't really see them very well, for example. Luckily enemies are completely brain dead, as you would expect from zombies. What this means is bad AI.- why is there fall damage in a boomer shooter lmao- why is the first boss of the game capable of one-shotting the player? In fact, if it ever lands any attack on the player, you die.- why does dying take away ammunition that the player has collected throughout the level?

_childDocuments_.review: Late to the party on this review. Very nice little game, this one. Playing all the stages on the hardest difficulties is really the way to go. Tons of baddies to kill, fun story to go through, some awesome giant setpieces (seriously the train and ship levels are great), and some really, REALLY good music on top of everything. _childDocuments_.review: One of the slickest nicest indie fps games I've played since DUSK, great art design combined with fun levels a simple but fun story and world, good game play and an grand ending  that really feels earned. It is an easy recommendation from me. And the way I started the game a little unsure of the rhythm of combat and the progression to being able to beat some levels with just the sword was fantastic. I felt like a monster hunter by the end and would love to revisit this game and world in more games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: The gunplay is great, which really carries the game, even moreso than the art style. I would imagine that the art style would turn some people off, but I really enjoyed it. It almost gives it a static feel when you're running, kind of like you're watching a B movie on an old fuzzy tube TV. The music ranges from OK to pretty good, but a lot of it doesn't seem to fit the tone very well. Lots of little bits of jank here and there, like "dropping" in to the office at the end of the level, weird/bad enemy AI and pathing, enemies getting stuck in walls, an iffy ammo pickup animation, etc. Really liked the look and characterization of the bosses.Get it on sale, and you'll likely enjoy yourself for an afternoon or two.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: Mechanically not deep enough for what it wants to be. The enemy designs make sense, but in execution very basic AI makes them feel very bland. The selection of weapons makes sense (melee sword, allrounder pistol, close quarters shotgun, long range rifle, does-it-all minigun), but it feels to unsatisfying and enemies are too basic to really encourage situational awareness of when which weapon would be best. Sword has a charge mechanic for an AoE attack, again cool concept but not that satisfying to use especially against this bland enemy design. The lever action rifle is redundant with the pistol aswell, as both are 100% accurate and most common enemies die with headshots from both. Overall every mission has the same pacing of the same weapons with about the same enemies, so it gets redundant quick and it's not satisfying enough to keep me engaged.The artstyle is unique and the dialogue + it's sound design give it a cool vibe, but I don't feel it's enough to elevate the base game behind it.Would recommend if it was really cheap, but it's a letdown for 15€.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: Game has an interesting visual style but can be buggy, if you enjoy 100% any games there are a few frustrating one even in less then 2 hours of gameplay...-enemies stuck inside wall (note that this bug is consistant so if you replay the level they'll remain at the same position)- level isn't counted as cleared in level selection. (Don't know if this one's consistant tho but it happened twice to me so i gave up clearing the whole game...)-Completing  then starting it again on high difficulty, getting the first checkpoint and quit somehow unlock the [Level completed in high dif] achievement...Those aren't bug but weird design choice :Most levels are already unlocked.Starting another level clear your inventory so you start with a revolver only each times.Dying mean you lose all your ammo. (so good luck for boss fight :))The IA on this game are a bit too predictable, you can shoot them once so they stop and headshot them... it feels way too slow and even on zone with a few more enemies they're easily defeated...Overall the game's art style is alright but sadly fell flat when it come to gameplay execution...
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: An FPS with a cool black and white art style where you fight legions of the undead. So my immediate problem is that the levels are checkpointed, but if I quit the game and come back I have to start the level completely over. These levels are not short. Apart from that the gameplay is okay. I like the art style and the music, but the gameplay feels so-so. Also the stutters every time I fire a gun. _childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: Core game is good. I really liked the art style, it was interesting. Gameplay was satisfying, albeit a tad easy. Level design was okay, the levels looked cool but they were usually fairly basic. The big issue with the game is the bugs. Game tends to bug out for me, enemies would often glitch into walls, I would get stuck etc. Achievements don't work properly, they are very bugged out and don't unlock when they should or when you should unlock one achievement you will instead unlock a random different one. These wouldn't be too big an issue if the dev fixed them. Game seems like it might be semi-abandoned, there was a patch a few weeks ago but it didn't seem to fix any bugs just add an endless mode I haven't tried and added achievements that don't work right. That's why I am ultimately not recommending it, the bugs that prolly won't get fixed. If the dev patches the bugs, fixes them etc I will come back and change my rating to yes. If not for the bugs the core game is pretty decent, and if you aren't worried about bugs it's still worth checking out.Update 1:I finished the game and pretty much everything I said stands. I do want to clarify on the level design, artistically the levels were beautiful and they played fine they just felt kind of basic. Usually there was a fairly linear level structure. I will say though that the levels get more interesting in the second half.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, I love the art style, a lot to look at. For a game you would think to take slow and drink in the atmosphere, you can go surprisingly fast if you want more of a classic shooter speed. I think the music is fantastic, but the synth sounds strangely out of place with the theme and vibe of the game? It's great anyway, definitely worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: KINGDOM of the DEAD

_childDocuments_.review: A absolute masterpiece of the old 90s shooter genre (AKA Serious Sam, Painkiller, Duke Nuke'em). Music is great, visuals are awesome since they recapture the era this type of game was made in, and the gameplay is amazingly fun. There is enough story to keep you interested, but not enough to be distracting from the exceptional gameplay. Playable slow and steady or able to be played like a speedrunner's dream. I loved the jumping/movement system in this game. Following the genre it was built for, the game has bunnyhopping, momentum, and the movement itself is smooth and fluid. Now to the 3 things I disliked, or could have been done better about this game, keeping in mind that none of the 3 of these "greivances" even slightly made me consider not recommending this game, just some flaws to be shared so you know what you are buying. #1: My playtime is me playing the entire game on the 2 star difficulty slow and steady, and then going back and basically speedrunning the 3 star difficulty of the entire game. So thusly the game is quite short. Though at $15 full price, nevermind a sale on this game, it was more than enough to satisfy my purchase. #2: The game could of used a gamma setting inside of the options. I had to use a third party program to change my gamma (I.E. Nvidia Graphics Settings, Gamma Panel, etc.) which was slightly inconveniencing, but not a game changer, for sure. and lastly #3: The game had slight fit and finish issues with clear holes in certain walls, floors, ceiliings, etc. that allowed you to see outside of the play area. Now keep in mind I never saw (save for literally a single spot, and I was able to wiggle myself out of it) a place where these holes allowed you to exit the level either to look at the level from underneath or outside of it, or to accidentally get stuck or die. Along a similar line, there is no glaring issues with level design that can be easily exploited to gain an advantage over the enemy or to circumvent parts of a level, save for ONE level, which I will not say here, as to not spread it's usage to others so that they may ruin the experience for themselves by using it. There is one last thing I want to say, there is a extra secret which I have been unable to unlock as of yet, having played the game basically 2 times through. I was slightly disappointed that I could not find whatever/wherever the secret was (which is all I'll say about it as to avoid giving away unnecessary details about the game that could spoil something) but am certain that I will find it eventually.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. Finished all levels on hard. 3/5+ great artstyle and theme+ gunplay is satisfying+ level design is pretty nice, reminds me of a few zombie escape maps from Counter Strike Zombie mod for some reason+ simple and fun, no unnecessary filler- technical issues (frame drops when looking - could really use some voice acting to bring forth the charm even more- soundtrack is spooky fun, but overall it's kind of underwhelming for a game dripping with visual style- despite some bosses killing you in 1 hit, their fights are too easy overall when compared to the rest of the level.Overall thoughts: it's a classic shooter with a really cool coat of paint and nice atmosphere, and a clear direction. I wonder what we would get if there was more budget to it! Felt like an alternative take on Painkiller (and perhaps Darkwatch as well but I haven't played that yet). With that said, it might feel odd for some players. Movement is super snappy and fast, but the guns don't really match it, which translates into a more tactical approach towards combat but enough speed to dodge projectiles and run away to a better position if push comes to shove.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I've played the psychological horror game, Mundaun, I've been obsessed with finding games that provide that distinct pencil-drawn black and white look and feel. And I'm glad to say that Kingdom of the Dead provides that in spades!! A dark-tone premise that doesn't take itself too seriously. Enemies variations suffice to keep you on your toes and offers that DOOM DANCE of gunning down everything with fast paced intensity complimented with the FANTASTIC choice of eerie goth music - it gets my heart racing!! I will admit that I did suffer from frame rate drops whenever I reach an area with TONS of enemies on the screen  (perhaps because I'm playing on a GEFORCE GTX 960m/ 16 GB RAM/ Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-6700HQ CPU @ 2.60GHz which is not enough to run this game properly). Nevertheless, it's still a phenomenal game that I hope many will try out and support.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom of the Dead is a neat game but I wish there was more to it. To start off with the positives, the art style, vibe, setting, and music are all fantastic. I love everything about the atmosphere it creates and the levels themselves are well designed. However the game is sadly rather simple and shallow with every level being full of the same enemies giving you the same weapons and same objectives over and over. There's always a few civilians to rescue, one thing to find in the environment, and that's it. Also the combat, while not terrible, feels a bit stiff and clunky. I also wish there was more story as you played through the levels, even dialog with your sword about what's going on while you fought would have added a lot to the game.You can easily see everything the game offers in under three hours. There are three difficulties for each of the missions but anyone who has played an FPS before will breeze through the first two. There's a bizarrely large gap between "normal" and "hard" but hey, difficulty is subjective so I can't fault the game too much for that. Also as of now there are some bugs in the game but no deal breakers, just mostly areas where you can see through the map and places you can get stuck if you go off course.Also PRO TIP: the game never tells you this but most of the weapons (including the sword) have an alt-fire that's bound to the middle mouse button. You NEED to know this for a certain point in the game but the mechanic is literally never explained. This is an oversight that needs fixing, especially it's something you could have been utilizing up until it was required.tl;dr: good game with some problems and a bit of a missed opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Rocks with a beautiful art-style that's reminiscent of Madworld, with extremely simplistic Doom style gameplay that's accompanied with an eccentric soundtrack.Thoroughly enjoyed the first level, it was a fantastic introduction to the game. The Clock tower is also a favourite of mine and the second half of the ship level was difficult, but awesome. The rest of the levels were okay; some of them felt slightly empty, short, unfinished and too easy at times and there's not a whole lot of interactivity also. The format and level design felt mostly primitive, but I think they were well set up, considering this game is stylised in this Retro manner.A few accumulative issues I experienced were far and few between, but I wouldn't consider ignoring them whenever they occur - The game is moderately buggy; clipped through a locked gate during a boss fight, enemies can clip through the ground and walls, sometimes they can even shoot through said walls, level assets not saving after loading checkpoints, etc. I'm not sure, but I think there were a few grammatical errors too, I could be wrong. And the first half of the last level was easily the worst part of the game in terms of cheapness. In contrast, some levels and bosses are a breeze, even in three star difficulty. The final part of the game was also kind of disappointing, much like the other game DEADBOLT, the endgame felt quite rushed. The animations for some enemies and weapons could use some polish, since they felt kinda janky.As I mentioned at the beginning - A number of issues are holding this game back from being absolutely great, but I think it's possible that all of them can be fixed. Even without the potential fixes, this game is still a worthy Game of the Year candidate, at least as far as indie first person shooters go.

_childDocuments_.review: kingdom of the dead is a bit janky but ive had a good time with it, i think its worth playing for the artstyle and atmosphere alone, if you like how it looks. enemy ai really isnt anything to write home about. i like how the guns feel and the combination of how the blood stains the monochromatic environment combined with the headshot plonk sound is just addicting to me.i havent had any game breaking/major issues so far, just minor ones such as enemies ocassionally spawning trapped inside walls for example. and for some reason keybinds seem to reset whenever ive closed and reopned the game, even though they still appear to be bound how i rebound them in the settings, not the end of the world or anything just a minor inconvenience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ahh man this game really has me conflicted. That art style is absolutely downright beautiful, and the ability to change the color scheme whenever is also a really neat addition. The guns all feel super good, especially the revolver in my opinion. The enemy design is also a really high note, as they are pretty unique and interesting looking, especially the bosses. But oh man that AI is very very bad. They as many have mentioned, just walk at a straight line towards you, even the ranged enemies typically just stand in place waiting to be head shotted. Another real downside is the bosses. Despite the variety and unique look, these encounters are also mindless, just around and blast them 3-4 times with dynamite or the rifle and you win. Even the end game bosses are a complete joke. Lastly the sound design could use a bit more work for future games. Directional audio really isn't much a thing here, the general sounds of levels are oddly loud and go on far to long, and the music is extremely loud unless turned down from default by a substantial margin. I also encountered a few times were enemies were just caught in walls blasting away at you, but you can brush that off as damage isn't really an issue here. This is a game where I really really want to like it, I think we need more games in this genre that push the visual style out of the comfort zone of "hell" or hell inspired. But to enjoy this and be satisfied you REALLY need to get this one on a discount. $15 is far to much of an asking price for what you get here. The potential is here, lets just hope some of its major downfalls are addressed if the devs decide to move forward with another game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sick. _childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game however it is quite short, quite easy, and therefore quite overpriced @ $15. You can get it to the end without rushing in about 4 hours. The biggest thing it's got going is its great visual style. However, it's somewhat unfortunate that the game is just a braindead shooter. Even though it works for a braindead shooter, I would much rather see it for a full on horror game. I wouldn't say it's entirely wasted - the game is creepier because of it and still fun regardless, but once you realize that this isn't a horror game (let alone a survival horror game like the tags say) and that it's just a shooter, it's a little disappointing. There's little to the AI, the higher difficulties aren't really 'harder', the boss fights are easy, but it really does look cool. If I wasn't enjoying myself through all of that I definitely would've refunded since I bought it on sale @ $10 ish.I guess just watch some gameplay, be aware it's short, and then wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: So.very.creative.I bought it within 5 minutes of having seen some fragmentary gameplay, and it only took me literal seconds to fall in love with the visual style and presentation on display. I'm extremely impressed with this perfect blend of trippy surrealism, horror, and adventuring—it sucks you right into the world and resonated very strongly with me.There's so much to enjoy with all the little details, the paintings hung around the world in the early game are a fantastic touch. The crypt was spooky, and I especially loved the larger areas, like the theater, the outdoor scenes, oh boy the forest level, and the frontline. The death screen is also really creative.Music is on point and not afraid to be varied and explore different tones, the lack blending (fading in/out) between the tracks or when the same track looped felt a bit jarring. Sound design in general I found pleasing and atmospheric, there are a few cases where there's some discomfort, like the footsteps of the glaive enemy with the helmet and one broken horn.Animation could use a bit of polish, but it doesn't detract from my enjoyment at all, and to a degree actually fits with the overall tone and look of the game. Doesn't feel too out of place.Movement feels great and handles smoothly.The filters are very appreciated feature. It would be fantastic to have a little bit more custom control over them, to tweak them further to the player's taste (would also help if the menu was a little bit less in the middle of the screen, so you can see the adjustment/preview better).The way save points are actual objects/locations to find, guns needing to be discovered, and by having secondary/bonus objectives, you've done a lot to incentivise exploration and add variety to the run and gun gameplay.Thorougly enjoyed my first fully completed run, and while I'm not usually one to replay, I'm looking forward to replaying them all on the other difficulties.Thank you for pouring your heart and soul into this, it shows.Please make more, you have a new fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Gorgeous aesthetic, unique for the genre and largely well executed (particularly in regards to the environments) Solid basic retro fps gameplay loopGood gunplay, enjoyable arsenal of ye olde boomsticksGreat soundtrack that's also pretty uniqueCool boss designsIntriguing atmosphereTwin Peaks referenceCons:Performance issues Janky character models that need a lot of polish, often moving in jarring ways and not feeling very responsive when shotSimplistic AI that basically only knows how to walk in a straight line at you, basic path-finding that gets stuck fairly oftenAwful sound-mixing, uneven volume and poor directional soundEnemies and breakables consistently spawning outside the world or in walls and sometimes still being able to shoot you from thereEnemy attacks could use more variety as currently they all either walk at you and deal melee damage, fire orbs at you or shoot youBasic lack of polish (getting stuck on the environment, various bugs, bosses phasing through the environment, parts of levels too dark to comfortably navigate, boss dying but the fight not actually ending hardlocking the game, movements a little floaty)The outline of a truly excellent boomer shooter is here but it's simply not finished. It's a shame because if this was in early access I'd be willing to give it the benefit of the doubt, but they shouldn't be selling this as a finished game in the state it's in now. Hopefully the developer is able to polish it up in the coming months, perhaps even hire a team to help with some of the proceeds. This is a truly unique experience: a brilliant setting with heaps of atmosphere that deserves to be done justice. I'm rooting for them.

_childDocuments_.review: The elements of this game are so familiar, so over-used, that within a few minutes of the opening scene we can predict with certainty almost everything that will happen.A professor turned General is part of an elite organization tasked with preventing an army of the undead from taking over the world with its vast monstrous horde. The General, it seems, has had a troubled past, haunted by encounters that have left him questioning the process of taking and giving life.After many battles, he comes back to his hometown and settles into the family home where he takes time to reflect. After a while, he will be summoned once more to face the demons of his past that are now wreaking havoc upon the land. By the game’s end, he will try to prevent it and in the process, attempt to justify the non-stop killing again. Welcome to the Kingdom of the Undead., by developer , takes you back to the glory days of  and  as it grabs you from the top, engulfs you, and shakes you to your very core. There are glimmers of a brooding terror and epic scattering of blood throughout the game, particularly since it is designed in a matte-stencil-painting backdrop that gives off an eerie vibe. The opening scenes, for example, create a dark and foreboding place making every level feel claustrophobic and sinister.If you’ve played any first-person shooters from the last decade or so, you’ll know exactly what to expect as you venture past a massive gate leading to a number of strange but well-designed areas. Naturally, each level is packed full of groaning and grotesque monsters that drag themselves from the ground and come charging at you from places of darkness.Like Doom,  offers many ways in which you can die. You can run screaming through a corridor with hundreds of demented monks chasing you or you scurry up a steep embankment only to be taken down by something that looks like a giant eyeball tossing giant fireballs at you in an attempt to smear your flesh to the ground. Conversely, a pitch-black room might seem like a good place to hide but an ominous giant bat will tell you otherwise.The weapon assortment consists of the usual ones you would normally find in games of this nature. You have the shotgun, the single barrel revolver, some dynamite, and the almighty sword you can go with when you run out of ammunition.And just like first-person shooters of years past,  is not restricted to range or angle, meaning you can be shot, pulverized, and brought down from miles away either from above or below. So it’s important to always scour your surrounding and to constantly be on the move.As the title so implies, the game features a mass of wholesale blood-letting with indefinable brain matter splattered across tombstones. Unlike the imps from , however, the monsters here are a lot more temperamental and display some advanced AI. They’re clever and won’t just wander into the sites of your shotgun.But my biggest nitpick with the game is that it has too much darkness. I know the design of the game is intentional, but I’ve spent way too much time stumbling around and back-peddling in pitch dark rooms; heck, even the outdoor scenes felt like I was inside a cave.There are just too many dark areas to navigate and when you’re tossed in a maze-like labyrinth and have enemies shooting at you with accurate precision and you can’t see them, minutes literally turn into hours.Even with these nitpicks, they weren’t enough to ruin my experiences with the game. At its core, Kingdom of the Dead is the equivalent of Doom, Night of the Living Dead, and Outlaws all mashed up brilliantly together, and is a proper example of a good game designed with limited resources. There are no fancy 3D effects or embarrassing voice actors, instead, the technical aspects presented are professionally done. To be clear, the overpowering element of this game isn’t just in its gameplay, but in its atmosphere.Overall, I was never bored or frustrated enough that I didn’t want to keep playing. Even if I had to restart a level, I was very much willing to do so just to keep the story moving along. Essentially,  is an evolution of the old first-person shooter that does not require a hefty PC to keep things entertaining. If you’re in the market to try a game that tests your reflexes rather than your wits, you should definitely give this one a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Hand Drawn for me and you! Dead, however, need not apply!When people think of Boom-Shoots, the 2D sprites of Doom or the Low-Poly Models of Quake come to mind. Many other shooters will happily serve that aesthetic up on a silver platter so it’s always charming to see one break that mold with its own touch of creativity! Kingdom of the Dead is more than happy to delve into the pulpy aesthetics of 50’s pulp magazines and gnarly graphic novels of the 90’s by mimicking a hand-drawn art style that genuinely works for the most part!KotD thrusts you into the roomy Trench coat and brooding Stetson hat of Agent Chamberlain, a Gatekeeper by trade whose job is to keep the Dead out of the affairs of the living with the help of his trusty talking sword. Right off the bat I was getting Nocturne vibes with the time period and overall story and while it doesn’t go flavor text up until the end, I was surprised by the actual writing chops on display, with bosses being astonishingly memorable even if they have about two or three lines and even an ending that kind of surprised me with the twist it took D:Gameplay wise, it’s a run n’ gun Shoot em’ up with a heavy focus on movement and agile navigation, swapping weapons to pound the dead back into the dirt with precision aiming and even dishing out a sword that can be charged for a devastating attack! Most of the time it felt pretty damn easy even on harder difficulties but I assume it’s to do with my precision as I reckon those who cannot get a hang of headshots would be in for a rough time.Levels are also large and well-crafted with boss arena’s that offer a ton of movement and attack opportunities and by and large, the designs of the bosses and their domains themselves are absolutely RAD.Despite that, it’s just… too easy!Bosses can go down in less than a minute if you know what you are doing with some weapons able to take a quarter of their health down in one blow while I found enemies in their large numbers more cumbersome when they box you in.Speaking of which, their animations leave much to be desired, as most of the time that is where my immersion broke away from the pulpy hand-drawn aesthetic when clumsy flailing and walking animations interrupted the mood. Weapons feel the same, with the shotgun firing almost too quickly with an animation that I swear is skipping frames.On the few times I died, I also noticed my ammo was not resupplied, which is especially infuriating when I lose hundreds of rounds to a monster spam but I assume it gave me the difficulty I so desired LOL.That being said, KotD is still a fun little romp and well worth the time investment, not to mention the music is pretty killer and fits the tone to a tee.Remember to quench the thirst of your Sword, Gatekeeper. Seriously, its secondary attack is OP as hell! ;D

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do, but the lack of a sprint-jump function means you can't make an integral leap in the very first level in order to complete a side objective. Now, side stuff is disabled on the lowest difficulty, meaning you can technically progress without finding all the collectibles but the lowest difficulty is far too easy to be enjoyable. Since the game is fairly obscure there are next to no "let's play" videos on the web, and nearly all of them skip the side stuff, so it took me forever to find one that covered the issue I was having. In the video the dude practically launches himself across the gap and I cannot for the life of me figure out how he did it other than conclude it's because it was an earlier build of the game, and sprinting was later removed without thought of how it would affect the ability to 100% the game.Since there is no way to save your progress during a level it means I had to replay the whole thing over and over to get back to that spot and try to figure out what I was doing wrong. It doesn't help that the music in the first mission is terrible and completely breaks the immersion.I'm sure there's a way to crack open an .ini file in the game's system folder and adjust some numbers to give myself the ability to run and jump without cancelling all my momentum, but I bought a game, not a hobby. Which is a shame because the art style on display and storytelling delivery here is a real treat, the actual shooting is a lot of fun and rewards precision skill and accuracy which is always welcome in an FPS.No help in the forums, so I'm hoping maybe a negative review will get the attention of the developers, though I'm not going to hold my breath as the game appears to be abandoned.

_childDocuments_.review: Watch My Full Gameplay Walkthrough here - Overall Score - 7/10Pros ---                                                                                  Smooth Responsive Control                                                     Great Artstyle Perfectly Creepy Environement Cons ---Basically another Doom like Overview ------It is clear Kingdom of the Dead heavily takes inspiration from the original Doom. There is a story, but like the more simple games of times past, it is more of a backdrop to the game rather than the driving force behind it. The player assumes the role of Agent Chamberlain, a mysterious figure working for a secret government program known only as GATEKEEPER. As Chamberlain, the player’s primary goal is to defeat Death and his armies.While the story is not the main focus, it does a great job of tying the gameplay, supernatural elements, and art style into a genuinely creepy package from start to finish. Kingdom of the Dead sports a black and white hand-drawn, ink-and-paper art style with splashes of colour to accentuate key aspects during the game; such as blood. The result seems to jump off the screen, and instead of feeling cheap or lazy like a lot of other Doom-style clones tend to; it instead looks dramatic, stylish and utterly terrifying while also still holding on to that old-school Cathode-ray Tube (CRT) monitor magic.The gameplay is pretty simple in Kingdom of the Dead. There are nine different locations to play through, each with multiple difficulty levels and goals to achieve. The available difficulty options are honestly appreciated, as it allows anyone to enjoy the game at a challenge level suited to them – and not just exclusive to people with the reflexes of The Flash. The difficulty also increases naturally as one progresses through the levels. Better still, the gradual way this is implemented means that before the change is noticed players will have already adapted to it. The controls are surprisingly responsive and smooth too, making for an old-school experience that feels very much inline with modern mechanics and flow.While many first-person shooters have a way of becoming almost instantly frustrating to those not skilled at them, Kingdom of the Dead never falls into this trap. With save points scattered throughout the levels and no real punishment for dying, the game maintains its adrenaline fuelled momentum, regardless of skill level, and never fails to be entertaining.There are very few ways to take a 90s style Doom clone and manage to make it feel different and new; yet somehow, Kingdom of the Dead manages to pull it off perfectly. There are eight different weapons to pick up throughout the levels and over twenty-two different enemies and old school bosses to fight. At its core, Kingdom of the Dead is a game many have seen hundreds of times over. However, the dark Lovecraftian horror themes are atmospheric and bold and, together with the game’s survival aspects, make it all feel new and fresh – even despite its nostalgic origins.In the same way some people have comfort foods or blankets, others have comfort games. For many, those are the games that make them nostalgic for their childhoods and a time in their lives when they first fell in love with the interactive art form of gaming. In this sense, while not standing up to the games of 2022 graphically, the original Doom games continue to remain prominent and comfortable, which is also the perfect way to describe Kingdom of the Dead. Thinking back on my childhood, there are vivid memories of sitting on my mother’s lap while she would play Doom, and just being able to feel the pure enjoyment she received from it. Booting up Kingdom of the Dead now, almost thirty years later, those emotions and feelings came rushing back. Even though Kingdom of the Dead is its own game in its own right, there was something about it that instantly connected me to the woman whose lap I once sat upon so many years ago.Context -----Over the years, many have tried to work out what exactly it is that makes games successful. Is it the art, music, mechanics, or a combination of all three? Although a definitive answer remains elusive, what is known is how games continue to stay with us, and the titles often remembered are not always the ones to win awards. Rather, they are often the kinds of games that reach into our souls and ignite an unforeseen passion. Kingdom of the Dead is a loving and thoughtful successor to a much-beloved series that birthed an entire genre, and maybe, just maybe, Kingdom of the Dead will be able to revive those same feelings of love and enjoyment once more for an entirely new generation.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun as hell but extremely rough around the edges+ The soundtrack and aesthetic are top notch+ Movement is very floaty and bouncy, calling back to memories playing Blood+ Writing is okay and somewhat sardonic+ Guns feel nice to shoot+ Level design is excellent and each level is unique+ Multiple difficulties to choose from- Frame drops in certain areas as well as graphical pop in- Soundtrack is a little too overpowering and can overshadow certain sound effects- Weapon sounds are underwhelming- Enemy variety is very low- Enemies can get stuck behind level geometry- Enemies make little to no impactful sound and can sneak up on you easily- Bosses are extremely easy to beat- In certain levels the game will railroad you on ammo- Animations are a bit janky and could use work- Collision is very weird and you will get stuck on plenty of objectsSad to say but this feels more like an early access game over a finished product, I really hope the devs take this feedback and build upon it, there's a solid game underneath this just waiting to be unearthed.

Got to the first boss and the game crashed when I died. Considering I didn't feel like I was having "fun" up until that point, seems like that's a good sign to not recommend this game. Movement is sluggish, guns feel and sound good (except this weird quirk with ADS and the revolver animation when you select it. It's horribly unpolished feeling). But they just lack... I don't know how to describe it other than needing a little extra "oompf." And the enemies. Pathfinding 101, with AI that b-lines straight to you, is dead set on finding a line-of-sight or both. _childDocuments_.review: The game is simple, and can be fun at times. It has a great soundtrack, excellent gun-play, very simple controls, and has very decent world-building. That being said, I can't recommend the game.-The sound, outside of the soundtrack, is done very badly. At times its very quiet, or very loud. There are also sound queues that are part of the ambiance that would normally signal incoming enemies, which can be very jarring.-The melee is terrible. The sword has an oddly short range, does terrible damage, and you are unable to block incoming hits.-Lighting is odd in some areas, which is very frustrating because there's no gamma control. This results in some enemies, especially fast ones, being difficult to see.-Some enemies are incredibly annoying because they will endlessly stun lock you. Boss fights are very easy, although annoying in the aspect that the boss can kill you instantly. It doesn't help that you get constantly spammed with enemies the entire time and they can block your movement. Some enemy pathing is also very slow or abrupt, and I saw multiple "wounded" enemies suddenly T-pose. Models are very stiff, and move awkwardly.-Dying makes you lose most ammo and almost all the gear you picked up. This can easily turn an easy mission into an absolute slog-fest on harder difficulties.-Progress is only saved inside the level, meaning that mission progress is only saved by completing the mission. If you leave mid-level you have to start that level all over again despite save checks. This is more of a quality of life nitpick, but its still incredibly annoying. To add to this, you can't pause the game. If you pause midfight, enemies will continue to attack you.-There are only 8 mission scenarios with 3 different difficulties, and that is the entirety of the game. Which means that it is basically an arcade game being charged for $15.Overall, I think this game had a nice vision, and was a good idea, it was just a bit poorly executed. It feels very unfinished, and like it needs a lot of polishing. I'm sure if more time was spent on fixing gameplay and adding a bit more content, then it would be a better end product. If that happens, and the game gets an updated build, then I will happily re-review.Score 2/5

_childDocuments_.review: Short and relatively sweet. Game feels like it chose a flavor—cool aesthetic and a setting acting in harmony—with everything else following afterward for better or worse. As a result the game's pseudo-monochromatic pen-and-ink visual style really pops in levels and locations that all feel extremely distinct from one another. This is probably the game's biggest appeal and it is fantastic in that regard. The music and the missions themselves are definitely entertaining (perhaps lacking in difficulty) and present as humorously mundane as killing droves of undead and sealing portals is quite literally your profession.⠀The gameplay elements lack that same full level of polish. Your arsenal covers the shooting essentials (with the inclusion of some amusing alt-fires), but they could use more punch and balance. The iconic double-barrel shotgun tickles anything bigger than fodder, and the rifle or gatling gun outclasses everything as long as ammo lasts. Ammo reserves tend to be ridiculously inexhaustible (If you have any sense of discipline), but the second you die you become wholly bereft of any ammo at all as that isn't saved by checkpoints and ends up being reset. Speaking of dying, the mid-level saves feel incomprehensibly inconsistent: Sometimes a death will just send you back a few feet, but sometimes it also undoes secondary objectives or retroactively re-incarcerates every freed prisoner. This can lock some levels in a fail-state on the highest difficulty, forcing a restart for full completion (Which admittedly isn't a huge task, this is more of a minor annoyance.)Beyond those ideas I spoke so fondly (or not so fondly) of, there is still a relatively splendid and enjoyable demonic shooting job-venture game here, and it is one that can be very casually consumed. It is definitely a game I would recommend to those who were allured by the aforementioned distinct visual style.

_childDocuments_.review: KINGDOM of the DEAD looks and feels like a love letter to old horror comics. I love the aesthetic, the music, and the stages.With how floaty the controls are and how strong some of the weapons are, you can easily take anywhere from 5 to 25 minutes per level. After playing through slow and meticulously, I cheesed the sh!t out of each stage. Despite the ability to quickly mad dash through each map, the level layout feels expansive and rewards some level of exploration with more ammo and health upgrades. What really took me in what the world. Maps are fun and range from tight corridor fighting to wide fields that you can haul ass across. I had a ton of fun blasting through enemies just as much as I did bobbing and weaving around and over enemies.Bosses were personable and enjoyable. I got the sense these were something you'd see in those old golden age horror comics. The forces of darkness in this game are a treat, though I will say some enemies are very much bullet sponges. The music and atmosphere made for a really fun, upbeat yet sp00ky setting, and I loved the color scheme. Black and white with colors for the powerups and magic made for a visually charming experience.A few criticisms: The giant birds (I'm assuming these are birds) could be difficult to see in stages with the open night sky. Another thing that players may find jarring is that the hitboxes are a bit off at times. I am unsure if it is the enemies' hitboxes or the weapon hitboxes, but I think it is a bit of both. This is particularly apparent with the sword. One last thing, the first boss is used twice early on in the game. I took to just be two different of the same type of boss but if you're just playing the first few stages and you get two of the same in a row, it can set an expectation that this will be the only boss for the whole game and then people may feel less inclined to play through the rest. Happy to say that was not the case.All in all, KINGDOM of the DEAD a short and sweet game that in my mind is worth the $15. It plays a little weird at times, but I feel like it's a worthy candidate in horror-shooters, and maybe in some people's minds, a resurgence in the retro/boomer-shooter genre.

_childDocuments_.review: A throwback to the old FPS games of yore, KINGDOM of the DEAD is a simple enough piece of entertainment that does not require excessive thought on the player's part. Certainly the supposed hand-drawn graphics are uniquely charming, and the soundtrack is reminiscent of the old MS-DOS MIDI music from my childhood. The weapons are varied enough, as are the monsters.Now, the drawbacks. I concur with some observers over the game's hand-drawn graphics, which although an interesting twist proved to be problematic at points in the game as the dimness may affected the eyesight of more myopic individuals like myself. The pathing for the human prisoners whom you have the option of rescuing is janky, and were it not for the fact that Likewise one of the secondary objectives  was hard to spot. The game  The apparent dearth of guides or followers of KINGDOM of the DEAD (oddly enough) made it more complicated. That admittedly soured me a little from the game.Nonetheless, for its asking price and the few hours I sunk into KINGDOM of the DEAD, I have no major complaints. Hell, it costs roughly the same for a movie ticket and I got a couple more hours from it. So if you enjoy the sprite-ish shooters of the past, then it's likely this will get your gears moving.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom of the Dead is a uniquely artistic FPS with some realsolid gameplay, albeit mixed in with some jank that has yet tobe completely ironed out as of the date of this review.-Unique and beautiful scratchboard-like art style-Short (Less than a handful of hours to complete)-Simple yet satisfying story-Excellent retro-horror style soundtrack and atmosphere-Well made level design-Slight weapon imbalance; some weapons are noticeably superior to others-Enemy animations are a bit jagged and rough-Enemies are either very easy or slightly annoying to deal with-Checkpoint system-Extreme lack of lighting in most areas, making navigation occasionally difficult-Certain bosses are bugged and can be very easily exploited (killed) in certain levels-Does not have a manual save function-Weapons do not carry over in each stage-Death penalty (Significant reduction in carried ammunition upon respawn)-There are still some bugs (such as enemies inside walls)Despite it's small problems and other mediocrities, Kingdom of the Dead is still asatisfying FPS that is absolutely worth your time if you're an FPS fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe it's because I just played Metal: Hellsinger, another excellent, unique first person shooter, but if I had to choose one adjective to describe the combat of this game, it would be "rhythmic." I don't mean this in the literal sense of Hellsinger, in which you're matching your shots to the beat of the music. But at its best, there's a palpable groove to the way it feels to move and shoot in Kingdom of the Dead. Few weapons in the game allow for anything resembling rapid-fire. After each shot of the pistol or rifle, Chamberlain performs a stylish flip of the weapon. Similarly, the double-barrel shotgun and rocket launcher need to be reloaded after each shot. So unless you're using the gatling gun, something that chews through bullets so quickly that it should only be used in specific dire situations, there's no holding down the left mouse button and letting led fly. There's a timing to each shot, the window of which gets even more narrow when enemy movement and incoming fire is taken into account, giving each pull of the trigger surprising stakes for a game that otherwise comes across as another run-and-gun twitchy throwback FPS.These stakes raise even higher once it clicks that most of these enemies are complete bullet sponges, if not next to invulnerable, unless you're aiming for the weak spot of a head or big eyeball. Dodge enemy fire, aim down sights, fire and watch their head pop off and blood geyser out like a shaken champagne bottle. Flip your pistol, reposition, aim, fire, flip. Dodge. Aim. Fire. Flip. One. Two. Three. Four. Then a couple big demons come out and break your rhythm, so you have to retreat - run back to the next room, wait for them to follow and bottle-neck themselves in the doorway, then try to find your rhythm again. Dodge. Aim. Fire. Flip. One Two. Three. Four.It's a propulsive flow, and it's not the only thing the game has going for it. The art is almost certainly the most immediate thing that makes it stand out in a crowd. The hand-drawn black and white style is gorgeous. This isn't the kind of game where I would have expected myself to get distracted from pushing forward through the level because I had to take a minute to admire the skybox I was staring at from the edge of a cliff, but it happened several times. And despite the monochromatic theme, the varied level design kept each new location feeling fresh. There are even a few surprising twists to certain levels, some of which are executed better than others, but I admire the ambition for what appears to be essentially a one-man team.As with any work of passion by a DIY developer, there's a certain degree of jank. The saving system took me a minute to figure out, for example. Your progress is saved at checkpoints throughout levels, but this only holds for when you die and respawn. If you quit out of the game, you have to start the level over again, and your progress isn't actually saved until you've fully finished the level. Levels can take as long as 30-40 minutes, so make sure you're able to commit to one once you've started it. Similarly, when you DO die and restart at a checkpoint, the actual progress you made isn't saved - you're started with just a little ammo for each weapon, and if you backtrack a little you'll find that all the enemies you killed (and all the hostages you've saved) are perplexingly back again. This isn't a huge deal, but it did take some getting used to. There are other notable glitches and idiosyncrasies, such as enemies getting stuck in walls but still being able to shoot you, or occasionally getting stuck on geometry that it doesn't look like you should be getting stuck on. Mild annoyances made entirely forgivable, in my opinion, by the fact that one person made this game.I award this game the most complimentary 7 out of 10 possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Fine, I'll give it a thumbs up...I wasn't initially on board with this game. The pencil sketch graphic is really cool, but there's also a cartoonish element to it, found in monster design and some of the music. Also, the dialogue between the protagonist and the sword feels like it's trying to imbue the game with some character, but it's too barebones to fulfill that goal.Nevertheless, in terms of mechanics, this is a simple, straightforward, old school shooter that is actually kind of fun. It has fast movement, it rewards headshots, and it has tactical considerations when choosing weapons. It has a reasonable amount of variety, giving you 10 different locations that capitalize well on the pencil sketch aesthetic, and throwing you enough curve balls that you're not bored, even though the different levels all follow the same formula. At the same time, it doesn't overstay its welcome, taking around 4 hours to complete.Overall, it's a good old school shooter, with unique graphics, and given its price and length, you don't have much to lose by giving it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Kingdom of the dead is an amazing game overall with few errors to speak of. It's story? Self contained and compelling, with a beginning and an end with a middle shaped to the player's experience directly. The dialogue is also witty and enjoyable.It's gameplay? Simple and effective. Doom-like in nature, I cannot help but enjoy the simple run and gun style of KOD. The map design allows for large, open combat that makes me enjoy moving around more than most shooters in the non-movement shooter genre. The gunplay is great, and the ability for each weapon to have an alternate fire adds more to the game than I believe many would think. The health system is very grueling, with healing and health increases being few and far between. However, the difficulty remains stagnant throughout the game except for the last mission, where it is drastically increased. This is a consequence of the freedom of level choice, so I cannot fault the game too much. However in the same breath, any difficulty below the maximum feels a bit too easy. I may be experienced in shooters more than the average joe, but there's still little difference between normal skill and easy.On a more positive note, enemy design and placement is great! Each enemy has a clearly defined weakpoint whether it's the head for humanoids or the glowing bits on eldritch horrors, I was never confused on where to shoot. Same thing goes for bosses as well.The artstyle? GORGEOUS. This is, in terms of style alone, one of my favorite games of all time. Never before have I felt like I was playing a comic book or graphic novel. The visuals with the few bright colors clashing with the overarching black and white creates an inherent sense of direction for the player, using the game's core feature in the gameplay loop.Overall, I cannot recommend Kingdom of the dead enough. It's an enjoyable -10 hour experience that will blow you away and leave you satisfied as a player.

_childDocuments_.review: This thing has crazy potential. I've gone through the entire first level, and for better or worse, I think I have a mostly complete idea of the game. Enemy variation is nice and terrifying- the distant growls really keep you locked and loaded as you come around dark corners. Although, I do have to say the variance in projectile enemies is some what disappointing. Not to say there isn't enough- there's plenty, but I don't quite feel the significance of their different weapons. Which, I think is a byproduct of the mismatched speed of player movement and general combat. It's stupid easy to go stupid fast and out maneuver your enemies but it doesn't feel like they're quite built for it. Take the wizard guys for example. They've got decent AI, but their projectiles lack the speed to push the players into encounters, where players have to "pick a line" in order to reduce the damage taken. Although, you really do start to feel the heat with large clusters of enemies and then the speed really does pick up. Which, mostly eliminates this problem but with so much chaos, difference in weapon, projectiles, timing, etc., is washed out by the sheer size of the hoard. Also, I do have a tendency to get stuck on level geometry in fast moving situations, and without "revert back to checkpoint" or something, its kinda frustrating. I know I've mostly talked about the bad of the game, but that's only because its waaaaay shorter to list the bad than the good. This game has astounding controls that have that soft slid-y feeling but still manage to be responsive enough to pop off fast headshots. And oh don't even get me started on the art design. It's surprisingly expressive despite being only black and white.The price tag, combined with the content makes it worth it. I do truly hope the devs take a look into adjusting some things for a little bit more of a fine tuned experience but its in a good enough place right now to stand on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: The game definitely has a lot of jank and rough edges, but it's probably one of the most imaginative games I've played as of late. While visibility is sometimes not great, the art style is spectacular. I enjoyed exploring the levels as each one is very unique and distinct, crammed with tiny details that made me smile. I also absolutely love the designs of the enemies, one of my favorite things being how the undead with guns twist their bodies all around to try to get a shot on you. While the movement can be weird at times, the gunplay is satisfying. If you're a fan of the new Doom games, quick swapping weapons is an effective strategy here and I found myself using different quick swap combos based on what enemy I was fighting. Headshots are also huge in this game and always great to pull off. There are only 8 levels, which means the game doesn't take long to beat, but the distinct looks and twists of each map makes the short length very sweet, and honestly I've been appreciating shorter games lately. All in all, this game has a lot of rough edges but shows that lots of love and charm was put into it, making it an overall enjoyable experience, enjoyable enough to make me write this review.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is *almost* great. The soundtrack is phenomenal, the weapons are neat, and the art style is unique. Unfortunately, the AI is just not interesting; the enemies move very erratically, and they don't attack you in any sort of intelligent way. As a result, the game is very easy and you can sprint past basically everything. It's a shame; this probably could have been resolved with a few more months of polish.For controller players that don't mind the subpar AI, I recommend using the DOOM controller configuration available via Steam Big Picture; the game feels a lot better when sprint is always on.

_childDocuments_.review: Check out the full review over at I really enjoyed what I got to play of this game. Once my eyes adjusted to only seeing monotone shades, I could really appreciate the art style in motion. On my first death I was a tad frustrated, as I hadn’t reached a checkpoint yet so feared it might be roguelike and was glad to later see it wasn’t. But it caused me to rethink my approach. That being trying not to get hit, as health is a resource not an auto regenerating bar.  This approach later changed again when I discovered running through Doom style proved more effective. Until it wasn’t, at which point I found the necessity in a balanced approach. I played with Mouse and Keyboard, which isn’t my preferred input for an FPS (I know, gasp), so would love to next time get the controller out on this one. There is also cheat codes which can be used, something which I find lacking in a lot of games since the early 2000s. As a fan of accessibility, I would like to explore those in some detail. Overall, the game is great, a fast-paced blast ‘em up which oozes style. Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some great ideas and surprising twists there, with nice, varied environments and bosses, but the game urgently needs some simple fixes: an always run toggle (the levels are HUGE and there’s often no reason to walk), turning off collisions on dead enemies (it gets especially troublesome on the ship, where you have to keep moving) and the inclusion of mipmaps, which I assume are not enabled since faraway scenery, combined with the high contrast textures gets really straining to the eye.The music is good and even worth listening outside of the game, but I recommend turning it off and try playing that way for a way more immersive, spooky experience. Doing so does wonders in the forest level, especially.The guns' fire and reload animations are rough, and I feel that contributes to the guns not feeling as powerful as they can be, which is surprising, because I felt the damage amounts were right. Headshots are fun to execute. Same thing with shotgunning the flying enemies. A bit more feedback could help, like bigger splotches of blood where the bullets hit. There’s also a surprising amount of bugs on level completion. Beating the mansion level on moderate registered a completion on the crypts. Beating the train level on the hardest difficulty didn’t register as a win either. That’s annoying.I liked the game, but I wouldn’t recommend it to everyone in its current state. If you have a moderate amount of tolerance for jank and like experimental weirdo shooters, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Delightfully early-00s-style FPS. As striking as the aesthetic is, it's not the only thing carrying the game—it also has a great range of levels and encounters, a pulp-y adventure mood, solid pacing, and despite a bit of roughness around the edges, some pretty satisfying shooting. Give me a nice revolver and I'll be happy to pop heads all days.Combat-wise it feels akin to the early stages of a Serious Sam game, before they've really ramped up the hordes—fast, but not too fast, with a healthy mix of cramped and wide-open spaces. Unfortunately the game does tend to chug a bit in the latter areas, which is really unfortunate for its opening level (the Mansion, one of the most ambitious and visually dramatic of the set). The boss fights are also mostly just 'backpedal away while shooting the big guy', but whatever, at least they're over fast.If you can get past that (and the occasional weird bug—I once lost my sword somehow and soft-locked myself out of finishing the level), you'll find a joyful little shooter that eschews radical design gimmicks for constant variety, and keeps up the surprises all the way to the end. Between this and Syscrusher, I've become quite fond of Dirigo Games—I hope we get to see more from them.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the potential for this game surpasses it's form upon initial release, I had a lot of fun and will recommend it based on it's overall game play and art style. Quick switching weapons feels smooth and necessary for optimizing damage, sorta like a 'Doom Eternal Lite.' Almost everything can die with one well-placed rifle shot, so you are rewarded for accuracy and finesse. The art style is super original and fun to look at. I did find myself using the default palette "Standard" and switching to "Softer" for the darker bits. There is just enough story element to make it 'interesting enough' and certainly not over-bearing. The music was great and I truly enjoy it! Midi/retro style music fits this game well; however, there were a few instances where the music felt slightly out of place.The game would benefit from a few bug fixes, ie. monsters stuck in the wall and a weird jump+ads bug. Also, it would benefit from a few balance tweaks; I overall felt the game was too easy, particularly the boss fights. Dynamite can literally kill bosses in two seconds, or you can just left click with the Gatling gun, and there is a TON of ammo everywhere. I was able to complete the game in 6 hours on the hardest difficulty for all levels. I wasn't rushing through it, though I do play a lot of retro shooters.I believe the game absolutely needs some sort of slaughter/horde esque mode, simply to help figure out how to balance the game better. The enemy types in the game are interesting, but are often utilized in a way where fights are trivial. I think a horde mode would help us figure out the limits of the game, and then help balance future custom maps, giving this game true longevity. This game's core mechanics and weapons are very strong, and I think the devs may have underestimated how much carnage these few weapons can truly cause.But yeah, the game feels super good and looks super good. I hope it receives updates and support, because its fun as hell.PS - It would be nice for qol to have the enemy/civilian count accessible while in-game for those who want to 100% -- and on that note, it would also be nice to have some achievements to grind for, and add some re-play value.
