_childDocuments_.review: Holy.I love this game, I really do. Would I recommend this game, though? Probably, but not 100%.First of all, I would like to talk about the positives. The artstyle is really nice. I am a fan of pixel games, sometimes even more so than realistic-looking games, and this game looks really good. The variety of animals you have in this game is also quite big. 63 animals may not sound like a lot, but when you factor in the 10 variations of each animal and the size of the zoo, I would say it is perfect. The morality system is also quite nice; the ability to be good or bad is a very nice addition, which sold the game for many people, and rightly so.However, as we all know, no game is perfect. I believe that, while the feature of making hybrids is cool, it is implemented poorly. First of all, to make a hybrid, you need to:a) Have two animals, which you would like to splice together, andb) Have discovered 5 variations of each animal, andc) Wait for the splicer to make the hybrid, which takes anywhere from 2 days to more than 10 daysAnd, after completing all of this, congratulations! You have created a hybrid! Except... They are mainly useless. In my whole time of playing this game, I have spliced together maybe 15 hybrids in total, most of which have been spliced because of a task. The only thing hybrids really do is increade your zoo rating which, unless you have a lot of them, doesn't really do much. And while they may be nice to look at, if you don't have a special enclosure for them, good luck finding them in between the other animals, while you are probably zoomed out to the max most of the time.Another thing I would like to talk about is the tutorials. In my opinion, the early game's tutorials are quite good, introducing the players to the basics one step at a time. However, as you get more into the game, you are bombarded with features that, in hindsight, are not complicated at all, but you have to understand them all by yourself, which may take a while. It is not that big of a deal, however, not everything requires a tutorial.The last thing I want to talk about is the grind. The horrible, horrible grind. I am an achievement hunter, and as such, I like to get my games to 100%, or as close to that number, as I can. Naturally, I went into this game with this mindset as well. Most of the base game achievements are alright, just progressing through the game, but some are just awful. The main one being Map Master, which requires you to map out Every. Single, Animal. Genome. The constant grind of just cloning the appropriate variants and breeding them, hoping to get the one you want, was painful. I did it, however. But it took so damn long. Apart from this, the grind to get all plots of land was similarly long.Anyway, again, I would recommend this game. It has a nice artstyle and a good gameplay, however, it also has some problems which, while not horrible, take away from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Full of bugs. I like the concept of the game, but the game has way too many bugs so that the experience is terrible, on top of a plethora of idiotic gameplay decisions.First off, the bugs. Once your zoo starts getting big, the lag becomes ridiculous, and moreover, it starts freezing on you. I literally lost 2.5 hours of progress because this dumb game decided to freeze randomly, and it just keeps playing its music while I can't move my cursor or click anything. This wouldn't be so bad if it weren't for idiotic game design description 1 - inability to manually save. Daily autosaves are fine for little flash web games. But when you reach the later stages in this game, where each in-game day can literally take hours, you absolutely need to give players the ability to save during the day. If nothing else, it's good insurance against crashes.Then there's the tech tree, which is for some reason 1. hidden and 2. has zero logic as to what unlocks what, forcing you to waste effort on suboptimal research paths just to get to the tech you actually want. These types of simulation games thrive on choice and flexibility, and hiding what the research is and also forcing you to unlock based on adjacency rather than what you actually want is the worst of both worlds.And of course, there's a bunch of other silly gameplay decisions also. You have only the one storehouse. You can't manually tell your individual employees to do stuff, you just have to trust their bad AI pathing and prioritizing. No vertical scrollbar when your lists get large. Poor explanations of what stuff does, for the longest time I couldn't make Craft Beer even though I had hops and the building and employees, until one day it just suddenly started making beer. At least, if it even bothers to explain at all; nowhere was it ever mentioned that you need an incinerator to remove dead animals, for example, and I had to Google for what to do about all the notifications I was getting. And of course, a ton of other small inconveniences that snowball into a festering pile of poor gameplay experiences that make you wonder if these guys ever had anyone playtest the darn thing before releasing it into production.Overall, the game concept is neat, and the art style is cute, but one does not game on concepts and art alone, and those two things are unfortunately all that this game has going for it.PS: Yes, I have a buttload of hours in this game. Therefore, I definitely gave it a fair shake before giving it a neg review.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had the game for a few days, and I can definitely say this is a charming, engaging tycoon sim that offers some rather complex systems in a cute, manageable way. The graphics are endearing as hell, and paired with a plethora of audio delights, it's a great little package of wonderful. One of the things that really engages me the most and I find most impressive is the morality system. You can choose to be a good little zoo and engage your due diligence by fighting for animal rights, building a wonderful release program for animal conservation, etc. Or you can totally choose to be the greedy, evil corp you've always wanted to be. The mafia needs you to dispose of dead bodies? Sure, why not. Robotic animals? Hell yeah. Want to feed your guests animal parts disguised as Totally Real Healthy Food? You bet.  On top of this morality system, this sim offers just an interesting way to hire and manage employees and their work spaces. All of this together makes for quite an interesting time - definitely something you can get lost in for hours at a time. And oh, did I mention the gene splicing? Sure, go ahead, make creatures that are totally cursed! Your zoo needs the revenue.However, there are several QoL improvements I believe the game could benefit from. An autosave feature is certainly at the top of that list, as you can currently only save once a day, but there are a few others that are just as important. The ability to cancel a choice isn't really here. For example, if I wanted to take in several animals, but then realize I don't have as much space as I thought or the proper enclosures, I have no choice but to either a) move forward with a bad decision or b) close the game and lose that day's progress. I also think there could be a better research system, in the sense that choices for research are a bit more clear beforehand. As it stands, you kind of just have to choose things willy-nilly. You can narrow down your search with a sidebar option (e.g. enclosures, etc.), but it still stands as a pretty vague guide. Finding new specific enclosures to further the progress of your zoo feels like a real chore - and almost impossible sometimes - when research begins to get costly, and there's no real avenue of choice that feels right.Overall, I think this is a great game with even greater potential to be fantastic. The team has already implemented a lot of great QoL updates, and I hope to see more in the future. I can't recommend this enough for folks looking to get lost in a relaxing and endearing game with some fun little twists. I'm beyond excited to start my evil playthrough. If you need any bodies disposed of, you know who to call.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Game is fun but needed more time in the oven.Let met get this out of the way: I really enjoy this game. It's quirky and scratches a certain itch, but it has weird issues that are probably the result of a rushed development.THE GOODGame does everything you'd want from a zoo game: Breeding animals, being creative (or not?) with zoo layouts, micro-managing what you sell at your shops, etc. The evil morality upgrades are comically evil at times. Also good AND evil both have useful things so one isn't clearly better than the other so you can choose what you want.THE BADThe morality system isn't super well designed: Some items you can't get unless you have a certain morality, but once you have them they work forever. Some require you get AND keep that morality. Also, you can't build up credit with both types: One kind of morality negates the other and you need quite a bit to get some of the higher end upgrades. The "Tech tree" is layed out poorly. Things are in weird directions so if you're looking for something, you either need to read a guide or hope the "Hint" to where something you need is in the direction you're heading.THE UGLYThe UI is kinda garbage and  it doesn't seem like you can change any of the keybinds. Also a lot of things that should *probably* be keybinds aren't (like a lot of the menus). Also the game has a *lot* of bugs. I didn't encounter any gamebreaking ones, but they exist and are irritating. Example: Sometimes if you move the window, it'll shift all the busses up a bit and they'll start running over the bottom of your zoo rather than on the road, and all the animals will be slightly out of position. The pathfinding AI for the visitors is randomly weird (I had them running CLEAR across the map from one subway station to another even though there was a subway at their destination). Menus also occasionally will refuse to close or will reopen once you close. Just little things that are prevalent enough that they should have been fixed before the 1.0 launch.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's build a Zoo is like a casual toned down planet zoo/zoo tycoon, with adorable pixel art that's extremely charming. However, casual doesn't mean toned down; maybe even crazier with it's own quirks.LBaZ has a tech tree that unfolds out beautifully in any direction that you want it to, provided that you've got the points to do so. This provides a gameplay that's quite unique to how you want to play and I enjoy that a bunch. It also has some of the funniest/quirky dialogue in a game as well, from wacky mafia bosses and mad scientists to the macabre like when I accidentally killed someone by letting them into a dangerous part of the zoo (oops).The ability to literally mix two animal's DNA together and create hybrids is just wild, find the funniest and wackiest ♥♥♥♥ you can create and laugh about it. This game really doesn't disappoint, especially when it has quite a low price-point during sales as well.Tip; If you're someone like me that's trying to min max, join the discord as it really helps! Also, don't be afraid to build larger enclosures, what you can see on the map is literally where you can build to; it's HUGE.Overall, solid game, I'd highly recommend it if you've got the time and need a good laugh as well as a proper zoo sim!

_childDocuments_.review: Advertised gameplay: Build a zoo and splice unique animals together! Actual gameplay: Spend all your time making "MoRaL" choices...  Honestly, this game would be so great if the devs used the time they put into their incomprehensible moral system on improved performance and a less clunky UI. The premise is so great, but the actual experience just falls so short.  It takes a LONG time to unlock new animals. According to steam, I've put about 5.5 hours into this game already, and I've only unlocked 6 unique animal types. (to put that into perspective, I believe there are something like 56?) Now, I have no issue with a slow burn of a game, but I came to realize that most of that time was not spent managing the animals, enclosures or breeding (you know, the things you actually play a zoo simulator for) but was rather spent monitoring the incredibly frustrating moral system, screwing around with the UI and getting lost in bad performance and the visual cluster of entities. The moral system is the primary offender for me. I can happily deal with a bad UI if the game is worth it, but I did NOT come to play a morality simulator. There are certain features that are only unlockable if you hold certain moral standings. Do you want to unlock the processor? (which turns deceased animals into usable resources?) well you gotta be EEEVIIIILL to unlock that. Do you want to unlock wind turbines? Well you've gotta be *self*righteous to use that! And not only do you need the proper moral standing to unlock certain features, but if you don't maintain that moral standing, then you won't be able to use them even if you already own them. (I had several wind turbines that legit shut down because I was too "evil" to use them or whatever) But what is even more frustrating than the limitations the moral system pose on how you build your zoo is how you gain moral points to begin with. One way to gain these points is through random (and horribly intrusive) events that constantly pop up and give you juvenile "do you want to lie for profits" choices. Annoying, but whatever. But it becomes an actual issue in how it affects the game play. You can't sell your animals... unless it's to shady black-market merchants (which gives you evil points of course); otherwise, you can either euthanize your animals (regardless of how young and healthy they are) for no moral points (okay...) or donate them (which costs YOU money for logistics fees or whatever) for good moral points. This is particularly frustrating when your animals are breeding out of control, and the only choice that doesn't affect you morally and financially is literally slaughtering the animal. (because selling it for a profit would be the EVIL choice, and you don't want to do that if you still want those turbines to run).  And this isn't even including the random, and completely pointless, moral choices you can make. Do you need to fire an employee? Well good news! you get to make the moral choice of paying them what you own, (neutral) paying them plus including a severance package, (good) or just not paying them anything (evil)... like, I don't freaking care at all what happens to this faceless, personalitiless npc; I just want to make an enclosure for my ducks!  Nobody is playing this game for any other reason than to make a zoo, so why are there all these utterly pointless choices that only serve a moral system which decides what buildings you get to place! I couldn't care less, and it's not enjoyable in the slightest. It's not funny, or witty, and creative: it's just dumb and constantly getting in the way of the rest of the game. Ultimately, it's very obvious that the only reason this "moral" system is in the game is to push the dev's personal ideology. (which is just horribly obnoxious if you don’t agree with it) Half of the "good" moral choice are basically just being green and ecofriendly (something that has nothing to do with morals btw) and the other half are either super basic "lie and steal for profits" or completely incomprehensible (like donating animals rather than selling them) There is this bizarre emphasis on CO2 output in this game to btw. It acts like you are running some large production facility rather than a little zoo. Oh yeah, and one of the quests is literally to hire three diverse employees or some sjw nonsense: meanwhile I couldn't care less what my employees look like; just go sweep up my animal's crap please. Stop making me pay attention to the random npc's and what they look like, I already have enough to manage. I'M HERE FOR THE ANIMALS, NOT THE FACELESS NPCs. Don’t tell me I need to cull out all the same looking people, regardless of their stats, to have my staff be diverse. I DON’T CARE. This is a perfect example of how forcing an ideology onto a game can make it worse. Staff in this game are a utility and nothing more, so stop making me pay attention to the skin color ratio of my staff: this is a game about getting diverse animals, not diverse staff members ffs. And that’s only the morality system The UI sucks bad; it's honestly the worst I've seen in any game. Just a couple example: If you want to manage your employees, you need to click the zoo's entrance; however, the entrance is at the very bottom of the screen, and because the zooming is awful, and there always seems to be a building menu in the way, it can be frustrating to click on the entrance when you need something. Another: If you want to get a large overview of what animals are in a cage, and quickly see their age and other status info, the best menu is the one a black-market dealer gives you when you are selling your animals to them; unfortunately, they only occasionally appear in your zoo, which means you are stuck with the inferior and inefficient interface that is normally available to you. These are two of the most frustrating UI issues for me, but there are many more. To top it off, the in-game cursor moves so slowly and has such bad precision, and since everything is buried in a different menu, it feels like you are wading through mud to reach anything. Also, this game becomes awful to play the longer it goes on. Animals breed out of control constantly; which, you can stop if you have time to micromanage everything. However, because progression relies on breeding different animal variants to trade for new animals, you have more incentive to just let them breed freely in hopes they produce something new. And this would be fine, if you weren’t penalized for having large amounts of animals, as getting rid of them is a moral choice, and letting them die of old age leaves decaying bodies lying around unless you have an incinerator (must be unlocked) or a processor (which is EVIL) and since there are 10 different variants of each animal, and you want to keep one of each kind for breeding purposes, you need to constantly be aware of everything going on. (Especially since it might take a long time to be able to breed/buy your way back to a specific variant if you let it die off) And in addition to the multitude of animals you’ll inevitably collect, visitors and employees are EVERYWHERE. Everything happens so fast, and so much needs to be managed that it just becomes a visual cluster and impossible to handle appropriately (and remember, I have like 10% of the animal types) and while everything happens so fast, progression is very slow. Pausing the game to manage things almost always feels like a waste of time since you spend so much time waiting on the important things to happen anyway. The more I play, the more frustrating it all becomes. I spend so much time trying to make sure everything keeps going, and trying to manage my morality, and so little time actually enjoying the process of creating a virtual zoo.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you found Planet Zoo too micromanagey/difficult/boring, you like pixel graphics, you like animals, you like customization, and you have a slightly darker sense of humor, this game is probably for you. Criticisms below.I tried Planet Zoo because I liked the idea, but found it too complicated/micro-managey for my tastes. I not only really like the look and idea of this game too, but the humor is definitely my speed, there's still a lot to manage without feeling overwhelmed, there's a lot of customization, and so far there seems to be a lot to it. There's replayability for reasons that could be considered spoilers, so I won't say what it is, but definitely replayability. You can also change the speed of the day if you need to just get through it/you did everything you needed to do that day.My only few of real criticisms are:1. The music is great, but does eventually get repetitive (you can turn it off if you like, though).2. Sometimes different game menus can get in the way of where you need to click on your zoo, and you have to struggle a bit to get around it. Can definitely use some tweaking.3. While not nearly as complicated as I personally found Planet Zoo to be, some functions in the game are poorly explained or not explained at all, but either through working it out myself or a quick online search, I was able to understand how to do things. Not all the mechanics were poorly explained, but I won't lie, some were. Maybe I'm an idiot, but I struggled to get water to my animals for a couple of minutes lol.All around, I really like this game and think it's worth what I paid, and I highly recommend it. They're still releasing updates for it, so it's not abandoned either!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Let's Build a Zoo is a cute and charming tycoon game that offers endless fun and entertainment. The game's pixel art style is adorable and adds to the overall charm of the game. One of the most exciting features of the game is the ability to splice animals together to create new and unique species, which allows players to let their creativity run wild.The game is easy to learn and fun to play, making it accessible to players of all skill levels. The gameplay is engaging and addictive, with a variety of tasks and challenges to keep players entertained for hours on end. As players progress through the game, they can unlock new features and technologies, making it even more exciting to play.Overall, Let's Build a Zoo is a fantastic game that offers a perfect balance of creativity, challenge, and entertainment. The ability to splice animals together and create new species adds a unique twist to the tycoon game genre, and the cute pixel art style and easy-to-learn gameplay make it a joy to play. Anyone looking for a fun and engaging game should definitely give Let's Build a Zoo a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Kairosoft game on steroids - extremely fun, cute, and varied. It's great to see the little animals - though they advertise 500, there are significantly less base types, but there are variants of each type of base animal - and you'd think that would make it less exciting, but the variants are so detailed it really does feel like 500 individual animals . The UI is a little confusing, but clicking around on your own will get you there in a few hours (if you're slow like me). The research system is chaotic, but in that way, is fun and engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not like the free mobile games you can get. This game is a step-up from that. From being able to customise exhibits with varying sizes and decorations, to making choices about your zoo such as whether to sell your animals to the black market or donating money to charity, this game focuses on your ability to manage the zoo at all times. It is slow gaining new animals and variants to be able to merge your animals, but i've enjoyed being able to expand my zoo quite easily and buy new land and stores to make a profit. The pixel art style is also very enjoyable.I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys micromanaging, decorating a massive zoo or/and people who love collector games. Summary Pros: Plenty to customise to make it feel unique, lovely pixel-art, not much of a grind for money required in the game, lots of animals and takes plenty of time to completeCons: gaining new animals takes a while, very difficult to idle in to gain the results you wantNeutral (depending on person can be a pro or con): the game relies heavily on your moral choices, such as co2 emissions or getting 'fake' animals or selling your animals on the black market
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: So anyone who down votes this game just can't build a zoo.Games fun and addictive with tons of things to unlock constantly with free content updates, hotfixes, and cheap pricing I can't find an area to complain.Cross breeding animals to make hilarious exhibits for your zoo (My favorite the goose pig *Pigoose*).10/10 a good game to sink your time into.A perfect game to even play on your side monitor in between whatever else you're doing with the ability to pause and speed up the pace of things on a whim.Go and build yourself a damn zoo.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable animals.Adorable animals on trampolines.Adorable animals on trampolines that you can genetically modify.Sounds good right?This game is definitely "busy work" lots to do and keep an eye on, perhaps a bit too much as your zoo gets bigger and the poop piles up but if you like that kind of game you will love this. I really like the moral choices element and so far have resisted pretending someones lost dog is a lion ..
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

For 20 Dollars its not that good of a deal but for 10 its allright.  If you want it to look like in the trailer you have to spend a lot of time. All that aside the game is beautiful and cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let's keep it real. "Let's Build a Zoo" is one of those games that makes you question whether you're a responsible zookeeper or an evil mastermind. I mean, where else can you splice a giraffe and a penguin to create the majestic "Giraffguin"?But wait, it gets better. As your zoo grows, so does the chaos! One moment you're trying to maintain a clean environment, and the next, you're chasing an escaped llama that's somehow acquired a jetpack. (Seriously, who gave the llama a jetpack? lmao)With its diverse cast of quirky animals, endless customization options, and the thrilling unpredictability of zoo life, "Let's Build a Zoo" is like the perfect mix of Noah's Ark and Frankenstein's lab. You won't be able to keep your paws off this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I have clocked 21 hours just here, but I've played this a lot longer on another platform, so it's easy to say that I do enjoy this game, a lot.  This game is similar to those tycoon type games that I grew up with, but it has a twist.  You can choose to build a zoo based on good or bad morals.  You get rewards according to which path you choose.  Like some have already stated, there are a few annoying little things that I believe would make the game a bit better, but they're definitely not deal breakers.  All in all, this is a really fun game to play, it can also be pretty funny (I think it is anyway, especially when you can create hybrid animals that look really weird).
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Pure enjoyment. Well worth the cost. Yet it takes itself seriously in your ability to properly finance your zoo without feeling like a desperate struggle and constant restart. It's very possible to be "moral" and "good" and still make a very profitable zoo.Anyways you should just get it. Go ahead. Get it. Do it.Just get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art style and animals are pulled off amazingly. As some other reviews state, the animals overpopulate very quickly.The only movement from the animals is bobbing around. Don't come into this if you want to look at the animals for a while.The appeal of the game is found by looking at you zoo more zoomed out. I have around 170 k and nothing to spend it on, the game really slows down to just managing tons of lifeless animals and breeding for new variations. "this one is rolling a ball around but it has white feathers."The good route farming wasn't explained very well.Getting new animals is much slower than something like planet zoo. You aren't buying them from a large library but you start with a handful and then have to spend lots of time breeding for other zoos to get new ones that you can buy.I love the game and the decisions you can make but the main part involving animals is kind of lacking for me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Zoo games, this will fit right in your alley and it comes with a nice little twist. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing retro style zoo sim of a game! Really enjoy it a TON and the most unique thing about this title vs other games is its vast scale. It is by far the LARGEST zoo I ever made. Definitely recommend it casually - but like other reviewers already mentioned, the UI and system accessibility is very BAD and the sheer scale of your zoo will spoil your fun. When I have covered the entire land with my zoo, I have just above 1000 employees in the zoo, and LITERALLY every 30 seconds in real life, someone wants a pay raise or they will resign. And you have to search the entire zoo to replace their backfill. And not just that, but even animals grow quickly in their pens until they die of overcrowding. There are ways to mitigate this like culling and donating and releasing back to the wild, but it is ALL MANUAL and you will find it super tedious after real life 1 hour of doing the same crap again and again. So yes, get this game for sheer joy of it, but definitely it will outstay itself because of its terrible manual system.P.S: Even the night system sucks. The entire screen goes dark and you really can hardly see anything... the lamps look beautiful at that time, but you sacrifice actual smooth gaming for it. And the best part? By midgame your 'night' portion should already be upgraded to the point it's almost 5 hours ingame, which means 1/3 if your gaming time you are squinting hard at a dark screen to find stuff.P.S.S: Getting 100% achievement specific to this game is really quite stupid and does not feel fun or rewarding at all. The points system going for 200 either good/bad is terrible towards the final points just to get the achievement. I also spent over 50 hours on unlocking all genomes, only to find out the Map Master is bugged on my game. It still remains locked despite all animals showing gold stars on them (meaning fully unlocked)
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

Honestly, the only negative is not being able to pet the cute animals (like the komodo dragons).My boyfriend bought this game for me when I was having a really down day and it's been a great way to help my mood when I have a hard day. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game with more features than initially expected. If you like decorating a pixel art zoo with cute critters, this is for you.Once you get to "endgame", however (it was about the time when i bought about half the available plots), I believe the dev might not quite understand the appeal or reward of their own game. There are way too many popups (staff level ups at every other second, "critical decisions" popup that i have answered all the same way for about 50hours now please let me turn this off thank you) and other pulls towards micromanagement that it gets tedious and distracting. Especially when some windows will close the window you had open beforehand and you cannot for the life of you remember which nursery and breeding pair you were inspecting bc your ADHD brain simply nuked that information out of your skull by ANOTHER pop up. The most satisfaction, and this is where I am questioning that the devs don't know about the appeal of their game, is when i get to lean back and let my giant zoo empire run smoothly all on it's own with as few clicks as possible. Kind of when you upgrade from watering all of your plants manually to automating everything with sprinklers in farming games.Trying to map out every of the 10 genomes for each animal has triggered my hyperfocus so badly it's like i'm high. Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: This game is way more addictive than I anticipated. I think it might be the breeding and hybrid systems combined with the cloning that really gets me. I have no idea how much I need to make them happy. I can only add so much before I run out of space.-Even with assigning zones to animal keepers and having the store room easily accessible, there never seems to be enough keepers. I keep having to hire them and it's never enough even if I don't have many changes in exhibits.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a blast. There’s plenty of content to explore and has endless replay ability. It’s easy to lose a few hours at a time playing, especially if you’re a fan of management tycoon sims. The graphics are cute and imaginative. The research and morality mechanics are rewarding and opens the game up to different play styles and design choices. There’s tons of depth and customizable options to experiment with. The game’s not without some cons, however. The construction is okay but editing existing structures can be tedious. Park ratings are also something that’s not explained much at all. It can also get overwhelming when you have a giant park but the devs already added a few more automation mechanics to combat this. It is very promising to see the devs already release a few patches after launch. There’s been a handful of bug fixes, qol changes and content in the patches. The dev team cares about the game and it shows. Overall it’s a strong entry into a genre that’s not the most popular in today’s esports age of gaming. If you’re searching for a (mostly) relaxing indie game that’s well worth the price, definitely look into Let’s Build a Zoo. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I. Love. This. Game. I can't believe how hard the devs have continued to work on it. I feel spoiled. They really could have just made a solid zoo game and called it a day, but I've had a blast with the dinosaur expansion, and I look forward to what else comes our way. Everything is adorable. Everything functions. The UI is easy to understand and memorize. It's navigable. Customization isn't overwhelming or difficult. The art and animations aren't 'simple' by any means; they're lovingly rendered. I adore the art style. It's more satisfying to decorate and build pens in this game than it is in Planet Zoo, imo. Like a super-detailed, realistic waterfall is great and all, but it doesn't make me feel good to have to spend an hour customizing and workshopping 4 square inches of my zoo. Let's Build a Zoo doesn't give me that problem.The music is enjoyable. The tasks are doable. Even when my many, many animals and their many, many needs make me feel "overwhelmed," I am not Actually overwhelmed in a way that is stressful or frustrating. This game helps me relax and focus and just have some fun. There's also a touch of comedy that I really appreciate. I feel like the only thing that needed a bit of clarification was the in-zoo product manufacturing mechanic. I had a hard time figuring out how to send my produced plastic to my gift shops without some online forum help. But that could have just come down to how well I comprehended what I read! 10/10, could play for hours and hours. I feel like it'd be good for older kids/tweens, too.

_childDocuments_.review: all my animals died because the store room decided to become inaccessible few times my animals starved to death because suddenly an established gate wouldn't workMoving the gate solved nothingtried multiple remediesnothing..your animals lifespan is about 1-2 hours in game, so the attachment is minimalZoo Tycoon it is..

_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I LOVE this game, it tickles that micro management itch I so often get, and would highly recommend, however there have been a couple of frustrations for me:1) late game staff managementI find that my animals always seem to be hungry even with a full shed, and I feel like i'm getting more staff endlessly, I know it would work a bit better if I assigned them zones but it's mind numbing and tedious to do when you have 100 staff and 40 enclosures and forget which member of staff you last assigned. solution: in the same way you set zones for janitors use that system for all staff that require zones, e.g player drags an area and creates "zone 1" that way you could have an option to select multiple staff for zone 1 in the same way you select animals to move into a different pen and have staff set to one zone at a time, that way you would be able to see unassigned staff easily. 2) Crashes!When the day is coming to an end in late game if you're to focused on a task (in my case I was building an enclosure) the day ended and the pop up appeared while i was clicking madly to add balls to a pen, and the game crashed. not once, not twice but three times I did this by accident, I think all games crash from time to time but I felt that was an avoidable oneSolution: (possibly?) Auto game pause when building/moving objects
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️☆ (4/5)I never thought I'd say this, but "Let's Build a Zoo" is the most fun I've had micromanaging animal poop and genetic monstrosities since my last family reunion. The game is a delightful mix of tycoon management, pixel art charm, and moral dilemmas that make you question whether combining a flamingo with a crocodile is a good idea (hint: it always is).Building enclosures, managing staff, and ensuring your animals are happy and well-fed is a blast. The visitors are perpetually delighted, even when they’re standing next to a pen full of penguin-goat hybrids. The sheer variety of animals and crossbreeding options keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting.But, oh boy, the notifications! If I had a nickel for every time I got a notification about research points, I could fund a real zoo. "You've got research points!" "Spend your research points!" "Don't forget your research points!" - I get it, game, I have research points! It’s like having a nagging mom who just discovered push notifications.Despite the notification overload, "Let's Build a Zoo" is an addictive and quirky ride that lets your inner mad scientist and animal lover run wild. Just make sure you’re prepared for your phone to buzz more than a beehive during honey season. 🐾🔬
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very cute and has some fun writing in it. Some of the management aspects can be a bit min-maxey and honestly stressed me out a bit. If you don't put your animals on contraceptives you'll constantly get new ones and it can be hard to keep track of how many animals you have and what they need because there is no organized overview of all your animals.I still very much enjoy the game a lot, but I think it needs some QoL updates to really shine.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the game but I cannot recommend it, freezes on me on a daily basis.I'm playing on an older gaming laptop, that runs Hogwarts legacy and I feel this is a less graphic \ memory intensive game so I find it unacceptable.EDIT: Set cursor to system profile, FIXED the issue. TRY this game on saleThere are some game play issues as well that sour the game experience. Cost of buses are way too high, stalling progression.Events way too close to each other in the beginning, which gets you with taking on loans, however the game fails to give you a second loan and just gifts it to you or fails to do anything about the event and it blinks out of existence? You can't decide the gender of the animal you clone --unfairEnclosure shape editing is a pain, I wish I knew the tile size.And other inconsiderate and non intuitive things, like unable to pay off loan in advance, failing to mention there is no interest on said loans. There is absolutely no explanation on building optimization and how it works. Internet to the rescue, where you learn that multiple benches in a single square area hurt this score, but a single bench will make your costumers whine about inadequate resting stops.Employees getting bonuses but work ethic declines still, stats are seemingly irrelevant, and only level count matters as I see things, but I'm not sure as the game keeps you in the dark. Once you have nutritionist and cullers you'd really really want to skip days, but no you have to sit thru whole days without a skip button or a decent speed up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly cute game, and well worth the asking price. This is a worthy successor to the tycoon games of old. The morality system is both adorable and amazingly fun.There's seriously a lot to love about this game, it's cute and a lot of fun.Criticisms:The late game does leave some to be desired - maybe I've been spoiled by other simulation games, like Dwarf Fortress or Civilizations. Management of pens and sectors after you get more than... 12? Becomes really tedious. I wish I could assign a manager to automatically add entertainment items, water bins, and release animals after I get more than X males or something. The UI is manageable in the early game, but after several rows of unlocks it becomes really difficult to find the right items or layouts you're looking for.Speaking of layouts, a copy/paste feature for layouts would be an amazing addition. _childDocuments_.review: It's finally here!I have been waiting for this game for quite a while now- played the demo, and now i have my hands on the full release. Absolutely not a disappointment so far!This is a zoo tycoon type game. Compared to the other one I play- Planet Zoo- it is much friendlier in a few, key ways;No inbreeding management to worry about, and the more important one; This might not sound like a big deal, but as someone who makes a huge mess out of every first zoo and has to clean up the spaghetti paths, wonky enclosures and nonsensical design, this is a lifesaver. Other takeaways I've noticed so far:The UI is pretty clean, which is important in this type of game.The gameplay is simple, but not shallow- there is a large tech tree, incentives to find subspecies through breeding and trading, a morality system, and tasks. The devs are incredibly responsive, answering questions and responding to feedback (and seems to be a running theme for games published by no more robots, which is lovely) There's animal splicing mechanics. You can make a giraffe-goose. Please make a giraffe-goose.I would recommend this game to anyone who likes zoo-tycoon type games!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I wasn't sure how much I was going to like this but bought it because it was on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Game becomes very repetitive very fast. After completing the first 2 species variations completely, you've basically seen everything. Unlocking new stuff is very slow (as researching new blueprints is not very linear or transparent so you might be waiting a long time until you randomly get the blueprint you need) and if you have bad luck with the blueprints, you're also barely able to make enough money to upgrade. And in order to get new species, you need to unlock specific variations through breeding which is also very slow. NPCs are also constantly mass-spamming symbols so that at times it's really hard to see what's going on where.It's also annoying that you cannot sell animals while going through the "good" path, you have to pay to get rid of them if you don't wanna lose your "karma" (which you need to unlock certain buildings).The dinosaur DLC is much better built, because it completely skips the variant mechanic and new species are unlocked by hiring more researchers. It's also way easier to make money early on than in the normal version.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has adored playing tycoon-style and management games for most of their life, this one caught me by surprise. The gameplay itself is very relaxing and, although there are many tasks to be performed, I have never felt overwhelmed by them. You can definitely play at your own pace and take your time to enjoy everything this game has to offer - which is a lot. There is a lot of variety between animal species, tasks, and scenarios during which player must make a choice; all of which makes for a dynamic experience. I've also realised I prefer the 2D style of the game to some other 3D ones, as that aspect tends to add more complications which leave me not wanting to play. Overall, this game has quickly become one of my favourites, due to its adorable artstyle, relaxed gameplay and cute animal noises :3

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great little pixel game to play. It's kinda .  There are lots of cute animals and buildings in the game. There are around 30-50 animals and each have 8 or so variants each. There are also lots of types of buildings, trees, tiles, animal pens, food places, etc. For a developer I've never heard of, their skills are very promising and they didn't release a half baked game like most AAA companies these days.The devs have put in enough features where it is unique enough than the comparable games. The art and pixel style are well designed and there are plenty of ways to optimize and expand your zoo, which gives it lots of repeatability. The devs are active and responsive to players and release updates pretty frequently. While there are still some bugs, the game is overall pretty solid and will likely run quite well, even on lower performance machines.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so much fun i am addicted. its like zoo tycoon with a really interesting twist. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled by the art style, this is not a game for kids. There are surprisingly a TON of moral choices to make that affect the look and progression of your zoo. I've only scratched the surface of what is offered in the 1.0 release, but suffice it to say, I'm hooked and look forward to the different things the developers may add to the future. Since the art style is seemingly simple, there are 10 options for every animal "style" For example. 10 kinds of rabbits, hares, etc, 10 styles of horses. donkeys, zebra, etc, 10 kinds of monkies, etc. and they are based on rarity. Every animal type has a breeding progression that is based on what skin the mother and father have, and with each successful offspring increases the chances for rarer breeds to pop up. The management system also has a wiiiiide variety of options that can lead you to growing food to supply ingredients for hotdogs, popcorn, etc you sell to visitors, or meat supplied from euthanized zoo animals to be fed to other zoo animals. It can get pretty dark from the little bit that I saw (trying for a morally good zoo right now). The base game is chock full of things to do and discover, so the future looks bright for this zoo builder game!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I like that it doesn't require a lot of time spent on building like in other games, and yet you can still get something that looks rather nice.  It's a great game for when you don't have a lot of time to spend, and you just want to put in like 20-30 min at a time (enough time for a couple days in game). The fusion of different animals is rather simple, but is still a fun theme to play with once you unlock several of the genomes.  However, this is not a game that can be completed in only a few hours. To reach 100% completion in this game will easily require at least 200-300 hours of time.  Even then, that depends on what your definition of complete is. If you just want to unlock all of the genomes, then it will still take a decent time investment to unlock/discover all 10 varieties of each animal genome, which is a requirement in order to use them in fusion experiments.  So, in summary, I think this is a great game that is rather relaxing to play. The controls are simple to understand, and you can easily spend either several hours at a time, or play in 20min sessions.  The animals are cute to look at, but breeding is based on percentages, so some level of chance/luck is involved when it comes to discovering new genomes.  Overall, I would definitely recommend this game to other players, especially if you are looking for something that is management based, but doesn't require quite as much brain power as other games in this category do.

The crew posted updates on the development weekly, so I was extremely excited to see the game finally finished! Boy, the game does not disappoint. It's the pixel zoo tycoon dream. _childDocuments_.review: I loved this game and I'm probably still going to keep playing it but man..This game is so cute and I love the concept. Everything is great for a while but everything slows down so drastically when you reach a certain point. Researching takes forever and it's not organized in any logical way. It took me so long to find the fries shop.My enclosures are giant so I can try to get all the variants but it's becoming a tedious overpopulation problem, my zoo keepers aren't able to keep the pen clean even when there's multiple only focused on one enclosure. I guess I could make multiple enclosures for the same species but that takes up a lot of space as well and overpopulation would still be a problem. Decorating becomes a huge pain. You unlock better things as time goes on (this is fine) but moving around a million tiny plants is miserable. Not being able to select groups of items drives me crazy (the same goes for the floor options). The path finding drives me crazy. Why are my visitors choosing to walk on the dirt over the path that I made for them? It makes them slower and they get tired faster. The same goes for employees taking weird roundabout paths.When you make a shop the game forces you to hire a random employee that more often than not has terrible stats. It doesn't do this with zookeepers when you make an enclosure. Firing and hiring employees is a pain as well.Hiring individual shopkeepers has been giving me so many difficulties. When you reach a certain upgrade you can hire 2 employees per shop instead of one. Why am I forced to go through each location to hire each employee individually? Then when you hire someone, it prompts you to close the position. Say you have four pretzel shops who each need an employee. You have to go the application menu, select a pretzel shop, pick an employee, confirm their rates and hire them, then confirm that you want to keep the position open. You have to do this three more times to fill up all of your positions. I don't know if it's my computer or if it's the game but every time I hire someone the interface says I don't have any more vacancies even when I do. This means that I also have to reopen the menu every time to fix everything. I don't know if this is just me missing something, but man it sucks.Small but annoying thing, my visitors will complain about being thirsty and then won't buy a drink. I only make 20 cents off each soda and all of my shops are set up similarly. I don't even add salt to my foods. My screen is always full of drink icons.  This game was so fun in the beginning, but has become so tedious that I can't recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dangerous lmao. It's perfect in so many ways, and SO SO SO SO hard to actually quit. I always having ONE MORE THING that I need to do, but because it saves at the end of each day, if I stick around to do the "one more thing", I need to play through the next day. It's so fun, so quirky, and sometimes I actually want to experience the "evil" decisions just because they seem hilarious lmao. Second playthrough for sure. I genuinely do recommend this. It's such a fun game, filled with just enough strategy to keep you thinking endlessly about it so that you lose time and want to keep playing, but not SO much that you're stressed out and don't want ot play anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a bit too basic I expected a little more to do in this game.Automation is very limited and you will be doing boring things on a regular basis such as:1. Population control some animals breed like mad and a building researched to automate is rather bad you have no option to set amount of each animal type and species you want but rather goes off just available space which for tiny animals you need a big pen just to fit in the many enrichments and water it will have excessive space available for animals. This means always getting messages of enrichment needed, water needed. Every few days I find I have to release/transfer/butcher a heap of animals which is tedious.2. Its annoying animal food isn't auto stocked but an extra researched building to do so. Food storage starts with 7 days worth of food max which is low, upgraded to 14 later on. I keep forgetting to check supplies and get a no food warning almost every time. Animal diets can be a pain to get right as some animals require weird % rates of the 4 foods to get proper nutrition. Some sort of nutrition guide as I can hardly think hippo poo is a great part of the diet of hippos.Splicing animals sounded fun but they can't breed (or rather I never have had them do so) and you will always need to keep making more. I don't like the forced splicing prompts where you must pick one of two to do. I would rather skip on making spliced animals as its just extra effort for little returns. The timer to make some takes too long and then having to manually release it into a correct pen as spliced animals count as what their body is. Regular animals are varied enough it seems like some extra uneeded thing or I could say its too shallow to be much fun.Every section of menus have no scroll bar and don't allow mouse wheel scrolling so when you get a long list of employees its a long scroll to the bottom for new one you just hired. Early on bus transport is incredibly lacking and it seems to just force rush players research involving bus capacity so you don't buy pointless low grade busses. You will end up with 1 level 4 bus per route anything else bought is considered a waste of money.I found much of the game I sit in fast forward mode just waiting for the research to be done. I was considering playing this game through twice once in good karma mode and then in bad karma mode but its getting rather dull.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR it's almost a good game, but definitely needs more work until it is worth this price. A management game needs management tools.Awesome potential. Got a lot of depth. Looks cute. But it is very sorely missing that level of UI polish that makes it actually fun to play for longer than a few hours.Some things that are in the game and truly grind my gears:-Zookeepers are retarded. They often walk into an enclosure and walk straight out again, even though it is filled with ♥♥♥♥. And they then decide to walk all the way to the other side of your zoo just to do the same thing again. And their speed is absolutely sluggish. Very frustrating.-The only way to make zookeepers slightly less retarded is to zone them to an enclosure. So is there a list of employees where you can click multiple keepers to zone them to an enclosure? Nope, ya gotta click em one by one and micro them to the enclosure you want. There is a list tucked away in the heat maps, but still no way to select more of them at once; you have to micro every employee to certain zones.-Decorations inside enclosures cannot be walked through, even if that decoration is grass. So, sometimes, zookeepers can't clean the animal ♥♥♥♥ out of a corner, because they cannot walk through a patch of grass. Even though the animals can walk through anything, mind you. No problem, you say, just click the blocking pieces of grass and remove it? No, you have to open the enclosure, open its list of items, and then go through that list of every decoration you placed inside of it until the game marks the right one for you, then click that- going into a submenu- then delete it. On a large enclosure, I just spent two minutes going through the list just to delete a single patch of grass. No way to select decorations with your mouse. Yeah.- If you want to move animals from enclosure to enclosure, there is a list with checkboxes to move multiple at once. But... the list is unsorted, with no way to sort them. Want to remove those 3 capybara from your enclosure with 40 geese and 60 rabbits? Get ready to scroll through the whole list.The below is more opinion or taste rather than what I see as true "issues":-The way you have to manage your campaigns to get new applicants for your jobs is in my opinion very clunky and requires a lot of clicks. Makes managing your staff just that little bit more tedious.-There is a notification for "ticket price too high" and for too low, but there is no info to be found on what the regular ticket price should be. So, trial and error and looking at the menu, I guess.I could write more, at both sections, but you get the gist. If the game is updated and these things get improved/fixed, I'll definitely come back and give it a positive review, because the rest of the game seems awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Part of the appeal of this game is creating crazy stupid hybrid animals...  Or I guess buying them from the black market.(A simple but personal favorite of mine is the Snicken)Bonus points in the sandbox mode allowing the player to crossbreed among the DLC packs creating even more bonkers abominations.This game definitely scratches the "sim/build something" itch and has some decently solid gameplay.Maxing out the good/evil track helps with the seratonins but unfortunately, there are other strange optimization things for each part of your parks that don't quite make much sense, Sometimes the workers get stuck but that's okay cause you can just click on them and reset themBut I gotta say, there's just something so satisfying to watch your giant pig/elephant hybrid playfully jump and hide in a bush, completely concealing itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game, but even within my 2-hour refund window of playing, I experienced multiple crashes & bugs. The learning curve on management games is enough without having to question if you're only getting errors due to bugs.Aside from that - the number of popups is truly wild. You can't go 30 seconds without getting a fullscreen popup that pauses the game til you close it. The UI is slow to navigate and oddly mobile centric.Some more issues - Can't pause the game to strategize & rebuild (if you pause, a popup comes up and you can't do anything til you close the popup, unpausing time)Can't manually save (game saves at night only)Lack of *useful* shortcuts, namely, something to close last popup without having to hit a little buttonI love Disco Zoo and Oxygen Not Included. This game should have been their perfect child, but instead I'm just gonna follow the patch notes going forward in the hopes that this game grows into its potential over time.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a true neutral review. It's a fun game, but the controls are very jank, and it doesn't go nearly deep enough into a lot of the mechanics. Hiring people is difficult, you can't fire and rehire easily, you can't choose who to hire in some cases, the tech tree is obtuse, things like that.Some pets like some enrichment objects more than others, but to find that out you have to go find a spreadsheet on the discord, and in normal play you just end up spamming balls.Resizing and moving enclosures is too hard, popups cancel out other menus when they shouldn't be popping up at all, your rabbit population grows out of control unless you micro it even with the new building.It needs a lot of work, and I don't feel like a new DLC is the answer. Hopefully the new patch brings out good stuff, but I feel that the price right now + the price for new DLC (which will be around £7.50) is just a bit much.

It gives a lot of freedom how to decorate your zoo and animals don't need a lot of space (except bigger ones) and all entertainment/decoration is not bound to a specific species. Unlike other Zoo Simulators the game not gives you very versions of an animal. All ducks can be in one enclosure. I also like that you can combine to animals to create mutants.On the downside animal needs for entertainment and customer needs are very high. Some other stats would need some adjustment. Overall the game is not so hard and some stuff can be ignored, until you further into it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little game, but as others have said once your zoo gets to a certain point it's just a chore to try and get animal keepers out to take care of the animals, and if you don't remember to turn on contraception suddenly there's 20 capybaras in your enclosure It would be very helpful if there were a player mechanic to manually feed a starving/uncared for exhibit, as sometimes the keepers just refuse to go to the enclosure even after being respawned at the entrance It's cute and I can tell a lot of passion was in the game, but it still has some bumps that need ironed out. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Management sims need good menus and the ability to focus on the fun parts. This has neither. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: overall good experience, needs some qol improvements (mass deleting, easier staff management) and some more lenient building placements (let me put multiple benches in the same zone! i want a nice little eating area!)still very fun tho. cute pixel art, progression feels good, and i love breeding for new animal varieties :) definitely check this out  if you're a park builder fan
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cute game that is entirely held back by it's UI. You don't really notice until get to a certain size of zoo, but the interface is incredibly backwards in many areas. If you're only looking to play it for an hour or two, I might actually recommend it. Beyond that, it turns into a bit of a chore, though, and that is such a shame.There aren't really any central screens to manage your employees and animals, it's pretty much all done piecemeal and a lot of it doesn't scale well as your zoo grows. It's not that bad to manually sort through your animals and keep one of each color when you have one enclosure, when you have 5 or 10, you're reenacting Trouble with Tribbles from Star Trek. Similar thing when you want to breed animals. Instead of having a screen where you just select two animals and you're done, you first need to find your nursery in the zoo, click on it, realise this nursery already has both of it's slots occupied, find the other nursery that you built and then select your two animals. The more nurseries you build, the more fun this gets. Instead of having one screen that gives you an overview and lets you assign things, you get to manually check every single one. Bonus points because even if you set the limit to "breed once", the animals aren't sent back to their pen afterwards, they just sit in the nursery until you find them and manually send them back. And sadly, it's like this for pretty much everything you want to do. It all seems to be designed to make you click a few extra times. What makes it extra weird is that there is so much unused space on the screen, you could easily fit a dozen buttons there that could bring up all sorts of useful management screens. Instead you're hunting for doodads to click on and then maybe you'll find what you want in a context menu.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I got in moral trouble with the public for buying an animatronic lion as if that wouldn't be the coolest thing to see in a zoo.I wish there was a much better way to move/design your zoo once you really get into the game but I love this game! I love the art, the animals, the silly newspapers everything!

_childDocuments_.review: it's an idle game in disguise, if it wasn't for the one button i have to click at the end of each day, i would just let it run indefinitely on its own to earn money and research points;there is no challenge or difficulty in thismight be worth a buck or two just to see the cute! animals! just jump around! clueless!!, but definitely not worth the full price:(
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Let's Build A Zoo is charming, relaxing, and whole lot of fun. My highlights include the pixel art visuals, cute animals and crazy combinations you can come up with using DNA splicing, the games meme-style humour, and the mountain of things to research, unlock, and build. That said, the game is totally worth your time and  if you're keen for a modern take on the Theme Park / Hospital style of management game!Here's some gameplay -
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game overall. I'm a fan of zoo games and this gives some good fun with all animals having 10 variants and you can splice animals together in your CRISPR facility. With over 300k possibilities, the opportunities are really endless. I did play the closed Beta of this game before they even launched the demo. There's definitely a learning curve with park management issues that could not have been forseen in the short beta. But, the devs already have a roadmap in place. The future looks good for this game. I personally found the price point to be reasonable; however, I did buy the game with the launch discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I have played the beta and the demo over and over and bought it instantly.There are tons of facilities and items that make you just want to keep on playing to discover them.Shops and food stalls are super cool because you can customize the quality of the products you're using to get more profit in expense of karma as well as "adding extra" ingredientes, for example, adding more salt will make your visitors thirsty and they will likely go buy a drink. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Put in a few hours and it seems fun will be playing a lot more. Water distribution though actually has a radius around the water pump. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Dude what a great game. Definitely my favorite game purchase in a while. I bought this because I grew up on zoo tycoon and loved that, but wanted a modern version that was complete at time of purchase vs sold in pieces of DLC at a time like Planet Zoo. This blows my memory of zoo tycoon out of the water, and I lose track of time while playing. The breeding system is sooooo fun because of how many different combinations there is, the pixel graphics makes it feel cozy and retro, the fact that you can be an evil zoo that has a glue factory on the premises or a good zoo that breeds and releases to boost failing wild populations is a new concept and I appreciate the dark details, the employee system is better, you can customize the animal's diet for health/profit, a healthy bit of random events that are fun/interesting, the list of things i like goes on. It's done pretty well and i'm happy I bought it, probably would have paid full price and gotten it last year if i knew how much fun I was going to have. The only things i don't like are some of the default keybindings which is easily fixed and rebound, the fact that i can't just save and hop off - it autosaves at night like stardew valley so I'll finish a day and then quit when the new day starts, and how the tutorial doesn't quite explain everything but that's okay that's what google is for. 10/10 from me, I'll probably buy the dinosaur DLC and hope they come out with more. It's nice to be able to buy a DLC because the game is fun and not because I NEED more content.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I am already a big fan of zoo games but a small pixel one that has moral options?Not only could I make pigs into bacon but I could also make an adorable little ice sculpture zone!The game itself isn't the most original concept but it's displayed brilliantly, I spent so much time just figuring out what bunnies I wanted to display for my zoo. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: It's a zoo tycoon that is charming in the beginning. After hitting a medium-sized zoo, however, there were so many glaring issues with the core loop and controls that I just resigned. Many of them emerge from the bad scaling of the game:You start out with a fairly small and manageable area, and buy new land at regular intervals. That is good in the beginning to get used to the mechanics and expand while learning; but even 12 hours into my first zoo, I was still continuously buying land to fulfill quests and host more animals. A small zoo can forgive the bad game controls which force you to mouse-click through vertical menus. However, at a medium-sized zoo, you are constantly clicking through these numb menus to hire more staff/adjust animal nutrition/upgrade the enclosures/etc because, tragically, these things are the main core loop of the game, and they are only interesting in the very beginning. Now, the game feels like administrating a bunch of Windows Vista PCs without scripting, and this is the essence of why I will abandon the game.Another disappointment is the mechanics of morality and events. There are only a few of the latter and they start to cycle very early and provide positive or negative morality. Sounds like an interesting concept for a zoo tycoon as I think that zoos are inherently morally questionable. In the game, however, it feels like an underexplored mechanic and has only little impact on anything except a few late-game technologies that feel tacked on (like farming).

_childDocuments_.review: Hello friends, today I will review the game called Let's Build a Zoo. This game is a game in the zoo management simulation genre, where you build and develop your own zoo. Let's Build a Zoo is both a creative and fun game. The game's atmosphere, graphics, sounds and story are very cute and immersive. While playing the game, you both choose your own animals and try to make your visitors happy. Some parts of the game are very funny and interesting, some parts are very challenging and stressful. The difficulty level of the game is also quite high, especially when dealing with DNA splicing and animal kidnapping. It takes a very long time to finish the game.Good points of the game:-  The graphics of the game are very nice and sweet. The movement of the animals, their appearance, their reactions, everything is very well designed. The game's environments are also very varied and detailed. Cages, roads, ornaments, plants, everything looks very nice. The colour palette is also very vibrant and cheerful. When you play the game, you really feel like you're in a zoo 😍-  The sounds of the game are also very successful and cute. I recommend you to play the game with headphones, because you hear the sounds that the animals make. These sounds increase the fun and realism of the game. The sounds are suitable for both the animals and the environment. All of the voices are very well dubbed. The music of the game is also very beautiful and appropriate. The sounds of the game are one of the most important elements of the game. 🎧-  The story of the game is also very interesting and unusual. The game tells both a realistic and a fantastic story. The story of the game tells both the past, present and future of your own zoo. The story of the game tells both the fate of animals and the secrets of a lost animal species. The story of the game is both entertainment and drama. The story of the game reflects both your own journey and your relationship with other players. The story of the game is very deep and meaningful. After finishing the game, you can't get out of the effect for a long time. 📚Bad aspects of the game:-  The battle scenes of the game are the weakest aspect of the game. The game's battle mechanics are very simple and boring. You only attack or retreat your animals with one button and select your animals with another button. There is not much variety in battles. You always fight with the same animals. You don't need much strategy in battles. It is enough just to ensure numerical superiority. Battles spoil the atmosphere and fluency of the game. Battles are the most annoying aspect of the game. 😡-  The puzzle sections of the game are not very interesting. The game's puzzles are usually based on placing the animals in the right cage or meeting the animals' needs. The puzzles are not very relevant to the story of the game. Puzzles slow down the pace of the game. Puzzles are the most boring aspect of the game. 😴-  The replayability of the game is also very low. After finishing the game once, there is not much reason to play it again. The game has no different endings or choices. There are no hidden items or side quests. Replaying the game just means doing the same things over and over again. Replaying the game reduces its impact. 😐Scoring of the game:In conclusion, Let's Build a Zoo is a very cute and immersive game. The game is very successful both visually and audibly. The game is very interesting both realistically and fantastically. The game is both entertainment and drama. The play is both a work of art and an experience. The play both entertained me and made me think. The play made me happy and sad at the same time. The play both frightened and encouraged me. The play both surprised and satisfied me. The play was an unforgettable play for me. I recommend the game to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: If you like designing a zoo then sure it's a good game, you have a good variety of animals (DLC or not) and you can splice them to make fun mishmash.However, once you start building out your zoo and buying more and more land the game starts to chug very badly, and for that to be an achievement is poor oversight since you'll only be able to barely place things just when the zoo opens and closes since the rest of the hours is intense lag. You'll end up with an artificial playtime like myself since you'll spend quite some time trying to just load in your game as well, perhaps even falling asleep while waiting for time to pass so you can buy more land for the achievement, and then you have to decorate it 100% for another so that's going to take even longer.All in all, it's a fun and decent game, if they ever fix the lag problems, sure I'll give it a thumbs up but for now, no just no.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game enough and I can't believe I haven't rated it yet. I've been streaming this game like crazy. Okay, where to start. Don't be fooled by the graphics. This game is clever with its events. There is some amazing writing. The management level skill is probably medium to high-level depending on how detailed of a manager you are. And I mean DETAILED. There is so much you can control. From what type of foods the animals receive, to the ingredients in what you sell to zoo guests, to wages, to where certain workers work and what types of skills they have. If you want to produce what you sell you can do that too. There's the moral and amoral routes for tech unlocking in this game. The stories behind them are so funny and sometimes shocking. If there was one wish I had it'd have, it'd be that tech trees can start over with morality when you open a new zoo.And I LOVE the dino expansion. It's like playing Let's Build a Zoo 2 and not a DLC. There is so much love and detail to this game. You can tell that the whole team worked hard. Tip:  If you are playing on a potat computer, turn layers off.

_childDocuments_.review: I do really enjoy this game because I like collecting pretty things, organising my zoo, having the option to either be a micromanager or just let the zoo run, and decorating my enclosures.I also really like trying to achieve the full 'good' or 'evil' route.However- I don't like the DNA splicing gameplay, and I hate that the game makes it mandatory.It is also a bit of a grind, it takes a loooong time to unlock each new animal type, and if you're aiming to 100% the game, collecting all the genomes takes absolutely forever.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this for a few hours offline, the time shown is low.Pigs bouncing on trampolines - what more could you want?This has tons of content and is low pressure, all in all an easy recommend. But, it does badly need a couple of improvements. You can't save on demand, you have to let it run through until the end of the day. It's 3 or 4 minutes at high speed, but sometimes I can't let it sit that long, so I have to go back and redo a day when I can go back to it. The way the UI is laid out is very confusing at first, it literally took me having to come on here to figure out how to place a water pump. It also doesn't have tool tips for a lot of elements, so you just kind of have to guess what they are.It's a good game but honestly I wouldn't have bought it and been happy with it if it hadn't been on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun management game with cute art and interesting gameplay mechanics. This game is either funny or downright disturbing at times. I highly recommend it. I bought this game because of the pixel art and the premise of hybrid animals. I don't normally enjoy sim or management games much but I really got into this one. This game is fairly accessible and can be as simple or as complicated as you want. You can just manage the zoo and ticket prices, or manage animal diets, employees, heck you can manage the food quality you serve to customers at a hot dog stand. Genuinely I was impressed with the amount of things you can manage. I won't talk much about the zoo gameplay. You can build enclosures and design them. Later you can gene splice animals that look weird but don't have much else going on for them. They're zoo attractions. You can trade animals with zoos around the world, or rescue them. I wouldn't say there's anything remarkable about this, it plays how you expect.  The thing that really surprised me about this game was the morality system. Early on someone offers to paint a goose into a peacock to scam your patrons. Harmless enough, I thought, my morality is loosely based on comedy. But this opened up  a terrible path. The evil things you can do are so damn abhorrent. You can: turn deceased animals into processed meat, siphon electricity illegally, recirculate water so everyone is drinking sewage, abuse your employees, illegally sell animals as exotic pets and so much more. It's hilarious how evil you can be. If you're good you can open a farm and recycle. If you're evil you can be a menace to society. My one complaint of this is that you really get stuck in either camp. You can be a good person and make bad decisions (and vice versa) but the buildings to each camp are limited to overall morality. If you want to siphone electricity, you lock yourself out of farming, at least early on it seems. And once you have enough morality that's good or bad it begins to snowball hard and it becomes difficult to switch sides. This game is funny, interesting, and has surprising depth. I think it's well worth the experience of playing it.
