_childDocuments_.review: edit: i still stand by this is a fun game and i have over 40 hours playing, the developers made some good changes and seems like they will make more quality of life changes. it's a fun game and i've been playing for 4 days now, but it really get very tedious micro-managing everything. and here's a list of why i don't recommend this game!-every single game day i have to click on the store room and manually buy food for the animals, there is no option to automatically buy food when it runs out! and have to do it every single game day, even though the game tells you you're buying food for  14 days! as it seems like it's buying the food for one habitat and not all of them!same goes for changing increasing the salaries of the employees.-also there is no option to type in numbers, you have move a bar which is very finicky, like i would set a number to 120, and it change it to 119. i have to do it multiple times before it actually get set to 120.-i find myself pausing the game for like 30+ min just so i make changes or else i get constantly get interrupted by "no food" and dying animals! -building roads is almost useless, since no one uses them unless every other way is blocked! like they would choose to walk slow on a dirt when there is a road parallel to the path they are taking!the game need some serious changes! so if you don't mind anything i listed above, then go ahead you will love this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Preface: a lot of my time in this game was afk. I only have about 10 hours actually playing.I absolutely love this game, but the population centre feature needs an update. Even just the ability to set a population at which to start donating would fix a major problem this game has. A massive part of my enjoyment of this game is building spacious and well decorated enclosures, but the fact that a 25 tile enclosure can hold more than 20 rabbits is kind of absurd. it also means that if you build even a semi-decent sized enclosure (around 100 tiles) you can hold pretty much infinite rabbits, and the population hub will never do anything.This issue has honestly kinda crushed my spirit. I've spent 10 hours building a decent-sized, well-decorated zoo that I really enjoy, but now I've found out that if I don't want to spend more than half my time releasing animals, I'd have to destroy all of my enclosures, and turn them into tiny, way too full enclosures. I'm not the first person to quit the game because of this realisation, and I definitely won't be the last if you don't fix this.Tldr; The game stops being fun at around 10 different species, since you have to manually release animals like every 10 minutes, and the feature meant to deal with this only works under absurd conditions. Until this is fixed, expect to be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game! Fun, cute, and addicting. Some problems slightly annoy me; otherwise, bearable ones. Things that annoy me are the heat maps that get displayed if you are trying to place down a rubbish bin somewhere on the map. The orange blinds me, and sometimes I have to exit out of selection to try and visibly remember where to put the bin before being promptly blinded again. Though, it's no biggie. Another thing is the UI. Pressing 'B' will open up the build menu, but pressing B again will not close the menu, though it's no big deal. It's just more efficient if they made it so that it can do that. And I hope that the developers will enable the setting so that hotkeys can use the numbers on the keyboard, as it's only set to allow letters. Though once again, it's not a big deal. I'd like to say I'm just being extremely nitpicky; otherwise, I highly suggest this game to those who want a cute and fun zoo simulator.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. I have a fair few hours in this game at this point and while I recommend it, it is not without it's issues.On the good side of things the game scratches the itch of wanting to play Zoo Tycoon. Yes there is Planet Zoo, but Planet Zoo feels like a completely different game than Frontiers flagship Zoo Tycoon. Let's Build a Zoo scratches a very similar itch.It also has added mechanics in that you can have a farm on your zoo where you grow your own produce or make vegetarian meat substitutes for your animals, as well as many other things to make your zoo more sustainable. You can also do hybrid animals and create a bunch of weird spliced together creatures.The game is the kind of micromanaging that just kind of teeters on the edge of being a bit much, but is still very fun.The overall design of the game is great. I love all the animals in the game. Their sprites are adorable and their interactions with toys are great.Overall for the price this is a decent little game to pick up if you like the genre. However... on to the bad because I have a lot more to say about the bad. Not in the sense that there is more bad than good... just that I have more to say on it.1) The UI in this game is TERRIBLE. There is no way that I've found where I can see all things happening in a subset of buildings and manage them in that one spot. You have to manage things on a building by building basis. Planning out specific routes for employees is a NIGHTMARE because again, you can adjust zones form one screen. You have to click on each individual worker... which takes you to a new screen... and then adjust it. The UI is just a mess in the sense that you will spend more time clicking on each individual building than you should ever have to. There should be just like... a screen that has all of the janitors and from that screen you can adjust zones and stuff like that. I shouldn't have to click on each individual for their own pop up screen to control this. There's also no way to filter a lot of things. Like I can't filter my animal feeds to see which animals have poor nutrition so I have to scroll and hunt down new animals. There is also no way to move an employee from one building to another. If you decide to get rid of a building all employees in it are fired. You can't just pick and choose who you want. When you build a building you are stuck with whatever employee you randomly get upon building and the only way to get rid of them is to fire them and either pay severance for an employee that never worked for good points or don't and take evil points. Just... an INSANE amount of UI issues.2) I just in general hate the idea of the "evil zoo". I don't like that it's even an option. The game kinda pushes this whole eco friendly thing, that I love because that's what zoos do... but then you have all these really gross evil options like having a glue factory. Then some things that are considered evil that I don't think should be. Like having a plant where you can butcher livestock animals. Something I think should be a thing for your meat eating animals as realistically a zoo isn't going to be making plant based meat substitutions for their carnivorous animals. Another thing that makes no sense is when I'm docked points for letting an animal die of old age in my zoo. I never released them back into the wild for conservation because realistically when an animal hits a certain age they shouldn't be released because they won't have the skills to survive and they won't be able to procreate. At that point it's better to keep the animal around and let them live out their life safe at the zoo. Yet somehow it's better for my zoo if I take an elderly animal and yeet it into the wild when it's been in my zoo all it's life. I feel like the game would be ten times better if the whole bad good thing would be tossed and just let their be a normal zoo. I also really don't like that their are achivements tied to doing an "evil run". 3) This one is short and sweet.... peacocks are all males in design. This will never not annoy me. Peafowl and Peacocks look completely different. The females don't have the colorful plummage. You put so much time into these animal designs and you couldn't be bother to make your peacocks right? Really?4) There are graphical problems that get frustrating. Such as little lines that go across the screen as you move around the screen. If you place an enrichment item and then place a decor item like a tree in front of it then the enrichment item will hover on top of the tree.5) The AI for your workers is AWFUL. I had a nice sized farm and I just watched while my farmers and food processors just ignored full crops that were ready to pick and let them die. On that subject the fact I have to unlock the ability WAY late game to allow me to have more workers in one building is ridiculous. I hate that I have to spend an intense amount of money to have more land to have a bunch of unnecessary buildings in order to have more of a worker type I want because for some reason only one worker is in each bulding... just to later have to delete all those unnecessary buildings once I unlock the ability to have more.6) The game is frankly awful at explaining anything in the game. It took me a while to figure out that I needed food processors not farmers to pick crops for instance. I also have no idea if I am putting in the right values for produce I want held back for my animals because the game does not tell you how and then on top of that the amount of each thing my animals eat is given in percentages and that's by each animal not overall. Then for some reason IN the processing building it doesn't have percentages as the value for how much I want to be saved. Once you get passed the "build exhibit, add animal" part of the game and get into the rest of it. It gets real confusing because the game explains very little.7) The hybrid thing is a neat idea and adds something new... but I don't really understand the point. It doesn't seem like it's ever done my zoo any good to do this nor help with conservation. It seems like a nothing mechanic that could have added something really cool but is just kinda... there for no reason.8) You need WAY too many lamps for a 100% lighting score in an area.Again. Overall. The game is fun, it just has some GLARING flaws that need addressed that are basic gameplay things like UI and AI issues and a decent tutorial. How they got one DLC out and are working on a second before fixing something like this I don't know. Strictly because of how much I hate the UI I wouldn't recommend spending more than $15 on this game because frustration may outweigh your fun.

The names of the animals constantly make me smile and laugh. I love the inclusivity in the game of rainbow/LQBTQA+  items to decorate the zoo with. _childDocuments_.review: As I'm sure is the case with any newly released game there are still some details that could be improved or added. That being said, I absolutely love this game! At first glance it looks pretty simple, with the small pixel animals, and I didn't really know what to think of it the first time I started the game up, just a few days after it was released. However, as I soon discovered, there is a lot more to this game than meets the eye. With morality as a big part of the game and the ability to splice animals to get ... interesting looking hybrids that have the body of one species and the head of another (some actually manage to look quite decent. Others look like failed experiments from a mad scientist. At least in my opinion anyway) this is a zoo game unlike any other I've played before. Personally I love the way morality is used to affect gameplay and influence what you can and can't build (though there have been days that I wished a middle ground was possible where you could build items of both good and bad morality in the same zoo and keep both items working) and I love how they put some humour in this game with stuff like certain critical/morality choices and visitors' reactions to certain things. Who says managing a zoo has to be serious business, right?Another thing I think this game has going for it are the developers/ people in charge. They seem very nice and involved in their community and they seem to care a great deal about their game. From what I've seen they do their best to help everyone who needs it, whether it's with a bug, game suggestion, or just random questions about the game.I would definitely recommend this game, and hope it will continue to grow into something even more amazing than it already is now.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game... with some caveats. 7/10. It floats. Sometimes, it's a 6/10, sometimes, it's an 8/10. So, with certain points, I'll give a mini score for that individual aspect of the game.Greats: Look, it's a zoo building game and at 65 hours, my first zoo hasn't finished it's first year, but I'm making bank and it's great. The morality system is amazing, making you decide to be a Good Zoo or Evil Zoo (10/10 feature). It's just hilarious what some of the options are and what rewards you get out of them. The research system is simple, fun to explore and discover "what is that enclosure item over there? I should head that way!"(8.5/10 feature). I love these sorts of games, I get really into them and with 65 hours at it's price point, I can't NOT recommend it. I've gotten my money's worth.But: time for my negatives, my caveats, the "oh that's wasted potential or just... really fault decision making".If you're like me, with over 60 hours in a game because you love to design, love to make it look awesome... and you love theming to decorating the zoo you own, this isn't... that deep or extensive, or even balanced. For example: There's 3 packs of "wild west" decoration (each like 2 objects pieces), 4 winter-type plant packs(also only 2 objects a piece), but anything savannah? It's all desert, and the decoration items are just Egypt. The whole of Africa: Egypt. Pyramids in your savannah. I can decorate my entire zoo like a winter wonderland or a farm, but Africa is only Egypt in the eyes of the decoration packs available. And this just feels particularly strange. It takes research points to unlock the decoration options, but it's lacking. I've gotten through the entire research in the late game, looking for deco. There's tons of insane (but fun) rainbow options. Nothing Africa savannah unless it's pure desert, and then you're sharing with the Aztec theme. (3/10 issue for those who love designing their parks)And there's the fact that animals don't care at all about decoration. A lot of empty enclosures stuffed with water troughs and toys, but not a single tree. (1/10 feature)There's also strange bugs. Building enclosures will bug next to the subway. Move subways before changing up an enclosure. Keepers randomly think an enclosure is blocked. (I don't normally judge on 1-3 bugs. They're there, you learn to work around them, and hopefully, fixes come)Other things:Population management is severely lacking, even with a new population management system building that does -very- little (it only donates elderly animals if there's no space left in an enclosure). Animals breed almost too quickly in a lot of cases and they do so non-stop. I guess the simple solution would be: If space is full, no breeding, but even that won't help. You can fit 300 rabbits in a tiny space and then you get into water and enrichment issues, but they'll keep breeding. It would be great if there was a "toggle contraception IF..." and list options: No enrichment available, no water available, no space available. This is what the population management center SHOULD do. Instead, they force you to sink a ton of time into the micromanagement of populations. This is fine with 5 species. This is okay with maybe 10. I'm at 15-16? It's tedious and it sucks the life out of the game later on. I worked REALLY hard to hunt down the population management center and it hasn't helped me.... at all. It's completely a waste. Don't bother. (1/10 feature.) This is a pure disaster to force tedium and length game time, even when you should be well beyond it through research. at 65 hours into a game, I shouldn't be handling this. This is the point where the game needs to be automated for those who make it this far. I see the forum discussions going "well there's ways to deal with it!" Look: I should be rewarded as a player for going this far into the game. I'm not. I'm punished for having animals and growing my zoo. I don't even know if I want to try and get every species but I have to if I want to have a real sandbox experience.And the sandbox discussion is a total thing: it is locked behind the story game play and it will only have the unlocks YOU have. At 65 hours, I'm not even halfway there! I'm sorry to anyone who loves sandbox. I personally don't mind it not being an immediate feature, but I wasn't expecting to be 65 hours into the same without everything, so... now I'm wondering if I'll ever get there and it'll be worth it.If none of my issues apply to you, then have at this game. Even with that laundry list of problems, I recommend it. Some of the systems are really fun. Some are not well thought out at all. It really depends on how much you want to get out of it in different areas of the game.(and I genuinely hope the developers see this because all of Africa =/= Egypt and a player shouldn't feel punished at 65 hours of game play. Come on!)

_childDocuments_.review: There's so much potential, but it's all wasted through the awful U.I. and compatibility issues. Want a game with text so tiny you cannot read it, no matter what settings you adjust, unless your face is less than a foot from the screen? Want a game where you spend most of your time trying to figure out a nonsensical and unpleasant U.I. -- often to the point of forgetting what you were trying to do in the first place? This is a game that feels like an Alpha demo, not a finished product, and it breaks my heart because the concept and the art style and the themes are marvelous... But this isn't worth $10 as is, much less the $20 they're asking!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a no from me. The game is too colourful and too bright. It’s really distracting and in the long run makes my eyes very tired. It also makes the game look very chaotic. UI is unfortunately very clunky and simplistic. Hiring and managing staff is chaotic and confusing. Other managerial activities are difficult to operate also. The font they are using in the messages and menus is a bit blurry and a notification menu is unreadable. The graphics and animations are nothing to write home about but I expected that. I liked splicing the animals and cross breeding them. That’s probably the only thing in this game that was interesting.Fortunately Steam refunded my purchase and I was able to get my money back. I won’t be picking this game up again.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best and most memorable games I've had the pleasure of playing! There is an astounding number of animal species, variations and combinations included in a cute pixel art style. The moral choices is a unique and engaging mechanism that you don't see often in tycoon games like this. There are still a few minor bugs that need to be ironed out (nothing game-breaking) but I am sure the devs will see to them. Overall, it is well worth the money, especially if you're a fan of the zoo tycoon series or Planet Zoo. I am looking forward to spending many more hours expanding my animal collection!

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun the first twenty or so hours! As a conversation with a friend went:Her, seeing me on the game: i wanna build a zooMe: I let the mafia hide a corpse in my hyena exibit.Her: i'mHer: WHAT KIND OF ZOO IS THISMe: 8]But after a while, it just becomes a matter of blasting through the days to earn unlimited amounts of money and getting enough research points to unlock the next shop/decoration/exhibit type/whatever while breeding animals to be able to trade them for another animal. The little quirks are your morality. You can have a good zoo or an evil zoo, evil including killing all the animals in an exhibit to stuff robots in their skins so they live forever and save you money on food, and good involving recycling and farms. There are no scenarios or goals to reach for an end-game win. You just keep playing forever. Overall, a fun experience, though! I had fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME!!! it's a really good mix between a good ol' simulation / business management game, but also has morality points and different upgrades based on routes you choose, plus it's a collectors dream since you can splice animals, mixing and matching to catch 'em all kind of thing.the only little irk i have is that some of the mechanics of the game are not fully explained, with a lack of tutorials or information. usually wouldn't be an issue because surely you can look up your questions online or on the wiki right? WRONG. there are barely any informational pages about the mechanics in this game - i actually had no idea how much i relied on online forums and stuff until it wasn't available omg. 70+ hrs and i still don't understand how the vending machines or farming stuff works, or what the symbols above the customers mean, or why the lines to my stores are out the door. the bright side is im still thriving i guess even without the knowledge? but i'd still like to know :(either way, still a really cute and good game. hopefully the more people that play, the more populated the wiki and stuff will become (please fellas)edit: I have one other little thing to mention which I wasn't originally cuz I thought I was just bad at the game but after reading others reviews it looks like I'm not alone - the bigger your zoo gets, the more you unlock and the more you progress, the game actually gets harder in the sense that there is WAY more micromanaging to do but not enough upgrades to actually help with them. I end up spending my entire day just on the breeding/splicers and that leaves me to forget to check the adoption thingy, if a streamer comes in, a health inspector, etc. it just becomes too much to do :( again though, very very cute and enjoyable game, I certainly had a blast with my 80ish+ hours, but something to keep in mind for a future game i suppose!

_childDocuments_.review: game is very fun, a lot of micromanaging if you are into something that keeps you busy for a while, although there is a point where there isn't much to do but wait for the devs to drop something new. for me it was 30 hours in, now im struggling to continue, that's just cuz im lazy. i really liked the game though, im going to replay heavily when the new dlc comes out. the game is unique in giving you a different concept. people complain about the managing but it is realistic. u have to hire people manually in real life and care for your animals to help them feel happy living with you. all in all a great game.

_childDocuments_.review: The UI needs too much work. It's hard to find overviews that you need, and even when you know where they are it takes so many clicks to get to them. There is so much micromanagement, none of it can be automated. In simcity games if you build a city well enough it can run itself, here that is not possible, you have to micromanage the same things on day 1 and on day 999. _childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Has everything I want from a zoo game + some unique mechanics that add to, instead of detracting from, the experience. I really appreciate that the variant animals are different species/subspecies/colors/poses instead of being like...hats or scarves, and I especially appreciate the ones that are based on real animals/colors. It's a good way to include more species & not have to pick just one for a broad type (example: instead of Generic Hyena, or being forced to pick just one and everyone who wanted a different one is SOL, there's spotted, striped, brown, aardwolf & a few variations of each!) The breeding mechanic is also very fun, as someone who loves breeding mechanics & genetics (even when they're wildly unrealistic lol!)My only complaint was going to be that it has no sandbox mode, but it turns out - it does! It's just hidden! Here's how to play sandbox: >start a new game>name your zoo "FreeZooBuild" (no "s) >play the tutorial til the in-game day ends>go to the map (top right), switch to "transport" (top left), & you will see in North America a free zoo! >"buy" that free zoo & go there>play the rest of the in-game day; when it ends, you'll be taken to sandbox modeYou can name your new sandbox zoo whatever you want :) Thanks so much for this feature devs, I always prefer sandbox in building & management games and now I can enjoy all the animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: Starting out is very fun and interesting, but as you get later in the game, managing so many animal enclosures is tiring and you can't focus on expanding the zoo further. If there was more automation late-game & easier inspection of employee stats without manually opening and inspecting each and every individual, then it'd be more about the fun of growth and less about the annoyance of having more crap to deal with.-Employees/HiringThis was my biggest complaint.Hiring new employees is ridiculous at times since you can't inspect the new candidates until you have an open spot available for them, AKA you have to fire your employee and take the risk of picking up somebody new who you can only judge from lvl (not work ethic). plus aforementioned inspecting all of your employees manually, one-by-one takes literal in-game days. When I had 100+ animal caretakers/janitors/shopkeepers, it felt like a waste of time finding the lowest lvl employee(s) to fire. Also for each store, you had to hire a shopkeeper for that type of store respectively. (The dude in the hotdog stand can't work in the fry stand). So you have to hire shop-specific shopkeepers for your 10~ different types of stores in the zoo rather than just firing and hiring them all as universal shopkeepers.-Animal overpopulationThere is some animal population size building later in game, but I saw no change in all in my enclosure pop-sizes. The animals just bred till all their space was taken up and I had to manually donate all my overpopulating animals just like usual. I wish there could be some easy tick of a box on my enclosure to automatically donate/release animals when a set pop-size is met. You can just prevent them from breeding with a check box, but if you forget you've done this, they'll get too old and become infertile then the whole species dies and back to square one.-After thoughtsAfter unlocking almost all the upgrades, I feel burnt out about running the zoo when expanding it felt like micro-managing more and more. If you're looking for a real time sink, look for something else probably. Fun for a while, but the end-game just doesn't feel rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s Build a Zoo is a fun strategy game, by developer Springloaded and publisher No More Robots, where you work to build your own Zoo. You play as the owner of a brand new zoo that you get to name, it's your job to manage and run the property the best you can. From researching new things to put into the zoo, to discovering new animals, there are a variety of ways to play and set up. It’s also your job to higher staff and manage the prices of tickets and food, really immersing you in the fact that pretty much every aspect of this zoo is relying on you to run, which can and will get hectic at times. Overall there is a lot to do and discover in this game.When you first start the Let’s Build a Zoo, you get to name the zoo you are building; from there the tutorial tells you how to complete tasks, as well as how to build enclosures and get animals for the zoo. Early on after you get your first animals and everything, you get introduced to a research system where you can unlock a variety of things to help the park run, from decorations, to food and gift stands, and even farms to grow your own food for the animals. On top of that, as you go, more animals will appear in the shelter where you can buy them for the zoo, as well as other zoos around the world that you can trade with to get new animals. All in all, one of the main things I can say about Let’s Build a Zoo is that it has so many things you can do and discover, so many animals, research, decorations, transportation, and even a gene splicer where you can create entirely new animals. It makes it so that not only can you spend hours on one game but so that you can replay it differently every time, from how you set it up, to the morality of it all. Speaking of which, one of my favorite mechanics is morality, you’ll be given prompts where you decide whether to take the morally wrong option or the right one, which will change how your zoo runs. It’s a very interesting mechanic.This game, while has a lot of stuff to do, gets cluttered and hectic quickly. The tutorial is quick but also doesn’t give enough information, to where especially in the earlier stages I was just clicking around unsure of what I was supposed to do. One of the most annoying mechanics is the feeding mechanic of the animals, for one you have to hire zookeepers and zone them to different enclosures, from there you have to stock the storehouse with all the food for them, then the zookeepers will bring the food to the enclosures. By itself seems pretty straightforward but not only are the zookeepers really slow about their jobs, you can only have one storehouse, which becomes problematic as your park grows because of how long it will take zookeepers to get to the enclosures from the storehouse.There are also a few bugs especially with the placement and use of objects. Sometimes, the zookeepers will get stuck or can’t find their way to the enclosure even if there’s nothing actually blocking them. Also, at times, something that is already placed will start flashing as though it’s overlapping something when there is nothing there. The  game is still fun and exciting but had its moments where it was just frustrating.Let’s Build a Zoo is a fun and hectic strategy and simulation game where you are the manager of a new Zoo. There is a lot to do and discover in this game, from animals, to stands, to decoration, and even choices to make that will impact the way your park runs. While there is a lot to do in the game, there are some aspects that can be annoying and frustrating, like the feeding mechanic for the animals, and the placement of objects. I’m rating Let’s Build a Zoo an 8 out of 10 for its playability and variety, even if it has a few frustrating aspects, it’s still a very fun and interesting game.

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that this game came out 5 days ago and I already put 21 hours into it (despite going to uni and studying) is probably telling enough of how much I adore this game. Despite many other games from my wishlist (and a huge Animal Crossing DLC) releasing, I was the most hyped to play this and I wasn't disappointed.I always wanted a pure zoo game, since playing Roller Coaster Tycoon 3 and always building zoos instead. Unfortunately most zoo tycoon games were rated as too shallow, repetitive, etc. This game fixes that by adding several unique mechanics such as breeding and - once you discover all 10 variations of the same species - crossing them with each other and creating all new types of animals. (They're pretty much the head of one animal on the body of the other, which is super fun)There is also a morality system and a huge skill board, so your playthroughs may differ immensely based on what skills you get and which options you take. I started with the high morality playthrough and I'm still nowhere near done after 20h. I did almost max out the research board though.This system also gives a lot of depth to the game, as a high morality player you might want to minimize your CO2 emissions, recycle your trash and start growing your own crops to meet the dietary needs of your animals. Side Quest and little events will happen frequently and especially in the beginning they might change your priorities up a lot. The descriptions of everything in the game are fun and I always check them out. So far my favorite was helping a goth kid be edgy and mysterious by opening my zoo at night. I wish he could be a VIP that just walks around my park, I love him.The few criticisms I had for the game have already been addressed by the developers and will be fixed in future updates. If I had to say anything negative that they didn't mention yet: - Other than mass releasing animals (which I'm already doing through a certain high morality building or potentially black market sellers on low morality), I would appreciate an option to put my animals on contraception that just stabilizes the population. Reproduce just enough to keep the numbers the same for another generation. Because I either run into the problem of too much reproduction - and annoyingly releasing them every few days - or all my geese dying because I forgot to check on them and take them off the contraception before they became too old. Oops. -  FIXED, but a little glitchy- A tutorial mode. I was really lost on some mechanics and I probably still am. Things like how buses work (is it better to have only large ones? Do I need small ones? Is it just a visual thing that they block the whole street or am I actually missing visitors from this?), how does farming and recycling work (why is the building underused, yet it doesn't recycle all my trash? Are my farmed crops immediately stored in the food storage? Do I need to process them first to feed them to animals?), is there a way to find certain research goals faster on the board (I got one that I needed for a rather important quest almost last..) - A few events repeat a little bit too often, which is probably not intentional I'm sure that eventually these minor issues will be fixed too, I would still 100% recommend this game if you're thinking it might be for you :) EDIT: Big update came a week after launch and fixed a few things. They already announced the next update as well! I have reached the "endgame" now, just optimizing some things and only a few trades left to own every species. Along the way I found a few more bugs and some things that are not in the game yet, but the developers seem very nice and responsive. I'll definitely keep playing once more updates come out, looking forward to it. I haven't praised a game this much since Stardew Valley, I'm basically selling this to all my friends (and even a stranger on the train who asked me about it) :)

_childDocuments_.review: On the surface level, Let's Build a Zoo may seem like there isn't much to it, but don't be deceived by this. There is much more to this game than there appears. The morality and management systems go quite a bit deeper than I had originally thought they would.The morality system in and of itself is a nice change of pace from other tycoon games which tend to either direct players into a more ethical route or where your actions have little impact on the overall game. Being able to be a champion among conservationists, a ruthless and greedy baron, or a balance between the 2 is enjoyable and offers replayability.Even with a little over 8 hours in the game, I feel I have just barely scratched the surface. I have only unlocked a fraction of the research tree, completed only 1 genome, and only have a handful of exhibits. All of these factors help contribute to a lengthy game and increase the replayability previously mentioned.With all of that said, as with anything, there are a few small flaws. Guests tend to wander all over the park and there doesn't seem to be any way to keep them on path's that have been built. The UI tends to feel clunky at times but it's not hard to adapt to. The only other issue I've run into are what I think are bugs? specifically robot animals still requiring food. Even with the few small issues, this game is well worth it's initial price. Based on what I've seen from the devs and their roadmap, I'm anxious to see what this game grows into.

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple zoo sim with a weird gacha mechanic for getting new animal variants that ends up becoming the entire game after a point. It's pretty trivial to create a zoo that is profitable since increasing your rating seems to increase both the number of visitors and the price they're willing to pay indefinitely. Your income increases much more quickly than the options available to you, however, so you reach a point where you have millions of dollars flowing in and nothing to spend it on because your stupid meerkats won't breed the specific variant that another zoo wants in order to trade you the next animal you need to do anything else. Getting that variant is just a matter of time, and since your zoo makes money all by itself, surely you can just fast forward? Well, no, because your animals breed variants you don't need at ridiculous rates that require you to be releasing unwanted animals multiple times a day in order to avoid overpopulation. 90% of what I was doing was tedious admin of breeding programs or exhibit populations that could easily have been managed automatically with a "don't let population go above x" or "keep breeding until I get variant Y" button, but the game makes you do it yourself. I released 300 geese in my 20 hours. 300! And that's just geese. The devs know this is a problem and added a way to release animals faster, but that's a band-aid on the glaring problem of the game constantly interrupting you for unfun nonsense. Oh, and speaking of nonsense, a lot of the other notifications are just wrong. I was told that my exhibits were blocked every few days even though they clearly weren't, and randomly picking up objects and putting them back in exactly the same spot would fix it. Lastly, the game brags about having loads of combinations of animals you can create, but there's no reason to make any of them. Sure, a Gooseduck is funny the first time you see it, but then you realize that all of them are just the head of one animal stuck on another and having more of them accomplishes nothing. It might increase your zoo rating, but there's no reason to care about that since it's so easy to increase in a million other ways. Hybrid animals will never contribute towards the trades or objectives that actually matter, however, and they take up space you could be using for animals that might actually help you. I never made hybrids unless the game forced me to, and then I'd just ignore the notification that my hybrids were ready so that I never had to put them in an exhibit. Let's Build a Zoo was fun for about half of my playtime, and then all the challenge drained away and there was nothing left except the tedium of the complaints above. I definitely think that this game can be fixed if the devs focus on eliminating those chores, but I have no idea if that will happen. As it is, I can't recommend a game that stops being fun so long before it ends.

_childDocuments_.review: An oddly addicting game, with a great need to 100% the whole thing. The art style is adorable, with the base game's animals having different variants with different styles of pixel art.On one end, this variant and breeding mechanic is great and can bring variety to enclosures. On the other end, I can't imagine the nightmare with breeding all of these variants for every animal in the DLC too. It got very tedious by the end, so I breathed a sigh of relief to see the breeding system being dropped in the DLCs.The morality system is fun. Outlandish scenarios to be evil are silly enough to not weigh too heavy on your choices (robot lions, robot lions!) and scoring good points can be rewarding. Good luck trying to get full evil and full good points for the achievement though, as even having a single tree on your zoo will keep you from having full evil points, and if your lions even as much as sniff at real meat, you're not getting your achievement. Multiple resets helped, but the strictness in general was extremely tedious at best.I think my favourite part was decorating my zoos though. Food squares, wonderful surroundings, making sure my guests dont go wandering around places they shouldn't be by making a thick line of weeds, it had it all.The dinosaur DLC was underwhelming. It grew into a waiting simulator to get all of the dinosaurs. The fish DLC fortunately fixed this by having boats instead, and if this game gets another dlc, I hope the animals aren't on a timer. This didn't take away the decoration aspect though, and I had a great time theming my zoos appropriately!All in all, a fun, addicting little game, with a lovely art style and an equally lovely way to create some gorgeous zoos! I'd say buy this if you're into designing zoos, rather than micromanaging one.

_childDocuments_.review: Had a gorilla called Harambe, trapped a ton of guests in the Gorilla cage, out of all the customers and the 4 gorillas only Harambe died. Great turnout at his funeral. I killed them all after.I usually don't care for simulation games, but upon hearing here that you get choices like feeding bodies to animals for the mafia, I was immediately certain that if I had to check one out, this one would be it.You see, my (now ex) wife wasn't really the type to play video games, but for whatever reason she obsessively played Zoo Tycoon ever since she was a kid. I first met her in probably 2005 when we were in high school and she passed away in 2017 and I can't ever recall a time where she didn't have it paused on her computer. She would have loved everything about this game. The Tycoon games never really appealed to me (outside of Operation Genesis and Rimworld if they count) but since she passed away l've considered picking one up from time to time in honor of her. Between work and my backlog l've just never gotten around to it. Until I found this game.Something about it just called to me. I liked the aesthetic a lot more than the old PC games and it looked like it had a lot of quality-of-life stuff not present in the old ones. It seemed pretty deep and engaging and I just had to try it. I don't know what I did to have this game suggested to me but I'm glad it was. I fell in love.I loved the game’s aesthetic. The pixel art is lovely and takes me back to my days playing Theme Park when I was younger (yes, I’m old). Really charming and the animal sprites are well made. The music is fantastic and a varied, mixed bag of styles. I even found myself listening to the soundtrack on Spotify while at work.The morality system is an interesting spin on the tycoon genre that’s rarely explored, and made for some fun twists. The general gameplay is also super fun, with the farming side of the game being a welcome distraction from the day-to-day zoo management. I also found it refreshing that the game turns a blind eye when it comes to the C.R.I.S.P.R. For some reason, not having recycling bins is a big moral no-no, but creating a walrus/owl hybrid abomination in a lab to display for profit is considered morally a-ok. In fact, the game continually pushes you to create hybrids and does not give you the option to decline.As a capitalist, I found it rather thrilling that the game goes so far in allowing the player to create an evil zoo where players can systematically slaughter the animals for profit. I love how it gives more freedoms than usual for players, and it doesn’t seem at odds for me at all with the game’s generally positive “green” message. For a German like me, the overall tone of the game felt very wholesome in most places. I haven’t been able to stop playing. Yes my zoo looks terrible in my current play through. Yes my progression is at a snails pace because I’m spending most of my time fiddling with things but I keep having a great time with it. I'm delighted at how kind this game is. We can build whilst the game is paused. We can release animals whilst the game is paused. We can move things whilst the game is paused and there is no financial penalty for it. It's a dream to people like myself who'd be otherwise overwhelmed.I like to call my current zoo Drunk Land because most of it was made without any level of thought or planning and will probably have major consequences for everyone involved. I hope to one day learn this game properly, but for now I will enjoy the trainwreck that is Drunk Land and its infinite money that allows me to make all the mistakes I want and the only people that suffer are the employees, the customers, and the animals. So... everyone except me. But I am the Great Zoo God, so their feelings are irrelevant. This one’s for you Janice. Rest in peace my love, you beautiful soul.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Love love the game! Played quite a bit. Very unique and quirky for a zoo sim! Everything was going well until my game began to frequently crash. Probably won't revisit this game for a while until I know that it's become more stable.All in all, really good game for it's price so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. From weird hybrid animals to completely customizable zoo designs, this has it all! It's not overly complicated and all of the mechanics make sense. Let's Build A Zoo isn't a face-paced game. It's very slow and methodic. I found myself staying up late choosing floor patterns for paths. However, there are some problems, of course. It can be a bit too slow at times. It's also very hard to get in-game currency. I found myself having almost no money in my bank account from just designing lights. It's very realistic but maybe a bit too much so. Overall not bad, though. I genuinely recommend this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! It's very cute. It's fairly simple but not too basic that it's boring (in my opinion). If you like Zoo Tycoon type games (or any simulation or sandbox game) you'll enjoy this. But I think other gamers will like it too!It has a satisfying gameplay loop, and once you get to the point of earning a lot of money, it's addicting to just keep building your zoo, getting new animals, completing research, etc. It has a lot of options for decorating your zoo and enclosures as well. I also really enjoy the silly jokes or characters they include - I've had a few laughs! It has a few annoying quirks with the UI and the building/decorating functions but nothing that prevents me from enjoying the game. (I also play on a touch screen laptop so that might be why I experience some of these quirks).The only other issue is that, if you don't understand how something works, there's not a lot of guides or help out there on the internet since this isn't a hugely popular game. But this hasn't been too much of an issue for me - just keep playing and you'll figure it out!I bought the DLC but haven't played it yet because I've just been so engrossed in my current zoo! Can't wait to try it out.Overall I recommend this fun little zoo game!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, HOWEVER......As someone who enjoys making things pretty and cool the sandbox mode of this game is awesome, I wont comment on the main story / gameplay because I strictly only play sandbox.I feel as the game is lacking in decoration. Don't get me wrong the items they have are amazing but if you were creating a snow specific area the decorations would become a bit repetitive. This also applies to the shops, I feel like you should be able to change the appearance of shops the same way you do with the zoo entrance, to breathe more life into areas and spaces.Another thing i'd like to note would be a "favourites" system for items like flooring / paths. I don't want to have to scroll 3 or 4 times to alternate between paths, I feel as it would be easier to favourite them and have them when you open up the build menu. ALSO PLEASE make the path tool size changeable I am tired of spending 30 min trying to cover a large area of dirt with grass. Although this is a zoo I feel like the game would benefit a lot from "attractions" not like a theme park but more experience attractions for example the ability to build a train track round your zoo to show it off, have events that you can plan and advertise like "seal show at 10AM"Have protesters rally outside your zoo fighting for animal rights if you're doing a bad route.just stuff like that !That's all my critiques this game is awesome and I love it so much.

_childDocuments_.review: Good little game, cute graph (if you like pixel art) with nice animations (have you ever seen a bunny go on a trampoline ?!) and a pleasant sound design.There is a relaxing atmosphere, without the extra precise money management that make other zoo management games sometimes difficult to deal with. You want to move this enclosure ? Just do it. Change its shape ? Just do it. No long planning ahead required. The "good" / "bad" karma point system adds a twist to a very well known kind of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I love this zoo building and management game.  As a huge fan of Zoo Tycoon 1 and 2, this game checks all most all of the boxes.  Easy to learn and relaxing to play this is the best Zoo sim I have played in years.  Lots of building options, moral choices to make and animals to care for.  If I were to be nit-picky I wish there were decorative fences, more decorations and shops in general, tutorials on using the farm buildings.  However this game has filled the Zoo Tycoon void and I do highly recommend this game if you enjoy this style of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a good experience so far and while I am already more than 30 hours in, I have not even touched on the DLC's.Here are my thoughts:This game feels very cozy, very well polished and can be very enjoyable if approached not as a race, but in a relaxing way. The amount of possibilities thrown at you can become overwhelming quickly, specially if you try to expand at a high pace. I felt the best when I opened up a new plot of land and only moved to the next, when this was fully decorated to my desire. That means lots of $$$ stacking up, but there is not rush to spend them all.I have to admit though that this sometimes feels repetitive whenever I sat through a longer session, but I got hooked again after a break of a few days.I palyed the game both with a PS controller and with mouse and keyboard. Both showed some advantages and disadvantages in the handling. Personally I liked Mouse and Keyboard more because I could maneuver through all the menus quicker and placing objects was faster too.Here is a short list of my subjectivels identified strength and weaknesses:Pros:- Controller and Mouse/keyboard support- The game loop keeps you engaged, always something to do.- You can be an ethical or totally unethical Zoo- You can farm your own veggies- The art is very cute and consitant- Great variety of unlockable animals- The variety of game assets to decorate your Zoo is big as well- Game progression is quick- The time you can sink into decorating and redesigning your Zoo is virtually endlessCons:- When beginning, the flood of pop ups and mission goals you get each day can become annoying.- The amount of water basins and recreation elements needed per enclosure are too high, leaving little to no space for decorations.- Turns very dark at night, making it difficult to place new things or expand the park.- The micromanagement can get overwhelming quickly with an expanding Zoo.- Lot of space wasted on ugly "utility" buildings, which are essential to not sink into chaos.Closing marks:The game let's you feel that a lot of developer love has been sunk into this game and they did very well for complexity this project brings with it. They have thought about and implemented many, many details, which comes along with a big amount of game design choices. A great job has been done with this game and I definitely recommend it to anyone who loves zoning out and building away for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: My wife and I have very different tastes in games we like to play.  I watched a youtuber I like (AngoryTom) play the demo for this and i knew it would work out great for us.  The city like management with fluctuating economy, heat maps for getting the best efficiency, and grid setup are what I like the most.  My wife loves the cute animals, quips by the npcs, animal mutation/ gene splicing, and decorating of it all.  Every single thing you do in the game effects the outcome of profit/loss.  Not enough decorations people leave the zoo. Not enough plants to counter your CO2 out put then you get fined. A massive research tree.  A moral compass that effects what you can do with your zoo.  Game changing choices.  Hundreds of tasks if youre a quest hunter.  It is just a well thought out and an all out beautiful game.  Thank you devs for this masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game for what feels like years. Release has been amazing. The game is just incredible. The zoo genre of games has really been stagnant with few changes. LBAZ shakes the whole thing up and drops it on its head. In LBAZ, you get all the familiar components of zoo games, such as taking care of animals, designing the zoo, working the shops, and mastering your profits, but it's also added in the idea of gene-splicing-- meaning you can make SO many different animals! LBAZ also incorporated a morality meter, meaning you can be a good zoo (think farms, eco-friendly, and expensive) or a bad zoo (think meat processing plants, cheap everything, blackmarket animals). The devs are committed to updating the game with more and more features, this game is only going to get better. If you're looking to add a new zoo game into your library, you really can't go wrong with this one!!

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely do not recommend.Tldr: game is frustrating and annoying to play The ui is atrocious, making you jump between 20 tabs to build something. Later in the game you unlock a tech that allows hiring 2 shopkeepers per shop and you have to hire EVERY ONE manually, clicking 6 times on 6 tabs for EACH shop. Who decided that was a fun experience?You're looking through menus for stuff to build? Well the game is going to close that menu for you because your employee leveled up! Yay, your stationary shopkeeper leveled his speed! And you get that popup every 2 minutes. Why do i have to be reminded every 15 seconds that I can spend my research points? Visitors will not enter my zoo because the ticket price is too high, but tickets are set to be free. Sometimes you move around with left mouse and sometimes with right mouse button, seemingly at random. Some may say those are minor annoyances but there's enough of those to the point when playing stops being fun anymore. It's kinda fun in the early stage but mid and late game is a chore. The whole game loop in those staged is add water, add enrichment, wait for money. The population hub building that's supposed to manage overpopulation of your pens does nothing so if you don't do the tedious task of removing animals manually every day, you end up with 100s of animals dead, decreasing the happiness and zoo rating.All in all its fun for the first ~15 hours, then it becomes a tedious and frustrating experience with not much going on other than trading for a new animal after 5 hours of spam breeding with 30 nurseries.This game needs some "automaton" and quality of life improvements like sliders to control population, hiring multiple workers at once, sliders on the sides of menus so i don't have to scroll for 10 minutes, letting me to chose what i get notified about.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun, and I love that it's not trying to be something that it isn't. It's a fun, simple and cute looking zoo game that gets harder the more things you have going on. I love the research aspect of it, and the natural progression of your zoo. It is hard at times, and easy at times. Some negatives: Having loans doesn't really have much of an impact on you in this game. As long as your zoo is making money, the loan will pull you down to $0, but it won't stop me from building an enclosure five minutes later because my zoo is poppin'. It makes the game much easier, but I could also do with the challenge. I also wish that there were a few QoL improvements, such as being able to check off animals we want to send to the wild without having to hit "select" each time. It could do with an entire UI overhaul.The devs seem to really be listening to the players, and even have a public trello board, which is always nice to see. I definitely think I'll get a decent bit of playtime out of this game, and frequent updates from the devs will have me coming back!
_childDocuments_.name: Let's Build a Zoo

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend it, even if I do try to change up what I'm doing and play it more as I already own the game either way.First off, unlike other zoo games, you can't really just straight up buy animals.  There's like 5 random rescues you can do a day, and I'm probably 30 or so days in, and half of them are always rabbits.  I don't need rabbit rescues, unless it's a breed I don't have, because you know, they breed like rabbits!  And it seems you can't rescue anything you don't already have unlockedOn my second play through, I got the 2 geese from a trade, and then ended up with like 5 baby males, and only the original female.  Anyone that knows anything about breeding animals, that's a fast track to extinction.Around 30 days or so in, and I still only have 3 major species.  Could have had 4, but thanks to the goose patriarchy, I only had one of the breed needed to trade for snakes, so I didn't want to do that yet.Controlling guests is a pain.  I have so many of them going around the "back" side of an exhibit, rather than staying on the path where there's things like trash cans or a restroom, also where they walk faster.Getting rid of animals, especially the rabbits popping out babies every day, was also a mildly bit costly if you're playing morally.  $25 an animal cost to you to donate them.  Alternatively you have to kill them or just let them overcrowd and die.The first time I played, I didn't figure out for a little while that I could adjust the diet to improve nutrition while I was slowly taking in things to do and how the game worked.  Fine tuning their diet the second time made the animals survive a good 50% longer, or more.  If you don't do that, then like 2 weeks in, your first rabbits will be nearly dead.Another game contributing to reminding me I wish the original Zoo Tycoon would get a modern digital port, even at its original resolution.

_childDocuments_.review: Can not recommend it enough, Got close to probably 70 hours in the base game ( time inflated cuz I forget to close it sometimes when I pass out) and I gotta say it really scratches that roller coaster tycoon 2 itch. Simple to learn, but difficult to get right. Not so much so that it's frustrating, but just enough to be engaging. The animal hybrids and skill trees along with the animal variants give you more than enough to chew on.My only complaint is there is no way yo turn down visitor density and the game can get real choppy when moving a 3x speed and fully zoomed out, making it a bit hard to do stuff when you have 5k+ visitors, this is a minor gripe, as it can be fixed by slowing the game down or zooming in a bit, or just pausing the time when you need to handle stuff.Special shout out to Mint Condish on the Let's Build A Zoo discord. My save got corrupted pretty deep in to the game, and while it took them about a week to get back to me about it, by the time they did we were able to get my backed up save file working in about 10 minutes thus saving my hard work. Now while a week may sound like a long time, I didn't receive any canned answers and got one on one help with my problem. As some one who plays alot of small indie games or even games by smaller devs in general, I haven't received this kind of one on one care ever. I was already planning to pick up the DLC but that really seals the deal for me.TL;DR Get it if you liked roller coaster tycoon, or the sims. Customer support via the discord is Triple S+

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure I would like this game when I saw it and it's reviews, but I ended up absolutely loving it! It's very addictive and fun, and so far everytime i've booted it up i've played it for at least 3 hours straight. The TL;DR is that I definitely recommend it. If you want a more detailed review, then read on.I think the main selling points of this game are it's morality system, genetic engineering, and wacky events. I  think all three of these things are very well executed and fun.The morality system allows you to choose between running a good, ecological zoo that treats it's animals and customers well, or, alternatively, a zoo which butchers and mistreats it's animals, deals with the black market, and scams it's visitors as much as possible. There isn't really a way to play both in a singular zoo, however due to how the system works, you can sometimes toe the line (i.e a morally good zoo can still buy from the black market or run a few scams from time to time, so long as it makes sure it keeps it's morality up).Another nice thing is that the genetic engineering portion is not considered moral or immoral, meaning that you can have fun with that regardless of what type of zoo you have. This is good, because in many games I tend to notice the evil routes are always way more fun, but in Let's Build A Zoo, I'd say you can have just as much fun playing evil as you can playing good.The art style, music and gameplay are all very good, and it's easy to understand the game's mechanics. You can micromanage, but it's ultimately not too complex and I would recommend it even to somebody who doesn't usually simulators. I usually play sandbox for most games, but I found this one pleasant in it's normal game mode.The typical research tree is replaced by a research grid. The research grid is not that different from a tree, but it's still novel and an interesting addition to the game. I find the research mechanic quite fun and unobstrusive, though I sometimes wish it went a little faster.Of course this game is not absolved of criticism and I do think there are a few things that could be better. Managing animal pens can be a bit of a hassle (I hear you can hire someone to do "population control", but I suppose I haven't gotten there yet). The thing is that for a lot of animals, the issue isn't even that the pen isn't big enough, it's that there isn't enough "enrichment" (=toys). This means that while a 5x5 pen might be able to theoretically comfortably house 50 rabbits, you'd need to jack it up with a ton of toys, which typically take quite a lot of space, so in reality you can only house half that amount of bunnies. This wouldn't be a big deal if animals didn't get so out of hand population-wise without contraceptives, which end up getting very micromanage-y; or just very expensive.The AI of the game itself could also be better, as often I got told my keepers could'nt have access to a pen which they'd just come out of and could 100% get in and out of.Finally I will say the AI is somewhat clunky, though in my opinion it's not that bad at all so long as you get used to it. Some notifications can't really comfortably be dismissed, so if you easily get bothered by them it might get on your nerves, but personally I haven't found it that much of a problem.I might have rambled a lot, again, I recommend this game to basically anyone. It's addictive, fun and original, and it's also accessible no matter what your skill level is.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is by far one of the best zoo simulators out there, top three for me and I'm picky when it comes to my animal games.What's about this game stand out compared to other games, its simple, it makes you feel involved. You're building habitats, making guests happy, the casual thing in a zoo game, but also factoring a morality system into the games gives you a more personal feel to this game. Do you want to be good and save the animals or do you want to be evil and make your "zoo" into a hell hole for the animals to bring yourself gain? I've never seen a zoo game bring that in before, and lets me real, if you played Zoo Tycoon, you, at some point wrecked havoc on the animals in your zoo (as well as the guests). This game makes it a reality to play nice or mean.I've gone 11 hours in this game and still have a lot left to do. The game has a slow start, makes you pick from a small group of animals and slowly brings you up to big animals. However if you happen to get stuck, the game doesn't leave to your own, they will give you another animal in the rescue to build off from. The research tree is quite large and actually takes time to get things you want, some play into the morals which can make it more difficult. But you aren't going to burn through the research tree and have nothing left to do.Something that stood out to me was the fact that the graphics in this game are just pixels, which everyone knows. But it surprised me because it's just a pixels. A lot of animal themed games heavily rely on graphics, which, if you're like me and rely on that to pick out zoo games, then its slim. However this game rides on the simple pixel art and it works really well into the game.But I won't lie when I say there are a few things that bug me like any other game, but they're easily avoidable once you figure out the game more. (Build new enclosures before getting new animals FYI)Overall, if want a casual game that's going to keep you on your toes then I recommend this game. It's entertaining to say the least. I hope it will only get better as time goes on.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who adores Planet Zoo but finds the building aspect of it a little tedious with how precise you have to be, Let's Build A Zoo suits me a bit more. It feels like a really solid modernisation of Zoo Tycoon and games like it. The morality options, customisation and general playing of the game are fun and feel good! It's a game you can easily sink hours into and even leave it running while you're doing other things for a little when you start hitting mid-late game on a zoo but that's also where a lot of issues start to crop up.Firstly, the fact the game does become mostly idle towards the end of your first story zoo is a bit frustrating. You could spend hours just waiting on getting that one variant of a lemur to trade with another zoo and then your back to square one trying to get another variant. I appreciate that's the primary way of advancing but the long periods of time of waiting, even with max speed turned on, can make the game just a touch tedious.Secondly, the population issue. My god the saying breeds like rabbits applies here. I spend most of my time in the conservation center just sending away animals on MASS. When I unlocked the population building I was really hoping for some way to set it so I would only have pairs of variants in a pen but it isn't even that. It's just that they donate the animal when it's old... That's it... It's not intuitive at all so it's a pointless building to have since I'll end up yeeting the animal myself.Thirdly, notifications are sometimes incredibly annoying. I don't need reminded for hours that I have 10 research points that could be spent... But they can't... I literally can't see anything I could be spending it on. I'm guessing it's basing it off the fact of the opposite morality stuff you won't be unlocking anyway but I'm not sure. The option to turn this off, or to set a goal of how many research points you want to gain before it reminds you would be ideal.Finally, filters are such a must for this game and there isn't enough of them. As you get near the end you will have a lot of keepers & janitors. Have fun scrolling through them all just to appoint them to a zone. An easy fix for this would be a filter to have unzoned staff at the top. That's a very simple thing. It's the same when you finish a CRISPR project and want to place a cloned animal in with the species. Good luck finding that one enclosure when you have 30+ pens all spread out. Especially for animals that look even slightly the same (looking at you horses and donkeys). It just gets frustrating. The early game is fun and exciting, it has it's points of tedium where your saving up money and trying to balance that with morality and breeding projects to advance but when you start approaching the end game a lot of that fun seeps away. It does sadly become a bit of an idle game. Speed through the day, check the adoptions, check your breeding projects and then continue speeding till the next day. Some more pop up events, notifications when an influencer is in the zoo and maybe some small crises (bad weather causing damage to pens, families complaining etc) could really add some much needed interest. I'm excited to work on my sandbox zoo but I need to finish the story first to get all the animals to fill it up, which means spending time scrolling tiktok while the game idles away.I like this game, but there's just some much needed adjustments to keep it from being a game I don't replay after a first or second runthrough. I would honestly give the game a 6/10 which feels a little disappointing to say.

_childDocuments_.review: #96  Lets build a ZooThis is one of those games that needs an in between score.  The graphics are bright, the sound is merely ok and it is surprisingly in-depth as far as the game play goes.  So why the merely ok rating?  Its really simple.  Its obvious the developers spent a lot of time polishing the game, but it just feels lacking.  Especially compared to other games like Planet Zoo.  You have a never ending supply of tasks that you have to accommodate, but the location doesn't change.  After four hours, you're in the same zoo you started in, and at this point i only have 5 different animals.  The fun comes with the Crispr machine.  You can design your animals and come up with things like a Capybagoose (a cross between a capybara and a goose).  But even this left me wanting.  You can't do it on your own until you have researched a genome 100%, otherwise you have to wait until the mission comes up and then pick one of the two options given to you.  So, it feels like a honey-do list of tasks, that never really feels complete.  It may be great for the younger crowd, but for the more experienced group, it's going to leave you wanting more and more.  And it never really gives you that more.  The tutorial really needs work( ok there really isn't one.  I was left wandering through tabs to find out how to place a water dish.  Also they don't tell you that you need to buy supplies until your animals are near starvation.)  So there is an aggravation level that really isn't needed.6/10

you can give them various toys and they'll bounce them around their enclosures, you can give them themed enclosures to match their natural habitats, none of it got particularly hard or engaging for me but the framework is there and it's a fun little nod to the idea that these things have inner worlds and not just needs bars, even if the game isn't necessarily about thatCONS -kind of inexplicable sometimes?: namely it kept telling me about new species i could get in the animal shelter and i uhhh never found any way to get there, and also putting things like water basins or balls in enclosures is under a completely different menu from everything else you can build - this part's probably just down to how enclosures seem to work as their own solid objects, but its still clunky and it still sucksmorality system kind of sucks; i tried this game out to spite another reviewer who went on this huge ridiculous rant about how it was pushing an """"agenda"""", and like. i dunno, barely? it has some political themes in it, but they're pretty toothless and to be honest i can't imagine many people disagreeing with the basic idea that we should, like. take care of the environment and each other. they did however point out that morality works to lock and unlock building choices, which is bizarre to me. i don't think you should have to maintain your commitment to animal rights for. your wind power to work??? imo it should be more like. building and using wind power Gives you morality rather than requires it, and high or low morality gives you opportunities - high morality, people make donations to you, low morality, you can make deals with the black market guys or whatever. it's not my game though and i guess it could be Interesting, if bizarre and unintuitive, for you to have to level up your good points to unlock recycling

_childDocuments_.review: Cute zoo tycoon that tries to take a few left turns that other tycoon games do not foray into-- namely adding morality and genetic splicing (and I am guessing, a whole lot more that I haven't even uncovered). I played the demo about 6 months before the release and was greatly anticipating the rollout to public and am not disappointed in my purchase or time in the game. It's a game that quickly captures your attention, it's got gatcha vibes with the popup icons and animal variations. If I didn't have to work in the morning, I could have easily gone for 12+ hours straight, haha! Well worth the purchase and time put into the game, kudos to the team, they've really hit it out of the park--erm--zoo!I am enjoying the game, though there are a few things that after 7 hours of play that I could suggest to developers at this stage:- Research Menu-- it's great that things are mixed in and it feels like a grab-bag of new items, this really hinders progress and is one of my main bottlenecks in the game as I have no idea where certain upgrades are for key advances like bus level 2- Tasks Advances-- I do like the quest atmosphere of having different people come in and ask for things to urge you on for progress, but it feels like a lot of the tasks are out of order and can be quite daunting--for example, my first week in I got a quest to upgrade the bus, but I couldn't find the research option until my fifth month in game. Some quests feel like they are stepping stones, while others feels like different planets.- Visibility options-- The only other minor thing that would be nice would be to disable the different popups after a while it gets a bit overwhelming (also cash/coin/dollar bills-- is there a reason there's three different icons for a $$ made notification from the public?).

_childDocuments_.review: While I really enjoy the far more complex Planet Zoo this game is much more relaxing to play.  Needs and buildings are straightforward and easy to understand.  I love the mechanics for restoring animals who are extinct in the wild, it is far more interesting than just releasing animals and never knowing what happened to them.  The DNA splicing feels more like a gimmick than anything useful but at least the game itself acknowledges that it is just a gimmick to attract more guests.The UI is massively easier to use than Planet Zoo but I think it could take some inspiration from Megaquarium.  Work zones should be their own thing rather than specific to each individual worker.I love the restoration of animals to the wild so much, I wish there was more to it that just releasing animals.  Some DLC that expands that aspect of the game would be so amazing!My only real dislike with this game is the pixel graphics and that is simply a personal problem.  I'm just not a big fan of retro pixel graphics but this game is so much fun that even that doesn't ruin it for me.Overall, if you like management games but are tired of them pretending that their buildings are not on a grid this is a great game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: How do I begin this review??? For starters, this game was unlike any game I’d ever seen on steam before. For a game that is so small, created by a team I’d never heard of before, this game shocked me in a lot of ways. Progression was clearly laid out in an understandable position, guides were incredibly helpful, and the game mechanics were flawless. Not only did this little 8-bit zoo capture my attention the moment I opened it, I played for eight hours straight after downloading. The sheer amount of stuff you can do, and the possibilities to do so behind endless— it pulled it all together. Aside from graphics and tutorials, the game keeps you involved. If you want an idle clicker go somewhere else, because my goodness does this game keep you busy! From animals being overcrowded, to constantly refilling food supplies, and influencers leaving bad reviews for no food reason, to the infinite amount of times I had to realize I couldn’t buy animals before I built their enclosures. Facepalm. This game is exciting. It’s riveting. It’s cute. And it’s fun. I’d recommend this game to anyone looking for an adventure, anyone looking for a hands-on storyline, and to anyone in need of some calm in their life. I hope the creators keep striving for greatness, because they certainly hit it this time.
