_childDocuments_.review: This is a collectathon style exploration game where you are taking over running an island park area that your grandma used to run. The park has gone into disrepair though and you have to clean up the park. Do repairs around the park and spruce things up. Place some tents, cooking areas, decorations, and activities.As you clean up the park you will find and unlock more areas. You'll find more things to explore. There is a touching story happening here though that ended in a way I *did not* expect. It was still a good ending though.There is... an odd bit towards the end where the game takes a weird more... I don't know. Fantasy turn? When the rest of the game is decidedly not fantasy in any way. This happens in a mine like area. Not gonna give spoilers.... but it was just a weird shift in the story. Then in that same area there's also a couple platforming areas that were INCREDIBLY frustrating. There's one spot where you have to jump that was so.... SO incredibly frustrating. It was the only part of the game that was frustrating.There's also certain questlines that were frustrating because the solutions don't feel readily apparent and I needed to look up a guide.Also... a LOT of my play time was backtracking trying to find things that needed repaired that I had missed or going back to a campsite to add something that I had missed. Because I was trying to get the achievements. So you might actually be able to beat the game in less time, but there was a lot of backtracking and it wasn't in a way that was always enjoyable for me.So.... some areas of this game were *incredibly* frustrating.Overall though it was a nice relaxing game and it felt worth my time to play. Especially since I was looking for a short game that was mostly exploratory. So it scratched a very specific itch.On a design level the look of the game and the sound design were really good and enjoyable as well.Now for the hyper specific parts of my recommendation:-If you are looking for a game to play while sick this is a great game. I played it while I was recovering from a minor surgery. I was on bed rest and this was a good game to play under the groggy effect of pain killers. It was easy to pick up and put down. It was also simple enough that I could play it while maybe not firing on all brain cells.-I played entirely on the steam deck. It ran well. It controlled well. The battery life was good on it. Zero complaints.All together this was a pretty good game with some frustrating parts that I overall recommend if you are looking for a chill game to sit down with for a few hours.If you don't like doing a lot of backtracking this might not be the game for you. I don't mind backtracking, and I did enjoy the game still, but this game got a bit much for me on the achievement hunting. Again though, I still enjoyed it. It just toed the line for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: "Haven Park is such a cozy, feel-good experience! You play as a little park caretaker, wandering around, fixing things up, and chatting with cute animal campers along the way. The art style is super charming, and the whole vibe just feels relaxing and inviting—perfect for winding down. It’s not too complicated, but that’s what makes it so enjoyable. If you’re in the mood for something calm and uplifting, this game is totally worth diving into!"
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is adorable!I read elsewhere that this game is "too short," but imo if you're rushing through a cutesy comfort game, you can't get too upset if you finish the "main story" in like 1.5 hours. Do the side tasks as they come up! Fix up the campsites! The game is a billion times more fun if you go with the flow. I also didn't find the game too grindy, but then again I like RPGs and play shovelware titles for fun. So, I may not have the most typical judgment on what is considered a reasonably grindy game and what is unacceptable.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute and cozy game with low stakes - Definitely fine for younger kids and adults alike.There are a few fun jumping sequences, but they are never unfair or feel like you get set back a lot if you don't make it. The puzzles and quests are always easy to understand and the solution is never far away - it really pays to look around on your own but NPCs will give you hints, too.The only negative point is that building something at a camp didn't work well with my controller sometimes, making me have to press random buttons/spamming X to make it work. It's a smaller point, though so I still recommend the game wholeheartedly.Absolute 10/10 cozy, casual and wholesome (love you grandma)
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often but I must say that this game is so fun and cozy to play ✧˖*°࿐One day I randomly found this and I decided to play whilst going through a surgery recovery so I was stuck in bed and I truly wished that this game lasted longer. I played it for around 10 hours (the game is shorter but I wanted to get all of the achievements) and I was so excited to wake up and play it in the mornings. So cozy and I couldn't recommend this game enough if winding down whilst playing is your thing.10/10 absolutely loved it and thank you for creating this beautiful lil game!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and relaxing game. Nothing in this game requires any sort of timing or rush (except maybe catching the fireflies). You can take your time, explore the island, and enjoy the peaceful vibes.I do wish there were either more characters, or more in-depth characters. But hey, it was still a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Wholesome, it's enjoyable gathering resources to decorate the campsites!It's very hard not to compare to Short Hike, given how similar they are -- a bird person conversing with animal neighbors, exploring a peaceful park from a top-down perspective, areas that are locked until you complete a task in another area, I think the story and environment hold up well on their own, but compared to Short Hike the writing isn't quite as masterful and charming. I wasn't as hooked by the story or the characters. There's also nothing much that's repeatable in the world after the quests are over, like fishing and racing and flying in Short Hike.I did like the different choices, like being able to customize campsites, and the soft 3d graphics! Also support for Mac, Steam Deck, and controllers is always a plus. Overall enjoyable game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: For fans of A Short Hike and Sneaky Sasquatch~ A casual park game about moving on with your life.I got (literally and figuratively) lost in this game. While some parts felt a bit repetitive/tedious, it was still easy and fun. As I gained experience and skills, the camp maintenance tasks blended in with the quirky campers requests and the general exploration of Haven Park. I never felt that anything was urgent or strictly necessary. You can take as long as you wish to progress through the game like I did or, if you so choose, you can definitely do a full run in a few hours.If I had to point out any cons... The UI was glitchy very occasionally, most especially in the menu and in tight spaces. It would have been nice if the Quests section provided a bit more information. (There was a quest that required a specific item to complete it but I had no clue how to get it; somehow I still managed to complete the quest later, having no recollection of acquiring said item.) Also, as of yet I haven't been able to complete the "Maintain the park" quest despite having all three checks for each region. A small note: I wish there was a way to pause? Pulling up the notebook still allows the day/night cycle to progress.Overall, I'm very glad I finally got to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game as part of a bundle, and one night, decided to play it on Steam Deck before going to sleep.Haven Park quickly became one of my favorite cozy games. Even though it's not long (even with all of the achievements, it can be completed in less than 4 hours) and perhaps its replayability is not very high, it is a cute and heartwarming experience, with just the right amount of everything. And let me tell you, it is the perfect game to play on Steam Deck before going to sleep.The map is just big enough for it to be a challenge with its unlockable areas, yet it's small enough to breeze through once you are familiar with its layout. If you fall down from a cliff, it's a bit annoying as you have to go around to climb it again, but it's okay as there is no fall damage or dying here.The quests are cute, and I was happy to fix the broken things on the map. I loved the main character, too.Overall, I am very content with this little game, and I recommend it wholeheartedly to anyone looking for a cozy experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and cozy game, my absolute favorite part is the fact that all controls can be used with one hand, so I can sip my tea or coffee while building up a park. The game play lasted much longer than I had thought just when I thought the story was over there was more to discover. Seriously recommend this game if you're a cozy gamer!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★☆ -  4 out of 5 StarsI DO recommend this game, but mostly I recommend it for children. This really feels like a children's game more than a cozy game, and while there's nothing wrong with that, it can be a bit too unchallenging for an adult. The graphics are amazing and remind me of stop-motion animation. The camera views can be an issue - the camera was blocked by hills or mountains a few times for me. But overall, it's a cute little game, though just a warning: there is some dealing with loss of a loved one involved. If you're looking for something less challenging and just an easy, pretty short game, or a game that would be nice for your kids, I definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: --- TL;DR ---It's just so stinkin' cute...the premise, the scenery, the little waddling protagonist <3 Pew pew!This is a game for your crow-brain. If you don't love wandering around and picking up everything shiny, this probably won't be your jam. But if you like games like Littlewood, Toem, or Wytchwood, this will be an adorable (if shorter) variation on that theme :) --- More thoughts if you want 'em ---Haven Park is a 9/10 for me. I've had a hard time finding games I could get into lately, but I knew this was gonna be a favorite about 10 minutes in :)Graphics: Low poly, cohesive, adorable. 9.5/10Sound design: Bouncy, unobtrusive soundtrack. Nice sound design between different biomes. 8.5/10Plot: Pretty minimal, but the little there is is very sweet :) 10/10Navigation: This is the reason it's not a 10/10 for me. The map is reasonably big, but Flint's little legs can only go so fast...would've really benefited from a fast travel option. Jumping is also kinda inconsistent; I ran into cases where I was able to get up slopes it felt like I shouldn't have, or couldn't get up them when it looked feasible. It got a bit annoying at times since crossing the island takes a while, but not enough to drastically affect the experience. 7/10UI: Intuitive and helpful. Only slight gripe is the "Quests" page of your notebook only shows the quests you've discovered, so I ran into a case where I'd finished the game and checked everything off my list, but I didn't get the "Completionist" achievement because there was a quest I hadn't found yet. A counter at the top (e.g. "13/15 quests found" or some such) would fix this. 9.5/10Overall, this is a ray-of-sunshine, low-stress gem of a game. And the fact that it seems almost exclusively done by a single dev/artist is really impressive!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I mainly only play cozy games and I thought I would love it. I still finished it, to a level but it wasn't the most fun. It's not bad. It's okay, some might find it quite fun. It's a cute and slow-paced game. But first of all, I didn't like the controls and the physics?, moving with a keyboard in this game felt a little slippery. It's supposed to be joyful and relaxing but it sometimes made me anxious just because of the controls. All you're supposed to do is unlock parts of the map, gather some stuff and build stuff. It gets a little repetitive to be honest, maybe every camps could've had their own tasks and unique characters. It's a very cheap game so I don't think we are supposed to expect much but I would love to have some interesting characters all along.  I find our character quite cute, but sometimes I press a key accidentally and it makes some sort of a noise. It started to get on my nerves after a while. I know it's very specific but.. So it's a good game, just not my cup of tea I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cute and the artwork is amazing. This is perfect if you want to relax and hangout. The story is cute and some of the dialogue made me chuckle a bit. If you are going for 100% completion, make sure you pay attention to all the dialogue and learn the map. Also, there are some audio reliant parts so listening to music while playing is not recommended in the later parts of the game, plus the soundtrack is good anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: 100% the game in 8 hours and they were some of the best hours of my life! There's a super cute and fun campsite customization that gave me way more freedom than I had gone in expecting and the little world and quests are adorable. The story is very short but sweet and I thoroughly enjoyed every second playing this game<3
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: What's not to love?Great sound /music, sweet (if very simple) story, adorable design and lots to do around the island!I played for around 7,5 hours to get it to 100% (and took my time designing the parks and such)I see myself playing this through again in a few months time.Worth it's money for sure- Pew!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely and short game, worth the price on sale to finish in a weekend. My partner and I enjoyed exploring the park and designing the camps, and were impressed with the level of polish. There are very few bugs, and surprising attention to detail in some parts that really delighted.Also, it has been said in other reviews but this game is really not a clone of A Short Hike, but I think scratches that itch if you were looking for more in this genre. While similar thematically and the developer saying he took inspiration from ASH, this game is fundamentally different. I saw in another review that it is more akin to a game like Spiritfarer which I think is right. They share cozy exploration elements - but does that make something a clone? I think the genre is so small and emerging there is room for both. ASH is a platformer with (relatively) tricky/satisfying maneuvers, and HP a crafting and checklist game.I know some non-gamers who had difficulty with ASH's controls, and I actually appreciated in HP that I didn't need to worry about falling off cliffs very much and could really relax. Zero difficult platforming that I needed to complete for my partner, who could get more immersed in the game that way.I could give some feedback about small things and it is not perfect, but all in all fun little change of pace that I recommend to anyone looking for a cozy, laid-back exploration game. Kudos to the dev on this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good short indie game.Looked a lot like A Short Hike in the trailers, but it's mostly park management.Gather materials, do quests for people, explore the island while you go to one campsite, decorate an area and then move to the next.The majority of time spent is post game trying to find the small stick torches you have to fix for 100% camp repairs.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun to play and super cute, a lot of collecting/foraging if you like those kinds of games. I like the map, the characters and the notebook to keep track of everything. The quests keep things interesting because it gives you side quests if you've already figured out the entire map. The only thing I don't like is some camera angles I can't see my character so I'm going blind hoping they don't fall off a cliff, otherwise good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A really calm little game about fixing up a neglected nature park. The gameplay is mostly exploring the different areas, meeting park guests, gathering building/repair resources, completing small quests to open new areas, and filling all the park campgrounds with everything the guests need and want. It's short (I finished the game and almost all achievements in 7 hours) and light on storyline, but if you like exploring, collecting, and basic decorating, it's fun and great stress relief.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. I was initially interested due to the 'campground building' elements, but the exploration and setting design is what won me over. I very much enjoyed finding secrets and getting to higher and higher areas.Don't feel like you need to rush. Even of the campers are demanding something and you don't have materials yet, nothing bad will happen.I went out of my way to avoid looking up any secrets or solutions and just took my time to explore. It was relaxing and exactly the kind of chill cozy game I was looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A Short Hike meets Animal Crossing. It's a campsite caretaking sim with limited dialogue, cozy graphics, and lovable characters. I also want to mention that there are no game play issues using controller. I just wish there were more game to play. 9/10 only because of how short the game is. Still, Haven Park is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very sweet and comforting game with a bit of humor. It's very relaxing to kick back with. It is very straightforward to play, with a single-hand WASD config, with E being the only other key you need. You can also switch to the other side of the keyboard seamlessly and use the arrow keys and enter to do the same things. There are many hidden mysteries to discover and fun little quests to do. I have not experienced any bugs, crashes, or glitches, so it is very well polished. You also don't need to make it to save points or anything, which makes it very convenient to bring up and play when you have an awkward amount of time. I believe this is a good game for kids or adults; I was very pleasantly surprised.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little game that held my interest for several hours.  I do think the map system could be improved because I got lost frequently and spent a lot of time wandering around aimlessly.  But I am okay with that because the scenery is pleasant and the characters are cute.  Most of my enjoyment came from decorating each campsite.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Very lovely little game, just finished getting all the achievements. At 5 hours of running around a pretty island with funny characters (I cackled at the wishing well), and the satisfaction you get from completing all the quests, it's well worth it for the full price. I think the only improvements I would make would be to make some of the skills more effective (such as the one that's meant to make you see better in the dark, or the one that's meant to make you faster/jump higher). I really like that there's no fall damage or stamina bars, though, means I can just enjoy exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I got a coupon for this from a humble bundle and it was just what I needed. It was a relaxing exploration game, all very laid-back, simple and enjoyable. I very much enjoyed my few hours but I think, unless I want to go back and redo all of my parks to be really pretty, that I'm all done for now. Short and sweet, great for unwinding after a hard day at work.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: All I say is: PIU PIU It´s one of the most entertaining game and cutest. Usually I don´t pllay with games where I have to collect resurces and build/ repair stuff, interact with NPC´s. This is the first game that locked me to my PC.I almost got all of the achievements. I wish there would be a little more in the near future ( what happens when someone updated all the camps, repaired everythong, etc.) I´ll wait here paitently for more games and maybe a dlc or addition to the main game Love and kisses to the developing Team
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved Haven Park. I enjoyed exploring the whole park even though I got lost A LOT. It was a bit of a struggle completing all the achievements (especially the treasure hunter one, that one seems a bit bugged) but I had a lot of fun playing and was motivated to get 100% completion. Big bonus for the PEW. Would for sure recommend playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Very cozy and relaxing game. The graphics are stunning and the sound effects create a nice ambiance. I just wish there was a bit more to the game. Maybe some additionnal quests, a slightly bigger map, or a longer story line. You can finish the game in a few hours, but can continue playing if you wish.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Really adorable & fun game, low stakes so it's no stress and you can take your time.My only issue was that the controls in the Abandoned Mine were suddenly not working on my controller so I had to switch to keyboard near the end. Other than that it's a great game, had no glitches or issues, just fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and quick game. I love the paper-like art style. The only thing I would have liked is to see Flint on the mini map, but otherwise it was fun and sweet. The quests are pressure-free but do push you towards the end. The few puzzles are not too hard. Just a nice cozy game. Finished 100% in about 8 hours (I take my time on things).
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Cute, chill little game with a few minor blemishes.Haven Park is a cool, stress-free experience for all ages. Run around the island, collect resources and manage the titular park while meeting park's guests and exploring the areas. The gameplay is pretty simple, there are no fail-states, the resources are a-plenty so you can never get stuck or have to wait to progess. You can always just go somewhere else and explore, which is the strongest part of the game. Discovering new things around the island is simply fun. The ol' castle, the mines, the farmlands, the mountains it's all pretty and exciting. There's stuff to do for about 4-5 hours.There's unfortunately not much more to the game than that. The story is pretty minimal if not non-existant and boils down to the main character "becoming brave" and just maturing as a person I guess. Out of my 4 hours with the game the story segments lasted about 5 mintues so it clearly wasn't a main focus. Managing the park itself is also pretty straightforward or rather simplistic. You just build a few things the campers ask for and that's pretty much it. There's usually no need to go back apart form maybe lighting up a campfire or collecting some coins. I guess running around the camps would just stop you from exploring, so again, it's understandable.During the gameplay I've encountered a few non-gamebreaking bugs and oddities like getting stuck on terrain for a few seconds or acquiring 1 more skill point than it's needed to unlock all skills but those did not ruin my fun in any way.Overall, the game is perfect for a chill evening, or a few short sessions full of adventuring. If you want to have a small, charming experience akin to Short Hike, then you're in the right place.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: it’s a lovely relaxing game, but unfortunately it has bugs in quests and achievements. If you complete quests in a random order the game will not understand that you are allowed to move on and you will get stuck in your journey.I completed the Old Tower first, later went to the old castle, gave gem to the snowman and in return got nothing. Crown is nowhere to be found, not in my inventory, not on a snowman that already has his shiny nose, not on Robin, and i see a quest to find snowman a nose as incomplete even though it’s definitely completed. This makes it impossible for me to open another part of the map to explore more and finish my other quests, which is a shame.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A great, very relaxing shortish game. Not at all deep and very cute and just generally *nice*.Note: the opening 20 crates achievement are for opening all 20 unique crates at least once not any 20 crates (they respawn closed after a while) this is *confusingly worded* and tripped me up.Completion of the main game takes about 3-4 hours, achievement hunting takes longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Haven Park is a short casual game about rebuilding a park. The gameplay consists of collecting resources and then spending these resources on repairs, accommodation and enrichment for your guests. Haven Park is very easy as there is no failure condition, the game has a couple of quests and puzzles but the focus is on exploration. I like the design of the island, the areas are diverse and there are enough secrets and jokes to keep the game fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable game that has you gathering materials from around the (surprisingly large and interesting) map in order to upgrade and build several campsites. Each campsite has a few different characters that have a lot of, well, character. I 100% the game in about 4 hours, but it was a very enjoyable experience. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game after finishing , as I've seen a review saying that if you enjoyed , you'd like  too.First off,  is focused on resource gathering and building rather than just exploring the map and enjoying the view. If you like building stuff, you'll enjoy making your own camps, opposed to having a full static map. On the other hand, at times, gathering resources seems a bit grindy, especially at the beginning of the game, when you don't have enough money and a market place to exchange resources.Secondly, the story is different than , it's not a copy of that game at all. The main message is the same, but it's presented in another way. It's about life, about fighting anxiety and being overwhelmed by solving problems one step at a time.The graphic design works very well with the story and the main character. One small issue here is that the colors are over saturated. For me it wasn't a problem, but it might create a bit of discomfort to some people. A color saturation settings would have been a nice-to-have feature.Controls and game play are straight forward. Building stuff is easy and interaction with NPCs and buildings is intuitive.One aspect of game design that I wasn't fond of is that some objects are not interactive until you get a certain mission, while you can free roam and interact with everything else.  The main idea is that, if you get stuck, search for help on the Steam discussions. Don't bother figuring out everything by yourself, sometimes you lose too much time and the game becomes less enjoyable because of one design choice.After finishing the main story, there was one thing that bothered me: fixing all the signs and fences. There are a couple of topics about this on the forums, and, I ran into the same issue: I couldn't find one last element (for me it was in Yellowfields). I went three times over the whole place, and I just couldn't find what was missing. Funny enough, after moaning about it in on one of the topics, I thought to give it one more try and call it a night, and, like magic, I found the last one element: it was a fence positioned on the vertical axis, near one of the village houses. :) In this situation I think it was a mix of tiredness, color, positioning and lack of hinting; my brain wasn't able to process that bit of broken fence after going round and round a few times. There is already a topic on the community forums suggesting better hinting for the last elements, to make it easier to find it. My advice here is to take a break and try one more time later, give your mind a break.Similar to a , there are a few extra pluses:+ Steam Cloud+ GNU/Linux support+ game runs almost perfect on 4K resolution with loser intel Arc A750 (there are some FPS drops in the misty area, but you won't spend too much time there)+ no 3rd party EULA spyware+ no freemium-like/DLC dark patterns money grab schemeNot as the other game:- there's a 3rd party publisher that might force the dev into making anti-consumer practices in the future (not the case so far, the core principles on Mooneye Studios web page seem positive, so this shouldn't count as a negative, but just a note the developer is not fully independent)All-in-all,  was a nice game to play. It was a bit more complex with the building feature, yet not quite as relaxing and polished as . I give it a 8.5/10, recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the definition of a hidden gem. The screenshots didn't really convince me, and I expected it to be much shorter than it really is. If you love exploring, collecting resources, and some light decorating mixed with clever little games and fun writing then by all means give this a try. It's an entirely chill experience in a beautiful and varied park.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game was exactly what I needed. It's cute, it's relaxing and it's very low stakes. You progress through the game play very quickly, and it's easy to make enough money to purchase the items for the camp sites. I love the graphics, the camp grounds and the little campers, and overall if you're looking for an easy cute little game then I would absolutely recommend it.  However, it's not perfect. I personally did not enjoy the weird electronic music and thought it clashes with the games's aesthetic and purpose. I also found getting around and navigating via the map a little frustrating at time. Lastly I think this game needs more items and customization. It would be so good to be able to add more activities to the camp sites and to choose the color of the items in use.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I personally enjoyed this game more than A Short Hike, but you should play both. If you had asked me after I played A Short Hike what my version of it would be like, Haven Park would be it. It's a cute, relaxing game with fun objectives and a sense of progression. I also really appreciated the sense of satisfaction you get from fixing up the park as you go. Go ahead and buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: When writing reviews, I typically consider the graphics, polish, and how I connected with the game emotionally. This game hit the mark for it all!Usually, low-poly games can have lots of issues, but this one is beautiful and I didn't run into any bugs. I loved the sounds in this game too. It ran perfectly on Steam Deck too!2 things stood out to me the most- the fair price and beautiful narrative. I've had issues recently with short indie games having absurd prices. Most importantly, the story of this game was so sweet. It made me pause & reflect on the relationships I have and the beauty of life itself.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cute. However, it is NOT made for PC controls are wonky at times and it makes for aggravating game play at times when you have to sprint jump from small platforms but the mouse button is the only way you can sprint but your mouse must be oriented in the same direction (even though you have no idea which direction your mouse is in because there is no indicator) I just wish you could bind your keys to whatever you wanted. and if the jumps were consistent sometimes you jump and it works fine and other times it just chooses not to jump at all. I had to take a break from this game because it is supposed to be a cozy/relaxing game but when you have spent most of your time climbing a mountain just to have your jump button not work and send you right back down to the ground it is so aggravating. Simple movement updates and mechanical fixes would make this game 100x better.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Haven Park was on my wishlist for a while before it was  to me a few days ago. I have played a lot, and it has been very enjoyable overall. The small storyline in the game is simple but sweet, and I loved the ending, which I found unexpected and bittersweet. Those who saw the ending might understand what I mean.The gameplay has lots of exploration, and the whole park was well thought out. I like how colorful the game is, how lively the island is (especially as you set up all the camps), and I very, very,  much like the puzzles! There were roadblocks (literally and figuratively) that you had to figure out, which were rewarding and pleasant to me. The characters are cute and at times funny. My only criticisms are: the game needs more polish, I think the sound design could use a little work, and the game may need more replay value (something I  because of how enjoyable the game was). The game as a whole isn't super deep, but that is by no means a problem. The game is not lacking in purpose and style, and more importantly, the game is simply fun, especially if you enjoy exploration, all the sights and scenery of creation, a few puzzles, and camp building.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant about buying this given the A Short Hike resemblance at first blush, got it from a bundle and it turned out to be quite different. There is a resemblance tonally but the gameplay here is focused around gathering resources to create camps and repair the park, with some overarching objectives thrown in. Devs sent back a quick response about patching a bug and rolled out a fix after the weekend. Readily recommended on sale and I would still recommend at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, simple game where you inherit park maintenance from your Grandmother. Collecting a few basic resources, you discover camps, rebuild them, and repair various signposts and fences throughout the park. Overall it took me about 3 - 4 hours to complete the main storyline. Relaxing simple gameplay has its place, and this is it!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: What a cute and calm game. I'm usually into horror and/or psychological games, so this one is such a fresh breath of air. There is no rush, no pressure to finish anything. The graphics are really smooth, everything blends so nicely. Also, the fact that it's PG 3 made me smile a lot, because the kid in me reaaaally enjoyed exploring the "not so little" park of Flints. The story, although, pretty short, but made me tear up quite a bit! An amazing game overall, if you're looking for something different, chill and heartwarming 🥺️
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game about a young bird person stepping into their grandmother's shoes as the new caretaker of Haven Park. It's become run down over the years as the grandmother got too old to take care of it properly.It is important to note that this isn't a  game, as evidenced by my 5 hour playtime even taking into account getting all the achievements. However, it is a neat little outing that people looking for something relaxing and simply can enjoy. The basic premise of exploring the rundown park and setting up campsites is appealing, even if there's not as much freedom in their customization as I'd like. Materials for building tents, food trucks, and other attractions can be found throughout the island.Gathering and building will net you experience points, and when you level up the skill points can be used to unlock useful traits such as a bigger backback or trading at any market you build. In fact, I'd suggest you grab those two skills sooner rather than later. Otherwise, just have fun and play at your own pace. Sometimes campers will have little quests or bits of info for you, too.My only real complaints is that it can be easy to get lost even with the marker stones, and sometimes you fall off ledges cause hill or tree obscured your character. Otherwise there's nothing stopping you from having fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun playing this game.  It's very relaxing and everything can be done at your own pace.  I spent a lot of time redoing camps and getting all the achievements so my time played is a bit longer than most people's, I think.  If you like exploration with some puzzle and building elements, you'll probably enjoy this.  Definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. This was a very relaxing game, but needed some fine tuning to make it great.Positives:* Art style is great, cute.* Puzzles were somewhat unique and fun.* Building camps was fun.* Exploration was honestly pretty difficult. There were some tucked away places in this game.Needed Work:* The developers let you do anything, to the point that I absolutely forgot what the primary quest was. When I met Grandma again for the first time I thought "Oh. That was a quest?". Gentle reminders could have still been ignored, but given me a reminder of my purpose.* Base building was fun, but some of the camps felt they weren't made with it in mind. The worst example would be the Black Tower campsite where the build area was so tiny. I didn't put things down because I wanted to, but rather because they felt like the smallest things that wouldn't block everything single path out of there.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked A Short Hike, you'll enjoy Haven Park. There's more to do and discover in this game than it initially seems. Customizing the camps is a fun and integral element of the gameplay, but exploring the island fully is rewarding. Interacting with campers gets you some humorous dialogue. It's well worth the price all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is my very first review of a game and I don't think that I could have picked a better one! This game is exactly what I was looking for. It was very bright and cute with lots of little puzzles to solve and the characters and dialogue are great as well. Simple enough game play and one of the few games that I have managed to get 100% achievements on! 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little, cosy game. The story was very sweet and the quests were fun. The style was lovely and I liked the day to night cycle. Oh, and the run animation was top tier 10/10 would run as a chicken againpewpewpewpewpewpewpewpewA couple of things that bugged me:The slowest hot air balloon known to man (which is really annoying to get anywhere without it)Not realising you were missing quests e.g. unless you happened to interact with the broken tractor.Trying to jump over fencesAnnoying map, just tell me where i am please!Overall I really liked this, definitely pick it up on sale!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10, 6/10 10/10 8/10 7/10  7/10, 7/10The plot of Haven Park is pretty simplistic and lacks a lot of substance, but that isn't what the game is about for the most part so I'm not going to put too much emphasis on the low rating for this or the dialogue.The setting and art design for this game is the main selling point of this game in my opinion. The game has a wonderful art design and the setting really makes you want to actively be in the woods right now. Haven Park really does seem like a Haven and I would like to visit a place like it sometime during my life. The soundtrack is simple, but effective. It helps to convey the relaxing mood of Haven Park by playing the same relaxing and joyful music throughout the game. The graphics aren't anything to write home about, but they look good and combined with the art design of the game, goes to make a very effective combination.Sound mixing is done well in this game, with many of the buttons and interactions having very nice sounds attributed to them. On top of that, whenever you just press E, the character says pew, which is very cute and brings a smile to my face. The gameplay is simple too, but it's cathartic to just take care of a park and to make it the best it can possibly be. There is also plenty of side quests for the player to embark upon.This game is a very cute and fun game that I would highly recommend for anyone to pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: On the whole I enjoyed this game. It's a huge open world and so pretty, I loved the additions of the cable cars and the balloon and the tasks kept it interesting. However, there are a few improvements that could be made in my opinion. At times the game is very dark, more than is necessary. I understand it's nighttime or I'm in a mine but it gets frustrating and even with the brightness up I could barely see in front of me. In the mine particularly it got frustrating because I couldn't even see to do the tasks at times. It would be really useful if you could get a torch or something to make it more manageable. Just because some of the routes are nigh on impossible to find when you're in the centre of the cave and it stops being fun at some point. The map was another issue at times. Would it be such an issue to have a "you are here" marker rather than having to look for the number stones? I get that it should be a challenge to find these places but I spent much more time than was necessary walking in circles because of how similar some places look.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Charming little adventure game that is engaging enough but won't take up too much of your time either.A big part of the game is gathering resources and building camps, there are also some rpg elements like skils and quests. Don't expect too much dept but its a nice blend of game-play. Graphics are pretty although there is heavy use of Depth of Field. You can disable it in the settings if not to your taste. Unfortunately no mouse support though. Overall recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Haven Park is a relaxing game where you repair and explore your grandmothers park full of campsites that you get to decorate and make your own. Think Animal Crossing meets more exploration. You run around as a cute little duck gathering supplies, and just fixing everything.  I'd totally recommend getting this game, it's relaxing and enjoyable and certainly a new favorite comfort game.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Quite an exploration in the park which took me the whole night to finish it eventually. Would like to recommend it for its fine pictures and smooth experience. For me it wasn't easy to feel tiresome until i unlocked all the areas including the Mine. Might not continue to fix all the fences at end. After all, recommended for its fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game! You can explore a lush green landscape of islands, flowing water, and peaks. The game characters are cute and funny. The achievements are simple, intuitive, and satisfying. I really enjoy exploring, which is a bit challenging as there are some obstacles and a story too. Love this game for the water and the greenery!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A cute game in the style of A SHORT HIKE, but with a little more customization since you get to decorate the park. This seems not to be a very long game, maybe 3-5 hours max? But the art style is cute, the minimal story is moving, and I just really enjoy building food trucks in the wilderness. If you need a chill time, this is the perfect game to unwind with. Probably good for younger kids too.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: very sweet. i love that it tackles a life experience in a serious, light but respectful way.graphics are stylized but beautiful, very relaxing to the eyes. and big plus for not being sys req demanding.i'm just in love with this game's overall atmosphere. and the characters are "wholesome" quirky.the main plot, i would say, is reasonably quick to finish. as for long-term gaming, you can still keep playing and designing even after finishing the plot, but i think it's far from being "infinite". let's just say that it plays largely as a small exploration/adventure game than a simulation, and repeat playing is not exactly in the picture.some tiny bugs:1) the game froze and closed 3x during gameplay, and i don't think i'll be able to recreate those moments, they seem rather random. (but your progress is auto-saved , so i'm guessing there's a minor bug on the save function? you won't lose any progress at all)2) at the very start of the game, i can hear some sfx running but the screen is just black. i'm assuming that's for the game dev's logo/intro? it's not visually showing up. but the game will continue to run anyway so no problem for players.overall, 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is the cutest and sweetest little game and I absolutely ADORE it. It's so much fun to explore and set up camps and collect items as I go along. This is the perfect relaxing game, there's no stress or pressure to do anything. I love games like this and Haven Park is going onto my favorite games list for sure. In fact, I love this game so much I also got it on my nintendo switch! This game gets 5 stars and ten out of ten from me!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this is my second run bacuse I finished this game on my Nintendo first. And OMG it looks so beautiful on the full screen!Being a huge fan of A Short Hike and Animal Crossing, I can assure you - if you are too and if you're willing to spend a couple of evenings in a complete state of comfort, joy and a tiny bit of light sadness, this game is for you. The main character is a cute birdie! How can you not? It is 100% on the level. One of the kindest and cutest games I've ever played. Maybe this year. Maybe ever. Thank you, guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A vibrant, beautiful little game. The art style reminds me of Breath of the Wild and AC: New Horizons, and I loved discovering how a new region looked in the style. The gameplay is very relaxed yet still rewarding, kinda the perfect escapist fantasy for someone fed up of commodified, modern living. Easy to complete all achievements, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a hidden gem of a game that I discovered on Steam.  I love everything it about it.  It's simplicity mixed with story line and quests, make the game feel relaxing and not that grindy.  The artistry is lovely, and the dialogue was more than I expected (in a good way.) The ending gives you all the feels, and I am so glad I played it.  Highly recommend.  Thank you to the developers!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: It's not the easiest game world to navigate, but it is fun to explore, figure out what each camper wants, and stocking each camp with it.I'm actually a little surprised at how quickly I found all the camps, and filled them up. Though some of the icons on the menu could be a bit more obvious about what they mean...
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A comfy casual game about maintaining a park/campground.  This has both exploration and a building aspect as well.  The movement mechanics are very forgiving.  You can jump up a lot of slopes that don't look possible and there's no falling penalty.  At one point very early in the game, I managed to clip into a mountainside, but I was easily able to extract myself and I never encountered a clip again.  It takes some time to get accustomed to the map, since it doesn't mark where you are.  You have to use landmarks and guideposts to find your way around.  It's very like finding your way on hiking trails IRL.  This is not much of a story-based game, as the story is very minimal.  That doesn't detract from the game, but I wanted to mention it.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute game about cleaning up a park and doing your grandma proud! Not a very long play, I was taking it very leisurely and it took me about 5 hours to complete, but it was well worth it. Pick this up if you're looking for something not overly demanding and just wanna get your head off of things for awhile :)
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Haven Park is a cute, atmospheric game about the changing of hands. Flint, the player's character, takes over the responsibilities of managing his grandma's park and making it into a fun environment for campers looking to spend some time in the great outdoors.The gameplay is charming, consisting of going around and exploring new places on the map while setting up campsites and repairing broken down areas along the way. As the player goes on, Flint grows more confident in the new role he inherited-- and just as well, considering his grandma doesn't have long left in this world.Haven Park is a little game about nurturing the things our loved ones leave behind, and improving upon them to share to others. There is still much to be done by the end of the game, but by the end the player knows everything will be just fine: after all, just as Flint takes care of the park, the park in turn takes care of him.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A must play if you love exploring or if you love animal crossing. It is a short game (I'd say probably about 4-5 hours for 100%) but it is full of life and much love was put in. Interesting little things and discoveries to find, cute commentary from numerous campers, and there is lore. Worth playing if you have any interest.-If you don't like walking around exploring and clicking on stuff, this probably isn't for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautifully simple game, if a bit short. About 5 of my 9 logged hours were idle.You play as a chick fixing up a park for your grandma, it has gameplay elements of Animal Crossing Pocket Camp but better executed.Its a gorgeous game with a not very big map that somehow they make feel big, its got layers and chill vibes, you can complete it in a few hours and 100% the achievements too. 9/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this lil game. It reminds me so much of A Short Hike, another game I love, and it's just cute as heck. It can get a bit frustrating, the camera angles especially, and I played most of it the few days after it came out, before the addition of the game telling you where you had missed fixing things. Let me tell you, I was stuck on 98% forEVER. But I finally went back and got all the achievements and now I feel satisfied. 10/10 would pew again.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cute, unique game for all ages! I'd say about 4 hours of gameplay, but maybe 6-8 or so if you try to complete every task. Beautiful graphics -- especially at night -- and I love the light "management" mechanics. I definitely think the developer could add a bit more to the management mechanics to extend the gameplay a bit more.I also wish there was an unlockable item (like a compass or whatever) that showed your position on the map.Also, I nearly completed the game before realizing how the "run" button worked. I didn't realize you had to click and then drag your mouse in the direction you wanted to run. I was so confused why the character was running in a seemingly random direction when I clicked.Definitely worth getting for a solid day of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: HOLY COW!Sweet cute game, lots of exploring, collecting, improving the camps, little side quests, AND THEN ENDING OH MY GOD WAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAT! I was like 'Are they serious?! IS THIS WHAT WAS GOING ON?! IS THIS REAL?!' and then stomping around and yelling followed because too much feeling. XD Great game, I thought it was going to be a simple little romp BUT NO! You had to make me feel emotions!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I took my time and enjoyed every minute. It's a beautiful game. I love the use of colors. If you liked A Short Hike, you won't be disappointed. It is worth every penny to play a game that makes you feel good, like Haven Park was for me. The story is cute but packs an emotional punch.Steam needs more well made, feel-good games with positive messages, like Haven Park, which is why I nominated it for a 2021 Steam Award.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: In 6 hours of casual and relaxed play I was able to explore the world until my heart was content, complete the main story, almost all side missions, and 17/19 achievements. Haven park is a delightful game experience that I would recommend for anyone who needs a break from the rat race. I first saw it on a short PlayFrame episode and could not wait to see the camp/park for myself. Changes and improvements are ongoing and the developer is currently very engaged with the content. Pew Pew!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of "A Short Hike", I really enjoyed playing this cute, relaxing game. I love the overall cozy vibe it gives, the mechanic of expanding the map the more campsites you find works out nicely, and the small optional tasks are a great way to explore the park more. The touching ending was an unexpected but huge plus for me. And two other positive surprises I love are the "pew pew" mechanic and the "hidden" transportation device. Highly recommend if you're into wholesome games!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing, nature-friendly adventure.Coming here after playing A Short Hike, I definitely didn't want this game to end! The PEW, the camp free-designing, the level up/xp collecting, the boat incident--Oh God the boat, the dialog, the tower, the story & ending.I love everything about this game. I didn't grow up near a forest, or have anything forest-like that I can go to. So I got a taste of what it's like going to the forest. I love how "real" this feels, with the map and not being able to see where you are, the echoes of the PEW when you go into a cavern-like place, the footsteps, the little to almost no music, makes it feel more immersive. Some people might be put off by it, but I enjoyed it. Still haunted by the boat. I'm so sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of this game for a while and it entirely lived up to my expectations. It made me laugh, it brought tears to my eyes, and I am infinitely amused by the "pew" button. Highly recommend for people who enjoy cozy management games like Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very chill, completely adorable, heartwarming, and relaxing. It can be done in one long play session, or enjoyed over multiple chunks, but there's a lot more to do than you would think! The tilt-shift-like graphics are wonderful, the sounds of nature are calming, and the music that comes in at different campsites would perk anyone up! There's a touching little story to it too. I HIGHLY recommend it - the dev did a GREAT job!!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game has some animal crossing vibes crossed with A short Hike. The control scheme is a little off-putting you would expect some form of mouse control. Recommend using a controller as it just feels more natural. It is fairly short but a fun 4-5 hours nonetheless. Some of the hidden achievements were a welcome surprise. There really does need to be a tracker for the repair of the island as that took an extra 1.5hrs to find for the final achievement. Overall a solid game, cant wait for what comes next on this.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome little game! You can easily "beat" it in 3-4 hours, but it gives you a balloon then that allows you to reach unreachable chests and "fast travel" to you camps so you can continue playing as long as you like. The camp management is really clever and not too tedious and it's fun to build a ferris wheel or a tiki bar. Also the dialogues are way more subtle and deep than I expected from a very "childish looking" game. All in all, a very pleasant and fun surprise!
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

_childDocuments_.review: Explore a tiny and peaceful open world. Meet and talk to the campers, find the resources required to build cosy little campings and keep the campers happy. You will also have plenty of side quests on your journey. But no rush, this place is your safe haven to discover. Haven Park was inspired by games like A Short Hike or Animal Crossing, so if you are a fan of those, this game is definitely for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Haven Park

name: SPRAWL
detailed_description: “You chose exile in search of penance, in place of revenge. I seek to give you both - and in return… I will be set free.” - FATHER Enter the dystopian world of SPRAWL, a hardcore retro FPS set in an endless cyberpunk megalopolis. Advances in cybernetics and artificial intelligence pushed humanity into a new era, but that golden age has crumbled…leaving behind a broken world. Play as SEVEN, a disgraced special ops super soldier who finds herself embroiled in conflict with government forces trying to kill her while a mysterious voice in her head pushes her to survive. Betrayed by her organization and on a mission to overthrow the Junta, a military regime that rules the sprawl with an iron fist, SEVEN must escape the walled city and discover what secrets lie at the SPIRE. The streets of the SPRAWL are vast and the armies of the corporate government seem endless. But the dark alleys and dilapidated apartment surfaces are all compatible with the “Icarus” cybernetic implant, allowing SEVEN to perform gravity-defying wall-running maneuvers and slow down time with excess adrenaline drops from dismembered enemies. With a horde of different troop types and carefully designed weapons, she will be pushed to the limit to survive. The SPRAWL eventually consumes us all…will you fight your way out? To escape the desolate, AI-controlled city you’re gonna need to think quickly and master your weapons in a high-speed game of combat chess. Slash with your katana, keep a steady hand for headshots with the pistol, and use the powerhouse shotgun to jump up and out of range. Quickly swap weapons with no slowdown as you finish your enemies with precision aiming and slow down time for headshots. Get the best of your enemies and defy gravity with a cybernetic implant. Experience a new approach to wallrunning with seamless transitions from the ground to the walls, creating an entirely new dimension for exploration and combat. Solve combat situations creatively to get different rewards: ammo, health boosts, and refills of your bullet time adrenal meter. Explore a retro-futuristic and dystopian world filled with deep lore and visually inspired by classics like Akira and Ghost in the Shell. While racing to the Spire, a variety of enemies will present new challenges to overcome. You’ll need to adjust on the fly to different attack patterns. Rapid fire bursts from the SMG elite will keep you on your toes while a riot guard will charge and block your bullets. Think fast and adapt to survive. Immerse yourself in the environment and sounds of SPRAWL with an original industrial electronic soundtrack. The dynamic music system responds to your actions, lining up with kills and movements as you progress.

_childDocuments_.review: Judging by the Achievements, i am already half-way through with the game after about two and a half hours, and if anything changes by the time i finish the latter half i'll redo this review, but anyways.Edit: Yes, nothing changed. So, Sprawl is another addition to the ever more popular movement shooter genre with quite amazing art, an absolute banger soundtrack and slow motion, which in this day and age is rather rare. You'll get a game heavily inspired by Ghost in The Shell where you wall run everywhere and slow-mo blast Jin Roh Panzercops, Ghosts, Mechs and what else might show up. The OST, just like the aesthetic, is heavily inspired by Ghost in the Shell as well. Ranging from japanese inspired Sci-Fi tunes, over techno to some Doom 2016 inspired tracks.Unfortunately, the positives end here already, as the rest is just not really that all that good. Not bad, but not good either.The biggest two issues i have are an extremely lackluster AI who gets its difficulty from sheer numbers and how fast they react and how extremely lackluster the weapons feel.AI will just run straight at you. Doesn' matter if it's the common soldier or a invisible, teleporting ninja. They will constantly get stuck on things, and don't really pose any threat.Weapons all look and sound amazing, but every single one of them safe for the explosives lack any and all impact. The starting pistol causes exactly the same reaction from enemies as the fricking Railgun you get later on. No larger blood spray, no stronger ragdoll, nothing. Weapons also all feel just slightly off enough to feel bad to use.The shotgun cycles just slightly to slow. The SMG hast just slightly too much spread. The Minigun slows you down just slightly too much, Railgun does not pierce enemies for whatever reason, etc.Level Design, while at times looking awesome, is also a tad rough. It's the genre typical corridors leading to larger arena's deal. The Arenas are decently designed, even though you don't really have to use their geometry that much as AI just gets stuck anyways, but it supplements the movement quite well. The amount of times i got lost in just 3 hours however is rough, especially in that one level on the roofs where everything looks the same and i just found my way completely random. Just doesn't flow all that well.As for the things i am neutral about, or just baffled;A lot of the story and lore is hidden around in Datapads, which isn't anything new in the industry, but what is new is the fact that they are QR codes that you need to scan to access them. Just.. why? I get the idea was to have a neat little thing that players can chase outside the game, but it's such a dumb idea to put your already thin story behind QR codes like that. Perhaps i am oldschool, but when i play an game i'd like to experience what it has inside the game, not outside of it. But since i don't play these for story, it's something that i just feel neutral about.As for my Verdict; Unfortunately i am someone who prefers gameplay over aesthetics. Yes, the game looks cool and the music is so well done that it's now on my playlist, but take both away and you get a dull movement shooter where there is just way better options out there, and i doubt that will change in the latter bits of the game, and if it does then i will edit this review to reflect that.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Since I see the devs responding here and there, I have to say this1 Audio. Whatever Godforsaken noise is at the start of each level and loading checkpoint, remove it. It's legit ear damage for anyone with a headset. 2. Parkour. the 'sagging' or small  downward momentum that happens when wall running really ruins the pacing and you end up falling flat on the floor more often then not3. Tooltips or a proper tutorial would help a lot, if I didn't play other games with parkour and bullet time/wall running such as Severed Steel I would have felt a little lost mechanics wise.hate to leave a bad review because for its price its worth it but that audio issue is horrendous.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Really scratching my head at some of these negative reviews I have seen..so I thought I would review the game before I finished it. SPRAWL wears a lot of its influences on its sleeve, most prominently in terms of the visuals and tone from Ghost in the Shell (1995) and from its gameplay the likes of Titan Fall 2 and FEAR. But theres definitley dashes of stuff like Mirrors Edge and Jin-Roh Wolf Brigade there too. Ultimately the gameplay isnt that deep, you parkour, use slow mo and blast various types of dudes. Theres a nice degree of enemy variety so far that keeps the gameplay fresh. I have seen some complaints that the game doesn't have more mechanics for its movement and combat and I think thats okay? I think a lot of boomer shooters are way too overloaded with mechanics that it can feel like im using the whole key board half the time. SPRAWL is a game with fun enough combat thats carried through a lot by its vibes and atmosphere.I do absolutely wish there was a quick save, some platforming sections are rather finnicky and some combat sequences are a bit long. I do also wish the AI was a tad better (its honestly fine just could use some extra work) and that the slide could let you push enemies as it feels a bit undercooked otherwise. Its genuinely nice to see one of these games that isn't incredibly over the top game where you fight monsters from hell (not thats a bad thing!). If your willing to immerse yourself in a really moody setting (lots of PS2 era vibes here) and some good combat to boot I think SPRAWL is worth a look. Its literally cheaper than some meals so go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE 3/28/2024:At the suggestion of a comment on the original review, I decided to give this one last try. I gotta say, while I'm still not nearly as enthusiastic about it as most other people, I've decided to switch this over to a Recommend, overall.The changes to the weapons like slightly reduced charge times on the Railgun and Chaingun, reduced shotgun spread and faster pump time, damage tweaks, etc, put the game in a bit of a better-feeling place. The addition of a third wallkick also helps the movement flow a bit better, though some of it still feels a bit awkward, especially without a mantle. It definitely works for this game's intended feel, flow and design, but it takes some getting used to.Episode 3 brings back some of the better pacing from E1, as you progress noticeably and rapidly through the final stronghold to the big showdown. If you pay attention you know you're still getting locked into arenas, but by now you have the whole arsenal and are expected to know how to use it, weapon switching and wallrunning, crouch-sliding and jumping your way around to avoid hordes of every enemy type in the game, big and small.Maybe the biggest negative from the game still is the boss fights, which have never really been the strong suit of FPS games anyway. They're...fine, but really I found myself zoning out until I could stop for a sec to unload the Chaingun into them, which feels like really the only consistently damaging weapon on them - the rocket launcher has this terrible random scatter effect and the railgun doesn't have nearly the punch it feels like it should against big guys IMO. Unfortunately, this means abandoning the movement abilities and being slowed to a crawl that the Chaingun forces you into, though you can usually sidestep just fast enough to avoid damage, or get a quick side-slide in before resuming fire.Overall, I'll say I enjoyed the few hours I had left when I came back to this. It'll probably take you an afternoon/night to blast through, and it's a well-put-together game with a neat presentation. With the updates made, most of my gripes with the game are personal preference now rather than overtly negative design problems. Episode 2 in general and the boss fights are the weakpoints - the rest makes Sprawl worth it. Shoutout to Thionaak in the comments (if you're even reading this five months later!) for suggesting I go back._____________NOTE: Original review below here.PROS:- Good-to-great soundtrack- Solid atmosphere in E1- Some great early level design that calls to mind other dystopian shooters like Half-Life 2 and makes good use of the limited movement mechanics- Good Railgun- Early encounters flow well for the most partCONS- Level design quickly degenerates into dull factories and boring locked arena encounters by E2, ruining the flow of both the narrative and the combat- Lore entries are on QR codes you have to scan with your phone instead of just reading in-game- Enemies are dumb and (mostly) spongey, resulting in unsatisfying cheesing or irritating plinking at weak points to pick them off slowly.- Weapons are weak and unsatisfying except for a couple, with little in the way of feedback and interaction with targets and the environment except for headshots or explosions.Starts off sort of interesting with a good soundtrack and some neat levels in Episode 1, but once you realize how repetitive the mediocre combat is and how limited the mobility and wallrunning mechanic is, it runs its course. By the middle of Episode 2, I felt like I had seen everything the game had to offer and just got bored.The weapons for the most part just don't feel quite right; the starting pistols are your only precise weapons until the Railgun in E2 (which, to its credit is the best-feeling weapon for my money, very satisfying), and the game is very particular about you using the slomo mode to assist in hitting enemy weakpoints - these kills generate more ammo, health and Adrenaline (slomo) pickups, along with melee finishers with your sword on low-HP enemies. Every other non-explosive is technically capable of these, but not reliably except at very close range. The shotgun in particular is disappointing - damage falls off very quickly over range despite it being a huge double barrel, and the pump time takes several SECONDS. Only the weakest of enemies will die to a single close-range trigger pull, and quick-swapping does little to alleviate the delay in shots if a foe fails to drop. The "Chaingun" is another disappointing mixed bag, having a huge windup, a slow rate of fire and tiny ammo pool (much like the other weapons), though it is surprisingly accurate and decently powerful per shot. It does slow you down to a walk when firing, however, and the shotgun blasts you backwards with its kick - too bad the power coming out the front doesn't match.The roster of enemies is not terribly interesting beyond the first few missions, especially once the level design begins to favor locking you into arenas versus crafting more "lived in" and immersive encounters that go hand-in-hand with your progression. E1 has some interesting and entertaining city maps that get more vertical as you ascend to the rooftops and through the canals to make your escape - some good Half-Life 2 vibes. After that though, it's industrial arena after industrial arena.Overall, I think this game has potential, but it seems content to be Cyberpunk Doom Eternal-lite with weak wallrunning. It could have been much more, if it dove deeper into the early game's "push forward" combat encounters rather than stopping you to fight huge hordes in walled-off rooms. My mind kept wandering back to Turbo Overkill while playing this - far from a fair comparison, and not one I am trying to make per say, but if you find yourself longing for a cyberpunk-style retro shooter with highly-mobile combat, it's the better option.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, GhostGunner.My wife calls it “what if Ghostrunner was Quake”.My wife’s boyfriend just says it’s just “Mirror's Doom Quake”.I'm not a boomer but this game looks like a fun shooter!A Fast-paced action game set in a dystopian future. There is little to no attention to detail but the story and gameplay more than makes up for it. It ends up as a fantastic action game with an emphasis on platforming, visually dazzling with its stunning style. + Dynamics and cycle of battles with opponents, + Style and specific graphics, + Spatial platforming puzzles, + Balance (although the enemies can be a bit large). The narrative aspect is lacking, which, however, is typical of the boomershooter genre. I’d also describe it as cyberpunk OG fps / movement shooter, that’s little bit conservative on when levels give you additional weapons (a la Quake I: E2M1). Enemies have weak spots, health bars, and flash when they enter a mode you can use finishers on and drop ammo/hp/armour/adrenaline (DOOM remake mechanic) which you use to enter slow motion mode. Soundtrack has songs reminiscent of Ghost in the Shell as well.The game just keeps kicking my ass, but in a good way. It's not the greatest FPS of the year, but the movement and gunplay is excellent, and the art & soundtrack is really great as well! It’s also not breaking the bank and giving some solid bang for your buck at least. Highly recommended. Personally, I’m just happy I can finally be John Wick in this. :)8/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Titanfall or Quake, this is a love-letter for you. Once you get the hang of the movement you'll instantly be reminded of Titanfall or Quake in a very good way. The parkouring really sets this apart from other retro-shooters. In all other aspects, this is a very basic shooter, the movement and high speed is all that it has going for itself (Exactly what  was searching for lol)  Set enemy damage to max, your damage to 0,50 and adrenaline regen to max. Game rewards you for headshots (One-shots grunts). Go for the head while wallruning, jumping, falling and running. Reall try to move and don't just stand there, it will be way more fun than staring at bots in koovaks or target discs in AimLabs.First off: I don't understand some of the reviews here. Someone said the level layout is confusing?Yes, levels are very dark and black, the way forward is  marked with some kind of green/bright light like, you know, every other game? They're almost always linear but sometimes you have to do objectives like keycards so the level becomes a bit more open. No markers, map or journal. You have to pay attention to what you are being told and are expected to figure stuff out on your own. I personally enjoy it more over modern game design. -Also someone said the levels weren't designed for wallrun? Plenty of movement opportunities,I had no trouble evading enemies as I got better at the movement.That said, the game is pretty short. There is only 3 Chapters and they only take like 6 hours to complete. Not enough secrets to reward exploring on playthroughs after you finish the game. Only thing to collect is qr codes (lore), more ammo and armor. No early weapons, extra features (think lego star wars) secret bosses or the like.Enemies are honestly pretty basic too. Lights, heavies, melee rushers, mechs, floating drones, turrets and bosses.Their AI is super dumb. Sometimes you can get up to a roof or platform and they won't even try to jump to you even though they have the ability to do so. Leads to them standing there and you can pick them off like a shooting-gallery.Sadly ach phase is pretty similar and they pack no real surprises.Weapon selection is also satisfying but very basic. Think of quake or unreal tournament. Some of the guns allow "rocket jumps" like the shotgun. Very fun and adds to the movement!No attachment or skin customizations.Soundtrack is SUPERB! In all honestly though, I'm a pretty big dnb-head so this is right up my alley! 90% is punchy drum and bass in a 90's fps style. This is my favourite track in the game, give it a listen!The design of the other sounds in the game is run off the mill though. No bad, not good, no issues here.Game is balanced, none of the levels are impossible no matter the difficulty you choose.The game heavily rewards headshots or hitting enemy-weakpoints. The pistol one-shots grunts heads and 2-3 shots for heavier enemies even when set to hard difficulty. In comparison it takes like 5 body-shots for a grunt to go down and they won't drop health/ammo-pickups when killed. Some enemies have no weakpoint so you are expected to use the right weapon for the right enemy. SMG and Pistol won't really scratch mechs but minigun, grenade launcher and rocket launcher work very well.There is also a slow-mo mechanic where you can hold a button (right mouse by default) to slow down time and highlight weakpoints and objectives. There is a bar in the middle and it drains as you use it. Enemies drop refills. Personally not a huge fan of it and how every singleplayer-FPS nowadays has one somehow. To me it feels like cheating and I never use it.All in all a good, kinda mediocre game. For 7€ on sale it was a no-brainer. Even for the standard 14€ it's a pretty good deal. Wish there was a level editor or extra levels beside horde mode though :(

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I'm an avid Titanfall (and movement shooters in general for that matter) fan and my eyes lit up when I saw the social media for this game toting it as a "Titanfall-like."Unfortunately, this game really misses the mark in everything it tries to do, in my opinion. It wants to be a movement shooter, but there are maybe 3 mechanics that I encountered that actually influence your movement (janky wallrunning with an arbitrary walljump limit, sliding, and the shotgun boost). The movement doesn't feel fun, deep, or rewarding.The combat, and wow there is a TON of it, is one-dimensional. The gunplay itself feels lacking and there's no real feedback for shooting an enemy. The enemy AI is very basic, and in nearly every encounter during my brief time with the game, all the enemies would follow the same pathing and run around in a single group. I was actually able to manipulate their poor pathing by standing in a certain part of the arena and moving back and forth to get them to aimlessly run back and forth as well while I made easy headshots.Speaking of arenas, the game is extremely brown and gray. Most levels just have a couple walls you can use to wallrun, maybe a building/box or two, and that's about 90% of the arenas I encountered. In short, I'm pretty disappointed. I'd been looking forward to this game for quite a long time (and boy did the trailers do a great job of selling it), but it ended up being the first Steam game I've ever refunded. I know the dev team is small (I think two people?), and I would genuinely love to see this game improve. I would be more than happy to check it out again then. Until that time, I can't recommend this, even to hardcore FPS fans.
