_childDocuments_.review: I've only found out about Sprawl recently, with the first thing that caught my eye being the key visual/cover art. After 10 hours with it I can confidently say that the game is fun but not completely free of blemishes. My first run through the campaign took me around 4.5 hours, then I spent somewhere under 3 hours on my second one and the rest of my playtime was dedicated to the auxiliary time attack and horde modes.First off some technicalities, I've played Sprawl on the patch 1.4. The game offers a good suite of tweakable options like the strength of the weapon bobbing effect, separate sliders  for camera tilt during strafing and wallrunning, couple of crosshairs to pick from, all of the keybinds can be changed and there's even a whole tab dedicated to tailoring the difficulty to one's needs. It's all really nice to see, especially the weapon bobbing as I find that somewhat distracting in most games. As for the performance, the game ran at locked 240 FPS at 1080p with maxed out details and DLAA enabled on my RTX 3060Ti. I've got no complaints here and I assume that the game will run well on just about anything.I'm going to keep the paragraph about story short and just say that it's there. It's a cyberpunk setting, the protagonist goes on a vendetta against the evil government while being aided by an AI voice in her head and that's pretty much it. It's neither original or nuanced and it doesn't have to be either as I don't think anybody expected a gripping narrative in an action oriented FPS.In a rather bizarre decision the devs decided to lock a lot of the game's lore and world building behind QR codes tossed around on every level that you need to scan and be redirected to a webpage with a lore dump. Regardless if you use your phone to scan them or take a screenshot for an online QR reader you are going to be physically taken out of the game which I find rather baffling. I've scanned a couple of them but to be frank, I couldn't be bothered to dig into it. I've read that the devs want to integrate them into the game but as of the day I'm writing this it still hasn't happened.Now for the main course - the combat. It's solid with a low skill floor and decently high skill ceiling that allows for good amount of player expression. While you can ignore most of the mechanics and still finish it, Sprawl is at its best when you master quickswapping guns, slide jumping, wallrunning and headshot/weakpoint kills during bullet time. I found quickswapping in order to cancel the lengthy delay more powerful weapons have between shots to be especially crucial. Wallrunning feels natural, however it works slightly different than it does in something like Titanfall. The player can only bounce off walls twice so keep that in mind. Bullet time mechanic is tied to resource management which I think is pretty interesting. In order for the enemy to pop a colorful pinata of pickups the player needs to kill them with a headshot or a weakspot while the time is slowed down. There are some exceptions to it, like the shotgun gibbing enemies always dropping resources but in general it's all nicely thought out. To me, the resource management works better than it does in modern Doom games where you're forced to see the same glory kill animations over and over again. It's all smoother and faster in Sprawl.The guns all sound and look great. The roster itself is a standard fare, however there aren't any dead weights that never get used and there is some fun in figuring the optimal one to use at the moment. If anyone rates a game based solely on how good the shotgun is then Sprawl passes with flying colors. It hits like a truck and it can double as a mobility tool for double jumps.While I can sing praises about the player options all day long, I can't do the same for the enemies. They are by far the biggest weakness of this game. They're just dumb. Like, really, really dumb. Their tactics involve two things, shooting and running at the player. Sadly the general lack of brain cells extends to bosses as well. They're far too easy and basic. That being said, the one area where it kind of works is the horde mode. The enemy density in there much higher than the campaign and I had to take a different approach when more than 20 goons were chasing me around. I definitely wish there was some kind of a "rival" enemy or a boss that utilizes the same mechanics as the player. The main part of the game is broken into episodes, much many other throwbacks shooters.  To me the very first one has the most distinct visuals but not necessarily the best combat environments and on the flip side, the later episodes can look bland at times but feature arenas that are much more fun to run through. I would say that the level design overall is a mixed bag.As for the visuals, Sprawl falls somewhere in the Quake era with its textures that look nice from a distance but turn into chunky pixels up close. There are modern lighting and reflection techniques but they all fit neatly into the overall presentation. The general aesthetic is very reminiscent of Ghost in the Shell and Akira in the first episode of the game while episode 2 and 3 kind of fall behind and end up looking like... Stroggos in Quake 2. If they were meant to reference other cyberpunk media like EP1 does then it completely flew over my head.Music on the other hand is consistently amazing throughout. It pays homage to the iconic chants Kawai Kenji used in his soundtrack for Ghost in the Shell and its sequel GitS Innocence while also carving out its own niche with absolutely filthy, chunky, industrial noise. It's definitely an OST that will show up on my playlist for a long time.I don't like rating games on a numerical scale so I will just end with this: Sprawl is a good game from a tiny team with a solid foundation that can be expanded upon in their next work. The areas where it shines are the player options, gunplay and music. The areas where it falls apart are the enemies (AI, variety, bosses) and level design. For me, the pros outweigh the cons and I look forward to seeing more from the people at MAETH.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet cyberpunk parkour FPS that's a little rough round the edges. Satisfying gunplay and movement with generous bullet time lets you feel like a cybernetic monster. Level design fits the bill but suffers from weak signposting, and AI pathfinding has a habit of send enemies leaping off building edges or back and forth between platforms. Boss designs are quite uninspired but makes up for it with a fairly interesting roster of enemies to sprinkle throughout encounters. Could do with a little more variety of NPC barks.Soundtrack is fantastic, taking inspiration from genre classics and Ed Harrison's fantastic work for Neotokyo. Pretty visuals contrasting low-fi cityscapes and cyberstructures with neon lights and the glow of computer monitors.Plot and writing are fine, barely remember what the player motivations really are beyond cool AI voice tells me what to do. Cute QR gimmick for out-of-game narrative interest but gets a bit tedious getting your phone out each time.A great choice for movement shooter and sci-fi fans to fill a Sunday afternoon for about a tenner.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so, so excited for this game. It dropped the day before my birthday and I was super stoked to have time off to play it and to jump into a new shooter with wallrunning and fast paced gameplay, not unlike Titanfall, which had been cited as inspiring the movement for the game.Unfortunately, I feel let down for a few reasons, they are as follows:The movement is really a pain. I haven't gotten through most of the game, but what I did play didn't feel good at all. There's a limit on walljumps per wallrun and it feels really bad, and I don't understand the motivation for adding it. It also seems to be missing the double jump that was so important to covering wide distances and changing direction midair in TF. Opportunities to run over as much distance as you can manage and to be unpredictable and adaptable is one of the things that I now realize make TF's movement so fluid, and at the same time so erratic. Gunplay in SPRAWL is nothing to write home about. Weapons are pretty standard from what I saw, if you've played Quake or DOOM, you know what to expect. The enemies that you're shooting with said guns are also nothing special, and something feels missing from the AI. They tend to group up a lot, which doesn't make them fun to fight, and the arenas in which you fight them are often either too small to feel good to navigate with the game's movement system, or too large for the enemies to handle, because they don't spread out. My last couple of issues are probably a bit more up to personal preference, or my own stupidity. Either way: The levels feel large, and easy to get lost in - which isn't a good thing, since there's not much to find. I kept finding myself getting turned around and accidentally walking back the way I came. The levels, while distinct from each other, don't do a good job at making navigation easy. Especially with the verticality that a movement system like SPRAWL's fosters, having the levels look so same-y the whole way through can really throw you off. Having to stop myself to reexamine just where exactly I'm supposed to be going just isn't good design. Lastly, the slow-motion ability adds nothing and is really counter-intuitive in a game that's meant to be fast paced - it breaks up the combat too much. "Well, if you don't like it, don't use it!" Sure, but that doesn't make it seem like a good design choice. I don't remember who said it, but somebody said something about players and how they will always find the least fun way to play the game, and do it. I would be lying if I said that I wasn't using it way more often than is actually fun.TL;DR: If you wanted Titanfall again, or DOOM again, you're looking in the wrong place.  SPRAWL probably isn't a bad game - but it's not going to be your next obsession.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting and preview looked interesting but when you get down to it, pure style over substance.The AI is braindead. It always rushes head on toward you, never uses cover, never flanks, does not grenade and never creates any distance to fire at you from afar. All you have to do to counter the AI is camp in a corner or run small circles. Most of the time you will find yourself clipping their heads off like zombies as they line up in a convenient straight line. When killed they turn into an unsatisfying puff of blood. I expect more from cybernetic warriors.The guns available for use are best described as generic, akimbo does not equal exciting. The guns did not even react 50% of the time to mouse clicks until I changed the settings from default windowed to fullscreen mode. It turns out this is a commonly reported error in an FPS! This game has been out for over a year....The multi-directional level design is bad because it makes the worst mistake of all, it's confusing, the game progression relies on travelling by jumps and wall-run through the map without strongly advertising direction to the player by environmental prompts, markers or arrows, this conflicts hard with the fast pacing the game tries to establish through the music and character movement speed, the result is this causes constant breaks to immersion and increases frustration.E1 is said to have the "best" design of the entire game. I decided to stop playing before E2,E3 to get a refund. Be aware this becomes an arena shooter. It is worth noting that there is woke political pandering squeezed into the codex for no apparent reason. The game is not very long, 5 or 6 hours so there is that too.

_childDocuments_.review: Has it's issues, but the music and art direction is excellent.It's like Ghost in the Shell and Ghostrunner had a LoFi-Neo Tokyo baby, with even more classic cyberpunk anime references mixed in. I really dig this style, especially when it pulls out all the stops.The wall run is a bit short & the three wall bounce limit feels a bit cludgy (has been adressed in updates!), but overall the movement can be fun & the level design supports it well. A lot of cues were taken from Titanfall 2 & Ghostrunner, though for me it doesn't emulate that "free flow" as nicely, and the basic pace isn't nearly as fast, unless you *really* get into the movement tech.Could definitly use a mantle ability that works regardless of wall bounce status.The guns feel alright, enemy types are distinct, easily recognizable & readable, but not that many.The difficulty curve nicely paced so far. Some encounters are too easily cheesed because of the *really* simplistic AI, especially early on, but the fights pick up in ferocity quickly. Bosses are - as per usual for FPS - a bit meh. If you don't nail your headshots, the TTK can be kinda high for such a relatively quick game.So far, I feel ~10 - 15 bucks is a fair price for this!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been following the development of this game for a year and half and now it is finally released. First I wanna say that I am an absolute sucker for wallrun mechanic (thanks Respawn for killing TF|1 and TF|2 I hate yall for that btw). Now I understand people might want to compare this game to Titanfall because of its emphasize on wallrun mechanic but with how the combat in this game is designed I think it's fair to say that this game flows more like traditional Doom 2016 instead of Titanfall. Hell, it probably doesn't even feel like Doom 2016 the way your positioning doesn't really matter because enemy AIs often swarms you in tight group instead of scattering (depending on how you view it, this might be easier or harder to handle). The wallrun mechanics also works nothing like Titanfall. You can't increase momentum while wallrunning  this game actually let you jump to reach higher side while wallrunning in the same wall. It felt janky when you first started it but when it clicks it feels good just to surf around some walls while kiting enemies. Some people might be familiar with also heavy-emphasize-on-wallrunning game Get To The Orange Door, which this game kinda play pretty similar to that but unlike GTTOD you can actually wallrun on  and the wall doesn't just suck you into it. Now into the nitpicks: the SMG and the Shotgun felt so weak. People complained the shotgun is slow to use but I guess it's intended to be that way because you're supposed to do fast weapon combo with it but the damage is honestly just isn't there. It felt so  to use especially when you have to engage multiple shotgun enemies to the point even the starting pistol is much more reliable. The SMG doesn't have good sound feedback to it and it sound like a stapler gun instead of actual gun, and I can't tell at all if the damage is consistent or not. Also a few sound bugging here and there but I'm pretty sure it will be fixed.With that being said, I think this is a pretty solid game. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: While Sprawl has some shortcomings in its AI capability, level design, and the final episode dragging on a bit (and not being able to turn off head sway or automatic weapon switching) these are drastically overshadowed by the quality and passion shining through the game. The weapons are chunky and satisfying, it's fun to blow up enemies, and the movement (while somewhat clunky compared to its high-mobility contemporaries) is excellent. Any time I died, it felt like it was me screwing up over the game being cheap. Well, besides the time it auto-switched my shotgun to my grenade launcher when I was up close. Enemy variety does tend to suffer toward the end, and I wouldn't call the final boss particularly challenging, but it wraps up nicely. The music... my god the music. It can be a bit too dubsteppy for my taste at times, but as a whole, I can tell I'll be listening to this in my car.There's clearly some lore scattered about via QR codes, though I didn't find the setting or characters compelling enough to really scan them all. Maybe it all leads to a secret second half of the game, iuddno.I get the feeling that the devs would have loved to do more with this and really expand the story, but I'm still going to give a standing ovation for this being primarily a two-person team. Like... damn. I saw this recommended by Civvie11 and decided to check it out. I noticed that it was 15 bucks and considered waiting on a sale, but every time I pick up one of these games at a discount, I later regretted not giving the devs every dollar they deserve, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do they deserve it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts off really strong. The fundamentals of moving and shooting are smooth, and the slow-mo bullet time keeps the focus on hitting enemy weakspots and managing resources Doom Eternal-style. Wall running is clunky, though, and some of the guns feel strange. The shotgun in particular is so much weaker than the other weapons that I wonder if some damage values got switched around by mistake.By the end of the second episode, enemy variety reaches a high point, making individual fights fun and engaging, but the pacing becomes a mess. The platforming section during the final mission gets a special mention for being extremely broken and in severe need of playtesting. The subsequent boss is a bullet sponge that barely fights back. I was ready for the game to be over long before the credits finally rolled.There aren’t many games with this exact combination of cool mechanics, but there are many games with more polish. SPRAWL is an impressive project from a team of just two developers, but not an outstanding play experience the whole way through. I would only recommend this one if you’re specifically looking for parkour and FEAR-style slow motion.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an experience. I enjoyed it, but it's a little short and the best levels (by far) are in the first third of the game. In the other two thirds I had a few levels where it wasn't obvious where to go at points and managed to softlock myself once. When the game flows, things are great, so these moments where I was stuck really stood out.There's a lot of parkour going on and the game is almost too leanient with it. It's pretty easy to recover from a slightly undershot jump and if you fall off you get put back where you were with no damage. It's less frustrating this way, but it did make me feel a bit less like I earned success. I definitely finished it feeling like there was more to master for getting around arenas.The soundtrack is really good. It's perfectly on theme and it made this one of the few games where I don't put something on in the background to listen to while playing. It also has a visual style that fits perfectly.Gunplay very occasionally felt off, but it was less of an issue than the weird weapon balance. The shotgun is better for taking out mechs than the grenade launcher. The rocket launcher is more of an explosive sawed off shotgun but without being anywhere near as fun as that sounds. This wasn't a fun-killer, but that and the enemy AI could really use tweaking.

_childDocuments_.review: As often with indie FPS, the visuals are appealing, but the game wears off after a while, and the real problems show.The lights, the artistic direction, the design of weapons and the sounds : everything is looking and sounding great !You truly feel like playing in a Ghost in The Shell / Observer / Blade Runner atmosphere.But as much as I find Sprawl really badass, it's not a rewarding shooter.Basically it's an fps in which it's not satisfying to shoot at things.Enemies take a lot a time to bring down, unless you manage to shoot their weak parts. And that is if the game consider that you did so. The hitbox/hitscan is not working well all the time imo.And if you don't hit the weak parts, well, it becomes a frustrating spongy mess.In order to help you, Sprawl introduces different interesting gameplay elements such as wallrun/jump and Bulletime adrenaline, which both works pretty well in-game.But the maps eventually get filled with so many various enemies archetypes that you lack bulletime more than often. As for the wallrunning stuff, it just buys you time to survive and look longer after ressources.It felt rather like a management game than a shooter. You have to plan very quickly your next moves because enemies shoot from afar or try to close you in, and they don't react equally to your weapons. So you end up managing a ton of parameters. Every threat encounter in the game was more and more of an unfun struggle as I progressed through the campaign. When you are done cleaning an area, you think "finally, god" instead of "wait, where is the rest ??".Otherwise I had a fairly good time trying to follow the story, discover the world and doing some platform exploration here and there. I feel just disappointed by the fps part.After scratching my head around it all, I figured it's likely that Sprawl is targeting a narrow public, which I'm maybe not a part of ?I tried my best to give it a long shot, but I grew bored of the gunfights eventually all turning into tiring puzzles.Regardless, I'll keep an eye out for future MAETH products.

_childDocuments_.review: Great movement, great Ghost-in-the-shell-esque OST, awesome cyberpunk atmosphere.Unfortunately, the gunplay is awful. The weapon impact is almost non-existent and enemies don't react to being shot. When enemies get low on health, they are stunned, and you are practically forced to 'decapitate' them with a melee slash (their head just evaporates out of existence) in order to get ammo and health & armour, exploding in a clownish confetti like a zoomer doom knock-off. After dying, they fall to the ground in a slow, exaggeratedly schematic way and turn into a poorly-made ragdoll.Neither shooting guns, nor killing enemies is satisfying in this game about shooting guns and killing enemies. It's not a big deal, though - the market is rife with boomer shooters nowadays.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is an exceptional first-person shooter that masterfully blends retro aesthetics with modern gameplay mechanics. Set in a dystopian future, the game offers a fast-paced, adrenaline-pumping experience that keeps players on the edge of their seats.One of the standout features of “Sprawl” is its incredible soundtrack. The music perfectly complements the intense action and dark atmosphere of the game, enhancing the overall immersion. Each track is meticulously crafted to match the high-energy gameplay, making every moment feel epic and engaging.The gameplay itself is a brilliant mix of classic shooter elements and innovative mechanics. The parkour-inspired movement system allows for fluid and dynamic combat, giving players the freedom to navigate the environment with ease. The gunplay is satisfying and responsive, with a variety of weapons that cater to different playstyles.Visually, “Sprawl” impresses with its unique art style. The low-resolution textures combined with modern lighting techniques create a distinctive look that sets it apart from other games in the genre. The level design is intricate and well-thought-out, providing a perfect playground for the game’s fast-paced action.In conclusion, “Sprawl” is a must-play for fans of first-person shooters. Its combination of thrilling gameplay, stunning visuals, and an outstanding soundtrack makes it a standout title in the genre. Whether you’re a veteran of retro shooters or a newcomer looking for an exciting challenge, “Sprawl” delivers on all fronts.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a sick retro FPS with a cyberpunk twist, inspired by Ghost In The Shell and Mirror’s Edge. You’ll zip through a gritty future city, blending smooth parkour with intense shooting. The game looks and sounds amazing, with a killer industrial soundtrack. While the story is light, the fast-paced combat and cool movement mechanics make it super satisfying. After finishing the main game, dive into time trials and horde mode for extra fun. Sprawl is a must-play for FPS fans. No seriously this game is so sick you have to play it.Full Review:

Story delivers a rich narrative experience set in a dystopian future where corporate power and underground factions collide. _childDocuments_.review: Very good shooter, interesting weapons with some unique quirks, great slow-mo, amazing movement. Level design is a bit all over the place, and way too much reliance on "find three switches". Enemy variety could be better, for the most part you just aim at a head and shoot, while there is reason to switch weapons and mix usage, it's rarely because of enemies, and mostly just because of how weapons are designed including relatively low ammo counts. Like shotgun has very long reload between shots, and smg is low range but very high dps, so you want to swtich to pistols in mid range, get a few headshots on weak enemies, then get a shotgun shot, then swap to smg and so on.Absolutely gorgeous visuals and music. Like, seriously, it's almost like soundtrack alone is worth the price of this game. Voice acting is also lovely. Very good experience overall and one of my favorite shooters of the last few years.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good for a game made by just two people. The bullet time and weak points are fun additions, wall running feels good and weapons are fun to shoot and mostly balanced so you need to do some weapon swapping combos. The difficulty felt right when setting the enemy damage to 1.5x. Also the soundtrack slaps.It has minor issues though. The game never really refine it's core ideas or introduce mechanically new enemies so it can get a bit repetitive, the number of enemies stays moderate through the whole game and the level design got me running in circles many times, even if it was for a couple of a seconds. On the other hand it's pretty short game so it doesn't overstay it's welcome. Get it on sale if you are in need of some decent shooting.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: What a great game! It is as if Doom and Max Payne had a child which grew up and made his own footprint. The game is addicting and the fluid, satisfying gameplay not only fills up my adrenalin ingame. It is so satisfying when you do a wallrun, jump towards a group of enemies and do 3 headshots midair during bullet time, all that combined with an incredible soundtrack. The only negative thing I could say is that sometimes it isn't clear where to go and - at least me - sometimes ran around several minutes to find the path. The narrator is well designed too, I do hope that the game is not that short and there will be an addon or even Sprawl 2 in the future. If you like fast-paced shooter, try it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game defines itself as a "good enough" boomer shooter. I do not like how sometimes the enemies get stunned and lock on 1HP when they should have died, which isn't rewarded by a glory kill but you're meant to slash when you could also just headshot, and it just feels like it simply shouldn't even be there to begin with. The enemies are fine, the map design is good, and the game is fun but it doesn't feel like it works right together, especially with the guns. The dual-wield pistol is my favorite but eventually it just becomes weak, the shotgun is fine but it doesn't work when the game demands you to get headshots, so you need to be far too close for comfort. The uzis, or whatever they're called, have spread and I barely used them because they do. The grenade launcher works fine but for some reason it is way too weak and doesn't feel satisfying at all to use against what is supposed to be lower-tier enemies to mechs. The laser cannon requires you to be too precise and you'll surely miss way more than you want to. The chaingun is really, really strong but it hinders your movement greatly which is far from recommended. The rocket launcher is an absolute sin, requiring mid range or else it kills you if too close or scatters all around when too far. The story is there, the game reminds me much of Ghostrunner, but while it is a fun game I don't recommend it unless you can get it for cheap, since it is a very short game.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing tons of boomer shooters I can easily say that FLOW is the most important thing in these games - at least for me. Some games gravitate more towards Doom-like vibe or heavier Quake-ish energy. SPRAWL is very close to the vibe of Dusk (in my opinion the best boomer shooter of all times) - you can bunnyhop, game keeps you on edge, but you don't die enough to break the state of your flow.On top of that - as we all know - shooter is only as good as it's shotgun and SPRAWL's shotgun is really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good.Grab it on sale. Game is great albeit really short. Once more content is added it will be well worth it - in a sense it already is, but you know what I mean.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't trust my steam hours- I have atleast 10+ hours of this game because I pirated it. But it was too good not to own it and the updates made it feel more fun and aggressive.What makes this game fun is that other games have wall-running. Other games have shooting. Other games have slow-mo. But Sprawl combines them where the movement feels so well-executed that you just want to keep playing until you mastered the movement mechanics.If a game makes you want to buy it instead of having it for free- I can't think of a better endorsement of it's quality.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fairly simple, fun and addicting game, bottlenecked by being really short.-Graphics are stylish, very simple yet polished. Enemies are varied, easily recognizeable and fit the theme, from common troops to mechs and mutants and such. Areas are your bog-standard cyberpunk dystopia locations (not a bad thing but they really are), these include city skylines, sewers, factories, big computer complexes etc. The guns looks great and feel great to shoot at things. Just good 8/10-Music is the star of the show here, great tunes, reminiscent of Ghost in the Shell which is great. Straight up bops, no problem here 10/10-Gameplay is fluid, you can bullet-time,you can wall run, wall jump 3 times, slide etc., it honestly feels like a mix of Titanfall 2 and Doom/Quake. Enemies have weak points, if you kill them with that you get your resources back, so you can chain enemies as much as you want. With the guns being pretty varied (Akimbo Pistols, SMGs, shotgun, railgun etc) the gunplay is fun, enemies are not the hardest (except anything with explosives) and yeah it's great. 8/10-Story: it exits, not the focal point, not really interesting, there is a plot twist that's pseudo intersting but that's all, not counting it into the experience, it's like saying Quake 1 is bad because the story is bad.-Sometimes slowdowns occur, not that annoying but it happens.-Really short, only around 3-4 hours, there are Time Trials and Horde modes, but those don't extend the gameplay as much as you would think.-Yeah that's about it. This is a great game when you buy it on a sale. Honestly I compare it to SUPERHOT (Which I reviewed , not by best review but still stands), short, fun, won't leave a mark in your brain most likely but you will enjoy it while it lasts, and honestly this game was made by 2 people who just wanted to make a game they liked, and they succeeded in that, which I respect. I give it a 7/10, not bad, just a wee bit short.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Hot damn, that was f%^$in fun! I just wish there was another 2 or 3 or 4 chapters!It's like Ghostrunner, if you didn't die in like two hits.Seriously though, if you like any of the following things: Ghost in The Shell, Titan Fall, Ghostrunner, Mirror's Edge, Max Payne, etc. this is the game for you. It's pretty short, but what is there is damn impressive for a two person dev team!Aesthetically this game looks very much like it came out of a Masamune Shirow Manga, like Appleeed, GitS, Tank Police, etc. And the music matches that vibe perfectly! With 90's Drum n' Bass/Industrial fused with Asian choral voices, and percussion (which after I saw the credits, I learned was composed by one of the two lead programmers.)I have to give the devs big props too for adding so many difficulty options. I found the perfect settings for my play through to maximize on the fun and cut down on the frustration. If you like your boomer shooters more punishing though, you can totally up the difficulty or tweak the range of incoming and outgoing damage and adrenaiine usage. Also big ups for not giving Six fall damage for falling in a pit, or worse, outright killing her.  Also, I really found this game to be a lot easier on my 46 year old hands, as the addition of the very generous Adrenaline meter adds a really nice ebb and flow to the gunplay. Unlike most Retro/Twitch/Boomer Shooters, the player doesn't have to be hyperfocused on everything happening around them all the time, because the bullet time effect gives you a nice amount of time to make those split-second decisions. And take a breath, between assaults.Overall, I am really glad I saw this mention in ZlimBratski's 2023 awards video, because this was definitely one of my favorite indie shooters of the year! Similar to Trepang 2, very short, but what is there is super fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun with an awesome soundtrack and it doesnt really outstay its length so much so that I went for 100% completion so why the negative review?Forced politics and bad game design, those two things are the core huge issues with Sprawl. On the forced politics front we have political refrences to things like feminism and identity politics in codex entries that make almost no sense, Most of the codex entries are fine insight into the world but quite a few are nothing but buzzword heaven with no appropriate use of these political references that make it feel as forced as some of the current Sweet Baby Inc stuff at the moment, its not clever and its not used well at all. Add to that a certain flag in the ending credits added only because one of the devs is that identity and you can see the kind of people Sprawl was made by, I found this especially wierd and voiced my questions about this in the steam discussion group for Sprawl to which I assured that I only wanted to discuss this aspect of the game and was as polite as I could be and my thread was locked along with a witty childish response from the lead developer. I don't like this kind of thing in games and to see it basically snuck into an otherwise good yet flawed game is weird bordering on creepy.The game has a bunch of weapons to use but none are paticularly designed well. Shotgun jumping may sound fun but doesnt work properly, the chaingun slows you down and also needs a long wind up in a game all about speed? The railgun also requires a charge up and is underpowered and the games big super weapon is a rocket launcher thats just not very nice to use. The core gameplay is satisying but these weapons are just not designed as well as they could have been.Sprawl could have been a cyberpunk lower budget version of the modern doom games but instead it feels like somones wierd political pseudo philisophical rants injected into a modern doom clone that needed a lot more dev time. Its not a good sign when the slowdown mechanic that your game sells itself on can basically be ignored for two thirds of the game. I enjoyed my short time with Sprawl but I do not reccomend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Either this game is a bit short or I just moved too fast; either way, great pick up to play for all you movement tech heads out there. This game draws heavily inspired by old boomer shooters, but the movement system it has feels very similar to Source Engine (with, imho, very notable influences from Apex's heavily modified SE). I don't think it gets overwhelming throughout, rather the game demands that you have figured out the mechanics and combos just in before the rampant amount of enemies to defeat. It's very fun, very fast, very quake. Wall-running is fun and I had fun shotgun bouncing off troops while slowing down time. Arenas are well-crafted, except for the first boss', and the gunplay is very fun. I love the setting, love the art direction, everything is gritty and dystopian.What I dislike about the game is the AI pathing, in where the enemies get loopy and stupid and bunch up together and that's just an easy clear + adrenaline refill with a grenade launcher/crit shot on jetpacks. The "bosses" aren't really bosses and just an introduction to enemy types you later on encounter especially when the game ramps up the amount of enemies present in the arenas. The game allows creativity in battles but it doesn't reward you for said creativity. I enjoy making my own routes to objectives instead of the normal route, but there's one specific chapter in the game that involves metropolitan even I got lost.Love this game, it has some replayability (atleast for me). I'm looking forward to this game's post-development and new projects from the team.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of a lightning-fast kinetic shooter is a great one, but is not applied in any way that could be called functional or fun. The main mechanic on display here is killing enemies by hitting their weak points while you are in "bullet time". Engaging bullet time costs adrenaline, a finite resource typically earned from killing enemies from bullet time. Are you noticing a problem with this loop? If you run out of adrenaline against an early enemy and have to get a normal kill, you're screwed. Not putting adrenaline refresh on a timer stops this tech demo right in its tracks. When the game is meant to be played in a fast frenzy, you probably shouldn't make it so difficult to play that way, or punish players for taking a more logical approach to playing. It takes a lot for a game to frustrate me, but I hate Sprawl. There is nothing at all beyond the surface layer. Avoid now and save yourself from the refund process.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is basically Ghost Runner as a boomer shooter with a boring soundtrack. It was advertised a lot with its wall-running mechanics and the shotgun jump, but they come absolutely short and don't have any real use in the game except for a few short parkour sections.I followed the development on Twitter for a long time, and after all my hype, SPRAWL is just... a boomer shooter. A very regular, average boomer shooter, in the same vein as Ion Fury, that doeesn't know how to make use of its redeeming qualities. After E1M1, you've essentially seen the whole game already. And after E1, when you leave the city, it becomes a sluggish grind through uninteresting environments with enemies that bring zero innovation except for being annoyingly bullet-spongy. After less than 2 hours of straight repetitive "jump around in bullet time like Max Payne and aim for weak points like those on Resident Evil bosses" action, I just found it absolutely tiresome and was already looking forward to seeing the credits. And I couldn't even vibe with a good soundtrack.SPRAWL is somewhat decent if you expect nothing more than a regular boomer shooter that throws in a short wall-run once in a while. I just wish I had anything positive to say about it other than that. It's only 3.5 hours in length, 1 of which is fun, and not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is gonna be a little bit complex.SPRAWL absolutely nails a good boomer shooter atmosphere. The guns sound and feel good. The enemies are cool. The soundtrack fits the game really well. The progression in the missions is also very good, starting out in outskirts and progressively getting deeper and deeper into the game. The game also has secrets in terms of the hidden "QR Codes" that you pick up as a lore thing, both regular types and very rare types called "Mother QR codes". It actually also has some minor secrets with item pickups here and there, but they dont actually count as secrets or anything. All the levels in the game are cool, and the bossfights or bosses themselves are cool. The game also comes with a few extra features. A horde mode with 5 maps and some different time trials that are actually quite good.There are so many cool and good things to say about SPRAWL, HOWEVER the game simply is first of all WAY WAY WAAAY too easy, and MORE IMPORTANTLY the reason WHY it is too easy is because of a huge design FLAW in the combat. I dont know if this game is this easy by intention. I only died once by enemy gunfire and that was solely due to playing like absolute crap in a moment of complete carelessness. So what is it that is so flawed with SPRAWL? The problem is extremely apparent when trying the survival mode for instance. The game just simply feeds YOU WAY too much health and adrenaline when getting a kill, and you kinda need adrenaline to enter slow-mode to hit the enemy weakspots. That is needed for enemies to drop ressources, like health and ammo and MORE adrenaline. So you enter a loop situation where you are pretty much unkillable, because you get so much health and adrenaline from drops that you can just keep going in slow-motion and hit enemy weakspots. Im honestly pretty confused why they made the game like this. This "loop" situation where you need to have adrenaline, to shot enemy weakspots to get more drops in my opinion kinda breaks the game. That is not too say that the game is unfun to play, but the truth is that this game is flawed at the core. I also never played a boomer shooter that was this easy before. Another minor complaint is that the dual SMGs in the game absolutely suck, but that does not really matter because all the other weapons are absolutely awesome. I also like how they made the Chain gun make you move slower while firing it if you are not jumping or wall-running. That is just a very original idea.TLDR: A really nice game with a great setting, weapons and somewhat satisfying combat, and the reason I saw somewhat is because the Adrenaline/Weakspot system is heavily flawed at the core and makes it WAAAAAY too easy.I think if such a thing as SPRAWL 2 would ever exist, then they REALLY should reconsider how they do this system. For the same reason, I think a horde mode in this game is useless and sucks, again, solely due to how this system is flawed at the core. It is just way too apparent when trying the horde mode.But by all means,  DEFINETLY get this game if you like Boomer Shooters. The game is easy as ♥♥♥♥ with the flawed system, but because the game IS excellent in pretty much EVERY other regard, it totally makes up for it. I highly recommend the game still.

_childDocuments_.review: Controller players beware.  The controller support is so bad it might as well not exist.  With controller aim assist on, the stickiness is way too high, and you will involuntarily spin in circles following any enemy that charges past you.  With it disabled, it's disabled.  Good luck getting headshots in a game where the main mechanic is getting headshots.  Also, adrenaline slows down your aim to the point where you actually can't keep up with fast moving / charging enemies that are close to you.  To top it all off, the menus pretty much don't work with a controller.  If you scroll down at the main menu, you can't even scroll back up to the new game / continue button.  Half the time the menu also just won't register button presses, so have fun constantly selecting the wrong option from the menu.So, yeah.  I know boomer shooters are kbm first type games, but it's obvious the controller support is completely tacked on just so they can check the box that it's technically supported.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad to say I've refunded this game and cannot currently recommend it. This is despite having followed its development and eagerly anticipated it for a long time. If the (clearly very talented, nice and passionate) devs see this review I've listed some of my issues and potential fixes below.1: wall-running: a lot of people have complained that this mechanic is janky. I actually found that once I worked out how it works (strafe into the wall as you go) it was ok mechanically. My issue and I believe many negative reviewers' issue is that this game was marketed to them as a "hardcore retro FPS" - not a platformer. The challenge should not be in getting to a combat arena, it should be in using these mechanics in combat. I don't think maps can be redesigned or the mechanic substantially altered at this stage of development, but perhaps a fix would  be a toggle for 10% further/higher wall-jumps or no height-loss during wall runs for folks who just want to get to the next combat arena.2: checkpoints: checkpoint systems work well in games with regenerating health. They do no work well in this game, as you can get stuck in a loop of getting to a checkpoint without the resources you need for the next fight and dying over and over - which in  turn means you need to redo the platforming to get to the next arena, compounding issue number 1. Sometimes you finally beat an encounter and feel like you've broken the loop, only to die a bit further on and go back to bad checkpoint because you haven't hit the next one. Again I doubt its feasible to completely re-engineer the save system at this juncture, so why not just add an option on death: "go to last checkpoint", "go to last checkpoint with at least 50% health and ammo", "go to last checkpoint with 100% health and ammo". 3: AI - this is really bad at times. If I'm standing on a roof and there are dog enemies on the next roof, firing one shot at one dog makes them all run straight off the roof. There is no easy fix here, but there does need to be a fix.4: gun play: guns feel weak to me. some improved sound, feedback on whether you are hitting (and whether hitting weak point or not, e,g. some red particles for the latter) would help a lot. Also, let me just hold down the fire button even on the pistols. constantly left clicking in a game like this is a pain. There are a whole bunch of minor bugs and issues I won't list, I'm sure the devs have seen the comments and will sort.In summary, would like to like the game, would repurchase if issues sorted or there was a commitment to sort them, but I simply can't have fun with the game right now. While I admire the attempt to launch in 1.0, this game would have benefited from early access. It feels like a 0.9 version - largely there but with a lot of polish and response to player feedback required.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Peak Peak Good fun, but I did find that the gameplay loop became somewhat repetitive in the later levels. As a result, I began to rush through the game more at some point. Additionally, I have mixed feelings about the boss fights in episodes 2 and 3. In general, though, the combat felt solid and satisfying.The movement in general is pretty good, but has some flaws. My main gripe is the lack of methods to maintain momentum/combat speed loss. There is a constant deceleration applied to your speed, causing you to inevitably slow back down, no matter what.When compared to games like Titanfall, where movement involves a smooth flow of gradually increasing speed and skillful utilization of movement mechanics to sustain it, Sprawl feels a lot more "stop and go" in that aspect, lacking a similar level of smoothness. This doesn't really matter for the combat arena parts, but is definitely noticable to me in the more open traversal outside of them. While I understand that the movement wasn't intended to be an exact replica of Titanfall, considering it likes to call itself "Titanfall-like," I wish it would have taken a bit more inspiration in that regard. While Sprawl isn't flawless, there is still a lot to like about it. I would still recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: incredible movement shooter. Very smooth movement that is simple on the surface but with more depth underneath. If you like movement tech in games then theres some good stuff on offer here: slidehop, wallrunning, shotgun jumps and these can be used in conjunction with each other to create even bigger boosts in speed. Lots of opportunities to chain together movement in a nice flow. If you don't have any interest in learning movement in fps games then i'm not sure how well you'll get along with the game but the combat and gunplay is at least a lot of fun so there is still that.Weapons are great to use. pistols and smgs feel satisfying. Shotgun is done very well. seems to be a trend recently in fps games to exclusively include fast rate of fire weapons (even shotguns will have fast rof) and it can feel too spammy with no aiming skill required so its great to see in Sprawl the shotgun is powerful with a low rate of fire. and you can quickswap the shotgun to get around this too so its the best of both worlds. feels a little bit more involved rather than just holding mouse1 the entire time.railgun used to be my favourite weapon but in a patch it was buffed to make the charge time insanely fast now. too fast for my liking. barely feels like a railgun now. I appreciated the high risk high reward nature of the old railgun. You could always feather the charge too which made the gun interesting but now theres no point as it shoots so fast.music is great and fits the atmosphere well.game is incredibly well optimised and runs smoothly.Episode 1, taking place in a grimy dystopian city, has some excellent level and environmental design but episode 2 and 3 drops off pretty severely in that regard giving way to vast open areas set in factories and large structures that will blend together quickly.Theres definite flaws to the game; some parts feel like development was rushed, cant skip cutscenes, some interactivity you'd expect from playing other games isn't present here like bottles are just static models and can't be shot, AI tend to chase the player and will end up bunching up into a mass blob if you move around too much, different enemy types have a lot of cross over and dont feel too unique unlike quake for example with each enemy filling a distinct role.But the flaws dont matter to me as the core of the game is so strong with movement and combat being a blast to play.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a hardcore first-person shooter set in a dystopic city in the future that takes a lot of inspiration from old classics like  and , but also from recent cyberpunk titles like . You play as Seven, a super soldier who ends up being betrayed and chased by a military regime known as Junta. After being saved by Father, a mysterious voice in her head, she accepts to free him if he helps her to find revenge in The Spire. Much of the story is narrated by the Father via text descriptions shown during each mission-loading screen, and QR codes that can be found in-game. Unfortunately, the plot of SPRAWL is not deep as I first expected. It can be often very generic and cliché, which is a pity considering what a setting like this can offer.The first thing that will certainly leave you impressed is the soundtrack. It really sounds like “Making of Cyborg” by Kenji Kawai (that’s the  soundtrack, for anyone who doesn’t know). I was actually surprised to hear a similar music theme in a videogame and I think the only time I did was in . I tried to find the lyrics as I’m genuinely curious to know what they say, but at this moment I don’t think they are available anywhere. It seems like a lot of attention went in the music department because even the other ‘90s industrial/electronic music tracks available in the game are fantastic and they enhance all the action sequences. The same cannot be said for the sound effects, unfortunately. There was an annoying sound bug capable of damaging your ears, suddenly increasing the volume on respawn. Fortunately, this was fixed with a very recent update, though it definitely had an impact on my playthrough. Other than this particular issue, the different weapons’ sound effects are decent enough to differentiate them.Starting the game and after a short cutscene you will go through a brief tutorial before jumping into non-stop action. The tutorial mostly focuses on wall running and shooting but, unless I missed a few messages, it doesn’t explain how to crouch, how to collect ammo (you will realize soon after that some enemies drop ammo) and how to switch weapons. If you have played enough FPS you probably don’t need a perfect tutorial, but I’m thinking more about those players who enjoy the cyberpunk setting but can be pushed away by the lack of complete info on how to play. Anyway, wall running is clearly the most important mechanic in the game. You will do that a lot and I must say it still feels a bit clunky and uncomfortable. Even when I jumped correctly, sometimes I had to double jump on the same wall because with my first jump I was about to fall down. The game has some serious difficulties starting wall-runs after jumping. Thankfully, there are no penalties for falling as you don’t receive any damage, but it can become quite annoying when you lose the momentum and you are being shot at from all sides.Other than wall running, combat requires you to be fast and shoot everything that moves. You can temporarily use your ability to slow down time, which helps to aim more precisely at enemies’ weak points (highlighted in orange), such as their heads and jetpacks. You can also attack them using your katana (which is also clunky) and more weapons will unlock as you progress through the story. Sometimes you can try to ignore the enemies and run past them, if you are good enough at wall running and dodging their bullets. Overall, combat feels good enough as it constantly requires you to mix real-time shooting with bullet time. The difficulty is mostly well calibrated, but you must avoid missing your targets and wasting ammo because in some chapters they are hard to obtain and you will need many for the boss fights.Visually the game looks really nice and I appreciated the retro FPS art style mixed with the cyberpunk setting and its neon lights. The performance is also nearly perfect; I didn’t run into any serious bugs or issues other than the ones mentioned above. SPRAWL is a fun and engaging FPS, also thanks to the incredibly good soundtrack and the fascinating cyberpunk setting. The shooting is good enough, though the clunky melee combat and the imprecise wall running can make it less enjoyable at times. It took me around 6 hours to complete the game. A decent length, perfectly in line with the content offered and the price tag. There isn’t any replayability though and the story is not worth experiencing twice, but if you are a fan of the old  and  games you will certainly appreciate SPRAWL’s fast-paced gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Fun gameplay and weapons. Gameplay is like Titanfall 2 plus doom 16 with bullet time.  getting headshots on enemies rewards you with health and ammo, but the small size of their weak points necessitates the bullet time. The aesthetic of this game is great. Dilapidated dense Japanese urban/industrial environments, kind of like Ghostrunner, with traditional Japanese music mixed with techno. Finished in four hours.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I got excited for Sprawl based off the first trailer. Motion based FPS action is something I have always been a fan of. Tribes, Quake, UT, Titanfall, Max Payne, Apex, even Ghostrunner -- they're all games that I have had a stellar time with. It feels like Sprawl attempts to channel all of those games, to mixed success. The motion is fun, with a heavy emphasis on your tipple jump and wall run. But the game itself just lacks the polish that I would want (and compared to the other games listed above). Both the story and aesthetics don't add too much to the experience. The music slaps! But most of my complaints come with the guns and enemies. The gunplay lacks some variety once you get to stronger weapons, and unless you're really practicing; you're going to be using a lot of bullet time to assist. This slows down the game. You'll do a lot of kiting enemies as you dance around their bullets and bodies. But then while you're dancing a random enemy may spawn around you and just do... comical amount of damage! The enemy pop-ins feel quite frustrating. I can't always tell where I am getting shot from and a strong enemy could be unforgiving. Other enemies are kinda a non-factor, like the rail gun turrets. At it's core there is something good and fun here. I played through it all on launch day in about four and half hours. I have empathy for the small team, but I think this just needed a little more polish to really be what it could.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: So far, the game is very fun. Movement and shooting feels very good.If there was anything I could change, it would be these two things:1. Let us slide instantly. At the moment, it only triggers if you're at max(?) running speed. So after a second or so of moving, maybe less. Reason: I use it to dodge and having to be moving for a moment first feels wrong and counter-productive to its main benefit.2. Let us walljump forever, but prevent gaining more height after the first couple walljumps or something so that it can't be abused to get to unintended areas. Reason: Some areas are cramped and when you try to walljump around shooting everything like a badass, you just awkwardly fall after the first couple jumps.A note for some of the players:I've seen some complaints in other reviews and in the forums about the wallrunning/jumping being bad or inconsistent. I have high standards when it comes to mechanics. I criticize the hell out of games when something is slightly off. I'm also usually on the side of, "devs just can't seem to get wallrunning/jumping right." But this time, I have had zero issues with it. It's intuitive. Not once did it do something I didn't want it to do. If you're struggling with it, it is actually a skill issue. It works completely fine. You just need to keep trying until it "clicks" because you clearly expect it to work differently than it does.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I like it. Fast, no reloads, simple but not bland aesthetics.Gameplay that doesn't force you to kill all enemies in every place, you're super fast, why not zoom zoom.One slight problem, you cannot shoot while in elevators, so I died a couple times in them, but hey, that's fine.Also motion blur is under post-processing, wish it was separate.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a vibeSprawl has some realy good atosphere from music and envorment.the Enemies are also great and have good variatythis game also realy pushes you to wepon switch alot becose of the low amo count wich is fine but than i would also like to have a better way to replenish the amo like in doom eternal with the chainsaw.one thing that i didn't like was the sound effects of the guns, they felt weak with no great punch. I am not a sound designer but maybe more echo could bring out the power of some gunsall in all i like the game and the world building i will definitly folow what comes next

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent high-octane time!Parkour cyberpunk shooter with some doom-like arenas and bouncing around. Controls are smooth and the music and atmosphere are phenomenal. Story isn't anything too involved but sets the scene well and there are some neat tidbits secreted around if you feel up to searching for them.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A straight to the point shooter with a retro style and a really strong 1990/2000s cyberpunk aesthetic and a great drum n bass soundtrack. It looks great, movement is really smooth with intuitive wall running which is used a lot for traversal. Combat feels enjoyable and fast, targeting weak points you can see through slow-mo to stun enemies, and executing them with melee whenever possible (killing with either of those methods gives health/slow mo/ammo). Weapons are punchy and sound design is on point.The story is very classic cyberpunk stuff and that's fine, it's there to give you a reason to go on a big rampage through the entire city. I finished the game on hard mode in 6.5 hours, the game is tough (enemies get tanky on hard) but feels fair and checkpoints are generous.I'd say that if you're looking for deep gameplay and platforming, you might be disappointed, but if you dig this style of game and the atmosphere, then it's really good.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought SPRAWL, I didn't even realize that I bought it on the day of release. Usually I never buy Day 1 releases for games I don't know anything about, but SPRAWL looked promising for what what shown, so I gave it a whirl.SPRAWL is pretty fun. If you enjoy parkour shooter games, SPRAWL is one of those types of games. It has a slow motion ability and wall climbing. The whole cyberpunk aesthetic is one I find myself not caring an opinion on in general, but I believe SPRAWL does it fine. I liked how I got a use out of every weapon, like switching to my pistols while my shotgun recharged, or how I wouldn't use adrenaline for my SMGs since they took out enemies faster that way. It's a simple to understand game: You parkour, you shoot enemies, you win. Plain and simple.Some iffy moments are having to get used to the parkour system. You can only jump twice off a wall, and looking where you jump actually does matter. The first area of the game can be troublesome due to adjusting to the mechanics, but it's overall fine. Though I would prefer if the jump height was increased a little, since I found myself barely making jumps, and I mean BARELY. Advice for anyone playing, try wall jumping on the same wall and looking up for extra height to make wall jumping easier.There's a few issues the game has. I got lost a few times, even with the red light indicating a way. Sometimes I would be in a fight and it distracted me from getting key cards, so I'd appreciate a QOL feature where getting a key card is shown on the UI. Sometimes I would spawn and immediately take damage from an enemy, though it only happened two times, three because I believe the one time could have been my fault. There could be fixes with the audio, as sometimes the volume would be too loud and it felt like my lower audio setting were ignored (mainly in the beginning of episodes). Finally, I encountered a bug where my mouses sensitivity would randomly increase for some reason. I did make my Melee MOUSE4, but I never had this issue in any other game.Overall SPRAWL was pretty fun. I played one chapter per day, and got it three days ago, with 4.5 hours upon completion. From what I know, this was made from a small team of developers, so kudos for the developers for the release. I hope the team can fix a few of the issues this game has, but as I said the product was overall a fun experience.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend SPRAWL. Particularly if you enjoy Titanfall, Trepang2, DOOM Eternal or all of the above. It is mostly good with some hiccups on boss fights and in the final episode.I would like to thank Rogue Games for the review key and wish Maeth all the best with SPRAWL.I will be streaming the game on  so please join me there to learn more and ask any questions.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: At its best moments, Sprawl is bullet-time parkour poetry teetering on the precipice of bludgeoning nihilism. While the boss fights are long-winded and offer little variety between them and the later levels feel more rote, acting as a dumping ground for an army of units, there is ecstasy in the way Sprawl moves. Considering this was largely made by two people, it's indeed quite impressive. If you're hankering for something between Titanfall 2's single player and a more forgiving Ghost Runner, Sprawl is more than adequate. While I played 85% of the game with normal functions, I switched it up at the end and beefed up my abilities thanks to the game's thoughtfully accessible settings, which means if you don't want the headache of bullet-hell and just the acrobatic rush, Sprawl has got you covered.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely cool title! Really great for the price. Thought it was gonna feel like quake II based on the screenshots but feels more build engine-y in practice. Like build shooting mechanics but quake ish movement with wallrunning n such. Also just a quick note for the dev, is the "efficiency" stat explained anywhere? Just curious what exactly that is lolol Pros:Environments, movement, pacing, are all very polished and kewl. It is incredibly artistic. The music also SLAPS but the loops can be a little repetitive. Not really an issue since they r gewd. Cons:My BIG gripe is that there is no "arthritis mode" - to continually fire the pistols you have to click each time, there seems to be no option to just hold down the button and have it keep firing. I reallllyyyyy need somethin like that cus my hands be hurtin after clickin away like that lol. The AI also isn't super smart or varied but that aint so bad. The performance also doesn't seem super great despite pixely textures, but it is good and steady enough. No stutters or drops or anything like that. Just wish it could push out a higher framerate lol.Overall it's a great time, worth it for the artistry on display in the environments alone. Looking forward to what the dev makes in the future :)

_childDocuments_.review: I got soft locked in the first 15 minutes. I reached a checkpoint where I was surrounded by enemies, I had no ammo, and I had 5 points of health. Each time I died, I'd start over from the checkpoint, get shot once, and die instantly. After this happened 5-10 times in a row, I uninstalled the game. Cool concept, but it falls apart.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, wanted to like it due to the mechanics, but the combat isn't all that good. You have to be completely reliant on the "slow motion" adrenaline part of the character; otherwise good luck actually killing any enemies, especially in the beginning of the game. If I wanted to rely on bullet time to beat a game I'd go play Max Payne again.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: ...Ok. It's Ghost in the Shell. ...And that's awesome!If it wasn't abundantly clear from the trailer, SPRAWL is a dystopian cyberpunk FPS with a strong parkour flavour and a pinch of time stop, and manages these mix mash of genre quit well, by providing ample maps and a think fast gameplay focused on taking down the enemies quickly and efficiently.Gameplay wise, there are a good variety of guns, robots and maps, and movement (here a key component) has been done with some clear vision in mind.But really, the bangers are the soundtracks (which are HEAVELY ''inspired'' from GitS) and design of environment and maps (again, Ghost in the Shell, especially for ep1, which is the best, in my humble opinion.)  However....To be perfectly frank, the game is loads of fun, but it does have some problem, which actually manage to take the game's level down a few notch (if it weren't for them, SPRAWL could have been an absolute masterpiece, and not just a good game).Number 1: it's a bit clunky. Not that noticeable at first, but there are some moments where it clearly shows (jumping system, hitboxes, ecc... there are many, and taken singularly are not that damning, but all together are a heavy burden for the game). Number 2: I have a strong feeling that the game was rushed towards the end. Actually, a little before that (precisely in the middle of EP2). Besides the point that ep1 is bigger of ep2 and ep3 combined, some part of the plot, the maps (ep2 and ep3 suffer a critical drop from the complexity and Dystopian beauty of the maps of ep1, and were filled by generic sci fi background - although not everything in them, thankfully), the enemies' variety, the bosses and all that really felt rushed, put together for time constrains more than anything else.Number 3 (this is more on a personal level, so you can just ignore this one): how the story is told is...peculiar (which, in theory, is not even bad, just not done ''right''). Basically, there are the main one, told through dialog in game, which is simple in some part, and obscure in other... because it requires  special QR code disseminated through the levels (the second way the game tells its story) which really sets it apart... but unfortunately, in my case, I couldn't enjoy it because some cell phones just don t read them (the whole thing was avoidable by just making something usable in game... but I also was intrigued by the devs choice and, overall, makes even knowing the lore look like a puzzle.To be frank, if it wasn't for that feeling of Ghost in the Shell, dystopian vibes and some really enjoyable fights, SPRAWL could be... welp, not mediocre - the game still has some good gameplay (just not that polished) - but forgettable. ....So! worth playing??YES!SPRAWL may have some defects, but even with those manages to be fun, interesting, striking even! and project like these deserves all the support they can get!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredibly fun from start to finish, with very frenetic combat and an intuitive wall-running mechanic that never became dull.It is, however, short.It took me just over 5 hours to beat the three episodes in the game, and it left me wanting *much* more. There are horde and time trial modes, but those never 'scratch the itch' in the way story mode does.Still, it's a worthwhile game that slowly but steadily ramps up the difficulty in a way that by the final fight, you'd have had no idea you could take on so many powerful enemies at the beginning of your journey. I recommend it for any fans of boomer shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a fun, quick boom shooter that kinda plays like Quake meets Titanfall meets Coded Arms. Some people will say it has a Ghost in The Shell influence and sure yeah that works. However, this game is definitely a little on the front-ended side where Kowloon is just too good of a setting to (spoilers) drop for the second half of the game. The story I can take or leave, especially when they expect us to get more of the background via broken QR codes scattered across the levels. There is decent enemy variety but not a ton, so you'll be against a lot of the same enemies over and over again. The most appealing elements of SPRAWL are definitely the gameplay, graphical presentation, and soundtrack. It looks a lot like an older PC shooter (or a lot like Coded Arms for the PSP), with up-to-date technology like high quality lighting and DLSS/DLAA to make the game look great on any display. The sound design is mostly good but definitely out-shined by that OST. The gameplay is also very fun for the most part, but input method will determine how "easy" the game is. Controller users who don't turn on gyro (mouse gyro with an RB trigger to turn it off on weapon select) are not going to have fun, I would say. Gyro gives you a better edge, but mouse & keyboard is definitely the way to go with this one. It just clicks a lot better for what mechanics the combat and platforming were designed for. Not to say controller & gyro (regular aim assist is an option but that's not fun imo).Final notes to point out that don't fit anywhere else in this short review is that the game works great with the Steam Deck, no problems here. I also feel the game is fairly priced (I personally got this game for 50% off) with an added Horde and Time Trial mode. I can see myself going back to certain levels and replaying those, so if you're looking for a quick, fun high-action shooter, this is a good choice for a weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges right now, but there is a very fun and satisfying shooter here. like doom eternal, meets ghostrunner, meets fear. it can be frustrating at times, but allows you to tweek the difficulty with sliders until you find what works for you. Something other reviewers here apparently missed.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: HeII yes, Mirrors Edge style movement and game mechanics, futuristic dystopian society, retro-feeling graphics and light-weight on even multi-generation old CPUs.  The adrenaline is similar to the bullet time in Mirror's edge and getting one-shot headshots with the perk-drops is so satisfying.  Wall-running is a blast to confuse the crap out of enemies while you blow their brains out with a shotty 15 feet above them.  Well worth the $15, I'd say even more possibly.Only drawback for me is that I've been out of the shooter genre a while and they really like to pack a lot of enemies in tight spaces.  So, make sure that you've got the wall run, double/triple jump, power slide, and adrenaline mechanics down once you advance a few levels or you'll be ambushed and find health sparse unless you can pull off lots of headshots and melee attacks for those sweet health/ammo/adrenaline drops!  But I won't knock the game for being a challenge.  Learning it is a blast just like it was for Mirror's edge.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, it is a bit repetive with the desaturated textures and gloomy look. But the gameplay is extremely fun, requiring you to constantly switch your weapons and prioritize your targets. Platforming can be a bit annoying at times, but it's not that bad. Music is fast-paced drum & bass and works very well (though individual tracks aren't memorable). All in all, it's a decent boomer shooter to satisfy your needs.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. Super fast-paced first person shooter that makes you feel like a bad-ass. I'm talking jumping off a wall over a guards head, hitting the head-shot in slow-motion before the body explodes in power-ups bad-ass.I dig the graphics, they have a cool retro meets now feel to them.The audio and music are top-notch. The game ALWAYS feels like the music is right in perfect sync with the action and has a cool hardcore house / rave feel to it. HIGHLY recommend playing loudly with headphones on.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: So far I have only completed 1 level (about an hour of playing time) and I haven’t had this much fun on a video game in years. From loading up , the music sets the tone for the experience of the game , dark and chills. The voices used as well are very deep and dark which helps with the feel of the game. In my opinion what sets apart this game from others is the movement. The movement feels fluid , fast , responsive and the wall running has been done very well. Every kill feels rewarding as you can pick up ammo , adrenaline and health. Adrenaline is another unique feature done very well which puts you in a slow motion feel. Towards the end of the first level there’s a closed off area where you’re left alone with a bunch of dogs , people shooting you and people with riot shields coming at you and it reminded me of the old Call of Duty Zombies feel , having to run around figuring out how to kill everyone with little resources. Overall this is a game I highly recommend for anyone whose likes shooters that require strategy.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, and I wish there was more to the campaign. Great soundtrack, art design, and atmosphere, coupled with fluid gameplay. To me this game feels like its got DNA from Ghostrunner, Mirror's Edge, Turbo Overkill, Quake, and Nier. I like stuff about all of those games, so if you find yourself in the same boat, you'll probably enjoy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a good FPS, but it just doesn't offer anything new and neither is it really outstanding in anything. It starts slowly, with two weapons that are not really that satisfying to use. The game improves once you get the shotgun, which might just be one of my favorite shotguns out there, but it really starts to get repetitive after that. Enemy variety is just not enough and all feel kind of similar in their way of attacking, although some are weaker to some weapons and that does make it somewhat interesting, its just really not enough to make this a great game.The music is great, but the atmosphere, levels, visuals and gunplay really feel kind of stale.Recommended for FPS fans that really already played everything available, but with how many great shooters are released recently, I just think that this one does not really stand out, and I would recommend it if the price wasn't above the average for this kind of games. If you like the general gameplay style and movement, I really recommend severed steel, which is, in my opinion, better.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: It's... fine.Its main strength is that it is basically DOOM meets Titanfall. It's fun and not too long.However, if you are anything like me, the default difficulty settings are set to insane values, the game encourages constant weapon switching, and it's hardly any fun to play (plus, ammo can be scarce). Thankfully, this game offers granual control over the difficulty, and playing with easy settings was enjoyable for me.Additionally, this game has terrible level design. While subjectively, I don't like how most maps are quite dark, objectively the levels suck because they do little to show the player where to go. It happened many times that I had no idea where to go.Lastly, I was hoping the game's main strength to be its time trials, but there are only 5 of them. It was a huge bummer (do try to beat my 00:48.74 Shotgun Jump time though).
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl very damn well captures the Retro FPS feel of Quake with a couple of modern mechanics to boot. I'm not certain if the game's wall-running mechanic was intentionally inspired by Titanfall or not, but chances are, this game will scratch that itch for you. To be frank, I hadn't played either Titanfall or Quake, so I'm glad Sprawl was able to synergize them enjoyably!Oh, and the Sound Design...ON POINT! I can't stress how important sound design is for video games, because it means the difference between immersion and distraction. The cyberpunk-styled sonic atmosphere is heavy in tonality, especially among the enemy tells, the punchiness and oomph to each gun...and the quantity of bangers to jam out to doesn't just place the cherry on top- it *slams* it on top.You've got nothing to lose with this one. As far as future support goes, well, it's only about to begin from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, the game is not flawless, but what I immediately appreciate is how fast the developers are answering your questions through Discord, and how damn fast is SPRAWL gameplay.
