_childDocuments_.review: I like what this game is going for art style wise.The soundtrack is nice. I really despise the endlessly repeating NPC voicelines.Dialogue with your guide/mentor/dude who 100% betrays you at the end of the game (or some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ like that) is a bit meh too. "GO MURDER THE GUYS! FIND THE GUN AND THEN KILL THE GUYS! YOU NEED TO SWITCH SOME LEVERS AND KILL THE GUYS!" yeah. I get it pal. I'm on it. The story is okay. Reading the stuff per chapter is nice but it seems rather run of the mill. My name is SEVEN and I'm meetin a guy named SIX? I sure hope its not one of my fellow killin machines that I'm havin some sort of conflict with all of the sudden! Next thing you're telling me I ate a guy called NINE?Combat can be fun, if you're not platforming, you're getting rushed and will probably die much faster so there's some challenge with tracking enemies while on the move. I just really dislike two enemies:The shield bull cops and the stealth warping gals. Shield cops ruin a bit of flow for me? Because I always seem to have to get very up close, jump over them and bullet time spam their heads as I fly by. I can't kill them from further away like every other enemy in the game. And the stealth units can't handle it if you jump around from roof to roof or platform to platform, their AI must ALWAYS warp them onto the same tile as you are so if you jump around you never get to see them until you stand still on that one platform and wait for their warp animation to end and then, because you know exactly where they'll spawn, instantly shoot them in the head. It's a major flow killer when that happens.I think the platforming is alright, its good that you can adjust how strongly you stick to the walls.Most of it consist of easy wall jumps. The biggest challenge in this game seems to be knowing where to go sometimes. (Though at the time of writing I'm rather sleep deprived so I guess that's kinda my fault.)I did drop the game the first time I played during chapter 1 because I just couldn't tell where to go at some point. Was good to pick it back up because I had more fun later. Although I must admit the first boss fight was rather boring...The weapon variety is nice. Enemies get a little bullet spongy the further you get and some weapons just don't feel as useful. The Dual Pistols and SMGs in particular. One of the later guns is interesting, because it slows your walking speed drastically so you're kind of forced to do some platforming while you do it. Speaking of platforming, I kinda wish there were some more challenging sections. There's some timing to do here and there but that's just standing around and waiting for a few seconds. I get that there needs to be a good balance between enemies, platforming difficulty and checkpoints, so that you don't get frustrated as much when you die, but I could do with some sections that aren't only difficult when you're trying to speedrun the game.I'm so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Neon UltraTitansprawl pilled!I'm a Krunkrokstrike 1.6 GTTODstrunner for real!!I'm DOOMed 2 Eternal-ly Edge until I make my Severed Hook Cluster Quask!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I remember being shown some twitter clips of this game and being certain that it was hand designed for me. I love retro movement shooters, I'm a sucker for the cheesy Ghost in the Shell aesthetic, and the soundtrack rips hard.I finally get a chance to play it and at first I'm impressed with the intuitive movement, the bullet time mechanics, the neat platforming. But after a couple of chapters it becomes clear that while the game's style and polish are strong, its core combat, level, and enemy design are shockingly and frustratingly underdeveloped.Weapons are varied but feel so weak and/or inconsistent. The Shotgun is maybe the most egregious offender. I use my slick parkour movement to get right up into a normal enemy's face but I'm one pixel off of their body? Miss. A clump of enemies just asking to be shredded by by a blast of shotgun pellets? Only hits one person, enjoy taking 5 seconds to pump and fire again.The game seems to want you to use specific guns in specific situations, but they're all just kind of underwhelming enough that I just simply found myself scrolling between them, shooting whatever happened to have ammo. To that point, Enemies, especially in later levels, just take an annoying amount of time to kill. Because the guns generally feel weak (aside from some select guns with oneshot potential). there are really no enemies that could be considered "fodder". Even with the "weakpoint" mechanic (Which half of the enemies don't even have) it feels like most guns have me shoot enemies multiple times for the kill. This is fine early on when each wave or room of enemies is like 5 people. It becomes annoying when you hit arenas of enemies with like 30 targets all shooting you at the same time.Additionally 90% of the enemies spend all of combat running directly at you. This makes combat eventually devolve into kiting a conga line of enemies back and forth as you pick them off one at a time. And this leads into the level design, which rotates between confusing maze-like claustrophic hallways and confusing cavernous expanses with the aforementioned conga lines of enemies. The game takes maybe the worst queues from retro FPS level design by having endless secret walls and hatches that you need to locate to progress, frequently shuffling you back through the same core area without a clear goal in sight. The game also frequently makes it hard to understand if I'm even supposed to be killing all the enemies in an area or just running past them. Often I'll be wandering around an empty room looking for an exit before realizing I didn't kill a random guy stuck in the corner, after which I spend another 5 minutes looking for the small door that opened up after I killed him.Overall, the frustrating thing for me was that this game seemed to have all the building blocks for a solid shooter, but just failed to produce a solid core design for those components. Even with all the wall running and slow motion, I just think it failed to make me feel cool or powerful in the way that games like DOOM and Ultrakill do, which is disappointing for a game that has everything else going for it on the style side of things.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying that the game was quite a fun ride for about 85% of the way through; the movement is slick and fun, wallrunning feels natural and precise, the slide could be a teensy bit longer (but it's serviceable as is), the gunplay is visceral and frenetic; every gun has it's place in the arsenal, and once you understand the role of everything, it flows very well, and creates a strong power fantasy when it clicks into place.And the music, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ MUSIC. Every piece is blood-pumping and fits the mood and aesthetics of each level, as well as being outstanding industrial tracks on their own. Enemies are fun to fight, and offer lots of cool interactions and ways of defeating them, ala Doom Eternal (certain weapons being more effective than others). Rushdown enemies keep you on your toes, while anything bigger than your normal goon will require the latter half of your arsenal to deal with. Again, the combat flow, mixed with how the arena design takes wallrunning into account makes for an experience that the market doesn't exactly have at the moment.The bosses are fine. I don't have anything really to say about them other than they are perfectly servicable.This review was originally negative, but they have since fixed the ear shattering bug, so I can now wholly recommend the game :)

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl was marketed as a movement heavy FPS, where parkour and slow-motion are going to play a big role. This is something that it ultimately fails at delivering. The movement is limited to a clunky wall running mechanic, which you'll only use for the platformer segments in between combat encounters. In the combat itself, it is completely impractical and it will, more often than not, get you killed. The slow-motion is useful in the first couple of levels, against the lower-tier enemies, but once the game introduces stronger opponents, you'll rarely even remember it exists.However, does that mean Sprawl is a bad game? Not at all, in fact, there was many things that positively surprised me. I liked the overall pacing of the game, with how nearly each level introduces either a new enemy or a weapon, keeping the gameplay fresh from start till' the end. It also doesn't overstay its welcome with its length, but at the same time, it isn't too short to leave you craving for more.The gunplay itself is also very fun. Nearly every weapon, except for the last addition to the arsenal, functions differently and has its own purpose. And even though the enemies are not standing out with their visual design, gameplay-wise, each of them has a different weakness, which encourages weapon swapping. Though, speaking of weakness, I wish the developers got more creative with the enemy weakspots.TLDR.: If you just want to play a decently long and nicely paced FPS with pretty good gunplay, Sprawl is a good choice. However, if you expected the parkour and the slow motion to play a bigger role in the overall gameplay, Sprawl will definitely disappoint you.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello Im Skill Incarnate and Welcome to My Games Review Series.My reviews cover indie games that i have bought, had gifted to me and have been provided by developers for review.In this episode I check out Sprawl, which was developed by Maeth and published by Rogue Games, the creators of Homebody. Sprawl is an Hardcore First Person Shooter with a Sci Fi/Horror Aesthetic, that takes inspiration from titles like Trepang and the iconic Fear series.The game takes place in the titular city of Sprawl, a dystopian city full of advanced technology and warring Megacorporations. The Player takes the roll of Seven, an exiled super soldier that is being hunted by her former employer. She is forced to join forces with the Father, another former soldier with his own mysterious agenda, in order to escape the city alive.Sprawl allows players to take advantage of a parkour system allowing you to run, slide and wall jump to navigate the gigantic city, along with the ability to slow time. Youll unlock an arsenal including dual pistols, SMGs, grenade launchers and a railgun as you wage a one woman war against the Sprawls inhabitants.This is a fantastic little obscure FPS with smooth controls, fast paced gunplay and some very impressive graphics for an indie game.Please note: All opinions in this video are my own. _childDocuments_.review: I never understand this school of gameplay design where the enemies are bullet sponges, but never mind, there are ammo packs anywhere, and a ton of enemies will spawn on top of you, but never mind, there are health packs everywhere. Why not balance the game around a reasonable number of enemies with reasonable health pools and a reasonable amount of survivability? You spend more time hunting the pickups than you do the enemies. Also I don't understand why there are so many different kind of health packs. Why do the one's the enemies drop look different to the one's that are placed on the map?Also, for a game that seems to be about fast movement, I spent a lot of time confused about the next step. Turns out there is some switch somewhere, but even when I did find it it was often really hard to see. Given it glows a pulse of yellow it's still very hard to find. It's like the game wants to help you on the one hand, but not too much. They could have just made the important stuff more distinct. I don't think it's supposed to be as complicated as it is but the game did grind to a halt several times.Having to walk over the top of a codex entry to pick it up is also really bizarre. I missed picking up the first one because apparently I did not get close enough to it, and there was no prompt to press the E key. Then accidentally walked over the top of the second one and figured out that was what you were supposed to do.The game does not explain the adrenaline meter at all. It would have been nice to know this early enough in the game where it actually mattered because later on when the enemies really start to come out in force it's pretty useless.Also, it was never clear if I needed to hold the space bar in or not in order to stick to the wall. Sometimes you just stick to the wall anyway, sometimes you don't stick until you press the space bar. All these parkour games seem to work the same way and the control scheme never feels right.The mechanism of stunning and enemy and then meleeing them so they drop more stuff is useless in actual gameplay. It never seems to actually work and usually there are other enemies around that will damage you if you try to get close to a stunned enemy.In the end I turned player damage up to 2x and that felt about right and enemy damage down to half but that was probably unnecessary when I started to see how many health packs there are littered around. As I said, I really don't get this kind of thing. I finished the first level. In the end I thought I'd be having more fun if I just replayed Hard Reset Redux or even Super Cloudbuilt.Between this and Fashion Police I think I have been cured of my desire to try a boomer shooter. Both games do what the do, but in the end didn't carry any interest for me. Fashion Police was better at being what it was.

_childDocuments_.review: Really want to recommend this game but it has a fatal flaw with the movement system:1) There seems to be an inability to wall jump infinitely. Seems like a limitation to prevent getting higher and higher in a level, but Titanfall had infinite wall jumping (as long as you touched a new wall)? If this is intended, it would be fine if there was Edge Clambering2) But there is no Edge Clambering. This is absolutely the main reason the game doesn't feel right. If the game had edge clambering, then the limited wall jumps won't be an issue.For example, If you are trying to jump over a small half wall, you have to jump twice to get over it. If you already used all your jumps from wall running, then you can't get on top of itWith edge clambering, you can jump over small gaps instantly by just walking into them, or get to hard to reach platforms more intuitively (even if you are out of jumps). Its in a lot of movement shooters: Doom, Titanfall, Apex, etc.How to do it:1) Spherecast in front of the player and detect a nearby wall, save the world position2) A downward sphercast a few units in front of the player to detect that there is indeed a corner / edge in front of the player (normal vector is almost perpendicular to the first world position)3) Save the world position that is on top of the wall4) Perform a collision check at the new position to ensure the player can clamber and fit inside the space (prevent clip out of bounds)4) Play a fast animation of hands climbing, interpolate player from point A (in front of edge) to point B (on top of edge/platform)Hope this helps, it will make the game feel SO much better. There's a great game here but the movement is really preventing me from recommending it, and I want to!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not great.  It is not difficult, gunplay feels mediocre, the AI is braindead.The soundtrack is not that good. It's decent, but it feels a bit uninspired - Feels like the dev just went up to someone and asked precisely "hey can you make an orchestral soundtrack with weird chanting and combat tracks that are vaguely cyberpunk techno", and that is it. It's just, alright.The art style is good, it is tight, the level design really does mirror the game's namesake - It is a giant sprawl of concrete and it's cool. Nothing to complain here.But the gameplay is where things really fall apart a bit - Movement feels great, but some weapons like the SMG just feel terrible to use, and honestly I just use the revolvers instead because I miss out on the bonus health and ammo from goring enemies and blowing their heads if I use that awful SMG. The minigun has similar issues, but it is actually somewhat usable compared to the SMG since the damage output is higher - But by god, the fact it slows you down (thus making you vulnerable because this is A MOVEMENT SHOOTER) compensates all of that, making it also a ♥♥♥♥ weapon. This leaves you with the following decent feeling weapons: Revolvers, shotgun, grenade launcher - Hardly a stellar lineup...Did I mention the AI is braindead and will not try to evade your attacks, let alone flank you, whatsoever? They'll just get in range with you and try to shoot or stab you. Not good! The entire difficulty of the game, in the few sections that get somewhat complicated, is due to the sheer number of projectiles flying at you, that is it.Overall, compared to other shooters on the market (even in the boomer shooter genre) this one kinda fails. Turbo overkill has a similar setting, but the gameplay is way more exciting (and challenging).At the current discount of 50% it is worth buying, but I'm not sure I'd be happy if I paid full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, cyberpunk world that the developers created here. I really wasn’t ready to review it as I just started playing it, but I really love the experience so far. I feel like this game is influenced a lot by Ghost in the Shell, which is one of my favorite flavors of the genre. The music on the title screen is definitely inspired by the 1996 original film. The gameplay is fast and tight, with a bullet time mechanic, wall running, and only being able to carry a finite amount of ammo (replenished by killing more enemies). You need to be deliberate in your movement and gunshots, or you could find yourself on empty with more enemies to dispatch and only having melee available.The game so far has been very high quality, the aesthetic is a beautiful blend of retro-inspired visuals combined with modern rendering techniques like screen space reflections and PBR materials. It’s more unique looking because of that, it has more modern lighting and looks all the better for it (while still looking like something from the late 90s, only better). Don’t take this as a full review, as I simply haven’t played enough, but the game has thoroughly impressed me so far. Only wrote this up because the developers asked for people to review the game to get them closer to 1k reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished this game yet but I'm pretty sure my opinion won't change much when I do get around to completing the game. Overall I enjoy the atmosphere/universe, the Father has good dialogue and voice acting, weapon designs are cool and wallrunning is always appreciated. The game is good, however I was let down more than anything. But I can't put my finger on why I can't enjoy this game to the fullest like I have with many other indie boomer shooters such as Dusk, Turbo Overkill, Severed Steel etc, the best way I could describe it is, its too clunky. I felt most comfortable when I had my finger perma-glued to shift so I could bhop and wallrun easier, sliding doesn't seem to provide the speed benefit that it should do in comparison to other similar games on the market, it definitely has a learning curve but I feel like only diehard quake/boomer shooter fans will persist with it in order to learn the mechanic, whether intended or not. The inclusion of some sort of upgrade system to make the player faster or add a double jump or auto pickup adrenaline would make the game more accessible to players unknown to this genre, but also so that they can enjoy the faster paced combat keeping them in the flow state longer, and this would then also apply to the better players as well.I'd also like to mention that it only seems that pistol ammo is dropped on enemy kill? Doom Eternal does this well with the chainsaw but I as the player shouldn't be handicapped for having a preferred weapon and when I run out of ammo, force me to no longer use it and find ammo later on in the mission to use for the next fight, or perhaps its more of an ammo capacity issue. There doesn't seem to be any reason to use the katana as your blows that are dealt are the same as hitting a headshot so a different animation for the katana would be another nice touch, or just giving the player a reason to use the melee weapon rather than just a last resort. The gameplay doesn't have much oompf that keeps you coming back, I love the fact that quick switching is encouraged but when you just have the same combo over and over just in different positions it gets old quick. I tend to get lost quickly in this game as well, on the highrise rooftop level, which I think is E2M2 (I'm probably wrong in that assumption) I couldn't work out initially where to go and ended up going in a loop as I kept missing the walled off wallrunning spot that was the intended route to get there, which I subsequently found after accidentally jumping over the barrier of where I was supposed to go. AI repeat the same lines and seem to be laser focused on your location, I would imagine that the adrenaline ability either slows down time for Seven or for everyone else around them, so to the enemies this should be reflected, their dialogue cutting off after they die would be a nice touch but this is a niche complaint. When fighting one of the bosses, it wasn't that engaging as even without using adrenaline or sliding I could avoid the bullets fired, and I don't think the ground slam was that difficult to avoid either. A classic use shoot the weak spots, target the vulnerable character inside, do this 3 times and then he dies. I think application of giving the player choice would benefit this game a lot, so for example in this boss fight, maybe his gun overheats which gives the player time to recuperate, or if enough damage comes his way in general (without targetting his weak spots) this also overheats him forcing him to kneel down giving the player another opportunity to shoot him in the back without him moving.

_childDocuments_.review: Went into the game really appreciating the aesthetic and music, but the game has a really limited amount of available weapons. There are no grenades, no abilities beyond slow motion, and no double jump. The game takes a lot from Ghost in the Shell in terms of its visuals and setting, a lot of its level design from Doom Eternal, and a lot of its storytelling methods from Ghostrunner. It has a nice variety of levels and considering the limited amount of people involved its pretty well put together. But unfortunately it stays mid gameplay wise. I found the later levels and culmination to be rather boring and anticlimatic. The resolution of the story has nothing to reference, and the motivations for the characters are not enumerated on outside of the gameplay or some interestingly placed QR codes that take you to websites that have text logs. I played this in search of a game where wallrunning and sliding would be central to gameplay, but while this is a nice detour with a lot of potential, I really don't think its worth the time to play it to find out its just ok.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this by saying that Sprawl is a good game. One of the goodest. Unfortunately though, I can't recommend it. I think the main issue is that it suffers from identity crisis. It wants to be a modern shooter while also trying to be a boomer shooter and combining those could end up creating an exceptional game but it falls short on both fronts. It also wants to try so many concepts but it doesn't have the environment or gameplay to make these ideas stick well. what works? The enemies, the environment, the soundtrack, the weapons, and the platforming all work well... until you finish the first level of the first episode and then you see that there's another 1 levels left and say, "wtf I have another 8 hours of this..." Lets quickly break down what I mean. - The enemies are good until you find out that 99% of them just run and gun for you with no tactical or other actions to try to defeat you. Nope, just run and gun for you. That's it. - The environment looks interesting until you find out that the theme gets regurgitated. Cyberpunk aesthetic with dilapidated buildings. Lots of walls, lots of pipes, lots of brown/grey color scheme. Seems alright except that world is barren, just you and the enemies. Nothing to interact with except a couple of levers to progress into the game. - The music is good until you find out why you're getting annoyed. In the beginning of each level, you get a edm/electronica headbanging soundtrack that makes you want to start blasting. And then that same song loops. and loops. and loops again. And then you wonder how much you got left to finish the level so you don't have to listen to these two androids banging again. I'm sure there were more than 1 song per level but it just all started mixing together, and not in a good way. -The weapons are actually very good until you see some flaws that makes you question what this game wants to be. The trailer shows that this game wants to be a fast paced parkour fps but some weapons take forever to reload, especially in the slow-mo setting. The shotgun is one of those. The minigun slows you down once you rotor the gun so you can't really run and gun with it, making it useless when you have these enemies just coming straight for you. The smgs are useless for getting headshots, which are needed so you can restore health, making them useless when you're low on health. So there are cons to every pro for every weapon, which is ok for choosing the right weapon for the right setting but sometimes you only have ammo for the wrong setting, making you really mess up a run. -The platforming is good until you find out that in order to get some backstory or lore of the world, you have to find these QR codes, stop what you're doing, pull out your phone, scan the code, and wait for the page to load to read an essay of text. Other than that, the wall-running is used a lot to get around and it's ok. Does get janky sometimes and hold you up but its minimal. But Mirror's Edge with guns this is not, just some basic, but good, wall-running. One thing to note is that the last 3 levels are more of a huge arena shooter, horde mode and those were really good, making me wonder why it didn't just do that. In summary, jack of all trades, master on none. Good game, but gets repetitive and, except for the last 3 levels, boring. If you're interested, I say try it but know that your mileage will 100% vary. Otherwise, can't recommend and I hate that I can't.Works great on steam deck!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game, with a somewhat one note story, some very confused game design, and some honestly... not great level design.Let's get the main thing out of the way. You're getting this game for the gameplay, and that is pretty rock solid. You can compare this game to ULTRAKILL and see a ton of issues that this game has that ULTRAKILL just doesn't, but this game is also doing things that ULTRAKILL isn't, and it does them pretty well. They're ultimately different games doing different things, but it'd be fair to compare them to a certain extent as well.The Good:Pretty stellar gunplayMovement and guns are responsive. For the most part. Wall running and wall jumping dodging bullets and using bullet time to line up headshots, knowing that standing still is a death sentence is a lot of fun. When it works. Also, the vibes in this game are immaculate. The music goes really hard when it needs to and the visuals can be truly inspired and well done.The Bad:Well... In summary, the game feels... really amateurish. The devil is in the details here.Let's talk about some enemies, starting with a very common enemy past the first 1/3rd of the game or so, the heavy unit.There are TWO variants of them.The first one is a "regular" heavy. He has a helmet, it takes two pistol headshots to stagger him, and he can die to one good shotgun blast. (Sort of)The other one is, like, an "elite" version. He has no helmet, and it only takes one shot to his head to stagger him, but he fires his shotgun two times in a row and he doesn't die to one shotgun shot anymore.Until you learn, first of all, that there's a difference AT ALL, as well as their different properties through trial and error, you'll probably have a frustrating time. Not to mention how sometimes the movement system just doesn't work very well and you lose all of your momentum right in front of them and just die.You can die very quickly in this game, and enemies are very accurate, though they don't track their targets, which is what makes the game possible in the first place.Let's talk about the regular units, there are, again, two versions of them. One of them is a regular foot soldier. They die to one headshot from the pistol and fire in bursts.Later on they get COMPLETELY replaced by robots who die to THREE headshots from your pistol, and once they start firing, they keep firing until you get farther away from them. Again, their silhouette is nearly identical to the regular human soldier, to the point where when they're replaced, you'll probably be wondering why the units (with the same name btw) aren't dying to one shot anymore. The robots also seem to be immune to being staggered, which makes being too aggressive less of a safe option.There's also two other human units, one is a spec ops type who dies in two headshots and fires a constant stream of bullets once he's close enough, and there's a ghost type of unit who teleports and is transparent (pretty visible) until they get close to you where they appear and do melee attacks. Both of them are seemingly removed from the game later on.It makes me wonder why they were added in the first place if they were just going to disappear. Like I said, the game feels amateurish and sloppy.In a game with a more refined design, every enemy would have some place in the game, and you'd try and make sure they're relevant throughout, instead of just removing them entirely.Let's talk about the heavy unit again, because you'll be seeing them A LOT. They're a bit taller than the regular units, but if you look at a group of enemies for the split second that you have as you're flinging across the room, it's very hard to figure out which is which during the very chaotic combat. Also, let's talk about finishers. DOOM has finishers, it's part of its combat loop, it works very well. This game... also... has finishers... for some reason. When an enemy gets to low enough(?) HP they get stunned and start flashing yellow. When they're like this, you can melee them to decapitate them and have them drop health and ammo...... or you can shoot them and have them seemingly do the same thing. Getting a finisher on an enemy seems like an absolutely pointless inclusion, especially considering that you have to get very close to them in order to do it, which can very easily get you killed. You're much better off shooting enemies in almost every scenario and not even bothering with this mechanic.I can imagine if they tweaked this it could work better. Maybe let you do a dash like Genji Overwatch with i-frames when an enemy is stunned, and refill your health/ammo and reposition at the same time, just as an example. That would make the feature both make sense at all, as well as work so much better in the current sandbox of the game. I can only imagine this feature was added because DOOM had it, honestly. It just doesn't fit the game. If the melee was removed, I wouldn't miss it. This game's main mode of mobility is WALL RUNNING. You know where enemies aren't placed? ON THE WALLS. Either make melee worth using, or just remove it, honestly.Let's see... there are 7 weapons, but you'll probably only be using 4 of them, with the other ones being more like "power" weapons. I kinda never bothered with them since it felt like it was taking away from the pretty satisfying counters to enemies I already had. I only pulled them out once or twice just because, but if they were removed from the game I honestly don't think I would notice. Some units are only damaged by explosives. OR the chaingun... so I just use the chaingun on them...Speaking of weapons, enemies will drop ammo, but I could never really tell which enemies dropped what ammo type, or if that's even how it works. Whenever I ran out of ammo, it was a bit jarring, to the point where maybe the game could benefit from just giving us unlimited ammo for our basic weapons instead. As it is, personally, the grenade launcher, rocket launcher, and railgun just don't feel good to use. How do you mess that up?Let's talk about the level design because oh boy...I can't remember the last time I felt so lost playing a game. Let's get something straight, this is not an exploration game, this isn't Half-Life, it's a breakneck boomer shooter like DOOM. I know I keep bringing up DOOM and ULTRAKILL, but the comparisons are very obvious.The levels are simply not made in such a way to be readable by players, they have serious problems. I have many years under my belt as a gamer (ew), and there's a sort of intuition that you can get when a games level is designed well. You're being pushed in one direction through some means or another. Valve perfected this, their games are masterpieces when it comes to leading the player in unobtrusive ways, but MANY times throughout this game I felt confused. I'd be progressing as normal and maybe I'd hit a switch or something, and then I'd come to the realization that I have no idea where the game wants me to go. Some levels can be a mess. The platforming is... decent, but being able to figure out where you're supposed to traverse can be half of the struggle, and then figuring out HOW to traverse it can be an issue as well. I know we all like to joke and laugh at devs using the yellow tape or whatever to point a player in the right direction, but honestly, while the levels look nice, it's far FAR too easy to get turned around in the chaos of battle as well as just be lost not knowing where to go. ALSO, tilesets are sometimes either RE USED or wrap back around on themselves with new enemies giving you a feeling of "Have I been here before...?" further adding to the sense of being completely lost. The level design is probably my biggest gripe with this game.ALL THAT BEING SAID.This game is good. I wish I could say it's great and a fantastic game that everyone should play... but...It's good. Just good.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like the newer doom games, but it didn't forget to be a classic shooter at the same time.Super sonic high speed combat, satisfying as hell weapon designs, a dreary cyberpunk world and a badass protagonist. What more could I ask for?Basically nothing.Great feeling controls, powerful weapons and a killer soundtrack.Some people complain the enemies are too tanky, I say those people need to learn what a headshot is.Enemies die quickly, if you shoot them in their weak points. Combined with your low ammo pool and the incredibly high speed SEVEN can move at the demand for accuracy creates a really good feeling core loop. Combat is tight and demands skill. All while making you feel like a gun slinging badass. The world of SPRAWL is as beautiful as it is ugly and sad. I dig the retro aesthetic that doesn't go whole hog and actually incorporates some modern lighting techniques. It just, looks right. Level design too is great, very easy to navigate and yet it still feels sprawling and claustrophobic at the same time. (except for literally the first jump of the final level. Screw that section)And that music...Dear GOD.It's like doing a line of coke at a Mongolian throat singing session. Writing could use some work though, the themes are very bluntly handled. SIX is a good nemesis but his final dialogue made him sound like a wimp rather than a badass final challenge. And overall it just feels predictable, its a grim sad tale in a grim sad universe and the collectable notes failed to broaden the world, they just made me feel confused or filled in interactions that didn't mean anything.Gameplay is where its at and the main thing that matters

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL sits right between the fine line that is recommending it.I was drawn into it by the fact that some reviews compared it to Titanfall. It is cumbersome, sometimes dumb.There is a lound gun clocking sound when you load a level. This is independent from the sound controls and when I first played it, it blew my right eardrum off... literally. I cannot hear well with that ear since yesterday. Not cool.HOWEVER, I do appreciate how heavily inspired the game is from pop culture (main theme sounding insanely similar to the one from Ghost in the Shell), the movement feels fluid, the graphics are quite good while still being retro, and the graphics settings are quite detailed. There are some bugs, with how enemies behave, but they can be ignored for the most part. The guns feel good, gunplay feels very DOOM-esque and the enemies balanced.Try it out, it's cheap. But watch out for your eardrums. SERIOUSLY.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has its problems but I still think it's worth a recommend at the price of only $15 USD. It's a short game of 12 levels that are ~15-20 minutes each. The game was a little longer than I'd like honestly, when the enemies got more bullet spongey. I'm just going to go through the negatives here, you can view the positives elsewhere.Some important things I disliked:- No preset difficulty option. There are ways to increase the difficulty but that is in the option menu. This is not a preset but just allows you to change three difficulty measurements, player damage, enemy damage, and adrenaline (your slow motion ability) burn rate. This is by no means a replacement for proper preset difficulties but is great to see. Some things I would like to see added as well would be pickup rate and pickup amount. I went through the game on the default difficulty since I don't want to mess with the sliders. That made it so I didn't have a challenge but I still enjoyed the game. - The level design is a lot more messy visually and geometrically and makes chaining wall runs and jumps more difficult/impossible. - The parkour in general is worse than Ghostrunner but it's still good for this game. All you have in this game is slow motion, wall running, and sliding. Starting a slide or wall run does not increasing your speed a significant amount. You don't have a double jump or a dash. - I'm not sure if there is enough visual and audio feedback in this game if you want a challenge. The audio and visual cues for getting hit and enemies shooting are not as clear as I would personally like. Whether or not an enemy has a jetpack when facing them is not super clear but is important information. Whether or not an enemy is dead when in slow motion is not as clear. - During the latter half (especially the last 3 levels), the enemies get harder to kill with the pistol. This isn't necessarily a negative but you will be shifting your play from the start where you almost always have adrenaline and constantly killing enemies with precision hits in at most 3 hits. Later on, this changes completely. You will (at least I personally did) be playing at regular speed a lot more frequently and using weapons that rely on precision way less. The lack of precision is either due to using a higher damage weapon or facing enemies that don't have any weakspots. You still get enemies that you can kill with precision and it is still ideal to use your pistol for some (jetpack + invisible enemies) but is definitely less often. Some smaller things I dislike that the developers may see as they do seem responsive:- I feel like running out of adrenaline is punished way too heavily. Only way to get adrenaline back is to be killing enemies and it's hard to kill enemies without adrenaline. There could have been a passive adrenaline recharge or adrenaline pickups on the map.- The pose for enemies firing downwards looks unnatural and causes them to cover their head an unnatural amount.- An enemy's jetpack is still highlighted in slow-mo even after they are dead and it is no longer able to be triggered. I would have liked if the jetpack fades if the enemy is dead or have it still able to be triggered.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really amazing. The levels strongly remind me of a Cyberpunk version of that Kowloon level from CoD: Black Ops, except the gameplay feels like a mix between Mirror's Edge, Doom 2016, Quake, and Ghostrunner. If you played Ghostrunner and wished that you wouldn't have to die in one hit and also had guns, Sprawl is for you. If you played Mirror's Edge and wished that it had good combat, then Sprawl is also for you. Once you get comfortable with the controls, you'll be able to whip out some truly slick moves and it never fails to look awesome. Nail that slow-mo dive through the air off a wall run, while spraying bullets from your gats into someone's head and you'll know what I mean.The game also has an amazing atmosphere. I'm especially vibing with the soundtrack which sounds like late 90s jungle, industrial, and dubstep. Now, you can play only so many retro games with synthwave music before it becomes a cliche, so listening to tunes that remind me of Unreal Tournament instead is a true breath of fresh air for a cyberpunk themed shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Six minutes is actually a new record for me to uninstall and refund a title. Bravo.A word of caution and advice: Maybe next time, don't arbitrarily limit people to 2 wall jumps and fail to include a ledge grab. I don't care, I don't want to hear it, I really don't have the patience for this type of trash. Your tutorial was not good, I found out the wallrun mechanic was too stiff and uninteresting ontop of lacking polish. Despite having all of the trappings of what in the trailers reads as a fast-paced movement shooter in the boomer variety, what is on display is more infuriatingly precise than the hot garbage of Mirror's Edge. A big portion of that is owed to the fact that your character has no elbows, ankles, knees, or even a spinal column.Wall running and jumping clearly do not work as intended, matching far too closely to what you'd actually expect if you tried this stupid idea in real life. Momentum bleeds and apparently you get one jump per leg your character has while wall running, making even some of the first 60 seconds feel painful. This is a critical gameplay feature, no? I thought it was. Apparently however it was not a priority to actually teach how wall running worked in any detail. I retried a two-step platforming section five times, and that's all you get of my time aside from this review. I'm thoroughly disappointed, the game looked fun if amateur. Having slogged through Metro Last Light, I really needed something fast and fluid. You created a stiff and uninteresting setting, a stiff and uninteresting movement system, and I'm going to guess that probably includes a stiff and uninteresting shooting experience.Increase the movement speed, remove the wall jump limit, add a ledge grab. This isn't hard, no one will want to play a game that immediately falls off less than 10 minutes in because your movement system isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's off to a great start when it blasts your ears when you startup the game. _childDocuments_.review: Solid game, solid retro shooter, great art style. Short game but not as short as my playtime would suggest - it actually took me about 6.5 hours to finish end-to-end. Only really had a few minor issues:-There was a problem initially with not being in full-screen mode and input delay on weapons, but that was solved by going into fullscreen-Some weapons in the arsenal did not land with the impact I feel they should've - like the cluster rocket launcher, which generally did less damage and was less predictable than the grenade launcher. The grenade launcher also has the ability to almost one-shot you with self-damage, and it feels a bit overtuned (to the point I didn't use it as often to avoid blowing myself up)-The final section involves a lot of platforming, which is fine, but I feel the game did a pretty good job merging platforming and combat up to that point, and in the final level they're often separatedNone of these is a dealbreaker and the game itself was still excellent. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent shooter. It claims to be a boomer shooter, and I guess it is… kinda. It reminds me of Severed Steel somehow. I guess it’s the movement system, which is very much parkour-like. The platforming in this was not too bad. There are some difficult to figure out segments, but the movement system feels pretty good, so I wasn’t ever too frustrated. The shooting however, I think that’s where most of this game’s problems lie. The maximum amount of ammo you can carry is absolutely anemic. This is because, like in Doom Eternal, you’re encouraged to use the game’s gimmick to earn more ammo from enemies. That gimmick being bullet-time that highlights enemies weaknesses with an orange glow. You shoot at the orange glow with the correct weapon and health, bullet time… time, and ammo drops. Bullet time… time doesn’t regenerate, although I think it should have. The combat, in my opinion, becomes very exhausting and boring because it all boils down to shooting at slow moving orange dots for the whole game. I also don’t like that there isn’t a quick save/load feature. I don’t care what justification the developers have for this; they’re wrong. If you don’t want to save scum, fine, here’s a cookie. I want to save scum, so give me the option. The music and visuals were… fine. The music in particular seems to be in the style of some Nier Automata bootleg. This was decently fun overall, but it’s far from the best indie FPS I’ve played.

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment you start playing this game, it gets you straight into the action, Killing everything on sight and taking advantage of your movement tech to move faster and get around enemies quick. Wallrunning is very smooth and easily controllable, setting up for some cool kills. The bullet-time mechanic made the game extra cool, shooting enemies while wallrunning, switching weapons midway and jumping to an approaching platform or an opposite wall. It's that constant High Octane action than made FPS from the past so incredibly well done and fun. Sometimes simplicity can get very creative.There's great variety in weapons, with your starting pistol, later getting the SMG and shotgun, grenade launcher, Minigun and many more. The switch speed is very fast and the encourages you to constantly swap depending on enemy type and positioning. Guns feel impactful and fun to use. Presentation-wise is straight out of the Late 90's era with a more simplistic approach and also darker lighting. It's lightweight, so almost any PC can run it.The game is short but has plenty of replayabilty with extra modes like Time Trial and Horde. More features and Quality of Life additions will also come in the future as announced by the Devs themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a very satisfying retro FPS. The campaign is short but sweet, with a standard variety of weaponry. The horde mode offers the challenge that you might feel is missing.Gunplay is solid. Movement is fun without overwhelming you with options. Slowmo can be activated at any point and its use is baked into the design well.Overall, it's great game to pop heads to.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better mobile first person shooters.Enemies go to down quickly and so do you if you are no constantly wall running, sliding and jumping.Nice urban hell visuals even if the first two to three maps overstay their welcome just a bit, for the rest of the game areas have enough variety and things to see beyond just repetitive gray corridors.Gun variety is relatively low but every weapon has it's use and few annoyances like the shotgun's very low rate of fire feel like intentional design choices to prevent player over relying on one part of their arsenal.Enemies are very stupid and often run at you in a straight line. Since you are a glass cannon that goes down in about three to five shots while unarmored it usually balances itself out.I feel that I also need to give props for the fact that the enemies do take a lot of damage from head shots and explosions but are otherwise very resistant to body shots from pistols and the shotgun. Meaning that unlike in these games usually the enemies body armor is not just for looks.To help on hitting the said head shots the game relies on pick up limited time slowing bullet time mode that you need to use a lot and makes you feel naked  whenever it runs out.One last thing this is probably the only game in recent memory that I feel the need to play with the Motion Blur -setting turned on. The effect is not over used or too over powering and it looks very apropriate for the slow time mode.Definitely one of my favorite games of the FPS genere as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Lotta fast parkour and big ole guns, what's not to like?SPRAWL is pretty simple. Play the role of cybernetic assassin and liberator of the people, fight against "the man" you once worked for, and topple their empire. Quite literally all you need to know, and all you really end up getting, but hey, I ain't complainin. I was entertained for about 6 hours by a tough but fair FPS. Is it perfect? No. Is it really all that difficult? Nah. But was it a blast? Sure was.(I should mention there is a time-trial and endless mode that I did not try, but that may add to your experience and overall time.)Wall-running and sliding will always be entertaining in video games. This alone gets a thumbs-up from me. You can sort of slide-hop rather than bunny hop, and its really useful. And don't underestimate the effectiveness of the wall-run, you can pretty deftly scale and hop along walls and reach places in combat pretty easily.Now, as for the bullet-time, while it is not necessarily core to the overall experience, it was a pretty handy tool to say the very least. It shows weak-points, and allows you to get that necessary time to refocus on a target you want gone. Plus, with how the resource system works, you'll usually not have too much of an issue running low on your "adrenaline".Weapons consist of dual pistols, dual smgs, a double-barrel shotgun, a grenade launcher, a mini gun, a rail gun, and a rocket launcher (that fires a hail of missiles, rather than one single rocket). Oh, and a quick melee katana, useful for a finisher on stunned, or nearly dead, enemies.Weapon-switching is viable, although I am not necessarily a practitioner of said play-style, and it helps you skip certain lags in firing your weapons. The shotgun has a particularly long reload, which can be skipped with a quick swap and swap back.I can see some classic FPS game design in the variety of enemies on offer, and I love it. Leaping "hounds", grenade-chucking "ogres", fairly ineffective "Demons" and the semi-transparent cousins... This game oozes with influence from DOOM and Quake, as well as Half-Life, Titanfall (perhaps Mirror's Edge as well?). It is all just so good.SPEAKING OF ENEMIES. As I mentioned, they have mechs called O.H.G.R.s, equipped with GRENADE LAUNCHERS. And that's not all. THE GRENADES MAKE THE SAME SOUND AS THE GRENADES IN QUAKE! **oh be still, my beating heart**I absolutely love this. And then, they GIVE YOU that same weapon. And I'm home. A fast way to my heart as an FPS fan is references to Quake. And this was such a wonderful little thing. I can only smile when I encounter them in-game, now.Level design was good fun, and far more the kind of parkour platforming action that I love... and prefer over any of the platforming in Doom Eternal. While there's a lot of "go pull that switch and come back", there is a lot of style and energy as you swoop through levels, demolishing all who stand before you.SPRAWL may be nothing too fancy, particularly when compared to the myriad of heavy-hitters that have been coming out lately, but let her cook. This is a sure-fire modern classic, taking the old and sprinkling in a little modern spice.My compliments to the chef.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all. Soundtrack is cool. Gameplay is cool.  I am writing this from a player who has played Titanfall 2 and have close to 1k hours on apex as well.What does the game do well?- The visuals are unique. they look pixelated from close but dont feel like you are playing a boomer shooter if you dont look closely at all. It feels quite half like like.- This gameplay sure has taken some inspiration from "Mirror's Edge". I felt it while playing through a lot of these levels. Even the enemy designs look a bit familiar.- The fast paced action is captured well. There is no sprinting since you already are sprinting.- Gun arsenal is quite varied. You have 7 weapons to experiment with.- Mechanics are decent. Sliding feels enjoyable as well.- Gun Damage is balanced (mostly).Things which felt a bit off-- The gun noises could use a bit of oomph. They SOUND weak.- There is quite sometimes shortage of ammo if you want to keep using a single type of weapon. I think the ammo drops are also fixed for certain enemies instead of being varied. Ofcourse there is ammo here and there but that makes this akin to DOOM 2016 where you have to be always a bit cautious of switching guns to spread your ammo use. I would have preferred a DOOM Eternal sort of experience where maybe a chainsaw or some sort of contraption could give me quite varity of ammo so that I could keep using my favourite guns longer.- The wallrun seems off.  Compared to Titanfall 2 where you get double jumps. This doesn't have a so called jumpkit. Thats still fine. But the wallrun here seems to start at the TOP of the ARC. While in Titanfall 2 your character draws an arc starting below, reaches peak and comes down.  I feel starting a wallrun with an arc starting below the top would make wallrun a bit better.Things which I am not sure about:-- The game throws perhaps the most highest skill ceiling weapon to you at the beginning. The pistol!! It is ridiculously fun to use but feels very underpowered if not using headshots. Yes I get you are supposed to use the Slow Time feature to get accurate but I try to not use it too much.  I feel like maybe reducing the dependency on Slow Time  and maybe buffing the pistol (either making body shots more powerful or increasing the projectile shots for easier headshots) can remedy and offer a better experience (hey but thats just me, I might just be bad at aiming LOL).- Anyways Playing this game with ONLY the Pistols WITHOUT any Slow Time is one of the best aim trainer. If you can manage to pull it off consistently, It feels rewarding for sure.All in All. The game is Fun. Can be replayed trying out new strats and techniques.  Wallrunning is fun. Guns are decent.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a little ego shooter with a nice retro look.Admittedly, I didn't pay much attention to the story and just played it for the shooter part but it is fine for what it is.And while I was probably way to bad at it, it felt immensely satisfying, when one of my headshots were set right.I just had a couple of times, when I did not know where to go next.And while we technically had a sniper with the plasma rifle, the possibility to aim through the scope was painfully missing for me.I also belive, this game would be perfect for it having secrets placed around the map.It also sometimes takes several inputs to fire a gun even with the weapon-stamina being full.-The owls shoot to approve.

_childDocuments_.review: The mixture in between games like DOOM (2016) in terms of shooting, Ghostrunner in movement and aesthetics and F.E.A.R. or Trepang2 with it's bullet time mechanics combined with the low resolution models and textures of a boomer shooter while retaining modern graphics (lighting, effects, motion blur making the game smooth and dynamic) it makes up for the great 3-4 hours of a pretty nice story. I won't spoil anything, just play the game!!!As for a HUGE positive I have to give the soundtrack. I really enjoyed the use of a dynamic soundtrack in calm and combat moments. And as being a drum and bass fan, it's appearance in the game's OST (combined with the choirs), was a really nice touch up.For the downsides I would give the game are:- It's aggressive wall running. To be clear: it's really well made, but in some moments, the player gets glued to the wall even if he wants to do a simple jump.- No objective markers. Sure, it's a boomer shooter so this is understandable, BUT - some players might get lost in some places. A small tag on a door or a way we are supposed to go (even optional in settings for example, would be a nice QOL change in my opinion)Apart from that. as for a 7,50$ random pick up, it was one heck of a ride! (right behind ULTRAKILL)

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game a lot. I'm glad that a good amount of achievements you're able to just get by playing the game through. The movement is great though, it reminds me of a mix of Krunker and Titan Fall movement. It's really smooth. Weapon progression is pretty good as well. I enjoyed each of the guns, with each of the enemies forcing me to use specific weapons just to kill them effectively. This truly allowed for some fun game play elements. _childDocuments_.review: Wish I could put the little recommendation thumb at like a 60-degree angle for this one. SPRAWL has a lot of good ideas and inspiration that it struggles to wrangle together and reconcile into a cohesive gameplay experience. I say this to emphasize that the hangups I have with the game are almost all related to the moment-to-moment "feel" of  the game. The visual and sound design is generally of really high quality, and if you like what you see on the store page the game has plenty of that bleak, washed-out cityscape to go around. That said, the gameplay has some deliberate choices that feel at odds with the fantasy it tries to deliver. ~This is less a review and more a granular/nitpicky rant, but I feel that SPRAWL is so close to being really special that the problems I have with it are outsized. Keep in mind that this game is still very much worth trying out if you love movement shooters. To make this review more digestible to read (and easier to write) I'll organize my few specific gripes under some headers below.~-MOVEMENT-SPRAWL is, as the marketing makes clear, a movement shooter that focuses heavily on the player's ability to outmaneuver enemies. However, the main tool for movement, the wall-running system, necessarily relies on access to walls to provide the player with the speed they need to evade enemies. While a lot of the early levels are excellent about providing the player with intricate pathways and walls aplenty to maneuver and take advantage of the system, later levels often are very open and grounded, leaving the player to rely on a rather silly feeling mix of bunny-hopping and keep away tactics.This is a result of the game not really having movement mechanics that feel fully fleshed out while the player isn't immediately next to a wall. The other main means of movement, a jump and slide, both feel a little too stubby to properly take advantage of, with many walls or barriers being just slightly too tall to jump directly up to. The end result is a movement system that shines in many of the game's arenas, but falls flat in others.-BULLET TIME-While intent is something that I can't vouch for, it certainly feels like the player character was designed to play like an untouchably fast entity, evoking the distorting afterimages and impossible reflexes made iconic in media like The Matrix or Cyberpunk. Because of the later level design and general lack of explicit mechanics related to movement, SPRAWL falls a touch short of fully realizing the feeling of speed that makes the fantasy appealing. In trying to compensate for this, the game implements another system to create that feeling - bullet time. At any point while the Adrenaline bar is not empty, the player can enter a slowed-down state that enables them to aim in a way that simulates a quick, decisive speed. Enemies and bullets move slower, while some visual and sound effects are added to emphasize the impact of each shot. However, there's a notable caveat - the player also moves, aims, and fires much slower while in the slowed time. The upshot of this is that your Adrenaline bar is a bit deceptive in terms of what you can actually do with it, especially considering the slow fire rates of some weapons. The shotgun is the most notable offender - the player can fire a shot at the start of a full adrenaline bar and barely squeeze in a second as the bar empties. In addition to the relatively short period in which the player can enter bullet time, the only way to replenish Adrenaline is in pickups from enemies or scattered around the environment. This results in occasional dry spells where the player is unable to enter bullet time while being pursued by a number of enemies. As such, I found during my playthrough that I was activating bullet time less and less as the game went on, using it only for enemies that strictly demand it to react to their attack patterns. While it makes sense that bullet time should be used sparingly, tying it to pickups that require the player to dive into the fray and potentially die due to high enemy damage makes engaging with the mechanic feel like a hindrance in later sections.-GUNPLAY-To it's credit, the Bullet Time mechanic does have an added bonus that makes it essential for tackling the game's challenges: an orange highlight on the weakpoints of enemies displays while the player is engaged. While in the early game most enemies are dispatched nicely with one to three headshots from the paired pistols, this doesn't last. Some armored enemies take no damage at all from small arms, requiring the use of either the Shotgun or one of the extremely unreliable explosive weapons. It is not uncommon to shoot the grenade launcher into a crowd in the late game and see none of the enemies you hit even stall their movement. The explosive weapons are often more deadly to the player than enemies due to their sky-high splash damage and inaccuracy, which meant that I was actively avoiding using them by the end of my playthrough. While the pistols feel great and like the game was built with them in mind, the general durability of enemies makes a lot of the weapons in SPRAWL feel unsatisfying to use.Many of the guns also feel very counterintuitive to the movement style the game seemingly wants you to employ. The shotgun actively directs your momentum when you fire it, causing you to fly backwards when shooting in the air. While this might function as a kind of niche movement tech, it functionally makes the gun feel finnicky if you're not just strafe-spamming it. The chaingun and railgun suffer from extremely slow wind-up times, that are further extended by activating Bullet Time, making them unwieldy to use in the pressure of a fight, to say nothing of the chaingun's massive inexplicable movement speed penalty while firing. While it may be a balancing method, spooling up the gun can accidentally kill the player's air momentum, which just feels horrible in a game where the player is very fragile like this one. I remember a low point from my playthrough where I heard FATHER, the game's objective narrator/omnipresent robotic voice, tell me that I was breaking into a weapons testing facility to "upgrade my arsenal", and I audibly asked nobody in particular to not be given another gun.--------While I can certainly rag on the niche points of the game's construction, SPRAWL is still undoubtedly a labor of love with a strong aesthetic style and great conceptual core for it's gameplay. However, it has some wrinkles in the gameplay texture that can make the experience a bit less than the sum of it's parts. Still, for genre fans, this is a good offering, and I look forward to seeing what the developers work on next.

_childDocuments_.review: A short but sweet shooter experience.Sprawl can best be described as a cross between DOOM, Titanfall, and F.E.A.R, the gameplay consists of you running off walls and blowing things up with your shotgun and watching them explode into a variety of ammo and health pick ups.If you've played other games in the "Boomer shooter" genre then you've pretty much played this one. _childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty old school but i find it really enjoyable, the gameplay loop is fun, Pros: - You can change the difficulty to your liking which is nice-  The slowmo in the game is really well done, you really need to keep moving in order to stay alive, reminds me of Doom / Doom eternal. I LOVE THIS- Achievements were a high point for me, these ones were really fun to get - some of them quite hard, even with reading some guides.- The platforming is also sooooo much fun, even just running up walls to get a nice shotgun blast from the top is also heavily enjoyable. - The right click to initiate slowmo is a really nice way of activating it, it became so natural very quickly.- Love the doomey voice of the dude who keeps telling you what to do / where to go- Checkpoints are generous (there are LOTS in each level)- Ammo pickups are fairly generous which i also really like.Cons:- Those SMGs are the worst guns in the entire game so far ( I have unlocked pistols, shotgun, SMG's and a grenade launcher). You CANNOT hit the weakpoints of any enemy with SMG's, if you do they just dont "explode" and drop ammo/ health so there's absolutely no gain in using them.- Absolutely no indication of the general direction of where the next checkpoint is, which leads to get a little lost at times.- No indication of the current objective. Even just a "head to the elevator " or "power up the generator" or something would have helped me to know what am i looking for.-  Due to there being no clear indication of where to go, you have to listen to the dude talking to know what is going on, sometimes he talks while i am fighting which means I need to activate slowmo and then i miss what he said. Adding a brief current objective would have solved this.- Needs a bit more achievements to make it more fun (things like kills with a certain gun or killing an enemy while airborne) I am at the last level of the first chapter and i must say i enjoyed this game so far a lot more than i expected to,  I enjoyed this more than i did severed steel so i honestly feel these devs need the love and support for what they builtEDIT: People who complain that there is no ammo are really a special kind of stoopit. you literally get awarded ammo with EVERY KILL.FINAL EDIT: After finishing the campaign and getting all achievements (with guides obviously), i can say that this game really was a lot of fun, but it also had potential to be so much more, I can just see myself doing more levels and panicking more when i just miss a ledge with all the parkour you have to do, also more achievements like providing a level with LOTS of shotgun ammo + an achievement to get 100% accuracy.This game feels like it has elements of Mirrors edge / painkiller (with the crazy jumping) + DOOM if anyone wanted to know, also i had a good laugh reading the credits, well done devs

_childDocuments_.review: A brief but very enjoyable movement based boomer shooter. It has a super slick cyberpunk aesthetic and there are a lot of cool levels that showcase the dystopian architecture. I've seen some people say that the movement can be finnicky, but it never got bad enough to ruin the game for me. As a matter of fact, the movement is empowering; running on a wall while gunning robots and cyborgs down feels like the super cool early 2000s Matrix FPS we never got. The pace is lightning fast, even with the slow down ability, which is well implemented. Basically the game encourages a hyper aggressive playstyle because the more you kill enemies the more adrenaline you get back. Only real complaints I have are that certain weapons feel less useful than others; the way to get a small health, ammo, and adrenaline replenishment is by killing an enemy via their weak point, but something like the SMGs makes it too easy to accidentally kill an enemy before being able to melee finish them to get resources back. Meanwhile, with the shotgun, every kill gives you resources no matter where you hit an enemy with it. Still, the arsenal is fun to use, and the game does a great job of encouraging you to use every weapon you have in your arsenal by the end, where the combat becomes you vs small armies. Overall Sprawl is a super cool boomer shooter the places just as much emphasis on acrobatics as it does the shooting action, and the ability to toggle slow motion means the game never stops its relentlessly fast pace.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a modern day sytlized FPS posing as a boomer shooter.  When I went into this game I was expecting a story driven atmospheric FPS with lots of cool set pieces and interesting enemy types and weapon types.  What I actually got was an arena shooter similiar to Doom 2016 with frantic fast paced movement.  That's not to say it was bad, just that my expectations didn't quite align which threw me off.  One thing I love about classic retro inspired FPS games is character and atmosphere.  Drop me into a shopping mall with aliens, or a theme park with weird ways to ride the rides and I'm in love.  Sprawl has opportunity to deliver on some of these feelings, but instead opts for blocky arenas where you're presented with lots of opportunity to wall run, but not a lot of opportunity to stop and take stock in the environment around you.  Instead, it all just blends together.  And again, that's usually fine if it does the arena shooter side of things well, and this is.... mediocre.  Compared to Doom 2016 which operates like a puzzle game, every enemy has it's own specific weapon, Sprawl is a bit more generic.  For the most part I simply used the shotgun close range, energy rifle long range and rocket launcher against larger enemy types.  The game is short and easy, with difficulty selection.  The secrets, or hidden objects are simply text logs, often abstract or giving a bit of lore behind the world you're in.  The biggest positive, for me, was the soundtrack.  An excellent blend of Ghost in the Shell orchestra cyberpunk mixed with pure drum and bass.  I plan on listening to this OST over the next couple of weeks.  Get this game on sale, finish it over a weekend and move on.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl seamlessly blends cyberpunk elements from iconic sources like Ghost in the Shell and "Blade Runner," creating a captivating dystopian world. The soundtrack, reminiscent of is excellent and fast paced, which sets a compelling tone, while the setting evokes the gritty atmosphere of Blade Runner and the chaotic allure of Kowloon's walled city. Drawing inspiration from JinRoh, the enemies offer a diverse challenge. With mysterious main characters, notably the enigmatic narrator, Sprawl delivers solid gameplay and an intriguing world. Personally one of my favorite games.The dystopian essence of cyberpunk is vividly portrayed, unlike the comedic interpretations seen in other games. Here, the absence of god is palpable, replaced by the omnipresence of technology, instilling a deep sense of godlessness within this bleak world. Give this game a look.

_childDocuments_.review: super fun lil game, took me about 4 hrs to beat itits a modern take on OG first person shooter games, do movement puzzles, merc lots of dudes, find keycards, progress. easy to pick up on. the movement is the star of the show, you have a pretty unrestrained wall run and a slide. you can get some serious speed going just hopping out of slides and chaining them together, it feels alot like modified source engine movement, but its simplified and easy to get down, which i think is a good choice for a shorter game like this one. you can also jump with the shotgun, much like the force a nature in tf2, they dont tell you this for some strange reason and it really enhances the movementthe level design is extremely refreshing. no objective markers or anything, the closest you get is some interactable objects are highlighted in bullet time and theres baked in lights on the textures of places youll need to go and things like that. it never babysits you and leans in to how free your movement is, sometimes it kinda feels like youre breaking the game with your movement but its totally intentional, i love it.the combat feels good, while some of the weapons do feel disappointing at first, once you find their niche youll be swapping between every gun pretty fluently. theres some difficulty adjustment sliders [that i didnt touch] but no 'easy mode', but there is a bullet time that highlights enemy weakpoints and slows your aim slightly to make hitting shots easier. its on a meter but its very generous with the pickups. if you dont like it, the game does not force you to use it at all, i barely used it, mostly to hit far away shots. enemies do get tanky near the end of the game but as long as you keep moving theyre still not too hard to deal with. theres no enemy that cant be defeated by wallrunning around them. the name of the game is how efficiently you can dispatch them while running circles around them.the boss designs are... eh? the first one is probably the worst, and they get slightly better as the game goes on. theyre not horrible but they were my least favorite parts of the game.the story is about what youd expect, its a motivator for the gameplay and not much else, standard dystopian hero stuff with datalogs to fill in some background details. perfectly serviceable. personally i would love to see some of the rebirth and new life themes of the cyberpunk genre explored in a more. direct and modern viewpoint. maybe our protagonist couldve had more personal changes during her cyberification. were all of the same kin here, you know what i mean.the art direction of the game is great, obviously extremely ghost in the shell influenced. everything is extremely inspired but never strays into being derivative. the first boss fight is in a sunbathed, open concrete field flooded with ankle high water, your go to guns are matever revolvers, theres cyberbrains and ♥♥♥♥, but its never really screaming "hey look! like that movie and tv show you like!". very creative while still being inspired.the soundtrack [which you should buy on b@ndc@mp! not on steam! support artists yo] is a similar story. lots of traditional sounding synth choirs accented with many members of the drum and bass family. kinda sounds like if noisia or rawtekk remixed the standalone complex ostoverall its a solid title and the devs very obviously had a lot of fun making it, and i had fun playing it too. i might go back and get the secret achievements and the datalogs i missed and stuff, but the first playthrough i got from it is def worth the $14 list price. some aspects of gameplay could be refined and theres a ton of room for a more fleshed out story, but nether of those things ruin the experience for me. 8/10 would reccomend

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda wish there was an air dash and the chain-gun had no spin-up time.It feels like you spend most of the time trying to gain height over your enemies and you don't have very many tools to prolong the time spent at the top when you finally get there.A horizontal air dash would let you have just a bit more time to get stuff done.As for the chain-gun, the spin up clashes with the wall running.
