_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game with a god-tier soundtrack but also some noticeable flaws. Shooting and moving around feel nice, wall running is solid, weapons have a nice punch to them, you get a bullet time ability that you activate with RMB and restore cutting almost dead enemies or by killing them using a weakspot. The bullet time mechanic plays well with the weakspot mechanic and although you do "run and gun" it manages not to feel mindless. Out of all three chapters I'd say that the first looks and plays best (or maybe I remember it most fondly), mostly because it's the one that is the most visually interesting with the best level desing in the game, giving you enough space to move around but also were tight enough to make enemies dangerous. Further down the line levels can be interesting in terms of layout, with some well though out loops to avoid backtracking but they kinda fall into the trap of "you see the door, now find keys" which would be fine but the arenas in the last two chapters are getting kind of dull (both in layout and style comparred to the first chapter). They let you use your wall running and stuff but given that the enemy AI is not that great it sometimes boiled down to me occupying a single spot on the arena and enemies simply coming at me. The arsenal is good but (and I rarely say this) could be smaller - this is also where the first chapter shines because you end up with the most balanced arsenal: Pistols, Shotgun, SMGs and a Grenade Launcher which makes most of those weapons have their place. When they introduce the chaingun, the swarm missile launcher and the railgun, things start to feel cluttered. First of all the dual pistols that were already struggling to compete with the shotgun and the smgs are now completely irrelevant (the weakspot gimmick that the game encourages you to use does not help them since at this point most enemies take forever to kill with them even when aiming at their head), then you introduce the chaingun that has a really limited use due to its gimmick of slowing you to a crawl but can be useful when dealing with bigger enemies but feels clunky in a game centered around running and shooting and then you make the grenade launcher irrelevant by adding the swarm missile launcher that I guess could be considered less reliable but first of all you get a lot of shotgun and rocket launcher ammo and second of all since you're moving around a lot it's easy to remedy this by closing the distance enough for all of the rockets to hit (swap-cancelling it with a shotgun feels good though, I'm not gonna lie). Then you get the railgun which is strong but feels clunky since you have to hold it down to shoot and if you do not hold it down it stops charging which was a bit annoying, I'd prefer for it to charge when I press the button once since it'd be much more intuitive, but that's very much a personal preference. It's not bad but it could be a better weapon. I feel like this is the situation where 'less is more' applies well, I'd prefer a smaller arsenal but each weapon remains relevant throughout the game. One more thing is that fights feel short, I don't know if this is because I have years of shooters behind me but most fights ended right when I was getting warmed up, with too few enemies to actually make it interesting, however, fights that were meant to be big, especially in the latter parts of the game, were better in this regard. Bossfights while few, were okay, however that section during (if I remember correctly) the Interloper, with the moving platform and the chopper was.... terrible. The story was getting interesting, we don't really get that much about the world, which is a shame but this is why I liked those first levels so much - they captured my imagination much better than the latter ones. The character of Father that accompanies you throughout the game is well put together, he has enough personality to be likable and talks often but never to the point where you've had enough of him. Also  In the end the game is okay, it has some blemishes but not enough for it to be a deal breaker and the music carries it HARD. Even when the level was mid the music boosted it to 'good' effortlessly.Would love to see more from the devs, with a little bit more polish and thought put into the entire experience this could be one of the classics so I hope they make another one.

_childDocuments_.review: right off the bat -if you like ultrakill, you'll probably like this game.shouldn't need a nasa pc to run it.loaded with nostalgic visuals.action addicts definitely check this out.platformer jockeys, give it a look too.doesn't have years worth of content, but what's there is far more than enough (in my opinion) to keep you entertained.starts simple and relatively slow (for a movement shooter), but quickly becomes an epic crusade of gore and high octane tricks you'll eventually pull off without even thinking; weapon variety is good, and although not all of them work perfectly against every enemy individually, finding that right combo to splatter bodies and pop heads is rewarding the first time, and entertaining to replicate. with such customization, albeit simple for difficulty, it can be pretty tuned to your skill or enjoyment level, if you're looking for a hardcore blood shower or a more cathartically relaxed blood sink; whatever your plumbing appliance equivalent, you should probably get it checked out on why it's outputting blood. like seriously.it is a little difficult to control your movement sometimes, but that just adds to the fun in my experience - those minor mishaps of misinterpreted fancy footwork can land you in disadvantageous situations, but that's what keeps you getting creative with your violent problem solving skills. for an fps this isn't an absolute mona lisa, but it stands tall above the hazy mess of clones that many others in the genre are, at least in my humble opinion. overall, gunplay, movement, story and visuals, i'd say its definitely worth full price, and even more so on sale, with how much fun i had with it; there's time trials and horde modes separate from the mainline game, too.there are no reloads in this game, only clicky clicky click, or brrrrt.pistols - 32 ammo max. great, and i mean perfect for popping heads on lower health/weaker enemies, as well as those random finishers after they just won't die from a grenade.submachine guns - 200 ammo max, but don't let that deceive you of its short lived firing time. don't go for headshots, this weapon has constant spread regardless of your reticle. maybe aim for jetpacks, but the best way to go is use these when you're out of/want to conserve adrenaline, and try to get enemies flashing yellow to farm drops to make up for the weapon's low accuracy.shotgun - 24 ammo max. oh boy. use it for everything. and i mean everything. from tapping elites down to one health, to bounding around mechs just barely out of their grenade explosions, this gun can do almost everything you'll need. pro tip (and really only) - use it after a jump/while midair in general, using your airborne arc to evade shots, and align your reticle so as it will pass over a head/weakpoint without having to directly aim; and only use adrenaline right before, and during your shot, then release to rechamber a shell to not waste slow motion time.grenade launcher - only 8 ammo max, keep a close eye on that counter. don't use it for general purpose. save it for groups, but primarily mechs since you may be using the other armor piercing weapons regularly. goes boom real nice, but the radius isn't terribly big.chain gun - 100 ammo max, its damage can make those bullets go a long way. hop repeatedly while using it since you're slowed down while on the ground, and don't use adrenaline unless necessary; its high damage will prevent you from really needing to slow down. works well for relatively distant enemies, but is inadvisable for close range unless you know you can kill them before they either shoot or get to melee range (if applicable). not as good for groups as advertised, in my experience.railgun - 16 ammo max, and pretty scarce most of the time. oh yeah. the good stuff (i love this kind of weapon). brief (and i mean brief) charge up, and one laser focused projectile. literally; best used to lower enemies to one health, or obliterate them entirely for assured drops - very difficult to use against more distant targets, and there's not as much hitsound/feedback if you do strike them at range, i believe. use for fast disabling of problematic individuals, and keep a sharp eye on your ammo - even if you have 6, it will be a long time typically before you get more, unless you're late game (the same goes for all other weapons besides pistols, smg and shotgun).rocket launcher - 24 ammo max, i believe (i barely use it so i don't quite remember). no it doesn't shoot one big projectile, the grenade launcher already has you covered on that. fires, redundantly, dumbfire rockets; they wiggle and spread out on a short trail outward and forward from where you were when you clicked. don't be afraid to get close and aim somewhat toward the ground, but don't be stupid and (too) reckless. very good for straight up removing mechs, and later flying enemies you'll encounter; and a real *click* noice weapon for weakening, or even deleting groups.movement you'll figure out, but pro tip, you can both go higher and get farther on a wall if you slide parallel to it and immediately jump once you're sped up.a nice dead set quest of blood, gore, bullets and finally redemption through struggle and violence, ironically adrenaline pumping fun from start to finish.why was six afraid of seven?because she has a big arsenal of lethal weapons.and she's coming to get him.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a very enjoyable shooter, split into 12 Missions over 3 Episodes. Taking between 5-7 hours to 100% complete. And if you are wanting more, it has optional extra modes, Time Attack and Horde Mode.As you progress through the game you find up to 7 different types of guns to switch though, each with different strengths and weaknesses. The game has a small handful of not very memorable boss fights, which are mostly just shoot weak points to be able to do damage. There is some good variety in different enemies to fight and while the AI is not super amazing, it doesn't have to be.The gunplay mixed with the movement, combined with the music makes up for the games flaws. It feels great slowing down time to pick off incoming targets with pistol headshots or lining up a blast from the rail gun and seeing a colourful explosion of drops with each kill.The level design is pretty linear with minimal backtracking which I love, you are constantly progressing and are never away from the action for long. There isn't many hidden away secrets, and you don't feel bad for missing anything as there is no level completion %. All in all, SPRAWL is currently up there as one of the most enjoyable shooters I've played, it never felt like a slog and it doesn't outstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: A FPS with fun platforming but combat that leaves more to be desired, but still fun.SPRAWL is a FPS game made by mostly I think 2-3 people. Taking place in a ruined cyberpunk world you play as SEVEN, a disowned super soldier, as she blasts her way throw simply all the evil government pawns in her quest to get to the spiral with Father guiding her. SPRAWL provides a interesting mixed of platforming and move shoot elements, while at times leave me feeling like there was lost potential here. But still manages to be a solid game that I though was worth a playthrough. Gameplay wise, SPRAWL takes a lot of notes from other movement shooters, but with platforming in it's gameplay mix. This is because Seven as the ability to wall run/jump off of basically any wall in the game. This gives you a lot of movement opportunities when it comes to combat. Especially combined with the bullet-time ability easily access with a click of the altfire. Likewise the weaponry is fairly standard, with a few exceptions. You have dual magnum pistols for great accuracy shots, a very chunky sounding shotgun, and so on and so forth. However, I feel like most of the latter half of the weaponry tends to not escalate forward from the first 4 weapons you get. Such as the Railgun feeling somewhat underpowered for it's namesake, or the minigun slowing down your movement to the point it's extremely tedious to use if you're not near a wall. However the Rocket Launcher does hit this mark with the amount of projectiles it fires out, like a explosive shotgun. It also doesn't help that a lot, if not all the enemies act more or less the same way. Either standing still and shooting projectiles at you or beelining towards you. Usually this isn't problem for other FPS games but it's because this game has a focus on movement and arena-to-arena level design where it starts becoming to get tedious fast. I feel like the first episode has the best of the combat since it manages to fit the fast paced gameplay, while shooting enemies running from rooftop to rooftop. Style wise, SPRAWL does look really good with it's stylized retro visuals. While yet again I think the variety and aesthetics peak during the first episode, the succeeding two episode still look well done. Especially from small team behind it. I'm fairly certain that this game was made in Unreal 4 or Unity since I was able to spot a stock jumping animation that's used on almost all of the enemies. But I am glad to say that this is one of those games that uses the engine effectively and looks the part because of it.Overall, SPRAWL is a fun, short FPS game! While I think it starts to overstay it's welcome near the end. It's still a pretty enjoyable ride thanks to some well mixed gameplay elements. Really my main issues come with minor stutters with the combat loop, like how you have a melee attack that basically means nothing since headshots do the exact same thing with giving you back resources, and other issues. But as a whole it was worth experiencing it. I highly hope the devs take what they learned and the feedback from SPRAWL for whatever they decide to make next!!

It is up to you because it's one of those games that is just worth every Cent.  - Maybe more Variation on Melee animation and Execution Animations for FinishersSPRAWL is one of those Games I will return to Yearly to cleanse my pallet or to satisfy my Craving for Virtual Gore with Pristine Visuals. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic game that I wish came out 20yrs ago. The campaign can be finished in about 5-6hrs and is non-stop FPS action from start to finish, with a fantastic soundtrack that I listen to frequently. Despite some of its flaws, I keep coming back to this game because everything just clicks and sends me back to the distant time of early 2000's.Ghost Wetware is the best song in the OST. PS, if you have Quake, head over to the Discord server and download the SPRAWL 96 mod for free.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the campaign in about 5 to 6 hours I can say the game is absolutely worth its price, the combat loop feels like Doom Eternal meets Quake meets Mirror's Edge, the fast paced agressive Drum & Bass soundtrack by Revel is incredible and all the different weapons are well balanced and satisfying to use.Sprawl stands out in a sea of colorful Cyberpunk shooters with its original take on the genre, showcasing mostly red and brown industrial environments that looks more like a Chinese City 17. The levels will take you to factories, rooftops, abandoned canals and junkyards, all the while Father a rogue AI provides guidance and additional context to your mission.Whether you like F.E.A.R. inspired indie shooters such as Severed Steel and Trepang2, or more popular boomer shooters like Doom Eternal and the original Quake, Sprawl feels like a successful mesh of the best aspects of each genre.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A Solid "Boomer Shooter" with good platforming and mobility options.  Enemies feel a little boring after awhile since despite the different types, they all have very similar animations if not the same animations.  Everything looks like and the soundtrack emphasizes a "Ghost in the Shell" influence, with a more dystopian "Blade Runner" theme.  Bosses feel a little bullet spongey.  Campaign is short and for those who dig the setting there's a bunch of hidden text logs throughout the levels to collect.  While the Cyberpunk aesthetic is there the gameplay doesn't particularly take advantage of the fact other than having a bullet-time mode and the ability to wall run.  These are both well done though and you frankly don't need anything else to make a good shooter but it does feel like a missed opportunity.  Still it works as this is a "Boomer Shooter".  Combat is fast and aggressive among large arenas and stages with the city stage being a real standout in both size and scope.  Campaign is short, it took me about five hours to complete on normal difficulty but that isn't necessarily a bad thing.  I also haven't collected all the text logs.  Overall if you're looking for a quick shooter to blast through with more mobility than the average game of this type, this is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: From the 'boomer-shooter' genre I find SPRAWL the most fun. It's quite simple game with simple story. Except of shooting, game includes wall running - with this mix I had feel of  similarities to Ghostrunner a bit. SPRAWL indroduces new weapons/enemies throughout the game, however not in large numbers.Aesthetics holds this game up - there is strong Ghost in the Shell vibe. I liked the pixelated textures technique used here (similar to System Shock Remake).But the music! Music is wonderful, it greatly enhances the fighting scenes. It mixes vibes of GotS and Matrix. I still listen to it after I finished the game.Speaking of finishing the game - it's really short, about 4 hours. I found it just right, considering the scope of gameplay.Fair to note - SPRAWL was created by two people, If i'm not mistaken, so it's quite impressive nevertheless.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly what it says on the box: a high-speed get-good Quake-style retro-shooter with wall running.  Combat feels awesome, the music is amazing, and the movement tech is incredibly satisfying.  Takes a lot of inspiration from the gritty cyberpunk of old (Ghost in the Shell, if the OST wasn't obvious enough lol), which I'm a huge fan of.  An easy recommend from me, as is the soundtrack.Also has time trials, horde modes, and scoring, so there's plenty of replay-ability.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I went to a Gamejam not too long ago and the organizers showcased the trailer for SPRAWL. After that, I knew I had to grab the game as soon as possible. As luck would have it, they were handing over two keys there and I managed to score one at the end of the event. Really enjoyed the gameplay, the atmosphere and the story. Mad props for the devs, y'all rock.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: One of the more unique boomer shooters in the genre at time of writing. Its faced paced, well executed, and its slow mechanic weak point gimmick is fun and interesting. It'll keep you engaged, and even at times make you feel kick*** when you hit a really cool combo with the slow. Enemy types are I think where the game hits its biggest wall, as variety is pretty lackluster. Boss fights are what I would say are "okay" at best. Nothing memorable about them, your true fun here is in the combat. Weapon sound and design are top notch, the wall running is done well, and definitely adds to the experience for sure. The story is mediocre, but honestly lets be real, we don't play this genre for the story. You play a boomer shooter for the action, and this game delivers in heaps. A modest asking price for the content provided, however try to get it on a sale if you can. But even at full price I feel that the game play and length is worth the $15, a great entry overall in this emerging genre!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game with unique look, rapid vertical gameplay and atmospheric OST.Pros: First chapter impress with its depressive cyberpunk style. Gameplay put you in flow as soon as you start to understand movement and shootings mechanics, and makes almost every battle to look cinematic. Unique 90/00s like OST with choral vocals, having strong vibes of Ghost in the Shell. Pretty descend weapon sounds and design. One of the best shotguns in the games. Game works perfectly on Steam Deck.Cons or Wishes to have: At third chapter game loses its visual style, also level design becomes simpler loosing complex verticality, and you get wallrun arenas with parkour sections between them. Soon you realize NPCs run after you in one heap like zombies, that allows you to abuse their stupidness)) Rail gun without charge bar or fire at will mode completely useless in rapid FPS as well as minigun which damage not compensate lack of maneuverability. Parkour movements would nice to be more flawless at transitions from state to state.Despite all the cons, I definitely recommend this game and wish the creator all the best, hoping to see more games with his unique vision and sound in future
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game. The movement feels really good and *most* of the weapons do as well. My only real issue is that I was able to beat the game and obtain all of the achievements in 5 or so hours and that was with the difficulty cranked up and having missed collectibles in the first 5 levels requiring me to replay through the entire first episode.Other than the length of the game, the only other thing I can think of that I didn't really enjoy was the rail gun. Rail guns are categorically my favorite type of weapon in these games and I just feel like this one has the power of a nerf gun. :/I think for the length of the game and the price point that it's at, you could purchase a few other FPS games here on Steam that will net you better bang for your buck. For $5.00 USD more than this game, you could get Dusk, Amid Evil or POSTAL: Brain Damaged, any of which will keep you entertained a little longer then SPRAWL.I would definitely recommend the game in general but I think it's better obtained during a sale since the play time is quite short and the price is $14.99 USD without discounts. If I hadn't missed some optional collectibles in my first play through, I likely would have only had 4 or 4.5 hours on record.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Just on the strength of it's combat alone, SPRAWL is an easy recommend. Lightning fast but never incomprehensible, this is slow-mo acrobatics at it's best. The mobility of Titanfall 2 is maybe the obvious comparison and for good reason. But while Titanfall's wallrunning and sliding works as key part of a larger toybox, here SPRAWL laser focuses on traversal to give even the most basic fights a momentum that not a lot of other shooters can match. Aiding this is REVEL's incredible score. Brutal, haunting, and perfectly drives the vibe of both the combat and the environment.I was very impressed by how well the weapons and enemy variety fit together. Enemies never feel like you're forced into one specific approach to counter them, but the array of behaviors and weak points to exploit naturally encourages mixing up your tactics. SPRAWL isn't punishing but it's not afraid to push you to use every tool at your disposal through large, aggressive mobs and relatively low ammo capacity. It hits my personal favorite kind of difficulty curve for games like this: the kind you feel like you're just *barely* out pacing. It never catches up to you enough that you're well and truly stuck, but you feel the need to use everything you can and the desire to hone your skill to be even better.As stated, if that were everything on offer here it would still be an easy get. But SPRAWL's secret weapon is it's exceptional setting and atmosphere. Sense of place will always count for a lot for me in any kind of game. And SPRAWL's decaying, brutalist cyberpunk hellscapes are a joy to just exist in, combat or not. I spent so much time stopping to take in the winding alleyways and vistas of this dying city. I want to be very clear about how much I love the combat, so there are no misunderstandings when I say the environment might honestly be my favorite part of the experience. It's just spot on.It's also worth mentioning that while SPRAWL isn't exactly a narrative *heavy* game, there's more to dig into here than one might expect on the surface. I really enjoyed piecing together the larger nature of the story and world through the small fragments you find as you go. And the context they lent brought some welcome added weight to the proceedings once it was all said and done.It's hard to think of an area where SPRAWL left me wanting more, except that I want more of it. I tore through it back at launch and haven't really stopped thinking about it since. This isn't a recommend, it's a must.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Don't sleep on this game it's an absolute gem. SPRAWL is a potent little FPS experience that blends aspects of Cyberpunk, Max Payne, Titanfall and Doom. The gameplay is extremely satisfying and fluid, with incredible atmosphere and art direction, a solid variety of weapons, diverse map design, varied enemy types, and a killer OST (REVEL on Spotify). All of this was created by just two people - unreal. Can't wait to see what they cook up next.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl has fun gun play, movement is well polished and can feel floaty in an intentional and fun way, level design although in some ways *looks* confusing I really didn't struggle to navigate through each level, Enemy design felt properly introduced and interesting, Music was very fitting especially on the final level imo. I really liked the VA and effects on "FATHER" as well as the story that unravels in such a short (3ish) hours of time. I encountered a couple bugs but only on my second play through to get to 100% such as a door that refused to open when it was supposed to and the  not activating when it was supposed to. Not many other issues beyond that besides minor personal subjective complaints.Overall 8 out of 10. a good game from a small dev team. Not much to say other than good job, i enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fantastic time, enjoyed the whole thing start to finish with no issues. Music is amazing, level design is great, all the weapons are fun, great visuals too. I liked the story as well, and the voice acting was solid. Honestly an all-around great game, no complaints. I think the length is fine for what they did and I cant wait to see more out of these guys. Definitely one of my top boomer shooters no doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is literally everything I wanted Ghostrunner to be. Immersive and challenging combat; but not impossible. The Doom vibes come through and work seamlessly with the parcore. If anything, I could have used more challenging areas that required intense parcore and shooting simultaneously. You can play the levels safe and peak corners or go wild running on walls popping headshots. The music is perfect, and keeps me going even when I reach a difficult part. The story is weaved through QR codes and a deep voice in your head that just feels very cyberpunk. I just wish there was more game here. Definitely recommend for the price. I hope to see more content from this creator, and hopefully levels that require difficult parcore alongside their combat in places.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to tell you to disregard most of the negative comments now. I've read most of them and, for the most part, they just aren't true.SPRAWL is a lovely little boomer shooter with excellent combat, level design, music, and atmosphere. Normally, I find these types of games rather tedious and while SPRAWL does suffer from issues common to the genre like repetitive gameplay and meh AI, it absolutely handle these issues better than its competitors. Overall, playing this game just feels awesome and the story, so long as you read the documents, isn't half bad, though it definitely takes a back seat. I'd recommend getting it on sale for around 10 bucks, as it's only about 3.5 hours long. Tons and tons of fun await you!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and I can't wait to start it again. First to look for all the QR codes, but above all to rediscover the first levels with a better understanding of the gameplay mechanics. The game really makes you want to improve, to learn how to chain combos, to move fluidly and as quickly as possible. The gameplay is very satisfying, in an "easy to learn, hard to master" kind of way. The weapon arsenal is interesting, each weapon adds its little something extra. The soundtrack is amazing and fits the game perfectly. I will for sure listen to it outside the game. Some levels can be a little confusing, but the game is never frustrating. I just wish there was a little more verticality in certain levels. Kudos to the duo behind this great project.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: At first I felt that the world doesn't always have the clearest or most suitable geometry for its parkour mechanics, which are quite simple and the AI doesn't do anything fancy, just chase you and shoot at you, but once you get more used to it and into the gameplay its really fun and easy to jump into. The world looks really cool and they really captured some aspects of Ghost in the Shell, which you can especially her in the excellent soundtrack. The devs did a good job and its really fun.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is what you get if you bred Titanfall, F.E.A.R., and Quake together. A fast paced twitch shooter with wall running and explosions. My only real gripe with the general gamplay was sometimes enemies felt like they could see through walls, or that shots would clip through them without doing damage. However those things rarely happened, and I greatly enjoyed the game. It's going into the list of my favorite shooters alongside F.E.A.R., Halo, COD Advanced Warfare, and Crysis. I look forward to seeing what this team makes in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is an incredibly fun, fast paced shooter where the action rarely stops with music that amps up the whole experience.Pros:- Adrenaline system which slows down time is exceptional, stringing together multi-weapon kills is very satisfying.- Enemy types are varied, each level introduces a new threat.- Movement is fast and frantic, you'll just be wallrunning off of walls to get stylish headshots for fun.- Soundtrack that changes depending on how much action there is currently.- Visual style of the game is beautiful, a retro aesthetic with modern lighting.- Weapons had nice variety but you'll always be switching between them depending on the situation.Cons:- Episode 2 boss due to constantly having to take damage during the fight with it taking place in water.- Final boss had way too much stuff going on, would have worked better if it went through phases instead of multiple different threats (including adds) at once.- When not using Adrenaline it can be very difficult to land a shot due to how fast paced everything is.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine those ♥♥♥♥♥♥ de facto pretentious pseudo-philosophic retro 80's-90's vaporwave cyberpunk japanese cartoons that japanincels on twitter love to whack off about, well Sprawl is the total opposite i mean is kinda like that but actually good, it has sauce and its an FPS so i totally recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game would be just another retro FPS if it weren't for the parkour and slo-mo. It's hard, but when you keep moving, run and jump off walls, and slow mo aim your shots while airborne it all comes together. The graphics are inconsistent, sometimes pretty, sometimes blocky or pixellated for no reason. Story dumb. Map levels can be janky. However, when it all comes together I have to admit it was fun. Recommended in a bundle or on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I bought this game at a discounted price ($11) This game is mechanically very strong, the wall running is intuitive and easy to learn which is crucial due to it being a central game-play tool. It is hard not to draw parallels with the Ghostrunner series but I think Sprawl is successful in creating a neat little cyberpunk visual palette of its own. By focusing on ranged combat, Sprawl deviates itself from Ghostrunner, allowing for a 'right tool for the job' approach, this combined with the movement brings Doom Eternal to mind.One has to go into this game as an arcade style experience as there is minimal world-building. The atmosphere, art design and OST immerse the player sufficiently for what this game ultimately is, a fun little romp in an obvious love letter to the cyberpunk sub-genre. It should be noted this game was made by 2 people (3 including the OST creator), which indicates a very high level of game design skill.The weapons feel punchy enough, and the bullet time 'weak point' system when combined with the parkour styled movement can create some nice little action moments. The OST is a strong point, and the voice acting is quality and functionally serves the story.Overall score 8/10 at an $11 purchase price.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Solid for the price. Just makes me want to play Severed steel, which has 100% destructible environment, or heck, even Get To The Orange Door for its sense of speed. But, that doe not mean this game lacks merit of its own. Pick it up if you like booters. Turn off aim assist if using controller, and, don't use controller lol.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Platformer/FPS in the similar vein of Trepang2Honestly, if you are craving more of that vibe then this is your go-to.  MORE OPTIONS as far as configurable right out of the box than even that title has.  Add to the fact that it is set in the FUTURE version of the walled city and it is a cyber-punkish winwin of action fun/joy!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 8/10, the mechanics, storyline, engagement are all done really well in this game. Each boss fight was really cool for the first time. I do wish there were either achievements for harder modes, or something that would reward aside form discovery aspect as this game did take 7 hours to 100%. For the price I would hope for more content around the game, obviously a player can make their own challenges, but a few small add ons can make this game go from a 7/8 out of 10 to a 8/9 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Great shooter overall.The mechanics are really well done: it's a mix of platforming (wall jumping / parkour, think titanfall), slow motion and shooting with a nice variety of satisfying weapons. These are all done spectacular well. In fact, I would argue that the platforming part is much more enjoyable than in doom eternal which is no small feat for an indie game.The graphics are also very nice, a cool mix of retro shooters and futuristic levels with a fair amount of flashy light (avoid this if you are sensitive, obviously).What's not so great: the music which is just OK, but quite repetitive.I've encountered a few bugs: one at the last level, where a room doesn't open so you remain stuck and gotta reload (this seems confirmed by some reviewers i.e.  bizzarrely, the game crashed at the end of the final credits but no big deal.When I started the game, the tutorial for the wall jumping involved some rather complex sequences, which concerned me for the rest of the game as I wasn't keen in that kind of things, but actually the game was much more forgiving and there weren't almost at all frustrating platforming parts.Despite the flaws, this is a must play and at some point I will replay it for sure.It's been bundled in humble, so you can probably find the key quite cheap also which is a bonus.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty action packed FPS that makes you "dance with guns" all around the screen!The gameplay reminds me a bit of the Ghostrunner game except with guns. It is fast paced kind like DOOM ETERNAL, where you have to move constantly or you're toast!The story is... better explained on the game page! From what I could gather, you or somewhat of a soldier from a elite group. You were betrayed long ago and you go on to take anyone in your way. Not much to go on but just let the guns tell the story!The music in SPRAWL is pretty good! Same goes with the visuals... not the best but quite decent for an Unreal Engine based game.ULTRAWIDE monitor has a good support with proper FOV option.My only gripe with SPRAWL would be in the technical side of things. I had two game game crashes. Thankfully, the game do save pretty often so no big deal here!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. Imagine a combination of the best parts of FEAR, Titan Fall 2, Half-Life 2 and Oni, with the soundtrack of Ghost in the Shell and aesthetic of Akira. I feel reasonably confident in saying if you love any of those games, you'll love this. It's short-ish, but is all killer no filler. I highly, highly recommend this game.-Graphics are excellent, the stylized aesthetic is grimey and fitting.-Music is great, catchy, reactive, not repetitive. I find myself going back and listening to the soundtrack on spotify from time to time now.-Guns are punchy and fun.-Lots of tasteful references to other games, like the grenade enemies being called "Ogres," and the robo-dogs being named "Okami," the grenade launcher manufacturer being "Shogo," etc. -Just the right runtime (not too long, not too short, beatable in two to three sittings or one long sitting).-Not a huge variety of enemies (enough, but there could be more, and one boss is semi-repeated).-Some of the level design is obtuse. Mostly there are "lines" that you can run and gain momentum, but a few levels it's somewhat hard to find the intended path, and I had to jankily climb.-The story is quite shallow (but the ending has a decent, semi-subversive twist).Definitely worthy of your support, even at full price I'd highly recommend this game. This game is inspired, very clearly a labour of love, especially considering the main developer team consisted of just two people!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A short but very solid boomer-shooter, with slow-motion that makes the game waaaaay easier. Still, it's good fun and you're always moving and jumping everywhere. The soundtrack is good. On the other hand, enemies sometimes get stuck in wall or forget you exist mid-fight, so it's a bit janky by moments. Also, and this is important, make sure to play "exclusive fullscreen" as there's an issue that prevents you from shooting if you play in "borderless fullscreen" mode.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: While it is certainly structured in a quake-like style, the wall running, sliding, and slow motion really makes this one feel a big step apart from your typical indie boomer shooter.Perfect length to provide fun challenge that wraps things up before it start to get repetitive. Ran perfectly on my set up and looks great.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: My background:1. Not a big shooter guy2. Not a boomer shooter guy3. Haven't played modern boomer shooter gamesSoooo it's good. As you could tell I'm not a shooter guy, especially boomer shooter. While the gameplay sound perfect to me: bunch of crazy guns, super high-speed movement, versatility and so on, it kinda does not click to me. Like I sometime get in the flow and everything, but just deep inside, it doesn't clickWhat I usually don't like about these games is the world building and the setting. And that's why I got to play this game over others, cuz this one has a really nice world. The art in this game is my favorite part, especially with the retro settings. The art direction is just amazing, and the execution! Oh my, these levels are badass. But.... Only like the 1 chapter. The second chapter is just grey corridors and the last one is better, but still not as great as the first one.The music is also great, fits the game perfectly.The gameplay is fun, movement is crunchy and the bosses are fun. Some of the enemies be killing me fast tho, but the adrenaline mechanic is neatIf you are not a boomer shooter guy or just wondering about this game, try it, it's fun and beautiful
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Deceptively simple at first, but more challenging, complex and satisfying as you progress. If you're a fan of movement-based FPS like Titanfall, Ghostrunner, and of course DOOM, then you'll enjoy this game. It's clearly inspired by many sources, but it has several enjoyable surprises of its own.- The story is a simple but easily digestible cyberpunk dystopia journey. Scanning the QR codes reveals more, optional, lore.- The aesthetic of the late 90s/ early 2000s PSone and N64 era graphics is endlessly charming. But with high frame rate!- The gameplay is always fast, intense and gets harder at a decent pace. You're fighting hordes by the end of the game.- The level design makes use of your movement in constantly creative ways. Wall running feels flawless and responsive. - The enemy design forces you to utilize your entire arsenal, your environment, and your decision making.It's also nice that there's no fall damage, no death from falling into voids, and there are generous checkpoints. There are, at times, some cheap deaths, because you're very squishy for the entire game, and you sometimes get caught by one or two enemies and die instantly. However, you're encouraged to wall run and slide to make every fight possible. Even when there's dozens of enemies around. And the soundtrack? Phenomenal, from start to finish.I highly recommend this game for fans of 'boomer shooters'. There's so many these days, but this stands out if you enjoy the wall-running and sliding variety of indie FPS. Very similar to Severed Steel, in that way. Seriously, worth the asking price for a deep, enjoyable experience in Sprawl.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a competent boomer shooter. A solid 7.5-8/10 from me.The aesthetic, sound design and music are the highlights of the game. This highly military yet ruined and destroyed aesthetic is nice. The music for blood pumping, and lack for a better word, HARD. It really enhanced the shooting, weapon switching and blood shed you'll be doing throughout the game. This rock EDM combined with slow ambiance or opera singing is great and doesn't get annoying. All the weapons feels and sound good and are fun to use, somewhat. The weapons really only feel good when they work together in this harmony of constant switching, Except the shotgun, chaingun and rockets of course. Even the rail gun is kinda meh. The weapons don't have a sick alt fire mode, but they still feel good. Just don't stand out. Except the rockets since like a dozen shoot out at a time. The highlight of combat is the bullet time that's activated at will and get constantly when killing enemies via weakpoint. The game feels built around this mechanic, it feels too hard otherwise with how fast paced and hectic it is. Though it might be the lack of experience with pc gaming, but even then the game feels like it wouldn't be as fun as it is without it. It's fast but basic, the main movement it has is wall running.The game is the perfect length with this gameplay loop. It does not overstay it's welcome. When it's getting tiring it's over. If you still want more, there's a horde mode as well. The game time is kinda bloated, would pause and take a break every so often with how intense the game can be. A nice fun little experience, a good recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a love letter to boomer shooters, ghost in the shell, quake in some regard, and the cyberpunk genre. This game deserves more praise. I've had my eye on this game ever since it was released and it deserves all the praise. Music is awesome as well, again reminds me a lot of Ghost in the Shell. I listen to it on Spotify all the time. Can't wait for the next game! Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment I dove into the game, it became an instant favorite for its adrenaline-fueled, high-octane action. The adrenaline feature is a nod to the iconic bullet time mechanics of Max Payne, adding a thrilling dimension to the gameplay. Set against a backdrop of dystopian, post-apocalyptic landscapes, the game immerses you in its dark and foreboding world, enhanced by a pulsating soundtrack heavy on bass.With just an hour of gameplay under my belt, I found myself already dreading the moment when I'll have to put the game down after completing it. The anticipation for what's next is palpable, and I can only hope that the developers have plans for DLC content to extend the adrenaline rush even further.In summary, this game delivers an electrifying experience that leaves you craving more. It's a testament to the developers' skill in crafting a thrilling and immersive world that captivates players from the very beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid boomer shooter with some great speed and world traversal. You can wall run, slide, etc as you race around arenas to fight enemies. The gun play is solid enough for a boomer shooter but the running is what really hooks you in. The gameplay loops is pretty solid. It's also pretty short and doesn't overstay its welcome. Almost every level introduces a new enemy and weapon as well to keep things fresh. There's also a slow mode button so you can pop heads!The only downside of the game is the AI is pretty bad. They just always run straight at you. Some can jump with jet packs to different platforms where they'll shoot you from. There are also some sections where enemies won't trigger until you shoot at them specifically. Shooting at one won't turn the whole room around which is a bit strange. The odd part of the pathing though is around certain ramps. Sometimes instead of jumping down at you, they'll have to run to the top of the ramp and then down the ramp towards you. Fortunately the dumb AI can lead to some fun. You can manipulate it since you know how everyone will react and try to lead them down a chokepoint where you can blow them all up with a rocket launcher. Sprawl is short and sweet. If you like high speed boomer shooters and want something with a little more freedom in movement, you should give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a fast-paced shooter with . Unfortunately, it’s also . Unless parkours movement and combat are enough to keep you entertained for 6 hours straight, , in my opinion at least. The game gives you all your movement options from the get-go, and only drip-feeds you a very limited arsenal of well-designed, but fairly standard shooter weapons (shotgun, railgun, rocket launcher etc.) over its 12 levels. Sprawl also manages to conjure , but then that’s where it stays for the entirety of the campaign, with little variation in the environments or the tone of the game.So right from the start, let me tell you: If you like to see something more from your shooters than movement and shooting, Sprawl is not for you. Even if you like your shooters simple and focused on action,  does a way better job of constantly feeding you new weapons, abilities, vehicle missions, new unique environments and so on, to keep the gameplay loop fresh.But  is also a good example for why Sprawl might just be exactly what you’re looking for. That’s because  than that of many other movement shooters: You only get a slow-motion power, a wallrun and a slide (so no double jumps or quick dashes), but  to move fluently around the levels while trying to avoid enemy fire and outmanoeuvring Sprawl’s pretty deadly enemies – no infinite rocket slides here! Some weapons can change how you move around, like the shotgun (which imparts backward momentum) and the minigun (which slows you down when firing). In that way, the movement in Sprawl actually reminds me a bit of  in how involved it can be. You also need to conserve your ammunition. That means that .Personally, the game gets a bit too repetitive for my taste, but I can absolutely see how well-made Sprawl is. It’s almost like an exercise in highly polished minimalism. . So if you count yourself amongst these kinds of players, I think you’ll really enjoy Sprawl.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, short, challenging, fast paced run-and-gunner with an old school aesthetic...or a "boomer shooter" as they are been coined nowadays. I never played old school shooter originals like Quake, DOOM or UT so I can't exactly say its nostalgic for me, but its still fun as hell. Certainly scratches that itch while I work my way around to Ghostrunner 2!Smooth parkour and the use of an adrenaline system that lets you slow down time for precision kills in between the madness deliver an overall satisfying experience that hones both your reaction time and target acquisition. Games like this are perfect for training you even if you're initially quite slow or uncoordinated, but MIGHT be overwhelming if you prefer slower paced games.Either way, the devs clearly wanted the game to be accessible to a wider audience, as they implemented things like "god mode" and damage/adrenaline modifiers right in the settings from the get go if you wanted more or less of a challenge to enjoy at your own pace, especially since there is no typical difficulty setting like Easy/Normal/Hard etc

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is a difficult game to like. It's got so much going for it: the art style is great, the levels are (mostly) well designed, the weapon roster is varied, and the systems that it uses are fun. It's just that some of these systems are in desperate need of tweaking in order to make this a consistent, fun package. IMPACT: weapons don't feel like they're that impactful. When I shoot a low tier fodder enemy at point blank range with a double barrel shotgun, I expect to see a fountain of blood followed by a flying ragdoll. What I see instead, is a still standing enemy with maybe a missing head that won't even fall over right away and didn't bleed much. This is an issue not only for lacking that feel good impact, but also because of bad feedback. Half of the time, I'm not even sure if I've killed an enemy or not because they're still standing for a second or two and I may shoot them again, wasting ammo and time. Although there is a very good, active system to recover not only ammo, but health and slow-mo adrenaline as well, this shouldn't make up for the fact that the damage feedback is awful. My other nitpick is with the somewhat very confusing path of progression. Sprawl's levels require a fair amount of backtracking, which in and of itself is not good, but on top of that, many of the levels (especially in episode 1) look VERY similar. You can easily get lost or turned around without any kind of monuments to guide you. Now I don't think that this would require an objective marker, or god forbid a map, but I do think that there needs to be a little more attention to environmental clues. This is also strange because the game already does this in other areas, but some are lacking. Just having the intended door or hallway lit up with new lights would suffice. I have faith in the devs, they seem to be responding to player feedback and I think that in time and after a few updates, the game will be in great shape. There's nothing inherently bad about Sprawl, (except for much of the voice acting), so I think that it could still shape up to be one of the better indie retro FPS games to have released in the last couple years. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: This a a fun little game that i would recommenced to somebody who wants another boomer shooter with max payne style time freeze ability's. Although there is problems that i would like to discuss, anyways here is the review. Starting with game play. Game play is fun for the 6 or so hour play through. It doesn't overstay its welcome or get bogged down with skill trees and weapon upgrades, which tend to make games feel like a slog. Instead you receive a new weapon in each section, which spices up the combat and makes it less boring. But notice how i said less boring; you see thats because the weapons you get are the most generic guns a game has to offer. i just wish one of these boomer shooters would come up with something unique. After you you get the shotgun, smg, and rocket launcher there is no use for the rest of the weapons, especially the rail gun. But the wall running, time slowing, and shotgun make it overall not to bad, but if this game was 10+ hours i could see it getting boring. 7/10 gameplay. Now talking about the bosses and enemies. Enemies are a bit generic as well. You have your standard normal solider, then your armored bigger solider, then robot dogs, and a few different mechs. There is a few other guys that look a bit different, but pretty much serve the same purpose as the rest, which is to run at you and shoot. The only cool and unique enemy is the ghost ninjas that are invisible, and the only way to kill them is to slow down time to see their head. It makes for a cool encounter as they can sneak up on you and get some damage in quick. Overall cool enemy. The bosses on the other hand are pretty bad. They all boil down to shooting their weak points as you run around in a circle in the empty arena to avoid getting shot. Aesthetically, they are all robots who fly in the air and look about the same, which is boring. AI design is like a 5/10.  Overall i would give the game a 6.5/10. That may sound harsh but i would like to give the devs criticism they need to hear for their next game or possibly dlc. My advice to them is to take the foundation you have right now for the game and make a big 2.0 update. It may sound odd but they need to go back in and re-due the game mildly. Keep the same levels, animations, and voice work; but remove half the enemies and weapons, and then redue the rest. Keep the basic weapons and enemies, but the rest make completely new. Make more quality weapon and enemy designs and the game could easily jump up to a 8 or 9 out of 10. But as it stands its held back by being to safe. Anyways that my review. i hope the devs understand i like the game but it needs work.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good and short game. I have some gripes, like for example, the chaingun. For a rotary barrel weapon, it fires slowly and slows you down when you're firing it. _childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is an exciting cyberpunk FPS. A strong mix of old school boomer shooter with modern movement, if you're a fan of the genre this game will catch your attention. It feels like a love letter, with every mechanic from a shooting game you've played smashed into one chaotic 4-6 hour experience. The look won't appeal to everyone, but the grimy colours and neon effects really stood out to me. At it's best Sprawl looks stunning. The music is strong, if a bit repetitive for me, but the sound effects stand out as engaging and powerful.Movement is fast, wallrunning and sliding feel fluid and smooth. They combine well with the bullet time (though this does have it's own problems), and the optional advanced mechanics like shotgun jumping do give you a large amount of options throughout the game. Unfortunately, this fluidity doesn't always feel utilised in levels. They can get repetitive both in look and objectives. Some (especially early on when you aren't as familiar with your capabilities) can be hard to navigate.Gunplay feels heavy and satisfying. Pistols crack and ping headshots. Shotguns have a bassy thump. A lot of guns have specific uses, however some quickly become overshadowed. One gun, found later in the game, reduces your movement speed significantly while being fired. I only found it useful when it was best not to move, a weird feeling in a movement based shooter. The time slowing ability you can use can be incredibly satisfying, highlighting weak spots and giving you time to think (or appreciate how cool whatever you did just was). It can also do the inverse, as you wait for seemingly hours to pump your shotgun or charge late game weapons while you get peppered with walls of bullets.Most levels consist of going to somewhere, shooting waves of enemies and turning on generators to get to new spaces. Occasionally a boss will show up, with specific areas you must shoot to deal damage. The variation of enemies is good, though most blend in with each other later down the line. The best really get you thinking, changing plans mid combat to deal with them optimally. Some enemies can do surprising amounts of damage, leading to a small portion of unfair deaths. This comes up a lot in areas with bottomless pits, if you fall in you'll respawn (with no penalty) on a nearby platform, potentially surrounded by enemies which will immediately fire.The story is vague. Most of it is hidden behind QR codes you have to find and can't be read in game. As interesting an idea as that is, it really takes away from any in game tension or flow - looking away from the game to scan and read something that I may never find again. I really want to give the story more credit, from what I've read it seems deep and detailed, but It'd make so much more sense to read the interesting notes and conversations at any time in the game. Maybe only some should have been hidden as an ARG? Overall I highly recommend Sprawl. It has it's flaws, but the punchy combat and smooth parkour make up for the little things. There are some extra modes too, if you like time trials or survival modes. It really is a game about feel, getting into a flow state and blasting through waves of sci-fi foes. A really good pick if you're looking for an evening or two of classic FPS fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Ghostrunner?  Quake?  Doom 2016?  Bullet time?  BOY do I have the game for you.Killing an enemy in slow motion in midair using a punchy shotgun, and then switching to double SMGs to cancel the shotgun’s reload to kill another enemy with a headshot before wallrunning across another wall will never not make me feel euphoricBanger soundtrack, great aesthetic too with its massive skyscrapers, dingy alleyways and neon lights in contrast to the bleak (brown) cityscape.   Your main path is marked by said neon lights without being *too* obvious and out of place.  It’s also useful to actually listen to the dialogue to know your next objective since there’s no waypoints or minimap.  Levels also don’t overstay their welcome.  I don’t have a clue what’s going on in the story as I’m not paying attention to anything that’s not pointing me to my objective but you’re here for the gameplay really.  Fun timeThough, one negative I can point out is that some areas aren’t built for a lot of wallrunning and parkour, it’s a little annoying but not too frequent and the further in I get it’s clear the levels are including more parkour.  So stick with it.Oh and as others have pointed out, definitely a ghost in the shell influence

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is an absolute triumph in the world of cyberpunk gaming, offering an immersive and thrilling experience that captivates from start to finish. From its meticulously crafted dystopian landscapes to its engaging narrative and gameplay mechanics, Sprawl stands out as a shining example of what a modern cyberpunk title should be.One of the game's standout features is its rich and detailed world-building. The sprawling cityscape, teeming with neon lights, towering skyscrapers, and gritty back alleys, creates a visually stunning backdrop that truly captures the essence of cyberpunk aesthetics. The attention to detail extends to every corner of the game, making exploration a delight as players uncover hidden secrets and stories within the urban sprawl.The narrative is a compelling blend of intrigue, conspiracy, and moral ambiguity, reminiscent of classic cyberpunk literature. The well-developed characters, each with their own motivations and backstories, add depth to the overarching plot. Choices matter in Sprawl, and the branching storylines ensure a high level of replayability, keeping players engaged and invested in the consequences of their decisions.The gameplay mechanics are seamless and intuitive, striking a perfect balance between action and strategy. Whether engaging in intense gunfights, hacking into corporate systems, or navigating the social intricacies of the city's underworld, Sprawl offers a variety of gameplay options that cater to different playstyles. The fluid controls and responsive interface contribute to a satisfying and immersive gaming experience.The soundtrack deserves special mention, as it complements the cyberpunk atmosphere flawlessly. The pulsating beats and electronic melodies enhance the mood, pulling players deeper into the immersive world of Sprawl.Multiplayer functionality adds another layer of enjoyment, allowing players to collaborate or compete in this cyberpunk universe. The cooperative and competitive modes are well-designed, providing hours of entertainment for those looking to share their Sprawl experience with friends.In conclusion, Sprawl is a masterclass in cyberpunk gaming, delivering on its promises of an engaging narrative, stunning visuals, and dynamic gameplay. For fans of the genre and newcomers alike, Sprawl is a must-play title that sets a new standard for excellence in the world of video games.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I got Sprawl through the humble bundle, and I kinda fell in love with the game. Coming from games like Titanfall 2 and Ultrakill I really like the movement, it basically never feels like you can't go where you want to because of a lack of mechanics (tumbling off a building because I can't count my jumps is not the game's fault :P). The environments of each level are unique but fit together too, actually making you feel like you are progressing through different areas of the same location. Piecing together bits of the story and things happening around me through QR codes has been very fun, every time I see a QR code laying on the ground somewhere I immediately get excited for it, which has also made me check behind every pile of boxes and in every dimly lit corner for them.Also the gunfights are so satisfying, the adrenaline mechanic makes this game shine even more than it already does, it makes you feel so cool so often without making the game feel too easy or feel like enemies are pushovers.I have only completed the first chapter at the time of writing, and absolutely love this game :)

_childDocuments_.review: A shooter worthy of experiencing - for those who crave feeling of speed & power. Level design does not hamper this experience, it empowers it. Weapons and weakpoint system work great in tandem. No issues with perofmance.And the music, for goodness sake, what an absolute BLAST - it just fits so well with the action, theme and the world-building.Thank you Sprawl creators - one could only wish for longer experience, but accounting for all constraints of indie creators - I get it, you've still managed to give me some hours of amazing content.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This felt like playing a mashup of many of my favourite and most nostalgic games. The level design feels a little like old school Doom. Weapons and kill mechanics feel a little more like modern Doom. Movement (wall running) feels second nature coming from Titanfall. And a bit of the bullet-time mechanic from various other games.Playing through the campaign took me a little over 3 hours total, but it felt like a good length. Progression was at a good pace and nothing felt like it got stale.The AI is basic, all enemies are only ever in attack mode and way-pointed to move toward you. They don't really strafe, dodge, hide, or coordinate. On one had it gives the game more of an old-school shooter feel but causes the game to lack some dynamism.There were also several times that I wasn't sure what to do as I missed the speech that goes with the game, or, just couldn't figure out where to go without having to wander around to find out.Beyond those minor criticism, the game is solid chunk of high movement FPS fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay- 9/10 great fps mechanics and weapon combos with a good enemy design that have weak points to hit and a variety of weapons. Slow motion feature is very cool and meshes with the gameplay quite well. The difficulty is finely tuned with how stong you get and there is never a dull moment. The movement options and gunplay are some of the best ive seen, your running on walls, jumping, sliding and using every weapon at your disposal while slowing time and regaining adrenaline (slow time juice) as you fight your way through.  Audio- 12/10 the music is badass and very well done, i seriously cant praise the music enough. sound design is also very good.story- 7/10 its not really what you are there for but it does the job and keeps the train moving. visuals- 8/10 very good, enemy designs are well done, environments are believable and hand crafted.overall- 9/10  the gameplay and audio nearly knock this one out of the park!!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great. It gets super fluid and fun when you get the movement tech working with the combat! You can for example launch yourself in the air while jumping with the kickback from the shotgun. Get swarmed by enemies? Slide-jump on to a wall, jump off and then gib one of them with the shotgun while flinging yourself further away with the kick-back. Then switch to the pistol and score a headshot before you've even landed.  AI is kinda dumb and the enemies will conga line behind you but that might be a feature. The voice acting is weirdly good but the story is minimal, but that's about perfect for this style of shooter. Got a lot of Equilibrium vibes but maybe it's just because there's a character called Father. Music needs a special mention because it's amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy recommendation. The atmosphere, great level design and story kept me thinking about it throughout the day, which is the highest praise you can give a game. It is worth whatever price you're likely to pay for it.While the story is probably pretty standard for the cyberpunk genre, the sparse amount of information and the way you have to piece it together based on the notepads found in game makes it intriguing. The combat is fun and made interesting mainly through the ever changing environments and the movement system which easy to get into and stays intuitive all throughout. One issue I could point out is that the enemy AI is not exactly challenging. The music is another standout though.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish the game was longer, and I wish the movement was a bit more polished. It feels kinda off when you're running on walls and most of the time you're wallrunning off the top of the wall. _childDocuments_.review: This game is what it is, a fast-paced modern shooter, forged the way of the old school. It looks and feels like what it was meant for: relaxing, having a good time, and doing flashy speedruns for your lame-ass Twitch / TikTok streams that no one sees.Among the things that I loved about this game, is that it gives you the option to customize the difficulty at which you want to play it, whether you want to play it as a casual or hardcore gamer, this simple detail says it all, as it isn't looking to be as ambitious as the rest of modern shooters, but rather a fun and striking experience that only an indie game like this can provide.So my final veredict it's: don't get carried away by any negative reviews and give this game a chance, because it is really worth playing, from the amazing graphic aesthetic that it carries, to the feeling that gives to master it's frantic gameplay. This ♥♥♥♥ right here was made to make you feel like a total badass that knows what's doing.

_childDocuments_.review: You play as  a dual-wielding wall-running slo-mo headshot-sniping cyber ninja running through the dystopian future. Art and music(especially music) is amazing,  the arsenal is classic (just listen for the grenade bounce sound). Overall the game pays tributes to lots of nice things which formed the vision of the future past (Blade Runner, Ghost in the Shell, etc.) However - there is not much variation to the gameplay loop, while it feels awesome - it doesn't last too long. The game seemingly understands that and is made short. While it gently inroduces new kinds of enemies and arsenal to the player - it moves to a classic old-school shooter - moving to heavy weapons  and heavier opponents - there is no wallrunning with a heavy chaingun. Level design looks nice, but at its core it's mostly a linear sequence of corridors and arenas (with occassional detour for switches/keycards). AI was supposed to be dumb, but it exceeds these expectations by beng stuck in level geometry. Sometimes the scripts doesn't work as expected (like a locked arena with nothing to kill).Some ideas (like the cables showing the link between switch and a door) are  good, . The game is a definitely a worthwhile experience.P.S. With the addition of codex - QR codes became accessible, gotta read them all :)

_childDocuments_.review: Throw doom and ghost in the shell into a blender with music that's similar to nier and you have Sprawl it's fast paced and unforgiving with alot of platforming.My one real complaint I could lay against it is the lack of an in game map,the levels can be pretty labyrinthine at times which can lead to frustration if you get lost,besides that it's decent for the price you're paying for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you love Doom and Ghostrunner?! This game is like the both got a baby. It is extreme fast paced with great shooting and Gameplay that makes you feel like a freakin shotgun cyber Ninja. All weapons have their usage and strenght and weaknesses and all of them are useful till the end. They feel great and powerful but of course the shotgun is the ♥♥♥♥. ("This once was your favorite, wasn't it :D)I also like the enemy design and the overall art design of the game. Being an indie title the game runs even on older systems on high frame rates and is only a few GB big (something about 3 to 4GB I guess) The story is fun to play and the voice acting is good although there is pretty much only one voice actor but his voice is badass. The whole sound design is wonderful and especially the weapons sound great.But the real star when it comes to audio is the Score. The Soundtrack is just freakin awesome.The only few negative things that I can say is that the parcour sometimes feels a bit weird. Soemtimes I can run on the walls forever and sometimes I am just falling off pretty fast. But that could be just me not really understanding the movement system yet after my first playthrough.And the collectibles being just QR codes that you cannot read ingame which sucks imo (but I just heard that the devs are planning ro change that) So for me it is pretty much the perfect Indie Boomer Shooter title and for this price it is a nobrainer imo.It is incedible that the game is only made by a team of 2 devs and one of them even used to be a DJ and made this awesome Soundtrack, too.I can highly recommend this game, imo it is a gem. A small little master piece that needs more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 Good game. The slow mo shooting hits one of my soft spots, the movement feels pretty good too. Loved the art style, the setting, the music is great too.The guns have some issues, like there is this weird delay with every gun before being able to shoot it, its noticeable but not that big of a deal without slow mo, but when its combined with it it feels like I am constantly just waiting to be able to shoot. Also the balancing of the guns are not that great, the SMG falls off completely towards the end, the rail gun is just way too slow in a fast game like this, the rocket launcher is the weirdest design, its cool that it shoots like 5 rockets but its so inaccurate you need to be up close to the point where you kill yourself with it.At first the game was like 80% combat and 20% platforming which is a good gameplay balance, however I still hated most of the longer platforming sections. Especally the one right before the end of the game where it turns into 80% platforming and 20% combat, that section was just painfull, most of the time I couldn't even see where to go next, every jump looked like it was too far away, and if I made a mistake I had to do the whole thing again, it pissed me off so much I almost stopped playing the game. _childDocuments_.review: It's a great movement shooter with beautiful art and lots of fun weapons. I'd probably still buy a DLC/sequel that's just a level pack--I really love this game--but the enemy variety and simple behavior is its weakest aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a very cool movement based shooter that just feels so smooth and responsive. The weapons are all punchy and a pleasure to use, plus there's games bullet time feature which is very well implemented and you will be using it quite a bit (Who doesn't love a good bit of bullet time!?). _childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥ this game is good man. A tight 5 (hours) of gore, guns, and these gorilla robot guys that really had me on the edge of my seat until I remembered it's a game about doing cool wall-runs.More guns than I could comfortably reach the numbers for, more weapon combos than I could realistically remember to use, and more guys to use them on than should be reasonably expected from an indie game.Seriously! every time I thought I'd seen all the enemy types they'd throw another one in just for fun, followed shortly after by a shiny new gun to kill it with.The movement is fun and fluid, if occasionally a little frustrating - but that may simply be coming from my preexisting over-familiarity with the Titanfall 2 style of wall running.Perhaps the one mechanic that I felt was a little under utilised is the bullet-time adrenaline slow-mo that's bound oh so zealously to right-click. Maybe it's just because I'm rather (and I admit this in shame, rather than to prate) good at pointing the cursor at things, but I sorta kept forgetting it was there. Every now and then I would get into the groove of slow-motion exploding the enemy's jump packs, or landing several head-shots in quick succession - but I do feel as though there could have been more incentive to use the adrenaline.It's certainly a tricky situation to be in - balancing a "rule-of-cool" type mechanic. I wouldn't want to be forced to use it, but I do kinda lament that I didn't use it as much as I could have.When it comes down to it I'm probably just sad that my gameplay doesn't look as cool as they stuff they pull off in the launch trailer - which is what convinced me to pick up the game in the first place.If you're on the fence about SPRAWL I'd recommend giving it a watch:You won't be doing all that fancy shotgun-jump, slow-mo-head-shot, shoot-a-grenade-out-of-the-air stuff the second you pick it up - but it sure as ♥♥♥♥ feels like it.And if you're like me, you'll be doing your damnedest to look half as cool on the second play-through.

_childDocuments_.review: Super addicting Indie retro FPS inspired by Quake, Ultrakill, Ghost in the Shell, Bladerunner, and most importantly, Titanfall, with its movement system. Enhancing the movement and combat is adrenaline, which is pretty much just Max Payne's bullet-time. The weapon selection is great and the pace of when you unlock them is done well.
