_childDocuments_.review: I held off on Sprawl for quite a while due to its reviews, but I'm glad to have finally played it. It's a fast-paced and movement-focused boomer shooter with no reloading (a huge plus) and the best bullet time mechanic I've seen implemented into an FPS, where it effectively serves as your aiming system (without the need for using sights or something stupid like that). Enemy and weapon variety is good, and there isn't too much bulletsponging. Weakpoint kills or melee finishes restore HP, bullet time, and ammo; this is the perfect incentive to press forward into bloodshed, and reflects great fundamental design. But the game is really at its best when the focus is on the pistols or shotgun and landing headshots. It gets worse as it gets more complicated. The biggest problem is level design. None of the environments feel like real places, which is fine, but there's also no navigational assistance except for occasional enigmatic instructions from CortanaMan. Sometimes you'll accomplish an objective, he'll say, "Good work!" and you will subsequently have no clue whatsoever where to go next--even if you do understand, broadly, what your overarching objective is. Doors that look like they shouldn't open are actually where you need to go, while doors that look like they should need a nearby console to activate, and doors that need a nearby console sometimes don't look like doors at all. I often found myself getting lost, although never for long, and the parkour sections in Act 3 overstay their welcome. There are plenty of games on the market with worse level design than Sprawl, but also quite a lot that do it better. Weapon balance is suspect. The shotgun is the best gun for anything within a thousand yards and the railgun and rocket launcher feel weak in comparison. Pistols are fantastic at the beginning but nigh unusable at the end. The SMGs go through ammo so quickly so as to be almost pointless. The GL isn't really worth the time it takes to equip. But they are each fun to use in their own right, and the final few missions are more generous with exotic ammo placement, which makes the rocket launcher especially far more competitive. I played on the middle difficulty. As you would hope in a movement shooter, projectiles are everywhere, but are generally easy to avoid so long as you stay moving. Stop moving, die almost instantly. As with the level design, I found this to fall apart in the third act, where I started dying occasionally--although not frequently--in a single hit, without any idea of what killed me. There's also a huge amount of health and ammo placed around every map that I found myself almost never picking up, because I was always full anyway! (This makes navigating the levels even harder; normally, in a Doom clone, you've been to any area with the consumables gone. Here, there are always consumables on the ground, which means it often looks like you haven't explored what you're seeing.) It's still a game I would recommend overall. Compared with Trepang2, a very different FPS that feels similar due to bullet time + jumping around a lot, it's miles ahead in gameplay design and way more fun. Some others might complain that 4 hours is too short, but it felt about right to me, and maybe even a tad too long.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game along with all the achievements in under 6 hours. This is a short, very unique FPS that everyone should at least try. The movement is addicting once you master some of its' hidden tricks. The level design is probably the only weakness I can really think of in this game, as it falters in some levels due to it being too needlessly complicated and drawn out at times, and I also got soft-locked on the second to last level and had to retry the checkpoint. But these are just minor nitpicks and complaints that are outweighed by the overall greatness of this game. You'll get your moneys worth it, and you even have a Horde Mode! :)I wish we also had an enemy that actually matched the player's abilities and movement, sort of like the Marauder in DOOM Eternal.Buy this, it's a quality product, and while it is already pretty polished, it just gets better with every update(as I've been following this project ever since the trailer in August).

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to all things cyberpunk, Sprawl beautifully mixes excellent sound design and art direction with accessible movement shooter mechanics and no-nonsense boomer shooter violence. While it's not the most content heavy game, it provides an impeccable experience that makes you feel cool as hell.Any review that doesn't mention's Sprawl's music is doing it a disservice. Its combination of atmospheric choral chanting and synth conveys the inhuman scale of its environment, eventually giving way to thumping industrial drum and bass to score your fast-paced violence. The music alone conjures countless memories of 80s/90s cyberpunk anime favorites like Ghost in the Shell and Akira. While PS1-era graphics aren't always my favorite, it's the perfect choice for this game's clear influences. It's grimy cyberpunk city oozes with character that would almost feel wrong in a higher fidelity. The narrative of Sprawl is largely left to the player to engage with as much or as little as desired, following the form of Doom 2016, but has several layers that can be peeled back with some additional depth and digging. Last but not least, the movement in this game feels just stellar. Simple rules and guidelines are laid out for wallrunning and jumping at the outset and with bullet time as a core mechanic, when the movement in this game clicks you will begin pulling off some of the coolest clip-able moments imaginable with ease that makes you feel like a god.

I bought this at 12 AM expecting to sleep in the next 30 minutes after I got bored, ended up staying up the whole night to beat the entire game plus all of the extra modes. Probably a "hit or miss" game for most, but if it hits, it HITS. Solid 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:For starters you have an adrenaline bar you use up for bullet time, trust me bullet time is essential, this isn't your usual retro shooter. The game also has Titanfall reminiscent movement, sliding and wall running. Now onto how you'll need to play the game, the most important thing is that while you're in bullet time enemy weakspots are highlighted, such as heads or explosive components they're carrying. THERE IS NO RELOADING so ALWAYS try to go for weakspots, it's faster and may result in multi-kills. Killing enemies always drops small health items and adrenaline to refill, so getting constant kills in quick succession will keep you alive.Weapons:The game has 7 weapons, although 2 of them do lose usefulness later through the game as stronger enemies become more common. THE SMGS CANNOT HEADSHOT. The SMGs are only for damaging enemies quick enough to make them vulnerable for melees, which grants extra drops. The rest of the weapons are great to use but personally the Chaingun's wind up and fire rate kill the rest of the game's momentum, shame since it becomes such a reliable source of damage otherwise. The shotgun in this game is amazing, the sounds are great and can instakill (via headshot) most of the basic grunt enemies, but the damage is still very reliable even late game, being able to take down the MECH enemies. You can also rocket jump with the shotgun.Music:The music mainly consists of breakcore with a harmonic choir backing the tracks and it's really a sensation to play with that music in the back. However, the music does vary to fit the tone of the levels and fights. I even fell asleep to the OST on youtube one night.Story:There is plenty enough of a story being told to you through your guiding voice as well as loading screen descriptions for levels, and cutscenes with voice acting, the protagonist is silent though, only making noise for jumping and pain. there are also QR codes you can find hidden around levels for what I assume is extra worldbuilding.Overall,This game is a HARD recommend, I INSIST you play it.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL wears its cyberpunk influences on its sleeve. Its name already being a reference to The Sprawl in William Gibson's Neuromancer, and its akimbo pistols those of Deckard's from Blade Runner. SPRAWL is not a mere collection of nods to popular culture tho, it has a cool style of its own and a believably dystopian cyberpunk world.This was my first so called modern "movement shooter" and I liked it a lot. Gameplaywise SPRAWL takes influences from classic games such as the Quake series, Half-Life 2, modern ones like Titanfall, and I imagine the developers having played the brilliant Source Engine powered cyberpunk game G STRING.The first part of the game was a definite highlight for me. The main character Seven gains more weapons and faces tougher enemies as the game progresses which keeps the gameplay interesting, but for me the levels and vibes remain best in the beginning of the game.If you're hankering for some cyberpunkering, I warmly recommend SPRAWL!

_childDocuments_.review: Bit of a mixed impression on this one! For the most part I think I'm leaning towards positive on the experience, but it definitely has some flaws that I think would dissuade the hardcore FPS crowd, while the more casual audience would enjoy the general adventure.PROS*Pretty cool cyberpunk world with some gorgeous vistas*Great music (very Ghost in the Shell chanting style)*Fun Titanfall/Ghostrunner-esque movement: lots of platforming and I love dodging enemy fire by wall-running and stylishly flipping around like a ninja*Cool slow-mo powers and lots of fun guns*Fun Doom Eternal-esque feedback loop: shoot enemy weakpoints highlighted with slow-mo or execute them with melee to get more slow-mo/health/ammo, repeat step 1CONS*Short (4 hrs)*Story is pretty basic and had no big twist or impact, just bare minimum revenge prompt to keep us going*World is a bit too dark and confusing at times where it's difficult to find way forward or spot enemies*Enemies are kind of boring, and their AI is easily exploitable where you can run circles around them*Slow-mo feels unnecessary: enemies already shoot slow projectiles so the game might've actually been better without it and played in real time? Or enemies should be deadlier with faster bullets to necessitate its use*Only really felt challenged around the last few levels where they throw a bunch at you, but its quantity over qualityBasically, a very flashy and fun game, but a bit flawed, not as memorable as I'd like, and kind of falls apart on closer examination for its combat design. But it's short, so like me, you might just beat it before you even notice its flaws and just think of it as fun cyberpunk ninja action overall.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine GITS but with DOOM style FPS, this is what you'll getSoundtrack is spot on with the environment, I like how it changes depending on the situationThe added verticality makes the game more fun since it adds another way to approach and react to battleAdrenaline (Slow-mo) system isn't really mandatory for survival if you are quick & accurate enough with your aim, and precise with your movementI wish there is a rouge-like arena mode with randomized weapons and enemies (and maybe some environmental hazard for each round?) so people can get creative and always engaged with the game even after completing story mode
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing yet short BOOMER SHOOTER featuring:- Parkour movements similar to GHOSTRUNNER, allowing wall jumps and slide jumps.- Active resource management like DOOM ETERNAL: killing enemies by targeting weak points or with the sword rewards you with health, ammo, and adrenaline.- A time-slowing ability (utilizing adrenaline) like FEAR.- Gorgeous music.I appreciate the use of handguns in later levels, a rarity in most FPS games where they become obsolete after obtaining better weapons. Here, survival still depends on utilizing handguns to gather resources. Additionally, the game has two extra game modes: time trial and horde mode with customizable difficulty.However, I have two complaints:1) A strange bug prevents mouse usage in the menu when the Steam overlay is used once.2) I have never used the sword after E1M1 in my playthrough. In my opinion, killing with the sword should also give armor along with the other rewards; otherwise, it serves the same purpose as the slow-time ability.If this represents the current standard for boomer shooters, I'm eagerly anticipating what the future holds. I am extremely happy and satisfied with the quality of this game!!

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played through Episode One. However, I already feel like I've got my money's worth and more.Gameplay-wise, it has aspects of F.E.A.R./Trepang2 meets Titanfall meets Quake 2. Atmosphere-wise, lots of cyberpunk and anime references as far as I can see e.g., Ghost in the Shell and Bladerunner.Fast-paced gameplay thanks to the free-running movement, but bullet time gives to the opportunity to plan out some nice movement tech or pinpoint head shots. _childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a fun, fast paced FPS game with platforming that is perhaps just a bit short, as it took me about 4 hours to beat. I'd probably recommend playing the game with slightly increased enemy damage in the difficulty settings as it makes the enemies more deadly without making them bullet spongy, aside from that it's not really a hard game as the developers are quite forgiving with the platforming and *very* generous with health and ammo pickups, and their placement of checkpoints is pretty much spot on for where you'd need one. Most of my deaths in the game were from blowing myself up with the explosive weapons lmao.The on demand bullet time with the adrenaline gauge mechanic is pretty fun to use in conjunction with the constant weapon switching I found myself doing during combat, as it allows for some ridiculous damage to be dealt. Aside from the first half of the game being set in a very brown environment, the game is surprisingly pretty, with some very nice scenery and a solid aesthetic. The OST also matches the game very well and helps further the aesthetic vision going on.The game runs really well at maximum graphics settings sitting around 160~ fps at a resolution of 1440p on a GTX 1080Ti.My only real complaints with the game are the un-skippable cutscenes, your radio companion near constantly talking to you, and the weirdly high number of slow moving elevators, but other than that it's a pretty good game, well worth picking up if it sounds like something you'd enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is one of the best games I've played this year, which is saying something next to games like RE4 Remake, AC6 Fires of Rubicon,  FF16, and Alan Wake II.The combat is engaging, high octane, fuel injected carnage and mayhem. The controls may seem odd at first, but they are super intuitive and feel natural as you're playing. The main actions are mapped to the shoulder buttons if you're using a controller like I did, and it's great because you never have to take your thumb off the right analog stick. You never have to sacrifice camera movement in order to jump or shoot. And don't even worry about reloading. Just aim, shoot, rinse, and repeat.It's an amalgamation of some of the best games ever made. It has wall running and versatile movement from Titanfall, powerful weapons that feel good to shoot like Doom, and a slow down mechanic that guarantees enemies won't see what hit them like Max Payne. It's such a beautiful marriage of great mechanics.The soundtrack is great. It's a soundtrack that Mick Gordon would admire and be proud of. It's so fitting and really gets your blood going for intense firefights.I can't praise the environmental design enough. The aesthetic is exactly what I want from a game of this nature. My favorite area was working my way through the streets of a dystopian city up to the rooftops. Such great tone and atmosphere. Reminded me of pictures of Kowloon or even the rooftops of Shanghai and Hong Kong. I can't recommend this game enough. If you love high speed shooters that challenge you and make you feel good while doing it, please, treat yourself to Sprawl. Then buy it three more times and gift it your friends. They'll thank you for it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL feels great to play. Sliding around and jumping into walls, then running on and jumping off of those walls to outmaneuver enemies and using the adrenaline (slow-motion) mechanic to get a perfect shot on an enemy or group of enemies feels incredibly satisfying, especially when paired with the breakneck soundtrack. The game makes you feel like a badass all throughout its relatively short campaign.The only time this game feels bad is when you're stuck in a room looking for the way out. It doesn't actually take long to figure out where you're going if you're lost, but in a high-paced shooter like this 30 seconds of downtime with no enemies to shoot or platforming feels a lot longer than that. These moments happen often enough that it's worth mentioning.Despite lacking obvious routes forward sometimes, I wouldn't let that be a deterrent. The level design is great for the fluid movement and gunplay most of the time. Aside from a few odd hallways or empty spaces, there's tons of walls, cargo containers, and platforms to use to your advantage to evade enemies or isolate them for easier kills. Most enemies can be killed quickly with the right weapons and SPRAWL gives you those weapons right when you need them.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little movement shooter, the wallrunning feels reminiscent of Titanfall. Excellent soundtrack, and the difficulty is fully customizable too. If I had to complain about something, it's that death can come quickly in the later levels, especially if you backpedal into a group of enemies and get deleted by a shotgunner. Mostly though, I just wish there was more game (hopefully there will be additional episodes at some point).
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: An alright game.I especially liked the part where the AI introduces himself with "My name is not important. What is important is what we are going to do... I just hate this world. And the human worms feasting on its carcass. My whole existence is just cold, bitter hatred. And I always wanted to see humans die violently. This is the time of vengeance and no life is worth saving. And we will put in the grave as many as possible. It's time for us to kill. And it's time for me to die."Other than the overly edgy dialogue the game-play is fairly good other than the game allows you to fire instantly when the game switches from an empty weapon to an explosive weapon causing more than 1 unintentional suicide. and many enemies having way too much hp causing many humanoid being able to shrug off point blank shotgun blasts to the skull. and the sword not taking priority over reloads causing a few brief stare-fests with stunned enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A short (~6 hours for me) game that masterfully combines the high speed movement of Titanfall, a retro horde-shooter style of Doom, and if that wasn't enough a bullet time mechanic too. The game controls very well and the combat is very satisfying and fluid. The larger, less linear maps are sometimes confusing to navigate that being my only sizeable gripe. this game feels like a high speed love letter to the classic shooters such as Doom and Quake, definitely worth picking up when on sale. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very maybe recommendation, while I enjoyed the game for what it is, i have reasons to like it that I can't really explain, it just had a particular feeling to it that I enjoyed. The weapons are sort of hit or miss, while some feel great to shoot like the shotgun, revolvers (albeit very outpaced by literally every other gun) and the smgs, the grenade launcher felt sort of weak taking three grenades to take down one shotgun boy, and I think I shot the railgun twice and never again. Level design can be a little confusing and unclear of what you have to do and where to go, the spire being the biggest example especially at the start, i was just flipping levers and trial-and-error-ing my way up. Enemies being spongy is something that can be annoying too but other people expressed that better than I can. Solid game with a few jagged edges.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl falls short compared to most popular movement shooters. However, the quality of the game is good considering the size of the team. The game drags moderately, but I still had a good time. The mechanics allow you to play in a cool way, but do not demand it. Therefore your gameplay can be very stale and boring unless you self-enforce schwag. It's a 5.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game both in game design and art style. It's relatively brief, but definitely a short game worth playing twice rather than a drawn out slog barely worth playing once.The QR codes hidden throughout the levels are cute, but I would definitely appreciate an in-game log book so I can collect the lore without having to stop every few minutes to read something on my phone.Edit: They added the lore codex :)
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Hell yes so far! Many modern games forget that games should be fun. And this one really is fun to play! And it has everything. Ghost In The Shell (1995) aesthetics and music. F.E.A.R. like bullet time. And you can run on walls! Tons of enemies to kill using all classic weapons like pistols, SMGs, miniguns, RAILGUNS, grenade launchers... and maybe more. You can even decapitate some poor sobs. And it's all fast paced, everything explodes, bleeds and dies. No moral dilemmas, just lots of running and gunning. Graphics is nice. It has this retro vibe, because textures are low resolution and not filtered at all, so everything is pixelated. But all the rest is high end, shadows, shaders, ambient occlusion, screen space reflections, motion blur its all there. The game support DLSS and ultrawide screens. Performance is great too, RTX3070, 3440x1400 and I got constant 120FPS.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Very rarely rate games, I'm actually enjoying this game more that Ghostrunner. This is Ghostrunner with guns - Just what I wanted. Really brilliant game so far, combat is extremely satisfying, guns are extremely chonky/well designed/enemy types are challenging in numbers but feels good to dispatch them en-masse. This game definitely rewards skill and planning and a good aim. I'm really enjoying this game and I hardly ever rate shooters. Pick it up full price its a no brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: The short: Blast through your enemies, cycle your shotgun for quicker firing and strafe shoot your way to victory after disabling head bob. Finish within 3~4hrs for skilled shooters. You play for the action, gunplay, wall hopping, bullet time and music. Don't expect the story to swoon you.SPRAWL is a very quick burn, but a fun one; if you're skilled at boomer shooters you'll blow through the base game easily. If you like strafe shooting, you can disable the head and weapon bob to properly replicate strafe shooting and not have your aim thrown off, which is a big plus. I appreciate the ability to choose between stylization and function. No major comment on the bullet time mechanic, I played without using it minus a few moments to find weakspots on bosses. Movement is very fluid, finite controls on wall stickiness appreciated, you'll enjoy wall bouncing if you're skilled with it.Soundtrack slaps. Lore is interesting but story presentation is mid and discount adam smasher is even more of a pushover than the CP2077 one (not a spoiler, you see him right in the game intro). Levels are very quake reminiscent, sadly degrade in overall build quality past first chapter, seems to have more quality in first portions than later ones. Would love to see follow up. I get the style choice of QR codes for lore bits but as a flip phone user that irks me and it won't last long run for the game's longevity years down the line, highly recommend they put that ♥♥♥♥ into the game as base.Recommendation: Pick it up on the sale like it's on right now of writing for Autumn sale. If you're one of those "hour to pay" people yeah you probably won't find enough content to last it if you're good at this, but I'd say it's personally worth it. If nothing else, buy the soundtrack if you love chanting and beats to blast things to death with.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Sound design is excellent, every gun feels good (especially the shotgun) and has some purpose to it besides sounding good to shoot. Movement is a little different than other games I am used to but once you get accustomed to it the game's overall flow is almost relaxing to engage in. The OST is top notch and memorable and it really pumped me up in every combat encounter. Really think the cyberpunk with an overlay of religious chanting really lends itself to setting the atmosphere of the game.The only gripe I would probably voice is the AI feels a little dim and exploitable at times but the game tends to make up for it by setting the combat encounters to overwhelm you with force which still gives you that feeling of overcoming adversity.Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing I've only beaten the first chapter(5 levels) and this game is so, unbelievably bold. Not many devs would be able to make eye contact as they served up a remix of things they love so much. There's the undeniable presence of GITS in it's OST. The gameplay is a blend of F.E.A.R, Doom Eternal, and Ghostrunner with a twist of Half-Life 2. A dynamic electronic album of violence.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl knows exactly how long it needs to tell its story and let you hone it's mechanics. It know's exactly what to throw at you and when to throw more. It pushes you to stay on your toes and change up your play-style; there isn't a one fix for everything. It's bullet time mechanic is some of the best I've seen in an FPS adding an extra layer of complexity rather than simplifying it. You will use everything at your disposal in order to climb the spire. You must get there at any cost. Fight for freedom.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it a lot. It never really reaches the highs I expected from the first hour or so of gameplay, but it was fun nonetheless.The absolute best part of this game is its atmosphere and setting. The environment, especially those set around residential areas are a pleasure to behold, and they really make me wish this was a different game. One that would allow me to really explore this city and its story in a different way. The soundtrack goes really well with the environment. Made me want to go see 'Ghost in the Shell' again. The story is about what you'd expect for the setting.There are some data-pads all around that can be read by scanning a QR code. While the idea piqued my attention at first, the novelty wears off quickly, since they're just static text notes, and the content of these made me give up on reading them after finding the fifth or so.The gameplay is solid, but it becomes less and less appealing over the course of the 4-5 hour campaign.Towards the end, the only way they managed to make the combat more engaging was by throwing spongy enemies and hundreds of them in smaller areas.Regardless, Sprawl is clearly a labor of love, and I really makes me want to check out what they get to work on next.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A fun movement + bullet time heavy boomer-ish shooter featuring some funky drum and bass tunes and Ghost in the Shell visuals.  Most of the game revolves around you wall running, headshotting and weapon switching to avoid reload animations. I could see why some find this repetitive, but I found it was a good length before I got bored of it. The plot is mostly found in QR code collectibles that are fun to scan the first time but sort of gets old quick. There are times the level design works against the game, in that the samey corridors can make you get a little lost, and I personally hated the last level, but I would overall recommend this to anyone looking for a short and sweet, very hectic game.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Very middle of the road game. The aesthetic is great, but the gameplay is kind of boring. There's some interesting movement mechanics but the level design isn't conducive to using them and the AI is too stupid to require good movement. The price is pretty fair though. Try to pick it up for 10 or less if you like indie boomershooters or FEAR and enjoy GitS aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Great soundtrack and atmosphere with some pretty fun gameplay. My main two points of complaint would be:1. The ammo economy seems pretty limited for the amount of enemies as well as their general sponginess. It wasn't a huge issue, but there were a few moments that I felt suffered for it.2. The QR code datapads. It's a neat concept, but it really hurts the pacing of the game to have to stop, pull out my phone, load up a QR code reader, scan it (50% chance it actually even works on my phone), and then read it. An in-game datapad option would be great.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing movement, amazing bullet time with weakness highlights, just generally an amazing experience. The story isn't exactly special, but it's still very good. Just in general an amazing game. Had no bugs, no crashes, no nothing and just a smooth ~6 hour experience. Will probably play it again when I want an amazing movement-shooter.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Currently in the middle of playing through Episode 2 but I gotta say this a really fun game. Soundtrack is amazing to listen to as you blast through Junta Soldiers with shotguns, duel-wield revolvers, chainguns, grenade launchers, and railguns. I also love the movement and the combat as they sync together really well to create this chaos of death and fun. One thing I think should change is how the story is told because the main gimmick here is QR Codes. Yes, if you want to learn more about whats going on you have to stop the game, pull out your phone, and scan the code which directs you to a website with said lore. It's cool to do once or twice but its a hassle after the novelty wears off. Should have just been logs you could read or better yet see in-game. But besides that its a really fun Titanfall-Quake combination.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I dont usually make reviews, but I usually also dont buy indie games that are less than 10 hours long this flippantly, I saw one review (that one dragon guy, forgot the name) and something about its presentation captivated me like few games do, the gameplay looked nice but it was every aspect of the presentation that made me pull the trigger on it.So lets instead start with the game itself: its good, maybe not great, but good, coming from titanfall 2 (which I love) and Doom Eternal (which I... dont love) this game tries to find a middle ground between the more character action side of boomer shooters with their crazy weapon swapping and resource regen on kills (headshots and other weakpoints being the killshot in this case) and movement shooters, from TF|2's wall running and slide hopping (simplified here to be less animation heavy and floatier, but also less abusable to gain height) and the slowmo jumps of Max Payne and FEAR, the end result is a game that is straight forward but has a relatively high skill ceiling, with clear cut controls and movement tech that is less about obscure mechanics (its pretty much just shotgun jumping) and more about mastery of the basic controls, which I appreciate.The enemy variety is pretty good, for its short length it tries to have every single enemy type have at least one variant, barring a handful, so the only criticism i would levy is that episode 2 is obsessed with putting tanky enemies from ep1 as the rank and file, like if Doom 2 replaced all the zombies with chaingunners that had shotguns, and then also had a variant that had even more health on top of that, tho ep 3 seems to weirdly back track on that, going for a larger amount of weaker enemies, which I think is better.As for the story, its good, but beyond the basic plot I feel I dont fully understand it, im pretty sure there is an unsolved ARG here which I cant begin to unravel, relating to the game's QR data pads and the achievement icon for them being a unique QR code.And now back to the presentation, HOLY ♥♥♥♥ its as good as I hoped, all the guns feel satisfying and have distinct, creative designs and sounds, which the enemies share so its helpful in that gameplay way (the grenade launcher using a distorted Quake 1 GL sound was a nice touch) and the enemies all have unique siluettes that, despite reusing animations whenever possible, are not too hard to distinguish, not to mention be memorable.The environmental art and music is the true standout here, varied, awe inspiring and a nice balanced of fitting with the setting and not getting in the way of gameplay, yes, this applies to both enviorment art AND music; weirdly though, it also applies to both of those things that there is a weird lull in variety in episode 2, which is a shame, but like I said before, the quality and variety picks back up in ep 3, even though its shorter than the previous 2 (could have used one more level, possibly with a mid boss IMO).Overall, highly recommend, one of my GOTYs for sure, I dunno if i'd come back to replay it (unless the devs add achievements for the side modes, which i'd gladly come back to) but as a one time experience (plus 2 hours to get all the collectables) it was a fun ride.EDIT: wow they are still updating this game, damn, also, someone please figure out that ARG, im too dumb for it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Simple but solid mechanics, satisfying guns (probaly one of the best videogame shotguns I've ever used), banger soundtrack and great aesthetics in the first episode: Sprawl certainly has a lot going for it, it's just a shame things start to kind of slowly come apart in the second half in a way that feels like the developers either ran out of time, money or energy. The combat encounters are still fun and the arenas well designed with lots of verticality and options for fun movements but it would have been nice to maybe design a couple of new enemies for them that aren't just tankier versions of earlier ones. The biggest downgrade from the first episode is probably the aesthetics of the levels, swapping clicheed but atmospheric neon-lit streets and canals for a progression generic factory halls. And, while, obviously this isn't exactly a story-focussed game in the first place, it would have been nice to at least know who or what the final boss was without (presumably) having to look in the logs scattered around the level, especially considering that the baffling choice was made to not actually have those entries be in the game itself but instead giving you a qr code to scan with your phone. Suffice to say, while I'm willing to do a lot to read a short entry in a diary where a scientist scoffs at the idea that their biomechanical monstrosity research could ever backfire, I'm not willing to leave the game for it. Without the context that might or might not be in those logs, the last chapter has some real "Poochie died on the way to his home planet." energy to it.That all sounds pretty negative but that's partially due to the fact that the game does so much stuff right that what it does wrong become all the more glaring. Overall, I still very much enjoyed my five hours with it and for this pricepoint, I don't think you can go too wrong picking it up if the thought of popping heads while wallrunning appeals to you. Also, pretty impressive that it seems like this was made basically entirely by two people if I interpreted the credits right.PS: Please nerf how much the grenade launcher does to yourself or how big its splash zone is because I'm pretty sure that was my number one cause of death over the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Game knows what it is and is generally good at it. My main issue is with the level design. Some parts could be awkward to navigate, and I found myself getting lost a number of times.The story is forgettable. There is some lore to flesh it out, but the game makes an interesting choice on how to deliver it, and I have mixed feelings about it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: A good retro shooter. The gameplay feels refined, and the pacing is excellent. The level design is good, and the environments are interesting but the visual style leaves something to be desired. While Sprawl clearly goes for a cyberpunk aesthetic, it lacks the color highlights required to make it look interesting, and while the retro pixelated art-style looks good, the brown and grey does not. Ghostrunner, another cyberpunk movement game, has way more color in its levels while looking no less grimy and lived in, a style which it think would have carried over well to Sprawl. Overall, worth playing, but wait for a sale, especially given its short runtime.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: First of all Well done to the very small team that made this game. I enjoyed every minute. Disclaimer: this is not a sprawling constructive review (pun intended) but more of a long comment to express what I enjoyed as was a thoroughly enjoyable experience. TL:DR - Music Slaps, runs like butter, gameplay is fast paced and fun, Cool art style. Short and sweet.  Highly recommend if you like fast pace games, such as DOOM 2016/ETERNAL shadow warrior etc. the game runs smooth with simple mechanics making the game-play very fun with some elements of ghostrunner mixed in especially with dystopian/apocalyptic cyberpunk style setting.Music SLAPS hard, which heightened the experience for me and got me bobbing my head as I amped up the pace wiping out cyborgs and androids, Easily one the best parts of this game, Also really like the aesthetic of this game and definitely another example for the Art style over Graphic fidelity argument. It gives the game an old school feel while also feeling pleasing to the eye and is a great balance, which im sure contributes to the butter smooth performance of this game. No frame drops no crashes as all games should be, However the game is very short, but every game does not need to be 20-60 hours long. The length felt right and fits the Short but Sweet category.  All in all I highly recommend this Indie title and I really look forward to possibly seeing more work from the folks that made this game.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun retro shooter; the aesthetic is solid and the music is very reminiscent of Ghost in the Shell, which I assume is intentional judging by a few points in the game that seem to reference the original film. Combat feels solid too, with the weapons all being quite satisfying to use (especially the shotgun), and the wallrunning mechanic works very well.The negatives are that it's very short, even by boomer shooter standards, and unlike most boomer shooters this one doesn't really offer the challenge or depth to make it worth replaying. Gameplay gets a bit samey very quickly too, but the game isn't really long enough for that to become too much of a problem. Also as nice as the aesthetic is, there's not much variety visually throughout the game. Overall for the price I'd say it's worthit if you're looking for a simple, fun shooter that you can blitz through in a weekend. It has enough going on to be interesting, just don't expect to be coming back to it after beating it like you might with the likes of Dusk, Turbo Overkill, or Hedon. I'll definitely be keeping an eye out for anything else the devs make though, as I think there's a lot of potential here.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game but for some reason I cant seem to tune the right mouse sensitivity for the life of me. Aiming in this game is just ...... weird!! Dont know how else to describe it. I still recommend it though as it is quite enjoyable for a boomer shooter. The soundtrack is amazing. I see some complaints on here about the fire rate/delay of the shotgun, but once you understand it and get used to it, it feels amazing. Switching to another weapon and instantly switching back to the shotgun resets the delay between shots. You're welcome ;)
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I had a fun time with this one and was hooked from the beginning to end. Good shooting, cool setting and a really great wall run mechanic that made the level design a lot more fun to explore. One nitpick I did have which is more so a steam deck related one as I played it all the way on it was that I wished the aim assist was a little bit more effective as it wasn't as reliable and had to awkwardly shoot accurately with the thumbstick in a very fast paced game. None the less, I had a good time with this shooter and glad I gave it a shot
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect example of showing your influences without directly copying said Influences. Everything about this game clicks together effortlessly and makes for a very enjoyable shooter experience. I really have to give credit to the maps as extra care and detail were put in to make sure that the movement mechanics got to shine. The guns are also punchy, feel good to use and are all viable in most circumstances. Easily worth the money and worth the excitement!
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: me go pew pew big gun boom. game funUPDATE: after finishing the story, can definitely recommend to anyone who likes Doom/Quake/Titanfall, or any other fast paced FPS games. There is only one part of the game I thought was lame - when you had to shoot the grenades out of the mechs. They would just never shoot the grenades at me so was just sitting there waiting for like 30 seconds while they slowly meandered around. Once I got a way of dealing with them without needing to do this, game felt way better. Fun game! Check it out! 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL combines multiple shooter sub-genres into a creative and entertaining package. It blends concepts from boomer/retro shooters, movement shooters, and a bullet time shooters. You wall run, slide, slow down time, fight in area combat against a myriad of enemy types all while scooping up health, ammo, and armor pickups. It blends all these concepts to make satisfying and frantic combat wrapped in a cyberpunk package. The level design is good, with a nice balance of jumping puzzles, arena combats, and traversing diverse map layouts. The settings take you to warehouse clubs, sewers and canals, cramped city streets, city rooftops, brutalist building interiors, factories and more. They are a definite strong point for the game, and I loved soaking in the environments. The graphics lean on the retro side but have an adjustable slider if you like your graphics more modern. Weapon selection is satisfying and swapping between them during bullet time and rapid movement felt satisfying and added to the depth of combat. The soundtrack and sfx are excellent. They nail the mood and build on the experience. For 15 bucks you get about 5-6 hours of gameplay. For the price I think it is worth it and I would recommend it for people who appreciate retro shooters inspired by cyberpunk aesthetics.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a great time with SPRAWL. It's very much the sum of its influences, but its influences are all awesome. The crunchy graphics feel very Quake, with Titanfall-inspired movement, and a Doom Eternal resource-loop built around bullet-time and headshots. The grungy cyberpunk city is straight out of Ghost in the Shell. The soundtrack has some songs that reference Kenji Kawaii's OST for that movie, along with plenty of techno bangers. If a blend of all these influences sounds cool, this is that game, go buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is nearly great, but has a list of issues making it 'ok' instead.Somewhere between 7.5 and 8 feels pretty correct, rating wise.The combat and interwoven platforming has shining moments, but a miriad of minor problems hold it back from being the peak retro movement shooter it could be.Let's list things from great to meh.1. The atmosphere and music is GREAT.This game nails an oppressive dystopian atmosphere.It's a blend of Quakes drabness with Bladerunner flair - the music especially underlines this seconed part.The map is a vast complex of city blocks and apartments, military facilities and claustrophic hallways.You fight on rooftops, in appartments, in large open areas and... sewers.2, Platforming is GOOD.While not as fluid an in depth as Mirror's Edge (or Titanfall), there is still some fun parcour to be had.Almost any wall can be wallrun on and jumped of to allow for multiple hops from wall to wall.There is some minor tech, such as slide-jumping to increase your momentum, and shotgun jumping (of which neither is really explained in game).However, there is no vaulting, no sprinting or dashing. The base movement speed is also a bit too slow for a movement shooter - it's more jogging than running. But you can just keep slide-jumping frequently to keep higher momentum; it is much faster if timed correctly. 3. ARESENAL is OK.Slow-mo is cool; but drains the same resource as the highlight mode and it does NOT recharge, but most enemies drop the related resource.The guns feel decent, but each has something that makes it feel slightly off, making the gunplay overall feel held back. Ammo economy is strange - you have low capacity for all guns and gain only little ammo from enemies, but the game constantly flushes you with ammo; meaning you run dry mid combat but gain back max ammo in the same arena after strafing around for a bit.The pacing in which you get weapons is somewhat slow, and by the time you end E2 the game somewhat runs out of goodies to hand out. There is no upgrades to weapons either. No extra abilities, or even simple things as upgrading ammo pools are to be found; meaning you very quickly get to to do everything you COULD do combat wise in sprawl. Slide-jumping to avoid damage and keep high momentum, wall running, shotgun-jumping and weapon swapping to cancel animations is fun, but that is more or less all there is to the depth.Meaning: You essentialy unlock you entire skillset very early on, and there is not that much diversity in your kit. You run, walljump and shoot; and that is it. As for the individual guns...--> The akimbo handguns: Low ammo and accurate. Precision damage is slightly too low, making headshots feel unrewarding...The rest of the weapons may be a spoiler.4. Combatants. Design wise, they are good, but gameplay wise more OK-ish / MEH.They look like they could come straight from JIN-ROH/ Wolf Brigade and fit well into the setting - them being tanky for the most part also fits the aethtetic better than Killzone ever did.But: Enemies have very simple behaviour and are very spongy, making many enemies feel very similar too. While ther is a decent amount of them, MOST enemies do not mix up combat enough to make it interesting. It's mostly well armored guys with guns, that either just try to get in sightline or run up to melee.And most of them are stupidly tanky too. Even basic enemies can take a beating and precision headshots are only doing little damage from your pistols and SMG; which are your most available weapons. The shotgun is essentially the only good feeling way of dispatching 90% of enemies... Only the explosive backpack *some* enemies have allow for quick precision takeouts... but not all enemies have those, and the hitbox feels off. Sometimes shooting it does nothing, sometimes shooting an enemy in the chest causes them to blow up.It somewhat feels like the enemies have highly boosted health to counteract how straight-forward they act; and combat can feel very repetitive and even tedious after a few hours.6.User interface, pickups and map-interactives.Not bad, but they could be  better. HUD readability is OK but could be improved.e.g., you only know how much ammo you have by taking out indiviual weapons. Larger issue is, for example, many resources bars and their corresponding pick-ups not have matching colors.--> Health is green, which is fine.--> HUD armor is blue, but: Armor pickups are NOT always blue. The item is the same shape,  with the color determining the strength. There is yellow, blue and purple armor; meaning most armor does not match the meter and cluttering readabilty.--> Adrenaline is yellow, but the related pickup is BLUE. This makes it feel unintuitive - you would assume small,blue pick-ups to be armor fragments, but those do not exist.(Speaking off: Armor is basically just an overshield, and not "armor"; and is not replenishable).--> Ammo may come in shaoe of props, but is also often just a red orb instead.Ammo readability is unclear. Red icons are hard to distinguish; and some props look very similar to another (such as grenades and energy cells having a VERY similar pick-up).-->Collision for picking up ammo and other drops is also very small.-->Environment readability is also not ideal at times. The maps are large and a bit drab color wise. Sometimes, there are eye-grabbing markers to direct player's attention; but they are sometimes too far spaced out. It is easy to get lost in the map sometimes._________Overall: The game is fun, but runs out of ideas after a while and can feel very same-ish quickly. The fun platforming, interesting maps and atmosphere are engaging enough, and most issues could be fixed with minor tweaks (or mods?) so i am optimistic!Which is why I still would recommend SPRAWL more than I would not.

_childDocuments_.review: I edited the review because they made several changes that addressed some of the issues i had so good job devs :)Overall an enjoyable game and I would recommend :)Pros:Great soundtrack, i really like the music, it fits the game really well and is pretty unique with the vocals mixed with electronic soundsgreat art style the city level is one of the most visually unique and interesting levels ever, the low resolution textures combined with the lighting make for a great visual style, although some levels are a little less interesting to look at cool enemy design, i like all the enemies, they look cool and there is an interesting varietymovement: movement is very good, the wallrun feels great, it took a little while for me to get used to the timing required to cross the most difficult walls but in most cases its very intuitive and reminds me a lot of titanfall. i have played games with inconsistent wall running but i dont think there was a single instance where the wallrun did not behave how i expected it to. air movement is good to and shotgun jumping is funweapons feel satisfying to use, good sounds and animations all round.combat loop is great fun, using bullet time to target weak spots and explode enemies is fun.Cons:Disclaimer, i go into more detail in this section and thats why its longer than the pros section, most of what i have to say here is relatively minor but i just wanted to leave honest feedback, overall i recommend the game so remember thatThere are a few little issues i had, although i think most could be solved with patches :)I think the late game suffers from a more repetitive aesthetic. I think the cityscape is the best looking part of the game but that comes fairly early in the game.a lot of later levels feature underground levels that all look a bit samey. although the final area is an exception it looks greatthere are a couple of little things that i think could be improved1: The slide: i think the slide is a bit useless other than for slide jumping because it slows you down heavily when you use it. my suggestion is to give a small speed boost upon leaving a slide, rather than a speed penalty that we have now2: Some weapons feel a bit generic and i think maybe they could have some more functionality that makes them stand out. For example, the railgun could pierce multiple enemies.  3 The rocket launcher:  perhaps it could fire a burst of rockets rather than fire every single rocket simultanously that way it could be used more as a crowd control weapon, although it is still pretty good for that4 (minor nitpick but ill include it) The switches are kind of difficult to press when you are moving fast, maybe a more generous hitbox could help this.5 Melee seems a little weak, its only really useful on stunned enemies. I think the ability to backstab enemies that are unaware for an instakill would be a cool featureOverall though i recommend the game, great visuals, soundtrack and fun combat loop. A polished and fun indie shooter,  we can never have too many of them

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: SPRAWL isn't a bad modern retro shooter by any means, but in the seeming tsunami of new releases in the genre coming out all the time, it's not what I would call a must buy over some others if you haven't played those.My simple description of SPRAWL is Ghostrunner + DOOM 2016 with a layer of cyberpunk on top. It has sword melee attacks, wallrunning and heavy use of slowdown, but also has their equivalent of glory kills and battle arenas where crowd control strategies are essential to success. You're in a cyberpunk world where an evil corporate junta runs everything and an AI is in charge. That AI goes rogue and is directing you to help it in its aims, though I will say the twist on that did surprise me a bit. You're slicing and shooting your way through the city to get to where it lives. It's a simple story, but gives a good reason for what you're doing.The combat isn't bad, but I don't think it's nearly as well tuned or polished as other boomer shooters. Enemies and new weapons are drip fed to you over the course of the campaign, which isn't a bad thing, but there can sometimes feel like a bit too big a gap between reveals. The weapon feedback also doesn't feel particularly strong and some essential FPS weapons like the shotgun don't feel great because while you don't have to reload anything, the recock time between shots is so long, it's borderline useless in large crowds, of which you'll face many. Most of the guns have limited ammo and they do cleverly space out what ammo you'll get and when, which forces you to use all the guns in your arsenal and learn what guns are best against what enemies. I think this is actually really good design, but I think the guns themselves need more punch.The platforming is also not bad, but not nearly as smooth and tight as Ghostrunner. You can wall run, but can only boost twice before touching the ground again. Large sections of certain levels involve platforming and some of them demand much more precision than I feel you need to. There's no quicksaving and the checkpoints are sometimes very close together, but other times so far apart, that missing one part of a long platforming sequence means having to do it all over again. Again, not bad, but could have been better.Despite these criticisms, this isn't a bad game by any means. It's about 5 hours long so it doesn't overstay its welcome and it's quite an impressive effort for a team of two developers. There's several other games I would recommend playing before this if you haven't, but if you're craving more boomer shooters, I think you'll still enjoy this, despite its flaws. I hope this succeeds so the devs can make another game with the experience they've gotten from making this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Sprawl is the textbook example of a diamond in the rough, and when I say rough, I mean ROUGH.When it's firing on all cylinders, it's exhilarating. A kickass cyberpunk quake game with Doom 2016 combat and the best parts of Doom Eternal's resource management and enemy weaknesses. Stellar art direction and creative level designs keep pushing you up and on with some weighty movement tech and slippery enemies. Despite some low-tech AI, the enemy will push you to the limit and always keep you on your toes. All of this is backed by an amazing soundtrack and an intriguing world. Ghost in the Shell and Half-Life 2 are some of my favorite scifis, and this game wears their influence on its sleeve.That being said, this things was 100% rushed out the door with some boneheaded design decisions and a terrarium of bugs. Certain enemy types are bulletsponges that clash hard with the flow, with a general aversion to weapon flinch or reasonable health values. It's bizarre because a bunch of the enemies, even some of the tanky ones, have specific weaknesses and critpoints that facilite fun, fastpaced duels. But others either have no weak points or tiny ones with giant health bars and next to no weapon flinch from your arsenal. You have any idea how much of a turnoff it is for an enemy to take a grenade or a rocket to the face, lose a tiny chunk of health, and just walk it off?That's not even mentioning some of the weapon balancing. Crunchy weapon sounds and models do their best to make up for the lack of impact. But when your industrial meat grinder of a shotgun can barely crunch through a twinky robot, it's a serious issue. Let's not forget a railgun that DOESNT over-penatrate, let alone get most high tier enemies to flinch.These issues are all pretty bad, but what kills it is the lack of polish across all areas. Clipping, earrape audio glitches, poor music cycling, and an aversion to difficulty balance in nightmare mode are the highlights (all world pickups are disabled on the hardest difficulty, meaning you have to get your health and ammo by criting enemies. Believe it or not, this is doable and super fun in the well designed areas. But in late game, power weapons are barely given ammo, and in the worst case scenario, the act two boss can be softlocked if you run out of ammo, which is insanely common). Throw in the odd mismatch of small bugs with the bad design choices and huge glitches, and one really starts to doubt their enjoyment of the game. I sure did.This is a mess, no doubt about that. But when it works, it's insanely fun. With some patching and a balance overhaul, this game could soar. The devs seem super happy to take feedback and consider ideas for future patches, so I'd like to think things are only going to get better from here. But only time will tell.This is a borderline recommendation: as it stands, playing it now is a roll of the dice. I had a lot of fun, but that's despite the laundry list of issues. I'd be curious to know where the team goes from here, because under all the mud, there's a killer shooter here. Arena shooters are in a renaissance right now, and I'd love to see this have the comeback it deserves.Update 9/1/2023: QoL updates and bugfixes have shipped in a recent update. Improvements are subtle, but absolute positives. Here's hoping it's a sign of momentum...

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. Some issues I have encountered:- when starting a new level or resuming after you die, a really loud crash-like sound plays. _childDocuments_.review: this game activates my brain in a way that i dont think any other game can. PLAY IT. one thing i see a lot in negative or middling reviews is criticism of the movement and its "limitations". you get two wallhops per jump, as well as a slide. as such, your movement is a limited resource you have to manage, but one that can be extended and expanded by trying new tricks, experimenting, and optimizing your paths through arena. it forces you to actually pay more attention to your surroundings in a much more involved way, rather than just letting you bhop or grapple in circles around arenas like the newer doom games, forcing you to think several steps ahead and plan for potential situations before they happen (i.e. low health, a new enemy, low ammo, etc). it really feels more like mirrors edge in terms of its movement and traversal philosophy more than titanfall. if you play it without being creative with your movement, doing the bare minimum to make it through levels, yeah, you probably wont think its mindblowing. frankly, the game is only as fun as you let it be for yourself. you owe it to yourself to turn up the difficulty (lower right corner of the start menu), crank up the FOV, and let yourself feel probably the closest to a gun wielding ninja you can in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a cyberpunk retro FPS game that blends nostalgia and innovation seamlessly. The game follows the story of SEVEN, a fallen super soldier, navigating a corrupt cyberpunk dystopia. The game features immersive storytelling and intense action, with gravity-defying wall runs and unique cybernetic enhancements for combat.The gameplay offers a challenging experience, requiring both reflexes and strategic thinking to overcome diverse and deadly enemies. The city of SPRAWL, from dark alleys to decaying skyscrapers, becomes a dynamic battleground. The game's mechanics, including bullet time and limited ammunition, add urgency and complexity to engagements.The game's visuals and art style capture the essence of retro gaming, with deliberate use of polygons reminiscent of PlayStation 2 graphics. The black and red color palette contributes to the grim atmosphere. The sound design, from explosive gunfire to a blend of retro and contemporary music, enhances the immersion.Level design is intricate and empowers players to explore and discover, with wall running adding a new dimension to navigation. The narrative, though familiar in its post-apocalyptic AI uprising theme, melds well with the retro backdrop. The absence of multiplayer modes harks back to the authenticity of classic FPS games, while the single-player experience remains engaging due to the QR code mechanic and replayability.SPRAWL's optimization ensures accessible gameplay across different hardware configurations, proving that cutting-edge graphics aren't necessary for an immersive experience. In conclusion, SPRAWL stands as a compelling choice for fans of classic FPS games, delivering a nostalgic yet creatively reimagined experience that captures the essence of retro gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive been really enjoying the base game right now but there are few things that I believe could be refined a bit more for an even better experience. _childDocuments_.review: Been really enjoying the game so far, played until E2M2. The controls are simple but it makes movement feel really flexible and smooth. I wasn't a huge fan of the wall running at first, but once I learnt that sliding before wallrunning increases the wallrun's momentum I felt like an absolute parkour god. Not to mention how fluidly you can switch between standard movement and wallrunning, and how you can just jump into the wall you're running on to reset your upwards momentum. I never felt like I was out of control of my character. Absolutely amazing for a 2 man passion project. First of all, the map. Several reviews here have already stated before, but the map can look REALLY samey. There's so much brown and gray and industrial sites everywhere that it can be REALLY easy to get lost. Not to mention it makes everything look pretty drab. It's also really frustrating trying to find the last mob you have to kill once you've already massacred most of an arena. Secondly, the ammo system. I'm accepting of ammo systems forcing you to diversify your use of your arsenal, but I feel like the way SPRAWL does it is a bit TOO limiting. Really not a big fan of only certain enemies dropping certain types of ammo. Instead of diversifying use and forcing creativity, it more often than not makes me think "Oh, this arena is gonna be filled with Oni Elites? Guess I'm busting out the shotgun!" Makes me wish that ammo drops were universal, or make enemies drop a decent amount of their ammo type, along with a small amount of a random ammo type. Speaking of enemies and ammo type: Thirdly, the mechs. I really, really don't like the mechs. Since they're fully invincible to any form of bullet damage, they really only have 2 forms of counterplay. Either spam 'em down with what super limited explosive ammo you have, which probably has been mostly used up in crowd clearing, or...you wait. and either spam down the tossed grenades with smg bullets/shotgun shells or spend adrenaline. When a mech comes up, the game slows down to an absolute crawl. Without explosive ammo, whether you can harm the mech or not is COMPLETELY up to the mercy of the mech itself. And for a movement shooter, especially one that encourages constant weapon swapping, I feel that's really unhealthy. It definitely needs more counterplay and/or less health. Disregarding that, great game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: AAA studios should take notes on the fact that 4k ultra-realistic textures are not necessary to make a game feel high quality- in fact, the pixelated, low-res textures work together with the lighting and phenomenal OST and punchy sound design to build a gritty, dark environment and the game genuinely feels better with these stylistic choices taken into account. If you like movement games like Ghostrunner, Titanfall, and Doom Eternal, pick this game up. You'll love it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome.The level designs are great and realistically capture what a dystopian future reality could look like, and it has a wonderful PS2-era feel to it all.The combat is satisfying when you manage to pull off some sweet, fluid combos.And the music is fantastic. I love my music, and it's really well done in this. Hits all the right spots.The reason why I refunded it is that it's just not the game for me, personally. Reason being that there isn't enough to kill in the levels I played, and this game incentivises speed, like the classic PS2 arcade games of the noughties, where you would be given a stat screen after a level showing you your completion time, collection % etc., which this game also does.Unfortunately, I misunderstood the trailers and thought the game was something else, so that's entirely on me. But this game definitely will appeal to many. Its gameplay is too epic not to.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the price for a romp, I'd say. It's like Ghostrunner had to be ported to a weaker console, but one of those weird ports where it's basically not the same game anymore? You know? Also there's guns and the guns are cool. Cute little shooter, lots of slow motion, headshots, ammo management, and moving around feeling cool. Setpieces are big and grandiose and pretty, weapons are very well animated and sound great (chaingun and railgun are amazing), enemies have cool designs, and the soundtrack is constantly pumping. Great pick-up if you need something bite-sized, strong recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is one of those games that does justice to retro games and I've had an absolute blast shooting my way through the city. The soundtrack is god tier and the way the music pumps up when you're fighting good is so kick ass. If you like ghost in the shell but wish it was more aggressive, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: SPRAWL

_childDocuments_.review: Great short game well worth the price, overall I'd give it a 7/10. Wallrunning and sliding around the beautiful neon lit environments and shooting baddies while listening to the soundtrack is exhilarating. I'm not exactly sure what the genre of music used in this game is called, but I need more of it. You can hear the ghost in the shell inspired chimes/singing in every track. Combat feels like a watered down version of Doom Eternal (not that thats a bad thing) with well a done parkour system. The cyberpunk art style is so pretty and this game is proof of that. The best part is that this game doesn't sacrifice performance for visuals. I get around 240 fps most of the time and 160 fps during combat, which is plenty. I'm hope I'm not the only one who cracked up when they recognized the free Mixamo jump animation for the default soldier enemies. Some annoying things for me are the reused enemies but with more health and some of the weapons feel awful to use like the sniper railgun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly excellent, especially coming from an indie studio. It's a well-executed dystopian cyberpunk story that combines all the best elements of Quake and Mirror's Edge. The difficulty can be a bit sharp off the bat but once you're used to it it's a truly engaging game. Beautiful cinematic visuals and absolutely gripping gameplay. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Did someone say "boomer shooter"? Apparently so!From the outset it's clear that Sprawl wears that badge with pride. Hardcore as it comes with a particular focus on wall running and mobility it's a shooter that doesn't hold your hand. Frantic and fun, delightfully retro and very, very rewarding to master.

_childDocuments_.review: SPRAWL is a hardcore retro FPS set in an endless cyberpunk megalopolis. Escape the walled city and take on the militarized government of the sprawl. Fueled by the blood of your enemies and a mysterious voice in your head, make your way towards the spire to topple whatever lays within.
